title: P0 heap red-zones are not comparable: rf2-2rtt6.4's 4 roots share one subscription set (amortised 4x) while the ladder uses distinct queries
description:
P0 AUDIT FINDING (read-only cold read of the P0 baseline wave, 2026-07-31, before candidate results open).

THE TWO RETAINED-HEAP RED-ZONE SETS ON rf2-2rtt6.1 ARE BOTH MARKED OPERATIVE AND THEY MEASURE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES.

WHAT IS WRONG. rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver holds P0_ROOTS=4 roots per arm and divides the retained delta by ROOTS*perRoot = 1,200 boundaries (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs lines 264 and 347). All four roots render (ux/u-root arms/frame-id) / (rg/u-root arms/frame-id) -- THE SAME frame-id and THE SAME [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors (p0_uix.cljs:111, p0_heap.cljs arm-table, p0_arms.cljs frame-id). One frame means one subscription cache, so the page holds 300 reactions at refcount 4 and divides them over 1,200 boundaries. ITS "EXCLUSIVE RETAINED PER BOUNDARY" AMORTISES THE SUBSCRIPTION HALF OF EVERY READ ACROSS FOUR BOUNDARIES.

rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder is the opposite BY EXPLICIT DESIGN and its page says so: "Every read is a distinct query ... so no two boundaries share a reaction and the per-read figure carries the subscription as well as the hook. That is ... the honest worst case: a page where many boundaries read ONE shared sub pays the reaction once, not once each."

MARKUP DENSITY AND BOUNDARY COUNT DO NOT EXPLAIN THE GAP -- THEY ARE HELD CONSTANT. .4's grid witness is 301 elements over 300 boundaries (1 el/boundary) x 4 roots = 1,200 boundaries. The ladder's Curve B is 1,200 span.cell boundaries (1 el/boundary). Same reader (CDP getHeapUsage after a forced collection), same arm-minus-floor rule against a component-free React floor, same one read per boundary. The answers still differ:

  exclusive retained B/boundary @ 1 read | .4 grid (4 shared roots) | .5 ladder (distinct queries) | gap
  Reagent-on-subs                        |   947                    | 1,565                       | 1.65x
  UIx-on-subs                            | 2,134                    | 3,811                       | 1.79x
  UIx / Reagent                          | 2.254x                   | 2.435x                      | 8%

THE SHARING MODEL PREDICTS THE GAP AND A THIRD INSTRUMENT CONFIRMS IT. Solving S + H = ladder and S/4 + H = .4grid for the subscription half S gives Reagent S ~= 824 B and UIx S ~= 2,236 B. rf2-2rtt6.12's same-run ablation (distinct queries) measures the Reagent subscription half directly at 866 B (5% apart) and the UIx side at 1,684 B live + 769 B retained-dead = 2,453 B (9% apart). Three instruments, one arithmetic. The RATIO survives only because the amortisation is common-mode across both arms.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, BEFORE THE TOURNAMENT.

(1) THE STATED REASON FOR NOT RE-RUNNING THE HEAP AXIS IS FALSE AS STATED. rf2-a4x1o, the studio README and p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md's "not superseded" banner all justify converging only the clock with: "three shapes differing 4x in markup density agree within 8% -- retained bytes per subscribing boundary is a property of the BOUNDARY". That is a RATIO agreement produced by a bias that cancels in the ratio. The QUANTITY the red-zone table is stated in disagrees by 65-79% between the two sources, on witnesses whose markup density and boundary count are identical. Portability of the ratio is real; portability of the quantity is not demonstrated and is contradicted by the wave's own numbers.

(2) THE BEAD PUBLISHES BOTH FORMS AS OPERATIVE AND THEY GIVE OPPOSITE VERDICTS. .4's ratios (list 2.262x, grid 2.254x) and .5's absolutes (208 B shell, 3,552 B/read, 3,807 B @1 read, 10,785 @3, 24,758 @7, 71,229 @20) are both on this bead as red-zones and neither is superseded. A candidate at 2,600 B/boundary at one read is 2600/947 = 2.75x -> RED under .4, and 2600 < 3807 -> NOT RED under .5. That is a red/green flip on the same measurement, decided by which published red-zone a reader reaches for.

(3) THE K3 / PAPER-BUDGET QUESTION HAS TWO PUBLISHED ANSWERS. validation.md line 35 sets exclusive retained per boundary at ~0.4-0.5 KB target, >1 KB paper-fail. .4 puts the Reagent denominator at 954 B -- UNDER the line, and its page says the denominator is "close to it". .5 puts it at 1,565 B -- 1.6x OVER it. Whether the shipped Reagent adapter already fails the paper budget at a single read is K3-relevant and is currently answered both ways in the same governance record.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, cheapest first:

  (a) STATE THE SHARING REGIME ON EVERY HEAP RED-ZONE ROW. A retained-per-boundary figure is only defined relative to how many boundaries share a subscription. The ladder's distinct-query regime is the honest worst case and is the one HD-002's grouped-tier prize (~2,600 B/read, ~18 KB on the seven-read archetype) is already priced against.
  (b) PREFER THE RATIO FORM for the red-zone, since it is the form that survived (2.262 / 2.254 / 2.435), and drop or relabel the absolute-byte red-zone rows so a candidate cannot be judged against two incompatible scales.
  (c) IF THE ABSOLUTES ARE TO STAND, re-take .4's heap rows with P0_ROOTS=1, or with per-root disjoint query ranges, so both sources measure the same quantity. This is an instrument change, not a witness change, so it does not disturb the clock convergence.

NOT A CLAIM THAT ANY NUMBER IS WRONG. Every figure cited is reproducible as published; each is a correct measurement of what its own arm measured. The defect is that two different quantities are labelled with one name and both are operative.

Files: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs (ROOTS, boundariesOf, bytesPerBoundaryCdp), implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_heap.cljs (arm-table, mount!), implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_uix.cljs / p0_reagent.cljs (u-root, w1-root), docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md, docs/design/hicasso/validation.md.

RED-ZONE AMENDMENT IS THE OPERATOR'S. This bead surfaces and prices the incomparability; it does not amend the bar, the budgets, the kill criteria or any red-zone.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-31, dossier review):

MECHANICS. rf2-2rtt6.1 is append-never (rf2-0znkn column limit) and was NOT touched. This note on rf2-2rtt6.16 is the AUTHORITATIVE INTERIM RECORD of the ruling. OBLIGATION: transcribe this ruling onto the standard's successor record as soon as rf2-0znkn's remedy executes (being ruled in parallel today). This bead stays open until that transcription lands.

THE FINDING RULED ON. The two P0 retained-heap red-zone families published as operative measure different quantities under one name. rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver holds 4 roots rendering the SAME 300 [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors against ONE frame -> one subscription cache, 300 reactions at refcount 4, divided over 1,200 boundaries: its "exclusive retained per boundary" amortises the subscription half of every read across four boundaries. rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder gives every boundary a DISTINCT query by design -- the honest worst case, carrying the full subscription per read. Same reader (CDP getHeapUsage after forced collection), same arm-minus-floor rule, same 1 element/boundary, same boundary count -- and the absolutes differ 1.65-1.79x: Reagent 947 (.4 grid) vs ~1,562 (.5 ladder) B @1 read; UIx 2,134 vs ~3,807 B. (This bead's description quotes 1,565/3,811 -- the superseded ladder publication; the current tracked publication after the R=0-fit correction reads 1,562/3,807, a <0.3% move that changes nothing in this decision.) The sharing model predicts the gap and a third instrument confirms the arithmetic: solving S + H = ladder and S/4 + H = .4grid gives Reagent S ~= 820-824 B vs rf2-2rtt6.12's directly measured 866 B (5% apart); UIx S ~= 2,231-2,236 vs 2,453 B (1,684 live + 769 retained-dead; 9% apart). Three instruments, one arithmetic. The "8% agreement across shapes" (2.262 / 2.254 / 2.435x) that justified not re-running the heap axis was RATIO agreement produced by a common-mode bias that cancels in the ratio: portability of the ratio is real; portability of the quantity was not demonstrated. Live consequence pre-ruling: a candidate at 2,600 B/boundary @1 read was RED under .4's family (2600/947 = 2.75x > 2.254x) and NOT RED under .5's (2,600 < 3,807) -- a verdict flip decided by which published row a reader reached for; and K3's paper line was answered both ways (.4's 954 B put shipped Reagent under the 1 KB line, .5's 1,565 put it 1.6x over).

SYNTHESIS. This ruling merges the dossier's three-part recommendation with the Codex Recommendation appended to the same dossier (source-verified down to the cache-key mechanics). Adoptions and rejections are attributed inline.

PART 1 -- CACHE CARDINALITY IS PART OF THE WITNESS; THE DISTINCT-QUERY LADDER IS THE MANDATORY WORST-CASE WITNESS AND THE OPERATIVE ENVELOPE (dossier part 1, sharpened per Codex rec 1). Neither published absolute family is crowned a universal bytes-per-boundary red-zone. The sharing regime (cache cardinality) is part of the witness definition. Every heap red-zone row stamps at least B (boundaries), E (boundary-query edges), Q (unique live query keys) -- hence reads/boundary E/B and mean fan-out E/Q -- alongside the version and instrument-hash provenance the studio pages already carry. The .5 ladder (Q = E) is the MANDATORY distinct-query capacity witness: its rows are the operative red-zone family, and where governance needs one conservative number (paper sizing), the distinct-query row is used and labelled "upper-envelope capacity budget", never "retained bytes per boundary" unqualified. The .4 grid is NOT corrected and is NOT an alternative calibration of the same quantity: it stands as valid evidence for the shared-query fan-out witness class (E/Q = 4); its absolute rows are relabelled "fan-out 4 (amortised x4) -- shared-query witness evidence, not comparable to distinct-query rows"; its ratios (list 2.262x, grid 2.254x) stay published as the cross-regime check that survives regimes. A candidate row is judged ONLY against donor rows measured under the same regime on the same witness (same B/E/Q and query values) -- which blocks the verdict flip in BOTH directions: an amortised candidate flattered against the worst-case family, and a fan-out-heavy candidate punished against worst-case-only baselines. Mechanism, source-verified (Codex): the production cache key is the query vector itself; a hit returns the existing reaction and increments a scalar ref-count; the per-frame cache is {query-vector {:reaction ... :ref-count n}} (subs.cljc 508-543, 1315-1378, 1662-1681; subs/cache.cljc 1-20) -- four consumers of one (frame, query-vector) retain ONE reaction plus four attachments. .4's driver divides the held delta by ROOTS*perRoot while every root renders the same frame-id and query vectors (p0_run.cjs 103, 312, 377-395 at the current tree -- this bead's description cites 264/347 at its revision; p0_heap.cljs 82-142, 176-192; p0_reagent.cljs 81-101; p0_uix.cljs 84-113): 1,200 edges over 300 unique keys, and a shared reachable cache node is counted once by the heap readers, so dividing by four consumers necessarily amortises it. CONFIRMATION AND PRICING SWEEP ADOPTED (Codex rec 4, subsuming the dossier's optional ROOTS=1 re-take): bench bead rf2-5prok -- non-gating for this ruling (which stands regardless), gating for freezing Part 3's component budgets. Prediction on record: the fan-out-1 rung lands on the ladder's distinct-query family (Reagent ~1,562 B, UIx ~3,807 B @1 read) within instrument noise; a material miss reopens this part.

PART 2 -- TWO MEMORY GATES, BOTH REGIME-MATCHED: THE RED-ZONE STAYS UIx-SOURCED AND THE REAGENT LINE GOVERNS THROUGH K3 (Codex rec 2 adopted OVER dossier part 2; the dossier's part 2 as stated -- replace the UIx red-zone source with per-axis-best Reagent -- is REJECTED). The finding that motivated the dossier stands and is recorded: on retained heap the frontier INVERTS. UIx wins the per-boundary shell (208 B vs Reagent 428 B, 0.49x) and loses the read by 3.77x (3,552 vs 943 B/read marginal; first-read increment 3,600 vs 1,137 B). The crossover is below one read -- any boundary that subscribes at all is cheaper on Reagent -- and the census seven-read archetype costs 24,758 B/boundary on the raw UIx spine vs Reagent's 6,587 B. A UIx-derived per-read red-zone is therefore 3.77x looser than the best measured option on the axis memory was declared most winnable. WHY THE REJECTION: HD-012 already assigns the two comparators different jobs -- K3 = per-boundary heap worse than matched Reagent with no paper path down (kill rule); the UIx material-cost rule = materially worse than direct UIx (the 2026-07-30 red-zone). Redefining the red-zone source as Reagent would collapse the two gates and erase the informative between-state: a candidate between Reagent and UIx has CLEARED the UIx material-cost threshold while K3 is STILL UNRESOLVED until it names and demonstrates a path down, and calling that state either "green" or "red" loses information. OPERATIVE STATEMENT: every candidate heap row reports BOTH matched-regime ratios. On the mandatory distinct-query witness the lines are: UIx 3,552 B/read [3,551-3,553] -- worse than this is RED, needing an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit (the 2026-07-30 threshold ruling's heap arm is not replaced but regime-QUALIFIED: "the measured UIx ratio for that witness family" now reads the witness family as including cache cardinality, so the amortised 2,134 B figure is never the threshold for a distinct-query candidate row); Reagent 943 B/read [935-944] -- worse than this with no named paper path down is K3 territory; between them is "UIx-rule cleared, K3 open until a path down is named", never plain green. The dossier's crisp tournament target survives untouched: BEAT 943 B/read is the K3-clean line -- what moved relative to the dossier is only where Reagent's line lives (in K3, where HD-012 already put it), not whether it governs. Resolution of the flip example: 2,600 B/boundary @1 read on the distinct-query witness = below UIx's 3,807 -> not red; above Reagent's 1,562 -> K3 open pending a named path down. Single-valued, three-state, no reader-dependence. The clock axis is untouched (the converged witness set governs there).

PART 3 -- THE K3 PAPER LINE SPLITS: SHELL vs READ, WITH THE THREE-TERM DECOMPOSITION AS THE TARGET SHAPE (dossier part 3 adopted now; Codex rec 3 adopted as the budget's end state, its numbers gated on the sweep). validation.md's "exclusive retained per boundary: target ~0.4-0.5 KB; >1 KB fails on paper" is amended to say explicitly that this target/fail line is the R=0 BOUNDARY SHELL. Both measured shells comply: Reagent ~418-428 B, UIx ~208 B. The per-read axis is judged separately, under Part 2's regime-matched gates. Consequences: the shipped Reagent adapter is NOT retroactively K3-failed -- its ~1,562 B @1 read = measured shell (~428 B; the dossier quotes ~418) + first-read increment (~1,137 B [1,125-1,141]), each judged on its own axis -- and candidates cannot pass the paper line by amortising subscriptions across boundaries. The K3 both-ways contradiction (954 B "under the line" vs 1,565 B "1.6x over") is dissolved: both were correct measurements of different quantities; neither was a K3 verdict. Codex refinement adopted as the budget's target shape: the read side decomposes into a per-edge (consumer attachment) term and a per-unique-subscription-key term; in the distinct-query witness (Q = E) the ladder's 943 B slope is their SUM -- a valid total marginal cost in that regime only, not a pure view-layer per-read price. Component budget rows (shell / per-edge / per-unique-key) enter validation.md only after the bench sweep verifies the additive model and prices the terms; freezing them today from cross-instrument algebra is REFUSED -- the algebra is sufficient to reject the unqualified scalar (solved subscription term ~820 B Reagent / ~2,231 B UIx vs .12's directly measured 866 / 2,453 B -- 5% / 9%) but the paired rows came from different instruments and runs.

WHY NOT THE OTHER ALTERNATIVES. Keeping both families operative leaves every future heap verdict reader-dependent -- the donor ruling would be contestable the day it issued. Ratio-only (this bead's option b) survives measurement but prices nothing absolute: HD-002's collector survival metric and the grouped-tier prize (~2,600 B/read, ~18 KB on the seven-read archetype -- priced in the distinct-query regime) lose their denominators. Crowning .4's amortised family would systematically flatter candidates that share subscriptions across boundaries -- the shape the census says real pages sometimes have, but the worst case doesn't.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS. The donor-gate advisory ruling (rf2-2rtt6.7, the HD-008 delegated advisory) was waiting on single-valued heap numbers. They are now single-valued per witness and regime: mandatory distinct-query envelope; UIx red-zone line 3,552 B/read; Reagent/K3 line 943 B/read (first-read increment 1,137 B; ~1,562 B @1 read); shell target 0.4-0.5 KB with both measured arms compliant.

DOC FOLLOW-THROUGH (mayor to dispatch as doc beads; deliberately not filed from this ruling seat): (i) p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md heap table -- relabel the absolute rows "fan-out 4 (amortised x4), shared-query witness -- not comparable to distinct-query rows", stamp B/E/Q, keep the ratios as the cross-regime check, point the operative family at the ladder; (ii) reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md -- stamp "distinct-query (Q = E), mandatory worst-case witness, operative upper-envelope family"; (iii) validation.md -- amend the budget row per Part 3 (shell line now; component rows only after the sweep); (iv) studio README banner accordingly.

title: P0 lane driver: the CLOCK row's unverified count and the positive control are printed, never adjudicated (p0_run.cjs)
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.3's audit discharge (PR #7272), REPORTED NOT REPAIRED — it is a fourth instrument, outside that bead's three riders, and worker/lane-control-cluster is live on the adjacent lane.cljs (rf2-egdaq control-verdict, rf2-pq7d8, rf2-9zysg).

THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THE PR #7262 AUDIT NAMED on hicasso_narrow_run.cjs item 2, and it is present in implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:

1. THE CLOCK ROW'S DOM VERIFICATION IS NOT A GATE. `unverified` is accumulated (lines 283, 331), stored (387) and printed (412) — 'N unverified of M mounts'. The exit logic then adjudicates ONLY the heap row: line 491 reads `out.heap.verification.unverified > 0`. A clock run in which writes never reached the page therefore prints its count beside 'VERDICT: reportable' and exits 0. Compare hicasso_narrow_run.cjs, which now exits 1 on any nonzero count from a verifiable arm.

2. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS PRINTED WITH A RATIO AND NEVER ADJUDICATED IN THE DRIVER. p0_run.cjs line ~409 prints 'predicted N B | measured M B [min-max] (ratio X)' and nothing reads the ratio. lane.cljs has `control-verdict` for exactly this, so the machinery exists and the heap driver does not call it.

WHY IT MATTERS: these rows feed rf2-2rtt6.1's P0 table, and 'the driver exited 0' is being used as evidence that the gates passed. rf2-2rtt6.1 already carries a MERGED-PR AUDIT #7265 note making precisely that point about a sibling driver ('do not treat driver exit 0 / reportable as evidence those omitted gates passed').

SUGGESTED FIX, small and fail-closed, NOT a framework: adjudicate the clock row's unverified count in the same place the heap row's is adjudicated, and route the heap driver's control through lane.cljs's control-verdict rather than printing a bare ratio.

SEQUENCING: the control half touches control-verdict's callers, and rf2-egdaq is tightening control-verdict right now. Sequence this AFTER that PR merges.
close_reason: Wired and proved in PR #7276 (worker/p0-driver-95s5b, commit 2fd3a362176e9a01b42dad5992e16817bdb5d1d5). p0-app/adjudicate replaces aggregate as the ONLY door onto the clock fold and returns the summed N-unverified-of-M plus lane/control-verdict's answer with the record; P0H.controlVerdict routes the heap row's control through the same lane rule. Driver exits 1 on either row's nonzero unverified count and on either control that is not ok, and names EVERY failed gate. control-verdict's DECISION logic untouched (rf2-egdaq remains the operator's). mount-sample! now excludes an unverifiable window (expected nil - the positive control) from the denominator instead of counting it as verified; control-round! always discarded those counts so no figure moves. Proved by mutation: floor bulk force! no-op -> 96 unverified of 264, exit 1; control-2x building the same page as control-1x -> measured 1.210x vs predicted 1.998x DISJOINT, exit 1; P0H.control allocating a tenth -> 470610 B vs 4700000 B, exit 1. Mutations restored byte-identical (p0_arms.cljs blob 89d26f8b9853d4fd06abfbdd99e6c7ac8a4cc060 == origin/main). NO PUBLISHED NUMBER WOULD HAVE FAILED: a clean run at the published sizes reproduces the studio page's denominator exactly - W1-list 200 + W3-form 1600 + bulk-broad 800 + bulk-narrow 4000 = 6600, 0 unverified; heap 0 of 48; both published controls sit INSIDE the +/-25% band, so neither reading of rf2-egdaq changes them. title: Decompose the UIx spine's 3,550 B per subscription read
description:
rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder measured a re-frame2 subscription read at 3,550 B/boundary on the UIx spine against 942 B on Reagent — 3.77x, and reader C says the whole difference is object COUNT (128.5 objects/read against 36.2) at ~27 B per object on both. 128 objects for one read is a lot for uSES + two useRefs + a useMemo, so something in re-frame.substrate.spine's use-subscribe is allocating more than the hook stack accounts for (the spine's own comments mention a durable subs/subscribe in the render-phase useMemo alongside the committed-ref path — worth checking whether a read registers twice).

This is not a Hicasso-only question: UIx is a FIRST-CLASS shipped adapter, so if the per-read cost can be brought toward Reagent's 942 B that is a direct win for shipping consumers, and it also moves the bar Hicasso is measured against.

Method: ride the same instrument. reads_ladder_run.cjs already takes LADDER_SUBSTRATES and the arms come from the page, so an ablation ladder over the spine's hooks can reuse the collector, the in-situ control and the order guard rather than growing a second one — which is how rf2-2rtt6.5 itself was built on B7.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md sections 1 and 3.

notes:
AUDIT PR #7259 (2026-07-30; completeness, correctness, implementation quality). The four authored commits are patch-identical to the four landed commits; all eight scoped files were reviewed; required checks were green; and `npm run bench:hicasso` reproduced to exit 0 on current main. The one-build/one-driver lane, per-round floor normalisation, reflecting schedule, advanced-browser provenance, and published range arithmetic are otherwise coherent. Reopened this exact source owner for two load-bearing proof gaps:
1. The mount positive controls are not verified as the doubled workloads they claim. `measure-mount!` sets `expected` to nil for every `:parity-exempt?` arm, `lane/parity` removes those arms from its count map, and `verify-m1`/`verify-m2` inspect only the base prefix (indices 0/299 and fields 0/11). Consequently all 200 measured control mounts (100 M1 + 100 M2) contribute to `0 unverified of 800` without an exact 1,801/99-element assertion or a far-end 599/23 probe. Make the stated 2x workload load-bearing; a control that renders only the base prefix must fail before any figure is reportable.
2. Teardown is part of the repeated-mount instrument but failures are silently swallowed: `lane/release!` catches every arm unmount exception, `release-bulk-arms!` does the same, removes the container, and the driver can still exit 0. There is also no post-release root/subscription-residue assertion. A failed Reagent unmount can leave roots or sub ref-counts alive across hundreds of later samples and bias the denominator while the guard sees only the contaminated page. Fail cleanup loudly and assert the existing frame/subscription residue returns to baseline outside the timed window. Keep it one bounded benchmark assertion, not a lifecycle framework.
The published run is not declared numerically false; these are missing load-bearing controls. Re-run the corrected instrument and retain or republish the rows according to its evidence.
AUDIT PR #7283 (2026-07-30; correctness/completeness follow-up). REOPENED this exact owner: the doubled-control arithmetic, far probes, fatal unverified tally, teardown-exception path, and inter-row settle point are well implemented and reproduced, but the claimed proof of a normally-returning non-release is incomplete.

`lane/release!` and `release-bulk-arms!` call an arm's `:unmount` and then unconditionally remove its container. `lane/residue` can thereafter see only body child count plus the re-frame sub-cache entry/ref-count census. A Reagent ratom arm (and likewise a floor arm) whose unmount returns normally without releasing its React/Reagent root leaves no container in the body and no entry in that frame cache; the ratom reaction is rooted in global `v/ratom-cells`, outside both counters. It can remain live on a detached tree and consume later writes.

Mutation evidence on landed `9737ed5cf815817d856c49eefb6824856df51668`: changing only the bulk ratom unmount to a normal no-op reached and passed `residue-after-bulk`; the run later exited 2 for an independent stochastic arm-order refusal, not cleanup. Restore was verified byte-clean. Make successful release observable for every arm family, especially ratom, and add a bounded normal-no-op mutation proof. Keep this benchmark-local; no generalized lifecycle machinery.

title: EP-0036 records the Freehand programme as withdrawn, and the six EPs that cite it stop implying it is live
description:
RAISED by Mike's 2026-07-30 ruling: the Freehand view-substrate programme is CLOSED AS A FAILED EXPERIMENT. No further work. The code is NOT removed yet.

The tracker half is done (rf2-drpa3 and its tree). This bead is the normative half: the EP corpus still describes Freehand as an accepted, in-flight programme.

WHAT IS WRONG TODAY
1. docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md carries 'Status: accepted'. Per EP-0009 that means 'ruled by the operator; graduation into the normative home' - it asserts a live programme.
2. Six further EPs reference Freehand and were written when it was the intended destination: EP-0030 (the compiled-view-substrate program), EP-0031, EP-0032, EP-0033, EP-0034, EP-0035.
3. docs/EP/README.md indexes them.

THE STATUS VALUE, AND WHY
EP-0009:85-87 makes the Status line MACHINE-READABLE with a CLOSED vocabulary: proposal, accepted, final, active, rejected, withdrawn, deferred, superseded-by EP-NNNN. Do not invent a value.

  WITHDRAWN is the honest one. EP-0009:79 glosses it 'author retracted - kept'. The programme was accepted, attempted at length, and retracted on evidence.
  NOT 'rejected' - EP-0009:78 is 'ruled no' - that describes a proposal turned down before implementation. Freehand was built.
  NOT 'superseded-by EP-NNNN' - there is no successor EP. A third view layer (Hicasso) is in design in ai/findings/new-view/ but has no EP number. If one is later written, THAT is the moment to consider re-pointing, and it is a separate decision.

  If the implementer believes a different value is more honest, STOP AND REPORT rather than choosing - the vocabulary is normative and this is the operator's call.

WHAT ELSE THE EP MUST SAY. A bare status flip loses the finding. The EP should carry, briefly, WHY it was withdrawn, because that reasoning is the durable value:
  - the Reagent standard (rf2-lbs3y, Mike 2026-07-27, verbatim 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent') was not met;
  - the residual gap is architectural, not an optimisation backlog - see docs/design/freehand/studio/ and the ablation on rf2-lbs3y;
  - CRITICALLY, do not repeat the superseded claim that the cost is the tear check. rf2-so3io / PR #7159 FALSIFIED that: dropping useSyncExternalStore AND the commit-side re-read returns only -13.6%/-14.8% on the broad clock and -375 B heap, and a contract-free boundary is still ~5.5x Reagent on clock and ~5x on heap. The guarantee is not what cost us. The same ablation found invariant 5 is worth MORE than Spec 006 claims (a staged site publishes stale and never self-heals).

THE OTHER SIX EPs. Do NOT rewrite them. EP-0009:118 says amendment is allowed only before implementation, and rf2-drpa3.57 records the standing intent that EP-0030..EP-0035 REMAIN as the historical record of the donor programme. What is needed is only that a reader does not mistake them for live: a one-line pointer where each names Freehand as its destination. Judge per file; several may need nothing.

THE CODE STAYS. Mike: 'not removed yet'. No implementation/freehand/** deletion, no build-id removal, no CI lane changes. This bead is docs/EP only.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. EP-0036's Status line is a legal EP-0009 value and the withdrawal reason is stated in the EP itself, not only in beads.
  2. No EP reads as though Freehand is a live destination.
  3. docs/EP/README.md agrees with the new status.
  4. python -m mkdocs build --strict exits 0 (note: mkdocs is not on PATH in Git Bash here - use python -m mkdocs), and check_doc_slugs.py exits 0.
  5. No file under implementation/ is touched.

FENCE: docs/EP/** only. spec/** is HOT-ZONE - report, do not edit. If a spec/ document also asserts Freehand is live, FILE IT, do not fix it here.

EP-0036 Status: accepted -> withdrawn, the EP-0009:79 value ('author retracted - kept'); Resolution line gains '; withdrawn 2026-07-30'. Dated withdrawal note carries the reason: the rf2-lbs3y standard was not met (broad repaint 27.78x the React floor interpreted / 24.83x compiled vs Reagent 2.639x - survives the hot tier, so architectural not an optimisation backlog). The note explicitly records the rf2-so3io/PR#7159 falsification and keeps invariant 5 as RETAINED AND VINDICATED, never as the cause. title: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2940 teaches v1 migrators that a boundary rejection 'reports nothing on either axis'
description:
FOUND BY rf2-j6e7r/v94d6/zfw16's sweep (2026-07-28 19:36 AUSEST, PR #7234).

VERBATIM on origin/main, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2940:

  '**Surviving the build is not the same as being visible in it.** A boundary rejection in production reports nothing on either axis: the emit is dev-gated along with the rest of the trace surface, the error category was never promoted onto the always-on substrate, and — because the skipped handler wrote no :db — the always-on :events record for that dispatch reads :outcome :ok. A quiet dashboard is therefore not evidence that nothing was refused. If the v1 interceptor you are replacing *logged* its rejections, that half does not come across: validate in the handler body and emit the signal from handler code.'

Every clause after the bold lead is false since PR #7203 (rf2-mwv4e), and the last sentence is the damaging one: it tells a migrator that the framework will NOT count their boundary rejections, so they must hand-roll the signal. The always-on record IS the count, so the advice creates the duplicate emission it was written to prevent.

This is the audience that can least afford it. A v1 migrator replacing a check-spec-style interceptor reads this paragraph to decide what they lose, and the honest answer is now 'less than this says': the rejection fans one always-on structural :rf.error/schema-validation-failure record (:source :boundary, identifiers only), settles :outcome :rejected on the dispatch, and — being projection-eligible — draws a 400 from SSR's default projector. What does not come across from a v1 interceptor that LOGGED the offending value is exactly that: the value. The record is deliberately structural, because a boundary payload is attacker-controlled.

THE BOLD LEAD SURVIVES AND SHOULD BE KEPT. 'Surviving the build is not the same as being visible in it' is the right frame; this arm simply moved to the other side of it, so the paragraph becomes a worked instance of C-000.35 rather than its counter-example. spec/010-Schemas.md §Production builds (corrected in PR #7234) is the wording to agree with; spec/Security.md §Input validation is the pattern-level statement.

title: Promote ssr-ring fail-closed-status's silent 200->500 flip to the always-on error axis
description:
rf2-dtpfv IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT ITEM 3, deferred out of PR #7204 (which landed items 1/2/4). Explicitly ruled NOT a prerequisite for the guards, and an egress-surface change of a different review class (same class as rf2-6jqa8; wants an rf2-ov56u-style review).

THE RESIDUE. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj's fail-closed-status coerces a non-integer :status to 500 and its ONLY signal is (trace/emit! :warning :rf.ssr/ssr-non-integer-status ...) — the DEV bus. On a production JVM the app's 200 silently becomes a 500 with nothing on either error axis. rf2-dtpfv named this 'problem 2' and its ruling note says the promotion 'probably wants promoting alongside' the guards.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER IT. PR #7204 made the reserved :rf.server/* fx guard their own args unconditionally, so the ACCUMULATOR is now well-formed in every build and fail-closed-status should no longer fire from the framework's own fx path at all. It stays as the last-line backstop for a host that hand-builds a response map, and the ruling is explicit that it is NOT the primary owner. So the promotion is now about an ADAPTER-level defect signal, not about the fx path — re-measure whether it can still fire before writing the promotion.

WHAT TO DO. Route the flip through the error-emit/emit-error-both! seam (the rf2-2hkfy pattern) with a CONSTANT :reason and never the offending value (the rf2-s3n6h precedent). Keep the Ring materialiser coercions as backstop. If a new :rf.error/* category is needed it MUST land with its Spec 009 §Error event catalogue row in the same PR — implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj source-scans every artefact src/ for throw-error!/emit-error! literals and its allow-list is EMPTY (TOTALITY), so an uncatalogued category reds the core lane. PR #7204 catalogued :rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid the same way and may be a usable model.

FENCE: implementation/ssr-ring/src + test. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE if a row is needed. Gates: implementation/ssr-ring clojure -M:test, plus the core error-catalogue conformance namespace.
notes:
PR #7210 (worker/ring-status-gblft). Item 3 of rf2-dtpfv landed.

RE-MEASURED FIRST (the bead's instruction), under the real gate (clojure -J-Dre-frame.debug=false -M:test, never with-redefs):
 - warning count under -Dre-frame.debug=false = 0; dev = 2 (a DOUBLE-EMIT, see below); always-on records = []. Total silence in production, confirmed.
 - AFTER #7204 the framework fx feeder is DEAD: [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"] leaves :status 500 (Long — guard threw, containment fanned :rf.error/fx-handler-exception, projector stamped); [:rf.server/redirect {:location "/ok" :status "302"}] leaves :redirect nil. Projector path closed too (public-error-shape? requires integer 400-599, else locked 500).
 - NO ARM IS DEAD. nil->fallback and integer?->passthrough run every request; the flip arm is a LIVE backstop reachable only from a HOST that hand-builds the accumulator (public response/swap-response!) or calls the public materialiser with its own map — exactly the caller the ruling reserved it for. Backstop, not dead code.

PROMOTION. One emit site (report-non-integer-status!) so the two axes cannot disagree. Record BUILT FROM the closed #{:error :frame :time :where :status-type :reason :recovery}. :frame is ALWAYS nil by design (the materialiser is a pure map->map fn; both with-frame blocks close before the happy-path call site, so an ambient read would be nil on the very path this bead is about) — the malformed-hydration-payload frameless spelling. :status-type is a CLASS NAME (program structure, the :ex-class residual class). REJECTED the raw :status value (rf2-s3n6h) — dev-trace-only, absence asserted by name AND by scanning every slot value.

CATEGORY MINTED, not reused: :rf.error/ssr-ring-response-status-invalid. server-fx-args-invalid names an fx arg + carries :fx-id (no fx ran — false attribution); sanitised-on-projection names a projector failure + carries :projector-id (no projector here). Spec 009 row + the coupled core always-on-categories literal in ONE commit. Also joined non-projection-eligible-errors (fires post-resolution; frameless so nothing routes today, but it stops a future frame-carrying change silently status-flipping).

BONUS DEFECT FIXED: a target-less redirect with a non-integer status called fail-closed-status TWICE (no-target warning payload + response map) = 2 signals for 1 rewrite. Would have been a double alert on a shipper. Wire status now resolved once.

NO new egress-chokepoint caller (reuses lifecycle/emit-always-on-error!, the seam emit-error-view-failed! already uses) — no allow-list edit. Spec-Schemas.md untouched (ssr-ring always-on categories carry no *Tags schema).

title: spec/009 + API.md: add :rejected to the event-outcome contract (follows rf2-mwv4e)
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-mwv4e (PR #7203), which adopted a NEW public event outcome. spec/** is HOT-ZONE, so the worker reported rather than edited. Split from rf2-lvsen because that bead's edit is coupled to the always-on-categories literal and this one is not — but both touch spec/009, so SEQUENCE them, never parallel.

THE ADDITION. `:outcome :rejected` on the always-on event-emit record: the `:rf.schema/at-boundary` interceptor REFUSED the event's payload against the handler's `:schema`. The handler never ran; entered interceptors still unwound in full.

WHY IT IS NOT AN OVERLOAD, which the spec should say once and plainly. Both existing non-ok values are wrong here: `:error` means the interceptor chain threw (it did not) and `:rolled-back` means a candidate state transition was refused before install (no candidate ever existed — the handler never ran). Keeping `:ok` preserved a known lie: the event stream's own stated contract is that an aborted dispatch is never reported as a clean settle.

THE SHARPEST LINE TO ADD is the COMPLEMENT of the `:rolled-back` caveat the spec already carries at length. `:rolled-back` has NO PRODUCER IN A PRODUCTION BUILD (candidate validation is dev-only). `:rejected` DOES — boundary validation is the one schema surface Spec 010 keeps ungated — so it is the outcome to alert on for hostile or malformed input at an untrusted ingress. Stating the pair together is what stops a reader generalising the `:rolled-back` warning to the whole vocabulary.

PRIORITY: `:rejected` is the LOWEST-priority discriminator. A chain throw, flow throw or candidate rollback during the unwind still wins; it fires only when the boundary skip is the whole story.

SITES:
  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md line ~1220 — the event-emit listener surface's `:outcome` enumeration (the long inline list).
  - spec/API.md line ~859 (Event-emit) — the record-shape paragraph.
  - spec/Spec-Schemas.md — no event-emit record schema with a closed `:outcome` enum exists today (verified: line 4314's enum is the EPOCH record's separate `:ok`/`:halted-*` vocabulary). If one is added, it needs the fifth member.
  - docs/core/observability.md line ~435/447 — the `:outcome :ok | :error | :rolled-back | :flow-error` comment + the prose after it.
  - docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md lines ~255-260 — SEE THE SIBLING DOC BEAD; that page's warning box is now actively wrong, not merely incomplete.

CODE IS ALREADY DONE and needs no further change: `re-frame.event-emit`'s ns docstring carries the full member contract, `re-frame.router`'s `commit-and-flow!` docstring and the pipeline-phase map comment enumerate it. Every consumer was audited in PR #7203 and none switches on a closed vocabulary — `observability/route-handled-event!` passes it to `:status`, `projection/project-handled-event` passes `:status` through as a summary key, the epoch and Xray-mutation `:outcome`s are separate vocabularies on separate records.
close_reason: PR #7207. :rejected added to the 009 :outcome enumeration (line ~1220) with the not-an-overload reasoning and the lowest-priority discriminator rule, plus the sharp line: :rejected is the exact COMPLEMENT of :rolled-back on the production question — :rolled-back has no producer in a release build, :rejected does, because boundary validation is the one ungated schema surface. spec/API.md 859 record-shape paragraph now enumerates all five members and carries the same asymmetry. No code change (event-emit ns docstring + commit-and-flow! already carry it); Spec-Schemas.md needs nothing — no event-emit record schema with a closed :outcome enum exists.

title: spec/010-Schemas.md §Production builds: 'the only difference is whether the check ran, not what happens when it fails' is false
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-05hy2 / rf2-mk8up sweep (PR #7189). HOT-ZONE: spec/010-Schemas.md — sequence, do not parallel.

SITE: spec/010-Schemas.md:227, inside §Production builds, directly under the at-boundary contract — i.e. the emit-site of record for this whole question:

  'Failures from the boundary interceptor flow through the same :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :event path as dev-mode step-1 failures — the recovery (skip handler; downstream queue continues) is identical. The only difference is *whether the check ran*, not *what happens when it fails*.'

The RECOVERY half is true and should stay. The SIGNAL half is false, and the last sentence is precisely the sentence that is wrong. trace/emit-error! is gated on interop/debug-enabled?, so in a production build the emit is DCE'd; the category was never promoted onto the always-on axis; and because the skipped handler produced no :db, the always-on :events record for that dispatch reports :outcome :ok. So what happens WHEN IT FAILS differs a great deal between builds: dev gets a structured trace, production gets silence that reads as success on the one always-on stream.

This matters more than an ordinary prose bug because 010 is the emit-site of record — spec/009's per-:where recovery table explicitly defers to it ('if the two ever disagree, 010 wins'), and 009 has now been corrected by PR #7189. Leaving 010 as-is re-opens the contradiction from the authoritative side.

SCOPE: doc fix only, stating what is true today. Do NOT propose promoting the category or making validation always-on — that is rf2-mwv4e's and an operator ruling (rf2-bkvu5). Change no code.

FENCE: spec/010-Schemas.md only. Hot-zone — sequence against any other 010 worker.

CITE: rf2-mwv4e, rf2-bkvu5, rf2-05hy2, PR #7189.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7194. §Production builds now states that the at-boundary check is ungated and runs on every build, and that what differs between builds is the report, not whether the check ran: emit-error! is debug-enabled?-gated, the category was never promoted, and the always-on :events record reads :outcome :ok. Doc fix only; no normative change.

title: spec/012-Routing.md tells a reader that :rf.error/schema-validation-failure rides the always-on error-emit substrate — it does not
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-05hy2 / rf2-mk8up sweep (PR #7189). HOT-ZONE: spec/012-Routing.md — sequence, do not parallel.

This is the single worst site in the corpus for the at-boundary observability gap, because it is the one place that POSITIVELY tells someone wiring 'register-listener! :errors' -> Sentry that schema-validation failures will arrive.

SITES, all in spec/012-Routing.md:
  - :780 — the navigate error table's 'Drain-level error fired?' cell for the programmatic ':rf.route/navigate {:to ...}' row reads 'yes — rides the always-on error-emit substrate ([009 §Production builds])'. False. implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:451 emits it with 'trace/emit-error!', which is gated on 'interop/debug-enabled?'; the category was never promoted onto the always-on axis.
  - :783 — reinforcing prose: 'a caller-bug surfaces as an exception in dev (and as a substrate error in production); an event-boundary failure surfaces via the standard error substrate'. Same error.
  - :771 — 'it survives production, unlike the dev-only :schema interceptor'. There is no dev-only schema interceptor. The framework's only schema interceptor is ':rf.schema/at-boundary', which is production-REACHABLE (its check is ungated). As written it names a production-reachable interceptor as dev-only.

The file already contradicts itself: :457 correctly calls the category 'the dev-only, schemas-artefact-gated validation channel', as does navigate.cljc:238-240.

THE FACT TO APPLY (rf2-mwv4e, and now stated in spec/009 by PR #7189): the ':rf.schema/at-boundary' check runs on every build and its rejection is real (handler skipped, payload never reaches app-db), but its emit is dev-gated and the category was never promoted, so a production boundary rejection reports nothing on either axis — and because the skipped handler produced no ':db', the always-on ':events' record reads ':outcome :ok'. Production-reachable and production-observable are different claims.

SCOPE: doc fix only. Do NOT propose promoting the category — that is rf2-mwv4e's and an operator ruling (rf2-bkvu5 settled that reg-app-schema validation is development-only and production trusts the programmer). Change no code.

FENCE: spec/012-Routing.md only. Hot-zone — sequence against any other 012 worker.

CITE: rf2-mwv4e (the framework finding), rf2-bkvu5 (the ruling), rf2-05hy2 (the 009 fix this mirrors), PR #7189.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7194. :457 was the correct side of the self-contradiction (emit-error! at trace.cljc:918 is debug-gated; 009 catalogues both ids diagnostic). :780 table cell, :771 ('the dev-only :schema interceptor' — no such thing; validate-route-shape is schemas-artefact-gated, not debug-gated) and :783 corrected; :457 sharpened so dev-only attaches to the report. Doc fix only.

title: Suspected intermittent stall in the browser lane: ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore across 73 test files
description:
Filed alongside rf2-15047 (browser timeout budget raise) so the budget raise is not silently doing double duty as a bug fix.

WHAT WAS SEEN (not investigated further, by instruction):
- PR #7183 (worker/witness-ownership-1829) times out in CI with NO cljs.test summary and NO failing assertion. It reached 66 namespaces on one run and 99 on another - same branch, same commit.
- PR #7181 timed out once and then passed UNCHANGED on re-run.
- Both observed stalls landed in HYDRATION suites, which deliberately toggle the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT.
- 73 test files manipulate that global with ad-hoc set/restore discipline (no shared fixture).

WHY IT IS STILL PROBABLY BUDGET, NOT DEADLOCK: the run-to-run namespace-count variance (66 vs 99) is consistent with a lane whose wall-clock is dominated by real-time settles racing a fixed ceiling - where the cut lands is a function of runner speed, not of a specific namespace. A true deadlock would stall at the SAME namespace. The lane is also demonstrably over budget on arithmetic alone (rf2-15047).

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: with the budget raised, a stall that persists past 360s is a real hang. Watch for a timeout under the new budget; if one appears, the namespace trail in the runner's diagnostics names the suspect. Separately, the ad-hoc set/restore of a PROCESS-GLOBAL across 73 files is a hazard on its own terms - a test that throws between set and restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace. A single shared fixture (use-fixtures :once/:each with restore in a finally) would retire the class.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a stall reproduces under the 360s budget and is diagnosed, or (b) no stall recurs over a sustained window and the ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore is consolidated into one shared fixture.
notes:
EVIDENCE PULLED FROM THE CI LOGS (2026-07-28), sharper than the filing text:

Run 30289345212 (PR #7183, worker/witness-ownership-1829), two attempts of the SAME unchanged commit:
  attempt 1 (job 90055797170): 'Timed out after 120000ms', 66 namespaces reached,
      last = re-frame.freehand.root-hydration-dom-cljs-test
  attempt 2 (job 90062056406): 'Timed out after 120000ms', 99 namespaces reached,
      last = re-frame.ssr.streaming-hydration-lifecycle-dom-cljs-test
  Both: no 'Ran ... assertions.' line at all, no failing assertion.

DECISIVE AGAINST A FIXED DEADLOCK: cljs.test runs namespaces alphabetically, and
attempt 2 ran PAST root-hydration (ns 66) all the way to ns 99. The namespace that
'stalled' attempt 1 therefore completed normally in attempt 2. There is no fixed
deadlock site.

THE 'BOTH STALLS WERE HYDRATION SUITES' COINCIDENCE IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: 13 of
the 99 reached namespaces (13%) are hydration/SSR by COUNT, but an expiring clock
does not sample namespaces uniformly - it samples them by DURATION, and the
hydration/SSR suites are the expensive ones (real hydrate + settles). Landing in one
is the expected outcome for a clock running out, not a signal.

CORROBORATION: PR #7181 timed out once and passed UNCHANGED on re-run. A hang does
not resolve itself; a run sitting on the boundary does.

MEASURED BUDGET (CI, not local): green main job 90042176242 - 'Serving ...' at
16:40:38 -> 'Ran 843 tests containing 5400 assertions' at 16:41:36 = 58s run phase.
CI and local are equivalent here, so the witness arithmetic is direct: ~+38s each,
three queued = ~213s against a 120s ceiling.

READ: this is the budget, not a hang. rf2-15047 raises it to 360s.

THE OBSERVABILITY GAP THAT KEEPS THIS OPEN: run-browser-tests.cjs buffers the browser
console and flushes it only on failure, so EVERY 'Testing <ns>' line in a timeout log
carries the same flush timestamp (verified: all 66 lines of attempt 1 stamped
17:35:28.09x). There is no per-namespace timing, so 'ns 99 was still running when the
clock expired' cannot be distinguished from 'ns 99 never returned'. A racy hang that
can strike in any suite is therefore not fully excluded by the above - only a fixed
deadlock is.

CHEAP FIX FOR THAT GAP (one line, deliberately NOT done in rf2-15047's PR to keep it a
lane tweak): stamp each diagnostics line with a monotonic offset at CAPTURE time rather
than at flush time. The next timeout then reports its own namespace-duration profile and
the verdict is unambiguous.
=== READ REVISED 2026-07-28 AFTER LOCAL MEASUREMENT: THERE IS SOMETHING REAL UNDERNEATH ===

I originally read this as pure budget. Local measurement says otherwise, and I am
recording the reversal rather than leaving the optimistic read standing.

MEASURED. The :browser-test bundle is 149 NAMESPACES (counted via
RF2_VERBOSE_TESTS=1, which flushes the diagnostics buffer on success too).
Five consecutive local runs of #7183's branch (worker/witness-ownership-1829,
plus only the timeout change), warm:

  iter=1 exit=0  68s  149 namespaces  851 tests / 5520 assertions / 0 fail
  iter=2 exit=0  52s  149 namespaces  851 tests / 5520 assertions / 0 fail
  iter=3 exit=0  51s  149 namespaces  851 tests / 5520 assertions / 0 fail
  iter=4 exit=0  65s  149 namespaces  851 tests / 5520 assertions / 0 fail
  iter=5 exit=0  57s  149 namespaces  851 tests / 5520 assertions / 0 fail

THE ANOMALY. Per-namespace rate, same bundle:

  CI green main (job 90042176242)  149 ns /  58s  = 0.39 s/ns   COMPLETES
  local #7183 x5                   149 ns / 51-68s= 0.34-0.46   COMPLETES 5/5
  CI #7183 attempt 1                66 ns / >120s = >1.82       4.7x SLOWER
  CI #7183 attempt 2                99 ns / >120s = >1.21       3.1x SLOWER

#7183 adds EIGHT tests. Eight tests do not make a bundle 3-5x slower. And the
slowdown is not confined to the new witnesses: attempt 1 was already 4.7x off
the pace by namespace 66, across a stretch of the alphabet #7183 does not touch.
Locally the same branch runs at exactly CI-green-main's rate, 5 times out of 5.

So the arithmetic story ('witnesses cost ~38s each, three of them exceed 120s')
is TRUE and is sufficient reason to raise the budget - but it does NOT explain
#7183's own CI failure. Something else is happening in CI only.

STILL NOT A DEADLOCK. Attempt 2 ran PAST attempt 1's stop point (ns 66) to ns 99,
so there is no fixed stall site, and both runs make broad progress rather than
stopping dead. This is SLOWNESS of an unexplained magnitude, not a deadlock -
which is why the budget raise (rf2-15047) proceeded rather than stopping for a
defect hunt.

BEST HYPOTHESIS, AND IT IS THE ONE ALREADY ON RECORD. A broad, uniform,
intermittent slowdown that begins partway through a run and affects everything
after it is the signature of a LEAKED PROCESS-GLOBAL, not of a hung test. If
IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT is left true by a test that throws between its ad-hoc
set and its restore, every subsequent React render in the run takes the act()
path with its extra flush/settle work. That predicts exactly what is seen:
everything after the leak point runs several times slower, the leak point varies
run to run (66 vs 99), it never fails an assertion, and it does not reproduce on
a faster/differently-timed local machine where the throwing race may not fire.
73 test files set/restore that global by hand with no shared fixture.

WHAT TO DO (this bead):
 1. Stamp each diagnostics line with a monotonic offset at CAPTURE time rather
    than at flush time in run-browser-tests.cjs. One line. It turns the next
    timeout log into a per-namespace duration profile, which names the leak
    point directly. Do this FIRST - it is cheap and it converts speculation
    into a measurement.
 2. Consolidate the 73 ad-hoc set/restore sites onto one shared fixture that
    restores in a finally. That retires the whole class whether or not it is
    the cause here.
 3. Re-check after the budget raise lands: with 360s the lane will go green
    while still degraded, so the symptom disappears from CI without the cause
    being fixed. That is the specific risk this bead exists to hold.

PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1: the budget raise legitimately masks this.
=== main IS ALREADY RED ON THIS LANE (2026-07-28) - and it sharpens the anomaly ===

Run 30291716420, sha 079905169 (post-splitter main), job 90063630119:
  'Timed out after 120000ms waiting for cljs.test summary'
  93 of 149 namespaces reached
  last = re-frame.ssr.phase-flip-hydration-dom-cljs-test
  no summary, no failing assertion

So the timeout is NOT specific to any witness PR. Plain main hits it.

THE SHARPEST VERSION OF THE ANOMALY. Two CI runs of main, one witness apart:
  main pre-splitter  (job 90042176242)  843 tests  58s   COMPLETES all 149 ns
  main post-splitter (job 90063630119)  855 tests  >120s RED at 93/149 ns
  main post-splitter + timeout raise
                     (job 90071495499)  855 tests  146s  COMPLETES
ONE 12-test witness moved the lane from 58s to 146s. At the ~38s/witness rate
measured locally that should have been ~96s. The observed CI cost is roughly
DOUBLE the local cost, and it varies 3-4x run to run on IDENTICAL code.

THREE TIMEOUTS NOW ON RECORD, all stopping in the contiguous ns-66..99 band:
  #7183 att.1  66 ns  re-frame.freehand.root-hydration-dom-cljs-test
  main         93 ns  re-frame.ssr.phase-flip-hydration-dom-cljs-test
  #7183 att.2  99 ns  re-frame.ssr.streaming-hydration-lifecycle-dom-cljs-test
Each stop point is PASSED by one of the others, so no fixed stall site - still
not a deadlock. And the 'always a hydration suite' pattern is explained by the
band itself: ns 66..99 IS the hydration/SSR block, so that is simply where
minute two lands. The pattern is a consequence of where the clock expires, not
independent evidence.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED, AND IS THE REASON THIS BEAD IS P1: the 2x cost inflation
per witness in CI vs local, and the 3-4x run-to-run variance on identical code.
That is consistent with the leaked-process-global hypothesis (a run that leaks
IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT early is slow for the rest of the bundle; a run that
leaks late, or not at all, is fast) and is not consistent with the lane simply
having grown.

rf2-15047 (PR #7184) raises the budget to 360s. main goes green again - WHILE STILL
DEGRADED. That is the masking this bead holds.
=== THE PROFILE IS IN, AND IT DISSOLVES THE ANOMALY (2026-07-28, PR for rf2-76lhy) ===

Capture-time stamping landed; the lane now profiles itself. Two green local runs
of the SAME bundle that timed out in CI job 90063630119 (855 tests / 5609
assertions, 148 namespaces):

  re-frame.freehand.bench.b10-two-clock-dom-cljs-test   35.9s / 43.3s  = 50-53% of the lane
  the 7 re-frame.freehand.bench.* namespaces           52.0s / 60.0s  = 73% of the lane
  median namespace                                     0.040s
  lane total                                           71.5s / 81.7s

THE DENOMINATOR WAS WRONG. This bead computed per-namespace rates (s/ns) and
derived '3.1-4.7x slower in CI' plus '3-4x run-to-run variance on identical
code'. Namespace count is not a clock for this lane: 73% of its wall clock is 7
of its 148 namespaces, and the remaining 141 are a dense tail averaging 40ms.

Placed on the measured wall clock, the three recorded CI stop points are:

  ns 66  (45% of namespaces)  reached locally at +67.9s = 92% of the lane
  ns 93  (63% of namespaces)  reached locally at +69.0s = 94% of the lane
  ns 99  (67% of namespaces)  reached locally at +71.0s = 97% of the lane

All three died in the LAST 8% of the lane, within 5 points of each other. The
'3-4x run-to-run variance' was the namespace denominator, not the runs: on wall
clock the three CI attempts made near-identical progress before the clock cut
them. And the sharpest form of the anomaly softens the same way - CI spent 120s
reaching a point this box reaches at ~68s, i.e. about 1.7x, uniform, not 4.7x.
Job 90071495499 completing the same bundle in 146s against a 71.5-83.8s local
total is the same ~1.7-2.0x factor. That is an ordinary CI-vs-dev-box factor.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HYPOTHESIS. 82s local x ~1.75 = ~143s against a 120s ceiling
predicts exactly what was observed: three runs dying a few seconds short, each
in the dense tail. A leaked IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT is not needed to explain
any of it. The 73-file ad-hoc set/restore remains a hazard on its own terms and
is worth retiring, but this bead's evidence no longer points at it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: re-measure CI. The CI figures above are this bead's own
recorded numbers re-derived against a correct denominator, on one dev box. The
profile now ships, so the next CI timeout answers this directly with its own
per-namespace stamps rather than by inference.

FILED FROM THIS: rf2-mf4uy (b10-two-clock is half the correctness gate; benches
belong in the existing browser-test-freehand-bench build) and rf2-dczpv (a
SECOND undocumented ceiling - Playwright's default 30s page.goto 'load' timeout,
which fired once locally during this measurement and which the 360s budget raise
does not touch).
close_reason: PR #7190. Capture-time stamping shipped — the deliverable this bead named as step 1. The profile it produced is recorded as a note above: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 of 148 namespaces, and the three CI stop points sit at 92/94/97% of the lane, which dissolves the '3-4x variance' (it was the namespace denominator) and reduces the CI/local gap to a uniform ~1.7x. Steps 2 and 3 of this bead are NOT done and are deliberately not carried here: the 73-file IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT fixture consolidation is its own work in a fenced tree, and 'recheck after the budget raise' is now answered by the shipped profile rather than by holding a bead open. Follow-ups filed: rf2-mf4uy, rf2-dczpv.

title: ci: raise the browser-lane timeout budget for the control witnesses
description: The :browser-test lane's cljs.test summary wait was 120s (implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs). Measured on the same bundle: pre-witness main = 843 tests / 58s; +virtual-collection witness (#7180) = 854 / 95s; +splitter witness (#7181, merged) = 855 / 99s. Each control witness costs ~35-40s for ~5-12 tests (mounted rows, real-time settles, 2-4s poll budgets). Three more witnesses queued (#7180, #7182, #7183) = ~+120s, which exceeds 120s on arithmetic. Raise the default to 360000.
acceptance_criteria: Default raised in the runner (not per-workflow); full browser bundle runs to completion on the #7183 branch; PR open.
close_reason:
PR #7218. VERIFIED NO CHANGE NEEDED -- 360s stands, and the baseline #7193's author asked for is now recorded in the file.

MEASURED 2026-07-28, two consecutive local runs of the built :browser-test bundle: 841 tests / 5459 assertions / 0 failures, 25.9s and 25.2s wall for serve+launch+navigate+suite+teardown, of which the summary wait proper -- the only thing TIMEOUT_MS bounds -- is ~22.5s. The 41.5s shadow-cljs compile is NOT on this clock. Confirms rf2-mf4uy's 73s -> 22.5s.

So 360s is ~16x the local green run, ~9.5x at the measured ~1.7x CI factor, against the ~3.6x rule that produced it; by that rule alone it wants ~140-180s. NOT LOWERED, for two reasons now recorded in the source:

(1) The growth this budget absorbs is WALL-CLOCK, not compute. Each control witness costs ~35-40s of mounted rows driven through real-time settles with 2-4s poll budgets -- setTimeout, which neither a faster runner nor another bundle split can shrink. 22.5s is a one-off structural change (the bench move), not a trend, and the witness corpus is still landing steadily. Three more witnesses puts the lane near ~135s, where a 180s budget has ~1.3x headroom and needs re-raising within weeks.

(2) The failure modes are asymmetric. Over-large costs only a slower failure on a genuine hang -- still 6 min, far inside timeout-minutes: 45, and still through THIS runner with the console trail and the rf2-76lhy per-namespace profile. Under-sized costs a FALSE RED on a loaded runner: precisely the failure this bead was filed to stop.

The bead's own acceptance criteria (default raised in the runner, bundle runs to completion, PR open) were already met by PR #7184; this closes the calibration follow-up. Comment-only change; DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS unchanged at 360000. Revisit when the lane's green run passes ~100s.

Separately, the SSR lane's RF2_MIN_TESTS floor drift is fixed in the same PR: 425 -> 510 against an observed 589, now that ssr-end-to-end-test came off the roster (rf2-lwtlk).

title: Two virtual tables in the tree: reconcile pilot-virtual-table with the shipped re-frame.freehand.collection
description:
PROBLEM
rf2-drpa3.182.11 (PR #7180) shipped `re-frame.freehand.collection` — a first-party fixed-size virtual collection under implementation/freehand/src, enrolled as FH-CTRL-019. The corpus ALREADY contained `re-frame.freehand.pilot-virtual-table` (1622 lines across pilot_virtual_table.cljc, _cljs_test.cljc, _compiled.cljc, _dom_cljs_test.cljs, from rf2-eq2vx / rf2-g5xxv / rf2-drpa3.176). The witness worker did not find it before building, and says so.

They are NOT the same question. The pilot is deliberately CONSUMER code proving the public surface can express a virtual table with no substrate machinery; it cites no FH id and is in neither the conformance index nor the roster. The shipped control is DC-04's answer: the framework ships one, with an accepted law. So this is a pilot and its promotion — but it landed as two IMPLEMENTATIONS, which is one too many.

OVERLAP (the pilot already proves all of these)
pure window arithmetic; windowing commits only visible rows; the window slides with the offset; a surviving row keeps its key across a scroll; caller row content via v/render-fn + v/slot; interpreted/compiled promotion parity; the scroll position as ordinary application state; a closed part roster; 10,000 rows -> a fixed number of DOM rows; a real browser scroll moving the window.

WHAT ONLY THE SHIPPED CONTROL HAS
an accepted conformance row + fixture + roster record; :residue :none across repeated scroll cycles, read after teardown over the connected-occurrence index and the document; focus continuity (viewport holds focus, aria-activedescendant, the active row unmounting without taking focus); keyboard reveal via reveal-offset; aria-posinset/aria-setsize honesty; and it lives in src/ rather than test/.

WHAT ONLY THE PILOT HAS
a reorder carrying the row element with its record; restore-scroll, a :layout behavior that writes a persisted offset back onto a LIVE viewport before paint — which also buys time-travel of a mounted viewport, not merely of the window value; aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex grid semantics; and an editing-grid application with 100 controlled cells.

That last one matters most: the shipped control has NO seam for moving a live viewport and pushes the direction to an application effect. That is a strictly weaker answer than the pilot's, and the docstring now says so.

THE RULING NEEDED
(a) Keep the shipped control and retire the pilot's component half (keeping its applications as callers of the shipped control), porting restore-scroll across if the :layout seam is wanted in the kit; or
(b) keep the pilot as the implementation, move it to src/, and re-point FH-CTRL-019 at it, discarding the duplicate; or
(c) keep both with stated, non-overlapping roles — worst option, and it needs a reason.

Until this is settled the shipped control's docstring names the pilot, names this bead, states the three differences, and says to prefer the shipped one for new code. Nothing is deleted.

SEE ALSO: rf2-cfhuv (the same namespace is absent from the API-manifest allow-list).
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — Option (a), adopted WITH both Codex boundary corrections. `re-frame.freehand.collection` (PR #7180's line) is the sole survivor; the pilot's component half is retired; the pilot's applications live on as callers of the survivor. One engine with several honest uses — not option (c)'s two engines. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-86i64.two-virtual-tables.md) is deleted with this record; both analyses are preserved below.

WHY THE COLLECTION LINE SURVIVES (merits, from both analyses)
It carries the product-grade half: the accepted conformance row + fixture + roster record, :residue :none proven across repeated near-total window turnover with reads after teardown, focus continuity, keyboard reveal via reveal-offset, aria-posinset/setsize honesty, and it lives in src/. Its design is props-and-intents rather than a component-owned app-db protocol; it takes a stable vector of identities so each visible row owns its narrow record read; and its `window` handles empty, clamped and unaligned ranges more cleanly than the pilot arithmetic — the pilot double-counts an extra "partially visible" row at an exactly aligned viewport boundary. Option (b) (pilot as survivor) rejected: every proof that makes the shipped control DC-04's answer would need rebuilding onto the weaker arithmetic outside src/ — strictly more work for the same end state. Option (c) (keep both) rejected: two implementations of one control is standing divergence and "which one do I use?" friction, exactly what the posture forbids.

CODEX CORRECTION (i) ADOPTED — SEMANTIC-NEUTRAL ENGINE
Not scope creep: the pilot's own editing-grid application is an EXISTING consumer that cannot honestly be a listbox — role "grid", aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex, 100 controlled cells containing inputs (pilot_virtual_table.cljc:306-327, verified in-tree 2026-07-28). W3C's listbox pattern explicitly sends collections of interactive elements to the grid pattern, whose cell/focus/keyboard contract is materially different. A listbox-hard-coded virtual-list cannot host the pilot's applications-as-callers without either a second engine (option (c) by the back door) or dishonest semantics. Mature virtualizers expose exactly this seam (TanStack Virtual: ranges/keys/scrolling independent of markup; react-window: List and Grid as distinct widgets over one mechanics class). Virtualization mechanics and widget semantics are different layers; the survivor splits along that line.

SURVIVOR SHAPE
- Engine (working name virtual-collection; final public naming is rf2-cfhuv's surface ruling): semantic-neutral, fixed-size only. Owns the viewport, full-height canvas, keyed positioned row shells, the window arithmetic, and the guarded :layout scroll reconciliation. The row slot receives key, absolute index, and total, so the caller or a thin wrapper supplies honest option/row/gridcell semantics.
- virtual-list: a thin LISTBOX WRAPPER over the engine — listbox/option roles, selection, aria-activedescendant, aria-posinset/setsize, keyboard reveal. It must contain NO second range or scroll engine.
- NO shipped grid wrapper. The pilot's editing-grid application supplies its own grid semantics through the slot; a first-party grid control is a separate future decision if evidence ever demands one.
- Do NOT add: variable row heights, a columns model, sorting, a grid framework, or a polymorphic :semantics option pretending to implement whole ARIA interaction patterns. Adopt only what the pilot's evidence already demands.

CODEX CORRECTION (ii) ADOPTED — CONTROLLED :scroll-offset
:scroll-offset is required, CONTROLLED, and ALWAYS reconciled onto the live viewport via the pilot's guarded :layout behavior (write only when the DOM disagrees, before paint — the substrate's one sanctioned state-config-to-host reconciliation seam). The pilot's opt-in :restore-scroll? prop is RETIRED: one prop must not carry two meanings, and the un-reconciled mode is a known bug — a required offset that chooses a render window but leaves a newly mounted viewport at 0 is the exact blank/inconsistent state the pilot's negative control proves (pilot_virtual_table_dom_cljs_test.cljs:601-635). User scroll stays cheap: behavior update runs only when config moves, and the guarded write is a no-op when the DOM already agrees. This also buys state-only time-travel of a MOUNTED viewport, not merely of the window value.

ACTIVE-DESCENDANT CORRECTION (Codex, adopted)
The branch's focus test deliberately keeps aria-activedescendant="inbox-row-3" after that element unmounts. WAI-ARIA 1.2 defines a non-matching IDREF as an author error and says the active descendant should be visible or scrolled into view. Keeping DOM focus on the stable viewport is correct; preserving a dangling IDREF is not. Fix: omit the attribute while the active item is outside the rendered range (or reveal it before naming it). Replace the test that blesses the dangling reference; do not carry the defect into the conformance law.

EVIDENCE-UNION OBLIGATION
The consolidation is the collection implementation plus the UNION of the two evidence portfolios — not preservation of both implementations.
Branch evidence retained as-is: whole-vertical compiled parity; bounded fan-out; keyboard reveal; repeated near-total window turnover followed by exact :residue :none reads; aria-posinset/setsize honesty; focus continuity (amended per the active-descendant correction); window arithmetic over empty/clamped/unaligned ranges.
Pilot evidence that MUST be migrated as tests against the survivor BEFORE any deletion:
 1. Surviving-row DOM NODE identity across a real browser scroll (actual element reuse, not merely keyed identity).
 2. Reorder carrying the row ELEMENT with its record (DOM identity across a reorder).
 3. Non-zero initial offset restored on first mount, plus a state-only/time-travel offset move of a MOUNTED viewport — the restoration law, now stated positively (the pilot's negative control dies with the un-reconciled mode it existed to indict).
 4. The 100-controlled-cell editing grid driven through the engine, grid semantics supplied by the application.

RETIREMENT PLAN — the pilot's four files (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_virtual_table{,_compiled}.cljc, pilot_virtual_table_cljs_test.cljc, pilot_virtual_table_dom_cljs_test.cljs), ordered; delete only after the migrated tests pass through the survivor:
 1. Extract the engine from virtual-list (mechanics down, listbox semantics stay in the wrapper); make :scroll-offset controlled via the ported :layout behavior; correct the active-descendant fixture and test.
 2. Re-enrol under the correct control id (below); regenerate fixture, conformance-index row, roster record.
 3. Rewrite the pilot's applications (ledger, reorder, editing grid, restore scenarios) as callers of the engine/wrapper; migrate the four discriminating browser tests above.
 4. Only then delete the pilot's component half: data-table, register!, tables-root, the duplicate window arithmetic, canvas/positioning/scroll plumbing, restore-scroll (now living in the survivor), the compiled twin's duplicate table, and pilot tests that duplicate survivor coverage. The pilot files remain as consumer-proof applications of the public surface; the second implementation does not.

FH-CTRL / CONFORMANCE CONSEQUENCES (verified against the tree, 2026-07-28)
- PR #7180 is OPEN as of this writing (gh: state OPEN, branch worker/witness-virtual-18211, checks green), NOT merged. Meanwhile main has allocated FH-CTRL-019 to the splitter and FH-CTRL-020 to the composed control, so the branch's FH-CTRL-019 enrolment now COLLIDES with main. The collection re-enrols under the next free id — FH-CTRL-021 as of this writing (re-verify at implementation time): rename the branch's fixtures/fh-ctrl-019.edn accordingly; index row and roster record follow.
- Merge-state posture: under the standing green-merge rule these corrections are REPAIR OBLIGATIONS, not a merge gate — with one exception: the id collision is a conflict with main and must be resolved at rebase/merge time regardless, since two FH-CTRL-019 rows cannot coexist. If the PR merges first, Package A lands as a repair PR on main; if not, it lands on the branch.
- ONE conformance row (the listbox control's). Amend its law for the controlled-restoration guarantee and the corrected active-descendant behavior. The engine is proven through the wrapper plus the migrated grid/restoration tests — no separate conformance row for the engine; that would be gold-plating.

OWNERSHIP — this bead SPLITS into two sequenced packages:
- Package A (rf2-86i64 is the implementation owner): survivor repair — engine extraction + thin listbox wrapper, controlled :scroll-offset via the :layout seam, active-descendant fix, id re-enrolment + fixture/index/roster regeneration.
- Package B (mayor to file as a follow-up bead, blocked on Package A): pilot retirement — rewrite the applications as callers, migrate the four discriminating tests, then delete per the plan above.
- Rationale: each package is a full worker's worth; bundling has a documented timeout failure mode; B cannot start before A's surface exists.

CROSS-REFERENCES
- rf2-cfhuv (API-manifest enrolment): must follow the surface shape ruled here — engine + wrapper split with controlled :scroll-offset and no :restore-scroll?, superseding the branch's original five-name listbox-only roster — and should land after Package A settles the shape. Dependency noted on rf2-cfhuv.
- Origin: rf2-drpa3.182.11 (witness), rf2-eq2vx / rf2-g5xxv / rf2-drpa3.176 (pilot programme).
PACKAGE A COMPLETE — PR #7180 (branch worker/witness-virtual-18211), rebased onto main, green, MERGEABLE.

Landed, in four commits so the rename reads separately from the design change:
1. 5de0e040fb — re-enrolled FH-CTRL-019 -> FH-CTRL-021 (main is dense through 020: splitter took 019, composed control took 020). Branch REBUILT on current main rather than replayed, because a faithful rebase would have clobbered main's fh-ctrl-019.edn. Five namespaces restored byte-identically (blob SHAs equal), fixture copied to fh-ctrl-021.edn (blob 58caabda both sides), index row re-inserted after main's 020. Pure-rename proof vs pre-rebase tip 47de09bfdd: 202 changed lines, ZERO lacking the ordinal.
2. b3065f51d3 — correction (i), the semantic-neutral engine. virtual-collection (engine: viewport, canvas, keyed positioned presentational shells, window arithmetic, no role, row slot gets key/absolute-index/total) + virtual-list (thin listbox wrapper, no second window arithmetic, no second scroll host). Engine takes :attrs as an explicit map — forced by the grammar: a render-slot callback is legal only as a literal call-site prop value, so a wrapper cannot merge its props AND pass :row.
3. 2de3a23a32 — correction (ii), controlled :scroll-offset via the ported guarded :layout behavior (reconcile-scroll). No opt-out; :restore-scroll? NOT ported. The application's :inbox/scroll-to effect is DELETED, so no host-writing effect remains anywhere in the suite.
4. 8b1ec8b7ab — the active-descendant correction. aria-activedescendant published exactly while the row it names is rendered; the test that blessed the dangling IDREF is replaced, not relaxed. Range decided from the SAME pure window the engine renders from.
   (+ 37b57c993d — residue read extended to cover both layers the split now renders.)

Evidence preserved and extended: :residue :none still earned (3 cycles x 8 stops, 318 counted row renders, now THREE exact-zero books because the split adds a node per row); 44 item reads for 10,000 items; empty :subscriptions roster on all THREE control manifests; whole vertical still promotes and trees still compared whole at every fixture offset. The manifest now makes the split machine-checked: engine events [:on-scroll :spread-safe], listbox [] (writes no element), row [:on-click].

Gates, all exit 0: freehand JVM 1288/8843; roster 25/362; check_freehand_conformance_index.py; npm run test:browser 846/5462; npm run test:browser-prod-elision 120/527 + 'ui mounted production elision: PASS'.

Mutation re-proved naming FH-CTRL-021 (019-era evidence NOT carried forward): (A) engine given :role listbox -> 2 structural failures; (B) dangling IDREF restored -> 1 structural failure; (C) reconcile-scroll-offset! made a no-op -> 3 browser failures including the keyboard reveal, which now depends on the controlled offset because its effect is gone. All restored to exit 0.

API-manifest gap (rf2-cfhuv) is LARGER, not smaller: the public surface goes from five names to seven, adding virtual-collection and reconcile-scroll. Nothing reds today — the namespace is still not scanned. rf2-cfhuv's roster must be written against the ruled shape (engine + wrapper, controlled :scroll-offset, no :restore-scroll?), superseding the branch's original five-name listbox-only roster.

Package B is rf2-pa57v; the surface it needs is noted there.
