title: studio: heap UNDER UPDATE — the one memory question Freehand still has an argument in
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-9oj7v (PR #7146), and the only surviving memory line for Freehand.

The cross-substrate STANDING-heap row went decisively against Freehand: 5.93x Reagent per sub-free boundary, 4.19x per reactive one, disjoint ranges, two independent instruments agreeing to 1%. That measurement mounts K roots and holds them still. It says nothing about what a WRITE costs in bytes.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONSOLATION-PRIZE BEAD. Fine-grained reactivity's whole trade is meant to be that a write touches only what changed. Reagent's broad write re-renders 300 components through its own reaction graph; Freehand's notifies 300 ViewCells. If Freehand allocates materially LESS per write than Reagent, that is a real property of the design and it is the one memory claim still available — standing heap is a per-boundary constant an app pays once, whereas allocation per write is paid at every interaction and drives GC pauses. The compiled-tier report's §1a explicitly names transient garbage as the thing retention cannot see and the likeliest explanation for its 1.216 clock term not showing on retained bytes.

INSTRUMENT WARNING, and it is sharper here than for the standing row. The retention instrument in b7_heap.cljs CANNOT answer this: what a write allocates and drops is by construction invisible to it. And the obvious tool is the exact one that is broken — V8's CDP SAMPLING heap profiler drops the samples of collected objects, which is what makes it useless for a mount/unmount loop and what produced the earlier wrong table. Measuring allocation-per-write therefore needs a DIFFERENT instrument from either, and choosing it is most of the work. Candidates worth pricing before committing: HeapProfiler.startSampling/stopSampling with a small sampling interval read as a RATE over many writes (the sampler's failure mode is dropped collected samples, which is fatal for a one-shot delta but may be tolerable when the quantity of interest is a steady-state allocation rate); Runtime.getHeapUsage sampled at high frequency across a long write loop to observe sawtooth amplitude x frequency; or Chrome's allocation-timeline. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN MUST CARRY AN IN-SITU POSITIVE CONTROL OF PREDICTED SIZE, as b7_run.cjs does — a known allocation rate driven beside the arms.

FIXTURE: b6's update grid already exists in both dialects (300 cells, Freehand v/sub against Reagent r/cursor) and both broad and narrow writes are already driven by b6-rows/timed-write! with DOM read-back. Reuse it; do not build a third grid.

Note the standing asymmetry that §2a of freehand-vs-reagent.md bounds rather than removes: the Freehand arm reads app-db through a subscription graph, the Reagent arm a bare ratom. Split the write leg from the render leg as that report does, or the number will be a re-frame result wearing a Freehand label.
close_reason:
Measured and reported. Freehand LOSES on transient allocation too — the memory hypothesis is falsified on both axes.

Broad write 4,572,680 B vs Reagent 269,229 (17.0x); narrow 478,787 vs 23,648 (20.2x); all ranges disjoint. But the narrow 20.2x is 95.5% re-frame's write leg (457,181 B re-evaluating 300 subs to find 299 unchanged — filed rf2-jr76s), and stripping it leaves Freehand's view substrate at 21,376 B against Reagent's 19,307 — 1.107x, disjoint, both ~7x better than the top-down React floor. Closest to parity anything in this studio has reached, still a loss.

The broad view-leg 13.5x is published as an UPPER BOUND not a substrate result: rf2-40kdm measured the read path as 95.3-97.4% shared re-frame cost and this Reagent arm pays none of it. rf2-mapni files the arm that would close it.

Instrument: collection-free window over V8's used-heap counter. Decisive control is kept-vs-dropped at 1.0001 (125,139 vs 125,121 B/copy allocated, 99,417 vs 11 B retained) — the counter does not care whether an object survives. Sampling profiler negative control reports 13% of allocation. Positive control's 8 B/double PREDICTION was wrong (retention says 16.002); reported as such. Bookkeeping identity exact 120/120; 0 unverified of 2,400 writes per row.

PR #7152. Report: docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-allocation.md

title: bench: B6's mount arm creates a frame per sample INSIDE the timed window — does the mount row overstate?
description:
Found while reconciling the W1-interpreted mount discrepancy on PR #7139.

B6's Freehand mount arm (b6_rows.cljs, freehand-mount-arm) calls v/mount with a :disambiguator and NO :frame:

    (v/mount [view props] container {:disambiguator (keyword "b6" ...)})

With no :frame in opts, v/mount runs plan-for / preflight! and creates a FRESH FRAME — and it does so inside the flushSync that b6-harness/mount-arm! is timing. So every B6 mount sample bills per-sample frame construction to the substrate, and the floor arm (a bare createRoot) never pays it.

The rf2-lnecd / rf2-xu6rx studio probe did NOT do this: it mounted every arm into ONE pre-existing shared frame (:frame fid). That is one of four named differences between the two harnesses, and it is the one that would bias in the observed direction (B6's ratio higher).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: the mount row is on the release gate too. Interpreted W1 mount is 2.987-3.075x floor against Reagent's 1.518-1.554, and if a measurable slice of that is per-sample frame creation rather than substrate cost, the published mount row overstates how far interpreted mount has to travel.

CHEAP TO SETTLE: mount the Freehand arms with an explicit pre-created :frame and re-run measure-mount!. If the delta is material, either hoist frame creation out of the timed window or state the inclusion explicitly in the report's method.

Do NOT change the published numbers without re-running the whole row — the ratio is only meaningful against a floor measured in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: A measured delta between B6's W1 interpreted mount with a per-sample frame and with a shared pre-created frame, and either a harness fix or an explicit statement in freehand-vs-reagent.md's method.
close_reason:
PR #7146. NULL RESULT: the mount row does NOT overstate, and the premise does not hold.

v/mount with NO :frame creates NO frame. root.cljs: plan-for answers nil when opts carries no :frame; preflight! opens (when (some? plan) ...); root-element wraps in the frame provider only (if (some? frame-id) ...). A frameless mount runs no plan, creates no frame and binds none - it does LESS than a mount that names one, not more.

Measured anyway, four arms differing only in the :frame opt, b6-harness unchanged, 6 rounds x (5 warmup + 20 samples), ratio to the in-run floor:
  W1  floor 1.000 | fh-no-frame 3.109 [2.889-3.588] | fh-shared-frame 3.229 [3.000-3.706] | fh-frame-per-sample 3.347 [3.111-4.059] | reagent 1.545 [1.471-1.647]
  W2  floor 1.000 | fh-no-frame 8.667 [7.00-10.00]  | fh-shared-frame 9.611 [7.67-11.00]  | fh-frame-per-sample 9.917 [7.00-11.50]  | reagent 2.528 [1.67-3.00]

Ranges overlap, so on ranges alone the three Freehand arms are indistinguishable. But the arms interleave WITHIN a round, so the paired comparison is available and is decisive:
  shared frame / published arm      W1 x1.038 higher in 6 of 6 rounds | W2 x1.109 in 6 of 6
  frame-per-sample / published arm  W1 x1.074 in 6 of 6              | W2 x1.138 in 5 of 6

The published arm is the CHEAPEST of the three shapes. Correcting to the studio fixture's shared frame moves W1 UP 3.8% and W2 UP 10.9%. Even the feared counterfactual would have been worth 7.4% on W1 against a 2x gap. NO PUBLISHED FIGURE CHANGES; acceptance criterion met by explicit statement in freehand-vs-reagent.md's method plus §3 of the new memory report.

BONUS: the row REPRODUCES on a different day against current main (incl PR #7133's extra React commit). Reagent W1 1.545 [1.471-1.647] vs published 1.554 [1.520-1.583]; FH interpreted W1 3.109 [2.889-3.588] vs published 2.987 [2.840-3.167]. That reproducibility had never been shown.

Source: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_mount_frame.cljs.

title: freehand: a retained-set fast path for cell/commit! — the largest single lever on bulk re-render
description:
Profiled on rf2-dq20a's follow-on (PR #7139, docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md).

cell/commit! is 29.43% of a broad-update window — 1.23 ms of 4.05 ms per write, against Reagent's ENTIRE layout-effect commit phase at 1.4 us. It is the single largest term in the ~10x deficit and it is O(DEPENDENCIES), not O(boundaries): an ablation that collapsed 300 boundaries into 1 (same DOM, same 300 reads) only moved it 1.23 -> 0.86 ms.

On a broad write EVERY site is RETAINED — same query, same target, same handle — and commit! still, per dependency: allocates two maps in stage! to say so; calls obs/read to re-deref the node; allocates a 300-element :observations vector of five-key maps; and republishes the whole dep map in one swap!.

THE OBSTACLE IS NOT CACHING. The commit-side re-read is the invariant-5 TEAR CHECK — it compares node-key, version and frame/registry epoch between the render that produced the element and the commit about to publish it. So a fast path is a change to WHEN the invariant is checked, not an optimisation. It needs a spec conversation against spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §The Freehand atomic shell before any code.

Estimated ceiling if fully realised: ~1.2 ms of a ~3.65 ms deficit (~33%). Would NOT on its own bring interpreted Freehand under Reagent — see the sibling beads.

## Context
cell.cljc is held by PR #7133 as of 2026-07-27 — sequence after it merges.
acceptance_criteria: A design decision recorded on whether the invariant-5 tear check can be satisfied without re-reading every retained dependency at commit; if yes, an implementation with before/after broad-update ranges from b6_profile_run.cjs.
notes:
PR OPEN: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7143 (worker/commit-fastpath-wxrrp, 2 files, +270/-73).

VERDICT. commit! is ~25% cheaper on a fully-retained 300-dependency broad update — 371.5-411.7 us BEFORE vs 287.5-333.7 us AFTER, 16 interleaved rounds each, DISJOINT, production-gated (RE_FRAME_DEBUG=false). B6's broad-update row CANNOT resolve it and is reported as indistinguishable: freehand/reagent per round BEFORE [9.20-11.17] mean 9.91 vs AFTER [8.29-11.17] mean 9.66, 12 rounds each, overlapping. commit! is 29% of the window and B6's round noise is +-10-15%, so a quarter off the term is ~7% of the window — under the instrument. The two instruments agree about why the row did not move.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE, and that is the most useful finding. 'The staged map could be republished by identity instead of rebuilt' cannot be done: a retained record carries the render's :value and :evidence, and on a broad write BOTH have moved — that is what a broad write is. Republishing prior by identity would feed last render's values into the next render's stabilization in record-read!. There is no identity republish available on this row at any price. What is available is the bookkeeping BETWEEN the reads: stage! now reports its own acquisitions (fresh-handles + :retained? deleted) and stages through a transient; commit-readings reads, tear-checks and builds the observations in ONE pass instead of three walks plus a re-lookup each; superseded-handles answers the fully-retained set in two counts; :dep-order publishes the render order instead of copying it.

INVARIANT 5 UNTOUCHED, and now tested for the first time — the repo had NO invariant-5 coverage before this branch. Two rows: one moves each of :node-key/:version/:frame-epoch/:registry-epoch ALONE over a mocked port with the kept-check held open (so the site is RETAINED), each paired with an unmoved control; one moves a real node in the real render->commit gap over the real port and sub-cache. Both falsified against two mutants — (a) the comparison dropped, (b) correction skipped when staging acquired nothing, i.e. the exact fast path this bead hypothesised. Each mutant: exit 1, 5 failures, all 5 the new assertions, nothing else in 8225 assertions moved.

INSTRUMENT FAULT CAUGHT: the first JVM microbench ran with interop/debug-enabled? TRUE (the JVM default), so it was timing the dev evidence plane including commit-facts' 300-element mapv select-keys, which Closure DCEs out of the bundle B6 measures — ~70% of the reading (1000 us with, 300 us without). Those numbers were discarded and everything quoted is production-gated. Positive control: zero-dependency commit 1.3-2.5 us vs 300-dep 300-400 us. Every measured commit verified by reading the written value back out of the published bundle's first and last observation: 0 unverified across every round of every run; 0 unverified writes in all four B6 runs.

GATES all exit 0: freehand JVM (1220/8225), npm test:cljs (11796/58722), BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 test:browser (833/5313), b6_prod_run.cjs x4. Full-spine + mkdocs deferred to CI.

NOT COVERED: the microbench is JVM and JIT-warmed (absolutes do not transfer to the browser; only the ratio, and only about commit!); one boundary holding 300 deps, not 300 boundaries holding one; no memory measurement; the browser row remains a null result.

rf2-21pck IS WARRANTED and its cheapest first move is on the RENDER leg: record-read! rebuilds the candidate's {:order :by-site} wrapper TWICE per reactive read (update :order conj, then assoc-in [:by-site ...]), so 300 reads allocate 600 wrapper maps nobody reads, on a leg #7139 profiled at 0.77 ms. Bounded, no invariant attached.

Raw per-round data: ai/findings/2026-07-27.commit-fastpath-wxrrp-raw.md (local-only, gitignored).
close_reason: PR #7143 open. commit! ~25% cheaper on a fully-retained 300-dependency broad update (371.5-411.7 us -> 287.5-333.7 us, 16 interleaved rounds each, disjoint, production-gated); B6's broad-update row cannot resolve it and is reported as indistinguishable (fh/reagent BEFORE [9.20-11.17] vs AFTER [8.29-11.17], 12 rounds each). Invariant 5 untouched and now covered for the first time, falsified against two mutants including the exact fast path this bead hypothesised. The bead's premise — republish the retained staged map by identity — is FALSE: :value and :evidence move on every broad write, so an identity republish would feed stale values into the next render's stabilization. Design decision recorded: the tear check cannot be satisfied without re-reading every retained dependency at commit; what can go is the bookkeeping between the reads.

title: [test] Flip b6_update_dom_cljs_test's flushSync non-vacuity row — Freehand now commits inside the flush
description:
PR #7133 (rf2-w2m25) fixed the defect that `a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync` PINS as expected behaviour. That test is in the Freehand-vs-Reagent bench worker's branch (worker/bench-vs-reagent), NOT on main, so #7133 could not flip it — file ownership fence — and it will start failing the moment both land.

The test says so itself: 'If this test ever starts failing, Freehand has gained a synchronous commit and the update row should be re-taken without the microtask yield.' It has.

Three things to do in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_update_dom_cljs_test.cljs (+ b6_rows.cljs):

  1. FLIP AND RENAME the non-vacuity row — never delete it, never loosen it to accept both outcomes. It now asserts the opposite: `(react-dom/flushSync (fn [] ((:write! arm) 0 4242)))` leaves the DOM reading 4242 on the very next line. Something like `a-freehand-write-commits-inside-flushsync`.
  2. CORRECT the namespace docstring's four-way table. The 'flushSync(write) -> no' row is now 'yes', and the paragraph that derives the measurement window's shape from it no longer holds.
  3. RE-TAKE the update row without the microtask yield if the numbers move. The window was shaped as 'write, yield one microtask, force the substrate's own synchronous drain, stop the clock' precisely BECAUSE the slowest arm needed the yield. Freehand no longer does — `flushSync(write)` is now a complete window for it — so the row can be timed the same way the mount row is, and the floor/Reagent arms stop paying a microtask they never needed.

PERF NOTE for whoever re-takes it: the fix arms one extra React commit per render batch — a two-fiber detached root rendering nil, whose layout effect closes the window. Outside flushSync the microtask closer still gets there first, so the sentinel's commit lands AFTER the measured window and does no work; but it is real wall-clock and the B6 numbers are the place it would show. If it is measurable, say so on rf2-w2m25 rather than absorbing it silently.

Sequence AFTER whichever of #7133 / the bench PR merges second.
notes:
=== MAYOR MERGE-ORDER RULING (2026-07-27). DO NOT MERGE #7131 AND #7133 INDEPENDENTLY. ===

This is the mutually-invalidating pair the method warns about: a test pinning today's broken behaviour, and the fix for it. Each is GREEN ALONE. Whichever merges second turns MAIN RED.

  PR #7131 (worker/bench-vs-reagent) ADDS implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_update_dom_cljs_test.cljs, containing 'a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync' - which asserts the DEFECT as correct behaviour. Verified present in that PR's file list.
  PR #7133 (worker/flushsync-w2m25) FIXES that defect (rf2-w2m25), so the pin becomes false the moment it lands.

THE ORDER, and it is not optional:
  1. Merge #7131 FIRST. It is the Freehand-vs-Reagent measurement and its pin is accurate against current main.
  2. Then #7133 REBASES on main and, IN THE SAME PR, FLIPS AND RENAMES that test - never deletes it, never loosens it to accept both outcomes. Per the method: the only coverage of this case must survive the flip. Its four-way docstring table needs correcting too, and the update row can be re-taken without the microtask yield.
  3. Then merge #7133.

WHY NOT THE OTHER ORDER: merging #7133 first would red #7131's own CI, forcing the bench worker to re-run a 6-round measurement suite for a reason unrelated to its work.

WHY THE FLIP BELONGS IN #7133 AND NOT A THIRD PR: the flip is only correct once the fix exists; a separate PR would be red on main until #7133 landed.

RESIDUAL RISK TO CARRY INTO THE RE-TAKE: #7133 adds one extra React commit per render batch (a two-fiber detached root rendering nil). Outside flushSync it lands AFTER the measured window and does no work, but it is real wall-clock, and B6's update row is exactly where it would show. Whoever re-takes those numbers must REPORT that cost rather than absorbing it silently.

Rebased worker/flushsync-w2m25 onto origin/main 1bb9b6157f (clean, no conflicts) after PR #7131 merged the B6 bench. a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync FLIPPED AND RENAMED to a-freehand-write-commits-inside-flushsync — not deleted, not loosened; it now asserts both legs (the flush window as the new guarantee, and the microtask window the row is still measured through). title: Freehand v/sub does not repaint inside react-dom/flushSync — its notification rides a microtask
description:
FOUND BY rf2-dq20a (the Freehand-vs-Reagent measurement), on the UIX adapter, in a real browser.

SYMPTOM. A mounted Freehand view whose body reads `(v/sub [...])` is NOT repainted by a state write made inside `react-dom/flushSync`. The store is written, the subscription recomputes, and React learns about it only after the current task's stack unwinds.

MEASURED, four ways, on one mounted 300-cell grid (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_update_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins the first two as a regression test):

  flushSync(write)                                -> DOM UNCHANGED
  write; await one microtask; flushSync(noop)     -> DOM updated, ~1 ms
  write; setTimeout 0                             -> DOM updated, ~2 ms
  write; requestAnimationFrame                    -> DOM updated, ~32 ms (two frames)

Neither `frame/replace-app-db!`, `rf/dispatch-sync [...] {:frame fid}`, nor `(:dispatch-sync (rf/capture-frame fid))` commits inside the flush. Reagent (r/cursor + reagent.core/flush) and plain React (root.render inside flushSync) both commit in the same window.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BENCH.
1. It is a real product property: a re-frame2/Freehand consumer cannot force a state change to the DOM synchronously through any public door. Anything that needs to read the DOM immediately after a write — a measurement, a scroll-into-view, a focus move, a test — has to yield a microtask first, and nothing documents that.
2. It cost this bead a whole measurement pass. The first update instrument timed each write inside flushSync and produced numbers for Freehand arms whose DOM never changed at all; only a DOM read-back inside the measured window caught it.
3. It is NOT the ratom-adapter bug. rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz record inert subscriptions under a ratom adapter. This is the UIX adapter, subscriptions are live, and the repaint does happen — one microtask late.

WANTED: either a documented synchronous-commit door (the equivalent of reagent.core/flush), or a spec sentence stating that Freehand commits are microtask-deferred and what a caller must do to observe one. Note the UIX adapter's own `flush-views!` did NOT commit the write when measured, and `react/act` did but cost ~600 ms a call.

Evidence: PR for rf2-dq20a; the four-way table is in the b6-update namespace docstring and pinned by `a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync`.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7133. Root cause: cell/mark-dirty! schedules no React work, so react-dom/flushSync had nothing to commit. Fix: the pending window gains a second, React-visible closer (re-frame.freehand.checkpoint) armed by the same first mark and running the same idempotent cell/flush!; the microtask is untouched. All four measured cases pass in a real browser under the UIx adapter, plus the flushSync(dispatch-sync) door. Batching proven unchanged by an adversarial three-writes-in-one-task row. Follow-ons: rf2-mo5mk (Spec 006 sentence, hot-zone), rf2-0fgth (flip the b6 non-vacuity row that pins the broken behaviour).

title: OPERATOR DECISION: do we keep the Freehand compiled tier at all?
description:
RAISED BY MIKE (2026-07-27), after reading rf2-lnecd's report: 'I don't think we can justify a 10,000 line compiler?'

DO NOT IMPLEMENT ON THIS BEAD. It records a decision Mike has not yet made. Removing the compiler is a ~25,700-line irreversible-in-practice change; it happens only on an explicit ruling.

=== THE COST, COUNTED NOT ESTIMATED (rf2-lnecd section 5) ===
  Compiler source (compiler/ + compiler.cljc)   10,276 lines, 14 namespaces, macro-time, SHIPS NOTHING
  Compiler-facing tests                         12,974 lines across 62 files
  The separate grammar, spec/004D                2,474 lines of normative doc
  Compiled browser runtime (compiled_react.cljs)   299 lines  <- the only part that ships
  Conformance fixtures                          14 of 97 (fh-diag-* / fh-struct-* families)
  Documentation                                 32 files mention {:compiled true} / the tier / 004D
  Diagnostics                                   83 distinct :rf.ui.compile/* ids, enumerated in no single place
The compiler is 29% of implementation/freehand/src (10,276 of 35,480) and its tests are 20% of the freehand test tree (12,974 of 66,360) - for zero runtime behaviour a browser executes.

=== WHAT IT ACTUALLY BUYS, after auditing every candidate consumer (section 6) ===
ONE production call site: react.cljs:637 reads the manifest to choose the wrapper via (not= :elided (:view-cell ...)). That is ELISION, and nothing else.
Everything else evaporated on inspection:
  - tools/xray does NOT consume the Freehand tier - it requires re-frame.ui.tool, the DONOR compiler, a different tier. tools/xray/src/ contains no re-frame.freehand reference at all.
  - tools/story: test-only, and against the donor tier; its own docstring says the shipped jar must not depend on it.
  - v/check DOES NOT EXIST as a public verb. Every caller is a test. Making it trustworthy is rf2-drpa3.182.6, P1, open and PAUSED.
  - MCP read-view-manifest is real and shipped, but it works for INTERPRETED views too, returning :basis :opaque with {:reason :no-static-analysis}. There is a dedicated conformance fixture for that arm.
  - NO APPLICATION IN THIS REPOSITORY DECLARES A {:compiled true} VIEW.

=== THE PERFORMANCE CASE IS THIN, AND IT IS NOT WHAT PEOPLE THINK ===
Mount cost as a ratio to the in-run React floor:
  W3 ordinary form, 51 el     tuned interpreted / compiled = 1.054 [0.846-1.222]  <- STRADDLES 1.0
  W1 large template, 1204 el  interpreted 2.747x floor, compiled 1.132x floor
  W2 300 elidable boundaries  interpreted 7.320x floor, compiled 2.183x floor
UPDATES ARE A NULL RESULT: 0.2-0.5ms p50 on every arm of every witness, tiers indistinguishable at timer resolution. Whatever compiling buys, it does not buy re-render speed.
The section-1a ablation decomposes the advantage: the ViewCell alone is 1.712x wall clock and 6.256x RETAINED HEAP; interpretation alone is 1.216x clock and 1.011x heap. A kept ViewCell costs 2,348 BYTES OF STANDING HEAP PER BOUNDARY (~700KB at 300 boundaries, ~7MB at 3000).
So the asset is ELISION, and elision is overwhelmingly a MEMORY win, not a clock win.

=== THE TAX COMPOUNDS ===
One view-language feature (v/defhost, commit c706fb01f2) cost +285 lines across five compiler/runtime files. The compiled arm's answer was not a lowering - it was a NEW BUILD REFUSAL (:rf.ui.compile/host-crossing-unsupported). Floor: every new feature must be classified by the analyzer and either lowered or explicitly refused with a stable diagnostic id and recoveries; the compiler can never simply not know about a feature. Ceiling: when lowering is hard the feature ships WORSE compiled, so the tier becomes a reason a user cannot use something they paid for everywhere else.

=== WHAT ARGUES FOR KEEPING ===
  1. The compiler does not ship. 10,276 lines are macro-time, proven absent from a production bundle against a positive control. The cost is maintenance, not user bytes.
  2. Only PROOF can elide safely. A compiler proves a body has no reactive site; a flag merely asserts it.
  3. Mike ruled KEEP earlier on 2026-07-26 ('the compiled tier is KEPT, for performance, as a SPECIALISED requirement - the paved path stays interpreted'). NOTE: that ruling predates the ablation, and the ablation undermines its stated premise, since there is no performance case on ordinary views.
  4. The measurement covers ONE shape (a 300-sibling boundary storm), MOUNT ONLY, no deep trees, no wide attribute maps, no reordering lists, no bundle dimension.

=== WHAT ARGUES FOR REMOVING ===
  1. ~25,700 lines of blast radius for one production call site.
  2. The compiled tier is strictly ADDITIVE: promoting three views cost +18,182 raw / +5,093 gzipped bytes, and every sentinel of the interpreted walk is still PRESENT in a fully-compiled bundle. There is no configuration where a consumer ships compiled INSTEAD of interpreted.
  3. The one clear defect the analyzer caught exclusively was closed by teaching the INTERPRETER to catch it too.
  4. Pre-alpha with zero external consumers is the cheapest moment this will ever be.
  5. The ecosystem already solves macro-time createElement without a bespoke compiler - UIx's $ macro does exactly that (unmeasured here; rf2-dq20a may quantify it).

=== THE OPTIONS ===
  A. KEEP AS-IS. Status quo; today's ruling stands; rf2-h4j7k closes 'no'.
  B. KEEP BUT NARROW. Stop describing it as a performance tier; price the non-elision parts separately next time they ask for budget. This is what rf2-lnecd's report itself recommends.
  C. REPLACE AND DELETE. Ship {:reactive false} (rf2-h4j7k) + the interpreter tuning (rf2-xu6rx), then delete the compiler, 004D, and the compiler test tree. Makes rf2-drpa3.182.6 moot.
  D. DEFER until rf2-dq20a (Freehand vs Reagent) and rf2-h4j7k are both settled.

=== MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: C, BUT STRICTLY SEQUENCED - AND ONLY IF THE CHECK IS TOTAL ===
Do NOT remove first: the compiler is the only current source of elision, and elision is the one asset the evidence supports. Sequence: settle rf2-h4j7k -> ship and verify the checked flag -> then delete on evidence rather than judgement.
The load-bearing technical question is whether the runtime check can be TOTAL rather than partial. The runtime already tracks every subscription deref - that is how reactivity works at all - so a check that notices a deref inside a body declared {:reactive false} looks cheap and complete. IF THAT HOLDS, the framing collapses from 'proof vs trust' to 'proof at build time for 10,276 lines vs detection at first render for a handful', and the compiler becomes very hard to justify. IF IT DOES NOT HOLD - if there is a way to read state inside a declared-inert body that the runtime cannot see - then proof is genuinely irreplaceable and the answer is B, not C. THAT QUESTION SHOULD BE ANSWERED BEFORE THE RULING, and it is a small spike, not a campaign.

Evidence: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md (PR #7112, sections 1, 1a, 3, 5, 6). Related: rf2-h4j7k (the {:reactive false} call - LOAD-BEARING), rf2-dq20a (Freehand vs Reagent), rf2-xu6rx (interpreter headroom), rf2-drpa3.182.6 (trustworthy v/check - moot under C).
notes:
=== OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-27) — DECIDED. OPTION C. DO NOT RE-LITIGATE. ===
Verbatim: 'Ignore compiled FH, we have already decided that it isn't worth it. 10K lines of code is too much overhead.'

The compiled tier does not earn its cost. The question is CLOSED. This bead now tracks the REMOVAL, not the decision.

WHY IT STAYS OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSING NOW: it is blocked by rf2-h4j7k, and that block is real engineering, not bookkeeping. Elision — proving a body has no reactive site and skipping the ViewCell — is delivered TODAY ONLY by the compiler's static analysis. Deleting the compiler therefore deletes elision, worth 1.712x wall clock and 6.256x RETAINED HEAP per elidable boundary (2,348 bytes each: ~700KB at 300 boundaries, ~7MB at 3000). rf2-h4j7k's checked {:reactive false} declaration delivers essentially ALL the heap win and 1.712 of the 2.079 clock win WITHOUT a compiler, and remains undecided.
ORDER OF OPERATIONS: settle rf2-h4j7k -> ship and verify the flag if adopted -> then delete. Removing first silently costs ~7MB of standing heap on a large page. This is not an argument to keep the compiler; it is how to remove it without a regression.

THE LIVE QUESTION IS NOW NARROWER, per the operator: IS INTERPRETED FREEHAND USABLE? If it is slower than Reagent, it is not. Interpreted-vs-Reagent as measured (rf2-dq20a), ratio to shared React floor:
  MOUNT W1 large template  2.987 vs 1.554  -> 1.9x SLOWER   FAILS
  MOUNT W3 ordinary form   1.664 vs 1.394  -> 1.19x SLOWER  FAILS, but close
  UPDATE broad 300 cells  27.78 vs 2.639   -> 10.5x SLOWER  FAILS badly
  UPDATE narrow 1 cell     8.802 vs 0.587  -> 15x SLOWER, but ~90% is re-frame's leg, not rendering — not a valid target as measured
So interpreted Freehand currently fails the standard on every axis that is a valid target. Tracked by the P0 standard bead; profiling of the broad-update deficit is dispatched.

CAVEAT CARRIED FORWARD: a 57% discrepancy on W1 interpreted mount (1.904 per PR #7077 vs 2.987 per rf2-dq20a, both post-#7077) is unreconciled and decides how far mount has to travel. Reconciliation is in the dispatched profiling brief.
=== SEQUENCING NOTE (2026-07-27, delegated ruling on rf2-h4j7k) ===
rf2-h4j7k is RULED (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27): ADOPT the checked {:reactive false} opt-out, gated on the totality spike rf2-3slzz (which now blocks rf2-h4j7k). Order of operations for this bead's Option C removal, unchanged but now concrete: rf2-3slzz answers whether the runtime check is TOTAL -> flag ships with the check (fires loudly at first offending render, prod + dev; contract is SHELL-FREE: no v/sub read and no committed event site in the boundary's own render — reactive children keep their own shells) -> flagged-vs-ordinary interpreted ablation verifies the elision value (6.256x retained heap / 1.712x wall clock per boundary, 2,348 B standing heap each) is delivered -> rf2-h4j7k closes -> the deletion tracked here dispatches. IF THE SPIKE FINDS THE CHECK NON-TOTAL: implement nothing, surface to Mike — proof would then be irreplaceable for elision and Option C needs revisiting (Option B, narrowed compiler). Full analysis (ablation decomposition, failure-mode design, contract correction, implementation shape, acceptance proof) is preserved in rf2-h4j7k's RULING notes; the dossier file is deleted.

=== SPIKE RESULT (rf2-3slzz, PR #7171) COLLAPSES THIS BEAD'S PROOF-VS-TRUST HEDGE ===
THE COMPILER'S OWN PROOF IS ALREADY DEFEATABLE, AND THE RUNTIME CHECK IS ALREADY WHAT SAVES IT. A {:compiled true} view reading reactive state through an ordinary two-hop helper analyzes to :view-cell :elided (asserted off v/manifest) and mounts SHELL-FREE. It does NOT go silently stale: it fails loud at the read, in dev AND under :advanced with goog.DEBUG=false.
So compiled elision was NEVER proof standing alone — it was proof PLUS the very runtime check {:reactive false} would rest on. The hedge recorded above (that deleting the compiler trades a static proof for author trust) does not describe the code that exists.
TOTALITY VERDICT: total on the REACTIVE-READ half, proved not argued — one door, and the probe asserts mechanically that cell.cljc is the only Freehand ns requiring the observation port and that v/sub IS cell/observe!. Capture is dynamic, so refusal is indifferent to how the read was reached: inline, through two defns, inside a lazy child the walk realises, or on a branch only a later render takes (an inert first render still succeeds — no false positive).
NOT total on the EVENT half: three silent degradations (declarative vector + options map, v/event / v/handler carrier, bare fn, plus v/defhost callbacks handed over raw). But that is three (some? cand) forks answering nil instead of raising — NOT an analysis problem, and closing it needs no static analysis. Bounded fix specified in rf2-oxlpy (P1): one dynamically scoped context, one diagnostic, three forks by file/line.
MASKING IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT BELT-AND-BRACES: on the JVM structural host, inside t/with-render, and under v/render-static, a nested body runs INLINE in the caller's dynamic extent, so a shell-free boundary there finds the OUTER candidate and silently DONATES its read to it. A violation that passes a structural test and only fails in a browser is exactly what the flag must not permit.
PRODUCTION CONTRACT DETAIL WORTH ONE SENTENCE WHEN THE FLAG SHIPS: under :advanced, react/act does not exist and flushSync does not rethrow — React 19 routes an uncaught render error to the root's onUncaughtError. The read IS refused with its stable id and NOTHING is committed, but the failure arrives as an uncaught page error rather than something a mount caller can try/catch.
close_reason:
MOOT — FREEHAND IS A FAILED EXPERIMENT (Mike, 2026-07-30). This bead serves only the Freehand programme, which is retracted: rf2-drpa3 closed, rf2-lbs3y answered no (interpreted Freehand ~5x Reagent on bulk repaint, ~1.6x on mount; the gap architectural).

The {:reactive false} opt-out and the compiled-tier question both existed to trade elision against compiler cost inside Freehand. With the substrate retracted there is no tier to keep and no elision to preserve.

NOT the tear check — rf2-so3io / PR #7159 ablated it and a contract-free boundary was STILL ~5.5x, so the guarantee was not the cost.

THE CODE STAYS ('not removed yet'). rf2-lgleu carries the EP withdrawal. DO NOT re-file — retracted, not paused.

title: Measure Freehand against Reagent (and UIx if cheap) on the same React floor, mount AND update
description:
OPERATOR REQUEST (Mike, 2026-07-27): 'MEASURE how fast freehand is relative to Reagent.'

WHY IT DOES NOT EXIST YET. rf2-lnecd measured Freehand-interpreted vs Freehand-compiled against a hand-built React floor. It never measured a competing substrate. Reagent appears exactly once in that report, as an aside about ^{:key ...} semantics. There is no cross-adapter benchmark anywhere in the repo.

WHY IT IS CHEAP NOW. The expensive instrument already exists: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/bench/ carries b1_react.cljs (the hand-built react/createElement floor, gated on canonical-DOM equality so a drifted transcription fails rather than flatters itself), plus measure.cljc, runner.cljc, falsifiability.cljc and provenance.cljc. Adding a Reagent arm against the SAME floor and the SAME witnesses yields an apples-to-apples number, because both substrates' overheads are then expressed above a React reconciliation both pay identically.

REQUIRED SHAPE.
1. Reuse the existing floor + witnesses. Do NOT build a second harness.
2. Reagent arm must be IDIOMATIC Reagent Hiccup as a user would write it (form-1/form-2, r/atom where a local model is wanted, re-frame subs through the reagent adapter) - not a strawman, and not pre-adapted react classes.
3. Gate the Reagent arm on canonical-DOM equality with the floor, exactly as the existing arms are. That equality gate is the fairness guarantee.
4. MOUNT IS ONLY HALF, AND THE MISLEADING HALF. Reagent's design point is fine-grained ratom reactivity on UPDATE. rf2-lnecd's update measurement was a null result (0.2-0.5ms p50, indistinguishable at timer resolution), so an update witness with enough work to resolve ABOVE the timer must be added. A mount-only answer would flatter Freehand and would not answer the question anyone actually cares about.
5. W1 (large template) and W3 (ordinary form) are the honest headline shapes. W2 (300-boundary storm) is elision-maximising and Reagent has NO elision concept, so report it but flag it explicitly as the shape that overstates the gap.
6. Report absolute numbers AND ratios. A 3x ratio on a 0.2ms operation is not a product decision.
7. Pin and state the Reagent version measured.

OPTIONAL, ONLY IF IT DOES NOT DELAY THE REAGENT RESULT: a UIx arm. Mike's hypothesis is that UIx sits near the floor because its $ macro expands to react/createElement at compile time - structurally the same position as compiled Freehand. The uix adapter exists at implementation/adapters/uix. Note the adapter also exposes set-hiccup-emitter!, so the arm must use the $ spelling to test the hypothesis as stated. UIx has no elision, so it should NOT inherit the compiled tier's boundary-storm win - that contrast is itself informative.

DO NOT CONFUSE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS. rf2-8cnxg and rf2-jt8vz record that FREEHAND RUNNING ON a ratom adapter has inert subscriptions and never repaints. That is Freehand-on-Reagent. This bead is Freehand-as-substrate vs REAGENT-as-substrate: two independent substrates rendering the same witness to React. This bead is NOT blocked by those bugs.

CAVEATS TO CARRY INTO THE WRITE-UP: measurements are taken on a loaded developer workstation, so arms must be interleaved and every figure floor-normalised in-run; nothing here is a release-worker number.
notes:
PR OPEN: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7131 (worker/bench-vs-reagent).
Gates all exit 0: freehand JVM (1215/8130), npm test:cljs (11592/58166), mkdocs --strict, test-fast-pr.sh (PASS), browser bench lane (23 tests/316 assertions incl. the five-arm canonical-DOM parity gates).
Findings + raw per-round data: ai/findings/2026-07-27.freehand-vs-reagent.md (local-only, uncommitted).
close_reason: PR #7131 merged. Freehand measured against Reagent and UIx on the shared React floor (:advanced, goog.DEBUG false, 6 rounds), mount AND update, with a canonical-DOM parity gate on every arm. Report at docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent.md. HEADLINE: on mount compiled Freehand beats Reagent (1.304x floor vs 1.554x, disjoint ranges) while interpreted Freehand is 1.9x SLOWER than Reagent; UIx is nearest the floor on every mount witness INCLUDING the elision-maximising W2 (1.361 vs compiled Freehand's 2.139), so elision buys no lead over a substrate that never creates a wrapper. On update Reagent wins decisively (~10x broad, ~15x narrow), though ~90% of the narrow-update cost decomposes to frame/replace-app-db! plus the re-frame signal graph, which a Reagent app reading re-frame subs would also pay; Freehand's own deficit is bulk re-render at ~7-8x, where compiling barely helps. Two instrument faults caught and fixed before publication (writes timed inside flushSync never reaching the DOM while returning plausible numbers; an empty flushSync leaving 80 of 320 floor samples stale) - every measured write is now read back out of the DOM inside its own window, 0 rejected of 384. NOT covered: memory across substrates, which the report names as the obvious and possibly more decisive next measurement. Filed rf2-w2m25 (P1, fixed in #7133) and rf2-n91mv (P3).

title: [bug] CI never runs any suite under the real -Dre-frame.debug=false production gate
notes:
Split out of rf2-9c2jf (P1, reproduced: under the documented production gate a handler registered after make-frame never ran).

THE GAP: nothing in .github/workflows or scripts/ ever sets re-frame.debug / RE_FRAME_DEBUG. Every suite that calls itself a production-gate test (jvm_prod_gate_integration_test, ep0008_producers_jvm_gate_test, and friends) rebinds interop/debug-enabled? with with-redefs AFTER the framework has loaded. The JVM gate is read ONCE at namespace-load time, so with-redefs cannot exercise anything the gate decided at load time — which is exactly the class of defect rf2-9c2jf turned out to be (a load-time defonce whose body was skipped, so the frame-generation freshener was never installed).

Result: the documented production configuration was never executed by CI at all, and a total dispatch failure under it stayed green for however long it had been broken.

rf2-9c2jf ships one suite that closes the hole for its own defect only: implementation/core/test/re_frame/prod_gate_dispatch_jvm_test.clj relaunches a child JVM with the property actually on the command line. That is a point fix.

WHAT THIS BEAD WANTS: a real lane. Run implementation/core (at minimum) with -Dre-frame.debug=false as a first-class job, so the whole suite is executed under the production posture rather than one hand-written probe. Needs a .github/workflows edit and probably a deps.edn alias, both hot-zone/fenced surfaces, so the mayor should sequence it rather than hand it to a worker mid-flight.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether the whole core suite can be green under the gate today (unknown — nobody has ever run it), and whether the lane belongs on PR or nightly.
close_reason: PR #7128. First-ever run of the core suite under the real -Dre-frame.debug=false gate: 91 of 174 namespaces RED, almost all asserting dev instrumentation inline with semantics (legitimate dev-posture tests, not defects). Roster is an EXCLUSION list (scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh) so new namespaces join by default. re-frame.prod-gate-lane-pin-test asserts unconditionally that the property reached the JVM and the framework honoured it — proven to have teeth by inverting the posture. Remainder split to rf2-r9bra (P1 triage of the 11 non-instrumentation failures), rf2-d2841 (P2 instrumentation/semantics split), rf2-f7qj4 (P3 misnamed with-redefs prod-gate suites).

title: B2 gates elision as a COUNT but never prices it: add retained bytes per elided boundary
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-lnecd's elision ablation (PR #7112).

re-frame.freehand.bench.b2 gates capability elision on an EXACT INTEGER — the number of ViewCell
shells a mass mount omits, read off v/manifest, with a three-read arm as the discrimination that
a zero is a real absence. Its own docstring is careful that this is a STATIC property and that
'nothing in this namespace sells a static count as a runtime one'. The runtime counterpart
(b2-dom-cljs-test) counts occurrences off document and reads back the wrapper React reconciled.

So the B-spine can prove HOW MANY cells were elided and can prove they really were. It cannot say
WHAT ONE IS WORTH. The elision claim — the load-bearing justification for the whole compiled tier
under the KEEP ruling — has no quantitative price anywhere in the gates.

The ablation produced one, and it is near-deterministic, which is rare on this box:

  one kept ViewCell   2348 B of standing heap per boundary  [free-ik 2794 vs free-ic 447, ranges
                      disjoint by 6x, and an independent performance.memory occupancy reading
                      agreed at 2295 B]
  a REACTIVE boundary 4134 B over the React floor — the extra ~1700 B is the subscription

METHOD, which is the transferable part. Mount K roots and KEEP THEM MOUNTED; read the heap around
that; release; read again. Do NOT reach for an allocation counter: V8's sampling heap profiler
drops the samples of COLLECTED objects, so pointed at a mount/unmount loop it reports the residue
of a discarded page (the same 80,000 objects read 4.77 MB when a global holds them and 0.00 MB
when nothing does). Retention is the right question anyway — a ViewCell is a cell object, a hook
record, a subscription registration and two layout effects that live as long as the mount.
ANY browser heap reading added here MUST carry a positive control of known size, in situ, in the
same window, or 'this arm is cheap' and 'the sampler is not running' are the same number.

SHAPE OF THE WORK: a retained-bytes-per-boundary reading on the existing B2 roster, published on
the :fixture (NOT a gate — it is a timing-class quantity and D021 puts those on the fixture, while
elision COUNTS gate). The instrument is recoverable from branch worker/hiccup-perf-lnecd2's
pre-deletion commits (scripts/studio-probe.cjs --retain, and studio-report.cjs for the reduction).

NOT urgent. B2's integer gate is sound and this does not fix a defect — it makes the tier's one
real asset measurable rather than merely counted.
notes:
PROMOTED P3 -> P1 (mayor, 2026-07-27). I had previously flagged this as minutiae and a candidate to close. THAT ASSESSMENT IS NOW WRONG, because the context changed under it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the operator ruled that Freehand cannot ship slower than Reagent (rf2-lbs3y, P0). The profiling verdict is that the broad-update gap is ARCHITECTURAL — the commit-side re-read IS the invariant-5 tear check, and even zeroing the boundary term and the write leg leaves ~7x. So the clock argument for Freehand is close to exhausted.

MEMORY IS THE ONE AXIS THAT HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED ACROSS SUBSTRATES, and it is the axis where Freehand's design might win outright: the within-Freehand ablation found 6.256x retained heap per elidable boundary (2,348 bytes each — ~700KB at 300 boundaries, ~7MB at 3000). Nothing comparable exists for Reagent or UIx. Pricing elision in RETAINED BYTES rather than counting elided cells is the first step toward that comparison, and it may be the measurement that decides whether Freehand has a case at all.

INSTRUMENT WARNING, non-negotiable: V8's CDP SAMPLING heap profiler DROPS the samples of collected objects — the same 80,000 objects read 4.77 MB when held and 0.00 MB when not. Any byte figure must come from a RETENTION instrument (mount K roots and keep them) with an in-situ positive control every round, not from the sampling profiler. That fault already produced one wrong table on this surface.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: B2 lives on the bench surface. Sequence against any live bench work (rf2-prjh0, rf2-huhno, rf2-wxrrp) rather than racing it.
close_reason:
PR #7146. ANSWERED, and the answer goes AGAINST Freehand.

Retained bytes per boundary ABOVE the React floor, 10 roots x 300 boundaries held, 6 rounds, :advanced:
  sub-free boundary   Freehand 2430 [2417-2450]  Reagent 410 [406-416]  UIx 251 [248-255]   -> 5.93x / 9.67x
  reactive boundary   Freehand 4346 [4332-4361]  Reagent 1037 [1035-1039]                   -> 4.19x
All ranges disjoint. Two independent readers agree to within 1% on every row.

So B2's elided boundary is worth 2430 B of standing heap (2427 on the independent reader) and the integer gate can now be multiplied out. That is the bead as filed. But the reason it was promoted to P1 - that memory might be the axis where Freehand wins outright - is FALSIFIED. Memory is the worst axis measured so far.

The framework-asymmetry rebuttal does NOT apply. The widest gap is on the witness with no reactivity, no app-db and no cursor on either side; going reactive NARROWS the ratio (Freehand's increment for a signal is 3.06x Reagent's, its wrapper is 5.93x). The larger term is the ViewCell, which is Freehand's own.

CORROBORATES the within-Freehand ablation from a different instrument and basis: 2430 here vs its 2348 B/kept-ViewCell; 4346 vs its 4134 for a reactive boundary. The ablation's figure was sound.

INSTRUMENT: retention only, never allocation. Positive control of PREDICTED size every round (587,500 unboxed doubles = 4,700,000 B): CDP usedSize measured 4,692,044 (-0.17%), heap-snapshot self_size 4,700,024 (+0.0005%). 0 unverified of 56 mounts. NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE HEAP WORK: CDP Runtime.getHeapUsage and performance.memory are two doors onto ONE V8 counter (3,868,954 both, to the byte) and are NOT independent - the heap snapshot is. And a 4.7 MB 'x'.repeat(n) string reads as 6 KB on all three readers, so it is useless as a control.

Published: docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-memory.md. Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_{heap,app}.cljs + b7_run.cjs.

title: Decide the {:reactive false} checked opt-out: the ablation says a flag would deliver ALL of elision's measured value
description:
OPERATOR CALL, raised in priority by rf2-lnecd's elision ablation (PR #7112).

The compiled-tier report already named this as 'the single change that would most undermine KEEP':
an opt-in author declaration {:reactive false}, CHECKED at runtime rather than PROVEN by analysis,
would take most of the compiled tier's measured advantage at a tiny fraction of its cost.

THE ABLATION MAKES THE STAKES EXACT. With the confounds removed (same 300 boundaries both
witnesses, same leaf body, a floor arm each, and the compiled body object asserted identical
between arms), the compiled tier's advantage on a sub-free witness decomposes as:

  free-ik / free-ic   the ViewCell alone       1.712 [1.583-1.879] wall clock, 6.256 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ik   interpretation alone     1.216 [1.092-1.425] wall clock, 1.011 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ic   the two together         2.079 [1.896-2.419] wall clock, 6.327 retained heap

A kept ViewCell costs 2348 BYTES OF STANDING HEAP PER BOUNDARY (2295 by an independent
occupancy instrument). 300 boundaries = ~700 KB; 3000 = ~7 MB.

So a checked flag would deliver 1.712x of the 2.079x wall-clock effect and essentially ALL of
the 6.26x retained-heap effect, because both are the ViewCell and nothing else. The residual
that only PROOF can deliver is the 1.216 interpretation term — and only on a sub-free leaf; on a
reactive leaf the two tiers measured 1.045 [0.922-1.173], straddling 1.0.

THE QUESTION IS NOT PERFORMANCE, IT IS SAFETY, and that is why it is an operator call rather
than a work item. A proven verdict cannot be wrong. A checked one can: an author declares
{:reactive false} and later adds a v/sub, and the boundary silently stops updating unless the
check catches it. What the check costs, what it catches, and whether a silently-stale view is an
acceptable failure mode for an opt-in are the design questions.

DO NOT IMPLEMENT ON THIS BEAD. It records a decision Mike has not made. If the answer is 'no',
close it and the ablation numbers stand as the justification for the compiler. If the answer is
'investigate', that is a separate spike.

Evidence: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md 1a (PR #7112).
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): ADOPT {:reactive false} — dossier Option 1, gated on the totality spike rf2-3slzz. Sequencing is fixed: spike (rf2-3slzz) -> ship the checked flag -> verify the measured elision value is delivered -> then, and only then, the compiler deletion executes rf2-zw1oo Option C. This is the only decision consistent with Mike's ruling already on rf2-zw1oo (Option C, the compiler goes, do not re-litigate): answering "no flag" would make the compiler the only source of elision again, and "delete with no replacement" silently regresses ~7 MB of standing heap on a large page — the zw1oo notes explicitly forbid that ordering. THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN as the sequencing gate: it closes when the flag has shipped and its elision value is verified, which unblocks zw1oo's deletion. rf2-3slzz now blocks this bead so the gate is visible in the dependency graph.

POSTURE ALIGNMENT: replacing 10,276 lines of build-time proof machinery with a one-key author declaration backed by a cheap, total runtime check is trust-the-programmer in miniature — minimal ergonomic API, the programmer states intent, the framework checks it cheaply and diagnoses loudly. Risk is bounded by the spike: if the check turns out non-total, stop before deleting anything (see TOTALITY below).

=== ABLATION DECOMPOSITION (rf2-lnecd, PR #7112; evidence to preserve: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md section 1a) ===
  free-ik / free-ic   ViewCell alone        1.712 [1.583-1.879] wall clock, 6.256 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ik   interpretation alone  1.216 [1.092-1.425] wall clock, 1.011 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ic   the two together      2.079 [1.896-2.419] wall clock, 6.327 retained heap
  reactive leaf, compiled vs interpreted    1.045 [0.922-1.173] — STRADDLES 1.0
A kept ViewCell costs 2,348 bytes of standing heap per boundary (2,295 by an independent occupancy instrument): ~700 KB at 300 boundaries, ~7 MB at 3,000. The checked flag therefore delivers essentially ALL of the 6.26x retained-heap win and 1.712 of the 2.079 wall-clock win, because both are the ViewCell and nothing else. The residual only proof can deliver is the 1.216x interpretation term — and only on a sub-free leaf.

=== FAILURE-MODE DESIGN (the bead's open questions, answered) ===
A silently-stale boundary is NOT an acceptable failure mode. The check must fire LOUDLY at the first offending render, in production builds as well as development — it is the safety mechanism, not authoring lint. First-offending-render semantics: a props-controlled branch that did not execute at mount may trip the check on a later render; that is acceptable because no stale dependency exists until the read is actually attempted, at which point the render fails loudly instead of committing stale UI. An unexecuted branch cannot be diagnosed without static analysis and does not need to be. Check cost: consultation of a dynamically scoped context on paths the runtime already instruments — cheap.

=== THE TOTALITY QUESTION, STATED PRECISELY (rf2-3slzz's charter) ===
Is there ANY way to read reactive state — or produce a committed event site — inside a declared-inert body that the runtime cannot observe at render time? If YES, proof is genuinely irreplaceable for elision, the answer reverts to keeping a narrowed compiler (rf2-zw1oo Option B), and zw1oo's Option C ruling needs revisiting with Mike. Evidence that it is total (Codex second opinion; the spike verifies rather than trusts this): every supported reactive read converges on one runtime function — public v/sub is an alias of cell/observe!, and the compiled spelling reaches the same recorder via observe-site!; both consult the render's dynamically scoped candidate before resolving or probing, and an absent candidate already raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc). Because capture is dynamic, a v/sub reached through an arbitrary ordinary helper is caught exactly like an inline read — FH-SUB-010 pins that property (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/sub_cljs_test.cljc). No sanctioned second reactive-read door exists. "Total" is scoped honestly: total over Freehand's SUPPORTED reactive semantics, not arbitrary Clojure. rf/subscribe-once is explicitly non-reactive and stays legal under the flag (a snapshot by request). Raw atom derefs and other private state channels were never ViewCell-tracked and remain the programmer's responsibility — detecting them would turn the opt-out back into a compiler.

=== CONTRACT CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion — ADOPTED) ===
A ViewCell is not merely a subscription tracker: it also owns the selected render's committed event sites and frame binding. The elision oracle keeps the cell for EITHER live site family — a v/sub read OR a committed event site (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/viewcell_elision_oracle_jvm_test.clj; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs). The flag's contract is therefore SHELL-FREE, not merely sub-free: "This boundary is shell-free: its own render performs no v/sub read and produces no committed event site. It may freely mount reactive child views; those children own their own shells." This matches the exact eligibility the compiler already used — no new optimization category invented. Known gap the implementation MUST close: react.cljs has two no-candidate fallbacks — native element handlers and declared-host callbacks — where declarative intent can currently disappear or a function can pass through without committed-site guarantees; under the flag these positions must RAISE, not silently degrade. The structural interpreter separately records every filled event position in :events (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/node.cljc). These are chokepoints, not an open-ended analysis problem.

=== IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (for the flag bead, filed after the spike) ===
One lightweight, dynamically scoped shell-free assertion context, carrying the declaring view id, wrapped around both the body and its normalization. It must MASK any outer render candidate, so a shell-free child rendered inside a structural test or another capture cannot accidentally donate its read to the outer boundary. Under that context: v/sub raises one dedicated opt-out-violation diagnostic BEFORE probing; any filled event position that would require a committed site raises the same diagnostic, naming the event capability. The error carries the view id and offending capability. One context, one stable diagnostic — do NOT build a policy framework around it.

=== ACCEPTANCE PROOF (keep the implementation gate narrow) ===
1. A shell-free view mounts without a ViewCell or the shell's React hooks, and the flagged-vs-ordinary interpreted ablation confirms the retained-heap and mount benefit.
2. Inline, helper-mediated, and later-branch v/sub violations fail before observation or ownership, in both development and production builds.
3. Native event intent, v/event / v/handler, bare handler functions, and declared-host callback positions all fail rather than disappear or lose committed-site semantics.
4. A reactive child mounted by a shell-free parent remains fully reactive.
5. Adding or removing {:reactive false} changes the hot-reload shell signature and causes one clean remount; React must never reuse hook state across that transition.

=== INDEPENDENT OBLIGATION (do not let this decision slow it) ===
Under the rf2-lbs3y standard, compiled Freehand was the only tier beating Reagent on mount (1.304 vs 1.554); UIx reaches 1.163 with a macro and no compiler, so compiling was never the only way to meet the bar. Not a reason to keep the compiler — but the interpreter tuning obligations (rf2-lbs3y items 1 and 2) matter independently of this decision and must not be slowed by it.

=== SPIKE rf2-3slzz ANSWERED (2026-07-27) — SEQUENCING GATE MOVES ON. ===
Verdict: the runtime check IS total over what it must OBSERVE (there is no door a declared-inert body can read reactive state or produce a committed event site through that the runtime does not already see — one read chokepoint, exactly three event-site forks, no fifth), but it is NOT yet total in what it DOES about three of them: a declarative :on-* vector or options map has its prop never written, a v/event / v/handler carrier is dropped the same way (a Callback deftype is deliberately not fn? in CLJS), and a v/defhost :event callback is handed over raw. Each is a single (some? cand) fork, so a masking assertion context closes all three. No static analysis is needed for any of it.
The finding that most affects rf2-zw1oo: the COMPILER'S OWN PROOF IS ALREADY DEFEATABLE. A {:compiled true} view reading through an ordinary two-hop helper analyzes to :view-cell :elided and mounts shell-free — and does not go silently stale, because cell/observe!'s candidate check refuses it, in development AND in an :advanced production bundle. Compiled elision was never proof alone; it was proof plus the very runtime check this flag rests on.
FLAG-IMPLEMENTATION BEAD FILED: rf2-oxlpy (P1), which now blocks this bead in place of rf2-3slzz. It carries the contract wording, the one-context/one-diagnostic shape, the three forks by file and line, two contract details the spike found by running it (subscribe-once's ambient form DOES still resolve, via the React frame-context tier — not via with-capture; and in production the refusal reaches the page as an uncaught error rather than something a mount caller can try/catch), and the sequencing constraint that cell.cljc is a serialized lane behind rf2-lbs3y and rf2-9f1s7. Also filed: rf2-nzmuy (P3, latent).
Full analysis: ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md. Probe suites kept on PR #7171.

The {:reactive false} opt-out and the compiled-tier question both existed to trade elision against compiler cost inside Freehand. With the substrate retracted there is no tier to keep and no elision to preserve.

NOT the tear check — rf2-so3io / PR #7159 ablated it and a contract-free boundary was STILL ~5.5x, so the guarantee was not the cost.

THE CODE STAYS ('not removed yet'). rf2-lgleu carries the EP withdrawal. DO NOT re-file — retracted, not paused.

title: Freehand view subscriptions are inert on the ratom substrates (Reagent / reagent-slim)
description:
FOUND while executing rf2-gzmg0 (merged-PR audit #7037 residual), and MEASURED in a real Chromium browser lane. Filed rather than fixed there: the defect is upstream of Story and upstream of the presence bridge, and its fix touches core's observation port or the ratom spine. THE SYMPTOM. A Freehand view mounted with v/mount under `re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter` renders ONCE and never again. Its `(v/sub ...)` reads never move. Measured (browser-test lane, Chromium, real react-dom/client), with a `(v/sub [:toasts])`-driven `(v/presence ...)` boundary: DIAG toaster render ids: nil DIAG after bare dispatch-sync html:
cell-pending: 0 DIAG after substrate/flush-render! html:
cell-pending: 0 DIAG after freehand-commit! html:
DIAG after microtask html:
DIAG after macrotask html:
The identical fixture under `v/adapter` renders three times. The ViewCell is never marked dirty (cell-pending stays 0), so this is not a commit-boundary problem — no notification is ever raised at all. THE MECHANISM, read off the sources rather than inferred. 1. `re-frame.substrate.observation/build-node-handle!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc ~:1959) activates a derived value by ADD-WATCH then DEREF, and its comment states the assumption: "Watch BEFORE the baseline observe: a watched reaction is live on the reactive hosts, so the observe below reads through the activated node." 2. That assumption is false for stock Reagent. Reagent's `Reaction` `-add-watch` is `add-w`, which only assoc's into `.-watches` — it does not run the reaction. And `Reaction`'s `-deref`, when `*ratom-context*` is nil AND `auto-run` is nil, takes its NON-REACTIVE branch: it recomputes `(f)` directly, WITHOUT `deref-capture`. So `watching` stays nil, the reaction never subscribes to the app-db ratom, `_handle-change` is never called, and `notify-w` never fires. 3. `make-derived-value` for the ratom family is a plain `(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn ...))` with no `:auto-run` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, make-ratom-spine). A Reagent COMPONENT never hits this because its render runs inside `*ratom-context*`, so the deref takes the reactive branch and the reaction captures its sources on first read. Freehand's ViewCell is not a Reagent reactive context, so it takes the dead branch. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TEST. - Spec 006's stated rationale for Freehand owning an adapter is that plain-atom's derived value reifies IDeref but NOT IWatchable while the spine's DOES ("That single difference is the whole reason a Freehand page needed a wrapper library it never rendered through"). Reagent's Reaction IS IWatchable, so it satisfies the letter of that test — while never notifying. IWatchable is necessary and not sufficient, and the spec rationale does not say so. - Both `re-frame.freehand` and `re-frame.freehand.substrate` docstrings state that bring-your-own-adapter "stays legitimate for a mixed application under the single-adapter runtime", qualifying it only with a caveat about test helpers and ViewCell-settling semantics. That is a stronger claim than the code supports. - Story's shipped topology IS this mixed shape: every Story testbed seats `re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter` (tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/core.cljs:75, story_static.cljs:39, login_form/core.cljs:82) because Story's shell is a Reagent application. A Freehand variant rendered in a Story canvas today would be frozen at its first render. - There is no existing coverage: `git grep reagent implementation/freehand/test/` returns only vs-reagent DOC-comparison hits. No test anywhere mounts a Freehand view under a non-Freehand adapter. WHAT A FIX HAS TO DECIDE (not for a worker to pick). (a) Make the observation port ACTIVATE a derived value rather than assume a watch activates it — e.g. an optional adapter-supplied activation op the ratom spine fills with a capturing run. Correct but adds a contract slot. (b) Give the ratom spine's `make-derived-value` an eager mode. Changes Reagent subscription semantics process-wide (eager recompute on every write instead of lazy-on-render) — a real perf/semantics change, almost certainly wrong. (c) Rule the mixed Freehand-under-ratom topology UNSUPPORTED and fail loud at `v/mount` when the seated adapter is not one whose derived values self-notify, and correct the two door docstrings + the Spec 006 rationale accordingly. (c) is cheapest and may well be right given `v/adapter` exists precisely so a Freehand page needs no wrapper library — but it is a product ruling, and it decides whether a Story canvas can ever host a Freehand variant. ACCEPTANCE. Whichever way it goes, the outcome must be a test that mounts a Freehand view under `re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter` and either observes a moving subscription or observes the loud refusal. A silent single render is the one outcome that must not survive.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #7118 (worker/freehand-ratom-lane). Root cause: build-node-handle! installed its per-handle add-watch on the assumption that 'a watched reaction is live on the reactive hosts'. False on the ratom family — a reagent.ratom/Reaction captures its sources only through deref-capture, and a deref outside *ratom-context* with auto-run nil runs the body raw and leaves `watching` nil, so _handle-change is never called and even reagent.core/flush moves nothing. The port held a watch on a node that could not fire.

Fix = option (a) from the bead, in its cheapest honest form: a new OPTIONAL routed late-bind hook :adapter/activate-derived-value! (re-frame.interop/activate-derived-value!), published by the ratom family ALONE and called by build-node-handle! before the watch install. Reagent supplies ratom/run; reagent-slim gains reagent2.ratom/activate! (the rewrite dropped IRunnable). Absent hook => no-op, so the React-hook spine / plain-atom / test-react / JVM are untouched. The ten-fn adapter contract SHAPE is unchanged — it rides the late-bind table exactly as :adapter/derived-container? does. Option (b) (:auto-run true) was found and deliberately rejected: it recomputes every Reagent-hosted subscription synchronously inside the app-db reset!. Option (c) is moot — the topology is legitimate and the docstrings needed no retraction.

ACCEPTANCE MET, and by the path that actually failed: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/freehand_cell_under_ratom_adapter_dom_cljs_test.cljs mounts a Freehand v/mount root under re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter in real Chromium and observes a MOVING subscription (0->1->2, plus a real DOM press arm and an adversarial no-movement arm). Falsified: with the one activation line commented out, that suite goes red 7/7 with cell/pending-count 0 and the DOM frozen at its first render — the operator's exact measurement. A second suite, observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs, pins the port-level fact plus the adversarial half (an unobserved sub is never made eager; activation idempotent across two owners; total no-op off its own derived values).

Also removed the ratom/run! DRIVERS both existing port suites stood — they were hand-supplying this very runtime step, which is why they never caught the defect.

Gates: test:cljs 11593/58183 0F0E; test:browser 817/5198 0F0E; core JVM 2126/10495 0F0E; freehand JVM 1215/8130 0F0E; adapter smokes 3/0F; reagent-slim smoke 1/0F; test-fast-pr.sh PASS. All exit 0.

Follow-ons filed: rf2-h24yb (spec/006 wording — hot-zone, out of fence), rf2-r83ni (xray testbed/spec + shadow-cljs prose that records the old behaviour).

title: A Freehand ViewCell never repaints under a ratom-family adapter, and Xray refuses to mount under Freehand's own — so no host both repaints reactively AND shows the Views panel
description:
Found while building the Freehand-hosted Xray testbed for rf2-6pohj (PR for that bead carries the reproduction as a shipped surface: tools/xray/testbeds/freehand_views/).

REPRODUCTION (real Chromium, headless, one page, one build — the ONLY variable is which adapter rf/init! installs):

  Page: a Freehand root (v/mount) over :rf/default carrying three declared views; one compiled view reads (v/sub [::count]); one compiled view dispatches (:on-click [::bump]).

  (a) rf/init! re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter
      Click '+': the dispatch LANDS. app-db moves — Xray's App-db panel shows {:count 1 <- was 0} and the Trace panel shows DISPATCH + EVENT HANDLER rows for [:freehand-views.core/bump].
      The cell NEVER repaints. The rendered <output> stays 0 through repeated clicks and long waits.
      re_frame.freehand.cell.pending_count() === 0 after the dispatch — the cell was never marked dirty, so this is NOT a flush/scheduling stall downstream of mark-dirty!. reagent.core.flush() does not move it; cell/flush! does not move it (nothing is pending to flush).
      => the committed read receives NO change notification. The repaint channel is never entered.

  (b) rf/init! re-frame.freehand/adapter  (same page, same build, query-param switch)
      Click '+': the cell repaints correctly, 0 -> 1 -> 2.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TESTBED: (b) is not an available workaround for anyone who wants to SEE this in Xray, because day8.re-frame2-xray.mount refuses :rf.adapter/freehand (rf2-qgfo4 — Xray's shell is hiccup, Freehand's :render is element-shaped). Xray does not mount at all on host (b): [data-testid=rf-xray-shell] count 0.

So on today's substrate NO single host both repaints a Freehand cell reactively AND renders Xray's Views panel. Any browser gate over that panel is bounded by this — rf2-6pohj's scenario drives commits through the mount verb instead, because a render reads current values regardless of the notification channel.

WHY THIS LOOKS LIKE A REAL GAP RATHER THAN A MIS-CONFIGURATION: re-frame.freehand.substrate's own docstring blesses this exact arrangement — 'Bring-your-own adapter also stays legitimate for a mixed application under the single-adapter runtime' — and records that before Freehand shipped an adapter, an interactive Freehand application 'had to install UIx or Reagent to obtain' the observation half. re-frame.freehand.release-app's docstring says the same ('This fixture used to install the UIx one, and it had to'). If the ratom family cannot drive the repaint channel, that blessing is currently false for Reagent and the docstrings overstate what a mixed host gives you.

NOT DIAGNOSED HERE (deliberately — implementation/freehand/** and the adapter/observation surfaces were fenced for this worker): whether the fault is the ratom Reaction's notification semantics under re-frame.substrate.observation/build-node-handle! (which add-watch'es BEFORE its baseline observe precisely so the reaction stays live), the ratom spine's derived value, or the cell's on-change wiring. UIx (make-react-adapter, same spine family as Freehand's own) was NOT tested — worth one probe, since it would separate 'ratom family' from 'any foreign adapter'.

REMEDY IS A RULING, NOT OBVIOUSLY A FIX: either (1) make the ratom family drive Freehand's repaint channel, or (2) state plainly that Freehand requires v/adapter and correct the two docstrings that say otherwise — in which case rf2-qgfo4 (a hiccup-capable Xray mount for element-shaped hosts) becomes the only route to Xray-over-Freehand and should be re-prioritised.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE (2026-07-26). No repair applied, as briefed. THE FINDING CHANGES THE DECISION — this is not "a combination nobody runs".

THE MECHANISM, NAMED: the absent function is reagent deref-capture on the acquired subscription Reaction. build-node-handle! (observation.cljc:1943-1978) installs add-watch then takes its baseline with a PLAIN @reaction. ITS OWN COMMENT ASSERTS "a watched reaction is live on the reactive hosts" — FALSE FOR THE RATOM FAMILY. reagent 2.0.1: -add-watch only RECORDS the callback; -deref outside *ratom-context* with auto-run nil runs f RAW, never through deref-capture, so `watching` stays nil; _queued-run requires (some? watching) — WHICH IS WHY reagent.core/flush MOVES NOTHING. The React-hook spine instead wires one watch PER SOURCE AT CONSTRUCTION. In a Reagent app THE RENDERER supplies the capture; a ViewCell is not a Reagent component, so nothing does.

EVIDENCE, and it answers the untested lead: three-adapter differential, one page, one build, shipped arms through the shipped fixture, adapter the only variable, TEN RUNS EACH, 10/10 IDENTICAL, zero page errors. Reagent pending=0 DOM stale; UIX pending=2 DOM MOVES; Freehand pending=2 DOM moves. SO THE SPLIT IS RATOM-FAMILY VERSUS REACT-HOOK-SPINE-FAMILY, not Freehand-versus-everyone. Then by intervention: one rx._run(false) on the Reagent arm flips watching nil->1 dep, pending 0->2, DOM 41->42. 10/10.

TWO VERIFICATIONS THAT COULD HAVE GONE THE OTHER WAY: Xray refuses UIx too (mount.cljs:216), so the bead "no host does both" HOLDS; and the Xray refusal set is THE SAME PARTITION as this bug — rf2-qgfo4 closes it for all four refused kinds, Repair A only for the Reagent pairing.

THE FINDING THAT INVERTS MY FRAMING: I told the operator no shipped application configures this and it was found only by building a testbed on purpose. TRUE OF APPLICATIONS, FALSE OF THE PRODUCT. docs/core/freehand/adoption.md IS A PUBLISHED GUIDE WHOSE ENTIRE PREMISE IS A MIXED HOST — four strategies, a rollout whose step 1 is "install Freehand next to the existing adapter". Under the single-adapter runtime, in a Reagent app, EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS A CELL THAT RENDERS ONCE AND NEVER REPAINTS, and the escape hatch does not exist because THE ADAPTER IS THE RENDERER. AN EXISTING REAGENT APPLICATION CANNOT ADOPT FREEHAND INCREMENTALLY BY ANY ROUTE TODAY.

The blessing was NEVER true for Reagent — introduced with the adapter in 1fc65ca878, and the fixture record says only "the UIx one".

RECOMMENDATION: B NOW IN ITS CORRECT FORM, A RULED SEPARATELY. The bead option (2) is TOO STRONG — "Freehand requires v/adapter" is false. The honest narrowing is "A CELL REQUIRES A PUSH-BASED DERIVED VALUE: Freehand, UIx, re-frame.ui." Eight assertion sites plus a spec sentence.

AND THE ONE-LINE FIX EXISTS AND IS NOT SHIPPABLE: :auto-run true in make-ratom-spine makes EVERY Reagent-hosted subscription recompute SYNCHRONOUSLY INSIDE THE app-db reset!. It was found and deliberately not applied.

THE OPERATOR QUESTION, and it is one question not more investigation: IS docs/core/freehand/adoption.md A COMMITMENT OR ASPIRATIONAL PROSE? If a commitment, Repair A has a real consumer and the worker lean is to keep the promise — it is smaller than I framed it: one late-bind hook (spec/006 sets that precedent), one make-ratom-spine implementation serving BOTH ratom adapters, two port call sites, and one genuine hazard (reagent disposes a Reaction when its last watch is removed). If aspirational, A has no consumer and B alone is complete.
