comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS (rf2-jt8vz, diagnosis-only dispatch, 2026-07-26 AUSEST). No repair applied. Full findings doc: ai/findings/2026-07-26.freehand-cell-under-ratom-adapter.md in worktree re-frame2-worktrees/mixed-host (the /ai/ tree is gitignored, so there is no PR — nothing tracked changed and the fence forbade a tracked change).

MECHANISM, NAMED. The absent function is reagent's `deref-capture` on the acquired subscription Reaction.
- cell.cljc:796 does `(obs/acquire! target (fn on-change [cause] (mark-dirty! cell cause)))`.
- observation.cljc:1943-1978 `build-node-handle!` installs `add-watch` on the reaction, then takes its baseline with a PLAIN `@reaction` (`observe-node!`). Its own comment asserts "a watched reaction is live on the reactive hosts". On the ratom family that is FALSE.
- ratom `make-derived-value` (spine.cljs:2846-2848) is a bare `ratom/make-reaction`, auto-run nil. reagent 2.0.1 ratom.cljs: `-add-watch` (:370) only records the callback; `-deref` (:461-478) outside `*ratom-context*` with auto-run nil runs `f` RAW, never through `deref-capture`, so `watching` stays nil; `_queued-run` (:419-421) requires `(some? watching)`, which is why `reagent.core/flush` moves nothing. reagent-slim's `reagent2.ratom` (:399-416) is the same shape.
- React-hook spine `make-derived-value-fn` (spine.cljs:585-846) instead wires ONE watch per source AT CONSTRUCTION (:793-800) — push-based from birth, no reader and no reactive context needed.
So the port's watch is real and the Reaction watches nothing. In a normal Reagent app the RENDERER supplies the capture (a component derefs the sub inside *ratom-context*). A ViewCell is not a Reagent component.
Pull still works: the non-reactive deref never clears `dirty?`, so `read-container` always returns current — which is why "Mount root" shows the moved count and why rf2-6pohj's mount-driven scenario is sound.

EVIDENCE (real Chromium, headless).
1. Three-adapter differential, ONE page / ONE build (out/browser-test), running the SHIPPED compiled_mount_dom_cljs_test arms (both-probes) through the SHIPPED test-support fixture with the adapter as the only variable. 10 runs each, 10/10 identical, zero page errors:
   reagent  -> pending-count 0, DOM stays 41 after cell/flush! AND reagent flush; reaction `watching` = nil
   uix      -> pending-count 2, DOM 42
   freehand -> pending-count 2, DOM 42
   => THE UNTESTED LEAD IS ANSWERED: UIx WORKS. The split is ratom-family vs React-hook-spine-family, not own-adapter vs foreign-adapter.
2. Intervention (runtime only, no source edit): same Reagent arm plus exactly one act, `rx._run(false)` (= deref-capture). 10/10: `watching` nil -> 1 dep (the app-db projection reaction), pending 0 -> 2, DOM 41 -> 42.

BLAST RADIUS. `obs/acquire!` has exactly two production callers: freehand/cell.cljc:796 and ui/reactive.cljc:3667 — both ViewCell substrates. The core's sub-cache invalidation does not route through `subscribe-container`, so nothing else consumes a derived container's WATCH surface; that is why no ordinary Reagent app notices. re-frame.ui cells on a ratom host have the same fault.

SPEC. spec/006 make-derived-value says "The derived container updates automatically when any source's value changes" and "subscribe-container works as on a base container". True of read-container, false of the watch surface => Reagent + reagent-slim are ALREADY non-conformant with 006 as written, on a surface only ViewCell substrates exercise.

WAS THE BLESSING EVER TRUE? No for Reagent; yes always for UIx; and no bridge ever existed. git log -S "stays legitimate for a mixed application" gives exactly two commits: 1fc65ca878 (feat(freehand): Freehand-owned React adapter on the core spine) introduced the adapter AND the blessing in the same commit, and 5728b74e27 only renamed adapter.cljs -> substrate.cljs. The same paragraph carries the true and the false half: substrate.cljs:11-12 says "had to install UIx OR REAGENT", while the fixture record release_app.cljs:88-93 says "used to install THE UIX ONE, and it had to". A UIx-only fact was generalised in prose; no commit ever had a Freehand fixture repaint under the Reagent adapter.

DOES ANYTHING SHIP IT? No shipped application — BUT the repo publishes a guide telling consumers to. examples/ui/minimal-counter installs v/adapter; every ratom-hosted example renders Reagent views; Story's Freehand presence suite seats v/adapter explicitly. The only mixed surface in the tree is tools/xray/testbeds/freehand_views/core.cljs:208, built the day before this bead, on purpose. HOWEVER docs/core/freehand/adoption.md ("Incremental adoption") opens "You already ship on Reagent or UIx ... can Freehand land next to what I have? Yes, with clear boundaries", names four strategies and a rollout whose step 1 is "Install Freehand next to the existing adapter". Under the single-adapter runtime every one of those, in a Reagent app, is a Freehand cell on the Reagent adapter. And the escape hatch does not exist: swapping such an app to UIx is not small, because the adapter IS the renderer. So today an existing Reagent application cannot adopt Freehand incrementally BY ANY ROUTE, and the published adoption path is unimplementable for half its stated audience (which is the whole re-frame v1 world).

STRUCTURAL FACT. Xray's refusal set is #{:rf.adapter/ui :rf.adapter/uix :rf.adapter/helix :rf.adapter/freehand} (mount.cljs:216) — the React-hook spine family. That is THE SAME PARTITION as this bug seen from the other side: the adapters that can drive a ViewCell are exactly the ones Xray's hiccup shell cannot mount into. So (a) this bead's headline "no single host does both" HOLDS — UIx does not rescue it, Xray refuses UIx too (verified, not assumed); (b) it is one partition, not two bugs; (c) rf2-qgfo4 closes the Xray side for all four refused kinds at once, whereas Repair A closes it only for the Reagent pairing and adds permanent contract surface.

REPAIR A COST (concrete). Bundle isolation forbids the port naming reagent, so the bridge must be a contract-level hook: (1) one OPTIONAL activation hook riding the LATE-BIND table — spec/006 already sets that precedent for :adapter/derived-container? "so the ten-fn adapter contract shape is unchanged", which lowers this cost materially; (2) ONE implementation, in make-ratom-spine, injected as a bare fn exactly like :r-atom / :make-reaction, serving Reagent AND reagent-slim; every other adapter implements nothing (absent hook = skip), so React-hook spine / plain-atom / SSR are untouched; (3) two call sites in observation (build-node-handle! + release!); (4) THE REAL WORK: reagent's Reaction.-remove-watch (ratom.cljs:371-377) DISPOSES the reaction when its last watch is removed, which must be reconciled with the sub-cache's ref-counting and its evict-before-interop/dispose! ordering that node-still-canonical? reads; (5) spec/006 wording + cross-adapter tests.
THE ONE-LINE FIX EXISTS AND I DID NOT APPLY IT: (make-reaction ... :auto-run true) in make-ratom-spine (reagent's make-reaction takes it, ratom.cljs:523-535) does fix the notification. It is NOT shippable — auto-run true makes _handle-change run the reaction synchronously inside the app-db reset!, so every re-frame2 subscription under Reagent recomputes eagerly, discarding the batching the spine's own comment relies on. Cheap version != correct version.

REPAIR B COST. Eight assertion sites: freehand.cljc:828-830 (the PUBLIC v/adapter docstring), substrate.cljs:11-12 and :31-35, docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md:208 (mirror), docs/core/freehand/adoption.md (the WHOLE page), tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md:305-306, tools/xray/testbeds/freehand_views/core.cljs:23-40 + :88-91 (its BOOT comment at :165-179 is already correct), implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1754-1756. release_app.cljs:88-93 stays TRUE (it names UIx) — no change. Two things narrowing also has to reach: spec/006 make-derived-value would still assert push semantics the ratom family does not deliver; and the bead's option (2) as worded is TOO STRONG — "Freehand requires v/adapter" is false, since UIx and re-frame.ui both work. The honest narrowing is "a Freehand cell requires a PUSH-BASED derived value: the React-hook spine family (Freehand, UIx, re-frame.ui); the ratom family supplies the container but not the notification."

RECOMMENDATION. Do B NOW in its correct (push-based, not v/adapter-only) form — it is true today and it stops a public docstring and a published guide promising something the substrate cannot do. Then rule on A SEPARATELY, and not from inside this bead: the bug is a testbed curiosity, but docs/core/freehand/adoption.md is a promise to every existing Reagent app, i.e. the whole v1 world, and A is that promise's implementation. My lean is keep the promise (B now, A next) — Freehand's EP-0036 case is that it is adoptable, and an adoption story that requires a whole-app renderer swap first is not one.

FALSIFIER. Overturned if incremental adoption from a REAGENT host is not a story Mike intends to support — i.e. if docs/core/freehand/adoption.md is aspirational prose rather than a commitment. Then the shipped-consumer evidence collapses to "nothing ships this", A has no consumer, and B alone is complete: retract the adoption page, narrow the docstrings, close A, let rf2-qgfo4 own the Xray gap. The check is ONE question to Mike, not more investigation: is docs/core/freehand/adoption.md a promise? Secondary/weaker falsifier: if the disposal hazard above turns out not to be containable without racing subs.cache's evict-before-dispose ordering, A's cost estimate is wrong; an A-worker should prove that first.

ALSO WORTH FIXING when the ruling lands (already noted in the merged-PR audit above): tools/xray/testbeds/freehand_views/core.cljs:128 says pressing + advances readout's committed generation — it does not on this host, and cell/generation is the hot-reload body revision anyway.

title: SIXTH resource-family leak: a read FAILURE continuation egresses the decoded error body raw, and both remedies have a named trap
description:
Found and MEASURED by the rf2-xx4ty worker while fixing the fifth leak, deliberately not fixed because it is a genuine ruling rather than a repair.

THE LEAK: a read FAILURE continuation :error envelope egresses raw on the same two carriers, at [... :rf.fx/args 1 :error :body :detail]. That is THE DECODED FAILURE BODY — and error-envelope-slot own docstring says it "routinely echoes the SUBMITTED FORM FIELDS". So the datum is user input coming back out, which makes this at least as sensitive as the response body just fixed.

WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY TAKE THE ARM THAT FIXED THE FIFTH LEAK, and this is the ruling:
  - OWNER-CONDITIONAL is wrong: on family rows :error is UNCONDITIONAL, so an owner-conditional arm here would make the two carriers DISAGREE — the exact rf2-irwsq shape, in mirror image, and the thing the fifth-leak worker specifically avoided.
  - UNCONDITIONAL is also wrong: :error is an FX-FAMILY WORD. The fifth leak established that :params and :value are words the fx family uses for its own data (an app managed-HTTP args carry {:request {... :params {...}}}, and [:rf.resource/commit-generation {:value 1}] rides the same effect vector). A name-only unconditional arm would over-redact ordinary fx payloads.

SO THE TWO OBVIOUS REMEDIES EACH BREAK A DIFFERENT INVARIANT. The fifth leak escaped this because the sibling :resource/key made the names safe to read; establish whether the failure continuation carries an equivalent discriminator before designing anything.

A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME WORKER, recorded here rather than filed separately: a resource projection-relative :sensitive declaration has NO READ-CONTINUATION ANALOGUE. {:sensitive [[:data :email]]} with no coarse :sensitive? is :serialize, so its reply rides verbatim. That is consistent with the rest of the family, but reads have no counterpart to the mutations redact-continuation-reply. Source-side, different surface, probably its own bead.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS THE SIXTH: wd9im (map-only fail-closed default), 5o52l (reversible plaintext key-ids), 1kiuj (18 raw paths under :rf.fx/args), 1zc33 (:scope on five row types), 425mm (free :scope inside the carrier), xx4ty (:value and :params on the reply). Every one was found by a worker, none by a gate. The conformance fixture cannot see this class either — it drives no :reply-to, never replays an HTTP reply, and harvests on op namespace while these rows are rf.fx.

DO NOT DISPATCH AS A REPAIR. Return a recommendation with the discriminator named, or the concrete failure if no discriminator exists.
notes:
INVESTIGATION COMPLETE (read-only run, 2026-07-26 23:15 AUSEST). Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-rnsv2.resource-error-egress-remedy.md. NO CODE CHANGED, bead stays OPEN — the fix is decided, not done.

VERDICT: ARM (a) — the discriminator EXISTS and needs no emission. It is :rf.reply/work-kind, already read by resource-reply? at trace_egress.cljc:471-481 and already the gate on the fifth leak's :value/:params arm. reply/base-reply (reply.cljc:192-222) stamps it BEFORE the status branch, so failure-reply (:236-260) carries it on both :status :error and :status :cancelled. The bead asked for a ':resource/key-equivalent' discriminator; the marker is strictly better — rf2-1kiuj audit #7059 already proved a bare sibling :resource/key is a CLASSIFICATION handle, not a RECOGNITION proof, and replaced it with this marker. Nothing surprising; no escalation.

GRAIN: marker-gated, UNCONDITIONAL inside the marker. That is what keeps the two carriers in agreement — error-envelope-slot (trace_egress.cljc:183-199) is consumed unconditionally on the family's own rows at :925-928.

THE NAMED TRAP: :error must NOT be added to reply-payload-slot (:258-283). That set is consumed at :832-833 under (and owner-redacts? ...) — a one-token edit that LOOKS like reusing the proven pattern and in fact implements the explicitly-rejected OWNER-CONDITIONAL remedy. It must be a separate arm of the entry cond. Sub-traps: :status is not the gate (an abort settles :cancelled and still carries :error); :page-error is a ROW spelling, the reply always spells it :error; guard redacted-token? before redact-value; hoist the marker read out of owner-redacts?.

SEVENTH LEAK FOUND, CLOSE IT IN THE SAME ARM: the MUTATION continuation reply leaks :error identically. classification/redact-continuation-reply (classification.cljc:255-301) re-roots only :value/:params/:scope and never :error (correctly — :error is a transport envelope, not a projection of owner data), and the mutation reply stamps :rf.reply/work-kind :mutation so resource-reply? is false and nothing looks at it. :rf.mutation/failed (mutation_events.cljc:2137-2139) tokenizes the same envelope on the row. So gate the new arm on the FAMILY's two work kinds #{:resource :mutation} (reply.cljc:108-118) — NOT (some? :rf.reply/work-kind), because managed HTTP stamps :http (http/reply.cljc:172) and is not ours.

SHARPEST EVIDENCE: on failed-handler's branch the settle row (events.cljc:2757-2761) stamps NO :error at all, so the fx carrier is the ONLY off-box copy of the envelope and it is raw. On :rf.resource/failed (events.cljc:3248-3252), :rf.resource/page-failed (:3294-3298) and :rf.mutation/failed the row copy IS tokenized while the carrier copy is raw — the literal rf2-irwsq disagreement. The envelope arrives unredacted: transport dispatch-failure! (http/transport.cljc:475-497) hands the raw failure to :on-failure; privacy/prepare-emit-failure only touches HTTP's own trace row.

SECOND (SMALLER) FINDING ON THIS BEAD — ALREADY CLOSED, NO ACTION. It was carved out as rf2-ko5lm and shipped in PR #7092 (f1887d5602, merged 1b18ad8ea0, 2026-07-26 18:31) as redact-reply-declarations (trace_egress.cljc:483-557), with the infinite-feed index-free follow-up as rf2-zaopo (d89df15e48). Residues rf2-dl7bz (open P3) and rf2-zaopo (closed) were filed rather than absorbed. The bead text predates that merge.

FOLLOW-ON FILED: rf2-uufoe (P2) — the continuation-reply egress gate drives only the SUCCESS settle. epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj has ZERO ':status :error' drives, and epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:621-631 says in its own prose it drives no :reply-to and replays no reply. Four settle branches fan out continuations nobody has projected. Sequence AFTER rnsv2's fix (same test file).

FIX DISPATCH: one file (trace_egress.cljc) + one test file (epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj). JVM gates only (implementation/epoch + implementation/resources 'clojure -M:test'). Full executable sketch in the dossier section 5, including the anti-owner-conditional control test that fails if someone re-implements the rejected remedy.

title: a :sensitive? resource's :value and :params egress RAW on the fx carriers via a :reply-to read continuation
description:
FOUND BY rf2-425mm while fixing the free :scope on the same two carriers. Reproduced against the MERGED rf2-425mm fix (PR #7054), so this is what REMAINS after it, not something it caused.

THE LEAK. EP-0016 D1 read continuations (rf2-p1yri7): an `ensure` / `refetch` MAY carry a call-site `:reply-to`. When the read completes, `re-frame.resources.events/read-continuation-reply` augments the canonical reply with the resource's TOP-LEVEL read facts and `re-frame.reply/complete` APPENDS that map as the final argument of the target's event vector, which the runtime dispatches via `[:dispatch <ev>]` in its :fx. So the map rides :rf.fx/args (the dispatch fx) and :rf.event/fx (the whole effect vector) — the same two carriers rf2-1kiuj and rf2-425mm addressed.

`read-continuation-reply` (events.cljc ~L235) assocs, from the scoped key it just destructured:

  :resource     <resource-id>
  :params       <canonical params>   <- LEAKS
  :scope        <resolved scope>     <- fixed by rf2-425mm
  :resource/key <scoped-key>         <- fixed by rf2-1kiuj
  :cache-hit?   <bool>

plus the canonical reply's `:value` — the resource's DECODED RESPONSE BODY. <- LEAKS

VERIFIED, post-rf2-425mm, through the public `epoch/projected-record`. A record whose :rf.fx/args is `[:app/loaded {:status :ok :value {:email \"topsecret-PII@example.com\"} :resource :derived/profile :params {:slug \"topsecret-PII\"} :scope [:rf.scope/session {:username \"topsecret-PII\"}] :resource/key <sk> :cache-hit? true}]` for a REGISTERED :sensitive? owner projects with :resource/key and :scope correctly tokenized and leaks at exactly:

  [:trace-events 0 :tags :rf.fx/args 1 :value  :email]
  [:trace-events 0 :tags :rf.fx/args 1 :params :slug]

WHY IT SURVIVES rf2-425mm. `project-embedded-keys` descends maps and speaks only for what the resource family PLANTED in the carrier — scoped keys, and (rf2-425mm) the free :scope. :params and :value are neither. The descend-don't-tokenize posture is correct and must stay (rf2-1kiuj: tokenizing a foreign payload wholesale would redact a PLAIN owner's request map), so this is a third named datum, not a change of rule.

WHY THIS ONE IS OWNER-CONDITIONAL, UNLIKE :scope. rf2-425mm's :scope arm is UNCONDITIONAL because the family's own rows classify a free :scope unconditionally (rf2-1zc33 — `off-box-plain-owner-free-scope-map-fails-closed-key-rides-verbatim`), and the two carriers must agree. :params and :value are different: they belong to a NAMED owner, the reply map carries that owner's `:resource/key` one slot over, and the family's own rows tokenize an owner's params iff `whole-entry-disposition` is non-:serialize. So the right grain here is `cursor-slot`'s — read the row's owner from the sibling :resource/key and tokenize iff it redacts — which keeps a PLAIN resource's reply fully readable. `row-owner-redacts?` already exists and does exactly this; it just does not run inside the carrier walk.

SCOPE NOTE. The mutation `:reply-to` (`mutation_events.cljc` `continuation-reply`) is the sibling shape and should be checked in the same pass.

NOT A REGRESSION and NOT rf2-425mm's to fix: that bead's acceptance criterion is the resolved IDENTITY at zero paths, which it meets. This is the same carrier, a different datum, and a different classification question.
close_reason:
PR #7115 (worker/res-egress-lane2, a7d13bc27f + 8bb3b0c60e).

FIRST FINDING, and it changes what this bead was: the repair this bead ASKS FOR is already on main and has been since 96c2867a55 ('tokenize a :reply-to read continuation's :value + :params on the fx carriers'), refined by rf2-1kiuj audit #7059 (the arm now gates on the reply's own canonical marker :rf.reply/work-kind :resource, not on a sibling :resource/key) and extended by rf2-ko5lm (the owner's DECLARED projection-relative paths, via the mutation half's redact-continuation-reply). [:vector :string] owner: 11 leaking paths on the async settle and 7 on the fresh-skip cache hit, spanning :work/id on the family's own rows, :rf.fx/args, and :rf.event/fx. Closed by the sibling commit's one-predicate repair (see rf2-wd9im); this commit is the acceptance + adversarial coverage, including the fail-closed arm named? exists for (an UNREGISTERED owner's non-map-params key under the reserved :resource/key must redact inside a carrier).

title: a :sensitive? resource with a {:from-db} scope egresses its RESOLVED IDENTITY MAP raw at 4 fx-args paths of a real ensure record
description:
FOUND BY rf2-0t7o8 (the epoch MCP-egress fixture widening) while inhabiting the resource cascade with an identity-bearing scope. Reported, deliberately NOT fixed there, per that bead's don't-widen / don't-touch-resources fence.

THE LEAK, verified against current main. Register a `:sensitive?` resource whose `:scope` is a `{:from-db <resolver-id>}` named-resolver reference, register the resolver so it derives `[:rf.scope/session {:username "topsecret-do-not-leak"}]` from an app-db read, then dispatch ONE real `[:rf.resource/ensure …]`. `projected-record` over the record that `ensure` settles egresses the resolver's IDENTITY MAP in the clear at exactly four paths:

  [:trace-events 10 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-success 1 :scope 1 :username]
  [:trace-events 10 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-failure 1 :scope 1 :username]
  [:trace-events 11 :tags :rf.event/fx 2 1 :on-success 1 :scope 1 :username]
  [:trace-events 11 :tags :rf.event/fx 2 1 :on-failure 1 :scope 1 :username]

WHY IT IS THERE. An `ensure` lowers into `:rf.http/managed`, and `re-frame.resources.events` builds that fx's continuation payload with the resolved scope in it (`{:work/id … :resource/key <scoped-key> :scope <scope> :generation … :rf.frame/id …}` — the stale-suppression verification payload the internal reply handlers check). `re-frame.fx/handle-one-fx` stamps the whole argument payload under `:rf.fx/args`, and `do-fx` stamps the whole effect vector under `:rf.event/fx`. So the resolved scope reaches off-box egress inside the fx carriers.

TWO CORRECT DECISIONS MEETING. `project-fx-args-egress` → `project-embedded-keys` walks those carriers by SHAPE and, unlike the family-row default `project-unknown-slot-value`, DELIBERATELY does not tokenize a map — an fx-args payload belongs to the fx family and tokenizing it wholesale would redact a PLAIN owner's request map (rf2-1kiuj's own docstring says so, and it is right). And rf2-1zc33 gave the free `:scope` tag to the shape-driven default — but only on rows the FAMILY projector runs over (`resource-family-op?`), which `:rf.fx/*` rows are not. Between the two, a free `:scope` slot sitting inside a continuation event's arg map on an fx row is reached by NOBODY.

IT IS THE rf2-1zc33 SHAPE ONE CARRIER FURTHER OUT, and it has rf2-1kiuj's signature too: on the SAME record the scoped key one slot over — `:on-success` position 1's `:resource/key` — tokenizes correctly, so the identical identity is redacted and leaked side by side, and the structured `:effects[*].args` twin reads `:rf/redacted`.

WHY NO EXISTING FIXTURE SAW IT: every resource in every epoch-egress fixture is `:rf.scope/global`. A global scope is a SCALAR — there is nothing in it to leak — so the carriers have never had an identity-bearing scope in them. Only a `{:from-db …}` resolver puts one there.

REPRODUCTION: on the rf2-0t7o8 branch, add back to `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` a `(rf/reg-resource :secret/session-article {:scope {:from-db :mcp/session} :sensitive? true :params-schema [:map [:slug :string]]} …)` and one `[:rf.resource/ensure {:resource :secret/session-article :params {:slug \"…\"} :owner resource-owner}]` in `drive-resource-family!`. `forwarder-projected-record-leaks-no-raw-resource-family-bytes` reds with the four paths above, named. That fixture stops deliberately short of the shape and says so in `drive-resource-family!`'s docstring; when this is fixed, add the ensure back — the widened cascade is one dispatch away from covering it.

WHAT TO WEIGH WHEN FIXING: the answer is probably NOT to tokenize maps in `project-embedded-keys` (that is the over-redaction rf2-1kiuj rejected). A `:scope`-slot-aware arm inside the carrier walk, or reaching the scope through the ROW's already-resolved owner classification the way the `cursor-slot` rule does, both look closer to the grain. Whatever it is, the two-sided control applies: a PLAIN owner's request map and a `:rf.scope/global` scope must still ride verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: epoch/projected-record over a REAL ensure using a :sensitive? resource with a {:from-db <resolver-id>} scope contains the raw resolved identity at ZERO paths across the whole record: both :resource/key and the sibling :scope inside on-success/on-failure under :rf.fx/args and :rf.event/fx are classified consistently. The pre-fix implementation makes the gate red at all four named paths. A plain owner request map and :rf.scope/global scope still ride verbatim, while the trusted-local :include-sensitive? opt-in still exposes the raw values intentionally.
notes:
WORKER (rf2-425mm, PR #7054, merged 76621e8b9e): fixed in `project-embedded-keys` — a `:scope`-keyed value inside an fx carrier now takes the FAMILY rule (`project-unknown-slot-value`) rather than the carrier walk, so the two carriers of one scope agree by construction. NOT a residual of rf2-1zc33 (that repair is consumed by `project-tags*`, routed by `resource-family-op?`, which never runs on `rf.fx` rows); it is rf2-1kiuj's bounded completeness remainder.

Two of this bead's suggestions corrected: (1) the alternative 'reach the scope through the ROW's owner classification the way `cursor-slot` does' must NOT be taken — `cursor-slot` is owner-CONDITIONAL while rf2-1zc33 made the free `:scope` fail closed UNCONDITIONALLY on family rows, so owner-routing here would make the two carriers disagree for a plain owner. (2) The arm keys on `:scope` alone, NOT on a sibling `:resource/key`, because a mutation execute's continuation payload carries a free `:scope` with no scoped key beside it.

Proof: reverting one token reds the acceptance arm naming THIS BEAD'S FOUR PATHS byte-for-byte at indices 10/11. RED and GREEN both 495 tests / 6665 assertions, differing only in 7 failures. Two-sided control green in both directions. Gates: epoch 495/6665 rc=0, resources 733/6799 rc=0, core 2115/10462 rc=0, test-fast-pr.sh PASS rc=0.

CONFORMANCE FIXTURE: cannot see these rows — `drive-resource-family!` deliberately drives no session-scoped ensure and says so, naming this bead. Its follow-on ('add the ensure here') is now unblocked (rf2-0t7o8).

FILED: rf2-xx4ty (P1) — same two carriers, different datum: a `:reply-to` read continuation's reply map egresses a :sensitive? owner's `:value` and `:params` raw. Verified post-fix.
close_reason:
PR #7054 MERGED (76621e8b9e), blobs verified byte-identical to the pushed tip.

THE QUESTION I ASKED FIRST, ANSWERED DECISIVELY: yes the {:from-db} scope HAS RESOLVED before egress, and no, rf2-1zc33 could not cover it. DISTINCT MECHANISM, NOT A RESIDUAL. rf2-1zc33 changed sibling-owned-slot, which is consumed by project-tags*, which the epoch tool-pair routes BY OPERATION NAMESPACE via resource-family-op? — and the leaking rows are rf.fx, so that projector NEVER RUNS ON THEM whatever sibling-owned-slot says. The leak lives in project-embedded-keys, the SLOT-reached carrier walk rf2-1kiuj added. It is THAT bead bounded completeness remainder: rf2-1kiuj taught the carriers about scoped keys and nothing else, while the runtime plants a second family datum — the free :scope — in the same continuation payload.

AND THE FIX INVENTS NO FIFTH MECHANISM, which is what I asked for: a :scope-keyed value inside the carrier now takes the SAME family rule rf2-1zc33 gave the same slot on the family own rows (project-unknown-slot-value), so the two carriers agree BY CONSTRUCTION the way the two carriers of one key already did. One arm, ~8 lines.

TWO OF THE BEAD OWN DETAILS CORRECTED, and the first would have caused a regression: its second suggested repair — "reach the scope through the ROW owner classification the way cursor-slot does" — MUST NOT BE TAKEN. cursor-slot is owner-CONDITIONAL, but rf2-1zc33 made the free :scope fail closed UNCONDITIONALLY on family rows, and its own test off-box-plain-owner-free-scope-map-fails-closed-key-rides-verbatim IS that ruling. Owner-routing here would make the two carriers DISAGREE for a plain owner — the rf2-irwsq shape in mirror image. Second: the arm keys on :scope ALONE and not on a sibling :resource/key, because a mutation execute continuation payload carries a free :scope with NO scoped key beside it — GATING ON THE SIBLING WOULD HAVE FIXED READS AND LEFT MUTATIONS LEAKING.

PROOF: reverting one token reds the acceptance arm naming the bead FOUR PATHS BYTE-FOR-BYTE at the bead own indices 10/11. RED AND GREEN ARE BOTH 495 TESTS / 6665 ASSERTIONS, DIFFERING ONLY IN 7 FAILURES — the rf2-1zc33 structural technique matched, which makes the applied-mutation check structural rather than a separate step. Two-sided control green in both directions.

THE CONFORMANCE FIXTURE CANNOT SEE THESE ROWS, DELIBERATELY, AND SAYS SO ITSELF: drive-resource-family! docstring already records that it drives no session-scoped ensure, names this bead as the reason, and ends "When rf2-425mm lands, add the ensure here." That follow-on (rf2-0t7o8) is now unblocked — a fixture that documents its own blind spot with the bead that will close it is the right pattern.

title: P1 CANDIDATE: under the documented production gate -Dre-frame.debug=false, dispatch-sync never runs its handler
description:
Found by the rf2-l260n worker while profiling, and NOT diagnosed further — it was outside that bead scope and it escalated rather than absorbing it. Filed at P1 because if it reproduces it means the DOCUMENTED PRODUCTION CONFIGURATION does not dispatch.

THE OBSERVATION, verbatim from the report: under -Dre-frame.debug=false — which SECURITY.md documents as the production setting, "SSR / long-running JVMs set false" — a plain dispatch-sync NEVER RUNS ITS HANDLER. handler-runs = 0, app-db unchanged, :rf.error/no-such-handler emitted — WHILE THE ROUTER OWN resolve-handler RETURNS THE HANDLER AT THAT SAME MOMENT. drain-test under the flag: 34 failures / 40 assertions.

WHY THAT LAST CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE FINDING: resolve-handler finds it and the dispatch does not run it. So this is not a registration problem — something between resolution and invocation is gated on the debug flag. A registry lookup succeeding while the invocation reports no-such-handler is a contradiction that should be impossible.

CORROBORATION, and the reason it was noticed at all: the l260n and sj5s7 beads both recorded "debug off" counts (95/88/82) that DO NOT REPRODUCE TODAY. That is consistent with the debug-off path having changed under them.

FIRST STEPS, in this order, and do not skip the first: ESTABLISH WHETHER THIS REPRODUCES OUTSIDE THE TEST HARNESS. A dispatch-sync in a drain-test fixture may be exercising a path a real production boot does not, and the gate may be doing something legitimate that only looks catastrophic through that harness. If it reproduces on a plain boot with the flag set, this is a release blocker and should be re-priorityed accordingly. If it only reproduces under the harness, the finding is that the harness and the flag disagree — still real, much smaller.

DO NOT FIX BEFORE DIAGNOSING. :rf.error/no-such-handler being emitted while resolve-handler succeeds means the two disagree about what "registered" means; converging them without understanding which is right would be picking a side, and this repo has a documented case today where exactly that would have deleted a real distinction across three artefacts.

CONTEXT WORTH HAVING: goog-define-style compile-time gates are used deliberately here — re-frame.performance/enabled? is a goog-define so Closure can dead-code-eliminate the instrumentation, and a proposed runtime toggle was DECLINED in favour of that. If the debug flag is the same shape, then a JVM -D property and a CLJS goog-define may not mean the same thing on the two hosts, which would be a plausible mechanism.
notes:
FIX FOR THE AUDIT REOPEN: PR #7176 (branch worker/reproj-race-9c2jf), opened 2026-07-28.

REPRODUCED FIRST, then fixed. The audit's barrier reproduction is now a committed regression test — implementation/core/test/re_frame/reprojection_install_race_jvm_test.clj, two deterministic with-redefs barrier tests. RED pre-fix at commit 50de1b4 (exit 1, 6 failures / 17 assertions): the contender observed {:hook? false :mark? false :flush? false}, handler-runs 0, (:late (app-db-value :audit/b)) nil — the permanently stale frame, exactly as recorded. GREEN post-fix at be6aeb3 (exit 0, 2 tests / 17 assertions). Test 1 parks the elected installer at the FIRST side effect (the registrar hook) and pins the full stale-frame end state; test 2 parks at the LAST (:live-frame/flush-projection!, whose twin :live-frame/mark-projection-dirty! is the registrar REMOVAL late-bind), covering the removal twin the reopen asked for.

THE ORDERING FIX: the whole once-body — flag read, three side effects, flag write — is ONE critical section under a new reprojection-install-lock (JVM monitor), and the flag is published LAST. CAS elected an installer but did not make losers WAIT; locking makes a concurrent caller either do the install or BLOCK until the elected installer finished it. Publish-last also makes the install failure-atomic (a throw leaves the flag false and the next make-frame retries). Deadlock-free by construction: the body runs three bookkeeping swap!s, no user code, no other monitor (notably NOT projection-flush-lock), no re-entry into make-frame; the monitor is released before make-frame does anything else. title: story-mcp register-variant returns a -32603 Server fault (not the tool error) on any schema-violating body: malli :explain is not JSON-encodable
description:
Found while proving rf2-jquiy's relay end to end at the REAL story-mcp JSON-RPC boundary.

REPRO (server/handle-frame!, allow-writes on):
  tools/call register-variant {:variant-id "story.button/x" :body {:compnent :some/view}}

WHAT THE CLIENT GETS:
  Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: class malli.core$_and_schema$reify$reify__4930

CHAIN:
  registrar/validate-shape! throws with the full malli :explain in ex-data
  (registrar.cljc, ':explain explain' slot). The :explain map carries LIVE
  malli schema objects (reified malli.core/Schema), not data.
  -> write.cljc register-or-error copies it onward:
       (select-keys (ex-data e) [:rf.error :explain])
     into the error-result's :structuredContent.
  -> cheshire hits the reified schema object and throws.
  -> that throw escapes the tool handler INTO server.cljc handle-frame!,
     which converts it to a protocol-level -32603 internal error.

CONSEQUENCE: the single most common authoring mistake an agent makes through
the write surface — a typo'd or wrong-shaped variant body — produces NO
diagnostic at all. The agent gets a transport-level fault with a malli class
name in it. The actionable :reason (which names the offending key and the
nearest declared slot, via unknown-key-reason) never leaves the JVM. It also
means the tool's own 'isError: true' contract is bypassed for this case.

STRICTLY WORSE than the bare-keyword message rf2-jquiy fixed, and it MASKS it:
rf2-jquiy made validate-shape!'s ex-message conformant, but a client calling
register-variant still cannot see it, because the response never gets built.

NOT fixed in rf2-jquiy (out of that bead's scope — that bead is the thrown
MESSAGE shape; this is ex-DATA wire-encodability).

LIKELY FIX: :explain must be projected to data before it crosses the wire.
malli.core/explain output is only wire-safe after (me/humanize) or an
equivalent schema->form pass; the raw :schema entries are objects. Either
project at the throw site (registrar) or refuse to relay :explain at the
write.cljc / recorder.cljc select-keys. Check recorder.cljc:128 too — same
select-keys, same fault.
close_reason:
PR #7042 — the P1 ergonomics defect on the AI-authoring surface.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced at the REAL JSON-RPC boundary as briefed: registrar/validate-shape! puts the raw Malli explain map in ex-data, and its :schema entries are LIVE REIFIED malli.core/Schema OBJECTS. The write handlers copied that slot into :structuredContent, cheshire threw on it inside protocol/write-frame!, and the throw escaped PAST the tool handler into server/handle-frame!, which answered -32603.

THE FIX USES EXISTING VOCABULARY, which is exactly what I asked for ("look for existing practice first"): one function, tools.result/wire-safe-ex-data, swapping :explain for :explain-humanized — the malli.error/humanize projection. spec/010-Schemas.md section humanize hook ALREADY defines that slot for precisely this value, so no new vocabulary was invented. It also stops the write surface error slot colliding with explain-variant unrelated plan-:explain. No new :rf.error/* id, so the keyword-catalogue gate stayed untouched and the fenced spec/009 was never needed.

THE PATTERN WAS THREE SITES, NOT THE TWO THE BEAD NAMED. tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:388 relays the WHOLE ex-data under :data in invoke-tool belt-and-braces catch. The worker description of it is the clearest statement of the defect: THE CATCH THAT EXISTS TO STOP A HANDLER THROW BECOMING A PROTOCOL FAULT, BECOMING ONE. All three now route through the helper. Reachability was CHECKED rather than assumed — only register-variant is reachable through the shipped tool surface today.

THE BOUNDARY PROOF CONFIRMS THE MASKING CLAIM, which we had only hypothesised. Before: -32603 Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: malli.core$_and_schema$reify$reify__4930. After: isError: true carrying RF2-JQUIY MESSAGE — so that sibling improvement really was invisible until this landed — plus structuredContent {"explain-humanized":{"compnent":["disallowed key"]}}. The mistyped key now produces the diagnostic an author needs.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, with the mutation CONFIRMED APPLIED via git diff --stat before any verdict was read: helper reverted to a pass-through gives 15 failures / 5 errors / rc=1 and the probe returns the fault; restored blob byte-identical to the committed one. And the two-sided control STAYED GREEN UNDER THE MUTATION — the worker notes that is what makes it a control rather than part of the gate.

ANOTHER DOCUMENTED CLAIM THAT WAS NOT KEPT: tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md already promised isError: true on a schema violation, and until this branch THE PROMISE WAS FALSE. Now pinned.

FILED NOT FIXED — rf2-2nbck (P3): the same select-keys harvests :rf.error while the registrar throws :rf.error/id, so that arm HAS NEVER FIRED and the structured error-id slot has never been populated on these paths. The canonical token still rides the message.

Gates rc=0, re-derived: story-mcp 298/1562 (+6), mcp-base 272/924, story 1847/6824, wire-vocab 100/1069, test:story and test:flag-gates conformance green, gen --check in sync, six python gates silent.

title: Bounded production-browser comparison: interpreted vs compiled Hiccup, with a keep/demote/remove recommendation
description:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26), quoted verbatim — this bead exists to execute the measurement half of it:

  "Reopen whether compiled Hiccup earns its permanent product cost. Pause discretionary compiler expansion
   and .182.6; common/interpreted correctness continues. D022 may use its already-accepted source-located
   compiled refusal rather than expanding lowering. Run one bounded production-browser comparison of
   interpreted versus compiled, including cell elision and bundle reachability, then return a keep/demote/
   remove recommendation. Profile before optimizing the interpreter. Do not build another syntax
   experiment."

THE DELIVERABLE IS A RECOMMENDATION: keep / demote / remove. Not a fix, not an optimisation, not a verb.

SCOPE — ONE bounded comparison, in a PRODUCTION BROWSER, covering at minimum:
  - interpreted versus compiled Hiccup on the same view
  - CELL ELISION — what the compiled tier actually elides that the interpreted tier does not
  - BUNDLE REACHABILITY — what each tier drags into an :advanced bundle

HARD BOUNDARIES from the ruling: do NOT build another syntax experiment (v/$ is settled as a non-goal — see rf2-drpa3.182.2 and docs/design/freehand/studio/er-01-architecture-comparison.md). Do NOT optimise the interpreter as part of this; PROFILE FIRST, and any optimisation is a separate bead after the recommendation lands.

WHY NOW: the ER-01 spike measured allocation on the JVM structural emitter and put compiled at 1.000 against interpreted 1.244, but stated plainly that the REACT HOST WAS NOT MEASURED and named that as the one avenue that could reopen the performance half. This bead measures that avenue.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, learned expensively in this repo:
  - Wall-clock is unreliable here under concurrent load — the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns in two JVMs. The ER-01 spike used getThreadAllocatedBytes and got min = p50 = max in nearly every arm. Prefer allocation; quote wall-clock only as a direction WITH the observed spread stated. That spike refused to give a wall-clock percentage because a 7-point spread on a 5-point effect does not support one — copy that refusal.
  - For BUNDLE questions, two naive oracles are both wrong: counting goog.DEBUG fails (225 occurrences survived a release where the surface was fully eliminated — docstrings carried in by var reification) and grepping function names fails for small functions (Closure inlines them). STRING LITERALS are the reliable sentinel, and a two-bundle control is INSUFFICIENT — you need a THIRD bundle with the tier absent, or a sibling namespace vocabulary reads as a survivor.
  - Interleave arms, clear the cache before each build, and state the method before the numbers.

DO NOT COMMIT THE SCAFFOLDING. The ER-01 worker committed its four measurement arms so an outage could not lose them, then DELETED them before the PR, and proved the deletion took the scaffolding and nothing else by showing the CLJS delta was exactly its one parity deftest. Copy that.
notes:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26) — KEEP, on a DIFFERENT rationale from the report. Quoted verbatim:

  "We will keep the compiler because there will be performance critical applications not seen yet,
   where 3x performance is essential."

HOW THIS RELATES TO THE REPORT VERDICT. The report also said KEEP, but explicitly on ELISION grounds and with the headline "stop describing it as a performance tier". The operator keeps it FOR performance, on the unseen-application argument. Both land on KEEP; the rationale differs, and the operator rationale governs.

THE MEASURED BASIS FOR THE 3x, so nobody later treats it as folklore: compiled beats the TUNED interpreter 3.35x on 300 SUB-FREE boundaries, 1.22x on 100 REACTIVE ones, and is INSEPARABLE on an ordinary form (1.054, spread straddling 1.0). Updates were a null result on every arm. So the 3x is real and is specific to the sub-free-boundary shape — which is precisely the shape a performance-critical application would exhibit. The operator argument is that such applications exist but are not yet in the corpus, and no measurement here can refute that: every witness in the repo is one we chose.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO. It does not retire the report other findings, which stand as measured: no application in the repo declares a compiled view; Xray reads the DONOR compiler; Story consumer is test-only; MCP manifest read serves interpreted views too; and the best defect the analyzer once caught exclusively is no longer exclusive because the fix taught the interpreter to refuse it too. Those remain true and remain the reason the non-elision parts of the tier are unpriced.

STILL LIVE AND STILL THE OPERATOR CALL: the report named the single change most likely to undermine KEEP — an opt-in {:reactive false} CHECKED rather than proven, which would take most of the measured advantage at a fraction of the cost. Under the new rationale that option is MORE interesting, not less: if a checked flag delivers the 3x for performance-critical applications without the compiler permanent cost, the unseen-application argument would point at it instead. Uninvestigated.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7032 (merge 6c35e4ec9b4d6551e255dc5e3f7c22d50a111f45, merged 2026-07-25T21:45:28Z) — exact owner reopened; no duplicate. Completeness: the requested production-browser report, three realistic witnesses, shipped/equal-semantics analysis, profiling-before-tuning, product-cost ledger, real-consumer census, bundle controls, recommendation, and scaffolding deletion are all present. The caller-key-slot cache is bounded and behavior-preserving over the same total name projection as before; all six authored commits landed exactly and checks were 41 pass/34 intentional skips/0 fail. Correctness residual: the report repeatedly says W2 and W2r differ only in reactivity and that the whole 3.35x-vs-1.22x contrast is ViewCell elision. The recoverable landed fixtures disprove that isolation: probe.cljs sets w2-free=300 and w2-reads=100; w2-free renders a literal leaf while w2-read additionally executes (str (v/sub [:studio/tick])); and W2r has no React-floor arm. Comparing speedup ratios across different boundary counts plus added common subscription/string work cannot assign the entire difference to elision. The 3.35x elidable-witness result and KEEP recommendation remain real, but the exclusive causal claim is not measured. Bounded completion: either run a same-count same-leaf ablation that forces the compiled ViewCell kept versus elided, with the same in-run floor where applicable, or qualify the report and rf2-xu6rx so the contrast is evidence consistent with elision rather than proof that elision is the whole delta.
AUDIT-REOPEN OBLIGATION DISCHARGED — the ablation was run, not a qualification written. PR #7112 (docs-only, one file).

The audit's finding was correct: W2 vs W2r varied THREE things (300 vs 100 boundaries, literal leaf vs (str (v/sub ...)), and no floor arm on W2r), so the 3.35x-vs-1.22x contrast could not assign the difference to elision.

THE ABLATION. react.cljs/compiled-component selects its wrapper from the manifest's :view-cell verdict 'and by nothing else', so the arm is leaf-free's own descriptor with that one entry flipped to :present — same compiled body OBJECT (asserted identical?, not assumed), same props, same 300 boundaries, same canonical DOM (gated, agree? true in all 12 rounds). free-ik - free-ic is 300 ViewCells and nothing else; free-i - free-ik is interpretation and nothing else. Base is post-#7077, so the interpreted arm is faster than any interpreter the report measured.

  RETAINED HEAP (6 rounds, 10 roots x 300 boundaries held live, CDP sampler AND performance.memory occupancy agreeing to 2%, ~4.7 MB positive control each round):
    one kept ViewCell                                   2348 B per boundary (2295 by occupancy)
    free-ik / free-ic  ViewCell kept vs elided          6.256
    free-i  / free-ik  interpreted vs compiled, both keep 1.011
    read-i  / read-ic  reactive leaf, neither may elide  1.003

  WALL CLOCK (12 interleaved rounds, fresh process each, floor-normalised in-run; floor drift 58%):
    free-ik / free-ic  the ViewCell alone     1.712 [1.583-1.879]
    free-i  / free-ik  interpretation alone   1.216 [1.092-1.425]
    free-i  / free-ic  the two together       2.079 [1.896-2.419]
    read-i  / read-ic  neither may elide      1.045 [0.922-1.173]  STRADDLES 1.0
  Decomposition closes: 1.712 x 1.216 = 2.082 vs measured 2.079. Elision is 73% of the log-effect.

VERDICT ON THE AUDIT'S QUESTION. 'The whole difference is the ViewCell' is right about which term dominates and wrong to claim all of it. On RETAINED HEAP it is exactly right (1.011). On the CLOCK elision is the dominant but not the only term — interpretation contributes a real 1.216 whose range excludes 1.0.

TWO HEADLINE FIGURES REVISED, and this is the consequential part: 3.35x -> 2.079x, and 1.22x -> 1.045 (inseparable). Both moved toward 1.0 for two compounding reasons — the counts and leaves now match, and the interpreter is post-#7077. The 3.35x was not wrong when taken; it is no longer the number. Anywhere the '3x' is quoted, the wall-clock figure is 2.08x.

KEEP IS UNTOUCHED and the operator rationale is undisturbed — every witness here is still one we chose. What the ablation ADDS is that the memory case is stronger and far better conditioned than the time case: 6.26x with disjoint ranges and two agreeing instruments, against 2.08x on a clock whose own floor drifts 58%. If the tier is defended on performance, standing heap per elidable boundary is the number to defend it with.

METHOD FINDING worth more than the numbers: the recovered driver's PRIMARY instrument was measuring nothing. Its header claimed 'allocation is a counter, not an occupancy sample: a collection inside the window cannot make it smaller'. FALSE — V8's sampling heap profiler DROPS the samples of collected objects. The same 80,000 objects report 4.77 MB when a global holds them and 0.00 MB when nothing does. Pointed at a mount/unmount loop it was reporting the residue of a discarded page; that is why every arm came back at 10-25 KB for a 301-element React tree. A positive control of KNOWN SIZE, IN SITU, is now the first thing the retained-heap mode does.

DECLINED, on the report's own refusal discipline: no CPU-time split. Three repeats of the same pair returned free-i/free-ik = 1.81, 0.85, 1.85.

Scaffolding committed for durability then DELETED before the PR; branch diff is the one doc. Findings doc (local-only, NEVER commit or link): ai/findings/2026-07-26.hiccup-elision-ablation-same-count-same-leaf.md

FOLLOW-UP BEADS: rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out — operator call, stakes now exact)
FOLLOW-UP BEADS (running list): rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out — operator call), rf2-9oj7v (B2 prices elision in retained bytes, not just counts).
close_reason:
AUDIT-REOPEN obligation discharged by running the ablation, not by qualifying the report. PR #7112 (docs-only, one file: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md 1a).

The audit offered two exits and this took the harder one. Same 300 boundaries on both witnesses, same leaf body, a floor arm each, and the compiled body OBJECT asserted identical? between the ViewCell-kept and ViewCell-elided arms — so free-ik - free-ic is 300 ViewCells and nothing else.

Elision is the dominant term but not the whole of it on the clock (1.712 of a 2.079 total, 73% of the log-effect, with a real 1.216 from interpretation whose range excludes 1.0) and IS the whole of it on retained heap (1.011 once both tiers keep a cell). Two headline figures revised: 3.35x -> 2.079x and 1.22x -> inseparable. KEEP untouched; the memory case (6.26x, 2348 B of standing heap per boundary, two agreeing instruments, disjoint ranges) is stronger and better conditioned than the time case.

Follow-ups filed: rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out, operator call, stakes now exact), rf2-9oj7v (B2 prices elision in retained bytes rather than only counting it). rf2-xu6rx qualified in place per the audit's wording. Method lesson recorded via bd remember (the CDP heap sampler reports retained, not allocated).

Findings doc, local-only, never commit or link: ai/findings/2026-07-26.hiccup-elision-ablation-same-count-same-leaf.md

title: projected-record egresses a :sensitive? resource owner's scope + params RAW at 14 paths on a real ensure record — :rf.fx/args and :rf.event/fx trace tags take NO projector
description:
Surfaced by rf2-isp3i's fixture widening, the moment the MCP egress gate got a
`reg-resource` with a `:sensitive?` owner. NOT fixed there — that bead's fence
is one fixture gains one family, and this is a projector change.

THE LEAK. `epoch/projected-record` over a REAL, naturally-captured
`[:rf.resource/ensure {:resource :secret/article :params {:auth-token
"topsecret…"}}]` record egresses that `:sensitive?` owner's resolved scope AND
canonical params RAW, at FOURTEEN distinct paths on ONE record. No splicing, no
hand-built record, no fixture trickery: a two-line `reg-resource` + one
`dispatch-sync` reproduces it.

The carriers are the fx TRACE ROWS:

  [:trace-events 5 :tags :rf.fx/args :work-id 1 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 5 :tags :rf.fx/args :request-id 2 1 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 6 :tags :rf.fx/args :request-id 2 1 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 6 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-success 1 :work/id 1 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 6 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-success 1 :resource/key 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 6 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-failure 1 :work/id 1 2 :auth-token]
  [:trace-events 6 :tags :rf.fx/args :on-failure 1 :resource/key 2 :auth-token]
  … and the same seven again under the `:rf.fx/do-fx` row's `:rf.event/fx`,
    which carries the whole fx vector verbatim.

Concretely, the `:rf.http/managed` row's `:rf.fx/args` egress

  {:request    {:method :get :url "/secret"}
   :request-id [:rf.req :test/mcp
                [:rf.work/resource
                 [:rf.scope/global :secret/article
                  {:auth-token "topsecret-do-not-leak"}] 1]]
   :on-success [:rf.resource.internal/succeeded
                {:work/id      [:rf.work/resource [… same key …] 1]
                 :resource/key [:rf.scope/global :secret/article
                                {:auth-token "topsecret-do-not-leak"}]
                 :scope :rf.scope/global :generation 1 …}]
   :on-failure [… identical shape …]}

and the `:rf.resource/record-work-handle` row carries the key twice more under
`:work-id` and `:request-id`. The `release-owner` cascade's record leaks four
more paths the same way (`:rf.resource/cancel-timers`' `:resource/keys`, and an
abort fx's embedded work-id).

WHY NO EXISTING ARM COVERS IT — two blind spots meeting.

  1. The resource family's own projector does not see these rows. The epoch
     tool-pair routes a row to `project-resource-trace-egress` on
     `resource-family-op?`, which tests the row's `:operation` NAMESPACE for
     `rf.resource` / `rf.mutation` / `rf.warning`-`resource-`. These rows are
     `:rf.fx/handled` and `:rf.fx/do-fx` — namespace `rf.fx`. The scoped keys
     are the family's, but the ROW is not, so the family arm is skipped
     entirely.
  2. The generic value-path walk cannot classify them. A resolver-owned scoped
     key's embedded scope + params are not app-db-rooted, so a frame's declared
     `:sensitive` PATHS never match — the exact structural blindness Spec 015
     §10 describes and the reason the family projector exists at all.

THE SHARPEST FORM OF IT. The SAME fx args ride TWO carriers in the SAME record,
and only one is projected: the structured `:effects[*].args` slot IS
`:rf/redacted` (the fail-closed fx-args axis — pinned by
`include-sensitive-reveals-app-db-but-keeps-fx-args-redacted`), while the
`:rf.fx/args` TRACE TAG carrying the identical payload rides raw. That is the
rf2-irwsq two-slot shape exactly: one value, two egress slots, one rule applied.
A reader of the projected record sees `:args :rf/redacted` on the effects row
and the whole payload three rows above it.

REACHABILITY. This is off-box egress: `projected-record` is what
`register-epoch-listener!` forwarders and `watch-epochs` ship. Any app with a
`:sensitive?` resource and an epoch forwarder attached is disclosing its
resolved scope + canonical params today. Note this is INDEPENDENT of rf2-hbmeb
(epoch capture dropping the `:rf.resource/*` rows) — the fx rows carry `:frame`,
so they ARE captured, and they leak the same identity the dropped rows would
have carried redacted.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, for whoever takes it. The cleanest is probably to route the
fx-args carriers through the SAME family projector the `:rf.resource/*` rows
take — `project-resource-trace-egress` is already shape-driven since rf2-wd9im,
so it recognises a scoped key wherever it sits and leaves scalars alone, which
is precisely what these payloads need. That means widening the epoch tool-pair's
routing beyond `resource-family-op?` for the `:rf.fx/args` / `:rf.event/fx`
slots (they are not resource-family ROWS, so the routing predicate is the thing
that has to change), or giving those two slots their own pass through the same
rule. The alternative — treating `:rf.fx/args` in trace tags with the same
fail-closed redaction the structured `:effects[*].args` slot already gets — is
simpler and closes it for every fx, not just resource ones, at the cost of the
attribution the shape walk would have preserved. Worth deciding deliberately
rather than by whichever is easier.
acceptance_criteria: epoch/projected-record over a REAL captured [:rf.resource/ensure ...] record (a :sensitive? owner, secret in params) contains the raw secret at ZERO paths — the :rf.fx/args tag on every :rf.fx/handled row and the :rf.event/fx tag on the :rf.fx/do-fx row project their embedded scoped keys through the resource OWNER classification, exactly as the row's own :resource/key does. A PLAIN owner's fx args still ride verbatim (no over-redaction). The whole-record scan in epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test's forwarder-projected-record-leaks-no-raw-resource-family-bytes is widened from the family rows back to the WHOLE record when this lands, and the carve-out comment naming this bead is deleted.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7031 (2026-07-26): REOPENED. The original 18-path raw-secret leak is completely closed and the real ensure/release fixture, whole-history scan, mixed sensitive/plain owner control, negative revert, late-bind inventory, and green suites provide strong completeness evidence. A correctness residual remains in the foreign FX carrier pass: scoped-key-shape? accepts any 3-vector with a keyword in slot 1 and map in slot 2, project-fx-args-egress recursively applies it to :rf.fx/args and :rf.event/fx on every row, and an unregistered slot-1 keyword then takes project-trace-scoped-key's fail-closed owner arm. Direct reproduction on merged code: (project-fx-args-egress {:rf.fx/args [:opaque :app/not-a-resource {:account-id 42}]} :audit/frame) returns {:rf.fx/args [{:rf/redacted "509eacb6"} :app/not-a-resource {:rf/redacted "78a0513e"}], :sensitive? true}. This is ordinary application FX data, not a resource key; its scope-like value and payload are destroyed off-box despite the function contract that every non-key value rides untouched. The existing plain control only exercises registered resource keys, so it cannot detect the collision. Bounded repair: disambiguate actual resource-key carriers from arbitrary foreign 3-vectors while retaining fail-closed projection for genuine unregistered resource keys. Add a regression where unrelated custom FX args containing a colliding 3-vector ride byte-for-byte and do not stamp sensitivity, alongside an actual unregistered resource carrier that still redacts. No new Bead: rf2-1kiuj exactly owns both the carrier projection and its no-over-redaction acceptance criterion.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7054 (merge 76621e8b9e0b8ca288f474914476d2164d6a9736, merged 2026-07-26T01:29:26Z) — keep open; this exact foreign-carrier over-classification owner has a new sibling collision. The intended rf2-425mm leak is closed: a real session-scoped ensure now tokenizes all four continuation :scope paths, keeps tier/digest attribution, preserves the global scalar, and trusted-local reveals raw values. Correctness residual: project-embedded-keys now special-cases EVERY recursively visited map entry whose key equals :scope, not only the runtime-owned resource continuation payload. Direct reproduction on the merged code: (project-fx-args-egress {:rf.fx/args {:request {:method :post :scope {:tenant "alice"} :body {:x 1}}}} :audit/frame) returns a request whose app-owned :scope map is {:rf/redacted "8667c723"} and stamps :sensitive? true. That is ordinary application FX/request data, contradicting the projector contract that everything except resource-planted data rides untouched. The PR's plain-request control contains only :method/:url, so it cannot see this key collision. Bounded repair: recognize the resource continuation context/provenance rather than any :scope key at arbitrary depth, while still covering mutation continuations that carry no sibling :resource/key. Add a custom/plain FX request with a map-valued :scope that must remain byte-identical and unstamped, beside both read and mutation resource continuation positives. No new Bead: rf2-1kiuj already owns project-fx-args-egress and its no-over-redaction acceptance.

title: epoch capture drops EVERY resource/mutation trace row (:rf.frame/id vs :frame), so the off-box resource-egress projector is unreachable from any real record
description:
Measured while widening the MCP egress conformance fixture (rf2-isp3i). The
resource/mutation trace family NEVER lands in an epoch record's
`:trace-events`, on any real producer path, so the epoch tool-pair's
`omit-off-box-resource-trace-keys` arm — and with it
`re-frame.resources.trace-egress/project-resource-trace-egress` — is
unreachable from the producer path it was written for.

THE MECHANISM, one line. `re-frame.epoch.capture/capture-event!` derives the
event's frame as

    frame-id (or (:frame tags) (:frame event))

and every branch that buffers is inside `(when (and frame-id ...) ...)`. The
whole `:rf.resource/*` + `:rf.mutation/*` family stamps `:rf.frame/id`, never
`:frame` — `events.cljc`, `timers.cljc`, `mutation-events.cljc`, `route.cljc`,
`ssr.cljc` all emit `{:rf.frame/id frame-id ...}`. So `frame-id` is nil for
every row in the family and NOTHING is buffered. The rows still ride the raw
trace ring and every `trace-tooling` listener; only epoch capture drops them.

MEASURED, not inferred. A real cascade on `:test/mcp` —
`[:rf.resource/ensure {:resource :secret/article ...}]` twice under one owner
then `[:rf.resource/release-owner ...]` — emits 7 family rows on the bus
(`work-started` / `fetch-started` / `owner-attached` x2, `owner-released`),
every one carrying `:rf.frame/id` + `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` and NO `:frame`.
The three epoch records the same cascade produced carry 9 / 9 / 8
`:trace-events` between them and not one `:rf.resource/*` row.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the sharper one.

1. FIDELITY: an Xray / MCP consumer reading `watch-epochs` or
   `register-epoch-listener!` sees the resource lifecycle NOWHERE in the epoch
   stream. The `:sub-runs` / `:renders` / `:effects` projections are unaffected;
   it is specifically the family's trace rows that vanish.

2. COVERAGE: the epoch-side resource-egress projector has never run over a real
   record. `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` (and the rf2-wd9im / rf2-3tysyj
   / rf2-7qbxbm suites inside it) all hand-build records with `record-with`, so
   they prove the PROJECTOR and the WIRING but not that the wiring is ever
   reached. That is the same canned-producer shape rf2-isp3i's own rescoping
   names. If the capture gap is closed, every one of those arms starts firing on
   real records for the first time — which is a good thing, and worth doing in
   the same breath as fixing it.

WHY THIS IS NOT ITSELF A LEAK. The rows never egress through epoch at all, so
nothing is disclosed by this gap. It is the reason the two P1 leaks
(rf2-wd9im, rf2-5o52l) were provable only through the resources-side suites
that call `project-resource-trace-egress` directly, and it is why rf2-isp3i's
fixture had to splice the real harvested rows onto a real record rather than
drive them in.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: rf2-isp3i's fence is one fixture gaining one
family, and the repair is a production-emit / capture-seam change with a
blast radius across the whole family. Two candidate shapes for whoever takes
it: teach `capture-event!` to read `:rf.frame/id` as a second frame source
(one line, covers the family and anything else that spells the frame that
way), or make the family stamp `:frame` at its emit sites (more sites, but
keeps one frame-tag spelling on the capture seam). The first looks right —
`omit-off-box-resource-trace-keys` ALREADY reads `(or (:rf.frame/id (:tags ev))
frame-id)`, so the epoch side already treats `:rf.frame/id` as the family's
frame spelling; capture is the one seam that does not.
acceptance_criteria: A real [:rf.resource/ensure ...] / [:rf.resource/release-owner ...] cascade lands its :rf.resource/* rows in the settling epoch record's :trace-events, and epoch/projected-record over that REAL record redacts a :sensitive? owner's scope + params while a plain owner's ride verbatim. The existing hand-built record-with fixtures in epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj gain (or are replaced by) at least one arm driven from a real cascade, so the wiring is proven REACHED and not only correct.
notes:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN CLOSE REASON — I MISREAD THE clojure.test OUTPUT AND MY EARLIER ACCOUNT ON THIS BEAD IS WRONG (2026-07-26).

WHAT I GOT WRONG. The assertion is (is (= <literal> (set (keys tags)))) — LITERAL FIRST. clojure.test prints "actual: (not (= <first> <second>))" in ARGUMENT ORDER. So in (not (= #{4 keys} #{5 keys including :frame})) the FOUR-KEY SET IS THE TEST EXPECTATION and the five-key set is WHAT THE CODE PRODUCED. The worker was ADDING :frame where those tests require it ABSENT. I read it as the reverse — as :frame being removed — and on that basis sent a long directive telling the worker to revert its rename and treat the finding as the deliverable.

IT NEVER RENAMED ANYTHING. The diff touches 6 files and ZERO of the 195 :rf.frame/id sites; every :rf.frame/id line in the diff is docstring prose. resources/, machines/, schemas/, ui/, routing/ and http/ were not edited at all. So my close reason claim that "it first tried the rename and CI reddened four suites" is FALSE and is retracted here.

THE :rf/default I KEYED ON WAS ALSO NOT WHAT I SAID. It is not a resolution floor surfacing; it is make-reset-runtime-fixture own ambient frame, which the over-broad stamp read at registry time.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is one defect of one shape: the worker applied Spec 009 first clause (supply the tag) but not its second — trace-event-frame returns nil for an event emitted OUTSIDE any frame-qualified run. Registry-time and boot-time emits were acquiring a frame they must not have. All four suites assert exactly that clause: machines reg-machine lint warnings, schemas "direct 4-arity call emits no :frame", ui carried-op warning (the stamp injected the very ambient frame the warning exists to complain about), and Xray FRAMELESS secondary ring. Fixed in 06573b4c by gating the stamp on :rf.trace/dispatch-id, the runtime own inside-a-run signal. All 7 resource-family rows carry one, so the fix still lands.

WHAT I GOT RIGHT, and the worker says so: the SEMANTIC instinct. :frame and :rf.frame/id are genuinely different keys for different jobs — [:tags :frame] is the raw trace-event routing tag (Spec 009), :rf.frame/id is the carried-frame stamp (Spec 002 / EP-0002) that the resource family additionally copies in as evidence. That is why it never renamed, never shimmed, and left all 195 sites alone. The vocabularies are disjoint and stay that way.

A DETAIL WORTH KEEPING: the general assertion the worker had already written — real-cascade-emits-no-frameless-correlated-row — ALREADY ENCODED the correlated-only rule. The test was right before the implementation was.

MEASURED RESULT: family rows carrying [:tags :frame] 0 -> 7; rows reaching the settled records 0 -> 7; :trace-events [9 9 8] -> [12 12 9]. Negative control: reverting reds 10 assertions including (not (= 7 0)). rf2-1kiuj is UNCHANGED — 18 raw-secret paths before and after, same :rf.fx/* rows; the 7 newly-reaching rows egress nothing raw.

THE LESSON FOR ME, and it is the sharpest of the day: I pulled the log myself specifically so the worker would not iterate blind, then inverted its argument order and issued a confident directive from the inversion. Reading a diff or a test failure is a MEASUREMENT, and I have now been wrong on six of them today by substituting a fast read for the real one. For clojure.test specifically: (is (= expected actual)) prints expected FIRST inside the (not (= ...)) form. Check which side the literal is on before concluding a direction.
close_reason:
PR #7026 MERGED — and the fix is the OPPOSITE of what the bead proposed, which is the right outcome.

THE BEAD SAID: capture-event! reads :frame while the resource family stamps :rf.frame/id, so rename to converge them. My brief told the worker to decide which spelling is canonical rather than pick the majority, and to STOP and report if the two meant different things.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: it first tried the rename and CI reddened four suites — JVM ui, JVM machines, JVM schemas and CLJS. The log was decisive. frame_ops_cljs_test.cljc:426 expected #{:origin-frame :frame :rf.sub/query-v :ambient-frame :reason} and got the set MINUS :frame; machine_cofx_lint_test.clj:225 expected {... :frame :rf/default} and got it without. So :frame is a LOAD-BEARING diagnostic-envelope key carrying a resolved frame including the :rf/default floor — NOT a misspelling of the resource-family frame id.

THE SHIPPED FIX, per its own title: "stamp the canonical [:tags :frame] at the producer so epoch capture stops dropping the resource/mutation family". capture-event! keeps reading :frame because :frame IS canonical; the trace producers now stamp it. Files: core trace.cljc, trace/projection.cljc, trace/tooling.cljc, epoch/capture.cljc plus two tests. Verified on main: zero :rf.frame/id reads in epoch.cljc, one :frame read.

THAT IS THE ONE-SEAM FIX IN THE CORRECT DIRECTION. Converging the consumer onto the producer would have deleted a real distinction to satisfy a mistaken premise, and forcing those four suites green by editing their expectations would have destroyed it silently.

WHY THE ORIGINAL SYMPTOM WAS REAL ANYWAY: 7 rows on the bus, 0 into the 3 settled records. The producer simply was not stamping the canonical key, so capture correctly found nothing. The consequence recorded on the bead stands — the epoch-side resource projector had NEVER run over a real record, so every record-with arm in epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj proved the projector while proving nothing about the wiring being reached. That is the gate-blindness family, and this fix is what makes those arms mean something.

PROCESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING: I pulled the failing log myself and handed the worker the two decisive assertions rather than letting it iterate blind, and I told it explicitly that "the bead premise is wrong, here are the two meanings" would be a complete and valuable result. It found the third option — canonical key identified, producer corrected — which is better than either.

WHY IT FAILED. The Reagent standard (rf2-lbs3y, Mike 2026-07-27: 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent') was not met, and the residual gap is architectural rather than an optimisation backlog. Interpreted Freehand measured ~5x Reagent on bulk repaint and ~1.6x on mount.

DO NOT REPEAT THE SUPERSEDED REASON. An earlier summary said the cost WAS the invariant-5 tear check. rf2-so3io / PR #7159 falsified that by ablation: dropping useSyncExternalStore AND the commit-side re-read returned only -13.6%/-14.8% on the broad clock and -375 B heap, and a contract-free boundary was still ~5.5x Reagent on clock and ~5x on heap. The guarantee was not what cost us — and the same ablation found invariant 5 is worth MORE than Spec 006 claims, since a staged site without it publishes stale and never self-heals.

THE CODE STAYS. 'Not removed yet.' No implementation/freehand/** deletion, no build-id removal, no CI lane or roster change. The Freehand prod-gate lane (137 of 137, roster empty) keeps running until an explicit removal ruling.

NORMATIVE HALF: rf2-lgleu (P1) records the withdrawal in the EP corpus — EP-0036 moves to Status: withdrawn per EP-0009's closed vocabulary, and the six EPs citing Freehand stop implying it is live.

DO NOT re-file this work as follow-ups. The programme is retracted, not paused.

title: Executable Freehand fixture spine and workshop application
description:
OUTCOME
Establish one executable Freehand workshop and fixture roster so a claim has one stable identity across source, checker/build, JVM structure, mounted browser behavior, guide prose, runnable route, and Xray evidence.

FIXTURE RECORD
Each record names canonical source, supported modes/hosts, expected structure or diagnostic, mounted entry/browser law, evidence expectation, and prose status: executable, expected-failure, or illustrative.

INITIAL SPINE
Integrate the declared-host, serious-form, and Vega-async fixtures delivered by their owning slices. Extend the same roster for Maps, Framer Motion, SpreadJS, Radix/compound React, and control witnesses as they land.

TEST SURFACE
Consume the re-frame.freehand.test mounted lifecycle facade ruled in ER-06/ER-08 and owned by rf2-gzmg0: frame/root/container setup, React act/settling, presence flush, unmount, subscription overrides, and leak assertions. Do not duplicate it locally.

HOST/MODE
JVM structural, CLJS mounted browser, interpreted/compiled as claimed, SSR where claimed, Xray/tool projection.

NON-GOALS
No browser-action DSL, query library, second simulation language, second evidence store, fixture generator, or documentation generator before repetition.

ACCEPTANCE
1. One stable fixture identity is visible in every applicable projection and failures name it.
2. The first three vertical fixtures run through the same roster with no pasted divergent implementation.
3. Mounted lifecycle and override cleanup are exact; no root, listener, override, or evidence residue remains.
4. Guide code is mechanically checked against canonical source; illustrative blocks are labeled and make no executable claim.
5. Existing rf2-fby7o and rf2-7gth0 consume this spine rather than creating parallel source/evidence authority.

PR #7243 (2026-07-29). PARTIAL — DO NOT CLOSE. The two false-green paths the merged-PR audit of #7178 recorded, plus a third of the same shape and a totality bug the first fix exposed.

THE RESIDUE RULE NOW READS STRUCTURE. It was a four-state character scanner that blanked comments and string literals and never saw `#_`. Replaced by `clojure.tools.reader` (already this artefact's reader, in compiler/harvest.clj and five check-*-jvm-tests): `#js` degrades, `::alias/kw` resolves, `#=` off, reader conditionals PRESERVED so both branches count. Not another regex, because `#_` discards the NEXT FORM: `#_ #_ a b` discards two and any token-level rule is wrong on it while looking right on the single case.

MEMBERSHIP IS `contains?` NOW, via a driven `roster/enrolled?`, matching the docstring. That immediately exposed a latent totality bug the truthiness spelling had been hiding: `defects` THREW on `:fh/record false` because `(keys false)` throws — unreachable for as long as no such record could arrive. Fixed in the same commit.

`:prose :executable` IS CHECKED EXECUTABLE. It held nothing but membership of a closed set — the exact shape `:residue :none` had. Every proof namespace of an `:executable` or `:expected-failure` record must now define a test, checked with the same reader and refuted against real testless files (`behavior-views`, `mount-support`). `:illustrative` is exempt, which is what makes declaring the other two cost something.

(D) FH-REACT-007's structural tier pointed at `re-frame.freehand.roster`, which cites the id and defines no test: origin/main exit 0; branch exit 1 naming FH-REACT-007. `git diff --stat` empty after every restore. Two further shapes closed in passing: a call inside `(comment …)`, and `#_ #_ a b`.

GATES, all foreground, exit 0: implementation/freehand clojure -M:test 1287 tests / 8850 assertions (1284 / 8803 before); npm run test:freehand 1392 / 7732; sh scripts/test-freehand-prod-gate.sh 137 of 137 namespaces with 0 excluded as known-red, 1289 / 8621; python scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py; focused roster JVM 28 / 409 (25 / 362 before). npm run test:browser and mkdocs build --strict deferred to CI — no mounted suite, view or page is touched.
