title: Publish trustworthy v/check and orthogonal compiler/contract evidence
description:
OUTCOME
Make compiled eligibility trustworthy and expose it through public v/check, with orthogonal props and controlled-site evidence shared by checker, exact build, manifest, guide, and Xray.

JUDGMENT
Classify child-producing expressions as known template/boundary, audited scalar producer, or opaque. Opaque child results are checker/build ineligible before render and report one stable id, source, expression summary, and executable recoveries. Carry the judgment through admitted bindings, branches, and collections; keep the audited scalar corpus deliberately small and evidence-grown.

EVIDENCE
Props report declared?, key closure, value-validation status, and generator availability independently. Controlled sites report known-open/known-closed/dynamic/unavailable plus basis. Legal doorless sites are facts, not warnings; sensitive values never enter diagnostics.

HOST/MODE
Read-only CLJ/CLJS analyzer data; exact compiled build; JVM structural fixtures; production evidence elision where required. v/check is a public-verb API-manifest serial-lane change.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-05/DC-06/DC-07 and ER-06; D009-D012, D020; 004D checker grammar, 008, 009, API/Ownership and FH-DIAG/FH-PROPS/FH-INPUT.

NON-GOALS
No general type system, hidden interpreter, auto-editing, promotion score, giant allowlist, mandatory private schemas, or warning on every legal callback.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Helper-produced markup through bindings/branches/collections is refused before render while a representative scalar corpus remains accepted.
2. v/check and exact build return identical stable facts and recoveries for the same source, with explicit .cljc/.cljs coverage.
3. Props and controlled-door evidence prove every vocabulary arm and never infer unavailable facts.
4. Guide, editor/CLI projection, manifest and Xray consume the same data rather than reimplementing judgment.
5. Relevant false-green mutation probes red the real checker/build lane.
notes:
OPERATOR FRAMING (Mike, 2026-07-26), and it resolves the tension between the report verdict and the ruling:

  "This is a specialised requirement"

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT POSITIONING AND SHOULD BE THE ONE THE DOCS CARRY. The compiled tier is a SPECIALISED tier serving a specialised requirement — performance-critical applications not yet in the corpus. It is NOT the paved path and should not be sold as one. That reading is consistent with everything measured:

  - Freehand PAVED PATH IS INTERPRETED. That is by design, not by omission.
  - NO application in the repo declares a compiled view — expected for a specialised tier, not evidence against it.
  - The 3.35x advantage is SHAPE-SPECIFIC: sub-free boundaries. 1.22x reactive. Inseparable on an ordinary form. A specialised gain for a specialised shape.

title: Deferred foreign-handle ownership recipe (docs-and-evidence slice)
description:
OUTCOME
Publish and prove the one async connection-owner recipe for Promise-acquired imperative integrations, without adding framework machinery.

RECIPE

Product-completion DC-02; D013, D019, D020; spec/004-Views.md, 008, 009 and FH-BEHAVIOR extensions.

NON-GOALS

title: ER-01 evidence spike: compare interpreted, compiled Hiccup, and v/$
description:
OUTCOME
Run the bounded ER-01 architecture comparison on one fixed-size virtual-table fixture: tuned interpreted Freehand, the shipped compiled-Hiccup path, and a minimal v/$ prototype. Return evidence and a recommendation to Mike.

LAWS
Preserve the same declared descriptor, D008 callback door, ViewCell/reactive behavior, structural-test result, SSR/evidence semantics, and user-visible DOM. Compare authoring friction and compiler complexity as well as runtime work.

HOST/MODE
JVM structural plus CLJS browser; interpreted, current compiled, and prototype. Use D021's deterministic-first evidence posture.

NON-GOALS
Do not publish v/$, retire compiled Hiccup, add a second declaration, or change production architecture. Pause only discretionary compiled-Hiccup completion; correctness/shared work continues.

ACCEPTANCE
1. One fixture and workload parameters are identical across all three arms.
2. Structural/DOM output and callback behavior are deterministic-equal before timing is considered.
3. Evidence separates interpreter/lowering work, React/host work, allocations, commits, bundle reachability, and p50/p95/p99 timing with provenance.
4. The report prices implementation complexity, error quality, AI editability, and migration cost.
5. Mike receives an explicit keep/change recommendation; no architecture mutation occurs without his later ruling.

AUTHORITY
Product-completion setpoint ER-01; EP-0036; D002, D008, D010, D021.
notes:
OPERATOR GATE — this bead stays OPEN on a decision that is Mike, not on work.

The reopen was class (B), a genuine new residual: the close was ACCEPTED and unmet sub-arms of acceptance items 2 and 3 were found. Pinned with history rather than inferred — a0be49a31d added only its three named narrowings, and the acceptance language is the bead original.

TWO OF THE FLAGGED ARMS WERE UNDER-CLAIMED, NOT MISSING, which is a distinction worth keeping: allocation distribution is DEGENERATE — min = median = max, so p95 and p99 ARE p50 and were measured — and bundle reachability is settled by SET MEMBERSHIP rather than by a number. Reporting them as unmeasured would have been false.

THREE ARMS STAY GENUINELY UNMEASURED, AND NONE CAN MOVE THE ANSWER, because the deciding finding is STRUCTURAL: the compiled analyzer REFUSES a $ body, so the two front ends are DISJOINT, NOT A DIAL. No measurement crosses a build-time refusal.

WHAT IS OWED IS A RULING, NOT A MEASUREMENT: the audit other branch asks for "an explicit operator reruling that narrows ER-01 acceptance". The worker presented both closes with their bills, RECOMMENDED THE NARROWING, and asserted no ruling — correctly. So the choice is: (a) narrow ER-01 acceptance to what the structural finding actually settles, and close; or (b) require the three remaining measurements, knowing in advance they cannot change the verdict.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (a). The verdict — keep v/$ a non-goal, not because it is slow but because it is free and free buys nothing here — rests on a REFUSAL IN THE COMPILER, and no timing number can overturn a refusal. Spending three measurements to satisfy acceptance language written before that was known is the definition of litigating a detail the answer does not depend on.

title: [BUG] resources trace-egress passes :scope through verbatim on five rows the sibling scope-resolved projector never touches
description:
Found by rf2-wd9im while surveying the resource-family trace tags. Deliberately
NOT fixed there: it is a different leak class (a name-keyed pass-through resting
on a premise that holds on exactly one row), it changes egress on five row types,
and it overrides a RECORDED EP-0025 decision — so it wants a ruling, not a
drive-by.

THE GAP. `trace_egress.cljc`'s `sibling-owned-slot` is `#{:input-values :scope}`,
and the projector passes those two slots through VERBATIM. Its docstring gives
the reason: they are "OWNED by the SIBLING `:rf.resource/scope-resolved`
projector … which the epoch tool-pair runs BEFORE this family projector on the
SAME row", so "they were already classified upstream (an already-redacted token
re-redacts to itself)".

THE PREMISE HOLDS ON ONE ROW ONLY. `omit-off-box-resource-scope-values`
(implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1425-1436) applies the
sibling projector under

    (= :rf.resource/scope-resolved (:operation ev))

— a single operation. The family projector that consults `sibling-owned-slot`,
by contrast, runs on EVERY `:rf.resource/*` / `:rf.mutation/*` /
`:rf.warning/resource-*` row (`resource-family-op?` is operation-agnostic). So on
every row that is NOT `:rf.resource/scope-resolved`, `:scope` has been classified
by NOBODY and rides raw.

Rows carrying a raw `:scope` today (all resolved CANONICAL CONCRETE scopes):

  - `:rf.resource/invalidated`      — `:scope cscope` (events.cljc:1811)
  - `:rf.resource/refetch-decision` — `:scope (first resource-key)` (events.cljc:1828)
  - `:rf.resource/removed`          — `:scope cscope` (events.cljc:2050)
  - `:rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved` — `:scope scope` + `:from-db`
                                      (events.cljc:2119-2122)
  - `:rf.mutation/started` / `:rf.mutation/optimistic-applied` — `:scope cscope`
                                      (mutation_events.cljc:1390, 1403)

A concrete scope is `[:rf.scope/session {:username "…"}]` / `[:rf.scope/tenant
{:tenant-id "…"}]` — the tier keyword plus an IDENTITY MAP. That map is exactly
what EP-0025 (rf2-71dr8t) made unconditionally fail-closed for the scope-resolved
row, and it egresses off-box in the clear on all five rows above. Note
`:rf.resource/refetch-decision` carries the SAME scope twice — once inside
`:resource/key` (correctly redacted for a sensitive owner) and once under
`:scope` (raw). The row redacts and leaks the same value side by side.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A DIFF.
rf2-wd9im replaced the map-only fail-closed default with a SHAPE-driven one that
would handle `:scope` correctly if it were simply dropped from
`sibling-owned-slot`:

  - `:scope :rf.scope/global` — a scalar, rides verbatim (no over-redaction);
  - `:scope [:rf.scope/session {:username "…"}]` — a 2-vector, so not
    scoped-key-shaped; the walk descends, the TIER KEYWORD rides verbatim
    (attribution preserved: a tool still shows "session scope") and the identity
    MAP tokenizes to `{:rf/redacted <digest>}` (distinct scopes keep distinct
    digests, so per-scope joins survive);
  - on `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` itself the sibling has already replaced the
    value with a token, and the projector's `redacted-token?` arm is checked
    BEFORE `sibling-owned-slot`, so it rides as-is and still stamps the row
    `:sensitive?` — idempotent, no double-digest.

So the mechanical change is: remove `:scope` from `sibling-owned-slot` (keep
`:input-values`, whose only emitter IS the scope-resolved row) and let the shape
default own it.

THE DECISION. Is per-scope tokenization with the tier keyword surviving the right
egress for these five rows, or should `:scope` be coarsely redacted whole (losing
the tier) for consistency with what the scope-resolved row does to it? The
former preserves materially more tooling value — the Xray invalidation graph
groups by scope tier — and is what the shape default gives for free. The latter
is a stricter reading of "resolved scope egress is unconditionally fail-closed".
Either way `sibling-owned-slot`'s docstring must be corrected: as written it
asserts a family-wide upstream classification that does not exist.

TEST OBLIGATION. A `:rf.resource/invalidated` row with a
`[:rf.scope/session {:username "topsecret-PII"}]` scope, asserting no raw secret
survives `epoch/projected-record` — and confirmed RED before the fix. rf2-wd9im
notes `epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` carries no resource-family rows at
all, so that gate cannot catch this (rf2-isp3i owns widening it).

GATES: `implementation/epoch` + `implementation/resources` `clojure -M:test`.
notes:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26): "make the change". EP-0025 is overridden for the five non-scope-resolved row types; drop :scope from sibling-owned-slot and let the shape-driven default classify it.

THE RULING WAS MADE ON THIS EVIDENCE, verified by the mayor before surfacing it:
  - trace_egress.cljc:189 defines sibling-owned-slot as #{:input-values :scope} and passes both through VERBATIM, justified by a docstring claiming the sibling :rf.resource/scope-resolved projector already classified them upstream.
  - tool_pair.cljc:1431 applies that sibling projector under (= :rf.resource/scope-resolved (:operation ev)) — ONE operation.
  - The family projector consulting sibling-owned-slot runs on EVERY :rf.resource/* / :rf.mutation/* / :rf.warning/resource-* row, because resource-family-op? is operation-agnostic.
  - Therefore on all five other row types :scope has been classified by NOBODY and rides raw: :rf.resource/invalidated (events.cljc:1811), :refetch-decision (:1828), :removed (:2050), :rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved (:2119-2122), and :rf.mutation/started + optimistic-applied (mutation_events.cljc:1390, 1403).
  - What leaks is the IDENTITY MAP — [:rf.scope/session {:username "..."}] — which EP-0025 (rf2-71dr8t) made unconditionally fail-closed for the scope-resolved row.
  - :rf.resource/refetch-decision carries the SAME scope TWICE: correctly redacted inside :resource/key and raw under :scope. THE ROW REDACTS AND LEAKS THE SAME VALUE SIDE BY SIDE — the fourth instance of that exact signature found today.

WHY IT IS ONE LINE NOW: rf2-wd9im replaced the map-only fail-closed default with a SHAPE-DRIVEN one, so dropping :scope from the set does the right thing per shape — :rf.scope/global is a scalar and rides verbatim (no over-redaction); a [tier {identity}] 2-vector is not scoped-key-shaped so the walk descends, the TIER KEYWORD rides (attribution preserved — a tool still shows "session scope") and the identity MAP tokenizes with distinct scopes keeping distinct digests (per-scope joins survive); and on :rf.resource/scope-resolved itself the sibling has already substituted, so nothing changes there.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER MUST NOT DO: do not blanket-redact the whole :scope value — that destroys attribution and is exactly what the shape-driven default was built to avoid. Do not remove :input-values from sibling-owned-slot; this ruling covers :scope only, and :input-values was not surveyed. Do not add a row predicate to keep the two projectors in step — that is the roster-that-rots shape this artefact keeps removing.
close_reason:
PR #7044 MERGED, on the operator ruling "make the change". ONE LINE: sibling-owned-slot goes #{:input-values :scope} -> #{:input-values}. All three prohibitions honoured — no blanket redaction, :input-values untouched, no row predicate. Landing verified by blob hash e1ee6c766bc31814e2393f9c63eba2bd32cfed08 whose line 226 reads #{:input-values}).

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE DELIVERABLE AND IT IS THE STRONGEST FORM YET SEEN. Pre-fix the identity map arrives IN THE CLEAR: actual: (not (redacted-component? {:username "topsecret-PII"})). All five row types confirmed leaking — and :rf.mutation/started was leaking UNFLAGGED, with :sensitive? nil. On :rf.resource/refetch-decision the two carriers now AGREE: neither :resource/key nor :scope leaks. They still differ in GRANULARITY (the key scope tokenizes whole by owner classification, the free tag keeps its tier) but no longer in CLASSIFICATION, which is exactly what the side-by-side signature meant.

AND THE PROOF THE MUTATION APPLIED IS BUILT INTO THE NUMBERS: RED and GREEN runs have IDENTICAL counts, 490/6611, differing only in failures 16 -> 0. As the worker put it, that identity is the proof the mutation applied rather than the gate quietly not firing — a silently-failed edit would have left 16. Correct and unavoidable — invalidated and removed carry no :resource/key to read a claim from, and an invalidation sweep spans owners — so off-box-plain-owner-free-scope-map-fails-closed-key-rides-verbatim pins it.

title: [BUG] :rf.resource/owner-released's :released egresses PLAINTEXT CEDN key-ids off-box — scope + params in the clear
description:
Found by rf2-wd9im while surveying the resource-family trace tags for
sequential values. NOT fixable by that bead's shape-driven fail-closed default —
this is a genuinely different leak class and needs its own decision.

THE GAP. `:rf.resource/owner-released` emits
`:released (vec (or owned #{}))` (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/
resources/events.cljc:1918). `owned` is a set of `state/key-id` values — the
handler iterates it through `state/entry-path-by-id`, whose docstring pins the
argument as "its already-computed `key-id` (the CEDN-1 byte string)"
(state.cljc:142-148).

WHY THAT IS A RAW LEAK. A `key-id` is `identity/canonical-bytes` of the scoped
key (state.cljc:43-65), and CEDN-1 is a REVERSIBLE PLAINTEXT encoding, not a
digest: `encode-string` emits `(str "s:" (pr-str s))`
(implementation/core/src/re_frame/identity.cljc:270-273), `encode-keyword` emits
`k:`-prefixed keyword text, `encode-map` space-joins key/value tokens. So a
key-id for `[:rf.scope/global :secret/article {:auth-token "topsecret-PII"}]`
literally CONTAINS `s:"topsecret-PII"`. state.cljc:59-61 says so explicitly:
"The bytes string is plain serializable EDN, so it rides the SSR / epoch / trace
wire with no custom transit handler."

Every released entry's resolved scope + canonical params therefore egress
off-box in plaintext on this row, for a `:sensitive?` / `:large?` /
derived-sensitive / unregistered owner alike.

WHY NO SHAPE RULE CATCHES IT. rf2-wd9im made the trace-egress fail-closed
default read value SHAPE, which closes every SCOPED KEY and every MAP payload at
any depth. A key-id is a STRING — correctly a scalar to that walk, since
tokenizing strings wholesale would destroy `:rf.frame/id` / `:cause` / short-id
attribution across the family. The payload is hidden inside an encoded scalar,
which is a class the shape walk cannot and should not try to detect.

DECISION NEEDED (this is why it is a bead and not a drive-by fix): what should a
key-id project to off-box?

  (a) Replace it with the PROJECTED SCOPED KEY. `:released` becomes a vector of
      `[<token-or-scope> resource-id <token-or-params>]`, i.e. identical in shape
      and treatment to `:matched` / `:blocking`. Best attribution (resource-id
      survives, per-key joins survive), and it makes `:released` consistent with
      every other key-bearing slot. Cost: the handler has the key-ids, not the
      scoped keys — the projector cannot recover a scoped key from a key-id
      without the entries map, so either the EMIT SITE must carry
      `(:resource/key entry)` instead of the k-id, or the projector needs a
      reverse lookup it currently has no access to. The emit-site change looks
      right and is small — the sibling `now-owner-free` computation in the SAME
      handler already collects `(:resource/key e)` (events.cljc:1911-1915), so
      the scoped keys are in hand two lines away.
  (b) Tokenize the key-id string via `ssr/redact-value`. One line in the
      projector, but it needs a KEY-ID SLOT vocabulary (a name roster — the very
      thing rf2-wd9im retired), and it destroys the resource-id, so a tool loses
      "which resource was released".

RECOMMENDATION: (a), at the emit site — carry `(:resource/key entry)` for
`:released` exactly as `now-owner-free` already does, so the existing
scoped-key projection covers it with no new vocabulary and better attribution
than today.

ALSO CHECK, same class, same question: grep the family for any other tag whose
value is a key-id rather than a scoped key. rf2-wd9im's survey found only
`:released`, but it was surveying for SEQUENTIAL SHAPES, not for encoded
scalars, so that is not a clean negative.

TEST OBLIGATION. A privacy fix needs a test that can red: assert no CEDN
plaintext (`s:"…"` / the raw secret substring) survives
`epoch/projected-record` for a `:sensitive?` owner's `:rf.resource/owner-released`
row, and confirm it fails on the unfixed code. Note rf2-wd9im's finding that
`epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` carries NO resource-family rows at all,
so that gate will not catch this either (rf2-isp3i owns widening it).

GATES: `implementation/epoch` + `implementation/resources` `clojure -M:test`.
notes:
PR #7018 (branch worker/released-keyids, commit 74e2346829). NOT closed — mayor closes on the merged SHA.

PREMISE CONFIRMED empirically, not by reading. Produced a key-id from a scoped key carrying a
recognisable secret and read it back:

  scoped-key : [:rf.scope/global :secret/article {:auth-token "topsecret-PII"}]
  key-id     : "v[k::rf.scope/global k::secret/article m{k::auth-token s:\"topsecret-PII\"}]"

key-id IS canonical-bytes (no hashing step exists); the raw secret, the `s:"…"` string token, the
resolved scope and the resource-id all come back. Recommendation (a) was correct, and the
`now-owner-free` sibling reading in the bead body checked out — it resolves each owned key-id through
`state/entry-path-by-id` and takes `(:resource/key e)`.

ALSO-CHECK RESULT — the survey the bead mandated found FIVE more instances of the same class, all in
`resources/ssr.cljc`, and ALL FIVE were confirmed leaking plaintext by the negative control (not by
inspection). `ssr.cljc` reconciles `:entries` with `reduce-kv`, so its fold key is a key-id too, and
its `:orphaned` / `:skews` accumulators feed trace tags:

  - `:rf.resource/hydrated`            `:orphaned-owners`  (hydrate)
  - `:rf.resource/hydrate-clock-skew`  `:resource/key`     (hydrate)
  - `:rf.resource/restored`            `:orphaned-owners`  (restore)
  - `:rf.resource/owner-released`      `:resource/key`     (restore)
  - `:rf.resource/restore-clock-skew`  `:resource/key`     (restore)

The three `:resource/key` ones are the sharper case: that slot is NAMED in the projector's
single-scoped-key vocabulary, so a key-id there defeated an arm written specifically to redact it.
Spec 009 already documents both clock-skew rows as carrying `:resource/key` (= the scoped-key vector
in this family), so those two were spec DRIFT as well — code now matches spec, no spec edit needed,
spec/009 untouched (rf2-p3u59's).

Fixed all six with the one move (carry `(:resource/key entry)`) rather than filing five follow-ups for
a mechanical change already identified on a P1 privacy surface. `:clock-skews` (a map keyed by the
same value) was already covered — the projector tokenizes any map wholesale.

LEAK SIGNATURE worth keeping: one unfixed `:rf.resource/owner-released` row carried the SAME identity
twice — tokenized under `:aborted` (the `[:rf.work/resource <scoped-key> <gen>]` work-id, covered by
rf2-wd9im's shape walk) and RAW under `:released` — so the row was stamped `:sensitive? true` while
the secret rode beside the stamp. Post-fix the two agree digest-for-digest, so per-key joins survive.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: 9 deftests / 52 assertions. Fixed 0 failures (rc 0); source reverted in place
33 failures (rc 1), the report printing the raw CEDN string; restored 0 failures (rc 0). 7 of 9 red on
revert; 2 green in BOTH directions — the premise guard and the over-redaction control
(`plain-owners-key-is-never-tokenized`), so over-redaction fails as loudly as leaking.

rf2-isp3i RESCOPING CONFIRMED on this checkout: `epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` has ZERO
occurrences of `reg-resource` / `:rf.resource/` / `:rf.mutation/` / `resources`, so this defect was
invisible to that gate too. Fixture NOT widened here. rf2-1zc33 untouched.

GATES (all foreground to completion, rc 0): resources 731/6781, epoch 476/6469, npm test:cljs
11462/57397 (new suite is dual-target and compiled into the node-test bundle), test-fast-pr.sh
"PASS fast PR spine". Full CI green on #7018, zero failing checks.
AUDIT OF MERGED PR #7018 (2026-07-25T18:00:49Z; merge f35d8fd865ba7c7904cf7e70e283fa408651ef1f) — REOPENED.

The emit-site privacy direction is correct, but the SSR widening changed the hydrate and restore `:skews` accumulator from a byte-keyed map to a scoped-key-keyed map. That loses the byte-identity invariant rf2-wgutc2 established: Clojure considers list and vector collections sequentially equal even though CEDN `canonical-bytes` makes them distinct resource identities.

Runtime reproduction on the merged code: two entries with the same scope/resource-id and params `{:xs [1 2 3]}` versus `{:xs '(1 2 3)}` produced `scoped-keys-clojure-equal=true`, `key-ids-equal=false`, two input entries, but only ONE `:rf.resource/hydrate-clock-skew` row and one `:clock-skews` summary member. The same accumulator shape exists on restore. Thus one distinct entry's diagnostic identity/skew silently disappears.

Bounded fix: keep byte key-id (or a sequence) as the internal uniqueness carrier while carrying each entry's scoped key in the accumulator value, then emit/project only the scoped key. Add a dual-target regression with both kind-colliding entries proving two hydrate and two restore skew rows/summary members, no CEDN key-id in trace tags, and correct owner-aware projection. Do not add string parsing, projector vocabulary, or a new framework.

Evidence: authored/merged blobs match for all three touched files; `git diff --check` clean; 75 checks (44 success, 31 skipped, none failed); new suite 9 tests/52 assertions green. The existing suite only supplies one skewed entry, so it cannot expose the collision. No exact separate Bead matched searches for hydrate/restore skew, scoped-key map collapse, or collection-kind identity; this PR's exact closed owner is therefore reopened rather than duplicated. Priority remains P1.
WORKER (this reopen): PR #7067 MERGED 554f50d71d — blobs verified byte-identical to the pushed tip for all four touched files.

REOPEN CLASS: **the close introduced it**. The emit-site privacy direction was right and that leak stays closed; the defect is collateral of the same widening. Carrying (:resource/key entry) put the scoped key in a MAP KEY position, and resource identity is the CEDN key-id, which is collection-KIND sensitive (rf2-wgutc2).

REPRODUCED on merged code, exactly as the audit measured: two entries with params {:xs [1 2 3]} vs {:xs '(1 2 3)} — scoped-keys-clojure-equal=true, key-ids-equal=false, 2 entries in — produced ONE :rf.resource/hydrate-clock-skew row and ONE :clock-skews member; same on restore.

SCOPE CONFIRMED, not assumed: :orphaned was a SEQUENCE from the start and reported BOTH entries in the same run (orphaned-owners=2 pre- and post-fix), so the defect is the accumulator's KEY, not the reconcile. Only :skews needed changing.

FIX: :skews is a sequence. reduce-kv visits each key-id once, so one entry in is one member out, and the scoped key rides in the VALUE where it is emitted rather than where it decides identity. :clock-skews therefore egresses as a vector of [<scoped-key> <skew-ms>] pairs — the shape :orphaned-owners beside it already had — which the shape default walks PER MEMBER, so each key projects through its own owner and per-key joins survive where the map tokenized wholesale. No string parsing, no projector vocabulary, no framework.

SPEC: :clock-skews appears nowhere in spec/, docs/ or tools/ (git grep over tracked files). No spec edit; spec/009 untouched (fenced).

COVERAGE: one dual-target deftest, both paths, both kind-colliding entries — 2 skew rows, 2 summary members, the two members carrying the two DISTINCT params collections (compared by KIND: = is precisely what cannot tell them apart, and a #{} literal of the two throws Duplicate key), 2 DIFFERENT digests off-box, no CEDN token, no plaintext.

title: [BUG] :rf.resource/route-plan's :blocking / :identities scoped keys escape the resources off-box egress projector
description:
Found by rf2-wsopx while verifying the `:rf.resource/route-plan` tag roster against
its emitting site (PR #7011). Documentation-only bead; this is the runtime half.

THE GAP. `:rf.resource/route-plan`'s activation shape carries TWO slots that are
VECTORS OF SCOPED RESOURCE KEYS — `:blocking` and `:identities`
(implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1091-1092). A scoped
resource key is `[scope resource-id canonical-params]`, so both slots carry the
resolved SCOPE and the CANONICAL PARAMS of every requirement in the plan.

The resource family's off-box egress projector
(implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc) exists precisely
to tokenize those through the resource OWNER classification. Its `scoped-keys-slot`
vocabulary (:127-137) is:

  #{:resource/keys :matched :removed :keys :exempt :committed :patched :populated
    :invalidated :restored :conflicted :refetched :restored-keys :conflicted-keys
    :refetched-keys :reconciliation-refetches :affected-keys}

NEITHER `:blocking` NOR `:identities` is in it.

The projector DOES run on this row — `project-resource-trace-egress` is applied to
every resource-family op (`resource-family-op?` is operation-agnostic,
implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1493-1497). And the
fail-closed default added by rf2-7qbxbm covers only MAP-valued unknown slots
(trace_egress.cljc:334); a SEQUENTIAL unknown value falls through to the verbatim
`:else` at :337. So a `:sensitive?` / `:large?` / derived-sensitive / unregistered
owner's scope and params egress RAW on this row, where the very same scoped keys
under `:matched` or `:keys` would tokenize to `{:rf/redacted <digest>}`.

WHY THE SLOT VOCABULARY MISSED THEM. The vocabulary was enumerated from the
events/mutation/reconcile rows (its own docstring lists exactly those families).
`:rf.resource/route-plan`'s `:blocking` / `:identities` slots are EP-0037 R1/R2
additions to a row that predates the projector, and the projector is keyed on slot
NAME rather than on value SHAPE, so a new scoped-key-bearing slot name is silently
uncovered. That is the class to fix, not just the two instances.

ADJACENT HAZARD, CHECKED AND BENIGN. `:removed` IS in `scoped-keys-slot`, and this
row carries `:removed` as an INT count, not a key vector (route.cljc:1090). The
`(sequential? v)` guard at :259 means it falls through harmlessly. No bug — but it
is evidence that the row and the projector were written against different mental
models of what `:removed` means, which is worth a comment wherever this is fixed.

WHAT THE WARM SHAPE DOES. `route-resource-warm-plan` (route.cljc:1236-1241) carries
NEITHER slot, so the warm-mode prefetch row is unaffected.

REPAIR (small, one file):
1. Add `:blocking` and `:identities` to `scoped-keys-slot` in
   `resources/trace_egress.cljc`, with a comment naming this bead and stating that
   they are `:rf.resource/route-plan`'s plan-membership slots.
2. Extend the projector's own tests with a `:rf.resource/route-plan` row over a
   `:sensitive?` owner, asserting BOTH slots tokenize per-key (so a tool's per-key
   joins survive) and the row is stamped `:sensitive? true`.
3. Consider — and this is the real question, so RULE it rather than assume — whether
   the fail-closed default should extend from map-valued unknown slots to
   VECTOR-OF-VECTOR-valued unknown slots. That would close the class rather than the
   instance: any future scoped-key-bearing slot name would fail closed instead of
   riding verbatim. The counterweight is over-redaction of legitimate scalar-vector
   slots (`:branch` is a vector of route ids on this very row and MUST ride
   verbatim; `:invalidated-tags` likewise), so a shape test alone is not sufficient
   discrimination and the guard would need to be "vector whose members are vectors"
   at minimum. My recommendation: do (1) + (2) now, and treat (3) as a separate
   design decision.

DO NOT widen the 009 documentation for this — PR #7011 already documents both slots
as scoped-key vectors, which is what makes the gap legible. This bead is the runtime
projector only.

GATES: the resources JVM suite; `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`.
Isolated surface (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc`
plus its test) — parallel-safe.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7013 (merge ddd1c5cf07dfcba51b9b72f33a89f0dd42e6954f, 2026-07-25T17:21:54Z) — exact-owner follow-up; priority raised to P1. The shape-driven fix closes map-param scoped keys, but scoped-key-shape? requires (map? canonical-params) even though registered params schemas can legally admit vectors/scalars/nil. Non-map sensitive scoped keys in unnamed slots fall through the recursive collection walk as structural scalars, so owner-aware projection never runs, the row is not stamped :sensitive?, and scope/params egress raw. Public-path reproduction on the merged commit: register :secret/vector with {:sensitive? true :params-schema [:vector :string]}, put [:rf.scope/global :secret/vector ["vector-secret-PII"]] under route-plan :blocking/:identities, then epoch/projected-record => {:projected-blocking [[:rf.scope/global :secret/vector ["vector-secret-PII"]]], :sensitive? nil, :raw-secret-survives? true}. This also reaches embedded resource work IDs and other unnamed slots carrying legal non-map-param scoped keys. Acceptance: owner-aware projection must cover every legal canonical-param shape without misclassifying structural owner/cause vectors; add a public-path sensitive vector-param regression for :blocking/:identities and the shared embedded-work-id path; assert no raw secret and :sensitive? true; preserve plain-owner and structural collection behavior; negative control must red against ddd1c5. Keep the centralized projector—do not add a second framework or an exhaustive slot roster. Existing rf2-5o52l, rf2-1zc33, and rf2-isp3i remain the exact owners of the PR's separate released-key-id, raw-scope, and conformance-fixture findings.
close_reason:
PR #7115 (worker/res-egress-lane2, 8bb3b0c60e + a7d13bc27f) — the MERGED-PR AUDIT #7013 finding on this bead is closed. `scoped-key-shape?` required (map? canonical-params), but :params-schema is REQUIRED and free, so a REGISTERED owner's canonical params are legally a vector / scalar / nil. Such a key wore the positional skeleton and failed the only proof, fell through the recursive walk as structural scalars, the row was not stamped :sensitive?, and scope+params egressed RAW under :blocking / :identities and inside every embedded :work/id.

REPAIR, one predicate: `scoped-key-frame?` (new) names the shared skeleton; `scoped-key-shape?` = skeleton + (map at 2 OR the RESOURCE REGISTRY knows position 1); `carrier-family-value?` now reads the bare skeleton plus its own two proofs instead of stacking the redundant map test on them. The registry is the family's OWN authority (carrier-family-value? already read it one carrier out for this exact question), not a roster, cannot rot, and says nothing about :owner's :l or :cause's :m/save — a MUTATION id is in a different registrar. Centralized projector kept; no second framework, no slot roster grown.

REJECTED, as the bead's own §(3) weighed: the vector-of-vector shape guard. :branch is a vector of route ids on this very row; the new negative control asserts a THREE-id :branch rides verbatim, which that guard could not do.

PROOF: public-path reproduction per the audit — register :secret/vector-params {:sensitive? true :params-schema [:vector :string]}, drive a REAL ensure with :reply-to, read back through epoch/projected-record. Reverting only the predicate reds the epoch suite at 523/6931 with 24 failures rc=1 vs 523/6931 0 failures rc=0 — identical counts, differing only in failures, all 24 inside the 9 new deftests. Two-sided controls (plain vector-params owner, :owner/:cause/:branch, :include-sensitive?) green in BOTH directions.

GATES: epoch 523/6931 rc=0; resources 734/6820 rc=0; core 2126/10492 rc=0; test-fast-pr.sh PASS rc=0 (CLJS node 11583/58140 rc=0).

RESIDUE FILED not absorbed: rf2-pwxsk (P3) — a non-map-params key naming an UNREGISTERED owner under an UNNAMED slot on a family row has neither proof left and is indistinguishable from [:app :l 1]; recommendation on the bead is close-as-accepted-boundary.

title: BLOCKS ALPHA TAG: CLOJARS_USERNAME/CLOJARS_PASSWORD do not exist as secrets, and release.yml comments claim they are configured
description:
Found by a CROSS-MODEL second-opinion review of alpha readiness, and independently re-verified by the mayor before filing. Five same-model reviewers and the mayor all missed it, because they all reasoned about code and docs while this one asked whether the CREDENTIALS EXIST.

VERIFIED TWICE, by two different agents:
  gh api repos/day8/re-frame2/actions/secrets        -> total_count: 0
  gh api repos/day8/re-frame2/actions/organization-secrets -> total_count: 0
  gh api repos/day8/re-frame2/environments           -> only github-pages, which the release workflow never references

Meanwhile .github/workflows/release.yml:371-372 consumes ${{ secrets.CLOJARS_USERNAME }} and ${{ secrets.CLOJARS_PASSWORD }}, and its own comment at :138-139 asserts "CLOJARS_USERNAME and CLOJARS_PASSWORD are configured at the repository level." That comment is FALSE. It is the same defect class as several found today — a comment asserting a fact nothing verifies — except this one gates the first public release.

CONSEQUENCE: pushing v0.0.1.alpha today CANNOT COMPLETE A RELEASE. It is NOT a partial-publish danger, which is the reassuring half: deploy-core gates every downstream leaf, so the run fails CLEAN and COMPLETE at step 3 of 14, before any Clojars upload. Nothing is published, nothing is orphaned, no coordinate is burned. But the tag itself is pushed and immutable, so the operator ends up with a public tag and no artefacts, and must either delete a public tag or bump VERSION to try again.

WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT: the pre-alpha sweep covered performance, back-compat, test rigour, clarity, docs and comments; two EP-0037 gates covered correctness, completeness and implementation quality; the merged-PR audit covers per-PR completeness/correctness/implementation-quality. NONE of those lenses looks at repository configuration. And docs/release-process.md pre-flight checklist does not ask anyone to verify the secrets exist — so the one document that should have caught it does not.

THE FIX, in order:
  1. OPERATOR ACTION: create CLOJARS_USERNAME and CLOJARS_PASSWORD as repository secrets (per re-frame v1 convention CLOJARS_PASSWORD is a deploy token, not the account password). This is Mikes to do; nobody else can.
  2. Add a pre-flight line to docs/release-process.md requiring the secrets be verified present before pushing a tag, so the checklist covers the thing the pipeline cannot run without.
  3. Correct the release.yml comment at :138-139 so it states the requirement rather than asserting a configuration that may not hold. A comment that asserts an unverifiable environment fact is worse than no comment.
  4. CONSIDER, and this is a judgement call rather than a requirement: a cheap pre-flight job that fails fast with a clear message when the secrets are absent, rather than failing inside clein deploy. Only worth it if it is a few lines — do not build a release-preflight framework.

NOTE the tag ordering makes this recoverable but annoying: the tag is pushed BEFORE the pipeline runs, so a failed run leaves a public tag pointing at a commit whose artefacts never shipped. Deleting a public tag is possible but is itself a public act. Better to verify the secrets first.

Filed P1 as a TAG BLOCKER of a different kind from the two already closed: rf2-9yvpf and rf2-p4a93 were "this would publish something wrong"; this one is "this cannot publish at all."
close_reason:
CLOSED BY OPERATOR INSTRUCTION (Mike, 2026-07-26): "Close rf2-i3gl2 - I will get to that later and it keeps coming up."

NOT FIXED, NOT REFUTED — deliberately parked. Closing so it stops surfacing in every ready-queue review. The finding below is preserved because the tag work will need it, and because a future reader hitting a failed tag deserves the answer immediately rather than re-deriving it.

THE FINDING, verified twice via the GitHub API by two different agents: CLOJARS_USERNAME and CLOJARS_PASSWORD DO NOT EXIST as repository or organisation secrets (total_count: 0 on both), while .github/workflows/release.yml:138 carries a comment asserting they are configured and lines 371-372 consume them.

CONSEQUENCE IF THE TAG IS PUSHED AS-IS: the release fails CLEAN at step 3 of 14. deploy-core gates every leaf, so NOTHING publishes and no Clojars coordinate is orphaned — the failure mode is a red pipeline, not a corrupt release. That is why this was never tag-BLOCKING in the destructive sense; it is tag-COMPLETING.

WHAT IT NEEDS: the operator to create the two secrets. No code change; nothing an agent can do.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, worth recording: a CROSS-MODEL review (deliberately dispatched at a different model tier) caught it after FIVE same-model reviewers had passed over the same workflow. It is the strongest argument in this session for varying the reviewer rather than repeating one.

title: Door parity breaks on :query-defaults — the named-address door resolves a different target, URL and resource identity than the three URL doors
description:
EP-0037 review gate 1 (rf2-kqxe6.14) finding — REPRODUCED on the JVM. The named-address door and the three URL-bearing doors disagree about the resolved target for any route declaring `:query-defaults`, which breaks EP conformance row 2 (door parity) and makes row 7's intent prefetch INERT for such routes.

## The defect

`:query-defaults` is filled in by `match-url` (Spec 012 §Reserved route-metadata keys: "Applied during `match-url`"; §Query strings: "populates absent query keys at match time"). The named-address path — `[:rf.route/navigate {:to … :params …}]`, `route-url`, `rf/route-link`'s href projection and `[:rf.route/prefetch …]` — never goes through `match-url`, so it never fills them. Spec 012's governing law for the programme says the opposite: "Doors differ in cause and history / scroll policy, not in target, entry, resource, or readiness semantics" (§The one planning pipeline; restated verbatim in `re-frame.routing.resolve`'s ns docstring).

Route under test — nothing exotic, the shape `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs` ships four times over (`:query-defaults {:page 1}`):

    (rf/reg-route :d/page
      {:params         [:map [:slug :string]]
       :query          [:map [:tab {:optional true} [:enum :overview :comments]]]
       :query-defaults {:tab :overview}
       :resources      [{:id :page :resource :d/page
                         :params (fn [r] {:slug (get-in r [:params :slug])
                                          :tab  (get-in r [:query :tab])})
                         :blocking? true}]}
      "/p/:slug")

Four doors, four fresh frames, same logical destination `{:to :d/page :params {:slug "x"}}` / `"/p/x"`:

| door | committed `:query` | derived URL | resource identity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:rf.route/navigate {:to …}` | `{}` | `/p/x` | `{:slug "x" :tab nil}` |
| `:rf.route/navigate {:url …}` | `{:tab :overview}` | `/p/x?tab=overview` | `{:slug "x" :tab :overview}` |
| `:rf.route/url-requested` (link) | `{:tab :overview}` | `/p/x?tab=overview` | `{:slug "x" :tab :overview}` |
| `:rf.route/handle-url-change` | `{:tab :overview}` | `/p/x?tab=overview` | `{:slug "x" :tab :overview}` |

So the same destination commits a different slice, derives a different URL (a different history entry), and selects a DIFFERENT resource cache identity depending on which door the user came through.

## The prism does not round-trip

    (routing/route-url {:to :d/page :params {:slug "x"}})   ;=> "/p/x"
    (routing/match-url "/p/x")                              ;=> :query {:tab :overview}

`match-url(route-url(x)) ≠ x`. Spec 012 calls `:path` / `:params` / `:query` / `:query-defaults` "the contract surface that `match-url` and `route-url` agree on" (§Reserved route-metadata keys, Shape row). They do not agree when `:query-defaults` is declared.

## Row 7's headline capability is inert for these routes

One frame. Hover the link, then click that same link:

    props  {:to :d/page :params {:slug "x"} :prefetch :intent}
    href                  "/p/x"
    prefetch payload      [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :d/page :params {:slug "x"}}]
    after hover  (warm)   {[… :d/page {:slug "x" :tab nil}]      {:attempt 1 :owners []}}
    after click (active)  {[… :d/page {:slug "x" :tab nil}]      {:attempt 1 :owners []}
                           [… :d/page {:slug "x" :tab :overview}] {:attempt 1 :owners [[:route :d/page "nav-1"]]}}
    entry count           2

The warm entry is orphaned — ownerless, GC-eligible, never reused — and the click starts a FRESH first load on a second identity (`:attempt 1`, new owner). EP-0037 R3's whole promise ("later activation reuses fresh/in-flight work and attaches its real owner") does not hold for any route with `:query-defaults`. It fails silently: a passive-looking prefetch is indistinguishable from a working one without measuring, which is exactly the argument `link/validate-prefetch!` makes for failing loud on a bad `:prefetch` value.

## Why no suite caught it

Nothing in the corpus combines `:query-defaults` with `:resources`. `git grep -l query-defaults` over `implementation/*/test` and `spec/conformance/fixtures` returns `routing_classification_test`, `routing_registry_test`, `routing_url_non_edn_cljs_test`, `routing-match-url.edn`, `routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn`, `routing-query-string-coercion.edn` — not one of which declares `:resources`. R6's `every-door-plans-the-same-branch-and-the-same-reads` compares all five doors over target / URL / chain / identity set, but its exercise app declares no `:query-defaults`, so the arm passes. `routing_prism_property_cljs_test`'s generative round-trip never draws a route with `:query-defaults` either, so property 1 never sees the case.

## Bounded repair — one rule, and the choice of rule is a RULING

Fill `:query-defaults` for absent keys in the ONE named-address→ResolvedTarget resolution (`re-frame.routing.resolve`), so every door resolves the same target. Two candidate spellings of the URL half:

  (a) FILL AND OMIT — the resolved target carries `{:tab :overview}`, and `route-url` continues to omit a query key whose value equals the route's declared default. URLs stay clean (`/p/x`), `match-url` refills on the way back, so target-level round-trip holds and all doors agree. Preferred by the reviewer: it changes no emitted href.

  (b) FILL AND EMIT — `route-url` emits `?tab=overview`. Simpler, but it changes every href a `:query-defaults` route renders and lengthens shipped URLs.

Either way the fix belongs in the one resolution seam, not per-door, and prefetch inherits it for free because it resolves through the same boundary (`rf2-kqxe6.7`'s destination-resolution gate).

REGRESSION COVERAGE OWED: (1) extend R6's door-parity arm's exercise app with one `:query-defaults` route + a resource whose identity reads that query key, so the five-door footprint comparison covers it; (2) one hover-then-click reuse arm asserting ONE entry with the activation's owner attached and `:attempt 1` (warm work joined, not restarted); (3) one `routing_prism_property_cljs_test` draw over a `:query-defaults` route. Each shown non-vacuous against current `main`.

NOT WANTED: a second normalisation pass, a per-door defaults hook, or a public `:query-defaults` resolution API.
notes:
AUDIT PR #7000 (2026-07-25): REMAINS OPEN — the optional-key case is repaired, but a schema-required query key supplied by `:query-defaults` still splits the prism and named doors.

Reproduction on the landed tip: register `{:query [:map [:page :int]], :query-defaults {:page 1}}` at `/audit-required-default`. `match-url "/audit-required-default"` succeeds with `{:query {:page 1}, :validation-failed? false}`, while `route-url {:to ...}` throws `:rf.error/route-url-validation` with `{:slot :query, :value {}}`. The route is valid: Spec 012 says every query key is optional from the URL's perspective and defaults populate absence.

Cause: `route-url` validates its nil-elided raw `emitted-query` before any call to `query-with-defaults`; it only removes equal defaults later for emission. Thus the public `route-url` and `route-link` href projection reject the destination, and prefetch's `destination-error` calls `route-url` before `resolver/resolved-target`, so hover warmup rejects too. Programmatic navigate happens to work because it fills through `resolved-target` before calling `route-url`. This directly contradicts the new claim that `route-url`, links, and prefetch all fill at the one resolution seam.

Repair at this exact owner: validate the filled query at the named-address/route-url boundary, then elide equal defaults only for URL emission. Add a required-schema/default regression through direct `route-url`, route-link href, prefetch, and the door-parity matrix. Do not add another defaults API or per-door hook. The landed optional-key matrix, canonical omission rule, and shared helper are otherwise sound. Both authored commits map one-for-one to landed commits by stable patch-id; all 73 PR checks were non-failing; local routing and resources JVM suites passed, so the required-default repro identifies a real coverage gap.
close_reason:
PR #7000 MERGED (2026-07-25T14:51:45Z). The only P1 EP-0037 independent correctness review found, fixed at ONE seam as instructed.

THE SEAM: re-frame.routing.resolve/resolved-target — the one ResolvedTarget fact-shaping function every door already lowers to. And spec/012 DEFINES a ResolvedTarget as planner output "after matching, DEFAULTS, and validation", so the defaults step was already specified at that seam and simply unapplied. That is the FOURTH instance in two days of the fix already being written down: frame.cljc docstring prescribing the get-in change four siblings missed; behaviours.cljc ns docstring stating the memory law 300 lines above the code that broke it; v/custom-element docstring plus dyn-attr-entry own comment stating the declared-property precedence; and now spec/012 own definition of ResolvedTarget.

THE ONE RULE that stopped this being four patches: a declared default lives in the TARGET, never in the URL. Because route-url omits a key already at its default, NO emitted href changes, each destination gets exactly one canonical URL, route-url composed with match-url becomes the identity on every URL re-frame2 emits, and the href builder needed no patch at all. The emission inverse (query-with-defaults / query-without-defaults) sits beside the fill rule in registry.cljc, the namespace that owns what :query-defaults means, both keyed off one accessor. It REJECTED the fill-and-emit spelling on evidence: it lengthens every shipped URL and still leaves the round-trip non-identity.

TWO INCIDENTAL WINS: navigate spelled the ResolvedTarget TWICE (inline for decisions/decide, via the seam for the plan) and now shapes it once for guards, plan and commit; and the fill landing before identical-nav? fixes a SECOND live symptom nobody had filed — a repeat navigate to a place first reached by URL compared unequal and re-fired :on-match on a fresh nav-token.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: revert-in-place gives routing 3 failures and resources 8 failures, rc=1 both; with the fix, 501/2705 and 722/6729 at 0. Gates re-run against the merged tree after main advanced. Fixture blindness closed on all three fronts the bead named, plus a seam unit test.

MOST INSTRUCTIVE PART, and the reason I trust the rest: its FIRST DRAFT of the hover-then-click arm was a self-inflicted false green. It dispatched a hand-written [:rf.route/navigate {:to ...}] for the click — the SAME named door the hover used — so both landed on {:tab nil} and the arm PASSED PRE-FIX. It caught that only by running the negative control, then rewrote both halves to come off one props map through the two seams a real anchor uses (prefetch-payload and link-model :payload).

title: F6c: migrate Xray's view instrumentation onto re-frame.freehand.tool - the ownership/receipt plane has no Freehand counterpart
description:
Split out of F6c (rf2-drpa3.55) after survey: this is a bead-sized architectural change, not a rename, and doing it half-way would ship a panel that displays facts Freehand does not have.

WHAT XRAY READS TODAY. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs (466 lines) requires [re-frame.ui.tool] AND [re-frame.ui.tool.evidence]. Its whole reason for existing is an OWNERSHIP/RECEIPT ledger layered over the donor evidence tier's install/uninstall registry: evidence/install!, evidence/uninstall!, evidence/installed-owner, evidence/force-release!, plus a per-span opaque receipt fencing every read against a same-key ABA reclaim, plus an ownership-revision reactive bridge into Xray's own :rf/xray app-db (panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs).

WHY IT IS NOT A RENAME. re-frame.freehand.tool has NO registry and NO ownership plane, deliberately and permanently - its own docstring says 'There is no accumulator... no root registry, no interval log and no history store' and names rf2-drpa3.167 as having ruled the donor accumulator out permanently rather than deferred it. So none of install!/uninstall!/installed-owner/force-release! has a counterpart, and the receipt fence protects against a hazard that cannot occur. The ownership plane and its reactive-revision bridge should be DELETED, not ported.

AND THE PANEL'S VOCABULARY CHANGES. viewcell_evidence/project-occurrence shapes rows around :count (lifetime render total), :batches, :first-epoch, :latest-epoch, :lifecycle (hide-vs-unmount interval log), :targets + :targets-exact?, :dropped-count + :dropped-exact?. Every one of those is a fact rf2-drpa3.167 named as DELIBERATE FIDELITY LOSS. reactive_panel_view.cljs:647-760 renders them, including a literal 'Cumulative per-incarnation render evidence' label. Freehand's read-mounted-views gives current-state rows (:view-id :occurrence :lowering :generation :connection :root :dispatch-id :at :commit, with :occurrence-facts naming the closed set) and explain-render gives a bounded read-time fold with :cap / :uncorrelated loss and :candidates as leads. The panel must be re-authored to those, showing honest absence where a lifetime figure used to sit - per the ruling, degrading a missing fact to an explicit unknown SATISFIES acceptance 2; fabricating one does not.

ALSO. The consumer-owned version pin moves from the integer expected-schema-version 3 (:rf.ui.tool/version) to :re-frame.freehand.evidence/v1 (:schema), exactly as pair-mcp did in the first F6c increment - see that PR for the shape.

SCOPE (ledger rows). tools/xray/deps.edn (drop the day8/re-frame2-ui coordinate), viewcell_evidence.cljs, panels/reactive_panel_{view,subs}.cljs, test/viewcell_evidence_cljs_test.cljs (682 lines), test/realworld_ui_evidence_cljs_test.cljs, tools/xray/spec/* - and per standing rule every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs mounts donor views and is a separate row.

SEQUENCING NOTE. realworld_ui_evidence_cljs_test.cljs reads a donor-authored example under examples/, whose migration is a carved-out parallel bead - sequence after it, or repoint the test at a Freehand fixture.
notes:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26), quoted verbatim across the two messages that settle it:

  "We intend to remove the donor (re-frame.ui)"

THIS SETTLES THE GATE. Both of the F6c gate beads asked the same either/or: build the Freehand counterpart, or retire the seam with the donor. The answer is BUILD THE COUNTERPART AND CROSS OVER. The donor is going (rf2-drpa3.57 / F6e deletes implementation/ui wholesale), so a tool still reading it is not a stable position — it is a dependency on an artefact scheduled for deletion.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c) has been in_progress and gated on exactly these two. F6c releases F6d (rf2-drpa3.56, the donor inventory ledger to zero) which releases F6e (rf2-drpa3.57, the deletion). That chain has sat at 97.3% all session with no dispatchable work in it.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7038 (2026-07-26) — REOPENED: schema-4 live upgrade deletes the donor plane from source but does not tear down the plane an already-running schema-3 process owns.

EVIDENCE. Before this PR, preload/core acquired re-frame.ui.tool.evidence under :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence. Schema 4 explicitly exists for no-reload upgrades from schema 3, but migrate-schema! only calls reactive-panel/install-mounted-views-subs!. Removing the namespace/require does not execute teardown in an already-loaded HMR process; every former teardown call was removed from preload, core and test-support.

IMPACT. Until a full page reload, Xray still owns and runs the donor sink, retains the donor span, leaves its sentinel visible, and rejects another tool attempting to claim the slot. The old handlers/listener also remain process-resident. That contradicts this bead's central completion claim that the ownership plane was deleted and Xray holds no state, and it makes the documented schema-4 no-reload migration incomplete precisely on the stateful boundary it removes.

ACCEPTANCE. Add a schema-3 -> schema-4 upgrade proof starting from a genuinely acquired donor span and installed old bridge. If cross-generation teardown is intentionally reload-only, remove the no-reload schema-4 claim and force/document a reload instead of stamping the live process current over resident donor state.

title: whole-output :large? sub value egresses RAW in the :rf.sub/run trace tag (off-box token-budget leak; the :sub-runs row IS elided)
notes:
Found while mirroring the epoch egress-redaction tier onto the CLJS lane (rf2-p4515, PR #6974). NOT a privacy leak; a TOKEN-BUDGET / size leak on the off-box wire.

SYMPTOM. A subscription registered with the whole-output size marker

    (rf/reg-sub :big {:large? true} (fn [_ _] <25 KB string>))

read inside a cascade produces an epoch record with the value in TWO slots:

    [:sub-runs 0 :value]                        <- structured row
    [:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.sub/value]       <- the :rf.sub/run trace tag

`projected-record` (the single normative off-box egress site) elides the FIRST
and leaves the SECOND raw. Verified on origin/main @8240ff91a5, JVM lane:

    RAW  big-leaf paths: [[:sub-runs 0 :value] [:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.sub/value]]
    PROJ big-leaf paths: [[:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.sub/value]]

and the projected row is the expected marker:

    row :big value= #:rf.size{:large-elided {:path [:value] :bytes 25002 :type :string
                                             :reason :classification ...}}

while the projected trace tag still carries the 25000-char string, with
`:large? true` sitting right beside it in the same tags map.

WHY THE 136-DEFTEST JVM TIER MISSES IT. epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj
DOES own the cross-cutting claim ("no raw large bytes anywhere in the projected
output - the token-budget claim the MCP wire boundary depends on", via
`count-leaf-strings-at-least`), but its fixture declares `:large` as an APP-DB
PATH ([:blob :payload]) - a shape the walker substitutes inside the db slots.
The whole-output `:large?` SUB shape is exercised only by
epoch_privacy_test.clj `projected-record-elides-large-sub-output`, which probes
the `:sub-runs` row by hand and never scans the whole record. Neither arm can
see the trace-tag twin.

MECHANISM. `tool_pair/elide-sub-run-row` handles the whole-output `:large?`
case for the structured row (and strips the spent flag). The `:trace-events`
slot goes through `elide-trace-events-slot`, whose walk matches APP-DB-ROOTED
classification paths; `:rf.sub/value` is not app-db-rooted and the whole-output
`:large?` is a REGISTRATION marker on the tag, not a path declaration, so
nothing acts on it. Per-PATH `:large` sub marks are unaffected - those are
substituted at the EMIT site (`classification/redact-with-paths`) so they are
already elided in both slots. Same for per-path `:sensitive` marks, which is
why privacy is intact: EP-0025 dropped the whole-output `:sensitive?` overload
(classification.cljc:147 "silently dropped if present"), so there is no
sensitive analogue of this gap.

BLAST RADIUS. Every off-box consumer of `projected-record` / `projected-history`
that reads `:trace-events`: Xray-MCP watch-epochs, re-frame2-pair-mcp
trace-window / watch-epochs / snapshot, hosted log shippers. Under the shipped
`:trace-events-keep 50` (= :depth) EVERY record in the ring keeps its
trace-events, so the payload rides on every projected record for that cascade.

REPRO. Any lane. `reg-sub` with `{:large? true}`, read it via
`subscribe-once` inside a `reg-event`, dispatch, then walk
`(epoch/projected-record (last (rf/epoch-history fid)))` for leaf strings at or
above the payload size. One survives.

DECIDE THEN FIX. The obvious fix is to teach the epoch `:trace-events` egress
projector the same whole-output `:large?` substitution `elide-sub-run-row`
applies (marker in, spent flag stripped) for `:rf.sub/run` / `:rf.sub/dispose`
tags. Worth a ruling on whether the trace-tag value should carry the marker or
be dropped, and whether the on-box ring keeps it raw (it should - Xray diff and
restore-epoch! read the raw ring).

CHARACTERISED IN CODE. PR #6974's new dual-lane suite
(implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc,
`large-sub-output-value-slot-elides-at-egress`) carries a clearly-labelled
CHARACTERISATION assertion pinning today's raw tag, with an instruction to
DELETE it when the fix lands. Do not read it as an endorsement.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6985 (branch worker/subrun-egress).

REPRODUCED first, exactly as titled — probe on the base commit, public path:
  RAW  big-leaf paths: [[:sub-runs 0 :value] [:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.sub/value]]
  PROJ big-leaf paths: [[:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.sub/value]]   <- tag raw, row elided
with :large? true sitting in the same tags map as the 25000-char payload. Title
needed no correction. Post-fix the same probe prints PROJ big-leaf paths: [].

FIX — one rule at one seam, no second mechanism. The row's inlined whole-output
:large? logic is extracted to tool_pair/elide-whole-output-large-slots,
parameterised by its two value-slot keys; both egress paths now call it:
  elide-sub-run-row            -> :value / :prev-value
  elide-large-sub-trace-values -> :rf.sub/value / :rf.sub/prev-value  (new)
scoped to :rf.sub/run, the only op whose tags can carry the flag. MARKER not a
drop (Mike's ruling): the tag now carries the identical :rf.size/large-elided
representation, spent :large? flag stripped; tests assert both markers agree on
:bytes, which is the structural evidence one rule built both.

TESTS. The #6974 characterisation assertion that PINNED the raw tag was FLIPPED
(not deleted) — it lives in a dual-lane .cljc, so it was green on the JVM lane
too and was mutually invalidating with this fix. The record-wide
count-leaves-at-least scan that file had deliberately withheld is now asserted
with a non-vacuity control. The JVM privacy arm gained the tag twin.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: reverting the single new pipeline call in place reds 8
assertions across both deftests (4 each, rc=1) with the raw XXXX... payload
printed at [:tags :rf.sub/value].

GATES: epoch 470/6415 rc=0 (baseline 470/6401 — +14 assertions); core
2115/10456 rc=0; test:cljs 11438/57241 rc=0; test-fast-pr.sh rc=0 (its mkdocs
step soft-skipped, so mkdocs build --strict was run separately: rc=0).

spec/009: the :rf.sub/value / :rf.sub/prev-value rows already CLAIMED the marker
but attributed it to the emit chokepoint, which is not where the whole-output
case is honoured. Rows corrected to state the truth (stamped at the chokepoint,
elided one seam later at off-box egress via the rule shared with the row).
rf2-jew4k (spec/009:2391) untouched.

NOTE for follow-up consideration, not actioned (out of fence): the token-budget
gate epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj still declares :large as an app-db
PATH in its fixture, so it structurally cannot see the whole-output :large? SUB
shape — that fixture blindness is why this shipped. The new dual-lane record-wide
scan now covers the shape on both hosts, but widening the conformance fixture
would close the class rather than the instance.

title: DECISION: Freehand public React host door (leaf + wrapper mint vs official react-el interim)
description:
## Context
Spec 004 already classifies declared host descriptors as the third legal vector head. F5i pilot shows classify-head answers :host, but no public verb mints a host descriptor and both emitters refuse crossing (host-lifecycle slice later). Meanwhile react/createElement as a child value works today (isValidElement arm) and is the only practical React-component door.

Adversarial review (ai/findings/freehand-design-review/grok.md) ranks landing this door P0 for everyday + React-library lenses.

## Decision needed
Choose one product path (or staged pair):

A. Full public mint now — e.g. v/host or v/react producing a host descriptor; leaf (value props + D008 callbacks) and wrapper (hooks/context allowed only inside foreign component). Emitters cross the boundary.

B. Official interim only — document + helper v/react-el (or similar) over createElement + prop conversion + v/event proxies; full host descriptor still a later slice.

C. Staged — B ships immediately as supported API; A remains the target grammar with an explicit slice id and conformance rows.

## Constraints (settled, do not reopen)
- No bare-fn internal vector heads (D002)
- No hooks in Freehand view bodies
- D008 closed callback roster (no bare-fn inference from prop names)
- Behaviors remain the imperative non-React boundary (D013)

- Spec 004 §Qualified host leaves / vector-head classification

Mike rules A/B/C (or amend). Ruling recorded as D022 (or amendment to host-boundary sections) and EP-0036 slice ownership updated if needed.

notes:
MAYOR POSTURE TRIAGE of the opus5 adversarial design review (2026-07-25). Doc at ai/findings/freehand-design-review/opus5.md (552 lines, gitignored). It filed no beads by design; this is my read against the standing posture — pre-alpha, elegance and power, NOT over-engineering, trust the programmer, low friction. Three of its seven already have beads (this one, rf2-3ubnm, rf2-vjdsc), which is independent corroboration since the reviewer was told nothing about them.

CLEAR KEEPS — these FINISH surface rather than adding it, which is why the no-gold-plating rule does not bite:
  1. THE QUALIFIED HOST LEAF (third vector head). Not new surface: the classifier already recognises it, :rf.ui.error/view-bad-head names it as the recovery, and composition.md documents a worked example — while no public verb mints one. Today the substrate DOCUMENTS a door it does not open. That is a promise not kept, not a feature request. Highest leverage of the seven.
  2. ONE VERB TURNING A HICCUP VALUE INTO A REACT ELEMENT. The textbook case the posture explicitly blesses: one small primitive closing a whole class of pain (every React integration is currently hand-rolled createElement + #js, invisible to the tree and refused by the compiled grammar). One verb, not a subsystem.
  3. MOVE THE COMPILED TIER'S LARGEST REFUSAL CLASS FROM RENDER TIME TO BUILD TIME. This is a LYING GATE, same defect class as the four census false greens fixed today: helper-fn markup, mapv over rows and runtime props maps compile silently and throw at first render while the checker reports compile-eligible? true. Correctness, not polish.
  6. RECORD THE CONTROLLED-DOOR VERDICT AS A FACT. Cheap, pins something already true, stops it being rediscovered.

KEEP WITH A SCOPE NOTE:
  4. :props SCHEMAS VALIDATE VALUES IN DEVELOPMENT. Verified by render: [:map [:a :int]] silently accepts {} and {:a "not-an-int"} — closure is enforced, values are not. 'Trust the programmer' does NOT argue against this: a programmer who WRITES a schema is asking for validation, so honouring it is the low-friction reading, and a schema that does not validate is worse than no schema. Keep the dev-only scoping the reviewer proposed — this must not become a production tax or a nag-diagnostic.

TASTE CALLS FOR MIKE — I am NOT dispatching these:
  5. SHIP FOUR DOM VERBS AS FIRST-PARTY BEHAVIORS IN A NEW re-frame.freehand.host. This one genuinely adds a namespace plus four verbs. It is ergonomics if those four are what everyone hand-rolls, and scope creep if they are not. Needs Mike's judgement on whether the substrate owns DOM conveniences or the app does.
  7. LET PRESENCE COMPLETE ON THE CHILD'S OWN ANIMATION END. A real capability gap (AnimatePresence-style deferred unmount is unreachable today), but it is lifecycle machinery, and lifecycle is where a view substrate accretes complexity fastest. Worth doing if the React-library story is a priority; worth deferring if not.

SEPARATE FROM ALL OF THE ABOVE: the review verified FIVE defects that are ordinary bugs, not design proposals, and should be actioned regardless of how Mike rules on 5 and 7 — composition.md's foreign-widget sketch is invalid code that throws, js-libraries.md Pattern C's AnimatePresence sketch is broken, forms.md's canonical email-field teaches the O(N) shape exactly where it costs keystroke latency, the :props closure-only gap above, and ~54 of 74 compile-error ids falling back to the :keep-interpreted 'give up' rung. Filing those separately.

METHOD NOTE: the reviewer verified by rendering real code through re-frame.freehand.test/render on the JVM rather than reasoning from docs, and reports three things it EXPECTED broken that work (bare fns at native :on-* sites, re-com-style :attr/:style via spread-safe, per-keystroke caret/IME proven by FH-INPUT-003). That is why I am treating its defect list as evidence rather than opinion.

title: Add a per-lane test-count floor: a zero-test run currently exits 0 on every whole-suite lane
notes:
Filed by the pre-alpha tests/clarity audit (rf2-ods8n, lens B), 2026-07-25 19:15 AUSEST.

THE CLASS. The nine silently-skipped .cljc files were fixed instance by instance; the DETECTOR was never built. Every lane's whole-suite path treats 'Ran 0 tests / 0 failures, 0 errors' as green.

REPRO 1 (live, JVM lane):
  cd implementation/epoch && clojure -M:test -r '^zzz-nonexistent-namespace^'
  -> Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions. / 0 failures, 0 errors. / exit 0
(use a regex matching no ns; any will do)

REPRO 2 (browser lane, via the runner's own library):
  cd implementation && node -e "const {summaryPartsFromText,parseFailureCounts}=require('./scripts/lib/browser-test-report.cjs'); const p=summaryPartsFromText('Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions.\n0 failures, 0 errors.\n'); console.log(p, parseFailureCounts(p.failErr));"
  -> {failures:0, errors:0}. implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs:215-255 decides the verdict from parseFailureCounts ALONE. No floor on the 'Ran N' count it already parsed.

UPSTREAM HALF. shadow.build.test-util/find-test-namespaces (thheller/shadow-cljs 3.4.10) filters classpath nses by :ns-regexp and returns [] on no match, with no warning and no failure. Four lanes are selected by a SINGLE suffix convention and nothing else:
  :node-test                            cljs-test$              ~380 files
  :browser-test                         -dom-cljs-test$          30 files
  :browser-test-prod-elision            -elision-prod-test$      20 files
  :browser-test-schemas-boundary-prod   -boundary-prod-test$      1 file
A rename, a dropped :source-paths entry, or a one-character suffix drift silently empties a lane.

Node :else branch: test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs ends execute-cli with (st/run-all-tests test-env nil) -- no floor.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A SUGGESTION -- the project already holds this exact standard in two places and simply did not generalise it:
  1. shadow_node.cljs:210-224, for the --test= SELECTOR path: 'A --test= selection that matches no test var must not be a false green: run-test-vars over an empty set reports a 0-test success. Reject any unmatched selector.'
  2. core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:1727-1733 (rf2-3hamsq): (is (>= (count run) 150) ...) -- a non-empty floor on the conformance corpus.

REMEDY. A per-lane minimum test count, ratcheted like the README inventory ratchet. run-browser-tests.cjs already has the integer in hand (RAN_RE captures it). The JVM side needs a floor in re-frame.test-quiet.runner or a per-artefact wrapper assertion. Self-test the floor (prove it fires at N-1) as the sibling gates do.

NOT AN ALPHA BLOCKER -- a missing detector cannot itself have broken shipped behaviour. But it is the highest-leverage test-infrastructure fix available and it is why the nine-file incident took weeks rather than minutes to surface.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6975 (merged 2026-07-25T11:07:34Z) — REOPENED this exact zero-test-floor owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS: the PR's inventory missed the required `ui-scaffold-smoke` CI lane. `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke`, whose `deps.edn` still invokes `cognitect.test-runner` directly instead of `re-frame.test-quiet.runner`. Live repro on current main from that directory: `clojure -M:test -r '^zzz-nonexistent-namespace$'` prints `Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions. / 0 failures, 0 errors.` and exits 0. Thus one whole-suite required check still has the exact false-green class this Bead and PR claim to close.

BOUNDED REPAIR: route this one CI test alias through the existing quiet runner/floor (with its local test-quiet dependency), or equivalently apply the same shared floor at that alias; pin its zero-test red path and ordinary scaffold-smoke green path. Keep `rf2-4hc9p` separate: it owns partial lane collapse, while this is the original total-zero case. Do not build another runner or generalized inventory framework.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the JVM summary hook, Node whole-suite preflight, browser summary-count verdict, two explicit resolution probes, and fast-PR disclosure are otherwise coherent and reuse existing seams. The three source commits range-diff exactly 3/3. Current `implementation/test-quiet` gate is green (45 tests / 247 assertions); the two directly changed JS policy/helper suites are green (9 + 18 tests). The aggregate Windows script-policy command has an unrelated existing `_playground-sci-inputs` fixture failure; fast-PR self-test's newly added Q/R assertions pass while four older doc-fixture cases exit 127 on this host.

EVIDENCE: PR merge 84b0217c58a0cddfc04617e2000695fc83c68ee3. Exact existing owner search found `rf2-qqzmf`; `rf2-4hc9p` is deliberately not duplicated.
close_reason:
RESIDUAL CLOSED — PR #7001 (worker/scaffold-floor), 2026-07-26.

The merged-PR-#6975 audit's one remaining item: implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke's :test alias called cognitect.test-runner DIRECTLY, so it was the one whole-suite lane the floor never reached — and it is a REQUIRED CI check (ui-scaffold-smoke, gated on examples_compile).
