title: release.yml: ssr-ring can publish an unresolvable coordinate when the ssr leaf fails (fail-fast:false + local-m2 masking)
notes:
From rf2-ods8n lens A (perf + back-compat audit), 2026-07-25. BLOCKS THE ALPHA TAG.

PROBLEM. implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn declares TWO in-repo coordinates in its
published :deps —

  :deps {day8/re-frame2     {:local/root "../core"}
         day8/re-frame2-ssr {:local/root "../ssr"}}

— and the Rewrite step converts BOTH to :mvn/version. So day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring's
published pom depends on day8/re-frame2-ssr at the lockstep version. ssr-ring is the
ONLY leaf with a published-pom edge to a sibling leaf.

But .github/workflows/release.yml's deploy-leaf matrix sets `fail-fast: false` and
justifies it (lines ~330-339) with: "by design, since the published-pom DAG has no
edges between leaves and a partial-leaf-success is coherent". That premise is FALSE
for ssr-ring. The workflow's own comment at lines ~396-404 acknowledges the edge —
the two comments contradict each other.

WHY THE LEAF CANNOT SELF-DETECT. The "Install ssr to runner ~/.m2 (ssr-ring only)"
step (release.yml ~462-465) satisfies ssr-ring's ssr dependency from the runner's
LOCAL m2, not from Clojars. So ssr-ring deploys green whether or not the sibling ssr
leaf ever reached Clojars.

FAILURE SHAPE (permanent). ssr leaf fails for any reason (Clojars 5xx, token blip,
transient network) while ssr-ring succeeds => day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring 0.0.1.alpha is
PERMANENTLY on Clojars declaring a dependency on a day8/re-frame2-ssr version that
does not exist. Clojars has no yank. The documented recovery (bump VERSION, re-ship
all) supersedes but does not REMOVE the broken artefact, so any consumer pinning the
original alpha gets an unresolvable tree forever. This is exactly the partial-publish
shape the first tag is exposed to, and it is irreversible.

FIX (small, clarity-preserving — makes the real DAG visible in structure rather than
in a comment that contradicts it). Either:
  (a) hoist `ssr` out of the matrix into its own job, as `core` already is, and give
      deploy-leaf `needs: [deploy-core, deploy-ssr]`; or
  (b) split `ssr-ring` into its own job with `needs: [deploy-core, deploy-leaf]`.
Update the fail-fast rationale comment either way so it stops asserting there are no
inter-leaf edges.

Hot zone: .github/workflows/* — sequence, do not parallel.
close_reason:
PR #6967 MERGED (main 52c749657b), 35/35 non-skipped checks green. TAG BLOCKER CLEARED.

VERIFIED BEFORE FIXING, structurally rather than by grep: implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn is the ONLY one of the thirteen published artefacts carrying a second :local/root in its production :deps. deploy-leaf ran fail-fast:false with both ssr and ssr-ring as matrix values, and GHA has no edge between matrix values, so ssr red did not stop ssr-ring; the local-m2 install meant the job never consulted Clojars and could not self-detect.

THE FIX satisfies the acceptance property exactly: ssr-ring moves out of the matrix into its own deploy-ssr-ring job with needs: [deploy-core, deploy-leaf]. A needs edge onto a matrix job requires EVERY value to succeed, so if the ssr leaf does not publish successfully, ssr-ring does not publish at all. github-release gains the new job, so a SKIPPED ssr-ring cannot still cut a Release announcing the artefact. 'Sequence after the matrix' was chosen over hoisting ssr out too, on the grounds that any leaf failure means bump-and-re-ship everything under the documented recovery, so blocking costs nothing while the alternative duplicates a job body — reasoning recorded in the workflow header, not only in the report.

COMMENTS RECONCILED, which was half the assignment: the fail-fast:false justification no longer claims 'no edges between leaves' but states the true premise and forbids adding a matrix value with a second in-repo coordinate. The Install-ssr-to-m2 step is KEPT with its comment corrected to say it is an index-latency shortcut and NOT what makes the dependency exist — and that resolving from ~/.m2 is precisely why the job cannot detect a missing sibling, which is the needs: edge's job. The same false premise was found and fixed in docs/release-process.md (mermaid graph, ASCII fallback, published-pom premise, fan-out rationale, roster sentences, inventory bullet).

MECHANICAL PROOF, with teeth demonstrated rather than asserted: new _release-dag-policy.test.cjs, wired into the always-on test:script-policy job, asserts the GENERAL rule — for every artefact the workflow publishes, the job publishing each in-repo dependency must be a strict transitive needs: ancestor of the job publishing the dependent. Publishers are discovered from clein deploy + working-directory expanded over the matrix; dependency ground truth is each deps.edn read as EDN. The suite reconstructs the pre-fix shape and REQUIRES the violation to be reported, plus a second control dropping the needs edge. Before/after closures recorded. Its new dependency-free workflow-yaml.cjs reader was cross-validated against PyYAML across all 13 workflows — 13/13 byte-identical canonicalised JSON.

ALSO RE-VERIFIED: a v* tag still touches no tools/ (release.yml is the only workflow on that glob; tools sit behind xray-v*/story-v*/machines-viz-v*/template-v*), and every working-directory in release.yml is under implementation/ or the repo root. The other four release workflows publish exactly one artefact per run, so none can carry an intra-run inter-artefact edge — no sibling defect.

title: App-registered :rf.route/entry-denied collides with the framework default (:rf.error/image-duplicate-id)
description:
Found 2026-07-25 12:25 AUSEST while verifying the EP-0037 corpus-wave doc samples (rf2-kqxe6.11, worker/ep0037-corpus-waves). REPORT-ONLY: implementation/** was fenced for that worker, so nothing was fixed.

SYMPTOM. The documented R4 auth recipe does not run. Registering `:rf.route/entry-denied` from an application namespace through the PUBLIC `rf/reg-event` collides with the framework's shipped no-op default at the next `rf/make-frame`:

  rf/image assembly: id [:event :rf.route/entry-denied] is selected from 2 distinct
  source namespaces with different implementations within image nil ...
  Colliding source coordinates: [{:ns nil} {:ns \"probe\"}].   [:rf.error/image-duplicate-id]

MINIMAL REPRO (JVM, plain-atom substrate, routing artefact only):
  (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)
  (rf/reg-route :app/settings {:can-enter [:auth/signed-in?]} \"/settings\")
  (rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied (fn [_ [_ d]] {}))   ;; the documented recipe
  (rf/make-frame {:id :probe/b})                            ;; THROWS

Ordering matters, and the failing order is the ordinary one: an app's namespaces load and register, then `frame-root` / `make-frame` creates the frame. Creating the frame FIRST and registering afterwards passes assembly, which is why this was not caught.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT. implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_entry_denied_test.clj registers the recorder through the INTERNAL `re-frame.events/reg-event`, with a comment that already names the problem: \"`events/reg-event` (not `rf/reg-event`): overriding a framework id from a test namespace collides in image assembly under the reload fixture.\" The whole R4 entry-denial suite therefore only ever exercises the non-public registration path.

BLAST RADIUS (everything below teaches the public spelling):
  - docs/routing/concepts.md §Guarding entry
  - docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md §3 The fresh-return recipe
  - docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md
  - docs/api/re-frame.routing.md (:rf.route/entry-denied row — \"a framework no-op default ships, so registering one is optional\")
  - examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:179 (rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied ...)
  - skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md (the fresh-return recipe)

Same shape almost certainly applies to any other framework-authority default an app is invited to override — check `:rf.route/navigation-blocked` too.

LIKELY CAUSE. image_assembly.cljc's default-image standard-shadow filter drops the framework's own no-provenance copy ONLY for `[kind id]` pairs contributed to the framework-STANDARD registry (`contribute-standard!`). `:rf.route/entry-denied` ships via `events/reg-event` + `framework-authority-meta` (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:237), not as a framework standard, so both descriptors survive selection and `resolve-within-image` raises the ambiguity error.

DECISION NEEDED. Either (a) the overridable framework defaults become real framework standards so the documented app override wins (and `check-standard-collision!` is taught that these particular ids are replaceable), or (b) the recipe changes to a spelling that works and every doc/example/skill above is corrected. (a) looks right: the whole point of the shipped no-op is that an app replaces it.

ACCEPTANCE: the minimal repro above runs clean; the entry-denied suite is re-pointed at the PUBLIC `rf/reg-event` so the regression cannot come back; realworld_http boots.
close_reason: PR #6932 merged (rebased onto main as 5b8e05... in the 2026-07-25 wave). Image assembly now drops the framework's own no-provenance copy of a REPLACEABLE DEFAULT when an application registration for the same [kind id] is present, keyed on the reserved :rf/framework-default? marker read together with an ABSENT :rf.provenance/ns. So the documented auth recipe assembles: an app can rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied without :rf.error/image-duplicate-id. Not a winner rule — two APP registrations of one framework-default id still collide, and framework STANDARDS are untouched (check-standard-collision! unchanged). Both properties pinned: denial-is-safe-with-no-application-handler still passes, and its new complement application-handler-registers-cleanly-and-fires-exactly-once counts invocations across an allowed navigation (0), a denied one (1) and a second denied one (2). The whole R4 entry-denial suite plus the can-leave :rf.route/navigation-blocked override were re-pointed from the internal events/reg-event at the PUBLIC rf/reg-event, so the regression cannot return through the back door.

title: F6: publish v/custom-element -- 13-line macro + cross-path parity (spread/interpreted/structural-SSR) + spec respell (004D, API.md) + donor test consolidation
description:
RULED on rf2-5gliq (2026-07-25, delegated authority): SHIP v/custom-element. This bead is the implementation vehicle. Full ruling + analysis in rf2-5gliq notes; essentials below.

WHAT EXISTS (all absorbed under Freehand's name, tested): compiler/custom-element* at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler.cljc:555-566 (validator custom-element** :473-553, emits rules/register-custom-element! at :552); registry rules.cljc:1407 with custom-element-properties :2024 and custom-element-property-name :398; compile-path read build/element-properties (compiler/build.cljc:406) consumed at analyze.cljc:2052; property lowering fork analyze.cljc:1939-1942; harvester already scans for 're-frame.freehand/custom-element — a var that does not exist (compiler/harvest.clj:54); passing classification test compiler_build_jvm_test.clj:726.

WORK:
1. Publish the ~13-line macro in re-frame.freehand (freehand.cljc, beside defview ~:340). Donor shape: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:129-142. Grammar stays CLOSED: (v/custom-element tag {:properties #{...}}) — no event schemas, property types, reflection rules, customElements inspection, public registry API, or second declaration form.
2. CLOSE THE PARITY GAP before export (verified 2026-07-25; this is a hard obligation of the ruling — the refused outcome is a macro that only helps compiled literal maps): today only compiled LITERAL props consume the declaration. (a) runtime rules/custom-element-properties has no consumer outside rules.cljc — route any interpreted/runtime prop writing through the same classification + kebab->camel law; (b) v/spread and v/spread-safe ride the runtime seam (analyze.cljc:1764, rf2-5r1af/rf2-drpa3.101) with no property classification — a declared property must preserve its raw value through spread, an undeclared name continues through the attribute grammar; (c) Freehand structural nodes never carry :rf.ui/property-props (donor assoc at ui/tree.cljc:283) so SSR omission (ssr/ui_tree.cljc:667-672, read at :860) never fires for Freehand — emit the marker on structural output. NOTE: the :rf.ui/property-props keyword rename is F6c's job (donor-namespaced, live SSR path) — coordinate, do not fork it here.
3. Spec respelling: spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md:804-823 ui/ -> v/ (owning spec); spec/API.md:287 roster row off the donor. spec/004B:616-619 (+:359) already says v/custom-element — this PR makes it true. HOT-ZONE (spec/*): sequence with other spec work, never parallel.
4. Manifest + conformance: api-manifest row (regenerated from live vars, CI drift-gated); conformance row + fixture in spec/conformance/freehand/conformance-index.md.
5. Tests: consolidate the donor family (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/custom_element_*, 9 files / 1,268 lines) into a compact matrix under Freehand proving: kebab->camel, arbitrary (non-attribute-grammar) property values, undeclared names -> attributes, literal AND spread parity, SSR omission/hydration, declaration-order independence (the harvester's reason to exist), reload/conflict law. Preserve every law the retained machinery needs, not nine files because nine exist. One browser DOM proof (donor: custom_element_classification_dom_cljs_test.cljs — the ce-accent fixture at :30-39, property assertion :62-64) stays.
6. Advanced-bundle reachability check: dev reload ledger stays development-only; an app using no declaration pays nothing for the writer/conflict machinery.
7. Ledger (spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md): row :177 (harvest.clj MOVE/done) becomes truthful; row :220 (custom_element_* MOVE/pending) -> done.

WHY (for the record): without the verb, an undeclared kebab prop passes react-prop-name verbatim (rules.cljc:375-382) — React writes an attribute, the property setter never runs, the component is renderable but inert, no warning. Hand-camelCase works in the browser but breaks SSR (key absent from the property-props set, so the server serialises an attribute the component ignores). React 19 cannot infer that :selected-id means the JS property selectedId, has no answer for the JVM structural renderer, and Freehand's closed attribute grammar must know at analysis time that a map/vector/object/fn value is a property value, not an invalid attribute.

Gates rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c). Feeds rf2-drpa3.56 (ledger to zero). Independent of the adapter bead.
notes:
MAYOR RULING on the scope call left open (2026-07-25): DO NOT port the two *_elision_prod_test.cljs arms into this slice.

They did not cross as suites and the ledger row records that. They are advanced-BUNDLE gates whose oracle is the donor-named bundle scanner — so porting them means re-homing that scanner, which is ONE F6 UNIT of migration work, not one law belonging to this verb. Item 6's reachability check already covers the claim this slice needs to make, and it was performed with a VALIDATED oracle (sentinels confirmed present in the dev compile before asserting their absence from :advanced), which is stronger evidence than an unvalidated ported suite would have been. Re-homing the bundle scanner belongs to F6c (rf2-drpa3.55) or F6d (rf2-drpa3.56) where the donor inventory is being driven to zero anyway. Porting it here would duplicate that work and couple this verb's slice to a donor artefact scheduled for deletion.
AUDIT PR #6955 (2026-07-25): REOPENED — the hard “one declaration, every lowering path” obligation is still false for a declared `:on-*` property, including the macro’s own `:on-detail` example.

Current-main reproduction: register `:ce-audit-on-detail` with `{:properties #{:on-detail :model}}`; `node/element` with dynamic `:model {:payload 1}` records the value in `:attrs` and `:rf.ui/property-props`, while the identical value at declared `:on-detail` throws `:rf.error/view-bad-event`. The same precedence is structural across the stack: the compiled analyzer partitions every `on-*` key into `handler-ks` before consulting the declaration; `node/dyn-attr-entry`, the interpreted React walk, and `compiled-react/forward-entry!` test handler position before declared-property classification. Thus literal, interpreted, `v/spread`, `v/spread-safe`, mounted, and SSR paths all ignore the declaration for this valid property-name family.

Repair at the existing owner: make the declaration the sole classifier, with declared-property priority before event-position handling at the shared seams, and add one cross-path matrix using a map-valued declared `:on-detail` plus an undeclared `:on-detail` control that remains a native event. PR #6964 already owns and fixes the separate `:class`/`:style` declaration refusal; do not duplicate it.

title: Template _shared/shadow-cljs.edn emits a re-frame.ui build hook neither remaining variant depends on
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING rf2-qmvep (PR #6904). Same CLASS of defect as rf2-qmvep -- a scaffold that is green in-repo and broken (or silently degraded) for an external consumer -- but a DIFFERENT surface: it affects the DEFAULT Reagent scaffold, not the retired :ui variant, and it interacts with the Freehand cut-over. Filed separately rather than widened into that PR.

THE DEFECT. tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/shadow-cljs.edn emits, for BOTH remaining substrates:

  :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}

That namespace lives in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build_hook.clj -- the artefact Mike ruled on 2026-07-22 is never published, and which rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e) DELETES. Neither emitted deps.edn declares a coordinate that provides re-frame.ui.*:
- :uix -- re-frame2 + re-frame2-uix + re-frame2-schemas + uix.core + uix.dom. Nothing supplies it.
- :reagent -- re-frame2 + re-frame2-reagent + re-frame2-schemas + re-frame2-xray. It resolves ONLY in-repo, transitively, because tools/xray/deps.edn:51 carries day8/re-frame2-ui {:local/root "../../implementation/ui"}. A consumer resolving day8/re-frame2-xray from Clojars would need xray's pom to name a day8/re-frame2-ui Maven dep that will never exist.

WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT. shadow-cljs does not fail on an unloadable build hook -- it warns and continues. Verified by a cold consumer-shaped compile of the generated :uix app during rf2-qmvep:

  [2026-07-25 07:28:46 - WARNING] :shadow.build/hook-config-ex - {:hook-idx 0, :hook-sym re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook, :build-id :app}
  FileNotFoundException Could not locate re_frame/ui/compiler/build_hook__init.class ...
  build hook: re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook failed to load and will not be used
  [:app] Build completed. (172 files, 171 compiled, 0 warnings, 14.67s)   <- exit 0

So the emitted-test tier passes while every generated UIx app silently runs WITHOUT the hook, and every generated Reagent app depends on an in-repo-only transitive edge.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST (do not assume): is the hook load-bearing for the ADAPTER substrates at all? The _shared comment claims 're-frame.ui compiles your views (reg-view / defui / defnc) ... without it the app throws on namespace load', but the :uix compile above completed green with the hook absent, and _reagent/views.cljs uses core's rf/reg-view. If it is NOT load-bearing, the fix is subtraction: drop the :build-defaults line and the template_test.clj assertion at :132 that pins it. If it IS load-bearing, the scaffold needs whichever published artefact will actually carry the hook post-Freehand -- which sequences this AFTER the Freehand publication gate.

SURFACE (verify line numbers at dispatch):
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:17 (comment) and :24 (the :build-defaults line)
- tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:122-135 -- assert-shape! pins the hook for BOTH :reagent and :uix, so the test and the resource change together
- tools/xray/deps.edn:51 -- the transitive edge that masks it for Reagent (xray's own publication story, likely its own bead)

NOT covered by check_donor_inventory.py: CENSUS_REQUIRE_RE is \[re-frame\.ui[A-Za-z0-9._-]*[\s\]] and the emitted form is [(re-frame.ui... -- the leading paren means the census never matches it, so _shared/shadow-cljs.edn carries no ledger row despite being a real donor consumer. Worth deciding whether the census regex should widen.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6906 (branch worker/template-hook-vwum3). SETTLED THE PRIOR QUESTION: the hook is NOT load-bearing for either adapter substrate. re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook is purely re-frame.ui compiler state (custom-element manifest harvest, warm-edit coarse invalidation, removed-source notify wiring, whole-build view/root/plan/descriptor registries). _reagent/views.cljs uses core's rf/reg-view (macro at implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:741, not the donor); _uix/views.cljs uses uix.core/defui. Neither scaffold has compiled views, so the fix is SUBTRACTION -- no replacement hook, no conditional, no shim.

CHANGED (3 files): dropped the :build-defaults line + its 7-line comment from _shared/shadow-cljs.edn; flipped the template_test.clj assertion from pinning the hook to pinning its ABSENCE (a scaffold names a build hook only when its own deps.edn supplies the artefact carrying it); widened CENSUS_REQUIRE_RE in scripts/check_donor_inventory.py to \[\(?re-frame\.ui[A-Za-z0-9._-]*[\s\]/] -- the leading paren AND the / terminator each defeated it independently -- plus one self-test case pinning the shape.

NO LEDGER ROW NEEDED, donor-inventory.md untouched: with the regex widened and the hook still present the gate named exactly _shared/shadow-cljs.edn and nothing else; removing the hook removes the consumer. Row count unchanged at 203/152. The widened regex also newly matches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and examples/ui/minimal-counter/*, both already claimed by pending rows.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE -- cold consumer-shaped -Tnew generate + npm install + shadow-cljs compile, outside any harness, both variants. :uix BEFORE reproduced the recorded defect exactly (hook-config-ex WARNING, FileNotFoundException on build_hook__init.class, 'failed to load and will not be used', then Build completed 172 files/171 compiled/0 warnings, exit 0). :uix AFTER: identical 172/171 build, ZERO marker matches. :reagent BEFORE compiled clean (532/531) ONLY because implementation/ui/src rode in transitively -- confirmed on the generated app's own classpath via clojure -Spath. :reagent AFTER: identical 532/531, zero markers, no longer dependent on that edge. Both AFTER variants also compiled the :test build, ran their emitted node tests green (3/3 each), and BOOTED IN REAL CHROMIUM via dev-page-boot-proof.cjs (mounted, counter 0->1, zero pageerrors) -- which directly disproves the removed comment's claim that the app 'throws on namespace load' without the hook.

GATES (all foreground, exit 0): tools/template clojure -M:test 59 tests/611 assertions 0F/0E; same with RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1 59 tests/696 assertions 0F/0E; check_donor_inventory.py clean; --self-test all passed.

SEQUENCING RESOLVED: this unblocks F6e (rf2-drpa3.57) on the template surface -- deleting implementation/ui can no longer degrade the Reagent scaffold from silent no-op to hard failure.

NO FOLLOW-ON BEAD FILED for the tools/xray/deps.edn -> day8/re-frame2-ui edge the bead flagged: it is already a pending F6 REPLACE row in the donor ledger (line 391), so the Freehand programme owns it.

title: DECISION: settle the two donor capability calls rf2-tb5yq does not cover -- v/custom-element and the Freehand React adapter ownership
description:
DECISION BEAD -- NEEDS A MIKE RULING, do not implement blind.

DISCOVERED-FROM the rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e terminal gate) dossier fold-in, 2026-07-25. The gate hazard: deleting implementation/ui/ removes 231 files and about 76,000 lines at once, and with them the ONLY working implementation of capabilities Freehand does not ship. Git remembers, but a capability with no owner, no test lane and no spec section after the cut does not come back by git revert -- it comes back as a new programme. So every donor capability needs an explicit call (ship it, rule it out, or record it as deferred) BEFORE the donor leaves the tree.

Of the five unexamined donor capabilities the dossier identified, THREE are already owned by rf2-tb5yq (the analyzer recognises re-frame.freehand/frame, /raw, /html, /frame-root, /frame-provider and re-frame.freehand.react/lazy, none of which are interned vars; that bead has a per-head publish-or-remove scope and a no-placeholder-API fence). THIS BEAD OWNS THE TWO THAT NOTHING COVERS.

CALL 1 -- custom-element. The donor publishes a declaring macro: spec/api-manifest.edn:523 records {:namespace "re-frame.ui", :var "custom-element", :tier :advanced, :kind :macro, :owner "004", :status "Spec-004 S1", :facade? false, :runtime-verified? true}. It declares which kebab-case props on a custom element are JS PROPERTIES rather than attributes. Freehand ABSORBED the machinery -- compiler/harvest.clj, rules.cljc and compiler/env.cljc all handle custom elements, and the harvest.clj ledger row is MOVE/DONE -- but publishes NO declaring verb (verified: custom-element absent from implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc and absent from spec/api-manifest.edn under the freehand namespace). Web components are therefore reachable as TAGS but not declarable as PROPERTY-BEARING. The donor test family custom_element_* is still MOVE/PENDING in the inventory ledger. Codex recommends SHIPPING v/custom-element: the canonical contract already rules the declaration grammar, most of the compiler/registry machinery is present, and this is a genuine interop capability rather than donor nostalgia. If the call goes the other way, the ledger rows must be flipped to DELETE and the compiler machinery pruned with them.

CALL 2 -- adapter. THE GENUINE ARCHITECTURE DECISION, and the only one on this bead that is not a one-liner. The donor ships a first-class React observation substrate (:rf.adapter/ui). Freehand ships NONE: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/release_app.cljs requires re-frame.adapter.uix and calls (rf/init! uix/adapter), with a docstring saying a real consumer ships one like it. That may well be the right architecture -- EP-0036 deliberately keeps external renderer adapters independent -- BUT the inventory ledger row for implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/substrate.cljs ("the first-party React adapter machinery, frame-context reader, and root-scoped adapter disposal") is MOVE/PENDING. The programme written record says that machinery is supposed to MOVE. Deleting the donor without disposing it converts an intended MOVE into a SILENT DELETE and makes Freehand permanently dependent on an adapter it does not own. Compounding evidence: the draft install guide still says the Freehand adapter name is TBD. Codex recommends a tiny Freehand-owned React adapter assembled from the shared substrate spine, so a Freehand application does not need UIx merely to initialize re-frame -- and says that if that proves non-tiny, explicitly MAKE the external-adapter requirement the contract instead. The one outcome to refuse is leaving it accidental.

POSTURE FENCE: the donor public API is NOT the target surface. local, generic effect/ref hooks, dispatch-fn, a second root API and a general in-view frame bundle are already RULED OUT and must not be restored merely because the donor had them. Behaviors, controllers, wrappers, capture-frame and the single mount/hydrate/unmount door are the coherent Freehand answer. This bead adds nothing donor-shaped; it closes two open questions.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. custom-element: a recorded ruling -- ship v/custom-element (with a conformance row and an api-manifest entry) or flip the ledger rows to DELETE and prune the orphaned compiler machinery.
2. adapter: a recorded ruling -- either Freehand owns a small React adapter, or the external-adapter requirement becomes the written contract (install guide, spec, release_app docstring) and the substrate.cljs ledger row flips from MOVE to DELETE with reasons.
3. Whichever way each goes, the inventory ledger row is updated so rf2-drpa3.56 can reach zero honestly.

GATE: settle BOTH before rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c) starts, so migration is not done against a surface that is about to change. Related: rf2-tb5yq (the analyzer-orphan heads), rf2-drpa3.56 (absorption ledger), rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e terminal gate).
notes:
RULING (2026-07-25 10:54 AUSEST, delegated authority from Mike via decision dossier ai/decisions/rf2-5gliq.custom-element-and-adapter-ownership.md — dossier folded in here and deleted per instruction).

== CALL 1 — SHIP v/custom-element, with cross-path parity as a hard implementation obligation. ==

The machinery is absorbed under Freehand's name and the entry point is missing: compiler/custom-element* at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler.cljc:555-566 (validator custom-element** :473-553, emits rules/register-custom-element! at :552); runtime registry rules.cljc:1407, custom-element-properties :2024, custom-element-property-name :398; compile-path read build/element-properties (compiler/build.cljc:406) consumed at analyze.cljc:2052; property lowering fork analyze.cljc:1939-1942; harvester already scans for the nonexistent var 're-frame.freehand/custom-element (compiler/harvest.clj:54); passing classification test compiler_build_jvm_test.clj:726. The missing macro is ~13 lines (donor shape: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:129-142).

Why it matters: without the verb, an undeclared kebab prop passes react-prop-name verbatim (rules.cljc:375-382), React writes an ATTRIBUTE, the component's property setter never runs — renderable but inert, no warning. The hand-camelCase workaround works in the browser but lies about author-space convention and breaks SSR (ssr/ui_tree.cljc:667-672 omits property-classified props from markup via :rf.ui/property-props at :860; a hand-camelCased key is not in that set, so the server serialises an attribute the component ignores).

(1) runtime rules/custom-element-properties has NO consumer outside rules.cljc itself; (2) v/spread and v/spread-safe ride the runtime seam (analyze.cljc:1764, rf2-5r1af/rf2-drpa3.101) with no property classification; (3) Freehand structural nodes never assoc :rf.ui/property-props (donor did at ui/tree.cljc:283), so the SSR omission law never fires for Freehand output. The implementation MUST close this before export: one declaration, one meaning, on every path (compiled literal, spread/spread-safe, any interpreted/runtime writer, structural/SSR). The refused outcome is the incoherent middle — a published macro that only helps compiled literal maps.

Grammar stays closed: {:properties #{...}} only. No event schemas, no property types, no reflection rules, no customElements inspection, no public registry API, no second declaration form.

Spec drift to fix: spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:616-619 (+ reserved-key row :359) ALREADY says v/custom-element — shipping makes it true; spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md:804-823 must respell ui/ -> v/; spec/API.md:287 roster row moves off the donor. HOT-ZONE (spec/*) — sequence, never parallel.

Ledger consequences (spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md): row :177 (harvest.clj, MOVE/done) becomes truthful once the harvested verb exists; row :220 (custom_element_* test family, MOVE/pending) -> done via consolidation, not blind copy — nine donor files / 1,268 lines collapse into a matrix proving kebab->camel, arbitrary property values, undeclared->attribute, literal+spread parity, SSR omission/hydration, declaration-order independence, and the reload/conflict law. Plus: api-manifest row (regenerated, CI drift-gated), conformance-index row, and an advanced-bundle reachability check (dev reload ledger stays dev-only; apps with no declaration pay nothing).

== CALL 2 — Freehand OWNS a small React adapter over the core spine. Name SETTLED: var re-frame.freehand/adapter, author-space (rf/init! v/adapter), canonical map :kind :rf.adapter/freehand. ==

The premise that made this look hard is false: the spine lives in CORE, not the donor. re-frame.substrate.spine (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, 3,147 lines) survives donor deletion; make-react-spine :2079, make-react-adapter :2611, parameterised on raw hook fns. The UIx adapter is the model (adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:18-28, :171-173 — working part ~14 lines). Donor ui/substrate.cljs (260 lines) splits: ~30 generic lines (spine-fns with raw React hooks :80-89, frame-provider-component :90-102, make-react-adapter :104-107, current-frame route :70-73) CROSS; ~135 donor-only lines (root-registry disposal :110-183, ViewCell reactor flush :185-245) DO NOT — Freehand has no donor reactor (freehand reactive.cljc is 105 lines, sub-read + event-site, zero flush machinery). No new dependency: Freehand already requires react and react-dom/client.

The IWatchable gap is why this is needed: plain-atom's CLJS derived value reifies IDeref but NOT IWatchable (core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc:78-96), and the observation port installs its watch only when (watchable? reaction) (observation.cljc:1955-1958) — so on plain-atom a moving subscription raises no notification, and render throws :rf.error/render-on-headless-adapter (:98-107). The spine's derived value DOES reify IWatchable (spine.cljs:810-811). That single difference is why release_app.cljs:82-92 installs uix/adapter today — an interactive Freehand app must currently ship UIx or Reagent purely to get a watchable derived value.

Implementation is spine wiring PLUS deliberate lifecycle composition (Codex analysis, keep): (a) Freehand creates React roots itself (root.cljs:216) recorded in freehand.root/live-roots, invisible to the spine's active-root registry — adapter disposal = Freehand root drain (root.unmount() releases subscriptions) THEN spine disposal; (b) flush-render! must publish pending ViewCells (freehand.cell/pending-cells via cell/flush!) inside the React synchronous commit boundary; if commit work can re-dirty a cell, settle via a bounded fixed-point driver, not an unbounded loop; (c) frame reading needs nothing new — the shell reads the shared context directly (shell.cljs:79-81), so the donor's :adapter/current-frame publication is not a lost capability. Conformance: init->mount->subscribe->dispatch->automatic re-render; flush-render! returns with Freehand DOM settled; disposal unmounts every root, disconnects cells, releases root-owned frames, then disposes the spine; dispose/re-init yields a clean generation; dual-failure ordering follows the existing primary/secondary cleanup convention.

Follow-on made true by this ruling: repoint release_app.cljs:92, release_app_lowered_full.cljs:116, release_app_lowered_none.cljs:109 to v/adapter (keep one mixed-host fixture on UIx so the adoption path stays proven); fill the install-guide placeholders docs/design/freehand/draft-guide/install.md:20, :56, :88 (placeholder note :52-54, status row :126) and build-a-view.md:149-150, :209. Ledger row donor-inventory.md:193 (ui/substrate.cljs, MOVE/pending) -> MOVE/done with honest row text: the generic spine wiring crosses; the donor ViewCell flush and root-disposal composition do not (no Freehand counterpart exists to settle).

EP-0036 preserved: Reagent/UIx/Helix remain first-class, independent renderer adapters. This is the substrate's own observation wiring (Freehand renders itself via react-dom/client), not a renderer adapter — it competes with nothing. Bring-your-own-adapter remains legitimate for mixed apps under the single-adapter runtime; a Freehand root is still unmounted via v/unmount! before destroying an external adapter. Non-goals: no second reactive system, no Freehand use-subscribe hook, no render-side state API, no wrapper-library dependency, no generic adapter factory or composition DSL, no automatic adapter selection, no non-React hosts.

== Shared fences ==
Both rulings preserve the derivative-view law: a custom-element declaration is static host metadata; the adapter connects committed external-store change to React; neither permits a view render to fetch, dispatch, acquire a resource, or own an effect. The donor public API is NOT the target surface — nothing here restores local, generic effect/ref hooks, dispatch-fn, a second root API, or an in-view frame bundle. rf2-tb5yq still owns the analyzer-orphan heads (frame-provider, frame-root, raw, html, lazy); the adapter's :frame-provider slot coordinates with that bead's outcome. The :rf.ui/property-props keyword itself is donor-namespaced on a live SSR path — renaming it is F6c's job; the Call 1 implementation coordinates with (does not fork) that rename.

DISPOSITION: both calls ruled; neither leaves the surface accidental. Implementation split per the dossier's own sizing into two independent beads (created now, both gating rf2-drpa3.55): Call 1 -> see child bead (custom-element), Call 2 -> see child bead (adapter). Acceptance item 3 (ledger rows) transfers to those beads. This decision bead closes as RULED.
IMPLEMENTATION BEADS FILED: Call 1 (v/custom-element) -> rf2-sv2oq; Call 2 (Freehand adapter) -> rf2-vo8fb. Both P1, both block rf2-drpa3.55, each carries its ledger-row obligations (acceptance item 3 transfers to them). Closing this decision bead as RULED.
close_reason: RULED (delegated authority, 2026-07-25): Call 1 -- SHIP v/custom-element with cross-path parity as a hard obligation (impl bead rf2-sv2oq). Call 2 -- Freehand owns a small React adapter on the core spine, name settled as re-frame.freehand/adapter, :kind :rf.adapter/freehand (impl bead rf2-vo8fb). Neither surface left accidental; full analysis in notes; dossier file deleted.

title: Release-contract reconciliation: make day8/re-frame2-ui non-publishable before any version tag
description:
BLOCKS EVERY VERSION TAG. Until this lands, pushing any tag matching the release glob v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+* publishes day8/re-frame2-ui to Clojars permanently, contradicting Mike's 2026-07-22 ruling ("day8/re-frame2-ui should not be published") and publishing an artefact rf2-drpa3.57 is scheduled to DELETE.

THE CONTRADICTION. The release machinery does not merely permit publishing the donor - it COMPELS it. Verified on main 8626c5da29:
- implementation/ui/deps.edn:80-85 - live :clein alias and :clein/build {:lib day8/re-frame2-ui, :version "../../VERSION"}.
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:286-288 - REQUIRED_PUBLISHABLE=(ui), a POSITIVE assertion deliberately stronger than the conditional inventory guard at :270, whose entire purpose is to make a core-only tag FAIL BEFORE DEPLOY. ui is also in ARTEFACT_PATHS (:82) and NON_CORE (:117).
- .github/workflows/release.yml:39-45 header "The re-frame.ui substrate is a REQUIRED artefact (rf2-vxgfnd.99.2)"; :220-224 jvm-ui pre-deploy test with no skip-on-empty fallback; :395 ui deploy leaf; :627 day8/re-frame2-ui release-body row.
- docs/release-process.md:15 (Policy 3) and :17 + :169 (Lockstep verification) both assert ui is a REQUIRED alpha artefact.
- implementation/scripts/_release-ui-required-gate.test.cjs - hermetic test proving the requirement holds.
- tools/template still ships the :substrate :ui variant and EMITS the coordinate: tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_ui/deps.edn:28 day8/re-frame2-ui {:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}, plus template.edn:7, tools/template/README.md:98-100, tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md:115-127, roster assert in tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:756.

The two states are mutually exclusive: drop ui's :clein/build to honour the ruling and REQUIRED_PUBLISHABLE fails the tag before deploy; leave it and the tag publishes the donor forever.

WHY IT DRIFTED. The machinery landed in PR #6654 (commit 42eeebbdba) early on 2026-07-22. Later the same day EP-0036 was accepted (af996f2cff), making Freehand the single native public view door and re-frame.ui donor-only; the initial Freehand artefact commit (8caffd379de) recorded that publication is F6 territory and the donor was ruled not to be published. rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 was then closed BY RETIREMENT, which did not revert the already-landed machinery. Its close reason is written in future tense ("stays pre-publication", "no UI row is added"), reading as an oversight rather than a deferral. EP-0036 states its topology and gates OUTRANK unmigrated donor-era specifications, so the release machinery is a superseded contract that was never reconciled.

Also relevant: implementation/ui/ is mid-disassembly. Commit 689ed82522 (2026-07-22) moved the analyzer, both emitters and the shared normalizers out from under it into Freehand ownership (33 source files against Freehand's 59). Whatever day8/re-frame2-ui 0.0.1.alpha would be, it is not a coherent library.

IRREVERSIBILITY. Clojars does not literally forbid deletion, but its official FAQ (github.com/clojars/clojars-web/wiki/About - "how do I delete a jar") says ordinary project/version deletion is discouraged and administrator deletion is reserved for malicious/security content or accidentally-published private material. Publishing the wrong product topology is not one of those reasons; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is immutable except by a valid deletion request. Recovery is bump-and-supersede, and the unwanted coordinate stays in the public record. docs/release-process.md Recovery section says the same.

SCOPE - one atomic config-prune-first PR, hot-zone:
1. Remove :clein and :clein/build from implementation/ui/deps.edn.
2. Remove ui from ARTEFACT_PATHS / ARTEFACTS / NON_CORE in .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh and delete the REQUIRED_PUBLISHABLE assertion.
3. Prune release.yml: the jvm-ui pre-deploy step, the ui deploy leaf, the day8/re-frame2-ui release-body row, and the REQUIRED-artefact header comment.
4. Retire implementation/scripts/_release-ui-required-gate.test.cjs.
5. Correct docs/release-process.md Policy 3 and Lockstep verification.
6. Park or remove the template's :substrate :ui variant and its emitted day8/re-frame2-ui Maven dependency - if ui is never published, that scaffold generates an unresolvable coordinate for every external consumer who picks it. G4 only ever verified the :ui variant via the documented pre-publication :local/root rewrite, an in-repo affordance no external consumer has.
7. Doc-truth in the same PR: EP-0036 Backwards Compatibility (docs/EP/EP-0036-*.md:88 and :269-270) still says "The shipped alpha-train re-frame.ui surface continues only during coexistence", wording that pre-dates the never-publish ruling and describes something that will never exist; README.md:183 project map still lists ui/ as day8/re-frame2-ui and the README never mentions Freehand.

ORDERING GUARD: config-prune-first or one combined PR. A source-removal-first PR reds ITSELF on always-on policy tests that read the deleted files - the same shape W13 (rf2-d6epb) already proved and rf2-drpa3.57 explicitly warns not to rediscover.

NON-GOALS: do not delete implementation/ui/ (that is rf2-drpa3.57 / F6e). Do not cut, push or prepare any tag. Do not rewrite CHANGELOG.md here - that is a tag-time pre-flight item.

The full ruling and its evidence live in the notes of rf2-drpa3.57 and rf2-drpa3.23; the short form is that all four F5 pilots used the form ZERO times, including rf2-drpa3.44's dropdown which D007 named as the exemplar, so Mike's own gate wording ("if the F5 pilots showed no repeated real use, DELETE the form rather than keep it for symmetry") discharges literally.

    :on-key-down (v/event [e] (case (.-key e) "Enter" (do (.preventDefault e) [:picker/accept]) "Escape" [:picker/close] nil))

  A component library may add its own local helper if repeated simple mappings emerge, without committing the substrate to that helper's grammar.

WHAT IS LOST, EYES OPEN

  Per-key dispatch suppression. Every keyboard-bearing control dispatches once per keystroke whether or not the key means anything, and each of those settles an epoch. On a buffered field that is two events per character (asserted at pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1183-1200). The compute is near-free - an unmatched handler returns {} so nothing commits, and not even :rf.event/db-noop fires, which requires a :db effect to have been present (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1333-1346). The real cost is observational: one dequeued event is one epoch record, the per-frame trace ring retains 50 slots (spec/002-Frames.md:528) and epoch-history keeps 50 epochs per frame (spec/Tool-Pair.md:100). That concern is filed separately against Spec 009 - it belongs at the trace surface, not at the listener.

EP-0037 orders each contributor by local :after edges, concatenates contributors parent-to-leaf, then groups materialized requirements by canonical resource identity and dispatches the earliest occurrence once. Runtime identity convergence can make that final dedupe erase a declared dependency. Concrete shape: local A resolves to identity R; B declares :after #{A}; later C also resolves to R and declares :after #{B}. title: v/->react silently accepts falsey :map-props and falls back to shallow props
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6783.

`re-frame.freehand.to-react/require-opts!` validates `:map-props` with `when-let`. A present falsey value therefore skips validation: both `{:map-props nil}` and `{:map-props false}` are accepted, then `exported-component` treats the value as absent and silently runs the default shallow prop conversion.

That contradicts spec/004-Views.md's closed option contract (`:map-props`'s value is a function) and the bridge's own rationale that a bad option must fail rather than select the default rule and produce a subtly wrong render. It is especially risky for a foreign mutable parameter object, where silently shallow-copying was the failure the explicit adapter exists to prevent.

Acceptance:
1. Distinguish an absent `:map-props` key from a present falsey value.
2. When the key is present, require a function; nil and false raise the same attributed `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` diagnostic as every other non-function.
3. Pin nil, false, and another non-function as refusals, plus `{}` / omitted opts as the default-shallow controls.
4. Keep the option roster at one key; add no adapter framework.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6803 (0ded6bf60e). REFUSE, not honour-as-shallow. require-opts! used when-let, so a PRESENT falsey :map-props skipped validation and exported-component read it as absent; fixed with contains?. Reasoning: the declared contract already says the option's value IS a function (spec/004 and D014 both), so honouring would be the implementation contradicting its own roster; a falsey adapter is essentially always a lookup that missed or a branch that fell through, never a request for the default (that spelling exists and is shorter — omit the key); and trust-the-programmer means not caging correct code, not silently substituting different behaviour for what was written. Honouring would also alias two distinct intentions ({} = never asked; {:map-props nil} = asked, expression produced nothing). SECOND EDGE FOUND: {:map-props false} keyed its own cache entry [view-id false] — a distinct React component type behaving identically to the default, so switching spellings would REMOUNT the foreign subtree. Reused the existing :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed + :supply-a-one-argument-function recovery, so NO spec/009 co-edit and no new id. Tests assert the ACTUAL props map the boundary is mounted with.

title: [bug] The React emitter has no :slot arm — a compiled render slot cannot be lowered for the browser
description:
FOUND BY THE F5h VIRTUAL-TABLE PILOT (rf2-drpa3.45).

## The finding

`:slot` is a member of `re-frame.freehand.compiler.grammar/admitted-ops`.
The analyzer lowers it, `grammar/check!` passes it, and
`compiler/emit-jvm` has `:slot (emit-slot e node)`.

`compiler/emit-react`'s `emit-node` has NO `:slot` arm. Compiling any
`{:compiled true}` body containing `v/slot` for ClojureScript therefore
dies inside the emitter:

    IllegalArgumentException: No matching clause: :slot
      re-frame.freehand.compiler.emit-react/emit-node (emit_react.cljc:376)

Two things are wrong with that, and the second is the smaller one.

1. THE CAPABILITY IS MISSING. A compiled component library that accepts
   caller-supplied content — a table with a row slot, a list with an item
   slot, a layout with named regions — cannot be promoted for the browser
   at all. The grammar advertises the form; the browser tier cannot
   deliver it. Since the compiled tier became browser-mountable
   (rf2-drpa3.113), this is the gap between "compiled views mount" and
   "compiled COMPONENT LIBRARIES mount".

2. THE FAILURE MODE IS A RAW HOST EXCEPTION. No diagnostic id, no source
   coordinate, no recovery ladder — against a substrate whose whole
   posture is that every refusal names what to do next. `emit-node`'s own
   docstring says "Every arm below is a `:re-frame.freehand/v1` node kind.
   There is no arm for anything else, because there is nothing else to
   reach here", and `:slot` reaches there.

## Blast radius today

`slot-views-compiled` is `.clj` and says so ("the compiled React lowering
of these forms lands with the compiled browser runtime and brings its own
suite") — written before the browser runtime landed. The F5h pilot's
compiled twin and its parity suite are JVM-only for the same reason, and
the pilot's compiled BROWSER cell is blocked rather than claimed.

## Acceptance

1. A compiled `v/slot` lowers through the React emitter, with the D010
   crossing law unchanged: a compiled render-fn answers a node, an
   interpreted one handed to a compiled slot still lands on the ruled
   refusal.
2. Slot arity is checked identically on both hosts (the existing
   host-independent contract), and keys on slot-rendered rows survive.
3. The F5h pilot's compiled twin returns to `.cljc` and its browser cell
   stops being blocked.
4. WHATEVER remains unlowered in either emitter answers a DIAGNOSTIC with
   a source coordinate and a recovery, never a raw host exception — an
   admitted op with no arm is a build failure the grammar should catch
   before an emitter is reached.
close_reason: VERIFIED DUPLICATE — already fixed on main before this bead was filed. The React emitter :slot arm landed as rf2-cqjwx in PR #6771 (ecba2a8a68 'emit-react lowers v/slot — the missing :slot arm' plus 4550d30843), and on current main it sits at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/emit_react.cljc:439 as ':slot (emit-slot e st node)'. The F5h pilot worktree forked before #6771 merged, so its observation was accurate at the time and is stale now. Pilot resumed to rebase, rebuild the compiled browser arm that its BLOCKED claim had ruled out, and correct three prose sites asserting a blocker that no longer exists.

title: emit-react silently DROPS v/spread and v/spread-safe on an element
description:
## Problem

`re-frame.freehand.compiler.emit-react/emit-element*` reads `(:attrs props)`, `(:class props)`, `(:style props)`, `(:key props)` and `(:events props)` — and never reads `(:spread props)` or `(:safe-spread props)`. The structural emitter reads both (`emit-jvm`, the `spread`/`safe` arms of its `cond->`, which build `node/spread-attrs` and `node/safe-caller-attrs` calls).

So a `{:compiled true}` declaration that forwards an attribute map onto a DOM element compiles cleanly, mounts cleanly, and renders an element **with the whole forwarded map missing**. Not a crash, not a diagnostic, not a warning — the attributes are simply absent in the browser while the same declaration carries them on the structural host and in interpreted mode.

This is NOT caught by `grammar/check!`. That walk refuses unadmitted node kinds by `:op`, and `:element` is admitted; a spread lives in the element's `:props` sub-structure, not as an op of its own. The per-node-kind emitter coverage table has the same blind spot for the same reason.

## Steps to Reproduce

On the `:clj` resolver, analyze and emit through the React emitter:

    [:div.sugar (v/spread attrs {:class "c"})]

emits

    (compiled-react/el "div" (js-obj "className" "sugar") nil)

The forwarded runtime map is gone AND the literal `{:class "c"}` override is gone. Only the tag shorthand survives.

    [:input (v/spread-safe {:value "v"} attrs)]

emits

    (compiled-react/el "input" (js-obj "value" "v") nil)

The guarded caller map is gone — so `v/spread-safe`'s whole reason for existing (a bounded consumer forward) silently forwards nothing in a browser-compiled view.

## Evidence

Observed directly off `emit-react/emit-react-body` on the analyzed AST for both forms. The sibling `emit-jvm/emit-element` handles both, so this is a one-sided omission in the browser emitter rather than an unimplemented grammar.

## Scope

Give the React emitter the two arms its structural sibling has, folding the forwarded map onto the emitted props object through the SAME `node/spread-attrs` / `node/safe-caller-attrs` seams both modes already share — so the merge, the deny law and the class composition stay one implementation. Do not introduce a React-only forwarding path or a second precedence rule.

Consider also closing the structural hole that let this through: the emitter coverage table proves one row per admitted `:op`, and a props sub-structure is invisible to it.

## Deduplication

Found while finishing the `:slot` and call-site-render-fn arms of the same emitter (PR #6771 / rf2-cqjwx). Those were the same defect class — an AST shape `emit-jvm` handles and `emit-react` does not — but they are separate shapes with separate fixes; neither PR touches element props forwarding. `rf2-drpa3.136` and `.137` own `v/spread` SEMANTICS (precedence, literal nil) on the seam both modes share, not the React emitter's failure to call that seam at all. `rf2-drpa3.132` owns the `v/spread-safe` React/carrier defect at a different site.
acceptance_criteria:
- A {:compiled true} React declaration using (v/spread base overrides) on a DOM element carries the forwarded map's attributes onto the mounted element, matching its interpreted twin read back off the DOM.
- The same for (v/spread-safe owned caller): the guarded caller map reaches the element and the deny law still fires.
- The literal part of a spread props map (e.g. the {:class "c"} override) is no longer lost.
- Class composition with tag .class sugar holds through a forwarded map, as it does on the structural host.
- A regression drives BOTH emitters from one declaration so a props sub-structure the React emitter ignores cannot pass again — the existing per-node-kind emitter table covers :op only, and a spread is not an :op.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6781 (25619e26f5 + cb071f20bc): the React emitter now reads v/spread and v/spread-safe, folded through node/spread-attrs and node/safe-caller-attrs so both front ends share one function (react/put-caller!). THE BEAD PREMISE WAS PARTLY FALSE — v/spread-safe did not work in interpreted BROWSER mode either; :rf.ui/caller reached the plain-attribute path and threw. STRUCTURAL FIX BEYOND THE POINT-PATCHES: the emitter coverage table gained a SECOND AXIS (grammar/element-props-carriers + grammar/crossing-prop-markers), proven by reverting the fixes — :spread and :safe-spread red on :reaches, and the crossing rows red reporting ':on-pick nil', the defect's own signature. The :render-fn row catches PR #6771's instance by the same mechanism. Writing the tables found TWO MORE instances, fixed here: (v/event ...)/(v/handler ...) at a call-site prop emitted nil in BOTH v1 emitters, and :ref on a compiled element was analysed and read by no emitter. Two further sites found and filed rather than fixed: rf2-ll1ah (#id sugar dropped with v/spread — needs a conflict-semantics ruling) and rf2-7x0ge (key-condition v/event branch cannot render on the structural host).

title: Compiled top-level v/event at a DOM site silently drops its dispatch
description:
CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY (not merely read) by the rf2-drpa3.149 worker during PR #6769. A compiled top-level v/event attached at a DOM site does nothing at all: the event is never dispatched, and nothing errors.

## The measured chain

    classification    = :ui-event
    lowered form      = (fn [ev] [:app/clicked])
    door is told role = :event      ; controlled/compiled-role
    runtime plan role = :bare-fn    ; events/event-plan of that lowered value
    dispatched        = []          ; fire!s :bare-fn arm ignores the return

## Mechanism

analyze-handler :ui-event arm lowers to a BARE (fn [ev] ...). emit_react/handler-writes hands :form straight to reactive/event-site -> events/site with no wrapping (compiled_react/handler! only gobj/sets the proxy). events/event-plan therefore classifies it :bare-fn, and fire!s :bare-fn arm APPLIES the fn and DISCARDS the returned event vector.

Meanwhile controlled/compiled-role tells the door that same handler is role :event. THE TWO HALVES DISAGREE: the door believes an event will be dispatched; the runtime treats the handler as a side-effecting bare fn and throws the event away.

## Why this is worse than a crash

It is a SILENT no-op. The author writes an ordinary event handler in a compiled view, the build succeeds, the door reports role :event, and the click does nothing. There is no diagnostic to search for.

## Not covered

Nothing in the suite exercises it — consistent with the gap being real rather than an artefact of the probe.

## Explicitly NOT affected

Key-map BRANCHES are fine. PR #6769 lowers a v/event branch to (events/callback :event (fn ...) 1) — the roster constructor — precisely so it classifies :event and dispatches. Any fix here should follow that same shape rather than inventing a new one.

## Acceptance

The dispatch actually fires from a compiled top-level v/event at a DOM site, proven in the browser lane; and the door role and the runtime plan role AGREE for that handler, pinned by a test. Assert the DISPATCHED EVENT, not merely that no error was raised — the defect raises nothing.

## Surface note for dispatch

Touches implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/analyze.cljc (the :ui-event lowering) and likely emit_react.cljc / events.cljc. analyze.cljc is a contended file — sequence this against any other analyze.cljc holder.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6780 (31b03c512e). analyze-handler now lowers a whole-handler v/event through (events/callback :event (fn ...) 1) — the roster constructor PR #6769 established for key branches — so it classifies :event and dispatches instead of being applied as a bare fn with its return discarded. Forced a second, older fix: node/classify-event knew vectors, maps and fn?, and a roster callback is deliberately none of those, so an INTERPRETED [:button {:on-click (v/event ...)}] was unrenderable on the structural host. Both modes now record the mode-neutral {:rf.ui/opaque :fn}, with 004B cited as the authority.

title: Restore the mayor checkout implementation/node_modules (emptied by junction cascade)
description:
The mayor checkout node_modules at implementation/node_modules is EMPTY (0 entries). Expected ~101 packages. Cause is the known junction-cascade failure mode: a worker worktree junctions its implementation/node_modules into the mayor real directory, and a git worktree remove that follows the junction deletes THROUGH it into the mayor tree. Reported independently by the rf2-drpa3.114 worker on 2026-07-24, which deliberately did NOT repair it to avoid racing another live build.

IMPACT: every worker that junctions into the mayor tree fails to build, and any node gate run from the mayor checkout fails. This is environmental, not a code defect.

REPAIR (operator or mayor, only when NO build is in flight — after a reboot is the ideal moment since nothing is running): npm ci --prefix implementation, from the mayor checkout. Then verify the canary: ls implementation/node_modules should show ~101 entries.

PREVENTION, already recorded in memory but repeatedly re-learned: before any git worktree remove, remove the node_modules JUNCTION FIRST using a call that does not recurse into the target — PowerShell [System.IO.Directory]::Delete(path,$false) — and confirm Test-Path returns False BEFORE removing the worktree. Never chain neutralize+remove. Run the ls canary before and after every removal batch so a cascade is caught immediately rather than discovered by the next worker.
close_reason: Repaired 2026-07-24 in the post-reboot window with no build in flight: npm ci --prefix implementation, EXIT=0. Canary verified: implementation/node_modules now lists 101 entries, matching the expected count. Prevention guidance retained in the description and in the junction-safe-worktree-cleanup memory.

title: Restore compiled parity for F2d key-condition event maps
description:
## Defect

PR #6761 adds F2d key-condition event maps to the common event normalizer, but the compiled analyzer still classifies every literal map as the older listener-options form. The merged conformance/runtime tests exercise `events/event-plan` and committed proxies, not a compiled declaration, despite the slice claiming one event shape across both modes.

## Steps to Reproduce

On merge `e939f56f8c1031f1fe24c3f2c89fb04584d3d6fc`, analyze `[:input {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:picker/accept]}}]` with the ordinary compiled analyzer/test environment. It returns `:rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options`, while `events/event-plan` accepts the same handler value as `:key-map`.

## Evidence

`compiler/analyze.cljc` `analyze-handler` has one unconditional `(map? form)` branch that validates keys against `rules/handler-option-keys`; #6761 did not change the analyzer or emitters.

## Bounded correction

Teach the existing compiled event grammar the same closed, one-level, all-string-key form used by the runtime normalizer, including key-listener legality and branch validation. Reuse the current plan/diagnostic vocabulary; add no wildcard, modifier DSL, nested map, or second event syntax.

## Origin

Completeness/correctness audit of merged PR #6761.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A `{:compiled true}` declaration accepts a non-empty exact-key map on `:on-key-down` and `:on-key-up` and lowers each legal branch with the same event/payload semantics as interpreted mode.
2. Empty, mixed-key, nested, non-dispatching-branch, and non-key-listener forms fail with typed, didactic diagnostics rather than falling into listener-options errors or emitting malformed code.
3. Existing event vectors, listener-options maps, `v/event`, and controlled-input analysis remain unchanged.
4. Add compiled accept/reject and structural lowering coverage driven by FH-EVENT-005 (browser mounting may remain behind the already-owned compiled-browser lowering gate).
notes:
[audit-pr-6769] Residual completeness/correctness finding from merged PR #6769. The analyzer now returns :classification :key-map, but compiler/emit_cljs.cljc handler-form has no :key-map case, so actual CLJS compiled emission reaches an unmatched case. The added compiled tests stop at ana/analyze and therefore cannot catch emitted or mounted failure. This reopens the exact owner rather than duplicating it; rf2-berc2 is separate and explicitly concerns top-level v/event dispatch.

Acceptance rider: author a {:compiled true} v/defview with a data key-condition event map and prove it compiles, mounts, and fires in the browser, including a v/event branch. The proof must fail if the emitter support is removed.
MAYOR NOTE 2026-07-24: this audit reopen may be RESOLVED BY DELETION rather than by a fix. The finding is that compiler/emit_cljs.cljc handler-form has no :key-map case — and Mike has RULED (see rf2-drpa3.108) that emit_cljs.cljc is to be DELETED as superseded, because it calls ~34 constructors that have never existed and nothing on the live v/defview path reaches it. That deletion is dispatched and in flight. I have asked its worker to (a) determine whether the audit premise that "actual CLJS compiled emission reaches an unmatched case" is TRUE — two prior investigations concluded emit_cljs is unreachable from v/defview — and (b) state in its PR body whether the deletion retires this finding. IF A REACHABLE PATH EXISTS, that is a live bug and far more important than the deletion; the worker is told to stop and report so the ruling can be revisited. Do not dispatch this bead separately until that comes back. The audit second observation is worth keeping regardless: the added compiled tests stop at ana/analyze and therefore cannot catch emitted or mounted failure — that coverage gap outlives emit_cljs.
RESOLVED BY REMOVAL — the audit premise DOES NOT HOLD. Established by the rf2-drpa3.108 worker (PR #6789) by reading the emitters rather than inferring.

THE AUDIT CLAIMED: "the analyzer now returns :classification :key-map, but compiler/emit_cljs.cljc handler-form has no :key-map case, so ACTUAL CLJS COMPILED EMISSION reaches an unmatched case."

WHY THAT IS FALSE: emit_cljs/handler-form was the ONLY place in the artefact casing over :classification at all. The LIVE emitters do not classify at emit time — emit-react/handler-writes passes the raw form to reactive/event-site, and emit-jvm/event-slots passes the raw form through. Classification happens in node/classify-event, AT RENDER. So no live compiled emission could ever reach that case; it was a latent defect in unreachable code, and it is now deleted.

THE AUDIT SECOND POINT WAS CORRECT AND WAS ACTIONED: "the added compiled tests stop at ana/analyze and therefore cannot catch emitted or mounted failure." That observation drove the worker to redirect the viewcell elision oracle off a phantom namespace and onto the live structural manifest — a real improvement that outlives emit_cljs.

Close this bead when PR #6789 merges.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6789. The audit reopen is RETIRED BY REMOVAL, premise refuted: emit_cljs/handler-form was the ONLY place in the artefact casing over :classification, and the live emitters do not classify at emit time (emit-react/handler-writes and emit-jvm/event-slots pass the raw form through; classification happens in node/classify-event AT RENDER). So 'actual CLJS compiled emission reaches an unmatched case' was false — a latent defect in unreachable code, now deleted. The audit's SECOND point was correct and was actioned: analyze-boundary tests cannot catch emitted failure, which drove the worker to redirect the viewcell elision oracle off a phantom namespace onto the live structural manifest.

title: Refuse runtime Hiccup in compiled browser expressions instead of interpreting it
description:
## Defect

PR #6762's browser emitter lowers every compiled `:expr` to `compiled-react/child`. That function delegates to `re-frame.freehand.react/child-elements`, which invokes the interpreted Hiccup walker. A child expression whose runtime value is a Hiccup vector is therefore interpreted inside compiled markup.

This directly contradicts ruled D010 and `spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md`: v1 has no dynamic-markup valve or automatic fallback; compiled code passes no walker; a runtime Hiccup vector must be refused by name. The JVM structural path does exactly that through `node/children`, but the new browser path bypasses it. The existing absence test covers only the structural body, so it stayed green while the React lowering added the forbidden reachability.

## Correctness impact

The analyzer cannot see the hidden markup, so the manifest, subscription ownership, capability elision, and static diagnostics can all be false. This issue's original symptom is one concrete result: when an ELIDED compiled view receives forwarded Hiccup containing declarative `:on-*` intent, the walk runs without an ambient candidate and silently omits the handler. The interpreted twin owns and attaches that site.

## Bounded correction

Make the browser lowering use the compiled child classifier/refusal used by the structural tier. Runtime Hiccup in a compiled expression must fail loudly with the canonical D010 recovery ladder; markup-as-value crosses through the already-ruled `v/markup` descriptor boundary or an extracted interpreted child. Keep the existing legal scalar/nil/sequence/React-child behavior and browser parity. Do not add `v/interp`, a new dynamic valve, or a public API.

## Deduplication

This audit expands the already-open rf2-drpa3.130 from its narrow elided-handler symptom to the ruled root cause instead of filing a duplicate. A full-ledger search found no other Bead owning the compiled-browser interpreter fallback.

## Origin

Completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6762 at merge commit `847ad222fa3e90546b4fe92aba2763d4875ed0a5`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In a browser-mounted compiled view, a dynamic child expression that evaluates to a Hiccup vector raises the canonical typed D010 refusal and names the existing recovery (`v/markup`, an extracted declared view, or keeping the containing view interpreted); it is never rendered by the interpreted walker.
2. The compiled React lowering has no call path from a normal `:expr` to the interpreted Hiccup walker, matching the structural emitter's classifier/refusal.
3. A regression arm covers the original elided-boundary case: forwarded Hiccup carrying declarative event intent fails loudly rather than silently losing the handler.
4. Existing browser parity for legal dynamic nil, text/number, child sequences, React elements, and declared-view crossings remains green.
5. No dynamic-markup valve, `v/interp`, new public API, or second child-semantics system is introduced.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6820 (merged): compiled browser emitter refuses runtime Hiccup.

title: Compiled v/behavior skips opaque-child validation and lacks full mounted parity proof
description:
FOUND BY THE SECOND PILOT (rf2-drpa3.44, PR #6749), reproduced as a named test.

## The finding

`[v/behavior …]` inside a `{:compiled true}` body classifies as `:op :foreign` and raises `:rf.ui.compile/unsupported-form`, recovery `:keep-interpreted`. The compiled grammar has no behavior form.

Because `v/defbehavior` with `:timing :layout` is the ONLY before-paint home in the substrate, the consequence is sharper than "one form is missing":

  ANY VIEW THAT MEASURES IS INTERPRETED FOREVER.

A view needing a measurement before paint — which is most overlays, virtualisation, and anything sizing itself to content — can never be promoted to the compiled tier, no matter how hot it is. That is a real ceiling on where the compiled tier can be applied, and it was invisible until something tried to build a measuring component.

Overlay markup itself promotes cleanly — the pilot asserts whole-tree structural parity for the compiled twin — so this is specifically the BEHAVIOR ATTACHMENT, not the top-layer intrinsics.

## Related, already filed
rf2-drpa3.116 records that the compiled tier has no `v/behavior` form and that FH-BEHAVIOR rows are interpreted-only. THIS bead is the CONSEQUENCE that makes .116 worth prioritising rather than deferring: it is not merely a missing form, it is a bound on the compiled tier's applicability. Whoever takes .116 should read this first and decide whether they are the same piece of work.

## Acceptance
1. A determination: is a compiled `v/behavior` form achievable, or is the interpreted-forever consequence intended and to be documented as a ruled limitation? Either is a legitimate outcome; picking one silently is not.
2. If achievable: the compiled form honours D013's closed timing, bounded commands and semantic-id targets identically, with cross-mode agreement proven.
3. If ruled a limitation: it is stated in `spec/004` where an author will meet it, with the reason — so someone deciding whether to compile a hot measuring view learns it from the spec rather than from a refusal.

## Non-goals
Weakening D013's constraints to make the compiled form easier. Introducing a second before-paint mechanism to work around the gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- The compiled browser path enforces the opaque-child law at runtime for literal and runtime-selected :use values, raising the existing :rf.error/behavior-bad-args before any behavior connects or child host state is overwritten.
- FH-BEHAVIOR-002 includes a discriminating compiled-browser opaque-child case plus a positive empty opaque host; JVM, interpreted browser, and compiled browser agree.
- The mounted D013 laws actually supported by compiled behavior are exercised across both modes, including abandoned-candidate/commit-only behavior, total cleanup, frame-scoped command success/refusal, and generation fencing; FH-BEHAVIOR-004/005/006 applicability is then re-cut to common browser.
- Keep one shared behaviors runtime and the existing public surface; no parallel lifecycle, command bus, selector, or defensive wrapper API.
notes:
rf2-drpa3.46 (F5i) confirms this on today main, now that compiled views are
browser-mountable, and adds two things.

(a) A SEPARATE diagnostic defect filed as rf2-drpa3.153: the refusal classifies
    v/behavior as :op :foreign — "a foreign component boundary" — misnaming the
    framework own attachment. v/route-link and v/markup compile fine.

(b) The RECOVERY works end to end and is worth recording as the interim answer:
    a compiled parent mounts the interpreted integration as an ordinary declared
    child, the manifest marks the crossing :interpreted, and it is ONE React tree
    on a real page — a command dispatched from the compiled parent button reaches
    the widget the interpreted child owns, and teardown across the crossing is
    still an exact zero. Tests: a-compiled-parent-can-contain-the-interpreted-integration
    (structural) and a-compiled-page-hosts-the-interpreted-integration-in-one-react-tree
    (browser).
PR #6856 audit (2026-07-24) reopened this exact cross-mode-parity owner. The compiled browser wrapper calls check-attach-opts! and then use-attachment!, but never runs read-opts' child-dependent opaque guard. analyze-behavior proves only that the child is an element; it does not (and for a runtime :use cannot) prove that an {:opaque true} behavior's element has no Freehand children. Therefore an interpreted/JVM use refuses bv/opaque-with-children with :rf.error/behavior-bad-args, while the compiled browser path connects and lets the host overwrite already-rendered children. This contradicts FH-BEHAVIOR-002 and Spec 009's identical host refusal claim.

The same audit found the parity proof incomplete: the new browser suite covers one happy connect/update/disconnect transcript, one command success, and layout timing, while FH-BEHAVIOR-004/005/006 remain labelled interpreted browser and the COMMON FH-BEHAVIOR-002 fixture still exercises only interpreted declarations. Reuse/parameterize the existing corpus; do not build a second behavior runtime or duplicate every test mechanically.
RESOLVED in PR #6866 (branch worker/compiled-behavior-residuals-127). The compiled browser path (behaviors/behavior-el) now enforces the opaque-child law at runtime for literal AND runtime-selected :use, via a shared opaque-child! + element-childless? over the built React element, raising :rf.error/behavior-bad-args BEFORE use-attachment! (no connect, no child-host overwrite). FH-BEHAVIOR-002 gains compiled twins (opaque-host-compiled control + opaque-with-children-compiled discriminator); JVM/interpreted-browser/compiled-browser agree. One shared runtime, no new API. Gates green: freehand JVM 901t/6469a, test:freehand 963t/5532a, test:browser 744t/4605a — 0F/0E.
PR #6866 audit (2026-07-24) reopens this exact owner. The shared runtime guard is correctly placed and the literal compiled opaque-host control/refusal cases pass, but the closing claim overstates the acceptance: the new compiled views hard-code :use bv/opaque, so there is no runtime-selected :use discriminator. Mounted parity coverage still stops at the happy connect/update/disconnect transcript, one command success, and layout timing; abandoned-candidate/commit-only behavior, total cleanup, frame-scoped refusal, and generation fencing remain unproved across both modes, and FH-BEHAVIOR-004/005/006 remain labelled interpreted browser. Close with the smallest load-bearing parameterization of the existing corpus; do not build another runtime or mechanically duplicate the suite.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6866 (merged) — opaque-child runtime guard + full mounted parity. Stale-open from a reset-desync; re-closing.

title: Toggle state is unreachable through the grammar the runtime advises
description:
FOUND BY THE SECOND PILOT (rf2-drpa3.44, PR #6749). Its own framing, which is the clearest statement of the defect:

  "R-B9 is delivered by the platform and the substrate but UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE GRAMMAR."

## The contradiction

The top-layer runtime emits a dev advisory telling authors to reconcile `:on-toggle` "with ordinary event intent". But:
- the closed reserved-projection roster is `::v/value` / `::v/checked` / `::v/key` — there is NO projection for `ToggleEvent.newState`; and
- `v/event` at a handler site raises `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` on the JVM, so the sanctioned escape is refused by the structural host (no SSR, no structural test).

So the substrate ADVISES a path its own grammar REFUSES. The platform provides the state, the substrate provides the intrinsic, and there is no spelling that connects them.

## Why the obvious workaround is not sufficient

The pilot's library counts toggle reports and treats the second as the dismissal. That is CORRECT FOR A SINGLE OVERLAY AND UNSOUND FOR A NESTED PAIR. Proven, not argued: a four-rung attribution ladder shows bare / structured / behaved / state-writing markup all nest correctly, and records the mechanism — opening a nested pair delivers MORE THAN TWO reports, observed as `[:outer :inner :outer]`.

## What a fix must do

Give the author a way to read the toggle's new state as ORDINARY EVENT INTENT — data, comparable, assertable on both hosts — consistent with how `::v/value` and `::v/checked` already work. Whatever shape it takes:
1. It must work on the STRUCTURAL host too (a handler site that only functions in a browser re-creates the gap).
2. It must nest correctly — prove it with the pilot's nested-pair case, not a single overlay.
3. It must not widen the reserved roster into a general escape hatch; the closed roster is a deliberate design property.
4. Interpreted and compiled must agree.

⚠️ THIS ENTERS THE API-MANIFEST SERIAL LANE if it adds a public verb or a reserved projection — sequence accordingly.

## Non-goals
A general event-object projection API. Reopening D015's no-neutral-portal exclusion. Changing the advisory's wording as a substitute for making the path real — the advisory is CORRECT about what an author should be able to do; the grammar is what is missing.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-24): the fix widens the CLOSED reserved-projection roster (::v/value / ::v/checked / ::v/key) and therefore lands in spec/004-Views.md, a HOT-ZONE file that is sequential and never parallel. rf2-drpa3.145 (dedicated key-condition event map subsection) is editing spec/004 right now. Dispatch .126 only AFTER .145 merges, and brief it to rebase onto that text rather than onto its fork point.
