MAYOR RULING 2026-07-24 — SEE THE FULL RULING ON rf2-drpa3.162; this bead is its sibling and the two ship TOGETHER in one dispatch.

Decision: the closed reserved-projection roster (::v/value / ::v/checked / ::v/key) gains DEMONSTRATED-NEED members, not a general host-property escape hatch. Toggle state is one of the two: the runtime advises reconciling :on-toggle "with ordinary event intent" while the grammar provides no projection for ToggleEvent.newState and v/event at a handler site raises :rf.ui.error/ui-tree-malformed on the JVM — so the substrate advises a path its own grammar refuses. A projection for newState resolves that contradiction directly, and is the same shape as ::v/value: one shallow scalar off the event target.

This supersedes the earlier note sequencing this bead behind rf2-drpa3.145 — .145 merged in PR #6774 and spec/004-Views.md is free. The remaining constraint is the roster surface itself (conversion.cljc, controlled.cljc, events.cljc, compiler/analyze.cljc), currently held by two live workers.

NOTE the pilot workaround that must NOT become the fix: counting toggle reports and treating the second as the dismissal is correct for a SINGLE overlay and UNSOUND for a NESTED PAIR — the pilot proved opening a nested pair delivers more than two reports, observed as [:outer :inner :outer].
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6806 alongside rf2-drpa3.162 — one roster, one decision, two members. ::v/new-state resolves the contradiction this bead reported: the runtime advised reconciling :on-toggle with ordinary event intent while the grammar carried no projection for ToggleEvent.newState and v/event at a handler site raised on the JVM. The pilot's counting workaround — correct for a single overlay, UNSOUND for a nested pair — is now removable; that removal is tracked in rf2-srk66.

title: Scope behavior commands to the originating frame
description:
PR #6744 records `:frame` on every live behavior connection, and re-frame's binary fx-handler contract supplies the originating `:frame` in the handler context. The command channel discards that authority:

- `claims-for` filters the process-global `connections` table by `:target` only;
- `command!` receives only `args`;
- the registered effect is `(fn [_ctx args] (command! args))`.

A command emitted by an event in frame A can therefore invoke the sole matching connection in frame B and mutate B's DOM node. Two independent frames that legitimately reuse the same library target are also collapsed into one ambiguous global target and both commands are refused. This violates the frame isolation already represented in the data and D013's ruled exact-frame command scope.

Real browser reproduction on current main: mount `[behavior-views/plain {}]` only under frame `:dom/behaviors-other`, then dispatch `[:probe/command {:target :probe/one :op :mark :args {:label "crossed"}}]` under frame `:dom/behaviors`. Expected `:rf.error/behavior-command-refused` and no host mutation. Actual outcome was `:re-frame.freehand.conformance/no-throw`, and the other frame's node acquired `data-mark="crossed"`. The temporary regression produced exactly two failures in 564 tests / 3297 assertions and was removed byte-identically.

Keep the repair local: thread the fx context's existing frame into command resolution and scope target claims to connections committed under that frame. This is not a request for a new command bus, root selector, host handle, or global identity framework.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for behavior/command frame scope, cross-frame behavior commands, `claims-for`, and host-command frame ownership. `rf2-drpa3.116`, `.117`, `.118`, and `rf2-0qdue` own compiled behavior support, tool projection, ref composition, and error attribution respectively; none owns command frame isolation.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a matching target live only in frame B, a behavior command effect originating in frame A is refused through the existing typed command diagnostic and performs no lifecycle/DOM work in B.
- With the same target id live once in each of frames A and B, a command from each frame reaches exactly its own connection; the pair is not falsely treated as ambiguous.
- Same-frame delivery, same-frame duplicate-target refusal, absent target, unsupported operation, post-teardown refusal, generation fencing, and total cleanup remain green.
- The repair consumes the existing fx `ctx.frame` and connection `:frame`; it adds no public verb, target syntax, root selector, handle registry, queue, or replay path.
- Add a real mounted regression with a decoy frame and assert both the typed outcome and host-node absence/presence, so a no-op or merely filtered transcript cannot pass vacuously.
close_reason: Closed

title: The three verbs a writable controller cannot be built without are not on the published API surface
description:
FOUND BY THE F5f PILOT (rf2-drpa3.43).

D004/D016 make control/record-key, control/reset-revision and control/current? the mechanism by which a controller is writable and buffered: 'asking for the key IS what makes a controller writable', and the reset revision is REQUIRED. A component library therefore cannot build the buffered field D016 designs without calling all three.

None of them is published:
- re-frame.freehand.control is ^:no-doc and its own docstring says 'Deliberately NOT on the re-frame.freehand door';
- the api-manifest generator scans exactly two namespaces, re-frame.freehand and re-frame.freehand.test, so control has no manifest row at any tier;
- consequently a rename, a signature change or an accidental export of these three is invisible to the public-API gate.

So the pilot — which is consumer code by construction — has to :require an internal namespace to exist at all. That is not a blocker (the functions work and the pilot is green); it is an unresolved question about what a component library IS on this surface.

The tension is real in both directions. The docstring's argument for keeping them off the door is good: publishing an authoring verb would advertise controllers as a normal way to hold state, which the ruling rejects. But a library author is not the audience that argument protects, and today they have no supported surface at all.

THREE HONEST OPTIONS:
1. Row the three in the api-manifest at a restrictive tier (:advanced, or a library tier) while leaving them off the re-frame.freehand door — publishes the contract without advertising it on the front porch.
2. Re-export on the door and accept the advertising cost.
3. Rule explicitly that component libraries are 'inside' and the three stay unpublished — in which case say so in 004, because a reader of D016 will otherwise write exactly what this pilot wrote.

Whichever is chosen, the F6 donor-deletion decision should not be taken while a shipped component library's dependencies are undeclared.

OWNING SPEC: 004-Views (Semantic controllers) + API.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: t/render cannot render a view that reads state — the public structural surface needs a render bracket
description:
FOUND BY THE F5f PILOT (rf2-drpa3.43). The blessed public structural-test surface refuses the views a form is made of.

REPRODUCTION (JVM or node, no browser):

    (v/defview counter [_] [:span (v/sub [:app/n])])
    (t/render [counter {}])
    ;; => :rf.error/view-read-outside-render

t/render walks a body but opens no render candidate, and v/sub is legal ONLY during an active declared render. So t/render works on props-only views and refuses every state-reading one — which is most of a real application.

The diagnostic's advice compounds it: it tells the author to 'use the frame-explicit one-shot read', i.e. to rewrite the view under test. That is the wrong recovery for a test.

WHAT THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN SUITES DO. They compose two INTERNAL functions:

    (cell/with-capture (cell/candidate (cell/cell :probe) frame-id)
      (fn [] (t/render form)))

controllers-cljs-test, buffered-controller-cljs-test and now pilot-field-cljs-test all carry a private render-on! helper doing exactly this. re-frame.freehand.cell is not on the API manifest, so a consumer has no published way to write the test the substrate writes for itself.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HARNESS. Fitness-harness R-A11 ('draft -> validity -> gate assertable without a browser') is reachable today only by reaching past the public door.

SHAPE OF A FIX (owner's call): a bracket on the re-frame.freehand.test surface — (t/with-render frame-id (fn [] ...)) or an opts arg (t/render form {:frame fid}) — that opens a candidate, walks, and discards it without committing. The semantics already exist; only the door is missing.

OWNING SPEC: 008-Testing (the t/ surface) with 006-ReactiveSubstrate on the capture. Do not widen v/sub.
notes:
rf2-drpa3.46 (F5i, third pilot to hit this) reproduces it verbatim again, on
today main. t/render on a view that calls v/sub raises
:rf.error/view-read-outside-render; the suite composes the INTERNAL
cell/candidate + cell/with-capture to supply the missing candidate. A
React-library integration reads state like any other view, so every structural
assertion in the pilot goes through that composition. Test:
t-render-alone-still-cannot-render-a-state-reading-view in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_react_interop_cljs_test.cljc
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6772 (eb8534d2ed + 07f39a86ac + a221e16cc4): t/with-render, a macro on re-frame.freehand.test taking NO frame argument. It opens the render the host would have opened (cell/candidate + cell/with-capture) and never commits it, so reads resolve and probe but acquire nothing — the shell's own abandoned-render path. Design calls: no frame arg (the surface's stated 'no frame option' law survives; the candidate binds no ambient frame so rf/with-frame still governs); a macro not a thunk-taking fn (house convention, removes call-site ceremony); t/render itself UNCHANGED (opening a candidate there would silently steal reads from the enclosing capture in the substrate's own suites). Diagnostic now names the bracket for a test caller and keeps the one-shot read for REPL/timer/callback callers; :recovery keyword unchanged so no tool contract moved. Seven co-edited files, not five — see the bead note. All gates EXIT=0 incl. the empty-diff manifest proof and the full fast-PR spine.

title: Behavior ref does not compose with a top-layer ref on one element
description: rf2-drpa3.36's v/behavior clones its decorated element with the behavior's ref (react/cloneElement). rf2-drpa3.34's top layer installs a ref through react-props for a ::web/popover-open? or ::web/modal-open? element. An element carrying BOTH would have the behavior's clone overwrite the top layer's ref, silently disabling the showPopover/showModal reconciliation. Neither slice's tests cover the combination. The decision is real, not mechanical: chain the two refs (and pay a stable-identity cost), or refuse the combination at the door naming the recovery. Filed by rf2-drpa3.36.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED — PR #6748 (worker/ref-composition-drpa3-118). Ruling implemented as ruled: refs CHAIN.

re-frame.freehand.refs (new, cljs-only) owns the composition; behaviors/attach and top-layer/install! both chain instead of writing a bare ref. A chain of one IS that one participant (identical?), so a lone mechanism keeps its own ref identity and attach frequency.

ORDER (obligation a): participants take the node INSIDE OUT — the element's own intrinsics, then each decorating boundary outward — and release in the exact reverse. Stated in spec/004 §Sharing one node; pinned as an exact sequence in refs_cljs_test.cljs.
RELEASE (b): total, under whichever protocol each participant answered with (cleanup fn called, or nil passed). Asserted as an absence after teardown against a CONTROL mount carrying neither mechanism.
BROWSER (c): ref_composition_dom_cljs_test.cljs mounts one element with BOTH; the behavior's DOM mark is read off the very element the browser promoted to its top layer. Hazard reproduced — reverting attach to the bare cloneElement fails the browser gate with exit 1.
SURFACE (d): no new public verb, no new diagnostic id; facade and api-manifest untouched.
NO REGRESSION (e): FH-BEHAVIOR-001..006 and FH-TOPLAYER-001..004 green.

New conformance row FH-BEHAVIOR-007 + fixture. Incidental: react.cljs behavior seam called note-failing-view! with the wrong arity (build warning + a throw while a render throw unwound) — fixed.

Gates all exit 0: freehand JVM 615/4306; test:freehand 524/3500; test:cljs 10649/53593; test:browser 563/3315; conformance-index, donor-inventory, doc-slugs, mkdocs --strict.
close_reason: Closed

title: Compiled v/behavior is invisible to manifest and render-static capability analysis
description: The compiled analyzer does not recognise a (v/behavior ...) form, so the boundary is interpreted-only and every FH-BEHAVIOR conformance row's applicability cell says 'interpreted'. Landing the compiled lowering means: an analyzer arm recognising the seq form, an emitter that reaches the same re-frame.freehand.behaviors runtime (one implementation, both modes, as presence does), and re-cutting the FH-BEHAVIOR-001..003 applicability cells to 'common'. Filed by rf2-drpa3.36.
acceptance_criteria:
- A server-reachable v/behavior site appears in a compiled declaration's :capabilities and :static-facts under one documented capability token; the manifest can no longer report both sets empty for bv/plain-compiled.
- v/render-static refuses a server-reachable behavior in BOTH interpreted and compiled declarations through the existing typed no-silent-elision paths; it never returns HTML that silently drops the attachment.
- A behavior reachable only in v/client-only's client arm remains excluded, while the capability-free fallback still renders.
- Focused regressions pin the manifest fact, direct compiled rejection, transitive dependency rejection, interpreted rejection, and client-only negative control without introducing a new render mode or public surface.
notes:
PR #6856 audit (2026-07-24) reopened this exact compiled-form owner. The new :op :behavior is absent from both compiler/capabilities and view-static-facts. Live reproduction on merged main:

  (select-keys (v/manifest bv/plain-compiled) [:capabilities :static-facts])
  => {:capabilities #{}, :static-facts {:caps #{}, :deps #{}}}

Both (v/render-static [bv/plain {}]) and its compiled twin return ordinary HTML instead of refusing, silently discarding a browser behavior from a NON-hydrating static page. That breaches Spec 011's no-silent-elision rule: a behavior is a live host lifecycle just as surely as an effect/ref. The omission also makes the finite manifest tell tools that a behavior-bearing view has no capability.

Deduplication: all-state searches for behavior + render-static/static-root/manifest/capability found no separate owner. This is the exact compiled-form integration owner; rf2-drpa3.176 owns the associated normative prose. Keep the repair small: teach the existing capability/static-facts walks and the interpreted static fold about the existing behavior marker, respecting server reachability (a behavior only in v/client-only's client arm remains excluded). No new SSR mode, behavior API, or hydration mechanism.
RESOLVED in PR #6866 (branch worker/compiled-behavior-residuals-127). :op :behavior taught to compiler/capabilities, view-static-facts, and the interpreted static fold (tree/live-capability-site) under one token :behavior, respecting server-reachability. Server-reachable behavior now appears in :capabilities + :static-facts; v/render-static refuses it in BOTH compiled (build-time static-capability-offender) and interpreted (render-time assert-static-renderable!) declarations; a behavior only in v/client-only's client arm stays excluded, fallback still renders. CODE-only (176 shipped the prose). Regressions: manifest fact, direct compiled rejection, transitive rejection, interpreted rejection, client-only control. Gates green (see .127).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6866 (manifest/render-static behavior visibility) — mistakenly re-opened by a claim-race; re-closing.

title: Compiled Freehand views are not browser-mountable: the CLJS React lowering + its runtime
description:
## Problem

Split out of rf2-drpa3.81, which fixed the CROSS-HOST half (re-frame.freehand.reactive/sub-read: a compiled view carrying a subscription could not LOAD). The BROWSER half is a strictly larger, separable tier and is untouched.

Today NO compiled view is browser-mountable — subscription or not. v/defview {:compiled true} calls compiler/compile-structural-view, which uses emit-jvm/emit-structural-body on BOTH hosts, so the descriptor carries ONLY a structural body. re-frame.freehand.react/interpreted-component refuses every compiled declaration with a deliberate :rf.error/view-lowering-unavailable ('the compiled tier React lowering is not built yet ... it lands with the slice that owns the ViewCell it renders inside'). This is that slice.

## The measured inventory (rf2-drpa3.81, 2026-07-24)

Whole namespaces the compiled emitters name that do not exist:

  re-frame.freehand.runtime  — 22 vars (Fragment, child, attr-val, style-obj, style-val, jsx-runtime, jsx-spread2/3, spread->props, spread-safe->props, spread-safe-props, foreign-spread-props, render-fn, memo-view, register-view!, props->map, props-equal-generic?, check-key!, check-slot-arity!, slot-ready?, assert-object-ref!, client-only, error-boundary, warn-bare-view-alias!)
  re-frame.freehand.viewcell — render-subs, render-events, render-subs-and-events, render-frame
  re-frame.freehand.hooks    — 12 vars (local-state, dispatch-fn, effect-value, effect-connect, use-ref/effect/layout-effect/effect-event/context/id, with-local-render-guard)
  re-frame.freehand.frames   — frame-ops, scope-element, provider-scope-element, jvm-root-scope, jvm-provider-scope
  re-frame.freehand.client   — create-root*, hydrate-root*, mount*, render!*, root-options, descriptor-index

Absent VARS in namespaces that do exist:

  re-frame.freehand.events/{data-handler, event-handler, handler-callback, dynamic-handler, passive-ref, value-placeholder, checked-placeholder, key-placeholder}
  re-frame.freehand.react/{lazy, use-context, use-effect, use-effect-event, use-id, use-layout-effect}
  re-frame.freehand.tree/{view-boundary, register-view!, jvm-host-op!, opaque-foreign, render-fn, slot-ready?, check-slot-arity!, client-only-fallback, emit-static-html, render-root-tree}

## Why it is design work, not transcription

compiler/emit_cljs.cljc is the DONOR's whole-view emitter and targets the DONOR's ABI, which Freehand does not have:

1. VIEW ABI. emit-component emits jsx(head-sym, props) where head-sym holds a Freehand DESCRIPTOR, not a React component type. In the donor a defview var IS the React.memo component; in Freehand it is a descriptor value. Every :view crossing needs a Freehand-native target that resolves the descriptor to its stable boundary.
2. EVENT ABI. emit_cljs emits five donor constructors whose integer flags PRE-ENCODE the controlled-input :sync bit. Freehand computes that verdict at record time from the ELEMENT facts (controlled/door?), through ONE constructor (events/site) taking an EXPLICITLY THREADED candidate. The compiled lowering has no candidate to thread, so the compiled tier needs an ambient events candidate bound by cell/with-capture — a real decision, and events cannot require cell (cell requires events).
3. DEFVIEW WRAPPER. emit-cljs/emit-defview emits a whole (def name (memo-view ...)); the public door needs a BODY carried on the descriptor beside :structural, the way emit-jvm/emit-structural-body is.
4. PROPS ABI. header-bindings reads slots off a host props object with unchecked-get; the interpreted boundary passes #js {props <clj-map>}. One ABI has to win, or crossings between modes break.

## Scope

The v1 grammar (:text :nothing :expr :element :fragment :view :for :if :let :letfn :case :presence) crossed with the published door (defview describe error-boundary event expand-defview handler manifest markup materialize-event parse-defview-args presence presence-phase projections raw-fn render-fn route-link sub view?) is the REACHABLE surface. hooks/* and frames/* are entirely unreachable through the door today (local, effect, v/ref, frame, frame-root, frame-provider are unpublished or outside v1) and should NOT be built here.

## Acceptance

- A browser test mounts compiled inert and reactive views through v/mount: the inert view renders with NO ViewCell; the event and subscription arms dispatch and read correctly; a subscription change repaints the mounted occurrence.
- The wrapper actually selected agrees with the manifest :view-cell / :reactive? verdict for every arm.
- Elision does not regress (npm run test:elision).
- No dependency on implementation/ui; git grep 're-frame.ui' implementation/freehand/ stays empty.
notes: Split from rf2-drpa3.81 (PR #6741). Sequence AFTER #6741 merges — it depends on reactive/sub-read and on the quoted descriptor manifest entry.
close_reason: Browser-mount half shipped + merged via #6762 (main @847ad222fa); compiled-mount-dom proof green. Sibling rf2-drpa3.81 (cross-host LOAD half) remains open.

title: (BUG) Promote initial-mount Freehand boundary failures after fallback commit
description:
## Problem

PR #6714 / rf2-drpa3.35 promises that a mounted Freehand error boundary emits its safe `:on-error` intent and private always-on `:rf.error/view-render-failed` record exactly once per failure generation, after the fallback commits. The React driver can strand the first generation instead.

A real Chromium probe mounted an interpreted boundary whose child throws on its initial render. The fallback committed, but the report listener still held zero records. An unrelated parent render with the same reset key caused the report to appear later. The lifecycle explains the result: `componentDidMount` calls `promote!` before `componentDidCatch` has called `capture!`; capture then schedules no boundary update, so `componentDidUpdate` has no guaranteed opportunity to promote. If normal recovery changes the reset key first, `componentDidUpdate` calls `reset-to!` before `promote!` and can clear that unpromoted capture permanently.

The probe was removed after reproduction. With it removed, the merged browser suite is green at 500 tests / 2,895 assertions, showing that the current gates do not exercise this initial-mount lifecycle.

## Smallest repair

Make the post-fallback capture path guarantee promotion of the captured generation, and order reset so it cannot erase an unpromoted failure. This can stay inside the existing driver/state-machine seam; no new public callback, scheduler, or reporting channel is needed.

## Deduplication

Searched Beads for initial-mount error-boundary promotion, `componentDidCatch`, stranded reports, and reset-before-promotion. rf2-drpa3.54 owns the final broad browser matrix but not this reproduced runtime defect; no existing follow-up owns it.

## Provenance

Correctness and completeness audit of merged PR #6714, following rf2-drpa3.35.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a child's initial mounted-render failure, the fallback is visible and both the safe intent and private always-on record are emitted once without any unrelated parent render.
- Changing the reset key immediately after the fallback cannot erase the captured generation; successful retry still works.
- Same-key rerenders and React StrictMode do not duplicate either egress for one failure generation.
- The repair remains internal to the existing boundary driver/state machine and adds no public API or reporting channel.
close_reason: SHIPPED PR #6732 (commit e2836a872d). Reproduced in Chromium first via a new errors-dom-cljs-test: one commit of an interpreted boundary over a child throwing on its first render left both channels at 0 (fallback on screen, expected 1 intent + 1 egress); a reset key changed on the very next render left them at 0 permanently. Root cause exactly as filed: React's commit runs componentDidMount/componentDidUpdate BEFORE the update queue's callbacks, and componentDidCatch is one of those callbacks, so the mount hook promoted an empty boundary and the capture that followed scheduled no render to flush it. Fix: componentDidCatch now captures AND promotes (it runs in the layout phase of the commit that put the fallback in the DOM, so this is still 'after the fallback commits'), and componentDidUpdate promotes BEFORE it reconciles the reset key. Law, state machine and once-per-generation gate unchanged; no public API. Browser-only by construction — the JVM structural host has no lifecycle to mis-order. Browser gate green at 507/2943.

title: Keep compatible Freehand hot reloads on the existing occurrence
description:
## Problem

PR #6715 claims that re-running v/mount after a view redefinition preserves the root occurrence and does not reseed what hangs below the host root. The host react-dom root is reused, but the interpreted emitter caches React components by descriptor object identity:

    ;; re-frame.freehand.react/component-for
    (get @components view)
    ...
    (swap! components assoc view c)

A reload mints a new descriptor value, so it also mints a new React component type. React therefore unmounts the old Freehand boundary and mounts a fresh one even when the qualified view id and the interpreted hook skeleton are unchanged. shell.cljs documents that remount explicitly. FH-ROOT-002 checks only that the react-dom root object is identical and the new text appears, so it passes while the mounted occurrence and its DOM state are reseeded.

The long-lived components atom also retains the obsolete descriptor, component, and render-body closure for each such generation unless the emitter namespace itself reloads.

## Reproduction

A temporary real Chromium/createRoot audit regression mounted a descriptor whose qualified view id was ::audit-reload and whose body contained an uncontrolled input. It then:

1. Set the mounted input value to "typed" and focused it.
2. Created a fresh descriptor with the same view id and a body-only change.
3. Re-ran v/mount into the same container.

All three compatible-reload assertions failed:

    DOM occurrence: old input was not identical to the new input
    value:          expected "typed", actual "seed-after"
    focus:          expected the input, actual document.body

The existing host-root identity assertion remained green. The temporary probe was removed after reproduction.

## Outcome

Keep the React boundary stable for a compatible redefinition of the same qualified view id, publish the new body through that stable shell, and wire the existing ViewCell body-generation fence so a render from the old body cannot commit after the reload. Remount only when a genuinely incompatible hook signature requires it. Retire obsolete descriptor/body cache entries rather than retaining every reload generation.

Complete Spec 004's current Identity, hot reload, and remount placeholder with the compatible-shell versus clean-remount rule, then make FH-ROOT-002 prove occurrence preservation instead of only react-dom root reuse.

## Non-goals

No multi-root identity, container-conflict handling, authored root ids, hydration, failed-root isolation, or total teardown; rf2-drpa3.42 already owns those. No generalized replacement for React Refresh, and no promise to preserve local state across an incompatible hook-signature change.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6715.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real-browser regression mounts an uncontrolled input, mutates and focuses it, then publishes a body-only redefinition with the same qualified view id; the new body is visible while the input DOM node, typed value, focus, and compatible component state remain intact.
2. The react-dom root and the compatible Freehand boundary remain identical across that reload; ordinary app-namespace reloads do not accumulate obsolete descriptor/component/render-body entries.
3. The body revision advances at the reload publication seam. A candidate rendered from the old body before publication but committed afterward is rejected as stale and publishes no dependencies, events, or evidence; a fresh render of the new body commits normally.
4. An explicitly incompatible hook-signature change, once applicable, performs one clean remount rather than corrupting hook state; body-only interpreted edits use the stable path.
5. FH-ROOT-002 and Spec 004 state and prove mounted occurrence preservation, not merely equality of the outer react-dom root object plus changed text.
6. Existing Freehand JVM, focused CLJS, and browser suites remain green.
close_reason: PR #6726 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6726

title: Keep presence elements commit-owned across abandoned React renders
description:
## Problem

PR #6713 absorbs the keyed presence runtime into Freehand and claims one exactly-once retention contract across both modes. PresenceComponent nevertheless publishes candidate React elements into its shared committed ref during render:

    elements (merge (.-elements state) (into {} incoming-pairs))
    (set! (.-elements state) elements)

That ref is shared by the current and work-in-progress fibers. A render that Suspense abandons can therefore overwrite retained element values even though none of its effects commit. A later timer callback force-updates the current tree and renders the abandoned value.

## Reproduction

A real Chromium/createRoot probe drove this sequence with the deterministic presence clock:

1. Mount keyed children b="committed-b" and c.
2. Remove c at logical t=0, advance to t=50, then remove b. C is due at 100 and B at 150.
3. Start a transition that re-enters b as "abandoned-b", then suspend in a sibling after PresenceComponent renders. Verify the candidate rendered and suspended while the DOM still says "committed-b".
4. Advance the clock by 51 so only c's earlier exit fires. Its removal callback calls force! on the current tree.
5. c is removed as expected, but b changes to "abandoned-b": the timer-driven current-tree commit published an element from the never-committed candidate.

The temporary audit regression failed exactly:

    expected: "committed-b"
    actual:   "abandoned-b"

The source comment says committed state is mutated only in effects/removal callbacks, but the render-phase elements assignment violates that invariant.

## Outcome

Keep the retained element snapshot commit-owned. A candidate render may derive the elements it needs to return, but it must not make those elements observable to timers or other committed updates until that candidate commits. Preserve the existing phase machine, first-appearance order, re-entry cancellation, exactly-once timeout removal, and shared runtime across modes.

## Non-goals

No new animation system, scheduler, transition API, state manager, or generalized Suspense abstraction.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6713.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real browser/createRoot regression reproduces the two staggered exits plus Suspense-abandoned re-entry: after the unrelated earlier timer fires, the retained child still renders its last committed element and never the abandoned candidate.
2. PresenceComponent performs no shared-ref element publication during render; element ownership becomes observable to timer/removal callbacks only after commit.
3. A normally committed same-key prop update still replaces the rendered element, and a committed re-entry still cancels its timer and returns to :present.
4. Existing deterministic-clock, terminal removal, duplicate identity, first-appearance order, StrictMode, and unmount cleanup behavior remains green.
5. The regression proves the candidate actually rendered and suspended before asserting that its value cannot leak.
close_reason: PR #6728: presence element publication moved from render to the commit effect (the atomic shell's own discipline). Real createRoot probe with a Suspense-abandoned transition reproduces the leak pre-fix (expected committed-b, actual abandoned-b) and guards it.

title: Finish checker reader-conditionals in sets and around declarations
description:
## Problem

PR #6717 fixes one CLJ-versus-CLJS body divergence by reading with :read-cond :preserve and selecting branches in a new resolve-conditionals helper. That handwritten resolver is incomplete in two legal .cljc placements, so the compile checker can still false-green or omit the CLJS branch it claims to inspect.

### Reproduction 1: reader conditional inside a set

A loaded .cljc namespace contained:

    (v/defview set-divergent
      [_]
      [:div {:title (str #{#?(:clj 1 :cljs v/sub)})}])

The public check-file result was:

    {:compile-eligible? true :findings []}

resolve-conditionals handles maps, vectors, and seqs but has no set branch, so the preserved ReaderConditional survives inside the set. Passing the correctly selected CLJS value, #{v/sub}, through the same analyzer returns :compile-eligible? false with :rf.ui.compile/unsupported-form because the bare reactive var would under-declare the manifest. The checker therefore still presents an eligible answer for a CLJS branch the compiler rejects.

Splicing conditionals in sets have the same traversal hole.

### Reproduction 2: reader conditional around the declaration

A second loaded .cljc namespace wrapped the whole declaration:

    #?(:clj  (v/defview branch-view {:compiled true} [_] [:div ...])
       :cljs (v/defview branch-view {:compiled true} [{:keys [tag]}] [tag ...]))

check-file returned zero reports. read-declarations tests seq? and resolves v/defview before it resolves a top-level ReaderConditional, so the declaration is skipped entirely even though the CLJS branch has the same dynamic-head refusal PR #6717 was meant to expose.

Both probes exercised public check-file and were removed after reproduction. rf2-drpa3.80 owns the distinct pure-.cljs build-environment and Spec 004D wording work; it does not cover incomplete .cljc conditional traversal or declaration discovery.

## Outcome

Make preserved reader-conditional selection cover the legal source shapes the checker accepts: sets, including splicing, and declaration-level conditionals before v/defview discovery. Keep one analyzer, one refusal per declaration, source order, metadata coordinates, and the read-only law.

## Non-goals

No general-purpose source analyzer, custom reader-feature framework, auto-fix, new diagnostic ids, or expansion of rf2-drpa3.80.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6717.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A public check-file regression with an ineligible CLJS-only form nested in a set reports the same analyzer-owned refusal as the correctly selected CLJS branch; it cannot return compile-eligible true.
2. Cover both ordinary #? and legal #?@ splicing inside sets while preserving set type and metadata.
3. A public check-file regression with a whole v/defview under a top-level reader conditional emits the appropriate declaration report(s) in source order and catches an ineligible CLJS branch; it cannot return an empty report vector.
4. Compare the repaired cases with real CLJ/CLJS reader or macroexpansion behavior, and keep the existing conditional-free identity/read-only/non-vacuity controls green.
5. Correct the new fixture prose that says the checker reaches CLJS via reader :features #{:cljs}; the implementation now preserves and selects the branch itself.
notes: HELD (mayor, 2026-07-23): this finishes the checker reader-conditional work from rf2-drpa3.76, so it touches compiler/check.cljc — which a compiler-follow-ups worker currently owns (rf2-drpa3.80 + rf2-drpa3.82). Dispatch the moment that PR lands, verifying the exact surface against the merged tree first. Its predecessor established the mechanism: read with :read-cond :preserve and select branches manually, because the JVM readers :clj feature is unconditionally present and cannot be disabled via :features. Build on that; do not re-derive it.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6724: two uncovered reader-conditional placements in the compile checker, both false-greens of the class #6717 fixed. SETS — resolve-conditionals descended maps/vectors/seqs but not sets, so a preserved conditional fell through the :else identity leg and the analyzer got a reader object where the browser build has a real set; fixed with a set? branch reusing resolve-children (so #?@ splices), rebuilt via (empty form) so set type and metadata ride through. WHOLE DECLARATIONS — read-declarations tested seq? BEFORE resolving, so a conditional wrapping a defview was skipped entirely and the file reported nothing about it; discovery now runs on the resolved branches. CONSEQUENCE: a declaration-level conditional diverges PARAMS not just body, so :cljs-body became :cljs-branch ([:params :children-policy :body] merged over the declaration) — without it the repro reported unresolved-head instead of dynamic-head, i.e. the right verdict for the wrong reason. Evidence: pre-fix both set cases compile-eligible with empty findings and only 3 declarations discovered; post-fix both refuse naming v/sub, 5 discovered, controls stay eligible. Hand-selection cross-checked against clojure.tools.reader at :features #{:clj}/#{:cljs} — an oracle independent of the code under test. Spec deliberately untouched: 004D already said the checker analyzes every branch a compile would visit, so the SPEC WAS RIGHT and the implementation was in violation. Follow-up filed as rf2-drpa3.90 (map splicing conditional throws under :preserve).

title: Finetune the runtime Hiccup interpreter for efficiency
description:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (Mike, 2026-07-23): "Make sure the agent who creates the run-time hiccup interpreter creates an implementation which is finetuned and efficient."

## Why this is P1 and not a nice-to-have

The runtime Hiccup interpreter IS Freehand's value proposition. EP-0036 positions the interpreted mode as the PAVED PATH — the default for unrestricted application authoring — with the compiled tier as a capability you reach for on hot boundaries, explicitly NOT a mandate ("compilation is a capability, not an instruction to compile every view", codex section 8). If the interpreter is a naive walk, that proposition inverts: interpreted becomes too slow for ordinary use, every view needs {:compiled true}, and the compiled tier silently becomes a requirement. The design's central claim collapses.

It is also the hot path: EVERY interpreted view render goes through it, on every commit.

## Scope

The runtime Hiccup walk and React element production — principally implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs (the interpreted React emitter), and the shared normalization it uses (conversion.cljc, node.cljc, tree.cljc's runtime path where it participates). Verify the exact surface at dispatch; the artefact has moved repeatedly.

## What "finetuned and efficient" means concretely

Tune the things a runtime Hiccup interpreter is known to spend on: per-node allocation, repeated attribute/style normalization, keyword-to-string conversion, props map rebuilding, children sequence realization, the fast path for the common shapes (a keyword tag with a literal props map and a small child vector), and avoiding work for nodes that did not change. Prefer measured wins over speculative cleverness.

## REUSE EVALUATION — reagent-slim (do this before writing new optimizations)

reagent-slim (implementation/adapters/reagent-slim, namespaces reagent2.*) contains reagent2/impl/template.cljs — a battle-tested, already-slimmed runtime Hiccup-to-React implementation carrying years of optimization. Freehand's react.cljs currently calls react/createElement directly and does NOT reuse it.

EVALUATE that code for reuse of its ELEMENT/ATTRIBUTE/STYLE PLUMBING and its performance techniques. Two hard boundaries:
1. Do NOT import Reagent's COMPONENT PROTOCOL — form-1/2/3 components, :key meta read off vectors, ratom deref tracking. D002 rejects all of it (Freehand has non-IFn descriptors, no ratoms through views, its own event materializer). Importing it would contradict ratified decisions.
2. reagent-slim is NOT a donor to be absorbed and deleted — it lives on as a first-class independent adapter. So the options are reuse-by-dependency, a deliberate copy of the plumbing, or study-and-reimplement. State which you chose and WHY, including the coupling cost.

If you conclude reuse is wrong, say so with reasons — a justified reimplementation is a fine outcome, an unexamined one is not.

## Measurement discipline (D021)

Do NOT guess at optimizations. Use the shipped B-spine harness and the B1 interpreted-vs-compiled fixture as the baseline. Deterministic properties (allocation counts, node counts, element-creation counts) are hard gates; wall-clock is EVIDENCE ONLY with no numeric pass/fail threshold — the harness enforces that split mechanically, so register measurements through it rather than hand-rolling.

Report before/after with full provenance. A speedup you cannot attribute is not a result.

## Acceptance

1. Reuse evaluation of reagent-slim stated explicitly with a decision and rationale.
2. Measured improvement on the B1 workload, published with provenance; deterministic counters (allocations or element-creations per render) show the win, not just wall-clock.
3. NO semantic change — the interpreted output stays structurally identical; the cross-host conformance corpus and every FH row stay green. Prove it: the same fixtures produce the same semantic values before and after.
4. No new public verb (this is internal tuning) — so it stays OFF the api-manifest serial lane.

## Non-goals

Making interpreted match compiled (they have different jobs); micro-optimizations that damage clarity for unmeasured gain (the posture rejects gold-plating); changing the semantic model; importing Reagent's component protocol.
notes:
CURRENT STATE (mayor, verified on main 2026-07-23): the interpreter ALREADY EXISTS and is merged — this bead TUNES it, it does not build it. Surfaces and sizes: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs (334 lines, the interpreted React emitter, four react/createElement sites), conversion.cljc (398, attribute/style/class normalization), node.cljc (421, the canonicalizer BOTH modes build through), tree.cljc (239, the JVM structural walk). Built by rf2-drpa3.17 (F1c interpreted tree) over rf2-drpa3.16 (F1b descriptor), then rf2-drpa3.26 (F3b) refactored tree.cljc into a front end over node.cljc builders so both modes share one canonicalizer.

IT WAS BUILT FOR CORRECTNESS, NOT SPEED. Every acceptance criterion on those beads was cross-host semantic equality and conversion-table fidelity. No performance pass has ever run on it, and it does not reuse reagent-slim plumbing.

MEASURED STARTING BASELINE — already published by the B1 evidence bead rf2-drpa3.48 (merged in PR 6709; JVM 21, 40 samples): interpreted p50 5.32ms / 5.69MB allocated; compiled p50 1.73ms / 2.67MB. So interpreted is about 3x the time and 2x the allocation of compiled. START FROM THESE NUMBERS — do not re-derive the baseline, re-run B1 to confirm it still holds on current main, then improve against it.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD ANSWERS: some gap is expected and correct — that is what compilation buys. Determine whether 3x/2x is the honest floor for a TUNED interpreter or whether a naive walk is inflating it. That distinction decides whether "compile only hot boundaries" is a real choice for users or a necessity, which is the EP-0036 value proposition.
RESULT (PR 6720, revision 8ff9fa9a, JVM 21, B-spine :warmup 5 :samples 40).

MEASURED — B1 interpreted arm allocation 5,658,160 -> 959,208 bytes (-83.0%); small template 155,512 -> 27,448 (-82.3%). Deterministic to the byte (min=p50=max=27448 across 40 samples). Interpreted/compiled ratio: allocation 2.15x -> 1.19x, self-time 3.13x -> 1.66x. The compiled arm improved 69% too, because node.cljc + conversion.cljc are shared by both modes.

ANSWERS THE BEAD'S QUESTION: 3x/2x was NOT the honest floor for a tuned interpreter — a naive walk was inflating it. 'Compile only hot boundaries' is a real choice, not a necessity.

SEVEN COMMITS, each with its own measured attribution: (1) memoize the .class#id tag parse per keyword, 1800 -> 0 b/call, -32.6%; (2) push the *ns-context* binding only when the context changes, 752 b/element elided, -18.3%; (3) class-string one-part fast path + no sugar copy, 656 -> 0, -20.4%; (4) drop empty text on arrival, deleting the per-node children rebuild, -17.4%; (5) fold authored attrs into ONE element map instead of merging two, merge 961 -> literal 112, -49.3%; (6) pos?/count instead of seq for emptiness, -10.5%; (7) remember the React prop + handler name projections, react-event-name 824 -> 0 (React path, outside B1).

REUSE DECISION — adopt reagent-slim's TECHNIQUE (its tag-name-cache / prop-name-cache idea), reject the dependency and the copy; reimplement. Reasons: the hot path is .cljc and runs on the JVM where reagent2.impl.template (.cljs, #js/aget) cannot run at all — 83% of the win is JVM-side; the two parse grammars genuinely differ (donor requires #id before .class, Freehand accepts both orders) so a dependency would change semantics; and an adapter classpath edge inverts the substrate's dependency direction. Two deliberate improvements on the donor: keyed on the KEYWORD not its name (the donor patched that aliasing class twice), and BOUNDED at 4096 so a keyword-minting caller loses the cache rather than leaking. NO component protocol taken — D002 respected.

SEMANTIC IDENTITY PROVEN: 57 plain-data conformance fixture cases + all four B1 renders dumped as EDN at the merge base and at HEAD — byte-identical, 120,477 bytes each, same hash. spec/ untouched. B1 structural-parity + node-count gates pass both sides.

DECLINED, unmeasured: three react.cljs-internal candidates (doseq over attrs, double :key lookup, void-tag predicate order) — no deterministic allocation counter in CLJS (node heapUsed is occupancy) and a React bench arm is bench/** work another worker owns. DECLINED, risk: splitting node/element's [attrs events] tuple fold (~8% of what remains) would reorder attribute-vs-handler diagnostics. title: Make compiled Freehand views runnable through the public door
description:
## Problem

Merged PR #6716 closes F3d and publishes a :view-cell elision verdict, while the public v/defview documentation presents {:compiled true} as the second runnable execution mode and v/sub as having the same semantics in both modes. The actual compiled runtime is not present in the Freehand artifact.

The compiler rewrites v/sub to re-frame.freehand.reactive/sub-read; that namespace does not exist. The CLJS emitter likewise names re-frame.freehand.runtime/*, re-frame.freehand.viewcell/*, and re-frame.freehand.frames/*, none of which exists under implementation/freehand/src. Thus inert and reactive compiled views can be analyzed and their expansion inspected, but their browser lowering is not runnable through the public door.

The #6716 suites avoid the failure: the subscription test injects a resolver and stops at structural-manifest; the ViewCell oracle walks the emitted form as data; the census calls v/manifest without mounting a compiled view. All ordinary suites can therefore remain green while the public compiled path is unusable.

## Steps to Reproduce

From implementation/freehand run this real public-path declaration:

    clojure -M -e "(require '[re-frame.freehand :as v]) (v/defview probe {:compiled true} [p] [:span (v/sub [:person/by-id (:id p)])])"

It fails before the view can be declared:

    ClassNotFoundException: re-frame.freehand.reactive

As a control, an inert compiled declaration succeeds and reports :view-cell :elided. Searching implementation/freehand/src shows none of the runtime namespaces referenced by the CLJS lowering.

## Outcome

Make compiled Freehand views runnable through the same public v/defview door. Absorb or implement the minimal Freehand-owned runtime targets the emitted lowering calls, connecting reactive reads and committed events to the existing Freehand cell/shell semantics. Do not add a second declaration form, donor dependency, compatibility layer, or parallel reactive system.

The manifest verdict must describe the lowering that actually runs: an inert compiled view uses the plain memoized path; a v/sub, committed event, dispatch function, or frame read keeps the reactive shell.

## Deduplication

Checked rf2-drpa3.49, .53, .56, .57, and .73. They cover later measurement/conformance/absorption gates or documentation, not this concrete currently-public runtime failure. The donor inventory still marks the relevant runtime/reactor rows pending.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Real source namespaces declare compiled inert, committed-event, and v/sub views through public v/defview with the ordinary resolver; no injected analyzer resolver and no missing-namespace/undeclared-var path.
2. A JVM structural test declares and renders a compiled v/sub view without ClassNotFoundException, and its public manifest reports the actual subscription site.
3. A browser test mounts compiled inert and reactive views. The inert view renders with no ViewCell; the event and subscription arms execute, dispatch/read correctly, and a subscription change repaints the mounted occurrence.
4. The emitted runtime references resolve entirely inside Freehand/core dependencies; implementation/freehand does not depend on the donor implementation/ui artifact.
5. The manifest :view-cell / :reactive? verdict agrees with the wrapper actually selected for all control arms, and the pre-fix public-path regression demonstrably fails before the fix.
6. Freehand JVM, focused CLJS, and required browser suites pass with non-zero plausible counts.
notes:
EVIDENCE FROM THE COMPILER FOLLOW-UPS SLICE (PR #6721, 2026-07-23) — a concrete instance of exactly what this bead must fix, found while building per-site manifest coordinates:

(v/sub ...) inside a COMPILED body lowers to re-frame.freehand.reactive/sub-read — A NAMESPACE THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. So a compiled view carrying a subscription WILL NOT LOAD. Consequence observed downstream: the :subscriptions and :frame-ops rosters are unreachable through the public v/manifest door, because no compiled census view can carry a sub without failing to load. That worker had to prove manifest totality using :events (list-anchored, locates itself) and :crossings (vector, inherits its declaration position) instead — which happens to cover both halves of the coordinate-totality question, but only because the sub path was closed to it.

ALSO STALE AND WORTH FIXING HERE: the manifest_views.cljc census docstring claims v/sub is "not yet a public var on the door". That is now WRONG — v/sub shipped as public in PR #6711. The real blocker was never the door; it is the missing runtime namespace. Correct the docstring when this bead lands so the next reader is not sent after the wrong cause.

This is not a separate defect to file — it is the compiled-runtime wiring this bead exists to complete. Scope check when dispatching: the compiled React/ViewCell lowering (viewcell/runtime/hooks namespaces) was explicitly deferred out of the F3d manifests slice as a later F3 concern, and this is where it comes due.
RUNTIME-TARGET INVENTORY, measured 2026-07-24 (worker rf2-drpa3.81). The bead's list is a FLOOR. Every re-frame.freehand.*/var the compiled emitters name, resolved:

ABSENT WHOLE NAMESPACES: runtime (22 vars), viewcell (4), hooks (12), frames (5), client (6). ABSENT VARS in existing namespaces: events/{data-handler event-handler handler-callback dynamic-handler passive-ref value-placeholder checked-placeholder key-placeholder}; react/{lazy use-context use-effect use-effect-event use-id use-layout-effect}; tree/{view-boundary register-view! jvm-host-op! opaque-foreign render-fn slot-ready? check-slot-arity! client-only-fallback emit-static-html render-root-tree}.

REACHABLE-THROUGH-THE-PUBLIC-DOOR subset: only reactive/sub-read. hooks/* and frames/* are unreachable (local, effect, v/ref, frame, frame-root, frame-provider are unpublished vars or ops outside :re-frame.freehand/v1); runtime/* and viewcell/* are named ONLY by emit-cljs/emit-defview, which v/defview does NOT call — the public door calls compiler/compile-structural-view, which uses emit-jvm/emit-structural-body on BOTH hosts.

CONSEQUENCE: no compiled view is browser-mountable today, subscription or not; react.cljs refuses every compiled declaration with a deliberate :rf.error/view-lowering-unavailable. That is not caused by the missing reactive namespace and is not closed by adding it. Split to rf2-drpa3.113 with the full inventory and the four ABI mismatches that make it design work rather than transcription (view ABI: a Freehand defview var holds a DESCRIPTOR, not a React component; event ABI: donor flags pre-encode the controlled-input sync bit that Freehand derives from element facts at record time, and events cannot require cell; defview wrapper; props ABI).
PR #6741 opened (worker/compiled-runtime-drpa3-81). Cross-host half landed; browser half split to rf2-drpa3.113. Gates: freehand JVM 573/3862, test:freehand 467/3169, test:cljs 10592/53262, test:browser 542/3170, test:elision PASS 60/60 absent, three python gates exit 0. Omitted-ViewCell count unchanged at exactly 4.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6762 — compiled Freehand views runnable through the public door. Verified landed; stale in_progress claim cleared during the 2026-07-24 reconcile.

title: API-manifest sidecar loader reintroduces the shadow.resource unbound-Var race
description:
## Problem

PR #6709 added a second lazy loader for `shadow.resource/slurp-resource` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj`. `read-sidecar` calls `requiring-resolve` directly whenever a CLJS macro expands.

That is the exact cold-load pattern already proven racy in rf2-sff2s: `requiring-resolve` performs its first `resolve` before entering the namespace require lock. While another macro-expansion thread is loading the un-AOT `shadow.resource` namespace, the Var can be interned but still unbound; the second resolver returns that Var and calling it fails with `Attempting to call unbound fn`.

The earlier fix put the Freehand conformance consumer behind one namespace-local delay. #6709 introduces an independent resolver in another macro namespace, so the old single-flight proof no longer covers the process: the API-manifest probe and a Freehand fixture macro can cold-load the same namespace concurrently.

## Evidence

The audit ran a clean Clojure process against shadow-cljs 3.4.10. One thread cold-loaded `shadow.resource/slurp-resource`; an observer waited until the Var appeared and then invoked the same direct `requiring-resolve` pattern. It returned `{:state :unbound, :same-var? true}` while the loader subsequently reported `:loader-bound? true`. This proves the call can return the interned-but-unbound Var rather than waiting for namespace initialization.

All ordinary post-merge lanes were green (JVM Freehand 425 tests / 2799 assertions, CLJS Freehand 308 / 2158, B1 suite exit 0). Those greens are expected for a scheduling race and are not evidence against it; rf2-sff2s documents why a rerun can win the coin toss with the defect intact.

## Outcome

Make every macro consumer of `shadow.resource/slurp-resource` cold-load-safe together. Enter the serialized `require` path before resolving the Var (or use an equivalent process-wide single-flight), then cache the bound function. Update both the conformance fixture loader and the new API-manifest sidecar loader so two independent consumers cannot race each other.

Retain the build-dependency behavior #6709 added: sidecar-only and fixture-only edits must still invalidate the corresponding warm shadow-cljs cache without any cache-clearing ritual.

## Deduplication

rf2-sff2s is closed and repaired the original one-consumer Freehand fixture failure. rf2-ze3ai is closed and owns the sidecar dependency edge. Neither owns the new second-consumer race introduced by PR #6709; this issue is discovered from rf2-ze3ai and reuses rf2-sff2s's proven failure model rather than inventing a separate loader design.

## Non-goals

No cache-clear step, retry loop, eager JVM dependency on shadow-cljs, alternate resource format, or general build-loader framework.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Both current macro consumers resolve `shadow.resource/slurp-resource` through a cold-load-safe path that cannot return an unbound Var; no direct per-call `requiring-resolve` remains at either site.
2. Add a deterministic concurrency control with TWO independent resolver sites starting from an unloaded namespace: the pre-fix shape observes an unbound Var, while the fixed shape returns one bound callable to every participant across repeated runs.
3. Re-prove the API sidecar property on a warm cache: a sidecar-only negative-control edit makes the CLJS manifest probe red without clearing `.shadow-cljs`, and restoring it makes the same build green.
4. Re-prove the Freehand fixture property on a warm cache for both Node and the browser-applicable fixture lane; restoring the fixture returns green without cache clearing.
5. JVM Freehand, CLJS Freehand, full CLJS, and browser suites remain green. A single cold green is not the race proof; criterion 2 is.

title: Atomic shell leaks staged handles when commit-side read fails
description:
## Problem

PR #6701 makes commit staging transactional only through observation acquisition. After stage! succeeds, commit! calls obs/read for every staged or retained handle outside that rollback guard. obs/read is a documented fail-loud operation and may also dereference/recompute application subscription code. If one read throws before publication, every newly acquired handle remains live even though the candidate publishes nothing.

This strands a subscription ref/watch and contradicts the atomic shell's central failed-candidate rollback law. The second currency check also currently occurs before those reads. If a read re-enters and advances body/frame authority, the stale candidate can still publish because authority is not checked again afterward.

## Steps to Reproduce

A deterministic audit probe opened one ownership-free candidate, recorded one read, mocked one successful obs/acquire!, made the subsequent obs/read throw, and recorded obs/release! calls.

Run that candidate through cell/commit!. The original exception propagates and the cell remains unpublished, but the release log is empty instead of containing the freshly acquired handle exactly once.

The focused probe ran 1 test with 2 assertions and failed only the rollback assertion:

expected one released handle; actual release log [].

The temporary probe file was removed after reproduction.

## Outcome

Make the entire pre-publication phase transactional, including commit-side reads. A read failure must release every handle freshly acquired for this candidate, in reverse acquisition order, leave the prior committed bundle untouched, and rethrow the original failure. A read that changes authority must cause the candidate to roll back its fresh staging and return :abandoned rather than publish stale ownership.

Keep retained prior handles installed and untouched. Do not hide or translate the original observation/subscription failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a deterministic regression where acquisition succeeds and obs/read throws before publication; assert the fresh handle is released exactly once, prior dependencies/events/evidence remain unchanged, and the original exception escapes.
2. Add a re-entrancy regression where a commit-side read advances the cell generation or frame authority; assert the candidate returns :abandoned, fresh staging is released, and nothing from that candidate publishes.
3. Preserve acquisition-failure rollback, acquire-before-release ordering, and successful commit behavior.
4. Run the Freehand JVM and CLJS suites; exercise the new law on both hosts where the common implementation applies.
5. Update Spec 006 wording/tests if necessary so the final currency boundary is truthfully after every callback-capable or fail-loud pre-publication operation.

## Non-goals

No new public API, alternate observation port, retry policy, exception swallowing, or broader transaction framework.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6701.

HELD this tick ONLY because it touches a file (cell.cljc / compiler-check.cljc / tree.cljc) that the in-flight F4+F1+F3 wave (v/sub, presence, errors, mount, test-surface, manifests) is actively editing — dispatching now would collide. Dispatch as top priority the moment those PRs land and the core settles, verifying the exact file surface against the merged tree first. Main is currently GREEN; these are latent correctness gaps, not a red-main emergency, so the one-wave hold is safe.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6718 (P1, merged): atomic-shell commit-side reads moved INSIDE the pre-publication transaction — a throwing read now releases every freshly-acquired handle in reverse acquisition order and rethrows untranslated; the final currency boundary sits after every callback-capable pre-publication op so an authority-advancing read rolls back to :abandoned. fresh-handles helper unifies reverse-order release (also corrected the pre-existing map-iteration-order abandon path). Non-vacuity: pre-fix RED 7 failures, post-fix GREEN, mutation RED 2. Invariants preserved: dual-axis currency, non-terminal disconnect!, failed candidate publishes nothing. spec/006 failed-candidate law updated.

title: Compile checker can false-green CLJS views by analyzing only the CLJ branch
description:
## Problem

PR #6708 says the read-only checker runs the same analyzer as the build for both compilation targets, but check-file always reads reader conditionals with features #{:clj}, constructs an analyzer environment with :host :clj, and resolves through a loaded Clojure namespace. The real compiler selects :host :cljs and uses the ClojureScript compiler environment when &env carries a CLJS namespace.

That makes the checker capable of reporting a SPA declaration eligible from its JVM branch while the CLJS branch the browser build compiles is ineligible. Pure .cljs namespaces also have no ordinary loaded JVM namespace for live-namespace to find.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a .cljc declaration with an interpreted CLJ branch [:div "JVM branch is eligible"] and a CLJS-only {:compiled true} branch [tag "CLJS branch has a dynamic head"], with tag bound from props.

1. Run check-file on the loaded JVM namespace. It returns :compile-eligible? true.
2. Compile the same namespace with shadow-cljs. Macroexpansion fails with :rf.ui.compile/dynamic-head and recovery [:use-a-literal-head :extract-declared-child :keep-interpreted].

The audit reproduced this with a temporary host-divergent fixture: clojure -M:test ran 1 test / 1 assertion green, while shadow-cljs compile node-test-freehand failed on the exact declaration. The fixture was removed after reproduction.

Current implementation points are compiler/check.cljc read-opts (:features #{:clj}), findings-for (:host :clj), and live-namespace. The actual compiler chooses :cljs from the macro environment in compiler.cljc compile-structural-view.

## Outcome

Make checker results target-host truthful. A CLJS eligibility query must analyze the CLJS branch with the same resolution environment as the CLJS compiler, or fail loudly that no CLJS build environment was supplied. It must never silently present the CLJ answer as the answer for a SPA build.

Keep the existing read-only, no-recommendation, and analyzer-owned-diagnostic laws. Do not add a second analyzer or heuristic approximation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pin the divergent .cljc case above: the CLJ target is eligible and the CLJS target reports :rf.ui.compile/dynamic-head, matching actual macroexpansion.
2. Define and test the supported .cljs workflow. Either check-file can receive or derive a real CLJS analyzer environment, or it refuses .cljs/CLJS-target checks explicitly and didactically; no fake loaded JVM namespace.
3. Reader conditionals are selected for the requested target rather than unconditionally #{:clj}.
4. Update the 004D host claim and tool documentation to name the real target/build-context contract.
5. Re-run JVM Freehand and CLJS Freehand suites with a non-vacuity probe for the host-divergent fixture.

## Non-goals

No auto-fix, promotion recommender, alternate diagnostic ids, or general-purpose source analyzer framework.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6708.
notes:
NEXT-WAVE PRIORITY (mayor, 2026-07-23): P1 correctness bug in freshly-merged Freehand core. HELD this tick ONLY because it touches a file (cell.cljc / compiler-check.cljc / tree.cljc) that the in-flight F4+F1+F3 wave (v/sub, presence, errors, mount, test-surface, manifests) is actively editing — dispatching now would collide. RESOLVED via PR #6717 (branch worker/freehand-checker-falsegreen-drpa3-76; do-not-merge, mayor merges). Root cause: JVM reader's :clj platform feature is always present, so :read-cond :allow resolves #?(:clj … :cljs …) to :clj regardless of :features — the :cljs branch was elided before the analyzer ran. Fix: read with :read-cond :preserve and select each target's branch in a new resolve-conditionals (in check.cljc only), analyzing BOTH branches; a refusal in either makes the view ineligible. Conditional-free declarations take an identity fast-path (byte-for-byte unchanged). title: Keep structural trees EDN-round-trippable for nested non-data values
description:
## Problem

Spec 004B promises that every structural tree is plain, serialisable Clojure data whose EDN print/read round-trips losslessly. The interpreted walk only replaces a prop when the prop value itself is a function, while nested non-data values survive unchanged; event vectors and option maps are also recorded verbatim.

The tree is therefore host-specific and cannot satisfy the central serialisability/cross-host contract. The relevant current paths are `re-frame.freehand.node/recorded-prop` and `event-entry`; the behavior originated in PR #6697.

## Steps to Reproduce

On the JVM, declare a simple Freehand view and render either `[view {:config {:callback identity}}]` or an element carrying `{:on-click [:app/go identity]}`. Print the result with `pr-str`, then call `read-string` on it. The tree contains `#object[...]` and read-back fails with `No reader function for tag object`.

## Expected Behavior

Every accepted structural tree is host-neutral plain data and round-trips losslessly through the documented EDN print/read boundary. Non-data values follow one explicit opaque-or-reject rule at every supported depth.

## Scope

Settle and implement one minimal rule for non-data values nested in view-boundary props and event intent. Either project them deterministically to the existing opaque vocabulary or reject them with the existing typed malformed-tree boundary; do not add public API or a second tree format. Keep ordinary EDN values unchanged and share the rule across interpreted/compiled producers where applicable.

## Provenance

Completeness/correctness/implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6697. Existing follow-ups rf2-drpa3.68, rf2-drpa3.69, and rf2-drpa3.70 cover number parity, React prop grammar, and browser routing respectively; none covers nested non-data tree values.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Representative nested functions/foreign values in a boundary prop and in an event vector/options map cannot leave a host object in the structural tree: they follow the newly stated deterministic opaque-or-reject rule.
2. Every accepted representative tree round-trips losslessly through EDN print/read on the JVM, with an equivalent CLJS read-back assertion, and the two hosts agree on the resulting value.
3. Existing top-level opaque-marker behavior and ordinary nested EDN props/events remain unchanged.
4. Spec 004B states the depth and treatment of non-data values unambiguously, with one conformance fixture covering the rule.
5. A mutation or known-bad control proves the round-trip/parity assertion can fail on the pre-fix behavior.
notes: NEXT-WAVE PRIORITY (mayor, 2026-07-23): P1 correctness bug in freshly-merged Freehand core. HELD this tick ONLY because it touches a file (cell.cljc / compiler-check.cljc / tree.cljc) that the in-flight F4+F1+F3 wave (v/sub, presence, errors, mount, test-surface, manifests) is actively editing — dispatching now would collide. Dispatch as top priority the moment those PRs land and the core settles, verifying the exact file surface against the merged tree first. Main is currently GREEN; these are latent correctness gaps, not a red-main emergency, so the one-wave hold is safe.

title: Route Freehand React surfaces into the required browser suite
description:
## Problem

PR #6697's source bead requires a real mounted-browser assertion in the existing Playwright lane, but a Freehand-only change currently arms the JVM and CLJS Node jobs only. The GitHub Actions browser job for #6697 was skipped.

The DOM test is also selected by the Node build but deliberately self-skips when no DOM exists, so a green Node result does not exercise mounting. Consequently a regression in the interpreted React emitter, its DOM test/view, or a browser-applicable FH-STRUCT fixture can merge while all required checks remain green and no real DOM assertion runs.

rf2-drpa3.66 is limited to routing Freehand conformance fixture changes into the JVM and Node suites and explicitly does not widen browser coverage. F6b owns later full browser matrices, not the required gate for this already-shipped F1 emitter.

## Recommendation

Route the existing Freehand React/browser surface and its actual transitive semantic inputs into the existing required browser job. Reuse the existing workflow and Playwright lane; do not create another workflow. Keep classification narrow enough to avoid routing unrelated documentation-only changes, but include shared conversion/fixture changes that can alter mounted output.

## Provenance

Completeness and correctness audit of merged PR #6697.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A PR changing the Freehand React emitter or its mounted-DOM tests schedules the existing browser job, and the required-check aggregator rejects an unexplained skip.
2. A browser-applicable FH-STRUCT fixture or shared conversion change that can affect mounted output also schedules that lane.
3. Deliberately inverting the mounted DOM assertion makes the required CI result red; the Node test's no-DOM self-skip does not count as proof.
4. Changed-surface classifier self-tests pin representative source, browser-test, view, and fixture paths.
5. No new workflow or duplicate browser runner is introduced.
