Dispatch them the moment that lane clears, and prefer them over further capability work — an ergonomics blocker on donor deletion outranks a new capability.
SECOND PILOT REPORT (rf2-drpa3.44, PR #6749) — richer than the first, and it changes what we know about the compiled tier ceiling.

WHAT HELD, and this is real positive evidence rather than absence of failure:
  - Retained-resource count across mount/open/close/unmount MEASURED AT ZERO — no net document or window listeners, zero observers, zero intervals, no rAF arm beyond control. The pilot notes this "deletes re-com whole leak class", which is the substrate beating its predecessor on a category of defect rather than on a feature.
  - Measurement lands BEFORE THE FIRST PAINT with no -10000px park — the trick every hand-rolled overlay library resorts to is unnecessary.
  - All six modal focus points come free from showModal().
  - The debounce needed NO framework primitive: :dispatch-later plus a token comparison beats a cancellable timer, and there is nothing to leak. A missing convenience that turns out not to be needed is worth as much as a shipped one.

THREE FINDINGS FILED:
  rf2-drpa3.126 (P1) — TOGGLE STATE IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE GRAMMAR THE RUNTIME ADVISES. The top-layer runtime dev advisory tells authors to reconcile :on-toggle "with ordinary event intent", but the closed roster is ::v/value/::v/checked/::v/key and v/event at a handler site raises :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed on the JVM. The substrate advises a path its own grammar refuses. The data-only workaround is correct for ONE overlay and UNSOUND for a NESTED PAIR — proven by observing [:outer :inner :outer], more than two toggle reports. Highest-value fix the pilots have found.
  rf2-drpa3.127 (P2) — A COMPILED VIEW CANNOT ATTACH A BEHAVIOR, and because v/defbehavior :timing :layout is the ONLY before-paint home, ANY VIEW THAT MEASURES IS INTERPRETED FOREVER. title: Audit merged PR #6645
description:
Audit merged PR #6645 through three independent lenses under the pre-alpha, ergonomic, no-overengineering posture.

All three lenses found the same material handoff gap. A fresh same-request-id issuance can supersede the old backoff and register its live handle while the old timer callback is paused. The stale retry then unconditionally overwrites that newer handle and clears itself after observing the abort, leaving the new live request undiscoverable by request id. Later abort/supersede cannot reach it and it may deliver an obsolete reply.

The existing abort-only handoff test does not create this ownership interleaving. The rest of the shared cancellation-cell repair is sound.

Action: reopened exact source owner rf2-6nczv9. Smallest fix is an atomic conditional predecessor->successor registry transfer, with one deterministic same-id superseder test. No locks, scheduler changes, public API, or state-machine framework.
close_reason: Audit complete; material retry-handoff ownership finding deduplicated into reopened rf2-6nczv9

title: S0 carrier proof: Shadow disk-cache round-trip of def :meta analyzer descriptors (premise spike for rf2-u53yy.1)
description:
RULED WORK (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-21): the S0 premise spike of the rf2-u53yy.1 install/cache-tax re-architecture. See the DECISION note on rf2-u53yy.1 (2026-07-21) for the full ruling. This bead BLOCKS rf2-u53yy.1 (edge wired): its answer selects the S2 views-carrier design, so it must be dispatched FIRST, before the re-architecture worker starts. Fully self-contained; no operator input required. Hours, not days.

THE QUESTION (exactly one): on a REAL shadow-cljs disk-cache HIT — daemon restarted, sources untouched, the consumer namespace verifiably NOT recompiled — does Shadow restore arbitrary namespaced, EDN-only metadata that macro expansion attached to (a) a def's :meta and (b) the namespace's analyzer data, into [:cljs.analyzer/namespaces] of the build state, as observable by a build hook at compile-finish?

WHY IT MATTERS: rf2-u53yy.1 moves whole-build registry truth (views/elements/roots+plans/descriptors) off macro-expansion side effects into per-namespace descriptors that survive Shadow's disk cache, so the :cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} entry and the exact shadow-cljs 3.4.10 pin can be deleted from every consumer's install contract. The views slice (S2, the hard core) wants the cached analyzer map as the descriptor carrier. This spike proves the carrier exists on a real cache hit.

PRIOR (strong prior of YES — this is a compatibility proof, not an architectural bet): Codex verified against the pinned shadow-cljs-3.4.10.jar that Shadow writes the ENTIRE analyzer namespace map for a compiled namespace into its disk cache (shadow/build/compiler.clj:1017-1090, esp. 1073-1084) and merges the complete map back under [:cljs.analyzer/namespaces] on a hit (:929-1007, esp. 989-997). The spike converts that source-reading into an owned proof on a real build. CAUTION: the probe project must NOT carry the re-frame.ui cache-blocker or the re-frame.ui build hook — cache eligibility is decided by is-cache-blocked? (compiler.clj:918-927); use a plain project so the hit is genuine.

HOW TO PROVE IT:
1. Minimal probe project, real shadow-cljs 3.4.10 (real npm + deps install, NOT synthetic build-state): one macro namespace whose macro emits a def carrying namespaced EDN-only :meta (e.g. :probe.rf2/descriptor with a small map value) and also stamps a namespace-level key into the analyzer data; one consumer namespace using the macro.
2. Attach a minimal probe build hook (compile-finish stage) that records (get-in build-state [:cljs.analyzer/namespaces CONSUMER-NS]) — both the def :meta and the ns-level key.
3. Cold build. Record the hook observation (baseline: metadata present because the namespace actually compiled).
4. Stop the daemon. Restart it. Rebuild WITHOUT touching any source. PROVE the disk-cache hit: the consumer namespace must not recompile (Shadow cache/verbose log, timing, or hook-observed compile membership). A pass that silently recompiles proves nothing — stop and fix the probe until the hit is genuine.
5. Inspect the hook observation on the cache-hit pass: is the stamped metadata present? Record the def-:meta variant and the ns-level variant SEPARATELY — they may differ.
6. If quick, repeat at the highest Shadow version the library intends to support (range endpoint). 3.4.10 is the mandatory minimum; endpoint runs turn the version range into an owned compatibility contract.

ACCEPTANCE: a definitive YES or NO per carrier variant (def :meta; ns-level analyzer data), committed as evidence: the probe project plus a short findings file in-tree (follow the existing probe convention, cf. implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/digest_probe/), the answer appended as a note on THIS bead and echoed as an append-note on rf2-u53yy.1. Consequence mapping (already ruled — do not re-litigate): YES selects the analyzer-map descriptor carrier for S2 (no sidecar files). NO selects plan-B: per-namespace sidecar EDN descriptor files keyed by source digest in a re-frame.ui-owned location, aggregated by the hook — last resort only (sidecars add filesystem lifecycle, invalidation, parallel-build, and cleanup problems Shadow's own cache already solves).

WORKER RULES: run the worker worktree guard from the intended checkout BEFORE any edit — sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh (POSIX) or powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1 (Windows) — and report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT. The worktree path is navigation-only — NEVER committed content. Commit first, then git pull --rebase; NEVER git stash (stash use has contaminated worker branches before). Gates in the FOREGROUND only; this is a probe — run only the probe itself plus anything it touches, NOT the full spine (CI owns the spine). If a genuine verifiable cache hit cannot be produced, STOP-report honestly rather than substituting a synthetic build-state result.
notes:
S0 ANSWER (worker/install-tax-rearch-u53yy1, 2026-07-21): YES for BOTH carrier variants, on a PROVEN real disk-cache HIT, across a tested Shadow version range.

EVIDENCE (committed in-tree at implementation/ui/cache-carrier-probe/ — a STANDALONE plain project, NOT on the main source-paths, carrying neither :cache-blockers nor the re-frame.ui hook so the hit is genuine; run via 'node run.cjs'):
- Mechanism: two independent one-shot 'shadow-cljs compile' runs, each a FRESH JVM (no persistent server), sharing ONLY the on-disk cache. A compile-time WITNESS file records every macro expansion. Pass 1 (cold): 45 nss compiled, 2 witness lines, both carriers present (baseline). Pass 2 (no source byte touched): Shadow reports 0 nss compiled and the witness does NOT grow — the macro did not re-run — yet both carriers are STILL present in the restored analyzer data. So they were RESTORED FROM DISK, not re-stamped. The compile-finish hook decides variant presence by EXACT EDN equality (not a presence check), so a truncated/key-stripped round-trip would fail.
- Variant A (def :meta; mirrors emit_cljs.cljc:1027 vary-meta): survives with exact EDN equality (nested maps/sets/vectors intact). YES.
- Variant B (ns-level analyzer key; mirrors emit_cljs.cljc:1004-1007 swap! cljs.env/*compiler*): the arbitrary namespaced key on the ns analyzer map ALSO survives with exact equality — CLJS does NOT strip it. YES.
- Version matrix (each: cache-hit proven + variant-a=YES + variant-b=YES): shadow-cljs 3.4.0, 3.4.10 (pinned min), 3.4.11 (latest). Not fragile to the exact patch — this is the evidence behind the parent acceptance's 'tested range, not one exact pin'.

KEY FACT for S2: the analyzer namespaces live at [:compiler-env :cljs.analyzer/namespaces <ns>] in the build state (NOT build-state top level — the bead's [:cljs.analyzer/namespaces ...] was shorthand). The hook reads them there at compile-finish.

CONSEQUENCE (per the ruling's consequence map, not re-litigated): YES selects the analyzer-map descriptor carrier for S2. NO sidecar files. Plan-B (per-namespace sidecar EDN) is not pursued.
PR #6638 CHRONOLOGICAL THREE-LENS AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-21) — reopen this exact probe owner for one tiny fail-closed guard; the YES/YES carrier conclusion remains valid.

The warm carrier observation is not mechanically proven fresh. run.cjs clears target only before pass 1, leaves cold summary.edn in place, then reads that same path after pass 2. If compile-finish unexpectedly failed to write on a zero-compile cache hit, readSummary would reuse the cold YES/YES while witness-flat + compiled=0 still pass. That contradicts the probe's "cannot be fooled" claim at the exact compatibility seam it exists to prove.

Smallest repair: delete summary.edn (and the human observation file) immediately before the warm compile, then require the hook to recreate the summary before accepting A/B. Rerun the already claimed 3.4.0 / 3.4.10 / 3.4.11 cases. No nonce protocol, concurrency lock, CI framework, or new harness.

RESULT STATUS: multiple exclusive pinned-3.4.10 runs independently produced cold 45 compiled / witness 2 / A+B true, then warm 0 / witness 2->2 / A+B true; Shadow source also stores and restores the complete analyzer namespace map. The architecture decision therefore stands. Concurrent reviewers briefly produced impossible counts by running this destructive manual probe against the same shared output directory; that is an audit artifact, not a product requirement, and no concurrency machinery is warranted.

PROVENANCE/DEDUP: authored 18714e8 and applied merge e9768f1 have stable patch d6a206af; no later commit touched the probe. CI broad green; the probe is manual. All-state search found no other exact owner; the open parent rf2-u53yy.1 consumes the result but should not absorb this one-line proof-harness repair.

title: EPIC: excise lease completely from re-frame2
description:
## Problem

Mike ruled on 2026-07-20 that the lease idea was a mistake and must be removed completely, not deprecated or preserved as a convenience. The repository-wide tracked inventory currently finds the concept or terminology in 3,582 lines across 309 files, spanning re-frame.ui, all React-shaped adapters, the observation port, Resources ownership, specs, EPs, docs, examples, skills, AI findings, conformance fixtures, Xray, Pair, Story, and tests.

A narrow deletion of re-frame.ui/lease would leave the same idea, vocabulary, public hooks, generated evidence, and AI guidance in many corners. That is explicitly unacceptable.

## Decision

- Delete every component/view-lifetime lease API and its runtime/compiler/tool machinery. Add no replacement helper, deprecation alias, compatibility shim, or retired-name error.
- Preserve valid resource management through explicit causal owners: routes, machines, SSR requests, and semantic app events. Preserve owner-driven GC, polling, cancellation, and release; remove the generic [:lease ...] owner kind and all lease terminology.
- Preserve the observation port's commit-time ref-count semantics, but rename its returned object and grammar to a neutral observation handle. This is a vocabulary/API cleanup, not a redesign.
- Remove the concept from all current and historical tracked authoring material, including specs, EPs, docs, examples, migrations, skills, evals, tools, and AI findings. Do not leave a supersession paragraph that continues teaching the rejected construct.
- Finish with an executable zero-residue guard over tracked product and authoring paths. The Beads database and Git history are the only exemptions because they are immutable/audit history and this removal program itself must name the decision.

## Staged delivery

1. Delete the public view-lifetime surfaces and their implementation/tool consumers.
2. Normalize surviving internals: observation handles and causal resource owners.
3. Purge all specification, documentation, example, skill, AI, and tool guidance residue.
4. Land a zero-baseline repository ratchet and integration proof.

Stages may use stacked PRs, but each merged PR must keep every public surface it touches truthful. No docs/code mismatch and no temporary compatibility layer.

## Acceptance

- No tracked product or authoring filename/content outside .beads contains the retired lexical concept in prose, identifiers, keywords, test names, fixture ids, schemas, manifests, or generated surfaces.
- re-frame.ui/lease, with-resource-lease, use-resource-lease, [:lease ...], ObservationLease, and every equivalent helper/descriptor/error/tool field are absent.
- Resource loading and lifecycle management continue through causal owners without component-presence ownership.
- The zero-residue check is part of normal CI and is proven capable of failing on prose, kebab/snake identifiers, camel-case identifiers, and filenames.
- Relevant UI, adapter, core, Resources, conformance, Xray, Pair, Story, docs, and skill gates pass with non-vacuous test selection.
acceptance_criteria: The rejected lease construct and lexical residue are absent from every tracked product/authoring surface outside .beads; causal resource ownership and observation handling remain correct; a zero-baseline CI ratchet prevents reintroduction.
notes:
STRUCTURE REVIEW ADDENDUM (2026-07-20, mayor):

Inventory verified against the tracked tree with the precise residue pattern `\b[Ll]eas(e|es|ed|ing)\b|Lease` (word-boundary — matches lease/leases/leased/leasing + camel Lease; does NOT match release/please). Census: ~307 files / ~3.4k lines, consistent with the description's 3,582/309 snapshot (drift = rf2-y4mgw + #6570 landing since). Naive substring 'lease' inflates to 744 files via release/please — S4's guard discrimination requirement is load-bearing, keep it.

Dispatch topology + hot-zone fences (per CLAUDE.md sequential-hot-file rule):
- S1 solo first (touches hot-zone spec/API.md, spec/004-Views.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn).
- S2A ∥ S2B is parallel-safe ONLY under the file fence recorded on each: S2A owns spec/006 + spec/009 (observation row) + spec/002-Frames; S2B owns spec/Conventions + spec/005 + 012/014/016 + conformance fixtures. Disjoint hot files.
- S3A ∥ S3B parallel-safe (docs/spec/examples vs ai/skills/tools — disjoint trees).
- S4 solo last, against the final merged tree.

title: IMPL: render-static RULED MACRO (delegated ruling 2026-07-20, see NOTES) — implement macro + facade-guard S5 bucket + API.md delta #6 (BLOCKS S6 entry token .97.3)
description: ⚠️ NEEDS A MIKE RULING — BLOCKS S6. The S5 conformance gate rf2-vxgfnd.97.3 (#6511) is RED BY DESIGN (fail-closed, JVM ui gate) because it caught a REAL GAP: re-frame.ui/render-static is a BLESSED S5 public name in the spec/API.md re-frame.ui surface freeze but has NO implementation anywhere in implementation/ (0 def/defmacro/defn matches — VERIFIED by mayor via ripgrep; only docstring/comment mentions in runtime.cljs + compiler/root.cljc). This is EXACTLY the names-without-implementations false-surface failure the gate's MERGE PRECONDITION exists to catch — the gate is working correctly and MUST NOT merge/--admin until render-static ships (its merge = the S6 entry token). ⚠️ THE DECISION (Mike's — a genuine API-shape/design call the gate can't make): render-static fn vs macro? spec/API.md §2+§2b freeze labels it a **fn**, BUT spec/004C §3 requires the LITERAL ROOT FORM at the call site (rejecting runtime-assembled vectors, the way mount/render!/hydrate-root's macros do) — which a **fn CANNOT enforce** (a fn receives an already-evaluated vector; only a macro sees the literal form). The other root entry points are macros. So: (a) rule render-static a MACRO (enforces literal-root like siblings, but contradicts the API.md fn label → API freeze row delta) — OR (b) keep it a fn and relax/re-rule the 004C §3 literal-root requirement for render-static (static render may not need literal-root enforcement?) — OR (c) something else. THEN IMPLEMENT: once ruled, a worker implements render-static (server-side static render, no manifest/no flip per spec/011 — render-static is pure :server phase, the non-hydrating static-page path) + fixtures + teaches the S4 facade exact-set guard an S5 bucket (adding render-static to the facade reds the S3/S4 facade-surface-is-exactly-the-catalogue guards — needs an S5 partition slot). THEN .97.3 greens + merges → S6 opens. SEQUENCE: Mike rules fn/macro → implement render-static + facade-guard S5 bucket → .97.3 greens → merge = S6 token. Cross-ref rf2-vxgfnd.97.3 (#6511, red-by-design), spec/API.md freeze, spec/004C §3, spec/011 (render-static = pure :server, no flip).
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 08:34 AUSEST) RULED: `re-frame.ui/render-static` is a MACRO. The 004C §3 verb-kind rule governs: it accepts a root form, so it must see the literal form at compile time. The `fn` labels in spec/API.md §2 (~line 304) and §2b (~line 371) are stale freeze cells written before the S1 verb-kind ratification — correct BOTH cells as row-level freeze DELTA #6 (deltas #1-#5 are the precedent), and add `render-static` to 004C §3's ratified macro roster (one line). Followed the dossier's Recommendation + the Codex second opinion + the S6-pause independent research, which all converged on macro, because a form-taking fn is impossible in principle in a substrate that ships no runtime hiccup interpreter (the evaluated vector `[#function ...]` is not a renderable value here) while the macro keeps 004C §3 literal-root-everywhere and §7 Layer-1 site indexing true as shipped. SHAPE: signature stays `(ui/render-static root-form)` -> HTML string. Same compile error as `mount` rejects runtime-assembled vectors. Transitive static proof runs at expansion: any runtime-requiring capability in the root's server-reachable view closure (subs, handlers, effects, refs, context, foreign heads, `lazy`) is a loud BUILD error with source coordinates — no silent elision, per EP-0034 §2. `use-id` stays exempt; `ui/client-only` stays legal (analyze only its capability-free fallback — that is the branch the JVM emitter emits; a static root never flips). The site registers into the existing `register-root-site!` Layer-1 duplicate-root-id build index. Pure `:server` output per spec/011 — no manifest, no payload, no flip. HOME + HOST STORY: lives on the ui artefact as `re-frame.ui/render-static` (needs the compiler; the Independence rule forbids `re-frame.ssr` from requiring it). CLJ(JVM)-host expansion ONLY; CLJS expansion fails loud with the mirror of `:rf.ui.compile/client-entry-on-jvm`. The runtime half renders the JVM realisation (client-only fallbacks via the shipped `tree.cljc/client-only-fallback` / `emit_jvm.cljc` path) and folds the tree through `re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree` resolved LATE (the `hydrate-root` late-require precedent, `client.cljs` ~1389-1398) — ui takes no hard artefact dep on ssr; a missing `day8/re-frame2-ssr` on the server classpath is a loud typed error naming the artefact, never a fallback. No Node arm, no opts map, no runtime interpreter, no compat alias, no second serializer. IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTION (Codex-verified against source, load-bearing for sizing): the transitive capability proof is NOT already in hand. `compiler.cljc` records each defview's LOCAL `:capabilities` (line ~276) and site collections; no direct-view dependency graph or capability closure exists. The worker must add one small internal projection of direct compiled-view dependencies (or an equivalent build-registry row) plus a cycle-safe closure over it. Required correctness, not new public framework. A test MUST prove a static root fails when only a NESTED view requires runtime capability — checking the root view alone would silently ship inert UI. The compile-time proof error rides the existing `:rf.ui.compile/*` family (suggested: `:rf.ui.compile/static-root-requires-runtime`) — do NOT mint a runtime `:rf.error/*` id, which would drag in a spec/009 catalogue row (hot-zone). HOW THE GATE GREENS: rf2-vxgfnd.97.3 (PR #6511) is red by design — its fail-closed merge precondition refuses S5 certification while a blessed name has no implementation site. It clears itself once `render-static` ships as a real facade var. Do NOT `--admin` merge #6511. Same PR as the implementation: teach the S4 facade exact-set guard (`s4_conformance_profile_jvm_test.clj`, `s1-s2-carryover-publics` partition) an S5 bucket so the new facade var classifies instead of redding the S3/S4 facade-surface guards; land fixtures per #6511's profile row (explicit static-root-policy + no-silent-elision, EP-0034 §2 SSR). Compact proof set: one exact-HTML success with runtime props + a client-only fallback; one runtime-assembled-form compile failure; one transitive (nested-view) capability failure; one typed missing-SSR-artifact case; facade/kind classification for the cumulative gate. title: Make special-element SSR honor ui/html and one coherent child contract
description:
PR #6477 added a `<script>`/`<style>` fast path in `re-frame.ssr.ui-tree/emit-element`, but the branch calls `(str/join (:children el))` instead of consuming the structural-tree child grammar. That silently breaks a NORMAL compiled-view form: `ui/html` is the explicit trusted-markup primitive, accepted as a sole DOM child; the CLJS emitter lowers it to React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, while the JVM emitter records `{:html s}`. `emit-ui-tree` now stringifies that map:

  {:tag :script :children [{:html "const x=1;"}]}
  -> <script>{:html "const x=1;"}</script>

The same happens for `<style>`, corrupting executable/style content and guaranteeing dual-emitter/hydration divergence. The fast path also bypasses the closed structural-tree validator, so an arbitrary malformed map under script/style becomes plausible EDN text rather than the existing typed malformed-tree error.

The sibling leading-LF fix has the same structural-child blind spot for React's trusted-markup path: React adds a compensating LF when `dangerouslySetInnerHTML.__html` begins with LF under `<pre>`/`<listing>`, but `leading-newline-compensation` only recognizes a direct string. A valid sole `{:html "\n…"}` child therefore emits one LF, which the HTML parser consumes.

Fix this as ONE small special-element child-contract correction, not a serializer framework. Decode the canonical sole trusted-HTML child deliberately; do not stringify structural nodes. Script/style `ui/html` must emit the trusted body with the same semantics as the CLJS/React path; pre/listing trusted HTML must receive React's leading-LF compensation. Invalid child shapes must use the existing malformed-tree/compiler diagnostics.

CONTRACT RECONCILIATION (same bounded work): current Spec 004B and this branch say ordinary script/style string content follows React raw-text semantics, while Spec 011/Security and the older hiccup `render-to-string` path still say body raw text fails loud. Two SSR dialects for the same view shape are poor ergonomics. Under the project posture (trust the programmer, minimal friction, React-aligned compiled substrate), recommend one rule: ordinary script/style text follows React's closing-sequence-safe raw-text behavior in both SSR paths; `ui/html` remains the explicit verbatim trust bypass; malformed/non-text structural children fail loud. Reconcile the prose and legacy emitter in this same focused change if that recommendation is accepted. Do not add sanitization, policy configuration, compatibility machinery, or a general checker.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real compiled-view/JVM-tree `ui/html` sole child under `<script>` and `<style>` serializes to its trusted body, not the printed `{:html ...}` map, with dual-emitter exact-output tests.
- A sole trusted-HTML child beginning with LF under `<pre>`/`<listing>` gets React's one compensating LF; exact-byte tests cover it.
- Script/style fast paths no longer stringify arbitrary structural children; invalid shapes fail through the existing compile-time or `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` path with location evidence.
- Spec 004B states the leading-LF rule, including the trusted-HTML case.
- Ordinary script/style string semantics are stated consistently across Spec 004B, Spec 011/Security, `emit-ui-tree`, and the legacy SSR emitter; recommended resolution is React-aligned raw text with the existing context-safe closing-sequence rewrite.
- No new public options, sanitization layer, compatibility mechanism, or generalized serializer/checker.
notes:

title: Keep deferred trace batches ahead of later listener-authored traces
description:
PR #6452's post-drain flush preserves FIFO only among the deferred items it has already inserted into a fan-out schedule. `drain-deferred-batch!` takes the captured pending vector but appends and drives one item at a time (both when integrating into an active `*fanout-ctx*` and when opening fresh outermost fan-outs). While driving the first deferred event, a listener can synchronously `trace/emit!`; that later trace is appended to the current schedule and delivered before the flush loop has inserted the older deferred events still sitting in `batch`.

A deterministic current-main public-API reproduction dispatches one event and has a `:rf.event/run-start` listener emit `:audit/listener-nested`. A second listener observed `[[:rf.event/run-start 10] [:audit/listener-nested 15] [:rf.event/run-end 14]]`: trace #15 overtook already-emitted #14. The focused temporary test failed 1/1 exactly on monotonically increasing delivery IDs and was removed byte-identical. This violates Spec 009 and the public trace-listener law that each listener sees events in runtime emission order; ring/ID emission order remains correct, so stateful tooling can now receive a different order from the authoritative IDs.

Repair the existing private seam narrowly: enqueue the whole captured deferred batch, with each append-time listener snapshot and continuation wrapper, into the active or fresh fan-out context before driving any callback. Then a listener-authored later emit appends behind every older deferred item while the existing resumable driver still preserves outer-before-inner delivery and synchronous nested completion. Do not add a scheduler, async queue, public synchronization surface, or event-shape inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- A causal JVM test reproduces the exact current failure: run-start and run-end are emitted/captured before the run-start listener emits a new trace; every observer sees monotonically increasing trace IDs and specifically run-start, run-end, then the listener-authored trace.
- The same ordering is pinned for a top-level post-drain flush and for a listener-initiated dispatch-sync whose batch integrates into an already-active fan-out context.
- The entire captured batch is scheduled before any of its callbacks run; per-event append-time listener snapshots and deferred continuation wrappers remain intact.
- Existing outer-before-inner ordering, nested emit/dispatch synchronous completion, continuation suppression, registration replacement, listener exception isolation, two-drain JVM serialization, and CLJS settled-state behavior remain green.
- Production elision and bundle isolation remain unchanged.
- The repair stays inside the private fan-out/deferral driver; no scheduler, async delivery, public API, classifier, or compatibility mode.
notes: Fixed in PR #6474 (worker/trace-fifo-t6vs3). Root cause: drain-deferred-batch! appended+drove ONE deferred item at a time, so a listener-authored trace emitted while the first item was being fanned out overtook the still-pending later items. Fix: queue the WHOLE captured batch onto ONE fan-out schedule before driving (integrate: into the active *fanout-ctx*; outermost: one fresh schedule for the batch). Unified the two outermost helpers into run-outermost-fanout! taking a batch, retiring the dead per-event entries arity. Within the existing private seam — no scheduler/API/classifier/platform-split; no Spec 009 change; no new error id. Red-before on both hosts (JVM+CLJS) via new dual-host suite trace_listener_deferred_batch_fifo_cljs_test.cljc; green after. Gates: core 2095t/10326a, machines 1195t/4164a, test:cljs 10288t/50738a all 0-fail; bundle-isolation + elision PASS.

title: Reentrant fanout bypasses post-drain deferral for listener-initiated dispatch-sync
description:
## Defect

PR #6365's post-drain deferral is bypassed for the most important reentrant path: a trace listener that calls `dispatch-sync`.

`re-frame.trace.tooling/deliver-to-tooling!` tests `*fanout-ctx*` before the new `deferred-drain-fanout` ThreadLocal. During an outer listener fanout, `*fanout-ctx*` is already bound. If that listener calls `dispatch-sync` into frame F, `drain-block!` correctly opens the ThreadLocal deferral scope and acquires F's `:drain-lock`; but each nested drain trace still takes the earlier `*fanout-ctx*` branch, appends to the existing schedule, and immediately calls `drive-fanout!`. Arbitrary listeners are therefore invoked while F's drain lock is held. The ThreadLocal never gets a chance to defer them.

## Deterministic proof

The existing `re-frame.trace-listener-drain-deadlock-test` already drives this exact listener -> `dispatch-sync` path. A temporary audit assertion recorded whether any `:rf.event/run-start` callback observed `@(:drain-lock (frame/frame :rf/default))` true. It failed on every iteration: 25/25 failures (`Ran 1 test containing 100 assertions`), each with `[:rf.event/run-start]` delivered under the held lock. The diagnostic was removed byte-identical after the run.

## Consequence

This directly violates #6365/rf2-wxy1c's load-bearing acceptance rule that listener code is never invoked or awaited while any target frame drain lock is held. It also leaves the AB-BA class reachable: the listener-initiated nested drain can run another listener while holding both the fanout monitor and F's lock; that listener may `dispatch-sync` into G while G's drainer has released/needs to flush through the same monitor, recreating monitor -> G-lock versus G-lock -> monitor. Even without that second frame, programmer/tool callback code still runs inside the protected drain region.

## Bounded repair

Make a live post-drain deferral scope take precedence over the reentrant fanout fast path. When the nested drain releases its lock, integrate its deferred events with the already-active fanout schedule so outer-before-inner ordering, synchronous nested completion, captured listener snapshots, and continuation suppression remain intact. Keep this inside the existing private fanout/deferral seam; no public lock API, event-shape classifier, general scheduler, or listener restriction is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- The deterministic listener -> `dispatch-sync` fixture records zero trace-listener callbacks while the nested target frame's `:drain-lock` is held, over repeated iterations.
- A bounded two-frame/monitor interleaving proves the remaining reentrant path cannot close a fanout-monitor/drain-lock AB-BA cycle and every event settles exactly once.
- Deferred nested events preserve each event's append-time listener snapshot and continuation semantics.
- Existing same-thread outer-before-inner ordering and nested emit/dispatch synchronous completion remain executable-pinned.
- Clean emits, two independent drains, public frame-tagged emits, listener exceptions, registration replacement, routing dispatch envelopes, CLJS behavior, and production/bundle elision remain green with non-zero focused counts.
- The fix stays within the existing private fanout/deferral seam; no public synchronization surface or general scheduler is introduced.

title: Story's Xray embed is an undeclared hard dependency, so the promised no-Xray shell cannot compile
description:
## Problem

PR #6418 makes Story's rationale claim graceful operation when Xray is absent: Story "never takes a hard dependency on Xray", renders an explicit unavailable placeholder, and gates popout on `xray-available?`. The shipped artifact cannot reach that state.

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs` directly requires `re-frame.story.ui.xray-embed`. That namespace directly requires `day8.re-frame2-xray.mount` and `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels`; `re-frame.story.xray-preset` directly requires the mount namespace too. But `tools/story/deps.edn` declares no `day8/re-frame2-xray` dependency. The repository-wide Shadow build masks the omission by putting `../tools/xray/src` on its global source paths.

A dependency-honest reproduction from `tools/story` proves the user path: its own `clojure -Spath` contains zero `tools/xray/src` entries. Compiling `re-frame.story.ui.shell` with the repository node_modules supplied gets past React resolution and then exits 1:

`No such namespace: day8.re-frame2-xray.mount ... in re_frame/story/xray_preset.cljc`.

So a fresh application that adds Story alone cannot compile the Story shell; it never renders the promised placeholder. `xray-available?` is also vacuous in the repository build: it is `(some? xray-mount/open!)` after a direct require, so successful compilation already guarantees the symbol.

## Smallest ergonomic correction

Make the package graph and public story agree. Preferred: treat Xray as the bundled diagnostic engine Story's shipped shell already unconditionally composes—declare the lockstep Xray dependency, remove the impossible absence branch/feature test, and teach one-coordinate Story installation honestly. This matches the actual six-panel + event-spine product and avoids inventing optional-plugin machinery.

If artifact independence is deliberately retained instead, restore a genuinely optional seam: Story must compile and render without any Xray namespace on the classpath, and Xray may register the mount surface when present. Do not use another runtime namespace-property walk (the source records that shape as unreliable), and do not build a general plugin framework.

Either resolution must fix #6418's new rationale plus the older active Story authorities that still promise optional activation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh consumer whose only tool dependency is `day8/re-frame2-story` can compile and mount the Story shell from the published dependency graph; no repository-global Shadow source path may supply an undeclared namespace.
- The contract is one honest shape: either Xray is a declared lockstep Story dependency and the impossible absence branch/prose is removed, or Story has no compile-time Xray require and a real no-Xray build renders the explicit unavailable state.
- Add a dependency-honest compile fixture using `tools/story/deps.edn` (or an emitted consumer), with a control that would fail if `tools/xray/src` leaks onto the classpath.
- If Xray becomes declared, release rewriting/order and the published Story manifest carry its matching version; one-coordinate Story setup is documented.
- Reconcile `tools/story/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md`, `005-SOTA-Features.md`, `003-Render-Shell.md`, and source docstrings/comments to the chosen truth.
- No general plugin system, compatibility shim, or namespace-reflection workaround is introduced.

title: Fence Promise-backed Story presence settlement with the run token
description:
PR #6367 added Promise-backed `[:flush-presence]` settlement to Story's run loop, but the settlement callback mutates shared run state before re-entering the existing run-token fence.

In `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc`, `run-loop!` checks that the `[frame-id play-key]` state exists and its `:run-token` still matches before any ordinary step mutates it. That is the documented protection for a newer concurrent `run!` taking over the same state slot and for frame teardown. The new `::pending-advance` branch instead calls `settle-step-result!`; when the host Promise settles, its callback calls `record-result!` immediately, then schedules `run-loop!`. The token check therefore comes after the mutation.

Concrete failure: run A reaches a deferred presence Promise; run B starts for the same frame/play and replaces the slot; settling A records A's result into B's state, advancing/skipping B's current step and contaminating its verdict. If the frame/state was removed while A was pending, `record-result!` can attempt to update nil inside the Promise callback, producing the unhandled-rejection class #6367 was intended to eliminate. Ordinary async paths are safe because they re-enter `run-loop!` with the token before recording.

Keep the repair at this ownership boundary: do not add a general async scheduler or cancellation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Before recording a settled Promise-backed presence result, the callback verifies that the state still exists and carries the same run token.
- A stale run settles its own completion path without mutating the replacement run, consistent with `settle-abort!`.
- Teardown while the Promise is pending does not throw or emit an unhandled rejection.
- Deterministic deferred-thenable tests prove: start A pending, start B, settle A, and B's step index/results/verdict remain unchanged; tear down while pending; ordinary resolve and reject still produce their intended pass/fail results.
- The interactive stepper's reset/new-cursor path receives the equivalent stale-settlement protection if it shares this vulnerability; no broad async abstraction is introduced.
notes:
PR #6405 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6405) — branch worker/story-run-token-6pfpt.

Fix: extracted the slot-ownership test to `stale-run?` (one definition, consulted by both run-loop! and the settled-Promise callback). The callback now checks it BEFORE record-result! and re-enters run-loop! unconditionally, so a stale settlement reaches the SAME settle-abort! every other stale exit uses rather than a second copy of that decision. Execution order is NOT pinned.

Mechanism: value fence, not a dynamic Var / ThreadLocal. The token is already conveyed correctly (argument through run-loop!, captured by the closure); the hazard is a run outliving its claim, so the check must compare the captured claim against the LIVE slot — something a conveyed mechanism cannot do (it would agree with the callback by construction). Check + mutation are one synchronous turn.

Stepper (acceptance criterion 5): it DID share the vulnerability. The bounds guard (idx < count results) is a size test, not an identity test — it declines while a reset has shortened :results, then permits the clobber once a new cursor grows back past idx. Now fenced on the provisional record's object identity (identical?, not =). Identity over a generation counter because session identity is mutated at five sites (begin-stepper!/step-back!/rewind!/end-stepper!/clear-all-play-state!) and because a session-level generation would WRONGLY refuse an amendment still owed for an earlier index across stepper-step-back! — pinned by a dedicated test.

Extra finding beyond the bead description: under teardown the unfenced callback does not throw on CLJS ((inc nil) is 1) — it RESURRECTS a phantom run-state entry carrying no :run-token, which the loop's token guard declines to abort on (it only fires when a token is present), so the resurrected run reached a finish! verdict of :status :pass for a frame that was gone. A fabricated green, not just a hang.

Measurement (deterministic thenable, settlement placed by the test): 10 trials with fix reverted = 10/10 RED, 11 failures each, identical failure set. 10 trials with fix = 10/10 GREEN. Fence state proved as a SEQUENCE (admit -> refuse -> admit -> refuse) for both fences, not just as cases.

Gates: tools/story clojure -M:test = 1836 tests / 6792 assertions, 0 failures. npm run test:cljs = 10140 tests / 50071 assertions, 0 failures. Vacuity-probed the CLJS gate (flipped an assertion -> full gate went red naming the probe -> restored), since the runner prints no per-ns headers. check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh OK. test:browser not run — no mounted behaviour involved.

Same shape elsewhere, NAMED not fixed: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs (run-axe!) + chrome_a11y.cljs mutate run-state / violations-by-frame inside .then callbacks with no frame-existence or supersession check. Also runner-events/run-step!'s settle callback emits an unfenced emit-trace! for an abandoned stepper session — left deliberately (public late-bound one-shot executor with no session identity; the recorded verdict IS fenced caller-side).

title: Close the post-selection registrar race for prepared spawn-all children
description:
PR #6298 fixes a prepared spawn-all child whose machine type diverges between preflight and install by selecting a pinned prepared definition when the registrar has changed. The selection is still too early.

In spawn-fx*, type-ref is computed by prepared-type-ref in the let binding, before the callback-bearing :rf.machine.spawn/spawned trace is emitted and before install-spawn! emits a callback-bearing :rf.error/system-id-collision trace. Both callbacks run synchronously before the snapshot write. A listener can therefore unregister or replace the admitted type after prepared-type-ref observed the original spec and returned the machine-id keyword. install-spawn! then stamps that now-stale keyword into :rf/machine-type; the synthetic bootstrap lazy-resolves nothing or an unrelated v2 definition, recreating the inert/split-authority actor #6298 was meant to eliminate.

The current tests mutate the registrar from :rf.machine.spawn-all/started, which runs before type-ref is selected, so they do not cover either later pre-install callback seam.

Defer the prepared-reference choice to the last safe point after callback-bearing pre-install emissions (including the collision trace), or otherwise ensure the installed snapshot uses the prepared definition whenever the registrar diverged at commit. Keep the existing simple definition-lifetime policy and do not add a registry transaction/coordinator. Add JVM+CLJS regressions where a :rf.machine.spawn/spawned listener unregisters and re-registers the child type (and, if applicable, the system-id collision listener does the same), asserting bootstrap and a later event use one coherent prepared definition.

title: Replace Shadow's timestamp-derived compile set with a causal fact
description:
PR #6270 treats Shadow 3.4.10's `[:shadow.build/build-info :compiled]` as an independent causal compile record and uses it to distinguish a genuine compiler-created markerless output from a non-scheduling whole-map replacement. In the pinned Shadow source, however, that set is computed by `shadow.build/resources-compiled-recently`: a resource is included only when `(not cached)` and `compiled-at > compile-start`. It is the same wall-clock ordering authority rf2-ialoij was meant to eliminate.

Exact pinned-library probe:
- compiled-at 1000 / compile-start 1000 -> `[]`
- compiled-at 999 / compile-start 1000 -> `[]`
- compiled-at 1001 / compile-start 1000 -> `[:app]`

For a genuine equal/backwards-stamp recompile, Shadow replaces the output map (dropping re-frame.ui's marker) but omits the resource from `:build-info/:compiled`. `compile-verdict` therefore sees marker absent + not compiled + `:cached false` and throws `:marker-dropped-without-compile` instead of classifying the real compile and evicting a removed final view. This directly violates rf2-8nn5k's equal/backwards-recompile AC and the PR's claim that such recompiles are still evicted.

The JVM tests manufacture `:build-info/:compiled` directly from their `scheduled` argument, even in the equal/backwards-stamp fixtures, so they assume the disputed fact rather than deriving it the way pinned Shadow does. The real-Shadow gate exercises ordinary forward-time compilation and cannot force the collision.

Use one actually causal per-pass compile membership fact, or explicitly revise the product contract to fail loud on the indistinguishable clock-collision/replacement state. Do not call a timestamp-derived set causal, reintroduce output identity, trust the output map's self-asserted `:cached false`, or add a general build provenance service. Prefer a small enforceable hook-order/compile instrumentation seam; keep accepted state last-known-good on ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria:
- A genuine compile is classified as compiled when Shadow's compiled-at equals or precedes compile-start; a zero-declaration recompile evicts its accepted row in sequential and parallel modes.
- A non-scheduling whole-output-map replacement with the same visible fields still cannot masquerade as compilation.
- Focused proof derives the corroborating fact through pinned Shadow's real computation (or the replacement causal seam), rather than manually inserting the expected resource id.
- Warm hits, disk-cache loads, marker-preserving transforms, normal recompiles, and fail-before-publication behavior remain correct.
- Comments and public claims identify the true authority; no output identity, wall-clock fallback, public token, compatibility branch, or generalized provenance framework.

title: ui/html is silently DROPPED by the CLJS emitter when the element also has a ui/spread props form
description:
Found while writing the S4-D trusted-markup guidance (rf2-yjhrt). NOT fixed there — the ui compiler was out of that bead's fence.

REPRO (verified by direct analyzer+emitter probe on this worktree, origin/main @ e71976a8b3):

  [:div (ui/spread base ovr) (ui/html s)]

- The analyzer ACCEPTS it: the AST carries :html.
- CLJS emitter: emit-element's :spread branch builds props via runtime/spread->props + jsx-spread2 and NEVER calls element-prop-pairs — which is the only place the html node becomes dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Emitted output contains no __html and an EMPTY children array. The trusted markup is SILENTLY DISCARDED.
- JVM emitter: KEEPS it — child-forms is computed before the branch, so the tree carries (re-frame.ui.tree/html s).

So the same source renders markup on the JVM and nothing in the browser.

WHY IT MATTERS: Spec 004 §Interop states of ui/html that 'both emitters treat it identically', and 004B pins trusted-HTML as a dual-emitter-identical opaque leaf. This is a silent dual-emitter divergence with no diagnostic. It is FAIL-SAFE from a security standpoint (dropping markup cannot inject) but it is silent data loss, and it falsifies a normative sentence.

NO TEST COVERS THIS COMBINATION today (confirmed by grep across implementation/ui/test).

RULING NEEDED (operator): the fix is either
 (a) make the :spread branch carry the html node (emit dangerouslySetInnerHTML through the spread props path), making the emitters agree; or
 (b) reject the combination at compile time (a new :rf.ui.compile/* roster id) if spread + trusted markup on one element is not a shape we want to support.
(a) preserves the spec sentence; (b) is the smaller surface and is defensible pre-alpha, but needs a roster id + error_roster_cljs_test row.

Surface: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc (emit-element :spread branch, ~line 341-415; element-prop-pairs html-p at 272-276); possibly analyze.cljc if (b). Add a dual-emitter regression either way.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:06 AUSEST)

RULING — option (a): ui/spread and ui/html COMPOSE. A DOM element may use (ui/spread base overrides) in props position with (ui/html s) as its sole child, and BOTH emitters must preserve the trusted markup. Option (b) is REJECTED — do NOT add a rejection rule, roster id, or error_roster_cljs_test row, and do not broaden this fix into general spread-policy hardening.

RATIONALE: The analyzer (stores :props {:spread ...} and :html on one element node with no cross-check), the manifest, the JVM emitter, the ui/spread-safe sibling branch (which already composes with ui/html correctly today), and both normative specs (004 §Interop "both emitters treat it identically"; 004B dual-emitter-identical opaque raw-markup leaf) all model the two features as orthogonal. The general-spread CLJS branch is the lone dissenter — this is a narrow emitter omission, not a grammar question. Rejecting would make ui/spread and ui/spread-safe differ on a dimension unrelated to their real distinction (the owned-key deny law). No security angle: the visible (ui/html ...) call is the trust assertion; dynamic attrs neither strengthen nor weaken it. JSX precedent: <div {...props} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: s}} /> is legal and the explicit attribute wins. Codex dossier and an independent Fable verification at HEAD efadbc46c2 both recommended (a); all load-bearing claims re-verified by spot-check at decision time.

IMPLEMENTATION (single seam, no hot-zone files): implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc, emit-element, the (get-in node [:props :spread]) branch (~lines 347-364). When (:html node) is present, attach the compiler-owned dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop — (cljs.core/js-obj "__html" <(:form (:html node))>) — to the runtime-built spread props object AFTER runtime/spread->props returns (so the explicit ui/html site wins any collision with a runtime-smuggled key), then invoke the jsx call. Cover BOTH variants: jsx-spread3 (keyed) and jsx-spread2 (keyless). Pinned semantics: (1) base and overrides evaluate once each, in authored order; (2) the ui/html expression evaluates once, AFTER the spread expressions — matches source order and the JVM path; use single-evaluation let temporaries as the adjacent :safe-spread branch does (see its rf2-m5h0f evaluation-order comment); (3) no React children entry for the html node — the analyzer already sets :children [] for an html-kid, so React's children-vs-innerHTML conflict cannot arise; (4) ui/html shape and trust semantics unchanged. NO change needed in emit_jvm.cljc (child-forms is computed before branch dispatch; its spread branch already carries the (tree/html s) leaf) and NO change in analyze.cljc (composition is already the accepted grammar).

TESTS: (1) focused CLJS lowering assertion — the combined form emits exactly one dangerouslySetInnerHTML with one __html value and no positional child for the markup, in both spread2 and spread3 shapes; (2) a shared dual-emitter parity fixture (parity_fixtures.cljc) pairing ui/html with general ui/spread AND with ui/spread-safe (pins the already-working sibling), using dynamic base + overrides + markup; (3) evaluation-order/once-each assertions on both hosts (base, overrides, then HTML); (4) existing spread-with-normal-children behavior unchanged. No test covers the combination today (confirmed 2026-07-18).

SPEC SURFACES: none REQUIRE amendment — the fix makes Spec 004's "both emitters treat it identically" and 004B's raw-markup-leaf sentences true again, and neither spec excludes spread-propped elements. If the implementer adds a clarifying sentence to spec/004-Views.md that spread props and a trusted-markup sole child compose, that file is HOT-ZONE — mayor sequences it; the code+test fix alone touches no hot-zone file.

CORRECTIONS to this bead's description: the repro baselines (e71976a8b3 / dossier's 52059e9b) are stale but every claim was re-verified at efadbc46c2 and again at decision time — the bug and all mechanics stand. The general-spread branch is ~lines 347-364 (341 is emit-element's start). Ignore the description's option-(b) guidance (roster id, error_roster_cljs_test row) — (b) is rejected.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-5pr75 — the runtime spread path can smuggle :dangerouslySetInnerHTML (and the other rejected-prop-spellings) past the compile-time deny: rejected-prop-spellings is enforced only on literal props (analyze.cljc:1600); convert-prop-map!/spread->props (runtime.cljs) pass the camel name verbatim via react-prop-name, and spread-safe-denied-structural does not cover it either. Out of scope here; the attach-AFTER-conversion order above already makes the explicit ui/html site win such collisions at this element shape.

DOSSIER: ai/decisions/rf2-29s75.html-spread-semantics.md is retired (deleted) per Mike's delegation; this note is the self-contained record.

title: Accept keyed literal elements inside ui/presence
description:
`ui/presence` promises keyed literal element/view/foreign/fragment children, but its analyzer checks element/fragment keys at `[:key :present?]`. Analyzed host elements store the key at `[:props :key :present?]`. On current origin/main, `(presence {:timeout-ms 300} [:div {:key "x"}])` therefore throws `:rf.ui.compile/presence-unkeyed-child`, even though the printed AST has `{:props {:key {:present? true ...}}}`. The S4 tests cover a keyed `for` and component rows, so they never exercise the documented literal-host route.

Read the key from the actual AST shape (and verify the fragment shape rather than guessing). Add focused analyzer/error-roster fixtures for accepted keyed literal host/fragment children and rejected unkeyed siblings. Keep the closed grammar and compile-time trust boundary; no runtime fallback or new API.
acceptance_criteria: A keyed literal host child accepted by the compiler; the same row without `:key` remains a build failure; fragment handling follows its actual analyzed key location; a mutation restoring the wrong AST path makes the focused test fail.

title: Keep prepared spawn-all children handler-resolvable after registry mutation
description:
PR #6262 skips the child-local registry recheck when a spawn-all child has an authoritative prepared entry, but the installed snapshot still stores only the original registered TYPE keyword under :rf/machine-type. Spawned actors have no per-instance handler; the lazy resolver must resolve that keyword back through the current registrar. Therefore the exact unregister seam the patch accepts installs a snapshot that is not a live/resolvable actor.

Current-origin/main JVM reproduction: register a child whose :idle handles the synthetic :rf.machine.spawn/spawned bootstrap by transitioning to :ready; unregister its TYPE from a :rf.machine.spawn-all/started listener; dispatch the parent. The child snapshot exists, but it remains :idle with :rf/bootstrap-pending? true, and the bootstrap tail emits exactly one :rf.error/no-such-handler. The shipped test uses an already-terminal-looking :running child and asserts only snapshot presence/state, so it false-greens this inert actor. title: Keep epoch restore exact-owned inside callback-bearing cleanup fan-outs
description: PR #6221 threads the captured incarnation token to outer restore seams, but callback-bearing cleanup batches still re-enter bare frame-id state after a single check. Resources checks A once, then timer/work-ledger cleanup runs by id; work-ledger abort-slot! calls an abort callback before a bare-key dissoc, so callback churn can seat B and reuse the same slot before A's returning cleanup deletes B's handle. Post-install quiesce checks once around a Machines→HTTP hook loop; a machine cancellation trace can seat B, after which the HTTP hook snapshots and aborts B's requests. Deferred resource-intent emission similarly fans out multiple callbacks under one outer check. This violates the promised exact-incarnation transaction and can mutate a live successor.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preinstall cleanup atomically detaches only A-owned timer/work handles while A's token is live; callbacks act on detached attempt identities and never re-read or dissociate a successor slot.
- Exact ownership is revalidated at every callback boundary inside deferred trace commit and the Machines/HTTP quiesce chain, or the captured token/A-owned snapshot is carried into each helper.
- A deterministic resource-abort callback seats B and reuses the same [frame-id work-id]; B's handle survives byte-for-byte and the stale restore fails.
- A deterministic first quiesce hook/trace intent seats B; no later A tail aborts, stamps, emits against, or quiesces B, while an already committed A install still returns true.
- Keep tokens internal and preserve the ordinary restore path; no public token, retry, lock, or general transaction framework.

title: Serialize trace listeners across concurrent frame drains at a post-drain seam
description:
PR #6248 (`127722fff4bf33d7dfad428319547c8f6d8f897c`, applied as `95ac9396cd8a0fe06ea50ebc8fad9841899197c4`) fixed the shape-based trace-listener bypass but did not restore the serial-listener contract required by source bead rf2-rakqk and Spec 009. `re-frame.trace.tooling/deliver-to-tooling!` still drives any drain-lock-owning emit inline, outside the process fanout monitor. Two DIFFERENT frames may drain concurrently on the JVM; each drainer owns its own frame lock, so both can enter the same arbitrary listener callback at once. The current implementation comment says "two ... drains of the SAME frame"; a single frame cannot have two simultaneous drain-lock owners, while independent frames are the actual public failure.

Deterministic current-main reproduction: register one listener; start `dispatch-sync` into `:rf/default`; latch its `:rf.event/run-start` callback while frame A's drain lock is held; start `dispatch-sync` into `:audit/other` on another thread. Frame B entered the same listener before A returned. Evidence: `{:b-entered-before-a-return true, :max-concurrent 2, :log-before-release [[:enter :rf/default] [:enter :audit/other] [:exit :audit/other]]}`. Both threads then completed, proving overlap rather than deadlock. The merged three focused suites remain green (3 tests / 275 assertions) because they cover clean-vs-clean, frame-shaped public emits outside a drain, and the one-frame AB-BA cycle, but not drain-vs-drain.

This also leaves arbitrary programmer/tool listener code running while the framework owns the target frame drain lock, directly contrary to rf2-rakqk's acceptance criterion. The practical risks are overlapping mutation in devtools/recorders, nondeterministic observation order across independent frames, and new lock cycles through listener-authored work.

Repair the timing seam, not the classifier. Preserve synchronous public/manual emits and same-thread nested ordering, but defer internal drain-owned listener fanout to one explicit post-drain boundary before the enclosing dispatch/drain call returns. That boundary must serialize listener callbacks process-wide without holding or waiting on a frame drain lock. Keep the mechanism bounded: no public lock/token API, compatibility mode, listener restriction, per-listener locking maze, or general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria:
- On the JVM, one registered trace listener is never entered concurrently with itself across concurrent drains of different frames, clean-vs-drain, and clean-vs-clean emits; each listener sees one defined total order.
- Arbitrary listener code is neither invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any target frame drain lock.
- The existing monitor→listener→`dispatch-sync(F)` versus `F.:drain-lock`→trace interleaving remains bounded and every event/trace settles exactly once; no fanout-monitor/drain-lock AB-BA edge returns.
- Externally authored/public emits remain synchronous through callback completion. Internal drain traces delivered at a post-drain boundary preserve emission order, expose no partially settled state, and complete before the enclosing public dispatch/drain operation returns.
- Same-thread reentrant outer-before-inner ordering, nested synchronous completion, listener exception isolation, continuation suppression, registration replacement, CLJS behavior, and production elision remain correct.
- Deterministic controls include two different simultaneous frame drains and prove both non-overlap and callbacks-outside-drain-lock ownership; existing deadlock and public frame-tagged controls stay green.
- The solution is one private ownership/post-drain seam, not event-shape inference, a public synchronization surface, listener prohibitions, or a general scheduler.
notes:
BLOCKED — #6365 MUST NOT MERGE AS-IS. Two genuine regressions found by an independent fix-worker (2026-07-18), verdict (b) on both, proven by controlled experiment rather than inferred.

REGRESSION 1 — deferred-continue latch is SINGLE-USE (the serious one).
The first check passes; every later check consults the LIVE predicate. Its docstring assumes a later false reading means a listener suppressed the event — but under deferral the fence is already false post-drain for ordinary reasons. So drive-fanout! abandons after listener #1 and SKIPS LISTENERS 2..N for every emit carrying a continuation fence.
Measured: reverting ONLY the five core source files, test tree untouched -> 25 traces with :rf.event/dispatched for four events. On the branch -> 22 traces with one. Three dispatch envelopes are DROPPED, not delayed (absent after an 800ms settle). run-start/run-end/frame-state-changed still arrive; only the dispatch envelope vanishes, taking the :source :router axis with it. A 3-listener probe confirms listeners 2 and 3 receive nothing.
BLAST RADIUS: any app with two or more trace listeners (Xray + Story + app) silently loses every cascaded event dispatch envelope.

REGRESSION 2 — machines spawn-all: DURABLE CORRUPTION, not an observation artifact.
install-spawn! selects the child TYPE reference on an explicitly documented premise that :rf.machine.spawn/spawned and :rf.error/system-id-collision fan SYNCHRONOUSLY to application listeners before the write. This PR falsifies that on JVM: type-ref-fn reads an un-diverged registrar, stamps the cheap keyword, and the unregister lands after. Children hold a dangling :rf/machine-type, raise :no-such-handler and stay inert — or SPLIT (v1 snapshot on a v2 handler). Exactly the modes rf2-rxjy3 and rf2-zo5n9 removed. Rewriting those assertions would BLESS REAL CORRUPTION.

FAMILY 3 — destroyed_exit_order (needs a ruling, does not block on its own): inline :exit action and deferred :destroyed listener no longer interleave. The file cites Spec 005:2138 for "a consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot" — deferral removes that. Flagged rather than silently rewritten.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THE REWORK MUST ANSWER: how to distinguish "the predicate went false because a listener body acted" (a real suppression, honour it) from "already false when the deferred fan-out began" (ordinary post-drain state, must NOT abandon the remaining listeners). The previous brief fenced off redesigning the deferral mechanism, so the worker correctly stopped. THAT FENCE IS NOW LIFTED for the rework.

ALSO STILL TRUE from the original work (preserve): the ThreadLocal (NOT a ^:dynamic Var — a Var binding leaks through bound-fn into next-tick/set-timeout! executor threads); the retired frame/thread-owns-drain-serialization? plus its late-bind hook and directory row; the unreachability argument (monitor at 2 sites, drain-lock at 3, each fully enclosed).

Evidence and control table posted on PR #6365.
REGRESSION 1 FIXED (44386ba13b). Root cause was NOT a stale latch as first theorised: deferred-continue LEVEL-TESTED a predicate that is not a pure function of registry state. router/dispatch!s target-live? reaches frame/event-owner-live?, which reads the DYNAMIC frame/*event-owner*. A deferred fan-out runs after the drain unwinds, so that var is unbound and the fence reads FALSE for every cascaded dispatch — no destroy, no suppression, just an unwound stack. drive-fanout! read that as suppression and abandoned listeners 2..N.
FIX: detect a TRANSITION, not a level. The first continue? call — taken in the flush, immediately before listener 1 — records a BASELINE and passes. Later calls run in that same flush context, so a change from baseline is attributable to the listener body that ran between the two reads. Baseline TRUE -> consult live; a later false is genuine suppression and still stops the remainder (preserves rf2-eaxnai exactly where it was about). Baseline FALSE -> already false before any listener could act; ordinary post-drain state, never suppression, cannot abandon anyone.
PROOF (3 listeners, 4-event cascade, 800ms settle): origin/main 35 traces/4 envelopes on each of L1,L2,L3. Branch pre-fix: L1 35/4 but L2 and L3 32/1. Branch post-fix: 35/4 on all three — IDENTICAL TO MAIN. The 25-vs-22 signature is gone. Both routing failures were the same defect; routing now green with NO routing change.

⚠️ REGRESSION 2 IS AN IRREDUCIBLE CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO PRIOR RULINGS — OPERATOR RULING REQUIRED. THE MAYOR IS NOT DECIDING THIS.
The worker established that install-spawn! needs NO change and the emit must NOT be carved out. type-ref-fn is still forced at the last point before the write; the definition-lifetime rule still evaluates at commit. Deferral falsifies only a PREMISE IN A COMMENT ("fan synchronously to application listeners") — under deferral there are NO pre-install callbacks, so the rxjy3/zo5n9 window is closed BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by late selection. Nothing in the mechanism weakens.
A 3-arm controlled probe shows what actually changes: arm 1 (listener unregisters mid-drain) on main gives a PINNED-MAP live child reaching :working; on the branch it gives a keyword, stranded, 1 no-such-handler. Arm 2 (same unregister one line AFTER dispatch-sync) is identical on both. Arm 3 (undisturbed) identical on both. So deferral RECLASSIFIES arm 1 into arm 2 — and that end state is not novel corruption, it is what re-frame2 already produces and accepts for a post-drain unregister (the deliberate cost of the revertible keyword; this suites own booting-child-v2 pins it).
THE CONFLICT, EXACTLY: rxjy3/zo5n9 protection is DEFINED as "the install observes what the listener did" -> the listener must run under the drain lock -> the exact negation of wxy1c charter ("neither invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any drain lock"). An inline carve-out would restore drain-vs-drain overlap and the jl75r AB-BA edge at precisely the emits most likely to carry tool listeners, via operation-keyed shape inference this bead forbids by name. NO THIRD OPTION EXISTS.
OF THE 17 MACHINES FAILURES: 13 are listener-as-intra-drain-MUTATOR (the semantic question above). 4 are listener-as-intra-drain-CLOCK — pure instrument artefacts (the validator still runs once by install time; the test samples at a trace listener and its own docstring names the assumption).
NO ASSERTION WAS REWRITTEN.

FAMILY 3 — CONTRACT CHANGE, CANNOT BE PRESERVED. Both children are torn down inside a single events fx walk, so no flush granularity short of inline delivery interleaves them. Spec 005:2138 ("a consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot") is in direct tension with this beads own criterion that post-drain traces expose no partially settled state. Flagged, not rewritten.

STATE: #6365 has 52 pass, 11 skip, ONE real failure — JVM machines (plus the aggregate rollup mirroring it). Routing, core and node-test are green. ThreadLocal intact; retired classifier still retired; unreachability argument and envelope ordering untouched. Ruling request posted as a PR comment.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:54 AUSEST)

RULING: Trace listeners are OBSERVERS, not participants. The wxy1c/rakqk charter stands in full: arbitrary listener code is never invoked nor awaited while the framework owns any frame drain lock; internal drain-owned emits deliver at the post-drain boundary, serialized process-wide, in emission order, completing before the enclosing dispatch/drain returns. Externally-authored/public emits stay synchronous through callback completion.

WHICH PRIOR RULING YIELDS: the rxjy3/zo5n9 "install observes what the listener did" framing yields — it was never a ruled principle, only the incidental mechanics of the inline delivery that existed when those beads shipped (a comment premise in install-spawn! plus fixture choices). Their REAL deliverable stands untouched and composes cleanly with this ruling: pinned prepared definitions, type-ref-fn forced at the last point before the write, definition-lifetime evaluated against the registrar at commit. Under deferral there are no pre-install listener callbacks, so the mid-drain-divergence window rxjy3/zo5n9 closed is closed BY CONSTRUCTION. install-spawn! needs no code change — only its "fan synchronously to application listeners" comment premise is now false; update that comment (2 sites in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc).

CROSS-PLATFORM CONTRACT: intra-drain influence by listener side effects is OUT OF CONTRACT on every platform. A mid-drain listener mutation takes effect when its callback runs — post-drain — equivalent to mutating after dispatch-sync returns (the worker's 3-arm probe: arm 1 becomes arm 2, an already-pinned, already-accepted end state). CLJS's inline delivery (the :cljs branch of the trace.cljc seam, load-bearing for bundle isolation) is an implementation detail, not a promise. Re-based tests must be platform-uniform on this point.

FAMILY 3: ACCEPTED. destroyed_exit_order_test moves to the batched order [:exit :exit :destroyed :destroyed]. Correction to the record: the test's Spec 005:2138 citation is stale and over-read — line 2138 is the state-tags worked example; the governing section is Spec 005 §"Composition with explicit :entry/:exit" (~line 3026), which guarantees only that the user's :exit ACTION reads the actor's final snapshot before auto-destroy — an in-drain action-vs-fx ordering deferral does not touch. The "consumer observing the db between :exit and :rf.machine/destroyed sees the live snapshot" sentence exists only in the test docstring, which extended an action-ordering guarantee into a trace-interleaving guarantee the spec never wrote. The batched order is also what wxy1c's own "no partially settled state" criterion prefers (the old interleaving let a listener at child A's :destroyed read the db with child B half-alive). Fix the docstring citation and narrow its claim when updating the test.

TEST REWORK DIRECTIVE (PR #6365, fence lifted):
1. Re-base the 13 listener-as-mutator machines tests (spawn_all_prepared_unregister_cljs_test.cljc, spawn_all_authoritative_preflight_cljs_test.cljc) onto a NON-LISTENER mid-drain mutator — an fx interleaved in the entry vector between preflight and install — asserting the same pinning outcomes, so the spawn-pinning mechanism (pinned prepared definition + last-point type-ref forcing) stays red/green meaningful under mid-drain registrar divergence. Add one JVM test pinning the new contract directly: a mid-drain listener mutation lands post-drain, arm 1 ≡ arm 2.
2. Fix the 4 listener-as-clock tests' sampling instrument (validator still runs exactly once by install time; the trace-listener sampling point moved past a later macrostep — their own docstrings name the assumption).
3. Family 3 per above.
4. Amend Spec 009 delivery prose (~lines 17 and 624) to the two-tier contract per rakqk's accepted criteria: public emits synchronous; internal drain-owned emits post-drain, serialized process-wide, emission order preserved, no partially settled state, complete before the enclosing operation returns; intra-drain listener influence out of contract on all platforms. Spec 009 is HOT-ZONE — sequence that edit, do not parallel it.
5. The inverted frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test assertion already on the branch (listener can no longer veto the handler its run-start names by destroying the frame mid-fan-out) is part of this ruling's package.

PATH TO GREEN: PR #6365 (head 44386ba13b, verified OPEN 2026-07-19) proceeds — regression 1 is already fixed on the branch with proof (35 traces/4 envelopes on all 3 listeners, identical to main); the only real CI failure is the 17 JVM machines tests this ruling re-bases. Merge on green. Option B was rejected because every variant provably breaks an accepted ruling (uw7hg overlap, jl75r AB-BA deadlock, or jl75r's "no listener prohibition"); option C (carve out spawn emits) is rejected as the event-shape classifier disease both rakqk and wxy1c forbid by name.

Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-wxy1c.trace-listener-ruling-conflict.md retired (deleted) — this note is the durable record.
close_reason: shipped #6365 — the session's longest-held PR, unblocked by the wxy1c ruling (trace listeners are OBSERVERS, not participants; the rxjy3/zo5n9 'install observes what the listener did' framing YIELDS, never having been a ruled principle). All five directives delivered: 17 JVM machines failures -> 0 (1195/4164 green). ⚠️ FINDING WORTH KEEPING: the ruling named 'an fx interleaved in the entry vector between preflight and install' — NO SUCH SLOT EXISTS. apply-transition-once composes all-fx as cascade-fx ++ after-cancel ++ destroy ++ spawn-fx ++ after ++ done, and handle-spawn-all-decl contributes [init-fx, spawn-a, spawn-b] as one contiguous framework-owned block, so application fx land strictly BEFORE the preflight. The worker REFUSED to add an fx-ordering hook to serve a test and instead used the mutator already in that window — the child's own [:schemas :data] validator, which prepare-spawn-all-child runs LAST, after the snapshot and before install-spawn! forces prepared-type-ref. Probed before rewriting. Delta -4 deftests: three rf2-zo5n9 later-seam suites FOLDED because their window is closed BY CONSTRUCTION under deferral, making them verbatim duplicates — the ruling's own logic applied. New JVM contract test (2 tests/12 assertions) pins arm 1 = arm 2 with its own lever: making call-with-deferred-listener-delivery the identity on JVM reds 7 of 12, arm-1 {:pinned? true :state :working} vs arm-2 {:pinned? false :state :hot-reloaded}. Family 3 batched to [:exit :exit :destroyed :destroyed] with the stale Spec 005:2138 citation corrected to :3026 and the docstring narrowed. Spec 009 amended at 17 and 624 to the two-tier contract, verified unheld at edit time. install-spawn! comments at THREE sites (my brief said two).

title: Reject spawn-all children whose resolved actor addresses collide
description: PR #6213 stores prepared children as {spawned-id -> prepared}, but spawn-all permits unique logical children to resolve to the same actor address through :fixed-actor-id or a fixed/generated collision. Validation checks only logical :id uniqueness. The map silently overwrites one prepared child; the first child can consume the other child's spec/snapshot and delete the only entry, while the later child falls back to a second resolution/validation.
