title: HD-008 bulk write row: the FLOOR sits on the clock clamp, so a resolved yield correction refuses it
description:
FOUND BY rf2-b69lw (PR #7282) while making the harness-microtask correction contract enforceable.

HD-008's BULK write row passes a batch of ONE — the pre-batch window exactly — and its FLOOR arm reads a p50 of about 0.1 ms, i.e. ONE 100us Chrome clock quantum.

That was tolerable while the harness-microtask asymmetry was unpriced. It is not tolerable now that it is adjudicated:

  * The floor is the row's only YIELD-BEARING arm in the slim run (reagent-slim is :microtask-scheduled, so its window holds no harness turns).
  * The one-turn aggregate yield reading is STOCHASTIC on this host. Across five observed runs of the same source: 0.0 ms three times, 0.0999999 ms twice.
  * When it resolves at 0.1 ms, the correction is THE WHOLE OF THE BULK FLOOR. hd8-rows/yield-correction returns :refused/:correction-exceeds-window and no figure in the row may be published.

This was found the hard way. With the survival test at  the row did NOT refuse — the corrected floor came out at ~1e-8 ms, still positive, and the row published a corrected reagent-slim/floor of 15,518,934x. The survival test is now 'what remains must exceed what was removed', which refuses correctly.

WHAT STANDS. The PUBLISHED bulk row (reagent-slim 11.000-13.667x floor) was taken on a run whose aggregate read 0.0, so :below-resolution applied, nothing was owed, and the figure is unaffected. Nothing is withdrawn.

THE FIX IS THE ONE THE NARROW ROW ALREADY GOT (rf2-9zysg): batch the bulk window so its floor clears the clamp. narrow-batch-k writes share one clock on the narrow row and lifted it from 4-12 quanta to 40-120. The bulk row needs the same, at whatever k puts its floor clear.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #7282: batching the bulk window CHANGES A MEASURED WINDOW, which obliges a re-take of the bulk row on every adapter. That is a re-publication of HD-008 figures and not a worker's to make on its own authority. rf2-2rtt6.7 is the owning gate bead.

CAUTION, same as rf2-zb3qg's: rf2-2rtt6.2 has a RECORDED GUARD REFUSAL from batching on a witness of this family (batched M2 mounts, 3.2x-5.4x last-third over first-third on all four arms, ranges disjoint, exit 2, batch withdrawn rather than tolerance moved). The arm-order guard must be re-run against any batched bulk window and the ARM repaired if it refuses. A batched figure the guard refuses may not be published at all.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md, 'Known limitations of this instrument' and 'The correction contract is enforced, not stated'.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description: one sentence lost a word to shell backtick expansion. It should read: "With the survival test at pos? the row did NOT refuse -- the corrected floor came out at ~1e-8 ms, still positive, and the row published a corrected reagent-slim/floor of 15,518,934x."
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7282: the description's "WHAT STANDS" conclusion is not supported by the measurement. :below-resolution treats aggregate max=0 as "nothing to subtract" and publishes unadjusted. With performance.now() quantized to 100 us, 0 means unresolved below one quantum, not true zero. This bead's bulk floor is itself about one quantum, and the same one-turn yield control alternates between 0 and 0.1 ms on the same source/host; unresolved yield can therefore be comparable to the entire denominator and change or refuse the result. Until batching and re-take lift the bulk floor, a zero aggregate must not certify that magnitude as unaffected: mark the bulk magnitude nonreportable or adjudicate against the clock-resolution upper bound. The existing batching/re-take owner remains correct; no duplicate Bead.

title: Hicasso lane: hicasso_narrow_run.cjs rides :hicasso-bench but is outside rf2-2rtt6.20's fence and still takes the shared-cache poison
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.20 (PR #7278) while fixing the shared-build-id cache trap.

rf2-2rtt6.20 established that `:hicasso-bench` hosts N different programs under
one cache entry, that the carrier is shadow-cljs's `shadow-js/` npm-conversion
cache, and that the repair is for each driver to clear
`.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench` before it builds. Five drivers were fixed:

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/{run,hd8_run,p0_converge_run,retention_run,z3vlz_run}.cjs

A SIXTH driver also rides `:hicasso-bench` through `--config-merge`:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs

It was outside rf2-2rtt6.20's fence (`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**`)
and was deliberately not edited.

RESIDUAL HAZARD, and it is one-sided. The five fixed drivers clear the entry
before building, so this driver can no longer poison THEM. But nothing clears
the entry on this driver's behalf, so it can still be handed a cache poisoned by
whichever arm ran before it — the same "compiles clean, dies at runtime under
:advanced with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')`" failure.

This driver publishes docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-ratom-spine-narrow-write.md,
so the trap can make that page look broken at HEAD in exactly the way it made
HD-008 look broken.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE plus the require:

  const { resetLaneBuildCache } = require('<path>/hicasso/lane_cache.cjs');
  ...
  function build() { resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BASE_BUILD); ... }

`lane_cache.cjs` (landed by PR #7278) carries the mechanism, the isolation

title: Hicasso P0 lane: one build id shared by three drivers leaves a cache that compiles clean and dies at runtime
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.19 (PR #7277) while re-reading HD-008's yield-cost control.

run.cjs, p0_converge_run.cjs and hd8_run.cjs all drive build id `hicasso-bench` with a DIFFERENT :init-fn supplied through --config-merge. That is HD-017's design and the reason it exists is good: a build-id touch is hot-zone, and four arms would otherwise be four of them.

THE HAZARD: running one driver after another leaves a .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench cache that COMPILES CLEANLY and then produces a bundle that DIES AT RUNTIME under :advanced.

Observed: after run.cjs (twice) and p0_converge_run.cjs, hd8_run.cjs exited 1 with

  pageerror: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')

before taking a single sample. It reproduces at UNMODIFIED HEAD — I reverted my own hd8_rows.cljs change to HEAD and it failed identically, which is how it was localised. It clears COMPLETELY with

  rm -rf implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench

after which the same driver on the same tree exits 0 and measures normally.

WHY IT MATTERS. 'Run the P0 lane, then run HD-008' is the natural sequence for anyone checking the wave's numbers, and it silently produces a dead page. The driver's own fail-closed logic (rf2-f5roa) behaves correctly — it refuses to publish anything from a page that threw — but its message cannot say why, so a reader's most likely conclusion is that HD-008 is broken on main. It is not.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in rough order of preference:
  (a) Each driver clears its own build cache entry before building, or keys the cache by :init-fn.
  (b) Distinct :output-dir already differ; the cache dir does not. Give each driver its own cache root via the shadow-cljs cache-root option.
  (c) At minimum, add the rm -rf line to each driver's failure message when a pageerror is the cause, so the next reader spends two minutes rather than an hour.

Not urgent for correctness of any PUBLISHED figure — a page that boots, passes canonical-DOM parity, passes read-back verification on every sample and passes its positive control is not a mis-compiled page, and every published run exited 0. This is a reproducibility trap, not a measurement fault.
notes:
PR #7278 open. REPRODUCED at unmodified HEAD 6509d8e5c5 and fixed.

MECHANISM (isolated, not assumed). Carrier is shadow-cljs's `shadow-js/`
npm-conversion cache, NOT the Closure name-stability maps (that was the first
suspect and is refuted: removing closure.property.map + closure.variable.map
from a poisoned cache leaves it dead). `convert-sources-simple` invalidates the
shadow-js index on SHADOW-CACHE-KEY / cache-affecting-options and never on the
set of npm modules the build needs; the Reagent arms cache 14 modules with no
react/jsx-runtime, and the UIx arm is then linked against that state.

The trap is HISTORY-DEPENDENT AND SELF-HEALING — once the index has accumulated
every arm's modules, re-running the poisoning builds cannot take them back out.
Every trial must start from a cold builds/hicasso-bench. A warm "control" came
back ALIVE and had to be discarded; that is the main methodological trap here.

FIX: each of the five hicasso drivers clears .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench
before building, via one helper `lane_cache.cjs`. Whole entry, not the one
directory now known to carry it — the failed first guess is why a surgical
clear is not worth a standing bet on shadow-cljs internals. shadow-cljs.edn NOT
touched. Measured cost is inside run-to-run noise (warm 34s/26s vs cleared
33s/37s).

z3vlz_run.cjs was poisoning ITSELF: four variants built back to back in one run.

FILED rf2-2rtt6.22 — hicasso_narrow_run.cjs (adapters/reagent tree) also rides
:hicasso-bench, was outside this bead's fence, and still takes the poison.

NEITHER is a cache/boot fault (0 unverified throughout, pages booted and
tabulated normally):

    DIAGNOSTIC row, on sub-ms readings (FIRST-THIRD 0.40 [0.30-0.50] vs

  - hd8_run.cjs slim run: positive control missed by a hair on one round of

title: Unexplained ~12 MB per adapter-segment retention in the P0 clock page
description:
MEASURED, not inferred, by rf2-2rtt6.4's own probe while building the P0 UIx-on-subs frontier arm.

SYMPTOM. Running the P0 clock rows as a single page, window.performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize climbed 34 -> 46 -> 55 -> 63 -> 75 -> 87 MB across six adapter-segment entries -- about 12 MB per entry -- while document.body.childElementCount sat at 2 the whole time, so nothing was leaking into the document. On that heap the FLOOR arm (a hand-written react/createElement walk with no substrate, no subscription and no re-frame state, doing byte-identical work every round) drifted 3.4 -> 5.8 -> 7.0 ms, and the arm-order guard refused on phase.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Three repairs were tried and none moved the climb, which narrows the cause:
 - a forced MAJOR collection (gc({type:'major',execution:'sync'})) between every sample -- no effect, so the memory is RETAINED, not garbage;
 - hoisting the arms so every round calls identical closures -- no effect, so it is not call-site polymorphism;
 - unwrapping the flushSync around every unmount -- no effect on the climb (though a root's own unmount() opens a flush internally and a nested flush is scheduled rather than performed, so the unwrapping is correct and was kept).

WHERE IT IS. Proportional to mounts. Absent from the floor-only positive control, which ran in the same page and the same run and stayed flat at 1.9167 / 1.9574 / 1.9574 -- and which installs and destroys NO adapter between its rounds. That places the retention on the substrate arms and their adapter segments (rf/destroy-frame! + rf/destroy-adapter! + rf/init! + rf/make-frame per segment, then ~200 mount/unmount cycles against the live frame), not on the harness.

Magnitude check: ~12 MB is about 18 W1 roots at ~500 KB plus 144 W3 roots at ~25 KB, i.e. consistent with EVERY root mounted in that segment being retained.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED. rf2-2rtt6.4 runs one round per page, so no round inherits another's heap and the published figures are unaffected. That is a workaround; the retention is still there.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BENCH. If mounted roots (or their subscriptions) survive unmount in an ordinary app under either adapter, that is a real leak on the hot path -- and the P0 retained-heap row already prices UIx-on-subs at ~2.1 KB exclusive per boundary against a ~0.4-0.5 KB budget.

NEXT STEP. Take a heap snapshot with retainer paths across a mount/unmount cycle under each adapter and name what holds the root. The instrument to do it with already exists: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_heap.cljs + p0_run.cjs already own a CDP session and a streaming-snapshot-capable driver shape.

See docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md, 'Instrument faults found and repaired' item 5 and 'Open items'.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7265: before going straight to heap-snapshot retainer paths, make segment teardown observable. p0_arms/enter-segment! catches and discards both destroy-frame! and destroy-adapter! exceptions even though this bead's finding is retained state across those exact segment transitions. A cleanup failure must stop the instrument and name the failing phase; then reproduce the retention. This is a bounded addition to this existing leak owner, not a new Bead.
RESOLVED in PR #7267 -- and the answer is that the retention is NOT retention. New diagnostic implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/retention_probe.cljs + retention_run.cjs, driving the P0 heap arm's own window.P0H door (no arm of its own), taking every reading from the driver over CDP TWICE: as the page has it, and after a forced major collection. Run in this bead's own shape -- six segment entries alternating UIx and Reagent, 50 cycles of 4 roots each (200 roots, 60,000 boundaries a segment), every cycle verified at 1,200 DOM elements. COLLECTED vs UNCOLLECTED MB by segment: baseline 4.73/4.75; 1 5.13/17.73; 2 5.42/65.03; 3 5.52/30.92; 4 5.50/81.03; 5 5.61/12.44; 6 5.63/55.72. THE UNCOLLECTED COLUMN IS THE OBSERVATION: it reaches exactly the reported magnitude and it SAWTOOTHS, which a leak cannot do. The COLLECTED column climbs 0.90 MB in TOTAL across six segments and settles. Repeated with RETENTION_COLLECT=page -- window.gc({type:'major',execution:'sync'}) alone, the same door this bead used -- it reads 2.99 -> 5.90 MB, so the page's own collector reclaims it too and the CDP door is not doing something the page could not ask for. So the ~12 MB per segment is GARBAGE: usedJSHeapSize read without a collection immediately before it measures how much rubbish is lying about, not how much is held. The floor-only control stayed flat for the same reason it stays flat here -- it allocates a fraction as much. NOTHING SHIPPED IS LEAKING, so this does not change owner or priority. H1 (unmount does not unsubscribe) is DEAD: the sub-cache census reads 300 entries with the roots standing and 0 after release, 6 of 6 cycles, positive-controlled. H2 (the segment entry retains its predecessor) is DEAD: the collected heap does not step at a seam. This corroborates p0_harness/collect!'s own landed note that a bare gc() is a SCAVENGE and not enough. INSTRUMENT LESSON, and rf2-2rtt6.4's one-round-per-page mitigation was right for a reason it did not have: 30-80 MB of uncollected rubbish in a page IS what makes an unchanging floor arm drift 3.4 -> 7.0 ms, because a scavenge inside a timed window is a measurement of the collector. A heap figure must be preceded by a forced MAJOR collection AT THE READING, not somewhere earlier in the run. LIMIT PUBLISHED BY THE PROBE ITSELF: the reaction-WATCHERS column is BLIND under :advanced (watches is a deftype field Closure renames), the driver's positive control says so in words on every run, and the conclusion rests on the ENTRIES column, which has a working control.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7267: the collected-versus-uncollected series and 300-live/0-released cache evidence support the narrow result that the observed 12 MB steps were collector debt, not the tested H1/H2 retention. Reopen for three evidence-contract gaps. (1) The prior #7265 audit requirement was not implemented: p0_arms/enter-segment! still catches and discards destroy-frame! and destroy-adapter! failures even though this diagnostic uses those transitions to reject H2. title: b6-harness/slot-order degenerates to a single order at k=2
description:
Found by rf2-2rtt6.7's arm-order guard, which REFUSED four rows with 'only 1 stratum - the question was never asked'.

THREE COPIES of one arithmetic, all with the same defect:
  - implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/order_guard.cljc  slot-order  (re-exported as re-frame.bench.hicasso.lane/slot-order, so the whole Hicasso lane inherits it)
  - implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_harness.cljs  slot-order
  - implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/order_guard.cjs  schedule

Each rotates the slot vector forward by the sample index and then REFLECTS on odd indices. For k>=3 that gives every arm two distinct predecessors in balance, which is the property the reflection was added for (rf2-88pie). AT k=2 THE TWO OPERATIONS CANCEL: rotating a pair by one IS reversing it, so the schedule returns [0 1] at every index and a two-arm plan runs in ONE ORDER for ever.

Consequence: any two-arm interleaved measurement on these harnesses has NOT had the order question asked, and the guard correctly refuses it. Nothing published to date is known to be affected (b6 and the P0 rows carry 3+ arms), but any future two-arm row is - and a two-arm row is the natural shape for 'candidate vs comparator'.

Fix: special-case k=2 to alternate [0 1] / [1 0], in all three copies, plus a self-test case pricing it (order_guard.cjs's selfTest already prices the k>=3 property and should price this one beside it).

rf2-2rtt6.7 carries exactly that as a LOCAL slot-order override in re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs, with the reasoning in its docstring, because sibling P0 arms were measuring on the shared copies concurrently and a shared instrument must not change under a measurement in flight. DELETE that override when this lands.

Repro: (slot-order 2 s) for s in 0..3 returns [0 1] every time.
notes:
RESOLVED in PR #7267. THREE copies carried the k=2 degeneracy: order_guard.cljc/slot-order, order_guard.cjs/schedule, b6_harness.cljs/slot-order. First two repaired (drop the reflection at n=2, where the bare rotation already supplies both orders two arms have); b6-harness's DELETED and made a def onto the guard, so three copies become two and the two remaining are the structurally forced ones. Stratum counts before -> after, distinct orders / predecessor strata per arm: k=2 1 order, strata 2,1, REFUSE -> 2 orders, strata 3,2, reportable. k=3 6/3,2,2 unchanged. k=4 4/3,2,2,2 unchanged. k>=3 byte-identical and the new suite asserts that, so NO published row is affected (every published row carries 3+ arms). Both self-tests gained a check carrying the pre-repair schedule inline; new order-schedule-cljs-test pins b6-harness and lane to guard/slot-order by identical?. hd8_rows' local override deleted. ALSO: found and repaired a sibling of the shadowed-binding fault, live in both shared guard copies -- a sample carrying a NON-FINITE :position was silently dropped from the phase contrast while the report printed the arm's full sample count, so 24 samples adjudicated phase on 4 and answered [ok]. lost-positions/lostPositions now separates 'records no positions' (documented, excused) from 'records and LOSES them' (refuses, naming the count).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7267: the k=2 arithmetic repair, k>=3 preservation, copy reduction, and 11-check shared self-test are correct. Reopen for one missed integration and one bounded edge in the new lost-position gate. (1) PR #7268 landed p0_converge_app immediately before this merge and its boot precondition explicitly requires slot-order to DEGENERATE at k=2. After #7267 fixes the shared function, the exact merged reproduction exits 1 before measuring on all four pages: “slot-order no longer degenerates at k=2”. Update that precondition and p0-converged-witness-set.md to assert the repaired two-order k=2 behavior (while retaining the three-arm control plan), then re-run. The published k=3 numbers are not moved because k>=3 is patch-identical; this is a current-tree reproducibility regression. (2) lost-positions/lostPositions excludes nil/null because it requires some?/non-null before testing finiteness. A direct landed CJS witness with 24 flat samples, six finite positions and eighteen null positions returns refuse=false and adjudicates phase over four survivors. A present-but-nil position, and a missing position when other samples do carry positions, is lost; only a run where no sample offers position should be excused. No duplicate Bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7280: REOPENED for the untested all-present-nil boundary in the new run-level exemption. Both copies decide that a run records positions only when at least one value is non-nil/non-null (`some?` / `!== null && !== undefined`). Therefore 24 samples each carrying `:position nil` / `position: null` are indistinguishable from 24 samples with the slot absent: CJS verdict is `refuse=false`, no phase factor, in both cases; CLJC `lost-positions` returns 0 for both. This contradicts the repair's own claim that a present-but-nil position is LOST and leaves the all-nil spelling of the recorded harness fault fail-open. Minimal repair: use run-level key/property presence to distinguish a recorder from a non-recorder, then count every non-finite value; pin all-present-nil versus all-absent in both self-tests. No new Bead.
close_reason: Verified already discharged on main: e176fed976 'bench(hicasso): stop the two-arm schedule running one order for ever (rf2-ouwh8)' fixed all three copies. order_guard.cljc drops the reflection at n=2 (docstring cites this bead, self-test case 9 prices the degeneracy); b6_harness.cljs slot-order now delegates to guard/slot-order rather than restating the arithmetic; order_guard.cjs schedule drops the reflection at n===2. Closed by mayor verification grep, no new work needed.

title: Measure whether a malformed (ns ...) form can vanish from a CLJS lane too
description:
rf2-vruo9 closed the JVM half: `re-frame.test-quiet.runner` now refuses to
start when any file in a lane's discovery directories will not reach the runner
as its own namespace. That rule is applied by `clojure.tools.namespace`, which
is what cognitect's discovery uses, so it covers every JVM artefact.

WHAT IS NOT COVERED. The CLJS lanes do not discover through
`clojure.tools.namespace` — shadow-cljs builds its own classpath index and
applies `:ns-regexp` to that. Whether a `.cljs`/`.cljc` test file with a
malformed `(ns ...)` form is a LOUD build error there or a SILENT omission from
the selected set was not measured, because measuring it needs `npm ci` plus a
cold shadow compile and that was outside rf2-vruo9's gate budget. It was not
guessed at either.

Note the exposure is real regardless of which way it falls: the `:node-test`
build carries ~380 files, and the `RF2_MIN_TESTS` floor on that lane is a
collapse detector with the same headroom problem the JVM floor had.

MEASURE IT, THEN DECIDE.

  1. `implementation/`, `npm ci`.
  2. `npm run test:cljs` — record tests/assertions/exit. That is the baseline.
  3. Add one unescaped `"` inside the ns docstring of a `*_cljs_test.cljs`
     file with a known deftest count (the JVM repro used
     `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj`, 8 deftests,
     2190 -> 2182, `0 failures, 0 errors.`, exit 0).
  4. `npm run test:cljs` again.

If it is loud (a compile/index error, non-zero exit), close this: shadow
already owns the property and a second guard would be noise. If it is silent —
the file simply absent from the selected set with the lane still green — the
guard belongs in `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node`, mirroring the JVM one:
compare what the build SELECTED against the files on its source roots, name any
file that is missing, and fail before the run.

THE RULE TO MIRROR, if it is needed: every source file on a lane's roots must
declare — readably — the namespace its own path spells. Not a count (satisfiable
by coincidence, and it cannot name the file), and not readability alone (it
passes a file declaring someone else's namespace, which runs nowhere). See the
`discovery-defects` docstring in `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/runner.clj`
for the reasoning, and PR #7249 for the measurement style.

ALSO NOT COVERED, and deliberately: `migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod` calls
`cognitect.test-runner` directly rather than through the wrapper (its deps.edn
says so and gives a reason). One artefact, one suite; noted here so it is not
rediscovered as a surprise.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 on origin/main @ 7558904791, worktree
re-frame2-worktrees/cljs-discovery-0i0ei, shadow-cljs 3.4.10.

VERDICT: OUTCOME 2 - the CLJS lane is NOT exposed. A malformed `(ns ...)` form
fails the BUILD, loudly, with file/line/column, before a single test runs. No
guard is warranted. Closing per this bead's own instruction.

## The measurement

`npm run test:cljs` = `shadow-cljs compile node-test && node out/node-test.js`.

  baseline  `[:node-test] Build completed. (2049 files, 2048 compiled, 0 warnings, 51.62s)`
            `Ran 11908 tests containing 59487 assertions.`
            `0 failures, 0 errors.`                              exit 0

Mutation: one unescaped `"` in the ns docstring of
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/interop_late_bind_cljs_test.cljs` (7 deftests),
the exact JVM recipe.

  broken ns `[:node-test] Compiling ...`
            `------ ERROR -----------------------------------------------`
            ` File: ...\core\test\re_frame\interop_late_bind_cljs_test.cljs:27:10`
            `  27 |   Source: implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:75 ff."`
            `----------------^-------------------------------------------`
            `re_frame/interop_late_bind_cljs_test.cljs [line 27, col 10] Invalid symbol: Source:.`
                                                                 exit 1
            ZERO tests ran; `&&` short-circuits before node is invoked.

The other two doors of the JVM rule were measured too, and are equally loud:

  declares someone else's ns   `Resource does not have expected namespace`
                               `Resource: re_frame/interop_late_bind_cljs_test.cljs`
                               `Expected: re-frame.interop-late-bind-cljs-test`
                               `Actual:   re-frame.somewhere-else-cljs-test`   exit 1

  two files, one ns            same error, naming the second file              exit 1

  restored tree                11908 tests / 59487 assertions, 0 failures,
                               0 errors, exit 0 - the mutation is reversible
                               and the lane is back where it started.

## WHY it is loud (the mechanism, not a guess)

Shadow does not read the `(ns ...)` form to decide WHAT to run. It reads the
PATH.

  `shadow.build.test-util/find-test-namespaces` -> `shadow.build.classpath/find-cljs-namespaces-in-files`,
  whose docstring is "searches classpath for clj(s|c) files ... returns EXPECTED
  namespaces" and whose body ends `(util/filename->ns resource-name)` - a pure
  path->symbol transform. `:ns-regexp` is then applied to that path-derived name.

So a broken ns form cannot subtract a file from the selected set: the file is
selected by its path regardless, becomes a module entry, and must therefore
COMPILE - where the reader error is fatal. This is deliberate; the classpath
indexer says so in `shadow.build.classpath/inspect-cljs`:

  (catch Exception e
    ;; when the ns form fails to parse or any other related error occurs
    ;; we guess the ns from the filename and proceed to the real error
    ;; occurs again when actually trying to compile

That is the exact inverse of `clojure.tools.namespace.find`'s
`ignore-reader-exception`, which is what made the JVM lane silent.

Doors 2 and 3 are caught by a NAMED check in the library -
`shadow.build.resolve/check-correct-ns!`, guarded by the comment "check if the
provided namespace matches the filename" - which is, verbatim, the rule
`re-frame.test-quiet.runner/discovery-defects` had to be written to add on the
JVM. Shadow already ships it.

## Does the JVM rule transfer, and at what cost?

It transfers, and it is already there. Building a second one in
`re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node` would re-implement `check-correct-ns!` with a
worse diagnostic (shadow's names the file, the expected ns and the actual ns),
one build stage later than shadow's own, and would have to re-derive source
roots shadow already resolved. That is the "second way to be wrong" #7249
declined. Cost of NOT doing it: zero, because the property is enforced.

## Is the guarantee stated, or merely observed?

Both, partially. Shadow's User's Guide states the general correspondence - "If
you have a `(ns demo.app)` namespace the compiler expects to find a
`demo/app.cljs` (or `.cljc`) on the classpath" - but documents neither the
test-discovery mechanism nor the reader-error behaviour. The enforcement is a
named function with an explaining comment in shadow's source
(`check-correct-ns!`), plus the deliberate `inspect-cljs` catch quoted above.
So: structurally guaranteed and explicit in the library's source, measured here
end to end, not promised in shadow's public docs.

## Is anything currently invisible in the CLJS trees?

No. Two independent passes agree:

 * `scripts/check_test_lane_bijection.py` - `PASS test-lane bijection: 1722
   test-defining files, 46 lanes, every file selected and every selector
   reached`, exit 0.
 * An independent sweep of all 73 shadow `:source-paths`: 1067 files containing
   `(deftest`, path-derived ns matched against all 10 lane `:ns-regexp`s. 52
   unmatched, every one accounted for - 51 `.cljc` covered by the JVM lanes
   (`tools/story`, `tools/machines-viz`, `source_coord_jvm_test.cljc`) or
   `src/` test-support macro files, and the single `.cljs`
   (`tools/xray/test/.../test_helpers/sub_reactivity.cljs`) is a helper whose
   only `deftest` sits inside its docstring.

## Out of scope, unchanged

`migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod` still calls `cognitect.test-runner`
directly (`deps.edn` `:main-opts ["-m" "cognitect.test-runner"]`). Nothing here
makes it reachable - it is a JVM artefact and this measurement was CLJS-only.

NO CODE CHANGED. NO PR. Worktree and branch worker/cljs-discovery-0i0ei carry
no commits; both trees verified clean after each mutation.
close_reason: MEASURED, NOT EXPOSED. shadow-cljs selects test namespaces from the FILE PATH (find-cljs-namespaces-in-files -> util/filename->ns), not from the (ns ...) form, so a malformed ns form cannot subtract a file from the selected set; it fails the compile instead. One unescaped quote in interop_late_bind_cljs_test.cljs took npm run test:cljs from 11908 tests/59487 assertions/exit 0 to a red ------ ERROR ------ banner with file:27:10 and 'Invalid symbol: Source:.', exit 1, zero tests run. The other two doors of the JVM rule are caught by shadow's own named check shadow.build.resolve/check-correct-ns! ('Resource does not have expected namespace / Expected / Actual'), also exit 1. No second guard warranted - it would re-implement check-correct-ns! with a worse diagnostic. Bijection gate PASS (1722 files, 46 lanes) and an independent 73-source-path sweep both confirm nothing is currently invisible. Full evidence in notes. No code changed, no PR.

title: Always-on :rf.error/classification-effect-shape record omits :offending-key
description:
Found during rf2-d2841 pass 4 (PR #7246).

`router/emit-classification-effect-shape!` fans the EP-0025 commit-plane
classification-effect rejection out through `error-emit/emit-error-both!`, so
the category IS promoted onto the always-on axis and a production build hears
that a malformed `:sensitive` / `:large` / `:clear-sensitive` / `:clear-large`
payload aborted an event.

It does not hear WHICH KEY. `emit-error-both!` lifts only `:failing-id` and
`:reason` out of the dev-trace tags, and only when `:failing-id` is present and
distinct from `:event-id`. This category passes no `:failing-id`, so
`:offending-key` — the one slot rf2-mz582u added specifically so a malformed
clear could be told from a malformed `:sensitive` — rides the DCE'd dev trace
alone. An off-box shipper learns an event was aborted for a classification
defect and cannot say which of the four axes was at fault.

The remedy is one line and the mechanism already exists: `emit-error-both!`
takes a trailing `record-attrs` map for exactly this case (the flow-eval
category lifts `{:flow-id ... :where :flow-eval}` through it), so
`emit-classification-effect-shape!` can pass `{:offending-key ...}` without
touching the shared lift rule or widening any other category's record.

Same shape as rf2-g0mep (:rf.error/no-such-fx omitting :failing-id) and
rf2-mlh1h. Production source (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc) is
outside the rf2-d2841 worker fence.

Coverage note: `classification-effects-cljs-test` now reads the always-on
count + `:event-id` off the `:errors` stream and keeps the `:offending-key`
rows in a dev arm, so whichever way this is ruled, the test says what is true.
close_reason:
PR #7247 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7247

The always-on record now names the key. `emit-classification-effect-shape!`
lifts `:offending-key` through `emit-error-both!`'s trailing `record-attrs`
seam (the flow-eval one), bound ONCE before either axis sees it. No other
category's record widened; the shared `:failing-id` lift rule untouched.

Record key set: `{:error :event :event-id :frame :time :exception :elapsed-ms
:source-coord}` → same + `:offending-key`. Identical in both postures.

The key ships, the value does not. `:offending-key` has a CLOSED domain —
`classification-effect-defect` stamps it from its own four-key literal, so it
is always one of :sensitive/:large/:clear-sensitive/:clear-large, framework-
owned, never caller-authored. `:value` (the rejected payload) and `:reason`
(prose that pr-strs that payload into a sentence) both stay on the DCE'd trace,
and the tags still carry NO `:failing-id` — which is what keeps the shared
:reason lift shut for this category.

New posture-independent namespace
`re-frame.classification-effect-shape-record-cljs-test` reads the always-on
:errors stream only, pins the key set CLOSED, pins the :offending-key domain
structurally (an app-authored effect key can never reach the slot), and asserts
the payload's content appears nowhere on the record. Joins the prod-gate lane by
default: 123 → 124 of 185, green.

Mutation-proved under the real gate (-Dre-frame.debug=false): slot removed →
exit 1, 8 failures, the closed-key-set assertion naming :offending-key;
restored → exit 0, git diff --stat clean.

Gates all exit 0: new ns dev + prod-gate, conformance quintet, core JVM dev
(2186/10897), core prod-gate lane (1407/6091), npm run test:cljs (11904/59431).

Follow-up filed: rf2-h4f0n — spec/009 marks this category AND
:rf.error/legacy-runtime-root `diagnostic` while both fan always-on via
emit-error-both!, and both are absent from the always-on-categories literal.
Channel ruling + coupled co-edit, deliberately not smuggled into this fix.

title: subs: two priced levers on the CLJS ambient-frame reader - a per-call IIFE in same-adapter? (140 B) and apply at route-hook!'s polymorphic site (120 B)
description:
FOLLOW-UP to rf2-f70iq, which ATTRIBUTED the 264.0 B/read but proposed no
change. Both levers below are measured, in one process, guard-reportable
(CLJS / node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer
compression OFF, n=300, 6 rounds, both arm orders, controls +0.03/+0.04%,
0 UNVERIFIED of 1932 windows). Arms live in
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs.

LEVER 1 - same-adapter?'s expression-position IIFE. 140.0 B/read, 53.0%.

  substrate/adapter.cljc ~L744:

    (defn same-adapter? [a b]
      (boolean
        (and a b
             (let [ka (:kind a)]
               (if (canonical-kind? ka) (= ka (:kind b)) (identical? a b))))))

  `boolean` / `and` / `let` are all statement-emitting forms in EXPRESSION
  position, so CLJS wraps the body in an IIFE closing over `a` and `b`, and
  :advanced does NOT remove it. Compiled: function $E(a,b){return
  be(function(){ ... a ... b ... }())}. One JS closure + context + feedback
  cell per call.

  The flat re-spelling (arm H-SAMEFLAT, held in the bench as a paired
  control) reads 4.1 B/read against the shipped 144.1:

    (defn same-adapter? [a b]
      (if a
        (if b
          (let [ka (:kind a)]
            (if (canonical-kind? ka) (= ka (:kind b)) (identical? a b)))
          false)
        false))

  Compiled: function(a,b){if(n(a)&&n(b)){var c=...;return ...}return !1} -
  verified in the :advanced output. Semantically identical; the bench's
  agreement gate runs both over 9 discriminating cases (nil, canonical
  match, canonical mismatch, kindless map, copied canonical map) and they
  AGREE. Local, pure predicate, touches NO contract surface.

  A worker applied this and measured S0-SCOPE 264.0 -> 152.0 B/read. It was
  REVERTED before landing for one reason: with the predicate at the floor,
  the arm-order guard could no longer certify H-SAMEH (phase split on a
  floor arm), so the harness could not certify its own fix. Landing it needs
  either a floor-aware quote for that arm or a separate reportable run.

LEVER 2 - `apply` at route-hook!'s own call site. 120.0 B/read, 45.4%.

  substrate/adapter.cljc route-hook!:

    (fn routed-hook [& args]
      (if (same-adapter? adapter-spec (current-adapter-spec))
        (apply impl-fn args) ...))

  ONE `(apply impl-fn args)` site is shared by every routed hook in the
  bundle (~11 keys), so its callee is polymorphic and cljs.core/apply cannot
  be inlined there. Measured at a private site with a single callee the same
  call reads 0.0 B/read - a fast path the shipped code never takes.

  Removing it means spelling routed-hook with explicit arities (0/1/2 +
  variadic tail) so `impl-fn` is called directly. Behaviour-identical at
  every arity, but it changes the closure shape of EVERY adapter's routed
  hooks - Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, test-react, plain-atom, re-frame.ui.
  HELD: that is an operator ruling, not a worker's call.

BOTH terms are per ROUTED-HOOK CALL, not per subscribe - so ambient dispatch
(router/build-envelope), rf/current-frame-id, use-frame and the spine's
use-subscribe pay them too. And once per PUBLISHING adapter: route-hook!
chains one closure per adapter, so an inactive adapter loaded in the same
bundle adds a link, and a link is another same-adapter? plus another apply.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED AND SHIPPED — PR #7253 (worker/reader-levers-2ix22). BOTH LEVERS LANDED.

LEVER 2 SURVIVED ITS MANDATORY FOCUSED COMPARISON. Run at the real shared, polymorphic site with the current harness unchanged (its documented --config-merge route onto :ui-bench); both arms carry lever 1, only lever 2 differs; CLJS / node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer compression OFF, n=300, 6 rounds:
  H-ROUTED (the whole routed call)  variadic+apply 152.0 B/read, rounds [24.9-152.0]
                                    explicit arities 0.5 B/read, rounds [0.5-4.0]
  residual at the apply site        151.4 B/read (99.6% of H-ROUTED) -> -0.1 (-1.3%)
Ranges are DISJOINT, and stay disjoint under the most hostile pairing available (candidate's worst round 4.0 vs incumbent's best 24.9, still 6.2x). Material by any reading, so lever 2 is KEPT.

READER BEFORE/AFTER: S0-SCOPE 264.0 -> 4.0 B/read; H-ROUTED 264.0 -> 0.5. At the top of the bead's predicted 4-40 band. Each lever's predicted term vanished exactly when its lever landed: lever 1 took H-SAMEH 144.1 -> 0.6 (now measuring IDENTICALLY to its own H-SAMEFLAT control, 4.1 -> 0.6) and the IIFE term 140.0 -> 0.0; lever 2 then took the apply residual 120.0 -> -0.1, after which the budget closes (H-CACHE+H-SPEC+H-SAMEH+H-IMPL = 0.6 vs H-ROUTED 0.5).

INSTRUMENT, HONESTLY: baseline run is guard-REPORTABLE at exit 0, so the 264.0 'before' is fully certified. Both after-runs exit 2 — the arm-order guard refuses arms the levers pushed TO THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN FLOOR (H-ROUTED, H-SAMEH, H-SAMEFLAT, S0-SCOPE, S1-CURFRM, S2-TGTID). Signature is a per-WINDOW floor, not a per-call cost: an identical ~6.37x phase ratio across arms with nothing else in common. Exactly the limitation the sequencing ruling anticipated; per that ruling NO harness change was made and the PR was not held. After-figures are honest UPPER BOUNDS; a certified headline quote remains available as separate bench-lane work (rf2-ktrvw / rf2-tmzie class).

TESTS: new namespace implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/routing_arity_cljs_test.cljc (new file — a sibling worker held core/test/**, so nothing existing was touched). .cljc, so it runs on JVM and in the :node-test CLJS lane; covers 0/1/2/3/4 arguments across the ACTIVE, CHAIN and FALLBACK routes (incl. that fallback-fn stays a ZERO-arg thunk at every call arity).

GATES all exit 0: new routing test 10/26; npm run test:cljs 11911 tests / 59519 assertions (this is where all six adapter suites live); core JVM 2193/11318; adapter JVM suites reagent 0, reagent-slim 11/12, uix 0, test-react 35/160, ui 702/17602; core prod-gate 1934/8332 at 159 namespaces of 186 — roster grew from 158/185 because the NEW namespace joined the lane by default, not a known-red change.

No harness, benchmark or adapter file modified. :adapter/current-frame's contract untouched.
close_reason: Closed

title: subs: the CLJS ambient frame reader costs 264 B/read - 15.6% of every subscribe, and the JVM profile cannot see it
description:
MEASURED (rf2-x0fe2, CLJS, node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer compression OFF, n=300, 6 rounds, both arm orders, controls +0.03%/+0.04%, 0 UNVERIFIED of 1638 windows), arms S0-VAR / S0-SCOPE in implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs:

  S0-VAR    (frame/current-frame)           0.0 B/read   <= instrument floor
  S0-SCOPE  (frame/resolve-current-frame) 264.0 B/read
  S1-CURFRM subscribe's shipped reader     264.1 B/read

264.1 B/read is the SECOND-LARGEST term in subscribe's cache-HIT allocation
(15.6% of 1698.1 B/read), behind only the ref-count attach.

WHAT IT IS. On the JVM frame/resolve-current-frame is a plain *current-frame*
dynamic-var read and costs ~0. On CLJS it consults the :adapter/current-frame
late-bind hook so the React-context tier is live (frame.cljc ~L535):

    (frame-value->id
      #?(:cljs (if-let [f (late-bind/get-fn-cached :adapter/current-frame)]
                 (f)
                 (current-frame))
         :clj  (current-frame)))

so every ambient subscribe pays a late-bind hook lookup plus the routed-hook
chain (substrate-adapter/route-hook! -> function-component-current-frame ->
chain-bottom frame/current-frame). The S0 pair isolates it: the dynamic-var
tier alone is at the instrument's floor, so essentially ALL 264 B is the hook
route.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. Every prior figure on this surface is JVM
(rf2-21pck, rf2-mvqwe, rf2-j8ls2, rf2-ncjyt). The JVM reader-clause is the
:clj branch, which does none of this. No JVM decomposition can show this term
at all -- it is structurally absent from that profile.

NOT YET DIAGNOSED, and that is the work: WHERE in the route the 264 B goes.
Candidates, none confirmed: get-fn-cached's own lookup; the routed-hook chain
allocating per call; function-component-current-frame reading _currentValue off
a nil provider; frame-value->id. The next step is a per-step CLJS arm ladder
over the hook route, the same shape as the S1..S4 prefix ladder, before ANY
change is proposed.

MEASUREMENT ONLY so far. No optimisation is proposed here and none should be
until the 264 B is attributed -- the read path's top term is the ref-count
attach at 1224.9 B/read (72.1%) and that is a separate question.

Runtime label: CLJS / node V8, pointer compression OFF. Chrome ships it ON, so
a tagged slot is 4 B there and 8 B here -- shares transfer, absolutes do not.

Raw: docs/design/freehand/studio/read-path-on-the-shipping-host.md
notes:
DIAGNOSED (PR pending). The 264.1 B/read is TWO terms, both per ROUTED-HOOK
CALL, neither of them the hook lookup and neither of them the impl.

CLJS / node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer
compression OFF, n=300, 6 rounds, BOTH arm orders reportable, controls
+0.03%/+0.04%, 0 UNVERIFIED of 1932 windows per run.

  S0-SCOPE - S0-VAR   the CLJS-only consult      264.0 B/read  [264.0-264.5]
    same-adapter?, SHIPPED                       144.1  54.6%  [144.1-144.3]
      ... its expression-position IIFE, per call 140.0  53.0%
    apply at route-hook!'s polymorphic site      120.0  45.4%
    current-adapter-spec                           0.0   <= floor
    get-fn-cached (the hook lookup)                0.0   <= floor
    function-component-current-frame (the impl)    0.0   <= floor
    frame-value->id                                0.0   <= floor
  budget closes: S0-SCOPE - H-ROUTED - H-FVID  =   0.0

WHAT ALLOCATES, NAMED. (1) `same-adapter?`'s body is
`(boolean (and a b (let [ka (:kind a)] ...)))`; all three are
statement-emitting forms in EXPRESSION position, so CLJS wraps the body in
an IIFE closing over `a` and `b` and :advanced does NOT remove it -
`function $E(a,b){return be(function(){ ... a ... b ... }())}` - one JS
closure + context + feedback cell per call. (2) route-hook!'s
`(apply impl-fn args)` is ONE site shared by every routed hook in the
bundle, so its callee is polymorphic and cljs.core/apply is not inlined
there; at a private single-callee site the same call reads 0.0.

The bead's four candidates: get-fn-cached NO (floor), the routed-hook chain
YES but only via same-adapter? (the chain is ONE link here - checked, not
assumed: :adapter/current-frame is unpublished before rf/init!),
function-component-current-frame NO (floor - *current-frame* is bound so the
_currentValue read never runs), frame-value->id NO (floor).

The VARIADIC `[& args]` arglist itself is NOT the cost; the polymorphic
`apply` is. A symmetric pair of route-hook! re-spellings was built to
separate them and had to be discarded: with one call site Closure
constant-folds the impl, V8 inlines the apply, and the arm reads 120 B
light. Same fault class as this file's two .slice() factories.

CALLERS. Both terms are paid by every ambient subscribe (subs/subscribe
1-arity), every ambient dispatch (router/build-envelope),
rf/current-frame-id, adapter/use-frame, and the spine's use-subscribe -
resolve-current-frame is the single seam. Once per PUBLISHING adapter too:
a loaded-but-inactive adapter in the same bundle adds a chain link, and a
link is another same-adapter? plus another apply.

REDUCIBLE? Term (1) yes, locally and with no contract surface: the flat
re-spelling reads 4.1 vs 144.1 in the same process (arm H-SAMEFLAT, kept as
a paired control; an agreement gate runs both over 9 discriminating cases).
Term (2) requires spelling route-hook!'s closure with explicit arities,
which changes the closure shape of EVERY adapter's routed hooks - HELD as an
operator ruling. Neither is applied in this PR. Both filed with their
measurements as rf2-2ix22.

Applying (1) was tried and reverted before landing: it works (S0-SCOPE
264.0 -> 152.0) but it puts H-SAMEH at the instrument floor, where the
arm-order guard can no longer certify it - the harness could not certify its
own fix. Noted on rf2-2ix22.

JVM counterpart, same session: require-current-frame! is 32.0 B/call there
(not ~0 as this bead's text said), against 264.1 B/read on CLJS.

close_reason: Diagnosed in PR #7239. The 264.1 B/read is two closures: same-adapter?'s expression-position IIFE (140.0 B/read, 53.0%) and cljs.core/apply at route-hook!'s single callee-polymorphic site (120.0 B/read, 45.4%). Hook lookup, adapter-state read, the routed impl and frame-value->id are all at the instrument floor; budget closes to 0.0. Both terms are per routed-hook call, so ambient dispatch and current-frame-id pay them too. Reduction filed as rf2-2ix22 - term (1) local and contract-free (measured 4.1 vs 144.1), term (2) needs route-hook!'s closure spelled with explicit arities and is HELD as an operator ruling. title: spec/011-SSR.md never documents the Ring materialiser's fail-closed :status rewrite — 009 and the implementation both carry it
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-gdkyo/sf4m9 sweep (2026-07-28, PR #7236) while cross-checking spec/011's projection-eligible enumeration against re-frame.ssr.error-listener/non-projection-eligible-errors.

THE GAP. `:rf.error/ssr-ring-response-status-invalid` (rf2-gblft) appears ZERO times in spec/011-SSR.md. Across the whole tracked spec + docs corpus it appears in exactly one file: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1951, which catalogues it as a promoted always-on SSR category and as a NON-PROJECTING member of the skip set.

The implementation ships it in three places:
  - implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj (report-non-integer-status! + the closed status-defect-record-slots allow-list)
  - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc (member of non-projection-eligible-errors)
  - implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/status_rewrite_always_on_test.clj (dedicated witness)

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERE OMISSION. This is a surface that CHANGES THE STATUS ON THE WIRE, and 011 is the document that owns the SSR status pipeline. 011 §Where sanitisation happens (:1746) walks the pipeline drain -> capture -> project -> set-status -> classify -> serialise, and §Drain-time error classification (:1757) locks 'classification is by the projected status, decided before the response body commits'. A reader finishing that section believes the projected/resolved status is what ships. It is not the last word: the Ring materialiser runs AFTER the response is resolved and flushed, and a non-integer `:status` is rewritten fail-closed to 500 (`:recovery :failed-closed-to-500`) — an app's 200 becomes a 500 at materialisation time, downstream of everything 011 describes.

011 is not WRONG anywhere — it makes no false claim about this — so this is a coverage gap rather than the contradicted-claim class rf2-gdkyo was. But it is the same silent-status family: until rf2-gblft promoted the record, the flip's only signal was a dev-bus warning, so a production host answered 500 with nothing on either axis.

FIX SHAPE. One paragraph in 011's Ring-adapter / status pipeline area (near :1809 `re-frame.ssr.ring` or the §Drain-time error classification refinements list) recording:
  - the materialiser's fail-closed rewrite of a non-integer `:status` to 500, as a caller-bug backstop, not a projection;
  - that it fires strictly AFTER resolution + flush, which is why it cannot fight the projector;
  - that it is FRAMELESS (`:frame nil` — the materialiser is a pure map-to-map fn) and therefore routes to no accumulator;
  - that it is always-on and NON-PROJECTING, per the skip set, so it ships an off-box record and never flips a status a second time;
  - that its record is built FROM a closed allow-list and deliberately omits `:status` by name — the offending value never egresses, only its class name (`:status-type`).
Agree with spec/009:1951 and with implementation/ssr-ring/.../pipeline.clj's own comments; do not re-derive.

VERIFY FIRST (a sibling worker found the routing case was not what its bead assumed by checking): confirm the category is still absent from 011 and still a skip-set member before writing.

FENCE: spec/011-SSR.md. HOT-ZONE — sequence against any live 011 worker.
GATES: python -m mkdocs build --strict; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py; scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py.
CITE: rf2-gblft (the promotion), rf2-gdkyo (#7236, the sweep that found this).
close_reason: PR #7237 — spec/011 §HTTP response contract now carries the Ring materialiser's fail-closed status rewrite, and the two pipeline walks (§Where sanitisation happens step 6; §Drain-time error classification refinements) point forward to it instead of stopping at the projector. Scope stated honestly: reserved :rf.server/* fx guard their own args in every build, so the live reachers are hosts writing the accumulator outside those fx or handing the materialiser their own response map. Record shape agrees with 009:2136 (frameless, non-projecting, built FROM a closed slot list that omits :status by name, one record per rewrite); no new normative obligation minted — the cross-adapter MUST is cited as 009's. Also fixed a pre-existing off-by-one: the refinements lead-in read 'Three' over four bullets. Gates: mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check_keyword_catalogue_drift 0.

title: skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md:347 tells port authors to decide whether to reproduce a silence the reference no longer has
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-l5ytn/l0oys/qja61 sweep (2026-07-28, PR #7235). Same family: a claim that outlived what it described.

VERBATIM on origin/main, skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md:347, closing the D5 'do not gate every check on the debug flag' constraint:

  'Note the asymmetry the reference implementation carries alongside this: the boundary *check* runs on every build, but its failure *report* is dev-gated, so a production rejection is real and silent. Decide deliberately whether your port reproduces that.'

Since rf2-mwv4e (PR #7203) the reference carries no such asymmetry. The :rf.schema/at-boundary rejection fans one always-on structural record (:source :boundary, identifiers only) from re-frame.router's pipeline tail via emit-boundary-rejection-record!, settles :outcome :rejected on the dispatch, and is projection-eligible so SSR's default projector answers 400.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS PRIORITY SUGGESTS. Every other site in this family misinforms a reader about the framework. This one invites a PORT AUTHOR to 'decide deliberately' whether to reproduce a silence — and the answer the constraint is steering them toward is now a conformance GAP, not a design choice. A port that reproduces it ships an opt-in security gate its operator cannot observe, which is precisely the hole #7203 closed.

THE REST OF THE PARAGRAPH IS SOUND AND SHOULD BE KEPT. title: spec/012-Routing.md:773 cites 009's catalogue for 'both are catalogued diagnostic' — 009's Channel cell for schema-validation-failure now reads always-on
description:
FOUND BY rf2-j6e7r/v94d6/zfw16's sweep (2026-07-28 19:36 AUSEST, PR #7234). Same failure mode as rf2-v94d6 — a cross-reference that outlived what it points at — in a second document.

VERBATIM on origin/main, spec/012-Routing.md:773:

  '**Both rejections survive a release build; neither report does.** route-url's validation is gated on the optional schemas artefact and a declared schema, not on debug-enabled? … Both errors are emitted through trace/emit-error!, which *is* debug-enabled?-gated, and NEITHER :rf.error/schema-validation-failure NOR :rf.error/navigate-bad-request WAS EVER PROMOTED onto the always-on error-emit substrate — BOTH ARE CATALOGUED  (per [009 §Error event catalogue] and [010 §Production builds]). THE SUBSTANCE IS PROBABLY RIGHT; THE CITATION IS NOT. The promotion (rf2-mwv4e, PR #7203) is ARM-LEVEL: only the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm (:source :boundary, :where :event, keyed on the :rf/boundary-rejected? marker the interceptor stamps) rides the always-on axis. A route-shape rejection does not stamp that marker, so its report does still elide — the routing paragraph's operational advice holds.

But the sentence as written makes a CATEGORY claim and cites spec/009 §Error event catalogue as its authority, and that section's Channel cell for :rf.error/schema-validation-failure now reads **always-on** with the arm split spelled out in the row's own prose (009:1996, plus the two paragraphs at ~1951/1953). A reader who follows the citation to check 'catalogued diagnostic' lands on the opposite word. The second citation, 010 §Production builds, was corrected in PR #7234 and now describes the promotion too.

FIX SHAPE: arm-level precision, not a normative move. Say that :rf.error/navigate-bad-request is diagnostic outright, and that the route-shape arm of :rf.error/schema-validation-failure is diagnostic even though the category's Channel cell reads always-on — because the promoted arm is the :rf.schema/at-boundary one and a route rejection is not it. That is the same distinction 009's own row draws for :rf.error/no-such-handler (row reads always-on; only the :kind :route arm was promoted), so the vocabulary already exists.

VERIFY FIRST, then write: confirm in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc (validate-route-shape, ~1190/1377/1845) and navigate.cljc (~440) that the route path emits without the :rf/boundary-rejected? marker, so the report genuinely does not survive. If it turns out a route rejection DOES reach the promoted arm, the paragraph's advice — not just its citation — is wrong, and that is a bigger finding: STOP and report rather than patching the wording.
