title: bench: write-attribution's C-FRAME hit reads 32 B/CALL in -main but 32 B/WINDOW in -diagnose — the same arm, disagreeing by the rep count
description:
FOUND while closing rf2-c0awb, which pointed C-FRAME at a frame the rig actually registers. Node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false.

THE DISAGREEMENT, one arm, one closure, two entry points of the SAME harness:

  -main, plan position, reps=4000, 42 windows, three runs:
    C-FRAME   (frame/frame on a REGISTERED id)   32.0 B/call  [32.0-32.0], rounds p50 [32.0-32.0]
    C-FRAMEG  (the registry (get @frames id) alone, same hit)  0.0 B/call
    C-FRAMEX  (frame/frame on an unregistered id, the MISS)    0.0 B/call
  Deterministic: 42 ok, 0 dropped, identical in runs 2, 3 and 4. So 32.0 B/call
  is attributable to frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?, the two-level
  :lifecycle / :construction walk behind the registry get -- the get itself is free.

  -diagnose PROBE 4, the same closures, swept:
    C-FRAME   raw 32.0 B per WINDOW at reps 64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4000 -- CONSTANT,
              so B/call falls as 1/reps: 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    C-FRAMEG  0.0 B/window everywhere
    C-FRAMEX  0.0 B/window everywhere

At reps=4000 that is 128,032 B/window in -main against 32 B/window in -diagnose: a
factor of ~4000 on the same arm, same rig, same node build, same measure/collect!/used-heap.

RULED OUT ALREADY.
- Not the registry get: C-FRAMEG is 0.0 in BOTH entry points.
- Not keep!'s branch: C-FRAMEG also feeds keep! a truthy value and increments the same
  counter, and reads 0.0 in -main.
- Not rf2-xu0ma's counter magnitude: -main never resets the counter and it stands near
  1.2e8 when C-FRAME is measured; PROBE 4 sweeps seed=1 AND seed=1.2e8 and both read
  32 B/window. Both are Smis with pointer compression off.
- Not the window size: PROBE 4's sweep is flat in B/WINDOW across a 62x range of reps.

WHAT IT MATTERS FOR. C-FRAME is one of the five components of rf2-78ejq's attribution of
RFWRITE-0's constant, where it was published as 0.0 B / 0.0% of the delta from the arm that
looked up an unregistered id. With the arm corrected it prints 32.0 B / 1.3%. Until this is
resolved that 32.0 must NOT be quoted -- one of the two readings is wrong and it is not yet
known which. The printed pair line says so.

FIRST THING TO CHECK: whether the difference is optimisation state -- in -diagnose the
measured loop is the only caller of frame/frame in flight, so escape analysis can remove
whatever the visibility walk allocates, while in -main the RFWRITE arms call frame/frame
through commit-frame-transition! between windows. If so, -main's 32 B/call is the figure a
real application pays and -diagnose's is a microbenchmark artefact -- but that is a
hypothesis, not a finding. The second thing is what a 32 B object in that predicate even is:
the walk is two keyword invokes and a not=, and none of them should allocate.

Fence: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/**. Diagnosing may need to READ
implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc (frame, frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?).

title: bench: write-attribution's C-FRAME arm looks up a frame id the rig never registers, so it measures a registry MISS
description:
FOUND while diagnosing rf2-xu0ma. Not the same fault; found by the same probe.

C-FRAME is published as 'the registry lookup commit-frame-transition! does before anything else' and feeds rf2-78ejq's attribution of RFWRITE-0's constant, where it reads 0.0 B and 0.0% of the delta.

THE ARM LOOKS UP A FRAME THAT DOES NOT EXIST.

  (def ^:private fid :wa/frame)                          ; write_attribution.cljs:355
  (defn- arm-c-frame [] (keep! (frame/frame fid)))       ; :443

but build-rig! only ever creates :wa/frame0 / :wa/frame1 / :wa/frame2 / :wa/frame3:

  (let [f (keyword "wa" (str "frame" k))] (live-frame/make-frame {:id f}))   ; :735-736

and frame/frame's own docstring (frame.cljc:858) says it returns 'nil if not registered'. So every call takes the MISS path, and the figure is the cost of a lookup that finds nothing, not of the hit a commit performs.

MEASURED CORROBORATION, which is how it surfaced. rf2-xu0ma's contamination charged 16 B to every keep! whose argument was TRUTHY. Every such arm stepped by 16.0 B per inner iteration on odd rounds. C-FRAME — a keep!-calling arm — did NOT step, in either of two contaminated runs, reading 0.0 [0.0-0.0] B/call in both strata with reps=4000. The only way keep! allocates nothing is the falsy branch. That is an independent measurement saying frame/frame returned nil on every one of 4000 x 42 calls. (P-EQDB likewise does not step, and for the same reason by design: (= db-a db-b) is false because the rig builds them different.)

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether the published 0.0 B is WRONG. A hit and a miss may both allocate zero — a registry hit that returns an existing record plausibly allocates nothing either. So this may be a correct number obtained from the wrong expression, which is still a fault worth closing: the arm does not exercise the path it is quoted as pricing, and nothing in the harness would notice if the hit path ever started allocating.

FIX SHAPE: point the arm at a frame the rig actually built — e.g. (first (:frames @rig)) — and RE-TAKE rf2-78ejq's RFWRITE-0 attribution, since C-FRAME is one of its five components. Print both a hit and a miss if the difference turns out to be non-zero.

Node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false.
Raw (local-only): ai/findings/2026-07-28.xu0ma-wa-contaminated.log (C-FRAME strata), 2026-07-28.xu0ma-wa-fixed-1.log.
Fence: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/**.
close_reason: PR #7230. Chosen outcome: REGISTER what it means to look up. arm-c-frame now looks up (nth (:frames @rig) 0) — frame 0, the frame RFWRITE-0 writes through — resolved once at plan-build time. A PUBLISHED FIGURE MOVES: rf2-78ejq's C-FRAME component was 0.0 B / 0.0% of the RFWRITE-0 delta and is now 32.0 B / 1.3%. Nothing under docs/ or spec/ quotes it; rf2-78ejq is closed and its close reason does. TWO arms added, not one, because a hit/miss pair cannot say WHICH HALF of frame/frame a difference is in (the miss short-circuits on the registry get and skips both halves): C-FRAME full lookup 32.0 B/call [32.0-32.0], C-FRAMEG the registry get alone on the same hit 0.0, C-FRAMEX the miss 0.0 — reps=4000, 42 windows, identical across three runs. So the get is FREE and the 32.0 B is the visibility walk. THE NON-ZERO IS DISPUTED AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED: -diagnose gains PROBE 4, which sweeps the same three closures across window sizes (a real per-call allocation is rep-INDEPENDENT; a floor is fixed bytes per WINDOW and falls as 1/reps). C-FRAME reads a CONSTANT 32 B per WINDOW at reps 64..4000 — ~0 B/call — against the plan's 32 B/CALL at reps=4000, a factor of ~4000 on one closure. Ruled out in the sweep: the get (0.0 in both), keep!'s branch (C-FRAMEG is truthy too and reads 0.0), rf2-xu0ma's counter magnitude (seeded 1 AND 1.2e8, both 32 B/window), window size. Filed rf2-tmzie; the printed pair line names it. Guard untouched and not loosened; three reportable runs on the final build, one earlier run refused P-RKV by PHASE (a near-zero arm at the floor, not an arm this PR changed).

title: bench: write-attribution's near-zero arms move ~2.42 MB per window with the plan — P-SCOPEH, P-INHERH, P-RKV
description:
FOUND by rf2-om73r, the first run of write_attribution under the arm-order guard. node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, WA_N=300, 6 rounds, 6 warm-up windows per arm.

Three arms REFUSE on the predecessor factor. All three are the SHIPPED half of a paired control — the half whose whole purpose is to price a saving:

  arm         low stratum                    high stratum                   step
  P-SCOPEH    32.00 [32.00-32.00]            637.96 [637.96-637.96]         605.96
  P-INHERH    48.00 [48.00-48.00]            653.96 [653.96-653.96]         605.96
  P-RKV       80.94 [80.93-80.94]            686.93 [686.93-686.93]         606.00

ZERO variance inside each stratum across three rounds each, and the SAME step on all three to within 0.04 B. At their calibrated window (reps capped at 4000 by calibrate's (min 4000)) that is ~2,423,900 B of heap appearing or not appearing according to where in the plan the arm sat. It is 13x to 20x the arm's own reading.

WHY IT MATTERS. These are the shipped halves of rf2-zxv06's and rf2-jr76s's paired controls. P-SCOPEM - P-SCOPEH is published as what hoisting the handler scope saves; P-VALS - P-RKV as what reduce-kv saves. If the shipped half reads 32 or 638 depending on plan position, every such saving moves by ~606 B/call and nothing in the old single-pass harness could have shown it.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Under a rotate-and-reflect schedule an arm's predecessor is a function of the round's PARITY, so the two strata are 'even rounds' and 'odd rounds' wearing predecessor labels. The figure moves with the plan — that is certain and is why the run exits 2 — but adjacency is NOT established as the mechanism. Separating them needs a third distinct order per arm.

TWO HYPOTHESES WORTH TESTING FIRST:
1. The window is too small. All three arms hit calibrate's 4000-rep cap, so their window is ~130 KB against the 2 MB target and a fixed ~2.42 MB artefact swamps it. Other reps=4000 arms (P-EMIT at 48.0 [48.0-48.0], C-FRAME at 0.0) did NOT move, so 'capped window' alone does not explain it.
2. collect! (two global.gc() calls) does not fully settle after a large-allocation predecessor, so used-heap starts the window high.

Raw: ai/findings/ (local-only) in the rf2-om73r worktree; reproduce with
  node --expose-gc out/write-attribution.js
after
  npx shadow-cljs release ui-bench --config-merge '{:main re-frame.bench.write-attribution/-main :output-to "out/write-attribution.js"}'

Fence: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/**.
notes:
REPRODUCED on a second full run (same config, fresh :advanced build). Same three arms, phase clean on all 33; the STEP MAGNITUDE differs between runs while the structure does not:

  run 1: P-INHERH 48.00 -> 653.96   P-RKV 80.94 -> 686.93   P-SCOPEH 32.00 -> 637.96  (step ~606 B/call)
  run 2: P-INHERH 48.00 -> 4848     P-RKV 82.93 -> 4883     P-SCOPEH 32.00 -> 637.96  (step ~4800 B/call on two of three)

Zero variance inside every stratum both times (n=3 each, identical to 4 dp). At reps=4000 the run-2 step is ~19.2 MB of heap per window. So the contaminant is a fixed BLOCK whose size varies run to run, not a per-call cost — which argues for the 'collect! does not settle' hypothesis over the 'window too small' one.
DIAGNOSED, and it is not adjacency, not warm-up, and not collect! failing to settle. The three arms were being charged for A BOXED NUMBER THAT BELONGED TO ANOTHER ARM.

THE MECHANISM.
  keep! is (vreset! sink (if v (inc @sink) @sink)) — a type-PRESERVING increment of ONE shared counter. Given an Smi it yields an Smi and allocates nothing; given a double it yields a double, and storing that double back into the volatile's tagged field boxes a fresh HeapNumber (8 B map word + 8 B payload = 16 B, pointer compression OFF).
  arm-ctl was (vreset! sink (aget c 0)) — it CLOBBERED that same counter with the control template's element 0.
  packed-doubles element 0 is 0.5 (a double); packed-smis element 0 is 1 (an Smi).
So after ANY DBL-* control the counter was a double and stayed one until an SMI-* control put an integer back, and every keep! in between allocated 16 B.

WHY IT SPLIT ON THE ROUND'S PARITY. slot-order runs the plan ASCENDING on even rounds — where SMI-200 (plan index 5) resets the counter before the whole body — and DESCENDING on odd ones, where a DBL-* arm is the last control the body sees. An arm with a 300-iteration inner loop therefore carried 300 x 16 = 4800 B/call on odd rounds and 0 on even ones. Deterministic, hence the zero within-stratum variance. The guard's own report names it: P-RKV's contaminated stratum is labelled predecessor DBL-100.

PREDICTED BEFORE MEASURING: 16 B x 300 iters = 4800 B/call, at every window size. MEASURED (node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false), bare keep! loop seeded Smi vs double, 5 windows per point, 0 unverified of 5 at every point:
  reps   64  step 4800.0  +0.00%
  reps  128  step 4800.0  +0.00%
  reps  256  step 4800.0  +0.00%
  reps  512  step 4800.0  +0.00%
  reps 1024  step 4800.1  +0.00%
NEGATIVE CONTROL: P-EMIT, the one 4000-rep arm with no keep! in it and the one the guard passed, reads 0.0 B/call under BOTH seeds.

THE 606-vs-4800 BETWEEN RUNS IS THE SAME 4800, TRUNCATED. calibrate caps reps at 4000. At that cap the contaminated window is 4000 x 4800 = 19.2 MB, far past the nursery (node's new space starts at 1 MiB), so scavenges run INSIDE the measurement window and used-heap reads survivors rather than allocation. Same sweep:
  reps 2048 (9.8 MB)   step  704.2   -85.33% of linear
  reps 4000 (19.2 MB)  step  606.0   -87.38% of linear
and the residue is 2,423,840 B to the byte — the exact block the bead recorded. So neither hypothesis in the description is right: the window was not too SMALL, it was too LARGE, and only because the contamination inflated it. Which figure a given run showed was decided by nothing but whether calibrate's 4-rep probe landed on the cap that time (P-INHERH: 4000 in one run, 844 in another, 818 in a third).

POSITIVE CONTROL, predicted vs measured, .slice() of a packed double array (predicted = JSArray 32 + FixedDoubleArray 16 header + 8 x D, + one 16 B box in the retired spelling):
  DBL D=100    864.6 vs 864   +0.07%
  DBL D=200   1666.9 vs 1664  +0.17%
  DBL D=1000  8129.8 vs 8064  +0.82%
  DBL D=10000 83720  vs 80064 +4.57%
0 unverified of 5 on every point.

THE FIX. arm-ctl now feeds element 0 through keep! instead of storing it, so keep! is the SOLE writer of sink, the counter is an Smi for the whole run, and no arm can allocate on another's behalf. Cross-check built into the fix: DBL-100 is predicted to lose its 16 B box, and it falls from 864.9 to 848.2 B/copy against 848 predicted (+0.02%).

GUARD AFTER THE FIX: reportable on ALL 33 arms, exit 0, in THREE consecutive runs. Figures identical across all three at the reported resolution (P-SCOPEM 744.2 / 744.2 / 744.2; P-SCOPEH 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.1; P-INHERH 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2; P-RKV 0.3 / 0.3 / 0.3; DBL-100 848.2 / 848.2 / 848.2).

WHAT MOVES (per sub, node; contaminated -> corrected). Every arm with a 300-iteration keep! loop was over-read by 16.0 B/sub. The RFWRITE-* ladder rungs, SPINE0*, C-TAGPAIR, C-BUMP*, Q-SCHED and Q-SCHEDJS contain no keep! and are UNCHANGED.
  P-SCOPEM  760.2 -> 744.2
  P-INHER   256.2 -> 240.2
  P-SCOPE   136.1 -> 120.1
  P-BODY    296.2 -> 280.9
  P-VALS    321.8 -> 308.6
  P-MEMO    644.9 -> 641.3
  P-SCOPEH    2.1 -> 0.1
  P-INHERH   16.2 -> 0.2
  P-RKV      16.3 -> 0.3
  DBL-100 control  864.9 -> 848.2 B/copy
  PER-SUBSCRIPTION SLOPE  836.4 -> 835.1 B/sub/write
The paired-control DIFFERENCES mostly survive, because both halves carried the same 16 B in the same stratum: inherit 240.0 -> 240.1, reduce-kv 305.5 -> 308.3. The ONE headline that moves is the hoist, where the shipped half was ALSO truncated: rf2-zxv06's saving is 744.1 B/sub, not 758.1.

The three shipped halves are the real correction: P-INHERH, P-RKV and P-SCOPEH allocate ESSENTIALLY NOTHING (0.1-0.3 B/sub), not the 2-16 B/sub previously quoted. The bead's worry was right — the shipped half's absolute was 50x-80x too high — but the saving it prices was not, because the contamination was common-mode.

STILL NOT ISOLATED, and stated rather than smoothed over: (a) near-zero arms retain a window-size-dependent floor — P-SCOPEH reads 0.2 B/call at reps=818 and 32.0 at reps=4000, P-RKV 106.8 at 1269 and 64.9 at 4000 — so 0.1-0.3 B/sub is an UPPER BOUND at the instrument's floor, not a measurement; (b) the SMI control reads 2x its own prediction, filed as rf2-l3jv4.

The guard's recorded caveat is vindicated exactly: a :predecessor finding says the figure moves with the plan, and here the mechanism was a STATE the plan carried, not adjacency. Nothing needed loosening.

Raw (local-only): ai/findings/2026-07-28.xu0ma-*.log. Reproduce the proof with the -diagnose entry point in the same harness.
close_reason: Diagnosed and fixed in PR #7229. The step is a boxed HeapNumber belonging to the control arm: arm-ctl stored packed-doubles' element 0 (a double) into the counter keep! increments, keep!'s increment is type-preserving, and slot-order's reflection puts a DBL-* arm last-before-the-body on odd rounds and SMI-200 on even ones — so a 300-iteration inner loop read 4800 B/call more on odd rounds. Predicted 4800 before measuring; +0.00% at reps 64/128/256/512/1024, with P-EMIT (the one 4000-rep arm with no keep!) at 0.0 under both seeds. The 606-vs-4800 between runs is the same 4800 truncated once calibrate's 4000-rep cap pushes the window to 19.2 MB and scavenges run inside it, leaving the 2,423,840 B residue the bead recorded. keep! is now the sole writer of the counter; the guard returns reportable on all 33 arms in three consecutive runs, and DBL-100 falls to 848.2 B/copy against 848 predicted. Two further faults filed rather than folded in: rf2-l3jv4 (SMI control reads 2x its prediction) and rf2-c0awb (C-FRAME looks up an unregistered frame id).

title: Extend the CLJS api-manifest probe to re-frame.freehand.splitter and .collection
description:
The CLJS public-surface probe (implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/test/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs, run by npm run test:cljs) reconciles a namespace's LIVE ClojureScript publics against its manifest rows in both directions. It covers five Freehand namespaces today: re-frame.freehand, .test, .tool, .form and .controls — each in the require list, the live-publics map and the fully-rowed set, with a <ns>-rows projection feeding the :classification rows in.

The enrolment PR for rf2-h0b0l + rf2-cfhuv added two more sanctioned siblings to the JVM lane — re-frame.freehand.splitter (14 names) and re-frame.freehand.collection (7 names) — and deliberately did NOT extend the probe. Reasons, stated so this is a decision rather than an omission:

- Nothing is red or dishonest without it. The generator sets :runtime-verified? true for every JVM-introspected row, and both namespaces are .cljc and host-neutral, so ns-publics on the JVM IS the existence check. The probe is an ADDITIONAL cross-host reconciliation, not the source of that flag.
- Verifying a probe change needs npm ci plus a cold shadow-cljs compile in the worker worktree; shipping it unverified risks a red PR on a gate the enrolment does not otherwise touch.

WHAT IS MISSING WITHOUT IT: a public var appearing on the CLJS side of either namespace but not the JVM side (a #?(:cljs ...) public) would carry no manifest row and nothing would say so. Neither namespace has such a var today — every public in both is unconditional, and only defn- helpers sit under :cljs reader conditionals — so this is closing the door rather than fixing a live hole.

WHAT IS NEEDED
- Add both namespaces to the probe's :require list, live-publics map and fully-rowed set, with splitter-rows / collection-rows projections in the established shape.
- Run npm run test:cljs to completion.

Note the collection carries three :implementation-tier rows (virtual-row, row-dom-id, reconcile-scroll) which rf2-axlmz proposes privatizing; sequence after that bead if it lands first, or the probe's fully-rowed direction-2 check will need updating twice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Privatize the virtual collection's engine-owned names (virtual-row, row-dom-id, reconcile-scroll)
description:
The rf2-cfhuv ruling PREFERRED privatization over enrolment for the collection's engine-owned names: 'virtual-row, row-dom-id — PRIVATIZE by default (declare ^:private virtual-row; make row-dom-id a defn-) rather than enrol'. It scoped that work to the witness branch or its rf2-86i64-directed successor, 'cheaper than post-merge churn'. Both merged without it.

The enrolment PR (rf2-cfhuv + rf2-h0b0l) changed no public surface — its fence forbade implementation/freehand/src edits — so it took the ruling's own stated fallback and enrolled all three at :implementation:

  virtual-row      — the listbox's own row shell; mounted only by virtual-list
  row-dom-id       — freezes a positional DOM-id string scheme
  reconcile-scroll — the engine's own guarded :layout write, attached by
                     virtual-collection and by nothing else

All three share a namespace with their only consumer, so no export is needed for any of them. :implementation says 'public for technical reasons, MUST NOT depend on it', which is honest but weaker than not exporting at all.

WHAT IS NEEDED
- ^:private virtual-row (or whatever v/defview's private spelling is), defn- row-dom-id, and the equivalent for the v/defbehavior reconcile-scroll.
- Any cross-namespace test calling row-dom-id moves to asserting the RENDERED relationship instead: the listbox owns aria-activedescendant, each mounted option owns its id / aria-posinset / aria-setsize. That is the supported contract; the helper is not.
- Remove the three :implementation rows from spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn and regenerate spec/api-manifest.edn (gen --check goes red on a stale sidecar entry, which is the gate that makes this a two-file change).

SERIAL LANE: touches spec/api-manifest*.edn, so it rides the public-verb serial lane — one adder/remover in flight at a time.
close_reason: Closed

title: Spec 011 SS-Trusted-shell-hook MUST calls the app-db slice a 'schema-validated' trust boundary, but app-db schemas are dev-only
description:
FOUND BY rf2-759sp (PR #7206) while writing the reserved-fx args-guard prose in the same file. Same class as rf2-bl8k7 / rf2-4engi, but outside both their fences (spec/011 is not in bl8k7's fence and this site is not on its list), so nobody owns it.

SITE: spec/011-SSR.md:1557, inside SS-Trusted shell hook contract, in the NORMATIVE MUST bullet 'Documented structured alternative for untrusted-customization use cases' - the reg-view* sub-bullet ends: 'the trust boundary is the schema-validated app-db slice, not the rendered string.'

WHY IT IS WRONG. app-db schemas are dev-only and settled as such (rf2-bkvu5 ruling (a); spec/010 SS-Production-builds says a violating candidate installs silently in a release build with no rejection, no rollback, no trace). So in the production build the sentence is describing, there IS no schema validation of that app-db slice. The bullet is telling an app author that admin- or tenant-supplied customization is safe to route through app-db BECAUSE the slice is schema-validated - and that is precisely the false-confidence reading spec/010:92 warns against ('your app-db schemas do not run in production builds').

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOAD-BEARING in that bullet is the OTHER half of the same sentence, and it is correct: the value flows through the SSR emitter, so string content lands as HTML-escaped text nodes and attribute values land as escaped attribute pairs. That escaping is always-on and is what makes the structured route safe. The fix is to let the escaping carry the claim and stop crediting the schema - or, if a production-surviving check is wanted at that boundary, name :rf.schema/at-boundary, which does survive.

SCOPE: prose only, change no code. Likely wants a spec/Security.md counterpart - Security.md SS-Trusted-shell-hook-contract cross-references this section, and Security.md:30 is already on rf2-bl8k7's list for a narrower form of the same error - so consider sequencing this WITH the bl8k7 Security.md pass rather than as a separate PR. Carry the settled distinction: production-REACHABLE and production-OBSERVABLE are different claims, and do NOT weaken the reg-app-schema dev-only posture (rf2-bkvu5, settled).

FENCE: spec/011-SSR.md (+ spec/Security.md if paired). HOT-ZONE both - sequence, do not parallel with other spec work.

CITE: rf2-759sp, rf2-bl8k7, rf2-bkvu5, rf2-4engi, PR #7206.
notes:
COMPLETE — PR #7216 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7216), branch worker/redaction-e1php, 2026-07-28.

SHIPPED (spec/011-SSR.md:1557, the reg-view* sub-bullet of the 'Documented structured alternative' MUST). 'the trust boundary is the schema-validated app-db slice, not the rendered string' is replaced. The MUST now names the SSR emitter's escaping as the trust boundary, grounds it on C-000.35 (a framework check on a framework boundary holds in every build), states that an app-db schema over that slice is a development aid that elides — a release build registers it and never consults it, so a value the schema forbids reaches the emitter with no rejection and no trace — and names that reading as the false confidence 010 §Production builds warns against. For an app wanting a surviving CHECK rather than surviving escaping the bullet names :rf.schema/at-boundary, and states that its rejection fans a STRUCTURAL-ONLY always-on record naming the event and carrying no payload (VERIFIED in source: router/emit-boundary-rejection-record!, closed key set, no :event slot). Closes with the point that matters: what makes the structured route safe is that the emitter escapes whatever arrives, conforming or not.

SECURITY.MD COUNTERPART — NOT NEEDED for this bead's error, and that is a MEASURED finding. Security.md:87 renders the same MUST and already credits the emitter's escaping ('the standard SSR emitter path applies attribute / text-node / raw-script escaping'); it never mentions a schema over the slice. The Build-posture cell for the SSR trusted-shell-hook row (:270) already reads 'Ships — the construction-time check runs in every build'. rf2-bl8k7's Security.md pass (PR #7209) has landed, so the bead's 'sequence with bl8k7' suggestion is moot.

ONE CLAUSE OF THE SAME CLASS WAS corrected, in the same bullet: ':rf.server/set-header for header-shaped customization (CRLF-checked, schema-validated)' credited the DEV-ONLY half. 011 §The reserved fx guard their own args is explicit that the step-5 fx-args schema boundary is dev-posture (validate-fx! reads debug-enabled? once at load) and that what runs in every build is the effect's own args guard. Now reads 'CRLF-checked and args-guarded in every build — the fx-args *schema* over the same effect is the dev-posture half and elides'. No table row added, no Build-posture cell touched.

DID NOT WEAKEN the reg-app-schema dev-only posture (rf2-bkvu5) — the new prose restates it. Production-REACHABLE vs production-OBSERVABLE distinction carried: the escaping is both; at-boundary is both (it now reports via the structural record); the app-db schema is neither.

OBSERVATION, NOT EDITED (outside fence): spec/011-SSR.md:1786 says of the at-boundary arm that 'the rejection happens and no status is stamped ... the silence is recorded as an open observability question'. The PROJECTOR claim still holds (it listens on the trace bus and is handed nothing), but the SILENCE framing may be stale since router/emit-boundary-rejection-record! landed. That line is on rf2-bl8k7's verified-correct list and outside this fence — reported, not changed. Worth a bead if someone wants it re-checked.

GATES foreground, unpiped, worktree-local: mkdocs build --strict 0 with ZERO warnings, check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_retired_spellings.py 0. Prose only, no code touched. NOT MERGED.

title: First-contact surfaces carry the blanket — README.md advertises zero production overhead for cofx, whose schema is a production hard error
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-4engi sweep (PR #7199). Same class as rf2-4engi / rf2-bx4bf / rf2-mnmzh, outside that bead's fence. These are the FIRST-CONTACT surfaces — the repo front page, the tutorial, and an example README — so the blanket here is what a newcomer's mental model is built from.

The blanket "all schema validation is elided in production" is FALSE: `:rf.schema/at-boundary` (ungated in re-frame/spec.cljc), recordable-coeffect `:schema` (ALWAYS-ON hard error, re-frame/cofx.cljc `emit-cofx-value-invalid!`), managed-HTTP `:decode`, and `validate-route-shape` all survive a release build.

SITES:
  - README.md:88 — "Malli-backed boundary validation, opt-in, production-elidable ... Validate at every documented boundary — event vector, sub return, **cofx**, app-db slice. Pay for exactly what you turn on; **production builds carry zero overhead**." Doubly wrong: the sentence itself advertises **cofx** as a boundary, and the recordable-cofx `:schema` is a PRODUCTION HARD ERROR that throws in release builds (spec/010 §Validation order step 2, §Per-step recovery row 2). "Zero overhead" is false for a boundary the same sentence sells. It also calls the feature "boundary validation" while describing the elidable arm, which is the confusion in miniature.

The clause about THESE TWO schemas is CORRECT; "every `:where` check" is the over-generalisation. (:31 is already correct that at-boundary is the production-side tool.)

title: The corrected SSR 400-arm passage has two un-updated twins — one ships into every generated SSR app
description:

docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:414-416 was already CORRECTED today — it now says "The `:rf.schema/at-boundary` interceptor is the exception ... its check is ungated and runs on every build ... the handler is skipped and the payload never reaches `app-db`." SITES:
  - docs/ssr/concepts.md:334 — "Schema validation is a development-build assertion ...: under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` ... **every validator returns true unconditionally**, `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` is never emitted, and the projector is handed nothing to map. **A malformed request body flows straight into the handler** and the endpoint answers `200`."

The MECHANISM given for it is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that inverts the security reading. Under at-boundary the endpoint may still answer 200, but it answers over a response the SKIPPED handler never contributed to — NOT over one that ran on an unvalidated payload. Same status code, opposite implications for a reader deciding whether their endpoint is exposed. Correct the mechanism; keep the conclusion.

Take the already-landed wording at docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:414-416 as the model — do not re-derive it.

SCOPE: doc prose only. Do NOT weaken the reg-app-schema dev-only posture — settled (rf2-bkvu5) — and do not presume a remedy for the observability question (rf2-mwv4e, open). Change no code.

title: Package B: retire the pilot's component half, re-point its applications at re-frame.freehand.collection
description:
PACKAGE B of the rf2-86i64 ruling (Mike, 2026-07-28, option (a)). BLOCKED ON PACKAGE A — do not start until PR #7180's rebase lands re-frame.freehand.collection on main with the semantic-neutral engine and the controlled :scroll-offset.

WHAT. re-frame.freehand.pilot-virtual-table (1622 lines across four files under test/) has a component half and an applications half. The ruling retires the COMPONENT half only: the pilot's applications live on as callers of the survivor. One engine, several honest uses.

WHY THE COLLECTION LINE WON, so this is not relitigated: it carries the accepted conformance row + fixture + roster record, :residue :none proven across repeated near-total window turnover with reads AFTER teardown, focus continuity, keyboard reveal via reveal-offset, aria-posinset/setsize honesty, and it lives in src/. Its design is props-and-intents rather than a component-owned app-db protocol. Its window handles empty, clamped and unaligned ranges more cleanly — THE PILOT DOUBLE-COUNTS an extra partially-visible row at an exactly aligned viewport boundary.

WHAT THE PILOT HAD THAT THE SURVIVOR DID NOT, and where it went: restore-scroll, a :layout behavior moving a live viewport to a persisted offset before paint (which also buys time-travel of a mounted viewport). Package A adopts it as the controlled :scroll-offset. Verify that before deleting anything — if the survivor cannot express what a pilot application needed, that is a finding, not a porting detail.

ACCEPTANCE. No pilot component code remains; every pilot application resolves against re-frame.freehand.collection; three beads cite the pilot (rf2-eq2vx, rf2-g5xxv, rf2-drpa3.176) so their notes must be updated rather than left dangling; the browser lane stays green and its test count is accounted for line by line.
notes:
PACKAGE A HAS LANDED ON PR #7180 (branch worker/witness-virtual-18211, green). The surface Package B builds on:

- `re-frame.freehand.collection/virtual-collection` — the semantic-neutral ENGINE. Props: :row-keys :row-extent :viewport-extent :scroll-offset :row :on-scroll :overscan :attrs. Names NO role; row shells are role="presentation" carrying data-part "row-shell"; the row slot is invoked with (key, absolute-index, total). Viewport attributes arrive as an explicit `:attrs` MAP (not loose leftover props) — the compiled grammar refuses a render-slot callback anywhere but a literal call-site prop map, so a wrapper cannot `merge` its props and also pass `:row`.
- `virtual-list` — the thin listbox wrapper. `virtual-row` — its `option`, now taking `:row` and invoking the slot itself; no positioning (the engine's shell owns that), `:style {:height "100%"}`.
- `reconcile-scroll` — the ported `:layout` behavior. `:scroll-offset` is CONTROLLED with NO opt-out; `:restore-scroll?` is NOT ported.

Consequences for the retirement plan:
1. The editing grid's home is `virtual-collection` + `:attrs {:role "grid" :aria-rowcount n}` + grid semantics through the row slot. PR #7180 already ships a `grid-caller` in virtual_collection_cljs_test.cljc proving that exact shape renders the same engine as the listbox — copy it.
2. description:

SITES:

The :where :flow-output claim is CORRECT and should stay; the trailing generalisation is the overreach. Smallest of the three — drop or qualify four words.

title: spec/011: state that a safe-redirect rejection NEVER projects a status (follows rf2-rprfg)
description:

The full prose already exists in spec/009's always-on paragraph as landed by rf2-rprfg - 011 needs the wire-behaviour statement, not a duplicate of the observability rationale.

title: Browser correctness gate spends half its wall clock in one benchmark namespace (bench.b10-two-clock)
description:
Measured with the rf2-76lhy capture-time profile, two green local runs of the :browser-test bundle (855 tests / 5609 assertions):

  re-frame.freehand.bench.b10-two-clock-dom-cljs-test   35.9s / 43.3s   = 50-53% of the ENTIRE lane
  the 7 re-frame.freehand.bench.* namespaces together   52.0s / 60.0s   = 73% of the entire lane
  median namespace                                      0.040s

b10 is roughly 900x the median namespace. The lane is 148 namespaces and 141 of them together cost less than a quarter of its wall clock.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. These are BENCHMARKS - they burn wall clock deliberately (the console trail shows ':control :control-burn, :predicted-ms 4' style calibration). They are riding in the PR-blocking CORRECTNESS gate, where their cost is charged against the summary timeout budget that rf2-15047 just had to raise 120s -> 360s. Every future budget conversation about this lane is really a conversation about b10.

It also distorts reasoning about the lane. rf2-76lhy computed per-namespace rates (s/ns) from namespace counts and derived a '3.1-4.7x CI slowdown' plus '3-4x run-to-run variance'. Namespace count is not a clock here; placed on the real wall clock the three recorded CI stop points (ns 66/93/99) sit at 92%/94%/97% of the lane, i.e. within 5 points of each other. The apparent variance was the denominator.

SUGGESTED: move the bench.* namespaces to their own build (there is already a browser-test-freehand-bench build with an npm script, 'bench:freehand-browser'), so the correctness gate stops paying for them. Needs an owner for implementation/freehand/** - fenced away from the rf2-76lhy/rf2-u0cy4 runner work that measured it.
close_reason:
PR #7193. The seven re-frame.freehand.bench.* DOM namespaces are excluded from :browser-test by an :ns-regexp negative lookahead and run in :browser-test-freehand-bench, which already existed with its own npm script and its own CI job.

MEASURED, one box, same bundle, same runner, wall clock read from the runner's own capture-time stamps so compile is excluded:

  before   152 namespaces   870 tests / 5804 assertions   73.02s   exit 0
  after    145 namespaces   840 tests / 5339 assertions   22.53s / 23.43s (two runs)   exit 0

69% off the lane, 3.2x faster, two after-runs 4% apart. The bead's profile reproduced exactly: b10-two-clock 34.63s (49%), the seven together 50.19s (71%), median namespace 0.040s.

NOTHING LOST, exact arithmetic. npm run bench:freehand-browser: 30 tests / 465 assertions, 0 failures, all seven namespaces named in the trail. 840+30 = 870; 5339+465 = 5804.

CADENCE, stated plainly because it is the one real cost: freehand-bench.yml is schedule + workflow_dispatch, not a PR workflow (deliberately, per D021 — the numbers are only comparable on a pinned worker and the lane asserts on words, never on a millisecond). So the MOUNTED measurement rows move from per-PR to nightly. The deterministic halves do not: 7 of those 30 rows carry no (browser?) guard, still match :node-test's untouched cljs-test$, and still gate on every PR — out/node-test-freehand.js --test=<the seven> runs 30 tests / 88 assertions green.

THE PARTITION IS NOW A GATE, not a comment. implementation/scripts/_browser-dom-lane-partition.test.cjs derives both patterns from shadow-cljs.edn and both namespace sets from the files' own (ns ...) forms — the rf2-k41ph posture the conformance census already takes — and proves every *_dom_cljs_test namespace in the repo is selected by EXACTLY ONE lane. Both failure directions are otherwise silent: matched by neither = it stops running in a browser with no exit code changing; matched by both = a benchmark is back in the gate. Verified against two mutants (tighten the bench selector -> orphans named, red; revert the exclusion -> doubles named, red), green when restored. Wired into test:script-policy.

BUDGET NOT LOWERED, deliberately. 360s stays until the new baseline has been seen in CI. For the record: ~23s local, ~40s at the measured ~1.7x CI factor, and the same ~3.6x headroom rule that justified 360s would put it near 180s.

OTHER ARTEFACTS CHECKED, nothing else to move: implementation/ui/bench/** has no *-cljs-test namespaces and rides the dedicated :ui-bench build behind cljs-ui-g1; the Freehand bench's NODE namespaces do ride :node-test per PR but cost 6s total for 54 tests / 629 assertions; core's write_attribution.cljs is a hand-run harness matched by no lane's regexp; tools/story/bench/bundle-size.cjs is a script with its own runner.

title: docs/core/errors.md and glossary.md tell a reader that production elides the schema CHECK — at-boundary and :decode both survive it
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-05hy2 / rf2-mk8up sweep (PR #7189). Consumer-facing docs, outside docs/core/how-to/ (which PR #7189 fixed).

SITES:
  - docs/core/errors.md:217-220, the admonition 'Gotcha — schema checks fire only in dev': 'The surprise is the asymmetry: production builds *elide* the check entirely, so this category fires **only in dev**. Treat schema checks as a development assertion that hardens your data at its source, not a runtime gate you can lean on in production.' The second half — the category fires only in dev, treat schemas as a development assertion — is CORRECT and is exactly the rf2-bkvu5 posture; keep it. 'Production builds elide the check entirely' is not correct, and the paragraph scopes itself (at :206) to 'an app-db path, an event, or an HTTP :decode step' — an event schema forced by :rf.schema/at-boundary IS checked in production, and :decode is an always-on gate too. The file never mentions :rf.schema/at-boundary anywhere, so a reader lands on 'no schema check survives production' with no counterweight and no pointer to the one that does.
  - docs/core/glossary.md:471, the 'schema' entry: 'Attach to an app-db path (reg-app-schema), an event, or an HTTP :decode step. Runtime checks at a named boundary in dev; elides the check in production.' The blanket applies to all three attach points and is wrong for two of them. Low severity on its own, but the glossary is linked from the errors and observability guides.

THE DISTINCTION TO CARRY (now stated in spec/009 by PR #7189, and in the three how-to pages it fixed): the ':rf.schema/at-boundary' check runs on every build and its rejection is real — the handler is skipped, the payload never reaches app-db — but its emit is dev-gated and the category was never promoted onto the always-on axis, so a production rejection reports nothing on either axis, and (the skipped handler having written no :db) the always-on :events record reads :outcome :ok. Production-reachable and production-observable are different claims. errors.md is a natural home for that sentence, since it is the page about what a failure looks like.

SCOPE: doc fix only. Do NOT weaken the dev-only posture for reg-app-schema — that is settled (rf2-bkvu5), and the 'development assertion, not a runtime gate' framing should survive intact. Change no code.

FENCE: docs/core/errors.md + docs/core/glossary.md. NOT docs/core/how-to/** (PR #7189 owns those).

title: SSR docs state the INVERSE error: they claim at-boundary validation is production-elided and a malformed body reaches the handler
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-05hy2 / rf2-mk8up sweep (PR #7189). Two sites, same wrong mechanism, reaching a right-ish conclusion for the opposite reason. One is HOT-ZONE (spec/011).

This is the MIRROR of rf2-t9x23 / rf2-g13lz: where those over-promise observability, these two under-state the CHECK — they say the at-boundary validation itself is elided in production. It is not. implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc calls validate-with-registered-fn OUTSIDE the interop/debug-enabled? gate and rejects by setting :rf/skip-handler? true. Only the trace/emit-error! above it is gated.

SITES:
  - spec/011-SSR.md:1766 — ':rf.error/schema-validation-failure has no production reject to project: boundary validation is *itself* production-elided (per 010 §Production builds every validate-*! returns true unconditionally under the gate), so under production hardening the value is never rejected in the first place. Eliding the projection is consistent, not a gap.' The CONCLUSION (nothing reaches the projector) is correct; the stated reason is backwards. The value IS rejected; what does not happen is the emit, so the projector — which listens on the trace bus — is handed nothing.
  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:416 — sharper, because it tells an SSR operator the wrong runtime behaviour: '...every validator returns true unconditionally. The candidate is never rejected, :rf.error/schema-validation-failure is never emitted, and the projector is handed nothing to map — so a malformed request body flows into the handler and the endpoint answers 200.' For a handler carrying :rf.schema/at-boundary this is wrong in three of four clauses: the validator does NOT return true, the candidate IS rejected, and the body does NOT flow into the handler — the handler is skipped entirely. (Which is, incidentally, why no [:rf.server/set-status 400] is emitted, and so why the endpoint can still answer 200 — but by a completely different route than the one described, and one an operator would want to know about.) NOTE this file was in the fence of an earlier merged pass in this sequence; the claim REMAINS wrong after it.

Also worth folding in while in the area: docs/async/rf2-rqje9.ssr-prod-404.md:125-126 says ':rf.error/schema-validation-failure is intentionally diagnostic because the validation itself is production-elided' — right conclusion, same wrong reason. That file is currently UNTRACKED in the mayor checkout, so check whether it has landed before touching it.

SCOPE: doc fix only. Do NOT propose promoting the category or changing the elision posture — rf2-mwv4e's, and an operator ruling (rf2-bkvu5). Change no code.

FENCE: spec/011-SSR.md (hot-zone — sequence) + docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md.

CITE: rf2-mwv4e, rf2-bkvu5, rf2-05hy2, PR #7189.

title: spec/009 contradicts itself on whether :rf.error/schema-validation-failure is production-reachable
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-ueopx sweep (PR #7185), which was fenced out of spec/** beyond Security.md. HOT-ZONE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md — sequence, do not parallel.

The doc says both things about the same category, ~500 lines apart:

  - 009:1949 (the always-on-substrate paragraph) — lists ':rf.error/schema-validation-failure' among the 'Registration-time / dev-only-validation categories' that 'stay dev-trace-only', with the justification: 'they fire on dev-only paths that production never reaches, SO THERE IS NOTHING TO SURVIVE.' The justification is what is wrong. The :rf.schema/at-boundary path IS production-reachable — that is the entire point of the interceptor, and rf2-bkvu5 kept it as the production answer for untrusted ingress. So there IS something to survive, and it doesn't.
  - 009:2457 (the validation-boundary section) — 'Every boundary below is dev-only ... (the boundary interceptor :rf.schema/at-boundary is THE ONE PRODUCTION-REACHABLE EXCEPTION, and it rides the :where :event recovery unchanged).' This one is correct.

Line 1949's claim is also the load-bearing premise for a promotion decision: the paragraph's whole test for whether a category belongs on the always-on error-emit substrate is 'is it production-reachable'. Schema-validation-failure is filed under 'no' on a false premise, which is exactly the question rf2-mwv4e asks the operator to rule on (its shape (b) is 'promote :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :source :boundary onto the always-on substrate').

SCOPE — this bead is the DOC FIX ONLY, and it should land whichever way rf2-mwv4e is ruled: 1949 must stop asserting the category is unreachable in production. The honest replacement states what is true today — the dev-time validate-*! family is unreachable in production, but the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm IS reachable and rides the dev bus alone, so a production boundary rejection emits nothing on either axis. That is a statement of fact, not a remedy, and it does not pre-empt rf2-mwv4e.

Cross-check while in the area: 009:1065 already carries the ':source :boundary' tag on the at-boundary emit, and implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:305-312 is the authoritative statement of which categories ride which bus (two ride the dev bus alone: :rf.error/no-such-route and :rf.error/schema-validation-failure). Use that comment as the source of truth.

FENCE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md only. Change no code. Hot-zone — sequence against any other 009 worker.

CITE: rf2-mwv4e (the framework finding), rf2-bkvu5 (the ruling), rf2-ueopx (the sweep that found this).
close_reason: PR #7189. 009 now states one truth: the at-boundary arm IS production-reachable; what it lacks is observability. Kept 2457's 'one production-reachable exception'; replaced 1949's 'they fire on dev-only paths that production never reaches, so there is nothing to survive' with a split justification plus a new paragraph. Also corrected the same false premise at two further 009 sites the bead flagged for cross-check: the §Production builds elision bullet (the check is ungated, only the emit-error! elides) and the catalogue row (was 'Production builds elide the validation entirely ... so this row applies only in dev'). Channel column UNCHANGED — row stays diagnostic, which is what ships; the stated reason moves from leg 1 (which it plainly meets) to legs 2/3 (ungraded, rf2-mwv4e). No category changed what it is; no promotion made.

title: Two how-to pages promise observability from an at-boundary rejection that production does not deliver
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-ueopx/rf2-0l4r7/rf2-2hjk3/rf2-bjkkd sweep (PR #7185), which owned docs/ssr/** but not docs/core/how-to/. Same class as the site that pass DID fix in docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md:421. The finding is rf2-mwv4e (at-boundary rejections are unobservable in production), applied to consumer docs.

MECHANISM (rf2-mwv4e, still open): implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc validate-at-boundary-interceptor runs the check ungated and on failure calls trace/emit-error!, which opens with (when interop/debug-enabled? ...). In a release build the check runs, the emit does not, and — the handler having produced no :db — the always-on :events record reports :outcome :ok. The refusal is real; the signal is not.

SITES:
  - docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:310 — the 'Coming from a fetch-boundary parser?' box: ':rf.schema/at-boundary is that idea, framework-native: the validation lives on the *handler* that receives the payload, survives production elision, and EMITS THE SAME STRUCTURED FAILURE TRACE AS EVERY OTHER CHECK — so an untrusted-response shape error reads identically to an internal one in your tooling.' The last clause is false in production, and it is the exact promise a reader coming from schema.parse() will bank on. Note rf2-bkvu5's ruling notes list this page under 'already-right consumer material (verify, don't rewrite)' — that verification was about the app-db elision claim, and predates rf2-mwv4e.
  - docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md:260 — correct about app-db (it explicitly says a quiet :rolled-back is quiet by construction), then closes with 'or validate untrusted input with the :rf.schema/at-boundary interceptor, WHICH DOES SURVIVE THE GATE.' True, but this is the page about production error REPORTING, so a reader takes 'survives' to include 'and I will see it'. This page is precisely where the caveat belongs: the interceptor is the production check AND it is the one that reports nothing.

MODEL THE FIX ON: the paragraph PR #7185 landed at docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md:421, which separates the refusal ('refused in every build: the handler is skipped and the bad payload never reaches app-db') from the signal ('in a release build the refusal is silent ... the check is real in production; the signal isn't'), and points at handler code for anyone who needs to COUNT refusals.

DO NOT propose a remedy for the framework gap itself — that is rf2-mwv4e's, and it is an operator ruling. These two are doc fixes describing what is true today.

FENCE: docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md + docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md. Change no code.

CITE: rf2-mwv4e (the framework finding), rf2-bkvu5 (the ruling), rf2-ueopx (the sweep that found this).
close_reason: PR #7189. Both named sites fixed, modelled on the build-a-form.md:421 paragraph. validate-with-schemas.md: the TanStack box no longer claims the boundary 'emits the same structured failure trace as every other check' (true in dev only); the section body now separates check from report and points at handler code for counting refusals. report-errors-in-production.md: 'which does survive the gate' now reads narrowly — the refusal survives, the report does not, a production boundary rejection reaches neither stream on that page, and its :events record reads :outcome :ok. Sweep found a third in-fence site, also fixed: configure-dev-and-prod.md:35, where the at-boundary bullet sits under 'Survives — always-on by design' two bullets below 'wire your APM and error monitor here'. build-a-form.md deliberately untouched (open PR #7185 owns it).

title: Enrol re-frame.freehand.collection in the API-manifest serial lane
description:
The fixed-size virtual collection witness (rf2-drpa3.182.11, PR #7180) landed a new production namespace `re-frame.freehand.collection` under implementation/freehand/src, publishing five names: window, reveal-offset, row-dom-id, virtual-list, virtual-row.

It is NOT in the api-manifest generator's allow-list (implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj `jvm-namespaces`), whose comment calls re-frame.freehand.tool 'the third and last sanctioned re-frame.freehand.* namespace'. Nothing reds today because the generator only introspects the listed namespaces — but the consequence is a public surface the manifest does not carry, which is the exact class rf2-ivuun repaired for re-frame.resources: doc_api_check derives its namespace roster FROM the manifest rows, so an unlisted namespace receives no documentation coverage check at all.

The fence on the witness PR excluded both implementation/scripts/api-manifest/** and spec/api-manifest*.edn, and rf2-drpa3.182 reserves public-verb additions for the existing API-manifest serial lane, so this is that lane's work rather than the witness's.

WHAT IS NEEDED
1. A ruling on whether the virtual collection is a sanctioned fourth re-frame.freehand.* surface, or whether it should instead be folded into re-frame.freehand.controls (which WOULD change spec/004-Views.md's 'Today it is field, buffered-field and release' paragraph and the generated manifest together).
2. If sanctioned: add the namespace to gen.clj's jvm-namespaces with its rationale comment, add tier/owner/status rows to spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn for the five names, regenerate spec/api-manifest.edn, and check whether spec/API.md needs a row.

Suggested tiers, for the ruling to accept or overturn: virtual-list :front-porch, window / reveal-offset / row-dom-id :advanced (a library author composing its own list needs the arithmetic), virtual-row :advanced or :implementation (it is the list's own row shell, not a call-site surface).
notes:
NOTE from the rf2-86i64 ruling (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28): that ruling changes the surface this bead enrols. The survivor splits into a semantic-neutral fixed-size virtualization ENGINE (working name virtual-collection: viewport, canvas, keyed shells, window arithmetic, and a required CONTROLLED :scroll-offset always reconciled onto the live viewport via a guarded :layout behavior) plus a thin listbox WRAPPER (virtual-list) containing no second range/scroll engine; the pilot's opt-in :restore-scroll? is retired. The branch's original five-name listbox-only roster (window, reveal-offset, row-dom-id, virtual-list, virtual-row) is therefore superseded — enrolment should follow the engine+wrapper shape and land AFTER rf2-86i64's Package A settles it. Also note: the branch's FH-CTRL-019 id now collides with main (splitter); the collection re-enrols at the next free id (FH-CTRL-021 as of 2026-07-28). Full ruling in rf2-86i64 notes.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — SANCTION `re-frame.freehand.collection` as a public re-frame.freehand.* sibling namespace (dossier option 1). Folding into re-frame.freehand.controls is REJECTED.

REASONING
- spec/Conventions.md (section "Freehand — one public namespace, one alias, one reserved root") already states the sanctioning rule AND is "the one place that holds the roster": a sibling is earned only where a separate edge materially clarifies a capability with its own audience. Fixed-size virtualization qualifies: a cohesive capability (window arithmetic + the mounted control) with a distinct audience (a library author composing their own list needs window/reveal-offset without the input-field kit). `(require [re-frame.freehand.collection :as coll])` reads exactly like what it is.
- The name-collision evidence is concrete on main TODAY, not a forecast: re-frame.freehand.controls/key-intent (controls.cljc:85) and re-frame.freehand.splitter/key-intent (splitter.cljc:231) already coexist. A flat controls grab-bag forces prefixed names (splitter-key-intent, virtual-list-window) or refusals; capability namespaces + aliases are the idiomatic answer.
- Fold-in would churn a just-landed conformance-enrolled control, move spec/004's "Today it is field, buffered-field and release" paragraph plus the enrolment, and re-opens the same question with a worse default as typeahead (rf2-drpa3.182.8) and further controls arrive. The corpus has already voted: splitter landed as its own namespace.

TIERS (defaults; the enrolment PR may refine; roster subject to the rf2-86i64 condition below)
- virtual-list, window, reveal-offset — :advanced, all three. This overturns the dossier's virtual-list :front-porch suggestion, adopting the Codex tier-hygiene argument: :front-porch is the tight day-one surface; fixed-size virtualization is opt-in scalability machinery an ordinary list never needs. Require the capability when the problem appears; keep the default programmer/AI context tight.
- virtual-row, row-dom-id — PRIVATIZE by default (declare ^:private virtual-row; make row-dom-id a defn-) rather than enrol. virtual-row is mounted only by virtual-list — its separate boundary satisfies the loop-capture law, but producer and consumer share the namespace, so no export is needed. row-dom-id freezes a positional string scheme that should stay replaceable: the supported contract is the rendered relationship (the listbox owns aria-activedescendant; each mounted option owns its id / aria-posinset / aria-setsize), and cross-namespace tests should assert that rendered invariant instead of calling the helper. Because PR #7180 is still OPEN (see corrections), the privatization belongs on the witness branch or its rf2-86i64-directed successor — cheaper than post-merge churn. Fallback if privatization proves wrong at diff time: enrol both at :implementation.

RF2-86I64 CONDITION (re-checked 2026-07-28 just before this ruling: still open, no ruling notes)
Enrolment EXECUTES only after rf2-86i64's ruling settles the name roster (its second opinion proposes reshaping the engine into a semantic-neutral virtual-collection with a thin listbox wrapper, which would change the five-name roster). The namespace-sanction decision recorded here is INDEPENDENT of that roster: whichever vars survive, they live in the sanctioned re-frame.freehand.collection. Encoded as a tracker dependency: this bead is blocked-by rf2-86i64, so it enters bd ready the moment that ruling closes.

FACTUAL CORRECTIONS (verified 2026-07-28 against a checkout current with origin/main)
- PR #7180 is OPEN, not merged: re-frame.freehand.collection exists only on worker/witness-virtual-18211. "Landed"/"shipped" in this bead's and rf2-86i64's descriptions means landed on the PR. Enrolment therefore also waits for the witness (or successor) merge.
- The collection's conformance fixture on the witness branch is fh-ctrl-020; fh-ctrl-019 on main is the SPLITTER. The FH-CTRL-019 references in both bead descriptions are stale.
- DISCOVERED SIBLING HOLE: re-frame.freehand.splitter is on main in production src with 10+ public names (bounds, settle, key-intent, intent-at, fraction-at, init, start, move, commit, cancel, plus the view) and is ALSO absent from gen.clj jvm-namespaces, spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, spec/api-manifest.edn, AND the Conventions.md sibling roster — the same defect class this bead repairs, with no tracking bead found. The enrolment PR SHOULD sweep splitter into the same serial-lane change (same files, same lane, same rule), or the mayor files a sibling bead.

ENROLMENT BRIEF (this bead is the implementation owner; one serial-lane PR, dispatchable once the rf2-86i64 dependency clears)
1. spec/Conventions.md, Freehand section — extend the sibling-roster sentence (the one place that holds the roster) with re-frame.freehand.collection, with its one-line earned-edge rationale (+ splitter if swept). HOT ZONE — serial.
2. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj — add re-frame.freehand.collection to jvm-namespaces with a rationale comment (fixed-size virtual collection, DC-04's first-party answer, fixture fh-ctrl-020); REWRITE the tool entry's "third and last sanctioned" comment to defer to the Conventions.md qualitative rule (a sibling is earned by a cohesive capability with its own audience) — never a count: the count is already false twice over (splitter, collection).
3. spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn — rows in the established shape, e.g. ["re-frame.freehand.collection" "virtual-list"] {:tier :advanced :owner "004" :status "EP-0036"}, for the final roster per rf2-86i64.
4. Regenerate spec/api-manifest.edn via the generator; run the manifest --check gate.
5. spec/API.md — add the namespace row (HOT ZONE — same serial PR).
6. Doc coverage: doc_api_check derives its roster FROM the manifest, so enrolment makes the docs gate bite — add docs/api/re-frame.freehand.collection.md plus the README inventory links; also check the CLJS public-surface probe's require / live-public / fully-rowed / classification-reconciliation sets (verify which of these gates exist at diff time).
7. Gates: JVM/CLJS public-roster checks, manifest --check, doc-API coverage, and the collection structural/parity/browser suites. Foreground, to completion.
8. SERIAL-LANE CONSTRAINT: one public-verb adder in flight at a time — do not dispatch alongside any other manifest/API.md-touching PR.
9. URGENCY: until enrolment lands, these names are public surface invisible to EVERY manifest-derived gate (no manifest row, no doc-coverage check, no roster reconciliation) — the exact class rf2-ivuun repaired for re-frame.resources. Ride soon after the condition clears.
CONSISTENCY ADDENDUM (2026-07-28, same ruling session): rf2-86i64's ruling landed between this ruling's final pre-check and its append (its cross-note precedes the ruling above). Reconciliation, having now read that ruling in full:

- CONSISTENT — the sanction stands exactly as conditioned. rf2-86i64 chose option (a): the collection line is the sole survivor, split into a semantic-neutral fixed-size virtualization ENGINE plus a thin listbox WRAPPER (virtual-list), both living in re-frame.freehand.collection. Nothing in that shape disturbs the namespace decision; rf2-86i64 explicitly defers "final public naming" to this bead's surface ruling.
- ROSTER DEFAULTS under the engine+wrapper shape (enrolment PR may refine at diff time): the engine var under its working name virtual-collection — :advanced; virtual-list (the listbox wrapper) — :advanced; window and reveal-offset — :advanced IF they remain public verbs after the engine extraction (they are the compositional seam the sanction reasoning leans on, so keep them public unless Package A internalises them). The virtual-row / row-dom-id privatization default above is unchanged and now falls naturally out of Package A's extraction (the engine owns the keyed row shells). The branch's original five-name listbox-only roster is superseded, as rf2-86i64's cross-note says.
- FIXTURE ID CORRECTION: the brief's step 2 said "fixture fh-ctrl-020" — superseded. Per rf2-86i64 (verified against the tree): main has FH-CTRL-019 = splitter and FH-CTRL-020 = the composed control; the collection re-enrols at the next free id, FH-CTRL-021 as of 2026-07-28 — re-verify at implementation time. The gen.clj rationale comment cites whatever id Package A lands.
- SEQUENCING CONFIRMED: rf2-86i64 is Package A's implementation owner, so the blocked-by dependency recorded above now means precisely "enrolment dispatches when Package A closes". The splitter-sweep suggestion in the brief stands independently.
close_reason: PR #7212, rode the same serial-lane change as rf2-h0b0l. SEVEN names enrolled, not the bead's five: the rf2-86i64 engine/listbox split added virtual-collection and reconcile-scroll, and the merged source is what was read. TIERS — virtual-collection / virtual-list / window / reveal-offset :advanced (the ruling's tier-hygiene call, overturning the dossier's :front-porch for virtual-list); virtual-row / row-dom-id / reconcile-scroll :implementation, which is the ruling's OWN stated fallback since privatization was scoped to the witness branch or its rf2-86i64 successor and both merged without it, and this PR changes no public surface. reconcile-scroll joins the fallback by the same reasoning: it is the engine's own guarded :layout write, attached by virtual-collection and by nothing else. FOLLOW-UPS FILED: rf2-axlmz (privatize the three engine-owned names — removes the three :implementation rows), rf2-m41gl (extend the CLJS probe to both namespaces). Conventions roster now names six siblings and states the consequence of absence. All api-manifest gates, both JVM suites, the conformance-index check and mkdocs --strict green.

title: B10: take the two-clock envelope under :advanced — the dev-build figure is a lower bound and 120 Hz is the row it could flip
description:
OUTCOME
Re-take the DC-09 two-clock envelope (rf2-drpa3.182.12, PR #7179) from an :advanced bundle with goog.DEBUG false, so the published rates describe the artefact a consumer ships.

WHY
Every figure in docs/design/freehand/studio/two-clock-operating-envelope.md is from :optimizations :none with goog.DEBUG true, so the Spec 009 instrumentation seam, schema validation and trace emission are all live on exactly the measured event path. Every cost there is an UPPER bound and every rate a LOWER bound. The direction is safe but the factor is unmeasured, and the 120 Hz row is exactly the row it could flip: at k=0 the crossing p95 was 9.2 ms against a 8.33 ms budget — a miss by 10%.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE
:advanced cannot compile shadow's :browser-test target, so the reading needs a plain :browser entry plus a build target in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn — a hot-zone file that was carrying four concurrent .182 siblings when .12 was measured. It was left alone rather than raced.

THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS
B6 hit this identically and solved it: re-frame.freehand.bench.b6-prod-app (a :browser entry) plus b6_prod_run.cjs (a node driver), with the rows themselves living in b6-rows so both entries call one method. B10 is already split the same way — b10-two-clock holds the fixture, arms and drivers with no cljs.test in it, and b10-two-clock-dom-cljs-test holds only assertions. So this is a prod entry plus a driver plus one shadow-cljs.edn build target, and NO new instrument.

SCOPE
Add the entry and the target; re-take M1 (sibling ladder), M2 (config equality at both read sites) and M3 (driven rates). Update the studio report's tables in place and delete the lower-bound caveat where it no longer applies. Keep the dev-build figures beside the production ones rather than replacing them — the gap IS the instrumentation cost and is worth publishing once.

SEQUENCING
Touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (hot zone). Sequence it; do not run it parallel with another shadow-cljs.edn bead.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The three rows publish from an :advanced build with :instrumentation? false in the D021 record.
2. The report states the measured dev-to-production factor rather than the direction alone.
3. The 120 Hz verdict is restated from the production p95, whichever way it falls.
4. The two positive controls (C1 computed duration, C2 computed mutation count) ride the production run too, and C2's predictions still hold exactly.
close_reason: Done in PR #7198. 120 Hz FLIPPED, at every rung. Measured dev-to-production factor on crossing p50: 6.0x-11.6x (k=0 3.5-4.6 -> 0.3-0.5 ms; k=200 18.3-22.2 -> 2.6-3.6), from 3 production runs agreeing within 0.4 ms at every rung. 120 Hz cleared its 8.33 ms p95 budget NOWHERE in dev; it clears everywhere in production, worst rung 5.1 ms. 60 Hz now comfortable across the whole ladder; 240 Hz clears to k=50. Driven arm: the k=200 offer ceiling (43-49/s regardless of ask) was an artefact of the build - production delivers 61/124/244 per second. ACCEPTANCE: (1) all three rows publish with :optimizations :advanced, :instrumentation? false, and runs 2-3 carry :d021 :release-evidence; (2) the factor is stated AND decomposed - an ablation arm (:advanced with goog.DEBUG back on, one define changed, same entry/page/driver) shows the flat 3-4 ms event half was the instrumentation seam essentially entirely (:advanced barely moves it; the define collapses it ~13x) while the commit half benefits about evenly from both; (3) 120 Hz restated from production p95; (4) C1 and C2 rode every production run - C2 predicted==measured at all 15 (mode x rung) combos in every arm, and the driven arm independently reproduced exactly 201.0 mutations/crossing in all 8 runs. 0 unverified of 800 per arm (0 of 5760 across the report). NO shadow-cljs.edn CHANGE NEEDED: the bead's premise was wrong - B6 had already shown --config-merge supplies :output-dir and :init-fn on top of :freehand-release, which already carries :advanced + goog.DEBUG false. Hot-zone contention was real; the dependency on it was not. Recommendation ('add no scheduling vocabulary') HOLDS and is stronger: backlog still 1 at 5x the throughput, equality arms now under Chrome's clock clamp, :update elision 52/52 in all three bundles. ONE claim revised DOWN: read-site penalty is a constant 3.1-3.3 ms (was 40-44), ratio 1.3-4.2x (was 8-19x) - guidance kept, urgency reduced. M4 not re-taken (correctness, already gated, out of scope). Report rewritten with dev figures kept beside production.

title: examples/core/login README says a malformed credential is 'rejected at the door' — it is not, in production
description:
Found by the rf2-byexd/rf2-pn648 sweep (PR #7175). The sweep's fence covered examples/capabilities/ssr/** (both READMEs corrected there); this one is under examples/core/. Same ruling: rf2-bkvu5 (a).

SITE:
  - examples/core/login/README.md:29 — 'A second schema (Credentials, riding AuthLoginEvent) validates the inbound event *vector* at the :where :event boundary. So a too-short password or a malformed email is rejected at the door, and the handler never runs.'

Why this one stings more than its priority: 'rejected at the door' on a CREDENTIAL boundary is exactly the reading the ruling forbids. :where :event is validate-event!, wrapped in (if interop/debug-enabled? ... true) — implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:884,908. The example registers no :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the README carries no dev/production qualification anywhere (its only 'production' mention, :57, is about file layout).

TWO WAYS TO FIX, mayor's call:
  (a) Qualify the prose — the schema is the dev tripwire and the introspection surface; the login handler is what must reject a malformed credential in production. Cheapest, and consistent with what PR #7175 did to the SSR example READMEs.
  (b) Make the example correct by construction — add :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary] to the login handler, since a credential ingress IS the canonical at-boundary case (Spec 010 SSProduction builds names exactly this shape), and let the prose say why. This changes example CODE, so it needs the usual example gates.

(b) is arguably the better teaching artefact — a login example that models the production-safe shape is worth more than one that models the dev-only shape and apologises for it in prose. But it is a code change, so it is a ruling not a mechanical fix.

FENCE: examples/core/login/** only.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (ruling), rf2-byexd (the pass that found this).

title: make-frame seals its generation before the record exists, so a racing reg-* leaves it stale
description:
Found while fixing rf2-9c2jf (PR #7176). DISTINCT from that defect and deliberately NOT folded into it — rf2-9c2jf was scoped to the once-initialization of the reprojection wiring; this is a window inside make-frame itself.

THE WINDOW (implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc, make-frame). The generation is SEALED near the top of the let (asm/assemble / assemble-default, ~line 742) but the record is not written until frame/upsert-frame! further down (~line 795). Those are two separate steps with real work between them.

A reg-* issued on another thread in that gap fires the registration hook -> reproject-on-registration-change! -> mark-dirty-and-schedule!, which SKIPS when (seq (live-frame-ids)) is empty (the rf2-h4q6cy hot-path optimisation: reprojection only ever touches image-loaded frames, so with none there is nothing to mark). The in-flight frame is not in `frames` yet, so it does not count. No dirty mark is set. Then upsert-frame! writes the record carrying a generation that PREDATES the registration, and nothing is left to flush it. Same permanently-stale end state as rf2-9c2jf: dispatch reports :rf.error/no-such-handler for a handler registrar/lookup is holding at that moment.

SCOPE. Narrower than rf2-9c2jf: it only bites when NO image-loaded frame exists at hook time — i.e. the FIRST make-frame in a process racing a reg-*. If any other frame is already live, the mark is set, and by the time the read-time flush runs the new frame IS in `frames`, so the resilient sweep picks it up. JVM-only (CLJS is single-threaded).

NOT YET REPRODUCED. Read off the code while fixing the neighbouring defect; it needs the same treatment rf2-9c2jf got — an executable barrier reproduction FIRST (park a thread between the seal and the upsert; the frame/*upsert-decide-probe* linearization seam used by frame_upsert_linearization_jvm_test.clj may already give the parking spot), then a fix, then the reproduction kept as a committed regression test. If it does NOT reproduce, close it saying why.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not a ruling: options include re-reading the source store (or re-checking the dirty flag) after upsert-frame! and reprojecting the just-created frame if the pool moved; or marking dirty unconditionally on the make-frame path so the frame's first resolution flushes. Prefer whichever keeps mark-dirty-and-schedule!'s no-image-loaded-frame skip intact — that skip is a real hot-path win (every reg-event/reg-sub/reg-fx fires the hook).

GATES, per the rf2-9c2jf precedent: core is source-scanned as text by egress_chokepoint_conformance_test.clj, so run BOTH postures — clojure -M:test and bash scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh — plus clojure -M:test:slow-test for the ^:stress lane.
close_reason: Closed

title: The app template's scaffold READMEs teach schema validation as a production guard (four claims across two files)
description:
Found by the rf2-byexd/rf2-pn648 sweep (PR #7175), which was fenced out of tools/**. Same ruling: rf2-bkvu5 (a). This one matters more than its priority suggests for the same reason spec/Construction-Prompts.md did — the template README is what a developer reads while STARTING a real app, so an unqualified claim here is how the misunderstanding gets manufactured at scale.

SITES (all under tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/):
  _shared/README_with_ssr.md
  - :103-104 — 'The default projector maps :rf.error/no-such-handler -> 404, client-input schema failures -> 400, and everything else -> a locked generic 500.' The 400 arm is dev-only (the category rides trace/emit-error!). Worth splitting the 404 too: per spec/011 SSSubstrate the :kind :route URL miss survives hardening; :rf.error/no-such-route does not.
  - :123 — 'a recognised-but-unhonourable config never silently degrades your intended 404/400 mappings into a 500.'
  - :218 — 'On the server the SSR error projector (above) maps those trace events onto sanitised HTTP-response shapes', where 'those trace events' is :214's list, which LEADS with 'schema violation'.
  - The file's only elision note (:234, 'schema validation elides automatically under :advanced goog.DEBUG=false release builds') sits ~110 lines away in a different section, is attached to app-db writes, and is never connected to the projector claim.

  root/README.md
  - :371-375 — 'The framework validates every write against the registered schemas; a non-conforming write rolls back the :db effect and emits :rf.error/schema-validation-failure. The error then flows through the error sink above — wrong writes are caught at the boundary, not N renders downstream.' 'The error sink above' is the PRODUCTION error-reporting section, so this tells a scaffold user their production monitoring will see schema violations. It will not. The correction at :427 is 56 lines later, is phrased as a bundle-COST fact ('registrations stay in source but cost nothing in production hot paths'), and never says the check does not run.

The fix is the same everywhere: keep the registration (it is genuinely wanted — it documents the slice and (rf/app-schemas) is what tools and agents read), say plainly that a production build registers and does not check, and point at the handler branch + :rf.schema/at-boundary as the seams that survive.

MODEL THE FIX ON: spec/Pattern-FormAction.md SSValidation is the handler's job; the spec/Construction-Prompts.md paragraph and the docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md paragraph added in PR #7175.

FENCE: tools/template/** only. Change no code. Note the template ships to real users — check whether a tools-SHA bump obligation applies (cf. rf2-7uxkt).
