title: docs/ssr/concepts.md promises a production 400 from the SSR error projector's schema arm
description:
Found by the rf2-byexd/rf2-pn648 sweep (PR #7175), which owned docs/api/** but not docs/ssr/. Same ruling: rf2-bkvu5 (a) — schema validation is a development-only assertion, and :rf.error/schema-validation-failure rides the dev-gated trace/emit-error!, so the projector's 400 arm is silent in a release build.

SITES:
  - docs/ssr/concepts.md:310 — 'The framework ships a default projector that maps the obvious cases — a routing miss to 404 :not-found, a *client-surface* schema-validation failure to 400 :bad-request, anything else to 500 :internal-error.' This is the SSR concept page's canonical statement of the projector contract, and it is where a reader forms the belief that bad client payloads get a 400 from the framework. Nothing in SSWhen the server throws (lines ~302-341) qualifies it.
  - docs/ssr/concepts.md:332 — 'A projected 4xx (a routing miss, a bad-input 400, an auth 401/403) is the app *working correctly*' compounds it by naming the bad-input 400 as a normal production outcome.
  - docs/ssr/concepts.md:334 — the section's only dev/prod sentence is about :ssr {:dev-error-detail? true}, which reads as 'production just loses the :details key' and so actively reinforces the wrong belief. Whatever wording lands should sit near this, not far from it.

Also worth a word while in the area: the 404 half. Per spec/011 SSSubstrate, :rf.error/no-such-handler (including the :kind :route URL miss) survives production hardening but :rf.error/no-such-route does not — it is caller misuse of route-url and dev-gated. PR #7175 split the two in docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md; concepts.md says 'a routing miss' without distinguishing them, which is defensible but could be sharpened.

SECONDARY, LOW PRIORITY (fold in only if cheap): docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md:17 calls the Malli schema 'the validation resolver ... that guards the slice', and :44 repeats 'here it guards what may be written into app-db'. The page corrects itself thoroughly at :73, :117 and :398, so a reader who continues gets the truth — but :17 sits inside a 'Coming from React Hook Form or Formik?' box a skimming React developer may read alone, and 'resolver' is that ecosystem's exact word for a PRODUCTION validator. A word swap, not a rewrite; drop it if it complicates the diff.

MODEL THE FIX ON: spec/Pattern-FormAction.md SSValidation is the handler's job (the handler guards and ships; the schema declares and vanishes), and the paragraph PR #7175 added under docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's default-error-projector-fn.

FENCE: docs/ssr/** (+ optionally the one line in docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md). Change no code.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (ruling), rf2-byexd (the pass that found this).

title: The SSR 400 for schema-validation-failure is dev-only — correct docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md and the ssr example README
description:
Remainder of rf2-cojqr's list (docs/api + examples were outside its spec/009 + EP-0027 fence), PLUS a correction to cojqr's own premise, which rf2-eane2's investigation showed to be wrong.

COJQR'S PREMISE IS TOO GENEROUS. rf2-cojqr describes docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:414 as 'Not false (the :where :event case IS production-reachable via :rf.schema/at-boundary)'. It is NOT reachable, on the SSR projection path. The at-boundary interceptor emits its failure through trace/emit-error! (implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc:246), which opens with (when interop/debug-enabled? ...) — and implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:305-309 says so in as many words: the trace-cb listener 'covers the :rf.error/* categories that fire through trace/emit-error!: :rf.error/no-such-handler, :rf.error/no-such-route, :rf.error/schema-validation-failure, :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded. They elide under interop/debug-enabled? = false.' The always-on error-emit listener carries only the promoted 500-class categories.

So the 400-for-schema-validation-failure arm of the default error projector NEVER fires in a release build, by any route. The doc site needs a plain statement of that, not the softer 'only when :where is :event' qualification cojqr proposed.

SITES:
  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:414 — ':rf.error/schema-validation-failure -> 400 :bad-request, but only when the failure :where tag is :event.' Add: this arm is fed by the dev-gated trace stream and is silent in a production build; a server that must answer 400 emits [:rf.server/set-status 400] from the handler. Cross-ref spec/Pattern-FormAction SSValidation is the handler's job (landing under rf2-eane2).
  - examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/README.md:118-121 — 'the [:articles] schema is registered explicitly against EACH frame at its entry point, so the server commit and the client commit VALIDATE AGAINST THE SAME CONTRACT.' Both commits validate in dev; under a production server build neither does. The symmetry claim is the point of the paragraph and survives — it is the same registered contract on both sides — so this is a qualification, not a rewrite.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK, same file as cojqr's spec/009 work: spec/009-Instrumentation.md's SSEmit-gate summary table has a row ':rf.error/* (run-level) | always-on | every run error'. The enumeration that follows correctly omits :rf.error/schema-validation-failure, but the :rf.error/* glob in the left column invites the opposite reading. Not touched by rf2-cojqr, which was scoped to the :rolled-back wording.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (RULED (a)), rf2-cojqr (parent sweep), rf2-eane2 (where the premise was disproved), rf2-mwv4e (the framework-side finding behind it).
close_reason: Closed

title: spec/Conventions and spec/Construction-Prompts prescribe reg-app-schema with no dev-only caveat
description:
Remainder of rf2-eane2's sibling list — these two files were outside that bead's fence (it owned spec/Pattern-*.md). Same class as the sites PR #7166 and rf2-eane2 fixed: guidance that reads reg-app-schema as a standing guarantee when it is a development-time assertion elided from production (rf2-bkvu5 RULED (a); Spec 010 SSProduction builds).

  - spec/Conventions.md:323 — 'reg-app-schema | the registrar name itself (THE VALIDATOR *IS* THE REGISTRATION)'. That parenthetical is precisely the conflation the elision breaks: the registration happens in every build, the validation does not. Worth a few words rather than a rewrite — the row is about NAMING, and the naming claim is fine; it is the gloss that overreaches.
  - spec/Construction-Prompts.md:638 — '(rf/reg-app-schema [:feature] FeatureSchema)' as a REQUIRED per-feature artefact row, no caveat. This one matters more than its priority suggests: Construction-Prompts is read by agents CONSTRUCTING apps, so an unqualified REQUIRED row is how the misunderstanding gets manufactured at scale. The row should stay required (registration is genuinely wanted — tools and agents introspect it) and say what it does and does not buy.

BOTH ARE HOT-ZONE (spec/Conventions.md especially). Sequence against other spec/Conventions work; the edits are small enough to ride with an adjacent bead touching the same file.

title: Arm cljs_prod for implementation/freehand/* — Freehand now carries an -elision-prod-test suite the PR gate skips
description:
Found while answering rf2-3slzz (PR #7171). The trigger the classifier's own comment names has arrived.

.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, the `implementation/freehand/*` case, deliberately does NOT arm cljs_prod, and says why:

    # Still NOT cljs_prod / bundle_isolation / ui_gates / ui_smoke: no
    # bundle those gates measure requires Freehand (cljs_prod builds the
    # `elision-probe` pair, bundle_isolation the examples set), and Freehand
    # mounts no testbed those smokes drive. Widen each the moment that
    # changes — the `implementation/ui/*` case above is the worked
    # precedent.

That premise is now false for cljs_prod. PR #7171 adds
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/reactive_false_check_elision_prod_test.cljs — the FIRST Freehand suite whose namespace matches the `-elision-prod-test$` regex, so the FIRST Freehand code that rides the `:browser-test-prod-elision` build (`:advanced` + `{goog.DEBUG false}`, runner re-frame.prod-elision-runner). The file is on the build's classpath already (freehand/test is in the global :source-paths), and it passes locally — 120 tests / 526 assertions, exit 0. What it does NOT have is a PR-time trigger: on a Freehand-only PR, cljs_prod stays false and the cljs-browser-prod-elision job SKIPS. Observed on #7171: that job reported "skipping" while cljs-browser passed.

This is exactly the false-green shape rf2-drpa3.58 / .61 / .70 closed one tier at a time for the same tree — a suite that rides a build nobody triggers.

EXPOSURE IS BOUNDED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS P2 AND NOT P1: expensive-tests.yml runs `npm run test:browser-prod-elision` unconditionally on the nightly cron, so the suite does execute on main. The gap is PR-time only — a Freehand change that breaks the production posture of the read check merges green and surfaces the next morning.

FIX: add `cljs_prod=true` to the `implementation/freehand/*` case in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, and replace the "Still NOT cljs_prod" paragraph with the reason it is now armed (Freehand carries an `-elision-prod-test` suite). The `implementation/ui/*` case is the worked precedent the comment already points at. Widen, never narrow — a POSIX `case` takes the FIRST match, and the two narrower Freehand cases above (freehand_evidence_elision, freehand_reachability) SHADOW this one, so they need the same line if a prod-elision suite could be invalidated by their inputs too (evidence.cljc / cell.cljc / shell.cljs are inputs to the new suite's subject matter — cell.cljc especially, since the check under test lives there).

Add a row to implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs pinning it, in the shape of the existing cljs_prod assertions.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ON #7171: .github/** and scripts/** were outside that worker's fence.

EVIDENCE: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (the `implementation/freehand/*` case and its "Widen each the moment that changes" note); .github/workflows/test.yml:2721 (the job's `if: needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_prod == 'true'`); .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml:108 (the unconditional nightly backstop); PR #7171.
notes: SIBLING GAP, SAME CLASS, SAME FILE — worth folding into the same change. test.yml carries production-gate JVM jobs (-Dre-frame.debug=false) for CORE and ROUTING only; there is no 'JVM freehand under the production gate' job. The Freehand artefact's own suites therefore never run under the JVM prod posture at PR time. rf2-3slzz's probe (reactive-false-totality-jvm-test) is written to be posture-agnostic and passes under both -Dre-frame.debug postures locally — it reads System/getProperty and asserts the live interop/debug-enabled? matches, so the second run is demonstrably the production posture rather than the same one twice — but CI only ever runs the dev one. Pre-existing, not introduced by #7171; noted here because the fix is one more job in the same workflow as this bead's one-line classifier widening, and because the {:reactive false} check (rf2-oxlpy) is precisely a safety mechanism whose production behaviour is the thing under test.
close_reason: PR #7177: implementation/freehand/* now arms cljs_prod (plus both shadowing cases, cell.cljc + freehand.cljc). Proven: classifier false→true on 5 real Freehand paths, prose stays false; the armed job's exact command (npm run test:browser-prod-elision) exits 0 with 120 tests / 526 assertions, and the :advanced bundle carries re-frame.freehand.reactive-false-check-elision-prod-test and all four of its deftests. Nothing turned red. Sweep: Freehand was the ONLY artefact with the hole — every other tree carrying an -elision-prod-test namespace already armed cljs_prod on src and test. Pinned in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs (275 passed) + TESTING.md. Sibling JVM prod-gate gap from the NOTES filed as rf2-8alkj.

title: Clojars verified-group policy blocks the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* tool coordinate
description:
Surfaced by rf2-2ii52 (ruling caveat, deliberately not solved inside the vendoring PR).

Vendoring day8/de-dupe fixed the DEPENDENCY GRAPH for day8/re-frame2-mcp-base and
day8/re-frame2-story-mcp — both now generate a complete pom, and PR #7169 wires their
deploy jobs onto the existing story-v* glob. It did NOT make the coordinates CLAIMABLE.

THE POLICY. Clojars requires NEW projects to live in a *verified* group, and verification
requires a reverse-domain group name. `day8` is not reverse-domain, so it cannot be
verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a NEW project may
not be created. This is not theoretical: day8/de-dupe's own tag-triggered publish workflow
ran on 2026-05-13 and received a 403 — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new
projects". That 403 is the reason route (a) (publish de-dupe) was ruled out.

THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TWO NEW JARS. The same rule applies to EVERY day8/re-frame2-*
coordinate that has never been published — which, as far as anyone has checked, is all of
them: the thirteen implementation/ artefacts as well as the five tool jars. If the day8
group cannot take new projects, then no v* tag can cut a first release either, and the
whole release pipeline is gated on this rather than on any code.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (Mike's, not a worker's):
  1. Does day8's Clojars standing permit new projects today? (An older group may have been
     grandfathered, or the account may hold a verified group already — VERIFY against
     Clojars rather than inferring from the 2026-05-13 403, which was a different group
     path.) If yes, nothing to do: tag and publish.
  2. If no: the artefacts need a verified reverse-domain group — io.github.day8/* is the
     obvious candidate, verifiable via the GitHub org. That renames EVERY published
     coordinate, which touches deps.edn :clein/build :lib for 18 artefacts, the lockstep
     gate, every release workflow's rewrite + preflight, docs/release-process.md, the
     template's pins, CHANGELOG, and every consumer-facing usage snippet in the repo.

VERIFY BEFORE TAGGING ANYTHING. Clojars has no yank, and a half-published set at a given
VERSION is recovered only by bump-and-supersede.

Flagged in .github/workflows/release-story.yml's header and docs/release-process.md
\u00a7How story-mcp and mcp-base got their publish path.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): recorded 2026-07-28 07:48 AUSEST from ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, reconciled; the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD).

DECISION, in three parts:
(1) VERIFICATION-FIRST SEQUENCING STANDS, but the canary-by-tag route is REJECTED as the verification instrument (Codex position, adopted). Mike's authoritative act is the zero-mutation one: verify io.github.day8 via Clojars' self-service GitHub-org proof (see MIKE'S ACT below), optionally glancing at day8's standing from his logged-in account or asking Clojars support as belt-and-braces.
(2) RULED FALLBACK GROUP if day8 is blocked (and the evidence below says it is): io.github.day8 for ALL 18 Maven coordinates, moved in ONE sequenced rename campaign BEFORE anything publishes.
(3) NO-TAG RULE: NO v*, story-v*, xray-v*, or machines-viz-v* tag is pushed until this bead resolves (io.github.day8 badge confirmed + rename campaign merged + lockstep/preflight/release-DAG gates green on the new coordinates). This is STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut-time checklist, ahead of its existing step 1 (credentials); rf2-2ii52 step 3 (manual first publish of mcp-base/story-mcp) is equally blocked on it.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMITS (three independent sources; two re-verified from primary sources 2026-07-28):
- The 2026-05-13 403 on day8/de-dupe's tag-triggered publish — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects" — is real but was a DIFFERENT project path; on its own it is suggestive, not conclusive (the bead itself warns against inferring from it alone).
- Clojars' Verified Group Names wiki (fetched 2026-07-28): since 2021-04-18 "creating new libraries in non-verified groups will be disabled", while "the group does not need to be verified for new versions" of EXISTING libraries. Bare `day8` is neither reverse-domain nor a githost-org pattern, so it is STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE — there is no route to a verified bare day8, and seeking a policy exception would couple every release to an exception Clojars explicitly designed away.
- clojars.org/users/mikethompson (fetched 2026-07-28): `day8` is listed WITHOUT the verified badge; only net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson carry it. Codex traced the badge to find-group-verification in clojars-web's web/user.clj (not cosmetic) and the enforcement to check-group+project in db.clj: an unverified group is accepted ONLY when that exact group/artifact pair already exists; a new artifact is rejected as group-non-verified.
- All 18 intended day8/* coordinates 404 on Clojars (re-verified 2026-07-27, per-coordinate) — every one is a NEW project as far as Clojars is concerned, so every one enters the rejected branch. The day8 group page returning 200 with mikethompson permitted proves only maintenance rights over existing projects, not creation rights.
- LIMIT: what stays unobservable read-only is Mike's account-side view and any bespoke admin exception. That residual is why this bead stays with Mike — but it is small, and it does not justify a canary.

VERIFICATION ROUTES WEIGHED (canary trade-offs recorded):
- (a) Account/settings check or asking Clojars admins: zero-risk, zero-mutation. Fine as belt-and-braces; not required given (c).
- (b) Canary publish by pushing the ready machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha tag: REJECTED as a probe. A 403 merely re-demonstrates documented policy at the cost of a burned tag-push cycle; a surprise success is an IMMUTABLE public act that permanently pins machines-viz to day8/* — either splitting the family when the rest moves, or accidentally committing the whole family to an unverifiable legacy group. Never use an immutable registry operation to learn an observable fact; if state might have changed, re-read the profile/API or ask support instead. (The primary analysis's "nothing is wasted on success" framing undercounts this: success is exactly the outcome that forecloses the group decision.)
- (c) The act that actually advances things — verify io.github.day8 NOW: create the empty public repo github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group while logged in as mikethompson, confirm the badge appears. Cheap, self-service, and harmless even in the unlikely event day8 turns out grandfathered (verifying a group publishes nothing). It doubles as the authoritative test: Clojars' own flow granting io.github.day8 while day8 stays unverified closes the question.

FALLBACK GROUP CHOICE (io.github.day8), alternatives weighed:
- io.github.day8 — CHOSEN. GitHub-org-verifiable self-service; matches the existing in-repo precedent io.github.day8/re-frame2-template; expresses the durable owner users already see (the day8 GitHub org).
- com.github.day8 — the verification flow verifies both com. and io. simultaneously, but io. is the cleaner match to the existing precedent. Publish under ONE only — Clojars itself warns that the same library under two group IDs can put both on a classpath.
- au.com.day8 — DNS-TXT-verifiable via day8.com.au; defensible if Day8 deliberately wants DNS (not GitHub) as the permanent package identity, but it adds a separate DNS proof and stewardship path, has zero consumer precedent, and buys no ergonomics.
- net.clojars.mikethompson — already verified and usable today, but makes organisation-owned libraries look personally owned. Rejected.
- Policy exception for bare day8 — structurally impossible (not reverse-domain) and bad posture even if grantable. Rejected.

WHY DECIDE BEFORE FIRST PUBLISH (irreversibility): Clojars has no yank; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is immutable. Any rename AFTER a first publish leaves permanently orphaned day8/* coordinates and creates the two-groups-one-library classpath hazard. The current all-404 state — pre-alpha, zero consumers — is the cheapest this move will ever be.

RENAME BLAST RADIUS (one sequenced hot-zone campaign, NOT parallel work; coordinate work ONLY):
- :clein/build :lib in all 18 publishable deps.edn (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), plus the internal cross-artefact dependency maps the :local/root rewrite resolves (31 in-repo coordinates inventoried by the lockstep gate).
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh (inventories + assertions).
- Release workflows and their scripts: release.yml (13-coordinate DAG + generated-POM assertions), release-story.yml (mcp-base -> story -> story-mcp ordering), release-machines-viz.yml, .github/scripts/rewrite-in-repo-coords.sh, preflight-tool-package.sh, preflight-story-package.sh.
- docs/release-process.md; CHANGELOG (its roster is gate-pinned to the publishable-runtimes authority); migration guide dep edits; every consumer-facing usage snippet; the setup skill; the template's emitted coordinates (tools/template — interacts with rf2-57bjg, whose template-coordinate fix should land on the NEW group).
- The pre-staged rf2-snjn5 docs-flip PR #7167 (8 sites teaching day8/* coords) must be RE-CUT on the new group.
- day8/reagent-slim — the one deliberately off-pattern coordinate (publication-time rename) — becomes io.github.day8/reagent-slim; give it its final eyeball in the same pass.
- Credentials: the planned group-scoped reusable Clojars deploy token must be scoped to io.github.day8, not day8 (rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist step 1 wording changes accordingly).
- EXPLICIT NON-SCOPE (Clojars documents that the Maven group does not constrain Clojure namespaces): NO Clojure namespace renames, NO repo URL changes, NO npm @day8 scope change.

INTERACTIONS: this bead is now STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut checklist (cross-ref appended there) — its steps 3 (404 re-probe: probe the NEW coordinates), 4/6 (PR #7167 re-cut) and 1 (token group scope) all shift under this ruling. rf2-2ii52's remaining step 3 (manual first publish per release-machines-viz.yml's header protocol) proceeds only after this resolves, on io.github.day8 coordinates.

MIKE'S ACT (why this stays OPEN and assigned to him): 1. create the empty public repo day8/clojars-mikethompson; 2. submit https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson at clojars.org/verify/group as mikethompson; 3. confirm io.github.day8 shows the verified badge (optionally also glance at day8's standing / ask support); 4. say go — the rename campaign is then worker-dispatchable as one sequenced campaign, and this bead closes when the badge is confirmed AND the campaign is merged with gates green.
RUNBOOK CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-28): Codex second-opinion review of the operator runbook (ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md, written 2026-07-28 16:36 AUSEST) CONCURS with the morning RULING on every decision point — io.github.day8 destination, canary-by-tag rejected, no-tag rule, verification-first sequencing, and the group-alternatives weighing all match. No contradictions; this is a consolidation, not a re-ruling. It adds the following NEW verified mechanics the ruling did not yet carry. The dossier file is deleted after this note — this note is the canonical record of its Codex section.

(1) VERIFY-FORM MECHANICS (verified against clojars-web verification.clj, 2026-07-28): the clojars.org/verify/group flow's GitHub/GitLab repository section takes the FULL proof-repo URL (https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson) — the form does NOT ask for the group name. It accepts exactly https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<clojars-user>, checks the public repo exists, and creates/verifies BOTH com.github.day8 AND io.github.day8 in one act. Publish under io.github.day8 as the ONE public Maven identity (per the ruling; never both). KEEP THE PROOF REPO PUBLIC PERMANENTLY — it is the standing evidence of org control, not a one-shot token. (As of the 2026-07-28 check, github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson returned 404 — the verification act has not yet happened.)

(2) TOKEN ORDER (inserts a step between MIKE'S ACT and the rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist's credentials step): create or replace the CI deploy token scoped to io.github.day8 only AFTER verification — Clojars does not allow a group-scoped token before the group exists (Deploy-Tokens wiki, Scoping). Verification usefully creates the group before any artifact exists, which is what makes the scoped token mintable at all. Sequence: badge confirmed -> mint io.github.day8-scoped token -> cut checklist step 1 (credentials) proceeds with that token, never a bare-day8-scoped one.

(3) ENFORCEMENT CONFIRMATION: current clojars-web db.clj check-group+project structurally confirms the ruling's reading — it first accepts an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair, then rejects a NEW artifact when the group has no verification record. Existing day8 projects therefore do NOT grandfather any new day8/re-frame2-* artifact.

(4) CAMPAIGN COMPLETION CRITERION (tightens the ruling's "gates green" close condition): a hand-written file roster is NOT a safe completion criterion — an exact-token scan (2026-07-28 snapshot) found ~428 candidate references to the 18 published coordinates across hundreds of tracked files, and the repo is still moving, so the count itself must not be relied on. Required instead: a structural re-scan at campaign START and again at COMPLETION; then generate and INSPECT all deploy POMs, proving every in-family GAV uses io.github.day8 at the lockstep version with NO old-group dependency (a partial migration can publish a valid jar whose POM points at an old-group coordinate that will never exist); plus verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test, the normal lockstep gate, the release-script policy tests, and each tool/package preflight — ALL green before the tag freeze lifts. Re-cut any staged documentation change (PR #7167) against the new group from the same structural inventory.

(5) COORDINATE-SPECIFIC FENCE (sharpens the ruling's explicit non-scope): NO repository-wide day8 -> io.github.day8 text replacement. GitHub org URLs, @day8 npm packages, Clojure namespace names, and ordinary prose about the Day8 organisation do not change. Any RETAINED legacy day8/* Maven coordinate must be an intentional historical example or negative test, and explicitly allowlisted as such.

title: ssr-conformance-test: pe-check sources the error event from the DEV bus, so BOTH public-error fixtures report nil under the production gate
description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-27 under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, AFTER rf2-ov56u landed the route-miss promotion.

THE RULING'S EXPECTATION WAS HALF RIGHT. rf2-rqje9 recorded that `ssr-conformance-test`'s blocking fixture `:ssr/error-known-mapping` would "clear with rf2-ov56u", while its sibling `:ssr/error-sanitisation` failed independently. It does NOT clear. Both fixtures fail for the SAME runner-side reason, and rf2-ov56u could not have fixed either.

THE MECHANISM. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj` ~753, the `:ssr/public-error` check:

    pe-check
    (when expected-pe
      (let [error-events (filter #(= :error (:op-type %)) @traces)
            last-error   (last error-events)]
        (if last-error
          (let [actual (ssr/project-error :rf/default last-error)] ...)
          {:expected expected-pe :actual nil :passed? false})))

`@traces` is the DEV trace bus. Under the gate it is empty for every fixture, so `last-error` is nil and `pe-check` reports `:actual nil` WHATEVER the framework did. The projector itself is fine under the gate (`re-frame.ssr-error-projector-substrate-test` is in-lane and green), and the framework behaviour `:ssr/error-known-mapping` is ABOUT — a route miss projecting 404 in production — is now separately proven in-lane by `re-frame.ssr-route-miss-404-production-test` (rf2-ov56u).

MEASURED under the gate after rf2-ov56u:
  :ssr/error-known-mapping  - public-error expected {:status 404 ...} actual nil
  :ssr/error-sanitisation   - public-error expected {:status 500 ...} actual nil
Both ALSO carry a `:trace-emissions` `:rf.event/run-start` claim, which is the ordinary rf2-lwtlk posture split and is shared with seven further fixtures.

THE FIX (the rf2-7vk3z shape). Re-source `pe-check` from the ALWAYS-ON axis: register a `re-frame.error-emit` listener alongside the trace listener the runner already installs, and prefer its record — synthesised into the `{:operation :op-type :tags}` envelope exactly as `error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener` does — when `@traces` is empty. Both categories involved are always-on today (`:rf.error/handler-exception` via `dispatch-on-error!`, `:rf.error/no-such-handler` `:kind :route` via `dispatch-error-record!`), so both fixtures then adjudicate the real production path rather than a dev artefact.

SCOPE. This clears the public-error half of two fixtures. It does NOT clear the namespace: nine fixtures fail the `:trace-emissions` claim, which is rf2-lwtlk group (c)'s posture split. The `re-frame.ssr-conformance-test` roster line in `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` comes off when both are done. This bead depends on no ruling and may land first or alongside.

The roster comment block in `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` already records this verification (PR #7168) so the next reader does not chase it as a framework regression.
close_reason: PR #7174: pe-check now sources from the always-on :errors axis with the projector's envelope; :ssr/error-known-mapping and :ssr/error-sanitisation both clear under the gate (mutation-proved). re-frame.ssr-conformance-test off the prod-gate roster.

title: spec/009 and EP-0027 describe :rolled-back / post-commit schema rollback as production-reachable
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-bkvu5's doc pass. rf2-bkvu5 fixed the two IMPLEMENTATION docstrings that carry this defect (re-frame.event-emit ns docstring and router.cljc's outcome enum, both now say the outcome has no producer in a production build). The spec-side and EP-side statements were outside that bead's fence — spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot-zone and EP-0027 is not EP-0025 — so they are filed here.

THE DEFECT. :rolled-back is one of four values on the ALWAYS-ON, production-survivable :events listener stream. Its producer — app-db candidate schema validation — is dev-only. So the enum reads as production-reachable and is not: in a release build a candidate that violates a registered schema simply installs and the dispatch reports :ok. A consumer wiring production observability will read a quiet :rolled-back metric as 'no schema violations', which is quiet by construction.

SITES:
  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1217 — the strongest framing. Introduces the substrate as 'a small ALWAYS-ON event-emit substrate ... that is NOT gated by re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?' and then enumerates ':rolled-back (candidate :db / machine-data schema validation REJECTED the transition BEFORE install per 010 §Per-step recovery row 4 ...)' with no note that this member alone has no production producer.
  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md:566 — ':rf.event/run-end ;; run-tail — fires LAST, with the always-on event-emit record's :outcome :rolled-back'.

SEPARATE, AND ALSO STALE:
  - docs/EP/EP-0027-frame-initial-events.md:95 — 'rides the NORMAL POST-COMMIT app-db schema validation / ROLLBACK like any :db effect.' Two defects in one clause: (a) it reads as unconditional when the check is dev-only, and (b) 'post-commit ... rollback' is the RETIRED pre-rf2-uhk9ko model — the contract has been validate-BEFORE-install with no write-pair since rf2-uhk9ko. The same stale wording was found and corrected in implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc by rf2-bkvu5; EP-0027 is the remaining copy.

LOW PRIORITY, same sweep:
  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:414 — ':rf.error/schema-validation-failure -> 400 :bad-request, but only when the failure :where tag is :event.' Not false (the :where :event case IS production-reachable via :rf.schema/at-boundary) but nothing says that is the only way it fires in production, so a reader assumes ordinary event-schema validation reaches it.
  - examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/README.md:118-121 — 'the [:articles] schema is registered explicitly against EACH frame at its entry point, SO THE SERVER COMMIT AND THE CLIENT COMMIT VALIDATE AGAINST THE SAME CONTRACT.' Asserts both commits validate; under a production server build neither does.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (RULED option (a)) and rf2-uhk9ko (validate-before-install).

title: no-such-fx always-on record omits :failing-id (the unknown fx-id)
notes:
Found while splitting fx-test for rf2-d2841 (prod-gate lane).

Spec 009 states the attribution rule as: "every always-on error record carries
`:failing-id <kw>` naming the failing COMPONENT's own code identifier whenever
that component is DISTINCT from (or more specific than) the dispatched event"
(009-Instrumentation.md ~L1230, §Observability channels / §Component attribution).

`:rf.error/no-such-fx` is catalogued ALWAYS-ON (009 L2150). Its emit site —
implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc ~L1623 — builds the trace-payload as

    {:rf.fx/id fx-id :rf.fx/args args :frame frame-id :recovery :no-recovery}

with NO :failing-id. `error-emit/emit-error-both!` lifts :failing-id/:reason
onto the always-on record ONLY when :failing-id is present and differs from
:event-id, so nothing is lifted: the production record is
{:error :rf.error/no-such-fx :event :event-id :frame :time :exception :elapsed-ms}
and an off-box shipper learns an fx was missing but NOT WHICH ONE. The fx-id
rides only :rf.fx/id on the DCE'd dev-trace tags.

  * :rf.error/fx-handler-exception (fx.cljc ~L1447, :failing-id fx-id)
  * :rf.error/override-fallthrough (fx.cljc ~L1060/1075/1087, :failing-id original-fx-id)
  * :rf.error/reserved-fx-override (fx.cljc ~L988, :failing-id fx-id)
so no-such-fx is the lone outlier, not a deliberate carve-out.

Same shape as rf2-mlh1h. Remedy is one key in the fx.cljc trace-payload
(:failing-id fx-id); the lift is automatic from there. Verified under the real
gate: implementation/core/test/re_frame/fx_test.clj

title: spec/006: invariant 5's justification names only the headless retained case — the staged case is stronger
description:
HOT ZONE, filed rather than edited (rf2-anmdr).

Spec 006 §The six frozen invariants, invariant 5 justifies the comparison in ONE direction:

  'On a non-watchable headless host a retained site has no value-movement watch, so this
   comparison is its only correction — a staged-only comparison would leave a retained
   site's headless movement caught by nothing.'

That defends the RETAINED half against a staged-only shortcut, and it is correct. It is also
narrower than the guarantee, and it leaves the worse failure undefended in prose: on a
WATCHABLE host a STAGED site has no watch either, because obs/acquire! installs that site's
watch DURING the commit that needed it — after the move. A retained site whose commit skips
the comparison self-heals one window later when its (earlier-installed) watch fires; a staged
site never heals at all.

Measured by rf2-so3io's ablation on a watchable browser host, now pinned by
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/shell_tear_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-anmdr):

  site      commit    revision advanced?  cell dirty?  published
  retained  shipped   yes                 no           FRESH
  retained  ablated   no                  YES          stale
  staged    shipped   yes                 no           FRESH
  staged    ablated   no                  NO           stale

Nothing in the shipped behaviour contradicts the spec — this is a justification gap, not a
behaviour gap. Suggested: add a sentence to invariant 5 saying the comparison is ALSO a
staged site's only correction on a watchable host, so a reader cannot conclude the guarantee
is a headless-only concession.
close_reason: Prose-only widening of invariant 5's rationale in spec/006 (commit b9f1a5e328): names the staged case on a watchable host, states why it is the stronger failure (a retained site self-heals one window later, a staged site never corrects), and cross-references the shipped rows in shell_cljs_test.cljc (PR #7143, retained) and shell_tear_dom_cljs_test.cljs (PR #7160, staged). No normative statement, invariant wording, or conformance requirement changed. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

title: bench: measure the narrow-write leg on the REAGENT substrate — the spine's scheduler term does not apply there
description:
FROM rf2-jr76s. The bead's framing says the 457 KB write leg 'is paid on every interaction in every re-frame application'. That needs qualifying and nobody has the arm that would settle it.

WHAT IS SUBSTRATE-INDEPENDENT: the SHAPE. A one-cell write marks every layer-1 subscription in the frame dirty and re-evaluates all of them, because a layer-1 reg-sub body is an opaque fn of the whole app-db and the graph holds no path. That is intrinsic and universal (rf2-jr76s SS-2).

WHAT IS NOT: the BYTES. The measured figure came from the b6 Freehand arm running the UIx adapter, i.e. re-frame.substrate.spine's make-react-spine, whose epoch scheduler is re-frame's OWN. make-scheduler is called from exactly one place (spine.cljs make-react-spine) and serves UIx, Freehand and the in-tree re-frame.ui substrate. Reagent and reagent-slim go through make-ratom-spine — bare reset! onto an r/atom, Reagent's own make-reaction, Reagent's own batching — and pay NONE of the scheduler term that was 60% of the pre-fix per-subscription cost.

Reagent is FIRST-CLASS and actively supported, so 'what does a narrow write cost a Reagent-substrate re-frame app' is the question most consumers actually have, and it is unanswered.

THE ARM. reagent.ratom works headless (no DOM needed for r/atom + make-reaction), so this can ride the existing node harness: build a second adapter through spine/make-ratom-spine with reagent.ratom's r-atom / make-reaction injected and the render fns stubbed, register the same N layer-1 subs, and measure.

ONE METHOD TRAP TO RESPECT: on Reagent the recompute does NOT land in the write leg. replace-container! is a bare reset!; the reactions re-run on Reagent's flush. B6's Reagent arm accordingly does its work in the FORCE leg (reagent.core/flush inside flushSync), which is exactly the point B8 makes when it says the legs are not comparable arm-to-arm and only their SUM is. So the Reagent arm must measure write+flush together, or it will report a flatteringly small write leg that means nothing.

Harness to extend: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs (rf2-jr76s), which already has the ladder, the controls and the both-orders discipline.

title: RULING NEEDED: subscribe's cache-HIT path pays a dynamic binding it never uses - but the wrapper also carries the read-time reprojection flush
description:
OPERATOR-GRADE. Not attempted by the rf2-j8ls2 worker BY DESIGN: it
trades an EP-0023 coherence guarantee for allocation, and that is a
ruling, not an optimisation.

MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000%):

  call-with-frame-resolution, whole      720 - 800 B/call
    the dynamic `binding` alone          ~760 B  (N-BINDONLY 752-808)
    flush consult + generation read + thunk call  16 - 40 B

That binding is 41% of `subscribe`'s pre-fix per-call allocation and
~46% of its post-fix figure -- the single largest remaining term on the
JVM.

THE OBSERVATION. `subscribe`'s cache-HIT branch performs NO `(kind, id)`
lookup at all: it reads `(:sub-cache frame-record)`, `(get @cache k)`,
bumps the ref-count and returns. `registrar/lookup` is called only in
`compute-and-cache!` -- the MISS path. So on a hit, the whole
`call-with-frame-resolution` wrapper, including the binding, is
established around a body that never resolves a registration.

WHY IT IS NOT A FREE WIN. `call-with-frame-resolution` also performs the
READ-TIME COALESCED FLUSH (rf2-h1vqa4): a `reg-*` since the last flush
marks the live-frame projection dirty, and the flush here is what makes
that registration visible to the very next subscribe IN THE SAME TICK.
A `reg-sub` replacement invalidates cache entries through the registrar
replacement hooks -- so skipping the flush on the HIT path can hand back
a reaction that a pending reprojection would have evicted. That is a
correctness question, not a byte question.

The flush itself measured 0 B (arm N-FLUSH; the late-bind
`get-fn-cached` consult plus the clean-projection check allocate
nothing), so the flush is NOT the cost. Only the binding is.

THE SHAPE OF A CANDIDATE, IF THE OPERATOR WANTS ONE: keep the flush
where it is and narrow only the BINDING to the branches that resolve
registrations (miss, hit-rebuild, and the CLJS dev override seam). That
preserves ALL-OR-NOTHING for every cascade that actually performs a
lookup, and leaves the hit path -- which performs none -- unbound. It
still needs a ruling because EP-0023 states the binding covers the whole
cascade, and "the hit path is not a cascade" is an interpretation.

CRITICAL CAVEAT, AND IT MAY MOOT THE WHOLE BEAD: this ~760 B is a JVM
artefact. CLJS `binding` expands through `with-redefs` to `let` + `set!`
+ try/finally restore (confirmed in cljs/core.cljc, clojurescript
1.12.145) -- ZERO allocation. A browser app pays none of it. Unless a
CLJS measurement (rf2-*, filed separately) shows a real cost there, the
honest answer may be "leave it alone; the JVM is not the target
runtime."

DO NOT dispatch this as implementation work without a ruling.

HOT-ZONE: implementation/core + spec/006 + the EP-0023 text. Sequence.
close_reason:
RULED CLOSED (Option 3) - no implementation change. Decision delegated by Mike (2026-07-27); recorded 2026-07-27 22:32 AUSEST. The cache-hit path stays inside call-with-frame-resolution; the binding of registrar/*generation* is NOT narrowed.

EP-0023 IS NOT REINTERPRETED. Its all-or-nothing rule remains exactly right for every operation that resolves registrations; the existing broader wrapper simply stays in place, with the hit path inside it. No coherence-contract text changes.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE:
(1) Original JVM decomposition (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, -Dre-frame.debug=false, 9 rounds, controls +0.000%): the binding alone ~760 B/call, ~46% of cache-hit subscribe allocation - a real JVM cost, not disputed.
(2) Independent Codex reproduction on this checkout (re-frame.bench.read-attribution, exact-size controls +0.000%): N-BINDONLY 752 B/call, N-FLUSH 0 B/call, full cache-hit subscribe 1,220 B/call. The JVM figure is solid.
(3) CLJS null result, twice over: cljs.core/binding (ClojureScript 1.12.145) expands through with-redefs to local captures + set! + try/finally restoration - no thread-binding map, no TBox, no Var$Frame, zero allocation; AND a seven-round Node microbenchmark (3M bindings/round) held bound and unbound loops within run-to-run noise (~2.6-3.0 ms) - no timing signal either. The CLJS-side datum Option 1 (hold for rf2-x0fe2) was waiting for has therefore effectively arrived: the binding term is structurally zero-cost in the target runtime, so rf2-x0fe2's harness can only ever report ~zero for this term.
(4) Architectural cost of narrowing: call-with-frame-resolution deliberately runs the reprojection flush BEFORE sampling the generation and BEFORE the cache lookup, so a same-tick reg-sub replacement can evict the old node before subscribe returns it. Any narrowing must split that one coherent flush-then-sample-then-resolve seam or duplicate part of it in subs.cljc - extra hot-zone structure (core + spec/006 + EP-0023 text) for no product-path gain.
(5) Even the JVM benefit is overstated: the persistently-held-hit benchmark shape is not the real JVM workload. subscribe-once's balanced subscribe/deref/unsubscribe lifetime disposes an otherwise-unheld entry in the same call, so ordinary SSR/tool one-shot reads are MISSES - where the generation binding is genuinely required - not the hit case this ruling would have optimised.

WHY NOT HOLD (Option 1 rejected): the hold bought nothing closing does not. The only datum rf2-x0fe2 could add for THIS bead is a byte count from the wrong execution shape, and reopening is cheap. Do not keep a decision open merely to await that.

REOPEN ONLY IF: (a) a representative optimized CLJS/browser benchmark attributes material wall-clock cost to this binding, or (b) a real JVM SSR/tool workload demonstrates persistently-held cache hits at consequential scale.

title: registrar: the generation-routed lookup allocates a [kind id] key vector per call - the exact cost its own docstring says it avoids
description:
MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000%, arms
N-LOOKGEN / N-LOOKATOM):

  registrar/lookup, generation-routed   138.3 - 138.5 B/call
  registrar/lookup, registrar-atom      40.0 B/call  (all arm overhead)

The 40 B on BOTH arms is the arm's own `(first query-v)`, which seqs the
vector. So the registrar-atom branch is ~0 B and the generation-routed
branch is ~98 B/call.

WHAT IT IS. `registrar/lookup`:

    (if-let [resolver (generation-resolver)]
      (get resolver [kind id])
      (-> @(active-registrar) (get kind) (get id)))

The generation resolver is keyed `[kind id]`, so the routed branch
builds a fresh two-element vector on every lookup. The function's own
docstring says:

    Uses paired `get` calls rather than `(get-in ... [kind id])` --
    `get-in` allocates a path vector per call, and `lookup` runs per
    dispatch (event handler), per fx (handler), and per sub (handler).

...which is exactly the cost the other branch pays. Documented intent
and implementation disagree.

WHEN IT FIRES: `*generation*` is bound whenever
`call-with-frame-resolution` targets an image-loaded frame -- and with
`make-frame` as THE one constructor, every frame carries a sealed
generation, so the generation-routed branch is the ORDINARY path, not
the exotic one. It runs per dispatch, per fx, per cofx and per
subscribe MISS.

SKETCH. Re-key the generation resolver from `{[kind id] descriptor}` to
nested `{kind {id descriptor}}`, so the routed branch becomes the same
paired `get` the atom branch already uses. The resolver is assembled in
`re-frame.image-assembly` and projected by
`registrar/kind-registrations-from-resolver`, which already walks the
`[kind id]` keys and would simplify. Cross-check `:rf.gen/resolver`
readers before touching the shape -- it is documented as plain map data
read by several call sites.

HONEST RANKING: ~98 B/call is 5% of `subscribe`'s per-call allocation
and 9% of `probe`'s pre-node lookups. Small. It is filed because it is a
documented-intent violation on a hot chokepoint, not because it is
large.

INSTRUMENT: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj,
RM_SUITE=subs, arms N-LOOKGEN / N-LOOKATOM.

JVM ONLY for the bytes; the shape (a vector built per lookup) is a
source fact and transfers.
notes:
MAYOR NOTE (2026-07-27): THE WORKER VERIFIED THE COST AND CORRECTLY STOPPED AT A SPEC FENCE. This now needs an operator ruling; do NOT dispatch it as a fix.

VERIFIED: N-LOOKGEN 138.3-138.5 B/call vs N-LOOKATOM 40.0, where the 40 B on BOTH arms is the arm's own (first query-v). So the generation-routed lookup costs ~98 B/call and the atom branch ~0 B. Reproduces exactly as filed, and it IS the cost the function's own docstring says it avoids.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED, and I endorse the stop: re-keying :rf.gen/resolver is a NORMATIVE SPEC CHANGE, not a refactor.
  - spec/API.md L808 pins {[kind id] descriptor} as one of frame-generation's FOUR DOCUMENTED STABLE PUBLIC KEYS.
  - spec/Conventions.md L59 fixes the :rf.gen/* member set as additive-by-Spec-change, so adding a nested-index key is equally a spec change.
  - The flat shape is read as PLAIN DATA by tools/xray (cross-frame [kind id] keyset comparison, documented in its spec 026), the Pair MCP runtime, tools/story, and ~50 core test assertions.
What landed instead is an honest docstring: which branch the paired-get claim actually covers, what the other branch costs, and what removing it would take.

ADJACENT FINDING the same re-key would fix: kind-registrations-from-resolver walks the WHOLE resolver on every registrations/ids call — O(n) where a nested index gives O(1).

THE RULING NEEDED: is ~98 B/call on the resolution chokepoint, plus that O(n)->O(1) query win, worth reshaping a documented public generation key?
  - If YES: it is a HOT-ZONE SEQUENCED job spanning spec/API.md + spec/Conventions.md + image assembly + registrar + tools/xray + the pair skill + tools/story + the test corpus. One worker, one lane, sequenced — not parallel.
  - If NO: close it. The docstring is now honest, which was the smaller half of the value and is already banked.

Filed at P2 rather than P1 because nothing is broken and the honest-docstring half has landed.
RULING (2026-07-27, decision DELEGATED by Mike; recorded by decision agent under the standing posture: pre-alpha masterpiece, trust the programmer, no gold-plating, don't drown in minutiae):

CLOSE - do not re-key. Reopen only on target-runtime evidence.

Two recommendations were weighed (dossier ai/decisions/rf2-ezwnl.registrar-generation-key.md, retired after recording):
- Primary rec: NO. ~98 B/call is ~5% of subscribe's per-call allocation, measured JVM-only, and rf2-x0fe2 established the JVM allocation profile misranks these surfaces for the browser target (its largest term, dynamic binding ~760 B/call, is ~0 in CLJS). Price of YES is one serialized hot-zone campaign across spec/API.md + spec/Conventions.md + image assembly + registrar + xray + pair + story + ~50 test assertions.
- Codex second opinion: YES, now, cleanly, no compat mirror. Its strongest point is perf-independent: the sealed resolver's shape is pointed the wrong way for its two runtime reads (lookup manufactures a pair key per call; registrations/ids reduce over the whole map); keep the flat map assembly-local and nest once at the sealing boundary; pre-alpha postponement only grows the external-reader count. Codex independently reproduced the measurement (N-LOOKGEN 138.5, N-LOOKATOM 40.0 B/call).

WHY NO WINS: Codex's shape argument was taken seriously - it is the strongest YES case - but it decides the shape by crowning the runtime lookup the resolver's primary customer, and the only evidence for that priority is the ~98 B/call: small even where measured, unmeasured on the target runtime, and known-unreliable as a browser proxy. Without target-runtime evidence the reshape moves complexity rather than removing it: today lookup pays a small vector per call so that xray's cross-frame keyset comparison, generation-diff, the Pair runtime, and Story read the documented flat shape directly as plain data; after, lookup is free and every one of those consumers projects or walks a nested map instead. The spec is the artefact; {[kind id] descriptor} is one of frame-generation's four documented stable public keys, and reshaping a documented public key on zero target-runtime evidence is gold-plating under the posture. The elegance defect actually FILED - docstring contradicting implementation on a hot chokepoint - is cured and banked. Nothing lies; nothing is broken.

REOPEN CONDITION: CLJS/browser evidence showing the generation-routed lookup's key allocation materially on the target-runtime profile. rf2-x0fe2 is the measurement bead; its CLJS counterpart measurement is the trigger. Secondary fold-in moment: if the :rf.gen/* surface is ever reshaped by spec change for other reasons, ride this re-key along rather than reopening it standalone.

PRESERVED ANALYSIS (so a re-opener does not re-derive it):
- Re-key sketch: {[kind id] descriptor} -> nested {kind {id descriptor}}. Keep the flat map LOCAL to the assembly pipeline (collision detection, image-order layering, shadow construction are naturally [kind id]-keyed) and nest ONCE at the sealing boundary - generations are immutable and cached, so the O(n) conversion is paid once per assembled generation, shared by its frames. Do NOT carry both indexes in the sealed value. lookup then uses the same paired gets on both branches and the docstring's paired-get claim becomes true everywhere.
- Kept as projections regardless: shadows' and generation-diff's public [kind id] result shapes; they do not require the runtime index itself to be pair-keyed.
- Blast radius (worker survey + Codex's count: ~26 non-decision files mention :rf.gen/resolver): spec/API.md L808 (four documented stable public keys); spec/Conventions.md L59 ('map from a [kind id] pair to exactly one descriptor'; :rf.gen/* member set additive-by-spec-change, so a fifth nested-index key is EQUALLY out-of-fence); image_assembly.cljc (assemble builds it, resolve-descriptor reads it, :rf.gen/kinds derived via (into #{} (map first) (keys resolver))); live_frame/generation-diff (diffs the two flat maps); registrar (lookup + kind-registrations-from-resolver); tools/xray image_view_reads.cljs keyset comparison (xray spec 026 pins the [kind id] keyset contract); pair skill preload runtime.cljs x2 (describe-image) + frame_registrar_test; tools/story story_runtime_test.clj; docs/api/re-frame.core.md, docs/core/images.md, docs/EP/EP-0026; ~50 core assertions of the form (contains? (:rf.gen/resolver gen) [:event :x]). If ever scheduled: one sequenced hot-zone worker, one lane, spec + core + three tools + test corpus in a single change.
- Adjacent win carried by the same re-key: kind-registrations-from-resolver walks the WHOLE resolver per registrations/ids call - O(n) where the nested index gives O(1). Query/introspection surface, not per-read hot path: a beneficiary of the re-key, not a justification for it.
close_reason: RULED NO (delegated decision, 2026-07-27): close on the honest docstring. The generation-routed branch's ~98 B/call is ~5% of one path's allocation, JVM-only, and rf2-x0fe2 shows the JVM profile misranks these surfaces for the browser target; reshaping documented public key :rf.gen/resolver (spec/API.md L808, spec/Conventions.md L59) on zero target-runtime evidence is gold-plating, priced at a serialized hot-zone campaign across spec + core + xray + pair + story + ~50 assertions. The filed defect (docstring vs implementation) is cured and banked. REOPEN on CLJS/browser evidence from rf2-x0fe2's counterpart measurement showing this lookup site materially on the target-runtime profile, or fold the re-key into any future :rf.gen/* spec reshape. Full ruling, re-key sketch (nest once at the sealing boundary, flat map stays assembly-local), blast-radius roster, and the O(n)->O(1) kind-registrations adjacent note are preserved in this bead's notes.

title: subs/live-frame: frame-resolution-target mints a throwaway frame VALUE on every subscribe, probe and dispatch - 200 B/call
description:
MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000% in all
of them, arm N-RESTGT): 200.0 B/call, EXACTLY, in every round, and flat
across n = 30 / 300 / 3000.

WHAT IT IS. `live-frame/frame-resolution-target` on a KEYWORD target
calls `live-frame`, which mints a frame VALUE via
`frame/make-frame-value {:id id :runnable-id id}` -- an argument map,
then a `cond->`-assembled two-then-three-entry map. Its SOLE consumer,
`call-with-frame-resolution`, immediately calls `frame-generation` on
it, which normalizes it BACK to the keyword it was built from and reads
the record's `:generation` slot.

EVERY call site in the repo is the same shape:

    (call-with-frame-resolution (frame-resolution-target X) thunk)

subs.cljc x2, substrate/observation.cljc x2, router.cljc x1, core.cljc
x2. There is no other consumer, and the value is discarded within one
function call of being built. It is 11% of `subscribe`'s per-call
allocation and 18% of `probe`'s pre-node lookups (rf2-ncjyt).

SKETCH. `frame-resolution-target`'s keyword branch can return the
KEYWORD rather than a minted value:

    (keyword? target) (when (some? (frame/frame-generation target)) target)

`call-with-frame-resolution` reads `frame-resolution-generation` off it,
and `frame-generation` is identity-on-keywords through
`frame-value->id`, so the resolved generation is the SAME value by the
same path. The frame-OBJECT branch and the nil (absence-is-default)
branch are untouched.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether the seam earns its existence at all. Given
every caller pairs the two functions and the consumer only ever reads a
generation, `frame-resolution-target` may be provably a no-op --
`call-with-frame-resolution` could take the raw target. That is the
cleaner end state but it retires a documented EP-0023 seam and touches
seven call sites plus ep0023_conformance_cljs_test / 
frame_resolution_cljs_test, which call `call-with-frame-resolution`
directly with values, keywords and nil.

FENCE: implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc. May touch
spec/006 or the EP-0023 text -- HOT-ZONE, sequence, do not parallel.

MEASURE WITH THE COMMITTED INSTRUMENT:
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj,
RM_SUITE=subs, arms N-RESTGT / S2-RESTGT / RGSUB.

JVM ONLY. The byte figure does not transfer to CLJS; the shape (a map
built and discarded per call) is a source fact and does.
close_reason:
PR #7157. ARTEFACT, confirmed and removed — the seam retired outright rather than made cheaper.

WHAT READ THE VALUE: nothing. All seven call sites are the identical shape
(call-with-frame-resolution (frame-resolution-target X) thunk), and the minted
value is discarded within one function call. The composition is provably an
identity for every X — frame VALUE (verbatim on both paths), frame id
(frame-value->id is identity on a keyword), nil, and any other value (frame/frame
is a total (get @frames id) that emits nothing for an unknown address). cwfr's own
docstring already documented accepting a value or an id, and
frame_resolution_cljs_test / ep0023_conformance_cljs_test already called it
directly with values, keywords and nil. No spec, no EP, no doc and no test
referenced frame-resolution-target.

title: freehand: two costed ViewCell memory levers (193 B + 231 B) — ship, or let the row stand
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-oob3g, which ACCEPTED the memory row. The byte accounting is in ai/findings/2026-07-27.viewcell-byte-accounting-oob3g.md. These two levers are measured, inside cell.cljc's fence, and deliberately NOT taken there, because the bead said the remedy is a separate decision and Mike's — and because together they move 5.86x to 4.85x against Reagent, which decides nothing under rf2-lbs3y.

LEVER 1 — the state map's key count. 193 B/boundary [189-204], 7.9%. ViewCell's state map has ELEVEN keys, so CLJS builds it as a PersistentHashMap (map object + 2 BitmapIndexedNodes + 2 arrays + 2 bitmaps boxed as heap numbers + the transient edit token fromArrays leaves behind). Collapsing the five keys a commit publishes together - :frame :deps :dep-order :evidence and the bundle's :generation - into ONE :bundle value takes it to EIGHT, which is a PersistentArrayMap: one object, one array, one backing store. Measured directly as its own arm, ranges disjoint.

  FOR: commit!'s docstring already says 'ONE publication ... dependencies, frame and evidence become live in a single write' and the code spells that as a five-key assoc; the change makes the code say what the docstring says. It also de-duplicates :frame, which the cell holds twice today (top level, and again inside :evidence).
  AGAINST: the published shape of cell/evidence and cell/dependencies changes, and both are tool/test reads.

LEVER 2 — the observations vector's transient. 231 B/boundary [226-235] on a boundary that reads nothing, 172 B [168-178] on one that reads four things, so it is the editable root and not the emptiness. commit-readings answers (persistent! obs) over a (transient []); persistent! RETAINS the editable root the transient cloned (a VectorNode over a 32-slot array) where conj onto a tail-only vector shares PersistentVector.EMPTY's root and allocates none. Five heap nodes per boundary. This is the single largest recoverable item in the ViewCell.

  AGAINST, and it is why this is a ruling and not a fix: it is a TRADE, not a free win. A transient is the right tool for a large accumulator and the wrong one for a small long-lived value - a boundary with one or two observations pays MORE for the transient than plain conj would cost it, one with hundreds pays less. Swapping it buys retention with render-leg throughput, which is the OTHER axis Freehand is losing (bulk re-render ~7-8x Reagent) and the leg PR #7147 tuned.

NOT A LEVER, recorded so it is not re-proposed: flattening the ViewCell into mutable deftype fields. That is worth ~200 B more and costs the atomic publication ('nothing can observe a partial bundle' - obs/read re-enters application code inside the commit and mark-dirty! arrives from the port's fan-out), the JVM's thread-safety story on :revision/:dirty/:listeners, and the 'everything here is common' property. Spec 006 promises, hot-zone, operator's call.

WHAT NEITHER LEVER FIXES: a Freehand boundary carrying the shell's six React hooks over a two-field JS object - no ViewCell at all - already retains 1,171 B above the React floor against Reagent's 418. useSyncExternalStore alone is 516 B. That half lives in shell.cljs, not cell.cljc.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): SHIP BOTH LEVERS, together, as one small ViewCell cleanup in cell.cljc — SEQUENCED so exactly one worker is on cell.cljc at a time relative to rf2-lbs3y (P0): fold this into the first cell.cljc change the lbs3y broad-update profiling mandates, or dispatch it immediately after any in-flight lbs3y profiling/tuning work on that file lands. NEVER concurrent with it. rf2-lbs3y remains the load-bearing investigation; this cleanup must not delay or contend with it.

REASONING (the dossier's two recommendations disagreed — primary: let the row stand, lever 1 opportunistically later, drop lever 2; Codex: ship both now — deciding for Codex on the merits):
(1) Lever 1 is elegance-positive by BOTH analyses; only timing differed. It is the better MODEL, not merely a smaller map: Spec 006 ("The selected render bundle") names the selected render as one bundle with all-or-nothing publication, and commit!'s docstring already says "ONE publication ... dependencies, frame and evidence become live in a single write" — the change makes the state say what spec and docstring say, and de-duplicates :frame (held twice today: top level, and again inside :evidence). "Park it as a rider on a future PR" creates an untracked dependency on an unknown vehicle; a delegated ruling should ship or drop.
(2) Lever 2's sole objection — that it spends render-leg throughput on the axis Freehand is failing worst — is REFUTED for the workload the library encourages. The shipping broad-update witness is 300 fine-grained boundaries with ONE v/sub each (b6_witnesses.cljc, b6_rows.cljs); the 300-read single boundary is explicitly an attribution ablation, "not a shape anybody should write" (b6_witnesses_flat.cljc). A directional Node microcheck against the pinned CLJS 1.12.145 runtime, arm order reversed, put the transient/persistent throughput crossover between two and four items: persistent construction was faster at zero, one, and two observations; transients won as vectors widened. So on the real broad row (one observation per cell), dropping the transient is neutral-to-faster, not a cost; only the anti-pattern-wide boundary may get slower, an acceptable and legible trade for the default representation. The microcheck is directional, not a production benchmark — hence the acceptance re-measure below.
(3) Posture: both levers SIMPLIFY the ordinary representation (fewer keys, plain conj is less machinery than transient/persistent!) while returning a measured ~424 B per mounted boundary — 17.3% of the ViewCell, not noise. That is elegance, not gold-plating; the gold-plating variants are exactly the ones banned below. The ratio motion (retained heap vs Reagent 5.86x -> 4.85x) decides nothing under rf2-lbs3y and is NOT the motivation; representation simplification with measured return is.

IMPLEMENTATION SPEC (the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-9f1s7.viewcell-memory-levers.md is deleted; this note is the complete record).

LEVER 1 — collapse the state map from 11 keys to 8. 193 B/boundary [189-204], 7.9% of ViewCell, measured as its own arm with disjoint ranges. At eleven keys CLJS builds the cell's state map as a PersistentHashMap (map object + 2 BitmapIndexedNodes + 2 arrays + 2 bitmaps boxed as heap numbers + the transient edit token fromArrays leaves behind); at eight it is a PersistentArrayMap (one object, one array). EXACT SHAPE: replace top-level :frame, :deps, :dep-order, :evidence with ONE :bundle key retaining the committed bundle as source of truth; committed-frame, dependencies, dependency-queries, and evidence remain the projection doors reading through it. KEEP TOP-LEVEL :generation — verbatim from the Codex analysis: "One detail matters: keep the top-level `:generation`. It is the cell's *current body authority* and can advance on hot reload before another render commits (`advance-generation!`, `cell.cljc:728-742`). The bundle's `:generation` is the generation of the *last selected commit*. They can intentionally differ. The eight-key shape is therefore obtained by replacing top-level `:frame`, `:deps`, `:dep-order`, and `:evidence` with `:bundle`, not by moving the authority generation into it. That leaves one honest state transition and one honest set of projections without weakening the atom, rollback, or acquire-before-release laws." (Arithmetic cross-check: 11 - 4 + 1 = 8; folding the authority :generation in too would give seven keys — the measured eight-key PersistentArrayMap arm corresponds to keeping it top-level, with the commit's own generation carried inside the bundle value.) The cell namespace is explicitly not application API, so the many tool/test reads through cell/evidence and cell/dependencies demonstrate encapsulation rather than create a compatibility burden — any readers whose read shapes change move in the SAME PR (coordinated, not large).

LEVER 2 — drop the observations vector's transient. 231 B/boundary [226-235] on a boundary that reads nothing; 172 B [168-178] on one that reads four things (so it is the editable root, not the emptiness); five heap nodes per boundary; the single largest recoverable item in the ViewCell. MECHANISM: commit-readings currently answers (persistent! obs) over (transient []); persistent! retains the editable root the transient cloned (a VectorNode over a 32-slot array), where plain conj onto a small vector shares PersistentVector.EMPTY's root and allocates none (tail-only growth below 32 items). CHANGE: start obs at [], use conj, return it directly. Pinned source anchors (ClojureScript r1.12.145 cljs/core.cljs): tv-editable-root, tv-editable-tail, TransientVector.-persistent!, PersistentVector.-conj. Measured directional crossover: between 2 and 4 items; persistent wins below.

DO NOT: no adaptive threshold, no hybrid accumulator, no JS-array special case, no mutable deftype fields. The mutable-deftype flattening stays REJECTED (recorded so nobody re-proposes it): worth ~200 B more but costs atomic publication ("nothing can observe a partial bundle" — obs/read re-enters application code inside the commit, and mark-dirty! arrives from the port's fan-out), the JVM thread-safety story on :revision/:dirty/:listeners, and Spec 006 promises.

If the B6 broad row regresses beyond noise, that falsifies the microcheck's directional claim — revert the lever-2 half; lever 1 stands on its own merits.

title: re-frame: a one-cell write allocates 457 KB re-evaluating 300 subscriptions that did not change
description:
FOUND by B8 (rf2-lcsjg, allocation under update). Not a Freehand finding — a re-frame one.

Changing ONE cell of B6's 300-cell grid allocates 478,787 bytes on the Freehand arm. Of that, 457,181 B — 95.5% — is the WRITE LEG: frame/replace-app-db! and the subscription graph re-evaluating all 300 :b6/cell subscriptions to discover that 299 of them are unchanged. The view substrate's whole share is 21,376 B, within 11% of Reagent's 19,307.

For contrast the same narrow write on a bare reagent.core/atom with r/cursor costs 4,018 B in its write leg. That is not a fair comparison (a cursor is not a subscription graph) but it is the order of magnitude a fine-grained store can achieve.

The measurement is collection-free-window allocation counting, ranges disjoint, 0 unverified of 2,400 writes, and the instrument carries a kept-vs-dropped self-test at 1.0001. See docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-allocation.md.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND A BENCH ROW: this is paid on every interaction in every re-frame application, and it scales with the number of registered subscriptions rather than with what changed. It is the largest single allocation term in a narrow write by a factor of twenty.

NOT filed as a defect and no remedy is proposed. Whether the signal graph can skip subscriptions whose inputs are structurally unchanged is a re-frame design question with correctness implications (equality semantics, sub-of-sub layers), and it belongs to whoever owns that graph. Filed so the number is on record.
close_reason:
PR #7156 merged. VERDICT: BOTH INTRINSIC AND ARTEFACT, split along a line the bead did not anticipate.

INTRINSIC — the CARDINALITY. Re-evaluating 300 subs to discover 299 unchanged is CORRECT, proven from the REGISTRATION CONTRACT rather than a benchmark: a layer-1 reg-sub body is (fn [db query-v] ...), an opaque function of the whole app-db; none of reg-sub's four shapes declares a path; the metadata map carries :doc/:schema/:sensitive/:large and nothing path-shaped; and the only graph edge (sub -> app-db projection) carries no path either. NO UNUSED INFORMATION EXISTS. commit-frame-transition! does compute a changed-set, but of PARTITIONS, and it is already fully exploited. Giving the graph path knowledge means a new declaration or read-tracking — a redesign, not a fix. This PR does not touch it.

ARTEFACT — 71% of the PER-EVALUATION cost, and it is fixed. Two private representation choices in re-frame.substrate.spine, neither observable, neither touching when a sub is considered current: :queue/:queued were a persistent vector and set used as single-threaded scratch inside one closure (the same file gives exactly that reasoning ONE LINE ABOVE for depth/flushing?), now a JS array and js/Set; and the >=2-subscriber fan-out walked (vals ws) where the 1-subscriber branch beside it already used reduce-kv.

MEASURED: frame/replace-app-db! on 300 subs 854,788 -> 286,714 B, 2.98x, DISJOINT. Per-sub slope 2,830.7 -> 940.8, and the superlinearity vanished (936.6/947.2/940.8 flat), independently corroborating that the removed term was the HAMT.
CREDIBILITY: the saving was a FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, not a before/after story — both spellings kept live as paired controls in one process, predicted 1,884 B/sub, measured 1,889.9, 0.3% error.

SCOPE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE: 'every re-frame application pays it' is true of the SHAPE, not the BYTES. make-scheduler is reached only via make-react-spine, serving UIx, Freehand and re-frame.ui. REAGENT AND REAGENT-SLIM GO THROUGH make-ratom-spine AND PAY NONE OF THE 60% TERM.
SCALE CAVEAT: figures are Node V8 (pointer compression OFF) against the browser's ON — the same write reads 854,788 Node vs 457,181 browser, 1.87x. Shares transfer, absolutes do not.

FOLLOW-ONS FILED, none actioned: rf2-gncxk (the layer-1 memo guard is provably guaranteed to miss on the flush path but cannot be removed without a contract change), rf2-88pie (tenth instrument fault: a large-object arm inflates its successor 2x, caught only by running both arm orders), rf2-ssn1o (a Reagent write-leg arm), rf2-3zenp (the published 457,181 B is now stale), rf2-78ejq (RFWRITE-0 is 4,470 B at ZERO subscriptions, undecomposed), rf2-zxv06 (production handler-scope 121 B/sub cannot be dev-gated — the always-on SSR error path reads the scope).

title: bench: a Reagent-on-re-frame arm, so the broad view-leg gap stops being an upper bound
description:
B8 (rf2-lcsjg, allocation under update) measures Freehand's broad view leg at 13.5x Reagent's, ranges disjoint. That figure CANNOT be quoted as a substrate result and the report says so.

The two arms do not carry the same framework: Freehand's grid reads 300 v/sub subscriptions through re-frame's subscription graph, the Reagent grid 300 r/cursor derefs on a bare reagent.core/atom. rf2-40kdm (PR #7151) measured the read path directly and found an idiomatic Reagent body reading @(subscribe q) pays 95.3-97.4% of what Freehand's port pays per read — nearly all per-read render allocation is SHARED reactive-system cost. Freehand's arm pays it 300 times a broad write; the Reagent arm pays none of it.

So 13.5x is an upper bound containing an unknown but large amount of re-frame, and the substrate difference could be far smaller.

THE FIX is a third update arm: Reagent views mounted on re-frame subscriptions (reg-sub + @(subscribe [:b6/cell i])), same 300-cell grid, same canonical DOM. Then broad view-leg allocation splits three ways — Freehand, Reagent-on-re-frame, Reagent-on-ratom — and the substrate term is the first minus the second rather than the first minus the third.

The narrow row is much less exposed (one read per write, so the shared term is small in absolute bytes) and already reads 1.107x, which is the closest thing to a like-for-like substrate comparison available today.

Same arm would sharpen the CLOCK rows too — freehand-vs-reagent.md 2a bounds this asymmetry by argument rather than by measurement.

title: bench: B6 has no Reagent-reading-re-frame arm, so no row isolates the view substrate with the reactive system held fixed
description:
THE MISSING ARM. Every published Freehand-vs-Reagent update row compares
Freehand reading a re-frame SUBSCRIPTION against Reagent reading a bare
`reagent.core/atom` through an `r/cursor`. Both are their substrate's own
idiom, and the report says so -- but it means the headline ratio is a
comparison of two REACTIVE SYSTEMS, not two view substrates, and no row
anywhere isolates the view substrate with the reactive system held fixed.

rf2-mvqwe made that gap expensive rather than theoretical. Measured on the
JVM, 95.3% - 97.4% of the per-dependency-read allocation attributed to
Freehand's observation port is ALSO paid by a plain `@(rf/subscribe [:q])`
with no view substrate at all. If the missing arm behaves the same way in
the browser, the broad-update row's headline moves. If it does not, we
learn that the JVM shape did not transfer -- which is worth knowing before
anyone acts on rf2-ncjyt or rf2-j8ls2.

WHY IT DOES NOT EXIST YET, per the report's own limitations list: Freehand's
`v/sub` is inert under a ratom adapter (rf2-8cnxg, rf2-jt8vz), so one page
cannot host a Freehand arm and a re-frame-reading Reagent arm on one
adapter. The report says it "would need two adapter phases bridged by the
floor". That is real work, and until now the cost was not obviously
justified.

WHAT TO BUILD: a `u-cell` for the Reagent arm that reads
`@(rf/subscribe [:b6/cell i])` against the SAME frame the Freehand arm
drives, so `frame/replace-app-db!` is the write for both and the only
difference left is the view substrate. Canonical-DOM equality already
gates the arms, so a divergence fails rather than flatters.

FIRST DECIDE THE HARNESS SHAPE. Two adapter phases bridged by the floor is
one option; a separate page carrying only the reactive-system contrast is
another and may be cheaper. Do not start writing arms before that is
settled -- and do not weaken the existing rows to make room, they answer a
different question and the operator's standard (rf2-lbs3y) is quoted
against them.

page) -- second waits for the first's PR to merge.
