title: The re-frame.freehand.test mounted lifecycle facade does not exist — three suites duplicate act, root/container and residue
description:
CORRECTS A FALSE PREMISE IN rf2-drpa3.182.7 AND IN THE MAYOR BRIEF THAT DISPATCHED IT. That bead TEST SURFACE section says to "consume the re-frame.freehand.test mounted lifecycle facade ruled in ER-06/ER-08 and owned by rf2-gzmg0" and not to duplicate it. The facade DOES NOT EXIST. rf2-gzmg0 shipped a Story presence bridge, which is a different thing. So the instruction was unfollowable, and three suites have each grown their own.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DUPLICATED — measured by the rf2-drpa3.182.7 worker, and narrower than "everything", which is why this is a small bead and not a framework:

  ALREADY SHARED, needs nothing: frame/runtime reset. All three use test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture.
  BYTE-IDENTICAL IN ALL THREE FILES: the React 19 act-as-promise wrapper.
  THE SAME TWO LINES TWICE: .unmount + .remove teardown.
  IN ONE FILE ONLY: the leak assertion — which is exactly why the other two cannot claim :residue :none.

SO THE SPEC IS THREE THINGS: act, root/container lifecycle, and a SHARED RESIDUE ASSERTION. Frame reset is done. Nothing else.

WHY THE RESIDUE ASSERTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING PIECE. PR #7105 found all three fixture records declared :residue :none while NOTHING CHECKED IT, and two were overclaiming: FH-BEHAVIOR-005 genuinely earns :none (both projections read the books empty as exact zeros); FH-CTRL-018 only unmounts and removes; FH-REACT-007 resets in its :init-fn — cleanup BEFORE each test rather than an assertion AFTER one, so a retained boundary is masked by the next reset. Those two now say :unasserted, and a JVM row refuses a :none claim whose suites make no emptiness assertion. That converted an unverifiable claim into a countable one — but the only way to move them back to :none is a shared assertion the three can all use.

A leaked React root contaminates every later suite in a shared-process bundle; this repo has seen that produce 98 failures across unrelated suites.

SEQUENCING. The rf2-drpa3.182.7 worker deliberately did NOT build this, for two stated reasons, both still true at filing: it collides head-on with the workers on rf2-drpa3.182.4 and rf2-drpa3.182.3, and its own bead forbids growing a parallel facade. Sequence this AFTER those land. It is also a candidate to fold into rf2-fby7o or a Freehand test-surface bead rather than standing alone — mayor call at dispatch time.

ACCEPTANCE. One facade carrying act, root/container lifecycle and a residue assertion, consumed by all three suites with no pasted copies remaining. FH-CTRL-018 and FH-REACT-007 move from :unasserted back to :none, and the JVM row that refuses an unearned :none still refuses one — prove that with a mutation, since a shared assertion that cannot fail is the defect this bead exists to remove.

DO NOT let this become a browser-action DSL, a query library or a second evidence store. rf2-drpa3.182.7 NON-GOALS names all three, and they still apply.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7111 (2026-07-27 AEST) — REOPENED. The patch renamed matrix-support to mount-support, added a lifecycle ledger/residue-clean!, and changed only the require path in the ten existing matrix consumers. It did not touch the promised owners: controls-kit-dom-cljs-test and host-mounted-dom-cljs-test still carry their private lifecycle helpers, the behavior proofs remain separate, and repository-wide residue-clean!/reset-ledger! have ZERO executable call sites outside their definitions/docs. The fixtures still say FH-CTRL-018/FH-REACT-007 :residue :unasserted, while roster-jvm-test explicitly expects those two unasserted; focused gate is green at 9 tests/33 assertions, proving the PR did not deliver its claimed transition to :none. Complete the exact original acceptance by migrating the named suites, calling the shared assertion after teardown, changing the two fixture records and current-state roster assertion, and proving the refusal mutation. No second facade or broader browser DSL.
PR #7162 (2026-07-27 21:13 AUSEST) — MIGRATION LANDED, ONE FENCED STEP REMAINS. All four mounted projections of the three spine fixtures (controls-kit-dom, host-mounted-dom, behaviors-dom, behavior-async-dom) now consume re-frame.freehand.mount-support for act + root/container lifecycle; four byte-identical act copies deleted. residue-clean!/reset-ledger! went from ZERO executable call sites to 8: every suite scopes the ledger in its :init-fn and reads the books AFTER teardown. roster-jvm-test recognises residue-clean! and gains the refusal mutation (a suite can consume the shared TEARDOWN and never read the shared BOOKS — the rule is run against both halves and still refuses the first). Gates green: freehand JVM 1221/8229 -> 1222/8231 exit 0; node 1302/7219 unchanged exit 0; browser 835 tests/5323 -> 835 tests/5383 assertions exit 0 — test count identical, +60 assertions are the residue rows. Deliberately NOT absorbed (and the bead's inventory held on all three counts): the frame/runtime reset was already shared; the controls kit's typing helpers differ (isComposing false, insert-at-caret not append) so absorbing them would be a behaviour change; host-mounted's teardown goes through the DOOR (v/unmount!) so destroy-root! would be wrong. FH-REACT-007: released! calls ms/residue-clean! over the door's live-root registry after teardown! (v/unmount! + ms/remove-node!), and all three mounting rows end there — its other two rows are emitter-only adapter refusals that mount nothing and so have no residue to read. residue-clean! carries its own non-vacuity: (is (pos? (count retired))) reds a suite that tore no root down through the facade.

AND the one comment naming it reds a-residue-none-claim-is-backed-by-an-emptiness-assertion at exit 1: "FH-CTRL-018 claims :residue :none, but its mounted proof re-frame.freehand.controls-kit-dom-cljs-test makes no emptiness assertion". AND THE HONEST HALF, WHICH BELONGS TO THE PARENT, NOT HERE. GATES. implementation/freehand JVM clojure -M:test: 1222 tests / 8233 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0 (8231 -> 8233 because the residue rule now scans two more mounted proofs). title: machines-viz share host accepts non-URLs despite its absolute-host contract
description: Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7088. The PR correctly removes the nonexistent hosted default and repeatedly contracts :host as the absolute URL of a viewer page the caller hosts. The landed encoder enforces only `(string? host)` plus trim/nonblank, then returns `(str host "#machine=" payload)`. Any nonblank value therefore passes: `banana` or `/viewer.html` produces a non-shareable string, preserving the same dead-link outcome the PR was meant to remove. A valid absolute URL carrying an existing fragment is worse: appending a second `#machine=` makes decode-share-url read from the first # and miss the machine payload. Existing tests cover missing/nil/blank only. Keep the repair at this boundary: parse and validate the host according to the documented contract (at minimum absolute http(s), with an explicit fragment policy), return the normalized viewer-page URL plus the one machine fragment, and add witnesses for relative/garbage input and a pre-fragmented absolute URL. Do not add hosting or deployment machinery.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7102. The worker MEASURED before validating, as instructed, and the measurement changed the answer: it probed encode-share-url with 17 hosts through the real CLJS lane and found TWO classes, not one.

LOUD (no guard warranted): 'banana', '/viewer.html', 'viewer.html', '//acme/viewer.html', 'javascript:alert(1)', 'data:...' all return a string BEGINNING WITH WHAT THE CALLER TYPED, with the payload intact and decoding fine. 'banana#machine=...' is not a link in any browser, the defect is the caller's own word at the front of the string, and it dies at first paste. Nothing is hidden.

SILENT (guard warranted, and this is the real defect): a :host that already carries a fragment. 'https://acme.example.com/viewer.html#foo' yields '...#foo#machine=...' which fails to decode with :malformed-fragment, because extract-fragment splits on the FIRST '#'. Right origin, right path, '#machine=' present, 400 characters of base64 nobody counts '#'s in. THE SENDER SEES SUCCESS AND THE FAILURE LANDS ON THE RECIPIENT.

OUTCOME split on exactly that line: a refusal for the fragment case only (:reason :host-carries-fragment, message naming the fragment, ex-data carrying :fragment-index rather than the host, which can carry a query token — consistent with this namespace's rf2-8nzxib discipline), and a CONTRACT CORRECTION for everything else. share.cljs, tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md and README.md claimed 'the absolute URL' while nothing enforced absoluteness; they now state what IS checked, what is not, and why. Same note added to export/share-url, which passes :host straight through. It refuses rather than strips, because the caller's fragment meant something and discarding it silently is a quieter wrong answer.

TWO REMEDIES THE BEAD ASKED FOR WERE DECLINED, and the mayor endorses both declines: (1) 'at minimum absolute http(s)' validation — file:///.../viewer.html is literally what the README's own build recipe leaves on disk and /viewer.html is a legitimate same-origin base, so a scheme allowlist REFUSES WORKING INPUT to catch input nobody can miss, and it is the per-value closed-set check this project has rejected; (2) returning a 'normalized' URL — normalising is guessing.

THE RULING IS PINNED IN A TEST, which is the part worth copying: non-url-host-is-accepted-and-fails-visibly asserts that 'banana', 'not a url' and 'javascript:alert(1)' STILL ENCODE, with the reason stated, so a future guard-adder must confront the decision rather than quietly reverse it.

MUTATION PROOF, each confirmed applied before its verdict was read: (A) refusal disabled -> 25 failures all in the positive test; (B) over-refuse on '/' -> suite-wide red including the negative control; (C) SURGICAL — still refuses every '#' but additionally refuses a query string -> EXACTLY ONE test red, fragment-free-hosts-are-untouched. C is the recorded failure shape (a guard proven only on refusals that rejects a legal form) and the negative control is its sole witness. Restored 0/0.

Gates rc=0: machines-viz JVM 632/2537, machines-viz CLJS 825/3311 with 0 warnings, plus hardcoded-paths, beads-boundary, thrown-error, test-lane-bijection (1672 files / 45 lanes), doc-slugs, readme-links and keyword-catalogue drift. Sibling rf2-8m344 deliberately untouched — the viewer still is not deployed by this repository and nothing here implies the share path works end to end.

title: 37 more wrong-arity reg-* examples: reg-resource (21), reg-flow (8), reg-mutation (8) all throw ArityException at registration
description:
Found while fixing rf2-txe8o (reg-route :path in metadata, PR #7094). That bead enumerated its verb correctly and completely — and its verb is one of FOUR with the same defect.

THE CLASS. Reading arglists off the live facade (not from memory), exactly four public reg-* verbs have NO 2-arg arity:

    reg-flow     [flow-id metadata derive-fn]
    reg-mutation [mutation-id metadata request-fn]
    reg-resource [resource-id metadata request-fn]
    reg-route    [id metadata path]

A 2-arg (or 1-arg) call of any of them raises a raw clojure.lang.ArityException at registration, so the registration never happens and everything downstream in the worked example is inert. NOTE the symptom is the ArityException, NOT the structured guard: rf2-txe8o attributed the throw to registry.cljc:455, but that guard only fires for a HALF-migrated 3-arg call that still carries :path in the map. The corpus form dies earlier, with no id, no :rf.error/* id and no grammar hint.

COUNTS (reader-based scan of every fenced clojure/edn block in tracked files; generated docs/spec + site excluded):

    reg-resource  21
    reg-route     18   <- rf2-txe8o, FIXED in PR #7094 (8 of 18; 10 left in docs/EP by ruling)
    reg-flow       8
    reg-mutation   8
    TOTAL         55   — rf2-txe8o covered 33% of the class

THE SHARP END: THREE ARE IN THE NORMATIVE SPEC.

    spec/015-Data-Classification.md  156  reg-resource :user-profile
    spec/016-Resources.md           1361  reg-resource :feed/timeline
    spec/016-Resources.md           1698  reg-resource :article/by-slug

Same argument rf2-txe8o made for its seven: the spec is the artefact, and every downstream reader — the guide, an AI generating code from the spec — inherits the broken shape as sanctioned.

THIS IS NOT A THIRD-SLOT MOVE. Unlike reg-route (where the :path was already present, just misplaced), a 2-arg reg-resource has no request fn to promote — the third slot must be AUTHORED. And correcting the arity alone is not enough; verified executably:

    3-arg, no :scope       -> :rf.error/resource-missing-scope-policy
    3-arg + :scope         -> :rf.error/resource-bad-spec (no :params-schema)

So each site needs a :scope policy, a :params-schema, and a plausible :request fn. That is example authoring, and it should be done uniformly across all 21 reg-resource sites by one worker who has measured the class — not ad hoc per file.

title: 18 documented reg-route examples put :path INSIDE the metadata map, so every one of them throws at registration
description:
Found while answering rf2-h5fkc (does the freehand sample gate extend past its own tree). That bead named ONE such example as "the known outsider". A reader-based scan of every fenced clojure block in `docs/**`, `spec/**`, `migration/**`, `examples/**`, `skills/**` and `implementation/**` finds EIGHTEEN, and the distribution is the interesting part.

THE DEFECT. `rf2-wvh95f F1` made the path pattern the THIRD positional slot of `reg-route`. `routing/registry.cljc` rejects a `:path` left inside the metadata map, loudly and by design:

    (when (contains? metadata :path)
      (throw (route-error :rf.error/route-bad-metadata 'rf/reg-route
               (str "route " id " declares :path inside its metadata map — per "
                    "rf2-wvh95f F1 the path pattern is the THIRD slot: …"))))

So each of these examples raises at registration and the route never registers. Everything downstream in the same worked example — the `:on-match` events, the `:resources` readiness projection, the classification declaration — is then inert for anyone who pastes it.

THE INVENTORY (file, the line the fenced block starts at, the route id):

  docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md   207   :password-reset
  docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md             1467   :route/article
  docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md             2323   :route/article
  docs/EP/EP-0011-uniform-async-reply-envelope.md 1187   :route/article

  spec/012-Routing.md                               891   :route/cart
  spec/012-Routing.md                               981   :rf.route/not-found
  spec/012-Routing.md                              1319   :route/search
  spec/012-Routing.md                              1430   :route/sorted
  spec/016-Resources.md                            1237   :route/article
  spec/016-Resources.md                            1699   :route/article
  spec/Derivations.md                               606   :route/article

SEVEN ARE IN THE NORMATIVE SPEC, and that is the sharp end. `spec/012-Routing.md` is the routing spec, and four of its worked examples — including the canonical `:rf.route/not-found` registration the runtime special-cases — teach a spelling the runtime rejects. The spec is the artefact; the code is downstream. This is the spec disagreeing with its own implementation, not a doc lagging behind.

TEN ARE IN docs/EP/**, which is a design-record tree. Those were correct when written (the grammar change came later), so the right disposition there is a judgement call the fixer should take deliberately: correct them so a reader who pastes an EP example gets a working route, or leave them as dated records and say so. Do not correct them silently as if they were live docs.

ONE — `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md` — is a live how-to, and it is the worst of the eighteen for its own reason: the whole point of the page is keeping a reset token out of traces, and the route that would carry the `:sensitive [[:query :reset-token]]` declaration never registers, so the reader's secret is not classified at all. Correct spelling is `(rf/reg-route :password-reset {:sensitive [[:query :reset-token]]} "/reset")`.

WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR, and why it is filed separately from the ruling. rf2-h5fkc asked whether extending the digest-pinned freehand roster to `docs/api` + `docs/core` + `docs/story` + `migration` would be worth it. Exactly ONE of these eighteen lies inside that proposed scope; seventeen live in `spec/**` and `docs/EP/**`, which nobody proposed rostering. The verdict on that bead is therefore "no", and the fix for this class is a corpus sweep now plus — if a standing check is ever wanted — a rule inside the EXISTING `doc_api_check` / `doc_guide_check` family, which already reads every doc tree and already asks call-position questions. Not a roster extension, and not a second gate.

title: v/spread at a v/defhost head is accepted and silently rewrites :className to :class - spec/004 now says it is illegal, nothing enforces it
description:
The implementation arm of rf2-33pts (spec half landed in PR #7090). spec/004 Props forwarding now states that v/spread and v/spread-safe are element forms and neither is legal at a v/defhost head. Nothing enforces that today, and the current behaviour is wrong in both directions - measured on the JVM structural path with a real (v/defhost date-picker ... {:callbacks {:onChange :event} :children :none :ssr :client-only}) head and the map built inside the view body:

  remainder key   | v/spread at host head        | plain merge at host head
  :placeholder    | :placeholder            OK   | :placeholder            OK
  :className      | :class  <-- SILENT RENAME    | :className              OK
  "class"         | :class  <-- LAUNDERED        | REFUSED (exactness law) OK
  :class-name     | REFUSED <-- wrongly          | :class-name             OK

Mechanism: node/spread-attrs projects both maps through canonical-slot-keys -> conv/attr-key -> rules/canonical-attr-key, which rewrites EVERY spelling projecting onto the className or style slot into :class / :style. At an element that is correct (they own a slot). At a host head it defeats descriptor/normalize-host-call's inexact-host-prop-names check, which runs FIRST precisely so every later law can be enforced BY name - the same class of hole rf2-c20nr's disjoint-plane guard was just closed against. And :className -> :class is not merely a laundered spelling: it is a DIFFERENT React prop, the one a third-party component most commonly reads, silently renamed to one it does not.

The other direction: assert-forwardable-attrs! applies conv/attr-key-refusal, the DOM attribute grammar, so :class-name, a mixed-case :data-fooBar and :key are refused - all three are ordinary names on a foreign prop ABI, and :key is how a host crossing is keyed at a plain head.

ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING - do not pick one silently. v/spread returns a plain map, so by the time normalize-host-call sees it the provenance is gone. Two candidate mechanisms:
(a) mark the spread's result the way node/carry-caller marks a v/spread-safe caller map, and have normalize-host-call refuse a marked map (reuses :rf.error/view-bad-props, no new id);
(b) leave it unenforced and treat spec/004 + the guide as the whole answer (pre-alpha, trust the programmer).
(a) costs a value mark on the hottest forwarding seam; (b) leaves a silent-corruption path the spec says does not exist. No new public verb is needed either way.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7100, merged; trunk re-verified green afterwards at 1212 tests / 8113 assertions, exit 0, on a main that also carries #7096's docs restructure.

MAYOR RULING, RECORDED LATE AND ACKNOWLEDGED AS SUCH: this bead said 'ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING — do not pick one silently' and listed (a) mark-and-refuse versus (b) leave it to the spec. My dispatch brief supplied (a) WITHOUT acknowledging the bead had reserved the question. The worker followed the brief and FLAGGED THE DIVERGENCE, which is exactly right — I tell every worker the bead is authoritative over the brief, so silently overriding a reserved ruling is my error, not its.

I STAND BY (a), on the house test: a guard is warranted when the failure is SILENT and has already happened. :className arriving as :class is a DIFFERENT REACT PROP — the component receives no class and nothing reports it. And the implementation cost turned out to be near zero, which the ruling could not have known in advance but which confirms it: rules/mark-element-forward leaves the author spelling in the result's METADATA and normalize-host-call refuses a marked map. Metadata rather than a value wrapper so the result stays an ordinary attribute map for the element fold — the LEGAL use, which must cost nothing — and =, hash and pr-str all ignore it. No new error id: a new arm of the existing :rf.error/view-bad-props with recovery :forward-to-a-host-with-an-ordinary-map, so no three-file co-edit.

TWO FINDINGS BEYOND THE BRIEF, the first of which the brief should have carried:

1. THE CHECK MUST RUN BEFORE THE EXACTNESS LAW. A spread canonicalises "class" into the keyword :class, so inexact-host-prop-names sees a CLEAN call — exactness would pass and the corruption would be the answer. Asserted, with its own non-vacuity leg.
2. RUNTIME-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The compiled tier refuses a v/defhost crossing outright (:rf.ui.compile/host-crossing-unsupported), so the interpreted walk is the only path that can reach a host head; tree.cljc and react.cljs both normalize through the one seam, so one guard covers both hosts.

THE MUTUALLY-INVALIDATING-TEST RISK DID NOT MATERIALISE, and my warning was over-broad: I named four files containing both 'spread' and 'defhost'. NONE pinned the accepting behaviour. composition_cljs_test.cljc already asserts the CORRECT behaviour (#7093 landed that flip); samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj's spread-forms row points at an element-level fixture and no fenced block changed so no digest moved; and pilot_react_interop.cljc / pilot_react_interop_dom_cljs_test.cljs were FALSE POSITIVES — they matched on 'spreadsheet' and 'spreadjs'. It also checked #7098's new roster spine, which mentions neither term.

PROOF: both forms refused with a diagnostic naming form, head and recovery; a control that an ordinary map of the same keys still normalizes; :className end-to-end through a real render against a merge TWIN showing the caller's name surviving — the counterfactual is what makes it more than 'something throws'. Negative control: both forms at an ELEMENT head still fold as before, :className composing into the element's own class. Mutation: neutering the mark reader red 14 assertions across the three refusal rows, exit 1, and left the element rows GREEN — the signature that the guard is load-bearing for the refusal and the control is independent of it.

Gates rc=0: freehand 1210/8071, core 2126/10492 (run because spec/009 changed), test:cljs 11575/57974, the fast-PR spine, hardcoded-paths and beads-boundary.

DISCLOSED FENCE CROSSING, and handled correctly: it also touched spec/004-Views.md — one sentence on the existing Props-forwarding bullet naming the id and recovery, since the bullet ruled the form illegal without saying what happens — which I had not sequenced it for, alongside #7096's 43-line rework of the same file. It merged clean and the worker disclosed the risk rather than hiding it. That is the right way to cross a fence: unavoidable, disclosed, proven non-conflicting.

title: docs/core/freehand/composition.md teaches v/spread at a v/defhost head, which spec/004 now rules illegal
description:

title: F6e trap: clearing check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py's SETUP error silently retires the preflight-before-render assertion
description:
Found by the rf2-ddu3i deletion probe (PR #7082).

With implementation/ui/ moved aside, scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py exits 1 with TWO SETUP lines:

  SETUP: expected Rule-7 source file missing: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs
  SETUP: expected Rule-7 source file missing: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc

The message tells the reader exactly what to do — 'the lifecycle guard's path list drifted; update the *_FILE constants' — and that is the trap. find_lifecycle_drift() reports the missing file and then passes None on, so lifecycle_realization_problems() SKIPS the arm entirely. The LIFECYCLE-SOURCE-ORDER assertion never fails; it stops being evaluated.

What is skipped is not small. The L5 arm is a per-function causal assertion over the compiled client's three production render paths: every host render preceded by its OWN live (run-preflight! ...) in the SAME function body, dead forms (#_ and (when false ...)) neutralized first, plus the one-shot pre -> create -> render triple. It exists because two real classes of bypass were found (rf2-8cncz). Delete the two *_FILE constants to clear the SETUP error and all of it goes, with nothing left to notice.

F6e (rf2-drpa3.57) is the change that will face this. The honest options are (a) re-point the two constants at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs and whatever owns Freehand's preflight, keeping the assertion alive, or (b) delete the L5 arm DELIBERATELY and record that the compiled preflight-before-render contract is now unguarded. What must not happen is (a)-shaped edit that lands as (b) by accident.

Rowed in spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md as REPLACE / F6.

THE JUDGEMENT THIS NEEDS, which is why it is a bead and not a follow-on commit: these are NOT one class. Some break outright when implementation/ui/ is deleted (the two drift gates, the JVM test script). Some become VACUOUS but do not break (the bundle-isolation and elision sentinels — they scan for bodies that will no longer exist). Some are policy assertions ABOUT the donor that become FALSE rather than broken (check_adapter_disposition.py demands docs say re-frame.ui is experimental; after deletion that text should be gone, so the gate would then demand text about a deleted substrate). A file with no row can never be undisposed, so the ledger can reach zero while these are still live, and F6e (rf2-drpa3.57) then deletes implementation/ui/ on a completeness signal that never covered them. The two drift gates are the sharpest case — they read donor source files by name and would red on main the moment the tree goes.

Partition the eleven files into breaks / goes-vacuous / policy-assertion, assign an evidenced disposition per partition against an already-rowed sibling, add each row and its ESTABLISHED_ROWS identity together, and prove it by deletion mutation the way the rf2-vfv8r PR did (move implementation/ui/ aside, record which gates red).

title: Machines-viz default viewer URL is 404; no workflow ships the page bundle
description:
Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7071. The PR correctly moves viewer.cljs out of the published machines-viz jar, but repeatedly asserts that the page still ships as public/viewer.html plus viewer.js and documents https://day8.github.io/re-frame2-machines-viz/viewer.html as the default share host.

That URL currently returns HTTP 404. There is no day8/re-frame2-machines-viz repository, and the re-frame2 repository has no workflow or script that compiles :machines-viz-viewer, stages viewer.js beside tools/machines-viz/public/viewer.html, or deploys those two files. release-machines-viz.yml only tests the JVM artefact and deploys the jar to Clojars. The Shadow build proves the bundle can be produced, but no delivery path consumes it.

This makes the share-url default and the new "ships as a page" API/README claims false end-to-end. Keep the repair bounded to making the existing page contract real; do not turn this into a general static-site framework.
acceptance_criteria:
The canonical machines-viz viewer URL documented and emitted by encode-share-url returns the checked-in viewer.html and its matching compiled viewer.js after the relevant release/deploy flow.
A repository-owned workflow builds :machines-viz-viewer, stages the exact HTML and bundle together, and deploys them to the documented host with a smoke check that loads the page and exported run entry.
The release documentation names who/what deploys the page and does not imply that publishing the Clojars jar deploys it.
If the day8.github.io/re-frame2-machines-viz host is deliberately not available pre-alpha, remove it as a default and stop calling the page shipped until a real host exists; keep self-hosting explicit.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7116 (merge a06227b68c62fdd3ab8ead3531f52302783ebc47, 2026-07-26T14:25:12Z) — REOPENED exact owner. The new A2 gate claims to prove viewer.js INSTALLS the global that viewer.html calls, but bundleExports is only a substring search. Its own green self-test demonstrates the false positive: it accepts a bundle containing only an unrelated array with segments a, b, viewer, run even though that bundle installs no window global at all; the dotted arm likewise accepts any unrelated occurrence of a.b.viewer.run. Therefore the required CI job can report that the page boot global is installed when the bundle merely contains the same segment sequence. This is the load-bearing coupling rf2-8m344 was closed for, so a false-positive proof leaves the exact owner incomplete. Keep the repair small: make A2 recognise an actual Closure export/install expression or execute the built bundle in a minimal isolated browser-like harness and assert the derived window path is callable. Add negative self-tests for decoy array and dotted occurrences, and mutation-prove that removing the install while preserving a decoy occurrence makes the gate fail. Do not turn this into a general browser smoke framework.

The 404 half was already on main (ee9ba1bed0): :host is REQUIRED, blank throws :reason :no-host, and the dead day8.github.io URL survives only in comments explaining its removal. This PR closes the audit reopen — a defect in the PROOF, not the page. The A2 assertion in stage-viewer-page.cjs was bundle.includes() over the export-path literal, and a substring cannot tell an export from a coincidence; its own green self-test accepted 'var x=["a","b","viewer","run"]', which installs no global at all. A2 now EVALUATES the bundle in an isolated vm context and asks whether window.<the path the page calls> came out callable. Not a proxy for the coupling - the coupling. Both sides stay derived, run() is never called, so it is a load-and-install proof rather than a render smoke. Self-test 7 -> 11 cases: decoy array literal, decoy dotted occurrence, non-function at the path, and a bundle that throws. title: The beads truncation guard lives only in beads-checkpoint.sh, and the path that actually empties the export does not go through it — second recurrence
description:
Found on the 2026-07-26 method reread, after an empty export reached main earlier the same day.

THE GUARD IS SOUND AND IT WORKS. scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh refuses an empty export outright and refuses any export below 90% of HEAD (line 236: export_rows * 10 < head_rows * 9). It re-exports from Dolt rather than trusting the working file, so a reverted or mid-write file is unreachable. Nothing about it needs changing.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE FAILING PATH DOES NOT USE IT. Commit 4d8042d80d — "chore(beads): audit merged PR #7063" — committed .beads/issues.jsonl at ZERO ROWS, a single commit deleting 2573 lines. It was made with a plain git add, not through the checkpoint script, so the floor never ran. Working tree, index and HEAD were all empty afterwards and git status was CLEAN — nothing on screen said anything was wrong.

AND THIS IS A RECURRENCE, NOT A FIRST. The checkpoint script own comment records it: "A git add that catches the JSONL mid-rewrite has landed an empty export on main before (incident 2026-06-10, commit 7aea52459)." Six weeks apart, same mechanism, and the mitigation written after the first incident did not cover the path that caused the second.

THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS REPO KEEPS FINDING: sound machinery, and the case it exists to catch arrives by a route it cannot see. Five-plus instances this week — a bijection gate green on all seven planted defects, a conformance projector that had never run over a real record, a checker that accepted a FILE as its scan directory and greened over zero, a CHECK C that could collapse its own population to nothing, and this.

THE FIX, and it should be cheap: PUT THE ROW FLOOR IN THE PRE-COMMIT HOOK, where it protects EVERY path rather than the one that already knows about it. scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh already inspects staged .beads paths — it enforces WHO may commit them (workers may not) but says nothing about CONTENT. Adding "if .beads/issues.jsonl is staged and its row count is 0, or below 90% of HEAD, refuse" reuses the checkpoint script own thresholds in the one place no committer can bypass.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT:
  1. THE HOOK MUST NOT BLOCK A GENUINE MASS DELETE. The checkpoint script answer is "refuse and say so; a genuine mass delete is rare enough to commit by hand" — mirror that, with the escape named in the message.
  2. IT MUST WORK FOR THE AUDIT PROCESS TOO. Hooks live in the primary checkout hooks directory and worktrees share it, but confirm the audit committer actually has hooks installed — scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check reports whether a checkout is guarded. A hook nobody installed is the same blindness one layer down.

RECOVERY IS NOT PART OF THIS BEAD AND IS ALREADY DONE: the Dolt database was never at risk, bd list worked throughout, and beads-checkpoint.sh regenerated 2576 rows over a HEAD of 0. Record that an empty export is a REGENERATION event, not a data-loss one — restoring an older export from git history would time-travel the tracker, reopening closed beads and vanishing new ones.
notes:
PR #7079 (branch worker/guard-ledger), NOT closed — mayor closes on the merged SHA.

FIX: a third pre-commit marker block, `beads-truncation-floor`, calling a new `check_beads_truncation` in scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh. The checkpoint script is UNCHANGED — its guard was always sound.

THE CRUX, and the reason the fix could not just be folded into check_beads_boundary: that classifier is gated by `rf2_beads_in_primary_worktree`, so it deliberately no-ops in the MAYOR checkout — which is exactly where 4d8042d80d and 7aea52459 were both made. The new block runs in EVERY worktree, primary included, with no marker file and no worktree derivation.

ONE CONDITION, the same arithmetic as beads-checkpoint.sh:236 (`staged*10 < head*9`), guarded by `head_rows > 0`. With HEAD non-empty a staged 0 is just the extreme of the same shrink, so there is one floor and one spelling of it; only the message branches on the count.

ITEM 2 ANSWERED: `sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check` in the mayor checkout exits 0 — that checkout WAS guarded and current when the empty export landed. So the blindness was not a missing install; it was a hook with no opinion about content. Landing this makes every installed checkout stale by one block, which the existing rf2-zt65l post-merge/post-rewrite advisory reports on the next pull.

ITEM 1 ANSWERED: a genuine mass delete is refused and the message names `git commit --no-verify` (after `bd status`), mirroring the checkpoint script's own "rare enough to commit by hand".

THE RULE IS IN THE MESSAGE: an empty export is a REGENERATION event, not a data-loss one; restoring an older export from git history would TIME-TRAVEL the tracker.

NOT EXTENDED to scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh: a mayor checkpoint goes to main directly and never appears in a PR diff, so neither incident could have been seen there.

PROVED BY MUTATION, three source mutants, each grep-confirmed applied before the verdict was read: (A) floor never fires -> 9a and 9b FALSE GREEN, rc=1; (B) floor over-fires -> 9c FALSE POSITIVE plus the pre-existing mayor-checkpoint scenarios (a) and (h) break, rc=1; (C) drop --no-verify from the escape case -> 9d fails, rc=1. All reverted, 66 passed / 0 failed, grep -c RF2MUTANT = 0. Mutation C also exposed a cascade where 9e/9f inherited 9d's side effect and reported misleading failures; both now establish their own precondition.

title: viewer.cljs makes day8/re-frame2-machines-viz unloadable for a consumer, and both obvious repairs are wrong (adapter-ns collision + un-rewritten pom coord)
description:
Split out of rf2-3d5u3, which fixed the uix.core half and deliberately held this one.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND PROVEN. Simulated a consumer whose ONLY dep is the published machines-viz coordinate (no repo :source-paths, no borrowed classpath) and compiled an entry ns requiring day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.viewer:

  The required namespace "re-frame.adapter.reagent" is not available, it was
  required by "day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/viewer.cljs".   rc=1

Fails at namespace LOAD, not first use. viewer.cljs:49 requires it and :152 calls (rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter).

WHY THE OBVIOUS REPAIR (add day8/re-frame2-reagent to :deps) WAS REFUSED — two independent reasons, both measured:

1. ADAPTER-NS COLLISION FOR SLIM APPS. day8/reagent-slim publishes ITS adapter at the canonical re-frame.adapter.reagent ns — release.yml's 'Rename adapter ns at publication (reagent-slim only)' step mv's reagent_slim.cljs -> reagent.cljs and rewrites the (ns ...) form before clein packages. release.yml states outright that downstream apps depend on EXACTLY ONE of {day8/re-frame2-reagent, day8/reagent-slim} so the adapter ns is single-source per app. A hard dep from machines-viz puts BOTH on a reagent-slim app's classpath, one bound to reagent.* and one to reagent2.*, and classpath order silently decides which the app's own (:require [re-frame.adapter.reagent]) resolves to. IN-TREE THE SLIM NS IS STILL reagent_slim, so the monorepo build can never surface this — the same masking mechanism rf2-3d5u3 is about, one layer over.

   (Stock reagent/reagent, already a machines-viz dep, does NOT collide: slim ships its Reagent as reagent2.*.)

2. IT WOULD NOT REACH THE PUBLISHED POM ANYWAY. clein pom SILENTLY SKIPS :local/root coordinates (rf2-do3m2 / #6340), which is why every leaf's release step rewrites :local/root -> :mvn/version first. release-machines-viz.yml calls rewrite-local-root-coord.sh ONCE, for '../../implementation/core'. A second in-repo coordinate is simply never rewritten and is dropped from the pom without a word. ssr-ring is today's ONLY leaf with two in-repo coords and it needs a second rewrite call (matrix extra-local-root, release.yml:738-739) to work. So the hard dep buys nothing published while introducing (1) for source consumers.

THE SHAPE THAT RESOLVES IT, and this is the ruling to make: viewer.cljs is a PAGE entry (^:export run, mounted by public/viewer.html), not library surface. Choosing a substrate adapter is an APPLICATION's job; this jar is a library, and core is deliberately adapter-free for exactly this reason. Moving the page out of the packaged :src-dirs takes the require with it, drops reagent.dom.client from the jar's requirements too, and needs no dep at all. That is a packaging + spec/API.md §Read-only viewer change, hence a ruling rather than a repair.

IF THE HARD DEP IS CHOSEN INSTEAD, it is incomplete without a fenced workflow edit: release-machines-viz.yml needs a SECOND rewrite-local-root-coord.sh call for ../../implementation/adapters/reagent, in the ssr-ring shape. Landing the dep without it publishes a pom that still omits the adapter — the defect surviving behind a deps.edn that looks fixed.

.github/workflows/** was fenced to a live lane worker for the rf2-3d5u3 dispatch, so neither half was attempted there.
close_reason: PR #7071 MERGED. This bead existed because a worker REFUSED half its own parent fix, and the refusal was correct: declaring re-frame.adapter.reagent as a hard dep would have put TWO adapters at the same canonical namespace on a slim app classpath — release.yml renames reagent_slim.cljs to reagent.cljs before packaging, downstream apps must depend on EXACTLY ONE, and CLASSPATH ORDER WOULD PICK THE SUBSTRATE. The masking was the exquisite part: IN-TREE THE SLIM NS IS STILL reagent_slim, SO THE MONOREPO BUILD CANNOT SEE THE COLLISION — the same class of defect the parent bead was about, one layer up. And it would not have reached the pom anyway: clein pom silently skips :local/root.

title: tools/machines-viz under-declares two deps its own src requires (uix.core, re-frame.adapter.reagent)
description:
Found while building the per-tool CLJS lane for rf2-odlm3 (PR #7063). Two namespaces in the PUBLISHED day8/re-frame2-machines-viz jar :require libraries the artefact's deps.edn :deps map does not declare:

  * src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/adapters/uix.cljs  ->  uix.core       (com.pitch/uix.core, com.pitch/uix.dom)
  * src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/viewer.cljs        ->  re-frame.adapter.reagent  (day8/re-frame2-reagent)

Both compile today ONLY because implementation/shadow-cljs.edn carries com.pitch/uix.{core,dom} in its own :dependencies and puts adapters/reagent/src on :source-paths, and borrows the machines-viz tree onto that classpath. A consumer whose only tool dep is day8/re-frame2-machines-viz cannot compile either namespace.

This is the rf2-r8trk shape one artefact over (Story could not compile its shell for a consumer whose only tool dep was day8/re-frame2-story, because the repo-wide Shadow build masked the omission with a global :source-paths entry).

REPRODUCTION: cd tools/machines-viz && clojure -M:cljs-test -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile machines-viz-node-test with the two deps removed from the :cljs-test alias. First failure: 'The required namespace "uix.core" is not available, it was required by "day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/adapters/uix.cljs"'. Second: 'The required namespace "re-frame.adapter.reagent" is not available, it was required by "day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/viewer.cljs"'.

PR #7063 declared both on the new TEST-only :cljs-test alias, with the finding recorded beside each entry, so the lane could be measured. It deliberately did NOT change the published graph.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD CARRIES: uix is an OPTIONAL adapter (adapters/uix.cljs is one of several substrate adapters) so a hard :deps entry may be the wrong answer — a provided/optional posture, or moving the adapter behind a late-bind hook the way core does for reagent, may be better. The reagent adapter in viewer.cljs looks like a plain missing runtime dep. Whoever takes it should also check the sibling artefacts for the same shape, since the masking mechanism (one consolidated classpath) is repo-wide.

(2) It would not reach the pom anyway: clein pom silently skips :local/root and the release workflow rewrites exactly one path. Filed rf2-k7l2o with the better shape: viewer.cljs is a PAGE entry, not library surface — move it out of the packaged :src-dirs and the require disappears. description:

- tools/story/test/re_frame/story/panels_e2e/share_url_state_popstate_stale_override_dom_cljs_test.cljs imports tools/story/test/re_frame/story/test_helpers/e2e_multi_frame.cljs.
- tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels_e2e/reactive_data_view_rows_dom_cljs_test.cljs imports test_helpers/e2e_multi_frame.cljs and test_helpers/host_fixtures/counter.cljs.
Direct classification of those helper paths returns cljs_browser=false, so a breaking helper-only PR runs the Node compile (where DOM suites self-skip) and skips their only real Chromium assertions.

A second concrete edge is tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj. re-frame.story.cljc delegates every public registration macro to this CLJ-only namespace; changing its emitted forms can change what Story DOM suites compile and mount, yet the new source predicate excludes .clj and leaves cljs_browser=false.

Keep the fix narrow: model the direct browser-suite support seams, not every test file and not a general dependency graph. The parent rf2-1sd8h is IN_PROGRESS and tracker-locked, so this audit records the residual in a follow-up rather than editing it.
acceptance_criteria: Known Story/Xray support files directly required by live *_dom_cljs_test suites arm cljs_browser, including Story/Xray e2e_multi_frame helpers and Xray host fixtures. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj also arms cljs_browser because it is the compile-time producer behind re-frame.story.cljc. Add focused changed-surface positives for each real edge plus controls that unrelated JVM-only tests/spec files remain excluded; retain cljs_node_test and existing gate outputs. The PR's cljs-browser job must execute real assertions for the importing DOM namespaces.

description:

title: story-mcp generic handler catch is still not wire-safe for opaque ex-data outside :explain
description:
Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7042.

WHAT #7042 FIXED. tools.result/wire-safe-ex-data correctly replaces the registrar's raw Malli :explain with :explain-humanized. The common register-variant typo path now returns the intended isError result, so rf2-2z9u3 itself remains correctly closed.

THE RESIDUAL. The helper's name/doc and the PR make a stronger generic promise: invoke-tool's belt-and-braces catch routes every handler throw through it so a handler exception cannot become a protocol fault. But the implementation only special-cases the top-level :explain key and passes every other ex-data value through unchanged. Any opaque value under another key still reaches Cheshire and recreates the same -32603.

REAL BOUNDARY REPRO on the merged code. Drive server/run-loop! with initialize then tools/call get-variant; seam story/variant->edn to throw (ex-info "opaque throw" {:opaque (Object.)}). The raw id=2 response is:

  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: class java.lang.Object: ...","data":{"exception":"com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonGenerationException"}}}

The smaller direct proof is likewise decisive: Cheshire cannot encode (wire-safe-ex-data {:opaque (Object.)}). The helper returns the Object untouched.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE. The original P1's reachable Malli producer is fixed. This is the latent generic-fallback contract #7042 chose to claim and implement at wire_pipeline.cljc: the catch that is supposed to contain arbitrary handler failures still fails for arbitrary ex-data. No existing Bead covered it. rf2-2nbck is a different structured error-id spelling bug.
acceptance_criteria: Make the generic invoke-tool failure path total at the JSON-RPC boundary. A handler throw may carry arbitrary nested ex-data; constructing and encoding its tool error must not throw or become -32603. Preserve ordinary wire-safe data and the existing :explain -> :explain-humanized behavior; represent or omit unsupported values with explicit bounded loss rather than leaking object addresses. Add a real server/run-loop! boundary test with an opaque value under a non-:explain key, including a nested occurrence, plus controls for Malli explain and plain ex-data. Ensure the sanitation/projection itself cannot escape the generic catch.
notes:
DELIVERED in PR #7056 (worker/reopens, commit c8ddd683c4), NOT closed — mayor closes on the merged SHA.

CLASS: fresh work, and not a reopen at all — filed new 2026-07-26 by the #7042 audit. #7042's fix for the reachable Malli producer is correct and rf2-2z9u3 stays closed; this is the GENERIC promise #7042 additionally chose to make and did not keep.

FOUND, at the real boundary. Driving server/run-loop! (initialize + tools/call get-variant) with story/variant->edn seamed to throw (ex-info "opaque throw" {:opaque (Object.)}), the id=2 line was:
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: class java.lang.Object: java.lang.Object@5d9d7f05","data":{"exception":"com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonGenerationException"}}}
Note the leaked identity-hash address in the message.

CHANGED — THE RULE IS THE VALUE'S SHAPE, NOT A ROSTER OF SLOTS. tools.result/wire-safe-value keeps a value when it is EDN data (nil, boolean, number, string, keyword, symbol, char, uuid, inst, or a collection of those) and replaces anything else with {:rf.story-mcp/unencodable "<class name>"}. Class name only — str of a bare Object carries an address. Map KEYS go through the same projection, because an opaque key does NOT throw: Cheshire strs it and leaks the address into a JSON member name, the worse failure because nothing reddens. The projection sits under its own guard so neither a throwing me/humanize nor an arbitrarily deep ex-data can escape the catch it exists to serve.

:explain and :rf.error/id stay named and NEITHER is load-bearing for encodability any more — the walk renders both safe on its own. They are vocabulary: :explain-humanized beats a marker, and :rf.error is story-mcp's own wire spelling of the thrown discriminator.

AFTER (same drive):
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Tool handler threw: opaque throw"}],"isError":true,"structuredContent":{"tool":"get-variant","exception":"clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo","data":{"opaque":{"rf.story-mcp/unencodable":"java.lang.Object"}}}}}

NO NEW :rf.error/* ID. :rf.story-mcp/unencodable labels a value that was WITHHELD, not a failure that occurred, and joins the existing tool-owned :rf.story-mcp/* vocabulary. It is outside check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py's scan surface (implementation/ only), so no fenced file is involved.

MUTATION PROOF. Planting `identity` in place of the walk (confirmed applied by git diff --stat and by grepping PLANTED back out) reddens exactly the three new run-loop! boundary tests and the all-shapes direct proof — 11 failures / 7 errors, rc=1 — while every pre-existing test stays green, INCLUDING the :explain arm #7042 fixed and both new controls. So the new coverage is not re-proving the old fix and the old fix is not masking the new one.

GATES. tools/story-mcp 303 tests / 1590 assertions, 0 failures / 0 errors, rc=0 (baseline 298/1565; +5 deftests / +25 assertions, exact). tools/mcp-base 272/924 0/0 rc=0, exactly the baseline. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS rc=0. Spec updated in the same PR: tools/story-mcp/spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md §Run-loop survivability and spec/API.md.

title: epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test's resource cascade inhabits ONE operation shape, so the free :scope tag family is invisible to it
description:

THE BLINDNESS, verified: epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj's drive-resource-family! dispatches exactly two [:rf.resource/ensure ...] and one [:rf.resource/release-owner ...]. SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLINDNESS: both fixture resources are registered :scope :rf.scope/global. A global scope is a SCALAR, which is exactly the value that correctly rides verbatim. The [tier {identity}] tuple shape — the shape that leaked — does not occur anywhere in that fixture, so even a row that did carry :scope would have proven nothing.

WHY IT IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM THE LAST WIDENING: the recent widening inhabited the resource family with a :sensitive? owner and a plain owner, which closed the SLOT-SHAPE blind spot (named slot vs unnamed slot vs embedded work-id). It did not close the OPERATION blind spot. resource-family-op? routes on namespace, so the gate's fixture needs to inhabit operations, not only slots — and a projector bug that is operation-conditional (which rf2-1zc33's was: the sibling ran on ONE op while the family projector ran on all of them) is invisible until it does.

DO NOT rebuild the gate, add a second scanner, or generalise into a fixture framework. One fixture gains one more inhabited operation.

title: tools/ thrown-error subset IS consumer-reachable: story-mcp relays ex-message onto the MCP tool surface, so registrar's bare-keyword throws reach consumer AI
description:
Found by the rf2-eo2y5 "what would change this ruling" check (the ruling asked for exactly one pass over the 38 tools/ sites before closing).

THE RULING'S CONDITION IS MET. rf2-eo2y5 ruled tools/ out of scope for the Spec 009 thrown-error shape on the ground that "its errors are seen by a developer running an inspection tool, never caught by a consumer app", and named the condition that would change it: "if any of those 38 sites throws an error that reaches a CONSUMER -- via the MCP tool surface, a published skill, or an error a consumer app can catch -- then the shape governs it and that subset is real work."

THE CONFIRMED CHAIN (traced end to end, not inferred):

  tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:262-274
    (defn- register-or-error [vk body-v]
      (try (story/reg-variant* vk (assoc body-v :origin config/origin)) ...
        (catch Throwable e
          (result/error-result (str "Registration failed: " (ex-message e)) ...))))

  -> re-frame.story.registrar/reg-variant* (registrar.cljc:451)
       calls assert-id! (:471) and validate-shape! (:477)

  -> registrar.cljc:365  (throw (ex-info (str error-kw) {:rf.error/id error-kw ...}))
     registrar.cljc:302  (throw (ex-info (str error-kw) {:rf.error/id error-kw ...}))

`error-kw` is built as (keyword \"rf.error\" (str (name kind) \"-shape\")) / \"-id-shape\", so ex-message is EXACTLY the stringified discriminator. An MCP client -- an AI agent, i.e. the \"consumer AI\" whose reading is the stated reason the shape is a contract -- calling story-mcp's register-variant with a malformed body receives, verbatim:

    Registration failed: :rf.error/variant-id-shape

That is the precise regression rf2-vvixub abolished, on a tool surface a consumer AI reads, with the human sentence available in ex-data :reason and discarded.

TWO MORE RELAYS ON THE SAME SURFACE, same shape, unaudited per-site:
  * tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:385
        (result/error-result (str \"Tool handler threw: \" (ex-message e)) ...)
    -- a catch-all: ANY story handler throw relays its message.
  * tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:40
        {... :reason (ex-message e)}
  * tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:535-539
        invoke-and-guard's .catch -> {:ok? false :reason :handler-threw :message (.-message err)}
    -- reaches tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/eval_form.cljs:128 and
       .../tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:268, both bare-keyword.

WHAT IS *NOT* REACHABLE (checked, so the subset stays honest):
  * server.cljs:321 / :331 (pair-mcp discovery). handle-call*'s .catch at :563 builds its payload from ex-DATA (:rf.error/id, :hint, :candidates) and never relays ex-message; the message only reaches stderr via log!. Correct by construction -- this is the shape the other relays should copy.
  * mcp-base cursor.cljc:123/188/218. Their own docstrings say \"Caught by the surrounding try in decode-cursor -> ::malformed\" and cursor.cljc:334 confirms `(catch ... _ ::malformed)` -- the message is swallowed, the sentinel is the contract.

TWO OF THE 38 ARE GATE FALSE POSITIVES, not defects:
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:877 and :914 already build a conformant message -- human sentence + trailing [:rf.error/<id>] token, with a comment citing Spec 009 and the bundle-isolation constraint -- but bind it to a local `msg` before the throw. The gate inspects the TEXT of ex-info's first argument, so `msg` shows neither a human-message call nor a literal token and it reports builder-bypass-message. Any future conformant let-bound message under implementation/ would false-red the same way.

SCOPE OF THE REAL WORK (deliberately small): convert only the sites whose ex-message is relayed to a consumer surface. registrar.cljc:302 and :365 are the confirmed pair; plan.cljc:137 (`fail!`, same (str id) shape, reachable from the same registration path) is the near neighbour. Everything else in the 38 stays out of scope under rf2-eo2y5 unless a relay is found for it. Hand-roll the shape inline as story.cljc:877/914 already do -- tools/ MUST NOT :require re-frame.error.
notes:
FINAL: PR #7036 head 8b52a45497. CI GREEN — 32 pass / 43 skipping / 0 fail / 0 pending. MERGEABLE. Left OPEN for the mayor to close on the merged SHA. Follow-ups filed: rf2-2z9u3 (P1, malli :explain not JSON-encodable -> -32603 masks the register-variant diagnostic entirely) and rf2-u3otj (P3, gate blind spot on let-bound / computed-discriminator messages).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7036: IMPLEMENTATION CORRECT, COMPLETION STILL OPEN FOR DURABLE BOUNDARY PROOF. The three authored commits land exactly and the relay inventory is careful: the converted messages render a human sentence plus the trailing token, the unreachable subsets stay untouched, assert-id reachability is corrected, and the raw Malli explain masking fault is separated to rf2-2z9u3 rather than hidden here.

What did not land is a permanent regression for the behavior this P2 exists to protect. The PR changes six source/comment files and zero test files. Its manual before/after JSON-RPC probe is good evidence for that run, but current main has no test containing the new consumer-visible phrases or tokens for pair-mcp rt-let, unknown wire kind, Story unknown-tag/plan failure, or diff-encode validation. Existing Story tests assert ex-data IDs only. The default thrown-message gate excludes tools/, and four computed-discriminator conversions are deliberately invisible even to an explicit tools scan, so reverting any of those messages to a bare keyword remains a green CI change.

Close the remaining gap with one small table through the existing real boundary helpers, not seven new unit suites: Story MCP handle-frame rows for one registrar failure and one plan failure; pair MCP invoke-and-guard/handle-call rows covering the rt-let binding, unknown wire kind, and diff-encode validation families. Each row should assert an error result rather than a protocol fault, a human phrase, and the exact trailing [:rf.error/...] token; retain the existing machine-id/ex-data assertions where that surface carries them. A mutation back to the pre-PR bare message must red these rows. The #7042 schema-explain regression may count for validate-shape, but it does not cover the other families. No new checker, builder, or broad tools sweep is needed.
close_reason:
Boundary proof landed in PR #7123 (branch worker/story-mcp-cluster). The CODE fix was already correct from #7036 — verified: re-frame.story.registrar validate-shape!/assert-id!/validate-tag-membership! and re-frame.story.plan/fail! all build the Spec 009 shape today, so nothing needed changing. What was missing was the regression the merged-PR audit asked for.

DELIVERED (story-mcp half): one table of three plan-failure families driven through the REAL boundary (server/run-loop!, no with-redefs) in tools/story-mcp/test/re_frame/story_mcp/wire_encodability_test.clj — story-extends-unknown, story-extends-cycle, story-compose-unknown. Each row asserts (a) a tool error not a -32603 protocol fault, (b) the human sentence, (c) the exact trailing [:rf.error/<id>] token. Plus a companion row keeping the machine :rf.error/id assertion through wire-safe-ex-data, and a two-sided happy-path control.

MUTATION-VERIFIED as the audit required: reverting fail! to (str id) reds exactly 6 assertions — the human+token rows for all three families — and NOTHING else. tool-error? and the ex-data id still pass under the mutation, which is precisely why the pre-existing tests could not catch this class.

The registrar half (variant-shape, unknown-tag) was ALREADY pinned at the same boundary by #7042's work, so it needed no new rows; the audit's 'one registrar failure and one plan failure' is therefore satisfied.

PAIR-MCP HALF NOT DONE — split to rf2-eaf20 (P2). tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ was outside this worker's file-ownership fence and is CLJS with a different test harness, so the story-mcp helpers do not transfer. The rt-let / unknown-wire-kind / diff-encode families remain unpinned exactly as the audit described.

Also filed: rf2-zrdog (P2) — record-as-variant-no-cofx-is-byte-identical flakes in aggregate runs (recorder captures 0 events); characterised as pre-existing, not from this diff.

title: Reconcile the 23 Spec 009 Tags-column rows the keys-set arm reds on (blocks rf2-6tags)
description:
BLOCKS rf2-6tags. The Tags-column keys-set arm is designed, measured and proven non-vacuous, but it CANNOT BE ARMED until these rows are reconciled, because it reds on them.

MEASUREMENT (worker/gate-detectors, PR #7027, against origin/main 5026a73078). The arm pairs a catalogue category to its schema by PascalCasing the name (:rf.error/resource-route-plan -> ResourceRoutePlanTags), diffs the schema's key set against the row's :tags column, and excludes exactly the two envelope slots the catalogue's own rule at spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1948 names ("Two envelope-level slots are therefore deliberately absent from every row" — :recovery and :category). That rule also says the column "lists the keys that genuinely ride under :tags on the wire — nothing else", so every finding below is a row the catalogue's own contract requires to change.

  pre-fix ded86cff64 (parent of the rf2-wsopx fix): 90 paired rows, 24 findings, INCLUDING :rf.error/resource-route-plan -> missing :contributor, :plan-cause
  main    5026a73078:                               90 paired rows, 23 findings, resource-route-plan absent (fixed)

So the arm reds on exactly its motivating defect and greens on the fix. The residual 23 are pre-existing instances of the same class — 44 undocumented schema keys.

THE 23 ROWS (schema keys the Tags column omits):
  :rf.error/coeffect-exception        (CoeffectExceptionTags)      :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception-message
  :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded      (DrainDepthExceededTags)     :frame
  :rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return (EffectHandlerBadReturnTags) :event-id :event
  :rf.error/flow-eval-exception       (FlowEvalExceptionTags)      :event
  :rf.error/fx-handler-exception      (FxHandlerExceptionTags)     :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/handler-exception         (HandlerExceptionTags)       :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/interceptor-exception     (InterceptorExceptionTags)   :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/machine-action-exception  (MachineActionExceptionTags) :event :handler-id :frame
  :rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1 (MachineGrammarNotInV1Tags)  :substitute
  :rf.error/malformed-schema          (MalformedSchemaTags)        :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/no-such-sub               (NoSuchSubTags)              :frame
  :rf.error/override-fallthrough      (OverrideFallthroughTags)    :failing-id
  :rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args          (RegSubBadArgsTags)          :frame
  :rf.error/sanitised-on-projection   (SanitisedOnProjectionTags)  :exception-message :returned :reason
  :rf.error/sub-exception             (SubExceptionTags)           :failing-id
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-bad-return   (SubInputFnBadReturnTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-exception    (SubInputFnExceptionTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/system-id-collision       (SystemIdCollisionTags)      :reason
  :rf.http/stale-suppressed           (StaleSuppressedTags)        :carried-token :current-token :event-id
  :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed(StaleSuppressedTags)        :event-id
  :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch          (HydrationMismatchTags)      :first-diff-path
  :rf.warning/multiple-redirects      (MultipleRedirectsTags)      :frame
  :rf.warning/multiple-status-set     (MultipleStatusSetTags)      :frame

THE ADJUDICATION NEEDED. Not all 23 are necessarily row-side. Several are ALIAS divergences: the schema declares :event / :event-id where the row documents :rf.event/v / :rf.trace/event-id. The 009 frame-destroyed row itself states the distinction ("The bare :event spelling is the ERROR-tag spelling ... :rf.event/v is the dispatch-PIPELINE spelling"), so for those the SCHEMA may be the side that is wrong. The rest (:frame on nine rows, :reason on four, :failing-id on four) look like plain row omissions. Each needs a one-line call: fix the row, or fix the schema.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN PR #7027. The dispatch fenced spec/009-Instrumentation.md's row content with an explicit instruction: "you are building the checker, not editing rows; if a row genuinely must change, STOP and tell me". Twenty-three rows genuinely must change. Reporting rather than editing.

ALSO MEASURED, against the ruling's premise. Spec-Schemas.md defines 111 *Tags schemas; the error/warning catalogue has 489 rows, not one schema per row. 89 schemas pair by name derivation, 22 do not (FxHandledTags, MachineUnhandledNoOpTags, SchemaValidationTags, NoSuchCofxTags, RoutePrefetchedTags, InvalidResourceSpecTags, BadAppSchemasArgTags, LargeValueUnschemadTags, ArtefactMissingTags, HttpInterceptorClearedTags, HttpInterceptorRegisteredTags, FxSkippedOnPlatformTags, DbReplacedTags, DecodeDefaultedTags, HeadMismatchTags, EpochCbSilencedOnFrameDestroyTags, InterceptorsInMetadataMapTags, InvalidMutationSpecTags, MachineActionRanTags, MachineGuardEvaluatedTags, MachineTimerCancelledTags, UnwrapBadEventShapeTags). Explicit in-row `Spec-Schemas §`XxxTags`` citations exist on only 3 of 489 rows, so citation is not a usable pairing key either. Closing those 22 needs either row edits or an alias table — and an alias table is the hand-maintained roster the rf2-6tags ruling forbids. Worth a second ruling alongside the 23.

REJECTED VARIANTS, for the record. Restricting the diff to non-optional schema keys gives 13 findings on BOTH the pre-fix and post-fix trees — VACUOUS on the motivating defect, because :contributor and :plan-cause are both {:optional true}. Widening the containment test from the Tags cell to the whole row changes nothing (24/23). Row->schema as the direction cannot catch the defect at all: the pre-fix row was a strict subset of its schema, which a subset check satisfies.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7030 (2026-07-26): KEEP OPEN. The PR correctly adjudicated and changed 18 catalogue rows, corrected 3 schemas, documented the http stale-suppressed name collision, and landed its three-commit series exactly with all required CI green. One of the original 23 findings remains despite the PR description claiming it was fixed: the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch Tags cell still spells the optional wire key :first-diff-path? at merge a337891285 and on current main. The emitter at implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc conditionally assocs :first-diff-path, Spec 011 names :first-diff-path, and HydrationMismatchTags declares :first-diff-path. The merged diff contains no hydration-row edit. This leaves the catalogue contract false and leaves rf2-zk1xu incomplete/blocking rf2-6tags. Bounded completion: change the Tags cell to the literal :first-diff-path and state optionality in prose; prove the Tags-column key parser observes the literal key. The adjacent findings disclosed in #7030 are already durably owned by later current-main Beads/work (rf2-qk8vj, rf2-k91an, rf2-dxuzp), so no duplicate Bead was created.
close_reason: PR #7109 merged. Last of the 23 Spec 009 Tags-column findings (#7030 corrected the other 22); tags-column-shrink-only-baseline now EMPTY, promoting tags-column-keys-are-documented to an unqualified invariant. Unblocks rf2-6tags.

title: Routing doors disagree on a path param the route pattern does not capture
description:
Found while settling rf2-kqxe6.7 (EP-0037 R3 prefetch identity). NOT prefetch-specific: the two ACTIVATION doors already disagree with each other, and prefetch merely inherits one of the two answers.

Route /probe/:id. Address {:to :route/probe :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}} — :extra is a path param the pattern does not capture, so route-url silently ignores it and builds "/probe/7".

MEASURED on JVM (worker/ep0037-remainder, post-fix):
  - programmatic [:rf.route/navigate {:to … :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}}]
      commits :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}
  - a real rf/route-link CLICK (link/link-model -> [:rf.route/url-requested {:url "/probe/7" :to … :params {…}}])
      commits :params {:id "7"} — it resolves through the URL, which cannot carry :extra
  - [:rf.route/prefetch …] warms {:id "7" :extra "x"} (it agrees with the programmatic door)

So hovering a link warms one resource identity and clicking that SAME link activates another — R3's original failure mode, by a different route than the one #6976 named. But the root cause is the door disagreement, not prefetch: Spec 012 §The one planning pipeline says doors differ in cause and history/scroll policy, NOT in target.

RULING NEEDED (this is a contract decision, not a worker fix — it changes :rf.route/navigate semantics):
  (a) reject an uncaptured path param at the address gate as a caller bug (fail-loud, consistent with route-url raising :rf.error/missing-route-param for the inverse), or
  (b) have the ResolvedTarget seam drop path params the route pattern does not capture, so every door commits the URL-expressible identity.

(a) is the fail-loud house style and surfaces the typo; (b) is silent but total. Either way it is ONE rule at ONE place — the address gate or resolve/resolved-target — not a per-door patch.

Deliberately NOT fixed on the rf2-kqxe6.7 PR: that bead's residual was prefetch-vs-navigation, and the two normalisations it did own (nil query values, empty fragment) are fixed at the seam there. A test arm on that PR records this gap and points here rather than asserting either answer.
notes:
MAYOR RATIFICATION (2026-07-27): the worker's ruling STANDS — an uncaptured path param is REJECTED LOUD at route-url (:rf.error/route-url-validation, :reason :uncaptured-params). Merged as PR #7120.

WHY I RATIFIED RATHER THAN REVERSED:
1. It honours an EXISTING spec rule rather than inventing a new stance. spec/012 Validity rule 2 states verbatim that letting address keys 'ride beside it and be silently ignored is the exact failure class this grammar exists to kill'. Verified in the source at spec/012:460.
2. route-url ALREADY fails closed on emission for every other prism break (the empty-string segment, the sequential-optional-group prefix chain). Truncating here would make this the one prism break that passes silently.
3. The decisive argument is the typo class truncation would swallow: /docs{/:section}? with {:sction "x"} elides the optional group and builds /docs cleanly, so :rf.error/missing-route-param can NEVER fire. Silent truncation converts a typo into a wrong-but-plausible URL, which is the worst available outcome.
4. POSTURE CHECK: 'trust the programmer' does not mean 'stay quiet when the programmer typed something the URL cannot carry'. A loud, actionable, immediate error is GOOD ergonomics and low friction; a silently divergent URL is neither. This is not a nag diagnostic.
5. One rule in one place: route-url is the boundary all three named-address doors already share, so prefetch needed NO code (it maps route-url's error ids verbatim per Spec 009) and the URL-driven doors need no rule at all. The single exemption, :rf.route/not-found, is principled — its slice :params are the framework's miss record, not path captures.

REVERSAL RECIPE, if Mike overturns: ~10 lines (swap the throw for a select-keys) plus flipping two pinned tests. The full argument is in PR #7120's body.

FOLLOW-ON SEQUENCED: rf2-jx5bw (P2) records the rejection in spec/012 Bidirectional URL<->params and widens the :rf.error/route-url-validation row in spec/009 to list :reason/:keys. Prose only, no new reserved error id. spec/009 was held by PR #7124 which has now MERGED, so rf2-jx5bw is dispatchable.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #7120 (worker/routing-doors-0iuh3).

DECISION TAKEN — neither committed value wins. An uncaptured path param is REJECTED LOUD at route-url (:rf.error/route-url-validation, :reason :uncaptured-params), i.e. the bead's option (a) fail-loud, sited at the registry-aware EMISSION boundary rather than the registry-free structural address gate. One rule at one place: route-url is the boundary all three named-address doors already share (programmatic URL build, route-link href synthesis, prefetch destination gate — prefetch needed NO code, it maps route-url's error ids verbatim). The URL-driven doors need no rule: a URL cannot carry an uncaptured param.

WHY NOT (b) drop-at-the-seam: the round-trip argument kills committing :extra, but truncation is the OTHER wrong answer. Spec 012 §Validity rules rule 2 already calls silently-ignored address keys 'the exact failure class this grammar exists to kill'; route-url already fails closed on emission for every other prism break (empty-string segment, sequential-optional-group prefix chain); and truncation swallows a typo class nothing else catches (/docs{/:section}? with {:sction "x"} elides the group and builds /docs clean, so :rf.error/missing-route-param can never fire). Dropping at resolved-target would additionally have had to special-case the reserved :rf.route/not-found params anyway — silently.

ONE EXEMPTION: :rf.route/not-found (its slice :params are the framework's miss record {:url … :reason …}, not path captures). Pinned by tests on both a helper and a live door.

MAYOR: the bead asked for a RULING and the worker took one — please ratify. Reversing to silent truncation is a ~10-line change (swap the throw for a select-keys) plus flipping the two pinned tests; the PR body carries the full argument.

Reproduced first as a failing test (27/43 assertions red on unmodified source, matching this bead's JVM measurements verbatim), then fixed. routing_registry_test/route-url-ignores-extra-path-params — the test that pinned the losing behaviour — was FLIPPED and renamed, not deleted.
