title: [BUG] minimal-counter claims HMR but :init-fn is initial-only, so Freehand mount never reruns
description:
Three-lens audit of merged PR #7020 found one bounded runtime/documentation defect in the otherwise complete minimal-counter Freehand cut-over.

The scaffold's shadow-cljs.edn and README say the :browser target re-runs the module :init-fn after every hot reload, so no separate after-load hook is needed. The app's run function carries only ^:export, and the build has no :devtools :after-load callback. Shadow's documented lifecycle defines module :init-fn as initial-load-only and provides ^:dev/after-load / :devtools :after-load for post-reload work: https://shadow-cljs.github.io/docs/UsersGuide.html

That distinction is load-bearing here. Freehand's mount path reuses the existing React root/frame, republishes the fresh descriptor/body, and avoids replaying initial events; existing mounted React work does not otherwise invoke the newly loaded root body merely because the namespace was hot-loaded. As shipped, edited scaffold views can remain stale until a full page reload, contradicting the scaffold's state-preserving HMR claim.

rf2-nutll is the exact migration owner but is currently in_progress and therefore locked. No exact existing owner for this scaffold lifecycle gap was found, so this is a distinct dependent follow-up rather than a mutation or duplicate of the parent. rf2-vxgfnd.281 owns the already-completed initial runnable scaffold, not this newly introduced Freehand reload regression.
design: Use the smallest native Shadow lifecycle wiring: keep run as the module :init-fn for startup and also make it the after-load callback (metadata or :devtools config). Re-enter v/mount so Freehand's existing idempotent root/frame reuse publishes the fresh descriptor. Correct the nearby comments and, if useful, pin only this structural hook in the existing scaffold smoke test.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Initial page load still invokes the scaffold's run/mount path.
2. Each Shadow hot reload invokes that same mount path using the native ^:dev/after-load metadata or :devtools :after-load configuration.
3. Reload reuses the existing Freehand root/frame and does not replay :initial-events or reset application state.
4. shadow-cljs.edn, app source, and README comments describe :init-fn as initial-load-only and the after-load hook honestly.
5. The correction uses Shadow's existing lifecycle hook; it adds no generalized reload machinery, framework, or speculative abstraction.
notes:
WORKER (PR #7041, rf2-omygl filed).

PREMISE CORRECTION: two sites, not the two named. The claim lives in examples/ui/minimal-counter/shadow-cljs.edn:33 and in the mount comment in src/my/app.cljs. The README carries NO HMR claim — grep -i "reload|hmr|survive|state|watch|edit" over it returns one line, the `npx shadow-cljs watch app` command. It was never a site.

CONFIRMED FALSE, from the shadow-cljs 3.4.10 jar rather than the docs page: merge-init-fn (shadow/build/targets/browser.clj:203) appends the :init-fn call to the MODULE output, which a reload does not re-evaluate; and the dev client prints "reloading code but no :after-load hooks are configured!" (shadow/cljs/devtools/client/browser.cljs:92) on exactly this configuration.

WHAT LANDED: the comments are narrowed to what the scaffold does. NO hook was wired — the dispatch explicitly fenced implementing HMR behind a docs bead, so the DESIGN section of this bead is NOT executed by PR #7041.

THE DESIGN IS SOUND AND VERIFIED, which is why it is preserved rather than dropped: rf/init! is idempotent (core.cljc guards install with (when-not (adapter/current-adapter) ...)), and re-entering v/mount under an equal frame fingerprint re-renders in place WITHOUT replaying :initial-events (root.cljs preflight!, "an equal fingerprint is the ratified idempotent no-op"). So acceptance criteria 1-4 are one metadata key away. That decision is now rf2-omygl.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS as of PR #7041: criterion 4 (honest comments) MET. Criteria 1-3 unchanged-by-design. Criterion 5 trivially met (nothing added).
VERIFICATION WORKER (no PR — nothing left to do). Dispatched to verify-then-fix this claim; found it ALREADY FIXED on main across two PRs. Verified the end state on origin/main adea123f4b.

THE CLAIM DID REPRODUCE, and it was fixed rather than merely narrowed:
  - PR #7041 (merged cd55060c5b) narrowed the false prose — acceptance criterion 4 only. It explicitly did NOT wire a hook, and split the capability question out as rf2-omygl.
  - Mike ruled on rf2-omygl 2026-07-26 ('the capability is one metadata key away' — WIRE THE HOOK), superseding that narrowing.
  - PR #7076 (merged ef8fb272d3) implemented it. rf2-omygl is CLOSED.

ALL FIVE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA NOW MET, checked against the files on main, not against the PR bodies:
  1. Initial load still invokes run/mount — shadow-cljs.edn still declares :modules {:main {:init-fn my.app/run}}. MET.
  2. Each hot reload invokes the same mount path via the native hook — app.cljs declares (defn ^:export ^:dev/after-load run []). MET, and it is the native Shadow lifecycle, not new machinery.
  3. Reload reuses the existing root/frame and does not replay :initial-events — the mount is re-entered as (v/mount [counter {}] node {:frame {:id :app :initial-events [[:app/init]]}}), which is the equal-fingerprint idempotent no-op in root.cljs preflight!. The PR #7076 worker proved this live under a real 'npx shadow-cljs watch app': without the key 'Count: 3 -> Count: 3' (state kept, VIEW STALE); with it 'Count: 3 -> Tally: 3' (view updated, count survived). MET.
  4. Honest prose in all three places. MET. shadow-cljs.edn now states :init-fn 'runs ONCE, on initial load' and names shadow.build.targets.browser/merge-init-fn; app.cljs says run 'RE-ENTERS it on every hot reload, and ^:dev/after-load is the whole of how'; README:69-72 says 'my.app/run carries ^:dev/after-load, so every reload re-enters the mount ... One metadata key, no reload framework.' Note the README acquired an HMR claim in #7076 and it is a TRUE one — this bead's own premise correction (that the README was never a site) was accurate at filing time and is now superseded.
  5. No generalized reload machinery. MET — one metadata key on one defn, no new file, five-file scaffold manifest unchanged.

ONE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD IS RETIRED AS FALSE, and the shadow-cljs.edn comment now records why so nobody re-derives it: the bead's NOTES say shadow 'literally prints' 'reloading code but no :after-load hooks are configured!' on this config. It never did — re-frame.freehand.rules already declares ^:dev/before-load notify-reload! and ^:dev/after-load commit-reload!, so a bare Freehand app is never hook-less. The metadata key does not add a hook where there were none; it adds the one hook that RE-RENDERS.

GATES on current main (shared with rf2-nutll's verification): donor ledger --ci rc=0; scaffold-smoke JVM rc=0 (7 tests / 17 assertions); ui shadow-config contract JVM rc=0 (4 tests / 9 assertions); changed-surfaces classifier rc=0 (270 passed). No file under examples/ui/minimal-counter/ was changed by me — the tree is byte-identical to origin/main.
close_reason: Already delivered on main across two PRs: #7041 (merge cd55060c5b) made the prose honest (criterion 4), and #7076 (merge ef8fb272d3) wired the hook under Mike's rf2-omygl ruling, which superseded that narrowing. The claim DID reproduce and is now fixed. All five acceptance criteria verified against the files on origin/main adea123f4b: :init-fn my.app/run still present (1); ^:dev/after-load on run (2); equal-fingerprint re-mount with no :initial-events replay, proved live in #7076 — without the key 'Count: 3 -> Count: 3' view stale, with it 'Count: 3 -> Tally: 3' view updated and count survived (3); honest prose in shadow-cljs.edn, app.cljs and README (4); one metadata key, no reload framework, five-file manifest unchanged (5). One bead premise retired as false: shadow never printed the 'no :after-load hooks are configured!' notice here, because re-frame.freehand.rules already declares before/after-load hooks. See the full note on this bead.

title: Control witness: fixed-size virtual collection/table
description:
OUTCOME
Deliver a fixed-size virtual collection/table as the fourth accepted control witness, demonstrating large-list ergonomics, caller rendering, narrow reactivity, keyboard/focus continuity, and measurable work.

USER SURFACE
A concise descriptor over item count, fixed extent, viewport/scroll state, stable item identity, caller-supplied row content, semantic parts, and explicit selection/focus intents. It is sufficient for ordinary large lists/tables, not a data-grid product.

LAWS
Visible-window calculation is pure; keyed row identity survives window movement; one row update does not subscribe/render every row; focus and keyboard navigation remain coherent; scroll host facts do not become a second state system; SSR/structure state the finite rendered window honestly.

HOST/MODE
JVM structural calculations, interpreted and compiled browser paths, large-list performance evidence under D021, and exact scroll/listener cleanup.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-04 and ER-05; D002/D003/D004/D010/D017/D018/D021; spec/004/004D/008/009 plus applicable FH-STRUCT/FH-CTRL/FH-DIAG rows.

NON-GOALS
No variable-height engine, spreadsheet/data-grid, sorting/filtering/query engine, selection framework, or automatic compile promotion.

ACCEPTANCE
1. 10,000-row and approximately 40-visible-window fixtures prove equal structure/DOM and stable keyed identity across interpreted/compiled modes.
2. Deterministic counters report visible rows, row commits, dependency fan-out, comparator work, allocations and cleanup before timing.
3. Keyboard, focus, selection and scroll behavior pass real-browser tests.
4. The same fixture can be reused by the v/$ comparison without coupling the production control to its experimental implementation.
5. The workshop/guide shows a short re-com-porting-quality call site and states omitted data-grid features plainly.
notes:
PR #7180 open. All local gates green (JVM 1245/8405, node 1330/7351, browser 847/5497 x4 runs, prod-elision 120/526, roster 10/66, conformance index + 3 adjacent python gates).

MAJOR FINDING — rf2-86i64 (P1) FILED: the corpus ALREADY contained re-frame.freehand.pilot-virtual-table (1622 lines under test/, from rf2-eq2vx / rf2-g5xxv / rf2-drpa3.176). I did not find it before building — my test-tree sweep was truncated and my greps looked for control/collection, never table. It proves most of the same windowing laws as CONSUMER code but cites no FH id and is in neither the index nor the roster, so this PR is its promotion into a shipped enrolled control rather than a competing design. Two implementations now exist; rf2-86i64 offers three resolutions, one of which (promote the pilot, discard this implementation) is a REWRITE of #7180 rather than a follow-up. The pilot is STRONGER in one place: restore-scroll, a :layout behavior moving a live viewport back to a persisted offset before paint, which this control has no seam for. Recorded in the control docstring, in a PR comment and in an IMPORTANT banner on the PR body.

CI: the browser-test job failed once on a 120s timeout. Confirmed a load flake and re-run — green on main (last 6 runs), the suite had NOT run when the clock expired (last Testing line was the namespace immediately before it), and an A/B locally measured 68s with the suite vs 71s without. That runner compiled in 77s vs 17s locally with four sibling witness PRs in CI. NOTE: the lane has very little headroom at 120s and four witness PRs each add a mounted suite - a shared-capacity problem that will bite whoever merges last.

ID COLLISION unchanged: #7180/#7181/#7182 all claim FH-CTRL-019; recipe posted on #7180.

ALSO FILED: rf2-cfhuv - the namespace is absent from the API-manifest allow-list.
close_reason:
PR #7180 merged as FH-CTRL-021 (Package A of the rf2-86i64 ruling). The fixed-size virtual collection witness is on main.

WHY IT TOOK A REBASE AND A RENUMBER: it was one of five witnesses built in parallel, three of which claimed FH-CTRL-019 because the conformance index allocates ordinals dense-and-ascending. The splitter merged first and took 019, the typeahead renumbered to 020, this took 021. It also went DIRTY against main by creating a fixture at the path the splitter's now occupies. The branch was REBUILT on current main rather than replayed — a faithful commit-by-commit rebase would have clobbered main's file — with all five namespaces restored byte-identically by blob SHA, and 202 changed lines vs the pre-rebase tip of which ZERO lacked the ordinal.

WHAT THE RULING ADDED BEYOND THE ORIGINAL WITNESS: the semantic-neutral engine (virtual-collection owns viewport, canvas, keyed positioned shells and the window arithmetic, names no role, hands its row slot key/absolute-index/total; virtual-list is a listbox wrapper with no second arithmetic and no second scroll host — machine-checked by the manifest, engine [:on-scroll :spread-safe], listbox []), and the controlled :scroll-offset, which ports the pilot's guarded :layout seam as reconcile-scroll, writing before paint only when the node disagrees. No opt-out; :restore-scroll? not ported. The application's :inbox/scroll-to effect was DELETED, so no host-writing effect remains and every scrollTop the browser suite reads is a fact about the collection.

ONE DESIGN DETAIL FORCED BY THE COMPILER, worth inheriting: the engine takes viewport attributes as an explicit :attrs map, because the compiled grammar refuses a render-slot callback anywhere but a LITERAL call-site prop map — so a wrapper cannot merge its props and also pass :row.

A GAP THE WORKER'S OWN CHANGE OPENED, AND CLOSED: the split renders two nodes per row, and the teardown residue read counted only [data-part='row'], so a leaked shell would have been invisible. It now reads three books. :residue :none still holds across 3 cycles x 8 stops, 318 counted row renders, exact zeroes after teardown.

FOLLOW-ONS: rf2-cfhuv must write its manifest roster against SEVEN public names, not the branch's original five — virtual-collection and reconcile-scroll were added. Package B (rf2-pa57v) can now retire the pilot's component half; still owed there and not claimed here are surviving-row DOM node identity across a real scroll, and reorder carrying the row element.

title: Control witness: first-party splitter with pointer and keyboard laws
description:

title: Ownership routing with Google Maps, Framer Motion, and Radix witnesses
description:
OUTCOME
Publish the ownership-routing guide and prove the two expensive routes: a behavior-owned Google Maps overlay with an explicit nested Freehand root, and a React-primary compound region registered through v/defhost.

ROUTING
Cover pure/headless cores, value/callback React components, hook/context/ref/compound React owners, imperative SDK behaviors, v/->react, host-created panes/nested roots, and explicit islands. State permanent limits and costs beside recoveries.

WITNESSES
1. Google Maps: behavior owns root identity, explicit frame selection, host-removal callback, update, and one idempotent reclamation path shared by host removal and disconnect.
2. Framer Motion: one exit-retention owner per keyed subtree; React-owned animation protocol remains React-primary.
3. Radix UI (or an equivalently popular hook/context/ref/compound library if dependency evidence requires substitution): wrapper uses v/defhost; asChild/ref cloning remains inside React ownership.

EVIDENCE
Each witness publishes top-level exports, boundary crossings, irreducible glue sites, and approximate glue lines as comparative evidence, plus explicit context/evidence/SSR loss. Counts are not a score or threshold.

HOST/MODE
Mounted browser and cleanup first; structural/SSR evidence where the route can honestly provide it; interpreted/compiled claims explicit.

NON-GOALS
No v/->element, behavior outlet, mount-child, portal manager, neutral hooks/refs, or promise that nested roots inherit outer context/Suspense/bubbling.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Maps ends with zero roots/listeners after host removal, disconnect, either order, and repeated reclamation.
2. Framer Motion and Radix witnesses preserve their native React protocols through the one host kind.
3. The routing page lets a programmer select the route from ownership facts, not library branding.
4. Any proposal for a new primitive cites Maps plus a second independent repetition and explicitly amends D013/D015; otherwise no proposal is filed.
notes:
EVIDENCE CLAUSE — DISCHARGED. PR #7251 (worker/evidence-counts-18209), opened green locally. The projection pass's PR #7244 is MERGED (2026-07-28), so acceptance 3's pending-merge hold is also released. All four numbered ACCEPTANCE criteria plus the EVIDENCE clause are now discharged — THIS BEAD CAN CLOSE.

THE FOUR COUNTS, PER WITNESS (exports / crossings / glue sites / glue lines):
  FH-REACT-009    compound React owner (Radix-shaped)         1 / 2 / 0 / 0
  FH-REACT-010    clock owner (Framer-Motion-shaped)          2 / 3 / 1 / 1
  FH-BEHAVIOR-010 imperative SDK + host-created pane (Maps)   1 / 2 / 4 / 27
  pure / headless core — THE CONTROL                          0 / 0 / 0 / 0

HOW THEY WERE OBTAINED: by READING the declarations, not by running anything. These are static properties of a route — they do not vary between node and a browser, so there is no runtime to label and no range across rounds to report. Each fixture carries `:method :read-from-source` in the value itself rather than leaving a reader to assume it was measured. Nothing asserts them and nothing gates on them; per the clause they are not a score or a threshold, and the largest route is largest because the library owns the most.

ONE DEFINITION, IN ONE PLACE. `docs/core/freehand/host/ownership-routing.md` §"What the counts count" defines export / crossing / glue site / glue line ONCE for all three witnesses — three definitions in three files would have been three incomparable numbers. Each fixture then writes out its own arithmetic name by name INCLUDING THE EXCLUSIONS: the library's own side (a wrapper composing a compound library's parts is React code an author writes in a pure-React app too, which is why Radix's glue is honestly 0 and not a sleight of hand), the application, and the fixture's measurement apparatus (Maps' two `:commands`, Radix's `as-child-probe`).

THE CONTROL is the check on the definition: a library that owns nothing routes to nothing, so the pure/headless core must be four zeros, and a definition producing anything else there would be the thing that was wrong. Maps' 27 glue lines were also reproduced mechanically — 1 + 8 + 14 + 3 + 1 over `reclaim!`, `:connect`, `:update`, `:disconnect`, with the suite's own `entries`/`worked` bookkeeping excluded.

NOTHING WAS LEFT OUT. All four quantities are well defined for all three hosts, so there is no honest-gap entry to report.

`:evidence :limits` GAINS ITS OTHER HALF. It carried what the PROOF cannot reach (no `google.maps`, no Radix packages, no `framer-motion`); each fixture now also carries a third entry stating what the ROUTE permanently loses. FH-BEHAVIOR-010: the island inherits no outer React context, Suspense or bubbling; the SDK's subtree is a leaf with no structural render and nothing in any manifest; no SSR for either tree since a behavior connects only on commit. FH-REACT-009: React context does not survive a Freehand boundary (which is WHY the wrapper is registered and not the parts), the withheld asChild/ref promise in the other direction, one manifest crossing with nothing under it, portalled content outside the container, `:ssr :client-only`. FH-REACT-010: retention lives in a ref no substrate vocabulary reaches, the retained child is on the page and in none of Freehand's books, `:ssr :client-only`.

NOTHING QUALITATIVE WAS REVISED. The routing page's verified claims are untouched; this pass only ADDS one section, one paragraph and a `:comparative` key plus a third `:limits` entry per fixture. `:evidence` sub-keys are free-form to the roster spine (only `:residue` is validated), so no roster.cljc change was needed and none was made — no overlap with the sibling worker on deps.edn / core.

GATES (foreground, worktree-local, exit echoed, never piped): check_freehand_conformance_index.py exit 0; freehand JVM clojure -M:test exit 0 (1288/8856, 0 failures, guide digest roster 114 of 138 unchanged); python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0 (no new warning); npm run test:browser exit 0 (842/5469); scripts/test-freehand-prod-gate.sh exit 0 (137 of 137, 0 excluded as known-red — roster empty, not regressed).

title: check_thrown_error_messages.py has the same invocation-scope gap rf2-kqxe6.25 just closed — tools/ carries 38 bare-keyword throw sites
description:
Found while widening the EP-0007 retired-spelling ratchet (rf2-kqxe6.25, PR #7005).

That gate and `scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py` (rf2-vvixub / Spec 009 $The thrown-error shape) are built to the same template: a fixture self-test gated ahead of a live scan, both invoked bare from `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and the always-on python job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, both defaulting to `DEFAULT_SCAN_DIR = 'implementation'`. rf2-kqxe6.25 widened the retired-spelling one to every Clojure source tree. The thrown-error one is still implementation-only.

MEASURED, from a clean checkout of the PR branch:

    python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py                     -> rc=0, 408 files under implementation/
    python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py --scan-dir tools    -> rc=1, 38 findings
    python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py --scan-dir examples -> rc=0
    python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py --scan-dir skills   -> rc=0
    python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py --scan-dir testbeds -> rc=0

So this is NOT the same shape of bounded repair. The retired-spelling widening was free — the corpus was already clean, so it cost one roster edit. Widening this one means either converting 38 throw sites in tools/ or ruling that tools/ is out of scope for the Spec 009 thrown-error shape.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING FIRST (do not dispatch as a mechanical fix): is the Spec 009 thrown-error shape a FRAMEWORK contract or a REPO contract? tools/ is bundle-isolated dev tooling, and a tool's ex-info is never on a consumer's error path, so 'implementation/ only' may be the correct scope — in which case the fix is to SAY so at the declaration (the way rf2-kqxe6.25 documented why scripts/ and docs/ are off its roster) rather than to leave the surface looking accidental. The current `DEFAULT_SCAN_DIR = 'implementation'` carries no such note; it reads as an unexamined default, which is exactly what row 9's did.

Either outcome is a small PR. Both touch `scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py`; only the widening touches the two invocation comments. Not a hot-zone conflict with anything in flight once #7005 merges.
notes:
MAYOR RULING: tools/ is OUT OF SCOPE for the Spec 009 thrown-error shape. Do NOT do the 38 conversions (2026-07-26).

THE QUESTION, as the filer correctly framed it: check_thrown_error_messages.py is built to the same template as the :query-retain ratchet and has the identical scope gap — it defaults to implementation/ and reports rc=0, while --scan-dir tools yields rc=1 with 38 findings (examples, skills and testbeds are clean). The filer explicitly declined to widen it, because unlike the ratchet this is NOT a free widening: it needs either 38 conversions or a ruling. That restraint was right.

THE RULING AND ITS REASON: the Spec 009 thrown-error shape governs the FRAMEWORK PUBLIC ERROR SURFACE — the errors a consumer application catches, whose shape is a contract because consumer code and consumer AI read it. tools/ is dev tooling: it is not among the thirteen coordinates a v* tag publishes, its errors are seen by a developer running an inspection tool, and no consumer ever catches them. Converting 38 sites to satisfy a contract that does not govern them is ceremony, and the pre-alpha posture rules it out — not over-engineering, trust the programmer, low friction.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and this is the actionable half: make the SCOPE EXPLICIT rather than accidental. Right now the gate covers implementation/ because that is its default, not because anyone decided so — which is exactly the shape that let 38 findings sit unseen and would let the next reader "helpfully" widen it. Declare the scan roster at the declaration site with a stated reason for each exclusion, the way rf2-kqxe6.25 did for scripts/ (own positive fixtures) and docs/ (mkdocs staging). One comment, one roster, no conversions.

CONSISTENT WITH: rf2-odlm3, where I ruled against sweeping 52 tools/** test suites for the same reason — unpublished surface, and a rushed fix there is riskier than the gap. And note the pattern this bead itself belongs to: a comment or a default that justifies an absence, unverified. The fix is to make the decision visible, not to erase the difference.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS RULING: if any of those 38 sites throws an error that reaches a CONSUMER — via the MCP tool surface, a published skill, or an error a consumer app can catch — then the shape governs it and that subset is real work. Worth one check before closing.
WORKER (PR #7033, worker/gate-scope). Roster declared; NO conversions.

FALSIFIER CHECK RESULT: FIRED. tools/story-mcp/tools/write.cljc:261-274 catches Throwable and relays (ex-message e) into result/error-result, wrapping story/reg-variant* -> registrar.cljc:302/:365 (ex-info (str error-kw) ...). An MCP client receives literally 'Registration failed: :rf.error/variant-id-shape'. Traced end to end. Mayor amended the ruling 2026-07-26 in response; the amendment is reproduced verbatim in the PR body alongside the original. Relayed sites are owned by rf2-jquiy and were NOT fixed here.

NOT reachable (checked): pair-mcp server.cljs:321/:331 (handle-call*'s .catch builds from ex-DATA, never the message) and mcp-base cursor.cljc:123/188/218 (swallowed to ::malformed at cursor.cljc:334). Two of the 38 -- story.cljc:877/:914 -- are gate FALSE POSITIVES: already conformant, but the message is let-bound so the first-arg text carries no token.

DELIVERED: DEFAULT_SCAN_DIR -> DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS roster whose comment states the scope as a reachability rule ('framework source, plus any tools/ path whose throw is relayed off-box') with a ground per excluded tree; --scan-dir repeatable; a vanished rostered tree now fails closed at rc=2. Both invocation sites verified already correct and left unchanged.

MUTATION PROOF (in PR body): M1 planted bare-keyword throw -> rc=1/1 finding, restored rc=0. M2 roster mutated to ('tools',) with a BARE invocation -> rc=1/38 findings, proving the constant drives the scan. M3 rostered tree renamed away -> rc=2 fail-closed, restored rc=0.

PREMISE CORRECTION for the mayor: both rulings say tools/ is not published. It is -- release-story.yml, release-xray.yml, release-machines-viz.yml and template-release.yml ship day8/re-frame2-{story,xray,machines-viz,template}, and mcp-base + story-mcp declare :clein/build Clojars deploys. Literally true that none rides the framework's v* tag; 'not published' is the stronger claim the text leans on.
close_reason:
PR #7033 MERGED. Scope declared as a rule rather than a directory default. But TWO of my premises were wrong and are corrected here.

CORRECTION 1 — "tools/ IS NOT PUBLISHED" IS FALSE, and both my rulings leaned on it. I verified the workers claim myself: FOUR release workflows exist (release-story.yml, release-xray.yml, release-machines-viz.yml, template-release.yml) and FIVE tools/ artefacts declare :clein/build (machines-viz, mcp-base, story-mcp, story, xray). What is literally true is that NONE RIDES THE v* TAG. "Not among the thirteen coordinates the alpha tag publishes" and "not published" are DIFFERENT CLAIMS, and I wrote the stronger one. A consumer can depend on day8/story and catch its errors.

DOES THE RULING SURVIVE? Partly, and only because the AMENDMENT replaced the reasoning. The original ground — dev tooling, errors seen only by a developer running an inspection tool — is undermined. The operative test is now the amended one: the Spec 009 thrown-error shape governs any path whose throw is RELAYED TO A CONSUMER, and tools/ is out of scope BY DEFAULT rather than by nature. That test does not depend on the false premise. The 38-site sweep stays refused.

CORRECTION 2 — TWO OF THE 38 ARE GATE FALSE POSITIVES, and the defect is not confined to tools/. story.cljc:877 and :914 are ALREADY CONFORMANT — human sentence plus an [:rf.error/...] token, under a comment citing Spec 009 — but the message is LET-BOUND, so the gate sees only `msg`. In the workers words: a conformant let-bound message under implementation/ would false-red identically. So the primary scope carries the same blind spot.

MY FALSIFIER FIRED AND THE WORKER FILED IT RATHER THAN ACTING: tools/story-mcp/.../write.cljc:261-274 catches Throwable and relays (ex-message e) into result/error-result, wrapping story/reg-variant* -> registrar.cljc:302/:365, both (ex-info (str error-kw) ...). An MCP client receives literally "Registration failed: :rf.error/variant-id-shape". Traced end to end. rf2-jquiy owns it. It also checked what is NOT reachable so the subset stays honest: pair-mcp/server.cljs:321/:331 build from ex-DATA and never relay the message, and mcp-base/cursor.cljc three throws are swallowed to ::malformed.

THE RULE IS STATED, NOT MECHANISED, and that was the right call: whether a message is relayed off-box is interprocedural across artefacts and a text scan cannot follow the chain. The roster carries the decidable part; the comment carries the rest with story-mcp named.

MUTATION PROOF: M1 planted bare-keyword throw -> rc=1, 1 finding, restored rc=0. M2 roster mutated to ("tools",) with a bare invocation -> rc=1, 38 findings, proving the CONSTANT drives the scan rather than a hardcoded path. M3 rostered tree renamed away -> rc=2, fail-closed.

title: A compiled declaration's structural manifest — and absolute developer file paths — ship into an :advanced production bundle
description:
Measured under rf2-etqma (2026-07-26) while proving the Freehand tool tier elides.

THE OBSERVATION. Bundle `out/freehand-release/main.js` — `:advanced`, `goog.DEBUG false`, entry `re-frame.freehand.release-app/-main`, i.e. exactly what a consumer ships — contains:

  - the compiled declaration's STRUCTURAL MANIFEST payload: `view-cell` (x2), `crossings` (x2), `html-sites` (x2), `source-coord` (x4), `re-frame.freehand/v1` (x1);
  - EIGHT occurrences of the string `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/fh-tool-class/implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/release_app.cljs` — absolute paths from the BUILD MACHINE, inside `{:file … :line …}` maps.

View docstrings do NOT ship (`The interpreted paved path` is ABSENT), so this is source-coord and manifest data rather than prose. shadow-cljs.edn's matched-pair comment already noted in passing that ':advanced does not strip [a docstring] and the view manifest ships it once per declared view'; this is the measured general case.

WHY IT IS NOT A TOOL-TIER ISSUE. The payload is the DECLARATION's, carried so the door's `v/manifest` can answer, and it is present in a bundle that requires no tool namespace at all. rf2-etqma's ruling (no bundle isolation for re-frame.freehand.tool) is unaffected and in fact strengthened: isolating the tool tier would remove none of this while creating the impression that it had.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING. Two questions, and they are separable.

  1. SIZE/PAYLOAD: should a production build carry the static-analysis manifest at all? `v/manifest` is a published door read, so removing it in production is a contract change, not a build tweak. The alternative is that the manifest stays and this is simply the door's stated cost — in which case say so in spec/API.md where `v/manifest` is rowed, because nothing currently states it.
  2. BUILD-MACHINE PATH LEAK: absolute paths are the sharper half and may be separable from (1). A shipped bundle disclosing a developer's home directory is an information leak independent of whether the manifest ships. Closure/shadow-cljs source-path relativisation may already be configurable; check before designing anything.

MEASUREMENT METHOD (reusable). String-literal sentinels over the bundle bytes, with a negative control: Closure renames symbols and inlines small functions but never rewrites string literals, and CLJS constructs a keyword with its name as a string literal. Do NOT count `goog.DEBUG` occurrences and do NOT grep function names — both oracles are measured wrong in this repo (see the header comment of implementation/scripts/check-freehand-reachability.cjs).

Owner is likely spec/004-Views.md (the door's `v/manifest` contract) plus spec/Privacy.md for the path half. NOT scoped by rf2-etqma or rf2-j3evb.
notes:
VERIFIED ALREADY CORRECT ON main — NOTHING CHANGED. Covered by PR #7056 (worker/reopens) as a verification lane only; that PR's diff does not touch spec/Privacy.md.

REOPEN CLASS: fresh work, and specifically a defect the CLOSE introduced. The #7028 audit reopened against #7028's OWN new text, not against the original bundle-disclosure finding, which it accepts as correctly measured. So neither "residual the close missed" nor "original defect re-asserted".

ALREADY DISCHARGED. The reopen's bounded completion — qualify the sentence claiming "every production error record shipped off-box carries one too" — landed on main as ac1441ba997795743d2b2a908ec47b90f2ce231d ("spec(privacy): qualify which production error records carry an absolute source path (rf2-12g5z)", 2026-07-26 10:19:07 +1000), confirmed an ancestor of origin/main.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE IMPLEMENTATION AND THE TESTS, not the prose:
  - error_emit.cljc:216 error-source-coord returns nil for an id with no captured coords and nil EXPLICITLY for frame-destroyed with :op :capture (`:capture nil` in the case). dispatch-on-error! at error_emit.cljc:427 cond->s the slot in, so nil means the key is ABSENT, not present-and-nil. Both match the landed paragraph exactly.

No speculative edit was made to give an open bead the appearance of being handled.

title: R6's rf/route-link intent-handler arm false-greens a doubled and reordered dispatch
description:
EP-0037 review gate 1 (rf2-kqxe6.14) finding, proven by mutation.

R6's `the-real-anchor-intent-handler-composes-and-dispatches` (the CLJS-only arm in `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc`) is the ONLY coverage anywhere for `rf/route-link`'s composed `:prefetch :intent` handler — row 7's "both link surfaces" clause. It is a FALSE GREEN on both laws it names.

THE MUTATION (the evidence). In `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc`, `compose-intent-handler` was changed to dispatch the prefetch payload TWICE and to dispatch BEFORE the caller's handler instead of after:

    (fn [e]
      (router/dispatch! payload {:source :router :frame render-frame})
      (router/dispatch! payload {:source :router :frame render-frame})
      (when caller-handler (caller-handler e)))

Both mutations violate the documented law (`link.cljc`: "runs a caller-supplied handler of the same name FIRST (compose, not replace) and then dispatches `payload`") and both violate what the arm's own `testing` string claims to prove ("must run the caller's `:on-mouse-enter` FIRST and then enqueue exactly the prefetch payload").

WITH THE MUTATION IN PLACE THE WHOLE CLJS LANE IS GREEN: `npm run test:cljs` → 11439 tests / 57281 assertions, 0 failures / 0 errors, rc=0 — byte-identical to the unmutated baseline (11439 / 57281, rc=0, same run on the same worktree). Not one assertion in the repository reds. Reverted; `git status` clean.

WHY IT FALSE-GREENS. Two assertions do no work:

  row (first (filter #(= :rf.event/dispatched (:operation %)) traces))
  (is (some? row) "the handler enqueued exactly one dispatch")

`(some? (first (filter …)))` is true for one match and for N matches alike, so cardinality is unasserted. And `caller-ran` is only read AFTER the composed handler has returned, so a dispatch that precedes the caller is indistinguishable from one that follows it. Ordering is unasserted.

This is a PROOF gap, not a production defect — the shipped `compose-intent-handler` does call the caller first and dispatches once. But the arm exists precisely so that cannot silently regress, and it cannot detect either regression.

PROVENANCE. This is exactly the residual merged-PR audit #6941 recorded on rf2-kqxe6.10 ("CORRECTNESS: lines 576-581 take `(first (filter ... traces))` and assert only `(some? row)`, so duplicate matching dispatch rows still pass; `caller-ran` is inspected only after the composed handler returns, so dispatch-before-caller also passes"), with the instruction "keep this exact owner open after rf2-kqxe6.20 is repaired". rf2-kqxe6.10 was subsequently CLOSED on its dependencies going green; the close reason does not mention the residual and the residual was not fixed. So this obligation currently has no open owner — hence this bead.

BOUNDED REPAIR (the audit's own prescription, unchanged). Keep the one focused arm. Capture an ORDERED milestone sequence — push `:caller` from the caller's handler and `:dispatch` from a trace listener into one atom — then assert (a) exactly ONE `:rf.event/dispatched` row matching the prefetch payload, and (b) `:caller` precedes `:dispatch`. No new harness, no broader refactor, no new production code.

VACUITY DISCIPLINE. The repaired arm must be shown non-vacuous by re-applying BOTH mutations above (each separately) and confirming each reds.
notes:
HOLD REASON CORRECTED (mayor, 2026-07-26) — the cluster reviewer caught that I held this for the right outcome on the wrong reason.

I said it was held because routing is a coupled artefact. It changes NO implementation/routing/src file at all — its entire repair is one deftest arm in implementation/resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc. The real collision is that PR #7000 (rf2-kqxe6.23, the :query-defaults door parity P1) rewrites +174/-17 in EXACTLY that file, because its regression coverage extends the door-parity arm in the same test.

So the hold STANDS and the trigger is unchanged — dispatch the instant #7000 merges — but anyone reading my earlier reason could correctly argue "this is not routing/src" and release it early, and get the conflict anyway. Recording the true reason so that cannot happen.
close_reason:
PR #7004 MERGED (e6e9f5cf207007b0379bd13adb4f62e3fd01e4f8). The residual I orphaned by closing rf2-kqxe6.10 without discharging its audit note is now repaired.

WHAT WAS BLIND, precisely: two assertions did no work. (some? (first (filter #(= :rf.event/dispatched (:operation %)) traces))) is as true for ONE matching row as for FIVE, so cardinality went unasserted; and caller-ran was read only AFTER the composed handler returned, so a dispatch PRECEDING the caller was indistinguishable from one following it. Both named laws, neither detected.

THE REPAIR IS ONE SHAPE, not two assertions: an ordered milestone sequence. The caller pushes :caller; a trace listener pushes :dispatch as the matching :rf.event/dispatched arrives (trace delivery is synchronous per trace/emit!). Then (= [:caller :dispatch] @milestones) says composed-not-replaced, once-not-twice AND after-not-before in a single read, with a sibling (= 1 (count rows)) pinning that nothing else enqueued.

IT DEFEATED THE TRAP I WARNED ABOUT, in two independent ways. The caller intent travels the REAL seam — route-link-render own composed handler taken off the rendered attrs, never a hand-written dispatch. And the expected payload is written as a LITERAL rather than read back through link/prefetch-payload, so the expectation CANNOT agree with the seam under test by construction. That is the stronger half: yesterday the rf2-kqxe6.23 worker first draft passed against unfixed code precisely because both sides of its comparison went through one seam.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, full CLJS lane each time with link.cljc mutated in place then restored: baseline 11453/57342 rc=0; M1 doubled dispatch -> 2 failures, (not (= [:caller :dispatch] [:caller :dispatch :dispatch])) and (not (= 1 2)), rc=1; M2 reordered dispatch -> 1 failure, (not (= [:caller :dispatch] [:dispatch :caller])), rc=1. Under BOTH mutations the ONLY failing deftest in the entire 11453-test lane was this arm — it is the sole detector, which is exactly what the bead existed to establish.

compose-intent-handler is byte-identical to HEAD and appears in no commit: the IMPLEMENTATION was always correct and only the proof was blind. Verified by content — the file blob on origin/main and on the tip are the same object d8ffa092c5d81571760dbedda5f9193305c00a6f — not by ancestry, which lies after a rebase-merge.

Gates: resources 722/6729 rc=0; test:cljs 11453/57342 rc=0; test-fast-pr.sh PASS with captured rc=0 cross-checked against the log own PASS marker after the harness backgrounded it at the 600s ceiling.

title: coming-from-tanstack-query still advertises route-plan prefetch as deferred to post-v1 -- R3 shipped it
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness).

docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md:192 -- the "Prefetch / route-plan preload" row of the capability-parity table -- reads:

  | **Prefetch / route-plan preload** | `queryClient.prefetchQuery` / `<Link prefetch>` (Router) | `prefetch` endpoint action | `preload` | per-resource warm `ensure` works today (ownerless, cause-only); a **route-plan-level** prefetch verb (`[:rf.route/prefetch target]` in WARM mode) is deferred to post-v1 -- the resources side is already warm-capable | **Deferred (later slice)** |

EP-0037 R3 SHIPPED exactly that verb. `[:rf.route/prefetch {address}]` is public, spec'd at 012 §Route-plan prefetch, spec'd at 016:1817 ("Shipped in EP-0037 R3"), catalogued in 009 (:rf.error/prefetch-bad-address), carries five conformance fixtures (spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r3-prefetch-*.edn), and has a runnable demo at examples/capabilities/resources/infinite_feed.

The page compounds the error twice over:
  - Its closing prose says "**The honest gaps -- out of scope on purpose.** The bottom two rows are the deliberate non-goals of this HTTP-only phase" -- which accounts for *Normalized / GraphQL cache* and *Offline persistence*, NOT this third stale `Deferred (later slice)` row. So the page's own honesty paragraph now under-counts its gaps.
  - "Every 'Landed' claim is pinned by tests in the reference implementation" invites the reader to trust the status column, which makes the one wrong cell worse than an unmarked omission.

WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT. rf2-kqxe6.11 (docs wave) scoped itself to docs/routing/** + docs/api/re-frame.routing.md; rf2-kqxe6.12 owned examples/; rf2-kqxe6.13 owned skills/. rf2-dx52g found "four guide pages the waves did not reach" -- this was a fifth, in a sibling capability tree. A corpus sweep for "deferred|post-v1|not built|later slice|unshipped" across docs/ and skills/ confirms this is the ONLY remaining stale claim about any EP-0037 capability, so the repair is one row, not a sweep.

EP-0037 §Guide impact names this class explicitly: "'Coming from' guides explain the adopted capabilities without importing outlet, hook, cache, action, or middleware ownership." A reader migrating from TanStack Query is currently told a shipped capability does not exist and that they should reach for per-resource warm ensures at every call site instead -- which is precisely the duplication the EP §Rationale says intent prefetch exists to remove ("Per-resource hover handlers make every call site reimplement target params, scope resolution, conditions, branch inheritance, and dedupe").

BOUNDED REPAIR -- one table row plus one sentence:
1. Rewrite the row's re-frame2 cell to describe the shipped verb: `[:rf.route/prefetch {:to ... :params ...}]` runs the destination's EFFECTIVE parent-to-leaf plan in warm mode -- every ensure ownerless under cause `[:route-prefetch <route-id>]`, `:blocking?` inert, no route state / guards / `:on-match`, frame-scoped, ordinary freshness+dedupe+GC, and a later activation joins the warmed work and attaches its real owner. The paired link opt is `:prefetch :intent` on route-link (the ONLY accepted value; absent is the only way to be passive). Set the status cell to **Landed**.
2. Name the divergence honestly, in this page's register, rather than claiming parity: there is deliberately NO global default, render mode, viewport mode, hover-delay knob, separate preload cache, or prefetch-stale clock -- resource freshness and dedupe already answer whether work is useful. That is the interesting contrast with `<Link prefetch>`'s mode matrix and is worth a sentence.
3. Fix the closing prose so the "honest gaps" paragraph counts correctly (the two genuine non-goals remain normalized/GraphQL caches and offline persistence).

Keep it to that. Do not restructure the table, do not add a prefetch tutorial here (docs/routing/concepts.md §"Warming a destination before the click" already owns the teaching), and do not touch other rows.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict; check_doc_slugs; check_readme_links. Parallel-safe (docs/resources tree only).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7012. Row rewritten to the shipped verb, status Landed, plus a divergence paragraph (no global default / render / viewport mode / hover delay / separate preload cache / prefetch-stale clock). Bead item 3 needed no edit: the honest-gaps paragraph points at 'the bottom two rows', which ARE the two genuine non-goals — it under-counted only because the prefetch row was a stale third gap mid-table, so flipping that row restores the count.

title: spec/009 never received the EP-0037 planner rows: prefetched trace missing, resource-route-plan row not widened
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness). spec/009-Instrumentation.md is the EP's NAMED contract home for "plan, prefetch, denial, planning-failure, and stale-suppression traces/errors" (EP-0037 Scope-and-authority table). Each slice added the NEW rows it introduced; nobody owned WIDENING the existing ones. Three sub-defects, one home, one root cause.

(a) `:rf.route/prefetched` IS ABSENT FROM 009 ENTIRELY. The EP's Spec 009 graduation roster names it: "new or renamed: event :rf.route/prefetch, event/trace :rf.route/entry-denied, trace :rf.route/prefetched, and error :rf.error/prefetch-bad-address" (EP:1011-1013). Mechanically, `git grep -i prefetch -- spec/009-Instrumentation.md` returns EXACTLY TWO lines, 2219 and 2220 -- the two ERROR rows. The trace appears in no op table (contrast 009:193-194, where its siblings :rf.route/planned / :rf.route/entry-denied / :rf.route/fragment-changed all do), in no narrative (contrast 009:235-236), and in no per-file emit-site list (009:1055 enumerates routing.cljc's ops and there is no routing/prefetch.cljc entry at all). It IS emitted (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/prefetch.cljc:176), IS schema'd (spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1718 RoutePrefetchedTags), and IS documented in 012:102 + 012:965 + 016:1817 + docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:508. 009 is the one home that missed it.

(b) THE `:rf.error/resource-route-plan` ROW WAS NOT WIDENED AND NOW CONTRADICTS THREE OTHER SPECS. EP Tooling-and-observability, ratified by name in Resolved Decisions ("the shared planner's :plan-cause diagnostic vocabulary and the widened :rf.error/resource-route-plan tags"): "Its tags require :route-id and :plan-cause ...; :nav-token is present only for an activation attempt, and :resource-id is present only when one declaration owns the failure."
   009:2034's Tags column reads: :route-id, :resource-id, :nav-token, :cause, :reason. NO :plan-cause. NO :contributor. spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1697-1716 (ResourceRoutePlanTags) carries BOTH -- :contributor was added by rf2-kqxe6.6, :plan-cause by R3.
   Worse, the row's NARRATIVE still teaches the pre-EP partial-plan model:
     - "A route :resources entry could not be PLANNED ... its :scope / :params did not resolve" -- narrower than the ratified failure set (:after missing/cyclic, :parent unresolved/cyclic, identity-collapse cycle), all enumerated at 016:1278 + 016:1281.
     - "FIRST-error-wins when several route resources fail to plan."
     - "The route still commits ...; the unplannable resource is simply not ensured."
   That last clause DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the ratified atomicity rule (EP:419-423 "Plan execution is atomic at this boundary ... no partial ensure is dispatched") and its two normative restatements at spec/012-Routing.md:851 and spec/016-Resources.md:1308. A reader of 009 today learns the opposite of the shipped contract.

(c) `:rf.resource/route-plan`'s R2 TAG ROSTER HAS NO SPEC HOME. The trace grew :branch / :ensured / :kept / :removed / :blocking / :identities / :redundant-children / :plan-error / (:plan-cause on warm) at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1084-1094. `git grep "rf.resource/route-plan" -- spec/` finds only a bare name-drop at 009:1057, the redundant-child advisory sentence at 016:1292, and the R2/R3 fixtures. No spec enumerates the tags, though 009 enumerates comparable rosters for every sibling op.

ROOT CAUSE (why no gate caught it, and why this is NOT a false green). implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj is the 009 ratchet. Its own docstring scopes it: it parses the catalogue table and pins the CHANNEL column, category uniqueness, the always-on set, and a co-edit ratchet against emit sites FOR :rf.error/* / :rf.warning/* / advisory CATEGORIES. It does not cover :rf.event-op-type TRACE ops (so (a) slipped) and it does not validate the TAGS column against Spec-Schemas (so (b) and (c) drifted). The gate never claimed this ground.

BOUNDED REPAIR -- documentation, no runtime change:
1. Add the `:rf.route/prefetched` row to 009: the op table near 193-194, the narrative near 235-236, and the per-file emit-site list at 1055 (a routing/prefetch.cljc entry). Tags per Spec-Schemas RoutePrefetchedTags: :route-id, :warmed, optional :plan-error, :frame. State that it is NOT an activation trace (no :rf.route/activated / nav-token-allocated pair).
2. Widen 009:2034's :rf.error/resource-route-plan row: add :plan-cause and :contributor to the Tags column so it matches ResourceRoutePlanTags; broaden the failure set to the ratified one; and REPLACE the partial-plan narrative -- delete "the unplannable resource is simply not ensured" and reconcile "FIRST-error-wins" with the whole-plan atomicity rule (the plan fails wholly; first-error-wins describes WHICH failure is reported, not that siblings still ensure). Cite 012:851 / 016:1308.
3. Give the :rf.resource/route-plan tag roster one home. 009 is the natural one given its sibling rosters; a cross-reference from 016 is enough if the roster lands in 009.
4. Consider extending the catalogue ratchet to trace ops and/or the Tags column ONLY if it is cheap -- if it needs a new parser or harness, file it separately rather than growing this bead.

DO NOT change any emitted tag, add a tag, or make :plan-cause required -- the :plan-cause narrowing is a separate finding (see the errata bead filed by the same gate). This bead makes 009 describe what ships.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict; check_doc_slugs; the error-catalogue conformance test; check_keyword_catalogue_drift. HOT-ZONE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md -- sequence, do not parallel with another 009 bead.
close_reason: PR #7011, sequenced AFTER rf2-8yx7g's :plan-cause erratum (its prerequisite). All three sub-defects fixed, documentation only, no emitted tag changed. (a) :rf.route/prefetched added to all three places it was absent from: the op quick-reference table (near 194), a full detailed-contract bullet (after the :rf.route/planned bullet) with the roster verified at routing/prefetch.cljc:192-196, and a routing/prefetch.cljc clause in the per-file emit-site list naming both it and :rf.error/prefetch-bad-address. Bullet states the two facts a consumer otherwise gets wrong: :warmed 0 is not an error, and a REJECTED prefetch emits no summary trace at all. (b) :rf.error/resource-route-plan's row: Tags column now carries :plan-cause and :contributor (matching ResourceRoutePlanTags); failure set widened to the ratified four; the partial-plan clause 'the unplannable resource is simply not ensured' DELETED and replaced with the atomicity rule cited to 012 §Failed activation + 016:1308; FIRST-error-wins kept but reconciled (it names WHICH failure is reported, explicitly not that siblings ensure). ALSO widened the Default :recovery column, which said only :fix-params while the emit sites produce five (:fix-params/:fix-when/:fix-scope/:fix-after/:fix-parent) - not asked for, same cell-group, verified at route.cljc:465,484,523,535,589,608,620,830,852,900; :fix-route-integration deliberately excluded because route.cljc:965,973 throw above the try and never reach the trace. (c) the :rf.resource/route-plan tag roster landed at 009:1057, the entry already serving as 009's home for per-op resources tag detail - BOTH shapes, with :plan-cause named as the discriminator and the mutual exclusions (:plan-cause XOR :nav-token, :plan-cause XOR :blocking/:identities) stated as combinations, plus the failed-plan row signature (:ensured 0 :kept 0 :blocking [] :identities [] and the whole prior set under :removed) which makes the atomicity rule legible on the trace itself. One-clause cross-reference added at 016:1681, whose summary phrase had gone stale. Item 4 (extend the ratchet): NOT done, per brief - noted in the PR body that the Tags-column arm is worth filing (Spec-Schemas already defines one *Tags schema per row, so a keys-set diff is a parser away and would have caught (b)) while the trace-op arm is the expensive half; left as a mayor design decision. FOUND-NOT-FIXED: :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch is also absent from the emit-site list but is THROWN (routing/link.cljc:58) not emitted, and its catalogue row already names its file - flagged, not changed. FILED rf2-wd9im: while verifying the roster, :rf.resource/route-plan's :blocking / :identities scoped-key vectors were found to escape the resources off-box egress projector (trace_egress.cljc scoped-keys-slot omits both; the fail-closed default covers only MAP-valued unknown slots, so sequential values ride verbatim) - a real privacy gap, runtime not docs. Root cause of THIS bead confirmed as gate-blindness, not a false green: the 009 ratchet pins the Channel column and the error/warning emit sites and its row parser reads columns 1-3 only (test:122); check_keyword_catalogue_drift Check A is scoped to :rf.error/* / :rf.warning/* literals, so a trace op is out of reach. No new always-on error id, so the three-way co-edit did not apply.

title: The route plan's :branch comes from the display :parent walk, so :rf.route/planned names unregistered routes while the activation aborts
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F2 (rf2-kqxe6.16). The R0 -> R2 seam leak.

TWO :parent WALKS EXIST, DELIBERATELY.
- subs/chain-from-meta - the DISPLAY walk. Defensive: swallows cycles, and INCLUDES an unregistered parent id in the returned chain.
- events/resolve-branch - the PLANNING walk. Fail-loud: {:branch-error {:kind :unknown-parent | :parent-cycle ...}}.

events.cljc:160-162 is explicit: "This is the PLANNING walk; re-frame.routing.subs/chain-from-meta (the display sub) swallows cycles defensively and is NOT A SUBSTITUTE HERE."

THE DEFECT. resolve/branch-of - which produces the route plan :branch field, and therefore the :rf.route/planned trace :branch tag - delegates to chain-from-meta, while commit-navigation independently calls resolve-branch for the resource composition. The plan REPORTS one branch and EXECUTES another, and they disagree exactly on the malformed-registration cases where a diagnostic earns its keep.

CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY on origin/main @ 7d6bcd672e - route :route/leaf declared {:parent :route/nowhere} where :route/nowhere is unregistered:

  unknown-parent branch-of      => [:route/nowhere :route/leaf]
  unknown-parent resolve-branch => {:branch-error {:kind :unknown-parent, :route-id* :route/nowhere}}
  plan :branch                  => [:route/nowhere :route/leaf]
  trace tags :branch            => [:route/nowhere :route/leaf]

So :rf.route/planned names :route/nowhere as a branch segment. No such route exists. The SAME navigation aborts activation with :branch-error :unknown-parent and lands :transition :error - a tool reading the trace sees a plausible two-segment branch with no hint that planning failed on that very chain. Same class for a :parent cycle (chain-from-meta terminates silently at the cycle entry; resolve-branch reports :parent-cycle with the chain).

WHY IT HAPPENED (the shape per-PR review cannot see). R0 exposed :branch as a diagnostic reflection of the chain sub, and branch-of docstring correctly claims it "can never disagree" with the chain sub. R2 then needed a fail-loud walk for composition and ADDED a second one rather than promoting the first. routing_plan_seam_test.clj:60 pins the R0 property (branch-of == chain sub) and nothing pins the R2 one, so the suite certifies the half that is no longer the interesting half.

REMEDY (net deletion; one walk instead of two per navigation).
1. Derive the plan :branch from events/resolve-branch (mapping its [{:route-id :route-meta} ...] to route-ids) and carry :branch-error on the plan.
2. Have commit-navigation read the branch off the plan the door already built instead of re-walking. Both doors already build the plan immediately before calling commit-navigation (navigate.cljc:482-493, url_change.cljc:275-277), so the value is in hand.
3. plan-trace-tags then gains an honest failure signal for free - emit :branch-error (a registration-time kind + route id, no carrier values) when present.
4. Keep chain-from-meta as the display sub walk. It is correct for what it does; it is just not the plan branch.

title: Programmatic {:url} door resolves its own URL: 2 of 4 not-found :reason discriminators and the malformed-URL warning never fire
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F1 (rf2-kqxe6.16). HIGHEST-LEVERAGE item of the review.

WHAT. navigate.cljc:271-282 resolves the raw-URL escape by calling registry/match-url-fail-closed DIRECTLY and re-deriving the not-found shape inline. It is the last surviving second reader of "what does this URL mean". Every other URL-bearing door lowers to resolve/url-resolution, which R0b created precisely because (resolve.cljc:95-99) the :rf.route/not-found fallback normalisation "has to be ONE definition".

THE INVARIANT THE SECOND READER BREAKS. plan.cljc:53-61 states: "The reason vocabulary is SHARED across both entry points ... a malformed percent-encoding stamps :malformed-url; a schema-validation miss stamps :validation ... Encoding the shape once keeps the two paths fallback params byte-for-byte identical." It does not. The inline branch never runs the malformed-url? scan and never inspects :validation-failed?; navigate.cljc:502 hardcodes :malformed? false into the shared telemetry call.

CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY on origin/main @ 7d6bcd672e (JVM, routing test fixture, same malformed URL through two doors):

  NAVIGATE   slice params => {:url "/a/%zz"}
  NAVIGATE   traces       => [... :rf.warning/no-not-found-route :rf.route/planned ...]

  URL-DRIVEN slice params => {:url "/b/%zz", :reason :malformed-url}
  URL-DRIVEN traces       => [... :rf.warning/malformed-url :rf.warning/no-not-found-route
                              :rf.error/no-such-handler {:reason :malformed-url} ...]

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS.
1. EP-0015 malformed-URL diagnostic never fires for a programmatic URL. egress.cljc:17-24 names the threat: a malformed / unmatched URL is "the class most likely to carry secret material (?token=, ?code=, #access_token=)". {:url ...} is documented (spec/012:503) as the form "for dynamic or user-supplied URLs the app did not build itself" - the door where hostile input arrives. It is the one door with no warning.
2. The slice :reason is a PUBLIC read surface with a door-dependent value. spec/012:993 tells authors to branch inside the not-found view on :reason. Nothing tells them the same malformed URL yields :reason :malformed-url or nothing depending on which door delivered it.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE - DO NOT CHANGE. The validation-fail asymmetry is RULED: spec/012 resolve-target table (509-521) and §Validation-error surfacing across the three paths (760-775) ratify caller-bug-rejects vs URL-driven-routes-to-not-found. Preserve it exactly.

REMEDY (a merge, not an abstraction; net deletion). Resolve through resolver/url-resolution and layer the ratified programmatic policy on the shared facts - the same way url_change.cljc:163 layers fragment-only? on the seam raw :match rather than on the normalised target. url-resolution already returns everything needed: :match, :matched?, :validation-fail?, :malformed?, :throw-reason, :target. Take (:route-id match) to preserve the ratified validation-fail behaviour; (when-not matched? url) for unmatched-url; thread :malformed? / :throw-reason into plan/fallback-telemetry-intents (which already accepts both) and into plan/not-found-params. Delete the inline cond arm.

ALSO FIX IN THE SAME PR. registry/match-url-fail-closed docstring still names url-change-fx as a direct caller - it reaches it through url-resolution now. The docstring documents the symmetry R0b intended, not the one that shipped.

TEST. routing_plan_seam_test.clj:329-337 already proves the two doors agree on a BARE miss. Extend to the malformed and throw discriminators (the cases the merged-PR audit could not see, because each PR only ever looked at one door).

title: Auth tutorial falsely retires response-side 401 session-expiry handling
description: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6990: docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md correctly keeps response-side HTTP 401 handling because cached identity is optimistic, but docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md still says the redirect-on-401 interceptor is gone entirely and replaced by :can-enter. A route guard only reads cached auth state and cannot react when a later managed request proves the session expired, so following the tutorial can leave user/token state present and protected routes apparently allowed after the server starts returning 401. Keep the fix bounded to accurate guidance and the existing auth lifecycle; do not add retry machinery or a broader auth subsystem.
acceptance_criteria: The resources tutorial and add-auth guide accurately distinguish route gating from response-side expiry handling; an authenticated 401 clears cached/persisted session state through the existing logout lifecycle; an unauthenticated 401 such as failed login does not trigger logout/navigation; cold-boot restore deferral and both restore outcomes remain unchanged; documentation/link gates pass, with a focused auth pin for the negative path if executable example code changes.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6995 (correctness): the landed one-file repair accurately restores response-side expiry guidance, but its frame-wide :after predicate treats every HTTP 401 as an expired session. This same frame issues the signed-out POST /users/login; if bad credentials produce 401, the hook queues :auth/logout, wipes the form slice, and navigates home before/alongside :auth.login-form/submit-failed. The identical unqualified hook is also in docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md. Keep the repair small: only dispatch logout when the failing request actually carried the bearer credential/session (the :after ctx is the post-:before request ctx), preserve structured failure matching and explicit frame dispatch, and pin an unauthenticated-login 401 negative path. No new auth subsystem or retry machinery.
close_reason:
PR #6998 MERGED; verified on main (the :after hook appears 3 times in docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md).

THE CLAIM WAS HALF FALSE, which is exactly the outcome I asked for rather than a blanket correction. Verified against source: the GATING job genuinely is retired — :can-enter stops the navigation before a request exists. The SESSION-EXPIRY job is not retired and STRUCTURALLY CANNOT BE — :can-enter reads cached auth state, so it cannot notice a token that dies AFTER entry was allowed. The tutorial had claimed the redirect-on-401 response interceptor was "gone entirely, not relocated".

EVIDENCE IT ASSEMBLED rather than asserted: add-auth.md teaches the hook and says it "is what turns that into a clean logout"; spec/014-HTTPRequests section Middleware names 401 response-side handling as a motivating case; spec/Pattern-Boot.md says :refreshing "is the answer to the token expired mid-session"; and nothing in implementation/ handles 401 automatically. The tutorial taught NO response-side hook anywhere — its only 401-adjacent handler was the cold-boot restore :on-failure. So a reader following it shipped an app keeping user and token present, protected routes apparently allowed, while every request 401s.

THE FIX: split the callout into its two jobs, and add the :after hook to the Sign out section where :auth/logout already clears cached and persisted session state — so logout gained a second TRIGGER, not a second code path. No retry machinery, because the token is discarded rather than refreshed. Code block verified against implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc: :after is (fn [ctx response] response) and ctx carries :frame. All settled decisions preserved — synchronous restore in add-auth.md, the Conduit async asymmetry, closed-boolean :can-enter, no {:sensitive ...} ceremony.

Note add-auth.md itself was correct and has no diff — the bead pointed at the resources tutorial.

title: semantic-controllers.md teaches the three controller verbs then ships a reference sketch that uses none of them
description:
Found while auditing rf2-abikw (PR #6993). Filed as EVIDENCE for the standing ruling that a general example-validation gate waits until a SECOND documented example is found violating its own page's rule - the mayor should decide whether this is that second instance.

docs/core/freehand/semantic-controllers.md spends lines 300-401 ('The three verbs a controller uses') teaching that:
  - v/controller-key is 'what makes a controller writable' and that an absent :control is refused with :rf.error/view-control-address-missing, an explicit nil separately with -address-nil (327-335);
  - v/controller-revision is REQUIRED, refused with :rf.error/view-control-reset-revision-missing / -nil (357-363);
  - v/controller-current? is 'ONE predicate, asked at BOTH boundaries', and that a hand-rolled (= a b) gets the missing direction wrong because two nils compare equal (365-398).

Its own reference sketch immediately below - 'What buffered-field looks like (library sketch)', lines 403-456 - does none of that. It keys storage on the bare (get-in db [:fh.buffer/by-control control]) rather than on the (kind, address) pair, never calls v/controller-key or v/controller-revision (so NONE of the four refusals it just documented apply to the code a reader copies), and fences with (= (:reset-key rec) reset-key) - the exact hand-rolled comparison line 395 names as the half that gets it wrong.

WHY IT IS WEAKER THAN rf2-abikw: the page never CLAIMS the sketch uses the verbs, so this is an inconsistency in taught practice rather than a false statement, which is why PR #6993 left it alone. It is nonetheless a documented example that does not honour the law of the page it sits on, and it is the artefact a library author will copy.

REMEDY OPTIONS (owner's call): (a) make the sketch use the three verbs, so the page teaches one thing; (b) leave the sketch minimal but say explicitly why it is minimal and what it forgoes; (c) rule it out of scope. Do not build a general gate on the strength of this alone.
notes:
MAYOR RULING: take remedy (a) — make the reference sketch use the three controller verbs (2026-07-26). The bead offered three options and called it the owner call; the cluster reviewer recommended (a) and I agree.

WHY (a) over (b) "say why it is minimal": the sibling artefact was corrected in exactly this direction. rf2-abikw fixed the form-kit reference sketch to use the real surface rather than annotating why it did not, and leaving this one minimal-with-an-explanation would have the corpus teaching TWO different answers to the same question — which is worse than either answer alone.

WHY NOT (c) "rule it out of scope": the page spends 100 lines teaching three verbs and four refusals, then its own reference sketch uses none of them and fences with the exact (= a b) that line 395 names as wrong. A page that contradicts itself in its own example is not out of scope for a docs-truth fix.

SCOPE FENCE: change the sketch, not the teaching. The 100 lines above it are correct and were not questioned. And note docs/core/freehand/ fenced blocks are DIGEST-PINNED by samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj, so the new digest lands in the same commit — which is also why this bead should ride with the other freehand-docs beads rather than alone, so the pinned tree is re-baselined once.

The view no longer destructures :control or :reset-key at all, so the two verbs are the only door and all four refusals reach copied code. title: Freehand's flush-render! performs no open-event-drain guard; :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch has no Freehand emit site
description:
Found while verifying rf2-jew4k (PR #6993). spec/009's :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch row claims 'one guard, not two copies' - and that claim is TRUE, but only because Freehand never guards at all.

re-frame.ui's substrate/flush-render! opens with (reactive/guard-open-drain! 're-frame.ui.substrate/flush-render!) at implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/substrate.cljs:232, and ui.test/flush! calls the same shared guard (test.cljc:543). The guard exists so a synchronous registry flush forced while a frame's run-to-completion drain is still open fails loud rather than publishing a partial render phase.

(implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/substrate.cljs:269-275) performs NO such check - it goes straight to spine-flush + cell/flush! + cell/converge-flush!. A grep for 'open-epoch|open-drain' across implementation/freehand/src/ returns ONE comment (substrate.cljs:254, about run-to-completion ordering) and no call.

Not actioned by PR #6993 - implementation/freehand/src/** was fenced read-only for that worker and this is outside rf2-jew4k's scope.

Corrected in the same phrasing the sibling convergence row carries.

title: epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test's fixture declares :large as an app-db PATH, so the gate owning 'no raw large bytes anywhere' cannot see the whole-output sub shape
description:
Filed by the mayor on the rf2-irwsq worker's finding — it fixed the instance and deliberately left the CLASS, correctly, per its don't-widen fence. This bead is the class.

WHY IT MATTERS: epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj is the gate that OWNS the claim 'no raw large bytes anywhere' in a projected record. Its fixture declares :large as an APP-DB PATH. The whole-output :large? sub shape is not an app-db-rooted path at all — it is a REGISTRATION stamp — so the gate structurally cannot see it. That blindness is precisely why rf2-irwsq shipped: a 25000-char payload egressed raw at [:trace-events <i> :tags :rf.sub/value] while the gate whose entire job is catching that reported green, and 136 JVM redaction arms alongside it also could not see it.

THE SHAPE OF THE DEFECT is one this project has now met repeatedly: the gate exists, the assertion is real, and the FIXTURE cannot reach the case. Compare the census false greens, where the checker was sound but the witness was computed over the wrong text; and the canned-stub class, where every suite passed over invented producer output. In all three the machinery was fine and the INPUT was wrong.

WHAT TO DO: widen the fixture so it inhabits the whole-output :large? sub shape as well as the app-db path shape, and prove the widening is not vacuous — the gate must go RED against the pre-rf2-irwsq behaviour and green after. The instance is already closed on both lanes by that PR's dual-lane scan, so this bead's whole value is the fixture reaching the class.

DO NOT rebuild the gate, add a second scanner, or generalise into a fixture framework. One fixture gains one more inhabited shape.

WORTH KNOWING while in there: the emit chokepoint DELIBERATELY leaves the value raw so the on-box ring retains it (Xray diff and restore-epoch! both need it) and stamps a bare :large? instead — the flag is the entire contract, and egress is where it must be honoured. The shared rule is now elide-whole-output-large-slots, parameterised by its two value-slot keys and called by both elide-sub-run-row and elide-large-sub-trace-values, so the two projections cannot drift. Any fixture widening should exercise BOTH callers.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING, and a trap for whoever edits that test tree: a .cljc test whose ns ends -cljs-test matches shadow's :ns-regexp AND cognitect's .*-test$, so it runs on BOTH lanes. The rf2-irwsq characterisation pin was therefore green on the JVM too, which is what made it and its own fix mutually invalidating.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP egress conformance fixture inhabits both large-value origins: an app-db path and a whole-output :large? subscription. For the subscription shape, distinct raw current and previous large values are present and proven in both carriers—the structured :sub-runs row and :rf.sub/run trace tags—and all four projected payload slots are canonical markers by default while an unmarked control remains raw. A deliberate regression at either caller/key (or the pre-rf2-irwsq behavior) makes the owning gate fail; current production passes. The fix remains a fixture widening, not a new scanner or fixture framework.
notes:
MAYOR RULING ON THE OPEN QUESTION: do NOT add :rf.mutation/ rows to this fixture (2026-07-26). The worker left the count at 0 deliberately and asked; I agree with its reasoning and am recording it so nobody "completes" the family later.

ITS ARGUMENT, which I am adopting: mutation rows take the IDENTICAL projector and the IDENTICAL slot vocabulary as the resource rows already installed. Settling one requires an HTTP reply round-trip that the ensure path does not need. So the marginal coverage is near zero and the cost is real machinery inside a conformance fixture — which is the direction this bead was explicitly told not to go ("do not generalise into a fixture framework").

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a mutation-only slot, vocabulary or projector branch that the resource rows cannot exercise. If one appears, that is a small follow-up bead with a named uncovered path, not a completeness sweep.

THIS IS THE SAME JUDGEMENT AS rf2-odlm3 and the thrown-error scope ruling: coverage is worth adding where it reaches an unexercised MECHANISM, not where it reaches more INSTANCES of an exercised one.

ALSO RECORDED: rf2-1zc33 did NOT red this fixture, and the reason is benign — the cascade emits no :rf.resource/refetch-decision row. So that bead remains genuinely open and still needs the operator EP-0025 ruling; its absence here is not evidence it is fixed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7021 (merge 6c89dd509ecfa9d0a11ebfaa9ceeb74036fbd691, merged 2026-07-25T19:29:17Z) — exact open owner updated; no duplicate. The resource-family widening is complete and high quality: it drives real producer rows, proves the sensitive/plain directions, records both historical revert signatures, and correctly leaves the already-ruled mutation instance out. The two production findings it surfaced were filed as rf2-hbmeb and rf2-1kiuj and have since merged; rf2-1zc33 remains the distinct open refetch/scope owner. Residual on this Bead original large-value acceptance: drive-mixed-ring! computes :sub/whole-output-large only once, so both raw previous-value slots are nil rather than a distinct large prior value, and forwarder-projected-record-elides-large-leaf-payloads asserts only :value and :rf.sub/value. It never asserts raw or projected :prev-value / :rf.sub/prev-value even though its own docstring says both callers and both slots are inhabited. Therefore deleting or breaking either previous-value projection still leaves this gate green, contradicting acceptance criteria requiring distinct raw current/previous large values and all four projected markers. Current main retains the gap. Bounded completion: drive one recompute with two distinct large values, pin both raw previous slots, all four projected markers, bytes/digest agreement per matching value, and the unmarked control; mutation proof must red when either previous-value projection is disabled. PR range-diff matched all four commits; checks were 49 pass/26 skipped/0 failed; author epoch/resources/CLJS/fast-spine and two historical revert proofs were green/red as claimed.
RESIDUAL CLOSED in PR #7052, merge c7b5c4d56dd118527a5a52e21b1a3318514e899a (blob a8d4c7344ce2a814f629702face75c4d07f6869f). This addresses the merged-PR-#7021 audit note's bounded completion, not the already-done family widening.

WHAT WAS WRONG: drive-mixed-ring! computed :sub/whole-output-large once, so both raw previous-value slots were nil and the acceptance test asserted only :value and :rf.sub/value while its docstring claimed both callers and both slots were inhabited. A nil previous value projects to a marker over nothing, so deleting or breaking EITHER previous-value projection left the gate green — including the cross-cutting 'no leaf of the payload's size anywhere' scans on the per-record AND bulk projected-history surfaces.

WHAT LANDED: the sub's output rides :n; :inc takes a first reading through subscribe (retained past the cascade) before its own increment commits, so :read-subs is a RECOMPUTE. Distinct large current + previous values, proven raw in BOTH carriers; all four projected slots pinned as markers; the two current markers agree on :bytes, the two previous markers agree on :bytes, and current differs from previous. The unmarked control's four slots all still ride raw.

MUTATION PROOF, both directions as the acceptance criteria required — passing a :rf.disabled/prev-value key to the shared elide-whole-output-large-slots rule: elide-sub-run-row off = 5 failures, elide-large-sub-trace-values off = 5 failures. Each names its own slot, both trip the two carriers' :bytes agreement, and both now trip the two cross-cutting scans that were silently blind.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE WORDING, and why: the acceptance criteria say 'bytes/digest agreement per matching value'. There is no :digest to assert at this seam — classification/large-marker is called without include-digests?, so the marker carries :path / :bytes / :type / :reason / :hint / :handle only. :bytes is the per-value agreement the two carriers actually publish, and distinctness is proved by current :bytes /= previous :bytes.

Fixture hygiene added alongside: install-resource-family! pins :trace-events-keep and a new control asserts every settled record kept its :trace-events, so the family cascade's LENGTH is no longer load-bearing against the suite-wide cap of 5.

Gates: epoch 490/6637 rc=0 (baseline 490/6611 — +26 assertions, no new deftest), resources 733/6799 rc=0, core 2115/10462 rc=0.

title: test.yml: tools/testbed-support and tools/machines-viz JVM suites gate no CI job
description:
