tools/testbed-support ships a fully wired :test alias (32 tests / 153 assertions, green, ~6s) whose suite ran in NO lane at all: open_in_editor_server_test.clj is .clj, so the node-test-testbed-support CLJS build that carries the tree on its source paths cannot load it, and the artefact was on neither JVM roster. PR #6988 added it to scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh's sibling scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh so the LOCAL lane exists.

It still has no CI job. test.yml's jvm-tools-* family is xray / story / story-mcp / mcp-base / template; the all-required-passed aggregator lists those five. So two entries on the local tools roster gate nothing in CI:

  tools/testbed-support        (no job at all)

  tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab  (verify: it may be covered by an mcp-conformance job rather than a jvm-tools-* one)

test.yml is hot-zone, so this is deliberately a separate PR rather than folded into the gate that found it. The cheap shape is: add the missing jvm-tools-* jobs (each is seconds), add tools/template to the local roster, and add the new jobs to the all-required-passed needs list.

A follow-on detector is possible and is the durable fix: the bijection gate's universe today is files on a lane root, so a test tree on NO roster is invisible to it. Repo-wide there are ~15 more deftest-bearing trees outside every roster it reads (tools/template/test, skills/*/tests, migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke). Asserting the two rosters against test.yml's job list would close that class, but it needs a workflow-job parser.

The bead's own 'cheap shape' had already landed in #6998/#7055 and I verified it on main before touching anything: the two rosters are bijective at 8 artefacts each way, and tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab is covered by mcp-conformance-wire-vocab (differently named, not missing). title: tools/{story,xray,machines-viz}: 52 .cljc test suites that no CLJS lane selects
description:
Found mechanically by the rf2-4hc9p test-lane bijection gate (scripts/check_test_lane_bijection.py, PR #6988).

The three tools test trees are on the consolidated :node-test build's :source-paths (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn lists ../tools/story/test, ../tools/xray/test, ../tools/machines-viz/test) but are only PARTIALLY converted to the dual-runtime *_cljs_test.cljc convention:

  tools/story/test        27 .cljc CLJS-selected, 43 NOT
  tools/xray/test         38 CLJS-selected,        7 NOT
  tools/machines-viz/test 18 CLJS-selected,        2 NOT

That is the rf2-ezbzvm class (a .cljc whose ns ends -test instead of -cljs-test is invisible to the cljs-test$ selector) with 52 live instances. ~20 of the 52 carry #?(:cljs ...) arms in their BODIES, i.e. they contain CLJS code that never executes; the rest are portable and may be JVM-only by intent. One is explicit about the opposite: tools/story/test/re_frame/story/run_owner_cljc_test.cljc documents 'Runs on BOTH runtimes' while its ns ends -cljc-test, which cljs-test$ does not match. tools/story/test/re_frame/story/viewport_test.cljc documents the opposite intent in prose.

The bijection gate's B2 rule deliberately does not reach these: it applies to test roots the CLJS build OWNS (a :source-paths entry local to the shadow project), not to a ../-escaping entry -- a foreign tree borrowed onto the classpath whose lane is defined by its own deps.edn. They are held by B1 (they DO run, on the JVM), so the gate is green. Widening B2 to reach them requires this work first.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. This is not a rename sweep: rf2-ezbzvm's own experience was that enabling nine such files in the shared node-test bundle EXPOSED two fixtures that called registrar/clear-all! without restoring, breaking sibling namespaces. Doing 52 at once needs per-file triage (does it want CLJS at all?), fixture-isolation review, and a real test:cljs count comparison. Per-file outcome is one of: rename to -cljs-test (dual-runtime), or declare JVM-only. Once every file has taken one of those two, B2's ownership predicate can be widened to the borrowed roots too and the gate holds the result.
notes:
STAYS OPEN ON THE WORKER RECOMMENDATION, and the reason is a real structural blocker rather than remaining effort.

WHAT LANDED (PR #7063, rf2-odlm3 arm): tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn with a :machines-viz-node-test build, selector scoped to the artefact prefix — NO RENAME, nothing joins the shared bundle. 821/3214 rc=0, both previously-unselected suites mutation-proved to execute, and THE OWNERSHIP MOVE ITSELF MUTATION-PROVED: narrow the selector back and the bijection B2 predicate names both files by path where before it said nothing. Bijection gate PASS at 45 lanes, up from 44.

CENSUS RE-DERIVED with the gate own parser and it matches the corrected premise exactly: 140 .cljc, 57 unselected, 52 define tests, 25 carry :cljs arms.

WHY XRAY AND STORY CANNOT HAVE THE SAME LANE YET — three reasons, and the second is the blocker:
  1. shadow-cljs resolves :deps {:aliases [...]} via clojure -A:<alias> and INHERITS :main-opts, so an artefact :test alias hands shadow arguments to cognitect test-runner. Every lane needs a duplicate, divergable alias.
  2. XRAY TEST TREE ESCAPES ITS OWN DEPENDENCY GRAPH FOUR TIMES — into Freehand TEST tree, into re-frame.story (WHICH DECLARES XRAY AS A HARD DEP, SO THE EDGE CANNOT BE A DEPENDENCY WITHOUT A CYCLE), into a testbed namespace, and into implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src. A per-tool lane for Xray would be the consolidated classpath under a new name. Story is the same shape and larger.
  3. Two genuinely UNDER-DECLARED DEPS IN THE PUBLISHED machines-viz JAR (uix.core, re-frame.adapter.reagent) — filed as rf2-3d5u3, declared test-only here, published graph untouched.

THE HONEST NEXT STEP IS ARTEFACT WORK, NOT CI WORK: make the test trees separable first. Four concrete :requires are enumerated on this bead. Do not dispatch a CI lane for Xray or Story until that lands — it would produce a lane that looks per-tool and is not.
close_reason:
PR #7116 (commits 64e023f556 + 33a9eda637). THE XRAY ARM IS DONE; STORY IS DELIBERATELY NOT, and the bead's own analysis is why.

WHAT LANDED: the seven .cljc suites under tools/xray/test whose namespaces ended -test rather than -cljs-test renamed to *_cljs_test.cljc with reader-conditional clojure.test/cljs.test requires. NO build config change -- tools/xray/test is already on the consolidated :node-test source paths -- and the ns still ends -test, so cognitect keeps them in the JVM lane. This is the half that needed NO LANE, ONLY THE SELECTOR, which is why it was landable while a per-tool lane is not. Xray unselected: 7 -> 0.

ARMING THEM FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION BUG ON THE FIRST RUN, which is this bead's thesis demonstrated rather than argued. palette/fuzzy.cljc computed (int ch) on a character taken from a string: a code point on the JVM, but cljs.core/int is (bit-or x 0) and JavaScript coerces a non-numeric string to 0, while (nth some-string idx) yields a ONE-CHARACTER STRING under CLJS. So upper? and lower? answered false for EVERY character in the browser -- the only place Xray's command palette runs -- and both bonuses depending on them went dead: word-start?'s camelCase branch and the explicit camel-boundary bonus in the scoring loop. Separator word-starts kept working (\- and friends compare fine as one-character strings), which is precisely why nothing else in the file noticed. The file's own docstring claimed 'every assertion runs equally under JVM clojure.test and the cljs node-test runtime' and that was false.

GENERALISABLE SHAPE: a .cljc helper that indexes into a string is a cross-runtime trap -- Character vs one-character String -- and it is INVISIBLE while the suite runs on one runtime. Suspect (int ch), (Character/...), and ^Character hints in any .cljc that no CLJS lane selects.

REGRESSION PIN: camelcase-boundary-bonus caught it incidentally (two different strings, so a weight change could make it pass for the wrong reason). Added camel-boundary-credited-on-both-runtimes, which isolates the mechanism: same-length separator-free candidates matched at the same two indices, so only the camelCase boundary can separate the scores, and the separator path cannot satisfy it. Mutation-proved BOTH directions on the real lane: restore (int ch) -> 2 failures rc=1; restore char-code -> 11758 tests / 0 failures rc=0.

EVIDENCE: all seven suites mutation-proved to execute (one sentinel deftest each -> exactly seven FAILs naming the seven paths, 11764 tests, reverted). tools/xray clojure -M:test 1271/5909 rc=0. Bijection gate PASS at 45 lanes. tools/xray/spec/017 updated (the hidden-indicator row named the old filename).

STORY'S 43 STAY OPEN-BY-DESIGN, NOT UNFINISHED: re-verified both blockers still hold. Xray's test tree escapes its dependency graph into re-frame.freehand and re-frame.story, and Story declares Xray as a HARD DEP, so that edge cannot become a dependency without a cycle. A per-tool lane for either would be the consolidated classpath under a new name. File a fresh bead against the artefact-separability work if Story's 43 are wanted; do not re-file this one as a CI task.

title: Freehand census: read a TAGGED LITERAL as the two-datum prefix it is (`#js`, `#inst`, `#?`)
description:
Found while discharging the `MERGED-PR AUDIT #6968` metadata-extent reopen on
rf2-drpa3.53 (PR #6984). REPRODUCED, NOT INFERRED. Deliberately NOT fixed there:
the dispatching mayor scoped that bead to `^` and asked not to be handed a silent
scope expansion.

THE SAME ARITHMETIC, A DIFFERENT PREFIX. `_datum_end` in
`scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py` now reads `^` as consuming its
metadata and then the annotated target. A TAGGED LITERAL has exactly that shape -
`#tag datum` - and is still read as consuming the tag alone:

    _datum_end("#js {:a fx}")        -> "#js"        (should be the whole literal)
    _datum_end('#inst "2020"')       -> "#inst"
    _datum_end("#?(:clj x :cljs y)") -> "#?"
    _datum_end("#?@(:clj [x])")      -> "#?@"

REPRODUCED against PR #6984's script, both false-green axes of the family:

  * (is (= '#js [fx] 1)) on a row bound to `fx` -> `fx` is read as a live
    reference, because the quote's extent ends after `#js` and `[fx]` stays in
    code. Same for the syntax-quoted twin. Neither evaluates the Var.
  * #_#?(:clj (def fx (conf/fixture :FH-CALL-001))) discards only `#?`, so the
    `(:clj (def fx ...))` list survives and the discarded proof site binds a
    fixture the reader never sees.

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE - measured, so the priority is honest. `#js` appears 143
times in `implementation/freehand/test/`, plus 2 `#inst`, 2 `#uuid` and 1
`#queue`, but ZERO of them sit behind a quote prefix or a `#_`, which are the only
positions where extent causes blanking. So no row is currently false-green from
it and the `--report` table would not move. It is a loaded gun rather than a
discharged one: the next author who writes `(is (= '#js [fx] 1))` gets a silent
green, and `#js` is the most common reader macro in the CLJS corpus by two orders
of magnitude.

rf2-mom1g DOES NOT FIRE ON THIS, on the test the mayor recorded for it: this can
be stated as "this existing pass mis-handles form X", not "this needs the pass to
know something only evaluation knows". No dataflow, no binding resolution, no
macro expansion. It is lexically closable by the same recursion `^` now uses.

THE FIX, AND WHY IT WANTS ITS OWN REVIEW RATHER THAN A FOLD-IN. One branch in
`_datum_end`: a `#` followed by a tag character consumes the tag datum and then
its target. But it needs an EXCLUSION LIST that `^` did not - `#'` is a var quote
(one datum), `#(`, `#{`, `#"` are dispatch forms whose datum is the delimited form
itself, and `#_` is already handled upstream. `'` and `_` are both inside
`_SYMBOL_HEAD`, so the naive "symbol character after `#`" rule mis-reads `#'x`.
That exclusion list is the part worth a reviewer's eye, and it is why this is a
bead rather than three more lines on a PR that had a different subject.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `_datum_end` reads `#tag datum` whole, including `#?(...)` and `#?@(...)`,
   with `#'`, `#(`, `#{`, `#"` and `#_` unchanged - proof: the four extents above
   return the whole literal, and a self-test pins each.
2. Red/control pairs on BOTH axes for BOTH quote spellings, in the established
   idiom: `'#js [fx]` and its syntax-quoted twin red at DEAD PROOF SITE;
   `'#js [panel]` beside `(v/defview panel {:compiled true} ...)` reds at
   UNWITNESSED MODE; `#_#?(:clj (def fx ...))` reds at DEAD PROOF SITE.
3. The over-tightening controls, which are the ones that matter here: an UNQUOTED
   `#js [fx]` still reads the fixture, and `'#'fx` has an extent of exactly
   `'#'fx` so a trailing `fx` beside it stays live. Both must be shown red if the
   exclusion list is wrong.
4. Every new case fails before the fix and passes after, both directions shown.
5. The per-row `--report` table stays byte-identical (md5
   bdb95d24524b6a460a687b408a7b1a48 as of PR #6984), and the live census stays
   exit 0.
notes:
SHIPPED in PR #7110 (worker/census-tagged-jl7gz).

THE FIX. `_prefix_end` now stops at a tag `#` the way it already stops at `^`, and `_datum_end` reads both with one recursive two-datum step. All four named inputs return the whole literal. Reproduced the false green first: `(is (= '#js [fx] 1))` had `fx` live because the quote's extent ended after '#js.

THE EXCLUSION LIST, stated positively - a `#` heads a two-datum dispatch when a symbol could start where it points, or a `:` does - with three shapes named out: `#'` (var quote), `#_` (discard), and a LOOKBEHIND for `##Inf`/`##NaN`. That third one is NOT hypothetical: `##NaN` is written straight into the adapter suites, and my first draft regressed `##Inf` to `##Inf 3`. The new extent table caught it.

BEYOND THE BEAD'S FOUR INPUTS, declared not silent: namespaced maps `#:ns{...}` / `#::{...}` are the same two-datum reach spelled with a `:`, measured zero occurrences in the scanned corpus, and included because excluding them would have been the EXTRA rule. Swept every other `#` dispatch: `#(`/`#{`/`#"` need no naming (none of those chars is a symbol head); `#=` gets the same extent either way; `#!` has zero occurrences in any .clj/.cljc/.cljs (the repo's hits are all .cjs shebangs the census never reads).

THE BEAD'S OWN AXIS-2 CASE CANNOT DISCRIMINATE, and this is the finding worth keeping. `#_#?(:clj (def fx ...))` reds under the OLD reader too. The reason is not the extent - read short it does leave `(:clj (def fx ...))` standing, exactly as described - but `_DEFINER_RE` is anchored to the head of a top-level form and the survivor's head is `:clj`, not `def`, so no binding registers and the row reds either way. The wrapper the miscount leaves is INERT. A TAG target is what discriminates, because there the survivor IS the form: `#_#js (def fx ...)` read short leaves the def at top level to bind the fixture -> silent green. Kept the `#?` case anyway, labelled as a regression guard on the top-level anchoring rather than as evidence.

PROOF. Self-test 96 -> 135: a new direct `_EXTENT_CASES` table (26, both directions - the exclusion list has no census-level symptom, so a mini-repo could not tell a correct reading from a lucky one) plus 13 mini-repo cases, 6 red / 7 green. Two of the greens were RED before the fix (the `~#js [fx]` unquote island and reader-conditional arm pairing), so the miscount was dropping real edges as well as inventing them.

GATES. Both CI commands exit 0 locally and 'Freehand conformance index' passes on CI. The per-row --report table is BYTE-IDENTICAL before/after, measured on one rebased tree with main's reader then mine: md5 e8ebf9d786a96d5b8e58e722d67cdc6a, 107 applicable / 107 reached / 108 total / 4 compiled. No row moves - expected, since the bead measured zero corpus exposure. (The bead's md5 bdb95d24... predates 83 commits of corpus movement; before==after on one tree is the invariant that survives.)

MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS, each confirmed applied via git diff --stat + grepping the marker back out before reading the verdict: reverting both functional lines fails 21 cases (14 extent, 7 mini-repo: 5 false-green, 2 false-red); dropping (?!['_]) fails 3; dropping (?<!#) fails 2.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT: only the `'` half of that exclusion is load-bearing. The `_` half changes just `'#_x y`, where it PRESERVES the pre-existing reading, and `_strip` eliminates every `#_` before any downstream pass asks about extent. Defensive, not weight-bearing.

NOTE ON THE DEFERRAL: this bead carried a 'STAYS DEFERRED - measured zero corpus exposure' note from the #7051 audit. The mayor dispatched it anyway; flagging rather than silently overriding. rf2-mom1g is NOT engaged either way - its own practical test ('can the fix be stated as this existing pass mis-handles form X') answers YES, and its notes already record that it does not fire on a defect in the shipped reduction.

title: RealWorld auth boot races async identity restore, while the resources sibling still teaches an interceptor
description:
Merged-PR audit #6965 found one coupled auth-boot defect across the two flagship RealWorld apps and the newly rewritten guide path.

The canonical realworld_http app declares :can-enter [:realworld.routing/authed?], whose sub is simply (some? [:auth :user]). core.cljs says frame :initial-events make session restore COMPLETE before the URL-bound frame's initial URL->slice sync. That is false for the real path: frame/run-setup-events! explicitly settles only synchronous work and does not await asynchronous effects; :auth/initialise writes {:user nil :token token} and starts GET /user; the live transport is asynchronous and the bundled demo deliberately delays replies by 20ms. The initial protected deep link is therefore judged while :user is nil, :rf.route/entry-denied replace-navigates to login, and :auth/session-restored deliberately performs no navigation, leaving a valid restored user stranded on /login.

The existing session-restore-with-token test false-greens because its canned override replies synchronously and it commits a PUBLIC article route before dispatching auth initialise. It never exercises the URL-bound frame lifecycle, a protected initial URL, or a deferred restore reply.

The realworld_resources sibling has the same async identity window but still carries the pre-EP-0037 frame-wide :realworld-resources.routing/auth-guard normaliser in routing.cljs, both frame configs, README, schema/auth comments, and tests. docs/routing/testing.md likewise still calls route-auth guards interceptors while linking the now-:can-enter recipe. This is not a request for a second auth subsystem: choose one minimal, explicit restore-before-route contract and make both examples demonstrate it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A URL-bound cold boot at a protected deep link with a valid saved token neither commits protected activation/data before identity is known nor redirects away permanently; after successful restore it remains at or enters the original exact destination.
2. Absent, expired, and failed restores remain fail-closed and follow the terminal :can-enter / :rf.route/entry-denied fresh-return contract.
3. Both RealWorld examples demonstrate the canonical route-owned :can-enter shape; remove the resources app's per-door auth normaliser/frame-interceptor wiring and update its README/comments/tests. If a different mechanism is retained, record the concrete reason it is the supported exception.
4. Add an adversarial CLJS regression using the real URL-bound frame lifecycle, a protected initial URL, and a deferred restore reply; a synchronous canned reply or a public-route pre-navigation is insufficient.
5. Correct the false 'restore completes before the guard' comments and docs/routing/testing.md's stale auth-interceptor pointer; relevant CLJS/browser, routing, example, and docs gates pass.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6983 (2026-07-25): PARTIAL repair; do not close this owner yet. The RealWorld HTTP runtime now correctly distinguishes token-present/user-unknown, defers :rf.route/entry-denied, settles the stashed destination after both restore outcomes, and shows an honest restoring shell. However, the PR adds no test/fixture at all: none of settle-deferred-entry, estoring-session?, or session-restoring occurs in a test/spec/fixture file. Required CLJS/browser/example gates compile and run existing suites, but the exact false-green named by this Bead remains: no URL-bound frame boots on a protected URL with a genuinely deferred restore reply and proves success/failure ordering plus no premature login bounce. The PR also touches zero realworld_resources files, so that sibling still carries :realworld-resources.routing/auth-guard in routing.cljs, both frame configs, README/schema prose, and related tests/teaching. Keep rf2-k85nd in progress until the behavior has a non-vacuous deferred-lifecycle regression and the sibling disposition is completed.
close_reason:
Fixed across PR #6983 (merged: realworld_http deferral) + PR #6990 (the stranded remainder: resources sibling migrated off the auth-guard interceptor to :can-enter, both AuthSlice :return-to schemas corrected to mirror :rf/route-destination, the adversarial URL-bound cold-boot regression, docs/routing/testing.md).

DESIGN: :can-enter stays a closed boolean; the DENIAL HANDLER distinguishes 'not signed in' from 'not known yet'. Mid-restore it stashes the destination and stays put (denial is terminal, so nothing protected commits while waiting); :auth/settle-deferred-entry resolves the stash once restore settles — fresh navigate on success, login on failure with the stash preserved. Machine's failed-restore split into :abandon-restore so a public deep link is no longer yanked home.

AC4 evidence: realworld-cold-boot-deep-link-race drives the REAL frame lifecycle (a :url-strategy whose :decode reports the protected URL, the app's ordered :initial-events, a managed-HTTP override that CAPTURES the restore and answers nothing). Verified 4 failures before the fix, 0 after. Fail-closed arms pinned: expired token, absent token, public deep link, full-address preservation.

SECOND BUG FOUND: both apps' AuthSlice :return-to demanded all four address keys while destination-of emits a MINIMAL :rf/route-destination — so a bare /settings denial failed post-commit validation and rolled the stash back. Load-bearing for the deferral.

title: Freehand behaviors: :update and command returns silently replace connection memory — void-returning JS mutators erase the instance :disconnect needs
description: Verified 2026-07-25 (sol-max.md finding, confirmed against source; see ai/findings/freehand-design-review/fable.md addendum). remember! writes unconditionally with no nil guard (behaviors.cljc:693-698); reconcile! replaces memory with :update's raw return (:735-738); every delivered command's return also replaces memory (:1055-1056). Ordinary JS mutators return undefined (map.setOptions, workbook ops, listener registration), so the first void-returning :update or command erases the stored instance and :disconnect loses the object it must clean up. Status split: :update-replaces-memory is normative (spec/004-Views.md:1669-1670 'Its return replaces the memory') — documented but hazardous, and the guide never states it (host-boundaries.md:131-132 documents return->memory for :connect only; the autosize example's :update returns (fit! node config) unstated). Command-return->memory appears in NO document and sits against 004:1778 ('It returns no handle') and D013:177 ('return values are not host handles') — implementation-invented. Concrete guide hazard: js-libraries.md Pattern D :update returning (retarget-fade! ...) erases {:anim ...}; (some-> (:anim memory) cancel!) then silently skips — leaked animation; the spec's own example at 004:1620 would throw instead. No test pins the semantics either way (fh-behavior-004.edn asserts only connect's return arriving at first :update). Proposed law (sol-max): only :connect establishes memory; :update/command/disconnect receive it and their returns are ignored; adapters needing evolving state return a mutable cell from :connect. Breaks zero tests; needs one spec sentence reworded (004:1669-1670); for commands it aligns better with the ruled text than the implementation does. Decide the law, align spec+impl+guide, and pin it with a conformance arm.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6991 (merged 2026-07-25T13:29:31Z) — REOPENED exact source owner; no duplicate. The two authored commits landed as an exact patch-equivalent range. Runtime review confirms remember! has one connect-only call site; update/command returns are discarded; FH-BEHAVIOR-009 proves void update + command preserve one instance through disconnect. The raw foreign-prop correction is also sound and proportionate: a real browser callback closes over capture-frame, the dead carrier is an identity-preserving negative control, and rf2-c1vvn is correctly closed with rf2-yn5nj owning only the typed-DX follow-up. Required PR checks are green; focused Freehand JVM passed 1099/7390 and the conformance index gate passed locally. COMPLETENESS FINDING: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1956-1962 and its generated docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md:1236-1242 mirror still show autosize with BOTH :connect and :update calling (fit! node config), then :disconnect calling .disconnect on :connect's return. The PR body correctly identified this exact shape as leaking a new observer per update and fixed spec/004 plus host-boundaries to use :connect (observe! ...) / :update (fit! ...), but missed the facade docstring/API example while claiming all eight readers aligned. Under the new law update's second handle is discarded and only the first is disconnected, so the copyable public example teaches the leak the change set out to remove. BOUNDED REPAIR: make the facade example match the ruled spec/guide (resource creation only in :connect, effect-only refit in :update/command), regenerate the API mirror, and run existing API/docs gates; no new lifecycle mechanism or general example-validation framework.
close_reason:
PR #6991 MERGED. Its worker reported both beads closed but only rf2-c1vvn was; closing this one on the merged SHA with its evidence.

RULING IMPLEMENTED: memory is the connection, established once with it. The connect return establishes it; update, a delivered command and disconnect all RECEIVE it and their returns are discarded. remember! now has exactly ONE call site. Host state that genuinely evolves returns a mutable cell from connect.

IT REJECTED THE NIL-GUARD ALTERNATIVE ON EVIDENCE, not taste: a nil guard would not have fixed the guide own Pattern D, whose update returned a NON-nil wrong thing — retarget-fade! erasing the anim entry, so the cancel call silently skipped and the animation leaked. Only the ruled law fixes that.

THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS FOR THE RECORD: (1) command-return-to-memory WAS documented, contrary to the bead — host-boundaries.md:175, the command-log facade docstring, and the generated docs/api mirror; the accurate claim is that it is absent from the NORMATIVE spec and sits against 004 It returns no handle. (2) behaviors.cljc own ns docstring ALREADY STATED the ruled law, 300 lines above the code that broke it. (3) Spec 004 flagship autosize example leaked under EITHER law — its update called the same fit! as connect, building a second observer per config move; now connect observes and update re-fits.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE BEST PART: reverting remember! in place reds FH-BEHAVIOR-009 with 2 failures + 1 error rc=1, and NOTHING ELSE in the 783-test browser suite reds. That absence is itself the finding — every other behavior in the corpus returned memory from update and each command, so no other row COULD have seen this defect.

Eighteen files was the multiple-readers hazard, not scope creep: the memory law had EIGHT readers that could disagree, and the single statement now lives in spec/004 with the rest pointing at it.

Gates: freehand JVM 1099/7390, test:cljs 11441/57250, test:browser 783/4933 with 0 build warnings, census self-test plus live census at 98 rows with FH-BEHAVIOR-009 witnessed in the browser lane per --report, test-fast-pr.sh PASS, all rc=0. THREE documented false-green vectors fired for real in that run and all three were caught: the backgrounding harness reported exit code 0 for the negative-control run whose captured log says RC=1; test-fast-pr.sh soft-skipped mkdocs and still exited 0; and grep FAILED over the spine log returned 14 hits that are all ok-to-FAILED negative self-tests.

title: Freehand: inward foreign-callback path is dead code — v/event carriers are non-callable in raw createElement props, and the guide prescribes exactly that
description: Verified 2026-07-25 (two independent reviews + implementation verification; see ai/findings/freehand-design-review/, esp. sol-max.md + fable.md addendum). v/event / v/handler return a Callback deftype with no IFn (events.cljc:372-374, deliberate: 'a foreign API handed one by accident fails at the call'). The child fold passes finished React elements through untouched (react.cljs:965-970), and no code path materializes a carrier found inside a foreign element's #js props — the only materialization sites are Freehand-owned event sites, slots, the route-link seam, and the compiled emitters. Consequence: all three documented inward-callback examples hand the library a non-callable object and can never dispatch — host-boundaries.md:42-45 (DatePicker :onChange), js-libraries.md:95-100 (Sparkline :onSelect), js-libraries.md:206-209 (Scrubber :onChange). The docs also prohibit the only spelling that works today ('never a bare function at a foreign callback position') even though a bare CLJS fn IS a callable JS function and the walk cannot see raw createElement props anyway. The F5i pilot exercises no callback through the raw-child path while its widget advertises one (pilot_react_interop_react.cljs:339-354). Fix has two horizons: (interim) correct the three guide examples to plain closures with an honesty note about phase/identity, or fence them as landing with the host leaf — guide code blocks are digest-pinned so each is a two-file change; (real) the qualified host leaf's declared callback positions are precisely the missing materialization point — all four sibling reviews independently rank landing it as the top change. Native :on-* sites and v/->react are unaffected (verified working).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6991 (worker/fh-behavior-defects). VERDICT: the guide was wrong AND an honest path already exists — so this is the '{:frame :app} equivalent' outcome, not the 'state the gap and stop' one. NO verb was invented. REPRODUCED the mechanism exactly as filed: v/event returns a Callback deftype with no IFn (events.cljc:372-374, deliberate); the child fold passes finished React elements through IDENTICALLY (react.cljs:965-970 — now asserted with identical?, not merely read); no path materialises a carrier inside a foreign element's #js props; the F5i pilot exercised no callback through the raw-child path while acme-widget advertised onPing. PREMISE ADDITION: there is a FOURTH prescribing site, not three — js-libraries.md:135 (Pattern C, Framer motion.div) carries :onAnimationComplete (v/event [] [:toast/settled id]) in raw #js props. All four corrected. THE HONEST SPELLING is a closure over (rf/capture-frame)'s :dispatch, which spec/004D already names for exactly this case TWICE ('A Freehand view binds its frame at the root instead ... and holds one across lifetimes with rf/capture-frame'; 'Outside a view, hold a frame across lifetimes explicitly with rf/capture-frame'), which docs/core/events.md §No ambient frame teaches for the same reason, and whose own docstring example is this pattern in a view body for observer callbacks. The frame is the load-bearing half and it is why a bare rf/dispatch closure is ALSO wrong: frame/*current-frame* is bound only for the synchronous body evaluation (cell.cljc:345) and there is no :rf/default floor (frame.cljc:726-755), so an ambient dispatch from a deferred foreign callback raises :rf.error/no-frame-context; capture-frame's bundle is incarnation-fenced and recover-but-emits rather than retargeting a same-id successor. The docs' blanket prohibition ('never a bare function at a foreign callback position') was wrong in BOTH directions at a raw createElement prop — nothing rejects a closure there because Freehand never sees the prop, and a closure is the only thing callable; event-plan (events.cljc:659) confirms :bare-fn is legal at a native :on-* site. The roster's real boundary is POSITIONS FREEHAND WALKS, now stated once under a new events-and-handlers.md §Where the roster reaches that host-boundaries.md, js-libraries.md and limits-and-escapes.md all link to; the trade (no site-owned identity, no retirement fence — use a behavior when either matters) is stated on every page that teaches it. NOT BUILT: the real fix is materialising the qualified host leaf's declared callback positions, and that leaf has not landed (spec/004 §Qualified host leaves is still a 'Lands in: F4' stub). Filed rf2-yn5nj separately for the DX half (a typed diagnostic when a carrier is invoked, with the full list of readers that must be audited before Callback gains IFn). PROVED BOTH WAYS in the pilot, closing its advertised-but-unexercised gap: a-roster-carrier-in-raw-js-props-can-never-be-called runs in BOTH node and browser lanes (not fn?, not ifn?, thrown? when invoked as a library would, plus identical? on the element AND on the carrier through the fold); a-foreign-component-calls-back-through-a-captured-frame drives a real DOM click on the third-party component's own button and asserts [:acme/pinged "click:beta"] landed in this page's frame with 0 nested roots and 0 behavior connections. Gates: freehand JVM 1099/7390 0/0; test:cljs 11441/57250 0/0; test:browser 783/4933 0/0 with 0 build warnings; mkdocs --strict clean; test-fast-pr.sh PASS; all six edited guide digests re-pinned in the same commit.

title: Freehand: control-address authoring sugar (explicit, non-positional, collision-loud)
description:
## Why
Dense UIs and re-com-style ports drown in :control address noise. Positional/derived addresses are rejected (D004) for good reasons; ceremony still needs product help.

## Work
Design + implement helpers that:
- keep addresses caller-owned and explicit in the data plane
- compose route/entity/field ids safely
- make duplicate-owner diagnostics impossible to miss
- optional control-scope patterns that still reify concrete addresses into the tree (no silent position identity)

## Constraints

title: RULING NEEDED: does day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring keep its published dependency on day8/re-frame2-ssr?
description:
Surfaced by rf2-p4a93 (PR #6967). Not a tag blocker — that PR closed the failure mode via the release DAG — but the underlying packaging contract is unresolved and a ruling is cheaper to make now than after a coordinate is public.

THE TENSION. ssr-ring publishing a dependency on day8/re-frame2-ssr diverges from spec/Conventions.md §Independence rule and Spec 006 §Adapter shipping convention, which expect a published artefact to depend on core and nothing else in the set. ssr-ring is the only one of the thirteen published artefacts that does otherwise.

MAYOR RECOMMENDATION — KEEP THE DEPENDENCY, and document the exception rather than removing it. Three reasons:
  1. re-frame.ssr.ring GENUINELY needs re-frame.ssr. It is the Ring host adapter for SSR; the dependency is real, not accidental coupling. The Independence rule exists to stop artefacts acquiring incidental edges, not to forbid a host adapter depending on the thing it hosts.
  2. Removing it breaks the consumer the rule is meant to protect. A consumer who pins only day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring currently resolves a working artefact. Drop the published dep and that same pin resolves something that cannot run until they discover and add a second coordinate — worse ergonomics, and exactly the low-friction failure the posture argues against.
  3. The failure mode it created is already closed. rf2-p4a93 made the ssr publisher a strict transitive needs: ancestor of the ssr-ring publisher, and added _release-dag-policy.test.cjs asserting that rule GENERALLY over the workflow's object model, with its teeth proved by reconstructing the pre-fix violation. So the risk that motivated revisiting the contract is handled by machinery rather than by amputation.

SO THE WORK, if this recommendation stands: amend Conventions §Independence rule and Spec 006 §Adapter shipping convention to name ssr-ring as the one sanctioned inter-artefact edge, with the reason, and cross-reference the DAG policy test as the thing that keeps it safe. CHANGELOG.md is not to be touched (ruled unmaintained).

IF MIKE PREFERS REMOVAL instead, note what it costs: every consumer pinning ssr-ring must add day8/re-frame2-ssr explicitly, the release-notes body and install docs need the pair documented together, and the DAG policy test's one real edge disappears — which is fine, but it also removes the only live case exercising that gate.

NON-GOALS either way: do not introduce a general dependency-tier scheme, and do not relax the Independence rule into vagueness. Name the single exception or remove it.
notes: OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): "these are my decision beads and we will look at them one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52". Do NOT dispatch. Do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate. Surface only when Mike asks, or when a merge makes one newly urgent.
close_reason:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26): "Keep". day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring KEEPS its published dependency on day8/re-frame2-ssr.

WHY THIS WAS A RULING AND NOT A DIFF: the question is what a CONSUMER gets. A published artefact declaring its real dependency is the honest shape — a consumer adding ssr-ring gets a working classpath, not a NoClassDefFoundError on first use. Removing the edge would have made the coordinate lighter and broken.

THE EVIDENCE THAT SETTLED THE ADJACENT QUESTION, from rf2-1zbpw (merged today) and worth keeping beside this ruling because the two are easy to confuse:
  - clein install WRITES NO POM AT ALL — clein/install is clean + copy-src + compile-java + b/jar + b/install and NEVER calls write-pom. Measured: the installed dir held only _remote.repositories and the jar; jar tf showed only MANIFEST.MF. SO YOU CANNOT REASON ABOUT PUBLISHED DEPENDENCY SCOPE FROM WHAT A LOCAL INSTALL PRODUCES.
  - The NEGATIVE CONTROL was decisive: ssr alone resolved rc=0 with core ABSENT, proving the missing edge is real and that ssr-ring OWN DIRECT core coordinate is what makes it inert.
  - THE PUBLISHED POM IS A DIFFERENT ARTEFACT AND IS CORRECT.

RELATED PRECEDENT SET TODAY, so the next dependency question is not reasoned from scratch: rf2-nucj0 asked to move Cheshire to :provided on day8/re-frame2-http and the answer was STOP — the JVM branch is SPECIFIED (Spec 014 section 26 ships that transport and line 168 names Cheshire as the JVM :json codec), the require is unconditional inside a reader conditional, and a simulated provided consumer got FileNotFoundException AT NAMESPACE LOAD. A boot failure for every JVM consumer. And ":provided means a container supplies it; there is no container."

THE GENERAL SHAPE ACROSS ALL THREE: PROVE IT AS A CONSUMER EXPERIENCES IT — simulate a classpath with only the published coordinate and observe the actual failure — rather than reasoning from :require forms or from a local install. Three beads used that method today and two of them reversed their own premise doing it.

title: test-fast-pr.sh claims to mirror CI's PR-gate matrix but runs 1 of the 20 JVM artefact suites
notes:
Filed by the pre-alpha tests/clarity audit (rf2-ods8n, lens B), 2026-07-25 19:15 AUSEST.

scripts/test-fast-pr.sh header states: 'Mirrors CI's PR-gate matrix so workers see local failures BEFORE pushing — and mirrors CI's *tiering* too...'

In .github/workflows/test.yml, TWENTY jobs gate on the single flag implementation_jvm == 'true': jvm-core, jvm-ui, jvm-reagent, jvm-reagent-slim, jvm-uix, jvm-schemas, jvm-machines, jvm-routing, jvm-flows, jvm-http, jvm-ssr, jvm-security, jvm-ssr-ring, jvm-epoch, jvm-resources, jvm-freehand, jvm-spec-resource, jvm-reply-conformance, jvm-derivation-conformance, jvm-event-conformance, jvm-test-quiet.

The spine runs exactly ONE:
  run "core JVM" "cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test" ...

So a worker touching implementation/routing/src and running the documented pre-checkin gate gets ZERO routing JVM coverage locally — 487 tests / 2542 assertions unrun — while CI runs them. Same for resources (719/6713), machines, ssr, epoch, schemas, http, flows, ssr-ring.

The coverage IS reachable (scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh, listed in CLAUDE.md). The defect is that the spine's own header asserts a fidelity it does not have, which is how a worker ends up trusting a green that means much less than it says.

SECOND HALF, same bead: the spine's one run_soft (mkdocs --strict) genuinely exits 0 when mkdocs is off PATH. Deliberate and documented, but it means 'PASS fast PR spine' on a Windows worker is compatible with the docs build never having been attempted. At minimum the final PASS line should enumerate what was SKIPPED, not just print PASS.

REMEDY OPTIONS (mayor's call):
  (a) correct the header to state the actual tiering (core JVM only + node/CLJS + static), and point at test-jvm-implementation.sh for the rest; or
  (b) have the spine delegate to test-jvm-implementation.sh when implementation_jvm fires, matching CI by construction (slower, but 'mirrors CI' becomes true); or
  (c) run the JVM suite of the artefact(s) the classifier actually saw change.
(c) is probably the right shape — cheap, and it is what a worker wants.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #6975 (merged 2026-07-25 11:07Z, commit 70835664fe), with a prose follow-up in PR #6982.

REMEDY TAKEN: option (a) — correct the CLAIM. The header now states what each tier really contains: JVM tier = implementation/core ONLY, with the seventeen other implementation_jvm artefact suites named and scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh pointed at; and the browser lanes, prod-elision/bundle-isolation/perf gates, adapter probes, adapter smokes, Xray matrix, mcp-conformance and tool JVM suites named as being in NO tier. Tier SELECTION still mirrors CI (delegated to the same classifier); tier CONTENTS are the spine's own narrower set, and the header says so.

VERIFIED COUNT CORRECTION: the bead said 'TWENTY jobs gate on implementation_jvm' and listed 21 names. The actual figure is EIGHTEEN (enumerated from test.yml); the three adapter probes (jvm-reagent, jvm-reagent-slim, jvm-uix) gate on adapter_diagnostic, which the spine does not consult at all. The landed prose uses eighteen.

SECOND HALF DONE: 'PASS fast PR spine' is now followed by 'NOT RUN by this spine (N):' enumerating every skipped tier AND the mkdocs soft-skip, so a green on a Windows worker no longer hides that the docs build was never attempted. --plan carries the same core-only note, pinned by two new self-test cases (Q/R) so the honesty note cannot silently vanish. TESTING.md's command table says the same where workers read it.

FOLLOW-UP PR #6982: the header quoted 'routing's 487 JVM tests'; routing measured 494 an hour later on the rebase, so the numeral is removed — a count in a comment is the exact staleness class these beads are about. Measurements live in PR gate evidence instead.

EVIDENCE: spine tiering self-test 18/18 rc=0 (Q/R new); --plan rc=0 prints the core-only note; scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh 22/22 artefacts PASS rc=0.

Option (c) (run the changed artefact's own JVM suite) NOT done here — the classifier emits one implementation_jvm key with no per-artefact granularity, so it needs new classifier outputs plus a wall-clock decision. Filed as rf2-uwszd.

title: epoch privacy/egress-redaction tier (136 deftests) runs on the JVM only; every consumer of that surface is ClojureScript
notes:
Filed by the pre-alpha tests/clarity audit (rf2-ods8n, lens B), 2026-07-25 19:15 AUSEST.

day8/re-frame2-epoch is a published coordinate. Lane split measured on origin/main @4b6db2ebb2:
  JVM : 25 .clj files, 441 tests, 6291 assertions
  CLJS:  4 files, 28 deftests total (epoch_cljs_test.cljs 20, epoch_committed_at_clock 2, epoch_late_bind_missing 2, epoch_elision_prod_test 6)
  .cljc (dual-lane) test files: ZERO

The redaction/egress tier is entirely inside the JVM-only set:
  epoch_privacy_test.clj                    39 deftests
  epoch_redact_fn_test.clj                  24
  epoch_egress_trace_events_test.clj        21
  epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj     20
  epoch_redact_fn_projection_test.clj       16
  epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj      16
  TOTAL                                    136

And: grep -c 'redact\|sensitive' epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_cljs_test.cljs  ->  0

Every real consumer of the epoch egress projection (Xray, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp, browser Tool-Pair time travel) runs in ClojureScript. The redaction contract is a DATA-LEAK guard, and this area has already produced one false-green — .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh carries the note: 'a PR that broke the epoch egress/redaction contract merged GREEN at PR time (a conformance false-green on a DATA-LEAK guard), surfacing only in the nightly cron.' That fix armed mcp_live / mcp_conformance; it did NOT add CLJS-lane coverage of the redaction tier.

MITIGATING (so this is scoped, not alarmist): only 17 reader conditionals exist across ~5800 lines of epoch/src, and the three in the egress ns (tool_pair.cljc:100,194,746) are fail-CLOSED validity catches — (catch #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) _ true) — not redaction bypasses. The host-divergence surface is genuinely small. This is about where the EVIDENCE lives, not a known bug.

REMEDY. Promote the smallest host-neutral core of the privacy tier to .cljc with a -cljs-test suffix. ONE file is enough to close the asymmetry: the projected-record sensitive/large substitution table (the shape epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj already exercises). Do not mass-convert 136 deftests.

Not an alpha blocker.
DONE. PR #6974 merged (merge commit affb7f6a266926e68e117fc29743d881ea308f69), head c08d47a489.

ONE new dual-lane file, +902 lines, no deletions, no build-config change:
  implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc
  ns re-frame.epoch-egress-redaction-cljs-test  ->  29 deftests / 110 assertions

Runs on BOTH lanes from one source: shadow-cljs :node-test selects it via
:ns-regexp "cljs-test$", and cognitect test-runner's default .*-test$ selects it under
implementation/epoch's clojure -M:test. implementation/epoch/test was ALREADY on the
:node-test source paths (shadow-cljs.edn:111), so the hot-zone build config is untouched.

EXACT DELTAS, both lanes (rc captured with rc=$? into worktree-local logs, cross-checked
against each log's own Ran/failures lines; nothing piped through tail or grep):
  JVM  epoch clojure -M:test : 441 -> 470 tests, 6291 -> 6401 assertions, rc 0
  CLJS npm run test:cljs     : 11382 -> 11411 tests, 56987 -> 57097 assertions, rc 0
  focused CLJS (--test=<ns>) : 29 tests / 110 assertions, rc 0
  selector-guard control     : the same selector with a deliberate typo exits rc 1
                               ("no tests matched --test= selector(s)"), so the green
                               focused run is POSITIVE proof the node lane DISCOVERS the
                               namespace rather than silently skipping it on a suffix
                               mismatch.

MUTATION CONTROL. implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc, walk-decider:
  (and sensitive? (not include-s?))  ->  (and sensitive? include-s?)
i.e. the off-box default stops redacting. Focused CLJS run, same bundle recompiled:
  before   0 failures, rc 0
  mutated 30 failures across 17 distinct deftests, rc 1
  reverted 0 failures, rc 0, git diff --stat empty
The 12 arms that stayed green are exactly the ones not on the sensitive axis (large
elision, bookkeeping pass-through, retention window, sub-output, nil input, rollup
badge) - the suite discriminates rather than being one undifferentiated smoke test.

CI on the exact merged SHA: 73 checks, 0 failing, 0 pending. CLJS (shadow-cljs
:node-test) pass 10m27s; JVM epoch (clojure -M:test) pass 39s; JVM core pass 3m54s.
Locally scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exited 1 ONCE, on a shadow-cljs par-compile abort
(re-frame.ui died in a par-compile worker with its exception swallowed; two dependent
waits cascaded) under six-worker contention. Reported as red, not rounded to green:
npm run test:cljs had passed twice standalone at the same commit, there was no zombie
shadow server, CI passed the same step on the same SHA, and the diff structurally cannot
reach re-frame.ui.

MIRRORED (the leak-critical arms, nine groups). Selection test: would its failure mean a
sensitive value actually escapes to a CLJS consumer?
  1. App-db substitution table - :db-after / :db-before sensitive -> :rf/redacted,
     :large -> :rf.size/large-elided, sensitive-dominates-large precedence, bookkeeping
     pass-through, nil / non-map input.
  2. The FACADE path - re-frame.core/projected-record + projected-history, and opts
     threading through the 2-arity. This is what Xray's runtime/egress-record and every
     pair-mcp epoch tool actually call, so it crosses the late-bind seam
     (:epoch/projected-record, :on-absent :nil). The JVM tier drives the artefact-internal
     re-frame.epoch/projected-record almost exclusively, so that seam had NO coverage on
     the consumers' host. Falling through to identity leaks everything; to nil ships
     nothing.
  3. Forwarder + bulk-egress shapes - register-listener! :epoch with project-in-ship!,
     projected-history == mapv projected-record, oldest-first order, triple-projection
     fixpoint, ring immutability (mutation would make browser restore-epoch! time-travel
     to redacted state).
  4. Axis orthogonality - :include-sensitive? must not lift :effects[*].args, the
     :rf.db/runtime partition, or large slots; :include-event-args? must not lift app-db.
     BOTH original bugs were CLJS-side: rf2-m9duxl (pair-mcp treating include-sensitive
     as a full raw-epoch bypass) and rf2-5w06uu (Xray walking the raw record on opt-in and
     lifting the orthogonal runtime-db partition). Each has an explicit negative control
     proving the axis is independently governed.
  5. :trigger-event event-args fail-closed (rf2-nm611o) - positional and map-nested
     secrets, head id retained, :include-event-args? orthogonality.
  6. :trace-events - the t1/t2 pending-db tag RE-ROOT (delete it and a secret nested at
     [:tags :rf.event/db :auth :password] survives while every :db-after assertion stays
     green - the exact false-green shape this bead is about), plus off-box
     :rf.http/off-box-body :omit fail-closed. The HTTP arm is NOT server-shaped: a browser
     XHR reply with an unschematized body lands in :trace-events the same way, and a
     bearer token there is the canonical leak. Both slots are read by Xray's Issues lens
     and pair-mcp trace-window.
  7. Classification RETENTION - a path classified once keeps redacting on later,
     unrelated cascades (a registry that only applied to the writing cascade would leak
     from every subsequent record, which is what a watch-epochs stream ships); the
     :rf.epoch/sensitive? rollup badge survives projection; the :trace-events-keep window
     bounds what a bulk egress can carry.
  8. The :redact-fn egress override - runs at egress not storage, still runs under
     :include-sensitive?, and falls back to the PROJECTED record when it throws.
     Genuinely host-shaped: the catch is #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) and CLJS
     :default catches non-Error throws for which no JVM Throwable clause is an analogue,
     so the arm throws both an ex-info and a bare non-Error value.
  9. Large sub-output :sub-runs value slot (rf2-at60h) - epoch_cljs_test.cljs exercises
     NO subscriptions at all, so the CLJS lane had zero :sub-runs egress coverage of any
     kind.

NON-VACUITY is structural, not asserted. Every redaction claim is paired with something
that would break it: an unclassified sibling path ([:audit :note]) carrying a benign twin
string through the SAME projection call, so blanket-redaction and an empty :db-after both
go red; a dedicated never-classified control frame running the identical cascade where
the secret rides through RAW; the explicit :include-* opt-in revealing the value; and the
raw ring asserted to still contain the secret wherever a "projected output is clean"
claim is made, so no clean-scan can pass against an empty ring.

JUDGED JVM-LEGITIMATE / NOT MIRRORED, ordered by strength of reason (full prose in the
PR body):

  A. GENUINELY JVM-SHAPED - 3 arms. epoch_privacy_test.clj
     projected-record-handles-empty-history-under-disabled-gate and
     projected-record-pure-fn-survives-disabled-gate; epoch_egress_trace_events_test.clj
     off-box-http-fail-closed-survives-cold-gate-false. All three drive
     interop/debug-enabled? FALSE by rebinding a JVM var. CLJS has no runtime analogue -
     the gate is compile-time goog.DEBUG DCE, already covered on the CLJS side by
     epoch_elision_prod_test.cljs (6 deftests, run under the dedicated
     :browser-test-prod-elision build via npm run test:browser-prod-elision, :advanced +
     goog.DEBUG false) plus the scripts/check-elision.cjs sentinel sweep. Mirroring them
     would test a var-rebind that does not exist where the consumers run.

  B. OWNED BY A DIFFERENT ARTEFACT - 16 arms, all of epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj.
     Every arm routes through :resources/project-scope-resolved-egress /
     :resources/project-resource-trace-egress, late-bound hooks the RESOURCES artefact
     publishes and owns; epoch's side is a nil-safe two-line delegation. Verified rather
     than assumed: implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc
     calls scope-registry/project-scope-resolved-egress directly (lines 468, 503), and
     resources/test carries 47 .cljc *-cljs-test suites including
     resources_classification_cljs_test.cljc, resources_derived_scope_sensitivity_cljs_test.cljc
     and resources_invalid_params_redaction_cljs_test.cljc. The projector is already
     proved on the CLJS lane by its owner; mirroring it into epoch would put the
     assertions on the wrong artefact.

  C. NO EGRESS PATH AT ALL - 5 arms. epoch_redact_fn_test.clj configure-accepts-fn,
     -accepts-nil-to-clear, -rejects-non-fn, -absent-slot-preserves-existing-fn,
     -partial-update-mixed-validity. Registry validation on rf/configure!. A host
     divergence here cannot leak: a rejected or absent :redact-fn means the built-in
     frame/profile projection runs, which IS the fail-closed default. What matters
     off-box is that an installed fn runs at egress and a throwing one falls back closed;
     both mirrored.

  D. ON-BOX LIFECYCLE, NOT EGRESS - 4 arms. wiring-settle-stores-raw-record,
     wiring-replace-app-db-stores-raw-record, wiring-halted-destroy-stores-raw-record,
     restore-replays-raw-value-under-redact-fn. These pin WHICH wiring stored the record
     and that restore replays raw material. Record assembly and restore already have CLJS
     coverage (epoch_cljs_test.cljs sections 1 and 2,
     epoch_committed_at_clock_cljs_test.cljs), and the projection applies at egress
     regardless of the storing wiring.

  E. SAME CODE PATH, DIFFERENT INPUT - the bulk (~55 arms), mirrored representatively
     rather than ported as a table:
       - 5 of 6 rollup-* variants: one true and one strict-false mirrored; the rest vary
         the input to one computation inside build-record.
       - 4 of 5 elides-fx-args-* row shapes (:skipped-on-platform, :no-such-fx,
         :handler-exception, idempotence): one projector, one :args keyspace, four row
         keywords. The default-redacted success row is mirrored.
       - 12 of 13 HTTP-body arms (:accept-failure, 4xx, 5xx, decode-failure, nested
         retry-attempt, on-box-preserved, no-stamp pass-through): one
         omit-off-box-http-bodies projector reading one :rf.http/off-box-body stamp across
         different operation keywords. One representative plus its :include-sensitive?
         lift.
       - 7 of 8 db-pending re-root arms (large-leaf variant, scalar-sentinel input,
         non-t1/t2 scoping, idempotency, three end-to-end live shapes). The central unit
         re-root and its sibling control are mirrored.
       - All 7 G1-G7 changed-sensitive-path COUNTER arms: arithmetic over the raw record,
         not an egress path.
       - 2 of 3 retention-cap-* (keep 0, keep >= depth): same clamp as the mirrored
         window arm.
       - share-redaction-vocabulary, handles-mixed-nil-and-real-records, both
         pure-no-side-effects arms, tool-profile-includes-structural-digest,
         unknown-profile-rejected: subsumed by the bulk-equals-per-record arm, the nil
         arm, the single purity arm, and - for the profile enum -
         core/test/re_frame/projection_cljs_test.cljc, which already proves the closed
         :rf.egress/* enum and its throw on the CLJS lane (33 deftests).

ONE PREMISE REJECTED. epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj's own docstring argues it
belongs on the JVM because "the framework's epoch artefact owns the projection emission
site ... pinning conformance from the artefact side keeps the test on the JVM next to the
contract owner". The premise does not hold: the emission site is tool_pair.cljc - a .cljc.
"Next to the contract owner" and "on the JVM" are independent, which is why a dual-lane
.cljc in the same directory is the right answer rather than a test in an MCP tree.

SPUN OUT: rf2-irwsq (P1, filed with the full mechanism and a repro). Writing the
whole-record "no raw large bytes anywhere" scan on the whole-output :large? SUB shape went
red for real. On main, projected-record elides the structured :sub-runs row but leaves the
:rf.sub/run TRACE TAG carrying the full payload at [:trace-events <i> :tags :rf.sub/value],
with :large? true sitting beside it. The 136 JVM arms cannot see it: the cross-cutting
token-budget scan lives in epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj but its fixture declares
:large as an APP-DB PATH, and the whole-output :large? sub shape is probed only by
projected-record-elides-large-sub-output, which reads the row by hand and never scans the
record. Token-budget axis only, NOT privacy: EP-0025 dropped the whole-output :sensitive?
overload (classification.cljc:147 "silently dropped if present"), so sub-output
sensitivity is path-based and substituted at the EMIT site, already redacted in both
slots. Not fixed here - it is an egress-projector behaviour change wanting its own ruling
on whether the tag should carry the marker or be dropped. The new suite carries a
clearly-labelled CHARACTERISATION assertion pinning today's raw tag with an in-code
instruction to DELETE it when the fix lands; flagged in the PR body in case a reviewer
prefers the assertion dropped instead.
Spine re-run verdict (added after the first report): scripts/test-fast-pr.sh re-run on the same commit exited rc 0, with its CLJS node integration step reporting the identical 'Ran 11411 tests containing 57097 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' The single earlier rc 1 was a shadow-cljs par-compile abort under six-worker contention, confirmed environmental by re-run rather than assumed. PR #6974's body has been updated in place with the full Quality gates table (it had merged carrying the placeholder body).

comments.text: Merged-PR audit of #6974 found a material completeness hole in this exact evidence owner. The PR classifies all 16 resource-trace egress arms as already covered on CLJS by the resources artefact, but the cited dual-lane resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test calls scope-registry/project-scope-resolved-egress directly. Across implementation/resources/test, no CLJS test calls epoch/projected-record, rf/projected-record, or projected-history. Therefore no CLJS row proves the production composition: re-frame.resources must publish :resources/project-scope-resolved-egress and :resources/project-resource-trace-egress, then epoch/tool_pair must discover and invoke them. Both epoch consumers deliberately pass trace events through unchanged when a hook is absent, so a CLJS-only publication/wiring regression would leak resolver values or scoped keys while #6974's 29/110 suite and the resources direct tests remained green. The JVM epoch_egress_resource_trace_test proves the seam only on JVM—the host asymmetry this bead exists to close. Add the smallest dual-lane end-to-end row(s) with re-frame.resources loaded and assert redaction through the public rf/projected-record boundary; do not port all 16 cases. This is distinct from active rf2-irwsq, which owns the large-sub trace-tag token-budget defect. Authored/applied range-diff is exact 4/4; the current focused JVM suite remains green at 29 tests / 110 assertions.

title: Before pushing the v0.0.1.alpha tag, workflow_dispatch expensive-tests.yml on the exact release commit (the release gate is a subset of a surface-gated PR gate)
notes: OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
close_reason:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26): "adopt". ADOPTED AS A STANDING PRE-TAG STEP.

THE PRACTICE: before pushing the v0.0.1.alpha tag, workflow_dispatch expensive-tests.yml ON THE EXACT RELEASE COMMIT — not on main, not on a near-neighbour. It is an operator-run action; no agent can dispatch it.

WHY IT IS ADOPTED RATHER THAN DONE: this is a step in a release that has not happened yet. Keeping it open asserted that work was owed today; it is not. The obligation now rides on the tag itself.

WHERE IT NOW LIVES so it cannot be lost: recorded here, and the alpha-tag cluster carries it — rf2-snjn5 (the 8 "not published yet" install-doc claims that flip the moment the tag lands) and rf2-vxgfnd.99 (EPIC S7, the Helix-removal wave plus the tag). WHOEVER TAKES THE TAG TAKES THIS STEP.

WHY IT MATTERS AND IS NOT CEREMONY: the PR spine deliberately does not run the expensive tier, so a release commit can be green on everything CI gates and still never have had the expensive suite pointed at it. That is the same shape this repo has found five-plus times this week — a gate that never ran over the artefact it is supposed to certify. The exactness is the whole point: a dispatch against main proves something about main, not about the commit that becomes the tag.

The decision dossier ai/decisions/rf2-o0agl.alpha-tag-release-gate.md is removed per the same instruction (local-only tree, untracked, so nothing to commit).

title: spec/Conventions.md + Spec 006: the canonical artefact inventory omits day8/re-frame2-resources and -ssr-ring (says seven per-feature artefacts; nine ship)
notes:
From rf2-ods8n lens A (perf + back-compat audit), 2026-07-25.

spec/Conventions.md §Adapter shipping convention's artefact table carries TWELVE rows
(core, reagent, reagent-slim, uix, schemas, machines, routing, flows, http, ssr, ui,
epoch), and its core row asserts:

  "Seven per-feature surfaces ship as separate artefacts alongside core:
   day8/re-frame2-schemas, -machines, -routing, -flows, -http, -ssr, -epoch.
   The per-feature split set is closed."

day8/re-frame2-resources and day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring are BOTH:

spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §CLJS reference scope repeats the same seven-item list:
"Other per-feature artefacts (schemas, machines, routing, flows, http, ssr, epoch)
stay flat under implementation/<name>/."

docs/release-process.md has the full thirteen right. So the OPERATIONAL doc is correct
and the NORMATIVE spec under-describes the shipped surface by two coordinates — and

other rows, correct "Seven per-feature surfaces" -> "Nine", and correct the Spec 006
flat-artefact list. Recheck the "per-feature split set is closed" claim reads correctly
