title: frame.cljc: literal-path get-in in frame-incarnation-closing? is the framework's largest allocation site (11% of sampled alloc); the file already documents the fix
notes:
From rf2-ods8n lens A (perf + back-compat audit), 2026-07-25. MEASURED.

SITE. implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:972 —
  (let [closing-token (get-in @destroying-frames [id :token])]

MEASUREMENT (from-clean JVM: fresh JVM, warm-up loop, System/gc before the timed
window; Clojure 1.12.0 / Temurin 21.0.10; JFR settings=profile over 400k
dispatch-sync calls on the published core via the plain-atom adapter).

  - jdk.ObjectAllocationSample attributes 2.784 GB of 24.63 GB sampled weight
    (11.3%) to frame-incarnation-closing? alone — 3x the next re-frame site and the
    largest single allocation source in the framework.
  - Top two allocated classes overall are PersistentVector$ChunkedSeq (2.759 GB) and
    ArrayChunk (1.898 GB) — 19% of ALL allocation combined. Both are the seq `get-in`
    builds over its literal path vector on every call.
  - Direct micro-timing, identical semantics:
        (get-in m [k :token])   35.2 ns/call
        (:token (get m k))      11.1 ns/call     -> 3.2x
  - frame-incarnation-closing? is called 105 times per SINGLE dispatch of a one-line
    :db-write handler (82 with -Dre-frame.debug=false), so ~105 x 24 ns ~= 2.5 us of
    the measured 66 us per-event total (~5%), plus the allocation/GC relief.

THE FILE ALREADY PRESCRIBES THE FIX. frame.cljc's own `frame` docstring (~lines
833-838) says: "2-level lookup written as keyword-invoke (`(-> f :lifecycle
:destroyed?)`) rather than `(get-in f [:lifecycle :destroyed?])` — `get-in` allocates
a path vector per call, and `frame` runs on every dispatch / subscribe through
`current-frame` resolution." The optimisation was applied to `frame` and not to its
siblings sixty lines away.

HOT-PATH SITES CARRYING THE SAME PATTERN:
  frame.cljc:907, :972, :2787, :3484   (get-in @destroying-frames [id :token])
  frame.cljc:820                        inside frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?,
                                        therefore 124x per dispatch
  router.cljc:3547, :3595, :3642, :4314 [:config :drain-depth], once per drain pass
  router.cljc:1703, :1713               [:coeffects :db] / [:coeffects :rf.db/runtime]
  subs.cljc:1319, :1345, :1348, :1657, :1660, :2305, :2308   [k :reaction] in the
                                        cache-swap retry loops

CLARITY VERDICT: strictly clarity-POSITIVE. `(:token (@destroying-frames id))` is
shorter, reads better, and makes the file self-consistent with the rule it already
documents. This is the one perf finding I would act on unconditionally.

Not alpha-blocking. Isolated surfaces (core/src, router/subs) — but frame.cljc +
router.cljc + subs.cljc together are a wide diff; consider one focused PR.
close_reason:
PR #6986 merged (merge commit facb868db3). Applied frame.cljc's own documented no-literal-path-get-in rule to all 20 sites the bead named across frame.cljc / router.cljc / subs.cljc, plus 5 same-shape siblings found by sweeping those three files (frame.cljc 2888/2891/3410/3542, router.cljc 2688). Those three files now have zero get-in in code; the only remaining hits are the frame docstring stating the rule and the reg-sub docstring example, both deliberate. 25 insertions / 25 deletions, no behaviour change.

MEASURED (JVM / plain-atom, NOT browser; Temurin 21.0.10+7, Clojure 1.12.0; fresh JVM per arm, interleaved before/after, warm-up + System/gc before each timed window, 3 timed reps per JVM best-of, 3 JVM pairs):
  - Primitive, deterministic and identical in all six JVMs: (get-in m [k :token]) allocates 128.0 bytes/call, (:token (get m k)) allocates 0.0. Timing ratio 1.79-2.92x (bead said 3.2x; the gap and the wide ns spread are concurrent-worker load on this box).
  - End-to-end dispatch-sync, 200k events: 78,569 -> 61,193 bytes/event median, -22.1%. Within-configuration spread 0.35% / 1.8%, so the gap is orders outside the noise band. This is the trustworthy figure and it is the bead's actual claim.
  - Wall-clock 45.81 -> 39.03 us/event median (-14.8%); after band 36.5-44.7 and before band 45.5-48.0 do not overlap across three pairs, so the direction is real, but n=3 under concurrent shadow-cljs/Chromium load is not a basis for quoting a precise percentage.

GATES: implementation/core clojure -M:test 2115 tests / 10456 assertions, 0 failures (matches baseline EXACTLY, rc=0). npm run test:cljs 11438 / 57234, 0 failures, rc=0 — and re-derived on pre-patch sources in the same worktree: 11438 / 57234, byte-identical (the brief's ~11423/57166 was stale, main moved). scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: log reads PASS fast PR spine, rc=0. Substitution-equivalence probe: 61 cases across all five shapes agree on value AND identity (java.util.Map, defrecord, non-associative inner values, false/nil leaves, sorted-map, non-keyword keys, and every branch of the 3-arity default). CI on the PR: 60 pass, 13 surface-gated skips, 0 failures, including both :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false prod-elision lanes.

Out of scope and untouched as instructed: rf2-l260n (record-only call-count hot spot), rf2-8o66x (no perf gate added).

title: SSR API reference documents two subscriptions that do not exist and a handler-defaults key the implementation deliberately omits
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). Two independent false-surface claims in the published SSR API reference.

A. TWO SUBSCRIPTIONS THAT DO NOT EXIST -- and the page contradicts itself three lines later.
docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:667-669, under `### Subscriptions`:
    | `:rf/head`         | The head model for the active route (resolved via `active-head` against the subscribed frame) |
    | `:rf/public-error` | The sanitised public-error projection when an error page is being rendered; `nil` otherwise |
And :264 in prose -- "The [`:rf/head`](#subscriptions) subscription returns the active route''s head-model."

VERIFIED: `grep -rn "reg-sub\|reg-runtime-sub" implementation/ssr/src implementation/ssr-ring/src` returns ZERO hits. re-frame.ssr and re-frame.ssr.ring register no subscriptions at all -- the only registrations are `reg-event :rf/hydrate` plus the nine reg-fx (`:rf.server/*`, `:rf.ssr/check-*`). `@(rf/subscribe [:rf/head])` cannot resolve.

The page''s own notes at :671-673 already say it: "no `reg-sub :rf/head`" / "no `reg-sub :rf/public-error`". But they frame it as **NOT USED** ("is never subscribed"), which reads as "exists but unused" -- when the truth is "does not exist". The table above them presents both as shipped surface, and the :264 prose presents `:rf/head` as the way to read the head model. The actual accessors are the re-frame.core facade fns the same page names at :263 (`render-head` / `active-head` / `head-model->html` / `head-snapshot`), all of which are real manifest rows.

B. handler-defaults DOCUMENTED WITH A KEY THE IMPLEMENTATION EXPLICITLY REFUSES TO DEFAULT.
docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md:164-167 and the example at :174 both show:
    handler-defaults
    ;; => {:emit-hash?   true
    ;;     :html-shell   default-html-shell
    ;;     :content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8"}
And :51 repeats it: "`:content-type` -- default `\"text/html; charset=utf-8\"`."

ACTUAL, implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:97-98: `{:emit-hash? true :html-shell shell/default-html-shell}`. Its docstring at :88-95 spells out WHY, and the doc states exactly what that docstring forbids: "`:content-type` carries no default: the opt is a genuine override that force-replaces the response Content-Type when supplied. A default of `text/html; charset=utf-8` here would force-replace an app''s own `:rf.server/set-header \"content-type\"` on every request; an absent (nil) opt instead leaves the runtime''s default-seeded `text/html; charset=utf-8` (Spec 011 §Status defaults) -- or the app''s explicit Content-Type -- in control."

So a reader who trusts the doc believes their `:rf.server/set-header "content-type"` will be force-replaced on every request, and may write a workaround for a behaviour that does not exist. The on-the-wire default really is text/html; charset=utf-8 -- the doc''s error is attributing it to handler-defaults.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The `### Subscriptions` table in docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md either goes away or says plainly that re-frame.ssr registers no subscriptions, pointing readers at the render-head / active-head / head-model->html / head-snapshot facade fns instead. :264 stops calling `:rf/head` a subscription.
2. docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md:164-167, :174 and :51 match ring.clj:97-98, and explain the deliberate no-default the way ring.clj''s docstring does.
3. mkdocs build --strict green.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6966. Acceptance 1: the '### Subscriptions' section is now 'Subscriptions — there are none', stating plainly that neither re-frame.ssr nor re-frame.ssr.ring registers any subscription (verified: zero reg-sub/reg-runtime-sub in either src tree; :rf/head appears nowhere as a registry id, only :rf/head-model / :rf/head-hash) and that both keywords name Spec-Schemas data shapes. A table routes readers to render-head / active-head / head-model->html / head-snapshot and to project-error / apply-error-projection!. §The head model no longer calls :rf/head a subscription. Acceptance 2: handler-defaults' signature, example and the :content-type opt bullet match ring.clj:97-98, and the Description explains the deliberate no-default the way ring.clj:88-95 does. Acceptance 3: mkdocs build --strict rc=0.

title: docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's reg-error-projector example is non-conformant: a reader who pastes it silently gets the locked generic-500 instead of their projector
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). The most consequential prose-vs-code defect that lens found: the documented example does the OPPOSITE of what the page says it does, silently, with no error the reader will notice.

THE EXAMPLE. docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:369-373:
    (rf/reg-error-projector :app/public-error
      (fn [trace-event]
        {:status  500
         :message "Something went wrong."}))

THE CONTRACT. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:73-77 -- `public-error-keys` is #{:status :code :message :retryable?}, "The four locked keys". And :98-105 -- `public-error-shape?` was TIGHTENED (rf2-oytx7j) to a CLOSED shape: `(= public-error-keys (set (keys x)))`. EXACTLY the four keys, no extra and none missing.

CONSEQUENCE. The two-key return is non-conformant, so `project-error` emits `:rf.error/sanitised-on-projection` and returns `fallback-public-error` -- the locked generic 500. The projector the reader just registered is discarded on EVERY error, forever, and the page''s own :391 text convicts the example: "If the projector throws or returns a non-conforming shape, this emits `:rf.error/sanitised-on-projection` and returns the locked generic-500 fallback." So the page states the rule 22 lines below the example that breaks it. :441 states it a third time ("Conformant projector output carries exactly these").

TWO MORE SITES WITH THE SAME 3-OR-FEWER-KEY SHAPE
  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:393 -- the `project-error` example return is commented `;; => {:status 404 :code :not-found :message "Page not found"}`. Actual (error_projector.cljc:166-169) includes `:retryable? false`; `:retryable?` is one of the four locked keys and is ALWAYS present.
  - docs/ssr/glossary.md:43 -- "maps a rich internal trace to a sanitized, client-safe `:rf/public-error` shape (`:status`, `:code`, `:message`)". Three keys. A reader writing that shape from the glossary hits the same silent fallback.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The reg-error-projector example returns all four locked keys, and is a shape that actually passes public-error-shape? (400..599 status, keyword :code, string :message, boolean :retryable?).
2. The project-error example return comment includes :retryable?.
3. docs/ssr/glossary.md:43 names all four keys.
4. Ideally: consider whether the api-manifest/doc gates can pin a public-error example against public-error-shape? so this class cannot recur -- the current gates check var EXISTENCE, not example conformance, and would not have caught this.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7168 (2026-07-28). PR #7168 correctly made the built-in projector fail safe: only :rf.error/no-such-handler with [:tags :kind] = :route is a 404; :event, :frame, and kind-less misses are server defects and stay 500. The public reg-error-projector example on this same surface was left behind. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc (and its docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md presentation) still cases only on :operation and maps every :rf.error/no-such-handler to 404. A programmer copying the canonical example therefore reintroduces exactly the misclassification the PR fixed. The API summary also states the mapping without the discriminator. Bounded repair: make both public examples/summaries name and test :kind :route, with all other no-such-handler shapes taking the generic 500; update generated API prose if applicable. No new mechanism or generalized doc gate.
close_reason: PR #7231. The reg-error-projector example branched on :rf.error/no-such-route -- the category docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md itself says a release build never reaches (caller misuse of route-url, dev-gated trace stream). Its only 404 arm was dead under production hardening, while :rf.error/no-such-handler + [:tags :kind] :route (the arm rf2-ov56u promoted onto the always-on axis, and the one PR #7168 gated) fell through to the example's generic 500 -- a real 404 answered 500. Example now branches on no-such-handler and gates on :kind :route. The default-error-projector-fn summary, which stated the mapping with no discriminator while its own next bullet spelled out the sibling :where :event gate, now names the gate and the three :kind misses. reg-error-projector's docstring in error_projector.cljc carried the same pre-#7168 ungated shape for BOTH gated categories (docstring only, no behaviour change) -- corrected per the bead's audit note, which names that file. Acceptance 4: new re-frame.ssr-doc-example-projector-test READS both examples out of the markdown fence at run time and executes them, so it cannot drift from the page; mutation-proved (reverting the 404 arm reds 4 of 13). No gate had caught this because doc-api-check verifies var EXISTENCE, not example conformance, and the runtime suites pin the BUILT-IN projector, never the documented one. Gates: mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs 0, ssr dev suite 0 (592/2892), test-ssr-prod-gate.sh 0 (594/2722). Swept the page's other examples -- every ';; =>' result claim matches source; nothing to file.

title: Published ssr/hydrate! docstring names ui/hydrate-root as 'the canonical' boot, and two shipped runtime error strings name day8/re-frame2-ui
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). Same failure mode as the (v/html ...) and v/raw diagnostics fixed on 2026-07-25: a shipped diagnostic or public docstring pointing at a form the reader cannot obtain.

A. PUBLIC DOCSTRING of `hydrate!` (defn at implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:147) -- a consumer of the published day8/re-frame2-ssr reading its hydration entry point:
  - :195 -- "**The canonical compiled-ui boot is `ssr/hydrate!` WITHOUT `:render-tree-fn`, then `ui/hydrate-root`**"
  - :192 -- "The COMPILED-UI substrate (`re-frame.ui`) has NO hashable client render-tree -- its views compile to React elements, not the structural tree the server hashes -- so it does NOT pass `:render-tree-fn`."
  - :201 -- "surfaced as `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` -- see `re-frame.ui.runtime/emit-hydration-mismatch!`"
The reader is told the canonical path runs through ui/hydrate-root, which is not obtainable (implementation/ui/deps.edn:19 NOT PUBLISHED; absent from release.yml deploy-leaf). The path they CAN use -- v/hydrate-root on Freehand, or a wrapper adapter -- is not the one named canonical.

B. TWO USER-VISIBLE RUNTIME STRINGS in published core that name the nonexistent artefact:
  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc:556-558 -- "re-frame2-ui was compiled against observation-port ABI ... ; core and re-frame2-ui release on a ..."
  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc:1360 -- "re-frame.ui defect to fix."
A consumer who trips either gets a diagnostic naming an artefact that does not exist on Clojars.

DELIBERATELY SCOPED SMALL. The same sweep found ~108 re-frame.ui references across 20 files in the thirteen published trees. Everything not listed above is legitimate provenance for copied version-pinned tables (ssr/ui_tree.cljc''s 13 public-def docstrings citing re-frame.ui.rules / re-frame.ui.semantic, ssr/manifest.cljc:95-97 and :239-241, ssr/install.cljc:59-60, core/frame.cljc, core/late_bind/directory.cljc:1144-1148, core/subs/override_schema.cljc, routing/link.cljc:62-63) and was NOT filed. Only the two categories above mislead a consumer about a path or an artefact.

PROCESS NOTE FOR rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e), recorded here so it is not lost: that deletion will orphan every one of those ~108 cross-references inside the PUBLISHED artefacts. Its acceptance criteria cover implementation/ui/ and full CI green but say nothing about the residual references left behind in core / ssr / routing docstrings and comments. Worth adding to F6e''s brief when it dispatches.

title: docs/core/freehand/ssr.md tells the reader the hydration verb has not landed; v/hydrate-root shipped and the page never names it
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). The one page that teaches Freehand SSR is the one page that will not tell the reader the verb.

docs/core/freehand/ssr.md:113-116 says:
    "Exact public helper names land with Spec 004C; do not treat a guessed
     `v/hydrate` arity as frozen API."

And the paragraph above (:106-112) routes the reader AROUND the name it believes is missing: "install the Freehand adapter, ensure the request/client frame is live (preflight / seed as appropriate), then run the product''s **hydrate** operation over the server markup."

v/hydrate-root IS PUBLISHED. Evidence:

title: v/custom-element accepts :properties #{:class :style} and silently omits them from markup
description:
Found by the rf2-sv2oq slice (PR #6955) and deliberately not closed there, because extending the v1 refusal roster is a ruling rather than a fix.

VERIFIED BEHAVIOUR: (v/custom-element :x {:properties #{:class :style}}) is ACCEPTED, and the serialiser then omits class and style from markup — observed output <ce-edge ok="a"> with both dropped. The structural fold is unaffected, so this is a serialisation-only divergence: the same declaration renders differently through the markup path than through the fold.

WHY IT IS WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY ODD: class and style are attributes, not JS properties. Declaring them as :properties is a category error, and the substrate's response is to silently produce markup missing them — wrong output with no diagnostic. Under the project's own posture that is the bad kind of quiet: trust-the-programmer means an ergonomic API with loud failures, not one that accepts a nonsensical declaration and degrades the render.

MAYOR RULING (delegated authority, 2026-07-25): REFUSE the declaration. Add :class and :style to the v1 refusal roster so the compiler rejects them at declaration time with a diagnostic naming the attribute/property distinction. The fix is a few lines in the validator, as the finding worker noted.

Rationale for ruling rather than deferring: rf2-5gliq ruled the v1 refusal roster, so extending it is formally a ruling — but the content of this extension is not a taste question. A silent wrong-markup path is a correctness defect, and refusing two well-known attribute names is the smallest possible remedy. It adds no framework, no general attribute/property classifier, and no new diagnostic machinery.

NON-GOALS (fence): do not build a general attribute-versus-property taxonomy; do not attempt to auto-coerce class/style into attributes; do not widen the refusal roster beyond what is demonstrably a category error. If other names turn out to belong, file them separately with evidence.

Sequence: the v/custom-element door is now free (PR #6955 merged), so this is dispatchable immediately.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6964 (2026-07-25). Reopened this exact owner for a bounded SPEC-COMPLETENESS residual. The implementation, public macro docstring, and docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md now refuse :class/:style correctly, but the two canonical contracts still describe the pre-refusal grammar. spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md §Template grammar says ':properties is the entire v1 grammar', then unconditionally 'Declared names -> JS properties', and its rejection list never names these two. spec/API.md's v/custom-element row repeats that :properties is the whole grammar and says only an unknown option key/namespaced tag/runtime map produces :rf.ui.compile/bad-custom-element. A programmer following either normative surface can still author the exact form the compiler now rejects. The sentence that :class/:style 'follow DOM rules' does not specify declaration-time refusal or its diagnostic.

Bounded repair: state the exact #{:class :style} refusal and existing diagnostic in 004D and the API roster row; do not grow a taxonomy or new machinery. Coordinate the two tiny spec edits with open rf2-sv2oq, whose remaining custom-element spec respell touches the same files, rather than creating a duplicate owner.
close_reason: PR #7019 (spec-completeness residual of the #6964 audit reopen). spec/004D §Template grammar now states the #{:class :style} refusal, its existing :rf.ui.compile/bad-custom-element id, the reason (a property-classified name is omitted from markup, so the declaration rendered the element with those values dropped from the HTML while the structural fold still carried them), the two REFUSED alternatives (coercion; a general attribute-versus-property taxonomy) and that the roster is exactly two names extended only by ruling; the unconditional clause now reads 'Declared names -> JS properties (bar the two refused below)'. spec/API.md's v/custom-element row gains the same fact in the sentence that already enumerates the diagnostic's causes. No taxonomy, no machinery, no new id, no restructured section. FOUND-NOT-CHANGED, both verified: (1) spec/API.md:311, the DONOR ui/custom-element roster row, still describes :properties as the entire v1 grammar with no refusal — implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler.cljc:497-527 confirms the donor validator does NOT carry refused-property-names, so the row is accurate for the donor and making it track the refusal would be a code change; (2) spec/004B §Custom elements restates the grammar as an explicit consumer deferring ownership to 004D and says only what a declared name lowers to, never which names may be declared, so the refusal does not falsify it. Also noted: 004D's 'Rejected:' list in that paragraph is rejected DESIGN ALTERNATIVES, not a roster of refused declarations, so there was no list to extend. Gates: mkdocs --strict rc=0, api-md-check rc=0 (253 var-rows), doc-api-check rc=0, implementation/freehand clojure -M:test rc=0 (1102 tests, 0 failures).

title: Freehand test renames vs the census lane derivation: fence implementation/freehand/test out of the rf2-lgozq sweep, or move the :node-test-freehand ns-regexp with it
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-07-25: the hazard as I relayed it was BACKWARDS, and the rf2-lgozq worker verified rather than obeying. Recording so nobody acts on my version.

WHAT I SAID: the rf2-lgozq sweep 'drops _cljs' from .cljc test filenames, so 64 of the 94 census rows would leave the node lane and red the unfiltered required check. I fenced implementation/freehand/test/** out of the sweep on that basis.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: the sweep ADDS a lane suffix — _test.cljc becomes _cljs_test.cljc or _jvm_test.cljc — so it moves suites INTO the node lane. Suites leaving the lane is the inverse of what it does. Even the one apparent exception, region_order_cljc_test -> region_order_cljs_test, converts _cljc_ to _cljs_ and thereby ADDS the suffix the node ns-regexp matches. Verified on the merged diff: zero freehand paths touched, zero shadow-cljs.edn touched, 'Freehand conformance index' PASSED, and all 76 implementation/freehand/test/*_cljs_test.cljc files intact. Freehand could never have been in the roster in the first place — every freehand .cljc suite already ends _cljs_test.cljc, and the 50 freehand entries in the raw census are view-fixture/support namespaces whose ns does not end in -test, so neither lane ever selected them as suites. My fence was therefore unnecessary; it cost nothing because no file needed skipping, and rf2-lgozq completed rather than partially.

THE REAL RESIDUAL, which stands on its own merits and is what this bead should close on: _lanes_for RESTATES the :node-test-freehand ns-regexp rather than DERIVING from it, so nothing mechanically keeps the two in step. A future edit to either can silently desynchronise the census's lane model from the build's actual selection. That is a genuine single-source-of-truth defect and is independent of any rename sweep — do not close this bead by observing that the sweep was harmless.

PROCESS NOTE FOR ME: I raised this as URGENT from a second-hand reading of another worker's bead note without checking the sweep's actual rename direction against its merged diff. The worker was right to verify the premise and say so. An urgent fence built on an unverified premise costs worker attention and can suppress correct work; check the direction of a transformation before fencing against it.
WORKER (PR #7010, merged as f40681892c — blob verified identical on origin/main). Closed on the REAL residual, as the MAYOR CORRECTION directed. Confirmed the correction first: all 66 .cljc freehand suites on main already end _cljs_test.cljc, so the rf2-lgozq sweep could never have moved one out of the node lane.

CHANGED: both CLJS lane selectors are now READ from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (:node-test-freehand and :browser-test), applying shadow-cljs's re-find semantics to the namespace munged from the path. Only WHICH BUILD owns which lane is written down. :browser-test carried the identical restatement plus a .cljs-only clause absent from the config, so it is derived by the same one helper. The JVM lane stays a stated rule — its discovery lives in the artefact's deps.edn :test alias, not in any file the census reads — and the comment now says so instead of implying all three are mirrored. EDN reader reused from check_test_lane_bijection.py (the gate whose thesis is that a lane roster is read and never listed) rather than written a second time; from check_doc_slugs import was the existing sibling-import precedent in this file.

VACUITY FLOOR — YES, and two-sided. Each derived selector must PARTITION the Freehand test tree: select at least one namespace AND reject at least one. Both failure directions are silent otherwise — a pattern matching nothing quietly empties a lane, one matching everything quietly serves every cell of every row, and both look exactly like a green census. A missing :builds map or a renamed build is a hard error naming the lane it orphaned.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all on implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, all reverted (file restored and confirmed identical to HEAD by blob hash; absent from the diff): (1) :node-test-freehand ns-regexp -> '-jvm-test$' reds the census with 68 UNEXECUTED CELL defects, rc=1; (2) the SAME mutation against the pre-fix script (git show HEAD:scripts/...) exits 0 with 'census OK: 97 APPLICABLE row(s)' — that is this bead's defect reproduced, the census blind to a build whose node lane runs nothing; (3) ns-regexp -> '-nope-nothing-matches$' trips the floor, 'selects none of the 235 namespace(s)'; (4) ns-regexp -> '.' trips it the other way, 'selects every one of the 235'; (5) build key renamed -> 'declares no :node-test-freehand build'.

CENSUS ROW COUNT: 98 rows in the index (97 active, 1 retired), 97 applicable — BEFORE and AFTER. --report is BYTE-IDENTICAL (103 lines) to the origin/main baseline. No row moves and none should: the derivation reproduces the previous restatement exactly on today's tree, which is the point — same answer, from an authority that cannot go stale. Re-derived rather than trusted from the brief's '~98'.

title: Four guide pages still teach the pre-EP-0037 route-auth and loader model
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10) while spot-auditing the pages the EP-0037 waves rewrote against the shipped surface. Filed rather than patched, per R6's process rule.

The routing guide tree itself is coherent — `docs/routing/concepts.md`, `glossary.md`, the two how-tos, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md`, the skill's routing reference and `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/` all verified correct end to end, and the retirement roster (`:query-retain`, `:rf.route/entry-blocked`, `:bypass-guards?`, route `:on-error`, `:enter-attempts`, `:rf.error/route-guard-loop`, `:inherit-resources?`) has ZERO residue in tracked docs/skills/examples.

But four pages the waves did not reach still teach the pre-EP-0037 model, and a reader who lands on one of them gets the retired mechanism as the primary recipe.

1. `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md:212` — "Route-level auth is an ordinary interceptor over the navigation events — **not a special routing mechanism**". Section 4 (lines 210-317) then builds a hand-rolled `:app/auth-guard` interceptor with `:rf/skip-handler?` over `:tags #{:requires-auth}`. `:can-enter` and `:rf.route/entry-denied` appear nowhere on the page. Shipped: `:can-enter` is first-class route metadata evaluated in the one planning pipeline for every door, and `spec/012-Routing.md` says in as many words that an interceptor attached only to `:rf.route/navigate` fails OPEN. The EP's Guide-impact roster ("the auth and unsaved-change how-tos split the fresh-entry and resumable-leave recipes") was executed for the leave half (`docs/routing/how-to/guard-unsaved-changes.md` is correct) and never for the entry half.

   Compounding: line 230 attributes the recipe to `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs`, which now contains no interceptor at all (`git grep -E "auth-guard|reg-interceptor"` over that dir returns nothing) — it is `:can-enter` + a public `rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied`. The attribution points at code that no longer exists.

title: O-8 sends popstate and SSR through the forward-only route event
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6935 under completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses.

PR #6935 accurately fixes O-8's retired `:on-match`-as-loader role, but the same edited migration recipe still sends two URL-driven doors through the wrong event and never tells the adopting app to declare a URL owner:

  step 5: replace popstate listener bodies with
          `(rf/dispatch [:rf.route/transitioned url])`
  step 6: dispatch `:rf.route/transitioned` for the SSR request URL

The canonical contract is explicit and consistent elsewhere:

- `:rf.route/transitioned` is the FORWARD door for route-link/programmatic pushes, with default scroll `:top`.
- `:rf.route/handle-url-change` owns popstate, initial page load, and SSR request URLs, with default scroll `:restore` and the SSR attribution path.
- Browser URL ownership is positive bootstrap policy: a frame must carry `:url-bound? true`; there is no default-frame floor. That frame lifecycle installs/removes the strategy-aware popstate/hashchange listener and performs initial URL sync automatically. With no URL owner, outbound history fxs no-op and inbound changes are skipped.

So O-8 step 5 is self-contradictory (keep a listener body, then remove the bespoke listener) and operationally incomplete: following the six steps without `:url-bound? true` yields a router whose slice can move while the address bar does not. Sending Back/Forward through `:rf.route/transitioned` also selects forward-navigation scroll semantics. Step 6 names the sibling event instead of the SSR door even though its new prose correctly links the SSR contract.

Evidence: spec/012-Routing.md public-surface rows 37-38, URL-changes section 517-522, SSR flow 1802, and URL ownership/lifecycle 1851-1869; docs/api/re-frame.routing.md rows 435-440 and 501-502. No exact Bead owns this door/ownership defect. rf2-3uiy8 was exact for the separate `:on-match` loader drift and was correctly closed by #6935.

Keep the repair documentary and small. Correct O-8's two door instructions and add the missing positive URL-owner bootstrap; do not change routing runtime or build a new checker for two stale sentences.
acceptance_criteria:
1. O-8 tells an adopting browser app to declare one URL-owning frame with `:url-bound? true` and to remove its bespoke popstate/hashchange listener because the frame lifecycle owns install, initial sync, and teardown.
2. Any URL-change event named for Back/Forward or initial browser load is `:rf.route/handle-url-change`; `:rf.route/transitioned` remains described only as the forward link/push door.
3. O-8's SSR step feeds the request URL through `:rf.route/handle-url-change`, matching Spec 012's canonical initial-event flow.
4. Step numbering and existing migration citations remain stable; prose/link gates pass. No runtime or checker machinery is added.
close_reason: Delivered on PR #6960. O-8 step 5 now opens with the positive URL-owner bootstrap (declare one frame with :url-bound? true) and instructs the app to DELETE its bespoke popstate/hashchange listener rather than rewrite its body, because the URL-owning frame's lifecycle installs the strategy-aware listener, performs the initial URL->slice sync, and removes it on destroy. Both doors are named by who fires them: :rf.route/handle-url-change for Back/Forward + initial load + SSR (:restore), :rf.route/transitioned for the forward link/push door only (:top). Step 6 feeds the SSR request URL through [:rf.route/handle-url-change (:uri request)] per Spec 012 SSR step 2. Step numbering and existing citations unchanged; no runtime or checker machinery added (AC 4). Gates: check_readme_links 0, check_doc_slugs 0, mkdocs --strict 0.

title: Replaceable route-default overrides drop URL-carrier sensitivity
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6932 under completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses.

PR #6932 correctly makes `:rf.route/entry-denied` and `:rf.route/navigation-blocked` replaceable framework defaults. But replacing either handler replaces the whole registration metadata map, including the framework's carrier classification:

  framework handler-meta => {:sensitive [[:requested-url] [:destination] [:target]],
                             :rf/framework-default? true}
  after ordinary `(rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied (fn [_ _] {}))`
                         => {}

That is the public spelling all canonical auth guidance teaches. The PR documents the loss at spec/012-Routing.md §Replaceable framework defaults and shows a safe redeclaration, but the fresh-return recipe immediately below (lines 1658 and 1722) still omits it. The same omission exists in docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md, docs/routing/concepts.md, docs/routing/testing.md, examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs, and the routing skill's auth guidance.

IMPACT. `:requested-url`, `:destination`, and `:target` can embed query values and path params. The routing facade already classifies those framework-constructed carriers as sensitive so dispatched-event/trace egress redacts them. Following the canonical application recipe silently drops that protection, so an otherwise ordinary auth redirect can expose the full destination to trace or off-box observation.

DESIGN POSTURE. Keep this small and ergonomic. The programmer is replacing behaviour, not redefining the framework-created denial payload. Prefer retaining the framework-owned carrier classification across a replaceable-default behaviour override, with app metadata still additive where appropriate. Do not introduce a general metadata-merging framework. If the whole-registration ruling is deliberately retained instead, every canonical spec/doc/example/skill recipe must include the metadata and a drift gate must make future unsafe omissions difficult.

PROOF. Authored and applied aggregate patches have identical stable patch id fe2554e1086e91e724573496007960107485365e; diff-check is clean. Core image-default tests pass 20/56, focused routing entry-denied + can-leave tests pass 41/139, and the full routing suite passes 482/2512. Those gates prove behaviour replacement but do not assert effective carrier classification after replacement.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A public application override of each replaceable routing default retains effective sensitivity for `[:requested-url]`, `[:destination]`, and `[:target]` without requiring hidden boilerplate in the ordinary recipe.
2. A test drives the actual public registration path and proves an emitted denial/block payload is redacted at the relevant trace/off-box projection; handler invocation and two-app collision semantics remain unchanged.
3. Canonical spec, guide, example, and skill guidance agrees with the shipped behaviour; no adjacent recipe demonstrates an unsafe omission.
4. The repair stays scoped to replaceable framework defaults/carrier classification—no general-purpose metadata inheritance machinery.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6949 (2026-07-25T06:57:09Z; merge f494ce528374863f0e767ac3dc19c872cf21bd36) — REOPENED this exact owner; no duplicate Bead created.

COMPLETENESS: The PR proves the ordinary default-first override, additive declaration, and hot-reload re-registration paths, but not the inverse namespace-load order. A public app `rf/reg-event` may run before `re-frame.routing` seeds its replaceable defaults. In that order `retain-framework-default-classification` sees no framework source-store descriptor, so the app descriptor is stored without the framework carriers; the later framework registration does not reconcile it.

CORRECTNESS: Fresh-process reproduction on current main (the PR's nine files have no later touch): register `:rf.route/entry-denied` first with `{:sensitive [[:guard]]}`, then require `re-frame.routing`, then make a frame. Process metadata is only the framework paths `[[:requested-url] [:destination] [:target]]`; frame-targeted handler metadata is only the app path `[[:guard]]`. The trace chokepoint therefore projects `{:requested-url "URLSECRET" :guard "GUARDSECRET"}` to `{:requested-url :rf/redacted :guard "GUARDSECRET"}`. The promised union is order-dependent and the app-authored classification leaks at egress in this legal load order, even though the app handler itself remains the frame's winner.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: The narrow registration-time retention seam is otherwise focused and adds no hot-path work. Its blind spot follows directly from timing: it can only enrich an override when the default already exists. Repair at this same bounded default/source-store seam so either registration order converges on one effective classification; add one inverse-order public-path test asserting app behaviour, frame-targeted metadata, and trace projection. Do not introduce general metadata inheritance or a new precedence mechanism.

GitHub: 63 pass / 10 intentional skip / 0 fail, no PR comments. The finding is outside those default-first tests and reproduces independently.

With the call present it is green.

REPAIR. Both halves of the seam now sit at the same bounded default/source-store boundary and share ONE union rule (image-assembly/union-carrier-classification, private). retain-framework-default-classification is unchanged and keeps the app-arrives-second path; the new reconcile-framework-default-classification! runs on the same register-event! path and unions the framework default's carrier keys into every application descriptor ALREADY recorded for that [kind id], writing each back through source-store/record-descriptor! Plus a host-symmetric unit case in image_assembly_default_cljs_test.cljc pinning the store-level reconcile, its idempotence, that the marker does not ride, and that the framework's own copy is left alone.

DOCS. AC3 needs no new ceremony. spec/012 §Replaceable framework defaults, docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md and the routing skill all state the retention FLATLY with no order caveat — which is now unconditionally true, so #6949's deletion of the :sensitive re-declaration ceremony STANDS and nothing comes back. One sentence added to spec/012 making order-independence explicit.

NOT DONE / for the auditor to weigh: the PROCESS resolver-map slot still differs by order — in the inverse order the framework's own registration is the last writer, so a bare (non-frame-scoped) rf/handler-meta reports the framework carriers without the app's [:guard]. That is last-write-wins, the same asymmetry rf2-0r6q4's supersession filter already confines to image assembly, and the framework carriers ARE present there, so no carrier leaks at that surface. Reconciling it would mean unioning app metadata into the framework's own descriptor, which reads as the precedence/inheritance machinery AC4 forbids. MERGED-PR AUDIT #6958 (merged 2026-07-25T08:18:54Z; merge 22f419be9d014316a587204cdafda829da298ad1; head 6b69ff0a9a2df508fbf2452300d21872e2950624).

title: RULED (route b): vendor day8/de-dupe into mcp-base; ship story-mcp + mcp-base publish path
description:
rf2-4u3t1 ruled that BOTH `tools/story-mcp` and `tools/machines-viz` get a release path.
The machines-viz half shipped (new `.github/workflows/release-machines-viz.yml` on a
`machines-viz-v*` glob, plus the `:main` fix its `:clein/build` map needed). The story-mcp
half CANNOT be delivered inside that bead's fence, for three reasons found by actually
running clein rather than reading deps.edn. All three verified locally at main bb86e780a2.

## Blocker 1 — `day8/de-dupe` is not on Clojars, and clein cannot express a git coord in a pom

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` declares `day8/de-dupe {:git/url … :git/tag "v0.3.0" :git/sha …}`
as a main-`:deps` RUNTIME dependency (the wire-boundary structural dedup, applied before the
wire-cap check). `clojure -M:clein pom` in `tools/story-mcp` reports:

    Skipping coordinate: {:git/url https://github.com/day8/de-dupe.git, :git/tag v0.3.0, …}

and the generated pom carries exactly two dependencies — `org.clojure/clojure` and
`cheshire/cheshire`. This is the same silent-skip behaviour `clein pom` has for `:local/root`
(rf2-do3m2 / #6340), which the `:local/root → :mvn/version` rewrite exists to repair. There
is no equivalent repair for a git coordinate: a Clojars search for `de-dupe` returns no
results, so there is no `:mvn/version` to rewrite it to.

Consequence: publishing `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp` today would ship a jar whose pom omits a
runtime dependency, and a consumer would fail to resolve `de-dupe.*`. That is precisely the
failure class `preflight-story-package.sh` was written to prevent, and Clojars has no yank.
`tools/mcp-base` carries the same coord and the same problem.

Resolving this is a product decision, not a mechanical fix: publish `day8/de-dupe` to
Clojars, vendor it, or accept that these two artefacts are not Clojars-publishable.

## Blocker 2 — `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base` has no release path either, and is un-BUILDABLE

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` depends on `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base {:local/root "../mcp-base"}`.
`tools/mcp-base/deps.edn` declares its own publishable `:clein/build {:lib
day8/re-frame2-mcp-base …}` — so story-mcp cannot publish until mcp-base does. mcp-base is
NOT in `verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s four-entry `TOOLS` array, so it is a fifth publishable
tool jar the lockstep gate does not guard. rf2-4u3t1's fence explicitly barred changing that
array, which is why the story-mcp half stopped there rather than quietly publishing an
unguarded coordinate.

mcp-base is also un-buildable for the same reason machines-viz was:

    $ cd tools/mcp-base && clojure -M:clein pom
    Error in the :clein/build map: {:lib day8/re-frame2-mcp-base, …} - failed:
      (contains? % :main) spec: :noahtheduke.clein.specs/build-opts

The day8 clein fork's `build-opts` spec requires `:main`. Every clein invocation in that
directory aborts before doing any work.

## Blocker 3 — the lockstep gate cannot see either failure

Both blockers are invisible to `verify-version-lockstep.sh`: it reads `:version` and the
`:local/root` coordinates, never whether clein would accept the `:clein/build` map, and
never whether a non-`:local/root` runtime coordinate survives into the pom. It reported
"all 17 artefacts … pinned" while `day8/re-frame2-machines-viz` could not be built at all.
Two candidate hardenings, both cheap:

  - assert every `:clein/build` map satisfies clein's own spec (in practice: assert `:main`
    is present, which is the only required key the repo's maps have been missing); and
  - assert every main-`:deps` coordinate for a publishable artefact is a kind `clein pom`
    can express — i.e. flag `:git/url` coords in a publishable artefact's `:deps`, since
    those are dropped silently.

## Suggested order

1. Rule on `day8/de-dupe` (publish / vendor / accept unpublishable). Blocker 1 gates
   everything else; without it neither story-mcp nor mcp-base can ship a correct pom.
2. Add mcp-base to the `TOOLS` inventory (five tools) and give it `:main`.
3. Add the deploy jobs. Per rf2-4u3t1's ruling story-mcp joins the EXISTING
   `release-story.yml` on the EXISTING `story-v*` glob so the pair cannot skew; mcp-base
   needs to deploy ahead of it on that same glob.
4. Harden the lockstep gate per Blocker 3 so this class cannot recur silently.

Nothing here is an alpha blocker: a `v*` tag does not touch `tools/` (re-verified after the
machines-viz work landed), so `v0.0.1.alpha` is unaffected.

title: Freehand manifest: publish the per-event-site classification the analyzer already records
description:
Found while landing increment 1 of rf2-lvvl2 (`re-frame.freehand.tool/
read-view-event-sites`). This is the SAME defect rf2-hytu5 fixed for
`:diagnostics`: a fact the compiler already records, collected in the analyzer
site index and published nowhere a reader can reach.

`re-frame.freehand.compiler.analyze` records five facts per event site beyond
its coordinates - `:prop` (the authored handler prop), `:classification`
(`:vector` / `:options` / the dynamic kinds), `:serializable?`, `:sync?` (the
controlled-input synchronous door, back-filled by `record-event-sync!`) and
`:handler` (the analyzed event vector). `re-frame.freehand.compiler/
structural-manifest` projects `(select-keys % [:sid :source-coord :path])` and
drops all five, so `read-view-event-sites` can say WHERE a view dispatches from
and cannot say WHAT it dispatches. That is the difference between an event-site
read an inspector can act on and one that only counts lines.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN INCREMENT 1: `spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/
fh-struct-010.edn` pins `:required-keys {:events #{:sid :source-coord :path}}`
and both `manifest_census_cljs_test` and `manifest_roster_coverage_cljs_test`
assert `(= ks (set (keys entry)))` - an EXACT key set, not a subset. So the
manifest change and the fixture row are one atomic edit, and that fixture was
fenced off increment 1 (another worker held the Freehand analyzer/emitter
serial lane that wave). Nothing about the change is hard; it is a lane
conflict, not a design question.

SCOPE:
  1. Widen `structural-manifest`'s `:events` projection to carry the per-site
     facts the analyzer already records.
  2. Update `fh-struct-010.edn`'s `:required-keys {:events ..}` row in the same
     commit (exact-key-set assertions, so the two move together).
  3. Apply the honesty rule the sibling `read-view-dependencies` already
     applies to `:query`: project the authored event vector VERBATIM only when
     it is fully literal, and otherwise carry the literal event-id with the
     dynamic arguments marked rather than shipping a lowered host expression
     to a reader as though it were the author's form.
     `re-frame.freehand.tool/literal-form?` is the predicate; do not write a
     second one.
  4. Retire or update the `:site-facts` key `read-view-event-sites` currently
     carries. It exists for one reason - to say "an absent `:handler` means
     unpublished, not absent" - so it must not outlive the gap it names.

HOT-ZONE / LANE: `spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-010.edn` plus
`implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler.cljc` - sequence this
behind any open worker on the Freehand analyzer/emitter lane.
close_reason: RE-CLOSE. Work verified present on main (fh-struct-010.edn pins :sync? in the :events required-keys row; the nine-fact projection ships). Originally closed on PR #6971 + #6979; the close EVAPORATED — almost certainly the close-evaporation race I found in my own merge loop, where git checkout HEAD -- .beads before pulling reverts an uncommitted export. Loop now checkpoints BEFORE any checkout. Flagged by the cluster reviewer as already-shipped, which is correct.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
BLOCKED ON THE FENCED tool.cljc — NOT a fh-struct-010 lane conflict (worker report, 2026-07-25, PR #6963).

The bead's stated blocker (fh-struct-010's exact-key-set assertions) is NOT the
blocker. fh-struct-010 was mine this wave and I moved it; with the projection
widened to [:sid :source-coord :path :prop :classification :serializable? :sync?]
and the fixture's :required-keys {:events ..} moved to match, BOTH manifest suites
go green — manifest-census and manifest-roster-coverage pass, and :sync? turns out
to be present on all three census event sites, so no analyzer change was needed for
them either.

The actual blocker is scope item 4. Measured, not inferred: with the widening
applied, 'cd implementation/freehand && clojure -M:test' = rc 1, exactly 2 failures,
both at tool_reads_cljs_test.cljc:246 —

    (is (= (:site-facts r) (set (keys site))))

:site-facts is re-frame.freehand.tool/event-site-facts, a literal
#{:sid :source-coord :path} in implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/tool.cljc.
read-view-event-sites passes (:events m) straight through, so the moment the
projection widens, the published :site-facts LIES about the entries beside it —
which is the exact false-green that assertion was written to catch (its docstring
says so: 'if the manifest starts publishing the classification and :site-facts is
not updated, this reds'). Editing only the TEST to expect the wider set would make
the suite green while the shipped value stayed false. So the manifest projection
and event-site-facts are ONE atomic edit, and tool.cljc was fenced for this wave
(rf2-cpfbg and rf2-xftdv are both in_progress on the tool-tier live-reads slice).

Scope item 3 lands in the same atom for the same reason: the honesty rule belongs
at the READ, beside dependency-site, because the manifest already carries :query
raw for :subscriptions and tool.cljc is where literal-form? applies it. So :handler
must NOT be added to the projection until item 3 can land with it — otherwise
read-view-event-sites ships a lowered host expression to a reader as the author's
form, which is precisely what item 3 forbids.

WHEN THE FENCE LIFTS, the whole bead is one small PR:
 1. compiler.cljc :events projection -> [:sid :source-coord :path :prop
    :classification :serializable? :sync? :handler]   (verified to work for the
    first seven; :handler needs item 3 alongside)
 2. fh-struct-010.edn :required-keys {:events ..} to match (verified green)
 3. tool.cljc: event-site-facts widened (or DERIVED from an entry, which retires
    the drift risk the literal set carries), and a handler-site honesty projection
    beside dependency-site using the existing private literal-form?
 4. tool_reads_cljs_test.cljc:244 hard-coded set updated with it

ONE LATENT TOTALITY GAP FOUND, worth fixing in that PR: :sync? is NOT total over
event sites. analyze.cljc's add-event-site! calls carry it explicitly at the two
spread sites and at the spread-safe site, and record-event-sync! back-fills it for
every handler analyze-element-props classifies — but analyze-component-callback-prop
(analyze.cljc ~line 2350, a v/event / v/handler as a PROP on a view or foreign
component) records {:prop k :handler :opaque :classification kind :serializable? false}
with no :sync?. select-keys drops an absent key, so such a site would carry a
narrower key set than its siblings and break the exact-key-set law. The census views
happen to carry no such site, so the fixture passed — a green over an uninhabited
case. Add ':sync? false' there (it is factually false: a component callback prop is
not a DOM controlled-input door site), matching what the spread sites already do.

title: Freehand tool tier live reads, source (3): the bounded explain-render over the Spec 009 ring
description:
Source (3) of rf2-lvvl2, split out because increment 1 (the manifest-backed
declaration reads) landed on its own. rf2-lvvl2 stays OPEN; this bead owns its
DONE WHEN criteria 4 and 5.

SCOPE: a BOUNDED `explain-render`. Enrich the selected-commit record only with
facts Freehand ALREADY HAS at commit - frame, committed reads/dependencies,
committed event sites, lowering, generation, and a trigger cause IF that cause
can be carried to commit without keeping history. Publish validated commit and
lifecycle facts into the EXISTING Spec 009 trace path. `explain-render` folds
the configured retained ring AT READ TIME and reports truncation or missing
basis through the schema's existing `:complete?` and `:loss` fields
(`re-frame.freehand.evidence/projection` refuses a projection that claims
completeness while reporting loss, so this is enforced at the door rather than
asked for). Background tools may fold those bounded records into UI summaries;
the substrate MUST NOT persist the summary.

IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD, worth the whole bead if missed: **Spec 009 DOES NOT
RETAIN FRAMELESS EVENTS.** So Freehand evidence must either join the applicable
frame/run correlation, or use an equally explicit RETAINED Freehand trace
operation under the SAME ring and the SAME retention knob
(`:rf.trace/events-retained`, applied via
`(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer {:events-retained N}})` - see
`re-frame.freehand.evidence/retention`). Merely calling a listener with an
uncorrelated record makes late explanations DISAPPEAR and does not satisfy the
contract. Pair attaches late; an explanation that only exists in the callback
that already fired is not an explanation.

NO SECOND RETENTION KNOB, and no Freehand history store. `evidence_boundary_
jvm_test.clj` proves both over interned vars and will govern this work: any
Freehand var whose name matches retain|retention|history|ring-buffer must be an
immutable value, and `re-frame.freehand.evidence` must hold nothing at all.

WHAT INCREMENT 1 ALREADY GIVES YOU: `re-frame.freehand.tool` is the read door
and is already OFF the render path, which is what lets it reach
`re-frame.freehand.evidence` without widening the one-seam roster that test
pins. `explain-render` belongs there beside `read-view-manifest` /
`read-view-dependencies` / `read-view-event-sites`.

DONE WHEN (rf2-lvvl2 criteria 4-5):
  4. A recent selected commit can be explained from the configured Spec 009
     window.
  5. Eviction and missing correlation are reported as LOSS, never silently
     presented as complete evidence.

SEQUENCING: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE (sequential, never
parallel) and a retained Freehand trace operation is a 009 change - hold this
until no other worker holds that file. Cross-host coverage (JVM + CLJS) in the
shape rf2-hytu5 and the increment-1 PR used. Pair's tool catalogue is a CLOSED
WORLD, so the consumer rewire (F6 ledger rows 392/393/394/395/397) stays a
separate slice and stays pending.
close_reason:
PR #6961 MERGED. tool/explain-render folds Spec 009's per-frame retained ring AT READ TIME under Spec 009's single existing knob.

THE HAZARD IS HANDLED BY JOINING THE REAL CORRELATION, which is what makes criterion 5 satisfiable: the row records (:dispatch-id trace/*handler-scope*), nil when no cascade is on the stack. That makes the loss arms genuinely DISCRIMINABLE rather than collapsed — :cap when the named run has left the window (provable, because the id is present and the ring is not), the new closed-vocabulary :uncorrelated when the commit named no run at all, and :cap again for an empty or disabled window. :candidates (query-joined runs) is offered but explicitly NOT presented as the answer.

A SYNTHETIC DISPATCH-ID WAS REJECTED ON EVIDENCE, not on taste: epoch/capture-event! buffers any :dispatch-id-bearing emit for a frame even with no cascade in flight, so minting one would strand phantom runs in epoch buffers. That is the right call and answers the question I put to this worker twice.

title: Freehand tool tier live reads, source (2): the minimal current-occurrence index and mounted-views
description:
Source (2) of rf2-lvvl2, split out because increment 1 (the manifest-backed
declaration reads: `re-frame.freehand.tool/read-view-manifest` /
`read-view-dependencies` / `read-view-event-sites`, plus the dev-only
declared-view index `re-frame.freehand.registry`) landed on its own and a
half-delivered live-state slice is the worst possible outcome. rf2-lvvl2 stays
OPEN and keeps its six DONE WHEN criteria; this bead owns criteria 1, 2 and 3.

THE ONE REQUIREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES ANY LIVE STATE AT ALL: Pair attaches LATE.
An MCP agent attaches to an ALREADY-RUNNING application, so Freehand's
fire-and-forget commit sink (`re-frame.freehand.cell/emit-commit-evidence!`,
cell.cljc:901) can never answer "what is mounted right now" - a sink installed
at attach time sees only commits that happen AFTER it. `read-mounted-views` is
a shipped tool in `skills/re-frame2-pair`. Nothing else in rf2-lvvl2 needs
retained state.

SCOPE: a MINIMAL LIVE INDEX of current dev-mode occurrences and their latest
committed projection. Insert-or-update on the selected commit, remove on
disconnect. Freehand's explicit shell cleanup is the natural release seam. It
must distinguish two simultaneous occurrences of one view, stay correct across
a COMPATIBLE hot reload, and report unknown facts as UNKNOWN rather than
manufacture root or lifecycle fidelity. `mounted-views` is a read over this
index.

HARD FENCE, carried forward VERBATIM from the rf2-drpa3.167 ruling: this is
CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORY.
  - No lifetime render/batch counts.
  - No accumulated target union.
  - No lifecycle interval ledger and no hide-versus-unmount proof labels.
  - No weak-keyed store and no HMR store migration.
  - No cell-to-root attribution.
  - No second retention knob.
If this starts to look like the donor's 1,049-line per-occurrence evidence
accumulator, STOP - that is the gold-plating signal and .167 already ruled
against it.

SEAM ALREADY PREPARED: `re-frame.freehand.cell/set-evidence-sink!` is the
installation point, and its docstring (reconciled by the increment-1 PR) now
names THIS bead as what installs there - a minimal current-occurrence index,
never the donor per-cell accumulator.

WHAT INCREMENT 1 ALREADY GIVES YOU:
  - `re-frame.freehand.registry` - the dev-only view-id to declaration index,
    gated in the `v/defview` expansion so it DCEs in production. Keyed by
    DECLARATION, one row per view id; the occurrence index is a SEPARATE
    structure keyed by runtime occurrence (`re-frame.freehand.evidence/
    occurrence?` - `{:parent .. :key ..}`), and the two must not be merged.
  - `re-frame.freehand.tool` - the read door, already off the render path
    (nothing reachable from `re-frame.freehand` requires it), which is what
    lets it reach `re-frame.freehand.evidence`. `mounted-views` belongs here.
  - `re-frame.freehand.evidence/commit-projection` + `commit-record` - the
    validated per-commit record the sink already receives.

BOUNDARY TESTS THAT WILL GOVERN THIS WORK (read them before writing code):
  - `evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj` - `re-frame.freehand.evidence` may be
    mentioned by exactly the roster the test names, and only `cell` may be
    REACHABLE from the public door. A live index in a new namespace that the
    render path requires would need that roster widened DELIBERATELY, with the
    reason stated; do not widen it silently.
  - the same file's `no-freehand-namespace-publishes-a-second-retention-store`
    - any Freehand var whose NAME matches retain|retention|history|ring-buffer
    must be an immutable value.
  - `npm run test:freehand-evidence-elision` - the control-build probe. A live
    index is exactly the kind of state that must not ship: add a dev-only
    sentinel for it to
    `implementation/scripts/check-freehand-evidence-elision.cjs` (increment 1
    added no new string literal to root one on, so this is the first slice
    that can).

DONE WHEN (rf2-lvvl2 criteria 1-3):
  1. Two live occurrences of one view are distinguishable.
  2. A late-attaching Pair session sees occurrences that were already
     connected before it attached.
  3. Disconnect removes an occurrence and releases its current projection.

Cross-host coverage (JVM + CLJS) in the shape rf2-hytu5 and the increment-1 PR
used. Pair's tool catalogue is a CLOSED WORLD - any change to the five view
tools is also `descriptors_data.cljs`, `registry.cljs`,
`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` and the mcp-conformance
gate - so the consumer rewire (F6 ledger rows 392/393/394/395/397) stays a
separate slice and stays pending.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6961 (2026-07-25): REOPENED — DONE WHEN 1 is not guaranteed on the JVM. `cell/occurrence-of` uses `{:parent nil :key (System/identityHashCode cell)}` and `occurrences/connected` keys directly on that map. `identityHashCode` is a 32-bit hash, not object identity and not collision-free. A current-main JVM probe retaining every minted `ViewCell` found two distinct live cells with hash `2134400190` after 78,850 allocations; their occurrence maps were equal. The second `observe!` therefore replaces the first row, and disconnecting either cell `dissoc`s the surviving cell's row too. The CLJS `goog/getUid` arm does not have this defect.

Bounded completion at this exact owner: mint a collision-free stable per-cell occurrence token on the JVM (or key the internal index by actual identity while exposing a safe token), preserving reconnect stability and the no-history fence; add a deterministic regression around the token allocator/index behavior rather than a probabilistic collision hunt. No interval ledger, weak store, or root attribution is needed.
close_reason: RE-CLOSE. Work verified present on main (read-mounted-views and explain-render documented at tool.cljc:12; occurrence-facts roster and the cell.cljc release seam both ship). Originally closed on PR #6961; the close evaporated via the same .beads checkout race in my merge loop, now fixed. Flagged by the cluster reviewer as already-shipped — correct.

title: Freehand: two conformance fixture rows pin a structural-tier event diagnostic that diverges from the mounted tier
description:
Split out of rf2-5xjxj. That bead fixed the ACCEPTANCE divergence (the
structural render recorded a non-roster map at an event position
verbatim). What remains is a DIAGNOSTIC-ID divergence for values both
tiers already refuse, and it is pinned by two conformance fixture rows
that rf2-5xjxj's worker was fenced from touching (an F6a false-green
worker was live on spec/conformance/freehand/** at the time).

THE IDEAL SHAPE, and why it is not what landed. node/classify-event
should delegate wholesale to events/event-plan:

  (case (:role (events/event-plan v))
    nil            nil
    :event-vector  (reject-non-data! tag k v "event intent")
    :event-options (reject-non-data! tag k v "options map")
    {:rf.ui/opaque :fn})

That is strictly LESS code than the cond it replaces, and it makes one
authored mistake get one verdict on every tier. It was written, run, and
backed out because exactly two fixture rows go red under it:

1. spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-003.edn:92
     {:form [:div {:on-click "go"}] :error-id :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed}
   A STRING at an event position. fh-event-002.edn:44 says the same
   authored mistake is :rf.error/view-bad-event, and FH-EVENT-002's modes
   are `common jvm browser`. So the two active rows describe one input
   two ways. Both tiers REFUSE it — only the id differs — which is why
   this is a diagnostic bug rather than the acceptance bug rf2-5xjxj was.
   Same for :number, :keyword and :set.

2. spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-struct-002.edn:73
     {:form [:form {:on-submit {:event [:cart/checkout] :after :fh/fn}}]
      :error-id :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed}
   The row's stated intent is the DATA law ("an options map is recorded
   verbatim, so it too is data all the way down"), but the map it uses to
   demonstrate that law ALSO carries an off-roster key (:after), so it
   fails two laws at once and the row silently pins which one wins. The
   row is under-determined rather than wrong. Remedy: make it
   roster-clean, e.g. {:event [:cart/checkout] :once :fh/fn} — then only
   the data law can fire and the ordering stops mattering.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD (PR for rf2-5xjxj): the map arm alone consults
events/event-plan, and reject-non-data! runs BEFORE that consult so
fixture row 2 keeps its current verdict. That ordering is defensible on
its own terms (a value that could never be recorded under ANY spelling
is not fixed by renaming the key it rode in on) but it is NOT what the
compiled tier does — analyze.cljc reports the roster first
(:rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options) and has no data check at all. Once
row 2 is roster-clean, roster-first becomes available and the three
tiers can agree on ORDER as well as on verdict.

DO: fix the two fixture rows, then collapse classify-event to the `case`
above and drop the now-dead fn-carried? helper and the :else malformed!
arm. Verify with `cd implementation/freehand && clojure -M:test` and
`cd implementation && npm run test:freehand` (the structural walk is
.cljc, so both lanes exercise it).

SEPARATELY OBSERVED, same seam, not yet filed anywhere: analyze.cljc
refuses `:passive true` with `:prevent-default true` as
:rf.ui.compile/contradictory-handler-options, but events/options-plan
accepts that combination at render. So the compiled tier refuses a
declaration the interpreted and structural tiers accept — the mirror
image of rf2-5xjxj, and arguably the same class. Worth deciding whether
options-plan should carry the contradiction check too.

title: Freehand: the JVM structural render passes a non-roster map at an event position through unclassified
description:

The two hosts disagree about a MAP at an event position.

BROWSER / mount: re-frame.freehand.events/event-plan classifies it against the closed roster #{:event :prevent-default :stop-propagation :once :passive :capture} and raises :rf.error/view-bad-event for anything else.
COMPILED build: analyze.cljc raises :rf.ui.compile/bad-handler-options for the same map.
JVM structural render: passes it straight through, unclassified.

Reproduced on the real classpath (rf2-rczed evidence run):

  (v/defview menu-bad [_]
    [:ul {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:menu/activate] "Escape" [:menu/close]}} [:li "Open"]])

  (t/attrs (t/find (t/render [menu-bad {}]) #(= :ul (:tag %))))
  ;; => {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:menu/activate], "Escape" [:menu/close]}}

So t/render does not catch this class at all. This is exactly how the deleted D007 exact-key map could sit in the guide and in a consumer's codebase behind a green .cljc structural suite: the interpreted browser tier and the compiled tier both reject it, and the tier a consumer actually tests on accepts it silently.

testing.md promises 'the same declaration answers the same tree on the JVM and in ClojureScript, so a .cljc structural test is a cross-host claim'. For event positions that promise does not hold today.

DO: run the site plan (events/event-plan) on the JVM structural render path too, so a non-roster map is rejected identically in all three tiers. FH-EVENT-002 already says 'rejected in both tiers' and lists 'common jvm browser' as its modes, so the conformance row arguably already binds this - check whether the row's JVM arm actually exercises a bad map, and add the tooth if not.

Distinct from rf2-erqin, which is the presence-phase host divergence.

title: Re-run install-git-hooks after PR #6921 merges (arms the new staleness advisory) + verify per-worktree arming at next idle hygiene pass
description:
Two loose ends after rf2-zt65l / rf2-txm8g, both cheap, both easy to lose.

1. RE-INSTALL AFTER #6921 MERGES. The mayor ran the installer BEFORE PR #6921 landed, so the install predates the new post-merge staleness block. Measured from a linked worktree at 2026-07-25 with the PR's registry:

     install-git-hooks: C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.git/hooks/post-merge block missing
     exit 1
     grep -c 'BEGIN re-frame2 worker beads boundary (rf2-ia8o7)' .git/hooks/pre-commit  -> 1   (repaired, good)
     grep -c 'BEGIN re-frame2 hook-install staleness check (rf2-zt65l)' .git/hooks/post-merge -> 0

   So the boundary guard IS armed, but the arm that NOTICES future drift is not - and it cannot notice its own absence. One more run closes it:

     git pull --ff-only && sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh && sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check   # expect exit 0

   After that the loop is self-reporting: every subsequent pull that lands a change under scripts/git-hooks/ without an install prints the repair command.

2. VERIFY PER-WORKTREE ARMING WHEN WORKTREES ARE IDLE. Deferred by the mayor on rf2-txm8g: the installer arms one shared hooks directory, and 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' from a linked worktree returns the mayor's .git/hooks, so inheritance is structural rather than per-worktree. PR #6921 layer 6 case (6d) asserts that property in a sandbox, and case (6e) proves the guard bites through an inherited install. An independent live check needs a probe commit inside a worker branch, so do it when no worker is in flight.

   Non-destructive probe (no commit, real hook, scratch index):
     IDX=$PWD/.git-scratch.index; git read-tree HEAD  # with GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX
     printf 'x\n' >> .beads/issues.jsonl
     GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX git add .beads/issues.jsonl
     GIT_INDEX_FILE=$IDX sh "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit"   # expect exit 1
     rm -f $IDX; git checkout HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl

ACCEPTANCE: --check exits 0 on the mayor checkout with the post-#6921 registry, and one worker worktree is observed refusing a staged .beads/issues.jsonl through the INSTALLED hook.
close_reason:
Post-merge reinstall DONE by the mayor 2026-07-25, immediately after PR #6921 merged (merge commit 4f047b8924). Ran 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh' from the mayor checkout: appended the new rf2-zt65l block to .git/hooks/post-merge; pre-commit and mayor-marker already up to date; exit 0. Then 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check' -> EXIT 0, so the checkout is now fully guarded on both blocks. The chicken-and-egg the worker named (the arm that notices drift could not notice its own absence) is closed.

MAYOR RULING on the open question that PR left: DO NOT wire 'install-git-hooks.sh --check' into scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. The worker correctly declined to make that call unilaterally and flagged the reason — CI legitimately runs without hooks installed, so the check would false-red on every CI run of the spine. A gate that is red for a correct reason trains people to ignore it, and this repo already relies on the spine being meaningfully green. The post-merge advisory is the right arm: it fires exactly where a stale hook matters (a developer checkout that just pulled new hook sources), is silent on a healthy checkout, and costs nothing at commit time. The CI arm remains scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh, which is where a boundary violation actually needs catching regardless of anyone's local setup.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT, recorded so it is not repeated: I told Mike '.git/hooks/pre-commit does not exist at all'. That was WRONG. The file existed (1914 bytes, dated 2026-06-01) carrying the rf2-ydl2p mayor-boundary block; what was missing was the rf2-ia8o7 beads-boundary block. My diagnostic was 'grep -c beads .git/hooks/pre-commit || echo NO HOOK' — grep exits 1 when the count is ZERO, not only when the file is absent, so the || fired on a present-but-unmatching file. Same shell-semantics class as the earlier && / || precedence bug that truncated issues.jsonl. Use 'test -f' for existence and grep only for content, never conflate the two.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: live per-worktree verification. The installer arms all worktrees through the shared hooks directory (measured: core.hooksPath unset; from a linked worktree 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' resolves to the primary checkout's .git/hooks), so inheritance is established structurally. What is NOT verified is a refusal actually firing inside a worker worktree, because proving it means writing a probe commit into someone else's in-flight branch. Do that at the next hygiene pass when worktrees are idle, using the non-destructive scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE probe this PR demonstrates.

close_reason: DONE by the mayor 2026-07-25. Ran 'sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh' from the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2, exit 0. Output: post-merge up to date; pre-commit up to date; APPENDED BLOCK to .git/hooks/pre-commit; refreshed mayor-marker at .git/mayor-marker. Verified after: grep -c beads .git/hooks/pre-commit returns 7. WHY THIS MATTERED: before this, .git/hooks/pre-commit DID NOT EXIST on the mayor checkout at all — not merely outdated. CLAUDE.md states the .beads database boundary is enforced by a pre-commit hook in linked worktrees, and that enforcement had been absent for this entire session; the boundary held on worker discipline alone (every dispatch brief carries the rule and no worker violated it), but the belt-and-braces the method describes was simply not installed. That is correct — the mayor is explicitly permitted to commit the tracker database ('the tracker database is the mayor's to commit'), and the installer refreshes .git/mayor-marker precisely so the hook can tell the two cases apart. The refusal path is for WORKER worktrees, which is where the boundary actually needs enforcing. The probe commit was reset --soft and removed; nothing junk was pushed. NOT YET VERIFIED: whether the five live worker worktrees each picked up the guard — the installer reports arming the mayor plus live worktrees, but I did not independently confirm the refusal fires inside a worker worktree, because doing so means writing a probe commit into someone else's in-flight branch. rf2-zt65l's PR carries the mechanism and its own bite-proof; re-verify per-worktree arming at the next hygiene pass, when worktrees are idle.

title: Freehand guide: accessibility.md claims exact-key maps on :on-key-down are a supported closed data form
description:
docs/core/freehand/accessibility.md (Keyboard section) says:

  'Exact-key maps on :on-key-down / :on-key-up are a **closed data form** for common chords (see [Events](events-and-handlers.md)).'

That is false, and events-and-handlers.md says the opposite two pages earlier: 'There is no key-condition map. A handler slot holds ONE handler form.'

The implementation is decisive. re-frame.freehand.events/event-plan classifies a MAP at an event position as the OPTIONS map and nothing else, against the closed roster #{:event :prevent-default :stop-propagation :once :passive :capture}. So {"Enter" [...] "Escape" [...]} raises :rf.error/view-bad-event at browser mount time (re-frame.freehand.events/site calls event-plan). Note the JVM structural render passes the map through unclassified, so t/render does NOT catch it — a consumer would ship this and find out in the browser.

rf2-qwsmv already corrected the two SAMPLES that taught the unsupported spelling (semantic-controllers.md blocks 1 and 14, replaced with the v/event branch events-and-handlers.md teaches). The accessibility.md PROSE bullet was left alone because that worker's write surface was sample corrections only.

DO: reword the accessibility.md bullet to name the two supported spellings (a key projection [:ev ::v/key] into a branching handler, or v/event at the site) and drop the 'closed data form' claim.

Separately worth considering: should the JVM structural render refuse a non-roster map at an event position, so t/render catches this class at all? Today the two hosts disagree.
close_reason:
