notes:
SCOPE CONFIRMED AND UNBLOCKS-CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-07-25 05:59:35 AUSEST, out of the rf2-drpa3.167 ruling.

rf2-drpa3.167 is now CLOSED, ruled REPLACE: the donor per-occurrence evidence accumulator does not graduate into Freehand, and donor rows 195-196 go MOVE -> REPLACE (ledger edit filed as rf2-d13hj). So this bead no longer unblocks .167; it now unblocks rf2-lvvl2, the Freehand tool tier live reads (minimal live-occurrence index, mounted-views, bounded explain-render over the Spec 009 ring), which is owned by F6c and depends on this bead.

THE STANCE FENCE IN THIS DESCRIPTION IS RATIFIED, with one clarification. "Do NOT port the donor re-frame.ui.tool surface" stands, and so does "do NOT build an accumulator" - permanently, not just here: .167 ruled the accumulator is never built. The clarification is that reads over the manifest the Freehand compiler ALREADY builds are IN scope for this reader door and are not a port. Those are what make Pair's read-view-manifest, read-view-dependencies and read-view-event-sites answerable against Freehand, they need no accumulator, no root registry and no interval log, and they are the highest-value cheap slice in this whole area. Exercise judgment on how much of that lands here versus in rf2-lvvl2; the fence that matters is NO retained state and NO history store in this bead.

One implementation fact worth knowing before starting: Freehand has no browser-global descriptor registry, so a view-id-keyed read either needs a small dev-only registry or an explicit descriptor input. Pair's view-id-oriented API makes the dev-only registry the more ergonomic default. That choice is recorded on rf2-lvvl2.
DONE by PR #6910 (commits bc8bce4ff6 + e28c21524d). Both verified defects closed; the stance fence held.

DEFECT 1 — the dangling docstring. re-frame.freehand.tool now exists: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/tool.cljc, publishing ONE var, view-manifest. compiler/a11y.cljc:46 now names something that resolves, and its docstring states plainly what was missing before, so the history is legible rather than silently patched.

DEFECT 2 — the unpublished findings. compiler/structural-manifest gains :diagnostics, projecting the a11y sites the compiler env already collected: [:sid :id :tag :path :suppressed? :reason]. SUPPRESSION is what made this load-bearing — a suppressed finding is silent by design, so the manifest entry carrying the author's reason was its ONLY trace, and with no :diagnostics key that reason went into a map no reader could open.

WHY IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF v/manifest: view-manifest is TOTAL. Every value has an answer and nil means 'nothing statically known' — non-view or interpreted declaration alike. LIVE STATE (the dossier header was stale). PR #6888 is MERGED — 2026-07-24T19:13:34Z, merge commit eeafe3f2d19c0ecdd0ee86d4c05af6c59f889413. The gate runs on main today. This bead was reopened by the merged-PR audit and now owns exactly one completeness defect, not the wire-it-or-not question.

WHY THE GATE EARNS ITS KEEP (measured, do not re-litigate).
Cost, from PR #6888 run 30119055201: whole job 85s wall clock; the gate step (both :advanced builds + grep) 63s; fixed setup before it (checkout, JDK, Node, cache, npm ci) 19s. Longest job in that same run 509s (JVM tools/template) — so the gate adds ~0s to PR wall clock, running in parallel far inside the critical path. Siblings for scale, nightly run 30106705162: test:elision (the 2-build pair) 54s warm, test:bundle-isolation (6 :advanced builds) 98s warm.
No invoice. day8/re-frame2 is PUBLIC and the job is ubuntu-latest, so GitHub-hosted minutes are not billed. The bead description premise — "a maintainer CI-cost call (added job minutes)" — does not survive contact with that fact. The real cost is one runner slot and some cache traffic.
Arming rate: exactly 5 of the last 110 non-beads commits on main touched an armed path (~4.5%, about one PR in twenty-two). Adding shell.cljs raises it to ~5.5%. Amortised expected added compute ~4s per PR.

WHY THE CHEAPER ORACLES ARE NOT ON THE MENU (each already measured failing in this repo).
- Counting a debug flag in the release bundle: 225 occurrences survived — inside DOCSTRINGS — in a build where the entire surface had in fact been eliminated. Reports a leak that does not exist.
- Grepping for a small function name: Closure inlines small functions, so the name is gone whether or not the behaviour shipped. The check can never go red; a green light wired to nothing.
- A require-graph reachability walk: this WAS the honest claim before rf2-3naow, when there was no emission site — the schema was pure values reached by nothing, so there was no gate for a control build to toggle. Measured then: 705,206 bytes release, 741,967 control, every schema string absent in BOTH. Its own docstring instructed that it be REPLACED, not relaxed, the moment an emission site appeared. That happened and it was replaced. The walk survives in evidence_boundary_jvm_test.clj answering a different question (how a render reaches this code) and explicitly disclaims the bundle question: a require-graph walk cannot see what dead-code elimination removed.
A two-build control probe is therefore the only non-vacuous oracle available for this claim.

WHY NOT FOLD INTO cljs-elision (the intuitive move; rejected on numbers). The Closure compile is paid PER BUILD ID, not per job — hosting the Freehand pair inside cljs-elision saves only that job's fixed setup, measured at 19s. And cljs-elision is gated on cljs_prod, which is armed very broadly: across the last 40 test.yml runs it RAN 19 and SKIPPED 21 (~48% of PRs). So piggybacking buys 19 seconds and pays for it by running two :advanced compiles roughly ten times more often than the proof can possibly have been invalidated, while lengthening the critical path of a frequently-armed required job. General lesson worth keeping: piggybacking is nearly free when a job's cost is SETUP; it is not when the job's cost is CLOSURE.

WHY NOT NIGHTLY-ONLY. Nightly alone is the reasonable minimum — it catches everything, a day late — but the regression then arrives as a red nightly against a batch of merged PRs rather than a red check on the causative PR, and bisecting a Closure-DCE regression across a day of merges is genuinely unpleasant. Scheduled workflows can also be delayed and, under load, dropped. The shipped split is right: the path-armed required job puts the red check on the PR that can break it, and the unconditional nightly (expensive-tests.yml + test-rigorous-local.sh) is the honest superset for breaks originating OUTSIDE Freehand — a core interop/debug-enabled? change, an adapter change, a shadow-cljs/Closure bump.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT STAKE IF THE PROOF SILENTLY ROTS.
- Bundle: the control/release delta is 51,304 chars — about 50 KiB raw, 6.9% of the release bundle. Gzipped that is materially smaller; extrapolating rf2-drpa3.52's measured 3.38:1 gzip ratio on this same artefact gives ~15 KiB, and that number is an ESTIMATE — nobody has actually gzipped the control.
- Runtime, and this is worse than the bytes: the seam builds AND VALIDATES a record through evidence/record then projection then defects on EVERY selected commit, which is the render hot path. That is per-frame work in production, not a one-off load cost.
- NOT a privacy leak, and do not inflate it into one. D019 is explicit that the envelope must not contain raw props, app-db, event payloads, host nodes/instances, the exception object, or arbitrary ex-data, and the schema is built to that shape — the record carries occurrence, generation, lowering and the four axes (:scope, :basis, :complete?, :loss). Shipped evidence code would be WASTEFUL, not exfiltration. The one residual concern is that set-evidence-sink! would become a live installation point on a production page, letting anything already running there receive per-commit metadata (view ids, generations, lowering). A surface you would not choose to ship; not user-data exfiltration.
- The load-bearing risk is the normative CLAIM. rf2-drpa3.37 acceptance criterion 6 states flatly that evidence/debug code does not ship, and rf2-drpa3.166 exists solely to prove it. In a repo where the spec is the artefact, silently publishing a false normative claim is the real cost. Note that the positive-control half degrades the same way: rename a door string and the sentinel goes absent in the CONTROL too, which is exactly what the control is designed to catch — but only if the gate RUNS. An un-run gate does not merely fail to catch regressions; it accumulates silent rot in its own oracle. That is the specific failure mode this project has already been bitten by twice (see the 225-docstring false positive and the inlined-name never-red above).

THE REMAINING DEFECT, RE-VERIFIED THIS SESSION RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
Running sh .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs prints implementation_jvm=true, cljs_browser=true, freehand_evidence_elision=FALSE.
implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs:165 is the SOLE call site of cell/commit! in the artefact — grepping implementation/freehand/src for commit! returns only docstring mentions, the cell.cljc definition, and the unrelated events/commit!. That call sits inside a react/useLayoutEffect reconcile on the mounted render path, and it is what roots emit-commit-evidence! and therefore BOTH positive-control door strings in the control bundle. release_app.cljs reaches it by mounting through v/mount into the shell.

Require-reachability is not call-reachability.
Arming shell.cljs is the right bounded fix precisely because it is a DIRECT primary input to the positive control, not a transitive one. It does not justify arming all of implementation/freehand/** — many transitive changes could theoretically stop the release app reaching a mounted commit, just as a core or compiler change could, and the unconditional nightly is the honest superset for those.

title: EP-0037 R3 follow-up: wire :prefetch intent into v/route-link + ui/route-link descriptors
description: Discovered-from rf2-kqxe6.7 (R3 intent prefetch, PR #6878). R3 published the consumable seam (:routing/prefetch-payload + :routing/prefetch-on-intent!) but deliberately did NOT wire the two route-link DESCRIPTORS (Freehand was off-limits with a live render-path worker; ui/route-link out of R3's routing/resources surface). MECHANICAL follow-up, one small change per artefact: (a) Freehand v/route-link (implementation/freehand — the descriptor) — add :prefetch to its control-key strip set + bind the 3 intent handlers (hover/focus/etc.) to prefetch-on-intent!, exactly as :activate! is bound for the click; (b) re-frame.ui ui/route-link (implementation/ui) — same wiring. Reuse the published seam; add NO new API. FENCE: two disjoint descriptors; can be one worker touching both (freehand descriptor + ui view) or split. GATE: adapter smokes + the DOM hover->dispatch prefetch conformance (row 3/7). Dispatch AFTER the emitter render cluster (3naow/otddd/.177) merges (frees the freehand render surface).
notes:
RESCOPED (mayor, 2026-07-26), on the cluster reviewer finding: the reopened obligation asks for a repair to code that F6e DELETES.

Its residual is the ui/route-link callback grammar in implementation/ui/**, and rf2-drpa3.57 removes implementation/ui/ wholesale. So: KEEP the Freehand descriptor half (v/route-link intent wiring) as live work; RECORD the ui/route-link half as retiring with the donor rather than as owed work. Do not brief a worker to fix the donor arm.

This is the same rule I already applied to rf2-qe9xk: donor parity is declined by default unless the behaviour is reachable by a consumer or by a gate that outlives F6e. Nothing here is.
VERIFIED ALREADY DISCHARGED — the Freehand half needs no code. PR #7023 (worker/ep0037-remainder) carries the evidence, not a change.

The v/route-link wiring landed in commit 42ae3bff30 ("wire :prefetch intent into the route-link descriptors (rf2-y29wg)", PR #6890) together with its tests. On current main:

- implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/route_link_seam.cljc: `:prefetch` is in `control-keys` (stripped before DOM emission, so `prefetch="intent"` never reaches the `<a>`); `prefetch-payload` is consulted on BOTH hosts (the JVM shell has to know whether it owns the intent keys, or the server would emit an attribute the browser render strips); the three `intent-keys` (:on-mouse-enter/:on-focus/:on-touch-start) are bound to `prefetch-on-intent!` on CLJS only; each caller value is normalised by `intent-callback` and run FIRST (composition, not replacement); and the prefetch dispatches to the same render-time-captured frame the click does, so a warm-up cannot land in a sibling.
- implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1800 declares [:prefetch {:optional true} [:= :intent]] — an unsupported value fails at the props schema.
- Coverage: five FH-ROUTELINK-008 deftests in route_link_cljs_test.cljc (control-key stripping + href unchanged; the opt-in binding all three positions with the JVM shell binding none; a passive link binding nothing and passing the caller's own event vector through verbatim; the closed callback grammar on an owned position; and that the narrowing is not a blanket refusal), plus two real-browser deftests in route_link_native_dom_cljs_test.cljs proving hover/focus/touch actually dispatch ONE :rf.route/prefetch for the link's own address after running the caller first, and that nothing warms without the opt-in.
- GATE: `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.freehand.route-link-cljs-test` = 17 tests / 258 assertions, 0 failures, rc=0.

ui/route-link half: NOT touched, per the mayor's rescope — it retires with the donor (rf2-drpa3.57 deletes implementation/ui/ wholesale). implementation/ui/** was read to confirm route_link_seam.cljc still lives there, and edited nowhere.

title: EP-0037 R1 completion: unify resources/core readiness reconciliation onto the shared projector
acceptance_criteria:
- One shared pure projector consumes Spec 016 resource facts at commit, retained-owner adoption/handoff, resource settle, hydration, and epoch restore.
- A fresh blocking resource that already has usable data commits :idle; a true first load commits/remains :loading only while work capable of settling that requirement exists.
- The adopt/handoff path has no private has-data/error/else readiness branch: missing, idle/no-work, in-flight, usable-data, refresh-error, and restored states project through the shared rules. rf2-kqxe6.6 owns the bounded missing/unusable-entry ensure fallback.
- Refresh failure with usable data stays on :refresh-error and does not become route :error; previous-data for a newly keyed requirement does not complete that first load.
- Hydration and restore recompute cached route :transition/:error from restored resource facts instead of preserving contradictory readiness.
- Remove the now-unconsumed :routing/route-blocking? hook and its settle-transition descriptors/comments, with focused cross-artifact regressions and no second readiness state machine.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6875: confirmed this open bead is the exact owner for the deliberately deferred completeness gap. The routing projector currently reduces only plan-error/blocking presence, while resources settle, hydration, and restore still do not share its resource-fact projection. Deduped here rather than creating another issue; acceptance now makes fresh-cache, refresh-error, previous-data, hydration/restore, and obsolete-hook outcomes explicit.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6877: updated this exact open owner for the new adoption integration point. :rf.resource/adopt-owner currently hand-codes usable-data -> success drain, status :error -> failure drain, else no-op. That branch can strand blocking readiness for an idle/no-work or restored contradiction and would become a second readiness state machine. Feed adoption/handoff facts through the shared projector here; rf2-kqxe6.6 separately owns falling back to ensure when a retained entry is missing/unusable.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6885 — COMPLETENESS / CORPUS OWNER UPDATE: PR #6885 correctly removed the production `:routing/route-blocking?` publication + late-bind directory row and the routing settle consumer, but three active contract passages at the merged tree still teach that retired path: `spec/012-Routing.md` at the cross-feature seam paragraph (~274) and route-resources introduction (~878), plus `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` runtime-routing row (~2923), which says routing's settle handler reads the blocking slot through that hook. Reconcile these while completing this exact readiness/projector owner; no duplicate Bead. This is separate from, but should be folded with, the two stale on-match-error-trap phrases already owned by open `rf2-b617w` per its dispatch guidance. Keep the repair prose-only/bounded unless the shared projector work itself requires code.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6895 — REOPENED after independent completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality review.

1. SETTLED-ABORT RE-ENTRY IS NOT BLOCKING. `route-resource-plan` seeds the new activation's blocking slot by removing every `requirement-met?` identity. Because `requirement-met?` includes `:inert`, an entry left `{:status :idle :data nil :attempt 1}` by a completed abort is omitted even when this NEW plan is about to run ordinary `:rf.resource/ensure` for it. Deterministic red witness: enter a blocking article route; leave it; settle `:rf.resource.internal/aborted`; re-enter the same article. The entry correctly starts a fresh load and becomes `:loading`, but the route commits and remains `:idle`, with no blocking slot, for the entire load. Focused JVM witness: 1 test / 5 assertions / 2 failures (expected route `:loading` and `#{scoped-key}`, observed `:idle` and nil). This is broader than the close note's “one turn early if unrelated settle” and violates the existing acceptance that a true first load commits/remains loading while settling work exists.

Bounded correction: plan-time omission and settle-time inert completion are different questions. At activation commit, omit only a requirement with its own usable data; a data-less inert cache record that the plan will ensure must enter the slot. The same `requirement-state` can stay authoritative, with a small context-appropriate predicate; no per-activation generation tracker or second readiness state machine is needed. Pin re-entry after the abort reply has settled, not only re-entry while abort-requested work is still `:loading`.

2. ERROR PROJECTION IS NOT EDGE-TRIGGERED. With blocking requirements A and B, fail the canonically later key first, reconcile into `:error`, then fail the canonically earlier key. `reconcile-readiness` re-sorts all outstanding failures, changes `err` from B to A, emits a second `:rf.error/resource-route-blocking` trace, and overwrites the first observed failure although the transition never left `:error`. Pure focused witness: 1 test / 2 assertions / 2 failures (2 traces instead of 1; route error changed from the first failure to the later failure). This contradicts the implementation doc and close reason's “once per transition into :error” guarantee.

Bounded correction: choose the deterministic failure when entering `:error`; while the same live activation remains `:error`, preserve its recorded first failure and do not emit again. Add reverse-canonical settle-order coverage plus the existing all-failed-at-once deterministic case. Keep the shared projector and restore trace deferral intact.
PREP AUDIT 2026-07-25 (read-only, worktree agent/ep0037-prep-audit @ caca857928): re-derived all four audit notes against origin/main. THREE of the five obligation clusters are ALREADY-SATISFIED; ONE is STILL-UNMET.

ALREADY-SATISFIED (#6895 finding 1, settled-abort re-entry): PR #6902 landed requirement-ready? (route.cljc:263-276) and route-resource-plan now seeds the blocking set with (remove #(requirement-ready? (entry-of %))) at route.cljc:1052-1056 — only :ready is omitted at commit, so an :inert settled-abort identity the plan will ensure IS recorded. requirement-met?'s docstring (route.cljc:255-259) now states the at-commit / post-commit split explicitly. Behavioural witness run on main: planning a blocking requirement whose entry is {:status :idle :data nil :attempt 1} returns :blocking #{scoped-key}. PASSES. NB the route-resource-plan docstring at route.cljc:905 still names requirement-met? for the at-commit read — stale by one PR, one-word fix.

ALREADY-SATISFIED (#6885, retired-hook prose): git grep 'route-blocking?' over tracked files is EMPTY repo-wide. spec/012-Routing.md:274 now reads 'There is no blocking-transition predicate on the seam — routing runs no settle step'; spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2927 now reads 'Routing has no settle handler and consults no blocking predicate'. settle-transition survives only in deliberate retirement sites (routing.cljc:180 clear-event, routing_r1_purge_test, Conventions.md:77). Nothing to do.

ALREADY-SATISFIED (hydration/restore + adopt-owner): hydration reconciles at resources/ssr.cljc:1029, epoch restore at resources/ssr.cljc:1606 (with :emit-error? gated on defer-traces?), adopt-route-owner-handler at resources/events.cljc:1992 — all through route/reconcile-readiness, no private branch. drain-blocking is gone (only the unrelated SSR loop drain-blocking-resources! remains).

STILL-UNMET (#6895 finding 2, error projection is not edge-triggered): reconcile-readiness re-picks the canonically-first outstanding failure on EVERY settle (route.cljc:382-385) and gates the emit only on value inequality (route.cljc:389-398). Reproduced on main with a focused JVM witness: blocking A+B, fail B first (route -> :error, err=B, 1 trace), then fail A (canonically earlier) -> err flips to A and a SECOND :rf.error/resource-route-blocking trace fires while the transition never left :error. 2 assertions red. Contradicts route.cljc:358-367's own 'fires once per transition INTO :error' guarantee.

RECOMMENDED BOUNDED FIX (emit gate only, ~1 line): inside reconcile-readiness, emit only on the EDGE into :error — add (not= :error (get-in db' (conj slice-path :transition))) to the (and err emit-error?) guard. db' still carries the PREVIOUS transition at that point, so no new state and no latch. Regression: extend resources_route_cljs_test/reconcile-readiness-projects-the-spec-012-table with a reverse-canonical settle-order case asserting exactly ONE trace across both settles.

RECOMMEND REJECTING the audit's other half ('preserve its recorded first failure'). Pinning the first failure requires a latch the projector does not have, and it is WRONG: when the pinned identity later refetches successfully the slice would keep reporting a stale error. spec/012-Routing.md:896 defines :error as 'the deterministic first failure' over the CURRENT outstanding set — a pure function of live facts, which is what the code does. Mayor call.

SEPARATE SMALL DIVERGENCE (in this bead's surface, worth folding in): spec/012-Routing.md:896 says the deterministic first failure 'in effective plan order', but reconcile-readiness sorts by state/key-id (canonical CEDN-1 byte key) because the blocking slot is a SET and plan order is not recoverable at reconcile time. Recommend the PROSE fix (say canonical byte-key order), not persisting plan order. spec/012-Routing.md is HOT-ZONE and R4 (rf2-kqxe6.8) is editing it — R4's hunks are at 37/99/287/438/680/799/1491/1549/1720/1735 and do NOT touch the readiness section at 889-925, so no textual conflict, but the serial-lane rule still applies.

BASELINE: implementation/resources JVM suite green on main, 703 tests / 6603 assertions, exit 0. R4's branch touches ZERO files under implementation/resources/** — no code collision.
PREP AUDIT 2026-07-25 (correction): the 'effective plan order' phrasing is spec/012-Routing.md:897 (readiness table row 3), not :896. Line 973 repeats it without the ordering qualifier and needs no change.
close_reason:
PR #6913 (worker/ep0037-r1r2-fixes, commit 0765d9415a). The one STILL-UNMET obligation — #6895 finding 2, the error projection not being edge-triggered — is fixed: reconcile-readiness now gates the :rf.error/resource-route-blocking emit on the EDGE into :error via (not= :error (get-in db' (conj slice-path :transition))) at route.cljc:400-405. db' still carries the previous transition there, so this is a pure edge test — no latch, no remembered first failure, no new state. Regression: resources_route_cljs_test/reconcile-readiness-emits-the-blocking-error-once-per-edge-into-error, a reverse-canonical settle-order case asserting exactly ONE trace across both settles (RED pre-fix: 2), plus a re-entry fence (:error -> :idle -> :error asserts TWO traces) proving the gate does not over-suppress a genuine second transition.

Also landed the one-word staleness the prep audit flagged: route-resource-plan's at-commit docstring paragraph (now route.cljc:924) named requirement-met?; it now names requirement-ready?.

VERIFIED ALREADY SATISFIED, re-fixed by nothing (each re-derived against the branch, not taken on trust): (1) #6895 finding 1 settled-abort re-entry — requirement-ready? at route.cljc:263-276 with the plan seed (remove #(requirement-ready? (entry-of %))) at route.cljc:1071-1074; (2) #6885 retired-hook prose — git grep 'route-blocking?' empty repo-wide over tracked files; (3) hydration reconciles at resources/ssr.cljc:1029; (4) epoch restore at resources/ssr.cljc:1606 with :emit-error? gated on defer-traces?; (5) adopt-route-owner-handler at resources/events.cljc:1987, no private branch, drain-blocking gone.

REJECTED (mayor call taken as recommended by the prep audit): the audit's other half, 'preserve its recorded first failure'. It needs a latch the projector does not have and is actively wrong — once the pinned identity refetches successfully the slice would keep reporting a stale error. Spec 012 defines :error as the deterministic first failure over the CURRENT outstanding set, a pure function of live facts, which is what the code does. NOT IN THIS PR: the spec/012-Routing.md:897 'in effective plan order' prose divergence. spec/012 is hot-zone and was held by the live EP-0037 R4 worker, so it was fenced out; filed as rf2-kqxe6.18 (P3) to be sequenced behind R4. None of the code changes depend on it.

title: EP-0037 R3: resource-only intent prefetch
description:
@
Slice R3 (EP section: Resource-only intent prefetch). HOT-ZONE spec/012 — serial after R2 (prefetch must warm the EFFECTIVE branch plan; a leaf-only interim would ship the wrong contract).

Deliver: (1) public [:rf.route/prefetch RouteAddress] — resolves the destination, builds the same effective plan, runs unique requirements through Resources in WARM mode: ownerless + prefetch cause; ordinary freshness/dedupe/GC; :blocking? inert; NO route state, nav-token, URL, history, scroll, focus, pending-nav; NO :can-leave/:can-enter/:on-match; resource failures stay resource failures; later activation reuses fresh/in-flight work and attaches its real owner. Frame-scoped. No-op when Resources absent or plan empty. (2) :prefetch :intent on BOTH rf/route-link and v/route-link — fires on credible user intent (focus/hover/touch) only, NEVER on render/viewport (Governing Law 1); stripped before DOM emission like the other control keys. (3) :rf.error/prefetch-bad-address rejects invalid addresses before planning; planning failure emits the ordinary diagnostic with cause :prefetch, no partial ensures, current readiness untouched. Prefetching an entry-deniable destination is permitted and means nothing beyond warmed cache. (4) One :rf.route/prefetched summary trace; plan/ensure traces carry cause :prefetch. NO global default, render/viewport modes, hover-delay knobs, preload cache, or SSR prefetch.

title: EP-0037 R2 follow-through: recover retained-entry loss and preserve contributor attribution
description:
PR #6877 delivered EP-0037 R2's parent-to-leaf composition, grouped identity dedupe, plan diff, attach-before-release handoff, partial revalidation, RealWorld receipt, and conformance rows. Two bounded R2 defects remain.

First, the planner classifies a scoped identity as kept solely because it appears in the previous plan set. If that entry has since been removed (clear/remove/reconciliation or hydration-like state mismatch), :rf.resource/adopt-owner is a no-op. A blocking slot and the new plan identity have already been committed, but no entry, work, or reply exists to drain them, so the route can remain :loading forever. An idle/no-data/no-work retained entry has the same liveness shape.

Second, per-contributor :after/:when/params/scope failures are caught only after contributor context has been lost. An ancestor failure is reported with the leaf target :route-id and resource id, but without the contributing route id or local declaration id required by the R2 contract.

Keep the repair small: treat a genuinely reusable existing entry as adopted; route a missing or unusable retained identity through the ordinary ensure/readiness path; and preserve contributor context while materializing each declaration. No compatibility layer, cache redesign, owner API, or second state machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- When a previous-plan identity is absent or cannot make progress (including idle/no data/no current work), the next activation takes the ordinary ensure/readiness path, attaches the next owner before releasing the prior owner, and every blocking slot settles; no permanent :loading.
- A genuinely retained usable or in-flight entry is still adopted without revalidation: generation/current work remain stable and releasing the prior owner cannot abort shared work.
- A planning failure in an ancestor declaration identifies both the leaf target and the contributing route/local declaration (plus resource) in the route error and trace; the whole plan remains fail-closed with no partial ensures.
- Focused cross-host regressions cover a missing retained entry, an unusable retained entry, and an ancestor resolver/:after failure. Reuse the existing ensure, owner, trace, and readiness seams.
notes:

Public handler repro: with current route token 2 in :loading, blocking #{k}, and resource-plan slots {1 #{k}, 2 #{k}}, dispatch semantics for adopt-route-owner-handler against a missing entry return no entry, no fx, and leave token 2 blocked/loading. The planner emits adopt solely from prev-identities, so no later reply can drain that slot. A second planner repro used an ancestor declaration whose :params returned nil: the plan error reported :route-id :route/leaf and :resource-id :audit/ancestor, but no contributor :route/ancestor or local id. Authored and applied 3-commit ranges are patch-identical (stable patch 75e21350f0340d5eef9249dad68ee0dfe099801b); diff-check, all five PR workflows, and the 685-test/6461-assertion resources JVM suite are green.
STATUS RECONCILIATION 2026-07-25: LIVE — the audit #6877 defect is still present on main (9cdc3652e6), verified by reading both named sites. PLANNER: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:851-853 still classifies purely on prior-plan membership — (if (contains? prev-ids scoped-key) [:dispatch [:rf.resource/adopt-owner base]] ...) — with prev-ids built at :845 from :prev-identities alone, no liveness check on the retained entry. HANDLER: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:1968-1970, adopt-route-owner-handler, still opens (if (nil? entry) {:rf.db/runtime runtime-db} ...) — a literal no-op returning the runtime-db untouched — and its own docstring at events.cljc:1961 states the behaviour outright: 'A missing entry (a kept identity GC'd out from under the diff) is a no-op.' title: Freehand frame-ledger: fresh incarnation created by a different root inherits the stale author
description:
@
## Defect (verified on main, root.cljs:849)

The preflight ledger write is `:installed-by (if owned? (or (:installed-by r) root-id) ...)`. When a root-ensured frame is destroyed EXTERNALLY while its root is still mounted (the row survives with the old author and dead :installed-value; the frame is absent), and a DIFFERENT root later runs a config-bearing ENSURE for the same id, make-frame creates a genuinely fresh incarnation — but the `or` keeps the OLD author beside the NEW handle.

No takeover (the handle is exact, per #6849), but the row lies about provenance: the root that actually created the incarnation reads as foreign to its own frame, and its later differing-fingerprint config refresh trips the differing-plan conflict arm with a message blaming a root that installed nothing.

## Fix

A new incarnation is a new ownership tuple: when the ENSURE plan ran make-frame because the frame was ABSENT (a create, not a proven-owner refresh), the ledger write records the CREATING root as :installed-by — never `(or old ...)`. The proven-owner refresh path keeps its existing author (it is the same root by construction: the differing-plan arm blocks a different root with a differing fingerprint, and the same-fingerprint path never runs make-frame).

Out of scope: refs semantics on the surviving row (a stale ref from the prior incarnation's root), release-side loudness, and the wider ownership-tuple refactor — all pending the design ruling (see ai/findings/2026-07-24.freehand-root-ownership-fable.md and siblings; design review bead rf2-kpmzn).

## Acceptance

1. A browser test in root_preflight_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins the sequence: R1 ensures {:id X} (incarnation A) -> external exact destroy of A (frame absent, row survives) -> R2 ensures {:id X} (creates C) -> ledger row for X names R2 as :installed-by (red before the fix), and R2's subsequent differing-fingerprint remount refreshes WITHOUT tripping :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict.
2. Existing preflight/teardown suites stay green.
@
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6861: preflight ledger write records the creating root as :installed-by on a CREATE (fresh incarnation = fresh ownership row); browser test pins the sequence and was proven red (exactly 2 failures) against the unfixed write. Gates: freehand node 960/5508/0, browser 743/4600/0. Out of scope per bead: release-side loudness, ownership-tuple refactor, destroy-hook — pending the design ruling (rf2-kpmzn corpus).

title: Polish EP-0037 after third critique
description: Apply the acceptance-ready third-critique clarifications to EP-0037: correct the R6 dependency cell, define the classified guard matrix wording, state that in-place query edits bypass RouteAddress validation, and keep resource identity collapse/cycle handling internal to planning with no public graph API. Publish as a focused follow-up PR from current main.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Correct the R6 dependency cell so integrated proof cannot start until every R0-R5 capability it exercises is complete.
2. Define the classified guard matrix unambiguously and state that in-place query edits are resolved as edits rather than validated as RouteAddress values.
3. Keep occurrence-graph collapse/cycle handling an internal planning technique, not a public graph API.
4. Make leave continuation replay-complete: the leave-only pending contract preserves the normalized destination, original cause, and applicable history/scroll policy, so :rf.route/continue changes only the one-shot leave bypass and cannot turn an authored :replace? into a push or lose a :scroll override. Pin at least blocked programmatic-policy and blocked-popstate replay arms.
5. Rule failed-activation owner handoff explicitly: when resource planning fails after a prior plan was active, committing the target/error leaves no stale prior route-plan owner, dispatches no new-plan ensure, and preserves attach/release and frame isolation invariants. Pin first-activation and prior-plan failure cases.
6. Resolved Decisions remain operator-owned; the focused docs/status/link gates pass and the follow-up PR is pushed.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #6857 addendum (2026-07-24): reuse this active EP-0037 polish owner; do not reopen rf2-hj9nm or create another Bead.

Two omissions survive the merged acceptance revision. First, the proposed leave-only pending map stores :destination/:target/:cause but no normalized navigation policy, while continue is specified as executing only the stored RouteDestination. A blocked [:rf.route/navigate {:to ... :replace? true :scroll ...}] would therefore have no contractual way to preserve replace/scroll on continuation; a blocked popstate likewise needs cause-aware replay after URL restoration. Continue should replay the original validated intent/policy and add only its one-shot leave bypass.

Second, a resource-planning failure commits the new target and route error and runs no ensure, but the EP never says what happens to the prior plan's resource owner. Retaining it would strand old-page ownership under a new failed target (including scoped data after an account/tenant change); releasing it is likely the coherent law, but acceptance must state and prove the chosen handoff. Keep both corrections inside the pending-schema/plan-owner contracts—no second request type, router cache, or general coordinator.

title: Make local fast-PR gate skip irrelevant runtime suites for docs-only changes
description: The local scripts/test-fast-pr.sh correctly detects Markdown changes, but markdown_changed only enables extra documentation gates. Core JVM, implementation JS helpers, CLJS integration, and per-namespace isolation still run unconditionally, even for a docs/EP-only diff. CI already uses changed-surface classification to skip heavy runtime jobs on docs/spec-only PRs. Align the local fast gate with that model so documentation work remains genuinely fast without weakening relevant coverage.
design: Use a generic changed-surface classifier, not a docs/EP filename special case. Prefer reusing or sharing the repository CI classifier rather than maintaining a divergent second map. Keep cheap repository-wide static/drift checks always-on; run documentation link/status/slug/MkDocs gates when documentation surfaces change; run JVM/JS/CLJS/isolation suites only when their owning code, fixtures, build configuration, or gate scripts change. Provide an explicit override that runs the complete fast spine regardless of classification. Keep behavior deterministic for staged, unstaged, untracked, and committed branch diffs.
acceptance_criteria: A docs/EP-only branch runs the relevant always-on and documentation gates but does not launch JVM, npm/CLJS, or per-namespace runtime suites. Representative implementation and test/config changes still select every required runtime gate. An explicit full-run override is documented and tested. Classifier tests cover committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked paths plus a conservative unknown-surface fallback. Local selection is demonstrably aligned with .github/workflows/test.yml changed-surface semantics, and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh help/comments plus TESTING.md are updated.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6854 (2026-07-24) — reopened the exact fast-PR tiering owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS: runtime selection correctly delegates to report-changed-surfaces.sh, but the documentation tier is a second hand-maintained predicate and is already narrower than `.github/workflows/docs.yml`'s PR-side `docs_surface` classifier. Public `--plan` probes on disposable repositories demonstrate the false negatives:

    docs/cljs/playground.css       => PLAN docs=false jvm=false node=false
    docs/images/audit-probe.png    => PLAN docs=false jvm=true  node=true
    spec/audit-probe.edn           => PLAN docs=false jvm=true  node=true
    .github/workflows/docs.yml     => PLAN docs=false jvm=true  node=true
    scripts/test-fast-pr.sh        => PLAN docs=false jvm=true  node=true

The docs workflow explicitly treats `docs/*`, `spec/*`, `migration/*`, its workflow file, fast/rigorous gate scripts, additional checker scripts/fixtures, testbeds, and tool spec trees as documentation inputs. For the recognised playground CSS arm the local spine runs only static checks; for unrecognised docs assets it wastes the full runtime tier but still skips link/slug/status/MkDocs validation. This contradicts the source acceptance that documentation gates run on documentation surfaces and the new prose's claim to mirror CI.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the runtime half is elegant—one shared classifier, deterministic committed/staged/unstaged/untracked gathering, conservative fallbacks, and explicit overrides. The doc half recreates exactly the duplicate-map drift that runtime reuse avoided. Bound the repair to one authoritative/tested docs-surface predicate aligned with the docs workflow's PR detector (preserving its deliberate PR-vs-push distinction), and add non-Markdown docs plus the gate/workflow scripts to the real `--plan` matrix. Do not add a general file-classification framework.

EVIDENCE: Git diff check clean; all 71 PR checks green; real fast-PR self-test 16/16 when the repository's existing `python` command expectation is supplied; changed-surface contract 209/209. Those tests cover Markdown docs but contain no non-Markdown/workflow-script docs-surface row, which is why the false negatives stay green.
close_reason: Verified shipped in PR #6854 (merged) — test-fast-pr.sh now tiers on the shared CI classifier. Stale-open from close race.

title: Correct stale defview props-schema reservation in public API docs
description:
## Defect

PR #6840 corrected the compiled-promotion claim in the canonical spec/API.md defview row, but that same row still describes the shipped props-schema slice as future work: it omits :props from the closed option roster and says {:props-schema ...} is reserved and refused. The generated public docs repeat the reserved-but-unimplemented paragraph.

The implementation is already authoritative and contradictory: defview-option-keys is #{:children-policy :compiled :props}; expand-defview validates and retains :props; declared schemas drive both compiled analysis and runtime boundary validation; describe projects the authored form under :props-schema. The public docs therefore hide a valid ergonomic option while advertising a nonexistent author spelling as future work. docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md even lists and demonstrates :props elsewhere in the same member section.

## Bounded correction

Reconcile the defview roster in spec/API.md and the stale generated/public docs paragraph with the shipped declaration API. Name :props as the author option, state its existing schema role compactly, and preserve the distinct :props-schema key used only by descriptor inspection. Remove only the obsolete future-slice claim; add no API, compatibility alias, generator framework, or runtime machinery.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6840. Completeness/correctness gap in the exact canonical row the PR edited; implementation quality of the one-line promotion correction is otherwise clean. Exact-owner search across all Bead states found no props-schema/API-doc owner. rf2-jx76g remains closed because it owns only the promotion overstatement fixed by #6840.
acceptance_criteria:
1. spec/API.md lists :props in v/defview's closed option roster and no longer says the schema slice is unimplemented.
2. docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md contains no contradictory reserved-but-unimplemented props-schema claim and agrees with the shipped facade docstring.
3. The wording clearly distinguishes declaration option :props from describe projection key :props-schema.
4. Relevant API-doc generation/check gates pass with no runtime or public-surface change.
notes: Keep this a small documentation reconciliation. Trust the programmer: state the real spelling and contract once; do not add migration aliases, defensive ceremony, or a general drift system.
close_reason: Reconciled in PR #6848 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6848): spec/API.md defview row + docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md now name :props in the closed option roster, state its schema role compactly, keep the distinct :props-schema describe-projection key, and drop the obsolete reserved/refused claim. Docs-only; api-manifest byte-identical; gen/api-md/doc-api/slug/mkdocs gates all green.

title: Freehand root ledger: migrate defonce rows across ownership-schema reloads
description:
## Defect (second gap from the rf2-drpa3.110 merged-PR audit reopen)

`re-frame.freehand.root/frame-ledger` is deliberately `defonce`, so a row created by pre-#6818 code survives a hot reload WITHOUT an `:installed-value`. On the ordinary same-plan remount, `frame/frame` is live and the config fingerprint matches, so `make-frame` is NOT called and `installed-value` stays nil; the ledger swap's `(or installed-value (:installed-value r))` therefore keeps nil. Final release then dissociates the row and calls `destroy-frame!` with nil — which carries no exact incarnation token and no-ops — leaving the root-owned frame LIVE and untracked. This breaks the hot-reload path the surrounding `defonce` comments explicitly preserve.

## Bounded correction

Migrate/backfill the exact authority for a legacy `:installed-by` row that is missing `:installed-value`, WITHOUT falling back to bare-id destruction. The core incarnation token, or an idempotent constructor return under an exact-current check, can supply the token. Keep it in the one existing ledger — no parallel registry, lease framework, settlement state machine, or public API (same constraint as rf2-drpa3.110).

## Acceptance

Add an idempotent reload-shape regression that seeds the legacy installed row (a row with `:installed-by` but no `:installed-value`), runs the current same-plan remount, and proves durable state is NOT re-seeded while final unmount destroys the EXACT original incarnation and empties the ledger.

## Origin

Second of two coupled gaps in the PR #6818 merged-PR audit that reopened rf2-drpa3.110. AC4 (the config-bearing-ENSURE-over-a-boot/external-frame authority gap) was fixed under PR #6836; this HMR-migration gap was out of that dispatch's scope and is split out here so the obligation is not lost when rf2-drpa3.110 closes. Same ledger owner (`implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs`) and its preflight/teardown tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A pre-#6871 flat defonce row carrying `:installed-value` is normalized losslessly to `{:ownership {:handle :plan-author :plan-fingerprint} :refs}` before frame-standing, release, or the destroy hook consumes it.
2. The migrated handle is the identical old incarnation token; author, fingerprint, and refs are preserved, with no bare-id authority or reseed.
3. An actual flat-row same-plan HMR remount succeeds as the idempotent no-op, preserves durable state, and final unmount destroys exactly that original incarnation and empties the ledger; the destroy hook can also tombstone that migrated row.
4. A genuinely tokenless historical row remains legacy/unprovable and follows the existing fail-loud/no-successor-takeover law.
5. Stay inside the one ledger/accessor with no public API, lease system, or general schema-migration framework.
notes:
PR #6871 audit (2026-07-24) reopens this exact defonce-ledger migration owner; no duplicate Bead.

The new ownership model is sound for a fresh page, but it changes the deliberately defonce ledger from the pre-#6871 flat row `{:config-fingerprint :installed-by :installed-value :refs}` to `{:ownership {:handle :plan-author :plan-fingerprint} :refs}` without normalizing rows already alive across a hot reload. Those immediately previous rows are not unprovable legacy data: `:installed-value` is the exact incarnation handle and can be migrated losslessly.

On the first reload under #6871, `frame-standing` reads `(:ownership row)` as nil and verdicts a live owned frame `:unowned-live`, so the ordinary same-plan `v/mount` HMR path fails `:scope-config-less-or-own-the-lifetime`. If the root releases instead, `release-frame!` also reads no nested handle and leaves the owned frame live; the new destroy hook likewise cannot match/tombstone the flat handle. The added downgrade fixture removes `:handle` from the NEW nested shape and therefore cannot catch this upgrade boundary.

Keep the repair bounded: normalize only the known flat row into the nested tuple before any verdict/release/hook read, preserving exact handle identity, author, fingerprint, and refs. A genuinely tokenless pre-#6818 row must remain unprovable/fail-loud; never backfill from a bare id. Pin an actual flat-row hot-reload fixture through same-plan remount (no reseed), external destroy/hook, and final exact unmount. No ledger-version framework, public API, or lease machinery.
Fixed in PR #6883 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6883). #6871's flat->nested ledger schema change did not normalize a defonce reload-survivor; fix normalizes the one known pre-#6871 flat row in place at the frame-standing/destroy-hook door (ledger-row!) — lossless handle/author/fingerprint/refs. Tokenless pre-#6818 rows stay :legacy-live/fail-loud (no bare-id backfill). No public API / lease / migration framework. 3 upgrade-boundary DOM fixtures added; non-vacuity proven (2 fixtures red by name when normalization flipped off). Gates: freehand JVM 916/6533, node 996/5626, browser 757/4724 — all 0 failures. PR NOT merged.
close_reason: Closed

title: poll-until timeout flake: supersede-distinct-work-ids trace test times out under concurrent load
description:
SECOND load-induced flake found 2026-07-24 (sibling of rf2-eq2vx, different lane).

## Signature
JVM lane (clojure -M:test): ERROR in (supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace) at error.cljc:120 — clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo: "poll-until timed out — supersede-stale" [:rf.error/poll-until-timeout]. NOT an assertion failure — a poll-until SETTLE that did not complete inside its timeout window.

## Why it is a flake, not a real failure
Observed redding PR #6817 whose diff is events.cljc (render-fn arity) + tests — ZERO path to error.cljc trace superseding. Under 6 concurrent worker agents (each running shadow-cljs compile + JVM + Chromium) the machine is saturated and the poll-until window expires before the async supersede lands. Same root cause as rf2-eq2vx (the scroll settle): a fixed-timeout async SETTLE asserted under load that measures machine speed, not correctness.

## The fix (same shape as eq2vx)
Make the settle deterministic OR give poll-until a generous, load-tolerant bound. Find the poll-until in the supersede-distinct-work-ids test (error.cljc / the trace test around :120), and either await the actual supersede signal or raise the timeout to a bound that survives a loaded CI runner. DO NOT delete or skip the test — the supersede/stale-trace canonicalisation is real coverage. DO NOT loosen the assertion — only the WAIT should tolerate load.

## Discipline
⚠️ Prove it under load: run the JVM suite repeatedly (10+) while the machine is loaded, or prove structurally the wait is bounded by the signal not a fixed sleep. A few green idle runs prove nothing.
⚠️ It is a poll-until TIMEOUT (an error), so a test asserting a throw would pass against it — assert the supersede RESULT after a bounded wait for the signal.

## Surface
Wherever supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace lives (error.cljc trace test ~120) and the poll-until helper it uses. This is core trace/error surface — check it is not held before dispatching.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6839 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6839). Raised the supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace poll-until backstop 5s->30s (probe 5ms->25ms); pred+assertions unchanged. Proof: 10x full http JVM suite green under 28-burner CPU saturation (0/0 each); delay-injection reproduces the exact flake (error.cljc:120, :rf.error/poll-until-timeout, :elapsed-ms 5010) at the old 5s bound and passes green (10 assertions) at the shipped 30s bound. Wait is signal-bound (delivered reply + :rf.http/stale-suppressed trace); timeout is a pure load-tolerant backstop.

title: Freehand: wire view render into re-frame.performance (rf:render:*)
description:
## Why

re-frame.performance brackets four hot paths with User Timing measures (opt-in re-frame.performance/enabled?). Event / sub / fx live in core and already cover Freehand apps. Render measures (rf:render:<view-id>) only fire in the reg-view frame-aware-view wrapper in re-frame.views — Freehand has no mark-and-measure call sites. Chrome Performance panel / PerformanceObserver / APMs therefore miss Freehand view timing under the named rf: channel.

## Goal

Wire Freehand view render (and/or the correct Freehand commit/render chokepoint) through (performance/mark-and-measure :render <view-id> …) so Freehand matches the Spec 009 :render bucket and adapter reg-view behaviour when re-frame.performance/enabled? is true. Default-off + DCE when flag is false must still hold.

## Scope notes

- Spec 009 §Performance instrumentation: :render is currently described as per-reg-view; extend substrate wording if Freehand is a first-class render path.
- Implementation: freehand render/commit path (not freehand bench harness — that is separate CI evidence via performance.now).
- Tests: emission of rf:render:* when enabled; absence / DCE when disabled; align with performance-cljs-test / nightly emit patterns as appropriate for Freehand.
- Do not invent extra buckets; reuse :render naming convention.

## Acceptance

- Freehand view renders emit rf:render:<view-id> measures when enabled? is true
- Off path: zero User-Timing cost / bracket DCEs under :advanced + enabled?=false
- Docs/spec updated only as needed for Freehand substrate coverage of :render
- No regression to event/sub/fx brackets
acceptance_criteria:
- Freehand render path uses performance/mark-and-measure :render with stable rf:render:<view-id> names
- enabled?=true: measures observable (observer or retain-entries? pattern used elsewhere)
- enabled?=false: no mark/measure / no leftover strings in off path per existing perf-bundle discipline where applicable
- Spec 009 and/or freehand notes reflect that :render is not reg-view-only
close_reason: Delivered in PR #6879 (day8/re-frame2). Render-path tail: dev-gated evidence seam / performance :render marks / dead defview chain retired. Gates green (JVM 916, node 993, browser 754); isolation proofs in the PR.

title: Prove compiled top-layer dynamic-handler advisory end to end
description:
PR #6792 repaired compiled top-layer installation by carrying the element facts needed by `top-layer/install!`. For event positions, `compiler/emit_react.cljc`'s `top-layer-context` records every analyzed `:on-toggle`, `:on-before-toggle`, `:on-close`, or `:on-cancel` site as `true` at compile time.

That is not the runtime predicate the shared advisory uses. `top-layer/reconciled?` asks `(some? (get attrs handler-key))`, and a dynamic handler is explicitly allowed to evaluate to nil. On the compiled path, `reactive/event-site` then returns nil and `compiled-react/handler!` writes no DOM handler, but the separately constructed context map still contains `:on-toggle true` (or its dialog sibling). The committed node can therefore spring back open after native dismissal with no handler to reconcile application state, while the diagnostic says nothing. The interpreted twin correctly treats the nil position as unreconciled and warns.

Reproduced from current main by driving the analyzer and React emitter on:

    [:div {:popover :auto
           ::web/popover-open? true
           :on-toggle (:handler props)}]

The emitted form writes the actual site proxy through `handler!` but independently calls `top-layer/install!` with `{:on-toggle true}`. This is a mode divergence introduced by #6792's presence shortcut, not a request for a new event form or top-layer abstraction.

Keep the repair local: carry whether the runtime site produced a handler without evaluating the authored expression twice, or derive the verdict from the finalized props object. Do not pass callbacks through the context, add a handler registry, or broaden the advisory.
acceptance_criteria:
- A compiled popover with a dynamic `:on-toggle` that evaluates to nil emits exactly one unreconciled advisory after commit, matching its interpreted twin; the actual DOM handler remains absent.
- The equivalent compiled dialog cases cover `:on-close` / `:on-cancel`, with at least one nil dynamic position.
- A non-nil dynamic handler suppresses the advisory in both modes and still fires normally; a literal/event-vector handler remains unchanged.
- The handler expression is evaluated once per render, not once for props and again for diagnostic context.
- Candidate/abandoned renders still publish no advisory, and no callback or new registry/API is added to the context transport.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6860 (2026-07-24) — reopened this exact owner; no duplicate.

The implementation now carries the right runtime some?-verdict and evaluates each reconciler site once, but the Bead was closed without its declared executable acceptance. The two new tests inspect emitted JVM forms only. They never mount a compiled view whose dynamic handler evaluates to nil, prove the actual DOM handler is absent, or observe the advisory channel after commit. Existing FH-TOPLAYER-005 calls top-layer/install! directly with a hand-built attrs map; the mounted top-layer matrix uses only literal event vectors and does not observe advisories. Those tests prove the layers separately, not the composition where #6792 failed.

Finish this with one focused real-browser parity matrix, not new machinery: a compiled and interpreted popover with a nil dynamic :on-toggle must have no DOM handler and emit exactly one committed advisory; a non-nil dynamic handler must suppress it and fire once; cover the dialog close/cancel axis with at least one nil dynamic position while leaving literal/event-vector behavior unchanged. Reuse the existing advisory listener and mounted matrix harness. Candidate/abandoned purity remains owned by the existing shared install! row unless the new integration exposes a gap.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6876. End-to-end browser proof added (top-layer-advisory-parity-dom-cljs-test): compiled+interpreted popover/dialog twins, nil dynamic handler emits exactly one committed advisory + no DOM handler, non-nil suppresses + reaches DOM, close/cancel axis each with a nil dynamic position, literal-handler control, non-vacuous (reds on compile-time-true regression). Structural single-eval stays in react-lowering-jvm-test. Browser runs on CI.

title: F5: make the per-door Layer-1 duplicate-root contract truthful end-to-end
description:
HOT-ZONE SPEC BEAD — spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md is a hot-zone file: sequence against ALL other 004C work, never parallel. Spawned by the rf2-12p25 ruling (2026-07-24, Option B: ratify Freehand's runtime-fn mount door).

WHAT: 004C currently states door-shape claims that are true of the donor (re-frame.ui) but false of Freehand:
- Section 3 (~line 204): 'mount remains a macro over a literal root form (ratified...)' — on Freehand, v/mount is a runtime fn (freehand.cljc:656) and spec/API.md already documents it as Fn.
- Section 3 Verb-kinds paragraph (~248-259): 'mount, create-root, render!, and hydrate-root are macros' — anchored on re-frame.ui's var metadata; Freehand ships mount/hydrate-root/unmount! as fns and ships NO create-root and NO render! at all.
- Section 7 Layer 1 (~366-376): 'the compiler indexes every mount/render!/hydrate-root/render-static site' — on the Freehand door only render-static participates.

AMEND so each claim is scoped per door: re-frame.ui keeps its macro door (truthful — ui.cljc:174-239 really expands through re-frame.ui.compiler.root); re-frame.freehand's ratified shape is runtime fns for mount/hydrate-root/unmount! with render-static as its only macro and only Layer-1 participant; duplicate/container/prefix detection for Freehand client mounts is owned by Layer 3 claim-before-render (which section 7 already defines, and which root.cljs implements and the root_* DOM suites prove). Add the one-sentence re-open trigger: the macro door / build-time root indexing is revisited only if a named consumer for mount-site descriptors or static frame plans materialises — not for door symmetry.

NO spec/API.md change (its Freehand rows already say Fn) and NO api-manifest involvement under this ruling. If a future fn-to-macro flip is ever proposed instead, that is a seven-file api-manifest serial-lane occupant — see the rf2-12p25 ruling note.

Rationale for the scoping (transplant from the ruling): each tier proves what it actually has — render-static has no client runtime, so it keeps build-time identity registration; a Freehand client mount has a live runtime that fails loud before render (claim-before-render), so that is where its detection belongs. 004C gets simpler and truer, not weaker. 004C already carries one honest [S1-CONFIRM] in this area (Layer 1 entry-closure scoping, ~line 374) — leave it; do not add a second open marker.
acceptance_criteria: 004C sections 3 and 7 no longer claim the macro door for re-frame.freehand; each verb-kind and Layer-1 claim is explicitly scoped to its door; the one-sentence re-open trigger is present; no API.md/manifest/facade edits; mkdocs build --strict green.
notes:
PR #6824 THREE-LENS AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-24) — REOPENED exact closed source; no duplicate Bead.

The per-door split is directionally correct, but its Layer-1 claim is not truthful end-to-end:

1. REAL SHADOW BUILDS EMIT THE WRONG DIAGNOSTIC SHAPE. Off the Shadow build-pass path, re-frame.freehand.compiler.root/register-root-site! raises the promised canonical `:rf.error/duplicate-root-id` through the shared error builder. On the actual Shadow path, compile-finish calls freehand compiler/build.cljc harvest-root-plan-registries, which instead throws ex-info carrying `:re-frame.freehand.compiler.build/error :re-frame.freehand.compiler.build/duplicate-root-id` and no `:rf.error/id`; compiler_build_hook_jvm_test explicitly pins that internal id. Thus the same public collision has a different, non-catalogued identity depending on build mode, defeating tools/AI that consume the Spec 009 discriminator. The donor re-frame.ui build carrier has the same internal shape; use one small consistent projection rather than leaving the two doors divergent.

2. THE CATALOGUE WAS NOT RECONCILED. Spec 009's `:rf.error/duplicate-root-id` row still describes Layer 1 as mount/create-root/hydrate-root sites and names only re-frame.ui.compiler.root as build emitter. It omits the newly normative Freehand render-static arm and re-frame.freehand.compiler.root/build hook path. Align the row with the actual per-door roster after canonicalising the Shadow path.

3. 004C OVERSTATES COVERAGE. The new sentence says build registration is “the only place” render-static identity can be caught, but the implementation intentionally REPLACES same-namespace registrations for watch/HMR and catches only cross-namespace duplicates; a static call has no Layer 3. The immediately following Layer 2 also specifies response-local manifest/render-static collision detection. State the bounded truth: Layer 1 catches the cross-namespace/build-visible class; Layer 2 remains the response-local owner. Do not implement a response registry here—its demand gate and future assembler trigger remain exactly owned by rf2-v2gv9.

BOUNDED ACCEPTANCE: canonical `:rf.error/duplicate-root-id` data on real Shadow compile-finish for both equivalent compiler doors (or an equally small single projection), focused tests for the real harvest path, Spec 009 emitter/site roster aligned, and 004C wording narrowed to the detection actually provided. No new diagnostic, registry, page assembler, API verb, or identity framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6846 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact per-door Layer-1 owner; no duplicate.

PR #6846 correctly canonicalises the Freehand Shadow compile-finish harvest, reconciles Freehand's 004C wording, and updates the catalogue. It does NOT complete this owner's bounded acceptance for both equivalent compiler doors. The donor `re-frame.ui` real-Shadow path still gates `register-root-site!` into `re-frame.ui.compiler.build/harvest-root-plan-registries`, where the same collision throws raw `ex-info` with the internal build id.

title: Reconcile ruled D014 with the shipped v/->react contract
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6783.

The shipped implementation and canonical specs deliberately chose a coherent `v/->react` contract, but the ruled D014 decision was not amended and now gives incompatible instructions on several programmer-visible axes:

- D014 clause 5 says React children are not guessed and React-element children require a wrapper; spec/004 and the implementation automatically map React `children` to Freehand trailing children.
- D014 clause 7 requires a truthful SSR adapter or `v/client-only` fallback; spec/004/spec/011 state that the bridge has no server arm and a use site owns any fallback.
- D014 clause 8 requires a common typed JVM host-operation error; the public verb is absent on the JVM.
- D014's headline says descriptor-keyed caching; the shipped identity is logical view-id plus adapter identity so a fresh HMR descriptor republishes without remounting.

The PR close record calls out only the JVM divergence. The decisions README says an implementation-discovered contradiction must amend the affected ruling explicitly. Leaving both texts live is costly for humans and AI: each can produce a locally well-supported but incompatible implementation or usage answer.

Acceptance:
1. Make one explicit ruling: amend D014 to the shipped contract, or change the implementation/canonical specs to D014; do not preserve both.
2. Reconcile children, server/fallback posture, JVM availability, and cache-key wording together.
3. Keep docs/design/freehand/decisions/README.md, spec/004-Views.md, spec/011-SSR.md, API docs, and FH-REACT fixtures mutually consistent.
4. Record the decision as an amendment in D014 rather than relying on a PR body as the only authority.

OUTCOME (2): THE DOCUMENT WAS WRONG, on all four axes — established from source, not inherited. v/mount, v/hydrate-root and v/unmount! are each under #?(:cljs ...) in freehand.cljc, so the bridge is the FOURTH MEMBER OF AN EXISTING SET, not a special case. :rf.error/jvm-host-op is absent from Freehand's error roster entirely — every raise site is under implementation/ui/ (donor), and spec/009's row names re-frame.ui.tree/jvm-host-op! as emitter. And re-frame.freehand.tree/jvm-host-op! is NOT A DEFINED VAR: the two references in emit_jvm.cljc sit in :raw and non-lazy-foreign arms whose node kinds are in grammar/op-rejections, so they are never emitted. CLAUSE 8's OBLIGATION (host-only execution) IS INTACT AND DISCHARGED; only its MECHANISM was donor-era wording for a deleted tier — which makes this an AMENDMENT, not a retirement, and therefore correctly not escalated. Also amended: same-test-on-children (slot identity, with refs made STRICTER than the clause), server posture (the truthful-SSR-adapter arm is unreachable for a verb absent on the JVM), and cache key (descriptor-keying would miss on every reload), plus a fifth clarification recording .169's presence rule. title: One CI job runs 31 invariant checkers, stops at the first failure, and its name misattributes the blame
description:
Filed 2026-07-24 after this cost real diagnosis time during a merge pass.

## Two distinct defects in one job

.github/workflows/test.yml line 121 defines a job named "Verify skill ↔ MCP allowed-tools drift (rf2-flzdp)". It runs 31 `python scripts/check_*.py` invocations (measured, lines 121..470).

DEFECT 1 — THE NAME MISATTRIBUTES THE FAILURE. When PR #6788 went red on this job, the skill↔MCP step had PASSED ("No skill <-> MCP drift detected"). The actual failure was a much later step, check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py, reporting that :rf.evidence/* was emitted with no reserved-namespace row in spec/Conventions.md. Nothing in the job name points there. Diagnosing it took fetching the job log through the API and reading 700 lines, because `gh run view --log-failed` refuses while the run is still in progress.

DEFECT 2 — AND THIS IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE. The steps run under `bash -e`, so the job STOPS AT THE FIRST FAILURE and the remaining checkers NEVER RUN. A worker fixes the one visible failure, pushes, waits for a full CI cycle, discovers a second broken invariant, and repeats. That is MOVING THE RED, not clearing it. There is precedent in this repo: a fix worker once found three independent reds stacked behind one first failure in the api-manifest job, and fixing only the visible one would have left the job red.

## The change

1. AGGREGATE INSTEAD OF SHORT-CIRCUITING. Give each checker step `continue-on-error: true` and record its outcome; add a final step that fails the job if any recorded a failure, printing the full list of which checkers failed. One CI round-trip then reports EVERY broken invariant instead of the first. This is the actual win.
2. RENAME THE JOB to its real scope — e.g. "Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)". Nearly free, and removes the misattribution.

## What NOT to do

DO NOT split this into one job per checker. That is 31 jobs each paying a fresh checkout plus Python setup, to parallelise checks that individually run in seconds. Real cost, no benefit over aggregation — the gold-plated answer.
DO NOT weaken or skip any checker. Every one of the 31 stays; the change is purely about WHEN the job decides to stop and WHAT it calls itself.

## Sequencing

.github/workflows/* is HOT-ZONE — sole owner, sequential, never parallel. It is also a file every other PR depends on, so land it quickly once started rather than holding the lane.

## Acceptance

A PR that breaks TWO invariants in this job reports BOTH in one run, naming each failing checker; the job name describes what it actually verifies. Prove it by deliberately breaking two and showing both named in a single run.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6801 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact owner; no duplicate Bead.

The aggregation and job rename work, but the final step's claim that every failure line doubles as a local reproduction command is false for every self-test step. It derives:

    script="scripts/${id%_selftest}.py"
    ... reproduce with: python $script

For all 17 ids ending `_selftest`, this strips the suffix from the filename but omits the required `--self-test` flag. Example: a failure in `check_keyword_catalogue_drift_selftest` is reported as `python scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py`, which runs the live scan and may pass while the self-test remains red. The same mismatch affects 17/35 checker steps; a YAML-derived audit enumerated each actual command and synthesized annotation.

Keep the fix inside the aggregator: when an id ends `_selftest`, append `--self-test` to the reported command (other verbosity/CI flags are optional unless required for reproduction); otherwise report the current live command. Add a structural assertion over all checker ids that the synthesized command selects the same live-vs-self-test mode as the workflow step. Do not split jobs, alter checker order, or add a reporting framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT REOPEN — PR #6815 (merged 2026-07-24T06:03:08Z, 89b629191202192264aeb030d6740925696a9911).

The shipped fix correctly derives today's 37 reproduce commands from their real `run:` lines. The new structural guard is not exhaustive over the aggregation contract it claims to protect, because `parse_checker_steps` first filters to steps that already have an id beginning `check_`; `audit_steps` never sees any Python checker lacking that id, and the parser does not retain or verify `continue-on-error`.

Exact synthetic proof against merged main:

- one `run: python scripts/check_foo.py --verbose` step with `continue-on-error: true` but no id;
- one id'd `check_bar` step with no `continue-on-error`.

`parse_checker_steps` discovers only `check_bar`, and `audit_steps` returns `[]` (clean).

Those are the two failure modes the original owner exists to prevent. A no-id checker is absent from GitHub's `steps` context; with `continue-on-error`, it can fail while the final aggregator sees no failure and the job goes green. A checker without `continue-on-error` restores short-circuiting, so later invariants never run and the report is incomplete. The new guard currently certifies both shapes.

Bounded correction: identify checker steps independently from their already-correct id (for example by their `python scripts/check_*.py` run shape within this job, or an equally small explicit boundary), then require a unique `check_*` id, `continue-on-error: true`, a parseable existing script, id/script agreement, and live-vs-self-test agreement. Add the two exact negative fixtures. Keep the current single job, step order, final aggregator, and derive-from-run behavior. Do not add a general YAML framework, split jobs, or build a reporting subsystem.

CI context: PR #6815's invariant job and both new helper modes passed. Its red browser lane was four assertions from the pre-existing virtual-table scroll event not registering (scroll-top remained nil); the diff is only test.yml plus this Python helper, and later main is green. No Bead is added for that off-surface flake here.

Dedupe: rf2-m6kdb is the exact closed owner and already carries the prior audit reopen; reopening it again avoids a duplicate.

title: F4g donor MOVE: bring the tool evidence projection under Freehand ownership
description:
The F4g slice landed its SCHEMA half — `re-frame.freehand.evidence`, one versioned occurrence-keyed schema whose one door refuses a projection that cannot state its scope, basis, completeness and loss. What it did not land is the EMISSION half: the donor disposition.

Still donor-owned, unmoved:
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool.cljc` (~305 lines)
- `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool/evidence.cljc` (~1049 lines) — the occurrence-keyed per-cell accumulator with the fold's first/latest frame-epoch, occurrence :count, cause set, capped shown-target sample and the :dropped/:dropped-exact? loss account. That loss account is where the schema's honest half came from.

The MOVE is not a copy: EP-0036 rules the donor is donor-only and absorbed code arrives by move, slice by slice, under Freehand ownership, never by classpath reference.

Two things the move must satisfy that the donor does not today:
1. every record it emits goes through `re-frame.freehand.evidence/record`, so scope/basis/completeness/loss is structural rather than conventional;
2. retention stays Spec 009's ring — the donor's own weak per-cell index is a live projection, not a history store, and must not become one.

Also update the F0c ledger. Sequence AFTER (or with) the donor-retirement work, and note it needs the compile-tier a11y `:diagnostics` sites to reach a reader — today they are collected in the compiler env and never published on the manifest, so `re-frame.freehand.tool/view-manifest` (referenced by the a11y namespace's docstring) does not exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- `re-frame.ui.tool` and `re-frame.ui.tool.evidence` are MOVED under Freehand, not copied, and the donor no longer carries them.
- Every emitted record validates through `re-frame.freehand.evidence/record`; a projection that cannot state its loss is refused at emission, not at read.
- A cap reports its loss in data (`:complete? false` plus an explicit `:dropped`), proved by a fixture that deliberately exceeds it.
- Retention still rides the per-frame retained-event ring; no Freehand history store and no second knob, proved the way `evidence-boundary-jvm-test` proves it now.
- The F0c ledger records the move.
