RULED 2026-07-25 05:59:35 AUSEST. Source: decision dossier ai/decisions/rf2-drpa3.167.freehand-evidence-accumulator.md, deleted after this note landed. Everything load-bearing is reproduced here; the dossier is gone.

=== THE RULING: OPTION B, SPELLED REPLACE ===

The donor per-occurrence evidence accumulator does NOT graduate into Freehand. Donor-inventory rows 195 and 196 go MOVE/pending -> REPLACE/done. This bead CLOSES as ruled-and-re-scoped. The surviving capability question belongs to F6c (rf2-drpa3.55), not to F4g.

Freehand publishes precise facts at the semantic seams it already owns. The tooling layer answers questions from those facts, from a minimal live-occurrence index, and from the existing Spec 009 retained ring. What must NOT cross is the donor answer: a cumulative, weak-keyed, HMR-migrated lifetime summary maintained as a second observability system inside the rendering substrate.

REPLACE, not DELETE, is the truer word: something in Freehand does take this job, it just takes less of it, on purpose.

=== REJECTED, EXPLICITLY AND BY NAME ===

Freehand does not grow any of these:

1. A window fold carried from mark-dirty! through to the selected commit. Today the per-window cause/count is discarded when the revision advances, which happens before the render. Carrying it to commit is surgery on the cell.cljc render path.
2. Cell-to-root attribution. VERIFIED 2026-07-25: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc contains exactly TWO occurrences of the string "root", both inside prose docstrings (lines 682, 839). There is ZERO cell-to-root association. root.cljs owns root-ids and live-root registration but nothing binds a cell to one. This would be new plumbing in both files.
3. A lifecycle interval log with proof-gated hide-versus-unmount labels. VERIFIED: Freehand cell/lifecycle is a bare keyword, :new / :connected / :disconnected (cell.cljc:171 init, :187 accessor, :1016 connect, :1062-1065 disconnect). No interval log, no :dead state, no proof annotation. This is the donor honesty machinery and the largest genuinely-new piece.
4. The donor weak-keyed store with its four-generation HMR migration, cause-vocabulary canonicalisation, single-owner claim with rejection-on-conflict, monotonic generation/ABA fence, JVM transition lock, and metadata-stripping value copier.
5. Cumulative render/batch counters, first-to-latest epoch spans, union cause sets, and sampled moving-target unions with identity-exactness flags.

DELIBERATE, ACCEPTED FIDELITY LOSS, named here so nobody later rediscovers it as a bug: lifetime totals; accumulated target samples and their identity-exactness flag; the saturating distinct-omission loss account; cell-to-root proof; hidden-versus-unmounted interval history. If a concrete debugging session later proves ONE of these essential, add THAT single fact at its true owner. Do not import the accumulator architecture to get it.

=== WHY ===

POSTURE. Option A builds three new framework capabilities that no Freehand consumer has asked for, on the render path and the root registry, while F5/F6 work is live on the same files, in order to feed a debugging panel. Building it BECAUSE A LEDGER ROW SAYS MOVE is the ledger driving the product. Cost was sized at 2,500-4,000 lines across three to five PRs, two of them on the render path, sequential against spec/API.md and spec/009-Instrumentation.md (hot-zone).

THE GATE DOES NOT NEED IT. F6d (rf2-drpa3.56) acceptance 1 is arithmetic: "the ledger script reports ZERO undisposed rows." Its own non-goal names "preserving a donor API merely because its implementation proved useful (EP-0036 non-goal)." That sentence was written for exactly this case. A REPLACE disposition satisfies F6d completely.

THIS IS NOT THE PACING ITEM. VERIFIED 2026-07-25 via python scripts/check_donor_inventory.py --report: 203 rows, 161 not yet disposed, 42 disposed. Undisposed by slice F1:23 F2:25 F3:15 F4:7 F5:16 F6:75. By disposition MOVE:115 REPLACE:31 DELETE:15. These two rows are 2 of 161. F6e (rf2-drpa3.57) is blocked by F6a (.53), F6c (.55), F6d (.56) and B5 (.52), all open and all larger. Treating this as critical-path pressure would have been a mistake.

THE LOSS IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. Xray has ZERO Freehand view instrumentation today. Nothing in tools/ requires re-frame.freehand. The Mounted View Evidence panel is already going dark for Freehand apps regardless of what rows 195-196 say. Under this ruling the developer loses nothing they currently have on Freehand; they lose the PROMISE that the donor version would be carried across intact.

THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT. rf2-drpa3.105 (F5i, ui/client.cljs + ui/runtime.cljs) was the same shape one slice over: a MOVE that could not be a MOVE, closed MOOT, rows re-dispositioned REPLACE / PARTIAL-REPLACE against re-frame.freehand.root, with the genuinely-unabsorbed teeth filed as one bounded audit bead (rf2-drpa3.172). Same resolution here.

MARKING THE ROWS done IS HONEST, NOT A DODGE. The ledger defines done for a donor SOURCE file as: "nothing further has to be extracted from that file, and deleting the donor costs Freehand nothing" (spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md, How to read a row). Under this ruling nothing further is extracted from either file: the Freehand tool tier, when it is built, is built from Freehand's own compiler manifest and its own commit records, not from donor code. The donor five projections are a SHAPE REFERENCE, not code to port. The consumer obligation is separately and correctly held by F6-owned rows that stay pending (392 xray viewcell_evidence.cljs, 393 xray reactive_panel_*, 394/395 xray evidence tests, 397 pair-mcp view_tool.cljs) plus the census rule "a row cannot claim done while the code it covers still requires the donor". So the safety net survives the flip.

=== WHAT WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE (2026-07-25) ===

Line counts, measured: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool.cljc 305; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool/evidence.cljc 1049; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/evidence.cljc 594; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc 1073; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs 1738; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs 466.

The Freehand seam EXISTS (blocker 2 of this bead is discharged): cell.cljc:799 set-evidence-sink!, :848 commit-evidence-record (dev-gated, runs BEFORE publication, validates through evidence/commit-record, fails loud), :901 emit-commit-evidence! (dev-gated, runs AFTER publication, throwing sink contained and reported, never rethrown), called from commit! at :1007 and :1040 threading the cell lowering (:interpreted / :compiled) and generation. set-evidence-sink! is a bare last-write-wins slot: no owner claim, no generation, no rejection, default nil. Nothing is retained behind it.

re-frame.freehand.tool STILL DOES NOT EXIST (blocker 3 still true): the only hit for that name in the whole tracked tree is the dangling docstring reference at implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/a11y.cljc:46. structural-manifest publishes no :diagnostics key, so compile-tier a11y findings collect in the compiler env and reach no reader. That gap is rf2-hytu5, already filed.

The two shapes side by side, which IS the whole decision:

Donor re-frame.ui.tool/explain-render, one occurrence:
  {:occurrence 7, :view-id :app.todo/todo-row, :root-id :app/main-root, :connection :disconnected, :lifecycle {:intervals [{:state :connected} {:state :disconnected :reason :activity-hidden :proof :settled-reconnect}] :dropped 0 :exact? true}, :causes #{:subscription :hmr}, :render-count 108, :batches 12, :first-epoch 4192, :latest-epoch 4310, :observations {:targets [...] :identity-exact? true}, :loss {:dropped 64 :exact? false}}

Freehand re-frame.freehand.evidence/commit-record, one selected commit:
  {:schema :re-frame.freehand.evidence/v1, :view-id :app.todo/todo-row, :lowering :interpreted, :occurrence {:parent nil :key 4211}, :generation 9, :projections {:commit {:scope {:committed-generation 9} :basis :observation :complete? true :loss nil}}}

Freehand's record is honest and correct and answers a DIFFERENT question. It says this commit happened, at this generation, and here is exactly how far the claim reaches. It does not say why, how many times, over which epoch span, against which moving targets, under which root, or whether the boundary is hidden or gone. Pointing tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs at it does not degrade Xray, it EMPTIES the panel and trips the version banner. That is what two independent workers found and it is why this was never a MOVE.

Donor accumulator sizing by inspection, for anyone tempted to revisit: bounded value copier + window/cumulative fold ~320 lines (portable, one donor call); weak-store host machinery ~360 (portable in shape, ~120 of it legacy-store migration a fresh v1 does not need); ownership/generation lifecycle ~185 (portable in shape, three one-line seam swaps); the reads, projection + instance-records, ~120 (NEEDS FREEHAND FACTS THAT DO NOT EXIST). Plus tool.cljc: explain-render + mounted-views ~60 lines, the other three projections ~210 lines needing a Freehand manifest registry and reader.

NOT independently re-verified this pass and quoted from earlier bead notes only: the 13,451-line / 12-namespace closure figure, and the elision gate byte counts 744,059 B release vs 794,898 B control.

=== THE ONE PIECE OF THE MIDDLE GROUND THAT IS ACCEPTED ===

A MINIMAL LIVE OCCURRENCE INDEX is warranted, and only for one concrete reason: PAIR ATTACHES LATE. An MCP agent attaches to an already-running app, so a pure fire-and-forget commit sink can never answer "what is mounted right now". read-mounted-views is a shipped tool in skills/re-frame2-pair. That index must contain ONLY current dev-mode occurrences and their latest committed projection, insert-or-update on selected commit, remove on disconnect. It is CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORY: no lifetime counts, no target union, no interval ledger, no weak-store migration, no independent retention knob. Freehand's explicit shell cleanup gives it a natural release seam. This is filed on the tool-tier bead, not here.

=== THE COMPANION RULING (also recorded on rf2-drpa3.55) ===

F6c acceptance 2, "every tool that consumed the donor's instrumentation consumes Freehand's", means AT FREEHAND'S OWN FIDELITY WITH THE DELTA STATED, not at donor fidelity. Under this ruling it must mean the latter or F6c is unsatisfiable by construction.

=== TENSION NAMED, EYES OPEN ===

docs/design/freehand/codex-design.md:1304 (the ratified target design) says "The existing view-manifest, mounted-views, explain-render, view-dependencies, and view-event-sites projections gain lowering and scope/basis/completeness/loss markers rather than forking by execution mode", and D020 says the same. The right reading is that Freehand EVENTUALLY offers those projections sourced from FREEHAND'S OWN FACTS AT FREEHAND'S OWN FIDELITY, not that the donor cumulative accumulator crosses intact. Building them should be triggered by a tool tier being built for TOOL reasons, with each missing fact justified on its own terms, scoped from first principles - never as a port of a 1,049-line donor namespace whose weak-store vintage migration and cause-vocabulary canonicalisation exist only because the donor accreted history across four schema changes. The same codex-design section already rules that mounted occurrence records are LIVE PROJECTIONS and that Freehand adds no second history store, which is consistent with this ruling.

=== FOLLOW-ONS ===

- Ledger edit (rows 195-196 -> REPLACE/done with named replacement and written fidelity delta): rf2-d13hj. Doc-only, parallel-safe, dispatchable NOW.
- Freehand tool tier live reads (minimal live-occurrence index, mounted-views, bounded explain-render over the Spec 009 ring): rf2-lvvl2, sequenced after rf2-hytu5, owned by F6c not F4g.
- Static reader door + manifest :diagnostics: rf2-hytu5, already filed.
- rf2-drpa3.37 closes once rf2-d13hj lands; its only remaining scope was this disposition.

Donor-inventory rows 195-196 go MOVE/pending -> REPLACE/done, replacement named as re-frame.freehand.evidence + the re-frame.freehand.cell commit seam, fidelity delta written into the row. Two independent workers had already verified the MOVE premise false at zero commits; the real question was a scope call on EP-0036, and the answer is no. Rejected by name: window fold carried to commit, cell-to-root attribution, proof-annotated lifecycle interval log, the weak-keyed HMR-migrated store, cumulative counters/epoch spans/target unions. Full ruling with file:line evidence and measured numbers is in this bead notes. Follow-ons: rf2-d13hj (ledger edit, doc-only, dispatchable now), rf2-lvvl2 (Freehand tool tier live reads, after rf2-hytu5, owned by F6c not F4g). title: F4g emission: the evidence schema's control-build production-isolation proof
description:
The F4g evidence schema landed as `re-frame.freehand.evidence` (one versioned occurrence-keyed schema; scope/basis/completeness/loss refused at one door; retention pointed at Spec 009's ring and no store of its own). Its production-isolation criterion asked for the F3d CONTROL-BUILD technique and that is NOT what shipped.

What shipped instead is a require-graph REACHABILITY assertion (`re-frame.freehand.evidence-boundary-jvm-test`): each source file's ns form is read, reader conditionals and all, the graph is walked from the public door, and the schema is proven unreachable. It carries its own positive control. That is the honest available claim today because there is no emission site — the schema is pure values, so there is no evidence code in a bundle to elide.

The moment an emission site lands (a dev-gated call on the render path), the reachability assertion becomes the WRONG one. It must be REPLACED by a control-build probe in the shape of the elision probe pair, not relaxed or deleted. The test's own docstring says this.

Now unblocked in a way it was not: `:freehand-release` exists on main (`npm run build:freehand-release`, out/freehand-release/main.js, genuinely :advanced), so the release side of a probe pair has an artefact.
acceptance_criteria:
- A control build proves evidence/debug code does not survive :advanced with goog.DEBUG false, in the shape of the existing elision probe pair (probe + positive control), not a grep.
- The positive control demonstrably RETAINS what the probe proves absent, so a probe that stopped rooting anything cannot pass.
- `the-evidence-schema-is-not-reachable-from-the-public-door` is REPLACED by the probe rather than relaxed, and its docstring's instruction is honoured.
- No timing assertion anywhere in the probe.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT SHIPPED 2026-07-24 — VERIFIED NOT-YET-PROVABLE. No PR, no code; the honest outcome is that criterion 6 cannot be proven today without proving a WEAKER thing.

re-frame.freehand.evidence is required by NOTHING in implementation/freehand/src (self-refs + one decision doc only). It is unreachable from any render path, and — the decisive point — it is NOT interop/debug-enabled?-gated at all: it is pure values plus validation fns (a door), so there is no gate for a control build to toggle.

MEASURED, using the mandated technique (present/absent discriminators, control build with goog.DEBUG the only variable):
 - out/freehand-release/main.js (goog.DEBUG=false): 705,206 bytes.
 - goog.DEBUG=true control (--config-merge, only the flag changed): 741,967 bytes.
 - In BOTH builds: all 3 present-control tokens present, the absent-control token absent (probe discriminates), and EVERY evidence-schema string literal ABSENT.

So an F3d control-build ELISION probe (probe + a positive control that RETAINS what the probe proves absent) cannot be honestly constructed today: nothing reaches the schema, and there is no debug gate whose flip makes it appear in control and vanish in production. The existing reachability assertion (the-evidence-schema-is-not-reachable-from-the-public-door) remains the correct claim and was NOT replaced, relaxed or deleted. The bundle measurement was NOT shipped as a gate — it would read as satisfying criterion 6 while proving unreachability, a different and weaker thing.

WHAT MUST LAND FIRST: a dev-gated evidence-EMISSION call site on the Freehand render path — which is .167 emission half. So .166 is BLOCKED ON the framework slice below, not dispatchable as written.

title: Virtual-table real-scroll browser test fails locally under concurrent load but passes CI
description:
Reported by the rf2-drpa3.108 worker, which did the right thing and BASELINED before blaming itself.

## The symptom

`npm run test:browser` exits 1 with 4 assertion failures in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_virtual_table_dom_cljs_test.cljs, in `a-real-scroll-moves-the-window...`.

## It is NOT a red trunk, and it is NOT that PR fault

The worker ran the same gate against origin/main freehand tree in its own worktree and got IDENTICAL failures at IDENTICAL line numbers with IDENTICAL totals (671/4115). And CI browser job on main is GREEN — verified independently by the mayor: run 30060439880 ("tests" workflow at cb071f20), job "CLJS (shadow-cljs :browser-test, headless Chromium)" -> success, zero failing jobs in the run.

So the failure is LOCAL ONLY.

## Likely cause

The test drags a REAL SCROLLBAR to a specific offset and asserts the resulting window. That is inherently timing-sensitive, and this machine routinely runs six concurrent worker agents each with shadow-cljs and JVM processes. A scroll-settle that is comfortable on an idle CI runner is marginal under that load.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

EVERY future worker touching the browser lane will hit these 4 failures, and each one must independently baseline against main to discover they are not its fault. That is a real and repeating friction cost — one worker already spent a full gate cycle on it. Worse, a worker that does NOT baseline may either chase a phantom regression or, having seen "browser is always red locally", learn to ignore a gate that is supposed to be authoritative.

## What NOT to do

Do not delete or skip the test — the real-scroll proof is exactly what makes the F5h promotion-parity claim meaningful (interpreted and compiled tables dragged to offset 3200, identical at rest and scrolled). Do not loosen it to accept any window either; that discards the coverage.
The likely honest fix is to make the scroll SETTLE deterministically rather than assuming a fixed delay — await the actual scroll event or poll for the expected offset with a generous bound, so the assertion is about the WINDOW, not about how fast the machine is.

## Acceptance

`npm run test:browser` passes on an idle machine AND under concurrent load, with the real-scroll assertion still asserting the exact window. State how you made the settle deterministic.
notes:
FIXED in PR #6823 (branch worker/scroll-flake-eq2vx, SHA 9124b1ffae). Root cause: the real-scroll assertions asserted the window after a single settle! macrotask; under concurrent load the scroll's async dispatch had not reached app-db, giving the signature scroll-top nil / 25 rows / window unmoved. Fix: new await-settle! helper polls (via test-support/poll-until, 8s bound) the real app-db ::v/scroll-top projection until the dragged offset lands AND the paint commits the expected window, THEN asserts the exact window (unchanged, still exact). Makes the failure UNREACHABLE, not merely unobserved. Applied to both real-scroll tests (a-real-scroll-moves-the-window + promotion-parity). Evidence: post-rebase full test:browser EXIT=0 (695 tests/4267 assertions, 0 failures); scroll test green across 11 consecutive real-browser runs incl one under demonstrable load; delay-injection proof (600ms scroll delay still green, poll waits it out); non-vacuity proof (assert 30 rows reds only that assertion). No production source changed.
RETIREMENT FOLLOW-UP (rf2-pa57v, 2026-07-28). The file this bug names — implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_virtual_table_dom_cljs_test.cljs — no longer exists: rf2-86i64 settled option (a) and PR #7180 + this PR retired the virtual-table pilot's component half. The DELETION does not moot the fix, and the fix was not lost with the file: the surviving FH-CTRL-021 mounted suite (virtual_collection_dom_cljs_test.cljs) drives every real scroll through the same deterministic discipline this bug bought — test-support/poll-until on the app-db ::v/scroll-top projection AND the committed window, never a fixed tick — in its 'settled'/'at-window' helpers. The two migrated element-identity rows added by rf2-pa57v use it too. Nothing here needs reopening; this note exists so the dangling path reference resolves.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #6823 — deterministic scroll-settle (poll the real ::v/scroll-top app-db projection until the async dispatch lands, then assert the exact window). Failure now unreachable, not merely unobserved.

title: Virtual-table pilot cannot restore the scroll state it stores in app-db
description:
PR #6776's virtual-table pilot calls its `scroll-top` app-db entry “restored by time travel like anything else,” but the dataflow is one-way. The viewport's `on-scroll` copies the live DOM `scrollTop` into app-db, and render uses that value to choose the row window; nothing ever writes the stored value back to the viewport.

That makes a restored or programmatically changed state internally inconsistent. If app-db contains 3200 before mount/remount, the view renders r96…r124 at absolute positions around 3072px while the new DOM viewport still has `scrollTop == 0`, so the visible viewport is blank. Time travel on a mounted table similarly moves the rendered window without moving the viewport. The headless rows dispatch `:acme.ui.table/scrolled` directly, and every browser row moves the DOM first with `scroll-to!`, so the claimed reverse direction is never exercised.

This matters to the pilot's headline conclusion: restoring scroll position is host work (normally a ref/behavior or a deliberately imperative seam), and the pilot explicitly uses “no behavior” to justify promotion. Either restoration is outside this component's contract and the state is only a DOM-derived cache, or the compiled/interpreted contract still needs an honest restoration path. Do not infer a general scroll service or virtualization framework from this narrow mismatch.

Deduplication: all-state ledger search for scroll position/offset restoration, remount and time travel found only the closed source owner `rf2-drpa3.45` and an unrelated routing cache issue. Existing `rf2-drpa3.162` owns projection-roster policy, `.163`/`.164` own compiler diagnostics, and in-progress `.51` owns B4 per-keystroke evidence; none owns DOM restoration.
design: Keep the resolution at the viewport boundary. A cache-only ruling is valid; a restoration implementation should use the smallest existing host lifecycle seam and acknowledge that a behavior requirement affects compiled promotion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rule and document whether the table's app-db scroll entry is a DOM-derived cache or controlled/restorable state.
- If it is cache-only, remove the time-travel/restoration claim and ensure stale retained state cannot make a fresh viewport render a remote window at DOM offset zero.
- If it is restorable, a real-browser regression seeds or restores a non-zero offset before mount/remount and proves the viewport `scrollTop`, rendered row window and app-db value agree; cover both execution modes or explicitly rule and document the mode cost.
- Preserve the pure window arithmetic and ordinary user-scroll path. Add no general scroll registry, measurement protocol, virtualization service or grid framework.
- The proof must be discriminating: it must fail when the DOM write/restoration step is removed, rather than moving the DOM first as the current browser tests do.
notes:
RETIREMENT FOLLOW-UP (rf2-pa57v, 2026-07-28). The pilot this bug is against is gone — rf2-86i64 settled option (a), and the component half plus all four pilot_virtual_table* files are deleted. The RESOLUTION outlived it, promoted and hardened:

- ':restore-scroll?' (opt-in, off by default, the table a DOM-derived cache otherwise) is NOT ported. PR #7180 ported the seam itself as re-frame.freehand.collection/reconcile-scroll — the same guarded ':layout' write of one property on one node — but ':scroll-offset' is now CONTROLLED with NO opt-out. One prop, one meaning; the un-reconciled mode is the blank-viewport bug rather than a lighter configuration of the same idea.
- The close reason's 'restoration is interpreted-only — attaching a behavior forfeits compiled promotion' is SUPERSEDED and was already stale when written: the compiled grammar admits the behavior form, and virtual_collection_compiled.cljc carries reconcile-scroll through the promoted vertical.
- The two discriminating regressions live on, stated POSITIVELY, in virtual_collection_dom_cljs_test.cljs: fh-ctrl-021-a-non-zero-offset-is-restored-onto-a-fresh-viewport and fh-ctrl-021-a-state-only-offset-move-drags-a-mounted-viewport.
- The third — the cache-only CONTROL (without-restoration-a-seeded-offset-leaves-the-viewport-at-zero) — was deliberately NOT migrated. It existed to indict the un-reconciled mode, and there is no such mode left to contrast with; migrating it would have preserved a test of something that no longer exists.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6834 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6834). Chose the restorable branch: opt-in :restore-scroll? wraps the viewport in a :layout v/behavior that writes the persisted offset back before paint (:connect on fresh mount, :update on a state-only move). Restoration is interpreted-only — attaching a behavior forfeits compiled promotion, which the docs now acknowledge; the default table stays a compilable DOM-derived cache and the compiled twin + parity suite are untouched. Three discriminating browser regressions (seed-before-mount, time-travel-on-mounted reverse direction, cache-only control) plus a mutation probe that reds exactly the two restore suites when the DOM write is removed.

title: Runtime select-multiple verdict still misses safe-spread callers and source order
description:
PR #6778 added the correct empty-array rule for a native `<select multiple>`, but the compiled React emitter settles `multi?` only from build-time attributes. A runtime-valued `:multiple` is excluded by `build-time-attr?`, so this compiled body:

    [:select {:multiple (:flag props) :value nil}]

currently lowers to `compiled-react/attr!` calls that pass `false` for both attributes. When `:flag` is true, the emitted props therefore contain `multiple=true` with scalar `value=""`; the interpreted emitter sees the same runtime map and writes the required empty JS array. React reports the multiple-select value-shape error, and the compiled declaration cannot reliably clear the selection.

This contradicts #6778's cross-mode claim and its source-owner close note that a computed `multiple` decides what EMPTY means. It remains present on current main. The exact emitted-form probe produced:

    (compiled-react/attr! ... :multiple (:flag props) false)
    (compiled-react/attr! ... :value nil false)

Deduplication: all-state ledger search found only `rf2-9g159` (the closed #6778 owner) and `rf2-b6poy` (in progress). `rf2-b6poy` owns the analyzer refusing a LITERAL collection value; it explicitly scopes itself to that literal-value corner and does not own the runtime `multiple` verdict. Do not expand or update that locked in-progress Bead.
design: Carry the whole-element multiple-select verdict at render time whenever the `multiple` value is dynamic, using a once-bound value shared by the `multiple` prop write and the nil-value normalization. Preserve the current build-time constant path for fully literal declarations.
acceptance_criteria:
- A `{:compiled true}` view with runtime-valued `:multiple` writes a JS empty array for an explicitly present nil `value` when the runtime flag is true, and the empty string when it is false, matching the interpreted view.
- The exact and normalized alias spellings (`:multiple` / `:x/multiple`, `:value` / `:x/value`) reach the same result.
- Each authored runtime expression is evaluated once per render; deriving the verdict must not duplicate a reactive read or arbitrary expression.
- A focused compiled-browser or equivalent host-level regression proves clearing and no React multiple-select value-shape diagnostic; an emitted-form assertion proves the runtime verdict reaches the `value` write and is non-vacuous.
- Keep collection acceptance scoped to the existing select-value rule. Do not add a form model, public verb, general collection attribute grammar, or absorb `rf2-b6poy`'s literal-analyzer work.
notes:
PR #6781 audit (2026-07-24): this owner also covers the new `v/spread` lowering. `compiled-react/spread!` computes controlledness from the forwarded map but calls `put-attr!` without the map's runtime multiple-select verdict, so `(v/spread {:multiple true :value nil})` still writes the scalar empty string instead of React's required empty array. A fix scoped only to direct dynamic props would be incomplete: reuse one runtime verdict for the direct and spread paths and include a focused compiled/interpreted spread regression. The separate `#id`-sugar residue is already owned by rf2-ll1ah.
PR #6820 AUDIT REOPEN (merge b2ba950e39bb5efdfd24acca1fc6678342457d30): direct runtime props and whole-map v/spread are fixed, but two coupled runtime-verdict gaps remain.

1. SAFE-SPREAD SPLIT MAP (current-main public JVM proof):
   (tree/render [:select (v/spread-safe {:value nil} {:multiple true})])
   => {:tag :select, :attrs {:multiple true, :value ""}, :rf.ui/tree-version 1}
   The alias pair {:x/value nil}/{:x/multiple true} is likewise scalar-empty. Keeping both facts owned is the positive control and yields :value [].

Cause: structural node/element and interpreted react-props settle multi? over owned attrs before folding caller; compiled caller-spread! also folds the guarded caller after owned writes and put-caller! uses put-attr!'s false-default arity. :multiple is legal in a spread-safe caller (only key/ref/value/checked and owned handler families are denied), so the final element can be multiple=true after its owned nil value was irreversibly normalized as a single-select string. Both modes therefore hand React the wrong shape.

2. DIRECT REACT EVALUATION ORDER (exact emitted-form proof): for authored attrs {:value (mark! :value), :multiple (mark! :multiple)}, the ordinary/interpreted two-entry map evaluates [:value :multiple]. The shipped React form binds (mark! :multiple) in the outer let before its first attr! write evaluates (mark! :value); measured string positions 184 vs 385. It still evaluates once, but promotion changes observable order and diverges from the structural emitter. This follows directly from hoisting dyn-multi ahead of every dynamic write.

Bounded repair: settle one whole-element multiple verdict over owned/dynamic plus the already-guarded safe caller before nil normalization, threading it through structural, interpreted React, and compiled caller folds. Bind dynamic authored expressions once in their existing host/map order (and the caller expression after owned expressions), then derive the verdict and write; do not special-case reads or add a form model. Pin exact+alias safe-spread output/browser shape and an evaluation-order/count oracle.

Dedupe: full all-state scan found no other spread-safe/multiple owner. rf2-9g159 is the closed parent feature; rf2-sf9n5 is the exact runtime-verdict owner already expanded once for v/spread. rf2-b6poy is closed and owns only literal collection admission; it was not edited.

Other #6820 work is clean: runtime Hiccup is refused through the shared D010 child classifier; slot value and args evaluate once in source order before the gate. Exact range passes diff-check; no review discussion; all required CI checks passed. Current full Freehand JVM suite is green at 875 tests / 6293 assertions, so these cases are uncovered rather than baseline failures.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6847 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact runtime-verdict owner; no duplicate.

PR #6847 correctly brings a safe-spread caller into the multiple-select verdict, but it ORs caller and owned sources before applying v/spread-safe's owned-wins law. Reproduced on the merged main lineage in BOTH interpreted and compiled structural modes:

    [:select (v/spread-safe {:value nil :multiple false} {:multiple true})]
    => {:attrs {:multiple false, :value []}}

The final emitted `multiple` is false because owned wins, so the owned nil value must normalize to the scalar empty string, not the multiple-select empty collection. The exact-key probe proves the defect without relying on alias representation. The alias variant (`:x/value` / `:x/multiple`) also shapes the value as `[]`; its structural tree additionally exposes the caller/owned spellings separately while the React prop slot remains owned-false.

The React paths have the same cause: interpreted `react-props` calls `multiple-select?` over attrs + caller as an OR, and the compiled emitter ORs the caller into `mverdict` even though `caller-spread!` later refuses to overwrite an already-owned `multiple` slot.

Bounded repair: derive the verdict from the EFFECTIVE `multiple` source after safe-spread precedence — an owned multiple-slot declaration wins even when false; consult the caller only when the owned props do not declare that slot. Pin exact + normalized-alias forms across interpreted/compiled structural and React/browser paths, retain the caller-only true and owned-true controls, and preserve once-only/source-order evaluation. No form model or broader forwarding abstraction.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6863 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact owner; no duplicate.

The owned-false fix is correct, but new `controlled/multiple-declared?` treats lexical key PRESENCE as ownership even when the owned value is nil. That conflicts with the existing nil-is-absent attribute law: node/attr-entry and react/put-attr! drop an ordinary `:multiple nil`; the later safe-spread caller therefore legitimately writes its `:multiple true`. The verdict nevertheless stayed false and normalized the owned nil value as a single-select empty string. Direct current-main proof in both interpreted and compiled structural modes:

  [:select (v/spread-safe {:value nil :multiple nil} {:multiple true})]
  => {:tag :select, :attrs {:multiple true, :value ""}}

The final emitted element is multiple=true, so React requires the empty collection/array, as the owned-silent control already proves. The same cause applies when a dynamic owned multiple expression evaluates to nil/undefined and in both React paths: put-attr! leaves no owned property, then put-caller! writes the caller. Derive precedence from the EFFECTIVE emitted source: owned false remains a real written decision and wins; owned nil/undefined is absent and hands the verdict to the caller. Pin exact and alias spellings, literal and dynamic nil, structural and React/browser outputs, while preserving once-only/source-order evaluation.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6863 (merged, commit 853efbdd1b) with cluster-siblings .164/5r1af — select-multiple owned-wins verdict fixed across structural/interpreted/compiled. Stale-open from close race.

title: Make the Freehand release build runnable and representative
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-07-24 on evidence from the rf2-drpa3.52 investigation.

## The gap

implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names exactly ONE Freehand build: :node-test-freehand. There is NO production/release build of the Freehand artefact.

Consequence: any evidence or gate that needs to measure SHIPPED cost — bundle bytes, parse/eval, reachability, elision — has no artefact to point at. rf2-drpa3.52 (B5 shipped cost) is blocked outright on this, and it is not a test gap: there is nothing to measure.

## What is needed

A release build id for the Freehand artefact (:advanced, goog.DEBUG=false), matching how the sibling artefacts declare theirs, plus whatever :dev-http/entry wiring the existing release builds use.

## Hot-zone warning — READ BEFORE DISPATCHING

implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is HOT-ZONE: sequential, never parallel. Build ids and :dev-http ports for testbeds live in that same file, so any other dispatch touching it must be sequenced, not run alongside.

## Do not over-build

This bead is the BUILD ID and its wiring only. Do not write the B5 probes here — that is rf2-drpa3.52, which unblocks the moment this lands. Keeping them separate keeps the hot-zone occupancy as short as possible.

## Acceptance

A Freehand release build exists, produces an artefact, and is reachable from the npm scripts the way sibling release builds are. State the build id and the produced path so rf2-drpa3.52 can target it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Replace both retired registrations with the shipped `rf/reg-event` shape, returning explicit `{:db ...}` effects.
- Rebuild the exact advanced `:freehand-release` bundle and load it in a real browser against `#app`; both interpreted and compiled counters mount at 0, a click advances the intended counter, and no page/console error occurs.
- Preserve the pinned advanced/goog.DEBUG=false configuration, output path, npm entry, and test-only source location outside the published artefact.
- Keep shipped-cost measurement/reporting in rf2-drpa3.52; this repair only makes its input artefact truthful.
notes: PR #6787 audit: the new release entry is not a runnable representative app. `release_app.cljs` invokes removed `rf/reg-event-db` stubs twice at namespace load; each unconditionally raises `:rf.error/reg-event-db-removed`, so `-main` and the claimed mount path are never reached. Rebuilt the exact `:freehand-release` target and loaded `out/freehand-release/main.js` in headless Chromium with `#app`: the page raised an error and the body remained empty. Current HEAD still has both calls. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate; rf2-drpa3.52 is blocked on the repair.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6814 (ca9d791940). REAL audit finding, worse than the bead stated: release_app.cljs had THREE load-time defects each masking the next under :advanced — reg-event-db x2 (removed stub, threw first), reg-sub :-> sugar (does not exist in this project's subs.cljc), and NO adapter installed (make-state-container threw). Fix: both reg-event-db -> reg-event returning {:db ...}; reg-sub -> layer-1 (fn [db _] (:count db)); -main installs (rf/init! uix/adapter) — uix chosen because the app is INTERACTIVE (a plain-atom adapter mounted both counters but did not bridge dispatch to a React re-render, so clicks left the counter at 0). Build config/output path/npm entry/test-only location unchanged; no B5 probes added. VERIFIED IT RUNS not just builds: rebuilt the advanced bundle, served it, loaded main.js against a real #app in headless Chromium, asserted on the DOM — both counters mounted at 0, clicking dispatched ::bump and both re-rendered to 1, zero pageerrors. Unblocks rf2-drpa3.52 with a truthful artefact.

title: F5: delete the dead compiled-mount machinery in freehand/compiler/root.cljc, re-anchor the build JVM tests, fix stale docstrings, re-row the F0c ledger (fn mount door RATIFIED)

title: A compiled key-condition map with a v/event branch cannot render on the structural host
description:
Found by the rf2-berc2 / rf2-51d4q worker (PRs #6780/#6781). Pre-existing since PR #6769; reported rather than folded in, correctly, because it is LOUD rather than silent and therefore outside that waves defect class.

## The defect

A key-condition map carrying a v/event branch throws on the structural host:

    :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed — "carries a scalar at [\"Enter\"]"

classify-event map arm runs the non-data walk over branches, and a Callback record is not data. Affects BOTH modes.

## Why it matters despite being loud

It means NO SSR AND NO HEADLESS RENDER for that form. A key-condition map with a v/event branch is a perfectly ordinary thing to write — PR #6769 deliberately lowers exactly that branch through (events/callback :event (fn ...) 1) so it classifies :event and dispatches — so the form is sanctioned by the compiler and refused by the structural host. That is the same shape as the bug rf2-drpa3.154 fixed on the behavior-command channel: the substrate admits a spelling its own structural host will not render.

## Likely fix direction, to be verified not assumed

node/classify-event now records {:rf.ui/opaque :v/event} for a whole-handler roster callback (fixed in #6780). The map arm needs the equivalent treatment for a BRANCH value — recognise a Callback inside a key-condition branch as opaque rather than walking it as data. Confirm against the merged #6780 shape before implementing.

## Acceptance

[:input {:on-key-down {"Enter" (v/event [e] ...)}}] renders on the structural host in BOTH modes, with the branch recorded opaque rather than walked as data. Prove it on the JVM structural path, not only in the browser.

## Sequencing

Touches node.cljc and possibly compiler/analyze.cljc — sequence against any analyze.cljc holder.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — merged PR #6809 (2026-07-24), correctness + completeness + implementation-quality finding.

The acceptance half is real: a v/event key branch now renders structurally and records {:rf.ui/opaque :fn}. But node/key-branch widened the same treatment to every fn-carried? value: bare functions and every Callback role. That contradicts the already-closed branch grammar in events/branch-plan, which admits only an event vector, branch options, v/event, or nil and refuses v/handler, v/render-fn, v/raw-fn, bare functions, and nested key maps.

Current-main reproduction:
  (tree/render [:input {:on-key-down {"Enter" (v/handler [e] nil)}}])
  (tree/render [:input {:on-key-down {"Enter" (fn [_] nil)}}])
Both return a clean structural tree with the Enter branch recorded as {:rf.ui/opaque :fn}. The live event planner rejects each with :rf.error/view-bad-event / :name-one-intent-per-key-branch. Thus SSR/headless render and structural tests bless declarations the browser event path refuses. The PR comment that both front ends had already policed the grammar is false for the interpreted structural walk: tree/with-attrs reaches node/element and classify-event directly.

The same direct path also demonstrates why a second local roster is fragile: mixed string/keyword maps, branch-local :once, and nested key maps are recorded as data even though events/event-plan already has the exact closed-form diagnostics (the branch-option subset is the contract previously delivered by rf2-drpa3.150). Keep this one owner: those are manifestations of the same skipped planner, not separate feature requests.

Bounded correction: preserve the new positive v/event behavior, but validate/classify the map with the existing events/event-plan contract before projecting its branches into the structural value. Do not add a new grammar, validator framework, callback role, or compatibility path.

Acceptance:
- v/event branches still render in interpreted and compiled structural paths and record the mode-neutral opaque marker.
- At minimum v/handler and a bare-function branch are refused structurally with the existing typed event category, matching the live planner; use the existing planner so its already-closed mixed-map, one-level, and branch-option roster cannot drift here again.
- A data branch remains recorded verbatim.
- The negative proof exercises tree/render directly, because that is the path the missed upstream-validation assumption left unguarded.
close_reason: PR #6860 — FIXED (audit-reopen scope). node/key-branch over-widened opaque to every fn-carried? branch. classify-event now validates the whole key-condition map through the shared events/event-plan -> branch-plan before projecting, so v/handler / bare fn / v/render-fn / v/raw-fn / nested key map / branch-local :once / mixed map are refused with the planner's typed :rf.error/view-bad-event; key-branch opaques only a callback? (v/event). Negative proof via tree/render directly, id-for-id with event-plan. v/event-positive + nested-non-data rows still pass.

title: #id sugar is silently dropped on an element carrying v/spread
description:
Found by the rf2-berc2 / rf2-51d4q worker (PRs #6780/#6781) while building the structural coverage check that catches this defect class. NOT fixed there, deliberately — the remedy needs a design call.

## The defect

analyze-element-props spread branch returns :attrs [], so:

    [:div#x (v/spread attrs)]

LOSES THE ID in BOTH compiled emitters, while BOTH interpreted walks keep it. Silent, cross-mode, no diagnostic.

## Why it was not fixed in that wave

The conflict semantics are a design call, not a determinable fact. The pair is "#id sugar" versus "a runtime :id inside the forwarded map":
 - the INTERPRETED tier THROWS on that pair;
 - the COMPILED tier CANNOT SEE IT at build time, because the forwarded map is a runtime value.
So compiled cannot reproduce the interpreted refusal, and the question is what it should do instead. Options include: keep the sugar id and let a runtime :id win or lose by a stated rule; refuse the COMBINATION at build time (sugar + spread on one element) as unprovable; or defer the conflict to a runtime check inside the fold.

## Related, already ruled

rf2-huf81 settled the sibling question — the #id sugar CONFLICT is judged on PRESENCE, not truth, so a nil-valued #id gets one verdict in every mode. Whatever is decided here should be consistent with that.

## Acceptance

[:div#x (v/spread attrs)] behaves the SAME in interpreted and compiled modes, with the chosen conflict rule stated in spec/004-Views.md and pinned cross-mode. Silence is not an acceptable outcome in either mode.

## Sequencing

Touches compiler/analyze.cljc — a contended file. Sequence against any other analyze.cljc holder.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, DEFERRED by the rf2-7x0ge worker (PR #6809) — a genuine RULING coupled to a fenced file, so nothing implemented and the exploratory analyze.cljc change reverted. KEY FINDING: the interpreted refusal of the conflict pair (#id sugar + a runtime :id in the forwarded map) is a RENDER-TIME guard (in tree.cljc/react.cljs, on the emitted id SLOT, on PRESENCE), not build-time — so BOTH tiers CAN judge it at render where the merged map exists. RECOMMENDED OPTION A (runtime refusal, presence-based, in the shared fold): both modes throw identically. Consistent with rf2-huf81 (id conflict is an ambiguity REFUSED not ranked) and its presence-not-truth rule extended to a forwarded map; keeps the legitimate no-:id case (the reported drop) working. Option B (spread later-arg-wins so forwarded :id wins) is defensible but RANKS an ambiguity the rest of the grammar refuses. WHY NOT LANDED NOW: Option A enforcement must land in BOTH compiled emitters render folds and the React half is in compiled_react.cljs (fenced at the time). Land coordinated once free, pin the rule in spec/004-Views.md. The pre-existing drop is unchanged, not worsened.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6863 (2026-07-24) — exact owner remains OPEN; updated, no duplicate.

PR #6863 correctly refuses the discriminating conflict `[:div#sugar (v/spread {:id "a"})]`, but it threads `sugar-id` into `node/spread-attrs` only to CHECK the conflict and still returns the forwarded map without restoring the sugar when no forwarded id exists. Direct current-main proof:

  interpreted [:div#sugar (v/spread {:class "c"})]
  => {:tag :div, :attrs {:id "sugar", :class "c"}}
  compiled
  => {:tag :div, :attrs {:class "c"}}

With an empty spread, interpreted retains `{:id "sugar"}` while compiled has no attrs. Both compiled structural and compiled React share the omission: analyze's spread branch records no literal sugar-id attr; emit_jvm hands only the spread map to node/element; emit_react hands only that map to spread!. The new acceptance control asserts merely `map?`, so it stays green while the id is absent. Preserve the now-correct sugar+forwarded-id refusal, then make the accepted no-id spread retain the sugar id in both compiled emitters. Pin exact tree/props value, not mere non-throwing.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6867 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6867). node/spread-attrs now restores the surviving #id sugar onto the forwarded map when the id slot is free, so compiled structural + compiled React retain the id exactly as the interpreted walk does; the sugar+forwarded-id refusal is preserved. Acceptance strengthened from map? to an exact-tree cross-mode pin. Verified: JVM 901 tests / CLJS 963 tests, 0 failures.

title: Compiled tier refuses a literal collection value on a multiple select
description:
Fenced residue relayed by the rf2-9g159 worker (PR #6778), which correctly did NOT cross into a file another worker held.

## The defect

compiler/analyze.cljc rejects a LITERAL collection attribute value with :rf.ui.compile/collection-attr-value BEFORE either emitter runs. So:

    [:select {:multiple true :value ["a" "b"]}]

fails to compile in a {:compiled true} view while rendering correctly in the interpreted tier. That is a mode divergence of exactly the kind rf2-9g159 set out to remove: a compiled declaration refusing what its interpreted twin renders.

## Scope of the fix

ONE widening of that guard, to admit the <select> value slot. Everything the compiled tier can currently reach is already proved by #6778 (computed selection and computed multiple both work) — this is the literal-value corner only.

## What NOT to do

The rf2-9g159 worker wrote select-value branches in emit_jvm and emit_react and then REVERTED them rather than ship dead code, because the analyze.cljc guard makes them unreachable. Do not re-add emitter branches without first widening the guard, or you will ship code nothing can reach. Widen the guard first, then confirm which emitter branches are genuinely needed.

## Sequencing

compiler/analyze.cljc is a CONTENDED file — several beads want it. Sequence against any other analyze.cljc holder rather than dispatching in parallel.

## Acceptance

[:select {:multiple true :value ["a" "b"]}] compiles and renders the same selection in BOTH modes, proved cross-mode. Sets remain refused (no cross-host order) — that refusal is deliberate and must survive.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6791 (analyzer-parity cluster). See the PR body for the per-bead detail and the four judgement calls the worker recorded.

title: A console-watching assertion may be vacuous: React validates select value shape at mount only
description:
Found by the rf2-9g159 worker (PR #6778) IN ITS OWN TEST, before shipping — and the same shape may already be on main.

## The mechanism

React 19.2 validates a <select> value shape at MOUNT ONLY, not on update. validateSelectProps never fires on a controlled->cleared transition.

The worker first wrote its browser test as exactly that transition, and it STAYED GREEN against a DELIBERATELY WRONG empty value. It dumped the captured console to confirm React emitted nothing at all, then restructured the test to mount the empty selection FIRST — at which point it correctly reds, capturing React own "must be an array if multiple is true" line.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed there

The worker flags that the PRE-EXISTING assertion fh-input-003-an-explicit-nil-clears-the-live-node ALSO watches console.error across a TRANSITION, and "may be carrying less weight than it appears to". That test is on main. If React does not validate on the update path, that assertion may be structurally unable to fail — a test that has never been able to detect the thing it names.

## What to do

Determine whether fh-input-003 can fail at all. The method the worker used is the right one and is cheap: feed it a DELIBERATELY WRONG value and require RED. If it stays green, the assertion is vacuous and must be restructured to mount the invalid state rather than transition into it.

Then sweep the browser suite for SIBLING assertions that watch console output across an update rather than a mount — the same blindness applies to any of them.

## The general rule worth capturing in the fix

An assertion that depends on a HOST library emitting a warning inherits that library WARNING POLICY, including when it declines to warn. Before trusting such a test, prove it reds on known-bad input. A console-watching test that has never been shown to fail has not been tested.

## Acceptance

fh-input-003 (and any sibling found by the sweep) is either proven to red on known-bad input, or restructured so that it can. State which, with the red output quoted.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6784 (71d529e22d). VERDICT: fh-input-003 is NOT vacuous, and this bead's proposed remedy would have BROKEN it. Proven both ways — dropping the nil :value slot (the exact emitter defect it names) reds it with React's own controlled-to-uncontrolled diagnostic; dropping the nil :checked slot reds it identically. The TRANSITION shape is REQUIRED, not incidental: React 19.2 raises that diagnostic only from updateProperties comparing lastProps against nextProps, so no mount can raise it. validateSelectProps is the mount-only one; the two are OPPOSITE, and that distinction is now written into the test. REAL DEFECT FOUND UNDERNEATH: didWarnControlledToUncontrolled is a PAGE-GLOBAL ONE-SHOT and the browser suite is one page of 657 tests, so an earlier consumer silences the later assertion. Added a control declared LAST that drives a genuinely uncontrolled field and requires the complaint; proved the hazard by injecting a latch consumer ahead of the clearing row (clearing row goes silently green, control reds with Captured: []). SIBLING SWEEP: one real find in the same file (the multiple-select row's trailing console assertions — React's select update branch has no controlled/uncontrolled complaint at all); reasons rewritten, conclusions kept. Two mount-path watches reported but not rewritten (no evidence against them, outside this bead).

title: Controller schemas admit nil values that the public verbs reject as missing
description:
## Problem

PR #6766 publishes v/controller-key, v/controller-revision, and v/controller-current? as the supported controller surface, but its public value contract disagrees with the implementation at nil.

The normative prose and public docstrings say the control address is caller-supplied immutable EDN and the reset revision is any EDN. The PR's own public component schemas spell both as :any. In Malli, :any admits nil. The implementation instead treats nil as absence: controller-key with {:control nil} raises :rf.error/view-control-address-missing; controller-revision with {:reset-key nil} raises :rf.error/view-control-reset-revision-missing; controller-current? nil nil is false.

That creates a public door whose advertised/example schema accepts a value that the same view rejects only after entering its body. Nil is also a natural initial revision when a caller reads an uninitialised counter, so this is not an exotic value-domain dispute.

## Deliverable

Choose one contract and make every layer say it. The smallest likely ruling is non-nil addresses and revisions: state that explicitly, use public component schemas that reject nil, and make the diagnostics say nil is invalid rather than claiming the prop was absent. If nil is intended as legitimate EDN instead, the fence must distinguish an unstamped record from an explicit nil generation without turning nil-equals-nil into accidental currency. Do not add controller machinery or a new API.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004, the three public docstrings, generated API docs, and exemplar/library props schemas agree whether nil is legal for :control and :reset-key.
- Public tests cover absent, explicit nil, a non-nil scalar, and a non-nil collection on both hosts.
- If nil is forbidden, schema validation and the controller verbs reject it under an accurately worded contract; no schema accepts a value the view body later calls missing.
- If nil is allowed, controller-current? distinguishes an absent stamp from an explicit nil stamp and both read/write fences remain identical.
- Existing sharing, rejection-by-equal-value, stale-write, door-only, manifest, and compiled/interpreted proofs remain green.
- No registry, sentinel exposed to authors, compatibility alias, or additional public verb is introduced.

Correctness probe on current main: {:nil-control {:error :rf.error/view-control-address-missing}, :nil-revision {:error :rf.error/view-control-reset-revision-missing}, :nil-current false}. Later edits to these files only add t/with-render and behavior-release documentation; the contradiction remains current. Deduplicated across all Bead states. Closed rf2-drpa3.122 owns publication, while closed rf2-3dfp1 concerns detecting value-derived revisions and does not own nil/schema legality.
NOT DELIVERED — the overlay/controller worker STOPPED on the api-manifest fence. Returned to OPEN. What it established first-hand (probe run on its own checkout, not inherited): an explicit nil and an ABSENT prop are INDISTINGUISHABLE — {:nil-control :rf.error/view-control-address-missing, :absent-control :rf.error/view-control-address-missing, :nil-revision :rf.error/view-control-reset-revision-missing, :nil-current false}, same id and same "was rendered with no" wording for both.

IT ALSO CORRECTED THE BEADS FRAMING: props_schema.cljc holds schemas as INERT DATA — nothing validates a value. So [:control :any] is a documentation/catalogue claim, not a runtime gate; "schemas that reject nil" is a notational change (:any -> :some) and the SUBSTANCE is the diagnostic wording.

ITS RECOMMENDED RULING, which I endorse: nil is NOT legal for :control or :reset-key, and that is CONSISTENT with the two prior presence-vs-value rulings rather than in tension with them. rf2-huf81 (presence not truth) and rf2-drpa3.125 (an explicit nil control VALUE is a present value, returned as a map entry) both forbid a truthiness test standing in for a presence test WHERE THE VALUE DOMAIN LEGITIMATELY CONTAINS FALSEY MEMBERS — an empty checked really is false. The controller case is the mirror image: the value domain of an ADDRESS and of a GENERATION EXCLUDES nil. v/controller-current? already rules exactly this — it exists because (= nil nil) is true, so an unstamped record would read as current — and record-key would otherwise collapse every address-less controller onto one record keyed by nil. title: The compiled for-body refusal names the wrong problem and omits the fix
description:
FOUND BY THE F5h VIRTUAL-TABLE PILOT (rf2-drpa3.45). Cheap, and it cost a
build cycle to work out.

## The finding

A windowed row needs the record beside the index, and the natural Clojure
spelling is a `let` in the loop body:

    (for [i (range start end)]
      (let [r (nth rows i)]
        [:div {:key (:id r) …} …]))

Compiled, that is:

    for body must be a keyed element/view/fragment — got let. Keyed lists
    compile to direct JS arrays; missing key = build failure

Two problems.

1. IT REPORTS A MISSING KEY WHEN THE KEY IS PRESENT. The row is keyed —
   one form deeper. The real rule is that a compiled `for` body must be
   an element / view / foreign / fragment DIRECTLY, with nothing between,
   and the message never says so.
2. THE RECOVERY LADDER DOES NOT CONTAIN THE FIX. `unkeyed-list-item`
   ladders to `[:key-each-row :extract-declared-child]` — "give every row
   of the list a :key" is advice the author has already taken. The actual
   fix is `for`'s `:let` MODIFIER, which the analyzer fully supports:

    (for [i (range start end) :let [r (nth rows i)]]
      [:div {:key (:id r) …} …])

   It is arguably the more idiomatic spelling anyway, which is what makes
   the omission worth fixing rather than arguing about.

## Acceptance

1. A `for` body that is a `:let` (or any admitted wrapper) is refused
   with its OWN sentence — the body must be the keyed node itself — and
   not with a missing-key sentence.
2. The ladder for that case names the `:let` modifier as a recovery, with
   the spelling.
3. A `for` body that genuinely has no key keeps the message it has.
notes:
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-07-24 — RAISED P3 -> P2 on the posture bar. This is squarely "excellent ergonomics and low friction": a pilot hit it writing the NATURAL Clojure spelling (a let inside a for body to bind the record beside the index), the refusal named the wrong problem, omitted the fix, and cost a build cycle to work out. A diagnostic that misdirects an author writing idiomatic code is exactly the friction the posture targets, and the fix is cheap — correct the message and name the recovery. Not minutiae; underpriced at P3.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6791 (2026-07-24) — reopened this exact diagnostic owner; no duplicate Bead.

The new `wrapper-body-ops` branch classifies every analyzed `:let` / `:letfn` / `:if` / `:case` body as `:rf.ui.compile/indirect-list-body` without checking that it actually wraps a keyed row. Reproduced on current main:

    (for [x xs] (let [y x] (str y)))

Actual: `:rf.ui.compile/indirect-list-body` and “this body is a let wrapping [a keyed node]”, followed by the `for :let` recovery. There is no row or key anywhere in that form. This contradicts the original acceptance that a body carrying no row keeps the general `unkeyed-list-item` answer, and the new sentence states a fact the analyzer has not established.

Keep the useful direct-wrapper diagnosis for the motivating keyed-row case, but either inspect through the wrapper before claiming a keyed node exists or make the wrapper sentence honest for both shapes. Add the wrapped-scalar counterexample beside the existing bare `(str x)` control.
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-07-24: audit reopen is ACTIONABLE (a real over-refusal introduced by the #6791 fix, not minutiae). Surface is compiler/analyze.cljc — HELD by the compiled-emitter cluster worker (rf2-drpa3.130/.133/sf9n5). Re-dispatch the moment that PR merges, clustered with the queued rf2-5r1af (same analyze.cljc surface) and rf2-ll1ah.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6837 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact owner; no duplicate.

The scalar-wrapper counterexample is fixed, but the new `wraps-markup-node?` proves only that a markup node exists, while `:rf.ui.compile/indirect-list-body` still says that wrapper contains "the keyed node." Direct reproductions on merge cdd55ad97cbbd38f1fc59fe7677f2a2552081423:

    (for [x xs] (let [y x] [:li y]))
    (for [x xs] (if x [:li x] (str x)))

Both return `:rf.ui.compile/indirect-list-body` and claim the body wraps the keyed node, although neither `[:li ...]` carries `:key`; the mixed branch does not even always render markup. An author following the one-step recovery gets another build failure for the missing key. This is the same diagnostic-honesty/low-friction acceptance, not a new feature.

Make the wrapper sentence honest for markup that may be keyed or unkeyed (or actually prove the key before claiming it), and add an unkeyed-markup wrapper plus a mixed markup/scalar branch beside the scalar control. Keep the bounded direct-wrapper guidance; do not build a general AST explanation engine.
close_reason: PR #6863: the indirect-list-body wrapper diagnostic no longer claims the wrapped markup is keyed — it names only the markup one form deeper (what wraps-markup-node? proves) and states keyedness as a requirement of the row node, so keyed and unkeyed markup wrappers get the same honest message; scalar wrappers still keep unkeyed-list-item. Docstrings corrected. Tests: keyed==unkeyed wrapper message equality, mixed markup/scalar branch, scalar controls.

title: [bug] A metadata key is silently dropped interpreted and a build failure compiled
description:
FOUND BY THE F5h VIRTUAL-TABLE PILOT (rf2-drpa3.45), on the first try —
it is the spelling a Reagent-shaped hand reaches for.

## The finding

    (v/defview meta-keyed [{:keys [xs]}]
      [:ul (for [x xs] ^{:key x} [:li x])])

INTERPRETED, this renders and the key is GONE:

    [{:tag :li, :children ["a"]} {:tag :li, :children ["b"]}]

No `:key`, no `:keyed?`, and no diagnostic — the structural tree carries
no metadata contract (004B: "no metadata-carried contract"), and nothing
on the interpreted path looks for one. The list is silently unkeyed, and
the only symptom is React's own console warning at run time plus a keyed
reconciler that reuses the wrong rows.

COMPILED, the identical source is a hard build failure:

    missing :key on the for body — every list row needs a literal :key
    prop (unkeyed list items are a build failure)

So one spelling means "quietly unkeyed" in one mode and "will not build"
in the other. For anyone arriving from re-frame v1 / Reagent — where
`^{:key …}` IS the spelling — that is a migration trap with a delayed,
misattributed symptom.

## Why the compiled message does not close it either

It says "missing :key", and the author's eye goes to a line that HAS a
key. The sentence an author needs is the one about metadata: keys are a
props slot, `{:key …}`, in both modes.

## Acceptance

1. `^{:key …}` on a child is a LOUD refusal on the interpreted path too —
   `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` naming metadata and the props-slot
   spelling — so the two modes agree about the same source, or a ruling
   that metadata keys are honoured in both.
2. The compiled `unkeyed-list-item` message names metadata explicitly
   when the offending form carries `:key` in its metadata, rather than
   reporting a key as missing when one is present a level away.
3. The migration guide says it once, plainly.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6791 (2026-07-24) — reopened this exact metadata-key owner; no duplicate Bead.

The PR correctly relayed, but did not assign, a surviving public-door example at `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1005`:

    ^{:key (:id r)} (v/slot row r)

That metadata is attached to a SEQ call form. Interpreted evaluation returns the slot value without the call form's metadata, so the new vector-only `node/refuse-metadata-key!` guard cannot see or refuse it. Reproduction on current main: metadata on an evaluated call is nil and `tree/render` returns an unkeyed `{:tag :li ...}` node. The compiled source path likewise must not be assumed to rescue a spelling the public doc teaches as common-mode.

Replace the source docstring example with the already-established keyed fragment spelling, `[:<> {:key (:id r)} (v/slot row r)]`, and make any broad “metadata is always refused” wording distinguish markup-vector metadata from metadata on an evaluated call if necessary. Keep generated/manual API docs in sync; the current docs page already shows a keyed props form, so avoid regressing it from the stale source.
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-07-24: audit reopen is ACTIONABLE (a real over-refusal introduced by the #6791 fix, not minutiae). Surface is compiler/analyze.cljc — HELD by the compiled-emitter cluster worker (rf2-drpa3.130/.133/sf9n5). Re-dispatch the moment that PR merges, clustered with the queued rf2-5r1af (same analyze.cljc surface) and rf2-ll1ah.

title: A stale batching claim survives in a live diagnostic and two docstrings
description:
Found by the rf2-drpa3.123 worker (PR #6774) while correcting the same claim in spec/004-Views.md. The spec half is fixed; these three sites still carry it.

## The stale claim

Three places assert that a forwarded caller vector at a controlled :on-input "takes the SYNCHRONOUS door interpreted and BATCHES compiled" — i.e. that promotion moves the field between lanes. THAT IS NOT WHAT THE LIVE COMPILED TIER DOES.

compiler/emit_react.cljc element-facts emits {:tag :controlled? :slot} as compile-time CONSTANTS, and reactive/event-site hands those plus the RUNTIME handler value to events/site, which asks controlled/door? at COMMIT with the role read off the actual value. A forwarded vector therefore classifies :event-vector and the door opens — in BOTH modes.

The analyzer :sync? fact is consumed only by the site record (manifest evidence) and by compiler/emit_cljs.cljc handler-flags — and emit_cljs has NO CALLER on the v/defview path (freehand.cljc routes {:compiled true} to compile-structural-view -> emit_jvm + emit_react). It survives only via root.cljc emit-inline.

## The three sites

1. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/analyze.cljc — the :rf.ui.compile/controlled-input-async-handler message says "so it stays on the ordinary batched path". This one is USER-FACING and therefore the important one.
2. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field.cljc — docstring.
3. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc — docstring.

## What is NOT wrong

The advisory is still RIGHT TO FIRE. Forwarding costs the site its STATIC EVIDENCE — the site is opaque, the intent is absent from the manifest, and nothing is assertable before it fires. That is a real loss and worth a diagnostic. It simply names the wrong CONSEQUENCE. Do not delete the advisory; correct what it claims.

## Acceptance

The diagnostic message and both docstrings describe the actual consequence (loss of static site evidence), not a lane change. If a test pins the current wording, flip it in the same change.

## Sequencing

Touches compiler/analyze.cljc, which is a CONTENDED file. Sequence against any other analyze.cljc holder rather than dispatching in parallel.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6791 (2026-07-24) — reopened this exact stale-batching owner; no duplicate Bead.

The PR corrected the three originally enumerated sites but explicitly relayed a fourth that is still present on current main: `spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md:807` says `:rf.ui.compile/controlled-input-async-handler` means the handler “misses the controlled-input sync door” and even names the donor spelling `(ui/event …)`. For Freehand, the runtime handler still opens the door at commit; what is lost is static evidence, and the common-mode spelling is `v/event`.

Update that warning-table row to the shipped opacity/evidence semantics and the Freehand vocabulary. Keep donor re-frame.ui documentation out of scope unless its own runtime semantics are independently shown stale.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6867 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6867). The 3 originally-enumerated sites were already corrected by #6791 on current main; this fixes the 4th site the audit relayed — the 004D controlled-input-async-handler warning-table row now states the shipped opacity/evidence semantics (door opens at commit; static site evidence lost) and uses the Freehand v/event spelling.

title: Re-check top-layer generation ownership during the ordered flush
description:
## Problem

PR #6753 makes a detached top-layer ref generation withdraw its pending operation before the microtask flush, but the ownership fence disappears once the flush starts. `flush-top-layer!` resets `pending` to nil and copies each entry into `[node fact]`, dropping its owner before it invokes any host call. If an earlier ordered host call synchronously causes a later generation to retire, `retire!` can no longer see the in-flight snapshot and the later stale operation still runs.

Top-layer calls have synchronous callback seams, including `beforetoggle`, and Freehand permits plain handlers. A focused real-Chromium probe used two connected ordered popovers; the first host call synchronously retired the second ref. The required call log was `[:first]`; current main produced `[:first :second]` and failed by name. The probe was then removed byte-clean.

This violates FH-TOPLAYER-004's generation-ownership law at the exact publication boundary: a generation that has already let go can still open or close its node before paint.

## Deliverable

Keep generation owner/currentness available through sorting and re-check it immediately before each `apply-desired!`. Retirement during an earlier host call must invalidate a later in-flight entry, while a successor's claim on the same node remains live. Keep document order, the single microtask batch, and zero retained registries/listeners/observers. A local owner token/current-node reading is sufficient; do not add a general cancellation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a real browser, two connected top-layer entries are queued in document order; the first host call synchronously retires the second generation, and the second host call does not occur.
- Removing the at-publication owner/currentness check fails the named test with `[:first :second]`.
- A predecessor retiring during the flush cannot cancel a successor's claim on the same node.
- Existing document-order, composed-ref release, selected-commit advisory, repeated-state no-op, and zero-retention proofs remain green.
- No registry, observer, timer, supervision layer, or public API is added.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6753 (completeness / correctness / implementation quality): deduplicated against closed source Beads rf2-drpa3.114 and rf2-drpa3.115 plus every ledger state. Those Beads prove retirement before the flush and typed selected-commit advisories; neither owns retirement after the flush has snapshotted and discarded owner identity. Focused browser probe: 638 tests / 3791 assertions, exactly one expected failure in audit-a-generation-retiring-during-the-flush-does-not-act; expected [:first], actual [:first :second]. Temporary probe/config edits were removed and the worker tree restored clean. The advisory half of #6753 is complete and needs no follow-up.

Highlights: .157 replaced a js-obj seen-key table (every Object.prototype name read as present, so the FIRST row keyed toString/constructor/__proto__ was refused) with a js/Set; .158 confirmed react-dom 19.2's defaults are TWO-TIER and the delegate replicated only the production tier, now gated on interop/debug-enabled? exactly where React gates on __DEV__, with no private import and no stack parser; .160 found the guard gated loop ENTRY only and now re-reads ownership INSIDE the drain; .156 split the refusal into direct and token-scoped events with idempotence asserted as byte-equal app-db across a duplicate.

title: Preserve React development diagnostics when root callbacks are omitted
description:
## Defect

PR #6765 makes host error callbacks late-bound by always installing custom React root delegates. That fixes callback replacement, but it also replaces React's defaults even when an application never supplied a callback. The fallback is only `reportError(error)` for uncaught/recoverable failures and `console.error(error)` for caught failures, and `host-callback-delegate` discards `error-info` on that arm.

With the pinned React DOM 19.2.0 development build, those are not the full defaults. `defaultOnUncaughtError` reports globally and emits the component/error-boundary guidance warning; `defaultOnCaughtError` logs the throwing component plus the boundary/recreation context. The new delegate suppresses both development diagnostics. A fresh root with no callbacks regresses immediately, and A -> omitted on remount does not “restore React's own default reporting” as the public mount docs and Spec 004C claim. Production reporting is mostly equivalent; the programmer-facing development evidence is what is lost.

## Completeness gap

The browser proof covers A -> B for caught/uncaught and omitted -> B for uncaught. It never exercises supplied -> omitted/default for any key, so the false restoration claim is untested. Its recoverable arm proves only the initial hydration callback reaches the cell; it does not prove a remount advances or removes that callback.

## Bounded correction

Keep the small stable-delegate design and callback late binding. Make the no-callback arm preserve the useful semantics of the supported React development default, including component-stack/boundary context and uncaught guidance, using the public `error-info` supplied to the delegate (or another bounded mechanism). Exact private React strings are not required and private React internals must not become a dependency. This is root error reporting, not a general logging framework.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state and the durable ledger for React defaults, root error callbacks, onCaughtError/onUncaughtError/onRecoverableError, component stack, console warnings, and removed callbacks. rf2-drpa3.139 owns late binding and is closed by #6765; no existing issue owns the default-diagnostic regression.

## Origin

Completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6765 at merge commit `fdad3ad983450f60ecb29d0182bea7abda3523d3`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A fresh development root with no authored callbacks retains global error reporting plus useful React-equivalent caught/uncaught component context and guidance; installing the stable delegates does not reduce the default diagnostic to the bare Error.
2. After a callback is removed by an accepted remount, the next matching failure uses that same default path and never calls the stale callback.
3. A -> B replacement still calls only B, with no duplicate default report; recoverable callbacks are proven to advance and to fall back after an actual hydrate-then-remount path while the framework hydration-mismatch signal remains composed.
4. Focused real-browser coverage exercises caught, uncaught, and recoverable supplied -> omitted arms against the installed React 19.2 development build.
5. The repair adds no public API, private React import, component-stack parser, or generalized logging/options framework.

title: Use a prototype-free seen-key table for compiled browser loops
description:
## Defect

PR #6762 implements duplicate-key checking for compiled browser `for` sites with a plain `(js-obj)` and `goog.object/containsKey`. In the pinned Closure library used by ClojureScript 1.12.145, `containsKey` is `key in obj`, so inherited properties count as present. A valid first key such as `"toString"`, `"constructor"`, `"hasOwnProperty"`, or `"__proto__"` is therefore rejected as a duplicate before any row with that key has been seen.

The JVM/structural `node/keyed-run` uses a Clojure set and accepts these first occurrences, so a view can pass structural tests and fail when browser-mounted. These are realistic domain identifiers, not malformed input.

## Bounded correction

Use a prototype-free seen table or an own-property membership test while preserving React-string coercion (including the intended collision between `1` and `"1"`). Keep this a tiny internal dev-time check; do not introduce a generalized key registry or public API.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state and the full JSONL ledger for duplicate key, keyed list, prototype, toString, containsKey, and JS object key. No existing issue owns this compiled-browser divergence.

## Origin

Correctness and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6762 at merge commit `847ad222fa3e90546b4fe92aba2763d4875ed0a5`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. At a compiled browser `for` site, the first occurrence of `"toString"`, `"constructor"`, `"hasOwnProperty"`, and `"__proto__"` is accepted and rendered.
2. A repeated occurrence of each still raises `:rf.error/ui-duplicate-key` at that list site.
3. React-string-equivalent keys such as `1` and `"1"` still collide exactly as the structural tier specifies.
4. Focused browser coverage proves agreement with `node/keyed-run`; the correction remains internal and allocation-conscious, with no new public API or generalized registry.
