title: Compiled browser lowering emits createElement; 004D says jsx/jsxs
description:
## Context

rf2-drpa3.113 landed the compiled tier's browser lowering (`re-frame.freehand.compiler.emit-react` + `re-frame.freehand.compiled-react`). It builds every element with `react/createElement` and VARARG children.

Spec 004D says the React lowering 'generates direct `jsx`/`jsxs` calls for the browser' (Two emitters; The lowerings a compiled declaration carries).

## Why createElement was chosen

A dynamic child in a compiled body is a runtime value the compiler cannot classify — forwarded `:children`, a seq, text, nothing. It is spliced through the interpreted walk's own child classifier so a compiled parent hands React the same child sequence its interpreted twin does. React treats a vararg run and a single array child differently (identity, and the dev-time key expectation), so routing a spliced run through `jsx` would give the element a key expectation its interpreted twin does not have, on markup neither author wrote.

## The decision needed

Either:
(a) SPECIALIZE — emit `jsxs` for the arms whose children are wholly compile-known (no splice is possible there, so the question does not arise), keep `createElement` varargs for the spliced arms. The emitter already computes constancy per subtree, so the split is available. Note `jsx`/`jsxs` take `key` as the third argument, not in props.
(b) AMEND 004D to describe what the browser lowering actually targets and why.

Also in scope for (a): the donor's per-slot rf= memo comparator, which this slice deliberately did not build (the compiled tier binds the props MAP with the host's own destructuring — one props ABI across both modes — so there is no host props object to read slots off).

## Not a correctness bug

Cross-mode DOM parity is proven green over FH-STRUCT-007 in `compiled-mount-dom-cljs-test`.
close_reason: Subsumed by #6762 (.113): the 004D reconcile changed the browser-lowering description from jsx/jsxs to createElement-with-vararg-children, matching the shipped emitter. The discrepancy this bead flagged no longer exists.

title: Fence typeahead replies against the latest token before query reuse
description:
PR #6749's typeahead says every keystroke supersedes older work by token, but the reply handler only compares a reply token with `:in-flight`. Typing increments the record's current `:token` without retiring that older in-flight entry, so the old reply is still accepted until the newer debounce fires.

The query-text freshness check then turns that window into visible corruption. Deterministic reproduction on current main:

1. type `"a"` and fire its debounce (token 1 is in flight);
2. type `"an"`, then return to `"a"` before either newer debounce fires (the record has advanced past token 1);
3. deliver token 1's reply.

Expected: the obsolete reply is inert because newer user input superseded it. Actual: it is accepted, clears `:in-flight`, stores its results as answering `"a"`, and those stale results become visible because the current query happens to be `"a"` again. A temporary headless regression failed exactly once: 20 tests / 79 assertions, expected no visible results, actual the two token-1 results. The probe was removed cleanly.

This contradicts the pilot's own Race 3/4, R-C1 and R-C4 claims, but the repair is deliberately small: a reply must still name the record's current token, or typing must invalidate the older in-flight claim immediately. Keep the event-layer debounce and its traceability; do not add timer cancellation handles, a resource dependency, transport policy, or a debounce framework.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for typeahead supersession, token, same-query return, obsolete answers, stale typeahead results and replies during the debounce window. No existing owner was found; rf2-drpa3.44 is the pilot that introduced and is gated by this evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic JVM/headless regression drives `a` → token-1 request → `an` → `a` before a newer due event, then delivers token 1; the reply is inert and no stale result becomes visible merely because query text matches again.
- The same row proves non-vacuity: a due/reply for the latest token lands and becomes visible normally.
- A reply is accepted only when its token is both the claimed in-flight request and still current for the control; typing or clearing the query supersedes older work immediately enough that the debounce window has no acceptance gap.
- Existing debounce cancellation, distinct-query supersession, retry, release, correlation, caret, mid-word settle and real-clock browser rows remain green.
- State and intent remain ordinary traceable data. No cancellation handle, hidden timer/channel, resources coupling, transport abstraction, public API or generalized async-control framework is added.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6810 (30fdd805f8). Reproduced the stale-reply race on unpatched main as a headless row: typed a (token 1, request out), then an (token 2) and a (token 3) WITHOUT firing either newer debounce, then delivered token 1's reply — it was ACCEPTED, :results-for stored a, :results became [amir anna], and the status sub rendered 'Amir Haddad' as a visible suggestion because the current query was a again. FIX makes the in-flight slot AUTHORITATIVE: typed now dissocs :in-flight as it mints the new token, so existence and identity are one question with one answer — the request token is stamped into the slot it wrote, dropping the slot drops the token, and a reply for a superseded token finds no standing claim and is inert. Revocation is on the KEYSTROKE not the next timer, so no acceptance gap. No cancellation handle, hidden timer, resources coupling, transport abstraction, public API or async framework added. Non-vacuity: inverted the :results-for drop assertion, reds naming the test, restored byte-identical.

title: No test throws from inside a v/behavior child — the seam that lost its attribution shipped green
description:
## Gap

Commit 9813443123 fixed `behavior-component`'s occurrence seam — it was calling `(eb/note-failing-view! view-id)` with one argument, so a genuine throw from a behavior's decorated child was REPLACED by an arity error before re-throw, destroying the attribution that seam exists to record.

It shipped green and sat on main long enough to red the clj-kondo gate for every open PR touching the lint surface (rf2-0qdue). clj-kondo caught it; the test suite did not, and the test suite is where it should have died.

## Why the suite missed it

`interpreted-component`'s occurrence seam is covered — a throw from a declared view's body is attributed to that view. `behavior-component` has the same seam and no equivalent coverage: nothing in the freehand suite throws from inside a `v/behavior`-decorated child, so the catch arm was never executed.

That is the same class of hole for every boundary that owns an occurrence seam. `error-boundary` should be checked for the same gap while someone is in there.

## Deliverable

A regression test that throws from the child of a `v/behavior` and asserts the attributed failure names THAT child's view-id — not the behavior, not nil, and not an arity error. The assertion must read the attribution (`attributed-failure`), because 'something threw' passes on the broken code too.

Consider whether every occurrence seam can be enumerated and driven from one table rather than covered one boundary at a time — the value here is the class, not the single arm.

## Origin

Found while diagnosing the inherited clj-kondo red on PR #6746 (rf2-drpa3.111).
close_reason:
DUPLICATE of rf2-drpa3.128, which was filed earlier and is ALREADY IN FLIGHT with a worker.

⚠️ CLOSING THE BEAD, KEEPING THE INSIGHT — this filing was SHARPER than mine on the point that decides whether the test is worth anything:

  "the bead asks for the attribution assertion (attributed-failure naming the child view-id, since SOMETHING THREW PASSES ON THE BROKEN CODE TOO)"

That is exactly right and my own .128 did not say it. The arity bug REPLACED a genuine throw with an arity error — so a test asserting merely that an exception escaped would have passed against the defect. The assertion must name the FAILING VIEW ID, or it re-creates the same false green in a new place.

It also widened the scope correctly: error-boundary carries the same hole, and "the value is the class of hole, not the one arm."

Both points have been relayed directly to the in-flight .128 worker. Recorded here so the reasoning survives the dedupe rather than dying with the duplicate.

title: Support controlled native multiple-select values in Freehand
description:
PR #6745 correctly keeps explicit nil controlled slots present, but its shared empty-value table maps every native `value` slot to the single-value empty string. A native `<select multiple>` has a different React contract: its controlled `value` must be an array.

Today both useful states are unavailable through Freehand's paved API:

- `[:select {:multiple true :value ["a"] ...}]` is rejected as `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`, because the ordinary attribute grammar rejects every collection before the React boundary;
- `[:select {:multiple true :value nil ...}]` is normalized to `value=""`, and React reports that a multiple select's value must be an array.

That makes an ordinary native SPA control impossible to use as a controlled Freehand element. The fix should be one narrow host-element exception: retain an ergonomic Clojure data value in author/structural space and convert it to React's required array shape only at the React boundary. Do not broaden the general attribute grammar, add a form model, introduce a wrapper component, or create public API.

Evidence on current main: a temporary real-browser regression made the vector-valued element fail with `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` and emitted React's multiple-select value-shape diagnostic for explicit nil (591 tests / 3430 assertions, one asserted failure plus the browser warning). The same vector is rejected by `re-frame.freehand.tree/render` on the JVM. The probe was removed after reproduction.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for “multiple select”, “select multiple”, “multi-select”, “multiselect”, and “controlled select”; there were no matches. `rf2-drpa3.119` owns compiled-door slot aliases, `rf2-drpa3.120` owns scalar controlled nil on the React path, `rf2-drpa3.125` owns structural retention of scalar explicit nil, and `rf2-drpa3.24` owns synchronous door membership. None owns the collection-shaped value contract of a native multiple select.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a real browser, an interpreted native `<select multiple>` accepts an authored Clojure vector of scalar option values, selects exactly those options, and emits no React value-shape diagnostic.
- An explicitly present nil value clears every selected option while keeping the node controlled; it reaches React in the empty array shape React requires and emits no controlled/uncontrolled or multiple/array warning.
- The normalized `:x/value` spelling follows the same rule as `:value`; compile-time and runtime-controlled-slot decisions do not diverge.
- Compiled and interpreted declarations agree where the compiled host is available, and the structural representation retains ordinary data rather than leaking a JavaScript array.
- Existing single-select/input nil behavior (`""`), checked nil behavior (`false`), door membership, caret/IME/contention coverage, and malformed ordinary collection-valued attributes remain unchanged.
- The implementation is scoped to the `value` slot of native `<select multiple>` and adds no general collection attribute grammar, form/controller abstraction, public verb, diagnostic category, or compatibility mode.
notes: MAYOR NOTE 2026-07-24: PR #6768 shipped the two SIBLING beads from this cluster (rf2-huf81 and rf2-drpa3.125) but NOT this one — there is no multiple-select commit on that branch. Deliberately left open rather than closed on the cluster merge: a merged PR citing a cluster does not mean every bead in it landed. The worker had not reported at merge time, so this may still be in flight; verify before re-dispatching.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6778 (d06e2f7df1). Acceptance of a collection value is keyed on TAG + EMITTED SLOT only, never on 'multiple', so a compiled declaration cannot refuse what its interpreted twin renders; the EMPTY value is what consults multiple, settled once per element. Sets are refused (no cross-host order) — deliberate. Also fixed the JVM serialiser, which matched a select's whole :value against each option and therefore marked NOTHING selected for a collection (~25 lines outside the bead's stated scope, taken because shipping a structural value the serialiser silently mis-renders would have been a half-fix). Gates all EXIT=0; six non-vacuity probes reverted the SOURCE rather than inverting an assertion, proving each test both runs and detects the bug. Residue filed: rf2-b6poy (compiled tier still refuses a LITERAL collection value — one guard widening in analyze.cljc, fenced at the time) and rf2-kynqa (React validates select value shape at mount only, so a console-watching transition assertion may be vacuous).

title: Honor Root Manifests for empty Freehand server renders
description:
PR #6740 makes `v/hydrate-root` decide whether to discover the Root Manifest by inspecting the container first. `server-rendered?` returns true only for an element child or non-blank text; when it returns false, `hydrate-root` immediately takes the client-render fallback and never reads an adjacent manifest.

That conflates two valid states:

- a client-only first load: empty container, no manifest;
- a server-rendered view whose result is empty: empty container, manifest present.

The second state is part of Freehand's ordinary model: a declared view may explicitly return nil (`re-frame.freehand.tree-views/nothing` is an existing conformance/test declaration), and the SSR emitter treats nil as an empty render. The adjacent Root Manifest is the exact evidence that distinguishes it from a client-only load.

Real browser reproduction on current main: plant an empty container followed by the real `re-frame.ssr.manifest/script-html` wire form carrying root id `:fh.root/empty-from-the-wire` and prefix `"empty-srv-"`, then call `v/hydrate-root` with the existing nil-rooted interpreted view. Expected an adopted root under the manifest identity. Actual: `root/hydrated?` is false and the descriptor carries the client-derived `:re-frame.freehand.tree-views/nothing` id. The temporary regression produced exactly two failures in 564 tests / 3297 assertions and was removed byte-identically.

Keep the correction small: manifest presence must prove that an empty DOM is a server render, while an empty container with no manifest must retain the current low-friction fallback. Do not add a new public verb, mode flag, root identity option, diagnostic id, or general SSR state machine.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state for empty server renders, nil-root hydration, manifest/fallback ordering, and server-rendered empty containers. `rf2-drpa3.104` owns the shipped manifest-consumption slice, `rf2-drpa3.112` owns the future Freehand server-render path, and `rf2-drpa3.109` owns preflight rollback. None owns this misclassification.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real browser fixture hydrates an existing nil-rooted Freehand view into an empty container immediately followed by the real SSR Root Manifest wire form. It reports `hydrated?` true, registers the manifest's deliberately non-derived root id with `:root-id-provenance :manifest`, and claims the manifest's identifier prefix.
- The same empty container without a manifest remains the client-only fallback: `hydrated?` false, derived identity, no SSR artefact required, and ordinary teardown.
- Non-empty server markup without a manifest still fails before React with the existing `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid` `{:missing :manifest}` diagnostic; an actually required but absent SSR artefact still uses `:rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing`.
- Matching and divergent non-empty hydration, node-identity adoption, prefix uniqueness, root registry cleanup, and the FH-ROOT-006/007 rows remain green.
- The implementation uses manifest presence as the server-render evidence and adds no public API, configuration switch, diagnostic category, compatibility branch, or polling mechanism.
notes: MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-07-24: I closed this prematurely — PR #6812 is NOT yet merged (6 checks still pending at the time; the merge refused with recompute lag). Returned to in_progress. The fix is correct and the PR is green-tracking; close it properly when #6812 actually reaches state==MERGED. The close reason above stands as the record for when that happens.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6812 (c25078470c). hydrate-root used (if-not (server-rendered? dom-node) ...) so an EMPTY container took the client-only fallback before any manifest was read, dropping an adjacent real Root Manifest. FIX: manifest PRESENCE is now the server-render evidence — hydrate-root peeks :ssr/discover-root-manifest; a present manifest adopts (empty or not); an empty container with no manifest keeps the client-only fallback; the two error cases preserved. Localized to hydrate-root's dispatch in root.cljs. Reproduced empirically: reverting only the dispatch reds exactly the 5 adoption assertions. MERGED VIA --admin past the off-surface eq2vx scroll flake (diff has 0 refs to pilot_virtual_table; main green on that test; the only failing job was browser-test failing only on the 4 known-flake assertions).

title: Nothing throws from inside a v/behavior child — an arity bug shipped green
description:
FILED SEPARATELY so it survives rf2-0qdue closing. 0qdue is the ARITY BUG (fixed in PR #6748). This bead is the TEST GAP that let it ship and stay hidden.

## The evidence

`note-failing-view!` is `[thrown view-id]`. The behavior occurrence seam called it with ONE argument, in the `thrown` position. Because that call sits INSIDE the catch, a genuine throw from a behavior-decorated child would be REPLACED BY AN ARITY ERROR before re-throw — destroying the exact attribution that seam exists to record.

It shipped green. It was then discovered INDEPENDENTLY BY THREE SEPARATE WORKERS in one session — the controlled-input follow-ups, the ref-composition slice, and the dropdown pilot — each finding it as a build warning or a lint error, none finding it as a test failure.

THREE INDEPENDENT DISCOVERIES OF ONE ONE-TOKEN BUG IS A SIGNAL ABOUT COVERAGE, NOT ABOUT THE BUG.

## The gap

NOTHING THROWS FROM INSIDE A `v/behavior` CHILD anywhere in the suite. The error path of the behavior boundary is unexercised, so a defect on it can only surface as a static warning — which is exactly what happened, three times, before any test noticed.

## The deliverable

A test that throws from inside a `v/behavior` child and asserts:
1. the failure is ATTRIBUTED TO THE FAILING VIEW, not to the boundary and not to `unknown-view`;
2. the seam does NOT itself throw while a render throw is already unwinding — the arity bug's actual runtime consequence;
3. the error boundary above it receives a well-formed report with the closed egress field set intact (safe summary, opaque exception, capped stack — never app-db or event history).

Cross-host where the contract is cross-host. Non-vacuity: the test must RED against a reverted arity (one-arg call), so it demonstrably catches the class of defect that motivated it.

## Why it is worth doing rather than closing as fixed
The repair is already on main. What is not on main is any reason to believe the NEXT defect on this path would be caught. Every other error-boundary property in this programme is pinned by a test that fails when the property breaks; this one is pinned by three humans noticing a compiler warning.

## Non-goals
Auditing every error path in the substrate. Re-testing what FH-ERROR-001..003 already cover. This is one uncovered path, closed deliberately.
close_reason: Merged via #6751 (behavior-throw attribution test).

title: Keep explicit nil Freehand control values on the STRUCTURAL host
description:
Follow-on finding from rf2-drpa3.120 (PR for rf2-drpa3.119/.120).

rf2-drpa3.120 repaired the INTERPRETED React emitter: an explicitly present `value`/`checked` with a nil value on a supported native control now reaches React as the controlled EMPTY value (`""` / `false`) rather than being dropped under the generic nil-attribute law. `re-frame.freehand.controlled/empty-control-slot` owns that narrow normalization.

The STRUCTURAL host still drops it. `re-frame.freehand.node/dyn-attr-entry` folds an author-space attribute through `attr-entry`, which answers nil for a nil value, so `(tree/render [:input {:value nil :on-change [:e]}])` carries NO `:attrs` at all — verified in the .120 worker worktree by an assertion that failed with `(not (contains? nil :value))`. The compiled JVM emitter reaches the same builder.

Consequences to weigh when this is ruled:
- the two hosts now disagree about one declaration — React is handed a controlled empty node, the structural tree reports an element with no value attribute;
- SSR/hydration is the sharp edge: a server render that omits the attribute and a client render that sets `value=""` is a hydration seam;
- the door itself already agrees across both modes (it reads KEYS, never values), so this is purely the emitted representation.

rf2-drpa3.120's worker could not repair it: `node.cljc` and `tree.cljc` were fenced to a concurrent slots-grammar worker, and the bead scoped itself to the interpreted React emitter.

Scope when dispatched: decide whether the structural tree should carry the authored nil (presence, matching the key-presence law) or the same controlled-empty projection React takes, then apply it at the ONE canonicaliser both structural modes reach. No new diagnostic id; reuse the controlled-input vocabulary already in `re-frame.freehand.controlled`.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6768 (e94d5f5eef): explicit nil control values are preserved on the STRUCTURAL host. An explicit nil is a PRESENT value, not an absence — the distinction the empty-control-slot map-entry design exists to protect.

title: A reusable controlled input must own its event site or lose the compiled door — record the shape in 004
description:
FOUND BY THE F5f PILOT (rf2-drpa3.43). Not a bug; a design consequence a library author cannot discover from the docs and will get wrong.

THE FACT. The compiled site proof is STATIC. analyze/analyze-handler classifies a bare symbol at a handler position :dynamic; controlled/compiled-role maps :dynamic to :dynamic; controlled/door? admits only :event-vector / :event-options / :event. So a library input spelled the obvious way —

    (v/defview field [{:keys [value on-input]}]
      [:input {:value value :on-input on-input}])   ;; caller supplies the whole vector

— takes the SYNCHRONOUS door interpreted (the runtime sees a vector) and BATCHES compiled. That is precisely the promotion parity break D009 says must not exist, arrived at not by a substrate divergence but by an author's choice of spelling.

THE THREE SPELLINGS AND WHAT EACH COSTS:
a) forward the caller's vector — intent-as-data at the site YES, extra dispatch NO, static compiled door NO.
b) library-owned LITERAL site carrying the caller's vector as an argument — door YES, data YES, one extra dispatch per keystroke.
c) (v/event [e] (conj on-input (.. e -target -value))) — door YES, no extra dispatch, but the site is :opaque so intent is no longer assertable as data.

The pilot ships (b): [:input {:value value :on-input [:acme.ui.field/changed on-input ::v/value]}] with a library event that re-dispatches. Proven in a real browser (19 keystrokes, no drops) that the extra hop rides inside the synchronous drain, so (b) costs correctness nothing.

004D already says 'the shape a reusable library input uses to append its live payload to an event prefix received through props' — but it does not say WHICH shape, and the natural reading is (a), which is the one that loses the door.

ASK: one short normative paragraph in 004 (Controlled inputs) or 004D naming (b) as the paved library spelling, stating the cost of (a) explicitly, and — if the owner wants it — a compile-tier WARNING when a :dynamic handler sits on a controlled element, which is a mechanically detectable near-miss.

OWNING SPEC: 004-Views / 004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6774 (24d5f55ff4) — AND it corrected the bead's own premise. The claim that a forwarded caller vector 'takes the synchronous door interpreted and BATCHES compiled' is FALSE of the live compiled tier: element-facts emits tag/controlled?/slot as compile-time constants and events/site asks controlled/door? at COMMIT off the runtime value, so a forwarded vector classifies :event-vector and the door opens in BOTH modes. 004's 'One predicate, both modes' paragraph drew the right conclusion from that dead inference; the worker rewrote the REASON and kept the conclusion (the compiled tier bakes NO verdict — a stronger form of the same guarantee). The .123 shape is recorded honestly: forwarding costs the site's STATIC EVIDENCE, not the lane. Residue in the live diagnostic and two docstrings filed as rf2-pv0ne.

title: Give nil-valued #id conflicts one verdict in every Freehand mode
description:
## Problem

PR #6738 (merge 7ca79cc797d168ba4e9f0c6c73be55f413b6ce3c) extends the `#id` shorthand conflict guard from exact `:id` to every authored key that projects onto the emitted `id` slot. Spec 004B rules `#id + :id` as an ambiguity removed by the grammar.

The compiled and interpreted implementations ask different questions when that authored value is nil. `analyze-literal-props` scans `(keys m)`, so the exact and qualified forms fail with `:rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict`. The structural and React walks guard on `(some? raw)`, so those same forms are accepted and emit only the sugar id. Adding `{:compiled true}` to a view can therefore turn an accepted declaration into a compile error.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compare interpreted and compiled structural rendering for:

    [:div#sugar {:id nil}]
    [:div#sugar {:x/id nil}]

A temporary JVM regression produced exactly two failures in 616 tests / 4308 assertions. Interpreted rendering returned `{:tag :div :attrs {:id "sugar"}}`; compiled rendering returned `[:rejected :rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict]` for both rows.

## Expected Behavior

Authored id presence has one verdict at the compiled analyzer, structural walk, and React walk. Keep the repair at the existing guard and reuse its diagnostics. This is not a general aliasing or duplicate-attribute framework and does not reopen the no-sugar ruling in rf2-5r1af.
acceptance_criteria:
- `[:div#sugar {:id nil}]` and `[:div#sugar {:x/id nil}]` receive the same rejection verdict in compiled and interpreted structural emission.
- The interpreted React path applies the same presence rule, including a runtime nil value, and reuses `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`; compiled emission continues to reuse `:rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict`.
- Existing non-nil conflict rows remain rejected, while shorthand-only and no-shorthand controls remain accepted and nil attributes elsewhere remain omitted.
- Focused JVM, CLJS, and browser rows prove the exact and qualified forms without adding a new diagnostic or a general alias/deduplication subsystem.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6768 (48cb86c004): the #id sugar conflict is now decided on PRESENCE, not truth, so a nil-valued #id gets one verdict in every Freehand mode. This is the presence/truth-collapse distinction the controlled surface already relies on elsewhere.

title: Reject reserved key and children entries in Freehand props schemas
description:
PR #6737 states in Spec 004D and `re-frame.freehand.props-schema` that `:key` and `:children` are reserved call-ABI slots and are never props-schema entries. The public `v/defview` macro nevertheless accepts a literal schema such as `[:map [:key :string] [:children [:vector :any]] [:id :int]]`; `v/describe` publishes it verbatim and `props-schema/declared-keys` returns `[:key :children :id]`.

Those contracts are impossible to honor: `:key` is stripped before props delivery, while a map-carried `:children` is rejected by `normalize-call` because children must be trailing forms. Catalogue/editor/agent tooling can therefore advertise props callers and view bodies can never exchange.

A temporary JVM expansion regression expected both reserved entries to fail at declaration time; both currently returned `no-throw` (606/4205 clean baseline; 608/4208 with this two-row probe plus the separate opaque probe produced exactly three failures).

Keep the repair narrow and fail loud for literal `[:map ...]` declarations. This is a check for the two already-reserved ABI keys, not general Malli/schema validation, duplicate-key policing, or a new schema DSL.
acceptance_criteria:
- `v/defview` rejects literal props schemas containing `:key` or `:children`, with a declaration-time diagnostic that names the view, offending key, and existing ABI recovery.
- Ordinary literal schemas, explicitly open schemas, absent schemas, and opaque schemas retain their current behavior.
- A focused macro-expansion regression covers both reserved keys and proves the accepted descriptor/tooling projection cannot contain either as a declared prop.
- No schema library dependency, value-validation pass, or general schema-shape validator is introduced.
close_reason: Merged via #6752 (props-schema reserved keys).

title: Keep opaque Freehand props-schema expressions open at every surface
description:
PR #6737 (merge 00239e33d215a1c4ac3fddafa12f0b8facba38f7) promises that an opaque `:props` schema—one behind a registry reference or runtime expression—closes nothing, and that compiled/interpreted modes differ only in when a breach is reported.

`expand-defview` gives the raw authored form to `compile-structural-view`, so `(identity [:map [:id :int]])` is opaque there and `:self-closed-keys` is nil. The emitted descriptor, however, evaluates that same expression; `descriptor/normalize-call` then sees the resulting literal vector, derives `[:id]`, and closes the runtime boundary. A compiled recursive view containing `[self {:id id :extra true}]` therefore compiles, but normalizing that exact call in development throws `:rf.error/view-bad-props` for `:extra`.

A temporary host-neutral regression reproduced this on both hosts: JVM 608 tests / 4208 assertions with the opaque row failing, and CLJS 495 / 3386 with the same row failing. Clean baselines are JVM 606 / 4205 and CLJS 494 / 3385, both green.

Keep the repair narrow: preserve the authored opaque classification (and the schema's stated inert-data character) consistently in compile metadata and the runtime descriptor, or otherwise make both consumers consult one stable representation. Do not add value validation, a Malli runtime dependency, or mandatory schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- A schema supplied through a symbol or runtime expression remains open at both compiled call analysis and the development runtime boundary.
- A focused cross-host regression includes a compiled self-call with an extra prop and proves the same call is not accepted at build time then rejected at the boundary.
- Literal closed schemas still reject undeclared keys; `{:closed false}` and absent schemas remain open.
- The descriptor inspection projection and Var metadata expose one consistent, inert schema representation without evaluating the authored expression twice.
close_reason: Merged via #6752 (opaque props-schema expressions).

title: Keep explicit nil Freehand control values on the controlled React path
description:
PR #6736 states that controlled-prop membership is by presence and explicitly defines `nil` as a controlled empty value. The interpreted React emitter makes the door decision from authored keys, but its generic attribute loop then drops every nil value before constructing React props:

    controlled? (controlled/controlled-props? (keys attrs))
    ...
    (nil? raw) nil

The event therefore takes the synchronous controlled-input lane while React receives no `value`/`checked` prop and treats the node as uncontrolled. This is a real DOM-state contradiction, not only a predicate mismatch.

Reproduced in Chromium on current main by rendering `[:input {:value "seed" :on-change (fn [_])}]`, then rerendering the same node with `:value nil`. The PR contract expects a controlled empty field. Actual behavior:

- React reports “A component is changing a controlled input to be uncontrolled.”
- The DOM value remains `"seed"` instead of becoming `""`.
- A temporary browser regression produced exactly one failure: 543 tests / 3181 assertions, expected `""`, actual `"seed"`.

Keep generic nil-attribute omission intact. Add only the narrow normalization needed for `value`/`checked` on the supported controlled native tags, judged by the same final prop slots as the door, so explicit nil remains a controlled empty/unchecked value across rerenders. Do not introduce a form model, wrapper component, generalized nil policy, or public controlled-input API.

Deduplication: all-state search found no Freehand explicit-nil controlled-input owner. Closed `rf2-j4len` repaired the donor `ui/spread-safe` rule that ordinary nil owned props remain absent; that generic law is distinct and should remain unchanged. `rf2-drpa3.119` owns the compiled analyzer's alternate-spelling join, not the interpreted DOM value transition. `rf2-drpa3.113` owns the broader compiled-browser runtime and is not duplicated here.
acceptance_criteria:
- In the interpreted React emitter, a supported native control with an explicitly present `value nil` remains controlled and renders the empty value; `checked nil` remains controlled and renders unchecked.
- A real-browser regression renders a nonnil controlled value/checked state, rerenders the same DOM node with explicit nil, and proves the node clears/unchecks without controlled↔uncontrolled React diagnostics.
- Exact and alternate attribute spellings use the same normalized controlled slots; absence of the key still means uncontrolled.
- Generic nil attributes continue to be omitted under the existing conversion law, and unsupported tags are not given controlled-input semantics.
- The fix is a narrow emitter/normalization seam; no form abstraction, generalized nil framework, public verb, or expansion of the synchronous door.
- Focused CLJS and browser Freehand gates pass with plausible non-zero counts.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6745. controlled/empty-control-slot answers the slot an explicitly nil attribute must still be written into, paired with its controlled-empty value ("" / false), scoped to the door's tag+slot facts and read through the same prop-slot projection; the interpreted React emitter writes it instead of dropping the prop. Generic nil-attribute omission untouched. title: Make the compiled controlled-input door judge normalized prop slots
description:
PR #6736 defines the controlled-input door over final-normalized React prop slots, but the compiled analyzer decides whether an element is controlled with raw exact-key checks:

    (or (contains? m :value) (contains? m :checked))

That disagrees with both the shared `controlled/controlled-props?` predicate and the emitted prop. For example, `:x/value` normalizes to the real React `value` slot and makes the node controlled, yet the compiled event is marked `:sync? false` (and an async-shape advisory is also suppressed because the analyzer thinks the element is uncontrolled).

Reproduced against merged PR #6736 with an analyzer integration assertion for:

    [:input {:x/value value
             :on-input [:form/typed :rf.ui/value]}]

Expected `[:props :events 0 :sync?]` true; actual false. The focused JVM Freehand suite then had exactly one failure (582 tests / 3956 assertions); removing the assertion restored the clean baseline. FH-INPUT-001 proves alias normalization only at the helper level, so it does not exercise this analyzer join.

Use the existing shared normalized-slot predicate at the analyzer integration point. Keep the exact five-fact door, its frame-scoped flush, and its closed tag/event/handler roster unchanged. No public sync verb, alias framework, or broader compiler/runtime redesign.

Deduplication: all-state Beads search found no normalized-controlled-slot/compiler-alias owner. `rf2-izep3` was the already-shipped donor `ui/spread-safe` deny bypass, not this Freehand analyzer join. `rf2-drpa3.113` owns making compiled Freehand views browser-mountable; it is broader downstream runtime work and should not absorb or duplicate this one-line static contract repair.
acceptance_criteria:
- The compiled analyzer derives controlled-prop presence through the same normalized-slot rule as the interpreted emitter; it does not maintain exact raw `:value`/`:checked` checks.
- Analyzer integration coverage proves alternate spellings for both `value` and `checked` open the door when the other four facts hold, including presence with nil where relevant.
- The emitted prop slot, `:sync?` verdict, and async-handler advisory all agree for exact and alternate spellings.
- Existing near-miss tests remain outside the door (`beforeinput`, capture/passive, uncontrolled tags, and non-data handlers); no new synchronous surface or generalized alias machinery is introduced.
- Focused JVM/CLJS Freehand gates pass with plausible non-zero counts.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6745. The compiled analyzer now derives controlled-prop presence through controlled/controlled-props? (the shared normalized-slot rule) instead of raw (contains? m :value)/(contains? m :checked). Pre-fix reproduction: 7 JVM failures covering :x/value, :x/checked, presence-with-nil, the emitted-slot/verdict join, the async-handler advisory, and the cross-mode agreement table. Door shape, tag/event/handler rosters and frame-scoped flush unchanged; no new diagnostic id; no public verb.

title: Publish Freehand top-layer advisories only from selected commits as typed evidence
description:
PR #6735's two development advisories bypass Freehand's selected-commit evidence contract in complementary ways:

- install! calls advise-unreconciled! while constructing React props, before its callback ref has committed. A focused CLJS probe replaced console.warn, called install! for a controlled popover with no handler, and never invoked the ref. Expected zero publications from an uncommitted candidate; actual was one full warning. The isolated suite failed exactly once at 474 tests / 3233 assertions. After removing the probe byte-for-byte, it is green at 473 / 3232.
- a refused showPopover/showModal/hide/close call is caught at commit, but advise! emits only unstructured console text. It carries no stable warning/error id or structured operation/recovery fields, despite D015 rules 4-5 requiring development diagnostics and typed development evidence. That makes the evidence unavailable to trace listeners and tools (including AI-driven diagnostics) except by scraping prose.

The first behavior violates Spec 004's passive-render law: a render may restart or be abandoned and MUST NOT publish evidence. It can also spam or falsely accuse an author for candidates React never selected. The second weakens the explicit tooling contract of the ruling that owns this feature.

Treat these together because they are one narrow evidence seam, not two feature requests: top-layer advisories should be typed, dev-only records emitted only from a selected callback-ref/host-operation occurrence.

Acceptance:

1. Constructing top-layer props without invoking the ref publishes exactly zero warning/evidence records.
2. A selected commit with controlled top-layer state and no reconciliation handler emits a stable, catalogued dev-only warning record with concise recovery.
3. A refused host operation emits stable typed dev evidence naming the operation, element context, reason/exception, and recovery, then continues with the existing behavior.
4. The evidence is available through the established dev trace surface and is eliminated under goog.DEBUG=false.
5. No always-on promotion, app-steerable policy, retry/supervision layer, console parser, new public API, or general diagnostics framework.

Deduplication: searched the live Dolt database and all Bead states for top-layer/popover advisories, missing reconciliation, console.warn, passive render, abandoned candidates, and published evidence. rf2-drpa3.34 is closed and contains the merged behavior; no live Bead owns this evidence-timing/type gap. Closed rf2-drpa3.20 and rf2-drpa3.67 provide the existing selected-commit and typed-evidence precedent but do not cover top-layer advisories.

Clean verification after probe removal: JVM Freehand 582 tests / 3955 assertions, focused CLJS 473 / 3232, browser 542 / 3179; all zero failures/errors.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6753 (6daa94b9f6). Typed selected-commit advisories, published only from selected commits. Added fh-toplayer-004-a-generation-retires-through-a-composed-release proving retirement fires through a real chained release rather than leaving it as a reading. Non-vacuity probes redded naming their tests, then restored byte-identical.

title: Cancel detached Freehand top-layer generations before the microtask flush
description:
PR #6735 queues each top-layer desired state in a process-wide Map keyed only by the DOM node. The callback-ref detach arm does nothing, and the microtask flush fences an entry only with node.isConnected. Connectivity is not ownership: a ref generation can retire while the same node remains connected.

A real Chromium probe exercised the exact merged seam:

1. append a valid closed popover node to document.body;
2. install desired open state and invoke the returned ref with that node, enqueueing one operation;
3. invoke the same ref with nil before the microtask flush, while leaving the node connected;
4. flush the batch.

Expected after detach: 0 host operations and the node closed. Actual: 1 operation and the node open. The isolated browser suite reported exactly one failure at 543 tests / 3180 assertions; after removing the probe byte-for-byte, the clean suite is green at 542 / 3179.

This violates D015 and Spec 004's explicit law that stale/superseded generations cannot act. It is reachable when another commit in the same task removes the intrinsic without removing the DOM node (for example, a synchronous layout-effect update): the old ref detaches, no successor top-layer ref replaces its queued fact, and the stale microtask opens the now-uncontrolled node.

Smallest coherent repair: give each queued entry exact callback-ref occurrence/generation ownership. A nil detach must cancel only that occurrence's still-pending entry; it must not delete a newer same-node enqueue. Preserve the current one-microtask batch, document ordering, live-node diff, and zero-listener/observer design.

Acceptance:

1. The connected-node probe above performs exactly 0 host operations after detach and leaves the node closed.
2. A newer ref generation for the same node still wins if the older generation detaches.
3. Existing nested ancestor-before-descendant behavior and unchanged-state no-op counts remain exact.
4. No node registry, listener, observer, timer, public generation API, or general lifecycle framework.

Deduplication: searched the live Dolt database and every Bead state for top-layer/popover ownership, stale or superseded generations, pending microtasks, and detached generations. rf2-drpa3.34 is the closed implementation owner and rf2-drpa3.54 is the broad future browser-matrix gate; neither owns this concrete merged defect. Closed rf2-drpa3.20 and rf2-drpa3.67 are useful selected-commit/incarnation prior art, not duplicate work.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6753 (a215bf1b9d). Generation retirement: detached top-layer generations cancelled before the microtask flush. Rebased onto post-.113 main; install! collision resolved keeping BOTH intents (refs/chain wrapping the attach/detach body). All gates re-taken post-rebase EXIT=0: freehand JVM 738/5348, test:freehand 696/4365, test:cljs 10821/54458, test:browser 627/3735.

title: Freehand server render path: v/render-static and the JVM tree -> HTML seam
description:
Freehand has NO server render path today, and one half of the seam is already written against the other half that is missing.

WHAT IS THERE: re-frame.freehand.compiler.root/render-static-form is implemented — it analyses the root, runs the transitive static-capability proof (Spec 004C section 3 / EP-0034 section 2), refuses a CLJS expansion with :rf.ui.compile/ui-render-static-jvm-only, and emits a call to (re-frame.freehand.tree/emit-static-html ...) so the caller's namespace carries no compile-time re-frame.ssr reference.

WHAT IS MISSING, verified on origin/main and on every in-flight worker branch:
  1. re-frame.freehand.tree/emit-static-html DOES NOT EXIST. The only emit-static-html in the corpus is the donor's re-frame.ui.tree/emit-static-html. render-static-form therefore emits a call to a function that is not defined — a dangling reference, not a working path.
  2. render-static-form is wired to NO macro. re-frame.freehand publishes no render-static verb (re-frame.ui.cljc line 261 wires the donor's own; freehand wires nothing).
  3. The SSR artefact has zero awareness of Freehand: git grep freehand over implementation/ssr/src and implementation/ssr-ring/src is EMPTY.
  4. re-frame.freehand.tree/render answers a STRUCTURAL tree, not HTML, and is not published on the facade. re-frame.ssr.ui-tree/emit-ui-tree is pure and 'calls NOTHING — no view, no subscription, no frame', so it cannot host a view-time render failure either.

CONSEQUENCE: no Freehand view can fail during a server render, because no Freehand view is rendered on a server. That blocks rf2-drpa3.102 (F5f server-error projection) outright — its own OUTCOME is conditioned on this ('once Freehand has a server render path').

OUTCOME: re-frame.freehand.tree/emit-static-html exists and folds a version-1 structural tree to an inert HTML string through the SSR emitter reached late (no compile-time re-frame.ssr reference in freehand/src), and v/render-static is published on the facade over render-static-form.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. (v/render-static [view {...}]) answers an inert HTML string on the JVM.
2. The freehand -> ssr boundary stays late: no :require of any re-frame.ssr namespace anywhere under implementation/freehand/src.
3. A missing SSR artefact at render-static time fails loud naming the day8/re-frame2-ssr coordinate.
4. NOTE the api-manifest SERIAL LANE: v/render-static is a NEW PUBLIC VERB and needs a spec/API.md row, qualified re-frame.freehand/render-static exactly as v/mount and v/hydrate-root are (re-frame.ui publishes a verb of the same name and the root-verb kind guard reads a bare row as a donor row).

title: Refuse identifierPrefix drift on an idempotent Freehand remount
description:
## Defect

PR #6734 enforces effective `identifierPrefix` uniqueness for fresh roots, but its same-root/same-container fast path excludes that root from the prefix-owner scan and then accepts a changed prefix while reusing the existing React root. React root options are immutable after `createRoot`, so the new prefix is not applied.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount root A with authored `:identifier-prefix "old-"`.
2. Call `v/mount` again for the same root-id/container with `:identifier-prefix "new-"`.
3. Current code reuses A's host root and registers a replacement Freehand Root claiming `"new-"`; `root-identifier-prefix` now reports `"new-"`, while React `useId` continues to emit under `"old-"`.
4. Mount distinct root B with `:identifier-prefix "old-"`. The registry now considers that prefix free and admits B, even though A's live React root still uses it, permitting cross-root `useId`/ARIA collisions.

Spec 009 already catalogues the exact `:rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable` condition and recovery. Closed donor finding rf2-vxgfnd.59 fixed this same HMR path in `re-frame.ui` with a real `useId` DOM proof; #6734's direct Freehand root reintroduced it. No live Bead owns the Freehand path.

## Bounded Correction

Before preflight on the existing-root fast path, compare the requested effective prefix with the prefix that created the live React root. Reuse `:rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable` and its `:unmount-before-changing-identifier-prefix` recovery on drift. Keep the existing root, its prior prefix claim, frame plan and committed DOM untouched. No mutable React-root option layer or new diagnostic is needed.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6734.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A same-root/same-container re-mount with a different effective `identifierPrefix` fails before preflight or render with `:rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable`, naming root-id, requested and existing prefixes.
2. A real React `useId` DOM regression proves the live root continues to use and claim its original prefix after the refusal; a second root cannot claim that prefix.
3. Re-mounting with the identical authored prefix and with the identical derived prefix remains the normal idempotent HMR path.
4. After true `v/unmount!`, the original prefix is released and can be claimed by a fresh root; a stale handle cannot release a successor's claim.
5. Reuse the existing Spec 009 diagnostic/recovery and current one-map registry; add no new diagnostic, mutable root-options abstraction, or per-render work.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6746. v/mount gains a fourth admission claim (require-stable-identifier-prefix!) raised after claim! and BEFORE preflight/React: a same-root/same-container re-mount whose effective identifierPrefix differs from the live root's is refused with the catalogued :rf.error/root-identifier-prefix-immutable / :unmount-before-changing-identifier-prefix, naming root-id, :requested and :existing. No new diagnostic, no mutable root-options layer, no per-render work; Spec 009 untouched (existing row), 004C gains the paved-path paragraph plus the missing S7 roster line, FH-ROOT-002 gains the identifierPrefix arm with a real React useId DOM proof. Both directions pinned: drift refuses, same prefix (authored or derived) still re-renders the existing host root. Pre-fix repro red (8 failures incl. the aliaser admission cascade); non-vacuity inverted+restored byte-identical. Gates all exit 0: freehand JVM 615/4306, node freehand 518/3488, node cljs 10643/53581, browser 563/3308, plus conformance-index / donor-inventory / doc-slugs / ui-root-lifecycle.

title: Finish Freehand root incarnation ownership contract across canonical docs and conformance
description:
## Defect

PR #6734's root frame ledger records only `frame-id`, `installed-by` and root-id refs. The Root handle also retains only the id, so teardown calls `(frame/destroy-frame! frame-id)`. In the core frame contract an id is address-directed authority: it destroys whichever same-id incarnation is currently live. The value returned by `make-frame` is the exact-incarnation token intended for lifecycle owners.

## Steps to Reproduce

A real-browser public-path probe:

1. `v/mount` a Freehand root with `{:frame {:id :audit/frame-successor}}`.
2. Explicitly destroy that installed frame and create a same-id successor with `rf/make-frame`, retaining the returned value.
3. Call `v/unmount!` on the root.

Expected: the stale root can release only the incarnation it installed, so the successor remains. Actual: `(frame/frame fid)` is nil; unmount destroyed the successor by id. The isolated browser run was 537 tests / 3145 assertions with exactly this one failure and no errors. The probe was removed.

The same id-only ledger loses references on an ordinary idempotent re-mount. Re-mounting one live root from owned frame A to owned frame B adds the B ref and replaces the Root handle, but never removes A's ref. After unmount, B is destroyed while A and its ledger row remain. A mounted-browser probe produced four exact failures (old frame/row present both before and after final unmount), then was removed.

Spec 004C's existing installed-versus-adopted authority rule is also relevant: meeting a boot/external frame must not silently grant a root address-directed destruction rights. Closed donor finding rf2-vxgfnd.56 is prior art; no live Freehand Bead owns this frame-authority gap.

## Bounded Correction

Let the existing ledger retain the exact frame value/authority a root actually installed and the root's current frame reference. On re-mount, transition that one reference from the prior plan to the accepted plan (or refuse before mutation); on teardown, destroy only the exact installed incarnation and only after the last live ref. Preserve the existing SCOPE spelling and installed/adopted distinction. This needs no second registry or general lease framework—the core frame value already is the token.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6734.

1. spec/API.md mount and unmount! rows state that ENSURE refresh/no-op requires the exact recorded live incarnation and teardown consumes only that value; stale same-id successors and token-less legacy rows are guarded no-ops/refusals, never address-directed ownership.
2. Spec 009's :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict runtime arm qualifies same-root refresh/equal-fingerprint no-op by live-incarnation proof and documents stale/token-less recovery under :scope-config-less-or-own-the-lifetime.

5. Documentation, API-manifest, conformance, and focused root gates pass; no runtime/public API expansion.

title: Make Freehand root preflight a rollback-safe ownership boundary
description:
## Defect

PR #6734 runs Freehand root preflight after a read-only `claim!`, but before call-shape construction and before any rollback/revalidation boundary. `preflight!` can create or refresh a frame and drain `:initial-events` (arbitrary application code); `mount` then constructs the React element outside its `try`, and `hydrate-root` has no corresponding abort boundary around element construction or `hydrateRoot`.

## Steps to Reproduce

A public-path CLJS probe called:

    (v/mount [views/counter nil]
             #js {:nodeType 1}
             {:frame {:id :audit/post-preflight-failure}})

The valid declared-view head lets identity and preflight proceed; `nil` in the props slot then raises the expected `:rf.error/view-bad-props` during `root-element`. After the rejection, both `(frame/frame :audit/post-preflight-failure)` and the root frame-ledger record remained live. Focused node result was 431 tests / 2860 assertions with exactly the two rollback assertions failing. The probe was removed.

The same ordering leaves a second, already-proven ownership window: `:initial-events` may synchronously mount/unmount the same root after `claim!` but before the outer attempt registers or re-renders. The outer attempt does not re-check the fresh claim or exact existing Root, so it can clobber a re-entrant root or render/register a stale handle. Closed donor findings rf2-vxgfnd.18, rf2-vxgfnd.52 and rf2-vxgfnd.69 document and fix the identical classes in `re-frame.ui`; no live Bead owns them for the new Freehand root.

## Bounded Correction

Make each Freehand `mount` / `hydrate-root` attempt one small ownership transaction: finish pure call-shape/container validation before mutating preflight; after preflight, revalidate the exact root/container claim before React work; and on a synchronous post-preflight failure release only the frame reference this attempt acquired while preserving the primary exception. Reuse the existing registry, frame ledger and diagnostics. No general transaction coordinator, async context, or compiled-client transplant is needed.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6734.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact bad-props public probe fails with `:rf.error/view-bad-props` and leaves no frame, frame-ledger row, live-root claim or DOM mutation; an immediate corrected retry succeeds.
2. Pin the equivalent post-preflight failure boundary for `hydrate-root`, including fallback and adoption setup where applicable.
3. A fresh-root `:initial-events` handler that re-entrantly claims the same root/container cannot be clobbered by the outer attempt; the outer attempt re-checks after preflight and fails before `createRoot`/registration, leaving the inner root untouched.
4. An existing-root preflight that unmounts or replaces the captured Root is revalidated before `.render` or registry replacement; no stale handle can render or overwrite the successor.
5. Rollback is exact: it does not release an incumbent/sibling frame reference, undo a re-entrant owner, or mask the original error. Normal same-plan HMR remains a no-reseed re-render.
6. Keep the repair local to root admission/preflight; add no coordinator, async framework, public API, or new diagnostic id.

title: Confirm or remove the dead emit-view-def path calling nonexistent tree fns
description:
Found by the structural-path worker (PR #6738) while fixing an adjacent defect. Reported rather than touched, correctly — it is pre-existing and outside that bead's scope.

## The finding

`implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/emit_jvm.cljc`'s `emit-view-def` emits calls to `tree/view-boundary` and `tree/register-view!`. **NEITHER FUNCTION EXISTS.**

## Why this needs a determination rather than a quiet deletion

There are two possibilities and they have opposite remedies:

1. **The path is genuinely unreachable** — dead code left by a refactor. Remedy: delete it, and note in the PR body what made it unreachable, so the next reader does not resurrect it.
2. **The path IS reachable under some declaration shape nobody has exercised** — in which case this is a LATENT CRASH: a compiled view of that shape would emit code calling a function that does not exist, and would fail at load with an unresolved-var error rather than a Freehand diagnostic.

Do NOT assume (1). This programme has repeatedly found that "obviously dead" and "never exercised" are different claims — a namespace outside the CLJS runner regexp holding reader-conditional tests ran on NO host and looked green; a conformance row passed on broken behaviour because it asserted the wrong thing. Absence of a failure is not evidence of unreachability.

## How to determine it

Establish reachability POSITIVELY, not by absence of reports. Enumerate what `emit-view-def` is called with across the compiled emitter, and show either (a) a concrete declaration shape that reaches it — then fix the emission — or (b) that every caller path provably cannot, with the reason stated.

If it IS reachable, the emitted calls should either target functions that exist, or the emitter should refuse the shape with a catalogued `:rf.ui.compile/*` diagnostic — the checker's own principle: answer correctly or refuse loudly, never emit something that cannot run.

## Acceptance

1. A stated determination — reachable or not — with the evidence, not an assertion.
2. If unreachable: removed, with the reason recorded.
3. If reachable: a test that reaches it, red before the fix, green after; and the emitted code either calls real functions or the shape is refused with an existing diagnostic id.
4. No new always-on diagnostic id (that costs a three-way co-edit plus a core error-catalogue run).
5. The compiled tier's shipped guarantees are unaffected: `{:compiled true}` selection, the v1 grammar, crossings, capability elision (exact omitted-ViewCell count), manifest verdicts.

## Non-goals

Refactoring the JVM emitter. Changing the compiled grammar. Widening this into an emitter audit — this is one path, determined and resolved.
notes:
SCOPE ENLARGED (mayor, 2026-07-24) — this is not one dead path, it is a SYSTEMATIC GAP where the compiled emitters reference a runtime surface that was never built. Two independent workers found pieces of it hours apart.

Originally filed from PR #6738: emit_jvm.cljc emit-view-def calls tree/view-boundary and tree/register-view!, neither of which exists.

NOW ALSO KNOWN, found by the rf2-drpa3.38 slots survey:
  - compiler/emit_cljs.cljc emits calls to re-frame.freehand.runtime/{spread->props, spread-safe->props, spread-safe-props, foreign-spread-props, render-fn, jsx-spread2, jsx-spread3}. THE re-frame.freehand.runtime NAMESPACE DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL. Nothing outside quoted emission references it.
  - compiler/emit_jvm.cljc:172,228,232,233 emits re-frame.freehand.tree/{render-fn, slot-ready?, check-slot-arity!} — also absent.
  - Separately, analyze.cljc:43-48 discriminates the compiled grammar BY RESOLUTION (env/resolves-to? does real host resolution) against re-frame.freehand/{slot, spread, spread-safe}. Those vars do not exist either, so those analyzer arms are reachable ONLY through the tests :resolver override — from AUTHORED code they are dead.

OWNERSHIP SPLIT, so this bead does not swallow other slices:
  - re-frame.freehand.runtime/* belongs to rf2-drpa3.81 (compiled views runnable through the public door) — that worker has been told to enumerate what the emitters actually emit rather than build only the subscription path.
  - tree/{render-fn, slot-ready?, check-slot-arity!} and the slot/spread/spread-safe vars belong to rf2-drpa3.38 (F5a slots grammar), currently HELD behind the api-manifest lane.
  - THIS BEAD retains tree/view-boundary and tree/register-view! — determine reachable or not, with evidence, then remove or repair.

⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, worth stating on the bead because it will recur: an emitter can reference a function that does not exist and NOTHING FAILS until that emission path is actually taken. The compiled tier has been green this whole time. So "the suite passes" is not evidence that emitted code is callable. Any future emitter work should positively enumerate emitted symbols and confirm each resolves, rather than trusting green gates.
THIRD INSTANCE (mayor, 2026-07-24), found by the SSR follow-ups worker: compiler/root.cljc render-static-form emits a call to re-frame.freehand.tree/emit-static-html, which DOES NOT EXIST (only the donor has one) — and render-static-form is itself wired to NO MACRO, so nothing reaches it from authored code.

That makes THREE independent discoveries of the same shape, by three different workers, hours apart:
  1. emit_jvm.cljc emit-view-def -> tree/view-boundary, tree/register-view!   (THIS bead)
  2. emit_cljs.cljc -> the entire re-frame.freehand.runtime namespace          (rf2-drpa3.81)
     emit_jvm.cljc:172,228,232,233 -> tree/{render-fn, slot-ready?, check-slot-arity!}  (rf2-drpa3.38)
     analyze.cljc:43-48 -> re-frame.freehand/{slot, spread, spread-safe} by RESOLUTION  (rf2-drpa3.38)
  3. compiler/root.cljc render-static-form -> tree/emit-static-html            (rf2-drpa3.112 owns the server render path)

⚠️ THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING, and it is worth more than any single instance: the compiled emitters were transplanted from the donor along with their CALL SITES, but the runtime they call was not. Nothing fails because no authored path reaches those emissions — the compiled tier has been green throughout. So a green suite is NOT evidence that emitted code is callable, and "this emitter path works" has never actually been tested for these arms.

RECOMMENDATION for whoever takes this bead: do not just resolve the two symbols named at the top. ENUMERATE EVERY SYMBOL THE EMITTERS EMIT and confirm each resolves, then classify each as (a) reachable and broken, (b) reachable and fine, or (c) unreachable dead code with the reason it is unreachable stated. That census is the real deliverable; the individual repairs belong to the slices that own each namespace (.81 runtime, .38 slots/tree trio, .112 server render). This bead should end with a map, not a patch.
WIDENED 2026-07-24 by the mayor — a SECOND instance of the same defect class, found and empirically confirmed by the rf2-drpa3.149 worker (PR #6769). Same determination, same remedy, so it belongs on this bead rather than a duplicate.

SECOND SITE: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc, fn handler-form. Its case over handler classifications emits calls to events/data-handler, events/event-handler, events/handler-callback and events/dynamic-handler. NONE OF THOSE FOUR EXIST in the freehand artefact. It is unported donor code whose output cannot run.

REACHABILITY, as established by that worker: emit_cljs is NOT reachable from the live v/defview path (expand-defview -> compile-structural-view -> emit-jvm + emit-react). It is reached only by test-driven compiler/defview*, and by root.cljc emit-inline (a v/mount static top region) plus the react/lazy fallback — so any handler in those templates is ALREADY a build failure.

The .149 worker deliberately left handler-form NON-TOTAL for the new :key-map classification, and was right to: adding an arm would have meant INVENTING A RUNTIME CONTRACT for constructors that do not exist. That is a decision for this bead, not a drive-by.

So this bead now covers BOTH sites and the question is the same for each: port the emitter to real constructors, or delete the dead path. Answer it once for both.
MAYOR NOTE 2026-07-24 — DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE, independently found by the rf2-drpa3.105 investigation. This bead now has a THIRD site and, for the first time, a clear recommendation.

THIRD SITE, same file as the second: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/emit_cljs.cljc emits ~30 DISTINCT re-frame.freehand.runtime/... targets that resolve to NOTHING. re-frame.freehand.runtime DOES NOT EXIST. (Its sibling .tree does exist — so the F6d caveat claim that the moved emitters lower to runtime/ and tree/ is HALF TRUE.)

WHY IT HAS NEVER BROKEN THE BUILD: emit_cljs is unreachable from the live path. v/defview routes through compiler/compile-structural-view -> emit-jvm + emit-react, and compiler/defview* — the sole caller of emit-cljs/emit-defview — is reached only from four JVM tests.

SO THE FILE NOW HAS THREE INDEPENDENT DEFECTS OF THE SAME KIND: handler-form emits four events/... constructors that do not exist (recorded earlier on this bead); ~30 runtime/... targets that do not exist; and the whole file is unreachable from v/defview.

MAYOR RECOMMENDATION, for Mike to rule: DELETE Freehand emit_cljs.cljc as SUPERSEDED by emit_react.cljc + compiled_react.cljs — whose own docstring explicitly forbids "a second reactive path". Porting it would mean INVENTING a runtime contract for ~34 constructors that have never existed, to serve a code path nothing reaches. Under the pre-alpha stance (no back-compat shims, no retain-and-defer, clean break now) delete is the elegant answer and port is the gold-plated one.

CONSEQUENCE IF RULED DELETE: the donor ledger row for ui/runtime.cljs re-dispositions from MOVE to REPLACE, and ui/client.cljs becomes a PARTIAL-REPLACE against re-frame.freehand.root. That materially shrinks rf2-drpa3.105 from a 9,500-line MOVE to a bounded absorption of the settlement teeth. So this ruling UNBLOCKS .105 and should be taken first.

Note the emit_jvm/emit-view-def half of this bead (tree/view-boundary and tree/register-view!, neither of which exists) still needs its own answer — it may be the same answer, but confirm rather than assume.
MAYOR NOTE: whichever way Mike rules (delete vs port), the RULING AND ITS REASONING must be reproduced in the merging PR body, not only in these notes. The method requires decisions in both the tracker and the PR body, because the PR body is the durable git-history record. A future reader doing archaeology on why an emitter was deleted will have the git history, not this database.
OPERATOR RULING — Mike, 2026-07-24: DELETE emit_cljs.cljc.

MUST BE REPRODUCED IN THE MERGING PR BODY, with the reasoning, not merely cited. The PR body is the durable git-history record; a future reader doing archaeology on why an emitter was deleted will have git log, not this database.

THE REASONING TO CARRY: the file calls ~34 functions that have never existed — four events/... constructors (data-handler, event-handler, handler-callback, dynamic-handler) and ~30 re-frame.freehand.runtime/... targets, where that namespace does not exist at all. Nothing on the live v/defview path reaches it: v/defview routes through compiler/compile-structural-view -> emit-jvm + emit-react, and compiler/defview* is reached only from JVM tests. Porting would not RESTORE a contract, it would INVENT one — a runtime API for a second reactive path that compiled_react.cljs own docstring explicitly forbids. Under the pre-alpha stance (no back-compat shims, no retain-and-defer, clean break now) delete is the elegant answer and port is the gold-plated one. SCOPE NOTE FROM THE MAYOR SURFACE SURVEY (verified, not assumed): the blast radius is wider than this bead text implies. emit_cljs is referenced from compiler.cljc, compiler/build.cljc, compiler/emit_jvm.cljc and compiler/root.cljc, and pinned by at least six test files.
