title: Rule on two authored id spellings with no #id sugar
description:
## Observation

PR #6738 (rf2-drpa3.101) makes the `#id` sugar conflict guard judge the emitted slot, so `[:div#sugar {:x/id "a"}]` is now refused in the interpreted structural walk, the interpreted React walk and the compiled analyzer, alongside the exact `[:div#sugar {:id "a"}]` that was already refused.

That bead scoped itself to the SUGAR conflict and explicitly said not to canonicalize an ordinary `:x/id`, so this form is still accepted on merged main:

    (tree/render [:div {:id "a" :x/id "b"}])
    ;; => {:tag :div :attrs {:id "a" :x/id "b"}}   ; two ids

    ;; React receives ONE prop; which value wins is map iteration order.

It is the same law the sugar guard enforces — two spellings of one emitted attribute on one element — reached without the shorthand. The structural tree reports both; React writes one; which one is not determined by anything an author can see.

## The question, not the answer

This is a ruling, not a determinable fact, which is why it is filed rather than folded into #6738:

1. REFUSE, extending the id conflict guard from 'sugar plus an authored id' to 'two authored keys projecting onto the id slot', wherever they come from. Uniform with the sugar case and with Spec 004B's 'ambiguities the grammar removes rather than ranks'.
2. LEAVE IT, on the ground that an author who writes two id keys in one literal map has written something visibly odd, and that the direct-attribute path already carries author-space names by ruling — an ordinary qualified attribute is not canonicalized, and any general dedupe starts to look like the aliasing framework rf2-drpa3.93 and rf2-drpa3.101 both refused.

Whoever takes this states the rule and its reason. If REFUSE: reuse the existing diagnostic ids (`:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` interpreted, `:rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict` compiled) — no new always-on id — and hold it identically in both modes, extending FH-STRUCT-009's rejected/accepted-keys tables in place.

## Scope note

Only the `id` slot is in question. `:key` aliases are already refused and `:class`/`:style` aliases are already routed and composed (rf2-drpa3.93), so neither can present this shape.

## Non-goals

A general aliasing framework. Revisiting rf2-drpa3.101's shipped sugar guard, or rf2-drpa3.93's routing.
acceptance_criteria: Refusal identical at all three guard sites (interpreted structural walk, interpreted React walk, compiled analyzer) PLUS the runtime v/spread seam, both modes, via a shared cardinality helper — a literal-sites-only patch that leaves compiled v/spread accepting the pair fails acceptance. Existing diagnostic ids only (:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed interpreted, :rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict compiled); message names both offending keys in the established spells-its-id-twice shape. grammar.cljc recovery for the compiled id gains a delete-one-spelling entry. FH-STRUCT-009 :rejected table extended in place (no-sugar pair rows incl. string variant; sugar+spread row); :accepted-keys single-id controls untouched. Parity tests in both modes: both pair orders, nil-valued member, runtime-merged map, past-array-map-threshold map, v/spread, sugar+spread; accepted controls: #id alone, each single spelling alone, :title + :x/title. Generalisation to ordinary attributes explicitly declined per the ruling in notes; spread-safe owned-wins boundary untouched.
notes:
RULING 2026-07-24 15:14:56 AUSEST (delegated review under Mike's 2026-07-24 direction): REFUSE — Option 1, scoped strictly to the id slot. Two authored keys projecting onto the emitted id slot on one element are refused, with or without #id sugar, in both modes. Stated as an element cardinality invariant: #id sugar, when present, occupies the id slot once; beyond that an attrs map may contain at most one key for which rules/caller-key-slot equals rules/sugar-id-slot. Presence counts, not value ({:id nil :x/id "b"} is still two declarations; each single spelling alone stays valid).

WHY: the grammar already owns the id slot (#id sugar writes into it, rules/sugar-id-slot names it, a conflict guard polices it, an established diagnostic pair exists for it) — this finishes an existing rule, not a new one. id is referential: CSS selectors, htmlFor, aria-labelledby, anchor targets, and this repo's own tooling (Xray, read-dom, testbed selectors) address elements by id, so a nondeterministic id breaks OTHER elements' references and every tree-based test, unlike a self-contained wrong title. FH-STRUCT-009 already states the invariant (the tree's id and React's id must be the SAME id); today main accepts [:div {:id "a" :x/id "b"}] and [:div {:id "a" "id" "b"}] with both keys retained in the structural tree while React writes ONE id via gobj/set under the projected prop name — the winner is map iteration order (authoring order for a small PersistentArrayMap, hash order past ~8 entries, construction order after merge/assoc), which is not contract on any host. The interpreted guard is a runtime-map walk check, so a pair produced by merging two attr sources is caught too — nothing visibly odd need appear at any single source site, which defeats the "author wrote something visibly odd" defence of leaving it.

RULE + SITES: extend the existing gate at the three guard sites — interpreted structural walk (tree.cljc ~:184, the (and sugar-id (conv/id-slot-key? k)) gate), interpreted React walk (react.cljs ~:290, same gate), compiled analyzer (analyze.cljc ~:2021-2024, the filter over (keys m) for sugar-id-slot) — from "sugar plus an authored id-slot key" to "id slot spelled twice, wherever the spellings come from". Sugar is the first spelling when present; with no sugar, the second id-slot key in the map is the conflict. The slot projection is already computed per key (attr-key-refusal calls caller-key-slot unconditionally), so the change is the gate, not new machinery. Compiled mode has no dynamic escape hatch (:rf.ui.compile/dynamic-props-map refuses non-literal props maps; string/symbol keys separately refused via :rf.ui.compile/non-keyword-prop), so the compiled literal half is keyword-pairs only.

SPREAD SEAM (load-bearing caveat from the dossier's second probe — do NOT implement from the three-site list alone): v/spread returns a plain runtime map. The interpreted walks see the post-spread map and refuse automatically, but compiled spread lowers through node/spread-attrs + compiled-react/spread!, bypassing the literal analyzer — patching only the literal sites creates a NEW interpreted/compiled disagreement. Put the cardinality check in a shared helper and apply it to the direct/literal map path AND the runtime-spread seam, with parity tests in both modes. Probed adjacent defect, covered by this same work: [:div#sugar (v/spread attrs)] with a two-id attrs map is refused interpreted, but compiled lowering currently emits both spread ids and drops the sugar id — the shared guard at the spread seam closes it; acceptance includes a sugar+spread refusal row in both modes.

SPREAD-SAFE: out of scope, deterministic by contract. A v/spread-safe caller :id under an owned or sugar id loses by the documented owned-wins law (node.cljc fold-caller), so no ambiguity exists there; the ambiguity this ruling removes lives only on the direct map path and the plain v/spread seam. Whether spread-safe should reject the caller collision or canonicalize its structural result is deliberately NOT decided here and NOT filed — do not let it creep into this bead.

DIAGNOSTICS: reuse :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed (interpreted) and :rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict (compiled); no new always-on id; identical refusal in both modes. Message mirrors the existing shape, naming both offending keys: "The element :div spells its id twice — once as :id and once as :x/id. Two id spellings on one element is an ambiguity; keep one." (keep the existing namespace-is-dropped explanation where a qualified key is involved). check.cljc already categorizes the compiled id as :element-id-declared-twice, which reads correctly for the new case. grammar.cljc currently maps the compiled id's recovery to [:use-a-literal-head], which misdirects for a no-sugar conflict — broaden that recovery with a delete-one-spelling entry (small, mechanical, correctness not polish).

FIXTURE: extend FH-STRUCT-009's :rejected table in place — at minimum [:div {:id "a" :x/id "b"}], plus string/symbol variants matching the existing table's pattern where the interpreted tier admits those spellings singly (e.g. {:id "a" "id" "b"}). The :accepted-keys single-id control rows ([:div {:id "plain"}], [:div {:x/id "alias"}]) stay untouched, proving the guard refuses only the pair. Tests in both modes cover: both pair orders; a nil-valued member; a runtime-assembled/merged map; a map past the array-map threshold; v/spread; sugar+spread; controls of #id alone, each single spelling alone, and :title + :x/title still accepted (proving this is an id-slot cardinality rule, not a namespace ban or alias canonicalization).

GENERALISATION — considered and DECLINED: [:div {:title "a" :x/title "b"}] and every ordinary-attribute pair remain accepted; ordinary attributes stay in author space per rf2-drpa3.93, and a general two-keys-one-emitted-name guard is the front half of the aliasing framework refused twice (.93, .101). A wrong title is a wrong tooltip, self-contained and visible — not a broken cross-reference. Not filed as work. The routed :class one-map last-wins case ({:class "a" :x/class "b"} resolves to "b", no compose) is adjacent and separately filed as rf2-c9kus — NOT part of this rule.

NON-GOALS: no aliasing framework; rf2-drpa3.101's shipped sugar guard and rf2-drpa3.93's class/style routing untouched; donor implementation/ui analyzer stays frozen under EP-0036 (its stale raw-key guard at ui/compiler/analyze.cljc is out of scope — noted so the extra grep hit does not surprise).
MAYOR QUEUE 2026-07-24: RULED refuse the two-id-spelling pair (reuse :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed interpreted + :rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict compiled, no new always-on id; extend FH-STRUCT-009 rejected table; identical refusal at all three guard sites PLUS the runtime v/spread seam; generalisation to ordinary attributes DECLINED). BLOCKED: needs analyze.cljc + react.cljs + node.cljc + tree.cljc — all held by the compiled-emitter cluster worker (rf2-drpa3.130). Dispatch only after that PR merges. Heed the load-bearing caveat in the dossier: v/spread returns a plain runtime MAP, so the seam guard is runtime not build-time.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6837 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact id-slot cardinality owner; no duplicate.

The direct-map and two-id-spread cases are fixed, but the merged PR explicitly leaves the closest common-mode case outside the guard: a compiled element with `#id` sugar plus a spread carrying one id. Direct JVM structural probe on merge cdd55ad97cbbd38f1fc59fe7677f2a2552081423:

    [:div#sugar (v/spread {:id "forwarded"})]

Compiled result: `{:tag :div, :attrs {:id "forwarded"}}`; no refusal, and the sugar id is silently dropped. Interpreted mode refuses the same two declarations. This violates this owner's ruled invariant that sugar occupies the id slot once and any further id-slot spelling is refused in both modes. The added sugar+spread test only uses a spread map that already contains two id keys, so `node/spread-attrs` rejects before the missing sugar-vs-spread comparison is exercised.

Thread the element's sugar-id fact into the compiled spread lowering, or use a comparably small shared check, so a single forwarded id beside `#id` refuses with the established runtime diagnostic in both compiled structural and compiled React paths. Add the discriminating one-id spread case; retain later-arg-wins for two exact `:id` writes inside a standalone spread and avoid any general aliasing framework.
close_reason: PR #6863: threaded the element's #id sugar fact into the shared node/spread-attrs seam (compiled structural via emit_jvm + compiled React via emit_react), so a single forwarded id beside #id refuses at runtime in both compiled paths, message identical to the interpreted element fold. Two-step order (spread's own cardinality first, tag-less; then sugar) preserves parity with the pre-existing two-ids-in-spread case. Reuses :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed; later-arg-wins retained; public interpreted seam untouched. Tests: discriminating one-id (exact+alias) with cross-mode message parity, accept-controls, react emitted-form wiring.

title: Refuse target-specific duplicate members in checker-resolved sets
description:
## Defect

PR #6733 makes checker-resolved maps refuse target-specific duplicate keys, but the adjacent set arm still rebuilds selected members with `(into (empty form) (resolve-children ...))`. A preserved set can contain distinct authored forms that select to the same target member; `into` silently coalesces them before the analyzer sees the target form.

This is the set counterpart of the map collision fixed by rf2-drpa3.98 in #6733 and a residual at the set resolver introduced for rf2-drpa3.85.

## Steps to Reproduce

Load a `.cljc` namespace containing:

    (v/defview collision
      [_]
      [:div {:title (str #{#?(:clj :a :cljs :b) :b})}])

`clojure.tools.reader` reads the CLJ target as `#{:a :b}` and the namespace loads normally. Told to read for `#{:cljs}`, the independent reader rejects the same file with `Duplicate key: :b`. Current `check/check-file` instead returns `:compile-eligible? true` with empty findings because resolution normalizes the invalid CLJS set to `#{:b}`.

The temporary probe exercised the public checker and was removed byte-clean.

## Bounded Correction

At the existing conditional-resolution seam, refuse selected set members that collide before constructing the target set. Cover ordinary and splicing reader conditionals, preserve valid sets and metadata, and keep the checker read-only. Use the existing didactic refusal style; this does not need a custom reader, general analyzer, new public API, or new diagnostic id.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6733.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A public `check-file` regression for `#{#?(:clj :a :cljs :b) :b}` agrees with real target reads: CLJ remains valid and CLJS is refused rather than reported eligible.
2. Pin the same collision through legal `#?@` set splicing, plus symmetric-target and non-colliding controls.
3. Valid resolution still returns a set with its metadata intact and leaves source bytes unchanged.
4. Keep the change local to conditional resolution: no custom/flat-form reader, general source analyzer, public API, or new diagnostic id.
close_reason: PR #6739: resolve-members refuses selected set members that collide, at the same seam the map arm refuses a duplicate key. Cross-checked both directions against clojure.tools.reader (11 refusals / 19 acceptances agree).

title: Keep Freehand error attribution failure-local across overlapping throws
description:
PR #6732 fixed single-failure attribution by relaying the innermost declared view through one process-global `failing-view` atom. That handoff cannot represent two failures awaiting two catches.

A real Chromium probe mounted two sibling `v/error-boundary` occurrences in one React commit, over two different declared throwers. Both boundaries contained and emitted (two egress records), but their summary ids were `{guarded-child, :re-frame.freehand/unknown-view}` instead of the two throwers. React can finish rendering both failed subtrees before either `componentDidCatch` callback consumes the relay; first-writer-wins keeps the first id and drops the second. The merged fingerprint proof does not catch this because it mounts and tears down the two failures serially.

A deterministic JVM probe exposed the same ownership defect: two concurrent `eb/contain` calls were rendezvoused after their occurrence seams noted `:audit/a` and `:audit/b`; the resulting ids were `#{:audit/a :re-frame.freehand/unknown-view}`. The singleton is also vulnerable to stale notes from an uncontained/abandoned throw being consumed by a later unrelated React boundary.

This is not a request for richer diagnostics or a general concurrency framework. Make attribution belong to the particular thrown failure / containment occurrence so independent failures cannot clear, steal, or suppress one another. Keep the existing truthful unknown result when no Freehand occurrence actually observed the throw, and keep the repair internal: no public identity API, component-stack parser, global component registry, or general async-context machinery.

The temporary probes were removed. The clean baseline is green at 510 JVM tests / 3345 assertions and 516 browser tests / 3018 assertions.

Deduplication: searched every Bead state and the live Dolt database for failing-view, unknown-view, overlapping/simultaneous failures, sibling boundaries, and concurrent boundary attribution. rf2-drpa3.95 owns the original catcher-as-thrower defect but is closed by #6732; no existing Bead owns failure-local relay lifetime.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two sibling Freehand boundaries whose known declared descendants fail in the same React commit each emit one summary naming its own thrower; neither becomes unknown or acquires the other failure's id, and their fingerprints remain distinct.
- Two concurrently rendered structural boundaries retain their own known view ids without cross-thread clearing, stealing, or suppression.
- An uncontained/abandoned failure cannot leave attribution that a later unrelated boundary consumes; a nested fallback failure is attributed to the fallback's declared view when observed, otherwise to the existing truthful unknown result.
- Existing deep-descendant/wrapper attribution, foreign-component unknown/loss semantics, initial-mount promotion, reset ordering, and StrictMode once-per-generation behavior remain green on their owning hosts.
- The repair stays private and bounded: no public API, component-stack parser, global component registry, or general async-context framework.
close_reason: PR #6742 - attribution relay keyed by the thrown value's identity (weak-keyed); first-writer-wins scoped to one throw; entry-time scrub in contain retired. Reproduced red on main first across five shapes. Gates: freehand JVM 571/3815, test:freehand 465/3107, test:cljs 10590/53200, test:browser 544/3177, conformance-index + doc-slugs clean. No new diagnostic id, no public surface, egress field set unchanged.

title: F5h Root Manifest consumption in v/hydrate-root: identity from the wire, not from derivation
description:
EP-0036 F5e (rf2-drpa3.42) shipped v/hydrate-root, but it DERIVES identity from the mounted view rather than reading it from the server-emitted Root Manifest.

WHY IT WAS SCOPED OUT: the manifest is the S5 SSR wire (re-frame.ssr.manifest, discovered by adjacency through the :ssr/discover-root-manifest late-bind hook). Reaching it is a packaging step of its own (freehand -> core late-bind <- ssr), and .42 had no server render path to emit a manifest from. The derived prefix agrees with the server today because both ends derive it from ONE function (re-frame.freehand.root-id/default-identifier-prefix), so the current behaviour is correct and forward-compatible — the manifest arm OVERRIDES derivation when it lands.

OUTCOME: v/hydrate-root resolves its manifest positionally (the container's immediately following element sibling) through the core late-bind hook, validates it, and takes :root-id and :identifier-prefix from its CONTENT.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A hydrating root takes root-id and identifier-prefix from the manifest, not from the mounted view — proof: a manifest whose :root-id differs from the derived one.
2. A hydrating root with NO adjacent manifest fails loud :rf.error/root-manifest-invalid data {:missing :manifest} — proof: fixture. NOTE this must be reconciled with the empty-container FALLBACK .42 shipped (FH-ROOT-007): decide and state which precedes which.
3. A missing SSR artefact is :rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing naming the day8/re-frame2-ssr coordinate — distinct from finding nothing adjacent.
4. git grep 're-frame.ssr' implementation/freehand/src stays EMPTY — the hook is the only seam.

SPEC OWNERS: spec/011-SSR.md (Root Manifest v1, Discovery) and spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md (section 4).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #6740. v/hydrate-root reads :root-id and :identifier-prefix from the Root Manifest via the :ssr/discover-root-manifest late-bind hook; the empty-container fallback precedes discovery (stated in Spec 011 and FH-ROOT-007's law); no new public verb and no new diagnostic id. Sibling rf2-drpa3.102 NOT done — premise re-verified and holds; blocked on the new rf2-drpa3.112.

title: F5g interpreted v/client-only and the root-scoped phase flip
description:
EP-0036 F5e (rf2-drpa3.42) shipped hydration and an empty-container fallback, but NOT the Spec 011 'fallback' proper: the client-only site's capability-free fallback plus the root-scoped :server -> :client phase flip.

WHY IT WAS SCOPED OUT: the interpreted tier has no v/client-only boundary at all — client-only exists only in the compiled analyzer (compiler/analyze.cljc). That is a feature slice of its own, not a corner of the roots slice.

OUTCOME: an interpreted v/client-only boundary with a mandatory capability-free :fallback, plus the root-scoped phase value a hydrating root boots at :server and flips to :client in ONE update after the hydration commit — strictly after the mismatch check, as a post-commit passive effect, per-root and independent, with one :rf.ssr/phase-flip info trace. A failed root never flips. A non-hydrating mount is born :client and never flips.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A hydrating root's first render produces the fallback; the flip swaps EVERY client-only site in the root in a SINGLE update (no per-site flip state, no tearing) — proof: fixture with two sites.
2. The flip runs strictly AFTER the adoption commit — proof: a mismatch-free hydration of a root whose client subtree differs from its fallback.
3. Non-hydrating v/mount is byte-identical to today — proof: existing FH rows unchanged.

SPEC OWNERS: spec/011-SSR.md (Phase flip) and spec/004-Views.md (the client-only boundary).
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-07-24: this bead adds a PUBLIC VERB (v/client-only), which makes it an api-manifest SERIAL LANE occupant — seven co-edited files in one PR (facade, REGENERATED spec/api-manifest.edn, metadata row, spec/API.md, docs/api member heading, AND the two non-vacuity anchors that hard-code the surface as a literal name list, only one of which fails loudly). The lane is currently held by rf2-drpa3.40 (v/->react). Do NOT dispatch until .40 MERGES — not when its PR opens, since beads close on PR-open.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6790 (2026-07-24) — reopened this exact feature owner; no duplicate Bead.

Two bounded implementation-quality/truthfulness residues remain at the merged tip 1f1c9b33fc6c8b981f8f88228fb0bc36e4a4eddb:

1. The public `v/client-only` docstring at `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1365` says "the walk enters only the selected arm." The React implementation says and does the opposite: `react.cljs:745-746` calls `emit` for BOTH fallback and client arms before `phase/boundary` selects one. The structural walk enters only the fallback; the browser React walk traverses both arms to build elements and record sites, while React renders/mounts only the selected arm. Make the public contract state that distinction accurately (or change the implementation and tests if selected-arm-only walking is intended). This affects validation/site construction and cost, so the current sentence is materially misleading rather than stylistic.

2. `phase.cljs:121` and `:171` still describe the deleted private `root/adoption-window-closer` as though a no-flipper hydration path remains. PR #6790 deliberately deleted that helper and unconditionally installs the flipper on adoption. Replace those archaeology references with the direct current invariant: the flipper's server commit closes the adoption window and schedules the phase change.

The feature itself is complete and its behavior/tests are sound; this reopen is only for the shipped contract and implementation commentary to describe that behavior truthfully.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6867 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6867). Doc-only reopen residues: v/client-only docstring now describes the React walk entering BOTH arms (build+site-record) vs the structural walk entering only the fallback; phase.cljs archaeology to the deleted root/adoption-window-closer replaced with the direct invariant (flipper's :server commit closes the adoption window + schedules the flip). Feature behaviour/tests unchanged.

title: F5f Freehand SSR server-error projection: a Freehand view failure projects with no private data
description:
EP-0036 F5e (rf2-drpa3.42) shipped the client root surface but did NOT discharge acceptance 7 — 'server-error projection carries no private data'.

WHY IT WAS SCOPED OUT: the projector is re-frame.ssr.error-projector, already implemented and field-set-pinned in the SSR artefact. Freehand cannot depend on day8/re-frame2-ssr (Independence rule — a static freehand -> ssr edge pulls server code into every client bundle), and .42 added no server render path to Freehand, so there was nothing Freehand-side to project.

OUTCOME: once Freehand has a server render path (render-static / the JVM tree -> HTML seam), a Freehand VIEW render failure during SSR projects through the Spec 011 projector, and the projection carries no private data.

ACCEPTANCE: exact field-set assertion on the projected record for a Freehand view-time exception — no app-db, no event history, no props, no ex-data, no host stack.

SPEC OWNER: spec/011-SSR.md (Server error projection).
notes:
BLOCKER CLEARED — re-verified 2026-07-24 against current origin/main source (not the note). Shipped in PR #6779.

Verdict on the four blocker reasons:
  1. 'emit-static-html DOES NOT EXIST' — FALSE NOW. It is DEFINED, not merely
     mentioned: implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/tree.cljc:437,
     a #?(:clj (defn emit-static-html [tree] ...)) that late-resolves
     re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree via resolve-ssr-emitter (:436-459). The lines
     the earlier note may have seen (391, 406) are indeed prose, but the defn
     sits below them. Its sibling render-root-tree (:402) is likewise real and
     is where the compiled root thunk RUNS.
  2. 'render-static is wired to no macro' — FALSE NOW. re-frame.freehand/render-static
     is a defmacro (freehand.cljc:726) over compiler.root/render-static-form
     (root.cljc:769), exported at freehand.cljc:109. Landed with .112.
  3. 'git grep freehand over ssr/src + ssr-ring/src is EMPTY' — STILL TRUE
     (0 hits, both trees), but it is NOT a blocker: it is the Independence
     rule holding. The edge runs the other way — freehand late-resolves ssr at
     render time — so ssr correctly knows nothing about freehand.
  4. 'emit-ui-tree is pure and calls NOTHING' — STILL TRUE (ui_tree.cljc:1000),
     but likewise not a blocker. The view-time failure does not live in the
     serialiser; it lives in tree/render-root-tree, which calls (thunk) — the
     compiled view bodies — before emit-static-html ever sees a tree.

So a Freehand view-time failure is now real and reachable, and the bead was
dispatchable. Two reasons were overtaken by .112; two were true but had been
read as blockers when they are the design holding.

WHAT SHIPPED: no new verb and no new seam — project-render-exception! already
generalises over a Throwable, and render-static propagates a view throw
unchanged. What was missing was a Freehand failure to hand it plus a statement
of who catches. Spec 011 §The server render on the Freehand paved path now says
render-static produces a value rather than driving a request pipeline (no frame,
no response accumulator), so the calling server code is the render-time seam.
Acceptance test: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/ssr_error_projection_jvm_test.clj
— exact map equality against the locked generic-500 shape (so no app-db, event
history, props, ex-data or host stack can ride an equal map), plus a run-time-minted
sentinel the test source never spells, asserted present on the throwable and absent
from the projection. Safe-by-default arm (no :ssr config) and a :dev-error-detail?
positive control prove the projector held the detail and withheld it by policy.

GATES (foreground): freehand JVM 0 (803/5668), ssr JVM 0 (528/2537),
npm test:cljs 0 (10872/54684), npm test:freehand 0 (747/4561). Non-vacuity
checked per test by inversion.

title: Make the #id sugar conflict guard see aliases of id
description:
## Problem

PR #6731 rules aliases reaching React-owned slots, but its supposedly complete slot roster names only `:key`, `:class`, and `:style`. The tag parser's `#id` sugar also owns the emitted `id` slot, and the existing ambiguity guard compares only the raw key `:id`.

Concrete merged-main reproduction:

- `(tree/render [:div#sugar {:x/id "alias"}])` succeeds as `{:tag :div :attrs {:id "sugar" :x/id "alias"} ...}`.
- On CLJS, `(react/element [:div#sugar {:x/id "alias"}])` has one React prop, `props.id == "alias"`; the aliased authored attribute overwrites the sugar after projection.
- `compiler/compile-structural-view` accepts the same literal and its structural lowering likewise carries both `:id "sugar"` and `:x/id "alias"`. The compiled React emitter emits the sugar-id pair before the authored pair; both project to JavaScript `id`, so the latter wins.

The exact `#sugar` + `{:id ...}` spelling is already refused as `:rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict` / `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`, and Spec 004B says two id spellings on one element are an ambiguity the grammar removes rather than ranks. A namespace changes only the authored spelling, not the emitted slot, so `:x/id` currently bypasses the contract and makes structural and React output disagree.

## Consequence

A harmless-looking namespace can silently replace a DOM id while structural tests continue to report the sugar id as well. Selectors, labels, hydration/debug tooling, and any code reading the semantic tree can therefore target a different id from the browser.

## Smallest coherent repair

When tag id sugar is present, make the existing id-conflict guard judge the emitted/caller slot rather than raw `= :id`, in the interpreted front end, React walk, and compiled analyzer. Reuse the current diagnostic ids and the key projection already introduced by #6725/#6731. This need not canonicalize ordinary `:x/id` when no sugar exists and must not introduce a general alias framework.

## Deduplication

Closed `rf2-drpa3.93` owns the key/class/style ruling implemented by #6731 but omits id from its roster. Closed `rf2-2bg4t` makes reserved/rejected refusal use emitted slots; id sugar is accepted and has its separate conflict guard, so it was outside that Bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- `#id` plus any authored key that projects to React's `id` slot is refused consistently before output can diverge; cover namespaced keyword and the interpreted string/symbol spellings where applicable.
- Compiled analysis reuses `:rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict`; interpreted structural/React paths reuse their current malformed-tree diagnostic.
- The exact `:id` behavior remains unchanged, and an ordinary qualified attribute with no sugar keeps its intentionally ruled author-space semantics.
- A cross-host/mode regression probe demonstrates that no accepted form can leave the structural tree with one id while React receives another.
- Extend the existing FH-STRUCT controls and shared key projection; add no aliasing framework or new diagnostic id.
close_reason: PR #6738: all three sites (interpreted structural walk, interpreted React walk, compiled analyzer) judge the emitted SLOT via rules/caller-key-slot — reached as the derived rules/sugar-id-slot and the memoized conv/id-slot-key?, beside the attr-key / attr-key-refusal pair that read the same projection at the same two moments. Existing diagnostic ids only: :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed interpreted, :rf.ui.compile/id-sugar-conflict compiled (now naming the offending key). The question is asked ONLY when the tag carries sugar, which is what keeps it a conflict guard and not an aliasing framework: with no shorthand :x/id stays an ordinary qualified attribute in author space, as ruled, and the exact :id is unchanged. FH-STRUCT-009's :rejected and :accepted-keys tables extended IN PLACE (four sugar-conflict spellings; four accepted rows carrying a :props map as the cross-host/mode probe that the tree's id and React's id are the SAME id). DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE per this bead: [:div {:id "a" :x/id "b"}] with NO sugar is still accepted — filed as rf2-5r1af for a ruling rather than widened here.

title: Give the React B-arm a runnable CLJS evidence lane
description:
## Problem

PR #6730 adds two CLJS-only React B1 workloads and says they are registered into the standing evidence suite, but no runnable evidence lane ever loads them.

Concrete merged-main evidence:

- `re-frame.freehand.bench.b1-react` is required only by its own CLJS test namespace; no runner, build entry, package script, or workflow requires it.
- `re-frame.freehand.bench.runner` requires only `re-frame.freehand.bench.b1`, and `clojure -M:bench` is a JVM process that cannot load the new `.cljs` namespace.
- `.github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml` runs only `clojure -M:bench` and uploads that EDN.
- A current `clojure -M:bench` run reports exactly the two structural workloads (`:B1/finite-template`, `:B1/small-template`); neither `:B1/react-template` nor `:B1/react-small-template` appears.
- `npm run test:freehand` exercises the new workloads inside assertions, but it neither runs the registered suite as a release command nor publishes their distributions/provenance as an evidence artifact.

## Consequence

The counters and tests exist, but the instrument is not operationally available where future `react.cljs` candidates need it. A programmer cannot run the standing evidence command or inspect the scheduled artifact to compare the React arm before and after a candidate; the only published benchmark evidence still contains the JVM structural arm.

## Smallest coherent repair

Give the existing CLJC runner one focused CLJS/Node entry that loads `b1-react`, expose it as a named package command, and run/upload its EDN in the existing Freehand benchmark workflow. Reuse the current registry, runner, provenance, and gate/evidence split. Do not create a second harness, add timing thresholds, or combine this with emitter optimization.

## Deduplication

Closed `rf2-drpa3.88` is the source task completed by #6730; it creates and tests the instrument but does not provide the missing runnable/published CLJS lane. No other all-status Bead mentions either new `:B1/react-*` workload or a CLJS Freehand benchmark runner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented, named CLJS/Node command loads the two `:B1/react-*` workloads and runs them through the existing `bench.runner`/registry path.
- Its stdout remains a valid evidence artifact with both React result records, provenance, distributions, deterministic properties, and the existing 0/1 exit-code law.
- The scheduled/release Freehand benchmark workflow runs that command and uploads the React evidence alongside the JVM evidence.
- A focused non-vacuity check fails if the React workload namespace is no longer loaded or either result disappears.
- Reuse the B-spine; add no timing budget, parallel harness, or emitter optimization.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6788. re-frame.freehand.bench.node — a CLJS/Node ENTRY (not a harness) — plus the :freehand-bench-node build, npm run bench:freehand-node, and a second job in freehand-bench.yml. Runs 8 workloads including both :B1/react-*; stdout parses as EDN. PREMISE WAS HALF-EXPIRED: 'the runner requires only b1' and 'clojure -M:bench reports exactly two workloads' were both false by the time it ran (b2 had landed); the core claim — that nothing loads b1-react — held.

title: (BUG) Preserve explicit nil keys on structural view-boundary nodes
description:
## Defect

PR #6728 / rf2-drpa3.87 correctly adds `:keyed?` to `descriptor/normalize-call` so an explicit nil key can be distinguished from an absent key, and the React boundary path now consumes that fact. The structural boundary path drops it immediately:

```clojure
(let [{:keys [key props]} (descriptor/normalize-call view args)]
  ...
  (node/boundary view-id props key kids))
```

`node/boundary` then emits `:key` only under `(some? key)`. Through the public renderer, `[view {:key nil}]` and `[view {}]` therefore produce identical view-boundary nodes with no `:key`, even though the normalizer reports `{:key nil :keyed? true}` for the first.

This directly contradicts Spec 004B: `:key` is present iff the site was explicitly keyed, and a keyed view-boundary must be distinguishable from an unkeyed one in either mode. Literal elements and fragments already thread key presence separately; only the internal view-boundary seam still flattens presence into value.

Public reproduction on current main:

```clojure
(contains? (tree/render [view {:key nil}]) :key) ; false
(contains? (tree/render [view {}]) :key)         ; false
(descriptor/normalize-call view [{:key nil}])
;; {:key nil, :keyed? true, :props {}}
```

## Bounded correction

Thread the normalizer's existing `:keyed?` fact through interpreted and compiled structural view mounting (including the reserved error boundary) and let `node/boundary` associate `:key` from presence plus value, as `node/element` and `node/fragment` already do. Keep `:key` stripped from body props and outside props equality. No new identity type, coercion policy, registry, or wrapper is needed.

## Dedupe

Fresh full-field search found only closed rf2-drpa3.87, which owns React/presence content loss and is correctly fixed by #6728. No Bead owns the structural view-boundary contract or the unused `:keyed?` result on the tree path.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tree/render` of an interpreted declared-view call with explicit `{:key nil}` contains `:key nil`; the same call with no key omits `:key`, and an ordinary non-nil key remains unchanged.
- The same explicit-nil/absent/valued table passes when the parent or child is compiled, proving the shared `node/mount` crossing preserves key presence in both modes.
- The reserved error-boundary structural node follows the same explicit-presence rule.
- `normalize-call` continues stripping `:key` from the body props and keeping it outside props equality; the React/presence behavior fixed by #6728 remains green.
- The existing element and fragment key-presence behavior is unchanged, and a conformance/public structural test pins the Spec 004B `:key iff explicitly keyed` law.
- No new key type, coercion policy, registry, wrapper node, or public verb is introduced.
close_reason: PR #6738: node/boundary takes key PRESENCE and value separately, as element and fragment already do; both interpreted mount paths (ordinary boundary and the reserved v/error-boundary) thread normalize-call's :keyed? into it. ALSO fixed the interpreted structural FRAGMENT arm, which computed its presence flag as (some? k) — the bead states fragments already thread presence, and node/fragment does, but its caller flattened it, so [:<> {:key nil} …] had the identical defect one line away. :key still stripped from recorded props and outside props equality; element and React paths untouched. structural_key_presence_cljs_test.cljc (JVM+CLJS) asserts all four keyable structural sites and runs the boundary rows in all FOUR parent/child mode pairings from one body.

title: (BUG) Make structural-tree data validation match its EDN round-trip promise
description:
## Defect

PR #6727 / rf2-drpa3.72 adds `non-data` to guarantee that every accepted structural tree is plain EDN which survives `pr-str` -> `clojure.edn/read-string` under the equality assertion used by the suite. The predicate does not actually implement that boundary: after maps/vectors it accepts every remaining `coll?` when its members are acceptable. Some Clojure collections have no EDN spelling.

Public-path reproduction on current main:

```clojure
(def q (conj clojure.lang.PersistentQueue/EMPTY :job))
(def tree (t/render [view {:payload q}]))
(pr-str tree)
;; ... :payload #object[clojure.lang.PersistentQueue ...]
(edn/read-string (pr-str tree))
;; throws: No reader function for tag object
```

The same scalar roster is wrong in both directions:

- `(char 97)` is ordinary JVM EDN (`\a`) and round-trips, but `edn-scalar?` omits characters, so the public renderer refuses it as `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`.
- `##NaN` passes the broad `number?` arm and prints/reads, but the suite's promised equality round-trip is false because NaN is not equal to itself.

This leaves the central claim of the repair false and makes otherwise valid data host-dependent.

## Bounded correction

Make the existing validation predicate describe the values the structural tree can actually promise to print/read under its documented equality contract. Refuse opaque/non-EDN collection implementations before recording them, admit supported EDN scalars such as JVM characters, and handle NaN honestly. Keep the current site-level function marker, nested-value refusal, error id, and error-boundary fallback treatment. Do not add a serializer, tagged-reader registry, schema framework, or deep rewriting pass.

## Dedupe

A fresh full-field Beads search found only the closed source Bead rf2-drpa3.72. No open or closed follow-up owns PersistentQueue, character, NaN, or the mismatch between `coll?`/`number?` and the structural-tree round-trip law.
acceptance_criteria:
- Through the public structural renderer, every accepted prop/event value yields a whole tree that satisfies the documented print/read equality round-trip on its supported host(s).
- A `clojure.lang.PersistentQueue` nested in a prop and in an event value is refused before tree emission with the existing `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`, while ordinary EDN maps, vectors, lists, sets, UUIDs, instants, and nested combinations remain accepted.
- A JVM EDN character is accepted and round-trips; the corresponding CLJS/source spelling remains consistent with the host-neutral contract.
- `##NaN` cannot produce an accepted tree that fails the suite's equality assertion; preserve ordinary finite numbers and infinities where they satisfy the stated law.
- Focused interpreted and compiled structural tests exercise the public path on JVM and CLJS, include a red-before/non-vacuity tooth, and existing Freehand gates pass.
- No codec, custom reader/tag registry, schema framework, or sanitizing copy of accepted props is introduced.
close_reason: PR #6738: non-data now names EDN's own grammar — the scalars plus its FOUR collections (map, vector, set, list) instead of any coll?; records and persistent queues excluded; JVM characters admitted; ##NaN refused. TWO judgement calls stated in the PR body: (1) ##NaN is REFUSED, because it prints and reads back yet is not equal to itself, so a tree carrying one is not equal to itself and the tree is an equality input (fingerprint, structural assertion); print/read alone is the wrong promise, print/read EQUAL is the one made. (2) the queue is refused on BOTH hosts — JVM prints #object[…], CLJS satisfies ISeq and prints #queue […], and neither reader takes the other's, so accepting it where it happens to read back would make one declaration answer a tree on one host and a refusal on the other. The rf2-drpa3.72 ruling (refuse, not represent) is untouched: site-level marker, nested refusal, :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed, error-boundary fallback all unchanged; no codec/reader registry/schema framework/sanitizing copy. Implementation note: == not = decides NaN — Util/equiv returns true on reference identity before comparing values, so (= x x) cannot detect it. Spec 004B §The opaque marker now states the boundary. structural_data_round_trip_cljs_test.cljc runs on JVM+CLJS with a permanent two-part control.

title: (BUG) Refuse target-invalid reader-conditional maps instead of normalizing them
description:
## Problem

PR #6724 / rf2-drpa3.85 states that the checker selects each target's reader-conditional branch as a real compile would. Its map arm does not preserve the target reader's map semantics. The file is first read with conditionals preserved into already-paired map entries; `resolve-conditionals` then resolves each key and value independently and rebuilds with `into`.

Two public `check-file` reproductions placed these maps in the CLJS branch of otherwise loadable `.cljc` views:

```clojure
[:div {:title #?(:clj 1)}]

[:div {#?(:clj :a :cljs :b) 1
       :b 2}]
```

The checker reported both views `:compile-eligible? true` with no findings. An independent `clojure.tools.reader` read with `:features #{:cljs}` rejects the first because conditional elision leaves an odd number of map forms, and rejects the second with `Duplicate key: :b`. The checker's resolver instead fabricates `{:title nil}` for the first and silently overwrites to `{:b 2}` for the second.

These are target branches that cannot be read by the compiler, presented by the checker as eligible. The temporary public fixtures were removed after reproduction.

## Smallest repair

Make map resolution fail loud whenever target selection would elide one side of an entry or make two authored keys collide. It is enough to preserve the real reader's refusal boundary and name the map/target; do not build a flat-form map reader merely to recover invalid source. Keep valid conditional keys and values on the existing fast path.

## Deduplication

Searched Beads for reader-conditional map elision, target-only duplicate keys, and fabricated nil/overwrite behavior. rf2-drpa3.90 owns a different limitation: a legal splicing conditional in a map throws while the source is initially read with `:read-cond :preserve`. Here preserve succeeds, then the checker's own resolver silently constructs a map the target reader rejects. No existing finding owns this false-green.

## Provenance

Correctness and completeness audit of merged PR #6724, following rf2-drpa3.85.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public `check-file` cannot report eligible for a target map whose conditional selection leaves an odd form count; it refuses before fabricating a nil value.
- Public `check-file` cannot report eligible when conditional key selection creates a duplicate target key; it refuses before silently overwriting either entry.
- The refusal is checked against an independent target reader, while valid conditional map keys/values remain eligible and retain metadata.
- rf2-drpa3.90's preserved-reader map-splicing case remains separately scoped; no custom flat-form reader or general source analyzer is introduced.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6733: checker reader-conditional cluster — .90 reframes only the even-number-of-forms reader failure as a refusal; .97 report identity [:view-id :compiled?], disagreeing branches refused, :source anchors findings at their own branch line; .98 refuses half-elided entries and duplicate keys while DROPPING both-sides-elided entries to match the real reader — a case found only by cross-checking what tools.reader ACCEPTS, which a naive rule would have shipped as a false-RED.

title: (BUG) Preserve target declaration identity in reader-conditional checker reports
description:
## Problem

PR #6724 / rf2-drpa3.85 makes `check-file` discover a `v/defview` beneath a top-level reader conditional, but it assumes the CLJ and CLJS branches are one declaration. `declaration-for` chooses `(or clj-decl cljs-decl)` as the report identity and copies only `:params`, `:children-policy`, and `:body` from the CLJS branch. A target-specific name/view id, source anchor, and `:compiled` option are discarded.

A real public `check-file` reproduction used this loaded `.cljc` namespace:

```clojure
#?(:clj
   (v/defview jvm-view
     [_]
     [:div "JVM view"])
   :cljs
   (v/defview browser-view
     [{:keys [tag]}]
     [tag "browser view"]))
```

The checker returned exactly one ineligible report. Its finding correctly contained the CLJS-only form `[tag "browser view"]`, but the report named `.../jvm-view` and both report/finding source pointed to the CLJ branch at line 5. The failing declaration is `browser-view` at line 9; that browser declaration never appears as itself.

This is worse than an unsupported-source refusal: the tool confidently attributes one target's failure to a different declared view. It violates the Spec 004D promise to analyze every branch a compile visits and answer the author which declarations are eligible.

## Smallest repair

Preserve the target branch's truthful declaration context when analyzing and reporting it. If two branches have the same declaration identity, carry the actual branch source and all checker-relevant options into that branch's analysis. If their identities differ, either emit truthful target-specific reports or refuse the divergent identity with a didactic recovery; never merge one branch's body into the other branch's view id.

Keep this inside the existing file reader and report vocabulary. Do not add a second analyzer, source index, or public checker verb.

## Deduplication

Searched Beads for top-level/whole-declaration reader conditionals, branch identity, view-id/source attribution, and host-specific declarations. rf2-drpa3.76 owns the original CLJS-body false-green, rf2-drpa3.85 owns the set and discovery repair just merged, and rf2-drpa3.90 owns the distinct map-splicing reader limitation. None owns this branch-identity collapse.

## Provenance

Correctness and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6724, following rf2-drpa3.85.
acceptance_criteria:
- A top-level reader conditional whose CLJ and CLJS branches declare different view names cannot produce a CLJS finding labeled with the CLJ view id; it either reports each target truthfully or refuses the identity divergence didactically.
- For a same-name declaration whose CLJS branch fails, the finding uses the actual CLJS branch/source anchor and checker-relevant branch options rather than the CLJ branch's source or lowering.
- The existing same-name set/declaration fixtures retain source order, both-target analysis, one-refusal-at-a-time behavior, and read-only operation.
- No second analyzer, general source index, or new public checker verb is introduced.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6733: checker reader-conditional cluster — .90 reframes only the even-number-of-forms reader failure as a refusal; .97 report identity [:view-id :compiled?], disagreeing branches refused, :source anchors findings at their own branch line; .98 refuses half-elided entries and duplicate keys while DROPPING both-sides-elided entries to match the real reader — a case found only by cross-checking what tools.reader ACCEPTS, which a naive rule would have shipped as a false-RED.

title: (BUG) Reject extra interpreted error-boundary children instead of dropping them
description:
## Problem

PR #6714 / rf2-drpa3.35 defines `v/error-boundary` as guarding exactly one child. The compiled checker enforces that grammar, but the interpreted public path accepts additional children and silently keeps only the first.

A direct JVM reproduction rendered:

```clojure
(tree/render
  [v/error-boundary {:fallback [:p "fallback"]}
    [:span "first"]
    [:span "second"]])
```

The resulting boundary tree contained only the first span. The descriptor's `:children-policy :required` admits one or more children, while both tree normalization and the React driver select `(first (:children opts))`. The second declared subtree disappears without a diagnostic. The same declaration is rejected by the compiled analyzer, so authoring behavior also diverges by execution mode.

## Smallest repair

Validate the existing exact-one-child rule on the interpreted normalization path before selecting the guarded child, using one named didactic diagnostic consistent with the compiled refusal. Keep the single guarded region and existing vector grammar; do not add multi-child boundary semantics or another public constructor.

## Deduplication

Searched Beads for extra/multiple error-boundary children, silently dropped children, and exact-one boundary grammar. Existing exact-one work concerns other surfaces; no open finding owns this interpreted boundary data loss or compiled/interpreted divergence.

## Provenance

Correctness and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6714, following rf2-drpa3.35.
acceptance_criteria:
- Interpreted `v/error-boundary` rejects zero or multiple guarded children with a named, didactic diagnostic before any child is discarded.
- A single guarded child retains current interpreted and mounted behavior.
- The compiled and interpreted paths agree on the exact-one-child grammar and test the same zero/one/many table.
- No second child region, fragment coercion, wrapper API, or new public constructor is introduced.
close_reason: SHIPPED PR #6732 (commit 1317603543). Interpreted v/error-boundary refused any child count but one, via a fourth arm of the existing :rf.error/error-boundary-bad-args (no new id). Reproduced on main first: [v/error-boundary {:fallback ...} [:span first] [:span second]] rendered only the first span. read-opts is the chokepoint both interpreted hosts pass through (structural walk + React class ctor), so one check covers both; zero children keeps its more specific owner :rf.error/view-children-policy. Interpreted suite now drives the same zero/one/many table as the compiled analyzer, which gained the zero-child case it was missing. spec/004 + the 009 catalogue row state the rule.

title: (BUG) Attribute mounted error reports to the failing descendant
description:
## Problem

PR #6714 / rf2-drpa3.35 requires an error summary to name the declared view that actually failed and to carry the boundary identity separately. The mounted React driver instead passes `:view-id eb/boundary-view-id` from `componentDidCatch`.

A real Chromium probe mounted `:re-frame.freehand.audit-error-boundary-dom-cljs-test/audit-throwing-child` beneath the public boundary. Once a later same-key render exposed the captured report, its summary named `:re-frame.freehand/error-boundary` as the failing view. The boundary identity is therefore fabricated into the failure field. Because the fingerprint is derived from view id and phase, failures in different descendants of the same boundary also collapse onto the same boundary fingerprint.

This is not a request for richer diagnostics. It is a correctness issue in the minimal record already promised: the record cannot truthfully correlate a failure when it labels the catcher as the thrower.

## Smallest repair

Carry the failing declared-view identity already available at the Freehand occurrence/driver seam into the boundary capture. For any case where exact descendant identity genuinely cannot be retained, report that limitation explicitly rather than substituting the boundary id. Keep the boundary id in its existing separate field; do not add a component-stack parser, public registry, or new identity API.

## Deduplication

Searched Beads for failing-descendant attribution, boundary-view-id, mounted error summaries, and collapsed render-failure fingerprints. rf2-drpa3.37 owns general evidence-schema honesty, not this concrete driver misattribution; no existing finding owns the runtime bug.

## Provenance

Correctness and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6714, following rf2-drpa3.35.
acceptance_criteria:
- A mounted direct declared child that throws is named as the failing view in both safe and private records; the boundary id remains separate.
- Failures from two known declared descendants under one boundary do not acquire the same fingerprint merely because the catcher is shared.
- If a failing declared view cannot be known, the record exposes truthful unknown/loss semantics and never labels the boundary as the thrower.
- No public identity API, global component registry, or component-stack parser is introduced.
close_reason: SHIPPED PR #6732 (commit 993add7ec6). Reproduced on main first on BOTH hosts: the React driver passed :view-id eb/boundary-view-id verbatim, and the structural walk's best-effort guess named the boundary for [:div [throwing-child {}]] and named an innocent wrapper for [wrapper {}]. Fix: each host's OCCURRENCE SEAM notes the view id as the throw unwinds past it (the React function component the interpreted emitter builds; the structural walk's mount), first-writer-wins so the innermost occurrence is the culprit and enclosing bystanders cannot overwrite it; errors/attributed-failure reads the note at the catch. No component-stack parsing, no registry, no identity API, closed egress field set untouched — it fills the :view-id slot that already existed. Unobservable thrower reports :re-frame.freehand/unknown-view with :complete? false and :loss {:reason :failing-view-unobserved}, never the boundary's id. Both hosts now agree exactly, so tree.cljc's boundary-child-view-id is DELETED and contain no longer takes a :view-id. Proven cross-host (three shapes + unknown) and in Chromium (boundary guards a healthy wrapper over the thrower — guarded child, catcher and thrower three different views; two descendants of one boundary fingerprint apart).

title: Rule on aliased keys reaching React's other structural slots
description:
Surfaced by the rf2-2bg4t worker (PR #6725) and DELIBERATELY LEFT UNRESOLVED, because the answer is a real decision rather than a determinable fact. It did not fold it in silently — the right call.

## The observation

rf2-2bg4t made the reserved/rejected refusal total by canonicalizing a direct attribute key the way the emitters classify it (by emitted name) BEFORE judging it. That closed `:x/children` -> React's `children` and `:x/ref` -> `ref`.

But the SAME alias shape reaches React's OTHER structural slots through the direct attribute path, and those keys are neither reserved nor rejected, so the refusal does not see them:

- `:x/key`   -> React's `key`
- `:x/class` -> `className`, around the sugar composition
- `:x/style` -> `style`

## The fork

There are two established precedents in this codebase and they disagree here:

1. REFUSE — what the direct attribute path now does for reserved/rejected names (rf2-2bg4t).
2. CANONICALIZE-AND-ROUTE — what `v/spread-safe` does for ACCEPTED keys (rf2-5pr75 / rf2-xdvob / rf2-izep3).

Both are defensible. Picking one without stating why is not.

## Analysis worth carrying into the ruling

`:x/key` is arguably NOT the same case as the other two. React's `key` is not a prop at all — the reconciler consumes it and it never reaches the DOM. An alias silently routing into it would change reconciliation identity, which is a correctness hazard rather than a cosmetic one. `:x/class` and `:x/style` route to ordinary props, but `:x/class` specifically bypasses the sugar composition (the `.class` shorthand merge), so canonicalize-and-route would have to compose rather than overwrite to be correct.

So the ruling may legitimately SPLIT: refuse the reconciliation-affecting one, route the ordinary ones. Whoever takes this must state the rule and its reason, not just make the tests pass.

## Acceptance

1. An explicit ruling for each of the three, with reasoning, recorded here and in the merging PR body.
2. Whatever is ruled is total across the representations the sibling bead covers (namespaced keyword, string, symbol) and holds IDENTICALLY interpreted and compiled.
3. Legitimate keys are untouched — reuse rf2-2bg4t's accepted-keys control table and extend it rather than writing a parallel one.
4. If any case is ruled REFUSE, it reuses an existing diagnostic id (no new always-on id and its three-way co-edit).

## Non-goals

A general aliasing framework. Revisiting rf2-2bg4t's shipped reserved/rejected behaviour. Touching `v/spread-safe`'s accepted-key routing.
notes:
RULED (mayor, delegated by Mike 2026-07-23). The fork is resolved as a SPLIT, because the three keys are not the same kind of thing.

RULING 1 — :x/key and every alias of it: REFUSE, on the same law rf2-2bg4t established for the reserved names.
REASON: React key is NOT A PROP. The reconciler consumes it and it never reaches the DOM. An alias that silently routes into it changes RECONCILIATION IDENTITY — which element React considers the same element across renders — so the failure mode is not a wrong attribute but wrong element reuse: preserved DOM state landing on the wrong row, or a remount where none was intended. That is the same class of hazard as :x/children (structural divergence), not the same class as a misspelled attribute. Refusing is also the only option that keeps the guard total: canonicalize-and-route would mean an author could address reconciliation identity through a namespaced alias with no declared spelling, which no decision in D001-D021 grants.

RULING 2 — :x/class and :x/style and their aliases: CANONICALIZE-AND-ROUTE, matching what v/spread-safe already does for ACCEPTED keys.
REASON: unlike key, these route to ordinary props that reach the DOM, and the substrate already has a precedent for accepting an aliased spelling of an accepted key and routing it to its emitted slot. Refusing them would make the direct attribute path stricter than the spread path for the SAME key, which is an inconsistency an author would experience as arbitrary. Trust the programmer: an author writing :x/style plainly means style.

⚠️ RULING 2 CARRIES A CORRECTNESS OBLIGATION, and this is the part to get right: :x/class must COMPOSE into the .class sugar, not overwrite it. The tag shorthand (:div.a.b) and an authored class are already merged by the class-string composition on the hot path; a routed alias that assigns instead of composing would silently drop the shorthand classes. Prove composition explicitly with a fixture combining a tag shorthand AND an aliased class. :x/style routes plainly (no sugar to compose).

SCOPE NOTE: the ruling is about the ALIAS shape only. The canonical spellings :key, :class, :style keep exactly their current behaviour — this bead must not change them, and a regression there would be worse than the bug being fixed.

DISPATCH GATE: hold until PR 6725 (rf2-2bg4t) MERGES. This bead extends that PR directly — its caller-key-slot canonicalization, its rejected-slot-replacement reader, and its accepted-keys control table are the foundation here, and dispatching before it lands would conflict in conversion.cljc, rules.cljc and analyze.cljc. When dispatched: EXTEND that control table rather than writing a parallel one, reuse existing diagnostic ids for the refusal (no new always-on id and no three-way co-edit), and hold the ruling identically in interpreted and compiled modes. The worker must put this ruling, its reasoning, and the rejected alternative in the PR body.
close_reason: Ruled and implemented in PR #6731. SPLIT: :key aliases REFUSED (key is not a prop — an alias changes reconciliation identity, the :children hazard class), reusing :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed and :rf.ui.compile/rejected-prop-spelling; :class and :style aliases CANONICALIZED AND ROUTED (ordinary props, matching v/spread-safe's accepted-key routing), with :class COMPOSING into the .class#id sugar. One canonicalization (rules/canonical-attr-key) applied at build time in analyze.cljc and at render time in node.cljc + react.cljs. FH-STRUCT-009's :rejected and :accepted-keys tables extended in place (accepted-keys gains a :props column pinning React output); new structural-slot-alias-jvm-test proves both modes from one declaration. Canonical spellings asserted unchanged. Ruling, reasoning and the rejected alternative are in the PR body.

title: Make FH-STRUCT-010 non-vacuously prove every manifest roster coordinate
description:
## Problem

PR #6721 / rf2-drpa3.82 promises that every finite compiled-manifest roster entry is source-locatable, and says FH-STRUCT-010 now pins the per-entry key shape with entry counts that keep the proof non-vacuous. The executable census does not exercise that promise for four of the six rosters.

Across every view in `manifest_views.cljc`, `:subscriptions`, `:slots`, `:html-sites`, and `:frame-ops` are all empty. Only `:events` (three entries) and `:crossings` (one entry) enter `every-roster-entry-is-source-locatable`. - `clojure -M:test`: 487 tests / 3184 assertions, 0 failures
- `npm run test:freehand`: 359 tests / 2499 assertions, 0 failures

The mutation was restored byte-identical. Equivalent omissions in the frame-op and HTML arms have no non-empty FH-STRUCT-010 row either. A future refactor can therefore regress most of the shipped promise while the named conformance law stays green.

Extend the existing census/fixture or add one compact table-driven manifest probe so each of `:subscriptions`, `:events`, `:slots`, `:html-sites`, `:frame-ops`, and `:crossings` contributes at least one real entry and is asserted through the highest public surface available on both hosts.
