title: Compile checker crashes on a map splicing conditional (:read-cond :preserve reader limitation)
description:
## Problem

The compile checker reads source with `:read-cond :preserve` so it can select each target's branch itself (the JVM reader's `:clj` platform feature is unconditional, so `:allow` always collapses to `:clj`).

Clojure's map reader counts the forms it read BEFORE any splicing is applied, and under `:preserve` a splicing conditional stays one form. So a legal map literal:

    {:a 1 #?@(:clj [:b 2])}

reads fine under `:read-cond :allow` (giving `{:a 1 :b 2}`) and throws under `:preserve`:

    java.lang.RuntimeException: Map literal must contain an even number of forms

Confirmed on this tree, both directions. A source file containing that shape therefore makes `check-file` throw a raw reader exception instead of answering a report — a false-ERROR (the opposite failure mode to the false-greens the placement work fixed), with a message that says nothing about the checker or what to do.

## Scope

Narrow. It is a limitation of the JVM reader in `:preserve` mode, not a hole in the checker's own branch selection — sets, vectors, seqs and declaration-level conditionals are all covered. Reaching this shape would need the checker to read maps as flat form sequences (its own map reader), which is squarely the "general-purpose source analyzer" non-goal.

## Options

1. Catch the reader exception and re-throw as a checker refusal naming the shape and the workaround (write the conditional around the whole map, or around each entry's value) — cheap, honest, no new reader.
2. Read maps flat and assemble after resolution — correct but a custom reader.

Option 1 is the pre-alpha-proportionate answer unless the shape turns out to be common.

## Origin

Found while covering set and declaration-level placements.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6733: checker reader-conditional cluster — .90 reframes only the even-number-of-forms reader failure as a refusal; .97 report identity [:view-id :compiled?], disagreeing branches refused, :source anchors findings at their own branch line; .98 refuses half-elided entries and duplicate keys while DROPPING both-sides-elided entries to match the real reader — a case found only by cross-checking what tools.reader ACCEPTS, which a naive rule would have shipped as a false-RED.

title: Preserve explicit nil keys in interpreted Freehand presence
description:
## Problem

PR #6713 promises one keyed presence identity contract across interpreted and compiled Freehand. An explicit nil key is legal authored key presence and React coerces it to the identity string "null"; the imported runtime says this explicitly. The interpreted emitter erases it before React sees it.

All three interpreted child paths test the key value with some?:

- react-props adds an element key only when (some? (:key attrs));
- boundary-node adds a declared-view key only when (some? key);
- fragment-node builds props only when (some? k).

Thus these forms all produce React elements whose .key is nil:

    [:div {:key nil} "draft"]
    [child-view {:key nil}]
    [:<> {:key nil} ...]

A temporary focused CLJS probe established the control and failure:

    React/createElement with #js {:key nil} => .key "null"
    interpreted element                      => .key nil
    interpreted view boundary                => .key nil
    interpreted fragment                     => .key nil

Under v/presence, collect-elements drops those keyless elements, so a legal explicit identity becomes silent content loss (with only the generic keyless development advisory). Compiled analysis tracks :key presence separately and emits the nil key expression to React, which becomes "null", so changing only {:compiled true} changes whether the child exists. normalize-call also returns only the value and currently cannot distinguish an absent view key from an explicit nil key.

No existing Bead covers explicit-nil React-key parity; rf2-vxgfnd.96.1 fixed keyed literal admission in the donor compiler, not this Freehand interpreted lowering.

## Outcome

Preserve authored key presence independently of key value in every interpreted React child path. Explicit nil must reach React and participate in presence as the "null" identity; an absent :key must remain absent. Keep :key stripped from a declared view's props and outside props equality.

## Non-goals

No new key type, generated key, key registry, identity coercion policy, or prohibition on nil keys.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6713.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Focused CLJS tests show interpreted literal elements, declared-view boundaries, and keyed fragments each produce React .key "null" for an explicit {:key nil}, matching React and compiled emission.
2. The same three forms still produce a nil React key when :key is absent; value nil and key absence cannot be conflated.
3. A real mounted interpreted v/presence regression renders an explicit-nil-key child, drives :mounting -> :present -> :unmounting -> removal, and never drops it as keyless.
4. Duplicate explicit-nil claimants collide in React's string-coerced "null" domain and retain the first claimant, matching the existing duplicate-identity law.
5. normalize-call continues stripping :key from child props and keeping it outside props equality while retaining enough presence information for the emitter.
close_reason: PR #6728: all three interpreted child paths now ask key PRESENCE with contains?; normalize-call reports :keyed?. Explicit nil reaches React as "null" in element, boundary and fragment paths; absent stays absent.

title: Put per-site source coordinates in compiled manifests
description:
## Problem

PR #6716 makes v/manifest a tooling surface for finite compiled sites and Spec 004D states: "Source coordinates ride each site so a manifest fact and a build-log line name the same lexical position." The implementation does not satisfy that contract.

structural-manifest projects:

- subscriptions as {:sid :query :path}
- frame operations as {:sid :path}
- HTML sites as {:path}
- crossings directly from analyzer entries containing only {:view-id :lowering :path}

Only event and slot entries currently carry :source-coord. The analyzer does not record source coordinates for subscription, frame, HTML, or crossing sites, so the projection cannot preserve them.

FH-STRUCT-010 checks roster counts, capabilities, and the elision verdict, but never checks the promised per-site field shape. A manifest can therefore pass all gates while most facts cannot name their source line.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the analyzer against forms carrying explicit line/column metadata and print the public manifest projection. A subscription at line 42 and frame read at line 43 currently produce:

    {:subscriptions [{:sid "..." :query [:count] :path [0]}]
     :frame-ops     [{:sid "..." :path [1]}]}

Neither entry contains :source-coord. The same omission is visible directly in compiler.cljc structural-manifest and the analyzer add-site! records for :subs, :frame-ops, :htmls, and :views.

## Outcome

Make each finite manifest roster entry source-locatable using the existing source-coordinate representation and analyzer metadata. Preserve the existing sid/path/query fields; do not add a second source-map format, indexing service, or separate tooling database.

Update the executable FH-STRUCT-010 contract so a count-only manifest can no longer read green.

## Deduplication

Searched existing Beads for manifest source coordinates, source coordinates, and FH-STRUCT-010; no issue owns this gap.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every entry in :subscriptions, :events, :slots, :html-sites, :frame-ops, and :crossings carries the established :source-coord shape whenever authored source metadata is available.
2. A table-driven test places at least two different site kinds on distinct known lines/columns and asserts their exact source coordinates through public v/manifest, not only through analyzer internals.
3. FH-STRUCT-010 pins the required per-entry keys as well as roster cardinality, capabilities, and the elision verdict.
4. Existing :sid, :path, :query, crossing mode, and other useful fields remain intact and serializable.
5. Spec 004D and the v/manifest docstrings remain truthful without introducing another manifest or source-map mechanism.
6. Freehand JVM and CLJS suites plus the conformance-index check pass.
close_reason: SHIPPED PR #6721 (commit fc35979855). AC1: :subscriptions/:frame-ops/:html-sites/:crossings now carry :source-coord alongside the existing :events/:slots — analyze.cljc's event-source-coord generalised to site-source-coord and recorded on the four remaining site kinds; structural-manifest projects it (crossings now an explicit select-keys rather than pass-through). No second source-map format, no index, no tooling DB, NO new public verb; :sid/:path/:query/crossing mode/:inline? untouched and serializable (AC4). Coordinate is TOTAL and never invented: the reader anchors lists not vectors, so a (v/event …) handler locates itself and a [child {…}] crossing inherits its declaration's position — the same discipline check.cljc established. Consequence recorded in 004D: the coordinate is the COMPILING reader's, so a .cljc site reports a narrower position under CLJS (tools.reader anchors every collection) than under the JVM — correct, not drift. AC3: FH-STRUCT-010 fixture gains :required-keys (per-roster entry key set) + :source-coord-keys; census suite asserts both on BOTH hosts plus entry counts so the key gate cannot pass over an empty table. AC2: new JVM suite manifest-source-coord-jvm-test pins EXACT coordinates for two site kinds of different reader provenance in one declaration, through public v/manifest (JVM-only because the reader is the variable; the host-neutral half is FH-STRUCT-010). AC5: 004D §The finite manifest + structural-manifest/v-manifest docstrings updated truthfully; docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md deliberately untouched (elided example, serial verb lane). AC6: JVM 468/3077, test:freehand 340/2398, test:cljs 10461/52478, conformance-index + keyword-drift + doc-slugs + mkdocs --strict all 0. Two pre-existing crossing assertions now dissoc :source-coord alongside :path. Non-vacuity probes red the named tests on both lanes; both files restored byte-identical.

title: Checker: pure-.cljs build-environment workflow + 004D host-claim wording (follow-up to drpa3.76)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-drpa3.76 / PR #6717, which fixed the .cljc reader-conditional false-green (checker now reads with :read-cond :preserve and analyzes BOTH branches). Two ACs from drpa3.76 were deliberately left out of that PR's scope and remain open:

AC2 (pure-.cljs workflow): a pure .cljs namespace has no loaded JVM namespace for live-namespace to find, and check-file today refuses it with 'is not loaded'. Define and test the supported .cljs/CLJS-target workflow: either check-file can receive or derive a real CLJS analyzer environment (a genuine &env), or it refuses .cljs/CLJS-target checks explicitly and didactically. No fake loaded JVM namespace. drpa3.76 scoped itself to .cljc views (whose namespace IS loaded on the JVM), so this is untouched.

AC4 (spec wording): update spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md section 'The read-only checker' > 'Where the checker runs' to name the real target/build-context contract — the checker reads reader conditionals with :read-cond :preserve and analyzes the branch each compilation target compiles, not unconditionally :clj. Also review 009 tool-contract wording. NOTE: spec/004* was hot-zone / in-flight during drpa3.76's dispatch, which is why the PR left the prose to a follow-up; verify the file settled before editing.

drpa3.76's PR docstrings in check.cljc already state the preserve-and-select contract accurately; this bead carries only the SPEC prose + the pure-.cljs runtime decision.
close_reason: SHIPPED PR #6721 (commit 5b87f4dc29). AC2 (pure-.cljs workflow): check-file now REFUSES a .cljs path up front, before the file is read — a .cljs namespace is never loaded on the JVM and a genuine cljs.analyzer env exists only inside a running ClojureScript compile, so there is no build context and no stand-in is loaded or invented. Refusal carries {:target :cljs} so a tool can discriminate it from the unloaded-namespace refusal, and names the two workflows that DO answer (write it .cljc — whose :cljs branch drpa3.76 already analyzes — or let the build answer). Previously such a file fell through to live-namespace and got 'is not loaded' plus a (require …) an author cannot perform. AC4 (spec): 004D §Where the checker runs now states the FORMS half — conditionals read :read-cond :preserve, each target's branch selected by the checker past the always-present :clj platform feature, every branch a compile visits analyzed — plus the .cljs refusal. spec/009 §The compile checker report needed NO change (it delegates shape+laws to 004D and records only id provenance) and was not touched; it is also in flight. Gates: JVM 468/3077, test:freehand 340/2398, test:cljs 10461/52478, keyword-drift + conformance-index + doc-slugs + mkdocs --strict all 0. Non-vacuity probe reds the named test, restored byte-identical.

title: Enroll re-frame.freehand.test in the canonical public API
description:
## Problem

PR #6712 introduces `re-frame.freehand.test` as a PUBLIC dev/test surface with five supported vars: `render`, `find`, `find-all`, `attrs`, and `text`. The namespace is nevertheless marked `^:no-doc` and is absent from every canonical public-API inventory surface that already protects `re-frame.freehand`:

- `spec/API.md` has no `re-frame.freehand.test` testing-tier row;
- `re-frame.api-manifest.gen/public-namespaces` enumerates `re-frame.freehand` but not its public test sibling;
- the CLJS manifest probe requires and reconciles `re-frame.freehand` but not `re-frame.freehand.test`;
- the metadata sidecar and generated `spec/api-manifest.edn` therefore carry none of the five vars.

Concrete evidence on merged main: `(ns-publics 're-frame.freehand.test)` returns `(attrs find find-all render text)`, while both `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` and `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.api-md-check` remain green (`517 public vars`, `216 var-rows`). The drift gate is green because it never looks at the new public namespace.

## Consequence

The paved test API is invisible to the canonical machine-readable API, absent from the human API catalogue, and hidden from generated namespace documentation despite being the programmer-facing outcome of F1e. A later rename, signature drift, accidental export, or removal in this namespace will not red the public-API gate. That weakens exactly the programmer/AI discoverability and boundary protection the API manifest exists to provide.

## Outcome

Enroll `re-frame.freehand.test` in the existing API catalogue and JVM/CLJS manifest machinery as a testing-tier public sibling, and make its five-name surface discoverable in generated API documentation. Reuse the current manifest, sidecar, and probe; add no parallel catalogue or new validation framework.

## Deduplication

`rf2-drpa3.63` is closed and enrolled the `re-frame.freehand` facade that existed then; #6712 added this separate public sibling afterward. `rf2-drpa3.73` covers stale `{:compiled true}` prose in the facade docs, not test-surface inventory. `rf2-drpa3.53` owns eventual all-row conformance execution, not public-API boundary reconciliation.

## Non-goals

Do not broaden the five-name test API, add behavior/click helpers, absorb the mounted tier early, or repair unrelated stale compiled-tier wording.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `spec/API.md` explicitly catalogues `re-frame.freehand.test` and exactly `render`, `find`, `find-all`, `attrs`, and `text` at the testing tier, owned by Spec 008.
2. The JVM generator and CLJS probe both enumerate/reconcile `re-frame.freehand.test`; the five vars appear in `spec/api-manifest.edn` with intentional classification and host-appropriate signatures.
3. A focused negative control proves that adding or removing a public var in `re-frame.freehand.test` makes the existing manifest gate red on each applicable host; restoring it returns green.
4. The namespace and its five vars are discoverable in the generated public API docs; `^:no-doc` does not hide a surface the product calls public.
5. Existing API-manifest, API.md projection, Freehand JVM, and Freehand CLJS gates remain green, with no second catalogue or validation framework.
close_reason: Closed

title: Canonicalize direct attribute keys before reserved-prop refusal
description:
## Problem

PR #6705 added `conversion/attr-key-refusal` so reserved and rejected props cannot make the interpreted structural and React emitters disagree. The refusal compares the raw map key (`= :ref`, or direct lookup in `rules/rejected-prop-spellings`), but both emitters later classify/project a key by `(name k)`. The compiler has the same split: it accepts any keyword key, checks the rejected map by raw identity, then emits `(rules/react-prop-name (name k))`.

That leaves alternate representations of the same emitted prop outside the guard. Reproduced on current main:

- `(tree/render [:div {:x/children "ghost"}])` succeeds and carries `:x/children` structurally. The React emitter projects that key to the reserved `children` prop, so the same declaration renders `ghost` content absent from the structural children.
- String and symbol `"children"` / `'children` keys are likewise accepted by the interpreted walk and project to `children`.
- `(macroexpand '(v/defview alias {:compiled true} [_] [:div {:x/children "ghost"}]))` succeeds, while the exact `:children` spelling is rejected.
- The same bypass shape exists for `:x/ref` and namespaced/string/symbol forms of the rejected raw-markup names. Their values still pass through the attribute-value grammar, but the promised reserved/rejected-key policy is not actually total.

This is not a duplicate of rf2-5pr75 / rf2-xdvob / rf2-izep3: those beads canonicalized the runtime `v/spread` / `v/spread-safe` path. This is the direct element-attribute path in the interpreted walks and literal compiled analyzer.

## Smallest repair

Classify a direct attribute key once through the same accepted author-name/canonical-slot rule used for emission, and base reserved/rejected refusal on that result. Alternatively, if namespaced direct attribute keys are intentionally outside the grammar, reject them explicitly and consistently before emission. Reuse the existing rule-table vocabulary; do not add a general compatibility parser.

## Provenance

Completeness/correctness audit of merged PR #6705, following rf2-drpa3.69.
acceptance_criteria:
- `:x/children` cannot reach React's `children` slot through a direct attribute map: interpreted structural and React walks reject it consistently, and a compiled declaration rejects it at analysis time.
- `:x/ref` and alternate accepted key representations of the current rejected-prop roster receive the same verdict as their exact spellings in every applicable mode; the raw-markup trust boundary still has only `(v/html ...)` as its visible spelling.
- Tests include the namespaced-key case in both interpreted emitters and the compiled analyzer, plus a behavioral React control proving no attribute-path alias can create DOM children absent from the structural tree.
- Ordinary allowed attributes and author-space structural keys keep their current semantics.
- Refusal and emission share one key canonicalization rule; no second alias table or general prop parser is introduced.
notes: DISPATCH LOST TO A HARNESS STALL (mayor, 2026-07-23): a worker was dispatched and killed by the stream watchdog (600s no-progress) along with three others simultaneously — a systemic harness event, not a work problem. Its worktree (attr-key-canon-2bg4t, branch worker/attr-key-canon-2bg4t) survived with ZERO commits and ZERO uncommitted edits, so NO work was preserved; its last position was "Now the React emitter side", meaning it had analysed the conversion half but nothing reached disk. Re-dispatch FRESH rather than resuming — there is nothing to salvage. Reuse the brief shape: canonicalize the key the same way the emitters classify it (by name) BEFORE applying the refusal, make it total across namespaced-keyword/string/symbol forms for both the reserved names and the rejected-prop roster, reuse the existing diagnostic id, and PROVE legitimate namespaced attributes and data-* still pass (an over-broad fix is worse than the bug). Note conversion.cljc was heavily performance-tuned in PR 6720 after this bead was filed — read the current code, and if the canonicalization lands on the per-attribute hot path prefer reusing an existing memoized projection.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6725. attr-key-refusal and check-rejected-spelling! now reduce the key with rules/caller-key-slot — the same canonicalization the runtime spread deny compares — and judge the emitted SLOT, so refusal and projection agree by construction. Total across namespaced-keyword/string/symbol forms for the reserved ref slot and the whole rejected-prop roster, in both interpreted walks and the compiled analyzer. Existing diagnostic ids reused; no new layer of checking. Over-broadness controls assert :x/title, :x/tab-index, :x/data-*, :class, :for and :x/on-click keep their exact semantics, and a behavioural browser control mounts a children prop through createElement around the emitter to prove the consequence is real. Gates: freehand JVM 489/3218, test:freehand 362/2550, test:cljs 10483/52632, test:browser 501/2912, conformance-index + doc-slugs exit 0 — all green.

title: Make the remaining skills Freehand-aware
description:
THE SKILLS-AWARENESS step of the EP-0036 epic. Filed 2026-07-23 (Mike): the epic had no step making the other skills Freehand-aware — F6c (rf2-drpa3.55) only removes stale donor references mechanically; it does not teach Freehand.

## Scope

The skills that reference re-frame.ui or teach the view layer, made genuinely Freehand-aware rather than merely de-referenced from the dead donor name:
- skills/re-frame2-ui — the re-frame.ui skill itself; it BECOMES the Freehand skill (rename + retarget content).
- skills/re-frame2 — the core authoring skill; its view-layer guidance points at Freehand.
- skills/re-frame2-setup — scaffolding a new app uses Freehand.
- skills/re-frame2-pair, skills/re-frame2-implementor, skills/re-frame2-improver, skills/re-frame2-xray — each made aware of Freehand views where it touches the view layer.
Verify the exact set at dispatch with: grep -rl 're-frame.ui' skills/ — the roster changes as the migration lands.

## Outcome

An AI (or programmer) invoking any of these skills is guided toward Freehand for view work, with correct v/defview / v/sub / event / controller / host-boundary idioms, not toward re-frame.ui or a raw adapter. This is content awareness, not a rename sweep — that mechanical half is F6c's.

## Sequencing

After the Freehand surface is stable (F5) and ideally after the guide (rf2-fby7o) and migration skill exist, so all three teach the same API. Cluster the smaller per-skill edits where they share a surface; keep re-frame2-ui (the largest, a full retarget) separate.

## Acceptance

1. Any Freehand idiom a skill emits compiles against the shipped surface — spot-checked, not eyeballed.
2. Every skill's allowed-tools and references reconcile: the skill-drift gate and skill<->MCP drift gate pass.
3. No skill leaf carries an rf2- bead id.
4. No remaining skill steers view work toward re-frame.ui as a live target (historical/migration mentions are fine).

## Non-goals

The mechanical donor-name removal (F6c owns that); the migration skill (sibling bead); deleting any skill (skill removal, if any, rides F6e donor deletion).
notes:
MAYOR NOTE 2026-07-24 — PARTIAL in PR #6775. DO NOT CLOSE ON THAT MERGE.

DELIVERED: content-awareness edits across re-frame2 (new Freehand section in views.md + routing), re-frame2-ui (repositioned as the donor-maintenance skill), re-frame2-setup, re-frame2-pair, re-frame2-xray, re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-implementor, plus skills/README.md, the docs-site mirror and mkdocs nav.

The rename therefore needs the generator to move with it AND a Freehand context sheet that does not yet exist — both outside that dispatch fence. The worker reported it rather than working around it, which is right.

WHEN RE-DISPATCHING: this is a generator + skill rename that must land in ONE PR, because the --check gate compares the generated file at its declared path. Treat it as its own bounded task, not as a docs edit. Confirm whether a Freehand context sheet is wanted at all before assuming the rename is the goal — it may be that re-frame2-ui SHOULD keep its name while it remains the donor-maintenance skill, and the rename only becomes right at donor deletion (F6e).

RENAME-TRAP EVIDENCE WORTH KEEPING: the worker grepped the gates before editing and found check_donor_inventory.py fires DONOR-LEDGER-DRIFTED on a PENDING row whose files no longer carry donor material. Stripping the migration skill donor vocabulary made its REPLACE row disposable, so spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md flips that one row pending->done in the SAME commit. It also confirmed the skills-check minimum-reference floor is 100 against a corpus of ~505, so these edits stay well clear.
PR #6775 THREE-LENS AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-24) — append to the existing in-progress source owner; no duplicate Bead. The new Freehand paragraph in skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md correctly says a make-frame opts map gives the root ownership and v/unmount! is total, then incorrectly says the old frame-root no-destroy-on-unmount law still holds. A port following the skill can leak root-owned frames. PR #6827 COMPLETENESS RESIDUAL (2026-07-24) — REOPENED exact closed source; no duplicate Bead.

The one-line ownership correction is correct, but this Bead was closed while its own durable note and the PR body say the `re-frame2-ui` rename + Freehand context-sheet generator move “remains its own held task.” No separate Bead exists (all-state search for the rename/context sheet finds only this owner), so closing it makes the explicitly retained work ownerless and prematurely releases its blocking edge to donor deletion.

That can still steer a port away from the intended paved path.

BOUNDED DISPOSITION: keep this exact owner open and decide the already-recorded demand-gated choice—either (a) a named consumer justifies a Freehand context sheet, in which case move generator + skill atomically, or (b) `re-frame2-ui` deliberately remains the donor-maintenance skill until F6e, in which case record that disposition and remove the stale future-tense targeting fence. description:

Do NOT dispatch until the public surface is stable enough that the guide will not be stale on arrival — the signal is the F5 composition/integration slices being largely landed (slots, theming, v/->react, roots/SSR), since the guide covers all of them. A guide authored ahead of that is rewritten twice.

Deleting the draft (it remains the design record); documenting unshipped surface; a Reagent-to-Freehand migration skill (that is the sibling skill bead); reference documentation (the spec owns that; docs/core/reference.md was retired).

title: Promote the Freehand draft guide into the tracked design record
description:

## Why

The draft is 22 markdown files (~252K) covering install, mental model, building a view, events and handlers, reactivity and ownership, state, semantic controllers, composition, presence, forms, host boundaries, js-libraries, compilation, SSR, testing, debugging, accessibility, limits and escapes, adoption, and a vs-reagent comparison. It currently sits in `ai/`, which is gitignored and local-only — so it exists on exactly one machine, is invisible to every worker and to a clean clone, and would be lost with that checkout.

Promoting it into the design record makes it durable, reviewable, and usable as the base for the guide-authoring work (see the sibling bead).

## Scope

`docs/design/freehand/` is the durable, frozen supporting record per EP-0036, and `mkdocs.yml` already excludes `design/freehand/` from the published site because its links are source-tree-oriented. So the draft lands as a design artefact, NOT as published documentation.

title: Make the Freehand public API docs tell the truth about {:compiled true}
description:
PR #6706 formalises `re-frame.freehand` as the public door, but the two user-facing API catalogues it added/edited describe the already-landed compiled option as unavailable.

Concrete contradiction on main:

- `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc` accepts `:compiled` in the closed option roster, documents `{:compiled true}` as the one-line promotion, and the Freehand suite proves `{:compiled false}` / compiled promotion.
- `rf2-drpa3.26` (F3b compiled selection) is closed and `spec/004-Views.md` correctly says the option raised only until that tier landed.
- `docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md` says the compiled tier is a declared vacancy and says `{:compiled true}` is a reserved-but-unimplemented key that raises.
- `spec/API.md` repeats both claims in the canonical Freehand door paragraph and `defview` row.

CONSEQUENCE: the exact public-door documentation introduced to improve programmer and AI ergonomics tells consumers that the supported one-line promotion is invalid. It also makes the canonical API catalogue disagree with the implementation, the normative spec, and the landed F3b contract.

SMALLEST COHERENT REPAIR: correct those two API documents to include `:compiled` (`false` default / `true` compiled tier) in the closed option roster, remove only the stale compiled-tier vacancy wording, and use a genuinely unimplemented props-schema key when illustrating reserved-option rejection. Do not add another catalogue, generator, compatibility path, or validation framework.

title: B-spine falsifiability test is itself timing-dependent and flakes under load
description:
Observed by the F3c worker while running gates under concurrent load, and reported unprompted as "one flake observed, not mine".

`re-frame.freehand.bench.falsifiability-cljs-test/the-moved-timing-really-moved` failed once with a timing ratio of 8.79 against a required minimum of 10, and passed on every other run.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The B-spine harness exists to enforce D021's split: deterministic properties are hard gates, timing is evidence with NO automatic numeric pass/fail. This particular test is a control proving that criterion 3 is meaningful — it asserts the timing measurement REALLY MOVED, because proving that an unchanged timing does not red the build proves nothing.

But the control is implemented as a numeric timing threshold, which is precisely the shape D021 forbids everywhere else. So the harness that mechanises "no timing thresholds" currently contains one, and it flakes for exactly the reason D021 gives for banning them: wall-clock is load-dependent. Under six concurrent workers on this box, a 50x workload produced an 8.79x ratio.

A flaky gate is worse than a missing one — it trains readers to re-run rather than read, which is how a real regression gets waved through.

## Options, for the implementing worker to weigh

1. Make the control deterministic rather than temporal — assert the harness ROUTED the measurement as evidence and that a gate-registered property is untouched, without depending on how much wall-clock moved.
2. Keep a timing assertion but make it robust — compare against a same-run baseline rather than an absolute ratio, or require only a directional move.
3. Widen the margin — cheapest, but leaves a load-dependent gate in place and only moves the flake threshold.

Prefer 1 if it can still prove what the control exists to prove: that the fixture genuinely did more work, so a green criterion-3 result is not vacuous.

## Acceptance

The control still fails if the timing measurement is wired as a gate rather than evidence (its real purpose), and does NOT fail under heavy concurrent load. Demonstrate the second by running it while the machine is loaded, not on an idle box.

## Non-goals

Removing the control; relaxing D021; adding retry logic to hide the flake.
close_reason: SHIPPED #6719 (merged): the B-spine falsifiability control no longer asserts a wall-clock ratio — the exact shape D021 forbids, previously sitting inside the harness that mechanises the ban. Replaced with :falsifiability/render-nodes (exact nodes rendered across the burst), which the repeats knob moves by EXACTLY its factor while leaving the first tree node count untouched; :move is now 50 deterministically. The wall-clock ratio survives as :timing-ratio, reported but deciding nothing. BOTH criteria demonstrated: still reds when mis-wired as a gate (deliberately re-declared render-ms as a gated :value with a threshold — 16 failures, 1 error, named directly); and does NOT fail under load (24 cores oversubscribed 2:1 with 48 burners alongside live workers, 50 runs — :move was 50 in ALL 50 while :timing-ratio ranged 22.40-99.34). ROOT CAUSE of the original 8.79: the ratio DENOMINATOR is the baseline arms p50, ~3.5ms over 5 samples; the moved arm (~91ms) averages its noise away but the baseline cannot, so one scheduling stall on the median baseline sample collapses the ratio. The fragile end was the small arm, not the big one — which is why widening the margin would not have been honest.

title: api-manifest CLJS probe inlines spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn with no build dependency: a sidecar-only edit can leave the probe asserting stale rows
description:
SAME DEFECT SHAPE as rf2-drpa3.65 (Freehand conformance fixtures), found while fixing it.

implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj slurps spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn at MACRO-EXPANSION time (find-sidecar + slurp in emit-cljs-only-rows / emit-classification-rows / emit-ui-test-signature-contract). shadow-cljs has no dependency edge from re-frame.api-manifest.cljs-manifest-probe-cljs-test to the sidecar, so a SIDECAR-ONLY edit does not invalidate the probe namespace's compile cache and the compiled probe keeps reconciling against the PREVIOUS rows.

Impact is narrower than the Freehand case: the sidecar usually changes in the same commit as the source whose publics moved, and a source change does invalidate. But a sidecar-only reconciliation (the common 'fix the drift report' edit) can report a stale green on a warm cache.

FIX, mirroring rf2-drpa3.65: read the sidecar through shadow.resource/slurp-resource under a CLJS expansion ((:ns &env) is the host test) so the file's last-modified participates in the cache key; that needs spec/ (or a narrower root holding the sidecar) resolvable via io/resource on the shadow classpath. NOTE the Freehand fix put spec/conformance on :source-paths for exactly this reason — the sidecar sits at spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, one level up, so the root choice needs its own thought rather than a copy-paste.

title: Make v/route-link's caller veto obey an explicit Freehand callback contract
description:
PR #6696 adds v/route-link as an ordinary Freehand view, but its :on-click control prop bypasses Freehand's event-position grammar. route_link_seam/anchor captures the caller value in a wrapper, and re-frame.routing.link/activate-link! executes it as `(on-click e)` whenever it is truthy.

That creates a high-probability grammar collision on a corpus-dominant surface:

- Freehand teaches `:on-click [:app/event ...]` as ordinary intent data. On v/route-link, the vector is instead invoked as an IFn collection lookup with the MouseEvent as its key; no application event is dispatched (or the call fails), then routing proceeds.
- `v/handler` is the declared form for imperative foreign work, exactly the role of a pre-navigation veto/confirm callback, but its Callback value is deliberately non-IFn and therefore fails when routing calls it.
- The v/route-link docstring says every other key including :on-click passes through as an HTML attribute, although :on-click is actually a framework-owned control key removed from the anchor and replaced by a routing wrapper.

The underlying Spec 012 donor contract expects an optional user fn. The bug is not that routing still has that compatibility contract; it is that the new Freehand surface neither translates nor fences the value at the boundary where its grammar differs. A programmer following Freehand's primary event idiom can therefore lose an event silently on one of the most common view forms.

NARROW REPAIR: define v/route-link's :on-click explicitly as the imperative pre-navigation/veto seam, not a second semantic intent site. Accept a bare function and the appropriate Freehand imperative callback form (`v/handler`) and invoke it exactly once before routing's decision, with committed freshness through the ordinary outer event site. Reject event vectors, event options and `v/event` at render with a typed, didactic diagnostic: the route click already produces the one routing intent; application reactions belong behind that routing event/transition, while imperative preventDefault/confirm work uses v/handler. Do not add a general callback-composition DSL or change the substrate-neutral routing hook.

Also correct the public prose so :on-click is listed among route-link control props, not among untouched HTML passthrough attributes.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. In a real mounted Freehand/React route-link, a bare fn and v/handler each run exactly once before the navigation decision and can veto with preventDefault.
2. A vector, options map and v/event at this prop fail at render with the named recovery; none is invoked as an IFn or silently ignored.
3. Plain navigation, modifier/middle/download/target deferral, frame capture and SSR remain unchanged.
4. The Spec 012 paragraph, v/route-link docstring and conformance fixture state the same accepted grammar.
5. Compiled and interpreted route-link exercise the same cases when compiled parity lands.

DEDUP: all-state Beads search for route-link / activate-link / caller-on-click / routing event found no issue owning this Freehand grammar boundary. rf2-drpa3.54 owns the broad final browser matrix, not the accepted-value contract.

title: Close remaining standard Markdown block boundaries in wrapped-link extraction
description:
PR #6692 correctly replaces blank-line grouping with shared inline-block scan units and fixes the two executable failures from rf2-8wcbe. The new `_inline_blocks` boundary recognizer still joins link-shaped text across three ordinary Markdown boundaries that the repository's Python-Markdown renderer keeps separate: 1. A quote-only blank line: > A stray [opening > > ](missing.md) The renderer emits two blockquote paragraphs; `_iter_inline_links` yields `(3, "missing.md")`. `_inline_blocks` tests `content.strip()` before removing the quote prefix, so `>` is not seen as blank. 2. Indented code followed by a paragraph: [literal ](missing.md) The renderer emits a code block and a paragraph; extraction yields `(2, "missing.md")`. 3. A block-HTML interruption: A stray [opening
separate
](missing.md) The renderer emits a paragraph, the div, and another paragraph; extraction yields `(3, "missing.md")`. The positive control remains important: `> A real [wrapped` followed by unquoted `link](target.md)` is a valid lazy-continuation link and must keep extracting. The current corpus and both gates remain green, so this is a bounded future false-positive risk rather than a claim that a document is currently broken. SMALLEST REPAIR: keep the one shared extractor and its line-number behavior. Make scan-unit formation respect these standard boundaries—at minimum, detect a blank after stripping the blockquote prefix and keep indented-code and block-HTML blocks out of adjacent inline units. Use renderer-oracle mechanism tests to pin the negative cases and the lazy-continuation positive case. Do not build a general Markdown parser, duplicate the extractor, or reflow documents around the gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- The three executable samples—quote-only blank separator, indented code, and block HTML—yield no extracted link in the shared mechanism and both consuming gates.
- A genuine blockquote lazy-continuation wrapped link still extracts with the destination line number; existing one-, two-, and three-line positive cases remain green.
- Tests compare the boundary cases with the repository's Markdown rendering semantics or equivalently pin both negative and positive controls.
- The current documentation corpus and both checker self-test suites remain green.
- The repair stays in the shared extractor and does not introduce a second parser service or a document-reflow workaround.
close_reason:
CLOSED AT TRIAGE on the posture filter, not on the merits of the analysis — which is correct as far as it goes. This is the THIRD CommonMark-conformance refinement in one chain: blank-line grouping was blind to wrapped links (real, 100 invisible, 6 already broken) -> the fix invented phantom links across headings and multiline code spans (real, would red the gate on a non-link and block unrelated PRs) -> now blockquote-only blank lines and indented code blocks. The first two earned their place; this one does not clear the bar.

REASONING: (1) NEITHER SHAPE EXISTS IN THE CORPUS. PR #6692 established the full file:line -> destination inventory is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after its change across 588 files and 16838 links, so these are hypothetical constructions, not latent breakage. (2) THE FAILURE MODE IS LOUD, NOT SILENT. A phantom link fails the gate with a named file and line — immediately diagnosable and fixable in minutes. That is categorically different from the original defect, which was a SILENT false green over 100 unchecked links, and different from a false green in a conformance gate. (3) COST/BENEFIT INVERTS HERE. Each further boundary rule (blockquote prefix stripping, indented-code detection, and whatever the next audit finds — reference-style links, HTML blocks, nested emphasis) moves us toward maintaining a general-purpose Markdown parser to check our own documentation. rf2-8wcbe explicitly said "do not grow a general-purpose Markdown parser"; that instruction binds the follow-ups too, not just the PR that carried it.

This is the pre-alpha posture applied deliberately: elegance and power without gold-plating, and no drowning in minutiae. The gate now catches the class of defect it exists for.

REOPEN TRIGGER, and it is cheap and self-announcing: if either shape actually appears in the corpus, the gate will FAIL LOUDLY naming the file and line. At that point the exposure is real, the fix is narrow and justified, and this bead should be reopened rather than re-derived. Until then it is exhaustiveness for its own sake.

title: Keep both rename endpoints visible to the Beads PR guard
description:
## Problem

PR #6691 made `scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh` a required PR gate and correctly changed its range to the branch delta. The path selection still uses:

`git diff --name-only "$BRANCH_POINT" HEAD`

Git's default rename detection collapses a detected rename to the destination path in `--name-only` output. Therefore an exact rename out of the protected tree, such as `.beads/issues.jsonl` to `tracker-snapshot.jsonl`, is presented to `check_beads_boundary` only as `tracker-snapshot.jsonl`. That destination is outside `.beads/**`, so the allow-list classifier exits 0 even though merging the PR deletes the tracker database from its canonical location.

The behavior is already known and fixed elsewhere in this repository: rf2-vxgfnd.137 added `--no-renames` to changed-surface discovery because a rename out of a protected source tree hid the deleted endpoint. A read-only forced-rename comparison during this audit likewise emitted only the destination, and feeding exactly that output to `check_beads_boundary ci` returned 0. Layer 5 of `test-pre-commit.sh` covers add/modify contamination and diverged history, but no rename endpoint.

## Consequence

The required guard can certify a PR whose effective branch delta removes `.beads/issues.jsonl` (or moves another database-derived `.beads/**` path to an allowed destination). The ordinary stale-snapshot case is covered; this is a bounded but material hole in the same tracker-integrity boundary.

## Recommendation

Disable rename detection for the guard's path enumeration: `git diff --no-renames --name-only "$BRANCH_POINT" HEAD`. This yields deletion plus addition, allowing the existing shared classifier to reject the protected old endpoint without any new path rules. Add one real-history rename-out case to the existing layer-5 fixture and keep the merge-base/event behavior unchanged.

Provenance: correctness audit of merged PR #6691. This is a new consumer of the already-understood rf2-vxgfnd.137 Git behavior, not a reopening of that closed changed-surface bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An exact-content rename from `.beads/issues.jsonl` to a path outside `.beads/**` fails the PR guard and names `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
2. A rename from any database-derived `.beads/**` path to an allow-listed Beads config path also fails on the protected old endpoint.
3. The guard enumerates both rename endpoints, preferably via `git diff --no-renames --name-only` rather than a second classifier or name-status parser.
4. A regression test creates a real Git history with a detected R100 rename; restoring the current `git diff --name-only` makes the test false-green.
5. Existing diverged-history, ordinary contamination, allow-list, missing-base, and mayor-push cases remain green; do not redesign the guard.

title: Keep wrapped-link extraction inside real Markdown inline blocks
description:
PR #6690 correctly makes wrapped link text visible, but `_blank_line_blocks` equates “no blank line” with “one Markdown inline block”. Blank lines are block boundaries, but they are not the only block boundaries, and CommonMark code spans may cross a line ending. The resulting join can invent links that the renderer does not produce.

Two executable counterexamples against main:

1. A valid multiline code span:

    `[literal
    link](missing.md)`

   (with one backtick opening before `[` and one closing after `)`). Python-Markdown renders one `<code>` span. Because `_strip_inline_code` masks each line separately, neither unmatched backtick is masked; `_iter_inline_links` joins the lines and yields `(2, "missing.md")`.

2. Real block boundaries without a blank line:

    A stray [opening
    # Separate heading
    ](missing.md)

   Python-Markdown renders a paragraph, an H1, and a second paragraph. The new blank-line block joins all three and again yields `missing.md` as a link.

If either sample appears in the scanned corpus, the doc-slug and shared README gate can fail on a non-link. Before #6690, line-oriented extraction did not create these false positives. The current corpus remains green; this is a parser-contract regression exposed by direct mechanism tests, not a claim that a current document is broken.

SMALLEST REPAIR: keep the shared extractor and wrapped-link behavior, but form scan units that cannot cross actual Markdown block boundaries and mask code spans over the same joined inline unit (line endings inside a code span are legal). Reuse the already-installed Markdown machinery if it preserves destination line reporting cleanly, or add only the bounded block/code-span recognition needed by the corpus. Do not grow a new general-purpose Markdown parser or reflow documents to hide the problem.
acceptance_criteria:
- A multiline backtick code span containing wrapped link-shaped text is not extracted by either doc-slug or README checking.
- Extraction does not bridge an ATX heading or another explicitly supported non-blank block boundary; the counterexample above yields no link.
- Genuine one-, two-, and three-line links, including blockquoted forms, still extract with the destination's line number and broken ones still fail the gate.
- Add direct positive/negative mechanism cases and at least one end-to-end fixture; mutation back to blank-line-only grouping makes them fail.
- The current 588-file corpus and both existing self-test suites remain green; no new parser service, duplicate extractor, or corpus reflow is introduced.

title: Reject silently malformed v/defview declarations
description:
PR #6689 documents `(v/defview name docstring? opts? [props] body+)` and assigns malformed declarations the typed `:rf.error/defview-bad-args` diagnostic, but the macro currently accepts two malformed shapes silently.

Reproduced against main:

1. `(macroexpand-1 '(v/defview bodyless [p]))` succeeds. `parse-defview-args` returns a nil body and the expansion creates `(fn [p])`, so an accidentally omitted body becomes a view that quietly returns nil.
2. `(v/defview misspelled {:chilren-policy :none} [p] nil)` succeeds and reports `:children-policy :optional`. Unknown option keys are discarded. The same happens today for reserved-but-not-yet-implemented `{:compiled true}` and props-schema options: the declaration remains interpreted and the option is absent from inspection.

The second case is especially hostile to programmer and AI productivity: a one-character option typo produces valid code with different semantics, and a design-documented future option currently pretends to work. This is a declaration-boundary validation gap, not a request for a general schema system.

SMALLEST REPAIR: make the macro validate the finite option keys whose semantics have landed and require at least one body form. Unknown keys, including reserved options before their owning slice implements them, should fail at macro expansion with `:rf.error/defview-bad-args`, naming the offending keys and recovery. F3b/F3f can extend the accepted-key set when they implement `:compiled` and props schemas. An intentional no-output view remains expressible with an explicit nil body.
acceptance_criteria:
- A declaration with no body fails at macro expansion with `:rf.error/defview-bad-args`; an explicit `nil` body remains valid.
- An unknown/misspelled option key fails at macro expansion and the diagnostic names the offending key plus the supported recovery.
- A reserved future option is never silently ignored: it is either implemented by its owning slice or rejected until then. In particular, `{:compiled true}` must not describe itself as interpreted without an error.
- The four documented declaration spellings with a body, valid children policies, destructuring, docs, source coordinates, and both host test lanes remain green.
- Focused mutation tests prove removal of the body/option validation makes the suite fail; no runtime option registry or compatibility layer is added.

title: check_doc_slugs.py is blind to markdown links that wrap across a newline
description:
## Summary

The repo's primary link gate cannot see a markdown link split across a line break, so any wrapped link is silently unguarded.

## Evidence (negative control, not inference)

Found while finishing the 004D ownership labels. `_extract_links` iterates `text.splitlines()` (scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:617-628), so a link whose `](target#anchor)` falls on the next line never matches.

Proved both directions on the real corpus:
- the inbound link at spec/API.md:272-273 IS such a wrapped link. Breaking its anchor back to a retired slug leaves the gate at EXIT 0 — undetected.
- breaking the single-line equivalent at spec/API.md:31 correctly reds with BROKEN ANCHOR.
Both were restored before commit; numstat confirmed no residue.

## Why it matters

check_doc_slugs.py is the REAL anchor gate in this repo — `mkdocs build --strict` does not catch broken anchors, it logs them as INFO and exits 0. So a wrapped link has NO gate at all. Every heading rename since this checker was written could have orphaned a wrapped inbound link with CI green. This is the third distinct instance of line-wrap blindness found in this repo's scanners, which suggests the fix should be a shared normalisation helper rather than a one-off patch here.

## Expected behavior

A link is validated regardless of whether it wraps. Scanning should operate on a joined/normalised view for link extraction, or explicitly document that it is line-oriented and add a separate wrapped-link detector.

## Acceptance

1. The negative control above reds: break the anchor of the wrapped link at spec/API.md:272-273 and the gate must exit non-zero NAMING it. Restore and confirm exit 0.
2. A corpus sweep reports how many currently-wrapped links exist and whether any is ALREADY broken. Report the count; a nonzero already-broken count is a finding in its own right.
3. No regression: the existing single-line detection still reds (keep a positive control).

## Non-goals

Rewriting the checker; reflowing the corpus to avoid wrapped links (that treats the symptom and will silently regress); widening into a general docs audit.

title: B4 evidence: controlled editing under contention, and honest per-keystroke scale

title: B-spine: the measurement harness, its provenance record, and the gate-versus-evidence split
description:

title: F3e the checker: read-only analyzer findings as stable EDN
description:

DELETE-BEFORE-RELEASE OBLIGATION DISCHARGED -- OUTCOME: DELETE (2026-07-25 05:56 AUSEST). This bead carried the D007 obligation; it is hereby settled. The form this bead shipped (FH-EVENT-005, the closed exact-key :on-key-down / :on-key-up key-condition event map, PR #6761) is DELETED before release. The deletion work is bead rf2-drpa3.178, wired ahead of rf2-drpa3.53 (F6a) and rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e). The full ruling with its evidence is in the notes of rf2-drpa3.57.

WHY. The gate asked a literal question -- did the F5 component/library pilots show repeated real use of the data form? -- and the answer is ZERO uses across all four pilots, including rf2-drpa3.44's dropdown, which D007 named as the exemplar. Mike's wording gave the default: DELETE rather than keep for symmetry. Three further findings make it more than a technicality. (1) D007's load-bearing argument, per-key preventDefault, has no call site in the pilot corpus; the single preventDefault anywhere in the pilots is form submission on the ordinary options map (pilot_field.cljc:682-683). (2) D007 predicted a dropdown's repeated movement keys would be state-INdependent; pilot_overlay.cljc:292-312 branches on application state first, so "ArrowDown" means two different things depending on :open? and a state-blind exact-key map cannot express it -- the exemplar falls on the v/event side of D007's own boundary. (3) The claimed tooling benefit never materialised: nothing in tools/ reads the :key-map classification, and compiler/a11y.cljc:411-435 only asks whether an :on-key-down is present.

All keyboard-bearing pilots independently wrote the same surviving spelling instead -- pilot_field.cljc:433, pilot_field_compiled.cljc:83, pilot_overlay.cljc:384, pilot_typeahead.cljc:351, each [:ns/key-pressed ... ::v/key] with the branch in an ordinary registered handler.

THIS BEAD'S OWN DISCOVERED CHILDREN ARE THE COST RECORD, and they are the argument's other half: rf2-drpa3.149 (P1 bug, compiled analyzer read every literal map as listener options -- one declaration, two meanings across modes), rf2-drpa3.150 (P2 bug, branches silently discarded :once/:capture/:passive), plus rf2-7x0ge (P2 bug, structural host refused a legal v/event branch, fixed then audit-reopened for over-widening the opaque marker) and rf2-drpa3.145 (the deferred hot-zone spec subsection). Four post-ship beads in three days with zero users -- the standing tax of a SECOND map-shaped form at an event position.

The one genuine counter-argument, rf2-drpa3.124's dispatch-suppression finding, is preserved as rf2-egt43 against Spec 009, where it belongs: it is trace/epoch-window pressure, not an event-grammar problem.

Nothing else this bead shipped is affected. ::v/key stays (spec/004-Views.md:495), v/event stays, and the ordinary listener-options map at an event position becomes unambiguous again.

DONOR DISPOSITION: this bead disposes nothing; it makes disposition auditable.

GATES: deterministic - the ledger-coverage script (wired to CI so a new donor file cannot appear undisposed). Evidence-only: the undisposed-row count trend, published per slice.

title: Guard .beads against stale worker-worktree commits + configure dolt remote
description: Incident: PR #6677 committed a stale .beads/issues.jsonl from a worker worktree (135+/136- unrelated: reopened rf2-oe9xi, removed rf2-ncm8j, replaced memories) — the stale-worker-snapshot failure mode; blocker recorded in rf2-x4wua. Root cause: bd auto-stages the full-DB JSONL export in EVERY checkout, so a worktree carries a stale snapshot that time-travels the tracker if committed. Fix in three layers, MAYOR-DISPATCHED (touches hot-zone .github/workflows + mayor-owned .beads policy): (1) pre-commit guard rejecting commits touching .beads/ from any non-primary worktree — POSIX sh + .ps1 pair, reusing scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh's mayor/worker derivation; (2) CI gate failing any worker/* PR whose diff touches .beads/; (3) worktree-creation step runs 'git update-index --skip-worktree .beads/issues.jsonl' in new worker checkouts; (4) durable fix: configure the bd dolt remote so beads sync out-of-band via 'bd dolt push' and the JSONL becomes a mayor-only checkpoint artifact (dolt remote currently unconfigured on this box). Acceptance: a worker worktree commit staging .beads fails locally AND in CI with a didactic message; mayor checkpoint flow unaffected; dolt push round-trips; merge-side rule documented (never --theirs/--ours on .beads; resolve-then-regenerate). Cross-platform per repo rule (Windows/Mac/Linux).
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #6683 (merged). Delivered: the shared classifier scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh, the pre-commit hook block, the CI-arm script scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh, a block-registry refactor of both installers, 25 hook assertions (up from 6), and CLAUDE.md Beads-durability prose. Guard proven in BOTH directions with a real git commit in a throwaway mayor+worktree pair, and the harness itself mutation-tested (neutering the classifier turns 25/0 into 17 passed/8 failed, so the suite can go red). SUBSTANTIVE FINDING recorded rather than shipped: layer 3 (git update-index --skip-worktree on .beads/issues.jsonl in worker checkouts) is WRONG and was measured, not assumed — with skip-worktree set and the file locally modified (the worker steady state, since bd rewrites it), git status shows a clean tree while git pull --rebase aborts, freezing HEAD at a stale base with nothing on screen to explain why. That converts a loud correct refusal into a silent one. Not implemented; a regression test now asserts the guard message never recommends skip-worktree again. TWO PIECES CARVED OUT rather than dropped: CI wiring is rf2-3mh2f (the .github/workflows hot-zone was occupied), and the Dolt remote is rf2-4l67v (operator action, assigned to Mike).

title: UIx frame-root real-DOM mount logs React child errors (fn-as-child + MapEntry-as-child)
description:
Found by the rf2-b16va G1-G4 external boot proof (2026-07-22 14:05 AUSEST). MOUNT-TIME defect, no interaction needed; the app stays functional (DOM renders, counter seeds and increments) but every real-DOM boot of a UIx frame-root logs one console.error and one uncaught pageerror.

REPRO (exact):
1. Scaffold the UIx template app (tools/template, :substrate :uix), :local/root-rewrite deps, npm install, npx shadow-cljs watch app.
2. Open http://localhost:8280 in Chromium; wait for mount. No clicks.
3. Observe:
   - console.error: 'Functions are not valid as a React child ... re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider ... <Fragment>{re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider}</Fragment>'
   - pageerror (uncaught): 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {key, val, __hash, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition1$})' — a cljs MapEntry reached React children.

SCOPE EVIDENCE: the Reagent scaffold uses the SAME frame-root two-pass pattern (rf/frame-root via reagent adapter) and boots with ZERO errors — so this is UIx-adapter-specific, likely in the defui prop/children folding into the shared two-pass core (re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-root -> boundary/frame-root-react-element -> re-frame.views.provider/frame-provider element build). The template's usage matches frame-root's own docstring exactly, so this is NOT a template defect.

WHY EXISTING GATES MISS IT: the UIx adapter smoke (implementation/adapters/uix/testbed) mounts via frame-provider after manual make-frame + dispatch-sync — frame-root's real-DOM path has no browser coverage; node-side tests don't surface React child console errors.

SURFACE: implementation/adapters/uix (+ shared provider spine in core if the fold is shared). Production src — out of rf2-b16va's validation scope, hence this bead.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (proven by isolated repro): NOT the UIx frame-root/defui fold — that path boots clean (verified: scratch UIx app, frame-root mount, real-DOM Chromium, zero errors without the Xray preload). The errors come from the XRAY PRELOAD on a UIx host: day8.re-frame2-xray.mount/mount-shell-into! (+ popout!) hands the HICCUP tree [rf/frame-provider {:frame :rf/xray} [shell/shell-view ...]] to substrate-adapter/render; the React-hook spine's make-render (shared by UIx/Helix/ui) passes the tree to React untouched inside its Fragment wrap. React iterates the CLJS vector as children: the frame-provider FN becomes a Fragment child (console.error #1, names re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider) and the props map iterates to MapEntry objects, which are not iterable -> uncaught 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {key, val, __hash, ...})'. Reagent template boots clean because its render slot is hiccup-native. Repro red/green captured with a scratch shadow build (template shape + xray preload): before fix = exactly the 2 recorded errors; after fix = 0 errors/pageerrors + one intentional console.warn. FIX: substrate render-shape gate in xray mount (denylist :rf.adapter/ui|uix|helix -> :unsupported-substrate diagnostic + console.warn, no mount); uix adapter smoke now mounts via frame-root and asserts a clean boot.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6673 (worker/uix-frameroot-qgfo4). Root cause was NOT the UIx frame-root/defui fold (proven clean by isolated real-DOM repro): the Xray preload handed its hiccup shell to the UIx host's element-shaped :render, so React iterated the hiccup vector as children (frame-provider fn-as-child console.error + uncaught MapEntry pageerror). Fix: xray mount verbs refuse React-element substrate kinds (:rf.adapter/ui|uix|helix) with an :unsupported-substrate diagnostic + one console.warn; uix adapter smoke now mounts via frame-root and asserts a clean boot (zero console errors / pageerrors). Red/green captured on the actual failing path. Follow-up (real Xray-on-UIx support or template preload removal): rf2-p6f6u.

title: Routing popstate-mid-push-stress flakes intermittently under nightly CI load (invariant-3 slice non-convergence)
description:
Split off from rf2-wh5to (nightly expensive-tests repair). The JVM stress test re-frame.routing-concurrency-stress-test/popstate-mid-push-stress (implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_concurrency_stress_test.clj:330) fails INTERMITTENTLY in the nightly 'JVM slow/stress tests (routing)' job — NOT every night. When it fails it fails HARD: e.g. run 29760811080 (2026-07-20) reported 28 assertion failures, invariant 3 'per-frame slice converged' — 'Frame :ksbur.pop/f7: slice should reflect the LAST URL pushed by this thread; expected "4999" got "694"'. The slug reflects a mid-run iteration, not the last one, while the per-thread on-match counters (invariants 1+2) are correct — i.e. the [:rf.runtime/routing :current] slice systematically lags for some frames under contention, even though every on-match event fired.

REPRODUCTION STATUS: could NOT reproduce locally on Windows (opus worker, rf2-wh5to). Ran popstate-mid-push-stress in isolation 12x + once standalone — 27 assertions, 0 failures every time. It is load/scheduling dependent (CI runners = 2-4 vCPU; heavier lock interleaving). This is why a validated root-cause fix was out of scope for the wh5to turn.

REGRESSION WINDOW: the test (rf2-ksbur) was added 2026-05-15 and was GREEN on the last-green nightly 2026-07-07 (run 28880733495). It began flaking intermittently within the 07-08..20 streak. Prime suspect: 02ec7dbc4c (2026-07-08 'refactor(api): consolidate frame-state I/O to replace-frame-state!', rf2-t3lftq) — landed on the first-red day and changed the per-frame commit path (commit-frame-record-transition! read-then-replace in implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1319). That path is 'effectively atomic' ONLY under the single-writer-per-frame assumption; this test has one thread per frame so that holds, which makes the slice-lag surprising and worth a careful look. Secondary leads: the routing module-level defonce caches keyed by frame-id (nav_counters.cljc nav-counters-cache, nav_fx.cljc url-claim-order [not used here — frames are :url-bound? false], routing/registry.cljc route-table-cache) and whether any part of url-change-fx's :current-slice publish is deferred past dispatch-sync's drain.

ACCEPTANCE: reproduce reliably (e.g. run under CPU-pinned/oversubscribed contention, or bump n-threads/stress-iters, or add controlled interleaving), root-cause the slice non-convergence, fix it deterministically (NOT a skip/retry/loosened invariant unless the invariant is proven wrong), and show the fix green under the repro. Do NOT touch the compiler-cache/digest surface (C0/u53yy.1). Hot-zone: expensive-tests.yml is NOT expected to change.
notes:
REFRAME (worker, definitive): NOT a concurrent-RMW slice race. Root cause = CPU-STARVATION WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT. Fetched the actual failing CI log (run 29760811080, routing job 88414672832): popstate-mid-push-stress per-thread counters were [648 660 660 696 664 639 695 689] (expected 5000 each) and Global AtomicLong got 5371/40000 -> the 8 threads completed only ~13% of their 5000 iters within the 120s per-future deref bound. So invariants 1 AND 2 ALSO failed (bead's 'counters correct' premise is FALSE); invariant-3 'slug=694' is a downstream symptom = the slug reflects the ~694th iter where the starved thread stopped, not a lost write. Prime suspect 02ec7dbc4c / commit RMW is a RED HERRING (the RMW predates it; introduced 38c9671d97). Evidence it is NOT a race: (1) instrumented multi-writer detector (add-watch each stress frame's container, flag any frame written by >1 thread) ran ~580 S1+S2 runs pinned 2-core -> ZERO concurrent writers; (2) faithful 'clojure -M:slow-test' normal-heap verified-2vCPU-pins -> 24+ runs green; (3) reproduced the EXACT CI failure signature locally only via extreme starvation (8 JVMs x 8 threads on 2 cores, 128m). Under single-drainer-per-frame (dispatch-sync sets router :scheduled?=true before draining so child :dispatch never arms the async executor) + linearizable clojure-atom containers, a 'counters-correct + slug-lags' race is architecturally impossible. FIX is test/infra tuning, NOT a framework RMW change: the 8x5000-iter test assumes ~60s but the loaded nightly runner starves it ~8x. Needs a decision (Mike/mayor): reduce CI iters (RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS override / lower default), raise the 120s deref bound, or de-contend the nightly runner so the routing job isn't starved. Does NOT loosen the correctness invariants (they stay; the test just needs to COMPLETE before they're checked). No code changed; worktree clean; blind-patching the RMW was correctly avoided (banned + wrong).
RE-SCOPE (worker STOP-report, evidence-backed 2026-07-21): NOT a slice race — it's a CPU-STARVATION WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT. CI log (run 29760811080) shows 8 threads completed only ~650/5000 iters before the 120s deref bound; invariants 1/2/3 all fail because the run never FINISHES, not because of a race. Multi-writer detector: ~580 runs, ZERO concurrent writers. The RMW 'prime suspect' predates the named commit + is a red herring. Faithful clojure -M:slow-test: 24+ runs green. The bead's prescribed atomic-RMW fix would fix nothing (blind-patch correctly avoided). NEEDS RULING (hot-zone expensive-tests.yml): re-scope to 'routing stress test times out under nightly CPU starvation'; options (none loosen invariants): (a) lower CI stress-iters (RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS~500), (b) raise the 120s deref bound (may be insufficient — ~925s needed at worst-case), (c) de-contend the nightly runner. Mayor: surface to Mike for the tuning call.
RULING (Mike, 2026-07-22 00:55 AUSEST): OPTION 1 — LOWER the CI iteration count. Set RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS ~500 for the nightly expensive-tests.yml routing stress run, so the popstate-mid-push-stress test COMPLETES within the 120s deref bound under the loaded runner (worker proved: it's a CPU-starvation wall-clock timeout at ~5000 iters, NOT a concurrency race; invariants 1/2/3 are correct — they just need the run to finish). Does NOT loosen any correctness invariant. Re-scope the bead to this tuning fix.
DELIVERED (worker, 2026-07-22): Option 1 per Mike's ruling. Set RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS=500 on the jvm-slow-tests 'Run JVM slow/stress tests' step in .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml, scoped to the routing matrix artefact (${{ matrix.artefact == 'routing' && '500' || '' }}). Before->after: nightly routing stress iters 5000 (default) -> 500 (CI override only). Test DEFAULT unchanged (stays 5000; scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh still full-strength; sibling machines/core/flows stress tests untouched). NO change to the correctness invariants (1/2/3), assertions, 120s deref bound, or frame-state I/O — ONLY the CI iteration count. Gates: RF2_KSBUR_STRESS_ITERS=500 clojure -M:slow-test (routing) EXIT 0 ~88s, 3 tests/73 assertions/0 failures (popstate-mid-push-stress green, completes far under 120s); clojure -M:test (routing) EXIT 0, 458 tests/2382 assertions/0 failures; YAML parse OK. Rebased onto current origin/main (post rf2-vxgfnd.99.2). Sole expensive-tests.yml toucher; disjoint from u53yy.1 S6 + vxgfnd.99.2. PR #6656 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6656 (NOT merged).
close_reason: shipped #6656 — CI stress-iters→500 per Mike ruling; test default 5000 kept; invariants unchanged

RULED: this is half 1 of 2 of the S7-ENTRY PROOF (kill-gate half), per the DECISION note on rf2-vxgfnd.99 dated 2026-07-21 17:20 AUSEST (Fable, delegated by Mike) — that note is AUTHORITATIVE over this brief and over the S6/S7 epics' stale ENTRY wording. rf2-vxgfnd.99 depends on this bead; S7 leaf children may not file until it and its sibling (PROOF 2/2, Story+Xray-as-consumers) are merged and the soak gates pass.

THE WORK: ship a COMPLETE re-frame.ui full-app variant of examples/real-apps/realworld_resources. The app must BOOT a re-frame.ui root end-to-end (ui mount of a defview tree) — not the existing Reagent path (core.cljs -> views.cljs) — covering ROUTING (the ruled ui route-link / routed-mount surface) and MEANINGFUL EDIT/WRITE PATHS (article editor, settings, auth as present in this variant: see article_editor.cljs, settings.cljs, auth.cljs, routing.cljs, mutations.cljs). The three checked-in S3 coherence fixtures (ui_counter.cljc, ui_dashboard.cljc, ui_editor.cljc) may seed pages but the proof is the booting full app, not fixtures.

CONSTRAINTS (all ruled):
- The Reagent variant is RETAINED UNTOUCHED alongside — W4 adds the ui arm, removes nothing (adapter disposition 2026-07-17; guard scripts/check_adapter_disposition.py).
- Share existing substrate-free models where natural; do NOT start an abstraction project to dedupe view-layer code.
- Examples are TEST-FREE (locked rf2-8cevm): no *.spec.cjs under examples/. Correctness = the app compiles + boots + the substrate contract suites stay green.
- Build wiring: check how the existing realworld example builds are wired FIRST. If a new build-id must land in top-level implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, that file is HOT-ZONE — flag and sequence (one owner at a time). Prefer the established example-build shape (the standalone consumer-shaped examples/ui/minimal-counter is the other precedent).
- Frames are isolated contexts; idiomatic re-frame2 only (app-db + events + subs; no raw atoms through views).
- SEQUENCING: rf2-y4mgw (realworld editor owner-release bug; fix bf52d0a899 recently landed) touches this surface — coordinate/sequence with the mayor; no concurrent workers on the same files. Also sequence behind the P1 nightly-repair bead if its diagnosis touches the examples/Story/Xray gate surfaces.

GATES (focused, foreground): the example's own build compiles; npm run test:cljs from implementation/; scripts/check_adapter_disposition.py stays green; mkdocs build --strict only if docs touched. Do NOT run the full spine or test:browser on a fresh worktree — CI owns those.

ACCEPTANCE: the realworld_resources ui variant boots on a re-frame.ui root with routing + edit/write paths working end-to-end; retained Reagent variant untouched; gates green. On merge, post the entry-proof evidence (build id + how to run it) on rf2-vxgfnd.99.

WORKER RULES: run the worker worktree guard BEFORE any edit (sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh or the .ps1) and report WORKTREE_ROOT; commit first then git pull --rebase; NEVER git stash; gates FOREGROUND only (backgrounded/tail-piped gates strand work uncommitted).

Every view on ui/defview; app boots a re-frame.ui root via ui/mount + ui/frame-root (realworld-resources.ui-core/run), NOT the Reagent core.cljs/views.cljs root. Files: ui_core.cljs, ui_views.cljs (incl markdown body via ui/raw hiccup->React), ui_auth.cljs, ui_settings.cljs; ui_editor.cljc reused. GATES: shadow-cljs compile examples/realworld-resources-ui = 0 warnings (clean post-rebase); npm run test:cljs = 10366 tests / 51226 assertions, 0 failures/0 errors; check_adapter_disposition.py green; check-no-hardcoded-paths green. Live DOM boot not runnable in worktree (no browser extension/jsdom) — deferred to P-2 (rf2-vvdzx) live consumers per the ruling. Not merged (sequences with P-2). Post entry-proof evidence on rf2-vxgfnd.99 on merge.
PR #6648 CHRONOLOGICAL THREE-LENS AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-21) — reopen P-1 for two bounded standalone-integration defects. The compiled-view architecture itself is proportionate; do not start a view-deduplication or routing-abstraction project.

1. MATERIAL ROUTE/MOUNT MISMATCH. The new build emits under out/examples/realworld-resources-ui, but ui_core.cljs reuses realworld-resources.routing/url-strategy, whose deployment base is hard-coded to /realworld-resources for the retained Reagent arm. Pure current-main proof:

  (strip-base-path "/realworld-resources" "/realworld-resources-ui/")
  => "/realworld-resources-ui/"

  ((:encode (with-base-path history-url-strategy "/realworld-resources")) "/login")
  => "/realworld-resources/login"

A browser audit against the UI build's declared output path reproduced the consequence: the shell booted into Page not found, and generated links targeted the Reagent mount. This defeats P-1's routing/full-app proof. Route declarations and dataflow are shareable; deployment strategy is entry-specific. SMALLEST FIX: define/use a UI-entry strategy with the UI build's coherent served base (normally /realworld-resources-ui), leaving the Reagent strategy untouched. Prove initial decode plus one outbound/deep-link route using an existing browser/config seam; P-2 can consume the repaired app, but it does not own this standalone defect. No generalized base-path registry or new runner.

2. BOUNDED ASSET-STAGING GAP. The standard standalone enumerator discovers examples/realworld-resources-ui and maps it to the shared source folder, but PER_EXAMPLE_ASSETS has no entry for that build. Direct Node projection returned assets=null. ui_views calls avatar-src throughout, the canned corpus intentionally has blank :image values, and avatar-src falls back to root-relative default-avatar.svg; clean staging therefore serves broken avatars. SMALLEST FIX: add the UI build to the existing examples-asset-manifest.cjs with the same colocated default-avatar.svg declaration, and extend the existing manifest/staging roster assertion. Do not generalize the manifest schema.

RUN/ERGONOMICS: ensure the README names one actually coherent command + URL topology for the UI arm after the base repair. Prefer the existing dev:example front door if its served mount is made consistent; do not invent another server.

EVIDENCE/DEDUP: all three independent lenses found the same route/base and staging omissions; root independently reproduced the pure route mismatch, the missing manifest projection, and a clean --force-spawn compile. All-state search found no separate exact owner. This bead is the P-1 full-app/routing/build-integration kill-gate, so reopen it rather than filing a duplicate. rf2-vvdzx remains the in-progress P-2 Story/Xray consumer proof and must not absorb these repairs.
