title: Testing docs + skills sweep: teach the seven-name surface (absorbs rf2-u53yy.10)
description:
Ratified from the 2026-07-21 ui.test dedup reviews, Mike-approved; all decisions final; no operator input needed. This bead is fully self-contained — do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees). The parent epic carries the end-state seven-name surface and the NOT-BUILD fence; obey both.

BLOCKED on the four sibling implementation children of this epic (dep edges wired on this bead): dispatch! deletion, find/find-all + 004D retirement, with-root-container + query deletion, render narrowing + JVM-arity deletion. Runs LAST — the docs must describe the shipped surface, not anticipate it. No runtime/API change in this bead: prose, skills, and generated-sheet regeneration only. This bead ABSORBS rf2-u53yy.10's ratified frameless-first testing-guide scope (that bead is closed superseded by the mayor; its note points here).

## The surface being taught (the seven names, final)

```clojure
;; JVM structural host
(ui.test/render [view props] {:sub-overrides {query-v value}}) ; opts optional; ONE grammar, ONE option
(ui.test/attrs node)
(ui.test/text node)

;; CLJS mounted host
(ui.test/with-root [container [app-root ...]] body ...) ; binds the connected DOM container
(ui.test/flush!)  (ui.test/flush! thunk)
(ui.test/flush-presence!)  (ui.test/flush-presence! ms)
```

## The work

1. REWRITE docs/core/re-frame.ui/testing.md around the final surface, LEADING with the frameless zero-fixture example:

```clojure
(deftest add-button-carries-intent
  (let [tree (ui.test/render [app/add-button {:product-id 42}]
                             {:sub-overrides {[:cart/locked?] false}})]
    (is (= [:cart/add 42]
           (-> (some #(when (= :button (:tag %)) %)
                     (tree-seq map? :children tree))
               ui.test/attrs
               :on-click)))))
```

(The rf2-u53yy.10 original of this example used `ui.test/find` — rewritten here to the tree-seq idiom because `find` is deleted; the `attrs` read is what closes the `:events` trap.) For a view with no sub reads, show the options map omitted entirely. The frameless example is within one concept of a pure-function data assertion while keeping real view identity — the shortest correct example is the one humans AND assistants copy.

2. THEN the runtime-bracket step-up: `rf/with-new-frame [f (rf/make-frame ...)]` (+ `:initial-events`); drive with `(rf/dispatch-sync [...] {:frame f})` (`{:frame ...}` accepts value or id); assert on a FRESH `(ui.test/render ...)`. State exactly when a test needs this tier: real registered sub derivation, event transitions, frame isolation.

3. THEN the mounted tier: `with-root` binding the connected DOM container; `flush!` zero + thunk arities — the thunk spelling `(ui.test/flush! #(rf/dispatch-sync ... {:frame f}))` is the mounted drive idiom; `flush-presence!` as fake-time advancement (advance the presence clock and settle — not a second flush); native `.querySelector` / `.querySelectorAll` and ordinary DOM properties/events on the bound container.

4. Teach the ONE canonical traversal idiom — `tree-seq map? :children` + a visible predicate; `filterv` for multi; `(:view-id %)` for view boundaries — taught as ordinary Clojure, never packaged as a helper (epic fence).

5. State the one-sentence story verbatim: "rf/ drives and reads state, test-support isolates and waits, ui.test renders, projects, and settles." (`poll-until` vs `flush!` is not overlap: one waits for an observable on a live scheduler, the other deterministically settles the mounted tree.)

6. `:sub-overrides` one-conceptual-owner prose: the single mechanism is the dynamic var `re-frame.ui.reactive/*sub-overrides*`; `ui.test/render` is the JVM carriage, Story's React context Provider is the mounted carriage; one resolver (`resolve-override`), one validator (`validate-sub-override!`). Fidelity warning retained verbatim in spirit: overrides affect render reads only — they do not mutate app-db or make `compute-sub` assertions pass.

7. docs/api/re-frame.ui.test.md — rewritten to the seven names (render one-grammar/one-option; attrs; text; with-root container binding; flush! CLJS x2; flush-presence! CLJS x2), frameless-first ordering in its examples too.

8. spec/008-Testing.md testing rows + spec/004-Views.md ui.test sections — final truing pass to the post-deletion surface (catch any residue the four implementation PRs left). spec/004 + spec/008 + spec/API.md are hot-zone: this PR is their sole toucher while open; sequence behind any sibling PR still open.

9. title: ui.test minimal surface (dedup-review ratified)
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-21; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement. Provenance: ratified from the 2026-07-21 ui.test dedup reviews (two converged adversarial reviews), Mike-approved. Every child bead is fully self-contained — implementing workers must NOT look for any ai/ dossier (the ai/ tree is local-only and absent from worker worktrees).

## End-state surface (SEVEN names, one namespace)

```clojure
;; JVM structural host
(ui.test/render [view props] {:sub-overrides {query-v value}}) ; opts optional; ONE input grammar (the literal plan-free view form); ONE option (:sub-overrides)
(ui.test/attrs node)
(ui.test/text node)

;; CLJS mounted host
(ui.test/with-root [container [app-root ...]] body ...) ; binds the connected DOM CONTAINER, not an opaque MountedRoot
(ui.test/flush!)  (ui.test/flush! thunk)
(ui.test/flush-presence!)  (ui.test/flush-presence! ms)
```

DELETED: `dispatch!`; `find`; `find-all`; `query`; render's `:frame` and `:props` options (and, with `:props`, the bare view-reference input form it serviced); the plan-bearing render route; the public JVM `flush!` arity; the JVM `flush-presence!` no-op; spec/004D-UI-Test-Selectors.md entirely (179 lines). The `^:no-doc` macro/runtime seams stay implementation-only (excluded from docs/manifest); seams only the deleted routes consume are deleted with them.

TAUGHT IN THEIR PLACE: `rf/dispatch-sync` + `{:frame ...}` (and the thunk form inside CLJS `flush!` for mounted); `rf/with-frame` / `rf/with-new-frame` for frame scope; ONE canonical `tree-seq` + visible-predicate idiom for traversal; native `.querySelector` / `.querySelectorAll` on the bound container.

THE ONE-SENTENCE STORY: rf/ drives and reads state, test-support isolates and waits, ui.test renders, projects, and settles.

## Organizing principle

Keep only what crosses a real host boundary, plus the two tree-ABI projections `attrs`/`text`. The projections close the schema traps: `(:on-click node)` silently misses because events live under `:events` — `attrs` is the one attribute read that merges element `:attrs` + `:events`, returns view-boundary `:props`, `{}` on fragment/html (test.cljc:198-226); `text` is document-order text concatenation with the trusted-HTML rule (trusted HTML contributes nothing, test.cljc:228-259). The schema-trap protection always lived in these projections, never in the selector verbs.

## Deletion roster (one-line evidence each)

- `dispatch!` — its entire body is `(router/dispatch-sync! event {:frame frame-target})` (test.cljc:749-756); loses the facade macro's `:rf.trace/call-site` capture (core.cljc:1133-1140); violates Spec 008:23's no-re-export rule; its attribution drifted twice (closed beads rf2-vxgfnd.208 / rf2-vxgfnd.293).
- `find` / `find-all` — a four-predicate selector grammar (tag kw, view-id kw/Var, attr-map by rf=, pred-fn — test.cljc:287-356) over deliberately plain data; `tree-seq` + a visible predicate is ordinary Clojure; its spec (004D, 179 lines) carries a rulings trail (prefix-find rejected, OPEN-2 dropped, find! parked) — the maintenance signature of a bespoke grammar.
- `query` — a guarded `(.querySelector (.-container root) css)` (test.cljc:705-738; its own docstring: "CSS is the whole contract"); with the container bound by `with-root`, the host API covers it — including the `querySelectorAll` the wrapper never offered.
- render `:frame` — the frameless arm inherits an outer binding (test.cljc:928-935, `:else (slice)`), so `rf/with-frame` / `rf/with-new-frame` (bind AND destroy on exit, core.cljc:1484-1504) already cover frame scope; a second spelling for one concept.
- render `:props` — a second input grammar; the literal view form carries props: `(ui.test/render [product-card {:product p}])`.
- the plan-bearing render route — ~200 lines of parallel frame-lifecycle policy (claimed-plan-ids CAS, must-create install, incarnation-pinned teardown — test.cljc:937-1110) for 19 call sites in three framework test files.
- the public JVM `flush!` arity — Tier-1's checkpoint is a fresh render after synchronous `rf/dispatch-sync`; the only verified JVM consumer (reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc:288-304) is the conformance test of the drain itself.
- the JVM `flush-presence!` no-op — false portability: JVM presence has no lifecycle (the JVM emitter renders `:present`, spec/004:648-661); dual-host runner code uses reader conditionals.
- spec/004D-UI-Test-Selectors.md — retired whole with the grammar it specifies.

## NOT-BUILD fence (permanent record; binds every child and all future work)

- NO replacement selector language of any kind. 004D's parked/rejected extensions — `find!`, path/vector selectors, prefix/testid sugar, `query-all` — die with 004D and are recorded HERE as not-build.
- NO gesture/event DSL (Spec 008: "There is no gesture DSL" — native events at Tier 3, intent-equality at Tier 1).
- NO test-only frame constructor or reset (test-support owns fixtures; `rf/make-frame` is the one grammar).
- NO re-export of rf verbs into ui.test (the Spec 008:23 no-re-export rule — the lesson of `dispatch!`).
- NO second flush idiom or setTimeout-settle helper (`flush!` is "the only test flush", spec/004:1207).
- NO test driver/scheduler object.
- NO compatibility aliases for any deleted verb.
- NO traversal helper fn shipped in ui.test — the tree-seq idiom is taught in docs, not packaged.
- Do NOT expose the adapter's `flush-render!` as a settle substitute — it is a synchronous production/tooling commit hook (adapter.cljc:620) without the awaited act/effect boundary that makes `flush!` correct.

## :sub-overrides — documentary consolidation (no code change anywhere)

One conceptual owner: the dynamic var `re-frame.ui.reactive/*sub-overrides*` (reactive.cljc:242-341). `ui.test/render` is the JVM carriage (binds the var around the render thunk, test.cljc:918-920); Story's React context Provider is the mounted carriage (implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/sub_override_context.cljs publishes the map; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/sub_overrides.cljs:1-36 reads it; implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:113-137 binds the SAME var around each compiled body). Both converge on `reactive/resolve-override` and the single `validate-sub-override!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/override_schema.cljc). Retain the fidelity warning: overrides affect render reads only — they do not mutate app-db or make `compute-sub` assertions pass. No public `with-sub-overrides`, resolver object, provider API, or second validation layer — the semantic core is already shared at the var.

## Sequencing (mayor executes)

- Child .1 (dispatch!) is dispatchable immediately.
- Children .2/.3/.4 ALL edit implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/test.cljc — SERIALIZE them (one at a time, any order; no wired dep edges among them). Child .1 also touches that file, so in practice keep exactly ONE of the four implementation children in flight at a time.
- Child .5 (docs/skills) runs LAST — dep edges wired (it depends on .1/.2/.3/.4).
- spec/004-Views.md + spec/008-Testing.md + spec/API.md are hot-zone — sole toucher per PR; never two open PRs touching them.
- EVERY child regenerates the api-manifest (from implementation/scripts/api-manifest/: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen`, then `--check` green — ui.test is under drift enforcement; the curated sidecar spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn rows for deleted vars are removed by hand, the manifest itself is generated, never hand-edited) and, where its surface changes, the generated ui-context sheet (`clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.ui-context` — regenerate, never hand-edit).

## Migration size (repo-internal; no external users)

~58 `dispatch!` sites (~18 files); ~112 `find`/`find-all` sites (15+2 files); ~143 `query` + ~103 `with-root` sites in one mechanical pass; 19 plan-bearing render calls in 3 framework test files; plus the spec/doc/skills sweep. Counts include comments/contract strings — migration-size signals. All mechanical.

title: Make data-rf-render-key an owned, truthful DOM stamp
description: PR #6601 stamps data-rf-render-key imperatively after a connected commit, but the stamp has no explicit ownership boundary. In development it overwrites a programmer-authored attribute that production preserves. If a direct host root changes from no ref to an authored ref while React reuses the DOM node, the old framework callback detaches without removing its stamp, leaving a stale render key on a now-opted-out node. This makes the DOM evidence lie and creates avoidable dev/production drift. Keep the repair narrow: treat own authored data-rf-render-key presence as an opt-out; track and remove only framework-owned stamps when the callback detaches or ownership changes; preserve authored callback/object ref semantics. Specify the exact dev-only attribute and ownership/collision rule in Spec 004. Do not add a history system or a new tooling API. The broader tool-projection work remains with in-progress rf2-vxgfnd.98.1.2.
acceptance_criteria: A programmer-authored data-rf-render-key survives development commits unchanged; framework-owned stamps update on each connected commit; a no-ref to authored-ref transition on a reused host node removes the prior framework-owned stamp without disturbing the authored ref; focused browser tests prove both transitions; Spec 004 names data-rf-render-key, commit-time ownership, development-only erasure, and the collision/cleanup rule; production elision remains green.
notes:
PR #6621 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6621), branch worker/render-key-stamp-98-1-3. Made data-rf-render-key an OWNED + TRUTHFUL stamp mirroring the rf2-x1nbv authored-wins law: authored value wins (opt-out at stamp time against the committed node), framework claims only unclaimed roots + re-stamps only its own node per commit, and removes ONLY its own stamp when host-cb detaches / ownership moves to an authored ref on a reused node (owned-ref tracks the owned node). All DEBUG-gated (host-ref/owned-ref/setAttribute/removeAttribute DCE under :advanced). Spec 004 §Source-DOM navigation now names the attr + commit-time ownership + dev-only erasure + collision/cleanup rule. Red->green proven in browser: pre-fix clobbered 'author-owned' with '339'/'340' and left stale '341'; fixed both green. Gates green: ui JVM 993/0, test:cljs 10366/0, test:browser 512/0 (ran to completion), test:elision 60/60 absent, test:browser-prod-elision 118/0. Disjoint from vz6a1. Not merged.
PR #6621 THREE-LENS AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21): REOPENED. The shipped ownership logic handles an authored data-rf-render-key from first mount and a no-ref -> authored-ref transition, but misses the ordinary same-node absent -> authored-attribute transition. Render 1 claims node and stores owned-ref. On render 2 React commits data-rf-render-key="author-owned", but stampable-host-root? ignores that final prop and the layout effect tests owned-ref identity before hasAttribute, so it overwrites the programmer value with the next numeric render key. This directly violates the authored-wins rule and recreates dev/production drift. BOUNDED FIX: recognize own data-rf-render-key presence on the current final React element props (including spread-produced props) before the owned-node update, relinquish framework ownership without touching the authored value, and prove one same-ViewCell/same-node absent -> authored browser transition. Keep cleanup and DOM collision fallback as needed. No general DOM-ownership framework or history/tool API.

title: Finish foreign ui/spread merge semantics and contract projection
description: PR #6597 added foreign-component ui/spread, but foreign-spread-props does not fully implement the open-props/literal-wins contract and no test executes it. It skips nil literal values, so a forwarded value survives although a normal foreign literal prop supplies an own null and literal ownership is specified to win every collision. It also assigns a forwarded __proto__ key onto {}, invoking JavaScript prototype-setter semantics instead of preserving an own verbatim prop, unlike the existing literal JSX invariant. The contract sweep also left final EP-0031 describing every ui/spread as a 004B rule-table conversion, and the Reagent migration skill says both spread choices are DOM-only immediately before documenting foreign spread. Complete the shipped feature without a generic validator, sanitizer, or merge framework.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve forwarded names and values as own props without changing the output object prototype, including __proto__; layer compiled literal keys by presence so they win collisions even for nil/null, while retaining false and 0; add a focused CLJS runtime or React-capture test that executes the helper and pins verbatim names, ordinary and nil collision precedence, and __proto__ ownership; add a dated EP-0031 correction distinguishing DOM/custom-element conversion from unconverted foreign spread; remove the migration skill contradiction; run focused UI, CLJS, skill, and docs gates; add no public API or generalized defensive machinery.
notes:
PR #6635 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6635) — foreign-spread-props now (1) layers every own literal key by presence (literal wins even for nil/null; false/0 retained) and (2) routes __proto__ through defineProperty (verbatim own prop, no prototype mutation) via a small private set-own!. Focused CLJS test executes the helper directly, red→green (5 failures pre-fix -> 0). EP-0031 dated erratum + reagent-migration catalog-judgment.md 'both DOM only' claim removed. spec/004-Views already correct (literal wins any collision; DOM vs foreign distinguished) so no spec change - disjoint from u53yy.9. Gates: test:cljs 10366/0-0, ui JVM 955/0-0, migration skill drift gates 0. Awaiting merge.
PR #6635 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-21) — reopen this exact source owner; no duplicate Bead and no generalized merge/object machinery.

Two bounded residuals remain after the otherwise sound #6635 repair:

1. FORWARDED KEY STILL BEATS LITERAL KEY AT REACT. The foreign merge helper correctly layers ordinary props, but the compiler extracts a literal :key from the literal object and calls runtime/jsx-spread3 with it as React's third argument while leaving a forwarded own "key" in the config object. React 19.2.0 applies the third argument first and then config.key, so the forwarded key wins and dev emits the key-spread warning. Reproduced against the checked-in runtime: jsx(F,{key:"forwarded"},"literal").key == "forwarded". This violates Spec 004/API's literal-wins-any-collision contract and the PR's own acceptance. Smallest fix: at the explicit-key jsx-spread3 seam, remove the runtime-built config object's own "key" before calling jsx/jsxs, so the separately compiled literal key is authoritative; add one real React-element regression proving a literal key beats a forwarded key and no config-key path remains. Do not add a validator or generalized props framework.

2. PUBLIC RECOVERY TRUTH STILL SAYS DOM-ONLY. re-frame.ui/spread's public docstring and direct-call error, the compiler's :rf.ui.compile/bad-spread recovery, the re-frame2-ui-context diagnostic row, and Spec 009's :rf.error/ui-spread-outside-template catalogue row still say the form is legal only at DOM/custom props and always uses the conversion rule table. Correct those existing surfaces to name both contextual forms: DOM/custom uses rule-table conversion with later-arg precedence; FOREIGN uses an opaque runtime map layered under compiled literal props. Strengthen the existing error-roster assertion and sync the generated spec mirror. This is a small truth sweep, not an API/runtime redesign or new test framework.

Everything else reviewed clean: own enumerable map-key semantics, null/false/0 layering, forwarded/literal __proto__ ownership, ref/children behavior, evaluation order/once-only, advanced stability, docs/EP + migration projection, and broad green CI. Raw JS objects, Symbols, inherited properties, and a generalized object model are not part of the runtime-map contract and are explicitly out of scope.

title: Correct form-action routing guidance across client and server
description: skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md teaches two incorrect/needlessly indirect routing patterns. Its success fx emits both a server redirect and universal :dispatch of :rf.route/navigate while labelling the latter client-only; on the server that event still changes route state and can run route work even though browser history is absent. The same paragraph tells programmers to register an app-owned effect for a bare URL, although the shipped request grammar directly supports [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/cart"}]. This is canonical copyable guidance and creates both wrong behavior and unnecessary app machinery.
acceptance_criteria: Make the worked success path choose the 303 redirect on the server and route navigation on the client using an existing platform boundary; do not claim the navigation event is a server no-op; teach the built-in {:url ...} request for raw URLs and reserve app-owned effects only for deliberate routing bypasses, if that exceptional advice remains useful; keep the change confined to the skill/doc and its existing drift checks.
notes:
PR #6614 three-lens audit (2026-07-21): reopen narrowly. spec/Pattern-FormAction.md and its docs/spec mirror still teach the exact rejected behavior: emit redirect plus navigate together, call route navigation a server no-op, and invent an app-owned fx for a raw internal URL. Reconcile that canonical source and mirror with the corrected skill. Also make the platform choice use coeffect-key presence rather than request truthiness: on a server frame the declared :rf.server/request key can be present with nil when the slot is unpopulated, while the client key is absent. Use one focused presence check; no platform abstraction or broader form-action redesign.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7172 (2026-07-28). The exact defects this owner was meant to remove are still present on origin/main in spec/Pattern-FormAction.md. The canonical :cart/add-item handler says it runs on both platforms but declares :rf.server/request and :app.csrf/active-token, both server-only; platform-skipped ambient cofx deliver no key, so the client arm compares the submitted token with nil and always takes the 403 branch. Its success fx also emits :rf.server/redirect and the universal :rf.route/navigate together while the prose calls navigation a server no-op; routing still runs and can perform server route work. The same paragraph still invents an app-owned bare-URL fx despite the shipped {:url ...} request. Apply this bead's existing acceptance literally: choose the platform arm from coeffect-key presence, emit one success navigation per platform, and teach the built-in URL request. Keep the fix in the canonical pattern and its actual mirrors.

The #7172 audit was right: 073acbd7e4 corrected the skill leaf only, and the canonical spec/Pattern-FormAction.md still taught all three rejected shapes plus a fourth the skill had introduced. title: Make the re-frame.ui tool schema-version boundary real
description:
PR #6582 advertised `re-frame.ui.tool/schema-version` 3 as a lockstep producer/consumer compatibility boundary, but the consumers do not independently own the version they understand. Xray compares an envelope to the producer's own `tool/schema-version`; Story defines `consumed-schema-version` as that same producer var and continues shaping manifest/mounted/render data after setting `:version-mismatch?`; Pair, which can connect to an arbitrarily old or new running app, forwards every stamped envelope as `:ok? true` and has no supported-version check. The changed tests and descriptor golden mostly replace version examples, so they stay green without proving mismatch degradation.

This makes the version contract nominal: an incompatible producer shape can be accepted as if understood. Keep the repair small. Give Xray, Story, and Pair a consumer-owned literal expected version; on mismatch, suppress shape-dependent parsing and return the consumer's existing explicit empty/status form or a typed `:ok? false` mismatch. Add one focused test per consumer that injects a producer stamp different from the consumer pin. Do not build negotiation, migrations, or a compatibility framework.
acceptance_criteria: Xray, Story, and Pair compare producer envelopes with a consumer-owned expected version rather than deriving support from `re-frame.ui.tool/schema-version`; Story does not return parsed shape-dependent fields on mismatch; Pair reports an explicit typed mismatch rather than forwarding it as success; focused mismatch tests fail if only the producer version changes; ordinary version-3 reads remain unchanged.
notes: PR #6618 opened (worker/tool-schema-version-98-1-1). Made the version boundary REAL: each consumer (Xray/Story/Pair) now owns a LITERAL expected schema-version instead of deriving it from the producer's tool/schema-version. Xray rows->[] + version-status mismatch; Story suppresses all shape-dependent fields on mismatch; Pair emits typed :view-tier-version-mismatch (isError) instead of :ok? true. One focused RED->GREEN mismatch test per consumer + a new conformance fixture. title: Make ui/->react's frame prop exact and self-attributing
description:
The public ui/->react bridge reserves a foreign React prop named frame. Its runtime currently reads the value and tests some?, so it cannot distinguish an absent property from an explicitly supplied frame={null} or frame={undefined}. Under an ambient frame provider, the explicit invalid value silently falls through to that ambient frame, potentially dispatching/subscribing against the wrong application frame instead of honoring the fail-loud frame-target grammar.

For other malformed or dead supplied targets, ui/->react delegates to provider-scope-element, whose validation is hard-attributed to re-frame.ui/frame-provider. The resulting error tells an outward-bridge caller that [frame-provider ...] failed even though they called ui/->react, adding friction at exactly the migration seam this API exists to simplify.

Bounded fix: detect whether the JS props object owns the frame property; if it does, validate every value including null/undefined. Reuse the existing frame-target validation and shared context provider, but attribute the typed error/recovery to re-frame.ui/->react. Keep omission as the sole ambient-resolution case. Add focused controls for omitted, explicit nil/undefined, malformed, dead, and valid targets. No new context, root/preflight, validation framework, compatibility mode, or ownership mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: - An omitted frame prop continues to use the ambient frame chain. - An own frame property is always validated, including null/undefined, and never silently falls through to ambient context. - Malformed and absent/dead targets retain the existing typed frame-target categories but identify re-frame.ui/->react and give bridge-relevant recovery. - A valid frame id/live frame scopes without ownership as today. - Focused CLJS DOM tests cover the boundary without adding a new abstraction.

PR #6609 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6609) — worker/react-frame-prop-01rwd. Fix: resolve reserved frame prop by own-property presence (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call), not some?; new frames/->react-scope-element self-attributes every typed failure to re-frame.ui/->react (no-frame-context / bad-frame-provider-arg / frame-provider-frame-absent) with bridge-relevant recovery; omitted=sole ambient case; explicit null/undefined now fails loud instead of silent ambient fallthrough. frame-provider path untouched. Sole spec/API.md toucher; disjoint from live workers; srezq (migration guidance, spec/004 + docs/skills/reagent-migration.md) NOT touched — no overlap, srezq sequences after S4. Do not merge (worker).
PR #6609 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RESIDUE (2026-07-21) — reopen the exact bridge diagnostic owner; runtime frame resolution itself is correct.

Three independent lenses found that self-attribution is only partial. `frames/->react-scope-element` passes `re-frame.ui/->react` as `:where`, but nil/undefined and malformed props still delegate to `frame/require-frame-provider-target!`: nil records `:operation :frame-provider` and inherits the generic frame-provider/frame-root/options reason; malformed inherits the hard-coded reason beginning "frame-provider :frame must...". `error/ex-info-from-data` derives the visible exception message from `:reason`, so an outward-bridge caller still sees the wrong surface blamed. The focused tests select only `:rf.error/id` and `:where`, so they cannot catch this.

title: Honor explicit fragment overrides on unmatched raw-URL navigation
description:
PR #6581 promises that :url + :fragment is legal and the explicit request fragment overrides any fragment embedded in the raw URL. That holds when the URL matches a route because route-url rebuilds the address, but the unmatched shortcut pushes unmatched-url verbatim.

Current-main reproduction: [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/missing#old" :fragment "new"}] commits the not-found slice with :fragment "new" but pushes "/missing#old". The address bar, route slice, and guard/pending target therefore disagree. An explicit nil similarly cannot clear an embedded fragment. The focused tests cover embedded-fragment preservation and unmatched URL preservation separately, but not their documented combination.

Use one effective requested URL for unmatched navigation: preserve the raw path/query, replace or clear its fragment from the explicit request key, and feed that same URL to guards, pending-navigation, not-found params, history push, and the committed slice. Add one focused regression including override and clear; do not redesign raw-URL parsing or not-found policy.

While touching the fragment contract, truth the remaining normative residue in spec/012-Routing.md that still mentions route-url's deleted 4-arity and navigate's deleted opt/target-map split. Comments-only fixture/test wording is not an audit deliverable.

BOUNDARIES: a small resolution fix, focused tests, and one normative sentence. No URL object/protocol, new public helper, compatibility form, or new navigation mode.
acceptance_criteria: - For unmatched {:url raw :fragment value}, the explicit fragment replaces the embedded fragment in the effective URL; nil/empty clears it per existing normalization. - Guards, pending-navigation, not-found :params, history push, and the committed slice observe one consistent effective URL/fragment. - Matched raw-URL and existing not-found behavior remain unchanged. - Focused regression tests cover override and clear. - The remaining normative deleted-arity fragment sentence is corrected; no parsing abstraction or public API is added.

A raw target such as {:url "/page#%" :fragment "ok"} first fails matching because the discarded embedded fragment is malformed, freezes :rf.route/not-found, then pushes the repaired /page#ok URL. title: Make flat navigate and route-url map boundaries exact and total
description:
PR #6581 replaced positional navigation with one flat request map and described the boundary as always-on, closed, and total. Several malformed or half-migrated shapes still escape that contract:

- An in-place request may include :params whenever it also carries :query, :query-merge, or :fragment. Reproduction: after navigating to /items/old, dispatching [:rf.route/navigate {:params {:id "new"} :fragment "x"}] emits no navigate-bad-request and pushes /items/old#x; the supplied params are silently ignored. The ratified table says :params is never accepted in-place because changing params requires :to.
- A non-map request reaches dissoc and throws a raw host exception. A third event element is silently ignored, so a plausible half-migrated [:rf.route/navigate {:to :route/x} {:replace? true}] navigates while dropping the trailing opts.
- Mixed-kind unknown keys reach plain sort and can throw instead of producing :unknown-keys.
- The public single-map route-url boundary has the same rough edge: non-maps/raw missing-:to shapes produce raw or misleading host errors, and mixed-kind bad keys can fail while sorting instead of raising :rf.error/route-url-validation.

This is one authoring-boundary repair, not a validation project. Before request processing, require exactly the two-element navigate event and a map payload; reject :params without a destination; make bad-key reporting total over arbitrary EDN keys. At route-url, require an address map with :to and route all address-shape failures through the existing route-url-validation error. Keep the current closed roster and existing rich behavior.

BOUNDARIES: small explicit checks plus focused JVM/CLJS parity tests. No compatibility shim, Malli/request-schema framework, builder DSL, strict-mode option, or generic validator.
acceptance_criteria: - :rf.route/navigate rejects non-map payloads, extra event elements, and :params without :to/:url through :rf.error/navigate-bad-request before guards; slice and URL stay unchanged. - Unknown-key reporting is total for heterogeneous EDN keys on JVM and CLJS. - route-url rejects non-map, missing-:to, and heterogeneous-bad-key addresses through :rf.error/route-url-validation rather than raw/misleading host exceptions. - Focused JVM/CLJS controls cover the boundary cases. - No compatibility syntax, schema framework, builder, or new public API is added.

(1) validate-request treats :url by key presence, but resolution uses some?; {:url nil} therefore passes as a destination then falls into the in-place branch, potentially rebuilding the current route instead of failing closed. Make the discriminator consistent and cover the nil case without a schema/validator framework. title: Attribute :local-state only after a real React commit
description:
PR #6577 claims `:local-state` is attributed only to an "actually committed" state change, but `local-state` calls `reactive/note-local-state!` as a side effect inside the React functional state updater. `Object.is(cur,nv)` proves that one queued step changes its input; it does not prove the batch produces a commit. React also requires updater functions to be pure and may replay/discard their render work.

A real React 19.2 Chromium probe demonstrates the residual contamination without speculative concurrency: one batched `0→1` update followed by `1→0` runs both updater callbacks and renders a candidate, but commits nothing because the final state equals the prior committed state. Probe result: `renders=1`, `commits=0`, `notes=2`, DOM value still `0`; a later unrelated prop commit then occurs with those external notes still present. In re-frame.ui that stale `:local-state` stash is drained into the next unrelated ViewCell commit — the same class of false attribution this PR intended to remove.

The new test does not mount React or invoke the actual local setter; it calls the private gate directly and manually commits a cell, so it cannot reject net-zero batches, replay, or abandoned renders.

Keep the fix commit-aligned and small. A promising shape is a DEBUG layout effect in the local hook that compares the current rendered state with a ref of the last committed state and records the cause before the wrapper's later ViewCell commit layout effect. Equivalent commit-aligned designs are fine. Do not add a scheduler, transaction protocol, or public API.
acceptance_criteria:
- React state updater functions remain pure: they do not mutate the ViewCell/evidence stash.
- A real mounted test through the actual re-frame.ui local-state setter proves a committed value change contributes exactly one `:local-state` cause to that connected commit.
- Same-value setters and same-batch net-zero sequences (for example `0→1→0`) leave no pending marker; a later unrelated subscription/prop commit does not report `:local-state`.
- StrictMode updater replay remains idempotent and does not create false attribution.
- Tests exercise React/host commit behavior rather than only calling a private comparison helper.
- Production erasure remains intact; no scheduler, general transaction machinery, or public API is added.
- EP/docstrings no longer equate Object.is inequality inside an updater with an actually committed change.
notes: RESOLVED in PR #6604 (commit aa4d5179f3). react-set updater is now PURE; :local-state attribution rides a DEBUG committed-value useLayoutEffect (commit-phase only, skips mount, StrictMode-idempotent); note-local-state! sets the commit-time flag. Deleted the note-committed-local-change! updater gate. Proof: MOUNTED browser test drives the real local setter — real change => exactly :local-state; net-zero 0->1->0 commits nothing and leaves no stale marker on a later subscription commit. test:browser + test:elision green.

title: Preserve each detailed view cause instead of fabricating a cross-target span
description:
PR #6577 changed `:rf.view/causes` from keyword tokens to detailed records, but stores pending detail as `{cause-kind -> one detail}`. `merge-commit-cause` therefore merges every subscription movement under the single `:subscription` key: the latest target/query/frame/to/epoch wins while `:from` is retained from the earliest movement regardless of identity.

This fabricates evidence when two dependencies move before one commit. A direct current-main reproduction folded node A (`[:a]`, version 2→3) and then node B (`[:b]`, version 20→21); the pending record became node B/query B with `:from 2` and `:to 21` — a transition that never happened — and node A disappeared. The same one-per-kind assumption drops sibling Story overrides because `mint-commit-record!` uses `some` over `to-acquire`.

EP-0033 deliberately makes causes a vector because one commit can have several causes and its UI may summarize multiple changed dependencies. Preserve one record per distinct causal identity; coalesce repeated subscription moves only for the same observed target, keeping that target's earliest `:from` and latest `:to`. Keep ordering deterministic and bounded by the view's actual sites. This is an identity-aware collection fix, not a general evidence/provenance framework.

Current `commit-record` prose also still says "nine ruled kinds" and mentions only `:epoch-restore` absence, while the shipped surface is six kinds plus fallback with both `:epoch-restore` and `:hmr-remount` deferred. Truth that docstring while touching this surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two different subscription targets moving before one connected commit yield two truthful `:subscription` cause records; no record combines identity/version axes from different targets and neither dependency disappears.
- Repeated movement of the same subscription target may coalesce to one record with that identity's earliest `:from`, latest `:to`, and truthful latest epoch.
- Multiple moved Story overrides in one commit retain one detailed record per override identity instead of `some` dropping siblings.
- Canonical kind ordering remains deterministic; same-kind ordering is stable and explicitly pinned.
- `commit-record` documentation names the current six shipped kinds plus fallback and both deferrals.
- Record schema/API stays the existing vector-of-records; no general evidence framework or new public option.
- Current UI JVM/CLJS cause tests and production-erasure gates pass.
notes:
RESOLVED in PR #6604 (commit 31dc5e4693). Coalescing is now per distinct causal identity (subscription keyed on :target), so two distinct targets stay two truthful records (no cross-target :from/:to span, neither disappears); mint collects ALL override siblings with keep (was some). commit-record docstring truthed to six shipped kinds + fallback, both :hmr-remount/:epoch-restore deferred. Proof: two-subscription-targets-yield-two-truthful-records + sibling-story-overrides-each-retain-a-record (red->green).
PR #6604 three-lens audit follow-up (rf2-z2ken, 2026-07-21): acceptance is not complete for repeated lexical sites on one override identity. mint-commit-record! collects override-details per to-acquire SITE, so two sites reading the same overridden query emit two identical {:cause :story-override :override-id … :version …} rows for one changed causal identity. The React 19 ref-as-prop direction is right, but three bounded obligations remain:

title: re-frame.ui boundary + friction programme (UIx-review ratified)
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement. Ratified from the 2026-07-20 UIx adversarial reviews, Mike-approved.

CONTEXT: two independent adversarial reviews of re-frame.ui vs UIx converged, after mutual cross-examination, on this exact programme. The substrate's non-negotiables are unchanged: closed grammar, JVM parity, DCE/elision, manifests. This programme removes boundary/product friction WITHOUT relaxing those.

THE 8 WORK ITEMS (each a child bead of this epic — ids in the CHILDREN list; each child is fully self-contained):
1. Remove the Shadow install/cache tax (pre-publication gate; blocks rf2-vxgfnd.99.2).
2. Ship ui/->react — the outward bridge (spec/API.md row flips planned->live).
3. Complete declared :ref forwarding (delete the stale ref-prop-declared-s1 pin).
4. Admit the if-let binder family (if-let / when-let / if-some / when-some) to both grammar tiers.
5. Allow ui/spread at FOREIGN component call sites (internal views keep the literal props requirement).
6. One effect-dependency equality doctrine: rf= across native and interop tiers.
7. Dev-time :rf.ui.compile/missing-effect-dep diagnostic (warning tier).
8. Generate the AI context sheet from compiler/API data (generated skills/ artifact + drift gate).

DEMAND-GATED ROSTER (recorded dispositions, NOT beads — each fires only on its named trigger; do not file or implement before the trigger):
(a) defview-part — a compiler-owned def-level unit analyzed and INLINED at the call site so local/effect/react sites become the caller's lexical sites (manifests stay sound, position law checked post-inline, elision preserved). TRIGGER: several views across the repo/examples repeat the same local/effect site pattern (the debounce/media-query/interval shelf). The runtime custom-hook mechanism is rejected permanently.
(b) react/use-memo with rf= deps — computation caching for expensive pure render-scoped computations over props. TRIGGER: a named consumer with a demonstrably expensive computation rerunning on unrelated local/sub churn. Never for callback identity (compiler-owned handler identity already solves that).
(c) internal-view code splitting — extend react/lazy to accept a loader yielding an exported defview, composing ui/->react. TRIGGER: a real route needs it. No general Suspense data semantics.
(d) ui/view registry heads — stays wave-2 behind its existing ruled triggers (spec/API.md:309 — the parts-ceiling ruling or a native-table need; re-com is the demand-bar consumer of record).

REJECT FENCE (binding on all children):
- No runtime interpretation fallback for unprovable forms (one fallback arm reintroduces the walker into browser bundles, unsounds the manifest, and collapses the elision proof).
- No concurrent-rendering authoring surfaces over app-db (use-transition / use-deferred-value / Suspense-as-loading). React's own documented contract — react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore#caveats: an external-store mutation during a non-blocking Transition restarts the update as blocking — makes an imitation API over-promise by construction; the guide states the cession honestly.
- No opt-out memoization.
- No configurable lint platform/framework.
- No generic internal-view prop spreading.
- No second state model (contexts / Suspense-as-data / use-atom).
- No use-state-style overloaded setter (local's set!/update! split stands).
- No UIx feature parity goal.
- No compatibility aliases.

SEQUENCING/CONTENTION (mandatory reading for the mayor loop at dispatch):
- spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE — the ref/grammar/spread/equality children (+ the diagnostic child's spec note) EACH touch it: SEQUENTIAL among themselves and behind whatever currently holds 004 (rf2-rvs56 slice d queues for 004; the rf2-5e8zv lease-excision stages also touch 004). NO ordering edges are wired among those children; the mayor sequences the hot-zone at dispatch time.
- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc and implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/hooks.cljc are not hot-zone but CONTEND with rf2-5e8zv.1 (lease S1 deletes lease sites in the same files) — do not run concurrently with it; sequence after 5e8zv.1 merges or before it dispatches, mayor's call at dispatch time.
- spec/API.md is HOT-ZONE for the ->react child (blessed table row flips planned->live).
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is HOT-ZONE for the install-tax child.
- No Spec 009 rows are owed by ANY child: :rf.ui.compile/* ids are catalogue-exempt per the Conventions reservation.

DOCS/EXAMPLES/EP COVERAGE (binding on all children; restated per child): every child owns its docs, examples, and EP updates in the SAME PR as the change, never trailing. EP DISCIPLINE: settled EP meaning is preserved through a DATED ADDENDUM/ERRATUM recording the old clause and the new disposition (the EP-0009 convention) — never silently rewrite accepted EP text.
notes:
SKILLS COVERAGE (Mike-directed, 2026-07-20, binding on every child): each child's PR (or an immediately-sequenced follow-up in the same child) must reconcile the EXISTING skills that teach its changed contract — the sweep is GREP-DRIVEN over skills/** for the child's surface vocabulary, not roster-driven. Census at filing time: skills/reagent-migration/{SKILL.md, README.md, references/catalog-judgment.md (12 hits), catalog-mechanical.md, catalog-reject.md, gotchas.md, procedure.md, evals/evals.json (5 hits), spec/authoring-prompt.md} + skills/re-frame2/{patterns/stateful-components.md, patterns/managed-http.md, references/fundamentals/views.md} carry if-let/spread/use-ref/use-effect/->react vocabulary. Evals that assert the OLD contract (e.g. a rejection that child 4/5 legalizes) must be updated in the same PR or they red the eval gates. Gates: check_skill_re_frame2_drift, migration-contract-drift, eval-docs/eval-packaging as applicable. The future re-frame2-ui authoring skill (rf2-cv8a2y, trigger-gated W6) self-corrects: it is authored from then-current contracts at dispatch. Child 8's generated context sheet is additive and unaffected.
REPLICANT-REVIEW ADDENDUM (Mike-approved, 2026-07-21). The 2026-07-21 Replicant adversarial reviews (fable + codex, converged after cross-examination) ratified two additions to this programme, filed as children .9 (react/use-ref -> ui/ref promotion + DOM-node recipe rewrite) and .10 (frameless-first Tier-1 testing docs). Everything else Replicant surfaced was already owned here (.1 install tax — now corroborated by a second competitor; .5 foreign spread; .8 AI sheet) or is recorded below so the analysis survives the local-only review documents.

DEMAND-GATED ADDITIONS (recorded dispositions, NOT beads; fire only on the named trigger):
(e) Compiled nested placeholder splicing — recognize the three existing placeholders (:rf.ui/value/:checked/:key) at any LITERAL position of a literal handler form, compiled as static path writes (no runtime walk). TRIGGER: the first real consumer hitting :rf.ui.compile/placeholder-not-top-level with a map-shaped payload (e.g. [:form/set {:field :email :value :rf.ui/value}]). No vocabulary growth ever.
(f) ui/node-effect — DEMOTED from an earlier draft recommendation; the refutation is preserved so the gate stays honest: object refs attach at commit BEFORE effects fire (no nil-first-pass cost); most widget/chart nodes are STABLE while their data changes, so a node-scoped callback cannot serve the common case without duplicating effect's deps (and tearing the widget down per data change is worse); React 19's ref-callback contract requires stable callback identity (fresh closures detach/reattach every render) — real compiler identity machinery, not a thin lowering; StrictMode deliberately replays ref setup/cleanup in dev; ui/raw-fn already exposes callback-ref cleanup for the expert case. TRIGGERS to revisit: several real cases where the TARGET NODE's identity changes while the view stays mounted, or per-keyed-row node work (focus-the-new-row) proves materially inadequate under ui/ref + effect or the explicit callback-ref path.
(g) Presence attribute-overlay SUGAR — at most a compile-time overlay spelling that LOWERS ONTO the existing presence state machine and literal :timeout-ms law (never a second retention mode). TRIGGER: repeated real-world presence demand beyond toasts/modals. Both reviews agree even the sugar lacks evidence today.

REJECT-FENCE ADDITIONS (binding on all children, from the Replicant axes):
- No transitionend-derived retention or CSS-duration inspection for presence. (Honesty note, verified at source: Replicant is not naive here — replicant/dom.cljc removes stuck unmounting nodes via a fail-safe timer at the longest computed transition duration + 200ms. The contrast is heuristic-CSS-derived bound vs re-frame.ui's explicit, testable, CSS-independent :timeout-ms — reduced-motion, animation-vs-transition, and interrupted commits never change ownership.)
- No lifecycle-as-dispatchable-data (Replicant's :replicant.trigger/life-cycle through global dispatch). A speculative React renderer cannot promise 'mount happened once' — the recorded :on-mount/:on-unmount rejection (spec/004-Views.md:1492-1494) stands; the guide states the cession.
- No optional list keys (the compiler cannot guess which repeated child owns state/subs/presence; the build failure stays).
- No runtime hiccup/alias interpreter arm (the team that wants Replicant's model has the Reagent adapter today; re-frame.ui.data when earned).
- No runtime placeholder interpolation (the postwalk pattern) and no open placeholder vocabulary; ui/event is the door beyond the three scalars.
- No action-vector batching in handler values (a second effects language); no :alias-data-style render-option config channel (that is app-db + subs, frame-scoped).

CROSS-CHECK RECORDED: Replicant's aliases are attractive evidence for the IDEA of concise composition but fire NONE of the existing trigger-gated checkpoints (ui/tpl rf2-1hm7a3, registered ui/view rf2-a62fje, defview-alias rf2-ho1iba) — gates unchanged. The .9/.10 briefs are self-contained; the review documents at ai/findings/replicant/ are local-only provenance, not required reading for any worker.
close_reason: EPIC complete: all 10 children shipped and MERGED. Programme delivered the re-frame.ui boundary + friction surface ratified by the 2026-07-20 UIx adversarial reviews: ->react bridge (.2), ref forwarding (.3), if-let binders (.4), foreign-site spread (.5), rf= equality doctrine (.6), missing-effect-dep diagnostic (.7), generated context sheet (.8), ui/ref (.9), Tier-1 testing guide (.10), and the capstone install/cache-tax removal (.1, S0-S6 programme, final cut-over PR #6659 merged 2026-07-22: one-setting install contract, warm-cache reuse proven, Shadow version range 3.4.0-3.4.11). No unmet audit obligations found on the epic (#6640 rider obligations discharged in S6; #6646 rider repair shipped in #6659).

title: Xray panels/resources tests contaminate the CLJS conformance corpus (order-sensitive test isolation)
description: Pre-existing latent test-isolation fragility exposed by rf2-5e8zv.1's compile-graph reshuffle. When the Xray `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources*` tests run before `re-frame.conformance-corpus-cljs-test` in the shared node-test bundle, 5 `:resources/*` conformance fixtures fail (`[:rf/resource …]` subs return nil; expected traces not seen). PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: (1) the corpus passes in ISOLATION; (2) origin/main WITHOUT rf2-5e8zv.1 reproduces the identical corpus failure with the same `day8|conformance-corpus-cljs-test` --config-merge subset; (3) the same day8 isolation subset fails the unrelated `palette/fuzzy` `camelcase-boundary-bonus` test on origin/main too. main's full-suite compile-graph order happens to avoid the exposure; deleting the lease test namespaces reshuffled it. Root cause not fully localized: resource-registrar + source-store resource-kind clears in `reset-resources!` had NO effect, so the polluted shared state is elsewhere (candidates: the `:rf/resource` sub/image-assembly resolution, egress/observability config, or the corpus's lazily-captured pretest baseline inheriting prior-suite state — the JVM leaf avoids this by requiring [re-frame.resources] + a :reload-style reset; the CLJS leaf does not). FIX DIRECTION: make the CLJS conformance corpus capture a clean baseline / reset resource+egress state robustly, OR make the Xray resources panel tests fully isolate. Surfaced by rf2-5e8zv.1 (PR #6572).
notes: FIXED in PR #6572 (commit 8bfb468ded). Root cause: the CLJS conformance corpus (conformance_corpus_cljs_test.cljs) captured its per-fixture reset baseline LAZILY at deftest start, inheriting sibling-suite (Xray panels/resources) registrations from the shared node bundle. Fix: capture a FRAMEWORK-ONLY baseline at NS-LOAD (before sibling test nses register) and restore to it per-fixture — the CLJS equivalent of the JVM leaf's clear-all!+reload; the lazy snapshot is retained only for the end-of-suite try/finally restore so sibling nses keep their registrations. Corpus now order-independent; full test:cljs green (10312/0). No corpus assertions weakened.

title: S3: tooling instruction examples — re-frame2-pair MCP + eval fixtures
description:
Parent epic rf2-vwwvp: its description is the full normative design and IS AUTHORITATIVE OVER THIS BRIEF — run `bd show rf2-vwwvp` first and read it in full. Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions are final. BLOCKED ON rf2-vwwvp.1 (the S1 vertical cut) — the runtime must be on main before tooling examples describe it. Do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees); this bead plus the epic are complete.

## The grammar tooling examples must emit (settled)

    [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]

One map. Address keys :to :url :params :query :fragment; policy keys :replace? :scroll :bypass-guards?; edit key :query-merge. Positional arities are gone; there is no compatibility form.

Validity rules any emitted example must satisfy:
- :to xor :url; :url excludes :params/:query/:query-merge (:url + :fragment legal, request fragment wins).
- :query xor :query-merge; :query-merge is in-place only (no :to/:url) — cross-route query carry no longer exists; :query-retain is the route-side replacement policy.
- Omitting both :to and :url = navigate-in-place: a PATCH of the current location by key PRESENCE (:query {} clears; :fragment nil clears; omitted keys carried; route+params carried, never accepted in-place). The reserved :rf.route/self target no longer exists.
- Empty maps and pure-policy maps reject; in-place before any current route exists rejects; unknown keys (namespaced included) reject. Structural rejects surface as :rf.error/navigate-bad-request.
- route-url is a single 1-arity taking {:to :params :query :fragment}, strictly address-only.
- Facts spell :route-id; requests spell :to.

Canonical example shapes:
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/home}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:to :app/search :query {:q "clojure"} :replace? true}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge {:page 2}}]
- [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/some/path"}]

## Scope — tooling instructions

- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp: instruction text and dispatch examples that show or synthesize :rf.route/navigate (the pair-MCP instructions surface, i.e. what get-re-frame2-pair-instructions serves, and any dispatch/dispatch-dry-run examples).
- Any remaining eval fixtures anywhere under tools/ that dispatch navigate in the old positional shape (grep for ":rf.route/navigate" with a following non-map argument, ":rf.route/self", and "navigate-arity-misuse"; S1 already swept implementation/, examples/, spec/, and tools/xray — this bead owns the remainder under tools/).

Acceptance: a grep across tools/ shows zero positional navigate examples, zero :rf.route/self, zero navigate-arity-misuse (outside .beads and historical EPs). Relevant tool test suites and the mcp-conformance gate green.

## Fence (binding — emit/describe none of these)

No bare-keyword sugar; no navigate! facade; no positional/deprecated forms; no :in-place? marker key; no :route-id alias in requests; no builder/constructor helpers; no history-stack surface.

## Worker rules (standard, mandatory)

- Worktree guard BEFORE any edit: run `sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` (or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1`) from your intended checkout and report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT.
- Commit first, then rebase. NEVER `git stash` (a prior stash caused work contamination; the ban is absolute).
- Gates run in FOREGROUND only — no backgrounding, no piping gate output through tail/head. Run the focused suites listed here; do not run the full spine on a fresh worktree (CI owns that).

Evidence (grep across tools/): (1) :rf.route/self = 0; (2) navigate-arity-misuse = 0; (3) route-url positional = 0; (4) navigate! facade = 0; (5) old {:url ...} TARGET form = 0. pair-mcp: ZERO :rf.route/navigate anywhere (instruction menu teaches dispatch/dispatch-dry-run in PROSE with generic app events; the :navigate hits are the fx-id + browser-tab prose, not the routing event); generated descriptors_data.cljs + tool-descriptors.edn carry 0 :rf.route/navigate (NO 0sray/STOP-report needed). tools/xray already flat: S1 (rf2-vwwvp.1, commit 1353c1f407) migrated all xray routing testbeds/tests + the Trace-Panel dispatch example (023:209 -> {:to :app/settings}); it DELIBERATELY kept the EPOCH-OPEN display render at 023:211 ('rf.route/navigate :app/settings') which is a panel summary consistent with the adjacent line 213 'ROUTING activated :app/settings' convention -- NOT a call site (no [ bracket). The one positional-shaped grep hit (routes_epochs core.cljs:233 [:rf.route/navigate (merge ...)]) is a COMPUTED flat request map, already correct. No source changes made; no PR opened (zero diff). title: S1: the CI-atomic vertical cut — runtime + specs + fixtures + tests + examples + Xray
description:
Parent epic rf2-vwwvp: its description is the full normative design and IS AUTHORITATIVE OVER THIS BRIEF — run `bd show rf2-vwwvp` first and read it in full. Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions are final; no further operator input is required. Do NOT look for any ai/ dossier (local-only, absent from worker worktrees); this bead plus the epic are complete.

Everything CI-gated lands in ONE PR (fixtures live under spec/, adapter tests compile the examples, Xray code moves with its specs — the cut is atomic or CI breaks).

## The grammar (settled)

    [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]

One map. Address keys :to :url :params :query :fragment; policy keys :replace? :scroll :bypass-guards?; edit key :query-merge. Positional arities DELETED, no compatibility layer (pre-alpha).

## Validity rules (the always-on structural gate enforces ALL of these)

1. :to xor :url.
2. :url excludes :params, :query, :query-merge (a raw URL IS the address). :url + :fragment is legal; the request's :fragment overrides a URL-embedded one (today's precedence, navigate.cljc:352-355).
3. :query xor :query-merge.
4. :query-merge requires an in-place request (no :to/:url). Cross-route query carry (spec/012:483) is DELETED; :query-retain is the replacement policy.
5. Destination (:to/:url) OR in-place change required; key PRESENCE discriminates (:query {} clears the query, :fragment nil clears the fragment — both valid lone in-place requests). Empty maps and pure-policy maps ({:replace? true}) reject loud.
6. In-place before any current route exists rejects loud.
7. Unknown keys reject, NAMESPACED INCLUDED. One internal exemption: the runtime's :rf.route/enter-attempts resume rider (can_leave.cljc:446-456) is stripped BEFORE the gate. No open extension surface.

## In-place resolution (settled semantics)

Destination request = FRESH address (omitted :query/:fragment empty, as today). In-place request = PATCH of the current location: :query replaces wholesale ({} clears); :query-merge folds (nil removes a key); :fragment sets (nil clears); omitted keys carried unchanged; route + :params carried from the current :rf/route slice and never accepted in-place (changing params is a destination). This deliberately fixes today's self-nav surprise ({:fragment "x"} previously cleared the query and re-fired :on-match via the self target): the new form carries the query and MUST hit the existing fragment-only short-circuit (fragment-only-nav-fx, navigate.cljc:510-526) — anchor change, not reactivation. Implementation note (trust-the-programmer): requests built with conditional key-dropping should assert their own :to; no marker key, no mode flag.

## Deletions

- Reserved :rf.route/self target + its resolver branch.
- opts-only-keys / misplaced-opts-keys (navigate.cljc:36-62).
- :rf.error/navigate-arity-misuse + its Spec 009 row.
- The {:url ...} TARGET form (becomes the :url key).
- route-url's 2/3/4 positional arities.

## Enforcement (settled)

Event :schema validation is dev-only + schemas-optional (router.cljc:752-794), so the handler carries a small ALWAYS-ON structural gate: closed key roster + the exclusions + destination-or-change rule, plain set logic, total over the roster. The Malli reg-event :schema rides alongside as the dev-time rich explainer. The gate rejects BEFORE guard evaluation (as today, navigate.cljc:527-557) — a malformed request never consumes a :can-leave run.

## Error surfaces, in order (settled)

1. Structural gate → NEW id :rf.error/navigate-bad-request ({:reason :keys} tags), a one-for-one Spec 009 row swap with the retired arity-misuse row. It is NOT :rf.error/schema-validation-failure: that category is dev-only/schemas-gated while this gate is always-on — the channel-classification distinction is deliberate.
2. Unregistered :to stays the handler-level :no-such-route reject.
3. Route-level :params/:query validation via the existing route-url throw path (navigate.cljc:459-498), unchanged.
4. Guards, unchanged.

## Preserved protocols (do NOT touch)

Pending-navigation ENVELOPE unchanged: {:id :requested-by-event :requested-url :reason :direction :rejecting-route :rejecting-guard :enter-attempts :url-restored?} (can_leave.cljc:347-355; Spec-Schemas PendingNavigation ~:3624-3646) — only the :requested-by-event interior becomes [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]; continue's guard-bypass injection becomes a map assoc. :rf.route/continue / :rf.route/cancel by pending :id unchanged. Guards keep receiving the resolved FACT target {:route-id :params :query :fragment :url} (can_leave.cljc:12-18,77-97). Facts spell :route-id, requests spell :to (deliberate intent/fact vocabulary); match-url and the :rf/route slice are NOT renamed.

## route-url (settled)

Single 1-arity taking {:to :params :query :fragment}; strictly address-only — policy keys, :url, :query-merge, unknown keys all reject loud. No in-place form. Callers project: navigate handler select-keys'es its request; link-model projects its target map.

## Scope — one PR

1. Runtime: navigate.cljc grammar swap + structural gate; route-url single map arity; :requested-by-event interior.
2. Hot-zone spec surfaces:
   - spec/012-Routing.md: rewrite §Navigation is an event; DELETE §Arities and §:rf.route/self (replaced by the in-place resolution table); reg-event schema :373-375; opts table :416-425; §Fragments programmatic examples; cross-route :query-merge sentence :483 (capability deleted).
   - spec/API.md: navigate row :477; route-url arity row :461.
   - spec/009-Instrumentation.md: the one-for-one row swap (retire navigate-arity-misuse, add navigate-bad-request).
   - spec/Spec-Schemas.md: PendingNavigation :requested-by-event docstring example ONLY (no navigate args row exists).
   - spec/Conventions.md needs NO edit (no :rf.route/self roster entry; packaging row :1789 names only the event id).
3. Spec conformance fixtures (spec/conformance/fixtures/): routing-navigate.edn, routing-history-replace.edn, routing-fragment-navigate.edn, routing-redirect-on-match.edn, routing-scroll-restoration.edn, routing-on-match-fires.edn, cross-spec-routing-in-ssr.edn, route-navigation-blocked.edn.
4. ALL cross-artefact tests dispatching navigate: routing suites + ssr, ssr-ring, resources, derivation-conformance, security, http-composed, core smoke/derivation-graph, epoch, adapter suites. NOTE: adapter CLJS tests COMPILE examples/real-apps — this pins the examples sweep to this same PR.
5. Examples: realworld_http, realworld_resources, todomvc, capabilities/routing. Expectation: query-carrying sites get shorter, bare/params-only sites slightly longer — the win is uniformity, not length.
6. Xray: simulate_nav.cljs (synthesizes navigate dispatches) + tools/xray/spec/016/017/018/023 — Xray code and its specs move in the SAME PR per the standing xray-spec rule.

## HOT-ZONE sequencing (mandatory)

This PR touches spec/012 + spec/API.md + spec/009 + spec/Spec-Schemas.md. It must be the SOLE toucher of those files while open; sequence behind the current 009 queue (rf2-rvs56 slice d, rf2-s5wby, rf2-z0lnf) — do not start until those PRs are merged.

## Fence (binding — build NONE of these)

No bare-keyword sugar; no navigate! facade; no positional retention/deprecation shim; no :in-place? marker key; no prod validation-mode flag; no :route-id alias in requests; no policy keys on route-link; no Location record/protocol; no builder DSL/constructor helpers; no history-stack surface; no :history enum rename; no [:rf/location] projection sub; no route→view auto-render metadata; no pluggable engine protocol; no nested query DSL.

## Acceptance

- All gates listed above green with non-vacuous test counts.
- A repo-wide grep proves: zero positional navigate call sites; zero :rf.route/self; zero navigate-arity-misuse — outside .beads and historical EPs.

## Worker rules (standard, mandatory)

- Worktree guard BEFORE any edit: run `sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh` (or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1`) from your intended checkout and report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT.
- Commit first, then rebase. NEVER `git stash` (a prior stash caused work contamination; the ban is absolute).
- Gates run in FOREGROUND only — no backgrounding, no piping gate output through tail/head. Run the focused suites listed here; do not run the full spine on a fresh worktree (CI owns that).

Corrected acceptance: grep proves zero positional navigate call sites, zero :rf.route/self, and zero navigate-arity-misuse across implementation/**, spec/**, examples/**, tools/**, and testbeds/** (testbeds verified navigate-free today — keep them that way). The REPO-WIDE zero (adding docs/**, skills/**, migration/**) is the EPIC's close condition after .2 and .3 merge, recorded on rf2-vwwvp.

title: routing: replace positional :rf.route/navigate with the flat request-map grammar
description:
Design ratified by Mike 2026-07-20; all decisions below are final; no further operator input is required to implement.

Provenance: design ratified from the 2026-07-20 routing-review dossiers, Mike-approved. THIS BEAD DESCRIPTION IS THE NORMATIVE DESIGN. It is fully self-contained: child beads cite it as the in-beads authority. Workers must NOT look for any ai/ dossier (the ai/ tree is local-only and absent from worker worktrees) — everything needed is below.

## The change

Replace the positional navigation grammar `[:rf.route/navigate target params opts]` (and route-url's positional arities) with ONE flat request map:

    [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}]

- Address keys: :to :url :params :query :fragment
- Policy keys: :replace? :scroll :bypass-guards?
- Edit key: :query-merge

Positional arities are DELETED. No compatibility layer, no deprecation shim (pre-alpha posture).

## Validity rules (all loud rejections)

1. :to and :url are mutually exclusive.
2. :url is also mutually exclusive with :params, :query, and :query-merge — a raw URL IS the address; letting address keys ride beside it and be silently ignored is the exact failure class this redesign exists to kill. :url + :fragment IS legal, with the request's :fragment overriding a URL-embedded one (today's precedence, navigate.cljc:352-355).
3. :query and :query-merge are mutually exclusive (one replaces wholesale, one edits).
4. :query-merge requires an IN-PLACE request (no :to / :url). This deliberately DELETES today's cross-route query carry (`[navigate :route/other {} {:query-merge ...}]`, spec/012:483) — the declarative :query-retain route metadata is the replacement policy. Carrying state into another route's query is that route's :query-retain policy, not the caller's imperative choice.
5. A request must carry a destination (:to / :url) OR an in-place change — discriminated by key PRESENCE, not truthiness: `:query {}` (clear the query) and `:fragment nil` (clear the fragment) are valid lone in-place requests. Empty maps (`{}`) and pure-policy maps (`{:replace? true}`) reject loud.
6. An in-place request dispatched before any current route exists rejects loud (there is nothing to patch).
7. Unknown keys reject, NAMESPACED INCLUDED — full closure: `:my-app/replace?` fails as loudly as `:replcae?`. ONE documented internal exemption: the runtime's own resume rider :rf.route/enter-attempts (threaded into a re-issued event's request by :rf.route/continue, can_leave.cljc:446-456) is stripped BEFORE the gate runs; it is continuation bookkeeping, absent from the published grammar, and not a reason to open the schema. No open namespaced-key extension until a real consumer appears.

## In-place resolution table

A DESTINATION request (:to / :url present) builds a FRESH address: omitted :query / :fragment are empty, exactly as today. An IN-PLACE request (no :to / :url) is a PATCH of the current location, discriminated by key presence:

| Key | Present | Omitted |
|---|---|---|
| route + :params | — (never accepted in-place; changing params is a destination) | carried from the current :rf/route slice |
| :query | replaces wholesale ({} clears) | carried unchanged |
| :query-merge | folds into current (nil value removes a key) | — |
| :fragment | set (nil clears) | carried unchanged |

Before a current route exists there is nothing to patch — reject.

Implementation note (trust-the-programmer): requests assembled with conditional key-dropping (cond->-style optional destination) should assert their own :to; the framework adds no marker key or mode flag for this.

This deliberately FIXES today's self-nav surprise: `[:rf.route/navigate :rf.route/self {} {:fragment "x"}]` silently CLEARS the current query, misses the fragment-only short-circuit, and re-fires :on-match. Under the new form, `{:fragment "x"}` carries the query, satisfies the same-route/params/query condition, and MUST land in the existing fragment-only anchor path (fragment-only-nav-fx, navigate.cljc:510-526) — an anchor change, not a reactivation.

## Deletions

- The reserved :rf.route/self target and its resolver branch (in-place = omitted destination now).
- opts-only-keys / misplaced-opts-keys misuse machinery (navigate.cljc:36-62).
- :rf.error/navigate-arity-misuse and its Spec 009 catalogue row.
- The `{:url ...}` TARGET form (becomes the ordinary :url key).
- route-url's 2/3/4 positional arities.

## Enforcement (honest)

Event :schema validation is dev-only AND schemas-optional (router.cljc:752-794: gated on debug-enabled?, late-bound on the schemas artefact) — a Malli schema alone would protect FEWER builds than today's handler-body guard. The design therefore requires a small ALWAYS-ON structural gate in the handler: closed key-roster membership, the exclusions above, and the destination-or-change rule — plain set logic, total over the roster where today's guard covers four of six opts keys. The Malli reg-event :schema rides alongside as the dev-time rich explainer. The gate rejects BEFORE any guard evaluation (as today's misuse guard does, navigate.cljc:527-557), so a malformed request never consumes a :can-leave run.

## Error surfaces, in order (one didactic story)

1. Structural gate (shape) → NEW id :rf.error/navigate-bad-request ({:reason :keys} tags), a ONE-FOR-ONE Spec 009 row swap with the retired :rf.error/navigate-arity-misuse row — no net catalogue growth. Deliberately NOT :rf.error/schema-validation-failure: that category is the dev-only, schemas-artefact-gated validation channel, while this gate is always-on and production-surviving. The channel-classification distinction is deliberate and Mike-visible.
2. Target resolution — an unregistered :to stays the loud handler-level :no-such-route reject (the gate cannot see the registry, and shouldn't).
3. Route-level :params / :query validation — the existing route-url throw path surfacing as schema-validation-failure with :where :event (navigate.cljc:459-498), unchanged.
4. Guards, unchanged.

## Preserved protocols (do NOT touch)

- The pending-navigation ENVELOPE is unchanged: {:id :requested-by-event :requested-url :reason :direction :rejecting-route :rejecting-guard :enter-attempts :url-restored?} (can_leave.cljc:347-355; Spec-Schemas PendingNavigation ~:3624-3646). ONLY the :requested-by-event interior becomes [:rf.route/navigate {request-map}] for the programmatic door; continue's guard-bypass injection becomes a map assoc instead of positional vector surgery.
- :rf.route/continue / :rf.route/cancel by pending :id — unchanged.
- Guards keep receiving the resolved FACT target {:route-id :params :query :fragment :url} (can_leave.cljc:12-18,77-97), derived uniformly across all navigation doors. Facts spell :route-id; requests spell :to — deliberate intent/fact vocabulary, not drift. match-url and the :rf/route slice are NOT renamed.

## route-url

Single 1-arity taking the address map {:to :params :query :fragment}. Strictly address-only: policy keys, :url, :query-merge, and unknown keys reject loud rather than being silently ignored. No in-place form (a pure helper cannot read the current route). Callers project: the navigate handler select-keys'es its request; link-model projects its target map.

## Fence — NOT to build (binding on all children)

- No bare-keyword sugar ([:rf.route/navigate :app/home]).
- No navigate! function facade.
- No positional-arity retention or deprecation shim.
- No :in-place? marker key.
- No prod strict-validation mode flag.
- No :route-id alias accepted in requests.
- No policy keys on route-link.
- No Location record/protocol or spec'd wrapper type.
- No builder DSL or request-constructor helpers.
- No history-stack surface (:rf.route/back, forward, go-n).
- No :history :replace enum rename (:replace? stays boolean).
- No pure [:rf/location] projection sub.
- No route→view auto-render metadata.
- No pluggable routing-engine protocol.
- No nested query DSL / deep :query-merge.

## Docs vocabulary (adopt consistently)

Four terms: route definition / location / navigation request / navigation state. No public renames ride on the vocabulary; it is how the docs talk.

## Staging

Three children: S1 (the CI-atomic vertical cut — runtime + specs + fixtures + tests + examples + Xray; blocks the rest), S2 (prose corpus sweep), S3 (tooling instruction examples). S2 and S3 are blocked on S1.
notes: EPIC CLOSE CONDITION (mayor, 2026-07-20): after .1/.2/.3 all merge, a REPO-WIDE grep (outside .beads/** and historical docs/EP archives) proves zero positional navigate call sites, zero :rf.route/self, zero navigate-arity-misuse. Each child's acceptance grep is scoped to its own surfaces (see .1/.2 notes); this repo-wide check is the epic's final verification, run by the mayor at close.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE: all children shipped — S1 grammar keystone (vwwvp.1 #6581), S2 prose sweep (vwwvp.2 #6596), S3 tooling (vwwvp.3, verified-satisfied by S1), residue clean-close (6isc2 #6598). Positional :rf.route/navigate fully replaced by the flat request-map grammar; grep-clean across product surfaces.

title: Write Codex routing API review and recommendation
description:
## Problem

The current routing navigation grammar uses adjacent positional maps: `[:rf.route/navigate target params opts]`. A query-only navigation therefore needs an empty params placeholder, and the runtime carries special misuse detection for callers who put opts in the params slot. Mike asked for an independent design note that defines this problem carefully, evaluates alternatives, and recommends a more elegant pre-alpha API in light of Replicant's data-driven routing model.

## Deliverable

Create `ai/findings/routing-review/codex.md`. Ground it in current Spec 012, routing docs/implementation, and https://replicant.fun/tutorials/routing/. Explain the whole surface affected (navigate, route-link, route-url, match-url, current route reads, self/query changes, raw URLs, policies), present credible options and consequences, and make an opinionated recommendation consistent with the project's minimal/ergonomic/trust-the-programmer posture. This is analysis only; do not change runtime/spec APIs.

## Acceptance

The document is self-contained, distinguishes route definition/location/navigation request/state, includes representative syntax for ordinary and edge cases, evaluates at least three options, recommends one coherent grammar, states what not to build, and is committed/pushed from a guarded worker checkout.
acceptance_criteria: ai/findings/routing-review/codex.md carefully defines the positional navigation problem, evaluates credible alternatives across the full routing surface, and provides a concrete, proportional recommendation; committed and pushed.
