title: S4: enforce zero lease residue and run the integration proof
description:
## Problem

A removal this broad is vulnerable to forgotten filenames, camel-case classes, generated artefacts, dormant tests, historical research, and future reintroduction. A one-time grep is insufficient, while a non-zero baseline would merely bless existing residue.

## Required work

- After all preceding stages reach zero, add one narrow CI ratchet that scans git ls-files content and paths, excluding only .beads/**. Git history is outside the worktree scan.
- Detect natural-language forms and identifier/path forms, including singular/plural/past/gerund, kebab/snake names, keywords, and camel-case names, while not flagging ordinary words such as release or please. The guard itself must not contain an allowlisted live occurrence; encode/construct its forbidden token if necessary.
- Use no baseline, ceiling, or allowlist for product files: the permitted count is exactly zero.
- Prove the guard discriminates by temporarily seeding and restoring, byte-identically, at least prose, kebab/snake, camel-case, and filename cases. Verify a second introduction after returning to zero still fails.
- Run independent manual residue scans in addition to the new guard, including tracked filenames and generated docs output.
- Run proportional slice gates: UI JVM/CLJS/browser and production elision; adapters; core observation; Resources and cross-subsystem conformance; Xray/Pair/Story; specs/docs/examples; skills/evals. CI supplies the full matrix. Confirm runners select plausible non-zero tests and that deleted/renamed test namespaces did not silently fall out of discovery.
- Audit all children and any files added concurrently since their inventories; zero must be established against the final merged tree, not an earlier snapshot.

## Acceptance

- The final tree outside .beads has zero forbidden content and path matches under both the CI guard and an independent scan.
- Every mutation arm demonstrably fails, restoration is exact, and an unmodified tree passes.
- All proportional gates pass with credible counts; no public export, schema field, example, test, generated page, skill, tool, or AI file retains the rejected construct.
acceptance_criteria: A zero-baseline tracked-content/path ratchet blocks every lexical form outside .beads, mutation proofs discriminate, independent scans are clean, and all affected slice gates pass with credible non-zero selection.

THE RULING: (b) UNTRACK now — git rm --cached ALL 85 tracked ai/ files (whole trees: new-substrate-synthesis 61 + new-substrate-codex 24; 62 of the 85 carry the lease pattern \b[Ll]eas(e|es|ed|ing)\b|Lease = 43 synthesis + 19 codex; census re-verified at ruling time), disk copies retained. title: [BUG] Native editor migration strands the article owner on ordinary route leave
description:
The native re-frame.ui RealWorld editor removed the Reagent Form-3 unmount dispatch, but its app-minted article owner was not fully re-homed. `:editor/load-article` ensures `:realworld/article` with owner `[:lease :editor/article slug]`. Explicit releases cover edit→new, edit A→B, delete, and the old Reagent component's unmount. The compiled `ui_editor.cljc` is a pure `defview`, so an ordinary successful navigation from edit to home/profile/settings fires no release and leaves the owner active, pinning the resource until frame teardown.

This contradicts `ui_editor.cljc`'s claim that `:editor/*` events release the app-minted owner and weakens MIG-17's concrete proof. The browser ergonomic fixture is vacuous at teardown: it says the unmount leaks nothing but asserts only `(is true)` and never inspects `:active-owners`.

This is not `rf2-kkqy6q`: that bead fixed edit→new/delete and explicitly relied on the Reagent unmount for edit→other-route. PR #6549 removed that safety in the native rendition.

Keep the fix proportional. Give the owner a real causal/framework lifecycle that covers every route exit—prefer route-owned `:resources` if it can preserve the seed-on-load continuation cleanly, otherwise a view lease when lifetime truly follows the compiled view, or another explicit causal end path. Do not add a generic `:on-leave` framework feature merely for this example. Tighten MIG-17 guidance so a D-tier view is held until every old teardown responsibility has a proven new owner; naming hypothetical future end events is not completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Leaving `:realworld.editor/edit` for an unrelated route releases the editor article owner; edit→new, edit A→B, save, and delete remain correct.
- A non-vacuous test observes the resource owner's active/inactive state across a real leave path and would fail on the current native-view leak.
- `ui_editor.cljc`, `article_editor.cljs`, and MIG-17 prose state the ownership model that actually runs.
- No new routing/lifecycle abstraction is introduced unless independently justified by broader demand.
notes:
PR #6553 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (three lenses, 2026-07-20). This open P2 remains the exact owner; no duplicate filed. #6553's lease-capability calibration is correct, but the specific changed canonical proof is not: `ui_editor.cljc` still says the route-minted `[:lease :editor/article slug]` is released by `:editor/*` events and the suite proves it, while ordinary edit -> home/profile/settings (and the ordinary successful-leave shape) has no native release. The old Reagent Form-3 still supplies component-will-unmount; the pure native defview does not; the browser teardown assertion remains vacuous `(is true)` and never inspects active owners. Later #6559 preserves this claim.

The same defect reaches the skill's eval id 19. Its prompt establishes only a Form-3 `component-will-unmount` dispatch; it supplies no acquisition site, owner token, route, or causal end events. Expectations 4-5 nevertheless require the answer to assert a route/app-minted owner and a pure no-lease defview. That rewards invented application architecture. In the bounded fix already described here, make the eval require the honest D-tier move: inspect/ask who minted the lifetime and what ends it, hold the whole view until every teardown responsibility has a proven owner, then choose causal re-homing versus `ui/lease`. A route-minted example may be conditional context, not an unstated fact. Keep the existing proportional remedy: real owner lifecycle + one edit-to-unrelated-route active-owner assertion + aligned example/MIG-17/eval; no generic `:on-leave` feature.
PR #6569 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT (three lenses, 2026-07-20) — REOPENED exact source; no new framework or duplicate Bead.

The route-owned resource lifecycle and settled-read exit proofs are sound, but the ownerless seed continuation is not correlated to the route instance/slug. `:editor/load-article` uses `:reply-to [:editor/article-loaded]`; that handler accepts any successful article and replaces the editor slice. Leaving A removes its owner and requests cancellation, but cancellation is best-effort and the resource live-reply gate checks current-work/generation, not the editor's current route/slug. A late accepted A settle (or queued ownerless cache-hit) can therefore reseed A after navigation to edit B, new, home, or another route; different slug keys do not supersede each other's generation.

Bounded repair: include the intended slug in the reply target (for example `[:editor/article-loaded slug]`) and apply only while the current route/editor still targets that slug. Add one deterministic A->B or leave-before-A-settle proof with ineffective cancellation; the late A reply must not overwrite current state. Do not add routing/resource lifecycle machinery. Existing rf2-7a3uc and rf2-8yedm own only the skill/doc/fenced DOM follow-ups.
PR #6628 (worker/native-editor-owner-y4mgw): closes the #6569 REOPEN — the seed-on-load continuation is now slug-correlated. :editor/load-article carries the intended slug in :reply-to [:editor/article-loaded slug]; :editor/article-loaded seeds only while the current route is still :realworld.editor/edit targeting that slug (read from the same :rf.db/runtime coeffect load-article reads — no new lifecycle machinery). This drops a late cross-slug reply (best-effort-uncancelled A settle accepted for A's own entry per release-owner-handler) that previously clobbered the current draft after edit A -> edit B/new/home. Regression: editor-late-cross-slug-reply-does-not-clobber-the-current-draft in the reagent-adapter realworld-resources contract suite drives the REAL reply path — RED before the guard (2 failures: re-slug to article-a + draft clobber), GREEN after. The route-leave OWNER release itself was already merged on main (route :resources model, 3 existing tests). Docstrings in article_editor.cljs + ui_editor.cljc refreshed to the slug-correlated model. Gates green: test:cljs 10371 tests/0 fail; example release build 0 warnings; JVM s3 ergonomic proof 7/0; hardcoded-path check OK. Not touched: routing.cljs (hot-zone; model already on main), MIG-17/skills (rf2-7a3uc/#6570, rf2-8yedm closed).
AUDIT OF MERGED PR #6628 (2026-07-21): REOPENED exact source owner; no duplicate and no framework expansion.

The shipped slug-correlated reply target and current-route/slug guard correctly close the cross-slug A->B/new/home race. Applied and authored substantive patches have identical stable patch-id 8a9b1e124af3df966efe5e66bc4c7ef945232c7b; the focused current-main Resources suite is green (25 tests / 163 assertions).

MATERIAL P2 RUNTIME OMISSION — SAME-SLUG INITIAL LOAD CAN STILL CLOBBER TYPING. The edit route is non-blocking. :editor/load-article resets to a blank draft while the read is pending, and both editor views disable fields only for the save mutation, so a user may type before the article arrives. :editor/edit-field records those fields in the existing :touched set. The accepted same-slug :editor/article-loaded reply passes the new route/slug guard and replaces the entire editor slice via editor-slice, silently discarding those keystrokes. The cross-slug regression cannot catch this because it settles B before editing B. Proportional repair: use the existing :touched set; make the server draft the baseline, seed untouched fields from it, preserve current values for touched fields, and retain the relevant validation bookkeeping. Add one real-handler regression: enter edit A, edit one field before A settles, settle A, and prove the typed field survives while untouched fields and baseline come from the server. No resource/routing abstraction.

MATERIAL TEACHING DRIFT — the canonical example still carries four obsolete/copyable claims: routing.cljs route doc uses uncorrelated [:editor/article-loaded]; article_editor.cljs editor-page doc repeats it; README.md says resource reads have no reply-side hook and seed-on-load remains a Form-3 reaction, then repeats that in the file table. Truth those passages up to the route-owned, ownerless, slug-correlated read :reply-to model. No synchronizer or new test framework.

title: Carry the public context frame through frame-only and event-only SSR wrappers
description:
PR #6550 correctly made `use-frame-context!` return the renderer-agnostic public `React.useContext` value and fixed every sub/lease ViewCell wrapper, but two production wrapper paths still discard that correct frame and re-enter the server-broken private-slot reader:

1. `re-frame.ui.viewcell/render-frame` calls `(use-frame-context!)`, discards its return, then invokes `thunk`. A compiled `(frame)` in that thunk lowers to `frames/frame-ops` -> `resolve-frame` -> `adapter-context/function-component-current-frame`, which reads `_currentValue`. React 19.2 `react-dom/server` populates `_currentValue2`, so a frame-only compiled view under a live `frame-provider` still raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
2. Compiler selection prioritizes `render-events` for a production view containing event sites plus `(frame)`. `render-events` retains the hook frame for event capture but invokes the body thunk without binding `frame/*current-frame*`, so the `(frame)` site takes the same broken `_currentValue` path on the server.

Root reproduced the first path with a temporary direct-wrapper Node regression: a live `:app/a` Provider around `render-frame` returned `{:error :rf.error/no-frame-context}`. The temporary diagnostic was removed. Normal DEBUG `defview` coverage is insufficient because DEBUG selects `render-dev`, which already binds the frame and masks the production-wrapper defect.

Keep the repair tiny: reuse the existing `with-current-frame` helper around synchronous body evaluation in the two wrappers. No `_currentValue2` probe, renderer detection, new context abstraction, API, configuration, or broad wrapper rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- `render-frame` retains the value from `use-frame-context!` and evaluates its thunk under the existing dynamic-frame binding so a server-rendered frame-only compiled view resolves the closest live provider.
- `render-events` likewise evaluates its body under that binding while continuing to pass the same frame to event capture; this covers production views combining event sites with `(frame)`.
- Focused Node `react-dom/server` regressions directly exercise the production wrappers (not only a DEBUG `defview` path): provider-scoped frame-only and frame+event bodies resolve the provider; an unscoped frame read still fails loud.
- Existing client provider-retarget, event ownership, wrapper-shape/economics, and UI gates remain green.
- No `_currentValue2` access, renderer branch, public API, spec expansion, or new wrapper taxonomy.
notes:
rf2-wobnf resolved in viewcell.cljs (both wrappers), post-lease-keystone (#6572). Re-verified against current origin/main:
- Item 1 (render-frame): STILL BROKEN post-keystone — discarded use-frame-context! return, invoked thunk unbound. FIXED: (let [frame-id (use-frame-context!)] ((with-current-frame frame-id thunk))).
- Item 2 (render-events): STILL BROKEN — kept frame only as event destination, invoked body thunk unbound. FIXED: wrap the body thunk in (with-current-frame frame-id ...) before events/with-capture (same frame still threaded to event capture).
NOTE on the brief's 'compiler render-events selection in emit_cljs.cljc' framing: the bead's acceptance criteria put the item-2 fix in the render-events WRAPPER, not the emitter. The selection cond (subs+events->render-subs-and-events / events->render-events / subs->render-subs / frame-ops->render-frame) is CORRECT as-is: render-events IS the right wrapper for an event+(frame) view (no ViewCell needed); routing it to a combined wrapper would install a needless ViewCell and violate 'no new wrapper taxonomy'. emit_cljs.cljc UNCHANGED.
Red->green proof: direct-wrapper Node react-dom/server regressions in viewcell_server_frame_context_cljs_test.cljs (call the PROD wrappers directly under a live provider-element, since DEBUG masks via render-dev). Pre-fix both threw :rf.error/no-frame-context; post-fix resolve :app/a. Vacuity guard (no provider) fails loud both ways. Behavior-preserving on the client (_currentValue populated there).
Gates: JVM ui 999t/19794a 0F; node cljs 10315t/50966a 0F; elision PASS; browser-prod-elision 112t/483a 0F (55zsd fixtures + selection green). No 55zsd regression; disjoint surface.

title: Server-rendered compiled ViewCell frame context: use-frame-context! reads _currentValue, which react-dom/server (React 19.2) does not populate
description:

THE GAP: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell (use-frame-context!) discards the public useContext return and re-reads React's private _currentValue to obtain the frame it binds into frame/*current-frame* (the rf2-4rwtd fix, shipped #6540). React 19.2's SERVER renderer (react-dom/server) populates _currentValue2, not _currentValue — so a server-rendered compiled sub/lease ViewCell can still raise :rf.error/no-frame-context. The client path is correct; this is the server-render leg only.

THE FIX (bounded): stop discarding the public useContext return — use it as the frame source (it is renderer-agnostic), or read the documented dual-slot pair the way React internals do. Add one JVM/react-dom-server test: server-render a compiled view whose body subscribes, under a provided frame, and assert no :rf.error/no-frame-context. title: Keep production-callable epoch projection fail-closed for HTTP bodies
description:
## Problem

`re-frame.epoch/projected-record` is intentionally callable as a pure off-box projection transform even when `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` is false, for already-held or synthetic records. Its public contract promises fail-closed handling of stamped unschematized HTTP response bodies.

The HTTP body-slot table in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` is currently created wholly inside `(when interop/debug-enabled? ...)`. In a real production-start JVM (`RE_FRAME_DEBUG=false`) or an advanced CLJS build, that table is nil. `omit-off-box-http-bodies` then passes every stamped HTTP body through. A fresh-process reproduction with a valid frame and a synthetic `:rf.http/replied` trace carrying `{:rf.http/off-box-body :omit :value "TOP-SECRET"}` returned the literal body from public `projected-record` while `debug-enabled?` was false. This violates the mandatory off-box-safe boundary and can expose response data from imported/held records.

Existing disabled-gate tests miss the seam: they load the namespace while the gate is true and project records with empty `:trace-events`.

## Smallest repair

Keep the five production-real HTTP operation rows available to the pure projector regardless of the debug gate. Conditionally add only the dev-only `:rf.http/retry-attempt` row so its keyword can still disappear from advanced production bundles. Add one focused production-start/advanced assertion for a stamped production-real HTTP body. Do not add a new projector, privacy framework, runtime switch, or compatibility mode.

- With the debug gate false from namespace/process start, public `projected-record` replaces a stamped unschematized body for each production-real HTTP operation (`:rf.http/replied`, `:rf.http/accept-failure`, `:rf.http/http-4xx`, `:rf.http/http-5xx`, `:rf.http/decode-failure`) with `:rf/redacted` by default.
- `:include-sensitive? true` remains the explicit trusted-local opt-in; normal dev behavior and idempotency remain unchanged.
- The dev-only `:rf.http/retry-attempt` row still redacts in debug builds, while its sentinel remains absent from the advanced production bundle.
- A focused JVM production-start or equivalent source-load fixture and the existing CLJS production-elision probe pin both privacy and DCE behavior.
- The fix stays within the existing slot table/projector and tests; no public API, generalized privacy sweep, new gate, or framework.

title: Make the documented UIx hydration path use the adoption reporter
description:
## Problem

PR #6523 correctly documented that native UIx/Helix React-element roots were outside both hydration-mismatch channels. PR #6526 then added the existing React-native adoption reporter to `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render` and changed Spec 011 to say native UIx/Helix roots now verify through that channel. That is true only when a programmer mounts through the low-level adapter-contract `re-frame.substrate.adapter/render` path.

The first-class UIx guide teaches the ordinary native idiom instead: `uix-dom/create-root` plus `uix-dom/render-root` (`docs/core/how-to/use-uix-helix-or-slim.md`), and the adapter namespace exposes no render/hydrate helper. `spine.cljs` and the shared adapter tests explicitly note that substrate-native mounting bypasses `make-render`. #6526's mounted mismatch proof calls `substrate-adapter/render {:hydrate? true}`; it does not exercise the documented UIx root path. A UIx programmer hydrating through UIx/react-dom therefore still gets React's own recovery but no framework `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, despite current Spec 011's unqualified promise.

## Bounded solution

Give UIx one canonical, ergonomic hydration boot path that passes through the existing adoption reporter, and teach it in the UIx/SSR guidance. Prefer a tiny adapter-owned hydrate entry/helper over asking application code to reach into `re-frame.substrate.adapter`; alternatively, if host-owned roots deliberately remain outside framework instrumentation, narrow Spec 011 and the guide explicitly. Keep ordinary client-only native mounting unchanged. Helix may inherit only if genuinely free through shared code; do not build Helix-specific API for an adapter scheduled for removal.

Do not intercept or monkey-patch arbitrary React roots, add a DOM diff/hash/introspection layer, duplicate the reporter, or build a hydration framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The canonical documented native UIx SSR/hydration boot goes through the existing `make-render` adoption reporter (or the contract is explicitly narrowed so host-owned roots are not promised framework diagnostics).
- A mounted UIx fixture uses that same public/documented entry: divergent adoption emits exactly one `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, clean adoption is silent, and an authored recoverable-error callback remains composed.
- The entry has a practical ownership result for teardown/HMR and does not require programmers to unpack the installed adapter map or call an internal-looking namespace.
- Spec 011 and the UIx how-to describe exactly which root owns reporting; no blanket claim covers direct `uix-dom` / `react-dom-client` roots the framework cannot observe.
- Client-only native mounting remains unchanged; no React monkey-patch, DOM diff, structural hash, new reporter, generalized hydration abstraction, or Helix-only work.

title: Put native UIx hydration in an honest verification tier
description:
## Problem

PR #6507 defines two hydration-mismatch tiers, but its new Spec 011 text incorrectly places native UIx and Helix views in the hashable Hiccup tier. Native UIx/Helix roots are React-element programs, not pure portable data trees, and their shared hydration path did not receive the new adoption reporter. They therefore satisfy neither framework verification path the specification claims.

## Evidence

- `spec/011-SSR.md` says “Reagent / UIx / Helix views are pure functions returning a hashable render-tree.” The same spec already says UIx/Helix are not Hiccup.
- `re-frame.views/apply-adapter-wrap-view` explicitly documents that UIx/Helix registered-view output is a React element. The UIx/Helix adapter testbeds use native `$` with `defui` / `defnc`; a registered UIx production test directly proves `(rf/view ...)` returns a React element.
- `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render` calls React `hydrateRoot` without root options. It has neither a structural `:render-tree-fn` comparison nor PR #6507's `onRecoverableError` adoption wrapper.
- Reagent/Reagent-slim can provide a Hiccup data projection; native UIx/Helix views, especially hook-using views, cannot be safely called headlessly and hashed as if they were Hiccup.

## Consequence

A UIx programmer following the new specification can hash an opaque React element and receive false confidence, while actual React hydration divergence produces no `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` framework diagnostic. This is a material hole for UIx, which remains a first-class adapter. Helix is planned for removal, so it does not justify adapter-specific machinery.

## Bounded Solution

1. Correct Spec 011 immediately: name the tier by representation, not adapter brand. The structural-hash tier covers Reagent/Reagent-slim and any host that explicitly supplies the same pure data render tree on server and client. Native UIx/Helix roots are React-element roots and are not currently covered by that channel.
2. Give the shared React-hook hydration path the same small adoption-recovery reporting primitive as compiled UI: pass `hydrateRoot` options, emit only for React-recoverable errors during the initial adoption window, and preserve React's default (plus an authored callback if the existing open render opts expose one). A one-shot passive adoption sentinel is sufficient; do not hash or introspect React elements.
3. UIx is the required proof. Helix should inherit only if the implementation stays genuinely shared and free; do not build a Helix-specific branch for an adapter scheduled for removal.

No structural realization, React-element walker, DOM diff, console scraping, or generalized hydration framework is warranted.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 011 scopes structural hashing to hosts that actually provide an equivalent pure data render tree; it no longer says native UIx/Helix views are hashable Hiccup.
- A native UIx hydration fixture proves: clean adoption emits no mismatch; a recoverable initial mismatch emits one `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`; post-adoption recoverable errors are not misclassified; React default reporting and any callback exposed through existing render opts are preserved.
- The implementation reuses one small shared React-root adoption reporter/passive sentinel. Helix inherits only through that shared path; no Helix-only work is added.
- No React-element hashing/introspection, DOM diff, console interception, structural realization, or new hydration framework is introduced.
notes: DOC portion done — PR #6523. Corrected spec/011 §Hydration-mismatch detection: native UIx/Helix removed from the hashable Hiccup tier (they are React-element roots per apply-adapter-wrap-view; spine/make-render calls hydrateRoot without adoption opts). AC#1 satisfied. REMAINING (code, out of doc-PR scope): AC#2/#3/#4 — extend the compiled tier's shared React-root adoption reporter to the React-hook hydrate path (spine/make-render) + native UIx hydration fixture. Keep OPEN or file a code follow-up bead; do not close on #6523 merge.

title: Reconcile threshold-as-cap guidance with the advisory-only runtime
description: The merged #6505 migration example now projects its raw epoch record and then calls `cap-or-elide` with `:threshold-bytes 65536`, claiming the second walk bounds the payload. It does not. `re-frame.elision` uses `:rf.size/threshold-bytes` only to emit `:rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd` for an unclassified large string, then returns that value unchanged; only explicitly declared `:large` paths become markers, regardless of threshold. The example can therefore forward an arbitrarily large undeclared value even while reporting a destination-specific cap. title: Reject static special-element child shapes that diverge across React and JVM SSR
description:
## Problem
The shared compiler currently accepts source shapes for statically-known special elements that the two hosts do not interpret alike. `[:textarea (ui/html s)]` lowers to React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, which React 19.2 rejects, while the JVM tree and `emit-ui-tree` emit trusted markup (and currently even apply leading-LF compensation). For `<script>`/`<style>`, multiple authored children reach React as an array that warns and loses the body, while the JVM tree coalesces adjacent text and emits it; statically structural children are likewise dropped/stringified by React but rejected later by the JVM serializer.

This is a developer-feedback and hydration-parity bug, not a request for a general HTML content-model checker. The analyzer already knows the literal host tag and source child forms, so the useful fix is a few local, static rules.

## Solution shape
At `analyze-element`, reject `ui/html` beneath static `<textarea>` with a didactic direction to use `:value` or ordinary text. For static `<script>`/`<style>`, accept no body, one non-structural text-producing expression, or sole `ui/html`; reject multiple source child forms and visibly structural sole children, directing the programmer to construct one string (for example with `str`) or use the explicit trusted-markup bypass. Keep runtime-dynamic values programmer-trusted. At the public structural-tree seam, reject a manual `{:html ...}` child beneath `<textarea>` through the existing malformed-tree path and limit trusted-HTML LF compensation to `<pre>`/`<listing>`.

Do not add a generic validator, sanitizer, policy option, compatibility layer, or runtime framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The compiler rejects `(ui/html ...)` beneath static `<textarea>` with a concise actionable diagnostic; ordinary text and `:value` remain supported.
- Static `<script>`/`<style>` source forms cannot compile into known host-divergent multi-child or structural-child shapes; no body, one text-producing expression, and sole `ui/html` retain their intended paths.
- `emit-ui-tree` rejects an equivalent hand-written trusted-HTML-under-textarea tree through `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`; trusted-HTML leading-LF compensation applies only to `<pre>`/`<listing>`.
- Focused CLJ/CLJS tests demonstrate the previously divergent React 19.2 and JVM cases and the accepted cases.
- The relevant 004/004B grammar prose is accurate; coordinate the leading-LF wording with `rf2-13mou`.
- No generalized HTML content-model checker or new public configuration.
- A static `<textarea>` accepts at most one non-structural text-producing child, and literal `:value` / `:default-value` cannot be combined with any authored child; host-divergent shapes fail at compile with an actionable diagnostic.
- `emit-ui-tree` validates the effective textarea child stream after transparent fragment/view-boundary splicing: nested trusted HTML, structural or multiple children, and value-plus-child reject through `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` at the actual offending path; valid value or sole text remains unchanged.

title: DECISION: reconcile ordinary script/style raw-text semantics across spec/004B, spec/011, spec/Security, and the legacy hiccup render-to-string emitter
description: ⚠️ NEEDS A MIKE RULING (STOP-reported by rf2-0spji #6500, criterion 5 — a recommendation needing acceptance, NOT a determinable fix). #6477 made the compiled emit-ui-tree serialize <script>/<style> as HTML RAW TEXT (React-aligned, with closing-sequence rewrite). QUESTION: should the LEGACY hiccup render-to-string emitter (the reference ssr-ring path, lifecycle.clj) ALSO adopt React-aligned raw-text for script/style, so BOTH SSR paths agree? And the normative reconciliation across spec/004B + spec/011 + spec/Security of what 'raw text for script/style' means (trust boundary, XSS posture, the :html bypass). THE FORK: (a) align both emitters to React-raw-text (consistency, but touches the legacy emitter); (b) keep them divergent (compiled=raw-text, legacy=escaped) and document the difference; (c) something else. This is a 'what should the two SSR paths agree on' design call across 3 hot-zone specs + a runtime — Mike's ruling. Cross-ref rf2-0spji (#6500), rf2-2dh3b (#6477), rf2-993fz (#6484).
notes: DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 08:34 AUSEST) RULING: Option (a) — ONE raw-text semantics for ordinary ` payload can no longer terminate the element and pivot into HTML parsing); residual JS/CSS-language-context safety of interpolated data is author-owned, exactly as in React. Raw-text emission is NOT sanitization — say so. - Data payloads (JSON-LD head channel, __rf_payload/EDN wire): UNCHANGED, keep their stricter data-aware escapes — `<` inside string literals -> `\u003c`, and the EDN breakout reject :rf.error/ssr-edn-script-breakout. This is the house "raw + context-appropriate guard" style (html_helpers.cljc :78-190). - Net effect: refusal is removed, not weakened — refusal was pushing real content into the genuinely unguarded trusted shell opts (:head/:body-end), which is strictly less safe than a guarded render-tree element. TESTS: convert the sync + streaming throw-tests into emission tests; both legacy emitters and emit-ui-tree must BYTE-AGREE on a representative inline script/style corpus: literal JS/CSS operators (`if (a < b)`, `a > .b { }`), `&` unmolested, case-insensitive `` that round-trips through JSON.parse. Do NOT duplicate the compiled path's exhaustive React byte-parity corpus (ui_tree tests own it); focused corpus only. WHICH RECOMMENDATION AND WHY: both recommendations independently converged on (a); I followed their union — the dossier's ruling text extended by Codex's three verified deltas (streaming.cljc as a second legacy surface, the nonexistent-`:head-extra` correction, docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md in the retirement roster) — because one semantics across client render, compiled SSR, and hiccup SSR is the elegance/clarity/correctness call with zero security cost: every path carries the exact guard React itself applies, and the stricter data-payload escapes are untouched. ⚠️ MAYOR HOLD — keystone collision (2026-07-20). RULED Option (a) is dispatchable, BUT it edits BOTH SSR emitters incl. compiled emit-ui-tree (implementation/ssr/.../ui_tree.cljc) — the SAME file the render-static keystone (rf2-oo5lb / #6511 branch) touches for the pure-:server static emit path. Two workers on ui_tree.cljc = collision risk on the S6-opening keystone. DISPATCH xbvzh AFTER #6511 merges (render-static shipped, S6 opens) + rebase on it. xbvzh is INDEPENDENT (not S6-gated) so the short wait costs nothing; protecting the keystone is worth it. Brief from the RULED semantics in this bead's DECISION note (author content trust-the-programmer visible escape; data payloads unchanged; convert sync+streaming throw-tests to emission tests; both legacy emitters + emit-ui-tree BYTE-match). Cross-ref rf2-oo5lb #6511. PR #6539 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20; three independent lenses, current origin/main rechecked after #6542). MATERIAL RUNTIME BUG: the new legacy raw-text fast path is gated by `(every? string? children)`. Ordinary no-content Hiccup children (`nil`, `true`, `false`) therefore disqualify an otherwise valid script/style string and fall through to entity escaping: for example `[:script "if (a < b) x()" nil]` emits ``, and `[:style "a > b {}" false]` emits `a > b {}` in both sync and streaming paths. Multi-string and mixed string/structural bodies are also silently joined or walked: two strings are accepted although React 19.2 renders an empty body with a warning and the static compiler rejects the authored shape; a nested `[:script "x" [:script "alert(1)"]]` can place a literal `` outside `escape-raw-text`, allowing the HTML parser to terminate the outer element early. `emit-ui-tree` likewise says multi-child is malformed but `(every? string? children)` accepts multiple strings. BOUNDED REPAIR: in both legacy emitters, discard only ordinary no-content children (`nil` and booleans) before classifying a raw-text body. Accept zero/one meaningful string as appropriate; if a body contains a string and is multi/mixed, fail loud instead of silently corrupting or diverging. Preserve the existing no-string structural legacy handling. In `emit-ui-tree`, accept empty or exactly one string (or the existing sole `:html` bypass) and reject multiple strings. Add focused sync, streaming, compiled, and React-parity cases for nil/true/false, multiple strings, and mixed string/structural children. Keep this local; no child-policy framework, compatibility mode, sanitizer, or new public API. PUBLIC API TYPO: `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` currently describes the JSON-LD escape as the no-op `` `<`→`<` ``. title: Correct migration guidance for projection-side epoch redaction
description: PR #6481 changed `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md` to recommend the epoch `:redact-fn` as a stronger alternative to per-forwarder projection, claiming it erases each record as committed and that the ring buffer and listener fan-out therefore see redacted data. title: Document epoch creation and listener publication as distinct cadences
description:
PR #6479 correctly changed ordinary epoch RECORD CREATION from once-per-drain to one record per dequeued event, but three edited listener descriptions then equated that with CALLBACK CARDINALITY (docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1234, spec/API.md:842, tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:645). The runtime contract is broader: listeners receive the initial publication of an ordinary event record; record-render!, record-sub-run!, and record-unmount! can re-publish that same epoch after post-settle backfill; replace-frame-state! publishes a synthetic :rf.epoch/db-replaced record without a dequeued event; and the depth-halt path publishes a record for the queued event that never ran. Treating callbacks as a once-per-event clock can make Xray/pair-shaped tools miss corrected snapshots or miscount events.

At the same time, live public and AI/tooling prose still retains the retired once-per-drain model: docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1184; implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2245,2308,2521; implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc:61; spec/Privacy.md:248; docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md:92; tools/xray/testbeds/runner/core.cljs:158; implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:1134; and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1137.

Make one bounded documentation/docstring sweep that separates the two concepts: ordinary processing COMMITS one epoch record per dequeued event (parent and child events are separate records), while the listener is a record-publication/change notification and can receive a later version of an existing record plus synthetic tool-write/halt records. Keep the public wording concise; detailed examples can live at one canonical spec site and be linked/reused. Do not change runtime behavior, add compatibility machinery, or build a general prose scanner.

EXISTING OWNERSHIP: rf2-yiwag already owns only skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1186. Leave that file to rf2-yiwag or close it as a duplicate only if this fix deliberately absorbs it; do not make two fixes for the same line.
acceptance_criteria:

- Public listener text no longer promises exactly one callback per event; it explains initial record publication, possible same-epoch backfill re-publication, and synthetic replace/halt records at an appropriate canonical level.
- The named core/API/Xray/Privacy/late-bind/manifest stale claims are corrected with a targeted grep showing no remaining misleading per-drain cardinality in those surfaces.
- No runtime/API-shape change, new checker, or compatibility layer; existing docs gates pass.
- rf2-yiwag's preload line is not duplicated.

title: Keep accepted tag names from poisoning reagent-slim's cache lookup
description:
## Problem

`reagent2.impl.template/tag-name-cache` is a plain JavaScript object, and `cached-parse` asks it for hits by calling `(.hasOwnProperty tag-name-cache n)`. String Hiccup heads are accepted. Rendering the valid string head `"hasOwnProperty"` therefore caches a `HiccupTag` under the same property name as the lookup method itself. Every later cache lookup attempts to call that record as a function and throws a raw host `TypeError`.

PR #6478 correctly moved the reserved-`:rf/*` rejection ahead of this lookup, but its audit exposed this adjacent accepted-input failure in the same cache chokepoint.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render `(template/as-element ["hasOwnProperty" "first"])`; it successfully returns a React element and seeds the tag cache.
2. Render `(template/as-element ["div" "second"])` in the same runtime.
3. Observe `TypeError: tag-name-cache.hasOwnProperty is not a function` rather than a `div` element.

## Expected Behavior

Any accepted tag head, including `"hasOwnProperty"`, can be cached without changing how later entries are looked up; the subsequent ordinary tag renders normally.

## Actual Behavior

The accepted head overwrites the cache object's lookup method. All later tag parsing crashes until the runtime is reloaded.

## Consequence

One data-driven or library-supplied string tag can take down every later render in the application with an opaque host exception. This is a small implementation defect with broad SPA impact, not a request for a new cache abstraction.

## Bounded Solution

Use an unspoofable own-property check such as `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(tag-name-cache, n)` at this cache lookup (and only widen further if the same exact pattern is present on an equally reachable cache). Add one focused ordering regression: seed `"hasOwnProperty"`, then render an ordinary tag and assert both React types are correct. Preserve the existing reserved-key exclusions and the PR #6478 reserved-head behavior. Do not introduce a cache subsystem or generalized map wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: A focused red-before CLJS test renders the accepted string head hasOwnProperty and then an ordinary tag without a raw exception; both returned React types are correct; cache hit behavior, reserved-key exclusions, exact reserved-head diagnostics, and PR #6478's string-seeded reserved-keyword rejection remain green; the fix uses an unspoofable own-property check at the existing cache seam and adds no cache framework or public API.
close_reason: shipped #6501

title: Make compiled-ui hydration verify the real server-phase snapshot
description:
## Problem

Spec 011 requires a hydrating root's mismatch snapshot to be the fallback-bearing `:server`-phase tree, before the passive `:server` -> `:client` flip. The canonical public boot is two calls: `ssr/hydrate!` installs state and verifies first, then `ui/hydrate-root` adopts the DOM.

The compiled-ui implementation cannot currently make that verification honest:

- `ssr/hydrate!` invokes `:render-tree-fn` synchronously in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc`, before DOM adoption.
- The phase context in `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/runtime.cljs` defaults to `:client`.
- The only `:server` provider is installed later by `runtime/with-phase-flip` inside `ui/hydrate-root*`.
- The CLJS compiler emits direct React elements, not the JVM structural UI tree. If a pre-mount verifier actually materialises the compiled UI, it is outside the provider and sees `:client`; if it merely returns a component vector or opaque React element, the generic structural hash walks an opaque value rather than the rendered fallback tree.

PR #6476's phase-flip browser vertical deliberately skips `ssr/hydrate!`, so it proves clean React adoption and the post-commit swap but not the framework mismatch snapshot that its implementation comments claim remains honest.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a `.cljc` compiled root containing `(ui/client-only {:fallback [:p "loading"]} [:button "live"])`.
2. Server-render the root's JVM structural tree and place its real fallback-bearing render hash in the hydration payload.
3. On CLJS, run the canonical boot: `ssr/hydrate!` with a `:render-tree-fn` for that same compiled root, followed by `ui/hydrate-root`.
4. Inspect the value hashed before mount and the resulting mismatch decision.

There is no current path for step 3 to obtain the compiled root's rendered `:server`-phase structural tree. Materialising it before the provider selects client semantics; returning its opaque React/component representation is not an honest rendered-tree snapshot.

## Expected Behavior

The client verifier hashes the same fallback-bearing semantic tree the server hashed, reports no framework mismatch for an identical root, React adopts that fallback DOM, and the one root-scoped passive update then swaps all client-only sites to their client subtrees.

## Actual Behavior

The pre-mount compiled-ui verifier lacks access to the hydration root's `:server` phase and lacks an equivalent structural snapshot. Depending on the host-supplied value, verification can compare the wrong representation/phase or provide false confidence by hashing an opaque wrapper rather than the rendered UI.

## Consequence

A valid compiled-ui hydration can produce a spurious `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` (and abort in hard-error mode), or the framework detector can silently fail to verify the content React is about to adopt. This breaks a central SSR correctness/tooling promise for ordinary programmers using `ui/client-only`.

## Bounded Solution

Give the canonical compiled-ui hydration path one honest server-phase verification seam: either expose a pure fallback-phase snapshot for the pre-mount verifier, or perform compiled-ui verification from the hydrating root's first `:server` render before the existing passive flip. Reuse the existing root phase; do not add parallel phase state, a general React introspector, or a new framework when a compiler/root-local seam suffices. Keep ordinary non-hydrating mounts defaulting directly to `:client`.

Add one end-to-end red-before fixture that carries a real server hash through `ssr/hydrate!` and `ui/hydrate-root`, asserts no framework mismatch for the same compiled root, observes fallback adoption, and then observes the client-only flip. The same vertical may cheaply pin two sibling sites and the single root trace; those proof details do not warrant separate issues.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compiled-tier documentation and catalogue describe the signal precisely as React-recoverable errors reported during initial adoption, not exhaustive server/client divergence detection; they explicitly note that attribute-only mismatches may be warned in development, left unpatched, and produce no framework trace.
- One focused DOM fixture pins that limitation alongside the existing recoverable/text mismatch fixture; host callback composition and the root-local adoption window remain unchanged.
- The public `re-frame.ui/hydrate-root` source docstring, generated API page, and SSR tutorial contain one compact compiled-ui boot example: `ssr/hydrate!` without `:render-tree-fn`, followed by `ui/hydrate-root`, including the optional `:on-recoverable-error` hook.
- Path A remains small: no structural realization/hash, render fingerprint, console scraping, React introspector, parallel phase state, or generalized hydration framework.
- The identical compiled-root DOM vertical uses a root id unique to that test and scopes its sole positive :rf.ssr/phase-flip witness by [:tags :root-id]; a wrong-id substitute probe reds it.

title: Make the static streaming SSR stand-in preserve failed-boundary hydration
description:
PR #6485 ships examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/index.html as a runnable offline stand-in. It pre-bakes the final swapped DOM and final payload, but removes every suspense mount/template/chunk marker. That shape is not equivalent to fully buffered streaming output: streaming.client/install! sees no failed outcome, finalize! records an empty failed-boundary set, and hydration renders the flaky boundary body (throwing-card) instead of the baked declared fallback.

The previous non-issue ruling correctly verified supported fully buffered server output, where all resolved/failed chunks remain present for the initial sweep. It did not verify this checked-in hybrid artifact, which the repository itself asks developers to run.

The same page also says its final boundary-resolved DOM is emitted by rf/render-to-string. That is false: standard rendering deliberately rejects :rf/suspense-boundary; the streaming shell/continuation/finalization path produces this DOM.

Keep the fix bounded to the example. Make the checked-in stand-in and bootstrap carry a coherent failed-boundary outcome using the existing streaming contract, and correct the explanation. Do not redesign the runtime or add general example-test infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Correct the remaining teaching claims in the static streaming example. In core.cljc's flaky-slot comment, explain that the recorded failed-boundary outcome makes ssr/boundary choose its declared skeleton fallback; do not say a missing delta makes card-view render a skeleton (the body is throwing-card and card-view has no such branch). Across README.md, core.cljc, and index.html, replace "captured verbatim" / "same bytes" wording with the precise bounded truth: the checked-in page assembles the emitter's exact shell and continuation chunks, while deliberately substituting the documented placeholder render hash in the final payload. Keep this a prose-only example correction; no runtime redesign, generator, generalized harness, or additional browser infrastructure is required.
notes:
REOPENED BY THE CHRONOLOGICAL PR AUDIT OF #6485 (2026-07-19).

Three independent lenses reproduced a narrower case the original investigation accidentally excluded. The 502-test browser evidence remains valid for real streamed output and for fully buffered output containing all chunks. It does not cover the hand-written index.html, which has final swapped DOM + __rf_payload but deliberately omits every resolved/failed template and mount. With seen={}, finalize! publishes failed #{}, then the CLJS boundary selects throwing-card rather than the baked fallback.

Reuse the existing protocol and keep this an example-coherence fix. The inaccurate render-to-string wording is part of the same cause and same-file repair, not a separate Bead.
REOPENED BY THE CHRONOLOGICAL PR AUDIT OF #6506 (2026-07-20).

PR #6506 fixes the runnable page: a fresh compile plus an exact checked-in-page Chromium smoke reached three resolved cards and the flaky skeleton with zero runtime/hydration errors, and the protocol mounts/templates/delta scripts were gone after finalization. The remaining defect is explanatory, not functional.

examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:168-174 says the failed chunk's missing delta is "the whole story" and makes card-view render a skeleton. Shipped behavior is different: the body is throwing-card, card-view has no nil/skeleton branch, and install!/hydrate preserve the server's failed-boundary outcome so ssr/boundary selects its declared fallback.

The three example files also call the hand-written page "captured verbatim" / the "same bytes" as handle-request while explicitly replacing the emitter's real render hash with "00000000". The shell and continuation chunks do occur byte-for-byte and the payload is otherwise semantically equal; describe that assembly honestly. This is one small prose repair on the existing owner, not a new Bead. Independent correctness review found no runtime defect. A proposed general generator/browser gate was rejected as unnecessary for this bounded example under the project's no-overengineering posture.

title: Bind the ViewCell frame into frame/*current-frame* so ambient subs resolve under ratom-family hosts (W7b prerequisite)
description:
FILED from the 2026-07-19 Xray-on-re-frame.ui investigation, AMENDED same day after the Codex counter-analysis (both in ai/findings/2026.07.19.xray-ui.md — local-only; this description is the durable substance).

THE FIX (unchanged by the amendment; both analyses agree): ambient (sub ...) sites resolve their frame through the routed :adapter/current-frame hook, and the ratom-family readers (Reagent/reagent-slim — provider/current-frame ratom, class-component (.-context cmp) read) return nil inside ui function components, so a compiled view's sub reads raise :rf.error/no-frame-context under a Reagent/slim host. ui's own event/(frame) paths are immune (direct context reader) — a sub-read-only asymmetry, same class ui patched for plain-atom (rf2-vxgfnd.24). FIX at the compiled boundary: re-frame.ui.viewcell's use-frame-context! already reads the frame from React context and discards it — retain it and bind it into re-frame.frame/*current-frame* while evaluating the compiled body thunk, so ambient sub/lease resolution hits the precedence-first dynamic tier regardless of which adapter's reader the hook routes to. Keep the binding scoped to the body evaluation (descendant ViewCells bind their own context; no ambient leak across React's lazy child rendering). REJECTED alternatives (for the record): broadening the Reagent reader (weakens its fail-loud boundary); route-publishing ui's reader for Reagent kinds (one artefact overriding another's installed-adapter behavior); per-site Xray special-casing.

FRAMING (the amendment): this is NOT an Xray-specific patch and NOT part of a guest-root contract. It establishes the general outward-interop invariant — once a ViewCell consumes its frame from React context, every re-frame op its body evaluates observes that frame, whichever compatible renderer owns the surrounding tree. The original filing's guest-root rationale (independent ui/mount roots surviving host-adapter disposal as a feature) is WITHDRAWN: renderer independence is not data-lifecycle independence — a guest root's views consume reactions/sub-caches the installed adapter owns, and dispose-adapter! takes those down (spec/006 adapter symmetry), so a surviving guest root is a zombie, not resilience. The ruled W7b architecture is instead: Xray becomes a ui-COMPILED SUBTREE hosted by the installed adapter — ui/->react (the blessed S6 outward bridge, spec/API.md:249) exports the compiled shell/panels as ordinary React components; Xray keeps its existing substrate-adapter/render mount + returned-unmount lifecycle for every surface (inline shell, overlay, popout, standalone panels). One adapter, one root owner, no guest-root machinery, no new public mechanism.

TEST: one hardening browser test — a ViewCell over ratom-family sub nodes under a Reagent-installed host reads a sub, dispatches, repaints (mechanism-sound via Xray's auto-open watcher precedent, currently untested). The W7b acceptance bar later adds: destroy the host adapter and prove the Xray root IS unmounted (host-owned lifecycle) — the opposite of the withdrawn guest-root expectation.

SEQUENCING: this fix is parallel-safe (viewcell.cljs, not hot-zone) and can land now — it is the general invariant, wanted regardless of W7b. W7b itself sequences behind ui/->react landing (S6). Cross-ref: rf2-vxgfnd.98 (S6 epic, W7b workstream), rf2-vxgfnd.24 (plain-atom precedent), spec/API.md ->react rows.
notes:
PR #6540 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6540) — bind ViewCell frame into frame/*current-frame* around the compiled body (with-current-frame) in all 7 sub/lease wrappers; render-events/render-frame unchanged. Hardening test uses a dynamic-tier-only ratom-family stand-in reader: no-binding fails loud, with-binding resolves, mounted ViewCell resolves provider frame + repaints, isolation pin (per-ViewCell, no leak). spec/API.md untouched (internal correctness fix). Gates green: ui-jvm 1016 / core-jvm exit0 / test:cljs 10350 / test:browser 514 / test:ui 904. Do NOT merge (worker).
PR #6540 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-20; correctness lens, independently reproduced on current React 19.2).

The browser/Reagent repair is correct, but `use-frame-context!` still loses the Provider frame under CLJS `react-dom/server`. It calls `React.useContext(frame-context)` and discards that correct value, then calls `adapter-context/function-component-current-frame`, which rereads the private `frame-context._currentValue` slot. React 19.2's server renderer uses the secondary slot `_currentValue2`: a direct repository-local probe under a Provider showed, during BOTH `renderToStaticMarkup` and `renderToString`, `useContext(C) = "provider"`, `C._currentValue = "default"`, and `C._currentValue2 = "provider"`. Consequently a server-rendered compiled sub/lease ViewCell with no outer dynamic binding binds nil/default instead of its Provider frame and can still raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.

The new test does not cover this host: its Node arms manually test the dynamic tier, while its mounted Provider bodies are skipped unless a browser DOM exists. No later edit to `viewcell.cljs` or `adapter/context.cljs` fixes the seam, and an all-state Bead search found no duplicate owner.

BOUNDED FIX: have `use-frame-context!` retain the PUBLIC `React.useContext` return and resolve it with explicit precedence: an existing `frame/*current-frame*` still wins, otherwise use the hook value through the existing sentinel/coercion/corruption-validation rules. Do not inspect `_currentValue2` or add renderer detection/configuration. Add one CLJS `react-dom/server` regression rendering a Provider plus compiled `sub` ViewCell (a lease twin only if essentially free). No new adapter API, server abstraction, compatibility mode, or framework. The public `ui/render-static` path remains JVM-only; this closes the source Bead's broader compatible-renderer/outward-interop invariant for ordinary React server hosts.

title: Reject reserved reagent-slim heads before type-aliased cache hits
description: PR #6460 makes the invalid-hiccup-head rejection carry the exact offending :element, but the rejection still occurs only inside parse-tag. cached-parse consults tag-name-cache first. The cache key for a string head "rf/x" and the reserved keyword :rf/x is the same string, "rf/x". Seeding the cache with the valid string form therefore lets the later reserved keyword take the cache-hit path, bypass reject-reserved-rf-head!, and produce a React element whose type is "rf/x" instead of throwing. A direct probe against the compiled current runtime observed {"seeded":true,"outcome":{"threw":false,"reactType":"rf/audit-cache-twin"}}. title: Treat omitted hydration prefix as React's effective empty prefix
description:
PR #6458 makes `ui/hydrate-root` obtain identity from a validated Root Manifest, but the optional `:identifier-prefix` case bypasses the existing live-root uniqueness fence.

Root Manifest v1 explicitly makes every extension key optional, and `re-frame.ssr.manifest/valid?` accepts an unmodified S1 descriptor. For such a bare manifest, `hydrate-root*` reads a nil prefix, omits React's `identifierPrefix` option, stores nil in the live-root registry, and `check-root-claim!` deliberately skips the prefix arm when nil. React 19.2 does not have a distinct “no effective prefix” state: `hydrateRoot` canonicalizes the omitted option to the empty string `""`.

The result is that two different valid bare manifests on one document are both admitted even though both React roots own the same effective prefix. That defeats Spec 004C Layer 3's promise that two live roots cannot share an effective `identifierPrefix` and can make their `useId` output alias.

A temporary public-API browser test planted two containers with exact matching server DOM and two adjacent valid manifests containing only schema-version and distinct root-ids. The first `ui/hydrate-root` succeeded; the second was admitted. The focused full browser run reported 493 tests / 2756 assertions with exactly two failures, both in the probe: the expected `:rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix` and expected effective prefix `""` were absent. There were no test errors or hydration-mismatch page errors. The probe was removed byte-identical afterward.

Correct this at the hydration identity boundary: canonicalize a missing manifest prefix to React's actual effective empty prefix for claim bookkeeping (and report it as `""` on collision). Do not derive a root-id prefix client-side—the server used no prefix, so that would break hydration. Preserve manifest optionality, the existing error id, and the existing two-call boot contract. Reconcile the narrow Spec 004C claim that collisions are “only possible” through authored prefixes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two live `ui/hydrate-root` calls using distinct valid manifests with omitted `:identifier-prefix` reject the second before React work with `:rf.error/duplicate-identifier-prefix`, reporting effective prefix `""` and the owning root.
- A single bare manifest still validates and hydrates successfully; manifest extension keys remain optional and no root-id-derived prefix is synthesized on the client.
- Explicit server-authored prefixes retain their current behavior, including collision detection and exact pass-through to React.
- The live-root registry records the actual effective prefix for hydrating roots, so unmount/release frees the claim normally.
- Spec 004C describes the omitted-prefix route accurately; no new error id, public option, negotiation, cache, fallback, or version machinery is added.
- Focused SSR/UI browser tests and existing root-registry tests pass with non-zero plausible counts.

title: Serialize script and style text with raw-text-aware React semantics
description: PR #6448's emit-ui-tree sends every text node through five-character HTML entity escaping. That is incorrect inside HTML raw-text elements: the parser does not decode entities in script/style, so a valid style node containing a & b < c becomes DOM text a & b < c rather than the authored CSS, and script/style content changes. Closing-tag text is also mishandled: React 19.2 emits context-safe spellings (for example a JavaScript Unicode escape in the script closing name and a CSS escape in the style closing name) so the raw-text parser does not terminate early, while emit-ui-tree emits entity spellings whose entities remain literal. This violates the one-conversion-table/client-SSR coherence contract and can cause hydration/behavior divergence. Fix narrowly with context-aware text serialization for script and style, pinned byte/parsed behavior against React 19.2 for ordinary ampersand/less-than text and embedded closing-tag sequences; update Spec 004B's blanket escaping row to name the raw-text exception. Do not add a general sanitizer or parser framework; ui/html remains the explicit trusted-markup bypass.

title: Linearize custom-element conflict admission across ledger and live registry
description:
## Confirmed cross-atom race

PR #6440 intends a rejected dev/JVM write-through registration to change neither the live `custom-elements` aggregate nor ledger `::sources`. The implementation first swaps `ledger-state`, using a snapshot of `@custom-elements` as a precheck, and only afterward calls the atomic live `write-element!` barrier. Those two atoms are not one transaction.

A forced current-main interleaving with two threads is deterministic:

1. Both conflicting registrations update separate ledger source rows while the live aggregate is still empty, so both prechecks admit.
2. Both reach `write-element!`.
3. One live write wins; the other correctly throws `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict`.
4. Both ledger rows remain. `projected-aggregate` is now nil/conflicting even though the live aggregate contains the winner.

Observed outcome: one `:admitted`, one anchored conflict, live `#{:a}`, invalid projection. This breaks the PR's atomic rejection and “rejected registration never enters the ledger” guarantees. A later reload operates on a ledger that already contains the rejected contradiction.

## Deliverable

Linearize write-through conflict admission across the dev ledger and live aggregate so a registration rejected by the winning live verdict cannot remain in `::sources`, while an admitted concurrent registration cannot be lost by a reload commit. Preserve the production direct path's one-atom/DCE shape and the existing reentrant-watch/commit generation behavior.

Choose the smallest protocol repair. Do not introduce a generalized transaction framework, public API, configuration, or per-render work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic two-thread fixture places both conflicting registrations after their ledger precheck and before their live writes; exactly one is admitted, the rejected row is absent from `::sources`, and `projected-aggregate` equals the live registry.
- The same proof covers both arrival orders and distinct build ids.
- Concurrent write-through versus commit still produces a legal serial result with no admitted row lost or applied twice.
- Reentrant registration from a publication watch retains the existing generation semantics and does not deadlock.
- Production keeps a single atomic live-registry barrier with the ledger DCE'd.
- No generalized transaction layer, second public registry, API, or new CI job.
notes: Fixed in PR #6475 (commit: linearize write-through admission via write-through-verdict inside the single ledger-state swap; publish live aggregate as a projection). Red-before: 200/200 JVM rounds fail projected-aggregate==live on pre-fix code; green after. Gates: ui JVM 1001t, cljs node 10289t, browser-prod-elision PASS, elision PASS, core 2093t.
close_reason: shipped #6475

title: Preserve every equal custom-element declarer before admitting a replacement
description:
## Confirmed defect

PR #6440 stores one canonical `::owner` on an aggregate entry when several sources contribute `rf=`-equal declarations. That makes the next same-source replacement unable to see the other equal declarers.

Concrete current-main reproduction:

1. `a.ns` declares `:x-el` with `#{:p}`.
2. `z.ns` declares the same `#{:p}`; the aggregate keeps canonical owner `a.ns`.
3. `a.ns` re-declares `#{:q}` on the write-through/REPL path.
4. The write is admitted by `(= owner source)`, even though live `z.ns` still contributes `#{:p}`.

The live manifest becomes `#{:q}` and the ledger projection is conflicting/nil. The next unrelated reload raises `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` only after the invalid value is already live. This violates the headline pairwise-`rf=` law, last-known-good retention, reject-without-writing guarantee, and ledger/aggregate coherence. The existing tests separately cover equal duplicates and sole-source replacement, but not their composition.

## Deliverable

Retain enough provenance in the same atomic aggregate entry to represent every equal live declarer (or an equivalent single-atom design). Replacing one source must remove/replace only that source's contribution, compare the arriving declaration with every remaining live declarer, and reject atomically when any differs. Keep `custom-element-properties` readers unchanged. The dev ledger must also decline the rejected row, and the production direct path must retain the same law under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`.

This is a bounded repair: no second atom, public API, config knob, generalized registry framework, or per-render lookup.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two equal declarers followed by an unequal re-declaration from the canonical owner is rejected before either aggregate or ledger changes.
- The same sequence from the non-canonical owner remains rejected with deterministic two-source evidence.
- A sole source can still replace itself; after another equal declarer is genuinely removed, the remaining source can replace itself.
- Equal duplicates remain order-independent, and a clean aggregate still equals the ledger projection.
- The focused advanced-production fixture composes equal-duplicate admission with canonical-owner replacement and proves the barrier survives DCE.
- Existing staged-reload, permutation, unrelated-reload, and linearizability gates remain green; no new framework or public surface.
notes: Fixed in PR #6475 (commit: ::owner->::owners set on aggregate entry; admit joins/replaces-if-sole/conflicts-naming-all; canonical-owner retired). Red-before: 8 assertions fail on single-owner code (only 2 declarers named, self-replace admitted). Advanced-prod composition pin (equal-dup then canonical-owner replacement rejected under DCE) green. Same gate run as u25hr.
close_reason: shipped #6475

title: Wire the missing G-16 keyed-reorder-under-slots proof
description:
## Confirmed gap

PR #6442 graduated G-16 to the wired roster, but the original slot feature bead `rf2-ri0k6n` required two distinct proofs: normalized client/JVM slotted-output parity, and keyed reorder under slots preserving identity/occurrence paths. The shipped `:slot-vtable` corpus case renders one fixed row order through SSR/static structural normalization. It never mounts, rerenders A/B as B/A, or observes identity/occurrence ownership across commits. `slot_render_fn_arity_cljs_test` covers only the separate dynamic arity contract. A repository-wide current test census finds no slot-specific reorder fixture.

This is a real behavioral boundary, not prose polish: a slot body executes deferred inside the reusable library seam, while the enclosing keyed row must still determine React identity and the runtime occurrence path. One-state SSR parity cannot catch a reorder that remounts or cross-retargets row-scoped evidence.

Add the smallest focused mounted-browser G-16 arm using the existing v-table-shaped slot seam: render two keyed rows through a caller-supplied `ui/render-fn`, rerender the same keys in reverse order, and prove each row keeps its own identity and occurrence ownership. Reconcile the G-16 wired claim only as needed to name that executable proof. Reuse existing root/flush/evidence helpers; do not add a new harness, CI job, generated matrix, or broader keyed-list sweep.

- The same fixture observes the slot-owned/enclosing occurrence identity (or an equivalent row-scoped committed behavior/evidence) and proves it remains attached to the correct key after reorder.
- A focused mutation of the slot/enclosing-row key propagation makes this fixture fail, then the restored tree passes.

- No new test framework, CI job, combinatorial matrix, runtime API, or generalized identity machinery.

notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 17:58 AUSEST)

RULED: spec/011 gains §Phase flip — the S5 ui/client-only completion contract. This block is self-contained for the spec worker (the dossier is retired). The ruled contract:

1. PHASE MODEL. A root renders in exactly one of two phases, :server or :client — deliberately the same vocabulary as the Root Manifest :phase key (011:455, ":server — the only v1 value; the field exists so a future phase is additive"): this contract cashes that reservation in rather than minting a third word. A ui/client-only site renders its fallback in :server phase and its client subtree in :client phase; the compiled site is phase-conditional, reading a root-scoped phase value that defaults :client when no hydrating root provides one. Non-hydrating roots (mount / render! / ui.test/render) are born :client and never flip — S3 behaviour is byte-identical for them, existing tests undisturbed. render-static is pure :server output with no manifest and no flip (004C:573 already states this).

2. SINGLE UPDATE. The phase is ONE root-scoped value written exactly once; all client-only sites in the root swap fallback->client in the single update that write produces. Per-site flip state is non-conforming (per-site flips = visible tearing, N updates, exactly what every promise site forbids).

3. TIMING. A hydrating root boots in :server phase: the first compiled (hydration) render renders fallbacks — this is what makes React adoption clean and keeps the §Hydration-mismatch hash honest (server hashed the fallback-bearing tree). The mismatch snapshot is taken over the :server-phase tree and the flip MUST NOT run before that snapshot. After the root's hydration commit, the runtime schedules the flip as the root's next ordinary update (React's own documented two-pass pattern for server/client-divergent content). A painted fallback frame before the swap is permitted and by design — the fallback is mandatory, presentable UI the user has been looking at since first paint. No synchronous pre-paint flush (flushSync in the hydration commit path buys nothing visible and is hostile to streaming/readiness-driven hydration).

4. FAILED ROOT. The flip is a stage of a SUCCESSFUL root boot. A root that failed to boot (011 §Failed-root isolation, the rf2-1b0po contract) never flips: its server-rendered fallback markup stays, inert, as part of what the failed root leaves behind. No additional error is emitted — :rf.error/root-boot-failed already fired naming root/frame/:phase; isolation is not recovery, and the capability-free fallback is precisely the part of the page designed to stand without a runtime. A root that booted but took the mismatch warn-and-replace path DID boot, so it flips normally; the replacement render is an ordinary post-commit client render, no special casing.

5. MULTI-ROOT. The flip is per-root and independent — each root flips when ITS hydration commits. No page-wide barrier; one slow or failed root never delays a sibling's flip (a barrier would couple what §Failed-root isolation decoupled and deadlock on any dead root).

6. OBSERVABILITY. One diagnostic trace: :operation :rf.ssr/phase-flip, :op-type :info, :tags {:root-id ...}, fired once per hydrating root at flip commit; diagnostic channel, DCE'd under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false like every non-error :rf.ssr/* row. It is NOT an event and mints NO epoch (the 009 epoch unit is a dequeued event; the flip is render-layer root bookkeeping — routing it through dispatch would pollute app event streams). The Spec 009 catalogue row (and Spec-Schemas if touched) lands in the SAME PR as the spec section's first emit description, per the one-catalogue rule.

ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCE (state it plainly in the section): today's client emit (emit_cljs.cljc:670) drops the fallback template entirely; under this contract the compiled site becomes phase-conditional, so the fallback template rides the client bundle. Unavoidable (React must materialise the fallback vdom during the hydration render) and cheap by construction — capability-free static markup in the same emit-standalone shape react/lazy fallbacks already use. Sites cannot be compile-time-gated per root (a root cannot see through defview boundaries). RULED proportionately: NO new elision/size gate — the existing perf-bundle budget gate already covers any real regression; the spec section states the cost in prose, nothing more.

SEVEN PROMISE SITES to reconcile (most need no wording change — their promises become true once §Phase flip exists; add cross-ref pointers only where natural):
  - spec/API.md:251 and :368 (011 named authority; S5 phase-flip hydration fixture)

  - spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:573 — render-static never flips (already correct)

title: Publish Story with every declared in-repo dependency in its generated POM
description:
## Problem

PR #6435 made `day8/re-frame2-xray {:local/root "../xray"}` a required Story dependency and documents that a future `day8/re-frame2-story` coordinate will bring Xray transitively at the same version. The source graph is now honest, but the package boundary is not implemented.

A clean `clojure -M:clein pom` from `tools/story` reports that it is skipping all five `:local/root` coordinates (core, reagent adapter, machines, HTTP, and Xray). The generated POM contains only Clojure, Reagent, and Malli. This is expected clein behavior and is why release workflows must rewrite local roots before packaging. No workflow currently deploys `day8/re-frame2-story` or performs those rewrites. The lockstep verifier inventories Story but also omits Story's HTTP and new Xray edges from `TOOLS_LOCAL_ROOTS`, so its current green result cannot catch either omission.

The README correctly says Story is not on Clojars yet, so this is a pre-alpha release gate rather than a claim that today's users can fetch it. It is still necessary before the first alpha: publishing the current generated POM would recreate the exact consumer compile failure rf2-r8trk fixed in source.

## Small correction

Give Story one concrete pre-alpha publish path, using the existing local-root rewrite helper and generated-POM verification. Rewrite every main-deps in-repo coordinate to the lockstep Maven version, ensure Xray and the framework leaves are available before Story deploys, and verify the generated POM contains them. Extend the existing lockstep inventory to cover Story's actual edges.

Do not design a general release platform or combine every tool cadence. A small Story-specific workflow or a bounded extension of an existing release path is enough.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is an executable, documented path that publishes `day8/re-frame2-story` for the first alpha.
- Before packaging, every main `:local/root` dependency in `tools/story/deps.edn` is rewritten to the repo `VERSION`; at minimum the generated POM contains core, reagent adapter, machines, HTTP, and Xray at that exact version.
- The release cannot deploy Story before those coordinates, especially Xray, are available.
- A pre-deploy check inspects the generated POM and fails if an expected dependency is absent or any in-tree dependency was silently skipped.
- `verify-version-lockstep.sh` accounts for Story's HTTP and Xray edges. No general release-orchestration framework.

title: Make Story's :xray :filters preset drive Xray's real filter surface
description:
## Problem

Story publicly accepts `:xray {:filters {:in [...keywords...] :out [...keywords...]}}`, but the runtime cannot apply it. `apply-filters!` probes `day8.re-frame2-xray.filters.config/configure!`; that namespace does not exist, so `filters-available?` is permanently false and every non-empty preset only warns. The warning cites `rf2-ak4ms`, which is not a Bead.

The needed Xray surface already exists: `day8.re-frame2-xray.config/configure!` accepts `:rf.xray/filters`, and Xray registers `:rf.xray/hydrate-filters` for the live `:rf/xray` frame. There is also a wire-shape mismatch: Story's schema/examples use bare keywords, while Xray's pill shape is `{:pattern <keyword-or-string>}` (or a typed pill). Executable probe: `(canonicalise-pill :my/noise)` returns `{:kind :never :params {}}`, while `(canonicalise-pill {:pattern :my/noise})` returns `{:kind :event-id-pattern ...}`. Simply redirecting the existing call would therefore still create inert filters.

This is a shipped ergonomic surface, not optional polish: a programmer can declare a schema-valid preset, receive no validation error, and get no filtering.

## Small correction

Keep Story's compact keyword-vector API and lower it at the Story→Xray boundary to Xray's real pill representation. Make the preset work both before the first embedded panel mount and when switching variants after the Xray frame already exists: seed the established config surface for first-mount hydration and update the live frame through the established filter event/helper when present. Reconcile the nearby stale “Xray absent/feature detect” docstrings while touching the seam.

Do not add `filters.config`, a plugin system, a general filter abstraction, or a second Xray registry. Reuse the existing config/frame surfaces and add focused behavioral tests around actual `:active-filters` and event survival.
acceptance_criteria:
- A schema-valid Story preset such as `{:filters {:out [:app/noise]}}` becomes Xray's canonical pill shape and actually hides matching events.
- The result lands for both an initially selected variant (before first embedded-panel mount) and a later variant switch with `:rf/xray` already installed.
- Missing/empty `:filters` remains a cheap no-op; switching to an explicit empty filter set has a deliberate, tested meaning.
- Tests assert the real `:rf/xray` active-filter state and at least one matcher outcome; they do not pass through a shimmed nonexistent namespace.
- Remove the nonexistent-namespace probe/warning and correct the adjacent absent-Xray wording. No new plugin/framework layer.
