title: Server-only render-tree heads have no client semantics: keyword view-refs + :rf/suspense-boundary silently paint phantom DOM
description:
Split out of rf2-o4rbh (which fixed the streaming SSR example; this is the framework/spec question it exposed). NOT a regression — every behaviour below is as currently specified. The problem is that two render-tree heads resolve on the JVM SSR emitter and silently mis-render on every client substrate, with no diagnostic on either side.

EVIDENCE (measured, not inferred). Rendering the example's client tree through stock Reagent + react-dom/server produced:

  <section class="cards">
    <suspense-boundary id="card.revenue"><card>revenue</card></suspense-boundary>
    <suspense-boundary id="card.signups"><card>signups</card></suspense-boundary>
    <suspense-boundary id="card.latency"><card>latency</card></suspense-boundary>
    <suspense-boundary id="card.flaky"><throwing-card></throwing-card></suspense-boundary>
  </section>

The same tree rendered by the JVM streaming emitter produced four correct <div class=\"card\"> subtrees.

TWO DISTINCT HEADS, SAME FAILURE MODE:

1. Keyword view-refs. spec/Conventions.md (Render-tree shape vs runtime lookup) + spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md 237 are explicit: a bare [:keyword args] head in a render tree is an HTML element, never a view; the runtime does not intercept the keyword case. Reagent's parse-tag runs (name tag), so :dashboard/card becomes tag \"card\" and the keyword argument becomes a text node. BUT spec/011-SSR.md 245/267/279 has the JVM emitter resolve keyword heads via (registrar/lookup :view head). So the same hiccup means \"registered view\" on the server and \"HTML element\" on the client. A .cljc app that shares views across both — the whole point of the SSR story — cannot write a keyword head that means one thing.

2. :rf/suspense-boundary. spec/011-SSR.md 277 pins it as recognised ONLY by the streaming shell walker, and the non-streaming JVM emitter fails loud on it (:rf.error/ssr-suspense-boundary-outside-stream) precisely because its name passes the DOM tag grammar and would otherwise emit a phantom element. The CLIENT has no such guard: re-frame.ssr.streaming.client is DOM-swap machinery only, so a boundary left in a client render tree paints exactly the phantom <suspense-boundary> the JVM emitter refuses to emit. The asymmetry is the bug: the server fails loud, the client fails silent.

WHY IT BITES. The mistake survives every server-side test — this is how it shipped in the flagship streaming example (rf2-o4rbh) and went unnoticed. Only a client render reveals it, and it reveals it as wrong pixels, not an error.

OPTIONS (Mike to rule — this is a spec question, spec/011 + Conventions are hot-zone):
 (a) Status quo + diagnostics only. Cheapest. Adapters warn (dev-gated) when a render-tree keyword head has a namespace that matches a registered view id, and when :rf/suspense-boundary reaches a client render tree. Keeps the normative model, kills the silence.
 (b) Make the JVM emitter stop resolving keyword heads — one rule corpus-wide (\"keyword heads are HTML elements, everywhere\"). Most coherent, but it is a normative change to 011 and breaks any consumer relying on the documented emitter behaviour.
 (c) Give keyword view-refs client-side semantics. Rejected by Conventions today, and it would have to land in every adapter (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, Helix, re-frame.ui) plus every cross-language port — not small, and it costs a hot-path registry lookup per keyword head.

RELATED, worth settling in the same ruling: what SHOULD a client render tree contain for a region the server streamed? streaming-install! materialises each boundary into a live <rf-suspense data-rf2-suspense-mount=\"<id>\"> wrapper, so on a genuinely streamed page the DOM carries wrappers the client render tree has no way to express — hydrate-root would see a structural mismatch. The rf2-o4rbh example is static (its hand-written index.html has no fallback templates and therefore no mounts), so it does not exercise this; a live streaming host would. Spec 011 does not say what the client tree should look like at a boundary. That gap is why the example had nothing correct to copy.

NOT actioned in rf2-o4rbh: that bead fixed the example (Var-headed children, a reader-conditional card-slot so the marker stays server-side, and a card view that falls back to its skeleton when its slice is absent) and added client-render cover at implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/ssr_streaming_example_cljs_test.cljs.
notes: PR #6378 opened (PR-1 of the ruling's SS7 split): keyword-head removal + corpus migration + spec prose. Gates green across ssr(405/1746), ssr-ring(199/978), core(2073/9912), template(60/705), cljs(10070/49708), browser(462/2589), adapter-smokes(3), mkdocs --strict, check_doc_slugs. Remaining ruling scope filed as rf2-ycz3k (SS2 component + SS3 lifecycle, blocks-on this) and rf2-01zvu (SS4 client-side loud :rf/* head). SEQUENCING NOTE for mayor: SS5 asked to sequence emit.cljc/streaming.cljc with-or-after rf2-8vi4q, which is still open/unclaimed - this landed first, so 8vi4q now rebases and inherits an emitter with the coord call sites already removed (its step 2 is half-done); server-side source-coord annotation is unreachable in the interim and pinned as such.

title: reagent-slim cannot release: duplicate :local/root literal aborts the release.yml rewrite
description:
FOUND by the rf2-do3m2 worker (#6340) while hardening the Clojars preflight; reported not fixed, as a distinct defect.

DEFECT: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/deps.edn contains the literal :local/root "../../core" TWICE — line 13 inside a prose comment, line 16 as the real coordinate. release.yml's rewrite step (which converts :local/root to :mvn/version before packaging) asserts src.count(before) == 1, so it ABORTS on reagent-slim.

CONSEQUENCE: the reagent-slim leaf CURRENTLY CANNOT RELEASE AT ALL. reagent-slim is the only leaf with a duplicate; the other twelve have exactly one occurrence.

SEVERITY REASONING: this is FAIL-CLOSED, which is why it has gone unnoticed — the deploy stops and nothing bad ships. It is filed P2 rather than P1 because no wrong artifact can reach Clojars through it. But it means a shipped adapter is unreleasable, and it would only be discovered at the moment someone actually tries to cut a release.

WHY IT MATTERS TOGETHER WITH rf2-do3m2: that rewrite step is what stands between the in-tree :local/root coordinate and the published pom. The same worker proved  SILENTLY SKIPS :local/root coordinates, so a pom built without the rewrite carries no day8/re-frame2 dependency at all. The rewrite is therefore load-bearing for correctness, not convenience — and on reagent-slim it aborts.

FIX (small): make the comment not contain the literal (reword it), or make the rewrite's occurrence assertion structural rather than a raw string count. Prefer whichever leaves the invariant honest — a count of 1 that is satisfied by luck is the same class of defect as the preflight bug #6340 just fixed.

⚠️ Do NOT run an actual deploy to verify. Exercise the rewrite step against the real deps.edn locally.

Gate: the rewrite step run against all thirteen leaves (all must produce exactly one substitution); npm run test:script-policy (preflight tests: 15 passed baseline). .github/workflows/* is HOT-ZONE if the rewrite itself is edited — check no other worker holds it.

title: Make unsupported scroll-strategy rejection genuinely always-on
description:
PR #6333 correctly removes map-form scroll strategies from the optional fx-args schema, but its schemas-absent fallback is not the always-on rejection the source and Spec claim. re-frame.routing.scroll/scroll-fx-handler calls trace/emit-error! in its default branch. trace/emit-error! is wrapped in interop/debug-enabled? and DCEs under CLJS :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false; delivery also depends on the optional trace-tooling hook. Therefore a production app that does not load the optional schemas artefact reaches the handler, performs no scroll, emits no production-surviving record, and returns nil — the same silent outcome #6333 set out to remove. Spec 009 compounds the contradiction by marking the row Channel=diagnostic while calling it the ALWAYS-ON leg.

Use the existing two-channel error seam, not new machinery. Fan :rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy through error-emit/emit-error-both! (or the existing equivalent already loaded by the routing artefact), preserving the dev trace while adding the production-survivable error record. Keep navigation unaffected and recovery :no-scroll. Update the one Spec 009 row/channel and its always-on roster as required. Do not add a strategy registry, callback, compatibility map form, or new error abstraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- With schemas absent and goog.DEBUG=false, an unsupported :rf.nav/scroll strategy performs no scroll but emits one :rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy record on the always-on error surface.
- In development the same occurrence still produces the structured trace, with no double emission on either channel.
- The record retains :strategy, :supported, :frame, :reason and :recovery :no-scroll; valid :top/:restore/:preserve behavior is unchanged.
- Spec 009's Channel and prose agree with the implemented two-channel behavior and the always-on category roster includes this runtime error.
- A focused advanced-production test/probe proves the record survives goog.DEBUG=false without the schemas artefact; an ordinary dev test proves both channels and no-scroll recovery.
- No scroll extension seam, registry, compatibility form or new error helper is introduced.
notes:
PR #6376 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6376) opened, not merged.

Gap CONFIRMED empirically before fixing. scroll-fx-handler's default branch emitted via trace/emit-error!, which is wrapped in interop/debug-enabled? and DCEs under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false. With the optional schemas artefact absent the fx-args gate soft-passes, so on a schemas-less PRODUCTION host the handler ran, performed no scroll, and emitted NOTHING on either channel.

title: Separate PR docs checks from the Pages deployment concurrency group
description:
PR #6329 made docs.yml the sole merged-tree build/smoke/deploy boundary for the now-untracked docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js, but docs.yml uses one workflow-level concurrency group for both main pushes and the unfiltered pull_request check:

  concurrency:
    group: pages
    cancel-in-progress: false

GitHub keeps at most one running and one pending run per group; a new pending run replaces/cancels the older pending run even when cancel-in-progress is false. This occurred immediately after merge: main push run 29638598705 for #6329/e0bd5479 was queued behind the preceding docs deploy, then PR #6330's unrelated always-present docs check (run 29638609140) entered the same group and canceled the main run before any job started. The next main commit touched only skills/scripts and did not match docs.yml's push.paths, so no successor deployment rebuilt, smoked, or published the SCI bundle. The old deployed playground therefore remains stale, and the exact consumption boundary #6329 established did not run.

Fix the concurrency key, not the deploy machinery. Give pull-request checks a per-PR group and keep main pushes in one serialized Pages group; for example an event/ref-scoped key such as docs-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }} (or equivalent). Do not add a new workflow, queue service, or commit-back mechanism. A workflow_dispatch or the fixing docs.yml push should then rebuild, smoke, and deploy current main.
acceptance_criteria:
- An unfiltered pull_request docs run cannot cancel or replace a queued/running main push docs deployment.
- Main push deployments remain serialized so Pages publishes one artifact at a time; a newer main docs-triggering push may supersede an older pending main push because it contains that history.
- The fixing change triggers a successful current-main docs build, playground Chromium smoke, and Pages deploy, replacing the stale pre-#6329 live-cell bundle.
- Keep the change to the concurrency key plus a small workflow-shape regression assertion if one fits the existing workflow sanity tests; no new workflow or orchestration layer.
notes:
PR #6374 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6374) opened. Premise confirmed unchanged: docs.yml had one workflow-level group 'pages' / cancel-in-progress: false covering push + unfiltered pull_request + workflow_dispatch. Observed behaviour is CANCELLATION of the older PENDING run (GitHub keeps 1 running + 1 pending per group and drops the older pending one even when cancel-in-progress is false) -- not a queue, not a skip.

Split: push/workflow_dispatch -> 'pages' (cancel-in-progress false, unchanged serialization); pull_request -> 'docs-pr-<number>' (cancel-in-progress true, matching the test.yml idiom).

Newly parallel: PR docs builds only -- against each other and against a main deploy. Two Pages deployments still CANNOT overlap: the deploy job is gated if: github.event_name == 'push', and all pushes remain in the single uncancelled 'pages' group. A PR run's upload-pages-artifact is run-scoped and never consumed by deploy-pages.

Added implementation/scripts/_docs-workflow-policy.test.cjs (5 assertions, mirrors _lint-workflow-policy.test.cjs) wired into test:script-policy; pins the event-scoped group, per-PR key, surviving 'pages' arm, PR-only cancel scope, and the push-only deploy gate (the interlock the split depends on). All 5 mutation-tested. _changed-surfaces.test.cjs pin NOT moved (still 168). rf2-kxork not absorbed.

Third acceptance criterion satisfies on merge: the commit touches .github/workflows/docs.yml which is on docs.yml's own push.paths, so merging triggers the current-main build + Chromium smoke + Pages deploy.

title: Await and surface Promise-backed Story presence-host failures
description: PR #6325 correctly provides the optional presence-host bridge and makes an absent host refuse :cannot-run. The canonical CLJS host, however, returns the Promise from re-frame.ui.test/flush-presence!. re-frame.story.play.presence/advance! invokes the host inside a synchronous try and immediately returns {:status :advanced}; exec-flush-presence! records a successful skip, and the run loop merely yields setTimeout 0. A later Promise rejection (for example React act failure or :rf.error/flush-convergence-exceeded) is outside that try, can become unhandled, and cannot change the already-recorded play result. A presence-bearing play can therefore report pass even though its real host flush failed. Existing tests cover a synchronously throwing host, not a rejecting canonical host. Keep the solution narrow: await/observe the presence host's thenable on CLJS before the next step and project rejection to the existing step-exception/failing run vocabulary, while preserving synchronous JVM/stub behavior. Do not introduce a general async-step framework or another clock. As part of the same correction, remove the adjacent retired no-host-no-op claims still present in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc:65-66 and tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1873; the runtime now refuses when no host is installed.
acceptance_criteria: A resolving canonical presence-host Promise settles before the next script step runs. A rejecting host Promise is observed, produces the existing exception/failure result, and prevents a false :pass; no unhandled rejection remains. The interactive single-step path and auto-run path agree for :flush-presence. JVM and synchronous custom hosts retain their current behavior; an absent host still yields :cannot-run. Focused CLJS tests include resolved and rejected thenable controls plus the existing no-host control. Runner/Spec 017 no longer say an absent presence host advances a no-op. No generic async runner abstraction, new clock, or dependency inversion.

title: Make the delayed-silence receiver decision atomic
description:
PR #6302 / rf2-qg98y documents an "exact" delayed-silence receiver rule as two separate public reads:

    (and (= (:observed-gen tags) (epoch-listener-generation cb-id))
         (not (epoch-listener-observing? cb-id (:frame tags))))

The decision is not linearizable. A same-id replacement/drop can land after the generation read but before the observing read. The first clause has already accepted generation G; the second then evaluates the new/absent registration as not observing and returns true, so the consumer accepts G's signal after G is no longer current. The real public-API sequence on current main printed `{:carried-gen 1, :clause-one-read 1, :current-gen 2, :clause-two-observing false, :two-clause-rule-accepts? true}`.

There is a second split inside `state/live-observer?`: it reads the observation stamp atom and then the listener registry atom without either ledger lock. A re-arm or replacement between those derefs can likewise yield a combination that never existed as one coherent receiver-time state. This predicate is safe inside `eligible-and-reserve!` only because that caller already holds both locks; the new public query calls it unlocked.

Expose one supported, race-coherent decision instead of asking every tool/AI/programmer to compose low-level reads correctly. Recommended pre-alpha shape: one predicate accepting `cb-id`, `frame-id`, and carried `observed-gen`, evaluated under the existing short-lived ledger locks (or one coherent snapshot), and retire the now-misleading two-query recipe/public query if it has no independent use. Do not hold locks across trace delivery or callback code and do not add retry/polling machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- One supported receiver operation decides whether a delayed-silence signal is current from `(cb-id, frame-id, observed-gen)` at a single linearization point.
- A deterministic JVM barrier places replacement, unregister, and same-generation re-arm at every former query/deref seam; no interleaving accepts a signal for a non-current generation or currently observing callback.
- Genuine silence with no superseding mutation is accepted; re-arm on another frame does not suppress this frame; replacement/drop and same-frame re-arm reject.
- Spec 009, Tool-Pair, API/docs, source comments, and examples teach only the coherent operation, not a two-call TOCTOU recipe.
- Prefer one minimal predicate and remove redundant low-level public surface while pre-alpha; no transaction framework, polling/retry loop, held lock across foreign code, or callback serialization.
- Existing reservation/publication deadlock freedom, privacy, generation opacity, and CLJ/CLJS behavior remain intact.

title: Stop accepting map-form scroll strategies as a silent no-op
description:
PR #6307 makes `:rf.nav/scroll` runtime validation explicitly accept any map as a "host-extensible" strategy, matching current Spec 012 prose. The live `scroll-fx-handler` has no extension seam: its default case—including every map—returns nil. The new CLJS test proves this exact behavior: `{:behavior :smooth :block :center}` passes validation, emits no violation, and leaves the window untouched.

This is a programmer-facing false promise. Spec 012 says maps allow host-specific strategies and gives a tangible example such as `{:to :element :selector "#article"}`, yet a conforming value is silently inert. There is no registry, callback, late-bound hook, or documented replacement of `:rf.nav/scroll` that interprets the value. Accepting arbitrary maps also weakens the new schema boundary without buying executable behavior.

Make the v1 contract honest. Recommendation for pre-alpha: remove the unproven map form from the schema/spec/planner contract now and fail malformed/unsupported strategies before effects, because the named registry is already explicitly deferred until a real need appears. If a concrete host strategy is already required, instead add one small explicit host seam and test that it executes; do not build a generalized registry speculatively. Never retain the current validate-then-silently-ignore behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented valid `:rf.nav/scroll` strategy always has executable semantics; no accepted map-form value silently falls into the handler's nil branch.
- Preferred bounded v1 resolution: schemas, Spec 012, API projections, planner validation, tests, and handler docs expose only `:top`, `:restore`, and `:preserve` until a concrete extension need exists.
- If map-form extension is retained, one explicit minimal host seam executes it and absence/malformed extension fails loud before navigation host mutation; no named-strategy registry without a demonstrated need.
- Runtime schema metadata remains truthful on CLJ and CLJS, and all four nav fx still reject malformed args before host mutation while accepting real planner output.
- Tests replace the current "map passes but no-ops" positive control with the chosen causal contract.
- No compatibility alias, general plugin/registry framework, or speculative strategy catalogue.

title: Preserve collision-group declaration order in spawn-all diagnostics
description:
PR #6306 / rf2-ri19s computes `spawn-all-address-collisions` as a deterministic vector of `[resolved-address child-id-vector]` pairs in first-appearance order, exactly so multiple collision groups retain declaration order on CLJ and CLJS. `reject-address-collision!` immediately discards that carrier with `(into {} collisions)` and exposes only the resulting map in the trace tags and reason.

That misses rf2-ri19s's explicit acceptance criterion: "Multiple collision groups retain declaration-order diagnostics on CLJ and CLJS without relying on unordered map presentation." The new adversarial test acknowledges the loss and deliberately asserts group membership only, saying that reading the map seq would rely on unordered presentation. Per-group child ids remain ordered, but ordering among two or more groups is no longer represented by the public diagnostic.

Keep the already-correct structural precheck and its privacy boundary. Carry the existing ordered vector through the diagnostic (for example as an ordered vector of pairs or small named records), and derive any human text from that carrier. Do not add an ordered-map abstraction or change unique-batch lifecycle behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- The duplicate-id diagnostic carries every collision group in first-appearance order on both CLJ and CLJS; consumers/tests do not infer group order from map iteration.
- Each group's logical child ids remain vectors in declaration order.
- The error remains one structural-only, privacy-safe trace emitted before type resolution, snapshot/schema work, or other reject traces.
- Fixed/fixed, fixed/generated, unique-batch, cleanup, and exact-incarnation behavior remain unchanged.
- Focused adversarial tests prove two collision groups in an insertion order that differs from plausible map/hash presentation on both hosts.
- No ordered-map library, general diagnostic carrier framework, or allocator redesign.

title: Runtime spread path can smuggle :dangerouslySetInnerHTML and other rejected prop spellings past the compile-time deny
description:
Found during the rf2-29s75 decision verification (2026-07-18). The compile-time "one spelling, and it is a node variant" rule (Spec 004 ~line 704; rules.cljc rejected-prop-spellings, lines 345-354) is enforced ONLY on literal props (analyze.cljc:1600). The runtime spread converter bypasses it: convert-prop-map! (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/runtime.cljs:408, shared by spread->props:456 and spread-safe->props:481) sends unrecognized names through rules/react-prop-name (rules.cljc:358), which passes them VERBATIM. So a runtime map like {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML #js {:__html s}} (or :inner-html / :dangerously-set-inner-html, or a "children" key) reaches React through (ui/spread m) — raw markup with NO visible (ui/html ...) trust assertion. The spread-safe caller guard does not close it either: spread-safe-denied-structural (rules.cljc:1211-1219) is only #{:key :ref :value :checked}.

PROPOSED FIX: deny the rejected-prop-spellings set (by canonical emitted slot, mirroring the rf2-xdvob slot-canonicalization approach used for the spread-safe deny) at the shared runtime seam convert-prop-map!, which covers both ui/spread and the ui/spread-safe caller path at once; mirror on the JVM runtime spread fold in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tree.cljc (~lines 172-245, the shared rule table). Whether it throws in every build (like assert-safe-caller!) or is a dev-only diagnostic is a design point for the implementer — the every-build spread-safe owned-key deny is the closest precedent, and the trust-boundary nature of innerHTML argues for every-build.

NOT a gate for rf2-29s75: that fix attaches the compiled ui/html prop AFTER spread conversion, so the explicit site wins any collision regardless of this hole.

Spec surface if behavior changes: spec/004-Views.md (ui/spread contract prose) — HOT-ZONE, sequence accordingly. Possibly a new runtime error id (Spec 009 catalogue row) if the deny throws.

title: fingerprint.cljc -write leads with map? — records digest identically despite claiming TYPE-PRESERVING
description:
FOUND by rf2-5h9td (#6318) while fixing the same defect in Xray. NOT touched there: outside its fence, and rf2-74vlo was live in implementation/ui at the time (74vlo has since merged, so this is now dispatchable).

THE BUG: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/fingerprint.cljc:136 — its -write implementation matches (map? x) FIRST. CLJS records satisfy map?, so the record tag is discarded: two records differing ONLY by type digest identically, and a record digests the same as a plain map with the same entries. The namespace docstring claims TYPE-PRESERVING, so the code contradicts its own stated contract.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE XRAY ONE (5h9td's assessment, which I share): fingerprint feeds config-fingerprint / build-digest plan-conflict detection. A false digest MATCH there reads as 'nothing changed' — i.e. a genuine plan conflict is silently treated as an idempotent no-op. Silent wrong-answer in the build system, not a display glitch.

THE FIX (mirror #6318 exactly — it is already proven): match (record? x) BEFORE (map? x) and tag the record. Factor entry rendering so a record's extension entries stay order-canonical like a plain map's (#6318 introduced canonical-entries for precisely this).

⚠️ CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION FACT established by #6318 — do NOT rediscover it the hard way: cljs.core/type->str is WRONG for records. It reads cljs, which deftype* sets but defrecord* does NOT, so it silently degrades to the constructor's JS source text. Verified against the ClojureScript 1.12.145 jar (cljs/core.cljc emit-deftype* vs emit-defrecord; cljs/compiler.cljc emit* :defrecord). defrecord sets cljs to a compile-time literal instead, so (pr-str (type x)) is the stable, :advanced-safe source. Also do NOT use (.-name (type v)) — munged under :advanced (the edn_inspector uses it for DISPLAY only, which is fine there).

TESTS TO MIRROR from #6318: two records differing only by type must digest differently; a record must digest differently from a plain map with identical entries; extension-map insertion order must NOT affect the digest ((assoc (->RecA 1) :b 2 :c 3) vs :c 3 :b 2); type preservation AT DEPTH ({:k (->RecA 1)} vs {:k {:x 1}}). Red-before is essential — reverting the fix must redden.

Surface: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/fingerprint.cljc + its tests. NOTE implementation/ui is NOT a baked playground input, so no bundle rebuild. Gate: implementation/ui JVM FROM THE ARTEFACT DIR (a bare 'clojure -M:test -n <ns>' from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and reads as green) + npm run test:cljs, both with non-zero counts. Also check whether any digest-conflict test currently passes only because of this collapse — if one does, that is a second false-green worth reporting.

title: Make Story presence playback installable and fail closed without its host hook
description:
PR #6295 adds [:flush-presence] through a late-bound :flush-presence! hook, but no production namespace in the repository installs that hook. The only calls to install-presence-flush! are tests and documentation examples. Story's published artefact intentionally has no day8/re-frame2-ui dependency, so merely loading or mounting the current Story shell cannot make the step reach re-frame.ui.test/flush-presence!.

The missing-hook behavior also false-greens. presence/advance! returns {:status :no-host}; exec-flush-presence! maps every non-error result to a skipped step; requirements assigns the step no capability. The justification says “the DOM assertion that follows” will refuse on an incapable runner, but the grammar neither requires a following assertion nor requires it to be :assert-dom—:assert-db and no assertion at all are legal. More fundamentally, “no hook installed” does not prove “no presence runtime exists”: an app can load re-frame.ui and simply omit the manual bridge call. Its presence-bearing playback then silently fails to advance the clock while Story reports no cannot-run condition.

Provide one canonical low-friction integration path when Story and re-frame.ui are both present (for example a small optional host bridge installed by the Story UI shell), and make a requested [:flush-presence] refuse with :cannot-run when its required hook is absent rather than silently skip. Keep Story clock-free and preserve the late-bound dependency direction; no general virtual-clock layer is needed. Pin tests for the uninstalled-hook refusal, the real shell/bridge installation, and a script whose only following assertion is :assert-db so the current false premise cannot return.

title: RULING: stop committing docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js — build the SCI bundle in CI
description:
ESCALATED WITH EVIDENCE (mayor, 2026-07-18). Previously surfaced as 'option (c)' and downgraded by the mayor to a velocity tax. That was WRONG — it is now demonstrably BLOCKING.

HARD EVIDENCE FROM TODAY: docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js was rewritten SEVEN times on main in ~6 hours. rf2-qg98y (#6302, a finished P2 correctness fix — the delayed-epoch-silence receipt-time rule) has burned FOUR full rebase cycles and still cannot land: it touches core_epoch.cljc (a baked input), so it must regenerate the bundle; each rebase restarts CI; during that window another baked-input PR merges and regenerates the bundle again, re-conflicting it. It is a losing race by construction, not a fault in the work.

THE MECHANISM: any PR touching implementation/{core,machines,flows,adapters/reagent-slim}/src must rebuild the committed bundle. Two such PRs ALWAYS conflict on that generated file. The freshness gate reads the bundle at HEAD, so the rebuild must be committed. Under concurrent dispatch this serialises every core-touching PR behind every other one.

WORKERS ARE ALREADY ROUTING AROUND IT: rf2-3neiv explicitly scoped core-src comment edits OUT of its PR to avoid triggering a rebuild, and filed rf2-qowmk to amortise them later. That is the tax distorting engineering decisions.

THE ASK (operator ruling): stop committing docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js; generate it in CI (and/or on docs deploy) and gitignore it. The freshness gate then compares generated-vs-inputs within a single CI run instead of against a committed artefact, and the conflict class disappears entirely.

ALTERNATIVES IF (c) IS REJECTED: (a) keep committing it but serialise all baked-input PRs (kills concurrency — currently ~6 workers); (b) merge-driver / .gitattributes union or ours-strategy on that path so rebases stop conflicting (smaller change, keeps the artefact committed, but the digest still has to be regenerated after every merge, so freshness would still flap); (d) status quo — accept 4+ rebase cycles per core PR.

MAYOR RECOMMENDATION: (c). It removes a whole class of merge conflict, stops distorting worker scoping decisions, and the bundle is a build product, not source. Related: rf2-nyjml (close playground freshness over its real inputs), rf2-ht4om (rebuild the stale bundle), rf2-i3e3q (the honest freshness gate that established the current design).
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:11 AUSEST)

RULING — Option C, with the smoke-on-deploy amendment. docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js is a generated test/deploy artifact, not source. Remove it from git and generate it at each consumption boundary (PR CI job, docs deploy). Do NOT serialize baked-input PRs (Option B), do NOT add a merge driver (Option D: union can concatenate two programs into broken JS, ours yields a digest-stale artifact, and custom drivers are per-checkout config that GitHub's server-side merge never runs), do NOT add a commit-back bot. docs/cljs/playground.js + playground.css keep their existing committed byte-deterministic policy — this ruling covers ONLY playground-rf2.js.

RATIONALE: the committed snapshot manufactured a write lock across implementation/{core,adapters/reagent-slim,machines,flows}: nine complete rewrites of the file on main in seven hours on 2026-07-18 (~41k changed lines on this one generated path), five rebase cycles to land #6302, workers scoping core comment fixes out of PRs to dodge the rebuild (rf2-qowmk exists solely to amortize one), and the mayor reduced to serializing finished correctness fixes. Deployment never consumed the committed copy — docs.yml has rebuilt the bundle fresh on every publish since rf2-ssxvg1. The snapshot's only genuine consumer was clean-checkout local convenience, which one explicit `npm run build` in docs/tools/playground replaces. Source/config/locks become the single authority; the conflict class disappears rather than being coordinated around.

AMENDMENT (supersedes the retired dossier's transition step 7 — do not follow that step as written): the post-merge canary is NOT redundant today. PRs merge via rebase (PR CI validated the pre-rebase tree, not the tree landing on main), docs.yml's deploy verification is only a non-empty + rf2sci grep, and expensive-tests.yml runs no playground job at all (all verified against the workflows 2026-07-18). Therefore the Chromium smoke must ride the deploy path: docs.yml's build job runs `npm run smoke` after the bundle rebuild, scoped to non-PR events, so the artifact that ships is the artifact that was smoked. Only with that in place is retiring the post-merge canary safe — its one surviving invariant (merged-tree runtime composition) then lives at the exact consumption boundary, and main-push CI drops from two heavy bundle builds to one.

TRANSITION PLAN — one atomic cutover PR. HOT-ZONE: it edits .github/workflows/test.yml and .github/workflows/docs.yml and deletes .github/workflows/post-merge-playground-freshness.yml — mayor must sequence it; no parallel workflow-touching PR while it is open.

1. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh — arm playground=true directly for implementation/core/*, implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/*, and implementation/flows/* (implementation/machines/* already fires, ~line 468), plus scripts/playground-sci-input-digest.mjs (copy-bundle.mjs is already covered under docs/tools/playground/*). Drop docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js from the case arm (~line 1016) — the path will no longer appear in diffs.
2. .github/workflows/test.yml tools-playground job — KEEP: fresh build, `npm run smoke` against the fresh output, and the committed-esbuild byte-diff for playground.js/.css (those stay tracked). RETARGET the "Verify committed SCI bundle is a valid re-frame2 prebuilt" step (~line 4310) at the freshly generated output — same non-empty / shadow$provide / rf2sci / 200KB-floor checks, errors reworded from "rebuild + recommit" to "the build emitted a wrong/truncated artifact". DELETE the check-playground-sci-freshness.sh step (~line 4347) — it reads the bundle from HEAD and fails by construction once the file is untracked.
3. .github/workflows/docs.yml — (a) extend push.paths with implementation/core/**, implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**, implementation/machines/**, implementation/flows/** (docs/tools/playground/** is already inside docs/**); LEAVE the PR-side detect classifier unchanged (docs surface only) so a core-only PR does not run a duplicate MkDocs build — PR-time playground coverage lives in tools-playground. (b) after "Rebuild playground bundles fresh from main": install Playwright Chromium and run `npm run smoke` in docs/tools/playground, gated `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`; keep the existing non-empty/rf2sci grep as the fast pre-check. (c) recommended one-liner, same non-PR scope: `git diff --exit-code -- docs/cljs/playground.js docs/cljs/playground.css` after the rebuild, preserving the canary's stale-committed-bootstrap detection on the post-rebase tree.
4. DELETE .github/workflows/post-merge-playground-freshness.yml in the same PR — both of its invariants now live at 3b (runtime composition on the merged tree) and 2/3c (esbuild drift).
5. Untrack + ignore: `git rm --cached docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`; add the EXACT line `/docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js` to .gitignore (never a broad docs/cljs/* rule — the bootstrap js/css stay tracked); remove the `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js text eol=lf` line from .gitattributes (line 17). Do NOT rewrite history to purge old blobs — it would invalidate every open PR for a ~15 MB packed saving; growth simply stops.
6. Retire scripts/check-playground-sci-freshness.sh and scripts/check-playground-sci-freshness.selftest.sh (both exist only to compare a committed snapshot with HEAD). KEEP the digest stamping in scripts/playground-sci-input-digest.mjs + docs/tools/playground/sci/scripts/copy-bundle.mjs as non-authoritative provenance inside the generated file. Sweep remaining references to the retired checker and to "committed/vendored" bundle language: docs/tools/playground/README.md, docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs (error text), TESTING.md, workflow comments, package descriptions.
7. Local contract (document in the playground README): `mkdocs build` alone builds static docs; live `cljs-rf2` cells require `npm run build` (or build:rf2) in docs/tools/playground first; keep the smoke's actionable "bundle not found — run build" error. Existing checkouts: pulling the cutover commit deletes the formerly tracked file; the next playground build recreates it as ignored output.
8. Verify: (i) classifier fixtures for core-only, flows-only, and sci-config-only diffs each set playground=true with no bundle diff present; (ii) a docs.yml build (workflow_dispatch or push simulation) produces site/cljs/playground-rf2.js and the Chromium smoke passes against the generated file; (iii) two disjoint baked-input branches rebase-merge with no conflict on the generated path.

FALLOUT (enumerated for the mayor — not closed here, lifecycle is the mayor's):
- rf2-ht4om (P1, rebuild the stale bundle): MOOT — the committed-snapshot invariant it enforces is retired by this ruling; no rebuild-and-commit is ever owed again.
- rf2-5qka5 (P3, canonical digest marker): MOOT — the committed-marker verifier dies with the committed artifact; the surviving stamp is non-authoritative provenance needing no verifier.
- rf2-nyjml (P2, close freshness over real inputs): FOLDS INTO the cutover — its trigger-enumeration findings (flows omitted from post-merge paths; copy-bundle/digest scripts not digest inputs; classifier arms only machines) are exactly steps 1 and 3a above; its committed-digest acceptance criteria are void.
- rf2-qowmk (P3, core comment reconciliation): UNBLOCKS — comment-only core edits no longer owe a bundle rebuild; strike its final acceptance criterion (rebuild bundle + pass check-playground-sci-freshness.sh).

CORRECTIONS to this bead's description (stale mid-race claims; do not re-litigate): rf2-qg98y (#6302) DID merge at 17:06 AUSEST after five rebase cycles — "still cannot land" was true only while the race ran, and the recovery does not refute the mechanism (the project had to serialize baked-input PRs to land it); the final count is nine bundle rewrites on main in seven hours (through 61ca27f at 16:57), not seven in six; alternative (b) merge-driver is refuted outright, not merely inferior (see RULING).

The decision dossier ai/decisions/rf2-tzy13.playground-bundle-version-control.md is retired (deleted) per Mike's delegation; this note is the durable, self-contained record.

title: Reconcile clear-http-interceptor's canonical API error rule
description:
PR #6278 correctly repairs the dedicated HTTP API page, but the canonical API catalogue still carries the retired error rule. `spec/API.md`'s `clear-http-interceptor` row (mirrored at `docs/spec/API.md`) says: "Either raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` when the frame is absent."

That is false for the explicit form in two ways:
- malformed or nil explicit opts (`{:frame nil}`, `{}`, typo/extra keys, non-map) raise `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` before frame resolution, not `:rf.error/no-frame-context`;

Only the single-arity form under no carried scope raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`. The two-arity contract is exact validation plus explicit targeting. The dedicated page, Spec 014, core/API docs, facade and implementation docstrings, and runtime tests already agree; this canonical catalogue row and its docs mirror are the remaining contradiction. Make the one row state the same narrow distinction. Preserve the current runtime and generated/hand-authored ownership model; no API sweep framework or compatibility behavior.

title: Give :rf.editor/open one truthful owner and load-order-independent contract
description:
PR #6246 made `spec/Conventions.md` authoritative that `:rf.editor/open` is a cross-tool effect which Story and Xray register idempotently: whichever loads first wins and the handlers are identical. The shipped implementation contradicts every load-bearing part of that claim. `re-frame.registrar/register!` is atomic replacement/last-writer-wins (`swap! ... assoc-in`), Xray calls its installer in production, and Story's production installer roster/shell never calls its open-in-editor `install!` (the sole call is in its test). If Story is wired, the two handlers are not interchangeable: they close over different Story/Xray editor, project-root, navigator, and Xray operator-override state. The later install therefore commandeers the shared global id for both tools, and cross-source duplicate provenance can also surface as a registration/image collision.

This is a pre-alpha contract correction, not a request for a registry framework. Give the effect one honest owner and one production registration, or use distinct tool-owned effects and retract the cross-tool reservation. The lowest-friction acceptable shape preserves each tool's configuration explicitly and makes load order irrelevant. Do not add aliases or compatibility machinery.

Evidence: Conventions.md:87; implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:538-586; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:961 and open_in_editor.cljs:399-403; tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs:390-460; tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc:130-148; the only Story installer call is tools/story/test/re_frame/story_open_in_editor_cljs_test.cljs:573. Three independent PR-audit lenses reproduced/reconfirmed the mismatch. No all-state owner exists; closed rf2-tr4uqq is the source decision and cannot absorb new work.
acceptance_criteria:
- `:rf.editor/open` has exactly one authoritative registration owner and implementation, OR Story/Xray use distinct tool-owned effect ids and the `:rf.editor/*` reservation is removed/recast.
- Story's documented dispatch-based open-in-editor path is actually installed in production if it remains public.
- Co-loading Story and Xray in either order produces no cross-source registration collision or last-writer policy takeover.
- Each tool's open action honors the originating tool's editor, project-root, endpoint fallback, navigator, and any tool-specific override/hint policy; configuration ownership is explicit rather than inferred from load order.
- `spec/Conventions.md` and both tool docstrings state the shipped registration semantics truthfully; no “first wins”, “identical”, or “idempotent double-registration” claim remains unless causally true.
- An integration test loads both tools in both orders with deliberately different configs and proves the selected editor/path is correct; a production-wiring test proves Story's public event exists if retained.
- No new registry policy/framework, compatibility aliases, or dual-read period is introduced.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:06 AUSEST)

RULING — Option A: open-in-editor effects are tool-owned. Retire `:rf.editor/open` and remove the `:rf.editor/*` cross-tool reservation entirely.

THIS DELIBERATELY REVERSES rf2-tr4uqq DISPOSITION 1 (the `:rf.editor/*` reservation shipped in PR #6246, merged 2026-07-18). That disposition's stated premise — "Story and Xray register identical handlers idempotently; whichever loads first wins; double-registration is free" — is refuted by the shipped code on every point: `re-frame.registrar/register!` is last-writer-wins (`swap! reg assoc-in`, implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc ~:586), the two fx bodies close over different tool config (Story's editor/project-root/static-export root guard vs Xray's three-tier editor resolution with per-operator Settings override, own root, and `editor-configured?` hint gate), separate navigator atoms, separate log identities — and Story's installer is never called in any production boot anyway (sole caller: its own test). A ruling built on a refuted premise carries no precedential weight; pre-alpha, the honest move is deletion, not preserving a day-old reservation for consistency. The reversal is attributed here so it stays discoverable; cross-reference rf2-tr4uqq.

DECISION DETAIL (self-contained; the ai/decisions dossier is retired/deleted — this block is the durable record):

1. Public API unchanged: `:rf.story/open-in-editor` and `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` remain the two ergonomic public events. Programmers/agents never see the fx ids.
2. Each event lowers to a new tool-owned effect: `:rf.story.fx/open-in-editor` and `:rf.xray.fx/open-in-editor`. Delete both `:rf.editor/open` registrations. NO alias, forwarding shim, dual-read period, `:tool` routing switch, registry ownership framework, or merged global editor config (dossier Options B/C/D all rejected).
3. Each effect uses its originating tool's editor, project-root, endpoint fallback, and navigator. Xray keeps its host/operator override and unconfigured-editor Settings hint — that policy stays in Xray's EVENT, not the effect.
4. Wire Story's open-in-editor `install!` into the canonical CLJS production installer roster (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc ~:130-148 — currently absent, so the documented `[:rf.story/open-in-editor coord]` dispatch has NO production handler today; the direct chip/imperative paths are why nobody noticed).
5. Rationale: `:rf.editor/open` was Xray's ONLY fx registered outside `:rf.xray.fx/*`/`:rf.xray.*` and Story's only reg-fx at all — Option A deletes the sole deviation from an established pattern, not introduces one. Co-loading is the FLAGSHIP topology (Story mounts Xray as its embed, story.cljc ~:892 + xray_preset.cljc), so load-order-dependent policy takeover is not an edge case. Shared machinery that deserves sharing (URI build, denylist, dev-server-first endpoint fallback) already lives in core `re-frame.source-coords.editor-uri` / `re-frame.source-coords.open-endpoint` and stays shared.
6. Future: a neutral core `:rf.editor/open` may only return via a separately ruled explicit launch-request payload (resolved editor + project-root IN the effect args; owner never discovered from load order) AND a demonstrated real third consumer. Do not build it now. (Verified: spec/Tool-Pair.md never names the fx-id; pair-mcp/story-mcp/machines-viz contain zero references.)

IMPLEMENTATION FILES:

SPEC SURFACES:

Use each tool's navigator seam plus the existing endpoint-launcher seam to force the URI fallback synchronously; do NOT stub via `:fx-overrides` (masks the ownership under test).

`node --require scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs scripts/check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs`
`node -r scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs scripts/check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs`

In both commands the checker is only a preload operand. Its `require.main === module` guard deliberately prevents `main()`, so no bundle work runs; the second script is the actual executable. This recreates the exact inert/argument-only false-green rf2-kfn9q was meant to close. The validator also uses `existsSync` despite the source AC requiring a regular checker file.

Keep the repo grammar deliberately small. Prefer requiring the current exact direct form `node <checker-path> ...` (the checker is the actual script operand immediately after `node`), and reject pre-script option operands unless a future real command requires a narrowly specified Node-option parser. Verify a regular file, not mere path existence. Do not add a shell parser or execute checkers during descriptor validation.

- Direct `node scripts/<checker>` remains accepted.
- `--require`/`-r` preload operands, other option-argument positions, later ordinary arguments, echo/comment/substrings, and unreachable false-and mentions cannot satisfy executable binding.
- A non-regular checker path cannot satisfy the descriptor.
- All current dedicated commands and real gates remain green; focused mutations restore each false form and fail.
- The implementation remains a bounded token check, not a general shell/Node command parser.

The descriptor loads the legitimate module under `scripts/`, while the package command can execute a different same-basename file. Fix should compare the normalized repository-relative script operand to the exact `scripts/<checker>` path (and retain Windows/Posix separator support), not basename alone.

title: Reject duplicate ownership identities inside ui/presence
description:
Presence treats each React key as one retained ownership identity, but it never validates uniqueness across the boundary's flattened incoming children. The compiler accepts `(presence {:timeout-ms 300} [card {:key "x"}] [card {:key "x"}])`; the pure runtime probe `reconcile [] ["x" "x"]` returns two `{:key "x" :phase :mounting}` entries, while the element and timer maps collapse them to one key. Render then duplicates the last element under duplicate Provider keys, and one exit timer removes every entry sharing that identity.

Existing keyed-`for` rows have their own list-site dev duplicate check, but explicit siblings, separate nested arrays, and dynamic keys can still alias at the Presence boundary. Add one small Presence-local uniqueness check over the already-flattened React keys, in the same string-coercion domain used for ownership. Fail loudly with the existing duplicate-key diagnostic where it fits (or one narrowly catalogued Presence diagnostic if necessary), and pin both literal and dynamic/multi-array collisions plus the unique control. Do not add a key registry or cross-boundary coordinator.
acceptance_criteria: A Presence boundary never reconciles/render-retains two children under one key; duplicate explicit and flattened dynamic identities produce a useful dev/build diagnostic before phase/timer ownership diverges; distinct keys retain current behavior; mutation removing the check fails focused tests.

title: Finish frame-target authority after exact-value teardown docs pass
description:
PR #6240 improved the frame value/ID contract and the later facade-only proof is now shipped and green, but active source/spec/API authorities still contradict the runtime model programmers and coding agents must follow.

Examples: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` says frames are not values and users hold keywords, then says value and ID targets are interchangeable everywhere (incorrect for destroy); `spec/002-Frames.md` still says a frame value is not an app-facing operation target and uses bidirectional `value↔id` shorthand; provider sections describe any non-keyword as invalid; `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` says `frame-provider :frame` must be a keyword. Runtime accepts either a keyword or live frame value for ordinary targets, normalizes a value one-way to its ID, and gives `destroy-frame!` its deliberate exception: returned values are exact-incarnation authority while keywords/tokenless values are address-directed.

Reconcile these already-named authorities without changing runtime or adding an accessor. This is a compact public-model repair: direct values should be ergonomic and safe for programmers and their AI tools, while the teardown distinction remains explicit.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reconcile the frame namespace overview, Spec 002 overview/resolved/provider/index wording, Conventions frame vocabulary/index wording, and generated/core API prose with the shipped target grammar.
- State the ordinary rule plainly: public operations accept a frame ID keyword or live frame value directly; implementation privately normalizes a value one-way to its logical ID; there is no public value-to-ID accessor.
- State the sole lifecycle exception plainly: one-argument `destroy-frame!` consumes a returned value as exact-incarnation authority, while a keyword or tokenless derived value is address-directed.
- Correct provider validation prose to reject targets that are neither a keyword nor a valid live frame value; do not claim every non-keyword is invalid.
- Remove misleading `value↔id`, “interchangeably everywhere,” “frames are not values,” and “not an app-facing operation target” claims where they govern the public target contract, while preserving the distinction between a frame value and its serializable routing address.

title: Make delayed epoch silence coherent with same-generation re-arm
description: PR #6235 / closed rf2-4go8s promotes the claim that :observed-gen makes every reservation-to-publication mutation race-coherent, including record-observation! re-arm. The event still carries that same generation, so the documented public filter (:observed-gen == epoch-listener-generation cb-id) accepts a silenced signal even though the callback is live again. The existing parked-publication test re-arms a different "other" callback, proving lock release but not subject-signal coherence.

title: Fix clear-http-interceptor contract on the dedicated HTTP API page
description:
PR #6257 reconciled Spec 014 and the migration guide to the exact fail-closed `clear-http-interceptor` facade, but the dedicated programmer-facing HTTP API page remains on the retired contract.

Current `docs/api/re-frame.http.md` under `### clear-http-interceptor` says:
- `{:frame nil}` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`; and
- the public 2-arity is "shape-discriminated", with a bare frame target in first position treated as internal frame-first `(frame id)` plumbing.

The shipped facade is deliberately different (rf2-s32bf / #6247): the only public two-arity is `(clear-http-interceptor id {:frame target})`, and the opts map must be exactly one `:frame` entry with a present non-nil target. `{}`, `{:frame nil}`, typo/extra keys, and non-map second args raise `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` before ambient scope resolution. The frame-first `clear-http-interceptor*` helper is a separate artefact-internal var, not a shape-discriminated arm of the public fn.

This leaves the feature's primary API page contradicting current Spec 014, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`, facade/home docstrings, runtime tests, and the just-merged correction. A programmer following it gets a fail-loud surprise and the wrong error/recovery model. All-state searches found closed rf2-hf4ts (fixed only the core API page), closed rf2-s32bf (runtime boundary), and closed rf2-i5t3h (#6257's two named docs), but no current owner for this exact residual.
design: Edit only the `clear-http-interceptor` entry in `docs/api/re-frame.http.md`: state the two exact public shapes, the fail-closed invalid-opts cases and `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor`, and that frame-first is a separately named internal helper rather than public overload discrimination. Keep the one-arity no-scope `:rf.error/no-frame-context` behavior. No runtime change, compatibility prose, generated-doc framework, or broad API sweep.
acceptance_criteria:
- The dedicated HTTP API page exposes only `(clear-http-interceptor id)` and `(clear-http-interceptor id {:frame target})` as public call shapes.
- It distinguishes single-arity no-scope `:rf.error/no-frame-context` from invalid explicit opts `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` before ambient state is touched.
- Empty, nil-frame, typo/extra-key, and non-map opts are described as invalid; no text calls the public fn shape-discriminated with a frame-first arm.
- `docs/api/re-frame.http.md`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`, Spec 014, migration guidance, and live docstrings agree; focused docs/link/projection gates pass.
- Documentation-only; no compatibility layer, public alias, or new validation mechanism.

title: Do not report a live capture target destroyed when only the event owner dies
description:
PR #6254 / rf2-a2x2w made a falsey `enqueued?` / `drained?` result trigger one captured-operation `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`, intending to cover loss of the captured target A after its token comparison. The falsey result is not target-specific. Both dispatch paths use `target-live? = owner-live? AND target-incarnation-live?`; `emit-dispatched-trace!` and the enqueue/drain guards can therefore stop because the ORIGINATING event owner died while the captured target is still live. The new tail nevertheless emits `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` naming the live target frame.

Current code:
- `router.cljc:3913-3915` / `4030-4032` conflate owner continuation and target liveness in one predicate.
- async `:3984-3987` emits whenever `capture-op` and `not enqueued?`.
- sync `:4197-4200` emits whenever `capture-op` and `not drained?`.
Neither tail distinguishes owner-cutoff from target-incarnation loss.

Deterministic current-main probes bound a genuine exact owner token for `:audit/owner`, captured `:audit/target`, and interposed at `emit-dispatched-trace!` to destroy only the owner and return false (the exact production outcome when continuation dies during that callback-bearing seam). Results:

async:
`{:target-live? true, :target-touched? nil, :owner-live? false, :errors [{:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed, :frame :audit/target, :event-id :audit/touch, :op :dispatch}]}`

sync:
`{:target-live? true, :target-touched? nil, :owner-live? false, :errors [{:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed, :frame :audit/target, :event-id :audit/touch, :op :dispatch-sync}]}`

Dropping the operation after its owner dies is correct and keeps the target untouched. Shipping a production-survivable record that says the live target was destroyed is not: off-box diagnostics point at the wrong frame/lifecycle failure. The existing #6254 tests interpose only target A→B replacement and cannot expose this second reason for the same boolean result. All-state searches found only closed historical false-frame-destroyed owners (for other surfaces) and the closed exact-target work; no current Bead owns this owner-vs-target conflation.
design: Keep the existing exact-target machinery. At the post-trace/enqueue and post-drain decision, preserve owner-continuation cutoff as the higher-priority silent outcome and emit only when the captured target incarnation itself is no longer live. A small final pair of explicit owner/target checks is preferable to inventing a general outcome protocol; use a tiny tri-state result only if it makes the already-callback-bearing seam substantially clearer. Do not change queue/drain locking, public error vocabulary, capture tokens, or ordinary address-directed behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic async and dispatch-sync tests make the exact originating event owner die after the captured target token comparison while the target remains live. The operation is not enqueued/processed and no `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` is emitted for the live target.
- The existing target-loss interleavings still emit exactly one realm-exact `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` for dispatch and dispatch-sync and never touch a successor.
- If owner and target validity move at adjacent callback boundaries, the decision is explicitly ordered: owner-continuation cutoff cannot be misreported as target destruction or retarget work.
- Ordinary address-directed dispatch behavior and captured subscribe behavior remain unchanged.
- Focused capture/router/on-error JVM and CLJS gates pass; no new public slot, lock, scheduler, or general provenance/outcome framework is added.

title: Clarify that late-bind hook keys may appear as opaque diagnostic facts
description: PR #6229 added a normative rule saying late-bind hook keys must not appear as identifiers on runtime data surfaces, explicitly including trace values and error ex-data. That is broader than the established contract: frame teardown, epoch restore/quiesce, and SSR cleanup intentionally publish the failing hook address in :hook / :hook-failures diagnostics. Those values identify the programmer-supplied DI seam that failed; they do not turn the directory key into application, domain, protocol, or runtime-state vocabulary. Treat this as a wording-boundary defect, not an invitation to rename stable payloads or invent a second taxonomy.
acceptance_criteria: Conventions prohibits late-bind directory keys from becoming application/domain/protocol/runtime-state vocabulary while explicitly permitting an opaque hook address in diagnostic correlation about the failing DI seam; the convention is reconciled with existing Spec 009/API teardown and restore diagnostics, including :hook and :hook-failures; existing registry lookups, the 216-key grammar, payload keys/values, event categories, cardinality, recovery behavior, and exception shapes remain unchanged; focused authority assertions prevent the prose boundary from again outlawing intentional diagnostics; no keyword migration, alias, compatibility layer, runtime guard, or new taxonomy is added.

title: Make the hooks adapter recipe single and causally guarded
description:
PR #6225 corrected the paragraph immediately below the per-adapter table, but the table still gives the opposite copyable rule. In `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md`, the UIx and Helix rows classify an ordinary view as `reg-view*` on `defui`/`defnc`; the next paragraph correctly says an ordinary hooks component uses `defui`/`defnc` + `use-subscribe` + `use-frame`, with `reg-view*` optional only for registry-keyed addressing. A programmer or model following the table therefore gets unnecessary registration and two adjacent authoritative recipes disagree.

Rule 6 remains green because its coherence floor anchors only `patterns/stateful-components.md` and `references/fundamentals/frames.md`, while its residue classifier intentionally accepts every `reg-view*` mention. Its physical-line/sentence-global predicates also miss wrapped and clause-local contradictions and can reject legitimate warnings. Exact probes on #6225 accept a wrapped `register ... via` / next-line `reg-view`, accept `Reagent has a :contextType; UIx gets a :contextType.`, accept `UIx has no :contextType; Helix gets a :contextType.`, and call `An ordinary UIx defui cannot use use-subscribe or use-frame.` coherent; they reject the legitimate `On UIx, do not use Reagent's reg-view; use use-subscribe and use-frame instead.` The separately repaired setup warning and Spec 006 recipe are not coherence anchors. Current corpus and self-tests pass despite the live table contradiction and these false classifications.
design: Make the table state the actual ordinary hooks lane directly, then guard the few canonical recipe blocks #6225 repaired. Normalize only those bounded blocks and use clause-local/fixed relationship predicates plus replacement mutations of the real text. Treat `reg-view*` as lawful only when explicitly optional registry addressing, not as ordinary frame/subscription wiring. Do not build a prose parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- The per-adapter table teaches ordinary UIx/Helix `defui`/`defnc` components using adapter `use-subscribe` and `use-frame`; it does not present `reg-view*` as required ordinary registration.
- `reg-view*` remains accurately documented as optional registry-keyed addressing, never as the source of hook frame wiring.
- The bounded guard anchors the exact views table/recipe plus the setup `first-counter.md` warning and repaired Spec 006 hooks paragraph, alongside the existing two leaves.
- Relationship checks work across normal Markdown wrapping and are clause-local: mixed Reagent/hooks comparisons and scoped negations cannot mask a contradictory hooks clause.
- A merely co-located or negated `defui` + `use-subscribe` + `use-frame` token set is not accepted as a coherent recipe.
- Real-block replacement mutations for required `reg-view*`, wrapped bare capture, semantic reversal, and `:contextType` attribution go red; legitimate optional addressing, Reagent comparisons, and warnings to avoid Reagent `reg-view` stay green.
- Existing skill drift/setup guards and self-tests pass. No general Markdown parser, adapter abstraction, runtime/API change, or compatibility machinery.

title: Close Playground SCI freshness over its real inputs and firing surfaces
description: PR #6219 makes the digest calculation honest when invoked, but the authority and its firing surfaces are not closed over the real artifact pipeline. The final bundle is post-processed by sci/scripts/copy-bundle.mjs and stamped by playground-sci-input-digest.mjs, yet those implementations are not digest inputs. PR classification arms the heavy playground job only for Machines, not Core, reagent-slim, or Flows; the post-merge workflow also omits Flows and the root digest/checker scripts. Consequently a build/postprocess change can keep an old artifact green, and ordinary baked-input changes can merge without the cheap committed-artifact proof. The current stale bundle incident is separately owned by rf2-ht4om; this issue owns prevention, not another rebuild.
acceptance_criteria:
- One bounded authority enumerates every content/build/postprocess input that can change docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js, including copy-bundle and the digest algorithm itself; changing any one requires a refreshed marker.
- Every baked source class (Core, reagent-slim, Machines, Flows) plus digest/checker/copy authority changes select a cheap PR-time committed-digest check; they do not force JVM+Playwright onto every Core PR.
- Post-merge path filters cover Flows and the digest/checker/copy authorities as well as the existing inputs.
- Table-driven changed-surface/path-filter mutations prove every class selects the check, and a behavior-changing copy/digest mutation without rebuild goes red.
- Preserve the current normal build, fresh-build smoke, and cross-host digest; no general build graph, attestation framework, or heavy low-friction regression.
notes:
⚠️ NOT STALE — I suspected it was and checked before closing. Recording so nobody re-suspects it.

rf2-tzy13 removed the COMMITTED BUNDLE docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js and the old verifier scripts/check-playground-sci-freshness.sh, plus .github/workflows/post-merge-playground-freshness.yml. It did NOT remove the playground: 91 tracked files still reference it, including docs/cljs/playground.js, docs/tools/playground/*, README.md, TESTING.md, docs.yml and test.yml.

THE LIVE MECHANISM THIS BEAD IS ABOUT: scripts/playground-sci-input-digest.mjs exists and is the replacement verifier — its own header says "The former verifier, scripts/check-playground-sci-freshness.sh, was ...". It exports computeInputDigest and ROSTER, and already carries an anti-vacuity guard ("roster matched no tracked files — the input paths drifted. Update ROSTER"). .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:1030,1041 wires it into the changed-surfaces arm.

⚠️ SEQUENCING AT DISPATCH: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and .github/workflows/* are touched by rf2-kxork (#6408, arming — it added a cljs-ui-facade-isolation job and moved the changed-surfaces pin 168 -> 172). Verify free before editing, and remember LIVE WORKERS HAVE NO PR YET so `gh pr list` alone is insufficient — scan every sibling worktree for dirty AND committed edits against its own merge-base.
⚠️ RELATED GAP filed on rf2-r4q98: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh is NOT SHELLCHECKED BY CI AT ALL (portability.yml covers only the two scripts/ gate scripts), despite CI executing it. If this bead touches that file, consider whether the shellcheck extension belongs in the same PR.
⚠️ THE ROSTER IS THE HAZARD: a hardcoded input roster that silently matches nothing is the exact false-green class this session kept finding. The existing guard makes an EMPTY roster fail — preserve that, and prefer deriving the roster (rf2-vxgfnd.167 replaced a hardcoded io/resource path with a git ls-files derivation and it immediately surfaced 16 offending lines nobody had listed).
PR #6411 (worker/playground-freshness-nyjml).

RECONCILED AGAINST rf2-tzy13 — several bead claims no longer describe reality:
- 'refreshed marker' / 'cheap PR-time committed-digest check' have NO REFERENT. The bundle is untracked+gitignored, generated at each consumption boundary. Digest is provenance, not gating.
- 'post-merge path filters cover Flows' — post-merge-playground-freshness.yml was DELETED by tzy13. No post-merge arm exists to extend.

Renaming implementation/flows/src left 140 of 144 files -> guard SILENT while a whole input class left the digest. Now expands per entry; original message preserved verbatim.

3. ZERO COVERAGE: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs (1964 lines) did not mention 'playground' once.

title: Make clear-http-interceptor's public opts form exact and fail-closed
description:
PR #6199 corrected one generated API example, but the public/internal boundary is still ambiguous and unsafe. The facade and its JVM/CLJS tests continue to accept the old two-scalar frame-first form `(clear-http-interceptor frame id)`, managed HTTP effects still call that form, and the migration guide plus installed API cheatsheet teach it as public/production syntax.

The shape discriminator treats any second map as opts, but resolves the target with `(or (:frame opts) ambient-frame)`. Under an ambient frame, `{}`, `{:frame nil}`, or a typo such as `{:fram target}` silently clears the ambient frame instead of failing. That violates the documented opts contract and makes a small programmer error act on the wrong owner.

Make the public facade exact and fail-closed: one argument clears by interceptor ID in ambient scope; two arguments are interceptor ID plus a valid explicit opts map carrying `:frame`. Keep any frame-first operation private if internal plumbing benefits from it, and route managed effects deliberately through that private seam or the public opts form. This is a narrow public-boundary correction, not a compatibility layer or a generalized argument parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- The public facade exposes only `(clear-http-interceptor id)` and `(clear-http-interceptor id {:frame target})`; two-scalar frame-first calls are not a supported public shape.

- Valid keyword and live frame-value targets retain their documented address/exactness behavior; the one-argument ambient form remains ergonomic.
- Managed HTTP effects use the deliberate opts form or a private helper, so removing the public legacy shape does not break internal cleanup.

title: Finish frame value/ID contract across public authorities and facade proof
description:
PR #6197 correctly reconciled the canonical lifecycle grammar: a `make-frame` value carries exact-incarnation authority for `destroy-frame!`, while a keyword/tokenless target addresses the current incarnation. Some imply destroy is ID-only or that values and IDs are universally interchangeable; others tell programmers to recover an ID from a frame value through a public accessor that does not exist. The intended public model is simpler: ordinary operations accept the frame value directly and privately normalize value to logical ID; no public value-to-ID accessor is needed. `destroy-frame!` is the one exact-value exception.

The existing lifecycle regression exercises public destroy behavior but constructs and distinguishes incarnations through private state/tokens and pins `:drain-lock`. title: Finish epoch silence schema and outside-lock source authority
description:
PR #6191 exposed listener generation so generation-qualified silencing is publicly implementable, but the public domain, canonical event schema, and runtime source authority do not yet agree.

`re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` accepts any comparable listener ID and the runtime emits that raw ID as `:cb-id`. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` restricts `EpochCbSilencedOnFrameDestroyTags/:cb-id` to keyword|string, so supported integer/vector IDs can register, query, and emit but fail the canonical schema. The same schema declares `:observed-gen :int` even though the public contract deliberately makes generations opaque and equality-only. JVM/CLJS public tests exercise only keyword IDs.

The runtime behavior is correct—reservation happens under the silence/listener locks and publication happens after both locks are released—but several comments/docstrings in `epoch/state.cljc` still claim locks span external emission or exclude replacement/drop/re-arm through publication. The reserve-only helper is also described as emitting an unqualified signal though it emits nothing. These are dangerous false authorities around a deadlock-sensitive seam.

Keep the comparable-ID, opaque-generation, outside-lock design. Reconcile schema, tests, and every nearby source claim without narrowing ergonomics, adding a new API, or redesigning locking.

title: Harden CI toolchain install against network flake (curl 35 / socket hang up in setup-clojure)
description: RECURRING FLAKE root cause (observed 5+ times: qxgve derivation-conformance, leeqp story-mcp, 1g5rt ssr): the DeLaGuardo/setup-clojure step (and the clojure -Sdeps toolchain download) fails with 'curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' / 'socket hang up' during the linux-install.sh CLI download — a transient network drop, NOT a test failure. Touches .github/workflows/*.yml (HOT-ZONE, sequential) — the setup-clojure step appears in every JVM job. Verify by confirming the retry/cache wraps each 'Install Clojure'/'setup-clojure' invocation. Do NOT change test logic — this is pure CI-infra resilience.

title: Make compatibility anchors render-faithful, unique, and manifest-driven
description:
PR #6193 / closed rf2-57k74 restored compatibility anchors and generalized source-comment checking, but the current proof can certify bookmarks that are absent or semantically misplaced in the rendered page.

In docs/routing/concepts.md, `<a id="when-a-loader-fails">` sits after the two-line loader-failure explanation and immediately before the unrelated "Declaring resources instead" heading. The historical bookmark therefore scrolls past the content it names.

In scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, `_slug_index` matches `<a id|name>` text inside HTML comments and inline-code spans, then collapses every target into a set. Replacing a live anchor with commented/backticked example text stays green even though the browser creates no fragment target; duplicate explicit/generated DOM ids also disappear into the set. Separately, the source-link regex is driven by a second hand-maintained `COMPAT_HANDBOOKS` tuple rather than `HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS`, and every source-comment mutation tooth uses only `docs/machines/page.md`. title: Make the consumed-container proof causally late and drift-guarded
description:
PR #6190's runtime denylist is source-sound, but its acceptance-named browser proof does not force the hazardous ordering it claims. The throwing fake schedules `queueMicrotask(replaceChildren)` inside one Promise continuation; JavaScript FIFO runs that microtask before the next `.then` re-initialises and mounts the successor. A focused host probe prints `queued-host-task` before `successor-then`. The late mutation therefore lands before any successor exists, and the later `next-macrotask` cannot make it late.

The same change left three current-truth contradictions: `reclaim-consumed-container!` says clearing enables deterministic same-container re-init, the adapter drain says successful reclaim proves the surface free, and a registry assertion says the marker is removed for same-container re-init. The actual invariant is the opposite: reclaim is only a snapshot; the exact node stays permanently denied.

Finally, the dedicated Root lifecycle drift gate still has only its 19 earlier anchors. It pins none of the consumed-node denylist, mark-before-release ordering, terminal fresh-container recovery, or causal queue-then-throw proof. Complete this proof/documentation boundary without adding runtime task tracking or a general prose framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The browser fixture queues predecessor DOM work before the host throw but holds it behind an explicit deterministic release; it records that the successor has committed before releasing the predecessor mutation, then proves the mutation executes and cannot touch the fresh successor node.
- The test is red if exact-container denial is removed or recovery reuses the poisoned node, and its ordering assertions are red if predecessor mutation runs before successor commit.
- Runtime/test comments and docstrings no longer say reclaim proves the surface free or enables same-container re-init; they consistently call DOM/marker clearing a snapshot and exact-node reuse terminally denied.
- `check_ui_root_lifecycle_drift.py` gains the smallest row-/site-specific teeth for consumed-container runtime ordering, the `root-container-consumed` fresh-node contract, and the causal fixture; each new tooth's mutation self-test fails independently.
- Existing ordinary deferred-settlement teeth remain intact; focused Node UI, browser DOM, lifecycle live, and lifecycle self-test lanes pass.
- Runtime scheduling and lifecycle design remain unchanged: no timeout, host-task tracker, scheduler, global lock, or general Markdown/Clojure parser.
