title: Make cleanup-failure root admission diagnostics structurally exact
description:
PR #6190 correctly distinguishes a terminally consumed container from an ordinary deferred teardown for different-ID and post-reclaim admission, but the same-root-ID cleanup-failure path still selects `:rf.error/duplicate-root-id` before the consumed-container arm.

After an isolated throwing `.unmount`, a same-ID retry therefore carries `:recovery :make-root-ids-unique` and an `:existing` projection that omits `:cleanup-failure?`. Its human message is more honest—it says there is no settlement and requires adapter re-init or a distinct ID plus fresh container—but structured consumers and AIs cannot recover that distinction. Spec 009's duplicate-root-id row still says a tearing-down predecessor may be waited on until settlement, which is false for cleanup-failure quarantine. The existing test asserts only the error id and message, leaving the wrong ex-data green.

Make the structured diagnostic exact for both relevant shapes: same ID plus the poisoned exact node, and same ID plus a fresh node while the old ID remains quarantined. Reuse the existing two error categories; do not invent a new lifecycle state or compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A same-ID retry against the exact cleanup-failure container reports the terminal consumed-container condition with `:recovery :use-a-fresh-container` and owner evidence, rather than allowing duplicate-ID ordering to hide the poisoned node.
- A same-ID retry on a fresh node while the cleanup-failure claim still holds the ID remains a duplicate-ID refusal, but its ex-data explicitly carries `:cleanup-failure? true` and a recovery that names the real choices: adapter destroy/re-init, or a distinct ID with a fresh node.
- Merely deferred teardown retains its settlement-based duplicate/container recovery and remains distinguishable from cleanup failure in both ex-data and Spec 009.
- Focused CLJS tests assert error id, recovery, owner/existing evidence, and message for same-ID exact-node, same-ID fresh-node, different-ID exact-node, ordinary deferred, and post-reclaim cases.
- Spec 006, both Spec 009 catalogue rows, runtime docstrings, and emitted payloads agree that cleanup failure never acquires an in-process settlement signal.
- No new public error category, global fence, retry scheduler, compatibility alias, or host-task tracker is introduced.

title: Make late captured-operation rejection realm-exact and exactly-once
description:
PR #6186 added a secondary exact-incarnation fence after a captured dispatch/dispatch-sync/subscribe passes its original precheck. Those rejection paths do not preserve the operation-specific observability contract.

First, the router's new A→B mismatch branches call the three-arity `emit-frame-destroyed!` without `:op`, and the subscribe mismatch emits attrs without `:op`. `error-source-coord` then uses its legacy `[:sub id]` then `[:event id]` fallback even though the capture seam knows the realm. A deterministic current-main late-mismatch repro seeded only an event coordinate and ran captured subscribe; exact record: `{:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed, :event-id :audit/collide, :frame :audit/late-mismatch, :source-coord {:ns audit.events, :file "events.cljc", :line 7}}`. The unrelated event coordinate should have been absent. Closed rf2-7xlvt/#6194 repaired only the earlier precheck emitter.

Second, if A is lost after the router's expected-token match but before async enqueue or sync drain-lock acquisition, the existing `target-live?`/lock guards correctly keep successor B untouched but silently return. The source acceptance promises recover-but-emit exactly once; current tests assert only that some emission occurs for the earlier mismatch and do not force this later loss.

Make every captured-operation rejection after the precheck emit one realm-exact `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`, without changing state/queue/cache fencing or ordinary realm-ambiguous bare-ID callers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Captured dispatch and dispatch-sync late rejections resolve source coordinates only under `[:event id]`; captured subscribe resolves only under `[:sub id]`.
- Same-keyword event/sub collision and missing-own-realm fixtures prove a late rejection never steals the other realm's coordinate; missing own registration omits `:source-coord`.
- Deterministic JVM interleavings cover (a) A→B before the secondary token comparison and (b) loss of A after that comparison but before async enqueue / sync drain acquisition; every rejected captured op emits `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` exactly once.
- Rejected async/sync dispatch never enters successor queue/state, rejected subscribe returns nil and never touches successor DB/cache, and attempted vector/head, frame, call-site, and recovery semantics remain intact.
- The already-known operation realm rides only the private captured-operation path; ordinary address-directed router/sub emitters retain their legacy fallback, and no public token, new error category, global lock, or general provenance mechanism is added.
- Resolve #6194's early-precheck record-shape contradiction explicitly: either keep `:op` genuinely private to source-coordinate steering and preserve the core always-on record's prior public keyset, or deliberately ratify/test/catalogue `:op` on core captured-operation recovery records. No payload expansion may remain private in prose but public in emitted data.
- Focused JVM/CLJS tests, source comments, router/sub emitter documentation, and Spec 009 distinguish the early precheck, secondary mismatch, and later lock/liveness rejection seams accurately and assert the chosen public keyset.
notes: PR #6194 audit (rf2-1kph4): the early precheck passes `{:op op}` as both trace tags and `record-attrs`; `dispatch-on-error!` merges all attrs into the always-on public record. Current test commentary calls this a private steering slot, tests do not assert the keyset, and Spec 009 says `:op` is present only on the UI throwing `(frame)` surface. Absorb this bounded schema/catalogue decision here before propagating the same realm mechanism to the late paths; do not open a competing runtime issue.

title: Complete G-8 with comparative latency and real React commit counts
description:
PR #6182's G-8 gate proves a useful Chromium/WebKit correctness subset, but it does not implement the complete canonical G-8 contract recorded in EP-0034 and the tracked S3 test plan: event-to-React-commit p95 within 10% of an equivalent hand-written React input and one React commit per input.

The current runner has no hand-written baseline or timing measurements. Its `revision-delta` counts ViewCell advancement, not React commits, and the IME assertion accepts `ime-revision-delta >= 1`, so duplicate updates remain green. The fixture dispatches programmatically-created events and places the caret manually; that is acceptable for bounded composition mechanics only if the gate is honest about it, but those operations cannot stand in for the missing latency and real-commit evidence.
design: Extend the existing dual-engine fixture with the smallest comparable hand-written React control and an attributable React commit counter (for example a local Profiler or layout-commit sentinel). Measure the same input path under the same browser/run and compare p95s, with enough samples and warm-up to make the stated relative budget meaningful. Keep correctness assertions deterministic and separate from the performance budget. Do not build a general benchmark framework or require OS-level IME automation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Chromium and WebKit report actual attributable React commits separately from ViewCell revisions, and every ordinary input plus the committed IME boundary produces exactly one React commit.
- The IME arm rejects duplicate revisions/commits (`= 1`, not `>= 1`) while retaining value, caret, ordering, and pre-paint correctness.
- The compiled reusable control's event-to-commit p95 is within 10% of an equivalent hand-written React control in each required engine, measured in the same warmed run with the sample count and noise policy recorded in the artifact.
- Mutation teeth fail when an extra React commit occurs, IME duplicates, the commit counter becomes vacuous, or compiled latency crosses the ruled budget.
- The report and workflow distinguish deterministic correctness from comparative performance and preserve useful per-engine artifacts.
- No general performance harness, arbitrary timing-as-correctness rule, or OS-level IME automation project is introduced.

title: Finish defview binding-plan correctness with real compiled CLJS proof
description:
PR #6185 closed rf2-wix0o, rf2-gvuoo, and rf2-nedxb, but every added proof is JVM-side emitter/form modelling. Their explicit real-compiled-CLJS and advanced-CLJS acceptance remains unproved.

There is also a current correctness defect beyond the exact-pattern collision fixture. On origin/main b0e20ccd, `(parse-header '[{[x] :other :keys [ns/x]}])` returns derived entries for both `[x] <- :other` and `x <- :ns/x`, with slots `[:other :ns/x]`. Native destructuring evaluates both initializers but the later `x <- :ns/x` is the only visible local. `collapse-entries` compares whole `:pattern` values, so nested or partially overlapping patterns leak dead slots into the comparator, manifest, and CLOSED-props acceptance.

Finish the host-faithful boundary with actual compiled CLJS evidence. Keep every host binding unit in executable order, but derive effective metadata by final bound-symbol ownership. Do not add a general destructuring macroexpander or metadata framework.
design: Use one small compiled-CLJS fixture corpus shared where practical with the JVM ground truth. Exercise real defviews rather than only inspecting emitted forms. For derived entries, perform a reverse winner sweep over the locals bound by each pattern: retain or trim an entry only where it contributes a final visible local, while preserving the full executable binding-unit plan and initializer order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real compiled CLJS and JVM defviews accept equivalent qualified key/ref spellings and bind the same values while genuinely bare key/ref slots still fail didactically.
- A real advanced CLJS fixture proves authored `^js` metadata survives to Closure-relevant interop/codegen; symbol equality or JVM emitter inspection alone is insufficient.
- Real compiled CLJS and native JVM agree on eager-default count/order/throws/final values and on duplicate-local initializer execution.
- Nested and partially overlapping patterns such as `{[x] :other :keys [ns/x]}` retain all executable initializers but expose only final visible-local slots in comparator, manifest, schema, and CLOSED-props validation.
- A mutation restoring whole-pattern-only collapse, conditional default evaluation, lost metadata, or omitted initializer makes the relevant host gate red.
- Existing ordinary collision/order/diagnostic behavior remains green; no general macroexpander or new public API is introduced.

title: Make publishable-runtime enrollment structural and causal
description:
## Problem

PR #6109 makes bundle-isolation auto-enrol future publishable UI and adapter runtimes, but its fail-closed claim can be discharged by text and names rather than repository truth.

Publishability is detected by stripping `;` to end-of-line with a regex and then searching anywhere for `:clein/build`. Valid EDN such as `{:note "semi;colon" :aliases {:clein/build {...}}}` loses the real alias and is silently omitted; a string mention or discarded `#_ :clein/build` form is invented as an alias. The release lockstep script repeats a textual variant, so it is not independent structural proof.

Coverage then reduces each discovered path to its leaf name. A future `implementation/adapters/schemas` is accepted via the unrelated flat `schemas` generic entry. Dedicated coverage is a truthy prose string: adding a descriptive map entry can make a new adapter green without a gate script or an invoked command. Current inventory and the four current dedicated gates are genuinely wired; the defect is that future auto-enrolment is not actually structural or causal.
design: Use one bounded, EDN-aware publishable-artefact discovery helper/authority that inspects the real `:aliases/:clein/build` key and can be consumed by bundle coverage and release lockstep. Key isolation ownership by exact implementation-relative path, not leaf name. Represent dedicated coverage as a small machine-readable descriptor tied to an existing checker and invoked package/CI command, then validate that wiring with focused mutations. Reuse current script-policy/changed-surface machinery where it already proves invocation; do not build a general EDN, workflow, or gate framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- A genuine `:aliases/:clein/build` survives semicolons inside EDN strings and is enrolled; token text inside strings, comments, or discarded forms is not.
- Bundle-isolation and release lockstep consume one structural publishability result or independently prove the same parsed EDN fact; duplicated textual greps are removed.
- Coverage is keyed by exact relative path, so `adapters/schemas` cannot inherit the flat `schemas` gate.
- A dedicated mapping is accepted only when its real checker exists and its declared package/CI command is invoked; a fictional prose entry or removed checker fails.
- Mutations cover semicolon-in-string, token-in-string, discard form, colliding leaf names, and nonexistent/uninvoked dedicated gates.
- The current publishable flat/adapters inventory, reasoned `core`/`ssr-ring` exclusions, unpublished UI state, and four real dedicated gates remain green.
- No runtime code, public API, general workflow parser, or speculative artefact hierarchy is introduced.

title: Make ui.test host-signature reconciliation kind-aware and exact
description:
## Problem

PR #6108 added a host-aware arity sidecar for the nine blessed `re-frame.ui.test` vars, but the sidecar is not reconciled as an exact public-surface contract.

The sidecar duplicates each var's `:kind`. The JVM reconciler ignores that field, while the CLJS reconciler trusts it as the switch deciding whether an arity is checked. Changing only `flush!` (or any function) from `:fn` to `:macro` therefore leaves the JVM lane green and makes CLJS skip the entry, even while the normal manifest correctly continues to classify the var as a function. A later CLJS-only arity reshape can then escape. A future CLJS-only public function can likewise be added to the manifest classification without an exact signature-keyset check.

The two host lanes also normalize arglists without the live Var kind. Both remove every parameter symbol named `&form` or `&env`, even for an ordinary function. `[x]`, `[&env x]`, and `[&form &env x]` all normalize to the same visible arity, so a real function arity change using legal programmer parameter names can remain green.

Focused API tests are green (83 tests, 176 assertions); these are adversarial false-greens outside their current mutations.
design: Treat the generated/live public classification as the authority for names and kinds, and keep the host-signature data responsible only for host arities. Reconcile signature keys and classified keys exactly on both hosts; reject kind disagreement rather than using unvalidated sidecar data to select checks. Make arity normalization kind-aware: ordinary function parameters are never erased, while defensive macro-slot handling applies only to actual macro metadata if it is still needed. Share the small normalization/contract projection between the JVM and analyzer lanes where practical; do not build a general API-schema framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Changing a signature sidecar entry from `:fn` to `:macro`, omitting an entry, or adding a classified CLJS-only function without host arities makes the relevant gate red.
- Signature names and kinds are derived from or exactly reconciled with the authoritative manifest/live classification; the sidecar cannot independently redefine them.
- An ordinary function arglist containing programmer parameters named `&env` or `&form` is counted exactly; adding either parameter changes the reported arity and fails against the old contract.
- Macro arities remain programmer-visible and correct, including fixed and variadic `render` / `with-root` grammar, without counting compiler-internal slots.
- The current nine vars and the intentional JVM/CLJS `flush!` difference remain green.
- Focused JVM and CLJS manifest/API gates pass; no runtime/public API change or broad schema system is introduced.

title: Complete scheduler failure semantics across epoch and direct-source boundaries
description:
#6106 correctly surfaces the first failure retained inside one scheduler drain, but the new rethrow is incomplete at its entry boundaries:

- At depth zero, each raw source-atom watch drains immediately. If the first derived value's recompute/subscriber throws, the surfaced failure escapes the atom's uncontained watch loop before later derived source watches can mark/enqueue, so a supported direct source mutation suppresses sibling derived work.
- `with-epoch` drains from `finally`. If the reset/watch body first throws E1 after queueing work and that drain throws E2, JavaScript finally semantics replace E1 with E2; caller-visible primary identity is no longer the earliest escape.
- The source Bead required the common zero/one-subscriber path to be allocation-free or measured. The patch avoids the fan-out capture cell, but every drain allocates another capture volatile (even an empty queue), and `(val (first ws))` constructs singleton map-seq/entry objects under the pinned CLJS implementation. No measurement justifies the claim.

Complete the one scheduler exception contract rather than adding a bus: contain/drain all owned work, preserve the earliest primary by presence, restore state, then surface once. Keep the hot path genuinely lean or measure and justify it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A direct raw source reset with two derived dependents still marks/drains the later sibling when the earlier dependent throws; the original first failure surfaces only after all owned sibling work is attempted.
- When an epoch body throws E1 and queued drain work throws E2, E1 remains the caller-visible primary by exact identity (including false/nil where representable), the drain tail is attempted, and scheduler depth/queue/queued/flushing state is clean afterward.
- Existing inner-drain first-failure, multiple-throw, re-entrant queue, snapshot, and later-recovery behavior remains correct.
- Ordinary empty/zero/one-subscriber mutations add no per-drain/fan-out capture or singleton map-seq allocation, or a focused benchmark measures and explicitly justifies the retained cost against the source acceptance.
- Focused CLJS mutations prove both boundary defects and the performance control without a general event bus, new public error id, or ratom-family change.

title: Close the raw fn* parameter and arity grammar at the UI letfn* boundary
description:
PR #6094 added `fn-init-shape?` to keep malformed host `letfn*` initializers on the typed `:rf.ui.compile/bad-let` surface, but the predicate treats any vector as a well-formed argv and any sequence of vector-led arity clauses as valid. Host-illegal raw `fn*` grammar therefore still escapes the UI compiler.

Reproduced on current main and the exact applied patch:
- `(letfn* [f (fn* [{:keys [x]}] x)] f)` -> UI analyzer accepts; JVM host rejects because raw `fn*` parameters must be symbols.
- `(letfn* [f (fn* [foo/bar] foo/bar)] f)` -> UI analyzer accepts; JVM host rejects the qualified parameter.
- malformed directives such as `(fn* [{:keys 42}] ...)` can still throw raw `IllegalArgumentException` inside binding analysis rather than typed bad-let.
- duplicate fixed arities such as `(fn* ([x] x) ([y] y))` pass the UI analyzer and fail at the host compiler.

The essential control is not to reject destructuring globally: macro `fn`/source `letfn` legally support destructuring and are accepted by both analyzer and host. Complete the bounded fn-versus-fn* grammar seam, preserving legal named/multi-arity/variadic/prepost/metadata forms. This is not permission for a general Clojure grammar framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Raw `fn*` initializers under host `letfn*` accept only host-portable parameter vectors and arity combinations; destructuring, non-symbol/qualified parameters, malformed `&` forms, duplicate/incompatible arities, and malformed directives fail deterministically through `:rf.ui.compile/bad-let` on both analyzer hosts.
- No malformed argv reaches `env/binding-syms`/binding-plan code as a raw `IllegalArgumentException`, and none is merely preserved for a later host compiler crash.
- Legal macro `fn` and source `letfn` destructuring remains accepted, including nested destructuring and pre/post maps. Legal raw `fn*` single/multi/variadic/named forms retain exact shape, mutual scope, metadata, and deferred-body rejection.
- Causal cross-host fixtures include raw-fn* reject vs macro-fn accept controls plus duplicate-arity/malformed-directive mutations; reverting the new boundary fails.
- Reuse `:rf.ui.compile/bad-let`; add no new error ID, broad special-form roster, or general grammar parser.

title: Make the synthesis-plan authority guard causal and durable
description:
PR #6090's synthesis-plan guard currently protects a citation and mappings that it cannot actually prove.

Current `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/12-implementation-plan.md` says the durable S0 coverage record lives in an `rf2-vxgfnd` NOTES entry named `S0 COVERAGE PASS (2026-07-12)`. `bd show rf2-vxgfnd` has no such note now: it contains only the later adapter-disposition note. The epic description says a pass ran but does not carry the named result or mappings, so the guarded citation is false for a fresh worker.

The checker is also non-causal. `REQUIRED_MAPPINGS` declares label/bead pairs, but `check()` only proves each label and bead occur independently somewhere in the anchor block. Swapping Q49/Q51 owners passes. The plan records `static-override-lease Tier-3 -> rf2-vxgfnd.8 / .12`, while the checker requires only `.8`; deleting `.12` passes. Removing the explicit authority clause can also pass because `rf2-vxgfnd` appears inside child IDs. Its prose advertises all unqualified live-stage claims, while the executable rule recognizes only same-line `not (yet) started`; `S3 is underway` passes and inactive Markdown-comment text can fail. Finally, `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` nests this check under the Markdown-only branch, so a checker-only local change skips its own self-tests even though CI routing is correct.

Repair the narrow authority seam, not documentation in general. Point the anchor at a durable record that actually exists (or make the plan anchor itself the durable record with honest provenance), validate exact associations, and make the status rule's stated scope match its deliberately small executable form. Prefer simplification and explicit structure over a prose parser or live Beads dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
- The plan no longer cites a nonexistent `rf2-vxgfnd` NOTES entry; its S0 SHIP result and unresolved mappings have one durable, discoverable authority a fresh worker can follow from the plan alone.
- Exact label -> owner associations are validated, including the complete `static-override-lease Tier-3 -> rf2-vxgfnd.8 / .12` ownership. Swapping Q49/Q51, dropping `.12`, or removing the actual authority attribution fails independently.
- The live-stage rule has an honest bounded contract: known active status syntax is checked causally, historical exemption requires a genuine dated snapshot, and inactive comment text does not create a false failure. Do not build a general Markdown/prose parser.
- Hermetic mutation fixtures isolate every failure above; the unmodified current anchor passes.
- Local fast checks and CI run the guard/self-tests when either the authoritative plan or the checker changes. No live Beads API call, generic documentation framework, or policy rewrite is introduced.

title: Make stale capture-frame errors operation-realm exact
description:
PR #6079 introduced `router/emit-captured-frame-superseded!` for stale captured dispatch, and #6084 reused it for stale captured subscribe. The helper ultimately calls `emit-frame-destroyed!` without carrying the failing operation realm. After rf2-xgkgx/#6131 made `error_emit/error-source-coord` operation-aware, an absent `:op` deliberately falls back to `[:sub id]` then `[:event id]` for legacy core emitters. That fallback is not sound for a `capture-frame` bundle because this seam knows whether the attempted op was dispatch, dispatch-sync, or subscribe.

A deterministic current-main repro seeded distinct coordinates and invoked a capture pinned to destroyed incarnation A after same-id B reseated. With both `[:event :audit/collide]` and `[:sub :audit/collide]` present, stale captured dispatch emitted the SUB coordinate. With only the event coordinate present, stale captured subscribe emitted the unrelated EVENT coordinate instead of omitting `:source-coord`. Exact output: `{:stale-dispatch-record {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed, :event-id :audit/collide, :source-coord {:ns audit.subs ...}}, :stale-subscribe-result nil, :stale-subscribe-record {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed, :event-id :audit/collide, :source-coord {:ns audit.events ...}}}`.

This misdirects Xray/off-box tooling and the programmer or AI to the wrong definition. Carry the already-known operation realm through this core capture emitter so source lookup is exact. Keep it private/tight; do not redesign the error substrate, expose incarnation tokens, or alter recovery behavior. The separate JVM exact-consumption race remains owned by rf2-dlld6.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stale `capture-frame` dispatch and dispatch-sync resolve source coordinates only under `[:event id]`; stale subscribe resolves only under `[:sub id]`.
- Same-keyword event/sub collision fixtures prove neither operation can select the other realm, and a programmatic or missing registration omits `:source-coord` rather than stealing one.
- The captured op carries its already-known realm through the shared frame-destroyed emission boundary without adding a public incarnation token, global lock, new error category, or general provenance mechanism.
- Superseded dispatch/dispatch-sync still no-op, subscribe still returns nil, successor state/cache stays untouched, call-site and elided attempted vector/head attribution remain intact, and each failure emits exactly once.
- Ordinary bare router dispatch and `subs/subscribe` destroyed-frame emitters retain their existing behavior; the UI throwing frame-bundle operation-aware path remains unchanged.
- Router helper documentation, Spec 009 catalogue wording, and focused JVM/CLJS tests agree on the core capture-frame operation-realm behavior.

title: Preserve defview group-symbol metadata through the canonical binding plan
description:
#6075's extracted `assoc-binding-units` reconstructs group locals with `(symbol (name bb))`. Real `clojure.core/destructure` preserves authored symbol metadata via `with-meta`; the JVM defview emitter keeps the raw binding form, but the canonical plan and generated CLJS binding discard metadata.

A current-main probe of `{:keys [^js node]}` shows the authored and native host local carry `{:tag js}`, while both `:local-pattern` and the emitted CLJS binding have nil metadata. Symbol equality ignores metadata, so current plan-order tests false-green. Losing `^js` and other portable type hints can change Closure interop inference, warnings and advanced-build code generation, undermining the host-faithful/programmer-trusting contract.

Preserve only the host's existing symbol metadata when reconstructing the local; do not invent a metadata framework or retain directive-only metadata that native destructuring drops.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group-symbol metadata retained by native CLJ and CLJS destructuring is retained on the canonical local and emitted CLJS binding.
- A real advanced CLJS fixture proves a supported interop/type hint such as `^js` survives and behaves without relying on symbol equality.
- Explicit locals and unhinted group symbols retain current behavior and diagnostics.
- Host-order/collision behavior and qualified lookup keys remain unchanged.
- Tests compare the relevant metadata directly so a `(symbol (name ...))` regression fails.

title: Preserve executable host semantics when defview header entries collapse
description:
The UI compiler advertises a host-faithful defview binding plan, but executable header lowering loses host-visible evaluation semantics in two related ways.

First, CLJS `slot-read` evaluates an `:or` default only when the property is absent, while native host destructuring evaluates the default operand as part of the lookup call even when the property is present. A current-main JVM probe with `{:keys [x] :or {x (swap! calls inc)}}` reports one call for both present and missing props, while the emitted CLJS form conditionally calls it only for missing.

Second, the later `collapse-entries` repair correctly removes dead comparator/manifest slots, but CLJS emission consumes only that collapsed winner projection. For `{:keys [ns/x] x :other :or {x expr}}`, native destructuring evaluates two distinct binding initializers before the later local wins; current CLJS emits one. Effects, throws, getters and final values can therefore diverge even though literal-value fixtures pass.

Keep the solution small: separate executable host binding units from the collapsed effective-slot projection, and lower default evaluation with the real portable host semantics. Do not reintroduce dead schema/comparator slots or add a general macroexpander.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real JVM and real compiled CLJS fixtures agree on evaluation count, order, thrown exceptions and final value for present/missing ordinary defaults.
- Qualified-group/explicit same-local collisions execute every host binding initializer in host order on both targets while the later binding remains the visible winner.
- Comparator, closed-prop schema and manifest continue to contain only effective winner slots; the dead-slot repair does not regress.
- Analyzer scope order and executable emission consume the same full host-unit plan; derived metadata consumes the separate collapsed projection.
- Mutations that make defaults conditionally/eagerly inconsistent or drop an initializer fail causal tests.

title: Accept qualified key/ref props in every defview :keys spelling
description:
#6075 added raw reserved-slot validation before canonical header collapse, but the bare `:keys` arm derives each group key with `(keyword (name s))`. That drops a qualified symbol's namespace, so legal `{:keys [acct/key]}` is rejected as reserved React `:key` and `{:keys [acct/ref]}` is rejected as bare `:ref`. Equivalent `{:acct/keys [key]}` and `{key :acct/key}` preserve `:acct/key` and compile.

This contradicts the qualified-symbol contract and makes equivalent host destructuring spellings behave differently. The canonical binding plan already knows the correct group-key transform; raw diagnostics should use that transform while still rejecting genuinely bare `:key` and `:ref`. No current Bead owns the residual; closed `rf2-qa5wkd` and `rf2-7imr5y` cover different normalization/collapse bugs.
acceptance_criteria:
- `{:keys [acct/key acct/ref]}`, `{:acct/keys [key ref]}`, and explicit qualified lookup forms all derive the same qualified slots and compile.
- Genuinely bare `{:keys [key ref]}` and explicit `:key`/`:ref` props retain their typed reserved-slot diagnostics before collapse.
- Raw validation reuses the canonical group-key transform rather than reimplementing namespace rules.
- Real compiled CLJS and JVM defviews cover both equivalent qualified spellings; emitter-form inspection alone is not the proof.
- Ordinary non-colliding header diagnostics remain unchanged.

title: Make the spawn-all runtime-key catalogue derive from its producer/consumer boundary
description:
PR #6073 added `:cancelled` to the spawn-all join schema and a catalogue test intended to prove every runtime-required key is required. The gate still has two independent authorities: `expected-runtime-owned-join-keys` is hand-written, the schema-required set is compared only to that copy, and the dissociation mutation iterates only that copy. Because the schema is intentionally open, adding a newly seeded and consumed required key to runtime leaves all assertions green if both copies omit it.

Current runtime already shows why a deliberate classification is necessary: the real produced join carries `:invoke-id` in addition to the seven listed fields, while `:invoke-id` appears to be optional bookkeeping rather than a required consumer input. The existing test's “EXACTLY the runtime-owned seed keys” wording is therefore already false, but blindly making every observed key required would also be wrong.

Use one small producer/consumer boundary roster or compare the real produced key set against `required ∪ explicitly-classified-open-bookkeeping`. New runtime-owned keys must fail until intentionally classified. Do not close the Malli map or build a generic schema synchronizer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real spawn-all-produced join's complete runtime-owned key set equals the union of schema-required keys and an explicit, reviewed optional/bookkeeping classification.
- Adding a new seeded-and-consumed key without classifying and requiring it makes a causal mutation test fail.
- Removing any currently required key, including `:cancelled`, fails through the actual consumer contract.
- `:invoke-id` is either removed as redundant or explicitly classified with a test proving why it remains optional.
- User/extensions keys remain legal under the intentionally open schema.

title: Make generation-qualified epoch silencing usable through the public API
description:
The later #6071 repair correctly moved delayed epoch-silence trace emission outside the ledger locks to eliminate the ledger↔frame-drain AB-BA deadlock. It preserves attribution by carrying `:observed-gen` and Spec 009/Tool-Pair tell a receiver whose current callback generation differs to self-filter the superseded signal.

That consumer rule is not implementable through supported APIs. `register-epoch-listener!` / `register-listener! :epoch` return only the listener ID; assembled epoch callback records do not expose the registration generation. The current generation is available only through internal `listeners-snapshot`, and the regression proves self-filtering by consulting that private state. A pair tool receiving `{:cb-id C :observed-gen G}` therefore has no supported way to learn whether C is now generation H.

The surrounding public prose also retains the superseded unqualified model: the Spec 009 catalogue omits `:observed-gen`, several rows say once per `(frame, cb-id)` across repeats while the detailed law says once per destroy-continuum, and state/schema comments still describe emit-under-lock exclusion. No live Bead owns this current boundary; closed `rf2-8b9twg`/`rf2-3a7yvd` implemented and documented the partial repair.

Choose the smallest coherent contract: suppress superseded delivery inside the runtime, expose an opaque supported registration-generation authority, or weaken the consumer claim to attribution-only. Do not expose mutable listener registry internals.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pair-tool consumer can handle a reserve→emit G→H replacement correctly using only public APIs, or the public contract no longer requires an impossible comparison.
- A black-box test, without `listeners-snapshot` or other private state, proves the chosen behavior at the public boundary.
- Spec 009, Tool-Pair, API/tag catalogue, schemas/comments, and epoch runtime docstrings agree on `:observed-gen`, once-per-destroy-continuum semantics, and outside-lock emission.
- The repair preserves the deadlock fix: no external trace emit runs while either ledger lock is held.
- Generation identity remains opaque/non-reused and ordinary listener registration stays low-friction.

title: Document exact frame-value teardown versus address-directed IDs
description:
PR #6072 deliberately changed lifecycle semantics: a frame VALUE returned by `make-frame` now carries opaque exact-incarnation authority, so destroying a stale value for A no-ops against same-ID successor B; destroying by keyword/ID remains intentionally address-directed and destroys whatever incarnation is current when the call begins.

The canonical public contract still teaches the old one-grammar equivalence. `spec/002-Frames.md` says frame values and IDs are accepted interchangeably by `destroy-frame!`, says a value is destroyed by reading its ID, and repeats that the value or ID “destroys it”. `spec/API.md`, the public `make-frame` docstring, and the retired `frame-value->id` explanation repeat the same claim. This directly misses closed source `rf2-moftbs`'s acceptance criterion that the documented frame VALUE have coherent lifecycle-token semantics while keyword/ID destruction remain explicitly address-directed.

The runtime representation stays hidden. The needed distinction is behavioral and ergonomic: callers who own the returned value can safely release that incarnation; callers who intentionally target an address pass the keyword.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 002, API.md, public `make-frame`/`destroy-frame!` docs, and directly linked lifecycle guidance state the exact-value versus address-directed-ID distinction consistently.
- Examples show that stale value A cannot destroy successor B, while keyword `:id` intentionally targets current B.
- Other routing operations that merely normalize a frame target remain documented accurately; the lifecycle exception does not falsely imply all operations become incarnation-pinned.
- The opaque token representation stays non-public and no second handle hierarchy or unwrap API is introduced.
- A public-surface regression pins the behavioral distinction and docs/API consistency gates pass.

title: Reconcile the live slice-memo draft and S3 spike with the CLJS host window
description:
PR #6070's executable inverse-FIFO proof establishes the honest CLJS law: the whole bounded host-microtask window is one slice, so a genuinely later callback interposed before the CAS-guarded clear may reuse the still-tagged memo. Later `rf2-er64a`/#6120 repaired canonical Spec 006, synthesis 03, the core observation contract, and their census.

Two still-live authority-shaped documents retain the rejected universal wording:

- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/spec-006-observation-port-amendment.md` calls the table scoped to the “current synchronous execution slice”, cleared by `queueMicrotask`, and says no entry survives a later slice.
- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/spikes/s3-ownership-report.md` says `queueMicrotask` always runs at synchronous slice end and no dispatch can interleave.

The amendment presents the S3 spike as its shape source and the synthesis/EP chain still points at these materials, so a programmer or AI can reasonably treat them as current design authority. This misses closed source `rf2-2g7pxq`'s explicit requirement to correct, tombstone, or clearly repoint both files. No live Bead owns the residual.
acceptance_criteria:
- The amendment draft and S3 ownership report either state the host-specific JVM/CLJS lifetime correctly or are prominently marked superseded with a direct pointer to current Spec 006/synthesis 03.
- No live-looking passage claims CLJS sharing ends with the originating synchronous call or that a pre-queued callback cannot interpose before the clear.
- Exact incarnation/epoch tag safety remains distinct from bounded within-window reuse; no runtime behavior changes.
- A narrow census or equivalent negative check covers these two authority surfaces without attempting a general prose parser.
- Existing slice-memo lifetime/census gates pass.

title: Make both Xray unchanged-sub disclosure controls operator-effective
description: PR #6069's data path is sound, but neither operator-facing disclosure contract is effective. The panel-local button installs a deferred React on-click that calls bare rf/dispatch. The facade reg-view delegates to reactive-panel without threading its lexically injected dispatcher, so after render scope unwinds the click emits rf.error/no-frame-context and leaves Xray state unchanged. The Settings view explicitly removed the promised Always show unchanged subs control while retaining its state slot; spec/021 and the source acceptance still promise a configured pin. Registry tests dispatch inside a manually bound :rf/xray frame, masking the click failure and proving only plumbing. No mounted test exercises the unchanged-section selectors, and the source-text singleton guard only matches dispatch immediately adjacent to an on-* attribute, missing this multiline callback.
acceptance_criteria: The panel-local button dispatches through the surrounding Xray instance's injected or captured frame-bound dispatcher; a real click emits no no-frame-context error, expands the memo-hit rows, and changes only that instance when two frame-scoped Xray panels are mounted. Settings visibly exposes the existing show-unchanged-subs setting and its pin expands the same disclosure according to spec/021; default remains collapsed and the local and configured axes compose intentionally. Mounted regression coverage uses real memo-hit rows and proves default collapsed, local click expanded, Settings pin expanded, and frame isolation. The narrow frame-singleton regression guard or equivalent causal test catches a deferred multiline bare dispatch without introducing a parser or new state machinery.
close_reason: shipped #6181 (merged)

title: Preserve concrete query identity in Xray skipped-sub disclosure
description: PR #6069 carries canonical rf.sub/skip evidence into the Reactive panel, but skipped-subs deduplicates and cross-excludes by the registered sub-id while the subscription cache and trace identify concrete instances by full query-v. In one epoch, if [:item/derived 1] recomputes and [:item/derived 2] memo-hits, project-record builds ran-ids containing :item/derived and suppresses the second instance's skip entirely. Multiple skipped parameterizations are likewise collapsed to the first. The view preserves neither distinction: it keys, test-ids, and labels rows only by sub-id even though each projected row already carries query-v. Xray can therefore claim that no concrete instance was skipped when one was. The canonical query vector is already present; no substrate or compatibility machinery is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Skipped-sub deduplication uses concrete query-v identity, so repeated evidence for the same concrete query is collapsed but distinct parameterizations remain distinct. A recomputed query excludes only a skip for that exact query, not every instance sharing its registration id. Rows display and key by the full query vector (with a small documented fallback only if canonical evidence genuinely lacks it), while source-coordinate lookup may continue using the registered id. A focused counterexample with one same-id recompute and a different same-id memo hit preserves and visibly disambiguates the skipped row; two same-id skipped queries both survive. Ordinary unparameterized behavior and recompute-vs-skip separation remain unchanged.
close_reason: shipped #6181 (merged)

title: Make the same-root supersession browser proof ordinary and causally complete
description: PR #6067 was opened to satisfy the explicit no-act/no-flush browser arm of rf2-5ep117: two ordinary back-to-back ui/render! calls through the live pending-attempt supersession path. Its fixture instead wraps both renders in one React act batch and describes that manufactured batch as ordinary. More importantly, the assertions do not make A-side settlement observable: removing the call that aborts the old receipt still leaves B able to replace the pending slot, commit its shared frame, clear its own slot, render B, and satisfy every current assertion. The test therefore proves B wins under act but does not causally pin the superseded receipt's terminal settlement. It also never asserts the committed live-root entry has no pending-attempt. This is a bounded browser-proof gap, not evidence of a current runtime defect.
acceptance_criteria: A real-browser fixture performs two ordinary back-to-back same-root ui/render! calls without React act or an explicit render flush between them, and proves the natural uncommitted A-to-B window occurred. A owns an independently observable write (for example a disjoint frame omitted by B) whose exact receipt is terminally aborted by supersession, while the shared frame commits B with zero frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch diagnostics. The committed live-root entry has no pending-attempt and teardown clears root/plan residue. Mutating either the pre-#6060 superseding-receipt handoff or the old-receipt abort makes the fixture fail. Public runtime APIs remain unchanged.

title: Make the exceptional Form-3 subscription recipe instance-safe
description:
PR #6065's copy-pasteable exceptional Form-3 recipe is not safe for multiple instances. Every `live-gauge` mount adds and removes a watch on the cached reaction with the constant key `::feed`. Equal `(frame, query-v)` subscriptions share that reaction and increment its ref-count, so a second mount overwrites the first callback; unmounting either removes the remaining callback and leaves the surviving widget stale.

A current-runtime probe with two captured subscribes to the same query confirmed the shared reaction and produced `{:after-one {:same true, :a [], :b [1]}, :after-removing-one {:a [], :b [1]}}`. The existing Form-3 browser matrix proves ref-count balance but does not exercise two imperative watches. Related owner prose also still states lifecycle subscription reads are categorically unsupported, without naming this rare captured/add-watch/balanced-unsubscribe exception.

Repair the example, test, and directly authoritative owner prose together. This needs a per-mount watch key and precise exception wording, not a new runtime API.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recipe allocates and retains a unique watch key per component mount and uses that exact key in teardown.
- A real Form-3 browser test mounts two same-frame/same-query widgets, proves both receive updates, unmounts one and proves the survivor remains live, then restores the final cache/ref-count baseline.
- Teardown remains balanced under React StrictMode and cannot skip unsubscribe/widget cleanup if watch removal fails.
- Reagent-slim, Stateful Components, migration, and skill owners distinguish ordinary unowned lifecycle reads from the rare explicitly captured and balanced imperative exception without weakening the default guidance.

title: Dispose page-owned playground registrations on instant navigation
description:
PR #6064's page disposal fixes roots and frames but not registrations. `docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs` exposes process-global `reg-*` APIs directly, while `disposePage` only unmounts cached roots and destroys frames. Its comment relies on incoming cells overwriting colliding IDs, which does not protect a later page that dispatches or subscribes to an ID it did not itself register.

Reproduced on current production code: page 1 registered `:page1/stale`; after the real instant-navigation loader disposed the page, page 2 created a fresh frame and dispatched `[:page1/stale]` without re-registering it. The fresh frame received `{:leaked-registration true}` and reported no page error. This violates source Bead rf2-io9mdr's acceptance that navigation cannot reuse another cell's registrations. Current smoke registers incoming handlers before frame creation and therefore remains green.

Keep the repair bounded: give playground cells explicit page registration ownership and clear or restore page `(kind,id)` registrations during disposal, while preserving bundle/framework baseline registrations. Avoid a general registration subsystem redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
- Leaving a Core page removes or restores every registration authored by that page before the incoming page can run.
- Framework/bundle-init registrations that intentionally span pages remain intact.
- A production-bundle instant-navigation test proves a fresh page cannot dispatch/subscribe through an outgoing page-only ID, including when it never re-registers that ID.
- Existing root/frame isolation, cell-less navigation, repeated navigation, and framework-registration controls remain green.
close_reason: shipped #6170 (merged)

title: Make the capture-once retarget guard reject semantic reversals
description:
PR #6061 added a positive cross-owner drift check for the Form-3 capture-once provider-retarget invariant, but the current helper searches each entire document for independent vocabulary tokens. It does not require those tokens to state the locked-handle relationship or reject the opposite polarity.

Reproduced deterministically on current main by importing `_form3_capture_once_problems` and supplying an adopter owner that says "Capture-once automatically follows any provider change; it never goes stale" plus unrelated provider-A-to-B, remount, and recipe-pointer fragments, and a canonical owner that says capture automatically retargets/re-resolves plus an unrelated A-to-B example. The result was `[]`. A second independent mutation saying there is no need to remount also passed. Existing self-tests only delete expected tokens, so they prove vocabulary presence rather than semantic teeth.

The shipped FORM-3 and canonical migration prose are currently correct. Closed `rf2-aalo4n` introduced this guard; closed `rf2-6m5qb` repairs a different Form-3 lifecycle classifier. No live Bead owns this false green.

Keep the repair bounded: validate the capture-once retarget statement within its owning section/paragraph, including polarity and relation, without building a general Markdown or Clojure parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- In each owner, the capture-once/locked-handle statement is causally tied to a surviving provider A-to-B retarget: the handle stays on stale A and does not follow B.
- FORM-3's owning section also carries a supported remedy and the canonical-recipe pointer; unrelated tokens elsewhere cannot satisfy the invariant.
- Explicit semantic reversals such as "automatically retargets/re-resolves", "never goes stale", or "no need to remount" fail even when every positive vocabulary token remains elsewhere in the document.
- Adversarial self-tests mutate each live owner to the wrong polarity while preserving A/B/remount/pointer vocabulary and fail before the repair.
- Current correct prose, legal unrelated mentions, the migration guard self-test, and the live CI scan remain green.
- No general-purpose Markdown parser or new documentation abstraction is introduced.

title: Authenticate the superseding receipt controller before silent settlement
description: PR #6060 suppresses an old preflight receipt's revision mismatch when a later same-root receipt owns the exact current write. The suppression authenticates only the superseding receipt's inner write fields: `superseding-index` discards the receipt's outer `:root-id`, and `benign-supersession?` compares the write root/revision with the old write and current record. A deterministic current-main probe executed attempts A and B for `:root/owner`, changed only B's outer `:root-id` to `:root/foreign`, and aborted A with that tampered superseder. Result: zero `:rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch` records while B remained owner-authoritative. Closed source Bead `rf2-5ep117` explicitly required foreign-root and stale-controller mismatches to remain dev-loud; its fixture changes both the outer controller and inner write, so it misses this split-envelope case. No live Bead owns the residual authority gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- Benign supersession authenticates the superseding receipt envelope: its controller/root identity must agree with the writes it presents and with the same current owner required by the suppression path.
- Changing only a legitimate superseding receipt's outer `:root-id` to a foreign controller emits exactly one typed `:rf.error/frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch` and never mutates the current record.
- Ordinary same-root A-to-B supersession remains silent, B remains authoritative, and disjoint old writes still abort normally.
- Foreign inner writes, missing/pruned records, reincarnation, uncovered revisions, and stale/non-supersession settlement remain dev-loud with no authority mutation.
- Keep the public API and single receipt/record ledger unchanged; add the smallest exact cross-host fixture rather than another authority subsystem.
- Focused UI JVM, node, and existing browser supersession gates remain green.

title: Make the Machines tutorial and executable companion one copy-pasteable program
description:
PR #6055 corrected the Machines tutorial to a three-total-attempt lockout policy and advertised it as copy-pasteable, but the complete teaching program still splits into incompatible and non-compiling copies.

First, `docs/machines/tutorial.md` Step 5 dereferences `draft-creds` in the Sign-in callback without defining it anywhere. Isolated compilation reports `Unable to resolve symbol: draft-creds in this context`, so the promised view cannot be copied into a real app.

Second, the linked executable companion says its `login-flow` is the same value lifted from the chapter, yet `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc` still guards with `< attempts 3`, locks on the fourth submit, and its terminal branch runs only `:lock-account` rather than recording the final error. Its README/browser prose and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj` explicitly pin that fourth-attempt behavior. `docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md` likewise calls its `< 3` table the tutorial value. The #6055 docs test block is not version-executed, so the green executable test protects the contradictory program instead of the corrected tutorial.

This is the residual of closed `rf2-099755`, whose acceptance required the third failure and timeout to be executable-gated with the final count/error retained. Keep one small canonical teaching program and one focused existing example test; do not build a general docs code-block runner.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tutorial defines or explicitly accepts every value its view uses, including credential draft state; the complete namespace/view compiles and can be copied without an unresolved symbol.
- Tutorial, inspecting guide, executable walkthrough, README/browser prose, and CI test all use the same three-total-attempt policy.
- The third failure records count 3 and the terminal error before entering `:locked-out`; the third timeout follows the same counted policy and records its message.
- The runnable `.cljc` companion is the actual table exercised by the focused JVM/CLJS tests; no separate hand-copied policy remains falsely green.
- Happy-path submit/effect/session behavior and the low-friction tutorial progression remain intact.
- Focused Machines/example/docs gates pass.

title: Finish the cross-handbook compatibility-anchor contract
description:
PR #6055 closed `rf2-t0ituo` after restoring and gating only the Machines subset, although that source Bead's final acceptance explicitly required one shared compatibility-anchor mechanism across Machines, Async, API, and Routing. Current main still lacks all 14 non-Machines targets:

- Async: `docs/async/examples.md#async-http-examples`; `docs/async/http.md#managed-http-reference`, `#setup`; `docs/async/index.md#in-this-section`.
- API: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md#with-frame--with-new-frame`.
- Routing: `docs/routing/concepts.md#carrying-global-state-through-the-url`, `#converting-routes--urls-by-hand`, `#navigate-in-place-change-the-query-stay-on-the-route`, `#navigating-to-a-raw-url-string`, `#routing-the-url-is-a-sub`, `#what-happens-in-order`, `#when-a-loader-fails`; `docs/routing/examples.md#routing-examples`; `docs/routing/index.md#in-this-section`.

A current-main slug-index probe reports all 14 absent while `check_doc_slugs.py` stays green because its manifest and source-comment scan are hard-coded to Machines. The new `_check_machines_compat_anchors` also skips a missing inventoried page, so deleting/renaming a listed page plus updating ordinary links makes every external bookmark disappear without failing the gate.

Complete the already-chosen small inventory mechanism; do not introduce a new documentation framework or duplicate visible headings. No open/in-progress Bead owns the unfinished closed-source acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- Restore every listed Async, API, and Routing fragment as an invisible stable compatibility anchor on its intended page, alongside the existing 20 Machines anchors.
- Replace the Machines-only manifest/check naming and path restriction with one bounded cross-handbook inventory covering all source-Bead targets.
- A listed page that is missing or renamed fails the compatibility check; fixture self-tests remain isolated through explicit fixture inputs rather than silently ignoring absent production pages.
- Relevant source-comment links across the covered handbooks are validated by the same mechanism without duplicating visible headings.
- Teeth tests prove deleting an individual anchor and deleting an inventoried page both fail.
- `check_doc_slugs.py`, its self-tests, and MkDocs strict build pass aside from independently owned unrelated baseline failures.

title: Make registration sequestering provenance-safe and truly no-op when absent
description:
PR #6056 corrected the API example to call `sequester-app-registration!` with registrar kind `:route`, but auditing the documented no-op contract exposed a runtime provenance bug in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`.

`sequester-app-registration!` first looks up `[kind id provenance-ns]` in the source store, then unconditionally removes `(kind,id)` from the live registrar even when that provenance row is absent. On current main, registering `:audit/same` for `"app.b"` and sequestering the same kind/id for `"missing.app"` produces:
`{:returned nil, :registrar-after nil, :source-after <app.b descriptor>}`.

The call therefore returns nil yet clobbers another namespace's live registration while leaving its source-store row behind. This contradicts the API promise that a mismatched/absent row leaves registration unchanged and can make co-loaded test suites observe missing handlers or registrar/source-store divergence.

Closed `rf2-kcd05e` corrected only the documented kind/lease claims and explicitly requested a focused capture/removal test; no live Bead owns this behavior. Keep the repair at the existing helper rather than adding new isolation machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- An absent `(kind,id,provenance-ns)` row returns nil and changes neither the live registrar nor the source store.
- A requested namespace cannot remove a live `(kind,id)` owned by a sibling provenance namespace; registrar and source-store authority remain coherent.
- A present matching row is captured, removed from both stores, returned, and reinstated by `reinstate-app-registration!` exactly once.
- Focused rows cover correct `:route` capture/removal/reinstatement, mismatched kind, absent provenance, and same-id sibling provenance.
- Existing namespace-tree sequester/reinstate and CLJ/CLJS test-support suites remain green.
close_reason: shipped #6160 (merged)

title: Finish SSR hydration, head-hash, and streaming truth reconciliation
description:
PR #6052 corrected three canonical SSR guides but left the same superseded contracts in sibling/canonical truth surfaces, and introduced two new copyability contradictions.

Current origin/main 0f2fc095321831ba1d30d8e7cbe0706784a8c2ae:
- docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:20 maps React hydrateRoot directly to state-only ssr/hydrate!; line 52 says hydrate! adopts DOM; line 64 promises automatic SPA head updates and the body's mismatch detector; line 70 promises inert-template fallbacks in the first painted byte.
- docs/ssr/streaming.md:68-70 says a non-JS client waits for the final payload and then hydrate! renders everything. Without JS, templates/chunks/payload remain inert and hydration never runs. A JS client that omits progressive installation is the case that may hydrate after the final payload.
- docs/ssr/head.md:57-59 tells a host to compare the active-head model map directly with the :rf/head-hash string. The host must compare (rf/render-tree-hash (rf/active-head frame-id)) with that hash.
- spec/011-SSR.md:673, 698, and 700 still say the client compares the head and replaces it, contradicting the same section's shipped-status text that the bundled runtime only carries/stashes the head hash and host attribution/reconciliation is external.
- spec/conformance/README.md:498 and spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-head-emits.edn:53-57 still describe the reverted unified body+head render hash and reserve the already-shipped separate head hash for post-v1.

These are one bounded documentation-truth cluster completing closed rf2-fzza7u, rf2-ttiv2i, and rf2-bgbght acceptance. No live Bead owns it. Correct prose and one narrow drift assertion are sufficient; do not build a head manager, no-JS streaming runtime, or new compatibility layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hydration prose consistently distinguishes ssr/hydrate! state installation/hash verification from substrate hydrateRoot DOM adoption; the Next.js mapping names both halves.
- Head prose consistently says body/head hashes are separate, the bundled runtime does no automatic head comparison/reconciliation, and a copyable host comparison hashes active-head before comparing with :rf/head-hash.
- Streaming prose distinguishes a JS client that skips streaming-install! from a non-JS client; it never claims non-JS can hydrate or paint inert boundary templates.
- Spec 011 default flow and mismatch section no longer claim bundled client head comparison/replacement while preserving the shipped optional head-hash channel and host-owned seam.
- The conformance index and fixture comments describe the current body-only :rf/render-hash plus separate optional :rf/head-hash, matching the fixture/runtime.
- Add the smallest focused truth/drift check needed to keep these canonical surfaces aligned; doc slugs and mkdocs --strict pass.
close_reason: shipped #6158 (merged): SSR contract reconcile

title: Correct Resources landing lease cleanup and mutation invalidation guidance
description:
PR #6050 corrected the Resources landing/concepts pages but introduced two copyable contract errors that remain on current main.

1. `docs/resources/index.md` now demonstrates `:rf.resource/ensure` with `:owner [:lease :article "hello"]` but never dispatches the matching `:rf.resource/release-owner`. Event-minted owners are durable liveness leases: the entry retains that owner in `:active-owners` and the reverse owner index, so normal stale/GC collection cannot reclaim it. The tutorial itself correctly warns that forgetting release is an orphaned-owner leak. The first landing example should not teach a permanently pinned cache entry.

2. `docs/resources/concepts.md` says final invalidation covers tags “the patch/populate did not already freshen.” Runtime `mutation_events.cljc` passes only `populated-ks` as the same-mutation exemption set, matching Spec 016's populate-only `:refetch-populated?` rule. A patched key is not exempt: the same mutation's invalidation may immediately mark it stale/refetch it. The page therefore overstates patch semantics precisely where it is teaching fixed arm order.

No later edit repairs either page, and no open/in-progress Bead owns these residuals. Closed `rf2-5gj77s`/PR #6050 is the incomplete source.
acceptance_criteria: The landing example either uses an ownerless one-shot ensure or shows the matching `:rf.resource/release-owner` at the consumer lifecycle boundary, with concise prose explaining event-minted lease ownership. The concepts page states the exact success order and accurately explains that only same-mutation populated keys are exempt from invalidation by default; patched keys can still be invalidated/refetched. Keep the example low-friction and copyable, preserve the passive-read/explicit-cause lesson, and pass documentation link/slug/build checks.
close_reason: shipped #6154 (merged, --admin: only-fail was inherited NAMING.md docs gate, 0 spec/003 touch, fixed on main by q75nc #6155)

title: Keep Xray bulk registration retryable after a partial install failure
description:
PR #6046 publishes `registered?` true at registry.cljs:186 before the roughly 900-line bulk registration/leaf-install block, while `installed-schema` is stamped only after the last installer at line 1079. If any registrar or leaf installer throws, the call exits with `{registered? true, installed-schema nil}`. On the next reload/call, the umbrella permanently skips the unfinished bulk install; the nil stamp is interpreted as schema 0, so migrate-schema! installs only the ViewCell bridge and then stamps schema 1. Every handler after the original failure point remains absent while the registry now claims to be current.

The initial error is correctly loud, but a transient install/programming failure followed by an HMR fix falsely succeeds into a silent partial Xray registry until a page reload. This is separate from schema deltas for changed handlers: it is failure atomicity of the fresh-install transition. Migration failures already leave the schema unstamped because the reset follows migrate-schema!.

Make the fresh-install sentinel retryable: use an explicit installing/installed state or catch bulk-install failure, roll the boolean back to false, and rethrow; publish registered/current only after every installer succeeds. Partial registrar writes can safely be replaced on retry. Add a throw-once mid-list leaf fixture proving the schema is not advanced after failure and a second call completes later handlers/topology instead of running bridge-only migration.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh bulk-install exception leaves registration retryable and schema unstamped; a second call replays/completes all leaf installers and reaches one coherent current schema; a throw-once regression proves no silent partial registry.
close_reason: shipped #6161 (merged)

title: Retire the captured failed-root reporter across re-entrant reclaim
description:
In PR #6048's same-drain recovery branch, client/drain-live-roots! proves the snapshot root exact, calls reclaim-consumed-container!, then retires reporter authority by re-reading the mutable live-roots registry with `(root-incarnation-of root-id)`. The sibling pre-existing-quarantine branch correctly uses the captured `(:root-incarnation current)` instead.

Container reclaim executes synchronous host code (`replaceChildren`), so a custom-element callback or the documented low-level/test seams can replace failed root A with same-id successor B during reclaim. The subsequent bare-id lookup returns B: retire-root-reporter! removes B from live-reporters, while release-root! root-id A correctly identity-fences and preserves B's live claim. B is then live without reporter authority, so its teardown may settle synchronously before React's cleanup; A's reporter token also remains strongly retained. This contradicts drain-live-roots!'s stated stale-snapshot rule that a bypass-installed replacement is not owned.

Use the exact incarnation captured in `current`, as the first recovery branch already does, and preferably share the reclaim → captured-token retirement → identity-fenced release sequence. Add a deterministic fixture whose replaceChildren callback installs and commits B, proving A is retired, B stays reporter-live, and B's claim survives.
acceptance_criteria: A same-id successor installed synchronously during container reclaim keeps its reporter authority and live-root claim; the failed predecessor's reporter is retired; recovery uses only the exact captured incarnation and is regression-tested.
close_reason: shipped #6151: reclaim captured-token reporter retirement

title: Migrate changed Xray handlers, not only newly added registrations
description:
PR #6046 introduces a registration schema seam, but its contract and migrate-schema! cover only newly added handlers. The same registered? umbrella also prevents changed handler implementations/topologies inside panel install! functions from being re-registered, so replacements require migration just as additions do.

Current main already demonstrates the gap. Commit f012c70e6f changed :rf.xray/reactive-data from two static inputs to four (adding :rf.xray/reactive-show-unchanged? and the Settings pin) inside reactive-panel-subs/install!, after #6046 shipped. registry/schema-version is still 1, and migrate-schema! only runs the `from < 1` ViewCell bridge clause. An already-running schema-1 process re-running register-xray-handlers! therefore no-ops both the umbrella and migration gates and retains the old two-input reaction body/topology. The newly shipped unchanged-sub disclosure does not respond to its panel or Settings axes until a full page reload.

Treat any gated registration addition OR replacement as a schema delta. Add the smallest version-2 migration that re-registers the changed Reactive-data surface (through its owning facade/seam), update the contract wording, and add a fixture that poses a schema-1 process with the predecessor two-input handler then proves current registration replaces it and invalidates the held cache. A lightweight governance test/check should make future gated registration edits name a schema bump or an explicit no-migration rationale.
acceptance_criteria: A live schema-1 process upgrades :rf.xray/reactive-data to the current four-input topology without a page reload; held cached subscriptions are invalidated; the registry schema contract covers handler additions and replacements with regression/governance proof.
close_reason: shipped #6161 (merged)

title: Reconcile flow single-store documentation and destroy conformance
description: PR #6045 correctly made `{frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}` the sole flow store and made replacement suppression per `(frame-id, flow-id)`, but active documentation and an executable conformance fixture still assert the retired frame-blind registrar model. `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/Managed-Effects.md`, `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md`, `late_bind/directory.cljc`, and `frame.cljc` describe flow registrar ownership/re-pointing or registrar queries. `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-frame-destroy-teardown.edn` normatively expects `:registrar-flow-slots-after #{:area}`, although the `:flow` registrar slot is reserved-empty. Spec 009 also states the process-global `(kind,id)` dedup rule without the flow exception. This contradicts authoritative Spec 013 and can make implementations/tests conform to two incompatible architectures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sweep active specs, runtime architecture prose, late-bind descriptions, and source comments to state the sole per-frame flow store and `flows-snapshot`/`flow-meta-at` introspection contract.
- The destroy conformance fixture asserts the `:flow` registrar remains empty before/after teardown while per-frame flow and dirty-input rows are released correctly.
- Spec 009 explicitly scopes generic process-global dedup to registrar-backed kinds and documents flow replacement evidence as the per-frame exception.
- Search/conformance gates fail if retired flow registrar ownership/re-pointing language or nonempty flow registrar expectations return.
- No runtime behavior change or new parallel store is introduced.
close_reason: shipped #6208 (merged)

title: Keep nil owned spread-safe props absent and host-parity preserving
description: CLJS always materializes owned dynamic props in an object, including values normalized to nil, then `Object.assign`s that object over caller props. JVM `tree/element` drops nil owned `:norm`/`:dyn` values before layering caller props. Thus `(ui/spread-safe {:class owned-class} caller)` with `owned-class=nil` erases caller `className` on CLJS but preserves caller `:class` on JVM. The same divergence affects ordinary dynamic owned attrs such as `:title`. Reproduced from the emitted forms plus runtime merge: JVM tree produced `{:attrs {:class "caller"}}`; the CLJS merge produced `{className: null}`. This violates nil-means-absent normalization and host parity; class also fails its special composition contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Nil-normalized owned dynamic props are absent before layering, on both hosts.
- A caller value survives when the corresponding owned dynamic value is nil; a nonnil owned value wins, and nonnil class values compose owned-first.
- Fix is shared/general for dynamic owned props rather than a class-only patch.
- Paired JVM-tree and CLJS-render tests cover dynamic `:class` and an ordinary attr (for example `:title`) at nil and nonnil controls.
- Existing static, event, style, custom-element, and controlled-input safe-spread behavior remains green.
close_reason: shipped #6209 (merged)

title: Preserve one authored evaluation order for spread-safe on CLJS and JVM
description: The authored form `(ui/spread-safe owned caller)` has divergent evaluation order. CLJS emits `spread-safe-props` with the caller object as its first argument, so it evaluates/guards caller before evaluating owned prop expressions. The JVM emitter evaluates the owned `:norm`/`:dyn`/event slots before its later `:spread-safe :caller` slot. title: Make destroyed-reason conformance fail closed on unresolved source and schema shapes
description:
The destroyed-reason conformance gate advertises exact, fails-closed channel/reason authority, but three unsupported shapes remain false-green.

1. Source census: `reason-key-values` extracts `:reason` only from literal maps. `enumerate-emit-sites` records an empty `:reasons` vector for `(assoc ... :reason :bogus)` or a local payload, and the validators merely `doseq` that vector. For `emit-destroyed!`, zero extracted reasons are treated as the `:explicit` default without proving the argument is a supported literal map that omits `:reason`. A direct in-memory reproduction against the exact helper returns `[:bogus]` for `{:reason :bogus}` but `[]` for both unsupported forms; existing literal sites still satisfy final set equality.

2. Host coverage: `read-source-forms` calls the conditional reader once with its default JVM feature view. A different reason under a `#?(:cljs ...)` emitter branch is never inspected. The same source can therefore be valid on CLJ and publish an undocumented reason on CLJS while the JVM-only structural gate stays green.

3. Spec-Schemas lifecycle row: the gate uses substring checks for the tags token and sole-reason sentence, then excludes only already-known competing reasons. Appending ``or `:bogus``` to the current ```:reason` is always `:parent-frame-destroyed` ``` sentence leaves the required prefix true, the tags substring true, and the known-other intersection empty. The normative row can therefore admit an unknown extra reason while its claimed exact check remains green.

Closed P2 `rf2-9q1zn2` explicitly required unparsed/dynamic emit reasons and extra Spec-Schemas reasons to fail; this is the current follow-up for those unsatisfied closure criteria. Keep the correction in the test authority: explicit parsing/failure, no runtime compatibility layer or speculative reason vocabulary.

- The structural census evaluates both CLJ and CLJS reader-conditional views; a reason that differs only in a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch fails.
- The lifecycle Spec-Schemas row is parsed with anchored captures for its exact tags reason slot and exact sole-reason statement; any additional unknown alternative fails.
- Mutation fixtures using `(assoc ... :reason :bogus)`, a local-symbol payload, a CLJS-only bogus reason, and an appended Spec-Schemas ``or `:bogus``` all fail; current literal/default/forwarding sites and the four ruled tuples stay green.
- No new public reason, runtime validation layer, or compatibility branch is introduced.

title: Make the frame-lifecycle preflight guard genuinely per-path
description:
## Current defect

#6033 describes the frame-lifecycle guard as causal per host path, but `_client_call_order` is a whole-file substring scan and `_preflight_causal_problems` pools textual preflight credit across function boundaries. Current-main probes leave the checker green when the `render!*` preflight is reader-discarded (`#_`) or wrapped in `(when false ...)`; moving that token into `create-root*` and removing the real `render!*` call can also preserve the expected global token sequence while `render!*` reaches `.render` without preflight. The self-tests remove/reorder tokens but do not exercise dead calls or cross-function migration.

## Required correction

Prove each owned path rather than treating the file as one token stream: the two `mount*` branches, allocation-only `create-root*`, and preflight-before-render `render!*`. A small behavioral seam is preferred if it stays bounded; otherwise scope the lexical checks to the actual function bodies and state their limits honestly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing-root refresh and fresh one-shot mount independently prove preflight before their render; fresh mount additionally proves preflight before createRoot.
- `create-root*` remains allocation-only by design, and cannot donate a preflight token to `render!*`; `render!*` independently proves preflight before every render.
- Reader-discarded, dead-conditional, and cross-function-moved preflight counterexamples all make the focused guard/self-test fail.
- The live guard and self-test pass on current source, while documentation no longer overclaims beyond the mechanism actually proved.
close_reason: shipped #6135 (merged): preflight guard per-path

title: Make ui/slot arity exact and host-identical
description:
## Current defect

#6032 declares `ui/render-fn` a fixed-arity callback, but `analyze-slot` never compares slot argument count with an inline render-fn parameter vector and neither runtime carrier records/validates arity. `(ui/slot (ui/render-fn [x] [:span x]) 1 2)` therefore diverges by host: JavaScript invokes the one-argument function and silently ignores the surplus argument, while the JVM emitter invokes the Clojure fn and throws `ArityException`. Too-few calls are likewise left to host behavior instead of the compiler-owned seam.

## Required correction

Make the compiler-owned slot boundary enforce one host-independent arity contract. Reject statically knowable inline mismatches during analysis; carry expected arity for prop-carried render-fns and fail didactically before invocation on both CLJS and JVM.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inline render-fn calls with too few or too many slot args fail at compile time with one didactic slot/render-fn arity diagnostic.
- Prop-carried render-fns carry expected arity and validate it before invoking on both CLJS and JVM; neither host relies on native function-call quirks.
- Correct-arity zero- and multi-argument slots retain current output, nil behavior, manifest evidence, and client/JVM parity.
- Too-few and too-many parity fixtures prove identical category/message data on both hosts, with a mutation control that makes the gate red.
