title: Make SSR emitter replay routed, failure-atomic, and precedence-safe
description:
PR #6028 added install-time replay of the retained SSR hiccup emitter. The happy path works, but the lifecycle transaction is neither failure-atomic nor cleanly routed, and its precedence/load-order contract is incomplete.

Current `install-adapter!` seats the new generation, then invokes `rearm-hiccup-emitter!`. The replay calls the global `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` broadcast chain, whose documented semantics propagate a step exception and stop later steps. A throwing setter for any loaded adapter can therefore make `rf/init!` throw after the target generation is already installed. Reproduced on current main: the first `rf/init!` threw `replay failed`, `rf/current-adapter` still returned `:rf.adapter/plain-atom`, and a second `rf/init!` returned success because it skipped the already-seated install. The process has reported failed boot but behaves as installed/partially armed.

The broadcast also re-arms every loaded adapter cell rather than only the adapter being installed. This lets an inactive setter break the active adapter's boot and muddies lifecycle ownership.

Precedence is surprising for the public direct seam. Adapter docs say `set-hiccup-emitter!` is last-call-wins and `nil` resets, but when `re-frame.ssr` is loaded, a pre-init explicit custom emitter/reset is silently overwritten by install replay of the retained default. Existing test-react prose explicitly acknowledges this classpath-dependent winner. Define and pin a low-friction rule: explicit direct override/reset remains authoritative; replay supplies the retained default only when the freshly installed generation is otherwise unarmed.

Finally, closed source bead `rf2-vxgfnd.204` required both clean namespace load orders. The current lifecycle namespace statically loads both namespaces in one compiled process and therefore proves only one selected order. Existing chain tests prove fan-out, not public `re-frame.ui` destroy/re-init in both isolated orders.
acceptance_criteria:
- Installing an adapter plus replaying its retained default is one failure-atomic transaction: any replay failure leaves no generation installed, preserves the replay exception as primary, performs bounded exact-generation cleanup, and permits an immediate clean retry.
- Replay targets only the adapter/generation being installed; a loaded inactive adapter's throwing setter cannot break the active adapter's boot.
- Public direct `set-hiccup-emitter!` precedence is explicit and consistent across re-frame.ui/Reagent/UIx/Helix/test-react: a custom override or explicit nil reset is not silently undone by default replay; default replay arms only an otherwise-unarmed fresh generation.
- Fault-injection tests cover active and inactive throwing setters, exact cleanup, current-adapter state after failure, and successful retry.
- Contract tests under an SSR-loaded classpath prove custom override/reset precedence.
- Two isolated CLJS entrypoints or fresh Node processes run the same public init/render/destroy/reinit assertion in opposite orders: SSR-before-ui and ui-before-SSR.
- Repeated generations still do not accumulate callbacks or let stale cleanup clear a replacement.
close_reason: shipped #6137 (merged): SSR emitter install-replay failure-atomic (exact-gen rollback) + routed via late-bind arm-hook + precedence-safe; frozen 10-fn adapter contract preserved

title: Complete ui/event warning evidence and controlled-input recovery guidance
description:
PR #6027 widened the controlled-input synchronous door to compiler-owned `ui/event`, but three adjacent current contracts remain incomplete.

1. Invocation-time warning arms are uncatalogued and unproved. `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/events.cljs` classifies a vector returned by `ui/event` and calls both `warn-dynamic-placeholder!` and `warn-unregistered!` when the committed callback fires. Spec 009 still describes `:rf.warning/unregistered-event-id` as render-time literal/data/dynamic-handler evidence and `:rf.warning/placeholder-in-dynamic-vector` as render-time `dynamic-handler` evidence only. The focused warning fixture exercises only the runtime-classified render path, not a committed `event-handler` result.

2. The unregistered lookup is generation-blind. `warn-unregistered!` calls bare `registrar/lookup`, which reads the process registrar when no frame generation is bound. Actual dispatch resolves through the committed frame's sealed image generation. After registration/image evolution this can warn falsely for an event present in the committed frame or suppress a valid warning when only the process-current table contains it.

3. The controlled-input fallback warning still says the handler is not a literal data event and prescribes only a literal vector, even though the accepted door is now `#{:vector :ui-event}`. For reusable controls needing the native payload, a literal vector may not express the intended fix; the diagnostic should name both valid forms.

This is one bounded ergonomics/evidence correction around the #6027 widening, not new handler machinery. Open G-8/G-15 production/browser work remains owned by `rf2-vxgfnd.95.10` and is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009 rows for `:rf.warning/unregistered-event-id` and `:rf.warning/placeholder-in-dynamic-vector` describe both render-time dynamic/data paths and invocation-time `ui/event` result paths, with exact timing/evidence.
- A committed-owner/event-handler fixture returns an unregistered vector containing a placeholder, invokes the stable callback, asserts both exact warning envelopes, and proves the unchanged vector dispatches as ordinary data.
- Registration existence is resolved through the committed/captured frame's exact image generation. A two-frame/generation fixture proves both mismatch directions: present only in the frame image does not warn; present only process-current but absent from the frame image does warn.
- The controlled-input async fallback message recommends a literal event vector or `ui/event` as appropriate, and a focused message assertion prevents regression.
- Dev-only/advanced-elision behavior and existing open G-8/G-15 ownership remain unchanged.

title: Reconcile shipped S3 local and internal fn-prop contracts across active authorities
description:
## Confirmed current gap

The component-library readiness amendment and shipped S3 implementation now define two contracts that active authorities still contradict:

1. `local` ships `[value set! update!]`, with `update!` applying to latest host state, but live `spec/004-Views.md` still specifies `[value set!]`. The readiness draft explicitly promised this live-spec update atomically with `.95.2`, which is closed.
2. C-13a and merged `.95.3` make ordinary function props between internal views legal opaque identity-compared values, but live Spec 004's narrow-fn prose does not state that exception and the synthesis skill says internal-view fn props are compile errors.

The canonical migrator table also contradicts both contracts (MIG-27 rewrites/gates every internal fn prop; the historical setter recipe can recreate stale last-write-wins). `rf2-vxgfnd.188` owns canonical migrator reconciliation and is amended separately; do not create a second rulebook here.

## Deliverable

Before `.95.4` proceeds into the same Spec/compiler hot zone, make the live normative Spec 004 and current authoring/skill authorities state the shipped contracts exactly. Preserve the important distinctions: internal fn props are opaque values with no promised invocation phase; `ui/handler`/`ui/render-fn` opt into a phase; foreign bare fn props remain errors; native event bare-fn shorthand stays narrow. `set!` stores functions as values; only `update!` is atomic latest-state transformation.

This is authority synchronization, not a new callback form, local abstraction, or generalized documentation framework.

- Spec 004 defines `(local init) -> [value set! update!]`, exact function-valued `set!`, and latest-host-state `update!`; no active authority retains the two-tuple/stale setter recipe.

title: Reconcile Spec 004 compile diagnostics with the runtime-only Spec 009 catalogue
description:
## Current defect

PR #6020 makes Spec 004 contradict itself about diagnostic ownership. The new React-interoperability position law says `:rf.ui.compile/*` diagnostics join the compiler roster and deliberately have no Spec 009 catalogue rows because only runtime-tier ids are catalogued. Later in the same document, §One catalogue says every error/warning id the Spec names, including the compile-error roster, gets or will get a Spec 009 row.

The earlier `rf2-gsa6i3` punch-list softened timing language but did not narrow the catalogue's domain, so #6020's explicit compile-time rule now conflicts locally with that paragraph. An implementer cannot tell whether S3 must add forbidden 009 rows or violate the one-catalogue statement.

State one consistent ownership rule: Spec 009 catalogues runtime diagnostic/error/warning ids; compiler-only `:rf.ui.compile/*` ids live in the maintained compiler roster/prose and do not get 009 rows. Keep the useful one-catalogue rule for its actual runtime domain.

title: Keep custom-element reload success honest when publication observers throw
description:
## Confirmed current failure

`commit-reload!` atomically reconciles/closes `ledger-state` and then calls `publish!`. `publish!` performs a bare `swap!` on the public `custom-elements` atom, which synchronously invokes its watches with no containment.

A throwing watch therefore escapes **after** the new ledger and aggregate are already authoritative:

```clojure
(add-watch custom-elements ::boom
  (fn [& _] (throw (ex-info "watch exploded" {}))))
(commit-reload! :app)
```

The independent correctness repro observed the exception propagate while the new aggregate was live and `:cycles` was empty. Shadow can interpret the after-load hook as failed even though the framework committed it; built-in watch fan-out can also skip later observers. This falsifies the reload outcome and risks partially notified DEV/tool consumers.

The repository already fixed the analogous descriptor-HMR problem in closed `rf2-vxgfnd.215`: authority commit and observer delivery need distinct failure semantics. That Bead does not cover this custom-element aggregate.

## Deliverable

Make the post-commit publication boundary honest. If arbitrary watches are intentionally supported, snapshot and isolate delivery. If they are only a test artefact, make the atom private and route the narrowly required framework observers through an explicit contained DEV path. In either design, a listener failure is diagnosable but cannot retroactively turn committed authority into a failed reload.

Do not attempt rollback after commit, add a general event bus, or carry listener machinery into production.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological correctness audit of PR #6018. All-status search found closed `.215` as an analogous owner but no live custom-element publication issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- A publication observer failure after ledger reconciliation cannot make `commit-reload!`/Shadow report the successful authority transition as failed or roll it back.
- The live aggregate, projected ledger, and cycle state remain coherent and quiescent after such a failure.
- Every framework-owned observer in the publication snapshot is attempted exactly once regardless of sibling failure; arbitrary atom watches are either explicitly unsupported behind a private state var or receive equivalent isolated semantics.
- The first/aggregate observer failure is surfaced through one bounded DEV diagnostic carrying build/cycle/publication context after delivery, without truthiness bugs for falsey thrown values where representable.
- Reentrant registration/publication still preserves the newer winner and does not duplicate delivery.
- A fail-before fixture installs a throwing observer before good observers and proves current code propagates/skips; restoring bare uncontained publication makes the repaired fixture fail.
- No public event system, production listener machinery, rollback-after-commit, or per-render work is introduced.
notes:
PR #6409. Delivered in full, with one deliberate deviation reported rather than faked.

Observers THROW here (not the silent no-op rf2-1b0po found): publish! swap!s the public custom-elements atom, whose watch fan-out is synchronous and uncontained, so the throw escaped commit-reload! into shadow's ^:dev/after-load and reported a committed reload as failed. publish! now contains the fan-out and reports one bounded DEV diagnostic, mirroring reactive.cljc's report-hmr-listener-escape! (rf2-vxgfnd.215). Containment is sound because both hosts set the atom's value BEFORE notifying watches, so the aggregate/ledger/cycle state survive a contained failure unchanged. Failure identity rides an explicit :failed? bit, so (throw nil)/(throw false) are not silently dropped.

DEVIATION from AC3: isolated SIBLING delivery is not implemented. Watch fan-out belongs to the host IAtom, which abandons remaining watches on a throw; replacing it means a listener framework with no consumer — there are ZERO framework-owned observers of custom-elements (classification reads custom-element-properties; the only add-watch in the corpus is a test fixture). Arbitrary watches are documented as explicitly unsupported observers: contained and diagnosed, delivery completeness left to the host. The atom was NOT made private: the rf2-vxgfnd.144 reentrancy proof legitimately needs to observe publication, and CLJS privacy would not stop a throw anyway — it would be a nominal guarantee, not a real one.

SCOPE: dev-only. Grep-verified in a pseudo-named :advanced bundle — publish_BANG_ and report_publication_escape absent from the re_frame$ui$rules$* surface. Dev-tooling correctness, not a production guarantee.

title: Give custom-element reload commits explicit cycle ownership
description:
## Confirmed contract hole

PR #6018 correctly moved source state and open-cycle staging into one atom for the concrete register-vs-commit race, but it did not give a reload cycle its own identity:

```clojure
:cycles {build-id {:staged ... :touched ...}}
```

`notify-reload!` blindly replaces `[:cycles build-id]`, while `commit-reload!` identifies the thing to close by `build-id` alone. With overlapping same-build activations:

1. cycle N opens/stages;
2. cycle N+1 opens and replaces that row/stages;
3. N's delayed after-load calls `commit-reload! build-id`;
4. it reconciles and closes N+1; N+1's own completion later has nothing to commit.

There is no generation/token that could distinguish the callers, despite the implementation describing a “generation rule.” This is exactly the overlapping-cycle interleaving that closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.144` required.

## Proof gap

The new JVM tests cover register-vs-commit, register-vs-notify, and distinct-build write-throughs. They never race notify against commit or model two same-build cycles. The register-vs-notify test also declines to assert the raced element after settlement, although both legal serial orders retain it; the independent audit ran that stronger assertion for 500 rounds with no current implementation loss, showing it is a cheap useful contract assertion.

## Deliverable

First pin the actual Shadow loader scheduling contract with a real integration fixture. If same-build activations can overlap, carry explicit cycle ownership through the lifecycle. If Shadow is strictly synchronous/single-flight, enforce that boundary fail-closed and retire the broader overlap claim instead of adding unused machinery. In either case, a stale completion must never act on a newer cycle.

Do not solve this with timing sleeps, a process-global lock around user callbacks, or an unowned retry loop.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological completeness/quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only closed `rf2-vxgfnd.144`; no live issue owns cycle identity/overlap proof.
acceptance_criteria:
- A commit can reconcile/close only the reload cycle that opened it; a delayed completion from cycle N cannot consume or close cycle N+1.
- Registrations and touched-source evidence are assigned to one documented live generation and are never lost, doubled, or left in an orphan row under overlapping scheduling.
- Either actual cycle identity is threaded through begin/stage/commit, or the real Shadow integration enforces and proves a strict single-flight rule that rejects/serializes a second open without replacing live staging.
- Deterministic tests cover notify-vs-commit and two overlapping same-build cycles, plus both legal register-vs-notify serializations; the raced registration is present exactly once after settlement.
- A mutation removing cycle ownership/enforcement makes the overlap proof fail.
- Failed cycles preserve last-known-good state and successful cycles publish only coherent aggregates.
- No sleeps, broad callback lock, unbounded retry, second ledger, public API, or per-render cost is introduced.
notes:
PR #6409. PARTIAL DELIVERY — needs an operator ruling on the remainder.

DELIVERED: notify-reload! no longer supersedes a live cycle silently (bounded DEV diagnostic naming the discarded staged/touched evidence, gated on what was LOST rather than on cycle-key presence); the overlap/ownership overclaim retired in prose; the bead's stated proof gap closed with a notify-vs-commit barrier race (400 rounds), a deterministic two-cycle overlap fixture, the strengthened register-vs-notify settlement assertion, and positive+negative diagnosis fixtures.

NOT DELIVERED — architecturally blocked, same class as escalated sibling rf2-vxgfnd.143. AC1 ('a delayed completion from cycle N cannot consume or close cycle N+1') and the arm-1 reading of AC3 ('actual cycle identity threaded through begin/stage/commit') cannot be implemented at shadow's real seam. Evidence read off the pinned shadow-cljs client (shadow.cljs.devtools.client.{browser,shared,env}):
  1. NO CONVEYANCE — lifecycle hooks are resolved by name off $CLJS and invoked with NO arguments, so a ^:dev/after-load invocation is anonymous and cannot present a claim minted by its own before-load. Any token would be minted AND checked inside the ledger, where commit-reload! could only compare it against the live slot it already reads — a tautology wearing an identity check's clothes.
  2. NO PAIRING — do-js-reload* abandons the remaining task chain on a throw, so a failed load never runs ^:dev/after-load. That also kills every depth/refcount scheme: one aborted reload pins the count above zero and hot reload silently stops committing forever.
Shadow has no single-flight guard of its own; what serializes cycles is JS itself, and only while every lifecycle hook is synchronous. An ^:dev/*-async hook anywhere in the build reintroduces overlap that this ledger cannot repair.

SCOPE NOTE: all of this machinery is dev-only. Grep-verified in a pseudo-named :advanced bundle — no commit_reload/notify_reload/publish_BANG_/ledger_state in the re_frame$ui$rules$* surface. Dev-tooling correctness, not a production guarantee.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:54 AUSEST)

Seam finding ACCEPTED. RETIRED: AC1, both arms of AC3 as written, and the overlapping-scheduling clauses of AC2 ("never lost ... under overlapping scheduling") and AC5 (the overlap-proof reading). Why, verified against the pinned shadow-cljs 3.4.10 client jar (byte-identical in 3.4.11; env.cljs unchanged in the jar since 2025-03): shadow resolves lifecycle hooks by name off $CLJS and invokes them anonymously — a sync hook gets ZERO arguments, an async hook only a continuation — so an ^:dev/after-load cannot present any identity for the cycle its before-load opened, and any token minted and checked inside our own ledger only compares against the slot it already reads (a tautology, the fake-guard class this repo rejects); and do-js-reload* abandons the task chain when a load throws, so a failed load never runs after-load — before/after are NOT a paired bracket, which kills every refcount scheme and makes reject-on-second-open wedge the ledger permanently (supersession IS the aborted-reload recovery, so AC3 arm 2's fail-closed single-flight is also unbuildable as written).

RATIFIED CONTRACT (delivered by PR #6409, merge bc0f7decd8): exactly one live cycle per build-id; a second before-load supersedes the live cycle with a loud, bounded, loss-gated diagnostic naming the discarded staged/touched evidence (silent on ordinary consecutive reloads, negative fixture pinned); overlapping same-build cycles (reachable only via ^:dev/*-async hooks, none in this repo) are UNSUPPORTED, with bounded self-healing degradation — possible stale classification rows until the next full page reload — documented in rules.cljc. AC4, AC6, AC7 and the diagnostic reading of AC5 are delivered and stand. Entire surface is dev-only: ledger is compile-time gated and grep-verified absent from :advanced bundles.

"Hold for upstream" was evaluated and REJECTED on evidence: it would require two coordinated shadow changes (hook-argument conveyance + a paired abort signal), neither of which exists or is hinted at, and the seam has not moved in over a year. Do not reopen against shadow-cljs upgrades unless the hook seam itself changes (hooks receive identity AND aborts emit a paired signal). No upstream feature-request chore unless a consumer actually reports the async-hook degradation (the diagnostic will name it). No joint disposition with rf2-vxgfnd.143 — same decision class, independent facts, ruled separately.

title: Make the reload-source producer self-upgrading across the trampoline boundary
description:
## Confirmed current failure

PR #6018's `.145` change puts the new tagged trampoline installer behind the same pre-existing `defonce` it is trying to repair:

```clojure
(defonce ^:private _reload-source-producer
  (install-reload-source-producer!))
```

A live process loaded before `.145` already has that var initialized and an **untagged raw function object** in `SHADOW_NS_RESET`. When the namespace hot-reloads to current code, ClojureScript preserves the defonce value, so `install-reload-source-producer!` never runs. The old object remains installed—the exact stale-callback state `.145` was filed to fix.

The PR's commit order exposes a second concrete live-upgrade failure. `.145` lands first and creates a trampoline capturing `::default`; `.142` then introduces `current-build-id`, but the realized defonce again prevents replacement, so that page keeps routing reset evidence to the placeholder owner.

## Why the tests miss it

`installed-producer-runs-the-current-implementation-after-a-reload` starts from a fresh bundle containing the **final** code, whose defonce has already installed a good trampoline. It then rebinds `reload-source-reset!`. That proves future redefinitions work after a clean final-code load; it does not drive legacy installed object -> new installer migration.

## Deliverable

Give producer installation an idempotent reload-time migration path with explicit ownership. It must replace/retire the exact predecessor shape and refresh the build-owned tag while leaving every foreign callback untouched. Seed the actual legacy array/sentinel shape before loading/evaluating the repaired installer so the regression is causal.

Keep this narrow: no clearing `SHADOW_NS_RESET`, no positional ownership assumptions about foreign callbacks, and no general callback registry.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological implementation-quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only the closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.145`; no live issue owns the failed upgrade boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Starting from the exact pre-.145 state (realized install sentinel plus an untagged raw `reload-source-reset!` entry), evaluating the repaired namespace makes Shadow's existing array entry execute the current implementation without a page refresh.
- The same migration refreshes an entry created by .145 before .142 so it routes through the current real build identity rather than captured `::default`.
- After migration/repeated reloads there is exactly one current re-frame.ui producer per intended build; no stale owned callback executes or accumulates.
- Shadow/foreign callbacks in the shared array are preserved byte-for-byte and in order.
- Subsequent implementation/coercion/routing changes are picked up by the installed trampoline.
- The fail-before fixture seeds the legacy installed state before loading current code; a fresh-final-code install alone is not accepted as migration proof.
- Advanced-production elision and ordinary reload behavior remain unchanged; no global callback-array reset or public API is introduced.
notes:
DELIVERED (PR #6434, 2026-07-19), with ONE deliberate AC deviation flagged for review.

PREMISE CONFIRMED: the defonce at rules.cljc ~1394 pins install-reload-source-producer!, so the installer never re-runs on a hot reload of rules.cljc — no change to the installer, the trampoline's construction, or the owner tag can reach a live page. Also confirmed the existing tests miss it exactly as the bead says: 'installed-producer-runs-...-after-a-reload' starts from final code and rebinds the var; 'producer-install-is-idempotent-...' calls the installer DIRECTLY three times, bypassing the defonce entirely — so the installer's idempotence was proven while the fact that it never RUNS was not.

FIX: install runs on EVERY load; retire-what-this-copy-owns via a defonce'd ownership cell. The defonce moved from the install (where it froze the machinery) to the ownership record (where surviving the reload is the point). It only ever existed to stop the pre-.145 .push appending duplicates — a job the owner TAG took over in .145, which is what made it both redundant and the blocker. Ownership is OBJECT IDENTITY, never tag: tag says which build an entry claims, identity says this copy installed it; they diverge in exactly the migration cases (our own entry whose tag went stale; a co-loaded bundle's entry carrying the tag we are leaving). Cell gated like ledger-state -> no prod allocation.

RED-BEFORE (CLJS, real path): drives shadow's OWN build-id carrier (the object graph current-build-id reads via shadow-build-id), not a stand-in seam. Unfixed source => 2 producers, survivor still tagged ':re-frame.ui.rules/default', array grew by 2 not 1.

DEVIATION FROM AC1 — NOT IMPLEMENTED, needs a call: migrating a PRE-.145 untagged raw reload-source-reset! entry. It is untagged, hence indistinguishable from a foreign callback by any SOUND test; the only handle is sniffing the munged CLJS fn name (.name === 're_frame$ui$rules$reload_source_reset_BANG_'), which is compiler-internal and permanent dead weight. It can only matter to a tab loaded from the ONE-COMMIT window between db31f0288d (.77) and 8c1653ad37 (.145) that then hot-reloads rather than refreshing — in-memory dev-only back-compat, which the pre-alpha stance declines. The GENERAL defect (defonce freeze) and every FUTURE upgrade across that boundary ARE fixed. If Mike wants the legacy sniffer, it is a small follow-up bead.

Elision confirmed unchanged (bead AC): test:elision 60/60, test:ui-advanced-elision 4/4, and test:browser-prod-elision runs custom_element_reload_elision_prod_test.cljs INSIDE the :advanced bundle — mounted prod elision PASS, 105 tests/414 assertions.
close_reason: shipped #6434

title: Finish real Shadow ownership and removed-source reconciliation
acceptance_criteria:
- Every emitted registration, lifecycle hook, reset callback, staged row, removal, and commit for a real dev build uses one stable build identity; no real path silently falls back to `::default`.
- A successful saved namespace delete/rename supplies the removed old owner to that exact build and evicts its runtime declarations without a page refresh; a same-namespace file move preserves ownership.
- Two genuinely co-loaded builds with equal namespace symbols are either proven isolated through real build-scoped identity, or a one-build-per-shared-runtime boundary is explicitly enforced and all synthetic multi-build claims/tests are removed.
- `note-reloaded-sources!` cannot inject a foreign `[build ns]` owner into another build's open cycle: ready-made pairs are rejected or normalized to the addressed build, and an adversarial cross-build fixture proves neither row can evict the other.
- Failed compile/evaluation keeps the last-known-good runtime ledger; a successful retry converges with a clean reload.
- One real Shadow warm-watch/file-edit fixture drives actual before-load -> source reset/evaluation -> after-load ordering without direct lifecycle/seam calls and covers zero-declaration, delete/rename, move, failure/retry, and the chosen build-topology contract.
- Removing a lifecycle annotation or the real build/source producer makes that fixture fail.
- The existing ledger is reused; no second manifest protocol, digest owner token, public API, or per-render work is introduced.
notes:
Independent correctness repro for the same build-ownership contract:

```clojure
(register-custom-element! :a-el {:properties #{:a}} 'shared.ns :a)
(register-custom-element! :b-el {:properties #{:b}} 'shared.ns :b)
(notify-reload! :a)
(note-reloaded-sources! [[:b 'shared.ns]] :a)
(commit-reload! :a)
```

Current `note-reloaded-sources!` accepts the ready-made foreign pair verbatim, so build A's cycle evicts build B's row. Normalize every source to `[build-id ns]` or reject a mismatched pair before it reaches `:touched`; preserve the ergonomic ns-only form.
PARTIAL (PR #6434, 2026-07-19). SHIPPED: the note-reloaded-sources! arm (bead NOTES repro + AC 'cannot inject a foreign [build ns] owner into another build's open cycle'). Sources are normalized to [addressed-build ns], so a cycle's reconciliation is total over its own rows. Chose NORMALIZE over REJECT (the AC allows either) deliberately: reject needs a new runtime error id -> Spec 009 catalogue row, and normalize adds no caller-facing failure mode. Verified NO caller in the corpus ever passed a ready-made pair, so the verbatim branch was unexercised ergonomics that was also the hole. Red-before on JVM: :b-el => #{} (build :b's row evicted by build :a's cycle), :a-el => #{:a} (:a's own row never reconciled) — exactly the bead repro. Green after: ui JVM 958 tests/18660 assertions, CLJS 10221/50503.

BEAD STAYS OPEN — remaining arms untouched, NOT attempted: (1) a real Shadow warm-watch/file-edit fixture driving actual before-load -> source-reset -> after-load ordering; (2) the removed/renamed saved-source graph delta projected from :build-sources into the ledger; (3) the co-loaded-build TOPOLOGY question. (3) needs a RULING, not a fix: the bead asks to either prove real isolation OR enforce one-build-per-shared-runtime and delete the synthetic multi-build tests/claims. rules.cljc lines ~805-808 already determine the FACT (two builds sharing ONE copy of the ns cannot be told apart by any mechanism shadow exposes — the hooks are a single shared singleton); what is undecided is the consequence, which has real blast radius over the explicit-build-arity tests. Worth splitting (1)+(2) into their own bead from (3).
⚠️ PARTIAL — one arm shipped in #6434, TWO REMAIN. Bead stays OPEN.

SHIPPED: the bounded determinable arm. Red-before reproduced the bead's exact repro — :b-el -> #{} (build :b's row evicted by build :a's cycle) and :a-el -> #{:a} (:a's own row never reconciled). The worker also verified a premise the bead did not state: NO CALLER IN THE CORPUS EVER PASSES A READY-MADE PAIR, so the verbatim branch was unexercised ergonomics that was also the hole. Real surface was implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc — NOT tools/builds, which my dispatch brief wrongly named (that is a LABEL on this bead, not a path).
⚠️ NOT the goog.DEBUG trap, and the reason is worth keeping: this fix DOES sit inside reload-ledger?, but the bug is UNREACHABLE in production rather than merely unguarded there — notify-reload! is a ^:dev/before-load hook shadow never installs in a release build, so no production reload cycle exists to inject into. That distinction (unreachable vs unguarded) is what separates a legitimate dev-only placement from the rf2-2hkfy / rf2-5pr75 defect shape.

REMAINING ARM 1 — ⚠️ NEEDS A RULING, NOT A FIX. The co-loaded-build TOPOLOGY question. rules.cljc already DETERMINES THE FACT: two builds sharing one copy of the namespace cannot be distinguished by anything shadow exposes. The bead asks to either (a) prove real isolation, or (b) enforce the boundary and DELETE the synthetic multi-build tests. (b) has real blast radius — it retires existing coverage — so it is an operator call.
REMAINING ARM 2 — determinable, dispatchable: the warm-watch fixture and the removed-source graph delta, both untouched.
⚠️ WORKER RECOMMENDATION, endorsed: SPLIT ARM 2 OUT into its own bead so it can ship without waiting on the topology ruling. Do that before re-dispatching.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 14:56 AUSEST)

ARM 1 RULING — option (b), scalpel version: enforce the boundary and retire the synthetic multi-build coverage. Do NOT attempt to prove real isolation (option a): Shadow's runtime seam conveys no build identity into lifecycle hooks or SHADOW_NS_RESET callbacks (verified in rules.cljc "Bounded by shadow's reload surface", ~lines 796-808), and the topology those tests simulate — two dev builds fused onto one $CLJS — is a broken realm below the custom-element layer (shared cljs.core, shared registrar, defonce collisions) that Shadow itself does not support.

THE BOUNDARY (normative wording, per the Codex refinement): "One Shadow dev build per CLJS global namespace root containing re-frame.ui.rules." NOT "one build per page" or "one bundle per page" — separate output files are not automatically separate runtime copies (standard Shadow dev output shares the global root; single-module release output is wrapped by default). Supported and isolated by construction: one app plus :preloads tools (one build), iframes/workers (separate realms), independently compiled release bundles (output-wrapped, own copy, no ledger), separate pages. Unsupported and unobservable: two dev builds fused onto one shared root.

WHERE IT LANDS: the topology commentary in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc only. Promote the existing "Bounded by shadow's reload surface" section (~796-808) to the normative contract statement; rewrite the ownership rationale at ~722-724 and ~758-771 that presents multi-build reconciliation as shipped behaviour. NO runtime detection, warning, or error — the fused condition is unobservable from inside the shared copy, so any check would be heuristic or tautological; consequently no new error-id and no Spec 009 catalogue row. NO spec/* or docs/* edits (dossier corpus grep verified no page claims runtime multi-build isolation) — so NOT hot-zone; the surface is implementation/ui/ src + test only, parallel-safe.

TESTS TO DELETE (implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/rules_cljs_test.cljc; all six verified present at these lines on origin/main 3947ac610a): build-ids-are-isolated (281), reentrant-registration-into-an-open-foreign-cycle-still-stages (408), co-loaded-builds-retain-independent-declarations (904), one-builds-cycle-never-consumes-another-builds-reload-evidence (932), installed-producer-notes-into-its-own-build-only (983), reload-producer-is-build-isolated (1074). Their sole subject is cross-build independence inside one shared namespace copy — a state no real call path can produce.

TESTS TO KEEP (reframe multi-build wording where present; do not weaken): ready-made-pair-cannot-inject-a-foreign-owner-into-an-open-cycle (946) and ns-only-and-ready-made-pair-are-the-same-evidence (966) — the shipped rf2-4vm19 normalization invariant; build-identity-is-one-rule-shared-by-every-arity (860) and build-identity-is-stable-across-calls (886) — single-build identity coherence; the producer-install trio (~742, ~786, ~823) — the shared SHADOW_NS_RESET array genuinely hosts other libraries' callbacks; the full JVM linearizability suite (rules_reload_linearizability_jvm_test.clj) — its explicit build-ids are re-documented as test-state partition tokens, not a topology claim.

MECHANISM STAYS: keep the [build-id ns] ledger key, current-build-id, the producer tag, and the explicit build-scoped arities — re-documented as the internal producer seam plus test-isolation tokens. The shipped normalization fix (PR #6434) sits on this key; collapsing to ns-only is a second refactor with zero user-visible gain and real regression risk. title: Expand the synthesis operation guard to every active authority
description:
## Confirmed current gap

PR #6015 added a classified retired-operation guard to `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, but the selected `SYNTHESIS_ROOTS` are only `guide/` and `drafts/`. The command's own verbose output enumerates 35 files and necessarily excludes live operational authorities that workers execute:

- top-level `11-adoption-workstreams.md` and `12-implementation-plan.md`;
- `prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md`, `prep/w2-migration-skill-extension.md`, `prep/w3-docs-disposition.md`, and `prep/w9-ci-matrix-disposition.md`;
- the parent program epic/export (`rf2-vxgfnd`).

The closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.136` explicitly required a classified guard over **all active synthesis operational surfaces plus the parent epic export**, plus existence checks for cited tracked inputs. The implementation corrected the known prose manually, but the permanent guard cannot observe a regression in any surface above. It also validates Markdown link targets, not the many paste-ready paths written as bare/backticked operational input paths.

## Deliverable

Give the operation check one explicit, reviewable authority inventory that covers every active runnable/dispatch surface without widening the ordinary docs corpus or sweeping unrelated `ai/` scratch. Include the parent program authority through its stable tracked export or an equally authoritative narrow projection. Validate that each operationally cited input path is tracked at the audited revision.

Keep historical review/spike prose out of the active inventory unless it is deliberately marked non-operative. Do not turn this into synthesis publication or a general-purpose Beads/Markdown parser.

## Fail-before proof

Add classified fixtures/mutations placing a retired copy-from-mayor directive in (1) an active `prep/` file, (2) a top-level active plan, and (3) the parent epic export. All three pass the current `--synthesis-only` guard; the repaired guard must reject them while retaining the existing historical exemption and narrow-scope controls.

## Provenance

Found during the chronological audit of PR #6015 on current main `bb201cdbc0f1973a60225776c8bae7957ac3ef7e`. All-status Beads search found only the closed source Bead `rf2-vxgfnd.136`, so this is a follow-up rather than a duplicate/reopen.
acceptance_criteria:
- One explicit narrow inventory covers guide/drafts plus every active top-level/prep operational surface and the parent program authority.
- The current `component-library-readiness.md` contradiction is corrected to the tracked exact-worktree rule and becomes a permanent fail-before fixture.
- Retired copy-from-mayor/gitignored/local-only imperatives in any inventoried surface fail, including runnable fenced commands.
- The historical exemption ends at the marked blockquote and cannot leak across a blank into a new quote.
- Benign copying into a worktree without a retired mayor/source-authority claim remains allowed.

title: Close lexical, polarity, and Markdown-boundary gaps in the Form-3 migration guard
description:
## Current defect

PR #6013 strengthened `scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py`, but the current Form-3 lifecycle guard remains bypassable and noisy at three narrow syntax boundaries:

1. **Clojure lexical context.** `_read_form` treats `;` comment text as arguments, so an actually bare multiline call with a comment is counted arity 6 and passes. `_form3_call_sites` also finds call heads inside strings, so `(log/debug "(rf/subscribe-once query-v)")` is falsely rejected.
2. **Example polarity.** `_polarity_at(..., carried)` carries an inline `BEFORE` exemption across every later block until a recognized `AFTER`; an ordinary later affirmative recipe passes. Polarity regexes also read arbitrary code/string contents: `(log/debug "BEFORE")` exempts a following unsafe call. Conversely ordinary negative prose such as `Not recommended: (rf/subscribe-once query-v)` is falsely rejected. These behaviors contradict closed rf2-vxgfnd.94.20’s criterion that historical examples cannot hide affirmative recipes.
3. **Markdown structural boundaries.** Setext headings are not recognized. A valid `Form-3 lifecycle` Setext section containing a bare call passes, while a later Setext H1 meant to start an ambient-render section fails to end prior lifecycle context. A CommonMark spaced thematic break (`* * *`) likewise fails to reset the bounded context.

Current self-tests and live-corpus scans remain green under these exact mutations. All-status searches for the mechanisms and syntax names found no live owner; closed rf2-vxgfnd.94.15/.19/.20 are the related prior work.

## Bounded repair

Add one small lexical masking/token pass shared by call-head discovery and balanced-form reading; scope historical polarity to explicit prose/comment labels and the concrete example they own; and recognize the missing Setext/thematic structural boundaries. Keep this a purpose-built guard, not a general Clojure or Markdown parser. Merely adding more positive-marker phrases is insufficient because unlabelled affirmative prose must be guarded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Call-head discovery and arity scanning ignore strings, character literals, and `;`-to-EOL comments consistently. Bare calls with comments before/after the sole argument remain arity 1 and dirty; call-shaped text inside a log/string remains clean.
- Inline/block `BEFORE`, negative-example, or “not recommended” prose exempts only the concrete historical example it owns and is not inferred from arbitrary code/string contents.
- A historical example does not bless a later unlabelled or explicit AFTER/positive recipe in the same section.
- Setext H1/H2 headings and CommonMark spaced thematic breaks bound lifecycle context like their ATX/plain-break equivalents: unsafe lifecycle sections remain dirty and a later legal ambient section stays clean.
- Self-tests and live-corpus mutation teeth contain every exact pre-fix repro plus historical, affirmative, multiline/vector/string/character, and frame-qualified legal controls.
- The current corpus passes deterministically without broadening into a general parser or weakening the fail-loud guide scan.

title: Enforce UI compiler-carrier identity at every read, write, and finish boundary
description:
PR #5970 / rf2-vxgfnd.192 introduced ambient-build-id to make the re-frame.ui private carrier authoritative and fail before mutation when its build id is missing or disagrees with Shadow. The validation is not on the actual registry paths. ambient-shadow-slice and ambient-accepted-slice read the compiler state directly; update-current-slice! checks only ui-owned-compiler-state? before mutating scratch/overlay; shadow-finish-candidate trusts its explicit build-id argument. Thus contribute!, aggregate and the property/descriptor/digest helpers can bypass the check that current-build-id performs.

Deterministic current-main reproduction: prepare a private carrier for :A, attach a still-present Shadow bridge id :B, and bind it as cljs.env/*compiler*. contribute! accepts :a/view and aggregate exposes it. current-build-id correctly throws ::private-build-id-shadow-disagreement, yet shadow-finish-candidate succeeds with explicit id :B and returns a snapshot stamped :build-id :B containing A's registry row. A private carrier missing its id likewise lets contribute! create an overlay and exposes the row even though current-build-id throws. A recognized Shadow bridge with no id can also downgrade to the session fallback when no fallback pass is marked open, despite the contract reserving fallback for genuinely plain environments with neither marker nor carrier.

This violates the source bead's fail-before-any-mutation guarantee and can cross-publish registries/digests under contradictory build authority. Focused compiler tests pass because they assert malformed identity only through current-build-id. All-status searches found no exact owner: closed .192 is incomplete; open .195 owns broader real-Shadow integration proof, not this code correction.
acceptance_criteria:
- One validated compiler-state resolver owns private-carrier presence, build-id extraction, and private-versus-Shadow agreement; ambient accepted/scratch/overlay reads and writes all traverse it.
- Missing private identity, a recognized Shadow bridge with no identity, or private/Shadow disagreement makes contribute!, aggregate/committed reads, element/property/descriptor lookups, pass/digest reads, and other ambient helpers fail before observing or mutating the malformed carrier.
- shadow-finish-candidate validates its supplied build id against the accepted private carrier and any still-present Shadow identity before deriving a candidate; contradictory A/B state cannot produce or carry a B-stamped snapshot containing A rows.
- Negative fixtures cover missing private id, missing bridge id, private/Shadow disagreement, ambient contribution/read bypass, and explicit finish bypass, asserting the compiler-env remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Valid private state with the outer marker absent still works; an agreeing canonical marker works; session fallback remains only for a genuinely plain CLJS/REPL environment with neither recognized marker nor private carrier.
- No speculative future-Shadow aliases, second successful-build authority, public API, or compatibility layer is added.

title: Classify rf.ui tree keys semantically in Conventions
description:

title: Fence older-first overlapping UI digest activations
description:
PR #5953 added a global monotone generation/high-water pair to digest_carrier, which correctly handles newest-first overlap completion. It cannot identify which reload an after-load callback belongs to because after-load carries no cycle token.

Deterministic older-first interleaving on current main:
1. accepted generation 1 is published.
2. reload A runs before-load and stages dA as generation 2.
3. reload B runs before-load and stages dB as generation 3, but its application sources have not completed.
4. older A after-load runs first.
5. A reads the global generation 3 > activated 1, publishes dB and clears updating before B finishes.
6. If B then throws and skips after-load, current continues advertising dB forever instead of remaining fail-closed.

The shipped fixture explicitly releases newest-first and therefore cannot catch this. The closed source bead's close reason acknowledges the older-first residual, but no open bead owns it. Establish exact activation-cycle ownership or explicitly serialize/reject overlapping script reloads. Keep it dev-only and local; no general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: RULED 2026-07-18 (delegated per Mike, see notes): keep shipped high-water semantics; doc/test PR only. (1) Carrier semantics unchanged: the generation/activated high-water rule stays; no FIFO/serialization, no overlap-reject fence, no loader-mode detection, no change to stage!/before-load/after-load behavior. (2) Docstring truth: the false ":script reload sources load asynchronously" premise in digest_carrier.cljs (lines 33-35 area) is replaced with the verified host fact (Shadow 3.4.10 reload chain is one synchronous macrotask absent explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks; :loader-mode affects initial-load flush only), and reload atomicity is named as a load-bearing host assumption to re-verify on any Shadow upgrade. (3) check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs: the c3 preamble's copy of the same false premise is corrected, and an older-first characterization stanza is added (before A / stage dA / before B / stage dB / after -> publishes dB early in the modeled world) whose comment carries the reachability rationale and cites the ruling. (4) Existing newest-first, stale-after-newer-fence, initial-load, and failed-reload recovery fixture cases remain green. (5) Advanced production remains free of the carrier machinery; no general concurrency abstraction.
notes:
BLOCKED on premise contradiction (czh5k analysis 2026-07-17, ~70min read-only, 0 edits). The digest-carrier after-load fix (digest_carrier.cljs:145-164, the ^:dev/after-load high-water rule from #5953) must satisfy two PROVABLY INCOMPATIBLE ACs: (a) 'failed-reload recovery stays green' → after-load MUST publish; (b) 'AC1 older-first fence' → overlapping older after-load must NOT publish. At the deciding after-load BOTH present identical carrier state (2 before-loads, 2 stages, 0 prior after-loads, generation 2-ahead-of-activated); Shadow's zero-arg :dev/after-load carries no cycle token, so a THROWN reload is locally indistinguishable from an IN-FLIGHT overlapping reload — opposite handling required, distinguishing fact is future/unobservable. Also the bead's own two new clauses (older-first-B-succeeds-publishes-dB vs B-throws-forward-recovery-publishes-dC) are mutually exclusive for the same reason. Context: :script loader-mode (only mode with older-first overlap) is NOT used for HMR in-repo (only a fixture) — purely defensive for downstream :script consumers. OPTIONS (Mike decides): (A) mode-gated serialize — under :script FIFO cycle-ownership (promote oldest unpromoted), :eval unchanged; achieves fence + older-first-B-succeeds, all tests green, residual: B-throws-recovery needs 1 extra clean :script reload; depends on :loader-mode runtime-readable (unconfirmed). (B) reject-overlap — overlapping reloads don't publish, next clean reload recovers; older-first-B publishes on NEXT reload not at B's after-load. (C) relax the acceptance — drop EITHER older-first-B-publishes-at-completion OR B-throws-recovery-publishes-once (they're exclusive). czh5k REC: (C) relax to preferred behavior, then implement (A) [closest to exact-cycle-ownership, zero test risk].
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): ADOPT OPTION C — keep the shipped generation/activated high-water semantics in digest_carrier.cljs unchanged. REJECT the dossier's Option B (reject/fence overlap) and the earlier notes' "relax then implement A" plan. One small doc/test PR closes this bead; no semantic change.

RATIONALE (keystones independently re-verified before ruling): (1) digest_carrier.cljs:160-164 is exactly the modeled state machine — after-load promotes whenever generation > activated, publishing whatever :staged holds. (2) Pinned Shadow 3.4.10 sources (client/browser.cljs:23-40 + 71-96, client/env.cljs:191-252, verified from the .m2 jar): hot reload is one synchronous macrotask — websocket load-sources -> do-js-reload -> do-js-load, a synchronous doseq of goog.globalEval; before-load hooks FILO, after-load FIFO; async only via explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks (zero in this repo, grep empty); hook throws still call next, only a load throw aborts. :loader-mode branches only the INITIAL-LOAD flush format — the carrier docstring's ":script loads reload sources asynchronously" premise (digest_carrier.cljs:33-35) is FALSE for reload on 3.4.10. So the feared older-first interleaving is unreachable on the pinned host: "staged but in flight" never spans a task boundary, and every reachable history (serialized chains, throw-then-recover, stale stragglers) is already handled correctly by the shipped rule. (3) Option B is unsound as stated: its trigger — a second before-load arriving while fenced — is exactly the signature of the TESTED throw-then-recover path (check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs:696-734), so B demotes every failed-reload recovery to a full page refresh; its ":eval recovery unchanged" claim is wrong. (4) Option A rests on the false :script-async premise and adds scheduler machinery for an unreachable corner — posture forbids. HOST-FACT COUPLING: correctness is now EXPLICITLY pinned to Shadow 3.4.10's reload atomicity. REVISIT TRIGGER: a Shadow upgrade that makes reload loading async (e.g. a CSP-safe script-injection reload path) RE-OPENS the hazard — re-verify atomicity on every Shadow bump alongside 004C section 2.1.1's pins; upstream shipping a reload cycle token or a load-failure hook converts this into Option D as a small exact fix with no contract change.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one doc/test PR, no semantic change): (i) digest_carrier.cljs docstring — replace the false async premise (lines 33-35, revising the 33-51 overlap paragraph) with the verified host fact (Shadow 3.4.10 reload chain = one synchronous macrotask absent explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks; :loader-mode affects initial-load flush only) and name reload atomicity as a load-bearing host assumption to re-verify on any Shadow upgrade. (ii) implementation/scripts/check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs — correct the same false premise repeated in the c3 preamble (lines 736-741), and append an OLDER-FIRST CHARACTERIZATION stanza after the existing c3 block (~line 808): before(A)/stage(dA)/before(B)/stage(dB)/after -> pin that the stale A release publishes the newest staged digest dB early in the modeled world; the stanza comment MUST carry the reachability rationale and cite this ruling (documented modeled behavior, NOT an endorsed race). (iii) Close this bead on that PR. OUT OF SCOPE: FIFO/serialization or overlap-reject machinery, loader-mode runtime detection, Shadow patches, any change to stage!/before-load/after-load semantics, spec edits (004C section 2.1/2.1.1 already promises only "consumers activate only successful build output"; EP-0032 does not govern this surface). HONEST RESIDUAL LEFT OPEN: a downstream consumer registering an async after-load hook in a namespace linearized before the carrier, plus an overlapping reload whose load throws, could see a false advertised digest in dev until the next successful reload or page refresh — dev-only, self-healing, not constructible in-repo; the fail-closed ideal is genuinely unmet in that corner.

AC AMENDMENT (old -> new): DROPPED the two provably incompatible clauses — "an older A completion after newer B has staged cannot publish B or clear B's fence" and "an older-first fixture keeps current nil until B's own successful completion; a B-throws variant stays fail-closed and later forward recovery publishes the newest accepted generation once" — and DROPPED "each completion is tied to its cycle or overlap is explicitly serialized/rejected" (no host cycle token exists). title: DECISION: late-bind DI hook keys (~300) use bare non-rf-root prefixes (:epoch/* :schemas/* :router/* …) — accept internal carve-out or unify under :rf.*?
description:
PROBLEM: The late-bind hook registry (re-frame.late-bind — cross-namespace/cross-artefact forward-reference DI seam so core does not hard-require optional artefacts) keys every hook with a BARE non-rf-root artefact prefix. This is the single largest body of framework keywords outside the :rf.* scheme (~300 keys). Distinct prefixes found via grep over implementation/core: :late-bind/* [111], :epoch/* [24], :schemas/* [19], :error-emit/* [13], :adapter/* [9], :router/* [8], :flows/* [8], :ui/* [5], :observability/* [5], :ssr/* [3], :routing/* [3], :live-frame/* [3], :trace/* [2], :reagent/* [2], :machines/* [2], :http/* [2], :views/* [1], :subs/* [1], :resources/* [1], :event-emit/*. Examples: :epoch/settle!, :schemas/validate-event!, :router/dispatch!, :flows/run-flows-on-db (see late_bind.cljc, core_epoch.cljc:31, core.cljc:2591).

CONTEXT: These are PURELY INTERNAL — a load-time function registry (set-fn!/get-fn), never on any public surface (not app-db, not trace, not error ex-data, not a return value). Already disciplined: an authoritative inventory (re-frame.late-bind.directory) + a drift test enforce the key set. Per the two-regime rule they read as 'closed-local grammar' (regime 1) — EXCEPT regime 1 sanctions BARE (unqualified) local keys, whereas these are namespaced under a NON-rf root, which the scheme does not otherwise permit for framework ids.

OPTIONS:
(A) ACCEPT as an internal-DI carve-out — document in Conventions that the late-bind hook registry is exempt from the :rf.* scheme (internal wiring, never public, own directory+drift-test). Cheapest; preserves the artefact-named grouping that makes the registry readable.
(B) UNIFY under :rf.* — e.g. :rf.hook/epoch-settle! or :rf.late-bind.epoch/settle! (keep artefact grouping as a dotted sub-area). Consistent with the framework's one-language identity. Cost: ~300 key renames across producer set-fn! sites + consumer get-fn sites + the directory + the drift-test; purely mechanical, no functional change (pre-alpha, no back-compat).

CONSEQUENCE: (A) = one Conventions.md note (hot-zone). (B) = large mechanical sweep across implementation/core, own coordinated PR.

RECOMMENDATION: LEAN (A) — the :rf.* scheme is explicitly for the PUBLIC framework surface (Conventions L8 enumerates events/fx/cofx/app-db/trace/errors/warnings), and these keys are invisible internal plumbing with their own guardrails; unifying is ~300 renames for zero public-surface benefit. BUT flag the tension: the rf2-lgeron require-alias ruling chose consistency 'INCLUDING keywords, the deciding lens' even on a non-public authoring surface — by that same lens Mike may prefer (B). Genuine call.

(from rf2-099q90 keyword audit; see ai/findings/2026-07-17-keyword-surface-audit.md §Non-reserved framework surfaces)
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): Option A — keep all 216 artefact-prefixed late-bind hook keys as-is. NO renames, NO aliases, NO migration layer.

RATIONALE: The carve-out already exists as normative spec text — spec/Conventions.md:1697-1716 (section "Late-bind hook key grammar", landed rf2-l8fi6 / commit b88578c8bb) specifies exactly these names, with the directory + drift test as authority. The real defect is that Conventions line 8 ("one root keyword namespace") and line 24 ("there is no third shape") were written without cross-referencing that section, so the file argues with itself. This ruling is therefore a RECONCILIATION, not a new rule. Option B was rejected: verified blast radius is ~2,840 occurrences across ~440 files including 7 sequential hot-zone spec files (not the "~300 renames" the bead estimated), it rewrites a normative grammar a prior ruling landed, and it dilutes the :rf.* signal (may-be-contract-bearing) across private wiring — gold-plating under the pre-alpha pragmatic posture. Option C (two dialects) strictly dominated. Verified during ruling: grammar section confirmed by direct read; :rf2/runtime-version confirmed host-facing (spec/011-SSR.md:64 — "when the host registers the hook at boot") with NO directory.cljc row — so the exception must be stated as the DATA boundary, not "never an extension point".

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one small PR; spec/Conventions.md is hot-zone — sequence it):
1. In the Reserved-namespaces / two-regime area (spec/Conventions.md:8 and :24), add a cross-link sentence: late-bind registry ADDRESSES are a sanctioned key shape governed by the "Late-bind hook key grammar" section (line 1697) — internal wiring addresses, not framework data identifiers. Soften "no third shape" (line 24) and the line-8 "one root" claim to acknowledge that section (which already sanctions the :rf2/ root at line 1705).
2. State the exception as the DATA boundary: hook keys MUST NOT appear as identifiers on any runtime data surface (trace tags/values, error ex-data, app-db keys, serialized/wire payloads); a key that must cross such a boundary takes the applicable reserved :rf.* vocabulary. Do NOT write "never escapes through extension contracts" — falsified by :rf2/runtime-version.
OUT OF SCOPE: renaming any of the 216 directory keys; any implementation/ src or test change; the conformance fixture capability vocabulary (:fixture/capabilities — :routing/match-url deliberately names both a hook and a capability, different registries); rewriting the grammar-section rules beyond an optional one-line preamble touch-up.
TRAPS FOR THE WORKER: (a) the bead census is polluted — ":late-bind/* [111]" counted the FUNCTION alias late-bind/set-fn!, not keywords; true inventory = 216 directory entries across ~30 prefixes; (b) tools/story publishes :subs/resolve-sub-override outside the directory BY DESIGN (see late_bind_drift_test.clj:41-56 docstring) — not a violation, no action; (c) hook keys DO appear in spec/docs prose (~259 mentions) — prose mentions are fine, the boundary is runtime data.
FOLLOW-UP: see discovered-from child bead for the :rf2/runtime-version governance gap (host-facing, spec-documented, no directory row, outside the drift gate).

DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): Option A — KEEP the :rf.nav/* / :rf.route/* two-prefix split. NO rename (options B and C rejected; D rejected outright). Bead reshaped from rename-decision into the doc-drift-fix task below.

RATIONALE (decisive): The split is SPEC-NORMATIVE, not drift. spec/Conventions.md:417 (fx sub-namespace rule, "Audit Finding 2") carries a written membership criterion — an fx-id lives under :rf.nav/* when it is a navigation PRIMITIVE: a thin wrapper over a browser/host navigation API (pushState/replaceState/scroll) that is NOT route-aware (no nav-token threading, no :on-match dispatch, no schema validation) — and states verbatim: "The split from :rf.route/* is deliberate: :rf.nav/* fx-ids could be invoked by a non-routing app that wants the primitive without the routing slice; :rf.route/* fx-ids require the routing artefact's slice and tokens to be meaningful." Override tiers track the criterion (all four :rf.nav/* fx OVERRIDABLE, Conventions.md:390-393; the one route-aware fx :rf.route/with-nav-token is REJECT, row 394). The bead's core premise — routing as the ONLY two-prefix subsystem — is FALSE: Spec 011 owns :rf.ssr/* AND :rf.server/* (Conventions.md rows 78/81), the identical domain-vs-host-mechanism layering mirrored server-side, and Spec 016 owns three prefixes (:rf.resource/*, :rf.mutation/*, :rf.optimistic/*). No one-prefix-per-subsystem rule exists anywhere in Conventions.md. Option C would additionally break routing's own audience signal (012-Routing.md:32 — dotted sub-areas = internal plumbing users must not touch) by demoting the most user-visible OVERRIDABLE fx into the plumbing position. A written spec-normative membership rule is the definition of deliberate; a ~102-file rename (incl. 11 behaviour-pinning conformance fixtures + 5 hot-zone specs) against it is over-engineering. AUTHORITY: ai/findings/re-com-port/synthesis.{fable,codex,grok}.md (tri-consensus; ai/ is gitignored — copy content into child briefs when filing). SHAPE (consensus): new native major/namespace/artifact + separately-named frozen Reagent compat tier; values-only props-map ABI with trailing compiled children; event prefixes + (conj prefix payload); three-category customization (data / pure slots / registered-stateful-if-ruled); headless pure .cljc transition kernels for hard widgets; async out of widgets into events/resources; theme as immutable data + explicit selection; CSS-first layout + pure geometry; .cljc structural views; deterministic keys/ids; per-namespace production requires; tables foreign-virtualization-first; inline overlays first. WAVE 0 — PRODUCT REGISTER RESOLVED (ruled 2026-07-16, R-1 coordinate confirmed 2026-07-17; the ten rulings R-1..R-10 are durable in docs/EP/EP-0035-component-library-readiness.md §Resolved Decisions and restated in this epic's NOTES, which are authoritative over any summary). The former "file children when Mike rules the product register" condition is MET — there is no outstanding product-register gate, and no ai/decisions/re-com-readiness.product-rulings.md file was ever created; do not wait on one. Wave-0 scope: freeze native ABI; classify all 72 public Vars (native view / pure helper / compat-only / replacement API / foreign-boundary); package names + cross-host date representation; modernize scripts/kwargs-to-map into dry-run/report; Story + visual baselines BEFORE porting; generic library-authoring internals + guide chapter (public middle artifact only on a second consumer). WAVES 1-5 per the syntheses (structural -> interactive -> overlays -> data-heavy -> adoption/removal); interactive waves depend on the S3 readiness children (rf2-8k14ia sync door, rf2-ri0k6n slots, rf2-isdqjv safe spread, .95.2 atomic local). Release gates: zero Reagent imports in native artifact; no runtime hiccup detection; controlled-input matrix through library APIs; JVM Tier-1 majority + kernel transition traces; StrictMode/reconnect/HMR coverage; visual baselines with CSS frozen; advanced-build one-view isolation; compat deletion criteria written before removal starts.
notes:
ADDITION (2026-07-16, completeness audit — codex §11 release gates 9+10, restored to the durable copy): the native-library release gates also include (9) Story states + accessibility/keyboard/focus checks for EVERY public component (automated coverage plus targeted manual review), and (10) deterministic keys/ids + explicit async cancellation/ownership asserted as GATES (not only ABI shape items).
RULED REGISTER (2026-07-16, delegated decisions per Mike's in-session direction; dossier weighed and retired):
1. PACKAGING — Option B. Same repo initially; native artifact re-com/re-com-ui with namespace family re-com.ui.*; frozen Reagent legacy stays at re-com/re-com and re-com.*. Rationale: side-by-side coexistence is mandatory for leaf-by-leaf migration, legacy apps need zero rename, ns family verified collision-free (MUI @material-ui -> @mui precedent). Final coordinate may be adjusted before first publication only; use distinct aliases (rc vs ui) in all examples.
2. PARTS CEILING — Option A. v1 :parts accepts data/style values plus pure compiled slots only; no registered stateful replacement views (the ui/view trigger rf2-a62fje does NOT fire for re-com v1); arbitrary fns/hiccup/component heads rejected permanently. SHARPENING (adopted as part of the ruling): the slot contract states slots receive the component's declared STATE (open/highlighted/disabled etc), not only item + occurrence — render-prop state access is the power users actually miss and keeps pressure for stateful replacement near zero. Escalation to registered views requires a concrete customization inexpressible via composition/data/pure slot.
3. UNCONTROLLED TIER — Option B, narrow. Controlled components are canonical and the only form recommended for durable application state; selected components may declare a separate uncontrolled tier via :default-value. :value and :default-value are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE; supplying both is a validation failure at the component boundary. Per-component admission only on demonstrated Story/ephemera pain. Type-based ownership inference (value-or-ratom) rejected permanently.
4. THEME TRANSPORT — Option A. Explicit props + frame subscriptions only in v1; no nested context mechanism. FORWARD-COMPAT CLAUSE (adopted): theme values are plain data only (no fns/closures inside theme values) so a later context graduation is non-breaking. Context reconsidered only when a real nested-theme consumer states the required cross-host (SSR/JVM/memo/reconnect) semantics.
5. TABLES/GRIDS — Option A. Foreign-virtualization-first behind a re-com-owned data/event/slot boundary. The ONLY accepted reasons to open a native-virtualization project are the four criteria verbatim: (a) re-com-specific behavior unrepresentable at the boundary; (b) material bundle/perf evidence favoring ownership; (c) JVM structural rendering value sufficient to justify the implementation; (d) a required a11y/interaction guarantee unobtainable from the foreign engine. Foreign-engine selection (TanStack-class vs react-window-class; bundle/license/upgrade surface) is a NAMED Wave-4-entry decision, not an implementation detail inside the prototype bead.
6. HELPER ARTIFACT — Option A. Generic internals (part/slot resolution, safe attribute splitting, event-prefix helpers, theme-data merging, focus/roving-tabindex, dismissal, deterministic-id recipes) written under generic discipline with independent tests, plus the normative component-library authoring guide, from Wave 0. Public middle artifact only after a second consuming library requests substantially the same contracts; organizational override allowed only if stated explicitly.
7. INPUT OWNERSHIP — Option B. Ownership law approved NOW: checkbox/radio, slider/splits, tabs, selected values, dates/ranges, tree selection, sort and filter models are fully controlled; text/time editing and other explicit commit experiences may use a separate commit/draft API; open/hover/focus/highlight/drag/uncommitted-search are local interaction state unless deliberately exposed; a rejected or externally refreshed draft is identified ONLY by an explicit caller-owned revision (:reset-key), never by model-value comparison. Concrete per-component roster frozen at Wave 2 entry as a named bead, then used as the evidence input to rf2-nzst23. Legacy hybrid ownership rejected.
8. CROSS-HOST DATE/TIME REPRESENTATION (new, was missing from the register) — Public date/time models are host-neutral plain data with ISO-8601 strings as the canonical ABI form: dates "YYYY-MM-DD", times "HH:mm[:ss]", datetimes full ISO-8601. No goog.date/cljs-time/js Date/java.time objects cross the public ABI; components parse/format internally at the boundary per host. Rationale: values-only ABI, EDN/app-db inspectability, JVM SSR, and consistency with the project's XState-v6 ISO-8601 duration ruling. Legacy datepicker's cljs-time/goog.date model is compat-tier-only.
9. ACCESSIBILITY TARGET (new, was missing from the register) — Native baseline is WAI-ARIA APG semantics per component class: roles/states/properties, keyboard interaction, and focus management per the matching APG pattern, shipped WITH each component in its wave (a component is not done without them). Release gate 9 is priced against APG, not legacy parity — legacy contains exactly ONE aria- attribute, so "parity" would ship an inaccessible library. Radix/React Aria set the expectation floor for a modern native library; retrofitting is costlier than building in during a rewrite that already touches every interaction.
10. CSS/BOOTSTRAP POSTURE (new, named deferred ruling now ruled) — The bootstrap-derived theme layer is RETAINED through the parity waves (CSS frozen for visual baselines, per the settled CSS-preserved-first posture), but MUST be isolated as a distinct removable theme-data layer in the native theme model so removal is a data change, not an API break. Long-term removal/replacement is a NAMED post-parity decision bead filed at Wave-5/adoption entry, not drift.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (for Wave-0/Wave-2 workers; evidence refs are into the legacy day8/re-com checkout):
- Facade inventory: re-com.core has exactly 72 (def alias impl/var) exports (src/re_com/core.cljs:45-135) plus reg-theme (core.cljs:137-146) = 73 public vars; core.clj adds 3 macros. reflect-current-component expands to reagent.impl.component/component-name — a PRIVATE Reagent import; the zero-Reagent release gate must explicitly catch it (classify compat-only).
- Parts overload evidence: part? = (some-fn map? string? vector? number? ifn? nil?) (src/re_com/part.cljs:117); part converts ifn values into dynamic heads [f props] (part.cljs:154-182); 18 files mention :parts, 33 require re-com.part. This is exactly the runtime polymorphism the native slot system replaces with data/style values + pure compiled slots.
- Slot contract (Ruling 2 sharpening): declared slots receive the component's declared STATE (e.g. open?/highlighted?/disabled?) in addition to item + occurrence info. Slots are pure; no stateful replacement views in v1.
- Uncontrolled mutual exclusion (Ruling 3): :value XOR :default-value; both supplied => validation failure; uncontrolled forms documented for demos/ephemera only, never durable app state. Mirrors the React DOM/Radix value/defaultValue dual.
- Two-owner input pathology (Ruling 7 evidence): input-text keeps external-model/internal-model ratoms with render-phase reset! sync (src/re_com/input_text.cljs:78,111-113), detects a 2-arity done-fn via .-length introspection (input_text.cljs:104), and re-creates showing? inside the render fn (input_text.cljs:90). Native commit/draft inputs take an explicit caller revision (:reset-key); NEVER infer rejection/refresh from value equality (saved "A" -> user edits "B" -> parent rejects by reasserting "A" is undetectable by value comparison).
- Theme evidence (Ruling 4): six dynamic vars incl *bootstrap* (src/re_com/theme.cljs:9-14) mutated by reg-theme via set! (core.cljs:141-146), read at render by theme/comp (theme.cljs:33-44); the args-desc itself says ":theme ... is not reactive" (theme.cljs:19-24). Native: immutable theme data via props/frame subs; theme values plain data only.
- Tables evidence (Ruling 5): v-table has exactly nine *-renderer args, all :validate-fn fn? typed -> hiccup, only :row-renderer required (src/re_com/v_table.cljs:505-513) — the seam maps 1:1 onto slots over a foreign engine.
- A11y/overlay evidence (Ruling 9): exactly 1 aria- occurrence in the entire legacy source tree; createPortal has 0 occurrences (inline-overlay-first is safe for visual parity).
- Test-anchor warning: legacy suite is 11 files / 1,126 lines against 94 source files / 18,185 lines (~6%) — it CANNOT anchor behaviour preservation; Story scenes + visual baselines BEFORE porting are load-bearing, not decoration.
- Migration tooling: scripts/kwargs-to-map/ (babashka rewriter) already exists in the re-com repo; Wave-0 migrator work modernizes it into dry-run/report mode, not greenfield.
- Dates (Ruling 8): legacy datepicker requires cljs-time/goog.date (src/re_com/datepicker.cljs:8-16), browser-only; native ABI uses ISO-8601 strings with conversion internal to components.

title: S3 ergonomic proof: RealWorld Resources article editor plus guide fixtures
description:
## Problem
S3 needs an ergonomic proof in real application code, not only compiler fixtures. The proof must exercise a representative vertical slice early enough to improve the programming model before the later documentation/migration fan-out.

## Scope
Migrate one complete `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources` vertical page to native re-frame.ui, choosing the article editor because it exercises controlled inputs, committed event vectors, validation, navigation, resource-backed data, error/loading states, and hot editing. Keep the surrounding app interoperating through the approved frozen adapter boundary; do not broaden this into the S6 whole-app migration. Add guide-backed counter and dashboard examples/fixtures so `defview`, `sub`, event vectors, local/effect where justified, callbacks, route-link, JVM structural tests, browser tests, hot reload, and Xray evidence feel coherent as one language.

## Constraints
Prefer direct idiomatic source over migration scaffolding. Do not retain dual Reagent/re-frame.ui implementations of the page, introduce a page-specific adapter, or rewrite unrelated RealWorld infrastructure. re-frame.ui is the optimized/default taught path; frozen Reagent/UIx compatibility is not feature parity work.
acceptance_criteria:
- The article-editor route is implemented once in idiomatic re-frame.ui and covers load/edit/validation/save/error/navigation with native controlled-input behavior.
- Headless JVM structural tests assert intent/event vectors; browser tests assert real interactions and resource ownership; the page works through hot reload without leaked state/leases.
- Xray can identify the page occurrence, dependencies, event sites, causes, and evidence loss truthfully.
- Counter and dashboard guide fixtures compile and run with the same API, with no private helper required to make the ergonomics acceptable.
- Diff review finds no compatibility shim, duplicate view dialect, unrelated app rewrite, or comment bulk inflating the proof.
close_reason: shipped #6163 (merged)

title: S3 Story and Pair consumers of the view tool tier
description:
## Problem
Story and Pair must consume the same S3 evidence/runtime model as Xray or the project will acquire three subtly different debugging truths. Their integration is also the proof that the tool projections are useful beyond one UI.

## Scope
Wire Story and re-frame2-pair-mcp to the versioned view evidence/tool tier. Story adds view-id/JVM structural-tree visibility and observation-target overrides using the existing host-specific mechanism (`ui.test/render` injection on JVM, observation-target protocol on CLJS) with honest `:owned? false` labeling. Pair exposes the five read-only projections and uses the existing nREPL HMR path for hot swap; update MCP descriptors/conformance vocabulary in lockstep. Reuse the S3 occurrence/cause/loss semantics and tolerate absent/older evidence explicitly.

## Constraints
No second runtime model, bespoke Story subscription ownership, remote mutation API, new HMR channel, or raw internal handles on the wire. Follow MCP elision/security policy and keep tool evidence out of production. Root hot-zone files remain serialized; never commit bead exports.
acceptance_criteria:
- Story fixtures show view id, JVM tree vocabulary, connected evidence, observation overrides, and honest non-owned status without acquiring/releasing app resources.
- Pair MCP descriptors and conformance fixtures expose all five read-only projections with stable schemas, version/loss fields, and normal sensitive-data projection.
- Hot swap travels through the existing nREPL HMR path and proves compatible retention plus incompatible remount; no parallel reload protocol exists.
- Missing, old-version, disconnected, and truncated evidence yields explicit unavailable/partial results rather than fabricated emptiness.
- Story/Pair focused gates and production-absence checks are green.
