title: S3 Xray consumption of compiled view evidence
description:
## Problem
The evidence substrate proves its value only when Xray answers real questions from it. Existing panels currently rely on older attribution paths and must consume the authoritative S3 records without presenting inferred or dropped data as exact.

## Scope
Wire S3 view evidence into Xray by enriching existing surfaces first: Event view gets event-site provenance; Epoch timeline gets per-view commit/cause rows and epoch-restore cause; Reactive/Views get occurrence identity, dependencies, causes, timing and render-argument truth; Issues gets new warning families and loss indicators. Delete the old cloneElement/post-render attribution path once equivalent evidence is live. Every Xray change updates the corresponding `tools/xray/spec/*` contract in the same PR.

## Constraints
No new tab/panel unless a separately reviewed information-architecture gap proves existing surfaces cannot answer the question. Never label truncated/inferred data exact. Do not expose internal handles or resurrect the old attribution as fallback. No root hot-zone edits without transfer; no bead export commits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Xray fixtures consume only the public/versioned evidence projections or their explicit internal transport, not React tree scraping or cloneElement attribution.
- Event, Epoch, Reactive/Views, and Issues surfaces each demonstrate their named S3 evidence with occurrence identity and loss/unknown labels.
- The legacy attribution implementation and its tests are deleted once replacement fixtures pass; no dual path remains.
- `tools/xray/spec/*` is updated atomically and projection/feature/browser gates fail if a panel silently drops or fabricates evidence.
- Empty, truncated, stale-version, disconnected, Activity-retained, and epoch-restore counterexamples render honestly.

title: S3 versioned view evidence and public re-frame.ui.tool projections
description:
## Problem
Debugging is a first-class consumer of the compiled substrate, but the public tool tier must expose truthful bounded evidence rather than internal handles or an unbounded retention graph. S3 must finish the evidence model before Xray/Story/Pair can consume it.

## Scope
Extend the S2 `re-frame.ui.tool.evidence` substrate; do not rebuild it. Define versioned manifest and connected-instance records, occurrence identity, observation targets, render/event causes, lifecycle annotations, capacity/loss accounting, and the five frozen dev-tool projections: `view-manifest`, `mounted-views`, `explain-render`, `view-dependencies`, `view-event-sites`. Records represent committed connected incarnations only; historical hide-vs-unmount labels remain explicit inference/tool labels, never fabricated runtime truth. Project serializable evidence, not leases/handles/React objects. Include literal/normalized/dynamic handler-site honesty and interop sites.

## Constraints
Use existing evidence capacity/weak-retention mechanisms unless a failing fixture proves a missing primitive. No new authoring API, production registry, general query engine, or new Xray panel. Tool functions are dev-only and absent from advanced production. Root Spec 009 / schema edits remain serialized; do not commit `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schemas and fixtures pin versioned view manifest, connected instance/occurrence identity, observation/cause/lifecycle fields, dropped counts, and explicit unknown/inferred states.
- The five public projections are deterministic, serializable, read-only, and tolerate missing/older evidence as contracted.
- Event-site projection distinguishes literal/normalized sites from `:dynamic` and never claims raw callback internals are inspectable.
- Disconnected ordinary instances become collectable; Activity-retained evidence remains deliberately visible; handles/leases/React objects never egress.
- G-7/G-11 advanced builds contain none of the tool registry, projection functions, debug strings, or evidence retention machinery.
- Spec 009 catalogue/schema and public API manifest changes land with focused JVM/CLJS/browser projection tests after hot-zone transfer.
notes: AMENDED 2026-07-16 — component-library readiness P1-5 (DIRECTED; owning doc drafts/component-library-readiness.md): the dev/test view-manifest projection becomes a VERSIONED PUBLIC SHAPE additionally exposing per-prop docs/defaults and declared render-slot (and, if later graduated, stateful-slot) metadata alongside the props schema, source sites, and capability bits — one source of truth so component libraries never rebuild parallel args-description systems (re-com maintains ~57 such Vars purely for validation messages + generated docs). Story/docs/Xray/agents consume this one projection. No runtime handles. Production absence proven with G-7/G-11. 04-debugging §1 carries the matching amendment.

title: S3 route-link as an ordinary compiled view
description:
## Problem
Applications need navigation links that preserve ordinary browser semantics while dispatching through the committed re-frame2 frame. The approved surface is useful only if it is a normal compiled view rather than a compiler intrinsic or a new dependency from the UI artifact into routing.

## Scope
Implement the approved `ui/route-link` ruling from `rf2-5yovjt` in S3 after committed events exist. Build it as an ordinary compiled view over the routing layer's late-bound link-model/activation contract. Preserve native href/open-in-new-tab/modifier/middle-click/accessibility behavior and use committed `ui/event` activation only when the routing model says the click is an in-app activation. Promote the public name into the frozen API/spec table during its serialized contract turn and make MIG-32 mechanical.

## Constraints
No compiler special case, no `re-frame.ui` → routing artifact dependency, no alternate router, no interception of browser gestures that routing has not claimed, and no compatibility wrapper. Do not edit protected hot-zone files until explicit transfer; do not commit bead exports.
acceptance_criteria:
- A route-link compiles through the ordinary view pipeline and its emitted code contains no route-link intrinsic branch.
- Browser fixtures prove normal left-click activation, href truth, modifier/middle-click/new-tab behavior, default prevention only on claimed in-app activation, and committed-frame dispatch after retarget.
- Missing/unavailable routing integration fails or degrades exactly as the late-bound routing contract specifies, without importing routing into the UI artifact.
- JVM tree/SSR output remains deterministic and accessible.
- API manifest, Spec 004/012 table, migration rule MIG-32, and focused tests are updated in the serialized hot-zone turn.

title: S3 frozen re-frame.ui.react interop tier
description:
## Problem
Interop with React libraries needs a deliberately tiny, frozen tier. It must behave like compiled re-frame.ui sites under HMR/JVM/manifest rules, not become an alternate authoring surface or leak general React machinery into production.

## Scope
Implement exactly the seven `re-frame.ui.react` names frozen in the v1 table: `use-ref`, `use-effect`, `use-layout-effect`, `use-effect-event`, `use-context`, `use-id`, and `lazy`. Treat `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/ui-react-interop-contract.md` and the checked-in API table as the call-shape contract; absorb and confirm/correct the `[S3-CONFIRM]` roster from `rf2-kvtn97`. Enforce the compiled position law, literal/signature contribution needed for HMR, host/JVM behavior, capability bits, and manifest evidence. Keep position-law compile diagnostic ids in compiler prose rather than adding Spec 009 catalogue rows unless a runtime diagnostic genuinely exists.

## Constraints
No additional hook wrappers, generic `use-hook`, alternate view grammar, UIx parity layer, or runtime hook ordering repair. This is an interop tier inside compiled views. Do not edit hot-zone files until transferred and never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only the seven frozen public names exist and their arities/return shapes match the normative contract.
- Compiler fixtures reject conditional/loop/unstable placement and prove deterministic site ordering and signature-hash contribution.
- HMR fixtures prove compatible edits retain eligible state and incompatible hook-shape edits remount according to the existing digest law.
- JVM/SSR fixtures prove each wrapper's specified structural behavior or typed rejection; lazy has deterministic fallback/activation behavior.
- Manifest and capability evidence identify the interop sites in dev while advanced production retains no debug registry or unused wrapper machinery.
- Public API manifest and focused compiler/browser/JVM tests are green after serialized hot-zone transfer.
notes: AMENDED 2026-07-16 — component-library readiness C-6 (DIRECTED; owning doc drafts/component-library-readiness.md): use-ref + use-layout-effect gain a SECOND SANCTIONED AUDIENCE — native component-library infrastructure doing measure-before-paint (popover/dropdown positioning, table viewport geometry): measure in the layout effect, compute placement with pure .cljc geometry, apply, clean up exactly; passive effect stays the home for listeners/deferrable work. ADDITIONAL DELIVERABLES: a guide recipe for this pattern + StrictMode/reconnect/HMR/JVM-metadata conformance fixtures exercised through a native (non-foreign-boundary) consumer. NO second layout-effect spelling ships (native alias only on repeated proven demand); component-did-* never returns. The interop contract draft (drafts/ui-react-interop-contract.md §1) carries the matching amendment.

title: Publish the load-bearing re-frame.ui Shadow configuration as a shipped integration contract
description:
## Problem

A consumer of `day8/re-frame2-ui` must configure both top-level Shadow settings:

```clojure
{:cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui}
 :build-defaults
 {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}}
```

The hook owns build transactions, version-zero retained-output invalidation, source reconciliation, and development digest-carrier projection. The cache blocker prevents invalidated UI-consuming sources from being restored from stale disk cache. Omitting either can publish incomplete or stale compiler authority, so configured UI builds deliberately fail closed.

The exact snippet and explanation exist only in the gitignored synthesis guide and internal Spec 004C. They are absent from shipped `docs/`, root installation guidance, and the public API/integration inventory. A fresh library consumer following tracked user-facing documentation can therefore install the artifact but cannot obtain a supported watch/HMR build. The hook must remain an internal integration verb rather than a general public API, but its required invocation and compatibility/version boundary are still a shipped contract.

## Required Correction

Publish one canonical re-frame.ui installation page containing the exact dependency and Shadow configuration, why both settings are load-bearing, supported Shadow version posture, failure diagnostics, and a minimal successful watch smoke. Link to it from the normal re-frame2 getting-started/UI entry points. Catalogue the build-hook integration surface with its intended stability boundary without presenting its implementation helpers as application APIs.

Coordinate with open canonical-guidance bead rf2-vxgfnd.179 to avoid parallel edits; this follow-up is narrower and specifically load-bearing.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tracked canonical user guide contains the exact top-level `:cache-blockers` and `:build-defaults/:build-hooks` form plus the `day8/re-frame2-ui` dependency.
- The guide explains the distinct correctness job of each setting, the supported Shadow version posture, and the fail-closed diagnostics for missing/misplaced configuration.
- Root/UI getting-started navigation reaches the page without relying on gitignored `ai/` material.
- The hook integration is catalogued/versioned as a required host seam while non-user implementation helpers remain internal.
- A docs/config drift gate compares the published snippet to the repository's own `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` wiring and a fresh minimal consumer build.
- Guidance remains compatible with stock Reagent's frozen tier and does not preserve UIx/Helix/slim as long-term alternatives.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — pin Shadow 3.4.10 as the sole supported version for the shipped re-frame.ui Shadow integration contract, explicitly marked pre-alpha / subject to change on deliberate retest. Widening to a range (Option B) is deferred until a multi-version test matrix exists (likely external-alpha prep).

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original recommendation + CComposer research) converge on A, and the evidence holds up: the hook is explicitly a "Shadow 3.4.10 build-lifecycle adapter" (build_hook.clj docstrings key off 3.4.10 compile stages, :compiled-at semantics, and output projection), Spec 004C section 2 already names 3.4.10, and every in-tree pin (implementation/package.json "shadow-cljs": "3.4.10", template {{shadow-version}}, tutorial) is lockstep. Promising a range (B) is an untested support contract and hostage to Shadow internal drift (.192 showed bridge-marker drift is real); shipping with no posture (C) leaves the acceptance criterion unmet and consumers guessing whether mismatches are bugs. A is honest, cheap, and strictly more useful — correct pre-alpha posture.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (docs work now dispatchable, coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.179):
- One canonical tracked installation/integration page for re-frame.ui: day8/re-frame2-ui dependency + the exact top-level Shadow settings {:cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}} — snippet must match implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (lines ~398-407) verbatim.
- State supported Shadow version = 3.4.10, pinned in BOTH package.json ("shadow-cljs": "3.4.10") and the deps.edn :shadow alias (thheller/shadow-cljs 3.4.10); include the pre-alpha disclaimer (other versions unsupported, may fail at compile or publish stale digests on warm start).
- Explain the distinct correctness job of each setting (hook = build transactions, version-zero retained-output invalidation, digest-carrier projection; blocker = prevents stale disk-cache restore of invalidated UI-consumer output) mirroring Spec 004C section 2 prose.
- Failure diagnostics section: :re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/cache-blocker-missing, carrier-output-invalid, and the fail-closed digest-carrier errors, each pointing at the missing/misplaced setting.
- Minimal watch smoke checklist for consumers; maintainers pointed at npm run test:ui-digest-carrier as the in-repo proof.
- Catalogue re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook as a required HOST INTEGRATION seam (versioned contract), NOT an application API; implementation helpers stay internal.
- Link from getting-started/UI entry points; no reliance on gitignored ai/ material.
- Drift gate per acceptance criteria: compare published snippet against implementation/shadow-cljs.edn wiring.
- rf2-vxgfnd.281 sequencing: the .281 scaffold (if executable) must embed these same two settings + the 3.4.10 pin verbatim from this page; if schematic, it links here rather than inventing a parallel recipe.
RESEARCH REPORT from the worker whose worktree I destroyed (2026-07-19); zero edits made, nothing lost. THIS BEAD IS READY TO DISPATCH IMMEDIATELY — ruling made, precedent in-tree, source to derive from already exists.

THE GAP IS TOTAL: zero hits for `cache-blockers` or `build-hooks` anywhere under docs/. No docs/ui/ directory, no UI installation or getting-started page. mkdocs.yml UI entries (lines 218, 219, 235) are all API reference; the only Installation nav entry (line 344) is Xray. The guidance exists ONLY in spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md §2.1.1 (load-bearing statement at line 200), the build_hook.clj docstring, and the example below. So .196 needs a NEW page plus a nav entry.

⚠️ THE MOST VALUABLE FIND: examples/ui/minimal-counter/ ALREADY EXISTS — a complete standalone consumer scaffold carrying both settings verbatim with a 15-line rationale comment ("Drop either and the dev build identity is false"). And implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke/test/scaffold_smoke_test.clj (242 lines) ALREADY does structurally what .196 asks: it PARSES THE FILE MANIFEST OUT OF THE README MARKDOWN AT RUN TIME, materialises only those files into a temp dir, runs real npm install + npx shadow-cljs compile app, then runs a PER-FILE OMISSION MATRIX (for each manifest file, rebuild without it and assert non-viability). That is both the derived-not-hand-copied precedent AND the per-arm red-before precedent, in-tree and passing.

⚠️ BUT IT CONTAINS THE EXACT DEFECT THIS BEAD IS ABOUT. Lines 110-117, shadow-config-carries-the-two-load-bearing-settings, HARDCODE the two settings as string literals in the test — a restatement of the rule rather than a comparison against the real config. That is the rf2-5e3ic failure mode (a gate that answers from its own copy of the truth). THE .196 DRIFT GATE MUST parse the snippet from the published docs page and compare it against BOTH implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (lines 423-424, top-level) AND examples/ui/minimal-counter/shadow-cljs.edn. Fixing the scaffold-smoke restatement is arguably in scope; say which you did.

MARKDOWN-AT-RUNTIME PRECEDENTS TO COPY: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/frame_destroyed_op_schema_jvm_test.clj (candidate-path vector for cwd-independence, anchor string + edn/read-string on the tail, SHAPE ASSERTION BEFORE ANY TEST ASSERTION — so a moved anchor reds instead of silently passing). For fenced code blocks specifically: guide_truth_jvm_test.clj and implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_guide_check.clj.

VERSION POSTURE already ruled in NOTES (3.4.10 sole supported, pre-alpha). Pins are lockstep: implementation/package.json:21, examples/ui/minimal-counter/deps.edn:39, template {{shadow-version}}.
DELIVERED PR #6390 (2026-07-19). Page: docs/core/how-to/install-re-frame-ui.md, nav Core > How-to recipes (first row). Gate: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/shadow_config_contract_jvm_test.clj — derives expected values from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn + examples/ui/minimal-counter/shadow-cljs.edn at run time; NO literal expected value in the test. Version posture derived from the page's :shadow alias vs implementation/package.json + scaffold deps.edn. FIXED the scaffold_smoke_test.clj lines 110-117 restatement (now derived). title: Replace the remaining synthetic digest-carrier obligations with real Shadow host gates
description:
## Problem

PR #5806's digest-carrier gate is valuable but several explicit proof obligations remain synthetic or vacuous, so CI can stay green while host integration drifts:

- Warm-cache version-zero reconstruction is exercised with a handcrafted compiler map, not by stopping one Shadow daemon and starting a second against the first daemon's disk cache.
- No-pass REPL isolation manually binds compiler state rather than driving an actual Shadow CLJS REPL compile/evaluate action.
- The two-build test constructs build A fully and then build B fully; it does not overlap two build lifecycles inside one daemon and cannot expose ambient compiler-env cross-routing.
- Production elision is grepped only in the node-script `:ui-bench` bundle and does not force an advanced browser consumer of the digest/descriptor path, so browser-specific retention can remain unobserved.

CLOSED rf2-vxgfnd.108 later added zero-carrier and hookless-build cases; do not duplicate them. This bead owns only the still-missing real-host dimensions above.

## Required Correction

Replace each synthetic/vacuous arm with the smallest deterministic integration falsifier through the real Shadow 3.4.10 entry point. Reuse one fixture project and process harness where practical. The tests must make their control mutation fail, so green proves the intended host boundary rather than merely reimplementing the production helper in test code.
acceptance_criteria:
- A two-daemon test performs a successful first build, stops the daemon, starts a fresh daemon on the same disk cache, and proves complete byte-identical compiler/client digest reconstruction without a clean.
- A real Shadow CLJS REPL action exercises macroexpand/never-evaluated/runtime-failed/successful no-pass edits and proves none mutate the finalized build digest; the next saved build reconciles source truth.
- Two configured builds overlap within one Shadow daemon with distinct build ids and source sets; accepted/scratch/carrier state remains isolated under deterministic interleaving.
- An advanced browser build contains an explicit dev digest/descriptor consumer in source yet emits no carrier, sentinel, `bd1-` literal, registry traversal, reload producer, or debug-manifest residue.
- Each arm has a documented mutation/revert that makes it fail while narrower unit tests remain green.
- Existing real-browser initial/warm/lazy/failure/recovery, JVM compiler, artifact-isolation, and production-performance gates remain green without adding a second authority.
notes:
PARTIAL via PR #6030 (merged): shipped the NOTES-prioritized final-schedule real-host arm (Shadow hook deep-merge/order, build-local :compile-prepare, seq+parallel scheduling, output-marker retention, fail-loud on missing schedule evidence; red-when-disabled proven). 4 broader DESCRIPTION obligations REMAIN: two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, real REPL isolation, overlapping build lifecycles in one daemon, advanced-browser elision consumer. Bead stays open for those.
RESEARCH REPORT from the worker whose worktree I destroyed (2026-07-19). It had made ZERO edits, so nothing was lost; all findings verified against source before deletion.

⚠️ #6030 CLOSED NONE OF THE FOUR DESCRIPTION ARMS. It shipped a FIFTH arm (final-schedule) never in the DESCRIPTION list. Each original obligation confirmed still synthetic:
  1. TWO-DAEMON WARM CACHE — compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj:155 accepted-warm-prepare-preserves-output-present-ui-consumer hand-builds a shadow-state map and hand-sets :cached true. NO daemon restart exists anywhere in the tree.
  2. REAL REPL ISOLATION — compiler_build_hook_jvm_test.clj and build_repl_hmr_convergence_jvm_test.clj both manually `binding` compiler state. No real REPL is driven.
  3. OVERLAPPING BUILDS — compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj:885 interleaved-build-values-carry-isolated-digests builds A fully THEN B fully. Sequential — exactly the defect the bead describes. Cannot expose ambient compiler-env cross-routing.
  4. ADVANCED-BROWSER ELISION — partially covered, NOT closed. The residue scan is real but lives inline in implementation/scripts/run-ui-bench.cjs:209-224 over out/ui-bench.js. Two gaps: ui-bench is :node-script (shadow-cljs.edn:797), NOT a browser target; and its forbidden list is only [__RF2_UI_DIGEST_XX__, bd1-, digest_carrier], omitting the sentinel/registry-traversal/reload-producer/debug-manifest residue the bead names. No source actually CONSUMES the digest path, so elision has nothing to elide.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE WHOLE PATTERN: compiler_digest_carrier_jvm_test.clj (924 lines, 21 deftests) drives build-hook/hook against a handcrafted map built by the private shadow-state/two-source-state helpers (lines 34-82).

HARNESS GUIDANCE FOR RE-DISPATCH — STAY NODE-SIDE. The established real-host pattern spawns the real CLI: spawnHarnessProcess from implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs, resolving require.resolve(shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js). Two existing consumers: check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs (839 lines, Playwright, port 8059) and check-ui-final-schedule.cjs (#6030 arm, documented TEETH list in its header). ⚠️ ARM 2 IS THE RISK: a real CLJS REPL needs a connected JS runtime; driving it non-interactively on Windows is research-grade. Sequence it LAST or split it out.

SCOPE RECOMMENDATION (worker, and I agree): SPLIT THIS BEAD. Four arms are four distinct real-host mechanisms, not variations on one — #6030 spent a whole PR on a single arm, the strongest available evidence for the right unit of work. Suggested: arms 1+3 together (shared daemon-lifecycle harness), arm 4 alone (cheap, independent), arm 2 solo and last.

BASELINE MEASURED IN-WORKTREE BEFORE DELETION: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs = 168 passed; npm install exit 0. Hot-zone (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, deps.edn) was FREE at 02:25 AUSEST.
✅ ARM 4 DELIVERED in PR #6413 (advanced-browser elision consumer). THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN for arms 1, 2 and 3, which the worker read, confirmed against the research report, and deliberately did not touch.

REMAINING: (1) two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, (2) real REPL isolation — research-grade on Windows, sequence LAST, (3) overlapping build lifecycles in one daemon. Arms 1+3 share the daemon-lifecycle harness; do them together. Do NOT go in-process: verified that no deps.edn alias puts thheller/shadow-cljs on a test JVM classpath and nothing calls shadow.cljs.devtools.api/.server in-process.

⚠️ ARM 4 FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION BUG, filed as rf2-vxgfnd.299: re-frame.ui.client/descriptor and /descriptor-index carry NO goog.DEBUG gate, so the registry traversal and the :build-digest keyword SURVIVE AN ADVANCED BROWSER RELEASE — exactly the browser-specific retention this bead predicted and the old :node-script scan could never observe. implementation/ui/src/** was fenced from #6413, so the leak is PINNED PRESENT with a self-announcing failure message rather than silently tolerated; that pin also serves as the production non-vacuity floor. Fixing .299 requires updating the pin in the same PR.

⚠️ THE ORACLE FOR ANY FUTURE ARM — both simple greps are WRONG, measured:
  - goog.DEBUG-count: appeared 225 times in a release where the surface was fully eliminated (all docstrings from var reification).
  - Function-name grep: Closure INLINES small fns, so stage_BANG_ and cell stay absent even with their gates REMOVED; before_load/after_load never appear in a DEBUG=true control at all. #6413 built this oracle, measured it, and REMOVED it rather than ship passengers that can never go red.
  USE INSTEAD: a CONTROL BUILD — same entry, same :advanced level, goog.DEBUG the ONLY variable — asserting each sentinel PRESENT in the control and ABSENT in production, string literals only (Closure never rewrites them, so they survive inlining). PLUS a token asserted PRESENT in the production bundle to catch a production-side mis-target the control cannot distinguish from real elision.
  Root consumers BY CALL, not by var — exporting by var keeps an empty fn alive and reports a leak no real consumer has. Keep the fixture HOOKLESS or the sentinel gets patched into a bd1- digest and the grep passes for the wrong reason. Rename teeth must use PREFIX changes: a suffix extension still contains the original.

ARM 4 SHIPPED NO HOT-ZONE CHANGE: no build-id or :dev-http port added (fixture carries its own config, per the digest_probe/{hookless,final_schedule} precedent), no workflow change, 172-assertion pin unmoved.
MAYOR ASSESSMENT (2026-07-20): arms 1-4 SHIPPED (d1e3c256cf real-Shadow-host-gates + e005987bd6 arm-4 advanced-browser-consumer; #6030 shipped a 5th final-schedule arm). REMAINING = (1) two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, (2) real REPL isolation — the bead itself flags these 'research-grade on Windows.' ⚠️ HELD FROM BLIND DISPATCH — needs scoping first: rf2-tm1xi (#6503, MERGED-pending) just shipped a REAL 8-pass Shadow warm-watch fixture that DELIBERATELY does SINGLE-build identity (per the 4vm19 Arm-1 ruling, explicitly NOT two-build isolation). QUESTION before dispatching .195's remainder: does tm1xi's single-build warm-watch fixture already discharge the INTENT of the two-daemon reconstruction (proving warm-cache topology survives real rebuilds), making the literal two-daemon arm redundant/over-engineered? Or is two-daemon genuinely needed for something single-build can't prove? This is a scope call — if two-daemon is research-grade-Windows-hard AND tm1xi covers the intent, the remainder may be closeable-as-covered (trust-the-programmer/no-gold-plating posture favors NOT building research-grade infra for a property already proven). Recommend: assess against merged #6503 before any dispatch; likely a Mike scope-confirmation or a close-as-covered. Do NOT dispatch a worker onto two-daemon Windows reconstruction without that determination.
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-20 08:34 AUSEST)

RULING: Close as covered — all three remaining arms (two-daemon warm-cache reconstruction, real REPL isolation, overlapping builds in one daemon). Scope correction first: the 2026-07-20 mayor note said "arms 1-4 SHIPPED"; in fact #6413/e005987bd6 shipped arm 4 and #6030/d1e3c256cf shipped a fifth (final-schedule) arm — arms 1, 2, 3 were the true remainder, and each closes for cause below. No new fixtures, no new beads.

ARM 1 (two-daemon): the AC as written ("byte-identical digest reconstruction from disk cache without a clean") targets a path the shipped architecture deliberately refuses. Verified at build_hook.clj:481-525: validate-ui-cache-blocker! throws unless dev UI builds declare :cache-blockers #{re-frame.ui} ("refusing a plausible but incomplete warm-cache digest"), and reset-cold-ui-consumer-output evicts retained UI-consumer output on every fresh daemon (accepted version 0), forcing real macroexpansion recompile. A restarted daemon never trusts the cache for the digest; it reconverges through the same real compile machinery #6030 and #6503 already prove against a live Shadow 3.4.10 daemon. Cache-shape drift (only possible via a deliberate pin bump) fails loud through three classified tripwires: the cache-blocker throw, output-marker classification, and missing-pass-provenance — the last proven red on the real host in #6030.

HONEST RECORD of what is NOT literally exercised: no gate restores a populated disk cache into a fresh JVM. #6503's fixture wipes .shadow-cljs/out before starting (check-ui-warm-watch.cjs:444-447), so all its warm passes are in-memory within one daemon lifetime — the answer to the mayor's literal question ("does tm1xi's fixture exercise the two-daemon path?") is no. The intent is discharged by architecture (refuse-and-recompile + loud tripwires), not by that fixture. Related: install-re-frame-ui.md:118 says "npm run test:ui-digest-carrier is the in-repo proof" adjacent to the step-3 warm-restart smoke — that sentence overstates warm-restart coverage; mayor may fold a one-line softening into a doc pass or leave it, since step 3 itself correctly instructs the manual restart smoke.

ARM 2 (real REPL): structurally enforced — no-pass REPL contributions go to a separate repl-overlay seeded from the accepted snapshot, never feed accepted registries or the digest, cleared on next prepare — and unit-pinned (compiler_build_hook_jvm_test.clj pins non-publication + clearing). A non-interactive connected-runtime Windows REPL harness is research-grade infrastructure for a dev-only, structurally-enforced property: declined as gold-plating.

ARM 3 (overlapping builds): the carrier keeps no ambient JVM state to cross-route (per-build compiler-env, no process-global authority; the two process atoms are test-harness fallbacks never consulted under a real compile). A real overlapping fixture would test pinned Shadow's internal per-build isolation, not a re-frame2 seam — the compiler-side analog of the topology rf2-4vm19 ruled not worth testing, and exactly the architecturally-refused-topology test the posture names as the trap.

RIDER (must survive this bead's closure): any future Shadow pin bump (currently pinned 3.4.10) MUST include one manual warm-restart smoke of a UI dev build before merge — stop a watch with output retained, restart it, app renders and digest finalizes; a process note on the bump PR, not new infrastructure. Mayor: on closure, record this via `bd remember` so it outlives the bead. The consumer-facing procedure already exists at docs/core/how-to/install-re-frame-ui.md steps 1-4 ("Prove it works", step 3).

OPINIONS WEIGHED: followed the dossier's primary Recommendation (Option A) over Codex's Option B (bounded restart pass) because B's only purchase is pin-bump CI insurance on a pinned dependency, bought with a permanent fixture plus an extra cold JVM boot in the gate forever — priced as gold-plating under the pre-alpha posture, with the rider covering the same residual.

FOR THE MAYOR: recommend closing rf2-vxgfnd.195 as covered, citing this block; record the rider via bd remember at closure. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-vxgfnd.195.two-daemon-scope.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization.

title: plan(ui S5): route the prepared Spec-011 UI-tree amendment into the active authority graph
description:
## Problem

The suite contains a prepared, anchor-verified Stage-5 amendment at `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/spec-011-ui-tree-amendment.md`, but it is absent from the active authority/navigation graph:

- `12-implementation-plan.md:159-163` does not name it for S5.
- Open S5 epic `rf2-vxgfnd.97` does not cite it.
- The synthesis README inventory mentions the 004/006/selector drafts but omits this Spec-011 amendment and does not provide top-level navigation for the `prep/`, `skill/`, and `spikes/` asset groups.
- No tracked inbound reference names the amendment.

A fresh Stage-5 worker can miss the prepared contract change, re-author it inconsistently, or land SSR roots without the intended Spec-011 integration. Because future-stage leaf beads must be filed from then-current contracts rather than memory, an unreachable draft is effectively absent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enter the synthesis through its README and follow the S5 row in `12-implementation-plan.md`.
2. Open the Stage-5 epic `rf2-vxgfnd.97`.
3. Search all tracked docs and beads for `spec-011-ui-tree-amendment.md`.
4. Observe that none of those entry points reaches the prepared amendment.
5. Enumerate the 54 tracked synthesis files and observe whole asset groups lack a classified top-level route/consumer.

## Deliverable

Add the Spec-011 amendment to the S5 authority chain and classify every active synthesis asset group by stage, consumer, and status. At minimum, link the amendment from the plan and S5 epic with its merge boundary/anchors, and update the README inventory so a fresh reader can reach drafts, prep, guide, skill, spikes, and reviews without filesystem archaeology.

Do not pre-file S5 leaf implementation beads or re-open ratified decisions. This is preparation/navigation so the leaf briefs can later be filed from the correct current contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The S5 plan and `rf2-vxgfnd.97` both cite the prepared Spec-011 amendment and state when it is consumed/promoted.
- The README provides a complete classified inventory of all tracked synthesis asset groups.
- Every active draft/prep artifact has an explicit stage consumer; every non-active artifact is marked historical/superseded.
- A clean-clone reader can navigate from README -> S5 -> Spec-011 amendment without search.
- A lightweight inventory check detects an active artifact with zero inbound authority/consumer classification.
- No future-stage leaf beads are created early and no frozen API/decision changes are made.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent completeness review of PR #5800 exact head `ef4225e3b01a411eb6ceaa763a9a81dfb1e2b630` confirmed all 54 synthesis files are tracked and durable but found this orphaned active asset. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`. Full all-status inventory found no bead that owns this amendment's S5 integration.

title: migration(ui): collapse the competing 36-rule and 34-rule W1 authorities into one rulebook
description:
## Problem

The tracked migration work has two incompatible documents claiming normative authority over the same W1 rewrite program:

- `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md:3,1019` says W1 implements 36 `R-*` rules.
- `prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md:4` tells the W1 worker to start from that table.
- `prep/w2-migration-skill-extension.md:13` declares its 34 `MIG-*` rules normative.
- The open implementation bead `rf2-gria2b` points only to the 34-rule prep table.

There is no complete 36-to-34 mapping, no explicit retirement record for unmatched rules, and no precedence law. A worker can implement either apparently authoritative rulebook and satisfy one document while silently omitting or duplicating another rule. PR #5833 edits the 36-rule document but, while inspected, did not establish one authority or a complete mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin W1 from `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md`; enumerate 36 `R-*` obligations.
2. Begin from the open W1 implementation bead/prep table; enumerate 34 `MIG-*` obligations.
3. Attempt to map them by number or heading.
4. Observe there is no normative crosswalk and unmatched/split/merged rules have no explicit disposition.
5. Follow W2's statement that its MIG table is normative; this conflicts with the draft's claim that W1 implements the R table.

## Deliverable

Choose one normative migration rulebook for W1/W2/S6 and make every active plan, README, skill-extension brief, and implementation bead point to it. Add a complete, reviewable mapping from each superseded rule to exactly one current rule, an intentional split/merge, or an explicit retirement with reason. Mark the non-authoritative document historical/supporting and remove language that grants it equal force.

Prefer the smallest representation: one canonical table plus a temporary crosswalk. Do not maintain two synchronized normative rule systems.

## Acceptance Criteria

- W1, W2, S6, README, skill preparation, and open implementation beads name one canonical rulebook.
- Every one of the 36 R rules and 34 MIG rules appears in a checked crosswalk with current canonical ID or explicit retirement.
- No rule is silently omitted, duplicated, or assigned two incompatible automation classes.
- A worker can implement or test a rule without resolving document precedence.
- The crosswalk has a bounded completeness check (unique source IDs, unique/current targets where required, explicit split/merge cardinality).
- The historical rulebook cannot be mistaken for live implementation authority.

## Evidence and provenance

Independent completeness review of PR #5800 exact head `ef4225e3b01a411eb6ceaa763a9a81dfb1e2b630` found this conflict. It persists on current `origin/main` `f5a4381ff5ada6928281f05b8d1611a11e7880b4`; no merged later correction was found. Full all-status inventory found no matching live or closed decision/implementation bead.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — `ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/prep/w1-migrator-rule-table.md` (MIG-01…34) is the single canonical W1/W2/S6 rulebook; `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md` (36 R-*) becomes historical/supporting, with a complete R->MIG crosswalk so nothing is silently dropped.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original recommendation + CComposer independent read) converge on A, and independent verification confirms the pillars: the R-* doc self-labels "DRAFT — not merged" and is pedagogical in shape (before/after/trap per rule), while the MIG table is machine-actionable (detector/transform/tier/ordering — the shape a rewrite-clj worker implements), independently derived from ratified specs (doc-10, 11 W1 row, Spec 004/004B/004C) plus the shipped `ui.cljc` surface, and is what the live chain (rf2-gria2b, w2-migration-skill-extension.md "normative on rewrite mechanics") already names. Option B re-points live artefacts at a self-labelled draft in the wrong document shape; Option C re-authors what is already near-canonical (gold-plating). The mandatory crosswalk protects CORRECTNESS in either direction; A wins on CLARITY (one live authority), ELEGANCE (smallest representation: one table + temporary crosswalk), and GOOD PRACTICE (least churn).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
1. Crosswalk: add `prep/r-to-mig-crosswalk.md` (or a section appended to the canonical table) mapping every R-01..R-X* id to exactly one of: a MIG-id, an intentional split/merge (cardinality stated), or retired-with-reason. Include the reverse direction: every MIG-only rule (no R source) noted as such. Bounded completeness check per the bead's acceptance criteria: all 36 R ids and all 34 MIG ids appear exactly once as sources; targets unique/current where required.
2. Starting map (CComposer preliminary — VERIFY, do not trust): merges R-C1+R-C2+R-C6->MIG-01; R-T3 + loop facets of R-H7/R-Q1->MIG-08; R-C3+R-C4+R-S1->MIG-16; R-H3+R-H4->MIG-18; R-X2+R-X3(+R-S4)->MIG-20. MIG-only: 03, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31, 32, 33. Likely retirements needing explicit disposition: R-T5, R-T10, R-Q2, R-M2 (-> reagent-compat-boundary.md concern), R-S3, R-X7.
3. Banner `drafts/migrator-rewrite-rules.md` as historical/supporting ("pedagogical catalogue; normative automation spec = w1-migrator-rule-table.md") and strip its lines claiming W1 implements the 36 R rules (header + ~line 1019).
4. Sweep W1/W2/S6 surfaces so only the MIG table is named normative: w2-migration-skill-extension.md (already correct), 11-adoption-workstreams.md W1 row, README/skill prep in new-substrate-synthesis, epic rf2-vxgfnd.98 text if it cites the R draft. Do NOT amend rf2-gria2b's description (already points only at the MIG table); note its "MAYOR CHECKOUT ONLY" caveat is stale — all three docs are git-tracked on main.
5. Escalation trigger: if the crosswalk finds an R rule whose mechanical obligation is missing from every MIG row and cannot be retired with reason, add it to the MIG table as a new numbered row (per-rule addition), not an authority flip; surface the addition in the PR description.
6. Acceptance = the bead's existing criteria: one named authority everywhere, checked crosswalk, no silent omission/duplication, historical doc unmistakable as non-live.
AUDIT CONTRACT INPUT 2026-07-17 (PR #6024; coordinate with rf2-vxgfnd.95.14): the canonical MIG rulebook must absorb two shipped S3 rulings while the R->MIG authority is consolidated.

1. Atomic local: any `swap!`/multi-writer migration must target the third tuple member `update!`, which applies to latest host state. Never emit `(set-a! (f a ...))` over a committed render value; `set!` stores its argument exactly, including function values.
2. C-13a: ordinary function props on INTERNAL defview call sites are legal opaque identity-compared values with no implicit invocation phase. MIG-27 must not call every such prop a compile error or gate/rewrite it automatically. It may recommend data intent for serializability or `ui/handler`/`ui/render-fn` where a phase/stable identity is required, while preserving foreign bare-fn rejection and the narrow native-event shorthand.

The checked crosswalk/one-rulebook work must make these semantics explicit and add truth fixtures; rf2-vxgfnd.95.14 owns current Spec/skill prose, not the migrator implementation.

title: Define UI render batches by host checkpoint, not router drain
description:
## Problem

PR #5790 replaces the false “one render per epoch” model with “one render batch at drain quiescence.” The first half is correct—epochs are write/evidence units, not render triggers—but the replacement names a router boundary the implementation does not observe.

The re-frame.ui scheduler has no hook from router drain finalization. Its boundary is a dirty-cell pending window:

- on CLJS, the first mark schedules one host microtask and every mark before that checkpoint folds into the same window;
- on JVM/headless, scheduling is inert and pending cells fold until an explicit test/host flush;
- listener re-entry after a batch has been completed can open another pending window without a new router drain.

Therefore one drain's entire queued write-side cascade always coalesces, but several distinct `dispatch-sync!` drains in the same JavaScript stack—and nested cross-frame drains—also coalesce before the same microtask. Host-yield-separated drains do not. Spec 004/006, Conventions, the glossary, reactive docstrings, and epoch-test banners currently state the stronger false rule that render separation follows each drain.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On PR #5790's exact head `dd83a720849f72ec4510518e70606ca403ca84e0`, run two independent `dispatch-sync!` calls back-to-back without yielding.
2. On CLJS, both drains complete before the scheduled UI microtask; one later notification batch advances the dirty cell once.
3. On JVM, after both drains the cell remains revision 0, notification count 0, dirty with one pending entry; one explicit flush produces revision 1 and one notification.
4. Drive a nested cross-frame synchronous drain and observe the same pending window.
5. In a listener, re-mark after phase-1 completion; a fresh batch is scheduled even though no router drain began.
6. Inspect `reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc`: it calls `mark-dirty!` and `flush-pending!` directly, so it cannot prove a router-drain boundary.

Later `rf2-vxgfnd.12.1` added the open-drain test-flush guard; retain that fix, but it does not couple automatic scheduling to drain finalization.

## Required Correction

Define the production boundary honestly as the pending read/render window ending at the next CLJS host microtask or explicit headless/test flush. State the guaranteed relationship: a synchronous drain cannot be split, while multiple drains before the same host checkpoint may share one read/render batch. This is both simpler and at least as efficient as per-drain flushing.

Reconcile all active contract/docstring/test wording and add real-router fixtures. Coordinate with open `rf2-vxgfnd.12`, which owns the queued-cascade and real-yield mounted gates; do not duplicate its harness. If exact one-batch-per-router-drain separation is instead required, that is a different contract and needs an explicit drain-finalization seam rather than timing inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Active specs, Conventions, glossary, implementation docstrings, and test banners define one pending read/render window closed by the next CLJS microtask or explicit headless/test flush; none equates every router-drain completion with a batch boundary.
- The contract says one drain's queued writes cannot split, several synchronous/nested drains before one checkpoint may coalesce, and host-yield-separated drains cannot.
- Real-router mounted tests cover a queued child cascade, two sequential no-yield drains, host-yield-separated drains, nested cross-frame drains, listener re-marking after completion, and JVM multiple drains before one explicit flush.
- The sequential and nested cases prove one notification/revision/root commit batch; the host-yield case proves two.
- The existing open-drain `ui.test/flush!` rejection remains green and is not misdescribed as the automatic scheduling boundary.
- The implementation remains one write-side drain-to-quiescence followed by a coalesced read/render opportunity; no per-epoch render trigger, global coordinator, or public API is added.
- Relevant S2 gates, browser tests, JVM UI, node UI, docs, and production-elision checks pass.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — the render-batch contract is defined by the host checkpoint: the pending read/render window ends at the next CLJS host microtask or an explicit headless/test flush. Strict one-batch-per-router-drain separation is REJECTED; no drain-finalization seam is to be built.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (decision file + CComposer) recommend A, and the evidence verifies in-repo: the scheduler boundary in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc is the first-dirty-mark microtask CAS (flush-scheduled?); router.cljc's only late-bound flush is the DEBUG-only :live-frame/flush-projection! hook, not a UI-scheduler seam; and no consumer needs per-drain painting (run-to-completion, Spec 002 render boundaries, and Pattern-LongRunningWork all state weaker guarantees that A preserves). A is honest (docs match code), simpler (no new router->scheduler coupling), and strictly more efficient — coalescing N same-stack drains into one batch is a win. B would add coupling to make the framework slower for a guarantee nobody asked for. CORRECTNESS + CLARITY favour truing up the prose; ELEGANCE + GOOD PRACTICE reject machinery for an unrequested contract.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: Contract wording: "a render batch is the pending read/render window ending at the next CLJS host microtask checkpoint or an explicit headless/test flush." Guarantees to state: (1) a synchronous run-to-completion drain cannot be split across batches; (2) N epochs/events within one drain coalesce to one batch; (3) multiple drains (or listener re-entry) completing before the same host checkpoint may share one batch; (4) drains separated by a host yield render separately. Retire "one batch per router drain" as normative — keep only as the common case when callers yield between drains. Surfaces: spec/004-Views.md, Spec 006 invariant 6, spec/Conventions.md, glossary, reactive.cljc (ns docstring section on drain coalescing, the S2d comment block, and schedule-flush!'s "one microtask per drain" wording — it is armed by the first mark and fires at the checkpoint, folding any number of drains), viewcell.cljs docstring, reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc banners ("separate drain" cases must use a real host yield, not a second same-task flush-pending!). Tests per the acceptance criteria: real-router mounted fixtures — back-to-back dispatch-sync! with no yield -> one notification/revision/commit; host-yield-separated drains -> two; nested cross-frame drains -> one; listener re-mark after completion opens a fresh pending window with no new drain; JVM multiple drains before one explicit flush -> one. Keep the rf2-vxgfnd.12.1 open-drain ui.test/flush! rejection green and do not describe it as the automatic scheduling boundary. Coordinate with open rf2-vxgfnd.12 (owns queued-cascade + real-yield mounted gates) — reuse its harness, do not duplicate G-3/G-13 infrastructure. No new public API, no per-epoch render trigger, no global coordinator. Option B is reserved for a future bead only if a NAMED consumer proves it needs per-drain rendering within one synchronous stack — that would be a new explicit contract with accepted performance cost.

title: Stop treating a microtask checkpoint as exact React commit identity
description:
## Problem

PR #5789 tries to distinguish React StrictMode's layout-effect replay from a genuine Activity hide/reveal by marking disconnect provisional until the next host microtask. It then treats any reconnect before that microtask as a same-commit StrictMode replay.

That inference is too strong. A microtask separates JavaScript checkpoints, not React commits. Two real commits can complete synchronously in the same stack:

```javascript
flushSync(() => setMode("hidden"));
flushSync(() => setMode("visible"));
```

React tears down layout effects in the first commit and recreates them in the second before the queued settle microtask runs. On exact head `93a903da12a5fe53f08e1d62caeba51df5e22bd6`, `connect!` sees the still-provisional flag and leaves the real hide interval `:disconnected {:reason :unknown}`. The existing Activity browser fixture inserts a microtask between hide and reveal, so it cannot expose this ambiguity.

The runtime remains ownership-correct; the defect is observability truth. Comments/docstrings currently say only same-commit replay can reconnect before settlement and that a genuine reveal always arrives later. Those claims are false.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Mount a sub-bearing view inside React 19 Activity in visible mode.
2. In one synchronous stack, call `flushSync` once to hide and again to reveal, without awaiting a microtask.
3. Observe two completed commits and layout-effect `cleanup` followed by `setup`.
4. Read the ViewCell intervals after the second commit and after the settle microtask.
5. The interval remains `:unknown`; the runtime has classified the sequence as indistinguishable from replay despite the two real host commits.

A real StrictMode setup→cleanup→setup replay is the control and should also avoid a fabricated Activity proof.

## Required Correction

Treat the provisional flag as what it actually proves: a conservative same-checkpoint/unsettled reconnect heuristic. Remove every claim that it identifies an exact React commit, uniquely identifies StrictMode, or proves that all genuine reveals occur in later tasks. Add the consecutive-`flushSync` Activity case as executable evidence and accept `:unknown` where the host supplies no exact discriminator.

If complete attribution is required later, introduce authoritative host/commit evidence and prove it against both React sequences; do not replace one timing heuristic with another or assume render-capture identity differs on every Activity reveal.

- A real React StrictMode replay control remains unannotated; no `:activity-hidden` fact is fabricated.
- Delayed Activity reveal still produces `:activity-hidden {:proof :reconnect}` under the existing settled-evidence contract.
- Source and owning contract prose consistently call pre-microtask reconnect unsettled/same-checkpoint evidence, not exact same-commit or uniquely StrictMode evidence.
- Any future complete-attribution path uses an authoritative host signal and proves consecutive commits, StrictMode replay, delayed reveal, repeated cycles, and root teardown precedence.
- Lease balance, root ownership, and dead/unmounted behavior remain unchanged; browser and lifecycle suites pass.

title: Give conflicting custom-element declarations one deterministic law
description:
## Problem

The custom-element registry accepts conflicting declarations for the same tag from multiple sources and currently has two different winner laws. Direct registration publishes the last evaluated call immediately. Reload commit rebuilds the aggregate from ledger rows in sorted owner order. An unrelated reload can therefore flip the effective property manifest without either conflicting declaration changing.

Deterministic current sequence:

```clojure
(register-custom-element! :x-el {:properties #{:z}} 'z.ns)
(register-custom-element! :x-el {:properties #{:a}} 'a.ns)
;; direct effective properties => #{:a}

(notify-reload!)
(note-reloaded-sources! ['unrelated.ns])
(commit-reload!)
;; sorted rebuild effective properties => #{:z}
```

This makes compiler/runtime property classification dependent on evaluation and unrelated reload order. It also obscures which source owns a contradiction.

## Required correction

Define one closed, deterministic cross-source declaration law used by initial evaluation, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, and aggregate rebuild. Recommended pre-alpha shape: rf=-equal duplicate declarations may co-exist; conflicting declarations fail atomically with both source/build anchors and leave the last-known-good aggregate unchanged. If a merge/winner law is chosen instead, it must be deterministic and semantically justified for every field—not last-call or incidental sort order.

Conflicts discovered during a reload must not partially publish or evict the previous valid manifest. The compiler must apply the same law before lowering consumers. Do not add silent precedence configuration or per-render conflict resolution.

## Proof discipline

Permute source names, evaluation orders, build identities, clean builds, and unrelated reloads. Every permutation must yield the same valid manifest or the same anchored conflict. The current unrelated-reload flip must fail before the fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal duplicate declarations are handled by one documented deterministic rule.
- Conflicting declarations either fail atomically with both source/build anchors (recommended) or follow one explicitly ratified deterministic merge law across all fields.
- Direct initial registration, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, and aggregate rebuild use the same rule.
- An unrelated reload cannot change the effective manifest for an untouched tag.
- A conflicting reload preserves the last-known-good manifest and does not partially publish ledger/aggregate state.
- All source/evaluation/build/reload-order permutations produce identical output or identical conflict evidence.
- No silent last-writer/sort-order precedence, per-render lookup, public configuration surface, or compatibility fallback is introduced.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — fail-atomically on conflict. For a given [build-id tag], the effective declaration is the unique value contributed by live sources iff every cross-source pair is rf=-equal; any non-rf=-equal same-tag declaration from a different source fails atomically with BOTH [build-id ns-sym] anchors (plus :file/:line on compiler paths), leaving the last-known-good aggregate unchanged. One law across all four paths: initial eval, compiler manifest aggregation, staged reload, aggregate rebuild. Option B (merge/winner) is rejected; no silent precedence, no configuration knob, no per-render resolution.

RATIONALE: Both the bead recommendation and the independent CComposer review converge on A, and code inspection confirms the premises: register-custom-element! (rules.cljc ~813) is last-call-wins write-through, rebuild-live! (~794) is a sorted-owner merge, and the compiler aggregate (build.cljc ~324) merges with no conflict check — three silent precedence paths, not two. A is the only total law that removes order dependence (CORRECTNESS), surfaces the contradiction to its owning sources instead of masking an ownership mistake (CLARITY), reuses existing infrastructure — contribute-checked!, the staged/commit last-known-good boundary, the rf= duplicate posture, the :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict error shape — rather than inventing per-field merge semantics (ELEGANCE), and matches the pre-alpha fail-closed posture (GOOD PRACTICE). No corpus case shows two sources legitimately contributing different property sets to one tag; property-set union would silently change SSR/hydration classification.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- rf=-equal duplicates coexist (idempotent); same-source re-declaration replaces per [build-id ns-sym] ledger row and is never a conflict (a source never conflicts with itself).
- Compiler macro expansion: switch the elements registry contribution from build/contribute! to build/contribute-checked! (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc); conflict-fn returns the existing decl when (not (eq/rf= existing v)).
- Compiler effective/aggregate: the rebuild aggregation must DETECT non-rf=-equal cross-source collisions, not rely on merge order.
- Runtime direct registration (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/rules.cljc register-custom-element!): before write-through, check the effective aggregate excluding own source; on conflict, anchored error, no assoc — the conflicting row never enters the ledger.
- Runtime rebuild-live!: replace the blind sorted merge with a conflict-checked fold; on conflict abort the rebuild and retain prior @custom-elements (defence in depth — no rebuild path ever picks a winner).
- Reload commit (commit-reload!): a staged source introducing a cross-source conflict must reject atomically — element-sources and custom-elements both stay at the pre-conflict snapshot; no partial publish.
- Error ids: compile-time :rf.ui.compile/custom-element-conflict (roster alongside :rf.ui.compile/bad-custom-element) and runtime :rf.error/custom-element-conflict mirroring :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict shape (:tag plus a :declarations vector of {:build :ns :properties}). Add Spec 009 catalogue rows for the new error ids.
- Acceptance: per the bead AC — permute source names, eval order, build ids, clean builds, and unrelated reloads; every permutation yields the identical manifest or identical anchored conflict evidence. The decision-file repro (unrelated reload flipping #{:a} to #{:z}) must be impossible: the second conflicting registration fails at its own registration point, so the ledger never holds both rows.

Deliberately did NOT ship a half-law: silently refusing a conflicting direct registration is first-wins = a THIRD order-dependent precedence rule, not a fix.

title: Make custom-element declarations deterministic compiler inputs
description:
## Problem

PR #5783 (head f68ba62b7aae69b315253fd1ea58e06ca768f2fd; merge db31f0288d223708d255cfe8b272a48f7c7f9c1d) wires runtime reload evidence for custom-element declarations, but compile-time property lowering still depends on declaration evaluation order.

A view compiled before `(ui/custom-element :x-card {:properties #{:model}})` sees no declaration and emits `:model` as an HTML attribute. The same forms in the opposite order emit a JS property. Cross-namespace declarations are worse: changing only the declaration namespace updates the runtime ledger but need not recompile dependent views, so already-baked literal property lowering remains stale. The current build digest/fingerprint projection includes view triples but not the effective custom-element declaration input that influenced their lowering.

Deterministic clean-build example:

```clojure
(ui/defview card [] [:x-card {:model model}])
(ui/custom-element :x-card {:properties #{:model}})
```

Reversing the two forms changes emitted behavior. Parallel source ordering can do the same. A declaration-only warm HMR edit may leave consumers unlike a clean build.

This violates deterministic compilation and the clean-build equals warm-build HMR law. Silently imposing declaration-before-use would be brittle and inconsistent with cross-namespace builds.

## Required correction

Make the effective custom-element manifest a deterministic compiler input available before view/template analysis, independent of source evaluation order. Track declaration-to-consumer dependencies so a declaration change invalidates/recompiles every affected literal consumer. Include the relevant effective declaration dependency in template/build freshness without turning the runtime reload ledger into a template interpreter.

Choose one authoritative manifest projection shared by literal properties and dynamic `ui/spread`; both must classify a given tag/property identically. Conflicting declarations are handled by their own closed conflict-law follow-up, not by whichever source compiles first.

Do not add runtime fallback classification on every property write, declaration-before-use ceremony, or a public API change.

## Proof discipline

Compile declaration-before-view and declaration-after-view clean builds, multiple source-order permutations, and a declaration-only warm reload. Compare emitted forms/fingerprints/digests and final DOM property behavior with a clean build. Mutating away the manifest dependency must leave the warm result stale and fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- Declaration-before-view and declaration-after-view clean builds emit identical custom-element property classification.
- Parallel/two-source compile-order permutations are deterministic.
- A declaration-only HMR change invalidates and recompiles every affected literal consumer; warm output/fingerprint/final behavior equals a clean build.
- The relevant effective declaration dependency participates in freshness/build identity without making unrelated declarations invalidate every view.
- Literal props and dynamic `ui/spread` use the same authoritative property manifest.
- Conflicts follow the separately defined deterministic conflict law rather than evaluation order.
- No per-render registry lookup, declaration-before-use rule, runtime template interpreter, or frozen/public API change is introduced.
- Compiler golden, clean-vs-warm HMR, and mounted custom-element fixtures fail under an order-dependent mutation and gate S4 conformance.
notes:
NOT STARTED (worker on PR #6006 did .143's compile arm only, 2026-07-15). SCOPE FINDING for the next dispatch: .143 does NOT subsume .141. .143 makes two DECLARATIONS consistent; .141's race is between a DECLARATION and a CONSUMER — a view compiled before the declaration reads an empty manifest and emits an ATTRIBUTE, reversed it emits a JS PROPERTY. Cross-ns without a :require edge the order is arbitrary and no recompile is triggered.

Macroexpansion cannot fix this from inside itself (a not-yet-expanded declaration is not observable). It needs a SOURCE-HARVEST phase: read each build source's top-level forms at :compile-prepare, extract declarations, seed the slice before any view analyzes. Tractable BECAUSE the grammar was ruled for it (declarations are top-level, literal, compile-resolvable; :properties must be a literal set — so a syntactic read is sound). But it lands in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build_hook.clj + a new harvest ns + consumer-dependency tracking + digest participation — outside the .141/.143 worker's build.cljc/rules.cljc fence, and genuinely bead-sized architecture. Dispatch solo with build_hook.clj in fence, rebasing on PR #6006.

IN-FENCE SUB-FINDING (candidate split-out bead): build/digest-for-slice folds ONLY views rows, and a view's template-fp fingerprints the SOURCE TEMPLATE not its lowering. So two builds with identical view sources but DIFFERENT custom-element declarations produce the SAME build digest — a real build-identity gap and one of .141's own ACs ('the relevant effective declaration dependency participates in freshness/build identity'). Left untouched rather than half-fix .141.

The shared plumbing already SHIPS, substrate-agnostically, in implementation/ssr/ — manifest.cljc (Root Manifest v1 discovery/validation/wire), install.cljc (preflight + idempotent payload install + the content-digest :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict arm), boot.cljc (:rf.error/root-boot-failed), with multi_root_hydration_* / failed_root_isolation_* tests. implementation/ssr/deps.edn is explicit that production re-frame.ssr never :requires re-frame.ui (the manifest is pure data, no cycle). === ITEM 2 — render-static — VERDICT (1) MISSING CODE, with DEAD REASONING in the stated reason ===
It is NOT merely "two docstring mentions". It is a BLESSED PUBLIC SURFACE that cleared the demand bar:
  - spec/API.md:304 (blessed freeze) | `render-static` | fn | guide 08 (static footer) | v1 (SSR tier) | — a named consumer, which is exactly what EP-0030 §The demand-bar-gated public surface requires ("Every public name needed a named consumer before Stage 1").

THE REPLACEMENT GAP IS TOTAL, AND WIDER THAN render-static. === ITEM 3 — :rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported — PARENT PREMISE REFUTED; VERDICT (1), strictly a RIDER on item 2 ===
The claim in my note above and in the audit brief — "it HAS a Spec 009 catalogue row — the catalogue outruns the emitter" — is FALSE. === ONE NARROW (3) CANDIDATE FOR THE OPERATOR — NOT A RECOMMENDATION TO RETIRE THE STAGE ITEM ===

Item 1 of that list (rf2-vxgfnd.97.1) is now STALE: that bead was RULED (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:55 AUSEST) — the prepared amendment is RETIRED as substantially consumed, and its surviving residue was re-filed as rf2-vxgfnd.97.2. Swept the epic's SCOPE line. One more genuine unbuilt item, consistently and honestly marked:

DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 14:49 AUSEST)

THE RULING, self-contained:
- The S5 serialiser re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree validates the root :rf.ui/tree-version FIRST, before any emission. A missing, non-integer, or unsupported version throws the canonical ex-info with :rf.error/id :rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported and ex-data {:got <received> :supported #{1}} — exactly as spec/004B:375-386 promises. KEEPS its deliberate reuse of the shared id — its docstring already documents the asymmetry; no change there. (Citation hygiene: earlier notes cite "validate-tree-query!" — that fn does not exist; the shipped gate is validate-tree-version! alone.)
- SCOPE FENCE: this ruling adds NO version negotiation, preflight API, fallback policy, compatibility registry, or retry machinery. One id, one fail-loud gate.

SPEC 009 CATALOGUE ROW (lands in the SAME PR as the first emit site — the one-catalogue rule: 004's rows-land-with-stages + Conventions co-edit invariant, spec/Conventions.md:130. NOT before; no name-without-emitter window). Draft row for the implementing worker to adapt to the then-current table:
| :rf.error/ssr-ui-tree-version-unsupported | :error | diagnostic | The SSR serialisation seam (re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree, Spec 004B §The SSR consumption boundary) met a structural tree whose root :rf.ui/tree-version is missing, non-integer, or unsupported — validated FIRST, before any emission, so a future-version or corrupt tree never emits plausible markup. Thrown ex-info (canonical builder). Emitted by re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree. Same PR also: re-point 009's forward reference inside the :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed row (line ~2352, "lands with the S5 serialiser") at the new row, plus whatever conformance/schema co-edits the current checks require.

004B FORWARD-REFERENCE RESOLUTION: MINT honours the tracked text as written — spec/004B:375-386 and :545, spec/004-Views.md:1210, the forward reference inside 009's ui-tree-malformed row, and the semantic.cljc docstring ALL STAND UNEDITED. title: Isolate evidence-sink failures from ViewCell flush completion
description:
## Problem

PR #5742 introduces a global debug/tool `evidence-sink` and calls it synchronously inside `flush-one!` before clearing `:dirty?`, clearing evidence, or advancing the ViewCell revision. `flush-scope!` has already atomically removed ALL matching cells from `dirty-cells` before it starts that `doseq`.

If the Xray/tool callback throws:

1. The current cell remains `:dirty? true`, retains its evidence, and never advances/notifies.
2. It has already been removed from `dirty-cells`; a later `mark-dirty!` sees `:dirty? true` and refuses to re-enrol or schedule it.
3. The exception aborts the `doseq`, so every later cell removed in the same scoped/global batch is also left dirty-but-unregistered.
4. The microtask wrapper resets `flush-scheduled?` before entering `flush-pending!`, so no automatic retry exists.

One diagnostic consumer bug can therefore strand an arbitrary batch of mounted views permanently in development. This violates the intended two-plane design: observability is a consumer of the scheduler, not an authority that may prevent the render correction. It is especially dangerous because Xray is the named sink consumer and excellent debugging is a primary substrate goal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create two dirty ViewCells and install `(set-evidence-sink! (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom" {}))))`.
2. Call `flush-pending!` or let the scheduled microtask run.
3. Observe the throw from the first cell; both cells were removed from `dirty-cells`, neither reliably completes the flush, and re-marking the first can no-op because its dirty flag is still true.

## Deliverable

Make evidence delivery failure-isolated and finally-safe. Capture the bounded evidence for the consumer, but complete scheduler state transition/revision notification for every drained cell regardless of tool behavior. Report the sink failure through an existing non-recursive diagnostic path (or disable the bad sink after one bounded report); never route that report back through the same evidence sink.

Preserve the production plane and DCE envelope: no new production hot-path allocation or exception wrapper should survive when debug is disabled.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic two-cell fixture installs a sink that throws on the first delivery; both cells leave `:dirty?`, advance exactly once, notify their listeners, and remain re-enrollable on a later invalidation.
- `flush-scope!`/`flush-pending!` cannot leave any cell dirty-but-absent from `dirty-cells`, even when the evidence consumer throws.
- One cell's tool failure does not abort evidence delivery or scheduler completion for later cells in the same batch; ordering is explicitly ruled and tested.
- The failure produces at most one bounded, useful diagnostic per ruled interval or disables/quarantines the bad sink; diagnostic reporting cannot recurse through `evidence-sink`.
- A re-entrant sink that marks the same or another cell preserves the drain-coalescing contract and does not lose the newly scheduled batch/evidence.
- Normal sinks still receive the captured pre-clear bounded summary exactly once per flushed cell.
- Advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` output retains the minimal dirty-bit/set-enrolment/microtask scheduler with the evidence sink and its failure machinery elided.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6879 (2026-07-25) — REOPENED as the exact existing owner of the same two-plane invariant, now regressed on the live Freehand commit seam.

`re-frame.freehand.cell/commit!` publishes the cell bundle, commits events, releases superseded handles, and only then synchronously calls the dev evidence sink. A throwing sink therefore makes `commit!` throw after the commit is irrevocably live. Deterministic JVM probe on the merged code returned `{:result {:thrown "audit-sink-failure"}, :lifecycle :connected, :evidence? true}`. The caller is told the commit failed even though the cell is connected and owns the published bundle.

Bounded repair: keep schema construction/validation fail-loud before publication (so malformed framework records preserve the documented all-or-nothing boundary), but contain/report arbitrary sink-consumer failure after a selected publication so it cannot change `:published` into an exception. Preserve the `interop/debug-enabled?` production-DCE envelope; no new diagnostics framework.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6884 (branch worker/cell-sink-isolation-vxgfnd-73). Split the Freehand commit seam along the publication line: the evidence occurrence-record is built+validated before publish (a malformed framework record fails loud + rolls back handles, preserving all-or-nothing), and the consumer sink is called after publish inside a guard that contains a throwing tool callback (single bounded last-evidence-sink-escape slot + one host console line, never recursing through the sink). Whole plane stays behind interop/debug-enabled? for DCE. Regression proven load-bearing (RES on unfixed seam: commit! threw audit-sink-failure + malformed cell already :connected) then green on both hosts. Gates: Freehand JVM 919/6548 exit 0; Freehand CLJS 996/5638 exit 0.
