title: [correctness-review][http] JVM abort-vs-retry race: cancelled request double-replies + re-issues a fresh attempt
description:
Correctness-review finding (rf2-k0pa70, http audit 2026-07-11). JVM-only concurrency race. VERIFIED by static reasoning; deterministic repro needs thread-interleaving injection.

WHERE
- transport.cljc `maybe-retry!` (~952-1061) samples the live-fetch handle's `:aborted?` cell ONCE (`aborted? (some? (aborted-snapshot ctx))`, ~985), decides `can-retry?`, then clears the old handle (~1020) and arms a fresh backoff handle via `schedule-backoff-handle!` (~1021).
- `schedule-backoff-handle!` (~807-950) registers a handle carrying a NEW `fired?` cell and its own abort-fn — NO `:aborted?`/`:finalised?` cell, and NO re-check of request-level abort state after `record-in-flight!`.
- The per-phase abort cells (`:aborted?`/`:finalised?`) are created fresh per live-fetch handle in `run-attempt!` (~1337-1475). They are per-phase-handle, not per-request.

REPRO (JVM: whenComplete runs on a ForkJoinPool thread, abort dispatch on the event thread)
1. whenComplete fires with a retry-eligible failure (5xx/transport/timeout matching `:retry :on`); `maybe-retry!` begins on the completion thread and samples `:aborted?` = nil.
2. Concurrently an abort (`:rf.http/managed-abort` / actor-destroy / supersede / epoch-restore / external signal) fires the OLD live-fetch handle's abort-fn BEFORE `clear-in-flight!` (~1020) removes it. The abort resolves the OLD handle (still in the registry), wins its `:finalised?` CAS, and delivers a `:rf.http/aborted` reply — REPLY #1.
3. `maybe-retry!` continues, arms the backoff timer via `schedule-backoff-handle!`. The timer's `fired?` cell is fresh; the OLD abort-fn knows nothing of it. The timer fires after the delay and `run-attempt!` issues a FRESH network attempt under a brand-new handle whose completion delivers REPLY #2.

Result: double terminal reply AND a fresh network attempt for a request the caller cancelled. For a non-idempotent POST, the cancelled request is re-sent.

NARROWER SIBLING: an abort landing between `clear-in-flight!` (~1020) and `schedule-backoff-handle!`'s `record-in-flight!` (~883) resolves NO handle, silent no-ops, and the timer still fires — the request is un-abortable for that instant.

CONTRACT VIOLATED
- spec/014:486-490 (abort always wins) + :490 ("`maybe-retry!` refuses to schedule a retry once the cell is flipped — a request the caller has cancelled MUST NOT issue a fresh attempt under any retry policy").
- spec/014:492 ("An abort ... during the backoff MUST cancel the scheduled retry — no further attempt fires" + "discoverable ... for the entire backoff window").

CLJS immune (single-threaded — `.then`/`.catch` and the abort dispatch cannot interleave mid-`maybe-retry!`).

NOT COVERED by http_backoff_cancellation_test.clj: that test settles 150ms AFTER the timer is armed, so its abort resolves the (correctly-cancellable) steady-state backoff handle, not this transitional window.

FIX SKETCH: carry ONE request-level `:aborted?` (and `:finalised?`) cell on `ctx`, thread it across all phases, stamp it onto the backoff handle, and re-check it after `schedule-backoff-handle!`'s `record-in-flight!` (the same post-registration re-check idiom already used there for `fired?`/`timer-cell` at ~948). Cancel the freshly-armed phase if the cell is flipped. Finding-3's identity-conditional `clear-in-flight!` is half of this fix.

ACCEPTANCE: a JVM stress/interleaving test that injects an abort between `maybe-retry!`'s abort-snapshot and the backoff `record-in-flight!` observes EXACTLY ONE terminal reply (`:rf.http/aborted`) AND ZERO extra server hits after cancellation. The narrower-sibling window (abort between clear and re-register) also yields one aborted reply and no retry.
notes:
AUDIT PR #6631 — the original finding explicitly named BOTH transition gaps, but #5632 fixed only live-fetch→backoff. Timer-fire→attempt N+1 is still non-continuous on current main: callback wins fired?, clears the backoff handle, checks the old aborted? cell, synchronously emits :rf.http/retry-attempt :retried, then calls run-attempt!, which mints fresh cancellation cells and only later registers the new handle. Deterministic probe at the emitted trace: {:retried-events 1, :abort-result false, :next-attempt-started 1}; a listener-issued abort saw no handle and the next attempt still started. JVM concurrent managed-abort/supersede/actor-frame-epoch cancellation has the same gap and can reissue a cancelled POST. Complete the original continuous-handoff acceptance: register/transfer ownership to the successor before clearing the predecessor or publishing :retried, carry/consult the request cancellation state end-to-end, and pin one deterministic abort-at-handoff/reentrant-listener regression asserting one aborted outcome, zero next attempt, clean registry, and no false :retried. No public API, lock, scheduler, or general state machine.
FIX SHIPPED (PR #6645, worker/http-abort-retry-race-6nczv9). Completed the SECOND transition gap (timer-fire->attempt N+1). The timer callback now hands the predecessor backoff handle + the SHARED :finalised?/:aborted? cells to run-attempt! (continuous handoff, mirrors rf2-wj8vv): run-attempt! reuses the shared cells, registers the successor FIRST, drops the predecessor only after (identity-conditional), and a post-registration re-check delivers the single :rf.http/aborted reply + suppresses the fresh attempt when the shared abort cell is flipped. The honest :retried emit moved with it (fires only after the successor re-confirms not-aborted). Deterministic JVM regression at a new :retry/before-attempt interleave seam: RED without the re-check (server hit twice; cancelled request re-issued), GREEN with it (one aborted reply, one hit, clean registry, no phantom :retried). Gates: http clojure -M:test 493/3787 green; npm run test:cljs 10365/51218 green. Spec 014:486-492 unchanged (runtime now compliant at the 2nd transition). Do NOT close until merged.
CHRONOLOGICAL THREE-LENS AUDIT RIDER — PR #6645 (2026-07-21): REOPENED P2 for one material ownership gap in the timer-fire -> retry-successor handoff.

The shared request-level finalised?/aborted? cells, successor-first ordering, abort re-check, and deterministic managed-abort regression are sound and proportionate. The remaining race is with a REAL same-request-id superseder, which the new test does not exercise.

Exact interleaving:
1. Old issuance N's backoff timer wins fired? and pauses at :retry/before-attempt.
2. Fresh issuance N+1 allocates its work id, supersede! clears/aborts the old backoff, then registers live handle H2 under request id R. The old abort flips the shared aborted? cell but loses the timer's already-won fired? CAS.
3. Old run-attempt! resumes and registry/record-in-flight! unconditionally assocs its stale retry handle under R, overwriting H2.
4. The old retry's post-registration abort re-check identity-clears its own stale handle. R is now absent while H2 remains live.

Consequences are material for ordinary SPA request supersession: managed abort and the next same-id supersede cannot reach H2, and H2 can later deliver an obsolete out-of-order reply.

Smallest repair: add one compact atomic conditional handoff used by retries: install the retry successor only if the request-id slot still holds the exact prev-handle supplied in :rf.http/retry-handoff. If that compare-and-replace loses (including the supersede clear-before-new-register interval), do not add the stale successor to either index and do not emit :retried, prepare the body, or issue transport; the newer issuance owns the id and supersede already owns stale telemetry. Anonymous/no-id first attempts keep the simple path. The existing prev-handle is the ownership token; do not add locks, scheduler changes, a public API, or another state machine.

Add one deterministic :retry/before-attempt latch/interleave test that completes a real same-id N+1 registration before releasing old N, then proves N never retries, H2 remains the lookup-visible/cancellable occupant, later supersession still reaches it, both indexes clean up, and only the current issuance delivers. Existing rf2-ous9e5 is precedent for identity-conditional clear but is not reopened; this is the missing conditional INSTALL/transfer in this bead's exact handoff.

title: HD-008's batched narrow window prices its microtask asymmetry as 10x an unresolved quantity; batch the yield-cost control the same way
description:
P0 AUDIT FINDING (read-only cold read of the P0 baseline wave, 2026-07-31).

HD-008'S BATCHED NARROW WINDOW BOUNDS ITS OWN ASYMMETRY BY MULTIPLYING AN UNRESOLVED QUANTITY BY TEN, AND THE PAGE'S OWN NEW TECHNIQUE IS THE FIX.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md, Known limitations, after the rf2-9zysg batched re-take (PR #7270):

  "The batched window also contains TEN harness microtasks for every arm except the microtask-scheduled one, which contains none; each such turn measures 0.0 ms against this clock, so the asymmetry is TEN TIMES A QUANTITY BELOW THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN RESOLUTION."

Ten times an unresolved quantity is not unresolved -- which is the exact argument that justified batching the writes in the first place ("timing k operations as ONE window lifts the sample clear of the clamp, and it is NOT the same as summing k separately-clamped readings"). hd8-rows/yield-cost! reads p50 0.0, min 0.0, max 0.0 over n=10 against Chrome's 100 us clamp. That bounds ONE turn at < 100 us. It bounds TEN turns at < 1.0 ms, not at "below resolution".

WHY THAT BOUND IS NOT COMFORTABLE HERE. The batched narrow sample is 3.8-7.6 ms, so up to ~1.0 ms is up to ~26% of the window -- and it falls on EVERY ARM EXCEPT reagent-slim, which is the arm being read against the others on this very row:

  reagent-slim  4.222 - 5.944 x floor      (window contains ZERO harness microtasks)
  donor-r1      5.182 - 6.790 x floor      (ten)
  donor-r2      5.400 - 6.579 x floor      (ten)
  reagent       4.130 - 6.947 x floor      (ten)

An unpriced term that is present in three columns and absent from the fourth, bounded only at up to a quarter of the window, is the shape of thing that decides whether reagent-slim reads faster than the donor rungs. HD-008 is the donor gate, so that comparison is the point of the row.

THE REPAIR IS THE PAGE'S OWN BATCHING TECHNIQUE, applied to the control rather than only to the arms: price TEN yields inside ONE clock window (as yield-cost! already does for one), report the per-turn figure as sample/10, and either state the resulting number or subtract it. That turns "below resolution x 10" into a measurement. It is a small change to hd8_rows/yield-cost! and does not touch any arm's window, so no published row moves and no re-run of the arms is needed -- only the control is re-read.

SECOND-ORDER, worth stating in the same pass: the same reasoning applies wherever a sub-quantum per-item cost is asserted to be negligible across a batch. lane/verified-write!'s :gap-ms is priced per window; if a future arm batches k operations under one clock on the shared lane, the same multiplication appears there.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE PUBLISHED NARROW ROWS ARE WRONG. The batch demonstrably did what it was for -- the floor moved from one-to-one-and-a-half quanta to nine-to-twelve, the per-write absolutes reproduce the unbatched run (reagent-slim 0.380-0.535 against 0.40-0.60 published), the guard did not refuse, the positive control passes HD-008's strict every-round-inside rule on all three runs, and 0 unverified of 780 on every arm. The defect is one sentence of arithmetic in the limitations section, and it is load-bearing because it is the only thing standing between the reader and a subtraction.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (yield-cost!, window-of, arm-scheduler), docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md.

Related, no duplicate: rf2-pq7d8 (CLOSED) lifted the two-shape window into lane/verified-write!; rf2-9zysg (CLOSED) owns the batch itself. This is the control that was not batched with it.

Nothing here amends the bar, the budgets, the kill criteria, the red-zones or the clock.

title: lane/verified-write!: the fixed microtask yield is not neutral across scheduler families
description:
lane/verified-write! yields exactly one microtask between the write and the arm's force!, for every arm. Its docstring justifies the yield — "load-bearing for any arm whose notification is queued rather than synchronous", priced in situ as :gap-ms — and that justification is correct for the React-hook arms. It is NOT neutral.

rf2-z3vlz established that for a substrate whose OWN render scheduler is a microtask queue (reagent-slim: reagent2.impl.batching), the harness's yield hands the commit to React before the drain runs, and the arm reads N unverified of N while the DOM is in fact merely LATE. Stock Reagent is immune only because its queue is rAF-scheduled. So the one shared yield cannot serve both scheduler families, and the harness silently produces a precise wrong number for one of them — the sixteenth instrument fault on these surfaces, and the same shape as the fifteen before it.

Proposed (additive, no behaviour change for any existing arm): let an arm declare a :drain-with! slot. When present, verified-write! composes (drain-with! write!) with NO microtask gap and reports :gap-ms 0.0 with the window's meaning stated; when absent, today's path is byte-for-byte unchanged. The docstring should name the hazard by scheduler family rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

NOT done under rf2-z3vlz on purpose: lane.cljs is a shared instrument with six live worker checkouts at the time of filing, and the arm that needs the slot (hd8_rows) is not on main, so the change would land unexercised and conflict-prone. Evidence and the exact composition are recorded in docs/design/hicasso/studio/slim-non-reactive-arm-diagnosis.md; the standalone rig that pins it is implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/z3vlz_*.

The engineering was already done by 86188c93fa; this closed the two claims that said otherwise. hd8_rows/window-of's docstring and hd8-composed-donor-arm.md now describe the landed shape (an arm declares :scheduler; :microtask = write-then-drain, nothing between; anything else or absent = today's window unchanged), keeping the reason it was not made in the same pass. ALSO corrected the page's Known-limitations bullet, which forward-referenced this bead as where the two-shape asymmetry gets settled: it landed and did NOT settle it, it carried BOTH shapes into the lane. No re-engineering, prose only, NO NUMBER MOVED (no arm outside HD-008 declares :scheduler).

title: Consolidate the HD-008 donor arm onto lane.cljs's batched window and multi-probe read-back
description:
rf2-2rtt6.7's HD-008 instrument was written before rf2-2rtt6.2's shared lane landed on main. It now sits in the lane's directory and uses lane.cljs for mount/release/parity/across-rounds/slot-order/now-ms/summarise, but it still carries its own round driver, its own verified-write and its own positive control.

Two of the lane's mechanisms are genuinely better and should be adopted:

1. lane/mount-batch! - Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100us. The HD-008 write-narrow row reads p50s of ~0.4-1.2 ms, i.e. 4-12 quanta, and its published ranges are correspondingly wide (uix 4.500-8.000 x floor). Timing k operations as ONE window lifts the sample clear of the clamp. The mount rows (4-13 ms) are unaffected.

2. lane/verified-write! multi-probe read-back - HD-008 verifies ONE cell per write. The lane verifies a SEQ of probes including the far end of the grid, because a stale page can still carry one fresh cell from the previous write, so a single probe can pass a partial commit. HD-008's bulk row (:all) probes only cell 0.

Also adoptable: lane/ratio-between (HD-008 has its own head-to-head), lane/tally, lane/control-verdict, lane/guard! + lane's CLJS-side verdict (HD-008 adjudicates in the driver instead).

Neither gap invalidates the published HD-008 rows - the guard passed all twelve, the positive control passed in all three runs, and 156 of 936 writes were flagged unverified and SUPPRESSED rather than published. But the narrow-write ranges are wider than they need to be and the bulk read-back is thinner than the lane's.

title: bench(hicasso): converge the two P0 measurement lanes onto one instrument
description:
EP-0038 wave-0 left two P0 harnesses in the tree, built in parallel by
rf2-2rtt6.2 and rf2-2rtt6.3, and they overlap.

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs

    normalise, across-rounds, slot-order, chain, verified-write!, tally.

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow*.
    (rf2-2rtt6.3) — narrow-write oriented: a per-write leg-split window
    with an in-window positive control, a per-write DOM read-back, a
    subscription-count ladder and its own driver with six pre-measurement
    gates. Self-contained; adds no build id.

Neither is wrong and neither subsumes the other — the windows genuinely
differ (a mount is one timed commit; a narrow write is write, microtask,
flush, verify). But summarise, slot-order, chain and the tally exist twice,
and this repo's own bench headers argue at length that a method expressed
twice is a method that drifts.

DO NOT do this before both PRs merge, and do not do it by moving numbers:

title: SSR durable wire key ignores a :scope-rooted declaration (only the params component is registry-projected)
description:
Found while landing rf2-dl7bz (trace/tool key honours a :serialize owner's per-slot declarations).

WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN. `classification/instance-declaration-paths` lowers a `:scope`-rooted declaration to the entry's ABSOLUTE `[:rf.runtime/resources :entries <key-id> :resource/key 0 …]` path — index 0 of the scoped key, the scope component — exactly as it lowers a `:params`-rooted one to index 2. The epoch/registry walk over the runtime-db therefore honours it.

But `ssr/project-entry` projects ONLY index 2:

    projected-key (if (= :serialize disposition)
                    (let [[scope rid params] projected-key]
                      [scope rid (classification/project-entry-params
                                   params key-id frame-id :rf.egress/ssr-hydration)])
                    projected-key)

There is no `project-entry-scope` counterpart, so on a `:serialize` owner declaring `{:sensitive [[:scope :tenant-id]]}` the resolved tenant id rides RAW in the SSR hydration wire key — while the same declaration redacts in the durable epoch export and (since rf2-dl7bz) in every trace / tool key.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN rf2-dl7bz. That bead's ruling is explicit: 'SSR untouched'. The trace/tool arm was fenced away from `ssr.cljc` deliberately, and widening the SSR projection is a separate change with its own byte-identity consequences for the hydration payload's key-id re-keying (`project-resources-runtime-db` re-keys wire entries on `state/key-id` of the PROJECTED key, so projecting the scope component changes the map key the client installs under).

SHAPE, if taken. The params counterpart is one call; the scope counterpart is the same call seeded at `[… :resource/key 0]` instead of `[… :resource/key 2]`, under the same `registry-classifies-under?` gate (so an undeclared scope rides verbatim and the CEDN-1 identity is preserved). Both would then agree with the trace/tool key, which rf2-dl7bz's `redact-key-declarations` already projects on both components.

PROOF STANDARD. A `:serialize` owner declaring `[[:scope :tenant-id]]` under a `[:rf.scope/session {:tenant-id …}]` scope: the SSR wire key's scope component must redact the declared slot, keep the tier keyword and any undeclared sibling, and the resource-id must survive. Two-sided control: an owner declaring nothing has its wire key ride BYTE-identical (`state/key-id` unchanged), and the client's `recompute-indexes` round-trip still lands.
notes:
CLOSED by PR #7255 (branch worker/wire-scope-5e2ye).

Q1 — THE RE-KEYING INTERACTION, established by probe before anything changed.
`state/key-id` is `identity/canonical-bytes` over the WHOLE
`[scope resource-id params]` vector, so the scope component IS inside the hashed
bytes and projecting index 0 DOES change the key-id. But that is the established
mechanism, not a hazard, and the probe showed it already firing on the params
side: `project-resources-runtime-db` re-keys each wire entry on
`(state/key-id (:resource/key wire-entry))` — the key-id of the PROJECTED key —
so the wire map key and the entry's own copy are one value by construction
(`project-entry` sets both from the same `projected-key`). The coarse
`:redact`/`:omit` digests have always re-keyed BOTH components that way; the
params arm has since rf2-d3pku1. Probe confirmed the raw key-id of a
params-declaring entry is ALREADY absent from the wire map today, and that the
scope component rode raw. `recompute-indexes` keys index members on the
`:entries` map keys it installed, so the client round-trip lands on the
projected identity. Nothing breaks. The honest consequence: a declared slot
makes the entry unaddressable by a client-re-derived key and it refetches — the
SAME designed consequence the coarse arm and the params arm already carry.
Closing the scope asymmetry extends an accepted cost by one index.

RESOLUTION — closed, not deferred. `project-entry-params` and the new
`project-entry-scope` are now two names for ONE parameterised body
(`project-entry-key-component`) differing in the index alone, so the two
components cannot drift into two rules again. Declaration gate and frame-scoping
kept on both arms.

BUILD POSTURE (the reason this half mattered more than rf2-dl7bz's): the SSR
hydration wire is NOT dev-only. It is the body behind
`:ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection`, called from
`payload-policy/project-runtime-db` on every SSR render, shipping to every
visitor of every page in a production bundle. No debug gate anywhere on the
path. rf2-dl7bz's trace/tool arm is dev-only by contrast. Stated explicitly in
the ns docstring and the suite docstring.

rf2-dl7bz RULING INTACT: `ssr/project-scoped-key`'s `:serialize` deferral
untouched; `project-scoped-key-still-defers-on-serialize` green (14 tests / 48
assertions, exit 0). Only its docstring changed.

TEST: new dual-target suite, 15 tests / 49 assertions, green in BOTH JVM
postures. Mutation-proved TWICE — (1) scope arm removed => 8 failures / 6 tests;
(2) declaration gate removed => initially PASSED, revealing the byte-identity
control was decorative. `=` cannot see a list<->vector collapse but
`canonical-bytes` can, so the undeclared owner's scope now carries
`:roles '(:admin :ops)`; with that, dropping the gate reds 4 assertions
(rf2-wgutc2). The no-over-redaction side is now load-bearing.

PROD-POSTURE MEASUREMENT (not asserted): `implementation/resources` has no
prod-gate lane and is not prod-posture-clean — 267 trace-emit assertions fail
under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` by design. Measured against origin/main
(ae1fb9b577) with this suite moved aside: baseline 757 tests / 6881 assertions /
267 failures; branch 772 / 6930 / 267 failures. +15 tests, +49 assertions,
+0 failures.

GATES: resources JVM dev 772/6983 exit 0; ssr JVM 592/2892 exit 0; epoch JVM
539/7131 exit 0; core egress-chokepoint source-scan 3/7 exit 0.

NOTE FOR THE MAYOR (not actioned, outside the fence): a `:serialize` entry whose
declared slot redacts is shipped with `:refetch-on-client? false` when fresh,
yet is unaddressable by a client-re-derived key. Pre-existing on the params arm
since rf2-d3pku1 and identical on both indices — not introduced here, and the
bead fenced the fix to the scope component. Worth its own bead if it matters.

title: bench: thunk-dominated arms read V8's escape analysis, not their own allocation - read_attribution_cljs's N-CALLTHUNK / N-CWFRNOG refuse by PHASE
description:
FOUND by rf2-x0fe2 while building implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs. node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer compression OFF.

THE FAULT. An arm whose allocation is dominated by a THUNK CLOSURE handed to
another function reads V8's optimization tier as much as its own cost. Three
distinct manifestations, all reproduced:

 1. ELIDED ENTIRELY. call-thunk was (defn- call-thunk [thunk] (thunk)).
    Closure inlines a private one-liner, so the thunk never escaped, so escape
    analysis removed it and the arm read 16.0 B/call -- the instrument floor,
    i.e. nothing. Fixed by storing the thunk in a volatile so it escapes for
    real; the arm then reads a stable 64.0 B/read, one closure.

 2. A 2x STEP THAT WARM-UP DOES NOT TOUCH. N-CALLTHUNK and N-CWFRNOG are
    REFUSED by the arm-order guard on the PHASE factor in the FORWARD plan:
    settled 19,217 B/call, FIRST-THIRD windows up to 38,420 -- exactly 2x, i.e.
    two closures per inner iteration where one is expected. BIT-IDENTICAL
    across 6 warm windows, 12 warm windows and 8 rounds, so it is NOT a
    settling curve (contrast rf2-tb345). The predecessor factor passes; only
    position separates it. The REVERSED plan passes cleanly. The same
    ~19,300 B/call step appears as the HIGH end of N-CWFRBIND / N-CWFRGEN /
    N-CWFRRAW's ranges simultaneously.

 3. AN ASYMMETRY INSIDE A PAIRED CONTROL -- the dangerous one. The binding was
    isolated by a symmetric pair: two sibling fns differing in exactly one
    token, (binding [...] (thunk)) vs (thunk), each handed a fresh thunk. At
    n=300 both allocate their thunk (112.1 B/read each) and the difference is
    0.0, correct. At n=30 V8 elides the NO-BIND half's thunk (48.0) while the
    binding's try/finally blocks the same elision on the bind half (112.0), and
    the difference reads 64.0 B/read -- ONE WHOLE CLOSURE, reported as the
    binding. A paired control is only symmetric while both halves are compiled
    the same way, and that is not guaranteed by writing them the same way.

MITIGATIONS ALREADY IN THE HARNESS (PR for rf2-x0fe2):
  * the PRIMARY binding figure is N-BINDONLY, which contains NO thunk and so
    has nothing to elide (0.1 B/read at n=300, 0.5 at n=30, floor in both);
  * a BUDGET reconstruction, N-CWFRRAW - N-CALLTHUNK - N-GENREAD, which
    accounts for cwfr's whole 112.2 B/read with ~0 left for a binding;
  * an explicit SYMMETRY CHECK printed with the pair: the no-bind half's thunk
    must agree with N-CALLTHUNK or the pair is declared NOT QUOTABLE.

WHAT IS NOT DONE. The guard still refuses the FORWARD plan on N-CALLTHUNK and
N-CWFRNOG. That refusal is REAL and was left in place rather than tuned away --
no headline figure depends on either arm (N-CALLTHUNK is a control, N-CWFRNOG
is the arm the write-up explicitly says NOT to subtract with), and the reversed
plan is reportable. Open questions:
  * can a thunk arm be made tier-stable at all (a pre-allocated thunk hoisted
    out of the loop would remove the allocation the arm exists to price)?
  * does write_attribution.cljs have thunk-dominated arms with the same
    exposure? Its Q-SCHED / P-VALS / P-RKV arms pass closures to run!/reduce-kv.
  * the guard has no way to say 'this arm is refused, the rest of the run is
    fine'. Today one bad arm makes a whole run unquotable, which pushes toward
    deleting inconvenient arms. Worth a per-arm verdict.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. Instrument hygiene, not a product defect.

title: bench: put the arm-order guard on the core allocation harnesses — write_attribution, read_attribution, B7
description:
FOUND by rf2-88pie (PR #7223). NOT DONE THERE because implementation/core/** was outside that worker's fence.

order_guard.cjs now guards b8_run.cjs and the B6 harness. The harness where the fault was actually FOUND is implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs, and it is untouched.

Two things to carry over.

1. THE ROTATION TRAP. b8_run.cjs, b6-harness/round! and b6-rows/update-round! all selected the arm for slot j of round r as ARMS[(j + r) % n] and all three described that in published provenance as 'arm order rotating'. A cyclic rotation changes which arm goes FIRST and not which arm follows which: arm a sits at slot (a - r) mod n, so its predecessor is arm (a - 1) mod n in EVERY round. Check whether write_attribution / read_attribution / b7_run.cjs do the same.

2. THE GUARD. require('order_guard.cjs') - or its CLJS counterpart h/slot-order - stratify every arm's samples by immediate predecessor AND by position in the run, and refuse on either. Note the live finding: position is worth 27% (5.3x on a cold window) where the immediate predecessor is worth 0.0-0.3%, so a plain both-orders pass is not sufficient - it confounds the two.

Sequence AFTER PR #7223 merges (order_guard.cjs must be on main).

title: ci: nine more page.goto sites outside implementation/scripts/ still inherit Playwright's 30s default (rf2-bhjzn sweep residue)
description:
SPOTTED while fixing rf2-bhjzn (which fixed run-ui-g8.cjs and named check-story-static.cjs's literal). The rf2-bhjzn PR pins the class with a SWEEP, but the sweep can only cover the directory that bead owned: implementation/scripts/**. A repo-wide grep on 2026-07-28 14:08 AUSEST found nine more page.goto calls with waitUntil 'load' and NO explicit timeout, so each takes Playwright's default 30s — a budget no lane can reach and whose CI failure line reads like the lane's own timeout:

  implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs:31
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_prod_run.cjs:89
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_profile_run.cjs:95
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs:151
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b8_run.cjs:129
  tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1156
  tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/live-e2e-fixture.cjs:346
  tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs:86
  tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs:110
  tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:2304

NOT edited by rf2-bhjzn: implementation/freehand/**, tools/** and the adapters testbed were outside that worker's fence.

RISK IS NOT UNIFORM. The freehand bench runners are the sharp end — b10_prod_run.cjs ALREADY carries {waitUntil:'commit', timeout:60000}, which is the tell that this exact ceiling was hit there before; its b6/b7/b8 siblings did not get the same treatment, and a bench page that burns synchronously during load is precisely the shape that fires it (rf2-dczpv's evidence was bench.b10-two-clock-dom's ~36s burn). The tools/story and tools/xray sites navigate cheap fixture pages, so they are lower risk — same argument the bead for run-ui-g8 made, and it was still worth fixing there because the FAILURE MODE, not the frequency, is the defect.

DEMONSTRATED for the class in rf2-bhjzn: against the exact two-line document these runners serve, a bare page.goto dies at 30082ms while the runner's own budget sits unused at 90000ms, whether 'load' is held by a slow subresource or by a synchronous burn. Raising the lane budget moves neither.

FIX, per file: pass an explicit timeout tied to the runner's own budget; prefer waitUntil 'commit' where the page does work during load (the bench runners) and keep 'load' where a short post-nav assertion budget assumes a loaded document (see the check-story-static.cjs decision in rf2-bhjzn). Consider extending the sweep test to these directories once they are clean — implementation/scripts/_impl-browser-runners-verdict-policy.test.cjs has the sweep, but it reads only its own directory.

Surface: implementation/freehand/test/**, implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/**, tools/**. HOT-ZONE-free. Sequence AFTER the rf2-bhjzn PR merges so the sweep helper is on main to copy.

title: verify-version-lockstep.sh: check_clein_main greps the whole file, not the :clein/build map
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2ii52 (PR #7217), same family as the defect that bead was reopened for; left alone there because it is outside the reopen's bounded repair.

`check_clein_main` in .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh asserts clein's required `:main` key with:

    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*:main[[:space:]]' "${deps_file}"

That is a whole-file text grep. It does not read the `:aliases -> :clein/build` map it claims to be checking, so it is satisfied by a `:main` key sitting in ANY alias, or in any other map in the file, or (since only `;;` is not even stripped here) by a commented-out one on a line starting with `:main`. An artefact could therefore be reported buildable while `clojure -M:clein pom` still aborts on `(contains? % :main)` — the exact failure the check was added to prevent (machines-viz under rf2-4u3t1, mcp-base under rf2-2ii52).

It is also line-layout-bound in the same way the git-coordinate check was: `:main` has to start its own line. `{:lib day8/x :main foo.bar ...}` on one line passes nothing.

REPAIR (cheap, and the machinery is now right there): read `:aliases -> :clein/build -> :main` structurally through implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs, the same node authority local_root_coords() and git_coord_libs() already use in that file — test.yml runs this gate on a bare checkout with no JDK, so node is the available runtime. Add cases to the existing `--self-test` (PR #7217): :main present in :clein/build (CLEAN), :main present only in an unrelated alias (FLAGGED), :main on the same line as :lib (CLEAN), :main absent (FLAGGED).

Today's tree is GREEN either way — all five publishable tools genuinely carry :main in :clein/build — so this is prevention, not a live break.
close_reason: Closed

title: implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs: readSeq throws on a trailing #_ discard in a collection
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2ii52 (PR #7217).

`Reader.readSeq` in implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs cannot read a collection whose LAST element is a `#_` discard form. `readForm` consumes `#_` plus the discarded datum and then `continue`s to read the next form — which is the closing delimiter — so `readDatum` throws "unexpected '}'".

REPRO (exact, verified 2026-07-28 at main e0e2e076da):

    {:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.12.0"}
            #_day8/de-dupe #_{:git/url "https://example.invalid/x.git"}}}

  -> EdnReadError: unexpected '}'

Putting the discard anywhere but last reads fine, so the bug is specifically 'discard immediately before the closing delimiter'.

BLAST RADIUS. Every consumer of this reader fails CLOSED rather than passing vacuously, so this is a availability defect, not a correctness hole:
  - .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh — both assert_local_roots_inventoried and (as of PR #7217) check_no_git_coords_in_runtime_deps exit 2 with 'failed to read this deps.edn structurally'. A deps.edn that ends a map with a discarded coordinate makes the lockstep gate un-runnable.
  - implementation/scripts/lib/publishable-runtimes.cjs and the bundle-isolation gate consume the same reader.

A `#_`-commented-out last dependency is an entirely ordinary thing to write while debugging a dep, so this is reachable by normal editing.

FIX: in readSeq, after readForm() returns, re-check for the closing delimiter before treating the result as an item — or have readForm signal 'discard consumed, nothing produced' rather than recursing into the next datum. Pin it with a fixture in whatever suite covers edn.cjs.

NOT FIXED IN #7217 deliberately: the reader is a shared authority the bundle-isolation gate also consumes, it is outside that PR's fence, and the defect predates it.
close_reason: Closed

title: ci: test-rigorous-local.sh no longer covers the seven Freehand bench DOM namespaces in a browser
description:
CONSEQUENCE of rf2-mf4uy (PR #7193), noted there because scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh is repo-root and was outside that PR's fence.

TESTING.md calls scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh the 'local mirror of the nightly sweep'. It runs test:browser, test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod and test:browser-prod-elision. It does NOT run bench:freehand-browser.

That was harmless while :browser-test also selected the seven re-frame.freehand.bench.*_dom_cljs_test namespaces. Since rf2-mf4uy it no longer does — those seven now run ONLY in :browser-test-freehand-bench, whose sole scheduled home is .github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml. So the local rigorous sweep has a hole the nightly CI sweep does not: 30 tests / 465 assertions of mounted Freehand evidence that a pre-release local run will not exercise.

THE DECISION, and it is a real one rather than an oversight to patch:

  (a) ADD 'npm run bench:freehand-browser' to test-rigorous-local.sh. Costs ~60s locally (measured: 16.5s compile + 31.8s run). Restores the mirror. But the script's inventory is pinned by implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs, so that pin moves in the same PR.

  (b) LEAVE IT and say so in TESTING.md. Defensible: the bench lane publishes EVIDENCE and asserts on provenance words, never on numbers; a developer workstation is not the pinned worker the records are comparable within; and freehand-bench.yml runs it nightly regardless.

Whichever way it goes, TESTING.md's 'local mirror of the nightly sweep' line should stop being ambiguous about it.

title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

title: Consolidate the Spec 015 URL-carrier scrub into core — two artefacts own one policy
description:
rf2-6jqa8 promoted SSR's safe-redirect rejections onto the always-on error axis, which required an EP-0015 fail-closed scrub on the caller-untrusted :location slot. The scrub policy already existed — re-frame.routing.egress/redact-url-carriers (rf2-ov56u applies it to the route-miss :url) — but implementation/ssr depends on core ALONE (Spec 006), so it could not be reached:

  - a production :require on routing would drag the whole route grammar onto the classpath of every SSR app that registers no routes;
  - a late-bind hook to routing's copy would FAIL OPEN in exactly the common case (a routing-free SSR host), and a fail-open scrub on a fail-closed egress boundary is the wrong failure mode by construction.

So implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/egress.cljc now carries a byte-for-byte sibling of routing's redact-url-carriers, deliberately spelled the same way (same fn names, same policy, same docstring shape) so this consolidation is a MOVE rather than a rewrite.

THE FIX: move redact-url-carriers / redact-url-tag into core, next to re-frame.privacy (which already owns redacted-sentinel and is the only thing either copy requires). Have re-frame.routing.egress and re-frame.ssr.egress delegate, or delete both and re-point the three call sites (routing/url_change route-miss-tags, routing's :rf.route/navigation-blocked :requested-url slot, ssr/response safe-redirect-tags).

NOTE the default slot differs between the two copies (:url in routing, :location in ssr) — the consolidated redact-url-tag should keep the two-arity shape and let each caller name its slot.

Low priority: the duplication is 45 lines of pure string surgery with no state, and both copies are covered by their own tests. It is a tidiness bead, not a correctness one.
close_reason: Closed

title: examples/core/login/model.cljs comments claim Credentials is enforced at 'the machine's :submit boundary' — it isn't
description:
FOUND BY rf2-bjkkd (PR #7185) while correcting the README's "rejected at the door" claim. The README is fixed; these are the source comments that taught it the same wrong thing, and they are the canonical login example's comments, so a reader copying the shape reads them.

THE FACT: Credentials never reaches the machine. AuthLoginEvent (model.cljs:136-146) is credential-free by construction — [:cat [:= :auth.login/flow] [:schema [:cat [:enum :submit :dismiss :success :failure] [:* :any]]] [:? :any]] — and the file says so itself at :121-127 ("Every sub-event here is credential-free ... the machine tracks the login lifecycle but never touches the password"). The only thing that checks a draft against Credentials is the private validate helper (:421-423, m/explain + me/humanize) called from :auth.login/submit-form (:539). That is a plain function call in a handler body: it runs in every build, and it is what actually rejects a too-short password.

SITES (all in examples/core/login/model.cljs):
  - :407-409 — "Its shape is Credentials (email regex, 8-char password) — the very schema the machine's :submit boundary will later hold it to." The machine's :submit boundary holds it to nothing; it never sees the draft.
  - :413-415 — "It checks the draft against the very same Credentials schema the machine's :submit boundary enforces, so the form and the machine agree on 'valid' down to the last character." Same error. The form is the only party that checks; there is nobody to agree with.
  - :121-122 — "The shape of every event vector dispatched at the :auth.login/flow machine. Get it wrong and the event is rejected at the boundary — the handler simply never runs." True in a dev build only (:where :event is validate-event!, inside the interop/debug-enabled? gate). Wants the same one-clause qualification the README now carries.
  - :516-521 — this block is CORRECT and is the model for the fix: "Handing a bad draft to the machine would only bounce off its :submit schema boundary — and since the view renders machine errors, that rejection would be *silent* ... So the form catches it first." Note it also says ":submit schema boundary", so it inherits the same imprecision even while reasoning correctly; the reasoning survives a rewording, the phrase does not.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the comments describe a two-layer defence (form checks, machine re-checks) that does not exist, and the layer they credit is the dev-only one. A reader who trusts the machine boundary and drops the form's validate call ships an endpoint with no credential check at all.

FENCE: examples/core/login/model.cljs comments only. THE CODE IS CORRECT — do not change behaviour, and do not add :rf.schema/at-boundary (PR #7185 explains why it is the wrong shape for an ingress that must answer with field errors). Comment-only diff; run the example gates.

CITE: rf2-bjkkd (the README fix), rf2-bkvu5 (the ruling), rf2-ueopx (the sweep).
close_reason: Closed

title: Publish the controls kit's composition reader, or the scalars a kit member needs
description:
GAP found building the FH-CTRL-019 typeahead witness (rf2-drpa3.182.8).

`re-frame.freehand.controls` publishes the composition DECISION — `key-intent`, a pure function of (key, composing?) — and its docstring explicitly invites reuse: 'a kit member with its own keyboard protocol answers the composition question through this function rather than re-deciding it'.

But the READER is private. `composing?` (controls.cljc) is a `defn-`, and it is the part that carries the real knowledge: the standard `isComposing` flag has to be asked of `nativeEvent` under React, and Chromium reports a composing Enter through `keyCode` 229 with `isComposing` FALSE. A kit member can therefore share the rule and cannot share the scalars.

CONSEQUENCE, observed: `re-frame.freehand.typeahead-witness` carries a four-line mirror of `composing?` (marked as such at the site). That is the exact duplication the kit's own design intends to prevent, and it is the duplication whose failure mode is silent — a member that mirrored only the standard flag is broken for every input method on Chromium and green on every keyboard its author owns. FH-CTRL-019's mounted tier presses the two signals separately for that reason.

OPTIONS (a ruling, not a foregone conclusion):
  a. publish `composing?` on `re-frame.freehand.controls` (a namespace-level public fn, not a door verb — no API-manifest verb lane);
  b. widen `key-intent` with an arity that takes the host EVENT rather than the two scalars, keeping the pure arity;
  c. rule that a kit member is expected to read its own scalars, and say so in the kit docstring so the next author does not treat the duplication as an accident.

Whatever is chosen, FH-CTRL-018's separate-signal press is the acceptance shape: an event carrying BOTH signals cannot fail for either one.
notes:
SHIPPED via PR #7201 (worker/composing-18216).

Published `re-frame.freehand.controls/composing?` as a documented public :advanced fn; `key-intent` unchanged as the pure (key, composing?) decision.

WEBKIT ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED in source, both browser suites (FH-CTRL-018/020) and the three conformance fixtures: the isComposing=false / keyCode=229 pairing was WebKit bug 165004, fixed April 2026 via bug 311717 (Safari branch backport) — not Chromium. 229 arm kept for deployed engines, documented as the UI Events legacy-algorithm compatibility signal rather than a Freehand policy value.

MIRRORS: exactly ONE existed — typeahead-witness/host-composing? — now deleted, call site reads c/composing?. Repo-wide 'keyCode 229' sweep found no others.

MANIFEST ROSTER: re-frame.freehand.controls IS on gen.clj's roster (unlike collection/splitter). Enrolled in api-manifest-metadata.edn (:advanced), regenerated api-manifest.edn (592->593), spec/API.md row, docs/api section, and FH-CTRL-017's exact :public-vars fixture (which went RED on the new var — that fixture is the 'exact ns-publics' check the ruling named). CLJS probe enumerates dynamically, no edit needed.

FOUR-CASE TEST added (raw flag / React nativeEvent / keyCode 229 alone / neither), each pressed alone.

GATES all 0: freehand JVM 1267 tests, test:freehand 1374 tests, test:browser 840 tests, plus all 6 manifest+projection checks.

title: The no-candidate handler fallback drops v/raw-fn and v/render-fn — the two roles that need no committed site
description:
Found while answering rf2-3slzz. LATENT and pre-existing — not reachable from any shipping declaration today, which is why it is P3 rather than a bug report.

WHAT. re-frame.freehand.react/handler-proxy's no-candidate fallback is:

    (if (some? cand)
      (events/site ...)
      (when (fn? raw) raw))

`raw` here is whatever the author wrote at a native `:on-*` position. For the two roster roles that need NO committed site — v/render-fn and v/raw-fn — events/site itself hands the carrier's function straight back (`(:f plan)`), records nothing on the candidate, and mints no proxy. They are deliberately outside the committed-proxy scheme: a render callback may run during an uncommitted foreign render, and a raw function's identity is the caller's to own.

So those two roles are exactly the ones that would be legal in a boundary with no cell — and they are the ones the fallback DROPS. A Callback deftype is deliberately not `fn?` in ClojureScript (carrier-called-directly! documents why at length), so `(when (fn? raw) raw)` answers nil for a (v/raw-fn f) or a (v/render-fn [...] ...) at a native `:on-*` with no candidate above it. The prop is never written. Nothing throws.

The same fallback is in re-frame.freehand.reactive/event-site (the compiled tier's lowering), spelled `(when (fn? value) value)` — identical shape, identical consequence.

WHY IT IS NOT REACHABLE TODAY. An `:on-*` key is an `:events` site to the compiled analyzer whatever value sits at it, so a compiled declaration carrying one never reaches `:view-cell :elided`; and the interpreted shell never elides. The only way to hit the fallback now is the documented "no boundary above this call" path (fr/element with a bare element), where dropping declarative intent is the documented behaviour — but dropping a v/raw-fn there is still wrong, because a v/raw-fn asks for nothing the fallback cannot give: it wants its own identity handed over unchanged, which is precisely what the no-candidate arm is for.

WHY IT MATTERS SOON. rf2-oxlpy (the {:reactive false} opt-out) makes shell-free boundaries reachable from ordinary interpreted declarations, and its brief already rules that these positions must classify with events/event-plan and let :render-fn / :raw-fn pass through. If that lands, this is fixed as a side effect and this bead closes as a duplicate. Filed separately so the latent defect is not lost if the flag is deferred, and so the fix has a home if someone reaches the fallback another way first.

FIX, if taken on its own: classify with events/event-plan in the no-candidate arm rather than testing `fn?`. nil -> nil (empty position). :render-fn / :raw-fn -> the carried function, unchanged, which is what the committed path answers for them too. :bare-fn -> the function (unchanged behaviour). Everything else -> nil, exactly as today, since those genuinely need a committed site the caller has no boundary to give.

EVIDENCE: ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs:256-268 and :957-974; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/reactive.cljc:99-105; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/events.cljc `site` and `carrier-called-directly!`.
