title: PR #7162 left five double-done calls in controls_kit_dom_cljs_test
description:
Found while flipping FH-CTRL-018 to :residue :none (rf2-n9rzw). Not a blocker for that flip — reported rather than fixed, because repairing it means touching a mounted suite and therefore owing a full browser gate, which would have widened a deliberately bounded PR.

WHAT HAPPENED. Before PR #7162, `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs` ended each async row with:

    (teardown! container root)
    (done)

`teardown!` did not call `done`. #7162 (commit 78531340ca) replaced `teardown!` with the shared `finish!`, which DOES call `done` as its last form:

    (defn- finish! [container root done]
      (ms/destroy-root! container root)
      (ms/residue-clean! "FH-CTRL-018 — after teardown")
      (done))

The pre-existing trailing `(done)` was left in place at every site, so all five now double-fire:

    (finish! container root done)
    (done)

Sites: lines 296/297, 328/329, 363/364, 431/432, 528/529 (as of 8f6779be3e).

WHY THE BROWSER GATE STAYED GREEN, and why this is P3 rather than P1. cljs.test guards it — `run-block` wraps the continuation in a `delay` and the second call takes the realized branch:

    (if (realized? d)
      (println "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.")
      @d)

So the second `done` is a no-op plus a console warning; async state is NOT corrupted and no test runs twice. That matches #7162's reported browser numbers (835 tests unchanged). The cost is five spurious warnings per browser run, plus five lines of dead code that contradict the file's own discipline — `mount-support`'s docstring warns specifically against double-firing `done`, and `run-async`/`each-mode` exist to make it impossible.

FIX. Delete the five trailing `(done)` forms. `finish!` owns the call; `fail-and-finish!` already does the same on the rejection path and has no duplicate.

GATE. Touching a mounted suite, so `npm run test:browser` with BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000, foreground. Expect the test count unchanged and the "called done more than one time" warnings gone from the log — the warning's disappearance IS the acceptance evidence, so capture the log before and after.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7164. Deleted the five trailing (done) calls; finish! keeps ownership, matching mount-support's run-async/each-mode. Browser lane: 6 double-done warnings before, 0 after; 835 tests / 5383 assertions unchanged, exit 0 both runs. freehand JVM exit 0 (1222 tests). Guard filed as rf2-u0cy4 (promote the warning to a fatal console pattern in the browser runner - outside this bead's fence).

title: trace: with-handler-scope allocates a HandlerScope + trigger-handler map on EVERY sub recompute in PRODUCTION (121 B/sub)
description:
FOUND by rf2-jr76s. Measured 120.8 B per subscription per write (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF) — 4.3% of the pre-fix per-subscription slope and 12.8% of the post-fix one, i.e. it is now one of the larger remaining framework terms.

subs.memo/validate-and-trace brackets EVERY sub recompute in

  (trace/with-handler-scope (trace/handler-scope-from-meta :sub query-id sub-meta) ...)

and that bracket is NOT under interop/debug-enabled?. So a production :advanced bundle, in which the trace emit inside it costs literally 0.2 B because Closure DCEs the body AND the argument map (measured), still allocates a 5-field HandlerScope record, the trigger-handler map that handler-scope-from-meta builds, the inherit-scope cond-> result, and a dynamic-var binding push/pop — per subscription, per write.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE DEV GATE, and why this is a bead rather than a patch: the scope is read by the ALWAYS-ON error path. validate-and-trace's catch branch routes :rf.error/sub-exception through error-emit/dispatch-on-error! and emit-error-both!, deliberately outside the debug gate, because Spec 011's SSR fail-closed posture depends on a sub that throws mid-render-to-string producing a 500 rather than a silent 200. Those paths resolve the failing handler's source-coord and trigger-handler from the in-scope HandlerScope. Gating the scope on debug-enabled? would therefore change PRODUCTION ERROR ATTRIBUTION — an error-contract surface, not a perf knob.

SHAPES WORTH CONSIDERING (none chosen):
  (a) Build the scope LAZILY — bind a thunk/holder and materialise the record only when an emit or an error actually needs it. Preserves the error path exactly; costs one closure instead of a record + map, or zero if the holder can be a hoisted constant per registration.
  (b) Hoist the per-registration part. handler-scope-from-meta's inputs for a given sub are (:sub, query-id, sub-meta) — all fixed at registration. Only :call-site / :dispatch-id inheritance is per-call. A scope cached on the registrar slot would make the per-recompute cost the inherit step alone.
  (c) Accept it and say so.

(b) looks the most promising and the least invasive, but it needs someone to check that nothing mutates a scope in place and that HMR/incarnation replacement invalidates the cached record — which is exactly the kind of thing rf2-vxgfnd.220 already had to reason about for sub-meta.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-1.
close_reason: PR #7158. Bead premise FALSIFIED then answered: the always-on SSR error path does NOT read the scope (implementation/ssr/src has zero handler-scope refs; error-emit resolves source-coord from the id-keyed source-coords registry, not the dynamic scope). But the scope still must not be dev-gated -- frame.cljc:2855's EP-0027 make-frame-in-handler guard tests scope PRESENCE, and frame.cljc:605 / router.cljc:2599 / freehand cell.cljc:1177 read :dispatch-id always-on. Shape (b) taken, matching the views.cljs:620 precedent: scope hoisted into the three memo wrappers' closures. Plus inherit-scope no longer assocs nil over nil (2 record copies per handler entry in production). Nothing dev-gated; scope still bound every recompute, every slot reads the same. Node V8 :advanced goog.DEBUG=false: coord-less slope 938.1/939.9 -> 815.9/818.3 (paired control predicted 120.0, measured 121.9, +1.6%); coord-carrying slope 1724.6/1567.5 -> 834.2/818.5 (predicted 744.1, measured 749.0 reversed, +0.7%).

title: frame: replace-app-db! costs 4,470 B with ZERO subscriptions — undecomposed constant that dominates a small app's write
description:
FOUND by rf2-jr76s while building the write-attribution ladder. Not a defect; an unexamined constant.

The ladder (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF — absolutes are node's, shares transfer, Chrome's tagged slots are half as wide):

  MKDB       the application's own new-db value          921 B
  BAREATOM   + reset! on a watch-free plain atom         890 B
  SPINE0     + the substrate's replace-container!      1,004 B   (epoch open, reset, close, empty drain)
  RFWRITE-0  + frame/replace-app-db!, ZERO subs        4,470 B

So frame/replace-app-db! adds ~3,470 B over a bare substrate write, on a frame with no subscriptions at all: commit-frame-transition! -> commit-frame-record-transition! (read-container, the partition carry-forward, the next-fs map, the changed-set cond->, the two not= partition comparisons), bump-commit-epoch!, and the two partition PROJECTION derived values (:app-db and :runtime-db) recomputing and fanning out.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. It is a CONSTANT, so at 300 subscriptions it is 1.6% of the write and invisible — which is exactly why it has never been noticed. At 10 subscriptions, the shape a small app or a per-frame tool panel actually has, it is a THIRD of the write. And every frame in a multi-frame page pays it per write.

NOT DECOMPOSED. rf2-jr76s measured it as one number and went after the scaling term instead, which was the right call. This bead is the decomposition nobody has done: split RFWRITE-0 into commit bookkeeping vs the two projections vs bump-commit-epoch!, the same way the per-subscription slope was split.

DO NOT assume there is a win here — report the split first. Some of it is the two-partition contract doing exactly what Spec 002 SS-One physical container, two projection reactions requires, and that is not negotiable for bytes.

Harness: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs already has the ladder and the RFWRITE-0 arm; this is adding rungs under it.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-1, SS-6.
notes: SUPERSEDED FIGURE (rf2-c0awb, PR #7230). This bead's close reason quotes 'C-FRAME registry lookup 0.0 B'. That arm was looking up :wa/frame, which build-rig! never registers, so it priced a registry MISS (frame/frame short-circuits on the registry get). With the arm pointed at a frame the rig actually built, the attribution reads C-FRAME 32.0 B / 1.3% of the delta, not 0.0 B / 0.0%. The other four components are unchanged. CAVEAT: that 32.0 is DISPUTED and must not be quoted — -diagnose PROBE 4 sweeps the same closure and reads a constant 32 B per WINDOW (i.e. ~0 B/call) where the plan reads 32 B/CALL at reps=4000. See rf2-tmzie.
close_reason: PR #7158. Decomposed. RFWRITE-0 4311.7 B minus SPINE0 1003.7 B = 3308.0 B to attribute (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG=false): C-BUMP bump-commit-epoch! 881.1 B (26.6%), C-PARTS partition bookkeeping 705.8 B (21.3%), C-PROJ the two partition projections 670.3 B (20.3%), C-TAGPAIR two [::ok v] pairs 232.1 B (7.0%), C-FRAME registry lookup 0.0 B, residual 818.6 B (24.7%). ONE artefact found: bump-commit-epoch! spelled (fnil inc 0) INLINE, so every commit called fnil and allocated a fresh multi-arity variadic closure to express a constant -- paired control C-BUMP 881.1 vs C-BUMPH 136.0 = 745.0 B/write, 22.5% of the whole constant. Hoisted. Everything else is INTRINSIC: C-PARTS is the changed-partition set the change traces depend on, C-PROJ is Spec 002 SS-One physical container two projection reactions. Untouched. RFWRITE-0 [4223.5-4414.7] -> [3268.0-3532.6], disjoint.

title: bench: arm ORDER contaminates the next arm when the preceding arm allocates orders-of-magnitude-larger objects
description:
TENTH instrument fault class on the allocation-measurement surface. FOUND by rf2-jr76s.

The write-attribution harness carries two controls: .slice() of a packed DOUBLE array (predicted 8.000 B/element, since V8 never pointer-compresses a double) and .slice() of a packed SMI array (predicted 8.000 B/slot on an uncompressed build).

The SMI control read:

  FORWARD arm order   16.1052 B/slot   (2.01x its prediction)
  REVERSED arm order   8.0027 B/slot   (+0.03% of its prediction)
  plain node, outside the harness, same code   ~8.5 B/slot

The only difference is WHAT RAN IMMEDIATELY BEFORE. In forward order that is the DBL-10000 arm, which allocates an 87 KB object per call. In reversed order it is not. So a large-object arm reproducibly DOUBLES the reading of its immediate successor, and nothing in the method predicts it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE HARNESS. Every allocation study in this repo (B7, B8, read_attribution, write_attribution) runs a plan of arms in one process, and several of them mix arms whose per-call allocation differs by three or four orders of magnitude. If proximity to a large-object arm can inflate a neighbour by 2x, then any single-order run can publish a wrong number for whichever arm happens to follow the biggest one — silently, with a tight range, looking green.

WHAT SAVED IT HERE was running the whole plan in BOTH orders (WA_ORDER=rev) and noticing the two controls disagreed with each other rather than with a prediction. Every other arm reproduced across the two orders to within 1%, so nothing quoted in rf2-jr76s is affected.

NOT DIAGNOSED: the V8 mechanism. Candidates worth eliminating are new-space page-tail filler left by the large arm, a semi-space growth heuristic firing between arms, and allocation-site pretenuring on the .slice() call. A gc() already brackets every sample, so it is not simply un-collected residue.

ACTIONABLE:
1. Treat BOTH-ORDERS as load-bearing method, not a nicety — a study that runs one order has not checked this.
2. Consider ordering plans so no arm follows one that allocates >100x its own per-call bytes, or interposing a settle arm.
3. Add this class to the running fault-class list the studio docs maintain.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-4.
close_reason:
Done in PR #7223 (worker/bench-method-88pie, 3 commits off origin/main).

THE HARNESS PROPERTY, and which of the three remedies was chosen: STRATIFY AND REFUSE, not randomise and not re-order. order_guard.cjs partitions every arm's samples by what ran IMMEDIATELY BEFORE it AND by WHERE IN THE RUN it was measured (first third vs last third), and applies the house rule - overlapping ranges are indistinguishable, so a stratification is a finding only when the ranges are disjoint AND the medians differ beyond a stated tolerance. One stratum on a factor is 'unchecked', and unchecked refuses as loudly as contaminated: a single-order result has not been checked and may not be quoted. Randomising was rejected because it spreads a contaminant across every arm instead of concentrating it in one; re-ordering by size was rejected because it needs each arm's per-call allocation before measuring it and produces no evidence that it worked.

IT CATCHES THE KNOWN 2x CASE, deterministically, by fixture replay: the recorded 16.1052 / 8.0027 pair is REFUSED at ratio 2.0125 on strata of ONE SAMPLE EACH (a guard insisting on ranges would have passed it). The same study's uncontaminated 2830.7 / 2842.8 slope passes. 7 of 7 self-test checks green; b8_run.cjs runs them before the browser starts, the way the key-renaming integrity probe does, and exits 2 on a refusal.

TWO FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT PREDICT.

1. THE MITIGATION EVERY B6/B8 ROW CLAIMED DOES NOT EXIST. b8_run.cjs, b6-harness/round! and b6-rows/update-round! all chose the arm for slot j of round r as ARMS[(j + r) % n] and published that as 'arm order rotating'. A cyclic rotation changes which arm goes FIRST, not which arm follows which: arm a sits at slot (a - r) mod n so its predecessor is arm (a - 1) mod n in EVERY round, and only the round seam differs - one sample in R. All three now rotate AND REFLECT on odd indices; the arithmetic is proven both ways in the self-test.

2. THE IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR IS THE SMALLEST FACTOR, measured twice. Plain node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6, pointer compression OFF: the same packed-SMI .slice() control, nothing else varying, reads 10.32 10.26 10.26 10.26 10.33 10.28 then 8.12 for ever - +27% for six windows, then a step to its 8.016 prediction, and 42.32 on the very first window. Holding position fixed, the predecessor is worth 0.0-0.3% (8.1377 after an 87 KB-object arm, 8.1377 after a 3-element one). Window size, a knob unrelated to order, is worth 2.03x cold and +1.4% warm. B8's own first guarded run agrees: the 'instrument' pseudo-arm read 4,361 B/write first window and 440 last (9.9x), while the predecessor factor came out CLEAN on floor and freehand-interpreted with the ladder's 100 KB-per-write windows as their strata. So the contaminant is how long the process has been running, and BOTH a plan reversal and a change of window size move that - forward-versus-reversed confounds adjacency with position and cannot say which it caught.

This does not restate what happened inside rf2-jr76s's own harness, which is not reproduced here and lives outside the fence; its mechanism stays undiagnosed as the bead says.

Fault class added to docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-allocation.md section 5, with a provenance correction (its figures were taken under the rotation that was not a mitigation; no re-take is claimed).

Follow-ups: rf2-tb345 (widen B8's warm-up - one 4-write window is not enough), rf2-om73r (put the guard on implementation/core's write_attribution / read_attribution / B7, which were outside the fence).

Gates: bench:freehand-browser 30/465 exit 0; implementation/freehand JVM 1284/8803 exit 0; test:browser 841/5459 exit 0; order_guard --live exit 0. Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.88pie-b8-order-guard-raw.txt (local-only).

title: subs: subscribe's 1-arity builds its no-frame-context error payload on every call - 136 B/call on the happy path
description:
MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000%, arm
S1-CURFRM): 136.0 B/call, EXACTLY, in every round, and flat across
n = 30 / 300 / 3000.

WHAT IT IS. `subs/subscribe`'s 1-arity:

    (subscribe-in-frame (frame/require-current-frame!
                          :subscribe
                          {:where    're-frame.subs/subscribe
                           :event-id (first query-v)})
                        query-v)

The `extra` map is built on EVERY subscribe. `require-current-frame!`
reads it ONLY when `resolve-current-frame` returns nil -- the
`:rf.error/no-frame-context` path. On the happy path it is pure
garbage: ~96 B for the two-entry map plus ~40 B for `(first query-v)`,
which seqs the vector.

8% of `subscribe`'s post-fix per-call allocation (1612 - 1668 B).

SKETCHES, none of them free of friction -- pick on CLARITY, not bytes:

  (a) `require-current-frame!` accepts a THUNK for `extra`, called only
      on the error path. One more concept at every call site; the
      payload construction moves into a `(fn [] {...})`, which reads
      about as well.
  (b) the call site becomes
        (or (frame/resolve-current-frame)
            (frame/require-current-frame! :subscribe {...}))
      -- zero-allocation on the happy path, but it reads as a redundant
      double-resolve and invites someone to "simplify" it back.
  (c) leave it. 136 B, and the map is genuinely part of what makes the
      error message good.

`(first query-v)` -> `(nth query-v 0)` would save the 40 B on its own
but `first` is the idiomatic spelling and this project does not buy
performance with clarity. Mentioned for completeness, NOT recommended.

RECOMMEND: do not action until rf2-x0fe2 gives a CLJS figure. On the JVM
this is the smallest of the four terms; in CLJS its RELATIVE share rises
(the ~760 B binding term vanishes there), which may or may not change
the answer.

FENCE: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc +
implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc.
INSTRUMENT: read_attribution.clj, RM_SUITE=subs, arm S1-CURFRM.
close_reason:
PR #7157. ARTEFACT, confirmed and removed by DEFERRING construction — the message is byte-identical.

Chose sketch (b), the reader-then-require spelling, over (a) the thunk: a thunk
would have added a concept at ~20 require-current-frame! call sites repo-wide (or
an ifn?/map type-dispatch) for a win at one, whereas (or (resolve-current-frame)
(require-current-frame! ...)) touches ONE call site and literally spells out the
relationship require-current-frame!'s own docstring already documents ('built on
this reader'). A comment names the site, says why, and says not to collapse it back.
Scoped to subscribe alone — subscribe-once / unsubscribe run once per slot and keep
the plain call.

ERROR UNCHANGED: same extra, same payload, same emit, same throw, same capture-site
ancestry. New .cljc test (subscribe_opts_arity_cljs_test, rides both lanes) pins all
four fields a caller on that path sees — :rf.error/id, :operation, :where, :event-id.
Existing coverage asserted the discriminator only.

MEASURED (JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, ThreadMXBean, n=300, 5 rounds = 3 forward +
2 rev, controls +0.000% in all 10): PAIRED CONTROL in read_attribution.clj —
S1-EAGER (retired) 72.0-136.0 vs S1-CURFRM (shipped) 32.0 FLAT in all ten
measurements. Saving 40.0-104.0 B/call.

THE BIMODALITY IS REAL AND EXPLAINED, not averaged away: S1-EAGER reads 136.0 in all
3 forward rounds and 72.0 in both reversed. 136 = 32 (JVM thread-bound
*current-frame* deref — Var.getThreadBinding allocates a MapEntry per read) + 40
((first query-v) seqing the vector) + 64 (the two-entry payload map). Reversed, the
64 B map is SCALAR-REPLACED by escape analysis when the arm runs earlier and
require-current-frame! inlines. The shipped arm is 32.0 flat because neither the map
nor (first query-v) is evaluated on the happy path.

The bead's 136 B figure was thus (var deref 32) + (payload 104), not (map 96) +
(first 40) as estimated. The 32 B floor does NOT exist in CLJS (no thread bindings),
so the SHARE this saves is larger there than on the JVM.

(first query-v) -> (nth query-v 0) NOT taken, as the bead recommended.

Gates: core JVM 2152/10616 green; npm run test:cljs 11799/58740 green.

title: bench: re-take B6's update row WITHOUT the microtask yield, gated on the non-vacuity check
description:
FOUND by rf2-huhno's re-take (PR #7152).

rf2-huhno asked whether the update row should be re-taken without timed-write!'s single microtask yield, on the reasoning that rf2-w2m25 / PR #7133 gives Freehand a synchronous commit so the yield is historical. b6-rows' own docstring carries the same suggestion.

THE RE-TAKE SAYS IT IS NOT A FREE TIGHTENING. Measured on main at 7c41225b4b, Freehand's broad-update window has RESTRUCTURED: the empty react-dom/flushSync that used to carry 3.0-3.5 ms now costs ~0.0, and the gap that used to be ~0.2 ms now carries 3.6-3.9 ms. Freehand's notification and React's render and commit run INSIDE that microtask.

So removing the yield does not remove the work. Either it moves into the flushSync (total unchanged, legs re-attributed again) or the notification has not yet fired when the empty flushSync runs, the commit lands after the measured window, and the DOM read-back fails — which is precisely the fault b6-rows records from the first attempt at this row (80 of 320 floor samples ended holding the old value).

WHAT IT NEEDS: a yield-free variant of timed-write! run against the flushSync non-vacuity check rf2-0fgth added, on all four arms, with the per-write DOM read-back as the gate. If every arm verifies, the row can be re-taken without the yield and every figure tightens by the microtask boundary. If Freehand fails verification, the yield stays and b6-rows' docstring should stop describing it as removable.

This is a change to the PUBLISHED WINDOW, not a re-measurement, which is why it is filed rather than folded into the re-take.
close_reason:
Done in PR #7223. ANSWER: THE YIELD STAYS.

b6_yield_app rides b6_prod_run.cjs's B6_INIT_FN seam so the driver, arms and fixture are the published ones. Chromium 147 headless via Playwright, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false. Six rounds of 3 warmup + 8 samples; THREE windows and five arms interleaved at the sample level (window rotating, arm order rotating and reflecting per rf2-88pie); every write read back out of the DOM inside its own window.

THE NON-VACUITY GATE, asked of every arm and every shape before any figure. Both Freehand arms FAIL the yield-free window. Across both rows 2,772 writes of 20,790 failed their read-back and EVERY ONE is a Freehand arm in the no-yield window: 66 of 66 per arm broad, 1,320 of 1,320 per arm narrow, and 0 in every other one of the fifteen (arm, window) cells. The write sits outside any flush, so rf2-w2m25 / #7133's closer never fires, the empty flushSync after it has nothing to commit, and the clock stops on the OLD value. It reads 0.7 ms against the published 3.5 - a 5x 'speed-up' that is the commit landing outside the window, exactly the fault b6-rows records from this row's first attempt.

BROAD, p50 ms/write, ranges across 6 rounds:
  floor                 yield 0.1 [0.1-0.2]  no-yield 0.1 [0.1-0.2]  in-flush 0.2 [0.1-0.2]
  freehand-interpreted  yield 3.5 [3.2-4.3]  no-yield 0.7 [0.6-0.8] INVALID  in-flush 3.5 [3.4-4.7]
  freehand-compiled     yield 3.1 [3.0-3.8]  no-yield 0.6 [0.6-0.8] INVALID  in-flush 3.2 [3.0-3.8]
  reagent               yield 0.4 [0.3-0.5]  no-yield 0.4 [0.3-0.5]  in-flush 0.3 [0.3-0.5]
  floor+spin (control)  yield 2.1 [2.1-2.1]  no-yield 2.1 [2.1-2.1]  in-flush 2.1 [2.0-2.1]

DID THE YIELD MATTER? No, and that is the second half of the answer. The ONE yield-free window that DOES verify on all four arms - flushSync(write) then the arm's drain - reads 3.5 [3.4-4.7] against the published 3.5 [3.2-4.3] on interpreted Freehand and 3.2 [3.0-3.8] against 3.1 [3.0-3.8] on compiled. OVERLAPPING RANGES on every arm, so indistinguishable. The legs say where it went: 0.6-0.8 write plus 2.5-3.2 gap becomes 3.4-4.7 write plus 0.0 gap. Same work, third re-attribution. rf2-huhno's hoped-for tightening does not exist, and #7133's extra commit pass is inside that window and not separable from it here.

THE NARROW ROW IS THE CAUTION. There the invalid no-yield window's range OVERLAPS the published one (7.5-9.9 against 8.9-11.5 per 20-write sample), so by this repo's own rule the clock would have called them indistinguishable and accepted a window in which 1,320 of 1,320 writes never reached the page. ONLY THE DOM READ-BACK CAUGHT IT.

POSITIVE CONTROL: :floor+spin, the floor arm with a 2.0 ms CPU spin around its own drain, predicted to read the floor's plus 2.0 ms PER WRITE OF THE SAMPLE. Broad predicted 2.1 / measured 2.1 (error 0.0) in two windows, -0.1 in the third; narrow predicted 41.7 / measured 41.1 (-1.4%). The per-write factor is not decoration - the first run predicted a flat +2.0 and read +39.1 on the narrow row, and the control caught the harness's own arithmetic.

b6-rows' docstring, its published :measurement-method string and b6_update_dom_cljs_test's namespace docstring have all STOPPED describing the yield as removable, which is what the bead asked for on this branch of the outcome. Recorded in docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md section 7, where rf2-huhno left the question. The gate's own first-version bug is on the record there too: it ran its shapes back to back and read in-flush as failing while the measured in-flush window verified 660 of 660 writes; it now settles before each shape.

Gates: bench:freehand-browser 30/465 exit 0; implementation/freehand JVM 1284/8803 exit 0; test:browser 841/5459 exit 0. Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.vxfjt-yield-ablation-raw.txt (local-only).

title: bench: B6's mount arm binds no frame, so the published row measures a shape no application uses
description:
FOUND while settling rf2-prjh0 (PR #7146). Filed as a METHOD note, not a defect - no published figure is wrong.

rf2-prjh0 asked whether B6's Freehand mount arm overstates because it creates a frame per sample. It does not: a frameless v/mount runs no plan and creates no frame. But the measurement that settled it turned up the opposite, smaller point.

EVERY REAL APPLICATION BINDS A FRAME. B6's mount arm does not - it passes only a :disambiguator. So the published mount row measures a mount shape that ships nowhere, and it is the CHEAPEST such shape. Measured, paired within round, 6 rounds:
  W1 (1,203 el)  a shared pre-created frame costs x1.038 more than the published arm, higher in 6 of 6 rounds
  W2 (301 el)    x1.109, higher in 6 of 6

So interpreted W1 mount against Reagent is ~3.8% better in the table than an application would see, and W2 ~10.9%. Both are small against a ~2x gap and neither changes any conclusion - which is exactly why this is P3 and not a correction.

THE CHOICE, and it is a real one: either (a) move B6's Freehand mount arms to a shared pre-created :frame so the row prices the shape consumers ship, re-taking the whole row against a floor measured in the same run (the ratio is only meaningful that way), or (b) leave it and keep the note that now sits in freehand-vs-reagent.md §1. Option (a) makes Freehand look slightly worse and is probably the more honest row; option (b) costs nothing. Not worth a re-run on its own - fold it into the next occasion the mount row is re-taken for another reason.

The arms already exist and are shipped: b7_mount_frame.cljs carries fh-no-frame, fh-shared-frame and fh-frame-per-sample side by side, so whoever re-takes the row does not need to build anything.
close_reason:
Resolved as option (b) — keep the frameless arm, state the magnitude in the table rather than only in a linked report.

The mount row was re-taken on main at 7c41225b4b (fresh, as part of rf2-huhno's b6_prod_run): published arm 3.056 x floor [2.931-3.226], Reagent 1.588 [1.500-1.742] -> 1.92x Reagent. Applying PR #7146's measured x1.038 for the shared pre-created frame puts the shipped shape at ~2.00x Reagent.

Option (a) rejected: the correction is 3.8% on W1, smaller than the row's own round-to-round spread [2.931-3.226], and re-basing a release-gate row requires re-taking the floor in the same run. The conclusion is identical either way — interpreted mount is about twice Reagent — so the change buys a third digit and costs a gate re-base.

freehand-vs-reagent.md §1's note now carries both numbers and the rejection rationale, so the row is no longer quietly generous. PR #7152.

title: pair-mcp: invoke-and-guard drops ex-data — relay 1's half of the two-relay asymmetry
description:
Mirror image of rf2-6tzm5, found while fixing it.

pair-mcp has two consumer-facing error relays. rf2-6tzm5 fixed relay 2
(`tools/probe.cljs` `err->result`), which kept the ex-data and dropped
the ex-message; it now carries BOTH.

Relay 1 — `server.cljs` `invoke-and-guard` (~line 539) — still has the
opposite defect:

  (wire/result {:ok? false :reason :handler-threw :message (.-message err)} true)

It keeps the MESSAGE and drops `(ex-data err)` entirely. So a throw that
fires while a tool body BUILDS its request loses its `:rf.error/id` —
the machine discriminator a consumer's agent BRANCHES on — plus every
actionable slot the author put in ex-data (`:where`, `:recovery`, and
the per-site payload).

Live example: `tools/eval_form.cljs` `emit-name`'s
`:rf.error/pair-mcp-rt-let-binding-bad-shape` throw. Its message rides
(error_boundary_test pins the sentence + the trailing token, so the
token at least survives INSIDE the message string), but its ex-data
does not — an agent must regex the token out of prose instead of
reading a keyword slot.

Fix shape mirrors rf2-6tzm5's: merge ex-data alongside, letting the
explicit `:reason :handler-threw` and `:message` keys keep their
precedence over an ex-data map that happens to carry the same keys
(note the precedence is the OPPOSITE way round from relay 2, because
here the relay's own `:reason` is the envelope discriminator).

Not folded into rf2-6tzm5 because it is a distinct blast radius:
every relay-1 handler-threw envelope gains ex-data slots, and
`error_boundary_test`'s relay-1 rows plus any `:handler-threw`
conformance fixture want checking first. rf2-6tzm5 verified relay 2's
consumers; relay 1's are unmeasured.
close_reason: Closed

title: freehand-views browser sweep can now assert a reactively-driven repaint
description:
Follow-on to rf2-r83ni (record correction) and rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz (the fix).

The freehand-views deck's browser scenario in
tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs drives commits through

the notification channel. It does that because, when it was written, a

observation port held a watch on a Reaction that had captured no
sources — so a reactively-driven re-render was not assertable on any
host that also mounts Xray.

activation fix holds end to end in a real DOM — the substrate contract
tests cover the port, but not a Freehand cell repainting on a page that
is simultaneously hosting Xray's shell.

scenario. Prose in tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md already
says this is 'tracked separately' — this is that bead.

title: Rename the with-redefs 'production gate' suites — they cannot reach a load-time gate

`re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` is read ONCE, at namespace-load time. Every

title: an unregistered owner's NON-MAP-params scoped key still rides verbatim under an unnamed slot on a family trace row
description:
FOUND while closing rf2-wd9im's merged-PR audit #7013 (non-map canonical params). Filed rather than fixed because the remedy costs more than the leak, and that judgement is the mayor's — this may well be a correct-to-close.

THE RESIDUE. `re-frame.resources.trace-egress/scoped-key-shape?` now recognises a scoped key `[scope resource-id canonical-params]` on either of two proofs: a MAP at position 2, or the resource REGISTRY knowing position 1. A key with NEITHER — non-map canonical params AND an unregistered / cleared / hot-reloaded-away owner — is not recognised, so under an UNNAMED slot on a resource-family trace row (`:blocking`, `:identities`, `:optimistic-keys`, an embedded `:work/id`, …) it falls to the recursive walk and its scope + params ride verbatim. The fail-closed posture says an owner we cannot read is not provably safe, so in principle it should redact.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED. There is nothing left to read. `[:rf.scope/global :gone/thing ["x"]]` and `:owner [:app :l 1]` are the same shape to the projector once the map proof and the registry proof are both gone, so closing it means redacting EVERY structural 3-vector in the family — `:owner`, `:cause`, a three-id `:branch`. That is the over-redaction the shape-driven default was specifically designed to avoid (rf2-wd9im's own `:branch` control asserts it), and for the resource tools it is as much a defect as the leak.

WHERE IT IS ALREADY COVERED, which is most of the surface:
  - a NAMED slot (`:resource/key` / `:resource/keys` / `:matched` / …) projects BY POSITION, so an unregistered owner's key redacts there whatever its params shape;
  - inside an fx CARRIER, `named?` does the same job — position 1 of a `[:rf.work/resource …]` work-id and any `resource`-namespaced map key are family-planted by construction (this bead's sibling arm in the same PR restored that, and `fx-carrier-named-slot-fails-closed-for-an-unregistered-non-map-params-owner` pins it).

So the uncovered case is exactly: unnamed slot + family row + non-map params + unregistered owner. A live app hits it only when a resource is cleared or hot-reloaded between the row's emission and its egress projection.

OPTIONS IF IT IS TO BE CLOSED, none of them obviously worth it:
  (a) accept and document — the docstring already states the boundary explicitly;
  (b) have the emit sites TAG the slot (a `resource`-namespaced slot name, or wrap the key), which turns a shape question into a naming one and reintroduces the roster rot rf2-wd9im removed;
  (c) carry the family's own marker inside the key, which changes the canonical resource identity — far too big for this.

MY RECOMMENDATION: (a). Close as accepted boundary unless a real reproduction turns up.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS ACCEPTED BOUNDARY (mayor, per the finding worker's own recommendation on PR #7115).

THE CASE: a scoped key with NON-MAP params, naming an UNREGISTERED owner, under an UNNAMED slot on a family trace row. Both of the projector's proofs are gone at once — the map-at-position-2 shape proof and the resource-registry proof — so the key is structurally INDISTINGUISHABLE from ordinary app data such as [:app :l 1].

WHY THE REMEDY IS WORSE THAN THE DISEASE: closing it requires tokenizing any 3-vector that merely wears the scoped-key skeleton. That is precisely the 'tokenize a foreign payload wholesale' move rf2-1kiuj already examined and rejected, because it redacts a PLAIN owner's ordinary request map. The vector-of-vectors guard was also weighed and rejected on PR #7115: ':branch' is a vector of route ids on this very row, and the new control asserts a three-id :branch rides verbatim.

WHY CLOSING IS SAFE: an UNREGISTERED owner has no :sensitive?/:sensitive declaration to honour in the first place — there is no registration to read it from — so the redaction obligation that makes the other seven leaks real does not attach here. The boundary is documented in scoped-key-shape?'s own docstring, which outlives a bead.

POSTURE: pre-alpha masterpiece, but not gold-plating and not drowning in minutiae. An explicitly documented and reasoned boundary is engineering; contorting the projector to cover an unreachable case is not. Reopen if a real consumer hits it.

title: Read continuation reply of an INFINITE feed: a :data-rooted declaration does not match the merged-items vector (no index-free fork)
description:
Surfaced by rf2-ko5lm's widening and FILED not fixed per the dispatch rule.

WHAT LEAKS. rf2-ko5lm gave read continuations the mutation's declaration redaction: `trace_egress/redact-reply-declarations` applies `classification/redact-continuation-reply` over the read owner's spec, re-rooting a `:data`-rooted declaration onto the reply's `:value`. That reaches `re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths` -> `walk-with-paths`, whose `:decide` is an EXACT path membership test (`(contains? sensitive-set path)`), paths built by conj-ing map keys and vector indices.

For a SCALAR resource that is exactly right: `{:sensitive [[:data :email]]}` becomes `[:value :email]` and matches.

For an INFINITE FEED it does not match anything. `events/infinite-reply-value` delivers the MERGED / flattened item list as `:value` (rf2-c64uiz — both the fresh-skip cache hit and the async page-0 settle deliver that one shape), so the runtime path is `[:value <i> :email]` and the declaration is `[:value :email]`. No index-free fork, no match, and the declared field rides the fx carriers verbatim.

THE DURABLE SIDE DOES FORK, which is what makes this a disagreement rather than a uniform limitation. `classification/project-entry-data` says so explicitly: "INFINITE feeds ride for free: the lowered decl is `[… :data :token]`, the runtime `:data` is the page VECTOR, and `elide-wire-value`'s index-free fork (`fork-index-paths`) matches the index-free decl against the indexed runtime path `[… :data <page-idx> :token]` on EVERY page — no special per-page branch." So a feed's declared field redacts in the durable entry and rides raw in the continuation echo of it — the same two-carriers-one-rule shape rf2-ko5lm closed for scalars, still open for feeds.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. The two walkers are different primitives. `redact-with-paths` is the path-substitution walker the carrier redactions use (mutation reply, execute event args, invalid-params error); `elide-wire-value` is the schema-first elision walker with the index-free fork. Making the carrier walker fork is a change to a CORE primitive with four callers, not a resources-family change, and it must not silently start matching indexed paths for the mutation reply / execute-args callers that never intended it. The alternative — route the reply's `:value` through `project-egress` instead — needs an absolute registry offset the reply does not have (it is a transient carrier value, not a runtime-db path), which is the whole reason rf2-ko5lm derived from the spec rather than reading the registry.

SCOPE NOTE. Only the `:data` axis is affected; `[:params …]` / `[:scope …]` declarations index a map and match fine. And a feed that declares its slot at the ITEM level today has no spelling that means "each item" — worth settling in the same ruling.

PROOF STANDARD: RED and GREEN with identical test and assertion counts differing only in failures, driving a real `[:rf.resource/ensure … :reply-to …]` against a registered infinite feed, plus the two-sided control (a feed declaring nothing rides byte-identical; an undeclared sibling field inside each item survives).
notes:
See rf2-dl7bz for the preserved in-flight state: a clustered worker holds uncommitted work for both beads in worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/egress-keyfork (branch worker/egress-keyfork-dl7bz), zero commits, no remote, during the 2026-07-26 API 529 outage. That worktree must not be reaped by the hygiene loop; recovery is to resume the same agent, never to dispatch a second worker onto the branch.

FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7099 (worker egress-keyfork, 2026-07-26).

SCOPING, which was the live question. The fork is OPT-IN and reaches exactly ONE
caller. `classification/redact-with-paths` gains a 4th argument; the 3-arity —
i.e. every pre-existing call site — delegates with `index-free? = false`, under
which the candidate declaration-coordinate set is the singleton `#{path}` and
matching is byte-for-byte the exact membership test the walker always applied.
`resources.classification/redact-continuation-reply` is the sole opt-in. The
mutation-reply and execute-args callers the bead warned about are NOT widened:
`project-execute-event-args` still calls the 3-arity, as do `redact-event-vec`,
`http.privacy-body/classify-decoded`, `machines.ssr/project-snapshot-data` and
`redact-by-classification`. `redact-continuation-reply` is shared by the mutation
reply and the read reply, and both get the fork deliberately — it is ONE
projection-relative declaration surface re-rooted onto ONE carrier shape, and
splitting them is what would let the two drift.

THE SPELLING QUESTION, settled rather than deferred. A feed needs no "each item"
wildcard: the index-free declaration already IS that spelling, because it is what
the DURABLE side has always meant by `[:data :email]` on a page vector
(`project-entry-data` -> `elide-wire-value` -> `fork-index-paths`). No vocabulary
was added; the carrier now honours the reading the durable side established.

GRAIN. Index fork ONLY — no `:map-of` key-skip fork. So the carrier walker stays
strictly MORE precise than the durable side's, and a positional index can never
float a declaration past a named slot.

PROOF. `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` §(rf2-zaopo), a real
`[:rf.resource/ensure … :reply-to …]` against a registered infinite feed
(`:declared/feed`, enveloped pages + `:page->items`), both continuation paths:
  RED   58 tests / 395 assertions / 19 failures / 0 errors
  GREEN 58 tests / 395 assertions /  0 failures / 0 errors
Identical test and assertion counts; failures the only difference.

TWO-SIDED CONTROL, both sides asserted:
  - `fx-carrier-keeps-an-undeclared-feeds-merged-items-byte-identical` — the SAME
    page through `:plain/feed`, which declares neither axis: every reply-carrier
    row's tags byte-identical raw vs projected, items readable field for field,
    no carrier row stamped `:sensitive?`. It PASSES ON RED AND ON GREEN (0
    failures in the RED run), which is what makes it a control rather than a
    second acceptance arm.
  - the undeclared sibling `:display-name` survives in EVERY item while `:email`
    redacts and `:large`-declared `:avatar` becomes the size marker.
  - `fx-carrier-index-free-fork-does-not-reach-an-undeclared-nested-slot` — an
    `:email` one NAMED slot deeper (`[:value 0 :meta :email]`) is a different
    position and rides verbatim.
  - `trusted-local-include-sensitive-keeps-raw-declared-feed-items` — the
    redaction is the off-box default, not a strip.

REGRESSION EVIDENCE for the un-widened callers (all foreground, EXIT=0):
  core       2126 tests / 10492 assertions / 0F 0E
  resources   734 tests /  6820 assertions / 0F 0E
  epoch       514 tests /  6859 assertions / 0F 0E
  http        493 tests /  3787 assertions / 0F 0E
  machines   1195 tests /  4164 assertions / 0F 0E
  test:cljs 11549 tests / 57808 assertions / 0F 0E

DOES NOT COVER rf2-rnsv2. That bead is the read-FAILURE continuation's `:error`
envelope. `carrier-decl-paths` re-roots `:data` -> `:value`, `:params` ->
`:params`, `:scope` -> `:scope` and nothing onto `:error`, so no declaration can
reach it and the index-free mode changes nothing there. Its ruling stands
untouched.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7107 (2026-07-26) — DEFAULT-MODE INVARIANT CORRECTED; CANDIDATE-CARDINALITY CLAIM STILL FALSE.

The new wording correctly says default mode carries `#{path}` while the concrete path remains a declaration prefix and `#{}` after pruning, so exact matching is preserved. But the preceding sentence still says the candidate set “stays bounded by the declaration cardinality.” In `:index-free?` mode, unchanged candidates ride an index while indexed interpretations are added, so one declaration can keep several of its prefixes alive at once. Against the merged private functions, declaration `#{[0 0 0]}` produced candidate counts `[1 2 3 4]` and final set `#{[] [0] [0 0] [0 0 0]}`: four candidates for one declaration. State the bound in terms of the finite declaration-prefix vocabulary (plus the retained root), not declaration count. No behavior defect was found; the projection gate remained green at 30 tests / 115 assertions and remote PR checks were 63 pass / 0 fail / 13 skipped.

title: Resource trace egress: a :serialize owner's projection-relative :params / :scope declaration is not honoured inside :resource/key
description:
SEVENTH-ish in the resource-egress leak family, surfaced by rf2-ko5lm's widening and FILED not fixed per the dispatch rule.

WHAT LEAKS. `re-frame.resources.ssr/project-scoped-key` projects a scoped key `[scope resource-id params]` by the COARSE `whole-entry-disposition` only. For a `:serialize` owner it returns the key VERBATIM. That is correct for the SSR durable path, which has a documented registry-driven counterpart (`classification/project-entry-params` walks the params component through `project-egress` seeded at the lowered registry offset, because it has the entry's `key-id` and the live frame). The docstring says so in as many words: "The trace / tool egress callers pass `:serialize` through verbatim (they rely on the coarse disposition + the digest below, not per-slot params)."

The TRACE / off-box egress callers have no such counterpart. So a resource declaring

  (rf/reg-resource :account/summary
    {:sensitive [[:params :account-id]] ...} ...)

with no coarse `:sensitive?` has its declared `:account-id` ride RAW inside `:resource/key` on every `:rf.resource/*` / `:rf.mutation/*` family row, inside every scoped-keys vector slot, inside every `[:rf.work/resource <key> <gen>]` work-id, and inside every fx carrier (`:rf.fx/args` / `:rf.event/fx`) the key reaches. Off-box, epoch, MCP.

THE SHAPE IS THE FAMILY'S USUAL ONE. rf2-ko5lm just closed the READ CONTINUATION REPLY's copy of those same params (`redact-reply-declarations` applies the owner declaration to the reply's `:params` slot). The key's copy sits one slot over on the same carrier and still rides. Two carriers of one value, one rule applied — the rf2-irwsq shape. `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` §(rf2-ko5lm) names this residue in prose and deliberately does NOT assert it, so no test has to change when this lands.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD, not part of rf2-ko5lm. The reply is ONE map on ONE pair of carriers and its fix is the mutation's own `redact-continuation-reply` reused. This is the scoped KEY, which is the family's universal carrier: the fix has to live in the shared `disposition+project-key` pipeline that SSR durable egress, the tooling algebra view, and the trace projector all reuse, so it changes three egress boundaries at once and has to be judged against `project-scoped-key`'s explicit deferral rather than around it.

THE HARD PART, which is why the deferral exists. A scoped key is a CEDN-1 byte-keyed identity (Spec 016 §Resource identity) and the cache-key-identity round-trip depends on it — `registry-classifies-under?` exists precisely so an unnecessary walk cannot collapse a list↔vector params kind (rf2-wgutc2). A per-slot substitution inside the params component changes the key's bytes, so any fix must decide what a tool's per-key JOIN means afterwards. Options, none free:
  - substitute in place and accept that a declared key no longer round-trips to its cache identity;
  - content-address the WHOLE params component when any `:params`-rooted declaration exists (the `:redact` shape, applied on a declaration rather than a coarse claim) — keeps distinctness and joins, loses the undeclared sibling params a tool can currently read;
  - leave the key and treat the declaration as data-axis-only, documenting that `[:params …]` declarations are an SSR-durable-only surface — which would need `reg-resource` to say so loudly rather than accept the path silently.

The second is probably right (it is the grain the coarse arm already uses and it preserves joins), but it is a RULING, not a mechanical fix.

PROOF STANDARD when it is taken: RED and GREEN with identical test and assertion counts differing only in failures, plus the two-sided control — a plain owner's key rides byte-identical and `:rf.scope/global` is untouched.
notes:
LANDED — PR #7254 (branch worker/slot-params-dl7bz), 2026-07-29.

RATIFIED SHAPE IMPLEMENTED AS RULED, and kept narrow. `ssr/project-scoped-key` is NOT widened: it still takes and ignores its spec argument and still rides a `:serialize` key verbatim, and `project-scoped-key-still-defers-on-serialize` is a standing test that reds if anyone moves the arm into the shared projection. `implementation/ssr/**` and `resources/ssr.cljc` are untouched by the diff. The per-slot arm is `trace_egress/redact-key-declarations`, beside `redact-reply-declarations`, built from the already-public `spec-declaration-marks`; `tooling/project-key-for-egress` opts into the same helper.

BOTH tooling.cljc DOCSTRINGS WERE STILL FALSE when checked, and are now true — one by implementation, one by CORRECTION. The EP-0015 section comment ('applies the resource's per-slot :params projection-relative declarations') is now true of the code. `project-key-for-egress`'s ':serialize projects per-slot :params-schema marks' could NOT be honoured as written — EP-0025 removed the schema route into durable classification — so that clause is corrected to name the projection-relative declaration, with the correction stated in the docstring itself.

A SECOND DEFECT SURFACED AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME PR. `row-owner-redacts?` borrowed `project-trace-scoped-key`'s `sensitive?` flag. Sound while that flag meant 'the owner makes a coarse claim'; UNSOUND the moment a `:serialize` key honours declarations, because a per-slot substitution makes the KEY redact (the row stamp must report it) while saying nothing about the free cursor or a reply's `:value` / `:params`. The epoch suite caught it: a declaration-only owner's whole reply body tokenized and its undeclared siblings vanished — the exact over-redaction rf2-ko5lm's grain argument forbids. The coarse arm is now extracted as `coarse-key-projection` and read directly. Regression-tested.

BUILD POSTURE: DEV-ONLY, stated plainly rather than implied always-on. Both callers sit behind `interop/debug-enabled?` (the epoch tool-pair's trace bus — `emit!` AND `emit-error!` are both gated) or bundle isolation (the tooling sibling). The always-on `:rf.observe/*` axis carries no resource scoped key.

MUTATION PROOF meets the bead's standard: src reverted to origin/main, test unchanged — 756 tests / 6930 assertions in BOTH runs, 14 failures vs 0. The `:341` failure prints the whole defect in one line (wire {:account-id :rf/redacted, :page 3} vs trace {:account-id "acct-SECRET-4417", :page 3}), and the tool-egress failures at :415/:418 are tooling.cljc's two claims red against their own prose. Every two-sided control passed in BOTH runs.

GATES all exit 0: resources JVM dev 757/6934; resources JVM prod-posture (-Dre-frame.debug=false, new ns) 14/48; epoch JVM 539/7131; ssr JVM 592/2892; core egress-chokepoint source-scan 3/7.

RESIDUE FILED: rf2-5e2ye — `ssr/project-entry` registry-projects only the params component (index 2) of a `:serialize` wire key; there is no scope counterpart, so a `:scope`-rooted declaration is honoured by the epoch/registry walk and now by every trace/tool key, but NOT by the SSR hydration wire key. Out of scope here by the ruling's own 'SSR untouched'.

title: Decide whether the docs/core/freehand sample gate extends past its own tree
description:
RULING NEEDED, filed rather than taken - the rf2-kem4o worker was told to report a scope extension, not decide it.

WHAT LANDED (PR #7085, rf2-kem4o). The docs/core/freehand sample gate no longer accepts a roster owner that merely RESOLVES: samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj now reads each fixture namespace's source, pairs every top-level definition with the names it mentions, seeds the relation with the deftest forms, and requires each owner to land in the closure. Turning it on flagged 39 rows across six fixture namespaces, every one of which is now rendered or run. It also caught a live defect nobody had found: composition.md block 13 called `field` with :on-input where the declaration 22 lines above reads :on-change, so (conj on-change ::v/value) folded nil into a seq and a pasted example raised :rf.error/view-bad-event at render.

THE EXTENSION QUESTION. That roster covers docs/core/freehand/** and nothing else. Documented examples elsewhere - docs/api/**, docs/core/**, docs/story/**, migration/** - are covered by the call-position discipline in doc_api_check / doc_guide_check, which asks "does this name still exist as a public surface?" and never "does this example run?". Two of the five known instances of the defect class lived outside the freehand guide:

  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's reg-error-projector example returned 2 of the 4 LOCKED public-error keys, so a reader who pasted it got their projector silently discarded (fixed in PR #6966); and
  - a reg-route example that throws at registry.cljc:455.

So the mechanism is proven and the scope is the open question: extend this roster to a second tree, or accept that outside docs/core/freehand an example is proof-read rather than executed. Extending is not free - the freehand roster works because a chapter fixture namespace exists per page and the samples are transcribed onto the real classpath. A second tree needs the same fixture spine before a roster row can point at anything.

NOT a request to build a second gate. That was already ruled out, and correctly: fixing this gate's holes is what made it BE the gate a parallel one would have had to become.

THE HONEST LIMIT, which any scoping decision must carry forward: this class of gate catches a fixture nobody exercises. It does NOT catch forms.md's instance, where a rendered example subscribes to the wrong thing. That is a correctness judgement about a running example and no mechanical gate finds it.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-h5fkc): NO. The docs/core/freehand sample roster does not extend past its own tree. Evidence and cost below; recorded here and in the PR body.

title: Revised ruling: the Tags-column pairing cannot detect a SCHEMA deletion/rename from the two corpora
description:
Follow-up from rf2-ehy4l (PR for rf2-66czz/rf2-ehy4l/rf2-f9v2s). The Tags-column arm now reports collisions and asserts CLAIMED == PAIRED, so a pairing the arm holds but never exercises reds. Two of the four mutation controls the bead asked for remain UNCAUGHT, and the acceptance criteria says to return to the ruling rather than close them with a roster.

WHAT IS UNCAUGHT (proved by mutation, both GREEN):
  * deleting a paired schema (removed the whole (def ResourceRoutePlanTags ...) form): claimed 93->92, paired 93->92, 19 tests 0 failures.
  * equal-count replacement (renamed ResourceRoutePlanTags -> SomeUnrelatedThingTags): 111 schemas before and after, claimed 92, paired 92, 19 tests 0 failures.

WHY IT IS NOT DERIVABLE from spec/009-Instrumentation.md + spec/Spec-Schemas.md:
  * 22 of the 111 *Tags schemas are legitimately claimed by NO active catalogue row - 10 belong to non-error-catalogue ops (:rf.route/prefetched, :rf.machine/action-ran, :rf.epoch/db-replaced ...), and 12 name no 009 operation by either derivation spelling. An orphaned schema is therefore indistinguishable from a correctly-unpaired one.
  * only 5 *Tags names are cited anywhere in 009, and git grep finds no *Tags name referenced from implementation/ - so there is no cross-reference totality to lean on either.
  * all 111 sit under one heading in Spec-Schemas (Per-category :tags schemas), so section scoping does not discriminate.

THE ROW HALF IS ALREADY COVERED: deleting :rf.error/resource-route-plan's row reds every-emitted-category-is-catalogued (invariant #5, same file). Note the python CHECK A did NOT fire - the id is still mentioned in 009 prose and catalogue_ids reads the whole doc.

THE RULING NEEDED: is a shrink-only orphan-schema baseline (22 entries, honesty-guarded like out-of-catalogue-allow-list and tags-column-shrink-only-baseline) acceptable here, or does rf2-6tags' no-roster ruling stand and the gap stay open and documented? Do not action without the ruling - a roster added against the ruling is the drift generator it forbids.
notes:
REOPENED — I CLOSED THIS ON A MERGE THAT DID NOT CARRY IT. My error, and the mechanism is one I warn workers about in every brief.

WHAT HAPPENED: PR #7087 carried both rf2-u3otj and rf2-23qsg on one branch. IT MERGED AT head.sha = 19c6ee3dcf — THE FIRST COMMIT ONLY. The bead-2 commit was pushed BEFORE the merge, but the PR object never advanced past the first. rf2-u3otj landed (blob-verified identical); rf2-23qsg did not.

I THEN CLOSED BOTH BEADS BECAUSE THE PR TITLE NAMED BOTH. That is precisely the failure the standing rule exists to prevent — VERIFY BY BLOB HASH, NOT BY PR STATE — and I apply it to workers reports while skipping it on my own closes. A PR title is a claim about intent; a merged blob is a fact.

THE RULE I NOW OWE MYSELF: WHEN ONE PR CARRIES MULTIPLE BEADS, VERIFY EACH BEAD ARTEFACT ON main SEPARATELY BEFORE CLOSING ANY OF THEM. A single merge event is not evidence that every commit on the branch landed — twenty PRs today merged a state older than the worker tip, and at least two merged at a stale PR OBJECT whose head.sha never advanced at all.

One integer, tags-column-paired-floor = 93, REPLACING A SLACK >= 80 — so the arm already HAD a floor and this is genuinely no new mechanism, just the number tightened to the truth. Its honesty guard runs the other way too: a floor left BELOW live coverage has rotted and would absorb the next lost pairing silently.

BOTH MUTATIONS PROVED, each confirmed applied by git diff --stat AND token grep-back before the verdict: deletion gives "PAIRED and diffed: 92, below the recorded floor of 93"; equal-count rename with schema count 111 BEFORE AND AFTER gives the identical red. title: The :rf.ui.compile/* family is outside every catalogue gate: bad-render-fn is emitted and has no spec home at all
description:
Found by the rf2-l1l0p worker while adding recovery vocabulary to spec/009. It referenced the verdict WITHOUT naming the id, deliberately, rather than plant a dangling reference — the right call.

THE FINDING: :rf.ui.compile/bad-render-fn is EMITTED by the compiled analyzer and has NO HOME ANYWHERE IN spec/. And check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py only scans :rf.error/* and :rf.warning/*, so NO GATE SEES IT — not Check A (source to catalogue), not the new Check C (catalogue to source). An entire keyword family sits outside the contract machinery.

THIS IS THE THIRD DIRECTION OF CATALOGUE BLINDNESS FOUND THIS WEEK, and each was invisible to the others: Check A verified source-to-catalogue and never asked the inverse; Check C (rf2-d89rs) added catalogue-to-source and found three documented ids nothing emits; this one is a whole NAMESPACE FAMILY neither direction covers because the scan is keyed on two prefixes.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST, and it is a real one: IS :rf.ui.compile/* MEANT TO BE SPEC-COMPLETE? These are compile-time analyzer refusals, not runtime traces — they may legitimately live in the compiler own documentation rather than the 009 catalogue. If they are meant to be catalogued, the scan prefixes widen and the family gets rows. If they are not, THE HONEST FIX IS A COMMENT IN THE CHECKER SAYING WHICH FAMILIES IT COVERS AND WHY — the same shape as rf2-eo2y5, where the roster was accidental rather than decided, and stating the boundary WAS the deliverable.

DO NOT WIDEN THE SCAN BEFORE ANSWERING THAT. Widening it blind would red the build on a family nobody decided to catalogue, which is a false red manufactured at scale — and this repo has spent two beads today fixing false reds.

CHECK THE DONOR ANGLE TOO: some :rf.ui.compile/* ids may belong to implementation/ui, which rf2-drpa3.57 deletes wholesale. The ledger has THREE dispositions — MOVE means the defect crosses into Freehand, REPLACE means the realization is not carried across, DELETE means it does not cross at all. That distinction decided two beads in opposite directions today.

PRs #7068, #7069, #7070 MERGED.

rf2-f9v2s — THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, which is the best possible outcome and better than my own framing. spec/Conventions.md:104 already decides it: :rf.ui.compile/* is "compile-time only: thrown at macroexpansion, NEVER EMITTED AT RUNTIME, NEVER A TRACE", home 004, roster pinned by the S1b analyzer reject tables. Spec 009 catalogue is the runtime error-EVENT vocabulary, so a never-a-trace id CANNOT have a row there by construction — widening the scan would have manufactured ~110 findings. The deliverable was the boundary comment, exactly the rf2-eo2y5 shape. Donor angle checked too: bad-render-fn is emitted from BOTH trees and Freehand copy survives, so the deletion takes the donor copy only; what crosses is the roster GATE, listed MOVE/F1/pending.

rf2-66czz — CHECK C now has a retired-reintroduction leg and FAILS CLOSED on a parse error (exit 2). Findings moved into a pure function so SELF-TESTS ENTER AT THE DEFECT LAYER, not under it — the old cases did their set arithmetic inline, which is precisely why they could not notice the retired set was never read. Population 445 active -> 445 active + 9 retired, and active can no longer silently reach 0. Self-tests 31 -> 42.

rf2-ehy4l — collisions REPORTED rather than dropped, CLAIMED == PAIRED asserted as an identity, live collision resolved in the corpus. Population 88 paired -> 93; claimed-but-never-diffed 1 -> 0. A newly-reachable row turned out to omit :frame and was FIXED IN THE ROW, not baselined. And it DECLINED two of its own mutation controls, reporting them as failures rather than passes — filed rf2-23qsg for the revised ruling, which I have now given: a shrink-only FLOOR on the paired count, one integer, no roster.

rf2-yn5nj and rf2-7g4qn — the carrier diagnostic and the prefetch constant, both audit reopens of merged work.

rf2-eyyd2, rf2-xnb1d, rf2-kx06s — the CI coverage remainder and two ledger rows.

THE DURABLE POINT ACROSS THE GATE BEADS: four blind spots were found in ONE contract surface today, each invisible from inside the others — Check A verified source-to-catalogue and never asked the inverse; Check C closed that and could collapse its own population; the Tags arm could shrink behind a floor; and a whole namespace family sat outside all of them because the scan keys on two prefixes. That is why the COVERED-POPULATION FIGURE is now part of every gate deliverable here, not a pass/fail.

description:
Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7057. The new Tags-column arm catches its motivating row omission, but its pairing coverage can silently shrink.

The live corpora currently produce 111 `*Tags` schemas and 88 unambiguous catalogue↔schema pairs. tags-column-pairing-is-live asserts only schema count >=100 and paired count >=80, plus one HandlerExceptionTags key anchor. Deleting or renaming a different paired schema such as ResourceRoutePlanTags yields 110 schemas / 87 pairs, both floors still green. tags-column-findings iterates only schemas that remain present, so the deleted pair disappears from the check rather than becoming a finding; the motivating-defect test uses its own synthetic schema map and also remains green. This is a static ceiling/floor, not a ratchet on pairing identity.

There is already a live blind instance: both :rf.http/stale-suppressed and :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed derive StaleSuppressedTags, so the implementation groups the two and deliberately pairs with neither. Spec-Schemas explicitly says StaleSuppressedTags belongs to the nav-token operation, but the new arm never checks that legitimate row. The code calls this whole-operation keying, yet it still derives only from (name category) and resolves collision by dropping coverage.

Do not fix this with another hand-maintained alias/row roster or an exact count; both are the drift generators the rf2-6tags ruling forbids. If the two existing corpora cannot derive a total, identity-preserving pairing without another authority, return to the ruling explicitly rather than treating broad count floors as proof. rf2-6tags is IN_PROGRESS and tracker-locked, so this is a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: A deletion/rename of any currently paired schema or catalogue row must red instead of merely reducing 88 toward the >=80 floor, and an equal-count replacement must not evade the guard. The live nav-token stale-suppressed row must remain paired to its owning StaleSuppressedTags schema (or be deliberately resolved by a corpus naming change) while the unrelated HTTP row stays unpaired; add mutation controls for schema deletion, row deletion/rename, equal-count replacement, and the collision. Do not introduce a hand-maintained alias table, static exact count, or silently widened baseline. If total identity pairing is not derivable from existing structured data, record and obtain a revised ruling before changing the corpus.
close_reason:
PRs #7068, #7069, #7070 MERGED.

rf2-f9v2s — THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, which is the best possible outcome and better than my own framing. spec/Conventions.md:104 already decides it: :rf.ui.compile/* is "compile-time only: thrown at macroexpansion, NEVER EMITTED AT RUNTIME, NEVER A TRACE", home 004, roster pinned by the S1b analyzer reject tables. Spec 009 catalogue is the runtime error-EVENT vocabulary, so a never-a-trace id CANNOT have a row there by construction — widening the scan would have manufactured ~110 findings. The deliverable was the boundary comment, exactly the rf2-eo2y5 shape. Donor angle checked too: bad-render-fn is emitted from BOTH trees and Freehand copy survives, so the deletion takes the donor copy only; what crosses is the roster GATE, listed MOVE/F1/pending.

rf2-66czz — CHECK C now has a retired-reintroduction leg and FAILS CLOSED on a parse error (exit 2). Findings moved into a pure function so SELF-TESTS ENTER AT THE DEFECT LAYER, not under it — the old cases did their set arithmetic inline, which is precisely why they could not notice the retired set was never read. Population 445 active -> 445 active + 9 retired, and active can no longer silently reach 0. Self-tests 31 -> 42.

rf2-ehy4l — collisions REPORTED rather than dropped, CLAIMED == PAIRED asserted as an identity, live collision resolved in the corpus. Population 88 paired -> 93; claimed-but-never-diffed 1 -> 0. A newly-reachable row turned out to omit :frame and was FIXED IN THE ROW, not baselined. And it DECLINED two of its own mutation controls, reporting them as failures rather than passes — filed rf2-23qsg for the revised ruling, which I have now given: a shrink-only FLOOR on the paired count, one integer, no roster.

rf2-yn5nj and rf2-7g4qn — the carrier diagnostic and the prefetch constant, both audit reopens of merged work.

rf2-eyyd2, rf2-xnb1d, rf2-kx06s — the CI coverage remainder and two ledger rows.

THE DURABLE POINT ACROSS THE GATE BEADS: four blind spots were found in ONE contract surface today, each invisible from inside the others — Check A verified source-to-catalogue and never asked the inverse; Check C closed that and could collapse its own population; the Tags arm could shrink behind a floor; and a whole namespace family sat outside all of them because the scan keys on two prefixes. That is why the COVERED-POPULATION FIGURE is now part of every gate deliverable here, not a pass/fail.

And the backslash hazard bit live during this work: "one heredoc did get mangled mid-session, exactly as warned" — the worker had already written its planter to a file.

title: CHECK C misses retired-id reintroduction and can collapse to zero rows
description:
Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7057. CHECK C correctly detects active catalogue rows with no reference emitter, but two fail-open directions remain.

1. RETIRED REINTRODUCTION. catalogue_ids() reads ids anywhere in Spec 009, including struck rows, so CHECK A treats a reintroduced retired id as catalogued. CHECK C computes only active_rows - emitted and discards retired_rows. A struck row whose literal emitter reappears therefore passes A, B, and C even though the implementation comments say a struck row is exactly the row that MUST NOT have an emitter. Direct pure probe: active=[], retired=[:rf.error/retired-but-reintroduced], emitted contains that id, check A findings=[], check C findings=[], while retired & emitted contains the defect.

2. ZERO-ROW COLLAPSE. catalogue_rows() returns two empty sets if the exact heading `### Error event catalogue` is renamed or no longer parsed. run_checks treats that as clean. A probe with a valid row under `### Error and warning event catalogue` still gives CHECK A the id from the whole document, but CHECK C sees zero active rows and reports nothing. The live verbose count (445 active + 9 retired) is output only, not an invariant.

These are the same CHECK C boundary, not a request for a general catalogue framework. rf2-d89rs is IN_PROGRESS and tracker-locked, so this is a follow-up rather than an edit to that Bead.
acceptance_criteria: CHECK C reports every retired catalogue row whose id is emitted by implementation source, while still allowing a retired row with no emitter. Add a self-test that reintroducing the emitter behind a struck row reds; CHECK A must not mask that result. The canonical catalogue-section parser must fail closed (setup error or explicit finding) when the heading/table cannot be found or the live active-row population collapses to zero, with focused valid/renamed/malformed controls. Preserve the single port-relative active-row exemption and its two stale-exemption honesty legs. Run self-test and live gate with the live 445-active/9-retired parse non-vacuous.
