title: Reconcile epoch MCP egress authority comments with the five-dispatch cascade and digestless whole-output markers
description:
Merged-PR audit of #7052 found active authority comments that no longer describe the fixture and projector they sit beside.

1. implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:627-638 still says record-carrying-resource-rows assembles a three-dispatch cascade and duplicates the last :rf.resource/owner-released row. #7052 widened the cascade to five top-level dispatches; its last record is the global :rf.resource/invalidated dispatch, so that is the row duplicated when the full listener harvest is appended.

2. The same file at :482-486 says the resource cascade settles more than five records. The producer driver contains exactly five dispatch-sync calls. Pinning :trace-events-keep to 50 is a reasonable future-proofing choice, but the current justification must say it removes sensitivity to future cascade growth, not claim a current sixth record that does not exist.

3. The large-value test docstring at :769-775 says the canonical :rf.size/large-elided marker contains :digest. The whole-output large-sub seam calls classification/large-marker without include-digests?, so its marker carries path/bytes/type/reason/hint/handle and no digest. The PR body explicitly recognized this and correctly asserted :bytes only.

4. The production authority docstring in implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1589 makes the same false digest claim for this exact whole-output marker.

These comments sit at the implementation and executable evidence authorities a programmer or agent will read to understand the wire contract. Behavior is correct; the repair is prose-only. The separate six-operations-as-five count cluster is already owned by rf2-ruiga and is excluded here.
acceptance_criteria:
- record-carrying-resource-rows accurately names the five-dispatch cascade and the actually duplicated final global invalidation row.
- The trace-events retention comment describes the 50 cap as protection against future cascade growth (or proves any additional settled records if they really exist); it does not claim an unproven current count above five.
- The test and production whole-output marker docs list only fields classification/large-marker actually emits without include-digests? and make clear no digest is present at this seam.
- Runtime and assertions remain unchanged; rf2-ruiga retains ownership of the separate six-as-five roster wording.
notes:
PR #7058 (branch worker/authority-prose, tip da4f8186dd). Prose-only, two files.

MEASURED, not inferred (probes replicating the deftest setup exactly):
- The cascade settles FIVE records, one per dispatch-sync: ensure / ensure / release-owner / invalidate-tags(session) / invalidate-tags(global). The LAST record's own family row is :rf.resource/invalidated (the GLOBAL one) — so that, not :owner-released, is the row that doubles when the bus harvest is appended. Both halves of the record-carrying-resource-rows docstring were wrong.
- The :trace-events-keep claim was wrong in a way that matters: under the INHERITED suite cap of 5 the cascade elides NOTHING (5 records, keep 5, retained [12 12 9 6 5]). There is no sixth record. At keep 4 the first record IS elided ([:ELIDED 12 9 6 5]) — the mechanism is real, the cascade just sits ON the boundary rather than past it. The pin is future-proofing, and the comment now says so with no number in it.
- :digest confirmed absent at the whole-output seam under EVERY profile — default, :rf.egress/off-box-tool, and a direct large-marker construction. A PATH-declared marker DOES get a digest under off-box-tool; the whole-output one never does, because elide-whole-output-large-slots builds via classification/large-marker (2-arity, {:reason :classification}) which never passes include-digests?. Both docstrings now state the asymmetry.

ALL FOUR SITES CHANGED; none were pre-fixed by the P1 that merged out of epoch/ + resources/.
Plus one clause: the historical '7 rows on the bus / 3 records' note in drive-resource-family! now carries a time qualifier (verified against 88a0aabd81 — the fixture really did have three dispatch-sync calls then), because 'the cascade' read as the present one.
VERIFIED ALREADY CORRECT, left alone: drive-resource-family! :574-575 'five dispatches / five records' — measured true, and it sits AT the authority.

trace_egress.cljc SIBLING DEFECT: LEFT DELIBERATELY. It is rf2-ruiga's (open, P4), whose scope also covers epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:381 and :537 — two lines INSIDE the file this PR rewrites. rf2-uozi8's own description and acceptance criteria both exclude the cluster by name. Taking half would split the bead and guarantee a conflict. Those lines are untouched and still say 'five'; dispatch rf2-ruiga whole.

GATES: epoch clojure -M:test 495/6665 0F/0E rc=0 (baseline re-derived; brief said 490/6637 — main moved, this branch is docstrings only). Targeted conformance ns 22/198 0F/0E rc=0 (the load proof).
close_reason:
PR #7058 MERGED. All four sites CHANGED — none had been pre-fixed by the P1 that merged underneath it.

SITE 1 — BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE, not just the count. Measured: the cascade settles FIVE records (ensure/ensure/release-owner/invalidate-tags session/invalidate-tags global), and the last record own family row is :rf.resource/invalidated — so :owner-released WAS NEVER THE ROW THAT DOUBLES; it belongs to record 3. The bead described a count defect and the worker found a wrong SUBJECT underneath it.

AND IT APPLIED THE RULE RATHER THAN THE FIX: it did NOT swap three for five. The parenthetical now reads "spread across as many records as it dispatches", and the duplication sentence names THE DRIVER LAST DISPATCH, says which row that is today and why, and states the harmlessness argument holds WHICHEVER dispatch ends up last. That sentence cannot go stale.

SITE 2 — THE FALSE CLAIM WAS LOAD-BEARING IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM EXPECTED. Under the inherited cap of 5 THE CASCADE ELIDES NOTHING (5 records, retained [12 12 9 6 5]), so the fixture would be GREEN WITHOUT THE PIN. At keep=4 the first record rows do vanish ([:ELIDED 12 9 6 5]) — the mechanism is entirely real, the cascade just sits ON the boundary rather than past it. Rewritten WITH NO NUMBER AT ALL, naming epoch.state/elide-just-crossed-trace-events as what drops the rows and the every?-comp-seq fixture control as what catches the pin rotting. That is the model for every count-in-prose fix.

SITES 3 AND 4 — MY LEAD WAS RIGHT AND THE TRUTH WAS SHARPER. elide-whole-output-large-slots destructures only :include-large? and calls the 2-arity large-marker, which hands ->marker just {:reason :classification}; ->marker adds :digest only under include-digests?. Direct construction yields {:path :bytes :type :reason :hint :handle}. End to end THE WHOLE-OUTPUT MARKER CARRIES NO DIGEST UNDER ANY PROFILE — including :rf.egress/off-box-tool, WHERE A PATH-DECLARED MARKER DOES GET ONE. That asymmetry is now stated in both docstrings rather than the claim merely deleted, and the production docstring keeps its size-oracle argument for :bytes while replacing the digest claim with "no digest oracle at this seam by construction".

ONE ADJACENT CLAUSE HANDLED WITH CARE: "the cascade put 7 rows on the bus and 0 into the 3 records" read as present-tense. It verified the numbers were ACCURATE FOR THEIR ERA via git show 88a0aabd81 — three dispatches then — and added a TIME QUALIFIER rather than rewriting history. Correcting a historical record to match the present would have destroyed the evidence.

VERIFIED ALREADY CORRECT AND LEFT ALONE: drive-resource-family! :574-575, "five dispatches, so its family rows are spread across five records" — measured true, AND it sits AT the authority, directly above the forms it counts. A count adjacent to the thing it counts is the one place a count is safe.

AND IT DECLINED THE ADJACENT FIX I OFFERED, with better reasoning than my offer had. I said take the trace_egress.cljc sibling if cheap. It found rf2-ruiga owns that WHOLE cluster, that the cluster scope is WIDER than I described — including two lines inside the file it was rewriting — and that rf2-uozi8 excludes the cluster BY NAME TWICE, in description and acceptance criteria. Taking half would have split one bead across two PRs and left rf2-ruiga owning lines that had moved underneath it. It reported the shift (:537 -> :544) so the next worker does not chase a stale coordinate; recorded on rf2-ruiga.

Gates: epoch 495/6665 rc=0 and the targeted conformance ns 22/198 rc=0, both with rc captured immediately and cross-checked against each log verdict line. BASELINE CORRECTION FOR MY BRIEFS: epoch is 495/6665 on current main, not the 490/6637 I briefed.

title: view-bad-event: the invoked-carrier arm and its :close-over-capture-frame-dispatch recovery appear nowhere in spec/
description:
Found by the fh-tail worker (PR #7051) and deliberately not actioned — spec/009 was fenced to a live checker worker.

THE GAP, two halves: carrier-called-directly! raises :rf.error/view-bad-event with :recovery :close-over-capture-frame-dispatch, and THAT RECOVERY KEYWORD APPEARS NOWHERE IN spec/. And the :rf.error/view-bad-event catalogue row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md lists five arms (a) through (e), NONE of which is the invoked-carrier arm that PR #7034 added.

WHY THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py is green, so this is OUTSIDE that checker scope rather than reconciled by it. Note the sibling finding rf2-d89rs — that checker verifies source-to-catalogue, never catalogue-to-source. This is a third direction again: a row that EXISTS but whose ARM ROSTER is incomplete, and a recovery vocabulary term with no spec home at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of rf2-yn5nj and rf2-llxsw was that calling a descriptor directly now produces a NAMED, RECOVERABLE diagnostic instead of an opaque failure. A recovery keyword the spec never defines is a recovery a consumer cannot look up — which undoes the teaching value the diagnostic exists for.

SEQUENCING: spec/009 has had three workers in it today. Dispatch only when it is free, and check whether rf2-k91an latest arm-roster work (merged) already covers part of this — that bead did exactly this job for a different row.
close_reason:
PR #7061 MERGED. Two markdown files, 8 insertions / 8 deletions — and every edit reported as "the claim went" rather than the duplication, which is the distinction I asked for and was right each time.

rf2-l1l0p — MY VERIFIED PREMISE WAS SIX TIMES NARROWER THAN THE TRUTH. I checked ONE keyword, :close-over-capture-frame-dispatch, confirmed it appears once in events.cljc and zero times in spec/, and briefed that. The worker found FIVE MORE SIBLING DISPOSITIONS the same row emitters raise, none of them in spec/ either: :fix-the-callback-declaration, :fix-the-render-fn-parameter-vector, :drop-passive-or-prevent-default, :write-a-read-door-as-a-keyword-or-keyword-path, :read-a-shallow-scalar-or-use-v-event. AND THE ROW SAID "FOUR ARMS" AND LISTED FIVE. The count is GONE, not corrected. Arms (f) through (h) appended with (a)-(e) letters unchanged, because the recovery and ex-data cells key off them. Emitter attribution corrected to re-frame.freehand.events plus re-frame.freehand.route-link-seam.

rf2-qk8vj — RESIDUAL ESTABLISHED BEFORE EDITING, and the prior two passes hold untouched. What survived is a CLASSIFICATION ERROR: build-event dissocs and hoists :recovery on every branch but MERGES {:category operation} INTO base-tags when error?, so :category genuinely IS a :tags key on an error envelope. A NEW BLINDNESS DIRECTION FILED FROM THIS WORK: :rf.ui.compile/bad-render-fn is emitted and has no spec home at all, and the drift checker scans only :rf.error/* and :rf.warning/*, so NEITHER Check A NOR the new Check C can see the family. title: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py checks source-to-catalogue only, never catalogue-to-source — three ids exist in spec/ and nowhere else
description:
Found by the rf2-dxuzp/rf2-k91an worker while reading the 009 catalogue arm by arm. Reported, not actioned — out of that bead scope.

THE FINDING, measured at ef495cfdc7: NO .clj / .cljc / .cljs file outside spec/ names :rf.error/ui-dispatch-unwired, :rf.error/ui-test-bad-selector, or :rf.error/ui-test-frame-collision. The catalogue documents three error ids that NOTHING EMITS.

AND THE GATE IS GREEN, which is the actual defect: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py evidently checks SOURCE -> CATALOGUE only — every emitted id has a row — and never asks CATALOGUE -> SOURCE, whether every row has an emitter. So a row for an id that no longer exists is invisible to it forever.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS EVERYTHING ELSE FOUND THIS WEEK: it is gate blindness — sound machinery, one direction it cannot see. Five-plus instances have been found in this repo in the last few days, including the 009 ratchet pinning the Channel column but not Tags, a bijection gate green on all seven planted defects, and a conformance fixture whose projector had never run over a real record.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a documented error id with no emitter is a promise to consumers that the framework can produce a diagnostic it cannot. A consumer or an AI reading the catalogue to write a handler for :rf.error/ui-test-bad-selector writes dead code. That is the same class as the reg-route example that throws and the "not IFn" prose — documented claims the code does not keep.

TWO THINGS TO ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING: (1) are these three DONOR-tier ids? All three carry ui in the name, and rf2-drpa3.57 deletes implementation/ui wholesale — if they retire with the donor, the honest fix is to record that rather than to add a reverse check for rows about to vanish. (2) If a reverse arm IS built, it needs a NON-VACUITY PROOF against these three, and it must be able to distinguish a row whose emitter was deliberately retired from one whose emitter was never written. Without that distinction the arm becomes a nag.

DO NOT build this as a general catalogue-completeness framework. One arm, or a recorded decision that the three rows go.
close_reason:
ALREADY LANDED — verified, no code change needed.

CHECK C (catalogue -> source) is present in scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py today, added by commit bb93ab09df 'scripts,spec/009: ask the catalogue whether anything still emits its rows (rf2-d89rs)' and extended by 6ef99e4a17 (rf2-66czz: retired-row reintroduction + fail-closed parse). The bead was simply never closed.

BOTH of the bead's preconditions were met by that work:
(1) DONOR-TIER QUESTION — answered by retirement, not by a reverse check over doomed rows. All three ids are struck in place in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (lines 2398/2402/2407), each carrying '**RETIRED (rf2-d89rs).**' with its own rationale.
(2) NON-VACUITY + retired-vs-never-written distinction — the strikethrough IS the structural distinction (_CATALOGUE_ROW_RE group 1), so disposition is read off the row, never from a list kept beside it. The one active row the CLJS reference is contracted never to emit carries a single cited exemption (_PORT_RELATIVE_CATEGORIES), kept honest both ways by legs 3+4.

ADVERSARIAL PROOF RE-RUN THIS SESSION (the bead/brief's requirement: an id in spec/ and nowhere in source must FAIL):
  - planted an ACTIVE row ':rf.error/planted-no-emitter' INSIDE the '### Error event catalogue' section
    -> exit 1, 'CHECK C - 1 Spec 009 catalogue row(s) whose emitter state contradicts the row', 446 active rows
  - removed it -> exit 0, 445 active rows. spec/ restored byte-clean (git status empty).
  NOTE a first plant placed ABOVE the '### Error event catalogue' heading did NOT fire (445 rows unchanged) - that is CORRECT scope discipline, not a hole: the doc carries a second quick-reference table and CHECK C is deliberately scoped to the canonical section.

GATES: python scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py --verbose -> exit 0 (379 impl files; 445 active + 9 retired rows; A=0 B=0 C=0). --self-test --verbose -> exit 0, 42 PASS, 0 FAIL.

Scope was honoured: one arm, not a general catalogue-completeness framework.

title: check_thrown_error_messages accepts an existing file as --scan-dir and greens over zero files
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7033 found a narrow false green in the new fail-closed scan-root validation. scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py builds scan_roots, rejects roots only when (not r.exists()), and then hands every survivor to _iter_source_files. Path.rglob over an existing regular file yields no source files, so the CLI accepts a value that is not the directory its help and contract require.

Direct reproduction on the merged behavior (still present on current main):

  python scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py --scan-dir README.md --verbose
  scanning 0 framework source file(s) under README.md (tests excluded)...
  no bare-keyword thrown-error messages in framework source.
  rc=0

This cuts across the PR's stated fail-closed reason: a future DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS edit or manual repeatable-root invocation can point at an existing file, silently erase that declared part of the scan surface, and report success. Missing paths correctly return rc=2; existing non-directories must take the same posture. This is not a request to widen the governed source roster or convert tools throws.
acceptance_criteria:
- Validate every resolved scan root with is_dir (not exists alone) before scanning; missing paths and existing non-directories both return rc=2.
- With repeatable --scan-dir, one invalid member fails the whole invocation before any success verdict; diagnostics name every invalid path without a traceback.
- Add a CLI-level regression covering a valid directory, a missing path, an existing file such as README.md, and a mixed valid/file root list.
- The 20 fixture self-tests and the bare live implementation scan remain green.
close_reason: PR #7049 MERGED (blob 340b98708356 identical on main and branch). exists() -> is_dir(), plus FOUR CLI-LEVEL SELF-TESTS DRIVING main() END TO END — and the diagnosis of why the hole existed is the durable part: the fixture cases call scan() DIRECTLY and could never reach argument handling. A test suite that enters below the layer containing the defect cannot see it, however thorough it is at its own level. Same family as the boundary-versus-unit lesson that overturned three unit-level beliefs today.

title: minimal-counter: decide whether the scaffold wires a state-preserving reload hook
description:

title: story-mcp write relays harvest :rf.error from ex-data, but the registrar throws :rf.error/id — the structured error id slot has never been populated
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2z9u3 (PR #7042).

Both write relays do:

  (select-keys (ex-data e) [:rf.error :explain])

Nothing anywhere in the repo puts a BARE :rf.error key into ex-data. The
canonical thrown-error shape (Spec 009) uses :rf.error/id, and that is what
registrar/validate-shape! and validate-tag-membership! actually throw. So the
:rf.error arm of that select-keys has never fired: a schema-violation or
unknown-tag error result reaches the client with NO machine-readable error id
in :structuredContent at all.

Verified at the real JSON-RPC boundary (server/run-loop!), post-rf2-2z9u3:

  register-variant {:variant-id "story.button/tagfail" :body "{:tags #{:nope}}"}
  -> structuredContent {"variant-id":"story.button/tagfail"}

No :rf.error. The discriminator is not lost — rf2-jquiy put the canonical
[:rf.error/unknown-tag] token in the MESSAGE, so an agent can read it there —
but the structured slot the code plainly intends to populate is dead.

:rf.error (bare) IS story-mcp's own structuredContent convention for
tool-EMITTED errors (docs.cljc, recorder.cljc, wire_pipeline.cljc,
result.cljc all set it). So the coherent fix is to keep the one wire
vocabulary and populate it from the throw:

  {:rf.error (:rf.error/id (ex-data e))}

rather than introduce a second spelling on the wire. Two sites:
tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc (register-or-error)
and .../tools/recorder.cljc (write-back!).

Deliberately out of scope for rf2-2z9u3, which was the encodability defect
(the response never got built at all). Narrow, one-expression change plus a
boundary assertion in wire_encodability_test.clj, which already drives both
paths.

title: 130 of 494 catalogue rows list :recovery in their Tags column, which the 009 reading rule forbids
description:
Measured during rf2-qk8vj (PR #7035), not estimated. The parse: every 6-column catalogue row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md whose first cell starts a ':rf.' operation keyword, matching a backticked ':recovery' anywhere in the sixth (Tags) cell.

  catalogue rows parsed        494
  rows listing :recovery       130
  rows listing :category         1  (:rf.error/observation-on-change-failed)

WHY THESE ARE DEFECTS AND NOT EXCEPTIONS. re-frame.trace/build-event does '(dissoc tags :recovery ...)' and hoists the value to the envelope TOP LEVEL on every branch ('(or error? recovery) (assoc :recovery recovery)'). So [:tags :recovery] does not exist on the wire on any branch, and a row listing it names a key no consumer can read. :category is synthesised INTO :tags on the :error branch only, so it is runtime-supplied rather than emit-site-supplied and is likewise not a per-row key.

WHAT PR #7035 DID AND DID NOT DO. spec/009's 'Reading the two right-hand columns' asserted these slots were 'deliberately absent from EVERY row' — a factual claim with 130 counterexamples. #7035 re-anchored it as a RULE with a stated disposition ('a row that still lists one is a row defect, not a counterexample') and made Spec-Schemas cite it instead of restating it. It deliberately did NOT touch the 130 rows: that is a corpus sweep, it collides with rf2-6tags, and it was outside the bead.

CONSUMER: rf2-6tags. Its Tags-column keys-set arm diffs schema keys against row keys, so it will flag all 130 on its first run. The exclusion list it needs is now a rule it can cite rather than a judgement call. Decide before building the arm whether the sweep lands first (arm starts clean) or the arm lands first with the 130 as a declared baseline — the second option is the one this repo has warned against, where a ledger entry that is real debt looks like arm noise.

MEASUREMENT NOTE: the three counts above are the only numbers in this bead and each is a parse, not a prose count. Re-run the parse rather than trusting them if the catalogue has moved.

title: ui-tree-malformed's recovery roster omits four v/->react dispositions
description:
Third of the three adjacent findings raised-not-actioned in PR #7030 and carried into rf2-qk8vj. The other two were cheap and landed in PR #7035 (sub-exception's :where over-claim; the machine-grammar-not-in-v1 three-way). This one is NOT cheap — it needs an arm-by-arm read of the Freehand and re-frame.ui throw sites — so it is filed rather than guessed at.

THE GAP (spec/009-Instrumentation.md, the :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed row). The Trigger cell rosters SEVEN emitter groups by namespace:

  1. re-frame.freehand.tree / re-frame.freehand.react — the interpreted walk's fail-loud arms
  2. re-frame.freehand.to-react — the OUTWARD v/->react bridge's argument + props guards
  3. re-frame.freehand / .node / .events / .rules / .top-layer — the door's remaining interpreted arms
  4. re-frame.freehand.root — the v/mount / v/hydrate-root opts-key + root-id-derivation guards
  5. re-frame.freehand.test — the structural TEST surface (render / find / find-all / attrs / text)
  6. re-frame.ui.tree / .rules / .runtime / re-frame.ui / re-frame.ui.test — the S1d tree consumers
  7. re-frame.ui.semantic/normalize — the parity/fingerprint boundary, two arms

The Tags cell names branches for groups 1, 3 and 7 only: ':value / :attr / :row (per branch), :recovery; the v/defhost crossing arms add :host, the adapter reserved-key arm adds :reserved; the re-frame.ui.semantic version arm adds :got + :supported, its node-discrimination arm adds :value + :got + :path'.

So groups 2, 4, 5 and 6 are rostered as emitters with NO named tag branch. A consumer reading the row cannot tell whether a to-react ref-refusal, a v/mount bad-opts-key, a freehand.test find failure or a re-frame.ui.test malformed-node failure carries :value, :attr, :row, something else, or nothing.

ALSO ON THE SAME ROW: the Tags cell lists :recovery. Per spec/009 'Reading the two right-hand columns' (rewritten in PR #7035 to be a RULE rather than a false description), :recovery is never a :tags key — build-event strips it and hoists it to the envelope top level — so a row listing it names a key no consumer can read there. See the sibling bead on the corpus-wide sweep for that.

METHOD, NOT NEGOTIABLE: verify against the EMITTING SITES, not against the row or the schema. That discipline turned a verdict around during the rf2-zk1xu adjudication and again in PR #7035, where sub-exception's Trigger prose promised a ':where :reactive' value that subs/memo.cljc does not stamp at all.

title: check_thrown_error_messages lets an outer let binding override an inner lexical shadow
description:
Split out of rf2-jquiy. rf2-jquiy landed the COMMENT documenting this; the logic is deliberately unchanged and is what this bead is for.

Both conformance escapes in _scan_builder_bypass require the token to be
LITERAL in the source text:

  _INLINE_TOKEN_MSG_RE     needs a contiguous "... [:rf.error/x]" in the msg arg
  _ASSEMBLED_TOKEN_MSG_RE  needs (str "... [" :rf.error/x "]") — literal keyword

Two conformant shapes are therefore reported as builder-bypass-message:

(a) LET-BOUND message. re-frame.story/configure! (tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:877
    and :914) builds a full human sentence + trailing token, under a comment
    citing Spec 009, then binds it to 'msg'. The scan sees the symbol.
    Confirmed conformant at runtime — story_authoring_validation_test.clj:749
    and sensitive_trace_cljs_test.cljc:177 both assert the rendered message
    matches #"\[:rf.error/<id>\]".

(b) COMPUTED discriminator. (ex-info (str reason " [" error-kw "]") ...) where
    error-kw is derived — e.g. registrar's
    (keyword "rf.error" (str (name kind) "-shape")) — or is a parameter of a
    shared throw helper (plan/fail!, diff_encode/validate-against!). The
    runtime message carries the token; the source cannot.
    rf2-jquiy converted four such sites; all four still report.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND tools/. The trees where this currently bites are outside
DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS, so CI is not red today. But the rule is identical inside
implementation/: the first conformant let-bound message written there fails the
gate, and the tempting 'fix' is to DE-conformise working code to satisfy a
blind scan. rf2-jquiy hit exactly that pressure.

OPTIONS (not ruled):
  1. Leave as-is. The comment now warns readers; rf2:builder-bypass-ok is the
     opt-out. Cheapest, and arguably correct — the gate is a ratchet, not a
     prover.
  2. Resolve a single-assignment local binding in the enclosing let and test
     the bound form. Covers (a). Does not cover (b).
  3. Treat (str ... " [" <symbol> "]") — a str concat whose bracket pair
     encloses a lone symbol — as conformant. Covers (b) but weakens the rule:
     any symbol would pass.

Suggest 1 unless a conformant let-bound site actually lands under

title: G-8 perf gate dies when the baseline is TOO FAST: p95Ratio refuses a zero denominator
description:
Diagnosed by the rf2-1kiuj worker while clearing a red that was NOT its diff — recording it because the failure is indistinguishable from a real regression at a glance, and it cost a round trip.

THE DEFECT. The G-8 controlled-input gate failed with no deftest named, no assertion, no pageerror — the build completed with 0 warnings and BOTH engines drove. It died in the MEASUREMENT GUARD: "baseline p95 must be a positive finite number: 0". The hand-written React baseline rounded to 0 ms and p95Ratio refuses a zero denominator.

SO THE GATE FAILS WHEN THE THING IT MEASURES IS TOO FAST. That is the opposite of what a perf gate should do, and it produces a red that looks exactly like a real browser failure in the PR checks list.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE RED: this is the eleventh distinct way a signal lies in this repo, and the first on the FALSE-RED side rather than the false-green side. Every other entry in that list is a green that should have been red. A false red is cheaper but not free — it consumed a mayor round trip and a worker investigation, and the standing rule is that a failing test on a touched surface is never a flake, which is exactly the rule that makes this expensive to dismiss.

THE FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: either floor the baseline measurement at the timer resolution, or treat a zero baseline as "too fast to compare" and skip the ratio with a stated reason rather than failing. Do NOT make the gate silently pass — that converts a false red into a false green, which this repo has ten of already.

EVIDENCE IT WAS NOT THE DIFF: :ui-g8 has ONE entry, re-frame.ui.g8.dev, and nothing under implementation/ui/g8/ requires epoch or resources. The gate only ran because core maps onto the ui_gates surface. The two sibling real-browser gates G-13 and G-18 PASSED on that same run, and G-8 passed on the re-run after rebase.

NOTE THE DONOR ANGLE BEFORE SPENDING EFFORT: re-frame.ui.g8.dev is donor-tier, and rf2-drpa3.57 (F6e) deletes implementation/ui wholesale. If this gate retires with the donor, the honest fix may be to record the hazard and let it go. Check that first.

title: spec/009 and Spec-Schemas contradict each other on which tag slots are envelope-level
description:
Found during the rf2-zk1xu adjudication of the 23 Tags-column rows, and deliberately not resolved there — the 23 were settled without picking a winner, but this contradiction outlives them.

THE CONTRADICTION: spec/009 reading rule names :recovery and :category as the envelope-level slots. Spec-Schemas section Per-category :tags schemas names those PLUS :failing-id, :reason and :frame, states that per-category schemas carry only the ADDITIONAL keys — and then re-declares all four anyway.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the rf2-6tags Tags-column arm diffs schema keys against row keys, so "which slots are envelope-level and therefore excluded" is load-bearing for every future adjudication. While the two documents disagree, the exclusion list is a judgement call rather than a rule, and the next person adjudicating a row will reach a different answer from the last.

DO NOT resolve this by adding a third statement somewhere. Pick the authoritative one, make the other cite it, and delete the duplicate declaration. This artefact has converged six times on "put the shared fact in the one place all readers already require, and delete the second path rather than leaving it".

VERIFY AGAINST THE EMIT SITES, not against either document — that discipline is what turned the alias-divergence verdict around during rf2-zk1xu: the divergences proved to be the ROW being wrong, the opposite of what the arm author suspected. A measured note from that work: :frame is producer-supplied by build-event stamp-frame for every in-run emit, so it is not category-specific.

RELATED, raised-not-actioned in PR #7030 and worth folding in if cheap: sub-exception trigger prose over-claims :where on the reactive arm; machine-grammar-not-in-v1 is a THREE-WAY disagreement on :failing-id versus :machine-id between Spec 005, the schema and the row; and ui-tree-malformed Tags column is narrower than its own Trigger cell arm roster.

WHICH CONVERGENCE: the CLAIM went, not the duplication — the per-category schemas are standalone and must re-declare the envelope's :tags keys to validate a real tags map alone, so 'describes only the ADDITIONAL keys' was the false part. Verified at build-event: :recovery is dissoc'd from :tags and hoisted on every branch; :category is merged INTO :tags on the :error branch only; :frame is supplied UNDER :tags by stamp-frame; :failing-id / :reason are untouched emit-site tags. title: Interpreter headroom the lnecd bounded change did not capture: memo caches are persistent maps in atoms
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-lnecd (PR #7032), which was capped at ONE bounded optimisation and took the one caller attribution named (memoising rules/caller-key-slot). This bead is the headroom that change deliberately did NOT capture, quantified in the report's 'Headroom the one change did NOT capture' section.

After the lnecd change, substrate is still 36.7% of the W1 interpreted mount in a production browser. Named remainders, from CDP caller attribution on the post-change profile:

1. THE MEMO CACHES THEMSELVES — 1.71%, the largest single remaining caller of cljs.core/array-index-of is re-frame.freehand.conversion/remembered. The caches are persistent Clojure maps held in atoms, so every HIT is a PersistentArrayMap linear scan plus a deref. A mutable js/Map on the CLJS side would remove most of it. NOTE: the cache lnecd added (rules/caller-key-slot-by-name) has the same shape and the same cost, so this applies to it too. The namespaces are .cljc and the JVM structural walk shares them, so a change here needs a reader-conditional or a shared abstraction — that is the actual work.

2. top-layer/present? via contains? — 0.42%, paid on every element.

3. react-style-name is STILL UNCACHED — it is the only one of conversion.cljc's four projections without a remembered cache, while the namespace's own §Remembered projections comment argues at length for the other three. lnecd memoised it speculatively FIRST, measured no effect (clojure.string/replace stayed at 5.89%), and REVERTED it, because self time had named the function but caller attribution named a different caller. Its real contribution is under 1%. Worth doing for consistency, not for speed.

Together these name 3-4 points of the remaining 36.7. The bulk is the walk itself — a props object per element, child classification, class composition, a persistent structure per node — and is not cacheable.

ESTIMATED CEILING: a determined campaign might take the interpreted arm from 2.75x the React floor to ~2.2-2.4x on the large-template witness. It would NOT close the gap to compiled (1.13x), because on that witness the remaining gap is substantially ViewCell elision rather than interpretation — see the W2 (3.35x, elidable) versus W2r (1.22x, not elidable) contrast in the report.

Method for anyone picking this up: the scaffolding is recoverable from git on branch worker/compiled-worth-it (deleted before the PR merged). Read the report's Method section first — wall clock on this box drifts 37% on an arm that cannot change, so everything must be normalised to an in-run no-substrate React floor.
notes:
QUALIFICATION from rf2-lnecd's elision ablation (PR #7112) — this bead's ESTIMATED CEILING paragraph cites the W2 (3.35x, elidable) versus W2r (1.22x, not elidable) contrast as showing 'the remaining gap is substantially ViewCell elision rather than interpretation'. Those two arms differed in three ways at once (300 vs 100 boundaries, a literal leaf vs one running (str (v/sub [:studio/tick])), and no floor arm on W2r), so the contrast was evidence CONSISTENT WITH elision, not a measurement of it.

The isolated ablation has now been run, on a base that INCLUDES this bead's own PR #7077. Same 300 boundaries both witnesses, same leaf, a floor arm each, and the compiled body object asserted identical? between the kept and elided arms:

  free-ik / free-ic  the ViewCell alone      1.712 [1.583-1.879] clock   6.256 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ik  interpretation alone    1.216 [1.092-1.425] clock   1.011 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ic  the two together        2.079 [1.896-2.419] clock   6.327 retained heap

The bead's directional conclusion SURVIVES and is now measured rather than inferred: elision is the dominant term, 73% of the log-effect on the clock and effectively 100% on retained heap, and interpreter tuning cannot reach it. What changes is the magnitude — the gap this bead was estimating against is 2.079x, not 3.35x, partly because the confounds are gone and partly because #7077 itself moved the interpreted arm.

TWO METHOD NOTES for anyone picking up the remaining headroom.

1. The ablation's WALL CLOCK shows a real 1.216 interpretation term (range excludes 1.0) that the RETAINED-HEAP instrument does not see at all (1.011). The likely explanation is that the interpreted walk's cost here is largely TRANSIENT garbage — which retention cannot see and which is exactly the class of cost this bead's remaining items (the walk itself: a props object per element, child classification, class composition, a persistent structure per node) would attack. That makes it a HYPOTHESIS about where the remaining headroom lives, untested, and the natural first question for any further work here.

2. DO NOT reuse the recovered scaffolding's --alloc mode. Its documented premise ('allocation is a counter, not an occupancy sample: a collection inside the window cannot make it smaller') is FALSE: V8's sampling heap profiler drops the samples of collected objects, so the same 80,000 objects report 4.77 MB when a global holds them and 0.00 MB when nothing does. Pointed at a mount/unmount loop it reports the residue of a discarded page. Any browser heap reading needs a positive control of known size, in situ, in the same window.

title: Pin both readiness projectors against one shared conformance assertion (rf2-wzqtu part 3)
description:

title: RULING NEEDED: should the open-drain guard sit on the public core flush-render! entry, making it universal across Reagent and UIx too?
description:
Surfaced while resolving rf2-87ouj (PR #6994) and deliberately NOT actioned there.

rf2-87ouj moved :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch's guard into core (re-frame.frame/guard-open-drain!) and gave Freehand's flush-render! the call it was missing, so the law is now enforced by both ViewCell substrates. The guard reads only the router-bound frame/*run-frame-state-before* and the frame accessors; it closes over no cell registry.

THE QUESTION: because it is registry-agnostic, the guard could just as easily sit ONE level up, at the public core entry re-frame.substrate.adapter/flush-render! (rf/flush-render!), which dispatches to whatever adapter is installed. That would be a single call site covering EVERY adapter and would make the law unconditionally universal rather than per-substrate.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE: it would silently impose the law on Reagent and UIx, which are first-class and have never carried it. Their flush-render! flushes a different queue (reagent.core/flush / react-dom flushSync over the spine), so whether an in-drain flush is a torn read there is a genuinely separate question, not a corollary of the ViewCell analysis. Extending it is a behaviour change on two supported adapters and could redden existing adapter tests. rf2-87ouj's scope was the catalogue row's false universality claim, and that is now honest either way.

IF EXTENDED: the guard's :where vocabulary gains a fourth value ('rf/flush-render!), spec/009's row and its :where enumeration need updating, and the two substrate-level calls become redundant (the entry would already have thrown) — so it is a simplification as well as a widening, which is part of why it is worth a decision rather than a shrug.

Deliberately filed rather than implemented: Mike has not ruled on whether the law is a ViewCell law or an adapter-contract law.
notes: OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
close_reason:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26): "No". The open-drain guard STAYS SUBSTRATE-LOCAL. Do not hoist it to the public core flush-render! entry.

WHAT WAS DECIDED: rf2-87ouj moved :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch guard into core as re-frame.frame/guard-open-drain!. Because it is registry-agnostic it COULD sit one level up, at the public core entry, where it would apply to every substrate. The ruling is that it does not.

THE REASONING I PUT TO THE OPERATOR, recorded so this is not relitigated:
  1. FLUSH DRAINS A DIFFERENT QUEUE IN EACH ADAPTER. A law proven correct against Freehand drain is not automatically correct against Reagent or UIx, and hoisting ASSERTS that it is, without evidence.
  2. It would SILENTLY IMPOSE A NEW REFUSAL on Reagent and UIx, which are FIRST-CLASS AND ACTIVELY SUPPORTED and have never carried it. An existing consumer working code would start throwing on a path they never opted into. That is the opposite of "trust the programmer".
  3. THE EVIDENCE BASE IS ONE-SIDED. The guard exists because Freehand ViewCell made the failure observable. Nobody has demonstrated the same hazard on Reagent or UIx, so extending it would be reasoning from a MECHANISM to a CONTRACT without a witness.

SO IT IS A VIEWCELL LAW, NOT AN ADAPTER-CONTRACT LAW. Freehand compiled cells have the drain semantics that make an open epoch meaningful; the adapters do not reason in those terms.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS, and it is concrete: a REPRODUCTION showing an open-epoch flush corrupting state under Reagent or UIx. That makes it an adapter-contract law and the hoist becomes correct. Absent that, the honest position is that it is a ViewCell law with a clear home.

COST AVOIDED: the hoist would have added a fourth value to the guard :where vocabulary (rf/flush-render!) and moved spec/009 row plus its :where enumeration — a real contract change, not a refactor.

THIS ALSO FITS THE GUARD-WARRANTED PRINCIPLE recorded today: a guard is warranted when the failure is SILENT AND HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. Here the failure has not been shown to occur at all on the adapters, so the guard would be protecting against nothing while breaking working code.

title: Spec 012 contradicts itself on whether route :sensitive covers the trace bus, and the plan trace's stated reason over-claims
description:
EP-0037 review gate 1 (rf2-kqxe6.14) finding. Spec 012 says two contradictory things about whether a route's `:sensitive` classification covers the trace bus, and EP-0037's own new text justifies the plan trace's lossiness by a closure that execution disproves. DOC/SPEC-ONLY — no code change is being asked for, and no extension of the classification to trace tags (that was ruled out, correctly).

## The contradiction

`spec/012-Routing.md` §Route data classification → Lowering and re-rooting:

> Classification is value-independent and read **only at egress** — the handler, subs, and views always see the real values while the route is active; **only the trace bus / Xray / MCP / off-box / SSR egress copies are redacted**.

`spec/012-Routing.md` §Resolved target and the plan diagnostic projection (added by EP-0037 R0b):

> A trace tag is an **egress** surface, and the route's `:sensitive` classification **cannot reach it** … says nothing about a tag map on the trace bus.

A reader takes the first as "declare `:sensitive` and the value stops appearing on the trace bus". The code implements the second.

## What actually happens (reproduced, JVM, one navigation)

Route `:probe/join` at `/join`, `:query [:map [:invite :string]]`, `:sensitive [[:query :invite]]`, one blocking resource whose identity is `{:invite <the query value>}`. One `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :probe/join :query {:invite "SECRET100"}}]` with a trace listener attached. `:rf.route/planned` behaves exactly as ruled:

    :rf.route/planned -> {:cause :navigate :route-id :probe/join
                          :url "/join?invite=rf/redacted"
                          :param-keys [] :query-keys [:invite] …}

And in the SAME drain, thirteen other trace rows carry `SECRET100` verbatim, among them:

    :rf.fx/handled           {:rf.fx/id :rf.nav/push-url :rf.fx/args "/join?invite=SECRET100" …}
    :rf.fx/handled           {:rf.fx/id :rf.nav/scroll   :rf.fx/args {:strategy :top :to {:id :probe/join :query {:invite "SECRET100"}}} …}
    :rf.event/dispatched     {:rf.event/v [:rf.route/navigate {:to :probe/join :query {:invite "SECRET100"}}] …}
    :rf.resource/route-plan  {:identities [[:rf.scope/global :probe/invitee {:invite "SECRET100"}]]
                              :blocking   [[:rf.scope/global :probe/invitee {:invite "SECRET100"}]] …}
    :rf.resource/work-started / fetch-started / owner-attached  (`:resource/key`, `:work/id`)

So the URL-carrier egress class is wide open on the trace bus, by design, everywhere except the one tag map EP-0037 chose to redact. The plan trace's lossiness is a LOCAL hygiene measure — a defensible one, and it is ruled — but §Resolved target's stated reason for it is not true:

> Emitting them raw would reopen, by a route the classification cannot see, exactly the URL-carrier egress class the routing sweeps closed.

Nothing was closed on the trace bus for it to reopen. `:rf.nav/push-url`'s fx args carry the identical string one row later.

## Why this matters enough to fix

It is a security-posture claim, and the document already knows the right register for these: "A **forgotten** classification is fail-open (the value ships raw — the hygiene bargain, not a security boundary)" and the query-key-promotion advisory's "silently fails open … the hygiene bargain, not a security boundary". §Route data classification's "only the trace bus … are redacted" sentence reads as the stronger claim and is the one an operator will act on.

## Bounded repair (spec/docs text only)

1. §Route data classification → Lowering and re-rooting: scope the sentence to what the registry actually governs — copies of the CLASSIFIED runtime-db PATHS (the `:rf/route` / `:rf.route/query` / `:rf.route/params` read surfaces per the seed table below it, Xray/MCP slice reads, SSR hydration) — and state plainly that arbitrary trace TAGS are not covered, cross-referencing §Resolved target. Name the ambient counter-examples (an event vector on `:rf.event/dispatched`, fx args on `:rf.fx/handled`) so the fail-open direction is explicit rather than inferred.

title: R1 and R2 slice acceptance criteria were destructively overwritten by their audit follow-throughs
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness). Bead-record repair only -- no code, no reopening.

THE FACT. Epic rf2-kqxe6 promised "Graduation slices R0-R6 per the EP Graduation slices table". Its 21 children include R0a (.2), R0b (.3), R0c (.4), R3 (.7), R4 (.8), R5 (.9), R6 (.10) -- and for R1 and R2, only:
  - rf2-kqxe6.5 -- titled "EP-0037 R1 FOLLOW-THROUGH: purge retired registrations on reload and stale contract references"
  - rf2-kqxe6.6 -- titled "EP-0037 R2 FOLLOW-THROUGH: recover retained-entry loss and preserve contributor attribution"

Both ARE the original slice beads. PR #6875 is titled "feat(routing): EP-0037 R1 -- honest fire-and-forget :on-match + resource-derived readiness, retire on-match error machinery (rf2-kqxe6.5)" and PR #6877 "feat(routing): EP-0037 R2 -- parent-chain resource plan composition, plan diff + attach-before-release handoff, partial revalidation (rf2-kqxe6.6)". Each merged-PR audit then rewrote its bead's TITLE AND DESCRIPTION into the follow-through defect instead of appending a note. `bd search "EP-0037 R2"` returns nothing; R1's and R2's slice acceptance criteria exist nowhere in the tracker.

THE CORRECT PATTERN, on the same programme, twice. rf2-kqxe6.3 (R0b) and rf2-kqxe6.7 (R3) each KEPT their original slice description and APPENDED their audit findings as notes -- which is precisely why review gate 2 could check those two slices against the tree at all, and could not check R1 and R2.

WHY THIS IS NOT HYGIENE PEDANTRY -- it has a named casualty. The EP assigns to R2: "R2 adds occurrence/dependency groups, contributor dedupe advisories, the grouped order, and the identity diff" (§Tooling and observability). The surviving rf2-kqxe6.6 acceptance criteria are four bullets about retained-entry liveness and contributor attribution and mention none of it. Nothing in bd would ever have flagged that clause as unowned; gate 2 found it only by reading the EP against the tree (filed separately as the Tooling-projection ruling request). R1 and R2 are the only two slices whose "done" mark attests to a NARROWER task than the slice it was cut for.

REPAIR -- non-destructive, append only:

Append a note to rf2-kqxe6.5 recording R1's ORIGINAL slice scope and where it landed: EP slice R1 "honest activation" -- :on-match fire-and-forget only after a valid plan; resource-derived transition/error via one pure projector; removal of global on-match correlation and route :on-error; SSR wait semantics; the post-v1 :load seam note corrected. 2. Append the same to rf2-kqxe6.6 for R2: parent-to-leaf resource composition, constraint-preserving grouped identity dedupe + redundant-child advisory, plan diff, attach-before-release, partial revalidation, SSR/hydration parity. Delivered in PR #6877 (7d824442c4 contract, 39142d0d6a impl, 4bdeff9dac fixtures + plan-diff trace + RealWorld receipt).
3. Record the convention for future merged-PR audits, wherever such conventions live for this repo (bd prime guidance / the audit skill / the mayor method doc -- author's judgement, ONE place, not three): a merged-PR audit that reopens the exact source owner APPENDS its findings as a note and leaves the title and description intact. Rewriting them erases the acceptance criteria a later review gate needs, and makes the epic read as if the slice were only its own follow-up.

DO NOT reopen .5 or .6 -- both slices shipped and both follow-throughs shipped. This is about the record being reconstructable, not about work.
notes:

BOTH SLICE RECORDS RECOVERED AND RE-RECORDED, verbatim, with the commit each came from. Full text is now appended as a note on each bead; this is the actionable summary.

WHERE THEY WERE RECOVERED FROM. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a full-database export committed on every checkpoint, so each bead is readable at any commit. The rewrite is pinned to a commit pair in both cases:
  - rf2-kqxe6.5 (R1): original last present at 3e7e880c6b (2026-07-25 00:40 +1000, "merge #6875 ...; dispatch+claim R2"); rewritten at 1e2627315c (00:59, "audit: advance merged PR cursor through #6875"). Bead updated_at 2026-07-24T14:22:32Z -> T14:58:49Z.

Both originals were also confirmed unchanged at their creation-adjacent checkpoints (e8ee42a74a for .5). NO EMPTY-EXPORT ARTEFACT was encountered in the window read.

FIVE RECORD-LEVEL FINDINGS, none blocking, all now written down so they are not re-derived:

1. R1's readiness criterion was finished by a LATER bead, not by #6875. #6875 shipped only the commit-time half (routing/readiness.cljc, `project-at-commit`). The reply-driven half, the Spec 012 table conformance and the restore/hydration reconciliation all landed at rf2-kqxe6.17 / commit b8872054cd / PR #6895 — seven named tests, each confirmed introduced by that commit via `git log -S`. Already correctly titled "R1 completion", so the tree tells this story; the bead did not.

2. R1's deletion roster completed across FOUR cuts: #6875 (source deletion), #6885 (this bead's own reload purge), #6895 (the two residuals its close reason listed as out of scope, core.cljc:2390 + Spec-Schemas.md:1751 — both now retirement notes), and rf2-kqxe6.19 / 973f68102b / #6928 (spec/API.md's reserved route-metadata line). Review gate 2 independently re-swept and found zero residue.

THE ONE CRITERION NOT SATISFIED AS WRITTEN: R1's blast radius promised "EP row 6 R1 fixtures added". #6875 added exactly ONE conformance fixture (routing-on-match-fire-and-forget.edn), which discharges only row 6's final clause. spec/conformance/fixtures/ contains NO readiness fixture at all; the twelve readiness states are proven by CLJS unit tests from #6895 instead. 4. TWO EVIDENCE GAPS ON R2, both small:
   (a) Row 5's parenthetical "including a requirement whose resolved identity changed" has no fixture and no test. ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn's added/removed identities are DIFFERENT resources (:acct/a -> :acct/b), not one declaration whose resolved identity moved. Structurally the diff keys on resolved [scope resource-id canonical-params], so a changed identity IS an add plus a remove — but nothing pins it.
   (b) R2 item (5), "`:on-match`/`:scroll`/`:head`/`:tags`/guards NOT inherited", is stated normatively twice (012:1567, 016:1272) and has no negative test anywhere. CANNOT VERIFY executable proof. title: RULING NEEDED: EP-0037's Tooling projection has no conformance row -- was the R2 plan-graph projection descoped or dropped?
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness). This is a RULING REQUEST, not an implementation bead. Per the gate brief: where a reviewer cannot tell whether something was descoped by decision or simply dropped, the ambiguity is itself the finding.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT. EP-0037 devotes a whole section (§Tooling and observability) to the plan projection -- nine bullets of what "Xray/trace projection shows" -- plus a staging clause:

  "This projection graduates with the planner. R0 exposes only the source, resolved target,
   cause, branch, and behavior-preserving leaf plan needed to prove the shared spine.
   R2 adds occurrence/dependency groups, contributor dedupe advisories, the grouped order,
   and the identity diff. R6 proves the integrated view."

But the EP's own §Conformance obligations rows 1-10 contain NO tooling/projection row. R6's per-row verdict table is therefore rows 1-10 and nothing else, so the R2 staging clause was never in an executable-proof matrix and nobody ever checked it. Compounding: rf2-kqxe6.6 is the only R2 bead in the epic and its title/description were overwritten by its audit follow-through (see the sibling bead filed by this gate), so the R2 tooling clause had no bead carrying it either.

WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED, checked against the tree. Mostly there:
  - source address and cause -- :rf.route/planned carries :cause; the source address is deliberately NOT carried, RULED on rf2-kqxe6.3 with rationale and both rejected alternatives recorded in spec/012 §Resolved target. CLEAN.
  - resolved target + parent-to-leaf branch -- :route-id, :branch, redacted :url, :param-keys/:query-keys. CLEAN.
  - blocking/readiness state -- :blocking (vec). CLEAN.
  - resource owners and activation/prefetch causes -- ensure :cause [:route-prefetch <id>]. CLEAN.
  - leave block / entry denial / planning failure -- :rf.route/navigation-blocked, :rf.route/entry-denied, :plan-error. CLEAN.
  - contributor dedupe advisories -- :redundant-children names ancestor + child + scoped-key. CLEAN (pinned by spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r2-identity-dedupe.edn).

NOT SHIPPED, and no ruling found:
  - "old/new kept/added/removed IDENTITIES" -- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1082-1092 projects :ensured / :kept / :removed as COUNTS; :identities is the whole next set. The diff IS derivable by diffing consecutive route-plan traces, and the fixtures pin the counts (ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn asserts :ensured 1 :kept 1 :removed 1) -- so this may well be the right shape. But the EP says identities.
  - "each route's contributed resource requirements" -- the contributor->requirement mapping is not projected; only :branch (route ids) plus :identities.
  - "local :after edges and plan order" -- plan order rides :identities order; :after edges are not projected at all.
  - "occurrence/dependency groups" (the R2 clause) -- not projected.

Also: tools/xray was touched exactly ONCE in the whole programme (5482fa18a3, R1, removing the retired on-match error display). tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:458 lists :rf.resource/route-plan as one lifecycle row with no tag detail, and there is no routing-plan panel.

WHY THIS IS PLAUSIBLY CORRECT AS SHIPPED, i.e. why I am asking rather than filing work. The same EP section fences hard: "No slice is permission to build a second Xray graph or a general-purpose public plan debugger", and the §Deliberate non-goals list rejects "a public general-purpose route-plan executor". The occurrence graph and identity collapse are explicitly called "internal planning mechanics" that do "not introduce a public graph API, a public graph value, or a new router abstraction" (EP:505-507). Under the pre-alpha posture -- trust the programmer, minimal ergonomic API, reject machinery for no consumer -- "ratified as a superset, shipped as the useful subset" is a defensible and probably correct outcome. Projecting :after edges and occurrence groups on every navigation trace, for no named consumer, is exactly the over-engineering triage rejects.

THE ASK, one of three:
  (A) RULE IT DESCOPED. Record that the shipped projection (counts + next identity set + redundant-child advisory) is the ratified subset, and that :after edges, occurrence/dependency groups, and per-contributor requirement mapping are deliberately not projected because the internal mechanics are not a public graph. Then this closes with the ruling as its artefact and a one-line erratum in the EP (see the errata bead filed by this gate).
  (B) RULE THE IDENTITY DIFF IN, only. The narrowest useful upgrade: carry :added / :removed as identity VECTORS beside the existing counts, so a reader of one trace can see WHICH identity moved without diffing two traces. One cond-> in route.cljc:1084, two fixture updates. Leave :after edges and occurrence groups out.
  (C) RULE THE WHOLE BULLET LIST IN. I do not recommend this -- it is the second-graph the EP forbids.

WHATEVER THE RULING: EP-0037's conformance matrix should not gain an eleventh row retroactively. If a future EP graduates a plan projection, that EP owns its own conformance row. Record the disposition here so gate 2's successor does not re-derive it.
notes:
OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): Option (B) — the identity diff is ruled IN, in the operationally-named form; every other unshipped item in EP-0037 §Tooling is DESCOPED by decision. Recorded from the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-9sluz.ep0037-tooling-projection.md (primary recommendation (B) + the appended Codex second opinion, which this ruling adopts in its corrected form; dossier deleted after recording per protocol — this note is the surviving artefact).

DECISION. The existing activation :rf.resource/route-plan trace row gains the exact identity partition beside the existing counts: :ensured-identities (requirements actually taking the ensure path), :kept-identities (requirements genuinely adopted without a fetch), :removed-identities (prior-plan identities absent from the next plan). Counts stay as the compact headline. :identities is corrected to carry the planner's grouped plan order (today it is (vec next-ids) from a SET — route.cljc:1060/:1110 — so the current vector does not in fact carry the order the EP names). Nothing else from the Tooling bullet list ships: no route-plan panel, no public plan value, no second graph, no new conformance row.

REASONING. (A) — descope everything — was defensible on the EP's own fences and pure no-gold-plating. But the descope pinches a real debugging workflow at exactly one spot: "which identity moved on this navigation?" today requires diffing two consecutive route-plan traces. Ruling it in costs ~one cond-> at the existing emit site, has an immediate consumer with zero new UI (Xray's Trace panel expands the raw trace event through the EDN inspector), and off-box safety already closes by shape, not tag-name roster (re-frame.resources.trace-egress/project-unknown-slot-value applies the owner's egress policy to scoped keys inside any collection — proven by existing epoch tests for the route-plan :blocking/:identities vectors). That is the "excellent tools" half of the posture: not machinery, legibility of the existing trace. (C) — the whole bullet list — is the second Xray graph the EP itself forbids; rejected by the bead author, the dossier, and this ruling. History note: this was compression, not silent dropping — commit 4bdeff9dac explicitly landed the "plan-diff trace" describing the counts as satisfying the EP's kept/added/removed-identity requirement; the gap is that identities were compressed into counts.

NAMING (load-bearing, from the Codex opinion, verified against the tree): since the retained-entry liveness repair (commit e95f46e6b6), a retained-but-unusable prior identity takes the ordinary ensure path (route.cljc:1044-1075) — so a vector named :added would disagree with the :ensured count. The operational names (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities) tell the truth about what the runtime did.

DESCOPE ENUMERATION — each unshipped §Tooling item, with its deliberate disposition, so gate 2's successor never re-derives this:
1. Identity diff as identities — IN (this ruling). Ships per the brief on rf2-dlkou.
2. Per-contributor requirement mapping — DESCOPED, deliberate. Xray already derives the static route/resource graph from route registrations (declared requirements incl. local :after data); planning failures carry contributor/cycle evidence; the successful dedupe case carries :redundant-children (ancestor + child + scoped-key, pinned by ep-0037-r2-identity-dedupe.edn). Re-projecting the mapping on every navigation would duplicate those authorities for no named consumer.
3. Local :after edges and "plan order" as a projected structure — DESCOPED, deliberate. The edges are internal planning mechanics (EP:505-507; Spec 016) introducing no public graph API; plan ORDER rides the corrected :identities vector, which is all a trace reader needs.
4. Occurrence/dependency groups (the R2 staging clause's groups) — DESCOPED, deliberate. Explicitly internal; projecting them on every navigation trace is the second-graph the EP forbids, would enlarge a privacy-sensitive trace, and has no consumer.
5. Route-plan panel / general-purpose plan debugger / public plan value — DESCOPED, deliberate (the EP's own §Deliberate non-goals). A dedicated Xray plan view waits for a concrete workflow the raw trace + existing static route/resource graph cannot serve, under a future EP that owns its own conformance row.

BOUNDARY CONDITION (ruled): EP-0037's conformance matrix does NOT gain an eleventh row retroactively. Conformance for this correction is the enriched shape pinned in the existing R2 partial-activation fixture plus the shape-driven egress test. If a future EP graduates a plan projection, THAT EP owns its own conformance row.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF — carried in full on rf2-dlkou (filed by this ruling, discovered-from this bead). Summary: route.cljc trace/emit! at ~:1102-1112 — cond-> the three identity vectors beside the counts (:ensured-identities via (remove adopted? ordered), :kept-identities via (filter adopted? ordered), :removed-identities via (filterv (complement next-ids) prev-identities) for deterministic prior-plan order); emit :identities as (mapv :scoped-key ordered) instead of (vec next-ids) (verify ordered is post-dedupe); do NOT touch the return map's :identities set (commit-navigation consumes it). Fixtures: extend spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn (which today asserts :ensured 1 :kept 1 :removed 1) to pin the vectors + ordered :identities, and extend the shape-driven egress test (implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj). EP erratum: one line in docs/EP/EP-0037-route-planning-and-activation-ownership.md §Tooling staging clause recording this disposition — the gate-filed errata sibling bead named in the dossier does not exist in the tracker (open+closed searched 2026-07-27), so rf2-dlkou carries the erratum.

DISPOSITION: this bead CLOSES with the ruling as its artefact; the implementation splits to rf2-dlkou (ordinary dispatchable bead, NOT operator-owned — the decision hold applied to the ruling, which is now made).
close_reason: RULED (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27): Option (B) — identity diff IN as the operationally-named partition (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities beside counts, :identities corrected to plan order); all other §Tooling items DESCOPED by decision (full enumeration + boundary condition in notes). No eleventh conformance row. Implementation split to rf2-dlkou; this bead's artefact is the ruling.

title: docs/routing/examples.md was never touched by EP-0037, though the EP names it among the four routing pages to rewrite
description:

It is a 13-line page and every defect is in the two-column "What it shows" table:

title: readiness.cljc claims to be the ONE readiness projector; resources re-derives the same table in a different vocabulary
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F6 (rf2-kqxe6.16).

readiness.cljc:12-22 presents a five-row table and states it is "the ONE pure implementation the navigation-commit assembler uses to seed the stored slice; the Resources artefact reply-driven reconciliation (Spec 016 §Route integration) and any hydration / epoch-restore reconciliation PROJECT THROUGH THE SAME TABLE".

They do not project through it. resources/route.cljc:329-413 (reconcile-readiness) re-derives the same precedence in its OWN three-row table with a DIFFERENT vocabulary - (:failed / :pending / empty outstanding set) vs (plan-error / blocking / usable-data) - and its own cond at line 393. Nothing links the two beyond prose. routing/readiness/project-at-commit has exactly ONE caller (commit-navigation, events.cljc:304).

ONE FUNCTION IS NOT THE REMEDY - and this is the point of the finding. implementation/resources/deps.edn makes routing a TEST-ONLY dep and the routing integration late-bound, so resources cannot require routing. Adding a :routing/project-readiness late-bind hook for a three-line cond would be exactly the over-engineering the house posture rejects. So the two implementations are STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED - which means the claim of unity is the thing that has to go, not the second implementation.

REMEDY (honesty plus one gate).
1. Correct readiness.cljc claim: say that resources holds the reply-driven sibling projection, NAME it (re-frame.resources.route/reconcile-readiness), and state that packaging requires two sites - so a maintainer editing the table knows to edit both.
2. Add the reciprocal cross-reference on reconcile-readiness (it currently mentions re-frame.routing.readiness only in passing, route.cljc:195).
3. Pin both against the same table in ONE place - one shared conformance assertion driving both projectors over the same input classes - so a divergence fails a test rather than being discovered in a later slice.

The two projectors ARE consistent today (error beats loading beats idle in both). This is about keeping them that way, and about not leaving a docstring that tells a maintainer one edit suffices.

title: rf/route-link inlines the click law and dispatch payload that activate-link! / link-model already own
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F5 (rf2-kqxe6.16).

link.cljc holds TWO copies of one decision. activate-link! (412-438) documents itself as "THE router-attributed click decision ... the SAME click law route-link-render applies to rf/route-link, kept inside routing so the ui artefact reimplements none of it" - but route-link-render (288-321) does NOT call it. It inlines the identical body: run caller handler, then (and (not native?) (not defaultPrevented) (plain-left-click? e)) -> preventDefault -> dispatch! with {:source :router :frame render-frame}. Likewise the [:rf.route/url-requested {...}] payload cond-> appears TWICE, byte-identical, in route-link-render (312-316) and link-model (404-408).

TWO FURTHER DETAILS THAT MAKE IT WORTH REPAIRING RATHER THAN TOLERATING.
1. route-link-render is the only link surface whose payload address comes from RAW ARGLIST DESTRUCTURING ({:keys [to params query fragment] :as props}) rather than address/extract-address. Its HREF goes through the extractor (via href-attrs, line 104); its PAYLOAD does not. Same values today - two readers of the address by construction, in the one namespace whose R0b comment says the address is selected "through the ONE shared extractor ... rather than a bespoke destructuring".
2. native? is read POST-strip in one path (native-anchor? base-attrs, line 278) and PRE-strip in the other (native-anchor? target, line 409). They agree today only because :target / :download happen to be neither address nor behaviour keys - coincidence of the key classes, not design.

NOT A DEFECT TODAY - no behaviour differs. This is a maintainability finding: the click law is the seam Spec 012 says "is not one an application should have to re-derive per link", and the framework re-derives it once internally.

REMEDY (net deletion ~14 lines, no new abstraction). A private url-requested-payload used by both route-link-render and link-model, and route-link-render :on-click calling activate-link! with that payload. href-attrs stays (route-link-render needs the stripped passthrough attrs, which link-model does not return). Read native? from one side consistently.

title: url-change-fx's decide branch re-assembles the ResolvedTarget it was handed three lines earlier
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F4 (rf2-kqxe6.16). One-line fix; filed because it is the exact shape the seam exists to prevent.

url_change.cljc:213-228 builds the decide call :target by hand:

  :target {:route-id route-id :params params :query query :fragment fragment :url url}

from locals destructured off `resolved-target` (lines 142-144, 166-168) - while the COMMIT branch of the same cond passes (:target route-plan), which IS that value.

They are equal today. The point is that the seam premise (resolve.cljc:12-13: "they all shape their resolved target and build their plan through THIS seam - so no door reinvents the ResolvedTarget shape") is violated INSIDE the door, three lines from where the door received the value. A future field on resolved-target would reach the guards target and the committed target DIFFERENTLY, and the guards decide against a shape the commit does not publish - which is the precise class of bug R0b was created to close (a link door deciding against an incomplete target while the commit hop committed the canonical one).

REMEDY. `:target resolved-target`. One line. The door two branches then structurally cannot disagree about what the target is.

title: url-change-fx grew to nine positional params, two of them adjacent same-shaped allocation maps a transposition would swap in silence
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F3 (rf2-kqxe6.16).

url_change.cljc:124:

  [rdb url default-scroll frame nav-allocation pending-nav-allocation app-db cause opts]

Nine positional parameters. Every OTHER function in the EP-0037 seam takes one map: decisions/decide, plan/scroll-plan, resolve/route-plan, plan/fallback-telemetry-intents, commit-navigation opts, navigate/fragment-only-nav-fx. url-change-fx is the outlier, and it grew `cause` (R0b) and `opts` (R4) as positions 8 and 9 - the "sixth positional argument" shape, arrived at the way that shape always arrives: one slice at a time, each addition individually harmless.

THE SPECIFIC HAZARD. nav-allocation ({:token :counter}) and pending-nav-allocation ({:id :counter}) are ADJACENT, SAME-SHAPED maps. Transposing them at a call site compiles, runs, and mints the wrong id class into either the slice nav-token or the pending-navigation value; nothing in the signature or the shapes objects. What has kept it safe is that both call sites (transitioned-handler:402, handle-url-change-handler:477) are 75 lines apart in the same namespace - not the design.

REMEDY. One map argument, keys named as the destructuring already names them. Private fn, two call sites, purely mechanical - no behaviour change, no test change beyond any direct call in the test tree.
