title: Freehand: invoking a roster callback carrier should name the fix, not surface as 'cb.call is not a function'
description: Follow-up from rf2-c1vvn (PR #6991). v/event / v/handler / v/render-fn / v/raw-fn return a Callback deftype with no IFn (events.cljc:372-374) — deliberate, so 'a foreign API handed one by accident fails at the call'. It does fail, but as a raw host TypeError ('cb.call is not a function' / 'is not a function'), which names neither the carrier nor the fix. rf2-c1vvn established that the ONE place this happens in practice is a carrier authored into a foreign element's raw createElement #js props — a position Freehand never walks — and the guide prescribed exactly that at four sites for months precisely because the failure was mute. The guide is now corrected (the honest spelling is a closure over rf/capture-frame) and the dead path is pinned by a negative control, so this is DX rather than correctness. Candidate: give Callback an IFn arity that throws a typed :rf.error/view-bad-event naming the roster form, the position class ('a raw createElement prop is the library's own ABI — Freehand does not walk it') and the recovery (a closure over rf/capture-frame's :dispatch, or a behavior when identity/retirement matter). CAUTION, and why this was NOT done inside rf2-c1vvn: adding IFn flips (ifn? carrier) to true on both hosts while leaving (fn? carrier) false in CLJS, and several walks branch on one or the other — events/event-plan orders (callback? v) before (fn? v) and is safe, but node.cljc/recorded-prop, props_schema, controlled/door?, route_link_seam and the compiler analyzer arms each need checking before the deftype changes. Verify every reader of the carrier's callability before landing; a half-audited change here silently reclassifies props.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7034: REOPENED. The typed carrier diagnostic works only when the caller is compiled ClojureScript using IFn dispatch; the PR and docs claim it works for a foreign JavaScript library calling a callback from raw createElement props, but the emitted value is not a native JS function.

Independent proof from the emitted node-test-freehand build: Callback is a constructor whose instances have prototype.call and prototype.apply shims plus cljs$core$IFn$_invoke$arity$N methods. Evaluating the built value reports NATIVE_TYPE object and CALL_MEMBER function. A native c("x") call throws TypeError: c is not a function. Only c.call(null,"x") reaches :rf.error/view-bad-event. That distinction is structural in JavaScript: adding a .call property to an object does not give it the Function internal [[Call]] slot.

The new tests do not cross that boundary. pilot_react_interop_react.cljs defines acme-widget in ClojureScript and invokes (on-ping ...), while the negative test invokes (carrier ...) in ClojureScript; both compile through the .call shim. Its assertion text says this is invoking it the way a library would, but an actual JavaScript component executes props.onPing(...) as a native call and still receives the raw host TypeError. The unqualified Spec 004 and guide promise that calling the carrier raises the Freehand diagnostic is therefore false for the exact foreign-library position used to justify the work.

Resolve the boundary explicitly, without discarding the good IFn diagnostic or its reader audit. Either make the carrier a genuine native-callable Function and then re-audit fn?, nominal classification, identity, printing, every host and every call arity; or, more proportionately, state that the typed diagnostic covers ClojureScript-authored callers only and that native JavaScript cannot be intercepted while the carrier remains an object marker. Add a regression that invokes through a literal/native JS call expression, not a ClojureScript function application, and remove the false test wording. Keep the raw-props recovery and existing registration/head-reader protections.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7051 (merge 21fd1b51cc1382d490e4940825a7eb9a968411b5, merged 2026-07-26T01:00:41Z) — keep open for one bounded documentation correction. The substantive host-reach repair is correct: Callback remains an object marker; ClojureScript IFn calls reach the typed diagnostic; the new genuinely JavaScript-authored Function("f", "return f('click:dead');") proof reaches a host TypeError and no :rf.error/id. The guide nevertheless says that the native props.onPing(...) call gets exactly "cb.call is not a function". A native JS call never invokes the object's .call member, so that is the former ClojureScript-compiled-call wording, not the native boundary just documented; V8 reports an expression-dependent "f is not a function" / "props.onPing is not a function" shape. Qualify this as the host's own TypeError without promising the old exact .call spelling. The same old phrase remains in explanatory source/test comments but is historically accurate there when explicitly describing the pre-IFn ClojureScript path; the guide's native-call sentence is the correctness defect.
close_reason:
PR #7070 MERGED (77358daeeb), blob-verified against the worker tip. BOTH ARE REOPEN CLASS (C) — the close itself introduced the defect — which is the class I only identified today, and this is the cleanest evidence for it yet.

rf2-yn5nj — PROVEN BY HISTORY, NOT ARGUED. git log -S pins the offending sentence to 2a6a0fcb44, THE #7051 FIX ITSELF. That fix rewrote the paragraph and MOVED "cb.call is not a function" OUT OF THE FRAMING WHERE IT WAS TRUE — the pre-IFn ClojureScript call, which CLJS compiles to carrier.call(null, x) — INTO THE NATIVE props.onPing(...) SENTENCE, WHERE IT CANNOT BE, because a native call never touches the object .call member. A true statement relocated into a false context. That is exactly what class (C) means and why no improvement in my close reasons would have caught it: the fix was correct and its accompanying prose was not.

AND IT LEFT THE SAME PHRASE IN THREE TEST FILES, correctly — each explicitly describes the pre-IFn ClojureScript path, where the phrase is accurate. Fixing all occurrences of a string is the wrong move when the string is true in some of them.

MUTATION PROOF, EXACTLY THE ASYMMETRY I ASKED FOR, both plants confirmed applied by git diff --stat AND token grep before any verdict, both reverted and re-grepped to absence: P1 stripping the call-protocol splice gives 34 failures rc=1 with every id assertion collapsing to ::no-id; P2 keeping the protocol but BLUNTING THE MESSAGE gives EXACTLY 12 failures rc=1, all at the roster-form / createElement / capture-frame CONTENT assertions, while the ID assertion and all three EX-DATA assertions stay GREEN. That distinguishes "the diagnostic appears" from "a string changed".

rf2-7g4qn — CLASS (C), AND NOT "ALREADY CORRECT", which is what I expected. The docstring still concluded "so no view substrate states the class for itself" while implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:840-848 STILL ASSOCS THE THREE KEYS LITERALLY. THE DONOR DELETION HAS NOT LANDED, so the earlier PR hope that F6e would remove the exception first did not come true — a docstring recording a FUTURE EVENT AS PRESENT FACT. Now names the donor as the one remaining, explicitly temporary exception and states the cost plainly. The inline note carried the same overclaim in miniature and is narrowed to its two actual readers.

A FOURTH FALSE-SIGNAL MASK, caught and discarded: the first core run returned rc=124 — timeout(1) killing a cold .cpcache compile at 590s, with NO DEFTEST AND NO ASSERTION in the log. Re-run without the wrapper: green. The tell held — an exit code that is not a test outcome.

Gates all green with baselines matched exactly: routing 511/2771, freehand 1132/7584, core 2122/10475, test:cljs 11495/57478, browser 798/5057, mkdocs --strict. Sample coverage 113 of 136 unchanged, proving the prose edit sits outside every digest-pinned fence.

title: Detect a PARTIALLY emptied test lane: build-file <-> registered-namespace bijection
description: The rf2-qqzmf test-count floor closes the ZERO case (a lane that discovered nothing). It cannot close the PARTIAL case — the nine silently-skipped .cljc files the audit cites would hide inside any headroom, and a calibrated per-lane floor would not have caught them either.
notes:
DELIVERED in PR #7064 (worker/checker-residuals, commit b29896b74f), NOT closed - mayor closes on the merged SHA. PR #7062 merged an earlier SHA and took only the rf2-u3otj half (verified by blob hash: origin/main:check_thrown_error_messages.py == 5397a03f, my first commit; origin/main:check_test_lane_bijection.py == ba4a7150, the pre-repair blob).

FOUND (the audit residual). NON_EXECUTABLE_PREFIX required the quote/discard run to reach the opening delimiter directly, so the metadata reader prefix restored a discarded/quoted form to the executable universe. Reproduced on main: '^:doc (deftest data (is true)) and #_^:doc (deftest dead (is true)) both give top_level_heads [ns, deftest] and defines_tests True; the unprefixed quoted control correctly gives False.

FOUND (second lookalike, while measuring the first). The same regex read a PRIME-SUFFIXED symbol as a quote: the ' closing db' / tags' / ring' is part of the symbol, but the run took it for a reader macro and marked the next delimiter as data. 352 occurrences across .clj/.cljc/.cljs. Same class the \' character-literal lookbehind already exists for. Latent, not live: every one is nested inside a binding vector where the walk cannot see it, so the universe is 1694 of 2850 tracked Clojure files under the old pattern, under metadata-only, and under the shipped pattern, empty symmetric difference. It is a false GREEN direction (a live suite silently leaving the universe), so it was closed with the same lookbehind.

title: re-frame.ui tool tier: an event site with a runtime argument is published as though its handler were known
description:
Found while landing rf2-z0blg (PR #6971), which gave the Freehand event-site
read a literal/dynamic honesty split. The SIBLING substrate has the same gap
the Freehand one just closed, and it is reachable from a live MCP inspector
today.

`re-frame.ui.tool/project-event-site` (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/tool.cljc,
~line 274) decides whether to publish `:handler` from `:serializable?` alone:

    (and serial? (not= :opaque handler)) (assoc :handler handler)

`:serializable?` is TRUE for the whole `:vector` and `:options` classifications
— it means "the handler is DATA rather than a callback body", NOT "the handler's
value is statically known". So `{:on-click [:basket/remove row-id]}` is
`:serializable? true` with a captured template local in it, and the row hands a
reader the ANALYZED form as though it were the event vector that will dispatch.
It is source code presented where a reader asked for data — the same defect
`read-view-dependencies` already refuses for a subscription's `:query`.

The MCP `read-view-event-sites` tool reads exactly this function
(tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn), and its own description promises
that a `:literal` / `:normalized` site "carries their inspectable :handler event
vector" — which is true only when every argument happens to be literal.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN, one substrate over. `re-frame.freehand.tool/event-site`
projects the handler verbatim only when a `literal-form?` predicate holds, and
otherwise publishes `:handler :opaque` with the literal `:event-id` still shown —
the part the compiler really does know — so the reader loses nothing it could
have used and is told plainly what is unknown. Mirror that, do not invent a
second vocabulary, and keep `:site-kind` as it is.

CHECK FIRST WHETHER THIS IS MOOT. `re-frame.ui` is the EXPERIMENTAL compiled-view
substrate and the donor Freehand is absorbing slice by slice (implementation/
freehand/deps.edn: "the donor artefact is donor only ... absorbed donor code
arrives by MOVE"). If the donor tool tier is being retired rather than absorbed,
close this rather than fixing it — the live-inspector exposure is the only reason
it is filed at P3 instead of being left in rf2-z0blg's notes.
notes:
MAYOR TRIAGE (2026-07-25): DEFER behind F6e, and apply the moot-check the filer correctly named first.

THE FINDING IS REAL AND WELL-MADE: re-frame.ui.tool/project-event-site gates :handler on :serializable? alone, which is true for the whole :vector/:options classes, so [:basket/remove row-id] is published as though its event vector were statically known. Freehand just closed exactly this gap (rf2-z0blg, PR #6971) by applying literal-form? at the read.

WHY DEFER RATHER THAN FIX: the donor is deleted at the EP-0036 F6e gate (rf2-drpa3.57), and F6c — the head of that last stretch — is IN FLIGHT right now on PR #6978, with F6d and F6e strictly downstream. So this is very likely work whose entire value expires within the next stretch of the chain. That is the same shape as the ruling I made earlier today declining :class/:style refusal parity for the donor custom-element.

BUT NOTE THE EXCEPTION THAT ALMOST APPLIES, because it is the reason this is a defer and not a rejection: my generalised rule was 'default NO on donor parity unless the donor behaviour is reachable by a consumer or by a gate that outlives F6e.' Here it IS consumer-reachable — it is live behind the MCP read-view-event-sites tool, so between now and F6e an agent pointed at a re-frame.ui app receives wrong data about whether an event vector is known. That is a genuine, if narrow and short-lived, correctness hole in a shipped tool.

SO THE DECISION PROCEDURE, in order:
  1. When F6e lands, CLOSE THIS AS MOOT with a one-line reason. The deletion resolves it completely and no code change is owed.
  2. If F6c/F6d/F6e visibly stall — the chain sits without progress for a materially long stretch — then FIX IT by mirroring event-site, exactly as the filer specified. It is a small change and the pattern is already proven in Freehand.
  3. Do NOT dispatch it speculatively in the meantime, and do NOT let it be swept into F6c: F6c's job is migration completeness, not repairing a donor about to be removed.

Recorded so whoever meets this bead next does not have to re-derive the reasoning — and so the moot-close is a decision already taken rather than a judgement call made under time pressure.
close_reason: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7053: CLOSED MOOT, NO CODE CHANGE. The donor project-event-site defect is real and implementation/ui still exists until F6e, but its job is explicitly REPLACE/done: the donor realization does not cross, and re-frame.freehand.tool already implements the literal-form honesty split. At the merge/current tree, Pair and Xray production source both read re-frame.freehand.tool; the old Xray donor reader file is absent. The only non-donor reader left is tools/story/test/re_frame/story/view_tool.cljc, a test-tree ledger row scheduled to move to the already-correct replacement. The original P3 live-MCP exposure is therefore stale and no product consumer receives the donor projection. Preserve F6e's eventual deletion; do not port or repair this vestigial donor implementation.

title: Freehand: 004D + FH-STRUCT-010 law text should name the per-event-site facts the manifest now publishes

title: If a FIFTH census false-green axis appears, narrow the fixture grammar instead of hardening the reader again
description:
RULED IN ADVANCE (mayor, 2026-07-25) so the decision is not made under pressure with a fifth audit finding in hand. Filed on the recommendation of the rf2-drpa3.53 worker (PR #6968), which earned the right to make it.

THE HISTORY: the Freehand execution census was hardened FOUR times in one day, each round closing a genuinely distinct false-green mechanism — presence-not-proof plus bare-word helpers (#6929), cross-platform OR-ing of the witness (#6950), keyword/numeric token boundaries (#6952/#6956), and evaluation context via quote/syntax-quote (#6968). Every round was justified: a conformance census that lies is worse than no census, and this one is gate 1 of donor deletion.

THE WORKER'S ANALYSIS, which I accept: on the LEXICAL axis no fifth is likely, because #6968 completes a set — there are exactly three ways code-shaped text fails to evaluate in Clojure and all three now sit in one pass (_evaluated, beside _strip and _read_as). But the reader is at its limit. The next axis will not be lexical; it will be DATAFLOW — (let [x fx] (is (= 1 1))), (when false (is ...)) — which no token boundary reaches and which would require a second Clojure front-end inside the gate. That is the point at which hardening becomes the risk.

THE RULING: do NOT harden the reader a fifth time. If a fifth axis is found, narrow the FIXTURE GRAMMAR so the ambiguous shape cannot be written — one declared prover per row, e.g. (deftest fh-call-001 (conf/proves :FH-CALL-001 {:mode :compiled} (is ...))). The census then asks a question about SHAPE, decidable from a single form: no name resolution, no closure analysis, no platform helper identity, no data-versus-code distinction, because a datum cannot occupy the prover position at all.

COST, stated honestly by the worker rather than hidden: a corpus-wide edit across the fixtures, a new macro on both platforms, and one permitted idiom instead of any. That is why this is NOT being done now — the class is closed on all three lexical axes, the dataflow shapes are hypothetical (nobody has written one in a fixture), and a corpus-wide edit to guard a shape nobody writes is exactly the over-engineering the pre-alpha posture rules out.

TRIGGER TO ACT: a fifth distinct false-green axis reproduced against the census, OR anyone proposing a fifth reader hardening. At that moment this bead becomes the work, and the answer is already decided — narrow the grammar once rather than chase semantics with a lexer.

DO NOT close this as stale. It is a standing decision, and its value is that it exists before the pressure does.
notes:
TRIGGER EVALUATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED (mayor, 2026-07-25). A fifth census false-green axis did appear — metadata-prefixed data, from the audit of #6968 — and this bead says to narrow the fixture grammar rather than harden the reader again. I am NOT firing it, and the distinction is the whole value of having written this down in advance.

WHY NOT: this rule was written against a fifth axis needing NEW CAPABILITY. Its reasoning, from the worker that proposed it: 'the next axis will not be lexical; it will be dataflow — (let [x fx] (is ...)), (when false (is ...)) — which no boundary reaches and which would mean a second Clojure front-end inside the gate.' That is what this bead exists for: the reader being asked to approximate evaluation semantics it cannot own.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IS A BUG IN THE REDUCTION JUST SHIPPED. _prefix_end miscounts datum extent for the metadata reader macro: ^ consumes its metadata datum AND THEN its annotated target, while the code treats it as consuming one following datum. So _datum_end stops after the metadata map, _evaluated blanks the quote plus the metadata, and [fx] survives as a live reference. Reproduced hermetically: (deftest t (is (vector? '^{:audit true} [fx]))) returns defects=0, as does the syntax-quoted twin, and both assertions evaluate true in Clojure with no fx binding at all. The explicit (quote ^{:audit true} [fx]) control correctly REDS, which localises the fault precisely to the prefix-extent calculation rather than to the concept. The audit's own words: 'one bounded reader-macro correction, not a request for a general parser.'

The predecessor's claim that three quote spellings 'complete a set' was simply wrong — it enumerated quote forms and missed that ^ is a fourth prefix macro feeding the same extent computation. An incomplete enumeration inside the existing mechanism is not a new class the mechanism cannot express.

THE TRIGGER IS THEREFORE TIGHTENED, not weakened. This bead fires when a new axis needs a CAPABILITY THE READER DOES NOT HAVE — dataflow, binding, control flow, macro expansion. It does NOT fire on a defect in the shipped reduction, however many of those there are. Fixing a miscounted extent is ordinary correctness work; conceding that a lexer cannot model evaluation is the decision this bead holds.

PRACTICAL TEST for whoever meets this next: can the fix be stated as 'this existing pass mis-handles form X' (=> fix it), or does it require the pass to know something only evaluation knows (=> fire this bead and narrow the grammar)?

PROCESS NOTE: I first wrote this onto a fabricated id (rf2-1i2fx) because I recalled it instead of looking it up — the same error I made earlier today with a non-existent rf2-t1nnf in three audit briefs. Look the id up; never type one from memory.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS RECORDED STANDING RULES, not as work done. Both beads are CONDITIONAL — they describe what to do IF a future trigger fires — and an open bead is a claim that work is owed. Neither owes work today; both owe a decision when a specific thing happens. The rule survives here and is searchable.

rf2-mom1g — THE RULE: if a FIFTH census false-green axis appears, NARROW THE FIXTURE GRAMMAR instead of hardening the reader again. The census has been hardened FOUR times: presence-not-proof; a witness OR-ed across platforms; keyword and numeric token boundaries; quote/syntax-quote evaluation context; and datum extent under metadata. Each hardening makes the reader more capable and more able to be wrong in a new way.

AND IT WAS TESTED TODAY WITHOUT FIRING. rf2-jl7gz asked the reader to treat a tagged literal as the two-datum prefix it is. Measured against STRIPPED text: 545 tagged literals in code, AXIS 1 (behind a quote) = 0, AXIS 2 (#_ target) = 0. A first pass over RAW source reported 56 hits — ALL MARKDOWN BACKTICKS IN DOCSTRINGS. So no false green exists to be the fifth, this ruling was not engaged, and rf2-jl7gz stays deferred on measured zero corpus exposure. That is the rule working: it told us not to harden.

rf2-kem4o — THE RULE: if a SECOND docs example is found violating its own documented rule, build a doc-example conformance gate. ONE has been found — a reg-route example putting :path in metadata, where registry.cljc:455 THROWS, so the route in the worked example never registers. One instance is a bug; two is a class. A worker was explicitly told today to file against this bead rather than build the gate, and correctly did not find a second.

REOPEN CONDITIONS, stated so this is not lost: mom1g reopens the moment a FIFTH census false-green axis is measured — not suspected, measured, against stripped text. kem4o reopens the moment a SECOND docs example is found violating its own documented rule.

WHY CLOSING IS RIGHT RATHER THAN TIDY: leaving them open makes the backlog assert that a census hardening and a conformance gate are owed. Neither is. This is the same disposition as rf2-bk7z5, closed today on its own advice because validating an unreachable case is a nag-diagnostic — and it fits the principle recorded today that A GUARD IS WARRANTED WHEN THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. Neither of these failures has happened a second time.

title: clein install pom fidelity on the ssr leaf is a never-exercised path on the first tag
description:
Surfaced by rf2-p4a93 (PR #6967) and deliberately not actioned there — pre-existing, unchanged by that PR, and fail-safe.

THE PATH: release.yml's 'Install ssr to runner ~/.m2 (ssr-ring only)' step runs from an UN-REWRITTEN implementation/ssr/deps.edn, which still carries :local/root "../core". So ssr-ring's dependency resolution reads whatever pom that install produces. Nobody has ever run it: git tag --list shows no v* tag and gh run list --workflow=release.yml shows zero runs, so the first tag is simultaneously a public act and this path's debut.

WHY IT IS NOT A TAG BLOCKER: it is fail-safe in the right direction. A bad pom here would cause resolution to FAIL and block the ssr-ring publish, not poison a published artefact — and after rf2-p4a93 the needs: edge means a blocked ssr-ring cannot leave a Release announcing an artefact that did not ship. So the failure mode is a stalled release, recoverable by bump-and-re-ship, rather than a permanent unresolvable coordinate on Clojars.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT: exercise the path once without publishing — install ssr to a scratch ~/.m2 from the un-rewritten deps.edn and confirm the generated pom resolves ssr-ring's :deps. That is a local experiment, not a workflow change. If it does not resolve, the fix is to rewrite the coord before installing, mirroring what the deploy step already does.

Related and already discharged: rf2-p4a93 fixed the inter-leaf ordering; this bead is only about the pom the install step produces.
notes:
CONFIRMED, and inert for a sharper reason than the reviewer note gave. Ran the
experiment locally at 0.0.1.alpha in worker/release-truth (PR #7028).

1. `clein pom` on the un-rewritten implementation/ssr/deps.edn reproduces the
   reviewer's result: "Skipping coordinate: {:local/root .../core ...}", pom with
   org.clojure/clojure as its only <dependency>.
2. But `clein install` -- the command release.yml actually runs -- writes NO POM
   AT ALL. clein/install is clean + copy-src + compile-java + b/jar + b/install
   and never calls write-pom (noahtheduke/clein.cljc:166-172 at pinned sha
   2b83503246). ~/.m2/.../re-frame2-ssr/0.0.1.alpha/ held only
   _remote.repositories + the jar; `jar tf` showed only META-INF/MANIFEST.MF.
   So the locally-installed artefact declares no dependencies at all.
3. Resolution unaffected. A probe with deploy-ssr-ring's post-rewrite :deps
   (core + ssr at :mvn/version) resolved rc=0, silent, both jars on the path.
   NEGATIVE CONTROL: the same probe with ssr ALONE resolved rc=0 with core
   ABSENT -- so the missing transitive edge is real, and what makes it inert is
   that ssr-ring names day8/re-frame2 as its own direct top-level coordinate.
4. The PUBLISHED pom is a different artefact and is correct: rewriting ssr's
   deps.edn with .github/scripts/rewrite-local-root-coord.sh and regenerating
   emits day8/re-frame2 at the release version. That is what the deploy-leaf
   matrix's `ssr` value produces, since its Rewrite step precedes its deploy.

Nothing touched Clojars; the release workflow was not run (and per rf2-i3gl2
could not complete). ~/.m2 pollution: installed day8/re-frame2-ssr 0.0.1.alpha
for the probe and REMOVED it; day8/re-frame2 0.0.1.alpha overwrote an existing
entry and was left.

Discharged by recording it: PR #7028 adds a comment block above the "Install ssr
to runner ~/.m2" step in release.yml. Comment-only -- no job, no step, no needs:
edge. Nothing executable changed.
close_reason:
PR #7028 MERGED. Three beads; two corrected their own premise.

rf2-1zbpw — clein install WRITES NO POM AT ALL (clein/install never calls write-pom). Installed dir held only _remote.repositories and the jar; jar tf showed only MANIFEST.MF. NEGATIVE CONTROL: ssr alone resolved rc=0 with core ABSENT, proving the missing edge is real and that ssr-ring own direct core coordinate makes it inert. The PUBLISHED pom is a different artefact and is correct. Proved locally; nothing touched Clojars. Deliverable: one comment block.

rf2-wns8d — TAUTOLOGY CONFIRMED BY MUTATION. It mutated the PRODUCTION WRAPPER ungated and THE SHIPPED DEFTEST STAYED GREEN while a probe went red. Four browser runs: clean/shipped 116-516-0 rc=0; mutated/shipped 118-518-2 FAIL; mutated/remedied 116-519-4 FAIL; clean/remedied 116-519-0 rc=0. Applied to BOTH jsx deftests — it found a second the bead never named. views.cljs byte-identical to main afterwards.

rf2-12g5z — CONFIRMED, AND IT MISATTRIBUTED HALF OF WHAT IT SAW. The manifest genuinely ships (seven sentinels present in release, ZERO in the tier-absent control). BUT two of the five sentinels the bead named DO NOT DISCRIMINATE — view-cell and source-coord appear IDENTICALLY in the control. AND THE ABSOLUTE PATHS ARE NOT MANIFEST PAYLOAD: the control, with no manifest at all, carries six occurrences of its own entry-file path, from core always-on error-coord registry which spec/001 contracts as RETAINED. Every re-frame2 production app carries them, Freehand or not.

DIRECT VINDICATION OF THE THREE-BUNDLE ORACLE recorded this morning: a two-bundle control is insufficient because a sibling vocabulary reads as a survivor. The third bundle with the tier absent exposed two false sentinels AND a wholly misattributed finding. Without it this bead ships a claim that Freehand leaks developer paths when core does it for everyone by contract.

TWO UNPROMPTED CORRECTIONS: spec/004D I-12 claimed the OPPOSITE, listing manifests on the "scanned absence roster" when nothing scans for them. And spec/004-Views was THE WRONG OWNER — no production-bundle language, and its own delegation table routes manifests to 004D. The bead named the wrong file; the worker checked rather than obeying.

TWO DESIGN DECISIONS NAMED AND STOPPED: v/manifest returning nil in production is a contract change to a PUBLISHED door; relativising the retained :file reverses rf2-wvsxg. Neither implemented.

Gates: test-fast-pr.sh PASS rc=0 over 31 steps including release-dag-policy and rewrite-local-root-coord, both parsing the edited release.yml; mkdocs --strict rc=0 zero WARNINGs run directly; browser prod-elision rc=0. release.yml COMMENT-ONLY, one hunk, +26 lines, verified with yaml.safe_load showing the same six jobs and identical needs: lists.

title: docs/ssr/glossary.md names only three of the four locked :rf/public-error keys
description:
Carve-out from rf2-0aqd4 acceptance item 3. The rf2-0aqd4 worker (PR #6966) owned docs/api/** and was fenced off docs/ssr/*.md guide pages, which another docs worker held at the time, so this one line was left unpatched.

docs/ssr/glossary.md:43, the 'error projector' entry: 'The pure function that maps a rich internal trace to a sanitized, client-safe :rf/public-error shape (`:status`, `:code`, `:message`) when a server render throws.'

Three keys. public-error-shape? (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:98-105) is a CLOSED four-key shape -- (= public-error-keys (set (keys x))) over #{:status :code :message :retryable?}, plus a 400..599 range check on :status. A reader who writes their projector's return shape from this glossary entry produces a three-key map, fails conformance, and has their projector silently discarded in favour of the locked generic-500 fallback on every error. Exactly the defect rf2-0aqd4 fixed on the API page.

FIX: name all four keys. One line. docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md now carries the full closed-shape rule above its reg-error-projector example if a cross-reference is wanted.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/ssr/glossary.md's 'error projector' entry names all four locked keys, including :retryable?. 2. mkdocs build --strict and check_doc_slugs.py green.

title: add-auth.md restores the token but never the user, and boots after the frame's first URL sync
description:
Found while rewriting docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md section 4 onto :can-enter (rf2-dx52g). PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by that PR — the old interceptor recipe read the same path and had the same hole — so it was filed rather than patched.

Two coupled defects in the page's boot story:

1. The session restore never restores the USER. :auth/init seeds
   {:user nil :token token}. The route guard reads [:auth :user]. So after any
   page reload a reader with a perfectly good saved JWT is treated as logged out
   by the guard, and a deep link to a protected route is refused. The token is
   restored; the identity it stands for never is. The realworld_http example
   closes this by having :auth/initialise pull the saved token and then fetch
   /user (auth.cljs), which is what actually repopulates [:auth :user].

2. The boundary dispatch runs AFTER the URL-bound frame's first URL to slice
   sync. The page's 'Wire the frame and restore the session' block calls
   make-frame with :url-bound? true and THEN
   (rf/dispatch-sync [:auth/init] {:rf.cofx {...}}). Per
   spec/012-Routing.md (the :url-bound? frame lifecycle) the popstate install and
   the initial URL to owner-slice sync run from a POST-CREATE hook — after
   :initial-events on first registration, but make-frame has already returned by
   the time the boundary dispatch runs. So the first :can-enter evaluation of the
   session sees an unseeded auth slice even if defect 1 were fixed.

   The example avoids this by restoring the session from :initial-events (via a
   RECORDABLE coeffect with a supplier) rather than from a PROVIDED coeffect
   stamped at the boundary — core.cljs states the ordering is load-bearing for
   exactly this reason. add-auth.md deliberately chose the provided shape (step 1
   explains why: a :dispatch fan-out cannot forward :rf.cofx), so the fix is a
   real editorial decision about which coeffect grade the how-to should teach,
   not a one-line patch.

Either defect alone makes a logged-in reload of a protected deep link bounce to
login. Worth one deliberate pass over the page's boot ordering + session-restore
shape, ideally against what the example actually does.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md's boot recipe leaves [:auth :user] populated after a reload with a valid saved token (or says plainly that restoring the identity is a further step and what it costs). 2. The session restore is established before the URL-bound frame's first URL to slice sync, or the page states the consequence for a protected deep link. 3. Whichever coeffect grade the page teaches is consistent with step 1's rationale. 4. mkdocs --strict + doc-slug gates green.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6965 (2026-07-25). The same restore-order defect is present in docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md, which this PR newly retargeted to :can-enter: it calls make-frame {:url-bound? true} before the boundary-stamped :auth/initialise dispatch, so the synchronous initial URL decision precedes even the token write; :auth/initialise then starts an asynchronous GET /user while the guard reads nil. Extend this docs owner across BOTH add-auth.md and the tutorial rather than filing a duplicate. The canonical RealWorld examples underlying restore-safe boot contract and deferred regression are owned by rf2-k85nd.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6983 (2026-07-25): despite the  ix(examples,docs) title, body claim that both guide pages are fixed, and Closes rf2-tgh45, the merged file boundary is only three xamples/real-apps/realworld_http/*.cljs files; no docs file changed. Both documented defects remain live. docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md still seeds only {:user nil :token token} and runs the provided-coeffect :auth/init after make-frame {:url-bound? true}; docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md still creates the URL-bound frame before its boundary :auth/initialise dispatch. Keep this exact docs owner in progress; update both recipes to restore identity and establish the token/unknown-identity ordering before or safely across the first URL decision.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #6990.

COEFFECT GRADE IMPLEMENTED: the SYNCHRONOUS restore in docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md. Persists the session (token AND cached identity) through its one effect, restores both from a {:recordable? true} coeffect with a supplier, and runs that restore from the frame's :initial-events — where a boot read has to be, because :url-bound? true syncs the first URL only after every :initial-events step. Identity is present before any route is judged, so the race cannot exist. Step 3's existing 401 response hook keeps the optimistic cached identity honest, and the page now says so.

ALTERNATIVE REJECTED: teaching the async identity fetch as the page's default — it drags request lifecycle, a pending state, and a guard that must await it into a page whose subject is route auth. Named in one note instead, pointing at the RealWorld examples and Part 3.

The provided/boundary-stamped cofx is retired here for a stated reason: :initial-events is frame config declared before the frame exists, and a supplier-backed recordable needs nothing threaded through it. Tests still pin an exact value via the dispatch-site :rf.cofx stub.

The Conduit tutorial (Part 3) genuinely holds only a bearer token and must exchange it, so it keeps the async fetch — honestly, including the deferred denial branch, the settle event, the 'restoring your session' shell state, and the Xray ledger. Part 5 follows Part 3's cofx shape; Part 1's 'an equivalent shape' note now names where :initial-events stops being merely equivalent.

title: skills/re-frame2 project-structure cites install-router! and auth-guard helpers that no longer exist
description:
Found while discharging rf2-dx52g (the four pre-EP-0037 guide pages).

skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/project-structure.md:99 says:

  'Route registrations belong in a single routing.cljs — the reg-route table,
   auth-gating helpers, and a small route-link helper view
   (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:1-49). The entry ns requires
   it for side-effects and calls its install-router! from run
   (realworld/core.cljs:536). ... keeps the auth-guard helpers private.'

Two claims cite code that does not exist:

1. install-router! — git grep over examples/ returns ZERO hits. The imperative
   install/remove exports were retired: spec/012-Routing.md line ~1881 states the
   popstate listener is wired by the :url-bound? frame LIFECYCLE and that
   install-url-listener! / install-history-listener! / remove-url-listener! /
   remove-history-listener! are retired with no back-compat shim. The example's own
   README says outright 'no hand-rolled popstate listener, no explicit install
   call'. (The only other install-router! in the tree is
   docs/spec/Construction-Prompts.md:847, a generated mirror.)

2. 'auth-guard helpers' / 'auth-gating helpers' private to routing.cljs — the
   example's auth gate is now :can-enter [:realworld.routing/authed?] on the
   :requires-auth routes plus a public rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied. There
   are no private normaliser helpers left to keep private, and the handler is
   deliberately public.

The structural advice itself (one routing.cljs holds the table + the auth gate) is
still correct — only the two cites and the 'helpers' framing are stale.

Deliberately NOT fixed in the rf2-dx52g PR: skills/ was outside that bead's four
pages, and the skill drift gates make a drive-by edit there a separate risk. Worth
checking whether check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py would have caught either cite.
acceptance_criteria: 1. project-structure.md:99 no longer cites install-router!; it describes the :url-bound? frame lifecycle doing the wiring, or drops the sentence. 2. The 'auth-guard helpers' framing matches the example's actual :can-enter + public :rf.route/entry-denied shape. 3. Skill drift gates + check_doc_slugs green.
close_reason: project-structure.md no longer cites install-router! (zero hits in examples/); the sentence now describes the :url-bound? frame-root lifecycle installing the popstate listener and doing the first-load URL->state sync (Spec 012 §popstate drives the URL-owner frame, both directions). The 'auth-guard helpers ... private' framing is replaced by the example's actual shape: two deliberately PUBLIC registrations -- a :can-enter guard sub on each :requires-auth route plus the framework's :rf.route/entry-denied handler. Also dropped the stale 'route-link helper view' claim (the example uses framework rf/route-link) and repointed two cites that pointed past core.cljs's 452-line EOF (:536, :575-586) at the live frame-root config :416-424. Open question answered: check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py does NOT validate file:line cites (it guards bead-id leaks, verification posture, launcher canonicality, machine/managed-http recipes), and nothing else in scripts/ does -- no cite-resolver gate built, per the standing deferral. Follow-up rf2-6er0d filed for spec/Construction-Prompts.md's surviving install-router! template. All 14 skill gates + check_doc_slugs green. PR #6999.

title: reg-view-output-has-no-jsx-source-props-under-prod is a tautology in the build it runs in
notes:
CONFIRMED BY MUTATION, and fixed. PR #7028 (worker/release-truth).

The bead's reading is right, and jsx-literal-absent-from-rendered-output (which
the bead did not name) was weak the same way: [:p "scan me"] has no props for a
prop-decorating regression to land on.

MUTATION PROOF -- mutated the PRODUCTION wrapper, not the test. At
core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:570 the tail was wrapped to decorate the rendered
root's EXISTING attrs map with the pre-rf2-rohdn _jsx* props, ungated. Four runs
of `npm run test:browser-prod-elision`, rc captured into a worktree-local log
and cross-checked against each log's own verdict line:

  1. clean   + shipped fixture   116 tests / 516 assertions / 0 failures   rc=0
  2. MUTATED + shipped fixture   118 / 518 / 2 FAILURES                    rc=1
  3. MUTATED + remedy fixture    116 / 519 / 4 FAILURES                    rc=1
  4. clean   + remedy fixture    116 tests / 519 assertions / 0 failures   rc=0

Run 2 is the proof: under a mutation re-growing exactly what the deftest forbids,
reg-view-output-has-no-jsx-source-props-under-prod stayed GREEN. The only reds
were two temporary probes -- one carrying the remedy fixture, one asserting
(map? attrs), which failed with `actual: (not (map? nil))`. Run 3 shows the same
mutation turns all four assertions of the remedied file red.

REMEDY (a), applied to BOTH jsx deftests: an explicit root attrs map, each
assertion pinning (map? attrs) as a precondition before reading a key, and the
(or (nil? attrs) ...) escape hatch removed. Chose (a) over (b) because it makes
the assertion load-bearing at the cost of one fixture character-change, and
because the ns docstring now records the measurement so nobody simplifies it
back. views.cljs is byte-identical to origin/main -- the mutation was reverted
before the final run and before any commit.

Corroborating: the framework has NO _jsx* producer. rf2-rohdn removed the
emission; live references are only the SSR stripper for USER-carried props
(ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc), a historical note in
core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, and the removed-sentinel comment in
scripts/check-elision.cjs.

PR #7028 MERGED. Three beads; two corrected their own premise.

rf2-1zbpw — clein install WRITES NO POM AT ALL (clein/install never calls write-pom). Installed dir held only _remote.repositories and the jar; jar tf showed only MANIFEST.MF. NEGATIVE CONTROL: ssr alone resolved rc=0 with core ABSENT, proving the missing edge is real and that ssr-ring own direct core coordinate makes it inert. The PUBLISHED pom is a different artefact and is correct. Proved locally; nothing touched Clojars. Deliverable: one comment block.

rf2-wns8d — TAUTOLOGY CONFIRMED BY MUTATION. It mutated the PRODUCTION WRAPPER ungated and THE SHIPPED DEFTEST STAYED GREEN while a probe went red. Four browser runs: clean/shipped 116-516-0 rc=0; mutated/shipped 118-518-2 FAIL; mutated/remedied 116-519-4 FAIL; clean/remedied 116-519-0 rc=0. Applied to BOTH jsx deftests — it found a second the bead never named. views.cljs byte-identical to main afterwards.

rf2-12g5z — CONFIRMED, AND IT MISATTRIBUTED HALF OF WHAT IT SAW. The manifest genuinely ships (seven sentinels present in release, ZERO in the tier-absent control). BUT two of the five sentinels the bead named DO NOT DISCRIMINATE — view-cell and source-coord appear IDENTICALLY in the control. AND THE ABSOLUTE PATHS ARE NOT MANIFEST PAYLOAD: the control, with no manifest at all, carries six occurrences of its own entry-file path, from core always-on error-coord registry which spec/001 contracts as RETAINED. Every re-frame2 production app carries them, Freehand or not.

DIRECT VINDICATION OF THE THREE-BUNDLE ORACLE recorded this morning: a two-bundle control is insufficient because a sibling vocabulary reads as a survivor. The third bundle with the tier absent exposed two false sentinels AND a wholly misattributed finding. title: EP-0037 readiness + prefetch coverage lives only in the resources suite; routing's own suite survives both mutations
notes:
Filed by the pre-alpha tests/clarity audit (rf2-ods8n, lens B), 2026-07-25 19:15 AUSEST. MUTATION-CONFIRMED, both mutations reverted.

M1 — routing/src/re_frame/routing/readiness.cljc, the EP-0037 R1 route-readiness table:
  -  (seq blocking) {:transition :loading :error nil}
  +  (seq blocking) {:transition :idle    :error nil}
  implementation/routing   -> Ran 487 tests ... 0 failures, 0 errors   (GREEN — mutation SURVIVED)
  implementation/resources -> 10 failures  (expected: (= :loading (:transition (slice))))

M2 — routing/src/re_frame/routing/prefetch.cljc, dropping the warm-plan fx splice:
  -  (seq (:fx plan)) (assoc :fx (:fx plan))
  +  false            (assoc :fx (:fx plan))
  implementation/resources -> 3 failures (a-real-link-warms-the-whole-branch-on-intent)

routing/test/re_frame/routing_prefetch_test.clj is 66 lines and NEVER invokes prefetch/prefetch-handler. It unit-tests address/prefetch-address-error and link/prefetch-payload only. The whole :rf.route/prefetch handler — the carried frame-stamp requirement, the :rf.error/prefetch-bad-address reject-before-planning path, branch resolution via routing-events/resolve-branch, the :routing/on-route-prefetch late-bind, the single :rf.route/prefetched summary trace, and 'writes NO route state' — has no coverage inside the routing artefact. The only behavioural exercise is resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc:816,851.

Likewise nothing in routing/test requires re-frame.routing.readiness; project-at-commit's :loading and :error branches are reached only through the Resources artefact's :routing/on-route-entry hook.

CI IS SAFE TODAY — one flag (implementation_jvm) arms all twenty JVM jobs, so a routing-only PR does run jvm-resources. Two reasons to fix anyway:
  1. Local signal: combined with rf2-dgzaf, a worker changing routing/src and running the documented gate sees NEITHER the routing nor the resources JVM suite.
  2. Brittleness: the moment anyone tiers the JVM jobs per-artefact (a natural CI-time optimisation) these two surfaces go dark.

REMEDY. A small routing-owned test that drives :rf.route/prefetch end-to-end with a stubbed :routing/on-route-prefetch (assert the fx splice, the one summary trace, the bad-address reject, and zero route-state writes), plus a direct unit test of readiness/project-at-commit's three rows. Neither needs the Resources artefact.

P3 because CI covers it; raise if JVM job gating is ever made per-artefact.
close_reason:
REJECTED AT TRIAGE (Tier 3, mayor, 2026-07-25) — not a defect today, and contingent on a change that has not happened.

The finding is real as an observation: a mutation of readiness :loading -> :idle left the routing suite green (487 tests) with only resources red, and routing_prefetch_test.clj never invokes the handler. But the auditor's own qualifier is dispositive — 'CI safe today (one flag arms all 20 jobs), brittle if ever tiered.' So there is no live false-green: every one of the 20 JVM jobs is armed by the same flag, and the coverage that exists does run.

What is being asked for is protection against a hypothetical future in which the gate matrix is tiered. Under the standing posture — pre-alpha, not over-engineering, do not litigate every last fine detail — relocating tests to guard against a tiering decision nobody has taken is premature. And if that tiering ever happens, rf2-dgzaf already owns the honest version of this concern (test-fast-pr.sh claims to mirror CI's PR-gate matrix while running 1 of the 20 JVM artefact suites), so the real risk has an owner.

TO BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT WOULD REVIVE THIS: if anyone tiers the JVM gate matrix so that a routing/src change can go green without running the resources suite, reopen this immediately — at that moment the mis-attribution becomes a live false green rather than a latent one. Until then, closing it keeps the backlog honest rather than carrying a bead whose premise is a future decision.

Rejecting is part of triage, not a failure of the audit: the method records that the mayor may reorganise or reject findings and that not every finding is actioned. This reviewer filed six findings and five stand — good calibration.

title: day8/re-frame2 has no performance regression gate (every bench in the repo covers an UNPUBLISHED artefact)
notes:
MAYOR RULING: DEFER, on a MEASURED ground rather than a preference (2026-07-26). Do not dispatch.

THE REASON IS THE NOISE FLOOR, and it was measured today by the compiled-tier report (rf2-lnecd, docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md): THE NO-SUBSTRATE FLOOR ARM DRIFTED 37% ACROSS ROUNDS — larger than most of the effects being measured — which is why every claim in that report is stated as a RATIO TO THE IN-RUN FLOOR rather than an absolute. On the same box, the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns across two JVMs.

A REGRESSION GATE ON A SUBSTRATE WITH A 37% FLOOR DRIFT IS A FLAKE GENERATOR. It would red on noise, and this repo has a standing rule that A FAILING TEST ON A TOUCHED SURFACE IS NEVER A FLAKE — which is exactly the rule that makes a false red expensive to dismiss. We already have one such gate (rf2-yumaq: G-8 dying because its baseline was TOO FAST) and fixing it took a worker. Adding a second, broader one before the measurement is stable would manufacture that cost at scale.

A PREMISE CORRECTION THE BEAD INHERITS FROM ME: its notes classify the Freehand benches as covering an artefact that is "NOT published". Freehand is PRE-PUBLICATION and expected to ship — docs/release-process.md forecloses only day8/re-frame2-ui, and implementation/freehand/deps.edn:29 says staying out of the lockstep inventory "leaves the release train untouched until Freehand actually ships". I propagated that error into six briefs today. So the gap this bead describes is narrower than stated: the benches cover artefacts that are not published YET, not artefacts that never will be.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DISPATCHABLE, in order: (1) a stable measurement method — the report shows allocation via getThreadAllocatedBytes gave min = p50 = max in nearly every arm, so an ALLOCATION gate is buildable where a wall-clock gate is not; (2) a named regression the gate would have caught, because a perf gate with no historical catch is an assertion that the future will resemble a past nobody measured; (3) the alpha tag, after which "published artefact" stops being a moving target.

NOT A REJECTION. The operator has ruled that performance matters — the compiler is KEPT for performance-critical applications not yet seen. A gate is the right long-term instrument; it is the wrong instrument today because it cannot yet distinguish signal from a 37% floor.

title: core: ~124 frame-registry re-resolutions per single dispatch (~36% of per-event cost) — record the number; take only the clarity-free half
notes:
From rf2-ods8n lens A (perf + back-compat audit), 2026-07-25. MEASURED. Filed as the
DIAGNOSIS behind rf2-sj5s7; deliberately NOT a mandate to refactor the router.

MEASUREMENT (from-clean JVM: fresh JVM per run, warm-up loop, System/gc before the
timed window; Clojure 1.12.0 / Temurin 21.0.10; published core via the plain-atom
adapter). Instrumented call counts for ONE dispatch-sync of a one-line :db-write
handler:

  re-frame.frame/frame                      124 calls  (95 with debug off)   86.1 ns each
  frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?    124        (94)                  (inside frame)
  frame-incarnation-token                   115        (88)                 105.4 ns each
  frame-incarnation-closing?                105        (82)                  37.7 ns each

~17 us of a measured 47 us ([:noop]) to 66 us ([:inc]) per-event total. Raw-handler
baseline with no framework — (swap! a update :n inc) — is 0.084 us. The JFR
settings=profile execution-sample profile over 400k dispatches agrees independently:
those five re_frame.frame predicates are the top re-frame frames in the profile.

Each frame-incarnation-token call re-reads the `frames` atom to fetch :drain-lock — a
value that is CONSTANT for the whole incarnation by construction, as its own docstring
states ("the token is CONSTANT across one incarnation and DISTINCT across a
destroy-frame! + fresh construction of the same id").

CLARITY VERDICT — partly free, partly not, and the not-free half should be LEFT ALONE:
  - FREE (arguably clarity-positive): the router already holds `frame-record` at most
    of these call sites (run-one-pass!, prepare-handler-ctx, commit-and-flow!,
    emit-pipeline-trailers! all take it). Record-taking arities would make explicit
    what is being read. And the literal-path get-in removal is unconditionally free —
    that is rf2-sj5s7, which is where the actionable work lives.
  - NOT FREE: collapsing all 115 token lookups to one per pass means threading a token
    through a chain where emit-pipeline-trailers! ALREADY takes eight positional args.
    That trades clarity for microseconds and should not be done for its own sake.

So: this bead exists to RECORD the number so a future reader knows where the per-event
cost goes and does not rediscover it. Do rf2-sj5s7. Do not refactor the router drain
signature chasing this.

Related, recorded without a claim: per-event cost scales at ~7.8 us per live
subscription on this substrate (72 us at 1 sub -> 185 us at 10 -> 456 us at 50,
measured, inclusive of the bench's own per-sub deref). That is the propagation SHAPE.
It is a JVM plain-atom figure and must NOT be read as a browser number — the browser
runs the ratom substrate and Closure-eliminates the trace path.
close_reason:
PR #7047 MERGED. RECORD BEAD, NOT AN OPTIMISATION — established from the bead own body, which de-scopes the refactor, and from the fact that the actionable half it points at (rf2-sj5s7, the literal-path get-in removal) is ALREADY CLOSED on main via PR #6986.

PROFILE FIRST, METHOD STATED, per the operator standing instruction. Counting wrappers over the four vars for one dispatch-sync; plain-atom, JVM, default debug gate. STRUCTURAL COUNTS, NOT TIMINGS — no wall clock quoted anywhere, which is the right call on a box that measured the same primitive at 10.4ns and 21.7ns across two JVMs with seven workers running.

[:inc] re-derives the bead exactly on three of four: frame 124, frame-incarnation-token 115, frame-incarnation-closing? 105. The visibility predicate is 125 NOT 124 — one call arrives from a registry enumeration rather than through frame.

CALLER ATTRIBUTION CHANGED THE ANSWER AND THE BEAD OWN VERDICT WITH IT, which is exactly the lesson I briefed from the interpreter profiling: 115 of the 124 come via frame-incarnation-live?, and 105 of THOSE via event-continuation-live?, consulted from TWENTY distinct sites per pipeline run — led by call-while-exact-owner (22) and process-event! inner continuation (21). THE FOUR RECORD-HOLDING ROUTER SEAMS THE BEAD NAMED AS THE FREE WIN ACCOUNT FOR 20 OF THE 105, ROUGHLY A SIXTH. So record-taking arities would NOT have moved the number, and the bead own proposed remedy was wrong.

NO OPTIMISATION TAKEN. A 33-line comment block in frame.cljc records the counts, the method, the attribution chain and the reason not to act. And the diff is provably comment-only: git diff origin/main...HEAD | grep "^+" | grep -v "^+;;" is EMPTY — 33 insertions, 0 deletions, one file. That is how a record bead should land.

Gates: core 2115/10462 rc=0, routing 511/2771 rc=0 matching the handed baseline exactly, test-fast-pr.sh PASS with test:cljs 11491/57471.

THE SEPARATE P1 IT ESCALATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED is filed: under the documented production gate -Dre-frame.debug=false, a plain dispatch-sync never runs its handler while resolve-handler returns it at that same moment. That also explains why the debug-off counts recorded on this bead and on rf2-sj5s7 (95/88/82) do not reproduce today.

title: SSR glossary and the Next.js comparison promise automatic head currency and head-hash mismatch detection that docs/ssr/head.md says outright do not exist
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). A direct self-contradiction between two pages on the same shelf, where the WRONG one is the page a newcomer reads first.

THE CLAIM. docs/ssr/glossary.md:39, entry "head model":
    "a pure `(db, route) -> head-model` function registered with `reg-head` and named
     by a route. Derived from app-db like a sub, so it stays current on client-side
     route changes and rides the same mismatch detector as the body."

Repeated with more force at docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:64:
    "... which is why an SPA route change after load keeps `<title>` and `<meta>`
     current with ZERO EXTRA WIRING, and why the head rides the SAME mismatch
     detector as the body."

THE TRUTH, from the recipe page the glossary links to:
  - docs/ssr/head.md:60-63 -- "**Keeping the document head current is the app''s job.** There is no DOM-head reconciler in v1. The first byte carries the server-rendered head; refreshing `<title>` / `<meta>` on an SPA route change needs an app- or host-level head manager." That is precisely the "extra wiring" coming-from-nextjs.md says is zero.
  - docs/ssr/head.md:56-58 -- "The bundled runtime compares only the body hash; it ships **no** automatic head comparison. The head *model* is reconstructible, so a host that wants the check recomputes `(rf/active-head frame-id)` ... itself -- that wiring is the host''s, not automatic."
  - head.md''s own troubleshooting table says it twice more: "SPA route change leaves stale `<title>` | No automatic DOM-head reconciler in v1" and "Expecting automatic head-hash compare | Runtime compares body `:rf/render-hash` only".
  - spec/011-SSR.md:1547 is normative: the head rides its own separate `:rf/head-hash` channel, and head-mismatch attribution by the runtime "remains a post-v1 follow-on".

So the two claims are not merely imprecise -- they are the two things head.md exists to warn against, and a reader who trusts the glossary ships an SPA with a permanently stale `<title>`.

ONE MORE ON THE SAME PAGE, worth fixing in the same pass:
docs/ssr/head.md:76 troubleshooting row -- "| Path put in route metadata | Route never matches as expected | Path is the **third** positional arg of `reg-route`, not a metadata key |". The stated consequence is wrong: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:455-465 throws `:rf.error/route-bad-metadata` when `(contains? metadata :path)`, so the route never REGISTERS -- a hard throw at registration, not a silent match failure. docs/routing/concepts.md:62 and docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:40 state this correctly; head.md is the drifted copy.

ACCEPTANCE

title: Two install snippets give :local/root paths only valid inside the monorepo, and the corpus's one broken internal link
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). Two small, independently verified defects, bundled because both are one-line fixes and neither justifies its own bead.

A. :local/root PATHS THAT CANNOT RESOLVE FROM A CONSUMER PROJECT
  - docs/xray/01-installation.md:14 -- `{day8/re-frame2-xray {:local/root "tools/xray"}}`
  - docs/story/index.md:107 -- `{day8/re-frame2-story {:local/root "tools/story"}}`
An external consumer''s deps.edn is not at the re-frame2 repo root, so both paths fail dependency resolution. Both pages are otherwise honest about pre-alpha status (01-installation.md:17 -- "When Xray is published, this becomes a normal Maven coordinate. Keep it in a dev-only alias.") -- the defect is purely the path.

Two exemplars in the same corpus already get it right and are the fix:
  - docs/resources/tutorial/index.md:66-68 -- `day8/re-frame2-xray {:local/root "../re-frame2/tools/xray"}` inside a :dev alias, with the sibling-checkout convention spelled out at :35-40.
  - docs/core/freehand/install.md:19-20 -- `{:local/root "../re-frame2/implementation/freehand"}`.

B. THE ONLY BROKEN INTERNAL LINK IN 434 TRACKED .md FILES
skills/reagent-migration/references/procedure.md:14 -- "route to [`re-frame-migration`](../re-frame-migration) and come back only when that is done."
From skills/reagent-migration/references/ that resolves to skills/reagent-migration/re-frame-migration, which does not exist. Correct target is ../../re-frame-migration.
Worth fixing because it is a ROUTING instruction inside a skill: an agent told to "route to" a path that does not resolve has nowhere to go. (A full relative-link resolver over all 434 files -- mkdocs .md, directory-index and anchor-stripped forms -- returned this one hit and nothing else, so the corpus is otherwise link-clean.)

ACCEPTANCE
1. Both install snippets use the sibling-checkout form the resources tutorial and the Freehand install page already use.
2. procedure.md:14 resolves.
3. mkdocs build --strict and the README-link / doc-slug gates green.

description:

rf2-dn6v7 fixed ONE instance: a .cljc test file whose ns ended in a plain -test, so the shadow-cljs :node-test build (:ns-regexp "cljs-test$") never compiled it while the JVM runner's .*-test$ did — half-covered, and reading as covered. rf2-ezbzvm had already fixed the same class once elsewhere, which is why the bead asked whether the class deserves a gate rather than another one-off rename.

A census of implementation/ after that fix finds NINE more .cljc test namespaces with neither a -cljs-test nor a -jvm-test lane suffix:

  implementation/core/test/re_frame/router_front_of_queue_test.cljc
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/router_transducer_test.cljc
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coord_test.cljc

title: beads-checkpoint still commits memory-row churn alongside every real update
description: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6936 (implementation quality). The checkpoint helpers correctly compare row sets to suppress a commit when an export differs from HEAD only by memory-row order, but they then copy the raw unordered export and commit it whenever any genuine row changed. That means the normal case still carries every unrelated memory reorder. Reproduced on the first real audit checkpoint after #6936: the staged ledger showed 211 additions / 208 deletions; exact-line matching found 200 added rows identical to 200 removed rows (pure relocation), while only 11 added and 8 removed lines represented real updates. This defeats the stated no-churn purpose, makes routine ledger review opaque, and increases conflicts in the high-concurrency checkpoint path. Fix narrowly in both scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh and .ps1 by canonicalising the committed memory-row order (or preserving HEAD order for unchanged rows) before copy/add, without changing issue semantics. Extend layer 8 with a database export containing one real row edit plus shuffled untouched memories; the resulting commit must not include the shuffled rows.
acceptance_criteria: With one real tracker-row change and arbitrarily reordered unchanged memory rows, both checkpoint helpers commit the real change without reorder-only diff lines; a reorder-only export still creates no commit; sh/dash and PowerShell sibling behavior remain aligned.
close_reason: Closed

title: resources_route_prefetch_test runs JVM-only — its ns name misses the CLJS lane
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10) while mapping conformance rows to lanes.

implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_route_prefetch_test.cljc is a .cljc FILE — written to run on both hosts — but its namespace is re-frame.resources-route-prefetch-test, with no -cljs-test suffix. The shadow-cljs :node-test build selects on :ns-regexp "cljs-test$", so the CLJS lane never runs it. The JVM runner's .*-test$ picks it up, so the file looks covered and is half-covered.

What that silently costs: the three warm-mode contract arms (warm-plan-ensures-are-ownerless-cause-only-and-blocking-inert, warm-plan-branch-error-is-a-prefetch-planning-failure, warm-plan-is-a-noop-when-no-branch-contributor-declares-resources) have no CLJS unit arm. EP-0037 row 7 (prefetch isolation) therefore rests on the host-agnostic corpus fixtures plus the DOM tests for the CLJS host, with the planner contract itself JVM-only.

This is the same trap rf2-ezbzvm already fixed once elsewhere (a plain -test suffix silently excluding a CLJS half) — worth noting because it means the class recurs and a rename alone does not prevent the next one.

Fix is a namespace + filename rename to resources_route_prefetch_cljs_test.cljc / re-frame.resources-route-prefetch-cljs-test, then confirm it actually appears in the CLJS run and still passes there — a .cljc that was never CLJS-compiled may have a JVM-only assumption in it.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The ns and filename carry the -cljs-test suffix and the file is discovered by BOTH clojure -M:test in implementation/resources and npm run test:cljs. 2. All three deftests pass on both hosts (fix any JVM-only assumption the CLJS compile exposes, or state why an arm is legitimately host-specific). 3. Consider whether a cheap gate can catch the class — a .cljc under a test dir whose ns lacks -cljs-test is almost always this bug; if a gate is judged over-engineering for the number of cases, say so on the bead and skip it.
notes: Acceptance criterion 3 (a gate for the class) deliberately skipped here, per the criterion's own escape hatch. Census after this fix: NINE more .cljc test namespaces in implementation/ carry neither a -cljs-test nor a -jvm-test suffix, so the class does recur and the gate itself is cheap — but each of the nine needs a per-file ruling (silently half-covered vs. legitimately JVM-only and wanting an explicit suffix), which is a different size of change from one rename. Filed as rf2-lgozq with the roster enumerated. Both-lane proof in PR #6946: JVM 704 tests/6613 assertions exit 0; CLJS 11237 tests/56369 assertions exit 0, with all three deftest vars present in re_frame.resources_route_prefetch_cljs_test.js in the node-test build.

title: EP-0037 row 9's :query-retain migration completeness has no mechanical gate
description:

title: SSR guides never document the route-entry-denial 403 floor
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10). Filed rather than patched — SSR docs, not routing's surface.

EP-0037 R4 made a server-frame entry denial stamp a default 403 BEFORE the denial event drains, with a defined supersession rule: the application handler may replace it with the canonical :rf.server/redirect (by redirect precedence) or set another status explicitly, and if it establishes neither, the protected route stays uncommitted and no resource or hydration data for the denied target is produced. spec/011-SSR.md:1500-1511 is normative on all of it, and the R6 proof exercises all three arms end to end.

The routing pages advertise it — docs/routing/concepts.md:525, docs/routing/glossary.md:99, and docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md:57 ('Under SSR the same refusal renders the shell under a 403'). The SSR guide tree does not: git grep over docs/ssr/ for 'denial|denied|can-enter' returns ZERO hits, and 403 appears once, incidentally.

That leaves the gap in the worst place. docs/ssr/response.md:14-22, 42-47 and 70-80 enumerate every :rf.server/* effect, the multiple-status policy and redirect truncation — every status the APPLICATION can write, and not the one the FRAMEWORK writes on its behalf. docs/ssr/concepts.md:310 presents 401/403 purely as something 'you register your own projector to add', which now reads as wrong for the routing case.

This is a gap, not a contradiction: nothing in docs/ssr/ states anything false. The fix is a short passage in docs/ssr/response.md (the framework-stamped 403 floor, and the two ways an application supersedes it) plus a correction to the concepts.md framing, cross-referenced to spec/011-SSR.md and docs/routing/how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md rather than restating the routing contract.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/ssr/response.md documents the framework-stamped 403 entry-denial floor alongside the application-written statuses, and both supersession paths (:rf.server/redirect via redirect precedence; explicit :rf.server/set-status under last-write-wins). 2. It states the no-hydration-data consequence for the denied target. 3. docs/ssr/concepts.md:310 no longer implies 401/403 are exclusively application-projector concerns. 4. The routing contract is cross-referenced, not restated (no second definition). 5. mkdocs build --strict and the doc-slug gate green.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #6946 (2026-07-25). The denial-floor content is otherwise accurate, but `docs/ssr/response.md` now says “There is exactly one [status] the framework writes on your behalf.” Canonical Spec 011 contradicts that exclusivity: the built-in/custom error projector also stamps the projected public error's status into the same response side-channel (default mappings include 404/400/500; §Response storage says it is written by the seven fx and “the projector's status-stamp”; §Server error projection step 4 sets the public-error status). Reopened this exact SSR-doc owner instead of creating a duplicate. Bounded repair: describe 403 as the framework's non-error route-refusal floor, distinct from projector-driven exception statuses; keep the two supersession paths and denial data-isolation text unchanged.
close_reason: docs/ssr/response.md no longer claims the entry-denial 403 is the only status the framework writes; the projector's status-stamp is named alongside it and the two are separated by kind. title: docs/core/images.md has no replaceable-framework-default category, and now over-promises fail-loud
description:
Found by the EP-0037 R6 integrated-proof pass (rf2-kqxe6.10). Filed rather than patched — this is the core/images doc surface, not routing's.

PR #6932 (rf2-0r6q4) introduced a THIRD registration category: the framework's REPLACEABLE DEFAULT, marked with the reserved `:rf/framework-default?` key. `spec/Conventions.md:497` reserves the key. `docs/core/images.md` never mentions it — `git grep -iE "framework-default|replaceable.*default"` over `docs/`, `skills/` and `examples/` returns zero hits — and as a result the guide now over-promises:

1. `docs/core/images.md:39` — "even the default path **fails loud** on a cross-namespace `[kind id]` collision (`:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`) rather than letting load order silently pick a survivor." An application `rf/reg-event :rf.route/entry-denied` beside the framework's own no-provenance copy is exactly a cross-namespace `[kind id]` pair, and since #6932 it assembles cleanly. That IS the fix, and it is the documented auth recipe.

2. `docs/core/images.md:217` — the error table row "Two selected descriptors for one (kind, id) (different source namespaces) inside one image -> :rf.error/image-duplicate-id" needs the same carve-out. Note the surrounding invariants are still exactly true and must stay stated: two APP registrations of one framework-default id remain `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id` (order still decides nothing), and the marker is only honoured together with an ABSENT `:rf.provenance/ns`, so an app descriptor stamping the reserved key on itself is still an ordinary app registration.

3. `docs/core/images.md:303` — "One boundary is absolute: **you cannot override a framework standard**" remains true, but with only two categories on the page a reader cannot tell why `:rf.route/entry-denied` is replaceable and `:rf/set-db` is not. The distinction (STANDARD = protected, `check-standard-collision!` unchanged; REPLACEABLE DEFAULT = the framework ships a safe no-op and expects you to replace it) is the useful thing to teach, and `:rf.route/entry-denied` / `:rf.route/navigation-blocked` are the two live instances.

Keep it to the three edits plus a short third-category paragraph. This is not an invitation to restructure the images page or to introduce a precedence-tier vocabulary — #6932's own commit message is explicit that the marker is neither a winner rule nor a precedence tier.

One adjacent claim on the same page was checked and is CORRECT, so do not "fix" it: `docs/core/images.md:307` says a `reg-*` re-eval resolves fresh sealed generations and swaps them into the affected frames. The R6 proof pins that behaviour for this exact case — a `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler registered AFTER its frame was sealed still receives the denial (`a-denial-handler-registered-after-the-frame-was-sealed-still-fires`, `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/ep0037_r6_integrated_proof_cljs_test.cljc`).
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/core/images.md names the replaceable-framework-default category, cites :rf/framework-default? (reserved at spec/Conventions.md), and names the two live instances. 2. The line-39 fail-loud claim and the line-217 error-table row carry the carve-out, while still stating that two APP registrations of one framework-default id remain :rf.error/image-duplicate-id and that the marker requires an absent :rf.provenance/ns. 3. The framework-STANDARD boundary stays stated as absolute. 4. No precedence-tier or metadata-inheritance vocabulary is introduced. 5. mkdocs build --strict green.

title: Migration corpus O-8 teaches the retired :on-match-as-loader role
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while sweeping the corpus for EP-0037 (rf2-kqxe6.13, PR #6930). Reported not fixed: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md is a HOT-ZONE path outside that worker's write surface, so it wants its own sequenced dispatch.

DEFECT. migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §O-8 ("Adopt the standard routing surface (Spec 012)") step 2 says:

  2. **Move per-route data fetches into `:on-match`.** What was probably a per-route-id
     multimethod or a `route->fetch-effects` helper becomes a vector of event vectors
     on the route metadata. The runtime owns the dispatch.

That is the pre-EP-0037 role. `:on-match` is fire-and-forget ACTIVATION work: it never drives `:rf.route/transition` / `:rf.route/error`, never awaits the async work its events start, and never turns their failures into route state (Spec 012 §Per-route data loading / §Route readiness is a resource projection). A v1 app's per-route data fetches are exactly the managed page reads that belong in `:resources`, which is what drives readiness. A migration performed to this step lands the consumer on a page whose progress bar and error surface never move.

The section intro has the same shape: "re-frame2 ships a first-class routing surface (`reg-route`, `:rf.route/navigate`, declarative `:on-match` data loading)".

SUGGESTED SHAPE. Split step 2 the way the runtime does: managed page reads a v1 router fetched per route become `:resources` entries (with `:blocking?` for anything the page cannot render without, which is also the SSR wait point); genuinely fire-and-forget route-entry work (analytics, host notification, seeding UI state) stays `:on-match`. Worth adding while the section is open: `:parent` composes ancestors' `:resources`, so a shared shell read is declared once (EP-0037 R2); entry gating is `:can-enter` + a `:rf.route/entry-denied` handler rather than a hand-rolled per-event interceptor, because the guard runs in the one planning pipeline and covers every door.

Also check the skill leaves that cite O-8 (skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md row O-8, references/auto-cross-cutting.md) stay consistent with whatever the corpus says — check_skill_migration_cites.py and check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py gate that pair.

The rest of the migration corpus's routing material was checked in the same sweep and is clean: the M-20 closed keyword-rename table, M-14 (not-found required), M-29 (routing artefact), and M-60 all name live ids.
close_reason: Migration corpus O-8 no longer teaches the retired :on-match-as-loader role. Premise verified on main first (:on-match never drives :rf.route/transition / :rf.route/error, never awaits its events' async work, no route :on-error). Step 2 now splits the way the runtime does: managed page reads become :resources entries with :blocking? on what the view cannot render without (the readiness projection + the only route-owned SSR wait point); analytics / host notification / UI seeding stay :on-match, dispatched and then left alone. Section intro and the SSR step (6) carry the same correction; a closing note adds :parent composing ancestors' :resources and :can-enter + :rf.route/entry-denied for entry gating. Step numbering held at 1-6 so existing 'O-8 step N' references resolve. Skill leaves citing O-8 (breaking-changes row O-8, auto-cross-cutting, guided-handlers-state) only reference the rule's existence/type — no loader role taught, no change needed; check_skill_migration_cites + contract_drift + o1617_router_drift all green. mkdocs build --strict exit 0.
