title: Spec 009: should an event that settles no state be cheap to OBSERVE, not just cheap to run?
description:
SURVIVING FINDING from the D007 key-condition-map gate (ruled DELETE, rf2-drpa3.178). rf2-drpa3.124 found the one genuine argument against deleting the form, and it is not an event-grammar argument at all - it is an observability one. Filed here so it is not lost with the form.

THE OBSERVATION. The paved keyboard spelling puts a site on the element that fires on EVERY key:

    :on-key-down [:acme.ui.buffered/key-pressed k g on-commit ::v/key]

Typing one character into a buffered field therefore dispatches TWO events - a key-pressed that settles a no-op, then the edit. Asserted at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1183-1200.

THE COMPUTE IS NEAR-FREE, and that is not the problem. An unmatched key's handler returns {} - no :db effect at all - so nothing commits. There is no :rf.event/db-changed and not even a :rf.event/db-noop, which fires only when a :db effect WAS present and the value did not move (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1333-1346). What remains is a queue turn, an interceptor chain over an unchanged frame, and a settle.

THE OBSERVATIONAL COST IS THE REAL ONE. One dequeued event is one epoch record (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:323,1064; spec/002-Frames.md, Drain versus event). The per-frame trace ring retains 50 slots by default, one per event (spec/002-Frames.md:528), and epoch-history keeps the last 50 epochs per frame (spec/Tool-Pair.md:100). So typing twenty-five characters into one buffered field consumes an entire post-mortem window with no-op key epochs, and halves the effective reach of Xray's epoch panel, Story's outcome chips and restore-epoch!. Any keyboard-heavy application hits this.

THE QUESTION for Spec 009: should an event that settles NO state be cheap to OBSERVE, as it is already cheap to run? Candidate shapes to weigh, not a design: a retention policy that does not spend a ring slot on a settled-nothing epoch; a fold/collapse of consecutive no-op epochs at the trace surface; a tool-side filter in Xray/Story rather than a substrate change.

EXPLICITLY NOT A REQUEST TO BUILD ANYTHING YET. There is no measured application pain - this was derived from a pilot, not from a real app under real use. The house posture is trust the programmer and do not pre-emptively engineer. Reconsider when a real application shows that no-op keyboard epochs make traces materially worse, and design from those measured cases. The one thing this bead rules out is fixing it back at the listener with a second event grammar: that was tried (FH-EVENT-005) and deleted, because suppression via an exact-key map forces a control that cares about eight keys to write eight branches identical but for the key string.
notes:
RULING (2026-07-25 10:54:16 AUSEST, delegated ruling authority from Mike; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-egt43.no-op-event-observability.md folded here and deleted).

DECISION: PARK CONFIRMED, BEAD CLOSED. Build nothing now, and never in the bead's leading candidate shape. Every citation in the bead was re-verified and holds; the analysis below corrects the framing and is the mandatory starting point for any future pickup.

CORRECTION 1 - "settles no state" is the WRONG DISCRIMINATOR. The controlled field's own site is a pure forwarder: (rf/reg-event :acme.ui.field/changed (fn [_ [_ on-input text]] {:fx [[:dispatch (conj (vec on-input) text)]]})) at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field.cljc:163-165. It settles no state - no :db effect, exactly like the unmatched key - yet it is the single most causally important row in the chain: it is why the next epoch (the caller's :acme.invoice/field-edited) exists at all (pair pinned at pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1174-1175). A retention policy keyed on "settled nothing" would drop pure forwarders, delegation sites and re-dispatch shims - precisely the rows that explain why the surviving rows happened. "Settled no state" and "not worth observing" are different predicates that coincide on the unmatched-key case and diverge badly everywhere else.

CORRECTION 2 - the retention pressure GENERALISES but the remedy DOES NOT. Paved :on-scroll [:table/scrolled table-key ::v/scroll-top] and :on-pointer-down spellings exist (spec/004-Views.md:473-483) and apply the same ring pressure, but those epochs DO settle state (ordinary db-changed), so a settled-nothing policy reclaims zero slots from them. General pressure, case-specific remedy - which is the argument for the general knob over the substrate.

WORKED EXAMPLE (why the remedy underperforms the shipped knob). Filling one invoice line is about 24 epochs, 10 settling nothing: typing REF-1024 into the buffered reference field = 16 epochs (8 settling nothing; two events per key, pilot_field_cljs_test.cljc:1183-1193); Enter-commit about 2; typing 12 into the controlled quantity field = 4 (2 settling nothing, via the forwarder above); save 1-2. The ring holds 50, so one line is half the post-mortem window. Suppressing settled-nothing rows: 24 -> 14, about 1.7x, and it deletes the forwarder rows per Correction 1. Raising the retention knob to 500: 10x, one config line or two Xray clicks, and it covers scroll/pointer too. The noise is caused by per-keystroke dispatch - the paved, correct design - not by the no-ops; they are 40 percent of the noise, not the noise.

SHIPPED MITIGATIONS (all verified live):
1. Ring depth is author-configurable twice over: (rf/configure! {:trace-buffer {:events-retained N}}), default 50, plus per-frame :rf.trace/events-retained (docs/core/observability.md:156-166; spec/002-Frames.md:528); epoch history (rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth N}}), default 50 (spec/Tool-Pair.md:100). Xray exposes the ring knob live in Settings -> Buffer, writing through rf/configure! (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs:472-490, settings/view.cljs:1034-1058). An author can fix their own session in two clicks without a rebuild.
2. Read-side filtering ships: Xray persisted IN/OUT filter pills with :kind :event-id-pattern (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters/matcher.cljc:170-181, filters/persistence.cljs:104-127); suppressing high-frequency noise is the docstring's own canonical example :out [{:pattern ":mouse-move"}] (filters/persistence.cljs:36-38). Honest limit: a pill filters display, not retention - it cleans the view without extending reach.
3. The MCP filters server-side: watch-epochs pred supports :event-id, :event-id-prefix, :effects, :touches-path, :sub-ran, :render, :origin, :frame, :timing-ms, applied before anything crosses the wire.
4. An explicit per-handler escape exists: registration metadata {:rf.trace/no-emit? true} silences a knowingly-uninteresting handler while it still executes normally. It stays explicit - never inferred from state equality.
5. Counter-signal against any default-on collapse: the Xray Trace panel's stated principle is "Show every op" completeness-first (tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:41), and it already treats a no-op event's absence of rows as information rather than scaffolding (023-Trace-Panel.md:172, :235). A default collapse would reverse a considered panel decision, not fill a gap.

SUBSTRATE RETENTION (a policy that skips a ring/epoch slot for settled-nothing epochs) is REJECTED ON THE MERITS, not merely deferred: the discriminator deletes causal links (Correction 1); it buys under 2x where the existing knob buys 10x (worked example); and it breaks the one-dequeued-event = one dispatch-id = one ring slot = one epoch invariant that keeps Xray, Pair and replay histories agreeing (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:323,1064; spec/002-Frames.md:528; spec/Tool-Pair.md:92,100). FH-EVENT-005 (fixing it back at the listener with a second event grammar) stays ruled out per the bead. If a measured case ever arrives, the shape to reach for FIRST is a tool-side, default-off, one-click filter or fold in Xray (reversible; the records survive underneath) - never substrate retention.

RESIDUAL QUESTION (narrowed): is 50 the right DEFAULT ring/epoch depth for input-heavy applications? That is a default-tuning question answerable from one measured report - a one-line change, not a retention policy. Not worth holding an open bead; raise it fresh with the measurement in hand.

REOPEN TRIGGER (concrete): a real application - not a pilot - reports a debugging session that lost the epoch it needed, AND (1) raising :events-retained / :epoch-history depth did not resolve it, AND (2) the crowding events are genuinely uninteresting rather than causal forwarders. If (2) fails, the answer is a tool-side filter. If (1) fails repeatedly across apps, the answer is a larger default (one line). Separately: a benchmark attributing material dev-time overhead to observing high-frequency events reopens as "optimize trace capture / epoch assembly / ring append" - never as "erase causal units to disguise an implementation cost".

DISPOSITION: closed rather than parked open, per the rf2-5wuikc precedent - closed beads stay fully readable via bd show, everything actionable here already ships, the bead's leading candidate shape is now known-wrong, and an open park bead is a re-litigation magnet. The dossier leaned park-open with close "defensible"; the independent Codex review recommended close; the drive-to-zero posture tips it to close.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-07-25 (delegated): park confirmed and closed. Substrate settled-nothing retention REJECTED on the merits (wrong discriminator - deletes causal forwarder rows; buys <2x vs 10x from the shipped retention knob). Mitigations already ship: events-retained knob + Xray Settings->Buffer, OUT filter pills, MCP watch-epochs pred, :rf.trace/no-emit?. Residual question narrowed to default ring depth for input-heavy apps - raise fresh with a measurement. Full ruling, corrections with file:line, worked example and reopen trigger in notes.

title: Spec 012 follow-up: record :prefetch + the intent-position grammar in the Freehand route-link descriptor section
description:
Discovered-from rf2-y29wg (route-link descriptor prefetch wiring). spec/012-Routing.md is hot-zone and was fenced for that wave, so two sentences in it are now stale:

(1) Section 'The Freehand route-link descriptor' still enumerates the view's control keys as ':to / :params / :query / :fragment and :on-click'. :prefetch is now one too — it is stripped before DOM emission by both v/route-link and ui/route-link. (The GENERAL law in 'Linking from views' already states that :prefetch is a routing control key on every link surface and is stripped before DOM emission, so the behaviour is specified; only the per-descriptor enumeration is stale.)

(2) The same section should record the Freehand-specific consequence: on a link carrying :prefetch :intent, :on-mouse-enter / :on-focus / :on-touch-start become framework-owned positions and therefore carry the SAME closed callback roster :on-click carries (a plain fn, a v/handler, or nothing), rejected at render on both hosts with :rf.error/view-bad-event + :use-a-plain-fn-or-v-handler. The narrowing is CONDITIONAL on the opt-in — every other link leaves those positions as ordinary open Freehand event positions — and it is forced by the composition law the spec already states (the installed handlers compose with a caller-supplied handler, which means the framework must be able to CALL it). ui/route-link needs no equivalent sentence: a React prop is already a plain fn.

Implemented + proven in the Freehand conformance row FH-ROUTELINK-008 (spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-routelink-008.edn), which cites the '#route-plan-prefetch--warm-mode-intent-preload' anchor; once (2) lands in the descriptor section that citation may be worth re-pointing at it. HOT-ZONE: sequence, do not parallel with another spec/012 bead.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin issue-prefix rf2 into tracked .beads/config.yaml
description:
Recovery trap found while folding the rf2-4l67v dossier (2026-07-25). The tracker prefix lives ONLY in the Dolt database, not in tracked config:

  bd config list  ->  issue_prefix = rf2
  .beads/config.yaml line 9  ->  # issue-prefix: ""   (commented out)

If the Dolt database is ever lost and the tracker is rebuilt from the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl (which is the documented bd bootstrap fallback and the accepted recovery floor - see rf2-4l67v), bd init auto-detects the prefix from the DIRECTORY NAME and comes up "re-frame2", not "rf2". Every existing bead id in 2,326 issues, in 6,869 commit messages, in every PR title and every spec cross-reference is rf2-*. A mismatched prefix on rebuild would be a nasty, silent, entirely avoidable mess.

THE FIX: uncomment line 9 of .beads/config.yaml and set it to rf2. One line.

  issue-prefix: "rf2"

This is safe to dispatch. .beads/config.yaml is named in CLAUDE.md as human-authored config that is fair game to commit from any worktree - it is NOT a database-derived path, so the .beads PR-boundary guard does not apply. Do not touch .beads/issues.jsonl or .beads/metadata.json in the same PR.
acceptance_criteria: .beads/config.yaml carries an uncommented issue-prefix set to rf2. bd commands still run normally afterwards (the file is read by bd init; setting it must not change behaviour in the existing checkout, where the DB value already says rf2). No other .beads path touched by the PR.

title: B5 build lane: matched interpreted/compiled/mixed release builds + per-promotion delta + initial-mount time
description:
The evidence-lane half of B5 (bundle bytes + honest parse/compile over the
ONE mixed :freehand-release bundle) shipped in PR #6881 (rf2-drpa3.52):
re-frame.freehand.bench.b5 + b5-bundle-cljs-test, with numbers raw 744,071
/ gzip-6 220,966 / brotli 183,238 / parse+top-level-compile p50 ~17 ms.

This bead is the BUILD-LANE remainder of D021's B5 row, which is out of
the bench/evidence surface because it touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn
(HOT-ZONE, sequential):

  - acceptance #2 of rf2-drpa3.52 wants all THREE bundle shapes
    (interpreted / compiled / mixed) and the per-promotion delta. Only the
    mixed :freehand-release build exists on main today, so only it could be
    measured.
  - the initial-mount time D021's B5 row names needs the mixed bundle
    mounted in a browser; the release build has no :dev-http.

re-frame.freehand.bench.b5/workload already accepts any measured artefact,
so once the matched builds exist this reuses the same probe — no new bench
framework. Sequence after / alongside rf2-drpa3.166 (the deterministic
control-build reachability gate), which also lands shadow-cljs.edn build
entries.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AMENDED (rf2-rhg4q, 2026-07-25) on D021's own wording — the B5 row asks for 'representative interpreted, compiled, and mixed production bundles', REPRESENTATIVE not matched. So: TWO matched :browser release builds in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn differing ONLY in lowering (:freehand-release-interpreted / :freehand-release-compiled, one source in two states, same optimizations, same goog.DEBUG false), PLUS :freehand-release as the representative mixed shipped-cost artefact, deliberately NOT byte-matched to the pair. A delta needs two arms held still against each other; it never needed three. 'interpreted < mixed < compiled' is not a lowering series. 2. re-frame.freehand.bench.b5 measures all three shapes (raw/gzip/brotli + parse/compile) and publishes the per-promotion BYTE delta between the MATCHED PAIR as evidence, with the attribution stated PER ENCODING (raw exact, gzip within a handful of bytes, brotli identity-sensitive) rather than 'only lowering' across the board. 3. Initial-mount time for the mixed shape measured in a real browser. 4. Evidence only - no byte threshold, no timing gate (D021 NON-GOALS). 5. Cross-checked against rf2-drpa3.166's deterministic control-build reachability gate; the two are complementary, not the same.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6887 (2026-07-24T18:53:36Z; merge 9cdc3652e6569d22a02a9b685b63a309826cc4cb) — REOPENED this exact B5 build-lane owner; parent rf2-drpa3.52 remains the open programme owner, so no duplicate Bead was created.

COMPLETENESS: The two release build ids, three-shape measurement loop, and real-browser mixed-shape mount exist, and all byte/timing observations remain evidence-only. The load-bearing matched-build promise is not met. The three targets do not use the same entry app with only lowering varied: they use three namespaces and retain different namespaced event/sub/frame keywords, different DOM ids, different view names, and different labels. The exact advanced artefacts retain re-frame.freehand.release-app[-interpreted|-compiled]/{seed,bump,count,frame} and freehand-release[-interpreted|-compiled] strings. The reported compiled-minus-interpreted number is therefore not attributable only to lowering. It is also a whole-app delta across three promoted declarations, not D021's per-promoted-view delta. Finally, the ordinary node test skips its real arm unless all bundles happen to exist, and the standing freehand-bench workflow builds none of the three, runs neither this test nor the browser row, and retains no B5 matched/mount record. Manual PR-body numbers are not the required durable publication with provenance.

CORRECTNESS: With RF2_REVISION and GITHUB_SHA absent, the exact shipped namespace ran 4 tests / 29 assertions green while printing every matched shape as citable with :revision "unattributed-local-build". The new code repeats the provenance defect already recorded on rf2-drpa3.52 instead of closing it: a fabricated nonblank revision passes prov/defects and prov/result. The separately printed promotion-delta map bypasses prov/result entirely and omits the full result provenance shape. Each twin's result also inherits measurement-method prose hard-coded to out/freehand-release/main.js although its :artefact names a different file. The mount figure is taken from the DEBUG browser-test recompilation of a duplicated shape, not by loading the advanced mixed release artefact, so it cannot be presented as the production bundle's initial-mount cost.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: Reusing b5/measure-bundle, b5/workload, the existing browser plumbing, and the no-threshold discipline is focused and appropriate. The quality fault is duplicating two 85-line entry apps plus a third browser copy while relying only on path/digest distinctness tests; the copies already drift in variables the evidence says are held constant. WHY DECLINE RATHER THAN BUILD IT, in order of weight:

1. THE NUMBER HAS NO CONSUMER. Criterion 4 of this same bead says evidence only — no byte threshold, no timing gate — and D021's NON-GOALS bar exactly that. So a more accurate mount figure changes no decision and reds no gate. Building a serve + MutationObserver + driver harness to sharpen an unconsumed number is gold-plating by the plainest available definition, and the standing posture rules it out: pre-alpha, elegance and power, but not over-engineering.

2. THE ACTUAL RISK IS ALREADY CLOSED, BY DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN BY MEASUREMENT. The defect this criterion guards against is a reader mistaking a debug recompile for production load cost. The published record carries :subject :recompiled-shape-not-the-release-artefact plus the reason in its own measurement-method prose, so no reader of the record can make that mistake. Honesty was the goal; honesty is achieved. Precision was the means, and the means is not owed.

3. THREE INDEPENDENT DECLINATIONS IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE CRITERION, NOT ABOUT THE WORKERS. Three separate workers reached this same conclusion on their own reasoning. When three competent attempts each refuse a criterion on the same ground, the criterion is mis-specified — the correct response is to amend it, not to commission a fourth attempt hoping for a different answer. title: Retire the dead defview*/defview**/emit-defview chain in Freehand compiler
description:
Follow-up from rf2-drpa3.108 (PR #6860). That bead removed the two phantom calls (tree/view-boundary, tree/register-view!) from emit_jvm/emit-defview, but the WHOLE chain that reaches it is dead from authored code and should be retired as one clean move (same class as emit_cljs.cljc, which Mike ruled DELETE in #6789).

FINDING (established positively in rf2-drpa3.108): the live v/defview macro routes through re-frame.freehand/expand-defview -> compile-structural-view (compiled) / descriptor/declare-view (interpreted). It NEVER reaches compiler/defview* -> defview** -> emit-jvm/emit-defview. That chain is reached ONLY from tests:
  - compiler_build_jvm_test.clj (declare-view!/declare-explicit-view! helpers drive defview* purely to exercise the build-registry machinery: build/contribute-view-checked! cross-namespace view-id uniqueness, per-build isolation, incremental rebuild).

  - compiler_macro_resolution_jvm_test.clj (emit-jvm/emit-defview directly; the self-fqn rows + the new rf2-drpa3.108 adversarial test).

BLOCKER TO INVESTIGATE FIRST: build/contribute-view-checked! has exactly ONE caller — defview** (compiler.cljc). compile-structural-view does NOT call it. On a real Shadow build, view rows are harvested at compile-finish (build/harvest-view-registries); contribute-view-checked! only runs on the plain-JVM/SSR/REPL path, driven solely by defview**. So retiring defview** may ORPHAN contribute-view-checked! and its build-registry test coverage. Determine whether the plain-JVM view registry has (or needs) a live producer before deleting; retarget or remove the build-registry tests accordingly. This is a compiler.cljc + build.cljc + build-test co-edit, out of the emitter surface rf2-drpa3.108 owned.

Also fold in the residuals rf2-drpa3.108 reported but did not sweep: analyze.cljc still lowers host hooks to the nonexistent re-frame.freehand.hooks/*; root/create-root-form emits nonexistent client/create-root*; the self-fqn rule exists in emit_jvm but not emit_react. Confirm each independently (some 'named but missing' claims on that bead were false, e.g. tree/emit-static-html DOES exist).

title: Freehand JVM emitter retains two arms that name an undefined host-op var
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #6803. The PR correctly reconciled D014 by proving that Freehand has no JVM host-operation tier, but it also exposed two stale JVM emitter arms that still name one:

- implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/compiler/emit_jvm.cljc emits re-frame.freehand.tree/jvm-host-op! for the non-lazy :foreign arm and for :raw.
- re-frame.freehand.tree/jvm-host-op! is not defined.
- The v1 grammar currently refuses both node kinds before emission, so the references are unreachable today. If either node is later admitted or the emitter is called across a weaker seam, expansion fails as an unresolved symbol instead of producing an intentional Freehand diagnostic.

This is modest latent correctness/implementation-quality debt, not a reason to recreate the donor host-op abstraction. Keep the compiler honest by removing unreachable dead arms or replacing them with a Freehand-owned fail-loud mechanism at the right layer; do not widen the grammar as part of this cleanup.

Deduplication: an exhaustive all-status Beads scan found only closed rf2-drpa3.113, whose inventory mentioned the absent var but explicitly scoped unreachable emitter targets out of its compiled-browser runtime work. It is not an owner for this residue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No reachable or retained emitted form names an undefined re-frame.freehand.tree/jvm-host-op! var.
2. Grammar and JVM-emitter coverage pin the chosen treatment for :foreign and :raw so later grammar widening cannot silently expose an unresolved symbol.
3. Do not resurrect a general Freehand JVM host-operation tier or widen the v1 grammar merely to fix dead code.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6876 (worker/emitter-tail-2-174). Both jvm-host-op! arms (non-lazy :foreign, :raw) replaced with the emitter's own env/fail! after establishing the path dead via grammar/admitted-ops + check!; lazy :foreign untouched. emit-jvm-dead-arms-jvm-test pins grammar + JVM-emitter refusal + lazy arm still emitting. freehand JVM+node green.

title: F5 audit: settlement teeth — does re-frame.freehand.root's simpler teardown/claim model cover the failure windows ui/client.cljs's machinery existed for?
description:
Bounded one-shot review spawned by the rf2-12p25 ruling (2026-07-24) when rf2-drpa3.105 closed as moot. Closing .105 must NOT silently decide Freehand never needs the donor machinery that re-frame.freehand.root did not absorb.

THE UNABSORBED MACHINERY (occurrence counts freehand/root.cljs vs donor ui/client.cljs): incarnation fences 0/102, consumed-container quarantine 0/49, :tearing-down state 0/47, release-root 0/5, phase-flip 0/2, and the failed-first-mount settlement transaction. Also noted in review: root.cljs registers the root in fresh client render AFTER calling .render, and 004C carries stronger settlement language than root.cljs implements.

THE QUESTION (one bounded audit, either answer closes it on the record): does root.cljs's simpler teardown/claim model — claim-before-render (:rf.error/duplicate-root-id at 562, :rf.error/root-container-in-use at 573/628), total teardown, per-document live-root registry (437) — cover the failure windows the donor machinery existed for (mid-teardown re-claim, container reuse after a failed/consumed mount, failed-first-mount cleanup)? If yes, record that the donor machinery is donor-frozen non-work and close. If a real gap exists, file ONE narrow bug bead with a concrete failure scenario and close this.

POSTURE: do not gold-plate. This is not evidence for a macro door — either public verb kind delegates to the same lifecycle; any fix belongs in root.cljs. Do not port ui/client.cljs wholesale; the donor code remains in git history and the donor tree as reference.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded answer on this bead: either (a) root.cljs's model demonstrably covers the donor machinery's failure windows (state which check covers which window), or (b) one narrow follow-up bug bead filed with a concrete reproduction scenario. No speculative machinery ported.
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE (delivered in PR #6818 alongside the .110 fix). PER-MECHANISM VERDICT — Freehand is the INTERPRETED substrate; the donor ui/client.cljs is the COMPILED one, so most of its machinery is compiled-substrate-specific and correctly absent:
 - Incarnation fences (0/102) — SPLIT: the root-generation reaper is correct-absence (React reaps on remount, pinned by FH-ROOT-005), but the FRAME-incarnation analogue (stale root -> same-id successor frame) WAS A REAL GAP = exactly rf2-drpa3.110, now fixed. The 102-vs-0 count conflated two different things.
 - Consumed-container quarantine (0/49) — CORRECT ABSENCE: Freehands error boundary catches descendant throws before .render, so the poisoned-node path never reaches attempt! catch.
 - :tearing-down (0/47) — CORRECT ABSENCE for reachable paths: would need a layout cleanup to synchronously v/mount onto the container being torn down (pathological).
 - release-root (0/5) — CORRECT ABSENCE: unmount! already identity-guards; FH-ROOT-005 proves a superseded handle no-ops.
 - phase-flip (0/2) — MISCOUNT not a gap: Freehand HAS it in re-frame.freehand.phase/with-phase-flip.
 - failed-first-mount settlement transaction — CORRECT ABSENCE: settles a preflight RECEIPT that Freehand never creates (synchronous ENSURE+drain).
VERDICT: no donor machinery ported to guard an impossible window; the one window that provably occurs is closed by .110. This is the posture working — the simpler interpreted model is SUFFICIENT, and we did not resurrect machinery to guard windows that cannot occur.

title: Namespace-less subsections still reattribute bare Freehand root verbs to re-frame.ui
description:
@
## Observation

implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/api_md_check.clj: root-verb-kind-problems classifies a spec/API.md row named create-root / render! / hydrate-root / unmount! by BARE NAME as a re-frame.ui row. Today the Freehand rows (API.md rows ~230-232: mount, re-frame.freehand/hydrate-root, re-frame.freehand/unmount!) survive only because they happen to be written QUALIFIED.

Surfaced during the rf2-12p25 investigation and due REGARDLESS of how that wire-vs-delete ruling lands: the hazard is in the gate, not the door.

## Failure modes

A future Freehand row written bare (the natural spelling once a section header already scopes the table) would be attributed to re-frame.ui and could:
- FALSE-RED: the row is judged against re-frame.ui verb kinds (mount/create-root/render!/hydrate-root are macros there) while the Freehand door ships fns — a correct Freehand row fails the gate; or
- FALSE-GREEN: a real Freehand kind drift is checked against the wrong surface and passes.

Both directions corrupt a gate whose whole job is kind-consistency between API.md and the generated manifest.

## Fix shape

Attribute rows by their owning section/namespace context rather than bare name — or, if qualification is to be the law, ENFORCE it: a bare root-verb row outside the re-frame.ui section is loudly rejected, never silently adopted.

## Acceptance

1. A bare root-verb row in the Freehand section of API.md is either correctly attributed or fails loud naming the ambiguity — never silently attributed to re-frame.ui.
2. A regression test covers both directions (the false-red and the false-green path).
3. Existing qualified rows and the re-frame.ui section stay green unchanged.
@
notes:
PR #6819 AUDIT REOPEN (merge c981a23fa5e7d4549f77554d5be6fb77b8771f1e): the namespace fix is incomplete at an ordinary nested heading.

Deterministic proof through the shipped pure parser:
- `## Freehand views — re-frame.freehand` establishes `:section-ns "re-frame.freehand"`.
- An intervening namespace-less `### Root lifecycle` makes `parse-var-rows` replace that context with nil.
- A following bare `hydrate-root | Fn` row is therefore parsed with `:section-ns nil`.
- `root-ui-row?` defaults nil back to `re-frame.ui`; alongside the real UI row, the shipped reconciler returns `{:kind :kind-row-duplicated, :var "hydrate-root", :lines [22 5]}`. The sibling deletion/same-kind shape can still false-green.

Cause: every Markdown heading replaces `section-ns`, even when a child heading names no namespace, and nil is treated as UI for compatibility. This violates the original acceptance that a bare root verb in the Freehand section be correctly attributed or fail loud.

Bounded repair: preserve the nearest owning namespace across namespace-less descendant headings (respect heading level), or fail loud for an unattributed bare root verb rather than adopting it as UI. Add end-to-end parser cases with a namespace-less child heading for both false-red and false-green. No Markdown framework is needed.

Evidence: exact PR diff clean; all ten `ui-tree-malformed` Freehand namespaces are correctly rostered by seam; API-manifest full suite remains green at 134 tests / 310 assertions, demonstrating this is an uncovered edge rather than a failing baseline.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6838 (2026-07-24) — reopened exact section-namespace owner; no duplicate.

The heading-level inheritance is correct for a child with no code span, but `section-heading-namespace` still treats the FIRST backtick span on ANY heading as a namespace without validating what it names. A code-form API name therefore turns a semantically namespace-less descendant into a new bogus namespace instead of inheriting its parent.

Direct probe on merge c045b84c360ca8d9f8f39ff9633ba6df4bba1a3c:

    ## Compiled views — `re-frame.ui`
    ### Root lifecycle — `hydrate-root`
    | `hydrate-root` | M | advanced | ... |

`parse-var-rows` returns `:section-ns "hydrate-root"`. `root-ui-row?` then excludes the correct bare UI row and the two-sided guard reports it missing. This is a natural Markdown shape, not exotic syntax: the real `spec/API.md` already contains code-span headings for `reg-sub`, `dispatch-*`, `:rf.http/managed`, and `reg-flow`/`clear-flow`, none of which name namespaces.

Bounded correction: distinguish namespace-bearing heading spans from ordinary code spans (for example, select a namespace-shaped/known namespace span rather than blindly taking the first), then let an API-name child inherit the established parent namespace. Add direct parser cases under both `re-frame.ui` and `re-frame.freehand`. Preserve the small level-aware loop; no Markdown framework or general document AST.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6845 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6845). section-heading-namespace now distinguishes a namespace-SHAPED span (dotted a.b.c) from an API-name/keyword/wildcard span and selects the first namespace-shaped span rather than blindly the first: an API-name code-span heading (### Root lifecycle — `hydrate-root`) is namespace-LESS and its API-name children inherit the established parent namespace; a genuine dotted namespace span sets it even when not first. The level-aware inheritance loop (#6838) is unchanged. Added direct parse-var-rows cases under BOTH re-frame.ui and re-frame.freehand plus a direct classification proof over the real spec/API.md headings (reg-sub / dispatch-* / :rf.http/managed / reg-flow). Non-vacuity: each new case reds against the buggy first-span parser and passes with the fix. api-manifest suite 141 tests/334 assertions/0 fail; api_md_check -main vs real spec/API.md EXIT=0 (0 regressions). PR not merged (worker leaves merge to mayor).

title: Routed :class one-map case: exact :class plus an alias last-wins instead of composing
description:
@
## Observation

Probed on merged main during the rf2-5r1af investigation (JVM structural render):

    (tree/render [:div {:class "a" :x/class "b"}])
    ;; attrs resolve to {:class "b"} — last map entry wins; "a" is silently dropped

Two things are notable against Spec 004B (Attribute names, the alias-of-:class/:style row, ~line 503):

1. The routed slot RANKS rather than removes or composes in the one-map case. The row promises a routed :class "composes into the class string beside the .class#id sugar exactly as the exact spelling does, never replacing it" — but that text is written for the sugar+alias composition. One literal map carrying BOTH the exact :class and a routed alias is unpinned, and today it silently keeps whichever entry the map yields last.
2. Unlike the two-id pair rf2-5r1af rules on (where the structural tree keeps both keys), the class pair COLLAPSES in the tree itself — routing canonicalizes :x/class onto :class at the walk, so the tree shows one key and the author sees no trace of the dropped value. For maps large enough to become hash maps, which value survives is iteration order.

For contrast, the spread seam (v/spread-safe) resolves the same collision deterministically — owned wins — per the rf2-5r1af investigation. The direct one-map path has no stated rule at all.

## Question to settle

For one attrs map carrying the exact :class and a routed alias projecting onto the same slot (and the parallel :style case), should the walk:
(a) COMPOSE both into the class string, parity with how a routed alias composes beside sugar (for :style, a defined merge order);
(b) REFUSE, as two authored spellings of one slot — the analogue of the id-conflict guard rf2-5r1af extends; or
(c) keep last-wins and STATE it in the 004B row, so ranking is at least a documented rule rather than an accident.

## Verify first

The probe was structural/JVM only. Before ruling, reproduce across all three sites (interpreted structural walk, interpreted React walk, compiled analyzer) and confirm what the rf2-drpa3.93 routing ruling actually specifies for the one-map case — the ruling text may already imply an answer.

## Acceptance

1. Behaviour probed at all three sites, not reasoned about.
2. The 004B alias row states the one-map rule explicitly, whatever is ruled.
3. A conformance fixture row pins it (FH-STRUCT-009 tables or the fixture that owns class routing).

## Non-goals

No general aliasing framework (refused by rf2-drpa3.93 and .101); rf2-5r1af owns the id slot and is not blocked by this.
@
notes:
MAYOR 2026-07-24: NOT done by the small-gate cluster (PR #6819 did etj5i + qtch0). Two reasons it was left: (1) FENCED — the last-wins DROP lives in the compiled/interpreted folds (node.cljc dyn-attr-entry, react.cljs, analyze.cljc analyze-literal-props), all held by the compiled-emitter cluster worker; canonical-attr-key in rules.cljc canonicalises correctly, but the drop is in the fenced folds. (2) UNRESOLVED RULING — like rf2-5r1af/ll1ah (the id-conflict pair), :class collision (exact :class + an alias :class) is a taste call: COMPOSE the two classes, REFUSE the combination, or DOCUMENT last-wins. Acceptance needs a spec/004B edit (hot-zone) + a conformance fixture.

MAYOR RECOMMENDATION for the operator: COMPOSE. Unlike the id-conflict (where two ids are a genuine ambiguity with no sensible merge), two :class values have an obvious, useful merge — concatenate them, sugar-first — which is what the class grammar already does elsewhere. Composing is the low-friction, trust-the-programmer answer; refusing would cage a case with a natural resolution. Route this into the analyzer cluster (with .164/.163/5r1af/ll1ah) once compiled-emitter merges AND the operator rules compose-vs-refuse.
RULING 2026-07-24 (delegated review, same direction as rf2-5r1af): COMPOSE. When an element carries an exact :class plus an alias projecting onto the class slot in one map, MERGE the two class values (last-wins is wrong) — identically in both modes. This is not a new decision: rf2-drpa3.93 already established that :class/:style aliases route and COMPOSE; c9kus is the one-map case of that same rule, currently mis-behaving as last-wins. Distinct from the id slot (rf2-5r1af REFUSE): id is referential and nondeterministic-on-conflict, so it must be rejected; class is set-valued with an obvious, deterministic union, so it composes. Reuse the existing :class routing/compose path from .93; no new diagnostic id. Surface: analyze.cljc/node.cljc/react.cljs — sequence AFTER the emitter-parity cluster (rf2-drpa3.164/.163/5r1af, PR pending) merges, since it shares that surface.
close_reason: Delivered in PR #6847 (worker/emitter-parity-2-132). Gates green: freehand JVM 888, test:freehand 915, test:cljs 11040, test:browser 701 — 0 failures each.

title: Make mayor worktree cleanup conditional on an actual node_modules junction
description:
Relayed by the PR #6807 worker, which found it while sweeping the mayor command files for stale instructions and deliberately did NOT edit it — the bead it was working scoped to stale-line removal, and this is a hazard rather than a stale line.

.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md instructs `git worktree remove <path>` for any worktree whose PR is verifiably MERGED. It says nothing about the node_modules junction.

## Why it matters

Capture-refresh worktrees junction their node_modules into the mayor tree. `git worktree remove` follows that junction and deletes the REAL node_modules out of the mayor checkout — which has actually happened here. The recovery is an `npm install` in the mayor tree, and until someone notices, every gate run from the mayor checkout fails in a way that looks like something else.

The command file is what a fresh mayor follows literally, which is exactly the situation this failure mode needs the warning to be in.

## Scope

One clause: `cmd /c rmdir` the junction BEFORE `git worktree remove`, and never chain neutralize+remove. Do not rewrite the loop — the rest of mayor-hygiene.md is current.
notes:
PR #6825 THREE-LENS AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-24) — REOPENED exact closed source; no duplicate Bead.

The warning fixes the dangerous omission, but the literal cleanup recipe is not yet safe/usable across the worktrees it addresses:

1. It unconditionally calls `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete($p,$false)`. Not every worker has a junction. The current dedicated audit worktree is a concrete counterexample: `Get-Item implementation/node_modules -Force` reports ordinary `Attributes=Directory`, with no LinkType or Target, and the directory is nonempty. The prescribed non-recursive delete therefore throws and `Test-Path` stays True, stranding otherwise-removable merged worktrees. Use the already-recorded narrow shape: inspect the item and remove it only when it is a reparse/link (`$i -and $i.LinkType`); an ordinary local node_modules remains ordinary worktree content for the later removal path. Keep the mandatory verify-before-remove fence.

2. The literal canary `101` is already stale on this machine: the mayor checkout currently has 103 top-level node_modules entries. It also varies with the lockfile/platform/install state. Capture the mayor count before the reap batch and require the exact same count after; do not compare against a committed package count. Use a PowerShell-native count in the PowerShell-native recipe.

3. Recovery should point at the already-proven reproducible command `npm ci --prefix implementation` from the mayor checkout (rf2-jmak7 / junction-rmdir-bash-quoting-trap), rather than an unscoped `npm install`.

BOUNDED ACCEPTANCE: one conditional reparse-point check, one dynamically captured before/after count, the existing separate verification step, and the proven recovery command. Do not create a cleanup framework or rewrite the mayor loop.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6835 (branch worker/hygiene-conditional-8pcxz). Made the mayor-hygiene reap recipe safe/usable: (1) junction delete now guarded on the path being an actual reparse point ($i -and $i.LinkType) with fall-through to git worktree remove when there is no junction, verify fence only when a junction was neutralized; (2) stale committed canary 101 replaced with runtime before/after (Get-ChildItem implementation/node_modules).Count; (3) recovery now npm ci --prefix implementation from the mayor checkout. One-line diff, no loop rewrite. Gate: check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh PASS.

title: B2 publishes view descriptors into its result record, so the bench EDN needs a tag reader
description:
`re-frame.freehand.bench.runner`'s docstring says everything on stdout is valid EDN, so the same bytes are both the thing a reviewer reads and the artefact a release cites. B2 weakens that: its `:fixture` publishes `:free-plan` / `:read-plan`, and a plan entry is `[<ViewDescriptor> <mount-count>]`, so the printed record carries `#re-frame.freehand/view` tagged literals.

Syntactically that is still EDN. Operationally a consumer must supply a `:default` tag handler to read the artefact back at all, which no reader of a benchmark artefact expects to have to do — `(clojure.edn/read-string (slurp \"freehand-bench.edn\"))` throws `No reader function for tag re-frame.freehand/view`.

Reproduced on `clojure -M:bench` (14 occurrences) and on the ClojureScript lane. Pre-existing; B3 and the Node lane both publish plain data.

The plan is published so a reader can see WHICH declarations earned each verdict, and the decomposition already carries `:view-id` per line — so the fix is to publish view IDS in the plan rather than descriptors. The browser mount half builds its own plan from `b2/plan` over the same rosters and would keep doing so; only the published copy changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `clojure -M:bench` stdout reads back with plain `clojure.edn/read-string` — no `:default` handler, no tag registry.
- The same holds for `npm run --silent bench:freehand-node`.
- The published decomposition still names which declaration earned which verdict.
- A test asserts the round-trip, so a future fixture carrying an opaque host value is caught at the door rather than by a reader.

title: Correct the remaining spec/API.md defview promotion overstatement
description:
Fenced residue from rf2-drpa3.155 (PR #6785), which fixed the same overstatement in spec/004D but could not reach these sites.

## The stale claim

004D previously said promotion "changes no call site, no test, and no structural output". That is FALSE and #6785 corrected it in the spec: a declared child is a VIEW-BOUNDARY NODE in the structural tree (004B node-kind table line 132), so extracting one genuinely moves the tree. Both compiled refusals were verified verbatim in compiler/analyze.cljc — check-loop-capture! at line 1361 and the :key check at line 3604 — and the pilot records both at the extraction site.

## The two remaining sites

1. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc — the v/defview docstring.
2. docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md around line 63 — the GENERATED row, which derives from that docstring.

Because (2) is generated from (1), fixing the docstring and regenerating should carry both.

## The corrected framing to reuse

#6785 rewrote the law to LEAD WITH THE INVARIANT THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS — the CALLER is unchanged — and scoped "one line" to a body ALREADY INSIDE THE GRAMMAR. It also added the unadvertised benefit: compile-tier a11y decides WHETHER, not merely when. Match that wording rather than inventing a third phrasing.

## Deliberately NOT in scope

docs/EP/EP-0036 line 24 carries the same claim and was left alone ON PURPOSE — it is a dated decision record, and rewriting history in an EP is wrong. Do not "fix" it.

## Sequencing

Touches implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc and a generated docs/api page, which puts it in the API-MANIFEST SERIAL LANE. A docstring edit that changes a generated page must regenerate and take the empty-diff proof. Sequence against any other holder of that lane.

The edit is a docstring change that regenerates docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md, so it needs the plain-generator + empty-diff proof like any other lane occupant.
AUDIT FOLLOW-UP — merged PR #6831 (e92775c1812f20dd8fe98053d72e23b08b608cd6, 2026-07-24T07:31:01Z).

The docstring and generated docs/api row now state the promotion law correctly, but the canonical `spec/API.md` `defview` roster row still says callers, structural output, and the view's own tests do not change without the required qualification. That is the exact overstatement #6785 and this Bead corrected elsewhere: it holds only for a body already inside the grammar; taking a named extraction recovery adds view-boundary nodes and moves structural tests with the declaration.

title: Overlay pilot still documents a compiled-browser blocker that may be right for the wrong reason
description:
Relayed by the F5h virtual-table pilot (PR #6776), which corrected its OWN stale blocker claims and then found the same shape in a sibling pilot it does not own.

## The site

implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_overlay_parity_cljs_test.cljc, around line 22, still says the compiled modes browser cell is BLOCKED because "the browser runtime refuses a compiled descriptor outright".

That REASON is stale — it has been false since rf2-drpa3.113 made compiled views browser-mountable.

## Why this is P3 and not a straight correction

The sentence may be RIGHT FOR THE WRONG REASON. The overlay pilot genuinely does have a compiled-browser blocker, but it is rf2-drpa3.127 (a compiled view cannot attach a behavior, so any view that MEASURES is interpreted forever) — which IS still real. So the conclusion "this cell is blocked" may still hold while its stated cause no longer does.

That is the true-conclusion-dead-reasoning shape: a reader who checks the stated reason, finds it false, and unblocks the cell would be wrong; a reader who trusts the sentence inherits a false claim about the runtime.

## What to do

Re-run that pilot compiled browser cell against current main and determine which it is:
 (a) the cell now works -> build it, delete the claim;
 (b) the cell is still blocked, but by rf2-drpa3.127 -> rewrite the REASON to name .127 and keep the conclusion;
 (c) blocked by something else -> name it.
Do NOT simply swap the sentence for a .127 citation without re-running — that would be inheriting the conclusion rather than establishing it.

## Precedent

The F5h pilot did exactly this correctly on its own claims: rebased, confirmed the blocker was gone, and REBUILT the arm rather than only fixing the prose — recovering 6 rows that had been JVM-only plus a browser proof of promotion parity. Same standard applies here.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-07-24: HOLD until PRs #6780 and #6781 merge. This bead asks whether the overlay pilot compiled-browser cell is still blocked — and #6780 changes exactly the behaviour that determines the answer: node/classify-event now records {:rf.ui/opaque :v/event} for a whole-handler roster callback, where before an interpreted [:button {:on-click (v/event ...)}] was UNRENDERABLE on the structural host. So the cell may go from blocked to working on that merge. Re-running it before those land would produce an answer that is stale on arrival — the precise failure this bead exists to correct.
MAYOR NOTE 2026-07-24: THE HOLD IS LIFTED. PRs #6780 and #6781 have both MERGED, so the behaviour that determines this bead answer is now settled on main: node/classify-event records the MODE-NEUTRAL {:rf.ui/opaque :fn} for a whole-handler roster callback (004B cited as the authority), where an interpreted [:button {:on-click (v/event ...)}] was previously unrenderable on the structural host. Re-running the overlay compiled-browser cell will now give an answer that is not stale on arrival. Dispatchable.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6792. Outcome was CASE (c) — neither the stated reason nor rf2-drpa3.127. Running the cell found A DEFECT, NOT A BOUND: the compiled emitter handed top-layer/install! only the desired-state pair, but that install judges a declaration against the ELEMENT that made it, and a compiled element's props are written imperatively onto a JS object — so it was judging an EMPTY element. Consequence: NO COMPILED VIEW COULD PUT A POPOVER ON A PAGE AT ALL, and any declaring :on-toggle was falsely accused of not reconciling. Undetected because no compiled top-layer view had ever been mounted (compiled fixtures are structural-only; the DOM tests mount interpreted twins). Fixed by naming the needed facts once in top-layer/context-keys beside the rules that consume them, with emit_react carrying them; handlers ride as PRESENCE since reconciled? asks some?. Per the F5h precedent the arm was REBUILT, not just re-prosed: two new browser rows. The stale sentence is deleted, not re-pointed.

title: Finish the [::v/read] one-reader/one-law contract across diagnostics, named sugar, and v/event results
description:
PR #6874 ships the general shallow-scalar read door cleanly on its direct happy path, but three small joins do not obey the advertised one-reader/one-law contract.

1. `payload-value` sorts available payload keys directly. Once a payload contains both a named keyword marker and a vector read marker, a missing projection throws a raw host comparison/ClassCastException instead of `:rf.error/view-missing-payload`.
2. Named sugar bypasses `read-scalar?`. The public materializer accepts a map/host object for `::v/value`, while the equivalent `[::v/read [:target :value]]` correctly refuses it, so the two spellings are not one law.
3. In the CLJS `v/event` arm, the callback result is computed only after `payload` scans `(:event plan)` (nil for that role). A read door in the returned event vector therefore cannot be read from the live callback argument, despite the public materializer contract explicitly including `v/event` results.

Keep the correction inside the existing reader/materializer/fire seam: no second door, expression language, selector DSL, or new public API.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A named marker and its equivalent `[::v/read path]` accept the same scalar domain and reject a non-scalar with the same typed `:rf.error/view-bad-event` shallow-scalar recovery; no host object or collection reaches dispatch through either spelling.
2. When a missing projection is diagnosed from a payload containing heterogeneous keyword/vector marker keys, it remains `:rf.error/view-missing-payload` and reports available markers safely; no raw comparison/ClassCastException escapes.
3. A browser `v/event` callback returning an event vector containing `[::v/read path]` reads the current live callback argument and dispatches the scalar, matching the public "every path" contract. If this path is intentionally excluded instead, refuse it explicitly and reconcile that public promise rather than failing as an accidental missing payload.
4. JVM/public-materializer and CLJS production-path regressions cover the three joins plus the direct happy path. Preserve top-level-only substitution and the existing scalar/path grammar.
5. Add no projection form, expression/selector language, dispatcher payload arity, or public API.
notes: CORRECTION to the note above (a shell backtick ate one word): the sentence should read "fire! passes (:event plan) for the declarative arms and the CALLBACK RESULT for the :event arm".
close_reason: PR #6893 (commit ae7fd3db47). All three joins corrected inside the existing reader/materializer/fire seam -- no second door, no expression or selector language, no new public API, no dispatcher payload arity. (1) DIAGNOSTICS: available-markers orders payload keys by pr-str instead of sort, total over the heterogeneous keyword/vector marker shapes the door admits, so a missing projection over a mixed payload is the typed :rf.error/view-missing-payload with the available roster reported rather than a raw ClassCastException. (2) NAMED SUGAR: one read-projection serves BOTH spellings, so ::v/value and [::v/read [:target :value]] accept the same scalar domain and refuse map/vector/nil with the same :rf.error/view-bad-event. (3) v/EVENT RESULTS: payload now takes the event vector about to be materialized -- fire! passes (:event plan) for the declarative arms and the CALLBACK RESULT for the :event arm -- so a read door in a returned vector reads the LIVE callback argument instead of scanning nil; the :key-map arm is unaffected (its branch plan carries its own :event). Coverage: cross-host public-materializer rows for joins 1+2 and a CLJS production-path row for join 3 firing a real committed site whose v/event body returns a door, with the named-member counterpart beside it and the scalar law still binding there. Door doc reconciled in the same cut -- spec/004-Views.md rule 3 now binds both spellings, and the "every path" paragraph states the v/event-result case. All five acceptance criteria met. Gates all exit 0: freehand JVM 933/6642, npm run test:freehand 1008/5717 (the CLJS arm of joins 2+3), npm run test:cljs 11147/55896, scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS.

title: Make v/render-static work for paved-path and precompiled Freehand views
description:
## Defect

PR #6763 publishes `v/render-static`, but its fact-publication path leaves the public verb usable only for a compiled view declared in the same build.

1. The ordinary Freehand paved path is interpreted. A capability-free `(v/defview plain-view [_] [:main "plain"])` followed immediately by `(v/render-static [plain-view {}])` fails at macro expansion with `:rf.ui.compile/static-root-unproven-dependency`. The diagnostic says the just-compiled view may be stale/AOT and should be recompiled, because the interpreted `v/defview` path publishes no `{:caps :deps}` facts at all. The API docs and Spec 011 example do not require `{:compiled true}`; the section is explicitly “the Freehand paved path.”

2. The new compiled path contributes facts only to the ambient `build/view-static` index. Its `structural-manifest` still omits `:static-facts`, so `registered-view-static-facts` cannot discharge the documented cross-build/AOT fallback. A live probe of a freshly compiled descriptor reports `MANIFEST_HAS_STATIC_FACTS false`. In a fresh build context, even a capability-free precompiled view therefore becomes UNPROVEN.

Together these leave a narrow same-build/compiled-only island behind a general, ergonomic public verb. They also recreate the exact cross-build manifest hole previously fixed for donor `re-frame.ui` by rf2-uv7n6/#6624.

## Bounded correction

Give public `v/defview` one conservative, server-reachable static-facts publication story across its two modes and supported build/load contexts. A simple capability-free interpreted declaration must render without a promotion-only caller change; an interpreted body that genuinely cannot be proven may fail loudly with an accurate recovery rather than the false “recompile a stale view” diagnosis. Compiled facts must ride the registered structural manifest as well as the ambient index, using one projection so the two cannot drift. Reuse the existing small `{:caps :deps}` closure; do not introduce a general dependency graph, runtime Hiccup API, or second render verb.

## Deduplication

Searched every Bead state and the durable ledger for interpreted render-static, paved path, same-build, structural-manifest, static-facts, cross-build, AOT/precompiled, and `static-root-unproven-dependency`. rf2-uv7n6 is the closed donor precedent; rf2-drpa3.112 is closed by #6763. No open Bead owns the Freehand regression.

## Origin

Completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality audit of merged PR #6763 at merge commit `efb7f9326b8b781f1e5f8927c0bb3dd3b2566b08`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A capability-free default/interpreted `v/defview` renders through the public `(v/render-static [view props])` macro to the expected inert HTML without requiring `{:compiled true}` or another caller spelling.
2. An interpreted view with a server-reachable subscription or committed handler fails loudly without silently eliding it; genuinely opaque/unprovable interpreted code gets a truthful diagnostic and actionable recovery, not a false stale/AOT recompile message.
3. A capability-free compiled view loaded from a precompiled/AOT namespace still proves safe after the ambient `view-static` index is empty; an interactive precompiled dependency still fails with `:rf.ui.compile/static-root-requires-runtime`.
4. The compiled descriptor's registered manifest carries the same inert `:static-facts` projection contributed to the ambient index, with a focused equality/drift guard.
5. Existing same-build compiled rendering, transitive refusal, client-only fallback, literal-root, identity, and late-SSR-resolution proofs remain green; no new public verb, general dependency framework, or runtime interpreter is added.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6804 (2026-07-24) — REOPENED FOR A BOUNDED PUBLIC-CONTRACT PROJECTION RESIDUE; runtime/compiler fix remains sound.

The PR correctly made v/render-static serve interpreted views and split the no-silent-elision proof by tier, but the public API surfaces still describe the old compiled-only contract:

- spec/API.md's render-static row says every runtime capability is a :rf.ui.compile/static-root-requires-runtime BUILD error with source coordinates. An interpreted handler now intentionally passes expansion and raises :rf.error/static-render-requires-runtime at RENDER, while v/sub raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render.
- The re-frame.freehand/render-static source docstring makes the same compiled-only promise, and docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md faithfully mirrors that stale text.
- spec/API.md's public v/manifest key roster omits the newly observable :static-facts summary, even though #6804 deliberately makes the manifest its durable cross-build carrier. Spec 004D's manifest contract should agree that this is a summary over sites, not another lexical-site roster.

Current origin/main still carries all of these mismatches; later edits to spec/API.md did not repair them. Spec 011 and the new Spec 009 error row already state the shipped split correctly.

Bounded acceptance: update the source docstring and canonical API/spec rows to name the build-time compiled arm and render-time interpreted arm accurately; document :static-facts on the public compiled manifest as the server-reachable {:caps :deps} summary (not a site roster); regenerate the API mirror. No code, new diagnostic, new manifest machinery, or second render verb.
PR #6824 CROSS-REFERENCE (2026-07-24): while performing this already-owned spec/API.md render-static row repair, also remove the now-false phrase “A MACRO like the mount verbs.” On the ratified Freehand door, render-static is the lone macro; mount/hydrate-root/unmount! are runtime functions. This is wording inside the same public row and does not widen the implementation scope.
close_reason: Docs/spec residue reconciled in PR #6853 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6853): two-arm no-silent-elision contract (build-time compiled / render-time interpreted) + :static-facts {:caps :deps} manifest summary across spec/API.md (render-static row + manifest row), the re-frame.freehand/render-static docstring, docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md, and spec/004D; removed the false 'A MACRO like the mount verbs' phrasing. Prose-only; api-manifest unmoved (gen --check in sync); slug + mkdocs --strict green.

title: Promotion is documented as a one-line change but a per-row event site and metadata keys both require a refactor
description:
F5i pilot (rf2-drpa3.46) finding — DOCUMENTATION accuracy, not a defect. Both
refusals below are CORRECT and both messages are excellent.

v/defview docstring: "{:compiled true} — the one-line promotion ... Callers do
not change, structural output does not change, and the view own tests do not
change." Spec 004D says the same.

The pilot promoted a headless-table view — a plain sortable data table, about as
ordinary as an application view gets. Adding {:compiled true} produced two build
failures in succession:

1. [:th {:on-click [:ledger/sorted key]} label] inside a `for`
     "event vector [:ledger/sorted key] at :on-click captures loop binding key —
      per-row committed slots need per-row instances. Extract a keyed child view
      and pass key as a prop"
   Recovery: extract a child view. The pilot ended up extracting THREE
   (column-header, data-row, data-cell).

2. ^{:key k} metadata on a list row
     "missing :key on the for body — every list row needs a literal :key prop
      (unkeyed list items are a build failure)"
   The interpreted mode accepts the metadata spelling; the compiled mode wants a
   literal :key PROP. So the key spelling changes too.

A third difference is a genuine BONUS and is recorded here for the same
accuracy reason: the compiled tier a11y analyzer refused :on-click on a bare
<th> (:rf.ui.compile/a11y-click-non-interactive), naming both recoveries. The
interpreted twin carried the identical mistake in silence. So promotion does not
only move WHEN a mistake surfaces — for a11y it decides WHETHER it surfaces at
all. That is a real reason to promote and is currently unadvertised.

SUGGESTED REMEDY: soften the docstring/spec claim to something true — promotion
is one line for a body already inside the grammar, and a mechanical extraction
for one that is not; the CALLERS never change, which is the part that genuinely
always holds. Optionally advertise the a11y analysis as a promotion benefit.

NOT A REQUEST TO CHANGE THE GRAMMAR. The per-row-slot rule is right, the literal
:key rule is right, and the a11y advisory is right. Only the "one line" claim
overstates.

EVIDENCE: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_react_interop_compiled.cljc
(the extraction, with both refusal messages recorded verbatim at the site) and
the-headless-integration-promotes-but-not-in-one-line in the cljs-test sibling.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #6785 (27bcbd03bf). Outcome (1): the document was wrong. 004D claimed promotion 'changes no call site, no test, and no structural output'. Both compiled refusals verified verbatim in analyze.cljc (check-loop-capture! line 1361, the :key check line 3604), and a declared child is a VIEW-BOUNDARY NODE in the structural tree (004B node-kind table line 132) — so extraction genuinely moves the tree. The law now leads with the invariant that HOLDS (the caller is unchanged) and scopes 'one line' to a body already inside the grammar; added the unadvertised benefit that compile-tier a11y decides WHETHER, not merely when. Fenced residue filed as rf2-jx76g (the same claim in the v/defview docstring and its generated docs row); docs/EP/EP-0036 deliberately left as a dated decision record.

title: The only reachable React-integration host shape is a behavior, so every third-party React component needs a nested React root
description:
F5i pilot (rf2-drpa3.46) headline finding.

THE SITUATION. Spec 004 offers four host shapes for foreign UI: a qualified host
leaf (value props), an explicit React wrapper (React-owned protocols), a
registered behavior (opaque host state), and the outward bridge v/->react
(component-as-prop). Exactly ONE of the four is reachable today - the behavior.

  * qualified host leaf - `descriptor/classify-head` answers `:host` for a host
    descriptor, so the third vector head is real and total. But NO public verb
    mints one, and BOTH emitters refuse to cross one:
      tree.cljc:298   "the v1 node set carries no host variant ... lands with
                       the host-lifecycle slice"
      react.cljs:659  "the React emitter cannot cross one yet - the host
                       boundary and its three host shapes land with the
                       host-lifecycle slice"
  * explicit React wrapper - same door, same refusal.
  * v/->react - absent from the door entirely (F5c, rf2-drpa3.40).

THE CONSEQUENCE. A behavior receives a DOM NODE, not a React parent. So the only
way to put a third-party REACT component on the page from Freehand today is to
open a SECOND React root inside the node an {:opaque true} behavior owns. The
pilot does exactly that against a real @xyflow/react graph and it WORKS - the
whole React ABI crosses (value props, children, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle,
mount/unmount effects, a window listener that comes back off) and cleanup is an
exact zero.

THE COSTS, all measured rather than asserted:
  1. It is a SEPARATE React tree. No shared context, no shared event path, no
     Suspense participation, no transitions, and no SSR at all.
  2. It is ONE-WAY. The {:opaque true} rule that makes the nested root safe is
     the same rule that forbids interleaving Freehand content into the foreign
     component's children. Radix-shaped compound components and flexRender-shaped
     cell APIs need exactly that interleaving and are therefore unreachable.
  3. Teardown cannot be synchronous - see the sibling bead.
  4. :config is data, so a component value cannot travel through a use site.
     Every foreign component needs its OWN v/defbehavior registration; there is
     no generic [v/behavior {:use react-host :config {:component X}}].

WHY THIS IS THE HEADLINE. "Can I use a third-party React component?" is the first
question any adopter asks. The answer today is "yes, through a workaround that
costs a second React tree, and not at all if the component wants your content in
its children."

EVIDENCE: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_react_interop*.clj*
  - a-react-component-cannot-enter-a-freehand-tree-today (structural refusal)
  - the-react-emitter-refuses-a-foreign-component-head (browser refusal)
  - no-public-verb-mints-a-foreign-component-boundary
  - the-outward-bridge-does-not-exist-yet
  - a-nested-react-root-carries-the-whole-react-abi (the workaround, browser)
  - a-real-third-party-react-component-renders-and-releases (@xyflow/react)

All four refusal assertions FAIL the day the host-lifecycle slice lands, which is
deliberate - this pilot has to be rewritten then, not silently kept green.
notes:
RE-EXAMINED 2026-07-24 AGAINST CURRENT MAIN — THE HEADLINE IS NO LONGER TRUE. Investigation only; no code written, no PR, probe deleted, both trees clean. RAISED-THEN-LOWERED: P1 -> P3, and it is now a DOCUMENTATION bead, not a bug.

WHAT CHANGED, and the second one the bead could not have known: v/->react shipped (#6783); and PR #6762 — one day AFTER this bead was filed — added a react/isValidElement arm to the interpreted child fold at react.cljs:796. Its comment scopes it to compiled->interpreted forwarding, but THE ARM IS TOTAL: any finished React element in a child position passes through untouched into the same React tree, and the compiled tier shares it (compiled_react.cljs:200 -> fr/child-elements -> the same collect).

SO A THIRD-PARTY REACT COMPONENT ENTERS A FREEHAND TREE TODAY AS AN ORDINARY CHILD VALUE. No host shape, no verb, no nested root.

PROVEN BY REAL MOUNTS, not by reading (probe run in both node and browser lanes, exit 0, then deleted; deliberate (is false) canaries fired to prove the deftests executed rather than skipped):
 - @xyflow/react renders as a DIRECT CHILD of a Freehand [:div.flow-wrap ...] — div.flow-wrap > .react-flow matched. No behavior, no {:opaque true}, no second root.
 - ONE REACT TREE, proven by context: a createContext Provider in a Freehand view body reached a useContext consumer TWO FREEHAND BOUNDARIES BELOW IT (value "outer", not "default"). With a nested root that read "default". Shared context implies shared event path, Suspense and transitions.
 - INTERLEAVING WORKS BOTH DIRECTIONS — a Freehand view inside a foreign components React children via v/->react, and React content interleaved BACK into that views trailing children. That is exactly the Radix-compound / flexRender shape this bead reported blocked.
 - TEARDOWN IS SYNCHRONOUS: (= "" innerHTML) immediately after v/unmount!, no microtask tick. rf2-drpa3.152 cost is a property of the NESTED ROOT and evaporates on this path.
 - THE COMPILED TIER ACCEPTS IT: a {:compiled true} view holding a raw foreign element compiled, carried a manifest, and mounted (analyze.cljc :else {:op :expr} lowers it as a dynamic child).

RE-MEASURING THE BEADS FOUR COSTS: shared context/events/Suspense — gone; one-way composition — gone; nested-root teardown — gone; behavior-only reachability — moot for React components (still correct for genuinely non-React imperative widgets).

WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS:
 1. ONE REAL LIMIT, BROWSER-ONLY: the structural walk has NO React-element arm — node/collect falls to opaque-child! with :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed. So a view holding a raw React element cannot be t/render-ed or v/render-static-ed. That is the SAME POSTURE as v/->react (absent on the JVM) and precisely what v/client-only exists for.
 2. ONE DELIBERATE LIMIT, ALREADY RULED, DO NOT "FIX": the typed callback roster does not cross into a raw #js props object — (v/handler ...) there yields a Callback deftype and the foreign call site dies with TypeError. Stated at events.cljc:201-205: a roster value is not IFn on either host, so a foreign API handed one by accident fails AT THE CALL rather than silently doing the wrong thing. An author passes a plain closure.

THE REMAINING DEFECT IS THAT THE SPEC IS SILENT. Nothing author-facing says a finished React element is a legal child; spec/004-Views.md:2139 states it only in passing inside the ->react children bullet, as a fact about the walk. "Can I use a third-party React component?" — the first question every adopter asks — has a GOOD ANSWER THAT NO DOCUMENT GIVES. That is now the whole of this bead.

SEQUENCING for the doc work: spec/004-Views.md is hot-zone; spec/API.md and docs/api/** were held by the door-projections worker. PR #6803 has merged so to_react.cljs / D014 / 004D are free.

NOTE ALSO: the residual host-lifecycle slice is much smaller than this bead claimed and is NOT an adoption blocker — it is Freehand data props plus the typed callback roster at a foreign boundary, a structural/SSR arm with a declared policy, manifest visibility of the crossing, and compiled-tier prop analysis. No bead currently schedules it, though two emitter diagnostics name it by that phrase.
close_reason: DISSOLVED (verified-moot, no code needed). The React-integration blocker no longer exists: PR #6762's total react/isValidElement arm (react.cljs:796) lets a finished third-party React element enter a Freehand tree as an ordinary child value (shared by the compiled tier via fr/child-elements), and v/->react (#6783) bridges the reverse direction. @xyflow/react renders as a direct child; Radix-compound/flexRender interleaving works both ways — no host shape, no verb, no nested root. Phantom in_progress reconciled.

title: Fill Spec 004's declared theming-and-parts vacancy
description:
## Defect

PR #6760 lands the F5b pilot and closes rf2-drpa3.39, but intentionally leaves `spec/004-Views.md` §“Theming and semantic parts” as a heading plus `Lands in: F5` marker with no contract body. Spec 004 explicitly defines such an empty marked heading as a declared vacancy—meaning the surface has not yet landed in its canonical owner.

The PR notes that another worker held the hot-zone file and says the prose should land through that lane, but no open Bead owns the handoff. rf2-drpa3.5, the former theming-spec owner, is closed as superseded and says its content moved to rf2-drpa3.39/.38; rf2-drpa3.39 is now closed. The ruled D018 record and test-tier pilot remain useful sources, but neither substitutes for the normative Spec 004 contract.

## Evidence

At merge `e43a2cee62d2cc5970c5d6cd16d48a8109f81057`, only three files under `implementation/freehand/test/` were added. Current `spec/004-Views.md` lines 1331–1334 contain only the heading and landing marker. The file’s own introduction says a heading in that state is an undocumented contract and may be authored only under its canonical heading.

## Bounded Correction

Fill that existing heading from D018 and the shipped F5a/F5b evidence. State the two-plane component-library contract, semantic part compatibility, CSS/JVM/SSR host boundary, safe per-part override relationship to `v/spread-safe`, and the explicit rejection of a portable late transform seam. Link rather than duplicate detailed decision rationale and existing spread/composition laws.

This is a spec handoff, not a request for new theming runtime, public API, styling DSL, catalogue system, or additional pilot component.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6760.
acceptance_criteria:

title: D007 evidence from the first pilot: CASE A wants suppression, not prevent-default
description:
FOUND BY THE F5f PILOT (rf2-drpa3.43). D007's delete-before-release gate asks whether the closed key-condition map earns its place; the bead asked this pilot to report if it used key maps. It did not, and the reason is more useful than the answer.

WHAT THE PILOT NEEDED. Two key intents on a buffered field: Enter commits, Escape reverts. Both are expressible today as ONE registered event carrying ::v/key:

    :on-key-down [:acme.ui.buffered/key-pressed k g on-commit ::v/key]

with the handler branching on the string. Intent stays data, a structural test drives it by equality, and the JVM runs it. So CASE A does not need the key map for the reason D007 argues from — per-key preventDefault. The one preventDefault the pilot wants is form-level submission, and the existing options map already covers it: :on-submit {:event [...] :prevent-default true}.

THE COST IT DOES PAY, which D007 does not currently name. The data site fires on EVERY key. Typing one character into the buffered field dispatches TWO events — a key-pressed that settles a no-op, then the edit — and the pilot's R-A12 row asserts exactly that. D007's boundary already includes 'a missing key is a no-op'; a key map would therefore SUPPRESS the dispatch entirely for unmatched keys, halving per-keystroke event traffic on every buffered control in an application.

So the strongest CASE A argument for the key map is dispatch suppression, not browser mechanics. That is a different argument from the one in D007 and it should be weighed on its own, because it applies to every keyboard-bearing control rather than only to the ones that need preventDefault.

NOT A REQUEST TO SHIP OR DELETE. The gate is the dropdown/typeahead pilot (rf2-drpa3.44). This bead exists so that decision has CASE A's datum in front of it.

OWNING DECISION: D007.
