title: Refuse non-list #?@ branches in the Freehand compile checker
description:
## Problem

PR #6739 (merge 3d238ed9d921da95e1ec41ecd6cfd8b8cb1bd00a) makes checker-resolved sets agree with a real target reader on duplicate members and describes its oracle as an equivalence in both directions. The shared `resolve-children` splice arm still calls `(seq branch)` for any selected `#?@` branch.

A real Clojure/CLJS reader only splices a branch implementing `java.util.List` (ordinary lists and vectors). With conditionals preserved, the checker accepts a selected set or map branch, sequences it, and can report a declaration eligible even though that target cannot read the file.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a JVM-loadable `.cljc` view whose CLJS branch supplies a set to a set splice:

    (v/defview subject
      [_]
      [:div {:title (str #{#?@(:clj [:a] :cljs #{:b :c})})} "x"])

`clojure.tools.reader` with `:features #{:cljs}` refuses the set with `Spliced form list in read-cond-splicing must implement java.util.List.` Public `check/check-file` currently returns:

    [{:view-id :.../subject, :compile-eligible? true, :findings []}]

The same private probe showed a map-valued branch is also sequenced and accepted. Searches for splice-carrier, non-list `#?@`, and the reader message found no owner. rf2-drpa3.90 is different: it handles a legal map splice that the initial preserved read cannot represent; here preserve succeeds and the checker's own selector accepts a target-invalid branch.

## Expected Behavior

At the existing splice-selection seam, refuse a selected non-list branch exactly where the target reader does, using the checker's existing unreadable-source path and recovery style. Keep valid list/vector splices and unselected branches unchanged. No custom reader, general source analyzer, or new public surface is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A public `check-file` regression for the JVM-loadable/CLJS-invalid form above refuses instead of returning `:compile-eligible? true`, and an independent target reader proves the same verdict.
- Cover at least set- and map-valued selected splice branches, plus valid vector/list controls and an invalid branch that is not selected for the other target.
- The refusal names the file and target and gives the existing whole-conditional/list-or-vector recovery; source bytes remain unchanged.
- Keep the repair in conditional resolution with no custom reader, general collection validator, new diagnostic id, or public API.
close_reason: Merged via #6756.

title: DECISION: should a buffered controller diagnose a :reset-key that is the value expression?
description:
Scoped OUT of rf2-drpa3.32 (F4b) deliberately, and surfaced for a ruling rather than dropped.

ORIGIN: closed bead rf2-nzst23 listed ten pins for the reset-key spike. Pin 9 was a misuse guard — 'the dev build detects/lints (local model model)-shaped keys (key expression identical to the value expression)'. The F4b bead's own ACCEPTANCE enumerates eight pins and pin 9 is not among them, so F4b did not build it; the bead is authoritative over the brief.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY WORTH BUILDING:
- The hazard it targets is already closed structurally. :reset-key is REQUIRED and refused loudly when absent (:rf.error/view-control-reset-revision-missing), and spec/004 §The buffered controller and the reset generation states in the normative text that the value cannot be the signal. The remaining failure needs a caller to type the value expression into the revision slot deliberately.
- A RUNTIME check would compare values, not expressions, and a revision that happens to equal the value is legitimate (a content-hash baseline is exactly that). False positives on a legitimate pattern.
- An EXPRESSION-identity check is compiler work: it can only run in the compiled analyzer, so it would be a mode-asymmetric diagnostic — the shape D009 is explicit about avoiding — and it would be a substrate rule about a LIBRARY's prop names, which D017 places outside the substrate.

OPTIONS: (a) leave it — the required prop plus the spec paragraph carry it; (b) a compiled-only advisory; (c) a doc-level warning in the buffered-control guide when one is written.

RECOMMEND (a), and close this bead if Mike agrees. Filed so the ten-pin roster is not quietly reduced to eight without a record.
close_reason:
REJECTED AT TRIAGE on the posture filter (mayor, 2026-07-24), accepting the filing worker own recommendation to leave it.

The proposal was a lint that :reset-key should not equal :value. The worker that filed it also argued against it, and the argument is correct on both halves: a RUNTIME check false-positives on a legitimate content-hash revision (an author whose reset revision genuinely IS derived from the value is doing something reasonable, and a nag that fires on correct code is friction with no payoff), and an EXPRESSION check is compiler-only, which would make the rule MODE-ASYMMETRIC — the interpreted and compiled tiers would disagree about whether the same declaration is acceptable, which is precisely the class of divergence this programme has spent the session closing.

It is also not in rf2-drpa3.32 eight-pin acceptance, so nothing is left unmet by declining it.

Posture: pre-alpha, trust the programmer, no defensive ceremony. A clear fail-loud error where the contract is genuinely violated beats a lint that guesses at intent. If a real author ever trips this shape in a way that costs them time, that is evidence and it can be refiled with the evidence attached.

title: (BUG) Enforce the Freehand test signatures the API gate promises
description:
## Problem

PR #6729 enrolls `re-frame.freehand.test` in the canonical manifest and repeatedly tells programmers that a rename, a signature change, or an accidental export will turn the public-API gate red. The new JVM and CLJS negative controls cover only add/remove/rename. The generated row for each var contains namespace, name, kind, tier, owner, status, facade/runtime flags—but no arglists or arity contract.

A disposable live-generator reproduction changed `re-frame.freehand.test/render` metadata from `([form])` to `([form opts])` and replaced its root with a two-arity function. `gen/build-manifest` returned the exact same `render` row and stayed green:

`{:namespace "re-frame.freehand.test", :var "render", :tier :testing, :kind :fn, :owner "008", :status "EP-0036", :facade? false, :runtime-verified? true}`

So a supported call shape can break on either host while every gate added by #6729 stays green. That contradicts the new public docs, the namespace docstring, and the source Bead's signature-drift consequence.

## Consequence

The five-name test API is discoverable, but its ergonomic call contract is not protected as advertised. A one-argument call such as `(t/render form)` can become a runtime/compiler failure without the API boundary detecting the break.

## Smallest coherent repair

Extend the existing, already-shipped host-aware signature reconciliation used for `re-frame.ui.test` to the five `re-frame.freehand.test` functions. These five signatures are simple and host-identical; do not redesign the whole manifest, parse prose, or create a second namespace inventory.

## Deduplication

Closed `rf2-5bcdi` and `rf2-d7sso` built and hardened the analogous signature mechanism for `re-frame.ui.test`; they do not enroll the separate Freehand test namespace. Closed `rf2-drpa3.79` is the incomplete source owner addressed by #6729.
acceptance_criteria:
- A failing Freehand CLJS signature assertion names `re-frame.freehand.test` and `:freehand-test-signatures`, never ui.test or `:ui-test-signatures`.
- The existing ui.test lane still names `re-frame.ui.test` and `:ui-test-signatures`.
- Focused report tests cover at least arity mismatch plus one context-bearing non-arity problem, so every hard-coded ui.test fragment is exposed.
- The pure problem reconciler and problem shapes stay shared and unchanged; add only the smallest contextual reporting seam, with no new reporting framework.
- The focused JVM API-manifest suite and CLJS manifest probe remain green with non-zero counts.
notes:
PR #6843 chronological audit residual (2026-07-24): completeness and enforcement correctness are green, but the reused CLJS failure reporter is not generic. `freehand-test-cljs-signatures-in-sync` passes its problems to `cljs-probe/signature-report`, whose current output is hard-coded to `CLJS ui.test host-signature DRIFT`, `re-frame.ui.test`, `:ui-test-signatures`, and (for some problem kinds) “a ui.test macro”. A synthetic Freehand `render` arity mismatch reproduced that exact misleading output on current main. When the new guard bites, it directs a programmer or AI to the wrong namespace and sidecar block.

This is the exact source owner, so it is reopened rather than duplicated. Keep the repair small: give the shared reporter the surface/authority context needed to name `re-frame.freehand.test` + `:freehand-test-signatures` for this lane while preserving the existing ui.test wording for its lane. Do not duplicate the reconciler or build a reporting framework. Focused JVM signature gate remains green at 10 tests / 35 assertions; authored/applied patch IDs match and all 71 PR checks passed.
close_reason: Verified shipped in PR #6843 (merged, commit 408ede9a0e) — re-frame.freehand.test signature protection is on main; stale-open from a .beads close race.

title: Keep compiled manifest coordinates total-or-absent without rejecting wrapper-generated defview
description:
PR #6874 prevents partial manifest coordinates by refusing a compiled `v/defview` whose generated form lacks reader line/column metadata. That satisfies the issue's older refusal wording, but contradicts its later mayor triage and the current low-friction posture: a wrapper macro emitting `v/defview` is a legal, useful authoring pattern, and totality can be made honest without rejecting it.

Use the explicitly preferred simpler fork: source coordinates are all-or-nothing. When a compiled declaration has truthful file plus positive line and column, publish the existing total `{:file :line :column}` value. When the wrapper preserved no reader location, omit `:source-coord` rather than publishing a partial map or refusing the declaration. Keep direct declarations and metadata-preserving wrappers unchanged. Do not add aliases, a naming graph, fabricated coordinates, or another coordinate representation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real wrapper macro may emit a compiled `v/defview` without copying `(meta &form)`; the declaration expands and its public manifest contains no partial `:source-coord` anywhere.
2. Coordinate presence is total-or-absent: every present value has truthful `:file`, positive `:line`, and positive `:column`; an unanchored generated declaration omits the field completely.
3. Direct compiled declarations and wrappers that preserve caller metadata retain their total call-site coordinates and existing manifest contents.
4. Reconcile the manifest/source-coordinate contract and replace the refusal test with real source-file total-or-absent coverage.
5. No alias API, compiler naming graph, fabricated location, second coordinate shape, or generalized metadata framework.
notes:
WORKER STATE 2026-07-25 (branch worker/fh-compiler-cluster, commit ef23417fc3, PUSHED + verified on origin). WORK LANDED, PR OUTAGE-BLOCKED (GitHub POST /pulls returning 500; mayor will open from his side). Disposition: took fork (b) per the mayor triage -- stopped over-promising rather than building a cage. :source-coord is now TOTAL-OR-ABSENT with no third shape. site-source-coord answers a whole {:file :line :column} built from ONE reader position (the site's own when anchored, else the enclosing declaration's) and nil when neither was anchored; the halves are never mixed across positions. New with-source-coord adds the field only when there is one, so an unanchored entry omits the KEY rather than carrying nil under it -- consumers read presence, never partial-vs-missing. The expansion-time refusal in freehand.cljc and its :preserve-caller-form-metadata recovery are DELETED: a wrapper-generated compiled v/defview expands and registers exactly as an interpreted one does. Direct declarations and metadata-preserving wrappers unchanged (census + manifest-source-coord-jvm-test still pin total coords against real files). The 82-line refusal suite manifest_partial_coord_refusal_jvm_test.clj DELETED, replaced by manifest_total_or_absent_coord_jvm_test.clj which BUILDS its declaration bodies at runtime (as a wrapper macro does, so no inner form carries its own reader position) and quantifies the law over every roster entry of both an unanchored and an anchored subject. Contract reconciled in the same cut: spec/004D §The finite manifest, structural-manifest docstring, site-source-coord docstring, public v/manifest doc. No alias API, naming graph, fabricated coordinate, or second coordinate shape. Gates: freehand JVM 933/6642 0f/0e exit 0; npm run test:freehand 1008/5717 0f/0e exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11147/55896 0f/0e exit 0; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in flight at time of writing. PR body drafted at pr-body.md in the worktree (uncommitted).
AUDIT OF MERGED PR #7019 (2026-07-25T18:14:26Z; merge 6080c79215bf74c3e5048390de8bf17c60a8b849) — REOPENED.

PR #7019 correctly documents the event-site facts, but its new 004D sentence says `:sid`, `:source-coord` and `:path` are fields “every roster entry carries.” That directly contradicts this owner’s settled and tested law a few lines later: a wrapper-generated compiled `v/defview` whose declaration has no reader location is legal and every roster entry omits the `:source-coord` key.

This is not hypothetical. `manifest_total_or_absent_coord_jvm_test.clj` synthesizes an unanchored declaration containing a subscription, committed event, and crossing, then proves each populated roster entry lacks `:source-coord` while retaining `:path`; the focused suite passes 6 tests/23 assertions on the merged code. `with-source-coord` also conditionally assocs the field only when `site-source-coord` returns one.

The same settled law is still over-promised by FH-STRUCT-010’s conformance-index sentence and fixture comment. title: Add a CLJS/React B-arm so react.cljs costs are attributable
description:
Follow-up from the interpreter tuning slice (rf2-drpa3.83), recommended by its worker.

## Problem

The JVM interpreter path now has deterministic allocation counters, which is what made the 83% reduction attributable commit-by-commit. The CLJS/React path does NOT: node's `heapUsed` reports OCCUPANCY, not allocation, so a change there cannot be attributed to a measured win.

Consequently the tuning slice DECLINED several `react.cljs` candidates on principle rather than on merit — the doseq over attributes, a double `:key` lookup, void-tag ordering. They may be real wins; today nobody can prove it either way, and the posture forbids shipping unmeasured micro-optimizations.

## Outcome

A B-arm that gives the CLJS/React render path a DETERMINISTIC counter, so the same attribution discipline the JVM path enjoys becomes available there. Element-creation counts are the obvious candidate (deterministic, meaningful, already the unit the manifest/elision work uses); an allocation proxy is acceptable only if it is genuinely deterministic across runs.

## Non-goals

Wall-clock thresholds of any kind (D021: timing is evidence, never a gate). Rebuilding the B-spine harness — extend it. Optimizing react.cljs in this bead: this bead builds the INSTRUMENT; the optimizations are a separate slice once they can be measured.

## Acceptance

1. A B-arm exercises the CLJS/React render path and reports a counter that is IDENTICAL across repeated runs on an unchanged tree — demonstrate by repeated runs, not by assertion.
2. The counter DISCRIMINATES: show it moves when the rendered workload changes, so a green reading is not vacuous.
3. Registered through the existing B-spine harness, so the deterministic-gate versus timing-evidence split is enforced mechanically rather than by convention.
4. No semantic change to react.cljs.

## Note on surface

`bench/**` is a shared surface — sequence this against any other bench work rather than running it in parallel.
close_reason: PR #6730 — B1's React arm: two deterministic counters (elements, props) gated through the existing B-spine, timings + heap delta published as evidence. No change to react.cljs.

title: Make Spec 006 describe Freehand's :abandoned stable-boundary fence
description:
## Problem

PR #6718 updates Spec 006's normative body-authority fence to include commit-side evidence reads, but the same passage still says a rejected candidate returns :stale.

Freehand has one different, consistently pinned outcome: cell/commit! returns :abandoned at both currency fences; its docstring says :abandoned; FH-SUB-003 conformance fixtures expect :abandoned; and PR #6718's new re-entrancy regression expects :abandoned. The older :stale wording survived the donor-to-Freehand contract migration recorded by rf2-drpa3.20, so the normative prose now contradicts the reference implementation and conformance corpus at the exact paragraph this PR refreshed.

This is small but externally relevant to anyone implementing the specified commit protocol: two literal outcomes are presented for one rejection path.

## Outcome

Make the Freehand-owned body-authority passage use :abandoned consistently. If the :stale text intentionally describes a separate legacy donor runtime, label and separate that contract explicitly instead of letting it read as the Freehand outcome.

## Non-goals

No runtime behavior change, new status value, public API expansion, or broader rewrite of Spec 006.

## Origin

Three-lens audit of merged PR #6718.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Spec 006 names :abandoned as the Freehand commit result at both entry and final currency rejection.
2. Any intentionally retained :stale contract is explicitly scoped to a distinct runtime and cannot be read as the Freehand result.
3. Existing cell implementation and FH-SUB-003 conformance expectations remain unchanged.
4. Keep the fix documentation-only and narrowly scoped.
notes: PR #6785 audit (2026-07-24): reopened because the corrected two-point-fence section is still contradicted later in Spec 006. `Body authority across a live cell` says replacing a whole declaration needs no fence because the fresh descriptor is a different boundary and the host remounts it. Freehand deliberately does the opposite for a compatible reload: `react.cljs` caches by qualified view id, `component-for` returns the already-mounted component type, `publish-body!` advances its slot revision, and the Fiber/ViewCell survive. Only an incompatible shell-signature change earns a clean remount, as Spec 004C already states. Replace the stale paragraph with that compatible/incompatible split or a precise 004C pointer; keep this documentation-only and do not redesign HMR.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #6829 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6829). Spec 006 'Body authority across a live cell' now states the compatible/incompatible reload split correctly: a compatible reload keeps the live cell (only body revision advances) — which is why the two-point fence exists — and only an incompatible shell-signature change earns a clean remount, pointing to Spec 004C. The :stale->:abandoned wording was already corrected by PR #6785; this closes the reopening contradiction.

title: Retarget the Reagent-to-Freehand migration skill
description:
THE REAGENT-TO-FREEHAND MIGRATION SKILL step of the EP-0036 epic. Filed 2026-07-23 (Mike): the epic had no step introducing a skill that migrates a Reagent codebase to Freehand.

## What already exists

skills/reagent-migration migrates Reagent -> re-frame.ui today (it has references/, evals/, spec/ and a .claude-plugin manifest). Since Freehand ABSORBS re-frame.ui and replaces it, the natural move is to RETARGET this skill's destination from re-frame.ui to Freehand, reusing its scaffolding, eval harness and reference structure rather than authoring a brand-new skill. Do not over-build: the migration mechanics (find Reagent forms, map them, rewrite) are largely there; what changes is the TARGET API and idioms.

## Outcome

A skill that takes a Reagent codebase and migrates it to Freehand — mapping Reagent component forms, ratoms, and lifecycle onto v/defview, the non-IFn descriptor, v/sub, the event materializer, semantic controllers, host boundaries and the compiled tier. The Reagent-to-re-frame.ui path is superseded, not kept alongside.

## The hard part

The skill must teach the ACTUAL shipped Freehand API, not the target design. It also has to be honest about the mechanical-vs-judgement split: some Reagent forms map deterministically (a simple component -> v/defview), others need a human decision (a form-2 component with a closure over a ratom -> controlled props, a semantic controller, or a host boundary depending on intent). Reagent idioms that do not cross (raw ratoms through views, form-3 lifecycle) map to Freehand's replacements per the codex absorption table, not to a shim.

## Sequencing

Dispatch after the Freehand surface the skill teaches is stable — the F5 composition/integration slices and the component pilots (F5f-F5i), since the pilots are worked examples of exactly the migration targets. Coordinate with the guide bead (its sibling): the migration skill should teach the same API the guide documents.

## Acceptance

1. The skill's worked examples migrate to CODE THAT COMPILES against the shipped Freehand surface — executed, not eyeballed. State the mechanism (the skill has an evals/ harness; use it).
2. Every Freehand verb the skill emits exists in spec/API.md.
3. The skill carries ZERO rf2- bead ids in its leaves (the skill-drift gate) and no stale re-frame.ui guidance.
4. The mechanical-vs-judgement boundary is explicit: deterministic rewrites are applied, judgement cases are surfaced to the author with the options, never silently guessed.

## Non-goals

Keeping the Reagent-to-re-frame.ui path alongside the new one; a re-frame-v1-to-Freehand migration (that is a different, existing skill surface); authoring the human guide (sibling bead rf2-fby7o).

At PR head 46091b5908, spec/API.md already exported SIX re-frame.freehand.test names after #6772, including t/with-render. But references/procedure.md still says the surface has five names and teaches raw (t/render ...); spec/inputs.md repeats the five-name roster. A migrated view using MIG-02 v/sub — the common case — therefore raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render in the skill's advertised cheap structural check. The original acceptance also required worked migration output to be COMPILED through the eval mechanism; #6775 evidence lists prose, packaging, drift, docs and framework gates, but no emitted example compilation. Bounded repair: add t/with-render to the roster and wrap the state-reading structural path; strengthen one existing behavioral eval or a minimal existing-harness smoke so removing the bracket reds. Reuse current gates; no executable-doc framework.
PR #6827 THREE-LENS AUDIT RESIDUAL (2026-07-24) — REOPENED exact closed source; no duplicate Bead.

The procedure and roster repair are correct, but the claimed eval tooth is false-green. Eval 13's prompt asks only “Convert this to Freehand”; it does not ask for a structural test. The added expectation begins “If it writes a structural test…”. A response can therefore omit the test—and all use of `t/with-render`—while satisfying every expectation. Removing the bracket from the skill's generated-test guidance does not red this fixture, contrary to the PR evidence and the prior audit acceptance.

BOUNDED REPAIR: make the existing MIG-02 behavioural prompt explicitly request a structural test for the converted state-reading view and make the bracket expectation unconditional (including the needed test namespace alias/frame setup). Demonstrate the same eval fails when its answer uses bare `t/render` and passes with `t/with-render`. Reuse the current eval mechanism; do not build an executable-doc or generated-code framework. The shipped procedure/example itself is sound and needs no redesign.
PR #6831 AUDIT RIDER (2026-07-24) — append to this existing OPEN migration-skill owner; no duplicate Bead.

`skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-reject.md` still teaches that Freehand “cannot yet host a foreign React component, and cannot yet be hosted by one,” calls the inward path a “remaining declared vacancy,” and tells migrations to leave every such view on Reagent. The current skill therefore rejects migrations that the shipped low-friction path supports.

title: B5 evidence: shipped cost - bundle bytes, parse/eval, initial mount, reachability
description:
D021 measurement B5.

OUTCOME: representative interpreted, compiled and MIXED production bundles measured. Published: gzip size, parse/eval time, initial mount time, and the per-promotion delta. GATED: reachable runtime modules.

NON-GOALS: a byte-size threshold; a compilation quota.

DECISIONS: D021.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. DETERMINISTIC GATE: unused runtime modules are absent from the production bundle - proof by reachability analysis, and use the CONTROL-BUILD technique from the F3d bead rather than a naive grep. Prove the oracle discriminates a known-present from a known-absent symbol in the same build configuration first.
2. EVIDENCE: gzip, parse/eval, initial mount and per-promotion delta published with provenance for all three bundle shapes.
3. A public numerical claim is WITHDRAWN OR QUALIFIED when its cited artifact no longer supports it - proof: the report format ties each claim to its artifact.

GATES: deterministic - bundle reachability. Evidence-only: bytes and timing.

DEPENDS: B0, F3d.

The naive oracles are already known-wrong here and F3d's data-walk oracle (viewcell-elision-oracle-jvm-test) works at the EMIT tier, not over a bundle, so it does not substitute.

WHAT B5 NEEDS FIRST (a build-lane slice, not an evidence-lane bead): three :release browser builds with matched entries differing only in lowering (interpreted / compiled / mixed), a fourth CONTROL build identical to the production one but with the elision variable flipped, and a Node script measuring gzip bytes + parse/eval over the emitted files. Stand up the B1-B5 measurement harness: B1 direct lowering (same 10^3-10^4-node finite template interpreted vs compiled; p50/p95 self time, per-node cost, allocation, equal structural/browser output), B2 capability elision (cells-shaped mass mount; exact omitted-ViewCell count), B3 generated row comparison (10,000 keyed records, ~40-row window; committed/skipped rows, comparator time), B4 controlled editing under contention (typing/selection/IME with a heavy sibling dirty at 20 Hz; zero dropped input, stable caret/composition), B5 shipped cost (gzip, parse/eval, initial mount, per-promotion delta, reachable runtime modules). EVIDENCE-ONLY per D021 (docs/design/freehand/decisions/D021-performance-budgets-and-release-evidence.md): deterministic properties (equal output, zero dropped input, exact commit counts, manifest/cell elision, bundle reachability) are hard CI gates; wall-clock and byte distributions are mandatory published evidence with named baselines and revision/fixture/hardware provenance — never automatic numeric pass/fail thresholds; adverse trends need attribution + explicit disposition. Fixtures arrive with the FIRST slice that can run each workload, not as a final optimization project. Sources: docs/design/freehand/codex-design.md §8 Measurement obligations + Release acceptance; docs/design/freehand/fable-design.md §7.4.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED. D021 requires B1-B5 fixtures to arrive alongside the FIRST slice that can run each workload, not as a final optimization project, so a single W6 harness bead was the wrong shape. Replaced by rf2-drpa3.47 (the B-spine harness + provenance record + the mechanical deterministic-gate-versus-evidence split, landing early) and one bead per workload attached to its enabler: .48 (B1, after compiled selection), .49 (B2, after elision), .50 (B3, after the virtual table), .51 (B4, after the controlled-input door and buffered controller), .52 (B5, after elision).

title: Xray on React-element substrates (UIx / re-frame.ui): hiccup-capable mount or drop the preload from those template scaffolds
description: Follow-up from rf2-qgfo4. Xray's shell is hiccup (reg-view'd Reagent components); the React-hook substrates' :render slot is element-shaped, so rf2-qgfo4 made the mount verbs REFUSE there (:unsupported-substrate diagnostic + one console.warn) instead of spraying React child errors. Consequence: the :uix template scaffold ships the Xray preload + [data-rf-xray-host] + day8/re-frame2-xray dep, but UIx users get NO panel (today they got a broken mount + uncaught pageerror; now a clean refusal). Options to rule on: (a) real support — Xray already carries day8/reagent-slim; mount the shell through its OWN slim renderer (the shared frame context composes cross-substrate), BUT reg-view subscription reactivity rides the INSTALLED adapter's derived values (spine reifies are not slim reactions), so panels would render static without a reactivity bridge — needs design; (b) drop the Xray preload/host/dep from the :uix template until (a) exists, so the scaffold stops promising a devtools panel it cannot mount (tools/template surface); (c) optional hardening — a fail-loud CLJS-data guard in re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render so hiccup handed to an element-shaped render slot raises a structured diagnostic instead of cryptic React child errors. Note: the panels.cljs mount-<panel>! aggregators (internal surface) share the same hiccup-through-render shape and are NOT gated by rf2-qgfo4's fix.
notes: RULING (Mike, 2026-07-22, in chat): execute (b) + (c) NOW as one bounded worker — (b) drop the Xray preload / [data-rf-xray-host] / day8/re-frame2-xray dep from the :uix template scaffold until real element-substrate support exists (scaffold stops promising a panel it cannot mount); (c) fail-loud CLJS-data guard in re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render — hiccup handed to an element-shaped render slot raises a structured diagnostic (also covers the ungated panels.cljs aggregators' failure shape). Option (a) — real Xray-on-element-substrate support via the bundled slim renderer + a reg-view reactivity bridge — is DEFERRED behind a named demand trigger, same shape as the re-com parks: fires when a consumer demonstrably needs live Xray panels on a UIx/re-frame.ui app (or the re-com port's tooling wave demands it). SEQUENCING: dispatch after PR #6674 (W13) merges — shared tools/template surface.
close_reason: Ruled scope (b)+(c) shipped in PR #6676. (b) tools/template: the :uix scaffold no longer ships any Xray piece (preload / [data-rf-xray-host] host + CSS / day8/re-frame2-xray coord / @xyflow+elkjs npm deps, plain AND tailwind cells) — Reagent keeps full wiring, :ui unchanged; README/emitted comments note the devtools story honestly; tests pin both sides; template spec docs 001/002/DESIGN-RATIONALE §9 amended. title: setup-skill references teach the npx+:main-opts shadow collision and omit Xray's npm deps
description:
Found by rf2-b16va (2026-07-22 AUSEST). Two consumer-breaking gaps in skills/re-frame2-setup/references — the SAME two defects rf2-b16va fixed template-side in PR #6671, mirrored in the skill's copyable snippets:

That combination dies with 'Unknown option: -m' — the npx wrapper appends its own -m and clojure prepends alias :main-opts. Fix: deps-only alias (the examples/ui/minimal-counter shape + post-#6671 template shape), with the pure-JVM form documented as 'clojure -M:shadow -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli watch app'.

2. deps-versions.md's package.json block (~line 150) carries only shadow-cljs/react/react-dom, but the skill's day-one deps include day8/re-frame2-xray and its shadow-cljs.edn block wires the Xray preload — whose machine canvas compiles against @xyflow/react + elkjs npm packages. A consumer following the skill verbatim fails their first compile with a missing JS dependency. Fix: add both pins (lockstep with implementation/package.json — 12.4.2 / ^0.11.1) to the documented package.json.

NOTE: the emitted-run tier's setup-skill fixture (tools/template/test/.../emitted_test_run_test.clj) can't catch either — it harvests the :shadow alias from the TEMPLATE emission (now deps-only) and junctions implementation/node_modules (masks npm-dep omissions). title: Fence detailed view causes to the render they actually drove
description:
PR #6577 fixed a lost-update race by making `mint-commit-record!` retry its compare-and-set and include any cause folded between its pending-cause read and record publication. That prevents mechanical loss, but the chosen boundary attributes a post-render cause to the wrong commit.

`mint-commit-record!` runs only after `publish-commit!` has published the rendered capture and `connect!` has connected the cell. A movement arriving inside `*commit-publish-barrier*` therefore cannot have driven that already-rendered commit; it marks the cell dirty for a subsequent correction. The CAS retry nevertheless re-reads the new cause, includes it in the current record, and clears it. The subsequent real correction commit then has no pending cause and falls back to `:foreign-or-react`.

A deterministic current-main probe observed exactly this: the current record expanded a prior subscription span from 2→3 to 2→4 using the barrier-time movement; the cell remained dirty; after flushing/rendering that movement, the next record was only `{:cause :foreign-or-react}`. The existing interleaving test currently pins the backward attribution as success.

Retain the good atomicity property while moving the semantic boundary to the render/capture that the record describes. One bounded direction is to capture a cause waterline/snapshot with the immutable render capture, then commit drains only entries at or before that waterline; later folds remain for the next render. Coordinate with rf2-sy536's identity-aware cause storage. Do not build a general transaction/provenance system.
acceptance_criteria:
- A cause present for and observed by render N is eligible for commit record N.
- A cause folded after render N's capture (including during record publication) is not added retroactively to record N; it remains pending and appears on the correction commit it actually drives.
- Concurrent folds are never lost, even when they share an identity with an earlier pending cause.
- The deterministic JVM interleaving proof asserts both records: current attribution stays fixed, the cell remains dirty, and the next commit owns the racing cause rather than `:foreign-or-react`.
- Single-threaded CLJS behavior and canonical cause ordering remain unchanged.
- Coordinate with rf2-sy536; keep the solution DEBUG-only, bounded, and free of public API or general transaction machinery.
- Production erasure remains 60/60 absent.
notes: RESOLVED in PR #6604 (commit da7fcaf841). :pending-commit-causes is now an append-only fold vector; with-capture snapshots a DEBUG :cause-waterline; mint drains only folds at/before it, keeping later folds (incl. a barrier-race) as residual for the correction commit. :local-state moved to a commit-time flag (not render-fenced). Proof: a-subscription-folded-during-publication-is-fenced-to-its-own-commit (red->green, JVM+node). All gates green.

title: Correct presence guide CSS and current behavior claims
description:
The copy-paste CSS in docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md declares `transition: opacity 250ms, translate 250ms` only on `.toast.unmounting`, while the same page promises that removing then re-inserting a key mid-exit makes the CSS transition reverse from its current position.

That promise is false for the shown CSS. CSS Transitions selects transition parameters from the after-change style. On exit, `.toast.unmounting` supplies a transition and animates correctly. On re-entry, the class is removed and the after-change `.toast` style has no transition, so the running transition is cancelled and opacity/translate snap to the present state.

A Chromium/Playwright probe using the page's exact CSS reproduced the visible failure: midway through exit opacity was ~0.47 and translate ~4.3px; immediately after removing `.unmounting` they jumped to opacity 1 and translate none, and remained there. Moving the transition declaration to the base `.toast` rule makes both exit and interrupted re-entry animate, matching the runtime contract and prose.

While correcting this paragraph, make the inline-phase explanation precise: inline markup reads the parent/outer presence context (normally `:present`), never its own per-child phase. In nested presence boundaries it is not categorically guaranteed to read `:present`.

Keep this bounded: documentation/CSS only. Do not change presence runtime or API, and do not introduce a CSS-testing framework for one example.
acceptance_criteria:
- The worked CSS keeps transition properties on `.toast`, with only the exit target values on `.toast.unmounting`, so a real browser exits smoothly and reverses smoothly when re-entry interrupts exit.
- The reduced-motion override remains correct, and the re-entry prose matches the copy-paste behavior.
- The inline-markup wording says it observes the parent/outer context (usually `:present`), not its own child phase.
- The a11y diagnostic is described truthfully as a suppressible compile warning for provably focusable inline literals, not a hard error or absolute catch-all.
- The SSR bullet states both halves of current behavior: hydration adopts server children at `:present` without replaying enter; ordinary client-only mounts still run `:mounting` to `:present`.
- Coordinate with rf2-1kb0v's separate order-contract edit to avoid churn on presence.md.
- `python -m mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` pass.
- No runtime/API changes or new test machinery.
notes:
The independent completeness/correctness audit found two more small corrections on this same page, so they are folded into this one docs touch rather than creating competing Beads:

1. The page calls `:rf.ui.compile/a11y-presence-exit-interactive` a "hard compile error" and says the trap "cannot hide." The implementation (`compiler/a11y.cljc` report!) records a diagnostic and calls `env/warn!`; Spec 004 explicitly says all four a11y checks are suppressible warnings which never fail a build, and dynamic/spread cases are deliberately silent. Say "provably focusable inline literal emits a suppressible compile warning" and keep the extraction remedy. No severity/runtime change.

2. Current main now includes PR #6593 / closed rf2-uqe1b: hydrated server-adopted children start at `:present` without replaying enter, while ordinary client-only mounts still start `:mounting`. The guide still gives only the server half. rf2-uqe1b explicitly deferred this one-sentence doc rider; all-state search found no leaf owner. Add that sentence here.

Coordinate this page touch with open rf2-1kb0v, which already owns the separate first-appearance child-order sentence. Do not duplicate or absorb its spec/runtime-docstring/test work.
PR #6600 opened (worker/presence-guide-css-1skue). CSS fix: exit transition moved to base .toast rule (was only on .toast.unmounting → snapped on re-entry). Behaviour claims reconciled to shipped runtime: inline reads parent/outer context not own phase; a11y is a suppressible compile warning not a hard error (dynamic/spread silent); SSR bullet now states both halves (hydration adopts at :present w/o replaying enter per rf2-uqe1b; client-only mount still :mounting→:present). Left the first-appearance child-order sentence to rf2-1kb0v. Gates: mkdocs --strict + check_doc_slugs both exit 0. Docs/CSS only, no runtime/API/test-machinery.

title: Fix SSR browser testbeds to read hydration metadata from runtime-db
description:
## Problem

The runtime correctly stores hydration metadata in each frame's runtime-db at `[:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration]`, but all three live SSR browser testbeds still subscribe to the retired app-db `:rf/hydration` slot. Their showcase evidence is therefore false even though hydration itself succeeds:

- `testbeds/ssr_basic/core.cljs` keeps its advertised marker at `not-hydrated`.
- `testbeds/ssr_hydration_mismatch/core.cljs` keeps its headline hydration marker false.
- `testbeds/ssr_multi_frame/core.cljs` reads nil metadata, so its three hydrated flags, per-frame hashes, and all-distinct cross-frame proof are wrong.

The canonical JVM hydration test already demonstrates the right shape with `re-frame.subs/reg-runtime-sub`. A fresh-process reproduction using the real handler produced runtime metadata while the testbed-style app-db marker stayed false. Nearby core comments and the three READMEs still teach the old app-db path; `verify-hydration!`'s public docstring likewise calls its runtime-db slot "in app-db". The testbed READMEs also claim `npm run test:adapter-smokes` stages these SSR builds, but that orchestrator does not reference them, and ssr-basic names the wrong output directory.

This is a testbed/tooling integrity repair, not an SSR runtime or public API redesign.

## Required work

- Require `re-frame.subs` in each testbed and register its hydration query with `reg-runtime-sub`, reading `[:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration]`. Preserve frame-explicit reads in the multi-frame surface.
- Correct the adjacent source comments and all three READMEs to name runtime-db and the canonical path.
- Correct `re-frame.ssr/verify-hydration!`'s one stale "slot in app-db" phrase.
- Make each README's build/output/serve instructions match an actually supported workflow; do not claim the adapter-smoke orchestrator covers these builds unless it truly does.
- Compile all three existing shadow builds and verify in a real browser that ssr-basic flips to hydrated, mismatch exposes hydrated plus its mismatch evidence, and multi-frame shows three distinct hashes. Reuse an existing browser harness if a tiny pin fits naturally; do not invent a new framework or restore the retired broad Playwright suite.

## Boundaries

No hydration storage migration, compatibility shim, app-db fallback, recovery-vocabulary work, new public API, or general sibling-testbed sweep. Keep the repair to these three concrete SSR surfaces, their truthful guidance, and the one public docstring.
acceptance_criteria: All three SSR browser testbeds read hydration metadata reactively from `[:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration]` in runtime-db; their advertised markers/hash evidence are true in a real browser; nearby source/README/docstring prose and run instructions match reality; all three builds compile and focused SSR/docs gates pass without new runtime/API machinery.

title: presence: elide the undefined-key diagnostic traversal from production
description:
PR #6575 added a useful development warning for a presence child whose key evaluates to JavaScript undefined and is consequently dropped. The corrected React 19 premise and browser fixture are valid: JavaScript undefined produces a nil React key, whereas CLJS nil / JavaScript null is coerced to the string "null" and renders.

AUDIT FINDING: the diagnostic scan is not actually development-only. incoming-identities always evaluates count-keyless before calling the goog.DEBUG-gated warning. A freshly regenerated :advanced, goog.DEBUG=false browser bundle retains the recursive counter and executes its result-discarded call on every production presence render. This adds a second full child-tree walk solely for the narrow advisory and contradicts the intended zero-production-cost posture.

WORK: place the count-keyless traversal itself behind the compile-time goog.DEBUG branch, retain the current warning and browser behavior, and verify in the existing advanced mounted build that the residual counter/call is absent.

BOUNDARIES: one small runtime gating change plus proportional verification. No new diagnostic framework, warning lifecycle state, API, test matrix, or behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: The undefined-key warning remains in development; a production advanced build performs no keyless-diagnostic traversal; existing presence browser behavior stays green.
notes:
HOLD behind S1 (rf2-5e8zv.1, mayor 2026-07-20): touches presence_runtime.cljc/analyze.cljc which S1's lease-deletion modifies-or-deletes (presence is part of the lease vertical slice). PREMISE CORRECTION (browser-verified, 2026-07-21 01:11 AUSEST, presence-review-cluster worker). The bead's stated trigger is FALSE. Verified against React 19.2 jsx-runtime (direct probe + headless-Chromium reproduction): a CLJS-nil key VALUE — e.g. the doc example {:key (:id t)} with a toast missing :id — is coerced by jsx to the STRING "null", a valid non-nil .-key, so the child RENDERS (it does NOT silently vanish). Proof: jsx(type,props,null).key === "null"; jsx(type,props,undefined).key === null. collect-elements drops a child only when .-key is genuinely nil, which through the compiled surface requires an UNDEFINED key value (a JS-interop read of an absent property, e.g. (.-id #js {})), NOT a CLJS nil. So the 'silent vanish on nil id' scenario the bead describes cannot occur for idiomatic CLJS keys.

WHAT SHIPPED in #6575: the warn is still CORRECT defensive behaviour (goog.DEBUG-only console.warn when a presence child's .-key is nil), mirroring warn-duplicate-identities!, and now covers the genuine undefined-key case; the browser test triggers it honestly via (.-id #js {}) and is GREEN. count-keyless docstring + warn message corrected to describe the real (undefined-key) case, not the false nil-id example.

Keep as-is (shipped, green, zero prod cost) OR judge it not worth the ~15 lines and drop. Worker recommendation: keep (correct, harmless, catches a real if narrow interop footgun); reclassify the bead's title/premise to 'undefined key' rather than 'nil key'.
AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (PR #6575, 2026-07-21): REOPENED. The warning is correctly stripped, but its supposedly dev-only scan is not. incoming-identities eagerly evaluates (count-keyless 0 incoming) before entering warn-keyless-drops!'s goog.DEBUG branch. A freshly regenerated real :advanced / goog.DEBUG=false browser bundle still contains the recursive key counter and executes

Therefore every production presence render performs a second full child-tree walk solely for this narrow advisory, contradicting the bead's zero-production-cost claim. title: presence.md doc completion: worked CSS block + four missing contract truths (enter-timing, literal timeout, re-entry phase, inline-markup fence)
description:
From the adversarial presence review (Mike-directed, 2026-07-20). docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md teaches 'the animating is your CSS's job' but shows zero CSS, and omits four contract truths a copy-paste reader will hit. Every claim below was verified against source on main.

SURFACE: docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md ONLY. No overlap with rf2-b1wv9's files (mental-model/reactivity/ssr/testing/state/api pages) or Mike's live pairing worktree (events.md, introduction.md). Not hot-zone.

WORK:

1. ADD one worked CSS block immediately after the existing toast example, teaching the robust split:
   - ENTER via CSS animation on insertion (e.g. .toast { animation: toast-in 200ms ease-out; } @keyframes toast-in { from { opacity: 0; translate: 0 8px; } }) — fires on DOM insertion, immune to effect timing.
   - EXIT via the phase class (e.g. .toast.unmounting { opacity: 0; translate: 0 8px; transition: opacity 250ms, translate 250ms; }) with the example's :timeout-ms 300 >= the 250ms transition, tying back to the page's existing 'match or exceed' sentence.
   - A prefers-reduced-motion block disabling the motion.
   - One sentence on WHY enter-by-class-transition (.mounting -> .present) is the fragile spelling: the phase flip rides a passive useEffect (presence_runtime.cljc PresenceComponent, step '3. flip every :mounting entry to :present'); it usually lands after first paint so a transition usually fires, but React does not guarantee passive-effect-after-paint (sync flushes, hidden documents) — when the flip lands before first paint the browser never computes the .mounting style and the enter transition silently does not fire. animation-on-insertion sidesteps this entirely; @starting-style is the modern alternative for transition authors. Do NOT add runtime hardening (double-rAF etc.) — deliberately rejected as gold-plating (review 2026-07-20); the doc teaches the immune pattern instead.

2. ADD one sentence: :timeout-ms must be a positive number LITERAL in the opts map — a var/design-token fails compile with :rf.ui.compile/bad-presence (analyze-presence, implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc ~2600-2635 checks (number? (:timeout-ms opts)) on the literal map).

3. TIGHTEN the re-entry bullet: removal-then-reinsertion interrupts the exit and resumes at :present — the enter animation does NOT replay (:unmounting flips straight back to :present, presence_runtime.cljc reconcile; a mid-exit CSS transition reverses from its current position, which is the good behavior worth stating).

4. ADD the inline-markup fence: the phase Provider wraps each child ELEMENT, so inline literal markup under the boundary evaluates its props in the PARENT's render and provably cannot read its own (ui/presence-phase) — the phase-reading child must be a separate keyed defview (the page's toast-card shape). Note the compiler backstop: focusable inline literals fail with :rf.ui.compile/a11y-presence-exit-interactive (compiler/a11y.cljc check 4, rf2-0ufty).

THE GAP (verified on main): PresenceComponent (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/presence_runtime.cljc) necessarily starts its committed state at entries=[] (useRef init), so EVERY first client render classifies children :mounting. On the JVM the structural render yields :present (presence-phase :clj arm), so server markup carries the :present styling. Under SSR-then-hydrate the client therefore re-renders server-adopted presence children as :mounting -> (passive effect) -> :present, producing (1) a React className hydration mismatch (server 'present' vs client 'mounting') and (2) a fabricated enter transition on page load for content the user already sees. Greps confirm ZERO presence handling in the hydration path (implementation/ssr/**, implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/client.cljs) and ZERO hydration coverage in all three presence test files; the S5 conformance profile has no presence-hydration row.

Pin a multi-root fixture proving hydrated presence starts present while a client-only mount still observes mounting->present, including sibling-root isolation.' S5 closed via the .97.3 gate without it; all-open sweep (2026-07-20) found no bead owning it.

SMALLEST FIX (per the rider; no presence redesign): a small root-scoped hydration fact the boundary consults on FIRST render only — when this root is adopting server markup, brand-new keys enter as :present instead of :mounting. Ordinary client mounts unchanged (:mounting -> :present is correct there, pinned by presence_dom_cljs_test). Pin the rider's fixture: hydrated presence starts :present (no mismatch, no transition), client-only sibling root still observes :mounting -> :present, failed-sibling isolation preserved. NO transition events, no inert/reduced-motion automation, no DOM observation — the rf2-0ufty timeout-only/DOM-agnostic ruling stands.

DOC RIDER (same PR or follow-up): docs/core/re-frame.ui/presence.md's SSR bullet currently states only the server half ('the structural render yields :present'); add the client half once fixed. Coordinate with rf2-b1wv9 (guide-truth owner) to avoid churn.

title: Give managed-HTTP retry timeline honest recovery dispositions
description:
## Problem

PR #6555 correctly makes the shared Recovery schema an open keyword vocabulary. Its independent audit exposed a pre-existing producer/contract mismatch in managed HTTP:

- Spec 009's `:rf.http/retry-attempt` catalogue row promises `:recovery :retried` and says a new attempt is scheduled.
- Spec 014 describes the per-attempt timeline and also deliberately retains a terminal-exhaustion marker with `:next-backoff-ms nil`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` emits `:rf.http/retry-attempt` in both places, but neither tag map supplies `:recovery`.
- `trace/build-event` hoists `:recovery` for `:info` events only when the producer supplies it, so Xray and other consumers receive nil rather than the documented disposition.

The two emit arms are not semantically identical: the intermediate arm schedules another attempt and is honestly `:retried`; the terminal marker schedules nothing, so blindly stamping `:retried` on both would make the metadata look complete while remaining false.

## Smallest coherent repair

Keep the existing category and timeline. Stamp `:recovery :retried` on the intermediate scheduling emit. Give the retained terminal-exhaustion marker an honest existing disposition (recommended `:no-recovery`, since no further retry occurs), and update the single Spec 009 row / narrow Spec 014 wording to document the two cases. Extend the existing managed-HTTP exhaustion test to assert the intermediate and terminal recovery values, including the `:next-backoff-ms nil` discriminator.

Do not add a recovery registry, runtime validator, new public API, new trace category, policy hook, Xray special case, or generalized conformance framework. The open keyword schema is correct; this is one producer's missing/ambiguous metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every emitted `:rf.http/retry-attempt` carries a keyword `:recovery` matching what that particular attempt did.
- An intermediate retry that schedules another attempt carries `:retried`.
- The retained terminal-exhaustion marker carries an honest non-retry disposition (recommended `:no-recovery`) and remains distinguishable by `:next-backoff-ms nil`.
- Spec 009's catalogue row and Spec 014's retry timeline describe both arms without claiming the terminal marker scheduled a retry.
- Existing HTTP retry tests assert both recovery values; focused HTTP tests pass.
- No registry, runtime-wide validator, new category/API/policy, or tooling-specific handling is added.
notes:
PR #6565 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-20) — reopen the exact source owner for one bounded correctness repair; no new recovery vocabulary/API/machinery.

The normal retry/exhaustion tags are correct, but the intermediate `:recovery :retried` emit is ordered before the existing cancellation-safe backoff handoff. `maybe-retry!` emits at transport.cljc:1177-1205, then the deterministic `:maybe-retry/before-schedule` interleave can abort the request, and the backoff guard correctly prevents any fresh network attempt. The existing `abort-injected-in-maybe-retry-window-no-double-reply-no-reissue` fixture proves exactly one server hit / zero retry, yet a trace listener observes `:rf.http/retry-attempt` with non-nil backoff and `:recovery :retried`.

That contradicts Spec 009's recovery law (the field tells tools what the runtime did; `:retried` means the runtime retried and surfaces the result) and this bead's own honesty AC. A tool can currently report a retry that never happened.

SMALLEST REPAIR: emit the intermediate `:retried` disposition only at the cancellation-safe point where the timer callback has won its transition, confirmed the request was not aborted, and is about to call `run-attempt!`. Preserve the existing event/category/tags and terminal `:no-recovery`; do not add a registry, validator, category, policy hook, or new recovery spelling. Extend the existing deterministic abort-race fixture to record traces and assert that an in-window cancellation with zero reissue does not claim `:retried`; retain the ordinary exhaustion proof for the two real retries plus terminal marker. If implementation details require a nearby equivalent commit point, the invariant is simple: no `:retried` row unless attempt N+1 is actually permitted to start.

Separate normative spec synchronization remains exactly owned by open `rf2-s5wby`; do not duplicate it here. The source comments/test prose are verbose, but cleanup is not standalone work—tighten only where the fix already touches them.
AUDIT PR #6590: the new normative wording calls every nil-:next-backoff-ms/:no-recovery row a terminal-exhaustion marker where attempts are exhausted. The actual guard emits after can-retry? fails whenever attempt > 1 OR the current kind is retry-eligible. Thus attempt 1 can retry a 5xx, attempt 2 can terminate on a non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3, and still emit the nil-backoff marker before the budget is exhausted. While repairing this same retry-timeline truth seam, use the honest term terminal retry-sequence/stop marker and state its two cases: budget exhausted, or a later failure became ineligible. Align Spec 009, Spec 014, and the abbreviated API rows; pin one mixed-category sequence. This is wording + one focused fixture, not a new category or mechanism. It is folded here because this open Bead already owns honest :rf.http/retry-attempt timing and the same source/spec/test seam.
AUDIT PR #6631 — one promised proof remains. The audit addendum required a mixed-category sequence, but current tests cover only retryable-5xx exhaustion. Add ONE focused attempt-1 retryable 5xx → attempt-2 non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3 fixture: exactly one actual :retried row, then one nil-backoff :no-recovery terminal STOP before max attempts; true nearby test prose that still calls every nil row exhaustion/scheduling. spec/API.md:635 residue is ALREADY owned by open rf2-4xobm — do not duplicate it here. No new category, policy, validator, or framework.
PR #6641 THREE-LENS AUDIT CONFIRMATION (2026-07-21) — reopen the exact runtime/spec owner because its final audit addendum remains unresolved through #6646.

The tree still lacks the one promised focused proof for the non-exhaustion terminal-stop arm: attempt 1 retryable 5xx -> attempt 2 non-retryable decode failure under max-attempts 3, yielding exactly one actual :retried trace, one nil-backoff/:no-recovery terminal STOP before the budget is spent, and one final failure reply. Current tests cover attempt-1 noneligible/no marker and all-retryable exhaustion only. Add this single fixture; do not create a framework or expand the retry API.

title: Complete reagent-migration's Form-3 lifecycle decision table
description:
The reagent-migration skill calls MIG-17 the Form-3 lifecycle decision but currently classifies only mount/unmount work. It never names three supported, deployed Reagent-slim shapes: `:component-did-update`, `:get-snapshot-before-update`, and `:component-did-catch` (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md`). This matters for the upcoming re-com rewrite: re-com has ten Form-3 sites using `:component-did-update`; re-frame-10x uses snapshot+did-update for scroll restoration; audited apps use did-catch boundaries.

These methods cannot safely fall through the generic host/DOM→effect advice. Did-update needs explicit dependency/update semantics and often a library-update recipe; snapshot+did-update is a paired pre-commit/post-commit protocol with no passive-effect translation; did-catch should route to the shipped `ui/error-boundary` when its recovery/logging semantics fit, otherwise the view stays on Reagent or is redesigned.

Add a compact method-routing table and focused eval coverage, not a new migration framework. Also repair the same skill family's one current operational-truth drift: `skills/README.md` labels its verification-posture table the single source but still says reagent-migration never runs compile/tests, while the current SKILL/design/procedure (fixed by #6559 / `rf2-sbje4`) instruct it to discover and run safe noninteractive project gates. Update that one row; do not add executor machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- MIG-17 explicitly routes every supported Form-3 lifecycle key, including did-update, snapshot+did-update, and did-catch.
- Advice preserves phase, frequency, dependency, snapshot-pairing, and error-boundary semantics; unsupported equivalents are held honestly.
- At least one focused fixture/eval protects the re-com-relevant did-update decision and the non-equivalent snapshot/error-boundary paths without multiplying the framework.
- `skills/README.md` agrees with the current trust-the-programmer policy: the skill runs discovered safe noninteractive gates; the programmer retains genuinely interactive/visual confirmation.
- Existing skill docs/package/API/slug checks pass.
notes:
PR #6564 (worker/reagent-slim-form3-qs6lf): completed the FORM-3.md side only — added a compact per-lifecycle-role decision table to §6 routing every Form-3 role to its native re-frame.ui target (MIG-17), incl. the three the skill omitted (did-update, snapshot+did-update, did-catch). Aligned with catalog-judgment.md §MIG-17 + ui/error-boundary + effect [deps]/use-layout-effect. Gates green (drift/slugs/hardcoded-paths/mkdocs).

Do NOT close this bead on #6564 alone.
PR #6553 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-20), folded into this existing MIG-17 pass rather than a new wording bead. `gotchas.md` correctly removed the false claim that Reagent class unmount runs only once, but its replacement overstates the rule as "every cleanup must be idempotent" and says balanced counter decrement / stack pop / token release necessarily double-fires and corrupts. React's documented StrictMode sequence is setup -> cleanup -> setup (and a matching later cleanup), not two cleanup calls for one setup. A setup increment plus cleanup decrement, or push plus matching pop, is replay-safe and correct. The useful migration law is: setup and cleanup must be symmetric, tolerate replay, and each cleanup must release the exact resource acquired by its corresponding setup; unpaired teardown/domain actions are the bug. Clarify that small paragraph while completing the lifecycle decision table. Do not add a lifecycle framework, runtime guard, or generalized idempotency machinery.
SKILL-SIDE remainder delivered: PR #6568 (worker/skill-mig17-align-qs6lf). (1) catalog-judgment.md MIG-17 now names the 3 shapes cell-for-cell with FORM-3.md §6: :component-did-update -> dep-keyed (effect [deps...]) / subscription+Form-1; snapshot+did-update paired -> honest hold on reagent-slim Form-3; :component-did-catch -> ui/error-boundary {:fallback :reset-key :on-error}. Existing mount/unmount prose untouched (no MIG-17 rewrite). (2) skills/README.md verification-posture row reconciled to the trust-the-programmer policy (SKILL rule 6 / #6559): skill runs discovered safe noninteractive gates, programmer owns render/visual (docs-site mirror already correct). (3) 3 focused evals (did-update dep-effect / snapshot-hold / did-catch boundary). Touched no FORM-3.md/impl/ai. All gates green (skills-check, eval-docs, eval-packaging, migration-contract-drift, doc-slugs, mkdocs --strict, no-hardcoded-paths). Do NOT close on #6568 until merged.
PR #6564 CHRONOLOGICAL AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-20) — reopen the exact lifecycle-table owner; no new Bead or lifecycle API.

The table/skill/evals need one bounded truth pass because the shipped one-to-one routes do not preserve all of the phase/frequency/error semantics they claim:

1. `:component-did-update` is layout/commit-phase and excludes the first commit. Plain `(effect [deps ...])` is passive and runs on the initial mount, then only when selected deps change. Teach the small intent-based fork: combine deferrable mount/update/unmount library work into one dependency-keyed effect with matching cleanup; use dependency-keyed `react/use-layout-effect` for DOM measure/mutate work that must precede paint/removal; if behavior truly must skip the initial commit, guard that explicitly with a ref or keep Form-3. Correct FORM-3.md, the #6568 catalogue row, and eval 22 together. This matters to re-com popover geometry and dropdown selection/focus; do not invent a lifecycle abstraction.

2. Correct the same table's mount wording: class `componentDidMount` is commit/layout-phase, not inherently "after first paint, once" (and dev StrictMode may replay mount/unmount/mount). Remove "kick off a fetch" from host-effect examples because application loading belongs in dataflow. Preserve only the useful timing choice: layout effect when initial DOM/visual state must exist before paint; passive effect when deliberately deferrable.

3. `ui/error-boundary` forwards `error` but not React's `info`/`componentStack`, whereas reagent-slim Form-3 does. State that the native boundary fits only when error-only reporting is enough; otherwise hold Form-3. In the #6568 catalogue/eval, remove the false claim that a fallback view cannot dispatch—the runtime deliberately imposes no such restriction.

4. Repair the adjacent stale Summary, which currently says error boundaries have "no substitute" and require Form-3 immediately before the new table routes suitable cases to `ui/error-boundary`. Keep one clear route: native boundary when its contract fits, otherwise Form-3.

5. Complete the already-recorded cleanup-law correction: setup/cleanup must be symmetric and replay-safe, and each cleanup releases the exact resource acquired by its matching setup. Do not require blanket mathematical idempotency or claim balanced increment/decrement, push/pop, or token release is inherently unsafe.

DEDUP BOUNDARY: open `rf2-sbje4` already owns the broader migration-skill timing/example and compile-shape cleanup. Coordinate or land these small source/skill edits in the same pass if convenient, but do not duplicate that bead's framework/tooling work. A generic Markdown-table comparator is unnecessary; at most add narrow role assertions to the existing drift check if the maintainer judges them worthwhile.

title: Make epoch listener guidance frame-qualified, publication-shaped, and terminal-record accurate
description:
## Problem

The epoch listener is a publication stream, but current public/spec/tooling prose conflates event handling, ring storage, and callback publication. The precise lifecycle is:

1. A successfully-started handled event assembles and publishes one initial `:rf/epoch-record` at run-to-completion. It is retained in `epoch-history` only when the frame's configured history depth permits storage.
2. A dequeued event rejected before `:rf.event/run-start` (for example, no handler) produces no epoch record or callback. “One record per dequeued event” is therefore only a shorthand for ordinary handled events, not a universal law.
3. `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` and `:halted-depth` are nonordinary publications with no completed event run. They are ring-retained when depth permits; `:halted-depth` names the queued event that never ran.
4. `:halted-destroy` is different: it exists only when an already-dequeued event started and was interrupted by frame destruction. It is delivered to listeners and deliberately absent from history after destroy cleanup.
5. Render/sub-run/unmount backfill can publish a corrected record carrying the same identity. A callback is not an event clock.
6. The listener is process-global, while the public contract guarantees `:epoch-id` uniqueness only within one frame. Consumer identity is `[(:frame record) (:epoch-id record)]`; `:outcome` is record state, not identity.

Current consequences:

- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` and `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` overpromise ring storage, misclassify destroy halt, and recommend bare-ID reconciliation.
- `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md` describes every history record as one per dequeued event, omitting db-replace/depth-halt entries and depth-zero storage behavior.
- `spec/API.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `docs/core/observability.md`, and the #6499-edited `spec/Privacy.md` still contain universal once-per-event assembly/callback claims. The Tool-Pair worked consumer performs accumulative work and can double-count a backfill publication.
- `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md` uses bare identity and treats terminal destroy as synthetic/eventless; `tools/xray/testbeds/runner/core.cljs` promises once-per-event delivery.
- Public docstrings in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc`, and `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs` retain event-only or universal cadence wording.
- `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md` and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/observability-logging-sweep.md` retain the callback-counting mental model for programmers and AI.

This is one documentation/consumer-contract defect. The Xray collector implementation is already safe: it carries `(:frame record)` and re-reads/replaces that frame's ring snapshot.

## Scope and proportional fix

Make one bounded prose/example pass over the named live surfaces. State ordinary handled-event assembly separately from conditional ring retention and listener publication; make consumer examples replace the latest publication under `[frame epoch-id]`; and describe no-record rejection, db-replace/depth-halt, destroy-halt, depth zero, and backfill only where the surface needs that distinction. Keep concise surfaces concise and put the lifecycle matrix in one canonical spec section.

Do not change runtime behavior, add listener dedupe, introduce validation/compatibility machinery, or build a prose checker. Do not rewrite narrowly-scoped test names that make no false universal claim.

## Ownership / deduplication

Closed `rf2-69fyr` / PR #6499 fixed the old per-drain language but left the lifecycle distinctions above incomplete and introduced some overbroad per-dequeued-event wording. Open `rf2-yiwag` separately owns only the Pair preload listener/streaming comments; leave those files to that bead. Closed `rf2-3fc89f.39` fixed Pair runtime attribution and independently proves why frame-qualified identity is required; this bead changes guidance only.
design: Use a small lifecycle matrix as the canonical formulation: handled event -> one initial publication, stored only when depth permits; rejected/no-run-start -> none; db-replaced and halted-depth -> nonordinary publications, stored when depth permits; halted-destroy -> already-started event, listener-only; backfill -> replacement publication with the same `[frame epoch-id]`. Consumer examples cache by `[(:frame record) (:epoch-id record)]`, replace the value, and inspect `:outcome` as state.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every named public/spec/tooling/AI surface distinguishes ordinary handled-event assembly, conditional ring retention, and listener publication; none claims universally that every dequeued event creates a stored record or exactly one callback.
2. Cross-frame consumer guidance uses `[frame epoch-id]`; `:outcome` is described as record state, not identity.
3. The Tool-Pair worked consumer is replacement/reconciliation-shaped, so same-ID backfill cannot double-count an epoch.
4. Rejected/no-run-start events, depth-zero publication, `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, `:halted-depth`, and `:halted-destroy` are described with their real event/storage lifecycles at the canonical explanation; concise surfaces link or avoid overbroad claims.
5. The explicit inventory includes `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md`, `spec/Privacy.md`, the epoch/core/late-bind public docstrings, and Xray `install.cljs` as well as the original public/spec/tooling/AI sites.
6. No runtime/API/checker/compatibility work is added. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` pass.
7. `rf2-yiwag`'s Pair preload files remain outside this bead.
notes:
PR #6499 AUDIT INVENTORY ADDENDUM (rf2-jugsp): keep this as the same bounded prose/example correction, but explicitly include three authoritative surfaces the original inventory did not name:
- `docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md` — its `get-epoch-history` description says each ring record is one per dequeued event, omitting stored `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` and `:halted-depth` records that have no completed event run.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` (`register-epoch-listener!` docstring) — “each assembled event epoch record” is still event-only callback guidance despite backfill republications and terminal/depth-zero listener-only delivery.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs` (`register-epoch-collector!` docstring) — describes the collector as firing on each event settle, omitting same-record backfill republication and nonordinary records.

These are the identical record-commit-versus-publication defect already owned here. Correct the wording alongside the named corpus; do not add runtime dedupe, new API, a checker, or another Bead.
PR #6499 correctness lens also falsified the shorthand “one stored record per dequeued event”: a no-handler/no-run-start dequeue produces no record, depth-zero records publish without storage, and halted-depth names a never-run queued event. The description and acceptance now use the bounded lifecycle matrix rather than another sweeping slogan.
PR #6515 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6515) — docs/api only, per mayor fence. Added the three missing angles to docs/api/re-frame.core.md (epoch-history desc + Epoch-settled listeners desc + example) and docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md (module intro + epoch-history intro + register-epoch-listener! desc + example): frame-qualified reconcile on [(:frame record) (:epoch-id record)] with :outcome as record state not identity; publication-shaped example that caches-and-replaces by [frame epoch-id]; termination-aware split of :halted-depth/db-replaced (ring-retained when depth permits) vs :halted-destroy (already-started event, listener-only, never retained), plus no-handler-dequeue publishes nothing. Preserved ablz8's #6498 per-event + re-publication prose verbatim; corrected only the destroy-halt-in-history misclassification and bare-ID reconciliation the bead flags. SCOPE NOTE: the mayor fenced this to the 2 api docs; the bead's broader inventory (spec/API.md, 009-Instrumentation.md, Tool-Pair.md, Privacy.md, docs/xray/api/runtime-seam.md, docs/core/observability.md, epoch/core/late-bind docstrings, tools/xray install.cljs, skills, migration) was NOT touched here and remains for follow-up beads. Gates: mkdocs build --strict exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. guide-truth JVM test N/A (pins docs/core+spec, not these api docs).
PR #6515 AUDIT REOPEN ADDENDUM (rf2-bp6pi, 2026-07-20): the main frame/publication/termination correction is sound, but two bounded API-page residuals remain.

1. CONDITIONAL RETENTION / DEPTH ZERO. `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md`'s introduction and Epoch-history summary still say every handled event is recorded into the ring. Runtime `state/record!` stores only while `:depth` is positive, while the listener fan continues at depth 0; the existing `depth-zero-still-fires-listeners` test proves two publications with an empty ring. Qualify the API summaries: handled events assemble/publish, records are retained only when configured depth permits, and `:depth 0` is listener-only rather than disabling publication. Keep the detailed no-handler, db-replaced, halted-depth, and listener-only halted-destroy distinctions concise/link-based; do not add another matrix.

2. COPYABLE REPLACEMENT EXAMPLE. The worked block in `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` first registers the replacement-shaped cache under `:my-app/epoch-watch`, then executes the “equivalent” direct namespace registration under the SAME id. By the documented same-id replacement law, copying the whole block immediately disables the cache it just demonstrated. Keep one executable cache registration; make the direct spelling a non-executed alternative or omit it.

ACCEPTANCE: reconcile the two API pages only; preserve `[frame epoch-id]` replacement and all current lifecycle truth; no runtime/API/test/checker/framework/general sweep. Existing epoch proof plus doc slug/MkDocs gates are sufficient.

title: Reconcile Xray filter-seed docs with the shipped boot baseline
