title: Align custom-element contract prose with the implemented law
description:
## Problem
PR #6475 changed the custom-element law from one canonical owner to a set of equal declarers and changed the dev/JVM authority path, but the normative and programmer-facing prose still teaches the old design. Spec 009 says a source always replaces its own row and calls evidence a sorted pair. `rules.cljc` still says every registration traverses `write-element!`, conflicts carry both anchors, and recovery should align both sources. In reality a source may replace only while it is the sole declarer; evidence is a sorted vector; dev/JVM decides in `ledger-state` and publishes its projection, while advanced production uses the direct `write-element!` barrier.

## Steps to Reproduce
Read `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` at the `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` row and the architecture comment/docstrings around `write-element!` and `register-custom-element!`, then compare them with `admit` and the dev branch added by PR #6475. Register two equal declarations and change either source: the implementation rejects because another declarer remains, despite the spec's unconditional self-replacement statement. The dev branch calls `write-through-verdict` plus `publish!`, not `write-element!`.

## Consequence
This is programmer and AI-facing contract drift, not cosmetic prose. It gives the wrong HMR/REPL expectation and points future maintenance at the wrong atomicity/DCE seam. It also over-specifies evidence cardinality: staged reconciliation currently stops after a deterministic contradictory witness pair, whereas direct admission can name all equal incumbents. Exhaustive evidence has no known consumer and is not needed to fix the declaration.

## Bounded solution
Update authoritative `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, its `docs/spec/009-Instrumentation.md` mirror, and the relevant `rules.cljc` comments/docstrings/error text. State equal co-declaration and sole-declarer-only replacement; describe `:declarations` as a deterministic sorted vector containing actionable contradictory declarations without promising a fixed pair or exhaustive N; distinguish dev/JVM ledger authority from the production-direct barrier. Coordinate the same hot-zone edits with open decision `rf2-k1ouh`, which concerns error-channel classification. Add no runtime machinery, state, API, listener, schema, framework, or CI job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009 and its docs mirror state the actual equal-declarer and sole-replacement behavior.
- Evidence is documented as a deterministic actionable vector without a false pair or exhaustive-cardinality promise.
- `rules.cljc` identifies `ledger-state` as dev/JVM admission authority and `write-element!` as the advanced-production direct barrier.
- Programmer-facing recovery text works for any number of declaring sources.
- The edit is coordinated with `rf2-k1ouh` and introduces no new machinery.
- Runtime-law prose in Spec 009, the rules.cljc architecture comment, and the runtime conflict-test namespace states that one shared JS realm is keyed by tag; [build-id ns-sym] is declarer provenance, not a partition key.
- The runtime realm-wide rule is explicitly distinguished from the compile-time arm's per-build registry; existing cross-build tests remain the proof, with no new machinery.
notes:
PR #6513 (worker/conflict-evidence-xdpje). Reconciled spec/009 :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row + rules.cljc comments/docstrings/error-text to the #6475 set-of-declarers law: SET of equal declarers (not one canonical owner), sole-declarer-only replacement, :declarations as a deterministic sorted vector (no false pair / no exhaustive-N), ledger-state = dev/JVM admission authority vs write-element! = advanced-production barrier, N-declarer recovery text. Prose-only: no runtime/classification/schema change. docs/spec/009 is a gitignored CI-generated cp mirror (edited source only). Gates green: core 2097t/0f, test:cljs 10326t/0f, ui-JVM conflict 1001t/0f, mkdocs --strict, check_doc_slugs, check_keyword_catalogue_drift. Not merged; awaiting mayor merge/close.
PR #6513 AUDIT RESIDUAL (completeness/correctness/implementation quality, source verified): the central phrase 'For a given [build-id tag]' still teaches false runtime build isolation in rules.cljc:1010, Spec 009's :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row, and the runtime conflict-test namespace docstring. Runtime admit indexes the shared aggregate by tag alone; build id is only part of declarer provenance [build-id ns-sym]. The existing cross-build runtime test proves :app and :lib conflict on a differing manifest in one JS realm, while the compile-time test correctly permits different manifests in different builds. Minimal fix is prose-only in those three teaching surfaces, explicitly separating realm-wide runtime scope from per-build compile scope. No code, API, schema, new test, registry abstraction, or isolation machinery. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate.
PR #6527 (folded with rf2-k1ouh, same 009 row + rules.cljc surface). RESIDUAL FIXED (three-outcome: (a) genuinely stale). The #6513 set-of-declarers reconciliation was correct, but the phrase 'For a given [build-id tag]' taught false per-build runtime isolation in three teaching surfaces. VERIFIED against code: runtime admit (rules.cljc ~1123) indexes agg by TAG; aggregate (~1190) folds ALL [build-id ns-sym] sources into one tag-keyed map; the two-builds-contradicting-one-tag-conflict-with-both-build-anchors test proves :app and :lib build-ids contradict on one tag in one realm. So [build-id ns-sym] is DECLARER PROVENANCE, not a partition key. Fixed prose-only in rules.cljc law comment (~1010), spec/009 :rf.error/custom-element-conflict row, and runtime conflict-test ns docstring -- each now separates realm-wide runtime scope from the compile arm's per-build registry. Changed NO law logic, NO test logic. Gates green (see rf2-k1ouh). NOT merged.
AUDIT OF #6527 (rf2-hpmeq, 2026-07-20): REOPENED for a material scope correction. #6527 replaced the false `[build-id tag]` runtime partition with the opposite overclaim: “one shared registry across the JS realm.” Current `rules.cljc` explicitly defines the isolation unit as ONE loaded `re-frame.ui.rules` copy / CLJS root. Independently compiled bundle copies can coexist in the same realm and remain isolated by construction; only sources/build ids sharing the same loaded runtime copy share its namespace-local `defonce custom-elements` atom.

The cross-build runtime test passes `:app` and `:lib` provenance through one loaded copy, so it proves build-id is not a partition key WITHIN that copy; it does not prove cross-bundle realm sharing. Correct the three #6527 teaching sites (`rules.cljc` law comment, runtime conflict-test namespace/comment, Spec 009 row) to: within one loaded rules runtime / CLJS root, the aggregate is keyed by tag and `[build-id ns-sym]` is provenance; separate runtime copies are isolated; the compile arm remains separately per-build. No registry bridge, realm singleton, runtime detection, new API, or new fixture framework.

The set-of-equal-declarers law, sole-declarer replacement, atomic rejection, evidence vector, and dev/JVM-vs-production authority split remain correct. Focused UI conflict tests 33/161 green; required PR checks green.

title: Derive the mounted proof-pack roster from the real library
description:
PR #6459 adds a mounted browser suite for all six current proof-pack views and names its final test `every-library-view-is-rendered-somewhere-in-this-namespace`. The test comment explicitly says that adding a seventh library view arms the test, but its only roster assertion is `(= 6 (count [lib/controlled-input ... lib/inline-popover]))`: both the expected count and the referenced vars are hand-maintained in the test. A new `defview` in `library.cljs` does not affect either side.

A temporary causal mutation added a seventh real proof-pack `defview` with its own `data-pp` sentinel and no mounted test. The fresh browser build completed 943 files / 259 compiled / 0 warnings, and the whole suite remained green: 495 tests / 2765 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. The mutation was removed byte-identical. Thus the suite can regress to the exact condition #6459 was intended to prevent—a shipped proof-pack view rendered nowhere—while its roster-completeness assertion stays green.

Keep the correction small and source-derived. `check-ui-facade-isolation.cjs` already derives the complete defview/sentinel roster from `library.cljs`; extend that existing authority (or an equally direct existing checker seam) to compare the derived roster with the mounted suite's explicitly covered selectors/views. A seventh library view must fail until it is mounted and exercised. Do not add a public/runtime view registry, generated CLJS namespace, new Shadow build, new CI job, or generalized source-analysis framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding a seventh proof-pack `defview` with a distinct render sentinel makes an existing required check fail until the mounted browser suite exercises that view.
- Removing or renaming a library view also detects stale mounted-suite roster entries rather than passing on a hard-coded count.
- The guard derives from the same complete library source roster already used by G-18, or another single direct source authority; it does not introduce a second hand-maintained list.
- The six current views remain individually exercised by their causal mounted tests, and the browser suite stays green with non-zero plausible counts.

title: op-nil ordinary-subscribe frame-destroyed egress — RULED Option A: stamp :op :subscribe, :event raw (see DECISION note)
description:
SPLIT OFF rf2-px0i9 (#6467). rf2-px0i9 fixed the coincidental-path-match identity mutation on a LIVE frame for sub query vectors on both error egress routes. RESIDUAL, out of that bead's scope by its own STOP-and-report fence:

An ORDINARY address-directed subscribe to a MISSING/DESTROYED frame emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed with the raw query vector and :op nil (subs/emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! 2-arity + the nil-expected-incarnation arm at subs.cljc ~1607; observation/throw-frame-destroyed!). Because the frame is UNRESOLVABLE, elide-wire-value fails closed to :rf/redacted (rf2-t55hxg.18, a DIFFERENT mechanism than the coincidental-path match). Per rf2-zwgqe the query vector is IDENTITY and should egress verbatim even here; per rf2-t55hxg.18 an unresolved-frame :event fails closed to avoid an empty-policy leak.

This is a genuine DECISION TENSION (rf2-t55hxg.18 vs rf2-zwgqe), NOT a clear fix:
 - Making it raw requires the emitter to carry the :subscribe realm on the op-nil ordinary path, which REVERSES rf2-a2x2w's deliberate op-omission in subs.cljc (outside the error_emit surface) and changes the pinned assertions frame-destroyed-subscribe-listener-survives-prod / listener-fires-on-frame-destroyed-subscribe (currently assert :rf/redacted).
 - Or rule that query-vector IDENTITY is exempt from the unresolved-frame fail-closed on the error :event slot (a rf2-t55hxg.18 amendment).

NEEDS A RULING before any code. Enumerated sites: subs.cljc emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! (2-arity + 1607 nil arm); observation.cljc throw-frame-destroyed! (814, always unresolvable).
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 22:20 AUSEST)

RULING: Option A — RAW. Query-vector identity (rf2-zwgqe, Spec 015 "A subscription's query vector is identity, and it egresses raw") governs the always-on error :event slot even under an unresolvable frame. The rf2-t55hxg.18 fail-closed protects policy-walked VALUE slots and does not apply to identity slots, which never consult frame policy. Stamp the ratified public :op :subscribe at both op-nil subscribe-realm frame-destroyed emit sites so the existing #6467 discriminator routes :event verbatim on both egress routes. Options B (spec carve-out enshrining an access-path-dependent asymmetry) and C (private realm channel, violates a2x2w's no-hidden-steering-slots criterion) are REJECTED.

EMITTER EDITS (2 source files; error_emit.cljc UNTOUCHED — raw-identity-query-vector-event? already routes frame-destroyed raw when :op is :subscribe):
1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc — emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! (defn ~934): emit :op :subscribe UNCONDITIONALLY; collapse the 2-arity nil arm (the fn is subscribe-realm by construction — its only two runtime call sites are ~1040, which already passes :subscribe, and ~1607-1608). At ~1607-1608 delete the conditional (when (some? expected-incarnation) :subscribe) — always :subscribe. Rewrite the docstring paragraph (~953-958) that documents the nil legacy-fallback arm.
2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc — throw-frame-destroyed! (~814): thread {:op :subscribe} as always-on record attrs through emit-and-throw! (add an attrs argument; ONLY throw-frame-destroyed! passes it — throw-no-such-sub!, retry-exhausted, and other emit-and-throw! callers unchanged). The port is subscribe-only by construction (called from acquire!/probe at ~1095/1647/2094) and its thrown ex-info already carries :rf.sub/query-v raw.

SOURCE-COORD UPGRADE (comes free with the stamp): with :op :subscribe present, error-source-coord resolves realm-exact [:sub id] and OMITS when the sub-id is unregistered — no more same-keyword event-coord stealing via the legacy [:sub]-then-[:event] fallback on the ordinary subscribe path.

SUPERSEDED: rf2-a2x2w's scoping sentence for the SUBSCRIBE realm only — Spec-Schemas.md FrameDestroyedTags comment (~1221-1224): "An ORDINARY address-directed dispatch / subscribe into a destroyed frame carries NO captured incarnation, so it omits :op and remains valid without it — that emit keeps its tight keyset and the realm-ambiguous [:sub]-then-[:event] source-coord fallback." The ordinary subscribe emitters now stamp :op; the ordinary DISPATCH path keeps op-omission, its elision, and its unresolvable-frame fail-closed (a dispatched event vector is payload, not identity). a2x2w's line was a scope fence for that bug-fix, not a privacy invariant; the same 009 row ratifies :op public wherever the emit site knows the realm, and :op is already optional in FrameDestroyedTags (no shape surgery).

TEST FLIPS (exactly 2; dispatch counterparts stay :rf/redacted untouched):
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/on_error_elision_prod_test.cljs:222 frame-destroyed-subscribe-listener-survives-prod — :event flips :rf/redacted -> raw [:any-sub]; may additionally assert :op :subscribe.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/on_error_cljs_test.cljc:232 listener-fires-on-frame-destroyed-subscribe — same flip.

WHAT STAYS: rf2-t55hxg.18 fail-closed remains fully in force for every policy-walked value slot — dispatched event vectors (incl. the router's op-nil dispatch-to-missing-frame :event), ex-data value slots, db slots, derived trees. No new dead-frame machinery in the frame-owned sink (routing already no-ops on unresolved frames); no arg-classification axis for query vectors (explicitly rejected in Spec 015 prose).

DOC PASS (same PR; ALL THREE ARE HOT-ZONE — sequential, never parallel; sequence behind any in-flight 009/015/Spec-Schemas PRs):
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md frame-destroyed row (~2122): :op now present on the ordinary subscribe emitters; :event raw in the subscribe realm.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md FrameDestroyedTags comment (~1213-1227): supersede the sentence quoted above for the subscribe realm.
- spec/015-Data-Classification.md section "Direct reads and fail-closed frame resolution": one cross-ref sentence stating identity slots are exempt from the unresolvable-frame fail-closed because they never consult frame policy.

PRIVACY DELTA (acknowledged, accepted): for a production run whose only egress is this one record, :event changes :rf/redacted -> raw query vector; the sibling raw paths (captured record, dev trace, port ex-data) make it near-zero in practice but not literally zero. Accepted because Spec 015 already rules query vectors public identity ("pass identifiers, not secrets"); a lone access-path-dependent redaction is the appearance of protection, not a secret-query model.

RECOMMENDATIONS WEIGHED: dossier Recommendation and Codex Recommendation both chose Option A with the same mechanics; I follow their shared substance, verified the load-bearing claims against origin/main (both call sites, discriminator, FrameDestroyedTags, 015 prose, both tests — all check), and adopt Codex's honest real-but-right privacy-delta framing over the dossier's "zero in practice".

Close rf2-alk8a on that PR's merge. Dispatch is the mayor's.
⚠️ MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-19): RULED Option A (raw) is determinable + ready, but HELD behind rf2-vb6an — both are raw-query-vector-identity work and both touch spec/015-Data-Classification.md (vb6an is LIVE and has spec/015 dirty). alk8a's DOC PASS (spec/009 + spec/015 + Spec-Schemas, all HOT-ZONE) would collide. Dispatch alk8a the moment vb6an's PR MERGES, as sole-toucher of 009/015/Spec-Schemas. Code half (subs.cljc emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! ~934 emit :op :subscribe unconditionally; observation.cljc throw-frame-destroyed! ~814 thread {:op :subscribe}; 2 test flips on_error_elision_prod_test.cljs:222 + on_error_cljs_test.cljc:232 flip :event to raw; dispatch counterparts stay :rf/redacted) is ready to brief verbatim from the DECISION block.

title: guide-truth JVM fixture positively-pins ~8 files but shares the synthesis-docs trigger — same inventory-vs-trigger bug class as rf2-2718r, different cost profile
description:
FILED by the mayor per the rf2-2718r RULING (Fable/Mike 2026-07-19 18:34), which explicitly carved this out as a SEPARATE bead needing its own proportionality ruling — the 2718r decision deliberately did NOT smuggle a partial fix for it.

THE GAP (same class as rf2-2718r / rf2-rf7gu / rf2-d9v3n): implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/guide_truth_jvm_test.clj (the compiler-model-authorities map) POSITIVELY PINS content in ~8 files including EP-0030, spec/004-Views.md, spec/Ownership.md, EP-0034, and compiler.cljc. But it runs in the synthesis-docs CI job, which is surface-gated by report-changed-surfaces.sh. So a PR editing one of those ~8 pinned files may NOT fire the job that guards it — the same "the guard does not fire for the files it pins" defect, one more level out.

WHY SEPARATE FROM rf2-2718r — the cost profile differs materially:
  - rf2-2718r moved a Python-stdlib guard (~1s) into the always-on verify-readme-links job — cheap, so unconditional (option e) was clearly right.
  - THIS is a JVM fixture: JVM setup + ~14s per run, NOT 1s. title: Reclassify custom-element-conflict instead of fabricating always-on fan-out
description:
## Confirmed contract mismatch

PR #6440 classifies `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` as `always-on`, but the real `re-frame.ui.rules` site calls only `error/throw-error!`. That helper builds and throws `ex-info`; it does not fan a record through the error-emit substrate. A registered `:errors` listener receives zero records when the conflict fires. The core conformance suite hides this by adding the id to its literal and calling `dispatch-on-error!` synthetically, even though its own test says every always-on category must be exercised through its real listener axis.

This contradicts Spec 009's explicit meanings:

- `always-on` means real production-surviving `:errors` listener fan-out.
- A thrown registration rejection is diagnostic-channel for catalogue purposes and is not delivered to that listener.
- Promotion requires all three legs. This category is production-reachable, but the caller immediately observes the throw and fixes the declaration at its call site; no suppressed state or silent compounding failure remains because the atomic barrier retains last-known-good.

The runtime law surviving `:advanced` is necessary and already proven by the UI production-elision fixture. That is independent of observability-channel classification.

## Recommended bounded correction

Reclassify the Spec 009 row as `diagnostic`, remove the id and synthetic special-case prose from the core always-on exercise literal, and correct `rules.cljc` comments that call a bare throw an always-on seam. Keep the unconditional production write barrier, canonical thrown id/evidence, and the real advanced-production elision proof unchanged.

Do not add an emitter, listener route, frame/sink plumbing, schema, hook, or new test job merely to justify the mistaken label.
acceptance_criteria:
- The `dispatch-on-error!` docstring no longer claims every production-reachable runtime error must fan through that helper or otherwise be silent; it accurately scopes the helper to categories promoted onto the always-on listener axis.
- Spec 009's channel/promotion and production-observability summary statements distinguish production reachability from listener promotion: caller-observed pure throws can be production-reachable while remaining diagnostic-channel.
- The `:rf.error/custom-element-conflict` row, always-on set, unconditional throw, atomic retention, and advanced-production proof remain unchanged.
- Prose-only: no emitter/listener/schema/hook/API/test-job/framework change.

It also touches rules.cljc, which the u25hr/7uyl9 cluster holds. Two reasons to sequence: (1) same rules.cljc surface as the live cluster; (2) removing an id from always-on must reconcile the catalogue row + Spec-Schemas + the core exercise literal together, and the core conformance suite parses that catalogue — a bungled reclassification reds core (exactly #6440's failure). Dispatch after the u25hr/7uyl9 PR merges, as a careful solo change. ⚠️ Verify the CLAIM first: does the real re-frame.ui.rules emit path make this diagnostic-not-always-on? If the runtime genuinely only throws it at a dev/compile boundary, reclassify; if it IS a production-survivable throw (which #6440's whole point was — the direct write path survives :advanced), then the catalogue is RIGHT and k1ouh's premise is wrong — STOP and report. This is a verify-which-is-wrong bead, not a mechanical reclassify.
VERDICT (2026-07-19 21:51 AUSEST, ce-prodbehav-7hyzr worker): k1ouh's PREMISE IS CORRECT — the always-on classification IS inconsistent with Spec 009's own definitions. No code change.

The mayor-brief decision rule ("production-survivable throw => always-on correct => STOP") CONFLATES TWO INDEPENDENT AXES: (1) does the throw survive :advanced? YES. (2) does the error FAN A RECORD to the error-emit listener (surface #4)? NO. Spec 009 defines always-on on BOTH conjunctively.

Factual premise CONFIRMED:
- rules.cljc throw-element-conflict! calls error/throw-error! (error.cljc:127) = a PURE (throw (ex-info ...)). It does NOT call dispatch-on-error! / emit-error-both! / any error-emit fan-out. A registered :errors listener receives ZERO records when the conflict fires.
- Spec 009 always-on definition (line ~1910): "the production-survivable always-on error-emit axis (surface #4)... fanning a tight record to registered error shippers."
- Spec 009 diagnostic definition (same block): "A `thrown ex-info` registration rejection (the 'Surfaced as a thrown ex-info' rows) is diagnostic-channel for catalogue purposes — it is not delivered to the error-emit listener." + "every always-on category is exercised through the error-emit listener in at least one test (so promotion is real, not documentary)."

- custom-element-conflict is that exact shape (production-reachable pure throw, no fan-out) — yet classified always-on. It is the ONLY thrown-ex-info row marked always-on, and the ONLY always-on category driven SYNTHETICALLY in the exercise test.

title: Honor raw query-vector identity on production sub-error egress
description:
PR #6441 deliberately rules subscription query vectors to be raw identity on every query-vector-bearing surface, with only the existing schema-validation-failure whole-slot scrub retained as a narrower exception. The production always-on sub-error path does not currently honor that contract.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION

1. Create a live frame.
2. Install a valid durable app-db sensitivity declaration at concrete path `[1]` through `elision/apply-classification-effects`.
3. Emit `:rf.error/sub-exception` with query vector `[:patient/record "SECRET"]` through `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!`.
4. The registered production error listener receives:

    {:error :rf.error/sub-exception
     :event [:patient/record :rf/redacted]
     :event-id :patient/record
     :frame :probe}

Directly, `elision/elide-wire-value` produces the same `[:patient/record :rf/redacted]` result. This is expected from the generic walker: concrete integer paths are valid and intentionally match vector coordinates (`elision_test.clj` pins this for position-precise app-db elision).

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT

`error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` currently runs every `event` argument through the frame's durable app-db elision registry. For event errors that is payload hygiene. For sub errors the argument is not app-db or an event; it is the subscription query vector. A coincidentally matching app-db path therefore mutates identity at egress, contradicting #6441 / rf2-zwgqe's explicit ruling that the always-on error `:query-v` / `:event` slots carry query identity verbatim. The closed decision note also incorrectly reasoned that an app-db path could not match a query vector; concrete integer paths prove otherwise.

SCOPE / POSTURE

Keep this narrow. Do NOT add a query-argument classification axis, blanket scrubbing, taint tracking, or new privacy policy. The required behavior is the already-ruled ergonomic contract: subscription identity remains raw; ordinary dispatched events keep their existing elision. Enumerate the production query-vector-as-`:event` callers, including realm-attributed `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` subscription cases, so the fix does not depend only on a category-name prefix. Preserve the separate schema-validation-failure scrub exactly as-is.

Also inspect the frame-owned observability sink route, which receives the raw argument after corpus-wide listener fan-out and may project `:event` independently; the identity contract must be consistent on every production error egress promised by #6441.
notes: PR #6467 (worker/subvec-identity-px0i9). Fix in error_emit.cljc (corpus route) + observability.cljc/projection.cljc (frame-owned sink route): structural raw-identity-query-vector-event? discriminator (query-vector-event-categories superset + frame-destroyed :op :subscribe), skips app-db elision for a sub query-vector :event on BOTH routes. FOUND-vs-NAMED: reading every emit site surfaced 2 query-vector categories NOT in sub-error-categories — :rf.error/read-after-release + :rf.error/observation-retry-exhausted (the latter fires on a LIVE frame). Residual op-nil ordinary-subscribe fail-closed case (rf2-t55hxg.18 vs rf2-zwgqe tension) split to rf2-alk8a — needs a ruling. Gates all green (JVM core 2093, CLJS 10264, elision, browser-prod-elision 113, catalogue-drift). No spec/009 touch, no new error id.

title: Keep data-rf-root out of the emit seam root-identity boundary
description:
## Problem

PR #6436 added a normative `emit-ui-tree` boundary in `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md`. Its "No container, no identity" bullet groups "the root marker attribute" with root-id, identifier-prefix, and element locator as root identity that is settled before the seam and stamped around its output.

That is false for the concrete marker this contract refers to. `spec/011-SSR.md` §Root Manifest v1 pins `data-rf-root` as a **bare discriminator on the immediately-adjacent manifest `<script>`**, explicitly carrying "no value, no identity". `re-frame.ssr.manifest/script-html` implements that rule, and the manifest tests assert the marker is bare. The tree-to-HTML seam should indeed stay free of identity/page assembly, but calling the marker identity obscures which layer emits it and invites an implementer to stamp it on the root container or emitted tree.

## Required correction

In the single 004B boundary bullet, keep root-id, identifier-prefix, and element locator outside `emit-ui-tree` as page/root assembly facts. Describe `data-rf-root` separately as the bare manifest-script discriminator emitted by the page assembler next to the container, and link the owning Spec 011 wire-form section. Do not change the marker spelling, add identity to it, alter the seam signature, or expand into the remaining S5 page-assembly work.

## Evidence

- `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:455-459` — newly added conflicting classification.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:471-487` and resolved decision at `:1670-1677` — marker is bare, on the manifest script, and carries no identity.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc` — `script-html` owns the wire element.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/root_manifest_cljs_test.cljc:253-267,699-701` — exact bare-marker and spelling pins.

This is the sole new correctness finding from the PR #6436 audit. The fingerprint algorithm/encoding and other page-assembly residue are already owned by the live S5 authority graph (`rf2-vxgfnd.97`, `rf2-vxgfnd.97.1`, and the delivered/residual notes on `rf2-vxgfnd.97.2`); no duplicate is filed for them.
acceptance_criteria: 004B no longer classifies `data-rf-root` as identity or suggests the emit seam stamps it; it names the marker's adjacent manifest-script placement and Spec 011 ownership; the edit remains confined to this boundary correction; doc slug and strict MkDocs gates pass.
notes: PR #6453 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6453). Doc-only correction; premise verified: code was already correct (script-html emits bare marker; #6448's ui_tree.cljc carries no root identity). Sites 1 found / 1 named. Gates: doc slugs + mkdocs strict + keyword drift exit 0; ssr 485 tests; test:cljs 10262 tests. No Spec 009 row needed. 004B sole-toucher verified by full worktree sweep at edit time.

title: Align the EP process and template with the PEP structure established by #6433
description:
## Current contradiction

PR #6433 deliberately puts EP-0030..EP-0035 into one PEP-style structure: Abstract → Motivation → Specification (with scope and guide impact) → Rationale → Backwards Compatibility → Resolved Decisions → Open Issues → References. The PR explicitly names EP-0009/template alignment as follow-up.

Current authoring authorities still prescribe a different shape. `docs/EP/EP-0009-the-ep-process.md` §Document conventions names Goals/Non-Goals, Relationships, Bead Plan / Reference Implementation, and Recommendation as standard top-level sections; `docs/EP/EP-template.md` emits exactly those headings and has no References or standard Resolved Decisions position. A programmer or agent following the template therefore cannot produce the corpus shape #6433 now presents as the improved standard.

## Bounded resolution

Make the two authoring authorities state one forward-looking structure. Recommended: adopt #6433's compact PEP shape for new and materially revised EPs, folding goals/non-goals into Specification scope, dependencies/provenance into References, implementation tracking into Beads, and landed rulings into Resolved Decisions. Preserve EP-0009 lifecycle/durability semantics, including rf2-r7ahi's freeze-meaning-not-bytes rule. If the six UI EPs are intentionally exceptional instead, say that explicitly in both authorities rather than leaving contradictory instructions.

Do not rewrite older EPs, manufacture missing sections, add a section-order checker, or build a documentation framework. This is two small authoring-document edits aimed at low-friction human/AI ergonomics.

## Dedupe

Fresh all-live-Bead census before filing: 52 open/in-progress. Exact searches for EP-0009, EP-template, template alignment, document conventions, PEP standard/PEP-standard, and section names found no owner. rf2-r7ahi owns how settled meaning is corrected; rf2-hgwpq owns residual EP-0009 ledger/status cleanup. Neither owns the section-structure contradiction.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/EP/EP-0009-the-ep-process.md` and `docs/EP/EP-template.md` prescribe the same forward-looking top-level structure and explain where scope, relationships/provenance, implementation tracking, resolved rulings, and recommendation material live.
- The choice is explicit: either the #6433 PEP shape becomes the authoring default or the six-EP exception is documented in both authorities.
- EP lifecycle, status, normative-home, guide-impact, and rf2-r7ahi durability rules remain intact.
- No existing-EP migration sweep, new checker/framework, or unrelated process rewrite is introduced.
- `python scripts/check_ep_status_sync.py`, `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` pass with non-vacuous repository counts/output.
notes: PR #6446 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6446): aligned EP-0009 §Document conventions + EP-template.md to the #6433 PEP shape (Abstract→Motivation→Specification[Scope open/Guide impact close]→Rationale→Backwards Compatibility→Resolved Decisions→Open Issues→References; preamble Status/Type/Created/Resolution). Stated where old sections (goals/non-goals, relationships/provenance, implementation tracking, resolved rulings, recommendation) now live. PEP shape = authoring default; older EPs left as historical record. Tier 1, no EP status flipped, hgwpq's Bead Plan item 3 untouched. Gates green: ep_status_sync (35 in sync), doc_slugs (531 files, no broken links), mkdocs --strict (exit 0). guide-truth skipped (pins only EP-0034/EP-0030). Awaiting review; not merged.

title: Align reagent-slim invalid-hiccup-head payload with the widened catalogue contract
description:
## Problem
PR #6431 widened Spec 009's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` catalogue row so the unrecognised-reserved-head arm is also thrown client-side by reagent-slim, while retaining the promised payload fields `:head`, `:element` "(both arms)". The existing JVM/server arm supplies both fields, but `reagent2.impl.template/reject-reserved-rf-head!` receives only `head` and emits ex-data with `:head` but no `:element`. The source Bead rf2-01zvu explicitly warned that the catalogue conformance test does not validate the tags column, and #6431's new tests assert `:head` but not `:element`, so all gates remain green while the newly widened contract is false.

Consequence: a diagnostic consumer following Spec 009 can show the complete offending hiccup vector for server failures but receives nil for the same category/recovery on reagent-slim. That is avoidable cross-host friction in a structured error API.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Render `[:rf/suspense-boundry {:id 1}]` through `reagent2.impl.template/as-element` and catch the `ExceptionInfo`.
2. Inspect `(ex-data ex)`: it contains `:rf.error/id`, `:head`, `:where`, `:reason`, and `:recovery`, but no `:element`.
3. Compare Spec 009's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` row, which promises `:head`, `:element` for both arms, and the server arm in `re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-reserved-rf-hiccup-head!`, which supplies both.

## Bounded Resolution
Prefer passing the original hiccup vector to the cache-miss reject and adding `:element` to the ex-data, with one direct assertion. If the client payload is intentionally narrower, change the catalogue row to state the per-emitter difference instead. Do not introduce a new error id, builder dependency, or diagnostic framework.
acceptance_criteria: For reagent-slim's `:rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head` reserved-head arm, runtime ex-data and Spec 009 agree about every promised payload field. A direct client test asserts the chosen shape (including `:element` if the cross-host shape remains canonical), the existing cache-collision and production-survival rows remain green, and bundle isolation remains intact.

title: Standing-census test can overwrite and delete a programmer's local draft
description: PR #6423 makes the synthesis census correctly ignore untracked local AI documents, but its new proof uses one fixed path in each real ignored directory: `zz-untracked-local-draft-probe.md`. The test unconditionally `(spit probe ...)`, which truncates any pre-existing file at that path, and its `finally` unconditionally `.delete`s it. Because `/ai` is deliberately a programmer/agent local workspace, that filename is not reserved and a normal UI test run can destroy local work—the exact surface the change is meant to leave alone. Use an exclusively-created unique temporary path inside each directory (or fail before touching an existing path), and delete only the file this test successfully created. Keep this local to the test; no new census abstraction or filesystem framework.
acceptance_criteria: The census test never overwrites or deletes a pre-existing file in drafts/, spikes/, or reviews/. Its probe is created exclusively with a unique name inside the target directory and cleanup removes only that created probe. A bounded control demonstrates that an existing sentinel path/content survives. The focused census namespace and full UI suite remain green with non-zero counts; no production or census-policy behavior changes.

title: a11y drop-frame-state! is never called in production
description:
FOUND while fencing rf2-2amkm (PR #6410), out of that bead's scope.

`re-frame.story.ui.a11y/drop-frame-state!` documents itself as 'Called from the canvas / shell teardown when a variant frame is destroyed'. It is not: `grep -rn drop-frame-state tools/` returns the definition and TEST callers only. No production caller exists.

CONSEQUENCE: a11y state for a destroyed variant frame is never reclaimed. `violations-by-frame` and `run-state` accumulate an entry per frame ever scanned, for the life of the page. The violations bag holds raw axe-core JS violation objects, each retaining DOM node references via :nodes/:target — so this also retains detached DOM for every scanned-then-destroyed variant.

NOTE the interaction with rf2-2amkm: the supersession fence now makes teardown SAFE (a settlement after drop-frame-state! refuses rather than resurrecting the frame — measured, 10/10). But safe-when-called is not called. Wiring the teardown is what makes the frame-destroyed path actually reclaim.

SCOPE: find the canvas/shell teardown seam that destroys a variant frame and call drop-frame-state! from it (the docstring names the intended caller). Check whether ui/chrome-a11y needs anything — it does not: singleton state, no per-frame accumulation.

Surface: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/ (+ wherever variant-frame teardown lives). Test: assert the per-frame slots are gone after a variant frame is destroyed.
notes:
DELIVERED — PR #6412 (worker/story-teardown-cpbut).

PREMISE VERIFIED, AND THE DOCSTRING WAS ALSO WRONG. drop-frame-state! genuinely had no production caller (git grep: definition + test callers only). BUT the docstring's named caller did not exist either: it said 'the canvas / shell teardown', and ui/canvas's component-will-unmount only clears canvas-last-run-key + the first-rendered sentinel — it never destroys a variant frame. NO ui/ namespace calls frames/destroy! at all. The UI reaches teardown only indirectly via runtime/reset-variant (test-mode re-run, stepper) and run-variant's fresh-run boundary. Docstring corrected to name the real path. Same defect family as render-static / the 19 catalogue rows.

LEAK MEASURED, not asserted. Object-identity reachability (deterministic, not a GC probe): without the eviction, after frames/destroy! the violations slot survives AND the scanned node object is still reachable from the panel, with status-for reading :done for a frame that is gone. With it: both slots absent, node unreachable, status :idle.

WIRED AT: frames/run-teardown-walks! (shared by destroy! and the in-place reset-state!) + frames/destroy-inline! — the SAME three sites where :drop-assertion-accumulators and :drop-run-state already evict per-frame state. Third instance of an established pattern, not an invented seam. Must be a late-bind hook (:drop-a11y-state) because frames is .cljc and ui/a11y is .cljs — the same inversion play/browser's a11y-reader seam already solves. Registered from canonical/install-late-bind-shims! so every install! re-arms it (a load-time defonce could not).

chrome-a11y NEEDS NOTHING — confirmed singleton state (violations vector + one {:status} map), no per-frame accumulation, exactly as the bead predicted.

#6410 FENCE STILL DECLINES: verified not assumed. A scan parked mid-flight, frame torn down through the production path, scan then released — settlement resurrects neither slot. Token-in-slot means this new clearing path revokes the claim for free, as #6410's rationale predicted. Asserted as slot ABSENT + status terminal, never as a throw (this class does not throw on CLJS).

SEQUENCE PROOF: SCAN -> DESTROY -> reclaimed -> SCAN -> DESTROY -> reclaimed, one frame id, one process, plus a pin that round 1's node does not come back in round 2. Also frame-scoped: destroying one frame leaves a sibling frame's a11y state intact.

RED-BEFORE, TWO LEVERS: (1) in-suite + permanent — every reclamation test runs the same teardown twice, once with :drop-a11y-state unregistered (exactly pre-fix: no producer ever registered it); (2) real revert of the two wiring files to origin/main -> full gate exit 1, 16 failures, ALL in this namespace, sole failing ns. Every reclaim assertion failed; every 'WITHOUT the eviction ... the leak' assertion PASSED — the leak measured on unmodified teardown. Restored byte-identical.

title: Story a11y run-state mutations are unfenced in .then callbacks
description:
FOUND by the rf2-6pfpt worker (#6405), named not fixed — outside its scope fence.

THE SITES: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs (run-axe!) and chrome_a11y.cljs both mutate `run-state` and `violations-by-frame` inside `.then` callbacks with NO frame-existence check and NO supersession check.

⚠️ WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC — the exact failure #6405 measured on the sibling path: under teardown the unfenced callback DOES NOT THROW on CLJS, because (inc nil) is 1. It RESURRECTS a phantom run-state entry. That entry carries no :run-token, and the loop guard only fires when a token is PRESENT, so the resurrected run was never aborted and ran on to :status :pass FOR A FRAME THAT WAS GONE. A fabricated green, not a hang, not a crash. Assume the same shape here until measured otherwise.

METHOD THAT WORKED ON #6405, REUSE IT:
  - Thread the existing run token (run! already mints one per run, stamps it as :run-token, and passes it to run-loop!). The token was already conveyed correctly on the sibling path — what was missing was the COMPARISON on the settled-Promise path: record-result! ran first, the check after, so the mutation sat on the far side of the fence.
  - Use a VALUE fence compared against the live slot, NOT a ^:dynamic Var or ThreadLocal. This is the rf2-vxgfnd.171 situation INVERTED: the hazard is a run OUTLIVING its claim, not a claim failing to reach a child, so a conveyed mechanism would agree with the callback by construction. Keep check + mutation in ONE synchronous turn so nothing can take the slot between them.
  - Do NOT pin execution order — re-enter the loop unconditionally and let its own stale branch settle via the existing abort path. One abort decision, not a second copy.
  - ⚠️ Beware a BOUNDS check masquerading as an identity check: #6405 found the stepper guard was a size test that declines while :results is short and then PERMITS the clobber once a new cursor grows back past the index. It now fences on object identity (identical?, not =). Identity was chosen over a generation counter because stepper-step-back! pops only the last step, so a session-level generation would be actively WRONG for an amendment still owed at an earlier index.

⚠️ MEASURE, DO NOT REASON. #6405 ran 10 trials reverted (10/10 RED, 11 failures each, identical failure set) and 10 applied (10/10 GREEN), after converting the intermittent race into a deterministic test — a real js/Promise settles on a microtask the test cannot interleave against, which is what makes this class flaky in the wild.
⚠️ PROVE THE SEQUENCE, not just the cases: ADMIT -> REFUSE -> ADMIT again -> REFUSE again, in one process. A guard carrying state can pass every single-transition test and still be broken (the ai/ ratchet was).
⚠️ VACUITY-PROBE THE GATE: the CLJS runner prints no per-namespace headers, so a green total does NOT prove your namespace ran. Flip an assertion, confirm the full gate reds naming your probe, then restore.

GATES: cd tools/story && clojure -M:test (~1836 tests) + npm run test:cljs (~10140). Never pipe a gate through tail/head. Use TEST COUNTS not assertion totals; what matters absolutely is non-zero — a bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN.

ALSO NAMED, DELIBERATELY LEFT by #6405: runner-events/run-step! settle callback emits an unfenced emit-trace! for an abandoned stepper session. It judged this acceptable — a public late-bound one-shot executor with no session identity, whose RECORDED VERDICT is fenced caller-side. Re-verify that judgement rather than inheriting it.
notes:
DELIVERED — PR #6410 (worker/story-a11y-fence-2amkm).

MEASURED FAILURE MODE (both sites): SILENT RESURRECTION, not a throw. Fence removed, 10/10 trials RED with 19 failures and **0 errors** — nothing throws. `(swap! run-state assoc frame-id :done)` over a dissoc'd map resurrects the entry; `status-for` then reads :done for a frame that is gone, and the resurrected violations-by-frame entry is what browser/register-a11y-reader! serves to :rf.assert/a11y. Value fence, not conveyed — the hazard is a run outliving its claim, so a conveyed binding would agree with the callback by construction. Token lives IN the slot so existence and identity are ONE question: every present/future clearing path revokes the claim by construction, no side atom to keep in step.

EXISTING GUARD AUDIT: there was NO guard at either site — every post-await mutation was unconditional, including the .catch's :error write (also fenced now). So no bounds-check-in-disguise to unmask, unlike #6405's stepper.

EXECUTION ORDER NOT PINNED: one predicate at each mutation point, chain otherwise untouched, every run still settles its own tail promise. A superseded run additionally declines to SCAN (nothing to learn about a torn-down tree).

run-step! title: Identify what advances a pending ViewCell batch on a second same-stack dispatch-sync
description:
## Observation (measured, PR #6393)

While pinning the rf2-vxgfnd.166 host-checkpoint contract on the mounted React 19 path, a real-browser measurement produced this sequence on the watchable `ui/adapter`:

```
base                : {:rev 0, :body-runs 1, :root-commits 1}
after dispatch-sync : {:rev 0, :dirty true, :pending 1, :body-runs 1}   <- drain 1 COMPLETE
after dispatch-sync : {:rev 1, :dirty true, :pending 1, :body-runs 1}   <- drain 2
```

Drain 1 behaves exactly as the ruled contract describes: the drain runs to completion and the pending window stays open (revision unmoved, cell still dirty). That is the guarantee PR #6393 asserts, and it is green.

The open question is drain 2. Between the two logs the revision advanced 0 → 1 while `body-runs` stayed at 1, so React did not re-render — meaning the advance came from a scheduler flush (phase 1 advances the revision; phase 2 notifies), not from `commit!` step 8. Something inside the second `dispatch-sync` flushed the first drain's pending mark, after which drain 2's own movement re-marked the cell.

A microtask cannot have run between two synchronous statements in one task, so this is a synchronous flush on the second drain's path.

## What was ruled out

- `flush-render!` — an explicit Tool-Pair/MCP surface; nothing in core or the router invokes it automatically.
- `re-frame.ui.events/dispatch-committed!` → `reactive/flush-frame!` — that is the DOM callback sync door, not `rf/dispatch-sync`.
- A late-bound core→UI flush hook — none exists; `:live-frame/flush-projection!` is the router's only late-bound flush and is a live-frame projection, not a UI-scheduler seam.
- The armed microtask from drain 1 firing early — impossible mid-stack.

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

The ruled contract says several drains before one checkpoint MAY share a batch. It is a permission, not a guarantee, so this behaviour does not violate it, and the headless fixture demonstrates real sharing where React is out of the loop. PR #6393 therefore asserts only the guarantee on the mounted path and documents the measurement rather than guessing at the cause.

But the mechanism should be named. Either it is deliberate (and belongs in the contract prose as a stated consequence of `dispatch-sync`), or it is incidental coupling worth removing.

## Suggested approach

Instrument `flush-pending!` / `flush-scope!` with a stack capture in a DEBUG build and re-run `re-frame.ui.render-batch-host-checkpoint-dom-cljs-test`, which already drives the exact sequence. Then either document the behaviour in the Spec 006 §Render-batch finalization prose or file the coupling as a defect.

Do NOT weaken the existing fixtures to accommodate whatever is found — the guarantee assertions are the deliverable and are green.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT rf2-l91ds (#6393): the open question is already tracked here, but the contradiction is stronger than the current notes record. Current active authorities still say the MAY-sharing case is a fact: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc lines 81-84 and spec/006 lines 1773-1776 say two back-to-back dispatch-sync! calls in one JavaScript stack render once, not twice; docs/core/glossary line 205 repeats it. The PR's own real-browser measurement says the second same-stack dispatch advanced the first drain's pending mark, so mounted React does NOT universally behave that way. Resolve this Bead by identifying the synchronous flush and then either remove the coupling or narrow all three authority statements to the actual permission; do not leave MAY followed by a false unconditional example. No new Bead filed (all-state dedupe to this open owner).
RESOLVED by measurement (see rf2-i3dvj for the ruling that remains). What advances the pending batch on a second same-stack dispatch-sync: the ORDINARY armed schedule-flush! microtask checkpoint, landing mid-call because dispatch-sync! yields to the host microtask queue. Traced with stack capture on flush-scope! + advance-revision! plus begin/end console markers, 3 browser runs identical: revision 0->1->2; every flush-scope! stack was flush-scope! <- flush-pending! <- the microtask closure, terminating there with NO router frame above it; advance-revision! (commit*/step-8) never fired. CONTROL: a plain js/queueMicrotask enqueued by the fixture just before the 2nd call also ran mid-call, so the checkpoint is genuinely the host's and no re-frame code is in that callback. There is NO hidden synchronous flush and NO incidental scheduler coupling to remove — the scheduler is correct as specified. The filer's four ruled-out suspects were all correctly ruled out; the closest (drain-1 microtask firing early) was right about the microtask and wrong only in assuming a mid-stack fire was impossible. ACTIONED: reactive.cljc guarantee 3 narrowed — the unconditional 'two back-to-back dispatch-sync! calls in one JavaScript stack render once, not twice' is RETRACTED (holds headless, false mounted); the DOM test ns docstring + in-test note carry the full instrumentation record. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: neither sharing nor non-sharing across two dispatch-sync! calls — the former asserts a permission as a guarantee, the latter freezes possibly-unintended router behaviour into a contract. The remaining question (should dispatch-sync! be microtask-atomic?) is a ROUTER ruling in implementation/core (held by #6365) and is filed as rf2-i3dvj. spec/006 ~1773-1776 + docs/core/glossary ~205 still carry the retracted claim; left for after that ruling (hot-zone, and would need rewriting twice).

title: Build digest ignores custom-element declarations, so two different builds share one identity
description:
FOUND by the rf2-vxgfnd.141 worker, in-fence and small but deliberately left because fixing it alone is a half-.141.

build/digest-for-slice (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc:712) folds only the `views` rows. Two builds with IDENTICAL view sources but DIFFERENT custom-element declarations therefore produce the SAME build digest.

WHY IT MATTERS: the digest is build identity. Anything keyed on it — caching, staleness detection, served-output freshness — cannot distinguish two builds whose element classification differs, and classification decides whether a prop is emitted as an attribute or a property. So the digest says "same build" for two builds that emit different DOM.

SCOPE: small and self-contained (one fold), unlike its parent rf2-vxgfnd.141 which needs a source-harvest pass, declaration->consumer dependency edges and a new namespace. Split out so it can land independently.

⚠️ ACCEPTANCE MUST BE CAUSAL, not a green run: construct two builds identical in views and differing only in custom-element declarations, assert the digests DIFFER, and prove the test reds if the declarations are dropped from the fold. Per rf2-wlqfq (#6387), give the assertion its OWN lever — a blanket mutation elsewhere can red neighbouring fixtures while leaving this one green, certifying falsifiability it never established.

title: G-14 quadratic-vs-runaway charter gap — RULED Option C: reword to runaway + refresh stale spec/008 G-14 row; no new arm
description:
SURFACED by the rf2-gv8gr worker (#6388), which refused to ship the stronger claim and rewrote its own docstring, the bar comment and EP-0034 to state the limit explicitly.

THE GAP: the bead charter language implies the watch-loop arm catches an accidentally-quadratic rebuild pass. It does not at the shipped roster size. Arithmetic from the worker: K=11 views, per-view ~1.6ms, so a quadratic pass costs ~K/2 = 5.5x linear (~95ms) — comfortably inside the 550ms bar (K x the ratified 50ms per-view bar). Separation only appears once K > ~64.

WHAT SHIPPED IS STILL REAL: an honest runaway tripwire with 4 mutations / 4 red, plus an anti-vacuity witness (K realisations, K DISTINCT fingerprints, forced inside the span) checked BEFORE any duration. The worker also closed a hole M2 surfaced: a lazy map would have moved every expansion OUT of the timed span and reported "cheap" — realisation is now forced in-span, and the lazy variant costs ~12.8ms rather than ~0. No bound was widened, no threshold tuned down, no retry added.

⚠️ THIS IS A COST/SCOPE DECISION FOR MIKE, NOT AUTO-DISPATCHABLE. Closing the charter arm needs EITHER a namespace-scale roster (K > ~64 views) OR a scaling ratio (compare per-view cost at two roster sizes and assert it stays flat). The worker was explicit that the answer is NOT a tighter number — tightening the bar at K=11 would just make the arm flaky without buying quadratic separation. A K>64 roster multiplies CI time on a gate that runs per-PR, and the worker-gate memory records that worker wall-clock is already dominated by cold shadow-cljs compile.

RECOMMENDATION: the scaling-ratio shape is cheaper and strictly more diagnostic than a big roster — it measures the property (per-view cost is constant in K) rather than a proxy for it. But whether the arm is worth closing at all is a posture call: the runaway tripwire already catches the failure that would actually ship, and the quadratic case is currently hypothetical. If the answer is "not worth it", the honest action is to AMEND THE CHARTER to say runaway rather than quadratic, so no future reader believes the arm proves more than it does.

ALSO NOTED, benign understatement, no action needed unless the /ai untracking (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1) leaves them in place: the G-14 rows in 07-testing.md and 12-implementation-plan.md still read "named open" because the worker correctly did not touch ai/**. Conversely 02-programming-model.md section 8, which an audit note flagged as prematurely claiming the rebuild was gated, is now TRUE with no edit.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:57 AUSEST)

RULING: Option C — amend the charter wording; ship NO new timing arm. The scaling-ratio arm (K=16/K=48) and the namespace-scale roster (K>64) are both REJECTED. The '⚠️ not auto-dispatchable' flag above is discharged: this bead is now dispatchable doc-only work.

WHY C, verified against the repo (not just the dossier):
1. The normative spec never made the quadratic promise about the rebuild arm. spec/008-Testing.md:682 attaches 'e.g. accidentally quadratic' to the single-defview EXPANSION-P95 arm — where the claim is defensible (a within-view quadratic multiplies the ~5ms large fixture by ~15-20x, through the 50ms bar) — and says only that the rebuild delta 'rides later stages'. The overclaim lives in the rf2-gv8gr bead brief and local ai/ synthesis rows, not in tracked normative text. Honesty is restored by wording, not machinery.
2. The proposed ratio arm is the wrong instrument. Verified in implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/build.cljc: contribute-view-checked! aggregates conflict evidence across OTHER sources ((effective slice views source) excludes the current namespace), so growing one namespace's roster does not exercise the path where per-view work actually aggregates across views — and that path is eval-time registration, which the rebuild arm (macroexpansion-only; register-view! emitted, never evaluated) cannot see under ANY G-14 shape. A ratio arm would claim 'quadratic scaling policed' while measuring flatness on a path with no realistic quadratic attachment point. That is the overclaiming-gate failure this bead exists to prevent, ~150 lines dearer.
3. No observed regression; S2 landed; all arms green with 10-58x / 29.5x headroom. Pre-alpha posture: proportionate, no gold-plating.

WHAT SHIPS (one worker, one doc-only PR):

  (a) staleness fix: the watch-loop-rebuild delta no longer 'rides later stages' — it shipped in PR #6388 (2026-07-18) in the jvm-ui job: K=11 structurally-distinct dashboard roster, derived K x 50ms = 550ms bar, anti-vacuity distinct-fingerprint witness forced in-span before any duration compare.

KEEP 'accidentally quadratic' on the expansion-p95 arm — it is earned there. CLJS-emitter half + guide-fixtures arm (S3) stay named open/later-stage, unchanged.

title: check-per-ns-isolation: RULED Charter A — add 2 allowlist entries (story open-in-editor + presence-real-clock) + header limits/rf2-ybqse review-bar section
description:
FOUND by the rf2-i36h6/qw31o worker (#6385), named not fixed: "widening its charter is a decision, not a worker call."

THE FINDING: implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs exists precisely to catch namespaces that only pass in company. Its curated allowlist is 15 re-frame.* frame-construction namespaces. THREE instances of this family surfaced on 2026-07-18/19 and the gate watched NONE of them:
  1. rf2-oslyz — Story open-in-editor ownership ns alone gave 5 :rf.error/no-adapter-installed errors; it only ever passed because an earlier ns had called init!. Selected in the other order: 5 :rf.error/image-duplicate-id errors.
  2. rf2-ybqse (#6336) — a fixture captured (.now js/Date) in a top-level def while the panel compared at render time; test:cljs loads all namespaces before executing any, so a 60s horizon decayed across the suite prefix.
  3. rf2-i36h6 (#6385) — tools/story presence_real_clock_cljs_test yielded one setTimeout 0 on the premise that a macrotask lands after React act settles. It does not. Alone it was RED on 4 of 10 runs.

⚠️ THE HARD PART, and why this is a decision not a chore: instance 3 is INTERMITTENT alone (4/10), not deterministic. A gate that runs each namespace once in isolation would have called it green six times out of ten. Any widening has to answer: how many runs, or what structural property replaces run-counting? rf2-ybqse established the standard — prove the failure is UNREACHABLE (a margin, an invariant) rather than merely unobserved. For instance 2 the margin was measurable (+30461ms of a 60s horizon already burned); for instance 3 the structural answer is "await the thenable rather than racing a macrotask against it".

ALSO NOT UNIFORM: instance 1 is missing setup (fixable by the ns installing its own adapter, as #6367 did), 2 is a clock captured at namespace-load, 3 is a lost race. A single mechanical check will not catch all three. Decide what the gate is actually for before widening the allowlist.

QUESTIONS FOR THE RULING: (a) widen the allowlist to all test namespaces, or keep it curated and add these three; (b) run-count or structural property; (c) is the cost acceptable — running every namespace in isolation multiplies CI time, and rf2-worker-gate memory records that worker wall-clock is already dominated by cold shadow-cljs compile.

Gate if actioned: the checker own self-test + npm run test:script-policy + whatever suite it gates. A bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-19 09:58 AUSEST)

RULING: the checker keeps its original rf2-32siq3.44 charter (Charter A). implementation/scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs IS a curated, one-pass, deterministic tripwire for test namespaces that are RED when run ALONE against the consolidated node-test bundle — fixtures leaning on sibling-leaked runtime state. It is NOT a certifier of test-order independence: it is structurally blind to green-alone/red-in-company defects (load-time capture, the rf2-ybqse class) and only probabilistically sensitive to intermittent races.

(a) ALLOWLIST — stays curated. Add exactly TWO entries to ISOLATION_NAMESPACES:
  1. re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test (rf2-oslyz, #6367) — the gate's exact design class; deleting its adapter self-install is visible ONLY alone; ~11s/run.
  2. re-frame.story.play.presence-real-clock-cljs-test (rf2-i36h6, #6385) — deterministically green solo post-fix (10/10 measured), so zero noise while healthy; its regression is company-masked by the warmed act path, making this gate the only automatic detector; on regression it becomes a ~40%-per-run tripwire that fires within a few PRs. (Codex's dissent on this entry was weighed and overruled: the "flaky gate" scenario only exists AFTER a real regression merges, at which point a red is a true positive of a bug nothing else in CI can see.)
Do NOT add day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources-cljs-test (rf2-ybqse, #6336): running alone SHORTENS the load-to-render gap and makes load-time-capture bugs GREENER — listing it spends ~11s/run forever while implying coverage the mechanism cannot provide.
Roster comment: note the list now carries a second stratum — shipped order-dependence regressions whose failure signature is red-alone — alongside the EP-0023 frame-construction lineage.

(b) DETECTION — one deterministic pass per namespace. NO run-counting; NO structural-property machinery in the gate. The rf2-ybqse structural-unreachability standard is a REVIEW-TIME bar for fixes in this family, not gate code: a fix must prove the failure UNREACHABLE (a measured margin, an invariant, an awaited thenable), not merely unobserved, and carry a positive control that fails in the consolidated run. Add to the script header (after "THE CHECK"; wording may be lightly fitted to house style):

  WHAT THIS GATE IS NOT
  ---------------------
  This gate detects ONE direction only: deterministic "red alone, green
  in company" fixture defects. It does NOT certify test-order
  independence. It is structurally blind to the inverse direction —
  green alone, red in company (e.g. a wall-clock captured in a top-level
  def decaying across the suite prefix, rf2-ybqse): running such a
  namespace alone makes the bug LESS likely, not more. And it is only
  probabilistically sensitive to intermittent races (rf2-i36h6 was red
  alone on just 4/10 runs unfixed). Do not add run-counting, order
  permutation, or timing analysis here. The bar a FIX in the
  order-dependence family must clear is the rf2-ybqse
  structural-unreachability standard, enforced at REVIEW time: prove
  the failure unreachable (a measured margin, an invariant, an awaited
  thenable) rather than merely unobserved, with a positive control that
  fails in the consolidated run.

(c) COST — the current ~2m39s curated pass (~3 min with the two additions) is ACCEPTED on CI and the fast-PR spine. REJECTED at any cadence, including nightly (whys recorded so these are not re-proposed):
  - Allowlist-all / blanket scan: real census is 744-778 test namespaces (.cljc files feed the bundle too, not just the 471 .cljs) = ~131-137 min/pass at the measured ~10.6s/ns — over 4x the job's 30-min timeout, lands on the compile-dominated worker spine, and still sees only half the defect family.
  - Run-counting / repetition: x6 for 95% confidence against a generous 4/10 flake, ~x300 for a 1-in-100 race — converts correctness into a statistics budget and still misses the rf2-ybqse direction entirely.
  - Structural-property machinery in the gate: "is this test's timing structurally sound" is a static-analysis research project, not a checker; the standard is enforceable at review, not by script.
  - Deleting the gate: it is cheap (bundle reused), self-tested, and the only automatic guard for the deterministic missing-self-setup class, which has bitten twice (live-frame-reload-cljs-test, rf2-oslyz).

IMPLEMENTATION (one small worker): two ISOLATION_NAMESPACES entries + roster-stratum comment + header NOT-section per above. Gates: node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs --self-test green; a live gate run green; verify BOTH added namespaces report NON-ZERO test counts solo (per the bead's gate note — a bare selector that matches nothing can read as green); npm run test:script-policy. No new checker-specific test harness.

Context: all three motivating instances were already fixed and merged with positive controls (#6367, #6336, #6385) before this ruling; only the charter question remained. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-fhnd5.isolation-checker-charter.md retired (deleted) per Mike's authorization; its evidence base is summarised above.
Implemented on PR #6422 (branch worker/ruled-trio-b72to). Charter A shipped: EXACTLY TWO ISOLATION_NAMESPACES entries added (re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test, re-frame.story.play.presence-real-clock-cljs-test); day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources-cljs-test deliberately NOT added per the ruling. Roster now labels two strata (EP-0023 frame-construction lineage + shipped red-alone order-dependence regressions). 'WHAT THIS GATE IS NOT' header section added after THE CHECK, recording both blind spots and pointing fixes at the rf2-ybqse structural-unreachability bar enforced at REVIEW time. No run-counting, no order permutation, no timing analysis; no logic changes. EVIDENCE the entries run (not no-ops): solo against the consolidated bundle, open-in-editor-ownership = Ran 5 tests containing 13 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors; presence-real-clock = Ran 6 tests containing 31 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors — matching their 5 and 6 deftest forms. Live gate: all 17 namespaces pass standalone (roster 15 -> 17). Self-test 5/5. npm run test:script-policy exit 0.

title: Make the synthesis standing census ignore local untracked AI drafts
description:
PR #6372 says its standing-marker census covers authority-shaped, git-tracked synthesis documents, but `directory-roster` uses Java `.listFiles` and therefore includes every local untracked `.md` under `drafts/`, `spikes/`, or `reviews/`.

That conflicts with the project policy shipped in #6368: `/ai` is local by default, current tracked exceptions are transitional, and programmers/agents are expected to create local AI material without force-adding it. A local scratch review or draft with no standing banner now makes the full `implementation/ui` suite red even though the file is ignored by Git, cannot reach CI, and changes no shipped authority. Conversely the stated roster is specifically the tracked authority surface.

Keep the marker-presence logic and directory discovery, but derive admission from Git's tracked set (or an equivalent exact tracked-file source). Do not replace it with a hand-maintained filename list or broaden into content validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding an ignored, untracked local `.md` under each censused directory does not change the census result or break the UI suite.
- A newly force-added/tracked `.md` in any censused directory is admitted automatically in that same commit and fails until it has an accepted preamble marker.
- Every currently tracked `.md` in drafts/, spikes/, and reviews/ remains covered; a censused directory with no tracked documents still fails non-vacuously until its S7 row is deliberately retired.
- The existing per-directory vocabularies, preamble/deep-link rule, real-disposition controls, and mutation teeth remain; no maintained filename roster, Markdown parser, or general content-consistency framework is introduced.
- Focused/full UI tests run with non-zero counts.
notes:
DELIVERED in PR #6423 (worker/ep0008-census-0b9b0), not merged.

MECHANISM: directory-roster kept .listFiles for DISCOVERY; ADMISSION is now a new tracked-markdown-names helper shelling 'git ls-files -z -- <dir>' (clojure.java.shell) from repo root, filtered to direct children ending .md. The roster is the intersection. -z avoids Git's quoted-path form. A non-zero git exit THROWS rather than yielding an empty set, so an unreadable tracked set cannot read as a clean census.

Because ls-files reads the INDEX (not HEAD), a force-added doc is admitted by the very commit that tracks it — acceptance criterion 2. Verified in a THROWAWAY repo in scratchpad (staged-but-never-committed file returned; untracked sibling not). Done outside this repo deliberately: nothing was git add -f'ed under ai/, and git diff --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD -- ai/ is empty, so the AI-tracking ratchet is safe.

Intersection rather than ls-files alone: a tracked file absent from the worktree stays out of the roster instead of throwing in slurp; the new coverage assertion reds on that instead.

PER-ENTRY, NOT UNION (the rf2-nyjml lesson): new deftest the-standing-census-roster-is-gits-tracked-set loops censused-directories and per directory asserts (a) tracked set non-empty, (b) roster == tracked set (coverage), (c) a real untracked file spat into that directory does not enter the roster. A roster that dropped one directory entirely would still look populated in aggregate.

PROOF BOTH DIRECTIONS (bug reproduced first, not assumed):
- BEFORE: 3 ignored untracked .md (one per directory) => 3 failures, message wrongly claiming each was 'authority-shaped and tracked'.
- AFTER: same 3 files present => green, 0 log mentions.
- STILL HAS TEETH ON A GENUINE TRACKED DEFECT: mutated the real tracked reviews/09-review-disposition.md to strip its '**Status:**' marker => census RED naming that file, while the untracked probes stayed silent. Mutation reverted; marker verified restored.

Counts: census namespace 13 tests / 120 assertions (was 12/111; +1 test, +9 = 3 dirs x 3 assertions). Full implementation/ui suite 956 tests / 18656 assertions / 0 failures (brief expected ~955 pre-existing + my 1 new deftest).

Untouched as required: marker vocabularies, preamble/deep-link rule, real-disposition controls, negative-arm mutation teeth. No filename roster, no Markdown parser, no content validation. Anti-vacuity message updated to name the tracked-set reason a directory can census nothing.

title: CI ratchet: the tracked-file count under ai/ must never increase
description:
PROPOSED by the rf2-4lv73 worker (#6368) as the mechanical pin for Mike end-state ruling. Filed because it prevents a demonstrated, expensive failure — not as tidiness.

MIKE RULING (2026-07-18, in-session): "Nothing under /ai should be tracked" is the END STATE; files stay tracked as long as necessary. rf2-4lv73 states that policy in CLAUDE.md and .gitignore as PROSE. Prose does not stop a force-add.

THE GUARD: a CI check that fails when `git ls-files ai/ | wc -l` INCREASES against a committed baseline. Properties that make it the right shape:
  - it pins the ruling mechanically rather than by linting wording;
  - a new force-add fails the build at the moment it happens;
  - the number can only FALL as S7 removes trees (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1), so the guard needs no maintenance;
  - it RETIRES ITSELF at zero.
Current baseline: 89 files — findings/new-substrate-synthesis 61, findings/new-substrate-codex 24, decisions 4. Verify before pinning; do not trust this number.

WHY IT CLEARS MIKE POSTURE BAR (rf2-seuvt): on 2026-07-18 a force-added ai/decisions/ dossier carried a literal personal worktree path into CI. scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh failed on main, and because CI evaluates the PR merge commit, EVERY open PR went red for about an hour. Cost: six worker dispatches — three chasing a phantom on clean branches, one diagnosing, one fixing main, one rebasing three branches. Four separate workers independently identified the tracking as the root cause and said the leak class will recur while it stands. This is a likely, already-realised failure mode with a known cost.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
  - Keep it to a count ratchet. Do NOT enumerate tracked trees — Mike ruled CLAUDE.md states policy only and git state is the roster; an enumerating guard would reintroduce exactly what the ruling forbids.
  - Decrease must PASS (S7 removals must not be blocked). Only increase fails.
  - The failure message must name the offending paths (diff the current listing against the baseline) — a bare count mismatch is not actionable.
  - .github/workflows/* is HOT-ZONE; check no other worker holds it, and note implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs pins workflow shape at 168 assertions.
  - Prove teeth by mutation: force-add a scratch file under ai/ -> gate fails naming it; remove -> passes. Also prove a REMOVAL passes.
  - Gate script itself should be shellcheck-clean if written in sh; portability.yml shellchecks its own gate for exactly this reason.
notes: PR #6380 (worker/ai-ratchet-lsp1i). Baseline VERIFIED at 89 (synthesis 61 / codex 24 / decisions 4) — matches the filing number. Gate: scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh (POSIX sh, invoked via 'sh' so no exec bit needed on runner; mode 755 to match siblings). Baseline: scripts/ai-tracked-baseline.txt (snapshot of git ls-files ai/, LF-pinned in .gitattributes; used ONLY to name offending paths in the message — pass/fail is the count comparison alone, no tree enumeration). title: Authority-shaped synthesis drafts and spikes are enumerated by no census — the reason stale claims keep surviving
description:

DEFECT: ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/drafts/ and .../spikes/ hold authority-shaped, git-tracked documents that NO census enumerates as a class.
