- check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only covers drafts/ for LINK VALIDITY only and does not cover spikes/ at all — the S3 spike report is not among its 41 files (established by #6359).
- mkdocs does not build the ai/ tree.

CONSEQUENCE: a document can state a retired model indefinitely and no gate objects. That is precisely how both files survived rf2-er64a, and how spec-004-interim-amendment.md sat at "Status: final draft / Merge condition: immediately" carrying wording Spec 004 had retired. Someone can act on these.

WHY IT CLEARS MIKE 2026-07-18 POSTURE BAR (rf2-seuvt): material maintenance/AI friction with a demonstrated failure mode, twice. Not exhaustiveness — these are documents an agent or a human is invited to treat as authority.

PROPOSED SHAPE (from #6359, deliberately bounded — do not build a cross-document consistency checker): a directory-level enumeration asserting every tracked file under drafts/ and spikes/ carries EITHER a current-status marker OR a supersession marker. Not content validation. #6359 already added a marker-presence arm to the existing bounded census slice_memo_lifetime_census_jvm_test.clj (rf2-2mop6r) for its two files — extend that shape to the directory rather than inventing a new framework.

⚠️ THE DISPOSITIONS ARE NOT UNIFORM — the guard must not force one. #6353 superseded a draft whose anchors were GONE from the live spec. #6359 superseded a draft whose anchors were all PRESENT but whose edits had ALREADY LANDED (re-applying would duplicate them), and deliberately did NOT supersede a dated experimental record whose model is still the binding shape source cited by live Spec 006 — retiring it would kill a document the spec depends on, and rewording it would falsify the record. A guard that demands a single marker vocabulary will force one of those into the wrong shape.

Gate: the census suite from implementation/ui (a bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from implementation/ silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts) + prove the arm reds on an unmarked file and greens on each of the three real dispositions.
notes:
REFERENCE CLASS EXTENDED (rf2-rzzlw / PR #6370, 2026-07-18): add reviews/ and the tombstone README.md to the uncovered set. check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only enumerates exactly 41 files (guide/, drafts/, prep/, 11-adoption-workstreams.md, 12-implementation-plan.md); reviews/, spikes/, README.md and the numbered chapters 01-10 are all outside it. rf2-rzzlw repaired six broken relative references in reviews/09-review-disposition.md - a doubled reviews/reviews/ prefix, a dangling markdown link, and four drafts/* spans wrong by one directory level - and NOT ONE of them would have been caught by any gate. The relocation that introduced them (rf2-mgy7pz #6231) also passed green. Post-S7 this matters more, not less: reviews/ and spikes/ are the permanent survivors, so they become the only synthesis paths left and the only ones still uncensused.
DELIVERED — PR #6372 (worker/synthesis-census-5jbev), 2026-07-19.

SHAPE: one directory-level marker-PRESENCE arm appended to the existing bounded census implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/slice_memo_lifetime_census_jvm_test.clj — the same file #6359 put the two-file marker arm in. No new framework, no new tracked file under ai/, no guide/** touched.

ROSTER = THE DIRECTORY LISTING (.listFiles filtered to *.md), for drafts/, spikes/, reviews/. A file landing tomorrow is censused the day it lands. A vanished/empty directory REDS rather than passing vacuously, so the S7 wave (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1) must drop the drafts/ row deliberately.

PRESENCE ONLY, PER-DIRECTORY VOCABULARY. Three marker classes, each a line-anchored presence regex: :status (**Status:** …), :supersession (leading **SUPERSEDED / HISTORICAL / RETIRED / ⚠ CORRECTION / DELTA BANNER / DRAFT** banner), :record (**Date:** / **Written:** / **When:**). drafts/ accepts {status, supersession} only — an undated draft is actionable, so a bare date does not declare standing there. spikes/ and reviews/ also accept :record, because a dated experimental/adversarial record's date IS its standing; demanding **Status:** of a 2026-07-11 review would be the wrong-shape failure this bead warned about. What a marker SAYS is never read.

ALL THREE REAL DISPOSITIONS PASS, and are pinned BY NAME in a dedicated deftest so a future edit cannot quietly exclude one: (1) drafts/spec-004-interim-amendment.md superseded/anchors-gone; (2) drafts/spec-006-observation-port-amendment.md superseded/edits-already-landed; (3) spikes/s3-ownership-report.md NOT superseded — dated experimental record still cited by live Spec 006, carrying a scoped ⚠ CORRECTION.

DEEP-LINK GUARD GENERALISED: the marker must sit in the preamble, ahead of the first ## heading. A directory census cannot name the section carrying a claim without validating content, but it can guarantee no anchor-linkable section precedes the marker.

MUTATION PROOF: 6 on-disk mutations, 6 RED. (1-3) a brand-new unmarked .md added to each of the three directories — red in all three, proving the roster is the listing, not a file list; (4-6) the live marker stripped from one file per directory (spec-004-interim-amendment, s3-ownership-report, 09-review-disposition) — red each. All reverted; tree clean. In-test the negative arm additionally strips markers from EVERY conformant document in all three directories and requires each to red, with a no-op guard that throws if a strip fails to land.

ONE PROSE FIX (per the rf2-cpalh precedent — fix the prose, not the checker): reviews/09-review-disposition.md was the single document in the three directories carrying no recognised marker. It gains a **Status:** line declaring what it is — a standing, append-only decision log and a permanent S7 survivor. Its dates were per-entry only, so nothing at the top declared the document's own standing.

GATES (all foreground, run to completion): implementation/ui clojure -M:test = 926 tests / 16114 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors (baseline 919/16016 + 7 new deftests); check_synthesis_plan_authority.py exit 0; --self-test exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py --synthesis-only exit 0 (41 files); mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

NOT ACTIONED (out of scope, deliberately): the bead's third-sighting 'smallest pin' proposal — two exact-token assertions in guide_truth_jvm_test.clj on spec/API.md's §2b dispatch! S1-clause row and the spread-safe rows. That is content validation of a graduated spec file, a different guard from this one, and guide_truth_jvm_test.clj was outside this dispatch's fence. title: Audit the microtask/task claim across story, pair-mcp and machines-viz — per-site, never a term sweep
description:
FOUND by the rf2-om8or worker (#6346), named not fixed. Sites: tools/story/ (settled_boundary.cljc, runner.cljc, xray_embed.cljs ~8 hits, a11y_dialog.cljs ~6 hits), tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/server.cljs + tests, tools/machines-viz/test/**.

⚠️ THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS BEAD IS THAT A BLIND SWEEP WOULD BE WRONG. The om8or worker was explicit: 'Several of those are likely genuine queueMicrotask — each needs the same per-site check, not a blind term sweep.' In Xray it found exactly that — reactive_panel_subs.cljs:720 and 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:872 describe the ViewCell tear-correction flush, which genuinely IS js/queueMicrotask (confirmed at implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:78), and were correctly left untouched. Replacing 'microtask' with 'task' everywhere would have made two correct statements false.

METHOD (established by rf2-iweic #6343 and rf2-om8or #6346, follow it):
1. For EACH site, determine what the code actually schedules with. next-tick -> a TASK (goog.async.nextTick's own docstring: 'This will not schedule the callback as a microtask'; JVM executor is a task boundary). js/queueMicrotask / Promise.resolve.then -> genuinely a microtask; leave the wording alone.
2. Where wording is wrong, use #6343's settled phrasing: 'schedules f asynchronously, as a task — never a host microtask, never inline', with mechanism and latency under an explicit 'What is not guaranteed — host-dependent, do not build on it' heading. Do NOT enumerate mechanisms as exhaustive (goog.async.nextTick has three paths incl. a setTimeout fallback: '5ms or more').
3. ⚠️ CHECK WHETHER ANY CODE DEPENDS ON MICROTASK ORDERING. If it does, that is a BEHAVIOURAL bug, not a wording bug — report it prominently and do NOT correct the comment around it (a fixed comment over a real ordering assumption removes the clue and leaves the bug). om8or proved Xray's case by showing it calls queueMicrotask nowhere.

ERGONOMICS NOTE (Mike's 2026-07-18 filter): filed P3. Nobody's SPA breaks from this. It is filed because the docs teach an ordering model, microtasks drain before tasks, and a reader reasoning from these comments orders things wrongly. Borderline — if the per-site audit finds the claim is mostly correct, close it as verified rather than manufacturing edits.

Gate: each artefact's own suite from its own directory (⚠️ a bare clojure -M:test -n <ns> from a parent dir silently runs 0 tests and READS AS GREEN — confirm non-zero counts) + npm run test:cljs + mkdocs build --strict + check_doc_slugs.py. Xray spec-currency rule does not apply here, but tools/story has its own spec surface — check it.
notes:
AUDIT VERDICT (rf2-7psvw): claim is CORRECT at every site. 0 edits, no PR.

Per-site audit of all 40 microtask/task-wording sites across tools/story, tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, tools/machines-viz.

CRUX: the file sets are DISJOINT. Files mentioning next-tick (7) and files saying 'microtask' (16) do not intersect. Not one site describes a next-tick call as a microtask — that is the exact error mode rf2-iweic/rf2-om8or found elsewhere, and it does not occur here.

Every 'microtask' site sits over a genuine microtask mechanism:
- story ui/xray_embed.cljs + ui/a11y_dialog.cljs -> real js/queueMicrotask calls (xray_embed 431/472/488; a11y_dialog 169/170/187/189). state.cljc:164, transitions.cljc:381, 018-North-Star:581/587, xray_embed_e2e:23/305 all refer to that same rf2-4l7t2 queueMicrotask path.
- pair-mcp server.cljs:625 -> shutdown! chains .then on close-p (Promise -> microtask). nrepl_test + test_utils -> .then/.finally microtasks.
- machines-viz compute_layout_error + auto_fit_view -> js/Promise.reject + .catch; the 'with-redefs unwinds BEFORE the rejection microtask' reasoning is exactly right, which is WHY those tests use set! instead.

Every next-tick site ALREADY uses the settled rf2-6343 phrasing:
- runner_events.cljc:1008 'genuinely deferred, never inline'
- step_runner_test.cljc:252/260-261 'genuinely deferred, never inline' + 'on the JVM next-tick runs on a SEPARATE executor thread'
No latency claim, no exhaustive mechanism enumeration. Nothing to correct.

MICROTASK-ORDERING DEPENDENCE (the finding that would have mattered): YES, three sites depend on microtask ordering — and ALL THREE ARE CORRECT, because the thing they order against is a real task.
- runner.cljc:142-145 + runner_events.cljc:1396-1397: the async yield is literally (js/setTimeout #(run-loop! ...) 0). The docstring 'a setTimeout 0 yield runs after the microtask queue has drained to empty' names the true mechanism and draws the true conclusion.
- presence_real_clock_cljs_test.cljs:74-78: says 'Yield one macrotask' explicitly, then the same drain reasoning. Exemplary.
- machines-viz set!-vs-with-redefs stubbing: correct, and load-bearing.
No behavioural bug. No comment was 'fixed' over a live ordering assumption.

LEFT ALONE, deliberately: the ':dom -> adapter act() / microtask flush' wording (settled_boundary.cljc:19/36, artifact.cljc:203, 017-Testing-Story.md:861/895). It describes a FUTURE adapter-supplied :dom flush hook — no such hook exists yet (only headless-flush-hooks, :provides :headless). It is a description of React act(), not of next-tick, so the bead's error mode does not apply. Spec 017 and settled_boundary.cljc already agree verbatim; no spec/impl drift to reconcile.

- tools/machines-viz clojure -M:test  ->  632 tests / 2537 assertions, 0 failures

title: Xray calls next-tick a microtask in ~20 places — same defect as iweic, different artefact
description:
FOUND by the rf2-iweic worker (#6343) and deliberately deferred: separate artefact, own section slug and cross-refs.

DEFECT: tools/xray describes next-tick as a MICROTASK scheduler. It is not — rf2-iweic established that goog.async.nextTick explicitly does NOT schedule as a microtask (Closure's own docstring: 'This will not schedule the callback as a microtask'), and on the JVM the executor is plainly a task boundary.

SITES: tools/xray/src/.../trace_collector.cljs calls its next-tick mirror refresh a microtask in ~9 places; tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md §Reactivity says it ~11 times ('next-tick (the microtask scheduler)').

WHY IT MATTERS: microtasks drain BEFORE the next task. Anyone reasoning about Xray's mirror-refresh timing from these comments will order it wrongly against real microtask work — and the ordering is the whole point of the sentence. Wrong mental model in the doc that teaches the model.

METHOD (from rf2-iweic, #6343): state only what the host actually guarantees. The portable fact is 'schedules as a TASK, never a host microtask, never inline'. Do not enumerate mechanisms as exhaustive; iweic found goog.async.nextTick has three paths including a setTimeout fallback ('5ms or more'), so any latency claim is host-dependent.

⚠️ Xray spec currency is MANDATORY: a change under tools/xray/ must update tools/xray/spec/* in the SAME PR. Here that is the point rather than an afterthought — the spec carries ~11 of the ~20 sites. If a §Reactivity section slug moves, update every cross-ref (iweic had to fix Design-TransducerRouter.md for exactly this reason).

Gate: cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test (baseline ~1270 tests / ~5908 assertions) + npm run test:cljs + mkdocs build --strict + check_doc_slugs.py. title: Spec 012 :scroll table wrongly says nil/absent is the same as :preserve
description:
FOUND by the rf2-px26m worker (#6333) and deliberately NOT fixed — adjacent, different bead, same silent-wrong-answer family.

DEFECT: Spec 012's :scroll table carries the row '| nil / absent | Same as :preserve |'. That is false. resolve-scroll-strategy treats nil/absent as the IMPLICIT DEFAULT — :top on forward navigation, :restore on popstate — NOT :preserve.

CONSEQUENCE: a user who wants no scrolling reads this row, omits :scroll, and gets scroll-to-top on every forward navigation. The doc actively teaches the wrong way to get the behaviour they want, and the symptom (page jumps) looks like a framework bug rather than a doc error. Passes the ergonomics test squarely: someone building an SPA hits this and has no reason to suspect the documentation.

FIX: correct the row to state the real default (:top forward / :restore popstate) and point readers at :preserve — or false — for actual suppression. Verify against resolve-scroll-strategy rather than against the prose.

CONTEXT: #6333 narrowed the :scroll enum and added :rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy; it also fixed one adjacent honesty gap in a line it was already rewriting (RouteMetadata's :scroll slot never admitted false, a documented suppression value). This row was outside that line.

title: analyze-fragment reports a key it does not have: :key {:present? has-props}
description:

DEFECT: implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc — analyze-fragment sets :key {:present? has-props}, conflating 'this fragment has a props map' with 'this fragment has a :key'. So [:<> {} ...] reports a key it does not actually have.

CONSEQUENCE: such a fragment would PASS the presence keyed-child check (presence-keyed-child?) despite being unkeyed. That is the same class of defect rf2-vxgfnd.96.1 just fixed for elements — a key-presence probe reading the wrong AST location — but on the fragment branch, and in the permissive direction (wrongly ACCEPTS rather than wrongly rejects).

WHY IT WAS LEFT: the 96.1 fix deliberately preserved :fragment's existing [:key :present?] shape after VERIFYING that is its real shape rather than guessing. Changing what analyze-fragment writes is a separate change with its own blast radius (anything reading fragment :key), so widening scope mid-fix would have been wrong.

ERGONOMICS CHECK (Mike's 2026-07-18 recalibration — 'excellent ergonomics for creating SPAs, do not litigate every last detail'): this one DOES pass. A user writing [:<> {} ...] inside ui/presence gets it silently accepted as keyed, and the presence machinery then has no real identity to track — a wrong-answer path, not a guard-exactness nicety. But it is narrow: it needs an empty-or-props-bearing fragment directly under a presence boundary.

title: Scope the ui/raw manifest claim to view-level enumerability
description:
PR #6321's `ui/raw` portal caveat is behaviorally correct, but its stated surviving containment guarantee overclaims the shipped manifest. Spec 004 now says "every site declares the `:raw` capability and is recorded in the manifest, so the set of such escapes is finite and listable."

The compiler records only a VIEW-LEVEL capability bit:

title: Align Xray concrete-query selectors with CLJS equality at NaN, regex, and sequential values
description:
PR #6318 correctly preserves CLJS record type in Xray's concrete-query `data-testid` encoder, but its new "honestly stated" supported domain still overclaims injectivity and equality-canonicality at three ordinary CLJS value seams.

REPRODUCED on the repository's current ClojureScript runtime:

  (pr-str js/NaN)                  => "##NaN"
  (= js/NaN js/NaN)                => false
  (pr-str (js/RegExp. "x" "g"))   => #"x"
  (pr-str (js/RegExp. "x" "i"))   => #"x"
  (= (js/RegExp. "x" "g")
     (js/RegExp. "x" "g"))        => false
  (= [1 2] '(1 2))                 => true

`canonical-str` sends NaN and RegExp values through the `:else (pr-str x)` branch, so two `=`-distinct NaN- or regex-bearing concrete queries mint one selector. It also renders vectors with `[...]` and seqs with `(...)`, so two `=`-equal query arguments can mint different selectors. This contradicts both directions of the function/spec contract: distinct supported identities are injective, and value-equal identities canonicalize to one selector.

The domain text explicitly includes every `number` and `regex`, so these are not covered by its raw-JS-object exclusion. Query-vector validation constrains only the vector and keyword head; these values are legal arguments. Xray's `skipped-subs` dedupe and the subscription cache describe identity in terms of the concrete query vector's ClojureScript equality, so the selector must align with that same equivalence relation.

Keep the local/no-framework posture. Canonicalize all ClojureScript sequential values that are `=` under one sequence representation instead of distinguishing vector vs list. Treat non-reflexive NaN and identity-equality host values such as RegExp as explicitly outside the injective domain unless a genuinely small, equality-faithful representation exists; do not add a WeakMap/object-id registry or general serializer merely to distinguish host identity. Correct the function/spec wording so it never names regex or all numbers as faithfully covered when they are not. Add adversarial rows for the supported equality law and explicit boundary tests/prose for excluded scalars.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equal vector/list sequential query arguments mint one selector, matching ClojureScript `=`.
- The supported-domain contract no longer claims regex or non-reflexive NaN are injectively represented by `pr-str`; excluded identity-like values are named honestly.
- A string containing an unmatched UTF-16 surrogate cannot throw during selector generation and remains distinguishable from other strings; adversarial coverage pins the URI-safe encoding.
- Adversarial CLJS tests pin the NaN/RegExp boundary and the supported sequential equality law.
- Record type preservation, map/set/record insertion-order canonicality, hash-collision coverage, labels, React keys, projection and `data-query-v` remain unchanged.
- The correction stays local; no general serializer, object-id registry, WeakMap identity system, lossy U+FFFD folding, or query-grammar redesign.
notes: ADDITIONAL SAME-SEAM REPRO (2026-07-18 audit): the supported-domain claim includes strings, but `concrete-query-selector` passes the final canonical string directly to `js/encodeURIComponent`. ClojureScript `pr-str` preserves a lone UTF-16 surrogate inside the quoted string; `encodeURIComponent` throws `URIError: URI malformed`. Exact probe: `(let [s (js/String.fromCharCode 55296) p (pr-str s)] ...)` produced code units `[34 55296 34]`, then `js/encodeURIComponent p` threw. Thus a legal string-bearing query can crash the Xray panel while generating its test id. Fix at the same small codec seam with an injective, URI-safe escaping of unmatched surrogate code units (preserve distinct input strings); do not merely replace them all with U+FFFD, which would introduce collisions, and do not add a general serializer.
close_reason: Filtered by product posture: rare NaN/RegExp/vector-vs-list/lone-surrogate behavior in an internal Xray data-testid codec does not materially affect SPA authoring ergonomics or correctness; fixing it would litigate edge semantics beyond justified value.

title: POLICY: are EP decision records editable in place, or frozen with dated addenda?
description:

[CORRECTED 2026-07-18: PR #6304 was OPEN/unmerged at decision time; an earlier version of this description wrongly said the mayor had merged the truth-fix.] [RESOLVED 2026-07-18: see the DECISION block in NOTES -- ruling (b) precised as "freeze meaning, not bytes", with the concrete PR-branch disposition for #6304.]

THE SITUATION: rf2-d1yhx corrected teardown terminology across active authorities. To do it, it edited EP-0008's 'The ruling' and 'R2' prose â€” clauses that made PRESENT-TENSE FACTUAL CLAIMS about where the runtime emits (they credited safe-call-hook! with stamping/conj'ing that record-teardown-failure! actually does). The worker limited itself strictly to those factual clauses, left the rest of the EP untouched, and FLAGGED the judgement rather than deciding it.

THE FORK:
(a) EDIT IN PLACE (what shipped in #6304): EPs read as current truth; a reader never meets a false present-tense claim. COST: the record of what was decided WHEN gets quietly rewritten â€” the EP stops being archaeological evidence.
(b) FREEZE + DATED ADDENDUM: the decision record stays honest about its own moment; corrections are visible AS corrections. COST: readers must reach the addendum to learn the prose above it is stale.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (b) freeze + addendum. An EP's value IS being the record of what was ruled and why; if it silently tracks the code it stops being evidence and becomes just more docs. But this is a call about the project's memory and taste, not correctness â€” hence a ruling, not a dispatch.

SCOPE OF THE RULING: it should settle the GENERAL policy (all EPs, all future corrections), not just EP-0008. If (b) is chosen, this bead's implementation is: revert the EP-0008 ruling/R2 prose to its as-written form and append a dated addendum recording the correction. The worker confirmed that is a clean follow-up â€” nothing about #6304 forecloses it. If (a) is chosen, close this bead and consider recording the policy in the EP template/README so future workers don't re-raise it.

title: Rule the normative home of the re-frame.ui head policy
description:
PR #6289 establishes the behavioral head policy but deliberately leaves an explicit `[S4-OPEN — normative home undecided]` marker in `spec/004-Views.md`: should the rule live normatively in Spec 004, Spec 011, or elsewhere? Source leaf rf2-yjhrt is now closed and all-state searches found no separate Bead owning this operator flag, so the decision is otherwise tracked only inside prose.

The decision is narrow. Recommended split: Spec 004 normatively owns the re-frame.ui surface fact—there is no compiled structural `ui/head`/head channel, body-root rendering stays beneath the root (qualified for the `ui/raw` host escape hatch in rf2-6u4cw). Spec 011 normatively owns the structured SSR head model (`reg-head` / `active-head`, escaping, ordering, hash/mismatch behavior) and is cross-linked as the supported path. Spec 009 is instrumentation authority and is not a natural home for the view-surface policy.

Mike must rule the normative home. Then remove the S4-OPEN marker, make the selected ownership explicit, keep only a concise cross-link/projection in the other spec, and record the ruling on the S4 epic. Do not invent a new spec, duplicate the full policy, or add head runtime machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mike's ruling names the normative owner for the no-compiled-view-head policy and the owner of structured SSR head behavior.
- The `[S4-OPEN — normative home undecided]` marker is removed and the selected source/projection split is explicit.
- Spec 004 and Spec 011 cross-link without duplicating the full contract; Spec 009 is touched only if the ruling gives it a real instrumentation fact.
- The `ui/raw` portal caveat from rf2-6u4cw is incorporated or sequenced so the final policy is not absolute beyond the structural surface.
- The ruling is recorded on rf2-vxgfnd.96; docs mirrors/strict links agree.
- No new spec, head API/runtime, dedupe engine, compatibility path, or broad prose move.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:06 AUSEST)

RULED: Option A — split ownership by responsibility.
- Spec 004 (spec/004-Views.md) is the NORMATIVE OWNER of the compiled-view structural boundary: re-frame.ui templates, their AST and JVM tree, and the root/mount surface expose no ui/head, no head target, and no portable head channel. The statement is qualified at the ui/raw foreign boundary (an explicit host-React escape hatch; a raw portal MAY target document.head — caller-owned host behaviour, outside Spec 011's head model/ordering/dedupe/hydration/hash guarantees).
- Spec 011 (spec/011-SSR.md) remains the NORMATIVE OWNER of the structured document-head mechanism: reg-head / render-head / active-head, head-model shape, escaping, shell emission, ordering, :rf/head-hash, mismatch behaviour, recovery.
- Spec 009 owns ONLY the trace/error projection (:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch head-mismatch arm, :rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed). Touch 009 only if a trace fact actually changes (none does).
RATIONALE: ownership follows the abstraction boundary, not the shared noun "head". Spec 011 specifies an OPTIONAL artefact (day8/re-frame2-ssr); the no-head-channel fact constrains every compiled template even in client-only apps that never load it, so only the grammar-owning spec can normatively define the grammar's completeness. title: Make README anchor checks use GitHub duplicate slugs
description:
PR #6290 correctly fixes literal `{#id}` suffixes because GitHub and the attr-list-disabled docs renderer both slugify that suffix as visible heading text. But review of the affected checker exposes a broader, explicit renderer mismatch: `check_readme_links.py` says these READMEs are read on GitHub and not in MkDocs, then intentionally validates MkDocs `_N` duplicate slugs and tells users the rules are "NOT GitHub's".

The bundled `underscore_disambig_ok` fixture blesses `#errors_1` for the second `## Errors` heading. GitHub's heading slugger uses `errors-1`; the fixture itself documents that fact. Current `_slug_index` returns `{'errors', 'errors_1', ...}`, so the gate can certify a fragment that the actual README renderer does not mint and reject the real one. This is latent in live links today, but tracked READMEs already contain duplicate headings, so the mismatch is not hypothetical structure.

Make this checker renderer-honest with the smallest GitHub-specific seam. At minimum, use GitHub's `-N` duplicate suffix and reverse the fixture controls (`#errors-1` green, `#errors_1` red), and reconcile the module/error prose. Verify the existing base-slug cases before widening; reuse a small local slug helper if the base rules agree. Do not import a Markdown renderer, call the network in CI, or force README content into MkDocs rules merely to share code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two `## Errors` headings index as `errors` and `errors-1` for README targets; `#errors-1` resolves and `#errors_1` is reported broken.
- The checker/module/error text states that GitHub-rendered README anchors use GitHub rules, not MkDocs `_N` rules.
- Existing `{#id}` full-title behavior, inline/fence masking, HTML anchors, target checks and current live scan remain correct.
- Focused controls cover real duplicate suffixes and the wrong-underscore negative; any further base-slug divergence is measured before inclusion, not assumed.
- No general Markdown parser, GitHub network call in CI, new renderer dependency, or repo-wide README rewrite.

title: Qualify the host-owned head policy for ui/raw portals
description:
PR #6289 correctly establishes that re-frame.ui has no structural head API and that `ui/html` cannot escape its DOM-element parent, but the new Spec 004 prose overstates containment across the deliberately opaque `ui/raw` boundary. It says "every template form ... produces nodes beneath [the body] root" and that no compiled-view form renders into `<head>`.

`emit_cljs.cljc` lowers an analyzed `:raw` node to `(:form node)` unchanged. A valid React node can be a portal. Independently reproduced with the repository's React/Playwright versions: a body-root render containing `ReactDOM.createPortal(<meta name=rf-portal-probe content=yes>, document.head)` produced the meta in `document.head` while the ordinary sibling stayed under the body root. Wrapping that portal value in `ui/raw` crosses the compiler unchanged by design. This does not mean re-frame.ui supplies or should supply a head channel—the programmer has explicitly entered host React—but the absolute structural sentence is false unless the foreign escape hatch is named.

Add a narrow caveat: compiled structural forms and `ui/html` target only beneath the root; `ui/raw` may carry host constructs such as portals that render elsewhere, and those are outside re-frame.ui's head ordering/deduplication/hydration guarantees. An app doing so owns the host behavior; use Spec 011 `reg-head` / `active-head` when the structured SSR head contract is wanted. Trust the programmer and keep the escape hatch; do not ban portals, inspect opaque React values, or add head machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 004's host-owned-head section scopes its containment claim to compiled structural forms and `ui/html`, not opaque `ui/raw` host values.
- It explicitly notes that a `ui/raw` React portal can target `document.head` (or another external container) and is caller-owned host behavior outside re-frame.ui head ordering/dedupe/hydration guarantees.
- The preferred structured SSR head path remains Spec 011 `reg-head` / `active-head`; no new view-level head API is implied.
- Existing trusted-markup and raw foreign-boundary contracts remain unchanged.
- Documentation-only; no portal prohibition, host-value inspection, head runtime, sanitiser, compatibility layer, or conformance promise for portals.
notes: MAYOR SEQUENCING (2026-07-18): genuine gap — S4-D (#6289) established that re-frame.ui has no structural head API and ui/html cannot escape its DOM element, but emit_cljs.cljc lowers an analyzed :raw node to (:form node) UNCHANGED, and a valid React node can be a PORTAL — which can render into <head>, escaping the host-owned head policy S4-D just documented. HELD, not blocked: its surface is spec/004-Views.md §Interop, where rf2-74vlo (S4-C, the last S4 feature leaf) is LIVE adding the compile-tier a11y warnings subsection. Dispatch after 74vlo merges. Also relates to rf2-3i7tr (the head-policy normative-home ruling) — if Mike rules the policy moves to Spec 011, this bead's surface moves with it.

title: Make the deferred-dispatch docstring guard prove enclosure
description:
PR #6284 makes every named deferred-callback example currently copyable, but its focused `testid` docstring guard does not actually prove lexical binding context. The new regex is `#"\(rf/reg-view [\s\S]*?#\(dispatch "`: it only requires a `reg-view` occurrence somewhere earlier in the docstring.

Reproduced in the same JavaScript-RegExp-compatible shape: it returns true for `(rf/reg-view already-closed [] [:div])\n[:button #(dispatch [:x])]`. Here the view has already closed and the deferred fragment is detached, so `dispatch` is unresolved—the exact regression rf2-ywwpx was supposed to turn red. The test description says the enclosing form "BINDS" the later dispatch, but the assertion proves only textual ordering.

Tighten this without a prose/Clojure parser. Pin the small canonical `counter-inc-button` example as one exact (or whitespace-normalized exact) snippet including its enclosing close, and add the already-closed/detached string as a negative control for whatever focused predicate is used. Keep the dual JVM/CLJS fixture and the existing explicit rejection of bare `#(rf/dispatch ...)`. Do not introduce a balanced-form parser or documentation framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- The focused fixture passes the current canonical `rf/reg-view counter-inc-button` snippet and proves its deferred `#(dispatch ...)` sits within that shown form.
- An already-closed `rf/reg-view` followed by a detached dispatch fragment fails the guard.
- A detached fragment with no binding form and a bare deferred `#(rf/dispatch ...)` remain red.
- The guard runs on both JVM and CLJS and stays narrowly tied to this canonical docstring example.
- No Clojure/Markdown parser, generated-doc framework, callback helper, or runtime change.

title: Rule 6b(i) :contextType suppression is blunt proximity — tighten it
description: FOUND by rf2-szw6c (#6299) and deliberately NOT fixed (outside that bead's acceptance; tightening changes an existing rule's semantics corpus-wide). scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py Rule 6b(i) suppresses a :contextType residue hit whenever 'Reagent' appears within ~40 chars (regex ':contextType[^.]{0,40}Reagent'). Concrete false-negative found in spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md: a :contextType attribution injected immediately BEFORE the lawful clause 'the reg-view macro stays Reagent-flavoured' is suppressed by that nearby 'Reagent' — so an unlawful attribution can hide next to a lawful mention. FIX: make the suppression attribution-aware rather than proximity-aware (e.g. require the Reagent token to be the SUBJECT of the same clause, or bound the window to the same sentence/clause rather than 40 chars). ⚠️ CAUTION: this rule runs corpus-wide over 50 skill leaves — tightening WILL surface currently-suppressed hits. Before changing it, run the current rule with suppression disabled to enumerate what a tightened rule would newly flag, and triage each (real residue vs lawful mention) so the change does not dump a wall of false positives. Report that inventory in the PR. Surface: scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py (Rule 6b(i) + its --self-test). Gate: --verbose + --self-test green; the 4 bounded blocks szw6c anchored (Rule 6c) must stay green.
notes:
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-18 18:10 AUSEST)

RULING: Option C — repair Rule 6b(i)'s attribution SCOPE and DELETE the proximity suppression; do not refine the suppression. This block is self-contained; the dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-xlxrl.contexttype-suppression-boundary.md) is retired/deleted.

SURFACE: scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py only — Rule 6b(i) in hooks_sentence_problems, the CONTEXTTYPE_REAGENT_OWNED_RE regex (~lines 463-467), and the --self-test fixtures (~lines 1281-1423). NOT hot-zone (scripts/ is not on the hot-zone list). Zero corpus edits are expected; if the implementation somehow ends up touching spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md or any other spec/ file (Rule 6c anchors), THAT is hot-zone and the mayor must sequence it.

THE DECIDED RULE:
1. Clause carving for 6b(i): split the sentence at strong clause separators — `;`, em dash `—`, and the contrast connectives `, while` / `, whereas` / `, but`. Do NOT split at `:` (that regresses the S2 fixture "UIx is not special: reg-view* gives it :contextType.", which must stay red). The connectives are required: carving alone leaves the lawful "Reagent's wrapper gives the component `:contextType`, while UIx uses `use-frame`." red.
2. DELETE all three arms of CONTEXTTYPE_REAGENT_OWNED_RE (Reagent-forward proximity, token-forward proximity, comparison-cue arm). Nothing live or self-tested depends on any arm — see EMPIRICAL FACTS.
3. The only Reagent-ownership allowance that remains: the token-adjacent possessive/compound — `Reagent's :contextType` / `Reagent-only :contextType` — recognised inside a clause that names a hooks adapter (it keeps "UIx components never get Reagent's `:contextType`." green, where the 8-char negation window misses). A clause that names Reagent and no hooks adapter is simply not a hooks clause and is never evaluated by 6b(i).
4. Keep the existing tightly-scoped "no `:contextType`" hooks negation (CONTEXTTYPE_NEGATED window), applied per clause.
5. REQUIRED ambiguity branch (not polish): a clause carrying `:contextType` plus a positive attribution verb but naming neither adapter, inside a sentence that names a hooks adapter, FAILS with a rewrite diagnostic ("name the owner or split the sentence"). This is load-bearing, not just principle: under clause carving, the existing Rule 6c block-mutation self-tests (e.g. the views-row insertion "use-frame, which gives the component a `:contextType`", fixture ~line 1376) land in a `;`-separated cell away from the adapter token — WITHOUT the ambiguity branch those established red mutations silently go green and the self-test loses its teeth.
6. Failure message: name the failing clause; suggest either "say the hooks adapter has no `:contextType`" or "split the Reagent comparison into a separate clause / name the owner explicitly".
7. Stay a bounded regex guard (~30 lines proven sufficient by prototype). No prose parser, no escape-hatch annotation (no corpus evidence either is needed).

SELF-TEST EXPECTATIONS (pin the fifteen validated probe shapes; at minimum):
RED — the reproduced false negative as a regression case, BOTH directions: (a) "On UIx / Helix, `reg-view*` gives the component a `:contextType`; the `reg-view` macro stays Reagent-flavoured." (passes today — the demonstrated hole); (b) "The macro stays Reagent-flavoured; UIx gets a `:contextType` too." (also green today). Also red: S2 stray-far-"not"; the ambiguity shape "UIx is not special; reg-view* gives it `:contextType`." (caught via the ambiguity branch); the Rule 6c block mutations.
GREEN — S3 "UIx/Helix differ from Reagent's `:contextType` mechanism." (note: green because it has NO attribution verb — it never depended on the comparison arm); S4 explicit hooks negation; S5 Reagent-only sentence; V2 Reagent-owned comparison; the token-adjacent possessive "UIx components never get Reagent's `:contextType`."; the `, while` mixed sentence; and the per-adapter semicolon HOUSE STYLE: "On Reagent register it via `reg-view*`, which gives the class a `:contextType`; on UIx / Helix carry the frame with `use-frame`." — this shape is a false positive under the CURRENT rule and under Option B; it must be green under the new rule.
ACCEPTED BOUNDARY: the period-variant pronoun attribution ("UIx is not special. reg-view* gives it `:contextType`.") is uncatchable today and stays uncatchable. Consistent, statable, not worth a parser.

EMPIRICAL FACTS WORTH PRESERVING (measured against the live checker, HEAD 2f4e8d8d2b, corpus unchanged since f5281a3b):
- The FULL --self-test passes with the Reagent-owned suppression disabled. Not one fixture depends on any of its three arms; their only measurable behaviour today is the false negative.
- The 40-char proximity rule ALREADY false-positives on the corpus's own house style (per-adapter semicolon sentences) — at natural prose distances the Reagent-to-token gap exceeds 40 chars; the shipped frames.md:24 survives only because it also says "no `:contextType`". The suppression fails in both directions at once: pardons the unlawful adjacency, fails to protect the lawful idiom.
- Suppression-dependent hits in the live corpus: ZERO. 50 leaves / 7,416 lines + 4 bounded blocks; 11 :contextType occurrences on 7 physical lines; only the two frames.md lines become hooks-recipe sentences with the token and both are green via the tight negation, not the suppression. Re-running with the suppression deleted produces zero new findings.
- Option B (delete suppression, keep shared sentence scope) was measured to turn four natural lawful shapes red including the house style — its zero-new-findings result is fragile (one ordinary rewording away from fighting the corpus voice). Rejected in favour of C. Options A (keep hole) and D (parser) rejected.

CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION:

title: Preserve record type in Xray concrete-query selectors
description:
PR #6274's local `canonical-str` promises an injective encoding of the full concrete-query identity, but its first branch is `(map? x)`. ClojureScript records satisfy `map?`, so the encoder discards their record tag/type and emits only canonicalized entries. Distinct concrete queries can still receive one `data-testid`.

Exact ClojureScript probe on current dependencies:
- `(defrecord A [x])`, `(defrecord B [x])`
- `a = (->A 1)`, `b = (->B 1)`, `m = {:x 1}`
- `(map? a)` and `(map? b)` are true.
- `(= a b)` and `(= a m)` are false.
- Applying the PR's map rendering to each produces the same string `{:x 1}`.

The product already calls out records as legal concrete query arguments in its fresh-object cache diagnostic (`map / collection / record built inline`), so this is not an exotic host-object expansion. Two surviving unchanged-sub rows keyed by these unequal query vectors remain unaddressable independently, violating rf2-haoip's every-distinct-valid-query AC and the updated normative Xray claim.

Preserve the small local solution. Add an explicit, stable record-type discriminator before canonicalizing record entries (and keep unordered extension entries canonical), or use an existing type-preserving canonical identity codec if one already exactly fits. Do not replace this test-id helper with a general EDN/DOM serialization framework. Audit the other supported scalar/tagged identity types while touching the encoder; state an honest supported domain if some values are deliberately excluded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Concrete queries containing different record types with identical entries mint distinct selectors; a record and a plain map with identical entries also differ.
- Equal instances of the same record type, including equal extension maps built in different insertion orders, mint one stable selector.
- Existing map/set insertion-order canonicality and the hash-collision pair remain correct.
- React keys, labels, `data-query-v`, projection, ordering, and unparameterized rows are unchanged.
- The test uses real ClojureScript records and proves each selector addresses exactly one row.
- The correction stays local/type-preserving; no general serializer or runtime registry is introduced.

title: Add public frame-destroyed :op to the canonical tags schema
description:
PR #6254 deliberately ratified `:op` as a public, small closed-enum realm attribution on `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`, and the runtime now emits it in BOTH always-on record attrs and dev-trace tags at captured-operation seams. Spec 009 accurately catalogues the public field and values. The canonical porting schema did not move with that decision: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` still defines `FrameDestroyedTags` as only `:category`, `:frame`, optional `:rf.event/v`, and optional `:rf.sub/query-v`.

Spec-Schemas says these per-category schemas are the canonical CLJS-reference shapes that ports translate mechanically. Its open-map convention means the implementation is not rejected at runtime, but omission of a deliberately public discriminator makes the mechanical contract incomplete: a port or tool generated from the schema cannot discover or constrain `:op`, and the schema no longer describes the reference emitter's known payload. All-state Bead searches for `FrameDestroyedTags`, frame-destroyed schema, and public `:op` found the closed source Bead rf2-a2x2w and historical runtime owners, but no current owner for this remaining schema drift.
design: Make the smallest contract repair: add optional `:op` to `FrameDestroyedTags`, using the exact public closed enum ratified by Spec 009 (`:dispatch`, `:dispatch-sync`, `:subscribe`, `:capture`), with a short note that ordinary address-directed emitters omit it when the realm is not known. Do not close the map, change emitters, add a new schema framework, or invent separate per-seam schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- `FrameDestroyedTags` contains optional `:op` with exactly the four public values ratified by Spec 009.
- The schema/comment states that the slot is present only where the emit site knows the operation realm; ordinary address-directed recovery remains valid without it.
- Spec 009 and Spec-Schemas agree on the field name, enum, optionality, and trace-tag role.
- Any focused schema/doc consistency gate passes; no runtime behavior or general schema machinery changes.

title: Make the SSR adoption regression execute the canonical startup recipe
description:

The mirror has already drifted in an adjacent detail: the real client-only branch dispatches `[:ssr/client-bootstrap]` before mounting, while the mirror does not. The browser assertions themselves are strong (exact server-child identity, live click handler, retained root, and fresh client-only mount), but they prove only the duplicate test implementation.

The source Bead explicitly required executing the payload-backed canonical SSR client boot path and a proof that causally fails when that path regresses. It allowed either the canonical recipe itself or the smallest shared seam it directly executes. The PR notes that co-loading the example in the consolidated browser bundle currently collides on `:auth.session/store`; that is a test-packaging constraint, not a reason to sever the causal dependency.

Current-main validation: the full browser suite is green (450 tests / 2505 assertions), demonstrating the false-green rather than a runtime failure. Git history after #6250 has not changed either the test or canonical example. All-state searches for the mirror, canonical startup recipe, and `ssr.core/run` found only closed rf2-byio7 / historical SSR owners and open rf2-8vi4q (the separate dev annotation-parity question); no Bead owns this causal gap.

Alternatively, place the browser proof in an isolated build that can load and invoke the actual example. Resolve the duplicate `:auth.session/store` registration only as narrowly as needed for that test topology. Do not add a general SSR harness, public framework API, compatibility layer, or reflection over example source text.
acceptance_criteria:
- The browser regression executes `ssr.core/run` itself or one production/example helper that `ssr.core/run` directly calls; there is no copied payload-vs-client-only mount conditional in the test.
- Changing the real canonical payload-backed path to `create-root` + `render` makes the regression fail.

- Any example-registration collision is resolved narrowly, and the canonical example remains runnable/copyable.
- The focused SSR/browser gates pass; no general test harness or public API is introduced.

title: Presence ruled DOM-agnostic/timeout-only: reconcile SPresence prose + ui/presence docstring to the ruling
description:
RULED 2026-07-18 (delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18 - full rationale in NOTES): presence stays DOM-AGNOSTIC and TIMEOUT-ONLY. No per-child wrapper/clone; :timeout-ms stays MANDATORY as THE exit retention duration and terminal bound; the three automatic refinements (transitionend early-completion, inert/aria-hidden on exit, reduced-motion immediate path) are REJECTED as framework automatics - presence-aware children own them via (presence-phase) = :unmounting. The SPresence prose bullets promising them are drift from the recorded Resolved-decisions ruling ('no reserved nodes'); this bead now carries the reconciliation.

SCOPE (doc/prose-only; spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE - sequence): (1) spec/004-Views.md SPresence ~553-563 - retract the three automatic promises; reword :timeout-ms as the explicit retention duration + terminal bound; add author-facing guidance (child stamps inert/aria-hidden + exit class against :unmounting; the child's stylesheet owns prefers-reduced-motion); keep the hydration sentence and the 'not an animation system' framing. (2) implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc ui/presence docstring - drop 'exit completes OR ... whichever first'. (3) Sweep docs/ + skills/ for echoes of the retracted promises. Resolved-decisions line ~1213 and S4 conformance row ~1161 stand UNCHANGED. NO runtime/grammar/test changes; JVM parity untouched.

ACs: spec prose, public docstring, and runtime agree on timeout-only; no automatic-DOM promise remains on any tracked surface; the rf2-74vlo coupling honoured (presence-exit-interactive remedy = author-owned stamping, never framework inert-on-exit). Future seam (child-attached exit-scoped completion signal racing the mandatory timeout) is consumer-gated on the first presence-using re-com widget (rf2-6ajm6z) - new bead then, per NOTES.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18 14:57 AUSEST, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18):
D1 = STAY MINIMAL / DOM-AGNOSTIC. The presence surface does NOT expand: no per-child DOM wrapper, no clone/ref contract, no automatic transitionend completion, no automatic inert/aria-hidden, no framework-owned reduced-motion path.
D3 = :timeout-ms stays MANDATORY - it is THE exit retention duration and terminal bound, not a safety cap over a completion mechanism that does not exist.
D2 = the follow-through (spec-prose retraction) happens NOW; this bead is re-scoped to carry it.

RATIONALE (spot-verified against main 2026-07-18):
1. The spec-already-promises reframe, verified - and decisive in the OPPOSITE direction from the dossier's Option-C reading. spec/004-Views.md SPresence prose (~553-563) does promise all three refinements while the runtime (presence_runtime.cljc) is timeout-only, so staying minimal is indeed not a no-op: a spec edit is required either way. BUT the prose contradicts the recorded Resolved-decisions ruling itself (line ~1213: 'wrapper form, NO RESERVED NODES; :timeout-ms mandatory') and the section's own boundedness declaration ('not an animation system - anything beyond enter/exit retention is out of scope', ~544-545); the S4 conformance row (~1161) matches the implementation. The prose bullets are DRIFT from the ruling, not ruled promises. Retracting them RESTORES the recorded ruling; expanding would OVERTURN it. The truth defect is fixed by reconciling prose to ruling.
2. Grammar correctness: presence children are fragments, compiled defviews, foreign components, and host elements - no uniform DOM root. A framework-inserted wrapper breaks HTML content models (ul>li), direct-child selectors, and SSR/hydration shape (the JVM emitter renders a fragment); display:contents removes the box, not the node or the content-model problem. cloneElement cannot reach a component's DOM (the defview declared-props ABI does not forward unknown host props to its root). Every automatic mechanism is false for part of the legal child grammar; a small contract true for every legal child wins under the masterpiece posture.
3. transitionend is not a one-event fact: one event per transitioned property, bubbling from descendants, transitioncancel yields no end event, and zero-duration transitions (exactly what reduced-motion CSS produces) never start so they fire NOTHING - a timer must always exist, and automatic first-event completion is wrong without an unambiguous DOM root + transition inventory the grammar cannot supply.
4. Automatic inert/aria-hidden is not a free a11y win: aria-hidden over sequentially-focusable descendants is itself a WCAG violation (ACT rule 6cfa84), and the HTML spec cautions inert is for content that is also visually obscured/non-critical - product facts the boundary cannot infer. The layer with that knowledge is the child / component library: presence-aware children (re-com widgets) stamp their own inert/aria-hidden + exit class against (presence-phase) = :unmounting. Explicit over implicit; trust the programmer; the same posture that rejected Suspense-as-loading for hiding behaviour in the substrate.
5. Determinism preserved: timeout-only keeps flush-presence! the sole and COMPLETE exit driver on both hosts; a browser-event completion route would create behaviour unit tests cannot reach.

FUTURE SEAM (ruled direction, consumer-gated - do NOT implement now; do NOT re-litigate from scratch): if the re-com port (rf2-6ajm6z) proves early completion materially necessary, the sanctioned extension is a narrow, exit-incarnation-scoped, idempotent completion signal delivered through presence context which the CHILD attaches to its own chosen DOM event (e.g. its onTransitionEnd on the root it knows); it funnels into the existing exactly-once fire-timer! registry (presence_runtime.cljc ~107-121, verified race-ready: a completion route is just a second route into the same atomic claim) racing the still-mandatory :timeout-ms. Wrapper elements, cloning, computed-style inference, and automatic attribute stamping remain rejected even then. File that bead (discovered-from this one) only when the first presence-consuming re-com widget lands.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (this bead, re-scoped; doc/prose-only; spec/004-Views.md is HOT-ZONE - sequence per CLAUDE.md):
- SPresence (~553-563): bullet 1 - the exiting child is retained for exactly :timeout-ms (mandatory, unit-suffixed, THE exit retention duration and terminal bound); drop 'until its transition/animation completes ... safety bound'. Bullet 3 - drop 'exiting children are inert/aria-hidden by default; reduced-motion takes the immediate path'; replace with author-facing guidance: presence-aware children own their exit styling and a11y - stamp inert/aria-hidden and the exit class against (presence-phase) = :unmounting; the child's stylesheet owns prefers-reduced-motion. KEEP 'hydration does not fabricate enter transitions' (S5-adjacent, outside this ruling) and keep the 'not an animation system' framing (now fully honest).
- Resolved-decisions line ~1213: stands unchanged (it was already correct); may append '(:timeout-ms is the exit duration - rf2-0ufty)'.
- Conformance row ~1161: unchanged (accurately names the fixtures that exist).
- implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc ui/presence docstring (~612-614): remove 'until its exit completes OR ... whichever first' -> retained until the mandatory :timeout-ms retention bound fires. presence_runtime.cljc docstring already truthful - no change.
- NO runtime, grammar, or test changes. JVM parity untouched (presence-phase -> :present; structural node; flush-presence! sole driver) - verified all DOM/clock code is cljs-fenced.
- Sweep docs/ + skills/ for prose echoing the three promises at implementation time (git grep transitionend/inert/aria-hidden/reduced-motion near presence on tracked files).

COUPLING TO rf2-74vlo (S4-C - that ruling can rely on this one): the presence-exit-interactive diagnostic is PROMOTED from interim mitigation to the PRIMARY a11y mechanism for exit windows. Its remedy prose must point at author-owned inert/aria-hidden against (presence-phase) = :unmounting - NOT at a framework inert-on-exit, which this ruling rejects; no S4-C check may depend on framework inert-on-exit existing. S4-C's 'Deps: after A' stands satisfied by S4-A as shipped.
CONVERGENCE NOTE (2026-07-18 15:30): an independent Codex analysis of the same decision dossier arrived after the delegated ruling above was recorded. It CONCURS with the ruling in full (for 0ufty: same conclusion incl. the retract-the-prose-promises call, with additional platform-contract citations — per-property transitionend/CSS-Transitions §6, React cloneElement-fragility guidance, W3C ACT rule 6cfa84 making automatic aria-hidden over focusable descendants itself a violation). Two independent analyses converging strengthens this ruling; no reconciliation needed.

title: Prove the G13 timed interval contains its own dispatch and commit
description: PR #6217 makes the cold-first pre-hot witness causal to the timed-cycle order, but the evidence still proves only state before the timed dispatch. title: Dev-mode SSR hydration annotation asymmetry: client stamps data-rf-view, SSR emitter does not
description:
Discovered while proving rf2-byio7 (SSR startup recipe adopts server DOM).

In a DEV build, the reagent CLIENT render stamps BOTH `data-rf2-source-coord` AND `data-rf-view` on a registered-view (`reg-view`) root DOM element (re-frame.views.source-coord-annotation / substrate.spine cloneElement). The SSR HTML emitter `rf/render-to-string` (re-frame.ssr.emit/inject-coord-on-root-hiccup) stamps ONLY `data-rf2-source-coord` — never `data-rf-view`. reagent.dom.server/render-to-string of the same tree likewise did not reproduce the client annotations in a quick probe.

Consequence: for a REGISTERED view, server markup (from either emitter) can never byte-match the same view's dev client hydrate render, so React 18 treats hydration as a mismatch and REGENERATES the subtree — discarding the server DOM (the 'no flash / adopt existing DOM' property is lost in dev). Production elides both annotations (interop/debug-enabled? gate + closure DCE), so prod hydration is clean; the divergence is dev-only.

This is why the rf2-byio7 proof (PR #6250) uses a PLAIN component (no view annotations either side) to get a clean adopt signal, rather than a reg-view.

Scope to decide: (a) confirm/quantify — does the SHIPPED capability example (examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr, reg-view-based) actually regenerate on dev hydration? (b) if so, should the SSR emitter also stamp data-rf-view for parity (making dev adoption clean), or is the dev-only regeneration acceptable (prod is fine)? The existing source_coord_parity_test only pins the data-rf2-source-coord VALUE format across hosts, not that both sides emit data-rf-view.

Files: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc (inject-coord-on-root-hiccup), implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs, implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (~1354).
notes:
RULING (Mike, 2026-07-18 18:00 AUSEST): Dev-mode view annotation is part of the view-registration contract on every host; SSR emitters carry no annotation logic. This is a dev-tooling decision, not an SSR feature: data-rf2-source-coord and data-rf-view are debug-gated development evidence for the programmer and AI tooling. Production output is annotation-free on both hosts and stays that way. The dev hydration warning is cited as the evidence the server half of the contract was missing, not as the thing being fixed.

IMPLEMENTATION (Option A-prime from the decision analysis; the emitter-side Option A is rejected — it only reaches keyword-ref boundaries, which hydratable pages cannot use):

1. In core reg-view* :clj branch, wrap the registered :handler-fn in a debug-gated annotation walk mirroring Spec 006's client injection rules: merge both :data-rf2-source-coord and :data-rf-view (value = (str id), same as client format-view-id) onto a hiccup DOM-tag root; preserve author-supplied values; recurse through Form-2 fns; skip fragment/fn-head roots per the documented exemption; degrade coordless (programmatic) registrations to the client's <ns>:<sym>:?:? coord form so both hosts match there too.

2. DELETE emitter-side injection: inject-coord-on-root-hiccup and both call sites (re-frame.ssr.emit, re-frame.ssr.streaming). Streaming shell/fallbacks/continuations inherit annotation through the wrapped handler-fn. This also removes the latent dev-mode arity leak where a keyword view-ref root got the coord map spliced in as the inner view's first argument.

3. No config knob, no wrapper element, no hydration-warning suppression, no post-hydration DOM patch, no ownership of Reagent's separate server renderer.

4. Specs: Spec 011 says SSR mirrors Spec 006's full view-tagging contract at the registration boundary (both attributes, value format, root exemption, preservation, production gate); Spec 006 names the registration boundary as the single architectural home on every host. Both are hot-zone files — sequence the spec edits.

5. Tests: standard + streaming parity; debug on/off; author-supplied value preservation; fn-ref composition parity against the client wrapper's output (the shape hydratable pages actually use); keyword-root shape; coordless-slot degrade parity; render-hash verify on the shipped example flow; browser hydration regression with a REGISTERED view (server node identity survives, handler live, NO hydration warning, both attributes present). Correct the plain-component adoption test's causal commentary: on React 18.3/19.2 an attribute-only mismatch warns and is left unpatched but does NOT replace the node — this bead's original "React regenerates the subtree" claim is refuted by browser probe.

KEY EVIDENCE (full dossier ai/decisions/rf2-8vi4q.dev-ssr-view-annotation-parity.md removed after ruling, per Mike): keyword view-refs are resolved only by the two JVM emitters and cannot render client-side (Reagent parse-tag drops keyword namespaces), so isomorphic pages compose via (rf/view :id) fn-refs, where the JVM stores the raw unwrapped handler-fn — emitter-side annotation therefore never fires on any boundary a hydratable page actually contains; the shipped non-streaming example reaches its DOM root with neither attribute server-side while the client stamps both.

Separate follow-up (NOT in this ruling's scope): the streaming example's shared views embed keyword refs ([:dashboard/card :revenue]) that the client renders as literal <card> DOM tags — deeper isomorphism break, filed as its own bead.
⚠️ YOU NOW INHERIT A HALF-DONE STEP 2 — from rf2-j81hs (#6378, 2026-07-19).

The j81hs ruling §5 said to sequence emit.cljc/streaming.cljc with-or-after this bead. That sequencing was INVERTED in practice: j81hs landed first because this bead is open, unclaimed, with no PR and no live worker (so there was no edit collision, but also nothing to sequence behind).

CONSEQUENCE, per the ruling that the coord injection "dies WITH the branch": server-side source-coord annotation is now STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE. j81hs deleted the keyword-head probe from both emitters and removed registrar + interop as dead requires, leaving the JVM emitter a pure hiccup->HTML function with no registry dependency.

WHAT j81hs DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR YOU: format-view-source-coord and inject-coord-on-root-hiccup are still in place. It did NOT delete them, so as not to pre-empt this beads design. It pinned the interim ABSENCE in both affected namespaces, and re-pinned the production-elision guarantee as an UNCONDITIONAL so it cannot lapse in the gap.

SO YOUR SCOPE IS NOW: decide whether the dev-mode SSR hydration annotation asymmetry (client stamps data-rf-view, SSR does not) is resolved by deleting those two functions outright, or by re-establishing the annotation through a route that does not reintroduce a registry dependency in the emitter. Read gh pr diff 6378 first — the emitter purity it achieved is a real simplification and should not be undone casually.

⚠️ Also from j81hs: examples/ README still asserts the emitter resolves keyword heads, which is now FALSE. That correction is owned by rf2-ycz3k (the example rewrite), not by this bead.

Emitter-side format-view-source-coord + inject-coord-on-root-hiccup DELETED (call sites already gone in #6378); ssr.cljc re-export removed. Tests: JVM ssr_source_coord_test rewritten (annotation-present + prod-gate arms), source_coord_parity_test extended to pin data-rf-view + end-to-end callable-head render, CLJS parity companion extended, NEW browser twin-run adoption proof (reg-view adopts annotated server markup / RED-before complains), byio7 causal commentary corrected, ssr_keyword_head_contract + smoke updated for the new dev annotation. title: Remove :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook — SSR-owned pattern-protocol constant read by both wire ends
description:

TASK: delete the :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook and make the SSR artefact own the hydration pattern-protocol version as a compiled-in constant (initially 1) read by both wire ends — server payload assembly (payload_policy.cljc resolve-version) and the client-side scalar :rf.ssr/check-version path (hydrate.cljc runtime-version-lookup). Keep the explicit :version payload-builder opt (higher priority) and the {:expected :actual} map form. Wire key :rf/version ([:rf/version :int], Spec-Schemas.md:3592) unchanged. Census baseline: 44 mentions across 14 files (2 src consumers, ~20 test sites, 3 hot-zone specs, docs/api + skills pages). One sequential PR (hot-zone: spec/011-SSR.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, spec/Conventions.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Zero occurrences of :rf2/runtime-version in tracked files (git grep clean; baseline 44 mentions / 14 files).
- Version resolution: explicit :version opt -> SSR-owned constant; invalid explicit values emit :rf.ssr/invalid-version and fall back; every payload carries an integer :rf/version.
- Scalar :rf.ssr/check-version compares the server value against the compiled constant; genuine skew emits :rf.ssr/version-mismatch; hydration stays degraded-but-running; the version-side compatibility-check-skipped branch is removed (schema-digest half keeps the emit alive).

- Tests updated including the deliberate meaning shift (skipped-mode baselines -> silent 1==1 match), called out in commit/PR text; docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md + skills ssr-authoring.md updated.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): REMOVE the :rf2/runtime-version late-bind hook. Replace it with an SSR-artefact-owned pattern-protocol constant (integer, initially 1) read by BOTH wire ends — server payload assembly and the client-side scalar :rf.ssr/check-version path. Keep the explicit payload-builder :version opt and the {:expected :actual} map form for overrides/tests. NO host-published directory marker, NO facade/configure! knob, NO :ssr/ rename half-measure.

RATIONALE (keystones spot-verified during ruling): (1) DEAD BY DEFAULT — the in-tree reference Ring host (implementation/ssr-ring) never registers the hook (sole mention: payload.clj:35 docstring); the only set-fn! sites are test fixtures, so the promised check runs in skipped mode in every real deployment including our own. (2) OWNERSHIP BACKWARDS — Spec-Schemas.md:3592/3618 defines :rf/version as the hydration pattern-protocol version, a fact compiled into the SSR artefact's wire code; a host cannot know it better than the artefact, and a host publishing a different value lies to the check. Both consumers (payload_policy.cljc:707, hydrate.cljc:436) live in the same artefact — no cross-artefact boundary for a late-bind hook to solve. (3) LONE SQUATTER — :rf2/runtime-version is the only framework :rf2/* key; the Conventions:1706 grammar row's other example claims are falsified in-tree (the schema digest ships as :schemas/app-schemas-digest with a real producer + directory row). Server and client chains are asymmetric. (5) GOVERNANCE OPTIONS ARE MACHINERY TO PRESERVE THE DEFECT — a directory row fails 3 drift-gate assertions without a host-published exemption (late_bind_drift_test.clj:248,276,327), making the parity invariant conditional for every future row; a public mutable API mints an unjustified facade export for a value with one honest producer. title: State only portable next-tick guarantees across CLJS and JVM
description:

On the JVM, `interop.clj` says the single-thread executor callback runs "after the caller returns". `Executor.execute` creates no such ordering edge: the worker may start concurrently before `next-tick` returns. Spec 002 already states that this can happen and uses the drain lock to make it safe.

State the exact guarantees only: asynchronous task-style scheduling, not a host microtask; implementation choice and relative start-versus-return timing are host-dependent. This is wording/test naming, not a scheduler redesign.

- CLJS docs say `goog.async.nextTick` is task/macrotask scheduling and accurately describe preferred immediate/message-channel mechanisms plus the supported setTimeout fallback; they do not promise absence of timer clamping.
- JVM docs say the callback runs asynchronously on the executor and may start concurrently with the submitting caller; they do not promise it starts after the call returns.
- Spec 002, interop docstrings/comments, and focused test namespace/names assert only the portable microtask-vs-task boundary.

- `ledger-state` is an unconditional `defonce (atom {:sources {} :cycles {}})`;
- every production `register-custom-element!` still performs `swap-vals!` against that atom before updating `custom-elements`;
- production cannot open a reload cycle, so this state is unused bookkeeping rather than part of classification.

The added production test proves that producer installation is inert, the identity falls back, and the visible classification works. It does not inspect hidden source/cycle state. The bundle scanners also carry no custom-element ledger sentinel. Thus the test comments promise a stronger elision result than the artefact proves or delivers.

## Deliverable

Use a compile-time `goog.DEBUG` split in the CLJS registration/state path: development keeps the existing source/cycle ledger; advanced production performs the one direct aggregate update it actually needs. Keep the JVM path needed by compiler/test fixtures. Add both lexical and causal elision proof so a future refactor cannot leave a renamed rooted atom behind.

This is a small pre-alpha cleanup, not a generalized registry abstraction or micro-optimization campaign.

## Provenance and dedupe

Found during the chronological completeness/quality audit of PR #6018. All-status search found only closed `.142`; no live issue owns the production residue.
acceptance_criteria:
- In advanced CLJS production, emitted custom-element registration updates the live property classification directly; no source/cycle ledger atom is allocated, rooted, read, or mutated.
- The dev build retains the one authoritative ledger and all reload semantics unchanged; JVM/test behavior remains available where required.
- A lexical advanced-bundle sentinel proves the ledger/reload state is unreachable, and a causal runtime oracle proves registration leaves no hidden ledger/root residue.
- A development-positive control proves the sentinel would fail if the ledger branch were accidentally removed from dev as well.
- Production lookup stays a direct map read and emitted registration remains once per declaration, never per render.
- No second production registry, public switch, compatibility branch, or measurable per-render cost is introduced.

title: Make observation current? total across throwing opaque equality
description:
## Current defect

PR #6014 / rf2-tuysqw reconciled the observation-port prose so `current?` is a total, pure, never-throw predicate, matching its docstring and the malformed/non-lease behavior. A supported `:story-override` lease can nevertheless throw through its opaque version comparison:

```clojure
(deftype Boom [] Object
  (equals [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom-from-equals" {}))))

(let [target {:kind :story-override
              :query [:demo/q]
              :value nil
              :override-id :slot
              :version (Boom.)}
      lease (obs/acquire! target nil)]
  (obs/current? lease (assoc target :version (Boom.))))
```

Current JVM result is `THREW boom-from-equals`. The target passes the port grammar and acquisition; the exception escapes later through `node-value=`. Non-lease `current?` and `owned?` correctly return false. All-status searches for throwing equality, opaque version, and current?/never-throws found no owner; closed rf2-tuysqw and rf2-vxgfnd.241 are related but do not cover opaque token equality.

## Bounded repair

Honor the total predicate contract at the kept-check boundary: an equality comparison that cannot establish sameness should classify the lease as not current, without weakening fail-loud behavior of the port’s non-predicate operations. Keep the catch local to predicate comparison unless evidence shows a shared no-throw equality helper is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- `current?` returns false, never throws, when a supported target/lease comparison encounters a version or identity token whose host equality implementation throws.
- Equivalent JVM and CLJS adversarial fixtures exercise throwing equality through a real acquired static/story-override lease.
- Ordinary identical/equal tokens remain current; unequal, released, malformed/non-lease, moved-frame, and retargeted controls retain their existing results.
- `probe`, `acquire!`, `read`, and `release!` keep their existing typed fail-loud contracts; the repair does not blanket-swallow equality failures outside the documented total predicate.
- Observation-port docs, Ownership wording, implementation docstrings, and tests continue to state one exact total/no-throw predicate contract.

title: Reject JVM child-thread mutation of a conveyed render capture
description:
## Problem

PR #5832 replaces the process-global ambient capture atom with a dynamic binding whose value is a `volatile!`. This correctly isolates separate JVM render threads, but Clojure conveys dynamic bindings into `future`/`pmap` workers. If one render body forks site reads and joins them, the child threads share the same non-thread-safe volatile capture and race `vswap!` at `reactive.cljc:726/780`.

The implementation contract is a deterministic, compiler-ordered render capture. Silently losing sites or corrupting order is worse than rejecting an unsupported parallel render body. The authored concurrency fixture runs separate renders, each with its own binding; it does not cover child-thread binding conveyance inside one render.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On JVM, enter `with-capture` for one render.
2. Spawn multiple `future` or `pmap` tasks that inherit `*ambient*`; have each perform a distinct `sub-read` or `lease-site`, then join them before the thunk returns.
3. All child threads mutate the same volatile capture.
4. In an exact-head 200-trial/16-site probe, 188 renders returned an incomplete capture; the minimum captured site count was one.
5. The call succeeds rather than reporting that render capture is single-threaded, so missing ownership can flow into commit/release logic.

## Required Correction

Enforce the intended single-threaded render-capture contract rather than engineering parallel render support. Record the JVM owner thread in the ambient capture and, before any `sub-read`/`lease-site` mutation, throw a typed malformed-tree/render-capture error if the current thread differs. Reject before mutating the capture. Separate top-level renders on different threads must remain valid because each has its own binding. Supporting parallel render bodies later would require atomic capture plus deterministic site ordering and is outside this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- JVM fixtures prove future- and pmap-conveyed `sub-read`/`lease-site` calls fail loudly with a typed error before capture mutation.
- The error identifies the render/site contract sufficiently for a developer to remove the fork; no partial ownership is committed.
- Separate concurrent top-level renders remain isolated and green.
- Nested same-thread captures preserve save/restore and deterministic site ordering.
- CLJS single-thread behavior and production output remain unchanged apart from development diagnostics as designed.
- A stress mutation that removes the owner-thread guard reproduces incomplete capture and fails the fixture.
