title: Framework: native React DevTools inspector panel for re-frame2 (à la Redux DevTools / Apollo / MobX)
description:
## Why

React DevTools has an extension API for libraries to register a
**custom inspector panel** for their components. Apollo Client,
MobX, Redux DevTools all use it — each gets a native presence in
DevTools' Components inspector alongside the standard Props /
State / Hooks panels.

re-frame2 could do the same. The substrate has rich data that no
generic React DevTools view can surface:

- The view's registered id (post-quick-wins bead, this is the
  React displayName — but the inspector panel can show MORE)
- Subs the view currently consumes + their LIVE values from the
  sub cache
- The frame the view is running in
- Last render epoch + duration (from the trace stream)
- Schema violations attached to the view or its parent handler
- Click-to-source jumping straight to the `reg-view` definition

This would make re-frame2 a first-class React DevTools citizen
the way Redux is — operators investigating a re-frame2 app
via DevTools see substrate context inline, not just generic
React props.

Blocks-on / sibling: P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX
source-coord props + Context labelling). The native inspector
builds on top of those.

## What changes — high level

A custom inspector panel registered with the React DevTools
backend API. The panel renders inside DevTools' Components
inspector right pane (alongside Props / State / Hooks), titled
"re-frame2".

For a selected reg-view'd component, the panel shows:

### Source surface
- Registered view-id (keyword)
- Source coord (file:line)
- "Open in editor" link → reuses Story's `open-in-editor` launcher

### Reactive surface
- Subs the view consumed during last render (read from sub
  cache; rf2-mrnur's dispose trace tells us the active
  derefer-set)
- Live values for each sub (via `edn-inspector/mini` for
  one-line rendering, expand-to-full inline)
- Visual indicator if any sub's value changed since last render

### Cascade surface
- Last render epoch-id + wall-clock duration
- "Show in Xray Trace" link → dispatches into the host's
  `:rf/xray` frame to focus that epoch
- Render-count since page load

### Frame surface
- Frame-id this view is in (`:rf/default` / `:rf/xray` / custom)
- Frame's preset / fx-overrides / etc. (from `rf/frame-meta`)

### Schema surface
- Any `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` events attached to
  the view's owning handler in the recent trace buffer
- Recovery posture (rolled-back / fx-skipped / etc.)

## Technical considerations

### React DevTools backend API

React DevTools is open-source; the API for libraries to
register inspector panels is in the `react-devtools-shared`
package (`reactDevtoolsAgent.addInspectorPanel(...)` or
similar — worker confirms exact API surface). Apollo's
implementation is a reference. The API is dev-only — there's
no production cost.

### Bundle isolation

The DevTools inspector code MUST live in a build path that
elides under `interop/debug-enabled? false`. The pattern
matches Xray's bundle-isolation contract (per
`npm run test:bundle-isolation`). Code lives in
`implementation/core/devtools/` or a sibling
`implementation/devtools/` artefact; nothing in production
paths `:requires` it.

### Cross-frame considerations

A view rendered under `:rf/xray` shows different data than the
same view under `:rf/default`. The inspector panel reads the
view's actual current frame (already known to the framework)
and surfaces frame-scoped data. Same view-id under two frames
shows two different sub-value sets.

### Hot-reload + identity

The inspector panel should survive `:after-load` hot-reloads of
the user's app. If the React DevTools backend tracks component
identity by displayName + position, the panel rebinds cleanly.
Worker confirms the API's reload semantics.

### Integration with existing Xray

The inspector panel's "Show in Xray Trace" link assumes the host
app has Xray installed. When Xray isn't present:
- Either degrade gracefully (link greyed out with tooltip "Xray
  not installed in this app")
- Or surface ALL the data inline in the DevTools panel without
  cross-linking

Lean: graceful degradation. The DevTools panel works
standalone; Xray is an optional cross-link surface.

## Possible scope additions (bundled or follow-on)

These naturally fold into the inspector panel work:

- **View args as named React props** (item 3 from pair-debug's
  bullet list): pretty-print CLJS view args instead of opaque
  varargs blobs. Reuses the inspector's edn rendering.
- **React Profiler integration** (item 6): tag `:rf.view/render`
  trace events with React's render-id so the operator can
  cross-reference Xray's per-cascade trace with React's profiler
  timeline.
- **Hot-reload identity preservation** (item 8): verify reg-view'd
  components preserve identity across `:after-load`. If they
  don't, fix or document.

Worker decides whether to fold into this bead or file as P4
follow-ons.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's runtime contracts — additive panel only
- Production builds — entire panel elides
- React DevTools itself — uses its existing extension API
- Xray's own surfaces — they remain the canonical heavy-data
  view; the DevTools inspector is the lighter Components-tab-
  embedded surface

## Acceptance

1. Loading a re-frame2 app with React DevTools installed shows a
   "re-frame2" subpanel in the Components inspector right pane
   when a reg-view'd component is selected.
2. Subpanel renders the source / reactive / cascade / frame /
   schema surfaces enumerated above.
3. Live values update as the underlying state mutates.
4. "Open in editor" + "Show in Xray Trace" links function (the
   latter degrades gracefully when Xray isn't installed).
5. Production builds elide the entire panel; bundle-isolation
   gate passes.
6. Worked example in `examples/<...>` demonstrates the inspector
   panel + documents the React DevTools setup required to see
   it.

## Coordination

- New code under `implementation/core/devtools/` (or a sibling
  artefact). Hot-zone consideration if it lives under core.
- Possibly spec/006 §Source-coord annotation + a new
  spec/DevTools-Integration.md normative doc.
- Pre-alpha posture: lock in to React DevTools backend API as
  the integration shape; no fallback for non-React-DevTools
  inspectors.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.

## Blocks-on

P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX source-coord props +
Context labelling). The native inspector layers on top of those
foundations.
notes: DEFERRED (Mike, 2026-05-28): post-alpha. Native React DevTools inspector panel is a feature epic; not pre-alpha-critical and Xray already covers live inspection (app-db, trace stream, epoch scrub). Revisit after alpha.
close_reason: REJECTED (2026-07-25). Two independent findings each settle it. (1) THE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG: React DevTools ships no public API for a library to register a custom inspector panel. react-devtools-shared is internal and unpublished with no documented extension points; the feature request for exactly this (facebook/react-devtools#1086) sits in a repository ARCHIVED 2020-06-26 and never shipped; Apollo Client DevTools and Redux DevTools are STANDALONE browser extensions with their own top-level tabs, not panels inside React DevTools; the addInspector/setupDevtoolsPlugin custom-inspector API the bead describes is VUE's, which is almost certainly where the premise came from. What React documents for libraries is only displayName, Context displayName and useDebugValue. So the bead is not expensive — as specified it is NOT BUILDABLE; the nearest buildable substitute is shipping and maintaining a re-frame2 browser extension (store listings, MV3 churn, a message-passing bridge), a materially larger commitment yielding a third surface rather than a panel. (2) ALREADY SERVED: all six requested surfaces (view-id, subs consumed with live values, owning frame, last render epoch, schema violations, click-to-source) are already rendered by Xray's Views tab (Dynamic tab 3 of 9, spec tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sec 3 - note 012-Views.md is superseded) plus the Epoch panel, and served to agents by the Tool-Pair MCP (list-subscriptions --include-values, read-sub, read-view-dependencies, explain-render, handler-meta, read-ui). The one gap is a per-view wall-clock duration column, which is a one-column Xray bead, not a reason for a second front-end. THE CHEAP HALF ALREADY SHIPPED under rf2-fa4ly: displayName, Context labelling (rf2-frame / rf2-sub-overrides) and data-rf2-source-coord are on main and work in React DevTools today. title: Audit local-atom-as-scratch-accumulator usage across the codebase; refactor to functional shape where idiomatic
description:
Mike directive 2026-05-11: prefer functional programming over imperative when given the choice; efficiency matters where it's measurable.

Mike spotted an instance at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:79 (pattern-shape) — three atoms (i, depth, seen) used as scratch accumulators inside a loop. Imperative-flavour code that would read more idiomatically as loop/recur threading state through.

Likely a class issue, not a one-off. Initial grep found 52 files matching the broad pattern (let [... (atom ...) ...] ...) but most are legitimate uses (registry atoms, test fixtures, async queues, anything where state persists or crosses thread boundaries). The smell is specifically: **local atoms used as scratch accumulators inside a tight loop, never escaping the function, where loop/recur or reduce/transducers would express the same algorithm functionally**.

## Audit scope

For each of the 52 files:
- Identify each (atom ...) call site at top of let binding.
- Classify:
  - LEGITIMATE: state genuinely needs to persist beyond the function (registry, fixture, queue), cross a boundary (async, thread), be observable to watchers, or back a public reactive API.
  - SCRATCH-SMELL: local accumulator inside a tight loop or recursive walk, never escapes, no concurrency.
  - HOT-PATH-EFFICIENCY: scratch-shape but materially faster than the functional alternative on a measurable hot path (worth keeping with a one-line rationale comment).

For each SCRATCH-SMELL site, propose a refactor (typically loop/recur threading the accumulator state, or a reduce/reduce-kv form).

## Principle (Mike's directive 2026-05-11)

Prefer functional over imperative. Trade-offs to weigh:
- **Readability**: functional is usually clearer. Win.
- **Aliasing safety**: functional is safer (immutable bindings can't be aliased). Win.
- **Performance**: imperative atom-mutate is sometimes faster on tight loops, but only when the loop is genuinely hot. For 99% of code paths, the difference is invisible.
- **Pre-release**: no back-compat concerns; refactor freely.

Rule: prefer functional unless there's measurable evidence the imperative form is needed for performance. If kept imperative for efficiency reasons, leave a rationale comment.

## Concrete starter

routing.cljc:79 (pattern-shape) — refactor to loop/recur threading [i depth seen]. ~15-line edit.

## Output

- findings/imperative-atoms-audit.md — per-file classification + refactor proposals.
- A bd bead per SCRATCH-SMELL site (or one bead per file, depending on volume).

## Dispatchability

Direction-set. Background agent can do the audit. The refactor work splits into per-bead PRs after Mike reviews the audit findings. Could batch into a single sweep PR if the volume is manageable.

Audit scope: SKIP these three; cover the rest of the 52 files matching the broad pattern. Output findings doc + file follow-up beads ONLY for sites not already covered by rf2-w0am/lckc/d6a2.

No HOT-PATH-EFFICIENCY sites found — every imperative-atom site has a functional alternative at parity. Test files all use atoms as legitimate assertion fixtures; not flagged. title: Independent research + refinement of re-frame-2-story SOTA features (compares vs rf2-m6tu)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-m6tu. Different framing: 'what features would make re-frame-2-story state-of-the-art?' rather than 'what should it minimally support?'

Two-phase work for one agent:

## Phase 1 — Independent research (no peeking at rf2-m6tu)

Agent does its own survey of component-development tools focused on the SOTA question:
- What's the highest-bar capability set? Not 'minimum viable.'
- Which tools (Storybook + non-Storybook) ship features that feel best-in-class?
- Cross-tool: what's been borrowed, refined, surpassed?
- Storybook addons (https://storybook.js.org/addons) — which are state-of-the-art? a11y? play / interactions / test? composition? designs? viewport with breakpoints? args + controls type-generation?
- Beyond Storybook: Histoire's vue-specific magic, Ladle's perf claims, React Cosmos's fixture model, Bit's component-as-package, Lookbook's Rails-flavoured ergonomics.
- The answer should reach for SOTA, not the average.

Agent writes its independent answer to a scratch file: findings/re-frame-2-story-sota-draft.md (or holds in agent memory).

## Phase 2 — Comparison + refinement

After own answer is written:
- Read findings/re-frame-2-story-feature-set.md (the rf2-m6tu output).
- Compare:
  - Where do they agree? (Confidence: both reached the same conclusion independently.)
  - Where does rf2-m6tu under-claim vs SOTA? (Add to refined doc.)
  - Where does rf2-m6tu over-claim vs realistic? (Question.)
  - Where does the independent SOTA framing surface features rf2-m6tu missed entirely?
- Refine the rf2-m6tu document in place: findings/re-frame-2-story-feature-set.md gets the synthesis.
- Drop the scratch draft after merging if used.

The refined doc should:
- Carry forward rf2-m6tu's organisation (don't restructure for its own sake).
- Add SOTA features the original missed.
- Surface tensions where SOTA-pursuit conflicts with re-frame2's ethos (e.g. 'Storybook composition is SOTA but conflicts with our spec-first / single-source-of-truth ethos — recommend skip').
- Preserve attribution: 'Refined 2026-MM-DD against independent SOTA research; the following sections were strengthened: ...'

## Why two-phase

Pre-loading the agent with rf2-m6tu's findings biases the research. Mike wants the independent eyes first — different agent, different framing prompt, no shared context — to surface SOTA features the original missed.

title: Interactive playground / tutorial for re-frame2 (inspired by Svelte's tutorial) — viable with self-hosted ClojureScript?
description:
Mike (2026-05-10): Svelte's tutorial at https://svelte.dev/tutorial is a brilliant interactive learning experience — edit code on the left, see live output on the right, compiled in the browser. Would love to create something like that for re-frame2.

## The question

Is self-hosted ClojureScript complete enough to power this?

## Background — what's needed

A Svelte-tutorial-like experience needs:
- In-browser code editing (Monaco / CodeMirror).
- In-browser compilation of user-edited code.
- Live execution into a sandboxed re-frame2 runtime.
- Tutorial step navigation with progressive concept reveal.

## Options — evaluate

### A. Self-hosted ClojureScript (cljs.js bootstrap)

CLJS can compile itself in-browser via cljs.js. Used by Klipse, Lambda Island, etc.

Open questions to research:
- Does Reagent work under self-hosted CLJS today? (Klipse demos suggest yes.)
- Does re-frame2's macro layer (reg-event-fx, reg-machine, reg-view, source-coord stamping) survive self-hosted bootstrap?
- Bundle size of cljs.js + Reagent + re-frame2 — is it acceptable for a tutorial site? (Likely 1-3MB minified.)
- First-compile latency — typical 'hello world' compile time in self-hosted CLJS is sub-second; complex deps slower.
- Macro packaging — re-frame2's macros need to ship as analyser metadata (cljs.analyzer) for self-hosted to expand them.
- Does the macro-rich code re-frame2 emits (reg-machine source-coord stamping, reg-view source-coord stamping) introspect okay under self-hosted?

### B. Klipse

Pre-built self-hosted CLJS playground. Mature. Used by lambdaisland.com and others. Could be embedded.

Open questions:
- Does Klipse handle re-frame2's adapter init (rf/init! adapter)?
- Per-step state isolation — Klipse cells share global state by default; may need adaptation.

### C. Pre-compiled snippets per step

Each tutorial step is a separately-compiled bundle. User clicks 'Next', the right-pane swaps to the next pre-compiled bundle. No in-browser compilation.

Pros: no self-hosted CLJS dep; bundle-per-step is small.
Cons: user can't edit code, defeating the Svelte-tutorial inspiration.

### D. Hybrid — pre-compiled lessons + Klipse for the user-edits-code part

Lesson narrative + hard-coded examples are pre-compiled; the 'try it' boxes are Klipse-powered. Best of both.

### E. Squint (CLJS-flavour to native JS)

https://github.com/squint-cljs/squint — fast in-browser compile. But: not full ClojureScript (subset). Macros work differently. Re-frame2's macro-heavy registration would likely need adaptation. Worth surveying.

## Likely answer

Self-hosted CLJS is viable but slow + large for a polished tutorial. A hybrid (lessons pre-compiled, Klipse for try-it boxes) is the pragmatic shape. Worth a research pass to confirm Reagent + re-frame2's macros work under self-hosted before investing.

## Disposition

P3 — post-beta. Outreach / DX investment, not pre-1.0 blocker. But the answer to 'self-hosted CLJS works?' affects what tooling we can ship in the guide chapters too (interactive snippets in docs/guide/).

## Recommended next step

A small spike: build one tutorial step ('your first counter') using self-hosted CLJS or Klipse, see if it works end-to-end. ~1 day of investigation. File as a separate bead when ready to spike.

title: CLJS reference: capture handler source-as-data on registration (dev-only)
description:
Mike's observation during the revertibility / atomification iteration: ClojureScript's macro story makes it natural for reg-* macros to capture the handler body as quoted-form data alongside the live fn value. The fn isn't serialisable; the source is.

Distinguish from source coords (already captured: :ns/:line/:file via existing macros). Source-as-data is the full quoted form of the handler body, attached as :rf/source on the registration entry.

Use cases (dev-only):
- AI introspection / explanation: AI reads handler source directly from the frame snapshot, no file-system access required.
- Pair-improver retrospective analysis: tool has handler source as input material for suggestions.
- Cross-process debugging snapshots: bug report includes frame value with handler source attached; dev loads snapshot complete with exact handlers, even after local source drift.
- Time-travel that survives hot-reload: snapshot remembers what each handler was at the moment the event fired.
- Auto-generated documentation: walk the registry, render docstrings + source.
- Conformance fixtures self-contained (overkill given fixtures-by-id, but possible).

Use cases that don't need source-as-data (work via plain serialisation already):
- SSR hydration (already specced).
- Persistence (localStorage / IndexedDB / backend).
- Bug reports (data only).
- Cross-tab sharing.
- Time-travel within a session.
- Test fixtures captured from real runs.

Cost / risks:
- Build size — strict dev-only.
- IP exposure — config flag to strip source before transmitting snapshots remotely.
- Deserialisation: source-as-data is for inspection; the live fn is what runs. Document carefully.

Where it fits in the spec:
- Pattern level: 'registrations are values' is already the spirit of the registry-in-app-db design.
- CLJS reference: dev-build macros attach :rf/source; production-build macros omit it (compile-time elide). Document in 009 §Instrumentation alongside source-coords.
- Conventions.md: reserve :rf/source as a metadata key (dev-only).
- Host-profile matrix: flag as CLJS-specific affordance other hosts may not match cheaply.

Action items (deferred):
1. Spec the macro extension for :rf/source capture.
2. Add :rf/source to the reserved metadata-keys list in Conventions.md.
3. Document compile-time elision in production builds (parallel to existing trace elision).
4. Spec the snapshot-strip mechanism for source before transmission.
5. Update 009 §Instrumentation with the dev-mode capture story.
6. AI-Audit: revisit AI-introspection rows once source-as-data is available.

Status: deferred — explore when dev-mode tooling sections of 009 are firmed up, and when the AI-introspection / pair-improver story is being concretised. Not blocking any v1 lock.
design:
SHIPPED MECHANISM (reg-event, dev-only)
compile-time pr-str of &form -> bound through the source-coords/*pending-form-source* dynamic var -> merged into registry metadata by the registrar. Two elision layers, both gated on interop/debug-enabled?: the macro emits (if interop/debug-enabled? <pr-str> nil), and the registrar gates the merge again. implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs pins the absence in the release bundle by asserting on the rf.handler/source keyword plus a captured-form sentinel.

Key pieces:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:291-336 (defreg-event-macro)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc (*pending-form-source*, already a GENERIC dynamic var)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:871-896,976-1040 (private merge-form-source; register-event!)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc:93-132 (machine guard/action source derived from the enclosing machine spec, not duplicated onto registrar rows)

DESIGN FOR THE DEFERRED WIDENING (do not build until a named consumer exists — see notes for the trigger)
Widening to the other fourteen registrars rides existing machinery; no new machinery is needed.
1. *pending-form-source* in source_coords.cljc is already generic. Nothing to change.
2. The only event-specific piece is the private merge-form-source in events.cljc. Move it to the shared registrar/register! chokepoint, exactly where source-coords/merge-coords already sits at each registrar.
3. With 2 done, the defreg-macro / defreg-event-macro split collapses into ONE macro. The fourteen coordinate-only call sites in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc then get the slot for free: reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx, reg-interceptor, reg-flow, reg-route, reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-resource-scope, reg-app-schema, reg-app-schemas, reg-error-projector, reg-head, reg-http-interceptor.
4. Elision story is IDENTICAL — same (if interop/debug-enabled? <pr-str> nil) macro gate plus the same registrar-side gate. check-elision.cjs extends by adding strings to its assertion list.
5. Delete or invert implementation/core/test/re_frame/handler_source_test.clj:127-136, which currently asserts reg-sub does NOT carry the slot.

COSTS OF THAT WIDENING (real but modest)
- More dev-bundle bytes. A reg-sub-heavy app has many more subs than events, so this is the dominant term, not a rounding error.
- Hot-zone tax: spec/009-Instrumentation.md and spec/Conventions.md are both sequential-lane files, so a widening PR cannot run parallel with anything else touching them.

SHORT VERSION: this bead shipped in May 2026 under a different key name than it proposed, and nobody came back to close it. The release condition ("when 009 dev-mode tooling is firm and the AI-introspection / pair-improver story is concretised") expired in May.

== WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED ==
- Key is :rf.handler/source, NOT the :rf/source this bead proposed. It landed under the :rf.handler/* sub-namespace rather than colonising the single-root :rf/* set. THIS IS THE REASON THE BEAD LOOKED UNIMPLEMENTED — record it so the next grep-driven triage does not reopen this.
- Value is a STRING, not a quoted form: pr-str of the whole user-written form, stamped at macro-expansion time. Deliberate — a string survives the EDN wire to a tool without the reader needing to be safe against arbitrary data-reader tags, and every documented reg-event shape round-trips without special-casing.
- Coverage is reg-event only (the single defreg-event-macro call site), plus machine guard/action source derived from the enclosing machine spec rather than duplicated onto registrar rows.
- Dev-only, two-layer elision: the macro and the registrar each gate on interop/debug-enabled?. Under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false the slot is absent and the source bytes are not in the bundle at all. JVM is always-on.

A dev-build registration entry therefore carries: :rf/id, :doc, :ns, :file, :line, :column, :interceptors, :handler-fn, and :rf.handler/source (the pr-str of the whole reg-event form).

== MEASURED VERIFICATION (fresh runs during the dossier investigation) ==
- npm run test:elision passed: all 60 dev-only sentinels ABSENT from the production bundle, all 60 PRESENT in the control bundle
- focused JVM capture/machine tests: 18 tests / 76 assertions passing
- frame-state egress boundary tests: 2 tests / 9 assertions passing

== THE SIX ORIGINAL ACTION ITEMS ==
1. Spec the macro extension — DONE (009 section; 001 source-coordinate capture)
2. Reserve the key in Conventions.md — DONE (full row, as :rf.handler/source)
3. Compile-time elision in production builds — DONE (001 elision classification + check-elision.cjs probe pinning the absence)
4. Snapshot-strip mechanism before transmission — DONE BY A STRONGER ROUTE, see below
5. Update 009 with the dev-mode capture story — DONE (same section)
6. AI-Audit: revisit AI-introspection rows — NOT DONE. spec/AI-Audit.md has zero mention of source-as-data (verified by grep, 2026-07-25). Rolled into the follow-up bead.

== THE IP-EXPOSURE CONCERN, RESOLVED STRUCTURALLY (action item 4) ==
The bead asked for a config flag to strip source before transmitting snapshots. The design went further and made the leak structurally impossible instead of strippable. Source-as-data lives ONLY on registry metadata; it never enters a frame durable state, and frame state is what actually travels off-box (SSR hydration, epoch/time-travel, Xray and pair-MCP snapshot, bug-report captures). handler_source_egress_strip_cljs_test.cljc deep-walks (rf/frame-state-value fid) after starting a machine and asserts none of :rf.handler/source, :source-code, :source-coords appears at any depth.

The one surface where a spec genuinely does travel off-box is the machines-viz share URL, and it strips explicitly: tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/share.cljs recursively drops :source-coords and :source-code, with comments calling out that local-filesystem coords reveal usernames and directory structure.

Residual exposure judged ACCEPTABLE: an agent running handler-meta against a colleague dev build sees that handler source — but that same agent can already run eval-cljs (default-ON per rf2-a0z0h) against the same runtime, so the marginal exposure over the existing surface is nil.

== TWO LIMITS OF THE SHIPPED CONTRACT — record accurately, they were MOTIVATING IDEAS ON THIS BEAD THAT DID NOT SHIP ==
The value lives on the CURRENT registry entry, not in an epoch or a frame snapshot. Xray performs a live handler-meta lookup when rendering an old epoch. Therefore:
(a) It does NOT preserve "the exact handler that ran" across a later hot reload.
(b) A standalone frame snapshot does NOT carry source for cross-process debugging.
Both were listed as use cases in this bead description. Neither is a property of the implemented contract. Historical source pinning would need its own privacy, size, retention and egress design and MUST NOT be smuggled into this completed registration feature. No consumer asks for it today; do not file it speculatively.

== WIDENING TO THE OTHER FOURTEEN REGISTRARS — REJECTED FOR NOW, WITH A NAMED TRIGGER ==
Ruled NOT to file a widening bead. A public surface here ships when a named consumer needs it. That is exactly how the May scope was chosen: reg-event shipped because the Xray Epoch panel needed it; the other fourteen registrars did not ship because nothing needed them. As of 2026-07-25 nothing has changed — no tool in tools/, no skill in skills/, and no open bead is blocked on reading a reg-sub body off a running runtime. Widening now would build a surface ahead of its consumer.

THE TRIGGER TO REOPEN THIS (a trigger that names a consumer, since this bead original vague trigger is precisely what aged badly): a specific tool that demonstrably cannot complete a real workflow using source coordinates plus file access, and therefore needs a particular NON-EVENT registration body over the runtime wire. When that tool exists, file the widening then. The design for how to do it is on this bead --design field.

== WHY THE "AN AI HAS FILESYSTEM ACCESS ANYWAY" REJECTION ONLY HALF-LANDS ==
The bead headline claim was "no file-system access required," and in this repo that constraint mostly does not bind: skills/re-frame2-improver is declared with allowed-tools [Read, Edit, Grep, Glob] and works entirely from disk, and the pair MCP deliberately hands agents vscode:// / cursor:// links via tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/source_uri.cljs (:rf.mcp/source-uri) precisely because it assumes an editor is right there. But it DOES bind in the two cases Xray actually exercises: reading what a handler was at the moment an epoch fired after source has drifted under hot reload, and reading a handler in a runtime the reader has no checkout of. Narrow, genuine, and reg-event coverage is the right size for it.

== THE ONE REAL RESIDUAL DEFECT ==
The pair MCP — the surface an AI actually drives — returns :rf.handler/source silently but does not advertise it. Verified 2026-07-25: zero occurrences of the key anywhere under tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/. The handler-meta tool descriptor and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md only promise source coordinates and generic "custom slots". An agent therefore reaches for the filesystem by reflex instead of reading what it already has. That is a discoverability gap, not a capability gap, and it is the whole of the remaining work. Filed as a documentation follow-up (see the linked bead) together with the missing AI-Audit.md rows.
FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-1tyxh (P3) — advertise :rf.handler/source on the pair-MCP handler-meta descriptor + spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, and add the source-as-data rows to spec/AI-Audit.md (original action item 6). That is the entire residual of this bead. No implementation, widening, or snapshot-strip work remains here.

title: The -e :requires-debug idiom is core-local; ssr/routing/freehand prod-gate lanes don't carry it
description:

title: ci: the rigorous-local inventory guard is structurally blind to gates scheduled outside expensive-tests.yml
description:
SPUN OFF from rf2-rmtj0 (PR #7227), where this mechanism was the root cause and is now mitigated for one command.

implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs derives its lockstep expectations from ONE job in ONE workflow: expensive-tests.yml's browser-bundle-and-story-gates. Any implementation npm script whose scheduled home is elsewhere is invisible to that parse — it can never appear in 'missing', so it can never make the guard red. rf2-rmtj0 is what that costs: bench:freehand-browser moved to freehand-bench.yml and dropped out of the local sweep in silence.

PR #7227 mitigates it for that one command via a new DIRECT_PINS map (command -> why the parse cannot see it), and hardened the parse so a comment can no longer satisfy a pin. It does NOT close the structural gap.

Sweeping every workflow against implementation/package.json, the implementation gates outside the guard's window today are:

  test.yml: test:ui-g1, test:ui-g8, test:ui-g13, test:ui-facade-isolation, test:ui-isolation, test:reagent-slim:smoke, test:testbed-tenant-switcher, test:tools-machines-viz, test:xray-feature-gate:smoke, build:machines-viz-viewer
  freehand-bench.yml: build:freehand-matched, test:freehand

NONE is judged a hole of the same kind right now, and this bead does NOT propose adding them to the rigorous script. They are PR-lane gates, and scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh is documented as the mirror of the EXPENSIVE sweep, not of test.yml. test:cljs and test:script-helpers are already covered transitively (test-fast-pr.sh invokes them).

The open question is whether the guard should be able to SEE the whole surface rather than one job — e.g. an explicit classification of every implementation npm script as (rigorous-sweep | pr-lane | manual instrument | build step), so a newly-added or newly-moved script must be classified rather than defaulting to invisible. That is a design call, not a fix; weigh it against over-engineering a guard that has now failed exactly once and has a working direct-pin escape hatch. Reasonable outcome is 'wontfix, DIRECT_PINS is enough' — but it should be decided rather than forgotten.

Surface: implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs.
notes:
DOSSIER REVIEW (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-29; recorded 2026-07-29 11:21 AUSEST): ai/decisions/rf2-0l1nv.inventory-guard-scope.md reviewed against the landed ruling; dossier deleted after this note. The dossier (written 2026-07-28 23:02, before shape 2 landed as PR #7241, merged 2026-07-28T13:33Z) recommended WONTFIX (shape 1: DIRECT_PINS as-was is enough). That recommendation is OVERTAKEN, not adopted: the close reason's rotted-pin counterexample (test:examples-compile pinned as 'never in the nightly sweep', false since a606d05763 on 2026-07-15, restated verbatim by PR #7227) is a concrete refutation of 'a stated reason is enough' - shape 2 makes the reason a checked claim, which is the minimal fix the dossier's own posture (no insurance without a consumer) permits, since the consumer already existed.

WHERE BOTH ANALYSES AGREE - and this part stands as reinforcement of the landed 'WHY NOT A CENSUS': no repo-wide npm-script classification, ever. Codex reasoning preserved for the record: (i) the 47 implementation npm scripts do not partition into one-of-four roles - a script can be PR gate + nightly gate + transitive fast-spine member + manual diagnostic simultaneously, so a mandatory classification would be inaccurate or grow into a multi-tag taxonomy costlier than the guard it serves; (ii) a complete inventory would NOT have caught the observed miss - bench:freehand-browser pre-existed; what changed was its ROLE (duplicate evidence -> unique coverage) when mounted suites moved out of test:browser, and a static classification catches that only if the programmer notices and updates the role, the same judgment a pin expresses more directly; (iii) the residual risk (a lane refactor changing coverage without updating a pin) is a review concern on explicit CI-topology changes, not a per-edit tax - now partially mechanised by the shape-2 basis check; (iv) revisit shape, ONLY after a second independent miss: one shared declarative inventory of the RIGOROUS commands, never a repo-wide script taxonomy. (iv) refines the close reason's reopen condition: if a name-level hole ever occurs, reach for the narrow rigorous-commands inventory, not the census.
close_reason:
DECIDED — shape 2: narrow and STATE the guard's scope, and make the escape hatch's reason a checked claim. PR #7241.

WHY NOT A package.json CENSUS (shape 3): it would not have caught the failure that raised this question. rf2-mf4uy (PR #7193) moved the seven re-frame.freehand.bench.* DOM namespaces between two builds that BOTH already existed - bench:freehand-browser had been a script since PR #6891 and already had its job in freehand-bench.yml - and the only line it changed in implementation/package.json was the test:script-policy chain. Every script NAME stayed put, so a name-level census would not have moved and would have stayed green while coverage narrowed. That was a migration of test CONTENT, and the gate for that class already exists: _browser-dom-lane-partition.test.cjs derives both lanes' :ns-regexp from shadow-cljs.edn. Content-level derivation answers content-level drift; a 47-entry name census does not, and would red on every new npm script.

WHY NOT WONTFIX (shape 1): the DIRECT_PINS escape hatch ALREADY carries a false reason and nothing could say so. test:examples-compile was pinned 2026-06-16 as 'never in the nightly sweep' (true then); a606d05763 put it in browser-bundle-and-story-gates on 2026-07-15; the reason went false that day and PR #7227 restated it verbatim six weeks later while making 'a stated reason' the point of the map. A reason that can rot unobserved is exactly the failure #7227 diagnosed for comments.

WHAT LANDED: each DIRECT_PINS entry declares a kind - parse-blind (scheduled outside the gates job; lockstep can never require it) or belt-and-braces (lockstep requires it, but only while the workflow keeps it) - and a new assertion checks the declaration against the workflow, kept separate from the presence assertion so a stale basis neither masks nor is masked by a real hole. Plus the stated scope rule: a command belongs in test-rigorous-local.sh when BOTH (a) it yields a VERDICT rather than a build artefact or a published record, and (b) no PR run gates it.

THE TWELVE ARE STILL CORRECTLY OUT OF SCOPE, and the two conjuncts derive that rather than asserting it: the ten test.yml-only gates fail (b) - test.yml is surface-classified, so the change that would break one is the change that queues it; build:freehand-matched fails (a) - it is the matched-pair build step, not a gate; test:freehand fails (b) - its assertions already gate every PR through :node-test via test:cljs, and test.yml itself calls it 'the cheap NAMED surface for local + worker iteration, not a second gate'. bench:freehand-browser is the only command satisfying both, which is why it alone is pinned.

MUTATION-PROVED: (A) declaring test:examples-compile parse-blind reds now, exit 1 - and the pre-change guard is exit 0 on today's tree carrying that same false claim, which is the live historical state rather than a mutation; (B) a pin with an undeclared basis reds now, pre-change accepted it silently; (C) deleting bench:freehand-browser from the script still reds, existing behaviour preserved.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: a second coverage hole that a name-level package.json census WOULD have caught - i.e. a gate lost because a script was added or renamed and nobody wired it into a lane. Today's one data point is the opposite kind.

PR #7066. NINE wrong counts, not eight — and the ROOT CAUSE was a layout artefact, not carelessness.

title: href-attrs and link-model each re-derive route-url + the strategy encode
description:
Found while collapsing rf2-e9974 (PR 7016); NOT fixed there, because it is a different seam and the bead's remedy was scoped to the click law and the dispatch payload.

implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc has TWO sites that turn an extracted address into a rendered href:

  href-attrs  — (registry/route-url {:to to :params (or params {}) :query (or query {}) :fragment fragment})
                then (assoc :href (encode path-url))
  link-model  — the SAME route-url call with the SAME (or … {}) defaulting, then
                {:href (encode path-url) …}

Byte-identical apart from what they return. After rf2-e9974 the payload synthesis IS shared (url-requested-payload) and native? is read off the same side on both paths, so route-url + encode is the last duplicated calculation between the two link surfaces.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE COLLAPSE (and why it needs a ruling rather than a mechanical fix). The two fns return deliberately different things: href-attrs must ALSO strip the control keys and hand back the open DOM-attribute passthrough map (route-link's documented extraction-law exception), which link-model must NOT do — the ui artefact owns its own markup and passthrough attrs. So neither can simply call the other. The candidates are:

  (a) a third private helper — (address -> [path-url href]) — that both call. Smallest,
      but adds a third name for a two-line calculation.
  (b) href-attrs calls link-model for the href and adds the strip. Wrong direction:
      link-model is the ui-facing seam, href-attrs is the rf/route-link internal.
  (c) leave it, and note the duplication where it is.

Note the ONE substantive difference to preserve: href-attrs takes encode as an ARGUMENT (the CLJS render passes the frame strategy's :encode, the SSR render passes identity), whereas link-model resolves encode itself behind a reader conditional (:cljs strategy lookup / :clj identity). Any collapse has to keep the SSR shell emitting path-form on both paths.

Low priority — no behaviour differs, and it is two lines. File-and-judge, not file-and-fix: if the mayor's read is that (a) is more names than the duplication costs, closing this as accepted duplication is a legitimate outcome, and the pair should then get a comment saying so.
notes:
MAYOR RULING: ACCEPT THE DUPLICATION, WITH A COMMENT THAT SAYS WHY (2026-07-26). The filer asked for a ruling rather than a fix and framed it correctly — neither surface can call the other, so accepting it is a legitimate outcome.

THE SITUATION: href-attrs and link-model each re-derive route-url plus the strategy encode. It is the last duplicated calculation between the two link surfaces, after rf2-e9974 collapsed the click law and the payload synthesiser onto single owners.

WHY ACCEPT RATHER THAN UNIFY: neither can call the other. A shared helper would have to live somewhere both already require, and the filer did not find such a home — which is the same structural wall rf2-wzqtu hit, where packaging made a single readiness projector impossible. This artefact has converged on collapse-to-one-owner SIX times and been right each time; this is the second case where the honest answer is the opposite, and recognising that is harder than applying the pattern.

WHAT TO DO, and it is small: write the comment at BOTH sites, each naming the other and stating that the duplication is structural rather than incidental — so the next reader does not spend an afternoon trying to unify them, and a future refactor that DOES create a shared home knows to collapse them. That is the rf2-wzqtu lesson applied forward: when you cannot have one implementation, stop implying you do.

DO NOT introduce a third namespace to hold a two-line helper. Do not add a gate. If a shared home appears later for another reason, collapse them then.

THIS RIDES WITH the next link-surface dispatch rather than alone — it is two comments. Reduced from a fix to a note by ruling, not deferred.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7043 (2026-07-26) — KEEP IN PROGRESS: the requested comments landed, but their stated structural rationale is factually false. href-attrs and link-model are both defined in re-frame.routing.link, in the same source file. A private helper already has a shared home: for example, it can accept the once-extracted address plus encode and own only registry/route-url + encode, while href-attrs retains stripping/passthrough and link-model retains payload/native assembly and its reader-conditional encode selection. No third namespace or inverted call is required.

The mayor may still prefer the two-line duplication because a third PRIVATE NAME costs more than it saves; the original Bead explicitly presented that as option (a). But the new permanent comments instead say there is no home both sites require and a namespace would need inventing, then analogize to a packaging wall. That sends the next reader away with a false topology and incorrectly calls factorizable duplication structural. Correct both comments to record the actual judgement (shared helper is possible but not worth its name), or revisit the ruling with the same-namespace evidence. Behavior is unchanged and no functional defect was found.
close_reason:
PRs #7043 (4da020a5af) and #7048 (c3ad198225) MERGED. Both ruled beads landed; all four files verified on origin/main by blob hash.

rf2-arenp — ACCEPT-THE-DUPLICATION ruling executed exactly. The premise was checked rather than taken: route-url appears 9 times in link.cljc, SEVEN OF THEM PROSE, and the two real call sites are exactly the pair the bead names. href-attrs must ALSO strip control keys and return route-link open passthrough map, which link-model must NOT do, and no namespace both already require can host the shared calculation — so the ruling ground holds on inspection. Comments only, at both sites, each naming THE OTHER BY NAME rather than "the two places" (the counts-drift discipline applied to cross-references), stating the duplication is structural, preserving the encode difference any future collapse must keep, and citing the rf2-wzqtu precedent. No third namespace, no helper, no gate.

rf2-7g4qn — the rescope held and the spec half was ALREADY DONE: Spec 012 already states the class and already declares the link surfaces behaviourally identical. Routing now owns prefetch-intent-keys, published on both hosts. The implementation/ui arm was NOT touched, per the rescoping that donor arms retire with F6e.

TWO DELIBERATE NON-ACTIONS WORTH KEEPING. It left two further enumerations alone with a stated reason: spec/012 (the authority) and the fh-routelink-008 conformance fixture, because A CONFORMANCE FIXTURE STATING THE CLASS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE IMPLEMENTATION IS THE POINT OF A FIXTURE. And it did NOT make the tests loop the published constant: "A TEST THAT DERIVES ITS EXPECTATIONS FROM THE CONSTANT UNDER TEST CANNOT CATCH A WRONG CONSTANT." That is exactly right and it is the same reasoning that makes a canned value matching a canned producer this repo eighth false-green class. It flagged the divergence rather than silently taking it.

MY RULING ON THE ONE THING IT ASKED ME TO OVERRULE — I ACCEPT IT, WITH A NOTE. The freehand arm cost a fifth late-bind hook: publication, a directory entry, and turning a def into a hook wrapper. The worker itself said that is more than "comments plus a constant move" and offered a one-commit revert. I am keeping it, because the bead OWN remedy names that exact mechanism ("reachable by both view substrates the way they already reach prefetch-payload") and my rescope narrowed the remedy without replacing it — reverting would restore the very duplication the bead exists to remove, in the artefact that is meant to own the constant.

BUT THE PROCESS NOTE STANDS: my brief said "if a change is more than comments plus a constant move, STOP and report". It proceeded and reported after. The reasoning was sound and the outcome is right, so this is not a reprimand — but STOP AND REPORT MEANS STOP, and a P4 growing into a fifth late-bind hook is exactly the signal that instruction exists to surface BEFORE the work, not after.

A MERGE-RACE INSIGHT WORTH RECORDING, in the worker own words: "OPENING THE PR AT FIRST COMMIT MEANS A LATER COMMIT ON THAT BRANCH CAN BE RACED PAST THE MERGE." That is the cost side of an instruction I put in every brief, and it materialised nine times today. The instruction still stands — pushed commits survive outages, and every race so far was recovered by a follow-up PR — but the tradeoff is now named rather than implicit.

BASELINE CORRECTION FOR MY BRIEFS: core is 2115/10462, not the 10459 I have been quoting. Same test count; the +3 assertions arrived with the 12 origin/main commits the branch rebased onto, not with the diff. Routing matched 511/2771 exactly.

title: re-frame.ui runtime accepts :passive with :prevent-default that its own analyzer refuses
description:
Mirror of the tier-drift rf2-uvcm3 closed for Freehand, in the re-frame.ui (EXPERIMENTAL) substrate.

implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc:1451 refuses an options map carrying :passive true with :prevent-default true as :rf.ui.compile/contradictory-handler-options, with the message 'the combination is a contradiction (in any stage)'. The runtime that reads the same map at render — implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/events.cljs:610 — destructures {:keys [event prevent-default stop-propagation capture passive once]} and carries no contradiction check, so it accepts what the compiled tier refuses.

That is the exact asymmetry rf2-uvcm3 removed on the Freehand side by teaching the canonical events/options-plan the same check (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/events.cljc:627, recovery :drop-passive-or-prevent-default, ex-data {:contradiction [:passive :prevent-default]}). ui/ has no equivalent.

FIX: one check in the ui options path, matching the freehand wording and recovery, plus the one regression row. No new validator. Freehand's shipped shape is the template.

The re-frame.ui skill's own teaching example carried the refused pair too; that half is fixed in PR #7010 (skills/re-frame2-ui/SKILL.md). Filed rather than fixed here because implementation/ui/ source was outside that dispatch's scope.

Note ui/ is the EXPERIMENTAL substrate, hence P4.
close_reason:
NOT A DEFECT — the bead premise is MISATTRIBUTED, and it is moot regardless. Verified under PR #7034 and closed on evidence rather than on a fix.

THE PREMISE IS BACKWARDS. The bead says re-frame.ui runtime ACCEPTS :passive with :prevent-default that its own analyzer refuses. events.cljs:610 is the DESTRUCTURE inside dynamic-handler; SEVEN LINES LATER AT 617 the same function refuses :passive OUTRIGHT — "dynamic :capture/:passive listener options cannot change the native listener phase after compilation". So the runtime cannot accept :passive WITH :prevent-default because it does not accept :passive at that position AT ALL. It is strictly STRICTER than the analyzer, the opposite of the drift described.

CORROBORATION, not inference: handler-option-keys has exactly TWO readers in the artefact (the compile tier and this one); passive-ref is documented as an internal compiler target fed by already-checked output; and re-frame.ui ships no interpreted walk that could read a literal options map at render.

WHY THE FREEHAND PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, which is the part I would have got wrong: rf2-uvcm3 needed options-plan to learn the contradiction because Freehand event plane genuinely accepts :passive as a LIVE LISTENER FACT. ui render tier does not, so there is nothing to teach it. I briefed "Freehand shipped check is the template" — that was wrong for this bead and the worker said so.

F6e DETERMINATION, which I asked for explicitly: MOOT, and the answer is the same either way. Every file the bead names — compiler/analyze.cljc, events.cljs, the regression row home in implementation/ui/test/ — is inside implementation/ui/, which rf2-drpa3.57 deletes wholesale. The one half with consequence outliving the donor was skills/re-frame2-ui/SKILL.md, and that ALREADY LANDED in #7010.

So this closes as not-a-defect on the code, and would have retired with F6e even had the premise held. Two outcomes, one answer — which is why the F6e check belongs in every donor-tier brief before any work starts.

description:

FIX: add 'implementation/shadow-cljs.edn' and 'scripts/check_test_lane_bijection.py' to that paths list. Two lines. Deferred out of PR #7010 because .github/workflows/** was fenced to a live CI worker for that wave.
acceptance_criteria: A direct push to main that can change either checker result always schedules Freehand conformance: this includes every canonical spec file/citation scanned by check_freehand_conformance_index.py and every tracked source/config/document path scanned by check_donor_inventory.py for a live donor consumer. A negative proof removes a cited spec anchor and adds an otherwise-unclaimed re-frame.ui consumer under a previously unlisted path; both changes must select the workflow and make the relevant checker fail. The pull_request trigger remains unfiltered and the required Freehand conformance status context remains stable.
notes:

Premise confirmed verbatim: check_freehand_conformance_index.py:187 imports the EDN reader from check_test_lane_bijection and :198 sets SHADOW_CLJS_REL = Path("implementation/shadow-cljs.edn"); neither was in the push filter. MERGED-PR AUDIT #7041 (2026-07-26): REOPENED for a bounded completeness residual. The two added paths are correct, the authored/applied four-commit range is exact, and the directly affected CI lanes are green. But the same push-only filter still omits larger input sets that these two checkers explicitly read. check_freehand_conformance_index.py scans every spec/**/*.md for FH-* citations and resolves every index citation against its target canonical spec file; the filter includes only spec/conformance/freehand/**, so a direct main push deleting the cited anchor in spec/004-Views.md or adding a dangling FH id elsewhere under spec/ skips the job that would fail. More sharply, check_donor_inventory.py runs git ls-files and scans tracked text across the repository for re-frame.ui libspecs and day8/re-frame2-ui coordinates. The workflow comment itself says this whole-working-tree census belongs on an unfiltered job rather than a path-filtered one, yet push remains path-filtered: a direct push adding a donor consumer in implementation/ssr/deps.edn (or any other unlisted source path) skips it. Because this bead's stated rationale is direct-push honesty, listing only the two newly derived CLJS-lane inputs does not complete the contract. Bounded repair: make the push trigger unfiltered, or express an inclusive filter that covers the checkers' actual read universes; preserve the deliberately unfiltered PR trigger and required status context.

title: Row 9's :query-retain ratchet is only invoked over implementation/ — examples, tools and skills are unratcheted
description:
EP-0037 review gate 1 (rf2-kqxe6.14) finding, mutation-verified. Row 9's `:query-retain` reintroduction ratchet is real and non-vacuous, but it is only INVOKED over `implementation/` source with tests excluded — so the corpus surfaces the docs / examples / skills waves rewrote are unratcheted.

## Verified good

`scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` carries the three `:query-retain` USE shapes (a `reg-route` metadata map, the accepted-key roster, the promotion vocabulary), a masking pass so retirement PROSE does not fire, and a bundled fixture self-test with three positives and two negatives. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` both run `--self-test` before the scan, so the gate's own non-vacuity is gated. That is a well-built ratchet.

## The gap

Both invocations are bare (`python scripts/check_retired_spellings.py --verbose`), and the script defaults to `--scan-dir implementation` with `--include-tests` OFF, over `.clj` / `.cljc` / `.cljs` only. So the rule is never applied to `examples/`, `tools/`, `skills/`, `docs/`, `spec/`, `migration/`, or any test tree.

Mutation, from a clean checkout of `main`:

    planted  implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/__probe.cljc  {:query-retain #{:theme}}
    planted  examples/__probe.cljs                                     {:query-retain #{:theme}}

    python scripts/check_retired_spellings.py           -> rc=1, 1 finding: the implementation file
    python scripts/check_retired_spellings.py --scan-dir examples
                                                        -> 1 finding: examples/__probe.cljs

So the RULE works corpus-wide; only the invocation is scoped. Both probes deleted; `git status` clean.

## Why it is worth closing

EP-0037 R5 removed `:query-retain` with no alias, and `rf2-kqxe6.12` / `rf2-kqxe6.13` migrated `examples/` and `skills/` off it. A reintroduction in exactly those trees — the ones a reader copies from — is the likeliest reintroduction there is, and it is the one the ratchet cannot see. R6's row-9 verdict ("green, and now mechanically enforced … The spine runs it unconditionally") is true for framework source and over-reads for the corpus.

## Bounded repair

Widen the invocation, not the rule: pass the additional CLJS-bearing trees (`examples`, `tools`, `skills`) to the same script in `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and `.github/workflows/test.yml`. `.md` trees (`docs/`, `spec/`, `migration/`) are out of scope for this script — its suffix filter is source-only and its masking is written for source comments/docstrings; if prose coverage is ever wanted it belongs in whichever gate already scans markdown, not here.

Check first whether the script's other two rules (the bare `:frame` coeffect, redirect `:url` / `:to`) stay green over the widened trees; if one of them legitimately fires in `examples/` the widening may need to be per-rule rather than per-invocation, and that is a design call worth stating in the PR rather than working around.

Low severity: this is a ratchet-scope gap, not a live defect. `git grep` over the widened trees at current `main` shows no `:query-retain` USE shape today.
close_reason:
PR #7005 (worker/ci-arming, commit c214e85c6f) — grouped with rf2-wq17m + rf2-xwa4n, same hot-zone CI files.

WIDENED THE INVOCATION, rule untouched — but the roster went into the SCRIPT (DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS in scripts/check_retired_spellings.py) rather than into the two call sites the bead named. Reason: duplicating a tree list across scripts/test-fast-pr.sh and .github/workflows/test.yml is how a widened gate narrows again on one side only, which is this bead's own defect class one tier up. Both invocations stay BARE and cannot drift apart.

ROSTER: implementation, examples, tools, skills, testbeds, migration, docs/tools. That is every top-level directory carrying a tracked .clj/.cljc/.cljs file (verified: git ls-files | grep -E '\.clj[cs]?$' | sed -E 's#/.*##' | sort -u), so no tree is left unratcheted — the bead's list plus three the bead did not name. testbeds/ (13 files) and migration/ (2, one under test/) are ordinary source and leaving them out would have recreated the defect in miniature; docs/tools is the playground SCI source, rostered as a subpath so docs/ itself stays off.

Scanning docs/ would double-report a real finding and could report a STALE one from a copy predating the fix.

title: events/callback does not validate :role against callback-roles — the closed set is documentation only
description:
Found by the rf2-c1vvn worker while checking its own diff against the eighth false-green class (a canned value asserting something the producer cannot emit). It noted this, deliberately did not touch it, and was right not to.

THE FINDING: events/callback accepts a :role without validating it against callback-roles. The closed set exists as documentation rather than as an enforced vocabulary.

WHY IT IS P4 AND NOT URGENT: unreachable today — every producer is in-namespace, so no caller can currently pass an out-of-set role. There is no live defect and nothing to reproduce.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING ANYWAY: this is exactly the shape that produced the eighth false-green class earlier today. A worker wrote :classification :callback into a canned MCP envelope because it read a docstring's prose as naming a value; the vocabulary was closed at seven members and that value did not exist, and every suite stayed green because nothing checks a canned value against the producing source. A closed set that is documentation only is one refactor away from the same failure: the moment a producer moves out of the namespace, an unvalidated role becomes representable and nothing reds.

THE FIX IF ANYONE IS ALREADY IN THAT CODE: validate :role against callback-roles at the callback construction site, and pin a red case for an out-of-set role. Small.

DO NOT dispatch this on its own merits — it is unreachable, and validating an unreachable case is the unevidenced-defensiveness the pre-alpha posture rejects. The right time is when someone is already editing events/callback for another reason, OR the moment a producer of callbacks appears outside that namespace, at which point it becomes reachable and should be fixed in the same change that makes it so.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS RECORDED-NOT-ACTIONED, on the bead OWN guidance and the standing posture. Its final line already says it: "DO NOT dispatch this on its own merits — it is unreachable, and validating an unreachable case is the unevidenced-guard shape."

WHY I AM CLOSING RATHER THAN LEAVING IT OPEN: an open bead is a claim that work is owed. This one is a NOTE — every producer of :role is in-namespace, so no caller can currently pass an invalid one, and the fix is explicitly conditioned on someone already being in that code. Leaving it open makes the backlog say there is a validation gap when what exists is a recorded observation. The record survives in this close reason and in the bead history.

THE POSTURE CLAUSE THIS IS ABOUT, and it is the one I apply least: WE TRUST THE PROGRAMMER. A closed set documented but unenforced is not automatically a defect. Enforcing it against a caller that cannot exist is a nag-diagnostic — it adds a failure mode, a message to maintain and a test to keep green, in exchange for catching nothing. That is the definition of gold-plating under this posture, and I have rejected the same shape at triage before (rf2-u53yy.7).

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT, and it is concrete: the moment :role becomes settable from OUTSIDE the namespace — a public verb, a config surface, an MCP tool, a consumer-facing map. At that point an unvalidated closed set stops being documentation and becomes a way for a consumer to construct a state the framework cannot name, which is the eighth false-green class in a new place. If anyone touches events/callback for another reason, validating there is cheap and welcome.

THE OBSERVATION IS STILL WORTH HAVING, which is why the finder recorded it: it was found while checking a diff AGAINST the eighth false-green class, and the pattern it noticed — a closed vocabulary that exists as documentation rather than as a constraint — is real and has bitten this repo. The distinction that matters is REACHABILITY, and this instance is not reachable.

title: EP-0037 carries no errata, though implementation changed two ratified clauses (EP-0009 rule 3)
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness).

THE OBLIGATION. EP-0009 §rule 3, verbatim: "Amendment is allowed only before implementation. Once an EP is accepted and beads are in flight, substantive changes go through a new EP or a recorded ruling -- not silent edits. (Mechanical corrections and errata-ledger updates are always fine.) Mechanical means the edit cannot change a reasonable reader's understanding of the proposal, alternatives, rationale, ruling, or scope; anything past that line is recorded as a dated erratum/addendum beside the affected passage, preserving the original text -- freeze meaning, not bytes (rf2-r7ahi)."

The corpus follows this: `git grep -ci "erratum|errata" -- docs/EP/` shows EP-0001 (8), EP-0005 (11), EP-0003 (7), EP-0013 (7), EP-0017 (7), EP-0006 (6), and a dozen more.
docs/EP/EP-0037-route-planning-and-activation-ownership.md: ZERO.

TWO RATIFIED CLAUSES WERE CHANGED DURING IMPLEMENTATION.

(1) READINESS TABLE, FIRST-FAILURE ORDERING. EP:615 ratifies "a blocking first load failed | :error | deterministic first failure IN EFFECTIVE PLAN ORDER". spec/012-Routing.md's readiness table now reads "the deterministic first failure -- the outstanding blocking set is ordered by CANONICAL CEDN-1 RESOURCE-KEY IDENTITY, NOT by hash or plan order, so the pick is stable across settles that prune siblings".
The change is CORRECT and well-reasoned: the blocking slot is a SET, so effective plan order is not recoverable at reconcile time, and persisting it was explicitly rejected when rf2-kqxe6.17 was ruled ("that is machinery -- a set becomes an ordered structure, threaded through commit/settle/hydration/restore -- to make an arbitrary-but-deterministic tie-break match a sentence"). The ruling is recorded on rf2-kqxe6.18's close reason and the prose fix landed as a drive-by on PR #6916. It is not recorded in the EP. A reader of the EP's readiness table today believes plan order.

(2) THE `:plan-cause` VOCABULARY. EP:1029-1036 ratifies that the widened :rf.error/resource-route-plan tags "REQUIRE :route-id and :plan-cause (one of :link, :navigate, :popstate, :initial, :ssr, or :prefetch)" and that "the :rf.resource/route-plan trace uses the same :plan-cause vocabulary". EP §Resolved Decisions ratifies this BY NAME in its knowing-ratification paragraph.
Shipped: :plan-cause is OPTIONAL and only ever :prefetch. spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1714 states the narrowing outright -- "[:plan-cause {:optional true} :keyword] ;; :prefetch on a warm-mode intent-preload planning failure; absent for a navigation-commit failure" -- and implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1208 sets it only inside `warm-err`. One of six values, on the warm path only; the five activation causes never appear on either the error or the plan trace.
The narrowing is DEFENSIBLE -- the door cause is already observable on :rf.route/planned's :cause tag, so carrying it a second time on the plan error would be redundant -- but unlike (1) I found NO recorded ruling for it anywhere: not in the EP, not in a bead close reason, not in a spec rationale passage. It reads as a design decision taken in the implementation and written into Spec-Schemas as though it had always been the contract.

REPAIR, per EP-0009 rule 3 -- dated addenda beside the affected passages, ORIGINAL TEXT PRESERVED:
1. Add a dated erratum beside EP:611-617 (the readiness table) recording that the first-failure ordering graduated as canonical CEDN-1 resource-key identity order rather than effective plan order, why (the blocking slot is a set; plan order is not recoverable at reconcile), and the ruling's provenance (rf2-kqxe6.17 ruling / rf2-kqxe6.18 / PR #6916).
2. Add a dated erratum beside EP:1028-1036 recording the :plan-cause narrowing as shipped, with its rationale. IF THE OPERATOR JUDGES THE NARROWING WRONG rather than merely unrecorded, this bead is the wrong instrument -- say so and the correction belongs on the routing/resources planner instead. Default recommendation: ratify the narrowing (the door cause is already on :rf.route/planned) and record it. Note that this erratum is a PREREQUISITE for the sibling 009-catalogue bead, which brings 009's tags column into line with what actually ships.
3. While in the file, check whether the rf2-kqxe6.3 plan-projection carrier ruling (source address and :params/:query VALUES deliberately not carried; key sets instead) needs an erratum too. My read is NO -- EP §Tooling says only "source address and cause" without promising the value rides a tag, and the full rationale plus both rejected alternatives are recorded in spec/012 §Resolved target -- but it is one line to check and the author is better placed to judge.

Do NOT rewrite EP-0037's body prose, do not restate the ratified text, and do not open an EP-0038 for either item -- both are recorded-ruling territory, which rule 3 explicitly permits.
GATES: mkdocs build --strict; check_doc_slugs. Parallel-safe (docs/EP tree only).
close_reason: PR #7011. DETERMINATION: the EP was the defective side; the shipped :plan-cause narrowing is correct and is now ratified by erratum, no code changed. Two dated errata added beside their passages with original text preserved: (1) the readiness table's first-failure ordering graduated as canonical CEDN-1 resource-key identity order rather than effective plan order, recording the rf2-kqxe6.17 ruling / rf2-kqxe6.18 / PR #6916 provenance the EP never carried; (2) :plan-cause graduated OPTIONAL and :prefetch-only rather than required/one-of-six. The rationale is stronger than 'defensible but unrecorded': :plan-cause is the COMPLEMENT of the door vocabulary, not a subset. commit-navigation has exactly two callers (routing/navigate.cljc:581, routing/url_change.cljc:366) and both emit :rf.route/planned with :cause immediately before consulting the resource plan, so all five activation causes are already on the wire in the same commit branch; prefetch is the ONE planning path with no :rf.route/planned at all, so it is the one cause not otherwise recoverable. Required-and-six would additionally need the :routing/on-route-entry hook contract widened to thread a door cause it deliberately omits. Item 3 (the rf2-kqxe6.3 carrier ruling) CHECKED, no erratum needed and none added: EP Tooling promises the PROJECTION explains source+cause and resolve.cljc/plan-projection does expose :source via r0-projection-keys; only the trace-tag lowering drops it, which the EP never promised. Gates: mkdocs --strict rc=0 (0 WARNING/ERROR, no anchor complaint on any added link); check_doc_slugs rc=0; check_keyword_catalogue_drift rc=0; check_thrown_error_messages rc=0; implementation/core clojure -M:test rc=0 (2115 tests, 10456 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors).

title: spec/012 extraction-law key-class block omits :on-click from the link behaviour keys
description:
@
EP-0037 gate-3 quality review finding F8 (rf2-kqxe6.16).

spec/012-Routing.md:809 states the normative closed key classes as:

  link behavior keys #{:prefetch}

But re-frame.routing.address/link-behavior-keys is #{:on-click :prefetch}; href-attrs strips both (link.cljc:106); and spec/012 own §The Freehand route-link descriptor says "The view control keys are :to / :params / :query / :fragment, :on-click and :prefetch."

WHY IT MATTERS. §The extraction law key-class block is the ONE place the closed classes are stated as a RULE - it is what a reader implements from, and what an audit measures the implementation against. A reader implementing from it would leave a caller-supplied :on-click on the props map, which reaches the <a> on the SSR path: route-link-render-ssr returns base-attrs unmodified, so a host closure would enter the server tree - the thing the Freehand descriptor explicitly forbids ("a serialized document has no click to intercept and must not carry a host closure").

The implementation is RIGHT. The normative table is one key short.

REMEDY. spec/012:809 -> `link behavior keys #{:on-click :prefetch}`, and one clause naming why :on-click is a behaviour key rather than a passthrough DOM attr (it is the imperative pre-navigation seam - replaced by the framework closure on the interactive host, dropped on SSR). Hot-zone file: sequence, do not parallel.

title: Compiled and interpreted emitters order the same element's attributes differently when one is literal and one runtime
description:
Found by the rf2-rrosy worker while writing cross-mode acceptance for v/html. Pre-existing, unrelated to v/html, and filed at P4 deliberately — it is a TEST-ERGONOMICS irritant, not a defect.

THE OBSERVATION: for an element mixing literal and runtime attributes, the compiled and interpreted modes emit the attributes in different orders — 'class id lang data-kind' versus 'class data-kind id lang'. Attribute order carries no meaning in HTML, so no rendered page differs and no consumer can observe it.

THE ACTUAL COST, which is why it is filed at all: it makes whole-markup cross-mode STRING equality impossible. Anyone writing a cross-mode test that compares serialised output byte-for-byte will find it fails for a reason that is not about their change.

THE SANCTIONED WORKAROUND IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, and it is the right pattern: the rf2-rrosy props row asserts the attribute SET plus the content verbatim, and says in the test why it does not compare whole strings. Copy that shape.

DO NOT FIX THIS BY NORMALISING EMITTER OUTPUT unless a real consumer needs byte-equality. Sorting or canonicalising attribute emission to make a test convenience possible would add work to every render on both paths to satisfy something no user can see — squarely the over-engineering the pre-alpha posture rules out. The honest remedy, if anyone wants one, is a test HELPER that compares attribute sets, not a change to the emitters.

Recorded so the next person writing a cross-mode markup test does not spend an hour discovering it, and does not then 'fix' the emitters.
close_reason: Merged PR #7051 records the cross-mode attribute-order divergence as accepted, non-semantic behavior at the normative portability law and corrects the trusted-markup test explanation with the measured structural orders plus SSR sorted-output boundary. The first/last class example belongs to the pre-existing virtual-table DOM fixture and does not contradict the distinct trusted-markup order example. No emitter normalization added.

title: If a SECOND docs example is found violating its own documented rule, build a doc-example conformance gate
description:

Fixed in PR #6966 (example now returns all four keys; the closed-shape rule moved above the example with the silent-discard consequence spelled out).

THE SUGGESTION was a gate pinning documented examples to the shapes they claim to satisfy. That is genuinely valuable — the defect class is 'the documentation lies in a way the reader cannot detect' and it is the single worst kind for a first public alpha.

THE RULING: do NOT build it yet. Reasons, in order: (1) it is new machinery for a class with exactly ONE observed instance, and the pre-alpha posture rules out building a subsystem where a fix will do; (2) a general doc-example conformance gate is not cheap — it means extracting fenced examples, knowing which predicate each claims to satisfy, and evaluating them in the right runtime, which is a second sample-harness beside the digest-pinning one that already exists for docs/core/freehand; (3) a pre-alpha docs corpus in active churn would fight such a gate constantly.

Note the precedent that DOES exist: docs/core/freehand fenced blocks are digest-pinned by samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj, so the mechanism for pinning doc content is not unknown here — but digest-pinning proves text has not DRIFTED, not that an example is CORRECT. Those are different gates.

TRIGGER TO ACT: a second documented example found violating a rule its own page states. One instance is a fix; two is a pattern, and at that point build the gate rather than fixing a third by hand. Do not close this as stale — its value is being decided before the pressure.

Same shape of standing decision as the census-grammar ruling filed earlier today.

title: day8/re-frame2-http forces Cheshire + the Jackson tree onto browser-only consumers (clein :provided scope is available and unused)
notes:
From rf2-ods8n lens A (perf + back-compat audit), 2026-07-25. LOW — leaving it is defensible.

implementation/http/deps.edn top-level :deps carries
  cheshire/cheshire {:mvn/version "5.13.0"}   ;; The JVM codec uses Cheshire; CLJS uses the host `JSON` object.

clein writes top-level :deps into the pom at COMPILE scope, so a CLJS-only app that
adds day8/re-frame2-http downloads Cheshire plus the Jackson tree it pulls and carries
them on the classpath permanently. Nothing reaches the bundle, so this is NOT a size
regression — but it cuts against the artefact's own "bundle isolation is guaranteed by
structure rather than by careful dead-code elimination" rationale one layer down, at
the classpath.

The mechanism already exists in the toolchain and no artefact uses it:
noahtheduke.clein.pom-data/get-provided-deps reads :aliases :provided :extra-deps and
stamps <scope>provided</scope> on each. (Verified in the pinned clein sha
2b83503246e8291fc023d688574640a9b23d8c50.)

Same question applies, at lower stakes, to core: implementation/core/deps.edn ships
org.clojure/clojure 1.12.0 and org.clojure/clojurescript 1.12.145 at compile scope on
day8/re-frame2. Maven nearest-wins means a consumer's own direct pin still takes
precedence, so this is cosmetic rather than harmful — but `provided` is the
conventional scope for a host platform dep and would express the intent.

If actioned: adding a :provided alias changes the PUBLISHED pom of every artefact
touched, so it wants a from-scratch `clojure -M:clein jar` + pom inspection per
artefact before merge, and verify-version-lockstep.sh's no-literal-:mvn/version check
must still pass. Not worth doing at the alpha; revisit if a consumer complains about
classpath weight.

title: 004D: compiled-tier enumerability claim for host-React escapes is untrue in Freehand
description:
Surfaced by the rf2-4gnrs ruling dossier (2026-07-25, ruled: retire v/raw). spec/004D:1407-1424 argues that raw widens the head-reachability surface but stays ENUMERABLE - "every site declares the :raw capability and is recorded in the manifest, so the set of such escapes is finite and listable". title: B5's :mixed release shape is not byte-matched to the matched pair
description:
Surfaced while discharging rf2-x4jda R1 (PR #6909).

Acceptance #1 of rf2-x4jda asks for THREE matched :browser release builds
differing only in lowering. R1 delivered TWO: :freehand-release-interpreted and
:freehand-release-compiled are now one source in two states, censused on every
run, and the published delta is taken over those two alone.

The third, :freehand-release (the MIXED shape), is NOT byte-matched to them. It
is built from re-frame.freehand.release-app, which has its own view names
(counter / counter-compiled against counter-a / counter-b), its own registered
ids, its own root DOM id and a ~1,486-byte namespace docstring that ships three
times. Its bytes therefore sit between the pair's by structure, not by
construction: reading interpreted < mixed < compiled as a lowering series is not
warranted.

R1 made the claim honest rather than making the artefact match -
b5/matched-bundle-paths now names :mixed as the SHIPPED-COST artefact, measured
for context, with no delta taken against it. That is defensible: the mixed
bundle's job is to be a real small app whose absolute cost is the headline
figure, and the delta only ever needed two arms.

MAYOR DECISION: either accept the two-arm reading and amend acceptance #1, or
fold release-app into the matched shape as a third arm. The second is not free:
release-app is named by check-freehand-reachability.cjs and
check-freehand-evidence-elision.cjs (both hard-code the sentinel
re-frame.freehand.release-app/bump), by b5_reachability_control_app.cljs, and by
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, which pins its path. A worker
was fenced out of the last two at the time of filing.

title: functional-style atom review: tools/machines-viz
description:

SCOPE: this surface under src/ only. Test trees are OUT OF SCOPE (atoms there are legitimate assertion fixtures). Donor implementation/ui/ is excluded repo-wide (deleted at rf2-drpa3.57).

- SCRATCH-SMELL: a local accumulator inside a tight loop or recursive walk that never escapes, no concurrency, where loop/recur or reduce/reduce-kv/transducers express the same algorithm. REFACTOR THIS.
- HOT-PATH-EFFICIENCY: scratch-shape but measurably faster on a real hot path. KEEP, add a one-line rationale comment.

The overwhelming majority of atoms in this codebase are DOM/listener/observer/timer ref-cells, once-only latches, async continuation accumulators and swap!-extraction cells: all LEGITIMATE. Refactoring those is regression risk for no gain. "Already idiomatic, no change needed" is a VALID and EXPECTED outcome. Do not invent refactors to justify the bead.

DELIVERABLE: either a PR refactoring the confirmed SCRATCH-SMELL sites (file:line evidence plus a one-line justification per change), or a no-change finding recorded on this bead naming each site and its classification.
