(1) `cmd /c dir /AL <path>` from the Bash tool prints only the cmd banner, no listing, so every directory reports 'not a junction'. (2) `fsutil file queryfileid` DOES NOT share the target's id - a control junction reported a DIFFERENT id from its target, so this test calls a real junction 'not a junction' too. THE WORKING DETECTOR, validated against a deliberately-created control junction: the `ReparsePoint` attribute plus `LinkType`/`Target` via PowerShell `Get-Item -Force`. Belt-and-braces that also validated: `[IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false)` unlinks a junction leaving the target's contents intact, and refuses a populated real directory - safe to run before every `git worktree remove`. THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL: a worker worktree's implementation/node_modules was confirmed a live junction into the mayor's real node_modules, the exact configuration that destroyed it once already. ALWAYS validate a detector against a control junction you create yourself before trusting it. Supersedes [[junction-detection-via-cmd-c-dir-al-path]].

Windows unclean-shutdown can ZERO-FILL .git/config (12KB of \0), breaking ALL git ('fatal: bad config line 1'). Diagnose: od -c .git/config shows all \0; scan .git top-level for other all-null files (only config was hit). Recover: back up the corrupt file, reconstruct config from surviving data — remote URL from .git/FETCH_HEAD, committer identity from recent commit objects (read with config moved aside), core/* Windows defaults; restore beads.role via 'git config beads.role maintainer'. Verify with git fsck-lite (cat-file -e HEAD + HEAD^{tree}), ls-remote, and 'only tracked file modified is the expected one' (a zero-filled tracked file would show as modified). Happened 2026-07-08.

A DEFECT-WITNESS TEST AND ITS FIX ARE MUTUALLY INVALIDATING — merging both without flipping the witness REDS MAIN, in either order. Cost a P0 red-on-main on 2026-07-24.

THE MECHANISM: a validation pilot reproduces a known hazard and writes it down as a LIVE TEST asserting the CURRENT (broken) behaviour. A separate slice FIXES that hazard. Each PR is green against a main lacking the other. Merge both and the witness test fails, because the defect it documents no longer exists.

THE CONCRETE CASE: the dropdown pilot independently reproduced the ref-composition hazard and shipped `a-behavior-and-a-top-layer-state-on-one-element-lose-a-ref` — a test that PASSES ONLY WHILE THE BUG IS PRESENT. I merged the pilot, then merged the ref-composition fix, and main went red with 2 failures. Every other gate stayed green, so it read like a mystery regression in a slice that had been CLEAN as a PR.

⚠️ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A MEMORY IS THAT I HAD ALREADY IDENTIFIED THE PATTERN AND FAILED TO APPLY IT. Days earlier I wrote into a different brief: "both pilots assert the current REFUSAL in a test, so the blocked cell re-opens loudly. THOSE ASSERTIONS WILL START FAILING WHEN YOU SUCCEED — update them deliberately as part of this slice." I understood it for the compiled-browser refusal and did not carry it to the very next fix I merged. Recognising a hazard in one place does not transfer it to another unless it becomes a CHECK.

THE CHECK, now standing — BEFORE MERGING ANY FIX, ASK: does a merged test currently ASSERT THE DEFECT THIS FIXES? If yes, the flip belongs in the SAME PR as the fix, or main goes red the moment both are in.
  git grep -l "<hazard keyword>" implementation/**/test/
Pilot and validation suites are the usual home, because documenting current-state honestly is exactly what they are FOR.

THE REPAIR IS A FLIP, NOT A DELETE, and it has three parts:
  1. Assert the FIXED behaviour positively (both participants ran), never loosen to tolerate either outcome — that discards the only coverage of the combination.
  2. RENAME the test. A name asserting the opposite of its body is a trap for the next reader.
  3. Sweep for SIBLING witnesses in the same suite rather than discovering them one merge at a time.

⚠️ AND THE DIAGNOSTIC LESSON: the failure looked like a regression in the fix. The worker got it right by READING CI OWN LOG for the failing test NAME and MESSAGE — the name said "lose-a-ref" and the message said "one of the two refs was lost", which is the test DOCUMENTING a defect, not detecting one. A test name that describes a BUG rather than a PROPERTY is the tell. My own grep for the failure lines used a pattern chosen before I knew what the output looked like and returned only the namespace roster — capture the log to a file and read it.

GENERAL FORM: this WILL recur wherever validation pilots run alongside active development, which is the whole point of running them. It is a property of the arrangement, not a mistake by either author.

WORKER 'BACKGROUND-GATES-THEN-END-TURN' PATTERN: several workers (xray-tail, m90brg-finish, schemas-5a5qwp) did the full implementation + committed-or-staged it, then spawned their gate runs (npm run test:cljs, JVM suites) as BACKGROUND tasks and ENDED THEIR TURN saying 'I'll pick up when the background tests report' — leaving the work uncommitted/unpushed with the bead still IN_PROGRESS. The harness fires a completion notification but there's no PR. RECOGNITION: worker 'completed' but result says 'background test runs still executing / I'll wait for completion' + worktree shows modified>0, commits/pushed=0. RECOVERY (fast, no work lost): SendMessage-resume the SAME agent → tell it to run gates in the FOREGROUND (wait inline), commit, rebase, push, gh pr create, bd close. Its WIP survives. PREVENTION: put 'run gates in the FOREGROUND — do NOT background them or end your turn waiting on a background task' in dispatch briefs (already added to recent ones; the pattern still recurs, so keep the resume-recovery reflex). NOT a stall — the work is done, just the push step remains.

Worker brief gate-scope lesson (2026-06-09): do NOT require a worker to run the FULL gate matrix locally (all per-artefact clojure -M:test + npm test:cljs/test:browser + elision + mcp-conformance + xray-feature-gate). That makes a heavy-core bead run multi-hour (B6/rf2-vzld77 ran ~2h+, mostly serial gates + build-cache churn of thousands of files). Instead: have the worker run its SLICE gates (the artefacts it touched) + a quick smoke, then OPEN the PR and let the PR's CI run the full matrix. The mayor merges on green CI. Reserve full-local-suite only for the very few beads where CI can't cover it. Applies to future B7/B9 + any big core bead.

Worker briefs MUST forbid committing .beads/issues.jsonl (the mayor owns it; bd auto-stages it in the worker worktree but the worker should NOT git add/commit it). Root cause of PR #3494 stuck CONFLICTING/DIRTY: the worker committed a stale jsonl snapshot that collided with 21 commits of intervening bead changes, blocking CI entirely. Add 'do NOT git add/commit .beads/issues.jsonl' to every worker brief alongside the 'bd close cross-ref' line. Greenup fix: rebase, resolve jsonl by 'git checkout origin/main -- .beads/issues.jsonl', confirm the branch no longer touches it.

WORKER LIVENESS (Windows mayor loop): TaskList can return 'No tasks found' for background agents launched in a PRIOR turn even while they are actively running, AND their output-file mtime does NOT advance during a run (transcript flush is buffered). Both gave false 'dead' signals — a realm worker that TaskList showed as absent + mtime static for 9min actually completed a 624s run. NEVER infer a worker is dead from TaskList/mtime; NEVER recycle/--force-remove a worker's worktree on that basis (it clobbers live workers mid-edit). The ONLY reliable liveness signal is the completion/kill <task-notification>. To recycle, wait for that notification or confirm via a pushed branch with the expected commits.

Background workers and review agents MUST NOT create, claim, or close beads. Beads are mayor action only — filing them makes the mayor think they own the work. Worker outputs go in chat and ai/findings/ (local). Use background workers freely for parallel drafts/research; never bd create for that.

Worker path-leak mechanism (CONFIRMED 2026-07-17, rf2-r09qj + flagged by rf2-klyw5): a subagent that Reads MAYOR-checkout absolute paths during exploration can have its SUBSEQUENT Edit tool-calls carry that mayor path — so edits land in the mayor checkout, NOT the worktree. Invisible in the worker's OWN git status (the worktree looks clean); visible only from the mayor side. MITIGATION that works: the boundary-block's post-write BOTH-TREES check catches it — the worker self-recovers (git checkout-restore the mayor file, copy completed work into the worktree, verify mayor clean). HARDEN BRIEFS: instruct workers to Read AND Edit only worktree-absolute paths (never the mayor checkout, even for exploration reads), re-verify rev-parse per edit, and run the both-trees check after the first edit + any new file. Mayor-side detection: 'git status --short | grep -v .beads' in the mayor checkout should be empty; a stray modified file there = a live leak (capture the diff, don't blind-revert if the worker may be mid-recovery). This is a REAL Agent-subagent mechanism, distinct from the Workflow args-undefined misdiagnosis.

Worker PR-creation hang gotcha (2026-06-09): a worker (B6/vzld77) completed + committed + pushed its work, then hung ~1h LOOPING on 'gh pr create' with a heredoc body containing backticks/parens (bash kept mis-parsing). Mayor salvaged by opening the PR from the pushed branch. LESSON: in worker briefs, tell workers to create the PR with a SIMPLE body or '--body-file', avoid backticks/parens/heredocs in the inline body; and if a worker is committed+pushed but PR-less + idle, the mayor can open the PR for it (git -C <wt> push; gh pr create --head <branch>) rather than killing the work.

Worker recovery hazard (learned 2026-06-22, the #4910/#4913 xray-testbeds incident): (1) A worker coming to rest is NOT proof it finished. The xray-testbeds worker came to rest waiting on a gate it launched; the mayor misjudged it as done, committed its UNCOMMITTED partial work as a recovery PR (#4910) — but it had not yet written standard_epochs/core.cljs, so #4910 merged an incomplete state that crashed the two-frame surface on load and left a red gate on main. RULE: only recover/commit a worker's work after a genuine final report with a PR URL; an idle worktree mid-task is not a completion signal. (2) NEVER git worktree remove --force a worktree whose worker may still be live — it destroyed the live worker's workspace AND emptied the mayor implementation/node_modules via the node_modules junction cascade (the worker had to npm install to restore the mayor tree). RULE: only remove a worktree for a worker that has genuinely completed (final report received); the junction-rmdir-before-remove step does not protect against removing a still-active worktree.

A WORKTREE YOU DID NOT EXPLICITLY DISPATCH MAY BE YOUR OWN WORKER SPAWNING A SECOND WORKTREE — not a concurrent session. Misdiagnosed 2026-07-24. I dispatched a 4-bead cluster to ONE worker; it did 3 beads in worktree A (PR one) then created worktree B for the 4th bead (PR two). My hygiene scan found worktree B, had no record of creating it, and I concluded a concurrent session was also dispatching workers. WRONG — it was my own worker branching per bead. THE COST: the false belief made me over-cautious about that surface being externally contested. THE DISCRIMINATOR before concluding concurrent-session: a branch named worker/<desc>-<beadid> whose bead you assigned to a live worker IS that worker, even as a second worktree. Check worker completion reports and open PRs first — a worker report names every worktree and PR it created. Track by BEAD ownership (who did I give this bead to), never by worktree count: one worker is NOT necessarily one worktree or one PR. The genuinely-separate process here (the pr-audit loop) FILES beads, it does not dispatch code-editing workers, so it never contests a code surface. No harm done — I correctly did not touch the worktree or re-dispatch the bead.

WORKER TRAP — git mv then edit (2026-07-25, found by the misc-cluster-a worker on PR #6946): after 'git mv old.cljc new_cljs_test.cljc', a subsequent 'git add <path>' does NOT pick up content edits made after the mv. The worker's first pushed commit therefore carried the RENAMED file with the OLD ns name still inside it — a commit that would not compile. It was caught only by noticing a stray 'M' in git status, then fixed by rebuilding both commits from the base and force-pushing with --force-with-lease. This is the exact shape of the rf2-dn6v7 / rf2-lgozq lane-suffix work (rename file + edit ns in one change), so it will recur. Put in briefs for any rename-plus-edit bead: after a git mv, re-run 'git add' on the path AFTER the content edit, and verify with 'git diff --cached' that BOTH the rename and the content change are staged before committing; a rename-only commit of a .cljc test file is a non-compiling commit.

Worker worktrees have NO node_modules, so browser/shadow-cljs gates cannot run there by default. Do NOT junction into the mayor checkout's node_modules to fix it — that is the configuration that destroyed the mayor's real node_modules once and nearly again. THE SAFE ANSWER IS `npm ci` INSIDE THE WORKTREE (one worker did exactly this today, exit 0, no junction created, canary unmoved). Cost is a few minutes; the alternative is deferring every browser gate to CI. Put this in any brief whose gate menu includes `npm run test:browser`, a shadow-cljs build, or an adapter testbed spec.cjs — otherwise the worker hits 'shadow-cljs is not recognized', concludes the gate is unrunnable, and defers coverage that actually matters (the real-DOM gate catches repaint bugs test:cljs structurally cannot see). Related: [[windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the]].

Workers can get stuck in a monitor-wait loop on slow test suites (rul3ov burned ~770K tokens over 3 segments re-arming a Monitor for the full CLJS conformance run before committing). Recovery: SendMessage the agentId with a firm 'do NOT arm another Monitor — commit FIRST, push, gh pr create NOW; CI runs the full suite so CI is the gate, not your local terminal.' Over-cautious 'won't PR until local green' is the anti-pattern; the PR's CI is the real gate.

Workers strand because the long gate outlives their TURN budget, not because they disobeyed 'run foreground'. Three workers in one session (dispatch-sync, ci-test-lanes, tags-ratchet) ended their turn mid-gate with 'Waiting on the spine/watcher' — commits pushed, NO PR, nothing mergeable. A brief that says 'run test-fast-pr.sh foreground to completion, THEN open the PR' makes stranding likely on a loaded box, because the spine can exceed the budget. BETTER BRIEF ORDER: commit -> run only the FOCUSED, fast, arm-specific gates (plus any non-vacuity/mutation proof, which is cheap and is the evidence that actually matters) -> OPEN THE PR -> name the slow gates as 'deferred to CI' in the ## Quality gates section. CI runs the same surface and IS the merge gate; the local spine never was. Recovery is SendMessage-resume, which works and keeps the worker's context.

Workflow rule (Mike, 2026-06-10): beads marked in_progress are LOCKED - never update their title/description/notes/scope (a worker is executing against them). To add findings or scope to in-progress work, CREATE A FOLLOW-UP BEAD (dep on the in-progress one if sequenced). Check status with bd show before any bd update.

Worktree cleanup: a directory can be REUSED and re-pointed at a different branch mid-session, so a name-based safe-list goes stale while you are acting on it. Observed live: a hygiene agent was handed 'ci-test-lanes-cluster - safe to remove, PR #7116 merged', but between the list being written and the removal, a worker reused that same directory on a NEW branch (worker/xray-fuzzy-regression-pin) carrying an open PR #7119. Removing by name would have destroyed an in-flight PR worktree. Re-read `git worktree list --porcelain` IMMEDIATELY BEFORE each removal and re-verify the branch AND its PR state at that moment; never trust a safe-list compiled minutes earlier. Corollary: 'PR merged' is a fact about a BRANCH, not about a DIRECTORY. Related: [[rebase-merge-makes-a-worker-branch-look-unmerged]].

Worktree hygiene: `git status` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH to decide whether a worktree holds work. The `/ai/` tree is GITIGNORED, so findings docs, gate logs, PR-body drafts and ad-hoc probes are INVISIBLE to git status — a worktree that looks pristine can hold real content. Sweep `ai/` (and any `.worker-logs/`, `.wt-logs/`) separately and READ any non-log file before discarding. Observed: three worktrees held hidden content (20 gate logs, a pr-body.md draft, an ad-hoc probe .clj) — all correctly judged residue, but only because they were looked at. Corollary for the other direction: a hygiene brief that says 'clean tree = safe to remove' is wrong on this repo.

WSL bash.exe DOUBLE-EXPANDS a -c command string. Found by rf2-sefx0 (#6357, 2026-07-18) with a decisive probe: bash -lc with FOO=hello then printf of the escaped dollar-FOO prints the literal dollar-FOO under Git Bash (single pass) but prints hello under WSL bash (an outer pass already substituted it). CONSEQUENCE: any -c string that READS BACK a variable the SAME string assigns is broken under WSL — the outer pass substitutes the not-yet-assigned name to empty. That is how a PATH= assignment referencing a FIXTURE_DIR assigned immediately to its left silently produced /bin:<real PATH>, so stub executables were never found and 15 of 15 cases failed before reaching the code under test. Pre-existing vars (PWD, PATH) survive both passes, which is why the bug looks selective. FIX SHAPE: build one env-prefixed command whose every dollar-NAME already exists in the parent environment; let the child script read the rest from its own environment rather than from the command string. DISPROVED on the way: the semicolon separator is fine, and double-quoting is fine — do not chase those. TESTING LESSON (the important half): a BEHAVIOURAL test for this cannot protect you, because Git Bash and the Ubuntu CI runner both expand ONCE — a reintroduced self-reference stays green on CI while breaking only for Windows contributors. sefx0 pinned the STRUCTURE instead (assert the command references only pre-existing variables) with a non-vacuity guard. Generalise: when a defect is invisible on the platform your CI runs, a structural pin beats a behavioural one.

title: scripts: beads-checkpoint must pass --include-memories under bd v1.1.2
description: rf2-fwij4 migrated the tracker to bd v1.1.2, whose bare 'bd export' EXCLUDES memory rows by default (565 'bd remember' memories; v1.0.3 always included them). scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh and scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1 call bare 'bd export', so every future checkpoint would silently drop the memories from .beads/issues.jsonl — and the shrink guard would refuse the commit (this is exactly how it was caught: the post-migration checkpoint refused at 1997 rows vs HEAD's 2561). Fix: add --include-memories to the export invocation in BOTH scripts; keep the shrink floor as-is (it just proved its worth). Verify: run sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh and confirm it commits a file whose row count = issues + memories, and that 'git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | grep -c _type.:.memory' returns 565-ish, not 0. Also check scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh and the pre-commit hook floor for any assumption about bare 'bd export'.
close_reason: Both checkpoint siblings now run 'bd export --include-memories' (bd v1.1.2 drops the 565 memory rows bare), the layer-8 stub models the v1.1.2 contract so 8a pins memory survival, and --pre-pull answers read-only from any worktree; verified 68/68 suite green, worker-worktree pre-flights exit 0, and the probe export = 1998 issues + 565 memories: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7294

title: reagent-slim arm is non-reactive in a mixed stock+slim bench bundle (HD-008 finding)
description:
Found by rf2-2rtt6.7's HD-008 donor-gate instrument. In the :advanced bench bundle that compiles BOTH stock reagent and reagent2 (reagent-slim), with the reagent-slim adapter installed, a reg-view component tree mounted through reagent2.dom.client renders CORRECTLY at mount (canonical-DOM parity passes at both sizes, values correct) but NEVER re-renders on a write.

Reproduced with: writes via frame/replace-app-db! AND via rf/dispatch-sync of a registered event; drains via reagent2.dom.client/flush-render!, reagent2.ratom/flush!, and both twice. 78 of 78 writes failed the DOM read-back in every configuration; the stock-Reagent arm in the identical harness passed 78/78.

The instrument SUPPRESSED the figures rather than publishing them: the unverified arm was reading 0.16-0.50x the floor while changing nothing, which would have published as 'reagent-slim narrow write is 2-6x faster than a top-down re-render'.

NOT yet established whether this is (a) a reagent-slim adapter defect, (b) a mixed-bundle artefact of stock reagent and reagent2 coexisting with re-frame.views late-binding to one component factory, or (c) a defect in the bench arm's composition. (b) is the leading hypothesis and would make it bench-only. Needs a minimal repro: slim adapter, reg-view, frame-provider, one sub, one write, in a bundle WITHOUT stock reagent — if that is reactive, it is (b).

Repro command: node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/hd8_run.cjs (see the slim run's :unverified map). Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/hd8_{witnesses,rows,app,run}.*
notes:
DIAGNOSED — candidate (c), the bench arm's composition. NOT (a) an adapter defect and NOT (b) a mixed-bundle artefact. No user is affected and no shipped code changes.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THE BEAD ASKED FOR. A single-substrate reagent-slim bundle — 96 compiled sources, stock Reagent verifiably ABSENT (checked against the build's own source map, not asserted from a :require list) — re-renders on EVERY write under the adapter's own documented drain contract: 0 unverified of 12, all at the sync rung, under both write mechanisms (frame/replace-app-db! and dispatch-sync). chromium 147.0.7727.15, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false.

BUNDLE COMPOSITION IS IRRELEVANT. Four bundles spanning 96 to 114 compiled sources — slim alone; slim + stock reagent; slim + uix; and the bead's own three-adapter mix — return byte-identical verdicts. Stock Reagent in the SAME mixed bundle passes all three orders 0 of 12, reproducing the bead's 78/78 control.

IT IS NOT LATE-BINDING EITHER. The positive control — a plain reagent-slim component reading a plain reagent2.core/atom, with no frame, no subscribe and no :adapter/* hook on its path — reproduces the failure EXACTLY, in every slim bundle. re-frame is not on the causal path at all.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, one microtask. lane/verified-write! writes, yields ONE microtask, then drains. reagent-slim's render scheduler is microtask-based, so by then it has already emptied its own component queue and issued forceUpdate OUTSIDE any flushSync boundary; React holds that work at the default lane and the flush-render! that follows finds nothing to flush. Stock Reagent survives the identical harness because its queue is rAF-scheduled and therefore still full one microtask later.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SYMPTOM AS FILED. (1) The arm is not non-reactive — its commit is LATE: all 12 of 12 writes reach the DOM at the macrotask rung, and no synchronous re-drain recovers them. (2) app-db took the new value on every write in every bundle (db-followed-all? true), so the failure was always on the view leg.

EXISTING COVERAGE WAS RIGHT. implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/testbed/smoke.cjs mounts a reg-view tree under rf/frame-provider through reagent2.dom.client, clicks, and asserts the counter text changes, in a slim-only bundle. Green throughout (npm run test:reagent-slim:smoke, exit 0).

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/slim-non-reactive-arm-diagnosis.md. RIG: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/z3vlz_* (four entries, one probe, rides :hicasso-bench via --config-merge; no new build id). Arm-order guard NOT ENGAGED — the rig publishes no timed figure and no arm-to-arm ratio.

FOLLOW-UPS: rf2-b69lw (fix the HD-008 slim arm's ordering and RE-TAKE the suppressed slim write figures — they price a commit that had not happened), rf2-pq7d8 (lane/verified-write!'s fixed yield is not neutral across scheduler families).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7266. Completeness and diagnosis are strong: exact landed six-page :advanced rerun with the checkout's real dependency tree reproduced the published matrix (four reagent-slim pages 0/0/12, two stock pages 0/0/0; mounts, raw controls, app-db evidence and bundle-source-map checks all pass). Keep the causal conclusion and existing repair owners rf2-b69lw/rf2-pq7d8. Repair three small durability gaps before re-closing: (1) z3vlz_run.cjs exits 0 for any completed result matrix; it fails only build/composition/page/fatal errors, so missing verdicts, failed mounts/controls, changed 0/0/12 results, non-identical slim bundles, or false db-followed evidence merely print `?`/different text and still end `[z3vlz] ok`. Assert the six declared page contracts in data and fail on drift—no new framework needed. (2) tally adds :db-followed-all? only when `(some :db-followed? rs)` is truthy, so the all-false event-leg failure omits the field precisely when it matters; test key presence, then `every?`. (3) raw/subs unmount exceptions are swallowed between arms; surface cleanup failure so the following arm cannot be certified on a contaminated page. Durable provenance should cite landed instrument bf5cd5a2a3 (producing f998a74c4a = authored 3f51f7053b = landed bf5cd5a2a3) and landed record e7426b9855, retaining authored mapping only as supplemental. Required CI and diff check are clean.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7279: the landed patch 2f3ee069c5 (authored head 1dbe4a49a0; stable patch a188410c05 exact) discharges all three #7266 durability gaps. Declarative six-page contracts now gate counts and escalation rungs; app-db population uses key presence plus every?; both unmount failures are recorded and adjudicated. Four cold-cache isolated advanced runs passed every declared variant/page (1 + 2 + 1 + 2), and synthetic adjudicator mutations refused missing gates/order, bad mount, count/rung drift, false db witness, and teardown failure. The default four-variant invocation still reproduced the shared Shadow-cache `reading 'd'` failure; that is exact owner rf2-2rtt6.20, reopened because its fix PR #7278 is not merged. No new Bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7291 (2026-07-30). PR #7291 correctly makes normal-return release observable in lane/release! and the P0 Reagent bulk path, but the exact z3vlz instrument still has two own release sites that call unmount, remove the container, and accept a normal no-op. This is distinct from in-progress rf2-jk3vj, whose locked scope names only p0_converge_app and hd8_rows. Reproduction at landed d6352dc8d707204b1a72fcabe0cbc12d5a0be088: replace only the raw-control `(unmount handle)` call with nil, then run `Z3VLZ_ONLY=slim-only node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/z3vlz_run.cjs`; the :advanced bundle reports raw-control `:teardown []`, all declared page contracts met, `[z3vlz] ok`, exit 0. Restore verified by identical normalized blob hash and clean worktree. Apply lane/container-released! after each successful z3vlz raw/subs unmount and before `.remove`, then require this normal-no-op mutation to red. Keep it diagnostic-local; no lifecycle framework.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7295 (folded in on mayor instruction as its own commit, 2a86358772). The PR #7291 audit's remainder: both of the z3vlz rig's own release sites — the subs arm and the raw control in z3vlz_probe.cljs — now perform lane/container-released! after a NORMAL unmount return and BEFORE the .remove, exactly as lane/release! does; the record lands in :teardown, which z3vlz_run.cjs already adjudicates as a page-contract refusal. The audit's exact reproduction now reds: raw-control (unmount handle) replaced with nil, Z3VLZ_ONLY=slim-only — exit 0 at landed d6352dc8d7, now exit 1 with '[z3vlz] FAILED: slim-only / install=reagent-slim / raw-control: 1 teardown failure(s)... the unmount RETURNED NORMALLY but its container still holds 1 node(s)'; plant reverted with git diff empty. Clean Z3VLZ_ONLY=slim-only run at the adoption exit 0, all declared page contracts met. Diagnostic-local, no lifecycle framework; causal conclusion and repair owners unchanged.

title: bench(hicasso): sibling own-release paths lack the container-released check
description: rf2-2rtt6.2's second-audit remainder added lane/container-released! — after an unmount RETURNS NORMALLY, the container is read BEFORE detach; a populated one is a root that was never released (a React root's unmount empties its container synchronously). lane/release! and the P0 Reagent app's release-bulk-arms! now perform it, so every mount-row release lane-wide is covered. Two sibling BULK own-release paths still remove the container unchecked: p0_converge_app.cljs release-bulk-arms! (~line 531) and hd8_rows.cljs's own release (~line 740). Both should adopt lane/container-released! exactly as p0_reagent_app does — one line per site plus the docstring sentence. Their arms are real React roots today, so this is closing the observability gap, not fixing a live fault. Keep it benchmark-local; no lifecycle machinery.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7295. title: Spec 009 marks two router in-band rejections diagnostic; the code fans them always-on
description:
Found while implementing rf2-eg61l (PR #7247).

Spec 009 §Error event catalogue's Channel column reads `diagnostic` for BOTH:

  - `:rf.error/classification-effect-shape` (009:2010)
  - `:rf.error/legacy-runtime-root`         (009:2041)

Neither is diagnostic in the code. `router/emit-classification-effect-shape!`
and `router/emit-legacy-runtime-root!` both fan through
`error-emit/emit-error-both!`, whose axis 1 is `dispatch-on-error!` — NOT
gated on `interop/debug-enabled?`, explicitly documented as the
production-survivable off-box-shipper source of truth. So both categories DO
reach Sentry/Datadog from an `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` build, and
their own router docstrings say so (`emit-legacy-runtime-root!`: "Always-on:
the corpus-wide listener observes the rejection in production").

Consistent with the stale Channel column, both are ALSO absent from
`always-on-axis-conformance-cljs-test`'s `always-on-categories` literal, so
neither is exercised through `register-error-listener!` by the EP-0008
conformance leg that exists to make promotion real rather than documentary.

Nothing catches this today. `error-catalogue-channel-conformance-test`'s
source scan proves every EMITTED category is catalogued and that the literal
== the parsed always-on rows; it does not cross-check the emit MECHANISM
against the Channel column, so a category emitted via `emit-error-both!` and
catalogued `diagnostic` passes.

The ruling: either graduate both rows to `always-on` (and add both to the
literal IN THE SAME COMMIT — spec/009's rows and that literal are coupled such
that either edit alone reds the conformance test), or demote the emissions to
`trace/emit-error!` and lose the production witness. Graduation looks right —
both are in-band FINAL-effects-boundary rejections that abort an event with no
commit, which is precisely the class an operator needs to see in production —
but it is a channel ruling, not a mechanical fix.

Worth considering alongside: teach the channel-conformance test to flag a
catalogue row marked `diagnostic` whose category is emitted through
`emit-error-both!` / `dispatch-on-error!` in non-test source. The scan
already harvests exactly those call sites; it just does not compare them to the
Channel column. That would make this class of drift impossible to reintroduce.

Fence note: spec/009 is hot-zone, and the co-edit means the spec row and
implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc must
move together in one PR.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-31, dossier review): GRADUATE — option (a) WITH the conformance rider. The Channel column is stale; the code's always-on fan-out was deliberate (451b6079cd shipped the final-boundary legacy-root rejection with an explicit production witness; ba27a72ffc routed the classification rejection through the same two-axis helper; 574d62ae15 tightened and production-tested the record) and matches the standing production-observability direction (rqje9, mwv4e, 6jqa8, g0mep): both are in-band FINAL-effects-boundary rejections that abort an event with no commit, invisible at the dispatch call site — exactly the class an operator must see in production. Option (b) REJECTED: demoting the emissions would delete a shipped production witness (and renounce the docstrings' promise) to preserve a stale table cell. Do NOT add a router-specific rejection channel, callback, or generic router-rejected category; the two existing category ids stay (they discriminate "retired runtime root" from "malformed classification effect" at a glance). Zero runtime change — spec + conformance catch up with the code.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (this bead is now the implementation owner — dispatchable, one PR):

1. COUPLED TWO-FILE COMMIT (either edit alone reds `parsed-always-on-set-equals-the-exercise-literal` in implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj — they move in the SAME commit):
   (i) spec/009-Instrumentation.md — flip the Channel cell `diagnostic` -> `always-on` on BOTH rows: `:rf.error/classification-effect-shape` (~line 2010) and `:rf.error/legacy-runtime-root` (~line 2041).
   (ii) implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc — add `:rf.error/classification-effect-shape` and `:rf.error/legacy-runtime-root` to the `always-on-categories` literal, each with a short graduation comment in the file's existing style citing rf2-h4f0n. Both are event-centric emit-error-both! categories, so the existing per-event exercise loop drives them through dispatch-on-error! automatically (the :rf.error/bad-frame-provider-arg precedent) — no bespoke exercise arm.

2. STALE PROSE: in the 009 `:rf.error/legacy-runtime-root` row, REMOVE the "Dev-tier; production DCE-elides" claim — it contradicts the always-on grading. Where the two rows' prose describes the channel, say the category rides the always-on error-emit axis (surface #4) alongside the DCE'd dev trace, mirroring sibling always-on rows. No other row restructuring.

3. THE RIDER (exactly this narrow): in implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj, the source scan already harvests literal call-site categories for emit-error-both!/dispatch-on-error! (emit-error-re, ~line 317; currently one alternation shared with the trace-only fns). Add ONE assertion: every category harvested from a literal `emit-error-both!` / `dispatch-on-error!` call site in non-test runtime source must be catalogued `always-on` — i.e. a `diagnostic`-catalogued category emitted through the always-on mechanism is an error. Implementation freedom: a sibling regex (or capture) narrowed to the two always-on fns, then one set/field comparison against the parsed Channel column. NO interprocedural analysis, NO helper taxonomy, NO new roster; literal-only stays literal-only (`:rf.error/handler-exception` passes a VARIABLE category — out of scope by design). Verified 2026-07-31: every OTHER literal always-on-mechanism call site in src/ is already catalogued always-on (frame-destroyed, no-such-sub, sub-exception, no-frame-context, bad-frame-provider-arg, write-after-destroy, flow-eval-exception, read-after-release, observation-port-version-mismatch, observation-on-change-failed, frame-preflight-evidence-mismatch, unsupported-scroll-strategy), so the rider lands green with exactly these two graduations.

4. RECORD-SHAPE DISCIPLINE (zero runtime change): the always-on records ship EXACTLY as today. Keep the rejected classification `:value` and the interpolating `:reason` OFF the always-on record — they ride the DCE'd dev trace only; `:offending-key` remains the lone always-on discriminator via emit-error-both!'s record-attrs seam. Do NOT add `:failing-id` to the classification trace tags (it would trip emit-error-both!'s shared lift and drag the interpolating `:reason` onto the record). The closed always-on record key set stays pinned by implementation/core/test/re_frame/classification_effect_shape_record_cljs_test.cljc and must not change.

5. FENCE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE — sequence this PR against any other in-flight 009 work (second waits for the first's merge). Files in the PR: spec/009-Instrumentation.md + implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc + implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj. Router source untouched.

title: bench: the allocation harness cannot certify an arm it has optimised to its own floor
description:
RAISED BY the rf2-2ix22 worker (PR #7253), which deliberately left it unfiled rather than expand its own scope, and flagged that it will bite the next worker on this surface.

THE PROBLEM. Every improvement on the ambient-reader / routed-hook surface now lands its arms AT the instrument's own floor, and the arm-order guard refuses a floor-level arm exactly as it refuses a contaminated one. So the better the optimisation, the less certifiable the result:

  rf2-2ix22's baseline run is guard-REPORTABLE at exit 0, so its 264.0 B/read BEFORE figure is fully certified.
  Both AFTER runs exit 2. The guard refuses H-ROUTED, H-SAMEH, H-SAMEFLAT, S0-SCOPE, S1-CURFRM and S2-TGTID -- every arm the two levers pushed to the floor.

THE SIGNATURE IS DIAGNOSTIC, and the worker named it: a per-WINDOW floor rather than a per-call cost, evidenced by an identical ~6.37x phase ratio across arms with nothing else in common. That is not the bimodality the phase factor exists to catch.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #7253. The rf2-2ix22 ruling resolved this exact sequencing question against holding the production change: 'the production cleanup must NOT be made hostage to a benchmark enhancement' (Codex position, adopted). The worker honoured that -- changed no harness, did not hold the PR, and reported its after-figures as honest upper bounds with 0 UNVERIFIED of 1974 windows so nothing was DCE'd into looking cheap.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. The floor-aware quote the ruling deferred. Same family as rf2-ktrvw (thunk-dominated arms read V8's escape analysis) and the resolved rf2-tmzie (a hardcoded 4000-window cap made a per-call cost indistinguishable from a per-window floor -- PR #7242 made the cap configurable, which is the precedent for how to approach this).

NOT A LICENCE TO REBUILD THE HARNESS. Fifteen instrument faults have been caught on these surfaces, each having produced a plausible precise wrong number first; a sixteenth instrument is the likeliest way to add one. The minimal honest change is what is wanted: let a run distinguish 'below the floor' from 'refused', and quote a floor-bounded arm as an upper bound rather than declining to quote it.

DO NOT loosen the guard's tolerance to make refusals go away -- four workers have hit refusals on this surface and every one repaired the arm, not the guard.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7292 (2026-07-30). The floor sweep is focused and the guard remains untouched, but `floor-verdict` is fail-open at its minimum legal boundary: it accepts `ratio >= span/2` with `span >= 4`, so at span 4 the threshold is exactly 2 and the known 2x closure-bimodality class it says must remain refused is classified `:floor`. Bounded live proof at landed 21d7b9ef4e1ba9df94e190422e160f6851370d70: temporarily add a self-test fixture `[{reps 1, p50 128}, {reps 2, p50 128}, {reps 4, p50 64}]` expecting `:per-call`; the :advanced ui-bench build succeeds, then the pre-measurement self-test prints `want per-call, got floor` and exits 1. Restore verified by identical normalized blob 014b9c649aeadc2625534b0ebfeeb98e6adde36e and a clean worker tree. Current origin/main still carries the inclusive comparison; no open PR or duplicate Bead owns this boundary. Make equality refuse (or otherwise separate the 2x class with a conservative margin/minimum span) and pin this exact minimum-span fixture; do not weaken order_guard or add another measurement framework.
close_reason: floor-verdict's collapse demand is now strict (> span/2, not >=) so the 2x closure-bimodality bound refuses at the minimum span 4, with the audit's exact minimum-span fixture pinned in floor-self-test; guard untouched. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7297

title: HD-008: fix the reagent-slim write arm's write/drain ordering, then re-take the slim write figures
description:
HD-008's reagent-slim write row must not put a microtask between the write and the drain. rf2-z3vlz established (evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/slim-non-reactive-arm-diagnosis.md) that this ordering — and nothing about the adapter or the bundle — is what made the slim arm read 78 unverified of 78.

Mechanism: reagent-slim's render scheduler is microtask-based (reagent2.impl.batching: "a microtask-based scheduler ... no requestAnimationFrame fallback is required"). lane/verified-write! writes, yields ONE microtask, then calls the arm's force!. By then reagent-slim has already drained its own component queue and issued forceUpdate OUTSIDE any flushSync boundary, which reagent2.dom.client/flush-render! documents as the exact hazard its boundary exists to avoid — React holds the work at the default lane, the subsequent flush-render! finds an empty queue, and the read-back reads the old value. Stock Reagent survives the identical harness because its component queue is rAF-scheduled and therefore still full one microtask later. A second synchronous flush does NOT recover the commit; only letting React's scheduler run does (the value lands at the macrotask rung, so the arm is LATE, not non-reactive).

The repair is the ARM. Either shape reads 0 unverified of 12 in the rf2-z3vlz rig, under both write mechanisms and in all four bundle compositions:

  (rdc2/flush-render! (fn [] (write!) (ratom2/flush!)))   ;; write inside f — the documented production contract
  (write!) (rdc2/flush-render! (fn [] (ratom2/flush!)))   ;; or: no yield between the two

ALSO: the suppressed HD-008 slim write figures (reading 0.16-0.50x the floor while changing nothing) must be RE-TAKEN through the corrected arm, never rescued — they price a commit that had not happened.

Depends on rf2-2rtt6.7's hd8_* instrument, which is not on main at the time of filing.
notes:
UPDATE (post-rebase): rf2-2rtt6.7's hd8_* instrument HAS since landed on main, so this bead now has a live target — implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (write-arm / spine-drain!) plus whatever opt-out rf2-pq7d8 settles on in lane/verified-write!. Held out of rf2-z3vlz's PR on purpose: the repair obliges a full HD-008 re-run to replace the suppressed slim write figures, which is a re-publication of that bead's numbers and not a diagnosis.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7263: when this owner corrects the drain ordering and retakes the slim writes, also repair hd8-composed-donor-arm.md and rf2-2rtt6.7's close/evidence record. They still describe reagent-slim as non-reactive with mixed-bundle composition the leading hypothesis, contradicted by rf2-z3vlz's landed diagnosis: the arm is late because the harness yields a microtask before drain; bundle composition is irrelevant. Replace the misleading “156 unverified of 936 measured writes” with like-for-like counts: 156/1248 executed operations including warmups, or 120/960 timed post-warmup samples.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7269: the scheduler-aware repair itself reproduces cleanly at landed source: full three-adapter clean-cache run exit 0, all 12 rows reportable, 0 unverified; HD8_ONLY=slim with HD8_TOLERANCE=0.10 also exits 0 with all four rows reportable. Reopen for two exact durability gaps introduced here. (1) yield-cost! is recorded but never adjudicated or subtracted. An exact-source full rerun measured the slim run {:p50 0 :min 0 :max 0.10000002384185791 :n 10}; the driver still exited 0 and emitted unadjusted ratios, despite the studio record saying any nonzero reading owes subtraction. Define and enforce the correction/refusal contract. (2) HD8_ONLY only filters adapters; HD8_ONLY=slim still emits mount-M, mount-U, write-narrow, and write-bulk, so it does not mechanically prevent the competing figures its comment/record say it prevents. Restrict or explicitly mark non-publishing rows. No duplicate Bead.
BOTH DURABILITY GAPS CLOSED (PR #7282, commit 931098b039). No published figure moved.
(1) THE CORRECTION/REFUSAL CONTRACT IS NOW CODE. hd8-rows/yield-correction adjudicates BOTH write rows of EVERY run; hd8-app fails the run on a refusal, the same fail-closed path the positive control takes. Four verdicts: :not-owed (all arms share one window shape), :below-resolution (mixed shapes, aggregate max 0.0 -- bound recorded, not assumed), :corrected (mixed shapes, aggregate nonzero -- subtraction APPLIED, corrected band published beside the unadjusted one), :refused (nothing publishes, run exits non-zero). Refusal has NO tolerance of its own: a row is refused when subtracting the bound moves a published range across 1.0 -- the instrument's OWN house rule :straddles-1? -- or when a bearer's reading does not survive the subtraction, or when the row's k has no measured aggregate (unevaluable rather than corrected with the nearest number). The bound is the aggregate's MAX. The aggregate for THIS row's k is used, never a per-turn figure multiplied up. Direction is fixed (removing turns makes a bearer smaller), so on the slim run the unadjusted figure is a LOWER BOUND and both ends publish.
LIVE VERIFICATION, full three-run sweep at this branch, exit 0: uix run :not-owed both rows (all four arms :write-yield-drain); reagent run :not-owed both rows; slim run :below-resolution both rows, bearers [:floor], exempt [:reagent-slim], aggregate {:k 10 :p50 0 :max 0 :n 10} narrow and {:k 1 :p50 0 :max 0 :n 10} bulk. The verdict is stamped in the cross-run table directly above the figure it governs.
(2) HD8_ONLY NOW MARKS NON-PUBLISHING ROWS. HD8_ROWS names what a partial run publishes. HD8_ONLY unset = the full sweep, everything publishes. HD8_ONLY set WITHOUT HD8_ROWS publishes NOTHING -- the driver cannot know which re-take was intended -- and every row is stamped NON-PUBLISHING on its heading and on every figure beneath it, in the cross-run table a reader copies from; the provenance block prints what the run may publish. An HD8_ROWS naming a row the instrument does not emit is exit 1, because a typo would otherwise silently mark everything. Marked rather than suppressed: every gate still runs over the whole set.
PAGE CORRECTIONS: 'the harness microtask is beneath this instrument's resolution' was a generalisation from one run -- corrected to a per-run reading, citing the 0.1 ms rerun this bead's audit found. The false 'HD8_ONLY exists so that a future re-take cannot mint a competing set of figures' is replaced with what the flag actually does and what now enforces it.
GATE-CAUGHT DEFECT IN THE CONTRACT ITSELF, REPAIRED (commits 1bb8adb4e9, b0cf8e4ff8). Recording because it is the fault this instrument exists to refuse and it was found by running the thing rather than by reading it.
The survival test in correct-round started as pos?. On an HD8_ONLY=slim gate run where the ONE-TURN aggregate resolved at 0.0999999 ms, the BULK row's floor -- p50 about one 100us clock quantum -- survived the subtraction at ~1e-8 ms, still positive, and the row published a CORRECTED reagent-slim/floor of 15,518,934x with :straddles-1? unflipped so nothing refused it. Now: a bearer survives only when WHAT REMAINS EXCEEDS WHAT WAS REMOVED -- two measured quantities, no invented constant.
SELF-TEST ADDED, because a gate nobody has watched refuse is not a gate and this one refuses rarely: the aggregate read 0.0 on three of five observed runs of the same source on the same host and 0.0999999 on two. yield-correction-self-test replays six fixtures through the live rule -- one per verdict, one per refusal reason -- in the bundle BEFORE any clock; hd8-app throws, hd8_run.cjs prints every check and exits 1. Fixture 4 IS the 15,518,934x row. Verified live, 6/6 ok, all three refusal reasons among them.
NEW LIMITATION RECORDED (not fixed, deliberately): the BULK row's FLOOR sits on the clock clamp at about one quantum. The published bulk row was taken on a run whose aggregate read 0.0 so nothing was owed and it stands; on a run where the aggregate resolves, the correction is the whole of the bulk floor and the row REFUSES. Lifting it needs the batched window the narrow row got -- that changes a measured window and obliges a re-take of the row, which is a re-publication and was NOT made on this worker's authority. Candidate follow-up bead.
FINAL GATES on the merged branch: full three-run hd8_run.cjs exit 0 (3 self-test blocks, 0 FAIL, verdicts 4x :not-owed + 2x :below-resolution); hicasso_narrow_run.cjs exit 0; HD8_ONLY=slim exit 0 with every row marked NON-PUBLISHING; HD8_ONLY=slim HD8_ROWS=write-narrow,write-bulk exit 0 with only the mount rows marked; HD8_ROWS=bogus exit 1; order_guard self-test 12/12; npm run test:script-policy exit 0; npm run test:browser exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0 with no warning on either changed page.
FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-d2tzk carries the bulk-row clock-clamp finding -- the bulk floor sits at one quantum, so a resolved yield correction refuses the row. Needs the batched window the narrow row got, which obliges a re-take and is rf2-2rtt6.7's to authorise.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7282: reopened for two material holes in the new correction/publication contract. (1) yield-correction decides whether subtraction "moves a published range across 1.0" solely by a change in boolean :straddles-1?. A band wholly below 1 before correction and wholly above 1 afterward is false -> false and is accepted as :corrected. Concrete live-rule counterexample: two slim-row rounds at floor 1.0 / reagent-slim 0.95 with a 0.1 bound yield 0.95x unadjusted and 1.0556x corrected; the bearer survives, neither band straddles, and the complete direction reversal publishes. Compare a three-state below/straddles/above classification and add this fixture. (2) :summary-corrected and :head-to-head-corrected are computed, but hd8_app/correction! exports only verdict/reason/bound/why and hd8_run/crossRun prints only run.summary. A :corrected run therefore says the corrected band is published beside the unadjusted one while exposing no corrected endpoints in the copyable table. Propagate and label both bands. Exact landed source f437495fc5; the six correction self-tests passed before the saturated host made the advanced bundle build non-diagnostic. PR CI: 64 success, 18 intentional skips. No duplicate Bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7295 (2026-07-31): reopened. The newly copyable corrected-band path can publish a number that the existing DOM-read-back contract explicitly marked UNPUBLISHED. At landed a3d18c79917171d691b5ac51318be8d74e473e28, `measure-write!` replaces a bad arm only in `row :summary` with `{:unpublished :failed-dom-read-back ...}` while retaining numeric `:per-round`; `yield-correction` rebuilds numeric `:summary-corrected` from those per-round timings; `correction!` exports every corrected entry; and `crossRun` prints `cv` without checking the original `v.unpublished`. Executing the landed `band`/`crossRun` functions with the exact reachable shape prints two lines for the same arm: `UNPUBLISHED (1/78 unverified) [UNADJUSTED]`, then `1.200 – 1.300 [CORRECTED]`. That defeats the rule that a failed DOM read-back has no publishable timing. Bounded repair: preserve the original summary/head-to-head publication mask when forming or exporting corrected bands (and have the table refuse/omit a corrected value for an unpublished original), then add a deterministic corrected-table fixture covering this polarity. No new measurement or lifecycle machinery is needed.
close_reason: Corrected bands now inherit the original row's DOM-read-back publication mask at formation (inherit-publication-mask), export, and the cross-run table, with the audit's exact 1-of-78 polarity pinned red-then-green by in-bundle fixture 8 and a driver-side corrected-table self-test — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7302

title: RULING: should the sub-cache tolerate a ref-count-0 tenancy so a render-phase materialisation survives to the commit?
description:
SURFACED by rf2-2rtt6.12. A RULING, not a patch - it changes re-frame.subs AND Spec 006 (HOT-ZONE), so nothing was edited.

THE OBSERVATION. On the React-hook spine every subscription read with no live cache entry BUILDS TWO REACTIONS. Measured exactly, by counting: witness counters report bodyRuns = 2.00N against Reagent's 1.00N, twice over disjoint cells (docs/design/hicasso/studio/uix-spine-per-read-decomposition.md, commit 0cf86fb580). Cause: use-subscribe's render-phase balanced round trip goes 0 -> 1 -> 0, and Spec 006 Reference counting and disposal makes 1 -> 0 dispose in-tick with NO grace period, so the render-phase build is destroyed microseconds before the commit-phase acquire rebuilds it.

rf2-2rtt6.13 stops the dead reaction being RETAINED (-22% of the read, measured). It does NOT stop it being BUILT. That second construction re-runs the user's sub body once per read at mount - and for a layer-2+ sub it re-derefs the whole :<- input chain.

THE QUESTION. Should a cache slot be allowed to exist at ref-count 0 - materialised, not yet claimed, reaped on some later policy - so that the commit-phase subscribe ADOPTS the render-phase reaction instead of rebuilding it? If so, committed would be identical? to the render-phase handle, the double build would vanish, and the retention term rf2-2rtt6.13 removes would cost nothing to keep.

WHAT IT COSTS. Spec 006's no-grace-period rule is load-bearing: it is why a resubscribe after unsubscribe is a clean miss, and the docstring in re-frame.subs.cache/unsubscribe! reasons explicitly about React remount churn on that basis. A ref-count-0 tenancy needs a reaping policy, and an unreaped slot is a leak by another name.

NOT COSTED HERE. rf2-2rtt6.12 priced RETENTION only; the CPU of the double build is unmeasured. Cost it before ruling - if the double build is cheap, the honest answer may be to leave it and take rf2-2rtt6.13 alone.

Also NOT costed: re-frame.substrate.spine/release-source-wire! filterv's the fan-out coordinator's dependent vector per release, so unmounting a frame with D live derived values is O(D^2) pair comparisons. Not on the mount path and not this bead's finding - noted so it is not lost.
notes:
PROVENANCE CORRECTION (audit of PR #7264, discharged by rf2-2rtt6.12 on branch worker/bench-audit-cluster). This bead's evidence text cites instrument commit 0cf86fb580, which is the AUTHORED PR commit and is not on main.

THE DURABLE LANDED INSTRUMENT COMMIT IS 24e8822d7f. Full mapping: bb8fc38173=811f6cec42, 0cf86fb580=24e8822d7f, fa30f51128=27fa21ac4e, 1f381947ed=86c50a5d83.

The observation is unaffected — bodyRuns = 2.00N against Reagent's 1.00N, twice over disjoint cells, is the same exact-integer witness at the same instrument. Only the SHA to quote changes. The ruling this bead asks for is untouched.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-31, dossier review): DEFER-WITH-DEFAULT - option (c) of the decision dossier with the default leaning (b). The dossier carried two concurring reviews (the original recommendation and an appended Codex review, independently source-verified); both said: defer behind a costing, default no. The dossier file (ai/decisions/rf2-2rtt6.14.subcache-refcount0-tenancy.md) is deleted; this note is the durable record.

PART 1 - RULED NOW, NO CLOCK NEEDED. The question AS POSED - a GENERAL ref-count-0 tenancy in the sub-cache - is refused outright, at any measured cost. Correctness, not perf:
(1) React gives the store NO cancellation signal for a render that never commits, and no maximum render-to-subscribe interval; React 19.2.0 (the pinned version, implementation/package.json) installs the uSES subscription as a passive effect - an implementation detail, not a timing promise, so no end-of-tick or microtask reaper can be assumed to survive until the adopting callback.
(2) The repo's own Suspense witness (react_shared_suite.cljs ~4309, assert-use-subscribe-suspense-abort-before-commit-no-refcount-leak) renders use-subscribe, commits only the fallback, and asserts the abandoned subtree leaves NO ref-count. That is the constraint any change must preserve: an acquisition whose only prospective owner is a never-committed render has no later cleanup hook.
(3) A zero-owner parent keeps its whole layer-2+ input topology alive - and potentially recomputing - since disposal is what releases input subscriptions (cascade + shared-input behaviour pinned in sub_cache_test.clj ~518); tolerating zero-owner parents needs a second dormant-state protocol on top.
(4) Semantic cost: today a clean unsubscribe/resubscribe is a fresh materialisation (fresh input-fn topology, current registration body). Reuse-across-zero would make resubscribe results depend on an elapsed-time reaping policy.
A slot with no owner capable of ending it is a leak by another name; no benchmark can repair that. Spec 006's synchronous 1 -> 0 no-grace rule STANDS.

PART 2 - DEFERRED BEHIND A COSTING. Whether the double build warrants ANY remedy is deferred behind rf2-2rtt6.15 (bench lane, filed with this ruling). The phenomenon is real and exactly counted (bodyRuns = 2.00N vs Reagent 1.00N, twice over disjoint cells; instrument landed 24e8822d7f), and the control flow DERIVES it without the counter: use-subscribe's render-phase balanced round trip (spine.cljs ~2359-2368) goes 0 -> 1 -> 0 on an empty cache; unsubscribe! makes 1 -> 0 an immediate eviction (cache.cljc ~192-207); the durable subscribe waits for the uSES commit-owned callback (spine.cljs ~2423-2502), misses, and rebuilds. What is missing is the CLOCK - .12 priced counts and retained heap only; .13 removes retention (-22% of the read's heap), not the build.

PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE (so this cannot drift):
- rf2-2rtt6.15 measures the double build's WALL-CLOCK on the mount witnesses (M1 primary, M2 diagnostic; layer-1 AND layer-2/3 subs; not bodyRuns) and reports it as a fraction of the MOUNT RED-ZONE - the UIx-minus-Reagent mount-clock excess computed in the same runs under the segment-order discipline (M1's published magnitude is withdrawn, direction only ~1.11-1.35x).
- MATERIALITY THRESHOLD: the double build must account for >= 20% of the mount red-zone, on both layer classes, before ANY Spec 006 / substrate mechanism is entertained.
- Below 20%, or unresolvable from round-to-round spread: CLOSE this bead as (b) - take rf2-2rtt6.13 alone; no-grace-period stands unamended. A term the instrument cannot resolve does not buy spec mechanism.
- At or above 20%: REOPEN for a design pass WITH the number, scoped to a HOOK-SCOPED PROVISIONAL HAND-OFF only - explicit, bounded, held by the hook, SEPARATE from ordinary ref-counted entries; never a change to the meaning of every cache entry. Entertained is not adopted: the prototype must prove identity adoption and demonstrate (a) no unbounded growth under repeated never-resolving Suspense renders; (b) no source recomputation while provisionally unowned, or an explicitly priced bound on it; (c) deterministic reaping independent of any promise that React will commit soon; (d) correct races with a second subscriber, Strict Mode setup/cleanup/setup, query/frame changes, HMR, cache clear, frame destruction, and SSR; (e) the current abandoned-render and disposal-cascade tests preserved. Any contract change ships its Spec 006 wording and the subs.cache docstring updates in the same PR.
- rf2-2rtt6.13 lands regardless: independent, already priced, unaffected by this ruling.

WHY 20%:
- Resolvability: the M1 mount red-zone is direction-only ~1.11-1.35x with wide per-round spread (reproduction sweep 1.2887 [1.1462-1.4242], p0-converged-witness-set.md); a sub-term below ~15% of that excess is inside the instrument's noise and can support no ruling in either direction. 20% clears the floor.
- Precedent parity at a costlier remedy: .13's retention term was actioned at 22% of the per-read heap with a ~6-line, spec-silent local fix. A provisional-hand-off protocol plus spec wording is strictly costlier, so it is not entertained below the same one-fifth materiality class that justified the cheap fix.
- Posture: below one-fifth, four-fifths of the red-zone lives elsewhere - effort belongs on the larger terms; lifecycle cleverness in the reactive substrate for a minor term is the class the Hicasso fence exists to refuse.

COST/BENEFIT CARRIED FORWARD (dossier deleted; recorded here):
(a) adopt the tenancy now: deletes a measured 2x body-run COUNT at mount, but on an unmeasured CPU axis, while adding a reaping policy to a spec whose simplicity is documented as load-bearing (subs.cache ns + unsubscribe! docstrings: no deferred-grace timer, no batched dispose; the remount-churn rebuild is reasoned there as acceptable by design). Ruling ahead of the costing is the predecessors' exact failure shape. REFUSED.
(b) refuse forever now: keeps Spec 006 pristine and banks .13, but risks relitigating later without the number it should have waited for. Kept only as the DEFAULT the costing must displace.
(c) defer behind a stated costing: ADOPTED, with the threshold above. The bead itself named the missing fact ("the CPU of the double build is unmeasured. Cost it before ruling").
Codex's independent assessment, concurring: the benefit is real but narrow (one avoided construction + one avoided first body run per cold hook mount); a short reap timer is not a correctness solution because React may subscribe later; a long one makes abandoned renders, Suspense retries, Strict Mode probes, and never-shown trees retain live reactive graphs for longer; too large a contract change for an unpriced cold-mount saving.

PARKED, RESTATED SO IT IS NOT LOST (also in this bead's DESCRIPTION): re-frame.substrate.spine/release-source-wire! filterv's the fan-out coordinator's dependent vector per release, so unmounting a frame with D live derived values is O(D^2) pair comparisons. Not on the mount path, not this ruling's subject, NOT covered by the threshold above. Same discipline: number first, no mechanism without a number.
COSTING ARM LANDED (rf2-2rtt6.15, PR #7300): the double-build clock is priced. Fraction of the mount red-zone, same-run: M1 layer-1 0.94-2.14x (every round of every estimator >= 0.93), layer-2 0.61-0.75x, layer-3 0.35-0.84x; M2 diagnostic rows unresolvable at the clamp. The pre-registered rule's >= 20% branch is satisfied on representative layer-1 AND layer-2/3 mounts -> IMPLIED VERDICT: this ruling reopens for a hook-scoped provisional hand-off design pass only (mayor reconciles; the worker did not reopen it). Full evidence + per-round tables: docs/design/hicasso/studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md. Spine measured: shipped, rf2-2rtt6.13 not landed. One observation for the design pass: the single-build handoff arm's M1 mount lands at/below the Reagent denominator.
DESIGN PASS COMPLETE (2026-07-31, per the reopen branch of the pre-registered rule; design doc local-only in ai/findings/, implementation bead below stands alone). THE DESIGN IN FIVE SENTENCES: the render-phase use-memo factory keeps its +1 in a one-shot ESCROW TOKEN (reaction-guarded, spent?-CAS) instead of balancing in-render, and the commit-owned subscribe-fn's durable subscribe then HITS and adopts the identical? render-phase reaction, releasing the token 2->1 — deleting the double build the same way the measured uix-handoff arm did (rebuilt 0, bodyRuns 1N, M1 mount at/below the Reagent denominator). Every token also has a host-macrotask reaper scheduled BEFORE the factory returns (one drain per burst), so an abandoned/errored/never-committed render's provisional is released deterministically <= 1 macrotask later regardless of anything React does, and an early reap merely degrades to today's dispose+rebuild — correctness never depends on React timing (clause c), and the horizon matches Reagent's own shipped macrotask disposal. The cache NEVER holds a ref-count-0 entry and its algorithm is untouched — the only cache-side change is one internal guarded-release helper (decrement iff the slot still holds the token's reaction, then the ordinary dispose-entry-now!), which makes stale releases provably no-op under HMR/cache-clear/frame-destroy/second-subscriber/StrictMode/key-change/SSR interleavings (clauses a, b, d; the (b) bound: abandoned-path extra recomputes <= app-db movements within one macrotask, vs 2.5-17.2 us saved per cold read). All JVM cascade pins and the rf2-8u8tx.2/rf2-879fe browser assertions hold verbatim (a predecessor-release rule keeps at most one outstanding provisional per hook); the ONE contract-visible change is the rf2-es09qq Suspense-abort witness, whose zero-point moves one macrotask later (amended: <= 1 immediately, == 0 after one settle) — adopting this design is effectively blessing that sentence (clause e). It composes with rf2-2rtt6.13 (land .13 first, same lines; adoption needs no handle from the memo), does NOT resolve rf2-gncxk (no touch to make-derived-value/compute-fn; that ruling stays held), degrades to nothing on Reagent/plain-atom, and carries the Spec 006 wording + subs.cache docstrings as a same-PR obligation with the coldmount uix-handoff arm as the acceptance witness. IMPLEMENTATION BEAD: rf2-2rtt6.25 (P2, HELD for operator sign-off — do not dispatch until this ruling records adoption). ASK FOR MIKE: adopt or reject the hook-scoped provisional hand-off as designed — specifically (1) the Suspense-abort zero-point moving to the one-macrotask horizon and (2) the macrotask reap primitive; on adoption, record it here and release rf2-2rtt6.25.

RULING: ADOPT (Mike, 2026-07-31 11:31 AUSEST, recorded by acting mayor).

The hook-scoped provisional hand-off designed under this bead is ADOPTED. Implementation bead rf2-2rtt6.25 is UN-GATED by this ruling.

WHAT IS ADOPTED. The render-phase use-memo factory in re-frame.substrate.spine/use-subscribe-2 stops balancing in-render; it subscribes and mints a ONE-SHOT ESCROW TOKEN holding the +1 provisionally, with an unconditional host-MACROTASK reap scheduled at acquisition. The commit-owned uSES subscribe becomes a cache HIT that adopts the render-phase reaction (identical?), then releases the token 2 -> 1. Unadopted tokens reap <= 1 macrotask later, degrading to today's dispose-and-rebuild, so correctness never depends on React timing. Release is one-shot (CAS) and reaction-guarded via one new internal helper in re-frame.subs.cache (unsubscribe-if-reaction!).

SCOPE LIMIT, unchanged from the reopening: hook-scoped provisional hand-off ONLY. NEVER a general ref-count-0 cache tenancy. The cache never holds a ref-count-0 entry; Spec 006's 1 -> 0 in-tick dispose is untouched; Reagent / plain-atom substrates are byte-identical.

WHAT THIS RULING BLESSES. Exactly one contract-visible change: the rf2-es09qq Suspense-abort witness's zero-point moves one macrotask later (<= 1 immediately, == 0 after one settle). Spec 006 wording + the subs.cache docstring update ride the implementation PR as a same-PR obligation.

EVIDENCE. The pre-registered decision rule on this bead fired its second branch: rf2-2rtt6.15 (PR #7300, docs/design/hicasso/studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md) measured the double-build clock at >= 20% of the mount red-zone excess in EVERY round at layers 1, 2 and 3, and the handoff transcription's M1 mount landed at/below the Reagent denominator.

SEQUENCING. rf2-2rtt6.13 lands first (same lines; they compose), then rf2-2rtt6.25. The reap primitive MUST be a macrotask — a microtask fires before React's passive-effect flush and erases the entire win. The coldmount instrument's uix-handoff arm is the acceptance witness (shipped hook must show commits N / rebuilt 0 / bodyRuns 1N at layers 1-3).

NOT DECIDED HERE: rf2-gncxk's flush-path guard question remains open and is deliberately untouched by this ruling.
IMPLEMENTATION FEEDBACK — TWO ADOPTED CLAUSES CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT (rf2-2rtt6.25, PR #7305; recorded by acting mayor 2026-07-31). The ruling stands and the design works; two of its stated clauses were estimates that implementation falsified. OPERATOR MAY WISH TO CONFIRM the amended wording.

(1) SUSPENSE-ABORT PRE-HORIZON COUNT IS 2, NOT '<= 1'. The blessed contract change was recorded as '<= 1 immediately, == 0 after one settle'. React REPLAYS a suspended render and each attempt is a fresh fiber with fresh hook state, so each attempt holds its own reference. The measured pre-horizon count is 2. This is consistent with the design's own clause (a) — bounded by attempts-per-macrotask, zero at the horizon — but not with the '<= 1' figure. THE BLESSED HALF HOLDS AND IS ASSERTED WITH EQUALITY: == 0 after one settle. Spec 006 now states the corrected form.

(2) THE STRICTMODE '2 -> 1 -> 2, dispose-count 0' CLAUSE IS NOT ACHIEVABLE and was not implemented. Release-at-adoption is required — without it every 'ref-count == 1 after mount' assertion in the existing suite breaks. What IS achieved and is now pinned exactly: a StrictMode mount builds 2 reactions rather than the pre-fix 3-4.

DESIGN REFINEMENT the ruling did not state but the verbatim-assertion requirement forced: the escrow is taken ONLY when committed-ref does not already hold this key's reaction. Once a durable +1 backs the slot, the render keeps its balanced round trip — this is what keeps rf2-8u8tx.2's 'ref-count pinned at exactly 1 across 6 forced memo re-runs' true verbatim.

MACROTASK REQUIREMENT SATISFIED AND EVIDENCED: js/setTimeout 0, one timer per burst, armed on the empty->non-empty edge BEFORE the deref that can throw. Proof asserted in both the amended Suspense witness and the SSR witness — synchronously after act() the reference is still held; one timer turn later it is zero. A microtask reaper would read 0 at the first leg because act drains microtasks.
close_reason: RULED ADOPT by Mike 2026-07-31: the hook-scoped provisional hand-off is adopted (escrow token + macrotask reap + commit-time identical? adoption), scope limited to hook-scoped hand-off and never a general ref-count-0 tenancy. Full ruling recorded in this bead's notes. Implementation un-gated as rf2-2rtt6.25, sequenced after rf2-2rtt6.13.

title: Hicasso lane: hoist lane_cache.cjs to the shared bench-helper directory, so all six drivers share one copy
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.20 and left explicitly open by rf2-2rtt6.22 (PR #7282).

rf2-2rtt6.22 made hicasso_narrow_run.cjs -- the SIXTH driver on the :hicasso-bench build id, and the only one in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/ -- clear the shared cache entry before it builds. It reaches lane_cache.cjs by path across the test trees:

  const { resetLaneBuildCache } = require(
    path.join(IMPL, "freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane_cache.cjs")
  );

That is the same idiom the file already uses for navigate.cjs, and the stated rule it serves is "one helper for the repository, never a second copy per lane". It works, and it is not a copy. But the helper now lives in one lanes directory while serving two trees, which is exactly the shape rf2-2rtt6.22 recommended fixing.

THE RECOMMENDATION, from rf2-2rtt6.22 verbatim: hoist lane_cache.cjs to the shared bench-helper directory implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/, where navigate.cjs, order_guard.cjs and sentinel.cjs already live.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #7282: the hoist moves a file and edits the require in five drivers --
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/{run,hd8_run,p0_converge_run,retention_run,z3vlz_run}.cjs
-- four of which were outside that PR fence. Doing it there would have put a mechanical rename across five measurement drivers into a PR about prose-and-provenance claims.

SCOPE: pure move plus six require-path edits. No behaviour change. lane_cache.cjs carries its own mechanism, isolation evidence and measured cost; none of it moves.

VERIFY AFTERWARDS: each of the six drivers still resolves the helper and still clears .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench before building. hd8_run.cjs and hicasso_narrow_run.cjs both print the clear line; the other four print their own equivalent.
close_reason: Hoisted implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane_cache.cjs to the shared bench-helper directory implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/ (git mv, history preserved) beside navigate.cjs / order_guard.cjs / sentinel.cjs, and updated all EIGHT requires — grep on current main, not the bead's five/six: the six in-lane drivers (run, hd8_run, p0_converge_run, retention_run, z3vlz_run, coldmount_run) now use the ../../freehand/bench/ spelling they already use for navigate.cjs; core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs and adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs keep their cross-tree path forms with the new path. No behaviour change. Verified by RUNNING THE TRAP from a cold worktree (no .shadow-cljs), foreground: run.cjs then hd8_run with the clear neutralised = compiled clean, then 'pageerror: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading d)', exit 1; run.cjs then hd8_run unmodified = cleared line, 114 compiled, all four rows, exit 0 — a paired A/B differing only in whether the moved helper ran. hicasso_narrow_run.cjs exit 0 and core p0_run.cjs --only heap exit 0 exercise the two cross-tree require forms live. title: Wave-1 gate: the composed donor arm (reagent-slim :f> + UIx use-subscribe)
description: The HD-008 stop-gate for EP-0038 (epic rf2-2rtt6) — test the central hypothesis BEFORE any API exists, from parts already in the repo. Two rungs: (i) reagent-slim's :f> function-component path + runtime hiccup + the existing UIx use-subscribe spine (prices markup + reactivity); (ii) plus ONE frame-context hook and native event-vector lowering (prices the product shell; the lowering here is a minimal disposable slice, NOT the shared front half). Run on the P0 witness shapes, browser-only, against the Reagent and UIx arms. May run alongside P0, but THE RULING (stop/continue) is a delegated advisory ruling (adversarial + creative pass) issued ONLY against the published P0 baseline table, recorded on the standard bead (rf2-2rtt6.1), operator-overturnable. STOP RULE: if this composed arm cannot clearly beat both Reagent paths and stay inside the UIx red-zones, the programme stops before an API is designed — adapters+sugar is the recorded successful outcome. Off-clock. Results with commit SHA + repro command.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7263 (landed cc563d519a; authored-to-landed range-diff exact 8/8). Scope, required CI, syntax, and the order-guard self-test are sound; an exact landed rerun with HD8_TOLERANCE=0.10 also passed all 12 arm-order verdicts. Repair the published evidence contract before re-closing: (1) hd8_run.cjs silently defaults the guard to 0.35 although its own explanatory/default contract is 0.10, and neither the effective tolerance nor an env override is recorded in method/provenance; the 10% rerun means this is reproducibility debt, not evidence that these samples fail. (2) The “every arm resolves dispatch the same way / one map lookup primed outside render” claim is false: donor/UIx call dispatch-for through the global adapter map, stock Reagent receives lexical frame dispatch, and floor is inert; correct the claim or level the arms and retake if the intended attribution requires it. (3) Durable provenance must cite landed instrument commit 172244521e (authored d46ede4fb0 may remain as an explicit mapping), not authored SHA alone. (4) “156 unverified of 936 measured writes” mixes warmups with a deduplicated conceptual denominator: the actual run executed 156/1248 unverified, or 120/960 timed post-warmup samples. (5) Coordinate the now-stale “non-reactive / mixed-bundle” slim narrative and retake with exact owner rf2-b69lw. Harness-wide fail-closed controls and cleanup belong to rf2-f5roa; no duplicate bead filed.
AUDIT-CLEARED by rf2-b69lw (PR pending): the suppressed reagent-slim write rows are RE-TAKEN and published — narrow 2.667-6.000x floor, bulk 11.000-13.667x floor, 0 unverified of 78 per row (was 78/78).
