title: bench(hicasso): lane/control-verdict passes a control the HD-008 rule would fail
description:
Found while consolidating HD-008 onto the lane (rf2-f5roa, PR #7267).

The two positive-control adjudications in the Hicasso tree do NOT agree, and the shared one is the weaker:

  lane/control-verdict           ok? = (and (<= min hi) (>= max lo))
                                 i.e. the measured RANGE need only OVERLAP the +/- slack band.
  hd8-rows/positive-control!     :within? = (and (>= lo (* p (- 1 tol))) (<= hi (* p (+ 1 tol))))
                                 i.e. EVERY round must be INSIDE the band.

HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule explicitly: 'a control whose worst round is wrong has caught something, and letting a good round vouch for a bad one is how an instrument stops being one.' rf2-f5roa deliberately did NOT adopt lane/control-verdict for that reason.

The lane is what the P0 arms use, so under lane/control-verdict a run with one bad round and one good one passes its own positive control. That is the shape of thing this programme keeps finding: a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything.

NOT REPAIRED IN #7267, deliberately: tightening lane/control-verdict changes the adjudication every published P0 row was taken under. Whoever takes this must decide whether the published rows are re-adjudicated (and say so on rf2-2rtt6.1) or whether the change applies only from the next run.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs (control-verdict); implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (positive-control!, the stricter rule).
notes:
FINDING (worker/lane-control-cluster, PR pending): tightening lane/control-verdict DOES retroactively fail a published run, so the strict rule was NOT installed. Re-adjudicating the 11 controls control-verdict has published under the overlap rule flips exactly one: docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md, M2 mount, UIx segment - predicted 1.9412, slack 0.25, band [1.4559-2.4265], published range [1.333-2.000]; worst round 8.4% BELOW the band floor, carries a green tick, holds it only because a good round vouched for a bad one. The other ten (3 in p0-reagent-on-subs-baseline.md, 7 in p0-converged-witness-set.md) pass under EITHER reading. lane.cljs commit b8fb831d1c states the defect in control-verdict's docstring so :ok? cannot be mistaken for the strict answer; no number moved. NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING on rf2-2rtt6.1: re-adjudicate that row (which also needs a re-run of the converged arm, p0_converge_app) or apply the strict rule from the next run only. Left OPEN deliberately.
FRESH CONTROL EVIDENCE from rf2-6i0i2's balanced ensemble. REPORT ONLY -- the
ruling is the operator's and nothing here decides it.

Ten independently launched six-round runs of p0_converge_app (counterbalanced
start, guard clean on all 40 row-runs, parity clean, 0 unverified of 92,160,
exit 0 on all ten) yield 80 positive controls -- 4 rows x 2 segments x 10 runs.
That is the first sample large enough to price the two adjudications.

  OVERLAP RULE (lane/control-verdict, what the P0 rows were taken under): 80 of
  80 pass.
  STRICT every-round-inside reading (hd8-rows/positive-control!): 64 of 80 pass.
  Runs with all eight of their controls strictly inside: 2 of 10.

Per row, strict passes / worst single round against the +/-25% band:
  M1 mount     20/20   worst 1.6875, inside the band [1.4992-2.4986]
  M2 mount     13/20   Reagent 6/10, UIx 7/10. Worst 1.1667 (Reagent), 19.9%
                       BELOW the floor 1.4559; worst UIx 1.3333, 8.4% below
  bulk broad   11/20   Reagent 7/10, UIx 4/10. Worst 1.3333, 11.1% below floor
  bulk narrow  20/20   worst 1.7544, inside

TWO OBSERVATIONS THAT BEAR ON THE HELD RULING.

1. The number this bead holds on reproduces exactly. Its M2 case is a control
range [1.333 - 2.000] whose worst round sits 8.4% below the 1.4559 floor; this
ensemble's worst M2 UIx round is the same 1.3333, the same 8.4%. Not a
coincidence -- 4/3 is a lattice point of a ratio built from readings of two to
five 100 us quanta. But the ensemble also reaches 1.1667 on the M2 Reagent
segment, 19.9% below the floor, which is more than twice the excursion the
ruling was weighing.

2. The strict failures are not spread evenly and their shape is diagnostic.
Every one falls on M2 or broad -- the two rows whose CONTROL leg is a handful of
quanta -- and every one is a LOW outlier. The two rows measured on 20+ quanta
legs, M1 and narrow, pass strict 40 times out of 40. So the cost of the strict
rule, priced: it would refuse the M2 row in 6 runs of 10 and the broad row in 6
of 10, on a page where every other gate is green. Whether that is the gate doing
its job on a clamp-limited witness or the gate mis-firing on quantisation is
exactly the question this bead owns.

Detail and the full per-run tables are on the studio page under "The strict
reading, over eighty controls (rf2-egdaq)":
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md
RULING — DO NOT TIGHTEN (issued by the acting mayor 2026-07-31 under authority delegated by Mike for Hicasso items; operator-overturnable).

THE QUESTION. lane/control-verdict adjudicates a positive control on OVERLAP (the measured range need only overlap the +/- slack band); hd8-rows/positive-control! requires EVERY round INSIDE the band. HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule. The bead asked: re-adjudicate the one published row the strict rule would flip, or apply strict from the next run only.

THE RULING: NEITHER. The overlap rule STANDS, the strict rule is NOT adopted, and no published row is re-adjudicated. What changes is only that the limitation is stated where it can be read.

WHY, on evidence rather than taste:
1. The strict rule's misses are a LATTICE ARTEFACT, not arm defects. The four recorded strict-rule misses miss by 0.0014 on a TWO-QUANTUM floor — that is the 100us Chrome clock clamp being reported as a control failure.
2. rf2-6i0i2's balanced ensemble (PR #7303, merged) re-adjudicated 80 controls: 80/80 pass under overlap, 64/80 under strict, and only 2 of 10 runs pass strict on all eight. The failures fall ENTIRELY on M2 and broad — the coarse-leg rows. A rule that fails 16 of 80 controls by landing on the clock quantum is measuring resolution, not correctness.
3. The specific row this bead was filed over is not the outlier it appeared to be. Its worst M2/UIx round reproduces exactly (1.3333, 8.4% below the band floor) — but in the same 80-control set the REAGENT segment reaches 1.1667, 19.9% below floor, more than TWICE the excursion under review. Tightening on the 8.4% case while the 19.9% case sits in the same data would be adjudicating the arm we happened to look at.
4. Tightening retroactively fails a published run, and this programme's standing discipline is that a superseded figure is re-taken, never rescued or re-labelled by a rule change after the fact.

WHAT IS OWED (already partly landed): lane.cljs commit b8fb831d1c states the defect in control-verdict's own docstring so :ok? cannot be mistaken for the strict answer — that stays. The coarse-leg limitation should be readable beside the affected rows: any control whose legs sit within a few clock quanta is resolution-limited, and its pass is a pass under overlap, not a claim that every round sat inside the band. That is a docs note, not a code change, and it rides the next Hicasso studio-docs pass (rf2-b0tz5 is in flight on those pages).

NOT A CLAIM that the strict rule is wrong in principle. If the clock clamp is ever escaped — batched windows lifting the coarse legs clear of the quantum, as rf2-9zysg did for the narrow row — the strict rule becomes adoptable and should be revisited then.
close_reason: RULED: do not tighten. The overlap rule stands; the strict rule is not adopted; no published row re-adjudicated. Evidence: the strict-rule misses are a lattice artefact (0.0014 on a two-quantum floor); rf2-6i0i2's 80-control re-adjudication passes 80/80 under overlap but only 64/80 under strict with all failures on the coarse-leg rows; and the Reagent segment in that same set runs 19.9% below floor against the 8.4% excursion this bead was filed over. The docstring defect-statement (b8fb831d1c) stays; the coarse-leg limitation rides the next studio-docs pass. Revisit if batched windows ever lift the coarse legs clear of the clock quantum. Ruling by acting mayor under delegated authority; operator-overturnable.

title: Hicasso lane: hicasso_narrow_run.cjs's cache-rule comment counts five drivers and calls itself the sixth; the tree has moved
description:
FOUND BY rf2-9smjn (PR #7307), which deliberately did not fix it.

implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs lines 85-94 say:

  'This driver is the SIXTH program riding :hicasso-bench ... so all six share one cache entry. The five drivers in freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ clear it before they build'

Both counts are now wrong, and neither was falsified by the hoist:

  * that directory holds SIX drivers that clear the entry — run, hd8_run, p0_converge_run, retention_run, z3vlz_run and coldmount_run (coldmount landed after the comment);
  * implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs was retargeted to :hicasso-bench by rf2-etmyc and clears the entry too.

So the programs on the id are EIGHT, and this driver is the eighth rather than the sixth. rf2-9smjn's fence was 'the require line, plus whatever that PR's own change falsifies', so it reconciled only the parenthetical about the hoist being outstanding and left these.

SCOPE: the counts in that one comment block. A count that has to be re-derived every time a driver lands is the real defect, so prefer wording that does not carry one -- 'one of N programs' stated as 'every driver on the id', with the enumeration left to the grep -- over a number that will be stale again by the next lane driver.
close_reason: The comment's two stale counts are gone, and it no longer carries a count at all. Verified by grep on the rebased tree: EIGHT programs ride :hicasso-bench and all eight require and call resetLaneBuildCache -- six in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ (run, hd8_run, p0_converge_run, retention_run, z3vlz_run, coldmount_run), plus implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs (retargeted by rf2-etmyc), plus hicasso_narrow_run.cjs itself. So 'the SIXTH program' and 'the five drivers' were both wrong. Per the bead's own scope note the fix does NOT substitute eight for six: the comment now states the invariant without a number ('every program on the id shares ONE cache entry', 'EVERY driver on the id clears the entry before it builds') and points at 'git grep -l resetLaneBuildCache' for the current roster -- the same count-free form lane_cache.cjs uses ('N different programs share one cache entry'), so the next lane driver cannot make it stale. node --check exit 0. title: Make spawn-all preflight verdict and prepared children authoritative
description: PR #6010 made `spawn-all-init-fx` the authoritative batch-admission preflight, but it only retains a boolean verdict. `schema-rejected-child?` resolves the spec, builds the initial snapshot, and runs the application schema validator; every accepted per-child `spawn-fx*` then resolves/builds/validates the same child again. A direct all-valid repro observes two validator calls. A `:rf.machine.spawn-all/started` listener can also re-register the type between those passes: preflight accepts v1 and publishes a live child-bearing join, then child spawn resolves rejecting v2 and installs no snapshot, leaving an impossible half-live join. This violates closed source Bead `rf2-7u8gen`'s authoritative-preflight and user-functions-at-most-once acceptance criteria and remains on current main.
acceptance_criteria: Each declarative `:spawn-all` child is resolved, prepared, and schema-validated exactly once for an attempt, before any live join or child side effect is published. Accepted per-child effects consume that exact framework-owned prepared result rather than re-resolving, rebuilding, or revalidating application state; it must not be forgeable as an unchecked public boolean. Prove validator/data callback cardinality, type re-registration and other callback mutation seams, all-valid behavior, and mixed rejection atomicity on CLJ and CLJS. No accepted preflight can end with a child-bearing join whose snapshot was omitted by a second verdict.
close_reason: shipped #6213 (merged)

title: Fence spawn-all-init admission and join writes to the exact frame incarnation
description: `spawn-all-init-fx` captures an exact-incarnation `continue?` before application callbacks, but after `schema-rejected-child?` and `reject-unregistered-spawn!` it writes the reject sentinel or live join through bare-id `frame/swap-runtime-db!` without rechecking ownership. A schema validator (or rejection trace listener) can synchronously destroy owner frame A and publish same-id successor B. Validation then reports `:rf/stale-incarnation`, which is deliberately not a schema rejection, and the outer handler installs A-derived live join state into B; later child fxs fence/no-op, leaving B with an impossible join. Confirmed by direct current-main repro after PR #6010. Closed `rf2-vxgfnd.153` covers the single-spawn pipeline, not `spawn-all-init`.
acceptance_criteria: Every callback/emission in `spawn-all-init-fx` is followed by an exact-owner continuation check before durable state or framework-owned tail work. Join/sentinel writes are bound to the raw owner token (including loss during the physical write), so same-id successor B remains byte-identical. Cover conforming, failing, and throwing schema validators plus unregistered-child rejection/listener replacement on CLJ and CLJS; prove no stale join/sentinel/started trace or child side effect lands on B while ordinary all-valid and rejection behavior remains unchanged.

title: Emit recursive defviews against their current-namespace Var
description:
PR #5909 correctly makes exact self-heads win during analysis, but the CLJS emitter still uses the raw authored :sym instead of the canonical :fqn. With a namespace that refers re-frame.ui/sub, compiling (defview sub [] [sub {}]) emits the render call against re-frame.ui.sub and defines the view at re-frame.ui.sub, rather than audit.self.sub. The analyzer warning confirms that the defining name replaced the referred name, while the emitted JavaScript still targets the authoring Var.

Existing coverage stops at AST or regex macroexpansion and uses a qualified authoring head, so it cannot detect bare referred-name capture in real JavaScript output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Carry and use one canonical current-view emitted symbol/FQN for both self component nodes and the defining Var; raw authored spelling is diagnostic only.
- The CLJS emitter targets the current namespace for the component call and definition.
- Handle declaration/order so the render function's self reference is valid without undeclared-name or public-authoring-Var capture.
- Add real cljs.analyzer plus cljs.compiler JavaScript-output tests for referred sub, lease, and frame: current-namespace definition/reference and zero authoring-Var definition/reference.
- Preserve local-shadow precedence, root reservation, and unrelated component-head behavior.
- Avoid a broad component-emission rewrite unless the canonical-symbol fix genuinely requires it.
notes:

title: Keep stale UI bundle failures out of same-id successor error sinks
description:
A compiled re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle is exact-incarnation authority, but its stale-operation error currently routes through successor state. After frame A is destroyed and same-id B is created with a frame-owned `:observability :errors` sink, invoking A's stale `:subscribe` (or dispatch) bundle emits `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` with A's captured bare frame id. `error_emit/dispatch-on-error!` publishes the required corpus record, then `observability/route-error!` resolves that bare id to current B and delivers A's failure into B's sink.

Deterministic current-main reproduction observed B's sink count become 1 with A's stale query and `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`. The #6516 reincarnation tests create B without observability policy, so they do not see this composition. This violates the existing exact-incarnation rule already enforced for predecessor teardown failures by rf2-vxgfnd.118: successor B must not own predecessor A's error routing.

Use a narrow internal seam to suppress only the frame-owned route for this known-dead-incarnation UI emission. Preserve exactly one corpus-wide always-on record, one dev trace in debug builds, and the typed throw. Preserve ordinary live/address-directed frame error routing. Do not add a policy snapshot, public option, general routing framework, or compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A JVM/CLJS reincarnation regression creates A, captures its UI frame bundle, destroys A, creates same-id B with an `:errors` sink, and proves invoking A's stale operation sends zero records to B's sink.
- The stale operation still emits exactly one corpus-wide `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` record, one dev trace where enabled, and then throws the typed bounded exception.
- Subscribe retains raw query identity; dispatch/dispatch-sync retain source redaction; capture remains payload-free.
- Ordinary live/address-directed errors still reach their frame-owned sinks.
- The fix is an internal, call-site-exact route suppression with no public API or general framework.
close_reason: shipped #6528

title: Elide literal inline-image :doc bytes from advanced bundles
description:
## Current defect

PR #6035 correctly removes `:doc` from assembled inline descriptors, but it does not fulfill its production-byte claim. Public `rf/image` is a plain function, so a literal inline registration metadata map is constructed before `image-assembly/strip-descriptor-documentation` runs. Spec 001 already records the relevant compiler fact: runtime stripping cannot DCE call-site string bytes; the `reg-*` macros need an outer `goog.DEBUG` gate for that reason.

An advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` reproduction on current main still contains the authored inline-image literals `Inline seed (image-only).` and `Inline inc (image-only).`. The new production test only `with-redefs` the debug gate and inspects the resulting descriptor, so it proves storage normalization but not optimized-bundle elision.

## Required correction

Make literal inline-image metadata cross a compile-time production gate at the public authoring boundary, while retaining runtime normalization for computed metadata. Keep the surface ergonomic and preserve `rf/image`'s value-oriented semantics; do not add per-kind runtime normalizers or defensive ceremony.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unique literal `:doc` sentinels for inline `:reg-event`, `:reg-sub`, `:reg-fx`, and `:reg-cofx` are absent from an advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` bundle and present in the debug control bundle.
- Production assembled descriptors still contain `:doc` at neither top level nor nested `:metadata`; dev descriptors retain it.
- Computed/non-literal metadata remains accepted and is stripped from production descriptor storage, with any unavoidable compile-time limitation stated honestly.
- Runnable slots, authored IDs, load-bearing metadata, and the ordinary `rf/image` authoring ergonomics are unchanged.
- The existing elision probe fails if any literal sentinel returns to the production bundle.

title: Make shipped React derived-value construction internally failure-atomic
description:
## Confirmed current defect

PR #6025/closed rf2-vxgfnd.198 states that every shipped adapter satisfies Spec 006 internal failure-atomicity. The React-hook spine used by re-frame.ui/UIx/Helix does not. `make-derived-value-fn` records and installs one watch per source in an unguarded loop (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:563-566`). If a later source's `add-watch` throws, earlier watches remain installed and no derived value is returned, so core has nothing it can dispose. The ordinary `-dispose` cleanup at lines 591-606 only exists after construction returns.

The adjacent `make-state-container` wording is also weaker than its heading: “throw before it returns” does not require a constructor that allocated/pinned a host resource before throwing to unwind it. The current JVM fixture throws before allocation, so its zero-residue state-constructor arm cannot detect that contract violation.

## Bounded repair

Make the existing construction paths honestly failure-atomic without changing the ten-function adapter API. In the React spine, catch installation failure, attempt removal of every successfully installed watch in reverse acquisition order, and rethrow the primary construction error after cleanup. Strengthen the state-container throw branch symmetrically: any host/registry resource acquired before an unreturned throw is released first. Keep resource-free/GC-owned returned state containers and the existing derived-value disposal seam.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CLJS fault fixture makes the second or later source `add-watch` throw after an earlier install and proves zero residual watches/registry entries.
- Partial React-spine installation unwinds successfully installed watches in reverse order, attempts all cleanup, and preserves the primary construction exception even if cleanup also throws.
- Successful construction, notification batching, idempotent disposal, and UIx/re-frame.ui paths remain unchanged.
- Spec 006 and the adapter contract explicitly require `make-state-container` to release any resource acquired before an unreturned throw; the state-constructor fixture allocates/tracks such a resource before its fault and proves cleanup.
- No eleventh adapter function, global reset, timing sleep, or new public surface is added; focused JVM/CLJS construction and adapter gates pass.

title: Make frame-destroyed attribution operation-realm aware and complete
description:
PR #5954 added exact :op to the compiled frame-bundle :rf.error/frame-destroyed records, but source-coordinate resolution ignores it. error_emit/error-source-coord handles every frame-destroyed category by trying [:sub id] before [:event id]. Event and subscription ids live in separate registries and may legitimately share a keyword, as PR #5957 itself demonstrates.

Therefore a stale bundle :dispatch or :dispatch-sync of [:x ...] is attributed to an unrelated subscription :x whenever both exist. A stale :subscribe has the inverse requirement. Off-box tooling points the programmer or AI at the wrong definition. Current comments incorrectly claim a sub id cannot collide with an event id.

The same helper also drops the attempted payload from the typed exception: thrown ex-data contains only :frame and :op even though rf2-vxgfnd.230 required the typed throw to carry attempted-payload attribution. Tests retain only err-id and cannot detect either gap.

Make source lookup operation/realm aware through a private input: dispatch and dispatch-sync resolve :event, subscribe resolves :sub, capture has no component source. Do not expose a new public record field merely to steer an internal lookup. Make the typed exception carry the safe attempted-payload evidence agreed by the stale-payload privacy correction, plus its head. Keep the shared category and exact-one fan-out.
acceptance_criteria: Same-keyword event and subscription registrations are discriminated correctly for frame-destroyed errors: dispatch/dispatch-sync records carry the event coordinate, subscribe carries the subscription coordinate, and capture fabricates neither. Tests cover both collision directions and programmatic registrations with no coordinate. The private steering input does not become a public schema slot. Typed stale-operation exceptions carry frame, op, attempted payload evidence, and event/query head without weakening the fail-closed payload policy in rf2-01ihi. Every arm still emits exactly one always-on record plus one dev trace and then throws the same category. Existing core router/subs frame-destroyed emitters remain correct.

title: S3 conformance, cross-browser G-8, production absence, and CI gates
description:
## Problem
S3 is not conforming until its cross-browser correctness, production absence, conformance profile, and consumer proofs are enforced by CI. Unit success alone cannot prove IME/caret/order/pre-paint behavior or that dev tooling vanished from production.

## Scope
Complete and wire the S3 gates after all product/consumer leaves: G-8 real-browser controlled-input matrix in Chromium and WebKit (IME composition, caret restoration, event ordering, pre-paint snapshot); the S3 arms of G-7/G-11 advanced-production absence; compiler/runtime/JVM/browser conformance rows for every S3 verb and explicit absence; HMR signature behavior; tool consumer smoke; and the stage proof combining counter, dashboard, RealWorld article editor, hot reload and live Xray. Integrate the smallest deterministic commands into CI and preserve useful failure artifacts.

## Constraints
No vacuous grep-only substitute for behavioral proof, no enormous all-purpose harness, no flaky timing budget as correctness, and no unrelated future-stage gate. CI/workflow/shadow/deps edits occur only during exclusive hot-zone ownership. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` remains the spine; touched-surface jobs add the minimum S3-specific real-browser/absence coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- G-8 runs real Chromium and WebKit counterexamples for composition, caret, ordering, and before-paint state and fails under deliberate async-door regressions.
- G-7/G-11 prove advanced builds omit tool APIs/evidence registries/diagnostic strings and unused S3 interop machinery while retaining required runtime behavior.
- The S3 conformance profile covers each frozen S3 verb, host behavior, HMR, event batching, callback law, evidence projections, and explicit non-surfaces.
- Counter, dashboard, RealWorld article editor, Story, Pair, and Xray stage smokes are green and actionable failures retain logs/artifacts.
- `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and the S3 CI matrix are green twice from clean state; an independent adversarial boundary review is then ready to run.

(b) NEW GATES G-15 (atomic-local writer matrix), G-16 (render-slot client/JVM parity + purity diagnostics), G-17 (safe-spread owned-key rejection in dev AND advanced; controlled proof retained under the policy form), G-18 (library facade isolation: advanced build importing ONE view retains no unused siblings/schemas/docs/dev-registration — fixture-first; a substrate packaging change is justified ONLY if this fails structurally; note the emitter already goog.DEBUG-gates ordinary registration, verified emit_cljs.cljc:529-537). (c) The COMPONENT-LIBRARY PROOF PACK lands in the conformance/parity corpus: controlled input, selection controller, slotted list cell, safe-attrs form control, schema-described component, inline popover, single-view advanced import. title: S3 explicit callback boundaries, error recovery, and client-only
description:
## Problem
Foreign React APIs and non-data event mechanics need explicit callback forms with phase, identity, and visibility semantics. Without one closed boundary law, stale closures and render-phase side effects become invisible correctness bugs.

## Scope
Implement the frozen callback decision table in `spec/004-Views.md`: `ui/event`, `ui/handler`, `ui/render-fn`, `ui/raw-fn`; the DOM-only bare-function shorthand; explicit callback refs; foreign-component rejection of bare functions; `error-boundary`; and the S3 `client-only` boundary with required deterministic fallback. Committed callback forms are per-site stable and read committed slots. `ui/event` receives the live host event and returns a vector to dispatch or nil. `ui/handler` performs explicit imperative callback work after commit. `ui/render-fn` runs purely during the foreign component render and cannot dispatch/read sub/acquire lease/use hooks. `ui/raw-fn` passes identity through and is the only callback-ref form. Error-boundary payload/phase and client-only SSR behavior must match checked-in Spec 004, not invent a second recovery protocol.

## Constraints
Native bare functions are legal only in known native event properties, never refs or arbitrary function-valued props. Foreign boundaries require an explicit form. No portals (wave 2), resumability, compatibility shims, or runtime guessing of foreign invocation phase. Do not edit the hot zone until transferred; do not commit bead exports.
acceptance_criteria:
- The complete form-by-boundary decision table has compiler and mounted fixtures, including legal DOM shorthand, illegal foreign bare functions, refs, nil, and identity-sensitive raw callbacks.
- Committed forms keep stable identity and observe only the winning commit; render-fn observes current render values and cannot perform forbidden framework operations.
- `ui/event` proves vector-or-nil filtering with live native event mechanics; raw host events never enter event vectors or SSR output.
- Callback refs are explicit raw-fn sites and make no committed-slot promise before layout publication.
- Error-boundary fixtures pin render/commit/effect failure phases and recovery/reset behavior; client-only fixtures pin JVM/SSR fallback and client activation.
- Diagnostics carry stable coordinates and actionable rewrites and are elided where the production contract requires.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-07-16 — component-library readiness C-13a fixture ownership (completeness-audit fix; owning doc drafts/component-library-readiness.md): this child additionally owns the internal fn-prop ruling fixtures named in 12 §2b's event/handler row — ordinary function props between INTERNAL views are legal opaque values, identity-compared, with NO implicit invocation phase; special phases require ui/handler or ui/render-fn. Fixtures: an internal fn prop is never invoked by the framework; identity change (fresh closure) repaints via memo identity-compare; ui/handler at the same seam gives per-site stable identity; didactic guidance points at ui/handler/ui/render-fn where a phase must be promised.
ALSO (2026-07-16): guide/skill decision-table rows for ui/render-fn were amended to name the internal ui/slot value audience; this child's fixture work should keep the foreign-boundary render-fn fixtures distinct from rf2-ri0k6n's internal-slot fixtures (no double-ownership).

title: Make day8/re-frame2-ui publication a blocking pre-tag S7 gate
description:
## Problem

The ratified packaging decision requires `day8/re-frame2-ui` to ship as a separate artefact on the lockstep re-frame2 release train, but the deferred publication work named by PR #5792 has no durable owner or pre-tag gate.

`implementation/ui/deps.edn` is deliberately pre-publication today: no `:clein`, `:clein/build`, version, or package descriptor. That is valid during construction. The gap is that the authoritative stage plan assigns S6 adoption/CI migration and S7 adapter deletion/tag cut, while neither the S7 epic nor the W9 release-pruning work requires adding UI package metadata, pre-deploy proof, deploy topology, or release-body wiring. The current tag workflow can therefore accept a core alpha tag and deploy core without UI once the program reaches tag cut.

Closed `rf2-pc479y` says this work will land in “the ui-publishing stage,” but no such stage/leaf exists. A comment is not ownership.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect `implementation/ui/deps.edn`; confirm the UI artefact is not publishable yet.
2. Inspect the authoritative S6/S7 plan, `rf2-vxgfnd.99`, W9 prep/`rf2-nojiwy`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
3. Observe S7 owns the tag cut and pruning UIx/Helix/slim release rows, but no live obligation adds `day8/re-frame2-ui` to package metadata, lockstep inventory, pre-deploy tests, deploy matrix, or release notes.
4. Set the repository VERSION to an alpha shape and inspect the present tag workflow: its verifier has no readiness condition requiring UI publication, so a core-only alpha is structurally allowed.
5. Search all bead statuses for UI publication/Clojars/release-matrix ownership; only the closed premature bead and general stage epics appear.

## Required Correction

Make UI publication an explicit blocking child/gate of the S7 tag-cut work, sequenced before release-DAG pruning and tag creation. The implementation slice must add the package/build/version metadata and every release surface in one coherent change, then prove the coordinate resolves at the root VERSION. It may be implemented late, but it must be owned now so the deferred work cannot disappear between stages.

Coordinate with the executable inventory validator follow-up from #5792. Do not publish an unfinished UI artefact early merely to satisfy this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The S7/tag-cut dependency graph has an explicit live owner for `day8/re-frame2-ui` publication, and tag cut is blocked on it.
- UI declares the final `:clein/build`/package/version metadata using the repository root VERSION and the ratified `day8/re-frame2-ui` coordinate.
- Lockstep inventory, JVM pre-deploy test, dependency-correct deploy leaf, release body/docs, and any package descriptor are added coherently before pruning old adapter rows.
- A release dry run/preflight proves core and UI resolve at the same alpha VERSION from the intended repository and that UI depends on the matching core version.
- Attempting a core-only alpha tag fails before deployment.
- No UIx/Helix/slim compatibility work is added; their release rows remain scheduled for S7 deletion, while stock Reagent's frozen tier follows its ratified scope.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-15, delegated ruling): Option A — rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 is ratified as the explicit blocking pre-tag S7 gate for day8/re-frame2-ui publication. Nothing is implemented now; the bead is the durable owner, and at S7 it must be sequenced BEFORE W9 WP-3 release-DAG pruning and BEFORE tag creation, failing the tag cut closed if UI is not publishable.

RATIONALE: Both recorded opinions (original recommendation + CComposer) converge on Option A, and independent verification confirms the hole: implementation/ui/deps.edn is deliberately pre-publication (no :clein/build, by design), release.yml documents the UI substrate as intentionally absent, and neither the S7 epic (rf2-vxgfnd.99) nor W9 WP-3 obligates adding the UI release surfaces — so a core-only alpha tag is structurally allowed today. Option B (trust epic memory) reproduces exactly the failure mode that killed rf2-pc479y ("lands in the ui-publishing stage" — no such stage existed). Keeping the gate owned-now/implemented-late satisfies CORRECTNESS (fail-closed release integrity) and GOOD PRACTICE (no early publication of an unfinished substrate) at zero present cost.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (for the S7 implementation slice — do not dispatch before S7 opens):
- Sequencing: when S7 leaf children are filed at the S6 boundary, wire this bead as a hard prerequisite of W9 WP-3 adapter-row pruning, tag creation, and external-alpha (rf2-deiym).
- One coherent hot-zone PR mirroring sibling per-feature artefacts (e.g. implementation/schemas/deps.edn):
  (1) implementation/ui/deps.edn: add :clein + :clein/build for day8/re-frame2-ui, :version from repo-root VERSION, dep on ../core via :local/root;
  (2) .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh: add ui to ARTEFACT_PATHS / ARTEFACTS / NON_CORE;
  (3) .github/workflows/release.yml: jvm-ui pre-deploy test (clojure -M:test from implementation/ui), deploy-leaf matrix row after deploy-core (local-root: ../core), github-release body row for day8/re-frame2-ui;
  (4) docs/release-process.md: artefact count + coordinate list.
- Jar/pom preflight (reagent-slim pattern) only if a publication transform risk exists — UI has no ns-rename, so JVM pre-deploy + lockstep likely suffice; do not gold-plate.
- Coordinate with the #5792 executable inventory validator (rf2-vxgfnd.173 / PR #5867): verify that guard is live on the tag-cut branch and fold any gap into this PR.
- Dry-run proof: a temp project must resolve day8/re-frame2-ui {:mvn/version <VERSION>} plus matching core at the same VERSION, with UI depending on the matching core version.
- Acceptance (per bead): tag cut blocked on UI publication; core-only alpha fails before deploy; no uix/helix/slim compat work; stock Reagent frozen-tier scope unchanged.
- Do NOT publish early (S5/S6) and do NOT split the surfaces across PRs (inventory guard + hot-zone release.yml discipline require one coherent change).
publication additionally gated on rf2-u53yy.1 (install-tax removal) per the 2026-07-20 UIx-review ratification — an experimental checkout may carry the cache-blocker tax; a published library may not. Dependency edge wired (rf2-vxgfnd.99.2 blocked-by rf2-u53yy.1).
DECISION (Fable, delegated by Mike, 2026-07-21 17:14:17 AUSEST) - ALPHA PUBLICATION SEQUENCING

THE RULING: Option A - HOLD THE RULED CHAIN. Options B (publish with the documented cache-blocker tax) and C (core-only alpha) are REJECTED. The alpha tag waits on ALL of the following, stated as CONDITIONS not dates: (1) rf2-u53yy.1 closes with its acceptance met (install-tax removal; dedicated solo compiler worker, day-one premise probe first - does Shadow restore arbitrary def :meta into cljs.analyzer/namespaces on a real disk-cache hit); (2) this bead's publication PR lands per the recorded 2026-07-15 implementation guidance, with dry-run resolution proof; (3) the S7-entry proof plus soak condition AS DEFINED BY the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling (delegated sibling ruling, same date) - the soak clock has NOT started (nightly expensive-tests.yml red on every scheduled run Jul 9-20, re-verified fresh 2026-07-21), so all dossier tag-date estimates are void; that ruling owns soak semantics and this ruling defers to it by reference. Sequencing within S7 unchanged: this bead before W9 WP-3 release-DAG pruning and before tag creation; a core-only alpha tag fails closed.

NAMED RE-DECIDE CHECKPOINT (adopted, evidence-form): Mike re-decides only on concrete evidence, never on predicted dates or slice counts. (a) If the u53yy.1 day-one feasibility probe FAILS, return to Mike with the failed mechanism plus the smallest honest Option-B contract - that is the reconsideration trigger. (b) If every other tag prerequisite is green (soak passed per the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling, Helix removed, W12 done, deiym G1-G4 done) and u53yy.1 is still open, Mike re-decides on that evidence. STRENGTHENER DECLINED: the count-two-green-nightlies-after-the-last-pre-tag-substrate-merge rule is NOT adopted - soak-condition definition belongs to the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling and the ratified EP-0030:145-146 wording is already clear; flagged there for consideration only.

BASIS: (1) Calendar pressure examined and found empty. The dossier's two-clock analysis showed B/C buy at most 0-2 median days even under its optimistic calendar; the Codex annotation then falsified that calendar's premise - twelve consecutive scheduled nightly failures (Actions runs 29032463675 through 29760811080, Jul 9-20; re-verified: Jul 16-20 all failure) mean zero of the two required greens exist and the one-week no-fallback clock has not started. With the soak gate genuinely unmet, holding the chain costs nothing: u53yy.1 runs while the nightly is repaired and the soak accrues. (2) Permanence: Clojars never yanks; whatever install story ships at 0.0.1.alpha is the substrate's first impression forever. Pre-publication is the free moment to shrink the install contract; post-publication every change is churn or breakage for exactly the earliest adopters the alpha courts. (3) The install tax is the ruled largest product defect (two top-level compiler-internal Shadow entries, no namespace caching ever, exact shadow-cljs 3.4.10 pin in both halves, failure mode surfacing only at app load), corroborated by two independent adversarial reviews (UIx 2026-07-20, Replicant 2026-07-21); publishing it as the front door inverts the alpha's low-friction thesis. (4) Option C additionally violates R-6 (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1164-1177 - core and UI release together) and is structurally the drift this fail-closed gate exists to prevent (the rf2-pc479y failure mode); the structural hole is confirmed real: implementation/ui/deps.edn deliberately has no :clein, release.yml documents UI as deliberately absent, and the #5867 inventory guard only catches incoherent publication - it cannot require UI to become publishable. (5) The Option-A ruling is Mike-ratified (2026-07-15; the may-not clause 2026-07-20), corroborated since, with no new contrary evidence - only calendar pressure, which per (1) is illusory.

OPINIONS WEIGHED: dossier recommendation (Option A plus checkpoint plus optional strengthener) - adopted except the strengthener. Codex Recommendation (Option A; corrected the soak-clock premise; staged path: bounded S0 probe, sliced solo re-home preserving the warm/cold/watch/module/advanced probe battery, atomic publication PR with an explicit UI-required release assertion, soak as an independent gate not schedule slack; probe-failure as the honest re-decide trigger; decline the strengthener) - adopted, including its checkpoint framing. Option B's honest case (alpha-grade promises are weak; a compiler rewrite can do more harm than a documented caveat) - acknowledged as the fallback contract IF the probe fails, not a reason to pre-empt a day-old Mike-ratified ruling.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (additive; the 2026-07-15 guidance above stays authoritative - one coherent hot-zone PR: ui deps.edn :clein and :clein/build at root VERSION, verify-version-lockstep.sh inventory, release.yml jvm-ui pre-deploy plus deploy leaf plus release-body row, docs; dry-run proof; no gold-plating): (a) the gate chain is condition-form as ruled above - never schedule from dates; (b) when folding gaps per the #5867 coordination clause, add ONE explicit release assertion that day8/re-frame2-ui is required for this alpha train - do not rely solely on the generic if-clein-then-inventory guard, whose hole (it cannot require UI to become publishable) is exactly what this gate closes; (c) u53yy.1 is dispatched as a dedicated solo worker, premise-probe first, when the compiler surface is free - its S0 spike bead is the u53yy.1 side's to file, not this bead's; (d) count nothing against the soak until the rf2-vxgfnd.99 ruling's S7-entry proof and soak condition are met - re-query Actions immediately before the tag.
IMPLEMENTED (worker, PR #6654, branch worker/ui-publication-gate-99-2). The blocking pre-tag S7 publication gate for day8/re-frame2-ui is wired per the 2026-07-15 + 2026-07-21 rulings, minimal, one coherent hot-zone PR:
- implementation/ui/deps.edn: :clein + :clein/build (day8/re-frame2-ui, :version ../../VERSION, :main re-frame.ui, dep on core via :local/root ../core), mirroring core/schemas.
- verify-version-lockstep.sh: ui in ARTEFACT_PATHS/ARTEFACTS/NON_CORE + a REQUIRED_PUBLISHABLE positive assertion (the explicit "ui is required for the alpha train" release assertion the ruling asked for — closes the conditional inventory guard's hole).
- release.yml: jvm-ui pre-deploy test, `ui` deploy leaf after deploy-core (local-root ../core), github-release body row, DAG/header refresh.

- _release-ui-required-gate.test.cjs (in test:script-policy): hermetic proof that a core-only tag FAILS the shipped gate.

Rebased onto origin/main; disjoint from u53yy.1 S4 + s1jur.

The gate is owned-now/implemented-here; the tag chain still waits on the ruled conditions (u53yy.1 install-tax removal with probe; the rf2-vxgfnd.99 soak condition; Helix removal / W12 / deiym). No UIx/Helix/slim compat work added.
IMPLEMENTATION MERGED (PR #6654 -> origin/main, rebase-merged as 42eeebbdba + 5be3c0439b + 16046bf9e8). title: Finish raw query identity on every frame-destroyed subscribe surface
description:
PR #6497 made the ordinary core subscribe and internal observation-port `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` records obey the ruled identity contract: a subscription query vector is public identity and egresses raw whenever `:op :subscribe` identifies the realm. The compiled re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle still violates that same invariant on its stale `:subscribe` arm.

Current `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/frames.cljc` funnels dispatch, dispatch-sync, subscribe, and capture through `emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!`, which replaces every non-nil payload with `:rf/redacted` before `error-emit` sees it. That remains correct for dispatched event payloads, but a subscribe query vector is identity under closed rf2-zwgqe and rf2-alk8a. The current UI regression test explicitly expects all three operation bodies to be redacted, proving this is live behavior rather than stale prose. It contradicts Spec 015's rule that query vectors ship verbatim on every query-vector-bearing slot and Spec 009's statement that `:subscribe`-realm frame-destroyed `:event` is raw; the same Spec 009 row and `FrameDestroyedTags` commentary still describe the UI arm as source-redacted.

Minimal correction: in the existing UI helper, pass the payload through unchanged only for `op = :subscribe`; keep source redaction for `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-sync` and nil for `:capture`. Split the existing UI regression expectations accordingly. Do not add a policy snapshot, new classifier, or new API.

Two small completeness pins belong in the same invariant pass. The separately modified observation-port branch is currently covered only for category/throw, so strengthen its existing destroyed-frame test to assert raw `:event`, `:op :subscribe`, and realm-exact (including anti-stealing/omit) source attribution. Correct the central `error_emit.cljc` architecture comments that still say core subs emitters omit `:op`; after #6497 only the ordinary router/dispatch path is op-absent. This is test/comment reconciliation around the same shipped rule, not a new framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stale re-frame.ui `(frame)` bundle `:subscribe` emits its query vector verbatim on the always-on `:event` slot with `:op :subscribe`; the thrown exception remains bounded to structural attribution.

title: Make spawn-all stale/late vocabulary match exact-attempt gate order
description:
## Current defect

The runtime order is precise: reject unknown child; classify missing or non-current exact-attempt coordinates as `attempt-unverified` / `attempt-superseded`; then check `:resolved?`; only in an unresolved join classify an exact-current already-closed child as `duplicate-completion`. Thus unverified/superseded `stale-completion` can occur on either side of resolution, while an exact-current duplicate-shaped carrier after resolution is `late-completion` / `join-resolved`.

Current prose conflates those gates. Spec 009's quick row says the combined exact-attempt/already-closed fence runs before resolution and fires on both sides; Conventions calls all three stale reasons PRE-resolution; Xray spec/source/tests say all three authority classes fire on both sides and still use the retired `exact-authority` / `passes authority` vocabulary after the `:rf.machine/join-attempt` ruling. The fabricated Xray `spawn-all-post-resolution-authority-suppressed` rows contain no resolution-state fact and duplicate existing projection assertions; the real producer-backed tests already carry the useful proof.

## Required correction

Reconcile the catalogue, Conventions, Xray prose/comments, and tests around the actual ordered exact-attempt fence. Use accident-gating/exact-attempt language, not authentication-like authority claims, and keep only tests that can prove the behavior they name.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec 009's quick row, Conventions, Xray Spec 013, source comments, and test prose agree: unverified/superseded are checked before resolution and can suppress on either side; duplicate-completion is exact-current and unresolved-only; exact-current post-resolution carriers are late-completion/join-resolved.
- Xray surfaces use `exact-attempt coordinate/fence` and `attempt-suppressed` vocabulary consistently with `:rf.machine/join-attempt`; stale `exact-authority` wording is removed where it implies authentication or the retired carrier model.
- Producer-backed coverage proves post-resolution superseded, unverified, and exact-current-late behavior plus unresolved duplicate behavior.
- The non-discriminating fabricated post-resolution projection block is removed or collapsed into an honest reason-to-row projection table; no duplicated claims remain.
- A narrow catalogue/Conventions guard fails if the pre/post-resolution classification drifts again; Xray and machines focused suites remain green.

title: Remove impossible machine-destroy trace branch and pin terminal projection
description:
## Problem

PR #6007 corrected Xray's managed-fx collector to consume the real `:rf.machine/destroyed` terminal and exclude `:rf.machine/destroy`, which is an fx-id command and never a trace operation. One contradictory downstream branch remains at current `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:343`: `surface-events->cancel-cause` still interprets the impossible trace operation `:rf.machine/destroy` as `:actor-destroyed`.

The branch is currently unreachable because `surface-events-for` filters against `machine-invoke-trace-operations`, so this is not a runtime status bug. A successful explicit destroy correctly remains `:status :ok`, `:phase :completed`, and `:cancel-cause nil`; actor cancellation belongs to the cancellation-cascade projection. However, the dead branch contradicts the adjacent command-vs-trace law and makes the closed source acceptance criterion harder for programmers and AI tools to understand and preserve.

The real-runtime integration fixture only proves operation-set membership. It does not exercise `machine-invoke-adapter` or `event-bundle->managed-fx-records`, so it does not pin the intended downstream behavior: a real `:rf.machine/destroyed` terminal contributes terminal timing while the handled destroy effect remains successful and non-cancelled.

## Required correction

Delete the impossible command-as-trace branch and add a focused adapter/event-bundle proof of the real terminal projection. Keep machine destruction distinct from HTTP/actor cancellation semantics.

title: Qualify parallel-always order independence and remove stale birth wording
description:
## Problem

PR #6008 correctly implemented and taught parent-owned parallel `:always` rounds, but two current teaching surfaces still overstate or contradict the law.

At current `origin/main`:

- `docs/machines/parallel-states.md:321` says reordering regions "cannot change the outcome" and declaration order never changes which transitions are chosen. Frozen selection guarantees that only within one round. Because selected actions apply in declaration order, non-commuting shared-`:data` writes can change the data frozen for a later `:always` round and therefore change a later selected transition.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_property_cljs_test.cljc` invariant 9 broadly says reordering cannot change resolved configuration or data, although the actual generator makes writes commute.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/birth_always_cljs_test.cljc:37,248-251,359-361` still says parallel birth `:always` transitions "settle independently". The assertions are valid for uncoupled guards, but that wording is the superseded region-local model that the guide truth guard itself classifies as false.

A concrete counterexample has regions A and B handle one event with ordered writes of `:x` to 1 and 2, then region C chooses a next-round guarded `:always` target from `:x`. Reversing A/B leaves each round's selection atomic but changes the later frozen value and C's target.

## Required correction

Qualify order independence to frozen selection within a round, and state plainly that non-commuting apply-phase writes may affect later rounds. Rename the stale birth fixtures/descriptions using parent-owned freeze/select/apply-round terminology. Extend the terminology protection to the executable teaching surface so the superseded "settles independently" claim cannot return.
acceptance_criteria:
- The guide no longer claims unconditional outcome independence under region reordering.
- It distinguishes order-independent selection within one frozen round from declaration-ordered action/data application and possible effects on later rounds.
- Invariant 9's prose matches its commutative-write construction.
- Birth `:always` fixture names and descriptions teach parent-owned rounds, not independent regional settling.
- A focused guard or test protects these corrected teaching claims.
- Relevant JVM and compiled CLJS machine gates pass.

title: Stop retaining the disposed render-phase reaction in the spine's use-subscribe
description:
MEASURED, PRICED, NOT LANDED by rf2-2rtt6.12 (production edit to a first-class shipped adapter, deliberately left for a reviewed change).

re-frame.substrate.spine/use-subscribe takes a balanced render-phase round trip (subs/subscribe then subs/unsubscribe) so a render that never commits retains no ref-count (rf2-es09qq). For a query with NO live cache entry that goes 0 -> 1 -> 0, and 1 -> 0 is the disposal edge: re-frame.subs.cache/unsubscribe! disposes in-tick with no grace period. The commit-phase subscribe-fn then misses the cache again and builds a SECOND reaction. The first is retained for the component's lifetime by use-memo's hook slot and by get-snap's closure - a disposed reaction with no source watches, no cache slot and no verb that can reach it.

MEASURED (docs/design/hicasso/studio/uix-spine-per-read-decomposition.md, commit 0cf86fb580, :advanced, headless Chromium): 769 B [765-793] and 23.0 objects per read, 22% of the shipped 3,501 B / 125.8 obj read. Witness counters (exact integers, twice over disjoint cells): rebuilt = 1.00N, bodyRuns = 2.00N on UIx against 0 and 1.00N on Reagent.

THE CHANGE (~6 lines): have the render-phase use-memo deref the handle and return the VALUE; have get-snap's pre-commit fallback read that value. Every subscribe/unsubscribe call, every hook and every watch stays put.

EFFECT: 3,501 -> 2,720 B/read, 125.8 -> 102.8 obj/read, UIx/Reagent 4.04x -> 3.14x. The noretain ablation arm in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation.cljs IS this change; re-measure after landing since the arm is a transcription.

BLAST RADIUS: make-react-spine is shared by re-frame.adapter.uix (shipped, first-class), re-frame.freehand.substrate and re-frame.ui.substrate. One change, three beneficiaries.

CORRECTNESS: the fallback stops being a live re-read. React calls getSnapshot again after subscribe returns, by which time subscribe-fn has published the committed reaction - so that call reads the LIVE one and a write landing between render and commit is still detected. That is measured, not inferred: bodyRuns = 2N is exactly that second call. A frozen value also satisfies React's cached-getSnapshot rule at least as well as the current live deref. The key-change guard (rf2-naz09e) is unchanged in shape.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: making the fallback live without retention via subs/subscribe-once is UNSAFE - a fresh reaction per call means a fresh memo cell, so a collection-returning sub yields a non-Object.is value every getSnapshot, React's documented infinite-loop condition.

Needs a spine unit test pinning the no-retention property and the post-subscribe live re-read.

NOTHING ELSE ON THIS BEAD IS TOUCHED. The ~6-line spine fix remains filed, priced and deliberately NOT landed.
AUDIT DISCHARGED IN CODE — PR #7313 (branch worker/concurrent-2rtt6-13). The audit's charge is met on both halves; no operator ruling is needed, because nothing here accepts a stale window.

THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED. New deterministic row
assert-use-subscribe-render-to-commit-window-first-commit (react_shared_suite.cljs,
driven by the UIx DOM suite) writes app-db from the RENDER BODY of a sibling that
renders after the subscriber in the same pass — so the write lands strictly between
that getSnapshot and the commit, by render order rather than by timing — and records
the FIRST committed, layout-visible DOM from a useLayoutEffect (a render React
discards before committing never runs one). Four rows: blocking and concurrent lanes,
each with an UNMOVED CONTROL on its own frame so every row is a genuinely cold read
and a null result cannot be confused with a probe that never fired.

MEASURED, BEFORE THE REPAIR:
  blocking   control    first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 0}   consistent
  blocking   moved      first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 1}   stale (React's own)
  concurrent control    first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 0}   consistent
  concurrent moved      first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 1}   STALE FIRST COMMIT
Both moved rows settled at {:dom "g=1" :db 1} — the passive-effect repair does
arrive, one commit AFTER the stale value was committed and paint-eligible.

CHARACTERISATION. Reachable deterministically; layout-visible, so paint-eligible, and
a same-commit layout effect or ref read observes it with no paint at all. The two
lanes are two different findings, because React pushes its pre-commit
store-consistency check ONLY on a non-blocking lane (0 !== (renderLanes & 127) ||
pushStoreConsistencyCheck) and consults it only when the render time-sliced:
  * BLOCKING (default lane, every shipped consumer's normal root.render) — React does
    NO pre-commit re-read at all. NOT a #7304 regression: identical before and after,
    React's semantics, unreachable by any getSnapshot implementation. Now PINNED so a
    React release that starts checking blocking lanes surfaces as a failure.
  * CONCURRENT (startTransition / useDeferredValue — opt-in, but per rf2-so3io
    reachable at any time because we mount through createRoot) — React DOES re-read
    and discards a torn render. #7304 made a frozen render value the only pre-commit
    answer, and a frozen value compares equal to itself, so the check became a NO-OP
    BY CONSTRUCTION. THIS HALF IS A GENUINE #7304 REGRESSION.

DOES IT REACH rf2-so3io / rf2-anmdr? In SHAPE yes, by the same route: the pre-commit
fallback is reached exactly on a FIRST MOUNT of a subscription and on a query-v/frame
CHANGE — rf2-anmdr's staged-site scenario verbatim (a panel mounting as a permission
drops, a user switches, a record is redacted). In SEVERITY no: rf2-anmdr's
staged+ablated case is stale FOREVER because no watch was ever installed; this window
always self-heals at the next passive flush. Transient-paint half of that class, not
the permanent half.

BOUNDED REPAIR, red -> green. get-snap now reads, in order of currency: (1) the
committed reaction; (2) the reaction the hook's UNSPENT ESCROW TOKEN is holding
(provisional-snapshot); (3) the frozen render value. (2) is live by construction —
that +1 is what keeps the entry tenanted for the commit to adopt (rf2-2rtt6.25) — and
retains NOTHING new: the token's hold predates this change (it is how
unsubscribe-if-reaction identity-guards its release) and ends at adoption or at the
macrotask horizon, never at the component's lifetime. The memo still returns a VALUE,
so .13's 769 B / 23.0 objects per read stays bought and no hook slot holds a handle.
Not the rejected alternative: this READS a reference something else already owns, so
it cannot build a fresh reaction with a fresh memo cell and cannot reach React's
infinite-render-loop condition; every source it returns is Object.is-stable.

GATES (foreground, exit codes echoed): test:browser BEFORE repair EXIT 1 (861 tests /
5562 assertions, 1 failure — the concurrent-moved row); test:browser AFTER repair EXIT
0 (0 failures); test:cljs EXIT 0 (11974 / 59724); adapter smokes EXIT 0 (3 specs,
Reagent + UIx + re-frame.ui); test:freehand EXIT 0 (1399 / 7752); test:ui EXIT 0 (801
/ 4057); clj-kondo CI-pinned 2026.04.15 with CI's exact --lint set EXIT 0, errors: 0;
mkdocs build --strict EXIT 0; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh EXIT 0 PASS (it soft-skips its
own mkdocs step — covered by the standalone run). rf2-es09qq's Suspense-abort witness
and rf2-2rtt6.25's adoption/horizon/SSR witnesses are untouched. spec/006 needs no
change: it already sanctions the provisional reference as an ordinary reference at
ref-count >= 1 throughout, which is exactly what makes source (2) live. The stale
concession in docs/design/hicasso/studio/uix-spine-per-read-decomposition.md is

(1) Deterministic evidence: assert-use-subscribe-render-to-commit-window-first-commit injects a write in the render→commit gap from a sibling's render body and observes the FIRST committed, layout-visible value, four rows over two lanes each with an unmoved control. It measured a real STALE FIRST COMMIT on a concurrent lane ({:dom "g=0" :db 1}) — the audit's charge confirmed, not delayed bookkeeping. (2) Bounded repair: get-snap reads the reaction the hook's unspent escrow token already holds before falling back to the frozen render value, so the pre-commit read is live while retaining nothing new and .13's 769 B/read win is untouched. RED before / GREEN after (test:browser exit 1 -> exit 0). The BLOCKING-lane row is React's own (no pre-commit store-consistency check on a blocking lane) — not a #7304 regression, unreachable from the substrate, and now pinned so a React change surfaces. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7304 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The retention repair is small and its object-tenancy proof is strong for the defect it targets. But it changes `getSnapshot`'s unmatched/pre-commit branch from a live deref to the frozen render value. The landed docs explicitly concede that on a concurrent lane a write in the render→commit gap is no longer rejected before commit; React's passive/post-subscribe check repairs it one commit later. That is a real stale commit/possible paint, not merely delayed bookkeeping, and it is the exact security-shaped class already priced in rf2-so3io/rf2-anmdr (permission drop, user switch, record redaction).

The new `assert-use-subscribe-render-phase-reaction-not-retained` test does not inject any write in that gap and does not assert the first committed/layout-visible value. It only proves that React later dereferences the committed reaction, so it cannot validate the prose claim that the render→commit window remains covered.

Keep the repair bounded: add a deterministic concurrent render→commit mutation row that observes the first commit (with an unmoved control), and preserve the pre-commit live-consistency contract without retaining the disposed handle. If the project intentionally accepts a one-commit stale window, that is an operator-level contract change and must be ruled explicitly rather than inferred from post-subscribe ordering. No new framework is warranted.

title: subs: the layer-1 memo guard is guaranteed to MISS on the flush path (147 B/sub)
description:
FOUND by rf2-jr76s while decomposing the narrow-write leg.

`make-layer-1-memoised-body` guards the user's sub body with `(= @last-db db)`. On the FLUSH path that comparison can never be true, provably:

  flush! runs only if the derived value was marked dirty
  -> which happens only if the app-db projection's notify fired
  -> which requires the app-db value to have MOVED by rf=
  -> and last-db was set to the then-current value by the previous flush
  -> rf= says moved => = says different.

So every layer-1 subscription re-evaluated by a write pays a full structural comparison of the changed app-db subtree that is known in advance to fail. Measured at 147.0 B/sub (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF), 5.2% of the pre-fix per-subscription slope and 15.6% of the post-fix one. Its TIME cost also scales with the shape of the changed subtree, not with the sub.

IT IS NOT DEAD CODE AND MUST NOT SIMPLY BE REMOVED. The spine's derived value is pull-based — `deref-derived` recomputes on every -deref — so this same guard is what stops a view render from re-running every sub body. It earns its keep on the READ path and cannot pay on the WRITE path.

The shape of a fix is therefore 'let the flush path tell the wrapper the input already moved' without weakening the deref-path guard. That crosses the compute-fn contract between re-frame.subs.memo and the substrate's make-derived-value, so it is a design question, NOT a mechanical edit — hence a bead rather than a patch.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md §2.

VERIFIED + HELD FOR RULING (PR #7233, worker 2026-07-28).

PROOF HOLDS for :db and :runtime-db — every link re-verified against current source (spine.cljs:796 mark-dirty / :833-836 wiring / :689 rf= notify gate / :570 rf= / frame/app-db-container is an rf=-gated projection).

PROOF FAILS for :frame-state, WHICH SHARES THE SAME WRAPPER. subs/single-source-input-kinds = #{:db :runtime-db :frame-state}, all three route to make-layer-1-memoised-body (subs.cljc:1262). :frame-state reads the RAW physical atom, not a projection. A raw-atom source is wired through the spine's per-source fan-out coordinator (spine.cljs:833-835), which is NOT movement-gated. commit-frame-transition! short-circuits only when BOTH partitions are identical? (frame.cljc:1401-1402). So an =-but-not-identical? commit installs a fresh frame-state, marks every :frame-state sub dirty, reaches the wrapper ON THE FLUSH PATH with a value-equal input — and the guard HITS. Confirmed empirically by test.

FLUSH IS NOT THE ONLY CALLER: deref-derived (spine.cljs:766) recomputes on EVERY -deref (the read path); flush! (:792) is the other. Ratom adapters wrap the same compute-fn in make-reaction (:2892); plain-atom has NO flush path at all (plain_atom.cljc:82) — there the guard is the only memoisation. compute-sub bypasses the wrapper entirely.

BOTH FIX SHAPES CROSS THE SPEC — needs Mike's ruling:
 (1) narrow to identical? — contradicts Spec 006 §Invalidation algorithm ('only when an input changes value by rf=') and Spec 009 §:rf.sub/skip ('input value was = to last-seen'); also reds existing pin sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj:84.
 (2) signal the flush path (the bead's own sketch) — changes the compute-fn signature Spec 006 §make-derived-value pins verbatim, AND must be gated on whether the source is movement-gated (the :frame-state finding), AND must degrade on Reagent/plain-atom/UIx.

MEASUREMENT re-run on the current post-#7229/#7230 harness: P-EQDB = 147.0 B/sub EXACTLY as recorded. node V8 24.13.0, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF. Forward [44050.6-44661.4] B/call vs reversed [44050.6-44701.6] — overlapping, indistinguishable. Arm-order guard did NOT refuse (8/8 self-tests, 70/70 strata ok).
CORRECTION to the bead: share is now 17.6% of the slope, not 15.6%. Absolute unchanged; the slope fell (~942 -> 835 B/sub) as later work landed.

PR #7233 lands NO src change — two pin tests only (sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs). Mutation-proof: weakening the guard to identical? makes flush-skips 0 and RE-RUNS the :frame-state body (5 failures).
DESIGN PASS DONE — RECOMMENDATION, ADOPT/REJECT ASKED (2026-07-31, design only: no code, no PR).

THE DESIGN IN FIVE SENTENCES. A derived container that gates its own propagation on rf= publishes,
through a new optional re-frame-owned protocol re-frame.movement/IMovementWitness, the value its
most recent COMPLETED movement departed FROM (spine: one volatile set inside notify's existing rf=
gate, cleared on mark-dirty!'s 0->1 transition so the container stops answering once its live value
may run ahead); the two fixed-arity-1 memo wrappers hold their lone source container and skip the
`=` walk exactly when that witness is identical? to the value they last saw — a proof, since the
witness contract guarantees the container's live value is not rf= (hence not =) to it. The source
OWNS the signal and core PULLS, so make-derived-value's pinned (sources compute-fn) signature and
compute-fn's pinned one-arg-per-source shape are BOTH untouched. This design does not key on "flush
vs deref" at all — which matters, because the bead's proof turns out NOT to license skipping the
compare on the flush path even for :db: two reachable interleavings make the guard correctly HIT
there (a DEREF between mark-dirty and the drain sets last-db to the new value; and a single-epoch
A -> B -> A' return-to-equal arrives at one coalesced flush with an =-but-fresh map), and the
identical?-anchored witness handles both by falling back to today's `=`. :frame-state keeps its
genuine hit STRUCTURALLY — its source is the raw physical Atom, which cannot implement the
protocol, so witness-src is nil and the guard expression is byte-for-byte today's; the exact fact
that broke the bead's proof is now the mechanism that protects it. The set of {hit, miss} verdicts
is bit-identical on every path on every adapter — a body-run or :rf.sub/run / :rf.sub/skip count
diff anywhere is the failure signal, and PR #7233's two pins plus sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj:84 must
pass UNMODIFIED.

SCOPE: new re_frame/movement.cljc (~35 lines), ~8 lines in spine.cljs's make-derived-value-fn, ~12
in subs/memo.cljc, 2 in subs.cljc, paired bench arms, and one Spec 006 subsection (HOT-ZONE).
Nothing in any adapter. Reagent / reagent-slim / plain-atom / test-react / JVM: no witness, no
behavioural change, two extra pointer compares per recompute, zero allocation. Composes with the
landed rf2-2rtt6.13 and .25 (disjoint regions, no sequencing dependency; .25's commit adoption
makes the proof's precondition hold MORE often, not less).

MEASUREMENT OBLIGATION (both halves, or neither): a new PAIRED arm pair in write_attribution.cljs,
one process, same objects — P-MEMOW (wrapper over a WITNESSING source, flush-path shape) must land
at P-MEMO minus 147.0 B/sub, and P-MEMOF (same wrapper over a RAW ATOM source, the :frame-state
shape, =-but-not-identical? db) must still carry the FULL `=` term; plus the RFWRITE-N slope
~835 -> ~688 B/sub on the :db ladder and unchanged on a :frame-state ladder; plus mutation proofs
in both directions.

IMPLEMENTATION BEAD: rf2-gncxk.1 (P2, child of this bead), design content INLINE, marked HELD for
operator sign-off — not dispatched.

THE ASK: ADOPT or REJECT the movement-witness protocol as a new OPTIONAL substrate capability
(sixth thing an adapter MAY publish; a protocol on the container rather than a late-bind hook
because it is read on the hottest path in the artefact). Three sub-questions if you adopt:
(1) `re-frame.movement` as the ns name — sits with re-frame.disposable / recordable / projection;
(2) the one memory cost — one predecessor derived value retained per derived container between
writes (structural sharing means the true delta is the nodes the last write replaced; layer-1 memo
cells already retain a full app-db each in last-db) — acceptable?
(3) Spec 006 is hot-zone, so sequence rf2-gncxk.1 against other Spec 006 PRs when dispatching.

NOT adopted-by-default and NOT part of gncxk.1 — two adjacent candidates worth their own beads if
you want them: (i) memoise deref-derived while the container is clean (removes the read-path
recompute entirely — a much bigger win — but converts the derived container from pull to
cached-pull, which Spec 006 leaves to adapter discretion and the spine deliberately declines);
(ii) movement-gate the raw-atom fan-out coordinator (collapses N :frame-state `=` walks into 1,
but changes WHEN :frame-state subs are marked dirty and would red the #7233 pin as written).

Design doc (local-only, gitignored, NOT committed):
ai/findings/2026-07-31.rf2-gncxk-flush-path-guard-design.md

OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE.)

WHY ADOPT:
