title: hicasso: settle HD-002 6.1 -- does ONE generation fence cover the THREE fields the commit-side re-read compared?
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). Assessed as the single
largest correctness risk in the programme, and it has had no bead.

THE SUBSTITUTION EVERYTHING RESTS ON. HD-002's allowed edge-diff operation is
affordable only because the commit does NOT deref. The predecessor's
`cell/commit!` called `obs/read` on every handle -- "a SECOND deref of every
subscription, after render already read it" -- as the invariant-5 tear check,
comparing THREE things (node-key, version, and frame/registry epoch) between the
render that produced the element and the commit about to publish it. It cost
1.19 ms of a 4.0 ms write for 300 reads
(docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md:228-251, and
:239-243 for the three fields).

Hicasso replaces all of it with a GENERATION FENCE -- one O(1) comparison per
boundary (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:57-60;
docs/design/hicasso/hd-002-adjudication.md:146-163).

THE HOLE, marked [OPEN] by the repo's own adjudication
(hd-002-adjudication.md:459-476):

  "the record does not demonstrate that one epoch comparison covers all three
   failure modes. This page cannot verify it on paper, and if it is wrong the
   allowed operation in section 2 is under-specified rather than merely fast."

WHY IT IS THE TOP RISK. The tripwire's checklist item 4 is "Am I re-reading
subscription values at commit? ... Fired" (hd-002-adjudication.md:74). If the
fence proves insufficient, the tear check must come back -- and item 4 then
fires on CORRECTNESS grounds. Under Mike's Surface B ruling a collector loss is
NULL, not a fallback to grouped. So this substitution can end the product, and
it can do so however good the clock numbers are.

And EP-0036's withdrawal note is explicit that the guarantee is worth MORE than
spec/006 claims for it: the ablation found that "without the tear check a staged
site publishes stale and nothing ever corrects it", so the tear check was
retained and vindicated, not implicated
(docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md:25-34).

WHAT SETTLES IT -- already specified, hd-002-adjudication.md:470-476. Two
witnesses, both stated as obligations BEFORE the fast path is trusted:
  (i) the staged-stale CI witness the record already names;
  (ii) an ADVERSARIAL witness that changes a subscription's VALUE between a
       boundary's render and its commit WITHIN ONE GENERATION, and asserts the
       committed DOM is not stale.

If (ii) cannot be constructed, record why -- the adjudication says that is
itself the answer, and it would be a strong one.

DO THIS BEFORE THE FAST PATH IS TRUSTED, not after. It is a witness, not a
runtime; it does not need the product to exist.
notes:
SETTLED — THE ANSWER IS NO. PR #7323 (branch worker/genfence-2rtt6-33). Witness: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs. Doc: hd-002-adjudication.md §6.1 is now [SETTLED — NO] with the verdict recorded on the page that marked it [OPEN].

THE GROUND TRUTH (three fields, each independently load-bearing). cell.cljc:811-824 moved? / ui reactive.cljc:3048-3071 evidence-moved?: cold branch = rf= on :value; live branch = four clauses over three axes — :version (ordinary value move), :node-key (a same-id frame REINCARNATION whose version and epochs can tie exactly; cell.cljc:99-110 pins observation-port ABI v2 for it and asserts it AT LOAD), :frame-epoch/:registry-epoch (a frame or registry move that did not change the value). Spec 006 invariant 5 is the normative statement. Axis-isolation is already pinned by shell_cljs_test.cljc:841 invariant-5-every-axis-is-still-compared-on-a-retained-handle, and I mutation-proved it: deleting the :node-key and :registry-epoch clauses reds exactly those two sub-rows ({:delta 0} vs {:delta 1}), leaving :version, :frame-epoch and the unmoved control green.

WHAT THE FENCE COMPARES IN THE BUILT RUNTIME (read off origin/worker/arm1-2rtt6-9 arm1/runtime.cljs, not the design record): render-body captures !generation, runs the body ONCE, compares, and on a match RETURNS. !generation has exactly one writer — flush! — reached only from mark-dirty!, whose only caller is the per-cell value-change watch that acquire-cell! installs AT COMMIT. The commit itself compares nothing ('no commit-phase deref' is the stated fence).

VERDICT: DOES NOT COVER, and the three axes share one answer because the two mechanisms do not guard the same WINDOW. Predecessor = render probe .. COMMIT re-read (the render->commit gap). Fence = capture gen .. one body run .. compare (closes when the body returns). The fence covers a hazard the three fields never addressed — a commit landing BETWEEN TWO READS OF ONE BODY — and does not reach the gap. One-for-one on a different axis, not one-for-three.

Residual coverage of the gap comes from the epoch-sum getSnapshot + React's own commit-time snapshot re-check — real, and row 1 proves it works — but keyed on the same counter: version axis covered for a RETAINED key only; node-key and frame/registry-epoch axes have no counterpart at all.

THE CONCRETE TEARING INTERLEAVING (row 2, reproduced green over the real sub layer / real frames / real watches on the React-spine host): a boundary reads key K that nothing holds; K has no cell, no watch, no epoch, getSnapshot = 0. A write moves K before React commits. Nothing is marked -> the generation does NOT move, so the change is genuinely WITHIN ONE GENERATION (exactly the adversarial witness §6.1 demanded). The commit acquires: baseline deref takes the NEW value, watch armed one move too late. getSnapshot answers the SAME number, so React's re-check finds no tear and schedules nothing. The boundary paints the OLD value and NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT. Verbatim Spec 006 invariant 5's stronger half.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN RECORD worth noting: arm1's own generation_fence_dom_cljs_test 'Case 2' is labelled as §6.1's case but dispatches AFTER the mount has settled — ordinary invalidation on an already-committed key, i.e. row 1's case, not the staged one. Its comment concedes 'the fence cannot see this one'. Also, acquire-cell!'s own comment records that HD-002's 'acquire without deref' is not implementable against this substrate; the baseline deref it added is the thing that swallows the staged move.

FILED, NOT IMPLEMENTED (Arm 1 owns the collector surface): rf2-2rtt6.42 (P0) the defect, with three candidate repairs costed against the tripwire — smallest is one comparison per NEWLY ACQUIRED key per commit, O(new edges), zero on a steady-state re-render, so it does NOT by itself fire tripwire item 4; what the finding removes is the record's stated reason for believing item 4 can stay unfired on correctness grounds. rf2-2rtt6.43 (P2) re-point the witness at the arm's runtime once it is on main (the generation machinery is transcribed today because the runtime is on a spike branch).

GATES: test:cljs exit 0 (12145 tests / 60617 assertions / 0 failures); test:freehand exit 0 (1399/7752/0); clj-kondo on the new file errors 0 warnings 0 (full surface: 10 errors, ALL pre-existing in untouched ui/epoch test trees, local binary v2025.10.23 vs CI-pinned 2026.04.15 which is unobtainable here); splint on the new file 0 warnings. mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/hicasso (mkdocs.yml:36 excludes it) — tables and the unchanged §6.1 anchor checked by hand. MUTATION PROOF both directions: A (delete two moved? clauses) exit 1 / 2 failures then exit 0 after revert; B (reinstate the commit-side tear check in the transcribed acquire-cell!) exit 1 / 2 failures in the staged row only, then exit 0 after revert; git diff empty both times.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso: the generation fence does not reach the render->commit gap -- a STAGED read tears and never heals
description:
FINDING from rf2-2rtt6.33, which settled HD-002 6.1's [OPEN] question. WITNESS: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs (three rows, green, mutation-proved).

THE ANSWER TO 6.1 IS NO, and not by an arithmetic margin. The predecessor's commit-side re-read and the generation fence do not guard the SAME WINDOW, so 'which of the three fields does the one fence cover' has one answer for all three.

  predecessor   render probes a site .. COMMIT re-reads that site   (the render->commit gap)
  fence         capture gen .. BODY RUNS .. compare gen .. RETURN   (one body run)

arm1/runtime.cljs render-body captures the generation, runs the body, compares, and returns. The commit that follows -- React calling the read-set entry's subscribe, where acquire-cell! installs the edge and the watch -- compares NOTHING, by design ('no commit-phase deref'). The fence therefore covers a hazard the three fields never addressed (a commit landing BETWEEN TWO READS OF ONE BODY) and does not reach the window they were about. One-for-one on a different axis, not one-for-three.

WHAT DOES REACH THE GAP: the epoch-sum getSnapshot handed to useSyncExternalStore, plus React's own commit-time snapshot re-check. Real, and row 1 proves it works -- but driven by the SAME counter: an epoch moves only when flush! bumps it, flush! runs only from mark-dirty!, and mark-dirty! has exactly one caller, the value-change watch acquire-cell! installs AT COMMIT.

  version axis        covered for a RETAINED key (the watch pre-dates the move).
                      NOT covered for a STAGED key.
  frame/registry      no counterpart at all -- an epoch move is not a value change
  epoch axis          on an acquired reaction, so it cannot reach mark-dirty!.
  node-key axis       no counterpart at all, same argument: nothing in the runtime
                      observes node identity.

THE TEAR (row 2, reproduced): a boundary reads key K, which nothing holds yet. K has no cell, no watch, no epoch; getSnapshot answers 0. A write moves K before React commits. Nothing is marked, the generation does not move (so the change IS within one generation -- exactly the adversarial witness 6.1 asked for), no epoch bumps. The commit then acquires: the baseline deref takes the NEW value and the watch is armed one move too late to have reported it. getSnapshot answers the SAME number, so React's re-check finds no tear and schedules no re-render. The boundary paints the OLD value and NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT -- the watch's baseline is already the new value, so no later notification is coming for a change that already happened.

This is verbatim Spec 006 invariant 5's stronger half: 'a STAGED site publishes stale and nothing ever corrects it, because a dependency's first render has no earlier channel to heal through' -- 'a panel mounting exactly as a permission drops, a user switches, or a record is redacted'. It is a P0 bug class by validation.md's own words.

REACHABILITY IS NOT EXOTIC. Every boundary's FIRST read of a key nothing else holds is staged, so every mount of a new row/panel/route is a candidate; and Arm 1's own runtime already contemplates a flush raised while a body is running (flush! defers notifications when rendering? is true), which is a sibling boundary writing during the same React render pass -- with the reading boundary's fence already closed. The window is at least as wide as React's passive-effect flush, since subscribe runs in an effect.

WHAT THIS BEAR ON: hd-002-adjudication.md's tripwire checklist item 4 is 'Am I re-reading subscription values at commit? Fired'. This finding does not fire it by itself -- the tear is fixable by channels that are not a per-read commit deref -- but it removes the record's stated reason for believing item 4 can stay unfired on correctness grounds. Under the operator's Surface B ruling a collector loss is NULL, not a fallback, so this is the programme's decision, not the arm's.

NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE, DELIBERATELY. rf2-2rtt6.33 was an analysis-and-witness bead and Arm 1 owns the collector surface. Candidate repairs, none costed, all needing the tripwire read against them:
  (a) make a staged key's FIRST commit compare the acquire-time baseline against the value the render read, and correct when they differ. One comparison per NEWLY ACQUIRED key per commit -- not per read per commit -- so it is O(new edges), zero on a steady-state re-render. This is the smallest repair and the closest to the predecessor's semantics.
  (b) fold identity/epoch into the epoch-sum so the node-key and frame/registry-epoch axes have a counterpart at all.
  (c) argue the staged case away with a reachability bound. The record would have to make that argument; it currently does not make any.

DO NOT close this by widening the fence's retry loop -- the fence's window closes when the body returns, and the tear happens after that.
notes:
CLOSED BY PR #7324 (branch worker/tear-2rtt6-42, head f4e6440e27). The tear is closed with a witness, mutation-proved both ways in node AND in real Chromium.

THE FIX — candidate (b)'s shape, not (a)'s, and smaller than either. A key with NO CELL now contributes its frame's `commit-basis` to the epoch-sum getSnapshot instead of nothing, and a cell records the basis it was CREATED at:

    commit-basis(frame) = @!generation + re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch(frame)

The second term is the SUBSTRATE'S OWN observation-port evidence counter — one bump per physical frame-state install at both write chokepoints — and Spec 006 already uses it, verbatim, to detect 'the frame's durable state moved in the render->commit gap ... without watching anything'. The arm was missing the one field the substrate had already built. Being a counter read rather than a watch, it has none of the generation's dependency on a cell existing, which was the whole of the defect.

A staged key therefore reads basis@render while the boundary renders and basis@commit once the commit acquires it: equal when nothing installed in the gap, different when something did. React stores each fiber's render-time snapshot and re-reads getSnapshot immediately after subscribe returns (mountSyncExternalStore pushes subscribeToStore as a passive effect and updateStoreInstance as the NEXT one; updateStoreInstance is checkIfSnapshotChanged + forceStoreRerender — React 19.2, read in react-dom-client). So the comparison is per boundary, is one number, and holds NO RECORD OF WHAT ANY READ RETURNED.

WHY NOT candidate (a). 'Compare the acquire-time baseline against the value the render read' needs somewhere to keep what the render read, and the only ledger-free place to keep it is a second render-populated buffer the commit reconciles — which is the tripwire. Comparing BASES needs no such record because React is already holding the per-boundary render-time value. The tripwire did NOT fire: no second scratch, nothing keyed by render/attempt/lane/generation, no per-read object, no commit-phase deref. hd-002-adjudication.md item 4 stays unfired, now for a mechanical reason rather than an argued one.

THE BASELINE DEREF IS NOT THE FIX, confirmed. It is already in acquire-cell! and is the right repair for the spurious-first-re-render problem; it gives a correct baseline and NO COMPARISON, so it silently adopts the moved value. Asserted as a row (the-baseline-deref-alone-cannot-see-the-move) rather than argued.

SIBLING HOLE ALSO CLOSED: the fence compared the generation, which cannot see a MID-BODY move of a staged key either (no cell -> no watch -> no mark-dirty! -> no bump), so a body that read a staged key, dispatched, and read again could straddle two commits with the generation still. It compares the basis now.

COST: hooks unchanged at 2; subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else; zero allocation; ZERO in steady state (a mounted boundary holds a reference to every key it reads, so its snapshot has no staged term at all). Conservative only in the safe direction — a boundary mounting exactly as an unrelated write lands re-renders once. Executable change: SIX LINES.

WITNESS: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/staged_read_tear_cljs_test.cljs (new, 6 rows, against the arm's OWN runtime rather than a transcription) + Case 3 in arm1/generation_fence_dom_cljs_test.cljs (real Chromium; staged as a SIBLING boundary writing during the same React render pass, so it needs no guess about passive-effect scheduling). Also noted in that file: its Case 2 is LABELLED as 6.1's case and is not it — it dispatches after the mount settles, so the key is RETAINED.

MUTATION PROOF (fix reverted, witness left in place):
  npm run test:cljs     exit 1 — 12,196 tests / 60,717 assertions, 3 failures, ALL in the new ns and nowhere else. 'expected: (not= at-render (rt/snapshot-of entry)) / actual: (not (not= 0 0))' — the bead's sentence, executed.
  npm run test:browser  exit 1 — 938 / 5,800, 1 failure: actual (not (= "true" "false")) — the real DOM, painting stale forever.
GATES (foreground, exit codes echoed):
  npm run test:cljs     exit 0 — 12,196 / 60,717 / 0 failures
  npm run test:browser  exit 0 — 938 / 5,800 / 0 failures
  scripts/test-fast-pr.sh  PASS, exit 0
  clj-kondo CI-pinned 2026.04.15, full CI --lint set, --fail-level error: exit 0, errors: 0; arm1/ re-lint errors 0 warnings 0.
No page under docs/design/hicasso/** touched, so the mkdocs-does-not-cover caveat applies to nothing here.

SCOPED OUT, FILED AS rf2-2rtt6.44: the registry-epoch axis (a :sub re-registration is not a frame-state install; and observation/registry-epoch* is ^:private with no public reader, so the arm cannot read it without a substrate change — closing it for a RETAINED key means re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration, a design decision rather than a defect fix) and the node-key axis (frame/dissoc-frame! clears the commit-epoch entry, so a same-id reincarnation RESTARTS at 0 — commit-basis is monotone only within one incarnation, which is exactly why the observation port carries :node-key as a third field). Both named in the runtime's docstrings with the bead id.

rf2-2rtt6.43 ANNOTATED: generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs (PR #7323) TRANSCRIBES the three functions this PR changed, so once #7323 lands its row 2 asserts a defect the arm no longer has.

title: hicasso: win condition (1) is internally inconsistent -- mount<=1.0x Reagent and codec<=1.10x UIx cannot both hold (OPERATOR)
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). ONLY THE OPERATOR
AMENDS THE BAR -- this bead surfaces an arithmetic contradiction, it does not
propose to resolve it under delegated authority.

THE CONTRADICTION. docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:240-241 states the
given-continuation win condition as:

  "(1) mount <= 1.0x Reagent-on-subs, same run and same instrument, with the
   codec inside 1.10x of direct UIx `$` on M1"

Post-rf2-2rtt6.25, UIx-on-subs and Reagent-on-subs are at PARITY on that exact
row: 1.0243x [0.9937 - 1.0549] (validation.md:268;
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md:522). A codec at exactly
1.10x direct UIx therefore lands at 1.0243 x 1.10 = 1.127x Reagent.

The two clauses cannot both be satisfied. Satisfying the codec clause fails the
ship clause by ~13%. Satisfying the ship clause requires a runtime hiccup
interpreter to run for <= 0.98x the cost of UIx's compile-time `$` -- i.e.
interpretation must be free or negative.

THE MEASURED COST OF INTERPRETATION, two independent instruments:
  - donor-r2 / uix (equal hooks, codec the only variable): 1.162-1.286 on
    mount-M, 1.125-1.222 on mount-U
    (docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:231,253)
  - free-i / free-ik (interpreted leaf vs compiled leaf, ViewCell held): 1.216
    [1.092-1.425]
    (docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md:275)

AND THE ONE MECHANISM THAT COULD CLOSE IT IS RULED OUT OF THE SURVIVING ARM.
HD-004 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:98-110) permits only codec-work caching
in the lean arm and assigns template extraction with data-encoded hole plans to
the PATCH arm. PATCH has been dropped by operator ruling. So the accelerant
class that could make interpretation approximately free is no longer in the
programme.

WHAT IS BEING ASKED. A ruling on the mount row. Candidates, stated without
preference:
  (a) mount <= ~1.15x Reagent, with bulk-broad and bulk-narrow as the hard rows
      (bulk is where the parent already wins: UIx 0.6291x Reagent,
      p0-converged-witness-set.md:347);
  (b) mount graded DIAGNOSTIC and the "codec <= 1.10x direct UIx `$`" clause
      promoted to the gate in its place;
  (c) leave the bar exactly as written and accept that K1/K7 is the likely
      terminal state -- a legitimate and pre-registered outcome
      (validation.md:356,362), and adapters-only is recorded as SUCCESS.

Whatever is ruled, the two clauses of win condition (1) must stop contradicting
each other before a worker is scored against them.

title: hicasso: a deferred read forced inside ANOTHER boundary's render is permanent silent staleness, not just 'the wrong reader'
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

THE DEFECT. `read-key!`'s guard is `(nil? (.-frame rstate))` — "is ANY body running", not "is
THIS boundary's body running" (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs:569-580;
`rstate` is one module-level object at :277-283). So a deferred read forced while a DIFFERENT
boundary is rendering does not throw: it is silently pushed onto that boundary's scratch.

The case IS named in docs/design/hicasso/studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:237-241, and
dismissed there as "not a missing edge — the reader does re-render — but it is the wrong reader".
THAT DISMISSAL IS WRONG. A LazySeq caches its realised values, so the wrong reader re-renders
exactly ONCE; on that re-render its body walks the already-realised seq, `sub` is not called
again, the row keys leave its read set, `subscribe` identity changes and React unsubscribes those
edges. The correct reader never re-rendered, so the seq is never rebuilt. Net: one correction,
then PERMANENT SILENT STALENESS with no edge left to notify — precisely the "correct on screen,
frozen thereafter, attributable to nothing" class the same page (:229-230) calls the worst
failure the ruled surface can have.

AND THE STRUCTURAL SAFETY ARGUMENT HAS A HOLE. judgement:206-212 and runtime.cljs:119-124 justify
laziness-safety with "a seq at a prop position goes through `clj->js`". True for a NATIVE tag
(front/codec.cljs:232-242, `convert-prop-value` sends any `coll?` through `clj->js`). FALSE for a
BOUNDARY: `boundary-element` (front/codec.cljs:341-349) builds `body-props` as a plain CLJS map
and hands it through untouched as `#js {"rfProps" body-props}`; `shell` reads it back as a CLJS
map (runtime.cljs:883). No conversion, no realisation. And `realize-children`
(front/codec.cljs:288-298) flattens EXACTLY ONE LEVEL, so a nested seq in a boundary's children
survives unrealised too.

REPRODUCTION (carrier (a) — lazy seq at a boundary's prop position; state layer is the arm's own):

  (defview child [{:keys [rows]}]
    [:ul.child (for [r rows] [:li.cell (str r)])])        ; realised HERE, in child's window

  (defview parent [_]
    [child {:rows (for [id (sub [:dogfood/visible-ids])]
                    (:title (sub [:dogfood/todo id])))}])

With visible-ids = [0 1 2]:
1. `parent` renders. `(sub [:dogfood/visible-ids])` IS called (the for's binding expression is
   eager); `(sub [:dogfood/todo id])` is NOT. parent's read set = #{[F [:dogfood/visible-ids]]}.
2. `boundary-element` puts the unrealised seq in `body-props` under :rows.
3. `child` renders; its `for` walks `rows`; `read-key!` sees rstate.frame = F (non-nil) -> NO
   THROW. Three [:dogfood/todo id] keys land on CHILD's scratch. parent holds no row edge.
4. dispatch [:dogfood/edit-draft 1 "x"] then [:dogfood/commit 1] -> [:dogfood/todo 1] moves ->
   index dirties CHILD.
5. `child` re-renders with the SAME props object; `rows` is the same fully-realised LazySeq, so
   `sub` is not called. child's read set collapses; React re-subscribes; all three row edges are
   dropped and the cells released.
6. EXPECTED: .cell for id 1 reads "x". ACTUAL: it still reads "todo 1", and no later write to any
   row will ever move it.

Carrier (b) is the same fault through nested children:
  (defview parent2 [_] [child2 (for [g groups] (for [id (ids g)] [:li (str (sub [:dogfood/todo id]))]))])

NOT COVERED BY ANY EXISTING WITNESS. `a-lazy-for-registers-its-edges-and-its-readers-re-run`
(arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:126-160) and `reads-inside-a-lazy-for-update-the-dom-on-a-later-write`
(arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test.cljs:197-217) both keep the `for` inside a NATIVE tag in the same
boundary — the one path the codec does force.

RECOMMENDED FIX — realise at the boundary hand-off. In `boundary-element`, walk `body-props` for
seqs the way `convert-prop-value` already does for native props, and flatten children fully
rather than one level. Cost is paid where the escape is and the read lands on the RIGHT boundary.
This is also the only change that makes judgement:206-212's structural claim true as written.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: giving `read-key!` a per-boundary render token to refuse against. That is
per-boundary render identity — one line from the HD-002 candidate-ledger tripwire — and must not
be taken.

ACCEPTANCE: a witness in the arm's own suites that mounts carrier (a) (and ideally (b)), writes
to a row query the parent produced, and asserts the DOM moved; plus judgement:237-241 corrected
so the residual case is not described as benign.
close_reason:
FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7329 (branch worker/escape-2rtt6-45).

REPRODUCED FIRST, independently, at the seam on the unfixed runtime: the parent's read set was #{[F [:dogfood/visible-ids]]} alone, the three [:dogfood/todo id] keys were on the CHILD, the child's second render with the same props read NOTHING, and a write to a row notified the child (hits 1) and not the parent (hits 0). Carrier (b) reproduced the same way once the outer for was written as the boundary's single trailing form (an 'into' at the call site splices it early and hides the fault).

THE FIX is the bead's own recommendation: realise at the hand-off. codec/realize-deep, called once on body-props in boundary-element —

  (defn realize-deep [v]
    (if-not (coll? v) v
      (do (if (map? v) (reduce-kv realize-entry nil v) (reduce realize-item nil v)) v)))

It forces every lazy sequence reachable from the props map and returns the map BY IDENTITY: realising a LazySeq caches into the seq, so nothing is rebuilt or copied. :children is a key in the same map, so ONE call covers both carriers — the nested-children carrier needed no change to realize-children's one-level flatten, and the ABI is therefore unchanged (forcing is sufficient; fully flattening would have altered documented semantics for no correctness gain). The two reducing fns are top-level vars because a fn literal at a reduce site mints a function object per collection visited and run! mints one of its own — hoisting them made the walk allocation-free and 31% faster.

NOT per-boundary render identity: rstate is still one object, nothing can tell one render attempt from another, no candidate ledger, no third hook. The <=2-hook budget is intact and measured at React's dispatcher (hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test's 1/7/20 rung, green); subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else (make-subscribe untouched).

COST, MEASURED not assumed (:none build, Node 22, best of five): 69 ns for the dogfood row's props = 6% of the 1089 ns the boundary element build already costs; 233 ns with two hiccup children; 13.5 us for a 100-row collection prop against 15.1 us for the whole build. That ceiling compares outwards: the SAME collection at a NATIVE prop position costs 70.7 us through clj->js, so the position the structural claim already rested on is 4.7x dearer than the one this repairs.

WITNESSES, mutation-proved by removing the single call and restoring it. arm1/boundary_crossing_cljs_test.cljs (8 rows, node): exit 1 with 7 failures before, exit 0 / 24 assertions after. arm1/boundary_crossing_dom_cljs_test.cljs (2 rows, real Chromium): exit 1 with 4 failures before — the cell frozen at 'todo 2' through TWO writes and the edge count collapsing 7 -> 1 on the first — exit 0 / 10 assertions after. Every first-paint assertion passed on the BROKEN runtime, which is exactly why the second half is asserted.

THE DISMISSAL IS REWRITTEN IN PLACE at docs/design/hicasso/studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md, as a new section 'One residual case, and one that was not residual': it states the freeze, retracts the structural claim it rested on, records the rejected alternative as rejected, and names what genuinely remains — a delay handed across a crossing is the same fault in a shape no walk may repair (forcing a delay eagerly is the opposite of what a delay is for), while a FUNCTION prop is not in this class at all, because the child re-runs it every render so the read repeats and the edge is kept. The same correction lands in the two docstrings that repeated the claim (arm1/runtime.cljs, arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs) and in the codec's ABI table.

GATES (foreground, worktree-local logs, exit codes echoed): npm run test:cljs 0 (12216 tests / 60780 assertions), npm run test:browser 0 (942 / 5831) — both re-run AFTER rebasing onto origin/main 6a90ce92e4, since main had moved under subs/cache.cljc and substrate/spine.cljs mid-flight; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0 ('PASS fast PR spine'); clj-kondo 2026.04.15 (CI's pinned version and exact --lint set, --fail-level error) 0 with errors: 0. mkdocs --strict does NOT cover docs/design/hicasso/** (exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml) and soft-skipped locally — the page was hand-verified AND is covered by scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, the fast-pr spine's docs corpus anchor validator, which scans it and validates the new in-page anchor.

Not merged — the mayor merges.

WHAT I KEPT WRITING INTO BRIEFS: 'mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/hicasso/** — verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so.' The first half is true. THE IMPLICATION THAT ANCHORS ARE UNGATED IS FALSE.

Nothing validates TABLE COLUMN COUNTS, rendering or nav, so verify those by hand and report the counts.'

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is the same one rf2-x5dvk was filed about and which I then committed myself: BEFORE NAMING OR DENYING A GATE, READ ITS EXCLUSION CONFIG AND PROVE IT WITH A CONTROL. A brief that under-claims coverage wastes worker effort on hand-verification; one that over-claims it is the fail-open defect this project hunts. Both are the same error.

title: hicasso: the read-set entry cache degrades to an O(N) scan selected by read ORDER, and :read-set-entry is misfiled as :shared
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).
File: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs

(1) THE O(N) BUCKET SCAN. `entry-for` buckets on `(aget scratch 0)` — the FIRST read — and then
linearly scans the bucket with an ordered pairwise compare (:673-676, :648-662). Read ORDER is
documented nowhere as significant, and it selects between O(1) and O(N) per render:

  ;; O(1): every row's first key is distinct, so every bucket holds one entry
  (defview row [{:keys [id]}]
    (let [todo   (sub [:dogfood/todo id])
          dense? (sub [:ui/dense?])] ...))

  ;; O(N): every row's first key is the SAME, so all N entries share one bucket
  (defview row [{:keys [id]}]
    (let [dense? (sub [:ui/dense?])          ; <- moved up two lines
          todo   (sub [:dogfood/todo id])] ...))

In the second form every probe passes the length test (2 == 2) and the index-0 test (identical
shared key) and fails only at index 1, so nothing short-circuits. Mounting 300 rows costs
sum(i) ~= 44,850 probes ~= 90k `=` calls on nested vectors; a write to [:ui/dense?] dirties all
300 and costs another 44,850. The first form costs 300. Same page, same edges, same DOM, ~150x
the entry-lookup work, chosen by which `let` binding an author wrote first.

Entries with refs >= 1 are never reaped (:638-646, :751), so the bucket does not drain while the
rows are mounted. `drop-entry!` (:630-636) then rebuilds the whole bucket vector per eviction, so
unmounting the list is O(N^2) again.

This lands on the bulk K=100/300 rung the programme benchmarks and is invisible to every current
witness, because the dogfood row happens to read its per-row key first
(arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs:59-61).

Candidate fixes (design, not ruled): bucket on a cheap content hash of the whole key sequence
rather than the first key; or keep a per-bucket map from a joined key-string to the entry. Either
keeps the false-negative-only property (a miss costs a second entry and a replace-set-with-itself,
never a missing edge — runtime.cljs:96-101) and must be argued to keep it.

(2) `:read-set-entry` IS FILED UNDER `:shared` AND IS NOT, IN THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS.
`retained-inventory` puts it under `:shared` at :926-927. For the bulk-row shape — a row body
reading [:dogfood/todo id], i.e. arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs:59-71 — every row has a DISTINCT
read set, so there is exactly one entry per live boundary: a JS object, a key array, a
PersistentHashSet of the same keys, and two closures. Any heap ladder reading the inventory
literally (rf2-2rtt6.34) will under-count per-boundary retention by one entry per boundary, on
the exact rung it is being taken for.

ACCEPTANCE: the scan is no longer O(live boundaries sharing a first key) — with a witness that
mounts N rows in the shared-first-key shape and asserts the probe count (or entry-lookup work) is
sub-linear in N; and `retained-inventory` states honestly that an entry is shared only across
boundaries with an IDENTICAL read sequence, so the bulk case is per-boundary.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso: the DOM suites' residue gates cannot fail -- mount/release! resets the runtime before the assertion, and React-driven teardown is unwitnessed
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

`mount/release!` calls `rt/reset-runtime!` (arm1/mount.cljs:65-76), which drops every cell,
entry, edge and boundary (arm1/runtime.cljs:962-980) — BEFORE the assertion runs. So:

  - `the-screen-leaves-no-residue` (arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test.cljs:344-355), and
  - `the-fenced-boundary-leaves-no-residue` (arm1/generation_fence_dom_cljs_test.cljs:219-227)

both assert `{:cells 0 :cell-refs 0 :boundaries 0 :edges 0 :entries 0}` against a table the line
above just emptied. They cannot fail. A gate nobody has watched fire is not evidence.

The property IS genuinely witnessed at the node seam, through `commit-boundary!` with an `async`
macrotask horizon (arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:462-499) — that pair is real and should be kept.
But that seam is NOT React. The stronger statement: NO SUITE WITNESSES THAT REACT'S OWN CLEANUP
RELEASES EVERYTHING. That is the path that runs in production, and it is the path a re-subscribe
cycle exercises on every read-set change (see rf2-2rtt6.47).

studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:176-180 states the opposite — "every DOM suite
asserts the same after its mount" — and needs correcting with whatever this bead lands.

FIX: assert the residue between the root unmount and `reset-runtime!` (either split `release!`
into `unmount!` + `reset!`, or take the reading inside `release!` before the reset and expose it),
and add the macrotask horizon so the cell/entry reapers have run. Then the DOM gate says what it
claims. Worth adding a deliberately-planted-fault check (as
`lane_release_dom_cljs_test.cljs` does for the lane's own residue gate) so the repaired gate is
shown to be able to answer false.

title: hicasso: record-reads' set difference is dead on the wired path -- every commit diffs against the empty set, so a one-key change costs a full teardown+rebuild
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

HD-002(b) is discharged against `front.sub-index/record-reads`'s set difference
(runtime.cljs:87-94; studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:128-135), and law 4 ("a re-run
with fewer reads drops edges") is proved for that algebra in front/sub_index_laws_cljs_test.

THE WIRED RUNTIME NEVER TAKES THAT PATH. Arm 1's boundary id is the REGISTRATION OBJECT minted
inside `subscribe` (runtime.cljs:738-745). A changed read set means a new entry, a new `subscribe`
closure, and therefore a NEW registration object. `index/mount!` (front/sub_index.cljs:100-108)
installs `#{}` for that fresh id, so in `record-reads` (front/sub_index.cljs:133-156) `held` is
ALWAYS the empty set: `added` is always the whole read set and `dropped` is always empty. The
narrowing half is done by `index/unmount!`'s drop-everything (front/sub_index.cljs:123-131), not
by the diff. arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:309-322 shows the shape without naming it — the test has
to `(release)` before committing the narrower read set.

CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE POINT AND NOT THE PEDANTRY: there is no cheap route for "19 of 20 keys
unchanged". Trace what React does when `subscribe` identity moves — previous cleanup, then new
subscribe:
  - cleanup (runtime.cljs:746-752): `index/unmount!` drops EVERY edge, then
    `(doseq [cell cells] (release-cell! cell))` decrements EVERY cell, each one reaching 0 arming
    its own js/setTimeout reaper (runtime.cljs:411-419, 489-492);
  - `entry-for` miss (runtime.cljs:673-686): `.slice`, `(into #{} ks)`, two closures, a
    `swap! !entries`, and one more js/setTimeout;
  - new subscribe (runtime.cljs:738-745): `mapv acquire-cell!` over EVERY key, `index/mount!`,
    `index/record-reads!`.
For a 20-read boundary with one key changed that is 20 releases + 20 re-acquires + ~22 scheduled
macrotasks + two whole-map rebuilds of :sub->bs. The judgement prices it as "an identity change
and one replacement" (:374-378). That understates it, and it is exactly the cost the same page
names as "the thing to watch on the bulk rows".

The steady-state claim is NOT under attack: an unchanged read set really is free and really is
witnessed (runtime_cljs_test.cljs:283-297, :392-400). What is wrong is the changed case.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this bead is a finding + a design question, not a prescription):
  (a) accept the cliff, and correct runtime.cljs:87-94 and judgement:128-135 to describe the path
      that runs (unmount-all + mount-all) rather than the algebra that is tested; or
  (b) give the boundary a durable id across re-subscribes so `record-reads`'s diff becomes live —
      note this needs care: a durable id is per-boundary identity, and the HD-002 tripwire bans
      per-RENDER/per-ATTEMPT identity, not per-MOUNT identity, so a mount-scoped token minted in
      `subscribe` and threaded through the cleanup is likely legal. Argue it against the tripwire
      explicitly before implementing.
Either way, `sub_index`'s law-4 coverage should gain a witness that drives it through the
runtime's own wiring, so the tested algebra and the running path stop diverging.

title: Hicasso presence: phase as a prop, and ::h/mounting / ::h/unmounting attribute overrides as data
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

This bead fixes a DOCUMENTED TRAP in the shipped predecessor and answers the
operator's 2026-07-31 steer about expressing mount/unmount as data.

THE TRAP. Freehand's presence boundary exposes phase as an AMBIENT READ,
v/presence-phase (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1756). Its own
guide records what that costs — docs/core/freehand/host/presence.md:62-66, verbatim:

  "Read the phase inside a DECLARED, KEYED CHILD VIEW, as above. Reading it in markup
   written inline in the parent is a trap: those props are evaluated during the
   PARENT'S render, so the phase you get is the parent's, not the per-child one you
   meant."

So a fading toast cannot be written inline. It must be extracted into a defview purely
so a dynamic var resolves against the right child, and getting it wrong yields the
wrong phase SILENTLY. The a11y obligation then costs three separate (when exiting? ...)
attributes on that child (presence.md:157-165).

Freehand explicitly rejected the alternative — presence.md:52-61, verbatim:
  "presence writes nothing onto your markup. There are no ::v/mounting /
   ::v/unmounting attribute overrides ... A boundary that stamped attributes would
   have to guess at a node it never sees."

That reason is sound for a boundary stamping BY ITSELF. It does not survive the AUTHOR
writing the override on the node.

PRIMARY SOURCE, verified 2026-07-31 (replicant.fun): Replicant has two mechanisms and
only one is data. ":replicant/mounting" / ":replicant/unmounting" are ATTRIBUTE
OVERRIDES — "Replicant allows you to specify overrides for any attributes during
mounting and unmounting. This allows you to declaratively transition elements on mount
and unmount". Separately ":replicant/on-mount" / ":replicant/on-unmount" are
CALLBACKS taking (fn [{:keys [replicant/node]}] ...) (replicant.fun/life-cycle-hooks/).
Only the attribute-override half is worth taking; the callback half is LESS
data-oriented than Freehand's registered behaviors and is rejected.

THE PROPOSAL — two changes.

(1) ::h/mounting and ::h/unmounting are ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDE MAPS on a native node. The
    presence boundary merges them into that node's attrs while the child is in that
    phase. The boundary already owns the retained-children list (that is what
    retention IS), so this is a pure hiccup->hiccup transform applied BEFORE the codec
    runs. React sees an ordinary element whose props changed: no wrapper node, no
    stamped data-* attribute, NO REF, NO EFFECT, NO HOOK, and no ambient read.

      (h/presence {:timeout-ms 300}
        (for [t (sub [:toasts/visible])]
          [:div.toast {:key (:id t)
                       ::h/unmounting {:class "toast toast--exit"
                                       :inert true :aria-hidden true}}
           (:message t)]))

    The child view has disappeared, and the three (when exiting? ...) attributes are
    one map.

(2) When the presence child IS a boundary, the phase arrives as an ORDINARY PROP
    ([toast-card {:key id :toast t :rf/phase :unmounting}]), never an ambient read.
    That deletes the trap by construction: a prop cannot be read from the wrong render
    scope, it appears in a structural test's props map, and a headless test can supply
    it with no clock.

Consequence: v/presence-phase has no Hicasso equivalent — one fewer public concept
against K5 (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360).

HONEST LIMITS TO RECORD IN THE DESIGN
  - The override applies to a node the boundary can SEE. An override written inside an
    opaque child view is invisible to it; that is exactly what (2) is for.
  - ENTER is the weak half and Freehand already says why (presence.md:130-135): "driving
    enter purely as a :mounting -> :present class flip can race paint ... An ANIMATION
    ON INSERTION (or modern @starting-style) is more reliable." Ship ::h/mounting, but
    teach the CSS answer for enter.

INHERIT UNCHANGED from Freehand: :timeout-ms MANDATORY, as retention length AND
terminal bound (presence.md:48, freehand.cljc:1739); "re-entry cancels exit"
(presence.md:87-89); keys required on every dynamic child; presence never dispatches
domain mount/unmount events (presence.md:181).

WITNESSES
  1. A toast written INLINE (no child view) gets the exit attributes while unmounting
     and loses them on re-entry.
  2. A boundary child receives :rf/phase as a prop and it is assertable headlessly.
  3. The node is gone after :timeout-ms; nothing leaks.
notes:
CORRECTION to the close reason: one phrase lost a word to shell backtick expansion. It should read 'step/expire take the current instant as an ARGUMENT, which is what makes that true' — the machine never reads a clock itself, which is exactly why a headless test can assert every phase, deadline and expiry with no timers at all.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. Presence reuses the same RAW #{:key :ref} dissoc for phase overrides. An unmounting override carrying "key" or :x/key survives with-phase and canonicalizes to React key after the child's real :key is removed, remounting the node that presence was meant to retain; ref aliases likewise reach the node. Reuse the canonical structural-slot filter owned by rf2-2rtt6.36 and pin retained key identity through the presence path. No ordering redesign or new presence option.
close_reason: AUDIT-REOPEN repaired in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7332. presence/with-phase no longer dissocs a raw #{:key :ref} from a phase override; it filters through codec/without-structural — the same canonical-slot filter :& uses, owned by rf2-2rtt6.36. Retained key identity is pinned by construction: the only :key in the merged attributes is the one the child is retained under, because no spelling can reach that slot. HD-025 records why sharing the filter is the point rather than a convenience. Witnesses: an unmounting override carrying "key", 'key or :x/key leaves the child's props exactly as found and child-key still answers the retention key; the same for "ref", 'ref, :x/ref; and in a real browser (arm1/presence_dom_cljs_test) a hostile override on a retained toast hands NO node to its "ref" while the appearance half still lands, and the retained node is the same DOM element instance across the exit. Mutation-proved both ways: reverting the filter reds the headless transform witnesses (node exit 1) AND the browser witness (test:browser exit 1 — the override's "ref" was handed a live HTMLDivElement). Honest note recorded on the PR: the key face's DOM consequence was already masked by native-element writing js-props.key from the child's own :key after conversion, so the key face's mutation red is at the transform; the face that was live in the DOM is the ref.

title: Hicasso: reserve :ref's vector value-space now, refuse it loudly in v0, so the imperative escape can become data later
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

This is a ONE-BRANCH design constraint, deliberately NOT a subsystem. It exists so
that Hicasso's best available lifecycle spelling stays reachable after v0 instead of
being designed out.

WHERE HICASSO STANDS TODAY. HD-003 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:83-86) rules the
v0 answer for imperative mechanics as "component mechanics (composition, measurement,
focus, animation, SDK handles) may use ORDINARY REACT HOOKS at the honest escape
hatch", and HD-016 (decisions.md:337-339) makes :ref "legal on native tags and
defhost/[:>] crossings (CALLBACK REFS ONLY)". That is defensible: the corpus census
finds ONE :ref in 85 idiomatic files
(docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md:336).

BUT IT IS THE ONE PLACE HICASSO IS PLANNED TO BE *LESS* DATA-ORIENTED THAN THE
SUBSTRATE IT REPLACES. Freehand's registered behaviors keep the USE SITE as data and
put the code in a registry — implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/behaviors.cljc:48,
"the use site is data all the way down and the implementation is registered code":

    [v/behavior {:use autosize :target :composer/body :config {:max-rows 8}}
     [:textarea.composer ...]]

with :config refusing a callback, a node, a ref or a host instance on both hosts
(docs/core/freehand/host/host-boundaries.md:211-213).

THE PROPOSAL (all of it). :ref accepts:
  - a function                       -> v0, the HD-003 escape hatch, unchanged
  - a vector [registered-id config]  -> RESERVED. v0 REFUSES IT LOUDLY with a
                                        diagnostic naming the reservation, rather than
                                        passing it to React as an opaque value.

That is the whole bead. One refusal branch and one error id. It costs nothing and it
keeps {:ref [::autosize {:max-rows 8}]} reachable without minting a second attribute
name later.

WHY THE LATER SPELLING IS MECHANICALLY SOUND — verified from react.dev
(react-dom/components/common, fetched 2026-07-31):
  - "React 19 added cleanup functions for ref callbacks."
  - "optional cleanup function: When the ref is detached, React will call the cleanup
     function."
  - on mount: "When the DOM node is added to the screen, React calls your ref callback
     with the DOM node as the argument."
  - on update: "React calls your ref callback whenever you pass a DIFFERENT ref
     callback."
  - Strict Mode: "React runs one extra development-only setup+cleanup cycle before the
     first real setup."

So a RUNTIME-minted ref callback is a complete attach/detach pair, with the node, in
the commit phase, and NO ref object or effect ever appears in user code. Three
obligations follow from those quotes and must be recorded when the later bead lands:
  1. the minted callback's identity must be STABLE PER SITE or React detaches and
     reattaches every render (this is Freehand's site-owned stable proxy —
     docs/core/freehand/authoring/events-and-handlers.md:404-414);
  2. connect/disconnect must be IDEMPOTENT because StrictMode adds a cycle;
  3. timing is commit-before-paint only, so Freehand's :passive (after paint) has NO
     ref-callback equivalent (behaviors.cljc:141 closes timings at #{:passive :layout}).

AND THE REAL GAP, STATED HONESTLY SO NOBODY REDISCOVERS IT: a ref callback fires on
ATTACH and DETACH, never on CONFIG CHANGE. Freehand's :update — "only when the
committed :config moves by rf=, receiving :prev-config alongside"
(host-boundaries.md:226) — has no equivalent without either changing the callback
identity (which detaches and reattaches the node owner: wrong for a Mapbox instance)
or spending an effect. The recommended later shape is attach/detach only, config
immutable for the connection's life, and steady-state change routed through a command
EFFECT, which is already data (behaviors.cljc:129-139 registers
:re-frame.freehand.host/command — "a command is data an ordinary event handler
returns").

NOT IN SCOPE, EXPLICITLY: a behaviors registry, a :timing option, a commands roster,
or any host-ownership subsystem in v0. The census (1 ref / 85 files) does not pay for
it and charter.md:144-149 defers the component-library tier past v0.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. check-ref! inspects only (:ref props), while this codec deliberately accepts string, symbol, and namespaced-key prop spellings and later emits them by canonical name. A reserved vector under "ref" or :x/ref therefore bypasses :rf.error/hicasso-ref-vector-reserved and reaches React as the opaque value this bead exists to stop. Detect the canonical ref slot and add alternate-spelling witnesses; keep the fix to the reserved vector arm.
close_reason: AUDIT-REOPEN repaired in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7332. check-ref! no longer reads (:ref props); it is called from inside convert-props' single walk at the position whose CANONICAL SLOT is ref, using the slot the walk has already computed — so it costs no extra traversal and holds for "ref", 'ref, :x/ref and ::h/ref as well as :ref. The ref position's exclusion from intent lowering is taken on the same slot, for the same reason, so a callback ref under an alternate spelling still reaches React by identity rather than being wrapped as a render-position callback. The fix stays on the reserved VECTOR arm exactly as scoped: no other :ref value moves, and the existing string/nil/map rows still pass. The diagnostic now carries :position, so it names the spelling that was written. Mutation-proved: reverting the check to the raw key :ref reds the alternate-spelling reservation witness (node exit 1, 5 failures); restored green.

title: [bug] core test: the weak-expunge proof pins a process-wide async count with `=`, so a loaded runner reds it
description:
SYMPTOM. `JVM core (clojure -M:test)` went red on PR #7331 (run 30655577476, job
91239771476) with ONE failure out of 2198 tests:

  FAIL in (jvm-provenance-entry-is-weak-and-expunged-when-its-throwable-dies)
       (observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:3515)
  "the cleared entry was expunged - private storage returned to baseline"
  actual: false

NOT THE PR. #7331 changed six `.cljs` files under
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**` plus one design `.md`.
`implementation/core`'s `:test` alias does not put `implementation/freehand` on
the classpath, and a JVM Clojure runner cannot load `.cljs` at all. There is no
mechanism by which that diff reaches this suite.

ROOT CAUSE. The failing assertion is

  (loop [i 0]
    (#'obs/source-covered-always-on? (ex-info \"post-gc access\" {}))
    (cond (= baseline (.size m)) true
          (>= i 40)              false
          :else (do (System/gc) (System/runFinalization) (recur (inc i)))))

`m` is the PROCESS-WIDE `java.util.HashMap` at
`(:by-throwable @#'obs/provenance-storage)`, keyed by weak identity keys and
reclaimed lazily by polling a `ReferenceQueue` in `expunge-stale-provenance!`.
`baseline` is `.size` sampled after ONE `System.gc()` and one drain - i.e. a
count of how many OTHER tests' entries happened to still sit in the map at that
instant. Two facts make the strict `=` unsound:

1. A Reference is CLEARED during GC but ENQUEUED asynchronously afterwards by
   the ReferenceHandler thread. A drain taken immediately after `System.gc()`
   returns cannot see references already cleared but not yet enqueued, so
   `baseline` over-counts by the size of that pending backlog - and the backlog
   grows with machine load.

2. Nothing inside the loop ever ADDS an entry (`source-covered-always-on?` only
   reads and drains), so `.size` is monotonically non-increasing. The instant
   any pending sibling lands, `.size` falls BELOW `baseline` and
   `(= baseline (.size m))` can never become true again; the loop exhausts its
   40 rounds and yields false.

So the test reddens BECAUSE unrelated collection succeeded. The busier the
runner, the likelier it fails - which is the load-sensitivity observed.

THE NAMED PROPERTY HELD ON THE RED RUN. The preceding `(is (gc-until-cleared?
t-ref))` PASSED, so the referent was collected and storage retained it via
neither key nor value. Only the global-count equality failed. The test's
docstring claims \"the cleared entry was expunged\"; what it checks is \"the
map's total size equals a number it had before a 40-round GC storm\". Those are
not the same statement.

NON-DETERMINISM, MEASURED. On #7331's head: `clojure -M:test` in
`implementation/core` green 3x (2198 tests / 11341 assertions, exit 0); the
namespace alone green 8x run CONCURRENTLY under CPU contention. Instrumented,
`baseline` is consistently 0 and the pre-loop size 1 - an idle box has no
pending backlog, which is precisely why it cannot reproduce locally.

RECOMMENDED FIX - stronger, not weaker. Assert the specific claim rather than a
global count. `.size` is `baseline+1` at attestation and can only decrease, so
`(<= (.size m) baseline)` states exactly \"the new entry was expunged\" with no
coupling to unrelated entries. Better still, track that entry's own absence
instead of any count.

PROVENANCE. Introduced 2026-07-14 in 620f5568e7 (rf2-qqvgk1); last touched
2026-07-29 in f685fccf42 (rf2-d2841). Pre-existing and independent of #7331,
and deliberately NOT patched from #7331's branch - different artefact, and
`implementation/core/test/**` is a surface the audit loop works actively.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7336 (branch worker/expunge-8vvdo, commit ab5e32c66d).

The diagnosis was verified against implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc and holds: m is the process-wide HashMap, keys are weak identity keys reclaimed only by expunge-stale-provenance! polling the ReferenceQueue, source-covered-always-on? only reads and drains (never adds) so .size is monotonically non-increasing inside the loop, and a Reference is cleared during GC but enqueued asynchronously afterwards - so baseline over-counts by the pending backlog and the size falls BELOW it under load.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the bead.

1. The RECOMMENDED FIX was NOT applied, because it is unsound. (<= (.size m) baseline) cures the false red by buying a FALSE GREEN under the same load: a sibling expunging in our entry's place satisfies it while our entry is still leaked. Measured, not argued - in a seeded-backlog run the probe (and (<= (.size m) baseline) (.containsKey m our-key)) PASSED, i.e. <= held with our entry demonstrably still in the map, before the throwable had even been released. The bead's own better-still alternative is what landed: the stored key is located by referent identity over the live key set and the assertion is (not (.containsKey m our-key)). Holding that key strongly retains the KEY, never its referent (it is a WeakReference subclass, and the HashMap holds its keys strongly in production anyway), so the lifecycle under test is unchanged.

2. The bead diagnosed only the poll loop at 3515. The SIBLING assertion carried the identical defect: (= (inc baseline) (.size m)) - 'the attestation bound exactly one entry' - reds whenever the attest's own drain reclaims a pending sibling before the .put. Left alone the test would have stayed load-sensitive after the loop was repaired. It is now (= 1 (count our-keys)) - exactly one key in the map has this throwable as referent - which is load-independent and a literal statement of what it claims.

3. Path: the bead names implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc; the file is implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc (no substrate/ segment). Line 3515 was correct.

MUTATION PROOF. Planted the defect in production code - expunge-stale-provenance! polls but never removes, so a cleared key leaks forever while the referent still clears. RED, exit 1, 1 failure of 4, with gc-until-cleared? and the exactly-one-entry precondition both still passing (the leak isolated from every other assertion). Reverted, git diff empty: GREEN, exit 0. Run twice - once before the mid-task API outage and once after on a since-idle box - identical.

OLD FAILURE MODE REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY. A scratch test (temporary, reverted, not committed) seeded the backlog the async enqueue produces on a loaded runner - a sibling entry cleared and still counted when baseline is sampled. Both OLD forms red and both NEW forms green in the SAME run, 3/3 runs: baseline=1, size-after-attest=1, final size=0 - the size fell below the sampled baseline exactly as diagnosed.

GATES (all foreground, exit codes echoed). clojure -M:test in implementation/core: 0 (2198 tests, 11341 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors) - the gate that reddened. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: 0 (PASS fast PR spine); its JVM implementation/core leg ran while sibling workers were active, i.e. under load. clj-kondo 2026.04.15 (CI's pinned version, CI's exact --lint invocation; local npm binary was v2025.10.23 so the pinned release was fetched): 0, errors: 0. TESTING.md matrix: the diff is one file under implementation/core/test/** with no production code, so the fast-PR JVM tier is implementation/core alone - confirmed by --plan printing PLAN-JVM implementation/core. test-jvm-implementation.sh is not mapped for this surface (TESTING.md scopes it to a broad refactor reaching artefacts the tier does not select); the wider CI fan-out runs in CI.

PR left OPEN for the mayor to merge.

I PRESCRIBED AN UNSOUND FIX AND A WORKER CAUGHT IT BY MEASURING (2026-08-01, rf2-8vvdo / PR #7336). Record the lesson, not the incident.

WHAT HAPPENED. A core test reddened under load because it asserted a PROCESS-WIDE weak-map count for strict equality; the diagnosing worker filed rf2-8vvdo proposing (<= (.size m) baseline) as a STRONGER replacement, and I briefed that fix as-is while telling the implementing worker 'the fix must be stronger, never weaker' and 'prove it still catches the original defect'.

THE IMPLEMENTING WORKER REFUSED IT AND WAS RIGHT. (<= (.size m) baseline) cures the false RED by buying a false GREEN under the same load: a SIBLING entry expunging in our entry's place satisfies it while OUR entry is still leaked. It did not argue this — it MEASURED it, with a probe of (and (<= (.size m) baseline) (.containsKey m our-key)) that PASSED, i.e. the proposed assertion held with the leaked entry still in the map, before the throwable was even released. That is precisely the fail-open class my own brief forbade.

THE CORRECT SHAPE, which the bead itself had offered as an alternative: assert THE ENTRY'S OWN ABSENCE, not a population count. (= (inc baseline) (.size m)) -> (= 1 (count our-keys)); (= baseline (.size m)) -> (not (.containsKey m our-key)). It also found the bead had diagnosed only ONE of the two assertions — the sibling assertion carried the identical defect and would have left the test load-sensitive.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is mine: WHEN A BEAD PROPOSES A SPECIFIC FIX, THE BRIEF MUST TREAT IT AS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A SPECIFICATION. I passed a diagnosing worker's proposed patch through to an implementing worker with my authority attached, which converts a suggestion into an instruction and invites compliance over judgement. Correct form: state the DEFECT and the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (here: 'the assertion must fail when this entry leaks, whatever else the process is doing'), cite the bead's proposal as one candidate, and say explicitly that a better shape is welcome and a refusal with evidence is a complete answer.

SECOND-ORDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: an assertion about a SHARED, PROCESS-WIDE quantity can almost never state a claim about ONE participant. Prefer identity over population whenever the property is about a specific object — count-based proxies fail open under concurrency in both directions.

DO NOT REAP A WORKTREE WHEN ITS PR MERGES — REAP WHEN ITS AGENT REPORTS DONE (2026-08-01, my error, caught by the worker).

WHAT I DID. After merging PR #7337 I ran scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh against worker/heapaxis-2rtt6-34. The removal FAILED on a Windows file lock — but the script had already done its first job and DISARMED THE node_modules JUNCTION. The agent was still alive. Its next shadow-cljs invocation failed with 'shadow-cljs not found', and it spent a tool round diagnosing before reporting 'my worktree's junction has vanished... Recreating it'. It recovered on its own and the mayor's real node_modules was verified intact at 101 throughout, so nothing was damaged — but I cost a live worker a diagnostic detour for no reason.

THE MISTAKE IS THE TRIGGER, NOT THE SCRIPT. A merged PR means the WORK landed; it does NOT mean the AGENT finished. Agents legitimately continue after opening a PR — updating the PR body, re-running a gate, hardening a mutation proof, answering a resume message. The safe trigger is the agent's own completion notification, or an explicit confirmation from it that it is done with the tree.

THE RULE: reap a worker worktree only when BOTH are true — (1) its PR is merged, AND (2) its agent has reported done (or has been confirmed dead). If a reap fails on a file lock, that is often a SIGNAL the tree is still in use; do not retry in a loop, and check whether the agent is alive before trying again.

RELATED, ALREADY KNOWN AND STILL TRUE: the guard script is correct to disarm the link before removing (that is what stops git worktree remove following it into the mayor's real node_modules), and it correctly refuses rather than forcing when the removal cannot complete. The failure mode here is entirely in WHEN I invoked it.

title: uix adapter: which controlled-input implementation a consumer gets depends on whether Reagent is in the bundle
description:
RULING NEEDED, and it is cheap to act on once made.

UIx decides, per element and at element-creation time, between plain React and
a port of Reagent's controlled-input workaround.
`uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input` branches on
`uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?`, which — with
`*use-reagent-input-enabled?*` unset, the shipped default — answers "is
`reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive*` present, and false?" (uix.core 1.4.4,
`uix/compiler/input.cljs:15-21`).

So a consumer's decision to ALSO use the Reagent adapter silently changes how
the UIx adapter's `<input>` elements behave. Measured in real Chromium
(rf2-n3dxw, docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md):

- plain React: the value converges INSIDE the discrete event; the caret is
  thrown to the end of the field on every write React makes.
- the port: the value and the caret both converge correctly, by offset from the
  end of the string — but one `requestAnimationFrame` later, never in-turn.

Those are materially different products. Today which one a consumer gets is a
fact about their classpath.

THE ACTION, once ruled: one `set!` of
`uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?*` at
`re-frame.adapter.uix` load, pinning the semantics re-frame2 wants. The cost is
the ruling, not the implementation.

NOT DISPATCHABLE WITHOUT THE RULING: pinning to `false` takes the caret
behaviour away from mixed-bundle consumers who have it today; pinning to `true`
makes every UIx consumer's controlled input converge a frame late and couples
the UIx adapter to Reagent's batching queue. Mike decides.
notes:
RULING (Mike, 2026-08-01, verbatim: 'rule rf2-heqwo — make the React path the default'). Recorded by acting mayor.

WHAT IS RULED: the UIx adapter's controlled-input implementation is REACT'S OWN by default. It must NOT be selected by whether Reagent happens to be on the classpath.

THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES. uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input branches on uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?, which asks 'is reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive* PRESENT and false?'. Every :browser-test bundle carries Reagent, and so does any app using both adapters — so adding Reagent alongside UIx SILENTLY changed how UIx's controlled inputs behave, with no diagnostic and no opt-in. The Reagent port makes the element UNCONTROLLED (deletes :value, installs defaultValue + a ref) and drives it from reagent.impl.batching/do-after-render, a requestAnimationFrame queue — one frame late. React's own path converges IN-TURN, before dispatchEvent returns, via its restore machinery (verified against react-dom 19.2.0 source in this repo).

THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE CONSUMERS WILL SEE, stated plainly because it is real and must be documented rather than discovered: on a REFUSED keystroke the two paths differ. React converges in the same turn but THROWS THE CARET TO THE END ('12345' + a refused 'z' with the caret at [2 2] lands at [5 5]). The Reagent port preserves the caret but only one animation frame later. This ruling takes in-turn convergence and React-native, predictable behaviour over late caret preservation — and, more importantly, takes DETERMINISM over a silent classpath dependency. An app that behaves differently because of what else is in its bundle is the worse defect.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO: it does not settle rf2-n3dxw, which stays open because NEITHER shipped path gives both same-turn convergence AND the caret where the edit left it. rf2-fki5d is the priced prototype that gets both halves (one flushSync per keystroke, a per-instance last-rendered value, no user-visible ref/effect/hook) and remains blocked on an element path to put it in. This ruling makes the default honest; fki5d would make it complete.

DISPATCHED. Operator-overturnable.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7339 (branch worker/heqwo-default).

RULING IMPLEMENTED (Mike, 2026-08-01: 'make the React path the default'). re-frame.adapter.uix now requires uix.compiler.input and pins the selector at namespace load:

  (set! uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?* false)

It really was one set!. Production diff = one require + one set! + the comment block explaining both. Namespace load runs ahead of any render and therefore ahead of element creation, which is where uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input reads the var. No classpath sniffing on the default path.

OVERRIDE PRESERVED: the var stays ^:dynamic and public, so a consumer who genuinely wants Reagent's port asks for it explicitly with (set! ... true) after requiring the adapter; binding works too. PR #7330's per-row pinning witnesses are undisturbed — all 16 pass in the browser (53 assertions), and NO measured row's expectation changed.

TWO WITNESS CHANGES, both explained in the PR: (1) unpin-input-implementation! now restores the adapter's pin (:react) rather than nil — release! calls it after every with-grid, so on main every row left the var cleared, handing the choice back to the bundle for every namespace running later in the same build; (2) the deftest was renamed the-input-implementation-is-the-adapters-choice-not-the-bundles, since its old premise ('the shipped default here is the port') is now false for a re-frame2 UIx app. It still asserts UIx's raw classpath answer, inside a with-uix-raw-default that clears and restores the pin.

MUTATION-PROVEN. Forcing the classpath-sniffing branch back on (set! ... nil) reds the new adapter suite: exit 1, 2 failures. Reverted with git diff empty. The proof is deliberately ORDER-INDEPENDENT: the suite snapshots the var at its own namespace load (value-at-load), because a live read inside a deftest can be masked by whichever sibling suite pins the implementation first.

DOCUMENTED, not hidden. docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md (published; mkdocs --strict covers it) gains a '## Controlled inputs and the caret' section stating the behaviour change consumers will see: React converges in-turn but throws the caret to the end ('12345' + refused 'z' at [2 2] lands at [5 5]); the port preserves the caret one animation frame late. It says why (a silent classpath dependency is the worse defect), how to opt back in, and names rf2-fki5d as the priced route to both halves. The hicasso studio page records Option C as TAKEN and re-hashes the witness blob.

DOES NOT SETTLE rf2-n3dxw — left OPEN deliberately. Neither shipped path gives both same-turn convergence and the caret where the edit left it.

SCOPE confirmed by the sibling: rf2-2rtt6.41 (PR #7338, not yet on main) proved Hicasso's boundaries are immune by construction (front.codec emits :input via react/createElement against the tag string, so create-uix-input is never on that path). This change is correctly confined to the UIx adapter. #7338 rebases onto this and updates its one row, the-selector-is-live-in-this-bundle.

title: spec/009: the three :rf.error/safe-redirect-* Tags columns still list :location (and :allowlist) — the always-on record no longer carries either
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-6jqa8's AUDIT-REOPEN tightening (PR #7205). spec/** is HOT-ZONE, so the worker reported rather than edited. Obligation (6)(c) of the rf2-6jqa8 ruling — it was assigned to rf2-rprfg, which CLOSED on PR #7192 before this tightening existed, so it needs its own bead.

THE DRIFT. PR #7205 made the always-on safe-redirect record a strict STRUCTURAL PROJECTION of the diagnostics: it carries #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme :host} and NOTHING else. It no longer carries :location in any form (scrubbed or otherwise), and no longer carries :allowlist. The dev trace still carries both. spec/009 does not yet distinguish the two axes:

  (a) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url (~line 2140):
      reads ':frame, :location, :reason, plus :scheme on the :scheme-without-host arm'
      — the always-on record carries :frame, :reason, and :scheme; never :location.
  (b) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected (~2141):
      reads ':frame, :location, :scheme, plus :reason on the non-http(s) arm'
      — always-on carries :frame, :scheme, and :reason on that arm; never :location.
  (c) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed (~2142):
      reads ':frame, :location, :host, :reason ..., :allowlist (the allowlist vector, when supplied)'
      — always-on carries :frame, :host, :reason; NEVER :location and NEVER :allowlist.
  (d) The always-on paragraph (~line 1949) says 'the tag map is built ONCE for both axes with the EP-0015 egress scrub applied to :location INSIDE the builder: the query / fragment carrier VALUES are redacted while the structured path, the scheme and the host are kept'. True of the DEV TRACE. False of the always-on record, which carries no URL at all. The 'built ONCE' claim stays true — the builder still runs once and the record is a projection of its output.

WHY THE TIGHTENING (recorded here so the spec edit can state the reason). The carrier scrub is the Spec 015 blanket policy and does string surgery only after the first '?' or '#'. Over the app's OWN URL space (rf2-ov56u's route-miss :url) that is right. Over an ARBITRARY ATTACKER-SUPPLIED FOREIGN URL it is not fail-closed: userinfo (https://alice:pw@host/), the whole path (a reset token), and value-less query keys all sit LEFT of the carriers and rode out verbatim. Demonstrated against HEAD under -Dre-frame.debug=false before the fix. :allowlist is the app's own security configuration — unbounded policy data naming the boundary being probed.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. The row's Tags column describes the trace tags; add a short always-on clause per row (or one sentence in the always-on paragraph) saying the always-on record is the closed structural projection #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme :host} with :scheme / :host lower-cased for aggregation, and that :location / :allowlist are DEV-TRACE-ONLY. Source of truth is re-frame.ssr.egress/safe-redirect-record-slots, pinned closed by the-production-record-carries-exactly-the-enumerated-slots in re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test.

NO CONFORMANCE TEST REDS TODAY. The always-on-categories literal is a set of CATEGORIES (unchanged by #7205), and there is no SafeRedirect*Tags Malli schema, so the rf2-6tags Tags-column arm has nothing to compare against these rows. The drift is therefore silent — which is why it needs a bead rather than a CI failure.

CROSS-REF rf2-mt4v3 (spec/011 should state the rejection never projects, plus the understated spec/Security.md entry) — same spec pass, adjacent scope; consider sequencing together since spec/009 and spec/011 are both hot-zone.
notes:
Audit of merged PR #7207: the axis split accurately documents PR #7205's current key set, but it also canonises the unsafe premise found while auditing that implementation: lower-cased `:scheme` and `:host` are still raw, unbounded attacker-selected URL components. Closed keys do not make their values structural or secret-free; custom schemes and DNS labels can carry sentinel material and attacker-driven cardinality. Exact implementation owner rf2-6jqa8 is reopened P1.

This Bead remains the exact Spec 009 Tags/paragraph owner. Reopen it, dependent on rf2-6jqa8, and do not duplicate the runtime design. After the always-on discriminator shape is made content-safe and bounded, update all three safe-redirect catalogue rows, the shared always-on paragraph and the named source-of-truth/key-set prose in one sequenced pass. Preserve the rich dev trace, one-record semantics and non-projecting wire behavior. Coordinate the hot-zone edit with already-open rf2-rprfg, which owns the separate promotion-criterion contradiction.
close_reason:
TAGS COLUMNS AND ALWAYS-ON PARAGRAPH RECONCILED WITH THE SHIPPED SHAPE — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342 (with rf2-6jqa8 + rf2-ycbhx's dependency rf2-6jqa8, one PR, which is what the reopen note asked for: 'after the always-on discriminator shape is made content-safe and bounded, update all three rows … in one sequenced pass').

THE DRIFT, AS FILED AND AS EXTENDED. The three Tags columns listed :location (and :allowlist on host-disallowed) as always-on tags; both had become dev-trace-only under #7205. The 2026-07-31 reopen then correctly refused to let the bead merely document #7205's key set, because that set canonised an unsafe premise — lower-cased :scheme and :host are still raw, unbounded caller-selected URL components. rf2-6jqa8 fixed the runtime in the same PR; this bead's edits describe the SETTLED shape rather than the interim one, so the spec never records a claim that was already known to be wrong.

WHAT SPEC/009 NOW SAYS.
(a)(b)(c) Each of the three rows' Tags columns is split explicitly into AXIS 1 and AXIS 2, so the two are never again confusable:
  invalid-url      axis 1 = :frame :recovery :reason, plus :scheme-class (:http/:https) on the :scheme-without-host arm; the parse-failure arm carries no class at all.
  scheme-rejected  axis 1 = :frame :recovery :scheme-class (:javascript/:data/:vbscript, or :other on the non-http(s) arm), plus :reason on that arm. The row states what the class does NOT do — it never spells the caller's scheme, so mailto: and s3cr3t-probe-token: both arrive as :other.
  host-disallowed  axis 1 = :frame :recovery :reason, and nothing else. ':host is DEV-TRACE-ONLY' is called out in bold with the three reasons it was given up.
