PROMOTION-CRITERION CONTRADICTION RECONCILED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342 (with rf2-6jqa8 + rf2-ycbhx, one PR).

THE 2026-07-31 AUDIT COMMENT'S FINDING. The three rows were correctly always-on (that half landed in #7192), but leg 2 of the authoritative criterion read 'contract breach or resource leakage … rather than a malformed input the caller can observe and fix at the call site'. A correctly refused attacker-controlled redirect is neither a leaked resource nor a corrupted invariant, so the criterion literally excluded the rows sitting beneath it.

BROADENED, NOT EXCEPTED — and that choice is the substance. The rf2-6jqa8 ruling offered either 'record the narrow exception' or 'broaden leg 2'. Broadening is right because the exception would have to be granted FOUR times over: :rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type, :rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy, the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm of :rf.error/schema-validation-failure and the three safe-redirect rejections are ALL refusals rather than leaks, and every one of them was promoted on the same reasoning. Leg 2 was under-described relative to what the axis already carried; naming the shape reconciles the criterion with the catalogue instead of carving a hole in it.

WHAT SPEC/009 NOW SAYS. Leg 2 is 'Locally invisible' with two limbs — (a) contract breach or resource leakage, unchanged; (b) a refusal whose only local effect is the ABSENCE of the action: a fail-closed gate declining as a NO-OP, nothing thrown, nothing returned, so the call site has no value with which to distinguish 'refused' from 'never asked'. A blockquote names the four families already on limb (b) so a reader sees it is descriptive, not an escape hatch.

THE EXCLUDED CASE IS UNCHANGED AND NOW SHARPER: a malformed input the caller can OBSERVE, where observing means something threw or returned. :rf.server/safe-redirect carries the whole contrast inside one effect — its CR/LF/NUL gate THROWS, so the caller is told and it rides :rf.error/fx-handler-exception; its scheme/host gate NO-OPS, so before promotion the identical class of refusal reached nobody. Two halves of one security surface, and only the silent half needed leg 2(b). That is the asymmetry this bead's own description cited, now doing work in the spec.

CHANNEL-PROMOTION CATALOGUE. Second graduated entry added (one per limb): 'Security-boundary refusals', walking the three legs for the safe-redirect family and naming its siblings on the same limb. It carries the record discipline this family taught — the criterion's closing 'structured data only … never raw values' is a PROJECTION obligation here rather than a redaction one, and the test to apply is 'could a caller choose the bytes in this value, or the number of distinct values it can take? If either, it is not structural.' The section header moves from 'one graduated catalogue row' to two.

Also made precise: the two DEMOTED resource categories now read 'fail leg 2 under BOTH limbs', so widening the leg cannot be misread as sweeping them onto the axis.

NO CONFORMANCE IMPACT, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED. No Channel cell moves, so error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test's catalogue-vs-literal invariant 4 is untouched — run green (22 tests / 55 assertions, exit 0) rather than reasoned about.

title: SSR safe-redirect rejections are invisible in production — an attempted open-redirect / javascript: scheme is silently no-op'd with no record on either error axis
description:
SURFACED 2026-07-28 by the rf2-lwtlk triage of `re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`.

NOT A SECURITY DEFECT. `:rf.server/safe-redirect`'s five-step gate (parse -> scheme -> relative-only -> allowlist -> pass) REJECTS correctly under the production gate; every `(is (nil? (:redirect (get-response f))))` assertion in the safe-redirect cluster is green there. The mitigation works.

THE GAP IS OBSERVABILITY. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc` `emit-safe-redirect-error!` (~line 681) is:

    (defn- emit-safe-redirect-error! [operation tags]
      (trace/emit-error! operation (merge {:recovery :no-recovery} tags))
      nil)

`trace/emit-error!` is the DEV bus only. So on a production JVM SSR host, an attacker-supplied `?next=javascript:alert(1)` / `?next=https://evil.example.com/` is rejected — and NOTHING reaches an off-box shipper. No Sentry event, no Datadog metric, no frame-owned `:observability :errors` record. A security team cannot see that open-redirect probing is happening against their app, and the rejection is a silent no-op with no wire signal either (the fx no-ops; the response simply carries no redirect).

The five categories affected, all emitted through that one helper:
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url        (:reason :scheme-without-host / parse failure)
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected    (javascript / data / vbscript / mailto / ftp / file …)
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed    (:reason :relative-only-violation / :not-in-allowlist)

WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A WORKER FIX. Promoting these onto the always-on `error-emit` axis changes what a PRODUCTION build sends off-box — an egress-surface change with the same review obligations rf2-ov56u carried (EP-0015 fail-closed scrub on the `:location`, which is BY CONSTRUCTION attacker-controlled and the class most likely to carry `?token=` / `#access_token=`; the redaction rf2-ov56u applied to the route-miss `:url` is the pattern). Spec 009's promotion criterion is the test to apply. It also increases the volume a shipper sees under active probing, which is a deliberate choice, not a default.

Note the asymmetry this leaves today: the CRLF/NUL gate on `:rf.server/redirect` and `:rf.server/safe-redirect` THROWS, so it rides `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` and IS always-on (fx.cljc `emit-fx-error!`). The safe-redirect scheme/host gate no-ops, so it is dev-only. Two halves of the same fx's security surface, opposite production observability.

MEANWHILE, in `ssr-end-to-end-test`, the safe-redirect trace assertions are the rf2-lwtlk posture split (dev arm); the `(nil? (:redirect …))` rejection assertions stay posture-independent and are the security-load-bearing half. That split is blocked behind rf2-dtpfv, which blocks the namespace for a different reason.
notes:
CROSS-REF rf2-mwv4e (ruled 2026-07-28, delegated by Mike, dossier review): the sibling at-boundary observability gap adopted the same promotion pattern — always-on structural record plus a NEW public event outcome :outcome :rejected. The paired egress review ran ONCE over both beads: this bead's half = EP-0015 scrub on the attacker-controlled :location (landed, PR #7191); rf2-mwv4e's half = structural-only record (identifiers only — no event vector/:value/:explain/schema form), so no scrub applies there. Deliberate divergence: mwv4e's record stays projection-eligible (boundary rejection on a server frame = 400) while this bead's three categories are non-projection-eligible (hostile probe must not conjure a 500). mwv4e's spec/009 edits touch the same always-on-categories literal as rf2-rprfg — sequenced there. Full ruling on rf2-mwv4e.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): PROMOTE — ratified — plus a MANDATORY egress-shape tightening. AUDIT-REOPEN: the shipped always-on record carries an unmet EP-0015 obligation (raw attacker-URL material + the app's allowlist ship off-box); this bead reopens to own that tightening and must not re-close until it lands. The decision dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-6jqa8.safe-redirect-observability.md, primary analysis + Codex second opinion) is deleted; everything load-bearing is recorded here.

(1) THE DECISION. The three categories (:rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url, :rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected, :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed — all emitted through the one helper emit-safe-redirect-error! in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc, ~681 at filing, ~743 at HEAD) belong on the always-on error axis. Reasoning: (a) the CRLF/NUL gate on the SAME fx throws, so it rides :rf.error/fx-handler-exception and was always always-on, while the scheme/host gate no-ops and was dev-only — two halves of one fx's security surface with opposite production observability is an accident of implementation (throw vs no-op), not a design; (b) Spec 009's promotion criterion (does production need this signal?) is answered yes by the category's nature — these fire only when someone is actively probing for open redirects / javascript: schemes, so the volume increase under probing is the feature, not a bug; (c) Codex concurs: a safe-redirect rejection is a production security-control activation whose only local result is the ABSENCE of a redirect — the effect caller receives no value with which to distinguish "rejected" from "did not write", and repetition is the operational fact that turns one bad target into visible probing; OWASP's Logging Cheat Sheet recommends logging server-side input-validation failures, and its redirect guidance treats a user-supplied destination as untrusted. The elegant carrier is the existing non-event dispatch-error-record! path: one established production surface, frame attribution, no new security channel, no :on-reject protocol. Rejected alternative (accept dev-only, document): zero change, but the CRLF asymmetry persists and the security-posture docs (already corrected for over-claiming under rf2-ueopx) would have to state that redirect-probe rejections are unobservable in production — an honest sentence that reads worse than the fix costs.

(2) ALREADY LANDED (PR #7191 — this bead's original close). safe-redirect-tags builds the tag map ONCE so the two axes cannot disagree, applies egress/redact-url-tag to :location inside the builder, and emit-safe-redirect-error! fans BOTH axes: the always-on record via the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (no-op when unbound; non-event union shape with :error and :time assoc'd) plus the unchanged dev trace. Load-bearing adjacent correction: the three categories joined non-projection-eligible-errors, otherwise the default projector's :else arm stamps the locked generic 500 and a hostile ?next= becomes an attacker-triggered DoS — mutation-proved (remove the entries and all three wire arms go 500 under the gate). That skip also closed a MEASURED pre-existing dev/prod asymmetry: at prior HEAD, dev posture stamped 500 on a rejected javascript: redirect while production answered 200. Rejection semantics stay emit-and-no-op: :redirect nil, response status 200, no status mutation, no app callback. Witness: re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test (8 tests / 52 assertions), posture-independent, in the ssr prod-gate lane by default; pins one record per rejection, per-arm category/:reason, frame attribution, happy-path silence, closed key sets per arm.

(3) THE UNMET OBLIGATION — WHY REOPENED. The shipped egress shape is not fail-closed; verified directly against HEAD (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/egress.cljc): redact-url-carriers performs string surgery only after the first '?' or '#', and a URL with neither rides back VERBATIM through the "bare path — nothing to scrub" branch. Consequences, each confirmed: userinfo survives whole (https://alice:password@evil.example.com/private/reset-token ships verbatim), path-borne opaque secrets survive (the complete path of https://evil.example.com/path/opaque-secret?x=value ships), and value-less query keys are deliberately preserved (?secret-without-equals ships). safe-redirect-tags additionally ships the application's complete :allowlist (unbounded policy data) in the record. That is not EP-0008's "structured data only — never raw values" contract, and it is weaker than current telemetry guidance: OpenTelemetry URL semantic conventions (URI user/password information must not be recorded), OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet data-to-exclude (access tokens, passwords, sensitive values removed/masked/sanitized/hashed/encrypted), RFC 9110 §17.9 (URIs are commonly logged and can contain sensitive or personally identifiable information). Query-value scrubbing is the right blanket policy for ordinary route diagnostics over the app's OWN URL space (rf2-ov56u's route-miss :url); it is NOT a fail-closed projection of an arbitrary attacker-supplied foreign URL.

(4) THE REQUIRED SHAPE (Codex recommendation, adopted verbatim as the implementation contract). Preserve the existing dual fan-out and the three non-projection entries. Project a CLOSED STRUCTURAL MAP before dispatch-error-record!: the always-on record carries ONLY :error, :frame, :time, :recovery, a closed :reason, and the normalized parsed :scheme or :host on the arms where that component is the useful discriminator (scheme-rejected -> :scheme; host-disallowed -> :host). OMIT :location and :allowlist entirely. Replace the fixed parse-failure prose with a keyword such as :parse-failed. Structural tags only — no raw URL, ever. Losing the exact URL in production is a good trade: operators retain an aggregatable probe class and target host without accepting credentials, opaque path material, arbitrary query keys, or unbounded policy data. If richer local diagnosis later proves necessary, derive a separate diagnostic view deliberately; do not force the production record to inherit dev detail merely so both axes share one map (the dev trace may keep the scrubbed :location and :allowlist — the production record is a strict projection of the diagnostics, which is exactly the EP-0015 relationship). One record per rejection stays: keep the honest count and leave sampling/rate limits to the configured sink, which knows its cost policy — framework-global deduplication would add state, erase recurrence, and solve the problem at the wrong layer. Do NOT add an app event, change the HTTP response, create a fourth observability channel, or add framework rate-limiting.

(5) TEST OBLIGATIONS. Extend re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test (debug-off) with userinfo, path-secret, and value-less-query sentinels and assert they appear in NEITHER the corpus record NOR a frame sink. Keep the existing assertions (exactly one record, nil :redirect, status 200, no record on the passing path); the per-arm closed key sets shrink with the tightening — update them in the same PR. The rf2-dtpfv-blocked ssr-end-to-end-test posture split proceeds exactly as mapped in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh's roster comment (~17 safe-redirect diagnostic reds -> dev arms; the (nil? (:redirect ...)) rejection assertions are posture-independent and green under the gate today): always-on coverage is owned by the dedicated witness namespace, so the split does NOT need to convert those trace assertions to always-on.

(6) SPEC OBLIGATIONS (spec/009 is hot-zone — sequential, ride with rf2-rprfg's pass, never parallel): (a) the three catalogue rows move Channel diagnostic -> always-on together with the always-on-categories literal (rf2-rprfg's existing P1 scope); (b) record the narrow promotion-criterion exception — EP-0008 leg 2 reads "contract breach or resource leak", and a correctly rejected attacker-controlled redirect is neither; it earns promotion as an otherwise-invisible SECURITY-BOUNDARY REFUSAL. Record that exception, or broaden leg 2 explicitly to cover otherwise-invisible security-control activations; leaving the rows promoted while the governing criterion literally excludes them is avoidable conceptual debt; (c) the tightened per-category tag sets from (4) once that lands.

(7) OWNERSHIP AND CROSS-REFS. This bead owns (4)+(5) — single-artefact implementation/ssr, parallel-safe. rf2-rprfg owns (6). rf2-6l2nc still owns consolidating the duplicated egress helper into core beside re-frame.privacy — the tightening removes the production record's dependence on redact-url-carriers, but the dev trace and rf2-ov56u's route-miss :url still use the policy, so do not delete the helper. Sibling rf2-mwv4e (at-boundary rejections unobservable in production) is the same class on the same axis and is ruled in its own pass; if its shape (b) (promote :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :source :boundary) is chosen, it should follow THIS record discipline — closed structural map, no raw payload values — so the two egress reviews land as one precedent. Cross-referenced only; scopes stay separate.
TIGHTENING IMPLEMENTED — PR #7205 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7205), CI green (48 pass / 0 fail). NOT closing: the ruling says this bead 'must not re-close until it lands', and it was burned once by a close-on-PR-open. Close on MERGE.

WHAT LANDED (obligations (4) + (5)).

Record key set BEFORE -> AFTER, per arm:
  scheme-rejected  #{:error :time :recovery :frame :location :scheme}                      -> #{:error :time :recovery :frame :scheme}
  host-disallowed  #{:error :time :recovery :frame :location :host :reason :allowlist}     -> #{:error :time :recovery :frame :host :reason}
  parse-failure    #{:error :time :recovery :frame :location :reason}                      -> #{:error :time :recovery :frame :reason}

Leaks demonstrated against HEAD under -Dre-frame.debug=false before the fix, then shown absent. Verbatim record for https://alice:s3cr3t-userinfo-pw@evil.example.com/reset/s3cr3t-path-token?code=v&s3cr3t-bare-flag#frag with :allow [app.example.com s3cr3t-internal-admin.example.com]:
  BEFORE {:recovery :no-recovery :frame :rf.frame/19876 :location "https://alice:s3cr3t-userinfo-pw@evil.example.com/reset/s3cr3t-path-token?code=rf/redacted&s3cr3t-bare-flag#rf/redacted" :host "evil.example.com" :reason :not-in-allowlist :allowlist ["app.example.com" "s3cr3t-internal-admin.example.com"] :error :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed :time ...}
  AFTER  {:frame :rf.frame/19881 :reason :not-in-allowlist :host "evil.example.com" :recovery :no-recovery :error :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed :time ...}
Four secrets were shipping: userinfo password, path-borne reset token, attacker-chosen value-less query key, and both allowlist entries.

SHAPE. New egress/safe-redirect-record-slots = #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme :host}; egress/safe-redirect-record-tags BUILDS the record from that set rather than filtering down to it (an unrecognised tag has no path in even in principle), omits slots whose component did not parse, and lower-cases :scheme / :host so a case-alternating prober cannot fragment one spike across dashboard buckets (RFC 3986 s3.1 / RFC 1035 s2.3.3). Projection applied in dispatch-safe-redirect-record! — the one fn reaching the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record hook — so it is inseparable from the egress rather than a discipline the eight arms must remember. Dev trace keeps the rich scrubbed map; the record is a strict projection (the EP-0015 relationship). Parse-arm :reason prose -> :parse-failed.

Chose PROJECTION over a wider scrub deliberately: widening redact-url-carriers to cover userinfo + path leaves only scheme and host anyway, and stays a DENY-list — one URL component from the next leak. redact-url-carriers is NOT deleted (dev trace + rf2-ov56u route-miss :url still use it), per the ruling's note to rf2-6l2nc.

ELIGIBILITY SKIP UNTOUCHED — error_listener.cljc is not in the diff; the three categories stay in non-projection-eligible-errors.

GATES. witness ns under -Dre-frame.debug=false: BEFORE 14 failures / AFTER 13 tests 66 assertions 0 (exit 0). ssr full dev posture 564/2719 exit 0. scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh 486/2159, 49 of 51 ns, exit 0. core dev posture 2163/10745 exit 0. core targeted prod-posture egress namespaces 28/73 exit 0. Mutation: removing the projection reddens 12 assertions naming :location and :allowlist returning; restored, diff clean. (Whole core suite under the gate is ~1198 pre-existing dev-surface failures — proved identical with and without the diff; there is no whole-core production lane.)

SPEC OBLIGATION (6)(c) FILED AS rf2-ycbhx (P1) — rf2-rprfg had already CLOSED on PR #7192 so could not carry it. spec/009's three Tags columns still list :location (and :allowlist on host-disallowed), and the always-on paragraph still says the record carries a scrubbed :location; all now true of the DEV TRACE only. No conformance test reds meanwhile (always-on-categories is a CATEGORY set, unchanged; no SafeRedirect*Tags schema exists), so the drift is silent.
Audit of merged PR #7205: the closed-key projection still ships raw attacker-controlled VALUES in :scheme and :host. `safe-redirect-record-tags` lower-cases those values but does not bound or classify them. A rejected `s3cr3t-probe-token:payload` reaches the non-http(s) arm with `:scheme "s3cr3t-probe-token"`; an off-allowlist `https://s3cr3t-reset-token.evil.example/` ships that complete host. Both are legal URI components, both are chosen by the same untrusted `:location`, and both can carry secrets or create attacker-driven cardinality/record-size. The closed slot set therefore prevents new keys but does not establish the PR's claimed "no URL secrets" / bounded structural record. Existing tests cover secrets in userinfo/path/query and the app allowlist, but use fixed benign scheme/host values and cannot catch this value-level leak.

Bounded acceptance: make the always-on discriminators safe by construction (for example, closed scheme classes and an omitted/hashed/bounded host representation—choose the smallest shape that preserves useful aggregation), while leaving the richer dev trace and non-projecting wire behavior intact. Add real production-gate witnesses with sentinel material and oversized input in BOTH the scheme and host positions, asserting no raw sentinel and no attacker-sized/high-cardinality value reaches either captured record or frame sink. Reconcile the Spec 009 tag wording in the same sequenced pass or coordinate with the already-open rf2-rprfg; do not reopen the completed key-set documentation bead rf2-ycbhx merely to restate the current shape.

No duplicate bead.
close_reason:
BOUNDED-EGRESS TIGHTENING LANDED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342 (with rf2-rprfg + rf2-ycbhx, one PR, so spec and code never disagree).

THE AUDIT'S FINDING, ADDRESSED. PR #7205 closed the record's key SET but left two of its VALUES caller-authored, on the premise that a parsed URL component is structural. It is not: parsing locates a substring in the grammar and says nothing about who wrote it. Both survivors were the prober's to write — a scheme is arbitrary text under RFC 3986 s3.1, and a rejected host is BY DEFINITION one the app did not authorise.

WHAT LANDED. The record now carries CLASSES, not components.
  :scheme -> :scheme-class, a LOOKUP into egress/scheme-classes (the union of the gate's own rejected-schemes + allowed-schemes) with :other as the fallback. The caller selects a bucket and never spells one. Never (keyword attacker-string) — that would intern the caller's chosen name into the runtime, a leak with a longer half-life than the record. A scheme longer than the longest the gate knows is classed :other WITHOUT being lower-cased, so oversized input is measured rather than copied.
  :host -> DROPPED. Three facts settle it: on every arm that carried it, it is a name the app did not authorise (that is what :relative-only-violation and :not-in-allowlist mean); the framework has already refused the redirect, so no defensive action depends on reading it back; and it was the last unbounded caller-authored string in the record. title: Browser lane has a second, undocumented ceiling: Playwright's default 30s page.goto load timeout
description:
run-browser-tests.cjs does 'await page.goto(URL, { waitUntil: "load" })' with no explicit timeout, so Playwright's DEFAULT 30s applies. That is a second ceiling on the lane, entirely separate from BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS (now 360s, rf2-15047), and nothing documents it.

OBSERVED FIRING, locally, 2026-07-28 while measuring rf2-76lhy: first run of the full bundle died with

  page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
    navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:8021/", waiting until "load"
    at main (scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs:254)

21 namespaces had already run and printed. The immediately following runs of the identical bundle passed (exit 0, 855 tests, 0 failures), twice.

WHY IT IS THIN. shadow.test.browser starts running tests during page load, so the 'load' event cannot fire until the suite yields to the event loop. The capture-time profile shows namespace 27, re-frame.freehand.bench.b10-two-clock-dom-cljs-test, starting at +8.3s and occupying 35.9s - a wall-clock BURN sitting directly under the 30s ceiling. When the box is loaded enough that the first yield slips past 30s, the lane dies at goto, having produced no cljs.test summary and no failing assertion.

WHY IT MATTERS. The failure mode is nearly indistinguishable in a CI log from the summary timeout this lane already suffers, but it is a DIFFERENT ceiling and the 360s budget raise does not touch it. A CI log showing 'page.goto: Timeout 30000ms' would be misread as the known problem.

SUGGESTED: either pass an explicit timeout to page.goto tied to the same budget, or use waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' / 'commit' - the runner does not actually need subresources, it polls the console for the summary afterwards. Small, and in the same file as rf2-76lhy/rf2-u0cy4; deliberately NOT bundled into that PR, which was scoped to the diagnostics and the double-done verdict.

title: JS harness self-tests fail under concurrent worktree runs (shared in-tree fixture paths)
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-01 from worker/heapaxis-2rtt6-34 (rf2-2rtt6.34) while sibling workers were running suites in their own worktrees.

SYMPTOM. `bash scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` fails in the node tier with failures that CANNOT be reproduced standalone:

  run A: implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs -- 127 failed
         every failure an execFileSync('bash', ['-lc', ...]) returning non-zero,
         including a bare 'git ls-files -s -- scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh'
  run B: implementation/scripts/_transform-reagent-slim-ns.test.cjs -- 4 failed
         'abort: destination already exists -> non-zero exit (in-tree ns clash)'
         'abort: ns form not found -> non-zero exit (in-tree source restructured)'
         'fixture path handed to bash is relative + drive-letter-free, and
          resolves under cwd (rf2-6m7pn4)'

EVIDENCE IT IS NOT THE DIFF. The worker's diff touched only
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_*.{cljs,cjs} and two
docs/design/hicasso/studio/*.md -- it cannot reach either test's surface. Both
suites pass standalone at the same commit in the same worktree:

  node scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs            -> 275 passed, exit 0
  node scripts/_transform-reagent-slim-ns.test.cjs   -> 6 passed,   exit 0
  npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers -> exit 0, 0 FAIL

and the full spine went green on a re-run once no sibling was active.

HYPOTHESIS. These tests materialise fixtures at paths that are shared across
worktrees rather than scoped to the checkout -- the 'destination already
exists' and 'in-tree ns clash' wording points straight at it, and this repo
already writes to machine-global locations elsewhere (the spine log shows
STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML at 'C:\tmp\downstream\index.html', outside every
approved root). Two worktrees running the node tier concurrently then race
one directory. Mike runs 5-6 workers in parallel by design, so this is the
normal operating condition, not an edge case.

WHY IT MATTERS. It costs a worker a full spine cycle (~16 min) plus the
diagnosis to prove the failure is not theirs, and it trains agents to treat a
red gate as noise -- which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through.

SUGGESTED FIX. Scope every fixture root in implementation/scripts/_*.test.cjs
to a per-checkout temp dir (mkdtemp under the worktree, or keyed on the
worktree path), and assert no test writes to a machine-global path. Same
treatment for whatever hands out 'C:\tmp\downstream'.

title: CI: Maven Central 403s under concurrent-PR load break classpath resolution on the MCP conformance lanes
description:
OBSERVED TWICE on 2026-07-26/27 during a high-concurrency session (6-7 workers, 6+ open PRs), on two DIFFERENT artifacts:
  - org.jsoup:jsoup:jar:1.15.2 -> MCP conformance tools/story-mcp (PR #7117)
  - com.cognitect:transit-cljs:jar:0.8.280 -> MCP conformance wire-vocab (PR #7123), explicitly 'status code: 403, reason phrase: Forbidden' from https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/

SHAPE: 'Error building classpath. Failed to read artifact descriptor' / ArtifactDescriptorException / ArtifactTransportException. The classpath never builds, so the MCP server never starts, and the CLIENT-side symptom is 'FAIL: MCP error -32000: Connection closed' - which reads like a code fault and cost real diagnosis time twice.

Both cleared on a plain re-run, so it is transient, not a broken coordinate. 403 (not 404) points at rate-limiting/throttling of the runner rather than a missing artefact.

WHY IT MATTERS: it costs a re-run and a diagnosis every time, and the misleading downstream symptom invites a wrong conclusion - the first instinct is to suspect the diff. Under sustained parallel dispatch it will recur.

POSSIBLE REMEDIES, none investigated, deliberately not chosen here: cache the Maven/gitlibs dependency tree across jobs so the lanes stop re-resolving from central; use a mirror; or retry the classpath build specifically. DO NOT gold-plate - if dependency caching is already configured for other lanes and merely missing on these, that is the whole fix.

ACCEPTANCE: the MCP conformance lanes stop failing on artefact resolution under load, or - if that is not economically fixable - the failure names itself as an infrastructure fault rather than surfacing only as 'Connection closed'.

Filed by the mayor after diagnosing both instances; neither was a code defect.
notes:
Merged-PR audit of #7132: the pre-resolution wrapper retries every nonzero `clojure -P` exit and, after exhaustion, categorically annotates it as `INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff`. That includes deterministic diff-owned failures such as a malformed deps file or nonexistent coordinate; the PR's own failure-path check used a bogus coordinate, demonstrating the misclassification. Keep the bounded resolution-only retry, but make the final annotation cause-neutral (or classify only known transient transport signatures) so CI does not tell programmers to rerun a real dependency defect.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7221 (2026-08-01): reopen exact owner. The classifier still makes the categorical claim this bead was reopened to remove. TRANSIENT_SIGNATURES includes broad ArtifactTransportException/MetadataTransportException plus every 403, UnknownHostException, connection-refused, and 5xx; those strings justify a retry, but do not prove ownership. A diff-added auth-protected repository, misspelled repository host, or intentionally unavailable endpoint can emit the same signatures. Hermetic reproduction with an exported clojure stub printing ArtifactTransportException: authentication failed for repository configured by this change plus status code: 403 produced three attempts and the final INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff / not of any coordinate annotation. Keep the bounded retry for transport-looking failures, but make the exhausted verdict cause-neutral and quote the signature as evidence that a rerun may help, not as proof the diff is innocent. Add a hermetic classifier test for matched, unmatched, success, and changing-signature attempts; no retry framework or broad parser needed.
close_reason:
AUDIT REOPEN SCOPE FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7343.
Read the rest of this reason before treating the ORIGINAL acceptance as met —
part of it is not fixable from inside this repo, and that is a finding, not an
omission.

WHAT THIS PR FIXES (the #7221 audit's exact reopen scope). The exhausted
verdict no longer makes the categorical claim the audit demanded be removed.
It read `INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff` / `not of any coordinate`. A transport
signature earns a retry; it does not establish ownership. The audit proved the
gap hermetically: a stub emitting `ArtifactTransportException: authentication
failed for repository configured by this change` plus `status code: 403`
matched, was retried three times, and was then told it was not its own fault —
of a failure the diff owned outright.

Narrowing TRANSIENT_SIGNATURES cannot fix that: the ambiguity is in the
strings themselves, not in the list's width — a diff-added auth-protected
repository, a misspelled repository host and a dead endpoint all emit them. So
the list is UNCHANGED and the bounded retry is KEPT; the verdict changed. It
still quotes the signature as evidence a re-run may help, and now says what
that signature does not establish, pointing the reader back at any repository
or coordinate the change touched.

HERMETIC CLASSIFIER TEST ADDED, as the audit asked, covering all four named
cases and two more: success on the first attempt; transient-then-success;
UNMATCHED (not retried, no cause claimed); MATCHED-and-exhausted
(cause-neutral verdict); the audit's own diff-owned auth 403; and a signature
that CHANGES between attempts, which must be re-classified per attempt rather
than latched from the first. It stubs `clojure` (scripted per-attempt output)
and `sleep` (so 45s of real backoff costs nothing) onto PATH and runs the REAL
script — no network, no JVM, no retry framework, no broad parser. Two of the
six FAIL against the pre-fix wording, so it is not vacuous. It lives in
test:script-policy because that CI job is Node-only (no Maven), which is also
why it stubs rather than resolving anything.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND CANNOT BE FROM HERE. The 403 itself. It is Maven
Central throttling a shared CI egress IP under concurrent load. Dependency
caching was already ruled out as the missing piece and remains so: every MCP
conformance lane already restores ~/.m2 + ~/.gitlibs + ~/.deps.clj, and a
cache MISS (a deps.edn the PR touched, a cold key) is exactly when the lane
must go to Central, which is exactly when this fires. The remaining options
both cost real money or real repo weight and are maintainer decisions, not a
worker's:
  - a mirror/proxy (Artifactory, Nexus, or a GitHub Actions Maven proxy):
    removes the class outright, but needs a hosted service, credentials in CI,
    and an operational owner;
  - vendoring the dependency tree: removes the network entirely, at a large
    and ongoing repo cost.

Closing on the ACCEPTANCE's second limb, which is satisfied: the failure now
names itself at the resolution step rather than surfacing only as the
misleading downstream `FAIL: MCP error -32000: Connection closed`, and it no
longer tells a programmer to re-run a failure their own diff owns. If the
maintainer wants the mirror decision tracked, that is worth its own bead.

title: diag-value-summary leaks raw scalar prefixes and unbounded map keys into safe diagnostics
description:
FOUND auditing merged PR #7204. That PR deliberately routes malformed reserved-SSR-fx values through `re-frame.error/diag-value-summary` in BOTH the thrown message and ex-data, explicitly noting that a cookie `:value` may be a session token and claiming the summary carries shape, never value. The shared primitive does not meet that claim.

`diag-head` returns any scalar string of 24 characters or fewer verbatim and the first 24 characters of longer strings. Thus a short token/password is reproduced whole, while a longer bearer/session token leaks its raw prefix into exception messages, browser consoles, SSR host logs and ex-data before any record projector can classify it. The current test only proves a long fixture is not reproduced WHOLE and that its tail was truncated; it expressly accepts the raw prefix. The map leg separately returns every top-level key, uncapped and unsanitised. App/user-controlled map keys can therefore carry secret content and arbitrarily enlarge the supposedly bounded summary.

DEDUPLICATION: the durable note on closed rf2-zwgqe previously called out the unbounded map-key leg and explicitly said it needed a separate bead; no such Bead exists in the remote ledger. This issue owns both value-level failures of the one shared primitive rather than reopening that unrelated query-vector owner.

BLAST RADIUS: `diag-value-summary` is shared by core and mirrored into bundle-isolated adapter diagnostics (the source docstring names reagent-slim); audit all callers/mirrors. PR #7204 is a concrete always-on path, not the only possible egress.
acceptance_criteria: Make the summary genuinely content-safe and bounded: arbitrary strings/unknown scalars must not expose a raw prefix, and map summaries must not reproduce attacker/app-controlled key content or grow with an unbounded key set. Preserve only the minimal shape information callers actually need; if a structural identifier is required, pass it through an explicitly trusted field rather than guessing that arbitrary values are structural. Update every in-repo mirror and parity guard. Add dual-runtime witnesses using (1) a short secret, (2) a long secret whose first 24 characters are the sentinel, (3) sentinel-bearing dynamic map keys, and (4) a very large map; assert the serialized summary, thrown message and ex-data contain no sentinel and have a fixed bound. Include the PR #7204 `:rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid` path with a malformed cookie/header value so the production-facing use cannot regress.

Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7341 (branch worker/diagleak-210uq, 3 commits).

ENUMERATION FOUND FIVE PATHS, not the two named. Beyond the string :head and the map :keys the bead called out: (3) keywords/symbols got a :head with NO length bound at all, on the guess that such values are always structural -- (keyword user-string) is not; (4) numbers/booleans/unknown :scalar got a :head, and the :scalar leg called toString on a value the framework knows nothing about; (5) that same (str v) THREW on a hostile toString, so summarising an exploding value destroyed the failure it was describing, and the leaked :keys propagated the exploding object into whatever printed the ex-data. Paths 1/3/4/5 all traced to one helper (diag-head).

The summary is now {:type <closed-vocabulary keyword>} plus an integer :count for a counted collection or string, and nothing else -- content-free BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by redaction quality, so there is no prefix to bound, no key set to cap, and a FIXED serialized size whatever arrives. title: re-make-frame: an :initial-events flush inside upsert-frame! reprojects against the PREVIOUS pool and clobbers the just-installed generation
notes:
REPRODUCED and FIXED — PR #7197 (branch worker/initial-events-rt4jz).

REPRODUCTION (deterministic, no threads, no barrier — unlike the rf2-djkr0
sibling): implementation/core/test/re_frame/make_frame_generation_pool_window_jvm_test.clj
Create :pool-window/target against pool V1, destroy it (the provenance row
survives — documented residue), arm pending-reprojection? with a reg-* while a
decoy image-loaded frame stands, re-create the id against pool V2 with
:initial-events. Pre-fix: expected ::inc-v2, actual ::inc-v1; the V2-only
registration is not resolvable at all. The ROW ends up correct (V2) and the
GENERATION is wrong — that asymmetry is what made the clobber silent.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S FRAMING: the trigger is the CREATE branch, not the
re-register branch. upsert-frame! does NOT replay :initial-events on
re-registration (EP-0027 §Reset re-records, never replays), so the in-upsert
resolution that flushes exists only on a first/after-destroy creation. §2 of the
new ns pins that a construction with no setup steps is unaffected. The reload
test surfaced it because its first make-frame IS a create-with-:initial-events
against an id carrying an earlier case's provenance row.

FIX: write the provenance row BEFORE the engine commit, roll it back exactly on
failure (restore-frame-generation-pool! distinguishes "no row" from "a row whose
value is nil" — nil is a legitimate pool meaning the live store). rf2-ktmto9's
no-residue contract is now STATED rather than implied by ordering.

REORDERING vs SOMETHING ELSE, adjudicated: flush-at-top-of-make-frame only
narrows the window and does nothing for the JVM-concurrent instance; suppressing
the flush for the frame under construction needs a COUNTED under-construction
table to be exact under same-id contention (upsert's per-id transaction fails
the loser rather than queuing it, so a plain set lets the loser's exit clear the
winner's protection). Making the two writes effectively one is what closes it.

RESIDUAL, named at the site: on a re-construction the row names the incoming
pool for the interval before upsert's surgical swap installs the incoming
generation, so a JVM-concurrent flush there re-resolves the OUTGOING composition
against the INCOMING pool. Transient, overwritten unconditionally by the swap
that follows, never observable to a completed call; at worst one spurious
:rf.warning/reprojection-failed.

CLJS IS AFFECTED (the read-time flush is synchronous on both hosts) — this is
rf2-djkr0 inverted: that was a JVM-only defect with a common-code repair, this
is a common-code defect.

rf2-djkr0's CONDITIONAL mark KEPT, on measured evidence. Full 2x2: pre-fix +
conditional = reload green / repro RED; pre-fix + unconditional =
reload-swaps-generation-preserving-frame-memory RED at lines 152-153 (the exact
djkr0 observation); post-fix + conditional = both green; post-fix +
unconditional = green. So the unconditional form is now safe, but NOT adopted —
its remaining cost argument (a full reprojection sweep armed after every
construction) stands on its own. The site comment now says which leg it stands on.

NO SPEC PROMISE MOVED — spec/ and docs/ untouched; the provenance table is
private process-local defonce bookkeeping.

assertions); bash scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh 0 (1196 / 5530, 102 namespaces
— 101 + this PR's new ns, no regression); clojure -M:test:slow-test 0 (4 / 8);
neighbouring live-frame/hot-reload/seal-race suites 0 (47 / 231).

PR #7197 audit reopening (2026-08-01): the repair closes the single-threaded stale-row window, but its provenance write still happens before frame/upsert-frame! acquires the exact per-id construction reservation. A same-id JVM contender therefore mutates frame-generation-pool even though the engine rejects it with :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress. While the winner is inside its commit/initial-events cascade, that transient losing pool can be read by a reprojection and clobber the winner's generation; after rejection, the loser's unconditional restore can also overwrite a newer attempt's row if ownership changes before its catch runs. This contradicts the issue's claim that the record and provenance writes were made effectively one and the engine's zero-write admission-loss contract.

Acceptance: put provenance publication and rollback under the same exact per-id transaction as the frame revision, or fence both operations with identity/CAS ownership; a rejected/stale attempt must never publish or restore over the winning/current row. Add a deterministic JVM witness with distinct pools and a paused winner/loser showing the winner's row and generation stay consistent, plus successor-safe rollback and the existing absent-versus-recorded-nil failure cases. Preserve the synchronous :initial-events fix and run core dev, production-gate, slow/concurrency, and CLJS gates.
close_reason:
Audit reopening closed by PR #7344 (branch worker/frame-rt4jz, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7344).

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, confirmed: PR #7197 fixed the ORDER (row before commit) and left the ADMISSION wrong. upsert-frame! admits one construction per id and fails contenders with :rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress — a ZERO-WRITE loss by design. Writing the provenance row ahead of the commit put it ahead of that admission, so a rejected same-id contender published its own pool into the shared table on its way to being rejected; a reprojection (a READ, taking no reservation, on any thread) landing in that interval re-resolved the WINNER's live frame against the LOSER's pool and swapped it on. The rollback was the same defect reversed: an undo computed from a row read outside any reservation can land on a newer owner's row.

FIX (the acceptance's first option, not the CAS fallback): publication, commit and rollback now run inside ONE exact per-id reservation. New internal frame/call-with-frame-construction-claim! claims the id, arms the engine hand-off so upsert-frame! enters that same reservation instead of colliding with it, and compare-releases in finally. A loser throws BEFORE its first swap!; a winner cannot interleave with any other attempt on the id, so the row its rollback restores is still the row it displaced. ADOPTION: re-frame.ui's execute-frame-plans! claims its plan set up front and hands each id off — an UNSPENT hand-off is adopted as-is (nothing claimed, nothing released); a SPENT one is not, so the nested public entry loses normally, and now loses without publishing.

WITNESS (new ns, deterministic, JVM): implementation/core/test/re_frame/make_frame_generation_pool_contention_jvm_test.clj. Winner parks inside its construction transaction on frame/*upsert-decide-probe*; the reader reaches the exact instant of a transient publication through an atom WATCH on the provenance table (fires synchronously, on the writing thread, inside the swap!) and runs the real reproject-live-frame! there. Four cases: the reproduction; publication+rollback both holding the reservation; recorded-NIL restored as present-and-nil vs absent; hand-off adopted / spent-hand-off not.

MUTATION PROOF: revert the claim wrapper -> exit 1, all four deftests red (rejected contender logged 2 transitions AND the reader produced 2 real reload diffs, :changed #{[:event :pool-race/inc]} / :removed #{[:event :pool-race/reset]} — the winner's live frame really was swapped onto the loser's pool; publication+rollback :reserved? false; 3 transitions instead of 1 under the hand-off). Restore -> exit 0.

NO PINNED CONTRACT MOVED: upsert-frame!'s signature/arities, the typed error, its 'rf/make-frame where-sym and the reservation primitives are unchanged; the provenance table stays private process-local defonce bookkeeping; spec/ and docs/ untouched. Preserved the synchronous :initial-events fix (make-frame-generation-pool-window-jvm-test still green) and rf2-djkr0's conditional mark.

title: test-quiet shadow-node self-tests flake under concurrent-worker load (spawnSync ETIMEDOUT)
description:
OBSERVED on worker/durab-b0tz5 (rf2-b0tz5), 2026-08-01, four full `npm run test:cljs` runs on one unchanged tree.

SYMPTOM. Tests in implementation/test-quiet/test/ fail with the child runner never starting:
  spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe ETIMEDOUT
  --- stdout ---   (empty)
  --- stderr ---   (empty)
Failing tests seen: real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet, red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn,
unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner,
large-red-replay-is-not-truncated, large-replay-warns-then-fails-when-armed.

CAUSE. These tests spawnSync a nested out/node-test.js under a 60,000 ms ceiling
(spawn-timeout-ms, test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:348). The comment calls 60s
'generous' on the assumption that 'a correctly-exiting child returns in well under a
second'. That holds on an idle box. It does not hold when sibling worker worktrees are
running browser suites and shadow-cljs compiles on the same machine: the child is starved
and killed before it produces a byte.

EVIDENCE IT IS LOAD, NOT LOGIC.
  * failure count tracks box load on an IDENTICAL tree: 0 failures (quiet box) ->
    9 -> 18 (two siblings running browser tests) -> 9.
  * the root cause is always a wall-clock timeout, never a value assertion, and both
    child streams are empty, i.e. the child never ran.
  * the branch that observed it does not touch implementation/test-quiet/ at all.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is indistinguishable, at a glance, from a real regression: a worker
sees a RED test:cljs and cannot tell whether its own change broke something. It burns a
15-minute suite per retry and can push a worker toward a false 'my change is fine' or a
false 'main is broken'.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES (not a ruling, for triage):
  1. raise spawn-timeout-ms, or scale it from an env var CI/local can set;
  2. on ETIMEDOUT specifically, retry the spawn once before failing;
  3. treat an ETIMEDOUT with both streams empty as SKIP-with-diagnostic rather than FAIL,
     since it is a statement about the box and not about the runner contract.
Option 3 keeps the gate honest (it still says something went wrong) without minting a
false regression signal. Whichever is chosen, the 60s constant should stop being
described as generous without saying 'on an unloaded box'.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING. A --config-merge '{:ns-regexp ...}' focused compile shares the
node-test build id, so it leaves the cache in a mixed state and the NEXT full compile dies
with 'aborted par-compile ... still waiting for' and no root error. Same class as the
lane_cache.cjs rule the bench drivers already implement (one build id, N configs -> clear
the cache). Worth either documenting on the node-test build or clearing automatically.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7343

CAUSE — the ceiling rested on a premise that was never true of this build.
`spawn-timeout-ms` was 60000, and its docstring justified that with "a
correctly-exiting child returns in well under a second". `out/node-test.js`
is a dev-mode LOADER: every spawn re-`require`s the whole consolidated
node-test output, measured on this tree at 4201 modules / 484 MB. Timing the
exact child `spawn-runner` makes:

  idle box            10.0 s, 11.1 s, 13.3 s      (all exit 0)
  under sibling load  30.5 s, 87.3 s, 112.4 s,
                      448.9 s                     (all exit 0)

So the 60 s ceiling was not catching wedged children — it was killing HEALTHY
ones, ~5x below the worst honest case. The resulting `spawnSync ... ETIMEDOUT`
with both child streams empty is indistinguishable at a glance from a runner
the diff broke, which is exactly why it cost diagnoses, and why the bead's
failure count tracked box load on an unchanged tree (0 -> 9 -> 18 -> 9).

A/B UNDER IDENTICAL LOAD. Same binary, same load generator, same suite; only
the ceiling differs (the old value reinstated through the new env var, so the
BEFORE arm is the pre-fix build in every respect that matters):

  ceiling  60 s (pre-fix)   35 failures, 20 ETIMEDOUT
  ceiling 300 s             4 failures,  2 ETIMEDOUT
  ceiling 600 s (SHIPPED)   0 failures,  0 ETIMEDOUT   (wall 2396 s)

The 600 s arm ran essentially wholly under load — 2396 s of suite against a
2400 s load window — and carried a provenance guard proving the bundle under
test really contained the 600000 ms constant (v1 of that arm was discarded
BECAUSE its compile had failed under load and it silently measured a stale
bundle; see rf2-6t03c).

Load used was HARSHER than the field: 32-48 CPU burners plus 6 I/O and
process-churn loops on 24 cores. The pre-fix arm produced 20 ETIMEDOUT
against the field's worst observation of 18.

WHY THIS IS NOT TOLERANCE. The fail-fast contract is pinned separately and
strictly by `spawn-timeout-kills-a-hanging-child`, which proves a
never-exiting child is SIGTERM-killed using its OWN 1.5 s ceiling. This
constant only bounds how long a wedged child may stall the suite before that
same mechanism ends it, so raising it costs nothing in strictness. An
ETIMEDOUT remains a FAILURE — a run whose child never started has verified
nothing, and downgrading it to a skip (candidate remedy 3 in this bead) would
be a fail-open gate. Candidate remedy 2 (retry on ETIMEDOUT) was rejected for
the same reason: it would hide a genuine hang.

WHAT CHANGED, then: the ceiling is 600 s (set above the slowest HEALTHY child
actually measured, 449 s — not a round number), overridable via
RF2_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, with a malformed override THROWING rather than falling
back; the docstring carries the measurements instead of the false claim; and
the ETIMEDOUT diagnostic now names the ceiling, the knob, and what the child
was doing, so a reader can tell an oversubscribed box from a defect in their
change. The ten copies of that assertion message route through one helper.

SECOND FINDING SPLIT OUT to rf2-6t03c, and BROADENED there: the
`aborted par-compile ... still waiting for` failure reproduced on this tree
with NO --config-merge at all — heavy load alone is sufficient — and it
silently left a stale bundle in play for a caller that did not check the
compile's exit code. Its fix belongs in the hot-zone shadow-cljs.edn, so it
is sequenced separately.

GATES: test:cljs exit 0 (12256 tests, 61283 assertions, 0 failures),
test:browser exit 0 (931 tests), test:script-policy exit 0,
test:script-helpers exit 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors 0 (zero findings on
the changed file). Full CI on #7343: 56 pass / 26 skipping / 0 fail.

title: machines-viz value-free-summary leaks unbounded map keys and raw keywords from a forged share URL
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-210uq (diag-value-summary disclosure). tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/share.cljs carries value-free-summary, an INDEPENDENT hand-rolled EP-0015 shape summariser for share-URL decode errors. It is not a mirror of re-frame.error/diag-value-summary (so rf2-210uq did not touch it), but it reproduces the same two defects rf2-210uq removed, over an input the function's OWN docstring describes as attacker-controlled:

  (map? v)     {:type :map :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys v))) :count (count v)}
  (keyword? v) {:type :keyword :value v}

1. The :keys leg returns every top-level key, uncapped and unsanitised. The docstring says 'a forged share URL can smuggle :snapshot {:data ...} / arbitrary runtime values' -- so the key set is attacker-chosen, both in CONTENT and in SIZE, and it rides into a thrown ex-info that names itself value-free.
2. The keyword leg returns the raw keyword as :value, justified inline by 'a keyword IS a state name/address, not data'. That is the same guess rf2-210uq rejected in core: (keyword attacker-string) is not structural, and the leg applies no length bound.

rf2-210uq's ruling for the core primitive was to make the summary content-free BY CONSTRUCTION -- a closed :type vocabulary plus an integer :count, nothing else -- rather than bound a raw prefix. The same argument applies here, and this input is less trusted than core's.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THE rf2-210uq PR: different artefact, different tree (tools/, bundle-isolated from production per CLAUDE.md), its own gates (tools_jvm_machines_viz / cljs-tools-machines-viz), and the keyword :value leg carries an explicit inline design justification that deserves its own ruling rather than a drive-by change.

NOT IN SCOPE (checked, different primitive): tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp's :rf.mcp/summary marker and its mcp-conformance wire-vocab schema deliberately ship :keys and a scalar :value as a documented cross-MCP dev-tool wire protocol. That is a token-budget marker, not an EP-0015 redaction primitive.

ACCEPTANCE: make value-free-summary content-free by construction or state why the share-decode path warrants keys; add a witness with a forged-URL payload carrying sentinel-bearing keys and an attacker-sized key set, asserting no sentinel in the thrown message or ex-data and a fixed serialized bound.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7345 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7345), merged as 71d18ca62a. NO RULING NEEDED on the keyword leg: its inline justification was read, and it does not survive its own threat model — see below.

FIVE PATHS, not the two the bead named. I walked the summariser leg by leg and then walked the ex-data of every throw site in the namespace:
1. :keys on a map — every top-level key, uncapped/unsanitised, attacker-chosen in CONTENT and SIZE; removing it also removed the (sort-by str (keys v)) that ran str over caller-supplied keys, where a key with a THROWING toString replaced the documented ex-info with its own exception (the rf2-210uq path-5 shape, reproduced here and witnessed).
2. keyword :value — raw, unbounded.
3. {:url url} on :malformed-fragment — the WHOLE caller URL, raw. NOT IN THE BEAD. The encoder forty lines up already refuses to record :host because 'a viewer URL can carry a query string with a token in it' (rf2-8nzxib, hence :fragment-index); the decoder — handed URLs from elsewhere, so the more exposed side — carried the lot.
4. :cause (.-message e) on the base64 + transit stages — NOT IN THE BEAD, and a leak nobody wrote: transit/read calls JSON.parse and V8 embeds a prefix of its input in the SyntaxError (Unexpected token 'h', "hunter2-sw"... is not valid JSON), so the slot named for the cause republished the payload's plaintext.
5. :payload-version — NOT IN THE BEAD. The forged :v, raw and unbounded, reachable with arbitrary content through the string-compare fallback as well as the numeric path.

THE KEYWORD LEG'S JUSTIFICATION, quoted: '; a keyword IS a state name/address, not data'. It is a real argument — allowlist-chart-state says almost exactly that of :snapshot's :state — but it does not hold HERE, for three reasons all visible in the same file: (a) this function is NEVER handed a :state; its three call sites pass the whole chart-state / envelope / chart; (b) the leg therefore fires only when the payload is not the shape it was meant to be, i.e. when someone forged it — its premise is false exactly in the situation that runs it; (c) transit decodes ~:<anything> into a keyword of any length, namespace and content, with no bound applied anywhere. So brief-option (a): fixed, not escalated. The reasoning is recorded in the docstring so the next reader meets the decision rather than its absence.

REMOVED, NOT BOUNDED: :keys, the keyword :value, :cause, the raw :url. The summary is now a :type from a closed vocabulary plus an integer :count and nothing else — content-free BY CONSTRUCTION, fixed serialized size whatever arrives. KEPT: size/cardinality (an integer cannot carry a token fragment, and '2000-key map where an envelope was expected' IS the diagnosis) and the version, as the INTEGER the comparison used (nil when :v did not parse). Vocabulary aligned with re-frame.error/diag-value-summary (:length->:count, :value->:scalar, :symbol/:fn added) — still an independent implementation, not a mirror, but no reason for the two to disagree about what to call a set.

THE CAPSTONE IS A GRAMMAR, NOT A SENTINEL HUNT — which is the point, because the section it joins already claimed to assert this and passed anyway: it planted a secret in a VALUE position and walked STRINGS only, so leaked keyword KEYS were invisible to it. Now: content-free-summary? (key set subset of #{:type :count}, :type in the closed vocabulary, :count a non-negative integer), discloses? (pr-str of the whole ex-data and the thrown message must contain no 8-CHARACTER WINDOW of the sentinel — a fragment proves a leak, since a host parser message discloses exactly a prefix), and a fixed serialized bound (summary <48 chars, ex-data <600) against ~50 KB payloads, plus a growth pin: a 2000-key forged envelope throws ex-data at most 4 characters larger than a 2-key one. A sixth leak fails those with nobody planting a sentinel for it.

ADVERSARIAL CORPUS: sentinel-bearing keys of every key type transit carries (string, keyword, namespaced keyword, symbol, vector, MAP-as-key, number, boolean); keys that are <script> markup, an ANSI escape, CR/LF and a NUL byte; a 2000-key map; a keyword built from a 20x-repeated sentinel; a 4004-char string; a 16-digit card number; nesting; a lazy seq; a live fn; an opaque host object; a host object whose toString THROWS and a map KEYED by one; a URL with the sentinel in a query string; a fragment decoding to sentinel-bearing non-transit; forged :v on both the numeric and the string-compare paths.

MUTATION PROOF, witnesses written and watched failing FIRST: machines-viz-node-test exit 1 with 50 failures / 0 errors on unmodified share.cljs (the log prints the whole leaked key set verbatim, ANSI and markup included, and :rf.error/id nil for the exploding key — the summariser destroying the failure it was called to describe), exit 0 with 832 tests / 3470 assertions / 0 failures after.

GATES, all foreground, all re-run after rebasing onto a main that had moved 16 commits, all repeating their result: cljs-tools-machines-viz rc=0 (832/3470, compile 250 files 0 warnings), tools_jvm_machines_viz rc=0 (632/2537), scripts/test-fast-pr.sh rc=0 (PASS fast PR spine; consolidated node suite 12263/61442), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 at CI's flags rc=0 errors:0 (4527 warnings, all pre-existing), check_doc_slugs.py rc=0. The rf2-hofhx load flake did not appear in either spine run. tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md gained a 'What the thrown ex-data may carry' section; mkdocs does not cover that tree (no machines-viz entry, not under docs/), so check_doc_slugs.py is its gate and the added table's column counts + the new anchor were verified by hand.

FILED, NOT FIXED: rf2-oztox (P2) — grammar/definition-summary is the THIRD independent summariser in the repo and carries the same :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys definition))) leg over definitions arriving from forged share URLs, LLM responses and SCXML/Mermaid input. title: test-quiet spawn harness flakes under concurrent load: spawnSync ETIMEDOUT at the 60s ceiling, red on main locally
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-01 while gating rf2-6jqa8 in a worker worktree, with sibling workers in flight.

`npm run test:cljs` reds in the `implementation/test-quiet` spawn harness. Every failure cascades from one assertion — `(is (nil? err))` where err is `spawnSync <node.exe> ETIMEDOUT`. That harness re-spawns `out/node-test.js` as a child to exercise the real CLI path end-to-end; `spawn-timeout-ms` (test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs ~line 348) is a fixed 60000, and the child loads the WHOLE consolidated bundle before it can answer.

MEASURED, three runs, same machine, same session:
  with the rf2-6jqa8 diff, cold : 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 35 failures, 6 namespaces
  with the rf2-6jqa8 diff, warm : 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 16 failures, 3 namespaces
  at origin/main (diff reverted in-tree): 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 14 failures, 3 namespaces

ATTRIBUTION IS SETTLED, and by measurement rather than assertion. The test and assertion COUNTS are identical across all three, so no diff adds or removes a cljs test; the only variable is which spawn happens to hit the ceiling. The failing namespaces differ between runs and only PARTLY overlap (real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet / unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green / unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner versus deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero / large-red-replay-is-not-truncated / red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn). That is what a load-dependent timeout looks like; a semantic regression does not move around. It is red at origin/main with no diff at all.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERE NOISE. This is a false RED, and the class it belongs to is the one this repo keeps finding on the other side. A gate whose verdict depends on machine load teaches everyone to discount it, and a discounted gate is one that gets waved through on the day it is telling the truth. The harness is also load-bearing in its own right: it is the guard against a false GREEN in the runner itself (unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner).

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed. The ceiling is a wall-clock constant standing in front of a whole-bundle load, so it measures the machine as much as it measures the child. Options include scaling it, distinguishing 'timed out' from 'answered wrongly' at the ASSERTION level (the harness already captures :timed-out? but the assertions read :error / :status, so a timeout presents as a content failure with an empty 'got:'), or having the spawn tier skip rather than fail when it cannot get a scheduling slot. Whoever takes it should decide which option keeps the false-green guard intact, since that is the property worth protecting.

CROSS-REF: matches the durable 'CI flaky gates under load' pattern. Filed from the rf2-6jqa8 / rf2-rprfg / rf2-ycbhx gating pass (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342), whose own JVM surfaces are green and whose cljs delta is nil.
close_reason: RESOLVED BY rf2-hofhx (PR #7343, merged). Same defect, observed independently: test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test's spawn-timeout-ms was a fixed 60000 ms, and the child it spawns re-requires 4,201 modules / 484 MB — 10-13 s idle but 30.5 / 87.3 / 112.4 / 448.9 s under concurrent-worker load, EVERY ONE EXITING 0. The 60 s ceiling was killing healthy children roughly 5x below the worst honest case. Verified on main: default-spawn-timeout-ms is now 600000 (line ~391), env-tunable, with the diagnostic still failing RED rather than passing. A/B under identical load: 60 s -> 35 failures/20 ETIMEDOUT; 300 s -> 4/2; 600 s -> 0/0 across a 2396 s suite in a 2400 s load window. Closed as duplicate rather than dispatched — verified by reading main, not by memory.

title: SSR: the boundary rejection now projects 400 under the gate — correct the stale listener comment and add the witness (follows rf2-mwv4e)
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-mwv4e (PR #7203). implementation/ssr/** was fenced (two live workers), so the worker verified by reading and reported rather than edited.

WHAT rf2-mwv4e CHANGED FOR SSR. A boundary rejection now fans an always-on STRUCTURAL-ONLY record `{:error :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :event :source :boundary :event-id :failing-id :schema-id :frame :recovery :time}`. Verified against HEAD by reading, NOT by running the SSR lane:
  - `error_listener.cljc` `error-emit-projection-listener` lifts EVERY non-`:error` slot generically onto `:tags`, so `:where :event` arrives where the projector looks.
  - `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` is NOT in `non-projection-eligible-errors` (verified at error_listener.cljc:137-144), so the record buffers for projection.
  - `error_projector.cljc` line ~222 gates the 400 arm on `(= :event (get-in trace-event [:tags :where]))` — which the record satisfies. So a boundary rejection on a server frame answers 400, closing the silent-200 hole that surfaced rf2-mwv4e.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from rf2-6jqa8, worth keeping straight: those three safe-redirect categories are NON-projection-eligible (a hostile probe must not conjure a 500). This one SHOULD project — a refused request payload is exactly a 400 (RFC 9110 s15.5.1).

(1) THE STALE COMMENT, and it is load-bearing prose rather than a nit — its own docstring calls itself 'the authoritative statement of which categories ride which bus'. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc` ~334 currently reads: 'Two projection-eligible categories ride the dev bus ALONE and therefore elide under interop/debug-enabled? = false: :rf.error/no-such-route ... and :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (boundary validation is itself production-elided per Spec 010 SSProduction builds, so no production reject exists to project).' Both halves of that parenthesis were already wrong before rf2-mwv4e (the CHECK was never elided — only its emit; rf2-mnmzh and rf2-bx4bf corrected the same overclaim elsewhere), and the sentence is now wrong outright: the boundary arm rides BOTH buses. Move it into the 'the rest arrive on BOTH buses' paragraph beside `:rf.error/no-such-handler`.

(2) THE WITNESS, which does not exist in any lane. Under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, a server frame dispatching an event whose handler references `:rf.schema/at-boundary` with a non-conforming payload must answer 400, with sibling-frame attribution intact. Model on `re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test` (posture-independent, in the ssr prod-gate lane by default). Assert: exactly one always-on record, status 400 on the wire, the record carries NOTHING from the rejected payload (use a sentinel), and a CONFORMING payload leaves the response untouched. Coordinate with rf2-dtpfv / rf2-lwtlk, which are live in this artefact.

(3) CHECK THE DEV/PROD SYMMETRY while you are here. rf2-6jqa8 uncovered a measured dev/prod wire asymmetry on its surface (dev stamped 500 via the trace-cb buffering path while production answered 200). Here BOTH buses now carry the rejection in dev, and `consume-pending-traces!` + last-write-wins should make the duplicate benign — but that is reasoned, not measured. Measure it: assert the dev arm answers 400 too, and that the duplicate buffering does not double-stamp.

TEST-ONLY / COMMENT-ONLY; no behaviour change is being requested in ssr src.

title: API manifest silently ignores a newly added public Freehand namespace
description: PR #7212 documents but does not close the recurrence class it repaired: api-manifest gen inspects only the explicit jvm-namespaces list, and doc_api_check derives coverage from the resulting manifest. A newly shipped public re-frame.freehand.* namespace omitted from both therefore leaves gen --check and doc-api-check green while every public var disappears from the manifest/API docs. This happened for re-frame.resources and again for splitter plus collection (21 names); the current sweep is only point-in-time. Add one narrow completeness gate around the explicit roster. Keep intentional classification and do not auto-publish implementation namespaces: every Freehand source namespace must be accounted for as supported/public or deliberately internal/excluded, and an unaccounted new namespace must fail with its name and required classification step. No open matching Bead exists; rf2-h0b0l and rf2-cfhuv are closed point repairs, while rf2-m41gl owns only CLJS cross-host reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A test/mutation adding a synthetic public Freehand namespace without classifying it makes the manifest gate fail before generation/doc checks can silently omit it. Every current Freehand source namespace is accounted for as supported/public or intentionally internal; internal and ^:no-doc plumbing are not auto-enrolled. Failure output names the namespace and one remediation path. Existing explicit roster and generated docs remain authoritative; no broad reflection framework or automatic public-API inference.
close_reason:
The api-manifest generator now reconciles every namespace under implementation/freehand/src against two rosters — the public one it introspects (jvm-namespaces) and an explicit internal one — and refuses to build the manifest when a source namespace is named by neither, failing with the namespace's name and both remediation paths. The assertion runs FIRST in build-manifest, before the three sidecar reconciliations, because all of those read jvm-namespaces and so can only report on namespaces the roster already names. Reconciliation is symmetric: unaccounted, stale internal entry, and both-rosters-at-once each fail. It infers nothing — no namespace is auto-enrolled and no var auto-published; only the OBLIGATION to classify is automated (^:no-doc could not have been the classifier: only 6 of 61 internal namespaces carry it).

MUTATION-PROVEN: a throwaway public re-frame.freehand.mutation-probe made 'clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check' exit 2 naming the namespace; reverting returned exit 0 with a clean git diff (baseline exit 0 first). The new test namespace was proven non-vacuous by inverting an assertion (clojure -M:test exit 1 naming the test) and reverting (exit 0); nine tests cover all three drift arms, the missing-root case, the file->namespace munge and a synthetic tree driven end-to-end through build-manifest.

NOTHING SLIPPED THROUGH while it was blind: the enrolled set is exactly the door plus the six siblings spec/Conventions.md §Freehand holds as the roster of record, and a test now pins that equality. Recorded rather than hidden: re-frame.freehand.evidence and .presence-runtime are required by TOOL production source (xray mounted_views, story presence_host) and evidence/schema is named in a normative Conventions row — classified internal here because §Freehand does not list them; whether a tool-consumed seam earns a :tooling row like re-frame.mcp-base.elision is left to that roster's owner.

title: Three skill sites teach the blanket — shadow-cljs.md names BOUNDARY validation as the thing stripped in production
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-4engi sweep (PR #7199). Same class as rf2-4engi / rf2-bx4bf / rf2-mnmzh, outside that bead's fence.

The blanket "all schema validation is elided in production" is FALSE — `:rf.schema/at-boundary` is ungated and runs on every build, as do recordable-coeffect `:schema`, managed-HTTP `:decode`, and `validate-route-shape`. THREE SKILL SITES still teach the blanket, and because this project is explicitly AI-first, a wrong blanket in a skill is guidance an agent follows literally.

SITES:
  - skills/re-frame2-setup/references/shadow-cljs.md:180 — THE WORST INVERSION IN THE SWEEP. "re-frame2's `:advanced`-compile elision contract (Spec 009) automatically strips dev-only diagnostics (`trace`, `epoch-history`, **schema validation at boundary**) when `goog.DEBUG` is false". It names *boundary* schema validation as the exact thing that gets stripped. at-boundary is the one check that provably survives — this tells an author setting up a production build the precise opposite of the truth. Fix first.
  - skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/schemas.md:50 — "It survives the production gate and is **the only schema surface that does**." Inverse form of the blanket: "the only" excludes managed-HTTP `:decode`, `validate-route-shape`, the recordable-cofx `:schema` hard error, and the always-on registration-time shape checks. This is the file skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:74 points at as "the full behaviour matrix", so it is load-bearing.
  - skills/shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md:17 — ADJACENT, not a validation claim but the same over-correction: the `app-schemas` row is marked `dev-gated`. Per spec/010:92 a production build still performs the REGISTRATION — "`app-schema-at` and `(rf/app-schemas)` keep answering, so tools and agents introspect exactly the same shapes". With this file's own legend at :27 defining `dev-gated` as "elided under `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`", the row tells a tool author that schema reflection goes dark in production when it does not. Should be `portable`.

Skill guidance must work for ANY consumer re-frame2 app — generic mechanism, repo specifics only as examples.

WATCH THE DRIFT GUARDS: scripts/check_skill_*.py. A skills edit will likely trip one — fix it honestly rather than loosening an assertion. (rf2-4engi's own skills edit tripped none; all 15 passed.)

COLLISION NOTE at filing time: PR #7167 (staged alpha-tag) holds skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md and skills/re-frame2-setup/references/{deps-versions,entry-namespace}.md — NOT references/shadow-cljs.md. Re-check before dispatch.

SCOPE: doc prose only. Do NOT weaken the reg-app-schema dev-only posture — settled (rf2-bkvu5) — and do not presume a remedy for the observability question (rf2-mwv4e, open). Change no code.

VERIFIED CORRECT — do NOT touch: skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:74; skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md:121; skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md; skills/re-frame2/patterns/{forms,remote-data}.md; skills/re-frame2/decision-trees/slice-or-machine.md:98. skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md was corrected by rf2-4engi.

title: hicasso: instrument the per-read heap axis early -- the one axis where the ruled architecture can beat its own parent by design
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). This is a "what
survived" bead: the axis the review could not break, and the one it recommends
the clock be spent on.

THE SITUATION. The per-read gates (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:136-140),
both on the mandatory distinct-query witness (Q = E), as marginal slopes:

  UIx material-cost red-zone   2,935 B/read  [2,852-3,055]
  K3, Reagent-sourced            943 B/read  [935-944]

and the record's own sentence: "943 B/read remains the number a native layer
actually has to beat."

WHY THIS AXIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE CLOCK ROWS. On mount, the ruled parent is at
parity with Reagent (1.0243x) and Hicasso's product delta is a tax on top -- the
review's central objection. On bulk-broad the parent already wins (0.6291x) and
Hicasso only has to not squander it. Per-read heap is the ONE axis where the
ruled architecture is structurally CHEAPER than the parent it is built on rather
than more expensive:

  - the parent pays N `useSyncExternalStore` hook cells per boundary;
  - Hicasso pays ONE hook per boundary plus edges in a SHARED GLOBAL INDEX --
    "Index edges live in global maps -- shared structure, not per-boundary
    object fan-out" (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:33-35).

That is a difference in kind, not in tuning. The parent's 2,935 B/read is
roughly 3.1x Reagent's 943; the grouped tier's own win condition already concedes
~2,000 B/read with a paper path down (validation.md:245-246). If one hook plus a
shared edge lands materially below 2,000, that is the programme's first
unambiguous structural win over BOTH comparators, and it is available before any
clock row is settled.

WHAT TO DO. Extend the existing reads-per-boundary heap ladder
(docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md, rf2-2rtt6.5) with
a HICASSO-SHAPED rung: one subscription/epoch hook per boundary plus N edges in
a shared index, at 1/3/7/20 reads, distinct-query (Q = E), against the SAME
instrument the gates are stated on (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs -- validation.md
:180-189 is explicit that a candidate is judged against the donor row taken on
its OWN instrument, and that a margin under 5% is instrument-limited rather than
cleared).

Report: the marginal slope, the shell intercept, and zero retained
per-occurrence objects after commit/teardown (the HD-002 survival metric,
decisions.md:55-56).

WHY NOW. It does not need the collector, the codec, the dogfood screen, or the
mount row. It needs a hook, an index and a ladder that already exists. It is the
cheapest evidence in the programme that the ruled architecture has an axis it
wins on its own merits, and it is measurable inside week one of K7.

(validation.md:80-82). This bead is filed against that deferral, not around it
-- it needs a release before dispatch.
