title: hicasso: enter Freehand's codec as a fourth donor arm before writing a third interpreter
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31).

WHY. HD-008's verdict is that "the residual mount deficit is the hiccup
interpreter rather than the spine" (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:238). But
the arm it measured was reagent-slim's interpreter, and it read
`donor-r1 / reagent-slim` = 1.000-1.120, i.e. INDISTINGUISHABLE from
reagent-slim itself (docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:239).
So what HD-008 actually established is that *reagent-slim's* interpreter is the
deficit. This repository contains a SECOND runtime hiccup interpreter that was
never entered in that comparison:

  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs   (1,203 lines)
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/conversion.cljc (906 lines)

conversion.cljc is the profile-driven, bounded js/Map-backed codec cache
(new-cache 111-114, remembered 116-130) that PR #7077 built after caller
attribution; docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md
:277-281 names exactly that mechanism as the proven shape of the win.

WHAT TO DO. Add a fourth arm to the HD-008 instrument
(implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_*): Freehand's
`react/element` codec driving the SAME `:f>` function-component boundaries and
the SAME UIx `use-subscribe` spine as `donor-r1`, on the SAME M and U witnesses,
in the same run. Everything except the codec held fixed. Canonical-DOM parity
gates it as usual.

WHAT IT ANSWERS. The single question the mount row turns on: is the deficit
"hiccup interpretation" or "reagent-slim's hiccup interpretation"? The published
figures make it decidable -- `donor-r2 / uix` is 1.162-1.286 on mount-M and
1.125-1.222 on mount-U (hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:231,253), and win condition
(1) asks for a codec inside 1.10x direct UIx `$` (validation.md:240-241). A
Freehand-codec arm either lands inside that band or it does not, and either
answer is worth more than six weeks of writing a third interpreter to find out.

FENCES. Instrument-only, bench lane (HD-017 carve-out). No shadow-cljs build id
(ride :hicasso-bench via the existing route). Do NOT edit
implementation/freehand/src -- the donor freeze stands; a bench arm may
`:require` it. Publish to docs/design/hicasso/studio/ and to this bead with the
producing commit SHA and reproduction command per validation.md:335.
notes:
MEASURED AND PUBLISHED (worker, rf2-2rtt6.29). Freehand's codec is entered as
HD-008's FOURTH DONOR ARM. Two full three-run sweeps, both exit 0, every gate
green. Studio page: docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-freehand-codec-donor-arm.md

=== THE ANSWER: FREEHAND'S CODEC IS MATERIALLY WORSE THAN REAGENT-SLIM'S ===

donor-fh / donor-r1 is THE CODEC RATIO — the boundary (slim's own :f>), the
outer skeleton, the single use-subscribe hook at its two-arity form with the
frame PINNED, the dispatch-for lookup, the author's handler closure, the page,
the floor arm, the rounds and the interleaving schedule are all held FIXED.
Only the codec that builds the markup inside the 300 boundaries varies: 900 of
the M page's 903 elements and 300 of the U page's 301.

Over both sweeps:

  write-narrow  1 boundary re-renders    0.898 - 1.143   INDISTINGUISHABLE 2/2
  mount-U       300 bnd x 1 el, + mount  0.973 - 1.363   disjoint above 1.0, 5/6
  mount-M       300 bnd x 3 el, + mount  1.078 - 1.306   disjoint above 1.0, 6/6
  write-bulk    300 bnd re-rendered      1.273 - 1.550   disjoint above 1.0, 2/2

Not one of the sixteen codec ranges sits disjointly BELOW 1.0, so nothing in
the record says Freehand's codec is ever the faster of the two. The gap tracks
how much of the window is markup construction, which is exactly what a codec
difference should do.

AGAINST RAW UIX (the comparison the operator asked for, since the mount bar is
suspended):
  donor-fh   mount-M 1.358 - 1.746   mount-U 1.127 - 1.655   bulk 1.722 - 2.000
  donor-r1   mount-M 1.179 - 1.373   mount-U 1.051 - 1.328   bulk 1.111 - 1.429
Both indistinguishable from uix on the narrow row.

AGAINST THE SHIPPING PATHS, sweep 1: donor-fh / reagent 1.391 - 1.625 (M) and
1.322 - 1.425 (U); donor-fh / reagent-slim 1.018 - 1.237 (M) and 1.036 - 1.135
(U). For scale in the same runs, donor-r1 / reagent 1.172 - 1.278 and
donor-r1 / reagent-slim 0.900 - 0.979.

=== WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THE PROGRAMME ===

1. HD-008's conclusion SURVIVES and is now quantified rather than inferred.
   "The residual mount deficit is the hiccup interpreter" was drawn from a row
   (donor-r1 / reagent-slim = 1.000-1.120) that is INDISTINGUISHABLE, so it
   established only that reagent-slim's interpreter is the deficit. Swapping
   ONLY the interpreter now moves mount-M by up to 31% and bulk re-render by up
   to 55%. Interpretation is the dominant term a codec controls.

2. "CONSUME FREEHAND'S CODEC RATHER THAN AUTHOR ONE" IS NOT A FREE WIN, and
   this arm makes that decidable without six weeks of work. On these witnesses
   it is the worse of the two codecs already in the tree. That does not make it
   the wrong codec to consume - it is also the more capable one (per element it
   asks the controlled-input door, the v/spread-safe caller split, the DOM
   top-layer pair, the declared custom-element property set, the id-slot
   cardinality check and the exact-first class/style alias composition, none of
   which reagent-slim's walk asks) - but the choice now has a price on it.

RECOMMENDATION (advisory, not a ruling): Hicasso should NOT author a third
interpreter AND should NOT adopt Freehand's. The cheapest runtime codec in the
tree is reagent-slim's, and the arm carrying it (donor-r1) is already at or
below reagent-slim on mount and within 1.05-1.37x of raw UIx. Consume it, and
spend the programme's clock on the three genuinely new REACTIVITY mechanisms
the adversarial review identified.

=== METHOD, AND WHAT IS NOT LEVELLED ===

NEW GATE 0b, codecs-differ?, fatal before anything is measured. A
donor-fh / donor-r1 reading of 1.0 would be unreadable without it: it could
mean "the codecs cost the same" or "the arm ran one codec twice", and no clock
reading tells those apart. The parity gate cannot answer it - making the arms
agree is its whole purpose. So the difference is DEMONSTRATED on a form the two
treat differently and no arm uses: ^{:key ...} vector metadata, which slim
honours and Freehand refuses by name. Pass on every run of both sweeps.

RESIDUALS, each with its direction stated:
 (a) :f>'s wrapper always converts the body's return through as-element.
     donor-r1 returns hiccup (the call does the work); donor-fh returns a
     finished element (the call is a pass-through). donor-fh therefore pays one
     extra call plus ~5 predicates per boundary. Bounded: the measured mount-M
     gap is 0.60-0.80 ms over 300 boundaries = 2-3 us per boundary, against
     tens of nanoseconds for the residual - under 1% - and it runs AGAINST
     Freehand.
 (b) The codec is measured with NO candidate above it, which is IN FREEHAND'S
     FAVOUR: a Freehand application renders inside a declared boundary and
     additionally records an event site per handler. So this prices
     Freehand-the-CODEC exactly and Freehand-the-SUBSTRATE from BELOW.
 (c) Adding the arm changes k in the interleaving schedule, so EVERY column
     here (including donor-r1/r2/uix/reagent/reagent-slim) is a fresh take on a
     5/6-arm plan and is NOT comparable figure-for-figure with the four-arm
     rows on hd8-composed-donor-arm.md. Nothing is quoted from that page and
     nothing here amends it. The one re-taken column that moved visibly is
     named on the page: donor-r1 / reagent-slim on mount-M reads 0.900-0.979
     here where that page published 1.000-1.120.

THE ONE UNSTABLE ROW, named rather than averaged away: mount-U in the uix run
straddles 1.0 in sweep 1 (0.973-1.247, one round at 0.9726 and five at
1.1233-1.2466) and is disjoint above 1.0 in sweep 2 (1.065-1.164). Read it as
"between indistinguishable and ~1.25x slower" and judge nothing on a finer
margin. Every other U row, both sweeps, is disjoint above 1.0.

GATES, both sweeps, every one of the three adapter runs: arm-order guard 12/12
reportable and ZERO refusals; canonical-DOM parity with can-fail? true (this is
what proves Freehand's codec builds the SAME page); codecs-differ? pass;
positive control predicted 1.9934 from the witness arithmetic BEFORE the run,
+/-30%, every round inside - pass 6/6 segments with 16 of 18 rounds BELOW
prediction, the direction a fixed per-mount term predicts; DOM read-back 0
unverified of 7,722 writes per sweep; rung-2 lowering check green; and the
guard's, the yield-correction contract's and the corrected-table's own
self-tests all before anything was measured.

NO BAR VERDICT IS ISSUED. The mount win condition is suspended pending the
operator's amendment (post-.25 UIx/Reagent parity at 1.0243x makes "mount <=
1.0x Reagent" require a free-or-negative interpreter and contradicts the
codec-within-1.10x-of-UIx condition). Everything is reported against raw UIx
and the existing donor arms.

FENCES HELD: instrument-only, bench lane; nothing under implementation/*/src
touched; no shadow-cljs build id added; :hicasso-bench reused.
FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-2rtt6.40 - stamp the LANDED whole-tree anchor on the
studio page after the PR merges (a worker cannot know its own rebased sha).
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7322 (branch worker/codecarm-2rtt6-29,
producing commit 62059f140bbac5d0cdeb11e1a72ee922d5dd3883). NOT merged - the
mayor merges.

title: spec/conformance/freehand/ donor ledger is a work-plan for the withdrawn EP-0036 programme
description:
ESCALATED from rf2-o61sn (PR #7274), which corrected the in-flight Freehand claims in spec/004-Views.md, Ownership.md, Conventions.md, 006-ReactiveSubstrate.md, API.md and 004D. The rf2-o61sn ruling ('a sentence that describes shipped behaviour is correct; a sentence that promises a future slice / a coming deletion / a transitional window is false — prefer the smallest correction') does NOT decide this site, so it was deliberately left untouched.

WHY IT DOES NOT DECIDE. spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md is not a document containing a few false sentences — it is WHOLLY a programme work-ledger. ~500 rows, each naming an owning programme slice (F0-F6) and a status of 'pending' or 'done'. Its opening premise: 'the standalone day8/re-frame2-ui artifact is deleted once every row below has been disposed. Absorption completeness is one of the release gates, and this ledger is the artifact that gate reads.' EP-0036 is withdrawn, so that release gate does not exist and the pending DELETE rows have no owner. There is no smallest sentence-level correction: the choice is between (a) a withdrawal banner that reframes the whole ledger as a historical record (mirroring how EP-0036 itself was kept under EP-0009's terminal-status rule), (b) freezing it, or (c) removing it. That is a ruling.

SECOND SITE, same class: spec/conformance/freehand/conformance-index.md:9 — 'The index is empty at establishment and grows one row at a time: each slice that lands a contract appends its own rows.' A one-clause fix on its own, but it was held back so the conformance/freehand/ tree gets ONE coherent disposition rather than two inconsistent ones.

IT IS LOAD-BEARING — this is a PAIRED spec + gate change, not a prose edit. scripts/check_donor_inventory.py enforces that its ESTABLISHED_ROWS roster covers the ledger EXACTLY (every roster identity still in the ledger AND every ledger row in the roster), that no row may be deleted (disposal = flip to 'done', the row stays as audit record), that no pending row goes stale, and that no live re-frame.ui consumer is unclaimed. It runs in .github/workflows/freehand-conformance.yml alongside check_freehand_conformance_index.py. Any banner/freeze/removal must land with the gate in the same PR or CI reds.

FENCE when dispatched: spec/conformance/freehand/** plus scripts/check_donor_inventory.py and scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py. spec/ is hot-zone — sequence, never parallel. Do not touch docs/EP/** (the withdrawal record landed and is correct) or docs/design/freehand/** (frozen).
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-31, dossier review): (a-split) — banner-and-archive the donor inventory, convert its gate to a snapshot-integrity validator in the SAME commit, narrowly correct the conformance index, and record an explicit EP-0038/P2 sunset. Two independent analyses (dossier + Codex second opinion) converged on this; counts and checker structure spot-reverified against the working tree 2026-07-31 before recording. This bead is now the dispatchable implementation owner. (This note is the sole record: the prior dossier edition was consumed unrecorded; the dossier file ai/decisions/rf2-lrtwj.donor-ledger-disposition.md is folded in full here and deleted.)

DISPOSITION — one atomic hot-zone PR; every piece in the same commit as the gate change or freehand-conformance CI reds:

(i) donor-inventory.md: a dated withdrawal banner as the FIRST substantive content, ahead of the current opening premise — the ledger is a snapshot at EP-0036 withdrawal. `pending` (149 rows: 96 MOVE, 41 REPLACE, 12 DELETE; 75 done; 224 total, exactly counted against the checker's grammar — not the ~500 this bead's description estimated) means "not disposed when the programme was withdrawn"; it confers no owner, authorises no work, and is not a release count; neither the pending count nor the artifact-deletion sentence authorises anything. ALL rows and their withdrawal-time statuses preserved.

(ii) scripts/check_donor_inventory.py, SAME commit: from live programme gate to snapshot-integrity validator. KEEP parsing, vocabulary, uniqueness, established-row retention; PIN the COMPLETE normalized row tuples, not just identities (disposition/slice/status/description could otherwise drift silently in an archive). REMOVE the worktree-comparison arms — check_partition, check_consumers, check_current (verified present today at lines 377/432/508) — and the pending-to-zero report. Any still-wanted product-neutral rule (e.g. donor-must-remain-unpublished, or a no-new-donor-consumers freeze during EP-0038) gets its own named authority and gate with a P2 sunset — never smuggled through the historical `pending` statuses of a withdrawn programme.

(iii) conformance-index.md: replace ONLY the stale growth sentence (line 9: "…and grows one row at a time: each slice that lands a contract appends its own rows") with timeless roster language. NO banner; its validator (check_freehand_conformance_index.py) and CI stay intact. Rationale (the Codex nuance the first dossier edition missed): EP-0036's withdrawal killed the PROGRAMME (F0-F6 ownership, drive-to-zero) but explicitly left the Freehand implementation, CI lanes, and shipped-behaviour specs in force pending separate disposition (docs/EP/EP-0036-...:352-354), and spec/Ownership.md still assigns those shipped contracts. The index is the live roster of executable laws for shipped code — archiving it would misclassify current behavioural evidence as history.

(iv) SUNSET (new from Codex; record it on the snapshot): EP-0038's HD-018 says a P2 win deletes the public Freehand and re-frame.ui surfaces and leaves "no donor inventory ledger". The archive's end condition: on a P2 win the snapshot and its snapshot-check retire WITH the donor surfaces they map; on a loss/null the snapshot stays as the historical record, and any future donor policy is made under fresh authority, never by reviving F0-F6. Removal before P2 is premature either way.

(v) freehand-conformance.yml: update workflow wording/comments and donor step names in the same commit, WITHOUT renaming the required job/status context.

VERIFIED FACTS to preserve (dossier + Codex, spot-reverified 2026-07-31): 224 parseable rows (149 pending / 75 done); pending split 96 MOVE, 41 REPLACE, 12 DELETE; matching 224-entry ESTABLISHED_ROWS retention roster; 229 tracked donor-tree files covered by 106 donor-tree row patterns; 30 mechanically detected external consumers; checker self-test AND live --ci --report both pass today; 42 commits touched the ledger between establishment 2026-07-22 and last update 2026-07-26. The record is substantial, validated, and currently coherent — a costly map, not stale prose.

REJECTED:
(b) Freeze verbatim, no banner — leaves an authorised work queue and release gate standing in present tense: the exact class of spec lie the rf2-o61sn cleanup just purged. The inventory's present-tense release gate, slice ownership, and pending-to-zero meanings are false authorities, not harmless old wording.
(c) Remove the tree, retire both gates — cleanest tree, but deletes the only structured absorption/consumer map while its subject code still exists; HD-018 contemplates deleting those surfaces on a P2 win — exactly when a consumer map is wanted; reconstruction from git history later costs far more than the banner costs now; and it would wrongly take conformance-index.md (live laws) down with it.

RISKS + mitigations: (1) a historical file under spec/ misread as normative -> the front-loaded dated banner is the mitigation; (2) losing the current census's protection against a new donor dependency -> if that protection is still wanted, an explicit narrow EP-0038 freeze rule under its own authority with a P2 sunset.

FENCE (for dispatch): spec/conformance/freehand/** plus scripts/check_donor_inventory.py and scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py. spec/ is HOT-ZONE — sequence, never parallel. Do NOT touch docs/EP/** (the withdrawal record landed and is correct) or docs/design/freehand/** (frozen). The spec edits and the gate conversion MUST land in the same PR (same commit) or CI reds — this is a PAIRED spec + gate change, not a prose edit.

NON-GATING for the ruling itself -- it stands regardless of this run. GATING for freezing numerical component budgets (shell / per-edge / per-unique-subscription-key) in validation.md's amended budget table.

WHAT. One same-instrument fan-out sweep on the existing P0 heap arm. Minimum form: P0_ROOTS=1 plus the already-published ROOTS=4 rows. Preferred form: disjoint/shared query rungs giving mean fan-out E/Q = 1, 2, 4, 8 in ONE scheduled run (per-root disjoint query ranges give fan-out 1 without dropping roots). Heap only (--only heap); instrument change, not a witness change -- the clock convergence is untouched.

WHY (from the rf2-2rtt6.16 finding). The .4 driver defaults P0_ROOTS=4 and divides the held-heap delta by ROOTS*perRoot = 1,200 boundaries while all four roots render the SAME frame-id and the SAME [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors -- 1,200 boundary-query edges over 300 unique keys, so its "exclusive retained per boundary" amortises the subscription half x4. Citations: the .16 description cites p0_run.cjs lines 264 and 347 (ROOTS, boundariesOf, bytesPerBoundaryCdp) at its revision; the dossier's Codex section source-verified at the current tree: p0_run.cjs lines 103, 312, 377-395; p0_heap.cljs 82-142, 176-192 (arm-table; mount-one ignores the root index); p0_reagent.cljs 81-101 / p0_uix.cljs 84-113 (same arms/frame-id into every root); cache mechanics subs.cljc 508-543, 1315-1378, 1662-1681 + subs/cache.cljc 1-20 (per-frame {query-vector {:reaction ... :ref-count n}}). Line numbers drift; the names are the durable anchors.

RUN (minimum): P0_ROUNDS=5 P0_ROOTS=1 node implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs --only heap
Keep the 4.7 MB dense-array positive control and the post-release residue check on every rung; arm-order guard and mount verification as published (.4 shipped 0 unverified of 48 mounts).

FIT AND REFUSAL RULE. Fit per-boundary = shell + (E/B) x edge + (Q/B) x subscription across the rungs. REFUSE to publish component prices if the fit is not linear enough to support them, and state the criterion on the page (Codex rec 4: the existing cross-instrument algebra rejects the unqualified scalar but cannot freeze allocations). Cross-instrument agreement to beat: solved subscription term ~820 B Reagent / ~2,231 B UIx vs rf2-2rtt6.12's ablation 866 / 2,453 B (5% / 9%).

PREDICTION ON RECORD (falsifiable). The fan-out-1 rung lands on the reads-ladder's distinct-query family within instrument noise: Reagent ~1,562 B/boundary @1 read (amortised x4 published 947), UIx ~3,807 B (published 2,134); the UIx/Reagent ratio stays ~2.25-2.44x (the amortisation is common-mode). A material miss REOPENS rf2-2rtt6.16 Part 1 -- report it there; do not smooth it.

PUBLISH. Regime-stamped rows (B, E, Q, E/B, E/Q, plus React/UIx/Reagent/Chromium versions and instrument blob hashes) on the studio page(s); results noted on rf2-2rtt6.16 or on the standard's successor record once rf2-0znkn's remedy lands. NEVER append to rf2-2rtt6.1 (append-never, rf2-0znkn).

LANE. Bench lane, parallel-safe: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/** plus studio doc page(s); no hot-zone files.

The note audits PR #7306 (the original sweep) and predates the repair: PR #7319 landed f01a4b0137 'docs(hicasso): the fan-out sweep's warrant, stated honestly', plus 61dd44950a, 8a3573c311 and a57bf3dd80 on this same bead. Verified by reading the page on main: line 390 now reads 'R2Q2B prices none of those four terms. It is NOT, however, held out of the adjudication'; line 15 records that the first revision advertised it as held out; line 441 says the page 'no longer offers it as independent evidence' and states what that costs; and section 7 records exactly what an independent adjudication would require. The repair went further than the charge — a worker derived the algebra showing the 'held-out prediction' was an exact IDENTITY of the other checks (M4 predicted minus R2Q2B measured = rho + dx(key - key2)), verified to the byte at +265 B against a measured +265 B, so the rung was never independent evidence at all. Two further dependences were found and stated. Closed on verification of main, not memory.

comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7306 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The B/E/Q witness construction, DOM and cache-cardinality read-backs, GC protocol, positive control, order guard, authored-to-landed range-diff (exact 5/5), and 69 successful GitHub checks are strong. The additive adjudicator's advertised held-out validation is not independent, however.

`R2Q2B` is assigned to `hi` and described as "never used above" / "held out of all of that". The same observation is then used immediately in `key-2 = (hi.y - lo.y) / dx`; `key-gap` feeds `key-ok?`; and `key-ok?` is a mandatory input to `model`. The value later scored as the held-out prediction therefore already participates in model admissibility and in the published alternate key price. For M4 the held-out residual and this R=2-pair key-gap are largely the same contrast, so they are not two disjoint validations. This contradicts the page's claim that R2Q2B is "the only rung whose value nothing above depends on" and weakens the precommitted evidence gate that allowed component prices into validation.md.

There is a second documentation correction, already mechanism-owned by open rf2-2rtt6.25: the provenance says .25 moves retained heap and that a cold read builds once. Audit #7305 demonstrated the public bare `createRoot.render` path still builds 2N because the timer wins; this heap harness forces `flushSync`, and no durable retained-heap delta from .25 is established. The .13 retained-reaction correction is separate and remains supported.

Bounded repair: give `R2Q2B` exactly one role. Preserve the stated independent gate by adding/re-running a genuinely untouched validation rung (or precommit an equivalent disjoint validation), then re-adjudicate the normative prices; alternatively retract the independent-held-out and gating claims and justify the reduced warrant. Correct the .25 provenance claim rather than duplicating its open implementation owner. Downstream normative owner rf2-hvl5s is reopened pending that adjudication.

title: bench(hicasso): test the segment-order effect with independent counterbalanced runs
description:
Found by rf2-a4x1o (PR #7283) while building the fail-closed segment-order verdict for p0_converge_app.

THE FINDING. Across THREE independent five-round runs of the converged witness set — the published run, the rf2-rjfz1 reproduction sweep, and rf2-a4x1o's corrected-instrument run — the cross-segment red-zone figure (uix-subs / reagent-subs, both floor-normalised in the same round and segment) reads HIGHER when the REAGENT segment ran first in 11 of 12 row-runs. One-sided binomial p = 0.0032.

Per-row disjointness could not see this and does not establish it: at rounds=5 the alternation splits 3:2, and under the null a disjoint partition arises in 2 of C(5,2)=10 assignments — 20% per row. Consistent with that, no row is disjoint in two runs (M1 and narrow in the published run, broad in the sweep). It is the SIGN across rows and runs that resolves.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY SHIPPED (PR #7283): segment-order-verdict publishes :order-balanced-mean — the mean of the two stratum means, which is unbiased under an alternating schedule whatever the parity of rounds — beside the raw mean, and marks a row :claim :direction-only when its strata are disjoint. rf2-2rtt6.1's 1.2301 and the narrow row's 1.1540 are withdrawn as magnitudes on that basis.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is two separable things:

1. BALANCE THE DESIGN. rounds=5 cannot balance two orders. An EVEN round count makes the raw and balanced estimators identical by construction and lifts the disjointness test from 3:2 (20% null rate) to 3:3 (10%). NOT taken in #7283 because it moves four published rows without deciding the question — it is a re-publication, and it should be taken as one: re-run all four rows at rounds=6, republish with a landed SHA, blob hashes and a verified repro, and mark the 5-round rows superseded IN PLACE.

2. EXPLAIN THE EFFECT. Something makes the second segment of a round systematically different from the first, and the page already carries an unexplained candidate: 'the per-page accumulation is still unexplained' — ~12 MB per segment entry, surviving a forced major collection, never reaching the document (rf2-2rtt6.4, rf2-flqpd). If the second segment runs on a heavier heap then whichever adapter goes second reads slower, which is exactly the observed sign (Reagent first => UIx second => UIx/Reagent reads high). retention_probe.cljs already has the census that would test it. That is a hypothesis with a cheap experiment, not a conclusion.

Not urgent: the DIRECTION verdicts survive the partition on every published row, so the bar rows and the red-zone rule still function. What is blocked is quoting a red-zone MAGNITUDE to four decimal places.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_app.cljs (segment-order-verdict, rounds), .../p0_converge_order_cljs_test.cljs, docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- Counterbalance or randomize which segment starts across independently launched runs; do not reuse four within-run row signs as independent Bernoulli trials.
- Report inference at the independent-run level or provide and validate a model that accounts for row/run dependence and temporal order.
- Re-run/republish the four rows with the balanced design and preserve the conservative magnitude holds unless stronger evidence resolves them.
- Replace the current corrected-run provenance placeholder with landed SHA 9737ed5cf815817d856c49eefb6824856df51668 plus supporting blob hashes; record landed provenance for the later rerun too.
notes:
AUDIT PR #7283 (2026-07-30; correctness/completeness follow-up). UPDATED this existing exact owner rather than filing a duplicate. The qualitative segment-order suspicion is useful, but the published inferential warrant overstates the evidence: 11/12 signs are four correlated rows inside each of only three sequential browser runs, not 12 established independent Bernoulli trials. The one-sided binomial p=0.0032 therefore has no demonstrated independence basis.

Every run also uses the same deterministic schedule: Reagent-first at rounds 0/2/4 and UIx-first at 1/3. Segment order is consequently confounded with round parity/temporal position, and Reagent-first always receives the extra observation. An even 3:3 count fixes unequal weighting, but a fixed start still does not establish exchangeability or isolate order from time. Treat “real/decisive” and p=0.0032 as unwarranted while retaining the conservative direction/magnitude hold.

Repair the experiment by counterbalancing or randomizing the starting segment across independent process-level runs, then analyze independent run-level replicates (or document a justified dependence model). Also replace the studio's still-landed placeholder “the landed SHA follows the merge” with landed SHA `9737ed5cf815817d856c49eefb6824856df51668` and the supporting blob hashes now, before the later six-round republication.
MECHANISM EVIDENCE from rf2-flqpd's instrument (fresh run on PR #7285's head, full default shape, exit 0, all validity gates green). The RETENTION version of the heavier-heap hypothesis is dead -- the COLLECTED column climbs 0.89 MB total across six segments and does not step at a seam -- but the GARBAGE version is alive and now has a measured, adapter-ASYMMETRIC magnitude: at the segment seams of SERIES C (50 cycles x 4 grid roots per segment, alternating substrate), UNCOLLECTED garbage read uix 17.86 / reagent 85.25 / uix 30.82 / reagent 83.13 / uix 30.45 / reagent 82.46 MB. The prior landed run shows the same asymmetry (reagent seams 65/81/56 vs uix 18/31/12). A Reagent segment's mount/unmount work leaves roughly 2.7-6x the uncollected rubbish of the UIx segment's identical-shape work, and rf2-flqpd settled that exactly this load is what moves an unchanging arm (the floor drifted 3.4->7.0 ms under 30-80 MB of rubbish, because a scavenge inside a timed window measures the collector). So within a round, Reagent-first puts the UIx segment under a far heavier collector debt than UIx-first puts Reagent -- the sign this bead observed (Reagent-first => uix/reagent reads HIGH, 11/12). CAVEAT: seam-level garbage from the retention page's workload, not the converge page's exact witnesses; a mechanism with measured asymmetry, not a verdict -- the counterbalanced independent-run design this bead owns remains the decisive test, and nothing here touches the rounds=6 re-publication.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7303 (2026-07-31): reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate. COMPLETENESS: the six-round counterbalanced instrument, M2 mount-budget repair, four-row republication, tests, and provenance landed, but the durable record contains only group means, intervals, ranges, and p-values. It does not contain the ten per-run threshold means and ten per-run d values, nor a deterministic derivation, so the PRs central statistics cannot be independently recomputed from the repository. CORRECTNESS: the ten start labels were deliberately alternated, not randomly assigned. Enumerating all C(10,5) relabellings is therefore not an assumption-free randomization distribution, and the 2^10 sign-flip result is exact only under an unstated sign-symmetry/exchangeability assumption. Keep the balanced six-round means as useful descriptive evidence, but either state the assumptions and downgrade the inferential wording or take a genuinely randomized assignment if exact randomization inference is wanted. Also reconcile the fail-closed per-run magnitude rule with the ensemble: 3 of 40 row-runs were magnitude-unresolved, yet all ten run means feed each precise ensemble threshold; state and pin the aggregate rule rather than letting an individually unpublishable point silently re-enter. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: bounded repair only—commit a compact 10x4 observation table or fixture plus its derivation, correct the false one-eight-minute-window wording if it means launch spacing, and avoid a general statistics framework.
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON. I closed this saying the 10x4 observation table 'CANNOT be completed' because the producing worktree was reaped. That was WRONG: the ten runs' console logs had been backed up out of tree and survived intact. The table is now committed COMPLETE -- all forty cells -- on PR #7312, and the two p columns I had recorded as 'not checkable by anyone, now or later' are both recomputed and both reproduce (View 1's 252-relabelling permutation p: 0.770/0.611/0.984/0.992; View 2's 1024-assignment sign-flip p: 0.084/0.889/0.856/0.302). So does every point estimate, every prose count (37 of 40 strata overlapping, 23 of 40 Reagent-first-higher, 59 of 60 M1 rounds above 1.0), and the composite's 0.823. Provenance is stated as RECOVERY, not measurement: nothing was re-measured, and run 1's vectors in the backup match the four the page already printed, which is what identifies the backup as this ensemble rather than a pilot. A test asserts that join. NEW FINDING that only the recovered data could surface: every 95% interval on the page was ~2% too wide. A t multiplier for EIGHT degrees of freedom was used where a mean of ten run means needs NINE (2.2622). The cause is nameable -- eight is CORRECT for the two-sample 5v5 'resolution limit' column beside it, that column reproduces exactly, and the same t was reused for the one-sample case. Reported in neither direction: old intervals struck in place with corrected ones beside them at all ten quoting sites, three tests pin the diagnosis, and the error is conservative so no verdict changes. Also corrected: the open item claiming nine tenths of the table was gone is closed as what happened, and rewritten to what genuinely remains -- this ensemble was verifiable by luck rather than by design. GATE CAVEAT worth carrying forward: mkdocs build --strict does NOT validate docs/design/hicasso/** (mkdocs.yml excludes it), so that page was checked directly instead -- all 15 internal anchors resolve, no malformed tables. Gates: test:cljs exit 0 (11,993 tests / 60,034 assertions, 0 failures); clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0; mkdocs --strict exit 0.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7312 (merged 2026-07-31T08:47:40Z; landed 64be09b79bb2db511957ba715e3a264b4494e7fc) — REOPENED this exact owner; no duplicate. COMPLETENESS: the recovered 10x4 table, provenance join, deterministic derivations, corrected 9-df intervals, aggregate inclusion rule, false-duration correction, and count-free lane-cache invariant answer the prior audit well. One inference remains uncorrected: the page and this Bead's close reason still say “a confound can manufacture an effect; it cannot manufacture a null,” then use that premise to call the rows insensitive to which segment starts. CORRECTNESS: because starts were alternated, Reagent-start is exactly odd launch parity. An unmeasured session effect can oppose a real start/order effect and cancel it (for example +x from start and -x from odd-launch drift yields an observed zero), just as it can reinforce one. The unconditional sentence is false. For the same reason, averaging the two start groups isolates “ORDER” and half their difference isolates “TEMPORAL” only under an additive, exchangeable/antisymmetric temporal model; the design did not establish that model. The conditional statement “no start effect detectable at this resolution, under exchangeability” is supportable, but the unconditional decomposition and practical insensitivity claim are not. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: keep the table, arithmetic, p-values, interval repair, and count-free cache comment. This needs a bounded record correction, not a statistics framework or automatic re-measurement: remove the false one-way-confound claim; label the order/temporal split and no-detectable-effect conclusion as conditional/descriptive. If an unconditional causal or schedule-insensitivity claim is still wanted, use genuinely randomized start assignment in a new ensemble.
close_reason:
WARRANT CORRECTED (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7351). Closing against the NEWEST note — MERGED-PR AUDIT #7312 — not the older #7283 one.

MY BRIEF WAS STALE AND I AM RECORDING IT. It asked me to remove the one-sided binomial p = 0.0032 whose independence basis was unmet. THAT CORRECTION HAD ALREADY LANDED (PRs #7303/#7312): the page has carried 'That warrant was wrong, and it was wrong in two separable ways' and an explicit withdrawal since. Re-doing it would have been a no-op. The live scope was #7312's different, still-uncorrected inference.

THE FALSE SENTENCE, NOW WITHDRAWN IN PLACE. The page argued 'a confound can manufacture an effect; it cannot manufacture a null' and used that premise to call the rows insensitive to which segment starts. It is false: because the ten starts were ALTERNATED, Reagent-start is exactly odd launch parity, so a session drift can OPPOSE a real order effect as easily as reinforce it — a true +x against a -x is observed as zero. A null under a confounded design is evidence of no NET effect along the one axis the design could see, not of no effect.

DOWNGRADED TO CONDITIONAL/DESCRIPTIVE, exactly the bounded repair asked for:
(1) The ORDER/TEMPORAL split no longer 'isolates' anything — the cancellation is exact only under an ADDITIVE, ANTISYMMETRIC temporal model, which counterbalancing makes AVAILABLE but does not test and this design did not. The columns are a descriptive split; the labels are the model's naming, not a measured attribution. Same conditioning applied to the derivation test's two docstrings, which asserted the unconditional version.
(2) 'Which segment starts a run does not detectably move the number' -> no difference RESOLVABLE at this power, under the same exchangeability the permutation p assumes.
(3) 'demonstrably insensitive to the schedule' -> no schedule effect resolvable in these ten runs, under exchangeability. The even round count's design-unbiasedness is kept SEPARATE and unqualified: that one holds by construction and carries no assumption.

DID A DEFENSIBLE STATISTIC SURVIVE? Yes, and nothing had to be removed. The permutation and sign-flip p values are exact UNDER A STATED ASSUMPTION (exchangeability / sign symmetry), and the page now states it at every quoting site instead of at none. The audit's own supportable conditional — 'no start effect detectable at this resolution, under exchangeability' — is what the page now claims, as a conditional.

THE P-VALUE'S LAST TWO LIVE CITATIONS, which the page's withdrawal never reached: p0_converge_app.cljs still said 'It found something ... one-sided binomial p = 0.0032', and coldmount_app.cljs cited it as the REASON for an even round count. Both now carry the withdrawal, and both KEEP the design repair, which never needed the effect — a balanced round count makes the raw and order-balanced means coincide BY CONSTRUCTION.

NO RE-MEASUREMENT: measurement is deferred by the operator and this was a warrant problem, not a data problem. Every number, interval, p-value and table cell is untouched, and test:cljs re-derives the committed 10x4 observation table's arithmetic to prove it.

STILL OPEN, NOT DONE HERE (file follow-ups if wanted): a genuinely RANDOMISED start assignment is what it would take to drop the exchangeability qualifier and support an unconditional causal/schedule-insensitivity claim. The acceptance criteria's earlier items (counterbalanced independent runs, run-level inference, six-round republication, landed SHA 9737ed5c + blob hashes) were satisfied by the #7303/#7312 line.

title: Spec 010 step-5 fx-args validation is dev-only, so malformed :rf.server/* fx args are NOT skipped in production — they land on the response accumulator
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 00:30 AUSEST on worker/ssr-triage-76gom, running `re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` under the REAL gate:

    cd implementation/ssr && clojure -M:test:prod-gate -n re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test

`ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary` contributes 16 of the namespace's 116 reds, and — unlike every other red in it — SEVEN of those are not trace spelling. They are the SEMANTIC assertions, and they fail because the behaviour differs.

WHAT THE GATE SHOWS. `re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-fx!` (validate.cljc ~989) is `(if interop/debug-enabled? (run-validation …) true)`. `interop/debug-enabled?` is read ONCE at namespace-load time, so under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` the Spec 010 §Validation-order step-5 fx-args boundary does not run AT ALL. Its documented recovery is `:skipped` (Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 5 — "the caller skips the offending fx only"). In production NOTHING is skipped: the malformed fx runs, and its args reach the per-request response accumulator.

MEASURED, at the documented host-adapter surface `ssr/get-response`:

  [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"]
      dev : fx skipped, (:status (get-response f)) = 200
      prod: (:status (get-response f)) = "not-an-int"   ;; a STRING status
  [:rf.server/set-header {:name "X-Foo"}]           ;; :value missing
      dev : skipped, no X-Foo header
      prod: (:headers …) = [["content-type" …] ["X-Foo" nil]]
  [:rf.server/set-cookie {:name "session"}]         ;; :value missing
      dev : skipped, (:cookies …) empty
      prod: (:cookies …) = [{:name "session"}]
  [:rf.server/safe-redirect {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}]
      dev : skipped, no :redirect
      prod: (:redirect …) = {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}

rf2-kjf3m.2 built this boundary for exactly the first case — its own comment reads "the bead's concrete failing scenario: a string status that pre-rf2-kjf3m.2 rode straight onto the wire". The gate says that scenario is still live in a release build.

WHAT SAVES THE WIRE TODAY, AND WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH. `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj` is defensive on purpose: `fail-closed-status` coerces a non-integer `:status` to 500, `Location` is `str`-coerced, and header values are string-coerced in `headers/merge-pair-into-header-map`. Its own docstring says "schema validation is optional, so this adapter is the last line". So on a Ring host the wire is well-formed. Three residual problems:

  1. The net is HOST-SPECIFIC. Spec 011 §1070 requires non-Ring adapters to emit the same error categories; nothing requires them to re-implement `fail-closed-status`. A host that trusts the accumulator (the surface `get-response` documents) ships a malformed response.
  2. The 200 -> 500 flip is SILENT in production. `fail-closed-status`'s only signal is `trace/emit! :warning :rf.ssr/ssr-non-integer-status` — the dev bus. On a production JVM the app's 200 becomes a 500 with nothing on either error axis.
  3. `get-response` / `flush-response-result!` are PUBLIC host-adapter surfaces whose contract now differs by posture. A host adapter branching on `(:status response)` or `(:cookies response)` sees a different shape in the build it ships.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT rf2-bkvu5 / rf2-mwv4e / rf2-byexd. Those cover ADJACENT surfaces:
  - rf2-bkvu5 (RULED (a), dev-only as designed) is the app-db candidate / flow-output validation — `reg-app-schema`.
  - rf2-mwv4e is the `:rf.schema/at-boundary` interceptor, which DOES run in production and has no surviving diagnostic.
  - rf2-byexd is the DOCS correction for the SSR 400 arm being dev-fed.
This one is the step-5 fx-args hot-path boundary, and its consequence is not observability — it is that a malformed fx RUNS and mutates the response accumulator where the spec says it is skipped.

THE RULING WANTED, one of:

  (a) INTENDED — hot-path fx-args validation is a dev-time developer aid, and the HOST adapter is the production boundary. Then Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 5 should say the `:skipped` recovery is dev-posture, Spec 011 should state that a host adapter MUST coerce/fail-closed on the accumulator (making ssr-ring's `fail-closed-status` a normative adapter obligation rather than one adapter's belt-and-braces), and the seven semantic assertions in `ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary` get a dev arm citing this bead.
  (b) NOT INTENDED for the RESERVED `:rf.server/*` family specifically — the framework's own reserved fxs should guard their own args unconditionally (cheap, closed set, no user schema involved), independent of the optional schemas artefact. Narrow, and it does not change the general step-5 gate.
  (c) NOT INTENDED generally — step-5 validation runs in production. Largest blast radius (a hot-path cost on every fx in every app) and almost certainly wrong under the project's posture.

Do NOT let a worker pick one to make the lane greener. Whatever lands, `fail-closed-status`'s dev-only warning (problem 2 above) probably wants promoting alongside it.

BLOCKS: `re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` cannot come off the `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` roster until this is ruled. Its OTHER ~100 reds are all mechanical trace-sourcing (see the roster comment for the per-cluster method) and can be done in the same PR once the ruling is in.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): (b) — the reserved :rf.server/* fx family guards its own args UNCONDITIONALLY; the general Spec 010 step-5 fx-args gate for user fx stays dev-only. Recorded 2026-07-28 07:50 AUSEST; the ai/decisions dossier is deleted per protocol, so this note carries everything.

WHY (b). (a) rejected: it assigns the repair to every adapter AFTER the malformed value has crossed the public get-response boundary, cannot repair correctly (a missing cookie :value is not inferable as "", omit, or bug), leaves the 200->500 rewrite silent, and makes get-response's contract permanently posture-dependent. (c) rejected: a hot-path cost on every fx in every app to protect seven closed framework effects — posture-hostile, and contra Spec 010's own production section. (b) is the rqje9 logic exactly: trust-the-programmer covers USER declarations, not the framework's own wire-adjacent contract. Decisive evidence beyond the dossier (verified in source 2026-07-28): the ownership pattern (b) asks for ALREADY EXISTS in the very file the fix lands in — implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc's validate-header-name!/validate-header-value!/validate-cookie-name!/validate-cookie-attr!/validate-redirect-location! all error/throw-error! unconditionally before swap-response! (the CRLF/token/injection surface). And the repo ruled this bug-class once already: routing scroll.cljc's emit-unsupported-strategy! docstring records rf2-px26m -> rf2-2hkfy — a rejection that fired only where the optional schemas artefact had already caught the value at step-5, fixed with an unconditional handler-owned rejection. (b) is not new policy; it completes an existing one. The Codex second opinion independently reproduced the failure and reached (b) on the same ownership grounds; its implementation contract is ADOPTED (below), including where it differs from the primary dossier's skip-silently sketch.

MECHANISM RULED (Codex contract over the dossier's skip-silently variant): the guards THROW through the canonical re-frame.error/throw-error!, before the first swap-response!. Existing registered-fx containment then supplies the wanted semantics with ZERO new machinery: no accumulator mutation, sibling fx continue, an always-on :rf.error/fx-handler-exception record survives production, and SSR's error projection serves the sanitised 500. Chosen over skip-silently because (1) it matches the sibling guards in the same file for the same fx family, (2) it needs no new skip/record plumbing, and (3) fail-closed is right for a wire-adjacent programmer error that survived to production — a silently-dropped Set-Cookie under a 200 is worse than an honest, observable 500. Taxonomy: malformed framework call (programmer error) -> throw/containment; untrusted-input POLICY decision (safe-redirect target rejection) -> stays the existing non-projecting no-op.

MECHANISM OF THE BUG (for posterity): re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-fx! (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, gate at ~989-990) is (if interop/debug-enabled? (run-validation ...) true); interop/debug-enabled? is read once at namespace-load time, so under -Dre-frame.debug=false the Spec 010 §Validation-order step-5 boundary does not run AT ALL and the documented :skipped recovery (§Per-step recovery row 5) never happens — the malformed fx runs and mutates the per-request response accumulator.

MEASURED at ssr/get-response (dev vs real prod gate):
  [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"]                   dev: skipped, :status 200 | prod: :status "not-an-int" (string status)
  [:rf.server/set-header {:name "X-Foo"}] (no :value)    dev: skipped              | prod: ["X-Foo" nil] in :headers
  [:rf.server/set-cookie {:name "session"}] (no :value)  dev: skipped              | prod: {:name "session"} in :cookies
  [:rf.server/safe-redirect {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}]  dev: skipped     | prod: the malformed redirect installs
Independently reproduced (Codex): ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary = 18/18 green on :test, 16/18 failures under :test:prod-gate, zero :where :fx-args traces. rf2-kjf3m.2 built the boundary for exactly the string-status case ("pre-fix rode straight onto the wire") — live again in every release build.

THE THREE RESIDUAL PROBLEMS, AND HOW THE RULING RESOLVES EACH:
  1. HOST-SPECIFIC NET — ssr-ring's fail-closed-status/coercions save the wire on Ring only; Spec 011 requires non-Ring adapters to emit the same error categories, not to re-implement coercion. RESOLVED: the handlers own the invariant; every adapter inherits a well-formed accumulator.
  2. SILENT 200->500 FLIP — fail-closed-status's only signal is the dev-bus trace. RESOLVED: promoted to the always-on axis (item 3 below).
  3. POSTURE-DEPENDENT PUBLIC CONTRACT — RESOLVED for the part that matters: get-response never yields a malformed :rf/response shape in ANY build. The recovery PATH still differs and is documented, not hidden: dev-with-schemas = Malli step-5 skip + rich :where :fx-args diagnostic, page renders; prod or schemas-less dev = guard-throw -> containment -> always-on record + sanitised 500.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT (this bead IS the implementation owner — it is a [bug]; no split):
  1. Cheap predicate guards (int?, string?, required keys — NO Malli, no schemas-artefact dependency) beside the existing always-on guards in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc, covering the seven standard fx per their published contracts: status int in 100-599; set-header/append-header explicit string :name and :value; set-cookie explicit string :name/:value plus documented optional attr types; delete-cookie per its published contract; trusted redirect optional string :location (KEEP its intentional no-target behaviour); safe-redirect required string :location; redirect statuses/:relative-only?/:allow per documented types. Args maps stay OPEN (no closed-map rejection of extra keys). Every guard runs before the first swap-response! and throws via error/throw-error!. Safe-redirect POLICY rejections unchanged.
  2. Tighten the status schema in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/server_fx_schemas.cljc to int-in-100-599 in the same change; guards and registered schemas share a small table-driven acceptance corpus so the canonical cases cannot drift. No :validate-in-production? flag, no generic second validator, no runtime Malli interpretation.
  3. Promote fail-closed-status's silent flip (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj) to the always-on error axis via the error-emit/emit-error-both! seam (rf2-2hkfy pattern; constant :reason, never the offending value, per the rf2-s3n6h precedent). The Ring materialiser coercions STAY as last-line backstop — explicitly NOT the primary owner. Egress-surface change, same review class as rf2-6jqa8 (rf2-ov56u-style review); may ride the same PR or a sibling; NOT a prerequisite for the guards.
  4. Tests: convert ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary into a two-posture semantic contract — assert the bad fx never mutates the raw accumulator and sibling fx still run (both postures); assert posture-specific diagnostics separately (dev: Malli :where :fx-args skip; prod-gate arm: always-on :rf.error/fx-handler-exception + sanitised-500 projection at get-response).
  5. Spec edits, BOTH HOT-ZONE (sequence this PR against any other spec-touching PR):
     - spec/010-Schemas.md §Per-step recovery row 5: qualify the general step-5 fx-args gate (user reg-fx :schema) as dev-posture — the :skipped recovery is a dev-time aid, stated once, loudly, in the bkvu5-(a) pattern; add that the reserved :rf.server/* family independently guards its own args in all builds (handler-owned invariant; richer Malli diagnostic in dev).
     - spec/011-SSR.md: the standard SSR fx handlers preserve :rf/response integrity unconditionally, so every host adapter inherits a well-formed accumulator from get-response; adapter-side coercion is defence-in-depth, NOT a normative obligation (explicitly rejecting option (a)'s "adapter MUST fail-closed" clause).
  6. Fence/sequencing: code surfaces (implementation/ssr/src + test, implementation/ssr-ring/src) are per-feature and parallel-safe; spec/010-Schemas.md + spec/011-SSR.md are hot-zone. implementation/schemas/validate.cljc is NOT touched — the general gate stays dev-only by design.
  7. The mechanical 39-deftest split of ssr-end-to-end-test can ride the same PR: the per-cluster method is recorded verbatim in the scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh roster comment (fx-handler-exception cluster needs NO guard; ditto projector-diagnostic; :rf.warning/* + hydration-mismatch genuinely dev-only; safe-redirect dev arms for the diagnostic only).

Audit of merged PR #7204: the guard/schema parity claim is false for presence and cookie-name cases that the shared corpus omits. Malli optional keys reject an explicitly present nil, but the always-on guard uses `some?`/`or`: `{:path nil}` / `{:secure nil}` on set-cookie are treated as absent and the nil-bearing cookie is persisted; redirect `{:status nil}` defaults to 302; safe-redirect `{:status nil :relative-only? nil :allow nil}` likewise passes the guard while the dev schema rejects it. Production therefore still admits accumulator shapes that dev skips, contradicting the bead's central invariant that both enforcements implement one published contract and `get-response` is posture-independent.

Bounded acceptance: decide one public shape for explicit nil and cookie names, then make the Malli schemas, unconditional guards, Spec 011 text and raw accumulator agree. Extend the ONE acceptance corpus with every optional key explicitly nil plus keyword/symbol cookie names; drive each row through both enforcements and add raw-accumulator witnesses under the real production gate. title: ci: the fast-PR spine SILENTLY SKIPS mkdocs --strict when mkdocs is not on bare PATH — and it is the only gate covering docs/EP/**
description:
FOUND by the rf2-m6if4 worker (PR #7351) and worth fixing because it is a fail-open gate on a normative surface.

THE OBSERVATION. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh prints 'NOT RUN: mkdocs --strict build (mkdocs not on PATH)' and CONTINUES GREEN. On this machine mkdocs is installed but reachable only as 'python -m mkdocs', not as a bare 'mkdocs' executable — so the spine's probe misses it and the step is skipped, silently, on every run.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. docs/EP/** is NOT in mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS do not cover it either. So for an EP edit, mkdocs --strict IS THE ONLY GATE — and it is the one that silently does not run locally. A worker editing docs/EP/ who trusts a green spine has had NO gate cover their change. The rf2-m6if4 worker caught this and ran 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' explicitly (exit 0) rather than leave it unrun; the next worker may not.

THIS IS THE FAIL-OPEN CLASS THIS REPO HAS NOW FOUND SIX TIMES IN TWO DAYS: a residue gate that reset before asserting; a drift guard that compared the runner against its own regex; a waiver whose 'bare.length > max' with max 1 permitted the FIRST regression; a capstone that walked strings and missed keyword keys; an API manifest that did not scan an unrostered namespace; and a drift check that reported BLINDNESS as though it were drift. Same shape every time: the gate reports success without having examined the thing.

THE FIX, in preference order:
  1. Make the spine's probe find mkdocs the way it is actually installed — try 'mkdocs' then 'python -m mkdocs' then 'py -m mkdocs' — so the step RUNS rather than skips.
  2. If it genuinely cannot be found, the step must be LOUD: name what was not checked and which surfaces are consequently ungated (docs/EP/** at minimum). A skip that reads like a pass is the defect.
  3. Consider whether a skipped-but-required gate should fail the spine outright on a diff that touches a surface only that gate covers. That is the strongest form and worth costing rather than assuming.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST: confirm mkdocs really is absent from bare PATH on this machine and present via python -m, confirm docs/EP/** is outside every other checker's roots, and say so with evidence rather than taking this description's word for it.

title: A malformed test (ns ...) form is silently dropped from the JVM lane
description:
Observed while landing rf2-d2841 pass 5 (worker/core-roster-p5).

A test file whose `(ns ...)` FORM is malformed — a stray unescaped quote in the
docstring is enough — is INVISIBLE to `cognitect.test-runner`'s namespace
discovery. `clojure.tools.namespace.find` cannot read the form, so the
namespace never enters the discovered set:

  * `clojure -M:test -n <that-ns>` reports `Ran 0 tests`, exit 0 (only the
    RF2_MIN_TESTS floor made it red, and only because the probe run had the
    floor pinned to 1).
  * a FULL `clojure -M:test` ran 2182 tests instead of 2190 — exactly the
    eight deftests of the broken file — and reported `0 failures, 0 errors`.

So a whole test namespace can leave the lane with the suite still green. This
is the same class of false green `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh` exists to
close, arriving by a different door.

NEITHER EXISTING GUARD CATCHES IT:
  * the prod-gate script's `verify_roster` guard #1 compares the file count
    under `test/` against the scraped `-test` namespace count, but it scrapes
    the `(ns ` line as TEXT with sed — it never reads the form, so a file with
    a broken body still scrapes fine;
  * the RF2_MIN_TESTS floor is a COLLAPSE detector calibrated ~3% under the
    observed count; eight missing tests out of 2190 is far inside that.

Remedy candidates (not ruled):
  a. have the runner compare the namespaces it DISCOVERED against the file
     list under `test/` and fail on any file it could not read;
  b. add a `-n`-selector post-check: every requested namespace must have
     contributed at least one test;
  c. make `verify_roster` require the scraped namespace to be loadable.

Reproduce: break the docstring of any `*_test.clj` (an unescaped `"` inside the
ns docstring), then run the suite.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7249 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact JVM discovery-integrity owner; no duplicate.

The malformed-form and wrong-path-name doors are fixed, but the shipped claim that the per-file path comparison also makes discovery injective is false for two legal source layouts:

1. One discovery root contains both `probe/duplicate_test.clj` and `probe/duplicate_test.cljc`, each declaring `probe.duplicate-test`.
2. Two `-d` roots each contain the same relative path and declaration.

In both cases every file passes the current check because `discovery-defects` derives `ext` from that file and compares it only to its own relative path. There is no cross-file uniqueness pass. Direct probe against the exact runner blob shipped by PR #7249 (blob 9d5e997024, unchanged on current origin/main) produced:

`{:discovered [probe.duplicate-test probe.duplicate-test], :defects []}`

This is the shadowing door the PR says the one rule closes. Cognitect `test` mapcats those duplicate namespace symbols, requires them in order (the second require is already loaded), then passes both symbols to `clojure.test/run-tests`; one physical file is loaded and run twice while the other never runs, green. A count/floor cannot detect the substitution.

Repair narrowly in this owner: retain the readable form + own-path comparison, then enforce global uniqueness of each declared JVM namespace across all files from all selected discovery roots, independent of `.clj`/`.cljc` extension. Name every colliding file in the diagnostic. Add regression controls for same-root `.clj` + `.cljc` siblings and same relative `.clj` path across two `-d` roots; keep the unreadable, wrong-declaration, multi-dir parsing, clean-tree, and process-boundary controls green. No new runner, roster, manifest, or source-root policy.
close_reason:
AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED — discovery is now injective, not merely per-file correct. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7353 (MERGED 710f9b0e73).

THE DOOR, CONFIRMED. Probed the exact blob the audit named (9d5e997024, unchanged on the base): both layouts reproduced verbatim — {:discovered [probe.duplicate-test probe.duplicate-test], :defects []} for a same-root .clj+.cljc pair AND for one relative path under two -d roots. discovery-defects derived ext FROM the file and compared it only to that file's own relative path, so there was no cross-file pass at all.

END-TO-END PROOF, not just the predicate: the .cljc sibling carried a deftest that fails if it ever executes. The shipped runner reported 'Ran 2 tests containing 2 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' exit 0. The .clj's single passing test ran TWICE; the failing file never loaded. The tally goes UP, so neither the summary nor the RF2_MIN_TESTS floor (a collapse detector) can see the substitution — that is what made it fail-open rather than merely wrong.

THE REPAIR, narrow to this owner as ruled. discovery-defects now runs two rules over one scan: own-path-defect (the existing readable-form + own-path comparison, behaviour unchanged) and collision-defects (global uniqueness of every declared namespace across ALL selected roots, independent of .clj/.cljc). Collisions are computed over the files that already spell their own path, since a file that does not is already named by the first rule. Every colliding file is named and each complaint points at the others. The scan dedupes by CANONICAL path so a lane naming one directory twice is not reddened over its alias spelling. verify-discovery!'s diagnostic now explains both doors, ASCII-only. No new runner, roster, manifest, or source-root policy.

NO ALLOWANCE WAS NEEDED and nothing was widened from error to warning — neither layout is ever legal on a JVM classpath.

WHAT IT HAD BEEN HIDING: NOTHING. Swept every quiet-runner lane in the repo — 44 aliases across 34 deps.edn, each with its own -d set resolved from its :main-opts (per-lane is the only correct semantics; separate lanes are separate classpaths), including the five-root tools :test lane. TOTAL DEFECTS 0. The door was open; nothing had walked through it.

MUTATION: collision present + fixed runner => exit 1 naming both files; collision removed, git diff empty => exit 0 reporting 'Ran 1 tests' (not 2 — direct confirmation the earlier 2 was one test run twice).

CONTROLS ADDED (each pins the DEFECT before the guard, via find-namespaces-in-dir first): clj+cljc sibling named both ways; one relative path under two roots named, AND either root alone stays clean so a single-root lane is not falsely reddened; canonical-path dedupe pinned so a refactor cannot reintroduce a false red. Unreadable / wrong-declaration / multi-dir / clean-tree / process-boundary controls unchanged and green.

GATES (all exit 0): test-jvm-implementation.sh (23 suites), test-jvm-tools.sh (five-root lane), test-fast-pr.sh (incl. CLJS node 12263 tests), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 CI pin with CI's exact --lint set, errors: 0. Rebased onto 4a9cfc71e7 (rf2-g7p7l) before the final gate run.

INCIDENTAL, left alone deliberately: top-level implementation/deps.edn :test resolves a test/ root that does not exist; it is not on the JVM roster and is never invoked, and roster policy was explicitly out of scope.

title: AUDIT: every published clock row is an IN-PAGE window, and an in-page window mis-reads a substrate arm by 300-610%
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01). This is the run's strongest
methodological finding and it is about the PUBLISHED rows, not the candidate.

rf2-0qj9w took both instruments on the SAME operations in the SAME samples: an
in-page performance.now() window around the substrate's own flushSync (which is
what p0_converge_app, p0_arms, hd8_rows and coldmount_app all use), and Chrome's
renderer counters over CDP read after the browser produced the frame the
operation caused.

MEASURED, run 5, ratio to the floor in that round of that segment:

  M1 mount        in-page          frame-inclusive
  reagent-subs    5.6068x          1.1321x     (+395%)
  uix-subs        4.7394x          1.1530x     (+311%)
  hicasso         8.7318x          1.3613x     (+541%)

  bulk300
  reagent-subs    5.8048x          1.0243x     (+467%)
  uix-subs        4.3333x          1.0242x     (+323%)
  hicasso         7.2986x          1.0266x     (+611%)

The error is NOT a scale factor that cancels in a ratio -- it differs per arm by
hundreds of points. On M1 the in-page window would put hicasso/reagent-subs at
1.56x where the frame-inclusive clock reads 1.21x.

The reason is in the decomposition: a substrate arm's mount spends roughly a
third of its frame-inclusive cost inside flushSync and the rest afterwards in
style, layout and paint -- and the AFTERWARDS half is where the three substrates
differ least, because they build byte-identical DOM. Measuring only the first
half exaggerates the difference between them.

The pure-React control arms differ by only 6-13% on the same comparison, which
is exactly how a lane that checks only its controls in-page would never see this.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. It does not overturn M1 mount 1.0150x or
bulk-broad 0.6291x: those are Reagent against UIx on a different harness and a
page whose two readings are closer. It does say that no published clock row in
this programme has ever been checked against a frame-inclusive instrument, and
that the check is cheap now that one exists.

SEQUENCING: this raises rf2-rguy1 (the krausest/js-framework-benchmark external
cross-check, which drives chromedriver and reads Chrome's timeline) from a
nicety to the next question. Two independent frame-inclusive instruments
agreeing would settle it; two disagreeing would be worth more than either row.

title: hicasso: the registry-epoch and node-key axes still have no counterpart in the epoch sum
description:
SCOPED OUT of rf2-2rtt6.42 DELIBERATELY, and filed rather than left implied.

rf2-2rtt6.42 closed the STAGED-read tear on the VERSION axis by giving the
epoch-sum getSnapshot a term that does not depend on a watch existing: a key
with no cell contributes its frame's `commit-basis` = the runtime's flush
generation + `re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch`. Two of the predecessor's
three compared fields are still uncovered, and for the same structural reason
rf2-2rtt6.33 gave.

1. REGISTRY-EPOCH. `observation/registry-epoch*` is bumped on every `:sub`
   registration (first-time AND replacement), which is how the observation
   port sees an HMR re-registration land in the render->commit gap. A
   re-registration is not a frame-state install, so it does not move
   `frame-commit-epoch` and does not move `commit-basis`. Row 3 of
   `generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test` is this case and is unmoved by
   rf2-2rtt6.42 -- correctly, since that row uses a RETAINED key, and closing
   the axis for a retained key means adding a registry term to EVERY key's
   contribution, i.e. re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration.
   That is a real design decision (bead rf2-2rtt6.42's candidate (b)), not a
   defect fix, and it wants costing before it is taken.
   BLOCKER IF TAKEN: `registry-epoch*` is `^:private` with no public reader,
   so this needs a substrate change (expose a reader) before the arm can read
   it at all. That is why rf2-2rtt6.42 did not fold it in as a one-liner.

2. NODE-KEY (a same-id frame REINCARNATION). `frame/dissoc-frame!` clears the
   destroyed frame's commit-epoch entry, so a same-id successor RESTARTS at 0
   -- `observation_port_cljs_test` asserts exactly that ("frame-commit-epoch
   ties across the reincarnation (epoch restarted)"). `commit-basis` is
   therefore monotone only WITHIN one incarnation, which is precisely why the
   observation port carries `:node-key` as a third field rather than trusting
   the two epochs. Arm 1 observes node identity nowhere.

REACHABILITY, honestly: (1) is an HMR / dev-time hazard, not a production
one -- an app that never re-registers a sub never moves the registry epoch.
(2) needs a frame destroyed and re-created under the same id while a boundary
is between its render and its commit; `runtime/forget-frame-ops!` exists for
the reincarnation case but is not wired to anything that would correct a
staged read. Neither is the P0 that rf2-2rtt6.42 was; both are the honest
remainder of "one comparison covers three fields", and the record should not
be allowed to imply otherwise.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRITTEN DOWN: `arm1/runtime.cljs`'s `commit-basis`
docstring and the ns docstring's "commit basis" section both name this bead.
notes:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW CORROBORATION + one refinement (origin/main @ 40e309600e, read-only).

CORROBORATED, and stronger than the bead claims for itself. I tried to construct a FOURTH axis
and could not, and the reason is structural:
  - The epoch SUM is provably sound. Every term in `make-snapshot` (arm1/runtime.cljs:711-723) is
    non-decreasing — a cell epoch is re-stamped only inside `flush!`, AFTER `(vswap! !generation inc)`
    (:519-523), so the new stamp strictly exceeds the old; a staged key's commit-time term is the
    cell's birth basis, which is >= the basis the render read. So Sum_commit >= Sum_render with
    equality IFF no term moved. Sum collision is impossible, and `Object.is` on it is exact.
  - Every physical frame-state install goes through exactly three sites — `adapter/replace-container!`
    against a frame-state container appears at frame.cljc:1406, :1540, :1563 — and all three bump
    (frame.cljc:1321-1326). The `identical?`-noop short-circuit at :1401-1402 skips the bump only
    when nothing is installed, so no value can have moved.
  - Every subscription in this substrate is a pure function of frame state: there is no
    `reg-sub-raw` and no external-signal registration kind (subs.cljc exposes `:input-signals`
    for the `:static` kind only). So there is no "sub over an external source" axis.
Conclusion: the two axes this bead names really are the two.

REFINEMENT WORTH FOLDING IN — a THIRD FACE of the reincarnation axis, which a reader will trip
over in the source and not recognise. The epoch bump is deliberately FENCED on owner loss
(frame.cljc:1401-1407 and :1568-1570): the install lands in the captured container but the bump is
suppressed so it cannot attribute to a same-id successor. That is an install that genuinely
happened and genuinely did not move the basis. It is reachable only when the boundary's own
incarnation is already gone, so it collapses into `:node-key` — but this bead should name it,
because "installs always bump" has a visible counter-example in the source.

RE-CHECK ITEM: 2d1f36866d ("a movement witness retires the wasted layer-1 compare", subs/spine)
landed after the tree this arm was written against. `acquire-cell!`'s watch gates on `(= old nu)`
(arm1/runtime.cljs:483) and this arm uses the notification ITSELF as the dirty signal, so the
sub layer's notification discipline is load-bearing here in a way it is not for the shipping
spine. Worth one read against the post-2d1f36866d tree.

Full review: ai/findings/2026-08-01.hicasso-landed-adapter-adversarial-review.md (gitignored).
COSTING DONE, BROAD OPTION DECLINED, BOTH AXES CLOSED BY A NARROWER ROUTE.
Branch worker/axes-2rtt6-44. No substrate change: registry-epoch* stays ^:private,
no public reader added, NO SPEC SURFACE TOUCHED.

THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. Neither axis was a blind spot in the epoch sum. Both events
DISPOSE the reaction an Arm 1 cell holds -- a :sub re-registration via
subs.cache/invalidate-sub-on-replace!, a frame destruction via frame teardown -- and
the spine's derived container does (reset! watchers {}) in -dispose (spine.cljs:949),
taking the arm's add-watch with it. MEASURED on the pre-fix runtime:
  registry:  read returns 2 where the live registration answers 20; next write
             notified 0 times; read after it returns 3 where the new handler gives 30.
  node-key:  read returns 1 where the successor holds 99; 0 notifications; still 1
             after a write on B.
  frame-commit-epoch A=1, 0 after dissoc-frame!, B=1 -- the basis TIES EXACTLY across
  the reincarnation, so no arithmetic over those two terms could separate them.
So the boundary is permanently deaf and derives through the RETIRED COMPUTATION (not a
stale value that tracks the db -- a stale computation, which looks alive).

WHY THE REGISTRY TERM WAS DECLINED. (a) It corrects nothing: the extra render a moved
number buys calls read-key!, finds the cell, derefs the disposed reaction. Pinned as an
assertion -- the held container answers 7 where the live registration answers 70.
(b) Frequency: registry-epoch* bumps per :sub registration, first-time AND replacement;
one HMR save re-registers a namespace = 8-15 reg-sub forms in this repo's own example
corpus (max 15, examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs). (c) Blast radius: the

updateSyncExternalStore(:8162) pushes updateStoreInstance on a moved snapshot ->
checkIfSnapshotChanged(:8250) -> forceStoreRerender(:8260); and pushStoreConsistencyCheck
(:8225) is recorded on every NON-BLOCKING lane, with isRenderConsistentWithExternalStores
(:16841) discarding the ENTIRE CONCURRENT RENDER PASS if any recorded snapshot moved.
Net: up to 15 whole-tree concurrent-render invalidations per HMR save, plus a forced
re-render per in-flight boundary, for ZERO correction.

WHAT WAS TAKEN. The substrate's own disposal event. wire-cell! arms
interop/add-on-dispose! ONCE PER UNIQUE KEY; invalidate-cell! synchronously drops the
reaction (read-key! then treats the cell exactly as a key with no cell and goes through
subscribe-once, so every render from that instant computes against the live registration
and the live frame) and rebuilds the durable attachment on a macrotask (deferred: the
callback fires inside the registrar's replacement hook and inside frame teardown, neither
a place to subscribe). A frame that did not come back is disposed instead.

NODE-KEY. Closed by the same event. frame/frame-incarnation-token is ALREADY PUBLIC
(frame.cljc:877) and would have been the cheap reader, but it is not needed and is
strictly worse: a token compare could only FLAG the reincarnation, where this repairs it.

FENCES HELD. Shell still 2 hooks (asserted). subscribe still closes over the read set
alone -- make-subscribe is untouched by the diff. Snapshot arithmetic untouched. No
candidate ledger; retained-inventory absences unchanged and asserted.

WITNESS. arm1/disposed_cell_cljs_test, 5 rows / 22 assertions, both failures carried as
their own deliberately-* rows. Mutation: removing the single add-on-dispose! line reds 8
assertions across all four substantive rows. generation_fence_coverage's assertions are
UNCHANGED and still pass -- the basis is still blind to both axes and should be; its
docstring now reads as a standing statement of scope.

NOTE: the witness's first green was FALSE -- rebuild assertions inside a setTimeout under
a fn-form fixture resolved after the run was reported (18 assertions, all sync). Now uses
cljs.test/async + the fixture's :async? true map form; count is 22.

title: UNEXPLAINED: run 3's 34% bulk300 floor seam is beyond 38,000 null draws AND beyond every load-ladder rung
description:
LEFT UNEXPLAINED by rf2-cvvb7 (PR #7360), which refused to smooth it over. Filed so it is not quietly forgotten.

WHAT rf2-cvvb7 ESTABLISHED, and it is a strong negative result. A load ladder of 19 runs at a STATED number of competing busy cores (0/2/4/8/12/20 of 24) found the cross-segment floor seam DOES NOT RESPOND TO LOAD AT ALL: 4.3% at zero cores, 4.6% at twenty, while the ladder unquestionably moved the box (floor +80%). Not a threshold, not a gradient, not bimodal. It is also NOT segment-attributable — under an exact within-round relabelling null, no run reached p < 0.2 and every observed seam sat at or below the null's median (5.5%; q95 14.1%). The variation lives on the ROUND, not the segment. And the perturbation is MULTIPLICATIVE, so floor-normalisation cancels it exactly: ctl-2x/floor moved 6.5% across an 80% floor span and moved the WRONG WAY for additivity (corr +0.41), while the bar row moved with neither the floor (-0.10) nor the seam (-0.18).

SO THE ORIGINAL PREMISE IS REFUTED: the seam is not what a loaded box does to the three-segment design. Section 6's ground 3 is withdrawn as refuted; the bulk rows stay refused on the grounds that hold.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED: run 3's bulk300 read 3.147 / 2.437 / 2.349 ms across the three segments — a 34% spread. That figure is BEYOND ALL 38,000 NULL DRAWS and BEYOND EVERY LADDER RUNG. Nothing in 19 controlled runs reproduced it. The worker had no mechanism for it and said so rather than inventing one.

WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING OPEN: a bench lane that produced a value its own null model says is essentially impossible has either (a) a rare regime nobody has characterised, (b) a defect that fired once, or (c) a recording or attribution error in that run. All three matter. If it is (a), the band that rf2-cvvb7 introduced may not bound it. Note ALSO that the clock-audit page's 31.9% seam is a SINGLE-ROUND figure and therefore routine — the same worker saw 45% in one round of an IDLE run whose pooled seam was 3.8% — so the audit corroborates the observation but not the load attribution, and does not explain run 3 either.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: recover run 3's per-round vectors if they survive anywhere (the producing worktree may be gone; check transcripts before concluding they are lost — that is how rf2-b0tz5's observations were recovered). If the raw record is unrecoverable, say so and mark the figure as an unreproduced outlier rather than reconstructing it. DO NOT re-take the ensemble to chase it; the operator has deferred measurement and the band already bounds published rows honestly.

SEQUENCING: low priority. It is a loose end on an instrument question that is otherwise settled, and it must not displace rf2-yd52q (the bulk-broad re-take) or rf2-rguy1 (the external cross-check).
