title: MEASURE: cross-check our clock harness against krausest/js-framework-benchmark — an instrument nobody here wrote
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01), who asked whether we should be considering https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark. Verified from the repository rather than recalled.

WHAT IT IS: 12 measured operations — create 1,000 rows; replace all; partial update (every 10th row); select row; swap rows; remove row; create 10,000 rows; append to a large table; clear; plus ready/run/update memory — with additional replace-memory, repeated-clear-memory and startup metrics, and Lighthouse figures (TimeToConsistentlyInteractive, ScriptBootUpTime, MainThreadWorkCost, TotalByteWeight). Driven by chromedriver against Chrome's timeline, with 5 warmup iterations. 186 implementations. Framework entries live under frameworks/[keyed|non-keyed]/<Name>, need npm install + npm run build-prod, FIXED version numbers (no ranges), the reference implementation's exact button ids, and must pass npm run rebuild-ci.

WHY IT IS WORTH USING HERE, and it is not mainly about the leaderboard: THIS SESSION FOUND FIVE DEFECTS IN OUR OWN MEASUREMENT APPARATUS — a contaminated run under load, a stale bundle silently measured after a par-compile abort, a segment-order effect, a null a confounded design could not have produced, and a 'held-out' rung that was an exact algebraic identity of the checks it was meant to validate. Every one was caught by auditing ourselves, which worked but cost a great deal. AN INSTRUMENT NOBODY HERE WROTE SIDESTEPS THAT WHOLE CLASS.

ITS OPERATIONS MAP ONTO EXACTLY WHAT IS UNMEASURED: create-1000 is mount; partial-update-every-10th is narrow; replace-all and swap are bulk. Those are the clock rows Hicasso has never taken. And it reports memory ALONGSIDE duration, which is the direct way to see whether the 415 B/read proxy shows up on the clock at all.

THE LIMITS, stated so nobody over-reads it: its app is a table of rows with essentially trivial state. re-frame2's value is subscription fan-out, frame isolation and boundary-scoped reactivity, NONE of which that workload exercises. It can say whether Hicasso's RENDERING is competitive with React/Vue/Svelte/Solid; it cannot say whether the reactivity design earns its keep — the census-derived witnesses still own that half. There is also a real Goodhart risk in optimising for a public leaderboard rather than for the shapes the census found. AND THERE IS NO CLOJURESCRIPT ENTRY among the 186, so there is no Reagent baseline in that harness; one would have to be written for the comparison to mean anything. That is the real cost.

THE RECOMMENDED SHAPE — a CROSS-CHECK, not a new bar:
  1. Implement the benchmark app in Reagent and in Hicasso, locally.
  2. Run both under its driver.
  3. Compare the RATIO against what our own harness reports for the equivalent operations.
  4. If the two instruments agree on the ratio, our clock rows become trustworthy. IF THEY DISAGREE, THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING AVAILABLE — it means our harness has a defect we have not found.

DO NOT upstream an entry yet. That is a maintenance commitment and pre-alpha is the wrong time; it is a separate decision once the numbers are known.

title: MEASURE: the bulk clock rows' cross-segment floor seam (22-34%) exceeds the effect they measure
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01), and SOFTENED by its own run 5.

The candidate's clock instrument refuses bulk300/bulk100/narrow, and one of its
three grounds is the cross-segment floor seam. The SAME floor arm -- identical
work, no substrate, untouched by which adapter is installed -- read
3.147 / 2.437 / 2.349 ms across the three segments on run 3's bulk300. A 34%
spread, against 23% on bulk100 and 22% on narrow.

Floor-normalisation cancels a MULTIPLICATIVE seam and not an additive one, so a
bar row formed across segments that disagree by 34% is quoting the seam.

BUT RUN 5, taken on a genuinely idle box, read seams of 3.8% / 8.4% / 5.7% on
the same three rows with NOTHING CHANGED but how busy the machine was. So the
seam is not a structural property of the three-segment design; it is what a
loaded box does to it. That is worth knowing and is still worth pinning down,
because a bench lane whose seam swings 3.8% -> 34% on machine load cannot tell a
reader which regime a given published row was taken in.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a run that alternates segments WITHIN a round, or that
prices the seam with a second floor taken at the segment's other end, would say
whether the residue is an order effect, GC, or the adapter install itself -- and
would give every future row a seam number to be judged against rather than a

The in-page reading lands INSIDE the published row's own run-mean spread

arm pays in the write leg before React is involved). Both pages already document

per frame. p0_converge_app runs an entire row in ONE macrotask by design —
dotimes inside doseq inside mapv — which lane/settle!'s docstring explains and
defends. Adding a settle between samples flushes Reagent's macrotask-scheduled
disposals that currently accumulate across the row, so the result is a NEW row
rather than a re-take. The re-take therefore needs a purpose-built
frame-inclusive bulk harness, and it must state what it changed.

which drives chromedriver and reads Chrome's timeline) should be pointed at THIS
row first — two independent frame-inclusive instruments agreeing would settle it,

title: MEASURE: ctl-2x is mis-specified for an UPDATE row -- it doubles the page, not the changed set
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01).

The lane's clock control is the floor at exactly twice the boundaries, and the
prediction written against it is 2.00x. On a MOUNT row that is right and it
passes: rf2-0qj9w measured 1.845x [1.5365 - 2.1136], every round inside the
+/-25% band under the strict rule.

On an UPDATE row it is wrong by construction. Doubling the page does not double
the work of a commit: rf2-0qj9w's decomposition measured layout scaling 1.79x
where the element count scaled 2.00x, and the non-layout half of the floor's
update barely moved at all. So even a perfect instrument reads below 2.00 on a
bulk row, and the three bulk controls failing at 1.70-1.82x is partly the
CONTROL being mis-specified rather than the clock being wrong.

THE REPAIR: a control that doubles the CHANGED SET at fixed page size -- e.g.
one commit writing 2K cells of a page that already holds 2K boundaries, against
one writing K of the same page. The prediction is then about the quantity the
row is actually about.

This is not a licence to move a threshold after a run. The 2.00x prediction
stands for every mount row; what this bead asks for is a DIFFERENT control for a
different question, registered before the run that uses it.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
SUPERSEDED BY THE REPAIR IT ASKED FOR, AND ITS DIAGNOSIS IS HALF RIGHT.
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7367

THIS BEAD'S DIAGNOSIS: ctl-2x doubles the PAGE, and doubling the page does
not double an UPDATE's work, so a bulk row's control is mis-specified. That
much is true and is now measured directly -- but it is not what was wrong.
rf2-emvod showed ctl-2x undershoots on the MOUNT row too (1.8173x), which no
update-row argument reaches, and one additive constant fits all four rows.

THE REPAIR THIS BEAD ASKED FOR -- a control that doubles the CHANGED SET at
fixed page size -- would NOT have worked: (2D+c)/(D+c) has the same shape as
(2W+c)/(W+c), so it would have produced a differently wrong number. What was
built instead is rf2-emvod's THREE-POINT control, which differences c away
rather than estimating it.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THIS BEAD, and it is the load-bearing half: CHOOSING THE
DIRTY SET AS THE AXIS IS RIGHT, and for a reason this bead did not claim. It
lets the control's arms build the FLOOR'S OWN PAGE -- same 300 boundaries,
same 901 elements -- so they stay INSIDE the canonical-DOM fairness gate
instead of being exempted from it the way ctl-2x is. All 15 non-control arms
hashed identically on every row. A page-scaling control has to be exempted
from the gate that would check it; a dirty-set control does not. That is
this bead's real contribution and the record says so.

ALSO CONFIRMED HERE, quantitatively: the update-row mis-specification is
real. c(2x) re-measured on this run is 1.0397 / 0.6763 / 0.9470 ms on
bulk300 / bulk100 / narrow -- 25-35% of a floor sample that does not scale
when the page doubles, which is exactly why ctl-2x cannot read 2.00.

THE OUTCOME: the three-point control refuses on all three bulk rows
(1.4280 / 2.1722 / 1.6014x against 2.0101x), so BULK IS STILL NOT
ADJUDICABLE -- but the reason has MOVED. It was blocked because the only
control was mis-specified (this bead). It is now blocked because a correctly
specified control refuses, for reasons that are properties of the page
(paint saturating, so the cost is not affine in the dirty set) and of the
instrument (a noise floor an order of magnitude too high for a strict
per-block difference-of-differences verdict). Both measured; see rf2-7iqb5's
close for the numbers.

'This is not a licence to move a threshold after a run' -- honoured. The
2.00x prediction was not moved; the control's prediction is 2.0101x derived
from the page's own declared dirty counts, registered before the run, and
the refusal is recorded as a refusal. The band is untouched by this change,
deliberately.

Closing as superseded: the repair is built, its axis is this bead's, and the
remaining work is not this bead's question. M1's mount row is filed
separately as rf2-jcm3p.

MEASURED, not argued: an arm's devtools term less the tare's baseline tracks that arm's own in-page window - floor 0.62 ms against an in-page 0.40, reagent-subs 2.76 against 2.30, uix-subs 2.01 against 1.60, hicasso 3.26 against 2.80 (one bulk300 run). The tell needed no arithmetic and was on the page already: on a substrate arm the in-page ABSOLUTE exceeds the taskNet absolute, which no superset can do. It went unnoticed because the driver printed only their ratio.

So taskNet is a frame-ONLY clock - style, layout, paint, with the script taken out - and very nearly the COMPLEMENT of the in-page window rather than a superset of it.

WHAT THIS TOUCHES. Every magnitude on docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md is stated on taskNet:
  - M1 'hicasso / reagent-subs 1.2107x'. On raw TaskDuration, rf2-yd52q's 8-run ensemble reads 1.4896x [1.3488 - 1.5989]. The candidate's mount deficit is MATERIALLY WORSE than published, not better.
  - 'hicasso / uix-subs 1.1865x' reads 1.5001x [1.4313 - 1.6544].
  - The keystroke row's task figures.
  - The 4.1 table 'an in-page window mis-reads a substrate arm by 300-610%' - the separation is real but the mechanism named for it is wrong; the two windows are complements, not a subset and a superset.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE. clock_run.cjs now reports every bar, the band and the control on BOTH clocks side by side (blob e145597127a87983377bd1a7ca40ca0388dfc18c). The banked primary is deliberately unchanged so no published row is silently restated.

THE CORRECTED CLOCK VALIDATES ITSELF on a row it did not fit: the donor bar on M1 reads 1.0011x [0.9464 - 1.0763] over 8 runs against a published M1 mount 1.0150x [0.9820 - 1.0480], and 0.9996x over the 4 control-passing runs. The frame-only clock reads that row 4% high and the in-page clock 10% low.

SCOPE: re-adjudicate the candidate's rows on raw TaskDuration, decide whether taskNet stays reported at all, and reconcile 4.1's mechanism statement. Full record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/bulk-broad-re-taken.md

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RE-ADJUDICATED. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7365

THE THIRD DEFECT, and it is what reconciles the three mount numbers. taskNet is
not one quantity. DevToolsCommandDuration bills page script only when that
script runs INSIDE a protocol command, so the same subtraction is frame-ONLY on
a harness driving through page.evaluate and script-AND-frame on one driving
through page.click or keyboard.press. Measured within one instrument in one run:
ScriptDuration reads 0.063 ms for a 901-element mount on the evaluate-driven M1
row and 49.97 ms for the keystroke control on the Input-driven row, while the
devtools term varies 7.836 ms across arms on the first and 0.069 ms on the
second. Confirmed on the cross-check harness directly: devtools spread 0.126 ms
against a ScriptDuration spread of 13.97 ms, and its ratios move <=1.7%.

So clock_run.cjs's M1/bulk300/bulk100/narrow were corrupted; its keystroke row
and the WHOLE of rf2-rguy1's cross-check were NOT, and need no restatement.

THE RECONCILIATION. 1.2107x is not a member of the comparison - it is on the
other clock. What remains: workload 1.4896 -> 1.2789 (ours throughout, ~7-17%,
loose) and instrument 1.2789 -> 1.1756 (same app, 8.8%, mechanism already
published - our window contains the post-paint macrotask). That the legs
multiply to the whole gap is ARITHMETIC, not evidence (a/b x b/c = a/c), and the
page says so; what carries it is that the previously invisible leg is
ELIMINATED. This invalidates the cross-check page's "workload moves it 5.6%",
which compared a frame-only reading with a script-and-frame one - corrected
there and in validation.md.

THE ROWS, 7 runs (one of eight discarded on a stated pre-condition):
  M1        1.3737x [1.3289-1.4331]  taskNet 1.1143  - 7/7 clear their band
  bulk300   1.1494x                  taskNet 1.0703  - REFUSED, control 3/7
  bulk100   1.1089x                  taskNet 0.9859  - REFUSED, SIGN CHANGE
  narrow    1.0236x                  taskNet 1.0352  - PARITY, instrument-limited
  keystroke 1.0049x                  taskNet 1.0078  - unadjudicated; uncorrupted

THE PUBLISHED M1 MAGNITUDE STAYS rf2-yd52q's 1.4896x, not my 1.3737x. My
pre-registered CORROBORATION control FAILED - the donor bar read 0.9394x
[0.8958-0.9837] against the published 1.0150x [0.9820-1.0480] - and the M1 floor
ran 5.98-6.95 ms, ABOVE the whole 3.06-5.50 ms range of rf2-cvvb7's 19-run load
ladder. Outside the calibrated regime, so the ensemble publishes a REGIME and
not the magnitude. Recorded as failed, not widened.

PREDICTIONS: E1 guard PASS, E2 control PASS (including its predicted failure),
E3 narrow-below-1.0 REFUTED and recorded as refuted, E4 bulk-above-1.0 PASS,
E5 the door PASS (27% against 0.3%).

rf2-7iqb5 IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT - the finding it needs. ctl-2x
undershoots on the MOUNT row too (1.8173x), which "mis-specified for an update
row" does not predict. One additive constant fits all four rows: c = 1.040 /
1.043 / 0.873 / 0.790 ms across a 901-element cold mount and a one-cell write.
Doubling the CHANGED SET leaves c untouched - (2D+c)/(D+c) has the same shape.
What removes it is a THREE-POINT control: dirty eps, D, 2D, adjudicated as
(T(2D)-T(eps))/(T(D)-T(eps)). NOT DONE HERE: it is a new arm in the page half
and would have changed the blobs this ensemble was taken at.

taskNet STAYS REPORTED, as a labelled frame-only diagnostic and never as a
figure a row is stated on - the gap between the two windows is how the door is
measured. Raw TaskDuration is now the published clock, and every gate that
adjudicated taskNet now adjudicates the published figure: arm-order guard on
both clocks, band ceiling on both, control on both.

ALSO: the JSON dataset now carries roundsTask and inPageRounds so a run's
published figures are recomputable from the file (rf2-cvvb7's durable-evidence
gap); clock_readjudicate.cjs makes the ensemble arithmetic a program that does
not select runs; jsfb_serve.cjs runs the cross-check without the upstream clone
and warns when its stylesheet is absent.

WITHDRAWN IN FLIGHT: a post-paint split meant to price the instrument leg raced
the renderer (93.3% of one arm's time after the mid-point, 1.2% of another's).
Code removed, attempt recorded. Also corrected my own tautology - an earlier
commit presented a/b x b/c = a/c as a verification.

Run 8 breached the band ceiling at 26.2%/28.4% - the 2nd and 3rd firings that
gate has had. Run 3 exited 0: the first fully clean five-row run this instrument
has produced.

title: MEASURE: re-take bulk broad with a control that doubles the CHANGED SET, not the page
description:
RAISED by rf2-rguy1's cross-check run (PR #7359), and it is the same repair rf2-0qj9w already filed for its own bulk rows — now with a second run that hit it.

THE FAULT. Every positive control this lane has for a bulk or update row scales the PAGE. On a mount row the work scales with it and the control passes; on an update row it does not, so even a perfect instrument reads below the predicted factor. rf2-rguy1's control took the other form — create-10,000 against create-1,000, exactly 10x the rows — and FAILED HIGH: 13.696 / 13.583 / 13.112x on Reagent, Hicasso and UIx against a band of 8-13x registered before the run. All three arms overshoot by 1-5%, so what it caught is the WORKLOAD scaling superlinearly (the script term grows faster than layout and style at 10k on every arm), not an instrument mis-reading one arm.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. An equal overshoot divides out of an arm-to-arm ratio, so rf2-rguy1's ratios are not invalidated by it. But under this lane's strict rule a failed control is a caveat on the rows it guards, and no control this programme currently has can certify a bulk or update row cleanly.

THE REPAIR, which is a different instrument rather than a wider band: a control that holds PAGE SIZE FIXED and doubles the CHANGED SET. Update every 10th row against every 5th row on the same 1,000-row table is the obvious form — element count, layout and paint are constant, only the dirty set doubles, and the prediction is 2.00x on the commit-side work.

Cheap to add to the rf2-rguy1 harness: it needs one more button on the three benchmark arms and one more row in jsfb_ours_run.cjs. The apps are at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/jsfb_*.

Blocked on nothing.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT — measured by rf2-emvod (PR #7365).

THE PREMISE IS HALF RIGHT. This bead's diagnosis is that a page-doubling control
is mis-specified for an UPDATE row, whose work does not double with the page.
That predicts the MOUNT row should be clean. It is not: over seven runs ctl-2x
reads 1.8173x on M1, against 1.7334 / 1.7696 / 1.7796 on bulk300 / bulk100 /
narrow. The mount row undershoots by 9% and no update-row argument reaches it.

AN ADDITIVE CONSTANT FITS ALL FOUR AT ONCE. A ratio of two arms one of which is
twice the other reads (2W + c)/(W + c), which is below 2 for any positive c and
does not care whether the row is a mount or an update. Inverting it:

  row       ctl-2x(task)   c/W     implied c    floor tared
  M1           1.8173     0.224     1.040 ms      5.695 ms
  bulk300      1.7334     0.364     1.043 ms      3.911 ms
  bulk100      1.7696     0.299     0.873 ms      3.788 ms
  narrow       1.7796     0.283     0.790 ms      3.584 ms

c = 0.79-1.04 ms across rows that do wildly different work — a 901-element cold
mount and a one-cell write — on floors spanning 3.58 to 5.70 ms. One constant
fits all four; 'mis-specified for updates' fits none of the mount row.

WHY THE FILED REPAIR IS NOT ENOUGH. Doubling the CHANGED SET at fixed page size
removes the update-row confound and leaves c exactly where it is, because
(2D + c)/(D + c) has the same shape as (2W + c)/(W + c). The control would still
undershoot, and it would still fail the strict rule.

THE REPAIR THAT WORKS is a THREE-POINT linearity control — dirty epsilon, dirty
D, dirty 2D at fixed page size — adjudicated as

    (T(2D) - T(eps)) / (T(D) - T(eps))  ->  2.00

which differences the constant away regardless of its size, and needs no claim
about what c is. Prediction 2.00x with the lane's usual slack, registered before
the run that tests it.

NOT DONE IN rf2-emvod, deliberately: it is a new arm in the page half
(clock_app.cljs / clock_views.cljs), which would have changed the blobs that
bead's ensemble was taken at and forced the whole ensemble to be re-taken.

This bead stays BLOCKING for bulk300 / bulk100 / narrow. On the corrected clock
those rows read 1.1494x / 1.1089x / 1.0236x with controls holding on only 3, 2
and 4 runs of seven, so they are still refused as magnitudes.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
BUILT AS RULED, AND IT REFUSES. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7367

THE FILED REPAIR IS NOT WHAT WAS BUILT, per this bead's own newest note. The
description asks for a control that doubles the CHANGED SET; the 2026-08-01
note supersedes it, because doubling the changed set leaves c untouched --
(2D+c)/(D+c) has the same shape as (2W+c)/(W+c). What was built is the ruled
THREE-POINT control, adjudicated as (T(2D)-T(eps))/(T(D)-T(eps)), in which c
is neither estimated nor bounded but CANCELS. It is also invariant under the
MULTIPLICATIVE block perturbation rf2-cvvb7 measured; ctl-2x survives only
that second one.

THE VERDICT: 1.4280 / 2.1722 / 1.6014x on bulk300 / bulk100 / narrow against
a pre-registered 2.0101x. Refusal on all three under the strict rule.
BULK IS STILL NOT ADJUDICABLE, and no bulk magnitude is published.

THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT WHAT FAILED, and this is the finding. The SAME
statistic on LayoutDuration alone -- collected per block for this purpose,
since the existing decomposition reports it as a pooled mean that cannot be
adjudicated -- reads 1.9703 / 2.1218 / 1.9889x, within 5.5% of prediction on
every row. The constant really does cancel. What refuses it is the PAGE:

  row       marginal us/cell [1,100]  [100,200]   on LayoutDuration
  bulk300   9.348                     3.124       3.543 -> 3.354
  bulk100   7.654                     4.512       3.167 -> 3.443
  narrow    7.434                     4.084       3.321 -> 3.186

Layout's marginal cost is flat to within 8%; task's halves or thirds. ~6
us/cell of NON-LAYOUT cost exists over [1,100] and has gone by [100,200] --
paint saturating once the damage region covers the viewport. A saturating
function of the very axis the control varies is NOT a constant, so no
differencing removes it.

c RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY rather than taken from rf2-emvod: c(2x) =
1.0397 / 0.6763 / 0.9470 ms. bulk300 reproduces rf2-emvod's 1.043 ms to
three decimals on a separate run. c is 25-35% of a floor sample.

A 3,000-CELL RESCUE WAS TRIED AND FAILED WORSE -- recorded, not discarded.
The constant scales with the page too (c(3pt) 7.93 vs 1.24 ms), so T/dT
barely moved; and the arms got NOISIER (within-block IQR 30-48% vs the
floor's 28%) because each sample allocates a 9,001-element React tree.
Per-block ratio [0.09, 9.63], one negative denominator in eighteen.

THE CONDITION THIS INSTRUMENT DOES NOT MEET, as arithmetic: a difference of
differences amplifies relative noise by T/dT, so the control needs
sigma(T)/T <= s/(2 sqrt2 . T/dT) ~ 3.5% against a measured within-block IQR
of 28-48%. It does NOT depend on which three points are chosen or how large
the page is, because T and dT scale together. So the refusals have two
independent causes stacked: a page not affine in the dirty set, and a noise
floor that would forbid a strict per-block verdict even if it were.

THE CONTROL CAN FAIL, shown two ways. Live: HCLOCK_CTL3_SABOTAGE=140 makes
the 2D arm render 140 while still DECLARING 200; the control refused at
1.1309x while the arm-order guard stayed reportable on both clocks, 0 of
3024 writes unverified, canonical DOM identical, band 10.9%. It was the only
gate that fired. Offline: --selftest runs 11 fixtures, no browser, fatal
every run -- superlinear refuses, declaring-200-rendering-140 refuses, a
degenerate denominator refuses rather than passing quietly, one bad block in
nine refuses.

SENSITIVITY STATED: at 1/100/200 a power law d^k is refused below k~0.55 and
above k~1.33. An equally spaced 1:2:3 design never reads below ln3/ln2 =
1.585 and could refuse NO sublinear workload -- which is why the ruled
placement, refuted first, is the one that ships.

ctl-2x is DEMOTED to a reported diagnostic on bulk rows, not deleted: it
still supplies the band. THE BAND IS UNTOUCHED, deliberately -- moving it in
the same change that repairs the control would make the repair
unfalsifiable.

RUN HYGIENE: guard reportable on BOTH clocks on all three rows, 0 unverified
of 3024 per row, canonical DOM identical across all 15 non-control arms (the
control's arms included -- keeping the floor's page is what bought that),
bands 20.1/13.8/15.7% taskNet and 16.1/12.3/17.5% TaskDuration, all under
the ceiling. REGIME: floors 2.70-2.98 ms, BELOW the 3.06 ms bottom of
rf2-cvvb7's ladder -- outside the calibrated range at the quiet end, stated
as the extrapolation it is (rf2-h8o80).

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS in-branch: I had written 'three blocks' where the
dataset says one negative denominator, and 'inside the ladder' where the
floors are below it. Both fixed in place.

M1 IS NOT COVERED and cannot be by a changed-set control -- a mount has no
changed-set axis. It keeps ctl-2x and its 1.8173x undershoot, so the
headline mount figure is still stated under a failing control. Filed as
rf2-jcm3p; it needs a ruling, not a measurement.

CORRECTNESS — THE NEW GATE CAN PASS WITH THE SIGNAL BACKWARDS. `ctl3Verdict` accepts a block solely when `(T(200)-T(1))/(T(100)-T(1))` lands in band; it never requires either difference, or the fitted slope, to be positive. That is exactly the outcome-based selection the aggregate law added in #7312 forbids: a direction-only split remains one ensemble observation because dropping it selects on the result and narrows/moves the estimate. Preserve genuine predeclared validity refusals such as the load-degraded run, but include the quiet M1 direction refusal (its report survives before exit) and recompute the exact red-zone point/CI; if the raw record is unavailable, the precise restatement is not durably warranted and needs a fixed launch set with no outcome-based drops. The missing fixture/test and inconsistent inclusion rule are the bounded residual; no broad rerun or gate redesign unless recomputation materially changes the row.
RULING — INCLUDE RUN 5; THE PUBLISHED M1 MAGNITUDE BECOMES 1.0150x [0.9820-1.0480] (acting mayor, 2026-08-01, under delegated Hicasso authority; OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE).

THE WORKER CORRECTLY FLAGGED A CONFLICT and correctly resolved it in favour of the bead: my resume message said '1.0243x stands', the bead directed recomputation with run 5 included, and the bead governs. My sentence was about the VERDICT (the red zone is closed), not the magnitude, and I should have said so.

WHY RUN 5 MUST BE INCLUDED — this is the substantive point, not a bookkeeping preference. Run 5 was dropped from the four-run set for ONE reason: its M1 strata pointed opposite ways across 1.0. title: hicasso: a read outside the render extent must be a LOUD ERROR, not a missing edge -- four witnesses
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). This is the deepest
consequence of the laziness finding recorded on rf2-2rtt6.

THE FAILURE MODE. A `(sub q)` evaluated outside the boundary's render extent
registers no edge. The boundary then never re-renders when that subscription
moves. The symptom is a permanently stale region of the page with NO error, no
warning and no diagnostic -- the worst bug class this repository has a name for.
Under Arm 1 an eager codec (HD-016's ABI: "nested/lazy sequences are realized
once and flattened one level", docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:337) fixes the
`for` case. It does NOT fix the residue.

THE RESIDUE, four cases that survive an eager codec:
  1. a lazy seq handed straight to React as `children` -- React iterates it
     during the PARENT's reconciliation, after the component function returned;
  2. `(sub q)` inside a render prop passed to a `defhost` / `[:> ...]` component
     -- invoked in the foreign component's render, a different extent and
     possibly a different boundary's;
  3. `(sub q)` inside an event handler (the charter retires `@`-anywhere,
     docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:255-258, but nothing enforces it);
  4. `(sub q)` inside a `delay` / `lazy-seq` the author returns as a prop value.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPOSITORY AND IS THREE LINES. Freehand's
collector refuses a read with no active candidate:

  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc -- `observe!` (426)
  raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render; `with-capture` (380-397) binds the
  candidate for the SYNCHRONOUS body evaluation only, and its docstring already
  names this exact hazard: "A view's children are elements the host renders
  LATER, outside this extent".

Hicasso's design record does not carry that guard anywhere -- not in HD-002, not
in HD-016, not in the HD-002 adjudication.

WHAT TO DO.
  - Pin "a `sub` with no bound collector THROWS" as a v0 runtime obligation, in
    production as well as dev (it is a branch on a nil check, not a subsystem;
    HD-005's zero-cost-when-absent posture is about the evidence sink, not
    about correctness).
  - Add the four cases above to the P1 witness set (validation.md:315-326) as
    named rows, each asserting the throw rather than asserting a re-render.
  - Record the verdict either way. If any of the four CANNOT be made to throw --
    e.g. because the read lands inside another boundary's live extent and is
    silently attributed to it -- say so explicitly; that is a real limit of the
    Surface B ruling and the guide must state it.

WHY P1. The Surface B ruling makes the ambient collector the only acceptable
read surface, so a silent-staleness class in it is a product defect, not a
polish item. It also converts the laziness finding from an open correctness
question into a bounded, testable one.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7329: PARTIAL DISCHARGE, owner stays OPEN. codec/realize-deep now closes the lazy-seq-at-boundary-prop carrier and the nested-boundary-children carrier inside the producing body's collector window; the node and real-Chromium witnesses prove ownership, two later writes, durable edges, teardown, and fail when the one hand-off call is removed. This does not discharge this Bead's explicit-deferral/render-prop remainder: PR #7329 itself correctly records that a delay handed across a boundary and deref'd in the child is the same wrong-owner/permanent-staleness fault, and a foreign render callback can still run under another live boundary extent. Keep the exact owner here; do not create a duplicate or extend realize-deep into forcing delay/function semantics. Finish the remaining loud-error/declared-limit witnesses at their real crossings.

In merge 9d3b423d17a0d971a06de0538ed9ffa880020a7d, realize-entry is (defn- realize-entry [_ _ x] (realize-deep x) nil): map values are checked, keys are not, despite the stated invariant covering every reachable unforced delay. Preserve ordinary map behavior and key/value identity semantics. Also add the originally requested named P1 validation rows, or explicitly record why their normative location changed.

title: MEASURE: rf2-emvod's corroboration control failed and the box no longer explains it
description:
RAISED by rf2-ymi6j, which removed the standing explanation without replacing it.

THE OBSERVATION, unchanged. rf2-emvod's seven-run M1 ensemble had every gate
pass — arm-order guard clean on both clocks, canonical DOM identical, 0
unverified, ctl-2x PASS on 7 of 7, every bar row clearing its own band by 3-6x
— and its PRE-REGISTERED corroboration control FAILED. The donor bar
uix-subs / reagent-subs read 0.9394x [0.8958 - 0.9837] against a published M1
mount of 1.0150x [0.9820 - 1.0480], which rf2-yd52q reproduced at 1.0011x on a
quiet box. Outside the published interval on the ensemble mean and on five of
seven runs.

WHAT HAS CHANGED. rf2-h8o80 attributed it to the box: those runs' M1 floor of
5.98-6.95 ms was said to sit above rf2-cvvb7's whole 3.06-5.50 ms ladder, so
the runs were "outside the regime the band was calibrated in". rf2-ymi6j's
ladder re-take dismantles that on two counts.

  1. The two figures are on TWO CLOCKS — 5.98-6.95 is raw TaskDuration,
     3.06-5.50 is taskNet. The same-sample gap measures +1.337 ms over nineteen
     runs, and emvod's own table gives the M1 gap as +1.401 ms. Converted, that
     ensemble's floors are ~4.58-5.55 ms on the ladder's clock — INSIDE the
     calibrated range.
  2. The band does not widen with load anyway. It is WIDEST ON AN IDLE BOX:
     24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3% at four, corr(band, floor)
     = -0.49, with the floor's per-sample dispersion falling 30.0% -> 15.2% as
     load rises.

So "a busy box" is no longer a mechanism for a donor bar 6% away from a row
three independent ensembles agree on. The failure is now UNEXPLAINED, and it is
the only pre-registered control failure in this lane that is.

WHY IT MATTERS. The corroboration control is the gate that decides whether an
instrument may restate anything. A control that fails for no identified reason
is either finding something real about that ensemble, or is itself noisy enough
that its verdicts do not mean what the pages take them to mean. Both are worth
knowing, and they have opposite consequences for every ensemble that has PASSED
it.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Take the donor bar uix-subs / reagent-subs on M1 across a
load ladder — the same six rungs, raw TaskDuration — and record, at each rung,
the donor bar beside the band. rf2-ymi6j's ladder ran bulk300 only, so this
specific measurement does not exist on the corrected clock. The question is
whether the donor bar's error tracks anything the run can see (band, floor,
per-sample dispersion, seam) or is independent of all of them. Roughly 19 runs
at ~70 s each on a silent box, plus a second row in the plan.

Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/seam_ladder.cjs
(--only M1), clock_run.cjs, and ladder_band.cjs for the arithmetic — the last
already emits a committed compact dataset, so this one will be restatable.
Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md
section 5, and the-band-re-calibrated.md section 4.

description:

THE OBSERVATION. rf2-emvod's seven-run M1 ensemble had every gate pass — arm-order

ladder — while the donor bar was simultaneously 6% away from a row three other
ensembles agree on. A gate that looks healthy exactly where the instrument has
stopped reproducing a known row is the shape of gate that should be checked.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Extend rf2-cvvb7's ladder upward — rungs beyond 20 competing
cores, or the same rungs on a busier baseline — and at each rung record BOTH the
band and the donor bar uix-subs / reagent-subs on M1, whose true value is pinned
by three independent ensembles. The question is whether the band stays predictive
of the donor bar's error as the floor rises past 5.50 ms, or whether it decouples.

If it decouples, the band needs a floor-level precondition attached to it — a row
may only be adjudicated when the floor is inside the calibrated range — and every
page that quotes a band should say which regime it was taken in. rf2-emvod already
states its regime for exactly this reason.

RELATED: rf2-ymi6j (band calibration) is the natural home if it is still open;
this is filed separately because it is a question about the band's DOMAIN rather
than its value.

Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/seam_ladder.cjs
and clock_run.cjs. Ensemble arithmetic: clock_readjudicate.cjs (new in #7365).
Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 5.
close_reason: Hypothesis refuted by rf2-ymi6j's ladder re-take: the band is WIDEST on an idle box (24.6% at 0 cores vs 8.3% at 4, corr(band,floor) = -0.49), both ceiling breaches are at zero load, and this bead's central evidence held a raw-TaskDuration M1 floor against a taskNet bulk300 range — a 1.34 ms clock mismatch that puts emvod's floors INSIDE the calibrated range. The proposed floor-level precondition would refuse the most reproducible runs. The unexplained corroboration-control failure is carried forward as rf2-20pab.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY THE LADDER RE-TAKE (rf2-ymi6j, PR #7368) — the hypothesis is
REFUTED in the direction it was posed, and its central evidence does not
survive either. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-band-re-calibrated.md

THE PREMISE IS A CLOCK MISMATCH. This bead holds emvod's M1 floor of
5.98-6.95 ms against rf2-cvvb7's ladder sweep of 3.06-5.50 ms and concludes
"above the entire ladder". Those are two clocks: the first is raw TaskDuration,
the second taskNet. The same-sample gap is measured on nineteen fresh runs at
+1.337 ms (positive on every one), and emvod's own absolutes table gives the M1
gap as +1.401 ms (task 6.242 against taskNet 4.841). Subtracting emvod's own
figure puts that ensemble's floors at ~4.58-5.55 ms ON THE LADDER'S CLOCK —
inside the calibrated range, its top level with the ladder's top rung. Two
further mismatches sit under the same comparison: it holds an M1 floor (901-
element cold mount) against a bulk300 range (300-cell update), and it uses the
floor as a load gauge.

AND THE MECHANISM RUNS THE OTHER WAY. Nineteen runs at 0/2/4/8/12/20 competing
cores, raw TaskDuration, band by rung:

  0 cores   floor 3.780 ms   per-sample CV 30.0%   band 24.6%
  2 cores   floor 4.386 ms   per-sample CV 22.4%   band 11.8%
  4 cores   floor 5.185 ms   per-sample CV 24.0%   band  8.3%
  8 cores   floor 5.901 ms   per-sample CV 23.9%   band 12.8%
 12 cores   floor 6.933 ms   per-sample CV 21.3%   band 13.2%
 20 cores   floor 6.927 ms   per-sample CV 15.2%   band  9.6%

corr(band, floor) = -0.49. THE BAND IS WIDEST ON AN IDLE BOX, by a factor of
three, and both of the ladder's ceiling breaches are at ZERO load. The floor's
per-sample dispersion falls monotonically with load while the floor absolute
rises — a busy box is slower and STEADIER; an idle one parks its cores between
samples and every sample pays a different wake-up.

SO THE PROPOSED REMEDY WOULD DO HARM. "A row may only be adjudicated when the
floor is inside the calibrated range" would, on this evidence, refuse the most
reproducible runs the instrument can take and pass the least. Not adopted.

WHAT THE CEILING FIRINGS ACTUALLY WERE: 25% sat inside the statistic's own
distribution. P(band > 25%) = 2.6% pooled / 9.0% within-run against a run-level
q99 of 29.1%. The ceiling is now 35%, set from that bootstrap. Full reasoning
on rf2-ymi6j.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ANSWER, and it is the part worth keeping. The corroboration
control on emvod's ensemble genuinely failed — donor bar uix-subs/reagent-subs
0.9394x [0.8958 - 0.9837] against a published 1.0150x that three ensembles
agree on and rf2-yd52q reproduced at 1.0011x. This bead's box explanation for
that is now WEAKER, not stronger, so the failure is more open than it was.
Filed as a successor rather than left inside a closed bead.

Closing: the question this bead asked — does the band decouple ABOVE the
calibrated load range — is answered no, and the framing that produced it was a
clock error.

title: SSR: per-slot-projected serialize entries hydrate under an unaddressable key but are classified no-refetch
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7255 (2026-08-01).

A fresh `:serialize` resource whose projection-relative `:params` or `:scope` declaration changes its SSR wire key is internally consistent on the wire but not addressable by the live client identity. `project-resources-runtime-db` keys the wire entry by `state/key-id` of the projected key, and PR #7255's own `projecting-the-scope-changes-the-key-id-exactly-as-params-does` test proves the raw key-id is absent. After hydration, however, `route-resource-plan` and `ensure-handler` derive the ordinary scoped key from live scope/params and read `(state/entry-path scoped-key)`, i.e. the raw key-id. They therefore miss the hydrated entry and issue a new load.

At the same time, `project-entry` sets `:refetch-on-client?` from coarse disposition/staleness only, so a fresh declaration-only `:serialize` entry is reported false. `hydrate-refetch-plan` independently sees fresh usable `:data` and omits the entry. Thus the server ships usable data and records no-refetch, while the client cannot consume that entry under the identity it can derive and refetches anyway. The projected ownerless entry can also remain beside the new raw-key entry. This predates #7255 for the params arm and #7255 extends the same behavior to scope; rf2-5e2ye explicitly noted it but fenced it out and no exact follow-up owner exists.

Keep the fix narrow: reconcile addressability, projection metadata, and the actual hydrate/route refetch behavior. Do not weaken key privacy or reintroduce raw declared scope/params on the wire.
acceptance_criteria:
- Choose and implement one coherent contract for a fresh `:serialize` entry whose key is changed by a per-slot declaration: either it remains reusable through a safe client mapping, or it is explicitly metadata-only/not shipped as reusable data and deliberately refetched.
- `:refetch-on-client?`, `hydrate-refetch-plan`, and route/ensure behavior agree; no fresh entry is labelled no-refetch while the live derived identity must miss it.
- Add end-to-end controls for both params- and scope-rooted declarations covering server projection -> hydrate reconcile -> live route/ensure/read. Assert either reuse with no request, or exactly one intentional request with truthful metadata/plan and no persistent unreachable duplicate.
- Preserve declaration privacy, wire map-key/in-entry-key agreement, coarse redact/omit behavior, and byte-identical undeclared-key controls.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7354 (2026-08-01): REOPENED. The landed end-to-end test explicitly gathers projected-key ghost rows after the raw-key ensure, then asserts only that any ghosts carry no :data. Production follows that shape: hydrate-runtime-db drops SSR owners but retains the projected entry and recomputes indexes around it; ensure-handler later assocs the live entry under the raw key without deleting the projected row. The ownerless, unaddressable row therefore persists beside the live entry, contrary to this Bead's exact acceptance criterion of no persistent unreachable duplicate. The returned hydrate-refetch-plan also names that projected identity even though the client cannot derive/use it. Keep the security fix (no data under the many-to-one projected key), but remove or explicitly lifecycle-bound the ghost and replace the weakened every-ghost-is-data-less assertion with a zero-persistent-ghost end-to-end control.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7369 (main: 6c7c19061a + e30e5e8830).

The AUDIT-REOPEN charge is met. The unaddressable row is REMOVED, not emptied. project-resources-runtime-db withholds a :key-projected row rather than shipping it metadata-only (reading project-entry's exact key-id comparison, not a shape sniff), and hydrate-runtime-db drops any such row that arrives anyway — the never-trust-the-wire half, which earns its keep because a hydration payload is HTML and cached HTML from an earlier deploy reaches a newer bundle. ensure-handler was considered and rejected: the ghost is not linked to the raw key, so removal there would be a resource-id-matched scan on every ensure, heuristic rather than exact, and would still leave the rows of every resource the client never ensures.

Established from the code that removal was the ONLY option available, not merely the tidiest: the row is unreachable AND uncollectable. Inactive GC is timer-driven (gc-fired-handler fires against a handle armed by a commit fx) and hydration arms no timers, so an ownerless hydrated row has no collector at all — 'explicitly lifecycle-bound' was not reachable without inventing a sweep.

hydrate-refetch-plan no longer names the projected identity (the second half of the same defect: a plan entry is consumed by its :resource/key, so a key no live derivation reproduces names a fetch nobody can issue). The filter lives in the plan itself, not only on the path that drops the row first, because hosts and tests call it directly on an unreconciled slice.

The security fix of #7354 is intact and the projected key was NOT made addressable. Both barred repairs stay barred, and the many-to-one collapse is now vacuous rather than merely harmless — nothing is shipped, so there is no surviving row to collapse onto. The coarse :redact / :omit arms are untouched in shape and in count (their token is content-addressed, one-to-one, derivable in principle); coarse-redaction-token? exists to stop the client-side scan reading their :rf/redacted map KEY as a per-slot substitution.

Test strengthened from 'ghosts carry no :data' (satisfied by a ghost that persists) to absence of the ROW, with two exact-key-id-set controls so over-withholding fails as loudly as under-withholding. 12 tests/42 assertions -> 17/65. Vacuous-on-nil assertions were re-pointed or restated; the scope arm now carries the same no-duplicate claim the params arm did.

projection-metadata gains :projected-key. Withholding removed the only carrier the projected key had, and the SSR projection must stay byte-equal to trace-egress/redact-key-declarations (rf2-5e2ye, rf2-dl7bz — two derivations, one answer). One observation point now, whether or not the row ships; egresses nothing new.

Mutation-proved at all three removal points: M1 (post-#7354 shape restored) 12 failures/8 deftests; M2 (server regresses, client drop intact) 4 failures, cache controls green — the two points are independently witnessed; M3 (plan filter only) 1 failure. M3 initially came back GREEN — a real gap in my own witness: the forged row carried :data, so freshness excluded it and the filter under test never ran. Fixed in a second commit (the plan control now uses the metadata-only row and asserts entry-needs-refetch? as a premise) before the PR opened.

Gates all exit 0: resources 790/7054, ssr 614/3088, ssr-ring 206/1002, test-ssr-prod-gate 616/2915, npm test:cljs 12286/61535, clj-kondo v2026.04.15 errors 0, mkdocs --strict, PASS fast PR spine. Spec 016 §SSR and hydration rewritten from 'metadata-only' to 'does not ride', including the emptied-row-is-not-sufficient rule and the client's must-not-trust-the-server obligation.

Follow-up filed: rf2-4bjep — the coarse :redact / :omit hydrated rows are unaddressed and uncollected in the same way; deliberately fenced out here because their substitution is content-addressed and one-to-one, so they have a repair (adopt) the per-slot arm does not. This PR's exact-set control pins today's behaviour rather than changing it silently.

title: Hicasso: the candidate's Reagent-segment per-read slope moved +6.2% and nothing has attributed it
description:
Found while measuring rf2-2rtt6.58 (the R=0 shell with HD-026's memo wrapper).
It is NOT the wrapper, and it is not the shell.

On worker/cascade-2rtt6-52, the Hicasso candidate's MARGINAL PER-READ SLOPE reads:

  Reagent segment   1,447 B/read [1,444-1,448]   vs section 6's published 1,363   +84 B, +6.2%
  UIx segment       2,289 B/read [2,284-2,291]   vs section 6's published 2,272   +17 B, +0.7%

Measured on p0_run.cjs --only ladder, six rounds, three runs, exit 0 each.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT OR BOX ARTEFACT. The DONORS reproduce section 6
exactly in the same runs — Reagent 948 B/read against a published 948, UIx 2,981
against a published 2,981, and both shells within a few bytes. The six P0
instrument blobs are BYTE-IDENTICAL to section 6's published run 3. So the
instrument and the box agree with the published record; only the CANDIDATE arm
moved.

WHY IT IS NOT THE MEMO WRAPPER. rf2-2rtt6.58 measured the same rung with the
wrapper toggled off by its single call site, and the slope is IDENTICAL in both
arms — 1,447 with and 1,447 without, to the byte, on both segments. The wrapper
is exactly R-independent and lands wholly in the shell. Whatever moved the slope
is something else.

WHAT IT COULD BE, UNRESOLVED. Either (a) the cascade branch's other changes —
112 lines of front/codec.cljs, which the same measurement showed to be
SHELL-neutral but which was never checked against the slope, or (b) anything
that landed on main between section 6's run (2026-08-01, worker/heapaxis-2rtt6-34
rebased onto main) and this branch's base, which is a later main. rf2-2rtt6.58
did not take a run at the merge-base and so cannot separate the two.

WHY IT MATTERS. The per-read axis is the one the regime-matched red-zone gates
are set on, and section 6's headline contrast is built from these slopes: "-708 B
is the design's win and +415 B is its bill". At 1,447 the Reagent-segment bill
becomes +499 B rather than +415 B, a 20% change in a figure the programme quotes.
Nobody has noticed because the wrapper work was all pointed at the shell.

DO: take the ladder at the cascade branch's MERGE-BASE with main, same
instrument, same session discipline. If the slope reads 1,363 there, the branch
owns the move and it should be priced before #7375 merges; if it reads 1,447, a
main landing owns it and section 6's slope rows are stale and need restating.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md section 6
and its new subsection "The memo wrapper, priced on this rung (rf2-2rtt6.58)".
close_reason: Attributed by bisection, 4 ladder runs 2026-08-02, all exit 0, donors 948/2981 reproducing in every run. (1) Merge-base 8d0e06f6d3 reads 1,446/2,289 — the shifted slope — so a MAIN landing owns the move and worker/cascade-2rtt6-52 is exonerated. (2) The convicted landing is 8e973eeace (rf2-2rtt6.44's disposal hook), merged 35 min before #7337 itself: at 4d3331fad5 (#7337's own merge commit) the only bundle-entering delta from run 3's tree is arm1/runtime.cljs 69bfc6fc->e1fd44ca and the full shift is present (1,447/2,289). Section 6's slope was stale the moment it landed; no main tree ever answered 1,363. (3) The line: removing the one interop/add-on-dispose! arming in wire-cell! returns the slope to 1,343/2,253 (A-B-A bracket, runs 2->3->4), splitting the commit into hook +104/+36 B/read and restructure -20/-19. (4) Mechanism: one invalidation closure per unique (frame,query) cell = per read at Q=E, stored as the SECOND on-dispose callback (sub-cache's ref-release closure is first); Reagent's Reaction has no on-dispose field so the second push grows a capacity-1 JS array (fresh elements store per reaction), while the spine pre-allocates on-dispose-fns (atom []) and pays a near-wash conj — that is the Reagent-side +104 vs +36 asymmetry, stated at the allocation level. Verdict: price worth recording, not a defect — the hook repairs the measured deaf-cell class and .44 already costed and declined the alternative; no fix filed. Main tip 316d34ef81 reads 1,447/2,289: the bill is +499 B/read (1.5264x), the win -692 (23.2%), bracket 1,447-2,289, crossover R=1.32. Page updated: reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md section 6 slope stamp + attribution subsection (measured rows untouched). PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7377

title: Hicasso: take the mount + bulk rows for the memo wrapper on the adjudicated clock (rf2-2rtt6.52 follow-up)
description:
rf2-2rtt6.52's landing measurement (docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-page-chrome-row-and-what-the-bail-out-costs.md) could not resolve the clock cost of HD-026's value-equality bail-out.

Two production runs, frame-inclusive, 7 measured rounds each:

  mount, 301 boundaries   1.0089x then 1.0756x   ranges overlap in both
  bulk                    0.9686x then 1.1159x   DISAGREE ON SIGN
  narrow                  1.101x  then 0.9009x   DISAGREE ON SIGN
  props                   1.0379x then 0.9695x   DISAGREE ON SIGN

So the honest statement in the record is a BOUND (the wrapper costs no more than ~10% on those rows) rather than a figure. That is enough to say there is no LARGE regression and not enough to say there is none.

One asymmetry is worth keeping: both runs put :memo on the slow side of parity on MOUNT, which is the direction an extra Fiber per boundary predicts. A few-per-cent mount regression is exactly what this instrument cannot see and exactly what matters, because mount is a bar row (HD-012; the candidate sits at 1.4896x on M1 already).

DO: take the M1 mount row and the bulk rows for the wrapper on clock_run.cjs — Chrome's own renderer counters over CDP, the three-point control, the arm-order guard — which is the instrument those rows are adjudicated on. NOTE the shared box: bench measurement is sequenced, and clock_run.cjs's own header records that a figure whose value depends on where in the plan it sat is not a figure.

title: Hicasso authoring: the ^{::h/prevent? true} opt-in is the one spelling that reads badly at the spine shapes
description:
AUTHORING FINDING from the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51), which was asked to report
plainly if any collapsed spelling was awkward at these shapes.

Three of the four collapsed spellings did not come up at all across shapes 1-4 - `h/fn`
was never needed (every event position took a literal intent vector, matching the census's
~97%), `:&` was never needed (the spine shapes have no remainder-forwarding wrapper; the
article-editor witness is where it earns its place), and presence never came up. That is a
good result and it is stated as an absence, not a pass.

The one that DID come up, and reads badly:

    [:a.nav-link {:href        "#"
                  :data-testid "your-feed-tab"
                  :class       (when your-feed? "active")
                  :on-click    ^{:re-frame.hicasso/prevent? true}
                               [:conduit/show-your-feed]}
     "Your Feed"]

Three things are wrong with it at a call site:

1. IT BREAKS THE ATTRIBUTE MAP'S ALIGNMENT. The value no longer fits on the key's line at
   any sane indent, so the one attribute that carries behaviour is the one that looks
   like a mistake. It is the ugliest thing in the roster and it is in both feed pages.
2. METADATA DOES NOT PARTICIPATE IN `=`. HD-021's headless door returns the tree as data
   with "intent vectors assertable by equality" - and `(= [:conduit/show-your-feed] ...)`
   is TRUE whether or not the prevent metadata is there. So the one axis of an intent that
   metadata carries is exactly the axis a structural test cannot see. (The roster fires a
   real cancelable click to check it instead:
   large_template_dom_cljs_test/the-prevent-metadata-is-what-prevents.)
3. IT IS INVISIBLE TO A READER SCANNING FOR BEHAVIOUR. `^{...}` before a vector reads as
   a type hint, not as "this stops the browser navigating".

WHERE IT BITES: the anchor-acting-as-a-button, which the census home page has three of
(feed tabs, tag pills) and every Bootstrap-shaped nav has more. The dominant case -
`:on-submit` - needs nothing, because the position auto-prevents. So the metadata form is
paying its ugliness exactly where it is used most visibly and never where it is used most.

NOT PROPOSING A SPELLING. authoring.md's rationale for metadata is real ("costs no new
prop, no new spelling, and no second calling convention") and the alternative the census
uses - `{:event [...] :prevent-default true}` - is the options map HD-024's collapse
deliberately deleted. Filed as evidence for whoever re-opens that trade, with the note
that (2) is the strongest of the three arguments because it is a correctness-visibility
problem rather than a taste one.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review): Option (a). Retire the ^{::h/prevent? true} metadata spelling. Adopt ONE in-band decorator head at event positions: [::h/prevent [:app/event ...]]. Both the primary dossier and the Codex review converged here independently. This bead now becomes the IMPLEMENTATION owner of that change — dispatchable.

WHY (defect 2 is disqualifying): metadata does not participate in =. Measured probe on this checkout — a metadata-carrying intent compares = AND hash-equal to the plain intent; the wrapper form does not:

  (= [:app/go] (with-meta [:app/go] {::h/prevent? true})) ;=> true
  (= [:app/go] [::h/prevent [:app/go]])                   ;=> false

So the prevent flag is invisible to HD-021's equality door, and equally to ordinary snapshots and logs (metadata is omitted from printing unless *print-meta*). preventDefault changes observable program behaviour (the event's canceled flag, per the DOM standard) — behaviour, not annotation — and a spelling that hides it from the product's own structural-testing story contradicts that story. Defects 1 (the value breaks the attribute map's alignment at any sane indent) and 3 (^{...} reads as a type hint, invisible to a reader scanning for behaviour) stand alongside; they alone would not have forced the change, defect 2 does.

FACTUAL CORRECTION — the implementation agent MUST NOT assume head-dispatch exists. The primary dossier's premise that "the intent materializer already dispatches on the head" is WRONG about the live code. front/intent.cljs substitutes ::h/value / ::h/checked markers; intent-handler dispatches the vector it is given, unexamined. The wrapper therefore needs a small, explicit CLASSIFY-AND-UNWRAP step at lowering time. That is still the right trade: classification happens once per render, the dispatched inner vector stays ordinary data, and the event-time path acquires no new allocation and no open-ended evaluator.

CLOSED GRAMMAR (keep it closed): exactly one inner intent vector; unwrap BEFORE marker analysis (so ::h/value / ::h/checked markers compose inside a prevented intent); accepted in key-map branches through the same path; fail LOUDLY on malformed decorators (wrong arity, non-vector payload). One reserved head in the same closed, tiny roster as the ::h/value placeholder — not an open DSL.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (part of the ruling, not optional): keep :on-submit auto-prevent exactly as is. The rare submit OPT-OUT uses the existing h/fn escape — callbacks deliberately do not auto-prevent. Only add a symmetric ::h/allow-default if dogfooding produces a real site needing BOTH native submission AND equality-based structural testing — do not add it speculatively. NO event-options map. NO modifier DSL. (Auto-prevent cannot absorb the click case: a click intent on a real link must NOT prevent by default — modifier-clicks, open-in-new-tab — so the anchor-as-button genuinely needs an explicit opt-in; this ruling only picks its spelling.)

PREVALENCE (why now): 35 direct preventDefault calls in examples/; 10 anchor-as-button sites across the two RealWorld implementations (pagination, feed tabs, active tags, tag pills). The Hicasso metadata key itself currently occurs ONLY in the experimental Freehand front and its tests — pre-alpha is the cheapest, cleanest moment to correct the spelling.

PIN SET (ships with the implementation):
  1. A structural equality assertion distinguishing plain from prevented intents — proving the headless door can now SEE the axis.
  2. The roster's real-cancelable-click behavioural witness (large_template_dom_cljs_test/the-prevent-metadata-is-what-prevents, carried forward to the new spelling) — proving prevention actually happens AND that the inner vector is what gets dispatched.
  3. Marker and key-map composition tests (markers inside a prevented intent; the decorator accepted through key-map branches).
Preserve the existing submit and callback tests unchanged.

REJECTED OPTIONS:
  (b) keyed attribute {:intent [...] :prevent? true} — makes maps legal at event positions: a second broad calling convention at every event key, against the census's ~97%-literal-vector grain, and an invitation to an options language (the shape HD-024's collapse deliberately deleted).
  (c) keep metadata + a headless-door lint — patches defect 2 with tooling (duplicating semantic knowledge there) while defects 1 and 3 stand, and equality/printing stay blind; the ugliest spelling in the roster would remain at the most frequent interactive shape.
  Also rejected (Codex sweep): a sibling element attribute (separates the policy from the intent it decorates); requiring h/fn for the recurring click case (discards the data/headless benefit exactly where a one-head wrapper preserves it).

SPEC HOME: an HD amendment in the HD-016/HD-023 family — one new reserved intent head, the metadata spelling retired, HD-021's equality promise made true at shape 5. The amendment text ships WITH the implementation PR, not as a separate doc change.

RELATION TO rf2-2rtt6.54: the eventual route-link will absorb the NAVIGATION subset of these anchor sites; the anchor-as-button remains this spelling's home. No dependency either way.

Total cost: one reserved head and one extra pair of brackets, for one legible data form that programmers, AI authors, and the equality door all see the same way.
close_reason: Implemented and merged as PR #7374 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7374). The ^{::h/prevent? true} metadata is retired for one reserved in-band head, [::h/prevent [:app/go]], classified and unwrapped at lowering in front/intent.cljs — the head dispatch the ruling's factual correction said did not exist. Closed grammar (exactly one non-empty inner intent vector, no nesting), refused loudly at lowering with :rf.error/hicasso-malformed-prevent naming the position, in Freehand's event-plan diagnostic style. Unwrap precedes marker analysis so ::h/value composes inside a prevented intent; key-map branches come through the same call. HD-026 ships with it, citing what the Replicant reading took (namespaced-keyword head + positional payload) and declined (sibling attribute option keys, which cannot travel with an intent handed to a child; and its no-diagnostics posture). PIN SET delivered: (1) a-prevented-intent-is-assertable-by-equality asserts the retired spelling's =, hash and pr-str blindness against the head's visibility to all three; (2) the roster's real-cancelable-click witness carried forward as the-prevent-head-is-what-prevents; (3) marker and key-map composition tests. Census feed tabs migrated in both spine shapes. Mutation-proved: removing the classification -> test:browser exit 1, the real click stops preventing and the browser follows the href; removing the refusal -> test:cljs exit 1, 7 malformed forms go silent. Gates green: test:cljs 0, test:browser 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors:0, check_doc_slugs 0. Hook budget unchanged (2 at 1/7/20 reads).

title: Hicasso: the tier-1 roster does not exercise framework subs (27% of census read traffic)
description:
Found while porting the census screens for the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51).

The charter counts framework subs at 27% of read traffic and says "the index serves them
first-class". The census screens the roster ports read exactly those:
  [:rf/resource {:resource :realworld/articles :params {...}}]
  [:rf/mutation {:instance [:favorite slug]}]

The roster reads plain reg-subs with the SAME READ SHAPE (a per-instance
:conduit/favorite-pending? alongside the per-row :conduit/article) but not the same
machinery, because standing up a resource cache behind a view-layer witness would put an
HTTP-shaped dependency in the roster's way.

So nothing in the Hicasso corpus currently witnesses that a framework sub reads
identically to an app sub through the collector. Two specific things go unchecked:
  - the query vector's arg is a MAP, not a scalar - so the index's sub-key identity

  - a framework sub's value moves on a different clock than a db write.

[:rf/resource ...] alongside its app sub, and asserts the same narrow law
(one commit -> one body). Sequence AFTER rf2-2rtt6.51 merges.

title: Hicasso: shape 5's 'zero dropped keystrokes' is witnessed one keystroke at a time
description:
Found auditing shape 5's coverage for the tier-1 roster (rf2-2rtt6.51), which was asked to
report what it found rather than rebuild it.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE, and it is a lot. `arm1/controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test` carries 17
deftests on the 100-cell grid covering R-A1 (a-keystroke-echoes-inside-the-discrete-event),
R-A2 across five caret cases (mid-string, normalising, grouping, cross-cell, range
collapse), both IME laws (a-composing-enter-commits-nothing;
reacts-synthetic-keyboard-event-drops-is-composing), refusal convergence in and out of the
event, and residue. `controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test` measures the UIx adapter's two
implementations against the same model. Shape 5 is the best-witnessed shape of the five.

THE GAP. The charter's clause is "zero dropped keystrokes", and every echo witness fires
ONE synthetic `input` event carrying the whole value:
    (type-into! n "hello")   ;; one event, value "hello"
That proves the door is synchronous for a keystroke. It does not prove that N keystrokes
arriving back-to-back all land - which is the failure mode the clause names, the one
Reagent needed reagent/impl/input.cljs for, and the one a batching/deferring substrate
actually exhibits.

WANTED: a burst witness - dispatch k successive cancelable `input` events into one focused
cell without yielding between them (h,e,l,l,o as five events, not one), and assert the
model holds "hello", the DOM holds "hello", the caret is at 5, and the body ran exactly k
times. Then the same burst against a REFUSING cell (:digits), where the model must hold
only the accepted subset.

Coordinate with worker/converge-fki5d (in-turn controlled-input convergence) - if it
changes what an author writes for a controlled field, this witness should be written
against the converged spelling rather than re-written after it.

Seven rows: event-carriage verified on the native event (insertText/data/bubbles/NOT-cancelable — the browser's input event never is, beforeinput is the cancelable one); plain burst h,e,l,l,o lands in order with caret 5 and body run exactly k times (plus the bare-loop form); refusing :digits bursts (append and mid-string) hold only the accepted subset with each next keystroke landing on the restored state; normalising :upper and length-changing :group bursts carry the caret through k successive converges; the mid-string ordering row requires the SEQUENCE's spelling (abcd, never abdc). Mutation-proved both ways: converge flushSync removed -> browser suite exit 1 (10 failures, burst spells [abd abdc], caret [[3 3] [4 4]]); door deferred to a macrotask -> exit 1 (153 failures, burst reads five empty strings, zero landed). Restored byte-identical, suite exit 0 (975/6108/0). THE DOOR HELD: no keystroke genuinely dropped — no P1 finding. Gates: test:browser 0, test:cljs 0 (12339/61730/0), fast-PR spine 0 (own exit code, clean capture), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0.

title: hicasso: h/boundary lowers its fallback and its children with no ambient frame - the retry button HD-020(c) sells cannot be written
description: Sibling of rf2-2rtt6.66, found while repairing it; NOT fixed there because that bead names presence. arm1/boundary.cljs's render does (codec/as-element (if (fn? fallback) (fallback error) fallback)) / (codec/as-element (into [:<>] children)) with NO intent/with-frame binding. Both the FALLBACK and the CHILDREN are hiccup DATA written in the parent boundary's body but LOWERED inside the class component's own React render, where intent/*dispatch* is unbound - the identical mechanism rf2-2rtt6.66 repaired in presence. Consequence: an intent vector at an event position on a fallback node, or on a native child of h/boundary, raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at render; an h/fn declared :event there raises the same id at invocation. The fallback half is the sharper one and is the surface HD-020(c) is sold on - a fallback whose whole point is a RETRY control ([:button {:on-click [:app/retry]}] beside :reset-key) cannot be written today, and a fallback that fails to render lands the app in the boundary's own error path. REPAIR: identical shape to rf2-2rtt6.66 and CHEAPER - the class already resolves its frame through contextType (frame-of, used by report! for the :on-error intent), so no new hook and no new accessor: wrap both as-element calls in intent/with-frame with rt/frame-dispatch, nil-tolerant the same way presence is. WITNESS: a fallback carrying a retry intent, clicked, plus a native child of h/boundary carrying one; both intent shapes; and the frameless case still naming the intent. arm1/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test is the template - its own h/boundary uses are deliberately fallback-intent-free and cite this bead.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7389 (branch worker/bdyframe-uo9di). arm1/boundary's render now binds intent/with-frame around its ONE crossing — the fallback and the children both — resolving the frame through the contextType accessor report! already used (frame-of), with runtime/frame-dispatch's memoised frame-locked dispatch. No new hook and no new accessor: the class had its frame already, which is why this was cheaper than rf2-2rtt6.66's presence repair. The binding is unconditional and carries nil with no provider, so a frameless boundary stays legal and an intent under one is still the loud error naming the intent. Reproduced first, on HD-020(c)'s own advertised case: a fallback retry button raised :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :intent [:bdy/retry], escaping to the boundary above. New witness arm1/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test carries 7 rows — retry button + reset-key round trip, h/fn on a function fallback, both shapes on a native child (separate subjects, since the shapes fail at different moments), frame isolation against a second live frame, the frameless case, and a hook-ledger row proving the class spends none even in its error state. Mutation red/green: binding absent EXIT=1 (7 failures + 3 errors, all in the new ns, naming the error id); binding present EXIT=0 (1002 tests, 6229 assertions). Gates: test:browser 0, test:cljs 0 (12387 tests), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors 0; CI 48/48 pass. NOT merged — the mayor merges.

value:
REAPING ON 'PR MERGED + AGENT REPORTED' STILL CATCHES LIVE AGENTS — twice now, and the guard saved it both times (2026-08-02).

WHAT HAPPENS: an agent sends its final report, the mayor merges its PR and reaps the worktree — and the agent is STILL RUNNING. It keeps working after reporting: extra confirmatory reruns, a last gate, tidying. The worktree vanishes under its cwd and its background process dies.

INCIDENTS: the heap worker (reaped on PR-merge while alive; recorded then as 'reap only when merged AND reported'), and now proc-6tags-7uxkt — which HAD reported done, then set up a node_modules junction and started an extra test:cljs run. It found its worktree gone mid-run.

WHY IT HAS BEEN HARMLESS BOTH TIMES, and this is the load-bearing part: scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh disarms the node_modules junction BEFORE removing, so the junction-following hazard (which has emptied the mayor's real node_modules twice historically) did NOT fire. Canary held at 101 entries across both incidents. The worker's commits were pushed before reporting, so nothing was lost either time.

THE REFINEMENT, since 'reported done' is evidently not the same as 'finished': the cheap check before reaping a just-merged worktree is whether its agent is still live (a task notification arriving after the report is the tell; so is a recent mtime under the worktree). It costs one look. But the honest weighting is that the GUARD is the real protection and it works — this is a courtesy to the worker's last few minutes, not a safety issue. Do not build ceremony around it; do not skip the guard.

DO NOT force removal or bypass the guard when a reap refuses — a refusal means something still holds the tree, which is exactly when following a junction would be catastrophic.

title: Hicasso: close the interpreter gap — decompose the slim-lineage walk against Reagent's own, then spend HD-004's codec-caching budget
description:
THE OUTCOME BEAD for the mount deficit. The attribution chain is complete and tight: UIx ($-macro, no runtime interpretation) mounts at parity with Reagent (1.015x); the donor rungs and the candidate — all riding reagent-slim's :f> walk — read 1.33-1.5x; Freehand's codec reads another 1.14-1.22x on top; per-keystroke and narrow are at parity everywhere. So the ENTIRE clock deficit follows the interpreter — and, decisively, REAGENT'S OWN INTERPRETER IS THE EXISTENCE PROOF that runtime hiccup interpretation can be nearly free at mount (its walk disappears into the shared React/frame work). The question is not 'can interpreted hiccup be fast' but 'why is OUR walk slower than Reagent's, and how much of HD-004's sanctioned budget closes it'.

STEP 1 — DECOMPOSE (measure before touching anything). Reagent's template machinery is in this repository (reagent.impl.template + slim's shared plumbing): put the slim-lineage walk and stock Reagent's walk side by side on the SAME witness markup and attribute the per-element delta to named terms — candidate suspects: the :f> function-component path's per-element allocations; prop-name conversion missing Reagent's warm caches (cached-parse et al.); children flattening; per-boundary wrapper cost. Frame-domination arithmetic matters: two-thirds of the mount window is shared style/layout/paint, so a 1.49x TOTAL implies the walk slice is SEVERAL TIMES Reagent's slice in absolute terms — the decomposition must report absolute per-element costs, not ratios. Respect rf2-2rtt6.62's finding: match roster workloads before attributing.

STEP 2 — SPEND THE HD-004 BUDGET, in measured increments: codec-work caching ONLY (parsed tags, prop-name conversion, cached stable component heads — same elements, same behaviour, safe invalidation, no public template hints). HARD FENCE (HD-004, verbatim class): NO template extraction, NO hole plans, NO node references, NO subscription-addressed anything, NO direct DOM writes — the first optimization that wants those IS the own-renderer strategy and must be declared as such, not smuggled. If the budget runs out short of the gate, REPORT THE FLOOR REACHED rather than widening the sanction — that is a P2-relevant finding either way.

ACCEPTANCE: the mount row on the adjudicated clock of record (raw TaskDuration, canonical M1, floor-normalised, instrument-stamped, per rf2-2rtt6.1's MOUNT GATE AMENDMENT 2026-08-02): candidate/uix-subs, before and after each increment, against the <= 1.10x gate line. Publish per-element decomposition + increments to the studio with blob-hash + landed-SHA provenance. SEQUENCING: after rf2-2rtt6.31's re-take publishes (so the before-number is the adjudicated one) and coordinated with rf2-2rtt6.62 (workload matching). Browser numbers only. This bead is the make-or-break of the mount axis: if a measured, fence-respecting caching pass cannot reach 1.10x, that is the honest input to the P2 fork ruling — not a reason to loosen the fence.
notes:
THE THIRD CLAUSE IS NOW ANSWERABLE — rf2-cno31's re-take supplies it (recorded by acting mayor, 2026-08-03).

You left this open because the census mount row on the clock of record was not yours to take while rf2-cno31 owned those windows and its fix changed the pages underneath any row. CORRECT AT THE TIME. rf2-cno31 has since completed (PR #7393) and re-took exactly those rows AFTER its fix, on the clock of record, quiet on attempt 1, guard reportable x6, exit 0:

  acceptance  1.4759x [1.3281-1.6302]  ->  1.1884x [1.1223-1.2660]  band 7.0%   FAILS THE 1.10x LINE
  feed        1.3311x [1.2357-1.4195]  ->  1.0737x [0.9669-1.1859]  band 6.7%   INSTRUMENT-LIMITED (straddles 1.10; NOT a pass)
  ordinary    1.2097x                  ->  1.1698x [0.9671-1.5014]  band 15.8%  INSTRUMENT-LIMITED + control FAIL

The feed's mean is now below 1.10 AND below its pre-migration 1.0875x — but a straddling range is not a pass, and rf2-cno31's page says so.

SO THE THREE CLAUSES NOW READ: (1) decomposition delivered — our walk 1.0588x stock Reagent before this bead, 0.9636x after, while reagent2.impl.template reads 1.73-1.90x stock; 92% of the divergence accounted for by named stages. (2) budget spent with the floor reported — the residual is one stage, +20.8 ns/element of shipped Hicasso semantics, ~0.6% of a mount. (3) THE CENSUS MOUNT ROW: acceptance FAILS at 1.1884x, feed instrument-limited at 1.0737x.

AND THE CONCLUSION THIS BEAD EXISTS TO REACH IS UNCHANGED AND STRENGTHENED: the remaining deficit is NOT the interpreter. The walk is at or below stock Reagent and its whole residual is 0.6% of a mount, yet acceptance still reads 1.1884x. Whatever carries that ~19% sits outside the walk. That is the question the next bead should ask, and it should ask it of the ~8.25 ms taskNet / ~6.10 ms in-page split rf2-cno31 published for the acceptance arm rather than of the interpreter again.

THE MAYOR'S DISPOSITION: no further work is asked of this bead. It may be closed on the strength of the above once PR #7393 merges; the third clause is answered by another bead's rows, which is the correct outcome for a measurement whose windows belonged elsewhere.
