title: Hicasso: a page-chrome write cascades to every row (no props-equality bail-out)
description:
MEASURED on the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51),
shapes/narrow_dom_cljs_test/a-page-chrome-write-re-renders-every-row.

A write that moves a key the PAGE boundary reads re-renders the page, and React then
re-renders all 300 card boundaries beneath it — even though every card's props and every
card's subscription values are unchanged. Measured: page 1, cards 300/300, and the DOM
after is byte-identical to the DOM before, which is why a DOM-only witness could never
have seen it.

CAUSE: `runtime/mint-view!` returns a plain React function component
  (fn hicasso-boundary [js-props] (shell body-fn js-props))
with no memo and no props comparison. React re-renders children of a re-rendered parent
unless the element is referentially identical (it is not — the page's `for` builds fresh
elements) or the component bails out itself.

WHY IT MATTERS ON THE BAR: Reagent's default `shouldComponentUpdate` compares argv and
stops exactly this cascade. So on any page with page-level chrome state (a tab, a filter,
a sort, a route param) Reagent re-renders N rows fewer than Hicasso does. That is the
axis HD-012's `<= 1.0x Reagent` bulk row is set on, and the roster's narrow law
(one commit -> one body) holds only for writes that DON'T touch the page boundary.

NOT REPAIRED by rf2-2rtt6.51 — the roster's job is to find what the shapes cost, and the
repair is a runtime change. Note for whoever takes it: `React.memo` alone does NOT fix it,
because the props object is a fresh `#js {"rfProps" <cljs map>}` each render and memo's
shallow compare is `Object.is`. It needs an `areEqual` doing `=` on the rfProps map —
which is Reagent's argv compare, and costs no React hook, so the <=2-hook budget is not
in the way.

MEASUREMENT (do not run here; siblings own the box): the cascade's cost belongs on the
bulk ladder as its own row - "page-chrome write, B mounted rows", against Reagent.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review):

AMEND HD-006 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md, "Memoization defaults"). The clause "No default `=`/argv memoization ... `React.memo` is an opt-in escape", with reopen pre-registered "only on keyed-row / broad witness evidence demanding it", has had its reopen condition fire: the tier-1 roster's own instrument (shapes/narrow_dom_cljs_test/a-page-chrome-write-re-renders-every-row) measured a page-chrome write re-rendering the page plus all 300 card boundaries with every card input value-equal, on exactly the axis the <=1.0x Reagent bulk row is set on (Reagent's argv compare stops this cascade). DECISION: value-equality bail-out becomes the DEFAULT at minted Hicasso boundaries — CLJS `=` over the complete rfProps value, implemented as a codec-level stable memo wrapper. This is the evidence-driven overturn HD-006 itself provided for; record it as such in the amendment.

EVIDENCE CORRECTION (Codex, verified against the shape test): the resulting DOM is NOT byte-identical — the tab chrome changes. Drop that phrase everywhere (this bead's description carries it; do not repeat it in the amendment or PR text). The 300 unchanged-row renders (page body 1, card bodies 300/300 with all card projections equal) are themselves the sufficient witness.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (binding):
- `React.memo(fn, compare)` returns a memo OBJECT, not a function, and the codec + runtime tests require minted heads to BE functions. Do NOT replace `mint-view!`'s return value. Keep the marked function as the public Hicasso head; the codec emits one stable internal memo wrapper for that head (or an equivalently contained internal mechanism). No memo object escapes as the public representation.
- Comparator: CLJS `=` over the complete rfProps value — every prop, including function-valued props, which compare conservatively unequal (correct: distinct functions must not bail out).
- Memoization must not block the boundary's own state/context/external-store updates: useContext + useSyncExternalStore invalidation still re-renders (React's documented memo contract). The comparator costs no React hook; the <=2-hook budget is untouched.
- Donor precedent: reagent-slim's default update check is argv `=`, and reactive invalidation bypasses it via forceUpdate. Same shape here — subscription invalidation bypasses the props bail-out by design.

CONTRACT: bodies stay pure and re-runnable — memoization is a scheduling optimization, never observable semantics. NO public `:memo false` option in v1. A boundary that intentionally wants parent-driven re-runs receives an explicit changing revision prop; add an opt-out only if a concrete case later proves that insufficient. No element caches, no per-call-site switches.

LANDING BAR (the implementation must clear this before merge; the amendment lands with its own number): one focused production-build measurement gate — the "page-chrome write, B mounted rows" bulk-ladder row before/after (witness: page body 1, card bodies 0 after settling; prop-change re-render still fires; context/external-store invalidation still fires; initial-mount and bulk-update time), PLUS the per-boundary retained-heap delta. The real cost being priced: the custom comparator takes the full MemoComponent path and adds an outer Fiber per boundary, and the R=0 shell heap is already ~1.14 KB against the 1 KB paper-fail line. The default lands if it removes the 300-row cascade without a material mount/bulk regression and without pushing retained heap meaningfully farther past the bar. If the extra Fiber fails the gate: retain HD-006 and ship the same comparator as an explicit boundary-level opt-in — a small, decisive experiment either way.

REJECTED:
(b) Keep HD-006 and teach React.memo+areEqual as an opt-in pattern — inverts the posture (the framework knows the right default and makes every programmer find it) and ships a known 300x re-render cascade on the most ordinary page shape there is (tabs above a list).
(c) Element-identity caching at the call sites — fights React's grain with exactly the caching machinery the anti-fence exists to refuse; every `for` site becomes a performance decision.

PROCESS: the HD-006 amendment text ships in the SAME PR as the runtime change (the .25 precedent). This bead is now the implementation owner — dispatchable.
OPERATOR RULING — MERGE AS DEFAULT (Mike, 2026-08-03, verbatim: 'merge as default'). Recorded by acting mayor.

THE BINDING LANDING BAR, and how it came out:
  CASCADE HALF — DECISIVE. A page-chrome write re-rendered 300 unchanged card boundaries with a BYTE-IDENTICAL resulting DOM (which is why no DOM-only witness could ever have caught it); now 0. Both halves witnessed — cascade gone AND real changes still propagate. Plain React.memo was shown to STILL cascade at 300, so the ruled codec-level shape was necessary rather than stylistic.
  HEAP HALF — MEASURED, and the projection was wrong by about a factor of two. The feared figure was approximately +17%; the R=0 boundary shell actually reads +106 B / +9.3% (1,141 -> 1,247 B) on the Reagent segment and +100 B / +8.8% on the UIx segment. A->B->A in one session (A arms agreeing to 0 B and 5 B), ranges disjoint, arms differing by ONE LINE, donors flat, slope identical to the byte with and without — confirming HD-026's own claim that the cost is constant in R.

WHY THE DISPOSITION WAS THE OPERATOR'S: 'without pushing retained heap meaningfully farther past the bar' is unquantified in HD-026, and the shell ALREADY FAILED the 1 KB paper line at 1,141 B before any wrapper existed. The wrapper widens a pre-existing failure rather than causing one. The rf2-2rtt6.58 worker refused to call that green by fiat and stopped — correctly.

THE RULING: merge as DEFAULT. The opt-in fallback is NOT taken. Eliminating a 300-boundary cascade on the make-or-break bulk shape is worth +9% on a line that had already failed and has its own separate remedy path (rf2-aqgr2, the 415 B/read decomposition, and the shell target on rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5).

ALSO SETTLED BEFORE MERGE: rf2-2rtt6.60 attributed the +84 B/read slope shift to a MAIN landing (8e973eeace, rf2-2rtt6.44's disposal hook, merged 35 minutes before section 6 published) — NOT to this branch. The cascade branch is exonerated; section 6's bill now reads +499 B/read and is recorded as such.
RENUMBERED HD-026 -> HD-028 on rebase, and the branch is unblocked for merge.

HD-026 and HD-027 were taken on main while this branch was held (the prevent head rf2-2rtt6.57, route-link rf2-2rtt6.54). Main's highest was verified as HD-027 before choosing 028. Every earlier note on this bead that says HD-026 means HD-028.

CONFLICTS RESOLVED KEEPING BOTH INTENTS, never --ours/--theirs: the title line became the full range HD-001 … HD-028, and main's HD-026 and HD-027 bodies survive untouched with HD-028 following in numeric order.

REFERENCES DECIDED PER SITE. The ten on this branch were all the cascade's and were renamed; the eleven that are main's prevent head were left. Two more repaired: the decisions index still read HD-001…HD-026 (route-link never bumped it) and studio/the-interpreter-walk-profiled-and-cheapened.md cited this amendment by the number it carried while held. The nine draft-guide range banners moved to HD-028; their HD-027 body citations are untouched.

ONE GENUINE INTERACTION FOUND. rf2-2rtt6.53 landed while this branch was held and restated the 300-row cascade on the resource clock, citing the roster pin by name as 'the same number, restated rather than contradicted'. shapes/framework_subs_dom_cljs_test now reads 0 where it read 1, on three assertions and in its docstring — the same correction the roster witness already carried. The page's own DOM is asserted to have moved so the zeroes cannot pass vacuously, and the mutation reds them, which is the check that they were moved to the truth rather than relaxed. No behavioural interaction with anything else that landed while held (the cold read, presence's frame binding, the walk optimisation, or PR #7389's boundary frame binding, which the branch was rebased onto).

WRAPPER UNCHANGED: memoize-boundary! one stable wrapper per head at definition, mint-view! returns the marked function, boundary-head? asks fn?, no memo object escapes. The operator's heap number was measured against these blobs.

GATES RE-RUN ON THE REBASED TREE, all exit 0: test:cljs 12,395/61,841; test:browser 1,009/6,258; test-fast-pr.sh PASS; clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0 (warnings 4,532); check_doc_slugs.py. MUTATION RE-RUN on the rebased tree: bail-out removed -> 9 failures, narrow actual (not (= 0 300)), exit 1; restored byte-exact -> exit 0.

No bench driver run and no clock row taken — linkterm-cno31 and walkdecomp-2rtt6-63 own the measurement windows.

NOT MERGED — the mayor merges. PR #7376 (shell58) targets this branch and is CONFLICTING after the force-push; its conflict is purely this renumber plus the moved HD section, but it also restates the heap figure (+100 B vs +200 B) so it needs its own rebase, not mine.

NEVER DELETE A BRANCH THAT ANOTHER PR TARGETS AS ITS BASE — it silently CLOSES the dependent PR (2026-08-03, my error).

WHAT HAPPENED: PR #7376 (worker/shell58-2rtt6-58) carried rf2-2rtt6.58's R=0 boundary-shell measurement — the +106 B / +9.3% figure the OPERATOR RULED ON for the HD-028 value-equality default. It TARGETED worker/cascade-2rtt6-52 rather than main, because two of its three files existed only on that branch. When #7375 merged I deleted worker/cascade-2rtt6-52 in the routine post-merge cleanup. GitHub auto-closed #7376. Its branch and commits survive; its measurement is NOT on main.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT COVER IT: the standing rule is 'never delete a branch BEFORE its own PR merges' (deleting auto-closes it). This is the mirror case — the branch's own PR HAD merged, but a DIFFERENT PR pointed at it as base. The post-merge cleanup checks the merged PR's state, not whether anything else depends on the branch.

THE CHECK, before deleting any worker branch: does any open PR name it as baseRefName? One call answers it:
  gh pr list --state open --json number,baseRefName --jq '.[]|select(.baseRefName=="worker/<name>")|.number'
If it returns anything, RE-TARGET those PRs to main first (gh pr edit <n> --base main), then delete. The dependent will usually need a rebase afterwards — that is a worker's job, not a blind resolution.

WHY STACKED PRs EXIST HERE AT ALL: a measurement PR must measure the branch that would merge, so it is cut FROM that branch and targets it. That is correct and will recur. The hazard is entirely in the cleanup order.

RECOVERY IS CHEAP IF CAUGHT: the branch survives deletion of its base, so the work is never lost — reopen or re-raise against main and rebase. The cost is latency and a confusing audit trail, not data.

AFTER A CRASH, CHECK LANDED-NESS WITH A 600-COMMIT WINDOW BEFORE SALVAGING ANYTHING (2026-08-03).

Recovering from a host crash that killed ~18 workers, I found 14 worker worktrees with commits and NO remote branch — the classic 'stranded work' shape. I pushed 13 of them for durability, which the method explicitly sanctions.

Then I compared their commit SUBJECTS against main. Against 'git log --oneline -60 origin/main' only 2 of 13 looked landed. Against -600, ALL 13 had landed. The branches were pure residue: workers that had already shipped via PRs that already merged, leaving behind unreaped worktrees whose local branch ref simply predated the squash-merge onto main.

THE COST OF THE NARROW WINDOW: I nearly dispatched ~11 salvage workers to 'finalise' work that was already on main, and I did push+delete 13 redundant branches. On a repo merging this fast, 60 commits is a few HOURS of main. A 2-day-old worker branch needs hundreds.

THE RULE: before treating an unpushed worker branch as stranded, diff its commit subjects against at least 600 commits of origin/main (use 'git log --format=%s -600 origin/main' + 'grep -Fxq' per subject). A worktree with commits and no remote is USUALLY residue, not loss. Real loss looks different: UNCOMMITTED modified files (that worktree genuinely died mid-edit), or commits whose subjects appear nowhere on main.

ALSO: 'gh pr list --state open' returning 0 is a strong corroborating signal — if no PRs are open, no worker is mid-flight, so every branch is either landed or abandoned.

title: hicasso: presence lowers its children with no ambient frame - intent props on any presence child are loud-dead
description: Found while proving the host hatch (rf2-2rtt6.65). arm1/presence.cljs presence-body renders retained children via (codec/as-element (into [:<>] (presence/render next))) with NO intent/with-frame binding: children handed to h/presence are hiccup DATA created in the parent boundary's body but LOWERED inside the presence component's own React render, where rstate.frame is nil and intent/*dispatch* is unbound. Consequence, for NATIVE and HOST children alike: an intent VECTOR at an event position on a presence child raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at render; an h/fn declared/lowered :event that returns an intent raises the same id at invocation. Loud, never silent - but a toast with an inline dismiss button ([:div.toast {:key id :on-click [:toasts/dismiss id]}]) cannot be written under presence today, which contradicts the ruling's whole pitch (the inline tray with no child view). Repair sketch: presence-body resolves the frame once (useContext adapter-context/frame-context - presence is not a boundary shell, HD-020's budget does not apply to it, but its docstring's 'two hooks in THIS component' claim must be updated) and wraps its as-element call in intent/with-frame with the frame-locked dispatch (runtime's memoised frame-dispatch needs a public accessor, or presence goes through rt/dispatch!). Witness: a keyed native child with an :on-click intent + a host child with a declared :event h/fn, both dispatching from the retained AND live phases. The host-hatch suite (arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test) deliberately keeps its presence-tray children callback-free and cites this bead.
close_reason: PR #7388 completed the exact owner: presence resolves the shared provider context and re-binds the stable frame dispatch around its one child-lowering call; browser witnesses cover native vectors, h/fn invocation, retained children, two-frame isolation, child boundaries, frameless diagnostics and the hook ledger. The unavailable defhost-specific witness remains in the active host-hatch owner rf2-2rtt6.65.

title: EP-0037 route-plan trace: carry the identity partition (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities) beside the counts; :identities in plan order
description:
Implements the ruling on rf2-9sluz (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): EP-0037 §Tooling's R2 "identity diff" ships as the exact identity partition on the existing activation :rf.resource/route-plan trace row. Everything else in the Tooling bullet list is DESCOPED by that ruling — see rf2-9sluz notes for the full descope enumeration. No new panel, no public plan value, no second graph, and EP-0037's conformance matrix must NOT gain an eleventh row.

CODE — implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc, the trace/emit! at ~:1102-1112 (the R2 plan-diff projection commented at :1094-1099). Add three identity vectors beside the existing counts; KEEP :ensured/:kept/:removed counts as the compact headline:

- :ensured-identities — scoped-keys of ordered requirements taking the ensure path: (into [] (comp (remove adopted?) (map :scoped-key)) ordered). Must agree with added-count (:1100).
- :kept-identities — scoped-keys of adopted requirements: (into [] (comp (filter adopted?) (map :scoped-key)) ordered). Must agree with the :kept count.
- :removed-identities — prior-plan identities absent from the next plan, in PRIOR-PLAN order for determinism: (filterv (complement next-ids) prev-identities) — do NOT build it from the prev-ids SET (nondeterministic iteration order would flake the fixture). Must agree with removed-count (:1101).

NAMES ARE DELIBERATE (from the ruling): since the retained-entry liveness repair (commit e95f46e6b6), a retained-but-unusable identity takes the ordinary ensure path, so a vector named :added would disagree with the :ensured count. The operational names tell the truth about what the runtime did: ensured = real ensure path (added OR retained-but-unusable), kept = genuinely adopted, removed = dropped from the plan.

ALSO in the SAME emit: correct :identities. Today it is (vec next-ids) (:1110) where next-ids is a SET (:1060) — the vector does not actually carry the grouped plan order the EP names. Emit (mapv :scoped-key ordered) instead; first verify `ordered` is post-dedupe (the :redundant-children advisory path) so no duplicate scoped-keys appear. Do NOT change the RETURN map (:identities next-ids at :1120) — commit-navigation consumes the set; only the trace tag changes.

TESTS/FIXTURES (this is the conformance for the correction — no retroactive EP row):
- spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn — currently asserts :ensured 1 :kept 1 :removed 1; extend the second navigation's expected route-plan tags to also pin :ensured-identities / :kept-identities / :removed-identities and the ordered :identities.
- the shape-driven egress test — implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj proves egress-by-shape (trace-egress/project-unknown-slot-value) for the route-plan :blocking and :identities vectors; extend it to cover the three new identity vectors (scoped keys inside any collection get the resource owner's egress policy — the safety already closes by shape, this pins it).

EP ERRATUM (one line, same PR) — docs/EP/EP-0037-route-planning-and-activation-ownership.md §Tooling staging clause: record that the R2 "identity diff" ships as the identity partition on the activation route-plan row (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities beside the counts, :identities in grouped plan order), and that occurrence/dependency groups, per-contributor requirement mapping, and local :after edges are deliberately not projected (internal planning mechanics; Xray's static route/resource graph + failure evidence + :redundant-children are the authorities). No live errata bead exists for this — this bead carries the erratum.

DISPATCH NOTE: spec/conformance/fixtures/ is under spec/ (hot-zone per dispatch rules) — sequence against other spec-touching beads.

ACCEPTANCE: a single :rf.resource/route-plan trace row answers "which identity was ensured / kept / removed on this navigation" without diffing two traces; counts unchanged; :identities carries planner order; partial-activation fixture and egress shape test pin the new shape; EP erratum line present; NO new conformance row, panel, or public plan value.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7170 (2026-07-28) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the new unit test and EP fixture each remove exactly one identity, so neither can exercise the promised ordering of :removed-identities.

CORRECTNESS: route.cljc says `(filterv (complement next-ids) prev-identities)` keeps the prior plan's order, and Spec 009 now makes that a public trace contract. The real routing caller stores `(:identities plan)` under `[:rf.runtime/routing :resource-plan token]`; that return slot is `next-ids`, a SET. The next activation reads and passes that set as `:prev-identities` (routing/events.cljc). Filtering a set in place preserves only its hash iteration order, not the prior planner's grouped order. The PR body itself concedes the live caller supplies a set, while calling its iteration merely “content-stable”. A multi-removal trace can therefore disagree with the spec and vary across host/runtime implementation even though the one-removal gates stay green.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: either carry the prior plan's existing ordered identity vector across the routing handoff (while retaining the set for membership/diff behavior), or explicitly make removed ordering unspecified and correct the source/spec claims. Prefer the former only if it is the small two-slot handoff it appears to be; do not add a new graph, panel, or plan projection. Add a case with at least two removed identities whose prior planner order differs from set iteration, and pin the order end-to-end. The ensured/kept vectors and all privacy projection work remain sound.
AUDIT-REOPEN DISCHARGED — PR #7228 (2026-07-28 17:22 AUSEST).

RULING (this bead's own): the ordering promise on :removed-identities is WITHDRAWN, not bought.

WHY. (1) Order carries no information there — removal is not an ordered operation; a plan releases the whole prior owner in ONE release-fx. :identities / :ensured-identities / :kept-identities are ordered because that order IS the plan execution order; removal has no counterpart. (2) Keeping it was not the small handoff it looked like: the only way to make it true is for the caller to stop round-tripping through a set, which changes the declared shape of a CROSS-FEATURE runtime-db slot documented in spec/Spec-Schemas.md, spec/016-Resources.md, and implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc (all outside this bead's fence). Paying that to manufacture determinism for a semantically orderless list is the wrong trade.

CODE. :removed-identities is now (into [] (remove next-ids) prev-ids) and :removed is its count — a pure function of the removal MEMBERSHIP (no caller ordering leaks in, so it is testable rather than merely unpinned), and it closes a latent inconsistency where :removed was counted from prev-ids while the vector was filtered from prev-identities (a duplicate-bearing prev-identities put them out of step with the counts=vector-size invariant 009 states). Same idiom as :blocking on the same row. implementation/routing is NOT in the diff — the caller still stores the set, which is now what the spec describes.

SPEC 009. One clause, roster only: '...and :removed-identities keeps the PRIOR plan's own order' becomes an explicit no-order promise with the reason, the evidence (the handoff records a set and hands it back), the replacement guarantee, and the :blocking precedent. Nothing else moved.

COVERAGE. r2-removed-identities-is-membership-not-caller-order removes THREE identities and supplies the same four prior identities four ways (vector / its reverse / the SET the live handoff threads / duplicate-bearing). Mutation proof: restoring the in-place filter reds it exit 1 with 4 failures naming the ordering — and empirically shows the live set path returning [c a b] for a supplied [a b c]. The pre-existing one-removal test stays GREEN under that mutation, confirming the audit's vacuity finding exactly. The EP-0037 fixture deliberately stays at one removal (no promised order = no pinnable multi-removal vector across hosts); a probe run perturbing its :removed expectation reds the corpus naming :ep-0037/r2-partial-activation, proving the lane executes it.

ROW STILL DEV-ONLY / EGRESS UNTOUCHED. Under -Dre-frame.debug=false the namespace runs 254 assertions / 17 failures on this branch AND on origin/main — byte-identical, so the new test contributes zero assertions in that posture. No slot is named, no shape changed, no projection lifted; epoch_egress_resource_trace_test green unchanged (83 tests / 667 assertions).

GATES. resources ns dev 0 (50/287); resources FULL dev 0 (743/6886); conformance corpus 0 (5/18); epoch egress 0 (83/667); check_doc_slugs.py 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict 0. Broader lanes deferred to CI.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7228 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the new multi-removal test varies vector order, set shape, and duplicates, but every test identity is distinct under ordinary Clojure `=`. It never exercises the repository's stricter CEDN-1 byte-identity boundary, where list- and vector-bearing scoped keys are deliberately distinct even though Clojure considers them equal.

CORRECTNESS: PR #7228 now computes `:removed-identities` from `prev-ids`, and both `prev-ids` and `next-ids` are raw Clojure sets. For `[:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p [1 2]}]` versus `[:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p (1 2)}]`, `(= a b)` is true and `(count (set [a b]))` is 1, while `state/key-id` returns two different CEDN-1 byte identities. The set therefore collapses one supported identity before `sort-by state/key-id` can canonicalize it. A transition that keeps one and removes the other can report no removal (and a wrong count), violating this bead's exact identity-partition acceptance. The same raw-set carriers also make retained membership and the next-plan handoff suspect for this supported pair.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: sorting by `state/key-id` is clean but occurs after irreversible equality collapse. Keep the repair local to the route identity carriers: perform membership/deduplication by byte `key-id`, preserve the scoped key as the emitted value, and carry both byte-distinct identities through the committed handoff (updating the documented slot shape only if necessary). Add an end-to-end route transition with list-vs-vector params that keeps one identity and removes the other; assert the exact `:kept-identities`, `:removed-identities`, count, and next handoff. Do not add a new graph, panel, or public planner value.
close_reason: Completed by merged PR #7391: route-plan membership, adoption, and removal use CEDN-1 key-id with direct and end-to-end twin witnesses. The deliberately larger simultaneous-plan/handoff shape remains exactly owned by open rf2-btdl1.

description:
Found while closing rf2-rjq9d (PR for the per-slot :key-projected arm).

rf2-rjq9d removed the row a per-slot :scope / :params declaration re-keys, because it hydrates as an ownerless, unaddressable, uncollectable duplicate. The COARSE :redact / :omit arms leave a row of the SAME class, and this PR deliberately did not touch them.

project-scoped-key replaces a coarse resource's scope and params with content-addressed {:rf/redacted <digest>} tokens, so the wire row installs under the DIGEST key-id. route-resource-plan and ensure-handler derive the ordinary scoped key and read (state/entry-path scoped-key) — the RAW key-id. So the coarse hydrated row is not addressed either, and, like the per-slot one, nothing collects it: inactive GC is timer-driven (gc-fired-handler fires against a handle armed by a commit fx) and hydration arms no timers. The new no-unaddressable-row-survives-hydration control in resources_ssr_projected_key_refetch_cljs_test PINS this: its exact expected key-id set names the two coarse rows under their PROJECTED key-ids beside three raw ones.

Why it was fenced out of rf2-rjq9d rather than folded in: the two arms are NOT the same hazard. The per-slot substitution is a CONSTANT sentinel, so it is many-to-one on precisely the slots that name a principal — two tenants collapse to one key, which is why no client may adopt by it and why removal was the only option. A coarse token is a content-addressed digest of the canonical value: one-to-one, and DERIVABLE in principle, since redact-value is a pure function of the live value the client already holds. So the coarse arm has a repair the per-slot arm does not.

Decide which contract the coarse arm should have, and make hydrate agree with it:
  (a) ADOPT — the client re-derives the digest from its live scope/params and reads the row under the projected key-id, turning the row into the cache hit it was presumably meant to be. Note this is a real behaviour change: these rows are metadata-only, so the win is the metadata, not data reuse.
  (b) DROP — treat it as rf2-rjq9d treats the per-slot row: withhold or drop, and let the client's one load stand.
Whichever is chosen, the acceptance criterion rf2-rjq9d was reopened for — no persistent unreachable duplicate — should hold for these rows too, and the end-to-end control should assert absence of the ROW rather than absence of its contents (the assertion shape that let rf2-rjq9d through).

Do not weaken key privacy: the raw scope/params must not ride, and the digest must stay one-way on the wire.
close_reason: Completed by merged PR #7391: coarse re-keyed rows are withheld server-side, dropped client-side, omitted from the refetch plan, and the host FNV arithmetic is aligned. Audit remainder rf2-hzcv8 owns the newly exposed off-box privacy/canonicalization defect without changing this locked scope.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7369 (2026-08-02) — the per-slot ghost removal is sound, but this owner’s coarse-token premise needs correction before choosing ADOPT.

PR #7369 deliberately exempts coarse `{:rf/redacted <digest>}` keys from `unaddressable-wire-key?`, and Spec 016 now calls that token “one-to-one and derivable in principle.” The current `redact-value` does not provide either property:

* Its CLJ branch hashes UTF-8 bytes with exact integer arithmetic; its CLJS branch hashes UTF-16 code units and multiplies 32-bit states with ordinary JS `*` rather than `Math.imul`. Even ASCII diverges: the landed CLJ `redact-value` maps `"tenant"` to `f93325e5`, while the CLJS branch’s source arithmetic maps the same `pr-str` bytes/text to `74e22aec`. Unicode has the additional UTF-8-vs-UTF-16 disagreement. A client therefore cannot re-derive the server token as option (a) assumes.
* FNV-1a-32 is a 32-bit non-cryptographic hash: it is necessarily many-to-one, reaches birthday collisions at roughly 2^16 distinct identities, and is brute-forceable for low-entropy tenant/account identifiers. The descriptions “one-to-one,” “never a collision,” “opaque,” and “one-way” are not true security properties of this token.

This does not undo #7369’s removal of constant-sentinel rows; it constrains rf2-4bjep’s coarse-row settlement. Acceptance should include a byte-identical CLJ/CLJS tokenizer fixture (ASCII, non-ASCII, surrogate pair), an explicit collision/privacy contract appropriate for identity-bearing scope/params, and no ADOPT path until the client can derive exactly the server’s token without making low-entropy identities enumerable. DROP remains available if durable metadata reuse is not worth a stronger token.

title: hicasso: establish the IME composition fence with a real CompositionEvent harness, on both input implementations
description:
STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and now against TWO implementations rather than one.

Arm 2 owned a composition fence because it owned the writes. On React the row
`:ime-composition-commits-nothing` was probed with synthetic `Event`s named
`compositionstart`/`compositionend`; those do not exercise React's composition
path, and the field never converged after `compositionend` in that probe. It was
deliberately left unasserted, because a fence asserted without being
demonstrated is worse than no fence (rf2-n3dxw, rf2-m6if4).

WHAT CHANGED. There are two controlled-input implementations in play, not one
(rf2-heqwo), and they face composition differently:

- plain React: `SyntheticCompositionEvent` plumbing on a controlled element,
  with React's own `beforeinput`/composition fallback deciding whether a change
  event is produced at all.
- UIx's port of Reagent's workaround: owns the write itself and never consults
  composition state — `input-handle-change` fires on every change, and
  `input-node-set-value` will rewrite the field mid-composition if the model
  moved (`uix/compiler/input.cljs:81-88`, `:28-69`).

WHAT IS NEEDED: a harness that dispatches real `CompositionEvent`s (and the
`input` events a composing IME actually produces, with the right
`inputType`/`isComposing`), against BOTH implementations, before anything is
claimed. `document.execCommand`-style synthesis and `js/Event.` with a
composition name are both insufficient; Playwright's CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`
is the likeliest route on Chromium.

Until then the row stays unasserted in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test.cljs,
and validation.md no longer lists it as an asserted row of the controlled grid.
close_reason: Completed by merged PR #7386: the landed CDP-driven harness establishes the IME commit fence across Hicasso, plain React, and the UIx port; rf2-digtt already owns the measured mid-composition rewrite ruling.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7371 — this owner's composition matrix now has a third behavior to cover. The PR says the converge “touches composition” nowhere because it wraps only the change slot, but `install!` wraps `onInput`/`onChange` — precisely the input events a composing IME produces — and every invocation calls `flushSync` and then `setSelectionRange`, even when no value write is needed. That can collapse the active composition range or rewrite a refused/normalised intermediate value. Extend the real CompositionEvent/CDP harness to Hicasso Arm 1's new converge as well as plain React and UIx, and pin that it neither writes nor moves selection mid-composition. Exact existing owner updated; no duplicate.

title: The reactive leg (headline 1) still has one witness: give reagent-ratom a second author
description:
RAISED BY rf2-2rtt6.17 (PR #7277), which was the audit's own item (d): 'consider whether the reactive leg deserves a second witness at all — one measurement is thin for the term the whole bar's like-for-like clause turns on.'

STATE AFTER rf2-2rtt6.17. Headline 1 — 'reading re-frame2 subscriptions rather than a bare cursor costs Reagent ~1.22x on mount and ~2.01x on a broad commit' — is now measured THREE TIMES rather than once:

  M1 mount reactive leg   1.218 [1.122-1.310] | 1.216 [1.185-1.241] | 1.213 [1.093-1.273]
  bulk broad reactive leg 2.008 [1.938-2.100] | 1.965 [1.875-2.000] | 2.073 [2.000-2.167]

publication run, plus two independent five-round re-runs at main 32cb224d6e. All disjoint from 1.0; the mount means sit inside 0.5% of each other.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. Three runs of ONE arm bound the instrument's run-to-run noise. They do NOT bound a systematic error in how :reagent-ratom is written — the same code produces the same bias every time. That is repetition, not replication.

THE GAP IS SPECIFIC. The converged witness set (rf2-a4x1o) IS a genuine second implementation of the DENOMINATOR: a different app namespace, a different schedule, and its reagent-subs/floor ranges overlap rf2-2rtt6.2's on all three shared rows. But it carries NO reagent-ratom ARM, so it corroborates the denominator and cannot touch the reactive leg at all. Every other P0 arm is likewise silent on it.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a reagent-ratom arm on the converged witness set (or any second author's page), measured beside its reagent-subs arm in the same run, so subs/ratom can be formed a second way. That is one arm on an existing instrument, not a new page.

The denominator page now states this limitation in its own 'What this settles, and what it does not' section rather than leaving it implicit, so nothing is currently overclaimed. This bead is the remedy, not a correction.
close_reason: PR #7310 delivered the requested second reactive-leg author; merged-PR audit defects were repaired by PR #7316.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7310 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The published M1/broad experiment is unusually well warranted: the ratom arm is opt-in, the measured rows share a segment and floor, starts are counterbalanced, per-round vectors and Student-t run intervals are durable, parity/read-back/control/order gates are fail-closed, the same-tree first-harness control is explicit, and the three authored patches landed exactly around unrelated chronological commits. The direction/magnitude distinction is also honest. Two implementation gaps remain under this exact owner.

The feature flag is global while arm presence is row-specific. With no `HICASSO_ONLY`, the driver intentionally selects all four rows; `HICASSO_RATOM=on` then reaches M2 and narrow. Those rows deliberately omit `:reagent-ratom` (`M2` ignores the flag and `bulk-arms` adds it only for `:broad`), but `row-record` still uses the global `ratom?` to divide by `[:reagent-subs :ratio :reagent-ratom]`, form `ratom-floor`, run the leg verdict, and label the row as carrying the arm. The natural flagged default therefore computes from a missing denominator (error or Infinity/NaN evidence) even though the driver says M2/narrow carry no ratom arm. Published runs avoided this only by always pairing `HICASSO_RATOM=on` with `HICASSO_ONLY=M1,broad`; neither CI nor the quality gates exercise the default flagged invocation.

The new replay test also asserts only `min(second-author rounds) > 1.24` while its diagnostic says 1.2500 exceeds first-author maxima 1.241 *and 1.273*. It does not exceed 1.273. The supported claim is that every second-author run mean exceeds every first-author mean; round ranges overlap, as the studio page correctly reports. The test message and threshold currently make a false round-level claim look pinned.

Bounded repair: decide leg presence from the actual row/slice (M1 or broad with a `:reagent-ratom` ratio), or reject flagged selections containing M2/narrow; add a cheap contract test for `HICASSO_RATOM=on` with the default rows and with M2/narrow-only, proving those rows emit no leg and no non-finite values. Rewrite the replay assertion to pin run-mean separation, or retract the round-level diagnostic. The published M1/broad measurements need not be re-run for either repair.

title: Release process should name the template's tools-SHA bump obligation
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-57bjg (PR #7173), filed because docs/release-process.md was outside that worker's fence.

rf2-57bjg made tools/template emit GIT coords for day8/re-frame2-xray and day8/re-frame2-story, pinned to a reviewed monorepo commit held in hooks.clj as :rf2-tools-sha. That pin has no in-repo source of truth (a commit of this repository cannot be lockstep-guarded against itself), so version_lockstep_test.clj's new tools-coords-are-git-coords guards the coord SHAPE only — git never :mvn/version, a real :deps/root, a full 40-char SHA, one commit shared by both tools. Freshness is a human obligation, documented only on the pin itself and in tools/template/spec/002-Generated-Shape.md §Tools-tier coords.

ASK: add the obligation to docs/release-process.md §The tools tier, in two places —
  (1) cutting a framework v* tag should bump :rf2-tools-sha to the release commit, so a generated project's tools ride the same code as its :mvn/version framework coords;
  (2) when xray-v* / story-v* finally ship, RETIRE the git coords: flip both tools back to {:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}, drop the day8/re-frame2-machines resolution pin from deps_with_story.edn (it exists only because two git coords into one monorepo get two checkouts), drop :rf2-tools-sha, and invert tools-coords-are-git-coords rather than deleting it.

Blocked-ish on nothing; it is a docs edit. Sequence it after PR #7173 merges so the release doc describes what is actually on main.

ALSO NOTED, not worth its own bead: tools/template/spec/003-DepsNew-Rebuild-Plan.md:309 still records the §2.4 history as adding 'day8/re-frame2-story {:mvn/version …}'. It is a DONE changelog entry describing what happened in May 2026, so it was left alone rather than rewritten.
close_reason: PR #7385 merged: the release guide now names the hooks.clj pin bump as the sole tools-side exception and verifies exactly that path.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7186 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality. docs/release-process.md says to edit tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj in the release commit so :rf2-tools-sha points at that commit parent. The same paragraph then says the release commit touches no tools file, and the checklist requires git diff --stat <pin> HEAD -- tools/ to be empty. The required pin edit itself makes both claims false, so a maintainer following the runbook must either fail its preflight or skip the check that is supposed to prevent tool skew. Keep the repair on this exact owner: state that the pin bump is the sole permitted tools-side release-commit difference (or choose a different explicit sequencing model), and make the artifact check validate that exact exception while requiring every other tools path to match <pin>. Preserve the no-self-SHA rationale; no general release framework is needed. The machines-viz executable export proof and the generated-smoke comment are otherwise complete and well bounded.

title: Grow the 009 ratchet by a Tags-column keys-set diff (NOT a trace-op arm) — ruled after rf2-wsopx
description:
MAYOR RULING: YES, and only the Tags arm (2026-07-26). The rf2-wsopx worker recommended this and asked rather than filing it, per its brief. I am adopting its reasoning as filed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING AT ALL: the 009 ratchet pins the Channel column and the error/warning emit sites — not trace ops and NOT the Tags column. That blind spot is why spec/009 never received the EP-0037 planner rows: :rf.route/prefetched appeared ZERO times in the catalogue while shipping, and :rf.error/resource-route-plan Tags column omitted both :plan-cause and :contributor while its narrative still taught partial planning against the ratified atomicity rule. A gate whose coverage never reaches the column where drift accumulates will keep reporting green over it.

THE RULED SHAPE — Tags-column keys-set diff, and nothing else: Spec-Schemas.md ALREADY defines one *Tags schema per catalogue row, and both files are ALREADY parsed by existing gates. So the arm is a keys-set comparison between the schema and the row, which the worker describes as "a parser away". It would have caught the Tags omission directly.

WHY NOT THE TRACE-OP ARM, which is the tempting other half: there is no per-op schema roster to diff against, so the only available check is "is every emitted op documented somewhere in 2500 lines of prose?" — a scan with a bad false-positive rate. That is the expensive half for the weaker signal, and this repo has already learned that a census whose pattern cannot distinguish a correction from a defect will fight every fix. Declined.

CONSTRAINTS: extend the EXISTING gate, do not add a new script. No new vocabulary. If the keys-set diff turns out to need a second source of truth to be meaningful, STOP and report — a gate needing a hand-maintained roster is the drift generator this repo keeps removing (see the derived evidence-producer roster that ended its class after going stale twice by hand-copying).

NON-VACUITY IS MANDATORY: prove the arm reds against the PRE-rf2-wsopx catalogue state, where :plan-cause and :contributor were genuinely missing from the row. An arm that cannot red on the defect that motivated it has not been tested — and this repo has shipped exactly that mistake before, where an audit method could not have caught its own motivating instance.
notes:
BASELINE MATERIALLY IMPROVED BY rf2-dxuzp (2026-07-26) — read this before building the arm.

I ruled that this arm ships with the 23 currently-redding rows as a SHRINK-ONLY BASELINE. The dxuzp adjudication has since changed what that baseline consists of, in the arm favour:

Spec-Schemas carries a :tags schema ONLY FOR TRACE-EMITTING CATEGORIES. Thrown rows and always-on record rows therefore FALL OUT OF THE PAIRING BY CONSTRUCTION — they have no :tags map at all (error/thrown-ex-info builds a FLAT map, and spec/009 section The thrown-error shape already declares :recovery among four REQUIRED slots on it). So the arm never had to reason about them.

CONSEQUENCE: the shrink-only baseline is roughly 20 rows of HONEST DEBT rather than 130 of noise. The worker words. That makes the ledger small enough to be drained rather than tolerated, and it means a row entering the baseline is a real signal instead of a category error.

ALSO STILL TRUE AND STILL OWED — the arm has a known defect I recorded earlier: its pairing keys off the NAME HALF of the operation keyword, so :rf.http/stale-suppressed and :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed collide and derive to the same schema name. Key the pairing off the WHOLE :operation. One line in the arm, not a corpus edit.
Audit of merged PR #7207: the PR explicitly confirms that the newly always-on `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` row is NOT protected by the Tags-column keys-set diff. The operation-derived name is `SchemaValidationFailureTags`, while Spec-Schemas publishes `SchemaValidationTags`, so invariant 6 never pairs or diffs them. The existing paired-count floor only catches loss of a previously counted pair; it cannot catch a row that was unpaired from the start. This is now a structural-only production egress record, making silent Tags drift material rather than theoretical.

Bounded acceptance: restore an explicit, stable pairing for this row—via a compatible canonical alias/mapping or a safe schema rename after checking consumers—without weakening the general operation-derived rule. Raise the exact paired-count floor in the same change, assert the live row is among the pairs, and mutation-prove that removing/adding a boundary-record key on either the catalogue or schema side reds the keys-set diff. Preserve the existing loss/rename floor tests and do not invent a second catalogue parser.
close_reason: PR #7385 merged: SchemaValidationFailureTags now pairs the live row, paired floor 94, with catalogue- and schema-side mutation proof.

title: Wave-1 arm: Hicasso lean-React (tournament)
description: Tournament arm 1 for EP-0038 (epic rf2-2rtt6; architecture.md Arm 1). React FCs minted by defview; <=2 shell hooks (subscription/epoch + frame, HD-020; callback refs, never useRef in the shell); re-render via commit->index->dirty set->epoch bump; generation fence (staged-stale CI witness); codec caching only (no extraction — that is PATCH machinery). Instrument: hooks/boundary, retained size vs the 0.4-0.5KB target, bulk K=100/300, per-read + per-keystroke paths, and the HD-002 tiers — grouped use-subs (the product default; canonical spelling in authoring.md) AND the ambient-collector challenger under the standard bead's adjudication clauses (tripwire overrides the clock). Build the DOGFOOD SCREEN (list + controlled field + sub reads) in THREE renderings — collector, grouped, raw UIx — judged on diff + preference. THE SIX-WEEK CLOCK STARTS at this arm's (or PATCH's) first commit that mounts the dogfood screen. Runtime skeleton stays OFF MAIN (spike branch); witnesses/instruments in the bench lane. Hard fences: no compiler, no dual mode, no ViewCell-class graph (= failed spike), no candidate ledger. Time-boxed per validation.md; results with commit SHA + repro command to the standard bead + studio.
notes:
LANDED AS PR #7321 (branch worker/arm1-2rtt6-9, head 9f614fe7e8). Runtime skeleton is in the bench/test lane at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/ — off every production source path (HD-017).

WHAT IS DONE.
- The two-hook shell, COUNTED AT REACT'S DISPATCHER rather than self-reported: ["useContext" "useSyncExternalStore"], and 2 hooks at 1, 7 and 20 reads. No useRef, useState, useMemo or useCallback. The mechanism that made two reachable is that the shell holds NO per-instance render-phase state at all: `subscribe` closes over the read SET only, so it is cached by that value, shared across boundaries, and identity-stable exactly while the reads are unchanged — which is React's own re-subscribe condition. React then hands that shared closure each fiber's own onStoreChange, and the registration minted inside is the commit-owned boundary id.
- HD-002 clause (a): no render-phase code mutates the index or a ref-count; one scratch array, reset by overwrite; abandoned renders need no cleanup. Clause (b): edge set replaced wholesale at commit, only when it changed, with the unchanged case detected WITHOUT BUILDING ANYTHING. The tripwire did not fire.
- The generation fence with its staged-stale witness, plus the 6.1 adversarial case (commit landing after the body returns).
- The dogfood screen MOUNTED in three renderings — K7 IS RUNNING. Canonical-DOM parity across all three with a can-answer-false control; narrow write touches one row; keyed reorder keeps the node; controlled field echoes in the caller's turn.
- The laziness finding from Arm 2: CHECKED AND REFUTED for this arm, structurally (the collector window closes around the eager codec), with three witnesses. Plus four deferred-read escapes now witnessed converting into a LOUD error rather than a silent missing edge.

HD-002's "acquire without deref" is NOT implementable against this substrate and fails silently: a derived value's `unset` baseline is never rf= a real value, and the render's own read went through subscribe-once (a different reaction, disposed), so a freshly acquired reaction reports movement on the first later commit whatever it did — every newly mounted boundary re-rendering once for nothing. One baseline deref per NEW UNIQUE KEY closes it.
2. The ambient frame outranks React context invisibly: the carried-invariant chain resolves the dynamic-var tier BEFORE context, so an ambient use-subscribe answers for the ambient frame while use-current-frame reports the provider's. It presents as a rendering difference. :ambient-frame nil is set in every DOM fixture here and a probe asserts the two read forms agree.

WHAT REMAINS (not blockers for this PR; each wants its own bead): the 100-cell controlled grid (K4's full row — caret, selection, IME, unchanged-model rejection, async normalisation); StrictMode / HMR body swap / a real h/boundary error boundary; H2 (render-side positional verification) untried; the survival metric's allocation-slope half; and no bar row published, per the restated-bar posture (rf2-b0tz5).

DESIGN INPUT FOR rf2-2rtt6.39 (delete the frame hook by threading the frame as a codec-supplied prop): I analysed exactly this while designing the shell and rejected it for v0 on CORRECTNESS, not cost. Threading works for boundaries the codec creates, but a frame-provider interleaved between two Hicasso boundaries is a React component the codec never sees, so a props-threaded frame would silently keep the outer frame across it. Any measurement of .39 needs an interleaved-provider witness or it will measure a design that is wrong in the one case providers exist for.

title: DC-09 evidence: measure the high-rate two-clock operating envelope
description:
OUTCOME
Measure Freehand's two-clock operating envelope and publish evidence-backed guidance for high-rate pointer/camera/animation/scroll hosts and controlled-input contention.

MATRIX
Offer 30/60/120/240 semantic updates per second; run one controlled field with 0/1/10/50/200 already-dirty siblings; compare stable-reference, fresh-but-rf=-equal, and one-leaf-changed behavior config at Vega/Spread-shaped sizes.

MEASURE
Separate offered host events, browser-observed events, accepted semantic events, reducer applications, commits, presentation opportunities, peak backlog, settlement tail, equality cost, host update cost, and p50/p95/p99. Include deterministic count/correctness/cleanup facts and full provenance per D021.

GUIDANCE
Name the default: a behavior may own high-rate host motion while semantic started, optional preview, and committed events cross. Keep host-local style/geometry/motion outside app-db unless semantically required. Measure dispatch-per-move before adding policy.

HOST/MODE
Pinned real browser for timing; structural/config equality probes where applicable; interpreted/compiled attribution.

NON-GOALS
No generic debounce/throttle/coalesce API, equality hooks, host-local state model, or assumption that 60 Hz is inherently safe or unsafe.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The complete matrix publishes deterministic counts and timing distributions with revision/build/browser/hardware/sample provenance.
2. Controlled input proves no drops and correct caret/composition before latency is discussed.
3. Costs are attributed to event/reducer/Freehand/React/host work rather than rolled into one latency number.
4. New scheduling/preview/equality vocabulary is proposed only for a material attributed bottleneck repeated in two realistic witnesses; otherwise the result explicitly recommends no new API.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED — PR #7240 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7240), branch worker/dc09-evidence-18212. All five gates green (exit 0): bench compile 259 files 0 warnings; bench browser 30 tests/482 assertions 0F/0E (466 + exactly the 16 added); order-guard self-test 8 checks, NO REFUSAL; npm run test:browser 841/5459 0F/0E; three b10_prod_run.cjs production runs, each :d021 :release-evidence.

THE FAULT, CONFIRMED AND FIXED. drive!'s :tail-ms was read off a clock started at SETTLE time. The interval callback that notices the drive duration has elapsed is the one AFTER the last offer -- one whole period later, by construction, since it is the next fire of the same setInterval -- so the clock omitted that interval, and where the last generation had already committed (most of the time at low rates) it published approximately the 4 ms polling delay. The audit's diagnosis was exactly right.

SO THE PREVIOUS NOTE'S 'tail <=5.4 ms even at 240 Hz against a 20 ms crossing' WAS THE POLL, NOT THE TAIL. That claim is retracted. Measured with the corrected instrument (HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15, rev 65abc3b99e):
  production, tail ms (3 runs): k=0 30/60/120/240 Hz -> 0.8-1.1 / 0.5-0.8 / 0.3-0.5 / 0.4-0.5; k=200 -> 4.6-5.4 / 2.2-2.5 / 2.4-3.7 / 3.2-3.5.
  development, tail ms (1 run): k=0 -> 5.1 / 3.9 / 3.8 / 3.0; k=200 -> 15.8 / 24.3 / 14.0 / 21.1.
  what the OLD field was actually publishing (the poll delay): 4.1-6.0 ms in all sixteen cells, essentially a constant set by the 4 ms poll period.
The old number was FLATTERING at k=200 dev by 3-4x and PESSIMISTIC at k=0 prod by 6-10x.

THE TAIL IS ONE CROSSING, at every rung of both bundles. Prod k=200 tail 2.2-5.4 against the synchronous window's p50 2.6-3.6 / p95 3.3-5.1; prod k=0 tail 0.3-1.1 against p50 0.3-0.5; dev k=200 14.0-24.3 against 18.3-22.2; dev k=0 3.0-5.1 against 3.5-4.6. Stated honestly in the report as an IDENTITY not an independent measurement -- the tail IS the last generation's own latency, same two timestamps -- and what makes it a RESULT is what sits beside it: outstanding 0 and settled? true in all sixteen runs. A settlement tail of one crossing means there was never a second one waiting. A draining queue would scale with the requested rate; it does not (prod k=200 tail at 240 Hz is 3.2-3.5, SMALLER than at 30 Hz's 4.6-5.4).

RECOMMENDATION 'ADD NO SCHEDULING VOCABULARY' HOLDS, and it survived a correction against its own interest: at k=200 dev the true tail is 3-4x the flattering published figure and the no-throttle case holds anyway, because one crossing is one crossing whatever it costs. A throttle exists to stop a queue forming; there is no queue.

C3, THE NEW CONTROL (the audit's 'assertion that would fail if the clock is restarted at settle time'). The gap between the last offer and the settle decision is one interval by construction, and the run predicts it from an INDEPENDENT counter, duration/offered. Predicted vs measured, ms, 3 prod runs: k=0 33.3-35.0 vs 33.4-37.1 | 16.3 vs 15.4-17.5 | 8.0 vs 7.0-8.1 | 4.0 vs 4.2-5.0; k=200 33.3-35.0 vs 32.7-41.0 | 16.3 vs 15.3-16.2 | 8.0 vs 7.1-7.9 | 4.0-4.1 vs 3.5-4.6. Agree at all eight cells, worst within 18% (the 30 Hz rung, where one interval is 33 ms), every other within 15%. :tail-anchored? is also a GATE -- it fails a run whose gap is under half a requested period, a floor setInterval cannot violate however far behind the browser has fallen; a settle-time clock has no last-offer timestamp and cannot produce the gap at all. Asserted in the browser row AND the production entry's coherence filter. :tail-source was :observer in all sixteen -- the poll never had to answer.

C1/C2 unchanged and still exact. 0 UNVERIFIED OF 5760 (0 of 1440 in each of three production runs and 0 of 1440 in the dev run).

AXES REUSED, NOT RE-RUN: the rate ladder, the sibling ladder, the behaviour-config axis (stable-reference / fresh-but-rf=-equal / one-leaf at Vega 96 and Spread 900 leaves) and controlled-input contention were all published by #7179 and #7198. Report sections 3-5 and 7 stand untouched. Re-running a published ladder is waste; the settlement tail was the ONE MEASURE-list item whose published figure did not survive its own audit.

GUIDANCE DELIVERED -- report section 9, 'Guidance for a high-rate host', which is what DC-09 was for and what the report did not have. Section 8 answers Freehand's API designers; nothing addressed the application author. In one line: DRIVE IT DIRECTLY, SPEND YOUR ATTENTION ON HOW MUCH YOU DIRTY RATHER THAN ON HOW OFTEN YOU DISPATCH, AND DO NOT BUILD A THROTTLE. Names the default (a behavior owns high-rate host motion; only semantic started, optional preview and committed cross); four things not to bother building, each answered by a measurement (throttle/debounce/rAF coalescer; memoised or ref-cached configs; a 'settling' UI state; a distinct preview lane); four things to do in priority order (move the v/sub to the boundary that uses it, worth a constant 3.1-3.3 ms; count cells dirtied, ~0.012 ms each; measure dispatch-per-move BEFORE adding policy; type into it); and the one caveat that would change the advice -- real coalesced pointer streams are still unmeasured and are the single shape that could produce a backlog above 1.

NO SRC CHANGE. implementation/freehand/src/** untouched -- this is measurement, not optimisation. No FH- id, no roster change, no shared build configuration touched. Report sections 9 and 10 renumbered to 10 and 11. Raw records local-only at ai/findings/2026-07-28.b10-tail-anchored-prod-{1,2,3}.log. Freehand-vs-Reagent untouched (held on rf2-lbs3y).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7240 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: The merged code correctly repairs the current `:tail-ms` formula and adds useful host guidance, but the promised regression assertion is not coupled to the value it claims to protect. Current origin/main is unchanged on this point.

CORRECTNESS: `:tail-ms` uses `(- t-settle t0)`, while `:tail-anchored?` validates only the separate `gap = t-poll-start - t0`; the browser and production gates then check only `tail-anchored?` plus that `tail-ms` is numeric and nonnegative. Mutating `:tail-ms` back to a settle-clock expression such as `(- t-settle t-poll-start)` leaves `gap`, `:tail-anchored?`, and the nonnegative check unchanged, so every new C3 assertion can remain green while the published field again measures the wrong interval. Thus the PR statement that the new assertion fails if the tail clock restarts at settle time is false.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: Make the final generation observer latency the single source of truth for `:tail-ms`, or expose the retained last-offer and observer timestamps and assert the exact algebraic identity used to publish it. Keep C3 as a separate check that the retained offer timestamp is the immediately preceding interval. Add one small mutation-style witness that changes only the tail start and must fail; do not rebuild the benchmark.
CRASH-RECONCILIATION VERIFICATION (read-only triage, 2026-08-03, tree at 0bfd309b67). Examined for closure; NOT CLOSED. The measurement work landed (5e6f28d26e, 8df9a6b6ab, c31e0ce29d, 662993367e, 3abe0f1be5 — newest 2026-07-28), but the #7240 audit-reopen obligation is UNMET, verified by reading the files, and the audit's 'current origin/main is unchanged on this point' still holds.

implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b10_two_clock.cljs:737 still publishes :tail-ms (when t0 (- t-settle t0)) with :tail-anchored? derived separately at :743 from the gap. The gates only check the anchor plus numeric/nonnegative: b10_two_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs:385 asserts tail-anchored?, :391 asserts (and (number? tail-ms) (not (neg? tail-ms))); the production coherence filter b10_prod_app.cljs:349-351 checks the same three. Mutating :tail-ms back to a settle-clock expression such as (- t-settle t-poll-start) leaves gap, :tail-anchored? and the nonnegative check all green — so the C3 assertions still cannot fail on the value they claim to protect.

REMAINDER: make the final generation's observer latency the single source of truth for :tail-ms (or expose the retained last-offer and observer timestamps and assert the exact algebraic identity used to publish it); keep C3 as a separate check that the retained offer timestamp is the immediately preceding interval; add one mutation witness that changes only the tail start and must fail. Do not rebuild the benchmark.

AN INTERRUPTED DOLT GENERATIONAL GC CAN ROLL THE BEADS TRACKER BACK MID-SESSION, AND IT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE CORRUPTION (2026-08-03).

SYMPTOM SEQUENCE, in one 10-minute window: 'bd export' failed with 'error opening table file: table file not found: .dolt/noms/<hash>'. Then EVERY bd command — ready, list, show — exited 1. THE MISSING TABLE NAME DIFFERED BETWEEN CONSECUTIVE CALLS (18uc3mpc..., then 5l677oov...), noms/oldgen existed but was EMPTY, and the noms/ file count went 7 -> 91 across a couple of minutes. That is a generational GC rewriting table files, not disk damage.

IT RECOVERS ON ITS OWN. Roughly two minutes later bd returned exit 0 with no intervention. DO NOT rebuild the database from JSONL while this is happening — 'bd export' failing is NOT proof of data loss, and a rebuild from a checkpoint would discard everything since it.

THE REAL DAMAGE IS A PARTIAL ROLLBACK, AND IT IS SILENT. After recovery the tracker had time-travelled: a bead closed ~20 minutes earlier was back to IN_PROGRESS with its ORIGINAL 'Updated' date, and 5 note-appends were gone. But it was PARTIAL — a second close from the same pass SURVIVED. So you cannot assume all-or-nothing; verify each write individually with 'bd show'.

WHAT SAVED IT: the worker that made the writes still had them in its transcript. When bd broke I immediately messaged it to STOP all bd use and report every close/update verbatim WITH its verification evidence, then re-applied the 7 writes by hand and checkpointed at once. WITHOUT THAT REPLY THE WORK WAS UNRECOVERABLE — the JSONL checkpoint predated the writes.

RULES: (1) a tracker-mutating worker's report is a durable artefact — make its brief require verbatim reasons + evidence, not a summary; (2) checkpoint IMMEDIATELY after re-applying, do not batch; (3) row counts move under you because an automated merged-PR-audit process also commits .beads — 'HEAD had N' changing between your own checkpoints is NOT necessarily corruption; (4) beads-checkpoint.sh's shrinkage guard is the right instrument to ask 'did I lose bulk data?' — a clean round-trip at the same row count means the answer is no.

title: MEASURE: the :& attribute-merge spelling's clock cost is unmeasured (HD-023 caveat)
description:
RAISED by the rf2-2rtt6.36 worker (PR #7328), which recorded the gap in HD-023 rather than letting it pass silently.

THE OBLIGATION IT TRIPS. The 'Hicasso authors no codec' ruling (rf2-2rtt6.29, PR #7322) carries an explicit caveat: reagent-slim's codec is cheapest AS MEASURED, and Freehand's extra per-element capabilities (controlled-input door, caller split, top-layer, declared properties, id-conflict, class/style alias composition) are a CAPABILITY difference rather than pure overhead — so 'if Hicasso later needs one of those capabilities, THE COST OF ADDING IT TO SLIM'S CODEC MUST BE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED'. The :& merge is exactly such an addition: a reserved key the codec must recognise and resolve at every element that carries one.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT KNOWN. The ergonomics case is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted — the RealWorld article editor was ported both ways with elements AND dispatched intents asserted identical, four repeated attribute maps collapsing to one helper plus four call sites, and the helper does not have to defend itself. What is NOT known is what :& costs on the clock, per element and per mount, against the same page without it.

THE WORK: price :& on the existing lane — same witness, same rounds, same arm-order discipline, the only variation being whether the page uses :& or the expanded attribute maps it replaces. Report per-element and per-mount cost with ranges, and state plainly whether it is inside instrument resolution. If it is free, say so and the caveat is discharged; if it is not, the figure belongs beside HD-023 so the ergonomic win is quoted with its price rather than without it.

SEQUENCING: needs a QUIET BOX (browser measurement) and should run after PR #7328 lands so it measures the shipped spelling. Do not re-litigate the ergonomics ruling — that is settled and demonstrated; this bead prices it.
notes: SHAPE NOTE from the rf2-2rtt6.36 worker (2026-08-03, the merged-PR audit #7332 repair): the codec this bead prices CHANGED SHAPE under it, so measure the shipped one. The tag shorthand is no longer folded into the props map — merge-shorthand and its dissoc/assoc pair are gone, and the shorthand is folded onto the object the walk emits instead (fold-shorthand!). convert-props' three lanes are two: the propless short-circuit, and convert-then-fold. The :& merge itself is unchanged (still one contains?, still the map by identity when absent), but the per-element denominator around it is not what it was, and the class slot now costs a class-names coercion at the slot rather than one in the map surgery. Nothing here is a timing claim — the repair PR ran no bench driver and published no row, deliberately, because siblings held the box. title: Browser lane treats a double-fired cljs.test done as diagnostic noise, not a failure
description:
Split out of rf2-0ke4x, which fixed five double-fired `done` calls in `controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. The fix is verified, but the class of defect remains UNGUARDED: no gate fails on a double-fired `done`.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. `cljs.test/run-block` wraps the async continuation in a `delay` and the second `done` takes the realized branch:

    (if (realized? d)
      (println "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.")
      @d)

So a duplicate is a console `println`, never an assertion failure. `implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs` taps `page.on('console', ...)` and buffers every line, but by deliberate design (rf2-mwx08) 'Console output stays diagnostic-only; only `pageerror` is fatal'. The warning is therefore captured and then discarded unless RF2_VERBOSE_TESTS=1. rf2-0ke4x's six warnings rode green through PR #7162's merge and were found by a human reading the diff.

THE CHEAP FIX, and why it is not in rf2-0ke4x. The runner already has the exact hook: it collects `consoleLines` and separately treats `pageErrors` as fatal. Promoting the single literal 'Async test called done more than one time' to a fatal console pattern is roughly five lines next to the existing `pageErrors.length > 0` arm. It is general — it catches ANY suite in the mounted tier, not one file — which is why it is the right guard and a bespoke textual lint over the suite sources is not.

It was left out of rf2-0ke4x for two reasons. It is outside that bead's fence (`implementation/freehand/test/**`); and it changes the VERDICT semantics of the whole browser lane, so any other suite currently emitting the warning would go red on the same commit. That needs its own full-lane gate rather than riding a five-line deletion.

ACCEPTANCE. Promote the warning to a fatal console pattern in the browser runner; confirm the full browser lane is green on main with the promotion in place (i.e. no OTHER suite is currently double-firing); add a policy test alongside the existing `_impl-browser-runners-verdict-policy.test.cjs` family covering the new fatal pattern. A verified-clean lane plus the promotion means the next PR #7162-shaped regression reds instead of merging.

EVIDENCE THE LANE IS OTHERWISE CLEAN (rf2-0ke4x, browser run at 835 tests): before the fix, exactly 6 warnings, all attributable to `controls-kit-dom-cljs-test`; after the fix, 0. No other suite emitted one, so the promotion should not red anything today.
close_reason: PR #7400. The fatal-console promotion itself landed in PR #7343; this closes the hole auditing #7343 found. serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs built its runner child env as '{ ...process.env, ...(cond ? {K: v} : {}) }', which only ever ADDS the key, so an ambient RF2_DUPLICATE_DONE_DRIFT_UNVERIFIABLE=1 rode through to the UNFLAGGED default test:browser lane and skipped the fail-closed duplicate-done matcher-drift verdict entirely. computeRunnerEnv (scripts/lib/browser-runner-drift-env.cjs) now pins both directions explicitly: the flag always forwards '1', its absence always DELETES the var. Extracted so the rule is unit-testable by CALLING it, not by asserting on source text (the same gap class a prior audit found in the matcher-drift check). Gates: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with the new _browser-runner-drift-env.test.cjs 6/6 in test:script-helpers; npm run test:browser exit 0, 1024 tests / 6335 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors on the UNFLAGGED default lane (the path that must CARRY the drift check).

It reads run-browser-tests.cjs and asserts that the runner still contains its own regex; if cljs.test changes the emitted warning, neither that file nor this test changes, so the gate remains green while FATAL_CONSOLE_RE stops matching. The manual fixture likewise emitted the copied literal rather than producing an actual cljs.test double-done. title: reagent-slim's hiccup walk is 1.7-1.9x stock Reagent's, and its prop-name cache is the named term — measured, in a SHIPPED adapter
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-2rtt6.63 (PR #7390), as a by-product of putting three interpreters side by side on one witness value in one process. This is not a Hicasso finding — `day8/reagent-slim` is a PUBLISHED artefact and this is a defect in it.

THE ROWS (`walk_vs_reagent_app`, the census acceptance page's 1,202-element hiccup realized once outside every timed window, 4 arms × 6 rounds × (4 warmup + 10 samples), arm-order guard REPORTABLE on both runs, diagnostic in-page clock):

    slim / stock reagent   1.9020 (run 1)   1.7273 (run 2)
    slim ms/walk           1.2125 [1.1125-1.4500]  vs stock 0.6375 [0.6000-0.9000]
    ns/element             1,009  vs  530

THE NAMED TERM, from the same instrument's stage table over the page's own 1,489 prop occurrences:

    cached-prop-name   slim 49.4 / 53.4 ns/op   stock reagent 24.5 / 26.2   hicasso 21.5 / 16.8

So slim's prop-name lookup is ~2x stock Reagent's for the same answer, and it is asked once per prop on every element of every mount. Stock's is a `.hasOwnProperty` plus a `gobj/get`; slim's adds `reserved-prop-key?` as a SET lookup (a string hash for a roster of three) and `own-key?` as `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, both on the HIT path.

Hicasso's answer to exactly this shape is on main as of PR #7390 and is worth reading before re-deriving one: an `Object.create(null)` cache makes the false-hit class structurally impossible and moves the poisoning refusal to the MISS branch, which runs once per distinct literal for the life of the build rather than once per element per mount (18.1 -> 11.1 ns/op on the prop cache, 16.6 -> 11.2 on the tag cache; the fast-mode + `instance?` alternative was costed at 13.8 / 12.1 and declined).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER. Every HD-008 donor rung and the pre-Hicasso candidate ride `reagent2.impl.template`'s `:f>` walk and read 1.33-1.5x, and this is where that comes from — the donor rungs were measuring reagent-slim's walk, not "runtime interpretation" as such. Any consumer of `day8/reagent-slim` pays it today.

WHAT TO DO.

1. Profile slim's `convert-props` / `cached-prop-name` path element-by-element the way rf2-y1jkm profiled Hicasso's. DO NOT assume the prop-name cache is the whole 1.9x — the stage table names one term and the whole-walk gap is far larger than that term explains. Candidates the code suggests but which must be costed, not assumed: `collapse-class-keys`'s `contains?` probes per element, `top-prop-conv`'s per-prop `native?` threading and its 3-arity `convert-prop-value`, `html-attr-name?`, `get-react-key`'s meta read per element, `void-tag?`.
2. Cost any change against slim's OWN witnesses and its own suite, on the clock, before landing.
3. Slim's reserved-head guard, keyword-prop warn-once diagnostic and source-coord stamp are real public-adapter obligations Hicasso does not carry. None may be dropped for speed — find the shape that keeps them off the hit path instead.

FENCES: this is `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim`, a published artefact with its own suite. Every behaviour witnessed, no diagnostics removed. Not a Hicasso bead and not bench-lane.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md
