title: hicasso: converge a controlled element in-turn, with the caret where the edit left it
description:
MEASURED AND GREEN AS A PROTOTYPE; needs a home.

Neither shipped path gives a controlled input both halves of what a
store-backed field owes its user — same-turn convergence AND a caret at the
position the edit left it. React converges in-turn and throws the caret to the
end; UIx's port gets the caret right one animation frame late. The matrix is on
docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md (rf2-n3dxw).

THE SHAPE, measured green on all five rows of the family in one turn
(`a-same-turn-converge-can-have-both-halves-at-a-stated-price` in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test.cljs).
At the end of the change handler, still inside the discrete event and still
ahead of React's own end-of-event restore:

  1. `flushSync` so the synchronous door's commit lands now rather than in the
     `finally` of React's `batchedUpdates$1`;
  2. if the field still disagrees with what the element renders, write the
     rendered value — which also makes React's later `updateInput` a no-op,
     because it only assigns when the two differ;
  3. put the caret back by offset from the END of the string.

PRICE, stated: one `flushSync` per keystroke on a controlled element; a
per-instance record of the value that element last rendered (the handler's own
closure carries the value from the render that MINTED it, which is stale after a
re-render, and `(= (.-value node) dom-value)` alone cannot tell a refusal from a
keystroke the model took verbatim — that trap is measured, not assumed); and the
synchronous door only, because `dispatch` drains on a macrotask so at the end of
the handler the model has not moved.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COST: no user-visible ceremony — the view writes an ordinary
`:value`/`:on-change` pair, no ref, no effect, no escape hatch; and no hook in
the boundary shell, so the HD-020 ≤2-hook budget is untouched. UIx's own answer
costs a wrapper COMPONENT per input with three hooks in it
(`uix/compiler/input.cljs:132-143`); this costs none, because it belongs in the
element path rather than in a component.

BLOCKED ON: an element path to put it in. Neither Hicasso nor the shipped UIx
adapter mints its own `:input` today — UIx does — which is why the prototype
sits in the witness's view labelled as a measurement. Dispatch when Hicasso's
interpreter owns element creation, or alongside a ruling on rf2-heqwo.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-02 (worker/converge-fki5d, PR #7371
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7371).

WHERE IT LIVES. `front.controlled/install!`, called from
`front.codec/native-element` — the element path, which is what makes it free at
the authoring surface. `grid.cljs` (the 100-cell witness's view) did not change
by a character: an ordinary `:value` / `:on-input` pair, no ref, no effect, no
escape hatch. NO HOOK WAS SPENT — nothing was added to the boundary shell and
`arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test` still reads exactly
["useContext" "useSyncExternalStore"].

THE FIVE ROWS, in one turn, on the arm's mounted grid
(`arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/the-family-converges-in-one-turn-with-the-caret-where-the-edit-left-it`),
every reading on the line after `dispatchEvent`, no `act` anywhere:

  refusal at the end   "12"    + a at [2 2] -> "12"     [2 2]
  refusal mid-string   "12345" + z at [2 2] -> "12345"  [2 2]   (React alone: [5 5])
  uppercasing          "ABCD"  + x at [2 2] -> "ABXCD"  [3 3]   (React alone: [5 5])
  regrouping           "1,234" + 5 at [5 5] -> "12,345" [6 6]
  accepted keystroke   "abcd"  + X at [2 2] -> "abXcd"  [3 3]

Two rows that recorded React's caret jump as RECORDED-NOT-DESIRED are corrected
to what the arm now does.

THE PRICE IS LOWER THAN QUOTED. One `flushSync` per keystroke and the
synchronous door only, as priced. But the third item — a per-instance record of
the value the element last rendered — IS NOT CHARGED. It is `node.defaultValue`,
which React already maintains on every commit of a genuinely controlled input or
textarea (`updateInput:1671-1672` -> `setDefaultValue:1737-1741`,
`initInput:1721`, `updateTextarea:1842-1851`, react-dom 19.2.0). No ref (which
would change the identity React uses to decide whether to re-attach — the
objection `front.intent/ref-position?` already documents), no WeakMap, no extra
prop. What remains is a DEPENDENCY, named in one place
(`front.controlled/last-rendered`) and pinned against a live React tree by
`the-record-is-reacts-own-mirror-and-is-not-the-handlers-closure`, which also
asserts the record MOVES when the rendered value moves — the half a closure
cannot do.

THE TRAP IS REPRODUCED, not assumed.
`front/controlled_dom_cljs_test/the-closure-value-wipes-a-keystroke-the-model-took-verbatim`
calls `converge-to!` twice with ONE ARGUMENT DIFFERENT: handed the handler's own
closure value it writes "abcd" over the user's just-accepted "abXcd" and the
character is gone; handed the record, nothing moves. A companion row measures
why nothing cheaper works — `(= (.-value node) dom-value)` reads TRUE on a
refusal and TRUE on a verbatim keystroke.

MUTATION-PROVED TWICE. Removing the one `install!` call reds 14 assertions, every
caret falling back to [5 5] with the refused character still on screen. Removing
only the `flushSync` reds 4, including the ORDINARY ACCEPTED KEYSTROKE — without
it the record is one render stale. Both restored, green.

GATES: test:cljs 0 (12290 tests / 61538 assertions); full browser 0 (940 / 5895);
fast-PR spine 0 (PASS, 17/17 per-ns isolation); check_doc_slugs 0; clj-kondo
2026.04.15 with CI's exact invocation, errors: 0, zero findings in any changed
file.

RAISED, NOT RESOLVED: HD-019 calls `flushSync` "the evidence-gated last resort,
never the default", and this makes it the default for every controlled element.
The evidence gate is met; the ruling's text is Mike's to amend. Filed separately.
close_reason:
AUDIT GAP FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7401 (branch worker/caret-fki5d-47sko).

THE GAP, as the #7371 audit stated it: install! decides an element is caret-bearing from the props that MINT the wrapper, but step 1 of the converge is a flushSync — and a flushSync is a render. A synchronous handler re-rendering the same <input> from type=text to type=number keeps the node (React updates the attribute), so the wrapper minted by the text render goes on running against an element with no caret, and setSelectionRange throws InvalidStateError.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE. converge! reads the caret a SECOND time, after the flush, and is inert when the answer changed:

  (when (and (string? rendered)
             (number? (.-selectionStart node)))
    (converge-to! node dom-value caret-was rendered))

converge-to! is untouched, so the trap row that calls it twice with one argument different still says exactly what it said. No hook added — this adds a READING, never a write; arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test is unchanged and green.

THE ROW: arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/a-type-change-inside-the-flush-leaves-the-converge-inert. A live React tree, no act, no flushSync in the path it reads; a type-flipping-cell derives :type from the model so ONE accepted keystroke re-renders text->number inside the converge's own flush. It asserts the premise rather than assuming it — (identical? before after) pins that React really kept the node.

A LISTENER WAS NECESSARY, and this is worth recording. React does not let a throw from inside a discrete event escape dispatchEvent; it hands it to reportError. The first draft of the row was GREEN OVER A LIVE EXCEPTION while the runner's uncaught-pageerror gate (rf2-mwx08) failed the build from outside — cljs.test read 0 failures, 0 errors. The row now installs a window error listener so the throw is its own to assert and it reds BY NAME.

MUTATION-PROVED: deleting only the post-flush reading gives exit 1 and EXACTLY ONE failure, by name —
  expected: (= [] errs)
    actual: (not (= [] ["Failed to execute 'setSelectionRange' on 'HTMLInputElement': The input element's type ('number') does not support selection."]))
Every OTHER assertion in the row passed under the mutation, including the stale-record one. That is what establishes the throw as the defect and record-staleness as the second, quieter reason to be inert.

THE RECORD IS STALE THERE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. setDefaultValue skips a FOCUSED number field (react-dom@19.2.0:1738), so defaultValue still holds what the TEXT render wrote — the row asserts (= "" (last-rendered after)) directly. The converge would write that over the field mid-event; React's own end-of-event restore happens to put the committed value back, so the field survives — by accident. The prose says exactly that and does NOT overclaim a data loss that does not occur.

THE FIVE LANDED ROWS ARE UNTOUCHED and green throughout.

rf2-digtt UNTOUCHED: this adds a DOM read and removes a write. It never consults, sets or clears composing state and does not change the composing path in either direction. The carve-out remains unruled and unimplemented.

GATES, foreground with exit codes: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS fast PR spine, per-ns isolation 17/17); test:browser 0 (1025 tests / 6345 assertions); test:browser under mutation 1 (1 failure, by name); shadow-cljs compile browser-test 0; adapter smokes --filter uix 0 (1 spec). NOT run: docs gates (no doc surface changed), the CI-only tier, and the non-UIx adapter smokes.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7371 — correctness gap in the shipped converge. `install!` decides that an input is caret-bearing from the props that minted the currently running wrapper, but `converge!` reads `selectionStart` before `flushSync` and `converge-to!` calls `setSelectionRange` unconditionally after that flush. A synchronous handler can re-render the same `<input>` from `type="text"` to `type="number"` (or another non-caret type) during the flush; React retains the node, after the commit `selectionStart` is nil, and the old wrapper throws `InvalidStateError` from `setSelectionRange`. Independent Chromium primitive: text/value/defaultValue `12345`, caret 2; switch the focused node to number; value/defaultValue remain `12345`, selectionStart becomes null, and `setSelectionRange(2,2)` throws exactly that error. Add a live React regression where the handler synchronously changes the type and require the converge to re-check post-flush applicability and remain inert, without weakening the five landed rows.

title: Hicasso: one attribute-merge spelling — a reserved :& key, with the owned-literal law unconditional
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

Freehand — the shipped interpreted substrate — makes an author choose between THREE
attribute-merge forms depending on where the target is, and the penalty for choosing
wrong is SILENT:

  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:233
    v/spread-safe — "internal DOM / library element that must keep controlled +
    identity invariants ... PRESERVES THE CONTROLLED-INPUT DOOR"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:234
    v/spread — "an element you own ... DOES NOT claim the door"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:389-393
    ordinary merge — forwarding onto a declared v/defhost head; "NEITHER SPREAD FORM
    IS LEGAL THERE"

The penalty is recorded twice, as a wall with no error attached:
  docs/core/freehand/operate/limits-and-escapes.md:32 — "Dynamic map on controlled
  input without spread-safe | forfeits door proof"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:416 — same row, "forfeits the door into
  batching"

There is no diagnostic. Caret and IME protection simply stop.

re-frame.ui has the same split (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:539 spread,
:554 spread-safe) and admits the cost at ui.cljc:573 — "General (ui/spread base
overrides) remains the visible-cost escape and STILL FORFEITS THE SYNC DOOR."

THE PROPOSAL. Hicasso has ONE merge, spelled as DATA in the attribute map, with one
unconditional law:

    [:input      {:& caller-attrs :value v :on-input ev}]
    [:div        {:& base :class "own"}]
    [date-picker {:& caller-attrs :selected d}]

  (a) :& is a reserved attribute key carrying a runtime map. It is data, not a call —
      so a forwarded remainder survives into a structural test and into tooling.
  (b) THE LAW: the literal keys written in the map ALWAYS win over :&. This is
      HD-010(a)'s owned-literal merge law (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:203-206 —
      ":key, :ref, controlled :value/:checked, and owned event handlers are
      unoverridable by theme or parts") applied to EVERY merge rather than only under
      theming. The controlled-input door then cannot be forfeited by a merge at all,
      which deletes the whole class of silent failure above.

PRECEDENT for the spelling: UIx already uses :& for exactly this in this repo —
examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs:148 (":& spreads the substrate-free
model/frame-config into these props").

WHAT IT COSTS. The case where a caller override SHOULD win is now spelled by not
writing the literal. That is the honest way round: the dangerous default is the other
one. ":&" cannot collide with a real DOM attribute.

SCOPE
  1. Specify the merge order and the owned-key set (start from decisions.md:203-206).
  2. Specify behaviour at a defhost crossing, where Freehand needs a THIRD rule today
     because spreads canonicalise :className into :class on the way through
     (composition.md:369-374). One rule must cover it or the bead has not landed.
  3. Witness: a controlled input whose :value and :on-input survive a hostile :&
     carrying :value, :on-input, :key and :ref — asserted through the public door.
  4. Witness: the same forwarding onto a defhost head.

ACCEPTANCE: two public concepts (spread, spread-safe) become zero — an attribute key
is not a concept in the K5 sense (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. merge-caller enforces owned literals and the :key/:ref exclusion by RAW map-key identity, but convert-props later canonicalizes strings, namespaced keywords, symbols, and kebab/camel spellings onto the same React slot. A remainder can therefore carry "key", "ref", :x/ref, or an alias such as :onInput against an owned :on-input; structural slots bypass the deny and same-slot aliases make the promised unconditional owned-wins law map-order-dependent. This is the already-established canonical-slot failure class, now on Hicasso's new :& door. Bounded repair: classify once at this merge boundary using the codec's emitted slot and prove alternate spellings cannot reach key/ref or an owned controlled/event slot. No general alias framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7332 (2026-08-01): REOPENED. PR #7332 correctly makes merge-caller, presence, ref reservation, and event callback arity total, but merge-shorthand still reads/dissocs only raw :id, :class, and :className even though this codec accepts strings, symbols, and namespaced keys and canonical-slot emits them into the same React slots. The defect is live through this bead's own :& door: [:div#tag.foo {:& {"id" "caller" "className" "bar"}}] passes both alternate keys through merge-caller, then merge-shorthand fails to see either, adds :id "tag" and :class "foo", and convert-props writes each pair to one JS slot in map iteration order. The explicit id can lose to #tag and the caller class can replace or be replaced by .foo instead of composing, contradicting merge-shorthand's explicit-wins/composes contract and convert-props's promise that forwarded class composes with tag shorthand. The same holds for symbol/namespaced aliases and direct attribute maps. Bounded repair: reuse canonical-slot while folding tag shorthand so every accepted spelling of the id/class slots has the canonical behavior; prove #tag plus alternate explicit id yields the explicit id, and .foo plus alternate class/className yields "foo bar", independent of cache/render/map order. Preserve near-miss custom props and the already-correct owned-literal deny. No general alias framework or new public concept.
close_reason:
PR #7404 — the tag shorthand is folded on the emitted slot; merge-shorthand deleted, three lanes become two.

WHAT THE AUDIT REOPENED IT FOR (merged-PR audit #7332) is closed: merge-shorthand read :id/:class/:className off the props map by RAW KEY, which is three of the spellings this codec accepts, so [:div#tag.foo {:& {"id" "caller" "className" "bar"}}] kept both ids and both classes as distinct map keys landing on one React slot each, and map iteration order decided which survived — the explicit id could lose to #tag and the caller's class could replace .foo instead of composing.

THE REPAIR is the audit's bounded one taken to its conclusion: the shorthand is folded onto the EMITTED object (fold-shorthand!), where the slot is not resolved because it already IS the slot. One undefined? test answers the id contest for every spelling; one class-names answers the class compose for every spelling. merge-shorthand and its dissoc/assoc pair are deleted from every path, and with them rf2-y1jkm's fast lane, which existed only to dodge that surgery. The class slot became a position beside the ref slot: coerced by class-names (so {"class" ["a" :b]} joins rather than reaching React as a clj->js array), and two spellings of it COMPOSE rather than the last write silently winning. No general alias framework and no new public concept — PropSlot gained one boolean field.

THE PINNING TEST WAS FLIPPED AND RENAMED IN THE SAME CHANGE, not deleted and not loosened: the-shorthand-fast-lane-emits-what-the-donor-map-produced asserted [:div.a {:x/class "b"}] emits "a"; it is now the-shorthand-composes-with-a-class-however-it-is-spelled asserting "a b", with a comment recording that the old pin matched a general path that was itself wrong. It was the ONLY test in the tree whose meaning changed — the first run after the codec change produced exactly one failure, that one.

HD-023 gains clause (c") in docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md; authoring.md gains one sentence. spec/Conventions.md deliberately NOT edited — EP-0038's sequencing law forbids spec/* before P2 graduation and this is bench-lane code; the reserved-key record for :& belongs there at graduation.

GATES (foreground, to completion, worktree-local logs, exit codes in the PR body): scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0; npm run test:cljs 12425 tests / 62067 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; npm run test:browser 1024 tests / 6335 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; compile-only checks of the two bench apps that consume the codec directly, exit 0 each. NO bench driver run and NO timing row published — the clock effect is unmeasured and is not claimed (rf2-pqyxz carries a shape note so it measures what ships).

FILED: rf2-2rtt6.70 — walk_profile_app's :shorthand-merge / :no-short arms now price a shape that ships nowhere.

GRANULARITY: VAR-LEVEL, AND NOT ONLY BY CHOICE. The bead said var-level; the
alternative was checked and it does not exist. cognitect-test-runner's
var-filter is `#((complement (apply some-fn exclude)) (meta %))` applied to each
interned test VAR — it never consults the (ns ...) form's metadata. A
namespace-level marker would have been SILENTLY INERT: the suppression would
suppress nothing while looking like it had, which is the same defect class as a
stale roster line. Var granularity is also what preserves the roster's polarity
one level down: the roster is an exclusion list so a new FILE joins by default;
the var tag means a new DEFTEST inside a tagged namespace is untagged and joins
by default too. A namespace marker would swallow it.

but the :prod-gate alias lives in implementation/core/deps.edn, and that is the
only deps file touched: `-e :requires-debug` appended to the alias's :main-opts
plus its rationale. The tag appears in no other :main-opts, so `clojure -M:test`
is unchanged, and :slow-test's `-i :slow -i :stress` carries no exclude at all
(test-exclusion is (constantly true) there), so the one ^:requires-debug

A THROW INSIDE A REACT EVENT HANDLER DOES NOT FAIL cljs.test — THE ROW READS GREEN OVER A LIVE EXCEPTION (2026-08-03, rf2-fki5d).

React does not let an exception escape dispatchEvent; it routes it to reportError. So a cljs.test deftest that dispatches a real DOM event and asserts 'nothing threw' sees 0 failures / 0 errors EVEN WHEN THE HANDLER THREW. The rf2-fki5d worker wrote exactly such a row first, and it passed while the code under test was raising InvalidStateError on every run.

WHAT CAUGHT IT: the runner's separate uncaught-pageerror gate (rf2-mwx08) failed the build FROM OUTSIDE the test. So the signal existed, but it was not attached to the assertion that claimed to cover the behaviour — the row itself was fail-open.

THE FIX, and it generalises: any row asserting 'this did not throw' inside a React event must install a window 'error' listener (and assert on it) so the row REDS BY NAME. Otherwise the only coverage of that case is a build-level gate that names no test.

DISPATCH RULE: when briefing browser/DOM work whose claim is 'no exception', require the listener explicitly and require a MUTATION PROOF — delete the fix, confirm the suite exits 1 with exactly one named failure. rf2-fki5d did this and it is what makes the row trustworthy.

RELATED CLASS (same shape, different mask): piping a gate through tail/grep returns the pipe's exit status, not the runner's. Both are fail-open instruments that report success while the thing under test is broken. Distrust any green whose failure path you have not personally mutated.

description:
SURFACED BY rf2-eane2's sibling sweep (the brief asked for other places a production path's validation story rests on a dev-only check, or on nothing).

NOT the same defect as rf2-eane2. Pattern-WebSocket makes no FALSE guarantee — it makes NO statement at all. That is the finding.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND. Across spec/Pattern-*.md, the schema-as-production-guarantee class is now clean: Pattern-Forms, Pattern-RemoteData and Construction-Prompts all carry explicit dev-tripwire qualifications, Conventions.md dropped the 'the validator IS the registration' parenthetical, and Pattern-FormAction is fixed by rf2-eane2. Pattern-WebSocket is the one with an untrusted-ingress surface and no validation story. Line 429: 'Server pushes (:ws/received events with no :request-id) are translated into named dispatched events the running-app handlers consume. The connection machine's role is mechanical — receive, validate the socket-id, translate, dispatch. The semantic interpretation lives in the per-feature event handlers.' The socket-id IS validated (framework routing concern). The PAYLOAD is handed to app handlers with no obligation stated.

WHY IT MATTERS. A websocket frame is attacker-controllable — 010 §Production builds names 'an untrusted HTTP response or websocket frame' as precisely the :rf.schema/at-boundary case, since at-boundary's check is ungated and survives the production gate. Pattern-WebSocket never mentions at-boundary, never says the receiving handler must validate, and never says a :schema on the translated event would elide. A reader who declares :schema on their :ws/message-received handler and stops has an unvalidated production ingress path, which is the exact mistake Pattern-FormAction now has a whole section warning against (§Validation is the handler's job).

THE RULE THAT SHOULD APPLY, already established twice: rf2-dtpfv/rf2-759sp — a dev-posture convenience check may be elided; a path that RECEIVES untrusted input guards itself unconditionally. The reserved :rf.server/* fx family guards its own args in all builds on exactly that reasoning, and re-frame.cofx's :rf.error/cofx-value-invalid is documented in-source as 'a PRODUCTION hard error'. Both are the framework guarding its own boundary. A websocket payload reaching an app handler is the app's boundary, so it is the Pattern's job to say so.

LIKELY SHAPE (needs a ruling — do not let a worker pick): either Pattern-WebSocket gains a short section pointing inbound-frame validation at :rf.schema/at-boundary (the designed production-ingress surface, and a status/drop is the whole answer owed for a frame — unlike a form POST, there is no page to re-render, so at-boundary fits BETTER here than it did there), or it states that the receiving handler writes the branch itself. The former looks right for exactly the reason the latter was right for FormAction.

FENCE: spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md is hot-zone; sequence it, do not parallel it with another spec/ claimant.

CITE: rf2-eane2 (the FormAction fix and its §Validation is the handler's job), rf2-dtpfv / rf2-759sp (the untrusted-input-guards-itself rule), rf2-bkvu5 (reg-app-schema is dev-only as designed).

title: subs,spine: movement-witness protocol — retire the provably-failing layer-1 memo compare (147 B/sub)
description:
HELD for operator sign-off on rf2-gncxk — do not dispatch until the ruling records adoption.

IMPLEMENT the movement-witness design produced by the rf2-gncxk design pass. This description
stands alone; the design doc is local-only.

WHAT IS BEING FIXED. `subs.memo/make-layer-1-memoised-body` guards the user's sub body with
`(= @last-db db)`. On the flush path, for `:db` / `:runtime-db`, that walk is provably useless —
147.0 B/sub, 17.6% of the ~835 B/sub per-subscription slope (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG
false, pointer compression OFF). It is NOT dead code: `deref-derived` is pull-based, so the same
guard is what stops a render re-running every sub body, and it genuinely HITS on the flush path
for `:frame-state`, which shares the wrapper.

A FOURTH CONSTRAINT THE BEAD DOES NOT STATE, and which kills "flush ⇒ skip the compare":
rf2-gncxk's proof establishes "the source moved since the source's PREVIOUS NOTIFY". The guard's
question is "did the input move since THE WRAPPER LAST RAN". Two reachable interleavings separate
them, and in BOTH the guard correctly hits on the flush path even for `:db`:
  (a) DEREF-BETWEEN. Source moves P -> N (mark-dirty). Anything derefs the sub before the epoch
      drain — `deref-derived` recomputes, so the wrapper sees N and sets last-db := N. The queued
      flush! then arrives with N: guard hits, correctly.
  (b) RETURN-TO-EQUAL. Two writes in one handler take app-db A -> B -> A' with A' `=` A but a
      fresh object. mark-dirty! dedups, so ONE flush arrives with A' against last-db = A: rf=
      moved twice, `=` says equal, guard hits, correctly.
So the fix must NOT key on "which caller am I". It must key on an exact fact about the SOURCE.

THE DESIGN — a movement WITNESS published by the source container. A derived container that gates
its own propagation on `rf=` publishes the value its most recent COMPLETED movement departed
from; the fixed-arity-1 memo wrappers hold their lone source container and skip the `=` walk
exactly when that witness is `identical?` to the value they last saw. The source owns the signal
(movement is its own notion, defined by its own rf= gate); core PULLS. No ambient state, no
dynamic var, NO change to `make-derived-value`'s pinned `(source-containers compute-fn)`
signature and NO change to compute-fn's pinned one-arg-per-source shape.

NEW CONTRACT SURFACE — one tiny .cljc ns `re-frame.movement`, sibling in spirit to
`re-frame.disposable` (the precedent: a re-frame-owned protocol reified by the spine's derived
container, consulted by core, no Reagent dep):
  (def no-witness   ;; distinct object identity; never identical?/= any real value nor ::unset
    #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js-obj)))
  (defprotocol IMovementWitness
    (-moved-from [this] "the value this container's most recent COMPLETED movement departed
                         FROM, or `no-witness`"))
Two obligations on an implementor — the whole normative content:
  (W1) FRESHNESS. Answer `no-witness` unless the container's own value has completed a movement
       AND no input change has been observed since. (Without W1 a pull-based container's live
       value can run ahead of the last movement.)
  (W2) SOUNDNESS. When it answers `f` != no-witness, reading the container at that instant yields
       `v` with (not (rf= f v)) — in particular (not (= f v)).
One on the consumer:
  (C1) VERDICT-PRESERVING. Use the witness ONLY to skip a comparison whose answer it determines;
       never change an observable outcome.
Publishing is OPTIONAL — the same posture Spec 006 already takes for `:adapter/derived-container?`
and `:adapter/activate-derived-value!`.

THE PROOF. Let S be the lone source, L = @last-db, V = @S (build-recompute-fn's arity-1 closure
is `(compute-fn @s0)`). If (identical? (-moved-from S) L) then (not (= L V)): W1+W2 give
(not (= f V)) for the returned f, and f is identical? to L. QED.

THE GUARD becomes, in `make-layer-1-memoised-body` AND
`make-layer-n-single-input-memoised-body`:
  (if (and (not (identical? (if witness-src (movement/-moved-from witness-src) movement/no-witness)
                            @last-db))
           (= @last-db db))
    <memo-hit branch, unchanged>
    <recompute branch, unchanged>)
`witness-src` is resolved ONCE at construction:
`(when (satisfies? movement/IMovementWitness source-container) source-container)` — nil wherever
the capability is absent, so the hot path is one closed-over-local truthiness test + one pointer
compare.

SUBSTRATE SIDE — `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-derived-value-fn`, six lines:
  * new cell `last-moved-from (volatile! movement/no-witness)`
  * in `notify`, INSIDE the existing `(when-not (rf= prev nu) ...)` gate, before fan-out:
    `(vreset! last-moved-from prev)`  — records departure exactly when movement is established (W2)
  * in `mark-dirty!`, inside the existing `(when-not @dirty? ...)` 0->1 branch:
    `(vreset! last-moved-from movement/no-witness)` — the container may now run ahead of its last
    notify, so it stops answering (W1). `flush!` clears `dirty?` BEFORE it recomputes+notifies, so
    the witness re-arms in the right order with no extra bookkeeping.
  * the reify gains `movement/IMovementWitness (-moved-from [_] @last-moved-from)`
  * `-dispose` resets it to `no-witness` (hygiene + releases the retained reference)
`build-recompute-fn`, the scheduler, the fan-out coordinator, `deref-derived`, `flush!`'s
structure, the failure-atomic wiring loop and `-dispose`'s release discipline are UNTOUCHED.

WHY IT CANNOT WEAKEN THE DEREF-PATH GUARD (structurally, not by care). The design never asks "am
I on the flush path?". After any wrapper invocation last-db holds the value just seen while the
witness holds the PREDECESSOR, so the proof cannot fire twice in a row on the same value: a
render that derefs 300 subs three times each still memo-hits 900 times, with `=` short-circuiting
on identical?. The only deref that gets the proof is the first invocation after a movement —
where the guard would have missed anyway. `compute-sub` bypasses the wrapper entirely.
THE SET OF {hit, miss} VERDICTS IS BIT-IDENTICAL ON EVERY PATH ON EVERY ADAPTER. Body-run counts,
`:rf.sub/run` counts, `:rf.sub/skip` counts and its `:reason :input-value-equal` do not move. A
trace-count diff is the failure signal, not a thing to re-baseline.

HOW `:frame-state` KEEPS ITS GENUINE HIT — three layers:
  (a) STRUCTURAL. `subs/single-source-container-for` maps `:frame-state -> frame/frame-state-container`,
      the ONE physical container — a `cljs.core/Atom` under the spine (`source-atom?` is
      `(instance? Atom s)`), an `r/atom` under Reagent. An Atom does not implement
      IMovementWitness, so witness-src is nil and the guard expression is byte-for-byte today's.
      The exact fact that broke rf2-gncxk's proof is now the mechanism that protects it.
  (b) CONTRACTUAL. A future gated frame-state could publish a witness only by honouring W1+W2 —
      which require precisely the rf= movement gate whose absence makes the `:frame-state` hit
      possible today. The design cannot become wrong, only inapplicable or applicable.
  (c) EMPIRICAL. PR #7233's `sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs` `:frame-state` arm must pass
      UNMODIFIED, plus a new mutation proof: forcing witness-src non-nil for `:frame-state` must
      RED that pin.

WHAT CHANGES — and nothing else:
  * NEW implementation/core/src/re_frame/movement.cljc  (~35 lines, mostly docstring)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs  (~8 lines, above)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc  (~12 lines + docstrings; the two fixed-arity-1
    wrappers each take the lone source-container as a new TRAILING param)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc  (2 lines: pass `(first inputs)` at :1263 and :1283)
  * implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs  (the paired arms below;
    :1101 is the one bench site constructing a wrapper directly)
  * spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md — a "Movement witness (optional)" subsection under
    §`make-derived-value` stating W1/W2/C1 + one cross-ref sentence in §Invalidation algorithm.
    HOT-ZONE — sequence against other Spec 006 PRs.
NO adapter file changes. `make-layer-n-memoised-body` (varargs, >=2 inputs, all parametric subs)
is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE — the mechanism generalises per-source-index but its cost is
dominated by the varargs seq and the measured 147 B is the fixed-arity-1 path. Spec 009 needs NO
change: `:rf.sub/skip`'s "input value was `=` to last-seen" stays exactly true, because the design
never skips when the values are `=`. Pre-alpha posture: positional param, NO compatibility arity.

DEGRADATION — none behavioural anywhere; two extra pointer compares per recompute where the
capability is absent, zero allocation.
  * Reagent / reagent-slim: make-derived-value is `(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn ...))`
    (spine.cljs:3127); a Reagent Reaction does not implement the protocol -> witness-src nil.
  * plain-atom (JVM+CLJS): recompute-on-deref, no notify gate, no witness; on the JVM witness-src
    is a constant nil local. `sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj` (incl. the =-not-identical? pin at :84)
    runs here and is unaffected.
  * test-react: own make-derived-value, publishes nothing, unchanged.
  * UIx / re-frame.ui / freehand: all ride make-derived-value-fn -> all three get the win on
    `:db` / `:runtime-db` / single-`:<-` layer-2 and no change on `:frame-state`.
  * Bundle: one sentinel + one defprotocol; a protocol call on a reify is a direct method dispatch
    under :advanced. Show the delta against the perf-bundle gate.
  * MEMORY — the one real cost, state it in the PR: `last-moved-from` retains ONE predecessor
    derived value per derived container while that container is clean (cleared on the next
    mark-dirty!). For the app-db projection that is one extra app-db generation held between
    writes; structural sharing means the true delta is only the nodes the last write replaced. Not
    a new class of retention — every layer-1 memo cell already holds a full app-db in `last-db`.

MEASUREMENT OBLIGATION (ranges quoted; overlapping ranges mean INDISTINGUISHABLE; arm-order guard
must not refuse; forward AND reversed reported):
  1. BASELINE. Reproduce or cite P-EQDB = 147.0 B/sub on the unchanged tree (node V8, :advanced,
     goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF, 8/8 self-tests, 70/70 strata).
  2. THE PAIRED ARMS — both, or neither. Added to write_attribution.cljs, living in ONE process on
     the SAME objects (the harness's own RC-ATTACH/RC-CAND paired-control discipline):
       P-MEMOW — the SHIPPED wrapper constructed with a WITNESSING source (a spine derived
                 container), invoked in the flush-path shape (witness identical? to last-db, db
                 changed). MUST land at P-MEMO minus 147.0 B/sub within the quoted range: the `=`
                 term is GONE.
       P-MEMOF — the SAME wrapper constructed with a RAW ATOM source (the `:frame-state` shape),
                 invoked with an =-but-not-identical? db. MUST still carry the FULL `=` term,
                 indistinguishable from today's P-MEMO at that input. This is the "still paid
                 where it earns its keep" half and it is NOT optional.
  3. THE LADDER. RFWRITE-N per-subscription slope falls by ~147 B/sub (~835 -> ~688, -17.6%) on
     the `:db` ladder, and is UNCHANGED on a `:frame-state` ladder (add one if absent).
  4. BEHAVIOURAL WITNESSES, UNMODIFIED (this discharges C1): sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs
     (both arms, PR #7233), sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj (incl. :84), and full test:cljs / test:ui /
     adapter smokes with ZERO change in any body-run or :rf.sub/run / :rf.sub/skip count.
  5. MUTATION PROOFS, BOTH DIRECTIONS. (i) forcing witness-src non-nil for `:frame-state` must RED
     the `:frame-state` pin; (ii) deleting the identical? proof term must RESTORE the 147 B in
     P-MEMOW. A change that cannot fail either way has not been measured.
  6. RETENTION. hicasso retention_run.cjs shows no growth beyond the one predecessor generation.

INTERACTIONS. rf2-2rtt6.13 (PR #7304) and rf2-2rtt6.25 (PR #7305) both LANDED and both COMPOSE —
no sequencing dependency. Both edited spine.cljs's make-react-spine / hook region; this edits
spine.cljs's make-derived-value-fn region — no textual overlap, but spine.cljs is contended by
Wave-1 workers, so treat it as sequence-sensitive when dispatching. One POSITIVE interaction with
.25 worth noting in the PR: commit adoption means the memo cells (last-db / last-result) survive
render -> commit instead of being thrown away with a discarded double build, so the proof's
precondition (last-db identical? to the witness) holds MORE often after .25, not less.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (do not re-litigate): (1) narrowing the guard to identical? — the
`:frame-state` value-equal commit AND a single-epoch A->B->A' return-to-equal both legitimately
memo-hit on an =-not-identical? input, so it turns a spec'd :rf.sub/skip into a :rf.sub/run and
reds both #7233 pins plus sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj:84; (2) an extra "moved" argument to
compute-fn — make-layer-n-memoised-body is `(fn [& in-vals])` and cannot tell a trailing flag
from an input value, and Spec 006 pins the one-arg-per-source shape verbatim; (3) an ambient
one-shot cell set by flush! — correctness would depend on nothing else running between set and
consume (the app-db projection's own compute-fn is the keyword `:rf.db/app`; a throw strands the
flag), and it answers the wrong question anyway (cases (a)/(b) above); (4) a movement COUNTER
instead of the departure value — cannot distinguish "moved once since you last ran" from "moved
once and you already read the result", and cannot see return-to-equal at all.

ADJACENT CANDIDATES, NOT THIS BEAD (file separately if the operator wants them): memoise
deref-derived while the container is clean (bigger win, but converts the derived container from
pull to cached-pull, which Spec 006 leaves to adapter discretion and the spine declines);
movement-gate the raw-atom fan-out coordinator (would collapse N `:frame-state` `=` walks into 1
but changes when `:frame-state` subs are marked dirty and would red the #7233 pin as written);
extend the witness to the varargs / >=2-source wrappers.

WHY A MAYOR HITS THIS: an automated merged-PR-audit process commits .beads rows to GIT directly, while the mayor's checkpoint exports DOLT. Those are two writers to one file. 'N rows, HEAD had N' in the checkpoint output is the DANGEROUS case, not the reassuring one — I saw it repeatedly in one session.

WHAT I VERIFIED (2026-08-03, 14 consecutive checkpoints): NO bead was dropped — 1951 stable rf2-* ids intact across every commit. So the coarse half of the hazard did not fire.
BUT THE AUDIT METHOD MATTERS: compare on the STABLE bead id ('"id":"rf2-..."'), NOT on the row UUID. Row UUIDs are REGENERATED on re-import, so a UUID diff shows phantom 'losses' — it flagged 3 for me and all three beads existed and were closed. A UUID-keyed audit will cry wolf every time.
AND IT ONLY PROVES PRESENCE, NOT FIELD STATE. rf2-rjqtj's real fault is field-level reversion at equal count, which an id-set comparison cannot see. Separately confirmed live the same day: an interrupted Dolt GC reverted a close and 5 note-appends while ids stayed intact.

THE CHECK THAT ACTUALLY COVERS IT: before overwriting, diff HEAD's issue ids AND updated_at AND status against the fresh Dolt export; import newer/missing Git rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse naming the exact ids/fields. Keep the count floor, but never treat equal counts as equality.

title: Worktree hygiene must rmdir a node_modules junction before git worktree remove (second occurrence)
description:
SECOND recorded instance of the class. On 2026-07-31 the worker worktree for rf2-2rtt6.8 (PR #7311, merged green) carried a Windows junction implementation/node_modules -> the mayor checkout's real node_modules, which is the established convention in this repo (a live sibling worktree had the identical junction, and a worker worktree cannot compile without one). Post-merge hygiene ran git worktree remove; it followed the junction and emptied the MAYOR checkout's real implementation/node_modules to 0 entries, breaking every local build in the repo until npm ci restored it (exit 0, back to the canary 101 entries). No source was lost - the PR had already merged.

REMEDY, both halves needed:
1. HYGIENE: before git worktree remove, run cmd /c rmdir <wt>/implementation/node_modules (junctions must be removed with rmdir, not rm -rf), then verify the mayor canary after each removal batch: ls <mayor>/implementation/node_modules | wc -l should stay ~101. Encode this in the hygiene skill/script rather than in an agent's memory, since memory already carried the warning and the class still recurred.
2. WORKER BRIEF: a worker that creates the junction should rmdir it as its last act before reporting done, so hygiene never meets one.

Consider also having scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh (or a companion) provision node_modules in a way that cannot alias the mayor's - e.g. npm ci in the worktree, or a marker file recording that a junction exists so hygiene can find it mechanically.

title: workers: backgrounded-spine completion notifications silently never fire — four stale-waiter incidents in one day
description:
PATTERN, now systemic (2026-08-02, four incidents): a worker backgrounds a long gate (fast-PR spine, typically) and ends its turn waiting on the completion notification. THE NOTIFICATION NEVER FIRES. The worker sits stale — sometimes through multiple idle ticks reporting 'standing by' — until the mayor notices the branch unmoved and sends a status check, which resumes it. Every resume has recovered cleanly because the work itself was committed; the only loss is hours of latency per incident.

INCIDENTS: burst-2rtt6-55 twice (once compounded by a wrapper-shadowed exit code), ime-o27h3 once, and the same shape underlies the walkopt/hosthatch 'placeholder expired' ticks. Distinct from the API-outage kills (those report failed status); this class reports nothing at all.

WHAT ALREADY MITIGATES IT: the standing brief line 'gates foreground only, to completion' — workers who foreground the spine never hit this. The incidents are workers who backgrounded it anyway, usually to keep working while it runs.

THE WORK, in preference order:
  1. Establish WHY the completion notification is lost for backgrounded shells on this box (harness-level: does the notification fire and get dropped, or never fire?). Evidence: the burst worker found one case where the notification DID fire but the exit code captured was the wrapper's — so there may be two defects wearing one symptom.
  2. If root cause is out of reach, harden the convention: briefs already say foreground-only; make the worker-side rule 'if you background a gate anyway, poll its log on a timer rather than waiting for a notification' — and put that in the dispatch template where the gates-foreground rule lives.
  3. Consider whether the mayor's status-check-on-unmoved-branch heuristic (which caught all four) should be a standing automation rather than judgement.

Cross-platform rule applies to any tooling. This is process/harness work — do not dispatch while it would displace implementation; it costs latency, not correctness.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and I am not claiming it: whether the completion notification fires and is dropped, or never fires, is internal to the agent harness. Nothing in this repository observes or controls that delivery path, so no repo-side change can distinguish the two — this needs harness-level instrumentation, not a script here. RULED OUT as a repo-side cause: the bead's 'two defects wearing one symptom' hint is right, and the second defect IS in-repo — the burst worker's 'notification fired but the exit code captured was the wrapper's' is a pipeline-exit-status defect, NOT a notification defect, and it is now closed by the no-pipe rule above. I did not attempt a deliberate reproduction by backgrounding a long gate: the cost is an unbounded wait for a signal that by definition may never arrive. Item 3 (making the mayor's status-check-on-unmoved-branch a standing automation) is a mayor-loop decision, not a worker's.

title: Beads checkpoint silently overwrites newer Git-only rows when Git and Dolt diverge at equal row count
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7394 / ledger durability. Before advancing the cursor, the merged main ledger at 43dcd2440a22a42e77d6ab773fb8df2a43a6a5a6 and the Dolt remote each contained 1,938 issues but different facts. Git alone carried rf2-3jw04, rf2-jv36i, rf2-lhdp0 and newer closes/statuses for rf2-2rtt6.52/.63; Dolt carried three newer audit issues. scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1 exported Dolt wholesale; its row-count floor passed (1,938 == 1,938), and commit 667c744dc875e31e4d4874586afcbec2d01ceb8a silently removed the three Git-only issues and reverted .52/.63. This is the remaining equal-count/set-substitution sibling of rf2-51uz1's time-travel fault.

Recovery proved the bounded mechanism: timestamp-aware bd import of only Git issue rows into Dolt created the three missing IDs, updated exactly the two newer Git rows, skipped stale rows, preserved every newer Dolt row/cursor, and yielded a verified 1,941-ID union with zero field mismatches.

DO: before checkpoint overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl, compare HEAD's issue IDs/updated_at/status to the fresh Dolt export. Either import newer/missing Git issue rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse with exact IDs/fields. Keep the existing row-count floor, but do not treat equal counts as equality. Add a regression where HEAD and Dolt have equal row counts but disjoint one-for-one substitutions plus one newer state on each side; neither fact may be lost. No generalized sync service needed.
close_reason: Closed via PR #7410. beads-checkpoint.sh + .ps1 now compare the fresh Dolt export to HEAD on the stable bead id, updated_at and status BEFORE overwriting .beads/issues.jsonl; the row-count floor is kept and runs first, but equal counts no longer imply equality. Three divergence classes, all 'Git knows something Dolt does not': GONE (issue id at HEAD with no row in the export - would be deleted), REVERT (id in both, HEAD's updated_at strictly newer - would be reverted), AMBIG (id in both, same updated_at, different status - neither side is newer). Forward motion (export-only ids, export-newer rows) is deliberately not reported, so ordinary checkpoints are unaffected. CHOSE REFUSE over auto-import: the script's own stated contract is that it does not import, and writing to the database from the one script that exists to be careful is not provably safe. To keep the refusal actionable it writes the GONE and REVERT rows verbatim to a temp file the message names, so the bead's own verified recovery is a single timestamp-safe 'bd import' then re-checkpoint; AMBIG rows are excluded because an import cannot adjudicate a tie. The message also names the escape for a deliberate bd delete/gc. No sync service. Regression on BOTH platforms from the bead's own fixture (equal row counts, disjoint one-for-one substitution, one newer state on each side): POSIX test-pre-commit.sh layer 8 cases 8j/8k/8l (72 passed / 0 failed; 3 of the 4 new assertions FAIL against origin/main); PowerShell a new -SelfTest switch, 28 assertions, green under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7.6.4 - the .ps1 had no test surface at all before and layer 8 is POSIX sh and cannot run it. 8k/T2 prove the recovery completes with neither side's facts lost. Also verified read-only against the REAL 2741-row tracker: the parser extracts exactly the 1951 ground-truth stable ids with zero comment-UUID leakage, identity comparison is silent, and a synthetic equal-count 2741-vs-2741 divergence catches all three planted losses. Both implementations produce byte-identical findings on identical input. Never run against the live database.

title: hicasso: a first registration inside the render->commit gap is pinned, not repaired
description:
FOUND while closing rf2-2rtt6.44's audit remainder (PR: worker/firstreg-2rtt6-44). Filed rather than left implied, and PINNED by an assertion rather than argued.

rf2-2rtt6.44 closed the MOUNTED case: a boundary that already holds a cell for a query registered for the first time now reaches the new computation and is notified by later writes, off registrar/add-registration-hook! funnelled into invalidate-cell!.

THE NEIGHBOURING CASE IS NOT CLOSED, and cannot be by the same route. A first registration landing in the RENDER->COMMIT GAP -- the body has returned nil, the registration lands, and only then does React run the effect that acquires the edge -- reaches NO CELL, because the boundary does not have one yet. first-registration! scans @!cells and finds nothing to invalidate. The epoch sum cannot report it either: a key with no cell contributes its frame's commit-basis, and a reg-sub moves neither term of it (that is exactly what generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test row 3 pins for a re-registration). So React's post-subscribe getSnapshot re-check reads the number the fiber captured at render, sees no tear, and schedules nothing.

MEASURED, and asserted as a deliberately-* row in arm1/first_registration_cljs_test:
  - the snapshot does not move across the commit;
  - the boundary is not notified (0);
  - BUT the cell the commit acquired holds the REAL handler (derefs 1, not nil).

So the cost is a DELAYED PAINT, not a retired computation: the boundary is correct from its next render onwards, and the next write to the frame notifies it. That asymmetry is why this is a P3 record and not a defect fix.

WHAT CLOSING IT WOULD COST, so the decision is costed rather than open:
  (a) the registry term in every key's contribution to getSnapshot -- the option rf2-2rtt6.44 costed and DECLINED (up to 15 whole-tree concurrent-render invalidations per HMR save, for zero correction in the mounted case). It WOULD correct this one, because here the extra render reads back through a cell that is alive and correct. That is a genuine argument the earlier costing did not have to answer, and it is the reason this bead exists.
  (b) recording what a read returned, so the commit can compare -- a fence Arm 1 exists to hold ("no commit-phase deref"; getSnapshot "holds no record of what any read returned").

Neither is obviously right, so this wants a ruling, not a worker.

REACHABILITY, honestly: needs a first-time reg-sub to land strictly inside one boundary's render->commit gap. That is a lazily-loaded module or a boot-order race, not steady state; and any subsequent write to the frame clears it.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #7411 (worker/rcgap-2rtt6-50).

RULED AS A FIX, NOT A RULING, AND THE BEAD'S OWN COSTING IS WHY. The bead
enumerated two closures and rejected both, then asked for a ruling. Option (b)
(recording what a read returned) is genuinely closed at Arm 1's fences and stays

A TWO-VALUED PROBE CONFLATES 'REJECTED' WITH 'CRASHED', SO TWO VALIDATORS THAT BOTH EXPLODE AGREE (rf2-dhl4d, 2026-08-03).

THE MECHANISM, and it is the best fail-open diagnosis this project has produced. A viz<->engine parity ratchet compared two validators by asking each "do you accept this definition?" — a BOOLEAN. On CLJS, engine-accepts? wrapped the call in (catch :default ... false). So when the engine raised a host ClassCastException on a non-Named key, the probe recorded FALSE — indistinguishable from a clean, documented rejection. The viz side crashed the same way. TWO VALIDATORS THAT BOTH EXPLODE AGREE, and the ratchet stayed green over a live crash in a security gate.

THE FIX IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE CASE: make the probe THREE-VALUED — :accept / :reject / :host-throw — plus a definition-validation-is-total assertion. Proof it now sees the divergence: (engine :reject, viz :host-throw).

GENERALISE IT. Any comparison harness that reduces its subjects to a boolean, or that catches broadly and maps the catch onto one of the two legitimate outcomes, is fail-open BY CONSTRUCTION — parity ratchets, differential tests, golden-file comparators, A/B benchmark agreement checks. Ask of every such harness: WHAT DOES IT RECORD WHEN THE SUBJECT CRASHES? If the answer is "the same thing as one of the normal outcomes", it cannot see the failure class it exists to catch.

ALSO FROM THE SAME BEAD, a distinct defect class worth naming separately: THE ERROR PATH ITSELF THREW. A (pr-str offending) in the diagnostic message reached an arbitrary object's toString, so a throwing-toString key DESTROYED THE FAILURE BEING DESCRIBED. A validator that rejects correctly but explodes while explaining why is still broken on hostile input. Exercise the diagnostic path with the same forged corpus as the validation path.

AND: the bead named ONE defect site; there were TWO (an inline copy elsewhere in the same file). A worker fixing only the cited line would have shipped a half-fix that passed its own new test. Grep for the PATTERN, not the line number.

MECHANICAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER WRITES THE NEXT MEMORY: do not pass prose containing backticks to bd through a shell double-quoted string — bash runs the backticked spans as command substitution and silently mangles the text. Write the body to a file and pass it with "$(cat file)", or avoid backticks entirely. I did exactly this while recording this memory, and a worker hit the same trap earlier the same day leaving a stray file in the mayor checkout.

title: docs(hicasso): the studio/design tree is excluded from mkdocs --strict, so every 'gate' run against it this session was decorative
description:
FOUND by the rf2-6i0i2 worker (PR #7312) while correcting its own earlier gate claim. VERIFIED by the mayor: mkdocs.yml:32-36 has an exclude_docs block listing 'design/freehand/' and 'design/hicasso/'. So 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT VALIDATE anything under docs/design/hicasso/ — it only proves the rest of the site builds.

WHY IT MATTERS. Across this session many Hicasso docs PRs cited mkdocs --strict as THE gate for edits confined to docs/design/hicasso/studio/**, validation.md, architecture.md and the draft guide. Those edits were effectively UNGATED: a broken internal anchor, a malformed table, or a dead cross-reference in the studio tree would not have been caught by the gate that was run and reported green. This is precisely the class this programme keeps hunting -- a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything -- except here it is our own docs gate, not a bench instrument.

NOT AN EMERGENCY: the excluded content is prose and tables, and at least one worker (PR #7312) checked its page by hand (15 internal anchors resolved, no inconsistent column counts) once it discovered the exclusion. Nothing is known to be broken. The defect is the missing check, not a known break.

THE EXCLUSION MAY BE DELIBERATE -- mkdocs.yml:27 says the Freehand design record is excluded as a durable record, and hicasso sits beside it. So the first question is a DECISION, not a fix: should docs/design/hicasso/ be published/validated by mkdocs at all? Options: (a) keep it excluded from the SITE but add a cheap standalone link/anchor/table checker over the tree, run in CI, so the pages are validated without being published; (b) include the tree in the site and let --strict cover it, accepting whatever nav and build cost that adds; (c) accept it as deliberately unvalidated and STOP citing mkdocs --strict as a gate for edits confined to it -- which then requires every future Hicasso docs brief to say plainly that no gate covers the change.

RECOMMENDATION (mayor): (a). The tree is a working design record, not user-facing documentation, so publishing it is wrong; but its internal anchors and cross-page references are load-bearing for the programme's own readers and are exactly what rots silently. A standalone checker is small and can go red.

Whatever is chosen, the second half is mandatory: dispatch briefs must stop nominating a gate that does not cover the surface being edited.
notes:
OPERATOR CORRECTION (Mike, 2026-07-31): 'design/freehand/ etc are not mkdocs published.' The exclusion is DELIBERATE — these trees are working design records, not user-facing documentation. OPTION (b) IS STRUCK: publishing docs/design/hicasso/ so that --strict covers it was never a real option and is not on the table.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION REVISED, and revised DOWNWARD. I previously recommended (a), a standalone anchor/link/table checker in CI. On reflection that is over-engineering for the failure it prevents: the tree is prose and tables read by this programme's own agents, the failure mode is a link that does not jump, and a bespoke CI job to police an internal design record is exactly the kind of machinery this project's stance rejects.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION — (c), plus one cheap check IF and ONLY IF it is nearly free:
1. THE MANDATORY HALF, which costs nothing and is the actual defect: dispatch briefs must STOP nominating 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' as the gate for edits confined to docs/design/hicasso/** or docs/design/freehand/**. It does not cover them. A brief that names a gate not covering its surface is the same fail-open class this programme hunts in its instruments, and the honest form is 'no automated gate covers this surface; the worker verifies anchors by hand and says so' — which is precisely what the rf2-6i0i2 worker (PR #7312) did once it discovered the exclusion: 15 internal anchors resolved, no inconsistent column counts, stated in the PR body.
2. THE CHEAP HALF, only if genuinely cheap: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and scripts/check_readme_links.py already exist and already walk tracked markdown with their own exclude sets (check_doc_slugs.py has EXCLUDE_DIR_REL = {docs/spec, docs/migration}). If either can be pointed at docs/design/** by adding it to an existing roster — a one-line change, no new job, no new script — do that. If it needs a new script, a new CI job, or non-trivial rework, DO NOT DO IT; item 1 alone discharges this bead.

Nothing is known to be broken in the tree today.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7318 (cursor-gap repair, 2026-08-03): REOPENED this exact owner; no duplicate. The M1 prose reconciliation is sound and later #7335 updated every affected site to the corrected five-run 1.0150x interval. The docs-gate guidance remains incomplete across active agent surfaces: PR #7318 added the exclusion warning to CLAUDE.md and the dispatch template, but AGENTS.md is the instruction file Codex workers in this repository are explicitly given and it contains no mkdocs/docs-design scope warning. Add one short cross-agent instruction or pointer stating that mkdocs --strict excludes docs/design/**, check_doc_slugs.py covers links/anchors, and tables/rendering/nav need direct verification. Do not duplicate the long CLAUDE paragraph, add a checker, or publish the design tree.

BRIEF FROM WHAT IS TRUE ON MAIN, NOT FROM THE BEAD'S DESCRIPTION (2026-08-03, five occurrences in one session).

THE PATTERN. A bead's DESCRIPTION records the state when it was FILED. Its bulk then ships, a merged-PR audit REOPENS it for a narrow remainder, and the description is never rewritten — the remainder lives in a NOTE further down. A mayor who briefs from the description sends a worker to redo landed work.

IT HAPPENED FIVE TIMES IN ONE SESSION: rf2-2rtt6.51 (built; only audit #7372's dispatchEvent receipts outstanding), rf2-2rtt6.41 (PR #7338 had merged; the notes still said NOT MERGED), rf2-3jw04 + rf2-n4mad (both swept by PRs #7394/#7398; four of five named pages already correct), rf2-x5dvk (half already satisfied), rf2-5dut1 (packaging half landed in #7349). In every case the WORKER caught it, because the brief told it the bead outranks the brief.

THE CHEAP FIX, and it is cheap: before writing a brief, run bd show and read the NOTES to the end — not just the description. Then grep main for the bead id: git log --oneline -400 origin/main | grep -i <id>. Bead ids appear in commit subjects here. Two minutes of mayor time saves a worker rediscovering it over twenty.

THE INSTRUCTION THAT SAVED IT EVERY TIME, so keep it verbatim in every brief: 'THE BEAD IS AUTHORITATIVE OVER THIS BRIEF, INCLUDING ABOUT WHICH FILES ARE INVOLVED. If what you find contradicts anything below, follow the bead and say so in your report.' Workers used it correctly in all five cases and reported the divergence rather than silently doing the wrong thing.

A RELATED TRAP FROM THE SAME DAY: an audit comment's timestamp is UTC while git log here prints +1000, so 'the audit predates the fix' is easy to get backwards. Compare in one timezone before concluding an obligation is discharged.

AND THE CONVERSE, which is NOT a failure: a bead marked 'this wants a ruling, not a worker' can still be legitimately overridden when the worker shows the RULING'S PREMISE WAS FALSE — rf2-2rtt6.50's costing had been made against the wrong shape, so once corrected there was no choice left to make. Surface such an override to the operator rather than merging it quietly, but do not treat it as insubordination.

title: hicasso: HD-019 says flushSync is never the default, and the controlled converge makes it the default
description:
DECISIONS-RECORD AMENDMENT, raised by rf2-fki5d (PR #7371) and deliberately not
made by the worker.

HD-019 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md) rules that on the lean-React arm
`flushSync` is "the evidence-gated last resort, NEVER THE DEFAULT". The
controlled converge shipped by rf2-fki5d calls `flushSync` once per keystroke on
every controlled element — so it IS now the default there.

The evidence gate is met and is recorded: removing only the `flushSync` from
`front.controlled/converge!` reds 4 assertions, all caret readings at [5 5],
INCLUDING the ordinary accepted keystroke — without it the per-instance record is
one render stale, the converge writes the wrong value, and React's own restore
repairs the value and throws the caret away. So the mechanism is not reaching for
`flushSync` to make the echo land (the echo already lands without it); it is
reaching for it to make the RECORD current before the caret is restored.

What is needed is one of:
  (a) amend HD-019's clause to name the controlled converge as the evidence-gated
      case, or
  (b) rule that the converge must find another way to make the record current.

Mike's call. Nothing is blocked on it — the code and the studio page both state
the tension plainly
(docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md, "One thing
for the decisions record").
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review): Option (a) — amend HD-019. The shipped converge stands; no redesign.

DECISION. HD-019's flushSync clause is amended to name the lean-React controlled-TEXT converge as the single evidence-gated exception, in the Codex review's narrower formulation (adopted over the dossier's broader "controlled elements" wording). Amended clause text:

"flushSync is never the general default. The lean-React controlled-text converge is the single evidence-gated exception: it may flush the synchronous door's pending commit before React's controlled restore so value and caret are correct when the discrete event returns."

MECHANISM (why the flush is the measured requirement, not a convenience):
- Record currency, not the echo. The echo lands without the flush (dispatch and store notification are already synchronous). The flush exists so the per-instance last-rendered record is current BEFORE React's end-of-discrete-event controlled restore runs.
- Evidence: removing only the flushSync from front.controlled/converge! reds 4 assertions, all caret readings at [5 5], INCLUDING the ordinary accepted keystroke — without it the record is one render stale, the converge writes the wrong value, and React's own restore repairs the value but throws the caret away. With it: browser lane green at 940 tests / 5,895 assertions; direct probes green in Chromium and WebKit (Codex).
- Ordering ground truth (Codex, verified against pinned React DOM 19.2.0): the outer discrete-event wrapper flushes pending sync work only in its `finally`, immediately before controlled-state restore (batchedUpdates$1); the converge runs earlier, inside the handler, so without its own flush it reads the previous commit's record. React's updateInput/updateTextarea mirror controlled commits into defaultValue, which is what makes the node-held record valid for the guarded cases.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (the fence's purpose — no reflexive flushSync — survives):
- Exactly one audited call site: react-dom/flushSync in front.controlled/converge! title: MEASURE: thread the frame as a codec-supplied prop and delete the per-boundary frame-context hook
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

A HYPOTHESIS TO MEASURE, not a proposal to adopt. It frees one of the two hook slots
the whole Arm 1 shell is budgeted at.

WHERE THE BUDGET GOES TODAY. HD-020(b) (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:404-407) and
the budget table (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:36) spend the <=2 hooks per
product boundary on "the subscription/epoch hook and the frame-context hook", and
"a third hook in the shell is a budget breach". The Arm 1 lean-React runtime pays the
second as useContext(frame-context) and then memoises the frame-locked op bundle per
frame so the per-render cost is one map lookup
(re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs, on the arm branch — see the frame-ops
docstring, "HD-020(a) has each boundary read the frame ONCE from the substrate's
single internal context; it does not ask each boundary to rebuild the bundle").

THE HYPOTHESIS. The frame does not need a hook at all, because it is ordinary data
that flows down the tree. When the codec turns [child-view props] into a React
element it can bake the frame into the element's props. The root's element carries it;
every descendant element is CREATED by an ancestor body that already knows it. A
foreign component in between is harmless: children elements were built with the prop
already in them, so passing props.children through preserves it. The only creator that
would lack it is an outward React bridge, which takes an explicit frame anyway.

IF IT HOLDS: one hook per boundary disappears. The P0 record prices an isolated
useSyncExternalStore rung at ~516 B (docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:66-69), which is
of the same order as the whole 0.4-0.5 KB boundary-shell target
(validation.md:37) — so this is a shell-budget-relevant quantity, not a rounding
error. It also frees the second slot for anything v0 later needs, which today it
cannot have.

WHAT IT COSTS. One extra entry in every boundary element's props map, on every render.
That is an allocation and a retention cost on the OTHER side of the ledger, and it is
exactly why this is a measurement rather than a ruling.

MULTI-FRAME CORRECTNESS IS THE HARD PART, NOT THE HEAP. Use case 16 is multi-frame
isolation (charter.md:190-191). Context gets frame isolation for free by construction;
prop-threading must PROVE it. A witness that mounts one app in two isolated frames and
asserts no read crosses is mandatory before any number is quotable.

SCOPE
  1. Build the prop-threaded variant against the SAME witnesses the context variant
     uses. Both variants on one branch, one instrument, one run.
  2. Count hooks at React's own dispatcher, the way the arm's existing hook-ledger DOM
     test does — never self-reported.
  3. Price retained heap per boundary on the 1/3/7/20 ladder, and the clock on mount +
     bulk. Browser numbers only, :advanced, per HD-012 (decisions.md:256-258); JVM/Node
     figures are diagnostic and are never quotable against the bar.
  4. Multi-frame isolation witness (above). A red here kills the hypothesis outright
     regardless of the heap result.
  5. Publish to docs/design/hicasso/studio/ and append to the standard bead rf2-2rtt6.1
     with the producing commit SHA and the repro command.

MEASUREMENT POSTURE: do NOT contend for the box with the instrument workers — build
and self-witness first, take the comparative rows when the lane is free.
close_reason: Correctness half done; measurement half split to rf2-2rtt6.72. Scope items 1, 2 and 4 are green: the prop-threaded variant is built BESIDE the incumbent (bead: 'both variants on one branch'), hooks counted at React's own dispatcher — context shell 2 (useContext + useSyncExternalStore), frame-prop shell 1 (useSyncExternalStore), and the count does not move with the read count on 1/7/20 — and MULTI-FRAME ISOLATION HOLDS, driven through both variants identically, plus a foreign component in the middle preserving the frame through props.children. Items 3 and 5 (retained-heap ladder, mount/bulk clock, studio row, rf2-2rtt6.1 append) need a quiet box and are rf2-2rtt6.72's. ONE DEFECT THE VARIANT CREATES was found and repaired in the same commit: React propagates a context change ahead of the memo comparator, so the incumbent cannot be bailed out of a frame change but a frame-fed boundary can; boundary-props= now compares rfFrame. Mutation-proved (remove the comparison -> exactly one named failure, exit 1). HONEST NOTE: simpler at the shell, slightly MORE machinery in total (codec/root-element for the one creator with no ancestor body, plus the comparator learning a channel it did not have to know existed). PR #7416.
