title: spec/Pattern-FormAction builds a PRODUCTION SSR form-POST validation path on a dev-only check
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-bkvu5's doc pass. spec/ pattern documents were outside that bead's fence (hot-zone, and the ruling authorised only the Spec 010 statement plus the EP-0025 qualification), so they are filed here rather than fixed.

THE SHARPEST SITE. spec/Pattern-FormAction.md describes the SSR progressive-enhancement form-POST path — a PRODUCTION server request path — and rests its validation story on app-db / event schema validation, which is elided from production builds (rf2-bkvu5 ruling, Spec 010 §Production builds).

  - spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:122 — 'If form-params fails the AddToCartForm schema, the framework structured-error trace fires (:rf.error/schema-validation-failure); the error projector maps it to a 400 response with the public-error shape. THE APP DOES NOT WRITE A SEPARATE VALIDATION BRANCH.' That last sentence is the load-bearing wrong advice: in a production server build the trace never fires, so the 400 never happens and the malformed form-params flow onward.
  - spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:21 step 4 — 'The domain event handler validates the form-params against the registered schema for the form. On schema failure, the handler writes structured errors into the form slice :errors map; the standard SSR render reads the slice and emits the form again with errors.' Same production path, same gap.

WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS (needs a ruling, do not let a worker pick): either the pattern routes its form-params check through :rf.schema/at-boundary (which SURVIVES the gate and is the designed production ingress surface), or the pattern states plainly that a server deployment must write the validation branch in the handler. The former is more likely right — a form POST is untrusted ingress, which is exactly at-boundary's job — but it changes the pattern's normative shape and Pattern-FormAction is hot-zone.

LOWER-PRIORITY SIBLINGS in the same class (schema-as-guarantee with no dev-only note), same sweep:
  - spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md:277 — 'Slice is reg-app-schema-bound (dynamic hosts) or typed (static hosts).' A conformance criterion equating a dev-only assertion with a static host's TYPE SYSTEM. The equivalence is false in production.
  - spec/Pattern-Forms.md:54-55 — two reg-app-schema calls introduced as 'Both are registered' with no timing note.
  - spec/Construction-Prompts.md:638 — a REQUIRED per-feature artefact row, '(rf/reg-app-schema [:feature] FeatureSchema)', no caveat.
  - spec/Conventions.md:323 — 'reg-app-schema | the registrar name itself (THE VALIDATOR *IS* THE REGISTRATION)'. That parenthetical is precisely the conflation the elision breaks: the registration happens in every build, the validation does not.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (RULED option (a) — dev-only as designed). Spec 010 §Production builds now carries the normative statement and both validation tables mark the reg-app-schema rows dev-only.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7172 (2026-07-28). The new explicit m/explain branch is the correct production-real validation seam, but the worked no-JS failure path is incomplete. On a server POST, form-params comes from the request while the rendered fields come from [:cart :add-form :draft]. The failure arm calls write-form-errors, whose shown implementation updates only :status, :errors, and :submit-attempted?; it never copies the submitted :item-id/:quantity into :draft. The following prose nevertheless promises that the user sees their bad input and no information is lost. With JS disabled, the re-render therefore shows the pre-submit/empty draft instead. Bounded repair: have the failure arm retain only the safe editable fields (not :csrf-token or other secret carriers) in the form draft before rendering errors, and make the prose/example agree. No framework form subsystem.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7232 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the docs-only gates prove links and vocabulary, but no executable witness checks that the canonical no-JS POST shape and hydrated-client dispatch shape are both accepted by the shared handler/schema. That missing cross-platform shape proof hides a contradiction in the copyable example.

CORRECTNESS: `AddToCartForm` requires `:item-id`, `:quantity`, and `:csrf-token`. The hydrated `:on-submit` dispatches `(assoc draft :item-id item-id)` and deliberately does not add the token; the handler then unconditionally runs `(m/explain AddToCartForm form-params)`. The client path therefore always takes the validation-failure arm in production and never navigates. In development, the event's `:schema [:cat ... AddToCartForm]` rejects the same client event before the handler. The example also registers `[:cart :add-form :draft]` against `AddToCartForm` while repeatedly ruling that the secret token must never live in that draft, so its own canonical draft is invalid by construction.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: preserve the strong server-only CSRF boundary and do not put the token into app-db or a client event merely to satisfy one schema. Split the editable field schema from the POST envelope (or otherwise select the schema by the already-computed platform boundary): validate the field schema on both hosts, require/check the token only for the server POST, type the draft with the field schema, and make the dev event tripwire accept exactly the two intended shapes. Add one small executable or mechanically checked witness for a valid client draft and a valid server POST. No framework form subsystem.
COMPLETE — PR #7406 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7406), branch worker/validscope-bl8k7, 2026-08-03. NOT MERGED. Rode one worker with rf2-bl8k7 + rf2-096js because two of the three edit spec/Pattern-FormAction.md. Addresses the 2026-08-01 audit comment on merged PR #7347 (the transport seam), which was this bead's live obligation.

THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT. The page required the host adapter to parse the request body and then defined no keywordisation or coercion contract over what it produced. HTML form encoding has no types and no keywords, so a real parsed body is {"quantity" "2"} — string keys, string VALUES. Handed straight to the documented handler a CORRECT submission fails: the CSRF compare looks up :csrf-token in a string-keyed map and finds nothing, so a valid token 403s; and even with keywordised keys "2" is not an :int and takes the 400 arm. The suite hid this by hard-coding already-normalised values as "the canonical body a browser submits".

THE OWNER IS :rf/server-init, and the reason is structural rather than stylistic. It is the one place the wire crosses into the domain, and normalising THERE is what makes the pattern's central claim true — below that dispatch the server's args and the hydrated client's args are the same shape, so "one handler, both platforms" is a fact rather than an aspiration. A handler that normalised its own input would first have to work out which platform called it, which is exactly the knowledge this pattern spends its effort not needing. That reasoning is on the page, not just in this note, and the converse is stated as an anti-pattern ("Normalising inside the action handler").

SHIPPED (spec/Pattern-FormAction.md):

- The section is renamed to "§:rf/server-init routes GET vs POST, and owns normalisation". The old anchor had NO inbound links — verified by grep before renaming.
- Copyable code now on the page. route->action is a single table carrying the action event AND its args schema, so a form cannot acquire an event without also declaring the shape its wire body decodes to. decode-form-params keywordises the keys and lets the SCHEMA drive the value coercion via mt/string-transformer.
- VERIFIED FROM SOURCE before writing it, not assumed: malli's string-transformer does decode [:and :int [:>= 1] [:<= 99]] from "2" to 2, and does leave "abc" untouched. Probed against the real ssr :test classpath.
- The seam NEVER throws and never rejects. A value the transformer cannot decode reaches the handler unchanged and fails the handler's own arm, so malformed input still takes the documented 400-with-repopulated-draft path. That is stated on the page, because the tempting alternative — reject at the seam — would quietly relocate the 400 away from the arm this bead exists to make load-bearing.
- Host variance addressed without hedging: a host that already keywordises (Ring's wrap-keyword-params) makes update-keys a no-op, one that also coerces makes the transformer one, and neither changes which layer is RESPONSIBLE.
- Also: shape steps 2-3; the Server-vs-client table (new Normalisation row, 3 cells like its siblings, checked by hand); the §Composition with :rf.server/request note (the declared-coeffect route hands the handler the RAW body, so a handler taking it owns the decode and owns keeping its client arm out of it); the §CSRF sentence about what the token travels through; two anti-patterns ("Assuming :form-params arrives as domain data", "Normalising inside the action handler"); two conformance criteria.

ACCEPTANCE (implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_doc_example_form_action_test.clj). Starts from a literal csrf-token=tok-abc&item-id=sku-1&quantity=2, parses it the way Ring's wrap-params does, and drives it through the page's OWN EXTRACTED seam — route->action and decode-form-params are read out of the markdown fence at run time like every other schema and helper in that suite, so a page that drops either goes red naming the anchor. Five new deftests:

- the parsed body is asserted to be strings keyed by strings, and to carry exactly the input names the view fence renders (the tie to the HTML is kept);
- the seam produces the handler's shape, and the route table resolves to both the event and the schema;
- a valid no-JS request reaches 303 from the wire bytes;
- THE COUNTER-PROOF: the UNDECODED parsed body is asserted to 403, so the seam is provably load-bearing and cannot be quietly dropped without going red. A page that deletes the normalisation step would otherwise turn the suite green in the worst possible way;
- quantity=0 reaches the 400 path with the coerced value back in :draft and no token beside it, and quantity=abc passes THROUGH the seam rather than exploding at it, landing on the same safe 400.

server-post is now a delay derived from the wire body rather than a hand-written map, so every PRE-EXISTING assertion in the suite is now downstream of the transport seam too. 16 tests / 50 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors.

PRESERVED: the typed hydrated-client path and both limbs of the fail-closed CSRF arm, unchanged.

RESIDUE FILED, NOT FIXED — rf2-1iclq (P1, bug): skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md is three corrections behind this page, INCLUDING the fail-OPEN CSRF compare (not= alone) that this very page lists as an anti-pattern, plus the single-schema shape the #7232 audit rejected. Out of this worker's fence and wider than this cluster. scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py exits 0 over that drift, which is itself worth a look.

Gates foreground, unpiped, worktree-local logs: mkdocs --strict 0 (python -m mkdocs; bare mkdocs still absent from PATH), check_doc_slugs.py 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0 ("PASS fast PR spine"), the ssr acceptance namespace 0, check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py 0. Fresh worktree had no node_modules — the first spine run failed at CLJS node integration on a missing shadow-cljs; ran a real npm ci in implementation/, created NO junction, mayor node_modules never touched, then re-ran the spine from the top.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7406 — REOPENED (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The new POST normalisation seam blanket-keywordises every untrusted form key: `(update-keys form-params keyword)`. That includes unknown attacker-chosen parameter names, not just `AddToCartSubmission`'s declared vocabulary. On long-running JVM SSR, each novel name is interned into the process-global, never-GC'd keyword table. This is the exact keyword-interning DoS the repo's security contract forbids: `spec/Security.md` requires bounded interning for structured input, and `spec/012-Routing.md` closes the analogous query path by promoting only schema-declared keys while leaving undeclared keys as strings. The page also says an unknown form key is “passed through untouched”; turning it into a keyword is observably not untouched.

The acceptance suite exercises only the three known static names, so it cannot detect this. An attacker can send a fresh unknown field name on every POST while all 16 tests remain green.

Bounded repair: keep `:rf/server-init` as the single seam and keep schema-driven value coercion, but promote only names from the route action's declared schema (or an equally explicit finite wire-name map); leave unknown keys as strings. A per-request cap is the fallback only if the implementation genuinely must keywordise arbitrary keys. Add one adversarial witness with a fresh undeclared string key: declared fields become their known keywords and coerce, while the undeclared key remains a string and no unbounded keyword universe is opened. No general form framework or second schema is requested.
close_reason: MAYOR RE-CLOSE 2026-08-03. This bead was closed when its PR merged, then REVERTED TO OPEN by a tracker-state rollback (the same class as rf2-rjqtj / rf2-51uz1 — five early closes reverted while every later one held). Re-verified before re-closing: PR #7406 is MERGED and 3 commit(s) naming this bead are on origin/main. No work is outstanding from the original scope; if an audit later reopens it for a NEW obligation, that reopen is legitimate and separate from this rollback.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: Audit of merged PR #7347: the new test calls its server-post the canonical body a browser submits, but hard-codes {:item-id "sku-1" :quantity 2 :csrf-token "tok-abc"}. HTML form encoding submits names and values as strings; the pattern only requires the host to parse form-urlencoded or multipart and defines no keywordization or type-coercion contract. A normal parsed body therefore has string keys and "2" for quantity. With string keys the handler sees no token or fields and returns 403; even if the host keywordizes keys, AddToCartFields requires an integer so "2" takes the 400 arm. The test derives only the input-name set and silently supplies the normalized values whose missing boundary is the defect, so its claimed browser-to-handler proof is vacuous at the transport seam. Bounded acceptance: state one normalization owner explicitly and include the copyable normalization code in the page; drive the extracted example from a representative application/x-www-form-urlencoded body or its actual string-key/string-value parsed shape, then prove the valid no-JS request reaches 303 while malformed values still reach the safe 400 draft path. Preserve the typed hydrated-client path and the fail-closed CSRF arm.

title: Hicasso arm 1: the survival metric's allocation-slope half (warm 1/3/7/20 reads)
description:
Re-homed from rf2-2rtt6.41 item 4, which is otherwise discharged. Not new scope - this is the last unowned half of that bead's witness set.

WHAT IS OUTSTANDING. validation.md's survival metric has two halves. The ZERO-RETAINED-PER-OCCURRENCE half is witnessed (after commit and after teardown, rf2-2rtt6.9 + PR #7338). The STEADY-STATE ALLOCATION SLOPE across warm 1/3/7/20 reads is not: it needs the bench, on the P0 instrument, against same-run donors - the same rig rf2-2rtt6.34 used for the per-read rung (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs, PR #7337).

WHY IT WAS NOT TAKEN ON 2026-08-03. Deliberate, and the reason is about trust in the number rather than effort. The box was carrying six concurrent workers, and absolute figures on that rig move by roughly 2x run-to-run on UNCHANGED arms under that load. A slope is a difference of such figures, so it is strictly less robust to the contention than the absolute readings are - measuring it then would have produced a number that read as evidence and was not. rf2-2rtt6.41's own worker had already held it off once for the same class of reason (contention with the heap worker's instrument).

PRECONDITION FOR DISPATCH: a quiet box. Take it when the worker count is low, take the warm 1/3/7/20 series in one session on one rig, and cite the SHA. Do not interleave it with other bench work on the same instrument.

Related and already answered, so do not re-measure: the shell-target half of item 5 is closed NEGATIVELY at 1,143 B against the >1 KB paper-fail line - structural, because the subscription hook is per BOUNDARY (rf2-2rtt6.41 notes, from rf2-2rtt6.34).

title: hygiene: nine worker worktrees will not reap — cause unknown, my first explanation was falsified
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-01/02. NINE worktrees refuse removal across many attempts, several quiet periods and a full session of the box cycling through other workers: axes-2rtt6-44, bulkretake-yd52q, diagleak-210uq, durab-b0tz5, flakes-2i1ay, heapaxis-2rtt6-34, readj-emvod, skills-89cn5, witness-2rtt6-41.

MY FIRST EXPLANATION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE SO NOBODY REUSES IT. I claimed the discriminator was workload — that a worktree running only doc checkers reaps cleanly while one running shadow-cljs or Chromium never does. I stated it twice with confidence and predicted it in advance. THEN ctl3-7iqb5, which ran a full bench ensemble WITH Chromium, REAPED CLEANLY ON FIRST ATTEMPT. The rule is false. Whatever holds those nine, it is not simply 'ran a heavy suite'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN: removal fails with the branch still in use by the worktree, i.e. something holds an open handle under the tree. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh behaves CORRECTLY throughout — it disarms the node_modules junction first, refuses rather than forcing when removal cannot complete, and the mayor's real node_modules has held at 101 entries across every attempt without exception. The guard is not the problem and must not be bypassed: following a junction into the mayor's real node_modules has happened twice in this repository and is exactly what it prevents.

WEIGH IT HONESTLY: every one of the nine is INERT — work merged, no branch on origin, nothing at risk. This is disk and clutter, not danger. The cost is that a cluttered worktree list makes the hygiene survey harder to read, which is where a genuinely stale tree would hide.

THE WORK, and step 1 is the real one: FIND OUT WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THEM. Identify the process owning a handle under one of the nine (Windows has tooling for this; keep any script POSIX-safe per the cross-platform rule) and compare against ctl3-7iqb5, which reaped. Only then propose a fix. notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7407 — REOPENED (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The new `--force-disposable` / `-ForceDisposable` promise is not fail-closed yet.

1. Both `Get-WorktreeDirt` implementations collapse a failed `git status` into “clean”: POSIX ends the command with `|| true`; PowerShell suppresses stderr and never checks `$LASTEXITCODE`. The caller sees zero dirt/KEEP lines and, under the disposable flag, invokes `git worktree remove --force`. A status failure (permissions, unsafe ownership, damaged worktree metadata, filesystem error) can therefore authorize the exact unreviewed deletion the flag exists to prevent. Direct probe: a failing PowerShell status returned exit 128 and zero lines. Nonzero status must be a refusal, never the clean state.

2. The disposable directory glob `*logs/` is not an anchored log-directory shape. It also matches ordinary untracked names such as `catalogs/` (confirmed in PowerShell; POSIX `case '*logs/'` has the same suffix semantics), so the “anything unmatched is KEEP” claim can silently delete unrelated work. A destructive allowlist must prefer a false refusal to a suffix collision.

Bounded repair: capture status output and exit together; on any nonzero exit, print a distinct refusal and do not force-remove (and ideally classify before unlinking so a refused tree is unchanged). Narrow the directory rules to explicit component shapes/names that mean generated output. Add cheap classifier witnesses in both siblings: failed status refuses; `catalogs/` is KEEP; the intended `logs/`, `bench-logs/`, `.gate-logs/`, `.wtlogs/`, `out/`, `.shadow-cljs/`, and `*.log` shapes remain disposable; tracked modifications remain KEEP. No cleanup framework or content inspection is needed.

comments.text: CAUSE FOUND (PR #7407) — nothing was holding them. Every one of the nine was DIRTY, and 'git worktree remove' refuses a dirty tree with 'fatal: <wt> contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it' (exit 128, non-destructive; --force then removes cleanly). Reproduced in a throwaway worktree. Field evidence: all nine carried exactly one untracked path (logs/, bench-logs/, .gate-logs/, .wtlogs/, PRBODY.md, g-fastpr2-exit.txt), and the two that reaped cleanly carried none. That is why the 'heavy workload' rule was falsified and why waiting through quiet periods never helped: untracked files do not evaporate, and ctl3-7iqb5 reaped because it left none. NO handle-holder was ever involved, so the candidate remedies aimed at terminating processes are moot. The script's own message was the trap: it reported every failure as REMOVE_FAILED=(safe to retry once the lock clears). Failures are now classified — REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY (paths listed, tagged [build output]/[KEEP], waiting will not help), REMOVE_REFUSED_KEEP, and REMOVE_FAILED reserved for a genuinely clean+locked tree. Added --force-disposable/-ForceDisposable, which sweeps ONLY when every untracked path is build/gate output and refuses anything else; a modified tracked file is never disposable. That guard is load-bearing: band-ymi6j held four ladder-*.md analysis files for an OPEN bead, and pairing-2026-07-17 / pr-audit-20260730 / toolsbugs-oztox carried uncommitted source and doc edits — a blanket --force would have destroyed all of it silently. --dry-run now reports the same partition up front so a hygiene survey can act before touching anything. Prevention at source: the dispatch template now tells workers to write gate logs where git ignores them (*.log already is).

title: machines-viz grammar/definition-summary leaks the top-level key set of a forged definition
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-m46qv (share/value-free-summary disclosure), and deliberately NOT fixed there: different function, different consumers, its own ruling.

tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/grammar.cljc's `definition-summary` is the THIRD independent EP-0015 shape summariser in this repo (after re-frame.error/diag-value-summary, fixed in rf2-210uq, and share/value-free-summary, fixed in rf2-m46qv). It reproduces the `:keys` defect both of those removed:

  base (if (map? definition)
         (cond-> {:type :map
                  :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys definition)))
                  :parallel (parallel-definition? definition)} ...

1. `:keys` returns EVERY top-level key of the rejected definition, uncapped and unsanitised. A definition reaches this function from a forged share URL (share/decode-share-url validates `…/chart`'s `:definition` through grammar/valid-definition?), from an LLM response (ai_generate.cljc), and from SCXML/Mermaid input (scxml.cljc, mermaid.cljc) — all three are untrusted, and the ai_generate call sites already say so in their own comments.
2. `(sort-by str (keys definition))` runs `str` over caller-supplied keys, so a key whose `toString` throws replaces the documented ex-info with its own exception — the rf2-210uq path-5 shape.
3. The `:else {:type :value}` leg uses a `:type` tag outside the closed vocabulary the other two summarisers now share (`:scalar`).

NOT a straight copy of the rf2-m46qv fix, which is why it is its own bead: this summary deliberately carries STRUCTURAL diagnostics the other two do not — `:parallel`, `:state-count`, `:region-count` and the rf2-j538f7.18 `:defect` (category + path + offending keys). Those are load-bearing for three emitters and are pinned by tests, and `:defect` itself may carry offending KEYS, so the ruling has to decide what a definition's structural diagnostic may name — not merely delete a leg. spec/API.md §SCXML + §ai-generate document `:spec-summary` as this shape.

ACCEPTANCE: rule on what `definition-summary` may carry over untrusted input; remove or justify `:keys`; align the `:else` tag with the closed vocabulary; and add the same GRAMMAR-shaped witness rf2-m46qv added — a corpus of hostile definitions (sentinel-bearing keys of every key type, an attacker-sized key set, a key whose toString throws) asserting the whole thrown ex-data discloses no sentinel fragment and serializes inside a fixed bound.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7408: REOPENED. The disclosure repair itself is sound, but the acceptance's grammar-shaped witness and the new normative API omit a reachable output. `transition-target-defect` passes `:spawn/on-error` into `target-defect`; direct evaluation of `definition-summary` over `{:initial :a :states {:a {:spawn {:machine-id :child :on-error :missing}}}}` returns `{:defect {:category :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target, :slot :spawn/on-error, :depth 1} ...}`. Yet `grammar_validation_cljs_test.cljc` defines `defect-slots` as only `#{:on :after :always :on-done}`, and API.md plus `defect-summary`'s contract list the same four. The hostile corpus has no spawn/on-error target, so both JVM and CLJS suites remain green while the advertised grammar rejects an actual summary shape.

Bounded correction: include `:spawn/on-error` in the closed slot vocabulary (or normalize it consistently if that is the intended public spelling), update the normative table/docstring, and add a spawn-on-error bad/unresolved-target corpus case that fails when the fifth slot is omitted. The value remains fixed and content-free; no new summarizer or abstraction is needed.

title: spine: hook-scoped provisional hand-off — adopt the render-phase build at commit (rf2-2rtt6.14 design)
description:
HELD for operator sign-off on rf2-2rtt6.14 — do not dispatch until the ruling records adoption.

IMPLEMENT the hook-scoped provisional hand-off designed under the reopened rf2-2rtt6.14 (decision input: rf2-2rtt6.15 / PR #7300, docs/design/hicasso/studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md — the double-build clock is >= 20% of the mount red-zone in EVERY round at layers 1, 2 and 3; the handoff arm's M1 mount landed at/below the Reagent denominator). Scope is the ruling's: hook-scoped provisional hand-off ONLY — NEVER a general ref-count-0 cache tenancy. This description stands alone; the design doc is local-only.

THE DESIGN. In re-frame.substrate.spine's use-subscribe-2 (make-react-spine — shared by the UIx adapter, re-frame.freehand.substrate, re-frame.ui.substrate), the render-phase use-memo factory stops balancing in-render (today: subscribe then unsubscribe, 0->1->0 on cold cache, in-tick dispose, commit-phase subscribe-fn rebuilds — the measured double build, bodyRuns 2N). Instead the factory subscribes and mints a ONE-SHOT ESCROW TOKEN {reaction, frame-kw, query-v, spent? atom} holding the +1 provisionally. Token is (i) stored key-tagged in a hook provisional-ref for the adopter, (ii) pushed on a spine-level pending queue whose macrotask drain (setTimeout-0 class; ONE timer per burst, scheduled on empty->nonempty) is scheduled BEFORE the factory returns. If the ref held a previous unspent token (memo discard / StrictMode double render / interrupted attempt), the factory releases it AFTER its own subscribe (subscribe-then-release ordering; at most one outstanding provisional per hook — this preserves the rf2-8u8tx.2 and rf2-879fe "== 1 after mount" assertions verbatim). The commit-owned subscribe-fn subscribes durably as today (cache HIT -> committed is identical? the render-phase reaction = adoption), publishes committed-ref, then releases the token (2->1). RELEASE = one-shot (spent? CAS) + REACTION-GUARDED via ONE new internal ^:no-doc CLJC helper in re-frame.subs.cache: unsubscribe-if-reaction! [cache k reaction frame-id] — decrement iff (identical? reaction (:reaction slot)), dropped-to-zero? -> dispose-entry-now! (same eviction, same :no-more-derefers emit, same CAS-after-snapshot discipline as unsubscribe!). Unadopted tokens (abandoned render / error / unmount-before-commit / key change) are released by the drain <= 1 macrotask later; 1->0 disposes in-tick per Spec 006 unchanged. The cache NEVER holds a ref-count-0 entry; no cache data-shape change, no entry state machine; unsubscribe!/eviction/cascade untouched. Reagent, reagent-slim, plain-atom: byte-identical (hook-only change + inert CLJC helper).

WHY IT CANNOT LEAK: drain scheduled by the host scheduler before the acquiring expression returns (React cannot unschedule it); one-shot spent? CAS (adoption + drain cannot double-decrement); reaction guard (a slot evicted by HMR/cache-clear/frame-destroy took the +1 with it — stale release no-ops, can never steal a successor entry's ref); one unspent token per hook. Early drain vs React's passive-effect flush degrades to today's dispose+rebuild — correctness NEVER depends on React timing; the perf is opportunistic. Reagent parity: Reagent's released subs already dispose on a macrotask (lane/settle! docstring), so the horizon matches the denominator's shipped behaviour.

CORRECTNESS PROTOCOL MAPPING (rf2-2rtt6.14 clauses): (a) growth bounded by attempts-per-horizon, zero at horizon; Suspense retries within a horizon HIT the provisional entry instead of rebuilding the chain. (b) provisional entry is live+source-wired; extra recompute bound = app-db movements within <= 1 macrotask on abandoned paths only (adopted-path recompute is not extra), vs 2.5-17.2 us/read saved per cold read. (c) reap scheduled unconditionally at acquisition, fires independent of React. (d) second subscriber = plain ref-counting (and can adopt an abandoned materialisation); StrictMode setup/cleanup/setup goes 2->1->2 (today 1->0->1 dispose+rebuild — an improvement); key change = predecessor release + existing rf2-naz09e guard; HMR/cache-clear/frame-destroy = guard no-ops (helper also nil-frame-safe); SSR net-zero after horizon (Node timers) with getServerSnapshot unchanged. (e) JVM sub_cache_test cascade/shared-input pins untouched; rf2-8u8tx.2 + rf2-879fe verbatim; ONE test amended: the rf2-es09qq Suspense-abort witness (react_shared_suite.cljs ~4309) asserts <= 1 immediately after fallback commit AND == 0 after one macrotask settle (zero-leak property kept; zero-POINT moves one macrotask later — this is the single contract-visible change the operator's adoption blesses).

SAME-PR SPEC OBLIGATION (per the protocol): Spec 006 hook-substrate subsection "render-phase provisional acquisition and commit adoption" (amend the rf2-es09qq wording: no retained ref-count BEYOND the provisional horizon = one host macrotask) + cross-ref sentence in §Reference counting and disposal stating the cache algorithm is unchanged; update re-frame.subs.cache ns + unsubscribe! docstrings (the remount-churn-acceptable paragraphs) + full contract docstring on the new helper. Spec 006 is HOT-ZONE — sequence against other spec PRs.

TESTS/BENCH (acceptance): (1) THE ACCEPTANCE WITNESS is the coldmount instrument's uix-handoff arm — post-land the SHIPPED hook must reproduce it: witness counters commits N, rebuilt 0, bodyRuns 1N per layer <= L at layers 1-3, shipped M1 clock inside the handoff arm's band; re-run all five rows of implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/coldmount_run.cjs; re-point the instrument's fidelity gate at shipped-vs-handoff (xcript stays the double-build reference); keep the residue gate (it is the leak detector). (2) adoption-identity unit test (spy-proxy, rf2-sqhjtu style): committed-ref reaction identical? the render-phase build. (3) Suspense-abort amendment per (e). (4) StrictMode: final refcount 1, dispose-count spy 0 across the effect cleanup gap. (5) reaper discipline: adopted token drain no-ops; stale-token-vs-successor entry unchanged; one-shot under adoption+drain. (6) layer-2 abandoned cold render: parent AND inputs gone after one settle (cascade at the horizon). (7) node SSR render without commit -> zero after one timer turn.

INTERACTIONS: rf2-2rtt6.13 (retention fix) COMPOSES — land .13 FIRST (same ~10 factory/get-snap lines; rebase on it; adoption needs no handle from the memo — identity flows through the cache hit, the token carries the reaction for the guard; .13's frozen pre-commit fallback unaffected). rf2-gncxk (flush-path memo guard, HELD ruling) is NOT decided here: no touch to make-derived-value/compute-fn/subs.memo; note for that ruling that cold-mount wrapper invocations halve (2N->1N) post-handoff.

SEQUENCING: depends on PR #7300 merging (the arm + page cited) and rf2-2rtt6.13 landed. Sized for a solo worker: ~20-line CLJC helper, ~50-70 line spine edit, spec wording, tests + bench re-run.

The timer reaper therefore wins before React's passive subscribe, disposes the provisional, and the commit rebuilds. The PR's entire measured benefit is absent on the actual public mount schedule; the forced-synchronous acceptance witness measured a different schedule.

Bounded repair: add a non-act, non-flushSync test through the canonical adapter render slot that pins identity and one body construction after settlement, then make the adopted protocol satisfy it or retract the shipped-performance/spec claims. Do not paper this over with an arbitrary longer timer; the horizon is an operator-approved lifecycle contract. The separate stale pre-commit snapshot finding remains owned by reopened rf2-2rtt6.13.

title: build: a --config-merge focused compile poisons the shared node-test build cache
description:
SPLIT OUT of rf2-hofhx (its "SECOND, SMALLER FINDING"), left unfixed there
deliberately: the fix belongs in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, a hot-zone
file, and rf2-hofhx's PR touched only test-quiet test sources. Sequencing it
separately avoids a hot-zone conflict with the five clusters in flight.

SYMPTOM. A focused compile of the node-test build via

    shadow-cljs compile node-test --config-merge '{:ns-regexp "..."}'

shares the `node-test` build id with the full compile, so it leaves the build
cache in a mixed state. The NEXT full compile dies with

    aborted par-compile ... still waiting for ...

and no root error, which reads like a compiler bug rather than a stale cache.

CLASS. Identical to the rule the bench drivers already implement in
lane_cache.cjs: one build id driven with N different configs must clear the
cache between configs.

FIX, either of:
  - document it on the :node-test build in shadow-cljs.edn (cheapest), or
  - clear the cache automatically when a --config-merge is detected.

CONFIRMED still current while working rf2-hofhx (2026-08-01): the workaround
used there was simply never to run a focused compile on the shared build id,
and to select namespaces at RUNTIME instead (`node out/node-test.js
--test=<ns>`), which needs no recompile and cannot poison the cache. That
runtime-selector route is worth naming in whatever documentation lands.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — merged PR #7400 (2026-08-03).

CORRECTNESS. `scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` handles `result.status !== 0` by returning `result.status`. Node's spawn result uses `status: null` when a child is terminated by signal; the top-level `process.exit(main(...))` then treats that null as exit 0. A dynamic audit proof against the real exported `main` (with only its captured spawnSync result replaced by `{status:null, signal:'SIGTERM'}`) printed `did not complete (exit null)`, returned null, and the wrapper process exited 0. The output bundle is still removed, so today's `compile && node bundle` npm chains eventually red on the missing bundle, but the compile wrapper itself falsely reports success—precisely unsafe for the unchained compile caller this bead documents.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY. No regression test references `compile-node-test.cjs`; the PR's green full compile exercises only the success path. Keep this bounded: map every signal/null-status termination to a nonzero wrapper exit, name `result.signal` in the diagnostic, and add a focused dynamic regression test that proves the real wrapper cannot exit 0 for that case (while retaining the stale-output deletion invariant). The browser drift-waiver half of #7400 is independently complete and remains owned by closed rf2-u0cy4.
close_reason: MAYOR RE-CLOSE 2026-08-03. This bead was closed when its PR merged, then REVERTED TO OPEN by a tracker-state rollback (the same class as rf2-rjqtj / rf2-51uz1 — five early closes reverted while every later one held). Re-verified before re-closing: PR #7400 is MERGED and 1 commit(s) naming this bead are on origin/main. No work is outstanding from the original scope; if an audit later reopens it for a NEW obligation, that reopen is legitimate and separate from this rollback.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-01 WITHOUT any --config-merge, so the bead's premise is
incomplete: heavy box load alone is sufficient.

While measuring rf2-hofhx, a plain `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test` (no
--config-merge, no focused ns-regexp) run against a box deliberately
oversubscribed with 32 CPU burners + 6 I/O loops on 24 cores died with:

  aborted par-compile, [:shadow.build.classpath/resource
    "re_frame/ssr_keyword_head_contract_cljs_test.cljs"]
    still waiting for #{reagent.dom.server}
  {:aborted [...], :pending #{reagent.dom.server}}

An identical compile on the same tree minutes earlier, on a quiet box,
succeeded in 42s. So this is a par-compile thread-pool starvation under
load, not only a cache-config mismatch.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FRAMING. The failure is silent in the
worst way for an automated run: the script that invoked it continued (no
`&&`), the STALE `out/node-test.js` from the previous compile was still on
disk, and the suite then ran happily against the wrong bundle. A measurement
harness that does not check the compile's exit code will therefore report
numbers for code it did not build. Recovery was `rm -rf
.shadow-cljs/builds/node-test` followed by a compile on a quiet box.

Suggests the fix wants two parts: whatever cache handling the bead already
proposes, AND that callers treat a nonzero compile exit as fatal rather than
proceeding to run a stale artefact.

title: hicasso: attack the 415 B/read gap — can the index edge, key cell or read-set entry be made cheaper or eliminated?
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01): 'I don't understand how hicasso can be worse than Reagent? At worst, I would expect it to be roughly the same. What is it that hicasso is doing that makes it worse?'

THE ANSWER, from the landed measurement (rf2-2rtt6.34, PR #7337, reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md section 6): Hicasso is NOT doing Reagent's job worse. On the SAME substrate Reagent costs 948 B/read [947-948] and the Hicasso candidate costs 1,363 B/read [1,360-1,364] — 1.4379x, and EXACTLY 415 B/read worse. The page names what buys it: THE INDEX EDGE, THE KEY CELL, AND THE READ-SET ENTRY.

WHY REAGENT DOES NOT PAY IT: Reagent's dependency tracking is free because the ratom's own watcher list IS the edge. A deref inside a reaction is captured by the dynamic binding, and the dependency lives in a structure that had to exist anyway. Nothing extra is allocated.

WHY HICASSO MUST: the operator's Surface B ruling makes sub an ordinary call, legal inside a when, a for, an inlined helper. That means THE RENDER MECHANISM CANNOT BE THE THING THAT RECORDS DEPENDENCIES, so Hicasso keeps its own — a shared boundary-to-query index edge, a per-key cell, and a read-set entry (which is what buys the <=2-hook shell, since subscribe is keyed on read-set CONTENT). The 415 B is the price of decoupling reads from the render mechanism, which is a capability Reagent does not offer at all.

IT IS A TRADE, NOT A REGRESSION: against UIx the same design WINS by 708 B/read on the identical substrate (2,981 -> 2,272, 0.7624x, a 23.8% margin, crossover at R=1.29 reads). Hicasso is cheaper than N useSyncExternalStore hook stacks and dearer than a deref-capture; it sits between them.

THE WORK — nobody has attacked this yet, and it is far more tractable than 'why is it slower':
  1. PRICE THE THREE TERMS SEPARATELY. 415 B is their sum; the split is not published. Which dominates?
  2. For each, ask whether it can be made cheaper or ELIMINATED. Specifically: can the read-set entry be derived rather than stored (it exists to key subscribe identity — is there a cheaper key)? Must the key cell be per-key, or can it be shared? Is the index edge's representation minimal, or is it carrying structure it does not need?
  3. Respect the fences: <=2-hook shell (useContext + useSyncExternalStore, measured at React's dispatcher, 2 at 1/7/20 reads), subscribe closing over the read set ALONE, no candidate ledger, no compiler, no analyzer, no ViewCell-class object graph. A saving that costs a hook or widens subscribe's closure is a finding to REPORT, not a cost to spend.
  4. Any measured claim needs a QUIET BOX, B/E/Q stamps, a positive control predicted before the run, and the arm-order guard reportable. Same instrument (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs) and same-run donors as section 6, or the numbers are not comparable.

A HONEST NEGATIVE IS A COMPLETE ANSWER: if all three terms are irreducible given Surface B, that is the price of the ruled surface and should be stated as such on the ladder page — it converts an open question into a known cost.

SEPARATELY AND SMALLER: the shell is 1,143 B against Reagent's 508 because the subscription hook is per BOUNDARY, so a boundary that reads nothing still pays it. That is the same design choice seen from the other end and is tracked as rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5's shell-target half, already answered negatively.
notes:
WORKED 2026-08-03 (worker/readgap-aqgr2). PR to follow; measurements and
per-suspect verdicts recorded here so the bead stands on its own.

THE ANSWER TO ITEM 2, PER SUSPECT.

1. THE KEY CELL — REAL, and it is the whole of the saving. Every cell minted
its own watch key, `(keyword "rf-hicasso-arm1" (str "w" (vswap! counter inc)))`,
to buy a uniqueness that was already structural: at most one cell per
(frame, query), `subs/subscribe` hands back that pair's own cached reaction,
and no two cells ever hold the same reaction. The mint retained a Keyword, its
name string and its fully-qualified string PER UNIQUE KEY — per read on the
Q = E rung — plus a field on the cell. Replaced by one namespaced constant;
the global counter goes with it. MEASURED -108 B/read on BOTH segments.

2. THE INDEX EDGE — the duplicate does not exist. HONEST NEGATIVE. It looked
certain: `front.sub-index/record-reads` calls `(set read-sub-keys)` on a value
the caller already holds as a set and retains the result as the forward edge
for the mount's life. An explicit share-if-already-a-set changed the slope by
ZERO — `cljs.core/set` returns a meta-less set unchanged, so the sharing was
already there. The code change was reverted. A probe that FORCES the copy
prices what the existing sharing is worth: +46 B/read (Reagent seg.) / +47
(UIx). That is a TERM PRICE the ladder did not have — one retained hash-set
membership is ~46 B/read on this rung — and the property is now asserted with
`identical?` in the index's law suite.

3. THE READ-SET ENTRY — not reducible as it stands. Its key array and key set
are not redundant with each other: the array is what `entry-matches?` compares
and what `getSnapshot` sums over; the set is what the index and
`acquire-cell!` consume. Eliminating either only moves its work.

THE MEASUREMENT. `p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, 6 rounds, 0/1/3/7/20, Q = E,
B = 1,200 — nine runs. The deciding pair is back-to-back on `main`
`1ef3fdb73e` with only `arm1/runtime.cljs` differing:

  arm                       before     after
  Hicasso, Reagent seg.      1,446     1,338   (-108)
  Hicasso, UIx seg.          2,283     2,175   (-108)
  Reagent donor                948       947   (control)
  UIx donor                  2,979     2,980   (control)

Shell (R=0) unmoved on both segments while the FIRST read falls with the
slope — the signature of a per-KEY saving rather than a per-boundary one.
Positive control ok, 0 unverified of 154 mounts, structural witness fully
answered, arm-order guard reportable, exit 0 — all nine runs.

RESTATED LIVE NUMBERS: the design's bill falls from +499 to +390 B/read
(1.5264x -> 1.4114x); the win against UIx widens from -697 to -805
(0.7661x -> 0.7299x, a 27.0% margin); the bracket becomes 1,338 - 2,175.
943/948 is STILL NOT BEATEN and the verdict's shape is unchanged. The
crossover is deliberately not restated — rf2-2rtt6.34 is reopened on which
model the page states it in.

BOX HONESTY (item 4). The box was NOT quiet — five concurrent workers — so
these are stated as DELTAS against same-run donors, not as replacement gate
rows, and the ladder subsection says so in those words. What makes them
quotable: both donors ride every run and answer 947-948 / 2,978-2,980 in all
nine; the positive control is ok in all nine; and the UNCHANGED arm reproduces
the published `main` figure of 1,447. `main` moved twice mid-session
(rf2-2rtt6.32's codec rewrite, rf2-2rtt6.50's registry term) and the pair was
RE-TAKEN on each new base rather than carried forward — both landings measure
at zero on this axis, which is itself now recorded.

FILED, NOT TAKEN: rf2-dabt3 (P2) — `:sub->bs` is a second global map over the
same B*R key space as `!cells`, plus a singleton reader set per key at
fan-out 1; on the measured 46 B/membership this is plausibly the largest term
left in the +390. It is an ELIMINATION, but it dissolves the shared front
half's six-law algebra and moves architecture.md's central sentence, so it
wants a ruling rather than a perf worker. Also rf2-ixb92 (P3, `:live` is a
redundant index — shell axis), rf2-6wh9o (P3, read_profile_app's local cell
copy still mints a watch keyword, so its "faithful copy" claim is stale) and
rf2-e3i6y (P3, the evidence seam builds its event map before the nil check).

DECLINED WITHOUT FILING: dropping the cell's denormalised `frameKw`/`queryV`
(both are `(nth subKey 0/1)`) — two object slots per read, below what this
instrument resolves, against a second lookup in `flush!`'s hot loop. Minutiae.

FENCES HELD: the shell is not in the diff — hook count still 2 at React's
dispatcher, `subscribe` still closes over the read set alone, no candidate
ledger, bodies unchanged.
close_reason: Closed by PR #7418 (worker/readgap-aqgr2). One of the three suspects was real: the key cell's minted watch identity, -108 B/read on both segments, taking the design's bill from +499 to +390. The index edge's duplicate read set does not exist (cljs.core/set already shares; ablation reads identical to the byte) and the forced-copy probe prices the existing sharing at +46/+47 B/read. The read-set entry's array and set are not redundant with each other. The largest remaining elimination is filed as rf2-dabt3.

title: Off-box resource redaction still emits enumerable FNV tokens and hashes pr-str instead of CEDN-1
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7391.

PR #7391 correctly proved that the existing FNV-1a-32 redaction token is neither injective nor one-way: low-entropy tenant/account values are recoverable by enumeration. It therefore withholds coarse :redact/:omit rows from SSR hydration. The same token still leaves the process through re-frame.resources.trace-egress: sensitive/large resource keys, free scope tags, page cursors, and related off-box tool/trace carriers still call ssr/redact-value, while Spec 009 and source comments call the result "opaque content-addressed". That contradicts Spec 015's normative sensitive marker contract: :rf/redacted carries no information about the underlying content and a sensitive value is not revealable by any observation surface. Removing the token from hydration while retaining it on off-box observability leaves the privacy defect at the other trust boundary.

The new cross-host determinism clause is also not implemented at the value boundary. redact-value hashes (pr-str value), although the repo's identity authority explicitly rejects pr-str over unordered values and provides identity/canonical-bytes. Concrete JVM witness: (array-map :a 1 :b 2) and (array-map :b 2 :a 1) are = and have equal canonical bytes, but redact-value emits 943e4859 and 08a47259. The shared fixture covers one map spelling and host arithmetic only, so it cannot catch this violation of "a fixed function of the canonical value".

One adjacent Spec 016 contradiction remains: the opening SSR paragraph still says every durable entry present at serialize time rides the projection and calls every non-blocking entry eligible for serialization, while the new MUST immediately below correctly withholds every re-keyed row, including all coarse sensitive/large entries.

Keep the repair bounded. Preserve PR #7391's server/client withholding and the useful shape-driven family projector. Decide the smallest safe off-box token contract: sensitive content must not produce an enumerable content-derived token merely to preserve joins; large-but-not-sensitive data can retain an appropriate structural/digest policy. Do not invent a general crypto subsystem. If any stable digest remains, derive it from CEDN-1 canonical bytes and pin equality/order variants on both hosts. rf2-fwp31 is the exact Spec 009 sentence owner and is reopened separately, blocked on this runtime decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- Off-box resource trace/tool egress satisfies Spec 015: a sensitive scope, params value, or cursor cannot be recovered or tested by enumerating a low-entropy candidate space; the trusted-local include-sensitive opt-in remains the only raw-content lift.
- Any retained content-derived token is limited to a classification that permits it and hashes identity/canonical-bytes (or another already-authoritative canonical encoding), not pr-str; equal canonical values with different map/set construction order produce the same token in CLJ and CLJS.
- Tests cover the real family projector paths for a sensitive scoped key, a free scope tag, and a pagination cursor, plus a negative large-only/plain control; a mutation restoring the current FNV-sensitive path reds.
- Spec 015/016 and source comments agree on the settled token semantics, and Spec 016 no longer simultaneously says every durable row rides and re-keyed rows do not ride.
- Preserve PR #7391's hydration withholding and do not broaden the public API or build a general hashing/key-management framework.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7419. redact-value's payload is now chosen by CLASSIFICATION, with the 1-arity as the SAFE default so a fail-closed walk cannot mint an enumerable token: :redact (sensitive, and every caller with no disposition) emits a content-FREE shape token (closed :type tag + integer :count, rf2-210uq's shape adopted verbatim); :omit (large — a SIZE claim, not a privacy claim) keeps a digest, now over identity/canonical-bytes instead of pr-str. Sensitive distinctness is surrendered deliberately — it was bought with the very token that was the leak — and costs nothing downstream because a re-keyed row is withheld either way (the withholding matches the token by its :rf/redacted KEY, never its payload, so PR #7391 is preserved and asserted). Determinism witness fixed: (array-map :a 1 :b 2) and (array-map :b 2 :a 1) emitted 943e4859/08a47259 and now emit one token, 64f7985e, pinned as a literal on both hosts. canonical-bytes is PARTIAL, so a value outside CEDN-1 falls back to the shape token — a redaction that throws is not a redaction. New cross-host suite covers the real family-projector paths (sensitive scoped key, free scope tag, pagination cursor) plus plain and large-only negative controls; the FNV-sensitive mutation reds all three carriers. Gate caught 7 transitive assertions in implementation/epoch pinning the surrendered distinctness — inverted rather than deleted, with cardinality/tier/resource-id/attribution asserted alongside. Spec 016 gains the normative token contract and no longer simultaneously says every durable entry rides and re-keyed entries do not. Spec 009's sentence deliberately NOT touched — it is rf2-fwp31's, blocked on this decision, which is now made.

title: machines validate-machine! throws a host ClassCastException on a non-Named node key
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-oztox (machines-viz definition-summary disclosure) and
deliberately NOT fixed there: it is in implementation/machines, a different lane
from tools/machines-viz, and the viz walker is only a MIRROR of it.

implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1432
carries the same defect the viz copy did:

  (->> (keys m) (remove #(namespace %)) (remove known) vec)

`namespace` THROWS on a key that is not `Named`. So a machine definition
carrying a String / number / vector / host-object key —

  {:initial :a :states {:a {}} "x" 1}

— raises a host ClassCastException out of `validate-machine!` instead of the
documented `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`. `reg-machine`'s registration
gate is the boundary that promises the structured error, and a definition
assembled at runtime (merged from config, decoded from JSON, produced by a
generator) can carry a string key without anyone hand-writing one.

The viz mirror was made total in rf2-oztox by testing Named-ness before calling
`namespace`:

  (remove #(and (or (keyword? %) (symbol? %)) (namespace %)))

which preserves the namespaced-extension carve-out exactly and flags a
non-keyword key as `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key` — the right answer, since
a key that is not a keyword is not a legal node key under any reading of the
grammar. Line 192 of the same file has the same `(remove #(namespace %))` shape
and should be checked with it.

NOTE THE PARITY RATCHET. tools/machines-viz/test/.../engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc
asserts viz and engine give the same accept/reject answer. Its corpus carries no
non-keyword keys, so the divergence rf2-oztox just introduced is invisible to it
today — the engine THROWS where viz now REJECTS. Closing this bead re-converges
them; the parity corpus should gain a non-Named-key case at the same time so the
two cannot drift apart again silently.

ACCEPTANCE: `validate-machine!` returns the documented
`:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key` for a definition with a String / number /
vector / throwing-toString key at the root and at a node; the namespaced carve-out
is unchanged; the parity corpus gains a non-Named-key case.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7419. TWO defect sites, not one: unknown-bare-keys at validation.cljc:1432 AND an inline copy in the :spawn-all block check at :192 — a reader of the bead alone would have fixed one and shipped. Plus a SECOND partial operation one level down: (pr-str offending) in the diagnostic message reaches an arbitrary object's toString, so a throwing-toString key destroyed the failure being described. Both made total once via namespaced-key? + key-label (reusing error/diag-value-summary's closed vocabulary). Engine keeps NAMING offending scalar keys — deliberate divergence from the viz (rf2-oztox/#7408), whose caller is handed a share-URL definition while reg-machine holds its own. Parity ratchet: it was blind for a second reason the bead did not name — the probes were TWO-VALUED, so on CLJS engine-accepts?'s (catch :default … false) recorded a HOST CRASH as a CLEAN REJECTION. Two validators that both explode AGREE, and the equality assertion passes them; that is exactly how this hid. Fixed with three-valued engine-answer/viz-answer plus a definition-validation-is-total deftest, and 5 non-Named corpus entries. Proof it now sees the divergence: (engine :reject, viz :host-throw). Green after #7408 merged: 11 tests / 203 assertions.

value:
A FAIL-OPEN GATE IS RARELY A SINGLE SITE — CHECK FOR COPIES BEFORE BELIEVING THE BEAD (rf2-2rtt6.73, 2026-08-03).

THE BEAD said the hicasso bench lane was compile-ungated because run.cjs checked only shadow-cljs's exit status, and shadow exits 0 on warnings. TRUE, BUT IT NAMED ONE FILE. The worker found EVERY ONE OF ELEVEN DRIVERS carried its own copy of the same fail-open eight lines. A worker fixing only the cited driver would have shipped, passed its own new test, and left the lane ungated through ten other doors.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS RETROACTIVE AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT EXPENSIVE: other workers had been MUTATION-PROVING their changes through that lane the same day. Their proofs were worth less than they appeared — a mutation that should have reddened the lane exited 0 with warnings and still PRINTED A FULL MEASUREMENT TABLE. When a shared instrument is found fail-open, the question is not only 'fix it' but 'what did people conclude from it while it was broken?'

THE FIX SHAPE that worked: one build door (lane_build.cjs) used by all eleven drivers, plus a separate compile gate over all 100 lane namespaces wired into CI and the fast-PR node tier, plus a test pinning all four refusals against real ANSI output. It rode the existing build via --config-merge so implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (hot-zone) needed no edit at all.

GENERALISE: when a bead names ONE site of a fail-open pattern, GREP FOR THE PATTERN, NOT THE LINE. The same day, rf2-dhl4d named one defect site and there were two (an inline copy elsewhere in the same file), and rf2-ncn5p's over-claim survived in a fourth page nobody had listed. Three separate beads, same under-count. Budget for it in the brief: say 'the bead names N sites; establish the real count before fixing any of them'.

AND WHEN ARMING A GATE, MAKE IT STOP RATHER THAN WARN: the pre-fix driver printed its measurement table even while failing. A gate that fails but still emits numbers invites someone to read them.

title: Hicasso: walk report double-counts prop sub-stages in its 92% decomposition
description:
PR #7390 publishes docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md as the decision record for rf2-2rtt6.63. Its section 3 claims the named stages explain 34.4 us of a 37.5 us whole-walk delta (92%), but the arithmetic adds nested measurements as though they were independent:

- walk_vs_reagent_app/stage-table measures `convert-props-hicasso` and `convert-props-reagent` by invoking each full convert-props pipeline over every element.
- Those full pipelines already perform the cached prop-name lookup and prop-value conversion for every emitted prop.
- The published sum adds the whole pipeline delta (+27.0 ns x 1,202 elements) and then adds the prop-name (-3.0 ns x 1,489 props) and prop-value (-0.4 ns x 1,489 props) deltas again.

The negative nested deltas reduce the non-overlapping total from about 39.5 us (about 105% of the observed 37.5 us) to the quoted 34.4 us / 92%. Therefore the statement that the decomposition closes to 92% is not proved. The raw interleaved whole-walk result may still support the broader conclusion, and the cache/string changes remain independently correct; this finding is specifically about the quantitative attribution used as decision evidence.

The exact owner rf2-2rtt6.63 is in_progress and locked, so this is a discovered-from follow-up rather than an edit to its scope.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Classify stage rows as nested or additive and stop summing a parent pipeline with its sub-stages.
2. Recompute or retract the 34.4 us / 92% closure claim in the studio record and every derived authority.
3. If an additive decomposition is retained, expose non-overlapping residual stages (or equivalent accounting) and show the arithmetic from instrument output.
4. Keep the independent whole-walk evidence and the correctness/performance claims for the two landed optimizations separate from the corrected decomposition claim.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hicasso: collapse the four callback forms to one — the position selects the contract
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

Freehand — the SHIPPED interpreted substrate this programme is measured against —
requires an author who cannot use a bare event vector to pick from a roster of FOUR
callback forms, each with a different contract:

  docs/core/freehand/authoring/events-and-handlers.md:343-352 (the roster table)
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1302  (v/event)     -> returns ONE event vector or nil
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1327  (v/handler)   -> "The body's return is ignored"
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1344  (v/render-fn) -> pure, runs during a FOREIGN render
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1287  (v/raw-fn)    -> identity passes through unchanged

There is a fifth rule on top: the roster only works at prop positions Freehand WALKS.
events-and-handlers.md:361-384 ("Where the roster reaches") and freehand.cljc:2355
record the failure mode outside that reach — a roster carrier handed to a raw
createElement #js prop is a non-callable marker object, and the library gets the
engine's own TypeError "props.onPing is not a function", "naming nothing you wrote".
freehand.cljc:1292 also hands identity management back to the author for raw-fn:
"re-render churn is the author's to manage".

THE PROPOSAL. Hicasso ships ONE callback form. The CONTRACT comes from the POSITION,
not from the form the author chose, because Hicasso already knows every position it
walks and the role is already declared exactly once per crossing:

  - a native :on-* prop      -> event position: a returned vector (or nil) is dispatched
  - a defhost :callbacks entry -> the DECLARATION already says :event or :handler
    (docs/core/freehand/host/host-boundaries.md:59 — "a finite map from EXACT prop
    names to :event or :handler; never inferred from an on* name")
  - a slot / render-prop position -> pure render phase; dispatching is the error
    (freehand.cljc:1395 — arity is "a CONTRACT, not a convention")

WHY THIS IS AFFORDABLE. Kill criterion K5 (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360) is
"> ~8 public concepts or > ~8 guide pages to ship CRUD". Four concepts collapsing to
one is half the budget back. The census supports it: keyboard-condition handlers
appear 3 times in 85 idiomatic files and stopPropagation 0 times
(docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md:331-332), and foreign React
components 0 times (:339) — the roster is priced for a component-library tier that
charter.md:144-149 explicitly defers past v0.

SCOPE
  1. Decide and record the one spelling (working name h/fn; naming stays unfrozen per
     docs/design/hicasso/authoring.md:3-7).
  2. Specify the position->contract table, including what a render-position callback
     that dispatches must do (a loud diagnostic naming the POSITION, not the form).
  3. State whether raw-fn's identity-passthrough ships in v0. Recommendation: NO —
     0 foreign components in the census; let the component-library phase earn it back.
  4. Witness: one test per position proving the contract, and one proving the
     diagnostic text names the position.

FENCES. No compiler, no analyzer. This is a runtime classification at positions the
codec already walks, not a build-time pass over body forms (charter.md:115-120).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. The new event-callback wrapper accepts exactly [e] and invokes (f e), so a defhost :event callback silently drops every foreign callback argument after the first (or raises an h/fn arity error). That contradicts the form's arbitrary parameter vector and the callback contract's live invoker arguments. Bounded repair: make only the event wrapper variadic and apply the marked function; add a declared :event witness with two arguments while retaining the one-argument native and no-frame diagnostics. No new callback form or ABI.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7396 (merged 2026-08-02T20:35:10Z): REOPENED. The new host door makes the declaration path real end-to-end and its h/fn rows are strong, but `lower-declared-prop` still lets the value override the declared position contract. Only the marked `h/fn` branch consults `contract`; every vector takes `intent-handler` and every map takes `key-map-handler` for `:event`, `:handler`, and `:render` alike. Thus a declaration that says `:handler` silently dispatches a bare intent, and a `:render` position can dispatch during the foreign component's render without the required `:rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position`. That contradicts HD-024's core law that the position selects the contract.

Bounded repair: make the declared contract govern every lowerable carrier. Preserve vector/key-map convenience for declared `:event`; reject them precisely at `:handler`/`:render` (or otherwise implement those contracts without dispatch), retain h/fn identity/purity semantics, and add real-host rows for all contract/carrier combinations plus one mutation proving a render-position dispatch goes red. No new callback form or public concept is needed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7398 (merged 2026-08-02T21:22:39Z): the new interop callback section exposes another carrier/contract mismatch under this exact owner. It says ::h/prevent at a declared :event position calls preventDefault on whichever invoker argument is the real DOM event. The landed vector path does not inspect or forward all arguments: intent-handler returns a unary fn [e] and calls .preventDefault on that first value. A value-first foreign call such as onPick(value, event) therefore calls value.preventDefault and throws instead of preventing the actual event. This differs from the variadic h/fn event-callback path the same paragraph correctly teaches.

Bounded resolution: as part of the existing all-contract/carrier matrix, pin the event-vector argument law with a real host witness. Prefer the minimal coherent API: either document that marker/prevent vectors require an event-first contract, or deliberately implement a stronger declared-event rule and witness it; do not add a new callback form.
close_reason: PR #7420. Both open audits closed. #7396: lower-declared-prop now dispatches on the CONTRACT first and the carrier second — :event keeps the vector/key-map conveniences, :handler and :render refuse both with :rf.error/hicasso-intent-at-a-non-event-contract naming the position; declared-callback deleted. #7398: resolved to ONE law — the vector spelling (::h/prevent, ::h/value, ::h/checked, :on-submit auto-prevent, key-map lookup) reads the DOM event from argument ONE; a value-first invoker raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event naming the position and pointing at h/fn, instead of the engine's value.preventDefault TypeError. The 05-interop.md sentence promising 'whichever argument is the real DOM event' is retired; HD-024 in decisions.md and authoring.md now state both laws and the declared row's third contract (:render). Witnesses: host_hatch §5b full contract x carrier matrix at a real minted host + mounted render-prop row + render-position dispatch refusal + the argument law at the widget's own value-first invoker; intent_cljs_test closure-level rows. title: Hicasso: the walk stage table cannot be totalled — a decomposition of record needs a quiet-box re-take
description:
Follow-up from rf2-mgegk, which retracted the "decomposition closes to 92%"
claim on docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md.

With the double-count removed, the BEFORE table's non-overlapping named
stages sum to +39.5 us against an observed +37.5 us whole-walk delta — a 5%
overshoot, which is inside the instrument's declared limits. Running the same
arithmetic over the AFTER table is worse: the named stages come to +5.6 us
against an observed delta of -25.0 us, so they do not agree in SIGN.

That is not a new defect in the walk or in the two landed cheapenings — the
page's conclusions rest on section 2's same-run interleaved arm ratios, and
the cache/predicate-order changes are adjudicated by their own before/after
micro tables. It is a statement about the stage table: it was taken on a box
section 7 declares was NOT quiet, its absolutes are explicitly ceilings, and
stock Reagent's own string-child row reads 8.8 in one run and 20.3 in the
other on identical code. The record now says so and reads the table as an
attribution rather than an accounting.

IF a per-stage decomposition of record is ever wanted (nothing currently
depends on one), it needs a re-take on a quiet box, and probably a residual
stage so the accounting can close by construction rather than by luck.

PRECONDITION — quiet box. Same as rf2-0qj9w and rf2-2rtt6.76: do not run the
bench drivers while the fleet is oversubscribed. This is not blocking
anything, so it should wait for a genuinely idle machine.

DO NOT re-open the 92% figure. It is retracted, not pending.

notes:
H2 — RENDER-SIDE POSITIONAL VERIFICATION: ATTEMPTED, DECLINED, SWING UNSPENT (2026-08-01, rf2-2rtt6.41).

No commit implements H2 and no bench row cites a SHA for it, so under HD-002's

itself positionally against the k-th entry of THE COMMITTED SEQUENCE P FOR THE
BOUNDARY CURRENTLY RENDERING. Arm 1's render phase cannot name that boundary:

title: Hicasso: PR #7393 omits failed controls from its secondary Reagent rows
description:
AUDIT FINDING from merged PR #7393 (`rf2-cno31`). The routing specialisations, twin parity repair, primary UIx gate, and landed measurement provenance hold. The durable studio record does not faithfully report the secondary Reagent run it quotes.

The committed `censusclock-cno31/reagent.json` adjudicates controls STRICTLY (every block inside the ±25% band):

- large-template: PASS.
- feed: FAIL — prediction 1.9943, band [1.4958, 2.4929], observed range [1.8533, 2.5099].
- ordinary: FAIL — prediction 1.7255, band [1.2941, 2.1569], observed range [0.9437, 1.6574].

Yet `the-route-link-render-term-priced.md` publishes the Reagent-run feed and ordinary ratios without carrying those failures, and its unqualified “Positive controls” paragraph reports only the separate UIx run (feed PASS, ordinary FAIL). Its provenance also says every row band was 6.7–15.8%, although the Reagent ordinary band is 29.79%. The established census record states the required posture explicitly: a Reagent comparison is not a second product gate, but every magnitude from a run whose control failed carries that failure (`census-real-clock-rows.md`, lines 197–201 on the landed tree).

DO: label control status per adapter run and row; mark the secondary feed and ordinary Reagent comparisons as carrying failed controls (or withdraw those magnitudes); correct the six-run band range. No primary rerun is required by this finding: the UIx acceptance/feed controls passed, the acceptance verdict and feed non-pass stand, and this is a durable-record correction rather than a challenge to the route-url fix.

title: ci: hermetically pin the fast-PR mkdocs module-only fallback
description:
FOUND by merged-PR audit #7352.

PR #7352 fixes the current behavior: the docs tier now prefers a bare mkdocs console script, falls back through python/python3/py -m mkdocs, hard-fails the build wherever a command resolves, and reports an unresolved skip honestly. The motivating module-only path is not durably protected, however.

title: hygiene: the gate exit-code file the dispatch template asks for is NOT gitignored, so following the guidance creates reap-blocking residue
description:
FOUND during the 2026-08-03 hygiene sweep, measured in a live worker worktree.

THE LOOP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (section 'How a gate is run, not just which one', landed as c6566415b8) tells every worker two things:
  (a) echo the runner's own exit code explicitly and quote it in the PR body; and
  (b) put the gate log where git ignores it -- '*.log already is'.
Workers duly write the log to *.log AND the exit code to a sibling file. But the exit-code file is not a .log. Measured just now:

  git check-ignore -v gate-fastpr.exit   -> NOT IGNORED
  git check-ignore -v g-fastpr-exit.txt  -> NOT IGNORED
  git check-ignore -v gate.log           -> .gitignore:14:*.log

So the untracked exit file survives, and 'git worktree remove' then REFUSES the tree -- exit 128, non-destructive but permanent until someone forces it. That is precisely the mechanism rf2-p0m6m diagnosed (nine worktrees would not reap; every one was dirty with exactly one untracked path, and the script's message misattributed it to a lock). The template's own residue examples even NAME 'g-fastpr-exit.txt', so the hazard was written down while the ignore rule that would prevent it was not added.

LIVE INSTANCE at the time of filing: re-frame2-worktrees/hostile-dhl4d carried '?? gate-fastpr.exit' with everything else clean.

DO, and keep it small -- this is a one-line class of fix, not a project:
  1. Extend .gitignore so gate exit-code artefacts are ignored alongside logs. Something in the shape of '*.exit' plus the '*-exit.txt' spelling the template already names. Check first whether any TRACKED file would be caught -- 'git ls-files | grep -E "\.exit$|-exit\.txt$"' must be empty before adding a broad rule.
  2. Make the dispatch template's wording close the loop: it currently says to put THE LOG where git ignores it, which a careful worker satisfies while still leaving the exit file behind. Say plainly that EVERY gate artefact -- log and exit code -- goes to an ignored path, and give one concrete ignored spelling workers can copy.
  3. Consider the same sentence in AGENTS.md, which PR #7412 established is the file Codex workers here are handed.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing how exit codes are captured. Redirect-and-read-the-file is correct and is load-bearing -- four workers in one day reported a pipe's exit status instead of the runner's. Do not weaken that; only make its artefact ignored.

title: The hicasso bench lane is compile-ungated: run.cjs passes with :undeclared-var warnings, and no PR gate compiles the arms
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.70 worker while mutation-proving that bead's
repair. It is the same fail-open class rf2-2rtt6.70 names, one level up:
the bead worried about an ARM that measures deleted code, and the answer
to "why did nothing go red" turns out to be "nothing could have".

TWO FACTS, both measured on branch worker/frameprop-2rtt6-39.

1. NO PR GATE COMPILES `walk_profile_app.cljs` — or any other arm in
   the hicasso bench lane. `:node-test` selects `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"`
   plus transitive requires, and nothing test-shaped requires the arms;
   `:browser-test` selects `-dom-cljs-test$` likewise. Verified by
   grepping the built bundles: `out/node-test.js` contains zero
   occurrences of `walk_profile_app`, and `out/browser-test/js/
   cljs-runtime/` has no such module. The ONLY compiler that ever sees
   these files is `:hicasso-bench`, driven by hand through `run.cjs`.

2. `run.cjs` DOES NOT FAIL ON COMPILE WARNINGS. It checks the
   shadow-cljs child process's exit status and nothing else
   (`if (r.status !== 0)`), and shadow-cljs exits 0 with warnings. The
   mutation that proved it: rename `M-NO-PROPLESS`'s def and leave its
   two use sites alone. Result —

     [:hicasso-bench] Build completed. (186 files, 131 compiled,
                      2 warnings, 35.49s)
     ------ WARNING #1 - :undeclared-var ------
      Use of undeclared Var re-frame.bench.hicasso.walk-profile-app/M-NO-PROPLESS
     ... [hicasso] ok
     MUT_WALK_EXIT=0

   Two undeclared vars, a full run, a printed table of numbers, and
   exit 0. Under `:advanced` an undeclared var is `undefined` at the
   call site, so an arm can silently become a different arm and still
   publish a plausible ns/element.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. This lane's whole product is numbers,
and its arms are deliberately LOCAL copies of shipping code (that is the
call-convention discipline rf2-2rtt6.32 established and it is correct).
Local copies drift by construction; the only thing standing between a
drifted copy and a published figure is a gate. There is none.

THE WORK, and the cheap half is most of the value:

  a. Make `run.cjs` refuse a build that emitted warnings — parse the
     shadow-cljs output for `WARNING #` / `warnings,` in the build line,
     or pass a compiler option that promotes them. Exit 1 with the
     warning text. This is the one that would have caught the mutation.
  b. Decide whether the lane wants a compile-only PR gate over
     `re-frame.bench.hicasso.**` (a `shadow-cljs compile hicasso-bench`
     with no browser run is ~35-40s and needs no quiet box, so it does
     NOT contend with the measurement lane). If yes, wire it into
     `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`'s node tier or a workflow; if no, say so
     on this bead so the next worker does not re-derive the question.

NOT a measurement task and NOT clock-contending: (a) is a driver change,
(b) is a compile.

title: The band calibration was taken on the frame-only clock (rf2-yd52q)
description:
rf2-cvvb7's nineteen-run load ladder, its seam null, its orthogonal decomposition and the BAND it calibrated were all computed on taskNet, which rf2-yd52q has since shown is a frame-ONLY reading with the operation's script subtracted out (see rf2-emvod).

WHAT PROBABLY SURVIVES. The band is ctl-2x/floor, and both of those arms are pure React whose script is small and nearly proportional to their frame - rf2-yd52q measured ctl-2x at 1.69-1.80x floor on BOTH clocks, agreeing to within 2%. So the band statistic is likely close to unchanged, and rf2-yd52q's own runs bear that out: band 10.3-23.6% on taskNet against 8.8-19.7% on raw TaskDuration over the same 16 rows.

WHAT NEEDS CHECKING. Whether the 25% BAND_CEILING and the 8.9% ladder average hold on the corrected clock, and whether the multiplicative-perturbation finding - which rests on ctl-2x/floor correlating +0.41 with the floor - is the same on a clock that includes script. A perturbation that is multiplicative in frame time need not be multiplicative in script time.

CHEAP: seam_ladder.cjs stores raw per-sample readings, but only taskNet ones. The ladder would need re-running at the current blob, or the driver's roundsTask added to its JSON output first.

Full record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/bulk-broad-re-taken.md
