PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7424 — merged-PR audit #7368's statistical finding is CONFIRMED by independent recomputation from the committed dataset, and the ceiling's derivation is WITHDRAWN. The code half is rf2-nk1hq.

NO NEW MEASUREMENT. ladder_band.cjs --from data/ladder-ymi6j.json reproduces the page digit for digit today, and everything below is arithmetic over that file. The band ladder is in fact the ONLY published ensemble on this instrument whose dataset survives — nothing from rf2-yd52q's eight runs or rf2-emvod's seven does.

CONFIRMED, at 200,000 draws on raw TaskDuration, against the audit's figures:
  quantile   pooled-block   run-preserving
  q50        13.0%          11.5%
  q90        19.9%          23.4%
  q95        22.7%          31.0%
  q99        29.4%          41.4%   <- audit said 41.4%
  P(>25%)     2.7%           9.1%   <- audit said 9.1%
  P(>35%)     0.2%           2.7%   <- audit said 2.7%
Frame-only run-preserving q99 is 45.9%.

So pooling blocks across runs is NARROWER through the whole upper tail, not wider. The page's parenthetical — 'a future run is a future run rather than a repeat of a past one, so the pooled figure is what a ceiling should be set against' — is refuted by its own arithmetic and is struck. The correct number was PRINTED all along, in the within-run column the page then declined to use.

WITHDRAWN RATHER THAN RESTATED. '35%, set from the statistic's own bootstrap q99, at a measured P(fire) of 0.2%' is retracted: 35% is the q99 of NEITHER model, and its real per-run false-fire rate is 2.7% — 13x the advertised one. No replacement ceiling is minted in the docs; the run-preserving q99 is 41.4% and whether the constant moves is code (rf2-nk1hq).

HONEST IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, on the page: 35% is still a 3.4x improvement on 25% (2.7% against 9.1% per run), it is the ceiling in force, and no published magnitude moves at either value. Section 8's check survives intact.

The band/ceiling/multiplicativity work this bead was opened for had already landed in its four earlier commits: band 4.4-31.1% mean 14.0% on raw TaskDuration against rf2-cvvb7's 8.9%, ceiling 25% -> 35%, multiplicativity withdrawn at ctl-2x/floor = 1.7138 [1.6228-1.8417].

2. No dataset from ANY published ensemble on this instrument survives — gitignored out/, and neither readj-emvod nor bulkretake-yd52q worktrees still hold them. Checked.

So a corrected-clock ladder is a RE-RUN, not a recomputation. Not done here: the box was busy with worker/ctl3-7iqb5 taking published rows.

THE BEAD'S NAMED BLOCKER IS GONE. The note (MERGED-PR AUDIT #7363) said HCLOCK_JSON omits roundsTask and inPageRounds. The +0.41 ctl-2x/floor-vs-floor correlation that evidences it has NO counterpart on the corrected clock. THE ANSWER TO THE CEILING QUESTION, WHICH IS NEITHER OF THE TWO OPTIONS.

box, both clocks in one pass, all six predictions committed before the first

NOT THE REGIME (rf2-h8o80's hypothesis) — refuted in the direction posed. The
band is WIDEST ON AN IDLE BOX: 24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3% at
four, corr(band, floor) = -0.49, with the floor's per-sample dispersion falling
monotonically 30.0% -> 15.2% as load rises while the floor absolute RISES
3.78 -> 6.93 ms. A busy box is slower and steadier. Both ceiling breaches on
this ladder are at ZERO load. And h8o80's evidence is a clock mismatch: its

runs, mean 15.3% against 14.0% — because taskNet is a difference of two
counters and a smaller number, so its relative dispersion is larger by
construction (28.5% against 23.2% per-sample). Real, and repaired: the gate now
adjudicates raw TaskDuration and reports the frame-only band without refusing
on it. But both breaches breach on BOTH clocks, so this is not what fired it.

THE CAUSE IS THAT 25% WAS ABOVE NINETEEN DRAWS OF A TAIL, NOT ABOVE THE TAIL.
Bootstrapping 18 blocks from the ladder's 342: run-level q99 29.1%,
P(band > 25%) = 2.6% pooled / 9.0% within-run. Three firings in two days is

comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7368 (2026-08-02) — correctness, completeness, and implementation-quality follow-up.

The 35% ceiling is not the claimed run-level bootstrap q99. `ladder_band.cjs` pools all 342 block ratios, then builds each synthetic 18-block run by drawing individual blocks across unrelated runs and load rungs. That destroys the run-level clustering/regime shared by the 18 blocks and estimates a synthetic mixed-regime block sample, not a future run. The script already exposes the contradiction: on raw TaskDuration it reports pooled P(band > 35%) = 0.2% but mean within-run P = 2.7%, while the source comment says the pooled estimate is wider and should set the ceiling. A run-preserving hierarchical bootstrap (choose one of the 19 runs, then resample its 18 blocks), against the committed compact data with the same deterministic band arithmetic, gives q99 = 41.4%, P(>25%) = 9.1%, and P(>35%) = 2.7%. Thus 35% is not q99 and the advertised 0.2% tripwire rate is understated by about 13x.

The recomputation output also still prints that an additive constant has a NEGATIVE corr(ctl-2x/floor, floor) signature. Across this ladder the varying quantity is W while c is roughly fixed, so (2W+c)/(W+c) rises with W; the positive sign is the additive signature. `seam.cjs` and the landed prose correctly withdrew the old sign argument, but `ladder_band.cjs` still emits it.

Acceptance: preserve run clustering (or otherwise justify a statistically valid run-level resampling model), recalibrate/describe the ceiling from that distribution without claiming 35% is q99 if it is not, remove the stale sign interpretation, and add a deterministic synthetic regression that distinguishes pooled-block from run-preserving resampling. Existing `seam.cjs` and `clock_run.cjs --selftest` pass but do not exercise the new bootstrap or its printed interpretation.

title: The window audit's 1.0509x and its +268-704% table are frame-ONLY figures (rf2-yd52q)
description:

See rf2-emvod for the measurement.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THAT PAGE:
  - 'bulk300 frame-inclusive 1.0509x' is a FRAME-ONLY figure. On raw TaskDuration - script AND frame - rf2-yd52q's 8-run ensemble reads 0.8602x [0.7709 - 0.9058].

  - 6's claim that TaskDuration 'does include style, layout and paint' is right; what is missing from the page is that the SUBTRACTION then removes the script, which is most of a substrate arm's operation.

The audit's CONCLUSIONS mostly survive - M1 robust, bulk broad's 0.6291x not reproduced - and rf2-yd52q reaches both again on the corrected clock. This bead is about restating the page's instrument description and its bulk300 number, not about reversing it.

comments.text:
SCOPE NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT — rf2-emvod (PR #7365).

This bead assumes the audit's 1.0509x and its +268% to +704% table were taken on
the same defective clock. Half of that is right and the half that matters for
the +268-704% table is not.

THE CORRECTION HAS A DOOR. DevToolsCommandDuration bills page script only when
that script runs INSIDE a protocol command. clock_run.cjs drives M1, bulk300,
bulk100 and narrow through page.evaluate (Runtime.callFunctionOn), so those were
corrupted. Its keystroke row drives through page.keyboard.press, and the whole of
rf2-rguy1's cross-check drives through page.click — the Input domain, whose
handler runs in a task the command does not own — so THOSE WERE NOT.

Measured, per row, pooled over seven runs: ScriptDuration reads 0.063 ms for a
901-element mount on the evaluate-driven M1 row and 49.97 ms for the keystroke
control on the Input-driven row of the SAME instrument in the SAME run; the
devtools term varies 7.836 ms across arms on the first and 0.069 ms on the
second. On the cross-check harness directly: devtools spread 0.126 ms against a
ScriptDuration spread of 13.97 ms, and its ratios move at most 1.7% between the
two clocks.

WHAT THIS LEAVES THIS BEAD. The audit's 1.0509x on bulk300 IS a frame-only
reading and does need restating — it came from clock_run.cjs's evaluate-driven
bulk300 row.

But the +268% to +704% table's MECHANISM STATEMENT is the thing to fix, and it
is not 'one window mis-read the other'. The two windows are near COMPLEMENTS:
taskNet is the frame with the script removed and the in-page span is very nearly
the script alone. In milliseconds on M1, pooled over seven runs, hicasso reads
8.507 ms in-page and 5.520 ms on taskNet with a raw TaskDuration of 14.738 ms —
the two add to the whole, less the tare, on every arm. A percentage difference
between complements is not an error rate, and the table should be read as the
SPLIT between two halves rather than as one instrument's inaccuracy.

rf2-emvod has already made that correction on the-candidates-clock.md section
4.1, which carries the same table from the other side. This bead still owns the

value:
A KILLED GATE CAN REPORT EXIT 0 — THE WRAPPER'S STATUS IS NOT THE RUNNER'S (2026-08-03, rf2-2rtt6.73).

THE MECHANISM, and it is worse than the pipe trap because nothing in the command looks wrong. A worker's spine ran past the 10-minute tool cap. The WRAPPER was SIGTERM'd, but the underlying sh.exe SURVIVED and kept running. The completion notification that arrived carried EXIT CODE 0 — the wrapper's own status, not the runner's. The worker nearly read that as a pass. The tell was that the LOG NEVER REACHED A 'PASS' LINE.

TWO COMPOUNDING CONSEQUENCES:
1. A green that never happened. 'exit 0' from a timed-out tool call means the wrapper exited, not that the gate passed.
2. A SECOND SPINE. Believing the first was dead, the worker launched another — so TWO spines ran in one worktree against one .shadow-cljs, which is exactly the contention that produces phantom failures in test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test. Two workers hit that shape today; one wasted a cycle diagnosing failures it had caused itself.

THE RULES THAT FOLLOW:
• NEVER trust an exit code that arrives with a timeout or cancellation. Confirm the run's OWN terminal marker in its log — 'PASS fast PR spine', a test summary line, whatever the runner prints on success. Absence of that marker beats presence of exit 0.
• BEFORE relaunching a long gate, CHECK FOR SURVIVORS by process ancestry. Do not assume a killed wrapper killed its children. The worker here found both alive, killed both, and then ran one clean spine, blocking in-turn with repeated foreground waits.
• This is the same family as: a pipeline's exit status is its last command's; a two-valued probe recording a crash as a rejection; a bench arm exiting 0 on :undeclared-var warnings. FOURTEEN instances in one week. The general form is: THE INSTRUMENT REPORTED ON ITSELF RATHER THAN ON THE SUBJECT.

MAYOR NOTE: when briefing, 'foreground to completion' is not sufficient guidance on its own — add 'if a gate is killed or times out, treat its exit code as MEANINGLESS and check the log's terminal marker; check for surviving processes before relaunching'.

title: hicasso: sub-index :live is exactly the key set of :b->subs — a redundant index on the shell axis
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2. Not actioned there: it is a per-BOUNDARY term,
so it moves the shell intercept and not the per-read slope that bead was
attacking.

`front/sub_index.cljs` keeps three structures in one atom:

    :sub->bs   sub-key     -> #{boundary-id}
    :b->subs   boundary-id -> #{sub-key}
    :live      #{boundary-id}

`:live` carries no information `:b->subs` does not already carry:

- `mount` adds to `:live` unconditionally and installs `#{}` in
  `:b->subs` when absent, so after a mount both contain the boundary;
- `unmount` removes it from both;
- `record-reads` only ever assoc's `:b->subs` for a live boundary.

So `(:live idx)` is exactly `(set (keys (:b->subs idx)))` at every
reachable index value, and `live?` is `(contains? (:b->subs idx) b)`.
Dropping it removes one set membership per mounted boundary from the
retained inventory (`arm1/runtime.cljs` `retained-inventory` files it as
`:index/live`), and removes a second place the mount/unmount pair has to
stay symmetric in.

WHAT IT IS WORTH: unmeasured, and honestly small — the per-read heap
ladder shows the Hicasso shell at ~1,240 B against Reagent's ~507, and
one persistent-set membership is a low-tens-of-bytes term in that. It is
filed as an ELIMINATION (a redundant index disappears, and the docstring
gets shorter) rather than as a saving.

WHAT IT COSTS TO DO: the ns docstring's three-line data model, the
matching sentence in `docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md`, `empty-index`,
`mount`, `unmount`, `record-reads`, `live?`, `stats`' `:boundaries`
count, and the law suite's uses of `(:live (idx/snapshot))`. Mechanical,
but it touches the shared front half's published shape, so it wants a
deliberate yes rather than a drive-by.
close_reason: Landed in PR #7425. :live deleted; live? is (contains? (:b->subs idx) b) and stats' :boundaries counts the forward-edge map. No complexity change either way (contains?/count are the same ops on a PersistentHashMap as on a PersistentHashSet). No byte figure claimed - shell-axis term, nothing measured. Derivability proved by liveness-is-the-forward-edge-entry-and-there-is-no-second-record-of-it, which walks the reachable values and also pins the index value to exactly #{:sub->bs :b->subs}. Mutation-proven twice (exit 1, 13 and 79 named failures), both reverted byte-identically. Two bead corrections: architecture.md needed NO edit (it never names :live), and the stats :boundaries site lives in arm1/runtime.cljs not in the index ns. Gates on 10c073f5e8: test:cljs exit 0 (12472/62526), test:browser exit 0 (1040/6468); fast-PR spine exit 0 on 11800137e6.

value:
UNBLOCKING A BEAD DOES NOT MEAN ITS PLAN IS STILL RIGHT — THE BLOCKER OFTEN CHANGED THE ANSWER (rf2-fwp31, 2026-08-03).

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-fwp31 was to record the free :scope tag's off-box egress rule in spec/009. It was BLOCKED on rf2-hzcv8. When rf2-hzcv8 merged (PR #7419) I treated it as simply unblocked and dispatched the bead's plan. But rf2-hzcv8 IS THE THING THAT CHANGED THE RULE: it made ssr/redact-value pick its payload by classification, so the identity map now tokenizes to a CONTENT-FREE shape token, not the content-addressed digest the bead described. Only :omit keeps a digest.

So the bead's text — and my brief, which repeated it — asserted that distinct scopes keep distinct digests and PER-SCOPE JOINS SURVIVE OFF-BOX. That is FALSE on main, and the redactor's own docstring says so: 'Preserving JOINS is not a reason to emit one — that is the trade rf2-hzcv8 settles.' Writing it in would have made a NORMATIVE SPEC PAGE FALSE, which is worse than the gap it was fixing.

WHAT SAVED IT: the brief said 'VERIFY EACH CLAUSE AGAINST THE CODE, NOT THE BEAD — if they disagree, the CODE wins and you report the divergence.' The worker read trace_egress.cljc and ssr.cljc, found the 1-arity path, and recorded content-free instead. It also caught a second error neither the bead nor I named: the sentence said 'a RESOLVED concrete scope', missing the clear-scope warning row whose :scope is UNRESOLVED.

THE RULE: WHEN A BLOCKER CLEARS, RE-DERIVE THE BLOCKED BEAD'S ANSWER FROM THE POST-BLOCKER TREE. A bead blocked on a decision was, by construction, written BEFORE that decision. The likeliest thing the decision changed is the very thing the bead was waiting to record. Treat 'unblocked' as 'now re-plannable', never as 'now executable as written'.

COROLLARY FOR BRIEFS: never paraphrase a technical clause out of a bead into a brief as if it were established. Either quote it as the bead's CLAIM and require verification, or verify it yourself first. My paraphrase inherited the bead's staleness and amplified it, because a brief reads as the mayor's instruction rather than as a bead's assertion.

title: The band ceiling's bootstrap is pooled-block, not run-preserving — 35% is not a q99 and its false-fire rate is 2.7% (rf2-ymi6j)
description:
AUDIT OF PR #7368, confirmed by independent recomputation from the COMMITTED dataset (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/ladder-ymi6j.json). Docs restated under rf2-ymi6j; this bead is the CODE half, which a docs-fenced worker must not take.

WHAT IS WRONG. ladder_band.cjs's bootstrapBand() pools all 342 block ratios from all 19 runs and then builds each synthetic 18-block run by drawing individual blocks across unrelated runs and load rungs. That destroys the run-level clustering the 18 blocks of a real run share, so it estimates a synthetic mixed-regime block sample rather than a future run. Recomputed at 200,000 draws on raw TaskDuration:

  quantile   pooled-block   run-preserving
  q50        13.0%          11.5%
  q90        19.9%          23.4%
  q95        22.7%          31.0%
  q99        29.4%          41.4%

  ceiling    P(fire) pooled   P(fire) run-preserving   observed of 19
  20%        9.8%             15.0%                    4
  25%        2.7%             9.1%                     2
  30%        0.9%             5.9%                     1
  35%        0.2%             2.7%                     0
  40%        0.06%            1.2%                     0

So 35% is the q99 of NEITHER distribution, and the advertised 0.2% tripwire rate is understated ~13x. The script already prints the correct number in its 'within-run' column (2.7%) and then argues in a source comment that the pooled column is the wider one a ceiling should be set against. It is not: pooled is narrower in the whole upper tail.

SCOPE (all code, none of it docs):
1. ladder_band.cjs — preserve run clustering in the bootstrap (draw a run, then resample its blocks), or justify a different statistically valid run-level model in the source. Correct the comment at the withinRun computation that argues the pooled estimate is the conservative one.
2. ladder_band.cjs — remove the stale sign interpretation still printed beside corr(ctl-2x/floor, floor): 'an additive c reads (2W+c)/(W+c), which FALLS as c grows, so a NEGATIVE sign is the additive signature'. Section 6 of the-band-re-calibrated.md and seam.cjs withdrew that argument; the printer did not. Across this ladder the varying quantity is W with c roughly fixed, so (2W+c)/(W+c) RISES with W and the sign carries no information.
3. Add a deterministic synthetic regression that distinguishes pooled-block from run-preserving resampling — a fixture of two clearly-different synthetic runs where the two models give different q99 by a wide margin.
4. DECIDE whether seam.cjs's BAND_CEILING moves off 0.35. A ceiling at the run-preserving q99 is ~41%. It is a judgement, not arithmetic: 35% already refuses nothing this ladder produced, and no published magnitude changes at either value (see section 8 of the page). Whatever is decided, seam.cjs's header comment currently states P(band > 35%) = 0.2% per run and must not keep saying so.

NO NEW MEASUREMENT IS NEEDED. Everything above is a recomputation over the committed compact dataset; ladder_band.cjs --from data/ladder-ymi6j.json reproduces the page digit for digit today.
close_reason:
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7428 — the CODE half. Bootstrap is run-preserving, the false 'pooling is conservative' comment and the stale corr sign line are gone, --selftest distinguishes the two models, BAND_CEILING stays at 35% with its derivation restated.

NO NEW MEASUREMENT. Recomputed from the committed dataset only; no bench driver run, no run published.

CONFIRMED, the bead's figures reproduce exactly at 200,000 draws on raw TaskDuration:
  quantile   pooled-block   run-preserving
  q50        13.0%          11.5%
  q90        19.9%          23.4%
  q95        22.7%          31.0%
  q99        29.4%          41.4%
  P(fire) at 20/25/30/35/40%: pooled 9.82/2.71/0.89/0.21/0.06%, run-preserving 15.0/9.1/5.9/2.7/1.2%, observed 4/2/1/0/0 of 19.
Frame-only run-preserving 12.5/26.2/33.1/45.9% and section 0.1's P3 row (11.3% run-preserving, 4.7% pooled) also reproduce. The script now prints EVERY bootstrap figure the docs half publishes — section 10's 'the one figure this script does not yet reproduce' is closed.

BOTH MODELS ARE PRINTED, run-preserving marked operative. The pooled column is kept because the withdrawn q99 derivation was read off it and a reader checking the retraction needs the number being retracted; its source ignores the run draw, so it consumes the same PRNG stream and still reproduces the pooled figures as first published.

BAND_CEILING STAYS AT 0.35 — a judgement, now stated as one rather than as a quantile. 25% false-fires at 9.1% per run against 35%'s 2.7%, so the 3.4x comparison the change was made for survives; 0 of 19 runs breach 35% where 2 breach 25%; moving to the genuine q99 (~41%) would RELAX the gate on the noisiest number in the table, a 1% quantile whose tail above 35% is carried by one or two of nineteen run-regimes (41.4% at 200k draws, 42.4% at 20k); and no published magnitude is adjudicated differently at either value. seam.cjs's header no longer states 0.2%. If the constant itself should move, that is an operator ruling and is left open, not taken here. seam.cjs is COMMENT-ONLY: 0 non-comment changed lines.

THE REGRESSION, mutation-proved BOTH WAYS. New 'node ladder_band.cjs --selftest', following seam.cjs's convention — no new file, no package.json or test-fast-pr.sh edit (#7423 owns those). Two fixtures covering both directions of the error: runs differing in CENTRE (run-preserving q99 0.0%, pooled invents 50.0%) and runs differing in DISPERSION, the ladder's own shape (run-preserving 41.2%, pooled 17.5% — the fixture that refutes 'pooling is at least conservative'), plus a four-seed sweep. Reinstating the defect in the operative function: all three checks FAIL, exit 1. Reverted byte-identically (blob 72417c781de6b6e60bebc646f33eefb4dd001492, git status clean): all three PASS, exit 0.

GATES. test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, PASS fast PR spine — core 2210/11510, freehand 1288/8857, CLJS node 12471/62501, all 0 failures 0 errors, 17/17 per-ns isolation. Taken on base 10c073f5e8; main then moved 7 commits, NONE touching either file, and the rebase was conflict-free. Re-taken on the rebased tree: ladder_band --selftest 0, seam.cjs 0, clock_run --selftest 0, recomputation 0 (byte-identical across repeat runs), npm run test:hicasso-compile 0 (101 lane namespaces, 0 warnings). NOTE for future workers: the first spine invocation was SIGTERM'd at the tool cap and left an .exit file reading 0 before the runner had printed any terminal line — a phantom. It was discarded and the surviving shell followed to completion; the verdict is the runner's own 'PASS fast PR spine' marker.

FILED: rf2-7cmco (P2, docs-only) — the-band-re-calibrated.md's three forward-references to this bead as OPEN work are now answered and read stale. Fenced off docs/design/hicasso/** here because #7424 owned those pages; sequence rf2-7cmco after this PR merges.

title: reagent-slim's residual 1.19-1.24x over stock Reagent is no longer in the prop pipeline — two named candidates, unpursued
description:
FOLLOW-ON FROM rf2-lhdp0 (PR pending), which took reagent-slim's whole-page hiccup walk from 1.82x stock Reagent to 1.19-1.24x on the walk_vs_reagent_app census witness (1,202 elements). Filed rather than guessed at, because rf2-lhdp0's own lesson was that the term you can name is not the term that weighs.

WHERE THE REMAINING MASS IS NOT. The per-element prop pipeline was 56% of the original gap (slim 619.4 ns/el against stock's 228.4 on the same roster, same run). After rf2-lhdp0's cuts the decomposition's cut-pipeline replica reads at or near stock's real convert-props row, so this is no longer the place to look.

TWO CANDIDATES THE CODE SUGGESTS, NEITHER COSTED:

  1. hiccup-shape allocates a 3-element PersistentVector per element — [head has-props first-child] — and every one of its five call sites destructures it immediately and discards it. has-props is (or (nil? head) (map? head)) and first-child is (+ first-pos (if has-props 1 0)); both are one expression. Stock Reagent allocates nothing here. NOTE THE COST SIDE: the helper exists so five sites ask the shape question identically (drift-proofing), and it is PUBLIC — reagent2/dom/server.cljs destructures it twice on the SSR path. Any change is an adapter-wide one, not a local one.

  2. vec-to-elem asks four (= tag :>) / :<> / :r> / :f> compares before reaching the hiccup-tag? branch that every DOM element takes. cljs.core/= is a fn call that falls through identical? to a protocol -equiv dispatch on a miss, so the common head pays four of them. keyword-identical? is the idiomatic answer and reads as 'these are keyword sentinels'; a case may be better still. Prior art in the same instrument: the CANDIDATES table's dispatch-all-ship 23.6 -> dispatch-all-stringfirst 12.3 rows are the same question asked of Hicasso's dispatch.

METHOD, and it is not optional here. Absolute ns/op in this instrument moves with the box — rf2-lhdp0's three runs differ ~2x on arms that did not change — so cost each candidate BESIDE the shipping shape in ONE process on the page's own roster, the way the SLIM DECOMPOSED table already does, and read the arm RATIO for the verdict. Two of rf2-lhdp0's costed candidates were DECLINED on those rows (a null-prototype index for the 3-name reserved roster; static reducers for the per-element closure, which needed two runs to show it has no reliable sign) — declining is the expected outcome for some of these, not a failure.

FENCES: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim + walk_vs_reagent_app. Every behaviour witnessed, no diagnostics removed, the reserved-head guard / keyword-prop warn-once / source-coord stamp all stay off the hit path. Not a Hicasso bead and not bench-lane.

title: Hicasso: no route-link, so census ports spell 106 tier-1 links as bare anchors
description:
Found porting RealWorld screens for the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51).

The census names route-link as one of the FIVE tier-1 shapes and counts 106 of them
across 85 idiomatic files. `front/intent`'s own docstring records that it deliberately
does not implement route-link ("routing-coupled, and outside this bead's three
deliverables"), and no arm has added one since.

Consequence for the roster: every author byline and every article link in
shapes/ordinary.cljs and shapes/card.cljs is spelled `[:a {:href (str "#/profile/" u)}]`,
hand-building the URL the router owns. That is a faithful port of the MARKUP and an
unfaithful port of the AUTHORING - the census author writes
`[ui/route-link {:to :realworld.profile/show :params {:username u}}]` and never sees a URL.

v0's definition of done says "the five tier-1 shapes beautiful". Four of them now have a
roster; the fifth tier-1 SYNTAX (route-link) has no Hicasso spelling at all, so it cannot
be judged beautiful or otherwise. Not blocking rf2-2rtt6.51 - filed so the gap is on the
record rather than implied by the ports.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Hicasso route-link with any present `:prefetch` fails loudly at render under the current HD-027 v0 ruling, including `:prefetch :intent`, and no declined control key reaches the anchor attrs.
- `unwrap-navigate` accepts exactly `#{:frame :payload :native? :veto}` with the existing value contracts; missing `:veto` or any extra key raises `:rf.error/hicasso-malformed-navigate`.
- Focused structural tests pin both refusals and the valid emitted form; the existing node/browser navigation witnesses remain green.
notes:
AUDIT FINDING (PR #7380, merged 2026-08-02). The implementation is complete on the intended framework-sub and route-click happy paths, but HD-027's fail-loud boundary is not closed in two places:

1. `front/route_link.cljs` explicitly declines `:prefetch :intent` for v0, yet `control-keys` omits `:prefetch`. The props map goes through routing's `link-model`, which validates and accepts `:intent`; Hicasso installs none of routing's prefetch handlers and then retains `:prefetch` in passthrough attrs. The result silently does no prefetching and leaks a stray DOM attribute.

2. HD-027 says `[::h/navigate MAP]` carries exactly `:frame`, `:payload`, `:native?`, and `:veto`. `unwrap-navigate` validates only the value types of the first three; a map missing `:veto`, or carrying extra keys, passes despite the promised closed grammar and malformed-navigate diagnostic.

Keep the repair small: under the current zero-census-site v0 ruling, reject any present `:prefetch` at render rather than implementing the trio; require the navigate map's exact four-key set. If HD-027 is deliberately changed to support prefetch, implement routing's full three-handler behavior rather than silent passthrough.
close_reason: PR #7429: closed the two fail-open seams the #7380 audit found in HD-027's boundary. (1) unwrap-navigate now asserts the EXACT key set #{:frame :payload :native? :veto} rather than the value types of three known keys, so a map missing :veto or carrying a fifth key raises :rf.error/hicasso-malformed-navigate; existing value contracts preserved. (2) route-link refuses any PRESENT :prefetch at render (:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined, contains? not truthiness), before the link model is consulted -- prefetch NOT implemented, HD-027's v0 decline unchanged. Mutation-proved in all three directions on the 12474-test node lane: dropping :veto from the key set, swapping the exact-set check for presence tests, and swapping contains? for truthiness each turn a named refusal green; baseline 0 failures; every revert byte-identical. Gates: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (jvm+node classified), npm run test:browser exit 0 (1040 tests). decisions.md HD-027 gained two enforcement clauses; no ruling changed, no spec/ touched.

value:
THE SHARED SCRATCHPAD IS A CONFIRMED CROSS-WORKER HAZARD — TWO INDEPENDENT HITS IN ONE HOUR (2026-08-03).

The per-session agent scratchpad is shared by EVERY concurrent worker on the box. Generic gate-artefact names collide, and the collision produces a plausible WRONG verdict rather than an obvious error.

HIT 1 (rf2-e7zxb): a sibling clobbered its fastpr.log mid-write — a NUL gap, TWO contradictory summaries, a bogus surface classification, and FAIL lines for surfaces its diff never touched. Later its pr-body.md was overwritten with a different worker's PR text.

HIT 2 (rf2-2rtt6.54), and this one is worse: a sibling's test-fast-pr.sh run TRUNCATED its fastpr.log AND WROTE THE fastpr.exit ITS WAITER THEN READ. The stale exit 0 carried 'jvm=false node=false' — a run that SKIPPED THE VERY LANE the change needed. It caught this only because its branch diff obviously contained .cljs files, so a node=false classification was impossible for its own work.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS: exit 0 from someone else's run is indistinguishable from your own pass unless you check the run's SURFACE CLASSIFICATION against your own diff. This is the same family as the pipe's exit status and the SIGTERM'd wrapper's exit 0 — the instrument reporting on something other than your subject.

THE RULES:
• PREFIX every scratchpad filename with your bead id (rl54-fastpr.log), or write gate artefacts INSIDE your own worktree — *.log and *.exit are both gitignored now, so worktree-local leaves no reap-blocking residue.
• BEFORE BELIEVING ANY LOG OR EXIT FILE, CONFIRM IT IS YOURS: check its classification line against your own diff (does the surface it claims to have run match what you changed?), and check its timestamps.
• A gate run that reports skipping the lane your diff touches is NOT a pass, whatever its exit code.

ALSO OBSERVED IN HIT 2: the harness RE-EXECUTED a backgrounded command, leaving two spine invocations rooted in one worktree. The worker found both by process ancestry and killed the older before either reached the CLJS lane. Check by ancestry, not by assumption — two spines share one .shadow-cljs and produce phantom failures.

title: The hicasso compile gate is dev-mode only: :advanced-only breakage in an unrun arm is still ungated
description:
Follow-up to rf2-2rtt6.73, which armed the lane's build door and added a PR-time compile gate (npm run test:hicasso-compile, in the cljs CI job).

THE REMAINING GAP, stated so it is not re-derived.

The PR gate runs a DEV-MODE 'shadow-cljs compile' of all 101 lane namespaces. That catches the class rf2-2rtt6.73 was filed for (:undeclared-var from a renamed/deleted def, a dropped require, a bad arity) because those resolve before optimization, and it is cheap (~30s).

What it does NOT catch is breakage that only appears under :advanced — the mode the drivers actually measure and publish from. Closure renaming, externs-inference faults, and the shadow-js module-index class rf2-2rtt6.20 documents are all :advanced-time. lane_build.cjs DOES refuse those, but only on a driver run someone performs by hand. So an arm nobody has run since it broke can still be :advanced-broken with every gate green.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN rf2-2rtt6.73: an :advanced release of all 101 namespaces in one module is not representative of any real arm build (no arm compiles the union), and doing it per-arm is ~15 builds x ~40s = 10min — a nightly cost, not a PR one.

LIKELY SHAPE, if taken: a NIGHTLY job that releases each arm's own :init-fn through the existing drivers' config-merge path (so each build is the real shape), judged by lane_build.cjs, which already refuses warnings. Wire into expensive-tests.yml rather than the PR spine.

ALSO UNCOVERED, recorded here rather than as its own bead: the ~15 driver .cjs files themselves are compiled/linted by nothing. Only lane_build.cjs's parser has a test (lane_build.test.cjs).
notes:
Verdict PR (comment-only correction, NOT a gate): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7430

GATES: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with its own terminal marker 'PASS fast PR spine' confirmed in the log (not inferred from the wrapper's exit code); npm run test:hicasso-compile exit 0 pre-rebase AND re-run exit 0 after rebasing onto main past #7425, which touches this lane. 101 lane namespaces / 0 warnings both times.
close_reason:
NOT WORTH BUILDING — verified negative. The nightly :advanced gate was NOT built, and no per-arm or partial gate was built either. This bead's premise was TESTED rather than assumed and all three legs of it fail.

MEASURED FIRST, so the cost is on the record (one Windows box, .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench cleared before each build because the lane's cache rule requires it — so no warm reuse is available between arms):

  dev compile, all 101 lane namespaces (the existing PR gate)   77s   0 warnings
  :advanced release, ONE arm (parity-probe-app)                 64s   0 warnings
  :advanced release, all 101 namespaces in one module          132s   0 warnings

The bead priced per-arm at ~15 builds x 40s. The real count is 25 -main entry points, and a cold-cache :advanced release is 64s here, so per-arm is ~27 minutes local, more on CI. But COST IS NOT WHY IT WAS REJECTED — coverage is. Even the 132s one-module release was rejected.

WHY. The bead states 'Closure renaming, externs-inference faults, and the shadow-js module-index class rf2-2rtt6.20 documents are all :advanced-time'. Each one:

1. EXTERNS INFERENCE IS ALREADY GATED AT PR TIME, IN DEV. :infer-externs :auto is shadow-cljs's OWN default-compiler-options (shadow/build/api.clj), and shadow/build/compiler.clj binds :infer-warning into ana/*cljs-warnings* for every non-jar source in BOTH modes — it is not a release-only pass. MUTATION-PROVED, and deliberately NOT with an :undeclared-var: in parity_probe_app.cljs, (some-> e .-message) (a known extern) became (some-> e .-hicassoAdvProbeZz) (an unknown property on an untyped binding), which under :advanced is renamed and reads undefined at the call site.
     :advanced release, mutated -> 'Build completed. (392 files, 332 compiled, 1 warnings)', WARNING #1 - :infer-warning, 'Cannot infer target type in expression (. G__31147 -hicassoAdvProbeZz)', File: ...parity_probe_app.cljs:52:33.
     npm run test:hicasso-compile (THE EXISTING DEV GATE), same mutated tree -> EXIT 1, same WARNING #1 - :infer-warning, '[hicasso-compile] BUILD REFUSED — :hicasso-bench compiled with 1 warning(s)', in 45s.
   Same catch, half the wall clock. The nightly would have added nothing. check-examples-compile.cjs already listed 'an externs-inference miss' among the classes ITS dev compile catches — compile_gate.cjs's LIMITS block was the outlier, and this bead was filed off that outlier.
   Reverted byte-identically: sha256 6c4983ae2a2f8d49decc61c7e2629029e2e08dbf93bc38c26eca6bd94d36bd86 before and after, git status clean, dev gate exit 0 at 101 namespaces / 0 warnings.

2. CLOSURE RENAMING FAULTS EMIT NO COMPILER DIAGNOSTIC AT ALL, in any mode. A release of a program that will die on a renamed property still exits 0 with 0 warnings. No build gate reaches them; EXECUTION does.

3. THE rf2-2rtt6.20 CLASS IS EXPLICITLY NOT BUILD-OBSERVABLE. That bead's own words: the poisoned shadow-js index 'COMPILES CLEANLY and then produce[s] an :advanced bundle that DIED ON ITS FIRST EXECUTION'. Its fix is lane_cache.cjs, already called by every driver and by the compile gate.

WHAT IS LEFT for an :advanced BUILD over lane sources is Closure hard errors, and that class is empty by construction: no lane source uses js* (no unparsed JS for Closure to reject); the only npm modules the lane requires directly are react, react-dom and react-dom/client, which test:bundle-isolation, test:perf-bundle, test:elision and test:ui-g1 already push through shadow-js under :advanced; and Closure type checking is off by shadow's default (:closure-warnings {:check-types :off}).

So NO FAULT COULD BE CONSTRUCTED that the nightly would catch and the existing gate would miss. A gate nobody can make fire is the fail-open class this lane keeps repairing, not a repair of it — which is why a partial/published-arms-only variant was rejected too: a cheaper slice of zero marginal coverage is still zero. Also worth stating: the one-module release's namespace set is a SUPERSET of every arm's, so per-arm 'representativeness' buys nothing for a BUILD check — it matters only for an artefact you intend to RUN.

THE RESIDUAL, STATED HONESTLY AND NOT CLOSED: an arm nobody has run since it broke can still be :advanced-broken AT RUNTIME with every gate green. That is real. The only instrument that reaches it is a BOOT of each arm's release bundle — ~30 min nightly across 25 arms, plus a per-arm sentinel contract because the drivers' completion protocols differ. Judged out of proportion to a P3 residual; recorded as NOT TAKEN rather than overlooked, so the option survives this close.

SHIPPED: a comment-only correction to compile_gate.cjs replacing the false LIMITS claim with the measurements above, so this is not re-derived a third time. Zero executable lines changed, one file, NO .github/workflows/* edit and NO implementation/shadow-cljs.edn edit.

CARRIED FORWARD: the bead's secondary item (the driver .cjs files are linted by nothing) is now rf2-2rtt6.78. Checked and re-scoped — there is no eslint config anywhere in the repo, so the gap is repo-wide (~50 implementation/scripts/*.cjs are in the same position), not lane-specific.

title: arm1/dogfood's UIx comparator inherits the controlled-input implementation instead of pinning it
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2rtt6.41's adapter-pin leak (audit defect 2).

implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test.cljs mounts a UIx comparator (uix-mount! at :106, rendering re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.dogfood-uix/root) whose screen mints two UIx :input elements (dogfood_uix.cljs:109 .new-input, :144 .draft). the-two-live-renderings-dispatch-the-same-intents-on-the-same-interactions (:398) then drives a 16-step type-into!/keydown! script through exactly those two fields and compares the intents against Hicasso's.

The namespace never pins uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?*. So WHICH of the two controlled-input implementations the comparator is comparing against is inherited, not chosen. Today it inherits false from re-frame.adapter.uix's load-time pin (rf2-heqwo) and is therefore correct — but only because the adapter pins it, not because this row asked.

MEASURED, not inferred: with the pin cleared (the rf2-2rtt6.41 defect, reproduced as a mutation), the whole dogfood namespace stayed GREEN while those two fields were built by Reagent's rAF-driven port rather than React's controlled input. The parity gate did not notice which product it was comparing against. That is the rf2-n3dxw fault mode - a green row measuring the port and reading it as React.

Remedy (small): pin explicitly in dogfood_dom_cljs_test, restoring the adapter default on the way out, the way arm1/controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test and hicasso/controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test now both do. Surface B, test-only, one namespace.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7431. arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test's :each fixture now pins adapter-default-implementation going in, and pin-is-adapters-default! reads the var back in the teardown — where it must live, because a row that leaves the pin elsewhere breaks LATER namespaces in the shared cljs.test runtime and never itself. title: hicasso: read_profile_app's local cell copy is no longer faithful — it still mints a watch keyword per cell
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2 (the 415/499 B/read gap).

`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/read_profile_app.cljs`
lines 361-414 carry a deliberate LOCAL COPY of the commit half
`arm1.runtime/make-subscribe` performs, and its docstring calls it a
"Faithful copy". It mints one watch key per cell:

    (def ^:private !local-watch-counter (volatile! 0))
    ... wk (keyword "rf-readprof" (str "w" (vswap! !local-watch-counter inc)))
    ... "watchKey" wk

rf2-aqgr2 removed exactly that mint from the runtime it copies
(`arm1/runtime.cljs`: one namespaced constant `cell-watch-key`, no
counter, no `watchKey` field), because the uniqueness it bought was
already structural — at most one cell per (frame, query), so no two cells
ever hold the same reaction. Measured saving on the per-read heap ladder:
-107 B/read (Reagent segment), -108 (UIx).

So the profiler now prices a cell shape the runtime no longer builds:
one Keyword, its name string and its fully-qualified string per cell, on
a per-read path, plus one extra field on the cell object. read_profile is
a CLOCK instrument (µs/read), not a heap one, so the drift shows up in
its phase-B stub deltas (C-FULL / C-NOWATCH / C-NOSUB / C-NOINDEX /
C-NOMAP) rather than in bytes — but the C-NOWATCH delta in particular is
now measuring "watch + disposal hook + a keyword mint" against a runtime
that mints nothing.

NOT fixed in rf2-aqgr2's PR deliberately: changing a timing instrument
moves its own published rows, and this worker had no mandate to re-take
them. The repair is small (a single `::rp-cell-watch` constant, keeping
its own namespace so it cannot collide with the runtime's watches on the
same cached reactions) but it should land with whoever re-runs the
profile and restates any row that moved.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7431. read_profile_app's commit-local! now installs one ::rp-cell-watch constant, mirroring arm1/runtime.cljs's own cell-watch-key (rf2-aqgr2, f7fd0c6a52); the !local-watch-counter and the cell's watchKey field are gone.

NO PUBLISHED CLOCK ROW MOVES — checked, not assumed, and this corrects the bead's own diagnosis. The bead expected the C-NOWATCH delta to be 'measuring watch + disposal hook + a keyword mint'. It was not: wk was bound UNCONDITIONALLY, before the (when-not (identical? mode C-NOWATCH)) guard, so the mint was present in every mode and appeared on BOTH sides of all four published phase-B deltas in the-cold-read-mount-term.md §1 (c-local minus c-nosub / c-noindex / c-nomap / c-nowatch). It cancelled exactly. No row was re-taken and none is restated.

The one published figure that does involve c-local absolutely is the 'copy fidelity c-local/commit = 0.9718' cell, whose OTHER term was already re-based by rf2-aqgr2's merged runtime change independently of this work. Filed as rf2-gttif (P3, blocked on this bead), scope pinned to that single cell.

value:
A BACKGROUNDED GATE CAN RUN IN ANOTHER WORKER'S WORKTREE AND GRADE THEIR DIFF (rf2-g2mxd, 2026-08-03).

THE MECHANISM, and it is the most dangerous false-green found this week. A worker backgrounded its spine as:

    cd <its own worktree> && sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh

THE `cd` DID NOT SURVIVE BACKGROUNDING. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh derives spine_root/diff_root from BASH_SOURCE[0], so a RELATIVE invocation adopts whatever cwd the shell actually has. The run executed entirely inside a DIFFERENT live worker's worktree (slimresid-e7zxb), classified THAT worker's diff, and produced the two-concurrent-spines signature — 13 phantom test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test failures — inside someone else's checkout.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE OTHER FALSE GREENS: the result is a REAL colour attached to SOMEONE ELSE'S DIFF. Not a truncated log, not a stale exit code — a complete, internally consistent run that graded the wrong work. The only visible symptom was a foreign path in an mkdocs INFO line NINETY LINES DOWN.

THE RULES:
• INVOKE BACKGROUNDED GATES BY ABSOLUTE PATH: sh /abs/path/to/worktree/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh — never 'cd X && sh scripts/...' for anything backgrounded.
• BEFORE BELIEVING A GATE, CHECK THE ROOT IT RESOLVED, not just its exit code. If the log names a path that is not your worktree, the run is not yours.
• Cross-check its SURFACE CLASSIFICATION against your own diff — a run reporting jvm=false node=false when your diff is full of .cljs is grading something else. (That is how a sibling caught a different collision the same hour.)

PROPOSED REPO FIX, on rf2-g2mxd: have the spine echo its RESOLVED ROOT as line 1 of its output, so the mismatch is visible immediately instead of ninety lines down.

FAMILY: this joins the pipe's exit status, the SIGTERM'd wrapper's exit 0, the shared-scratchpad clobber, the two-valued probe, and the ungated bench lane. The general form is THE INSTRUMENT REPORTED ON SOMETHING OTHER THAN YOUR SUBJECT — and the defence is always the same: verify the instrument was pointed at you before believing its verdict.

title: hicasso: attack the interpreter-walk mount cost — the located deficit is 100% script, +1.06ms where uix pays +0.38ms on byte-identical DOM
description:
THE OPTIMISATION LANE'S PRIMARY TARGET, opened under the operator's 2026-08-02 directive ('keep going on the actual implementation, the optimisation can happen in parallel').

WHERE THE DEFICIT LIVES, from three independent measurements that agree:
  - rf2-0qj9w located it: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. The runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements.
  - rf2-emvod/rf2-yd52q: taskNet reads every gated pair 0.98-1.08 — the gap is ENTIRELY script, zero frame.
  - rf2-2rtt6.56 (census rows): typical census shape 1.16-1.22x vs UIx (instrument-limited at the 1.10 line); worst case 1.3053x on the ONE-BOUNDARY 1,202-element page — the pure interpreter-walk shape. The deficit scales with elements-per-boundary, not boundaries.
  - rf2-2rtt6.31 (HD-008 re-take): donor arms show the same ~10-13% interpreter cost over UIx at their shapes.

SO THE TARGET IS THE PER-ELEMENT COST OF THE HICCUP WALK: parse/classify/convert per element per mount. The one-boundary page (1,202 elements, one commit) is the acceptance shape — it currently FAILS the 1.10x line at 1.3053x [1.1044-1.4660] with an 18.7% margin clearing a 6.7% band; the census feed is the guard shape (it must not regress from 1.1646x).

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, to be costed not assumed — and the PRIOR-ART DIRECTIVE applies in full (mine Freehand, re-frame.ui, Replicant, Reagent, UIx; cite taken/declined):
  1. CACHE THE STATIC SKELETON: most census markup is static per view; Replicant and every compiled substrate exploit this. re-frame.ui's compiler shows what static extraction buys; the question is what a RUNTIME can cache keyed on the hiccup's identity without a compiler (fences: no compiler, no analyzer — but a value-keyed cache at the codec is neither).
  2. CHEAPEN THE PER-ELEMENT PATH: prop-map conversion, keyword->string, intent classification — profile first, the walk has never been profiled element-by-element.
  3. AMORTISE ACROSS COMMITS: the walk re-runs per render; the memo wrapper (HD-026, #7375 pending) already stops child re-walks — what remains is the FIRST walk, which is what mount prices.
  Reagent's own answer (interpret once into a render fn, cache on the component) and UIx's (macro-compile to createElement at build time — unavailable to us by fence) bracket the space.

FENCES, all standing: Surface B; no compiler, no analyzer, no candidate ledger, no ViewCell graph; <=2-hook shell; subscribe closes over the read set alone; Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's codec — a cache AROUND the codec is in scope, a fork OF it needs a ruling.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: the full instrument canon (raw TaskDuration, quiet box, absolutes+ratios, B/E/Q, bands, blob provenance, discarded-if-died, announced windows). Profile and optimise in the implementation lane; PUBLISHED rows only on the clock of record against same-run donors. An optimisation claiming X% must show it on the one-boundary acceptance shape AND show the feed did not regress.

AN HONEST NEGATIVE IS AN ANSWER: if the walk is irreducible within the fences, say so with the profile — that converts 'the interpreter is slow' into 'the interpreter costs exactly this, here', which is what a ship/kill decision needs.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The local baseline owns the pre-PR convert-prop-value implementation, and no helper changed by the candidate leaks into the baseline. 2. Re-run the diagnostic interleaved profile with the guard clean and publish corrected old/new and phase figures. 3. Correct the studio page and Bead close record while preserving the unchanged clock-of-record results and their verdicts.

The production codec optimisation survives review, but the post-change diagnostic A/B does not have the frozen pre-change baseline the landed record claims. walk_profile_app.cljs:269-270 implements walk-value by calling codec/convert-prop-value; this PR changes that shipping function to put string? first. than when it was taken. NONE OF THOSE NEED RE-TAKING.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. Re-take the `commit` and `c-local` arms of phase B and
restate the two absolutes plus the share columns on both sections. Nothing
else on the page moves.

SIZE OF THE PRIZE, so nobody over-invests: 141 keyword mints per commit
against a phase-B grid that resolves to 0.025 ms/commit (raw 0.1 ms clock
/ 4 frames per window). The instrument's own micro table prices its
nearest anchor - a two-element vector mint - at 53 ns. So the drift is

PRECONDITION FOR DISPATCH: a quiet box. Absolute figures on the Hicasso
bench rigs moved by roughly 2x run-to-run on UNCHANGED arms under
