title: Hicasso: count the fibers behind the memo wrapper's 2x instrument disagreement
description:
rf2-2rtt6.58 measured HD-026's memo wrapper at ~+100 B per boundary on the R=0
shell (p0_run.cjs --only ladder). The page-chrome row (rf2-2rtt6.52,
chrome_run.cjs) measured the SAME wrapper at +195/+220 B per boundary. Both
reproduce on their own instrument, so the ~2x disagreement is real and belongs to
the shapes rather than to a bad run.

LEADING EXPLANATION, PUBLISHED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT AS A RESULT: React's
double buffering. The ladder MOUNTS AN ARM AND HOLDS IT with no writes, so only
the current tree exists and a memo wrapper costs one extra fiber. The page-chrome
instrument performs its four write ops BEFORE reading heap, and an updated
component retains an `alternate` fiber beside its current one — so a wrapper
position there can be holding two. Roughly 2x is what that predicts, and roughly
2x is what the two instruments differ by.

It was deliberately NOT claimed, because neither run counted fibers.

DO: count them. A heap snapshot on each instrument, classifying FiberNode objects
by tag (MemoComponent vs the boundary's own) and by whether an alternate is
present, would settle it outright. If confirmed, the general statement the
programme should carry is that a memo wrapper costs ONE fiber on a held tree and
TWO on a tree that has been updated — which is a per-shape rule, not a constant,
and it changes how any future Fiber cost is quoted.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3: the adjudication rf2-2rtt6.58 was filed for does not depend on
it. Both numbers are measured and both are published against the shape they were
taken on. This is about being able to state WHY, and about not quoting either
figure onto the other's shape by accident.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md,
subsection "Why this instrument reads half of what the card-shaped one did".
close_reason: PR #7433. VERIFIED NEGATIVE — closed WITHOUT the fiber count, because the count is not needed. VERDICT: the PREDICTION (the published hypothesis) was wrong; both instruments are right. The double-buffering explanation rested on the page-chrome rig writing before it reads heap, and it does not: chrome_run.cjs:242-243 runs heapForArms to completion first, under the comment 'the heap half, first, on a quiet page', and the clock half's runOp calls do not begin until line 264; heapOnce (164-182) is resetRuntime -> baseline -> mountArm -> held, with nothing between the mount and the read. Byte-identical ordering at cb179b6b3c, the commit that published +195/+220, verified by git show. The ladder's own window (p0_run.cjs:588-593) is gc/pre-read/mountOne/gc/held-read. BOTH INSTRUMENTS MOUNT AND HOLD, so no alternate fiber exists on either, and the general rule this bead proposed — one fiber held, two updated — is NOT adopted: no measurement on this programme has read an updated tree's wrapper. Corrected in all three places it was published (the ladder subsection, the page-chrome page's 2026-08-02 correction block, HD-028 in decisions.md), struck through rather than deleted. Every measured figure stands; only the account of WHY was wrong. The ~2x itself remains open as rf2-2rtt6.79, which asks the fiber count on a different question: is the wrapper ONE fiber on both shapes, i.e. is the difference in what a fiber HOLDS rather than how many there are. No quiet box needed — snapshot classification is structural.

title: bench: write-attribution's SMI control reads 2x its own prediction (16.11 B/slot, not 8)
description:
FOUND while diagnosing rf2-xu0ma, on node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false.

write-attribution's SMI control is a .slice() of a PACKED SMI array. A tagged slot is 8 B with pointer compression OFF, so a D=100 copy is predicted at 32 (JSArray) + 16 (FixedArray header) + 800 = 848 B, and D=200 at 1648.

MEASURED (5 windows each, 0 unverified of 5):
  SMI D=100   1681.7 B/copy   predicted 848   +98.31%
  SMI D=200   3293.5 B/copy   predicted 1648  +99.85%

Almost exactly 2x, at both sizes, so the printed ';; SMI slope, SMALL pair (100->200) 16.1146 B/slot' is 2x the 8 B it is checked against.

WHAT IT IS NOT.
- NOT rf2-xu0ma's boxed HeapNumber. The SMI arms store an Smi, which does not box, and the 2x is unchanged after that fix landed (measured on both sides of it).
- NOT a window-size effect: the same figure comes back at reps=590 (~1 MB window) and reps=2193 (~3.6 MB).
- NOT a misread of the pointer-compression regime. The DBL pair beside it lands at +0.04% against 8.0000 B/double, and the SMI readout's own threshold is (< si 6.0), so 16.11 still answers OFF, which is correct for node.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY IT IS P3. Nothing published rests on the SMI absolute: the pair exists to READ OFF the pointer-compression regime, and it gets that right. But it is the one control on this surface whose prediction is not met, and the whole discipline of the harness is predicted-vs-measured. Either the prediction is wrong (in which case the comment stating 8 B/slot should be corrected) or the arm is not measuring what it says.

FIRST THING TO CHECK: whether packed-smis' .push construction leaves the template with backing-store capacity beyond its length, and whether V8's .slice() fast path copies capacity rather than length for PACKED_SMI_ELEMENTS but not for PACKED_DOUBLE_ELEMENTS.

Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.xu0ma-probe-postfix.log (local-only), PROBE 2.
Reproduce: npx shadow-cljs release ui-bench --config-merge '{:main re-frame.bench.write-attribution/-diagnose :output-to "out/wa-diagnose.js"}' then node --expose-gc out/wa-diagnose.js

Fence: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/**.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7230 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: PR #7230 adds the right absolute SMI/DBL readout and current healthy runs exercise it, but adds no negative-path proof that a broken calibration makes the benchmark non-reportable. Every listed gate uses values inside the expected bands, so the newly introduced failure branch is never adjudicated.

CORRECTNESS: when the SMI/DBL ratio is outside both 0.95–1.05 and 0.45–0.55, the harness prints `*** NEITHER — the SMI arm is not measuring a tagged-slot copy ***`. That result does not feed any refusal state. The only assignment of process exit code 2 remains behind `guard/verdict`'s arm-order refusal. Thus the exact recurrence this bead exists to catch — a shared/changed call site making the SMI control invalid — can still end with exit 0 and an order `VERDICT: reportable`, despite the calibration explicitly saying the instrument is not measuring its stated control.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: retain the useful paired measurement and deliberate per-kind factory duplication. Compute one calibration-refusal boolean from the already printed SMI ratio/slope evidence, combine it with the existing order refusal for the final exit code/verdict, and add a small hermetic failure-path check with injected ratios. Do not turn the known large-object DBL deviation into a gate or build a broader benchmark framework; this owner only needs its own invalid-control state to fail closed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7238 (2026-08-01) — UPDATED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: The new read_attribution_cljs.cljs copies this control protocol onto the CLJS read-path instrument, but adds no negative-path witness that an invalid small SMI calibration makes a run non-reportable. The 69 passing CI checks exercise only healthy recorded values.

CORRECTNESS: At the merged commit and current origin/main, the SMI/DBL ratio branch prints `*** NEITHER — the SMI arm is not measuring a tagged-slot copy ***` without contributing to refusal state. Only arm-order refusal or nonzero read-back verification sets process exitCode 2. Consequently this second harness can also exit 0 and print an arm-order `VERDICT: reportable` after its own calibration says it is not measuring the stated control. This is the same failure mode already owned here, not a new issue.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: Extend this owner fence to implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs. Derive a calibration-refusal boolean from the existing small SMI ratio/slope evidence, make it participate in final nonzero exit status, and add a hermetic invalid-ratio check. Preserve the deliberately separate SMI/DBL factories and do not gate the documented large-object DBL tail.
close_reason: PR #7433. VERDICT: the INSTRUMENT was wrong, not the prediction — already settled in 4231917178 (one arm-ctl body over both template kinds gave the harness a single polymorphic .slice() site; a PACKED_SMI receiver there loses the clone fast path and allocates its elements store twice, 16.11 vs a tagged slot's 8). What this PR closes is the audit reopening: the NEITHER branch printed and nothing consumed it, so a run could exit 0 under 'VERDICT: reportable' with its own control saying it was not measuring a tagged-slot copy. New re-frame.bench.calibration turns the ratios + slope into a boolean (ratio names a regime / sizes agree / slope within 25% of the width THE RATIOS selected — not one read off the slope, which cannot see a doubled slope at all). Both write_attribution and read_attribution_cljs now exit 2 on the OR of their refusals and run the calibration self-test before measuring. DBL LARGE pair's ~+9% deliberately not gated, with a fixture pinning that. calibration_cljs_test replays the injected ratios incl. the recorded 1681.7/848 and 16.1146 under npm run test:cljs. Mutation-proved: slope-tolerance 0.25 -> 2.0 gave exactly the 8 predicted failures in exactly the 2 predicted deftests out of 12,481 tests; reverted byte-identically.

title: hicasso: the-cold-read-mount-term's commit row and copy-fidelity ratio predate rf2-aqgr2's runtime change
description:
FOUND during rf2-6wh9o, which repaired the OTHER side of the same drift.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md §1 publishes the
commit-half table:

  | whole commit (`commit`, shipping seam) | 0.8875 [0.8000-1.0750] |
    - (6.29 us/key; copy fidelity c-local/commit = 0.9718) |

Both figures in that cell were taken against an `arm1/runtime.cljs` that
minted a `Keyword` per key cell. rf2-aqgr2 (f7fd0c6a52, merged 2026-08-03)
removed that mint from the shipping commit half - it was the whole
-107/-108 B/read saving - so the `commit` arm is now cheaper than the
0.8875 the page reports, and the 0.9718 fidelity ratio compares a local
copy against a seam that no longer does what it did when the ratio was
taken.

SCOPE IS EXACTLY ONE TABLE CELL. The four DELTA rows beneath it are
unaffected and must not be re-taken on this bead's account: they are all
`c-local - variant`, the mint was bound unconditionally in `commit-local!`
(before the C-NOWATCH guard, present in every mode), so it appeared on both
sides of every delta and cancelled. Verified by reading the code, not
inferred. That is also why rf2-6wh9o could make the local copy faithful
without moving a published row.

WHAT IS NEEDED: re-take the `commit` and `c-local` arms on a quiet box and
restate the one cell, or - equally acceptable and cheaper - annotate the
cell with its provenance SHA and the note that it predates f7fd0c6a52. The
page already carries a "nothing here re-baselines the canonical witness"
disclaimer; this is a diagnostic clock, not a gate row, so an honest
provenance note may be the whole fix.

DO NOT bundle this with rf2-0qj9w or rf2-2rtt6.76. Both carry an explicit
quiet-box precondition and both are about axes this cell is not on
(rf2-0qj9w: Hicasso has no clock rows of its own; rf2-2rtt6.76: the warm
allocation slope, a heap axis). This is a stale-provenance repair on one
existing diagnostic cell.
close_reason:
Restated in PR #7434 (docs-only, two pages). NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN — every figure restated from the merged commits and the page's own arithmetic.

THE FOUR PHASE-B DELTAS REALLY DO CANCEL — confirmed against 54a2a78924's diff, not inferred: wk was bound in commit-local!'s let, ABOVE the C-NOWATCH guard, and "watchKey" sat on the cell in every mode including C-NOSUB (where r is nil and add-watch is never reached). 0.4125 / 0.0750 / 0.0375 / 0.0250 do not move.

ONE MORE ROW MOVES THAN THIS BEAD (and rf2-6wh9o's close reason) EXPECTED: the SHARE column. delta-line computes (/ d base) where base is c-local, NOT the whole commit — read_profile_app.cljs:663-666 — and c-local carried the same mint until 54a2a78924, so its absolute moved and all four shares are lower bounds. c-local recovers to 0.8625 two independent ways (0.9718 x 0.8875, and 0.4125/0.478), both on the instrument's 0.025 ms grid. The column header now names its denominator, which nothing on the page did.

NOTHING RETRACTED. 0.8875 and 6.29 us/key are real readings of a real commit; what was stale was what they claimed about today. Provenance stamp + stated direction (upper bounds), the route this bead itself offered.

ONE FIGURE GOT STRONGER. The 0.9718 copy-fidelity ratio STANDS: the mint sat on BOTH arms when it was taken and BOTH have since lost it (f7fd0c6a52 from commit, 54a2a78924 from c-local), so the perturbation is common-mode and cancels in the ratio for the same reason it cancels in the deltas — and rf2-6wh9o restored the copy to STRUCTURAL identity with the seam, a better warrant for the c-* ablations than a clock agreement alone. The window in which the ratio was genuinely broken is f7fd0c6a52 -> 54a2a78924, and it is closed.

SECOND SITE, found by grep: the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md §6(b) quotes the 0.7625 beside its own 0.827; its run closed 2026-08-03 05:28, seven hours before f7fd0c6a52. Comparison stays like-for-like, both absolutes are upper bounds, one sentence added. Also stamped: this page's own §4 re-read (0c0ff21f0d, 0.7625 + 51.9/5.6/3.7%), same figure class. No third site.

SIZE OF THE DRIFT: 141 keyword mints/commit against a phase-B grid resolving to 0.025 ms/commit (raw 0.1 ms clock / 4 frames per window — every published phase-B p50 lands on that grid or a half-step). The micro table's nearest anchor, a two-element vector mint, is 53 ns. About ONE QUANTUM; may not be resolvable on this clock at all.

FILED rf2-d360z (P3, discovered-from) — quiet-box re-take of the commit and c-local arms, in the rf2-0qj9w / rf2-2rtt6.76 precondition wording, stating that the deltas and the ratio need no re-take and the instrument must not be edited to chase it.

Gates: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (terminal marker PASS fast PR spine), both foreground. mkdocs --strict ran in the spine and verified NOTHING of this edit (exclude_docs drops design/hicasso/). Hand-verified: 2 outbound / 1 inbound links on the cold-read page, 0 outbound / 1 inbound on the sibling, 0 dead, 0 anchor fragments in play, no heading touched; 8 tables and 10 tables respectively, 0 column-count mismatches.

title: The repo has no JS linter: ~25 hicasso driver .cjs files (and ~50 implementation/scripts/*.cjs) are syntax-checked by nothing until they run
description:
CARRIED OVER from rf2-2rtt6.77's description so it survives that bead's close, and RE-SCOPED after checking: the gap is REPO-WIDE, not lane-specific.

rf2-2rtt6.77 recorded 'the ~15 driver .cjs files themselves are compiled/linted by nothing. Only lane_build.cjs's parser has a test (lane_build.test.cjs).' Verified and widened:

  * There is NO eslint config anywhere in the repo (no .eslintrc*, no eslint.config.*, no eslint dependency), and .github/workflows/lint.yml mentions no JS lane at all.
  * So the ~25 .cjs under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ are in exactly the same position as the ~50 under implementation/scripts/ — a syntax error or a typo'd require is discovered the first time someone runs the file, not by any gate.
  * The lane is therefore NOT worse off than the rest of the repo, which is why this is a repo-wide chore rather than a hicasso bug. Filing it under the hicasso epic only because that is where it was found.

CHEAPEST HONEST OPTION, if wanted: 'node --check' over every tracked *.cjs is a syntax-only pass costing milliseconds per file and needing no new dependency. It would NOT catch a bad require path, an undefined identifier, or a wrong argument — only parse errors. State that limit wherever it lands, or it becomes the fifteenth instrument that implies coverage it lacks.

FULLER OPTION: adopt eslint. That is a new toolchain, a config to maintain and a large first-run cleanup across ~75 files. Probably not worth it pre-alpha; recorded so the choice is deliberate.

NOT URGENT. No known defect has escaped through this. Filed so it is not lost.
close_reason:
BUILT — PR #7435. Verdict: worth building, at a deliberately small size.

WHAT LANDED. A hand-picked bug-class ESLint config at repo root (eslint.config.mjs) over all 206 tracked .cjs/.mjs/.js files, plus a root package.json carrying eslint+globals and nothing else, plus an 'eslint' job in lint.yml wired into the 'Lint required' aggregator. Errors block, warnings informational — same shape as clj-kondo's --fail-level error and Splint's --fail-on-errors.

NOT js.configs.recommended, and that was measured not assumed: recommended reports 148 findings across 60 files over this corpus (mostly no-empty / preserve-caught-error / no-useless-escape hygiene); the curated set reports 24 across 17, every one dead code. No style/format/quoting/import-order rule, no prettier, no type-aware config. ZERO suppressions in the tree; it also REMOVED two vestigial eslint-disable directives already sitting in story_feature_load.cjs.

DID IT FIND ANYTHING? Yes. 24 findings, 17 files, all fixed by deletion. Two beyond tidying:
  1. tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs still carried runAppDbPrivacyLarge + runConfigurePartialUpdate — 131 lines of Playwright scenario superseded by the rf2-rviu8 CLJS port and referenced by nothing, so neither had run since. tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md was STILL citing runConfigurePartialUpdate as the live home of the L-10 configure! multi-key contract — the matrix claiming coverage from a scenario the gate had stopped executing. Dead scenarios deleted; row now names configure_multi_key_e2e_cljs_test.cljs.
  2. run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs accumulated the setup child's whole stdout+stderr into two strings nothing ever read (recordChunk was always the real consumer) — unbounded growth for the life of the promise.

MUTATION-PROVEN, both directions, on a real driver, reverted byte-identically (sha1 match + empty git diff):
  FIRES (exit 1, names file:line): dead require - typo'd free identifier ('lenght' is not defined) - misspelled require binding ('pth') - syntax error (Parsing error) - unreachable code.
  DOES NOT FIRE (exit 0), now documented IN THE CONFIG so it can't imply coverage it lacks: (a) a misspelled property/method on an object that exists — console.errr passes, since no-undef resolves free identifiers and knowing .errr is not a member needs type info; (b) a require() path that does not resolve WHEN ITS BINDING IS USED — core ESLint has no module-resolution rule. Useful partial: a bad require whose binding is unread IS caught by no-unused-vars, which is the shape a dead import actually takes.

The bead's 'cheapest honest option' (node --check) was rejected: it is parse-only, and the bead itself warned that shipping it would make the fifteenth instrument implying coverage it lacks. The set here catches the parse errors node --check would, PLUS no-undef and the dead-require class, for one small config and a ~3s npm ci.

GATES. sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (terminal marker 'PASS fast PR spine', log line 939 — a first attempt via 'nohup &' returned wrapper exit 0 while truncated mid-spine and was discarded). npm run lint:js exit 0. _lint-workflow-policy.test.cjs 4 passed. lint.yml YAML parses. Detect classifier extracted from the committed YAML and driven over 10 synthetic diffs: 10/10. Clean rebase onto origin/main (+19 commits); main's three newly-changed hicasso .cjs pass as-is.

HOT ZONE. .github/workflows/lint.yml edit surgical — no existing job body moved. No collision: rf2-2rtt6.77 landed as #7430 (docs-only, verdict AGAINST the nightly :advanced job) and no open worker branch touches .github/workflows/. js_surface is a SEPARATE detect output, not another arm of lint_surface, because 'case' is first-match-wins — an arm appended after implementation/* would never be reached and an implementation-JS-only PR would skip the linter that lints it.

Also removed /package-lock.json from .gitignore: its comment stated its own premise ('there is no repo-root package.json'), which no longer holds. Deleted rather than negated with a ! exception, which would leave the stale rationale readable as if it still applied.

title: worker gates: a backgrounded relative-path gate invocation runs in ANOTHER worktree — reproduced, with the one-token fix
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-03 during rf2-6wh9o/rf2-2rtt6.75, not inferred. This is the
harness path-resolution leak CLAUDE.md already names ("mitigates observed
harness path-resolution leaks"), caught with a full log, plus a fix that costs
one token per dispatch.

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker in
C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/insttruth-6wh9o backgrounded its spine
as, verbatim:

  cd C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/insttruth-6wh9o && \
    sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > <log> 2>&1

The `cd` DID NOT TAKE in the backgrounded shell. The identical command run in
the FOREGROUND minutes earlier resolved correctly, so this is specific to
backgrounding.

WHY THAT SILENTLY RETARGETS THE GATE. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:97-99 derives
everything from its own path:

  script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  spine_root="$(cd "$script_dir/.." && pwd)"
  diff_root="$spine_root"

With a RELATIVE invocation, `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`,
so `dirname` resolves against whatever cwd the shell actually has. The run
therefore adopted a DIFFERENT worktree wholesale — as its spine root, as its
diff root, and as its classifier input.

THE EVIDENCE, from the log:
  * mkdocs:  "Building documentation to directory:
             ...\re-frame2-worktrees\slimresid-e7zxb\site"
  * story:   approved roots named ...\slimresid-e7zxb\implementation\out
  * shadow:  "config: ...\slimresid-e7zxb\implementation\shadow-cljs.edn"
  * classification: "docs=true jvm=false node=false" — slimresid's diff shape,
    not the running worker's (which is docs=false jvm=true node=true).

CONSEQUENCE, and it is BOTH directions:
  1. The verdict is meaningless — a PASS or FAIL about someone else's diff,
     reported in this worker's PR body as its own gate. A green here is a
     FALSE GREEN of the rf2-n3dxw family: the colour is real, the subject is
     not.
  2. It becomes a SECOND concurrent spine inside a live worker's checkout,
     sharing that checkout's .shadow-cljs — the configuration CLAUDE.md and
     every dispatch brief forbid. It duly produced the documented signature:
     13 phantom `re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test` failures
     (unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, red-run-replays-buffered-console-
     warn, spawn-timeout-kills-a-hanging-child, ...). The victim worker sees
     phantom reds in ITS run and has no way to know why.

BLAST RADIUS IS LIMITED, AND WORTH STATING SO NOBODY PANICS: `git status` in
the invaded worktree was CLEAN afterwards. A spine only writes gitignored
build output (out/, site/, .shadow-cljs/). No source was touched. The damage is
wasted wall-clock, phantom reds, and a verdict attributed to the wrong diff.

THE FIX (one token, no new machinery): invoke a backgrounded gate by ABSOLUTE
PATH. `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is then absolute and `spine_root`/`diff_root` are
pinned no matter what cwd the shell has.

  sh C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/<wt>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh

Verified: the same worker's third run, changed ONLY in this way, classified
correctly (docs=false jvm=true node=true), had ZERO occurrences of the foreign
worktree in its log, and reached `PASS fast PR spine` exit 0.

PROPOSED, for the mayor to rule on:
  A. Dispatch briefs' GATE MECHANICS section gains a numbered rule:
     "backgrounded gates are invoked by ABSOLUTE path — `cd` does not survive
     backgrounding, and a relative `BASH_SOURCE[0]` silently adopts another
     worktree." Same register as the existing four (no `tail` pipes, no two
     spines, artefacts to gitignored paths, foreground to completion).
  B. Cheap belt-and-braces in the script itself: have test-fast-pr.sh print
     its resolved `spine_root` as its FIRST line. Today the only way to notice
     is to catch a foreign path in an mkdocs INFO line 90 lines down. One
     echo turns a silent misfire into an obvious one, and makes it greppable
     from a PR body.
  C. Consider whether scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh should be re-run (or
     its WORKTREE_ROOT re-asserted) at GATE time, not only before the first
     edit. The existing guard fires at session start and cannot see a leak
     that happens forty minutes later.

A alone is worth doing immediately; B is a two-line change to one script and
would have made this diagnosable in seconds rather than in a log post-mortem.
close_reason: PR #7436. All eight gate scripts under scripts/ now print 'gate root: <path>' as line 1 (not just test-fast-pr.sh — the pattern was 8-wide). Proposal B implemented; proposal A landed as the fourth GATE MECHANICS rule in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md plus the matching AGENTS.md section, and both files' worked examples now spell the absolute form. Proposal C (re-assert assert-worker-worktree.sh at gate time) deliberately NOT done: the brief ruled against any guard that could refuse a legitimate run. Audit: the spine's other 15 Python checkers derive their root from Path(__file__) and are cwd-immune, so the BASH_SOURCE shell scripts were the only exposed link. Mutation-proved both directions in a throwaway tree; spine exit 0, PASS fast PR spine, 0 FAILs.

title: hicasso: the evidence seam's 'detached cost is one deref and one nil test' is false at record-reads!
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2 while reading the read path's allocation profile.
Clock/allocation axis, not retained heap, so it was out of that bead's
scope.

`front/sub_index.cljs`'s HD-005 section promises:

  "Detached cost is one deref and one nil test at each of the two tap
   points. No evidence subsystem ships..."

That holds at the `commit!` tap point. It does NOT hold at
`record-reads!`, which builds the event before it asks whether anyone is
listening:

    (when (not= held reads)
      (evidence! {:event    :edges-changed
                  :boundary boundary-id
                  :added    (set/difference reads held)
                  :dropped  (set/difference held reads)}))

`evidence!` is `(when-some [sink @!evidence-sink] (sink event))`, so the
map literal and both `set/difference` calls are evaluated on every call
whether or not a sink is attached. On Arm 1's wiring `held` is ALWAYS
`#{}` (the boundary id is the registration React mints per `subscribe`,
so a changed read set arrives as a fresh id — `arm1/runtime.cljs` clause
(b), and `the-wired-path-never-takes-the-diffs-dropping-half`), so the
`not=` guard is true for every non-empty read set and the map is built
once per boundary per commit.

The two differences are cheap on this path — `clojure.set/difference`
returns its first argument untouched when the second is empty, and `#{}`
minus anything reduces to `#{}` — so the residue is one four-entry map
per boundary per commit. Nothing is RETAINED (the sink is nil, so the map
is immediately garbage), which is why the heap ladder never saw it.

FIX: move the construction inside the nil check — a thunk, or push the
`when-some` out to the call site — and either way make the docstring's
claim true rather than aspirational. Small, and worth doing while the
claim is still only one call site out of date.
notes:
2026-08-03 — VERIFIED, NOT ACTIONED: the file is held. rf2-ixb92 is IN_PROGRESS
on `worker/subindex-dabt3`, which carries unmerged changes to this same
`front/sub_index.cljs` (plus the law suite). Per the worker fence, stopped
rather than racing it. Everything below is read-only verification from
origin/main @ 5362fdf382, done so the fix is a five-minute job for whoever
holds the file next.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED, AND UNDERSTATED. The bead says the claim "holds
at the commit! tap point". It does not — `commit!` violates it too:

    (evidence! {:event :commit
                :dirty-subs (set dirty-sub-keys)
                :dirty-boundaries dirty})

is a 3-entry map literal built unconditionally, before `evidence!` derefs the
sink. So the HD-005 docstring's "one deref and one nil test at EACH OF THE TWO
tap points" is false at BOTH, not one of two.

THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS OUT (clojurescript-1.12.42, read from the jar):

  * `clojure.set/difference` with `held = #{}`:
    `(difference reads #{})` -> `(< n 0)` false -> `(reduce disj reads #{})`
    -> reduce over an empty coll returns the init, i.e. `reads` ITSELF,
    identical, zero allocation.
    `(difference #{} reads)` -> `(< 0 n)` true -> `(reduce f #{} #{})`
    -> `#{}`, zero allocation.
    So the bead is right that both differences are free on Arm 1's wiring.

  * `cljs.core/set` on an already-meta-less set is `(with-meta coll nil)`,
    and `PersistentHashSet`'s `-with-meta` returns `coll` when the meta is
    `identical?` -- zero allocation. So `commit!`'s `(set dirty-sub-keys)` is
    free too, and its residue is likewise exactly one map literal.

DETACHED RESIDUE, TOTAL: one 4-entry PersistentArrayMap per boundary per
commit (`record-reads!`), plus one 3-entry PersistentArrayMap per commit
(`commit!`). Nothing is retained -- the sink is nil, so both are immediately
garbage, which is why the per-read heap ladder never saw them.

RECOMMENDED FIX (and it makes the file SMALLER, not larger). Do not use a
thunk: `(evidence! #(hash-map ...))` allocates a closure capturing the same
locals, so it trades a map for an object and the claim stays false. Push the
`when-some` out to the two call sites and drop the `evidence!` indirection --
the indirection is precisely what hides the cost:

    (defn- evidence-sink [] @!evidence-sink)

    ;; record-reads!  (sink test FIRST -- it is the cheaper guard, and
    ;;                 putting it outside is what makes the claim literal)
    (when-some [sink (evidence-sink)]
      (when (not= held reads)
        (sink {:event :edges-changed :boundary boundary-id
               :added (set/difference reads held)
               :dropped (set/difference held reads)})))

    ;; commit!
    (when-some [sink (evidence-sink)]
      (sink {:event :commit :dirty-subs (set dirty-sub-keys)
             :dirty-boundaries dirty}))

Both guards are side-effect-free, so hoisting the sink test above the
`not=` is behaviour-preserving. The ns docstring's "Three lines -- a holder,
a setter, and a nil-checked emit" needs restating to match (holder, setter,
accessor; the nil check moves to the tap points), and that sentence is
adjacent to the data-model paragraph rf2-ixb92 is rewriting -- another reason
these two want sequencing rather than parallelism.

VERDICT: worth doing (it is a load-bearing HD-005 design claim, not
decoration, and the repair removes indirection rather than adding it), but it
belongs in the same hand as rf2-ixb92 or immediately after it merges.

Deleted the evidence! indirection and moved its when-some out to record-reads! and commit!, so the nil test is now the outermost form at each tap point. Avoided the thunk trap (a closure captures the same locals and leaves the claim false). Net +1 line, one fewer defn, detached path strictly cheaper. value:
THE SUBSTITUTE FOR "MONITOR ARMED, WAITING" IS A FOREGROUND UNTIL-LOOP THAT BLOCKS IN-TURN (rf2-e3i6y worker, 2026-08-03).

SEVEN workers stranded in one day by ending a turn to wait on something outside it — a completion notification, a backgrounded gate, an armed Monitor. Prohibitions did not stop it; each worker found a new mechanism to wait on. What finally worked is a CONCRETE SUBSTITUTE ACTION, stated by the worker that used it: "I blocked IN-TURN with a foreground until-loop, which works and does not end the turn — that is the pattern that should replace 'Monitor armed, waiting'." Several workers also blocked in-turn past the 600s tool cap in repeated increments, successfully.

SO BRIEF THE SUBSTITUTE, NOT THE BAN: "if a gate outruns a single call, block in-turn with a foreground loop that re-checks the log; never end a turn expecting to be woken."

AND THE UNTIL-LOOP ITSELF CAN BE FAIL-OPEN — this is the sharp part. That worker's loop matched on '|FAIL' as its terminal alternative, and INCIDENTAL FIXTURE OUTPUT ('-> FAILED' from a POM self-test) tripped it: the loop reported MARKER SEEN while 'PASS fast PR spine' was still absent, and the spine was in fact alive at pid 550478 and later finished green. So the waiting instrument reported on the wrong string.

THE RULE THAT CATCHES IT: match ONLY the runner's own terminal marker, anchored, and never a generic failure word that fixture output can contain. Absence of the marker beats presence of anything else. This is the same family as the pipe's exit status, the SIGTERM'd wrapper's exit 0, the clobbered scratchpad, and the backgrounded gate that graded another worktree — THE INSTRUMENT REPORTED ON SOMETHING OTHER THAN THE SUBJECT — and it is worth noticing that the family now includes the tools workers write to watch their own work.

title: method: the mayor must verify a close HELD, not just that it was made
description:
docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md says to close items 'only after merge or verifiable completion' and to record close reasons concretely. It does NOT say to verify the close STUCK. That gap cost real work on 2026-08-03.

WHAT HAPPENED. Five beads closed after their PRs merged — rf2-6t03c, rf2-2rtt6.25, rf2-eane2, rf2-p0m6m, rf2-oztox — were SILENTLY BACK TO OPEN when the mayor later reread the raw list. Each had been verified CLOSED at the time. One (rf2-p0m6m) had additionally been bumped P3 -> P2, which is what made the mayor look twice. Traced through the committed .beads snapshots: rf2-oztox read status open in EVERY snapshot from 11:54 onward while bd show had returned CLOSED right after its merge. All five were from the EARLY merge window and every later close held, so it was a rollback to an earlier snapshot — the same family as rf2-rjqtj (equal-count set substitution) and rf2-51uz1 (checkout-then-reimport), and consistent with the interrupted Dolt generational GC observed the same morning.

The mayor re-verified all five PRs as MERGED with commits on main and re-closed them with evidence. Nothing was lost, but the running 'beads closed' count was overstated for part of the session, and NOTHING IN THE LOOP WOULD HAVE SURFACED IT — it was found only because the operator asked for a full reread.

WHAT TO ADD, and keep it to the register of the existing hard-won list: a tracker write can silently revert, so re-verify closes on a LATER cycle, not only at the moment you make them. Concretely, a cheap per-tick audit: re-check every bead closed this session and re-close any that reverted, with evidence.

TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH CARRYING, both learned by getting them wrong:
• AUDIT ON THE STABLE BEAD ID, never on the row UUID. Row UUIDs are regenerated on re-import, so a UUID-keyed diff reports phantom losses — it flagged three for the mayor and all three beads existed and were closed.
• PARSE THE STATUS FIELD, not the line. A first attempt grepped the whole show output and matched the substring OPEN inside a bead TITLE ('the fail-OPEN CSRF compare'), reporting a false reopen. A verification tool that misreports is the same defect class as the instruments this repo spent the day fixing.

SCOPE: docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md (the hard-won list). This is method prose only — no script, no tooling. The tracker-side fix already landed separately as rf2-rjqtj (PR #7410), which makes the checkpoint compare ids/updated_at/status instead of trusting a row count; this bead is about the MAYOR'S habit, which no script covers.
close_reason: Added one Hard-won bullet to docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md — 'A tracker write can silently revert' — placed next to the tracker-checkpoint bullet. Carries the per-cycle re-verify habit plus both audit caveats (stable item id not row UUID; parse the status field not the line). Kept general to any tracker, no script/tooling per scope. PR #7438. title: RULING: the provisional reap horizon — accept the double build on the public mount schedule, or move the timer?
description:
OPERATOR DECISION, carried forward from rf2-2rtt6.25 when that bead closed (PR #7402, 2026-08-03). rf2-2rtt6.25's audit remainder is discharged and the bead is CLOSED; this is the part of it that was never work. Filed so the decision has a home rather than living in a closed bead's notes.

THE FACT. On the PUBLIC mount schedule — rendered through re-frame.substrate.adapter/render with NO act and NO flushSync — the shipped hook BUILDS TWICE. Two acquisitions, two different reaction objects, bodyRuns 2.00N, and the cache tenant is the commit's rebuild. The setTimeout 0 reaper releases the escrowed reference before React's passive useSyncExternalStore subscribe; the entry disposes on the ordinary 1->0 edge; the commit misses and rebuilds. So the hand-off rf2-2rtt6.14 adopted delivers its benefit ONLY under forced-synchronous rendering. Pinned deterministically by assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds (numbers read from inside the probe's own mount use-effect, which React orders after the same fiber's uSES subscribe BY CONSTRUCTION).

NOTHING IS UNSOUND. The lost race costs a CONSTRUCTION and never correctness — the steady state is one durable reference either way, asserted on the public-schedule row too. Spec 006 Render-phase provisional acquisition and commit adoption already requires that correctness must not depend on the reaper losing the race, and it does not. rf2-2rtt6.13's concurrent-lane window also stays SHUT on this schedule: React's pre-commit store-consistency check runs in the SAME host task as the render, so no macrotask (the reaper included) can have run between the escrow and the check, and get-snap's escrow leg is necessarily reachable there. What the reaper beats is the PASSIVE-EFFECT FLUSH, a later task. Both rows are asserted together so a horizon repair cannot silently cost the window that is currently closed.

THE SWAP-THE-PRIMITIVE PROBE (three trials each, temporary diagnostic, not committed): setTimeout 0 (SHIPPED) = 2.00N at N=1 AND N=300. setTimeout 4 = 1.00N at both. setTimeout 32 = 1.00N at both. requestAnimationFrame = 1.00N at N=1 but 2.00N at N=300. MessageChannel = 2.00N (React posts its own message later on the same FIFO source). EVERY WINNER IS A MARGIN, NOT A GUARANTEE — React documents no maximum render-to-subscribe interval to size a delay against.

THE CHOICE, and it is Mike's because rf2-2rtt6.14's ruling PINNED THE PRIMITIVE (workers correctly have not touched it):

(a) MOVE THE HORIZON. setTimeout 4 is the smallest tested delay reading 1.00N at both sizes. COST: abandoned renders, Suspense retries and never-shown trees hold their reactive graphs ~4 ms longer; the Suspense-abort zero-point moves out with it (a contract-visible change, so Spec 006 wording moves too); AND IT IS STILL A RACE, not a contract.

(b) ACCEPT AND KEEP THE HORIZON AS RULED. The hand-off's benefit is then real only under forced-synchronous rendering, and the retractions on rf2-2rtt6.25 stand permanently: the coldmount instrument's shipped rows, the xcript before/after clock, and the M1L1 red-zone closure are withdrawn as shipped-performance claims (already done and now stamped in the source and in every emitted record, PR #7402).

(c) SOMETHING ELSE — e.g. a non-timer signal that is a contract rather than a margin. Nobody has proposed one; React exposes no cancellation signal for a render that never commits.

WHAT A RULING COSTS TO IMPLEMENT: small. The public-schedule assertions were deliberately written to be INVERTED, NOT DELETED (assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds says so in its own docstring: 'Flip these five assertions to the act-driven row's — identical?, = 1 — when the horizon question is ruled'). Under (a) the work is one constant, five flipped assertions, the Suspense-abort zero-point, the Spec 006 sentence, and un-stamping the coldmount provenance PR #7402 added. Under (b) the work is ZERO — everything already says the right thing.

DO NOT let a worker pick a longer timer to make a row go green. That is the failure this bead exists to prevent.

THE RULING. The provisional-escrow reaper moves setTimeout 0 -> setTimeout 4: the smallest probed delay reading 1.00N at N=1 AND N=300 (not 32 — the horizon is the shortest winning margin, so abandoned renders/Suspense retries hold their graphs no longer than needed). The claim stays NARROW: one build on the tested shipping schedule, with the safe two-build fallback; adoption remains a best-effort optimisation, never a React guarantee. No new hook, no new public mechanism to harden it — Spec 006's "correctness MUST NOT depend on the reaper losing the race" is untouched and is exactly what makes a 4 ms heuristic acceptable.

RATIONALE + how main-vs-Codex resolved. The dossier's main rec was (b) accept-and-keep, resting on "the double build prices at 1.0054x -> 1.0011x, indistinguishable from free." title: hicasso: the converge rewrites a refused/normalised value MID-COMPOSITION, destroying the IME exchange — as does React's own restore; carve-out needs a ruling
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-o27h3 harness (ime_run.cjs, real CDP composition — trusted compositionstart/update, input events with insertCompositionText + isComposing true, a real composition range), first run 2026-08-02, branch worker/ime-o27h3.

THE FINDING. The PR #7371 audit asked the harness to pin that front.controlled's converge 'neither writes nor moves selection mid-composition'. It does not hold — and neither does the plain-React baseline:

- REFUSING model (digits): the IME composes し into '12'; the model refuses; the converge writes '12' back INSIDE the composing input event. A JS value write mid-composition silently ABORTS the browser's composition — no compositionend fires, the next IME update mints a fresh compositionstart, and the user's in-flight kana are gone. Plain React does the IDENTICAL thing in the same turn via its own end-of-event restore (updateInput), and UIx's Reagent-port does it one animation frame later (input-node-set-value on the after-render queue). Measured matrix identical across all three: field '12' after settle, composition aborted, model never moved.
- NORMALISING model (upper): same class — 's' composes, model holds 'S', the write lands mid-composition, exchange aborted. All three implementations.
- MODEL-AGREEING field: the exchange SURVIVES on all three — exactly one compositionstart through to compositionend. The converge's flushSync + unconditional setSelectionRange did NOT disturb the CDP composition range (measured), and its equal-value write branch never fires; a mutation making the write unconditional was ALSO measured harmless (Chromium's value setter short-circuits an equal write).
- On the refusing field a CANCELLED exchange never sees compositionend at all — the abort already happened. Field and model still end exactly as before (the restoration law held everywhere).

SO: the converge is nowhere WORSE than the plain-React baseline (comparative rows green in the same run), but the pin the audit demanded is false for every implementation that converges a store-refused/normalised field mid-composition. The fence that would make it true is a composition carve-out: suppress convergence while a composition is live (the change handler can read isComposing off the native input event) and converge ONCE at compositionend against the then-current model. That changes what a composing user sees on a refusing field (their composition survives until commit, then is refused whole) — it is a BEHAVIOURAL choice inside HD-019's controlled-text-converge exception scope, and per rf2-o27h3's brief it needs a ruling, not a worker's judgment. If ruled in, the carve-out belongs to front/controlled.cljs (and the same question then stands, unanswerable by us, for plain React and the UIx port, which have the same conduct and no carve-out seam).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
[2026-08-03 15:45 AUSEST] DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

RULING: carve-out IN. Controlled-text convergence is suppressed while a composition is live; the field converges ONCE at compositionend against the then-current model. Automatic for any :value/:on-input pair — no public option, no config knob.

WHY (what the composing user experiences): under parity (out), a CJK/IME user on a refusing or normalising field has in-flight kana silently destroyed mid-word — no compositionend, no feedback, the field snaps back while they are still composing. Under the carve-out, the composition survives ('12shi'...'12shin' in kana) and refusal happens whole at commit: the field snaps back visibly at compositionend. The composition is a browser-owned draft of the user's; destroying it silently is not a parity target worth keeping. Hicasso becomes deliberately better than React in its flagship territory. HD-019 already frames this exact choice as inside the converge exception's scope and names rf2-digtt as its reopen trigger, whichever way ruled.

MAIN vs CODEX: both dossier reviewers recommend IN; Codex adopted on mechanism. The bare "skip converge! when isComposing" is proven insufficient by this bead's own measured matrix: plain React — which has no Hicasso converge in the loop, i.e. exactly the path a bare skip falls through to — still aborts the exchange via its own end-of-discrete-event controlled restore (ChangeEventPlugin enqueues a restore target, the post-handler flush performs it, the value is assigned whenever DOM differs from the controlled value). The carve-out must therefore ALSO make React's restore a no-op during composition.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (supersedes the description's one-line mechanism sketch):
- Surface: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/controlled.cljs (+ ime_run.cjs + existing controlled tests). Mechanism: an internal composition shadow for controlled text only — while a composition is live, the value React sees agrees with the live DOM draft (so React's restore finds nothing to write); the authored handler still runs normally and the model may refuse/normalise as usual; at compositionend release the shadow and converge once against the then-current model. Prefer a small public-React mechanism (e.g. one internal stateful controlled-text wrapper) over React-private mutation or value-setter interception. Preserve any authored composition handlers; authoring API unchanged.
- Safety rider: shadow release must be unconditional (compositionend, and the blur/unmount paths); worst-case degradation is today's conduct (a converge), never a stuck field diverged from the model.
- The ime_run.cjs s5 rows are a DELIBERATE TRIPWIRE: they go red the day this lands and are flipped on purpose — Hicasso rows re-pin one uninterrupted compositionstart->compositionend exchange with commit-time refusal/normalisation; the react and uix-port rows keep pinning the old abort conduct, now asserted as divergence, not parity. Retain the agreeing-field, cancel, commit-fence, mid-string caret and restoration laws; price the per-input machinery on the existing grid.
- Honesty riders: the evidence page and authoring doc state the divergence from React plainly (a claimed win, precisely scoped to Hicasso's converge), AND state witness scope: Chromium CDP only. Codex flagged WebKit's recently-fixed composition/key-ordering defect; this harness cannot drive WebKit composition (CDP is Chromium-only) and mandating a new driver is gold-plating — name the caveat on the evidence page instead. WebKit misconduct, if ever observed, is a new bug bead.
- HD-019 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md) gets a dated addendum recording this ruling in the same PR; rf2-dfz6f then rewrites R-A2 (guidance noted on that bead).
- If the public-React shadow cannot meet the existing gates (caret laws, agreeing-field survival, perf grid), return the mechanism for a ruling rather than shipping a private-React hack.

title: RULING NEEDED: the route planner's dedupe grain and the two :rf.runtime/routing identity slots collapse a byte-distinct scoped-key pair
description:
Found closing rf2-dlkou (audit of PR #7228). rf2-dlkou's repair made route-resource-plan's OWN identity arithmetic byte-exact (membership + the removal partition are keyed on state/key-id now, not Clojure =). Two carriers UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM of it still collapse the same pair, and closing them needs a ruling because it moves documented cross-feature shapes.

THE PAIR. Resource identity is state/key-id (CEDN-1 canonical bytes), which is collection-KIND sensitive (rf2-wgutc2). [:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p [1 2]}] and [:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p (1 2)}] are (= a b) TRUE and (count (set [a b])) 1, while state/key-id yields v[...v[i:1 i:2]] vs v[...l(i:1 i:2)] and state/entry-path yields two distinct cache slots. Verified on the JVM.

WHERE IT STILL COLLAPSES.
1. resources/route.cljc collapse-and-order — (group-by :scoped-key occs). Two route entries in one branch requiring the same resource+scope with vector-vs-list params group into ONE dedup-req, so ONE ensure is dispatched and the second byte identity is never fetched. That is a DISPATCH defect, not a diagnostic one, which is why it was fenced out of rf2-dlkou.
2. The handoff slot [:rf.runtime/routing :resource-plan <nav-token>] is documented as #{<scoped-key> ...}, and its sibling [:rf.runtime/routing :resource-blocking <nav-token>] likewise. A Clojure set cannot hold both members of the pair, so even a byte-exact planner cannot hand both to the next activation, and reconcile-readiness prunes a blocking set whose membership is =-based while looking entries up by byte path.

WHY IT NEEDS A RULING. The fix is a shape change to two cross-feature runtime-db slots, documented in spec/Spec-Schemas.md (:rf.runtime/routing), spec/016-Resources.md, and implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc, plus routing/events.cljc which reads and writes them. The natural shape is the one :entries already uses — {<key-id> <scoped-key>} — which also carries no order promise and so preserves rf2-dlkou's ruling that removal has no meaningful order. But Mike's ruling ON rf2-dlkou declined a cross-feature slot change once already (for the ordering question), so this one should be decided rather than assumed.

ALTERNATIVE WORTH CONSIDERING: rule that a scoped key's params are CANONICALIZED to vectors at construction (state/scoped-resource-key), making the =-collapse correct everywhere instead of making every carrier byte-exact. That is the smaller change but it retires a distinction the repo currently calls supported (rf2-wgutc2), so it is equally a ruling.

REACHED TODAY? A single plan needs two route entries whose :params fns return a vector and a list for the same resource+scope — constructible, not accidental. The cross-navigation case (prior plan list, next plan vector) is REPAIRED by rf2-dlkou and pinned by r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact-not-clojure-equal in resources_route_cljs_test.
close_reason: PR #7443 — option (a) implemented: the planner's dedupe grain and both :rf.runtime/routing identity slots (:resource-plan, :resource-blocking) are byte-exact {(state/key-id k) k} maps with no order promise. collapse-and-order groups by key-id (stamped once in materialize-occurrences); reconcile-readiness + the SSR blocking drain + the plan diff read the carriers' own keys; xray's panel read adapts. Spec surgical: Spec-Schemas :rf.runtime/routing (2 lines), 016 Plan diff + readiness (2 hunks), 012 readiness cell (1 line), 009 no-order evidence reworded to the map with the no-order promise KEPT. Twin regression added and MUTATION-PROVEN both directions: reintroducing the =-grain dedupe exits 1 with 16 failures, all in the two new deftests naming the collapsed pair; reverted byte-identically -> 0 failures. resources_cache_key_identity (0 lines), r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact (0 lines) and r2-removed-identities-is-membership (0 assertion changes; 3 prose spots corrected) all stayed green. comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-03 15:46 AUSEST — delegated dossier-review ruling (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

DECISION: (a) — CEDN-1 byte identity stays authoritative; make the last two =-based carriers byte-exact using the established shape {(state/key-id scoped-key) scoped-key}. Option (b) (canonicalise params to vectors at construction) is REJECTED on verified facts, not taste. Option (c) rejected: the collapse is a real dispatch defect in a documented slot.

WHY (b) FAILS — every one of the counter-recommendation's factual attacks HELD under verification:
1. VERIFIED: the live route path never calls the defensive state/scoped-resource-key. route.cljc:720-723 builds keys with scoped-resource-key* from params canonicalized upstream (registry/validate+canonicalize-params) + scope via resolve-scope-for-event; scoped-resource-key* does not re-canonicalize (rf2-rplgkw). Changing scoped-resource-key alone fixes NOTHING on this bug — (b)'s "one choke point" premise is false as written.
2. VERIFIED: Spec 016 §Canonicalization rule says "this artefact does not define a second canonicalizer... sets and vectors keep their value semantics." A resource-local seq->vector coercion violates it; moving coercion into CEDN-1 itself (Conventions) rewrites identity for the whole framework — vastly broader than this bug.
3. VERIFIED: b53c1195d7 (Mike-authored, rf2-wgutc2) DELIBERATELY removed the old resource-local list->vector canonicalizer: "it collapsed lists->vectors; now the list-vs-vector EDN distinction is preserved." (b) re-introduces the exact divergence Mike ruled out.
4. VERIFIED: 8589517857 (rf2-9e0tyq) byte-keyed all 4 cache carriers and explicitly rejected normalization: "No list-to-vector normalize (would re-erase the kind)" — and byte-keying surfaced 3 latent production =-collapse bugs, evidence the byte grain does real work.
5. VERIFIED: resources_cache_key_identity_cljs_test.cljc adversarially pins kind-preservation across 4 carriers, incl. "the list entry's :resource/key PRESERVES the list kind (not coerced to a vector)". (b) flips deliberate pins.
6. HELD (structural): scope is arbitrary canonical CEDN too; a vector-vs-list nested in SCOPE collapses identically, so honest (b) means deep-normalizing scope+params — a broad semantic change, not the dossier's one-liner.
So (b) is neither the smaller change nor a fix at the point it names; it fights the repo's ruled, spec'd, adversarially-tested identity architecture. (a) is the same pattern already applied by rf2-9e0tyq (cache carriers) and rf2-dlkou/PR #7391 (planner arithmetic), extended to the last known =-based carriers — one identity story: identity-bearing collections key on state/key-id, values stay kind-preserving scoped keys.

FOOTGUN ASSESSMENT (map->mapv renames a resource): real but self-healing — worst case is a cache-miss refetch under the new identity, and the REQUIRED :params-schema is where an author pins param shape (vec at the boundary). No machinery here. If Mike wants a guardrail (e.g. Xray lint for =-equal-but-byte-distinct sibling keys), that is a separate explicitly-scoped ruling, not this bug.

rf2-wgutc2 DISPOSITION: its kind-distinctness claim STANDS unchanged under (a). NB the id no longer resolves in bd (compacted); nothing to amend. rf2-dlkou stays closed; its close reason already names this bead as exact owner of the handoff shape.

- resources/route.cljc: collapse-and-order (~:791) groups + builds the topo graph by (state/key-id scoped-key) (group-of, group-by, gkeys/gedges/group-rank); dedup-req keeps the kind-preserving scoped-key value. Plan return :identities and :blocking become {key-id scoped-key} maps (no order promise — preserves rf2-dlkou's withdrawn-ordering ruling). reconcile-readiness + clear-blocking-slot prune/dissoc by key-id. Plan-diff (:ensured/:kept/:removed + identity vectors ~:1060-1180) reads prev/next off the maps' own keys (the "one derivation of the identity" comment already points there). Rewrite the "WHAT REMAINS" comment ~:1176.
- resources/ssr.cljc: the reconcile-readiness/blocking drain consumes the map shape.
- routing/events.cljc ~:253/:296/:302: prev-identities read + the two assoc-in writes carry maps; verify (seq (:blocking plan)) sites.
- routing/readiness.cljc project-at-commit: consumes :blocking as a map.
- core/late_bind/directory.cljc :routing/on-route-entry description (~:645): :blocking/:identities shapes -> byte-keyed maps.
- SPEC (hot-zone): Spec-Schemas.md :rf.runtime/routing bullet (~:2952) — both slots {<nav-token> {<key-id> <scoped-key>}}; 016-Resources.md (2 refs); 012-Routing.md (6 refs, readiness prose); 009-Instrumentation.md (2 refs — reword the no-order evidence clause "the handoff records a set and hands it back" to the map, keep the no-order promise). ep-0037-r2-* fixture mentions are prose-only; verify no shape pin.
- Ordered trace vectors STAY vectors; only unordered identity carriers become maps. No new panel/public plan value (rf2-9sluz descope stands).
- TESTS: end-to-end twin regression (the acceptance the rf2-dlkou audit demanded): one plan containing BOTH members of a byte-distinct =-equal pair as two route entries -> two dedup-reqs, two ensures, both identities in the :resource-plan map, both independently blocking/reconciled/SSR-drained; and a transition keeping one + removing the other -> exact :kept-identities/:removed-identities/counts + next handoff. Existing pins (resources_cache_key_identity, r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact, r2-removed-identities-is-membership) stay green unchanged.

title: hicasso: a refused keystroke stays on the screen on the React adapter (controlled-restore, mined from Arm 2)
notes:
STILL OPEN 2026-08-02, and deliberately not rounded up. rf2-fki5d shipped
(PR #7371) and answers the headline residue FOR HICASSO'S ARM 1 ONLY.

WHAT IS ANSWERED. On Arm 1's element path a refused keystroke now converges
inside the discrete event WITH THE CARET AT THE POSITION BEFORE IT — mid-string
included — and so does every keystroke a normalising model rewrites. Both halves,
same turn, no ceremony in the view and no hook in the boundary shell. Measured on
the 100-cell grid at
`arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/the-family-converges-in-one-turn-with-the-caret-where-the-edit-left-it`.

WHAT IS NOT, and why this bead stays open:

1. THE REACT ADAPTER — which is what this bead is titled for — IS UNCHANGED. A
   UIx consumer's `:input` is minted by `uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input`, not
   by `front.codec`, so it is not on the path the converge was installed in.
   For that consumer a mid-string refusal still converges with the caret thrown
   to the end of the field ([5 5] where [2 2] is wanted), and so does every
   normalisation. Closing this bead would require either porting the converge
   into `re-frame.adapter.uix` — which today mints no `:input` of its own — or a
   ruling that Hicasso is the answer and the UIx adapter keeps React's caret.
   That is a decision, not an implementation, and it is filed separately.

2. THE RANGE ROW. A range still does not survive a converge that WRITES, on any
   path: React collapses to a cursor at the end of the value it wrote, the UIx
   port writes one offset into both ends. Restoring a range is a second
   algorithm — two offsets, not one — and out-of-band corrections (a server
   normalisation, a debounce) fire no change event at all, so they are off the
   converge's path by construction. Asserted as recorded behaviour on both
   shipped paths and on the arm.

3. IME. Still not established either way; rf2-o27h3 holds it with the real
   `CompositionEvent` harness that would settle it. Nothing in rf2-fki5d touches
   composition — the converge wraps the CHANGE slot only, never a key or
   composition event.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md.

description:

Ruling (a) is IMPLEMENTED (spine horizon setTimeout 0 -> 4). Item 2 of the
ruling — flipping assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds to the
act-driven row's integers — was ATTEMPTED, MEASURED, and HELD. This bead
carries the measurement and the decision it needs.

THE FACT. With the ruled setTimeout 4 in place, the flipped assertions FAIL:
the row still observes two acquisitions, two body runs, and the commit's
reaction (not the render's) as the cache tenant. Deterministic, reproduced in
a narrow single-ns browser-test build in ~1 s, not a load artefact.

THE SWEEP (narrow :browser-test build, uix-use-subscribe-dom-cljs-test only,
one run per cell; the integer is the row's :builds):

  horizon 0 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 ms, as shipped (one timer per burst)   2
  horizon 4 / 32 / 128 ms, rewired to one timer per TOKEN             2
  reaper disabled entirely                                            1
  horizon 256 / 1024 / 5000 ms                                        1

So the reaper IS the releaser — disabling it adopts — and the gap this page
puts between the render and React's passive flush is > 128 ms and <= 256 ms.
Two to three orders of magnitude above any horizon worth shipping. Per-token
arming was tested and rejected as the explanation, so burst coalescing is not
the cause either.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT evidence against ruling (a): the ruling's
swap-the-primitive probe measured a dedicated single-mount instrument page,
where the gap is under 4 ms, and nothing here contradicts that. It IS evidence
that this assertion cannot serve as the adoption witness the ruling assumed —
the browser test page (30 async rows, cljs-test done plumbing, a display
renderer competing for the main thread) is not a faithful clock for a
millisecond-scale race. Greening the row would take a horizon in the hundreds
of milliseconds, i.e. holding every abandoned render's reactive graph for a
quarter of a second — exactly the trade rf2-2rtt6.71 declined, and exactly the
"worker picks a longer timer to green a row" failure rf2-2rtt6.25 warned about.
So the worker did not do it.

  * spine horizon = 4, as ruled, with the margin-not-contract prose.

    environment) and not enough to pin the win.
  * every horizon-crossing settle in the shared suite moved off a bare

    fires strictly BEFORE a 4 ms reap, so those rows measured nothing.
  * spec 006 and the hicasso studio/instrument stamps cite the ruling's probe
    as the evidence for the win, never this assertion.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD WANTS. Either (i) build a public-schedule adoption
witness on a representative page — a dedicated single-mount browser target
whose render-to-flush gap is measured and asserted to be small before the
adoption integers are read, so the tripwire the ruling wanted actually exists;
or (ii) accept that the adoption is witnessed only by the coldmount-class
instrument and say so once, in Spec 006, retiring the expectation of an

rf2-2rtt6.71 explicitly valued: without it, a React scheduling change that
moves the passive flush past 4 ms reintroduces the double build silently.

ALSO WORTH RULING, cheap: assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds

NOT done under rf2-2rtt6.71 (not in the ruling's enumerated items, and the name

title: hicasso: the sub-index's reverse edge duplicates the cell table's key space — the largest per-read elimination still on the table
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2, which attacked the per-read gap and landed one
elimination (-107 B/read). This is the biggest one it costed and did NOT
take, because it is a redesign rather than a byte shave.

THE OBSERVATION. On the distinct-query rung the ladder is taken on, the
Arm 1 read path keeps TWO process-global persistent maps keyed by the
SAME B·R sub-keys:

  arm1/runtime.cljs   !cells     sub-key -> the key cell (reaction, epoch, refs)
  front/sub_index.cljs :sub->bs  sub-key -> #{boundary-id}   the reverse edges

Every read therefore pays two persistent-hash-map entries where the
design needs one table keyed by sub-key, plus — at fan-out 1, which is
what Q = E means — a SINGLETON PersistentHashSet per key whose whole job
is to hold one pointer.

THE PRICE, partly measured. rf2-aqgr2 measured one retained hash-set
membership at +46 B/read (Reagent segment) / +47 (UIx) by forcing
`record-reads` to copy the forward edge and re-taking the ladder
(p0_run.cjs --only ladder, 6 rounds, donors unmoved). That prices the
MEMBERSHIP, not the whole singleton-set-plus-map-entry shape, so the
reverse edge's total is not yet split out. It is plausibly the single
largest remaining term in the +391 B/read bill (down from +499).

THE CANDIDATE ELIMINATION. Put the reader set on the cell — one table
keyed by sub-key holding both the reaction and its readers — and the
second map, its per-key entry and its per-key set object all go away.
`dirty-boundaries` becomes a walk of the dirty cells' reader sets;
`commit!` already receives cells (`flush!` maps `.-subKey` over them and
the index maps them straight back).

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE UNDER rf2-aqgr2:

- it dissolves `front/sub-index`'s role in Arm 1, and that namespace is
  the SHARED FRONT HALF with its own six-law discharge
  (`front/sub_index_laws_cljs_test`);
- `architecture.md:33-35` states the design claim in terms of those
  maps ("index edges live in global maps — shared structure, not
  per-boundary object fan-out"), so the doc moves with the code;
- it is a design decision about where the dependency index LIVES, which
  is above a perf bead's pay grade.

WHAT A DISPATCH NEEDS TO DECIDE FIRST: does the reverse edge stay a
general, separately-testable algebra (its current value), or does Arm 1
own one fused key table now that the tournament is over and the shared
front half may be evolved as the adapter needs (epic note, 2026-07-31)?

Measure on the same instrument and the same terms rf2-aqgr2 used:
`p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, 6 rounds, both donors riding as the same-run
control, quiet box, and an ablation run so the split is attributed
rather than asserted.
notes:
MAYOR: HELD FOR OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-03. Escalated by the rf2-ixb92/rf2-dabt3 worker BEFORE editing, which was the right call — the investigation materially changed what this bead is.

THIS BEAD UNDER-SCOPES ITSELF. It names :sub->bs. But once readers live on the cell, the FORWARD edge has no reader either: record-reads exists to feed :sub->bs, and Arm 1's registration already holds .-reads (make-subscribe sets a reads field, the entry's own key set). So the honest end state is not 'the index keeps :b->subs' — it is that front.sub-index HAS NO ROLE IN ARM 1 AT ALL. With Arm 2 retired it has no other production caller. The HD-005 evidence sink (:edges-changed, :commit) would have to be re-homed or dropped with it, and four files consume the namespace directly (front/dogfood_cljs_test, read_profile_app — which drives mount!/record-reads!/unmount! as a MEASURED arm — shapes/framework_subs_dom_cljs_test's readers-of witness, arm1/runtime_cljs_test).

ALL SIX LAWS ARE STATEMENTS ABOUT THE REVERSE EDGE, so there is no keep-the-algebra/move-one-map split available: laws 1,2,5,6 are dirty-boundaries (:sub->bs read), law 3 is unmount clearing it, law 4 is the edge-set diff maintaining it. front/sub_index_laws_cljs_test (269 lines) loses its SUBJECT entirely, not partially. architecture.md §2's 'Index edges live in global maps — shared structure, not per-boundary object fan-out' is the sentence that moves, and it is the deliverable-2 framing of the whole shared front half.

SO THE RULING IS NOT 'refactor the index'. IT IS: **is deliverable 2 of the shared front half retired?**

WHAT IS SETTLED, so the ruling is cheap to take:
  • The elimination is REAL — two persistent maps over one B·R key space, plus a singleton PersistentHashSet per key at fan-out 1. PR #7418's run D prices ONE retained set membership at +46/+47 B/read, so the reverse edge's total is plausibly several times that.
  • NO LOOKUP GETS WORSE. dirty-boundaries becomes a walk of the dirty cells' own reader sets, and flush! ALREADY HOLDS THE CELLS — it maps .-subKey over them purely so the index can map them straight back.
  • The cost is therefore not algorithmic. It is the six-law algebra's home, plus one architecture sentence.

SIBLING rf2-ixb92 PROCEEDS SEPARATELY and is unaffected: :live is provably (set (keys (:b->subs idx))) at every reachable value, contains?/count are the same operations on either structure, the laws suite uses the live? FUNCTION rather than the key, and architecture.md needs no edit because it never names :live (:live is not an edge). Do not conflate the two.

DO NOT DISPATCH THIS BEAD until the operator rules on retiring deliverable 2.

title: hicasso: defhost's macro docstring teaches ::h/value at react-datepicker's value-first onChange
description:
The `defhost` macro docstring in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/lang.clj (lines 71-80) carries this worked example:

    (defhost date-picker DatePicker
      {:callbacks {:on-change :event}})

    [date-picker {:selected  due-date
                  :on-change [:task/set-due ::h/value]}]

It names date-picker/DatePicker — the exact pair the draft guide's interop opening uses for react-datepicker — and puts a ::h/value-carrying intent vector at :on-change. react-datepicker's onChange is VALUE-first (onChange(date)), so under HD-024's landed event-first law (front/intent.cljs event-arg!) that call raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event. The guide (docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md) teaches the h/fn spelling there for exactly this reason, so a reader who checks the macro against the guide finds the two contradicting each other on the same component.

The docstring is not wrong about the GRAMMAR — ::h/value at a declared :event slot is correct whenever the foreign invoker is event-first — so the fix is to stop naming a value-first library. Either rename the example component to an event-first one (the host-hatch witness's onDraft shape), or keep date-picker and switch the call site to the h/fn the guide teaches.

Found while landing rf2-2rtt6.64; not fixed there because that bead's surface is docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/** and implementation/** was fenced.

title: bench: widen B8's warm-up — one 4-write calibration window is not enough, the data says six
description:
FOUND by rf2-88pie (PR #7223).

order_guard.cjs's live sweep and B8's own first guarded run agree: a measurement site reads well above its settled value until it has run several windows.

  plain node, packed-SMI .slice() control, nothing else varying, sixteen consecutive windows:
    10.32 10.26 10.26 10.26 10.33 10.28 | 8.12 8.12 ... 8.12
  +27% for SIX windows, then a step to the 8.016 prediction. The very first window read 42.32 - 5.3x.

  b8_run.cjs, B8_ROUNDS=4 --kind narrow, real Chromium harness: the 'instrument' arm - the pseudo-arm whose entire purpose is to price the harness's own footprint as a CONSTANT - read 4,361 B/write in its first window and 440 in its last. 9.9x.

b8_run.cjs warms each (arm, D) with ONE four-write calibration window, which the calibration loop doubles as warm-up. That is not enough, and the arm-order guard's phase factor now refuses the run because of it (exit 2).

ACTIONABLE:
1. Warm each (arm, D) for >= 6 windows before the first measured one, or drop the first N measured windows per arm.
2. Raise the default ROUNDS so the guard's phase strata are not single samples - at ROUNDS=4 each stratum is n=1 and the guard has to adjudicate on a ratio rather than a range.
3. Re-run and confirm the guard passes.

title: Hicasso: a :render prop that returns lowered hiccup poisons the row's own handlers
description:
FOUND while landing rf2-2rtt6.35 (HD-024's two laws). Not fixed there, because it
is a capability question about the :render contract rather than a defect in the
carrier-governance repair, and answering it needs a ruling on which frame a
render-produced row dispatches to.

THE SHAPE. A `defhost` `:render` slot is the ecosystem's `renderRow`/`renderItem`
prop. For React to render what the body returns, the body has to hand back an
ELEMENT, so the author calls the codec's hiccup->element conversion inside the
callback:

    [grid {:on-render-row (h/fn [row]
                            (h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick (:id row)]}
                                           (:title row)]))}]

THE PROBLEM. `front/intent/render-callback` enforces purity by BINDING the
ambient `*dispatch*` to a poison fn for the call's dynamic extent, and
`front/intent/intent-handler` captures `*dispatch*` AT LOWERING TIME (via
`require-dispatch`). So the `:on-click` above closes over the POISONED dispatch,
and clicking the rendered row raises
`:rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position` — for a click, which is a
perfectly legitimate event position that happens to have been LOWERED during a
render.

The rule HD-024 states is "dispatching from inside the call is a loud error". A
closure that will dispatch LATER is not dispatching from inside the call. The
poisoning conflates the two because lowering captures the same var the poison
replaced.

WHY IT MATTERS. A render prop that produces a NON-interactive row works; one that
produces an interactive row does not. That is most of what render props are for,
and the failure lands on the user's click rather than at the author's site.

OPTIONS, none of them ruled:
  (a) Poison only DISPATCH, not lowering: have `render-callback` bind a poisoned
      dispatch that `intent-handler` refuses to CAPTURE, i.e. keep a separate
      "capturable" binding — the callback's enclosing boundary's real dispatch —
      so rows lower against the boundary that owns them and only an immediate
      dispatch during the call is refused.
  (b) Rule the case out: state that a :render body must not build lowered
      elements, and refuse `as-element` inside a render callback with a
      diagnostic naming the position. Cheap, but it removes the interactive
      render-prop entirely.
  (c) Leave it and revisit at the component-library tier (charter.md:144-149
      defers that tier past v0; the census counts 0 foreign components).

NOT WITNESSED DELIBERATELY. rf2-2rtt6.35 did not add a test pinning the current
behaviour, because pinning it would record a defect as the contract.

Sites: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/intent.cljs
  - `render-callback` (the binding)
  - `require-dispatch` / `intent-handler` (the capture)
close_reason: PR #7449: render-position enforcement is invocation-scoped (gate armed in a finally); owner = the supplying boundary's frame, rebound for the invocation. Three witnesses incl. the two-frame ownership row at the declared-:render crossing; both purity edges unmodified and still raising; HD-024 dated addendum.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
[2026-08-03 20:18 AUSEST] DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

RULING: (a), sharpened — repair now, inside HD-024's existing laws, via an INVOCATION-SCOPED ARMING GATE in render-callback, NOT the naive "second capturable binding" this bead's option (a) text sketches.

MECHANISM (the capture/poison discrimination, exact): render-callback captures the ambient *dispatch* AND *frame* at wrapper-creation (lowering) time — the supplying boundary's, because the wrapper is minted during that boundary's eager with-frame + as-element walk (arm1/runtime.cljs ~1329). Each invocation mints a fresh gate closing over an armed? flag + the captured owner dispatch; binds *frame* = captured frame and *dispatch* = gate around (apply f args); arms the gate in a finally. Gate while active: raise the existing :rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position naming the position (message unchanged). Gate after: forward to the captured owner dispatch; if NO owner was in scope at wrapper creation, raise the existing :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary — loud, never silent. require-dispatch / intent-handler / event-callback stay UNCHANGED: they keep capturing *dispatch*, which inside a callback is now the gate — that is what makes lower-now/fire-later work while lower-now/fire-NOW still fails.

FRAME ANSWER (dossier main rec CONFIRMED): a render-produced row dispatches to the frame of the boundary whose codec walk lowered the :render prop — the supplying boundary. Only candidate: the wrapper is created inside that boundary's with-frame extent, the foreign component has no frame of its own, and frames-as-isolated-contexts forbids any other. Rebinding the captured *frame* per invocation is part of the SAME repair, not growth: route-link's require-frame! (front/route_link.cljs ~174) reads intent/*frame* and today fails loudly inside any render-prop body.

WHY NOT NAIVE (a) — the main-vs-Codex resolution: both recs chose repair-now-(a); they split on mechanism, and Codex's objection VERIFIED. deftest at-a-render-position-...-dispatching-is-a-loud-error (front/intent_cljs_test.cljs, second testing block) pins the SYNCHRONOUS lower-and-fire error: it lowers :on-click [:oops] inside the callback and fires it immediately. Under a second capturable binding, that inner handler captures the REAL dispatch and the immediate fire dispatches silently — the pinned witness breaks and law 1 is weakened (a dispatch that actually happens during the call succeeds). The gate discriminates temporally — call-active vs call-complete — which is exactly the law's own line ("dispatching from inside the call"). Codex's gate adopted; Codex's frame-rebinding and two-frame-witness additions verified load-bearing and adopted.

WHY NOT (b)/(c): (b) deletes the interactive renderRow pattern — most of what render props exist for — to preserve a mechanism conflation. (c) ships a booby trap on a surface HD-024 just landed: the error fires at the USER's click, far from the author's site (worst failure geometry), and census-zero measures the old corpus, not this product. Both punish the obvious usage — anti trust-the-programmer.

SCOPE FENCE: front/intent.cljs render-callback (+ its docstring and the ns-docstring's mechanism sentence) only. Change what lowering-inside-a-render-callback captures/forwards; NOTHING about scheduling; no new API, no config knobs, no new error ids; no auto-conversion of arbitrary render returns; no component-library machinery. If implementation hits a genuinely hard case — anything at the no-owner-at-creation edge (a callback lowered outside any boundary) that would be silent or ambiguous rather than the loud outside-boundary error above — STOP and return for a follow-up ruling instead of inventing policy.
