title: ci: a CANCELLED check fails the aggregate gate, and cancellations are hitting PRs that cannot violate the check
description:
OBSERVED by the mayor across three consecutive merges on 2026-08-03.

THE SYMPTOM. 'Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)' came back with conclusion CANCELLED on PR #7440 and again on PR #7442. A cancelled required check makes the aggregate 'All required checks passed' report FAILURE, so the PR reads red and cannot merge, even though nothing actually failed.

WHY IT IS SPURIOUS IN BOTH CASES, verified per PR rather than assumed:
  • #7440 changed 8 files (spine.cljs, react_shared_suite.cljs, two studio pages, spec/006, uix dom test, coldmount app/run). NO .beads path.
  • #7442 changed exactly ONE file: docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md. NO .beads path.
In both, the gate's own subject is absent from the diff, so it had nothing it could legitimately fail on. In both, a fresh run of the workflow cleared it with no code change.

THE COST. Each occurrence blocks a merge until someone notices the conclusion is CANCELLED rather than FAILURE, verifies the diff cannot violate the gate, and re-runs. That is a judgement call every time, and the failure mode it invites is worse than the delay: a mayor who learns to wave away 'that check is always spurious' will one day wave away a real violation. A gate that cries wolf is a gate that stops being read.

WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED — do not assume causation. A plausible mechanism is a concurrency group: the mayor pushes a .beads checkpoint to main every ~11 minutes, and if PR runs share a concurrency group with push-to-main runs, a checkpoint push would cancel in-flight PR jobs. Evidence is suggestive but thin: 'gh run list --workflow=test.yml --limit 12' showed exactly one cancelled run in that window and it was event=push on branch=main, not a PR run. So the cancellations may have a different cause. ESTABLISH THE MECHANISM BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING.

DO:
  1. Read .github/workflows/*.yml for concurrency: blocks — which workflows share a group, and whether the group key distinguishes PR head from main.
  2. If a push-to-main run can cancel an in-flight PR run, fix the group key so it cannot (a per-ref key is the usual shape). Keep it minimal.
  3. Independently of the cause: consider whether the aggregate 'All required checks passed' job should treat CANCELLED distinctly from FAILURE, so a cancelled job reads as 'incomplete, re-run' rather than 'failed'. That is the part that turns a transient into a false red.
  4. Do NOT weaken the beads-boundary gate itself — it is load-bearing (a tracker database in a PR time-travels the tracker) and it is not the thing at fault here.

FENCE: .github/workflows/** is HOT-ZONE, sequential-only. Keep the edit surgical and say so in the PR body. Mutation-prove whatever you change: demonstrate the cancellation path before and after, or state honestly that it could not be reproduced.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-03 — the leading hypothesis in the description (a push-to-main run cancelling PR runs) is probably WRONG, and the likeliest cause is the mayor's own repeated re-runs. Evidence, from .github/workflows/test.yml:16-18:

  concurrency:
    group: tests-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
    cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

For a pull_request event every run joins group tests-<PR number> with cancel-in-progress TRUE. So a SECOND run in that group cancels the first. On both #7440 and #7442 the mayor called 'gh run rerun' on consecutive ~11-minute ticks while the previous attempt was still queued or running — each new attempt would cancel its predecessor, producing exactly the observed queued -> cancelled -> 'cannot be rerun; already running' -> cancelled cycle. The mayor was cancelling the job it was trying to rescue.

WHAT THIS CHANGES:
• Re-running is the correct remedy for a genuinely cancelled check, but it must be done ONCE and then left alone. Do not re-run on a cadence; a loop that re-runs every tick can never let the job finish.
• The push-to-main theory should not be assumed. Note the group key already distinguishes PR from non-PR (it falls back to github.run_id, which is unique per run, so push runs cannot collide with each other or with PR runs). That is evidence AGAINST the original hypothesis.
• The item that still stands on its own merits is #3 in the DO list: the aggregate 'All required checks passed' job treats CANCELLED as FAILURE. Whatever cancels a job — a rescue attempt, a superseding push, an infra blip — the aggregate turning that into a red PR is what makes a transient look like a defect. Distinguishing 'incomplete, re-run' from 'failed' is the durable fix and does not depend on the cause.
• Items 1-2 (audit concurrency groups) are now LOW VALUE unless a cancellation is observed with no concurrent re-run in play. Do not spend a worker on them speculatively.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: this is the same family as the day's other findings — an instrument (here, the rescue action) interfering with the subject it was measuring. The tell was 'gh run rerun' reporting 'cannot be rerun; This workflow is already running' and the run then reading cancelled a tick later.
close_reason: PR #7448, item 3 of the DO list ONLY — items 1-2 (concurrency-group audit) skipped per the mayor's correction note that ruled them low-value. The aggregate 'All required checks passed' now adjudicates CANCELLED separately from FAILURE, failure arm first, and the cancelled message names the trap: for pull_request events test.yml's group is cancel-in-progress, so re-run ONCE and leave it alone. BOTH STILL BLOCK — the gate's pass/fail behaviour does not move on any input; only the words change. Verified by simulating every result spread against the committed steps parsed out of the YAML (if: expressions and exit codes read from the file, not hardcoded), before and after: identical verdict in all five cases. Shell bodies extracted and executed: sh -n clean on all three steps, both blocking steps exit 1, the pass step exits 0. HONEST GAP: I could not contrive a real GitHub-side cancellation — inducing one via a superseding push cancels the whole run including this always() job, which is not the observed shape. I did not manufacture a reproduction. NEW FAIL-OPEN INTRODUCED AND PINNED: splitting one blocking step into two means deleting the cancelled arm would let a cancelled required job read green silently (demonstrated — every cancelled spread flips to PASSING). _changed-surfaces.test.cjs now pins both arms with their own exit 1 in that order; mutation-proved by deleting the arm (red) and by reversing the two (red), test.yml restored byte-identically. THE BEADS-BOUNDARY GATE IS UNTOUCHED and is no weaker — job, script and needs: position all unchanged. Hot-zone edit is surgical: 32 insertions / 7 deletions confined to the steps: of all-required-passed; no job added to or removed from needs:.

title: bench: the ladder's structural witness still expects the PRE-FUSION meaning of :boundaries, so --only ladder cannot gate the fused arm
description:
FOUND by rf2-zei9w on 2026-08-04 on a verified-quiet box. `p0_run.cjs
--only ladder` EXITS 1 on the current `main` (2926049d5e) with 12
structural read-back failures, all of one kind and all on the R=0 rung:

  round N reagent-subs|lad/hicasso#R0: hicasso boundaries 0, expected 1200
  round N uix-subs|lad/hicasso#R0:     hicasso boundaries 0, expected 1200

EVERY OTHER GATE PASSED. ladder-fit self-test 3/3 ok, arm-order guard
self-test 12/12 ok, positive control OK (4,698,566 B measured against
4,700,000 predicted, ratio 0.9997), `0 unverified of 154 mounts`,
arm-order verdict `reportable`, and zero residue failures. The run is
otherwise clean; only this one expectation refuses.

THE EXPECTATION IS STALE, NOT THE ARM. rf2-dabt3 changed what
`:boundaries` MEANS and `p0_run.cjs` was not moved with it:

  before (383ba2d645^, arm1/runtime.cljs `stats`):
    :boundaries (count (:b->subs idx))
  after  (383ba2d645, the fusion):
    boundaries (reduce-kv (fn [acc _ ^js c] (into acc (.-readers c))) #{} cells)

`:b->subs` was populated by `index/mount!` — one entry per MOUNTED
boundary, whether or not it read anything — so `:boundaries` was
R-independent and 1200 at R=0. Post-fusion there is no per-boundary
registry at all: the forward edge lives on the registration itself
(`.-reads`) and the runtime knows a boundary only through cells' reader
lists. At R=0 nothing is read, so no cell exists, so `:boundaries` is 0.

THE RUNTIME SAYS SO ITSELF. `stats`'s docstring: \":boundaries counts the
distinct registrations holding at least one such slot; a boundary whose
body read nothing retains nothing in this table, so it is correctly
absent (its read-set entry is still counted by :entries)\". And rf2-dabt3
landed a test for exactly this — 7838e3f7ad, \"an edgeless boundary
retains no membership\". `:entries` at R=0 expects 1 and PASSES, which is
the same fact from the other side.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. `--only ladder` is opt-in and is in no gate;
`p0_run.cjs` was last touched by rf2-2rtt6.34 (f72f2586f5), before the
fusion. rf2-dabt3 deferred its measurement for a quiet box, so between
the landing and 2026-08-04 nobody ran the driver.

THE FIX, three sites in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs`:

  1. line 875, `ladderStructuralFailures`'s `want`:
       boundaries: B                 ->  boundaries: R === 0 ? 0 : B
  2. line 855, the legend comment: \"boundaries === B  one registration
     per boundary, R-independent\" is now false — it is one registration
     per boundary THAT READS, and it is R-dependent only at R=0.
  3. the printed legend (~line 1029): \"boundaries = B\" wants the same
     qualification it already gives `entries` (\"B (1 at R=0)\").

At R>=1 every boundary reads R distinct keys, so every registration holds
at least one slot and `boundaries === B` — which is why only the R=0
rungs failed. Do NOT weaken the check to admit the run: it should assert
0 at R=0, which is a STRONGER statement than the one it makes now (it
pins the edgeless-boundary property the fusion was taken for).

BLOCKS rf2-zei9w, which cannot publish a magnitude until this run exits
0. rf2-zei9w's own runs are recorded on that bead but published nowhere.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7451. The expectation was stale, not the arm: rf2-dabt3 (383ba2d645) fused the sub-index into the cell table, so :boundaries counts registrations holding a reader slot rather than mounted boundaries, and 0 at R=0 is correct. Changed to R === 0 ? 0 : B at p0_run.cjs:889 plus both legends (855, 1044), and a FOURTH site the bead did not name: p0_heap.cljs:394, the producer, carried the same claim in prose. Real count of drivers carrying it: one (verify.hicasso has exactly one consumer in the tree). Nothing widened. Mutation-proved both directions through the driver's own exported witness at 6 rounds x 2 segments: stale form gives 12 failures verbatim as filed and CANNOT detect a boundary retained at R=0 (0 failures on that mutant); fixed form gives 0 on the real runtime and 12 on each mutant direction. Revert byte-identical (sha256 b8247f2c...3800). Added p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs, 14 tests in test:script-helpers, so the opt-in ladder's witness is gated on every PR. No measurement taken, no magnitude published; rf2-zei9w stays open and owns the figure.

title: hicasso: the fused reader array costs 91-92 B/read — the largest term this page has attributed to a container rather than a value
description:
MEASURED, NOT SPECULATED. rf2-zei9w's ablation attributes 91 B/read (Reagent segment) / 92 (UIx) to the cell's fused reader array — the container itself, not the membership it holds. Per-round bands are disjoint across all six rounds, the R=0 shell does not move, and donors moved 0.05/0.19 B/read, so this is a per-KEY term and the attribution is solid. Published in docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md (2026-08-04 section), PR #7452.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.

    +195/+220 figures.

BOTH instruments mount and hold. Neither has ever read an updated tree, so the
rule 2rtt6.61 proposed — a memo wrapper costs ONE fiber held and TWO updated —
must not be adopted, and is not.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. The ~2x itself. Both figures reproduce on their own
instrument and both are published against the shape they were taken on, so
nothing rests on this; it is about being able to state WHY.

THE ASK, and it is a DIFFERENT question from 2rtt6.61's. Classify FiberNode
objects in a heap snapshot on each instrument, by tag, and answer: is the
wrapper ONE fiber in both? If yes, the difference is in what a fiber HOLDS on
each shape, not in how many there are, and the programme should stop quoting a
Fiber as a fixed byte count. If no, the count itself is the finding and the
mechanism has to be named.

NOTE ON COST. No such capability exists anywhere under implementation/: a
tree-wide search for FiberNode, _reactInternals, memoizedState, queryObjects,
Runtime.queryObjects, writeHeapSnapshot and v8.getHeapSnapshot returns nothing.
The nearest scaffolding is snapshotTotal() in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs:228,
which streams HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot and sums self_size plus a raw node
count — it never reads the snapshot's strings table or a node's type/name, so
it cannot isolate FiberNode. Classification is a new instrument, not a flag.

NOT a clock bead: a snapshot classification is structural and does not need a
quiet box.

Shapes, for whoever takes it: chrome is 301 boundaries, each a 17-element card
reading two subscriptions, ~11 KB retained per boundary; the ladder rung is
1,200 R=0 cells reading nothing, ~1,141 B per boundary. An order of magnitude
apart in what the boundary holds, against a 2x in what the wrapper adds.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md,
subsection 'Why this instrument reads half of what the card-shaped one did'
(corrected 2026-08-03 under rf2-2rtt6.61).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-04 directive); operator-overturnable. 2026-08-04 04:12 AUSEST.

RULING: PARKED at P3; no instrument built. The COUNT half of the ask is now SETTLED FROM SOURCE, no snapshot needed: the wrapper is ONE extra fiber per boundary on BOTH witnesses. mint-view!'s bail-out is (react/memo f boundary-props=) — front/codec.cljs:935, a CUSTOM comparator — so React 19.2 (pinned, implementation/package.json:19) keeps a MemoComponent wrapper fiber above the component's own instead of collapsing to SimpleMemoComponent; both witnesses share that single wrapper impl (the ladder's Hicasso arm mounts via arm1.runtime/arm1.mount, p0_heap.cljs:73-74); both mount-and-hold, so no alternates (rf2-2rtt6.61). The tree already records this mechanism at arm1/runtime.cljs:1720 (:react/memo-fiber token, rf2-2rtt6.52). The bead's fork resolves YES: the ~2x is NOT a fiber-count difference.

WHAT STAYS PARKED: the BYTE-level decomposition of +195/+220 (card, ~11 KB/boundary) vs +100/+106 (R=0, ~1.14 KB). Do NOT upgrade "shapes differ" into "the delta is what the wrapper fiber holds" — both rigs read whole-isolate Runtime.getHeapUsage (chrome_run.cjs:160, p0_run.cjs:470), which attributes nothing to a constructor; retainers/topology/allocator effects are unexcluded. The tag classifier this bead spec'd would only re-confirm the settled count and cannot decompose the delta; the true instrument is a differential probe on matched memo/plain snapshots (tag counts + self_size + retainer/dominator paths) — MORE machinery than the classifier, with zero customers.

MAIN vs CODEX: both recommended park; no disposition disagreement. Codex sharpened it and every load-bearing claim verified in-tree (comparator; getHeapUsage in both rigs; 19.2 pin; the in-tree memo-fiber token matching its React-source reading). Its cheaper route answers the count free while raising the true cost of the WHY — both strengthen the park. Minor: Codex quoted the ladder as +105.5/+105.0; the published +100/+106 band stands. Rationale: the bead's own "nothing rests on this" + pre-alpha no-gold-plating posture; both figures reproduce and are published per-shape, so the record is honest without the mechanism.

DOCTRINE (adopted): a custom-comparator React.memo adds one outer MemoComponent fiber (React 19.2), but the wrapper's incremental heap price is an empirical property of the complete witness+instrument+version — NEVER a fixed "bytes per Fiber" constant. Wrapper costs are quoted per-shape, against their instrument. The studio ladder page already carries this as its practical-reading line ("a Fiber is not a fixed tax"); any future consumer-facing cost prose for the memo default quotes per-shape numbers, never a per-fiber constant.

BUILD TRIGGER (do not dispatch before one exists): a concrete customer needing the byte-level mechanism named — (a) a consumer-facing/public cost model or v0 doc for the memo default; (b) a P2 advisory or default/opt-in disposition decision turning on the mechanism; (c) a React upgrade or re-measurement moving a per-shape delta unexpectedly. Acceptance bar then: tag counts AND self_size AND retainer/dominator paths, matched snapshots, per witness.

title: clock_run.cjs REFUSES on main on every row tried (M1 and bulk300), and destroys the ex-info that would say why
description:
BLOCKER FOUND WHILE TAKING rf2-2rtt6.72's CLOCK HALF. It blocks the mount
row of rf2-2rtt6.72 and of every other bead that needs `clock_run.cjs`'s M1.

## The symptom

    HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs
    ;; HCLOCK ready
    [clock] row M1
    [clock] FAILED: M1: page.evaluate: vj
    exit 1

It dies in round 0, immediately after `HCLOCK ready`, in the first
`page.evaluate` of `runRow` — the `enterSegment` / `plan` / `canon` /
`prepare` sequence at clock_run.cjs:885-899. No `[clock] PAGE ERROR:` line
is printed, so the throw is a `page.evaluate` REJECTION and not a
`pageerror`.

## What has been ruled out, by running it rather than by reasoning

1. **Not the caller's tree.** Reproduced on pristine `origin/main`
   `1ce64c06a2`, `arm1/runtime.cljs` blob `9f3d42be7b3aa529e8fc6ef8531262ceb4d65f1a`
   — the shipped blob.
2. **Not PR #7416's `root-element` change.** `arm1/mount.cljs` reverted to
   `1c4d395374^` (the `codec/as-element` `render!` that predates the
   frame-prop landing) fails identically, same message, exit 1.
3. The bulk rows are a separate question and are being taken separately;
   this bead is about M1.

## The second, compounding fault: the message is destroyed

`vj` is not a symbol from this lane. In the `:advanced` bundle
(`implementation/out/hicasso-clock/main.js`) `vj` is
**`cljs.core/ExceptionInfo`** — its neighbours are `wj` = `ex-info` and
`xj` = `ex-data`:

    function vj(a,b){var c=Error(a);this.message=a;this.data=b; ... }
    vj.prototype.__proto__=Error.prototype;
    function wj(a,b){return new vj(a,b)}
    function xj(a){return a instanceof vj?a.data:null}

So the page threw a CLJS `ex-info` — almost certainly one of the arm's own
`fail!` calls, which carry an `:rf.error/*` id, a `:where`, a `:recovery`
and an ex-data map — and **the driver reported its minified TYPE NAME and
nothing else**. Every field that would identify the fault was discarded at
the boundary.

This is the same class PRs #7448/#7450 closed across four bench runners:
a condition that reports a token instead of the fault. Here it is worse
than a silent exit-0, because the run DOES fail loudly and still hands the
reader nothing to act on. An `ex-info` crossing `page.evaluate` needs its
`ex-message` and `ex-data` serialized — Playwright cannot do it, because
the value is not a plain `Error` and `ex-info`'s `toString` is `pr-str` of
a `#error {...}` map that minifies away.

## Suggested shape of the fix (not prescriptive)

Have the in-page entry points catch, and re-throw as a plain `js/Error`
carrying `(ex-message e)` and `(pr-str (ex-data e))`, or park the fault on
`window.HCLOCK` for the driver to read back. Then re-run M1 and diagnose
the ACTUAL fault, which is still unknown and is the real subject of this
bead. **Fixing the reporting is not fixing M1** — it is what makes M1
diagnosable.

## Repro

    node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs --selftest   # exit 0, 20+17+12 checks ok
    HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs  # exit 1

Box was quiet throughout (occupancy 2.3-3.0%, zero java, no other worker,
no open PR), so this is not a load artefact. `clock_run.cjs` blob
`0bdb9eaa6a9559775b4a67471a8a1c34c65aca9c`.
notes:
FIXED — PR #7456 (branch worker/clockerr-029ed). Both stages.

STAGE 1 (the deliverable). lane.cljs gains `legible-doors` / `describe-throw`:
a front door's functions are wrapped once, at construction, ON THE PAGE SIDE
where ex-message/ex-data are still in vocabulary, and any throw leaves as a
plain js/Error naming the door, the :rf.error id and the ex-data. Nothing is
special-cased to an id. clock_run.cjs also carries a `trace.step`, so a death
names the round and segment (and inside the sample loop the sample and arm) —
the rotating segment order no longer hides WHICH segment threw.

THE ERROR, as it now prints:
  [clock] FAILED: M1 at round 0, segment reagent-subs: page.evaluate: Error:
  enterSegment threw :rf.error/image-duplicate-id — rf/image assembly: id
  [:sub :p0/cell] is selected from 2 distinct source namespaces with different
  implementations within image nil ... — ex-data {:rf.error/id
  :rf.error/image-duplicate-id, :where rf/make-frame, :recovery
  :narrow-the-selection-or-rename-the-id, :reason "...", :image nil, :kind :sub,
  :id :p0/cell, :colliding-coordinates [{:ns "...p0-reagent-views"}
  {:ns "...clock-views"}]}

MUTATION PROOF, both directions. A known ex-info with a distinctive id thrown
from inside the first page.evaluate printed
  enterSegment threw :rf.error/mutation-probe-029ed — MUTATION PROBE rf2-029ed
  — ex-data {... :canary 4242, :seg "reagent-subs"}
i.e. id + message + every ex-data key crossed. Reverted byte-identically
(git grep for the probe is empty). A first probe attempt was refused by the
lane's own build door for `unreachable code` — that door working as designed.

REAL COUNT of front doors that swallowed ex-infos: FOUR, all the identical
`#js {...}` shape, so one line each against the shared helper — HCLOCK
(clock_app), HD8CLOCK (hd8_clock_app), C56CLOCK (shapes/census_clock_app),
HCHROME (chrome_app). All four fixed here. window.RETENTION
(retention_probe.cljs) is NOT this class and is left alone: it does not require
lane, and its one door is a heap census running no arm code.

STAGE 2 — THE ACTUAL FAULT, and it is not the runtime.
[:sub :p0/cell] is registered AT LOAD from TWO namespaces in this bundle:
p0-reagent-views/register! (the shared floor accessor every other row's arms
read) and clock-views/register-subs! (the same computation via v/cell-value,
behind the keystroke witness's recompute census). A second reg-sub from a
second namespace does NOT overwrite the first — the registrar keeps both,
tagged with provenance, and default image assembly refuses to let selection
order decide. The refusal is CORRECT. Introduced by bacb5dc4db (rf2-0qj9w,
2026-08-03), which added the second registration; the clock driver has been
dead on every row since that commit.

FIX: the override is made deliberate, through the mechanism the refusal itself
names — two composed images unioning to the whole store, the census-bearing
registration in the LATER one. That reproduces exactly the registry
register-subs!'s own docstring already describes (enter-segment! calls it on
every segment entry, for every row, so the census-bearing body was always the
intended survivor).

CONFIRMED BY THE HARNESS'S OWN WITNESS, not by argument: the keystroke row's
recompute census now reads `p0/cell x100, p0/draft x4` on ALL THREE substrate
arms and `no subscriptions at all` on every floor arm — validation.md's stated
104 layer-1 recomputes. That shape is only reachable if the census-instrumented
registration is the one the Reagent and UIx arms run.

The clock lane is unblocked: M1 and keystroke both run the full row end to end,
0 unverified writes, teardown clean.

NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN. No timing row published or amended, no figure quoted. The
two live runs were 1-round designs run to verify the driver RUNS; both exited 2
on the arm-order guard — the instrument correctly refusing a statistically
meaningless design.

GATES (all foreground to completion): test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS fast PR spine),
lint:js 0, test:hicasso-compile 0 (101 lane namespaces, zero warnings),
clock_run.cjs --selftest 0.

title: bench: three instrument gates are documented or implied but never COMPUTED — the inverse of rf2-rr6do
description:
FOUND by the rf2-rr6do sweep (PR #7450) while classifying every bench runner condition-by-condition. These are NOT the rf2-rr6do defect class — no refusal is computed and left unread — they are its INVERSE: a gate the file promises, or that every sibling has, which is never computed at all. A gate that does not exist cannot be seen to fail, which is why the sweep for printed-but-unread refusals walked straight past them.

1. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/inpage_ladder_aggregate.cjs
   Its own header (:15-16) states it exits 1 on 'a run that recorded a guard refusal or a failed control'. Nothing in the file reads any guard-refusal or control field out of the EDN datasets it aggregates; the only exit is the 'problems' array (:166-169), which reproduces the published aggregates and nothing else. An unimplemented header promise, the same shape as census_clock_run.cjs's P4 that #7450 repaired — except here there is no computed value to gate, so the repair is to compute one.

2. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs :496-509
   implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs :609-617
   Both print an in-situ positive control — predicted vs measured, error % — with NO pass/fail computed at all. Their siblings do compute one: p0_run.cjs gates control.verdict.ok on all four rows (:1309/:1326/:1341/:1364) and spine_ablation_run.cjs collects gateFailures (:561-563). A control printed without a verdict is a number beside a number.

3. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_run.cjs
   Reads four page flags (pageErrors, refused, controlFailed, orderRefused, :229-233) but NOT window.HICASSO_CLAIM_FAILED, which its near-sibling coldmount_run.cjs reads at :169 and exits 4 on. Only a real gap if the converge page ever sets that flag — CHECK THE PAGE FIRST; if it does not, close this arm as moot rather than adding a read of a flag nothing raises.

ACTIONABLE, but each needs a judgement before code: whether the promise in (1) should be implemented or withdrawn from the header, and whether (2) should adopt a control verdict or state in-file why these two rows are printed-only. Neither is a fail-open of an EXISTING gate, so neither is urgent.

TAKE NO MEASUREMENTS. Any repair here is exit-path only; no timing or allocation row may be published or amended. If a change implies a re-measurement, file it separately with the quiet-box precondition (see rf2-0qj9w / rf2-zei9w / rf2-t0j8b for the established wording).

comments.text:
2026-08-04 04:17 AUSEST — delegated dossier-review ruling (Mike's 2026-08-04 directive); operator-overturnable.

The 4 EDNs store all 900 samples ([round arm ms], 6 rounds x 150) in measured order, proven 1:1 with the page's guard stream (rounds-async! conj's rows at the same site as lane/collect!, warmups excluded from both; collect! = {arm value predecessor=prev position=index}, lane.cljs:472-491). A stricter every-round rule would retro-fail run D ONLY (one round 1.2653 < band floor 1.4819) — and lane.cljs:848-876 already records overlap-vs-strict as a KNOWN DEFECT reserved to operator ruling rf2-2rtt6.1 (rf2-egdaq); a stricter aggregate would front-run that open ruling.
- Arm 2: b7_run.cjs:90 and reads_ladder_run.cjs:124 TOLERANCE=0.25 is the ARM-ORDER guard knob — numeric coincidence with control slack, keep them separate. p0_run.cjs precedent confirmed (core bench p0_run.cjs: CONTROL_SLACK env||0.25 at :135, lane-rule verdict over {min,max,mean}, verdict stored beside the control :680-687, report-then-gate :1339/:1356/:1371). spine_ablation CONTROL_BAND=0.01 is specially justified (0.13% noise floor) — NOT the precedent. title: MEASURE: M1's mount row is still stated under a control that FAILS — ctl-2x undershoots 1.8173x and no changed-set control can reach a mount
description:
RAISED by rf2-7iqb5's three-point control work (PR #7367).

THE GAP. rf2-7iqb5 built the three-point control rf2-emvod ruled and it applies
to BULK rows only. A mount row's operation IS the mount: there is no standing
page to write a changed set into, so there is no changed-set axis to be linear
in. M1 therefore keeps ctl-2x and keeps its measured 1.8173x undershoot against
a 2.00x prediction.

WHY IT MATTERS. M1 carries the programme's headline mount figure -- hicasso /
reagent-subs 1.4896x [1.3488 - 1.5989], the number the operator's 2026-08-02
continuation ruling was taken against. That magnitude is currently published
under a positive control that FAILS, which is exactly the condition the strict
rule refuses bulk rows for. The asymmetry is not defensible on its own terms:
either the rule binds on M1 too, or the reason it does not is stated.

WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN, from rf2-7iqb5's runs:
  * c is real and re-measured independently -- c(2x) = 1.0397 ms on bulk300
    against rf2-emvod's 1.043 ms -- so ctl-2x's undershoot on M1 is explained
    by the same additive constant, not by anything about mounts.
  * The three-point ARITHMETIC is sound: on LayoutDuration the statistic reads
    1.9703 / 2.1218 / 1.9889x against a predicted 2.0101x.
  * The instrument's noise floor forbids a strict per-block difference-of-
    differences verdict: sigma(T)/T <= s/(2 sqrt2 . T/dT) needs ~3.5% against a
    measured within-block IQR of 28-48%. A mount-axis three-point control
    (mount 150 / 300 / 600 cells, predicted 3.00x) would face the SAME noise
    condition, so it is not obviously buildable either.

THE CANDIDATE CONSTRUCTIONS, neither yet tried:
  1. A three-point control on the MOUNT axis -- 150 / 300 / 600 boundaries,
     adjudicated (T(600)-T(150))/(T(300)-T(150)) -> 3.00x. Differences c away
     on the axis a mount row actually varies. Costs two more arms on M1 and
     inherits the noise condition above.
  2. Accept that M1 has no passing control and RESTATE the row as such --
     i.e. apply the same refusal the bulk rows get, which would withdraw
     1.4896x as a magnitude and leave it a regime.

Which of those is right is a RULING, not a measurement. Do not dispatch as
implementation until Mike has ruled.

Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/a-control-that-differences-the-constant-away.md section 7.
notes:
INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED IN rf2-0qj9w's QUIET WINDOW, 2026-08-04, ON A BOX VERIFIED IDLE AT BOTH ENDS. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7459.

This bead's gap is not a property of a loaded box, and the window rules that out as an explanation. Occupancy was 1.484% at open and 1.796% at close, measured as summed per-process CPU-time deltas over the core count; no other worker, no open PR, no live gate.

ctl-2x on M1 read 1.8443x [1.3837 - 2.4233] on raw TaskDuration and 1.8319x [1.3114 - 2.4745] on taskNet, over 18 segment-rounds, against 2.00x +/-25% under the strict every-round rule. At least one round fell below the 1.5 floor, so the row REFUSED and clock_run.cjs exited 1 naming it. Every other gate on the run cleared — arm-order guard reportable, canonical DOM identical, 0 unverified of 1008, band 21.4% against the 35% ceiling — so the control is the sole obstruction, exactly as this bead states.

THE ADDITIVE CONSTANT RE-MEASURED, a third independent reading: c(2x) = 0.8284 ms [-1.6220 - 3.5490] over 18 blocks, from floor_tared 4.6573 ms and ctl-2x/floor 1.8443x. That is c/W = 0.2164 — 17.8% of a floor sample does not scale with the page. It sits alongside rf2-7iqb5's 1.0397 ms and rf2-emvod's 1.043 ms on bulk300; this one is on M1's own mount samples, which is the reading this bead did not yet have. The description's diagnosis holds: ctl-2x's undershoot on M1 is the same additive constant, not anything about mounts.

WHAT THE WINDOW ADDS TO THE RULING CHOICE. This bead offers two constructions and says which is right is a ruling. One datum now bears on construction 1 (a three-point control on the MOUNT axis, 150/300/600): the description already warns it inherits a noise condition needing ~3.5% against a measured within-block IQR of 28-48%, and the window's band on a fully idle box was 21.4%, in the regime the-candidates-clock.md sec 6.2 measured as WIDEST AT ZERO LOAD (24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3% at four, corr(band, floor) = -0.49). So the quietest achievable box is the WORST case for that construction's noise condition, not the best. A mount-axis three-point control cannot be bought with scheduling.

title: eslint lints the gitignored .shadow-cljs build output, so npm run lint:js exits 1 after any local :advanced build
description:
After any local :advanced build (e.g. a hicasso bench driver, which builds into implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/<id>/release/), `npm run lint:js` from the repo root reports ~587 errors from implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/*/release/externs.shadow.js and exits 1.

Reproduced 2026-08-04 on worker/clockerr-029ed: HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node .../clock_run.cjs, then npm run lint:js -> 590 problems (587 errors), every error in externs.shadow.js (no-unused-vars on AbortController/Map/NaN/..., no-shadow-restricted-names on NaN/globalThis). Deleting implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench/release and re-running -> exit 0.

implementation/.gitignore line 2 already ignores .shadow-cljs/, so this is generated output that is not source. eslint's ignore config does not exclude it. CI never sees it because a fresh checkout has no .shadow-cljs, so the gate is green there and red only locally — which is the wrong way round: it trains a developer to disbelieve their own lint run.

Fix: add .shadow-cljs/ (and any other generated build output) to the eslint ignores alongside the existing ones. Small.

Found while fixing rf2-029ed; not caused by it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7460 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7460).

ROOT CAUSE, beyond the missing entry: eslint.config.mjs's ignore block asserted that 'node_modules and dotted directories are ESLint defaults'. Flat config ignores exactly two paths of its own accord — **/node_modules/ and .git/ (eslint/lib/config/default-config.js:68, ESLint 10.8.0). Dot-directories in general were the OLD .eslintrc behaviour. That belief is why .shadow-cljs/ was never listed, so the comment was corrected, not merely extended — otherwise the next generated dot-directory gets omitted the same way.

COVERED, derived from the repo's own fourteen .gitignore files and narrowed to trees that can carry JS:
  **/.shadow-cljs/**           8811 JS files in a fully built checkout (vs 215 tracked JS files in the whole repo)
  **/resources/public/js/**    shadow-cljs :output-dir (minimal-counter example + tools/template scaffold)
  **/public/js/compiled/**     shadow-cljs :output-dir (skills/re-frame2-pair)
  .claude/worktrees/**         whole second copies of the source tree
  examples/.edge-cdp/**        Chrome user-data-dir from the CDP runs

NOT added, each checked rather than assumed: .cpcache/ (34 dirs in a built checkout, zero JS), __pycache__/, .dolt/, .scratch/ (EDN/CLJS fixtures), docs/{spec,migration}/ (staged copies of markdown-only trees).

MUTATION PROOF, both directions:
  - With real :advanced output present: before exit 1 / 542 errors, after exit 0. Then the stronger version — scripts/test-fast-pr.sh itself compiles and leaves 2685 generated JS files, and lint:js is exit 0 afterwards; the old config would have put 161 extra generated files in scope. Running the repo's own canonical local gate is by itself enough to arm this defect.
  - Fail-open check: file census before/after is 307 -> 214 inspected, ALL of the loss under .shadow-cljs (93 -> 0); implementation/ 233 -> 140 and tools/51, examples/13, docs/6, testbeds/2, scripts/1 all unchanged. 214 matches the tracked-file census exactly. A live no-undef + no-unused-vars injected into two real tracked files (one under implementation/, one under examples/) still exits 1 naming both, with build output present; reverted byte-identically (sha256sum -c OK, git diff clean).

No rule was touched, relaxed or disabled, and no suppression comment was added — the fix is what gets linted, not which rules apply.

Gates: npm run lint:js (root, CI form) exit 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, terminal marker 'PASS fast PR spine' present.

Filed rf2-o4ohg (P4) for three pre-existing dead eslint-disable directives in adoption_witness_run.cjs — warnings only, non-blocking, untouched by this PR.

value:
A BEAD'S DESCRIPTION READS FIRST AND CAN BE OLDER THAN ITS COMMENTS — I DISPATCHED THE SAME ALREADY-DONE WORK TWICE (rf2-2rtt6.31, 2026-08-04).

WHAT HAPPENED. I dispatched rf2-2rtt6.31 ("re-take HD-008's donor rows") and, having learned that paraphrase loses distinctions, quoted its DESCRIPTION verbatim into the brief — WHAT TO DO, WHY, the BLOCKED-BY note, the FENCES, and the pre-registered ~1.13-1.22x prediction. All accurate. All superseded. A 2026-08-02 COMMENT on the same bead records that the work was ALREADY DONE and PUBLISHED: commit 1ac48c4a0b, PR #7378, every commissioned deliverable present in hd8-composed-donor-arm.md — the re-take section, the provenance table with SHA and both reproduce commands, all three adapter runs, rows published beside the originals, the bulk row fenced against rf2-d2tzk by name, and the stop rule stated plainly. The worker read the whole record, found the conflict, refused to take a second draw, and told me. Its closing line: "this is the SECOND dispatch to re-take rows that were already taken. The bead's description and its newer comment describe different work, and the description is what reads first."

THE MECHANISM, and it is not the same as the NOTES-vs-COMMENTS blindness. That earlier failure was a tool that could not SEE a field. This one is ordering: bd show prints DESCRIPTION before COMMENTS/NOTES, a description is written once at filing and rarely amended, and comments accrete. So the OLDEST text is the most prominent and reads as current. Quoting the description verbatim — the very discipline I adopted to stop paraphrase errors — made this WORSE, because it lent stale text the authority of a direct quote.

THE RULE: BEFORE DISPATCHING, READ THE BEAD BOTTOM-UP. The newest comment or note is the operative one; the description is the oldest thing on the record. If they describe different work, the later text governs and the description is history. Say so explicitly in the brief rather than quoting the description as though it were live.

COROLLARY FOR VERIFICATION: "is this already done?" is answered by the tree and the bead's own tail, not by the bead's status. rf2-2rtt6.31 was OPEN with its acceptance ALREADY PUBLISHED — open meant "residual items remain", not "the work has not been done". Check what is on main before commissioning a measurement; a published row is cheaper to read than to re-take, and re-taking one after reading its result creates a selection opportunity that invalidates both draws.

WHAT THE WORKER DID RIGHT, and it is the general lesson: it declined the second draw because "having read the published results, taking a competing draw without a pre-registered rule for which one counts is exactly the selection opportunity the brief forbids." Reading a result changes what a later measurement means. That is true whoever takes it.

title: docs(hicasso): HD-011 dated addendum — the activated :ssr policy and the gate's cost (from rf2-2rtt6.85)
description:
SEQUENCED OUT OF rf2-2rtt6.85, NOT DROPPED. rf2-2rtt6.85 (defhost's :ssr policy) shipped the code and its fence named 'docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md (HD-011 addendum)' as in-scope for the same PR. The dispatching brief overrode that on sequencing grounds: rf2-2rtt6.83 owns the SSR doc record and was being dispatched in the same wave onto decisions.md, and decisions.md is sequential-never-parallel. The worker followed the brief, edited no docs, and filed this.

THE WORK (docs only): a dated addendum blockquote atop HD-011 (model: the HD-019 IME addendum, commit 0342d3787d), recording:

1. THE ACTIVATED SHAPE. defhost's opts carry :ssr with exactly two values — :client-only (the DEFAULT, applied when :ssr is absent: the host region renders nothing until the client adopts the markup) and {:fallback <hiccup>} (that markup renders there instead). Any other value, an explicit nil, an empty or multi-key fallback map, and any opts key outside #{:callbacks :ssr} are all refused AT THE DECLARATION (:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy, :rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option). The fallback hiccup is walked once at mint, so a fallback that is not hiccup also fails at the declaration.

2. THE MECHANISM, and that it is ONE. Each declaration mints a gate whose single useSyncExternalStore answers false from its SERVER snapshot and true from its client one. That covers the server render (renderToString honours the policy by rendering, so no server walk needs to know about it), hydration's first client pass (same markup as the server, nothing to reconcile) and a fresh createRoot mount (component on the first pass, no placeholder flash).

3. THE COST, WHICH CHANGED A RECORDED PROPERTY. Before this, the door minted no wrapper, no fiber and no hook — the foreign component was the element's own type, and arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test witnessed exactly one useSyncExternalStore on a hosted page. It now mints one gate per declaration, so a crossing costs ONE fiber and ONE hook. HD-020(b)'s <=2-hook BOUNDARY-shell budget is untouched (shell-hook-ledger still declares two; the gate holds no subscription and reads no frame), and the witness was updated to state the new truth rather than deleted. This is the one thing on this bead an operator might want to price rather than merely record.

Also worth a line in HD-020(d), whose 'defhost's SSR-placeholder default is declared policy for later phases, inert in v0' is now false — though rf2-2rtt6.83's HD-020 addendum may already cover it, in which case say so and do not write it twice.

FENCES: docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md only. SEQUENCE AFTER rf2-2rtt6.83 — same file. Outside mkdocs --strict, so anchors and table column counts are hand-verified and said so in the PR body (check_doc_slugs.py must pass).

MY INLINE REAP DELETED A WORKTREE WHILE ITS WORKER WAS STILL GATING, AND THE GATE FAILED FALSELY (2026-08-04).

WHAT HAPPENED. Earlier in the session I twice merged a PR and forgot to reap its worktree, so I folded the reap INTO the merge loop to make it unskippable. That fixed the leak and introduced a worse failure: a worker was still running the fast-PR spine in the worktree I deleted. PR #7469 merged at 02:24:42 UTC; the branch and worktree were removed; the worker's spine finished at 02:24:53, eleven seconds later, reading a directory that no longer existed. It reported FAIL implementation JS harness helpers with 11 reagent-slim policy failures, all of the form "Cannot find module", "missing workflow: .github/workflows/test.yml", "missing changed-surfaces script" -- files that are tracked in git and were present. The worker correctly discarded the result under the killed-gate rule and confirmed the CI counterpart was SUCCESS on main.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS BEYOND THE WASTED RUN. The failure LOOKS like a real policy regression naming real files. A worker with less discipline would have "fixed" the missing modules, or reported a red that does not exist. It is the mirror of the backgrounded-gate bug we fixed today, where a relative invocation graded ANOTHER worktree: same class, opposite direction -- the gate reads a tree that is not the one it thinks it is reading.

THE RULE: A MERGE DOES NOT MEAN THE WORKER HAS EXITED. The PR opening is the worker's LAST reported act, not its last act -- it may still be running gates, updating the PR body, or answering a message. Before reaping a worktree, confirm the worker is actually done: no live agent for that bead, or the worktree quiescent across a tick. When in doubt, leave the worktree; a stale directory costs disk, a deleted one costs a false red and possibly a spurious "fix".

THE CORRECTED SHAPE: keep the reap adjacent to the merge so it cannot be forgotten, but gate it on the worker being finished rather than on the PR being merged. Reaping on the NEXT tick after the merge is the cheap approximation and is what I should do by default.

RELATED, SAME SESSION: the same worker corrected two claims of mine. Local clj-kondo here is 2025.10.23 while CI pins 2026.04.15; the local build reports 0 errors on the line CI fails and 10 different errors CI does not, so a local clj-kondo pass proves nothing about the gate -- fetch the pinned binary. And my "the tree has exactly one suppression" figure was ESLINT's census applied to CLJ-KONDO: there are at least four #_:clj-kondo/ignore sites. A census of one linter says nothing about another.

title: hicasso SSR: activate HD-011's placeholder — defhost :ssr policy (:client-only default, :fallback)
description:
ACTIVATE HD-011'S SSR PLACEHOLDER — defhost :ssr policy. From the 2026-08-04 SSR design programme (consensus on the epic). HD-011 declared "fns pass through, SSR placeholder" as defhost policy; the 2026-08-04 runtime audit found the placeholder is ABSENT, not inert: mint-host! reads only :callbacks and SILENTLY IGNORES every other option (front/codec.cljs:1036).

THE WORK (bench lane):
1. defhost gains an :ssr option: :client-only (DEFAULT — the host region renders nothing server-side) or {:fallback <hiccup>} (server + pre-adoption placeholder markup). Any other value = mint-time refusal. While here: mint-host! refuses UNKNOWN options loudly instead of ignoring them (the silent-ignore is its own defect).
2. Client behaviour: a host boundary renders its placeholder/nothing during hydration adoption and the real component after adoption (and immediately on fresh non-hydrated mounts). Implementation sketch from the design record: the host shell's single useSyncExternalStore((noop), ()=>true, ()=>false) yields false during server/hydration first pass, true after — no new hooks beyond the shell budget (<=2, HD-020), no fake hook dispatcher ever (HD-021(a)).
3. Server behaviour lands with the Node-entry bead (sibling): the server walk consults the same :ssr policy. This bead makes the policy REAL on the client and mint-time.
4. Witnesses: mint-time refusal row; :client-only host absent from a hydration fixture's server HTML then mounted after adoption; {:fallback} host's placeholder present in server HTML then swapped after adoption with no mismatch warning.

HD addendum: record the activated shape as a dated HD-011 addendum in the same PR (rf2-digtt pattern).

FENCES: bench lane + docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md (HD-011 addendum) only. Coordinate with the hydration-door bead if both touch runtime.cljs; front/codec.cljs is this bead's primary file.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7468 (2026-08-04) — REOPENED: the promised mint-time fallback refusal is incomplete.

Landed evidence: front/codec.cljs:1068 declared-ssr accepts any one-key fallback map whose value is merely non-nil. mint-host-gate! then calls the deliberately permissive as-element; at front/codec.cljs:1749 its final branch returns an unrecognised value unchanged. Consequently a declaration such as {:ssr {:fallback {}}} mints successfully, then hands a ClojureScript map to React during server render or hydration, where it fails late as a non-renderable object. Raw JS objects and other unsupported values have the same hole. The only negative witness uses [], which vec->element already rejects, so it does not cover the permissive fallthrough.

title: hicasso SSR: the Node render entry — renderToString of the existing runtime, fixture bake, live dogfood demo
description:
THE NODE RENDER ENTRY + FIXTURE BAKE + LIVE DEMO — one renderer, run in two places. From the 2026-08-04 SSR design programme (consensus on the epic): the server engine is the EXISTING Hicasso runtime under Node react-dom/server renderToString — hydration parity by construction, no second renderer anywhere.

WHY THIS IS SAFE (verified in the programme): every shell already passes getServerSnapshot (arm1/runtime.cljs:1540/:1595), so under renderToString React never subscribes, every sub read is the mutation-free cold probe, commits/effects never run — the render is HD-002's abandoned render by design, leaving zero durable registration (the ledger discipline holds). react-dom 19.2.0 ships server.node.js (pinned); the runtime already loads under Node on every PR.

THE WORK (bench lane):
1. The render entry: a Node namespace that (a) makes a per-request gensym frame, (b) seeds app-db via the framework doors (:initial-events / snapshot-in), (c) renders (provider frame (codec/root-element frame hiccup)) via renderToString, (d) builds the payload with the FRAMEWORK'S OWN bytes — ssr apply-policy + build-payload + escape-edn-script-body producing the #__rf_payload EDN script — nothing Hicasso-specific in the payload path (R0), (e) destroys the frame after render (destroy-frame! — lifecycle verified sound, frame.cljc:2076-2091; no per-request leak).
2. Determinism: same bundle + same snapshot means byte-identical HTML (SHA-256 double-render check in the driver). Verified in the programme: no useId anywhere, no randomness on the render path (the lane's seeded LCG stands), comment separators deterministic; renderToString runs synchronously so module-level render context is sound per-request. NO streaming — renderToPipeableStream is out of scope, per adversarial review.
3. The BAKE: a driver producing static HTML+payload fixtures in the existing SSR-testbed pattern (testbeds/ssr_basic bakes at build time — reuse the shape), for the witness bead's X-rows and as the standing conformance corpus (feature census over the dogfood + tier-1 shapes).
4. The LIVE DEMO driver: a minimal node script that serves the dogfood screen per-request (frame, render, payload, HTML out). PAGE-LEVEL, bench-lane, explicitly NOT a production host: Spec 011's HTTP response contract (accumulator, cookies, redirects, CRLF fail-fast) stays ssr-ring's; this driver exists so live per-request Hicasso SSR is DEMONSTRABLE at the P2 sitting (the adapters demo live SSR; Hicasso must too).
5. Build id: FIRST try to carry this on existing node-build infrastructure (:freehand-bench-node pattern, shadow-cljs.edn:1067); mint :hicasso-ssr-node ONLY if needed — a shadow-cljs.edn edit is HOT-ZONE and must be sequenced by the mayor, stated in the PR.
6. defhost regions honour the :ssr policy (sibling bead) server-side: :client-only renders nothing; {:fallback ...} renders the fallback hiccup.

FENCES: bench lane (+ possibly one sequenced shadow-cljs.edn hot-zone edit). No implementation/ssr edits — its payload fns are consumed, not modified. No ssr-ring edits. The production host story is NOT this bead: it is priced and ruled at the P2/graduation sitting (see the ruling-prep bead).

title: hicasso SSR: the Node render entry must open the adoption window around renderToString (presence ships ::h/mounting overrides)
description:

as a corpus row + a red-when-fixed witness rather than left as an argument.

THE DEFECT. `arm1/presence.cljs` starts a child at `:mounting`
(`(react/useState presence/initial)`) and applies that child's `::h/mounting`
attribute overrides for as long as it is in that phase. The SSR entry renders
with no adoption window open — it cannot open one, see below — so the server
HTML ships the ENTER appearance: the class (and, in the shapes that use one, the
`opacity: 0` style) an animation is about to move off.

rf2-2rtt6.84 makes the hydrating client's FIRST pass render those same children
`:present` instead — born-present under an open adoption window, its clause 3.
Server markup and client first pass then disagree, and React reports a hydration
mismatch on every presence-managed node. That is exactly the class rf2-2rtt6.87's
X-rows exist to catch, and it is better caught here.

MEASURED. `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/fixtures.cljs`
carries a `presence-mounting` corpus row whose children declare `::h/mounting
{:class "toast--enter"}`; the baked fixture contains `toast--enter` twice.
`the-server-render-ships-presences-mounting-overrides` in
`ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs` asserts that, with a non-vacuity control that the
tray rendered its children at all. The row is written to go RED when the repair
lands — its docstring says to delete it and assert the opposite.

THE REPAIR, AND WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN .86. One line: `renderToString` in
`ssr/entry.cljs` must run between `runtime/open-adoption-window!` and
`runtime/close-adoption-window!`. NEITHER FUNCTION EXISTS ON MAIN — both are in
rf2-2rtt6.84's PR #7469, still open at the time .86 was written. A call to a var
that does not exist does not compile, and guessing at one is how two beads come
to race one file. So .86 named the gap in `ssr/entry.cljs`'s docstring (§The one
thing this entry does not do yet) and filed this.

BLOCKED ON: rf2-2rtt6.84 merging.

ALSO CHECK WHEN WIRING IT: #7469 puts the hydrated root's shape in one place
(`mount/tree`, keyed off `:hydrated?`) — a Fragment carrying the
adoption-window closer beside the app, because React reconciles a root by its
top element and a bare provider tore the adopted tree down. The SSR entry builds
its own root shape today (`(mount/provider frame … (codec/root-element …))`);

title: hicasso SSR: reconcile the server :ssr policy READ with rf2-2rtt6.85's WRITE (slot spelling + nested-host coverage)
description:
rf2-2rtt6.86 landed the SERVER half of `defhost`'s `:ssr` policy — which
rf2-2rtt6.85's own clause 3 hands to the Node-entry bead — while rf2-2rtt6.85
(the OPTION, the mint-time refusal, the client adoption behaviour) had not
landed. Two seams were therefore made ahead of their other half, both isolated
deliberately, and both need one pass once .85 is on main.

1. THE SLOT SPELLING. `ssr/host_policy.cljs` reads the policy off ONE own
property, `host-policy/policy-slot` (currently the string "ssr"), in ONE reader
(`policy-of`). If rf2-2rtt6.85's `mint-host!` stores it under a different
property, this is a one-line change plus a witness that a `defhost … {:ssr …}`
declaration is what the server walk actually reads — which nothing proves today,
because the fallback row stamps the slot by hand.

2. NESTED HOSTS. `host-policy/apply-policy` walks the hiccup the render entry is
HANDED: the root tree and everything reachable through vectors and seqs
(including inside a `for`, witnessed). A host minted inside a boundary BODY is
NOT in that tree — the body runs inside `renderToString` and the codec's own
crossing creates its element, and `front/codec.cljs` is rf2-2rtt6.85's file, not
.86's. The consensus architecture covers that case from the other side:
rf2-2rtt6.85's host shell reads adoption through
`useSyncExternalStore(…, …, (constantly false))`, so under `renderToString`
React takes the server snapshot and the region renders its placeholder without
the walk touching it.

THAT IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT A WITNESS. The work here is a fixture with a
`:client-only` host and a `{:fallback …}` host declared INSIDE a defview body,
asserted on the SERVER HTML through the SSR entry — and then a ruling on whether
two mechanisms for one policy is the right shape or whether one should be
retired in favour of the other.

FILES: `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/host_policy.cljs`
+ `ssr/fixtures.cljs` + `ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs` (bench lane).
notes:
VERIFIED AGAINST #7468 BY rf2-2rtt6.86 (2026-08-04), which sharpens this bead
from "reconcile" to "RETIRE the server walk":

1. THE SLOT SPELLING AGREES. #7468 stores the policy on the minted head under
the own-property "ssr" and reads it back with `codec/host-ssr`
(`(unchecked-get head "ssr")`) — the same property `host-policy/policy-slot`
names and the same read `host-policy/policy-of` performs. No mis-read is
possible in either merge order; a `{:fallback …}` host is never taken for a
`:client-only` one.

2. THE GATE SUPERSEDES THE WALK. #7468 enforces the policy AT THE ELEMENT'S
TYPE: `mint-host-gate!` wraps the foreign component in a gate whose
`useSyncExternalStore(noop, (constantly true), (constantly false))` answers
false under `renderToString`, so the gate renders the pre-walked fallback
element — or nothing — with no walk involved. That mechanism reaches a host
minted inside a boundary BODY, which the walk cannot, and costs no per-request
tree rebuild. #7468 carries its own server witness
(`the-server-render-honours-the-policy`).

3. BOTH MECHANISMS AGREE ON MARKUP, so merging in either order is safe:
`:client-only` renders nothing either way, `{:fallback hic}` renders `hic`
either way, and if both are live the walk simply gets there first.

"PR OPENED" IS NOT "WORKER FINISHED" — I BROKE THE SAME ASSUMPTION TWICE IN ONE SESSION, IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS (2026-08-04).

INSTANCE 1, THE REAP RACE. I folded worktree-reaping into the merge loop so I could not forget it. A worker was still running the fast-PR spine in the tree I deleted: PR merged 02:24:42, worktree removed, spine finished 02:24:53 and reported FAIL implementation JS harness helpers with 11 "Cannot find module" failures naming files that are tracked and present. It looked like a real policy regression.

INSTANCE 2, THE DISPATCH RACE, and this one is worse. PR #7474 could not merge because main had moved, so I dispatched a rebase worker onto the SAME BRANCH. The original worker had not exited -- it was still resolving that very conflict. Its worktree's .git file was deleted underneath it and a new worktree appeared holding its branch at its own rebased SHA. It handled this better than I did: it verified the branch tip carried its complete resolution and pushed a ref-only update from the mayor checkout rather than racing, then flagged the orphaned directory. Nothing was lost, but only because the worker was careful.

THE COMMON ERROR: I treated the PR opening as the worker's last act. It is its last REPORTED act. After opening a PR a worker may still be running gates, updating the PR body, answering a message, or -- as here -- resolving a conflict I asked about.

THE RULES:
1. BEFORE REAPING A WORKTREE: require the worker to be finished, not the PR to be merged. The cheap approximation is to reap on the NEXT tick, once the tree is quiescent.
2. BEFORE DISPATCHING ONTO AN EXISTING BRANCH: confirm no live worker holds it. If a PR needs a rebase or a fix and its worker may still be alive, SEND THAT WORKER A MESSAGE instead of dispatching a second one. Resuming an existing worker is cheaper and cannot race.
3. A branch with a live worktree is CLAIMED. Treat a worktree the way you would treat an IN_PROGRESS bead.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE WASTED RUN: both failure modes produce evidence that looks real. A deleted worktree yields a gate failure naming real files that are present; a hijacked branch yields two agents with divergent views of the same tip. Neither announces itself as an infrastructure fault, and both invite a "fix" for a defect that does not exist.

title: hicasso SSR: the arm's hydrate door passes no onRecoverableError — a mismatch is an UNCAUGHT pageerror, not a diagnostic
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-2rtt6.87 SSR spike witness while building X2's mutation proof.

THE FINDING. arm1/mount/hydrate-root! calls react-dom-client/hydrateRoot with NO root options, so React's DEFAULT onRecoverableError runs — reportError — and a recoverable hydration mismatch becomes an UNCAUGHT window error. Measured: hydrating the 8-row dogfood screen against 9-row server bytes produced exactly one complaint, and it arrived as 'window.error: Uncaught Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client'.

WHY IT MATTERS THREE WAYS.
1. The browser lane's runner treats ANY uncaught pageerror as fatal whatever the cljs.test tally says (rf2-mwx08). So a Hicasso row that deliberately or accidentally hydrates mismatched markup REDS THE WHOLE BROWSER GATE with no way to attribute it. rf2-2rtt6.87's mutation proof had to call preventDefault on the error event (open-console-capture!'s :swallow-uncaught?, one call site, documented) to keep the gate honest — that is a workaround at the witness, not a repair at the door.
2. THE TWO SIBLINGS ALREADY DO IT. re-frame.substrate.spine/hydrate-root-options builds an :on-recoverable-error option and emits the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch diagnostic from it (rf2-qfz65); arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test's own hydrate! passes onRecoverableError explicitly and says why. arm1/mount is the outlier.
3. Spec 011 carries :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch as the framework's own diagnostic. A door that never emits it is a door whose mismatches are invisible to every tool that reads the instrumentation stream.

THE WORK. Give arm1/mount/hydrate-root! the spine's shape: an options map carrying :onRecoverableError that emits the framework diagnostic, gated the way the spine gates it (hydrate-root-options answers nil in production). Then rf2-2rtt6.87's :swallow-uncaught? call site can go — its docstring names this bead as the reason it exists.

NOT A BLOCKER for rf2-2rtt6.87: every X-row published with the door as it stands, and the mutation proof measured the mismatch on the channels the witness watches. This is about what a CONSUMER of the door sees, not about the spike's readings.
close_reason:

title: hicasso: implement h/reg-state — the instance-key sugar (explicit-key ruling, 2026-08-04)
description:
IMPLEMENT h/reg-state — the instance-key sugar, per the 2026-08-04 ruled design (3 designs, 3 adversarial reviews, unanimous synthesis on the epic; operator ruled the feature INTO v0, amending HD-009). Bench lane.

THE SURFACE (exact; do not grow it):
1. (h/reg-state ::concern {:default v}) — a plain .cljc FUNCTION (not a macro). One namespace-qualified concern keyword; {:default v} is the ONLY option; unknown options refused loudly at registration. It mints, as ORDINARY core artefacts (no new runtime state, no hooks, no context — nothing for the anti-regression fence to catch):
   • parametric sub: (sub [::concern ikey]) -> (get-in db [:ui ::concern ikey] default)
   • concern-named setter event: [::concern ikey v] -> assoc-in
   • the documented path [:ui ::concern ikey] (the tier: ONE app-space conventional root, concern-first; per-frame free because app-db is per-frame; NEVER an :rf/* app-db root — Conventions two-partition doctrine).
2. Clear is a FRAMEWORK-NAMED EVENT, not a value sentinel: [::h/clear ::concern ikey] restores the default by REMOVING the entry (dissoc-in; empty concern maps pruned). The value-sentinel variant (::h/clear in v position) is REJECTED by the ruling — a keyword-valued concern could silently dissoc.
3. Loud refusals: nil or non-(keyword|string|number|vector-of-these) instance keys refuse at read AND write with :rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-key naming the concern — converting the guide's silent every-instance-shares pitfall into a loud error. Registration refuses a non-namespaced concern kw and unknown options.
4. (h/child-key k part) => (if (vector? k) (conj k part) [k part]) — the one pure composition helper for widget-in-widget nesting.

WITNESSES (unit + DOM, bench lane): two instances of one widget with distinct ikeys are independent; same ikey shares (and that is stated as correct); [::h/clear ...] restores default and removes the entry (db shape asserted, pruning included); bad-key refusal fires on nil and on a map key, naming the concern; frames isolated (two frames, same concern+ikey, independent state); h/child-key induction (nested widget forms [parent-key part] and deep-nests conj); HD-028 memo bail-out unaffected by fresh-but-equal key vectors (value equality row). Register-twice behaviour: re-registration with a different :default refuses (or last-wins with a loud warn — pick the stricter, state it).

TAUGHT RULES the implementation does NOT police (they land in the guide bead, but your docstrings state them in one line each): domain ids first; entity-qualified id VALUES ({:id [:order/id 42]}) when one widget serves multiple entity types (bare-id cross-entity bleed); placement-like concerns key by placement, value-like by entity; "if it would be a good React :key, it is a good instance key" (SSR determinism); graduation to named domain events when an occurrence means more than an assignment.

value:
MTIME ON THE WORKTREE IS NOT A QUIESCENCE SIGNAL — MY FOURTH WORKTREE-REMOVED-MID-GATE, WITH THE FIX ALREADY IN PLACE (2026-08-04).

WHAT I HAD ALREADY DONE. After three instances of reaping a worktree while its worker was still gating, I replaced "reap when the PR is MERGED" with "reap when the PR is MERGED **and** the tree has been idle >= 10 minutes", idleness read from the mtime of the worktree's implementation/ directory.

WHY IT STILL FAILED. The rf2-2rtt6.99 worker was running its SECOND fast-PR spine when I reaped. The mtime check said 34 minutes idle. It was wrong: a running spine does not necessarily touch the directory I stat. Its work goes to out/, .shadow-cljs/, a temp dir, or a detached child process, and none of that has to bump implementation/ itself. The worker's run died with "bash: ./.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh: No such file or directory" for a script that plainly exists -- the fourth false red of this exact class today, and the second whose symptom names a real file.

NOTE THE SCRIPT PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED, WHICH IS ITS OWN HAZARD. remove-worker-worktree.sh disarmed the node_modules link and DEREGISTERED the worktree, then failed to delete the directory on a Windows file lock and reported REMOVE_FAILED honestly. So the tree was already gutted -- node_modules emptied, git worktree list no longer listing it -- before the failure. A partial reap is as fatal to a running gate as a complete one.

THE RULE, and I have now been wrong three ways about it: PR STATE is not worker state; ELAPSED TIME is not worker state; DIRECTORY MTIME is not worker state. The only reliable signals are (a) the agent that owns the bead has reported completion, or (b) no process has a working directory inside that tree. Everything else is a proxy that has failed in practice.

WHAT I SHOULD DO INSTEAD: do not reap on the same tick a PR merges, and do not reap any worktree whose owning agent has not yet delivered its completion report. Those reports arrive as task notifications; until one lands for that bead, the worker may be mid-gate no matter how quiet the tree looks. Cost of waiting: a stale directory. Cost of not waiting: a red that names real files as missing, four times today, twice mistakable for a genuine regression.

WHAT THE AFFECTED WORKERS DID RIGHT, every time: discarded the exit code under the killed-gate rule rather than reporting it, said plainly which coverage was therefore unmeasured, and named the cheap substitute check. The rf2-2rtt6.99 worker flagged npm run ssr:hicasso-bake as its one unmeasured gate; I ran it on the mayor checkout in 30 seconds -- exit 0, 8 fixtures, both new rows baked clean.

title: Story full-gate runner changes can merge without executing the gate
description:

title: hicasso SSR: the hydration door's two stated limits — one adoption window per page, no onRecoverableError door
description:
Follow-ups RECORDED (not defects) by rf2-2rtt6.84, the hydration door. Both are stated honestly in the shipped docstrings; this bead exists so they are not re-derived.

1. THE ADOPTION WINDOW IS MODULE-LEVEL (arm1/runtime.cljs, 'adoption'). One flag for the whole runtime, matching every other slot in this arm (rstate, scratch, the cell table). A page hydrates once at boot, so one window is the shape the case has — but a SECOND hydrating root opened while the first window is still open would share it, and presence would be born-present in both. The spine keeps its equivalent flag ROOT-LOCAL by handing it to its closer as a prop (spine.cljs hydrate-root-options / adoption-window-closer); doing the same here would put a prop or a context read on arm1/presence, which is a cost this arm had no case for. Revisit ONLY if a real multi-root hydration case appears.

2. hydrate-root! CALLS hydrateRoot WITH NO OPTIONS. The spine composes an onRecoverableError reporter when the host authored one or debug is on (spine.cljs hydrate-root-options), and installs the window-closer only then. The door here always rides the closer and passes no options, so a hydration mismatch surfaces only on React's default channels — console.error and reportError/window 'error'. rf2-2rtt6.84's witnesses capture BOTH (arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test capture-console!), so the spike's X2 'zero mismatch warnings' row is answerable as shipped. A structured :on-recoverable-error option would be nicer and is NOT needed for X2; price it only if a consumer asks.

ALSO RECORDED: the bead rf2-2rtt6.84 clause (6) asserted the body-run counter 'is DCE'd goog.DEBUG-gated today'. It was not gated — it did not exist. The only body-run counter in the lane was arm1/grid.cljs's !body-runs, an always-on atom inside one fixture's view. runtime/body-runs now lands it on the shared render path, always on.

title: the fast-PR spine is not a superset of the required checks, and nothing says which it omits
description:
THE PROBLEM, observed three times on 2026-08-04 and each time costing a round trip. A worker runs scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, sees PASS fast PR spine, opens its PR, and CI goes red on a REQUIRED check the spine never ran. Nothing tells the worker which required checks the spine does not cover, so each discovers a different one the hard way and the next worker rediscovers it.

THE THREE FOUND SO FAR, all real reds after a green spine:

1. clj-kondo (fail on errors, warnings informational) -- lint.yml. Fired on a single error, mount.cljs:130 "Expected: array, received: function" (an aset on a function; unchecked-set is the arm's idiom). Compounding trap: the locally installed clj-kondo is 2025.10.23 while CI pins 2026.04.15; the local build reports 0 on the line CI fails and 10 DIFFERENT errors CI does not. A local clj-kondo pass proves nothing -- the pinned binary must be fetched.

2. The chained JS harness gate -- npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers. A worker ran only the second half, reported it green, and a red got through. The two are one gate in CI and must be run chained.

3. The EP-0036 donor-boundary check -- reports under the name "JVM freehand (clojure -M:test)" and IS NOT A TEST. It is a git grep for re-frame\.ui / re_frame/ui / re-frame2-ui over implementation/freehand. It fired on a DOCSTRING naming re-frame.ui/hydrate-root in prose. The gate cannot distinguish prose from a require, and that is correct design for a boundary rule -- a cleverer grep would eventually admit a real dependency.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it should be done once properly rather than accreted: enumerate the REQUIRED checks from .github/workflows/test.yml and lint.yml, compare against what scripts/test-fast-pr.sh actually runs, and publish the difference where a worker will see it. The spine already prints which tiers it skipped by diff classification; the gap is the checks it never runs AT ALL, at any classification.

ACCEPTANCE: a worker who has read the spine's own output can state, without guessing, which required checks remain unrun and how to run each locally (including the clj-kondo version pin). Whether that lives in the spine's output, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, or TESTING.md is the implementer's call -- but it must be somewhere a DISPATCH BRIEF can cite by path rather than by my re-listing it each time.

DO NOT WEAKEN OR WIDEN ANY GATE. This bead is about VISIBILITY, not coverage. In particular the EP-0036 grep stays exactly as conservative as it is.

CAVEAT ON THE LIST ABOVE: three is what I have tripped over, not a count. The bead's own work is to derive the real set from the workflow files.
notes:
REFINEMENT from the rf2-2rtt6.97 worker, 2026-08-04, and it changes what this bead has to look for.

The EP-0036 donor-boundary check is NOT a job the spine skips. It is a STEP INSIDE a job the spine does run -- test.yml line 2123, the last step of the JVM freehand job, a plain git grep. So the spine's own skipped-tier enumeration CANNOT SEE IT: the tier is not skipped, and the step is not a test.

That makes 'compare required jobs against what the spine runs' insufficient as an approach. The comparison has to reach STEP granularity inside jobs the spine believes it covers, not just job granularity. The worker called this the nastiest of the three found so far for exactly that reason.

Also worth carrying: the check reports under the name 'JVM freehand (clojure -M:test)', so a worker reading a red sees a test-suite name for something that is a grep. Any output this bead produces should name the CHECK, not the job, or the next person will go looking for a failing test that does not exist.
DONE — PR #7485 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7485), branch worker/gatemap-13zre.

MECHANISED, not prose. scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the whole list at print time; the spine appends the digest to its own PASS line (--brief), TESTING.md carries the citable section, dispatch-prompt-template.md tells briefs to cite one path.

THE BEAD'S FRAMING WAS INCOMPLETE IN TWO PLACES, both found by the derivation:

1. THERE ARE THREE REQUIRED STATUS CONTEXTS, NOT TWO. The bead named test.yml and lint.yml. docs.yml posts 'Docs required' via its own docs-required aggregator, and its 'build' job carries four residue gates (check_failure_corpus_residue, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys) plus the playground bundle-drift and esbuild-bootstrap checks — none of which any spine tier runs.

2. THE CHAINED JS HARNESS GATE (item 2) IS NOT A SPINE GAP. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh line 821 already runs 'npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers' chained, exactly as CI does. That red came from a worker running the halves separately, not from anything the spine omits. The report now says so rather than repeating it as a hole.

THE ITEM-3 CLASS TURNED OUT TO HAVE THREE MEMBERS, not one:
  * the EP-0036 donor grep, last step of jvm-freehand (the known one)
  * 'npm run test:ui-isolation', a step of the cljs job whose node-test build the spine DOES run
  * 17 required 'python scripts/check_*.py' invariant checkers with no local lane at all
The third is much the largest and was invisible to everyone. Filed as rf2-ejm7m (coverage, not visibility — deliberately out of this bead's scope).

HOW THE DERIVATION WORKS, so the next person does not re-list anything: required set from the three aggregators' needs:; gate steps from each job's run: bodies minus anchored whole-body setup shapes; coverage from eleven SPINE_LANES signatures, with the python-checker lane derived from the spine's own source so it needs no maintenance. Local commands are READ FROM THE STEP (no required gate step interpolates a workflow expression), including the clj-kondo pin, read from that job's installer step so a bump cannot leave prose stale.

THE RATCHET: a SPINE_LANES signature that stops matching any required gate step is RED — the spine claims a lane for a check CI renamed, moved or deleted. Runs in the spine's always-on block and in CI's verify-skill-mcp-drift job.

NO GATE'S BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. The EP-0036 grep is untouched.
