title: MEASURE: the per-keystroke row has NO band-supplying control, so a clean run still yields an UNADJUDICATED magnitude
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7459), where this was the finding rather than a side note.

THE GAP. clock_run.cjs's keystroke row is gated by ctl-50ms, which burns a fixed 50 ms inside its own handler. That makes it an excellent CONTROL — it proves the instrument moves when the work moves, and it passed convincingly in the window (49.84 ms [49.43 - 50.27] of extra task time over 18 segment-rounds against a predicted >=40, and Event Timing interactions at duration p50 48.0 ms over n=180 against a predicted >=48). But control/floor reads (F + 50)/F, which MOVES WITH F. It is therefore not a pair whose true ratio is a property of the page, and the-candidates-clock.md sec 6.2's band is defined on exactly such a pair. The driver knows this and says so: it prints 'band NOT AVAILABLE on this row' and labels all three bars UNADJUDICATED.

WHY THAT IS DECISIVE RATHER THAN COSMETIC. Under sec 6.2's rule a magnitude whose distance from 1.0 is inside the band is instrument-limited, and a bar with NO band is not adjudicated at all. So the per-keystroke row cannot produce a publishable magnitude no matter how clean the run is — and rf2-0qj9w's window produced a maximally clean one. Every gate the row has cleared: both controls, arm-order guard reportable, canonical DOM identical (9320 B), 0 unverified of 756, the repaired four-field witness reconciling 540 keys sent as 466 observed + 74 censored, and a recompute census reading exactly p0/cell x100 + p0/draft x4 on all three substrate arms and no subscriptions at all on every floor arm. It was still unpublishable. This is a property of the rig, not of the box or the arms, and no scheduling fixes it.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT OBSTRUCTION AT THE SAME PLACE. The row's smallest non-zero per-sample delta was 0.146 ms over 1003 distinct values, while the candidate/Reagent separation is 0.052 ms per sample on raw TaskDuration — about a third of one grid step. Even given a band, this witness may not have the resolution to state a sign. A median over many samples can resolve below the grain, but the driver's own ranges agree that it does not here: every bar straddles 1.0. Any repair should say what separation the row is powered to detect, not merely give it a band.

NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WHAT IS ALREADY PUBLISHED: the-candidates-clock.md sec 5's figures predate the band rule and would be labelled UNADJUDICATED if re-taken today. rf2-0qj9w's window banded sec 5 accordingly (for the separate reason that its witness was the superseded one-field one) but published no replacement.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none tried, and choosing between them is likely a ruling:

1. Give the row a three-point control on an axis it actually varies, in the idiom of docs/design/hicasso/studio/a-control-that-differences-the-constant-away.md — the construction that differences the additive constant away rather than assuming it cancels. The keystroke row's natural axis is the number of subscriptions a keystroke dirties (the witness already localises 100 cells + 4 fields), so arms dirtying 1 / 100 / 200 boundaries per keystroke are available on the page that exists.
2. Add a SECOND control alongside ctl-50ms whose ratio to the floor IS a page property — the simplest being a ctl-2x-style doubled page driven by a keystroke — purely to supply the band, leaving ctl-50ms as the sensitivity control. Note this inherits ctl-2x's additive-constant undershoot, which is rf2-jcm3p's open problem.
3. Rule that a paint-inclusive per-keystroke row is adjudicated by Event Timing rather than by the band — every arm reads 16.0 ms, one frame, and the honest published statement is 'indistinguishable, all three one frame' with the censoring published. That is arguably what sec 5 already says in prose, and it would make the taskNet bars diagnostics rather than magnitudes.

Option 3 costs nothing and may be the right answer: the row's job is to show the candidate is not over the frame budget, and it is not. Options 1 and 2 are instrument work.

SEQUENCING: this blocks any rebook of rf2-0qj9w's per-keystroke row. Rebooking the window without it buys another clean run and another UNADJUDICATED bar. rf2-jcm3p is the sibling gap on M1 (ctl-2x undershoots and no changed-set control reaches a mount) and is likewise held for a ruling; the two are the same shape and may want one ruling between them.

EVIDENCE: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-0qj9w/run1.json on worker/window-0qj9w, re-adjudicable with clock_readjudicate.cjs — the clean keystroke run is on disk, so any repair can be adjudicated against real samples without a new window.

DO NOT DISPATCH AS IMPLEMENTATION until Mike has ruled which repair, for the same reason rf2-jcm3p carries that hold.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY by rf2-0qj9w's SECOND quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7486, run2.json).

Reproduced exactly, on a different tree (070be81738) and a different box state. The keystroke row again cleared EVERY gate it has — ctl-50ms 49.84 ms [49.36 - 50.45] over 18 segment-rounds against predicted >=40; Event Timing p50 56.0 ms over n=180 against predicted >=48; arm-order guard reportable; canonical DOM identical 9320 B; 0 unverified of 756; the repaired four-field witness reconciling 540 keys pressed as 449 observed + 91 censored under the 16 ms floor, 60 sent on each of nine arms; the recompute census reading p0/cell x100 + p0/draft x4 on all three substrate arms and no subscriptions at all on every floor and control arm. And all three bars are UNADJUDICATED again, for exactly the reason this bead names.

TWO CLEAN RUNS, TWO IDLE BOXES, SAME UNPUBLISHABLE ROW. That settles the question this bead was raised on: the blocker is the rig, not the box, and no further scheduling can move it. This bead is the repair.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LIMITER SHOWED UP ON THE SAME ROW and whoever designs the control should know it: the keystroke grain is 0.181 ms over 1002 distinct values, and the candidate-to-UIx separation is 0.043 ms — under a QUARTER of one grid step. So even given a band-supplying control, that pair is not resolved as to sign at this n. Candidate-to-Reagent is 0.277 ms, about 1.5 steps. A control alone may not be sufficient to make this row adjudicable; the design should say what n it needs.

RELATED DEFECT FILED: rf2-y7mw7 — the driver's exit code does not gate adjudication at all, so HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke alone exits 0 and prints 'REPORTABLE: keystroke ... Publish those' for a row whose every bar is UNADJUDICATED. That is a separate fail-open from this bead's missing control, and it is what would let this gap actually bite.

title: MEASURE: Hicasso has NO clock rows at all — mount, bulk and per-keystroke are unmeasured, and the clock is what a user experiences
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01): 'the real test for performance is not bytes, that's a potentially poor proxy, it is browser performance.'

HE IS RIGHT, AND THE GAP IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKED. Verified against the tree: what has been taken for the Hicasso candidate is HOOK COUNT (2, flat across 1/7/20 reads) and PER-READ RETAINED HEAP (rf2-2rtt6.34, PR #7337). rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5 lists as NOT taken: retained size against the 0.4-0.5 KB shell target, bulk K=100/300, and THE PER-READ AND PER-KEYSTROKE PATHS. Every clock figure the programme has published — M1 mount 1.0150x [0.9820-1.0480], bulk-broad 0.6291x — is about the ADAPTERS (UIx vs Reagent), not about Hicasso.

SO THE PROGRAMME HAS NO WALL-CLOCK MEASUREMENT OF ITS OWN CANDIDATE.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEAP RESULT. Heap is an INDIRECT proxy: allocation rate drives GC pressure and GC pauses land in frame time, but the direction and magnitude of that transfer are unknown. 415 B/read more than Reagent could be invisible on the clock or could dominate a bulk update; nothing measured so far distinguishes those. There is an irony worth recording: the adversarial review named per-read heap as the programme's best remaining case BECAUSE it is the axis the architecture wins by construction — which made it the most attractive thing to measure and the least decisive.

THE WORK: take the candidate's clock rows on the same instrument as the donor rows they are judged against (validation.md is explicit that a candidate is judged against the donor row taken on ITS OWN instrument, and that a margin under 5% is instrument-limited rather than cleared). Mount, bulk K=100/300, narrow, and per-keystroke. Same-run donors, B/E/Q stamps, positive control predicted before the run, arm-order guard reportable, machine QUIET.

SEQUENCING: this outranks rf2-aqgr2 (the 415 B/read decomposition). Optimising a proxy before knowing whether the proxy matters is backwards. It also outranks any further heap work.

CROSS-CHECK: see rf2-<js-framework-benchmark bead> — an external instrument is the honest way to find out whether OUR harness is telling the truth about the clock.
notes:
INSTRUMENT GUIDANCE — DO NOT REACH FOR performance.mark BY DEFAULT (Mike asked whether the Performance API gives good benchmarking information, 2026-08-01; recorded by acting mayor).

THE SPLIT, and it decides which tool each row wants:

WHERE THE PERFORMANCE API IS GENUINELY GOOD
  - EVENT TIMING (PerformanceEventTiming) is the RIGHT instrument for the PER-KEYSTROKE row. It decomposes real input latency into input delay, processing time, and time to next paint — and it CAPTURES THE PAINT. That is strictly better than what the controlled-restore witnesses do today, which assert on the line AFTER dispatchEvent returns and therefore stop before the browser has shown anything. Use it.
  - Long Animation Frames (LoAF) gives attribution for frames that blow the budget — useful for the bulk row as a diagnostic, not as the headline number.
  - mark/measure are fine for coarse IN-PAGE RELATIVE timings.

WHERE IT WILL MISLEAD, and this is the half that matters
  - IT ONLY SEES WHAT YOUR JAVASCRIPT DOES. A mark around a render call captures your work and NOT the style recalculation, layout, paint and composite the browser performs afterwards. For MOUNT and BULK — where the interesting cost IS that downstream work — in-page timing systematically under-reports, and under-reports DIFFERENTLY per framework depending on how much each defers. Hicasso's whole design concerns WHEN work happens, so this is exactly the wrong error to make: it would flatter whichever arm does least synchronously.
  - THE CLOCK IS DELIBERATELY COARSENED. performance.now() is clamped for Spectre mitigation and meaningfully finer resolution requires cross-origin isolation. VERIFY THE CURRENT FIGURES against Chrome's own documentation before relying on any specific number — do not take a remembered value. The shape is certain even if the number needs checking: do not assume microsecond resolution; short operations need many iterations rather than one precise measurement.

Ruling item 1 is discharged in full. All four repairs are in:

FOUR-FIELD WITNESS per validation.md. `kb-form` now renders four controlled fields over an indexed `[:p0/draft i]` above the 100-cell grid, on all three substrate arms and the floor, canonical-DOM identical. A sample types one physical key into ONE field, rotating with the sample.    Also included: SUB-RECOMPUTE LOCALISATION, which validation.md's per-keystroke budget line requires ("which subs recompute, not merely which boundaries re-run") and note item 1 named ("gates which subscriptions recomputed"). Both layer-1 queries are registered behind a recompute census; the driver arms it for ONE WARM-UP keystroke per arm, so no measured sample carries its cost. A substrate arm must recompute exactly 100 + 4; a floor arm must recompute NONE. Either disagreement refuses the row.

2. ONE RECORD PER PHYSICAL KEY, web-vitals' interaction-id rules, in a new pure adjudicator `clock_witness.cjs` (seam.cjs / order_guard.cjs's idiom). interactionId === 0 entries are part of no interaction — counted and published, never a record. Entries sharing a nonzero id are one interaction whose latency is the longest of them. The driver COUNTS THE KEYS IT PRESSES (`sentKeys`) rather than deriving them, so the 180-for-540 arithmetic is gone, and it stamps the whole physical key in the page AT OBSERVATION TIME (it stamped the arm only, and let the driver add round/sample at drain time — an entry one drain late inherited the next sample's index).

3. CENSORED <16 ms SAMPLES PUBLISHED. Keys that raised no entry are left-censored observations, not gaps and not zeroes. Every arm publishes sent / observed / censored (%); the observed statistics are labelled CONDITIONAL on clearing 16 ms; and the one population fact censoring permits is stated on the row — above 50% censoring the arm's true median is below 16 ms whatever the observed subset reads. `observed + censored === sent` is itself a gate.

title: RULING PREP: the production server arm — JVM structural walk (default) vs Node sidecar, priced from the spike corpus
description:
RULING PREP — THE PRODUCTION SERVER ARM, PRICED FOR THE P2/GRADUATION SITTING. Paper-only dossier bead; dispatch AFTER the X1-X5 spike witness lands (its corpus is this dossier's arithmetic). DECIDER: Mike, at the SAME P2/HD-013 sitting — one sitting, no separate gate (the 2026-08-04 adversarial reviews killed the two-sitting variant as not decision-grade).

THE QUESTION: which production server arm does Hicasso graduate with?

DEFAULT DIRECTION (to be priced, not presumed): THE JVM STRUCTURAL WALK — a JVM twin of the codec's pure analysis rules emitting the Spec 004B v1 structural tree, folded to HTML by the SHIPPED react-dom-19.2.0-pinned emit-ui-tree, reads resolving via rf/compute-sub against the request snapshot, in-process with ssr-ring (the platform's host; Spec 011's HTTP response contract stays there). Uniquely, this route also co-discharges HD-021(a)'s headless testing door (same structural-render core, two resolvers: snapshot for SSR, override-map for tests). KNOWN RISK ROWS the dossier must price from the spike corpus: (1) the walk's real surface is ~35-40 rule-bearing sites (not "~10 rules"), against a codec that was in its highest-churn phase in early Aug (wait for the walk-attack lane to stabilise before building); (2) the TEXT-SEPARATOR row — emit-ui-tree coalesces text runs (ui_tree.cljc:724-731) while React renders children as authored, so [:div "Count: " n] mismatches by construction; 004B:613 flags it [S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — this row must be closed in the tree spec/emitter before any JVM HTML meets hydrateRoot; (3) the conformance apparatus (two-sided rules corpus + renderToString-authored parity fixtures) is an eternal maintenance tax re-opened at every react-dom bump — price it honestly.

THE ALTERNATIVE (priced beside it): A NODE SIDECAR behind an EDN render contract (JVM keeps HTTP + the event drain via ssr-ring; Node renders markup per request through the SAME entry the spike shipped). No parity tax ever; costs a second production runtime and an ops surface — and it must NOT be framed as replacing the Ring host (the adversarial review's host-fork finding: Node-native-serving-as-reference-host is rejected on the record).

INPUTS: the spike's baked-fixture corpus + feature census + tolerance probes; the live churn state of the codec lane; the HD-021 headless-door demand (does anything else need it by then); K7/P2 timing. OUTPUT: a no-verdict dossier on the standard bead (rf2-2rtt6.1's advisory-input slots) with both branches priced in beads/weeks, named tripwires for the default, and the recommendation stated — the RULING is the operator's at the sitting.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7488 (merged 2026-08-04T11:29:06Z) — REOPENED. The Node-sidecar topology and B1 estimate assume “the JVM serialises the request's db snapshot plus the root form as EDN” and price an “EDN render contract — snapshot + root form out.” The shipped Node entry instead requires `:hiccup` whose Hicasso root is `[<minted head> {props}]`; that head is a CLJS/JavaScript function created by `defview`, does not exist on the JVM, and is not an EDN value. The dossier's own §6 relies on exactly this fact when explaining why canonical EDN renders every function identically. A viable sidecar needs an application-defined stable root/entry identifier (and serializable arguments) resolved inside the per-app Node bundle, or another explicit cross-host registry; it must also state the portable serialization domain/projection for a snapshot rather than assuming arbitrary app state crosses EDN. Reprice B1/B4/B5 and the compliant-topology arrows around that real contract. While touching the census, reconcile §4's “75 top-level forms” with the same section's measured 77 top-level `def*` forms. No duplicate bead: rf2-2rtt6.88 owns this dossier and its estimates.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DOSSIER LANDED — PR #7488, branch worker/serverarm-2rtt6-88, commit 3bed72d29f.
Page: docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md. NO VERDICT and NO
RECOMMENDATION drawn. decisions.md, validation.md and rf2-2rtt6.1 untouched;
no runtime change, no gate, no spec edit; implementation/ssr and ssr-ring
untouched.

TWO INSTRUCTION TEXTS DISAGREE, and the page says so in its own section 0
rather than resolving it silently. This bead's DESCRIPTION asks for "the
recommendation stated"; the dispatching brief, quoting Mike later the same
day, says "do not recommend" and calls it a no-verdict dossier. The page
follows the later text. If a recommendation is wanted it is one paragraph on
top of the page, not a rewrite of it.

LANDING SITE, likewise flagged rather than assumed. The description says the
output lands on rf2-2rtt6.1's advisory-input slots; the brief fences
rf2-2rtt6.1's own notes. The conservative reading won, so the dossier is a
design-record page (the hd-002-adjudication.md precedent) indexed from
docs/design/hicasso/README.md and pointed at from draft-guide/10's "Not
settled" row. Appending the pointer to rf2-2rtt6.1 is the mayor's or the
operator's to do.

=== BOTH ARMS PRICED — the headline asymmetries ===

THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD TEXT IMPLIES. emit-ui-tree ships and is
final (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc, 1,040 lines; 004B
calls it pure, deterministic to the byte, JVM-runnable, react-dom 19.2.0
pinned four times in source). A JVM interpreted structural walk to the v1
tree ALREADY SHIPS, for Freehand — re-frame.freehand.tree (678) + node.cljc
(1,438) + conversion.cljc (906), reaching emit-ui-tree via emit-static-html
(tree.cljc:632-654) behind the Independence wall, driven by the shipped
v/render-static macro. So the walk arm's back half is a thing to be CALLED,
not built. What has no precedent in this tree is READS: Freehand's JVM walk is
a pure function of its argument, and v/render-static fails a v/sub loud with
:rf.error/view-read-outside-render rather than resolving one.

BOTH ARMS NEED THE SAME NEW SEAM. ssr-ring hard-calls ssr/render-to-string on
hiccup at ring/pipeline.clj:546 — the stock-Reagent tier 004B freezes. Named
so neither arm looks cheaper by having it quietly assumed.

THE SPIKE BUILT THE NODE ARM'S RENDER, NOT ITS TOPOLOGY. ssr-ring is JVM-only
.clj in EVERY file, so the spike's Node entry hand-writes what it cannot
reach: the #__rf_payload script tag (entry.cljs:184-200, with a docstring
obliging byte-identity with shell/payload-script-tag) and the whole page
envelope (entry.cljs:202-231). Its own docstring says "Not a production host";
the driver's serve() disclaims the response accumulator, cookies, redirects
and CRLF fail-fast. THERE IS NO JVM<->NODE CONTRACT IN THE TREE. The
R0-compliant sidecar — JVM host, JVM payload, JVM shell, Node returning a body
string — has not been built and has not been measured. That is the single
largest unmeasured thing in the dossier.

THE CORPUS SPLITS CLEANLY, and this is the reading most likely to be got wrong
at the sitting. X2/X3/X4/X5 are CLIENT-half rows: the hydration door, the
adoption, reactivity-on-React's-schedule, liveness and teardown hold whatever
produced the bytes, so they transfer to BOTH arms unchanged. Only X1 speaks to
a server half, and only Node's.

THE WALK ARM'S LIKELIEST DIVERGENCE IS THE ONE NOTHING CAN SEE. 004B: two
emitters, divergence "detected, not prevented". 011 Hydration-mismatch
detection: React-native adoption deliberately does NOT report attribute-only
mismatches (React documents no guarantee that attribute differences are
patched; neither onRecoverableError nor any production equivalent fires).
Composed: a JVM-table vs react-dom attribute disagreement is invisible at
runtime, so detection must come from the parity corpus in CI or not at all.
The Node arm cannot produce that class — one emitter makes both sides.

THE PARITY TAX, PRICED HONESTLY RATHER THAN RHETORICALLY. The apparatus EXISTS
and RUNS — parity_fixtures.cljc 643 lines / 66 cases, JVM side computed at CLJS
compile time and embedded (no checked-in goldens), emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc
pinning the serialiser's table copies byte-for-byte against re-frame.ui.rules,
and implementation/ui/dev/react-conform-probe.cjs as the tool that talks to a
real react-dom. So the bump tax has a NAMED HOME and is bounded work, which is
cheaper than "eternal maintenance tax" suggests. Less comfortably: that pin
anchors the serialiser to the UI COMPILER's table. A Hicasso twin has no such
anchor and owes a second pinning relationship — new apparatus, not an
extension.

CHURN, MEASURED. front/codec.cljs was CREATED 2026-07-31 and has taken 23
commits in four days: 1 / 6 / 8 / 6 / 2. All semantic (tag shorthand onto the
emitted slot, frame-as-codec-prop, the IME composition shadow, defhost's :ssr
gate). Wider: front/ 3/11/17/19/4 and arm1/ 8/17/17/26/13 over the same days.
A twin started at the beginning of that week would have needed four semantic
amendments in four days. This is the sharpest number on the page and the one
the sitting can act on immediately.

BEADS/WEEKS (ESTIMATES, labelled as such in the page). JVM walk: 6 beads,
5-8.5 weeks (the .cljc twin 1.5-2.5, the read resolver 0.5, intents/controlled/
presence/route-link 1-1.5, the text-separator settlement 0.5-1.5 AND IT MAY
REACH THE SPEC, the parity extension 1-2, the ssr-ring seam + witness 0.5).
Node sidecar: 6 beads, 4-6.5 weeks (EDN render contract 0.5-1, a callable
process with supervision 1-2, the JVM side 0.5-1, the per-app server-bundle
build story 1-1.5, a skew detector 0.5, the end-to-end witness 0.5). THE BANDS
OVERLAP — on build cost these arms are not far apart and the choice is not a
schedule choice. The durable differences are one runtime against two and one
emitter against two, and both are permanent where build cost is paid once.

=== THE TWO INSTRUMENT FACTS ===

1. :rf/render-hash. NOTHING IN THE DOSSIER LEANS ON IT. Three observations for
rf2-2rtt6.91's owner, offered as observations and not rulings: (a) NEITHER ARM
REPAIRS IT — the degeneracy is a client-side fact, and a deep server hash the
client cannot reproduce makes every page a mismatch, which is why rf2-2rtt6.86
declined to invent one; (b) the PRODUCTION call site takes the hash from the
root hiccup BEFORE the render (lifecycle/render-document-hash at
pipeline.clj:543), so the degeneracy reaches production identically whichever
arm renders; (c) SPEC 011 ALREADY HAS A STATED POSTURE — its mismatch section
is tiered by client render-tree representation, and both the compiled tier and
native React-element roots "deliberately carry no such hash", verifying by
React-native adoption through onRecoverableError instead. Hicasso is a React
adapter minting React-element roots. On that reading .91's candidate (c) is not
a concession but 011's own existing answer for Hicasso's tier, and rf2-2rtt6.97
has already landed the door that answer requires.

2. UTF-16 BYTE ACCOUNTING: STILL UNREPAIRED. driver.cjs has exactly ONE commit
in its whole history (9214396f73, its creation). documentBytes is still
document.length (driver.cjs:176-187) and the live log still prints a
".length B" figure (driver.cjs:235-237). NO SIZE FIGURE FROM THAT MANIFEST
APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THE DOSSIER. X1(a)'s 3,101 is used only as an identity
claim, never as a size. The SHA-256 is unaffected (explicit utf8 encoding at
driver.cjs:129).

=== TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DISPATCHING BRIEF ===

(1) THE TEXT-SEPARATOR CITATION WAS WRONG. ui_tree.cljc:724-731 is
emit-children, a str/join — the serialiser receives children ALREADY coalesced
(its own docstring says so at line 541). Coalescing lives at TREE-BUILD time,
in three independent .cljc implementations of one algorithm:
ui/tree.cljc:110-116, ui/semantic.cljc:208-219, freehand/node.cljc:359-374.
The ROW is real and open — spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:613,
[S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — and it carries NO BEAD (the merged-PR audit rf2-7uil4
recorded it as "already an explicitly open 011-owned row, not rediscovered
here" and deliberately left it unfiled). A Hicasso JVM twin would need a FOURTH
coalescer: the CLJS codec has none, which is exactly why React's own render is
separator-correct and a structural tree's would not be. AND X1(b) DOES NOT
RESCUE IT — "the comparator skips comment nodes" is a property of
lane/canonical, and React's hydration reconciler is not that comparator; X1(b)
was also judging bytes react-dom/server itself produced. Worse, the existing
parity corpus renders its React side with renderToStaticMarkup
(parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs:36), which emits no separators — THE GATE THAT
EXISTS CANNOT SEE THIS ROW.

(2) "~35-40 RULE-BEARING SITES" IS CORROBORATED, and the page enumerates the
roster rather than asserting the count. front/codec.cljs: 77 top-level def*
forms, 57 of them defn/defn-; the rule-bearing subset lands at 35-40, rostered
with line ranges (reserved-name? 180-202, parse-tag 241-245, prop-name 274-308,
the one-slot-per-spelling family 405-465, fold-shorthand! 488-524, merge-caller
571-618, check-ref! 624-654, convert-props 656-791, memoize-boundary! 847-945,
mint-host!/declared-ssr/mint-host-gate! 1039-1173, the lazy-seq forcing walk
1201-1414, the emission dispatch 1420-1673, vec->element 1677-1706, as-element
1708-1749, root-element 1751-1770).

=== UNMEASURED, NAMED EXPLICITLY (9 items in the page) ===

No JVM emitter of Hicasso semantics exists, so no parity row does. No
JVM<->Node seam exists, so no sidecar latency, throughput or
snapshot-serialisation figure does. NEITHER ARM HAS A CLOCK ROW AND NEITHER IS
OWED ONE — SSR speed is off the bar by HD-012 and validation.md, so a sitting
asking for a speed comparison is asking for something the programme has ruled
it does not measure. The cost of resolving reads through compute-sub on a real
page (the mechanism and a shared memo both exist — subs.cljc:2183 and
compute-sub-with-memo at :2236 — but the census seven-read archetype has never
been run). The text-separator fixture. The attribute-only class, on either arm.
HD-021(a)'s headless demand — the door is genuinely absent
(draft-guide/08-testing.md says "Not built yet", "sketch — not built", "does
not exist yet") and NO open bead requires it, so the walk arm's co-discharge is
a benefit whose absence nobody has costed. How many of the 66 parity cases need
Hicasso siblings. And Node's runtime pin is CI-only: the workflows pin node 24,
package.json carries no engines field and there is no .nvmrc.

TRIPWIRES for whichever arm is chosen are in section 11. For the walk: a parity
case where the emitters disagree about the TREE rather than the markup (004B
under-specified for Hicasso), a separator settlement that changes the canonical
form (every v1-tree consumer in scope), a rule that cannot be twinned because it
needs a live React value at render time, a third emitter appearing. For the
sidecar: anything beyond body markup crossing the contract (the rejected host
fork arriving by increments), the sidecar needing to drain events, a view-code
skew reaching a deploy, snapshot serialisation appearing in a profile.

GATES: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 PASS (classified docs=true jvm=false
node=false; the documentation tier ran, including mkdocs --strict at 23.53s).
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 — run AFTER staging, since its roster is git ls-files
and it would have skipped the new file while untracked; --self-test also exit 0.
mkdocs --strict is NOT claimed as the gate for this diff (exclude_docs keeps
design/hicasso out of the site). TABLES HAND-VERIFIED: 13 tables across the
three touched files, 0 mismatches (the new page carries 9 at 2/3/3/4/2/3/3/3/3
columns). shellcheck is not installed and no shell files changed. No required
check came back CANCELLED.

title: clock_run.cjs is FAIL-OPEN on adjudication: a row whose every bar is UNADJUDICATED still exits 0 and is announced 'REPORTABLE ... Publish those'
description:
FOUND by rf2-0qj9w's second quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7486), while
verifying the run's own exit code rather than trusting it.

THE GAP. clock_run.cjs computes two verdicts per row and only one of them
reaches the exit code.

  * ROW-LEVEL: did the positive control see the change its arithmetic
    predicts? This is `ctlFailed` (clock_run.cjs ~2098), and it is the only
    thing the final block gates on: `if (ctlFailed.length > 0) { ... exit(1) }`,
    else `console.error('[clock] ok')` and an implicit exit 0.
  * BAR-LEVEL: does the row have a band-supplying control, so that a magnitude
    can be adjudicated at all? On the keystroke row the answer is NO — the
    fixed-50 ms control makes control/floor read (F+50)/F, so the driver
    prints `band NOT AVAILABLE on this row` and labels all three bars
    UNADJUDICATED (that gap itself is rf2-swwud).

These never meet. A row can pass its control, clear every whole-run gate, and
have no adjudicable bar — and the driver exits 0 announcing success.

THE CONCRETE FAIL-OPEN. `HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke` alone, on a perfectly clean
box, produces: both controls PASS, guard reportable, canonical DOM identical,
0 unverified of 756, the four-field witness reconciling exactly — and
`ctlFailed` empty, therefore `[clock] ok`, therefore EXIT 0. Every bar in that
run is UNADJUDICATED. A worker reading the exit code as a pass publishes an
unadjudicated magnitude and is not warned.

WORSE, THE SUMMARY LINE ACTIVELY INVITES IT. Even when another row refuses,
the driver prints (clock_run.cjs ~2133):

  [clock] REPORTABLE: keystroke — control passed, guard clean, canonical DOM
  identical, 0 unverified. Publish those and mark the rest.

"Publish those" names a row whose every bar the same driver has just labelled
UNADJUDICATED, four hundred lines above.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET, WHICH IS LUCK RATHER THAN DESIGN. Both windows ran
HCLOCK_ONLY=M1,keystroke, and in both M1's ctl-2x refused, so the driver exited
1 for an unrelated reason and the worker read the block carefully. Run the
commissioned keystroke row on its own — which the payload permits and a
rebook might well do — and the protection disappears.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND IS NOT A BAND. This bead does NOT ask for the missing
control (that is rf2-swwud, and it is the real repair). It asks only that the
driver stop claiming success it has not established:

  1. Fold "every published bar carries a band" into the exit condition, so a
     run whose bars are all UNADJUDICATED exits non-zero naming itself, in the
     idiom of the six witness refusals.
  2. Make the REPORTABLE line say what it means — a row that is reportable but
     unadjudicated is not a row to publish, and the sentence should not say
     "Publish those".

Whichever way it is resolved, the property to preserve is the tree's own
standard: an instrument that can exit 0 while emitting a verdict nobody may
act on is a fail-open instrument.

EVIDENCE. PR #7486, docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md sec 3.5,
and the retained dataset
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-0qj9w/run2.json.
notes:
BASIS OF THE COUNTERFACTUAL, stated so nobody has to re-derive it: the HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke-alone claim is established by READING clock_run.cjs's final block, not by running it. The block is unambiguous — 'if (ctlFailed.length > 0) { ...; process.exit(1); } console.error("[clock] ok");' — and on a keystroke-only invocation ctlFailed is empty because that row's two controls pass, so control falls through to the ok line and node exits 0 naturally. The window did not spend box time proving it empirically; whoever takes this bead should run it once as the first act, because a fail-open is exactly the kind of claim that deserves a reproduction rather than a reading.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7489 (merged 2026-08-04T11:46:14Z) — REOPENED. The fix correctly closes the concrete “every bar UNADJUDICATED” path, but the new fold does not implement its own stronger contract. `clock_run.cjs` sets `adjudicable` with `names.length > 0 && unadj.length < names.length`, and `clock_readjudicate.cjs` uses `names.some(!unadjudicated)`: one adjudicated bar therefore makes a row reportable even when another published bar is UNADJUDICATED. The driver then exits 0 and says “every published bar adjudicated,” and the readjudicator admits that run into the reportable subset for every pair, including the unadjudicated one. Current `seam.assess` makes availability row-wide, so today's generated rows are uniform, but the persisted-data reader and advertised fail-closed contract must not rely on that incidental coupling. Require a nonempty bar set and zero unadjudicated bars in both places, and add the missing mixed-bar fixture/mutation proof. No duplicate bead: this is the exact fail-open owner and a one-condition completion of its acceptance.

title: DESIGN-DECISION: the theming taught default (A vs B, per-root vs per-document) — delegated ruling via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements the guide change
description:
DESIGN-FIRST DECISION (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS — here "implement" = the guide rewrite teaching the ruled default, plus any tiny mechanism the ruling names). The theming taught default — guide 06-theming.md:121: "Neither is the taught default yet — whether A's cost holds at one boundary under multi-frame load, and whether the theme attribute is per-root or per-document, are still open."

THE TWO OPTIONS (both already work; 06 documents both):
A. RENDER A FACT: one boundary reads the theme sub and renders the attribute; everything below bails via HD-028's memo default. Cost: one boundary re-render per switch. Keeps derivation (theme can be computed from app-db).
B. IMPERATIVE FLIP: an fx sets the attribute on the root node; zero subscriptions, zero boundary, zero render. Gives up derivation.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. THE MULTI-FRAME COST QUESTION (06's first open): does A's one-boundary cost hold under multi-frame load? Argue it honestly BEFORE reaching for measurement: a theme switch is a rare, user-initiated action (not a hot path); N frames = N one-boundary re-renders per switch with memo bail below each. If argument suffices, SAY SO and close the question without a quiet-box row (over-measurement is a named posture violation); if the designer believes measurement is genuinely warranted, the case must survive the adversarial pass.
2. PER-ROOT vs PER-DOCUMENT (06's second open): frames-are-isolated-contexts is doctrine — a document-level attribute leaks theme across frames (multi-frame testbeds mount one app in N isolated frames; two frames with different themes must be expressible). That argues PER-ROOT decisively. The honest counter to weigh: real apps often want document-level chrome (scrollbars, ::backdrop) themed — does per-root strand any real CSS surface, and is the answer "the app ALSO sets a document attribute itself if it wants, outside Hicasso's contract"?
3. THE TAUGHT DEFAULT: the data-first posture (render a fact; derivation preserved; testable as a :db write; Xray-visible) argues A-as-taught with B documented as the zero-React-work alternative for apps that want it — the same honest-tradeoff shape 06 already has, but with a default stated so a new author does not have to adjudicate. SSR note: A's server render emits the attribute deterministically from the snapshot (rides the existing story); B is a client-side fx (its SSR story is "the server renders A-style or the attribute is absent until hydration" — state it).
4. GUIDE DELTA: 06 rewritten to teach the default + the tradeoff table updated; the troubleshooting row at :156 checked against the ruling.

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: the per-root argument's CSS reality (option 2's counter), whether declaring a taught default actually helps or just adds prose, and the no-measurement claim.

PROCESS: one designer (both options argued), one adversarial reviewer with a forced verdict, synthesis appended here as a delegated ruling marked operator-overturnable. The mayor implements the guide change from it. No AI attribution.

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS = THE DELEGATED RULING (2026-08-04; design + adversarial review complete; 0 FATAL / 4 MAJOR / 5 MINOR; verdict RATIFY WITH THE NAMED REPAIRS; operator-overturnable). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE: docs-only — the guide 06 rewrite + a dated HD-010 addendum. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.theming-design.md + theming-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE RULING:
1. OPTION A IS TAUGHT: one boundary reads the theme sub and renders the attribute on the frame's root; below it the value-equality bail-out keeps the tree quiet. A's case rests on SSR (the same renderer emits the attribute from the snapshot; hydration adopts — by construction, no flash), derivation (theme computable from app-db), boot coherence, testability (a :db write), and Xray visibility. Option B (imperative attribute flip via an app-owned fx) stays DOCUMENTED as the zero-render alternative, with its SSR bullet stated: the attribute is absent until client boot — a user-visible flash of wrong theme on the order of 100ms-3s. REPAIR F2 folded: B per-root is NOT machinery — an fx reading the frame id from its ctx (spec/002:1516) + an app-owned frame->node map is ~5 lines; the ruling does not claim impossibility, only that A wins on the grounds above. REPAIR F4: the taught A + the document-chrome echo below is an ASYMMETRIC pairing (the root attribute is the only carrier of app theming; the document echo is a redundant cosmetic projection of the same db fact) — state it, so the anti-hybrid teaching does not condemn its own pattern.
2. THE ATTRIBUTE IS PER-ROOT (per frame root), decisively: frames are isolated contexts; side-by-side story variants (light and dark mounted together) are unwritable per-document. Document chrome (scrollbars, canvas, theme-color) belongs to the PAGE: the app may ECHO the one db fact document-level OUTSIDE Hicasso's contract — server via the shipped :html-attrs head, client via one app-owned fx (do NOT name it :theme/apply! — 06's existing block uses that for the root flip; pick a distinct name, repair F8). Teach the echo with the ~6-line code block (repair F5), not a hand-wave. REPAIR F3 folded (in the ruling's favor): ::backdrop is scope-NEUTRAL — pre-Chromium-122/FF-120/Safari-17.4 engines strand it under per-document exactly as under per-root (it inherited from nothing), post-change engines serve both — so per-root cannot break the top layer; state the version floor; the optional witness names itself in top_layer_dom_cljs_test.cljs (Chromium lane) if anyone wants it pinned.
3. THE MULTI-FRAME COST QUESTION IS CLOSED BY ARGUMENT, NO MEASUREMENT: a theme switch is a rare user action; per switch, per frame, the cost is one small boundary body + one = compare per child (identical props object, identical children vector) — a fortiori under the shape HD-028 already measured at 300->0 bodies. REPAIR F1 (mandatory conditioning sentence): this claim rides HD-028's default bail-out, whose Reopens clause is LIVE as of the 2026-08-04 amendment (the wrapper carries the R=0 shell past the 1 KB line); if HD-028's default is ever revised, option A's quiet-tree claim is re-derived on the successor mechanism — the RULING (A taught, per-root) survives either disposition, only the mechanism sentence moves.

GUIDE DELTA (the mayor's implementation): 06 rewritten — the default stated up front; A's section first with the per-root subsection + the echo pattern code block + the prefers-color-scheme fallback note; B's section kept with the SSR-flash bullet (drop "every realistic deployment" — no SSG/prerender tier exists in this repo's SSR story today, repair per the attack); the tradeoff table updated; :156's troubleshooting row reordered per the design; BOTH Not-settled rows retired; the version-floor sentence for ::backdrop. Plus ONE dated HD-010 addendum (digtt format) recording this ruling. Optional one-liner in guide 10 (SSR) noting the theme attribute rides the snapshot render.

FENCES: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/06-theming.md + decisions.md (HD-010 addendum) + optionally guide 10, one PR. Outside mkdocs strict: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 + hand-verified anchors/tables stated in the PR body. No code, no new fx, no measurement. No AI attribution.

title: DESIGN: for-binding key sugar — build-or-rule-out via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements if ruled in
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). Guide 02:66: "Sugar that would derive the key from a for binding is not yet — you write :key yourself."

THE HONEST QUESTION THIS PASS MUST ANSWER BEFORE ANY CODE: is a keying sugar worth a public concept? The design pass is REQUIRED to allow the verdict "no — writing :key is the right permanent answer" and to argue it against K5 if that is where the evidence lands. If the verdict is do-not-build, the bead closes as ruled-out (operator-overturnable) with the guide taught accordingly; the operator is surfaced the recommendation either way.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. MECHANISM: the codec cannot see a for binding (bodies are ordinary Clojure; for evaluates before the walk). Price the options: (a) an h/for macro — a NEW PUBLIC FORM (K5 cost; the collector grammar currently has ~zero control forms and that absence is a marketed virtue); (b) defview-macro analysis rewriting for forms (macro-magic on user code — check the record's "the macro is not a compiler" line near HD-016/lang for whether this is fenced); (c) nothing — status quo taught as permanent.
2. THE AUTO-IDENTITY PRECEDENT, argued honestly both ways: the 2026-08-04 instance-key adversarial wave FATALLY killed ordinal/structural identity for STATE (silent state teleport). React keys are reconciliation identity only — a wrong/absent key costs a remount, visible and recoverable. So the kill does not transfer automatically; but the same instability arguments (which binding value? conditional siblings?) apply to what the sugar picks. The sugar would derive from the BINDING VALUE the author already iterates — is that always the right :key (multi-binding fors, destructuring, index bindings)?
3. SCOPE IF BUILT: exactly (h/for [x xs] [child {...}]) single-binding with the binding value as :key? What refuses (multi-binding, non-boundary bodies, non-sequential)?
4. K5 ACCOUNTING + guide delta either way (if not built: 02:66's "not yet" becomes a taught permanent with the reason).

PROCESS: one designer arguing BOTH stances honestly, one adversarial reviewer with a forced verdict, synthesis appended here; sequenced behind the [:>] programme's agent slots (rf2-2rtt6.103). Implementation (if any) is the mayor's, from the appended spec.

FENCES if built: lang/codec + witnesses + guide 02. Gates as usual. No AI attribution.

Docs branch executes via rf2-2rtt6.111; the dominating keywarn extension folded into rf2-2rtt6.104. Full synthesis on this bead.

title: DESIGN: the Hicasso-minted missing-key warning — spec via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS). A compact design + adversarial pass runs before any code; the synthesized spec will be APPENDED to this bead; do not dispatch implementation until it is present.

THE FEATURE: the Hicasso-minted missing-key warning. Guide 02-views-and-reads.md:64-66 promises it: "a bare seq of boundary children needs keys... you get React's own key warning in development; a Hicasso-minted warning is planned but not built." Its reason to exist: React's warning names a component stack; the Hicasso warning can name the AUTHORING-level facts — the defview head and the child position — which is what a Hicasso author actually greps for.

DESIGN QUESTIONS (the pass's inventory; verify all sites against the tree):
1. SITE + MECHANISM: the codec's seq-expansion region (front/codec.cljs ~:1420-1431 expand-seq; nil law nearby) — where exactly does the check live so it sees "seq of boundary children" and the enclosing view head? Does the walk carry the head name at that point (dev builds), or does that need threading?
2. DEV-ONLY GUARANTEE: goog.DEBUG gating with a witness that :advanced carries no trace (string-absence or DCE check per the lane's idiom). The hot path must pay ZERO in production — and near-zero in dev (the check runs per seq expansion; price it).
3. FIRE SEMANTICS: once-per-site vs per-render (a 60fps list must not spam); cheapest dedupe shape; what "site" means (view head + code position?).
4. RELATIONSHIP TO REACT'S OWN WARNING: both fire in dev? State the relationship in the docstring; do NOT suppress React's (suppression machinery = over-engineering). Verify what React 19.2's warning actually says for this shape so the two are visibly complementary, not duplicate noise.
5. SCOPE: exactly the guide's case — bare seqs of BOUNDARY children. Keyed seqs silent; native-tag children silent; the codec's nil law respected. Does [:<>] fragment content count? Does the [:>] crossing's children (per the in-flight rf2-2rtt6.103 design) count?
6. GUIDE DELTA: 02:64-66 true-up (the warning built; the for-binding key SUGAR remains rf2-2rtt6.105's separate question — do not conflate).

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: false positives (keyed-but-computed keys, seqs of mixed children, presence-retained children), the dev-cost claim, and whether the warning's wording will age (it names [unfrozen] spellings).

FENCES for the eventual implementation: front/codec.cljs + test + guide 02 only; coordinate on codec.cljs with rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation. Gates: hicasso compile + DOM suite + fast-PR spine, foreground. No AI attribution.

THE RULED SHAPE:
1. A dev-only pre-pass at the top of expand-seq (front/codec.cljs ~:1420-1431) fires when a member of a lowered child seq is a boundary-headed vector whose props give (nil? (:key props)) — exactly the emission gate at :1513, so nil-and-absent are one case.

3. The warning names the AUTHORING facts React cannot: the enclosing defview head, the member head, the first unkeyed member's index, and the fix spelling. THE THREE MANDATORY REPAIRS (from the attack):
R1 THE ID: :rf.warning/hicasso-missing-key — the CATALOGUED :rf.warning/* family (spec/Conventions.md:72-73, spec 009; spec 001:543-546 already specifies this family's fire semantics). The design's :rf.warn/* "first of its family" claim was false; strike the API-freeze note.

description:

defect in clock_run.cjs. Established by CODE READING, not by a run — whoever
takes this should reproduce it first, as rf2-y7mw7 did.

hd8_run.cjs's exit block (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/
hd8_run.cjs ~608-631) reads exactly three things — `hardFail` (~608),
`contractFailed` (~612) and the arm-order `refused` (~619) — and then prints

    [hd8] ok — measured, and no arm reads differently for its position in the plan

Two refusals it COMPUTES AND PRINTS never reach that block.

(a) A FAILED DOM READ-BACK. hd8_rows.cljs ~913-944 (`mask-failed-read-backs`)
writes `{:unpublished :failed-dom-read-back :unverified n :of m}` into the
row's `:summary`. It does NOT set HD8_ERROR (only hd8_app.cljs ~53-56 does,
from -main's catch), so `out.err` stays null and `hardFail` stays null. The
driver renders `UNPUBLISHED (1/78 unverified)` in the cross-run table
(~321-324, ~396, ~405) and exits 0. Every sibling instrument treats the
identical condition as a hard refusal: hd8_clock_run.cjs ~760-766 (exit 3),
shapes/census_clock_run.cjs ~805-811 (exit 3), clock_run.cjs ~2177-2185
(exit 1), p0_run.cjs ~1333-1338, b7_run.cjs ~673-675, reads_ladder_run.cjs
~814-817, spine_ablation_run.cjs ~923-928.

MITIGATION TO WEIGH, so the bead is not overstated: the figure IS suppressed
— replaced by the UNPUBLISHED marker, and head-to-head pairs touching the arm
are dropped at hd8_rows.cljs ~939-944 — so a reader cannot copy a number out.
What is missing is the process's own statement, and a green exit is what a
future worker banks.

`:verdict :refused` with reasons `:unevaluable`,
`:correction-exceeds-window`, `:correction-changes-the-verdict`. The driver
prints `YIELD CORRECTION: REFUSED (correction-changes-the-verdict)` at
~365-371 and then reads the flag ONLY for `c.verdict === 'corrected'`
(~378-379). On `refused`, `cSummary` is `{}`, `correctedBand` (~391) returns
null, and the UNADJUSTED number is printed at ~396 with no [UNADJUSTED] label
and no stamp — directly beneath a line saying the correction was refused
because it CHANGES THE VERDICT. Exit 0.

never read `watch.failures` after `race` returns. coldmount_run.cjs ~192,

pure function directly and asserts the wiring. See

for the shape, and rf2-y7mw7's PR for a worked example including the mutation
proof in both directions.

MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-04: MY "COPIED SHAPE ACROSS THE FLEET" FRAMING WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THIS BEAD'S. Measured by the sweep worker across the whole lane; recording it because the wrong framing invites a fleet-wide refactor nobody needs.

WHAT I SAID: three fail-opens found by three different workers in three different drivers "is the signature of a copied shape, not three coincidences", and I put roughly sixteen drivers in the affected set. This bead's own framing called its defect "a third instance of the same shape".

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, from a derived census of all 23 tracked *run.cjs (48 .cjs total) rather than from either bead's list: THE LANE PARTITIONS CLEANLY - 1 defective, 5 correct watchPage callers, 9 bare handlers, 7 already collect-and-refuse. hd8_run.cjs is THE ONLY ONE of the six watchPage callers that never read .failures; the other five read them AND reach an exit. So there is no widely-copied fail-open in the watchPage family. There is ONE defective driver, now fixed.

The nine-driver pageerror class (rf2-jvheq) is REAL and SEPARATE, and its audit came back POSITIVE rather than speculative: nine demonstrated-live, zero structurally-impossible, zero could-not-determine, SETTLED BY RUNNING IT rather than by reading. Its mechanism is not a copied mistake either - React 19.2's defaultOnUncaughtError routes through reportGlobalError to reportError INSTEAD OF RETHROWING, so a page-side try/catch cannot see it; measured live, pageerror fires, the surrounding catch never runs, and the app carries on to READY. All nine mount through flushSync, so it is NOT closeable inside the apps.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: "sixteen drivers share a copied fail-open" argues for a shared exit-handling framework. "One driver was defective and nine are defeated by a React behaviour they cannot catch" argues for exactly what shipped - a narrow fix in the one driver, no framework, and the nine recorded once in sentinel.cjs where the policy already lives rather than in nine drifting copies. The worker declined to ship nine unproven gate wirings on the ground that "nine unproven wirings would be this same fault in reverse", which is the right call and the reason rf2-sib23 exists instead.

GENERAL LESSON FOR ME: I inferred a class from three independent sightings and stated it as a signature. Three sightings are a reason to COUNT, not a count. The instruction that produced the truth here was "derive the roster, do not take it from either bead" - and what it found was that both beads' rosters were wrong in opposite directions, one overstating the family and the other exactly right about its nine.

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs ~200
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation_run.cjs ~222

benchmark that threw and kept going publishes a precise number for a page

WHY IT MAY NOT BITE. Each of the nine also waits on

any throw path can reach pageerror without the sentinel, the nine are
fail-open and should collect-and-refuse like their neighbours. If none can,
the nine should still say so in a header comment, because the next reader
will ask this question again.

DO NOT WEAKEN ANYTHING TO CLOSE THIS. The remedy, if it is one, is
collect-into-an-array-and-refuse, matching the hicasso tree — not removing
the handler and not relaxing a sentinel.

BRIEF FROM THE BEAD'S NEWEST NOTE, NOT ITS TITLE OR DESCRIPTION — AND TREAT STALENESS AS STRUCTURAL, NOT AS CARELESSNESS. Four instances in one day (2026-08-04), all caught by workers, none by me.

THE FOUR:
  1. rf2-2rtt6.103 — I briefed IMPLEMENTATION from the description's "Build it". A note twelve minutes older than my dispatch had inserted a DESIGN PHASE and stopped implementation before any edit. The worker created no worktree and refused.
  2. rf2-2rtt6.88 — my brief said "no verdict"; the bead's description asked for the recommendation stated. The worker followed the later text and flagged the disagreement in the artefact's own section 0 rather than resolving it silently.
  3. rf2-2rtt6.64 — I scoped it to audits #7396/#7398. The bead carried FIVE audit notes and the live reopen was #7482/#7484, both filed the same day AFTER my picture formed, naming a different defect on a different page.
  4. rf2-2rtt6.84 — I described the #7469 reopen and its capture-lifetime defect in detail. Audit #7475 SUPERSEDES it and the capture repair had ALREADY LANDED. The real remainder was one prose line.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXABLE BY READING HARDER: a brief is a SNAPSHOT and this tracker moves faster than a dispatch cycle. On the day of these four, the tracker gained roughly forty rows from workers filing as they worked, and two of the four beads were re-noted between my read and the worker's start. bd show also prints DESCRIPTION FIRST, so the OLDEST text is the most prominent — and quoting it verbatim, which is the discipline adopted to stop paraphrase errors, LENDS STALE TEXT THE AUTHORITY OF A DIRECT QUOTE.

SO THE ANSWER IS RECOVERABILITY, NOT PREVENTION. Every brief must carry, verbatim and near the top: "RUN bd show FIRST AND READ IT BOTTOM-UP - newest note first, description LAST. THE BEAD OUTRANKS THIS BRIEF. Tell me where I am wrong." That sentence caught all four. It is a MECHANISM, not a courtesy, and it should never be trimmed for brevity.

TWO SECOND-ORDER RULES THAT FALL OUT:
  - Name the bead and the verification, not your recollection of its contents. Where a brief must supply a fact, mark it as the mayor's recollection to be checked, not as an established premise.
  - Do not mandate a PR title. On rf2-2rtt6.84 the title I specified would have misdescribed a two-docstring diff; the worker used an accurate one and explained the deviation. A title asserted before the work is another snapshot claim.

AND THE MIRROR CASE, so this does not become an excuse: a worker that finds the bead and the brief in conflict must SAY SO rather than silently choosing. All four did. The value of the instruction is the report, not merely the override.

title: DESIGN: the Reagent [:>] migration codemod — spec via design+adversarial pass after the [:>] contract lands; mayor implements
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). The Reagent migration codemod — guide 05-interop.md:164 + :286: "A codemod is planned and not built."

DEPENDENCY: the [:>] programme (rf2-2rtt6.103) — its migration-fidelity designer is drafting the CODEMOD CONTRACT (what [:>] must guarantee so a mechanical [:> X ...] -> defhost rewrite is always behaviour-preserving). This design pass runs AFTER that synthesis lands and consumes the contract as its ground truth.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. INPUT DIALECT: Reagent [:> Component ...] sites. Survey what else migrating code actually carries — r/adapt-react-class values in head position, reactify/adapt round-trips — and rule each in (rewritable), out (left with a named report line), or [:>]-preserved (now legal in Hicasso, so "leave as [:>]" is a valid output for sites the rewrite cannot make behaviour-preserving; the codemod's job narrows to executing "declare what you use twice").
2. OUTPUT SHAPE: ONE defhost declaration per distinct component (dedupe across N sites), hoisted to namespace level; the minted declaration's naming convention; what happens to per-site prop differences (the declaration carries policy — if two sites need different policies, that is a report line, not a guess).
3. NON-MECHANICAL SITES: dynamic component expressions, computed props spreads, children with Reagent-specific forms — each class enumerated with its disposition (rewrite / preserve-as-[:>] / report). The codemod NEVER silently changes behaviour; the contract from .103 defines "behaviour-preserving" and every site outside it is reported, not rewritten.
4. RESIDENCE + TOOLING: where it lives (tools/ vs scripts/ — it is dev tooling operating on consumer source; check how existing tools are packaged and the bundle-isolation law: nothing in implementation/ requires tools/); rewrite-clj (or equivalent) as the parsing substrate — verify what the repo already depends on before adding a dependency; CLI shape (paths in, diff/report out); idempotence (running twice = no-op).
5. WITNESSES: a golden-file corpus — input namespace -> expected output + expected report — covering the rewrite, the dedupe, each preserve class, each report class, and idempotence. The corpus IS the spec.
6. MIGRATION DOCS DELTA: guide 05:164/:286 + the migration guide tree (migration/from-re-frame-v1/ is hot-zone README territory — check whether the codemod belongs in its docs and flag sequencing if so).

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: silent behaviour change (the only fatal class), the dedupe-vs-policy-divergence edge, and scope creep (the codemod must not become a general Reagent migrator — [:>] sites only).

Implementation is the mayor's, from the appended spec. No AI attribution.

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; design + adversarial review complete; 2 FATAL / 5 MAJOR / 7 MINOR; verdict BUILD WITH THE NAMED REPAIRS — both fatals are one root error, repaired inside the fence). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment, SEQUENCED AFTER rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation MERGES (migrated output preserves [:>] sites, which must exist at runtime). Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.codemod-design.md + codemod-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE TOOL: migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/ — the exact sibling precedent shape (migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/: standalone deps.edn, rewrite-clj 1.1.49 already a repo dependency, cognitect :test, clojure -M:run CLI, whole-file writes, parse failure = skip file + report). Zero public library concepts. The corpus IS the spec: corpus/<case>/{input.cljs, expected.cljs, report.edn, post-report.edn}, ~40 cases after repairs, one JVM harness deftest asserting every case + IDEMPOTENCE (rewrite∘rewrite = rewrite byte-for-byte + report stability).

THE ONE GOVERNING LAW (the root-error repair, F1): SITE-LOCAL REWRITES APPLY AT EVERY [:>] SITE — collected-and-hoisted OR preserved-as-[:>] alike. The four rewrites are properties of the CROSSING, not the head: (1) ^{:key k} metadata -> :key in props (NO Hicasso path reads metadata — verified; unrewritten = dead keys); (2) nested kebab :style literals -> the shallow-door-safe spelling (unrewritten at a preserved site = silently unstyled); (3) literal :class collections -> the ruled spelling (else "a,b" strings); (4) r/partial and other non-fn IFn LITERALS at props -> plain fn-wrap, or report where non-literal (the door's IFn refusal is [:>]'s to land per .103; the codemod's write-time wrap/report is its OWN net and stands regardless). Plus the guards: vector/key-map literals at event props on STRING-TAG rewrites are the inert->live fatal class — REPORT, never rewrite silently; dangerouslySetInnerHTML at any rewritten site -> report (Reagent deleted it, template.cljs:131-135; both Hicasso paths resurrect it).

INPUT DIALECT (verified against reagent 2.0.1): IN — [:>] sites; adapt-react-class def-site (renamed-preserving defhost) AND inline-head; string tags (MANDATORY rewrite to native tags — the ruled [:>] refuses strings; R1/R3 conduct equivalence verified clean: the converge door, deep-camel boundary, class-names, fn-identity, custom elements all match the donor); ^{:key} metadata. PRESERVED as [:>] + report: dynamic heads, reactify/create-class heads. REPORTED only: :r> (raw JS props unhoistable), :f> (out of scope), r/as-element islands inside rewritten sites, computed props maps (map?-at-index-1 undecidable for non-literals — report-only, coverage capped honestly).

F2 REPAIR (adapt-react-class def-site): a def-site rewrite changes every call site's conversion regime (deep->shallow, live keys->dead) — SAME-FILE call sites of a rewritten def become collected sites (the site-local rewrites apply there); CROSS-NAMESPACE exposure gets a named report line, never silence.

M1+M2 REPAIR (the hoist gate): the sibling's shadowing analysis does NOT transfer (wrong question, rosters missing defn params + with-let — as specified it would hoist the FLAGSHIP ruled use case, (defn row [component] [:> component ...]), into a load-time mint-host! nil refusal). The gate is: ANCESTRY-WALK analysis with POSITIVE VAR EVIDENCE (hoist only heads resolving to a var) + the TEXTUAL-ORDER precondition (the component's def textually precedes the minted defhost's placement — defhost evaluates its component at ns-load, so declare-then-def inputs PRESERVE + report).

DEDUPE + NS SURGERY: one (h/defhost kebab-name X {}) per distinct component EXPRESSION per namespace, placed before first use, reusing pre-existing declarations; collision chain -host suffix -> report+skip (verified non-shadowing). NS injector is the NARROW v1: append to the first :require clause, recognized ns-form shapes only; anything else (reader conditionals, exotic forms) = skip the HOISTS + report, while the require-free site-local rewrites STILL APPLY (a skipped injection never suppresses them).

M4 REPAIR (the equivalence witness): the one fixture-pair witness covers the host walk only — add ~6-8 named codemod-contract rows in the bench lane (door-side, part of THIS bead's PR; witnesses of existing behaviour, not door code) pinning the NATIVE-walk equivalence the string-tag rewrite relies on (same props through Reagent's [:> "input"] conduct vs Hicasso's native [:input]: converge, class, style, fn-identity rows). WEAK-POINT 2 DECLARED, not engineered around: the equivalence theorem is inherited from the one-shared-walk fact — door drift (.119, .104-class changes) invalidates the contract without failing a codemod test; the contract rows are the tripwire, and .119's resolution should land before or with this tool.

REPORT: first-class — suggested :callbacks declarations (the position-table vocabulary as STATIC-ANALYSIS language only, never runtime semantics), computed-props sites, preserved dynamic heads (WITH the warning that Reagent-only literals at those sites were rewritten per the governing law — the report explains what changed and what could not), cross-ns adapt exposure, skipped ns-surgery. Missed sites fail loudly at the doors' own refusals (the runtime net).

DOCS: guide bead rf2-2rtt6.112 (already filed, deps this bead) teaches it after the implementation PR MERGES; the migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md question is flagged there (hot-zone, mayor sequences). No AI attribution.

title: spec 008 contradicts spec 004B: 'the v1 node set carries no host variant' is stale
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design A (rf2-2rtt6.103), researching what 'reduced structural identity' concretely means. Not fixed there: that bead is fenced to docs/design/hicasso/** and this is a spec/** edit in a hot-zone file.

THE CONTRADICTION. Two spec files make opposite claims about the SAME v1 node set.

spec/008-Testing.md:770-771 (the tier/coverage roster, 'qualified host' row):
  'a foreign boundary is opaque to the structural render (the v1 node set carries
   no host variant), so a qualified-host law is proven by connecting the real
   behaviour or wrapper in a browser under its own host-boundary slice, never by
   the structural surface.'

spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:122,134 — heading 'The node schema — version 1',
whose closed roster carries a host variant explicitly:
  | **host** | map | :rf.ui/host :rf.ui/host-ssr :children | :props :rf.ui/host-children :rf.ui/host-map-props :key |
and :146-148 puts :rf.ui/host in the discriminator's pinned order, and :350-353 states
the fields ARE a node rather than annotations on one.

004B IS THE SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR, so 008 is the stale side. Three confirmations:
  1. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/test.cljc — node-kind's pinned
     discriminator has a host arm reading :rf.ui/host.
  2. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/structural_test_surface_cljs_test.cljc
     — deftest attrs-reaches-a-declared-hosts-props finds the crossing with
     #(contains? % :rf.ui/host), asserts (= ::date-picker (:rf.ui/host host)) and
     (= :client-only (:rf.ui/host-ssr host)).
  3. That test's own docstring records the repair (rf2-c20nr): before it, the host node
     fell through the discriminator to the FRAGMENT arm and attrs answered {} —
     silently, because that arm is documented total. 004B:459-462 states the same
     hazard as a rule.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. 008's sentence tells a reader that a declared host
crossing CANNOT be asserted structurally and must be proven in a browser. That is
advice to write a browser test where a headless one already works, and it is the
exact wrong reading for anyone reasoning about what a foreign crossing costs a test
suite — which is a live question on EP-0038 (HD-011's 'reduced structural identity').

THE FIX is one paragraph in spec/008-Testing.md: the v1 node set DOES carry a host
variant with an identity (:rf.ui/host), its SSR policy (:rf.ui/host-ssr) and its
:props; what stays opaque to the structural render is what the foreign component
RENDERS BENEATH the crossing, not the crossing node itself. Check the surrounding
tier table (~:620-630) for the same claim restated, and re-grep 008 for 'opaque'
and 'host variant' before editing.

FENCES: spec/008-Testing.md only. It is a hot-zone file (spec/*) — sequence, do not
parallel with another spec/008 bead. mkdocs build --strict DOES cover spec/, plus
check_doc_slugs.py and the fast-PR spine.

3. MY GUIDE INSTRUCTION INVERTED THE BEAD. I wrote that the guide is not the worker's to grow and that guide prose would be a separate bead. The bead MANDATES a guide true-up IN THE SAME PR at five named sites, all still reading as unbuilt: 02-views-and-reads.md:78, 05-interop.md:48/148/151/164 plus :286, and 08-testing.md:14 and :44. BOOBY TRAP FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS — surfaced by design B (PR #7490), recorded here because the implementer meets it and the design page is not what they will be reading when it fires.

X2's BODY-RUN EQUALITY IS DELIBERATELY BROKEN BY ANY :client-only CROSSING. arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:414 asserts (= boundary-count (rt/body-runs)), read after adoption. It is green today ONLY because no page it drives carries a client-only crossing. IT GOES RED ON CORRECT CODE the moment the first one is added - via [:>] OR via a defhost :ssr :client-only, so this is not specific to the escape.

WHY THAT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY INCONVENIENT: the implementer will see a red assertion in a hydration witness they did not touch, on a tree where their own change is correct. The two obvious readings - my change is wrong, or this test is wrong - are both wrong. The count is SUPPOSED to move, because a client-only crossing legitimately runs a body the server never ran.

WHAT TO DO WHEN IT FIRES: do not delete the assertion and do not loosen it to a range. Restate it in terms that stay falsifiable - body runs equal boundary count PLUS the number of client-only crossings on the page - so it still fails if a body runs twice or a boundary is skipped. A SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME DESIGN, which is a live latent hazard independent of any of this: :> IS NOT CURRENTLY AN ERROR. hiccup-tag? accepts it, so [:> Foo {}] on main today asks React for an element literally named <>.
