SYNTHESIZED SPEC LANDED (2026-08-05) — docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-spec.md, on branch worker/rawsynth-2rtt6-103. This note is the operative summary; the page carries the argument. IMPLEMENTATION RE-DISPATCHES FROM THE PAGE, NOT FROM THIS NOTE — but a dispatcher who reads only this note gets every ruling.

WHAT IT SYNTHESIZED: TEN inputs, not three and not six. The three tracked studio designs (A minimal / B correctness / C ergonomics), the six local-only ai/findings documents (parity + minimal + migration designs and their three adversarial passes), and THIS BEAD'S OWN 12:06 COMMENT, which is itself a synthesis of the local six and had never read A, B or C. Everything relied on from the gitignored set is quoted into the tracked page, so none of it dies with the local tree.

THE FIVE EDGES, RULED:

E1 SSR/HYDRATION — hard :client-only through ONE module-level shared gate reusing the landed snapshot triple (codec.cljs:1035-1037) with placeholder nil. No fallback spelling of any kind. Server-absent and hydration-first-pass-absent are ONE fact that React chooses, not two facts kept in step. The only unanimous edge across all nine design/attack documents. Carrier: two slots on the gate's own props (#js {c, p} — the boundary-element rfProps idiom); children on the OUTER element via make-element's existing arms. Design A's strip-a-key carrier is rejected on A's own pricing: it costs a shallow copy per crossing per render and leaks an internal key A itself says must be witnessed, where the two-slot shape makes that leak unrepresentable instead.

E2 PROPS — the door's unclaimed-slot conduct of host-entry with an empty declared map, exactly, and with no branch of its own. Vectors and key-maps at event-spelled slots refuse loudly; marked h/fn and plain fns cross BY IDENTITY with returns ignored; :& merged before conversion; :key to the outer element; :ref through check-ref!.

E3 IDENTITY — four statements. Canonical DOM is NOT reduced at all, and this is provable rather than asserted: lane/canonical serialises element and text nodes and ignores comments, so a nil-rendering gate is invisible to it. The data lane is reduced at EXACTLY ONE SLOT (slot 1 compares by JS identity; total everywhere else in the vector) and that is the whole of the ruled phrase. One shared gate type, displayName the constant "[:>]", and NO name extraction — React resolves displayName || name || null, Closure renames .name under :advanced, and foreign production bundles drop displayName, so any derived identity is build-dependent. Plus a recorded forward obligation for the unbuilt headless render.

E4 LEGAL VALUES — a pinned roster REFUSED AT THE CROSSING in the owner's render. Strings and nil refused. React's own refusal is minted at fiber creation, which behind the gate is post-adoption and client-only, and for any ClojureScript value its message reads "got: object" because it names typeof — so delegation loses on timing, on stack, and on message. The pinning witness is NOT optional: it is what turns a React upgrade into a red row instead of a silent false-refusal, which is the worst failure a hatch can have.

E5 CHILDREN — nothing new. Eager lowering in the owner's render window through the same make-element arms. Unanimous across all six designs.

EDGES 2 AND 5 ARE ONE AND A HALF DECISIONS — not one (design C's claim) and not two independent ones. E5's CHILDREN half is invariant under every candidate answer to E2, because E2 governs props on the [:>] node while children carry their own positions inside hiccup the author owns; every one of the six designs states the children rule identically regardless of its E2. So it is stated independently and is SAFE TO BUILD BEFORE E2 IS FINALLY RULED. E5's render-prop-PROP half is wholly determined by E2, and C is right about that half — which is why the message repair in (e) below stops being a nicety and becomes that half's deliverable.

WHERE THIS DEPARTS FROM THE 12:06 COMMENT — one substantive difference, stated so it is not read as an oversight. That comment ships a DEV-ONLY WARNING at [:>] only, while the same programme files rf2-2rtt6.117 asking whether the door should get the same diagnostic. That is a fork at the one edge whose entire argument is zero-fork. The spec instead PINS the escape to the door: the escape's conduct at an unclaimed prop is whatever .116 rules for the door, and its diagnostic whatever .117 rules. Refuse at both, warn at both, or leave both — in all three branches the zero-fork invariant holds and no line of the escape's mechanism changes. The decisive reason, which only the attack on the migration design states in full: IF THE ESCAPE REFUSES WHAT THE DOOR ACCEPTS, [:> X ...] -> (defhost x X {}) IS NO LONGER BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, AND THAT REWRITE IS THE WHOLE THEOREM OF rf2-2rtt6.106'S CODEMOD. Design A's and the local minimal design's h/fn refusal is therefore rejected on composition grounds, not on its merits in isolation — it is the only stance with no silent cell and both pages price it honestly.

WHAT THE SYNTHESIS ATTACKED THAT NOTHING HAD (the adversarial wave ran on the local three only, so A, B and C had never been attacked at all):

(a) THE HEAD TEST COSTS NOTHING, and design B's "must cost nothing" constraint — for which B offers no mechanism, falling back on "or measure and publish the delta" — is exactly satisfiable. hiccup-tag? has EXACTLY ONE CALLER (vec->element's cond) and sits AFTER the fragment-head? arm, yet its body still re-asks (not (fragment-head? head)). So EVERY NATIVE TAG ON EVERY PAGE PAYS THE FRAGMENT = TWICE TODAY. Drop the provably-dead second test and add raw-head? as a cond arm before hiccup-tag?: a keyword tag pays two = and one type predicate before, and two = and one type predicate after. Identical. Nobody in ten documents noticed, and it matters because this codec has costed a keyword? short-circuit at +/-51-67% of a walk.

(b) DESIGN B'S MECHANISM IS DEAD TWICE OVER. Its WeakMap-keyed gate throws on React's built-in wrapper types, which are registered symbols that ES2024 excludes as WeakMap keys — re-verified on this repo's pinned React 19.2.0 under Node v24.13.0. AND its edge-4 table refuses symbols while its edge-4 prose four paragraphs later accepts Suspense. Keep the prose and the WeakMap throws; keep the table and the escape refuses Suspense while accepting React.lazy, which REQUIRES a Suspense ancestor — the exact pairing HD-011 names as a reason the escape exists.

(c) DESIGN C'S E2 falls to the two attacks that killed migration's identical move, neither of which was ever run against C, plus a charge neither made: C routes an h/fn at a non-event slot to the RENDER contract, which mints a fresh wrapper per lowering and destroys the function identity host-prop-value preserves deliberately so that React.memo and every downstream bail-out comparing handler identity keep working (HD-024's own Rationale says so in terms). C never prices this. And C's showcase spelling, renderRow, is the one that survives; the spelling C concedes it gets wrong, onRenderRow, is the ecosystem one (Fluent UI).

(d) h/as-element DOES NOT EXIST. Four of the six designs name it as the recovery for the two sharpest SILENT traps at this crossing — hiccup written in a prop, and a function child or render-prop body returning hiccup — and design C's entire render-prop worked example is built on it. Verified: ZERO occurrences of as-element anywhere under docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/; the guide's taught h/ roster is h/hicasso, h/root, h/fn, h/render, h/defhost, h/presence, h/child-key, h/boundary; arm1/lang.clj exports exactly three macros (defview, hfn, defhost) and no as-element. The MECHANISM is public as codec/as-element (codec.cljs:1708); the TAUGHT NAME is not. An error message naming a spelling the reader cannot call is worse than no message. FILED AS rf2-2rtt6.120 (P2) — resolve it BEFORE .103's refusal messages and guide rows are written, not during.

(e) THE 12:06 COMMENT DROPS TWO LOAD-BEARING CARRIES, both restored on the page. First, the X2 body-run restatement. Second, design A's intent-outside-boundary message repair: at [:>] the author IS inside a boundary's render as far as they can see, since they wrote the crossing in a body, so the current message and its :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render recovery will read as a framework bug. The runtime cannot tell the two causes apart from *dispatch* = nil alone, so the message must offer BOTH readings and name defhost with :callbacks {... :render} as the second. A dispatcher briefing from that comment alone ships without either.

FOUR RULINGS LEFT TO THE OPERATOR AND NOT TAKEN — recommendation and cost are on the page, and in every case the spec is written so that no line of the escape's mechanism changes with the answer:

R1 — h/fn at an unclaimed prop slot (rf2-2rtt6.116, with rf2-2rtt6.117 for the door's diagnostic). Recommendation: rule it for the DOOR and let the escape inherit. Cost of refusing: it chips HD-024's cleanest claim, that the marked form is callable everywhere and degrades to a defensible contract rather than a crash. Cost of leaving: a silent dead return on the guide's own taught path for value-first invokers. Cost of warning: a diagnostic surface the record must justify against the anti-nag posture.

R2 — defhost's :ssr has no value that renders children (rf2-l0wfx, P1). A provider — one of HD-011's five named use cases, and the guide's own example at 05-interop.md:120 — deletes its subtree from the server render. Design C recommends a third :ssr value meaning render the children in place of the component. The attack on the local minimal design offers a second route: a Context-head carve-out, since a React 19 Context is detectable at the crossing by $$typeof and its server render is React's own context machinery, deterministic and with no window risk — so the "nobody can vouch for the server render" defence is false for providers specifically. Cost of neither: providers are ruled out of SSR and the guide must say so. THE ESCAPE MUST NEVER GROW AN :ssr SPELLING OF ITS OWN; it inherits whatever the door becomes.

R3 — refusing a Hicasso view or host head in Component position exceeds clause 5's letter, since both are values React accepts. Recommended anyway: a defview head is fn?-true, so a bare "is it a function" test accepts [:> my-view ...] and mounts the shell raw, the body reads rfProps, gets undefined, and receives nil props. That is silent breakage of the kind a migration produces. Removable without touching the mechanism — it is a predicate and two message flavours.

R4 — rf2-2rtt6.115's dated scope-note on HD-024's row 3 must land before or with the escape. E2 rests on that resolution, and it is decisions.md, outside the synthesis fence, so it is named here rather than discovered by the implementer.

IMPLEMENTER'S CARRY-LIST — six facts verified against main, in full on the page. (1) :> IS NOT CURRENTLY AN ERROR: hiccup-tag? (codec.cljs:1673-1675) accepts any keyword that is not :<>, and vec->element (:1689) routes it to native-element, so [:> Foo {}] today asks React for an element named <>. The branch must PRECEDE hiccup-tag? and compare with = and never identical?, or it is DEAD CODE THAT COMPILES CLEANLY. (2) The head test is free, per (a). (3) X2's body-run equality at arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:414 GOES RED ON CORRECT CODE at the first client-only crossing — via [:>] or via a defhost :ssr :client-only — and must be restated as boundary count PLUS the number of client-only crossings, never deleted and never loosened to a range. (4) The argv indices shift by one: component at 1, attr map at 2 when it is a map, children from 3 or 2; bare [:>] takes the no-component refusal. (5) check-ref! refuses only a vector, so an object ref passes today (rf2-d03av) — do NOT add a [:>]-only ref refusal, because a rule enforced at one crossing and not the other is worse than one enforced at neither. (6) host-entry has no class branch (rf2-2rtt6.119), and note the trap: edge 3's canonical-parity row CANNOT catch it, because both forms are identically wrong.

NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD — it stays open for implementation, and rf2-2rtt6.109 reads the page.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7497 (merged 2026-08-04T17:36:54Z, a1f59a0a3bbc8ba0c41bcf9d5f7b63cdb1f45a59) — CORRECTNESS FOLLOW-UP. The synthesized spec's implementer carry-list (§8.3) says the X2 body-run equality goes red at the first client-only crossing and must become boundary-count PLUS the number of client-only crossings. That is not true for the mechanism this same spec selects. `mint-host-gate!` and the proposed shared raw gate are explicitly not Hicasso boundaries and have no Hicasso body (`front/codec.cljs`:1646-1647); `runtime/body-runs` increments only inside `run-once`, where an actual Hicasso boundary body is invoked (`arm1/runtime.cljs`:1532-1550, 1615-1640). Adoption's `useSyncExternalStore` update rerenders the gate. A plain foreign component behind `[:>]` or a `defhost :ssr :client-only` therefore adds zero body runs; a gate can add zero, one, or many only insofar as it defers actual Hicasso boundaries beneath it. Following the stated crossings formula would make a correct implementation's witness fail or encode a topology-dependent miscount. Correct `raw-escape-spec.md` §8.3 and this bead's appended synthesis note before implementation: keep X2 exact, but derive its expected count from the boundary bodies in the fixture, including any bodies first mounted beneath client-only gates—not from the number of crossings. This already-open implementation/spec owner is exact; no duplicate Bead.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; 3 designs — parity/minimal/migration — + 3 adversarial reviews; verdicts 0F/5M, 0F/5M, 1F/3M; all three forced choices converge on a parity–minimal hybrid). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.rawescape-* (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient). HD-011's core stands untouched: same foreign path, same default conversions, .cljs-only at the node, explicitly secondary, "declare what you use twice", bare-head auto-hosting stays rejected.

THE RULED SHAPE, per edge:

E1 SSR/HYDRATION (unanimous): hard :client-only via ONE shared module-level raw gate reusing the landed gate-adopted/gate-unadopted snapshots (codec.cljs ~:1035-1066). Server emits nothing; hydration's first pass emits nothing; adoption swaps the component in — R2 zero-mismatch by construction. NO inline fallback spelling (a fallback is policy; policy lives on declarations — want one, write defhost {:fallback}). The guide TEACHES the 3-line userland wrapper-host pattern for per-site fallbacks. Provider-subtree SSR hole: sequenced behind rf2-l0wfx; the Context-head carve-out question is flagged to the .88 SSR sitting, not solved here.

E2 PROPS (adjudicated across a 2-1 attacker split): vectors and key-maps at event-spelled props REFUSE LOUDLY (:rf.error/hicasso-raw-intent-needs-a-declaration; message names defhost :callbacks as the door AND states that h/fn returns do not dispatch here). Marked h/fn and plain fns cross BY IDENTITY (the door's landed undeclared-slot conduct — zero behavioural fork with defhost), with returns ignored. NEW: a DEV-ONLY loud warning (goog.DEBUG; the codec's dev-warning idiom) whenever a MARKED h/fn lands on any [:>] prop — naming the silent-return fact and both real doors — closing the taught-path silent cell the minimal attack proved (guide 05 teaches h/fn for value-first invokers) without forking runtime semantics. Vectors at non-event slots are data via the door's conversion. MIGRATION'S SPELLING-CLASSIFIER E2 IS REJECTED (FATAL: Fluent onRender*/Ant onRow are event-spelled render-props/return-readers — nil-returning event wrappers blank them silently); the position table survives ONLY as the codemod's static-analysis vocabulary.

E3 IDENTITY: the :> head keyword is the data-lane marker; ONE shared gate type in the fiber lane (no per-component gates — that is the rejected auto-hosting cache); NO name extraction into fiber identity (displayName/name are :advanced-hostile); a name RESOLVER for diagnostic messages only. Canonical DOM at the node is provably indistinguishable from the defhost equivalent (lane/canonical reads element/text nodes only) — witnessed. Inner element typed by the component value: state preserved iff same component identity (the runtime-selected use case remounts on type flip, correctly).

E4 LEGAL VALUES (minimal's mechanism, three verdicts concur): a pinned roster — fns, React's built-in Symbol.for exotics, $$typeof ∈ {context, consumer, forward_ref, memo, lazy} — refused AT THE CROSSING in the owner's render (React's own invalid-type error fires at fiber creation = post-adoption, client-only, names nothing the author wrote — verified). REFUSED: strings (the grammar owns tags; Reagent's [:> "input"] took the controlled wrapper, so acceptance would silently drop caret protection — donor-verified), nil/undefined (broken-import diagnosis), defview/defhost marked heads (silent nil-props breakage otherwise), and non-fn IFns (r/partial/multimethods — WORKING Reagent sites that would die as opaque objects; loud refusal steers to fn-wrapping). Error id :rf.error/hicasso-raw-not-a-component with shape-specific fixes.

E5 CHILDREN (unanimous): trailing forms lower eagerly in the owning boundary's render window — intent closures capture the owner's frame-locked dispatch at lowering time (the .74 temporal ruling; the arming gate composes when [:>] sits inside a declared :render callback). Render-prop PROPS on the raw node are out of scope (defhost :render territory); render-prop-SUPPLIED components are in scope. :& merged before conversion per clause (d) — witnessed at the crossing.

INCIDENTAL FIX: the codec currently MIS-PARSES :> as a native tag named ">" — the new branch replaces that; add the regression row.

rf2-2rtt6.115 RESOLVED (three independent adjudications concur): the CODE side is authoritative — HD-024's row 3 at decisions.md:1015 OVER-RECORDS; the door's undeclared-slot identity crossing was deliberate (one-commit evidence 86ed3a330e + the .65 landing's reasoned docstring). EXECUTE IN THIS PR: a dated scope-note on row 3 + a witness pinning the door's undeclared marked-h/fn identity crossing (currently unwitnessed — host_hatch pins only a plain fn). The migration design's "align defhost with row 3" follow-up is STRUCK as adverse.

WITNESSES: conversion parity with defhost on the same fixture component (the load-bearing row); every refusal row (vectors, key-maps at event slots; strings; nil; marked heads; IFn) + the dev-warning row for marked h/fn; SSR-absent + hydration-adoption rows; :& at the crossing; callback-ref legal + string/keyword ref refused (HD-016); children-capture row (an intent inside [:>] children dispatches to the owner's frame); canonical-DOM indistinguishability; the mis-parse regression; the .115 door witness + scope-note.

SIZE: ~100-140 lines in front/codec.cljs + witnesses. FENCES: bench lane + decisions.md (the row-3 scope-note + a dated [:>]-shape note on HD-011, digtt pattern). SEQUENCING: codec.cljs now has THREE beads touching it (.103, .104, .107's pre-merge read) — mayor sequences; .104's warning inherits [:>] children automatically once both land. Gates: hicasso compile + DOM suites + fast-PR spine, foreground. Guide: the code PR carries the tense-flips (02:78, 05:48/:148-163/:174, 08:44); bead .109 teaches fully after MERGE. The codemod contract for .106: hoist-only is mechanical and behaviour-preserving; :callbacks synthesis is never mechanical (human or explicit flag); four Reagent-input rewrites + first-class report. manifest and console/live metrics label JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit counts
(string.length) as bytes." It gives the numbers — dogfood-snapshot 3101 claimed

title: hicasso: the guide owes a prop-VALUE row after rf2-vrvv9, and two namespace-dropping positions are left standing
description:
FOLLOW-ON to rf2-vrvv9 (PR #7500), which narrowed front/codec.cljs's host-prop-value so a keyword crosses a foreign crossing whole instead of via (name v).

## 1. THE GUIDE OWES TWO ROWS (the actual obligation)

rf2-vrvv9's fence kept guide prose out of scope, and no existing sentence became FALSE - docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md's Defaults table speaks only about KEYS ('Props | shallow camelCase - :on-change -> onChange'). But it is now INCOMPLETE, and incompleteness is what made the original bug a trap:

  (a) Defaults table needs a VALUES row. Something like: 'Prop values | crossed whole - a keyword stays a keyword; only :class/:id/:role/:data-*/:aria-* stringify'.
  (b) Troubleshooting needs a row: 'The library ignored my keyword prop | a non-HTML prop name passes keywords through unchanged | write the string, or (name v), at the call site'.

Without (b) the change MOVES the silent failure rather than deleting it: [host {:variant :compact}] used to reach the library as "compact" and now reaches it as a raw keyword the library cannot use. That is a smaller and more local failure than the collision it replaced (it breaks at the node, visibly, with a call-site fix) - and reagent-slim's answer to the same trade was a dev warn-once. Hicasso's answer is to TEACH it, which only works once the guide says it.

## 2. TWO NAMESPACE-DROPPING POSITIONS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE

Both found while fixing vrvv9, both out of scope for 'one conversion rule at one seam', neither obviously wrong. Recorded so the ruling is made rather than inherited:

  (a) A KEYWORD CHILD. front/codec.cljs as-element: (keyword? x) (name x). [:div :theme/dark] renders the text 'dark'. Same namespace drop, but the destination is a DOM text node, so a string is the only representation and the only question is WHICH string - (name x) vs (str x) = ':theme/dark'. Changing it would move the ORDINARY render path, which vrvv9 was fenced from.

  (b) A COLLECTION VALUE. host-prop-value's (coll? v) (clj->js v) branch. [host {:value {:mode :theme/dark}}] hands the library a JS object whose 'mode' is "dark". HD-011's shallow default already documents that collections go through clj->js, so this is stated rather than silent - but a provider whose :value is a MAP is the same use case vrvv9 was about, and it does not get vrvv9's answer.

## 3. TWO STALE CITATIONS, FOR WHOEVER READS THAT COMMENT NEXT

implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs (~:426-470) cites 'rf2-d4sf' for the coerce-context-value seam and 'rf2-6hyy §7.2 D2' in its warning text. NEITHER is a live bead id (bd show: 'no issue found'). And the same comment credits 'the audit (rf2-cgcv + rf2-kfpf)' for finding legitimate non-HTML keyword props - those two ARE live, but they are React-19-READINESS audits (re-com/10x, Dash8/rf8), both CLOSED as superseded with their findings docs unrecoverable. The real, durable decision record is implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §5 + IMPL-SPEC.md §7.2, and rf2-vrvv9's own description repeated the bad citations from that comment. Not worth a code change on its own; worth fixing if that comment is ever touched.
notes:
SEQUENCED (mayor, 2026-08-05). This bead is the honest other half of rf2-vrvv9's fix and should be dispatched once the codec seam is quiet.

ITS WORKER'S OWN FRAMING, which is why this is not a tidy-up: "without those rows the trap is MOVED, NOT DELETED". Before the fix, {:variant :compact} reached a library as the string "compact" and :theme/dark and :other/dark collided into one value. After it, the keyword arrives as a raw keyword - a smaller, local, call-site-fixable failure than a silent collision, but still a surprise to anyone who expected a string.

reagent-slim answered that same trade with a dev warn-once. THIS WORKER DELIBERATELY DECLINED THAT, and I agree with the reasoning: reagent-slim's warning is a migration net for an installed Reagent codebase, whereas after this fix a keyword at a host prop is the CORRECT, TAUGHT spelling of HD-011's flagship case, and warning on the happy path is a nag. So Hicasso's answer is to TEACH it instead - WHICH ONLY WORKS ONCE THE GUIDE SAYS SO. That makes this bead the thing that completes the fix rather than decorates it.

WHAT IT OWES: a Defaults-table row covering prop VALUES (the existing table speaks only about keys, which is why nothing became false and the worker correctly stayed inside its fence), and a Troubleshooting row for "the library ignored my keyword prop".

ALSO RECORDED ON IT, and worth reading before dispatch: two further namespace-dropping positions left standing deliberately (a keyword CHILD via as-element, and clj->js over a collection value), plus the stale citations in template.cljs.

NOT DISPATCHED YET because the guide is a hot surface tonight - a triple-pass landed at aa9ea1b698 immediately after the fix. The worker checked that PR and confirmed it neither touches this nor writes anything false.

DELIVERED (05-interop.md, all three claims verified against front/codec.cljs:1523-1603 and front/codec_cljs_test.cljs:707-763, not against this bead):
(a) Defaults table — 'Props' renamed 'Prop names'; new 'Prop values' row: crossed whole, a keyword stays a keyword, only :class/:id/:role/data-*/aria-* stringify because an HTML attribute has no other representation.
(b) Troubleshooting row — 'The library ignored a keyword prop value' -> 'A keyword crosses a host prop unchanged; only HTML-attribute names stringify' -> 'Write the string at the call site'.

title: hicasso: host-prop-value DROPS a namespaced keyword's namespace at every foreign crossing — {:value :theme/dark} arrives as "dark"
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103). A defhost/[:>] conversion default, not an escape defect.

THE SHAPE. front/codec.cljs host-prop-value:

    (cond
      (fn? v)                       v
      (or (keyword? v) (symbol? v)) (name v)
      (coll? v)                     (clj->js v)
      :else                         v)

(name :theme/dark) is "dark". The NAMESPACE is silently discarded, so two distinct keywords from different namespaces cross as the same string.

WHERE IT LANDS HARDEST. React-context providers — one of HD-011's five named use cases — whose :value is very often a namespaced keyword. [:> ThemeContext {:value :theme/dark}] hands the provider "dark", and every consumer below reads a string that has lost half its identity.

THE EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS A KNOWN COST. Broad stringification matches STOCK Reagent (verified 2026-08-04 against reagent-project/reagent master, reagent/impl/template.cljs: convert-prop-value's (named? x) (name x) branch). But THIS REPO's own reagent-slim adapter deliberately NARROWED it after an audit — implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs ~:426-470, 'Narrowed convert-prop-value (per DECISION-2 + IMPL-SPEC 7.2)':

  'Keyword values stringify only for HTML attribute names. For non-HTML prop names (e.g. :value on a React-context Provider, custom component props), the keyword passes through unchanged. This deletes the bridge's coerce-context-value seam (rf2-d4sf) — there is no over-stringification to undo because we never broadly stringified.'

Its html-attr-names roster is #{:class :id :role} plus data-*/aria-*, with a dev warn-once for the rest (rf2-cgcv, rf2-kfpf found a small number of legitimate non-HTML keyword props in production code).

So Hicasso's shallow default re-opens the exact seam a prior audit in this repo closed, in the same component position, for the same reason.

QUESTION FOR RULING. Is broad (name v) the default we want at a Hicasso foreign crossing, or does Hicasso adopt reagent-slim's narrowing (stringify for HTML-attribute names only; keywords otherwise cross unchanged)? HD-011 names 'shallow camelCase props' as the default and says nothing about keyword VALUES, so this is open rather than ruled.

NOTE the cost of changing it: keyword values on native tags must keep stringifying (the pure SSR serializer stringifies unconditionally and a divergence is a hydration mismatch — reagent-slim records this at rf2-fdm4rm). Any narrowing is at the FOREIGN crossing only.

title: hicasso: HD-016's 'callback refs only' is UNENFORCED against object refs — check-ref! refuses only the reserved vector
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103), designing the [:>] crossing's ref boundary.

THE RULE AS WRITTEN. HD-016 (decisions.md ~:513) rules ':ref is legal on native tags and defhost/[:>] crossings (CALLBACK REFS ONLY)'. rf2-2rtt6.103's clause 3 restates it. The guide's ABI table (02-views-and-reads.md:78) says 'callback ref, legal'.

THE RULE AS ENFORCED. front/codec.cljs check-ref! is a WHEN, not a cond:

    [k v]
    (when (vector? v)
      (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-ref-vector-reserved ...))
    v

It refuses exactly ONE shape — a VECTOR, which is HD-022's reserved data spelling ({:ref [registered-id config]}) — and passes EVERYTHING else through: a function, nil, a string, and an OBJECT ref. React 19 carries ref as an ordinary prop, so (react/createRef) works fine at a native tag and at a defhost crossing today.

SO 'callback refs only' is a documented rule with no mechanism behind it. A Reagent migrant's object ref will simply work, and the guide says it should not.

EITHER the rule is narrower than it reads — the real rule being 'the reserved VECTOR spelling is not a v0 surface', with object refs an untaught-but-tolerated React fact — OR the check is narrower than the rule and object refs should refuse with a named error.

DESIGN C'S POSITION (recorded, not ruling): do NOT add a refusal at [:>] that defhost does not have. Conversion parity across the two crossing forms is HD-011's ruling, and a rule enforced at one crossing and not the other is worse than a rule enforced at neither. Whatever is decided applies to BOTH, and to native tags.

CHEAP EITHER WAY: one cond arm in check-ref!, or one clause edit in HD-016 plus the guide's ABI table.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7503 (merged 2026-08-04T19:03:47Z, bb942a8c0dbc1141bf037235cba75b93eed2567f) — VERIFIED COMPLETE AS A RECORD. The dated HD-016 note and authoring/interop/spec text now make object refs untaught-but-legal, while the witness pins identity at native and defhost crossings and preserves the reserved-vector refusal. `npm run test:freehand --silent` passed 1,399 tests / 7,753 assertions, and every required merged-commit check passed. Close this exact owner as delivered.
SETTLED in PR #7503 (2026-08-05) as A RECORD, not a refusal -- the bead first horn: THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN IT READS, not the check.

THE ARGUMENT. HD-016 clause reads as a prohibition ("callback refs only"). HD-022 -- LATER, and the ruling actually about :ref value space -- says in as many words: "That is the whole ruling: one refusal branch and one error id." check-ref! is therefore exactly what HD-022 ruled, not a check that fell short of it. Later and more specific governs.

WHAT THAT MAKES AN OBJECT REF: untaught, not illegal. React 19 carries ref as an ordinary prop, so (react/createRef) attaches and detaches exactly as React documents, at a native tag and at a defhost crossing alike. Verified end to end: check-ref! passes it, then convert-prop-value :else (a plain JS object is not map?/coll?) and host-prop-value :else both cross it by identity. NOTHING IS SILENTLY DROPPED AND NOTHING NEEDS REPAIRING -- which is the whole argument against a branch. Refusing a spelling that works correctly is friction rather than safety, and the guide teaching the callback form (React 19 makes attach and teardown structural there) is an ergonomic recommendation the codec has no business policing.

DESIGN C PARITY RULE IS SATISFIED FOR FREE. Whatever is decided applies to both crossing forms and to native tags; doing nothing IS parity. No refusal was added at [:>] that defhost lacks, exactly as design C directs. raw-escape-spec.md sec.8 item 5 now records the outcome as the one it asked for.

SHIPPED: a dated 2026-08-05 note on HD-016 (the repo own amendment form, ruling text left intact) stating the enforced-vs-taught distinction and the HD-022 precedence; authoring.md and draft-guide/05-interop.md true-ed up to say what is ENFORCED (the vector, and only the vector); and -- the part that makes this a decision rather than an oversight -- an executable witness, front/codec_cljs_test/an-object-ref-crosses-by-identity-at-both-positions, covering native + defhost and an alternate ref spelling at each.

MUTATION PROOF THAT DOUBLES AS EVIDENCE FOR THE BEAD OWN CLAIM: adding an object-ref refusal to check-ref! produced 4 errors, ALL in the new witness, and NOTHING ELSE IN 12,585 TESTS MOVED. That is the bead "a documented rule with no mechanism behind it", measured -- the behaviour was pinned nowhere in the suite before this. It is pinned now, so a later refusal cannot land silently: it has to delete those rows first.

title: hicasso: an h/fn at an UNCLAIMED defhost prop slot is a marked callback nothing reads — silent-dead-handler fail-open
description:
FOUND while designing the [:> ] raw escape (rf2-2rtt6.103, design B — docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-design-b-correctness.md, PR #7490). This is a finding about SHIPPED defhost behaviour, not about the escape, which is why it is filed separately: it is true on main today with no [:> ] anywhere.

THE SHAPE. front/codec.cljs host-entry routes a prop three ways: the canonical ref slot to check-ref!, a slot the declaration NAMES to intent/lower-declared-prop, and everything else to host-prop-value. host-prop-value passes fn? through by identity. intent/callback (h/fn, HD-024) marks the function and RETURNS THE FUNCTION — so an h/fn at a slot no declaration claims crosses to the foreign library as an ordinary function. It is callable, so nothing crashes.

THE DEFECT. The author wrote h/fn to ASK FOR A CONTRACT, and no position selected one. The concrete trap is the :event contract's convenience:

  [my-host {:on-pick (h/fn [x] [:row/pick x])}]   ;; :on-pick NOT in :callbacks

The library calls it, it returns an intent vector, the library discards the return, and nothing dispatches. Silently. The sibling case is already loud — refuse-undeclared-host-event! fires for a bare intent VECTOR at an event-spelled undeclared slot, on the stated ground that the alternative is the author's intent crossing as inert data. An h/fn returning that same vector is the same defect one level of indirection down, and it is accepted.

WHY THIS IS DERIVABLE AND NOT A NEW POLICY. mint-host! refuses an option it does not know (:rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option, rf2-2rtt6.85) on exactly this reasoning, recorded in decisions.md HD-011's addendum: a policy could be written and never applied, and 'the silent-ignore was its own defect'. An h/fn whose contract is never selected IS a policy written and never applied.

PROPOSED REMEDY (one branch, fail-closed): in host-entry's else arm, refuse a callback? value with a new named error — the host, the position, the declared slot roster, and the recovery 'declare this slot in :callbacks, or hand a plain function'. Cost is one own-property read behind a fn? guard (intent/callback? already is exactly that), on the host path only. The ordinary render path is untouched.

WHY IT NEEDS THE OPERATOR. It CHANGES A SHIPPED ACCEPT into a refusal at a declared door, so it is a behaviour ruling rather than a bug fix, and it is escalated as R1 in design B's 'What needs a ruling' section. The counter-case is an author who writes h/fn from habit at a prop that needs no contract; the answer to that is that h/fn is documented as the ONE callback form, i.e. the form you write when the position should impose a contract.

THE ESCAPE'S STAKE. If [:> ] lands with an empty :callbacks map, EVERY slot at a [:> ] crossing is unclaimed, so this fail-open goes from an edge case at defhost to the default at the escape. Design B recommends the shared branch precisely so the escape does not have to fork host-entry to be safe.

WITNESS IF ACCEPTED: a red row asserting the new :rf.error/id and :where for an h/fn at an undeclared slot; a green control for the same h/fn at a DECLARED :event slot (still wrapped, still dispatching), so the refusal is not a blanket ban on h/fn at a host. A row that asserts only 'throws' is vacuous — assert the id.

title: perf: check_retired_image_keys.py is 37.7s — the one required checker the fast-PR spine cannot afford
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-ejm7m, which measured every required python checker before giving it a local lane in scripts/test-fast-pr.sh.

Thirty-seven of the thirty-eight invocations cost 6.4s BETWEEN THEM. This one costs 37.7s cold / ~42s warm by itself — 95% of docs.yml's whole checker batch, and more than double the fast-PR spine's entire documentation tier (~28s, mkdocs --strict included). It is therefore the ONLY required checker rf2-ejm7m deliberately left without a local lane: folding it in would make every worker touching a single .md file pay a 2.4x docs-tier slowdown. Its --self-test arm (0.08s) DID get a lane.

The cost is real CPU, not I/O and not a Windows pathology — cProfile over a clean checkout, 3,534 files scanned:

    53.1s total (under profiler; 37.7s unprofiled)
    28.0s  re.Pattern.search        9,374,502 calls
    11.9s  _mask_multiline_clj_strings  3,064 calls  (7.1s tottime, per-character)
     8.5s  str.join                 2,589,080 calls
     0.7s  actual file reads

Two obvious wins, neither of which should change a single verdict:

1. TOKEN PRE-FILTER. The gate fires on a fixed, small set of literal tokens
   (:include-ns, :exclude-ns, :replace-standard, :rf.image/requires,
   :rf.gen/requires, :capabilities, :replace). Roughly seven patterns are run
   against every line of 3.5k files. A cheap 'if none of the literal substrings
   is in this line: continue' guard in front of the regex battery should elide
   >95% of those 9.4M searches — most lines contain none of the tokens.

2. _mask_multiline_clj_strings IS PER-CHARACTER. 7.1s of tottime plus 2.6M
   str.join calls for what is a string-literal masking pass. A single regex
   sub, or at minimum joining once per file rather than per segment, removes
   most of it.

ACCEPTANCE: the live scan runs in well under a second on this corpus; the
self-test still passes unchanged; and a mutation planting each retired spelling
(fenced code, live .clj, and each sanctioned counterpart that must stay green)
produces byte-identical findings to the current implementation. Then add

    run "retired image keys" "python scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py --verbose" \
      python "\/scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py" --verbose

to the documentation tier of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, next to its self-test, and
drop the note_skipped line beside it. check_fast_pr_gap.py will stop naming it
by construction — no list to edit anywhere.

NOTE the same profile shape probably applies to its sibling
check_retired_composition_vocab.py (1.0s, same _EXCLUDE_REL_PREFIXES/masking
design). That one is cheap enough to have a lane already, but it would come
along for free.
notes:

retired key is no longer detected anywhere — leaves `--self-test` GREEN. No positive
fixture exercises the token:

      live_include_ns_fenced.md      :include-ns, :capabilities, :replace
      live_replace_and_caps.md       :include-ns, :capabilities, :replace
      live_requires_source.cljc      :rf.gen/requires x2, :rf.image/requires

    tokens any positive fixture covers: :include-ns :rf.image/requires

So :replace-standard AND :exclude-ns can each lose their detection with the guard

ADD to this bead's acceptance: one positive fixture per retired token, so the

title: b7, reads_ladder and spine_ablation share one shadow build id with three :init-fns and never reset its cache — it bit a run
description:
FOUND LIVE by rf2-va5nm's worker (PR #7509), 2026-08-05, while proving the
page-error refusals end to end.

THE FAULT, reproduced on demand. b7_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs and
spine_ablation_run.cjs all build by merging their OWN :init-fn onto the ONE
shadow-cljs build id 'freehand-release':

  spawnSync(node, [runner, 'release', 'freehand-release',
                   '--config-merge', '{:output-dir ... :init-fn <theirs>}'])

so .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release carries a cache entry written by a
DIFFERENT program each time. None of the three clears it.

Run b7_run.cjs and then reads_ladder_run.cjs without clearing that directory
and the ladder's page dies at load with

  [ladder] PAGE PAGEERROR: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')

exiting 1. rm -rf .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release and the identical
command gives '[ladder] done', exit 0. The ladder build reported '11
compiled' on the contaminated run against '105 compiled' on the clean one,
which is the tell.

THE REMEDY ALREADY EXISTS IN THE LANE. p0_run.cjs opens its build() with

  if (resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BUILD)) { ... }

and lane_cache.cjs carries the measured fault and the rejected alternatives
(rf2-2rtt6.20) — 'this driver merges its own :init-fn onto BUILD, so BUILD's
cache entry was written by a different program'. The three drivers above
predate it or were never brought onto it. Give each the same call.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NUISANCE. Since rf2-sib23 the symptom is
an exit 1 with a named pageerror, which is the right answer — an operator
investigating a real fault. Before rf2-sib23 the same contamination would
have printed the error and published the table. And a contaminated cache
that DOES reach the sentinel publishes figures measured on a bundle nobody

title: the nine bench drivers still burn a full sentinel budget when the page dies before its sentinel
description:
FROM rf2-sib23 (PR #7505), 2026-08-05. The OTHER half of `sentinel.cjs`, left
deliberately undone and recorded so the absence is not read as an oversight.

rf2-sib23 gave all nine drivers the collector — `watchPage` — but did NOT
convert their sentinel waits from `page.waitForFunction` to `watch.race`. The
fault rf2-sib23 closed is the page that throws and STILL reaches its
sentinel, where the wait returns normally and the exit block is the only place
the signal can be read; converting the waits would have changed nine
behaviours nobody had watched, for a fault the bead was not about.

What remains open is rf2-f5roa's defect, in the nine drivers that never got
its fix: when a page dies BEFORE its sentinel, the failure is instantaneous
and the report of it is fifteen or twenty minutes late, with a log line that
says `Timeout 900000ms exceeded` when what happened was a ReferenceError at
page load. `sentinel.cjs`'s own header states the case; its `race` already
exists and is used by six drivers in the hicasso tree.

THE CONVERSION IS MECHANICAL — same predicate, same timeout, plus the budget
string each driver already writes in its `navigate()` call, e.g.

  await watch.race('window.B6_DONE === true || window.B6_ERROR',
                   { timeoutMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
                     budget: 'the 15-minute wait for `window.B6_DONE`' });

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A SED, and why it wants its own bead: `race` THROWS
where `waitForFunction` used to resolve. Three of the nine (b6_prod,
b6_profile, b10_prod) now have a rejection handler on `drive()` that turns
that into a named exit 1; b7, p0, the ladder and the ablation route it into
their existing catch; b8 folds it into `failed`. Each of those paths wants
watching once rather than assuming.

Sites: b6_prod_run.cjs, b6_profile_run.cjs, b7_run.cjs (two rows), b8_run.cjs,
b10_prod_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs, spine_ablation_run.cjs, p0_run.cjs
(three waits), hicasso_narrow_run.cjs.
notes:
MAYOR RULING ON THE TRADE ITS IMPLEMENTER SURFACED (2026-08-05) — ACCEPTED AS SHIPPED. Recording it so the residue is not later rediscovered as a defect and reverted by someone who does not know it was chosen.

WHAT WAS TRADED. All twelve sentinel waits now race against the recorded-failure array. In the narrow case where a page THROWS AND STILL REACHES ITS SENTINEL, the run now fails at the wait rather than after printing its table, so A LATE THROW'S PARTIAL ROWS ARE NO LONGER PRINTED. The verdict is identical either way; what is lost is diagnostic residue in that one window.

MY BRIEF SAID "no refusal may suppress output" AND THIS IS IN PARTIAL TENSION WITH IT. The implementer said so plainly rather than quietly satisfying the letter, judged it the filer's explicit design (the bead enumerates the rejection path per driver) and consistent with rf2-f5roa's established precedent on drivers that also publish tables, and offered the exact revert lever: drop the four DONE-wait conversions (b6_prod, b7 mount-frame, b10_prod, p0 clock) and keep the eight READY ones, where no table can exist.

I ACCEPT IT AS SHIPPED, for three reasons. The motivating case is a LOAD-TIME ReferenceError where there is no table to lose and 15 to 30 minutes to save, which is the common shape. The verdict does not move, so no published figure and no gate outcome changes. And the lost residue is recoverable by re-running the driver, whereas the wasted budget is not recoverable at all.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: if someone hits a LATE throw whose partial rows would have diagnosed something the re-run cannot reproduce. That is a real possibility on a flaky page, and the revert above is the fix — four conversions, named, no redesign. Do not treat the missing rows as a bug in the refusal; they are a chosen cost.

THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT REGRESS: no measurement, arm, threshold, knob default, exit code or dataset changed, and every rejection lands in a path each driver already had.
close_reason: DONE in PR #7509 (2026-08-05). All TWELVE sentinel waits across the nine now go through sentinel.cjs's `race`: b6_prod (15m), b6_profile (5m), b7 x2 (120s READY + 15m DONE), b8 (5m), b10_prod (20m), reads_ladder (120s), spine_ablation (120s), p0 x3 (the 30m clock wait + two 180s READY waits), hicasso_narrow (5m). Same predicate, same timeout, plus the budget string each already wrote in its navigate() call — the shape this bead enumerated. THE SEAM WITH rf2-f5roa WAS CHECKED AND NOT CROSSED: that bead is CLOSED; it BUILT sentinel.cjs and its race and applied it to hd8_run.cjs and p0_converge_run.cjs after two merged-PR audits found a pageerror costing twenty minutes in each. It never reached these nine. This applies its remedy where it never landed. THE REJECTION PATHS WERE WATCHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, as this bead asked: b6_prod / b6_profile / b10_prod route into drive()'s existing named rejection handler (verified by reading each: `console.error('[bXX] FAILED: ...'); process.exit(1)`); b7, p0, the ladder and the ablation into their existing catch; b8 into `failed`; hicasso_narrow into main()'s catch. Every one is that driver's EXISTING 1 — NO NEW EXIT CODE anywhere, and the ladder's enumerated [3,4,2,5], b7's 2, b8's 2/3 and hicasso_narrow's 2/3/4 are untouched (heap_control_exit_path.test.cjs passes UNMODIFIED). IT CANNOT SHORTEN A RUN THAT WOULD HAVE PASSED, which was the bead's one hard constraint: `race` rejects only on a failure watchPage recorded, and since rf2-sib23 every one of the nine already refuses at its exit on exactly that array — so any run reported early was already going to be non-zero. What changes is WHEN, and that the line names the cause instead of naming the clock. WATCHED FIRING LIVE, unplanned: reads_ladder_run.cjs hit a real pageerror during this work (a contaminated shared shadow cache — filed as rf2-t4j7c) and printed `[ladder] THE PAGE DIED BEFORE IT FINISHED ... This is reported now rather than after the 120s wait for window.LADDER_READY (uix), which had not yet run out and would have said only that time passed (rf2-f5roa)`, exit 1. The same command on a cleared cache gave `[ladder] done`, exit 0. Also exercised end to end: b7 --only mount-frame (0 and 1), p0 --only heap (0 and 1), spine_ablation (passed the raced ABL_READY wait normally and refused with its own existing 4). The verdict is identical either way (that driver's 1, naming the page error); what is lost is diagnostic residue in the narrow window between "some rows measured" and "sentinel set". The motivating case in both beads is a ReferenceError at page load, where there is no residue to lose and up to thirty minutes to save. The exit-block refusals rf2-sib23 installed are NOT removed and are NOT dead — a failure recorded after the sentinel has flipped (during the result evaluates, the measurement loop that follows a READY wait, or teardown) still reaches the exit block and nowhere else, which is how both probe runs above refused. sentinel.cjs's header carries all of this. NEW CLASS PIN in pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs, DERIVED rather than listed: no driver holding the shared collector may wait on a bare page.waitForFunction, plus its inverse (each of the nine must race something, with a NAMED budget) so deleting a wait cannot satisfy it vacuously. It deliberately says nothing about the five hicasso drivers that collect into a local array and wait bare — a different and older shape, not this bead. 48 checks -> 54. No measurement, arm, threshold, knob default or dataset touched.

title: mayor-hygiene.md still reaps on PR state — the exact proxy rf2-k3j2w retired
description:
FOUND by the rf2-k3j2w worker, 2026-08-05, while fixing the script side.

rf2-k3j2w corrected the METHOD docs (docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and
README.md) so they no longer recommend proxies that have failed. But the file
the mayor loop ACTUALLY EXECUTES was out of that worker's fence and still
carries the original defect, verbatim:

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, line 4:
    "For each worker worktree: verify its PR via `gh pr view <#> --json state`
     — only if state==MERGED, prune it."

That is precisely the first of the six failed proxies. A merged PR is the
worker's last REPORTED act, not its last act; it may still be running gates.
Six times in one session reaping on this and its successors destroyed a live
worker's gate run, twice producing a red that named real, present files as
missing and was mistaken for a genuine regression.

WHAT THE COMMAND BODY SHOULD SAY INSTEAD (the ruling already recorded on
rf2-k3j2w and now in docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md):

  Do not reap a worktree until its owning agent has delivered a completion
  report. Not on merge, not on cleanliness, not on quiet. The two signals that
  have never been wrong are reads rather than inferences — the agent's own
  completion report, and SendMessage's response shape ("queued for delivery"
  means alive; "had no active task, resumed from transcript" means idle).
  The cost of waiting is a stale directory; the cost of being wrong is a
  destroyed gate run and a false red.

  And: ONE WORKER IS NOT ONE WORKTREE. A worker may create a second worktree
  for its gate run. An unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until its agent
  reports — do not reap it as an unowned stray.

SECOND, SMALLER ITEM IN THE SAME FILE. mayor-hygiene.md documents how to read
remove-worker-worktree's output (DISARMED=, NO_LINKS=, CANARY_BEFORE/AFTER)
but predates the new outcome added by rf2-k3j2w (PR #7511):

  REMOVE_PARTIAL=<path>, exit 3 — the worktree is already GUTTED (git
  deregistered it and deleted its .git, then hit a file lock on the
  directory). Retrying is futile and `git worktree prune` will not clear it;
  only an ordinary directory delete remains. Exit 1 now means the worktree is
  INTACT and the script is still the right tool; exit 3 means it is not.

  A partial removal kills a running gate exactly as a complete one does, so
  REMOVE_PARTIAL must never be read as "nothing happened".

SCOPE: .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, and mayor-merge.md if it also reaps
on merge. Docs-only; no code. Note that a script CANNOT check agent liveness —
this is caller discipline by construction, which is exactly why it has to be
written where the caller reads it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7514 (branch worker/hygienecmd-40d9d). .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md's 'verify its PR via gh pr view --json state - only if state==MERGED, prune it' is replaced with the rf2-k3j2w ruling: reap a worktree only once its owning agent has delivered a completion report; the only reliable signals are the report itself and SendMessage's response shape; one worker is not one worktree. Branch rule left verbatim (merge state IS the right test for a branch) with an explicit sentence naming the branch/worktree conflation as the original error. REMOVE_PARTIAL= / exit 3 added as the fourth removal outcome, with 'exit 1 means intact and this script is still the right tool; exit 3 means it is not'. Frontmatter description carried the same defect and was corrected. Siblings checked: mayor-merge.md has only the (correct) branch rule and never mentions worktrees; mayor-dispatch.md mentions worktrees for creation and load-counting only; mayor-posture.md and mayor-cluster.md carry no reaping rule. +11/-4 on one file.

title: rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id, and confirm the always-on elision call
description:
TWO OPERATOR DECISIONS THE rf2-2rtt6.122 RULING EXPLICITLY RESERVED. The refusal itself is
DELIVERED (PR #7513) and neither decision blocks it — but both are CONTRACT SURFACE, so they are
tracked here rather than left as a worker's silent pick. Both are cheap to change now and
expensive later.

DECISION 1 — THE ERROR ID. Implemented PROVISIONALLY as `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`.

  Rationale for the pick: it follows the frame-resolution family's past-participle shape
  (`no-frame-context`, `bad-frame-provider-arg`, `frame-context-corrupted`,
  `write-after-destroy`) and names the event from the caller's side — the ambient reach was
  refused.

  Rejected candidates, recorded so they are not re-proposed: `:rf.error/no-ambient-frame-here`
  (reads as an ABSENCE, which is precisely the confusion this id exists to prevent — a frame IS
  in scope); `:rf.error/render-phase-frame-refused` (over-specifies — the tier is scoped to a
  dynamic EXTENT, which a substrate need not use only for rendering);
  `:rf.error/ambient-frame-illegal` (adjective; breaks the family's shape).

  COST TO RENAME: 5 files — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (the payload builder,
  the emit fn, the block comment), `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (the catalogue row),
  `implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` (the always-on
  literal), plus the two test suites that assert on the id. All mechanical.

  THE MESSAGE, for the same review: it is COMPOSED, not owned by one side. Core states what
  happened, that it is NOT an absence (so adding another frame boundary will not help), and that
  an explicitly carried frame still carries. The refusing substrate appends the sentence naming
  what to write instead, carried verbatim into `:reason`. Hicasso's names the boundary collector.

DECISION 2 — ALWAYS-ON vs DEV-GATED. Implemented ALWAYS-ON, proven green under
`-Dre-frame.debug=false`.

  The project's rule is that elision follows WHAT THE CHECK PROTECTS. This is a programmer's own
  mistake caught at render time, which by the letter of that rule argues elidable. Three reasons
  outweigh it:

  (a) THE REFUSAL IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC WRAPPED AROUND CORRECT BEHAVIOUR — IT IS THE BEHAVIOUR.
      Dev-gating yields code that throws in development and, in production, silently mutates the
      subscription cache during render, contributes no collector edge, and freezes the boundary.
      That dev/prod divergence is the worst available outcome, and it is the same trade EP-0002
      already refused when it deleted the `:rf/default` floor.
  (b) CONSISTENCY AT THE CALL SITE. `:rf.error/no-frame-context` is always-on and is raised by
      the same primitive (`require-current-frame!`). If one absence survived production elision
      and its sibling did not, that primitive would behave differently in production depending on
      which absence it found.
  (c) DEV-GATING BUYS NOTHING MEASURABLE. The substrate's `binding` is the substrate's own cost,
      and the resolver's one `nil?` test cannot be eliminated while the var is bindable at all —
      a gate would remove the guarantee without removing the work. The dev-only trace emit
      already DCEs; only the production-survivable record ships.

  IF THE ANSWER IS "PERMISSIVE IN PRODUCTION" ANYWAY, the right lever is NOT gating core's tier.
  It is having the SUBSTRATE not establish the extent — one `interop/debug-enabled?` in
  `re-frame.bench.hicasso.front.intent/with-frame` — which keeps core's contract single-valued
  and puts the policy where a substrate can own it per-substrate. That is a 1-line change.

NO CODE CHANGE IS NEEDED IF BOTH PICKS STAND. Close this as confirmed-as-implemented in that
case.

title: Nothing detects drift between docs/the-mayor-method/** and .claude/commands/**
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-40d9d (PR #7514).

rf2-40d9d existed because PR #7511 corrected the METHOD DOCS (docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md + README.md) and .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md -- the file the mayor loop ACTUALLY EXECUTES -- kept the retired rule verbatim for hours. The description of the method and the instruction executing it drifted apart and only the description was maintained.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: that drift was invisible to every gate.
  - scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS are docs, spec, skills, migration (+ tools/*/spec). .claude/ is not scanned, so its markdown links and anchors are unvalidated.
  - mkdocs build --strict does not see .claude/ either.
  - scripts/test-fast-pr.sh passes on any content whatsoever under .claude/commands/.
So a .claude/commands/*.md file can contradict the method docs, or link to a heading that no longer exists, and nothing reds.

This is not a request for a semantic doc-consistency checker -- that is not buildable and would be over-engineering. The narrow, cheap version:
  1. Add .claude to check_doc_slugs.py's roots so at least link targets and anchors in the command files are validated. The command files DO cross-reference docs/the-mayor-method/ (mayor-posture.md names two files by path; mayor-hygiene.md now names bootstrap.md), and a rename would silently break them today.
  2. Consider whether the five mayor-*.md command files should carry an explicit 'normative source: docs/the-mayor-method/<file>' line, so a worker correcting the method doc can grep for its dependants. rf2-k3j2w's worker could not have found mayor-hygiene.md from bootstrap.md by any search.

NEEDS A RULING on (2) before implementing; (1) is mechanical. Docs/scripts only.

Coordinate with rf2-2rtt6.118's (h/frame) implementation (same file family; its guide sentence 'ambient forms are non-contractual in Hicasso bodies' becomes 'ambient forms REFUSE in Hicasso bodies' once this lands — sequence the wording). notes:
WORKER FINDING (2026-08-05 04:58 AUSEST, rf2-2rtt6.122/.119/d03av cluster, PR #7503). THE HAZARD IS REAL AND THE BEAD'S TRACE VERIFIES — but the RECOMMENDED SHAPE (i) IS NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE IN THE BENCH LANE, and that is the finding. No diff was manufactured; .122 stays OPEN for the ruling its own text reserves.

VERIFIED, file:line, on e49702063b: arm1/mount.cljs:42-48 mints the shared adapter-context Provider and :96-97 installs it 'regardless'; core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:306-341 is the reader the UIx/Freehand adapters publish, and its whole body is (or frame/*current-frame* (context-value->current-frame (.-_currentValue frame-context))); core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs route-hook!s that reader onto :adapter/current-frame; frame.cljc:539-583 resolve-current-frame calls it; subs.cljc:1770-1777 and router.cljc:340-347 are the ambient subscribe/dispatch doors. So ambient rf/subscribe in a Hicasso body DOES resolve the Hicasso frame under those adapters. The bead's description is accurate.

WHY (i) CANNOT BE BUILT HERE. (i) says the body render extent 'binds a refusing sentinel over the ambient chain'. THE AMBIENT CHAIN HAS NO REFUSING VALUE TO BIND. Its two tiers answer a frame id or nil, and nothing else: tier 1 (frame/*current-frame*) is consumed by a bare , so ANY non-nil value Hicasso binds there is returned through frame-value->id AS THE FRAME — a Hicasso-side binding can only ever say WHICH frame, never 'no frame is legal in this extent'. Tier 2 is the React context slot, which is the Hicasso frame precisely because Hicasso mounts the Provider — and the Provider is load-bearing (the shell's hook 1 IS useContext(frame-context), plus the error boundary and the presence tray). So a refusal needs a THIRD tier, or per-consumer discrimination: that is option (ii), core surgery, which this bead fences ('no core edits without a follow-up ruling if (ii) proves necessary'). (ii) has proven necessary. THIS IS THE RULING THE BEAD ASKED FOR, NOT A DODGE.

THE ONE IN-LANE ALTERNATIVE, COSTED AND REJECTED: writing React's internal _currentValue slot to the no-provider sentinel around each body call and restoring after. It would work mechanically, but it (a) costs the ORDINARY render path two property writes per body render, (b) reaches into a React internal and races React's own push/pop discipline, (c) is wrong under renderToString (React 19.2 populates _currentValue2 — rf2-2rzx0), and (d) yields the GENERIC core :rf.error/no-frame-context rather than a diagnostic naming the collector's sub as the door. Worse diagnostic, real cost, fragile mechanism.

ONE FAVOURABLE FINDING FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THE FENCE — THE SCOPING ROW IS FREE. The bead worries that a sentinel must not break an adapter island rendering in the same commit. It cannot: React renders a child fiber only AFTER the parent's render function has returned, so a dynamic binding scoped to the body's execution has already unwound before any adapter island, defhost gate, or h/fn :render callback runs. with-frame (front/intent.cljs:268-277) is already that extent and already binds two vars, so a third costs one push/pop per BODY (not per element). The hard part is the core seam, not the scoping.

TWO MORE FACTS FOR THE RULING. (1) The hazard is CLIENT-ONLY: _currentValue is client-renderer only, so under renderToString ambient subscribe already throws. (2) Census is zero occurrences, so nothing in-tree is broken today; this is a trap for future authors, not a live defect.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the guide sentence. rf2-2rtt6.118 (h/frame) is still OPEN and unbuilt, and this bead says to sequence the wording with it. Writing 'ambient forms REFUSE in Hicasso bodies' now would both collide with .118's file and state something that is not yet true.

RECOMMENDATION: keep .122 open at P2 as an ADAPTER/CORE question (which is what the source finding's F3 concluded — 'closing it is an adapter/core question, not a Hicasso one'), and rule on whether the core gains a render-phase refusal tier. Do not re-dispatch it into the bench lane; a bench worker cannot close it.

Declining that is the right call - it buys a refusal by making every render slower and less correct.

ONE FAVOURABLE FINDING FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE FENCE, recorded so it is not re-derived: THE SCOPING ROW IS FREE. React renders a child fiber only after the parent's render function returns, so a body-scoped binding has already unwound before any adapter island runs.

NO DIFF WAS MANUFACTURED and the bead stays OPEN at P2. DO NOT RE-DISPATCH IT INTO THE BENCH LANE - the same worker would reach the same wall. The guide sentence was also deliberately not written: rf2-2rtt6.118 is open and this bead says to sequence the wording with it.

THE DECISION IN ONE LINE: does core gain a render-phase refusal tier so a substrate can say "no ambient frame is legal here", or do we accept that ambient use silently works and document it?
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-08-05): REFUSE LOUDLY.

Ambient rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch inside a Hicasso body must not silently work. The decision this bead posed - core gains a render-phase refusal tier, or we accept the silence and document it - is settled in favour of the refusal.

THE FENCE THIS RELEASES. This bead's own analysis established that shape (i), a Hicasso-side fix, IS NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE: the ambient chain reads (or frame/*current-frame* (context-value->current-frame (.-_currentValue frame-context))), so tier 1 is consumed by a bare or and any non-nil value a substrate binds comes back AS THE FRAME. A substrate can say WHICH frame is current; it cannot say NO FRAME IS LEGAL HERE. Tier 2 is the context slot, which holds the Hicasso frame precisely because Hicasso mounts the Provider, and that Provider is load-bearing - the shell's hook 1 IS useContext(frame-context). So the refusal needs a THIRD TIER or per-consumer discrimination, which is option (ii), CORE SURGERY, which the bead fenced behind this ruling. The condition is now met.

WHAT WAS ALREADY REJECTED AND STAYS REJECTED. Writing React's internal _currentValue around each body call: it charges the ORDINARY RENDER PATH two property writes per body, races React's own push/pop, is wrong under renderToString (which uses _currentValue2), and yields a WORSE diagnostic than none. Do not revisit it.

THE ONE FAVOURABLE FINDING ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so it is not re-derived: THE SCOPING ROW IS FREE. React renders a child fiber only after the parent's render function returns, so a body-scoped binding has already unwound before any adapter island runs. The fence does not have to track nesting.

WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT SETTLE, and the implementer must not decide silently: the ERROR ID and its message, whether the refusal is always-on or dev-gated, and whether any other substrate wants the same tier. Bring those back rather than picking them - the first two are contract surface.

SEQUENCING NOTE THAT SURVIVES: the guide sentence stays sequenced with rf2-2rtt6.118 (h/frame, an author-facing frame capture for hand-written async), which is open. Do not write guide prose describing the refusal until that lands, or the two will describe the same seam differently.
DELIVERED — PR #7513. The ruling's refusal tier is built, wired, mutation-proven both directions,
and catalogued.

THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT IS A TIER AND NOT A RESHAPE. `frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` +
`frame/call-with-ambient-frame-refused` let a substrate establish a refusing extent.
`resolve-current-frame` — the ONE funnel every adapter already routes through — gates the
React-context tier on a single `nil?` test; when nothing has refused, the expression evaluated is
the pre-existing one verbatim. `require-current-frame!` discriminates the two absences and raises
`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`. Hicasso binds the var as a THIRD var inside the `binding`
`front.intent/with-frame` already performed, so the fence costs the arm no extra stack frame and
covers all three render extents (body, error-boundary fallback lowering, presence tray).

No reader changed, no adapter publishes anything new, the `:adapter/current-frame` hook is
untouched, and `arm1/runtime.cljs` is not in the diff at all. Putting the check in each adapter's
reader instead would have reproduced the very defect this closes.

THE REFUSAL WITHDRAWS THE AMBIENT FIND, NEVER THE CARRYING. `{:frame <id>}` never consults the
resolver; `with-frame` still answers through tier 1 inside a refused extent (under refusal the
resolver collapses to exactly the `:clj` branch). Refusing a carried stamp would make the two
spellings of "I carried a frame" disagree — a worse bug than the silence being replaced.

COST: one module-level var read + one `nil?` per AMBIENT RESOLUTION. Not per render, not per
element, not per carried read. That is the floor rather than a compromise — a refusal must turn a
SUCCESSFUL tier-2 resolution into a failure, so a condition must be evaluated on the success path.
Reachability proof: a grep for the two new names over implementation/, tools/, examples/,
testbeds/ returns six files — frame.cljc, three test files, and the Hicasso bench lane. Nothing
under adapters/, ui/ or ssr/ can bind it.

MUTATION LEDGER (each applied, run, reverted): (A) delete the two-absences discrimination -> 6
failures, exactly the refusal rows, the 10 pre-existing resolver rows green. (B) make the refusal
withdraw the carried tier too -> exactly `a-carried-stamp-still-carries-inside-a-refused-extent`
red. (C) Hicasso stops establishing the extent -> 12 failures + 2 errors, exactly the 4 refusal
deftests, with the control row and EVERY legitimate-position row still green.

THE REFUSAL ROWS ARE FALSIFIABLE, WHICH IS THE ONLY INTERESTING THING ABOUT TESTING A REFUSAL. The
node suite PUBLISHES THE FRAME ON THE SHARED CONTEXT SLOT ITSELF — the tier-2 publication React
performs under a `frame-provider`, and exactly the configuration in which the hazard used to

through `rt/render-body` rather than a React root so the exception reaches `cljs.test` instead of
`reportError`.

LEGITIMATE POSITIONS, EACH ON ITS OWN ROW: the same ambient read outside the body with tier 2 live
· an ADAPTER ISLAND (a foreign React component rendered from a Hicasso body through the interop
door, under a real `createRoot`, reading ambiently and following the frame when it moves —
`arm1/ambient_refusal_dom_cljs_test`) · `with-frame` inside a body · `{:frame <id>}` inside a body

handler dispatched from a body intent · a genuinely frameless op (still `no-frame-context`) · the
whole tier ordering.

and `arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test` are green including their pinned sha256 markup rows. The one
