title: four of the nine page-error refusals have never been watched firing — b7, reads_ladder, spine_ablation, p0
description:
FROM rf2-sib23 (PR #7505), 2026-08-05. Filed BY the worker that wired all nine,
naming the half it could not prove rather than reporting nine green wirings.

WHAT IS PROVEN, and how. All nine now route `pageerror` through
`sentinel.cjs`'s `watchPage` and read `watch.failures` at their exit. Five of
the nine were watched refusing on a page that had ACTUALLY thrown, against a
real headless Chromium (Playwright 1.59.1, react-dom 19.2.0):

  * b6_profile_run.cjs — END TO END, in the driver's own process, both
    directions. `--no-build` plus a hand-written stub in `out/b6-profile`
    that sets `B6_READY`, completes its run, and throws from a detached task
    AFTER the sentinel is already set. Clean stub -> exit 0. The same stub
    with one line added (the throw) -> exit 1, naming the error.
  * b6_prod, b10_prod, b8, hicasso_narrow — at the DECISION, live: a real
    Chromium page throwing inside rAF, inside setTimeout and via an unhandled
    rejection, the real `watchPage` recording all three while the completion
    sentinel STILL flipped, and each driver's real exported `verdict` fed
    exactly that array. All five returned 1; all five returned 0 on the
    clean page.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, which is this bead. b7_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs,
spine_ablation_run.cjs and p0_run.cjs have no pure exported decision — their
exit is an enumerated inline block — so their refusal cannot be driven from a
unit test, and it cannot be driven end-to-end either:

  * none of the four has a `--no-build` knob, so the driver always spends an
    `:advanced` release build before it will serve anything; and
  * their page APIs are far too large to stub faithfully (b7's `window.B7H`
    reader surface; the ladder's and the ablation's `window.LADDER` /
    `window.ABL` plans and rounds; p0's four rows, one page per clock round).
    A wrong stub is not a cheaper proof, it is a fiction that can pass or
    fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the gate.

WHAT COVERS THEM TODAY, so this is a gap and not a hole: the collector is the
same shared `watchPage` proven live above; the mapping
`PAGE_WATCHES.flatMap((w) => w.failures).map(...)` is character-identical in
all four; and `pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs` pins, per file, that the mapping
is read and that its refusal precedes the line announcing a clean run. What is
missing is a run in which one of those four processes actually returns
non-zero.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the choice is a judgement rf2-sib23 declined to make
on its own:

  (a) Give each of the four a pure exported `verdict`, the shape rf2-y7mw7 and
      rf2-x6g04 established. This is the fleet's answer to exactly this
      problem and it makes the refusal checkable in CI forever. It is also a
      real refactor of four long enumerated exit blocks, and rf2-jvheq's mayor
      correction warns against reading this class as an invitation to
      refactor the fleet.

  (b) Run each of the four for real, once, on a page made to throw — which
      needs an `:advanced` build and a way to inject the throw that none of
      them has today.

DO NOT close this by adding `--no-build` to the four as a shortcut. b6_prod
and b10_prod publish production evidence, and a knob that serves a stale
bundle beside a published figure is a new fail-open in the same family.
notes:
ROSTER CORRECTED IN PR #7509 (2026-08-05): THREE OF THE FOUR ARE NOW WATCHED
REFUSING, END TO END, IN THE DRIVER'S OWN PROCESS. THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR
spine_ablation_run.cjs ALONE.

WHAT WAS WRONG IN THE PREMISE, and it is the half that moved. This bead read
the four as unreachable for two reasons at once — no pure exported verdict AND
no way to make the page throw. The first is true. The second is not true of
all four: b7_run.cjs has published `B7_INIT_FN` (documented as the seam an
ablation ladder rides) and p0_run.cjs has `P0_INIT_FN`, already recorded in its
own provenance as `out.initFn`. Pointing an EXISTING seam at a namespace that
`:require`s the REAL app and adds one detached throw reaches the refusal
end to end without touching the driver, without a stub, and without the
`--no-build` knob this bead forbids.

PROVEN, both directions, against Playwright 1.59.1 / react-dom 19.2.0 /
HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15, `:advanced` with goog.DEBUG false:

  b7_run.cjs --only mount-frame
    published entry                    -> `[b7] ok`, EXIT 0
    B7_INIT_FN=<probe>                 -> `[b7] PAGE PAGEERROR: ...` then
                                          `[b7] FAILED: the page threw and kept
                                          going`, EXIT 1. Both W1/W2 records
                                          printed BEFORE the refusal.
  p0_run.cjs --only heap
    published entry                    -> `[p0] done`, EXIT 0
    P0_INIT_FN=<probe>                 -> `[p0] PAGE PAGEERROR: ...` then
                                          `[p0] FAILED: the page threw and kept
                                          going — pageerror: ...`, EXIT 1. The
                                          heap table printed before the refusal.

  reads_ladder_run.cjs                 -> PROVEN WITHOUT A PROBE, and it is the
                                          better evidence. A real run refused a
                                          REAL pageerror — `Cannot read
                                          properties of undefined (reading 'd')`
                                          — and exited 1. Cause: b7, the ladder
                                          and the ablation all merge a different
                                          `:init-fn` onto the ONE
                                          `freehand-release` build id and none
                                          resets its cache the way p0_run.cjs
                                          does, so the ladder was served a
                                          bundle b7's earlier run had cached.
                                          Filed as rf2-t4j7c. A cleared cache
                                          and the identical command gave
                                          `[ladder] done`, EXIT 0. So the
                                          refusal fired on exactly the
                                          environmental fault sentinel.cjs names
                                          as the common one. Reproduces on
                                          demand: run b7_run.cjs, then the
                                          ladder, without clearing
                                          .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release.

WHAT REMAINS, and why it was not padded. spine_ablation_run.cjs alone has no
`:init-fn` override — it is a bare `const`. Adding one purely so a test could
reach it would be a knob that lets a published figure be measured on an entry
nobody built on purpose, which is a cousin of the family this bead forbids; and
stubbing `window.ABL` (the plan, the rounds, the read-back) is the fiction this
bead already rejected. It WAS run under the PR's diff (ABL_SUBSTRATES=uix): it
passed the raced ABL_READY wait normally, ran all four rounds and both snapshot
rounds, wrote both artefacts, and refused with its EXISTING enumerated exit 4 on
its fidelity control — evidence that no exit code shifted, but not a page-error
refusal. The two honest routes in the description are unchanged for it.

THE FIXTURES, so the next reader can watch it again rather than re-derive it:
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_pageerror_probe.cljs
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_pageerror_probe.cljs
Each is the REAL app plus one `js/setTimeout` throw — rf2-sib23's exact fault
shape, a task the app has already returned from, invisible to its
`(catch :default ...)`, setting no `window.*_ERROR`. Each carries the two-command
reproduction in its docstring. pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs pins that each
requires and CALLS the published entry (not a stub), that the throw is detached,
and that NOTHING SHIPS THEM — no driver default, no build id in shadow-cljs.edn.

rf2-sib23's false green was the thing to avoid and was avoided: the exit code
alone was never the proof. `watchPage`'s own `PAGE PAGEERROR` line is in every
throwing log, so the throw demonstrably happened before the page went away.

No measurement, arm, threshold, knob default, exit code or dataset changed.
MAYOR NOTE (2026-08-05): THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, AND THAT IS THE DELIVERY.

This bead read the four drivers as unreachable for TWO reasons at once - no pure exported verdict AND no way to make the page throw. THE FIRST IS TRUE. THE SECOND IS FALSE FOR TWO OF THEM: b7_run.cjs already publishes B7_INIT_FN, documented as the seam an ablation ladder rides, and p0_run.cjs already publishes P0_INIT_FN, recorded in its own provenance as out.initFn. Pointing an EXISTING seam at a namespace that requires the real app and adds one detached setTimeout throw reaches the refusal end to end - no driver change, no stub, no --no-build.

So the answer was neither of the bead's two options. It was that two of the four ALREADY HAD THE INJECTION.

THREE PROVEN, ONE NOT. b7 and p0 proven end to end in both directions through their own seams. reads_ladder proven NOT BY ARRANGEMENT - a clean run refused a REAL pageerror it had no business seeing, which is how the shared-build-cache defect was found (now rf2-t4j7c).

spine_ablation_run.cjs REMAINS UNPROVEN AND THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR IT ALONE. Its :init-fn is a bare const, and the implementer declined to add an override on the ground that a knob letting a published figure be measured on an entry nobody built on purpose is worse than the gap it closes. I agree. It was nonetheless RUN under the diff and refused correctly with its existing exit 4.

ALSO DECLINED, correctly: lifting the four exit blocks to pure verdicts. heap_control_exit_path.test.cjs fingerprints b7's and reads_ladder's drive() source hard, so lifting would have meant rewriting four of its assertions to prove something a live run proves better. That file is unmodified and passes.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON THE RULING ITS OWN IMPLEMENTER MADE, WHICH I ACCEPTED AT THE TIME (mayor, 2026-08-05). Closing rather than leaving it open, because leaving it open asks a future worker to do the thing we decided not to do.

WHAT REMAINED: spine_ablation_run.cjs alone. Three of the four drivers this bead named were proven - b7 and p0 end to end through seams they ALREADY PUBLISHED (B7_INIT_FN and P0_INIT_FN), and reads_ladder not by arrangement but by refusing a real pageerror it had no business seeing, which is how the shared-build-cache defect rf2-t4j7c was found.

WHY THE FOURTH IS NOT WORTH CLOSING: spine_ablation_run.cjs's :init-fn is a bare const. Reaching its refusal needs an override added for no reason except that a test wants one - and THAT KNOB WOULD LET A PUBLISHED FIGURE BE MEASURED ON AN ENTRY NOBODY BUILT ON PURPOSE. Its implementer declined on that ground and I agree: the knob is a worse hazard than the coverage gap it closes, on a driver whose entire job is to be trustworthy about what it measured.

WHAT WE HAVE INSTEAD, and it is not nothing: the driver WAS run under the diff. It passed the raced ABL_READY wait, ran all rounds, wrote both artefacts, and refused with its existing exit 4. So the wiring is exercised; what is missing is only a watched firing of the pageerror arm specifically.

IF THIS EVER MATTERS AGAIN, the honest reopening condition is that spine_ablation gains an :init-fn seam FOR A REAL REASON of its own - not for a test. At that point the proof is free and someone should take it. Do not add the seam to close this bead.

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-05; design + adversarial review complete; attack 1 FATAL / 3 MAJOR / 5 MINOR — the FATAL corrected the design's premise and STRENGTHENED its verdict). VERDICT: BUILD (a) — (h/frame) — from the corrected premise. MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-05.hframe-design.md + hframe-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE CORRECTED PREMISE (the attack's F1, verified file:line): the platform keystone rf/capture-frame (core.cljc:1452; spec/002:1421 "the ONE public carry primitive") does NOT throw in Hicasso bodies today — it ACCIDENTALLY WORKS on the dominant configurations: Hicasso mounts the shared adapter-context Provider regardless (arm1/mount.cljs:46,:96-97), and make-react-adapter routes :adapter/current-frame to a raw context _currentValue read (spine.cljs:3233-3235; context.cljs:337-339), published by the UIx and Freehand adapters. ONE SPELLING, SIX BEHAVIOURS: works-correct (UIx/Freehand/plain-atom+ui browser), throws (ratom family, test-react, none), THROWS ON SSR (_currentValue is client-renderer-only, context.cljs:330-335), and sentinel-throw or SILENT WRONG-FRAME inside .74 render callbacks (the ambient chain answers the INVOKING render's context; the arming gate rebinds intent/*frame* to the owner — intent.cljs:424-425,:457). The door is not missing; it is accidental, config-dependent, server-broken, and wrong-frame-capable. A documented nondeterministic keystone is a worse artefact than the ten-line fn that removes the nondeterminism.

THE RULED SHAPE:
1. (h/frame) — returns the current frame id (keyword), readable in a Hicasso body and inside .74-gated render callbacks (it reads the intent/*frame* binding the runtime + arming gate maintain — IMMUNE to tree position, adapter, renderer, and timing, unlike the ambient chain). NOT a tracked read: frame identity is render-constant; no scratch append, no hook spent, the ledger and the <=2-hook shell untouched. OUTSIDE any render extent: loud :rf.error/hicasso-frame-outside-render (the .74 temporal idiom).
2. The carry spelling is COMPOSITION with the platform keystone: (rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) — Hicasso adds the deterministic frame READ; core keeps the one carry primitive. The two-step spelling vs the adapters' one-step is the taught asymmetry, and the guide says why in one sentence: ambient lookup is what breaks under Hicasso's stricter body discipline.
3. rf2-2rtt6.125 landed the Performance `:render` wiring (PR #7524): `defview` boundaries now emit one `rf:render:<view-id>` User-Timing measure per render under `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true}`, and the id is the head's `displayName` (`"<ns>/<sym>"`).

That bead's last acceptance bullet asks for **one honest sentence** in the draft guide saying so. It is **not** in PR #7524 and must not be added blind, for a mechanical reason:

- `docs/design/hicasso/**` was fenced during that work — two workers were in flight **renaming `draft-guide/11-performance.md` → `draft-guide/11-below-hiccup.md`** (`worker/hframe-841vn`, `worker/fallback-nv07k`, plus the `docs/hicasso-performance-rename` branch). Writing the sentence into `11-performance.md` would have written it into a file that is being deleted.

## Do this after those PRs merge

1. Confirm the rename has landed on `main`; edit whichever file now carries the Performance chapter.
2. Replace the current framing — which correctly told authors to reach for React DevTools + Xray because per-view `rf:render:*` did not exist — with the true one: **event / sub / fx / render are all live for a Hicasso app** under the perf goog-define; ids are `rf:render:<ns>/<view>`, the same string React DevTools shows.

4. Worth one line: a memo bail-out emits no measure, and a boundary React invoked twice under StrictMode emits twice — both correct, and both the kind of thing an author reading a measure count will otherwise file as a bug.

Reference: Spec 009 §What gets bracketed (the substrate-general `:render` rule and the three consequences) and §Naming convention (the id rule), both updated in PR #7524.

title: hicasso/core: an enclosing with-frame makes the ambient carry answer the WRONG frame inside a refusing render extent
description:
FOUND by rf2-841vn while grounding the SSR witnesses; behaviour is PINNED
(arm1/hframe_cljs_test/a-carried-outer-scope-makes-the-ambient-carry-answer-the-wrong-frame)
but NOT endorsed. This is a design question, not a clear-cut fix.

rf2-2rtt6.122's refusal withdraws the AMBIENT (React-context) tier only —
'the refusal deletes the FINDING, never the carrying'. So a tier-1 stamp
still answers inside a Hicasso body:

    (rf/with-frame :b
      (render a boundary whose frame is :a
        (rf/capture-frame)))      ;; => captures :b, silently

Core is behaving exactly as EP-0002 specifies: :b WAS carried. But the
boundary is rendering under :a, and everything else in that body targets
:a — the collector's reads, the lowered intents, the presence tray. One
body, two frames, selected by which spelling the author reached for, with
no diagnostic. That is the 'silently wrong frame' class rf2-2rtt6.122 was
meant to close, surviving in one configuration.

Reachable in practice wherever a host renders a Hicasso tree inside a
with-frame: a synchronous flushSync mount under a scope, an SSR host that
wraps renderToString, a test fixture (test-support's :ambient-frame
default root-binds *current-frame* to :rf/default, which is exactly how
this was found — every SSR witness in ssr/entry_cljs_test runs with that
stamp live).

THE QUESTION, and it is genuinely open:
(a) leave it — the carried invariant is the spec, and a carried stamp
    winning is the whole point of EP-0002;
(b) refuse a MISMATCHED carried stamp inside a substrate render extent —
    i.e. the refusal detail carries the extent's own frame, and
    require-current-frame! raises when tier 1 answers something else.
    Costs a comparison on a path that already failed, and makes
    'a body has ONE frame' true by construction;
(c) diagnose only — a dev-time warning naming both frames.

(b) collides with a-carried-with-frame-still-carries-inside-a-body, which
pins that an explicit with-frame answers inside a body — but that witness
carries the SAME frame the boundary renders under, so (b) would leave it
green. Worth checking rather than assuming.

The composed spelling (rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) is immune under every
option, so rf2-841vn does not block on this.

Related: rf2-hnrww (the refusal's advice text), rf2-k0rbk (the
provisional :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused spelling).

CORRECTED 2026-08-05: A BARE LOCAL mkdocs build --strict DOES COVER spec/** IN THIS REPO. My earlier claim was wrong and I told several workers to work around a problem that does not exist.

WHAT I HAD RECORDED: that mkdocs reads docs/ and not spec/, that docs.yml's cp -r spec docs/spec is what makes the coverage real, and therefore that a bare local run exits 0 over a tree not containing the edited file.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, verified by the rf2-2rtt6.125 worker and confirmed by reading mkdocs_hooks.py: ON_PRE_BUILD MIRRORS spec/ INTO docs/spec/ ITSELF, idempotently, on every build - it rmtree's and copytree's. So a bare local mkdocs build --strict DOES see a spec edit. docs.yml's cp -r is belt-and-braces, not the mechanism.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG: the rf2-whfte worker reported staging spec/ manually before building and said a bare run "would not have seen my file at all". That was a reasonable inference from the workflow's cp -r line, and I promoted it to a rule without checking the hook. It then went into four briefs.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/hicasso/** - exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site, so it exits 0 having verified nothing there. That exclusion is real and still worth stating in every brief touching the design records or the draft guide.

THE GENERAL FORM, which is the actual lesson: a gate is a claim about WHAT IT READS, and the way to establish that is to read the gate's own configuration - not to infer it from a workflow step that happens to sit near it. I inferred, and the inference survived four briefs because nobody had reason to check it.

title: hicasso: wire defview into Spec 009 Performance :render (and view-render traces)
description:
# Product gap: Hicasso defview does not own Spec 009 Performance :render (or the matching view-render traces)

## Problem

re-frame2's Performance instrumentation (Spec 009 §Performance instrumentation, channel #5) brackets four hot paths when `re-frame.performance/enabled?` is true:

| Bucket | Entry name | Owner today |
|---|---|---|
| `:event` | `rf:event:<id>` | core router — **substrate-independent** |
| `:sub` | `rf:sub:<id>` | core subs — **substrate-independent** |
| `:fx` | `rf:fx:<id>` | core fx — **substrate-independent** |
| `:render` | `rf:render:<id>` | **view substrate** — must call `performance/mark-and-measure` around the user body |

A Hicasso app therefore already gets **event / sub / fx** User-Timing measures under the opt-in flag. It does **not** get a first-class **per-view `rf:render:*`** trail.

Reference shapes that *do* own `:render`:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs` — `build-frame-aware-view` wraps the user render-fn in `(performance/mark-and-measure :render id …)` and emits the view-render / view-rendered traces Xray's Views panel consumes.
- Freehand — `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs` (and `react.cljs`) brackets the same `:render` bucket.

The experimental Hicasso arm under `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/` (`arm1/runtime.cljs` mint path, `front/*`) has **no** `mark-and-measure` / `rf:render` call sites. `defview` is therefore **not a peer** of `reg-view` / Freehand for production-friendly render timing or for the full Xray Views timing story.

This is a **product-parity gap**, not a programme bar row. The Performance guide page (draft-guide/11-performance.md) correctly tells authors to use React DevTools + Xray for islands; it must not claim Hicasso ships `rf:render:*` until this lands.

## Goal

Make Hicasso-minted views **first-class consumers** of Spec 009's Performance `:render` channel (and, in the same seam, the view-render **trace** pair that Xray expects), with the same contract shape as `reg-view*` / Freehand:

1. **Performance** — when `re-frame.performance/enabled?` is true, each boundary body run emits one `rf:render:<view-id>` measure (options-bag measure, clear-after-emit unless `retain-entries?`), including on throw (try/finally). When the flag is false under `:advanced`, the bracket **DCEs** to a bare body call — zero prod cost.
2. **Trace (dev)** — emit the same ordered pair the adapter path uses: render-start then post-render (with elapsed / deref-set / mount flag as the existing Spec 009 view ops require), gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` like core. Do not invent a second op vocabulary.
3. **Id identity** — `<view-id>` must be stable and filterable (`rf:render:…`); align with how `defview` / mint-view already names heads (keyword or registrar id — pin one rule and witness it).
4. **Boundaries only** — plain inlined helpers are **not** separately bracketed (they are not React components and not reg-view peers). Document that.
5. **SSR / abandoned render** — brackets must not leave durable registration or wrong-frame ambient pollution; match Freehand/core discipline for server and StrictMode double-invoke (two measures in dev is correct React behaviour, not a bug).

## Non-goals

- Changing the Performance API surface, goog-define names, or naming convention (`rf:<bucket>:<id>`).
- Instrumenting the Hiccup **walk** as its own User-Timing bucket (interpretation cost is not this bead; read shape remains the primary author-facing lever).
- Replacing React DevTools Profiler or inventing Hicasso-private APM.
- Claiming the programme mount/bulk **bar** is closed by this work — this is observability parity, not a clock row.

## Acceptance

- With `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true re-frame.performance/retain-entries? true}`, a Hicasso page of N distinct `defview` heads produces `rf:render:<view-id>` measures that a `PerformanceObserver` / `getEntriesByType('measure')` can filter by the `rf:render:` prefix; ids match the pinned naming rule.
- With both performance flags **false** and a production-shaped build, no User-Timing calls remain on the defview path (DCE / no-op parity with core tests).
- Dev build: Xray-consumable view-render traces fire for Hicasso boundaries with the same op types and required fields as the reg-view path (or an explicit, witnessed subset documented if any field is substrate-impossible — prefer full parity).
- Witnesses: unit/DOM tests in the Hicasso bench arm (or product tree when graduated) that assert measure names and trace ops; no dependence on internal clock harnesses for acceptance.
- Guide: one honest sentence on draft-guide Performance (and/or Getting started feature map) that Hicasso **owns** `rf:render:*` once this lands — update tense in the same PR or a paired docs child, no overclaim before merge.

## Design notes (implementation sketch — not a free design pass)

- Prefer the **same macro** `performance/mark-and-measure` used by core/Freehand; do not reimplement User Timing.
- Place the bracket at the **single chokepoint** that runs every boundary body (mint-view / render-body), not at every codec site.
- Trace emit helpers: reuse or thin-wrap core's view emit functions if packaging allows (`implementation/` may not `:require` tools; core view emit is fine). If the arm cannot depend on `re-frame.views` helpers, copy the **contract** (op types + field set) not a divergent dialect.
- Confirm interaction with HD-028 memo bail-out: skipped bodies must **not** emit a render measure (bail-out means no body run — same as React not calling the FC).

## Sequencing

- Parent: **rf2-2rtt6** (Hicasso programme).
- Natural follow-on after experimental arm mint path is stable; can land in the bench arm first and carry into `implementation/hicasso/` at graduation.
- Does **not** block controlled-input / interop correctness beads; **does** block any marketing claim that Hicasso is a full peer for prod render RUM.

## Context

Surfaced 2026-08-05 in guide/product Q&A: authors asked whether Hicasso integrates with the Performance API. Answer: event/sub/fx yes; per-view `:render` no — this bead closes that gap.

title: DESIGN: the revision prop on controlled elements — spec via design+adversarial pass around the fixed reset law; mayor implements
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). The revision prop on controlled elements — guide 04-controlled-inputs.md:159's not-settled row: "Reset law fixed; the attribute name is still open."

STEP ZERO OF THE DESIGN PASS: find the fixed reset law. Grep decisions.md / authoring.md / the studio record for the revision/reset ruling and quote it verbatim in the design doc — the pass designs AROUND a ruled law, it does not re-derive one. If the law turns out to be less fixed than 04 claims, STOP and report the gap (that is a finding, not a licence to invent).

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. SEMANTICS TO CONFIRM AGAINST THE LAW: a revision value change resets the field to the model (uncommitted draft discarded) WITHOUT remount. What exactly survives — focus? caret (and to where — start/end/model-length)? selection? The law's own text governs; where it is silent, the design proposes and marks the proposal.
2. SPELLING: the natural candidate under Conventions' reserved namespace is ::h/revision, [unfrozen] like every spelling (the API freeze rides later — the name question in 04's row dissolves into the general freeze rather than needing its own sitting). Confirm no collision in the reserved-key roster.
3. INTERACTIONS, each designed explicitly:
   a. THE IME CARVE-OUT (rf2-digtt, landed): a revision change arriving MID-COMPOSITION — reset immediately (destroying the exchange the carve-out exists to protect) or defer to compositionend like the converge does? The composition-shadow machinery in front/controlled.cljs is the site; the coherent answer likely mirrors the carve-out, but it must be argued, not assumed.
   b. THE CONVERGE PATH: revision-reset vs the in-turn converge ordering; no second flushSync site without naming it (HD-019's addendum audited the existing two).
   c. SSR/HYDRATION: revision is a codec-level prop consumed before emission (never a DOM attribute — verify); server HTML carries the model value; hydration adopts with the defaultValue invariant row extended (the .84 pattern). A revision change during hydration adoption = same deferral question as (a).
   d. HD-028 MEMO: a revision change is a props change — body re-runs; confirm no special-casing needed.
4. REFUSAL EDGES: revision on a non-controlled element (no :value) — silent no-op or loud refusal? (The lane's posture says loud.) Revision value equality semantics (= on any value, the instance-key grammar's lesson about authored data applies).
5. WITNESSES: revision change discards draft + resets to model with focus/caret per the law; unchanged revision never resets; the IME row (mid-composition revision per the designed answer, on the ime_run harness); the hydration row; the refusal row.
6. GUIDE DELTA: 04's not-settled row resolves; the buffered/revision LADDER stays post-v0 (charter) — this bead is the single revision prop only, not the ladder; state the boundary.

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: the IME interaction (the one place a wrong answer destroys user text), the reset-without-remount claim under React 19.2's actual controlled-input behaviour, and scope creep toward the post-v0 ladder.

Implementation is the mayor's, from the appended spec. Fences: front/controlled.cljs + codec prop handling + witnesses + guide 04. No AI attribution.

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; design + adversarial review complete; 0 FATAL / 3 MAJOR / 7 MINOR; verdict BUILD WITH THE NAMED REPAIRS). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.revision-design.md + revision-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE LAW (found, verified, binding): HD-019 via decisions.md:668-670 carrying D016 — resets fire on EXPLICIT CALLER REVISION, never value equality; a revision may change while the value stays equal; a value change under an unchanged revision continues the draft; the caret may move only when a new revision establishes a new baseline. The attack's law challenge FAILED: an agreeing-field no-op is React's effect-idempotence guard, not a value-equality trigger — D016:40-41 protects equal BASELINE values across revisions, which the design honours.

THE RULED SHAPE:
1. Spelling ::h/revision (:re-frame.hicasso/revision), [unfrozen], exact-keyword match like :& — NEVER slot-claimed. FREEZE FLAG: three reset-ish names now exist (element revision, h/boundary :reset-key remount, D016's ladder :reset-key) — the API freeze must face them together.
2. Semantics: a revision change (CLJS =) re-baselines the field to the model WITHOUT remount — focus and node kept, caret to end-of-model on the carrying commit (platform conduct, D016:225-226 licensed). Equal-but-fresh revision values are inert (= semantics; authored-data rule: a good instance key is a good revision value).
3. Mechanism (verified at react-dom 19.2.0:12537-12541, :20865-20874, :1666-1667): React's own per-commit controlled re-assert off fresh codec props — ZERO new machinery, no keyed re-render, NO third flushSync site (in-turn resets ride the keystroke converge; deferred resets ride the compositionend site; out-of-band resets ride ordinary commits). One invariant row pins the input chain; ADD a textarea row (parallel chain at :20978, unpinned in the design).
4. IME: a mid-composition revision DEFERS to the exchange's close — every shadow-release path (compositionend / non-composing change / BLUR — verified a release path at controlled.cljs:529-533 / unmount) converges to the then-current model; immediate writes re-import the measured abort + SSHSH corruption. ADD a blur-mid-composition witness variant.
5. Refusal: :rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled, per-render, on non-controlled elements (check-ref!'s cost shape). Value-carrying checkbox is accepted-inert — say so plainly, do not overstate refusal coverage.
6. SSR/hydration: the codec strip is server-safe (shared renderer); server HTML carries the model value; the defaultValue invariant row extends.
7. SCOPE: the single prop ONLY. No generation fencing, commit/cancel, controller, acknowledgement, opt-outs — the post-v0 ladder consumes this trigger, never extends the prop.

THE THREE MANDATORY REPAIRS (from the attack; each with its witness):
R1 THE :& DOOR (the big one): the brief as designed matched ::h/revision in convert-entry, which walks the MERGED map — {:& {::h/revision r}} would arm a live reset from the hostile-remainder door (merge-caller denies only #{key ref}+owned, codec.cljs:431/465). FIX: read ::h/revision off the AUTHOR'S OWN pre-merge map in native-element (the :key pattern, codec.cljs:1468/1474), skip-or-refuse it in the walk, and add the witness row asserting {:& {::h/revision r}} NEVER resets (refusal or inert — pick refusal, the lane's posture).
R2 THE OVERCLAIM: strike "the reset cannot be lost" — on an accepting field the post-bump composition echo (including the commit's own final input) overwrites the reset's model write and can resurrect discarded text through the draft echo. The witness row for reset-during-composition pins the ACTUAL conduct at the close (field = the model as of the echo, stated honestly), not the overclaim.
R3 MID-ADOPTION: the "lands on the first post-adoption commit on the server's node" claim has no source cite — DEMOTE to witness-gated intent. Its row RUNS FIRST in the hydration suite; pre-committed fallback if React deopts (server-node loss observed): the reset defers past adoption through the same deferral shape as IME, and the row pins that instead. Never ship the claim unpinned.

WITNESSES: the design's ten rows + R1's :& row + R2's honest composition-close row + R3's gated adoption row (first) + the textarea chain row + the blur-mid-composition variant. Bench lane; ime_run.cjs for the composition rows; the hydration rows on the .84 harness.

GUIDE: bead rf2-2rtt6.113 (already filed, deps this bead) teaches it after the implementation PR MERGES; 04's not-settled row resolves; the ladder boundary stated.

FENCES: front/controlled.cljs + front/codec.cljs (the pre-merge read) + witnesses. Coordinate on codec.cljs with the [:>] implementation (.103) and the key-warning (.104) — three beads now touch that file; the mayor sequences. title: hicasso: rf2-2rtt6.122's refusal fires on rf/capture-frame but its advice text does not address a CARRY — and no witness pins it
description:
Found while re-grounding rf2-2rtt6.118's design on the post-rf2-2rtt6.122
tree (PR #7519). Small, real, and in LANDED code.

rf2-2rtt6.122 fused core's refusal tier into intent/with-frame -- the one
binding every Hicasso render extent performs -- so ambient frame
resolution refuses for the whole extent. That is correct and is the
point. But the refusal catches a THIRD consumer the arm's advice text was
not written for.

THE DOOR HAS THREE CONSUMERS, and frame.cljc says so itself: ambient
subscribe, ambient dispatch, and current-frame-id/capture-frame. The
arm's refusal detail (front/intent.cljs, ambient-frame-refusal) is
written for the first two -- it advises reading through the boundary's
collector (`sub`) and dispatching through an intent at a handler
position. An author who trips the refusal via (rf/capture-frame) --
0-arity, in a body -- is doing NEITHER. capture-frame is Spec 002's "the
ONE public carry primitive", and the reason it resolves ambiently is to
capture, not to read or to dispatch. They get a paragraph that never
names their recovery.

The honest recovery today is the 1-arity (rf/capture-frame <frame-id>),
which never consults the resolver -- and, once rf2-841vn lands,
(rf/capture-frame (h/frame)), which is the sentence the advice should
contain.

AND NO WITNESS PINS IT. arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test covers ambient
subscribe, ambient dispatch, a carried with-frame still carrying, an
explicit {:frame ...} opt still resolving, the unwind, the two-absences-
two-errors split, and the untouched collector. capture-frame under
refusal appears in none of them, so the keystone's behaviour inside a
body is currently a consequence rather than a contract.

SCOPE. Arguably two lines of advice text plus one witness row. It is
filed separately rather than folded into rf2-841vn because it is true of
landed code even if h/frame never ships -- though h/frame's landing is
the natural moment to close it, since the ideal advice sentence names
(h/frame).

Note :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused is PROVISIONAL (rf2-k0rbk).
close_reason:
BOTH GAPS CLOSED in PR #7522 (branch worker/hframe-841vn).

GAP 1 -- THE ADVICE TEXT. front/intent.cljs's ambient-frame-refusal :reason
now carries a third sentence for the third door: 'CARRYING a frame out of
the render is a THIRD thing, and its recovery is neither of the above:
(rf/capture-frame) resolves ambiently, so it refuses here, but
(rf/capture-frame <frame-id>) never consults the resolver at all. Write
(rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) ...'. It is a module-level constant built once
at load, so establishing the extent still allocates nothing.

GAP 2 -- THE MISSING WITNESS, which the bead correctly called the larger
half. arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test gains a CARRY section:
 - a-carry-inside-a-body-refuses-exactly-as-a-read-does (the design's W10,
   INVERTED -- the designed row pinned that the 0-arity SUCCEEDS, and
   rf2-2rtt6.122 is exactly the change that made it refuse). Pins
   :operation :capture-frame, :substrate :hicasso,
   :extent 'hicasso/boundary-render, :where 're-frame.core/capture-frame.
 - the-refusal-never-consults-the-adapter-which-is-why-it-is-adapter-independent:
   'refuses under EVERY adapter' cannot be settled by trying adapters, so
   the :adapter/current-frame hook is wrapped with a counter -- ZERO calls
   inside a refused body, with a control proving it IS called one line
   outside.
 - the-refusal-tells-a-carry-what-to-write (the advice text, asserted)
 - the-one-arity-carry-still-carries-inside-a-body
 - the-composed-carry-is-refusal-immune
Each legitimate carry position is proved on its own, carried through to a
dispatch that lands after the extent unwinds -- a refusal that also refused
a valid carry would be worse than the silence it replaced.

THE PROVISIONAL ID DID NOT LEAK (rf2-k0rbk). The rows do not repeat
:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused: a carry's refusal is pinned as 'the SAME
id an ambient read gets', taken live from a sibling row. The literal stays

title: EP-0038: does the programme EP want a dated addendum for K5's removal?
description:
K5 was removed as a kill criterion by operator ruling 2026-08-04 (PR #7457). That PR removed the row from docs/design/hicasso/validation.md, added the dated note there, and superseded the one other OPERATIVE statement of the criterion (charter.md item 4, which restated K5 inline without naming it — invisible to a K5 grep).

LEFT OPEN, deliberately: docs/EP/EP-0038-the-hicasso-view-layer-programme.md:57 says the standard bead pre-registered 'the budgets, kill criteria K1-K7'. That sentence is NOT false — nothing was renumbered, so K1-K7 remains an accurate span of the identifiers, and it describes what wave 0 pre-registered as a historical fact. So PR #7457 left it alone rather than churn it.

THE JUDGMENT CALL for the operator/mayor: withdrawing a PRE-REGISTERED kill criterion is a governance-level change to the programme, and this repo's practice is that operator rulings on Hicasso get recorded as dated EP-0038 addenda (cf. commit cd06df2f2e, 'record the Surface B/HD-002 ergonomics ruling as a dated EP-0038 addendum'). Whether K5's removal earns the same treatment is a call I did not have authority to make from a docs worker brief that scoped me to validation.md/decisions.md/the two bench sources.

If YES: a dated 2026-08-04 addendum to EP-0038 noting the ergonomics kill was withdrawn, no replacement, identifiers unrenumbered. If NO: close this — validation.md's dated note is already the anchor and EP-0038 stays a historical record of what was pre-registered.

Note EP-0038 is a shared/hot-ish doc; sequence it rather than parallel it.
close_reason:
ANSWER: YES. Dated addendum added to EP-0038 in PR #7533.

The house pattern decided it. EP-0009 rule 2 puts operator rulings in Resolved Decisions; rule 3 says anything past a mechanical correction 'is recorded as a dated erratum/addendum beside the affected passage, preserving the original text — freeze meaning, not bytes'. EP-0038 already carries THREE addenda in exactly that shape (2026-07-31 Arm-2 drop; 2026-07-31 Surface B — the cd06df2f2e the bead cites; 2026-08-04 SSR), each opening '### Addendum, <date> — <ruling>' under Resolved Decisions and each naming which earlier text it deliberately leaves standing.

The decisive detail: NONE of those three is one of the two rulings the Resolved Decisions preamble enumerates by name (the donor-gate and P2 fork rulings). So the EP's own practice already reads rule 2 broadly — any operator ruling that changes the programme is recorded here. Withdrawing a criterion this EP pre-registered is squarely that class, and is arguably the strongest case of the four since wave-0's own line is what pre-registered it.

The addendum is deliberately short (heading, the ruling, the rule-2/rule-3 sentence, two bullets, design-record pointers) and it records that EP-0038:57 ('the budgets, kill criteria K1-K7') is LEFT AS WRITTEN — which is this bead's own reasoning: nothing was renumbered, so it stays a true historical statement of what wave 0 pre-registered. The addendum is precisely how the EP holds both facts at once, which is what rule 3 exists for. No other EP-0038 passage states K5 operatively (checked Specification, Open Issues, Graduation, Non-goals).

NO VERBATIM RULING TEXT EXISTS: commit 417fd06c65 (PR #7457), validation.md, charter.md and decisions.md all record the ruling by date only, and bd search finds none. The addendum says so and points at validation.md's dated note as the authoritative statement, rather than inventing a quote — the other three addenda open with a verbatim only because one was on the record.

No edits to validation.md, charter.md or decisions.md (fenced, and each already carries its own dated note).

title: hicasso guide 05: does the value-equality bail-out actually reach a defhost head? mint-host! never calls memoize-boundary!
description:
FOUND while narrowing 02's boundary definition for rf2-2rtt6.102 (PR #7532). NOT decided there -- it is a correctness question about a mechanism, not a wording fix, and it sits outside that bead's scope.

THE CLAIM. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md, section 'Memo and hosted components' (lines ~164-179):

  'Every Hicasso boundary is a React.memo that compares props by value. That
   bail-out reaches a hosted component the same way it reaches a native one'

and, against a sample where chrome-page re-renders because its own sub moved:

  'A write that only moves :hatch/label re-renders .chrome and stops.
   hosted-row never re-enters the foreign component.'

THE TENSION. front/codec.cljs:912 memoize-boundary! is explicit that the wrapper is opt-in AT THE MINT SITE, with the reason spelled out: 'Opt-in at the mint site rather than applied to every marked head, so heads that are not reactive boundaries -- h/boundary's error-boundary class, presence -- keep the semantics they were written with.'

Its only two callers are arm1/runtime.cljs mint-view! (:1880) and mint-frame-prop-view! (:1905). codec/mint-host! (:1090) does NOT call it. So a defhost head carries no Hicasso memo wrapper, and when its parent boundary re-renders, the parent's body mints a fresh element for it.

WHAT NEEDS SETTLING, one of:
 (a) the guide's claim is right for a reason the page does not name -- React's own reconciliation, or the fact that a library's exported component is often already a memo product -- in which case name the mechanism, because as written a reader will believe Hicasso is doing it; or
 (b) the claim needs narrowing to what actually holds (the enclosing BOUNDARY bails out, and a hosted child of a boundary that did not re-render is not re-entered), which is a weaker and different statement than the sample teaches; or
 (c) mint-host! should carry the wrapper, which is a product decision, not a docs one -- note h/boundary and presence were deliberately left out for a stated reason, so hosts may have been too.

Cheap to check: the arm has host DOM suites (arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test) and the inpage ladder already isolates the memo wrapper's cost (inpage_ladder_app.cljs:47 'nomemo'). A witness that re-renders a parent boundary and counts foreign-component invocations settles it in one test.

FENCE NOTE: 05-interop.md has carried concurrent dispatchers; sequence, do not parallelise.

title: mayor: worktree reaping is keyed on PR state, not worker state, and manufactures false reds
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.92 rebase worker, 2026-08-04, and confirmed by the mayor as SELF-INFLICTED.

WHAT HAPPENS. The mayor's hygiene/merge loop reaps a worker worktree once its PR reads MERGED. But a merged PR is the worker's last REPORTED act, not its last act: it may still be running gates. When the tree is removed mid-run the gates do not fail cleanly, they fail LOUDLY AND FALSELY, naming real files:

- the fast-PR spine reported 4 RED namespaces whose stack traces are Module.load reading out/node-test.js from a directory being deleted
- npm run test:cljs died on "Cannot find module 'readline-sync'" -- a package present in the mayor tree throughout
- npm run test:hicasso-compile reported "Missing script" because npm walked up past a deleted implementation/package.json

None of that announces itself as infrastructure. A worker with less discipline would have chased "missing readline-sync" or reported a red that does not exist. Three worktrees were hit in one sweep: rebase-2rtt6-92, spike-2rtt6-87 and ssrnode-2rtt6-86. Nothing was lost because all three PRs had merged, but that was luck, not design.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE ROOT CAUSE IN A SINGLE SESSION, and the first two were already recorded:
1. Reap folded into the merge loop deleted a tree 11 seconds before its spine finished (11 phantom "Cannot find module" failures).
2. A rebase worker was dispatched onto a branch whose original worker was still resolving that same conflict; its .git file was deleted underneath it.
3. This one -- the hygiene sweep, again keyed on PR state rather than worker state.

WHY THE FIRST FIX WAS NOT ENOUGH. After (1) I adopted "reap on the NEXT tick, once quiescent". That is a DELAY, not a CHECK, and a delay does not help a worker whose gates run for fifteen minutes. The tick cadence is roughly eleven minutes; the fast-PR spine alone can exceed that.

THE ACTUAL FIX -- reap on worker state, not PR state or elapsed time:
- Do not reap while any live agent is associated with that bead or branch.
- Cheap proxies when agent state is not visible: mtime on the worktree's out/ or .shadow-cljs/ directories, or a running node/java process whose cwd is inside the tree. A tree touched in the last few minutes is not quiescent.
- When in doubt, LEAVE IT. A stale worktree costs disk. A deleted one costs a false red, a possible spurious "fix", and -- if the worker is mid-rebase -- a hijacked branch.
- Never remove a worktree whose branch has an OPEN PR, regardless of how quiet it looks.

WHAT THE AFFECTED WORKER DID RIGHT, and it is the model: it discarded all three voided exit codes under the killed-gate rule rather than reporting them, and substituted the authoritative evidence -- CI on the exact rebased head, 47 SUCCESS / 36 SKIPPED / 0 failures, whose rollup includes the very per-ns-isolation gate its local run had called red.
notes:
FOURTH INSTANCE, 2026-08-04, WITH THE FIRST FIX ALREADY DEPLOYED — the fix was insufficient and the bead's scope should reflect that.

I replaced 'reap when MERGED' with 'reap when MERGED and idle >= 10 min', reading idleness from the mtime of the worktree's implementation/ directory. It still removed a worktree out from under a running fast-PR spine: the mtime said 34 minutes idle while the rf2-2rtt6.99 worker was mid-run, because a running spine writes to out/, .shadow-cljs/, temp dirs and detached children rather than necessarily touching implementation/ itself.

ALSO: remove-worker-worktree.sh PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED before failing. It disarmed the node_modules link and deregistered the worktree, then hit a Windows file lock on the directory and reported REMOVE_FAILED honestly. The tree was already gutted at that point. A partial reap kills a running gate exactly as a complete one does, so 'the removal failed' is not 'the worker was unaffected'.

SO THE BEAD IS NOT 'key the reap on a better proxy'. Three proxies have now failed: PR state, elapsed time, directory mtime. The remaining honest signals are (a) the owning agent has delivered its completion report, or (b) no process holds a working directory inside the tree. Everything cheaper has been tried and has produced a false red naming real files — four times today, twice in a form mistakable for a genuine regression.
SIXTH REAP-DURING-GATES, AND THE DIRTY-TREE GUARD I ADDED HOURS EARLIER DID NOT CATCH IT (2026-08-05, rf2-vrvv9's worker).

WHAT HAPPENED. I merged PR #7500 on green and the merge loop reaped worker/nskeyword-vrvv9 because the tree was CLEAN. The worker was still running scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Its spine died on FileNotFoundError for source files vanishing underneath it - first re_frame/elision, then ssr-ring payload.clj - twice, because it started a second run. Minutes later I reaped a worktree called vrvv9-gate as an unowned stray; that was ITS SECOND GATE WORKTREE, also in use. Nothing was lost only because every commit was already pushed.

WHY THE GUARD FAILED. I had just added "reap only when the tree is dirty=0", on the reasoning that a dirty tree is in use. THAT IS TRUE BUT NOT THE CONVERSE. A worker that has committed and pushed everything - exactly the discipline every brief demands - presents a CLEAN tree while running a twenty-minute gate. So the better a worker follows the push-as-you-go rule, the more likely my guard is to destroy its gate run.

THE FULL LIST OF PROXIES THAT HAVE NOW FAILED, all of them plausible when adopted: PR state; elapsed time; worktree directory mtime (read 250 minutes stale on a worker that was committing as I looked); worker shape (zero commits + clean + no PR matches both an abandoned tree and one that started a minute ago); and now CLEANLINESS. Five wrong answers to one question.

THE TWO SIGNALS THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN WRONG: the agent's own completion report, and SendMessage's response shape ("queued for delivery" means alive; "had no active task, resumed from transcript" means it was idle). Both are reads rather than inferences, which is the whole point.

THE RULE, and I am done trying to be cleverer than it: DO NOT REAP A WORKTREE UNTIL ITS OWNING AGENT HAS DELIVERED A COMPLETION REPORT. Not on merge, not on cleanliness, not on quiet. The cost of waiting is a stale directory; the cost of being wrong is a worker's gate run destroyed and a false red that names real files as missing - which has now twice been mistakable for a genuine regression.

AND A SECOND-ORDER TRAP THIS EXPOSED: ONE WORKER IS NOT ONE WORKTREE. This worker created a second worktree for its gate run, and I reaped it as an unowned stray because I did not recognise the name. Before removing any worktree I do not recognise, ask whether a LIVE worker might have created it - the honest default is that an unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until its agent reports.
DELIVERED, 2026-08-05 — PR #7511, worker/reapguard-k3j2w. NO seventh proxy was
added; the deliverable is narrow, as briefed.

THE MECHANISM IS NOW REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, not inferred. Hold one open file
handle inside a throwaway worktree and run `git worktree remove --force`:

  exit 255, "failed to delete '<wt>': Invalid argument"
  git worktree list  ->  ALREADY GONE (deregistered)
  <wt>/.git          ->  ALREADY DELETED
  <wt>/**            ->  every other file still present

So git deregisters and deletes .git BEFORE it deletes the files, and the note
above ("remove-worker-worktree.sh PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED before failing") was
right about the shape. Two husks were sitting in the worktree parent while this
ran: procpair (full checkout, no .git, unknown to git) and goto-dczpv (emptied
shell). Both left in place — an unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until
its agent reports.

WHY EVERY SIGNAL POINTED THE WRONG WAY. `git worktree prune` does not clear a
husk (prune drops admin records for directories that VANISHED; here the
opposite happened). `git status --porcelain` inside one FAILS and prints
nothing, which the clean/dirty split read as "tree is CLEAN" and reported as
REMOVE_FAILED "safe to retry once it clears" — and retrying is futile, because
the registered-worktree check refuses the path forever. Verified head-to-head
against main.

THE FIX: REMOVE_PARTIAL=<path> and exit 3. Codes now split on what the caller
should do next — 1 means the worktree is INTACT and the script is still the
right tool, 3 means it is gutted and only a plain directory delete remains.
Reported from both entry points (a removal that fails this way, and a later
call handed a path that is already a husk).

WORSE THAN A BAD MESSAGE, AND THE REASON THIS WAS NOT COSMETIC: a husk was
refused WITH ITS JUNCTION STILL ARMED, while the message recommended `git
worktree prune`. The only remedy left for a husk is `rm -rf` — so the old
output was a loaded gun aimed at the mayor's node_modules. The disarm is now
factored out and runs on the husk path before anything recommends a delete.

TWO PRE-EXISTING WINDOWS DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, both reproduced against main
before being touched:
1. The .ps1 CRASHED instead of classifying. Under $ErrorActionPreference =
   "Stop" a native command writing to stderr raises a terminating
   NativeCommandError, and neither 2>$null nor 2>&1 suppresses it — so `git
   status` in a husk aborted the script, and the same trap sat under `git
   worktree remove`, the one call guaranteed to write to stderr on the path
   that must be classified rather than crashed on.

title: test:perf-bundle is wired to nothing -- Spec 009 names it as the perf-elision CI gate and no workflow runs it
description:
# `npm run test:perf-bundle` — the gate Spec 009 names as its perf-elision enforcement — is wired to NOTHING

FOUND while delivering rf2-2rtt6.125 (Spec 009 `:render` for Hicasso `defview`), looking for the gate that would catch a perf bracket surviving DCE.

## The claim, and the fact

Spec 009 §Production-elision verification (the one inside §Performance instrumentation) says:

> "The bundle-isolation contract is enforced in CI by `npm run test:perf-bundle` (the dual of `npm run test:elision`)."

It is not. `git grep` over `.github/`, `scripts/` and `TESTING.md` finds **zero** invocations of `test:perf-bundle`, `check-perf-bundle`, or the `:examples/counter-perf` build:

- `implementation/package.json` line 58 defines `"test:perf-bundle": "shadow-cljs release examples/counter examples/counter-perf && node scripts/check-perf-bundle.cjs"`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-perf-bundle.cjs` exists (8,736 bytes, executable).
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` declares `:examples/counter-perf` (line ~1629) with `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true}`.
- **No workflow runs any of it.** `.github/workflows/*` has no match. `TESTING.md` has no row. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` mentions "perf-bundle" only in a comment listing gates the spine does NOT run — so `check_fast_pr_gap.py` cannot surface it either, because the gap script derives from the workflows, and the workflows do not contain it.

Its stated dual, `npm run test:elision`, **is** wired (`cljs-elision`: "CLJS production elision (Spec 009, bead rf2-11hn)", green on every PR). The asymmetry is the whole finding.

## Why this matters more than an unwired script usually would

The perf channel's entire safety argument is compile-time: `mark-and-measure` expands to `(if enabled? <bracket> (do body))` and Closure is trusted to fold and DCE it. The dual-bundle grep is what makes that trust checkable, and Spec 009 explains at length why it must be a DUAL:

> "Without the on bundle the off-bundle assertion would be vacuous — a refactor that MOVED the strings out of the gated branch would silently turn the negative grep into a false pass."

So the repo reasoned carefully about how the gate could go fail-open, built the non-vacuous version — and then never ran it. **A gate nobody has watched fire is not evidence.** As of rf2-2rtt6.125 there are now five `:render`/`:event`/`:sub`/`:fx` bracket call sites relying on it, one of them newly added.

## Remedy

1. Add a `cljs-perf-bundle` job to `.github/workflows/test.yml` beside `cljs-elision`, running `cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle`. **HOT-ZONE** (`.github/workflows/*`) — sequence it, do not parallel it with another workflow edit.
2. Add the matching row to `TESTING.md` so the catalogue and the workflow agree.
3. Run it once by hand first and record the result on this bead. If it is RED today, that is the more urgent half of this bead and the fix belongs before the wiring — a newly-wired red gate blocks every open PR.
4. Consider whether `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list` should also flag npm scripts that exist but appear in no workflow; that is what would have caught this class automatically. Separate bead if wanted.

## Not blocked on

rf2-2rtt6.125 (PR #7524). That PR's `:render` bracket uses the identical macro with a compile-time-constant id, and its own witnesses assert the off-path at `:node-test` optimization; but neither it nor any other perf call site has an `:advanced` bundle grep actually running anywhere.
notes:
RUN BY HAND 2026-08-05 (rf2-2rtt6.125's worker, clause 3 of the remedy). THE GATE PASSES TODAY, so wiring it is safe and will not red every open PR:

    cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle
    [:examples/counter]      Build completed. (147 files, 92 compiled, 0 warnings, 28.50s)
    [:examples/counter-perf] Build completed. (147 files, 92 compiled, 0 warnings, 11.55s)
    PASS perf-bundle: off-count=0; on-count=8;
      off=out/examples/counter      (627300 chars)
      on =out/examples/counter-perf (628089 chars)
    exit 0

So this bead is purely 'unwired', not 'red'. Clause 3 is discharged; clauses 1, 2 and (optionally) 4 remain.

SEPARATELY, the same dual-bundle methodology was run by hand against a HICASSO arm (:hicasso-bench :advanced release of jsfb-hicasso-app, cache cleared either side per rf2-2rtt6.20), because rf2-2rtt6.125 added a fifth bracket call site in that tree:

  OFF bundle (651632 bytes): performance.measure 0, clearMeasures 0, "rf: 0, performance.mark 0
  ON  bundle (652430 bytes): performance.measure 4, clearMeasures 4, "rf: 1, performance.mark 0

798 bytes is the entire cost of the perf channel with the flag on, and zero with it off. Non-vacuous in both directions. That run is also unwired anywhere -- if clause 1 lands, consider whether the arm deserves a row too, or whether the counter's coverage of the shared macro is enough (probably it is; the macro is the thing being trusted).
DELIVERED 2026-08-05 — PR #7530 (worker/perfgate-eegpw).

OUTCOME: wire it per-PR. Remedy clauses 1 and 2 done; clause 4 filed as rf2-6ckzl.

MEASURED (cold, fresh worktree, empty .shadow-cljs):
  [:examples/counter]      29.99s   [:examples/counter-perf] 13.64s
  PASS perf-bundle: off-count=0; on-count=8 -- 75s wall clock end to end, exit 0.
  46s warm. Per-PR territory, so a PR job, not nightly. Confirms the filer's by-hand run.

NOT REDUNDANT WITH test:elision -- checked, not assumed. Different goog-define
(re-frame.performance/enabled? vs goog.DEBUG), different entry (counter.core/run vs
re-frame.elision-probe/run), disjoint sentinels: grep -c 'performance.measure|clearMeasures'
over check-elision.cjs returns 0. :elision-probe is built goog.DEBUG=false with the perf flag
at default, so the perf brackets elide there too -- but nothing asserts it and there is no
perf-ON control, so test:elision cannot make the claim even accidentally.

WIRED AS: new cljs-perf-bundle job in test.yml immediately after cljs-elision, gated on the
SAME cljs_prod output as its dual, added to all-required-passed needs: (a job absent from that
list is advisory whatever its own gate says). A job, NOT a step inside cljs-elision -- the two
prove different claims from disjoint sentinel sets and one job would make one failure
indistinguishable from the other in the checks UI. test:elision untouched.
Step list mirrors cljs-freehand-evidence-elision: JDK 21 + Node 24 + Maven cache, no Playwright
and NO Clojure CLI (shadow-cljs.edn resolves through :dependencies, not :deps), sharing that
job's runner.os-cljs- cache key rather than minting a fourth ~/.m2 entry.

NOT added to expensive-tests.yml: _rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs asserts lockstep between
that workflow's browser-bundle-and-story-gates job and scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh, so a step
there obliges an edit outside this bead's fence. Deliberate. Same reasoning left release.yml
alone. Both worth a follow-up if the nightly superset is wanted.

PROOF IT CAN FAIL (both arms broken, watched red, restored; build cache cleared each run):
  A. mark-and-measure CLJS expansion (if enabled? ...) -> (if true ...) -- the exact regression
     the gate exists to catch. All three sentinels FAIL as PRESENT in the off bundle,
     off-count 0 -> 8, exit 1. The off bundle also grew 627300 -> 628089 chars, byte-identical
     to the on bundle: the signature of a flag that no longer discriminates.
  B. build-name prefix "rf:" -> "xx:" -- the 'a refactor MOVED the strings' scenario Spec 009
     names as why the dual must exist. Off arm all OK; perf-ON control FAILs on the missing
     sentinel; exit 1. So the non-vacuity control has teeth too.
  Restored: git status clean, PASS off-count=0 on-count=8, exit 0.

SPEC 009 NEEDS NO CHANGE. Its sentence ('enforced in CI by npm run test:perf-bundle') is now
true as written. No spec/** file touched.

GAP MAP STAYS DERIVED: check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the required set from each aggregator's
needs: and reads each reproduce command from the step's own run: body, so adding the job to
needs: is the whole maintenance. --check now reports 76 required jobs (was 75) and stays clean;
--list names cljs-perf-bundle with 'cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle'. No edit to
the script, none to the spine (whose one-invocation-per-line shape is untouched).

GATES: perf-bundle cold 0; test:elision 0 (dual verified not weakened); test-fast-pr.sh 0
('PASS fast PR spine', 1927s); check_fast_pr_gap.py --self-test 0; --check 0;
check_ci_reproduce_commands.py 0; check_jvm_lane_rosters.py 0; mutation A 1; mutation B 1;
perf-bundle after restore 0.

title: nine bench drivers are FAIL-OPEN on pageerror — confirmed live; wire the refusal to the exit code
description:
CONFIRMED LIVE by rf2-jvheq's audit (PR #7494, 2026-08-04). The audit asked
whether the nine drivers' `pageerror` path is reachable without the sentinel.
It is — settled by RUNNING it, not by reading — so the conditional remedy the
audit bead named is now unconditional. This bead carries it.

THE NINE, each a bare handler that prints and records nothing:

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_prod_run.cjs      ~90
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_profile_run.cjs   ~96
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs           ~190
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b8_run.cjs           ~185
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b10_prod_run.cjs     ~123
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs ~200
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation_run.cjs ~222
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs                        ~383
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs ~317

THE EVIDENCE, all measured against this repo's own pins rather than argued:

  1. Playwright 1.59.1 raises `pageerror` for a throw inside
     `requestAnimationFrame`, a throw inside `setTimeout`, AND an unhandled
     promise rejection — while a completion sentinel set elsewhere STILL
     becomes true. All three exit 0 today.

  2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it defeats every page-side try/catch:
     React 19.2.0 does NOT rethrow an uncaught render error to the caller of
     `flushSync`/`render`. `defaultOnUncaughtError` hands it to
     `reportGlobalError` -> `reportError` (react-dom-client.production.js
     ~5888-5890, ~2307). Measured live: `pageerror` fires, THE SURROUNDING
     CATCH NEVER RUNS, no `window.*_ERROR` is set, the `page.evaluate` does
     not reject, and the app carries on and sets its sentinel. Every one of
     the nine mounts through `react-dom/flushSync`. Adding `catch :default`
     to the apps would NOT close this — only wiring `pageerror` to the exit
     code closes it.

  3. b10_prod_run.cjs has a SECOND, non-React path and is the worst of the
     nine: b10_two_clock.cljs ~670/694/709 drives the run from two
     `setInterval`s and a live `MutationObserver`. A throw in any of those is
     a detached task that escapes both `-main`'s try and the promise chain's
     `.catch`, and `setInterval` keeps firing after a throwing callback — so
     the run COMPLETES, sets `B10_DONE`, and publishes a mangled M3 record.

WHY THE AUDIT PR DID NOT SHIP THE FIX. Each of the nine needs an `:advanced`
release build and a headless Chromium to make its refusal fire, and a gate
nobody has watched fire is not a gate. Nine unproven exit wirings would be
the same fault in reverse. The finding is recorded in `sentinel.cjs` (the

title: RED ON MAIN: cljs-browser aborts — PR #7522 merged before its worker's fixture fix; PR #7531 is the repair
description:
MERGE PR #7531 (branch worker/hframe-841vn-followup). It is green and it
is the whole fix.

WHAT HAPPENED. PR #7522 (rf2-841vn / rf2-hnrww, h/frame) was merged at
commit 49acc9a704 while its worker was still running gates. Four commits
pushed to worker/hframe-841vn after that point did not travel, and one of
them is load-bearing.

THE BREAKAGE. main now carries
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/hframe_dom_cljs_test.cljs
with a FN-FORM test fixture. That file has an async test (the W2 row fires
its capture from a real macrotask, which is the entire content of the row),
and cljs.test refuses an async test under a fn-form fixture:

  [browser:pageerror] Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.  Testing aborted.

It does not fail one row -- it ABORTS THE WHOLE RUN at that namespace. The
required cljs-browser job therefore fails, and every namespace discovered
after hframe-dom-cljs-test goes unrun.

Reproduced locally on the pre-fix tree: npm run test:browser exit 1,
aborting at re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.hframe-dom-cljs-test. With the fix
(:async? true -- the map shape arm1/generation_fence_dom_cljs_test already
takes for the same reason): exit 0, 1097 tests / 6792 assertions, 0
failures, 0 errors. Verified on the follow-up branch built off CURRENT
main, not just on the worker branch.

NOTHING ELSE ON MAIN IS RED from that merge -- the node lane, the hicasso
compile gate and the fast-PR spine were all green at 49acc9a704. #7531 also
carries three small review-pass commits that were in the same push (a
vacuity fix in the carry-refusal id comparison, W4's premise asserted
rather than described, and the design record marking W7 unbuilt).

PROCESS NOTE for the merge loop, not a complaint: a PR whose worker has not
yet reported is not necessarily at its final commit. The green that was
merged was CI's read of an intermediate commit.

Close when #7531 is merged.
close_reason:
CLOSED — MAIN IS REPAIRED (mayor, 2026-08-05). Verified rather than assumed.

THE FIX IS ON MAIN: 863b3d428b "fix(hicasso): the h/frame DOM suite needs the map-shape fixture", merged as PR #7531, reachable from origin/main.

THE CAUSE WAS MINE. I merged PR #7522 on green while its worker was still running gates. Four of its commits had not travelled, and one carried the map-shape fixture. Main was left with an async test under a fn-form fixture, which cljs.test refuses - "Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps. Testing aborted." - taking the WHOLE browser run at that namespace, so every namespace after it went unrun and the required cljs-browser job failed.

THE BLAST RADIUS, recorded because it is the real cost: two other PRs went red on the identical abort, neither at fault. Worse, I told one of them main was green - citing three runs that PREDATED my own merge - and it spent over an hour hunting a hang in its own test that did not exist. It eventually ran the decisive control I never did: PURE origin/main with none of its commits, exit 1, identical abort. Both PRs cleared the moment their branches were rebased onto the repaired main.

TWO DIAGNOSTIC ERRORS OF MINE WORTH KEEPING, because each cost a cycle:
1. "main is green" IS A CLAIM WITH A TIMESTAMP. I quoted three green runs without checking whether my own merge had invalidated them.
2. gh run rerun RE-RUNS THE SAME RUN ID, so createdAt never moves. I read the unchanged timestamp as evidence the re-run had not happened; it had, and could not help, because the BRANCH lacked the fix. The discriminator is git branch -r --contains <fix> - a stale red re-runs clean, a stale BASE needs a rebase.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: green is a property of a TIP, not of a worker's intent. A worker that is still committing has commits that have not travelled, and merging its current tip merges unfinished work. Merging promptly remains right - it has caught far more than it cost today - but not while a worker is demonstrably mid-flight.
