title: Xray nightly gate: 'static mode chrome and chord' flakes ~29% of nights (5s locator timeout)
description:
Found while costing rf2-rliq7 (2026-08-05 16:40 AUSEST).

The nightly full Xray feature matrix (expensive-tests.yml, 'Gate - Xray
feature matrix') has failed 4 of the last 14 nights, ALWAYS on the same
scenario and ALWAYS with the same signature:

  FAIL static mode chrome and chord: locator.waitFor: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.

Runs: 2026-07-22 (29935235079), 07-24 (30106705162), 07-27 (30282895276),
07-31 (30645068521). Green on 07-23/25/26/28/29/30 and 08-01..08-04, and
green in a local full sweep on 2026-08-05. So it is INTERMITTENT, not a
standing red - roughly a 29% per-night failure rate, unfixed for two
weeks.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAKE. 'static mode chrome and chord' is a
NON-SMOKE scenario, so it never runs at PR time; the nightly is its only
executor. A system of record that reds ~1 night in 3 for a known flake
cannot be used to distinguish a NEW regression from the usual noise -
which is precisely the fail-open shape this project has been clearing
out. rf2-rliq7's option (1) (WONTFIX, 'the nightly sweep is the system of
record') is only honest once this is green, and its option (3) (arm the
full sweep at PR time) is actively DANGEROUS while it stands: it would
red ~1 in 3 PRs touching scenarios.cjs for an unrelated known flake.

So this is on the critical path of the rf2-rliq7 ruling and should be
fixed before that policy call is taken.

SCENARIO: tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs, the scenario
named 'static mode chrome and chord' (runStaticModeChromeAndChord). The
5000ms figure is a locator budget inside the scenario, well under the
gate's own 45s XRAY_FEATURE_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling - the same class
rf2-taj9b fixed for the one bare navigation in that file. History note:
this same scenario was RED for real once before (rf2-wxu4l3, fixed in
9bc9e6c9a2 2026-06-10) for a genuine ':rf.error/no-frame-context' crash
in the Static Machines browse-list, so a timeout here is not
automatically 'just a flake' - confirm which.
close_reason:
PR #7535. NOT a short timeout and NOT runner slowness — a TOCTOU double-toggle in the scenario harness's openXray helper, reproduced under control.

MECHANISM (from the 2026-07-31 nightly, run 30645068521, plus source): Ctrl+Shift+C is a TOGGLE (mount/toggle!), and Xray's preload runs a second concurrent opener — mount/auto-open-inline! polls every 50ms until rf/init! has installed the substrate adapter, then calls open!. openXray sampled shell PRESENCE once (count()) and pressed the chord on a 0. When auto-open landed in the gap between that sample and the keydown, the chord arrived at an already-open shell, toggle! took its close! branch, and close! hid the container while leaving the React tree mounted. expectVisible then burned its full 5000ms on a shell the helper had hidden itself. CI evidence is decisive: '15 x locator resolved to hidden <div ... data-testid="rf-xray-shell" data-rf-xray-mode="inline">' with diagnostics reading 'mounted=true visible=none', epochCount=1, and ZERO pageerrors. Raising the timeout could never have gone green — nothing was going to un-hide it.

SECOND DEFECT, one line apart: count() asks 'is it in the DOM', but close! keeps the node, so presence never meant open. The failure state is itself one the old code would misread as 'already open', skip the chord for, and then fail the visible-wait on.

REPRODUCED: a scratchpad A/B forced the interleaving deterministically (early presence sample, then a widened gap so auto-open lands inside it). OLD 6/11 failures, byte-identical signature (resolvedToHidden=true, final mounted=true/display=none); NEW 0/11. Perfect correlation — every OLD failure had sample=0, every OLD pass sample=1.

WHY ONLY THIS SCENARIO, of ~14 calling openXray: it is the SOLE navigate/reload site in the 3991-line file. On the harness's cold page.goto the adapter is installed long before 'load' resolves, so auto-open always wins the peek; on a warm reload the two converge and the race opens. The nightly record matches: ~180 cold-path openXray calls over 14 nights with zero failures, 14 warm-path calls with four.

FIX: one ordering guarantee, not a longer wait. Settle on presence first (mount-state is a monotone latch — once mounted, auto-open's tick short-circuits forever), then decide on VISIBILITY, the same condition the assertion uses. Settle budget = auto-open's own retry bound (120x50ms), the point at which it has provably stopped. No duration raised; the 5000 assertion is untouched. No assertion weakened, no retry added, chord still fires at most once. 53 insertions / 2 deletions in one file.

RULED OUT with evidence: runner slowness (element present+hidden for all 15 polls); chord-handler registration race (keybinding/attach! runs synchronously at preload, before auto-open; the keydown was plainly received — that is what hid the shell); transient selector match (one stable element for 5s); product ordering bug (zero pageerrors, clean boot); and the historic rf2-wxu4l3 :rf.error/no-frame-context crash (that one threw; this does not).

GATES: fast-PR spine PASS(0); tools/xray clojure -M:test 1271 tests / 5909 assertions, 0 failures(0); xray-feature-gate:smoke 5 scenarios 0 failures(0); eslint clean(0); FULL xray-feature-gate run 6x (5 pre-rebase + 1 post-rebase), 17 scenarios each, 0 failures every run = 102 scenario executions, 0 failures.

NOTE FOR rf2-rliq7: this unblocks the policy call — the nightly's known flake is now mechanised and fixed, so a red nightly can again be read as a real regression.

NOTE ON THE TWO WEEKS: the gate's diagnostics were ALREADY sufficient to diagnose this from the first failure on 2026-07-22 (mounted=true visible=none + 'resolved to hidden' is the whole answer). No instrumentation was missing and none was added. What was missing was anyone being told — the expensive-tests.yml alerting gap, rf2-6sg25.

title: perf: nine required checkers share the rglob+relative_to walk that cost the image-keys gate 37s
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-e1xx0 while making check_retired_image_keys.py sub-second (37.7s -> 0.9s).

rf2-e1xx0's bead predicted the sibling check_retired_composition_vocab.py would 'come along for free' because it shares the _EXCLUDE_REL_PREFIXES/masking design. MEASURED: it does NOT. It has no _mask_multiline_clj_strings at all (that was the 12s item), so nothing came along for free -- it is a separate file needing its own pre-filter and its own equivalence proof.

What it DOES share, along with eight others, is the file-walk shape:

  sorted(scan_root.rglob('*'))  +  path.relative_to(...) per file

That was ~0.5s of pure pathlib churn in the image-keys gate, and rglob enumerates implementation/node_modules (~50k paths in a checkout that has it -- which every worker worktree does) only to discard it one entry at a time. rf2-e1xx0 replaced it with an os.walk that PRUNES _EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES in place plus prefix-string rel paths, proven to yield the same paths in the same order on a node_modules-populated checkout.

The nine sharing that shape:
  check_ambient_durable_reads.py       check_retired_composition_vocab.py
  check_failure_corpus_residue.py      check_retired_image_keys.py  (DONE)
  check_freehand_conformance_index.py  check_retired_spellings.py
  check_inject_cofx_residue.py         check_thrown_error_messages.py
  check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py

MEASURED COST: check_retired_composition_vocab.py is 1.3-1.5s -- now the most expensive single python checker in the fast-PR spine. The other 36 cost ~6.4s between them. So the whole remaining prize is roughly 1s across the batch, against a documentation tier of ~28s.

THIS IS DELIBERATELY P4. The payoff is small and every one of these gates already has a local lane; nothing is blocked. File it so the measurement is not lost, not because the backlog needs it. If it is ever picked up, the non-negotiable is rf2-e1xx0's method: hold the finding SETS identical (real corpus, allowlist-bypassed corpus, and a per-token x per-context synthetic corpus), not merely both exit 0. A pre-filter that elides most of the regex battery is exactly the change that can silently narrow a gate.

DO NOT bundle these into one worker -- each checker needs its own equivalence proof, and a shared-mechanism refactor across nine guards is a much bigger change than nine small ones.
close_reason:
MEASURED. PR #7539. The answer splits by TREE, which is why the bead priced it low
and was right about CI and low by ~10x about the local lane.

CI: NOT WORTH IT, as filed. All nine run in bare-checkout Python jobs
(test.yml "verify-skill-mcp-drift"; freehand-conformance.yml) with NO npm ci and
no build. Walk cost across all nine there: 0.85s -> 0.46s. A 0.38s prize.

LOCAL (mayor checkout): 19.76s -> 0.62s of walk. Not one second.

WHY THE BEAD UNDER-PRICED IT: the driver is .shadow-cljs (35,423 entries), not
node_modules (3,410). Entries under implementation/: clean checkout 2,365;
freshly built worktree 13,839; long-lived mayor checkout 52,236. The win scales
with accumulated BUILD CACHE, so it does not exist in CI and grows the longer a
local checkout lives.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD:
 1. check_retired_composition_vocab is NOT "the most expensive python checker in
    the spine". It is 1.46s. check_retired_spellings is 3.55s clean / 8.07s built.
    Composition-vocab walk is 0.02s - its cost is regex, not enumeration, so a
    shared walk does nothing for it at all.
 2. Only FOUR of the nine have anything to win (they scan implementation/ or
    repo_root). The other five scan docs/spec/skills/testbeds and save 0.07s
    BETWEEN THEM. Touching a required gate for 20ms is over-engineering; left alone.

SHIPPED (three, each edited in place, NO shared abstraction per this bead):
  check_retired_spellings        6.43s -> 3.63s
  check_keyword_catalogue_drift  4.76s -> 1.46s
  check_thrown_error_messages    3.81s -> 1.29s
  total on mayor checkout       15.00s -> 6.38s  (8.62s saved)
All three already had _EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES, so pruning drops exactly what the

sorted(rglob()) order (os.walk directory-grouped order is NOT the same).

NOT SHIPPED - the biggest single win (7.0s), deferred to rf2-mjfj9 for a RULING:
check_ambient_durable_reads has no exclusion roster; it excludes build trees only
incidentally via endswith on DURABLE_WRITE_SUFFIXES. Pruning therefore NARROWS it
(a source copy nested in out/ or .shadow-cljs/ is scanned today). Harness proved
the divergence: 12 findings, all planted; 0 of 18 real files affected. A scope
change to a required invariant gate is not a worker call.

EQUIVALENCE HELD AS FINDING SETS, NOT EXIT CODES:
 - path sequences identical in SET AND ORDER across 19 root x include_tests
   comparisons on the built tree;

title: ssr-ring emits a render-hash for ANY root shape — including adoption-tier ones Spec 011 now says must carry none
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING rf2-2rtt6.91 (PR #7510). Not fixed there, because
the fix needs a host-level fact the undecided server arm owns.

rf2-2rtt6.91 established the rule and PR #7510 put it in Spec 011
§Hydration-mismatch detection: an ADOPTION-TIER root (compiled donor
substrate, native UIx, Freehand) MUST NOT carry :rf/render-hash in its
payload nor data-rf-render-hash on its root element, because the only
tree such a root can offer a server-side hash is the UNRESOLVED root
form, whose canonical EDN is [#fn[] {props}] — a constant.

ssr-ring does not know about tiers. pipeline.clj:543 computes
  hash-str (lifecycle/render-document-hash hiccup)
over (lifecycle/resolve-root-view root-view) unconditionally, and passes
:emit-hash? through, for whatever :root-view the host declared. Correct
for a hiccup-tier host; silently degenerate for an adoption-tier one.
The server-arm dossier already recorded that 'the degeneracy reaches
production identically whichever arm renders'. Nothing serves a Freehand
root through ssr-ring TODAY, so this is a trap laid rather than a live
defect — but the first server arm that does will re-create exactly the
fail-open gate rf2-2rtt6.91 just closed, in production rather than in a
bench.

SECOND, SEPARABLE HAZARD ON THE SAME LINE — the HICCUP tier's own root
form. resolve-root-view accepts a hiccup VECTOR verbatim, so a host
declaring :root-view [#'app/root] makes the SERVER hash the shallow
[#'app/root] while the documented client boot (:render-tree-fn
#((rf/view :app/root)) — note the outer call) hashes the DEEP tree the
view returns. Those can never be equal, so that host fires
:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch on EVERY page — and under :ssr
{:on-mismatch :hard-error} that is a crash on every page. Fail-CLOSED
and noisy rather than fail-open, so much less severe than .91, but it is
a live foot-gun: resolve-root-view's docstring says 'Prefer the 0-arity
fn form' for an unrelated reason (opts built before registration) and
never mentions the hash consequence, which is the sharper one.
VERIFY BEFORE FIXING — I read this from the source and did not run it.

Likely shape: a :root-view whose resolved form is a single callable-headed
vector cannot produce a meaningful body hash, so either refuse
:emit-hash? for it with a typed error naming the 0-arity fn form, or
require the host to declare its tier. Ruling needed on which — do not
default into one.

Hot-zone: implementation/ssr-ring/** is not in the hot-zone list, but
spec/011-SSR.md is, and a fix probably touches it.
notes:
THE UNKNOWN THIS BEAD'S CLOSE RECORDED IS NOW CLOSED — IT REPRODUCES, AND tools/template WAS THE LIVE INSTANCE (mayor, 2026-08-05).

WHAT I WROTE WHEN CLOSING: "WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, and am recording as unknown rather than assuming: whether the SECOND, separable hazard on pipeline.clj:543 reproduced - the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep... WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled."

IT REPRODUCES. Found by the rf2-qfct9 worker, measured in the emitted project rather than argued: the template's two ends declared the root differently - server (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)]), a REFERENCE; client (fn [] (rf/with-frame app-frame ((rf/view :app/root)))), the TREE. Client tree hashes a2aa3d1d; the server's unresolved root hashes f1d63f7e - the exact per-arity constant that render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)].

SO THE TEMPLATE WAS BROKEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BEFORE AND AFTER THIS BEAD: before, it shipped a hash that MISMATCHED ON EVERY PAGE; after, the hash is simply absent. Both wrong for a hiccup-tier host, which is what it actually is.

THIS BEAD'S FIX IS CORRECT AND UNTOUCHED. The template's root belongs to the hiccup tier and SHOULD carry a hash - it was merely spelled the one way that structurally cannot have one. The repair is the outer call, (fn [] ((rf/view :app/root))), which lifecycle.clj's resolve-root-view docstring already names as the symmetric spelling. HTML is byte-identical either way.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: a worker fenced to implementation/ssr-ring/** could not see that a tools/ artefact asserts on the emitted markup, and nothing connects "this code emits X" to "that test asserts X" across an artefact boundary. The fence was right; the coupling is invisible from both ends. That is the same class as test:perf-bundle wired to nothing and :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id documented but never set.

AND A FAIL-OPEN IN THE VERIFYING LANE ITSELF, which the fixing worker hit first: plain `clojure -M:test` in tools/template SKIPS the failing rows - they sit behind RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1. Its first run came back GREEN with the bug still present. Anyone verifying that lane locally must set the env var or they get a false green.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY THE MAYOR FROM THE LANDED EVIDENCE, because the implementing agent was killed by a watchdog stall before it could close this itself (2026-08-05). Its last line was "Green. Committing and opening the PR now" - it did both, and the work merged as PR #7520.

WHAT LANDED, verified on main rather than taken from a report that never arrived:
  fix(ssr-ring): the unresolved root form carries no render-hash on the server either
  test(ssr-ring): pin the server-side tier rule and its measurement
plus implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/render_hash_tier_test.clj, which is the pin.

THE ANSWER IT REACHED, readable from the PR title and worth recording because the brief asked the question directly: THE SERVER CAN DISTINGUISH, AND IT DISTINGUISHES BY ROOT FORM RATHER THAN BY TIER. The brief had flagged that if pipeline.clj could not tell the tiers apart at that point, that would be a design finding worth reporting rather than a hack worth writing. It could tell - by whether the root form resolves - so no hack was needed and no tier-detection framework was built.

THIS COMPLETES THE PAIR. rf2-2rtt6.91 removed the degenerate hash on the client, on the ground that Spec 011's adoption tier deliberately carries none; this removes it on the server, so the first Freehand server arm no longer re-creates the fail-open in production. The two ends now agree.

WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, and am recording as unknown rather than assuming: whether the SECOND, separable hazard on pipeline.clj:543 reproduced - the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep. The filer flagged it "verify before fixing" and the brief passed that on. If it reproduced and was fixed, it is in the diff; if it did not, that finding is lost with the agent. WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled.

title: spec 009: the :rf.error/no-frame-context row has the SAME incomplete :operation enumeration, and both frame-resolution rows list a :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id payload key no builder ever sets
description:
FOUND by rf2-e28wl (PR #7533) while fixing the sibling row. Two defects, one file, deliberately NOT folded into e28wl because that bead scoped itself to one row and spec/** is a hot zone.

DEFECT 1 -- the same enumeration bug, one row up. spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/no-frame-context row says:

  trigger: 'A frame-scoped op (subscribe / dispatch, the ambient 1-arity rf/ forms)'
  payload: ':operation (:dispatch / :subscribe), :where (:re-frame.router/dispatch! / :re-frame.subs/subscribe)'

Both are incomplete for exactly the reason e28wl's row was: no-frame-context is raised by the SAME primitive (frame/require-current-frame!), so every op that can hit the refusal can hit the absence. Grepping implementation/*/src finds 18+ call sites and these :operation values: :subscribe :subscribe-once :unsubscribe :dispatch :capture-frame :current-frame-id :use-frame :clear-sub-cache! :elision-declarations :elision-sensitive-declarations :reg-flow :clear-flow :flow-meta-at :route-link :reg-http-interceptor :clear-http-interceptor :machine-by-system-id :frame-provider, plus re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc which passes its CALLER's operation keyword (so the set is open by construction). The :where enumeration is wrong the same way.

PR #7533 fixed the ambient-frame-refused row by stating the RULE (the category is defined by the door) and treating the names as illustration. Same remedy applies here. Doing it makes the two rows consistent; leaving it means one row states the rule and its sibling lists two ops.

DEFECT 2 -- a payload key that is never set. BOTH rows end '...plus the capture-site ancestry correlation keys :rf.trace/dispatch-id / :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id'. Neither payload builder sets the parent. frame.cljc's no-frame-context-payload and ambient-frame-refused-payload each merge only

  (when-let [did (some-> trace/*handler-scope* :dispatch-id)] {:rf.trace/dispatch-id did})

and the call sites' 'extra' carries only :where / :event-id. :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id IS set elsewhere -- router.cljc:3982 puts it on the dispatch envelope's trace tags -- but it never reaches either frame-resolution payload. Either the rows should say :rf.trace/dispatch-id alone, or the builders should thread the parent when a handler scope has one; that is a real call, not a wording fix, which is why this is filed rather than guessed.

WHY NOT FIXED IN #7533: defect 2 is a claim SHARED by both rows, and correcting one of two would read as a deliberate distinction to a reader. Both wanted fixing together, and no-frame-context is a heavily cross-referenced always-on / security-surface row (cited by 004D, Security.md, 011) -- out of a one-row bead's scope.

SCOPE: two rows in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (plus, for defect 2, a decision about frame.cljc's two payload builders). spec/** is a hot zone; sequence, do not parallelise.

NOTE :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused remains PROVISIONAL (rf2-k0rbk).

description:

  on:
    schedule:

(rf2-7jevo).

DELIBERATELY nightly-only precisely because the nightly is treated as
the system of record - TESTING.md says so, and rf2-rliq7's option (1)
rests on it entirely. A system of record that can be red for thirteen
nights with nobody paged is an instrument that reports nothing and is
believed anyway. That is the same shape as the 26 fail-open instruments
cleared this week, one level up: the gate runs, it catches, and the
catch goes nowhere.

against any live workflow worker). Cheapest credible fix is a final
'if: failure()' step that opens or updates a single tracking issue, or

PR #7536. expensive-tests.yml gains a final always() job that opens, edits and closes ONE tracking issue via .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py.

The second rule mattered as much as the first -- ten of the fourteen remaining came from FLAP (the rf2-7jevo Xray flake closing and reopening the issue every other night), not from the streak. 3 is read off the data: green runs between two flake failures ran 1 and 2; every genuine recovery ran 3+.

That live run found a bug no self-test could: GitHub's label-filtered issue index is eventually consistent, so two invocations 3s apart both read 'no issue' and both opened one. Read is now unfiltered + client-side label match with a self-healing duplicate collapse.

title: cljs_prod / bundle_isolation are not armed by examples/* — both example-bundle gates can be skipped by a change to the example they compile
description:
rf2-eegpw follow-up (found while wiring the cljs-perf-bundle job).

## The gap

.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh's generic `examples/*)` case arms ONLY `cljs_browser` + `cljs_node_test` (plus `examples_compile` from the earlier combined case). It does NOT arm `cljs_prod` or `bundle_isolation`.

But both of those outputs gate jobs whose bundles are compiled FROM examples source:

- `cljs-perf-bundle` (new, rf2-eegpw, gated on cljs_prod) builds `:examples/counter` + `:examples/counter-perf`, both `counter.core/run`.
- `cljs-bundle-isolation` (gated on bundle_isolation) builds `:examples/counter`, `:examples/counter-uix`, `:examples/login`, `:examples/login-uix`, `:examples/realworld-resources`.

So a PR that changes only `examples/counter/**` recompiles the exact entry both gates grep, and neither gate runs. The perf gate would not notice a counter change that stopped reaching a mark-and-measure call site (which would make the perf-ON control vacuous); the isolation gate would not notice a counter change that pulled in a tools/* symbol.

## Why it was not fixed in rf2-eegpw

The fix is one classifier change in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` that widens BOTH gates at once, and rf2-eegpw's fence was `.github/workflows/**` + TESTING.md + implementation/package.json. It is also a shared decision (how much extra `:advanced` build cost to spend on examples-only PRs), not something the perf-gate bead should decide unilaterally.

## Remedy

Arm `cljs_prod` + `bundle_isolation` from the generic `examples/*)` case — or, if that is judged too broad for the whole examples tree, from the specific example entries the two gates compile. Note the classifier is deliberately conservative elsewhere (see the rf2-8ckcf2 comment in that same case, which widened it to cljs_node_test on exactly this reasoning), so the broad widening is the more consistent choice.

Also consider the second half of rf2-eegpw's remedy clause 4: nothing detects an npm script that exists but appears in no workflow. That is the class that hid test:perf-bundle for as long as it did.
close_reason:
PR #7536. Classifier fix: the generic examples/*) case now arms cljs_prod + bundle_isolation. Mutation-proved on examples/core/counter/core.cljs (the entry both gates compile): cljs_prod=false/bundle_isolation=false at HEAD, true on the branch. Cost measured on run 30980305020 -- docs-only PR pays zero (never reaches the case); examples-only pays +4 jobs / +469s runner time / ~0 wall clock, all four running in parallel beside the 778s :node-test and 644s examples-compile jobs such a PR already queues.

Remedy clause 4 TAKEN, and the count was wrong: the bead named ONE unscheduled gate, the measured answer is FOUR of 40. New .github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py asserts every test:*/bench:* command is reachable from a workflow (closure walked through npm-script chains) or carries a machine-CHECKED disposition. Follow-ups filed: rf2-a9oic (three orphaned verdict gates need homes), rf2-k78o2 (promote the audit from the nightly to PR time -- it landed in the nightly only because test.yml was fenced by #7530).

title: check_ambient_durable_reads does not reach a host read wrapped in a call
description:
FOUND while writing rf2-g1xpb fixtures (PR #7541). NOT actioned there: it is a SCOPE question about a required gate, not a self-test question, and widening a required invariant gate needs a ruling.

THE SHAPE. `_VIOLATION_RE` is `:KEY\s+(READ)` — the ambient read must sit IMMEDIATELY in the durable keys value position. So these FIRE:

    :restored-at js/localStorage
    :started-at  (.now js/Date)

and this does NOT (verified, zero findings):

    :restored-at (.getItem js/localStorage "session")

The gate already handles three call-wrapper spellings by enumerating them as their own roster entries — `(.now js/Date …)`, `(.getRandomValues js/crypto …)`, `(.matchMedia …)`. The host-fact entries `js/location`, `js/navigator`, `navigator.`, `js/localStorage`, `js/sessionStorage`, `js/matchMedia` have no such wrapper spelling, so they are reachable ONLY as bare symbol values.

WHY IT MAY NOT MATTER. A bare `js/localStorage` in a durable key value position is not how anyone reads localStorage; `(.getItem js/localStorage …)` is. If the call-wrapper shape is the realistic one, the six host-fact roster entries are close to unreachable in practice, and the gate is narrower than the roster advertises.

WHY IT MAY BE FINE AS IS. EP-0010 governs a DURABLE WRITE being non-deterministic; a durable field taking a host fact through a getter is the same defect, but widening the value-position match to "an ambient read anywhere inside the value form" risks false positives on a legitimately threaded value.

NO CHANGE MADE. rf2-g1xpb left the walk and the match alone deliberately (see also rf2-mjfj9 for the sibling scope ruling on the same checker). Both branches need Mike, not a worker.

title: Three verdict gates run nowhere: test:schemas-bundle, test:ui-warm-watch, test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly
description:
Found while taking rf2-6ckzl's fourth remedy clause (PR #7536). The new
audit .github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py enumerates every
`test:*` / `bench:*` command in implementation/package.json and asks
whether any workflow reaches it. rf2-6ckzl named ONE such gate
(test:perf-bundle). The measured answer is FOUR:

  40 gate commands, 30 scheduled, 10 declared,
  4 of the 10 being genuine holes.

  * test:perf-bundle          -- rf2-eegpw / PR #7530 gives it a home.
  * test:schemas-bundle       -- releases `schemas-bundle-probe` +
    `schemas-bundle-probe-malli` and runs check-schemas-bundle.cjs.
    That checker is referenced by this npm script and by NOTHING ELSE
    in the repo, so the malli-boundary bundle claim has never run in CI.
  * test:ui-warm-watch        -- runs check-ui-warm-watch.cjs, likewise
    referenced by this npm script and nothing else.
  * test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly -- the sharpest one: a build named for
    the nightly that is in no nightly. `:node-test-perf-nightly` selects
    `-emit-nightly-test$`, which the consolidated `:node-test` build's
    `cljs-test$` does NOT match, so every `*_emit_nightly_test.cljs`
    namespace runs in that lane alone -- and that lane runs nowhere.
    check_test_lane_bijection.py cannot see this: the lane HAS a
    selector and the selector DOES reach files, so the bijection holds.
    What no gate asserted until now is that the lane is ever RUN.

The other six unscheduled commands are legitimately covered and are
declared as such in the audit's DISPOSITIONS table, with the premise
of each declaration machine-checked (test:security / test:ui /
test:testbed-support are strict `cljs-test$` subsets run by the
scheduled consolidated lane; test:cljs-isolation and
test:mcp-conformance have their teeth run directly by test.yml;
bench:hicasso yields records, not a verdict).

REMEDY. Give each of the three a scheduled home. The cheap one is a
step in expensive-tests.yml's browser/bundle sweep -- which per
rf2-6sg25 now alerts when it reds, so a nightly home is a real home
rather than a second silent one. NOTE THE LOCKSTEP: adding an
`npm run` step to `browser-bundle-and-story-gates` obliges the same
command in scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh
(implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs pins it).
Run each gate green locally FIRST -- wiring an unvalidated gate into
the nightly the week alerting lands would file an issue on night one.

Delete each command's DISPOSITIONS entry in
.github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py as it gains a home. The audit
deliberately does NOT go red when an `unscheduled` entry becomes
scheduled -- that transition is the hole closing, and reddening main
for it would punish the fix.
close_reason:
Delivered in PR #7542 (merged, 25e404f434). Each of the three was RUN before it was scheduled, per the bead's own warning.

test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly -- 32s cold, GREEN (12 tests / 37 assertions).
WIRED into expensive-tests.yml's browser-bundle-and-story-gates as its own
named step. Nightly on the build's OWN documented grounds rather than on cost:
shadow-cljs.edn says its User-Timing assertions are noisy under per-PR runner
load. The defect was the missing schedule, not the tier.

test:ui-warm-watch -- 48s cold, GREEN (all 8 passes + WARM-CACHE REUSE PROVEN).
WIRED into the same job. NOT the watch-mode command the name suggests: it
drives a real Shadow warm watch and one live emitted runtime through eight
scripted edit passes plus a disk-cache restart, then terminates with a verdict.
Nightly because it spawns two watch daemons and a live node child and polls at
50ms under a 120s timeout -- the process-orchestration class, most prone to
false negatives under per-PR load. Cost would have allowed either tier.

Both added to scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh in the same PR: both satisfy that
script's documented two-part derivation (verdict + nightly-only home), and
_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs pins the lockstep.

test:schemas-bundle -- 47s cold, RED. NOT WIRED, and that is the real finding.
Both probes measure 124.9 KB gzipped against a 100 KB ceiling, 24.9 KB over,
while Spec 010 Bundle cost still catalogues ~91 KB and the checker's own
threshold comment repeats it -- both statements now false. A gate that had run
nowhere since it was authored had accumulated a real 25% regression. The
schema-implies-validation equality guard is still green (12-byte delta), so the
structural claim holds and only the absolute budget moved.

It stays declared 'unscheduled' repointed at rf2-kybsf (filed, P1), with the
measured red in its why. Not threshold-bumped: Spec 010's budget table is
normative and the checker's own failure text says rule the spec section first,
move the threshold in lockstep. Narrowing a gate to make it pass is the one
move this audit exists to prevent.

DISPOSITIONS entries deleted for the three gates that gained homes
(test:perf-bundle, test:ui-warm-watch, test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly).
Census: 40 gate commands, 31 -> 33 scheduled, 9 -> 7 declared, 3 -> 1 hole.

Mutation-proved: unscheduling either newly-wired gate reds the audit by name
(exit 1); perf flag off reds emit-nightly across four deftests; a shrunk card
fixture reds warm-watch at cold accept. All reverted.

title: Promote the gate-scheduling audit from the nightly to PR time
description:
Follow-up to rf2-6ckzl remedy clause 4 (PR #7536).

.github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py asserts that every
`test:*` / `bench:*` command in implementation/package.json is either
reachable from a workflow or carries a machine-checked disposition
saying why not. It is a ~0.1s pure-Python static check with a
self-test arm -- exactly the shape of the twenty-nine checkers already
in test.yml's always-on repo-invariant job and in
scripts/test-fast-pr.sh's always-on block.

It landed in expensive-tests.yml instead, for one reason only: PR #7536
was fenced OFF .github/workflows/test.yml because rf2-eegpw / #7530 was
open on it. Nightly is not nothing -- rf2-6sg25 landed alerting in the
same PR -- but a PR that adds an unscheduled gate should learn so in
three minutes, not in twenty-four hours.

REMEDY, once test.yml is free:
  1. Add the self-test + live arms to test.yml's repo-invariant job,
     with the `id:` + `continue-on-error: true` shape
     scripts/check_ci_reproduce_commands.py requires of every checker
     step there, and the matching aggregator entry.
  2. Add both invocations to the always-on block of
     scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, ONE PER LINE in the literal
     `python "$spine_root/scripts/check_<name>.py"` form --
     check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the spine's coverage by reading that
     literal shape, and a loop breaks the derivation.
  3. NOTE: the script lives at .github/scripts/, not scripts/, so the
     spine's literal-shape derivation may need it moved to scripts/
     first -- check check_fast_pr_gap.py's matcher before wiring.
  4. Drop the nightly `gate-scheduling` job, or keep it; it is ~10s of
     runner time and the nightly's `nightly-result` job `needs:` it.
close_reason:
Delivered in PR #7542 (merged, 25e404f434). PREMISE CHECKED FIRST, as the brief asked: the nightly placement had NO merit -- it was accidental. The workflow comment named the cause (test.yml fenced by rf2-eegpw/#7530 the day it was written) and TESTING.md itself recorded the move as a follow-up. Cost measured before moving: 0.75s / 0.86s / 0.93s for the self-test + live pair over three warm runs on Windows, both arms within ~50ms of each other. Both read only implementation/package.json and .github/workflows/, so neither grows with the tree.

Remedy clause 3 was the load-bearing one and the bead was right to flag it. The script is now scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py -- moved AND renamed to underscores. That is not cosmetic: check_ci_reproduce_commands.py matches ^python scripts/check_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.py and check_fast_pr_gap.py matches ^python scripts/(check_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\.py, so a hyphenated .github/scripts/ script is invisible to BOTH. Its failure would have been reported with a reproduce command that does not exist (the aggregator's id-based fallback would emit 'python scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py' for a file that was not there), and the fast-PR gap map would never have counted it. main() also moved parents[2] -> parents[1] for the new depth.

Clause 1: two steps added to test.yml's verify-skill-mcp-drift repo-invariant job in the required id: + continue-on-error: true shape (check_gate_scheduling_selftest / check_gate_scheduling). Verified by check_ci_reproduce_commands.py --check and by --emit on both ids, which now round-trip to the exact commands the steps run.

Clause 2: two invocations added to the always-on block of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in the literal one-per-line python "$spine_root/scripts/check_<name>.py" form. No loop -- the derivation would have gone fictional. Verified: the spine run shows both arms green, and check_fast_pr_gap.py --check stays clean and derived (76 required jobs, 26 covered, 4 partly, 46 not). The 'MEASURED BEFORE ADDING' comment was extended with the new pair's real numbers rather than left stating 29.

Clause 4: the nightly gate-scheduling job is DROPPED, not kept, and nightly-result's needs: updated to the 4 remaining jobs. An always-on per-PR gate means main cannot carry a violation overnight, so a nightly arm would re-prove a property proven on every merge, and a second copy is a second thing to keep in step. Workflow YAML re-parsed to confirm the job graph.

TESTING.md updated: the audit is described as per-PR, the census restated, and the remaining hole named with its measured red.

title: SSR: the inline HydrationPayload conformance schema is still loose in three more slots
description:
SPUN OUT of rf2-2rtt6.91's MERGED-PR AUDIT #7510 remainder, which fenced its own scope: 'Align that ONE schema slot ... do not broaden into a payload-schema rewrite.' PR #7545 aligned :rf/render-hash and stopped there. This bead carries what it deliberately left.

implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy_cljs_test.cljc pins an inline HydrationPayload it calls 'the canonical v1 HydrationPayload schema (Spec-Schemas :rf/hydration-payload)'. Against spec/Spec-Schemas.md's block (~L3793-3801) three divergences remain:

  1. :rf/schema-digest  — test says {:optional true} [:maybe :string]; spec says {:optional true} :string.
  2. :rf/runtime-db     — test says {:optional true} [:maybe :map];    spec says {:optional true} :rf/runtime-db.
  3. :rf/head-hash      — ABSENT from the test schema; the spec carries it {:optional true} :string, and build-payload emits it. The map is open, so a payload carrying :rf/head-hash validates while nothing checks its type.

NOT A LIVE DEFECT TODAY. payload-policy/build-payload assembles via cond-> with (some? runtime-db), schema-digest and head-hash arms, so it provably never emits a present-and-nil value in any of the three. The gap is that the schema calling itself canonical would ACCEPT shapes the spec forbids — the same fail-open class rf2-2rtt6.91 closed for :rf/render-hash, one slot over.

THE WORK. Tighten 1 and 2 by dropping the [:maybe ...] (NOT by importing the spec's :rf/runtime-db registry ref — that needs a malli registry in the test ns and IS the rewrite the audit fenced). Add slot 3. Each wants a focused case in the manner of build-payload-render-hash-is-optional: real value preserved, nil omits the key, hand-stamped nil rejected. Mutation-prove each new assertion.

JUDGEMENT CALL AVAILABLE. If the mayor would rather the inline schema stop claiming canonicity than chase Spec-Schemas slot by slot, retitling the comment is a legitimate cheaper answer and should be argued rather than defaulted into.

title: Nothing gates a docstring's prose against what its module exports — one docstring seeded four design records and a guide page
description:
FOUND while landing rf2-2rtt6.120 (2026-08-05, PR #7543).

THE SHAPE. front/intent.cljs's render-callback docstring illustrated the row a
`renderRow` prop exists to build with `(h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick
(:id row)]} (:title row)])`. No such var exists: arm1/lang.clj exports exactly
defview, hfn and defhost, the mechanism is codec/as-element and it is internal,
and no h/ spelling reaches it. FOUR independent design documents
(studio/raw-escape-design-{a,b,c}.md, raw-escape-spec.md) plus decisions.md and
one guide page copied the spelling out of that docstring. Design C built its
entire render-prop worked example on it.

WHY IT PROPAGATED. Every executable surface is gated — clj-kondo resolves every
symbol in a form, the compile gate compiles 126 namespaces with zero warnings —
but a docstring is a string literal. Nothing reads the prose inside it, so a
docstring can name a function that does not exist and stay green forever. The
teaching surface with the widest blast radius is the one with no gate behind it.

THE CANDIDATE GATE. scripts/check_retired_spellings.py is the right home in
kind: it already scopes to exact retired SHAPES rather than bare keywords, for
exactly this reason. `h/as-element` is a precise, unambiguous shape — it is not
sanctioned anywhere, so a bare git-grep for it has no false positives, except
that rf2-2rtt6.120's PR deliberately leaves several NEGATIONS in the records
('there is no h/as-element'). So the gate cannot be a bare grep either; it wants
the shape 'h/as-element inside a code fence or a paren-call position' versus
'h/as-element in prose immediately preceded by a negation'. Alternatively, and
more cheaply: a doc-fence-only rule, since every surviving occurrence is prose.

THE GENERAL CASE IS BIGGER AND MAY NOT BE WORTH IT. Verifying every qualified
symbol in every docstring against the ns it appears in is a real analyzer.
Recommend the narrow ratchet (one known-dead spelling, plus a place to add the
next one) over the general check, unless a second instance shows up.

NOT DONE IN rf2-2rtt6.120's PR: scripts/ was outside that dispatch's fence.
Bench lane. No AI attribution.

title: hicasso: the guide's taught 'h/as-element' recovery does not exist — four [:>] designs name a spelling no reader can call
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.103 synthesis (2026-08-04, verified on main). Four of the six [:>] designs name h/as-element as the recovery for the two sharpest SILENT traps at a foreign crossing: hiccup written in a PROP (which crosses as clj->js data and renders as text, no error), and a function child / render-prop body returning hiccup (React: 'Objects are not valid as a React child'). Design C's entire render-prop worked example is built on it.

VERIFIED: zero occurrences of 'as-element' anywhere under docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/. The guide's taught h/ roster is h/hicasso, h/root, h/fn, h/render, h/defhost, h/presence, h/child-key, h/boundary. arm1/lang.clj exports exactly three macros - defview, hfn, defhost - and no as-element. The MECHANISM is public as codec/as-element (front/codec.cljs:1708); the TAUGHT NAME is not.

WHY IT MATTERS: an error message naming a spelling the reader cannot call is worse than no message, and the [:>] escape is where authors meet an UNFAMILIAR component and are most likely to guess a prop's shape. Both traps are silent, so the message is the only teaching surface there is.

RESOLVE EITHER WAY, but resolve it BEFORE .103's refusal messages and guide rows are written: (a) export the taught spelling in the arm (one line) and keep every message and guide row as drafted, or (b) rule that the taught name is something else and rewrite the rows to name what the arm actually exposes. Do NOT let .103's PR be where this is discovered. Bench lane + draft-guide. No AI attribution.
notes:
WORKER PR #7523 (guide half only; NOT closing). The brief said the GUIDE teaches h/as-element; the bead's own VERIFIED line is correct and the brief was wrong — zero occurrences under draft-guide/, then and now. Every occurrence is in docs/design/hicasso/studio/** (designs A/B/C, raw-escape-spec) and decisions.md, both outside the dispatched fence.

WHAT THE GUIDE ACTUALLY HAD: 05-interop.md's :render paragraph taught a hiccup return as legal — '[:li {:on-click [:row/pick id]} title] is fine'. It is not. render-callback ends in a bare (apply f args) at front/intent.cljs:506, so the return crosses UNCONVERTED and a vector is refused by React. The only witnessed :render body returns a STRING (host_hatch_dom_cljs_test.cljs:310, :792); the one test that builds a real row wraps every return in codec/as-element explicitly (:868, :871). PR takes option (b) for the guide: says the recovery does not exist, in prose and in a Not-settled-yet row, rather than naming a spelling no reader can call.

SECOND SILENT TRAP RECORDED: hiccup at a non-callback host prop hits (coll? v) (clj->js v) at front/codec.cljs:1611 and arrives as ["h2" "Tasks"] — rendered as text, no error. refuse-undeclared-host-event! only guards on*-spelled props, so defhost reaches this today with [:>] still unbuilt. New troubleshooting row.

STILL OPEN, AND WHY THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN — two surfaces outside the fence still name the spelling:
  1. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/intent.cljs:437 — render-callback's OWN docstring writes (h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick (:id row)]} (:title row)]). The implementation names the nonexistent function to explain itself.
  2. studio/raw-escape-design-{a,b,c}.md and raw-escape-spec.md rows 8 and 9, plus decisions.md:1045.
The (a)-vs-(b) ruling the bead asks for is still unmade for the ARM: either export the spelling from arm1/lang.clj (which exports exactly defview/hfn/defhost) or rule a different name. codec/as-element is live at front/codec.cljs:1821 (bead cites :1708 — stale). Guide is now truthful under EITHER ruling, so this no longer blocks .103's messages on the guide side.
THE SOURCE OF THE as-element MYTH IS THE IMPLEMENTATION'S OWN DOCSTRING (mayor, 2026-08-05, verified on main).

WHY THIS WAS PUZZLING. Four INDEPENDENT design documents named h/as-element as the recovery for the two sharpest silent traps, and one built its entire render-prop example on it. Four designers converging on a function that does not exist is not four coincidences; something taught it to them.

IT WAS front/intent.cljs:437 - render-callback's own docstring, which writes:

    (h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick (:id row)]} (:title row)])

...to explain what a renderRow prop exists to build. A designer reading the function to understand the crossing reads that line and reasonably concludes the spelling exists. THE IMPLEMENTATION NAMED A NONEXISTENT FUNCTION TO EXPLAIN ITSELF, and every downstream document inherited it.

THE MECHANISM IS REAL; ONLY THE SPELLING IS NOT. codec.cljs:1821 does the conversion. arm1/lang.clj exports exactly defview, hfn, defhost - so no h/ spelling reaches it. (The bead cites :1708 for the mechanism; that is stale, it is :1821.)

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The bare (apply f args) at intent.cljs:506 means a :render return crosses UNCONVERTED, so a returned hiccup vector reaches React and is refused. The guide taught exactly that shape and called it "fine" - now corrected by PR #7523. The docstring is the same claim in the code, and it is still there.

NOT FIXED HERE: implementation/** was fenced (two live workers) and the (a)-vs-(b) ruling for the arm is unmade, so a rename would be premature. WHOEVER TAKES THE ARM RULING SHOULD FIX THE DOCSTRING IN THE SAME PR - it is the upstream of four documents' worth of error, and leaving it means the next reader re-derives the same wrong conclusion.

GENERAL LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a docstring that illustrates with a spelling the module does not export is a teaching surface with no gate behind it. Nothing checks that prose in a docstring names something real, and here that gap propagated into four design records and one guide page before anyone noticed.
WORKER PR #7543 (records + the upstream docstring; NOT closing).

THE ARM RULING (a)-vs-(b) IS STILL UNMADE, and it did not block this delivery.
Scope taken accordingly: stop the records asserting a function that does not
exist, say what is available and what is not, and leave the spelling to the
ruling. Nothing here invents a replacement.

FIXED THE UPSTREAM. front/intent.cljs render-callback's docstring is corrected in
the same PR - it is what taught four documents the same wrong thing, and leaving
it would have guaranteed the next reader re-derives it. DOCSTRING-ONLY: the diff
is entirely inside the string literal, no executable form changed; clj-kondo in
place reads 0 errors / 0 warnings, and CI's pinned clj-kondo job passed. The
docstring now shows the bare hiccup row, then states that the return crosses
UNCONVERTED, that codec/as-element is the conversion and is internal, that the
recovery has no author spelling (rf2-2rtt6.120), and that there is no
h/as-element - naming the propagation explicitly so the negation travels.

EVERY SITE, AND WHAT REPLACED IT.
  - decisions.md HD-024 addendum: (h/as-element [:li ...]) -> bare hiccup row;

title: tools/template's SSR scaffold declared its :root-view in the UNRESOLVED form — server and client hashed different trees
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-q1b96 (PR #7520), WHICH IS CORRECT AND STAYS. That change made ssr-ring omit the render hash for the unresolved root form (a callable-headed vector), because its canonical EDN is a constant. Three tools/template SSR tests went red on unrelated branches, asserting data-rf-render-hash is present.

THE TESTS WERE RIGHT. The template is a Reagent host — HICCUP tier — and Spec 011's hash channel is exactly its. What was wrong is the scaffold's own :root-view spelling:

  server (core_with_ssr.cljc)  (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)])   ;; reference
  client (:render-tree-fn)     (fn [] ((rf/view :app/root)))               ;; resolved tree

Those two ends can never hash the same thing. MEASURED in the emitted project: the client tree hashes a2aa3d1d, the server's unresolved root hashes f1d63f7e — the exact per-arity constant render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)]. So BEFORE rf2-q1b96 the emitted SSR scaffold shipped a hash that mismatched on EVERY page; after it, the hash is simply absent. Both are wrong for a hiccup-tier host.

This is the SECOND, SEPARABLE HAZARD rf2-q1b96's description flagged 'VERIFY BEFORE FIXING' and its close note recorded as unknown ('whether the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep reproduced'). IT REPRODUCES — tools/template is the concrete instance. Recording that here so the unknown is closed.

FIX (fenced to tools/template/**): root-view gains the outer call, ((rf/view :app/root)) — the spelling resolve-root-view's own docstring names as the hiccup tier's way to keep the channel. Byte-identical HTML; the hash returns and now equals the client's. Plus one added assertion in the emitted ssr_test.clj pinning the pairing itself: (= render-hash (rf/render-tree-hash (app/root-view))). No assertion deleted, no hash re-added to ssr-ring.

MUTATION-PROVEN: with the old form the new assertion reads (not (= "a2aa3d1d" "f1d63f7e")) and the three original failures reproduce; with the fix, both SSR emitted cells are 0 failures / 0 errors.
close_reason:
CLOSED — the fix is on main as f8e2de3025 "fix(template): the SSR scaffold's :root-view resolves, so it keeps a render hash", merged as PR #7540. Verified by reading origin/main, not inferred from the PR state.

WHAT IT ESTABLISHED, and it is the more useful half: the template's root IS hiccup-tier and SHOULD carry a hash. It was merely spelled the one way that structurally cannot have one - server (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)]), a REFERENCE; client ((rf/view :app/root)), the TREE. Measured in the emitted project: client a2aa3d1d, server f1d63f7e - the exact per-arity constant render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)].

SO THE TEMPLATE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: before rf2-q1b96 it shipped a hash that MISMATCHED ON EVERY PAGE; after, the hash was simply absent. rf2-q1b96 is vindicated - it did not over-remove, and its fix stands untouched.

TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:

1. THIS CLOSED AN UNKNOWN I HAD RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. rf2-q1b96's close said "whether the SECOND, separable hazard reproduced... WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled." The very next worker in that area found it reproduces, and tools/template was the live instance. Recording an unknown as unknown is what made that possible.

2. A FAIL-OPEN IN THE VERIFYING LANE: plain `clojure -M:test` in tools/template SKIPS the failing rows - they sit behind RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1, and the fixing worker's first run came back GREEN with the bug live. Anyone verifying that lane locally must set the env var or they get a false green. Also note the job is SURFACE-GATED and never ran on main at all, which is why main showed green while the artefact was broken.

THE NEW ASSERTION IS BETTER THAN THE ONES IT JOINS: the old rows could only say "a hash is present"; the added row asserts (= render-hash (rf/render-tree-hash (app/root-view))) - the RIGHT hash, which is the property that was silently false.

value:
CITE BY NAME, NOT BY LINE — LINE NUMBERS IN DESIGN RECORDS AND BRIEFS ROT WITHIN HOURS (established 2026-08-05, measured).

THE MEASUREMENT, not an impression: raw-escape-spec.md section 10 carried FIVE codec line numbers and THREE WERE ALREADY WRONG when a worker checked them. Same day: production-server-arm.md:205 cites "fragment-element (1420-1673)" where it is actually 1801. codec/as-element moved to :1852 - the bead said :1708, I corrected it to :1821 in a brief, and :1821 had itself stopped being true that morning. render-callback's docstring is at :565; the bead and my brief both said :437.

SO A LINE NUMBER IN A DESIGN RECORD IS A CLAIM WITH A HALF-LIFE OF HOURS on an actively edited file, and a brief that quotes one is passing on a hypothesis as a fact. I did exactly that three times today and a worker corrected each.

THE FIX THE WORKER APPLIED, and it is right: DROP THE NUMBERS AND CITE BY NAME. A symbol name survives every edit that does not rename it, and a rename is exactly the event you want a stale citation to fail on loudly rather than silently point at the wrong line.

FOR MY BRIEFS: give the SYMBOL and the FILE, never the line - and when a bead supplies a line, mark it as the bead's claim to be re-grepped rather than repeating it as established. Several workers have independently reported re-grepping and finding drift; the ones who trusted the citation wasted a lookup.

THE SAME SHAPE AS THE OTHER LESSONS TODAY: derive it rather than record it. The gap map derives its required set from needs:; the reaping rule waits for a read rather than an inference; a docstring naming a symbol is checkable where prose is not. A line number is the least derivable citation available and the first to go stale.

title: schemas-bundle gate should assert a DELTA against a Malli-free control, not an absolute ceiling
description:
Follow-on from rf2-kybsf's attribution work (measured 2026-08-05). BLOCKED ON rf2-kybsf's budget ruling.

THE STRUCTURAL DEFECT. check-schemas-bundle.cjs asserts an ABSOLUTE gzipped ceiling on two probe bundles. But the quantity Spec 010 Bundle cost actually budgets is a MARGINAL cost -- 'malli.core's reachable body (~24 KB gzipped headline)' plus 're-frame.schemas ~5.6 KB on top of malli.core'. Those are deltas. The probe's absolute size is dominated by things the budget is not about: cljs.core is 186 KB of the 494 KB raw bundle (37.6%), and re-frame.core contributes another ~150 KB raw (router 22.7, cofx 12.6, fx 12.1, classification 9.7, subs 7.8, frame 7.6, elision 7.6 ...).

Consequence: EVERY unrelated framework feature moves this gate's number. Measured proof -- between 2026-05-14 and 2026-08-05 the probe grew 80.1 -> 124.9 KB, of which Malli's marginal cost accounts for 1.0 KB (29.8 -> 30.8) and cljs.core + re-frame.core account for 43.8 KB. The gate fired at the schemas artefact for growth that happened entirely outside it. Whatever absolute constant is ruled will be wrong again within a quarter, for the same reason.

THE FIX. Add a Malli-free control build (the existing probe ns with the facade's adapter require absent, or an equivalent control ns) and assert the DELTA between control and probe against Spec 010's ~30 KB marginal budget. That is immune to core's growth and actually enforces the normative claim, which the current gate never has.

Keep an absolute backstop so core growth is not invisible -- but as a generous ratchet whose job is 'something dragged a heavy transitive ns in', not a precision budget. Core's own size is owned by the perf-bundle and bundle-isolation gates, not this one.

NOT A NARROWING. This widens what is enforced: it adds a build and pins a quantity the gate has never checked. It stops the gate failing on a quantity it was never about.

SEQUENCING. Blocked on rf2-kybsf's budget ruling -- the delta budget needs the same ruling the absolute one does, and both should land together with the check_gate_scheduling.py DISPOSITIONS entry deleted and the gate given a per-PR home under cljs_prod (47s cold, sibling test:perf-bundle is per-PR at 75s).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
BRIEF AMENDED TO THE RULED DESIGN 2026-08-05 20:00 AUSEST (rf2-kybsf ruling recorded — the blocker this bead was waiting on now exists; dep edge removed, bead is dispatchable). The ruling sharpens the description's fix in three ways; where they differ, THIS comment wins.

1. THE CONTROL IS A CORE-ONLY BUILD, NOT AN ADAPTER-STRIPPED FACADE. Description said "probe ns with the facade's adapter require absent"; ruled instead: a minimal control probe requiring re-frame.core ONLY, because the A/B must price what a consumer actually opts into — re-frame.schemas pulls the Malli adapter statically (schemas.cljc line 21), so the full schemas+adapter surface IS the opt-in cost. The counterfactual adapter-stripped build measures a posture no consumer can buy; it stays an attribution technique, not the gate.
2. REPLACE, DO NOT ADD. schemas-bundle-probe-malli is byte-identical to its sibling (5-12 B across runs; both require the same graph, the explicit adapter require is redundant). Replace it with schemas-bundle-control (init-fn touches minimal core surface; identical :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false + browser target). Two builds total, ~47s unchanged. Update the npm script, shadow-cljs.edn build entries (HOT-ZONE file — flag for mayor sequencing), the BUNDLES array, and delete probe_malli's ns.
3. ASSERT THE DELTA TWO-SIDED, NUMBERS FROM THE FIRST MATCHED RUN. (schemas-probe minus control) <= ceiling AND >= floor. Ceiling = Spec 010's marginal budget, set from the first matched A/B run + stated headroom (measured vicinity: 30.8 KB marginal; do NOT inherit 100/125 or any prior constant). Floor (~15-20 KB region, set from the same run) restores rf2-fqbcy's original strictly-larger methodology guard: a reverted facade require collapses the delta to ~5.6 KB and trips it — the in-gate structural echo of schema-implies-validation AND the gate's non-vacuity guard. The 12-byte equality guard retires with the -malli probe; the invariant's primary owner is the existing behavioural test schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_implies_validation_test.clj (hook wired + bad write fires failure) — verify it still passes, cite it in the checker comment.
UNCHANGED FROM DESCRIPTION: no generous-absolute precision budget — core size is owned elsewhere; spec/010-Schemas.md Bundle-cost prose restated as the marginal budget with the matched figures (SPEC = HOT-ZONE, mayor sequences the edit — never batch silently); CI home = new per-PR cljs-schemas-bundle job in .github/workflows/test.yml (hot-zone) surface-gated on cljs_prod, modeled on cljs-perf-bundle (same JDK/Node/Maven-only step list, own job so failures stay distinguishable in checks UI); delete test:schemas-bundle's DISPOSITIONS entry in scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py in the same PR. rf2-kybsf closes against this bead's implementation landing green.

title: test:schemas-bundle is RED: schemas probe bundle is 124.9 KB gzipped against a normative 100 KB ceiling
description:
Found by rf2-a9oic while giving the three orphaned verdict gates homes (PR for
rf2-a9oic / rf2-k78o2). The bead's filer warned: run each gate green locally
first, or you file an issue on alerting's first night. Two ran green. This one
did not.

MEASURED, cold, on origin/main (c17e9437e3), Windows, node 24, malli 0.20.1:

  npm run test:schemas-bundle   -> exit 1 in 47s

  [FAIL] schemas-bundle-probe        124.9 KB gzipped (127927 bytes)
  [FAIL] schemas-bundle-probe-malli  124.9 KB gzipped (127939 bytes)
         threshold: 100.0 KB (102400 bytes) -- over by 24.9 KB
  [OK]   schema-implies-validation guard: |delta| 12 bytes (<= 2 KB)

So the STRUCTURAL claim still holds -- both probes carry Malli, the facade
still auto-wires the adapter, schema still implies validation. What has
regressed is the ABSOLUTE budget, by 25%.

WHY NOBODY KNEW. test:schemas-bundle runs nowhere. check-schemas-bundle.cjs is
referenced by that npm script and by nothing else in the repo, so the gate has
never executed in CI since it was authored. That is precisely the class
rf2-6ckzl's audit was built to surface, and this is the audit's first real
catch rather than a bookkeeping one.

THE CLAIM THAT IS NOW FALSE, IN TWO PLACES.

  spec/010-Schemas.md 'Bundle cost' catalogues the row
    '[re-frame.schemas] required => Malli wired | ~91 KB'
  and states 'the current schemas-bundle-probe measures ~91 KB gzipped,
  within the <= 100 KB gate ceiling'.

  implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs repeats it:
    gzippedMaxBytes: 100 * 1024,   // 100 KB (empirical ~91 KB + ~9 KB headroom)

The real figure is 124.9 KB. The spec's normative budget table and the gate's
threshold comment are both stating a measurement that no longer holds.

LIKELY PROVENANCE (dates from git log, not asserted as cause):
  2026-05-12  2252f1f379  metosin/malli 0.13.0 -> 0.20.1 (rf2-zyiy, PR #468)
  2026-05-14  ce6c0f4784  the bundle-cost gate is authored (rf2-fqbcy)
  2026-06-01  d0b95fdc54  schema implies validation: the re-frame.schemas
                          facade starts :require-ing the Malli adapter
                          (rf2-v96fh) -- this is what turned the plain probe
                          from its Malli-free ~59 KB figure into a
                          Malli-carrying one, and it rewrote this gate's
                          expectations without ever running it.

Bundle composition of out/schemas-bundle-probe/probe.js (499280 raw / 127927
gz): malli.core PRESENT, malli.error PRESENT, and malli.transform /
malli.generator / malli.registry / malli.util / clojure.test.check all ABSENT.
malli.error is on Spec 010's own 'restrict to dev/test' list at ~6 KB, so it is
worth asking whether the facade is dragging the humanise path into production
-- but 6 KB does not explain 34 KB, so that is a lead, not the answer.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not 'bump the threshold'. The checker's own
failure text says it: 'if the new figures reflect a deliberate substrate
change, update the spec section first, then bump the thresholds here in
lockstep.' Spec 010's budget table is normative, so the order is a spec ruling
first and a threshold second. rf2-a9oic deliberately did NOT touch either --
narrowing a gate to make it pass is the one thing that audit exists to
prevent.

REMEDY, in order:
  1. Attribute the 34 KB. Compare against the 0.13.0 pin and against a build
     with the facade's adapter require removed, to split 'malli grew' from
     'the facade pulls more'. Decide whether malli.error belongs on the
     production path at all.
  2. Mike rules on the budget: is ~125 KB the accepted cost of
     schema-implies-validation, or is there a reduction to make first?
  3. Update spec/010-Schemas.md 'Bundle cost' -- the table row and the
     'measures ~91 KB' sentence -- to the ruled figure.
  4. Bump gzippedMaxBytes in implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs
     in lockstep, with the comment restated against the new measurement.
  5. Give test:schemas-bundle a scheduled home and delete its DISPOSITIONS
     entry in scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py. Its sibling test:perf-bundle
     is per-PR at 75s cold; this one measured 47s cold, so per-PR under the
     cljs_prod surface flag is the obvious tier.

Until step 5, scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py keeps test:schemas-bundle
declared 'unscheduled' pointing at THIS bead, with the measured red in its
why. That is the honest state: a real gate, running nowhere, red when run,
tracked.
notes:
ATTRIBUTION COMPLETE (worker, 2026-08-05, PR #7544). No threshold raised, no probe narrowed, gate still red at 124.9/100 KB. The budget ruling (remedy step 2) is still yours.

MEASURED, all gzipped, cold, malli 0.20.1:

  probe, Malli-bearing (as shipped)                124.9 KB (127917 B)
  probe, facade adapter require removed             94.1 KB (96332 B)
  => Malli marginal cost TODAY                      30.8 KB

vs the baselines rf2-fqbcy RECORDED IN ITS OWN COMMIT MESSAGE on
2026-05-14 (ce6c0f4784): probe 50.3 KB, probe-malli 80.1 KB, delta 29.8 KB.

  Malli marginal cost   29.8 -> 30.8 KB   (+1.0 KB in three months)
  cljs.core + core      50.3 -> 94.1 KB   (+43.8 KB)

SO: THE SCHEMAS SURFACE DID NOT REGRESS. Malli's marginal cost is flat
and sits inside Spec 010's own ~24 KB malli.core + ~5.6 KB schemas
(~29.6 KB) claim. The normative claim is CONFIRMED by measurement. The
entire overage is framework growth underneath the probe -- cljs.core is
186.0 KB of the 494 KB raw bundle (37.6%), re-frame.core ~150 KB raw
(router 22.7, cofx 12.6, fx 12.1, classification 9.7, subs 7.8, frame
7.6, elision 7.6 ...).

THE MALLI BUMP IS EXCLUDED, BY DATE. 0.13.0 -> 0.20.1 landed 2026-05-12
(2252f1f379). ce6c0f4784 is 2026-05-14 and already pins 0.20.1 in
shadow-cljs.edn. The 80.1 KB baseline was taken AFTER the bump, so the
bump cannot explain growth measured against it. The +1.0 KB row confirms
it independently. This bead's prime suspect does not survive.

WHERE THE CEILING CAME FROM (this is the real story). rf2-fqbcy lifted
100/125 KB verbatim from Spec 010's REPRESENTATIVE-APP harness rows (a
Reagent/React counter: 97.2 / 120.8 KB) and applied them to a BARE PROBE
measuring 50.3/80.1 KB. Its commit message says the figures are not
commensurable: 'probes are minimal -- no reagent/react overhead so the
absolute figures are smaller than the spec rows'. ~50 KB of unexamined
slack, no relationship between measured and asserted.

Then rf2-v96fh made BOTH probes Malli-bearing and, instead of adopting
the Malli-bearing 125 KB ceiling ALREADY IN THE FILE, LOWERED the
Malli-bearing probe to the Malli-FREE 100 KB one, citing a '~91 KB
empirical' figure no run ever produced. A transcription inversion that
nothing contradicted for 83 days because the gate had no home.

(Curio, not a recommendation: left at its original 125 KB, today's
124.9 KB would pass by 73 bytes. That is an argument AGAINST absolute
ceilings on this probe, not for 125.)

RECOMMENDATION. Spec 010's budget needs no loosening -- 30.8 vs ~29.6 KB.
What needs ruling is what the GATE asserts. Filed rf2-v4o7e (blocked on
this bead): assert the DELTA against a Malli-free control build, with a
generous absolute ratchet behind it. Immune to core growth, and it
enforces the normative claim the gate has never checked. If you want a
holding number instead: 135 KB (today + ~8%), explicitly not a budget.

malli.error IS on the production path (12.0 KB optimized; the adapter
requires it for :schemas/humanize-explain!) and Spec 010's own
restrict-to-dev/test list says it should not be. Real, feeds your
ruling -- but ~4 KB gzipped against 24.9 KB over, already inside the
80.1 KB baseline, and removing it changes Ruling A's surface. Untouched.

LANDED IN PR #7544: only the false measured claims. spec/010's '~91 KB
within the <= 100 KB ceiling' -> the measured +30.8 KB margin; the
'~91 KB | ~+0-30 KB' table row (incoherent against its own 91.7 KB
baseline) -> the harness-measured 120.8 KB | +29.1 KB it replaced; the
stale '~59 KB' guard figure; and the checker comment, which now carries
the measured history and tells the next reader how to attribute a rise
instead of bumping. gzippedMaxBytes UNTOUCHED.

check_gate_scheduling.py's 'unscheduled' disposition is accurate and
stays -- do not schedule this gate while it is red (remedy step 5 still
waits on steps 2-4).
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-05: I REPORTED THIS AS A 25% BUNDLE REGRESSION. IT IS NOT A REGRESSION AT ALL, and my attribution trail disproved itself.

WHAT I SAID: that malli 0.13.0 -> 0.20.1 on 2026-05-12 was the likely cause of a 124.9 KB probe against a 100 KB ceiling.

WHY THAT WAS IMPOSSIBLE, from the dates I supplied myself: malli 0.20.1 landed 05-12; the gate was authored 05-14; ce6c0f4784's shadow-cljs.edn already pins 0.20.1. THE BASELINE WAS MEASURED AFTER THE BUMP, so the bump cannot explain growth measured against it. Measured anyway: malli's marginal cost moved 29.8 -> 30.8 KB in three months. PLUS ONE KILOBYTE.

WHAT ACTUALLY GREW: cljs.core and re-frame.core, not the schemas surface. cljs/core.cljs alone is 186.0 KB of a 494 KB raw bundle - 37.6%. SPEC 010'S NORMATIVE CLAIM IS CONFIRMED, NOT VIOLATED: it predicts ~24 KB malli.core plus ~5.6 KB schemas, about 29.6 KB; the measurement is 30.8 KB.

HOW THE CEILING GOT WRONG, and it is a two-step transcription error nobody could see: rf2-fqbcy lifted the 100/125 KB pair from Spec 010's REAGENT/REACT COUNTER-APP HARNESS rows and applied them to a BARE PROBE then measuring 50.3 KB - its own commit message says the figures are not commensurable. Then rf2-v96fh made both probes malli-bearing and, instead of adopting the 125 KB MALLI-BEARING ceiling ALREADY IN THE FILE, LOWERED it to the 100 KB MALLI-FREE one, citing an "empirical ~91 KB" figure NO RUN EVER PRODUCED. An inversion, unchallenged for 83 days BECAUSE THE GATE HAD NO HOME.

THE NUMBER THAT SETTLES IT: left at its original 125 KB, today's 124.9 KB would pass BY 73 BYTES. That is an argument against absolute ceilings on this probe, not an argument for 125.

WHAT THE WORKER CORRECTLY DID NOT DO: it did not raise ggzippedMaxBytes (still 100 * 1024, gate still exits 1) and it did not narrow the probe. It fixed only measurably false statements in spec/010 and the checker's comment, and filed rf2-v4o7e proposing the gate assert the DELTA against a malli-free control with a generous absolute ratchet behind it - immune to core growth, and enforcing the claim this gate has never actually checked.

THE LESSON FOR ME: I passed on a bead's attribution trail as though it were evidence. The dates in it contradicted the conclusion, and I did not check them before briefing. A trail is a hypothesis; the worker measured instead, and the measurement inverted the story.
