title: hicasso SSR: defhost :ssr has NO value that renders CHILDREN — a provider crossing deletes its subtree from the server render
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103, docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-design-c-ergonomics.md, section 'Needs a ruling' R1). Not the escape's defect — defhost's, which the escape inherits.

THE SHAPE. mint-host-gate! (front/codec.cljs) walks the declaration's :ssr fallback into a SINGLE element once, at the declaration, and the gate returns THAT element when unadopted:

    (let [placeholder (when (some? fallback) (as-element fallback))
          gate (fn [props]
                 (if (useSyncExternalStore ...)
                   (react/createElement component props)
                   placeholder))]

props is ignored on the unadopted branch, so props.children is DROPPED. :client-only (fallback nil) renders nothing; {:fallback hiccup} renders that hiccup INSTEAD of the children.

WHY IT MATTERS. For a LEAF widget (a chart, a date picker) dropping children is right — there are none. For a TRANSPARENT WRAPPER it deletes the application. A context provider contributes no markup of its own and exists solely to carry a subtree, so a provider at a crossing renders NOTHING server-side and takes every descendant with it. The server sends an empty document and the whole page appears after hydration.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The draft guide's own provider example is exactly this shape — 05-interop.md:120, '(h/defhost themed (.-Provider some-context))' — and it has no :ssr option, so it takes the :client-only default. Providers are also one of HD-011's five NAMED use cases for the raw escape (decisions.md ~:412-421), so the escape has no recovery either: [:>] carries no declaration, so its only answer to 'my provider vanished server-side' is 'declare it', and declaring it does not help.

RULING NEEDED. The 2026-08-04 :ssr ruling (rf2-2rtt6.85) says TWO VALUES and 'there is no third value', and mint-host!/declared-ssr enforce that at the declaration. Either:
(a) a THIRD value exists — :ssr :children (or :transparent): render props.children in place of the component until adoption. One extra row in a table the guide already has; the honest reading of what a transparent wrapper IS; and
(b) providers are ruled OUT of SSR and 10-server-side-rendering.md + 05-interop.md's Providers section say so in terms.

DESIGN C RECOMMENDS (a). Without it the provider use case has no recovery at any crossing form.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation: [:>] inherits whatever defhost's answer is, and clause 6 (renders nothing) is unchanged either way.
notes:
DECISION INPUT FROM rf2-nv07k (mayor, 2026-08-05) — THE FALLBACK ASYMMETRY CONSTRAINS THIS RULING BOTH WAYS, so its worker deliberately took no position and stopped. Read this before ruling on :ssr.

THE ASYMMETRY IS NOT A RULE, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF ONE. A fallback is walked into an element ONCE, at the declaration, outside any frame. So what gets refused is exactly what that walk can EVALUATE: an intent vector, a sub call in the form, non-hiccup. A boundary head is neither - it is an element whose body runs later - so THE WALK NEVER LOOKS INSIDE IT. The bead's framing that "the rule is simply narrower than it reads" is generous; it is not narrower, it is about a different thing.

TWO FACTS THAT WERE NOT ON THE RECORD AND THAT DECIDE IT:

1. THE DECLARED PLACEHOLDER IS NOT A VALUE. One declaration, walked once into one element, renders ALPHA in frame A, BRAVO in frame B, and ALPHA-TWO after a write. mint-host-gate!'s OWN justification for walking once is "a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder" - and that justification is FALSIFIED BY WHAT IT PERMITS.

2. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE ARM'S OWN OTHER BOUNDARY VARIANT. mint-frame-prop-view! (rf2-2rtt6.39) reads intent/*frame* at ELEMENT-CREATION time, which in a fallback is mint time, where the var is nil. It bakes nil in and throws mid-server-render. So whether a boundary head in a fallback works is a property of WHICH MINT THE HEAD CAME FROM - which is not a rule an author can hold in their head. That removes "bless it as it stands" from the table.

HOW IT CONSTRAINS THIS BEAD, BOTH DIRECTIONS: refusing the defview head deletes l0wfx's ONLY recovery and empties candidate D, whose content IS that workaround - favouring A or B. Blessing it sanctions "write your subtree twice" - favouring D. Either direction pre-empts this P1, which is why its worker took no ruling.

THE EVIDENCE HAS A DIRECTION AND IT WAS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the codec's own law - walk once, reuse everywhere, BECAUSE a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder - ENTAILS OPTION (b), INERT MARKUP. And that removes the only thing people can do today. Its worker's recommendation: this should probably be ruled TOGETHER WITH rf2-l0wfx rather than ahead of it.

WHAT LANDED MEANWHILE (PR #7525): docstrings only on the executable side - every changed codec.cljs line is inside a docstring literal, no executable form changed, no hook added. The new arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs is written as A RECORD OF TODAY, NOT A CONTRACT, so it does not entrench either answer before you rule.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:02 AUSEST (delegated review pass, dossier ai/decisions/rf2-l0wfx.ssr-transparent-children.md — now deleted; operator-overturnable). Ruled TOGETHER with rf2-nv07k as one coupled ruling.

THE RULING: a third :ssr value EXISTS and it is :ssr :render — not :children/:transparent. Paired with nv07k's (b'): fallbacks become genuinely inert, boundary/host heads refused at mint. Option (b) (providers ruled out of SSR) is DEAD — it contradicts the operator's 2026-08-04 required-scope SSR ruling, and providers are an HD-011 NAMED use case (decisions.md ~:415, "providers an ecosystem library hands you").

WHY NOT :children (the dossier's main rec — REFUTED on the repo's own measured record, defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md + the dossier's Codex section, claims verified against codec.cljs and React 19.2.0 installed):
1. WRONG BYTES: :children renders the subtree with NO provider above it, so every consumer reads the context DEFAULT (measured: "unset" vs "dark", costing doc candidate-A control + Codex's independent run — same result). Server HTML under the wrong theme/locale/auth/route. Silent-absent becomes silent-wrong.
2. REMOUNT AT ADOPTION: the gate's client snapshot is constant true (codec.cljs gate-adopted), so adoption fires right after hydration, and the position's type swaps children->Provider(children). React reconciles by type at position: the whole just-hydrated subtree is destroyed and rebuilt (react.dev preserving-and-resetting-state; witnessed in-kind by the green fallback-swap row). Every provider wrapping the app root remounts the app immediately after hydrating it.
3. UNVERIFIABLE ASSERTION: :children on a non-transparent wrapper emits HTML structurally unlike the client render, and both passes agree so nothing reports it.
The "zero-mismatch" argument for :children covers hydration pass 1 only; it is true and beside the point — the defects are the bytes and the post-hydration swap.

:ssr :render CONDUCT (exact): the declaration asserts "this component is safe to render on the server". declared-ssr accepts the bare keyword :render as the third policy. For :render, mint-host! mints NO GATE — the head's "gate" slot carries the foreign component itself (HD-011's original zero-wrapper/zero-fiber/zero-hook shape restored for this policy; do not stamp displayName onto the foreign object, the head map already carries it). Same component, same props (host-entry walk unchanged), same children run on the server, on hydration's first pass, and on a fresh createRoot mount. SYMMETRY: one tree everywhere — server HTML, hydration pass and fresh mount render the SAME element type with the same props/context/children, so zero mismatch by identity, no snapshot pair, no adoption event, no swap, NO REMOUNT. For the case that filed this bead the assertion is trivially true: a Context.Provider is React's own component and the server renderer fully supports context — consumers below read the DECLARED value in the server HTML (the costing doc's "dark" control becomes the contract).

SPELLING justification (one sentence): :render names both the conduct (the component renders) and the assertion (server-safe to render) — where :children/:transparent assert an unverifiable structural property and deliver wrong-context bytes. :children, :transparent, :passthrough, :server STAY REFUSED (:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy; the no-ssr-value-expresses witness keeps those rows, drops :render). :client-only stays the DEFAULT — the conservative reason in the .85 addendum stands; :render is the author saying, never the door guessing (costing-doc candidate C stays rejected on exactly that law).

CHILDREN / FRAME BINDING (.74 composition, verified): children are lowered in the CALLER's body inside its render window (host-element/make-element run there), so intents in them close over the caller's frame-locked dispatch and a frame-fed head among them gets rfFrame baked in the caller's body (codec.cljs boundary-element :1550; mark-frame-prop!'s own docstring: a foreign component between two Hicasso boundaries passes children through with the prop already in them). :render changes ONLY the element type; the children path is today's adopted-arm path, byte-identical. Composes.

[:>] (clause 6 UNCHANGED): the escape carries no declaration, so no server-safety assertion to carry — it renders nothing server-side, and it must never grow an :ssr spelling of its own (raw-escape-spec standing instruction unchanged). The answer to "my provider vanished server-side" becomes "declare it: (h/defhost themed (.-Provider ctx) {:ssr :render})" — which now actually works.

NV07K HALF (b', ruled here, cross-ref on that bead): with :render the write-your-subtree-twice workaround is unnecessary, so the mint walks the declared fallback hiccup STRUCTURALLY and refuses any boundary head (boundary-head?) or host head (host-head?) at any position — new error id :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head, naming the host, the offending head's displayName and its position; recovery: a fallback is inert markup — write plain hiccup, or declare :ssr :render and render the real subtree. This catches the frame-fed nil-bake variant for free (it is a boundary head), deleting the per-mint inconsistency, and restores the walk-once law's own justification (a placeholder that differs per site/write is not a placeholder).

WITNESS LIST (both halves):
- provider crossing under :ssr :render round-trips server->hydration: server HTML contains the subtree AND a consumer below reads the DECLARED value (not the default); hydration attaches with zero React error-channel traffic (the existing (is (empty? seen)) pattern) and no extra child mount.
- host_ssr_dom_cljs_test: refusal row keeps :server refused; gains the :render acceptance + a server-render CHILDREN row (today's only children-through-the-door row runs post-adoption — costing-doc bill).
- arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test FLIPS from record-of-today to CONTRACT: defview-head, defhost-head and frame-fed rows all assert :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head at mint; intent/sub/non-hiccup rows unchanged.
- ssr/ fixture corpus row for :render; pinned byte budgets move accordingly (bill).

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (one worker, same gate region, ~23 co-edits per costing-doc bill, Hicasso bench lane ONLY):
- front/codec.cljs: declared-ssr third arm; mint-host! no-gate branch for :render; fallback structural refusal; update SSR policy comment ("TWO VALUES"->three), mint-host!/host-ssr docstrings ("enforced by the gate" -> "enforced by which TYPE the declaration mints").
- arm1/lang.clj defhost docstring ("There is no third value").
- Tests per witness list + arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test boundary-count row restated, ssr/driver.cjs + bake_bytes budgets.
- decisions.md: NEW DATED ADDENDUM under HD-011 (digtt pattern — SAME PR as implementation), amending the 2026-08-04 .85 addendum: three values; record that the two-value ruling pre-dated the provider witness; conservative default stands; optionally the stale HD-020(d) "inert in v0" line.
- Guides: draft-guide/05-interop.md — Providers section teaches {:ssr :render} on the themed example (NOTE: example is at ~:153 under ## Providers, the :120 citation in this bead is stale per costing doc §3) + Defaults table SSR cell + Not-settled row; draft-guide/10-server-side-rendering.md — policy block gains the third line + prose + troubleshooting rows ("window is not defined under :render -> the assertion is false; use :client-only or {:fallback}" and the fallback boundary-head refusal); draft-guide/11-performance.md :ssr sample. mkdocs --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** — worker verifies anchors + table column counts by hand and says so in the PR body; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py is the gate that runs.
- studio/raw-escape-spec.md comparison table + R2; production-server-arm.md pieces table + codec line-range citation; EP-0038 R5 status line.
- FREEHAND DOOR: NO edits — v/defhost's "counted, not walked" projection rationale (the JVM never executes the React component) genuinely cannot support :render and does not transfer; the two doors honestly diverge (costing doc §bill). Spec 009/011 take zero edits (they say nothing about this door).
- Browser lane: the remount claim is reasoned-from-law, not DOM-measured (costing doc caveat); the :render hydration row in the browser lane is the closing measurement.

RECORDED HONESTLY — what :render does NOT solve: a provider whose VALUE is genuinely client-only (window-derived) still has no server story; its value prop is computed in the caller's body, so the host stays :client-only or takes a fallback and is client-only below. No candidate solved that case (:children would render it under the DEFAULT value = silent-wrong).

title: RULING NEEDED: validation.md's stated ship bar and the operative mount gate disagree
description:
FOUND by the HD-013 CREATIVE ADVISORY PASS (2026-08-04) and verified in tree by the mayor before filing. This is a RULING REQUEST, not a dispatch: nobody may change a stated ship bar from a docs brief.

THE DISCREPANCY, both sides quoted.

docs/design/hicasso/validation.md line 9, under "## The bar (HD-012)", still states:
  "Ship bar (clock): mount AND bulk view-work <= 1.0x Reagent, like-for-like - both sides reading re-frame2 subscriptions - on the witness shapes. The only ship number."

The operative mount gate carried on this bead since the 2026-08-02 amendment is one line: the codec inside 1.10x of DIRECT UIx on M1. The creative pass reports that the amendment explicitly REJECTED keeping <= 1.0x Reagent and named a consistency edit to validation.md; that edit does not appear in the file.

WHY IT WAS NOT SIMPLY DISPATCHED. The bead the amendment points at for validation.md edits, rf2-hvl5s, is CLOSED and was scoped to the COMPONENT BUDGET ROWS (shell / per-edge / per-unique-key, PR #7319) - not to the bar. So the ship-bar consistency edit has no owner, and picking one of the two texts as authoritative is a governance act on an operator-owned standard. The mayor declined to make it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The P2 fork ruling is pending and both HD-013 advisory passes are recorded on this bead. A programme whose written bar and operative bar disagree cannot have its fork adjudicated cleanly against either: a stop or a continue ruled against <= 1.0x Reagent means something different from one ruled against <= 1.10x direct UIx. The adversarial pass independently found that K3 is the only criterion the programme can currently adjudicate and that the fork question "is not currently answerable on its own terms"; this is one of the reasons why.

WHAT IS NEEDED: an operator ruling on which text is the bar, and then a worker to make the losing text agree with it. Two candidate dispositions, neither endorsed here - (a) validation.md is stale and is amended to the 1.10x-of-UIx line the amendment ruled; (b) the amendment was narrower than the creative pass reads it and validation.md stands, in which case the amendment's scope should be stated on this bead so the next reader does not re-derive the conflict.

DO NOT DISPATCH A DOCS WORKER AT THIS UNTIL IT IS RULED. Changing a ship bar by inference is precisely the failure mode HD-013 reserves to the operator.
notes:
MATERIAL REFINEMENT from the rf2-0qj9w quiet window (mayor, 2026-08-04) - the two texts may not be RIVALS at all, which changes the shape of this decision.

I have been framing this bead as "two ship-bar texts disagree on a THRESHOLD - which is authoritative?". The measurement worker read both and found they differ in DENOMINATOR:

  - K1's own row at validation.md:557 is REAGENT-denominated: "Mount > Reagent on the reference list+form".
  - The rf2-2rtt6.1 amendment's 1.10x is UIX-denominated: "mount <= 1.10x direct UIx-on-subs".

And validation.md:267 states the win condition CONJUNCTIVELY - "<= 1.0x Reagent-on-subs ... WITH the codec inside 1.10x of direct UIx".

So a reading on which BOTH hold simultaneously is available and may be the intended one, rather than one text superseding the other. That is a different question from the one this bead currently poses, and it should be settled before either line is treated as the operative gate.

NOTHING CURRENTLY DEPENDS ON THE ANSWER. The window's M1 row REFUSED on its control, so no bar was transcribed in either denominator and no published row rests on this. The decision is therefore unblocked-but-unforced.

title: STANDARD: the Hicasso bar, budgets, and kill criteria (operator-owned)
description:
The operator-owned governance record for EP-0038 (the lbs3y pattern; rf2-lbs3y is the retired predecessor standard). Workers append measurements; only the operator (or an explicitly recorded delegation) amends the numbers.

THE BAR (HD-012): ship = mount AND bulk view-work <= 1.0x Reagent, like-for-like (both sides on re-frame2 subs), CLOCK ONLY as the ship number; memory first-class via kill rules (K3 + UIx material-cost). ALL BAR NUMBERS ARE BROWSER NUMBERS (:advanced, real browser); JVM/Node = diagnostic only. Architecture-kill: bulk > 1.5x after two serious runtime iterations.

RED-ZONES (set when P0 publishes, BEFORE candidate results open): one UIx clock ratio + one UIx retained-heap ratio per witness family; a red row needs an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit; silence is not a pass; the donor-gate 'acceptably close' is judged against these.

BUDGETS: <=2 runtime/shell hooks per product boundary (scalar comparator exempt, priced by the 1/3/7/20 ladder); ~0.4-0.5KB exclusive retained target (>1KB paper-fail); ViewCell-class object graph = failed spike; per-read tier-3 survival metric = steady-state allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20 reads + zero retained per-occurrence objects after commit/teardown; per-keystroke path stated (4-field form + 100-cell grid) with sub-recompute localization; template identity named for any cached shape work.

HD-002 ADJUDICATION (pin before P1 code): (a) render/commit ownership state machine for the collector (candidate reads survive winning renders, vanish on abandon/replay/teardown; needing the forbidden candidate ledger = immediate tripwire); (b) the exact allowed edge-diff op vs the forbidden ledger class; (c) two pre-registered collector strategy hypotheses, counted only by benchmarked commits; (d) tripwire OVERRIDES the clock.

KILL CRITERIA K1-K7 + the six-week clock (starts at the first Hicasso-arm commit that mounts the dogfood screen; P0/donor/paper are off-clock) per docs/design/hicasso/validation.md. DECIDERS (HD-013): donor gate = delegated advisory ruling (adversarial+creative pass vs the published P0 table, recorded here, operator-overturnable); P2 fork = THE OPERATOR, advised by recorded reviews. Adapters-only is a successful outcome.

P0 BASELINE TABLE lives here + docs/design/hicasso/studio/: Reagent-on-subs mount/bulk, ratom write+flush, UIx-on-subs, the 1/3/7/20 ladder, and the W1 carry-over (~2.99-3.08x floor / ~1.9-2.0x Reagent, already resolved in docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md appendix — no re-litigation).

=== DELEGATED RULINGS (mayor, 2026-07-30, on Mike's explicit 'accept your recommendation and proceed'). OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE. Recorded here because this bead is the governance record and silence is not a pass. ===

RULING 1 — THE RED-ZONE RULE, so P0 publishing does not stall Wave-1.
The standard requires red-zones set when P0 publishes, BEFORE candidate results open, and rf2-2rtt6.4 names UIx as the arm they are set from. Numbers cannot be pre-stated because P0 has not run, so the operator supplies a RULE instead:

  RED-ZONE THRESHOLD = THE MEASURED UIx RATIO FOR THAT WITNESS FAMILY, on both axes (clock, retained heap).
  A candidate row WORSE THAN UIx on either axis is RED.
  A red row needs an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit. Silence is still not a pass.

  THE SHIP BAR IS UNCHANGED: mount AND bulk <= 1.0x Reagent, like-for-like, clock only as the ship number. Red is not fail — red is 'needs a waiver'. The two are independent: a row can clear the bar and still be red (if UIx beats Reagent), and that is the intended tension.

  RATIONALE. UIx is the frontier comparator: the best existing React-idiomatic option on re-frame2 subs. A native view layer that cannot match it has no case — that is precisely the lbs3y lesson, where the predecessor sat ~5x Reagent and was withdrawn. Deriving the threshold from the measurement rather than from a guessed constant also means nobody has to defend a number invented before the data.

  MECHANICAL, SO NO WORKER NEEDS TO ASK: when rf2-2rtt6.4 publishes its UIx rows, those figures ARE the red-zones. Append them to this bead's table labelled as such. No further operator input required to proceed.

RULING 2 — HD-002 ADJUDICATION IS A DELEGATED ADVISORY, not an operator gate tonight.
The standard requires HD-002 pinned before P1 code: (a) the render/commit ownership state machine for the collector, (b) the exact allowed edge-diff op vs the forbidden ledger class, (c) two pre-registered collector strategy hypotheses counted only by benchmarked commits, (d) the tripwire.

  This is delegated to a dedicated worker producing a written adjudication into docs/design/hicasso/, recorded on this bead, ADVERSARIALLY REVIEWED, and OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE — the same pattern HD-013 already uses for the donor gate.

  RATIONALE. It is deep design, not a coin-flip, and it should be argued on paper by someone who has read HD-002 properly rather than ruled from the mayor's chair. It gates only the tournament arms (rf2-2rtt6.9, rf2-2rtt6.10), which are post-donor-gate and start the six-week clock, so there is time to do it properly.

  NOT URGENT TONIGHT: P0 (.2/.3/.4/.5), the draft guide (.6) and the donor-gate measurement (.7) all run without it.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY THE OPERATOR'S: the P2 fork (HD-013 — 'THE OPERATOR, advised by recorded reviews'), and any waiver for a red row. Neither is reachable tonight.

=== TWO THINGS FOR THE OPERATOR (surfaced, not decided) ===

(1) ON RETAINED HEAP, UIx IS NOT THE FRONTIER — IT INVERTS. RULING 1 derives
    the red-zone from UIx because UIx is the frontier comparator. That holds on
    the sub-free shell (212 B vs Reagent's 431 B, 0.49x) and REVERSES on reads
    (3,550 vs 942, 3.77x worse), with the crossover below a SINGLE read. A
    per-read red-zone taken from UIx is therefore 3.77x looser than the best
    measured option: a candidate could clear it comfortably while being worse
    than the Reagent adapter that already ships. The rule as written stands and
    is applied above; whether the memory red-zone should instead be the
    per-axis BEST is the operator's call. 942 B/read is what a native layer
    actually has to beat.

(2) THE ~0.4-0.5 KB EXCLUSIVE-RETAINED BUDGET IS A SHELL BUDGET. Both donors
    clear it sub-free (212 / 431 B). NOTHING MEASURED MEETS IT FOR A BOUNDARY
    THAT READS ONCE: UIx 3,811 B (7.6x the 1 KB paper-fail line), Reagent
    1,565 B (1.6x). The budget table in validation.md wants a per-read row
    beside the per-boundary one; the honest anchor for it is 942 B/read.
    Derived target for HD-002's grouped tier: grouping can only remove the HOOK
    half of a read, so its floor is ~Reagent's 942 B and the prize is ~2,600 B
    per read — ~18 KB on the census's seven-read archetype. That is a concrete
    pre-registered number for clause (c).

=== HD-002 ADJUDICATION (delegated advisory, worker, 2026-07-30). OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE. Per RULING 2 above. Full text: docs/design/hicasso/hd-002-adjudication.md (PR #7261). Adversarial review pending. ===

All four clauses pinned. Ordered tripwire-first because the tripwire overrides the clock. Every claim in the document is marked RULED (the record says it) / DERIVED (follows from quoted normative text) / INFERRED (my conclusion from React or re-frame2 semantics) / OPEN (cannot be adjudicated; what would settle it is named).

(d) THE TRIPWIRE — one question a worker applies at the moment they reach for a data structure: "does anything I am about to write need to survive from one render attempt to a DIFFERENT render attempt of the same boundary, or need to be told apart from another render attempt's version of itself?" Yes = candidate ledger = the collector has LOST, regardless of clock. Six mechanical checks (a second candidate slot; anything keyed by render/attempt/lane/generation id; render-phase mutation of shared state; commit-phase re-read of sub VALUES; a per-read object required for CORRECTNESS; a registry of in-flight renders). Tripwire vs budget failure is NECESSITY vs COST: needed-for-correctness is fatal on sight, merely expensive is measured and survivable. On firing: stop collector work, record the construct + the correctness obligation + the commit SHA on rf2-2rtt6.9 and here, arm continues on grouped. A firing kills the TIER, not the arm and not the programme. Operator may waive; default is loss; silence is not a pass.

(b) THE BOUNDARY — allowed: ONE operation, commit-phase only. Symmetric difference over sub-keys between the committed sequence P and the candidate sequence N; add/remove edges on the shared index; then P := N. Three constraints keep it out of the ledger class: (1) THE COMMIT DOES NOT DEREF — zero subscription values read at commit; the generation fence (O(1) per boundary) replaces the predecessor per-read commit-side re-read, measured at 1.19ms of a 4.0ms write for 300 reads against Reagent 1.4us for its entire layout phase; (2) ALLOCATION IS PROPORTIONAL TO THE CHANGE, NEVER TO THE READ COUNT — this is the standard warm-1/3/7/20 survival metric seen from the other side; they are the same statement, and a collector satisfying one but failing the other has an instrument bug; (3) the unchanged case must be detectable without building anything. NEAREST ALLOWED: a per-boundary reused scratch buffer overwritten unconditionally each render (the closest allowed construct to the fence); the retained committed set P; a generation counter compared once per render; ONE candidate slot. NEAREST FORBIDDEN: a SECOND candidate slot (one line from the allowed buffer, and the definitional case); any map keyed by render/attempt/generation over read sets; per-read records (the predecessor five-key :observations maps); commit-phase value re-read; a root registry of in-flight renders; a content HASH of the read set used to decide "unchanged" (a collision is a silently missing edge and therefore a stale boundary, not a slow one — a device whose failure mode is wrongness).

(a) THE OWNERSHIP STATE MACHINE — four states (UNMOUNTED / RENDERING / PENDING / COMMITTED) reduced to ONE invariant: no render-phase code mutates anything outside the boundary own single candidate slot; the index is mutated ONLY in the commit phase. THE MACHINE DOES NOT DETECT ABANDONED RENDERS, IT MAKES THEM COSTLESS — an abandoned render needs no cleanup because it never did anything that needs cleaning. Abandon and replay are both PENDING to RENDERING, where the unconditional top-of-render reset destroys the prior candidate by overwrite (the reset must be unconditional, or StrictMode double-invoke concatenates two renders worth of reads). PENDING to nothing (tree discarded) leaves the index describing the last COMMITTED render, which is what is on screen; a boundary whose first render is abandoned never had index membership at all. Teardown removes P edges (the standing zero-leaked-refcount assertion). Forced consequence, INFERRED and NOT collector-specific: render-time reads must not acquire — warm reads are pure derefs, cold reads use subscribe-once semantics (acquire and release both complete inside the render, so abandonment leaves nothing behind), and acquisition happens at commit. useSyncExternalStore has the same shape, so grouped and the scalar comparator inherit the identical constraint: SHARED FRONT-HALF CONCERN, CHARGE IT TO NOBODY.

(c) TWO PRE-REGISTERED HYPOTHESES — both inside the allowed operation, differing only on WHERE unchanged-case detection happens (the sole strategic axis the operation leaves open). H1 COMMIT-SIDE ORDERED COMPARE: fill the scratch in read order; at commit compare length then pairwise, falling through to the diff on mismatch. Predicts ZERO BYTES steady-state commit allocation on the 300-boundary bulk witness and a FLAT allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20; the clock prediction is directional only (not worse than grouped) because no P0 baseline exists to state a number against. H2 RENDER-SIDE POSITIONAL VERIFICATION: each (sub q) verifies itself positionally against P as it reads, setting a divergence flag; the commit is O(1) and independent of k when the flag is clear; yields allocation-free RENDERS, not merely allocation-free commits. Falsified if the render leg rises by more than the commit leg falls at k=7 and k=20 — directional, needs no P0 number. Risk asymmetry recorded: H2 loads the hot render path the predecessor measured at 0.77-0.86ms per 300 reads. COUNTING RULE: a hypothesis is CONSUMED only by a commit implementing it PLUS a bench row citing that SHA and its repro command — both halves, or it is not consumed. Tuning passes consume nothing and un-consume nothing. An abandoned implementation that produced no bench row leaves the hypothesis unconsumed, but the attempt is recorded (an unrecorded abandonment is how two swings quietly become five). Both consumed and neither meeting the survival metric means the collector loses, grouped stays default, and there is no third hypothesis without an explicit operator ruling — the same grammar HD-014 uses for the clock: never silently. A TRIPWIRE FIRING CONSUMES NOTHING AND ENDS THE TIER; it overrides the count as it overrides the clock.

SETTLED — the gap the rf2-2rtt6.6 draft guide flagged (HD-016 calls helper-donated reads "collector-contingent" and never states the GROUPED answer). VERDICT: NO, an inlined helper cannot read under grouped — DERIVED from HD-002 own words ("one fixed hook receiving the COMPLETE QUERY COLLECTION BEFORE THE BODY"; a helper queries are not knowable before the body, since the body must run to reach the helper). That is stronger ground than the guide React-hook-rules inference. Supporting: HD-020 budget is already fully consumed, so a helper calling use-subs is a third hook in the boundary. NOTE the guide inference slightly overstates React — a helper called unconditionally and exactly once, itself calling use-subs unconditionally, IS a custom hook by React own definition and React would permit it; the "before the body" clause is what forbids it, not React. ALSO NAMED (INFERRED, and no new API since it is only data): grouped answer for helpers that need reads is a QUERY-CONTRIBUTING helper returning a query-map fragment the caller merges into its single use-subs call. FAIRNESS CONSEQUENCE FOR rf2-2rtt6.9: if the dogfood screen grouped rendering is written as "helpers read nothing, pass values down" while the collector rendering gets free helper reads, the ergonomics half of the verdict runs with one hand tied and the collector wins a point it did not earn. RECOMMENDATION: the grouped rendering exercises query-contributing helpers explicitly, and the diff comparison notes where they were used.

NOT ADJUDICATED (3), each with what would settle it. (1) Whether ONE generation fence covers what the predecessor commit-side deref compared with THREE fields (node-key, version, frame/registry epoch). architecture.md asserts it and names the staged-stale CI witness as its guard; the record does not demonstrate it and it cannot be verified on paper. If it is wrong, clause (b) is under-specified rather than merely fast. SETTLED BY: the staged-stale witness PLUS an adversarial witness that changes a subscription VALUE between a boundary render and its commit WITHIN ONE GENERATION and asserts the committed DOM is not stale — filed as an obligation before the fast path is trusted; if it cannot be constructed, record why, because that is itself the answer. (2) The cold-read double-compute cost (uncached compute at render, then compute again at commit acquisition; three times under StrictMode). SETTLED BY: a cold-read counter reported on the 100-cell grid and keyed insert/delete/reorder witnesses — rare flips make it noise, common flips make it a genuine collector-specific charge belonging in the tier comparison rather than the shared front half. (3) Clock predictions for both hypotheses, OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION until P0 publishes — allocation numbers are pre-registered because zero is absolute, but no clock number can honestly be pre-registered against an unbuilt bar, and inventing one is exactly the failure mode pre-registration exists to prevent. SETTLED BY: the P0 baseline table on this bead; restating the directional predictions as ratios against the published UIx red-zones is mechanical and does NOT consume a swing.

AUDIT PR #7261 — adversarial review of the delegated HD-002 advisory found a material correctness contradiction; update this exact governance owner, no duplicate. The allowed "single candidate slot" cannot establish concurrent React ownership. If the reused scratch/candidate is shared, a later suspended or urgent WIP render can overwrite it before a different render's effect commits, so "the effect runs only for the render that won" does not make the slot belong to that render. If the candidate is captured/render-local, concurrent attempts necessarily retain distinguishable candidates — exactly the second-slot/attempt distinction that the document's tripwire declares fatal. Before collector P1, either record that the tripwire has fired and promote grouped, or prove a representation under a transition+suspense/urgent-commit witness that associates the committed key sequence with the winning render without shared render-phase mutation or multiple live candidates.

The cold-read ruling is also not correctness-pinned. Section 3 says commit acquires without deref because the render value is already known and claims useSyncExternalStore has the same shape, while section 6.1 leaves a same-generation subscription-value change between render and commit OPEN. React's external-store contract performs a second getSnapshot just before applying every Transition and restarts when it changed; the proposed acquire-without-deref path names no equivalent freshness barrier. Resolve that witness before treating the allowed commit operation as adjudicated. This audit is the required adversarial pass; the document's authored and landed patches are range-diff exact, and its structure/provenance are otherwise coherent.
=== MERGED-PR AUDIT #7265 — VALIDATION HOLD, NUMBERS NOT AMENDED ===
The published UIx red-zone values remain the recorded measurements, but they are not yet a fail-closed baseline. === PROVENANCE PRACTICE: ANCHOR A PUBLISHED ROW BY BLOB HASH, NOT ONLY BY COMMIT SHA (mayor, 2026-07-31) ===

WHY. A producing commit SHA is rewritten by rebase and again by rebase-merge. Twice today a published row cited a SHA that was no longer an ancestor of main, and once a worker discovered its published SHA COULD NOT RUN ITS OWN REPRODUCTION COMMAND and had to re-take every number. A row nobody can reproduce is not a measurement.

THE PRACTICE, proposed by the rf2-9zysg worker and adopted: alongside the producing SHA and the repro command, record the BLOB HASH of each instrument file the row was produced by (git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, or git hash-object <path>). A blob hash is content identity — it survives rebase, squash and merge, and it answers the only question that matters: is the instrument that produced this number the same bytes as the instrument in the tree today?

HOW IT HAS ALREADY PAID: the PR #7268 rebase was trusted because all four bench files came out blob-identical; the #7267 rebase likewise verified eight instruments byte-identical; and #7270 anchored its re-published narrow-write rows by blob hash precisely because it knew the merge would rewrite its SHA a second time.

SO A PUBLISHED ROW SHOULD CARRY THREE THINGS: (1) the producing commit SHA, as history; (2) a reproduction command VERIFIED TO RUN AT THAT SHA; (3) the blob hash(es) of the instrument file(s), as content identity. Cite the SHA for provenance; check the blob hash for validity.

COROLLARY FOR REBASES: after any rebase of a branch carrying published numbers, verify by blob hash that the instruments are unchanged BEFORE pushing. If a blob moved, the row is either re-run or marked superseded in place — never left reading as current. That rule has held across five rebases today with no published row silently invalidated.

=== CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING: THE HEAP AXIS IS NOT PORTABLE ACROSS WITNESS SHAPES (mayor, 2026-07-31) ===

I RECORDED, EARLIER TODAY, that rf2-2rtt6.4's retained-heap thresholds STAND while its clock rows are superseded, and I justified it like this: 'retained bytes per boundary is a property of the boundary; the clock is not, because element count decides what fraction of the window is React's own work.' Three shapes differing 4x in markup density agreed within 8%, and I took that as portability.

THAT JUSTIFICATION IS FALSIFIED. The rf2-p0-audit cold read (findings doc, gitignored) established the mechanism:

  rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver sets P0_ROOTS=4 and divides by ROOTS x perRoot = 1,200 boundaries. But all four roots render the SAME 300 query vectors against the SAME frame. One frame means one subscription cache: 300 reactions at refcount 4, divided over 1,200 boundaries. So its 'exclusive retained per boundary' AMORTISES THE SUBSCRIPTION HALF OF EVERY READ ACROSS FOUR BOUNDARIES. rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder gives every boundary a DISTINCT query by explicit design, and its own page already names the shared case as the cheaper one.

  Hold markup density and boundary count constant — .4's grid (1 el/boundary, 4x300 = 1,200) against the ladder (1 el/boundary, 1,200) — and the answers still differ: Reagent 947 vs 1,565 B (1.65x), UIx 2,134 vs 3,811 B (1.79x).

  The sharing model SOLVES: a Reagent subscription half of ~824 B against rf2-2rtt6.12's independently measured 866 B (5% apart), and a UIx half of ~2,236 B against its 2,453 B (9% apart). THREE INSTRUMENTS, ONE ARITHMETIC.

  THE 8% RATIO AGREEMENT I RELIED ON SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE THE BIAS IS COMMON-MODE. Both arms amortise identically, so the RATIO is preserved while both ABSOLUTES are wrong. That is exactly the shape a ratio-only check cannot see, and I read agreement-of-ratios as evidence-of-portability.

WHAT IS NOW LIVE AND CONTRADICTORY, and this is the operator's to settle (rf2-2rtt6.16, P1):
  (a) THIS BEAD PUBLISHES BOTH .4's RATIOS AND .5's ABSOLUTE BYTES AS OPERATIVE RED-ZONES, AND THEY GIVE OPPOSITE VERDICTS. A candidate at 2,600 B/boundary at one read is RED under .4 and NOT red under .5.
  (b) The K3 paper-budget question — does the SHIPPED Reagent adapter already fail the >1 KB line at a single read — is answered BOTH WAYS: 954 B under .4, 1,565 B under .5.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISTURB. The heap RATIO between two arms measured in one run remains sound, because the amortisation is common-mode; UIx is still worse than Reagent on the read by a factor the audit did not challenge. What is unsafe is (1) any ABSOLUTE bytes-per-boundary figure from .4, and (2) any comparison of a .4 absolute against a .5 absolute.

SO THE CORRECTED ASYMMETRY IS NARROWER THAN I WROTE: a heap RATIO is portable across witness shapes; a heap ABSOLUTE is not, because it depends on how many boundaries share a query. I generalised from the ratio to the absolute without checking, and the check that would have caught it is the one this programme keeps rediscovering — ask what would have to be true for the number to be measuring something else.

RULING — HD-002 FORK, ERGONOMICS HALF: ONLY SURFACE B IS ACCEPTABLE (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim: 'Only surface B is acceptable from an ergonomics point of view', citing docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/02-views-and-reads.md). Recorded by acting mayor.

WHAT IS RULED. Of the two real candidates the guide sets out, SURFACE B — the ambient collector, where 'sub' is an ordinary function call usable inside a when, inside a for, and inside an inlined helper, with one fixed runtime hook collecting reads and the runtime diffing the edge set after the body returns — is the only ergonomically acceptable authoring surface. SURFACE A (grouped use-subs: one hook at the top of the body receiving the complete query collection before the body runs) is ergonomically REJECTED. The guide states the mechanism of A's limitation plainly: 'Grouped takes the complete query collection BEFORE the body, so a helper's queries are out of reach' — helpers cannot read, loops cannot read conditionally, and the author must hoist every query.

WHAT IS **NOT** RULED, and must not be read into this. The collector's CORRECTNESS and COST gates are untouched and still bind:
  - The standing TRIPWIRE that OVERRIDES THE CLOCK: the first time correctness requires a candidate ledger or generic post-render dependency reconciliation, THE COLLECTOR DIES, however good its numbers look. This ruling does not waive it and cannot.
  - The four pre-registered adjudication clauses (render/commit ownership state machine; the exact allowed edge-diff operation distinguished from the ledger class; two pre-registered strategy hypotheses each counted only by a benchmarked commit; the survival metric — steady-state allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20 reads plus zero retained per-occurrence objects after commit or teardown).
  - hd-002-adjudication.md stands as written.

THE CONSEQUENCE THE PROGRAMME MUST NOW CARRY. The guide names three outcomes: collector wins and ships; collector loses and grouped stays the default; both fail and the outcome is null. THIS RULING REMOVES THE COMFORT FROM OUTCOME 2. 'Grouped stays the default' is no longer a benign fallback — it is now, by the operator's own judgement, shipping an ergonomically unacceptable surface. So if the collector trips its tripwire or fails its survival metric, the honest positions are (a) the outcome is NULL and no Hicasso read surface ships, or (b) a mechanism not yet on the table earns its way in. Falling back to grouped and calling it a result is closed off. Whoever adjudicates HD-002 must state which of those it is rather than defaulting to A.

Ergonomics is half the verdict per the guide; that half is now decided. The other half is still measured, not asserted.
RULING REINFORCED (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim): 'use-subs (Surface A) is not sufficiently ergonomic for a programmer to use.'

This is STRONGER than a preference between two workable surfaces and must be read that way. Surface A is not merely less pleasant than Surface B — it is judged BELOW THE USABILITY BAR for the programmer this library exists to serve. It is therefore NOT a viable fallback, NOT a viable default, and NOT a viable ship state.

Restating the consequence so no future adjudicator can soften it: the guide's outcome 2 ('collector loses and grouped stays the default') is CLOSED. If the ambient collector trips its ledger tripwire or fails its survival metric, the outcome is NULL — no Hicasso read surface ships — or a mechanism not currently on the table must earn its way in. Shipping grouped use-subs as the product read surface is ruled out on ergonomics, independently of any measurement.

Unchanged and still binding: the tripwire that overrides the clock (a candidate ledger or generic post-render dependency reconciliation kills the collector however good its numbers), the four adjudication clauses, and the survival metric. so control/floor reads (F+50)/F and supplies no band, and the row's separation is
0.052 ms against a 0.146 ms quantisation grid). Against that, the one thing the
programme did establish in the last four days is a DIRECTION REVERSAL of its own
central diagnosis: the interpreter was believed to be the deficit and is not —
0.9636x stock Reagent, with the donor's own at 1.73-1.90x. That result landed
after the last M1 magnitude was taken, and M1 has not been re-taken since.

I tried to defeat this and could only wound it. The wound: rf2-jv36i prices the
walk increment at about 9% of the walk, the walk at about 0.66 ms of a 10 ms
mount, hence about 0.6% of a mount — well inside every band the census clock has
ever reported, so the walk work cannot plausibly move M1 from 1.4896x to 1.0x.
But that only shows the re-take would not RESCUE the row; it does not show the
row is currently ADJUDICATED, and it does not touch the point that the deficit's
attributed mechanism has changed under it. "May be unobtainable" is not "was
obtained and failed". A negative fork ruling issued today is issued on a mount
row nobody has been able to reproduce on an idle box, and on bulk rows the
programme has refused to publish at all.

--- CAN THE EVIDENCE BASE BEAR A FORK RULING AT ALL? ---

My judgement, stated plainly because the brief asks for it: THE EVIDENCE BASE
CAN BEAR A RULING ON HEAP AND CANNOT BEAR ONE ON THE CLOCK.

The heap axis is adjudicable, well-controlled, reproducible across sessions and
authors, and it returns a clear K3 verdict. If the operator is willing to rule
the fork on K3 alone — which is legitimate, K3 being a kill criterion in its own
right that nowhere requires the clock — then the evidence supports a stop, and
the honest form of that ruling says "on heap, on K3, with the clock unresolved".

The clock axis is not adjudicable at all right now, and it is not one instrument
fault but THREE independently diagnosed ones on three different rows: mount's
control is systematically unsound and its idle-box re-take refused; bulk's
control cannot be repaired because the obstruction is paint saturation, a page
property; per-keystroke has no band-supplying control in principle and no
resolution to state a sign even given one. Two beads holding those rulings
(rf2-jcm3p, rf2-swwud) are OPEN and both say in terms that choosing between the
repairs is a ruling and not a measurement. The bar bead itself, rf2-2rtt6.1, is
open. A programme cannot be said to have measured its own kill criteria when
three of the four clock-bearing rows are unpublishable for structural reasons.

So the adversarial finding that I think outranks the others is not "stop". It is
that THE FORK QUESTION IS NOT CURRENTLY ANSWERABLE ON ITS OWN TERMS, and a
ruling taken today — in either direction — is a ruling taken on an evidence base
that failed to produce the numbers it pre-registered. The cheapest things
standing between the operator and an answerable question are three rulings the
record is already holding: rf2-jcm3p (does the strict control rule bind on M1,
or is the reason it does not stated), rf2-swwud (option 3 — adjudicate
per-keystroke by Event Timing and be done — costs nothing), and HD-028's live
fallback. K7 has 38 days left, which is a generous budget for exactly that work.
That observation is offered as advice, not as a recommendation to defer; the
choice between ruling now on partial evidence and ruling later on complete
evidence is the operator's and nobody else's.

--- WHAT I FOUND THAT CONTRADICTS THE FIGURES I WAS BRIEFED WITH ---

1. THE ACCEPTANCE ROW IS NOT AT 1.2409x AND ITS VERDICT IS NOT
INSTRUMENT-LIMITED. 1.2409x [1.0371 - 1.5371] is rf2-y1jkm's reading. It then
moved to 1.4759x when rf2-2rtt6.54 migrated the census anchors to route-link,
and rf2-cno31's remedy took it to 1.1884x [1.1223 - 1.2660], band 7.0%, control
PASS — where the page's own verdict is "FAILS THE LINE: whole range above 1.10,
margin 8.0% clears the band". That is a RESOLVED failure, not an instrument-
limited straddle. The row that reads INSTRUMENT-LIMITED is FEED, at 1.0737x
[0.9669 - 1.1859]. The brief understated the acceptance failure and attached the
straddle to the wrong row.

2. THE reagent-slim CENSUS FIGURE IS REAL BUT IS NOT IN THE DOC TREE. 1.1667x ->
0.9762x (and 0.9649x on a second after-run) is verified, but only in rf2-e7zxb's
close reason for PR #7427; the string 0.9762 appears nowhere under docs/. The
single strongest piece of evidence for the null hypothesis currently lives only
in a bead close reason, and a P2 ruling that turns on the null's strength should
have it on a studio page.

3. K3's CURRENT RATIO IS 1.3492x, NOT 1.44x. The 1.44x that appears in this
bead's 2026-08-01 note predates the fusion; the live figure is 1,278 B/read
against 947. The verdict does not change, but the magnitude has moved and the
older number is the one still circulating.

Everything else in the brief verified exactly as stated: the 994/992 and
1,099.5/1,097 B shell pair and HD-028's withdrawn justifying sentence and live
fallback; the walk at 1.0588x before and 0.9636x after against the donor
interpreter's 1.73-1.90x; rf2-409ab's 70% read-shape / 30% interpreter split
with no fence-legal remedy surviving pricing; the frame-as-a-prop variant
returning 45 of 105 B, below the ~75 B shape sensitivity, not clearing the line;
rf2-swwud's structural (F+50)/F obstruction; rf2-0qj9w's M1 control refusal on a
verifiably idle box against a band that is widest at 24.6% when idle versus 8.3%
at four competing cores; and rf2-2rtt6.1 still open.

=== END OF ADVERSARIAL PASS. Advisory only. No bead was closed, reprioritised or
amended; no measurement was taken; no file outside this note was written. ===
=== HD-013 CREATIVE ADVISORY PASS — 2026-08-04 07:44 AUSEST, prepared by a
delegated worker, ADVISORY ONLY. THE DECIDER IS THE OPERATOR. ===

Read-only over the mayor checkout at e160af77a5. No code, no decisions.md, no
validation.md, no bead closed or reprioritised. The adversarial pass ran
independently; nothing here was coordinated with it.

WHAT THIS PASS WAS ASKED FOR: not optimism and not advocacy — reframings the
record has not considered, options that are cheap because of what has landed,
and paths that dissolve a problem rather than solving it. Three findings
survived that test. NONE OF THEM IS A ROUTE TO A "GO" ON NUMBERS, and the pass
says so up front: the mount gate (1.10x direct UIx, the 2026-08-02 amendment on
this bead) is failed on every row that resolves, and I found no framing that
turns that into a pass.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 1 — THE P2 NULL MOVED, THE PROGRAMME IS WHAT MOVED IT, AND NO ROW
MEASURES IT.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The facts, all committed.

rf2-2rtt6.63 put three interpreters over one witness value in one process and
found ours already at stock Reagent's cost (1.0588x before the bead touched
anything, 0.9636x after two cheapenings), while the interpreter the donor rungs
actually ride, reagent2.impl.template, read 1.7273-1.9020x stock. That finding
was handed to reagent-slim as its own defect. Two landings followed, both in the
SHIPPED adapter at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:

  rf2-lhdp0 (PR #7405)  1.82x -> 1.19-1.24x stock Reagent
  rf2-e7zxb (PR #7427)  1.1667x -> 0.9762x and 0.9649x, guard clean on both

Canonical DOM byte-identical at 1,202 elements / 58,529 bytes across all five
runs, agreement failures empty including 22 hostile heads. Both are on main.

Three consequences, and they do not all point the same way.

(a) THE NULL IS NOT WHERE IT WAS MEASURED. Adapter-Prime — the P2 null, the
composed reagent-slim :f> plus UIx use-subscribe arm — rides that walk. HD-008's
donor rungs read 1.33-1.5x stock Reagent, and rf2-2rtt6.63 attributed that
deficit to exactly this interpreter. The last time the donor rows were taken is
rf2-2rtt6.31, 2026-08-02, which predates BOTH landings. So the fork's null
control has probably become materially faster since anything measured it, and
the ruling is scheduled to compare the candidate against a control whose current
position is unknown. This is the cheapest decision-relevant measurement I found
anywhere in the record and nobody has booked it.

(b) THE CODEC ADVANTAGE OVER THE DONOR HAS EVAPORATED. Hicasso reads 0.9636x
stock Reagent on the walk witness; reagent-slim now reads 0.9762x and 0.9649x on
the same witness. That is parity. rf2-2rtt6.63's hicasso/slim of 0.5567 and
0.5579 is stale — it was a ratio against a codec the programme has since fixed.
Any statement of the form "we extracted the donor's plumbing and cheapened it,
we read 0.56x the donor we were built from" is no longer true of main. I flag
this because it is a figure a decider could reasonably carry forward, and it has
moved against the candidate.

(c) THE PROGRAMME'S OUTPUT IS ALREADY BANKED IN A SHIPPED ARTEFACT. On a P2
stop, "adapters-only is a successful outcome" stops being a consolation clause
and becomes a description of something that has already happened: a
first-class, shipped adapter is 1.87x faster on the census witness than it was
two beads ago, its caches are structurally safer than the guards they replaced
(null-prototype rather than defended-against), and the mechanism came out of
Hicasso's codec. That is a real deliverable that survives either ruling, and the
record does not currently frame it that way anywhere.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE (b) AND (a), AND WHAT IT COSTS. (b) is one run: the
walk_vs_reagent_app instrument already runs all four arms in one process on one
witness value under the arm-order guard, so a single run on current main puts
hicasso and post-fix slim in the same windows and answers it outright. Roughly
ten minutes of box time. Note the two figures I have compared are from different
sessions on a shared box, which the instrument's own discipline says is exactly
what its ratios are NOT for — so (b) is a hypothesis until that run exists. (a)
is larger: a donor-row re-take on the census or M1 instrument, which needs a
window that can adjudicate — see Finding 2.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 2 — QUIET IS THE HARD CASE. THE PROGRAMME'S SCARCEST RESOURCE MAY BE
THE WRONG RESOURCE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The brief asks whether the measurement crisis is a reason to stop or a sign the
evidence needs a different instrument. I think it is neither, and the record
already contains the reason.

The band ladder (rf2-ymi6j, nineteen runs, same box, both clocks) measured the
band at 24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3-13.2% everywhere from four
cores to twenty, with corr(band, floor) = -0.49, and the floor's per-sample
coefficient of variation falling MONOTONICALLY with load, 30.0% -> 15.2%. A busy
box is slower and steadier; an idle one is faster and jumpier. rf2-0qj9w's
window then refused M1's positive control on a verifiably idle box — ctl-2x at
1.8443x with at least one segment-round below the 1.5 floor, band 21.4% — and
its own note says the rebook should not assume more quiet is the repair.

WHAT NOBODY HAS PROPOSED. The refusal mode is per-round dispersion, and
dispersion is the one quantity the ladder measured falling with load. So the
affirmative move is to run the adjudicating rows under a DECLARED, CONTROLLED
synthetic load — four to twelve competing cores — rather than under maximum
quiet. I searched the tree and the open beads: rf2-h8o80 proposed a
floor-in-calibrated-range precondition and was refuted; the band page names
pinning the CPU governor as a falsification of its mechanism hypothesis; no page
and no bead proposes load as a measurement CONDITION.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A GUESS. The ladder also measured what happens to an
arm-to-arm floor-normalised ratio across those same rungs: ctl-2x/floor reads
1.7347 / 1.7272 / 1.6818 / 1.6604 / 1.7111 / 1.7604 at 0/2/4/8/12/20 competing
cores, with corr(ctl-2x/floor, floor) = -0.04. That is direct evidence that the
KIND of quantity the bar adjudicates does not trend with load over exactly the
range that cuts the band by two to three times. The instrument to do it also
already exists: seam_ladder.cjs forks N spinners, runs the clock and kills them.

COST AND THE EXPERIMENT. One row, taken at rung 0 and rung 8 in one session,
asking two questions: does the ratio agree across the rungs, and does the strict
every-round control rule pass at rung 8 where it refused at rung 0? Half a day,
no new driver. If it holds, the programme's scarcest pre-P2 resource — quiet
windows, named as scarce in rf2-0puue's own parking ruling — is partly
self-imposed, and rows that have been unpublishable for weeks become takeable.

HONEST LIMITS, STATED. The ladder is a bulk300 ladder and M1 is a mount row, so
this is an extrapolation across witnesses. The mechanism (an idle machine parks
cores and drops clocks between samples) is the band page's own hypothesis and it
did not measure frequency or C-state residency. Pinning the governor, if this
box permits it, is the cleaner variant of the same idea — steadiness without the
load — and it is the falsification the page already invited and nobody has run.
And none of this touches the three-point control's OTHER refusal, which is a
property of the page rather than the box: paint saturating once the damage
region covers the viewport is not a constant, so no differencing removes it.

ONE ADJACENT OPTION, CHEAPER THAN A NEW INSTRUMENT. Bulk is unadjudicable on our
harness and the record says so in terms. But the krausest cross-check
(rf2-rguy1) is the ONE harness the clock correction never touched — it drives
through page.click, an Input-domain door, so its taskNet was script-and-frame
all along and its ratios move under 1.7% between the clocks — and it already
carries all three arms implemented against one shared model with canonically
identical DOM. It is the instrument in this tree least exposed to the defect
that broke ours. Its own limits are real and must ride with it: its positive
control failed at 13.1-13.7x against a pre-registered 8-13x, and its app has
trivial state, so it prices rendering and says nothing about subscription
fan-out — which is the term rf2-409ab found dominant. It cannot answer the read
question. It may be able to answer bulk, which ours cannot answer at all.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 3 — THE 1 KB LINE ADJUDICATES ABOUT 2% OF WHAT A PRODUCT BOUNDARY
RETAINS, AND THE CRITERION THAT ACTUALLY KILLS IS ABOUT REAGENT.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The rows are exact and I take them as published. R=0 shell, tree that ships:
994 / 992 B without the wrapper, 1,099.5 / 1,097 B with it. Marginal slope on
the same runs: 1,278 B/read (Reagent segment). Donors in the same runs: Reagent
shell about 505 B and 947 B/read, UIx shell about 224 B and 2,979 B/read.

Both candidate fits are lines in R on all six rounds, so the page's own model
gives a three-read boundary. The arithmetic, which is mine over two published
terms rather than a measured rung:

  Hicasso, wrapper       1,099.5 + 3 x 1,278 = 4,933 B
  Hicasso, no wrapper      994   + 3 x 1,278 = 4,828 B
  Reagent                  505   + 3 x   947 = 3,346 B
  UIx                      224   + 3 x 2,979 = 9,161 B

The wrapper is 2.1% of what the candidate's three-read boundary retains. Against
Reagent the candidate is 1.47x with it and 1.44x without. Against UIx it is
0.54x either way. On the card-shaped boundary that was actually measured, the
page-chrome row put the same fiber at +1.8% of 11,018 B.

THE REFRAMING THIS MAKES AVAILABLE, offered as a framing and not a
recommendation. The disposition under ruling is not "does the wrapper fail the
bar" — it is "which of two configurations does v0 ship", and the R=0 line does
not separate them at the level a product pays. Meanwhile K3, which is the
criterion that actually kills, reads "per-boundary heap worse than Reagent with
NO paper path to the floor": the candidate is worse than Reagent on both terms
with or without the wrapper, so the wrapper does not decide K3 either, and the
"paper path" half is exactly what rf2-0puue's ruling has already recorded in
staged form (91-92 B/read of reader array, with a mechanism named and a probe
that reads it as mostly push growth). The 1 KB line is the only place the
wrapper is decisive, and it is a paper budget written before any code, on the
one boundary shape a product never ships.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, WHICH IS STRONG AND BELONGS HERE. The R=0 regime was ruled
deliberately, on 2026-07-31, precisely so a candidate cannot pass the line by
amortising subscriptions across boundaries. So the framing above argues against
a live ruling and needs the operator to WANT it. It is not a worker's to assume,
and I do not assume it.

THE LEVERS WERE PRICED BUT NOT COMBINED. The frame-as-a-prop variant returns
45.0 / 46.5 B of the wrapper's 105.5 / 105.0 B, on the same instrument, the same
rung and the same A-B-A design, with the two sections' A arms reproducing each
other to half a byte. Both terms are measured as exactly R-independent
per-boundary constants. Composing them predicts a no-wrapper frame-prop shell
around 949 / 946 B. That is a PREDICTION, not a row — and it would not resolve
as a clear pass anyway, because 51 B under 1,000 is inside validation.md's own
~75 B component-shape sensitivity. Cost to turn it into a row: one more A/B on
the rung both sections already share, one session.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
THE QUESTION I JUDGE THE PROGRAMME HAS BEEN ASKING WRONGLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The programme is spending its scarcest resource — adjudicable box time — on a
performance residual its own decomposition says is a capability price, while the
one input the P2 ruling genuinely lacks costs no box time at all.

rf2-409ab took the acceptance row apart through the published in-page door and
reproduced ship/uix to within 0.6% of the published ratio before decomposing it.
Of a 1.858 ms deficit: 55% the read term by ablation, 30% the interpreter
against a compile-time macro, 8% routing spelling, 2% the shell and the memo
fiber together and both indistinguishable from zero. A coarse arm — the
candidate at the twin's read shape, byte-identical DOM — prices the read-shape
asymmetry directly at 1.300 ms, 70% of the deficit. And the roster's own second
row corroborates it: on feed, where both arms spell 603 per-instance reads, the
published ratio is 1.0737x. Where the read shapes match, the deficit is
essentially gone. The page's honest negative is that nothing available inside the
fence moves this row much, and its own sentence is that the comparison charges
the candidate for a capability the control does not have.

So the residual is priced, named and attributed. Another quiet window does not
change what it IS. What the ruling is actually missing is on this bead already:
the charter-v0 dogfood preference verdict, outstanding since 2026-08-03, held
across three delegated dossier rounds, each landing "preferred, with
reservations", and the hold note says in terms that until a dated operator note
records it, the HD-013 P2 graduation advisory HAS NO ERGONOMICS LEG. With K5
removed by ruling on 2026-08-04, ergonomics no longer has a kill criterion
either — which makes the preference verdict the only place ergonomics enters the
fork at all.

Put plainly: the open P2 question is no longer "can interpreted hiccup be fast".
It is "is a read surface that can sit inside a for, inside a branch, inside a
plain helper worth about 1.2x direct UIx on pages where UIx cannot spell the
same reads, and about 1.07x where it can" — and that is a preference question
with a measured price, not a measurement question. One dated sentence on this
bead is worth more to the ruling than any row still outstanding.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CORRECTIONS TO FIGURES I WAS BRIEFED WITH, VERIFIED IN TREE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. "The interpreter the donor rungs actually ride reads 1.73-1.90x" is TRUE of
   rf2-2rtt6.63 and STALE of main. rf2-lhdp0 and rf2-e7zxb have since taken it
   to 0.9762x / 0.9649x. See Finding 1.

2. "read shape ~70%, interpreter-vs-macro ~30%" reads as a partition and is not
   one. rf2-409ab's ablation partition is reads 55 / markup 30 / routing 8 /
   shell+memo 2 / residual 4. The 70% is a separate counterfactual measurement
   (local minus coarse, 1.300 ms of 1.858 ms), and the coarse arm still walks
   hiccup, so 70% and 30% overlap and must not be added.

3. The reagent-slim 1.1667x -> 0.9762x figures are on rf2-e7zxb's close note,
   not in any studio page, and they are the diagnostic in-page walk clock on
   walk_vs_reagent_app — not the clock of record and not the census clock rows.

4. Worth the decider's attention because it is not a briefing error but a doc
   one: validation.md still states the ship bar as "mount AND bulk view-work
   <= 1.0x Reagent". The operative mount gate since the 2026-08-02 amendment on
   this bead is one line, <= 1.10x direct UIx-on-subs, and that amendment
   explicitly REJECTED keeping <= 1.0x Reagent (as an implicit kill of the mount
   axis) and named "a bounded consistency edit to the stale HD-012 /
   validation.md Reagent-parity wording (docs follow-up, not performed here)".
   That edit does not appear to have been made. A decider reading validation.md
   today reads a bar that is not the operative one. Recorded as a fact; the
   correction is not mine to make.

Everything else I was briefed with reproduced exactly: 1.0588x / 0.9636x on the
walk; 994/992 and 1,099.5/1,097 B on the shell; 45.0/46.5 B for the frame-prop
variant against 105.5/105.0 B for the wrapper, not clearing the line at
1,054/1,051 B; -60 B/read banked by the fusion with 91-92 B/read of surviving
reader array parked at P3; the per-keystroke row's missing band and the
(F+50)/F control; M1's control refusing on a verifiably idle box; the band
widest when idle; K5 removed 2026-08-04 with K1-K4, K6, K7 standing and the
guide at nine pages.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
HOW THIN IS THE CREATIVE GROUND — HONESTLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Thinner than the volume above suggests, and I would rather say so than pad.

There is no reframing here that makes the clock evidence a pass. The mount gate
is failed clearly on M1 and on the one census row that resolves; the bulk leg of
the bar cannot be produced on our harness at all; the outside instrument puts
candidate bulk at 1.43-1.62x, its worst row, agreed by both instruments. What I
found instead is one measurement nobody has booked whose answer moves the NULL
rather than the candidate, one instrument option that is cheap and unnamed and
may unblock rows that are currently unpublishable, one framing of a heap line
that argues against a live ruling and therefore needs the operator to want it,
and one observation that the ruling's remaining gap is a preference verdict
rather than a number.

If the operator's reading of the numbers is that the candidate does not clear
its bar, nothing in this pass should be read as arguing otherwise. What the pass
does argue is that two of the four things above are cheap enough that not doing
them before the ruling is a choice worth making deliberately.
ADVISORY INPUT LANDED — the production server arm is priced (mayor, 2026-08-04). Pointer appended here because the dossier worker correctly declined to write into this bead's notes itself: its brief fenced them, the bead it worked told it to land here, and it flagged the disagreement rather than resolving it silently.

THE ARTEFACT: docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md, landed by PR #7488 under rf2-2rtt6.88 (now closed). Twelve sections - the three jobs both arms must do, the shipped floor, how R0 bites each, Arm A (JVM structural walk), Arm B (Node sidecar), the two instrument facts, what the spike corpus licenses, the unmeasured roster, a thirteen-axis asymmetry table, bead and week estimates, per-arm tripwires, and an explicit section on what the page does NOT say. Indexed from the design-record README and pointed at from draft-guide/10's Not settled row.

THE FOUR THINGS THE SITTING SHOULD READ FIRST:

1. THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD IMPLIED. emit-ui-tree ships and is final, and a JVM interpreted structural walk to the v1 tree ALREADY SHIPS for Freehand, driving emit-ui-tree behind the Independence wall. So the walk arm's back half is a thing to be CALLED, not a thing to be built. What has no precedent is READS - Freehand's JVM walk fails a v/sub loud rather than resolving one.

2. THE SPIKE BUILT THE NODE ARM'S RENDER, NOT ITS TOPOLOGY. ssr-ring is JVM-only .clj in every file, so entry.cljs hand-writes the payload tag and the page envelope and says in terms that it is not a production host. THERE IS NO JVM-TO-NODE CONTRACT ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. The R0-compliant sidecar has not been built or measured, and the page names that as the largest unmeasured thing on it.

3. THE SHARPEST ASYMMETRY, and it is a composition neither document states alone: spec 004B says two emitters diverging is DETECTED, NOT PREVENTED, while spec 011 says React-native adoption deliberately does not report attribute-only mismatches. Composed, THE WALK ARM'S LIKELIEST DIVERGENCE IS INVISIBLE AT RUNTIME. The Node arm cannot produce that class of defect at all.

4. THIS IS NOT A SCHEDULE CHOICE. Walk 6 beads / 5 to 8.5 weeks; sidecar 6 beads / 4 to 6.5 weeks. THE BANDS OVERLAP. Anyone hoping the estimates would decide it should stop hoping.

WHAT THE CORPUS DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE: X2 through X5 are client-half rows and transfer to BOTH arms unchanged; only X1 speaks to a server half, and only Node's. So the spike is not evidence for the walk arm in the way a quick reading might suggest.

RENDER-HASH: nothing in the dossier leans on it, and neither arm repairs it - production takes it from the root hiccup at pipeline.clj:543 regardless. One observation recorded for rf2-2rtt6.91's owner rather than as a ruling: spec 011 already tiers detection so that React-element roots carry NO HASH AT ALL, which may mean .91's candidate (c) is the spec's own existing answer for Hicasso's tier.

NO VERDICT WAS DRAWN, and the disagreement about whether one was wanted is recorded in the page's own section 0. Mike's 2026-08-04 directive commissioned a NO-VERDICT dossier; the bead's older description asked for the recommendation stated. The page prices both arms and stops.

ALSO FILED: rf2-2rtt6.114 (P2, bug) - the Node entry's byte accounting reports UTF-16 code units labelled as UTF-8. I had told the worker rf2-2rtt6.86 was reopened for this; IT IS NOT - .86 is closed and its close reason enumerates .91, .92 and .94 as follow-ups while omitting this one. No size figure from that manifest appears anywhere in the dossier.

=== APPENDED MEASUREMENT (worker, rf2-2rtt6.4) — THE P0 RED-ZONE THRESHOLDS ===
Workers append; only the operator amends. Full page:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md

PRODUCING COMMIT ea5d01ab9d (arm at bc5f38f10a).
REPRO clock: P0_ROUNDS=5 P0_SAMPLES=10 P0_WARMUPS=4 node implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs --only clock

RUNTIME: HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15 (Chromium/Playwright), Windows x64; :advanced,
goog.DEBUG false, plain :browser module; React 19.2.0, Reagent 2.0.1, UIx 1.4.4.
BROWSER NUMBERS ONLY. No JVM/Node figure appears.

Per RULING 1 these figures ARE the red-zones. A later candidate row worse than
the stated mean on either axis for that witness family is RED and needs an
explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit.

--- RED-ZONE, CLOCK: UIx-on-subs / Reagent-on-subs, both floor-normalised in the
--- same round and the same adapter segment. 5 rounds, ranges are min-max.

  W1-list mount (1,203 el, 300 boundaries, 1 sub/boundary)
      1.057x  [0.907 - 1.156]   STRADDLES 1.0 -> INDISTINGUISHABLE
  W3-form mount (51 el, 12 fields, 1 sub/field)
      0.893x  [0.843 - 0.956]   UIx faster, disjoint from 1.0
  U-broad bulk  (301 el, 300 boundaries, one commit ALL read)
      0.838x  [0.760 - 0.953]   UIx faster, disjoint from 1.0
  U-narrow bulk (301 el, one commit exactly ONE reads)
      1.536x  [1.226 - 1.876]   UIx SLOWER, disjoint from 1.0

  Against the floor: reagent-subs 2.350 / 1.948 / 8.064 / 4.277;
                     uix-subs     2.472 / 1.738 / 6.729 / 6.502.

--- RED-ZONE, RETAINED HEAP: exclusive (arm - floor) B/boundary, UIx / Reagent,
--- same segment. CDP getHeapUsage after a forced collection, 4 roots held.

  list (300 sub-reading rows)   2.262x  [2.196 - 2.335]   (absolute 1.580x)
  grid (300 sub-reading cells)  2.254x  [2.217 - 2.288]   (absolute 1.989x)

  Exclusive per boundary: Reagent-on-subs ~954 B (list) / ~947 B (grid);
  UIx-on-subs ~2,156 B (list) / ~2,134 B (grid). NOTE FOR K3 AND THE BUDGET:
  the frontier comparator is itself over the 1 KB paper-fail line by >2x, and
  the Reagent denominator is close to it. Red (>2.26x) and over budget (>~0.5 KB)
  are far apart; a candidate can sit between them.

--- INSTRUMENT DISCIPLINE
  Arm-order guard REPORTABLE on every row, both axes; driver exit 0. Self-test
  8/8 before anything was measured. Canonical-DOM parity clean under :advanced in
  both segments and across the seam, all rounds. Every measured write read back
  out of the DOM inside its own window: 0 UNVERIFIED OF 6,600 clock windows and
  0 OF 48 heap mounts. Both orders: segment order and witness order alternate
  with the round; arm order within a segment chosen by measured adjacency.
  POSITIVE CONTROLS, predicted vs measured, every run:
    heap  predicted 4,700,000 B  measured 4,700,317 B [4,699,074-4,700,974] 1.0001x
    clock predicted 1.9975 (2403/1203 elements) measured 1.8381 [1.8182-1.8548].
    The 8% shortfall is the mount window's FIXED per-root term: solving
    (f+2403k)/(f+1203k)=1.8381 gives f ~= 229k, ~19% of the 1,203-element page.
    Consequence: the clock compresses ratios toward 1.0, so a threshold above 1.0
    is conservative and one below 1.0 is generous to UIx.

--- WITNESS-SET CAVEAT THE OPERATOR SHOULD SEE
  These shapes do NOT match rf2-2rtt6.2's (unmerged at time of measurement): that
  arm uses a 901-el M1 list and a 51-el M2 form, both reading [:p0/cell i]; this
  arm uses a 1,203-el W1 reading [:p0/row i], a 51-el W3 reading [:p0/field i],
  and a 301-el 300-boundary grid reading [:p0/cell i]. The thresholds remain
  sound AS THRESHOLDS because each is a ratio between two arms measured in the
  same run, same shapes, same sub graph, same rounds -- but they are thresholds
  ON THIS WITNESS SET. If P0 converges on rf2-2rtt6.2's witnesses the UIx arm
  must be re-pointed and the red-zones re-derived. Closest correspondence today:
  this arm's U-broad (300 boundaries, one commit all read, [:p0/cell i]) matches
  that arm's bulk row in boundary count and sub graph, differing only in markup
  density. Filed as a follow-up bead.

--- WHAT THE NARROW ROW SAYS
  U-narrow is the only row where UIx-on-subs is materially behind, and the window
  decomposition puts the cost in the WRITE leg -- before React is involved --
  i.e. the useSyncExternalStore notification fanning out across 300 subscribed
  boundaries, not UIx's rendering. That is the row a native view layer has the
  clearest structural claim on.

--- main, owns the lane per HD-017, is the denominator HD-012 states the bar
--- against, already carries the in-plan control and the labelled lower bound,
--- and .4's own Open items nominated it.

--- RED-ZONE, CLOCK: UIx-on-subs / Reagent-on-subs, both floor-normalised in

--- HOW MUCH THE MISMATCH MATTERED: THREE OF FOUR VERDICTS FLIP.

  large-list mount  .4 W1  1.057 [0.907-1.156] INDISTINGUISHABLE
                    ->  M1 1.2301 [1.110-1.354] UIx SLOWER, DISJOINT
  form mount        .4 W3  0.893 [0.843-0.956] UIx faster, DISJOINT, published

  MECHANISM. The broad margin widens on the 901-el page because more of the

  runtime hiccup walk; the narrow margin narrows because the floor's top-down
  re-render — the thing a narrow write is compared against — is 3x the work.
  A clock ratio on this axis moves by more than the effects being measured
  when the page changes. That is the whole case for converging.

--- A GRADE MISMATCH THAT IS NOT ABOUT WITNESSES AT ALL. rf2-2rtt6.2 grades its
--- 51-element form row DIAGNOSTIC and says it must not be quoted against the
--- bar (3-6 clock quanta at one mount a sample). rf2-2rtt6.4 batched 8 mounts a
--- sample, lifted the same-sized witness clear of the clamp, and published its
--- form row as a THRESHOLD. So a candidate's form row would have been judged
--- red against a threshold whose bar-row counterpart is unquotable. Resolved
--- here by grading the converged form row diagnostic, like its bar row.

--- ONE ARM RE-RUN, NOT TWO. THE HEAP AXIS WAS ALREADY CONVERGED IN SUBSTANCE.
  .4 list (1,203-el page)     2.262x [2.196-2.335]
  .4 grid (301-el page)       2.254x [2.217-2.288]

  Three shapes differing 4x in markup density and 4x in boundary count agree
  within 8%. Retained bytes per subscribing boundary is a property of the
  BOUNDARY; the clock is not, because element count decides what fraction of
  the window is React's own work. THE HEAP RED-ZONES ON THIS BEAD STAND
  UNCHANGED. (Stated as a claim the operator may reject: the three figures come
  from two instruments and are not a strict replication.)

--- THE DENOMINATOR REPRODUCES rf2-2rtt6.2. The Reagent arm here is a second
--- implementation on the same witnesses, different app ns, different schedule.
--- Its reagent-subs/floor ranges OVERLAP that arm's published ranges on all
--- three shared rows: M1 3.899 [3.447-4.300] vs 4.352 [4.063-4.625];
--- M2 1.874 [1.750-2.050] vs 2.102 [1.625-2.800]; bulk 7.064 [6.200-7.700] vs
--- 7.443 [7.000-8.000]. The convergence moved the FRONTIER arm onto the
--- denominator's pages without moving the denominator.

--- STABILITY, AND THE ONE ROW THAT IS NOT STABLE. The identical instrument was
--- run twice, 5 rounds each. M1 disjoint both times; M2 straddles both times;
--- broad disjoint both times. BULK NARROW: 1.1556 [1.042-1.250] disjoint at the
--- published commit, 1.0405 [0.750-1.333] STRADDLING in the second run. Four
