(ii) Evidence page: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-dogfood-preference-case.md. It establishes: both renderings current and idiomatic (the UIx control strengthened, not strawmanned - its dead IME gate fixed to read the native event); same-screen proof on elements AND intents (canonical-DOM parity at mount and again after a 17-step real-DOM script driving all 8 handler sites and both branches of both key-maps; dispatched vectors captured at the :events port, asserted equal AND equal to a stated expectation; mutation-proved, incl. one divergence the DOM half structurally cannot see); authoring measured: 47 vs 72 lines (symmetric count, arithmetic shown twice), 8 data event positions vs 8 hand-written closures, 0 vs 2 threaded values, 5-5 concept-count tie; honest losses stated (UIx wins compile-time shape checking, event-in-hand, fixed subscription identity, smaller machinery bet). Over-claim retracted on the page: UIx CAN express conditional/helper-local reads - at the price of a component boundary or a hook call-site contract; one case (a read inside a variable-length for) has no hook-shaped route. HD-028 makes the value-equality bail-out Hicasso's boundary default; uix.core/memo is a per-component opt-in no repo example uses.

(iii) HOW TO MAKE THE CALL WELL (dossier recommendation): read the page once; then make the SAME small edit in BOTH renderings - e.g. add a "priority" field with a validation rule (touch model, event, row rendering) in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs and dogfood_uix.cljs; record the verdict HERE the same day, while the feel is fresh, in whatever form is true - "preferred, with reservations" is a valid sentence. If NOT preferred, name the loss that decided it: that sentence is the top input for interpreter-gap/surface work, and not-preferred removes the ergonomic-win half of the K-rule defence (weighs toward adapters-as-success).

(iv) JUDGING CRITERIA worth keeping (compressed from both dossier sections): do not rule from the summary table - the counts favour Hicasso, but the 5-5 concept tie means the win is texture, visible only in the editor. Markup is a draw; the gap concentrates where events and reads live - the edit stays local data + local reads in Hicasso, while in UIx it also grows the fixed hook set and the event plumbing (dispatch acquisition, event extraction, submit prevention, app-owned IME gate). Intent-as-data is the stronger win (the first UIx cut got the IME law wrong - React's synthetic event drops isComposing; vectors are equality-visible to tests and tools). Weigh honestly against: compile-time checking, the live event in hand, stable subscription identity, far less novel machinery, and Hicasso's still-incomplete tool payoff (headless render API unfrozen; manifest/explain doors post-v0). The memo default is supporting evidence, not the reason.

CODEX ADVISORY (the dossier's independent second review; it re-counted the forms and traced the priority-field edit through both sources): lands "preferred, with reservations" and would record now, without another trial edit. Advisory only - no agent may record the verdict. If the page plus that trace settles your taste, adopting it is one dated sentence here; otherwise run (iii). ARM 1 — THE ADAPTER — HAS LANDED ITS CORE (PR #7321, recorded by acting mayor 2026-07-31). The ruled architecture is now demonstrated rather than proposed, and three of the programme's open correctness risks are closed by evidence.

THE <=2-HOOK SHELL IS HELD, AND MEASURED AT REACT'S DISPATCHER rather than declared: ['useContext' 'useSyncExternalStore'], exactly 2 at 1, 7 AND 20 reads, with no useRef/useState/useMemo/useCallback anywhere in the shell. The mechanism is the interesting part: React gives a function component no per-instance storage except a hook cell, so a shell wanting one has already spent a third hook. Arm 1 gives the shell NO per-instance render-phase state at all — 'subscribe' closes over the read SET and nothing else, so it is a pure function of a value: cached by that value, shared across boundaries, identity-stable exactly while the reads are unchanged, which is precisely React's own re-subscribe condition. getSnapshot returns a monotone epoch sum, so Object.is on one number is a correct change test with no memo. The raw-UIx comparator on the same probe and page RISES with read count. If React's internals slot moves, the witness records UNWITNESSED and FAILS — it cannot silently go green.

THE CANDIDATE-LEDGER TRIPWIRE DID NOT FIRE. Closest approach named honestly: the read-set entry cache is one line from the fence — keyed by read-set CONTENT, never by render or attempt, evicted by a macrotask reaper, and dropping an entry early costs one re-subscribe and no correctness.

THE LAZINESS DEFECT IS REFUTED FOR THIS ARCHITECTURE, STRUCTURALLY: the collector window closes around codec/as-element and the codec is eager everywhere (expand-seq, realize-children, clj->js). No doall, no widened window, no cost, hook budget untouched. Three witnesses, each asserting the SECOND half (a later write re-renders), because a broken implementation passes the first. Further, the four DEFERRED-read escapes (stored handler, invoked handler, delay, stashed lazy seq) now convert into a LOUD ERROR NAMING THE QUERY rather than a silent missing edge — which discharges the substance of rf2-2rtt6.32. One residual is named rather than hidden: a deferred read forced inside another boundary's render is attributed to that boundary.

SURFACE B IS PREFERRED ON EVIDENCE, AND NOT FOR BREVITY. Identical canonical DOM across collector / grouped / raw UIx with a can-answer-false control. The collector is the only surface where the read sits at the value's POINT OF USE, so 'what does this boundary depend on?' is answered by reading the body; grouped's declaration and body can DRIFT, and on the collector that drift is not expressible. Raw UIx loses decisively (no conditional read, no helper-donated read, seven hand-written handlers). Measured: the collector's conditional read holds FEWER edges than the declaration on the same page. This is direct evidence for the operator's Surface B ruling.

One baseline deref per new unique key closes it. Caught by the narrow-write witness.
2. THE AMBIENT FRAME OUTRANKS REACT CONTEXT, INVISIBLY. The carried-invariant chain resolves the dynamic-var tier BEFORE context, so an ambient use-subscribe answers for the ambient frame while use-current-frame reports the provider's — and it presents as a RENDERING difference. ':ambient-frame nil' is now set in every DOM fixture here, with a probe asserting the two read forms agree.

DESIGN INPUT ON rf2-2rtt6.39 (delete the per-boundary frame hook by threading the frame as a codec prop): REJECTED FOR v0 ON CORRECTNESS, not cost. A frame-provider interleaved between two Hicasso boundaries is a React component the codec never sees, so a props-threaded frame SILENTLY KEEPS THE OUTER FRAME across it. Any measurement of .39 needs an interleaved-provider witness or it measures a design that is wrong in the one case providers exist for.

K7: Arm 1 also mounts the dogfood screen (arm1_dogfood_dom_cljs_test), so the clock is confirmed running from 2026-07-31 on both arms' evidence. rf2-2rtt6.9 stays IN_PROGRESS with rf2-2rtt6.41 filed for the remainder (100-cell controlled grid, StrictMode/HMR/h-boundary, H2, the allocation-slope half, candidate bar rows).

RISK the worker named and I am carrying forward: the subscribe-identity mechanism means a body whose control flow changes its read set pays a re-subscribe per change — cheap and proven correct, but a real difference from a static-edge surface, and the thing to watch on the bulk rows.
RULING — HICASSO AUTHORS NO CODEC AND CONSUMES reagent-slim's (acting mayor, 2026-07-31, under the Hicasso authority delegated by Mike; OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE).

THE EVIDENCE, from rf2-2rtt6.29 (PR #7322): Freehand's codec was entered as a fourth donor arm — 'donor-fh' is 'donor-r1' WITH ONE TOKEN CHANGED, the row function, everything else held fixed (same :f> boundary reached by the same slim-element call, same skeleton, same keyed for, same use-subscribe arity with the frame pinned as a literal, same dispatch-for lookup, same author closure, same tags, same floor arm, rounds and interleaving schedule). Only the codec building markup inside the 300 boundaries varied — 900 of the M page's 903 elements.

RESULT: Freehand's codec is WORSE on every row that resolves. donor-fh / donor-r1 reads mount-M 1.078-1.306 (disjoint above 1.0 in 6/6 segments), write-bulk 1.273-1.550 (disjoint 2/2), mount-U 0.973-1.363 (disjoint 5/6, the one straddle named rather than averaged), write-narrow indistinguishable. Against RAW UIx: donor-fh 1.358-1.746 on M where slim's codec reads 1.179-1.373. NOT ONE of the sixteen codec ranges sits disjointly BELOW 1.0.

INSTRUMENT NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the worker added a fatal boot gate 'codecs-differ?', because a donor-fh/donor-r1 reading of 1.0 is AMBIGUOUS between 'same cost' and 'ran one codec twice' — and the parity gate cannot distinguish them, since agreement is its whole purpose. The two doors are forced to answer differently on ^{:key} vector meta (slim honours it, Freehand refuses it). Passed every run. This is the kind of gate that makes a null result trustworthy.

THE RULING: Hicasso AUTHORS NO CODEC. It does not write a third runtime hiccup interpreter, and it does not adopt Freehand's. It CONSUMES reagent-slim's, which this measurement establishes as the cheapest interpreter in the tree.

WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE OPERATOR'S DIRECTION, not a departure from it. Mike ruled Hicasso is 'a Hiccup interpreter that is highly efficient very data oriented... targeting React'. Consuming the cheapest proven codec IS being a highly efficient hiccup interpreter — it is the efficient answer. What is ruled out is AUTHORING a third one, which the adversarial review identified as the programme's single largest available waste (this repo already holds two: freehand/react.cljs ~1,203 lines with conversion.cljc ~906, and reagent-slim/template.cljs ~1,161). The three capabilities the review found genuinely new — the subscription-to-boundary index, intent-as-data lowering, one-hook-per-boundary — are all REACTIVITY mechanisms, and that is where the six weeks go.

CAVEAT CARRIED FROM THE MEASUREMENT, so nobody misreads it later: Freehand's walk asks per-element questions slim's does not (controlled-input door, caller split, top-layer, declared properties, id-conflict, class/style alias composition). That is a CAPABILITY difference, not merely implementation cost. If Hicasso later needs one of those capabilities, the cost of adding it to slim's codec must be measured rather than assumed — this ruling says slim's codec is cheapest AS MEASURED, not that Freehand's cost buys nothing.
THE P0 STAGED-READ TEAR IS FIXED (rf2-2rtt6.42, PR #7324; recorded by acting mayor). Worth recording HOW, because the shape of the fix is the finding.

THE DIAGNOSIS: the epoch-sum getSnapshot was driven by exactly one counter, and that counter sits downstream of a watch that only exists AFTER commit. For a key nothing holds yet there is no cell, hence no watch, hence no mark-dirty!, hence no bump — getSnapshot answered 0 before the commit and 0 after it, however far the value had moved. React's own post-subscribe re-check therefore had nothing to see.

THE BASELINE-DEREF REMEDY IS NOT A TEAR FIX, confirmed against the code rather than argued: it is ALREADY in acquire-cell! on main. It gives a fresh cell a correct baseline and NO COMPARISON, so it silently adopts the moved value as though it had always been that. It remains the right fix for the spurious first re-render (Arm 1's separate finding) and nothing more. The worker asserted this as a test row rather than a paragraph.

THE FIX — and this is the part to remember: a key with no cell contributes its frame's commit-basis = @!generation + re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch(frame); a cell records the basis it was CREATED at; flush! re-stamps rather than increments. frame-commit-epoch IS THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN observation-port evidence counter, and Spec 006 already uses it verbatim to detect 'the frame's durable state moved in the render->commit gap — without watching anything'. In the worker's words: THE ARM WAS MISSING THE ONE FIELD THE SUBSTRATE HAD ALREADY BUILT. Executable change: SIX LINES plus commit-basis and a snapshot-of accessor.

COST: hooks unchanged at 2; subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else; zero allocation; ZERO in steady state (a mounted boundary holds a reference to every key it reads, so no staged term appears). Conservative only in the safe direction — a boundary mounting exactly as an unrelated write lands re-renders once.

THE TRIPWIRE DID NOT FIRE, and the reasoning is worth preserving: candidate (a), 'compare what the render read', was DELIBERATELY REJECTED because keeping what the render read requires a second render-populated buffer that the commit reconciles — which IS a ledger. Comparing BASES needs no record at all, because React already holds the per-boundary render-time value. That distinction is the difference between a legal fix and a design kill.

WITNESS: 6 rows in arm1/staged_read_tear_cljs_test.cljs against the arm's OWN runtime, plus Case 3 in the DOM test in real Chromium (the staged writer is a sibling boundary writing during the same render pass, so it needs no guess about passive-effect scheduling). Mutation with the fix reverted: test:cljs exit 1 (3 failures, all in the new ns), test:browser exit 1 — 'the real DOM painting stale forever'. After: both exit 0.

STILL OPEN, scoped out with reasons on rf2-2rtt6.44: the :registry-epoch and :node-key axes have no counterpart. Registry — a :sub re-registration is not a frame-state install, and observation/registry-epoch* is ^:private with no public reader, so the arm cannot read it without a substrate change; closing it for a retained key would mean re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration, which is a design decision rather than a defect fix. Node-key — frame/dissoc-frame! clears the commit-epoch entry, so a same-id reincarnation RESTARTS AT 0, making commit-basis monotone only within one incarnation, which is precisely why the observation port carries :node-key as a third field.

MERGE-ORDER NOTE for rf2-2rtt6.43: PR #7323 (already merged) carries generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs, which TRANSCRIBES the three functions #7324 changes — so its row 2 now asserts a defect the arm no longer has. It tests its own copy, so nothing reds, but .43 should RE-POINT it at the arm's runtime rather than repair the transcription.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE LANDED ADAPTER (Arm 1), read-only, origin/main @ 40e309600e — arm1/ and
docs/design/hicasso/ are byte-identical to 6494d6e039; arm1's last commit is 7e40db6481.

BOTTOM LINE. The mechanism survives; the cost model does not, and one named correctness hole is
mischaracterised. I could not move the two-hook budget, could not find a candidate ledger, could
not construct a fourth blind spot in `commit-basis`, and could not make a read outside ANY render
go quiet. The strongest defect is the FIFTH ESCAPE, and the judgement already names it
(studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:237-241) while dismissing it as "not a missing edge
— the reader does re-render": that dismissal is wrong, because a LazySeq caches its realised
values, so the wrong reader re-renders ONCE, does not re-execute the read, drops the edge on the
next commit, and the value is then frozen for the life of the mount — the exact "correct on
screen, frozen thereafter, attributable to nothing" class the same page calls the worst failure
the ruled surface can have. The structural argument meant to make that class impossible ("a seq at
a prop position goes through `clj->js`") is FALSE at the boundary-prop position: `boundary-element`
(front/codec.cljs:341-349) hands the props map through raw, and `realize-children` flattens
exactly one level. Two further real findings: the read-set entry cache degrades to an O(N) scan
selected by read ORDER (an undocumented authoring detail, on the bulk K=100/300 rung), and
`record-reads`'s set difference — the operation HD-002(b) is discharged against — is never
exercised by the wired runtime, because every re-subscribe mints a fresh registration id and
therefore always diffs against the empty set, making a one-key change a full teardown+rebuild.

VERDICTS. (1) two hooks at 1/7/20 — SURVIVES, honestly measured at React's dispatcher with an
explicit UNWITNESSED failure path; the COST model sold with it does not. (2) no candidate ledger
— SURVIVES; entries are keyed purely by content, `refs` is a commit count, and the macrotask
reaper opens no disagreement window (walked three interleavings). (3) staged-read tear —
SURVIVES, and more strongly than claimed: the epoch sum is term-wise monotone so collision is
impossible, all three `replace-container!` sites bump, and there is no `reg-sub-raw`, so
rf2-2rtt6.44's two axes really are the two (corroboration + one refinement noted there).
(4) "Surface B is preferred, MEASURED" — PARTLY SUPPORTED: DOM parity and the collector<grouped
edge count are real, but the edge count is an efficiency reading against the arm the operator
removed, and nothing is measured against the surviving raw-UIx control; the preference itself is
an argued judgement, which the page is honest about. (5) the loud-error guard — BROKEN, see above.

WHAT SURVIVED: the two-hook budget; the tripwire; `commit-basis`'s completeness and the generation
fence including the mid-body staged move; the four witnessed escapes; the correct rejection of
"acquire without deref"; teardown symmetry (a stale cleanup cannot release a successor's cell);
and the parity plumbing probe that turned the ambient-frame bug into a finding.

BEADS FILED: rf2-2rtt6.45 (P1, the fifth escape, with a full reproduction and a recommended fix
that does NOT need per-boundary render identity), rf2-2rtt6.46 (P2, the O(N) entry-cache scan +
`:read-set-entry` misfiled as `:shared`, which will mis-price rf2-2rtt6.34's heap axis),
rf2-2rtt6.47 (P2, the dead edge diff and the re-subscribe cliff), rf2-2rtt6.48 (P3, the DOM
residue gates cannot fail — `mount/release!` resets the runtime before the assertion, and
React-driven teardown is unwitnessed anywhere).

Full review, with file:line for every claim and the list of what source could not settle:
ai/findings/2026-08-01.hicasso-landed-adapter-adversarial-review.md (gitignored, do not link).
A CAPABILITY GAP OF THE RULED ARCHITECTURE IS NOW MEASURED — rf2-n3dxw (P1), found by rf2-m6if4 while porting Arm 2's controlled-restore witnesses onto the shipped React adapter (PR #7327). Recorded by acting mayor 2026-08-01.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. Arm 2's decisive controlled-input row was :unchanged-model-rejection — the user types a character the model refuses, NOTHING re-renders, and the field still converges back to the model with the caret at the position before the refused character. Arm 2 (the dropped own-renderer) DEMONSTRATED this in real Chromium. Ported to the shipped React adapter it DOES NOT HOLD: the model refuses and nothing re-renders (both correct), but THE REFUSED CHARACTER STAYS ON SCREEN. The repro is committed and the test asserts the measured value naming the bead, so it cannot be forgotten.

TWO RELATED ASSERTIONS WENT WITH IT: a range selection across a converge that writes measured [2 2] against Arm 2's [2 5] (folded into rf2-n3dxw); and :ime-composition-commits-nothing was DROPPED as not established either way, because synthetic Events do not exercise React's composition path and an undemonstrated fence is worse than none. That is the right call and is recorded as such.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE OPERATOR'S RULING. Mike dropped Arm 2 on product direction, explicitly not on measurement, and the record says Arm 2 MET its hard gate. This finding sharpens what that trade actually costs: the own-renderer owned end-of-event convergence off React's discrete-event path and could therefore restore a refused character; the React adapter does not get that for free, and on this evidence does not get it at all without further work. NOT a reason to revisit the ruling — it is a consequence of it, now priced rather than assumed, and the operator should see the price.

ALSO WORTH KEEPING: the same port found that :same-turn-echo is NOT free on React either — re-frame.core/dispatch drains on a macrotask by design, so the queued door cannot echo inside the discrete event; the SYNCHRONOUS door buys it. Both doors are witnessed. Eight of the eleven ported assertions are green on React.

A PREMISE OF MINE WAS FALSIFIED, recorded so it is not repeated: rf2-m6if4 asserted that Arm 2's five DOM suites taxed the PR-blocking browser lane's 360 s ceiling. Measured on one machine in one session: with arm2 948 tests in 31 s / 29 s; without 889 tests in 29 / 29 / 28 s. NO measurable run-phase cost at the +/-3 s noise floor. What did move is COMPILE: 1,087 -> 1,073 namespaces, cold compile 70 s -> 65 s. The tree still goes, on the operator's ruling — but the wall-clock justification I wrote into the bead was wrong and the worker reported it rather than letting it stand.
THE CONTROLLED-INPUT DEFECT IS NOT A REACT DEFECT — IT IS CROSS-ADAPTER INTERFERENCE (rf2-n3dxw investigation, PR #7330; recorded by acting mayor 2026-08-01). This is the most consequential finding of the night and it reaches beyond Hicasso.

REACT DOES NOT LOSE THE REFUSED CHARACTER. Read out of react-dom 19.2.0 in this repo with line numbers: createAndAccumulateChangeEvent records the target; batchedUpdates$1's finally flushes sync work then calls restoreStateOfTarget, which hands the committed props to updateInput, which assigns element.value whenever it differs — ALL BEFORE dispatchEvent RETURNS, with ZERO boundary body runs. Measured: field '12', caret [2 2]. React's restore machinery works.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: UIx PICKS ITS INPUT IMPLEMENTATION FROM THE CLASSPATH. uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input branches on uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?, which asks 'is reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive* PRESENT and false?'. Every :browser-test bundle carries Reagent, so the branch takes the Reagent port — which makes the element UNCONTROLLED (value deleted, defaultValue + ref installed) so React's restore has nothing to restore, and drives the value from reagent.impl.batching/do-after-render, a requestAnimationFrame queue. ONE FRAME LATE. Found by dumping the node's committed React props and seeing defaultValue + a ref where the view wrote :value; narrowing the build to one namespace without Reagent flipped the row green instantly.

THE GENERALISED HAZARD, filed as rf2-heqwo (P1, NEEDS MIKE'S RULING): A CONSUMER'S CHOICE OF A SECOND ADAPTER SILENTLY CHANGES THE FIRST ONE'S INPUTS. An app that adds Reagent alongside UIx changes how UIx's controlled inputs behave, with no diagnostic and no opt-in. That is not a Hicasso question — it is a shipped-adapter question about this repo's own multi-adapter story, and the fix is reportedly one set! once ruled.

FALSE COMFORT CORRECTED: two rows that were quietly green were MEASURING THE PORT, NOT REACT. They are now pinned per row via uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?* with BOTH implementations measured, so neither can masquerade as the other again. Tripwire mutation: pin neutered -> exit 1 with 7 assertions red; restored -> exit 0.

rf2-n3dxw STAYS OPEN, honestly: NEITHER shipped path gives BOTH same-turn convergence AND the caret at the position before the refused character. React converges in-turn but throws the caret to the end ('12345'+z at [2 2] -> [5 5]). The port gets the caret right one frame late. The priced option (rf2-fki5d, P2) is converge!, measured green on all five rows in one turn — cost one flushSync per keystroke, a per-instance last-rendered value, sync door only, and NO user-visible ref/effect/hook. Its naive form regresses the ordinary keystroke, and that trap is MEASURED rather than assumed.

RANGE SELECTION answered and scoped rather than fixed: Arm 2 wanted [2 5]; React gives [7 7], the port [2 2] — a range collapses BY CONSTRUCTION on both. Asserted on both with the reason. IME left dropped with the reason strengthened (two implementations now face composition differently), filed as rf2-o27h3 with the CDP harness that would settle it.
OPERATOR RULING — THE PROGRAMME CONTINUES (Mike, 2026-08-01, verbatim: 'Keep going with Hicasso'). Recorded by acting mayor.

RULED AGAINST THIS EVIDENCE, so the record is honest about what was known when the call was made:
  - MOUNT 1.2107x Reagent-on-subs [0.9756-1.7208] — above the <=1.0x win condition and above the restated 1.0150x M1 red zone. Five runs, all above parity, none below.
  - PER-KEYSTROKE indistinguishable from both donors; all three arms are one frame.
  - BULK K=100/300 AND NARROW refused — no control held.
  - PER-READ RETAINED HEAP: a real structural win (-708 B/read same-substrate, 23.8% margin, crossover at R=1.29) that still MISSES the K3 floor (1,363 vs 943 B/read, 1.44x) and the <1 KB shell target (1,143 B).
  - AND every older clock figure is under audit (rf2-8nqsl) after the in-page/frame-inclusive divergence finding.

HD-008's stop rule is therefore NOT invoked. The operator has weighed a mount deficit, a missed floor, a missed shell target and two refused rows, and continued.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO: it does not relax any bar line, and it does not make a refused row publishable. rf2-2rtt6.1's criteria stand as written and as relaxed by the 2026-08-01 mount ruling.

WHERE THE EFFORT SHOULD GO, given the deficit is LOCATED rather than diffuse: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. It is the runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements, which is the interpreted-vs-compiled cost HD-008 already identified from the other side. That is a concrete, attackable target rather than a mystery. It also means rf2-aqgr2 (the 415 B/read decomposition) stays DEPRIORITISED — no per-read byte count explains a codec walk.

SEQUENCING FROM HERE: (1) rf2-8nqsl, running now — the audit of every previously published clock row, because the baseline the deficit is measured against may itself move; (2) rf2-rguy1, the external krausest/js-framework-benchmark cross-check, upgraded in urgency by the clock worker's own advice — it is the independent check on our harness; (3) rf2-cvvb7, the segment seam that swung 3.8% -> 34% on machine load alone; then the remaining construction work (rf2-2rtt6.41's witness remainder, rf2-2rtt6.44's epoch axes, rf2-fki5d's in-turn converge, rf2-n3dxw).
OPERATOR RULING, SECOND AFFIRMATION — THE PROGRAMME CONTINUES (Mike, 2026-08-02, verbatim: 'programme continues'). Recorded by acting mayor.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT DECISION FROM THE FIRST 'keep going' (2026-08-01), and the record should not blur them. The first was ruled against a mount deficit of 1.2107x. THIS ONE IS RULED AGAINST 1.4896x — the corrected figure after three instrument defects were found and fixed. The operator has now continued the programme TWICE, the second time on worse evidence than the first.

THE EVIDENCE AS IT STANDS AT THIS RULING, on instruments whose behaviour is now understood:
  MOUNT 1.4896x — deficit real and larger than first published; corroborated in DIRECTION by an external instrument (krausest/js-framework-benchmark, its own driver, its own app) at 1.1756x, with the residual gap attributed to a workload leg (~7-17%, loose) and an instrument leg (8.8%, mechanism published) rather than left unexplained.
  NARROW 0.72-0.76x — A GENUINE WIN, agreed by two independent instruments. This is the programme's only positive clock row.
  BULK — REFUSED. Sign-changing between configurations (bulk100 raw 1.1089x vs taskNet 0.9859x); control held 3 of 7.
  PER-KEYSTROKE — all arms one frame, indistinguishable; verified UNCORRUPTED by the door defect.
  PER-READ RETAINED HEAP — a real structural win (-708 B/read same-substrate vs UIx, 23.8% margin, crossover R=1.29) that still MISSES the K3 floor (1,363 vs 943 B/read, 1.44x) and the <1 KB shell target (1,143 B).
  BULK-BROAD 0.6291x — WITHDRAWN. Four frame-inclusive readings near parity; the published figure was the ratio of the arms' SCRIPT quoted as the ratio of their OPERATIONS.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO: it does not relax any bar line, does not make a refused row publishable, and does not settle rf2-2rtt6.50 (the render->commit-gap first registration) or rf2-5dut1 (Xray unpublishable while it depends on Freehand). HD-008's stop rule remains uninvoked rather than repealed.

WHERE EFFORT SHOULD GO, given the deficit is LOCATED: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. It is the runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements: the interpreted-versus-compiled cost HD-008 identified from the other side. That is attackable. rf2-aqgr2 (the 415 B/read decomposition) stays DEPRIORITISED — no per-read byte count explains a codec walk.

IMMEDIATE SEQUENCING: rf2-7iqb5 + rf2-5xrcd first (ctl-2x is mis-specified and BLOCKS bulk adjudication; the re-adjudication worker showed the specified fix cannot work — one additive constant fits all four rows and doubling the changed set leaves it untouched, so a THREE-POINT control differencing c away is required). Then rf2-aj15b and rf2-ymi6j (figures and band calibration taken on the frame-only clock). Then rf2-ph85f (HD-008 donor rows and bulk narrow, still in-page).
STANDING DIRECTIVE — MINE THE PRIOR ART (Mike, 2026-08-02, verbatim: 'When considering implementation or design decisions, keep freehand and re-frame.ui in mind. Plus replicant from a data oriented point of view. Make sure you mine them for ideas. As well as Reagent, and Uix itself of course.'). Recorded by acting mayor; goes into every Hicasso design/implementation brief from now on.

THE FIVE SOURCES AND WHAT EACH IS GOOD FOR:
  - FREEHAND (implementation/freehand/) — the shipped interpreted substrate this programme is measured against. Its codec question is already settled (Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's), but its DESIGN decisions — the controlled-input door, caller split, declared properties, the roster of callback contracts it needed and Hicasso collapsed — are the map of problems any interpreted view layer must answer. When Hicasso hits a design fork, check what Freehand did and WHY before choosing.
  - RE-FRAME.UI (implementation/ui/) — the EXPERIMENTAL compiled-view substrate. It is the other pole: what a compiler can do that an interpreter cannot (and rf2-2rtt6.41 already used its analyzer's :rf.ui.compile/sub-in-loop refusal as proof a compiler cannot deliver Surface B). Mine it for what compilation bought that the runtime should approximate cheaply, and for the analysis passes whose LESSONS transfer even where their mechanism cannot.
  - REPLICANT — from a DATA-ORIENTED point of view specifically (Mike ruled 2026-07-31 it is 'just an example, not an objective'). Its relevant ideas: pure-data hiccup all the way down, lifecycle as data (mount/unmount hooks in attributes — the ::h/mounting/::h/unmounting presence design is already in this family), event handlers as data. The in-band [::h/prevent ...] head ruling is exactly this school: behaviour carried IN the data where = can see it, not beside it where it cannot.
  - REAGENT — the incumbent. Its default shouldComponentUpdate (value-equality bail-out on props) is DIRECT prior art for the HD-006 memo ruling on rf2-2rtt6.52 — the cascade Hicasso just hit is precisely what Reagent's default stops. Also: ratom deref-capture (the 943 B/read floor nothing beats), cursor/track granularity, and its known losses (the charter's 'Known losses coming from Reagent' section).
  - UIX — the React parent. Its per-hook useSyncExternalStore pattern is what Hicasso's one-hook-plus-index beats on fan-out; its input wrapper (three hooks per input) is what the element-path converge beats; its classpath input-selection defect (rf2-heqwo) is the cautionary tale about implicit selection. Mine it for React-19 integration technique — it is the closest thing to a reference for driving React from CLJS without a legacy adapter.

HOW TO USE THIS IN BRIEFS: when a bead involves a design decision, name which of the five have faced the same decision and what each chose, BEFORE proposing. A choice that contradicts all five needs an argument; a choice one of them already made and regretted needs the regret cited.

Resolves the ripeness dispute between the P2 dossier's two recommendation sections; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-2rtt6.p2-graduation-ruling.md deleted after this note.

K1 - now SCOREABLE (the "two serious iterations" happened) but not yet SCORED. Operative gate = the 2026-08-02 MOUNT GATE AMENDMENT (<=1.10x direct UIx, canonical M1, clock of record). Post-fix rows: acceptance 1.1884x [1.1223-1.2660] FAILS (whole range above); feed 1.0737x [0.9669-1.1859] instrument-limited, mean below the line; ordinary instrument-limited + control fail. title: perf+scope: check_ambient_durable_reads walk is 7.0s on a built checkout, but pruning NARROWS the gate — needs a ruling
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-76c76 (PR #7539), which measured all nine shared-walk checkers and shipped three of them.

check_ambient_durable_reads is the BIGGEST single win of the nine and the only
one deliberately left on the table.

MEASURED (median of 5, live --verbose arm, python 3.14, Windows):
  clean checkout (== what CI runs) : 0.63s
  built mayor checkout            : 8.37s   <- of which 7.00s is the walk alone
  walk isolated                   : 7.00s -> 0.16s under a pruning os.walk

It scans repo_root (the WHOLE repo), so it is the most expensive walk of the
nine: it enumerates ~48k vendor/build entries to reach 18 allow-listed files.

WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED. Unlike its eight siblings it has NO _EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES.
It excludes build/vendor trees only INCIDENTALLY, via DURABLE_WRITE_SUFFIXES
matched with str.endswith(). So adding a prune is not a no-op refactor - it is a
scope change to a required invariant gate:

  a copy of a durable-write source file nested inside out/ or .shadow-cljs/ or
  node_modules/ is scanned TODAY (endswith matches the tail of the path) and
  would NOT be after pruning.

PROVEN, not assumed. rf2-76c76's equivalence harness planted 396 known-violating
fixtures inside every excluded directory, including the pathological
'<excluded>/vendored/implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc'
shape. Old vs new --verbose stdout diverged by exactly 12 findings, ALL of them
that planted population; all 4 genuine live findings identical. On the REAL built
tree the prune drops 0 of 18 files.

THE RULING NEEDED: is a durable-write source file copied into a build cache in
scope for EP-0010's ambient-read gate?
  - If NO (my read, and what all eight siblings already assume): add
    _EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES = {node_modules,target,out,.shadow-cljs,.git,.beads,.cpcache}
    and prune it in os.walk. ~7s off every local test-fast-pr.sh run on a
    long-lived checkout. The genuine violation is still caught at its real path;
    only DUPLICATE reports of the same violation against a generated artefact go.
  - If YES, close this as wontfix and the 7s stays.

NOTE it is ~0.6s in CI either way - CI runs these in bare-checkout Python jobs
with no npm ci and no build. This is purely a local-lane fix.

The three-line change and its equivalence harness are described in PR #7539.

title: hicasso: Spec 009's view-trace pair needs an instance-token, which needs a third hook (HD-020 conflict) -- RULING
description:
# The Spec 009 view-trace pair cannot be emitted by a boundary shell under the ≤2-hook budget

FOUND while delivering rf2-2rtt6.125 (Performance `:render` for `defview`). The Performance half landed; **goal 2 of that bead — the `:view/render` / `:rf.view/rendered` trace pair — is blocked by an architectural conflict, not by effort.**

## The conflict, stated from both documents

Both view ops require `:rf.view/render-key` = `[view-id instance-token]`:

- Spec 009 §Trace ops: `:rf.view/render` carries `:tags {:frame <id> :rf.view/render-key [<view-id> <instance-token>]}`. `:rf.view/rendered` carries the same tuple plus `:rf.view/mount?`, which is **keyed off it** ("stable across an instance's re-renders and fresh per new instance").
- Spec-Schemas §`:renders`: "the second slot is an integer instance-token minted at mount time from a runtime counter atom".
- Spec 009 §`:rf.view/unmounted` already states how the **React-hook family** obtains one: *"The instance-token is minted into a `useRef` so the `:rf.view/render-key` tuple is stable across re-renders."*

A `useRef` is a **third hook**. HD-020(b) spends the whole ≤2 budget on `useContext` (frame) + `useSyncExternalStore` (subscription/epoch), and `arm1.runtime`'s ns docstring is explicit that this is load-bearing rather than incidental: *"no per-instance render-phase state at all … React offers a function component no per-instance storage except a hook cell, so a shell that wants one has spent a third hook (`useRef`/`useState`) before it starts."* `arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test` counts hooks at React's own dispatcher, so a third hook fails a test rather than a review.

## Why there is no side door

- **The `useSyncExternalStore` registration** is minted inside `subscribe`, which React calls at **commit** — after the body has run, and never at all on a render that does not commit. `:rf.view/render` fires at render START. It cannot supply a render-phase identity, and on a first render it does not exist.
- **The module-level `rstate`** carries the running frame and the scratch read-set. It has no per-instance axis and cannot grow one without becoming per-instance storage.
- **The memo wrapper** is per-element, not per-instance.
- **React's current fiber** (via internals, as `arm1/hook_probe.cljs` reaches for the dispatcher) is double-buffered — React alternates between two fiber objects for one instance — so it is neither stable nor shippable.

## Why a degenerate token is NOT the answer

Emitting `[view-id nil]` for every boundary would collapse every instance of a view into one row in Xray's Views panel, and `:rf.view/mount?` — which is derived from the render-key's stability — would be meaningless. That is precisely the shape rf2-2rtt6.91 ruled against on the render hash: *"A degenerate value is worse than an absent one: an absent key cannot be mistaken for evidence, a constant one is a fail-open gate wearing the shape of a check."* Nothing was emitted for that reason.

## What a decision looks like

This is a genuine ruling, not an implementation task. The options, none of them free:

1. **Spend the third hook** in the boundary shell (`useRef` for the instance token), gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` so production still costs two. React does **not** permit a conditionally-called hook — the gate would have to be compile-time (`goog.DEBUG`), which makes the dev shell and the prod shell two different shells. HD-020's budget would need an explicit dev-build carve-out.
2. **Weaken the trace contract**: make `:rf.view/render-key` `[view-id nil]`-legal and document `:rf.view/mount?` as absent on substrates without instance identity, i.e. accept a documented *subset* (the bead's own escape hatch — "an explicit, witnessed subset documented if any field is substrate-impossible"). Costs Xray's per-instance Views rows on Hicasso pages.
3. **Ship Hicasso without the view-trace pair** and say so — Performance `:render` (delivered) plus React DevTools plus the arm's own `body-runs` instrument, which is always-on and counts real body runs.
4. **Find a render-phase instance identity React actually offers a function component.** As of React 19 there is none that is stable and public. `useId` is a hook.

## Not blocked on

`rf2-2rtt6.125`'s Performance half is delivered and merged independently (PR #7524). This blocks only the trace half and any claim that Hicasso is a full peer for the Xray Views timeline.
notes:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:01 AUSEST (delegated dossier-review pass; operator-overturnable) — OPTION (3): the bench arm ships WITHOUT the :rf.view/render / :rf.view/rendered trace pair, and says so. No degenerate emission of any kind: no [view-id nil] render-key, no absent-or-false mount? through the current pipeline, no fabricated token on :rf.view/unmounted. Absence, never a constant.

WHY (2) FELL — the dossier's main rec was mispriced; verified against the consumer. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc: [view-id nil] does NOT crash (rows are index-keyed) but FABRICATES twice: (a) view-rows' {render-key => render-args} accumulator (~L2632-2693) aliases simultaneously-mounted instances of one view — the panel diffs instance A's props against instance B's = false instance evidence; (b) render-cause (~L2552) reads (true? mount?) — absent mount? classifies every MOUNT as :props '<- parent re-render', wrong cause + wrong mount/re-render stripe (view.cljs ~L1430). Exactly the .91 class ('a constant one is a fail-open gate wearing the shape of a check' — quote verified verbatim). Making (2) honest = marked aggregation shape + spec edits (009 L283: mount? 'Always present'; Spec-Schemas L4347: tuple REQUIRED on :renders rows) + Xray branches suppressing prev-args diff/cause on tokenless rows — a mini-project buying a permanently second-class panel. The Codex section's critique of naked (2) is VERIFIED CORRECT.

WHY NOT (1) NOW — Codex's dev-only useRef is technically sound (uSES registration is commit-time; Rules of Hooks force two compile-time-selected shells; prod DCE preserves the heap claim) but it forks the arm's most defended invariant with ZERO precedent: HD-020(b) carries no build qualifier ('never useRef — a third hook in the shell is a budget breach'), arm1/runtime.cljs claims 'no per-instance render-phase state at all' as a design property, arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test counts at React's dispatcher (exactly 2, neither useRef nor useState, count independent of read count), and a forbidden-token roster (runtime.cljs ~L1953) pins 'no useRef anywhere in the shell'. Every prior hook spend was priced OUTSIDE the shell (presence's 3, controlled shadow's per-field useState, host gate's 1, class boundary's contextType costing none). A dev/prod shell fork to buy a dev-tool nicety while K1/K2 are open inverts priorities on a bench arm.

WHY (3) IS FREE AND HONEST — verified: views-step is conditional (nil when no view-render AND no unmount events — step OMITTED; projection.cljc ~L2729) and the Reactive panel's reader-join (reactive_panel_subs.cljs ~L325) unions view-ids off :rf.view/rendered ops, degrading to empty reader lists. Absence cannot be mistaken for evidence. Zero consumer change, zero spec edit, HD-020(b) + both witnesses byte-identical. Coverage stated: Performance :render measures MERGED (PR #7524) + the arm's always-on body-runs instrument + React DevTools. The stated gap: Xray's VIEWS step and per-sub reader lists do not populate for Hicasso pages.

GRADUATION CLAUSE (named so it cannot be lost) — when the product shell for implementation/hicasso/ is minted, re-price deliberately: (1) dev-only useRef (Codex sketch is the reference: two compile-time-selected component fns with fixed hook order, two-ledger witness by build, advanced-bundle elision gate proving ref/token/trace machinery absent in prod — if the gate cannot prove absence, fall back) VS an honestly-MARKED tokenless subset (:rf.view/rendered carrying view-id + deref-subs serves per-view aggregation AND the reader-join without instance claims — needs Spec-Schemas change + Xray branches suppressing prev-args diff/cause; priced above, not cheap) VS staying dark. Any non-full-pair outcome amends Spec 009 (mount? 'Always present' + the uniform-wrapper sentence) and Spec-Schemas §:renders — spec/* is HOT-ZONE: sequence that edit, never batch. No spec sentence is needed NOW: the spec's view-trace claims scope over the shipped adapters; the bench arm is not claimed by them.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-08-05: option (3) — ship the bench arm without the view-trace pair, stated; no degenerate [view-id nil] emission ever (verified to fabricate evidence in Xray's epoch projection); HD-020(b) + witnesses untouched; graduation clause in the ruling note re-prices dev-only useRef vs marked tokenless subset when the product shell is minted. No implementation follows from this ruling.

title: hicasso: a fallback is NOT inert markup — a defview head in :ssr {:fallback ...} renders a live boundary
description:
FOUND while pricing rf2-l0wfx (docs/design/hicasso/defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md). mint-host-gate!'s docstring states the rule the guide teaches: 'a fallback is inert markup — it is not a body, so a subscription or an intent written there is the same loud error it would be anywhere outside a boundary.' MEASURED, both arms, via react-dom/server renderToString on the arm1 bench: [:button {:on-click [:x/y]} "go"] in a fallback -> :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary (enforced, as documented) [some-defview {}] in a fallback -> mints fine; renders a LIVE boundary server-side that READS SUBSCRIPTIONS

SUBTREE

quarterly

WHY. The fallback is walked once at MINT time, outside any frame binding, so an intent vector lowered eagerly there fails. A boundary head does NOT lower eagerly: it creates a React element whose body runs later, inside the boundary's own with-frame, taking its frame from React context. So it is frame-CORRECT — the rule is simply narrower than it reads. WHY IT MATTERS. This is currently the only recovery for rf2-l0wfx: an author who wants a provider's subtree in the server response writes it a second time as the declaration's fallback. That works today by accident of the walk's laziness, not by ruling. RULING NEEDED. Either (a) it is a feature and the docstring + guide say a fallback may carry a boundary (and what a boundary in a fallback may and may not do), or (b) it is a hole and a boundary head in a fallback is refused at the declaration alongside the intent. Doing neither leaves a documented rule that is half-true and a workaround nobody sanctioned. NOT a blocker for rf2-l0wfx: every candidate there is unaffected by which way this goes.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7525 (2026-08-05): UPDATE EXACT RULING OWNER, NOT A DUPLICATE. PR #7525 disproves the older simply-narrower/frame-correct framing: one declaration renders different content per frame and after a write, while a frame-fed view bakes nil at mint and throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop. The mint-time rule is about what the walk evaluates, not inertness. Evidence is pinned in fallback_contents_cljs_test and the provider costing addendum; the ruling stays open and should be taken with rf2-l0wfx.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MEASURED AND PINNED — PR #7525. No ruling taken; the ruling is still yours. THE ANSWER IS NONE OF (a)/(b) AS FRAMED: the rule is ABSENT, not narrow. What is enforced is not a rule about CONTENT but about the WALK. The fallback is walked into an element once, at the declaration, outside any frame — so what is refused is exactly what that walk can EVALUATE: intent vector -> :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary a `sub` call in form -> :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render non-hiccup -> :rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector a defview head -> MINTS; renders a live boundary, subscription read a defhost head -> MINTS; renders that host's own gate + fallback a FRAME-FED defview -> MINTS; throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop mid-render A boundary head is neither an intent nor a subscription — it is an element whose body runs later — so the walk never looks inside it, and every refusal it carries is deferred past the declaration. That is the one thing the mint-time walk exists to prevent. It is not `defview`-specific: a `defhost` head crosses identically, so the hole is DEFERRAL. TWO NEW FACTS THAT DECIDE IT — neither was on the record. 1. THE DECLARED PLACEHOLDER IS NOT A VALUE. One declaration, walked once into one element, renders three different documents: frame A ...

ALPHA

... frame B ...

BRAVO

... frame A, one write ...

ALPHA-TWO

... mint-host-gate! walks once and reuses the element everywhere, and its stated reason is "a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder." A boundary head makes it differ per site AND per write. The design's own justification is falsified by what the design permits. 2. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THIS ARM'S OTHER BOUNDARY VARIANT. Arm 1 ships two mints: mint-view! (context-fed, what `defview` mints) and mint-frame-prop-view! (rf2-2rtt6.39, which frees a hook slot in a fully spent <=2 budget). A frame-fed head reads intent/*frame* when its ELEMENT is created — in a fallback that is MINT TIME, where the var is nil. So it bakes nil in, mints happily, and throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop one render into the server response. The two heads are indistinguishable in hiccup. => whether a boundary head in a fallback works AT ALL is a property of WHICH MINT the head came from. That removes "bless it as it stands" from the table: what you would be blessing is variant-dependent. If rf2-2rtt6.39 ever wins its measurement, the workaround dies silently. WHERE THE EVIDENCE POINTS (recommendation, not a ruling): the codec's own stated law — walk once, reuse everywhere, BECAUSE a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder — entails option (b), inert markup. The refusal would be walk-scoped and would catch the frame-fed case for free. WHY THAT WAS NOT LANDED: it deletes rf2-l0wfx's only recovery, and l0wfx is an open P1 awaiting your :ssr ruling. Both directions constrain it — refusing empties candidate D (whose content IS this workaround) and so favours A/B; blessing sanctions "write your subtree twice" and so favours D. Not this bead's to pre-empt. ALSO: the workaround is WORSE than defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md priced it. Not merely duplication + wrong context value server-side + remount at adoption, but additionally variant-fragile and in violation of the placeholder invariant. LANDED (PR #7525) — docstrings only on the executable side, no hook added, ordinary render path byte-identical: - arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs (new): 4 tests, 12 assertions, every row above. Written as a record of TODAY, explicitly not a contract, so the ruling is an edit there and never a silence. - front/codec.cljs: mint-host-gate!'s docstring no longer asserts "a fallback is inert markup" as enforced; states what is, marks the gap UNRULED, names the l0wfx dependency and the frame-fed fragility. - arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs: five lines of ns docstring pointing at the new suite ("neither stated nor discoverable" was half this bead). Three mutation proofs, each run, codec restored from a byte copy after each: bind *dispatch* around the mint walk (option (a)'s shape) -> 1 failure force `placeholder` to nil -> 9 failures boundary-element refuses a nil-frame frame-fed head ((b)) -> 2 errors NOT touched: draft-guide/**, spec/**, decisions.md, validation.md, implementation/core/. The guide never made the false promise — it says "placeholder markup" / "a skeleton", not "refused" — so it needs an edit only if the ruling goes toward (b). STILL OPEN. Needs your ruling on (a) vs (b), and it should probably be taken together with rf2-l0wfx rather than ahead of it.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: RULED 2026-08-05 20:02 AUSEST, together with rf2-l0wfx (full ruling + implementation brief recorded there; operator-overturnable). This bead's half: (b') — INERT MARKUP ENFORCED. A declared :ssr fallback is walked structurally at mint and a boundary head OR host head anywhere in it is REFUSED at the declaration — new id :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head, naming the host, the offending head's displayName and its position. This is walk-scoped, catches the frame-fed nil-bake variant for free (it is a boundary head), deletes the which-mint-did-the-head-come-from inconsistency, and restores the walk-once law's own justification. (d') rejected: the placeholder-is-not-a-value and per-mint-variance measurements (PR #7525, pinned in arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test) remove "bless it as it stands". The workaround this refusal deletes is superseded: l0wfx is ruled as a THIRD :ssr value, :ssr :render (NOT :children — refuted on the costing doc's measured wrong-context-default + reasoned adoption-remount evidence), so a provider's subtree reaches the server response the honest way — the component itself renders server-side with the correct context value, no duplication, no remount. fallback_contents_cljs_test flips from record-of-today to CONTRACT: defview-head, defhost-head and frame-fed rows assert the mint-time refusal; intent/sub/non-hiccup rows unchanged. One worker implements both halves in one PR (same gate region) per the brief on rf2-l0wfx.

title: re-frame.ui: rule on whether compiled view bodies adopt core's ambient-frame refusal tier (same silent-freeze class as rf2-2rtt6.122, one substrate over)
description:
FOUND while building the ambient-frame refusal tier for rf2-2rtt6.122 (PR #7513, merged code
below is on that branch). NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING — it is a behaviour change to a shipped
substrate, not a mechanical follow-on.

THE TIER NOW EXISTS AND IS GENERAL. `re-frame.frame/call-with-ambient-frame-refused` +
`frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` let ANY substrate declare "no ambient frame is legal in this
dynamic extent"; `resolve-current-frame` withdraws the React-context tier while it is set (a
carried stamp still carries) and `require-current-frame!` raises
`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`. Hicasso is wired. Wiring a second substrate is ~3 lines.

RE-FRAME.UI HAS THE IDENTICAL LAW AND THE IDENTICAL SILENT HAZARD, verified file:line:

  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:20-27` — render RESOLVES + PROBES *without
    ownership* via `reactive/with-capture`; the LAYOUT commit acquires the captured targets, and
    abandoned renders "acquire no ownership and publish no speculative capture state".
  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/substrate.cljs:18-20` — compiled views' "sole read owner
    is `re-frame.ui.reactive` (probe/acquire/read/release)"; `:75-79` the legacy `use-subscribe`
    surface is "deliberately not exported".
  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:1059-1098` — `with-capture` binds ONLY its
    own `*ambient*`. `rf/subscribe` knows nothing about it, so an ambient read in a compiled view
    body contributes ZERO to the capture: no dependency edge, no ViewCell revision advance, no
    repaint.
  - AND IT RESOLVES ANYWAY: `substrate.cljs:26-45,:66-72` publishes the React-context reader
    through the `:adapter/current-frame` late-bind hook, so under any `frame-provider` /
    `frame-root` an ambient `rf/subscribe` in a compiled view body succeeds silently and bumps a
    ref-count with no matching release (`subs.cljc:514-543`) during the render phase — a
    StrictMode double-render double-bumps and an abandoned render leaks.

So it is the same silent-freeze class rf2-2rtt6.122 just closed for Hicasso, one substrate over.

WHY IT WAS NOT WIRED IN #7513, deliberately: re-frame.ui is SHIPPED (experimental, but shipped),
and turning an ambient read in a compiled view body from silently-working into throwing is a
behaviour change for any consumer who wrote one. rf2-2rtt6.122's ruling authorised the tier and
Hicasso's use of it; generalising to a second substrate is its own call. Census of in-tree
occurrences was not taken — take it before ruling.

THE DECISION: does re-frame.ui establish the refusing extent around a compiled view body's
render (the same one-line `binding` fusion Hicasso used in `front.intent/with-frame` — here it
would fuse into `reactive/with-capture`, which already binds), or does re-frame.ui accept that
ambient reads in compiled bodies silently produce no edge and document it?

NOT IN SCOPE HERE, and settled the other way: the three shipped ADAPTERS (Reagent, reagent-slim,
UIx) must NOT get this tier. For Reagent / reagent-slim the render body IS the reactive context
(`reagent2/ratom.cljs:87-93` — a deref inside it is how a Reaction discovers dependencies) and
UIx documents ambient reads as the norm (`adapter/uix.cljs:139-160`). Ambient subscribe is
correct there.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:00 AUSEST (delegated dossier review, operator-overturnable): DEFER — do NOT wire the refusal tier into the present re-frame.ui donor; the proposed ~3-line fix is INERT, not merely cheap. Re-scope this bead: the SUCCESSOR compiled substrate implements the refusal at absorption (EP-0036 F3+), after sanctioned compiled reads carry their frame EXPLICITLY.

VERIFICATION (all Codex claims checked against tree, file:line):
(a) VERIFIED — viewcell.cljs:324-345 with-current-frame binds frame/*current-frame* to the ViewCell frame around EVERY compiled body (all 5 wrappers: :399,:412,:433,:450,:467); deliberate, commit 4580267a15 (rf2-4rwtd 2026-07-20) fixing :rf.error/no-frame-context under ratom-family hosts.
(b) VERIFIED — frame.cljc:691-697: armed refusal collapses resolve-current-frame to the CARRIED tier — (frame-value->id (current-frame)) — so *current-frame* still answers; only the React-context tier withdraws. Hicasso works because front/intent.cljs:342-347 binds its OWN *frame* + *dispatch* + *ambient-frame-refusal* and NEVER core's *current-frame* (tier 1 empty → refusal bites). The .122 witness suite itself proves the inertness: ambient_refusal_cljs_test.cljs:192-207 asserts a *current-frame* binding (rf/with-frame) resolves raw rf/subscribe INSIDE a refused extent by design. viewcell is exactly that binding → wrapping with-capture in call-with-ambient-frame-refused would let raw rf/subscribe keep resolving = false confidence, worse than no fence.
(c) VERIFIED — observation.cljc:1606-1611: resolve-target calls frame/require-current-frame! when site-ctx has no :frame pin, and reactive.cljc:1045-1047 builds site-ctx WITHOUT one — sanctioned compiled sub depends on ambient resolution. Removing/sentineling the viewcell binding breaks sanctioned subs; real enforcement = thread the resolved frame into the observation target (site-ctx :frame) / substrate-owned capture, i.e. the frame/capture architecture the successor owns. No salvage of the 3-line fix exists.
(d) VERIFIED — EP-0036:67-68 "re-frame.ui is donor-only now: no new standalone surface"; :126 never published, deleted at the gate; :315-316 no day8/re-frame2-ui coordinate ever; hicasso/charter.md:147-149 end state. FLAG: CLAUDE.md's "EXPERIMENTAL, offered alongside" reads softer than the EP record — one-line discrepancy noted; this ruling rests on the inertness proof (a)-(c), not donor status.
(e) VERIFIED — census: examples/ui/minimal-counter uses compiler-owned (sub …) only; implementation/ui/{testbed,bench,g8,g13,proof-pack,dev}: zero raw core subscribe (prose mentions only); ui's own test fixture uses explicit {:frame owned} pin (never consults ambient resolver). No consumer to rescue.

ACCEPTANCE RULE for the successor (carry forward verbatim-in-spirit, per Codex): inside a framework-owned interpreted or compiled collector body, an unqualified core ambient read/dispatch MUST fail loudly; adapter-native component bodies remain unaffected; explicitly carried frame operations retain core's trusted-programmer semantics. Implementation shape: at absorption, thread the resolved frame through the substrate-owned capture or explicit observation target, THEN establish call-with-ambient-frame-refused around the author body; witnesses for raw ambient subscribe/dispatch (refuse), sanctioned sub (works), carried frames (work), adapter islands (untouched), dev/prod/JVM. If re-frame.ui is ever reversed into a supported product before deletion, implement the real thing there — never land a refusal binding that frame carriage renders inert.

Hazard remains REAL (raw ambient subscribe in a compiled body contributes no capture edge → silent freeze + unbalanced ref-count) — this deferral is not an endorsement; ui/sub stays the taught spelling and the census shows no in-tree offender. Bead stays OPEN, re-scoped as above. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-iwh5c.ui-ambient-refusal-tier.md reviewed and deleted per process.

title: Configure the beads Dolt remote (operator action)
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the .beads guard work. This is layer 4 of that bead and is OPERATOR ACTION — it cannot be done or verified from a worker worktree, which is why it was carved out rather than attempted.

THE WORK: configure the Dolt remote for the beads database so tracker state has a durable home independent of the git-tracked JSONL export, and confirm bd dolt push / bd dolt pull round-trip.

WHY IT MATTERS: the JSONL export is a mirror, not the source of truth. Today a git-side accident is recoverable only because Dolt still holds the real state locally; without a configured remote there is no off-box copy.

ACCEPTANCE: bd dolt push succeeds; bd dolt pull round-trips on a second checkout; the configuration is recorded somewhere durable rather than living only in one machine's local config.

ASSIGNEE: Mike (operator). Do not dispatch a background worker at this.
notes:
OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): ROUTE = dedicated private GitHub repository as the Dolt origin, over HTTPS — github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads — per the Codex second opinion in the dossier. NOT DoltHub (the dossier's original recommendation), NOT a self/file-based remote, NOT nothing. Pre-authorized fallback: if the initial push trips GitHub's 2 GiB per-push ceiling, switch the same origin to a private DoltHub repo and accept the $50/month — do not build split-push tooling. Timing: before the alpha tag.

WHY (facts re-verified 2026-07-27 against the installed bd 1.0.3 and primary sources):
- DoltHub private storage is free only up to 1 GB/month, then $50/month (dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolthub/permissions/ — fetched today). The live embedded DB measures ~1.8 GiB, so the DoltHub route costs $50/month from day one. A private GitHub repo is free, the same vendor/trust shape that already holds the code, and this machine's GitHub HTTPS credentials already work (SSH currently fails).
- Git-backed Dolt remotes are first-class in bd 1.0.3, not a trick: the installed `bd bootstrap --help` lists both "If sync.remote is configured: clones from the remote" and "If git origin has Dolt data (refs/dolt/data): clones from git". Dolt stores git-backed data under refs/dolt/data; ordinary source clones never fetch that ref, so a DEDICATED repo keeps ~1.8 GiB out of the code repo entirely.
- Current origin is file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) — same disk, same checkout, gitignored. That is not durability; it is what this ruling replaces.
- The remote must be PRIVATE: the Dolt DB carries ~15K historical event rows including old/new values — more history than the public JSONL mirror exposes.
- Rejected: self/file-based off-box storage (setup + credential overhead matches or exceeds DoltHub with fewer affordances); doing nothing (standing single-disk loss of all tracker + ruling history, and a session-close protocol mandating a push with nowhere to go).

OPERATOR RUNBOOK (~15 min, mayor checkout):
1. Create an empty private repo: `gh repo create day8/re-frame2-beads --private` (no README — Dolt data lives under refs/dolt/data).
2. `bd dolt remote remove origin` then `bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git`; confirm with `bd dolt show`.
3. `bd dolt push` — the first push uploads ~1.8 GiB, let it run to completion. Verify off-box: `git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` must list refs/dolt/data. [acceptance 1]
4. Durable config: check `bd config get sync.remote` and `git diff .beads/config.yaml` — bd should record sync.remote in the tracked config.yaml; if it did not, run `bd config set sync.remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` and confirm the tracked-file diff. Commit config.yaml via the normal path (it is committable human-authored .beads config; do NOT hand-commit issues.jsonl outside the checkpoint script). [acceptance 3]
5. Round-trip in a genuinely separate fresh clone — NOT a worktree (a worktree can resolve the mayor's database): `git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git <tmpdir>`, then inside it `bd bootstrap --yes` followed by `bd dolt pull`; verify `bd show rf2-4l67v` displays this ruling and `bd dolt show` matches the primary checkout. Delete the tmp clone afterwards. [acceptance 2]
6. FALLBACK if step 3 fails on the 2 GiB per-push ceiling: create a private DoltHub repo, repoint the same origin (`bd dolt remote remove origin` / `bd dolt remote add origin <dolthub-url>`), accept the $50/month, re-run steps 3-5 (recording the DoltHub URL as sync.remote in step 4).
7. Optional cleanup once acceptance passes: delete the old same-disk file remote .beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) to reclaim disk. The JSONL checkpoint remains the cheap human-inspectable recovery floor. Do NOT add a second cloud remote, scheduled backup system, or remote-management abstraction.

title: Xray full feature-matrix: new non-smoke scenarios merge unrun (policy call)
description:
SPUN OFF from rf2-9n2cv, which fixed the named defect (test:story-static) and deliberately did NOT fix this one, because it is a different shape.

NOT the rf2-65ajl / rf2-9n2cv defect. Those were 'the file that DEFINES a command is classified to no job that RUNS that command' — the file was never loaded at PR time at all. That is not true here: 'npm run test:xray-feature-gate:smoke', a command the story-xray-browser PR job already runs, require's the WHOLE of tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs. The file is loaded, parsed and validated on every PR that touches it, and the launcher fails loud if the smoke set is ever empty. A malformed or unparseable scenarios.cjs cannot merge.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNCOVERED: the non-smoke ROWS are not EXECUTED at PR time. A new scenario added without 'smoke: true' merges having never run. Its first execution is the nightly sweep.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN rf2-9n2cv: that is the documented two-tier policy, not a fail-open instrument. TESTING.md states it outright — tag a scenario 'smoke: true' only if it earns a slot on every PR AND loads an already-staged smoke surface; 'everything else is nightly by default'. Closing this gap means running the all-scenarios/all-surfaces sweep on every scenarios.cjs edit, which reverses a deliberate cost decision. That deserves its own ruling rather than being smuggled into a bug fix.

THE QUESTION TO DECIDE: is 'a new non-smoke scenario merges unrun' acceptable? Options, cheapest first:
  (1) WONTFIX — the nightly sweep is the system of record; a scenario that has never run is no worse than one whose surface regressed overnight, and the author can run the gate locally.
  (2) Run ONLY THE ADDED/CHANGED ROWS at PR time — needs a way to select scenarios by diff, plus staging only the surfaces those rows load. Most signal per second, most machinery.
  (3) Arm the FULL gate on scenarios.cjs changes — trivial to implement (one classifier arm + one conditional step, exactly the rf2-9n2cv shape), but pays the whole nightly matrix for any edit to the file, including a one-word rename.

SURFACES if actioned: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, .github/workflows/test.yml (HOT-ZONE), implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, TESTING.md.

NOTE the current pin: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs asserts doesNotMatch(block, /npm run test:xray-feature-gate(?!:smoke)/) in 'PR story-xray-browser job still keeps the rest of the sweep nightly'. rf2-9n2cv kept that pin deliberately and annotated it with this reasoning. Options (2) and (3) both require changing it — change it deliberately and mutation-prove the replacement.
close_reason: WONTFIX by delegated ruling 2026-08-05 (see ruling comment): two-tier policy stands, nightly is the system of record for non-smoke rows. Docs rider filed as follow-up P4; re-open trigger = 3 never-run-scenario nightly reds in a rolling month.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: RULING 2026-08-05 19:59 AUSEST (delegated review, operator-overturnable): Option (1) WONTFIX. The two-tier policy stands; a new non-smoke scenario may merge having never executed, and the nightly sweep remains its system of record. VERIFIED: (a) TESTING.md already documents this deliberately — the para after the two rf2-65ajl/rf2-9n2cv exceptions says the Xray full matrix is 'deliberately not a third such exception ... policy working as designed rather than a hole in it; everything else is nightly by default'. (b) The pin stays: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs 'PR story-xray-browser job still keeps the rest of the sweep nightly (rf2-wa3oo)' asserts doesNotMatch /npm run test:xray-feature-gate(?!:smoke)/, annotated with rf2-9n2cv's reasoning; (2)/(3) would require a deliberate, mutation-proved replacement of it. (c) LAUNCHER HAS NO PER-ROW FILTER: serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs selects via SMOKE = RF2_GATE_SMOKE=1 or --smoke, else ALL scenarios (ACTIVE_SCENARIOS = SMOKE ? filter smoke:true : SCENARIOS). No --only/name filter exists, so the dossier MAIN rec's 'npm run test:xray-feature-gate -- --only <id>' spelling is WRONG; the correct local-run line is: cd implementation && npm run test:xray-feature-gate (full sweep, ~3min scenario time + compile). title: hicasso SSR: :rf/render-hash is DEGENERATE for an interpreted root — the hydration-mismatch instrument is fail-open
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-2rtt6.86 while building the SSR Node render entry, and pinned
there by `the-render-hash-is-degenerate-for-an-interpreted-root` in
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs`
so it cannot quietly become load-bearing.

THE FINDING. Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection carries `:rf/render-hash` —
a structural hash of the RENDER TREE, computed server-side and recomputed by the
client at hydrate so a divergence is caught rather than rendered. The framework's
own door is `re-frame.ssr.hash/render-tree-hash` (via
`ssr-ring/lifecycle/render-document-hash`), and it works because a
hiccup->hiccup substrate hands it the WHOLE tree.

Hicasso does not. Its root hiccup is `[<minted head> {props}]` and the tree is
walked INSIDE React, so what reaches the hash is one vector whose head is a
function — and `canonical-edn` renders every function identically. MEASURED: the
dogfood screen (`[dogfood-collector/screen {}]`) and the ~1,200-element Conduit
feed page (`[large-template/page {}]`) BOTH hash `83b865f8`. A root whose hiccup
is ordinary markup hashes differently (`04cc3cdb`), which is the non-vacuity
control — the hash function is fine; the interpreted root defeats it.

CONSEQUENCE. Server and client would compute the same constant and always agree,
so the instrument never fires: a FAIL-OPEN gate of exactly the class this repo
has been closing all week. It is not wrong today (nothing computes a client-side
hash yet — that is rf2-2rtt6.84/.87's half), but it will be silently vacuous the
moment hydration verification is switched on.

WHY rf2-2rtt6.86 DID NOT FIX IT. R0: that bead does not invent a payload byte,
and a real repair is a SERVER AND CLIENT contract — whatever normalisation the
server hashes, the client must reproduce exactly, and inventing one server-side
ahead of the client half would make every page a mismatch instead of a
non-check.

THE WORK. Decide what Hicasso's render-tree hash should be over, and land both
ends together. Candidates named but not chosen: (a) normalise minted heads to
their `displayName` before hashing, so the hash is at least a function of WHICH
screen rendered (cheap, still shallow); (b) have the runtime record the walked
tree's shape during the render and hash that (deep, costs a server-side
accumulator); (c) accept the shallow hash and say so in the spec, relying on
React's own hydration-mismatch reporting for the deep case. (c) is a legitimate
answer and should be argued rather than defaulted into.

FENCES: whatever lands must keep the payload path R0-clean — the bytes stay
the framework's.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7484 (merged 2026-08-04T09:47:51Z) — USER-GUIDE CONSEQUENCE. The rewritten draft-guide/10-server-side-rendering.md says the client verifies its first tree against the structural render hash and that disagreement raises :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. That reads as a reliable deep parity guard, but this exact open owner proves Hicasso's interpreted root makes :rf/render-hash degenerate: different screens share 83b865f8, and the #7480 witness explicitly refuses to lean on it. Until this owner chooses and lands a real hash contract (or explicitly accepts the shallow hash), true up the guide to state the limit and distinguish the fail-open hash comparison from React's real onRecoverableError mismatch report. No new bead: rf2-2rtt6.91 is the exact owner.
DELIVERED via PR #7510 (green: 50 success / 33 skipped / 0 fail).

OUTCOME 1 OF THE THREE: THE SPEC ALREADY ANSWERED IT. Spec 011
§Hydration-mismatch detection tiers detection BY RENDER-TREE
REPRESENTATION, not by adapter brand. The hash channel is the HICCUP
tier's (Reagent, reagent-slim — pure fns returning a hashable data
tree). Every root that reaches React as an ELEMENT is in the adoption
tier: the compiled donor-substrate root ('no hashable client
render-tree ... the hash channel does not apply'), a native UIx root
(trace carries 'no hash'), and a Freehand root (§Hydration on the
Freehand paved path: 'Verification is React's own adoption, and it is
bounded exactly as the compiled and native tiers' is'). 011 says of
those tiers verbatim: they 'deliberately carry NO such hash'.
re-frame.ssr.boot's own docstring names Freehand explicitly:
'Compiled view — Freehand ... likewise NO :render-tree-fn'.

So Hicasso was emitting where the spec says not to. The fix was to STOP
EMITTING, not to hash better.

ON CANDIDATE (c): it is HALF the spec's answer, and the weaker half.
(c) said 'accept the shallow hash and say so in the spec, relying on
React's reporting for the deep case'. The reliance-on-adoption half IS
the spec's answer. The keep-a-shallow-hash half is NOT — the spec
carries NONE. A degenerate value is worse than an absent one: an absent
key cannot be mistaken for evidence, a constant one is a fail-open gate
wearing the shape of a check.

CANDIDATES (a) AND (b) ARE BOTH UNAVAILABLE, for one shared reason.
(a) normalise minted heads to displayName — reverses rf2-jsa2ml's
ruling (the #fn[] token exists because no fn .toString is stable across
JVM and CLJS, and dropping fn identity is what stops the HICCUP tier
firing a spurious mismatch on every page), and would still only say
WHICH screen rendered: every divergence WITHIN a screen — the entire
class this instrument exists to catch — would still compare equal.
(b) accumulate the walked tree server-side — needs the client to
reproduce the accumulation byte-for-byte, i.e. re-deriving the hiccup
tier under a substrate built not to have one.

MEASUREMENT RE-DERIVED, NOT QUOTED. 83b865f8 is not a Hicasso fact: it
is the FNV-1a of the canonical-EDN string '[#fn[] {}]', and ANY
[<some fn> {}] root takes it. Reproduced on the JVM with two throwaway
fns written for the purpose; a markup root gave 9e28d7ef as the
non-vacuity control.

WHAT LANDED. entry.cljs stops computing the hash, stamping
data-rf-render-hash, and passing one to build-payload.
payload-policy/build-payload now OMITS :rf/render-hash on a nil hash —
required, not cosmetic: Spec-Schemas types the slot '{:optional true}
:string', NOT '[:maybe :string]', so a present-and-nil key is not a
legal spelling of absence. The 'three always-present keys' docstring was
drift; the spec's payload table has said '(optional)' throughout.
Spec 011 gains the SERVER end of the tier rule — it had stated the split
almost entirely as a client-side 'do not pass :render-tree-fn', which is
how a server came to emit a degenerate hash without contradicting
anything in writing (12 insertions / 2 deletions, hot-zone surgical).
The draft guide's false structural-hash-verify claim is trued up — the
merged-PR-audit-of-#7484 obligation recorded on this bead.

THE WITNESS ROWS. the-render-hash-is-degenerate-for-an-interpreted-root
said in its own docstring it should go red the day the defect was
repaired. It has, replaced by an absence row plus a row keeping 83b865f8
measured. The three rows that CHOSE byte digests over the hash now take
it from ssr-hash/render-tree-hash directly — the degeneracy is a fact
about hashing an unresolved [<fn> {props}] root, not about the entry, so
every figure the spike-witness and server-arm dossiers publish stays
exactly reproducible.

NOT CHANGED, DELIBERATELY: ssr-ring's hiccup-tier hash (correct for
hiccup-tier hosts; gating it for an adoption-tier root needs a
host-level fact only the undecided server arm can supply — the new spec
rule now binds whichever arm lands), and the dated dossiers (records of
a measurement true when taken and still reproducible).

The runtime repair is correct: the interpreted entry emits neither :rf/render-hash nor data-rf-render-hash; build-payload omits the optional key on nil; focused entry tests pin absence while retaining the 83b865f8 degeneracy measurement; Spec 011 and the guide now state the adoption-tier rule; 50 applicable GitHub checks passed.
